11100015.label: Realisation of objectives
11100015.value: All Objectives were completed. Figures and References are attached in Part C. Section 11 Other Impact. Objective 1.1: To investigate the motor functional synapse formation and PC dendritic arborization after peripheral nerve injury (PNI): We first assessed functional recovery in control (Lhx1fx/fx, Lhx5fx/fx) and Lhx1/5 double knockout (DKO) (Pcp2-Cre, Lhx1fx/fx, Lhx5fx/fx) mice after a single sciatic nerve crush (SNC) (Fig. 1A). Mice usually fully restore function in 4 weeks after a single SNC (1-3). DKO mice exhibited significant delay in motor functional recovery (Fig. 1B-D). Sensory functional recovery was unaffected (Fig. 1E). Severe motor coordination and balance deficits was detected in DKO mice by rotarod test (Fig. 1F) as described (4, 5). To examine motor functional synapse formation, we performed weekly electromyography (EMG) recording in proximal (gastrocnemius) and distal (interosseous) muscles after SNC, which is a definitive method to measure motor functional recovery quantitatively (1, 2, 6). Delay of motor functional recovery in DKO mice was validated by reduced compound muscle action potential amplitude (CMAP) (Fig. 1G-H). NMJ formation was quantified by immunohistochemistry (Fig. 2A), which was reduced significantly in the distal target muscle (Fig. 2B). Golgi staining of Purkinje cells (PCs) revealed abnormal formation of PC dendritic arborization in DKO mice (Fig. 3). We performed additional electrophysiology study of deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN) neuronal spike firing by multi-electrode array (MEAs) at 1-2 weeks after SNC (Fig. 4A). DCN neuronal spike firing pattern reflects PC dendritic arborization quantitatively since PC is the sole output of DCN. DKO mice exhibited statistically significant increase in neuronal firing rate (Fig. 4B), reduced neuronal interspike interval (Fig. 4C) and increased numbers of neuronal bursts (Fig. 4D). Raster plots of DCN neuronal spike activity showed frequent and irregular firing pattern in DKO mice (Fig. 4E), and heat diagram demonstrated significant reduce in interspike interval time (Fig. 4F). We observed a trend of increasing neuronal firing rate in DKO and control mice after SNC but not reaching statistical significance (Fig. 4B-D). Objective 1.2: To examine the temporal dynamic of functional recovery during critical period in animal model of PNI: We investigated if conditional knockout of Lhx1/5 shortens the critical period that there is no functional recovery if regenerating axons arrived at the motor endplate after 35 days. We have established a mouse model to study critical period by performing repeated SNCs (most severe PNI) at different time interval. (3). We crushed sciatic nerves 4 times at 2-day intervals (preventing reinnervation for 16 days) (Fig. 5A) and observed a significant delay in motor functional recovery in DKO mice (Fig. 5B-E). Sensory functional recovery was unaffected (Fig. 5F). DKO mice demonstrated severe motor coordination deficit (Fig. 5G). The delay in motor functional recovery was validated by EMG recoding, whereas the CMAP amplitude was significantly reduced in DKO mice (Fig. 5H-I) similar to DKO mice after single SNC (Fig. 1G-H). We performed additional work to crush sciatic nerves 4 times at 4-day intervals (preventing reinnervation for 22 days) (Fig. 6A), that the mice are able to fully recover normally (3). Surprisingly, DKO mice were not able to recover motor function (Fig. 6B-E), and sensory functional recovery was unaffected (Fig. 6F). DKO mice demonstrated severe motor coordination deficit (Fig. 6G). Motor function deficit in DKO mice were confirmed by reduced CMAP amplitude (Fig. 6H-I). We performed additional work to confirm the shortening of critical period by crushing sciatic nerves 4 times at 5-day intervals (preventing reinnervation for 25 days) (Fig. 7A). Motor function were fully recovered in control mice by 27 days; however, DKO mice were not able to regain toe spreading reflex and grip strength (Fig. 7B-E). Sensory functional recovery was unaffected (Fig. 7F). Typical ataxia motor coordination deficit was detected (Fig. 7G). The lack of motor function recovery in DKO mice was validated by EMG recording (Fig. 7H-I). The number of regenerating axons in sciatic nerves remained the same in both groups of animal two months after injury, indicated that motor deficits was not due to the lack of axon regeneration (Fig. 8) but the reduced formation of NMJs in target muscle (Fig. 9). Objective 1.3: To examine the intrinsic growth capacity of injured DRG neuron from Lhx1/5 mutant mice: This objective was completed in the mid-term report (Figs. 10 and 11). Intrinsic growth capacity in injured neurons of DKO mice was unaffected. Objective 2.1 To examine the cerebellum and motor cortex electrophysiological activity by using EEG recording during PNI: We examined the baseline electroencephalography (EEG) power spectrum of cerebellum and motor cortex in DKO and control mice, respectively (Figs. 12-13). Abnormal EEG power spectrum was observed in DKO mice at low- (Theta) (Figs. 12A and 13A) and high-frequency (Gamma) bands in cerebellum (Figs. 12B and 13B), which contributes to the ataxia phenotype such as motor coordination deficit and tremor. We performed electrical and optogenetics stimulation to investigate the cerebellum network architectural connectivity. DKO mice exhibited slow propagation of neuronal signal in descending motor pathway from DCN to target muscle via motor cortex and spinal cord (Fig. 14). We performed additional proof-of-concept experiments to conclude our major hypothesis that DCN is crucial for motor functional recovery after injury. We performed unilateral electrical lesion of DCN (Fig. 15A) and was confirmed by histology (Fig. 15B). DCN lesion mice demonstrated typical ataxia motor coordination deficit on a rotating rod similar to DKO mice (Fig. 15C). Motor functional recovery was delayed significantly in DCN lesion mice (Fig. 15D) and confirmed by EMG recording (Fig. 15E). Sensory functional recovery was unaffected (Fig. 15F). Hippocampal lesion was served as a negative control to show that lesion on motor-unrelated brain region would not affect PNS regeneration (Fig. 16A). Hypothalamus plays an important role in spatial cognition and memory. Lesion was confirmed by histology (Fig. 16B). Y-maze and Morris water maze tests were performed to confirm the successful of hippocampal lesion by showing memory deficits (Fig. 16C-D). Motor coordination, sensory and motor functional recovery, and EMG activities of hippocampal lesion mice were comparable to sham lesion mice after SNC (Fig. 16E-J). Lastly, we consider the most important proof-of-concept studies to demonstrate that daily deep brain stimulation (DBS) could rescue the motor function deficit after single and multiple SNC (Figs. 17-18). Neuronal firing pattern was largely returned to baseline levels assessed by MEAs DCN recording after 1-2 weeks of DBS post-injury (Fig. 19). Objective 2.2 To investigate the underlying mechanism of Lhx1/5 by bioinformatics analysis: We performed bioinformatics analysis to identify potential genes that are highly related to Lhx1/5 using a public database GeneMANIA. Interestingly, Lhx1/5 were found to co-express with regeneration-associated genes (RAGs) such as Atf3, Fos, Jun, Mapk3, and Prph2 (Fig. 20A). Functional annotations revealed that Lhx1/5-associated gene were functionally related to development and differentiation of spinal motor neuron and skeletal muscle (Fig. 20B). We performed qPCR analysis in motor neurons of ventral horn at different time points after a single SNC. We showed that 13 out of 15 genes were differentially expressed in DKO mice which are related to neuronal survival (BDNF, Gap43, Mapk3 and IGFBP6), neuronal activities (cFos and CaMK2a), presynaptic protein (SNAP25), and motor neuron specific RAGs (Fgf1, Hsp12a, Cdh22, Lynx1, Sema3a and Anxa5) (Fig. 21).

11100015.label: Major findings and research outcome
11100015.value: Current study examines how the changes in cerebellar plasticity alter the regenerative capacity of the peripheral nervous system. We demonstrate for the first time that a conditional knockout (KO) of Lhx1 and 5 in purkinje cells (PCs), transcription factors that are crucial for PC development, delays motor functional recovery after peripheral nerve injury (PNI). Lhx1/5 KO mice exhibit ataxia phenotypes which resembles clinical features of spinocerebellar ataxia. We confirm the shortening of critical period in Lhx1/5 KO mice, which normally allow meaningful motor functional recovery within 35 days post-injury in animal model of chronic muscle denervation. We perform unilateral electrical lesion of deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN) to validate and confirm that disruption of cerebellar circuity reduces regenerative capacity of peripheral nerve after injury. Our in vitro and in vivo indicate that the intrinsic growth capacity and axon growth rate of injured neurons in Lhx1/5 KO mice, which are unaffected. We also hypothesize that the lack of regenerative capacity in Lhx1/5 KO mice is due to the alternation of cerebellar plasticity. Abnormal electroencephalography (EEG) power spectrum of cerebellum and motor cortex is observed in Lhx1/5 KO mice. Reduced neuronal firing rate and interspike interval recorded by multi-electrode array is found in Lhx1/5 KO mice. Daily deep brain stimulation of DCN in cerebellum rescues motor deficits and neuronal firing rate in Lhx1/5 KO mice after sciatic nerve crush and restores critical period in Lhx1/5 KO mice. We perform bioinformatics analysis to identify regeneration-associated and motor neuron specific genes that are closely related to Lhx1/5 expression. Our qPCR data show that most of these genes are downregulated in Lhx1/5 KO mice, which might account for the motor deficits after injury. Further investigation is required to uncover the underlying mechanism, which can provide new insight into the development of therapeutically regulating cortical changes such as neuroprosthetics to improve rehabilitation after PNI. Four papers were published in top Journals in the area of Neuroscience. Two PhD students (Bennett Au and Chine Virendra) are involved and trained in current studies. We presented the work in the largest Neuroscience Meeting in the US for three consecutive years and in a local HK Neuroscience Meeting in 2016.

11100015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11100015.value: We demonstrate that genetic ablation of Lhx1/5 specially in purkinje cells, disrupts cerebellar circuity and reduces regenerative capacity of the peripheral nerves. However, detail mechanism underlying the inhibitory effects of Lhx1/5 ablation on motor function recovery requires further study. More importantly, deep brain stimulation (DBS) of deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN) reverses the ataxia phenotype and restores neuronal firing in DCN. Our data show that cerebellar circuity plays a key role in peripheral nerve regeneration which remains largely unexplored. For the last decade, neuroprosthesis becomes an emerging field of significant interest to neuroscientists or bioengineers alike, which has been rapidly progressing to revolutionize the biomedical field aiming to improve mainly patient’s motor functional outcomes. DBS has been widely used in treating neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease. Knowledge obtained from current project will shed new light on the development of neuroprosthetics and neurorehabilitation strategies for improving ataxia patient’s quality of life. Our study will certainly spur new scientific investigation in the development of novel therapeutic opportunities to manage the catastrophic loss of functions caused by nervous system injuries such as patients with spinal cord injury and neurodegenerative diseases.

11100015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11100015.value: Nervous system injuries often result in catastrophic loss of motor function, and are indeed the most challenging problems faced by clinicians. There is currently no effective treatment associated with the loss of sensory and motor function, but there are limited options to manage the symptoms such as physiotherapy. Therefore, there is an immediate need for potential therapy to direct at promoting nerve regeneration, and ultimately to achieve full functional recovery in patients. Current proposed study aims to address this important question by examining how the cerebellar circuity affect regenerative capacity of injured neurons. We show that disruption of cerebellar circuity by genetic ablation of transcription factor Lhx1/5 in purkinje cells or electrical lesion of cerebellum result in motor function deficits. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is able to reverse motor function deficits and restore brain circuity after peripheral nerve injury. Our studies imply that patients with neurodegenerative diseases which possess disruption of brain circuity due to progressive loss of neurons, are likely not able to regain full functional recovery after peripheral nerve injury. We believe that current study provides new insight into the development of rehabilitation strategies for improving nervous system injury patient’s quality of life.

11100215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100215.value: Aim This study aims to investigate the molecular mechanisms of protein kinase PIM1 response to facilitate human Enterovirus 71 (EV71) infection. Project Background EV71 has repeatedly emerged as a major threat to the public health in the Asia-Pacific regions in the past decade. EV71 have infected over a million children that caused hand-foot-and-mouse disease (HFMD) and have led to hundreds to thousands of deaths in China annually. No effective therapy or vaccine is available to prevent or treat EV71 infection. To promote antiviral drug development, it is urgent to better understand how the host responses combat or facilitate viral infection. Brief Project Description Our team has investigated the host responses to EV71 infection by microarray studies. After validation by quantitative RT-PCR and western blot assays, we have shown that PIM1 is one of the most elevated proteins which responds to EV71 infection. Knockdown of PIM1 or inhibition of PIM1 activity by a specific inhibitor significantly reduced virus yield secreted in culture media, whereas overexpression of PIM1 increased viral production. Further studies have revealed that PIM1 plays an important role in facilitating viral package and secretion. In this study, we will investigate the underlying mechanisms of PIM1 enhancing virus infections via phosphorylation of Hsp90β. Furthermore, we will reveal whether PIM1 inhibitors could be used as potential antiviral drugs. Significance of Project The results of this study will provide new insights into the strategies that are used by the virus to facilitate its life cycle in host cells and will promote the development of new antiviral agents against EV71. 過去10多年來，腸病毒71型（EV71）在亞太地區反復感染已成為公共衛生的主要挑戰。EV71感染可導致人類手足口病， 在中國每年導致數百至上千兒童死亡。然而目前仍無有效的疫苗或藥物去預防、治療EV71 感染。 目前急切需要瞭解宿主與病毒的相互作用機理以促進抗病毒藥物的研發。 我們團隊研究了病毒感染後的宿主基因表達譜，發現PIM1的表達在EV71個人後顯著上升。 沉默PIM1的表達以及PIM1抑制劑顯著降低培養基中病毒的含量，而過表達PIM1 促進EV71的病毒產量。進一步研究發現，PIM1 在病毒包裝及分泌過程中起著重要作用。本研究將研究PIM1如何通過磷酸化Hsp90β增強病毒感染， 以及PIM1抑制劑是否可作為抗病毒藥物的可能性。

11100215.label: Realisation of objectives
11100215.value: Address to Objective 1: To reveal the regulation pattern of Pim1 in EV-A71 infection, we used RT-qPCR assays to analyze Pim1 mRNA levels of RD cells infected with EV-A71 or inactive EV-A71 (UV light-inactive virus) at MOI of 1 and 10 at different time points (post infection, p.i.). We observed that the mRNA level of Pim1 notably increased as early as 3 h p.i. at a high MOI of 10, and significant upregulation was observed (Figure 1, iScience, 2019). Notably, although virus treated with UV would not affect virus entry, it did not stimulate Pim1 response. To address which viral protein stimulates Pim1 expression, we transfected all viral protein expression plasmids into 293T cells, and found that viral 2Apro as well as VP4, 2B, and 3B slightly stimulated Pim1 expression, but only 2Apro significantly increased the mRNA level of Pim1 by more than two times (Figure, iScience, 2019). Address to Objective 2: We transfected a Pim-1 overexpression plasmid into RD and HEK293 cells. 48 hours post-transfection, we infected the cells with EV71 at MOI of 1. We harvested cells 12 hour p.i., and applied cell lysate for western blot to detect the total amount of Hsp90β and phosphorylated Hsp90β. We confirmed that Pim-1 overexpression increased the phosphorylation of Hsp90β. There were multiple phosphorylated Hsp90β bands, suggested multiple sites can be phosphorylated by Pim-1 during EV71 infection. Furthermore, we conducted immunoprecipitation assays to demonstrate whether Pim-1 could directly interact with Hsp90β. We observed that antibody against Hsp90β successfully precipitated Hsp90β in Pim-1 overexpression cells, which was detected by an antibody against Ser/Thr phosphorylated proteins; while no obvious phosphorylated Hsp90β protein was precipitated in control cells. We employed TOF/TOF mass spectrometry to identify Hsp90β phosphorylation sites of Pim1. Due to technique problem, we tried twice but did not figure out the phosphorylation sites. Because the second budget allocation was suspended and finally cancelled by GRF council, we did not further address this objective. Address to Objective 3: We first investigated the biological functions of Pim1 in EV-A71 life cycle. We designed 2 siRNAs to knock down Pim1. The level of Pim1 mRNA was reduced in RD and HeLa cells by 80% and 70% by siPim1-1- and siPim1-2-specific siRNAs, respectively. The extracellular virion RNA levels and viral titers were strongly decreased in Pim1-specific siRNA-treated cells; and viral protein (VP1) expression level was also significantly decreased in both RD and HeLa cells after silencing Pim1 (Fig.1, iScience, 2019). Then we examined viral replication in cells with ectopic expression of Pim1. We observed that Pim1 increased viral titers both in RD and HeLa cells. The VP1 protein level also significantly increased in the cells with ectopic expression of. Furthermore, we performed a rescue experiment to show the function of Pim1 in EV-A71 infection. We first knocked down the endogenous Pim1 expression by an siRNA that specifically targets the 3′ UTR in RD cells, ectopically expressed Pim1 (resistance to siRNA) then infected with EV-A71. We demonstrated that the reduced VP1 level by Pim1 depletion was restored (Figures 2, iScience, 2019). Next, we used a dicistronic reporter plasmid to evaluate the IRES activity when Pim1 was modulated. The relative IRES activity was calculated and presented by the ratio of FLuc expression to RLuc expression. We observed that over-expression of Pim1 increased the EV-A71 IRES activity to 200%, whereas Pim1 knockdown decreases EV-A71 IRES activity to 40% of the control. We later co-transfected pIRES plasmid and a viral protein-expressing plasmid individually. The results showed the viral 2Apro is the most effective protein that increased the IRES activity. To further address our findings, we then performed the rescue experiments. We silenced Pim1 and then ectopically expressed 2Apro. Obviously, 2Apro rescued the reduction of IRES activity after knockdown of Pim1 (Figure 3, iScience, 2019). Knockdown of Hsp90β decreases 60% of virus replication 12h post infection (p.i.), while the secreted virions decrease by approximately 80%, indicating the crucial roles of Hsp90β in both virus replication and secretion. knockdown or knockout of Hsp90β decreased the proteins expression level of EV-A71 structure protein. Hsp90 inhibitors 17-AAG, Geldanamycin (GA) and VER50588 all dramatically inhibit EV-A71 protein expression. Among them, VER50588 display the strongest inhibitory effect which has not been reported before. Upon overexpression PIM1 and knockdown of PIM1, the phosphorylated status of Hsp90β is increased and decreased, respectively. More importantly, knockout of Hsp90β by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing almost completely abolishes the effects of PIM1 signaling on EV-A71 replication (Fig.4, Signal Transduction and Target Therapy, 2020). As Pim1 signalling plays crucial role in innate immunity and inflammatory response, in addition to the proposed work, we used protein array combined ELLISA assays to reveal the cytokine status in EV-A71 infected patients. We demonstrated that Eotaxin, IP-10 and IL-8 could be potential indicators for predicting HFMD progression with EV-A71 infection. MMP-8 is a specific indicator for mild infection, while IL-1b and leptin display potential for predicting the severity and criticality (Cytokine, 2019). Address to Objective 4: Pim1 inhibitors CX-6258, SGI-1776 and AZD-1208 are novel, orally bioavailable inhibitors for treating patients with cancer in clinical trials . To test whether Pim1 is a potential drug target against EV-A71 infection, we examined the effects of these inhibitors on EV-A71 infection in both RD and HeLa cells. Our results showed the VP1 expression level was remarkably repressed by Pim1 inhibitors in a dose-dependent manner. CX-6258 showed the best inhibitory effects in RD cells. We further used CX-6258 as a Pim1 inhibitor to determine the extracellular viral mRNA levels. After inhibiting Pim1, viral mRNA levels were significantly decreased both in RD and HeLa cells. In addition, the viral titer was also decreased by more than 1000 folds after inhibiting Pim1 activity with CX-6258 in RD and HeLa cells (Figures 4, iScience, 2019). To address how Pim1 affects the IRES activity regulated by 2Apro, we first tested whether Pim1 inhibitors could affect the cleavage of eIF4G after virus infection. RD cells were treated with CX-6258 at different concentrations and then infected with EV-A71. After 9 h p.i., the cleavage of eIF4G was significantly inhibited. To further demonstrate the underlying mechanism, HEK293T cells were first treated with CX-6258 for 2 h and then co-transfected with a 2Apro-expressing plasmid for 36 h. We found that the cleavage of eIF4G was also inhibited with Pim1 inhibitor in a dose-dependent manner. Similar results also obtained from 293T cells. To test whether the Pim1 inhibitor would directly affect 2Apro activity, we further examined the status of 2Apro -mediated eIF4G cleavage in Pim1 knockdown cells treated with CX-6258 at different concentrations. As expected, CX-6258 did not further affect 2Apro activity in the Pim1-depleted cells, demonstrating that the inhibitory effects of 2Apro-mediated eIF4G cleavage were mediated through the suppressed Pim1 kinase activity (Figures 5, iScience, 2019). Animal study was given up because of the cancellation of second budget allocation.

11100215.label: Major findings and research outcome
11100215.value: Major findings: Host-virus interactions play key roles in establishing viral infection and determining the disease progression and outcome of antiviral therapies. In this study, our major findings are: (1) the expression of Pim1 was significantly upregulated in EV-A71 infection. The viral protease 2A protein plays a major role in stimulating Pim1 expressions. (2) Ectopic expression or silencing of Pim1 promoted or inhibited EV-A71 replication through two distinct mechanisms. (3) Pim1 enhanced viral IRES activity by increasing viral 2A protease-mediated eIF4G cleavage.(4) Pim1 blocked AUF1, a suppressor of IRES, translocation from the nucleus to cytosol. (5) Pim1 inhibitors (SGI-1776, AZD-1208, and CX-6258) reduced EV-A71 reproduction. Particularly, CX-6258 remarkably reduced EV-A71 reproduction more than 1,000 times, providing a potential therapeutic agent for EV-A71 treatment. (6) Hsp90β play an important role in EV-A71 infection, knockout of Hsp90β by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing almost completely abolishes the effects of PIM1 signalling on EV-A71 replication. Research Outcome: 1) We published three research papers (2 papers are directly from the objectives—iScience, 2019; Signal Transduction and Target Therapy, 2020; 1 additional paper related to the consequence of Pim1 signaling cascade—cytokine 2019). 2) We trained 3 Ph.D students; 3) The PI was invited for 3 key talks in international conference (with abstract attached) 4) Filed a US patent.

11100215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11100215.value: 1) Pim1 inhibitors showed potent antiviral effects in culture cells. To further push to clinic trials, animal studies should be conducted with new fund support. 2) We revisited and analysed an unbiased RNA sequencing data from ZIKV infected Vero cells. Result from KEGG pathway assays showed that ZIKV infection involved in many pathways, such as pathways in cancer, spliceosome, herpes simplex infection and so on. Most interestingly, the upregulation of PIM1 is much obvious than others. We confirmed the increased pattern of PIM1 in in both RD and A549 cells with ZIKV infection. Further studies showed that Pim1 may undergo both ZIKV dependent and pathogen-free independent pathways for virus escape of host immune immunity. Further investigation may pave a new way for antiviral therapy against many viruses, including flavivirus (Dengue virus, hepatitis C virus, Zika virus, etc), enteroviruses, and coronaviruses (SARS-CoV-1, SARS-CoV-2 and MERS-COV, etc).

11100215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11100215.value: As an oncoprotein, Pim1 kinase play a crucial role in many kind of human cancers. Several Pim1 inhibitors have been developed for antitumor treatment. Currently, these inhibitors are undergoing Phase I to Phase III clinical trials. Our study demonstrated that EV-A71 infection stimulates Pim1 expression that further facilitates virus replication through two different mechanisms. Most importantly, Pim1 inhibitors can decrease viral titer over 1,000 folds, demonstrating great potential to further develop these inhibitors or their novel derivatives into antiviral drugs for treating multiple infections by different positive-sense single-stranded RNA viruses such as EV-A71, Zika virus, SARS-CoV-2.

11101215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101215.value: The thalamocortical network has been proposed to be strongly involved in neuronal plasticity and memory consolidation. The thalamocortical network displays tonic, slow wave, spindle, and high-frequency-burst firing modes. Our earlier studies exhibited that the auditory thalamus, medial geniculate body (MGB) displays slow-wave and spindle oscillations, and burst firing. In several recent experiments, we found that the medial temporal lobe modulates the neuronal plasticity in the auditory cortex through cholecystokinin (CCK). Puffing CCK before pairing glutamate puffing with depolarization of the patched neuron that generated action potential induced long-term potentiation in excitatory post-synaptic potentials to the glutamate puffings. Retrogradely labeled thalamocortical neurons in the auditory thalamus after True-Blue injection in the auditory cortex were mostly CCK-immunopositive. Putting above two separated stories together, we hypothesize that the cortical neuronal plasticity involves the CCK release of thalamocortical neurons and burst firings are necessary to trigger the CCK release of the thalamocortical neurons. In the proposed study, we will activate the MGB with pulse trains, each of which will be followed by 5 repeats of the probe auditory stimulus. The auditory responses to the probe stimulus will be monitored for a long period (up to 1.5 hr) and compared with the baseline before pairings of electrical stimulation of the MGB and the auditory stimuli. We will then examine the effectiveness of electrical stimulation of the MGB in different modes: tonic and burst, in inducing the potentiation in the neuronal responses to the auditory stimulus. We will also examine the effectiveness of the electrical stimulation of different frequency. The most important objective is to investigate whether the burst-stimulation of the MGB induced potentiation will be suppressed by local application of CCKB antagonist in the auditory cortex. The CCK knockout mice and CCK B-receptor knockout mice will be adopted as other controls. The last objective is to investigate how burst-stimulation of the MGB induced neuronal potentiation is reflected in the cortical tonotopic organization in the anesthetized rat. Thalamocortical plasticity has been demonstrated and could happen after the critical period. The proposed experiment will unveil the mechanism leading to such plasticity and the conditions needed for this plasticity. As proposed by early studies, the thalamocortical circuits are involved in the memory consolidation during slow wave sleep. The proposed study linking the high-frequency burst firing with the neuronal plasticity may add on an important piece of the puzzle to unveil the mechanism how the thalamocortical oscillation facilitates the memory consolidation. 丘腦皮層網絡對於神經元可塑性和記憶鞏固是具有很強的作用。丘腦皮層網絡展現慢波，以及梭形和高頻簇狀發放模式。我們之前的研究顯示，聽覺丘腦、內側膝狀體（MGB）展現慢波和梭形振盪，以及簇狀發放模式。丘腦皮層在最近的幾次實驗中，我們發現大腦內側顳葉通過膽囊收縮素（CCK）調節聽覺皮層的神經元可塑性。在離體實驗中，CCK噴射谷氨酸與嵌置神經元去極化產生的動作電位配對之前註入，可誘導谷氨酸引起的興奮性突觸後電位產生長時程增強作用。在聽覺皮層注射True-Blue染色劑後，聽覺丘腦內逆行標記的丘腦皮層神經元大多呈現CCK免疫陽性。綜合以上發現，我們假設皮質神經元可塑性涉及丘腦皮層神經元的CCK釋放，而簇狀發放模式是激發丘腦皮層神經元CCK釋放的必要條件。在提案的研究中，我們將利用脈衝串刺激激活MGB，每個脈沖之後將重複5次探測聽覺刺激進行配對。然後，我們會在一段長時間（不多於1.5小時）監測對探測刺激的聽覺反應，並與配對前基線水平作比較。然後，我們將研究不同模式(強直和猝發)的MGB電刺激，對誘發神經元對聽覺刺激作出反應增強的效能。我們也會研究不同頻率的電刺激所產生的效用。這項研究的最重要目標，是研究MGB猝發刺激引致的增強作用，是否受到在聽覺皮層局部應用CCKB拮抗劑的抑制。我們會在實驗中採用CCK基因敲除小鼠和CCK B-受體基因敲除小鼠來作為其他對照標準。研究的最後一個目標是研究MGB簇狀刺激導致神經元增強作用，是如何在麻醉大鼠的大腦聽皮層音頻拓撲組織體現出來。 前人的研究已經證明丘腦皮層可塑性在發育關鍵期後也可發生。本提案的實驗將揭示這種可塑性的發生機制，以及這種可塑性所需要的條件。根據早期研究提出的論點，丘腦皮層環路參與慢波睡眠期間的記憶鞏固。建議進行的研究把高頻率簇狀發放模式與神經元可塑性連在一起，也許能夠得出解開謎團的另一個重要環節，揭示丘腦振盪式發放促進記憶鞏固的機制。

11101215.label: Realisation of objectives
11101215.value: Objective 1 and 2. we first applied HFS (high-frequency stimulation) in the MGB (medial geniculate body) to induce thalamocortical LTP (long-term potentiation) with in-vivo preparation and examined whether this LTP would have an impact on cortical neuronal responses to the natural stimulus. We placed a stimulation electrode array in the MGB and recording electrode array that recorded neuronal responses to electrical stimulation, and the noise burst in the ACx (auditory cortex). Those electrodes showed neuronal responses to the noise-burst stimulus were selected as the stimulation electrode in the MGB or recording electrodes in the ACx. Field excitatory postsynaptic potential (fEPSP) to the electrical stimulation of different currents in the MGB was measured. Consistent with the previous findings in other sensory modalities, HFS successfully induced thalamocortical LTP in the young adult rat. The slope of fEPSPs that was measured 1 h after the HFS was potentiated by 56.76 ± 7.21% compared to the baseline before the HFS (n=11, one-way ANOVA, p<0.001). We then investigated whether the neuronal responses to the natural auditory stimulus in the ACx was also potentiated after the HFS-induced thalamocortical LTP. The firing rate of the neuronal responses to the noise-burst stimulus in the ACx increased after the HFS. The mean Z-score of the neuronal responses to the noise burst stimulus showed a significant increase (n=12, from 6 rats, two-way ANOVA，p<0.001; post-hoc, Tukey test, before vs. after HFS, 10.58±2.28 vs. 19.19±3.04, p< 0.001) after the HFS of the MGB, indicating that the supposed thalamocortical LTP facilitated neuronal responses to the natural stimulus. On contrary, LFS (low frequency stimulation) could not induce thalamocortical LTP (n=8, before vs. after, 103.18±4.53% vs. 93.57±4.99% post-hoc, Tukey test, p=0.05). Therefore, only burst stimulation pattern could induce the potentiation in the ACx. Objective 3. We next examined whether CCK-expressing neurons in the MGB send projections to the ACx. True Blue, a retrograde tracer, was injected into the ACx, and CCK expression in the retrogradely labeled neurons was then detected with a CCK antibody. The high level of True Blue and CCK colocalization indicated that most of the thalamocortical projecting neurons in the MGB expressed CCK. We then surmised that the CCK-/- mouse would show deficits in thalamocortical plasticity. HFS induced no LTP in the thalamocortical pathway of CCK-/- mice (CCK-CreER mice, examined in Chen et al., 2019), but significant LTP in C57 wild-type mice (CCK-/-, n=9; C57, n=8, two-way ANOVA, p<0.001; post-hoc, Tukey test, CCK-/-, 108.41±3.92% vs. 101.68±11.49%, p=0.983; C57, 103.47±1.85% vs. 159.75±7.23%, p<0.001). In the next experiment, we infused L365,260, a CCK-B receptor antagonist, into the ACx of rats before the HFS in the MGB for the experimental group, and artificial cerebral-spinal fluid (ACSF) for the control group. HFS-induced thalamocortical LTP was totally blocked in the L365,260 infusion group, but not in the ACSF infusion group (L365, 260, n=9; ACSF, n=8, two-way ANOVA, p<0.001, post-hoc, Tukey test, L365, 260, before: 100.43±1.17% vs. after: 94.74±4.20%, p>0.05; ACSF, before: 99.16±1.32% vs. after: 118.31±2.94%, p<0.001), suggesting that the dependence of CCK of the thalamocortical LTP is via CCK-B receptor. In order to exclude other possibilities than the thalamocortical CCK-positive projection, we injected a Cre-dependent virus, AAV-EFIa-DIO-hChR2 (E123T/T159C)-EYFP into the MGB of the CCK-Cre mouse. Many MGB neuron were labeled with EYFP, indicating that thalamocortical projection neurons were CCK positive. EYFP labeled thalamocortical projection fibers, mainly targeted layer IV of the ACx. After we stained CCKB receptors, we found that CCK-positive thalamocortical terminals (green) were colocalized with CCKB receptors. These results imply that thalamocortical terminals may release CCK targeting at CCKB receptors in layer IV of the ACx. Then we inserted an optic fiber into the MGB and placed the recording electrode in layer IV (350-500 µm) of the ACx. After a stable baseline of 15 min recording of laser-evoked thalamocortical fEPSPs, HF laser stimulation (HFLS) was delivered into the MGB. A robust LTP was achieved after HFLS (before vs. after, 99.29±1.57% vs. 134.19±4.65%, n=8, one-way ANOVA, p<0.001). These findings suggest that HF activation of CCK-positive thalamocortical neurons trigger the release of CCK at the thalamocortical synapses, which in turn enables thalamocortical LTP. Objective 4. We further investigated whether the CCK-induced neuroplasticity could enhance the frequency discrimination ability of the young adult mouse. We infused CCK-8S to the ACx and delivered a supra-threshold tone stimulus for 200 trails to the anesthetized mouse. The tuning curves of the auditory cortical neurons were measured before and after the intervention. CCK-8S did not cause the shift the characteristic frequency (CF) of the tuning curve to the frequency of the exposed tone. The responding threshold was significantly lowered to the frequencies near the exposed tone in the range with one octave in the auditory cortex of the experimental group with the CCK-8S infusion, while the responding threshold was not lowered to any frequencies near the exposed tone in the shame control group with ACSF infusion (8.66±1.91dB at exposed frequency, p<0.001; 6.66±2.32dB P<0.001 and 5.33±1.33 dB, p< 0.05 at frequencies of 0.4 octave lower and 0.4 octave higher than the exposed frequency respectively; CCK, n=15; ACSF n=12, two-way ANOVA, p<0.001, post hoc: Tukey test, CCK-8S vs. ACSF, p<0.001), suggesting that the application of CCK-8S and the sound exposure induced thalamocortical LTP and led to the lowered response threshold near the exposed tone. In the next experiment, we adopted a prepulse inhibition acoustic startle test to examine the rat’s ability in frequency discrimination. The prepulse inhibition (PPI) level indicates how well the animals perceive the frequency differences between the background tone and prepulse tone. The higher PPI means the mouse can differentiate the two frequencies better. Both CCK-8S and ACSF infused mice were exposed to tone stimulations (9.8 or 16.4 kHz) in a soundproof chamber immediately after the infusion. The frequency discrimination ability was tested by comparing the PPIs between the two groups at 24 h after exposure. As expected, in both ACSF control groups, mice showed a gradual increase in PPI as the difference of the frequencies between the background tone and the prepulse tone became larger. The differences between the experimental and the control groups mainly appeared at the frequencies near the exposed frequency. The PPI showed a significant difference in detecting the prepulse tone with the 2% difference from the background tone (9.8kHz, CCK-8S group, n=7, ACSF group, n=7, two-way ANOVA, p<0.05, 32.50±3.86% vs 13.67±2.77%, post-hoc, Tukey test, CCK-8S vs. ACSF, p<0.001; 16.4kHz, CCK group, n=7, ACSF group, n=7, two-way ANOVA, p<0.05, 39.15±3.01% vs 15.43±4.97%, post-hoc, Tukey test, CCK-8S vs. ACSF, p<0.001). The PPI difference for both exposed frequencies reached > 18.8% when the difference of the exposed frequency and the prepulse frequency was 2%. This result indicates that CCK infusion and tone exposure at anesthesia enhanced the animal’s ability for frequency discrimination near the frequency of the exposed tone.

11101215.label: Major findings and research outcome
11101215.value: Major findings. In the present study, we hypothesized that CCK, which is expressed in the MGB, plays an essential role in the formation of thalamocortical LTP based on our precious findings that CCK could prompt neuroplasticity (Li et al., 2014). To test this hypothesis, we examined the existence of the HFS-induced thalamocortical LTP in the CCK-/- mouse and the blockage of thalamocortical LTP by CCK-B receptor antagonist in the wild-type C57 mouse. We then selectively activated with optogenetics the CCK-positive thalamocortical neurons for LTP induction. We further examined whether the rescued thalamocortical neuroplasticity can improve sound discrimination in a behavioral experiment (Feng et al., 2019). Our results showed that thalamocortical LTP could be induced using the standard protocol of HFS, indicating that thalamocortical synapses are still plastic after the early critical period defined by Malenka. We show here for the first time the HFS induced thalamocortical LTP in the ACx of the young adult rat with in-vivo preparation. In the present study, we confirmed that nearly all the thalamocortical projecting neurons expressed CCK. HFS induced no thalamocortical LTP in the CCK-/- mouse. Likewise, a CCKB receptor antagonist, L365,260 blocked thalamocortical LTP in the wild-type rat, suggesting that CCK is a necessary condition for the induction of thalamocortical LTP in the young adult brain. By using optogenetic method, our results showed that the thalamocortical CCK neurons followed the HF laser activation, supposedly released CCK, and then induced thalamocortical LTP, supporting our hypothesis that the thalamocortical LTP is CCK dependent. Our behavioral experiments showed that CCK infusion in the bilateral auditory cortices significantly increased the frequency discrimination ability by facilitating salubrious plastic changes induced by the passive tone exposure in adult animals. Our current study proposed a potential method to trigger thalamocortical plasticity in the adult brain. CCK induced plasticity may provide a possible treatment plan which can be applied to enhance the function of late cochlear implants in prelingually deaf children. We are developing CCKBR agonists for the purpose (Zhang et al., 2019). Our findings could be generalized in different sensory modalities, including, but not limited to perception, learning, and memory formation (Su et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2019).

11101215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11101215.value: Thalamocortical plasticity in the adult brain has been reported to be induced by reversing the critical periods of the sensory cortices in different ways. Zhou and colleagues reported that exposing juvenile or adult rats to a moderate level of noise exposure could reinstate the high susceptibility of the tonotopic map in the ACx. In a recent study, Blundon and colleagues demonstrated that thalamocortical plasticity could be restored by restricting thalamic adenosine signaling. In parallel, our current study proposed another potential method to trigger thalamocortical plasticity in the adult brain. CCK induced plasticity may provide a possible treatment plan which can be applied to enhance the function of late cochlear implants in prelingually deaf children. It is now known that thalamocortical plasticity not only participates in the refinement of the sensory cortices but also learning processes. Thus, our findings may be generalized in different sensory modalities, including, but not limited to perception, learning, and memory formation.

11101215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11101215.value: Here, we investigated whether and how thalamocortical plasticity is modulated by cholecystokinin (CCK). We found that thalamocortical neurons expressed CCK. High-frequency stimulation of the medial geniculate body (MGB) induced thalamocortical long-term potentiation (LTP) in wildtype mice, but not in CCK-/- mice. A CCK-B receptor antagonist completely blocked LTP. CCK injection in the auditory cortex of the aged rats partially restored this LTP, together with a significant improvement in frequency discrimination, implying a potential therapeutic intervention for neurological deficits related to thalamocortical neuroplasticity.

11101315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101315.value: In the animal and human, available evidences indicated that activation of vagal afferents plays a role in the behavioral control learning and memory storage. Clinical evidence has shown that patients with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) who seek treatment have psychiatric comorbidity, usually suffer from memory deficiency. Dysfunction of vagal nerve has reported in IBS patients. Until now there has been no experimental animal model to study visceral pain related cognitive deficits, and little is known about the underlying mechanisms. Cholecystokinin-octapeptide, which is a gastrointestinal hormone released during feeding, has been shown to enhance memory retention. Our series of published observations have shown CCK acting on vagal afferent fibers mediates various physiological functions. Our recent ongoing studies have clearly shown the impairments of the spatial and working memory in viscerally hypersensitive (VH) rat model. We hypothesize that CCK acting via vagal afferent facilities learning and memory process in normal subjects. Further, exogenous or endogenous released CCK enables to rescue memory deficits associated with chronic visceral pain. To test these hypotheses vagal afferent neural responses to CCK-8 will be examined by electrophysiological recorded single-neuronal firings in the nodose ganglia following neurobiotin labeling and double staining to characterize the neurochemical coding. Various behavioral experiments will be performed to establish a visceral pain animal model with cognitive deficits. The effects of CCK on rescuing learning and memory impairment will be examined. The physiological implications will be further strengthened by the similar effects observed in the rats with gastric infusion of peptone, which has been shown to induce increases in plasma CCK levels. Oscillatory of local field potential (LFP), coherent of LFP and neural spikes activity are increasingly recognized as a fundamental hallmark of cortical integrative functions. Given the fact that our ongoing project (GRF11100914) showed for the first time that block of LTP, suppresses phase-locking of anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) neurons and desynchronization between medial thalamus (MT)-ACC pathway in VH rats, in the last phase of our experiment, we will perform multi-electrophysiological recording to clarify that the CCK enables to restore the reduced coherences, and repair theta-phase-locking of ACC neurons and further maintain the synchrony in MT-ACC pathway in VH rats. These results reinforce the view that gut-brain axis plays an important role in modulating learning and memory, and may help the design of experimental approaches aimed at exploiting synaptic reinforcement as a means for ameliorating the impact of visceral pain on learning and memory dysfunction.

11101315.label: Major findings and research outcome
11101315.value: In addition to described in section of 5.3 Realisation of objectives, we have demonstrated that Cholecystokinin enhances visceral pain-related affective memory Pain contains both sensory and affective dimensions. Using a rodent visceral pain assay that combines the colorectal distension (CRD) model with the conditioned place avoidance (CPA) paradigms, we measured a learned behavior that directly reflects the affective memory component of visceral pain, and showed that perigenual anterior cingulate cortex (pACC) activation is critical for memory processing involved in long-term visceral affective state and prediction of aversive stimuli by contextual cue. Mice access to food immediately after training session enhanced memory retention. It has been well demonstrated that CCK acting on vagal afferent fibers mediates various physiological functions. We showed that CCK activation of vagal afferent enhances visceral pain-related affective memory. We showed that infusion of CCK-8 at physiological concentration combining with conditional training significantly increased the CRD-induced CPA scores, and enhanced the pain affective memory retention. In contrast, CCK had no effect on CPA induced by non-nociceptive aversive stimulus (U69,593). The physiological implications were further strengthened by the similar effects observed in the rats with duodenal infusion of 5% peptone, which has been shown to induce increases in plasma CCK levels. CCK-8 receptor antagonist CR-1409 or perivagal application of capsaicin abolished the effect of CCK on aversive visceral pain memory, which was consistent with the notion that vagal afferent modulates affective aspects of visceral pain. CCK does not change the nociceptive response (visceral pain sensitivity) and anterior cingulate cortex neuronal responses to CRD. We conclude that CCK activating vagal afferent C fibers enhances memory consolidation and retention involved in long-term visceral negative affective state. Thus, in a number of gastrointestinal disorders, such as irritable bowel syndrome, nutrient content may contribute to painful visceral perception by enhancing visceral aversive memory via acts on vagal afferent pathway.

11101315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11101315.value: Recently, progress has been made and suggested that activation of vagal afferents plays a role in the behavioral control nociception and memory storage processes. In human patients, electrical vagus nerve stimulation enhanced retention of verbal learning performance. Cholecystokinin-octapeptide (CCK), which is a gastrointestinal hormone released during feeding, has been shown to enhance memory retention. We identify the effects of CCK in the formation, consolidation and retrieval of visceral pain aversion memory in the ACC and other brain regions of rats by using electrophysiological techniques. These results reinforce the view that gut-brain axis plays an important role in modulating learning and memory, and may help the design of experimental approaches aimed at exploiting synaptic reinforcement as a means for ameliorating the impact of visceral pain on learning and memory dysfunction. The data may serve as a basis to develop fundamental notions regarding neurophysiologic biomarkers for therapeutic Vagal Nerve Stimulation in cognitive impairments.

11101315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11101315.value: Clinical evidence has shown that patients with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) suffer from multiple psychiatric disorders, including learning and memory deficits. Visceral hypersensitivity (VH) is common among patients with IBS, who are also reported to have a dysfunctional vagal nerve which plays a role in learning and memory storage. There is a lack of an experimental animal model to study visceral pain related cognitive deficits, and little is known about the underlying mechanisms. Cholecystokinin (CCK), gastrointestinal hormone released during feeding, has been shown to enhance memory retention. Our previous series of published observations have shown that CCK acting on vagal afferent fibers mediated various physiological functions. In the current project, we demonstrate the impairments of spatial and working memory in a VH rat model, and demonstrate that CCK acts via the vagal afferent nerve to facilitate learning and memory in normal rats. Exogenous administration of CCK rescues learning and memory deficits, and restores brain circuit desynchrony associated with chronic visceral pain. Our findings reinforce the view that the brain-gut axis plays a vital role in modulating learning and memory, and facilitate the identification of potential therapeutic targets in the brain-gut axis for memory impairment in human functional bowel diseases.

11200015.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11200015.value: X-LAMP: 大規模多執行緒程式潜在數據競爭的檢測方法

11200015.label: Project Objectives
11200015.value: To investigate empirically the inherent properties of and challenges in hiding and exposure of latent races from multithreaded programs. To formulate a thread schedule generation scheme for latent race detection. To study and compare effective thread schedule generation with respect to the characteristics of latent races. To develop and implement the X-LAMP framework.
rows: To investigate empirically the inherent properties of and challenges in hiding and exposure of latent races from multithreaded programs.
To formulate a thread schedule generation scheme for latent race detection.

To develop and implement the X-LAMP framework.

11200015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200015.value: Program testing by executing programs over test cases is the most widely practiced approach to exposing problems in these programs, thereby assuring their quality during software development. Programs are increasingly complex and large in scale. More and more programs use the multithreading technology in handling their processing tasks. Many important programs adopt the multithreaded technology. Critical failures of these useful multithreaded programs such as halts and crashes are reported by users from time to time. They show that there are still many hidden issues in these programs even after comprehensive program testing to have tried to expose them. Many of them are originated from the presences of concurrency bugs in these program execution traces. Moreover, the presence of data races in programs often indicate the presences of other concurrency bugs in the same program. A data race in an execution trace means that multiple threads in the trace put pieces of data in the same memory location or get the data from that location, but without any mechanism to coordinate the actions taken by these threads from resulting in conflicting accesses. Detecting latent races, which are races that are still unexposed even after comprehensive testing, are essential in order to improve the quality of these programs further. Static analysis and model checking techniques in analyzing large-scale multithreaded programs are either imprecise or impractical. Dynamic approach to testing is essential to demonstrate the presence of data races instead of merely reporting the potentials of the code to produce them. Nonetheless, the state of the art techniques can only reveal very small amount of latent races. Our experiment also confirms similar points. This project aims at developing a novel X-LAMP framework to support the detection of latent races in large-scale multithreaded programs. X-LAMP addresses the key challenge in interleaving-sensitive issue in precise latent race detection through thread schedule generation. This project will also educate students so that they can effectively contribute to the growth of the software industry after graduation. 程式檢測是工業界用於確保軟件質量的解決方案。根據之前的研究估算，軟體測試基礎設施的改進每年可以節省600億美金的支出。 多執行緒程式在企業級應用、案頭應用、雲端應用和移動平臺的應用中越來越得到廣泛的使用。許多重要的軟體應用，例如FireFox瀏覽器和MySQL資料庫，都是多執行緒程式。對於這樣的程式，一次執行包含多個線程。每個線程包含一序列的程式語句，不同線程的語句會相互交錯執行。多個線程為了使用共亯的資源，例如一個共亯的記憶體位置，其中一個線程可能會首先請求並獲取一個共亯資源的鎖，在使用該共亯資源的過程中持有這個鎖，直到不再需要該資源的時候釋放這個鎖。 開發高品質的多執行緒程式對開發人員提出了新的挑戰。因為程式師一般習慣於線性地理解程式碼，然而由於多執行緒程式中線程的交錯這種理解會產生誤區。由於越來越多的軟件程式採用這種主流的並行程式設計管道編寫，解决多執行緒程式種的並行錯誤問題將會花費越來越多的軟體發展預算。如果軟體產品中存在這樣的並行錯誤，開發該產品的公司將在市場競爭中處於不利的地位。數據競爭是一種基本的並行錯誤。如果兩個線程並行地訪問同一個記憶體位置並且其中一個進行寫操作，那麼數據競爭就會出現。多執行緒程式中數據競爭的出現經常意味著該程式中同時存在其他的並行錯誤。許多測試技術可以準確地從程式的執行軌跡中檢測出數據競爭。在工業界的開發專案中，這些科技被廣泛地使用。 有一些數據競爭非常難以被檢測到，我們稱之為潜在數據競爭。現有的軟體測試基礎設施可能會漏檢潜在數據競爭。然而，程式的終端用戶有可能觸發這些潜在數據競爭，並遭遇嚴重的軟件失效，如程式崩潰。許多多執行緒程式的錯誤庫中包含終端用戶提交的錯誤報告。其中有一部分報告的軟件失效可以被追跡到是由程式中的數據競爭導致。 程式執行軌跡中的數據競爭意味著多個線程對同一個記憶體空間寫入或讀取數據，然而並無任何機制協調這些操作，從而導致訪問衝突。潜在數據競爭即使在系統的測試之後仍難以發現。它們的檢測對於進一步提高程式質量十分重要。 對於大規模多執行緒程式，靜態分析和模型檢測科技或者產生不準確的結果或者無法實現。對於證實數據競爭的存在而非僅僅報告可能產生數據競爭的程式碼，動態方法非常必要。然而，現時最先進的科技只能發現少量的潜在數據競爭。我們的實驗也驗證了類似的觀點。 本項目致力於開發一個新穎的架構來支持大規模多執行緒程式中潜在數據競爭的檢測。準確的潜在數據競爭檢測存在對線程交錯敏感的問題，本項目通過線程調度來解决這一關鍵挑戰。這個項目同時也可以教育學生，從而使他們在畢業後能够更好地貢獻於軟件產業的發展。

11200015.label: Realisation of objectives
11200015.value: The first objective is to investigate empirically the inherent properties of and challenges in hiding and exposure of latent races in multithreaded programs. To realize the objective, we collected the source code of representative multithreaded programs, including the PARSEC 3.0 benchmark suite, SPLASH-2 suite as well as MySQL and derby database engines, Apache and Jigsaw web servers, PBZip file compressor, Aget FTP client, Eclipse Integrated Development Environment, and Apache Xalan XSLT processor. They were real-world and widely-used programs and covered a wide range of application domains from high performance computing, network application, financial analysis, computer vision, enterprise storage, animation, similarity search, rendering, data mining, multimedia processing, server applications, database engine, and client applications. We either used the test cases associated with the programs or used the test cases that their bug repositories show these test cases able to reveal data races from the corresponding programs. We mainly used two methodologies in achieving this objective. The first methodology was a typical one used in testing multithreaded programs. For each program, we ran the program over each test case multiple times. To analyze the situations of data races, we implemented three kinds of data race detectors, including happens-before-based detector, lockset-based detector, and lockset-and-happens-before-based detector, which detected data races in different scopes of visibility, detection precision, memory overheads and runtime overheads. We applied these detectors to each such applicable program execution and collected their sets of reported data races as well as runtime performances. We then checked whether a particular reported data race was more difficult to be detected by a particular kind of detector or how different detectors compare among them. We also examined the source code of these data races to find out from the code viewpoint on why a data race was more challenging to be detected. The second methodology was an original proposal of this project. For each program, we transformed the program using different code optimization strategies and executed these transformed programs over the same test case. We then checked whether a particular reported data race was more difficult to be detected. In this way, we empirically answered whether a data race to be challenging to be detected in one transformation context may become easier to be detected in another transformation context. We have then designed a new scheme to allocate testing resources to maximize the expected number of data races to be reported. The second objective is to formulate a thread schedule generation scheme for latent race detection. To realize and achieve this objective, we studied how different program execution characteristics (such as lock patterns enclosing share memory accesses on memory locations) may adversely affect the analysis accuracy and runtime performance of race detectors. We then designed new thread generation schemes to address the challenges. For online detectors, we found that a key challenge was due to not keeping historic events (e.g., shared memory access performed by a thread) as it was not practical to keep all possible historic events before the execution ends. We designed a new scheme, known as HistLock, to keep a small number of historic events per block sharing the same timestamp of each thread in a trace. We also analyzed the situation in a theoretical manner, and proved that some of such events were not necessary to be kept and the online detection of a major kind of races (called lockset violation) can still be sound and complete. Based on the theoretical results, we accordingly designed a new and efficient race detection scheme, known as HistLock+, to detect this kind of races in a sound and complete manner. There was another major kind of races called happens-before races. We attempted to analyze it offline through parallel computing since the difficulty in identifying latent races are those hidden deeply behind the happens-before relations in the trace. We formulated a scheme to firstly divide the execution of each thread into consecutive blocks of events (memory locations of these events precisely) sharing the same happens-before vector-clock in the profiled trace followed by computing whether two such blocks of events from different threads can be run in parallel. We designed a novel schedule to find common memory locations in the interaction of each selected pair of blocks where such common memory locations were happens-before races, which unlike existing happens-before detectors, it does not rely on “joint operations” between the vector clocks of events at the memory location events. In this way, all happens-before races hidden in a trace can be detected via our new scheme called BlockRace. We also formulated a new scheme to capture the happens-before orders of events in a trace (with detected races) and a new scheme to replay that orders to re-produce a trace equivalent to the captured trace fron the happens-before order’s perspective. A key challenge is to reduce the amount of inter-thread dependencies to be captured and make the replayer to depend on fewer inter-thread dependencies so as to reduce perturbation to the original program execution (when running natively) and reduce the record log size. We studied whether different dependencies may be shared and represented by the same dependency and explore the possibility of sharing the timestamp among consecutive reads before the next write on each thread, which leads to the formulation of AggrePlay. In SDA-Cloud, we have also transformed a program through the optimizations performed by compilers and develop a partition-oriented strategy to allocate test runs among virtual machines each hosting the binaries of a compiled program with a race detector. By doing so, we can leverage the power of program transformation to detect races difficult in one transformation context but easy in another transformation context. The third and four objectives are to study and compare effective thread schedule generations with respect to the characteristics of latent races and to develop and implement the X-LAMP framework. We compared HistLock, HistLock+, BlockRace and AggrePlay with their respective existing techniques. To achieve it, we implemented our suite of techniques as tools to support the analysis of C/C++ or Java multithreaded programs with latent races. Our tools were developed in C++, Java, and Python languages with the use of both industry-strength and research-oriented dynamic instrumentation frameworks. We used the benchmarks we used to achieve the above-mentioned Objective 1 and comprehensively evaluated our techniques via these tools in terms of detection effectiveness and runtime performance (memory overhead and runtime slowdown). By comparing to the corresponding results of the implementation of prior arts, we can analyze the merits and limitations of our techniques. We have designed a partition-based allocation strategy to assign test runs to programs transformed by different compiler optimization options and implemented an environment called SDA-Cloud to support race detection.

11200015.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200015.value: We have mainly formulated five novel techniques, HistLock [C1], HistLock+ [J5], BlockRace [C21], AggrePlay [C16], and SDA-Cloud [J3]. We have found that keeping slight more historic events can improve the detection of races significantly [C1], yet it suffers from heavier performance overheads. We have further found that using thread epoch and lock release events can infer whether two memory accesses on the same shared memory location from the same thread in between consecutive lock release operations have any lock subset relation without performing expensive lockset comparison so that all but the first event of each kind (with further optimization) in such a segment can be dropped. We have proved that this strategy can guarantee exactly one racy memory access event to be reported on each thread segment separated by lock releases and hard-order thread synchronizations, and it never reports false positive on lockset violation [J5]. Our method was 122% faster and 28% more memory-efficient than the previous state-of-the-art complete hybrid race detector [J5]. We have also found that it is possible to parallelize race detections by decoupling the program order dependency and lock order dependency among threads via a pre-computation of their vector clocks and a novel dependency-aware schedule generation scheme [C21]. By doing so, in our experiment, our method can achieve 1.96x to 5.5x speedups compared to its sequential counterparts [C21]. We have also found that it is possible to condense inter-thread read-write dependencies. Together with write-read and write-write dependencies, they fully capture the full set of data dependencies in a trace, precisely capturing the happens-before orders in a trace. We have shown that if one can record a read count vector clock for each thread on each memory location in a trace recording phase and each thread checks the logged vector clock against the current read count in the replay phase before a write event, it is possible to regenerate the same set of happens-before dependencies of the original trace in a new trace [C16]. We have found that our method can produce smaller record logs, 56% better runtime slowdown during the record phase and 41% higher probability in the replay phase [C16]. We have formulated a model to continually select virtual-machine instances, each hosting a different compiled version of the same program and running a race detector, and have shown that this model can detect different races both in amount and in detection probability [J3].

11200015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200015.value: HistLock+ indicates that the detection of lockset violations may still report some race warnings undetectable by online happens-before race detectors, and yet whether such a warning is a false positive still requires further confirmation. One requirement to confirm such a warning is to reproduce a trace prefix before the corresponding code locations of the warning. AggrePlay has been developed to enable such trace reproduction with a high probability of success. However, to have both a race detector and a trace recorder enable to monitor a program execution, the memory and runtime overheads can be large. They make the analysis of races on some program executions inapplicable. A possible way to address these problems is to allow stepwise-refinement on traces to be analyzed and reproduced. The challenge is to ensure equivalent traces to be reproduced during the refinement process, and yet the state-of-the-art replayer technique (AggrePlay) has only reached 86% in reproduction probability. Further researches are needed to increase the AggrePlay’s success rate and to lower the overhead of HistLock+. We should study how to determine two traces being equivalent when some events are non-observable in the refinement process, what these events are, and when they are profiled.

11200015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200015.value: A data race is a condition when two conflicting program instructions performed by different components of a multithreaded program can be run in parallel. If these conflicting program instructions could not be run in parallel in a program execution due to the internal design of the program, even if the program instructions are racy, the race could not be triggered and thus detected. Latent races are these bugs in multithreaded programs in use that are not yet discovered, albeit heavy testing has been performed. These races have caused severe problems in daily life. Identifying them is a crucial step in eliminating their potential threats on their uses and misuses. In this project, we tackle the problem of finding such races through running programs with monitors. We has developed a series of race detectors and an execution replayer. These race detectors can find races with high probability, high precision and low performance overheads, and the replayer can reproduce racy program executions with high probability. They can detect races difficult to be found by prior online happens-before detectors, thereby providing more timely feedbacks to application developers to re-examine racy program executions and fix race bugs before they are exploited.

11200115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200115.value: Soils and rocks are natural geo-materials, whose properties are affected by many spatially-varying factors during the geological process, such as the properties of their parent materials, weathering and erosion processes, transportation agents, and sedimentation conditions. In-situ geotechnical properties therefore vary spatially and such variability is site-specific/project-specific in nature. During geotechnical site investigation, however, only a small portion of geo-materials is examined. The amount of geotechnical data is generally too sparse to sufficiently characterize geotechnical variability of the site. This can lead to a difficult situation commonly referred to as “unexpected site condition” in Hong Kong. Unexpected site condition often causes both significant project delays and additional project costs. For example, in 2014, construction of the high-speed railway that connects Hong Kong and mainland China and has a budget of HK$62.4 billion suffered from at least a two-year project delay and required an additional several billion HK$. Unexpected site condition has been listed as a main reason for the delay and over-budget problems. This project aims to develop methodology and computer software to quantify site-specific geotechnical variability. The proposed method will integrate sparse project-specific test data with pre-existing site knowledge (e.g., geological information, geotechnical property statistics, and local engineering experience available prior to the project) under a Bayesian framework to provide updated knowledge of geotechnical properties. It will express the updated knowledge numerically and quantify their variability through Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulation. The major research components include (1) theoretical development of the MCMC-based Bayesian method, (2) calibration of the developed method by field data and observations, and (3) development of computer software for the developed method. Supported by a donation for research project from industry, some preliminary studies were performed and showed promising results. This project will effectively solve the problem of how to quantify site-specific geotechnical variability and obtain meaningful statistics of geotechnical properties from sparse project-specific test data. It will offer computer software to facilitate such quantification in engineering practices. The research outcome will be beneficial to not only Hong Kong but also many other countries where probability-based design codes (e.g., Eurocodes or Load and Resistance Factor Design codes) have been implemented or probabilistic analyses are performed in geotechnical engineering (e.g., quantitative risk assessments of geohazards such as landslides and earthquakes), because quantification of site-specific geotechnical variability is a prerequisite for the implementation of these design codes or probabilistic analyses. 岩土體是經過復雜地質作用而形成的天然材料。受復雜地質成因的影響，岩土體工程性質隨著空間位置的變化而不同。然而，岩土勘察中所獲取的勘察資料通常是相對有限的，並沒有在不同的空間位置上大量地重復測量。這種地質勘察資料的不足會導致所謂的〝不可預見的地質條件〞的困境。2014年香港高鐵工程項目的超支延誤的一個重要原因就是不可預見的地質條件。本項目將建立一套完整的貝葉斯理論方法，應用馬爾科夫蒙地卡洛法，系統地、充分地利用有限的勘察資料（包括先驗信息和有限的測量數據），合理地考慮岩土工程勘察中的各種不確定性因素的影響，科學地量化具體工程場地岩土體工程性質的空間變異性，完善勘察資料的分析理論。此外，本項目將根據所創新的算法，開發應用軟件包，為工程應用直接提供所需的岩土體工程性質參數信息。隨著本項目的開展，如何從有限的測量數據量化具體場地的空間變異性及合理地估計岩土工程參數的統計值這一難題將會得以合理解決。

11200115.label: Realisation of objectives
11200115.value: All project objectives have been successfully achieved. A Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)-based Bayesian framework has been developed in the project for a realistic representation of geotechnical property characterization problems. To facilitate development of the framework, the procedure of geotechnical site characterization was revisited from a Bayesian perspective, and the occurrence and propagation of inherent spatial variability, statistical uncertainty, measurement errors, and transformation uncertainty during characterization of a project site were mapped explicitly to different stages in site investigation (Wang, Cao, and Li, 2016). Based on the mapping, a robust framework is developed that streamlines the formulation of likelihood functions for various soil and rock properties when estimated using different field or laboratory tests, leading to a streamlined process for applications of the proposed Bayesian framework to different site characterization problems. The MCMC-based Bayesian framework has been applied to various soil and rock properties, including effective friction angle of soil from standard penetration tests (SPT) (Wang, Zhao, and Cao, 2015), cross-correlation between effective cohesion and friction angle of soil (Wang and Akeju, 2016), shear modulus reduction curve in soil dynamics (Akeju, Senetakis, and Wang, 2019), liquefiable soil thickness in geotechnical earthquake engineering (Wang, Fu, and Huang, 2017), uniaxial compressive strength and Young’s modulus of rock (Wang and Aladejare, 2016a), and geological strength index (Wang and Aladejare, 2016b). Real site-specific data (e.g., SPT-N values) were used in all applications, and the results obtained from the proposed methods have been validated against geotechnical properties (e.g., soil effective friction angle) directly measured at the same site. The MCMC-based Bayesian methods have been shown to perform well. In addition, a Bayesian sequential updating method was developed to make full use of multiple-sources information in geotechnical practice. The Bayesian sequential updating method has been applied to undrained shear strength of soil (Cao, Wang, and Li, 2016b) and rock mass deformation modulus (Aladejare and Wang, 2019). A Bayesian method was also developed to quantify the unknown transformation uncertainty in empirical design chars that are commonly used in geotechnical engineering (Wang and Zhao, 2017). One key element of the MCMC-based Bayesian methods is prior knowledge. In geotechnical engineering practice, characterization of a project site often starts with desk-study and site reconnaissance, which provide site information available prior to the project (e.g., existing data in literature, engineering experience, and engineers' expertise). Such information can be used as “prior knowledge” under a Bayesian framework and be quantitatively reflected by a prior distribution in Bayesian methods. Two different methods have been developed to quantify prior knowledge during geotechnical characterization of a project site (Cao, Wang, and Li, 2016a). Where there is no prevailing prior knowledge on the site, a non-informative prior distribution (e.g., uniform prior distribution) is used to reflect quantitatively the engineering common sense and judgment. As prior knowledge improves and becomes much more informative, a subjective probability assessment framework (SPAF) was developed to estimate the prior distribution from prior knowledge. The proposed SPAF framework assists geotechnical engineers in formulating and expressing their engineering judgments in a quantifiable and transparent manner. The proposed methods have been tested using real information from a sand site of the US National Geotechnical Experimentation Sites (NGES) at Texas A&M University (Cao, Wang, and Li, 2016a). In addition, a comprehensive literature review has been conducted to develop a geotechnical property statistics database for various soil and rock properties (Cao, Wang, and Li, 2016a; Aladejare and Wang, 2017). The statistics database can be used as a starting point for quantifying prior distribution. To remove the mathematical hurdles of the MCMC-based Bayesian method for practicing engineers and facilitate its application by geotechnical practitioners, A user-friendly and flexible Excel VBA program, called Bayesian Equivalent Sample Toolkit (BEST), has been developed (Wang, Akeju, and Cao, 2016). The BEST VBA program can be free downloaded from https://sites.google.com/site/yuwangcityu/best/1, and it has been used by engineers and researchers from various countries, such as USA, Spain, Australia, and China. The BEST program offers a user-friendly toolkit for obtaining reasonable statistics and probability distributions of geotechnical properties from limited observation data. It probabilistically integrates the prior knowledge with observation data and uses the MCMC simulation to transform the integrated knowledge into a large number of equivalent samples. Although a thorough understanding of the Bayesian formulations and the MCMC simulation algorithm is always advantageous, such understanding is not a prerequisite for geotechnical practitioners to use BEST. In addition, the BEST program not only incorporates 12 pairs of design and measured properties in the built-in models for direct application of the Bayesian method, but also provides a user-defined model that allows users to define their own design and measure properties as far as the necessary transformation model can be specified by the users. To facilitate application of the developed method in reliability analysis or design in geotechnical engineering, step-by-step illustrative examples, starting from site-specific geotechnical property characterization, have been developed for reliability analysis of rock slopes (Aladejare and Wang, 2018) and probability-based design of retaining wall (Wang et al., 2016).
