11200115.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200115.value: In geotechnical engineering practice, the lack of adequate information or site-specific test data is often mitigated by so-called engineering judgment and local experience of geo-materials. This typically involves a review of the geotechnical information that exists prior to the undergoing project and interpretation and synthesis of the pre-existing information in an ambiguous and unquantifiable manner. This project developed an MCMC-based Bayesian method and computer software for integrating sparse site-specific test data with pre-existing knowledge about the sites and effectively expressing the combined information using MCMC simulation in a rational, transparent, and quantitative manner. The proposed method takes advantage of today’s rapidly developing computing technology and commonly available computers, and it relies on MCMC numerical simulations to quantify the geotechnical variability through a collection of MCMC samples. This simulation-based approach effectively removes the constraints of mathematical complexity in the formulation and allows general geotechnical property characterization problems to be represented realistically and properly under the Bayesian framework. The proposed method has been further developed as computer software for facilitating its applications by geotechnical practitioners in engineering practice. The developed method and software effectively solve the problem of how to obtain meaningful statistics of geotechnical properties from sparse project-specific test data. As summarized in Part C, this project has led to 16 papers published in highly reputable international journals, one invited book chapters, and five international conference papers and presentations in USA, Singapore, Korea, and China, respectively. Three PhD students have been trained under this project and successfully graduated.

11200115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200115.value: In this project, a geotechnical property is modelled as a random variable, without explicit consideration of spatial coordinate. To model the spatial variability explicitly, the spatial coordinate should be modeled directly, and the spatial variation of a geotechnical property shall be modelled as a random field, i.e., a collection of a series of geo-ordinated and spatially correlated random variables. However, the model complexity in random field increases dramatically, and it poses great challenges on properly estimating the random field parameters and developing the random field models from usually sparse test data at a specific project site. A new sampling paradigm called compressive sensing/sampling has potential to deal with this challenge.

11200115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200115.value: Soils and rocks are natural geo-materials, whose properties are affected by many spatially-varying factors during the geological process. In-situ geotechnical properties therefore vary spatially, and such variability is site-specific/project-specific in nature. During geotechnical site investigation, however, only a small portion of geo-materials is examined. The amount of geotechnical data is generally too sparse to sufficiently characterize geotechnical variability of the site. This can lead to a difficult situation commonly referred to as “unexpected site condition” in Hong Kong. Unexpected site condition often causes both significant project delays and additional project costs. This project developed Bayesian method and computer software to quantify site-specific geotechnical variability. The method integrates sparse project-specific test data with pre-existing site knowledge under a Bayesian framework and transforms the integrated knowledge into a large number of equivalent samples by Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulation. It effectively solves the problem of how to obtain meaningful statistics of geotechnical properties from sparse project-specific test data. The research outcome is beneficial to not only Hong Kong but also many other countries where probability-based analysis methods have been implemented, because quantification of site-specific geotechnical variability is a prerequisite for probabilistic analyses.

11200315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200315.value: 這個研究項目，是要藉發展由固體氧化物燃料電池所驅動的微型冷電聯產系統 (SOFC-mCCP)，為濕熱氣候下樓房提供更有能源效益的空調和電力裝置。該系統設計主要包括SOFC發電組件、變頻壓縮式空調機 (AC)、固體除濕冷卻機 (SDCU)、以及中央監控部件。SOFC生產的電力會滿足樓房的基本電器需求，亦會驅動AC去處理圍護傳遞和内部的熱源。為了令室內空氣質素滿意，從SOFC竭取的廢熱會驅動SDCU，用作供應和處理所需的鮮風量。要令廢熱回收和應用更有效，熱儲能設計亦會考慮其中。由於SOFC-mCCP的系統元件較多，合適的控制法則十分重要，使系統中的SOFC、AC和SDCU能有效調配和操作。從可持續發展的角度，SOFC-mCCP為濕熱氣候城市帶來能源效益和減少碳排放的優點。

11200315.label: Realisation of objectives
11200315.value: This research project is to develop a micro combined cooling and power system driven by solid oxide fuel cells (SOFC-mCCP) for premises in hot and humid climate. In the course of development, the associated distributed multi-energy resources were also involved, like combined cooling and power (CCP), CHP (combined heat and power, or called cogeneration) and CCHP (combined cooling, heating and power, or called trigeneration). All the project objectives have been fully achieved, and realization of the objectives is reported as follows: Objective 1 – Dynamic simulation models of system and control components of SOFC-mCCP system A new two-dimensional (2D) dynamic model was developed in Fortran to study the mass and energy transport, the velocity field and the electrochemical phenomena of high-temperature SOFC. The key feature of this model was that gas properties, reaction heat, open circuit voltage, ohmic voltage and exchange current density were temperature-dependent. Based on this, the change of gas temperature and related characteristics could be evaluated. In this 2D dynamic SOFC model, chemical and electrochemical reaction, flow field, mass and energy transfer models were coupled in order to determine the current density, the mass fraction and the temperature of gas species. Since SOFC is a high-temperature prime mover with high electrical efficiency, its efficiency can be further boosted up with bottoming cycle like gas turbine, Stirling engine and organic Rankine cycle. As such, system models with various bottoming cycles were therefore developed, and their part-load performances were investigated. The effects of fuel inlet temperature and current density of fuel cell stack; compression ratio of gas turbine; Stirling engine type; working fluid of organic Rankine cycle; and fuel cell stack part-load ratio were explored. It was found that the CCP system with bottoming cycles of gas turbine and Stirling engine would have higher boost of electrical efficiency. Gas turbine bottoming cycle is recommended when building energy demands are relatively constant, while Stirling engine bottoming cycle is suggested for variable energy demands. The entire SOFC-mCCP system model, which would provide high-grade heat to energize desiccant cooling during electrical power generation, was developed using TRNSYS. For system appraisal in hot-humid climate, its performance in a 24-hour restaurant was analyzed. It was found that by performing year-round dynamic simulations, a 10% reduction in the total electricity demand could be achieved in the tropical Singaporean climate compared to a 5% reduction in demand in the sub-tropical Hong Kong climate. This reflected the effect of different seasons on the performance of the SOFC-mCCP system. In addition, at most 24% and 38% reductions in the primary energy consumption and carbon dioxide emissions for both regions could be achieved. Objective 2 – Design and operation parameters of SOFC-mCCP system for different types of premises under hot and humid climate The transient performances of SOFC unit during the heat-up and start-up phases were evaluated, and the effects of operating parameters (i.e. fuel/air inlet temperature, fuel/air inlet pressure, inlet fuel composition) were also assessed. The effect of various geometric parameters of hydrogen- and methane-fed SOFC units was investigated, including anode thickness, electrolyte thickness, cathode thickness, electrode porosity and electrode tortuosity. The results have indicated that smaller anode thickness, electrolyte thickness, electrode porosity and electrode tortuosity would provide better cell performance in power generation. But the effect of cathode thickness was not obvious. These results provide useful insights in SOFC design and production. For the desiccant wheel involved in SOFC-mCCP, one of the essential design and operation parameters is the adsorbent type. As such, the performances of the desiccant wheels using RD silica gel (SG), AQSOA-Z02 and CECA-3A were compared. The variation of the absorbent condition through the entire cyclic humidification/dehumidification process was evaluated in order to review the role of adsorption isotherms. With the ambient humidity ratio of 16.04 g/kg, the desiccant wheel using SG, AQSOA-Z02 and CECA-3A would decrease the humidity ratio of the process air by 33.0%, 22.6% and 18.7% respectively at the regeneration temperature of 50 degC; while further by 65.2%, 64.5% and 51.1% respectively at 90 degC. Although AQSOA-Z02 was presented to have higher dehumidification capability from the adsorption isotherms, it was found that the desiccant wheel using SG would generally have better performances due to its lower heat of adsorption. New perspectives of desiccant wheel designed for desiccant cooling have been derived, which are helpful to achieve an energy-efficient design in the SOFC-mCCP system. Under the circumstances of handling the ventilation load in the hot and humid regions, it was found that desiccant cooling provided tangible cooling capacity both with and without the regeneration heat. In the presence of regeneration heat, the desiccant wheel should be operated at a low speed, with a sensible heat exchanger and a regenerative air evaporative cooler. The coefficient of performance was found decreased with the regeneration temperature in such scenario. It was also identified that the regeneration temperature should be higher than 60 degC, otherwise the desiccant wheel would function even worse than that without regeneration heat. Objective 3 – Robust operation strategy and control algorithm of SOFC-mCCP system Initially, a control strategy was developed for year-round system operation in response to the changing climatic and loading conditions of building premises. Through a CCP system using SOFC with bottoming cycle of gas turbine (GT), the capacity ratio of cells in operation; the ratio of exhaust heat delivered to GT; and the ratio of cooling load shared between cooling devices were chosen as the decision variables in the control strategy. In order to minimize the system energy consumption, particle swarm optimization (PSO) was constructed in MATLAB and coupled with TRNSYS for control optimization. It was found that with the proposed control strategy, the yearly energy saving of the SOFC-GT CCP system would be 6.89% compared to the reference case. The distributed multi-energy resource would feature with high electrical efficiency, but contain the highly coupled equipment units for cooling, heating and electricity supplies. Due to such complex nature of multiple supplies and demands, a new approach, called multi-supply-multi-demand (MSMD) control strategy, was proposed. The MSMD control includes two core algorithms: rolling optimization (RO) and feedback correction (FC). In the SOFC-GT CCHP system with energy storages for building application, it was found that RO could determine the operating schedules of the related equipment units at lower primary energy consumption than the conventional mean, while FC could effectively rectify the prediction errors incurred from the real-time loading conditions. Owing to the complex nature of multiple energy supplies and multiple building demands, an integrated demand and supply side management (IDSSM) strategy was further proposed. The IDSSM strategy included three core algorithms: demand side rolling optimization, supply side rolling optimization and feedback correction. Demand and supply side rolling optimizations were simultaneously implemented to determine the schedulable appliances and operating capacities of energy supply equipment units over the next 24-h planning horizon. The IDSSM strategy was evaluated in a CCHP system primed with SOFC-GT which served an apartment building with electric cars. It was found that the primary energy consumption, the design capacity of the prime mover and the capacity of electricity storage would be decreased by 8.75%, 10% and 43% respectively through the IDSSM strategy.

11200315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200315.value: This research project has laid down fruitful ground works to put forward system realization of SOFC-mCCP. It is planned to collaborate with a SOFC manufacturer, which can provide comprehensive operating data of SOFC during heat-up, start-up, step-up and step-down. In addition, the performance data of SOFC (primarily the current density, the electrical efficiency and the overall efficiency) in different operating conditions can be acquired. These sets of field data are useful to further verify the component and system models of SOFC-mCCP, hence an integrated design can be more practically figured out. A novel solution of extracting the high-grade waste heat from SOFC will be explored, so that the cooling and power performances of the SOFC-mCCP can be maximized for different types of premises. Once a SOFC manufacturer, as well as a desiccant wheel supplier, can be lined up, application of funding (like Innovation and Technology Fund) will be proceeded in order to advance the SOFC-mCCP system in the context of commercialization.

11200315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200315.value: In this research project, energy and environmental feasibility of the SOFC-mCCP system, as well as the associated distributed multi-energy resources, is assured for building application in hot and humid climate. The proposd system is driven by the high-temperature SOFC and provides simultaneous cooling and electrical power. Here, desiccant wheel is designed for desiccant cooling. The project started from dynamic modeling of the key system components, including the SOFC; the associated bottoming cycles; the desiccant wheel; and the entire SOFC-mCCP system. The design and operation parameters of various system components, such as those of SOFC; the part-load performances of SOFC with different bottoming cycles; the adsorbent type on desiccant wheel; and the operating conditions of desiccant cooling, were fully appraised. Performance evaluation has been made in different types of premises under hot and humid climate, including office building, hotel building, apartment building, residential building, sports center and 24-hour restaurant. Robust control strategy for distributed multi-energy resources has been gradually evolved, from the one through performance optimization, then the multi-supply-multi-demand control strategy, finally to the integrated demand and supply side management strategy. The research outcomes have fully demonstrated the SOFC-mCCP system to be a promising sustainable solution in distributed multi-energy resource.

11200415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200415.value: Multi-agent systems seek to coordinate multiple agents or subsystems to achieve a collective goal based on local, distributed information, of which notable examples are sensor networks, formation control, flocking, distributed computation, etc. Many of such tasks can be formulated as one of achieving consensus among agents: a set of agents are to reach a common state via local distributed control executed over a communication network. This project launches an in-depth study of robustness issues of multi-agent systems, an area of pressing needs in the research of multi-agent systems. We identify the transmission delay of information exchange between the agents and the network topology governing their interactions as two overriding concerns in achieving robust consensus, which require novel understanding and where we believe significant advances can be made. Our primary goal is to investigate how multi-agent systems may or may not achieve consensus robustly in the presence of uncertain, time-varying, and random noises and perturbations in the network topology and in the transmission delays. Drawing upon advances in robust control and networked control theories, we advocate an integrated robust and networked control approach, which seeks to first cast the consensus robustness problem into one of robust stabilization and next solve it based on analytic interpolation and optimal control theories, leading ultimately to numerically efficient algorithms in the form of linear matrix inequality (LMI) optimization solutions and in some cases, analytical results. Our preliminary studies and ongoing work show that this approach is highly feasible and may potentially deliver results of significance, answering to the key challenges in the present theory and future applications of multi-agent systems. 多智能體系統旨在通過局部、分布式信息的交換，協調多個自主 體或子系統，以求達到共同的全局目的。其顯著的應用範例包括 傳感器網絡、編隊、集群、分布式計算等。諸如此類的問題俱可 抽象成多智能體系統的一致性問題，即一組自主體通過通訊網絡 進行局部的分布式控制，達致同一狀態。本項目擬深度研究日呈 緊迫的多智能體系統中的魯棒性問題。我們認為，多智能體系統 中信息傳遞延遲與網絡拓撲的交互作用對系統的魯棒性有突出的 影響，該問題需要新的理解，並可引致重要的發現。基於此，本 項目的一個主要內容就是探索在具信息延遲且網絡拓撲受到不確 定、時變及隨機噪聲和擾動的情況下，系統是否仍能達致一致。 我們提出一個以魯棒控制和網絡化控制理論為基礎的方法，利用 魯棒控制和網絡化控制理論中成熟有效的工具。具體的路線圖為 ：我們首先將魯棒一致性問題轉換成一個魯棒鎮定問題。其次， 我們采用可析函數插值方法和最優控制的理論工具求解該問題， 冀最終通過線性矩陣不等式的數字求解算法解決魯棒一致性問 題。在一些特殊情況下，亦可能獲得解析解。我們現有的研究成 果顯示，該方法及路線具相當可行性，極可能導出重要成果，從 而對解決目前多智能體系統的理論及其未來應用中的關鍵挑戰， 提供參考。

11200415.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200415.value: 1. Consensus robustness. Under this overarching objective of the project, we have investigated robust consensus problems for networks subject to stochastic and deterministic uncertainties and noises, where unlike in the conventional formulations the network topology is no longer a constant, fixed Laplacian matrix, but instead consists of communication channels with stochastic noises and bounded but unknown modeling errors. Specifically, in the stochastic channel uncertainty formulation we model each communication link between the agents as a noisy communication channel subject to a multiplicative stochastic uncertainty. We derived conditions for robust consensus in the mean square sense. The results show that under a fundamental condition relating the network synchronizability, the unstable agent dynamics, and the channel uncertainty variances, the consensus can be ensured and consensus protocols can be designed based on the state information transmitted over the uncertain channels, by solving a modified algebraic Riccati equation. With deterministic modeling uncertainties in the communication network, we showed that the robust consensus problem can generally be solved by solving a simultaneous H∞ control problem for a set of low-dimensional subsystems. We also derived necessary conditions for the existence of a protocol achieving robust consensus, and sufficient conditions in terms of linear matrix inequalities for design of robust consensus protocols. Furthermore, we obtained bounds on the maximal time delay allowable if such inter-agent communications are subject to time delays. The results are reported in Papers 4, 6, 11. 2. We formulated and solved such performance problems as the optimal energy management problem for multi-agent systems under distributed control. At present, the overwhelming majority, if not all, of the multi-agent consensus algorithms have not addressed performance issues, and our work constitutes perhaps the first investigation into this open, more challenging problem domain. We introduced a network approximation scheme in the energy minimization criterion, which ensures that a distributed optimal consensus algorithm always exists, for any given connected network topology. This distributed algorithm can be constructed by solving a single-agent-level parametric algebraic Ricatti equation. The performance of the optimal consensus algorithm can be determined accordingly, and its robustness against uncertain tome delay was further investigated. The results are reported in Papers 5, 9.

11200415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200415.value: 1. We have expanded our research into bipartite consensus problems (Papers 1, 2, 7). This problem area addresses both collaborative and competitive interactions that coexist among agents, which has a close bearing on social networks, opinion dynamics, and the Google’s famed PageRank search algorithm. We designed state and dynamic output feedback control laws for the agents to achieve bipartite consensus. Distributed control laws are proposed for several classes of graph topologies. Bipartite consensus networks are widely considered to provide a viable model for social and opinion dynamics, and increasingly appear to emerge as a an important interdisciplinary research area. The results obtained in this project will provide a launch basis for the PI's continuing investigation into this promising area. 2. The project has also outgrew to the investigation of security issues of cyber-physical systems (CPS), as reported in Paper 10. CPS are the backbone of the today's technological and social worlds. The information and physical security is essential to the reliable and safe functioning of CPS, which in turn has attracted considerable research interest across scientific and engineering disciplines. The results obtained in this project will enable the PI to launch new initiatives into CPS security research.

11200415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200415.value: Multi-agent systems (MAS) seek to coordinate multiple agents or subsystems to achieve a collective goal based on local, distributed information, of which notable examples are sensor networks, formation control, flocking, distributed computation, etc. Many of such tasks can be formulated as one of achieving consensus among agents: a set of agents are to reach a common state via local distributed control executed over a communication network. MAS are seen as enabling units for large-scale tasks that require coordination over spatially wide areas, and as such are building blocks for cyber-physical systems and the Internet of Things (IoT). This project launches a study of robustness and performance issues of MAS. Our primary goal is to investigate how MAS may or may not achieve consensus robustly in the presence of uncertain, time-varying, and random noises and perturbations in the network topology and in the transmission delays. Among other results, the project led to the discovery of fundamental bounds on the time delay and communication noise variances required for robust consensus, as well as algorithms that can achieve the robust consensus. The energy requirements for robust consensus are also characterized. The results constitute novel, significant advances into the robustness and performance studies of MAS.

11200715.label: Realisation of objectives
11200715.value: In this project, we have performed analysis of the relationship between lung cancer drug response level and atom connectivity dynamics based on trimmed Delaunay triangulation. We related the number of EGFR residues that are close to gefitinib and the corresponding response level for each EGFR mutation. We studied 137 EGFR-mutated NSCLC patients, corresponding to 30 EGFR mutations, and an additional EGFR mutation L858R_T790M. MD simulations were implemented to simulate the motions of EGFR mutant-gefitinib complexes, and a trajectory of 1000 position frames was obtained for each complex. For each position frame, 3D trimmed Delaunay triangulation was applied to construct connections between EGFR residues and gefitinib atoms. Those EGFR residues that connected with any atom of gefitinib were defined to be close to gefitinib. We calculated the average number of EGFR residues close to gefitinib for the 1000 position frames and derived a conclusion that as the number of EGFR residues close to gefitinib increases, the response level of the corresponding EGFR mutation tends to descend, which means patients with the corresponding EGFR mutation are more likely to response well to gefitinib. The findings here can lead us a better understanding of dynamic features of EGFR mutant gefitinib complexes, and establish a useful link between these features and patients’ responses to gefitinib. Our studies provide a useful reference for personalized NSCLC treatment plan. We have proposed an Eigen-binding site based method to analyze the EGFR mutation induced drug resistance. Instead of using all the original features of the drug-binding site, we project these original features to an Eigen-binding site space to obtain new features. Then we built a classification model based on SVM to correlate the new derived features with the response level to gefitinib for NSCLC patients. With a group of EGFR mutants generated by Rosetta, we employed alpha shape modeling to extract the geometric properties of the drug binding site for each mutant. Amber was used to implement MD simulations for a mutant-drug complex, and the binding free energy was calculated using the MM-GBSA protocol. The derived local surface geometric properties of a mutant, coupled with the mutant-drug binding free energy, were used as major features to characterize a mutant. We built an eigen-binding site space using PCA, after which the original features were projected to this space. When the first two or three PCs were considered, the mutants with different response levels were separated. Finally, SVM was employed to build a classification model and to predict whether a mutant responds or not to gefitinib. The best accuracy of the leave- one-out cross-validation mechanism reaches 85.48 percent. As one of our future works, more clinical data will be collected to refine our model. When sufficient patients have the same mutation type, relatively-accurate drug response levels of the corresponding mutants can be obtained. In addition, more features of the drug-binding sites can be extracted to describe each binding site in more detail. These further studies will benefit cancer drug discovery and personalized therapy design. We have analyzed the motion trajectories of the EGFR mutants obtained from MD simulation. The EGFR mutant structures were generated using Rosetta. Amber was employed to carry out MD simulation of the EGFR mutant-drug system. The motion trajectories were collected every 10 ps and a total of 200 frames were obtained for each mutant. Then we computed alpha shape model of each trajectory frame and characterized the curvature of the atoms at the drug binding site using the solid angle. In one aspect, we calculated the average convex degree at the drug binding site of each trajectory frame, and obtained the knob level of a mutant by computing the mean value of the convex degrees of the 200 frames. On the other hand, we calculated the mean of the solid angle value of each atom at the drug binding site from the 200 trajectory frames. In this way, an average drug binding site could be obtained, and the average convex degree of this binding site was calculated to measure the knob level of a mutant. Finally, we analyzed the relationship between the knob level of the drug binding site and the drug response level of the mutants. Results show that 90% of the mutants can be grouped correctly by setting a certain knob level threshold. To validate our model, we can compare the predicted response with the clinically obtained drug response of the EGFR mutants collected from literature. Meanwhile, the newly collected clinical data provide resources to refine our model to make further prediction more accurately. For example, L858R_T790M is a well-known mutant which is resistant to gefitinib. Then we can compute its alpha shape model and derive the knob level of the drug binding pocket in the aforementioned two ways. As the best grouping accuracy is achieved when the solid angle threshold equals to 0.01 for both the two-way situations. We set the threshold to 0.01, and obtained the knob level of 0.5298 and 0.4964 with the two approaches, respectively. According to knob level thresholds of the drug Response mutants and the No-response ones, the mutant of L858R_T790M can be categorized to the No-response group, which is consistent with our knowledge. By using the obtained relationships between knob level and drug response level of the EGFR mutants, we can have a general classification of a new EGFR mutant before measuring the drug response from clinical evaluation. We can model the 3D structure as well as the alpha shape of a new EGFR mutant to derive the knob level of the drug binding pocket. According to the obtained knob level threshold of the drug Response and No-response groups, we are able to predict the drug response of the new mutant. The results can be used for clinical guidance and can benefit the patients with a more effective therapy. We have developed singular value decomposition (SVD) based method to detect the co-clusters in mutant-atom matrix data of solid angle. A set of significant patterns are found in the given matrix data with coherent solid angle values on both mutants and atoms. These patterns could provide clues about the main mechanism associated with drug resistance. In one pattern, all the mutants have the same response level to gefitinib at all atoms, which means that protein mutants with similar surface geometric properties at the key points of the drug binding site show similar responses to drug molecules. Compared with the Cheng and Church method, the SVD based technique is able to detect larger co-clusters. These co-cluster patterns suggest that protein-drug surface characteristics play a very important role in drug resistance levels. The findings provide useful insight to the mechanism of drug resistance and search for more effective drugs.

11200715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200715.value: Analysis of biomolecular interactions is important in biology and medicine. The methods developed in this project can have several useful applications. Our focus in this project is to study EGFR and drug complexes. The 3D alpha shape models can be further developed to analyze many other biomolecular interactions, such as those involving protein-protein, protein-DNA/RNA, and protein-ligand. Drug resistance is a major problem for targeted therapy of many diseases. Our methods can be adopted to assess drug effectiveness for other diseases, for which protein mutations are the root cause. Currently, there is a pandemic of the coronavirus COVID-19. Our group is already employing the methods developed in this project to verify if existing drugs can be used as COVID-19 inhibitors. By analyzing the surface properties of COVID-19, we can determine of a drug can bind to the virus and stop its duplication. We can have already published a number of papers and are awarded a US patent for 3D alpha shape based models for biomolecular modeling. We can further develop the mathematical formulations, improve their accuracy and find many more useful real-world applications.

11200715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200715.value: In this project, we have developed 3D alpha shape models to analyze interface patterns between biomolecules. The mathematical formulation is used to study the properties of a protein called EGFR. The mutations of EGFR can cause non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although several drugs are effective for curing NSCLC initially, almost all patients develop drug resistance after about a year due to one or more additional mutations of EGFR. We employ the 3D alpha shape models to analyze the surface properties of EGFR mutants and why a dug is no longer effective once the surface is changed at the binding site between the EGFR mutant and the drug. Based on the atom positions of an EGFR mutant and a drug at the binding site, their dynamic properties, and the surface curvature of the EGFR mutant, we are able to predict the drug resistance level. In addition, we have analyzed the common properties of many protein-drug complexes and introduced the concept of Eigen-binding site. The eign characteristics can reveal important features for drug resistance analysis. Our studies provide a useful reference to medical doctors for personalized NSCLC treatment planning based on advanced computational and data analysis tools.

11201015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201015.value: With the ever growing data-rate faster than ever, the bandwidth requirement is substantially increasing. However, current wireless technologies deployed in over-crowded microwave spectrum are not capable of handling the growing demand. This issue has aroused considerable interest in the millimeter wave multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. Fundamental theory shows that Multi-Gbps data-rate is possible if the system employs very large phased-array antennas to overcome the orders-of-magnitude high pathloss, while accommodating much wider bandwidth. As the research progressed, however, it was quickly revealed that many challenges have to be addressed, before any of the promised gain could be harnessed. At the forefront of them are questions related to advanced precoder/combiner alignment between the transmitter and receiver in the sparse millimeter wave MIMO channels. The advanced precoding/combining is the key to scale the data-rate promised by the MIMO theory. However, as the sampling frequency at baseband increases substantially for the millimeter wave systems, the promising digital precoding/combining becomes infeasible. Consequently, a large portion of digital precoding burden is offloaded to the analog domain. This transfer undesirably makes the digital baseband unable to process the signal at each antenna. This limitation prevents the system from employing advanced precoding/combining alignment techniques. As a result, the state-of-the-art millimeter wave MIMO systems rely on conventional beam scanning techniques, in which the transmitter and receiver iteratively sounds beams and align the best beam pair from pre-designed codebooks. As the array size increases, the beam scanning performance becomes considerably suboptimal, unless the sounding overhead increases substantially. This limits the potential throughput increase promised by the millimeter wave MIMO systems. Our goal is to tackle the above limitation by investigating new approaches that innovate the precoder/combiner design for the millimeter wave MIMO systems. Our focus is to optimize the precoder/combiner alignment between the transmitter and receiver, which is specialized to the sparse MIMO channels. The novelty of the project mainly lies in introducing fundamental techniques for multimode precoder/combiner alignment that perform power and rank adaptation by leveraging channel reciprocity. Exploiting channel reciprocity makes the system directly estimate the sparse eigenmodes of the channel without estimating the large-scale sparse channel matrix. The adaptation of the devised technique to the millimeter wave MIMO systems will result in an upgraded precoder/combiner alignment that greatly scales the system performance. Such a framework could serve as a reference for developing advanced millimeter wave MIMO systems that could potentially be evolved into the fifth generation wireless standards. 隨著數據速率的急劇增長，通信系統對帶寬的需求大幅度提升。然而，目前部署在過度擁擠的微波頻譜上的無線通信技術已經無法滿足這種快速增長的信息率需求。這一問題的出現引發了人們對毫米波多入多出系統的強烈興趣。 基礎理論表明當通信系統在基於更寬帶寬的情況下應用大量相控陣列天線來克服高數量級的路徑損耗時，數千兆比特每秒的數據傳輸速率將成為可能。但是，隨著研究的進一步開展，實踐表明在得到期望的增益之前尚有許多挑戰性問題亟需解決。其中首要的問題就是相關如何校準稀疏毫米波信道中發射端與接收端之間的先進預編碼器和組合器。先進的預編碼和組合技術正是大幅度提高多入多出系統理論支撐的數據速率的關鍵。然而，隨著毫米波系統在基帶的採樣頻率急劇上升，頗有價值的數字預編碼和組合技術將無法得到應用。因此，大部份數字預編碼將轉移到模擬域上處理，這種轉變將使得數字基帶無法處理每根天線的信號。該種局限性將阻止系統應用先進的預編碼和組合校準技術。為此，現有技術下的毫米波多入多出系統將依靠傳統波束掃描技術，具體來說，該種技術就是發射機和接收機重複探測波束并從預先設計的碼本中選取匹配的最佳波束對。隨著天線陣列維度的增加，該種波束掃描方法的性能將會變得非常次優，除非系統顯著增加訓練開銷成本。從而，該種方法將會限制毫米波多入多出系統所會帶來的潛在的吞吐量的增加。 我們的目標就是要探索創新的毫米波多入多出系統預編碼器和組合器的設計方法來有效解決上述這種局限。我們專注于優化發射端與接收端之間的預編碼器和組合器的校準，而且該種設計方法適應於稀疏毫米波信道。此項目的創新點主要體現在通過利用信道的互易性介紹了有關功率和秩自適應的多模預編碼器和組合器校準的基本技術。通過利用信道互易性，系統可以直接估計稀疏信道的本征模，而不用估計大規模的稀疏矩陣。該項毫米波多入多出系統的發明技術的應用將導致預編碼器和組合器校準方法的升級，從而可以顯著提升系統性能。這種基於改進先進毫米波多入多出系統的框架有很大機會演變成第五代無線通信標準。

11201015.label: Realisation of objectives
11201015.value: Initial research activities were carried out to address Objectives 1 and 2, where we devised efficient multimode precoder/combiner design techniques based on the algebraic Arnoldi approach (Objective 1). In this approach, precoding/combining does not rely on the entire channel matrix, but it rather leverages the sparse subspace of mmWave channels. Straightforward perturbation analysis was conducted to verify strong resilience to the channel aligned noise, especially, when the channel is substantially sparse (Objective 2). These benefits demonstrated as compared to other existing millimeter wave precoder/combiner alignment techniques. We accomplished Objective 3. In this category, the underlying idea is to employ an iterative block-coordinated successive minimization technique to solve the sparse subspace decomposition problem. The devised technique does not guarantee global optimality, but it rather sub-optimally solves the problem. Nevertheless, since it is based on the convex sub-problem formulation, it guarantees the convergence to a stationary point. On the other hand, an alternative strategy for reducing the hardware complexity via the filterbank approach which can result in closed-form solution, was also developed. Their improved performance is evidenced. To achieve Objectives 2-4, we studied a non-adaptive, hence rather simple, open-loop mmWave MIMO channel estimation techniques. We presented a random phase rotation design of channel subspace sampling signals and showed that they obey the restricted isometry property (RIP) with high probability. We then formulated the channel estimation as a low-rank subspace decomposition problem and, based on the RIP, verified that the proposed framework reveals resilience to a low signal-to-noise ratio. The required number of channel uses ensuring a bounded estimation error is linearly proportional to the degrees of freedom of the channel, whereas it converges to a constant value if the number of RF chains can grow proportionally to the channel dimension while keeping the channel rank fixed. The objectives achieved are summarized below.

11201015.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201015.value: To address channel estimation and precoding in hybrid analog-digital millimeter wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, a method based on the Arnoldi iteration was developed by exploiting the channel reciprocity and sparsity of the channel eigenmodes. We also modified it to operate under the constraints dictated by the hybrid analog-digital architecture, and showed via simulations that our approach can result in significant saving in energy and cost compared to conventional methods [8-1]. Moreover, its extension to wideband mmWave MIMO systems was studied [9-1]. On the other hand, by making use of analog delay lines, we proposed an alternative scheme based on the FIR filterbank framework to lower the transmitter hardware complexity and power consumption with closed-form solution [9-2, 8-4, 11-1]. We also investigated the localization aspects in mmWave MIMO systems, which corresponds to an important application in 5G communications [8-2]. Moreover, with the use of the restricted isometry property of the channel subspace sampling signals, we formulated the mmWave MIMO channel estimation as a low-rank subspace decomposition problem and the resultant framework reveals resilience to a low signal-to-noise ratio. A simple non-adaptive open-loop technique is then developed as the problem solver, which demonstrates improved channel estimation accuracy with a substantially low channel use overhead as compared to the traditional adaptive closed-loop methods [8-3].

11201015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201015.value: One future work is to solve the non-linear coupling problem for the analog and digital precoders, which corresponds to another subspace estimation in the hybrid analog-digital architecture of mmWave MIMO systems. This may be achieved by machine learning techniques to estimate the sparse mmWave channel subspace in a more efficient manner and perform under one-way open-loop training. In doing so, the huge overhead of channel sounding in large-scale antenna array mmWave MIMO systems, especially those of FDD, can be reduced. Furthermore, we can extend the FIR filterbank framework to semi-blind equalizer design under the low-hardware cost and low-power consumption constraints. As closed-form solution is possible, low computational cost on actual mobile devices will be realized. It is expected that the developed equalizer will not only optimize the detection accuracy under low-power consumption but also work well in the presence of severe interference signals.

11201215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201215.value: Awareness of climate change has resulted in international pressure to reduce the energy use of buildings. As heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems represent the largest primary energy end-user, generally consuming over 30% of the total energy used in commercial buildings, it is important to reduce the energy use of HVAC systems. Among the many tools that are used to improve the energy efficient operation of HVAC systems, real-time optimal control (RtOpt) is a very efficient option that regularly optimizes or resets the set-points or decision variables for local control loops regarding the energy use. Although RtOpt of overall HVAC systems can reduce energy use more than RtOpt of individual local loops or subsystems, it presents a large-scale mathematical programming issue, including the challenges of considering many decision variables and a large number of nonlinear models and complex constraints. Currently, the RtOpt of overall HVAC systems involves optimizing all decision variables simultaneously at each decision-making time using genetic or other evolutionary algorithms. There are many difficulties with the conventional optimization mechanism, including a heavy online computational burden, and scenarios for which optimal solutions may not be found. The stability and robustness of the system under overall optimization need to be systematically analyzed. This project aims to provide a new strategy for the RtOpt of overall HVAC systems that is more stable and robust than the conventional optimization mechanism and that suffers less from online computational burden, without sacrificing energy performance. To this end, we will develop a new RtOpt mechanism, namely multiplexed real-time optimal control (MRtOpt). Unlike the conventional mechanism, the new mechanism optimizes only one decision variable at each decision-making time with a higher optimization frequency. Each decision variable is optimized sequentially following a predefined order. Preliminary studies show that the new mechanism can significantly reduce computational burden (over 98%) without sacrificing energy performance (6.7% energy saved by the conventional method vs. 6.8% by the new method). After our encouraging preliminary results, in this project we will further develop MRtOpt strategy regarding modeling, stability, and robustness. The main tasks are to identify the most suitable modeling method for MRtOpt, improve the stability, and enhance the robustness. The output will be a complete MRtOpt toolbox with guidelines, which would help HVAC professionals to understand and implement the MRtOpt strategy.

11201215.label: Realisation of objectives
11201215.value: (1) Develop a dynamic simulation platform for an HVAC system using TRNSYS and MATLAB, which will be used to develop and validate the MRtOpt strategy This objective was achieved. We developed a simulation platform for a HVAC system using TRNSYS-MATLAB co-simulator. The HVAC system was constructed in TRNSYS, including chillers, cooling towers, cooling coils, fans, pumps, pipes and ducts; and the fluid and gas dynamics with respect to transportation time delay and control loops were also considered. All the supervisory and optimal control algorithms were developed based on the system performance models and coded separately in MATLAB module and linked to TRNSYS by a MAATLAB interface. The platform was configured using field data collected from a real building. Tests showed that the platform satisfied the basic requirements from the research project, such as its dynamics, transient response and local-loop control performance. (2) Identify the decision variables for the MRtOpt strategy using the dynamic simulation platform and sensitivity analysis This objective was achieved. We carried a number of simulation studies as well as sensitivity analysis to identify the decision variables that will be used in the MRtOpt strategy. We identified that decision variables for a very typical central air-conditioning system should be chilled water supply temperature set point, condenser water return temperature set point, and supply air temperature set point. Tests showed that these set points were the most important settings for the energy use during the operation of the central air-conditioning system. (3)Identify the most suitable modeling method for the MRtOpt strategy from current available modeling methods, such as detailed physical modeling, grey-box modeling and black-box modeling This objective was achieved. We compared three different types of models (physical models, grey models, and black-box models) in terms of computational efficiency, accuracy and reliability for the main components in a central air-conditioning system, including chillers, cooling towers, AHUs, pumps and fans. We used the data generated from the simulation platform and genetic algorithm (GA) to identify the parameters for these three types of models. After comparing the accuracy of the models, grey-box models were selected, which ensured a good agreement between model prediction and operational data, with high computational efficiency. (4) Improve the stability of the MRtOpt strategy by introducing a degree of freedom in resetting set-points and identifying the optimal order of resetting set-points This objective was achieved. We developed a degree of freedom (DOF) based set-point resetting method. The basic idea is to allow the reset have different magnitudes at each step, and optimize the magnitudes regarding to tracking errors. We compared this new method with the conventional set-point reset methods, i.e. rate-limited reset and step-change reset. Case studies were carried out using the developed simulation platform, and results showed that when compared with the conventional step reset and rate-limited reset, the proposed approach introduced much smaller disturbances during the reset process whether in the control loop that was experiencing the reset or in the control loops that was supposed to be influenced by the set. (5) Enhance the robustness of the MRtOpt strategy by developing data fusion methods and adaptive modeling to reduce uncertainties. This objective was achieved. We carried out uncertainty analysis and adaptive modeling to enhance the robustness of MRtOpt strategy. Using sensitivity analysis, critical parameters that had significant influence on the cooling load prediction were identified. To reduce the uncertainty, a Bayesian MCMC method, which was found better than data fusion, was developed. This method was validated using in-situ data from AC3 building in City University of Hong Kong. Adaptive modelling was also investigated. To balance the model accuracy and computational efficiency, regression models for the main components in the central air-conditioning system were adopted due to their simple structures, which could make this strategy practically applicable. We also investigated the length of training data using a systematic way of similarity check instead of a conventional ‘try-and-error’ method. (6) Identify experimentally the advantages and disadvantages of the MRtOpt strategy by comparing to the conventional optimization mechanism. This objective was achieved. In order not to disturb the operation of the BEMS system in the AC3 building, we chose to calibrate our simulation models using experimental data from AC3 building and other tall building in Hong Kong. Using the simulation platform, we compared the MRtOpt algorithm with a conventional optimization algorithm under same operation conditions, and thus identified the advantages and disadvantages of the MRtOpt strategy. We found that the MRtOpt was able to achieve similar energy performance but reduced the computational load significantly. Thus, the proposed MRtOpt strategy should be more practical for applications. (7) Develop guidelines for the practical application of the MRtOpt strategy This objective was achieved. We summarized the optimal control algorithms in our publications, providing guidelines for development and application. Particularly, we illustrated the details in the model development (both complex gray-box models and adaptive regression models, the procedure in sensitivity analysis, uncertainty analysis and DOE-based set point reset. All these details can help engineers understand the propose strategy and guide them to develop suitable tools for applications.

11201215.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201215.value: The main findings are summarized as follows. First, the Multiplexed Real-time Optimal control (MRtOpt) can greatly reduce the time that is used to seeking optimal values for decision variables. Case studies showed that the computation time could be reduced up to 98.3% when compared with the traditional optimization method that optimizes all decision variables simultaneously. Moreover, unlike the conventional scheme, the computational burden of the proposed scheme does not increase in an exponential way with the number of decision variables. Second, regression models should be a good choice for real-time optimal control of air-conditioning systems. Due to their simple model structure, the use of regression models can well balance the online computational burden of both model updating and optimization and model accuracy. Third, through energy performance comparison, the performance achieved by the MRtOpt strategy should be comparable to that achieved by the conventional method. This is supported by case studies, which showed that in a typical central air-conditioning system the multiplexed optimization strategy saved annual energy use about 6.8% compared with 6.7% that was saved by the conventional method under the Hong Kong weather climate. Fourth, the MRtOpt strategy can enhance the system operation stability by reducing the tracking errors of local closed loops. The stability can further be enhanced using the DOE-based set point resetting scheme. When compared with the conventional step reset and rate-limited reset, the proposed approach introduces smaller disturbances during the reset process whether in the control loop, which experiences the reset, or in the control loops that are influenced by the set. The main research outcome is a complete MRtOpt strategy, including the real-time optimal control algorithm, the DOE-based set point resetting algorithm, the main components models and their updating algorithm, which would help HVAC professionals to understand and implement the MRtOpt strategy. Five journal papers and two conference papers were published to illustrate the strategy and case studies, providing guidelines to design and implement the proposed MRtOpt strategy.

11201215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201215.value: Real-time optimal control is a very efficient option for reducing the energy use of HVAC systems, which regularly optimizes or resets the set-points or decision variables for local control loops regarding the energy use. However, it always presents a large-scale mathematical programming issue, including the challenges of considering many decision variables and a large number of nonlinear models and complex constraints, leading to the challenges of heavy online computational burden and unstable operation. The proposed MRtOpt strategy can efficiency solve these challenges, but its optimization actions are triggered by time (with a fixed frequency), which cannot deal with unpredictable changes efficiently. Since there are many unpredictable changes in the HVAC system operation conditions, a new mechanism to triggering optimization actions might be needed, which will be our further development of this research. We already carried out preliminary research on event-driven optimal control, which has the potential to deal with unpredictable changes in the HVAC system operation conditions.

11201215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201215.value: Because heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems represent the largest primary energy end-user, generally consuming over 30% of the total energy used in commercial buildings, it is important to reduce the energy use of HVAC systems for building sustainable development. This research has studied real-time optimal control of HVAC systems, which is considered as an efficient tool to reduce the energy use HVAC systems. However, the current optimal control strategy, which optimize all decision variables simultaneously, is not ready for practical use due to its heavy and complex online computational burden. Therefore, this research proposed a new strategy, titled as multiplexed real-time optimal control, which optimizes one and only decision variable at each optimization time but use a higher optimization frequency. Through numerical and experimental studies, the proposed method has been shown to be able to reduce the online computation burden significantly and at the same time save energy use efficiently.

11201315.label: Project Objectives
11201315.value: To design an iDDPM that combines Unscented Particle Filter (UPF) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithms. The iDDPM will enhance the capability to learn from the nature of historical pump operating signals, and then, based on the selected vital fault indicators, create accurate degradation trends for damaged slurry pumps. To design an iAFTM that integrates iDDPM with the Statistical Process Control (SPC) technique. This will adaptively set the dynamic failure threshold that is most suitable for the currently collected suspended Condition-based Monitoring (CBM) data, even if a certain amount of empirical information and experimental data are missing. To develop an iMWPHM that uses suspended CBM data and run-to-failure data to estimate failure probability density functions of a monitored pump. The iMWPHM is expected to handle typical wear-based failure modes. (Only the typical wear-based failure will be investigated.) To integrate the above three models and form the iPM, which will use a combination of population and individual characteristics, failure data and suspended data, statistical analysis and reliability models. (The portion of work load in the last process of optimization will be minimized.) After successful integration, an effective prognostic system will be implemented and used to predict the RULs of on-site and operating slurry pumps.

11201315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201315.value: Slurry pumps are commonly used in mining and heavy industry. A typical example is in the production of synthetic crude oil extracted from oil sands containing around 60% sand, 20% clay, 15% bitumen and 5% water. The pump impellers are continually bombarded by sand and small stones, and hence are prone to significant degradation due to these adverse operating conditions. As the amount of sand and stones contained in the pumped mixture is unpredictable, a temporal plot of the vibration magnitude shows significant fluctuations. These fluctuations lead to difficulty in deriving slurry pump degradation trends, which are very different from the linear and obvious trends associated with pure fluid pumps. Hence, the prediction of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) becomes difficult and inaccurate. To date, most of the reported methods of RUL prediction are workable only for relatively linear trends. Few reports can be found dealing with the prediction of RUL generated from machines that exhibit a high fluctuation in their monitored sensor signals during operation. In 2007 there were 8,020 slurry pumps in China, and this number continues to increase. Slurry pumps are expensive to replace and generate the most severe fluctuations in monitored signals. The frequent and unexpected failure of slurry pumps can interrupt oil production, cause serious contamination due to oil leakage from broken pumps or, in the worst case, cause human casualties. An unexpected shut-down of a slurry pump can cost $1.3 million per day in lost oil production. Hence, we aim to design a novel and intelligent prognostic system that can accurately predict the RUL of slurry pumps operating in an ever-changing operating environment. Such a prognostic system should be self-adaptive and self-optimized in terms of prognostic parameters. It must automatically recognize relationships between the current operational status (health) of the monitored slurry pump and its simultaneously monitored sensor signals. No prognostic system of this kind, based on operational data collected from on-site slurry pumps, has yet been designed. Once a successful system can be implemented for slurry pumps, the system can be modified and applied to other types of machine that exhibit similar fluctuations in sensor signals collected during operation. Potential candidates include reciprocating machines and car engines that also experience drastic changes in monitored signals during their operating. . 11201315.label: Realisation of objectives
11201315.value: All the necessary research activities required by objectives 1 to 5 have been successfully completed (100%). For objective 1, the required iDDPM was designed and implemented successfully. Vibration measurement was enforced as a mean of measuring the degradation of the pumps. The vibration amplitude would be in proportion to the degradation. After extensive tests conducted by the site workers in the oil exploration field, accelerometers for monitoring the pump generated vibrations were mounted on each monitored slurry pump. Raw vibration signals were then collected daily by these accelerometers. Feature extraction was imposed to decrease the dimensionality of the collected vibration data. These features were used to characterize the health conditions of the pumps. Some of the key features helped to classify the raw data to valid to invalid data sets. The Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm was used to maximize or optimize the Euclidean distance between valid and invalid data sets. After applying such intelligent algorithm, the valid and invalid data sets became separable. Because of the help of iDDPM and PSO, the system can automatically classify the collected raw data into valid and invalid data sets. Only the valid data sets were retained. For objective 2, from the valid data sets, 18 features were identified and extracted from the data sets. However, if all the 18 features are selected to generate the required fault related trends, the size and dimension of the data sets will be very large. Hence, it is necessary to refine and select the most appropriate fault feature to create the degradation trend of the monitored pump. To achieve such task, another intelligent algorithm, the iAFTM, was designed and tested. Part of the iAFTM algorithm involves the use of Principal Component Analysis (PCA). PCA is an orthogonal transformation to convert a set of observations of possibly correlated variables into a set of values of linearly uncorrelated variables called principal components. In the iAFTM, the conjunctive principal components were also extracted. A threshold limit of one tenth of the overall variances was set to assure the selected principal components were still able to represent the variability of the data. That is, the iAFTM is used to select the best fault trends from all trends generated from the 18 features. The selection is based on computing the covariance between the factors and the best fit curve of the fault/degradation trend. The most appropriate degradation trend was automatically selected by iAFTM. Moreover, from the analysis done on the selected fault trend, we had discovered the characteristics and behavior of wearing parts of the monitored pump. The vibration trend generated from a worn-out part will be continuously increasing until it peaked at certain level. After reaching such highest peak, then the vibration trend will be dropped gradually as the impacts caused by sharp surfaces of wearing part will be smoothed out by continuous contact with other parts’ surfaces. Hence, the magnitude of trend will be dropped after reaching such peak. The aim of iAFTM is to automatically determine such highest peak and then set such value as the desired threshold. Once this dynamic threshold can be found, then iAFTM can use it as the proper time to alert the maintenance staff to prepare necessary remedy action or an overhaul to repair or replace the deteriorating pump. Note that different slurry pump running at different loading condition will have its own threshold value. The iAFTM can be adaptively identify such dynamic threshold based on the current operating condition of the inspected pump. For objective 3, after setting the dynamic threshold value, then the iMWPHM was used to predict the remaining useful life (RUL) of the inspected slurry pump and then further estimate the failure probability density functions of a monitored pump. A Relevant Vector Machine (RVM) based intelligent learning process was designed to learn the characteristic of the selected pump degradation trend and predict the RUL of the pump according to its current health status. The algorithm of RVM was designed based on the well-known Bayesian sparse kernel model that introduces a prior distribution over the model weights that are governed by a set of hyper-parameters. In comparison with the popular algorithm of Support Vector Machine (SVM), the most compelling feature of the RVM is its superior generalization performance and a shorter time for prediction because relatively few “relevance vectors” are used in effecting the prediction. The RVM was designed to learn the characteristics of the current and past fault trends and then estimate the RUL based on the current health status of the pump. After the success estimation of the RUL, then another intelligent algorithm, called particle filter, was used to approximate the failure probability density functions based on the learned RULs obtained from past operating history of the same pump and the current RUL. Hence, the iMWPHM is embedded with RVM and particle filter. Note that the accuracy in calculating the failure probability density functions for risk assessment is assuming that the same pump was operating at roughly the similar operating conditions after each overhaul of the pump. For objective 4, in the fault prognosis phase, the system must know how to integrate different types of input data that have different characteristics as the same pump may not work at the same operating condition as assumed in iMWPHM as defined in objective 3. To handle such variety of input data, a new type of intelligent system, named iPM, was designed. The iPM used a novel and recently popular method called Deep Learning. Deep learning (DL) is an unsupervised learning method, which has been widely used in automatically extract data feature information from a large number of non-tagged data for classification in recent years. We considered a DL-based Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) prognostic prediction model. The developed LSTM model predicted RUL of a degrading slurry pump with a small Root Mean Square Error compared to the actual life of the degrading pump operating at field. The results revealed that the DL-based LSTM model outperformed other conventional prediction methods in terms of accuracy. For objective 5, the research work is focused on verifying the effectiveness of all intelligent systems implemented from this research project. The process of verification used not only the historical data, but also real-time data collected from on-site and operating slurry pumps. A field trip was arranged to visit the site in Canada to complete the requirements as stated in objective 5. The results prove that all implemented systems work as expected. The iPM that integrated all designed systems is found to be an effective prognostic system. If a fault has occurred, the iPM system can diagnose the seriousness of the fault caused to the pump and finally predict the RULs of the inspected slurry pump. Every time, after an overhaul was conducted on a deteriorating slurry pump, the iPM system will restart again to learn another new set of characteristic and degrading behavior of the overhauled pump. With such continuous learning process and have sufficient numbers of degradation trends generated by the pump and stored in the intelligent iPM system, the accuracy in predicting the RUL and the estimation of the pump failure probability density function will be enhanced after completing each new learning and prediction process.

11201315.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201315.value: As of today, 25 peer-reviewed journal papers have been published. 23 out of these 25 papers are SCI indexed and high-ranking journal papers. Besides, there are 12 referred papers presented and published in a number of international conferences. That is, a total of 37 pieces of publication. Two of the post-graduate students are using the funding of this GRF project to partially support their studentship. The major findings and outcomes include 1) an automatic system to collect raw data from sensors mounted on the slurry pumps. The time and interval for collecting data could be set by maintenance staff and then run automatically. 2) A smart algorithm for checking the validity of captured raw data. A number of fault related features were selected based on the characteristics of raw data in order to reduce the size of data and eliminated invalid data. A variety of filters were used to test each collected data set. Only those sets that truly reflected the fault situation of the pump were retained. 3) An automatic system was designed to extract the temporal information from each feature so that its degradation trend vs operating hours could be generated. 4) An intelligent system was then automatically identified the most important trend from the 18 fault trends obtained from 18 features. The selected fault trend should truly represent the deteriorating condition of monitored pump. 5) With the help of fault trend and its dynamic threshold, the current health condition of the pump was determined and the severity of deterioration caused by the fault related feature could be known. 6) An intelligent system was then predicted the RUL of the deteriorating pump. Each pump and its unique running condition should have its own tailor-made intelligent algorithm to predict its RUL. 7) Beside the predicted RUL, the boundaries for degree of confidence and failure probability density functions were also determined for risk analysis. The more the stored fault trends, the higher the reliability or better accuracy in the prediction of RUL. With the help of this fully automatic and intelligent system, maintenance staff can have a scientific and countable prediction in RUL for any deteriorating machine. Hence, the occurrence of sudden breakdown of machine can be avoided. Scheduled repair or shifting of production to other line can be arranged in advance and at a time that will cause minimum production or service interruption.

11201315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201315.value: Based on the knowledge and experience gained from this research work, the PI suggests in further development, one should focus on Deep Learning neural networks (DL). The original proposal of this research does not include DL. However, to fulfil the research as stated in objective 4, we later found that DL has more potential in prediction than the originally proposed RVM in iPM system. There are many types of DL models. The Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) prognostic model is a special kind of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) that is capable of solving long-term dependencies. LSTM not only comprises of recursive property of RNN, but also handles long term time series, like the temporal fault trend generated by a deteriorating machine. Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is another class of DL. The advantage of CNN is its automatic feature extraction for raw data. Here, we propose a hybrid model LSTM-CNN for predicting the RULs. The CNN focuses on the feature extraction from input data. The LSTM is responsible for generating regression in sequential data. In a preliminary study, we found that the root-mean-squared-error generated from CNN is higher than that by LSTM-CNN in prediction. Therefore, LSTM-CNN is recommended for predicting RULs.

11201315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201315.value: Sludge and slurry pumps are commonly used in mining and heavy industry. The internal pump are continually bombarded by sand and small metals, and hence are prone to significant degradation due to these adverse operating conditions. Because the fluctuation in pumping materials is substantial, the prediction of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of pumps becomes difficult. In oil industry, an unexpected shut-down of a slurry pump can cost $1.3 million per day in losing oil production. Hence, an intelligent prognostic system is designed to accurately predict the RUL of any deteriorating pump. The designed system proves to be self-adaptive and self-optimized in terms of prognostic parameters. Even each pump has its unique running condition and loading characteristics, a tailor-made intelligent algorithm was developed to suit such deviation. The predicted RULs prove to match closely with the actual RULs of the monitored pumps. With the success in implementing such AI system for slurry pumps, the system can be modified and applied to other types of machine that exhibit large fluctuations in their operation. The expected results are the minimization of production downtime, a dramatic decrease in maintenance costs and the avoidance of human casualties due to sudden and fatal machine breakdown.

11202315.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202315.value: 智能数据平面：数据中心网络中的分布式拥塞感知负载均衡

11202315.label: Project Objectives
11202315.value: Enabling distributed congestion-aware load balancing in the data plane for data center networks. Designing a scalable congestion information collection mechanism for complex topologies like fat-tree. Designing a distributed congestion-aware path selection mechanism. Improving the path selection mechanism to better deal with failures and network asymmetry. Performance evaluation of the proposed design using testbed implementation.
rows: Enabling distributed congestion-aware load balancing in the data plane for data center networks.
Designing a scalable congestion information collection mechanism for complex topologies like fat-tree.
Designing a distributed congestion-aware path selection mechanism.
Improving the path selection mechanism to better deal with failures and network asymmetry.
Performance evaluation of the proposed design using testbed implementation.

11202315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202315.value: Traditional wisdom says the network data plane ought to be as simple as possible for packet forwarding at line rate, and coordination can be performed in the control plane which may be logically centralized. This principle has been followed in data center networks, which provide a large number of equal-cost paths and abundant bandwidth between server machines. To load balance flows, the data plane runs ECMP---Equal Cost Multi-Path---that forwards packets among equal-cost egress ports based on simple hashing. A dumb data plane with ECMP cannot satisfy the increasingly stringent performance requirements of data center networks, including low latency both on average and at the tail for interactive services, and high throughput for data-processing frameworks with bulky data access. ECMP suffers from the well-known hash collisions problem. When happening among elephant flows, hash collisions cause low throughput and bandwidth utilization. When happening between mice and elephant flows, they cause long queueing delay for mice flows. ECMP's local and congestion-agnostic nature fundamentally limits its ability to make intelligent load balancing decisions. Towards a smart data plane, we propose a novel distributed congestion-aware load balancing protocol called Expeditus. Expeditus can direct flows to near-optimal paths based on instantaneous network state, leading to better latency and throughput with little overhead and zero centralized control. This project builds on our deep understanding of the practical challenges of designing a smart data plane, and contains four integrated components. First, we will develop a novel one-hop information collection mechanism that enables switches to collect real-time congestion information in a scalable and efficient manner. Second, we will propose a two-stage path selection mechanism to aggregate relevant information across switches and make near-optimal path selection decisions. Third, link failures may cause the system to make poor load balancing decisions in certain cases. We will study how to prevent the selection of congested paths due to failures using an explicit notification mechanism. Finally, we will evaluate the performance of Expeditus using both theoretical analysis and prototype implementation. We will implement Expeditus using Click software router and deploy it on the Emulab testbed with realistic topologies. We are committed to making our implementation code publicly available and readily usable for the community. 一直以来，人们认为网络数据平面应该尽可能得简单，以实现数据包的高速转发。网络的控制协调可以在逻辑上集中式的控制平面上进行。这一原则在数据中心网络中也一直被遵循。数据中心网络提供了大量的等价路径来满足服务器机之间的带宽需求。为了负载平衡流量，数据平面普遍运行ECMP---等价多路径协议---来实现基于简单的哈希的多路径转发。 简单的ECMP并不能满足数据中心网络日益严格的性能要求，包括为互动服务提供低延迟（平均和最差），和为数据处理框架与庞大的数据访问提供高吞吐量。ECMP的静态和拥塞无关的性质从根本上限制了它做智能负载平衡决策的能力。为了建立下一代的智能数据平面，我们提出了一种分布式的拥塞感知负载平衡协议，Expeditus。Expeditus可以基于瞬时网络状态为每个网络流选择最优路径，从而以很小的开销和零集中控制提供更好的延迟和吞吐量。 本项目建立在我们对设计智能数据平面的实际挑战的深刻理解的基础上，包含四个集成部分。首先，我们将开发一个新的单跳信息收集机制，使交换机能够有一个可扩展的和有效的方式收集实时的拥塞信息。其次，我们将提出一个两阶段的路径选择机制，以跨交换机聚合相关的信息，做出接近最优的路径选择。第三，链路故障可能导致系统在某些情况下，使负载平衡的决定不理想。我们将研究一个明确的通知机制来解决不对称情况下的路径选择。最后，我们将采用理论分析和原型实现的方式对Expeditus的性能进行评估。我们将在Click软件路由上实现Expeditus，并部署在Emulab的测试平台。我们致力于使我们的实现代码公开可用，并随时可用于社区。

11202315.label: Realisation of objectives
11202315.value: We designed and implemented Expeditus, a novel congestion-aware load balancing protocol in the data plane. It has a scalable congestion information collection mechanism that only monitors local switch port information. It relies on a distributed congestion-aware path selection protocol that piggybacks congestion information from different switches to the sender/receiver to make a path selection decision. The work was published in ACM Symposium on Cloud Computing in 2016, a top conference on cloud computing, and then in IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking in 2017, the top journal in computer networking. Thus we fully achieve objectives 1 and 2. We then proposed Luopan, another congestion-aware load balancing protocol to improve the path selection mechanism to better deal with failures and network asymmetry. It relies on random sampling instead of information piggybacking to make path selections and is much easier to implement. Luopan was published in IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems, a top-tier journal in distributed systems. Thus we fully achieve objective 4. Both Expeditus and Luopan were evaluated using testbed implementation. Thus we fully achieve objective 5. Summarising the above, we conclude that we achieve the overall objective 1.
