11205815.label: Realisation of objectives
11205815.value: In this project, the following objectives have been achieved: 1. The study of dynamic characteristics of the electrophysiological recording process have been achieved. Patch clamp technique is an intracellular bio-electrical signal recording method through measuring the electric current flowing through ion channels in a cell membrane. It is well understood that the ion channels played important roles in regulating the flow of ions across the cell membrane, which are involved critically in various physiological processes. Therefore, patch clamp recording was widely used for studying the electrophysiological properties of cells and investigating the effect of different drugs on cells. The technique is an electrophysiological recording process, which dynamic characteristics were studied involving the change of pressure and electrical resistance or impedance during the process. In the project, during the electrophysiological recording of cell in the whole-cell state, both electrical signal and real-time images were recorded from optical microscope. The transmembrane current was recorded when a voltage pulse was applied to the pipette in the voltage clamp mode. A peak current called capacitive current, Ic was observed from the transmembrane current curve, representing current flow across the membrane capacitance. The membrane capacitance is the stored charge of ions across the cell membrane. In addition to monitoring the electrical signals, the real time images of cells were observed under the optical microscopy. Three different types of cells were used, including human neuroblastoma cells, Dorsal root ganglion neuron and HepG2 liver hepatocellular cells. 2. The development of visual based feedback approach based on the Blob Detection algorithm that enables detection and identification of the target cell. To enhance the usability and reduce the human errors of patch clamp recording, the visual based feedback approach based on image processing with blob detection algorithm was developed for identification of biological cells and micro-pipette during the operation. This approach was implemented in the automated electrophysiological recording system. The experimental setup was built for implementing the patch clamp recording based on the visual based identification. The cells and pipette were first observed under an inverted microscope. The live video and digital real time image were then captured using a CCD camera. Based on image processing with blob detection algorithm, the coordinates of the cell and the pipette can be obtained from the image and the movement of the manipulator was subsequently calculated. The blob detection algorithm was used as the main method to detect cells and pipettes for patch clamp. Blobs are the binary objects or points which are in the same state. Blobs can be classified as different objects based on color, shape, area, perimeter and etc. Therefore, this method can be applied to identify the target cell based on its own shape and feature, and to separate the cell from other neighboring cells in the same image. For identification of biological cells, the image processing was conducted using several kinds of transform methods. The digital image of the sample was first transformed to a grayscale image. In the grayscale image, every pixel was represented by an intensity value ranging from 0 to 255. The image was then processed by applying two basic morphological operations, namely dilation and erosion. The concept of the dilation operation was to increase the area of bright regions in the image, while the erosion was to increase the area of dark regions in the image. To verify the performance of cell identification, a batch of cells were tested independently. To find out the optimal parameters for cell identification including the structural element and threshold value, a certain range of size of structural element and thershold values were applied. The cell identification were conducted on 95 cells, with the applied threshold value ranging from 130 to 250 and the structural element ranging from 31 to 61. A cell was considered as successfully identified when its center and boundary were accurately located from the output image. The results indicated that the highest yield of identification which was equal to 90% was obtained, when the threshold value was 160-180 and the size of structural element was higher than 51. 3. The derivation of the contact-to-patch algorithm based on the electrical resistance feedback that is capable of monitoring the contact point and condition between the micro-pipette and cells has been achieved. A new algorithm was developed for the patch clamp system to automatically perform engaging, gigaseal formation and whole-cell recording on adherent cells by algorithmically detecting cell conditions and analyzing electrical resistance changes. This system can avoid suspension procedures of adherent cells and increase the yield of gigaseal formation. As a result, patch clamp recording can be finished in few minutes. Program execution for automated patch clamp with contact-to-patch algorithm based on the electrical resistance feedback. The operational diagram for automated patch clamp execution includes strategies for stage execution, and quantitative milestones that govern process flow and decision making. The operational diagram was designed for the four key stages of the automated patch clamp execution. The electrical resistance between the electrode in the intracellular buffer and the signal ground in the extracellular buffer was calculated based on the voltage and measured current. This electrical resistance was a critical parameter for determining the seal quality. The electrical resistance also indicated if the operational diagram made options, such as starting the next stage and pausing. Therefore, monitoring resistance was critical to the system performance. After the gigaseal was formed, it enabled the rupture of the patched membrane at the end. Two methods could break the patched membrane: a strong negative pressure of 30 kPa or a high voltage pulse of 200 mV at 5 μs called a “zap.” These two methods complement each other, particularly if one method cannot break the patched membrane. 4. The development of the automated electrophysiological recording system to detect the electric currents through the ion channels has been achieved. An equivalent electrical model was established to monitor two situations. The real time current response during the microinjection was studied. In addition, the current trace under voltage stimulus was recorded in order to verify the survivability of the cells after microinjection. The equivalent model for the cell cytoplasmic microinjection and the electric model for cell survivability verification have been found to enable the system. A cell interacting with a micro-pipette can be regarded as an electrical circuit containing several electrical components. ENa, EK and EOther ions are the equilibrium (Nernst) potentials of Na+, K+ and other ions between the cell membrane. For the equivalent model for the cell cytoplasmic microinjection, the microinjection was performed on single living cell when it was at the resting state. SK, SNa and SOther ions are anticipated to be open because RNa, RK and Rother ions are expected to be very large since nearly none of ion channels will be activated without the voltage stimulus. Hence, INa, IK, and IOther ions will become zero. For the electric model for cell survivability verification, after the injection to a living cell, its vitality and survivability are of great concerns and can be verified by the study of ion channel activities. When the cells are alive after the microinjection, the activities of ion channels can be activated by applying the voltage stimulus for verification.

11205815.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205815.value: The major findings and research outcome of the research and development of the technology for the automated electrophysiological recording system can be divided into two aspects: (1) Research and implantation for the system; (2) Using the developed system for relevant applications. 1. First, the automated patch clamp systems have been developed to eliminate the need of manual handling. We develop a systematic approach to apply electrical resistance feedback for automated patch clamp recording on adherent cells. We analyze the critical parameters that affect the performance of the automated patch clamp recording. By using the new algorithm for automated engaging and formation, the cell-attached and whole-cell recordings on adherent cells were performed in less than 5 minutes with the yield of over 70% [J1]. 2. Second, the electrical feedback for the automated system for cytoplasmic microinjection of biological cells have been proposed. In order to realize the cytoplasmic microinjection on small adherent cells, an electrical model is built and analyzed according to electrochemical properties of target cells. In this find, we have verified the effectiveness of current measurement for monitoring the injection process and the study of ion channel activities for verifying the cell variability of the cells after microinjection [J2][C1]. 3. Third, ion channel study is relevant research in electrophysiology. We showed that the formation of Aβ ion channel on the membrane depended on cholesterol concentration which cholesterol levels affected the stability and assembly of lipid bilayers. Measurements on planar lipid bilayers indicated that a small amount of cholesterol interacted with Aβ proteins and promoted the insertion process. Results demonstrated that Aβ ion channel promoted Ca2+ flux in the presence of 15% cholesterol but prevent Ca2+ flux in high cholesterol. Overall, this study suggested a possible approach to consider cholesterol levels for the treatment of AD patients. The finding has already been heighted in the journal cover [J10]. 4. Four, the developed system also enable further collaboration in the field of stem cell research. This study has demonstrated for the first time that biocompatible iSECnMs enable the rapid self-organization of functional miniature brain-like structures (i.e., mini-SNLSs) derived from naïve primary NSCs. Moreover, these mini-SNLSs definitively delivered early and progressive amelioration of the motor symptoms associated with 6-OHDA-induced PD rats. It demonstrate the great potential of our mini-SNLS for the achievement of better therapeutic results in subjects with PD [J7].

11205815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205815.value: 1. The accuracy of cell detection and screening can be further increased, which can gain a higher performance of the system. 2. There are various types of cells, which can have different cell morphologies. A novel way may need considered to finding the correct cell type of recording. AI and Deep learning approach can be one of the possible method, which enable the study and learning for various cell types. Therefore, the target cells can be identified through the training process. 3. It has been found that the stages of cells could affect the recording signal of recording. More experiments are needed to explore the functional signals in various cell conditions, which reflects their physiological condition in different environments and responses. It also indicated the healthy, unhealthy, young and mature stages etc.

11205815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205815.value: To date, patch clamp is the one of the very popular technique to study biological cells. It is an intracellular bio-electrical signal recording method through measuring the electric current flowing through ion channels in a cell membrane. It is well understood that the ion channels played important roles in regulating the flow of ions across the cell membrane, which are involved critically in various physiological processes. Patch clamp recording was widely used for studying the electrophysiological properties of cells and investigating the effect of different drugs on cells. However, current practice of patch clamp recording requires manual work. In order to success, a specialized operator needs to control the instrument for several hours carefully, while these processes require high-skill training. This further shows that the conventional patch clamp recording is one of the most labor-intensive techniques, which results in low throughput and high demands on experimenters. Therefore, the development of the project grealy enhance the efficient and performance of the recording process which benefit to the field of neuroscience, drug discovery and biology .

11206115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206115.value: 本項目旨在將矽上氮化鋁薄膜壓電諧振器和聲子晶體這兩種器件結合起來，創造一種新型器件。這兩種器件一般是運用在不同的領域，因此很少會被聯繫在一起。具体来说，本項目採用的是二維聲子晶體。它的優點是易於加工製造，而且能够通過按比例縮小的方法工作於較高的頻段。聲子晶体好比機械波操控者，能够將通過諧振器錨點逃逸出來的機械波反彈回諧振器本身。利用這種方法，我們就能够在不改變諧振器結構的前提下提高諧振器的品質因數。我们前期的實驗結果已經證明了通過結合二維聲子晶体的方法，可以將諧振器的品質因數提高一倍。我們在本項目會先研究不同結構的二維聲子晶體，並用它们來提高諧振頻率在300MHz以上的壓電諧振器的品質因數。然后，我們會對二維聲子晶體和一維声子晶體對品質因數提高的效果做出比較。

11206115.label: Realisation of objectives
11206115.value: Objective 1: We have fully achieved the objective at the end of the project. We have successfully implemented and evaluated various designs of phononic crystals (PnCs) hybridized with piezoelectric resonators. We have experimentally shown that by applying these PnCs, we obtain quality factors that are among the highest reported in the literature for AlN MEMS contour mode piezoelectric resonators of similar thickness and resonant frequency. We have proposed and validated novel PnC topologies with very wide acoustic bandgap that are able to boost quality factors up to the limit whereby we begin to observe the effect of other types of damping. Objective 2: We have fully achieved the objective at the end of the project. We have compared the characteristics of one-dimensional PnCs with two-dimensional PnCs. We have found that 1D PnCs limit the choice of PnC topologies available and practically more difficult to implement compared to 2D PnCs. Using 2D PnCs, we are able to propose novel topologies that can deliver very wide acoustic bandgap to boost the quality factor of piezoelectric resonators, which are difficult to implement in 1D chains. Furthermore, we have also explored mixing different types of PnCs in a 2D array to combine the merits of 1D-viable PnC topologies and other PnC topologies that deliver wide bandgap but can only be practically implemented in 2D.

11206115.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206115.value: 1) We have proposed a novel solid disk PnC design that delivers very wide acoustic band gap, the widest among previously proposed PnC designs. By hybridizing this novel PnC topology with AlN piezoelectric resonators, we have experimentally demonstrated piezoelectric resonators with quality factors that are among the highest for devices with similar thickness and frequency range. The results have been published in an open-source journal as an invited contribution. The device was selected the cover page image of the journal. 2) Using the PnCs explored in this project, we have demonstrated quality factors that are notably higher than the preliminary devices applying conventional PnC designs (of which the results formed the basis of this project). The quality factors have been boosted to such a level that we have begun to see the effects of other types of damping. These findings are very interesting and exciting as they converge with similar trends observed using other methods of boosting quality factor that we have been studying (e.g. biconvex resonators). 3) We have verified that the effect on quality factor by these PnCs agrees well with theory. For example, we have verified experimentally that their effect on the quality is frequency specific. In other words, if the resonant mode lies within the band gap, we see that the quality factor is boosted. If the resonant mode lies outside the band gap, the PnCs have no effect on the quality factor. In addition, as with previously explored conventional PnC designs, we have continued to observe that the size of the band gap affects the amount of increase in quality factor. For a wider band gap, we observe a higher increase in the quality factor. We have been unable to experimentally measure the transmission through the various phononic crystals that we have studies in order to correlate the transmission band gap with the simulated gap. We had fabricated and tested many delay lines incorporating types of PnC designs of varying periods with the aim of measuring the attenuation and frequency response.These experiments and investigations go beyond the proposed scope of the project. We suspect that the amount of coupling in AlN is too weak. This exploration of the effect of the acoustic band gap in relation to the PnC design and geometry is important to not only AlN systems but also other piezoelectric device platforms being explored for acoustic devices.

11206115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206115.value: We have been unable to consistently experimentally measure the transmission through the various phononic crystals that we have studied in order to correlate the transmission band gap with the simulated gap. We had fabricated and tested many delay lines incorporating types of PnC designs of varying periods with the aim of measuring the attenuation and frequency response.These experiments and investigations go beyond the proposed scope of the project. We suspect that the redesign of the delay lines are required to increase the strength of the generated signal. This exploration of the effect of the acoustic band gap in relation to the PnC design and geometry is important to not only AlN systems but also other piezoelectric device platforms being explored for acoustic devices. A better grasp of PnCs would allow further exploitation of these interesting structures for applications beyond frequency control to sensing.

11206115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206115.value: In this project we have explored the combination of phononic crystals with piezoelectric resonators. Piezoelectric resonators are highly interesting for both radio-frequency applications and as well for sensors. In general, a high quality factor is desirable. Piezoelectric resonators can be provide very low motional impedance, making it easier to interface them with electronic circuitry compared with capacitance resonators that suffer from high impedance. However, the quality factors of piezoelectric resonators are much lower than the material limits. In this project, we have explored different types of phononic crystals (PnCs) as a means to boost quality factor through the manipulation of acoustic waves at the microscopic level. We have demonstrated quality factors that are among the highest in the literature for resonators with similar sizes.

11207215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207215.value: Metallic glasses are well known for their superb strength and high elastic limit; however, their fatigue resistance, in terms of fatigue endurance limit, is usually low, being less than 10% of their ultimate tensile strength according to the prior results. Aside from the lack of tensile ductility, this also hinders the use of metallic glasses as a structural material. Meanwhile, although the fracture toughness of some metallic glasses, such as Zr-, Pt- and Pd-based, is comparable to conventional alloys, the fracture toughness of some others that have important functional applications, such as Fe-, Mg-, and Ca-based metallic glasses, are very limited. In order to mitigate these problems, metallic glasses are often being mixed with crystalline phases to form metallic-glass matrix composites. Despite that the composite approach was effective on some alloy compositions, however, it also destroys the overall structural amorphousness and simultaneously reduces the alloy strength, which is not desirable in the applications which prefer a full amorphous structure. By comparison, we have recently shown that, by carefully controlling the degree of structural rejuvenation in as-cast amorphous states through thermo-mechanical treatments, appreciable tensile ductility of 2-4% can be achieved even in monolithic Zr-based bulk metallic glasses without scarifying their tensile strength. In this project, we would like to propose further research, combining experimental, theoretical and computational efforts, to understand the underlying physical mechanisms behind this phenomenon of ductility enhancement and carry out a systematic study of the various methods, including the thermo-mechanical treatment and sample architecture design, which can enhance not only tensile ductility but also fracture and fatigue resistance in the metallic glasses with a high economic feasibility for industrial applications, such as Fe- and Mg-based. The successful implementation of the proposal is expected to achieve the following: (1) to construct a structural evolution map, as related to various thermo-mechanical treatments, which enables quantitatively controlling the degree of rejuvenation and/or relaxation of the amorphous structure in a metallic glass, (2) to understand and model the basic micromechanical processes of fracture and fatigue damage in a metallic glass and (3) to provide guidelines for improving fracture and fatigue resistance in metallic glasses through controlled structural evolution and sample architecture design. 由於原子尺度上的長程無序和缺乏一般晶體結構的微觀組織，金屬玻璃常常表現出高強度低韌性（低斷裂韌性和拉伸脆性）的特點。在本項研究中，我們致力于通過調控金屬玻璃的熱歷史和試件形態來達到增加斷裂韌性和疲勞抗力的目的。此項研究成果可提高金屬玻璃作為結構及軟磁材料應用的效率。

11207215.label: Realisation of objectives
11207215.value: 1. To understand the micromechanical mechanisms of damage initiation and growth in metallic glasses under cyclic loading Through molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, we explored the mechanism of cyclic loading induced elastic softening. Our results clearly show that, while cyclic loading causes atomic bond breaking in metallic glasses (MGs), the elastic softening at the lower stress rate is mainly due to the viscoelasticity resulting from the activation of more and larger string-like “liquid-like” atomic clusters. Since yielding in MGs is strain controlled, fundamentally being correlated with the glass transition temperature or the elastic modulus, the continuous elastic softening in MGs with cyclic loading can ultimately lead to yielding (or shear banding) even for an applied stress lower than the quasi-static yielding strength, thus giving rise to fatigue failure from the sites with severe elastic softening. 2. To understand the processes of structural evolution in metallic glasses with different thermo-mechanical treatments Through theoretical modeling and extensive annealing experiments, we develop quantitative relations between the unrelaxed overall elastic properties and local structural heterogeneities in MGs. General formulas for the unrelaxed elastic moduli are derived based on the well-established Eshelby’s theory, which are verified afterwards by the extensive experimental results obtained from the isothermal relaxation experiments on various MGs. Our current findings reveal that the softening behavior of the soft regions plays a key role in setting the general trend of the Poisson’s ratio of the MGs that varies with the annealing time before a crystallization process sets in. In general, shear softening favors plasticity, leading to a decreasing Poisson’s ratio with thermal annealing; while hydrostatic pressure softening results in embrittlement, leading to a slightly increasing Poisson’s ratio with thermal annealing. Furthermore, we also find that the relaxation dynamics in different MGs can be correlated with the size non-uniformity of their soft regions. These important findings provide quantitative insights into the structural origin of mechanical properties of MGs. More importantly, given the generality of the Eshelby’s theory, the outcome of our current work should be applicable to other elastically heterogeneous materials of great technological importance. In addition, we explored the magnetization effect on mechanical properties of a ductile Fe83C1B11Si2P3 metallic glass (MG). We firstly demonstrated that magnetic anisotropy can be systematically created by plastic deformation using high-load Berkovich indentation, and then provide compelling evidence by subsequent spherical nanoindentation which revealed tunable magnetization-induced submicron elastic heterogeneity. A new mechanism of magnetomechanical interaction, different from the alteration of “flow defect”, was proposed for explaining the apparent softening in the region without plastic deformation. Our studies have significance for modification and controlling of the microstructure and mechanical properties of MGs with respect to magnetic effect. Based on substantial dynamic mechanical analyses, we identified a fast beta relaxation common to a variety of MGs is identified in the present work. Compared to the slow beta relaxation that is generally related to chemical bond breakage, STZ activation and yielding in MGs, the fast beta relaxation correlates with a more confined inelasticity process activated at a much lower energy. This subtle relaxation process is more sensitive to the local atomic packing variation than the chemical bonding in the amorphous structure of MGs, therefore insensitive to the corresponding glass transition temperature. By fully activating the fast b0 relaxation, multiple shear banding can be triggered in different MGs near a temperature being much lower than the glass transition point but close to the peak temperature for the fast secondary relaxation. These interesting findings unfold an intrinsic correlation between relaxation, structural evolution and mechanical deformation in MGs. Through our extensive molecular dynamics simulations of creep in MGs, we find that a significant portion of viscoelasticity in MGs is mediated through back-and-forth anharmonic motions of atoms. Interestingly, we also show that such anharmonic oscillatory atomic motion stems mainly from collective atomic rotations, which generates local vorticities with an intensity ten folds of the vorticity induced directly by local shear. As deformation proceeds, the “vortex-like” atomic motion shows an increasing correlation with local atomic slips or the activation of shear transformation zones. Our findings indicate that the viscoelastic deformation during creep in MGs is a two-step process, which echoes very well with the recent discovery of two secondary relaxations in a variety of MGs 3. To develop rate-dependent micromechanical models to quantify the damage process in metallic glasses Given that recent experiments showed that irreversible structural change or plasticity could occur in metallic glasses (MGs) even within the apparent elastic limit after a sufficiently long waiting time, we developed a stochastic shear transformation (SST) model based on a unified rate theory to predict delayed yielding in MGs, which was validated afterwards through extensive atomistic simulations carried out on different MGs. On a fundamental level, an analytic framework is finally established that links time, stress and temperature altogether into a general yielding criterion for MGs. On the other hand, the effect of thermal history on shear band initiation in metallic glass is investigated with spherical nanoindentation. Our results clearly show that the indentation size effect on the metallic-glass hardness varies systematically with the thermal history, which is in excellent agreement with the softening-induced shear-band initiation model we previously developed. Through the size effect study, we show that shear band initiation is influenced by the thermal history of a MG. This thermal history dependence as revealed by the spherical indentation can be captured very well by the shear-band initiation model we previously developed. Meanwhile, the variation of the shear-band initiation length scale with the thermal annealing can be rationalized by the well-established model in the earthquake mechanics, thus revealing the mechanistic similarity between shear-band initiation in MGs and earthquake initiation in the earth mantle. Next, we also studied how sample surface could affect shear band initiation. It was previously reported that the strength of metallic glasses (MGs) would scale inversely with the size of a sample or a deformation field, commonly known as “smaller-being-stronger”. However, based on the extensive spherical nanoindentation experiments conducted across a variety of MGs, we demonstrate that such strength-size scaling breaks down at a critical indenter tip radius, which is caused by the transition of the yielding mechanism from bulk- to surface-controlled shear band initiation. Our experimental findings also provide an explanation for the unusual strength scattering observed in the micro-compression of MGs. Physically, this is attributed to the transition of the yielding mechanism from bulk or homogeneous shear band nucleation to surface mediated shear band nucleation. The critical size is correlated positively with the shear modulus but negatively with the shear softening rate, which, interestingly is found to further correlate with Poisson’s ratio of a MG. Furthermore, the significant data scattering of the yield strengths obtained from micro- and nano-compression of MGs can be rationalized based on the indentation data we obtained

11207215.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207215.value: Scientifically, the major findings of this project include the following (1) the origin of elastic softening/damage initiation is associated with rearrangements of atoms. Atomic bond breakage occurs after atom rearrangements. (2) Shear band initiation is size dependent and can cause stochastic or deterministic size effect, depending on the loading condition (indentation versus microcompression) (3) Shear band initiation is rate dependent. The rate dependence is due to the stress dependence of viscosity of the supercooled metallic liquid. On a theoretical basis, the stress, pressure and temperature-dependence of the liquid viscosity can be related to the dynamic heterogeneity in supercooled liquids. Part of the funding of this project was also used to partly support the training of two PhD students and attendance of several international conferences. With the support of this GRF, we published 15 papers, from 2016 to 2019.

11207215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207215.value: In my opinion, the further development of the research would be on the design of metallic glasses with a better resistance to shear band initiation and damage initiation. In light of the mechanisms we identified, we could develop metallic glasses which can resist shear band formation/instability upon mechanical loading.

11207215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207215.value: Amorphous metals, or metallic glasses, are alloys without a crystalline structure. They are also called frozen liquids because they are usually obtained by rapid quenching of metallic melts through their glass transition point. At room temperature, they are strong because of the lack of crystalline defects; however, how damage initiates or yielding occurs remains elusive. In this project, we carried out a systematic study by combining experiments, simulations and theories to understand the thermodynamic and micromechanical origin of yielding and damage initiation in this type of materials.

11207615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207615.value: Information theory (Shannon theory) is important to engineered networks as it tells us a set of "physical laws" that all communication or storage systems must obey regardless of the design of the system. Information inequalities (Shannon-type inequalities) are important to derive these physical laws. They are fundamental in information theory as well as in other related mathematical subjects, e.g., probability theory. The basis of systematically verifying valid information inequalities was crystalized and laid down in a 1997 seminal work by R. W. Yeung, in which he developed a linear programming framework to verify linear information inequalities. This leads to a computer-aided approach to verify information inequalities using the Information Theoretic Inequality Prover (ITIP), which is a widely-used state-of-the-art software package. Recently, we discovered that, beyond merely verification of inequalities, this linear programming framework can be used to explicitly construct an analytic proof of an information inequality or an analytic counterexample to disprove it if the inequality is not true in general. Unfortunately, there are severe limitations in the ITIP software. Firstly, it cannot handle many of the large problem settings arising in information theory and network coding problems (the size of the linear program grows exponentially with the problem size). For example, ITIP is not fast enough to solve a problem involving more than 10 random variables that is very common in network coding for distributed storage. Secondly, the ITIP only verifies an inequality but it does not provide a mathematical proof. A proof or counterexample is important because it can provide engineers insights to designing an optimal system. Thirdly, it cannot handle a broader class of information inequalities known as the non-Shannon-type inequalities. Our recent discovery and work thus open the door to new computational approaches to automate the search for new information inequalities that are useful to network information theory. We will be leveraging the modern theories and tools of convex optimization and distributed computation to develop the next-generation ITIP software that can solve large-scale problems. To scale up computing, we will exploit optimization decomposition theory and cloud computing resource allocation optimization to automate the search for an analytic proof or counterexample. We expect the software developed in the project to be widely used in the information theory community for a long time. The impact of this project is even larger on its novelty in Automated Theorem Proving in computer science as well as solving challenging practical network applications. 信息论（香农理论）对网络工程设计是非常重要的，因为信息论提供的“物理规律”是所有的通信或存储系统都必须服从的。信息不等式（香农不等式）是建立这些“物理规律”中的工具。信息不等式在数学中例如概率论也是非常重要的。 Raymond Yeung 在1997年开创了一个线性规划的数学框架来系统地核实有效的信息不平等式以验证线性信息的不平等规定，并且还开发信息论不等式证明器（ITIP）。这个软件在学术界中被广泛使用。我们最近发现这套线性编程数学框架可以用来显式地构造一个信息不平等的数学证明或分析反驳它的反例解析。这意味着计算机可以自动化验证信息不等式。 不过，ITIP软件存在严重的问题。首先，它不能处理许多在信息理论所产生的网络编码问题（庞大的线性程序问题）。因此，ITIP不能够有效解决涉及超过10个随机变量的网络编码或存储的问题。其次，ITIP仅仅验证一个不等式，而不能够提供数学证明。一个数学证明或反例是非常重要的。第三，它不能处理更广泛的类被称为非香农不等式。我们的发现和工作缔造新的计算方法来自动化寻找新的信息不平等式。我们将充分利用凸优化和分布式计算工具来开发下一代ITIP软件来解决庞大型的网络编码问题。此外，我们将扩大计算规模有效的利用最优化分解理论和云计算资源优化配置自动化地提供数学证明或反例。

11207615.value: We have published in four top-tiered peer-reviewed journals and two top conferences in the field based on the achievement of the four objectives where we developed mathematical theories for proving and disproving information inequalities by linear programming and develop algorithms for finding the shortest proof or the smallest counterexample automatically by machine, scale up computation using Lagrange duality and optimization decomposition theory, optimize virtual machine resource allocation in cloud computing to enable automated proof checking by the software implementation and also conduct extensive experiments with the cloud computing software. Lastly, we have considered a few applications of algorithms and software to problems in probability theory.

11207615.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207615.value: Our research outcome and findings can be summarized as follows. We make major findings the use of linear programming for proving and disproving information inequalities using proximal methods in the IEEE ISIT 2019 conference paper, demonstrating a new way to solve gigantic linear programs, thus satisfying Objective 1 and 2. And we have demonstrated how this technique and software tool can aid in the scientific discovery of information inequalities relevant to some problems in probability theory and classical information-theoretic cryptography and network coding related to a large number of random variables and problem-specific constraints, with both work respectively published in IEEE Transactions on Communications and IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications in 2018. In both work, we showed that optimization techniques that leverage the problem-specific constraints can be incorporated in the proving and disproving of information inequalities, thus satisfying Objective 2 and 4. Also, our research outcomes have made contributions on how large-scale optimization algorithms can be developed in cloud computing as shown in the 2016 IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering, contributing to efficient methodologies to optimize machine resource allocation in cloud computing satisfying Objective 3. Our work in 2016 SIGMETRICS and Journal on Selected Areas in Communications 2017 study how to develop a novel cloud virtual service mechanism that enables a large group of users to access the service related to scalable computation. In both our SIGMETRICS 2016 and our JSAC 2017 paper, we studied the economics of computation with utility maximization and optimization-theoretic algorithms, showing that some form of robust incentive mechanism are needed for scalable computation. We have conducted extensive experiments with the use of cloud computing for solving large-scale optimization problems, satisfying Objectives 2 and 3. This mechanisms are important when we open up the AITIP software infrastructure freely-accessible on the Internet to any user in the world who wants to discover proofs or validate information-theoretic inequalities.

11207615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207615.value: There is great potential for further developing the research to apply to other scientific areas beyond classical information theory applications. For example, we recently found that quantum computing and quantum cryptography also relies on examining new information inequalities. Also, machine learning applications such as deep learning can be analyzed using information theory tools and thus our research work should be extended to address these new challenges. The development of novel cloud virtual service mechanism that enables high workload need to be further developed.

11207615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207615.value: Information theory (Shannon theory) is important to discovery of "physical laws" that all communication or storage systems must obey regardless of the system design. Information inequalities (Shannon-type inequalities) are important to derive these physical laws. We have built on a 1997 work by R. W. Yeung, whereby linear programming is used to verify linear information inequalities and developing a computer-aided approach called the AITIP software, which is a Software-as-a-Service driven by cloud computing. Our research shows how to construct analytic proofs of information inequality or an analytic counterexample to disprove it if it is untrue by solving gigantic linear programs. Our research demonstrated how new discoveries can be made in classical information theory such as secure asymmetric multilevel diversity coding systems and random linear network coding. Furthermore, our Software-as-a-Service AITIP on the cloud is freely-accessible to anyone in the world as an interactive theorem prover, which is of altruistic significance. The significance and value of our research are that modern theories and tools of convex optimization and distributed cloud computation can solve large-scale problems relevant to the scientific community.

11208215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208215.value: Upconversion nanoparticles are a class of luminescent nanomaterials that can convert near infrared (NIR) excitation into visible and even ultraviolet (UV) emissions. Since biological tissues display reduced absorption in the NIR spectral region, these nanoparticles have been developed as promising luminescent markers for applications ranging from molecular detection to cancer therapy. Although biolabeling with upconversion nanoparticles has become the state-of-the-art with the potential to impact fundamental biomedical research and clinical practice, it is not without limitations and complications. For example, classical upconversion nanoparticles are not useful in theranostic applications because their excitation-independent optical properties can hardly offer temporally separated diagnostic and therapeutic processes. This proposal seeks to address the problems by developing a new class of spectrum kinetic upconversion nanoparticles that show distinct optical emissions in response to excitations of different wavelengths. Specifically, we aim to realize excitation wavelength switchable visible and UV emissions for the purposes of diagnosis and therapy, respectively. A significant amount of effort will also be devoted to boosting the upconversion efficiency in the high-energy UV spectral region. Once refined, we envisage that our study will open up new opportunities for therapeutic and diagnostic imaging applications that outperform existing upconversion techniques. 由于可将生物组织吸收微弱的近红外的激发光转换为可见甚至是紫外发光，上转换纳米颗粒特别适合作为荧光标记物用于分子检测和癌症治疗等领域。目前基于上转换已经发展了一系列非常先进的生物标记技术，其对生物医学研究和临床诊断也产生了积极的推动作用。然而，现有上转换颗粒的一些固有光学性质问题制约了其进一步的发展。如传统的上转换纳米材料在治疗诊断学这一新兴应用中比较受限，因为其不依赖于激发光波长的发光性质很难提供实时分立的诊断和治疗过程。此计划书旨在设计一种新的光谱动力学上转换纳米材料以解决上述问题。此类上转换纳米材料预期能在不同波长的激发条件下会产生波长动态可控的上转换发光。我们期望做通过改变激发波长，获取可自由转换的可见及紫光发光，分别用以实现诊断和治疗。同时我们会探索新的方法用以增强深紫外波段的发光效率，以提升现有上转换技术，开启其在治疗和诊断上的新应用。

11208215.label: Realisation of objectives
11208215.value: This project focuses on the development of new compositions and core-shell nanostructures to realized distinct light/heat emissions by excitation at different wavelength for biomedical applications. We have achieved these objectives through the following deliverables. 1. We establish an oleylamine-mediated synthesis that allows quick formation (several minutes) of upconversion nanoparticles with tunable size (7-70 nm) at reduced temperatures (< 200 degree Celsius). By contrast, conventional synthesis typically requires a high reaction temperature (> 300 degree Celsius) and long reaction time (> 1 hr), yielding a large particles size (around 100 nm). By taking advantage of hot-injection and interfacial strain, we further establish a method for precise control of epitaxial growth, resulting in well-defined core-shell morphologies such as spheres, prisms, dumbbells, cones, and ribbed rods. By controlling successive hot-injection, we succeed in controlling shell thickness from sub-1 nm to more than 10 nm as well as multishelled nanostructures. 2. We demonstrate that core-shell nanostructures can be accurately characterized by high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD), coupled with theoretical simulations. We show that lattice distortion and strain distribution can be revealed by fast Fourier transform (FFT) and geometric phase analysis (GPA) of HR-TEM images. In addition, whole pattern and single peak fitting of XRD spectra are shown to precisely calculate the lattice parameters as well as strain buildup and relaxation processes. 3. By using core-shell nanostructure, we have achieved strong enhancement of upconversion luminescence by overcoming concentration quenching. By further combining the use of a microring resonator excitation platform, we have achieved intense ultraviolet emission at 380 nm by near-infrared excitation at 1550 nm through a multiphoton upconversion, with an power conversion efficiency of over 5%. 4. By controlling the concentration and distribution of lanthanide dopants in core-shell nanoparticles, we have realized rational control of optical emissions by changing the excitation wavelengths (e.g.; 254 nm, 808 nm, 980 nm, and 1550 nm) or excitation power (1.25-46.25 W cm^2). We also achieve heat generation by photon excitation at 808 nm. 5. We demonstrate sensitive DNA detection based on energy transfer between luminescent nanoparticles. The optical nanoparticles are demonstrated to kill cancer cells by generating heat or toxic radicals. The optical emissions from upconversion nanoparticles have also been harnessed to activate or inhibit neuron activities in free-moving mice. The tunable optical emission is expected to provide combinational neuron modulation.

11208215.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208215.value: We have established several wet-chemistry methods for synthesis and surface modification of various nanomaterials including metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) nanocrystals and lanthanide-doped fluoride nanocrystals. Particularly, we have proposed an oleylamine-mediated synthetic protocol that allows facile large scale synthesis of NaYbF4 nanocrystals of tunable particle size from 7-70 nm (Chem. Mater. 2019, 31, 4779). By leveraging interfacial strain in conjunction of controlled hot-injection, we have succeeded in precise modulation of epitaxial habits towards the formation of various core-shell morphologies including prism, dumbbell, cone, and satellite (Adv. Funct. Mater. 2019, 29, 1903295; Nanoscale 2018, 10, 19898). We have achieved deliberate light and heat emissions by controlling excitation wavelength. For example, we have developed a class of graphitic carbon nanocubes derived from MOF nanomaterials, which can efficiently convert 808-nm irradiation into heat with a high efficiency of 40.4% (Inorg. Chem. 2016, 55, 5750). By constructing core-shell structure, we have realized intense and broad band UV emission by 980-nm excitation (Small 2017, 13, 1701479). We also developed a class of Er-sensitized upconversion nanocrystals that show emissions spanning visible and NIR by excitation at 1532 nm (Nat. Commun. 2019, 10, 1811). Notably, we have realized tunable color outputs by excitations at different wavelengths (Nanoscale, 2017, 9, 2701) or fixed wavelength of varying excitation power (J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2016, 7, 4916). We also have realized spatially resolvable optical emissions by creating hollow structures inside crystalline materials (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2017, 56, 10383). By using the newly developed optical nanomaterials, we have demonstrated several new methods for biomedical applications. For example, the advances in material’s property have enabled an all-nanoparticle based biosensor for in vivo DNA detection (Molecules 2017, 22, 1085). By using MOF-derived graphitic carbon nanocubes, a photothermal therapy of cancer was developed under excitation of 808 nm (Inorg. Chem. 2016, 55, 5750). In addition, we have pioneered remote neuron modulation by using the upconversion nanoparticles under near infrared irradiation (Adv. Healthcare Mater. 2017, 6, 1700446; Nano Lett. 2018, 18, 948). Due to our innovative and systematical works in this field, we have been invited to contribute review papers by the Royal Chemical Society (J. Mater. Chem. B, 2018, 6, 2924) and the Asian Chemical Editorial Society (Chem. Asian J. 2018, 13, 373). Our work has been extensively cited by the community and the PI has been named a Highly Cited Researcher for 2018 by Clarivate Analytics.

11208215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11208215.value: The synthetic protocol developed in this project can be tested for preparing other types of nanomaterials that are unlikely to be accessed by conventional methods. The optical materials synthesized in this project can be explored for upconversion lasing and photoacoustic bioimaging. Notably, the upconversion nanomaterials featuring temporally and spatially tunable optical emissions hold the potential for combinational optogenetic modulations.

11208215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11208215.value: Upconversion nanoparticles convert near infrared (NIR) excitation into visible and even ultraviolet (UV) emissions. Since biological tissues display reduced absorption in the NIR spectral region, these nanoparticles are promising for applications ranging from molecular detection to cancer therapy. This project has developed several methods for enhancing the upconversion efficiency and expanding the spectral tunability, thereby providing new possibilities for biological applications. For example, we can selectively generate emissions at different wavelengths by controlling the excitation wavelength, which allows for diagnosis and therapy to be conducted in an on-demand manner using a unified platform. In addition, we have achieved strong UV emissions by NIR excitation. The UV emissions are useful for activation of biological processes and photon-patterning of various samples. By using the newly developed luminescent nanomaterials, we have established several methods for DNA detection, cancer therapy, and optogenetic modulation of free-moving mice.

11208515.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11208515.value: 異質線性節點多通道有向網絡的牽制能控性和能觀性

11208515.label: Project Objectives
11208515.value: Demonstrate that the conclusion of strong structural network controllability is true for a general finite-sized directed network of identical nodes with multi-channel connections Extend the result obtained in Task 1 to a general finite-sized directed network of non-identical nodes Study the observability of the two settings described in (1) and (2), respectively Study the pinning controllability of the general setting of directed networks with multi-channel connections
rows: Demonstrate that the conclusion of strong structural network controllability is true for a general finite-sized directed network of identical nodes with multi-channel connections
Extend the result obtained in Task 1 to a general finite-sized directed network of non-identical nodes
Study the observability of the two settings described in (1) and (2), respectively
Study the pinning controllability of the general setting of directed networks with multi-channel connections

11208515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208515.value: This proposal aims to study the controllability of directed complex networks with non-identical linear node dynamics which, differing from almost all existing settings, have multi-channel connections. The main objective is to derive some precise graph-theoretic controllability conditions and criteria for such practical networks. The dual topic of network observability will also be investigated. Several basic settings and typical scenarios will be considered, including networks with identical node systems and non-identical node systems, respectively, for various complex network topologies. The problem with external pinning control input by linear state-feedback controllers is considered, to find out how many and which nodes are needed to be pinned, so as to achieve the structural controllability of a general multi-channel directed network. Four technical objectives are proposed to achieve: (1) Demonstrate that the conclusion of strong structural network controllability is true for a general finite-sized directed network of identical nodes with multi-channel connections; (2) Extend the result obtained in Task 1 to a general finite-sized directed network of non-identical nodes; (3) Study the observability of the two settings described in (1) and (2), respectively; (4) Study the pinning controllability of the general setting of directed networks with multi-channel connections 本項目旨在研究具有異質線性節點有向網絡的能控制性和能觀察性。與其它研究不同的是，這裏考慮網絡具有多通道連接。研究的主要目標是爲這些實用網絡尋找一些簡明的用圖論描述的能控性和能觀性條件和判別准則。 將會考慮幾類典型的情形，包括同質和異質節點系統的各種拓撲的網絡。對有外來牽制控制器的問題，研究有多少節點需要加以控制，以及哪些節點應該加以控制，才可以實現一般多通道有向網絡的能控性。 將會具體研究四個技術性問題：（1）驗證具有同質線性節點系統的有向多通道網絡的強結構能控制性；（2）把上一結論推廣到異質節點系統的網絡；（3）研究上述兩種網絡的能觀性；（4）研究一般有向多通道網絡的牽制能控性。

11208515.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208515.value: (1) We tested and verified that the conclusion of strong structural network controllability is indeed true for a general finite-sized directed network of identical nodes with multi-channel connections. (2) We have then extend the result obtained in Task 1 to a general finite-sized directed network of non-identical nodes. (3) We have also investigated the observability of the same networks in parallel to the controllability study. (4) We have studied the pinning controllability of the general setting of directed networks with multi-channel connections, as well as its application to networked multi-agent systems.

11208515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11208515.value: Along the same line, the investigations could be further extended and broadened to cover more realistic complex networks such as some nonlinear networks and sampled-data networks, which are equipped with digital devices in applications.

11208515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11208515.value: This project has accomplished a few tasks on the strong structural network controllability of a general finite-sized directed network with identical nodes having multi-channel connections. The major advancement in this research is to extend the existing results with single-channel connections, part of which were contributed by the PI, to multi-channel connections, which are more realistic and more useful for engineering applications.

11210015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210015.value: Airborne transmitted pathogen infection can cause various diseases and severely threaten human health and lives. In highly crowded and enclosed environments such as health-care facilities, large shopping malls, commercial buildings, and public buildings, human-generated indoor pathogens may be transmitted, dispersed, and lead to cross-infection in people through heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) systems. Infection can also affect work productivity and have a substantial economic impact. To reduce infection risk, several engineering strategies can be implemented: increasing ventilation rates, using high efficiency filtration systems, and adopting active disinfection systems. In many scenarios, the first two options are very energy costly in the long-term and are not feasible for many premises. Due to their low pressure drop, ultraviolet germicidal irradiation (UVGI) and electrical corona wire ionization have been introduced to HVAC markets as alternative technologies. Studies have demonstrated that these installations are effective in the stationary phase. However the disinfection efficacy decreases with airflow velocity. Even worse, ozone gas is generated as a by-product. Literature on measuring their disinfection efficacy for HVAC systems is rare. No systematic study has investigated how to improve and optimize these two technologies. Technical information on maximizing the performance is lacking. The project will aim to propose a feasibility study on developing an optimal, energy efficient and high efficacy in-duct disinfection system for HVAC installation under practical scenarios. The system will be hybridized by a modified UV-C and a corona pin-type ionization system. In the first stage, the UVGI and the pin ionization system will be studied alone. By designing an optical system, the irradiation zone and intensity of the UVGI lamps will be magnified and a more uniform irradiation zone will be formed. A new bipolarity pin ionization system using carbon fiber as emission tips will be fabricated. Different types of bacteria will be selected to cover a wide range of sizes. Synergetic effect will be investigated to further enhance the performance. Scanning electronic microscopy and atomic force microscopy will be used to study the disinfection mechanisms by examining cellular structure changes after exposure to the active systems. In addition, a computational tool will also be developed. The UV irradiation, air ion transport, microorganism continuity equations will be solved. The results and deliverables of this proposal will provide valuable information for future development of new methods for controlling indoor microorganisms. In the future, fewer indoor airborne pathogens can be achieved with low energy implication.

11210015.label: Realisation of objectives
11210015.value: (1) To design a new UVGI system with better efficacy by modifying the irradiation zone. This objective task was completed very satisfactory and leaded to publish of an archival paper (Indoor Air vol 28(6), 806-817, 2019). Another revised manuscript has already been resubmitted to Indoor Air after receiving comments from the reviewers. A plate and a concave mirrors were tested. The mirror was put at the bottom of the duct wall right beneath a UV-C mercury vapor lamp. Irradiation intensity was measured and the results were compared with black surface and a “control” such as the galvanized iron. A full-scale ventilation duct system was built for experimental testing. The duct was 9 m long, 200 mm wide × 200 mm high, and made of galvanized steel. Air velocities of 3, 4.5, and 6 m/s were used. Serratia marcescens, Pseudomonas alcaligenes, Escherichia coli, Salmonella enterica, and Staphylococcus epidermidis were the selected bacteria. The UV device (lamp) was installed in a ventilation duct. For controlled experiments, each challenged bacteria was tested with a 100% luminous length UVC lamp at three different velocities. When the supply air velocity reached 3 m/s, very high disinfection efficacies of tested five types of bacteria by the UV lamp were observed (nearly 100%). The results showed that the disinfection efficacies decreased with increasing airflow velocity from 3 m/s to 6 m/s. It was observed that the efficacy of the duct with black surface was low, probably because it produced very low or no UV reflection. There is an important practical implication: particles deposited on a poorly maintained duct surface might cause it to turn black and decrease the performance of the originally designed UV system. For modified irradiation zone experiment using mirrors, the challenged bacteria was E. coli. We found that the disinfection efficacies of airborne bacteria by the UVGI system under mirrored conditions were obviously higher than that under black surface conditions. Compared with non-surface reflectance for the UV light, the enhanced spatial irradiances in the ventilation duct were also observed by the use of mirrors. In summary, using mirrors or high reflectivity materials can be regarded as a good and applicable approach to improve disinfection performance of UVGI system through enhancing the reflection of the UV light within the concerned space. (2) To design a high efficacy corona pin ionization system utilizing bipolarity ions with low ozone emissions. The objective was successfully achieved, which led to the publication of two papers in Building and Environment (vol 127, pg 204-210, 2018; vol 158, pg 295-301, 2019) An experimental system with one positive and one negative ionizers was designed and tested. Two environmental conditions were considered, RH and temperature, which were tested at the lower, middle, and higher levels, corresponding to 50%, 70%, and 90% for RH and 17.5°C, 21°C, and 25°C for temperature. The concentration of ions and disinfection efficacy were measured and correlated. This study involves two phases. In the first phase, both positive and negative ionizers were tested independently. In general, the positive ionizer showed better disinfection performance than the negative ionizer by 29 to 41%. Increasing the velocity from 3.0 to 6.5 m/s yielded a reduction in the disinfection efficiencies of positive ionizer from 88.5% to 44.0%, 49.0% to 38.7%, and 35.1% to 19.8% for E. coli, S. typhimurium, and S. epidermidis, respectively. For the negative ionizer, the disinfection efficiencies reduced from 62.9% to 35.4%, 54.2% to 30.0%, and 42.9% to 30.2% for E. coli, S. typhimurium, and S. epidermidis, respectively. In the second phase, only the positive ionizer was further tested at three relative humidity. From 50% to 90% relative humidity, the disinfection efficiencies decreased from 46.0% to 23.6%, 35.2% to 22.5%, and 24.8% to 20.7%, for E. coli, S. typhimurium, and S. epidermidis, respectively. At the same time, the efficacy of the ionizer increased as temperature decreased. The ozone emission rates of both ionizers were measured in the duct and found to be very small and the estimated emission rate was 0.63 mg/hr. (3) To optimize the operation of this hybridized system and maximize the synergistic effects. This objective (3) was also satisfactorily accomplished. A manuscript is ready to be submitted to Building and Environment by 2019 December. The experimental system was similar to the one described for objective (2) above. The results showed that E. coli and S. typhimurium were more susceptible to ions (positive or negative) than S. epidermidis. Also, there was no significant difference between the killing effects of one positive ionizer and two positive ionizers as well as one negative and two negative ionizers for all three bacteria. Although we concluded that no synergistic effect occurred between polarity of air ions, further experiments may be needed to verify this claim. After completing the first two objectives (2) and (3), the UV-C tube and ionizers were also combined in a hybrid system. While we observed a synergistic effect for S. epidermidis under the combining impact of ionizer and UV lamp in relation to individual effects, no synergistic effect was observed for E. coli and S. typhimurium. (4) To develop a computational numerical model for simulating disinfection performance for systems developed in (1), (2) and (3). The objective was completed satisfactory. For modeling the inactivation rate of in-duct UV lamps, we developed a new mathematical model to predict the spatial irradiance based on the view factor approach. In the ventilation duct, the spatial irradiance of a grid cell from an in-duct lamp was calculated as the sum of emissive irradiance directly from the UVC lamp and the diffuse reflection from the duct walls. The emissive irradiance was then saved in the grid cell memory, and the value of calculated emissive irradiance in the first spatial grid cell adjacent to the duct wall was treated as the energy source of the diffuse reflection. When the viewpoint located in a spatial grid cell, the diffuse reflection from each wall face grid cell was calculated with the algebraic combination using the view factor method. Finally, the total irradiance of each point of the flow field was obtained by summing the emissive irradiance and diffuse reflection irradiance at this point. The developed UV irradiance model was accurate. The modelled emissive irradiance was directly validated by the measured emissive irradiance. The model also was employed to predict the irradiance and disinfection performance of in-duct UV lamps when different duct wall materials or modified irradiance zone were involved. The results indicate that although the change in the diffuse irradiance is slight when different duct wall materials are used, the duct wall reflection has considerable effect on the disinfection. (4) SEM and AFM The objective was completed. Scanning Electron Microscopic (SEM) images for bacteria before and after the exposure of UV-C were also taken. Atomic Force Microscopic (AFM) images are also completed. From the current SEM images, it can be seen that the membrane of the bacteria were disrupted under exposure of air ions. Preliminary results of AFM showing an interesting observation. The images suggest that UV radiation penetrates to the inner of the cell and causes damage to the DNA.

11210015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210015.value: The work is completed very successfully. We understand more fundamental issues which can help us to further develop a better in-duct disinfection device. Since the UV irradiance generally decreases with the distance from the device and a lower irradiance for the places far away from the device means lower disinfection efficacy, the disinfecting pathogen would become difficulty if the ventilation duct is very larger than the designed device. Nevertheless, an increase in the size of UV devices will naturally increase their performance but additional pressure drops may be occurred. From the perspective of energy-efficient air-conditioning systems and sustainable buildings, any improved in-duct cleaning/disinfection devices should not only involve the high performance for the pathogen sterilization, but also concern less pressure drop or smaller fanning energy consumption induced. When the pressure penalty and the disinfection are considered simultaneously, the overall evaluation index is necessarily needed for comparing and maximizing the hydraulic-pathogen disinfection performance of in-duct devices. These issues should be further explored for developing in-duct air cleaner. The current UVC device is good but with the advancement of electronic technology, the device can be made even smaller. Also the PI is conducting more experiments to test more pathogens to establish a larger database.

11210015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210015.value: We conducted both laboratory experiments and numerical simulations of various aspects of air disinfection of a custom-made ventilation duct. During this work, it was intended to understand the disinfection efficacy of UVC lamps and ionizers (positive and negative). The outcomes of our research project would significantly contribute to a reduction in the cost of healthcare due to disease outbreak and improve human productivity. This study resulted in a better understanding of factors that influence the disinfection performance of UVC and air ionization against microorganisms in ventilation ducts. UV irradiation and air ionization could significantly inactivate bacteria, but one of our most important discoveries was that bioaerosols differ in their vulnerability to air ions and UV irradiation. This discovery aided us to understand that the some bacteria which were most difficult to kill, could be successfully disinfected through the hybridization of UVC and air ions. Another useful finding was that flow rate, relative humidity and temperature could significantly dictate the performance of these air disinfection methods. Therefore, a clearer understanding of factors affecting the efficacy of these air disinfection methods and their synergy is a necessary step towards enhancing good indoor air quality.

11210315.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11210315.value: 機器人輔助單細胞手術作業系統的研究

11210315.label: Project Objectives
11210315.value: Development of microwell array based cell manipulation tools for cell patterning and vision sensing. The automation of cell surgery requires the development of a microfluidic chip based cell processing system that will permit multiple suspended cells to be positioned for cell surgery. Additionally, organelles, and nuclei removed from cells with the system must also be patterned for subsequent processing. To achieve this, we will develop a microwell array microfluidic device to allow accurate positioning and patterning of a number of mammalian cells for cell surgery, controlled by vision guided tweezers manipulators. Closed-loop control for reorientation of suspended cells using vision feedback and laser tweezers input. Cell surgery is hampered by the fact that there are many membrane structures, cytoskeletons, and other organelles which obstruct access from the upper hemisphere of the suspended cell, the only available access direction. Hence, the suspended cell must be reoriented. After imaging the internal three dimensional structure of the cell, the cell will be reoriented using optical tweezers manipulators. While access to the cell may be obtained by reorientation in only two rotational coordinate directions, through variation of the relative position of the laser traps, the cell can be reoriented in three angular coordinate dimensions, hence exposing the area of interest. This process will be carried out automatically under closed-loop control, using vision feedback. Cell surgery application: robot-aided somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT). The proposed robotic single cell surgery system will be applied to SCNT, a complex single cell surgery task. With the cell reoriented to access specific features, laser scissors will be used to perforate the cell wall, under automatic control with vision feedback. Images processing technique will be used to identify specific feature within the cell, determining the cell feature coordinates, permitting the cell to be reoriented for a perforation to be made. Vision feedback will be utilized to identify the nucleus for removal, and to provide the coordinates for the tweezers manipulators to trap and remove the nucleus through the perforation, for implantation in another cell. The nucleus is then transferred into the enucleated oocyte to reprogram the somatic nucleus and hence develop an embryo which has the same epigenetics as the somatic cell donor. This proposed procedure is sufficiently complex to demonstrate the single cell surgical techniques.

11210315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210315.value: Enabled by new sophisticated research tools, investigations into single cell behavior have been carried out over the last several years. While great strides have been recently made in the development of these research tools and techniques, much work is left to do. The advent of highly sophisticated tools to assist with micro-scale biological task execution, such as robot-aided optical tweezers, has created new opportunities for ground breaking research in the investigation of biological cells and other objects at the micro/nano-scale. The opportunity exists to create even more powerful cell testing and evaluation tools through the introduction of established principles of automation to this new and exciting biological testing field. In this proposal, we propose to develop a robotic system for single cell surgery. The system will be based on a microfluidic system to pattern cells, sophisticated robotically controlled optical tweezers with the capability to independently control many optical traps, coupled with an integrated optical scissors. Through vision based feedback control, the system will enable numerous tasks to be executed for cell surgery, such as patterning cells in a microwell array device, re-orienting cells for perforation, perforating cells and extracting cell organelles. We will then demonstrate the performance of such a robotic single cell surgery system by evaluating a test procedure, e.g., somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT). SCNT is a widely used method to clone animals, e.g., sheep, pig, bovine, mice and so on. The nucleus is transferred into the enucleated oocyte to reprogram the somatic nucleus and hence develop an embryo which has the same epigenetics as the somatic cell donor. This development will provide a new robotic approach with greater throughput and higher success rates compared with manual techniques. Procedures carried out manually introduce uncertainty due to human operator variability, leading to uncertainty in the results obtained. The development of robotic single cell surgical task implementation has the potential to remove human operator variation from these complex biological processes, leading to more consistent results, higher throughput and greater cell survival rates. 此專案致力於研究用於單細胞手術的機器人作業系統。該系統基於微流技術實現細胞陣列，機器人輔助光鑷技術實現各類複雜的單細胞操作，以及光剪技術實現細胞的精密切割。通過視覺回饋控制，該系統可實現服務於細胞手術的各類操作，如細胞排列，細胞旋轉，細胞切割及摘取細胞內的物質等。作為應用例子，將進一步研究如何用此細胞手術作業系統實現細胞核的互換。

11210315.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210315.value: In this project, we developed a robotic system for single cell surgery. The research was conducted in the following three aspects. First, we developed a microwell array based vision-guided optical tweezers cell manipulation system that can achieve efficient cell transportation for patterning. An artificial first-order kinematic model of the tweezers was considered in the controller design to reduce controller oscillation. An automated method based on the drag force model and gradient descent optimization was presented to calibrate cell dynamics online. Simultaneous automated transportation of multiple cell types was also investigated. A control constraint was introduced to confine the offset of cells within the optical trap to prevent cells from escaping the trap during transportation. Experiments were performed on the transportation of yeast cells and osteoblast-like MC3T3-E1 cells to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in cell patterning for cell surgery applications. Second, we developed a closed-loop control for reorientation of suspended cells using vision feedback and laser tweezers input. Orientation control of biological cell is a basic and vital technique required in cell surgery procedures, which is typically carried out with manual operations. In this study, we utilized two optical traps, generated by robotically controlled holographic optical tweezers, as two special manipulators to manipulate the cell for out of image plane rotation. By utilizing the T-matrix approach and experimental calibration, the relationship between the relative vertical height of the optical traps and the rotational angle was characterized. A visual feedback controller was further developed to rotate the cell to the pre-determined orientation accurately. Experiments are performed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Third, we performed cell surgery applications with the developed cell manipulation system. With the developed robotic optical tweezers system, we fused the hepatocellular carcinoma cells and human embryonic stem cells (hESC) to reprogram somatic cells to a pluripotent state, and also studied the adhesion between leukemia cells and stromal cells, as well as the interaction between leukemia cells and adhesion molecules. We further performed the experiments on small suspended (NB4 ~18 µm) and adherent cells (HDF ~20 µm), in which the mitochondria and nucleus were biopsied using the proposed system and methodology. The experimental results have shown that the developed system can automatically perform organelle extraction with high precision and repeatability, thereby reducing human fatigue and error involved in complex single cell biopsy procedures.

11210315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210315.value: The developed robotic single cell surgery system can be further applied to perform mitochondria transfer and injection, cell injection, preimplantation genetic diagnosis and cloning. Furthermore, the proposed robotic manipulation tools with optical tweezers can be used for cell fusion and drug assessment at the single cell level.

11210315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210315.value: In this project, we developed a robotic system for single cell surgery, on the basis of a microfluidic system to pattern cells, and sophisticated robotically controlled optical tweezers with the capability to independently control many optical traps. Through vision based feedback control, the system enabled numerous tasks to be executed for cell surgery, such as patterning cells in a microwell array device, re-orienting cells for perforation, extracting cell organelles for biopsy. We demonstrated the performance of such a robotic single cell surgery system through numerous experiments, including cell fusion, cell adhesion characterization, as well as cell organelle biopsy such as mitochondria and nucleus biopsy on single cells. This development will provide a new robotic approach with greater throughput and higher success rates compared with manual techniques.

11211015.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11211015.value: 纳米复合材料的强化作用和变形机制

11211015.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11211015.value: Prof Liao, Xiaozhou Dr Lu, Chunsheng Prof Shen, Yao-gen

11211015.label: Project Objectives
11211015.value: To quantify the relationships between hardness, grain size, amorphous volume fraction, and mechanical deformation of nanocomposite TiC-C films fabricated by using close-field un-balanced magnetron sputtering and ion plating (CFUBMSIP) by systematically varying process parameters; To understand the mechanism of strengthening by observing deformation processes during the deformation of TiC-C with grain sizes in the range of 5−20 nm using a combination of in situ tensile straining and in situ nanoindentation in a high-resolution TEM; To correlate mechanical properties with the local structural feature and deformation mechanisms at nanometer and sub-nanometer resolutions through simultaneous in situ nanoindentation high-resolution force-displacement measurement and TEM imaging; and To conduct atomic-scale MD simulations to probe the influence of microstructures on mechanical behaviors and develop corresponding deformation models.

To understand the mechanism of strengthening by observing deformation processes during the deformation of TiC-C with grain sizes in the range of 5−20 nm using a combination of in situ tensile straining and in situ nanoindentation in a high-resolution TEM;

To correlate mechanical properties with the local structural feature and deformation mechanisms at nanometer and sub-nanometer resolutions through simultaneous in situ nanoindentation high-resolution force-displacement measurement and TEM imaging; and
To conduct atomic-scale MD simulations to probe the influence of microstructures on mechanical behaviors and develop corresponding deformation models.

11211015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211015.value: 纳米过渡金属碳化物复合材料已很好地建立， 并且已经深入得到研究。与他们传统的微米级（粗粒度）同行相比，这些纳米材料具有其显着的特性，如高硬度，优异断裂韧性，低摩擦系数，氧化增强抵抗力，增强的耐磨性和抗裂。这些优异的性能部分归功于其独特的变形机制。在一般情况下，人们相信纳米复合材料具有与粗粒同行不同的变形机制，而这些机制是由通过纳米结构的稳定性，晶界和界面所确定。最近，纳米碳化钛/碳（TiC-C)复合材料的力学加强和变形引起的堆垛层错已报道。然而，在纳米级上的原子机制和纳米结构变形的关系背后的优异的力学性能基本上还未得到直接的实验验证，进而严重阻碍了纳米结构的TiC-C复合材料的设计和优化具有优越的力学性能。 通过国际合作的综合实验和模拟工作，这个项目的目标是在高分辨率透射电镜 (high-resolution transmission electron microscopy) 内应用原位的拉伸应变 (in situ tensile straining) 和纳米压痕技术 (in situ nanoindentation) 以及原子尺度的分子动力学模拟(atomic-scale molecular dynamics simulations)，揭示纳米TiC-C复合材料的强化效应，揭开其变形机制以及确定触发变形的纳米结构。从这项研究中获得的结果，对于了解纳米复合材料的变形行为，指导TiC-C的结构设计和加强材料的高韧性/延展性，具有重要意义。这项研究又将对小批量材料的力学行为激励进一步的实验和模拟研究。
