11211015.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211015.value: The original Principal Investigator (PI),Prof. Shen, was retired in the summer of 2018, and Dr. M. HUA was named as PI when Prof. Shen was retiring. In this project we have combined experimental synthesis, structural characterization, and mechanical testing of nanostructured composite TiC-C films. The nanostructured TiC-C films were fabricated on Si(100) wafers (for structural and mechanical measurements) and high-speed-steel (HSS) substrates (for tribological analysis) by un-balanced close-field magnetron sputtering ion plating (UBCFMSIP, Teer Film Limited UDP 650 & UDP 450). A Ti/TiC/TiCN graded interlayer was introduced between substrate and film to improve adhesion. A dc-biased, unbalanced magnetron sputter source was operated under conditions of intense Ar-ion plating. The Ti metal layer improves coating adhesion and increases strength of the coating by serving as a barrier to crack formation and propagation. The average crystalline grain size, grain morphology, grain orientation, and amorphous boundary thickness were adjusted through properly controlling the TiC-C growth conditions including Ti and C target currents, Ar sputtering gas pressure, negative bias voltage, and Si substrate temperature, etc. Films with average equiaxed grain sizes in the range of 5-20 nm and with columnar structures having aspect ratios of length to cross-sectional diameter 2-10 and the diameters of 5-20 nm, and amorphous boundary thickness of 1-5 nm were grown.

11211015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211015.value: From the findings and research outcome, it can be seen that the influences are rather complex and they are materials and/or processing dependence. Systematic and logical investigations on specific material and effect due to its processing is advantageous, and followed by various materials, is surely contributed greatly to the production of special purpose materials for the use in engineering and technological developments. Furthermore, it is felt that the use of adequate MD in simulations facilitates the visualization of mechanisms involved in resulting in different purpose materials for specific application in various technical applications.

11211015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211015.value: Via the studies on different materials being processed differently with the use of TEM, typically: barium titanate with oxygen vacancy, Ni2MnAl, CaHPO4 filmed with bioglass solutions, composition and pressu-induced relaxor ferroelectrics, BaPb(1-x)BixO3 and Ba(1-x)KxBiO3 perovskites, amorphous silicon carbide thin film, aluminum and tinanium dnder ultrasonic assisted compression, metallic multilayers integrated with Hall-Petch relation and atomistic simulation, comparative study of mechanical and microstructural behaviors of aluminum and titanium under ultrasonic assisted compression, and the study of interfacial layers, and etc., it allows the deduction of the effect of oxygen in crevices of grain boundaries due to different levels of temperature being identified, Results suggest that situating gas elements in the crevices of different grains tends to expand voids/porosities, hence weakening the materials. Maintaining material strength, it requires to alleviate such gas elements in the materials wherever possible. Also the mechanisms affecting to the mechanical properties of materials in macro and micro scales been clarified. The clarification of such mechanisms facilitates the engineering of special purpose materials used in engineering and technological developments. The studies also provide the understanding of mechanisms relevant to hardness of materials, and interfacial interlayers bonding. The finding allows the providence of accomplishing hard materials and techniques in filming and coating of materials so as to improve their services conditions. It is felt that more detail MD simulations need to be performed so as to explore various materials fabrication techniques.

11211215.label: Project Objectives
11211215.value: To investigate the fatigue mechanism of a biomimetic ceramics/FGM/nano-composite. The structure is inspired by the superior fatigue resistance demonstrated in natural structures and has potential to provide enhanced fatigue life comparing to ceramic/non-FGM/nano-composite multilayers. To investigate 3-D fatigue crack growth process with multi-scale mechanical experiments and to analyze the crack driving force with both theoretical modeling and FEA. To evaluate local heterogeneity of nano-composites with a novel AFM assisted dynamic indentation experiments. Since degree of local heterogeneity is highly related to size and dispersion status of the nano-particle clusters, this study provides in-depth mechanism of toughening and/or weakening mechanism of nano-particle reinforced polymer composites. To develop a hybrid damage accumulation model which capture the fatigue behavior of ceramics/FGM/nano-composite. The model will then be backtested and validated by compared with the experimental results.

11211215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211215.value: 大自然運用多層結構來抗疲勞。牙齒、骨頭和毛發都是抗疲勞的天然多層結構。更神奇的是，大自然的設計理念是提高構型在裂紋已存在情況下的疲勞壽命，而非杜絕裂紋的產生。師法自然，人們研發了由陶瓷/復合材料組成的多層結構。並寄望該結構可以兼顧材料的可以集剛韌於一體來抗疲勞。但是，雖然已被廣泛采用，陶瓷/復合材料多層結構仍然無法達到天然多層結構的抗疲勞性能。問題來自於幾個方面。首先，天然多層結構的界面阻止裂紋擴展，而人造多層結構的界面產生和加速裂紋擴展。其次，由於機械、化學和物理各方面的問題，制造單層的抗疲勞材料已經很難，更遑論多層。最後，如眾所周知，疲勞研究復雜、耗時，並且高成本。 本項目旨在從損傷力學和結構材料科學的角度研究上述問題。首先，制作陶瓷/功能梯度材料/納米復合材料構成的多層仿生結構，並且研究其在赫茲接觸載荷下的疲勞行為。功能梯度材料的作用是減少陶瓷頂層和納米復合材料基底之間的應力集中。接下來，通過多尺度實驗探究每一單層的疲勞性能和失效機理。最後，結合顯微表征、有限元輔助失效分析以及損傷力學建模，深入探尋多層及各單層結構的疲勞機理。 本項目的重要性體現在以下幾個方面。首先，引進仿生的功能梯度層來提高人造多層結構的總體疲勞壽命。其次，觀測並表征陶瓷/功能梯度材料/納米復合材料多層結構中的復雜三維裂紋演化過程。接下來，結合多尺度實驗和有限元分析，研究各單層的疲勞行為。開展基於原子力顯微鏡的納米壓痕實驗，及一系列其它宏微觀實驗，探尋納米復合材料的增韌機理。最後，建立一個新的混合型損傷模型來描述疲勞行為。該模型在經過實驗驗證後將被用於預測結構的剩余壽命。從長遠考慮，本項目可以為設計新型多層仿生結構提供指導。

11211215.label: Realisation of objectives
11211215.value: 1. A biomimetic ceramics/FGM/substrate structure, which was inspired by the superior fatigue resistance demonstrated in natural structures, was fabricated, examined by mechanical test and investigated for fatigue behavior and mechanism by finite element analysis (FEA) assisted Goodman diagram. Mechanical testing results show that the biomimetic structure has higher failure strength than the conventional ceramic/non-FGM/substrate structure. FEA assisted Goodman diagram analysis suggests that biomimetic structure is likely to have longer fatigue life than conventional structure. FEA demonstrated that FGM reduces stress concentration in ceramic layer. Biomimetic structure is therefore able to provide enhanced strength and fatigue life comparing to conventional structure. 2. Investigated 3-D fatigue crack growth process with 3-point bending experiments associated with in-situ video system. Deformation and fracture mechanism was studied by both theoretical modeling and FEA. 3. Evaluated effect of local heterogeneity of nano-composites with both experiment and FEA. Since degree of local heterogeneity is highly related to size and dispersion status of the nano-particle clusters, this study provided in-depth mechanism of toughening and/or weakening mechanism of nano-particle reinforced polymer composites. 4. Developed a hybrid computational/analytical model which capture the deformation, damage accumulation and fatigue behavior of FGM structure. The model was validated by comparing with experimental results. 5. 4 peer-reviewed publications arising directly from this research project are in preparation. 2 invited talks and 1 oral presentation were delivered in recognized international conferences in which papers related to this research project were delivered. 1 Ph.D. student and 2 undergraduate students have been trained and 1 Ph.D. student is in training process by conducting research arising directly from this research project. 1 US patent application was aroused directly from this research project. Research collaboration has been carried out between PI of this project and Professor Lifeng Wang at Stony Brook University in USA. 6. Due to a physical injury of PI (hospitalized and home-rested for 5 months from mid-October 2019 to mid-April 2020) and COVID-19 pandemic (PhD student Bo XU was quarantined in Mainland and Hong Kong for 3 months from late January to mid-April because his hometown is Wuhan. The contact of the research assistant Huanyun JI, whose hometown is also around Wuhan, has been lost from November 2019.), journal publication of this project is somehow delayed. Yet, given the current progress and the return to work of PI and Bo XU in late-April 2020, we are confident that the documentation will be wrapped up by the end of 2020. PI have following plan on journal publications and promise to send updated publication records to RGC in following time frame: August 31st 2020: at least 3 of the 4 journal drafts listed in item 8 of Part C will be in review. December 31st 2020: 2-4 journal drafts listed in item 8 of Part C are published.

11211215.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211215.value: 1. A biomimetic glass/FGM/substrate structure was fabricated. The structure was inspired by the failure resistant biological structures and can be utilized in many different applications in everyday life. In this project, it was utilized as a mechanical equivalence of large screen smartphone. The structure was developed and validated by large scaled FEA (more than 400k quadratic solid elements) and experimental data extracted from commercially available data released by renowned smartphone manufacturers, fabricated with commercially available smartphone materials, studied by 3-point bending test for failure resistance, characterized by in-situ video recording system, optical microscope, scanning electron microscope (SEM) and Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) for cracking process and fracture surfaces, and investigated by FEA for fracture resistance and by finite element analysis (FEA) assisted Goodman diagram for fatigue resistance. This work is comprehensive in both methods and findings. It covers objectives 1, 2 and 4. The findings were documented as the items 8.3, 8.4, 9.2, 10.2, 11.1 and 11.2 in Part C. 2. Evaluated effect of local heterogeneity of nano-composites with both atomic force microscope experiment and FEA. Since degree of local heterogeneity is highly related to size and dispersion status of the nano-particle clusters, this study provided in-depth mechanism of toughening and/or weakening mechanism of nano-particle reinforced polymer composites. This work covers objective 3. The findings were documented as the items 8.1, 9.1, 9.2, 9.3 10.1 and 11.2 in Part C. 3. Investigated fatigue behavior of a 10-layer composites with graded, alternating and monotonic mechanical properties along thickness direction. The materials, nanoparticle contents, dimensions and weights of all three composites are all the same. 3-point bending fatigue experiments were conducted on all three types of composites. Biomimetic graded composite showed superior fatigue behavior than the alternating and monotonic composites. Fatigue mechanism was investigated by both analytical model and FEA. This work covers objective 2. The findings were documented as the items 8.2, 9.1 and 10.3 in Part C.

11211215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211215.value: Nature develops graded structure which has superior fracture and fatigue resistance. In this project, novel layer-by-layer biomimetic structure with graded mechanical properties was developed by learning from nature. The graded structure was fabricated with newly invented methods, investigated for the performance when both standing alone and being applied between two other dissimilar materials, and demonstrated superior than its conventional counterpart under both monotonic and cyclic loading. Then, stress concentration and deformation mechanism of the new structure acquired from experiments were investigated with computational simulation and analytical modeling. State-of-the-art instrument were adopted to characterize the composition, microstructure and distribution of mechanical property of the newly developed graded structure and fracture surfaces and crack paths of fractured specimens. In addition, computational and analytical models validated by experimental results were utilized to provide mechanical design for the next generation structures. The project outputs can benefit development of layer-by-layer structure for versatile engineering devices.

11211815.label: Realisation of objectives
11211815.value: The main objective of this project is to investigate the temporal composition and diversity of bacteria associated with air, surfaces and occupant skins in 19 households in Hong Kong using amplicon sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene. The mechanisms and extent bacteria are transmitted between air, surface and occupant skin microbiomes are determined and quantified. All objectives in this proposal have been successfully achieved. Specifically, in Objective 1, we elucidated the taxonomic composition and diversity of the bacterial communities present in household air, surfaces and occupant skins over four seasons. We further identified attributes associated with the occupant and the household that influenced the dynamics of the skin bacterial communities, which subsequently influenced the air and surface microbiomes of the households. Through network analysis, we found that there were complex interactions between bacteria and their fungal counterpart on skins. Subsequently, in Objective 2, we developed a mechanistic framework to describe and quantify the transmission of bacteria between air, surfaces and skins in households. We found that the stability of the bacterial communities varied significantly over time depending whether there is replenishment or transfer of bacteria from external sources to the sink. We showed significant turnover of the bacterial communities occurred on a seasonal timescale. Overall, through this study, we have gained insights into the bacterial communities that are present in the residential built environments in Hong Kong. The results are useful to building managers and health practitioners to develop healthy built environments in the densely populated city of Hong Kong in the future. As part of the education plan of this study, we have trained a number of undergraduate students on molecular techniques, bioinformatics and building science.

11211815.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211815.value: The results from this project have been published in a number of journal publications (Part C). Part of the goal of Objective 1 is to examine the temporal composition and diversity of bacteria associated with air, surfaces and occupant skins in 19 households in Hong Kong over four seasons using amplicon sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene. As described in the manuscript of Wilkins et al. (2017), the household surface and occupant skin microbiomes contained microbial populations that persisted for many seasons, making up ~30% of the observed Operational Taxonomic Units (OTUs) at any time, but also contained transient OTUs that persisted for one season or shorter. On average, the contribution of the air microbiome to the surface was found to be ~17%, which was substantially less than the contribution from skin microbiome (~60%). An important investigation in Objective 1 is the potential roles household occupancy has on the extent of variation in the occupant skin microbiome and the association network structures of the microbial communities. This is especially relevant to Hong Kong as typically many people live together in a household. In the manuscript of Leung et al. (2018), we reported that the relationships between the skin microbiomes of an occupant, his/her cohabitants, and those of non-cohabitants over time were highly personal and were possibly governed by living conditions and nature of interactions between cohabitants within households over four seasons. The individualized nature of the skin microbiomes extended to various aspects of the microbial association networks, including co-occurring and excluding taxa, as well as overall network structural properties. Furthermore, household occupancy was also associated with the extent of seasonal changes in microbial diversity and composition within an occupant skin. Interestingly, the bacteria that were present on occupant skins were shown to further interact with the fungal members in the communities. Using network analysis, we showed in Leung et al. (2016b) that there were co-abundance and co-exclusion relationships between bacteria and fungi in the skin microbiomes, suggesting that changes in the relative abundance of members of one domain influenced members of another domain. The interactions that occur in the skin microbiomes between bacteria and fungi could subsequently influence the microbial populations that are transferred onto surfaces in households (reported in Objective 2). The goal of Objective 2 is to develop a mechanistic understanding of how bacteria are transferred between skin, surface and air in each of the four seasons over the course of a year in households. As reported in Wilkins et al., (2017), we found that while household surface microbiome traces could be matched to the correct occupant or occupants with 67% accuracy, accuracy decreased substantially when skin and surface samples were collected in different seasons, and particularly when surface samples were collected long after skin samples. The matching accuracy dropped to zero when the surface samples were collected three seasons apart from the skin. Most OTUs were found to persist on skin or surfaces for less than one season, indicating that OTU loss was the major cause of decreased matching accuracy. OTUs that were more useful for individual identification persisted for less time and were less likely to be deposited from skin to surface. Therefore, rate of decay and replenishment from occupants play important roles dictating the bacteria that are on household surfaces. Overall, the findings from this project enhance our fundamental understanding of the bacterial members in the indoor microbiome of Hong Kong residential environments, a unique habitat due to its high occupant density. The roles of outdoor air and occupants in shaping the indoor built environment microbiome are highlighted in our review article (Leung et al., 2016a).

11211815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211815.value: The microbiomes that are present in the built environments have important public health implications. The long-term goal is to be able to manipulate the design of the built environments to steer the microbiomes to be free of the harmful microorganisms while retaining the ones that are beneficial to occupants. To follow up on the results of this project, we have received funding from the General Research Fund of Research Grants Council to conduct a comprehensive investigation of the fungi that are present in the residential built environments and to conduct a meta-analysis to compare the microbiomes that are present in residential and commercial built environments. The two projects are currently on-going and they will further provide insights into the indoor microbiome in Hong Kong.

11211815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211815.value: Citizens living in urbanized cities typically spend 90% of their time indoors with residential homes being a primary habitat. Within the residential homes, a diverse array of microorganisms are present in air and on inanimate surfaces, while human-associated microbes are frequently transferred between the air and surfaces. In this study, culture-independent amplicon sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene was used to study the seasonal composition and diversity of bacteria associated with air, surfaces and occupant skins in 19 households in Hong Kong. In this research, we learned that the bacteria associated with skins contributed about 60% of the microbial communities found on surfaces in households. Furthermore, household occupancy influenced the seasonal changes in the diversity and composition of the bacteria on occupant skins, while the skin microbiomes of occupants are also highly personalized. Most bacteria were found to persist on skin or surfaces in households for less than one season. Overall, the results of this study enabled us to gain a deeper understanding on the bacteria present in Hong Kong households over the course of four seasons and the mechanisms of transfer between air, surface and occupant skins. The information will be useful for establishing healthy homes.

11212915.value: 2011年的福島核洩漏事件使人們重新考慮裂變核反應堆的安全性。現役的商業化核反應堆為第三代核堆。為了提高其安全性和效率，許多國家在大力發展四代核堆。美國能源部在2005年已啟動了下一代核能計劃。高溫氣體反應堆從六個中四代核堆中托湧而出，並且Idaho國家實驗室開始其興建。另外一種可行的核能是聚變技術。與裂變反應堆相比，聚變更加清潔和安全。然而，核材料的發展成為現有工程實施的挑戰。 對於核堆中使用的工程材料和包殼材料，立方結構的碳化矽是理想的選擇之一。因為在高輻照溫度下，這中材料表現出優異的抗輻照、力學和抗化學腐蝕的性能。但是，積聚的輻照缺陷會帶來不利的結構變化，如晶體到非晶結構的轉變，體積膨脹，和力學性能的降低。因此，研究此材料中輻照缺陷的產生和演變的機制極為重要。 我們將在9SDH-2 Tandem加速器上模擬核反應堆中輻照環境。在真空和高溫環境下，我們採用5MeV的矽離子對碳化矽樣品進行輻照，輻照劑量為2×1017 ion/cm2 。SRIM軟件將用來計算注入的矽離子在樣品中的分佈情況。為了避免入射的矽離子在SiC材料中積聚，我們將選擇特定厚度的外延膜和入射離子能量。 本研究的目的是研究溫度效應、表徵體積膨脹行為、以及在高輻照劑量和溫度下輻照缺陷的原子尺度結構。通過球差修正掃描透射電鏡的圖像表徵和同步輻射的平均結構信息和相關定量分析，我們可以更好研究SiC材料的輻照現象。

11212915.label: Realisation of objectives
11212915.value: The five objectives proposed in the project have been successfully achieved. In this project, several ion-irradiation experiments were conducted in the oversea institutions, including the National Tsing Hua University (Hsinchu, Taiwan) and Kyoto University (Kyoto, Japan). The post-irradiation characterizations were performed in City University of Hong Kong. The details of objectives realization were illustrated as follows: 1.Two types of promising silicon carbide (SiC) materials, named as the 3C-SiC, and SA-Tyrannohex SiC-fiber composite were investigated in this project. The pristine microstructure of as-received samples were carefully examined before irradiation. 2.The completed ion irradiation experiments could be divided into three parts. The first part is the single beam He+ irradiation with helium ion. Using 175, 225 and 275 keV of He+ formed a region that has 15000 or 45000 appm He. The two candidate materials were tested at the temperatures of 800, 1000 and 1200℃. In the second part, the single beam ion irradiation were conducted by 2.9 MeV Si2+ to 20 dpa at 40, 200℃ for 3C-SiC, and 1200℃ for SA-Tyrannohex composite. The last part is the dual beam ion irradiation with 201, 467, 737,1000 keV He+ and 5.1 MeV Si2+ at 1000 - 1350℃. The average dose in implanted area is about 100 appmHe/ 1 dpa, both materials were tested. 3.The microstructural evolution of irradiated samples was examined by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The crystalline structure of radiation induced defects were characterized. Different types of defects were identified and their size and number density were quantify through the obtained TEM images. Moreover, the lattice swelling of 3C-SiC irradiated at the low temperatures were measured by the synchrotron radiation based X ray diffraction (XRD) at the BL17B beam line of the National Synchrotron Radiation Research Center (NSRRC) in Taiwan. Importantly, the nano voids in ion irradiated 3C-SiC were observed through ABF and HAADF STEM images. A quantitative method was used to analyze HAADF images in which atomic columns with a difference in the number of atoms could be identified and scattered intensities can be computed. 4. To identify the structural nature of small radiation defects, that displayed as the black spots in the TEM image, we perform a series of simulation of a high-energy particle irradiation on a 3C-SiC at low temperature through molecular dynamic analysis. The formation mechanism of black spot defects and the evolution of defect clusters during the cascade process were examined. 5. Several graduate students and undergraduate students (for final year projects) were involved in the projects, they were training to use the advanced research facilitates. Through the research funding, we have published a few papers in the top journals such as Journal of Nuclear Materials, Acta materialia, Scripta Materialia, Scientific Reports, etc.

11212915.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212915.value: Silicon carbide is a promising material for first wall and blanket components in fusion reactors due to its great strength and low radioactivity under high temperature environment. Two materials of the single crystal 3C-SiC and SiC-fiber composite were investigated in this project. The major findings and research outcomes could be briefly introduced as the following three parts. For the 3C-SiC materials, three important findings were concluded. 1) in the single He+ irradiation, there is only 66% of implanted He atoms diffuse into the bubble at 15000 appm, 1200℃. When the dose increase, the percentage will also increase. However, the percentage of helium atoms diffuse into bubble does not reach 100% at 45000 appm, 1200℃. It suggested that the number of defects caused by ion irradiation are less than implanted helium ion. 2) the 3C-SiC become amorphous when irradiated to 20dpa at 40℃, but it is still crystalline at 200℃. The swelling is 7.7% at 40℃. Besides, using synchrotron radiation based XRD radial scanning to get the interplanar information of 200℃. Besides, humps are found in Si (002) radial scan result, it may caused by the defect cluster. 3) He bubbles were observed in the dual-beam irradiated samples, the bubble density decrease but the bubble size increase as temperature increasing. The increasing dose will cause bubble size and density become lager and denser. For the SA-Tyrannohex all fiber SiC composite, we found that cavities (or helium bubbles) can be observed in dual beam irradiated SA-Tyrannohex SiC composite specimens and 45000 appm single He implanted specimens. Comparison to single crystal SiC, CVD polycrystalline SiC and CVI polyctstalline SiC irradiated in the same condition, SA-Tyrannohex all fiber SiC appears to have excellent radiation tolerance under high temperature condition by suppressing the cavities formation. Besides, grain boundaries seems to hava a capability to enhance the point defects recombination. The third major contribution of this project is that, we first demonstrated the structural nature of point defects clusters, named as the black spot defect which can be observed at all temperatures and is the major defect at low temperature. Our studies showed that the point defect clusters, especially large defect clusters, contain more vacancies than interstitials. In contrast, the number of interstitials is significantly higher than vacancy in isolated defects. Since interstitials are more mobile than vacancies, more interstitials are able to migrate and leave the defect clusters eventually.

11212915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212915.value: 1) In order to confirm that the (002) diffraction peak shift of 3C-SiC measured by the synchronous XRD in the single beam test is caused by the point defects arranged in a specific direction, the irradiated sample can be examined by a spherical aberration corrected Transmission Electron Microscopy. When the structure of point defects could be resolved and the swelling induced by the single point defects was measured, we can finally verify the XRD observation. 2) In the actual situation of nuclear fusion environment, hydrogen is also the main nuclear transmutation product, which accounts for about 40 appm per dpa damage. Therefore, the triple-beam ion irradiation experiment (Si+He+H) is encouraged to perform, and the role of hydrogen on the defects evolution can be evaluated. 3) Nanoindentation experiments on the irradiated samples are deserved to conduct, so that the change of mechanical performance can be evaluated.

11212915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212915.value: Silicon carbide (SiC) or silicon carbide compoiste is one of the attractive nuclear structure materials in the future, because it has many outstanding properties like high melting point, good mechanical property at high temperature, small cross-section of absorbing neutron, and so on. In this project, we systematically investigated the radiation resistance of two types of SiC materials with different crystalline structures. Through the methods of ion accelerator, advanced electron microcopy and high energy X-ray, the microstructural evolution of irradiated samples are investigated, the swelling induced by the He bubble or voids were measured. The obtained data points will benefit the future studies of this field. Importantly, the black spot, a prevailed defect under irradiation, its structure was firstly revealed in this study. We believe that the completion of this project will not only promote the application of SiC in the nuclear industry, but increase the impact of Hong Kong in the nuclear material community.

11213115.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11213115.value: 可运行于严酷环境下的透明日盲深紫外纳米薄膜探测器

11213115.label: Project Objectives
11213115.value: Establish the cost-effective synthesis technique to prepare high-performance Ga2O3 nanowires with the controlled crystallinity, diameter and length, surface morphology, structural and optoelectronic properties. Fabricate and evaluate the performance of fully see-through solar-blind detectors based on the single Ga2O3 nanowire for the deep-ultraviolet detection in extreme conditions. This would yield the optimal nanowire synthesis condition as well as the corresponding spectral and dynamic responses for the efficient photodetection. Employ the nanowire contact printing method to heterogeneously integrate optimized Ga2O3 nanowire thin films and well-developed high-mobility In2O3 nanowire thin films on transparent substrates. These nanowire films can be configured as detectors and transistors, respectively, and next be interfaced to facilitate an all-nanowire on-chip integrated circuitry in order to detect and amplify deep-ultraviolet signals. Build and assess the operation limits of large-scale, transparent, all-nanowire circuit arrays with the deep-ultraviolet imaging capability. The ultimate target is to accomplish a versatile, low-cost and powerful platform to achieve the fully see-through, solar-blind, high-performance detector arrays based on multi-functional nanowire thin films for the practical utilization in harsh environments.

11213115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213115.value: 近年来，可运行于严酷环境的透明日盲深紫外探测器的发展得益于其在国防、商业和科学领域的大量应用。例如，第一个采用生长在晶体蓝宝石衬底的b-Ga2O3薄膜制备的高温运行透明深紫外探测器刚刚被证实具有可观的性能；然而，底层晶体衬底的要求将不可避免地限制了相应的探测器的设计、材料的选择和器件的集成，影响了进一步的性能增强、实际应用和商业化。与此同时，由于纳米科技的出现，晶体半导体纳米材料诸如纳米线被认为是有前途的未来探测器技术的基础材料，得益于其完善的具有成本效益的合成方法和可通过调整大小、形态和原子组成控制其材料性能。具体地说，这些晶体纳米线可以容易地在高度晶格失配甚至无定形衬底上制备，然后印刷到任何异质衬底例如玻璃板上。而且，与传统薄膜探测器相比，纳米线固有的大的比表面积和二维载流子和光子限制，使纳米线探测器在极端环境运行时具有优良的光敏性、低的暗电流和优异的光电导性增益。即便如此，在控制纳米线合成、了解其基本性能、多功能纳米线集成平行排列的薄膜、制备和评估这些纳米线薄膜探测器电路阵列的性能极限的方面仍存在很多显著的挑战。在该提案中，我们将集中研究b-Ga2O3纳米线薄膜系统作为严酷环境下的活性光敏材料，基于其优良的结晶度、电容差、热稳定性和对小于280nm波长的有效光谱响应。目标是在透明衬底上不同类地整合优化的b-Ga2O3纳米线薄膜和完善的高迁移率的In2O3纳米线薄膜。这些纳米线薄膜可以分别配置为探测器和晶体管，然后相交互成为一个可以检测和放大深紫外信号的全纳米线芯片集成电路。最后，我们计划建立大规模电路矩阵并评估其运行极限，建立一个多功能、低成本的强大平台，实现基于多功能纳米线薄膜的全透明日盲高性能探测器阵列在恶劣环境下的实用化。

11213115.label: Realisation of objectives
11213115.value: In this project, we have successfully accomplished all the objectives with 100% of completion. To be specific, we have achieved a new synthesis technique, known as solid-source chemical vapor deposition, to synthesize single-crystalline Ga2O3 nanowires (NWs) as well as In-doped and In, Zn codoped Ga2O3 NWs with well-controlled growth density, chemical stoichiometry, diameters, surface morphologies, electrical and optoelectronic properties (Objective 1). For example, in order to synthesize In2xGa2-2xO3 NWs with different chemical stoichiometry of In and Ga, the metal granules of Ga and In were used at different molar ratios (e.g., 3:1 for In1.8Ga0.2O3, 1:1 for In1.52Ga0.48O3, and 1:3 for In0.66Ga1.34O3 NWs; 1.5 g of the source materials in total for each growth) in order to control the NW composition. Also, 0.5 g of a graphite powder was mixed with the metal source as the precursor. During the growth, the precursor mixture was placed at the sealed end whereas the substrate was positioned at the open end of a small quartz tube. The entire set-up was then placed in the center of a large quartz tube, located in a single-zone horizontal tube furnace. Next, a mixed gas of 4% oxygen (99.999%) and 96% argon (99.9995%) was introduced as the carrier gas into the quartz tube. The furnace was heated to 1030 °C in 30 min, held for 30 min, and then cooled to room temperature naturally. After the synthesis, a fluffy white product was found on the substrate. The growth was also noted to be highly sensitive to the temperature. When the temperature was set below 1,030 °C, no NW was obtained. Once the temperature was adjusted to > 1,030 °C, significant coatings were observed on the NWs. Based on the material characterization, such as scanning electron microscope (SEM) and transmission electron microscope (TEM), etc., the NW properties are fully evaluated and used to further optimize the NW growth to achieve the crystalline, long, smooth and straight NWs for subsequent studies. At the same time, optical properties of these grown In2xGa2-2xO3 NWs in a wide compositional range are systematically assessed (Objective 2). Based on the complementary optical absorption, photoluminescence, photoacoustic spectroscopy, bandgaps of pure Ga2O3 and In2O3 NWs can be reliably determined to be 4.71 ± 0.02 and 3.01 ± 0.02 eV, respectively. Bandgaps of In2xGa2-2xO3 NWs are around 400 meV higher than that of pure In2O3, which spread over a range of only 50 meV (from 3.38 to 3.43 eV) despite big stoichiometric diﬀerences. The band gap increases with the Ga content, following the expected trend. Such small changes in the compositional band gap dependence cannot be explained by ﬂattening caused by the bowing parameter, held true only for high In contents. In the proposed interpretation we state that the In2O3/Ga2O3 phase separation leads to dominating contribution of In2O3 in the measured absorption. The signiﬁcant blue-shift might originate from a simple fact of smaller In/Ga volumetric ratio there. All these valuable findings give us thorough understandings of the optical properties of NWs that are essential for the design of NWs based UV photodetector operating in harsh environments. By using the well-established NW contact printing, NW parallel arrays can be readily conﬁgured onto any substrate, such as Si/SiO2 wafers, with the source/drain electrical contact of Ni ﬁlms (Objectives 3 and 4). It is evident that the output current increases accordingly with the increasing illumination light intensity (261 nm). The device also exhibits a characteristic linear relationship of I-V curves, indicating the ohmic-like contact property, which favors collecting the photogenerated carriers eﬃciently. Moreover, the relationship between the photocurrent and the light intensity can as well be described by the power law of I=AP^ θ. I is the photocurrent, A is a constant, P is the light intensity, and θ is the empirical value. The θ value is determined to be 0.62, which is again less than 1, suggesting the complex processes of electron-hole generation, trapping, and recombination on the NW surface. Besides, the responsivity decreases gradually with the increasing incident light power. It gives a maximum responsivity of 1.64E5 A/W with the source/drain bias of 1 V and gate bias of -20 V. For the photoswitching measurement, the device delivers a stable on- and oﬀ-state with an on-oﬀ current ratio of ∼5, which reveals the stability and reproducibility of the photodetector. The rise and decay times are determined to be 4.42 and 11.1 s, respectively. More importantly, these NW arrays can also be fabricated onto glass substrates with indium tin oxide (ITO) source/drain electrodes in order to achieve fully-transparent solar-blind UV photodetectors. The photodetector has a high optical transparency, above 80%, for a wide range of wavelengths spanning from 400 to 800 nm. All these performance parameters of the fully transparent photodetector device are already comparable to or even better than those of state-of-the-art transparent photodetectors as reported in the literature. At the end, these NW arrayed UV photodetectors can be heterogeneously integrated with In2O3 NW transistors to achieve the imaging capability. The transistors are used to amplify the detected current signals. Notably, because of the large bandgaps of both detector and transistor channel materials, the fabricated imaging devices are insensitive to operating temperature. In specific, these devices can operate up to 150 deg C without significant degradation of photocurrent. Majority of their performance parameters, such as the photoresponsivity and transient time, etc., can be maintained. In the future, the photodetector performance can be further improved through the optimization of the NW parallel array density, alignment and channel length scaling, etc. In summary, we have developed a versatile, low-cost and powerful platform to realize the fully see-through, solar-blind, high-performance detector arrays based on multi-functional NW thin films for the practical utilization in harsh environments.

11213115.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213115.value: In this project, there are several key findings, which lead to 14 high-impact journal publications (2 ACS Nano, 2 Nano Energy and 1 Advanced Energy Materials, etc) as well as 9 invited presentations at different international conferences. In specific, as reported in ACS Nano 2019, using solid-source catalytic chemical vapor deposition, crystalline, dense and uniform Ga2O3, In2xGa2-2xO3 and InGaZnO nanowires (NWs) are successfully fabricated via vapor-solid-liquid (VLS) growth mechanism with controlled chemical composition, surface morphology, electrical and optoelectronic properties. Particularly, when In2xGa2-2xO3 NWs are configured into field-effect transistors, the optimized individual NW device exhibits the electron mobility reaching up to 750 cm2/Vs, which is much higher than the one of typical In2O3 NW devices, due to the reduce in the number of oxygen vacancies and ionized impurity scattering centers in optimized NWs. Moreover, when InGaZnO NWs constructed into individual NW photodetectors, they deliver an excellent responsivity to deep ultraviolet (UV) illumination (261 nm). For instance, the individual NW device can deliver an impressive responsivity of 1.95E5 A/W and external quantum efficiency of as high as 9.28E7 % together with a rise time of 0.93 s and a decay time of 0.2 s for the UV photodetection. The obtained performance parameters, such as photoresponsivity and transient time constants, etc., are comparable or even better than the state-of-the-art UV photodetectors. More importantly, these NWs can be assembled into large-scale parallel arrays on glass substrates by NW contact printing to achieve fully-transparent solar-blind UV photodetectors. The fabricated photodetector has a high optical transparency, above 80%, for a wide range of wavelengths spanning from 400 to 800 nm. More importantly, the device performance is mostly maintained at different operating conditions. In summary, all these major findings are significant, which would bring forward the deployment of metal oxide NWs for high-performance UV imaging device operating in harsh conditions.

11213115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213115.value: Even though there are significant results generated from this work, there are still a number of areas which is worth for further investigation to enhance the device performance of developed robust transparent solar-blind ultraviolet (UV) photodetector arrays based on metal-oxide semiconductor nanowires. For example, the quantum efficiency of fabricated detectors can be additionally improved since the current device limitation may come from the reflectance of incident UV irradiation, insufficient absorption of light attributable to the finite thickness of NW and anisotropic absorption of light arising from the one-dimensional geometry, etc. Moreover, there are substantial amount of trap states existed for NWs because of their large surface-to-volume ratio, dictating the performance limit of these detectors. In this case, it is essential to enhance the quantum efficiencies of photodetectors and to perform appropriate surface passivation schemes to alleviate the negative impact of trap states on the nanowire device channels. Moreover, we can perform further works to extend the operating conditions for harsh operation, such as enhancing both higher and lower operating temperature limits as well as the humidity levels, especially since there is a lot of advanced utilizations (e.g. flexible optoelectronics, internet of things and etc.) that require high-performance and cost-effective UV photodetector arrays operated in the non-conventional manner. All these further works would push forward the substantial technological development of nanowires based photodetector arrays for practical applications.

11213115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213115.value: In recent years, high-performance, cost-effective and robust see-through solar-blind deep ultraviolet photodetectors capable to operate in harsh conditions are urgently required for various advanced technological applications. However, the current detector design and processing schemes typically rely on crystalline underlying substrates and high-temperature epitaxial material fabrication processes, which are not compatible with low-cost transparent substrates. Due to the advent of nanotechnology, nanostructured materials, such as crystalline semiconductor nanowires, can be easily manufactured on highly lattice-mismatched or even amorphous substrates. These nanowires can then be employed as ideal active materials for the reliable photodetectors. In this project, we have successfully achieved a hybrid and low-cost approach utilizing the bottom-up Ga2O3 based nanowire arrays with the conventional top-down device fabrication processes to configure as detectors and transistors, respectively, and next be interfaced to facilitate an all-nanowire on-chip integrated circuitry in order to detect and amplify deep-ultraviolet signals. Ultimately, we established a versatile and powerful technology platform to establish a versatile, low-cost and powerful platform to obtain the fully see-through, solar-blind, high-performance detector arrays based on multi-functional nanowire thin films for the practical utilization in harsh environments.

11213415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213415.value: The cooperative formation control problem of mobile robots has attracted increasing attention over the last decade. Its objective is to force a team of networked mobile robots to form and maintain some desired positions and orientations so that a common goal is achieved. Mobile robots have been widely used in various applications. Classified by working environments, mobile robots are often named as Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs), Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs), or Unmanned Air Vehicles (UAVs). Thanks to the rapid advances and developments of mobile robots, the formation control problem becomes more and more important due to its great application potential. In fact, multiple mobile robots with a desired geometric structure are able to complete more complicated tasks with greater flexibility and higher efficiency. Typical engineering application examples include, fixing a damaged oil drilling machine by cooperation of multiple UGVs, securing or monitoring a moving vessel by a group of AUVs, and scouting an unknown area in severe environment by a team of UAVs. Almost all the above mentioned vehicles are subject to nonholonomic constraints. More importantly, in practice, a mobile robot is driven by its motor with limited technical specifications. Due to the pitch rate limit, thrust limit, and stall conditions, a mobile robot is subject to constraints of the saturated heading rate, bounded maximum velocity, and positive-minimum velocity respectively. All these velocity constraints need to be taken into account in the formation control problem of mobile robots, otherwise the performance of the concerned system would be adversely affected. Unfortunately, most of the existing results on formation control of nonholonomic mobile robots are developed without full consideration of those velocity constraints. The objective of this project is to investigate several fundamental problems in cooperative formation control of multiple nonholonomic mobile robots subject to velocity constraints. We aim at developing distributed control laws for a team of nonholonomic mobile robots by addressing several critical issues, including constrained controller design, limited local information usage, time-varying communication networks, environmental disturbances and parameter uncertainties. Two typical formation problems, that is, leader-follower formation and circular formation, will be comprehensively investigated. The success of this research project will provide answers to a number of fundamental and critical issues facing formation control of multiple mobile robots, and thus facilitate its applications in more practical scenarios. 在過去的十幾年中，移動機器人的協同編隊控制問題受到了廣泛關注。該問題的研究目標是讓一隊移動機器人通過通訊形成並保持期望的位置與方向，從而完成一定任務。隨著移動機器人領域的迅速發展，編隊控制問題由於其重要的潛在應用，正在變得愈發重要。事實上，在執行一些複雜任務時，完成編隊的移動機器人組能夠帶來更多的靈活性並具有更高的工作效率。在不同的工作環境下，移動機器人通常也被具體稱為無人地面車輛，自主水下機器人或無人飛行器。幾乎所有上述移動運載工具都受到非完整約束限制。更為重要的是，在實際中，移動機器人的驅動電機受到技術條件的限制。由於電機轉動矩，推動力和失速條件的限制，移動機器人的速度分別受到飽和轉向速度，有界最大速度和正向最小速度的限制。所有的這些速度限制都應該在移動機器人編隊控制問題中考慮，否則受控機器人的性能會受到不利的影響。 本項目將研究速度受限的非完整移動機器人的協同編隊控制問題。此問題將考慮以上提到的速度限制，以及時變通信網絡，外部環境干擾和系統參數不確定性等帶來的技術性難題。本項目將全面研究兩類典型的編隊問題：領導者跟隨編隊和圓形編隊。此研究項目的理論結果將會為許多移動機器人協同編隊控制的基礎關鍵問題提供答案，從而提高編隊控制器的實用性。

11213415.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213415.value: Several fundamental problems on cooperative formation control of multiple nonholonomic mobile robots subject to velocity constraints have been investigated. In particular, two typical formation problems, that is, leader-follower formation and circular formation, have been studied. Effective distributed control laws for a team of mobile agents have been developed to tackle several critical issues, including constrained controller design, limited local information usage, time-varying communication networks. The leader-follower parallel formation problem of multiple nonholonomic mobile robots with velocity constraints has been solved. Each follower only has access to the local information and the information of its neighbors in a network of which the topology is modeled by a directed graph. Then the problem is considered for the more practical case where a common reference direction is not available, each mobile robot needs to use its own local coordinate frame. Compared with some previous work, vehicles are not required to share a common reference direction. Moreover, circular formation problems are studied with static-target and moving-target respectively. Distributed formation control laws are designed for nonholonomic vehicles subject to velocity constraints, such that the controlled vehicles travel along a common circle with the given center and radius, while maintaining a desired spaced formation. The center may not be known to all the vehicles. The proposed controller does not require any communication and only uses local measurements based on a sensor graph of which the topology is modeled by a directed graph satisfying a certain acyclic condition. It is noted that direct distance measurements are not needed. At the same time, some coverage control problem for mobile sensor network is also considered and several results are obtained including the case that the mobile agents are subject to measurement errors and the case with limited interaction range respectively. On the other hand, consensus and the cooperative output regulation problem of linear multi-agent systems and certain nonlinear multi-agent systems are addressed under certain conditions. These studies are important because formation control problems can be converted into these two problems in certain circumstances. Finally, the application of the developed control strategies to formation of ground mobile robots has also been investigated. It is concluded that the formation control problems for multiple mobile agents are intensively studied in more practical settings, and the developed control strategies will provide more feasibility for a wide range of applications.

11213415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213415.value: A number of results have been obtained and published on the cooperative formation control of multiple nonholonomic mobile robots subject to velocity constraints, as well as related cooperative control problems with constraints on communication. At the same time, many intriguing problems in cooperative control of multiple agents are identified. For example, when we investigated the application of the developed control schemes to the formation of multiple mobile wheeled robots, we found that the case where vehicles with disturbances and the obstruction of the line of sight also deserves more attention because it appears in real scenarios very often. It has been one of our recent interests and could be one of the future research focuses.

11213415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213415.value: Several fundamental problems on cooperative formation control of multiple nonholonomic mobile robots subject to velocity constraints have been studied. In control of mobile robots, velocities can be usually viewed as inputs. Velocity constrains can thus be treated as input constraints. All these physical constraints will severely degrade the performance of the closed-loop control system if they are not well taken into account. In this project, two typical formation problems, that is, leader-follower formation and circular formation, have been addressed. A number of critical issues, including constrained controller design, limited local information usage, time-varying communication networks and/or with time-delays, have been tackled in this project. The developed techniques and approaches will considerably narrow the existing technical gaps in constrained cooperative control of multiple nonholonomic mobile robots and enhance their control performance in real life applications. The expected outcomes of this project will advance the current state of cooperative control research, and provide a wider scope of applications for formation control of multiple mobile robots under more practical situations.

11213515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213515.value: 人們對準確、快速、低成本醫療診斷設備的需求不斷增加。在生物醫學領域，時間分辨的冷光檢測是一種功能強大且被廣泛採用的技術。該技術在疾病篩查及癌症研究等方面有廣泛應用。時間分辨技術能提取分子結構和分子周圍環境等大量包含在時域中的資訊。而該技術所需設備極為昂貴，僅能應用於資金充足的實驗室，這限制了其在普通場合的應用。因此，亟需一種成熟、系統的設計方法來研製出低成本、高性能的時間分辨探測系統。 本專案擬設計、研製並實驗驗證一種新型的時間分辨冷光檢測微傳感系統。該樣機將由光子探測和信號處理兩部分電路進行光學檢測且由化學或生物樣品進行驗證。 該專案主要有如下三個創新點。第一，寬的動態範圍可檢測較寬範圍的冷光壽命，大大擴展了單一器件的應用範圍。第二，新型的時間/數位轉換器（TDC）結構支援電路共用，可實現並行處理，同時減小電路面積。第三，接觸式探測可顯著地減少系統中的光學部件，進一步減小系統體積、降低成本。 本專案致力於開發高選擇性、高靈敏度的小型化傳感系統，基於此研製出新一代針對快速、定點醫療診斷的高集成、可擕式的分析儀。這將緩解與日劇增的醫療保健帶來的經濟壓力，同時提高生活品質。

11213515.label: Realisation of objectives
11213515.value: All objectives were executed 100% to completion. Four high-impact SCI journal papers resulted from this project. The realisation of each objective is described one by one below. Objective 1: Design, prototype, and validate a microsystem consisting detection device and signal processing circuits, which are targeted for chemical or biological detection. Photon-counting analysis plays a key role in many areas, such as biology, chemistry, and medicine. Based on this approach, we have designed, prototyped, and validated an integrated time-correlated single photon counting (TCSPC) lifetime analytical system with a complete signal path—from fluorophore excitation, emission detection, to lifetime extraction. The time-to-digital module of the proposed TCSPC system achieves a root-mean-square differential non-linearity of 4% of the least significant bit and a full width at half maximum temporal resolution from 121 to 145 ps within the 500-ns full-scale range. To evaluate the lifetime extraction and detection limit of the proposed TCSPC system, a wide variety of samples, such as fluorescein in water, coumarin 6 in dimethyl sulfoxide, and rhodamine 6G in water, each prepared in 14 concentrations from 0.5 nM (nanomolar, 10−9 mol/L) to 25 μM (micromolar, 10−6 mol/L), are tested. With the optimized hardware and firmware design, the proposed TCSPC system can accurately extract the fluorescence lifetime of fluorescein, coumarin 6, and rhodamine 6G down to the concentration of 1, 1, and 2.5 nM, respectively, significantly outperforming similar fluorescence lifetime analysis systems. Details on this objective are reported in our first and forth journal publications. Objective 2: Design a wide dynamic range circuit with a time-to-digital converter for lifetime measurements. Time-to-digital module of TCSPC applications requires conversion with reliable pico-second temporal resolution and has been realized with compact printed circuit boards using custom analog/mixed-signal circuit design techniques. Particularly noteworthy is the use of the Texas Instruments time-to-digital converter TDC7200, selected to convert elapsed time between the input signal pair to digital values because of its temporal resolution, self-calibration and insensitivity to temperature. TDC7200 is a stopwatch integrated circuit with 55 ps least significant bit (LSB) resolution used to measure the elapsed time between a single event (an edge on START pin) and multiple subsequent events (an edge on STOP pin). An internal self-calibrated timer base inside TDC7200 compensates for drift over time and temperature. All these features make the TDC7200 specifically suitable for TCSPC lifetime measurement. The completion interrupt status of time-to-digital conversion is continuously checked by the MCU during the measurement. When a time-to-digital conversion has completed, the result is read into the MCU and the next conversion is initiated. Since the output high voltages of the excitation source and the alternative detectors are not compatible with the TDC7200, a signal conditioning circuit with Texas Instruments LSF0102 two-channel bidirectional multi-voltage translator is designed as the interface between the input signal pair and the TDC module to satisfy signal compatibility. Our circuit is capable of conducting TCSPC measurement in forward or reverse START-STOP mode. The wide dynamic range performance allows the module to support a wide variety of biomarkers such as organic dyes and quantum dots. Details on this objective are reported in our first and third journal publications. Objective 3: Quantitative modeling and comparison of characteristics for quantum dots and upconversion nanoparticle based microsystems. Quantitative modeling of the key relationships linking design parameters was the reason behind the high performance achieved in our prototypes. Among many parameters modeled, the dimensions and geometry of the liquid core waveguide optical component is critical because it influences both the compactness and optical performance of the system. By split-mode 3D ray tracing analysis, it was found that a quartz LCW with round/round cross-section geometry could achieve both good excitation rejection. Excitation light emitting into the LCW with an incident angle α, designed to be smaller than the critical angle, is guided within the LCW. As the excitation light reaches the inner side wall of the LCW, partial reflection occurs because the refractive index of the wall is larger than that of the liquid core. Therefore, at the inner wall, a portion of excitation light enters the wall while the rest is reflected within the liquid core. When the excitation light reaches the outer wall of the LCW, if the angle β is larger than the critical incident angle between the wall and the air, as the refractive index of the wall is higher than that of the surrounding air, TIR occurs. If α is small enough, all the excitation light is confined within the LCW. Simultaneously, as the direction of the emission light is isotropic, a large amount of emission light is able to exit the LCW and reach the detector. Therefore, the LCW performs the dual function of excitation guiding and emission filtering, in a single component, which is a key contributor to overall system size reduction. Details on this objective are reported in the third publication but also to various degrees in the other three journal publications as well.

11213515.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213515.value: Major findings were published in 4 high-impact SCI journal articles. The existing limitations and our breakthrough are summarized below: J1: Low Detection Limit Time-Correlated Single Photon Counting Lifetime Analytical System for Point-of-Care Applications Photon-counting analysis plays a key role in many areas, such as biology, chemistry, and medicine. This paper presents an integrated time-correlated single photon counting (TCSPC) lifetime analytical system with a complete signal path—from fluorophore excitation, emission detection, to lifetime extraction. With the optimized hardware and firmware design, the prototyped TCSPC system can accurately extract the fluorescence lifetime of fluorescein, coumarin 6, and rhodamine 6G down to the concentration of 1, 1, and 2.5 nM, respectively, significantly outperforming similar fluorescence lifetime analysis systems and demonstrating our innovations. J2: Liquid-core waveguide TCSPC sensor for high-accuracy fluorescence lifetime analysis Liquid-core waveguide (LCW) has many advantages such as the elimination of optical artifacts typically exhibited in systems employing lenses and filters. However, due to the effect of temporal dispersion, LCWs have typically been employed in steady-state fluorescence detection microsystems rather than in fluorescence lifetime measurement (FLM) systems. This paper presents a compact liquid-core waveguide time-correlated single-photon counting (LCW-TCSPC) sensor for FLM. The propagation of excitation within the LCW is analyzed both analytically and in simulations, with results in agreement with experimental characterization, which is an important contribution to design methodology. J3: A Low-Cost Time-Correlated Single Photon Counting Portable DNA Analyzer DNA analysis is the core method for many biosensing applications. This paper presents a portable, low-cost TCSPC analysis system for DNA detection. Both optical and electronic subsystems are carefully designed to provide effective emission filtering and size reduction, delivering good DNA detection and fluorescence lifetime extraction performance. DNA detection has been verified by fluorescence lifetime measurements of a V-carbazole conjugated fluorophore lifetime bioassay. J4: Fully Integrated Liquid-Core Waveguide Fluorescence Lifetime Detection Microsystem for DNA Biosensing Time-resolved fluorescence is a widely adopted technique for DNA detection due to its high sensitivity and selectivity. However, due to stringent requirements on optics and electronics, instrumentation with time-resolved capability is bulky and expensive, prohibiting their use in portable and point-of-care applications. This paper presents a fully-integrated DNA biosensor based on liquid-core waveguide (LCW) optics for fluorescence lifetime analysis. The level of performance and integration is unprecedented.

11213515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213515.value: In the project, we have devised several advanced techniques (and developed several prototypes) for TCSPC based photon counting analysis. These devices have a substantially cost and size advantage over existing components. From the initial evaluation, some of these devices show that they have performance and cost advantages that rival their conventional counterparts. Further development of the research will be carried out in two paths: 1) From the research front, focus will be placed on the continuation of expanding the capabilities of the developed platform. For example, the use of nanomaterials and nanoparticles will be used to enhance the selectivity of these devices to various analytes. 2) In view of the commercial potential of the developed technology, we are actively soliciting partner from the industries to work toward commercializing components, based on our filed patent, for the medical diagnostics market.

11213515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213515.value: Demand for accurate, rapid, and low-cost medical diagnostics has been ever rising. Time-resolved luminescence detection is a powerful and well-adopted technique in the biological and medical sciences. It has wide applications such as diseases screening and cancer research. The time-resolved technique extracts a wealth of information embedded in the temporal domain, such as the structure and surrounding environment of a molecule. The technique, however, demands sophisticated equipment. Today, there is a lack of mature and systematic approach to design the equipment without severe performance compromises. The high equipment cost is merely tolerated by well-funded labs but prohibitive to ubiquitous in-field deployment. In this project, we have investigated the design, prototype, and experimentally validation of novel microsystems based on time-resolved luminescence detection. The prototypes generally consist of a photon detector and signal processing circuits. The microsystem will be demonstrated using a practical medical diagnostics application, such as disease screening or pathogen detection. The sensory technologies developed in this project have enabled an unprecedented level of selectivity, sensitivity, and miniaturization, thus help bring about a new generation of highly-integrated, portable analysis devices, particularly for rapid, point-of-care medical diagnostics.

11213915.label: Project Objectives
11213915.value: Develop a novel bio-inspired superhydrophobic surface with asymmetric structure. Asymmetric superhydrophobic surfaces with different radii of curvature will be fabricated. The droplet spreading and retraction dynamics on engineered surfaces under different impact conditions will be characterized. The preferential spreading and retraction in the axial and azimuthal directions on surfaces with different radii of curvature will be compared. The effect of curvature on the contact time (fast droplet detachment) will be examined. Elucidate the effect of asymmetric structure on the droplet impact through the Lattice Boltzmann (LB) simulation and analytical analysis. Based on the LB simulation, the spreading time to reach the maximum spreading in the two directions on the asymmetric surface (one in the axial direction and the other in the azimuthal direction) can be calculated and these results will be compared with the experimental data to illustrate the effect of asymmetric structure on the droplet bouncing. The momentum analysis will be used to validate our hypothesis. Determine the effect of substrate stiffness on droplet impact dynamics. To further probe the effect of substrate stiffness on the droplet bouncing, we will engineer PDMS-based structured surface with asymmetric structure but different rigidity. The maximum spreading lengths and retraction velocities in both the axial and azimuthal directions as well as the contact time for the droplet to completely detach from the surface with different stiffness will be measured and compared to establish the correlation between substrate stiffness and bouncing dynamics. Inhibit the liquid droplet rebound on the solid surface by tailoring the liquid property. Droplets with different nanoparticle concentrations will be used to examine the effect of nanoparticle additive on the impact behavior. The critical concentration beyond which the droplet anti-rebound occurs will be determined. The effects of the contact line friction and liquid bulk property on the impact dynamics will be examined.

11213915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213915.value: 理解和控制液體碰撞固體表面的復雜動力學，在過去的一個世紀裏吸引了眾多科學家，並且在與能源，水和全球健康有關的領域裏有著廣泛的技術應用。盡管之前有關的大量研究，預測液滴碰撞帶有紋理的表面後所產生的結果仍然具有很大的挑戰性，因為這個問題進一步被三相接觸線上繁復的動態過程復雜化了。此外，之前報道的人為合成的紋理表面大多局限於微米/毫米尺度，並且表現著各向同性的潤濕度。 很多自然界植物的表面都有大尺度的凸面或凹面結構。受此啟發，我們猜想各向異性的結構可以產生令人激動的物理現象和出乎意料的功能。的確，我們最近發現液滴碰撞在自然界的一種植物——玉蓮表面時，可以更容易從表面脫離，同時展現出了有趣的不對稱碰撞行為。因此，該項目的主要目標是系統地利用實驗的，建模的和分析的方法去闡明這種獨特的碰撞動力學的基本原理。簡言之，我們將會利用新的方法，通過模仿玉蓮的表面，制造有不對稱結構的超疏水結構。當然，我們也會通過改變液滴的性質，研究如何抑制液滴在自然界的或者工程的表面上的反彈。 發現和研究這種有趣的不對稱碰撞的意義不僅在於加深和推廣我們關於潤濕現象的理解，也會為理性地發展有不同工業用途的仿生結構提供新思路。我們關於潤濕動力學 (Physical Review Letters, 2012; Nature Physics, 2014) 和多功能的超疏水結構(Advanced Functional Materials, 2011; Scientific Reports, 2013 and 2014)的基礎研究為該預算為該項目的成功完成提供了重要基礎。項目的實施也會使主要研究員持久地並且專註地繼續他在熱-流體方面的研究。

11213915.label: Realisation of objectives
11213915.value: The study of droplet impact on solid surfaces dates back one century ago. Previously we have shown in our Nature Physics paper that we can shape the drop to bounce from the surface in a pancake shape directly at the end of the spreading stage without going through the receding process. As a result, the droplet can be shed away much faster. Interestingly, it is demonstrated that the contact time is constant under a wide range of impact velocities. In other words, the contact time reduction is very efficient and robust and the novel surface behaves like an elastic spring. The magic really lies in the surface texture. Inspired by the observation that the surfaces of many natural plants are associated with large scale convex or concave architecture, we hypothesize that the anisotropic structure on the natural surfaces might lead to exciting physics and unexpected functionalities. Indeed, we recently found that droplet impacting on the natural Echeveria surface can detach from the surface more easily and displays an intriguing asymmetric bouncing behavior. Thus, the main goal of this project is to implement an integrated experimental, modeling and analytical approach to elucidate the fundamental mechanism responsible for the unique bouncing dynamics.

11213915.value: Over the past several years, there is a surge in the fundamental understanding of droplet dynamics on macrotexture as well as its practical application. In particular, it is recently shown that asymmetric macrotexture can also promote dropwise condensation and anti-icing. Also we are actively extending this study for the droplet based power generation (paper under review). We are very excited about the impact brought by this project and its general implementation.

11213915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213915.value: This project aims to fundamentally understand how the macrotexture as well as its rigidity affects the droplet dynamics as well as its related application in anti-icing. Manifesting in different size, form, dynamics, droplets are probably the most complex and also the simplest matter in the word. The fundamental understanding and engineering new surfaces to better control droplet dynamics has profound impacts for a wide range of areas. This research has produced many exciting results and will provide important insights for the development of new nature-inspired materials for various applications.

11214115.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11214115.value: 面向自供能嵌入式系统的非易失处理器的软件重设计

11214115.label: Project Objectives
11214115.value: Execution progress aware checkpointing. When detecting an energy risk, instead of starting checkpointing immediately, we want to identify the best checkpoint position so that the program can make the most progress with limited energy; Checkpoint size oriented checkpointing. This task will develop a checkpoint strategy that identifies a reachable program state which requires the smallest non-volatile memory size; Correctness aware checkpointing. We will observe and fix possible errors introduced by checkpointing and resumption; Re-design of the software stack to reduce stack size for checkpointing through static program analysis; Live registers reduction to reduce checkpoint size for register files; Joint stack and register aware software design. We will explore software design and optimizations by combining studies from both stack and registers to develop effective approaches to reduce the overall checkpoint size; Scheduling considering checkpointing for multiple applications. We will develop efficient application scheduling algorithms to generate checkpointing-friendly schedules for both preemptive and non-preemptive systems.

11214115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214115.value: In recent years, we have witnessed exponential growth of embedded systems such as Internet of Things and wearable devices, which have and will continue to revolutionize the quality of our daily lives. These intelligent systems often employ sensors to collect relevant data, which are then analyzed and transmitted to information hubs. Traditionally, these embedded systems are powered by batteries. However, in wearable devices such as health monitors, batteries are no longer favored due to size limitations, safety concerns, and recharging inconvenience. Energy harvesting is becoming a favorable power source, as it can harvest energy from solar, electromagnetic radiation, or thermal sources to power electronics. It provides better user experiences in an environment-friendly manner. However, energy harvesting power sources are intrinsically unstable. Due to this instability, program execution may be frequently interrupted. With CMOS-based volatile processors, the intermediate results will be lost after power outages and thus result in vain re-executions, which impose heavy energy overhead and even infeasibility to finish for large tasks. Non-volatile processors, in which non-volatile memory is attached to the volatile logics to backup program state information, have been developed recently to address this issue. Currently, most work for non-volatile processors focuses on hardware layer modeling and optimizations. Little work has been done on software level for non-volatile processors. This project aims to fill this gap and develop a reliable and efficient software framework tailored for non-volatile processors in energy harvesting powered embedded systems. The challenge lies in the simultaneous consideration of energy harvesting, application, and non-volatile processor characteristics. As frequent power interruptions become the norm of execution, the key is to design an ultra-efficient checkpointing strategy from the ground up. First, we will focus on a single application to minimize the program state information that needs to be saved. Instead of an immediate backup of the full program state upon energy low signals, both time and space dimensions of program execution will be explored. At the same time, the correctness of execution will be ensured. Secondly, scheduling multiple applications will be analyzed with checkpointing and different objectives. Preliminary results show that with proper software design, significant reduction can be achieved for the program state that needs to be checkpointed, which greatly improves both reliability and efficiency. The success of this project will enable pervasive adoption of user-friendly and environment-friendly embedded systems powered by energy harvesting, constituting a new renaissance for the innovation industry of Hong Kong. 近几年，以物联网和可穿戴设备为代表的嵌入式系统呈现指数级增长，将会持续对人们的日常生活带来革命性的变化。这些智能系统通常通过传感器来收集和处理相关数据，然后发送到信息中心。传统上，这些嵌入式系统由电池供电。然而，在可穿戴设备（比如健康状况监视器）中，电池由于尺寸过大，安全问题，以及充电不便不再受青睐。 自供能机制可以从太阳能、电磁辐射或热源来收集能量给电子设备供电，因而成为一种比较受欢迎的方式。它可以以一种环保的方式提供更好的用户体验。然而，自供能能量的来源本质上是不稳定的，这种不稳定性可能使得程序执行频繁地被打断。在基于CMOS的易失性处理器中，程序的中间结果会在断电之后丢失，从而导致程序重新执行，这会造成沉重的能源开销，甚至根本没有办法完成大型任务。为了解决这个问题，非易失性存储被添加到系统中用来存储断电容易丢失的数据，这种新型处理器被称为非易失性处理器。目前对非易失性处理器的研究集中在硬件的建模和优化，而很少涉及软件层次。 该项目旨在为自供能系统中的非易失性处理器提供可靠、高效的软件架构，其挑战性主要在于要同时考虑能量收集、应用程序和非易失性存储特性三方面，提出综合性的解决方案。由于自供能系统中存在频繁的断电，关键问题是如何重新设计一个高效的备份机制。首先，我们针对单个应用程序研究如何将需要备份的数据减到最少。不同于即时备份所有信息的机制，我们从时间和空间两个角度去考察收到低能耗信号之后的备份策略。同时，我们将探讨如何保证程序执行的正确性。其次，我们将分析有多个应用程序，有多种优化目的的情况下，如何备份易失数据。初步数据显示，通过设计好的软件管理机制，需要备份的易失数据可以大大减少，从而明显提高可靠性和程序执行效率。 该项目的研究成功将会使得有着良好用户体验和环保性的自供能系统被广泛应用，成为物联网发展的一个重要部分。

11214115.label: Realisation of objectives
11214115.value: For energy harvesting powered systems, efficient, progress-aware, correct checkpointing is of great importance. In this project, we make several important changes to the current system software for better support of energy harvesting powered devices. First, when and where shall checkpointing shall be executed is revisited; Second, correctness for checkpointing is considered at the upper system level, including compilers and OS layer; Third, system stack is redesigned to optimize memory usage through program analysis.

11215415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215415.value: 近些年，由於人類對醫療保健需求的不斷增加，生命科學已成為密集的研究領域。作為生命科學的重要分支，生物工程和生物醫學工程的研究正在以非常快的速度在發展，這些研究包括分析建模、計算模擬和實驗。因此生物技術應用同樣也處於快速發展中。現在基於高強度超聲的許多類型的生物醫療診治設備和裝置在生物醫學治療上都是已經實現了。最常見的壹種治療方法是組織摧毀術，其涉及腎結石的粉碎以及腫瘤細胞的摧毀。利用碳納米管(CNT)技術的出現以及碳納米管的許多優良的特點，本項目提出一種新的基於碳納米管的聚焦超聲設備，這種新的設備產生的聚焦高強度超聲不論是聚焦區域的空間精度，還是聚焦區域內的能量聚集（聲壓強度）都大大優於目前技術下的聚焦超聲。本項目將重點放在發展基本理論、實驗驗證以及確立能夠產生聚焦超聲的碳納米管-聚二甲硅氧烷（CNT-PDM）復合光聲透鏡的應用上。該項目涵蓋三個主要方面。其目標是為由CNT-PDMS復合物和彈性襯底制成的高強度聚焦超聲（HIFU）光聲透鏡建立一個解析模型並獲得其解析解。然後這種光聲透鏡將被設計制作以此來表征其不同的熱力特性、靈敏度以及光學性能。最後,通過測試此種光聲透鏡在結石粉碎和腫瘤摧毀中的聲空化作用，確定其在生物工程和生物醫學中的應用。此項目中，試驗僅使用人工樣本，並不涉及人類道德倫理和生物安全。預期在相同的能量輸入條件下，CNT-PDMS光聲透鏡產生的聲壓和尺寸精度上都要比現代技術下的生物醫療設備產生的超聲高出好幾倍。

11215415.label: Realisation of objectives
11215415.value: There are three major objectives in this project and Objectives (I) and (III) have been fully achieved while Objectives (II) is also achieved in principle [1,2]. In particular, the theory, modeling and analysis of the subject have been established where the thermal-acoustic wave response generated by using suspended multiwall carbon nanotube (MWCNT) thin film in different fluidic environments is developed [1] (Objectives I and III). In addition, the acoustic field response to broadband input signals applied to both free-standing and nano-thinfilm-substrate thermo-acoustic devices have been successfully developed [2] (Objectives I and III). The fabrication of optoacoustic lens using CNT have been developed in principle while the infiltration of PDMS into a CNT network is currently in progress [2] (Objectives II). In addition, the outcome of the theory, modelling and analysis developed [1,2] also generated significant research spin-offs [3-7]. Specifically, the nonlinear model and methodology have been further extended to yield asymptotic approximations solve for the dynamic response of dielectric elastomer balloon [3,4]; the idea have helped in a new bifurcation and hybrid control, model [5] and the mathematical approach further landed in the static-dynamic response for vibration of beams [6,7]. These outcomes are beyond the scope of the objectives.
