11215415.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215415.value: The major outcomes of the project have been reported in two research publications [1,2]. The first work deals with the theory, modelling and analysis of the subject for thermal-acoustic wave response generated by using suspended multiwall carbon nanotube (MWCNT) thin film in different fluidic environments in different fluidic environments [1] (Objectives I and III). The second work reports the acoustic field response to broadband input signals applied to both free-standing and nano-thinfilm-substrate thermo-acoustic devices (Objectives I and III). The fabrication of optoacoustic lens using CNT have also been reported in the second work [2] (Objectives II). For the first work, a simplified analytical pressure solution for thermal-acoustic wave response generated by using suspended multiwall carbon nanotube (MWCNT) thin film in different fluidic environments has been developed [1]. The solution consists of the near-field solution and the far-field solution. The electricity power input is a key element to control the thermal-acoustic wave pressure level. The dependence of the solution on axial distance from the source origin is investigated for different fluidic environments. Excellent agreement between analytical solutions and published experimental results has been reported. A number of numerical examples for different parameters have been studied for various liquids and gases including air, argon, water, and ethanol. Accurate analytical approximations for the thermal-acoustic wave response, and amplitude functions for different temperatures in fluids of varying densities have been proposed. It is concluded in this project that the analytical work not only agrees better with experiment but also offers more convincing analytical prediction for the generation and propagation of thermal-acoustic wave in different fluids. For the second work, acoustic field responses to broadband input signals applied to both free-standing and nano-thinfilm-substrate thermo-acoustic devices are developed theoretically by using the Fourier transformation have been established [2]. A series of signals, including single-frequency signal, square root signal, periodic triangle wave signal, and periodic rectangular pulse signal, have been applied to these TA devices in simulations and the acoustic pressure responses have been investigated. The single frequency results show good agreement with previously published experimental results. Alternative methods for reproducing the original signals with small distortion and low power consumption have been introduced. The excellent performance of the TA devices on broadband signal responses has been concluded and the research will provide a design approach for sound parametric array and underwater communication equipment.

11215415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11215415.value: There are two directions for further development, direct research extension and the research spin-offs. Direct further research will focus mainly on the application of CNT thin-film and related devices for generating focused and intensified ultrasound in two areas, (i) sonar equipment for underwater imaging and detection [1]; and (ii) medical equipment for detecting tumor, killing cancerous cells, fracturing biological stones, etc [2]. For research spin-offs, it has been proven that the theory, analytical modelling and numerical approach are certainly useful in nonlinear dynamical systems [3,4], bifurcation and chaos [5] and static-dynamic response for vibration of structures [6,7]. Further works in these directions will be pursued and reported.

11215415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215415.value: In this project, a practical research on the theory, analytical modeling, numerical simulation and experiment on carbon nanotube focused and intensified ultrasound has been developed. The research results for intensified ultrasound have been compared in numerical analysis and experiment data available and very good agreement has been reported. The research outcomes will have practical and engineering applications in medical equipment and sonar devices. The project has produced direct outcomes and significant research spin-offs in a total of seven research journal papers.

11216115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216115.value: As compared with the third-generation (3G) mobile communication, the fourth-generation (4G) system provides a much higher data rate and hence better enjoyments of mobile devices. However, with the rapid developments of mobile internet network and internet of things, it is anticipated that much faster data rates will be needed in the foreseeable future. To meet the need, the fifth-generation (5G) system is being actively developed and would be available around year 2020. While the 4G system is operated in the microwave (MW) band, it is almost certain that the 5G network will be operated in the millimeter wave (MMW) band. Thus, to obtain a smooth transition, the 5G system should also support the existing MW 4G system. As a result, it will require dual-frequency wireless systems that can be operated in both MW and MMW bands. Existing dual-frequency MW/MMW antennas were designed on planar (2-D) structures such as patch/reflectarray antennas. Since the design flexibility of 2-D structure is limited, the MW/MMW antennas have been obtained by just putting two separate MW and MMW antennas together, with no integration or optimization to reduce the antenna size and weight. In this project, the three-dimensional (3-D) dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is used to provide one more degree of freedom for the design. Other advantages of DRA include its small size, low loss, ease of excitation, and relatively wide bandwidth as compared with the microstrip antenna. For the first time, the MW DRA will be integrated with MMW antennas to obtain very compact hybrid MW/MMW antennas. In this project, both high- and low-gain MMW antennas will be used to meet different needs of MMW systems. In the former, the high-gain resonant cavity antenna (RCA) obtained from a hollow DRA will be used. Also, the circularly polarized hybrid DRA/RCA antenna will be investigated in the project. For the latter, the low-gain Fabry-Perot resonator antenna (FRPA) fabricated from the U-shaped DRA will be used. The hybrid DRA/FPRA design will be extended to obtain dualband/wideband characteristics for each of the MW and MMW bands. The hybrid antennas will be designed using Ansoft HFSS and substantiated by measurements. Systematic parametric studies will be carried out, and design guidelines will be given to facilitate designs of the hybrid antennas 相較於第三代（3G）移動通信，第四代（4G）的通信系統擁有更高的資料傳輸速率，從而使移動設備有更好的體驗。然而，隨著移動互聯網和物聯網的快速發展，可以預期的是在不遠的將來資料傳輸速率仍然需要進一步提升。第五代（5G）通信系統應運而生，並將於2020年前後完成構建。現有4G系統工作于微波（MW）頻帶，而一般深信5G網路是工作於毫米波（MMW）頻帶。為了平穩過渡，5G系統需要同時覆蓋既有的4G系統。因此，同時工作于微波和毫米波的雙頻系統是很有必要的。 現有的雙頻微波毫米波天線均為2D平面結構，例如貼片天線和反射陣天線。但是2D結構的設計有很大局限性，已有的微波毫米波天線僅是將兩個獨立的微波天線和毫米波天線放在一起，並未採取任何優化措施來縮小天線體積或減輕天線重量。本項目將採用三維（3D）介質諧振器天線（DRA），這種天線將比平面天線多一個維度的設計自由度。DRA還具有體積小，損耗低，易激勵，較微帶天線頻寬等優點。在本專案中，工作于微波頻段的DRA將首次與毫米波天線集成，形成一個結構緊湊的微波毫米波混合型天線。 本項目將分別設計高增益和低增益的毫米波天線，可以滿足不同毫米波系統的需求。對於高增益情況，我們將利用一個中空DRA來形成諧振腔天線以實現高增益。此外，還將研究圓極化的介質諧振器天線和諧振腔天線的混合型天線。對於低增益情況，我們將利用U型的介質諧振器來實現低增益的法布裡佩羅諧振器天線。隨後，分別工作于微波和毫米波頻帶的DRA和FPRA的混合型天線將會被擴展到雙頻帶和寬頻帶特性。 該混合型天線將採用ANSYS HFSS軟體模擬，並進行實驗驗證。本項目將系統性地進行參數模擬，並由此給出設計方法，這將大大提高設計這類混合型天線的進程。

11216115.label: Realisation of objectives
11216115.value: (a) Objective 1: Investigation of the basic microwave/millimeter-wave hybrid DRA/RCA antenna with high millimeter-wave antenna gain This part has been completed successfully. Both the microwave and millimeter-wave antennas have been integrated into a single hollow dielectric. A hollow dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) has been used for the microwave part. The aim of introducing this hollow region is to obtain a millimeter-wave Fabry-Perot resonator antenna (FPRA) in addition to the microwave DRA. For the microwave part, the DRA is excited in its HEM11delta mode by a vertical excitation strip. The excitation strip was cut from a piece of adhesive copper tape and stuck onto the DRA directly. It was soldered to the connector pin of the DRA port. Since there is a hollow dielectric cavity, the FPRA is also a resonant cavity antenna (RCA). It was fed by a WR-34 waveguide. To increase the FPRA gain, the cross-sectional area has been maximized in our design. The DRA was fabricated from a dielectric bar with a cross-sectional area of 5mmx50mm and the radius of the DR is given by RS = 24mm. The heights of the hollow region (HC) and dielectric superstrate (HS) have been designed as HC = 6.25 mm, HS = 1.19 mm at frequency f = 24 GHz. But since the resonant frequency of the DRA is much higher than 2.4 GHz for these heights, the DRA size has been increased to decrease the resonant frequency to 2.4 GHz. It has been found that the resonant frequency of the DRA is close to 2.4 GHz when HS = 12.99 mm. In this case, the maximum simulated gain of FRPA can be found at 24.25 GHz, which is the upper frequency of 24-GHz ISM band (24-24.25 GHz). To shift the maximum-gain frequency closer to 24.0 GHz, the values of HC and HS have been increased to 6.30mm and 13.10 mm, respectively. The hybrid antenna was simulated with ANSYS HFSS, with reasonable agreement between the measured and simulated results. (b) Objective 2: Investigation of the basic microwave/millimeter-wave hybrid DRA/FPRA antenna with low millimeter-wave antenna gain This part has been completed successfully. The hybrid antenna consisting of a microwave DRA and a millimeter-wave FPRA has been investigated. Each part has its own excitation port. The DRA and FPRA share a single dielectric block, giving a compact design. To avoid using bulky metal plates, adhesive copper tapes in place of conducting plates were stuck on the inner surface of the DR groove to form the FPRA. It not only simplifies the fabrication process but also reduces the antenna weight. To obtain the FPRA mode, the separation of the two parallel plates has been set at about a half wavelength. The DRA and FPRA were excited by a vertical conducting strip and sleeve-integrated L-probe, respectively. To reduce the cross-polar fields, the sleeve has been used to introduce a current opposite to the L-probe current. The groove has three sections to suppress the side lobes of the FPRA, with the groove width of the first and last sections being smaller than that of the middle section. The dual-frequency hybrid antenna was designed at 2.4GH/24GHz. A prototype was fabricated and tested to verify the simulations. (c) Objective 3: Design of the wideband/dualband hybrid DRA/FPRA antennas The wideband part has been completed successfully. It was directly extended from the second design of (b) above. Whereas a simple rectangular excitation strip was used in the basic DAR/FPRA antenna, a vertical inverted trapezoidal strip is used in this part to broaden the bandwidth. To further widen the bandwidth, the TE111 and TE113 modes of the DRA have been merged in the microwave band. For the millimeter-wave band, the FPRA and L-probe modes have also been merged to widen the bandwidth. As a result, a wideband dual-frequency hybrid DRA/FPRA antenna has been obtained. Reasonable agreement between the measured and simulated results has been observed. The dualband part, which is an extension to the wideband part, was started. However, the student finishing Objective 1, Objective 2, and Objective 3 (wideband part) graduated and returned to China before completing the dualband part. There was no experienced person who could follow up the work in the remaining project time. Nevertheless, given the success of the wideband part, it will not be a problem to design the dualband part.

11216115.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216115.value: (a) Dual-frequency hybrid antenna with high millimeter-wave antenna gain The dual-frequency hybrid DRA/FPRA with a high millimeter-wave antenna gain was designed at 2.4GHz/24GHz. It has been found that at 2.4 GHz, the measured impedance bandwidth, antenna gain, and total efficiency are given by 30.77%, 6.81 dBi (at 2.4 GHz), and 94.1%, respectively. For the FPRA (millimeter-wave) part, the measured impedance bandwidth and antenna gain are 4.67% and 18.2 dBi, respectively. The results have been summarized and published in the first journal paper of Part C. To obtain a very high millimeter-wave antenna gain, a millimeter-wave DRA reflectarray providing a high antenna gain of 23.9 dBi has been designed. The result has been summarized in the second journal paper of Part C (submitted). A low profile DRA that covers the entire reflectarray will be used to obtain the microwave band. (b) Dual-frequency hybrid antenna with low millimeter-wave antenna gain In this dual-frequency design, the measured and simulated impedance bandwidths of the microwave DRA are 10.06% and 7.32% respectively. For the DRA part, the measured and simulated boresight antenna gains of 6.71 dBi and 6.86 dBi have been obtained, respectively. Its maximum antenna efficiency is 94%. For the FPRA part, the measured and simulated impedance bandwidths are 6.3% and 5.1% respectively. The results have been summarized in the third journal paper of Part C (submitted). A dual-function DRA that simultaneously used as a panel switch has also been investigated. It has been found that the plastic switch does not affect the performance of the DRA. The result has been summarized in the fourth journal paper of Part C (submitted). The plastic switch will be replaced by a millimeter-wave DRA to obtain the millimeter-wave band. (c) Wideband hybrid DRA/FPRA antennas For the microwave DRA part, very wide measured and simulated impedance bandwidths of 38.24 % and 38.53 % have been obtained, respectively. Its measured and simulated boresight antenna gains are higher than 5 dBi. The measured total antenna efficiency has been found to vary between 74.6% and 95.4% across the impedance bandwidth. For the wideband FPRA part, the measured and simulated reflection coefficients are 16.18% and 18.99 %, respectively. As expected, broadside radiation patterns have been observed. It has been found that the measured and simulated peak gains are 11.30 dBi and 11.93 dBi, respectively. The findings have been summarized in the third journal paper of Part C (submitted).

11216115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216115.value: In this project, dual-frequency antennas with high frequency ratios have been developed. Today, energy harvesting is a hot topic due to the strong concern of green energy in the modern world. With the forthcoming 5G technology, the millimeter-wave power (e.g., 28 GHz) will increase in our environment. It is therefore of great interest to develop the dual-frequency energy-harvesting antenna or “Rectenna” (which is a technical term combining “rectifier” and “antenna”) with a high frequency ratio. To do this, we can make use of the dual-frequency hollow DRA that has been investigated in this project. The hollow region can be used to accommodate the rectifier circuits with a high frequency ratio (e.g., 3.5 GHz and 28 GHz for the 5G system). This is an attractive research topic.

11216115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216115.value: The fifth-generation (5G) system is being actively developed. It has been announced that the 5G system will include both the microwave (MW) and millimeter wave (MMW) bands. As a result, it will require dual-frequency wireless systems with a large frequency ratio. In general, existing dual-frequency MW/MMW antennas have been obtained by simply putting two separate MW and MMW antennas together, with no integration or optimization to reduce the antenna size and weight. In this project, the dual-frequency antenna has been integrated into a single structure, giving a very compact hybrid MW/MMW antenna. Both the high- and low-gain MMW antennas have been used to meet different needs. In the former, a hollow dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) has been used to obtain a high-gain MMW resonant cavity antenna. For the latter, the low-gain Fabry-Perot resonator antenna (FPRA) has been used. A wideband hybrid DRA/FPRA antenna has also been developed. The hybrid antennas have been designed using Ansoft HFSS, and reasonable agreement between the measured and simulated results has been obtained. Guidelines have been given to facilitate their designs.

11216215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216215.value: Metallic glasses constitute a class of new materials with unique properties for structural and functional use. Our ability to exploit the benefits of metallic glasses depends on identifying alloys of superior glass-forming ability. The nature of glass formation, particularly the glass-forming ability (GFA), is a long-standing key issue in the metallic glass community. Metallic glasses are inherently unstable. The culprit is crystallization, which can take place in the supercooled liquid region, both during cooling and heating. A fundamental question concerning crystallization and stability in metallic glasses is how the nanoscale crystalline particles nucleate and grow from the supercooled liquid state. Here we propose a concerted study to investigate the physical mechanisms of nanoscale crystalline precipitation in metallic glasses. We will achieve this goal by experimentally determining the crystallization pathways and kinetics, and use the results to elucidate the microscopic origin of the glass forming ability. The outcome of this project is expected to have broad implications in the study of disorder and non-equilibrium systems, and in developing processing technologies for nano-forming and 3D printing of metallic glasses for future applications. 金属玻璃因其独特的性能可广泛用作结构及功能材料。对合金的卓越的玻璃形成能力的判定是应用及发展金属玻璃的重要依据。金属玻璃形成的本质，尤其是玻璃形成能力，是金属玻璃领域长久未能解决的难题。由于金属玻璃具有不稳定性，在过冷状态下，冷却和加热都会导致结晶现象。纳米尺度的晶粒在过冷液态中的形核及长大过程是关于金属玻璃结晶及其稳定性的一项基本问题。我们在此提出一个同一筹划的研究计划用以考察金属玻璃中纳米晶粒的物理析出机制。通过各种实验手段，我们将确定结晶路径和晶化动力学，以此来阐述玻璃形成能力的微观本质。本项目对于无序及非平衡态体系的研究有着深远的意义，同时将推动金属玻璃纳米成型和3维打印技术的发展前景。

11216215.label: Realisation of objectives
11216215.value: This project was designed to study crystallization behavior in metallic glasses and correlate the crystallization kinetics with the glass forming ability (GFA). Metallic glasses constitute a class of new materials with unique properties for structural and functional use. Our ability to exploit the benefits of metallic glasses depends on identifying alloys of superior GFA. The nature of glass formation, particularly the GFA, is a long-standing key issue in the metallic glass community. Metallic glasses are inherently unstable. The culprit is crystallization, which can take place in the supercooled liquid region, both during cooling and heating. A fundamental question concerning crystallization and stability in metallic glasses is how the nanoscale crystalline particles nucleate and grow from the supercooled liquid state. In this project, we proposed a concerted study to investigate the physical mechanisms of nanoscale crystalline precipitation in metallic glasses. The crystallization pathways and crystallization kinetics were experimentally determined, and the results were used to elucidate the microscopic origin of the glass forming ability. The outcome of this project is expected to have broad implications in the study of disorder and non-equilibrium systems, and in developing processing technologies for nano-forming and 3D printing of metallic glasses for future applications. The proposed project had four objectives, see above. With respect to these project objectives, the project has been well executed overall, ultimately leading to 10 publications. In addition, two students and one postdoc has been trained. Specifically, (1) In-situ time-resolved neutron and synchrotron measurements were carried out to determine crystallization pathway and kinetics in a several prototypical metallic glass alloys. The experimental data were collected at world-leading facilities such as Advanced Photon Source, Argonne National Laboratory (USA), Spallation Neutron Source, Oak Ridge National Laboratory (USA), Australia Nuclear Science and Technology Organization (Australia). (2) In-situ study by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were conducted at Laboratory of Quantum Beam System Engineering, Hokkaido University (Japan). The laboratory operates one of the few ultra voltage TEM in the world, which enabled in-situ study of crystallization behaviors (see publications by Lan et al., Nature Communications (2017), and Wei et al., Intermetallics (2019)). (3) Atom probe tomography was carried out Nanjing University of Science and Technology (China). The results from this study, described in the PhD thesis by Xuelian Wu, have not yet been published. (4) A systematic study was carried out on crystallization kinetics for Zr-based metallic glass alloys with different compositions. Similarly, a concerted study was carried out on a Pd-Ni-P alloys, where a hidden phase and a liquid-to-liquid phase transformation was established. (5) The experimental data were analyzed to establish a correlation with GFA. For Zr-based alloys, a transition in nucleation mechanism was observed which is linked to GFA. For Pd-based alloys, a dynamic phase diagram was established showing regions of the newly discovered liquid phase. (6) Collaborations with other research groups worked Fe-based metallic glass alloys as well as Ni-P based nanoglass, see publications by Ge et al., Journal of Alloys and Compounds (2019) and Lan et al., Communications Physics (2019). (7) The project supported two PhD students and one postdoctoral research fellow. a. Ms. Xiaoya Wei, who received a PhD degree in 2018 b. Ms. Xuelian Wu, who received a PhD degree in 2019 c. Dr. Si Lan, Postdoctoral Fellow, who has later on become a Professor at Nanjing University of Science and Technology. The PhD students and postdoc all have travelled multiple times to many synchrotron and neutron sources in US, Japan, Australia, and all have received ample training and experience on the use of neutron and synchrotron scattering techniques.

11216215.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216215.value: This project led to 10 publications on crystallization kinetics in metallic glass. The studies were carried out in distinct metallic glass alloys, as a function of alloy composition, under pressure, and with different characterization methods. In a systematic study, crystallization kinetics of a series of Zr-Cu-Al bulk metallic glasses with different GFAs were investigated using differential scanning calorimetry, time-resolved neutron diffraction, and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy. The experimental results revealed a transition of classic-to-avalanche types of nucleation for the Zr-Cu-Al glass alloys upon isothermal annealing. Fundamental understanding of nucleation helps to control the crystallization products and the process. This work was published in Acta Mater., 2018. The study of Pd-Ni-P alloys revealed a hidden amorphous phase and the associated liquid-to-liquid phase transition in the supercooled liquid state. An anomaly in differential scanning calorimetry has been reported in a number of metallic glass materials in which a broad exothermal peak was observed between the glass and crystallization temperatures. The mystery surrounding this calorimetric anomaly is epitomized by four decades long studies of Pd-Ni-P metallic glasses, arguably the best glass-forming alloys. Here we show, using a suite of in situ experimental techniques, that Pd-Ni-P alloys have a hidden amorphous phase in the supercooled liquid region. The anomalous exothermal peak is the consequence of a polyamorphous phase transition between two supercooled liquids, involving a change in the packing of atomic clusters over medium-range length scales as large as 18 Å. With further temperature increase, the alloy reenters the supercooled liquid phase, which forms the room-temperature glass phase on quenching. This work was published in Nature Communications, 2017, which was featured in Nature Communications collection series, Metallurgy, see https://www.nature.com/collections/gxfyskqtkm/content/bulk-metallic-glasses Using simultaneous wide- and small-angle X-ray scattering (WAXS/SAXS) with high-energy synchrotron X-ray, the low-temperature crystallization kinetics of Zr46Cu46Al8 bulk metallic glass was investigated during isothermal annealing. Quantitative analysis of the WAXS intensity data indicated that the crystallization process was dominated by steady-state homogeneous nucleation and three-dimensional diffusion-controlled growth. This observation was corroborated by quantitative analysis of the SAXS data showing a saturation of the growth of nanoscale crystallites. Comparison of simultaneously measured WAXS and SAXS data showed evidence of composition fluctuation prior to crystallization, suggesting that the crystallization was facilitated by nanoscale phase separation which established regions of favorable compositions catalyzing crystallization. This work was published in Appl. Phys. Lett., 2019.

11216215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216215.value: The stability of supercooled liquid phase remains a key issue in the study of metallic glass. During the study of crystallization in Pd-Ni-P metallic glass alloys, we found an anomalous exothermal peak (AEP). Using a suite of in situ experimental techniques, it was demonstrated that Pd-Ni-P alloys have a hidden amorphous phase in the supercooled liquid state. The anomalous exothermal peak is the consequence of a polyamorphous phase transition between two supercooled liquids, involving a change in the packing of atomic clusters over medium-range length scales as large as 18 Å. The discovery of a hidden low-temperature liquid phase in Pd-Ni-P alloy renewed the debate on the nature of liquid-to-liquid phase transition. From practical point of view, the outcome of our study raises a possibility to manipulate the structure and hence the stability of metallic glasses through heat treatment. We hope to continue the study of stability of supercooled liquids, particularly with regard to liquid-to-liquid phase transition, and to characterize the nature of the phase transition. The proposed study will call for unique sample environment, such as a electrostatic levitator, for access to supercooled liquid region, and fast measurements in order to resolve the rapidly changing structures before crystallization sets in.

11216215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216215.value: Metallic glass is considered to be the material of the future. It is stronger and more compliant than crystalline alloys, a combination that leads to high resilience that can sustain larger elastic deformation than found in crystalline alloys. Because of these properties, metallic glass has been used in a range of applications such as sports equipment, medical devices and electricity transformers. A long-standing issue in metallic glass research is to figure out the structure or atomic packing in the material. In this project, the research team discovered a hidden amorphous phase in the formation of metallic glass, where atoms show a different kind of packing. This research achievement, which has been published in the internationally acclaimed journal Nature Communications solved a 40-year scientific mystery. The paper was also featured in Nature Communications collection series, Metallurgy, see https://www.nature.com/collections/gxfyskqtkm/content/bulk-metallic-glasses This project embodies the true spirit of international collaborations, involving scientists from four continents. The research has been designed at CityU, but the team took advantage of state-of-the-art facilities, the synchrotron source at Argonne National Laboratory in US, the ultra-high voltage electron microscope at Hokkaido University in Japan, and the neutron scattering instrument at the Australian Center for Neutron Scattering in Australia.

11216415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216415.value: Near field measurement has been widely used as an efficient and effective method for EMC diagnoses purpose in PCB designs. The far-field radiated emission level of an electronic device, in accordance with the EMC test requirements, can be evaluated based on the measured near field emission level of that device. To predict the far field emission, an equivalent current source from near-field measurement is first reconstructed based on the Huygens’ equivalence principle; the far field radiation pattern can then be calculated from the equivalent current source. This Huygens’ equivalence principle typically requires the measurements of at least two tangential electric and/or magnetic field on the measurement plane of the device. When the dimension of the device is smaller than the wavelength of the concerned frequencies, it can be considered as electrically small, especially in the case of an IC chip or a PCB. The equivalent current source can easily be reconstructed by using only one single field component of the near field measurement. By employing the Uniqueness Theory, the far field solution exists with the knowledge such boundary values, which can be evaluated from the equivalent current source. In the project, we investigate a novel approach in obtaining a planner equivalent current source to that of an electrically small PCB, using only the normal components of the magnetic field perpendicular to the surface of the PCB. This study will establish a simple and yet novel approach to estimate the far field radiation pattern, for EMC diagnostic and redesign of PCBs.

11216515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216515.value: “Strain engineering” originally refers to a general strategy employed in semiconductor manufacturing to enhance device performance (or saying, electron/hole mobility) by modulating strain in the transistor channel. Recently a new concept of “elastic strain engineering (ESE)” has been proposed to tailor the physical and chemical properties by mechanically changing the lattice strain (elastic strain). Unlike those strained by epitaxial growth in conventional strain engineering, the functional properties tuned by elastic strain engineering can be flexible, continuous and reversible. As a theoretical concept, tuning lattice parameter for desired properties wasn’t new, but one of the key factors to experimentally achieve ESE was to have materials that can sustain very large elastic strain (ε>1%) without being relaxed by plasticity or fracture (most conventional materials can only sustain 0.2-0.3% elastic strain). Until recently, as the advances in synthesis and the explosive proliferation of nanomaterials with “ultra-strength”, ESE has become an experimental reality. Despite that elastic strain engineering has been theoretically proposed as a powerful way of fine-tuning nanomaterials’ properties to create functional nanodevices with novel applications, experimental studies are still very scarce. So in this project, we propose to carry out a range of in situ nanomechanical, electro-mechanical and spectroscopy characterizations for a few representative low-dimensional nanomaterials, to quantify their tensile elastic strain limits and “ultra-strength”---the foundation of ESE. Through the in situ TEM, we try to further understand the origin of “ultra-strength”, and investigate the corresponding size effect in crystal elasticity at the atomic level. Through in situ tensile straining, we will quantitatively characterize the piezoresistive responses of semiconductor (Si and Ge) nanowires as well as 2-D atomic sheets (e.g. MoS2) with large elastic strain, and investigate conductance characteristics of strained ultrathin Au nanowires. In addition, we will try to tailor the bandgap structures of extremely strained semiconductor nanowires (e.g. Ge nanowire was predicted to have an indirect-to-direct bandgap transition at ε>5%) and possibly 2-D atomic sheets. The successful implementation of this project will strengthen our understanding on the concept of ESE and allow us to identify a few “ultra-strength” materials with highly tunable functional properties for device applications, for which the potential commercial value has been already demonstrated by the billion-dollar strained semiconductor industry. Scientifically, our in situ experiment results will greatly complement the theoretical and modeling efforts, and together they shall provide unprecedented details and quantitative insights into how nanomaterials response to applied strain with desired functional properties. 作為半導體工業中的一種成熟而通用的技術，“應變工程”所謂的通過調節晶體管內部的應變來增強器件性能（提高電子、空穴遷移率）已被廣泛認可。近年來，一種新的概念“彈性應變工程”被提出：通過力學手段改變晶格應變（彈性應變），以此調控物理和化學性能。不同於在傳統的“應變工程”中使用的外延生長來引入應變，通過彈性應變工程調控材料的功能性質具有靈活，連續，以及可回復的特點。盡管從理論概念的角度並不難以理解，但在實驗上實現“彈性應變工程”要求材料能夠經受較大的彈性應變（沒有塑形弛豫過程也不發生斷裂），而大多傳統塊體材料只能經受極微小的彈性變形。直到最近，得益於材料制備技術的發展和雨後春筍般“超強”納米材料的出現，“彈性應變工程”才在實驗上可能實現。因此本項目中，我們將對一些具有代表性的低維納米材料進行原位定量力學加載，定量化測量其拉伸彈性應變極限（“彈性應變工程”的基礎）。同時利用原位透射電鏡，我們可以進一步理解材料“超強”性能的微觀結構起源，並且在原子尺度下研究晶體中的“彈性”的尺寸效應。此外，我們將通過原位力電耦合及力光耦合的測量，嘗試調節具有超大彈性應變極限的半導體納米線（或者二維原子薄膜）的能帶結構。 這一項目的成功實現將增強我們對於“彈性應變工程”概念的理解，並且幫助我們尋找具有工業上器件應用前景的，可調控其功能性質的“超強”（Ultra-Strength）低維納米材料。從基礎科學上講，我們的原位實驗結果可以對先前的理論和模擬工作進行驗證，並為材料在小尺度上其物理性質如何受應力應變影響提供前所未有的微觀細節和定量數據。

11216515.label: Realisation of objectives
11216515.value: 1. We quantified the tensile elastic strain limits and “ultra-strength” of a few representative semiconductor nanowires, ultrathin metallic nanowires and 2-D atomic sheets --- the foundation of elastic strain engineering (ESE): In 2016, we reported the discovery on the “ultra-large elasticity” in nanosized silicon, one of the most important electronic materials, demonstrated that high quality single crystalline silicon nanowires can be stretched above 10% elastic strain, with a few cases reaching 16% tensile strain, approaching to the theoretical elastic limit of silicon. Published by AAAS in “Science Advances” (2016) entitled "Approaching the ideal elastic strain limit in silicon nanowires", this work has stimulated great interests in both academia and semiconductor industry, and received extensive media coverage worldwide. On the other hand, we have successfully developed a new platform for 2D materials mechanical testing, and performed in situ tensile tests of freestanding monolater graphene in a scanning electron microscope. The experiment showed that the tensile strength of CVD (chemical vapour deposition)-grown monolayer graphene can reach 50 to 60 GPa (gigapascal), with elastic strain up to 6%, and the measured Young’s modulus is very close to the theoretical value of ~1,000 GPa. Its strength and stretchability make graphene a suitable material for manufacturing flexible electronic devices, such as transistors with better robustness, organic light-emitting diodes, and other mechanical components. This work has been recently published in “Nature Communication” (2020) titled “Elastic Strain of Free-Standing Monolayered Graphene” and highlighted by “Editor’s Choice” in the 21 February 2020 issue of “Science”. 2. Through in situ TEM study, we obtained some essential understanding about the origin of “ultra-strength” and its underlying mechanisms, and we also investigated the corresponding size effect in crystal materials’ elasticity at the atomic level. For example, the fracture behaviors of Si nanowires at above high elastic strain were studied by postmortem TEM analysis while MD simulation was used to confirm the multi-step process of the fractured nanowires. This work was published in the journal “Acta Mechanica” titled “Fracture of A Silicon Nanowire at Ultra-Large Elastic Strain”. Ultra-strength and fracture mechanisms of multilayer 2D materials were also studied by in situ TEM. In-plane fracture behaviors of multilayer graphene nanosheets are characterized and quantified under tensile loading. Published in the journal “Nanotechnology” titled “In situ tensile fracturing of multilayer graphene nanosheets for their in-plane mechanical properties”, we show that, generally, the fracture strengths of graphene nanosheets decrease as the thickness (or layers) increases; fracture process of the thicker nanosheets includes the initial flattened stage, the stable elastic stage, and the rapid fracture with brittle characteristics, while the thinner nanosheets show obvious delamination between the atomic layers at fracture. Also, the in-plane mechanical properties of MoS2 membranes were investigated by in situ SEM tensile testing. Published in the journal “Nanoscale”, we show that, under the uniaxial tensile loading, brittle fracture caused failure in a highly localized region of the MoS2 membranes and their mechanical properties showed a thickness effect: the strengths of the relatively thicker MoS2 membranes (thickness around hundreds of nanometers) distribute from ∼100 to ∼250 MPa, while the corresponding values of the MoS2 nanosheets (thickness around tens of nanometers) increase significantly to more than 1GPa. 3. Through in situ tensile straining, we characterize the electro-mechanical/piezoresistive responses of various semiconductor nanowires and their hierarchical composite structures under large elastic strain, and investigate their flexible electronics applications: For example, MnO2 nanowires were used to fabricate a wearable sensor for the practical application in a healthy system and human-computer interaction. The nanomechanical behavior of the graphite flakes and MnO2 NWs composed of the sensing materials in the sensor was quantitatively analyzed by in situ TEM and SEM, respectively, for application in flexible electronics. As a proof-of-concept, the flexible sensor using a leaf vein and graphite flakes-MnO2 nanowires-Melamine foam showed a highly sensitive and durable ability, which is published on the journal “Applied Materials Today” (2020) titled “Nano electromechanical approach for flexible piezoresistive sensor”. 2D materials such as graphene could be used in flexible electronics. We employed a 3D cellular copper foam (CF) combined with the graphene sheets (GSs) as the support matrix to bridge the active material with nickel fiber (NF) current collector, significantly increasing surface area and decreasing the interface resistance. The in situ scanning electron microscope (SEM) microcompression test demonstrated its superior mechanical recoverability while the assembled flexible and wearable device presented a superior energy density, and can power a flexible strain sensor, solar cell, and nanogenerator. This work in published on the journal “ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces” titled “Graphene-Bridged Multifunctional Flexible Fiber Supercapacitor with High Energy Density”. Moreover, in order to make a highly sensitive portable piezoresistive sensor with a fast response time in an extended linear working range to meet the rapid development of artificial intelligence, interactive human-machine interfaces, and flexible electronics, we introduced the hierarchical pores across several size orders from micro- to larger scale into the intrinsically flexible graphene-based electrode materials. We achieved a flexible sensor with a prominent sensitivity of 11.9 kPa-1 in the linear range of 3 Pa to ∼21 kPa and a rapid response time of 20 ms to positively monitor the pulse rate, voice recognition, and true force value for biomedical and interactive human-machine interface application assisted by an analog-digital converter. This work in published in the journal “ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces” titled “Cellular Carbon-Film-Based Flexible Sensor and Waterproof Supercapacitors”. 4. Through in situ tensile straining, we demonstrated that one can tune the bandgap structures of extremely strained semiconductor nanowires (such as single crystalline Si nanowires). Based on first-principles calculation, the geometric and electric properties of <110>-oriented Si nanowires with diameter ~1.5nm under ultralarge strain are firstly investigated, we show the bandgap reduction upon tensile straining. When the applied strain is more than 19%, the Si nanowires could even transform from semiconductor to metallic behavior, with no bandgap. The work is published in the journal “The Journal of Physical Chemistry” (2018) titled “Deep Ultra-Strength Induced Band Structure Evolution in Silicon Nanowires”. Later, based on refined first-principles calculation, the structural and electric properties of much larger silicon nanowires, more realistic and comparable results to our experimentally tested samples (∼100 nm diameter), under ultralarge strain are comparatively investigated. The simulation result, published in the journal “Journal of Applied Physics” (2019) indicates that strong anisotropic effects are induced by loading strain along all different orientations. Simultaneously, the band structures evolution demonstrates electronic anisotropy with the loading strain on three orientations. Silicon keeps an indirect bandgap under the increased strain along with the (100) orientation while transforming to a direct bandgap with strain along <111> orientations. Ultimately, >16% ultralarge elastic strain would diminish the bandgap and result in metallization in strained Si certain orientation. This result may serve as a guide for further experimental investigation of such “elastic strain engineering” and potential electronic and optoelectronic applications

11216515.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216515.value: Through the research of this project, we successfully achieved large elastic strain deformation of various 1D and 2D nanomaterials, including single-crystalline Si nanowires with diameter ~100nm can be repeatedly stretched above 10% elastic strain at room temperature, with a few samples even reached ~16% tensile strain, approaching the theoretical elastic limit of silicon (17 to 20%). (see our Science Advance paper). Furthermore, the fracture behaviors of Si nanowires at high elastic strains were studied with the assist of TEM analysis and MD simulations. (see our Acta Mechanica paper). Based on the experimental result, the strain-induced electric property changes of silicon nanowires under ultralarge strain are comparatively investigated via DFT first principle calculations. Direct-to-indirect bandgap transformation was predicted to occurs for <111>-oriented Si nanowires when applied strain is larger than 14%. When the applied strain is more than 16%, Si nanowires with <110> orientation could even transform from semiconductors to metallic state (see our Journal of Applied Physics paper). These results provide insights into understanding “elastic strain engineering” of semiconductor applications and demonstrate the possibility of tuning the electronic and optical properties through pure mechanical straining of functional materials. Beside 1D nanomaterials, elastic properties of 2D materials were also investigated by using our developed new platform, for example, the elastic properties and stretchability of free-standing single-crystalline monolayer graphene grown by CVD has been demonstrated, for the first time (see our Nature Communications paper). The measured Young’s modulus is close to 1TPa, aligning well with the theoretical value, while the representative engineering tensile strength reaches ~50-60GPa with sample-wide elastic strain up to ~6%, which is significantly higher than previous estimations. In addition, elastic straining and fracture behavior of multilayer 2D materials such as graphene and MoS2 multilayers were also studied (see our Nanoscale and Nanotechnology papers) and we later characterized their electro-mechanical and piezoelectrical responses in their composite structures and devices, to demonstrate many functional applications, in particular in flexible electronics and energy devices.

11216515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216515.value: The further development regarding this project is to experimentally explore the bandgap modulation of various 1D and 2D semiconductors, in particular wide-bandgap semiconductors. According to our findings, including large attainable elastic strain and calculated bandgap changes, many of the 1D and 2D covalent crystals could be tuned for their electronic properties, through changing the elastic/lattice strain, as well as the investigation on the practical device application based on “elastic strain engineering”. Combine our developed nanomechanical straining methods with in situ electrical/optical detection methods, such as cathodoluminescence (CL), photoluminescence (PL) and Raman spectroscopy, the change of bandgap with the increasing or decreasing of elastic strain would be measured in real time. Moreover, theory and calculations remain needed to further predict upper bound of the elastic strain and how much change in properties can be induced by strain in real crystals. The effect of elastic strain on other physical properties, such as thermal properties and optical properties etc., as well as chemical properties could be also numerically and experimentally investigated. In the long run, well-controlled microfabrication of the semiconductor nanostructures from bulk crystals, even at wafer scale, would be necessary in order to bring such “strain engineering” device applications in to reality.

11216515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216515.value: The concept of “elastic strain engineering” (ESE) is actually based on the fact that material’s physical and chemical properties are functions of the lattice parameters of the underlying crystal lattice, or the elastic strain with respect to the stress-free state. In this project, we experimentally demonstrate that ultralarge elastic strain can be indeed achieved through uniaxial tensile straining nanoscale semiconductors (such as silicon nanowires) and 2D materials (such as graphene and MoS2). Based on first-principles calculations, the reduction of bandgap with the increasing of elastic strain is measured, and the desired direct-to-indirect bandgap transformation (such as for silicon as an indirect bandgap material) under certain strain condition may also occur. Moreover, underlying mechanisms of such “ultra-strength” phenomena and associated fracture behavior of various 1D and 2D nanomaterials were studied by in situ TEM method with the assist of molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. Our quantitative experiment results well complement our modeling efforts, to build more confidence in ESE practices. Our research opens up new possibilities for tuning the functional properties, such as electronic, optical, thermal properties, of a low-dimensional material, by mechanically stretching only, leading to unprecedent electronic and optoelectronic device applications in the future.

11216815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216815.value: 高能材料包括煙火劑和推進劑等，有著廣泛的民事和軍事應用，比如採礦、爆破、汽車安全氣囊、軍品、空間技術等。高能材料通常可以分為單分子高能材料和復合高能材料，單分子高能材料通常具有較高的能量釋放速率但它們的能量密度較低，復合高能材料能量密度較高但它們的能量釋放速率較低。納米高能複合物繼承了傳統高能材料的高能量密度優點，同時也可以實現較高的能量釋放速率。尽管納米高能複合物的研究已经开展了二十几年，有两个重要问题亟需研究。一个是将納米高能複合物和煙火劑相復合，在反應過程中煙火劑分解所產生的氣體可以促進納米高能複合物的火焰對流傳播，而納米高能複合物所產生的高溫高熱可以彌補對環境的熱損失從而有利於在微小型裝置中的應用。另外一個重要問題是納米高能複合物在小尺度下的燃燒傳播機理仍不明確，納米高能複合物的一個重要應用是作為微小系統裝置的能源，因此它們在微小尺度下的燃燒性能亟需研究。本項目將合成新型煙火劑內嵌的納米高能複合物陣列，並且深入系統地研究它們的放熱特性和燃燒性能，特別是在微小尺度下的燃燒性能。本項目研究將會填補納米高能複合物和傳統煙火劑之間的空白，提供製作煙火劑內嵌的納米高能複合物陣列的方法，揭示它們的壓力和熱力補償機理和在微小尺度下的燃燒行為，為實際應用提供指導。

11216815.label: Realisation of objectives
11216815.value: (1) This project developed a precisely controllable preparation process of novel explosive-embedded nanoenergetic composite arrays. A silicon wafer is used as the substrate. It is ultrasonically cleaned in acetone and ethanol sequentially, rinsed with deionized water, and then blow-dried by compressed air. A thin layer of Cu2O with a thickness of 100 nm is deposited onto the silicon wafer by sputtering. A layer of copper film with a thickness of 1 µm is then deposited on the top of the Cu2O layer by e-beam evaporation. After that, the wafer is put into a muffle furnace for thermal oxidation in static air so as to grow the CuO nanowire arrays on the substrate. Al layer with a nominal thickness of 1,500 nm is then deposited onto the wafer by sputtering to realize the CuO/Al nanothermite arrays. CL20 is then loaded into the CuO/Al nanothermite arrays by dissolution and recrystallization process. CL20 solution with a certain molarity is prepared by dissolving raw powders in acetone. The solution is then dripped onto the as-prepared CuO/Al arrays. The hybrid CuO/Al/CL20 nanocomposite arrays are then finally achieved after the recrystallization of CL20. (2) This project obtained the detailed energetic properties and micro scale combustion/explosion behaviors of the explosive-embedded nanoenergetic composite arrays. Thermal analysis is conducted for raw CL20 powder and scraped CuO/Al/CL20 sample. The heat release properties of the material are analyzed by differential scanning calorimetry, and the loading amount of CL20 is analyzed by thermogravimetric analysis. Open burn experiments are carried out for the combustion of raw CL20, CuO/Al nanothermite, and hybrid CuO/Al/CL20 nanocomposites, respectively. The nanocomposite samples are scraped and loaded into a channel of a metallic block. The sample is ignited from one end by a vertical laser in air atmosphere, and then the combustion flame self-propagates throughout the channel. The combustion propagation process is recorded by a high-speed camera. The decrease in activation energy for CL20 after integrating with CuO/Al could be attributed to the nano-sized and/or the catalyst-effect of CuO/Al nanothermite arrays within this energetic system rather than the change in crystal form. The improved thermal conductivity due to the nanoscale metal, or the more physical adsorption sites caused by nanosized components would trap more pyrolysis products, subsequently would help to activate the molecules and promote the decomposition of CL20. (3) This project achieved the chemical reaction and micro scale combustion wave propagation mechanisms of the explosive-embedded nanoenergetic composite arrays. It is found that the hybrid CuO/Al/CL20 composite exhibits a vigorous and stable combustion in the open burn experiments. This can be attributed to the embedded CL20. Integration of explosives with nanothermite has a complementary effect. An intimate contact between CL20 and CuO/Al arrays could benefit the conduction mechanism of heat transfer. The embedded CL20 could be ignited by the large amount of heat released by the thermite reaction of CuO-Al and rapidly decomposes with the catalysis of the nanothermite arrays. The enormous gaseous products produced by CL20 could react with aluminum and also promote the convection dominated heat transfer to a certain extent, contributing to the energy release and forming a virtuous circle of explosive-nanothermite, which complement the entire energetic system. As a result, the more sufficient and vigorous combustion with a steady flame is obtained. Various factors, such as the loading density and constrained state can influence the flame propagation speed. For nanoenergetic materials with low TMD, the more trapped air in the voids would result in the convection dominant mechanism of heat transfer and lead to accelerated flame propagation. However, the gases attenuate this effect in acceleration by liberatingly escaping from the reaction zone rather than enhancing the convection due to the open characteristic. A majority of energy is scattered abroad with the escaping gaseous intermediates or products that cannot be trapped by the open channel, accompanied by rapid pressure loss, which would not effectively contribute to the convective mode of energy propagation, resulting in a slow flame propagation speed. This is one of the possible reasons why CL20 embedded sample with a higher gas output has a slower flame propagation speed in open configuration. Despite the low burning rate, the sample integrated with CL20 exhibits a relatively stable combustion flame. In this perspective, the stable combustion of hybrid CuO/Al/CL20 composite could provide continual energy output and enhance the reliability in practical application. (4) Many interesting results based on CuO arrays have been achieved (please refer to the publications in item 8 of Part C: Research Output), which are considered as the by-products of this project.

11216815.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216815.value: Major findings: (1) Explosive CL20 has been in situ integrated with core/shell CuO/Al nanothermite arrays to form hybrid nanoenergetic composites. The CuO/Al nanothermite arrays are fabricated by thermal oxidation of deposited Cu film followed by sputtering of aluminum. CL20 is then in situ embedded in the nanothermite arrays by a dissolution and recrystallization process. (2) It is found that instead of forming particles, the recrystallized CL20 fills and connects the CuO/Al arrays and the gaps of the curved wires as a linker with a filmy morphology. The integration of CL20 with CuO/Al arrays is facile and in situ, taking advantage of the core/shell array structures, and realizes an intimate contact between the explosive and nanothermite. The loading amount of CL20 is proved to be controllable, and the total heat of reaction is enhanced after the integration of CL20. (3) The activation energy for decomposition of integrated CL20 decreases 18.2% compared with that of raw CL20 material. Moreover, the CL20 embedded nanoenergetic composite exhibits a favorable burning behavior with a violent and steady combustion flame. Research outcome: Ten SCI journal papers, one patent, and one conference paper have been published as the major research outcome of this project. Moreover, three research students have been awarded PhD degrees via undertaking the related research work of this project.

11216815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216815.value: Although much progress has been made in this project, the limitations still exist. The combustion propagation speed for nanoenergetic composites developed in this project is lower than the detonation velocity of TNT, a commonly used explosive. In order to achieve higher combustion/deflagration/detonation speed, new energetic materials with excellent inherent energetic characteristics should be employed. Energetic coordination polymers (ECPs) are mainly constructed from energetic nitrogen-rich organic ligands and metal centers, have recently attracted great attention as highly energetic materials. They possess abundant gas elements from organic ligands, which allow them to generate large amounts of gas during thermal decomposition, producing high peak pressures. Novel energetic materials with high energy density, high reactivity, and especially high-pressure output can be obtained by combining ECPs with aluminum. We plan to in situ synthesize nanostructured ECPs/Al energetic composites on microchips. The exothermic properties, combustion/explosion, and pressure output of the ECPs/Al energetic composites off and on the energetic microchips will be studied comprehensively. Special attention will be given to the combustion/explosion behavior at micro scale.

11216815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216815.value: Energetic materials, mainly including explosives, pyrotechnics and propellants, are widely used in various civilian and defense applications such as mining, deconstruction, automobile airbags, ordnance, and space technology. Energetic materials can be categorized as monomolecular energetic materials (e.g. TNT) and energetic composites (e.g. gunpowder). Normally, monomolecular energetic materials exhibit ultrahigh energy-release rates, but their energy density is low; on the contrary, energetic composites have high energy density, but their reaction rates are lower than those of explosive compounds. Nanoenergetic composites inherit the high-energy-density merit of traditional energetic composites. At the same time, as the mass diffusion distance reduces and interfacial area increases drastically, the reaction rate is boosted. This project synthesized novel explosive-embedded nanoenergetic composites which are based on metal oxide nanosphere arrays. The nanosphere arrays are prepared by interfacial self-assembly of colloidal particles. Explosives are then formed among the voids of nanosphere arrays by controlled crystallization. The energetic properties and combustion/explosion characteristics are studied comprehensively and in depth. The project enriches the knowledge about the energetic materials in terms of construction method of explosive-embedded nanoenergetic arrays, pressure and heat compensation mechanisms, and combustion behaviors at micro scale. The research outputs can also serve as guidance to the future practical applications.

11216915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216915.value: Antennas play an important role in recent mobile communications. Forecast of 5G mobile communications launching in the year of 2020, it will boost the data rate up to several giga-byte per second for instant massive data communications with seamless mobility and high coverage. 5G networks probably require high integration with 2G, 3G and LTE systems to achieve the proposed ultimate goals. These enforceable requirements post challenges to our antenna designers and researchers. Unlike the conventional generations of mobile communications, the operation of 5G networks may move to the millimeter-wave spectrum with the steerable directional beam at mobile phones and base stations. Wireless industries often look into emerging antenna technologies that can provide a low-cost and high-performance antenna with wideband, high gain, stable radiation, and steerable beam characteristics. This study attempts to explore a number of new approaches that will apply to mobile devices and base stations for the coming 5G communications. The devoted antennas combined with conventional PCB and recent 3D printing technologies to be developed is low-cost and simple. In this proposal, four identified research objects will be investigated. Firstly, a study of wider bandwidth of directional differential-fed or SIW-fed antennas will be carried out. The solution by composing slots and dipole/patch radiating sources shows improvement in the gain and bandwidth. Secondly, the gain enhancement technique for the antenna by adding a novel dielectric polarizer will be investigated. A noticeable gain improvement resulted in potential frequency spectrums can be used in next generation of mobile communication systems. Thirdly, a new dielectric polarized lens antenna is formed by incorporating the positive results driven from the first & second hypotheses. Lastly, a multi-port and steerable directional beam antenna for high-gain achievement with linear or circular polarization will be demonstrated. 天線作為電磁波發射與接收的重要部件，在現代無線通訊系統中具有十分關鍵的地位。預計到2020年，第五代（5G）移動通信技術將達到每秒幾千兆比特的傳輸速率，並且實現無縫遷移以及更高的信號覆蓋率。為此，我們需要將5G 網路與 2G、3G 以及 LTE 等無線通訊系統整合在一起。為了滿足未來的通信系統的要求，天線的設計將會面臨更多的挑戰。與傳統的移動通信不一樣的是，第五代移動通信網路將會使用毫米波頻段，並且將波束可調技術應用到手機與基站上邊。因此，無線通訊的研究人員正在試圖尋找一些新的天線技術來降低天線的成本，提高天線的整體性能，實現天線的寬頻，高增益，方向圖穩定，波束可控等技術指標。 本文針對5G通信系統的要求，提出了一些新的天線的設計方法，並將其應用於手機設備與基站之中。這些天線的設計方法將傳統的PCB工藝與新型的3D列印技術相結合，從而有效得簡化天線的加工過程，降低天線的生產成本。本文提出了以下四個研究目標：第一，研究寬頻的差分饋電天線以及介質集成波導饋電的天線；通過將縫隙天線與偶極子天線或者貼片天線相結合，可以有效地拓展天線的頻寬，提高天線的增益。第二，通過添加一個新型的介質極化器來實現圓極化，並且進一步提高天線的增益。這種方法能夠有效的提高天線的增益，適用於第五代移動通信對天線的要求。第三，根據上面提出的兩種方法，設計出一款新型的具有極化器特性的透鏡天線。最後，研究具有線極化以及圓極化特性的波束可調的高增益天線。

11216915.label: Realisation of objectives
11216915.value: This research project demonstrates new antenna technologies for millimeter-wave applications. The project is successfully completed with excellent outputs that matched with our defined objectives in this GRF project. The outputs of this project have been published in the leading journals of antenna research area. We here give an overview of this project achievement. 1. To investigate wideband differential-fed and SIW-fed antennas. To begin this research, we proposed to develop a wideband feeding source which can be later applied to other designs in this GRF project. We have successfully developed a wideband-fed structure integrated with the dielectric resonator antenna. The feed source can provide a wide impedance bandwidth of 50% for the millimeter-wave bands. The proposed source can produce a balanced electric field distribution on an aperture fabricated on high-frequency PCB. This work has been reported and published in [a]. [a] K. X. Wang, and H. Wong, “A wideband millimeter-wave circularly polarized antenna with 3D printed polarizer”, IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, vol. 65, no. 3, pp. 1038-1046, Mar. 2017. 2. To investigate and design wideband antennas with dielectric polarizers. We introduce a novel 3-D-printed polarizer, which consists of several air and dielectric slabs to transform the polarization of the antenna radiation from linear to circular. The proposed polarizer is placed above a radiating aperture operating at the center frequency of 60 GHz. An electric ﬁeld, E, radiated from the aperture generates two components of electric ﬁelds, Ex and Ey . After passing through the polarizer, both Ex and Ey ﬁelds can be degenerated with an orthogonal phase difference which results in having a wide axial ratio bandwidth. With the help of the thickness of the polarizer, the directivity of the radiation pattern is increased so as to devote high-gain and wideband characteristics to the antenna. The proposed antenna with the polarizer achieves a wide impedance bandwidth of 50% from 45 to 75 GHz for the reﬂection coefﬁcient less than or equal−10 dB, and yields an overlapped axial ratio bandwidth of 30% from 49 to 67 GHz for the axial ratio ≤ 3 dB. The maximum gain of the antenna reaches to 15 dBic. The proposed methodology of this design can apply to applications related to mmw wireless communication systems. The ultimate goal of this paper is to develop a wideband, high-gain, and low-cost antenna for the mmw frequency band. This research has been published in [a] and also received the best paper award [b] in the international conference of iWEM, London UK, in 2017. [b] K. X. Wang, and H. Wong, "A wideband millimeter wave CP antenna by using tapered dielectic polarizer", 2017 International Workshop on Electromagnetics: Applications and Student Innovation Competition, 30 May-1 June 2017, London, UK. 3. To investigate wideband and high-gain circularly-polarized antennas. A mode reconﬁgurable dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) to realize radiation pattern reconﬁguration was introduced in this project. We were the ﬁrst research group to demonstrate mode reconfiguration in the DRA for antenna applications. The DRA is composed of two zones: the inner zone is a solid cylinder fabricated by K9 glass (εr =6.85) and the outer zone is ﬁlled with a dielectric liquid—ethyl acetate (εr = 7.1). Both of them are put into a cylindrical container fabricated by 3-D printing technology and excited by a single coaxial probe. A mechanical reconﬁguration of broadside and conical radiation patterns can be achieved over a wide impedance bandwidth of 35.5%. This work has been published in IEEE TAP [c], and its extension work of a patch antenna version also reported in IEEE AWPL [d]. Furthermore, we exhibited the concept of mode reconfiguration in helical antennas, which has been successfully proved and published in IEEE TAP [e]. [c] Z. Chen, and H. Wong, “Wideband Glass and Liquid Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Pattern Reconfigurable Design”, IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, vol. 65, no. 5, pp. 2157-2164, May 2017. [d] K. X. Wang, and H. Wong, “A Reconfigurable CP/LP Antenna With Cross-Probe Feed”, IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters, vol. 16, pp. 669-672, 2017. [e] X. Yi, and H. Wong, "Reconfigurable Quadrifilar Helical Antenna", 2018 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation & USNC/URSI National Radio Science Meeting, 8-13 July 2018, Boston, USA. 4. To design steerable directional antennas for mobile communications. We extended the reconfigurable antenna technology from the project objective 3, and develop antenna array with beam forming and beam steering. A reconﬁgurable aperture-fed patch antenna array for ±45◦ polarization was first to carry out. We successfully integrated RF switches with a cross aperture to excite a square patch for achieving radiations from two orthogonal polarizations. This proposed antenna technology is suitable for recent high-speed mobile communications. This research work has been reported in IEEE Access [f]. On the other hand, we introduced a wideband millimeter-wave Fabry–Pérot cavity (FPC) antenna with switched-beam radiations for 5G applications. We proposed to use a quasi-curve reﬂector to excite multiple resonant modes in FPC. The proposed successfully building up a wideband FPC antenna at millimeter-wave frequency bands, which achieved an impedance bandwidth of 24% with the antenna gain of 17.6 dBi and a directivity of 18.8 dB at 60 GHz. The overall efﬁciency and aperture efﬁciency are 76% and 31%, respectively. In addition, a switched-beam antenna based on our proposed FPC antenna was developed. It achieves three switched beams at −18°, 0°, and 18° related to the broadside direction with a realized gain of 16 dBi at 60 GHz. Compared with the other switched-beam FPC antennas, our proposed antenna acquires the characteristics of wideband, high gain, and large beam tilted angle. This antenna technology ﬁnds a potential application in millimeter-wave communications such as 5G applications. This work has been published in IEEE TAP [g]. [f] W. Lin, and H. Wong, “Polarization Reconfigurable Aperture-Fed Patch Antenna and Array”, IEEE Access, vol. 4, pp. 1510-1517, 2016. [g] Q. Y. Guo, and H. Wong, "Wideband and high gain Fabry-Perot cavity antenna with switched beams for millimeter-wave applications", IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation, vol. 67, no. 7, pp. 4339-4347, July. 2019.

11216915.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216915.value: This research has published 6 journals and 8 conferences papers. Two PhD student, Mr. WANG Kaixu, and Mr. CHEN Zhe under my supervision completed their PhD degree in 2018. Parts of their research works were supported by this GRF project. One of our project entitled "A wideband millimeter wave CP antenna by using tapered dielectic polarizer" received a best paper award in iWEM conference in London UK in 2017. Major findings in this GRF are listed as follows: 1. 3D printed technology can work and design for high-frequency radiator, polarizer and array antenna for millimeter-wave applications. 2. Reconfigurability of multiple modes at patch antennas and dielectric resonator antennas are very useful in developing wideband performance in millimeter-wave bands. 3. Integration of lens, FPC, and substrate integrated technique can realize high-gain antennas at millimeter-wave. 4. Polarization reconfigurable, pattern reconfigurable, and beam reconfigurable techniques can improve the signal quality in millimeter-wave communication.

11216915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216915.value: This research focused on developing newly low-cost antenna technology for millimeter-wave applications. A further work of this research can be extended to terahertz frequency applications, which will be related to 6G communications. In addition, the developed reconfigurable technology in this project can be further investigated to other wireless systems and applications.

11216915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216915.value: This project proposed a low-cost antenna solution for millimeter-wave systems. The output of this research work can be applied to 5G mobile communications. We successfully demonstrate 3D printing technology and PCB fabrication technology can use to develop wideband and high-gain antennas. Four defined objectives are achieved including: 1. To investigate wideband differential-fed and SIW-fed antennas; 2. To investigate and design wideband antennas with dielectric polarizers; 3. To investigate wideband and high-gain circularly-polarized antennas; and 4. To design steerable directional antennas for mobile communications.

11217515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217515.value: Spatial-coupling is a recently proposed design technique for low-density parity check (LDPC) codes. The extension of the spatial-coupling principles to multi-user interference cancellation has also been reported. A relatively long codeword length is required to obtain a satisfactory performance for the existing spatially-coupled LDPC codes. In this project, we will investigate the application of the spatial-coupling principles in multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. MIMO has been identified as a key technology for future fifth generation (5G) cellular communication systems. It is known that multi-user concurrent transmission, over the same time and frequency, is necessary to fully exploit the advantages provided by MIMO. It is, however, a challenging problem to acquire accurate channel state information (CSI) required for multi-user MIMO transmission. This project aims at developing a solution to the channel estimation problem using spatial-coupling principles. Our research plan is as follows. We will study the length problem and devise short codes. This will provide coding methods that are applicable to practical systems. We will study the application of spatial-coupling in data-aided channel estimation in MIMO systems. It is known that the correlation among pilots of different users results in the so-called pilot contamination problem for large MIMO systems. The problem can be alleviated by a data-aided channel estimation technique, but code design becomes a difficult issue due to the variation of channel environments. Spatially-coupled codes are more robust for this purpose. We will develop optimization techniques for the spatially-coupled systems and analyze the achievable rates for the data aided scheme. We will also study a superimposed pilot and data scheme. Traditionally, dedicated time slots for pilots may result in serious loss of information rate in a multi-user environment. This problem has become a bottleneck for large MIMO systems for future wireless communications. The superimposed scheme can largely recover the rate loss by avoiding dedicated time slots for pilots. However, there is severe interference between superimposed pilot and data signals. Recent progress on spatially-coupled codes reveals a promising treatment for the interference problem. We will develop interference cancelation and system optimization techniques for the superimposed scheme based on spatial-coupled codes. Spatial-coupled LDPC codes are a very interesting topic that has attracted considerable research interests in coding theory community. The outcomes of this project will extend this principle to the channel estimation problem and develop practical solutions. 空間耦合是一个关于低密度奇偶校驗（LDPC）碼的設計技術。空間耦合也可应用于多用戶干擾消除。空間耦合LDPC碼需要足够長的编碼長度才能獲得令人滿意的性能。 在此項目中，我們將研究的空間耦合原理在多用戶多輸入多輸出（MIMO）系統中的應用。 MIMO已被確定為未來第五代（5G）的蜂窩通信系統的一個關鍵技術。多用戶傳輸可以充分利用MIMO系统提供的優點。但如何獲得精確的信道狀態信息是多用戶环境中一個困难的問題。此項目旨在应用空間耦合原理以解决信道估計問題。我們的研究計劃如下。 我們將研究空間耦合LDPC碼的长度问题并设计實用的空間耦合碼。 我們將研究所謂的導頻污染問題。這個問題可以通過一個基于數據輔助的信道估計技術來緩解。由於信道環境的快速變化，编碼設計成為一個困難的問題。我們將開發用于空間耦合系統的设计及優化技術。 我們也將研究一種導頻數據疊加技术。在多用戶環境中，專用的時隙可能導致嚴重信息速率損失。這個問題已成為大的MIMO系統的一个瓶頸。導頻數據疊加技术可以很大程度上恢復这种損失。然而疊加的導頻信號和數據信號之間有嚴重的干擾。空間耦合原理可用缓解以这种干擾。 空間耦合的LDPC碼已經引起編碼理論界广泛的研究興趣。此項目的研究成果將空間耦合原理用MIMO系統，並制定切實可行的解決方案以解决多用戶环境中的信道估計問題。

11217515.label: Realisation of objectives
11217515.value: Regarding objective 1, we carried out research work under a unified framework of massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA), and interleave division multiple access (IDMA). Our emphasis is on multi-user gain that refers to the advantage of allowing multi-user transmission in massive MIMO. We showed that such a gain can potentially offer tens or even hundreds of times of rate increase. The main difficulty in achieving multi-user gain is the reliance on accurate channel state information (CSI) in the existing schemes. This problem is especially acute when short data packets are involved, since then the overheads related to pilot becomes a serious burden. In our study, we showed that with accurate CSI, both OMA and NOMA can deliver performance not far away from capacity. Without accurate CSI, however, most of the existing schemes do not work well. We outline a solution to this difficulty based on spatially coupled IDMA and iterative data-aided channel estimation (DACE). This scheme can offer very high throughput and is robust against the pilot contamination problem. The receiver cost is low, since only maximum ratio combining (MRC) is involved and there is no matrix inversion or decomposition. Under time division duplex, accurate CSI acquired in the up-link can be used to support low-cost down-link solutions, such as zero forcing. These findings offer useful design considerations for future systems. Regarding objective 2, we studied robust transmission techniques for spatial coupled codes. We observed an error floor problem for a spatially coupled sparse-regression code with limited sparsity in low-to-medium rates. The problem stems from the fact that although a sparse-regression code can achieve channel capacity in theory with an infinite block length, a practical code always has a finite block length. This problem imposes a serious problem in practice. We resolved the problem using a scheme that involves spatial-coupling and compressed-sensing similar to sparse-regression codes. We replaced position modulation in a sparse-regression code by a general concatenated forward error control code. We introduced a chaining principle that improves the error floor behavior of the underlying code. We showed that our new coding scheme based on chained Hadamard codes can achieve significantly reduced error floor. We also made an interesting finding in our investigation of spatially coupled codes. Gaussian signaling of spatially coupled sparse superposition codes incurs a high peak-to-average-power ratio (PAPR) problem. Clipping can be used to reduce PAPR. At the receiver side, generalized approximate message passing algorithm can be employed to handle the non-linear clipping distortion. Surprisingly, we observed empirically that clipping can actually improve the performance in low-to-medium rate region. We developed a semi-theoretical explanation of this observation based on potential function analysis. Our finding provided a solution to an open obstacle of spatially coupled sparse-regression codes. Regarding objective 3, we investigated pilot transmission schemes in large antenna systems. We investigated two pilot structures—orthogonal pilot (OP) and superimposed pilot (SP). In OP, pilots occupy dedicated time (or frequency) slots, while in SP, pilots are superimposed with data. We devised an iterative data-aided channel estimation (IDACE) receiver, where partially decoded data are used to refine channel estimation. We analyzed the achievable rates for systems with IDACE receivers for both OP and SP. We showed that the optimal portion of pilot power tends to zero for SP with Gaussian signaling. This result is consistent with existing findings obtained via the replica method in statistical physics. The latter involves multiple codes, which is convenient for theoretical analysis but difficult to implement. As a comparison, IDACE is potentially implementable in practice. We demonstrated that, with code optimization, SP can outperform OP in a high mobility environment with a large number of users. The main findings of this project are summarized in an invited paper in IEEE Access [journal attachment 6]. This paper provides a comprehensive overview on multi-user NOMA systems, IDMA principles, data aided channel estimation and spatial coupling. The work also attracted attention from industry (see Subsection C.11 “Other impact”). These evidences demonstrate that this project is highly successful.
