11217515.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217515.value: We investigated the basic structures of spatial coupled systems. Our main objective is to extend the spatial coupling principles to multiple input multiple output (MIMO) systems. We devised a novel “linear coupling” technique for this purpose. In this approach, coupling is accomplished using linear additions in the complex field instead of binary additions in the discrete field. This leads to a very flexible transmitter structure in MIMO environments. More specifically, the main findings of this project are summarized below. We develop a novel approach to the design of short forward error control (FEC) codes based on linear spatially coupling. This technique is particularly suitable for a multi-user system. We showed that the performance of a linearly spatially-coupled code is comparable to the best short FEC codes reported in the literature, yet the former has much lower complexity than the latter. This work is reported in journal attachments 2 and 6, and conference attachment 1. However, linear coupling results in a Gaussian type signal distribution, which has a high peak to average power ratio (PAPR) problem. We employed a clipping technique to reduce PAPR. Interestingly, contrary to common believing, we noticed that clipping can actually improve performance in a spatially coupling setting. We reported this surprising finding in journal attachment 5. We devised an orthogonal approximate message passing (OAMP) algorithm that is very efficient for decoding coded spatially coupled systems. This algorithm can overcome the shortcoming of the original approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm encountered when sensing matrixes are not IID-Gaussian. This finding is significant, since it opens the possibility of using AMP type algorithms in a wide range of applications. We reported this finding in journal attachments 1, 2 and conference attachments 2 and 4. We developed an optimization technique for superimposed pilot and data transmission scheme. We derived a semi-analytical proof that such a scheme is nearly optimal and can outperform the conventional orthogonal pilot scheme. We also developed a design methodology for such a scheme in multi-user MIMO environments. We devised a design method for the underlying LDPC codes using the matching principle. We reported this finding in journal attachment 4 and 6, and conference attached 3. In particular, journal attachment 6 is an invited paper which provides a comprehensive overview on the findings of this project.

11217515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217515.value: In this project, we investigated spatial-coupling, data aided channel estimation and multi-user The implementation issues related to the spatial-coupling, data aided channel estimation and multi-user transmission techniques developed in this project are crucial for industrial applications. We want to avoid high complex MMSE estimation and we need to develop low-cost alternatives. Also, the impact of finite quantization bits at the receiver end is also a major concern, since RF chains are very costly in massive MIMO systems. These topics will be of high practical values. We are currently continuing the work of this project. We are investigating low cost algorithms that can offer similar performance as the optimal MMSE algorithm, yet to maintain affordable receiver complexity.

11217515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217515.value: The outcomes of this project have attracted both theoretical and industrial attentions. We have been invited to the report our findings to IEEE Access and IEEE VTC. The algorithms developed in this project have also been studied by industry for the 5th generation (5G) cellular systems. Linear spatial-coupling, data aided channel estimation and multi-user transmission techniques are promising techniques for future wireless systems. In summary, the project is highly successful.

11217915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217915.value: Cell patterning is an essential technique for cell culture at specific environment, which is significant for the study of cell growth, drug test, tissue regeneration and so on. Comparing to the traditional cell culture in 2D, 3D cell patterning provides a more accurate approach for cell biology research, because 3D culture environment is much more closely to cells’ living condition in vivo. However, current 3D cell patterning techniques has the drawbacks of low flexibility or low productivity. Moreover, they are difficult, if not impossible, to culture the cells selectively, that to select the particular cells and then to culture them in 3D. This project aims to propose a novel 3D cell patterning method to address the above issues. This method is based on optically-induced micro manipulation and fabrication, which will enable the selective, flexible and productive 3D cell patterning automatically. First, an optically-induced microchip will be developed and integrated to our current optically-induced dielectrophoresis (ODEP) manipulation system. Then, we will transfer the particular cells to the target positions based on ODEP manipulation. After that, we will generate the hydrogel to embed the selected cells based on electrodeposition by controlling the light pattern, DC voltage and the duration time. Finally, We will develop a control system with human-machine interface to implement the above 3D cell patterning process automatically. This project will derivate a novel 3D cell patterning system by integrating the micromanipulation and electro deposition patterning techniques together. In this project, the cell patterning is controlled by the light projection and the applied voltage, through which ensures the high flexibility and high productivity. In addition, this method allows the selectively cell patterning based on ODEP manipulation, which will benefit the in-depth understanding of the single cell growth and the interaction between different types of cells. Moreover, the visible light, rather than UV light or laser, is used to generate the hydrogel, which will provide a more safety fabrication process for cell analysis. Last but not least, the 3D cell patterning process can be performed automatically, which will not only improve the working efficiency, but will also promote the wide application of this method potentially. We believe the outcome of this research will greatly benefit the basic cell biology, tissue engineering, medical development and other related fields. 細胞的三維培養在細胞生長、藥物測試、組織再生等領域有著重要的意義。與傳統的2D細胞培養相比，細胞的三維培養技術能夠更好的模擬細胞在人體的生長狀態，從而為細胞生物學的研究提供更精確的模型。本項目的目的是提出一種全新的基於可見光誘導的三維細胞生長方法，該方法具有選擇性、靈活性和高效性的優點。首先，我們將開發一種可見光誘導的微芯片，並將其集成到光學感應介電泳（ODEP）操縱系統。然後，我們將通過DEP技術把特定的細胞移動到目標位置。在此之後，我們將通過可見光控制生成水凝膠包裹選定的細胞，實現細胞的三維培養。最後，我們將開發相應的控制系統和人機界面，自動執行上述三維細胞培養的過程。該項目的順利實施將開發出一套全新的三維細胞系統，其研究成果將在細胞生物學，組織工程學，醫學等相關領域有廣泛的應用。

11217915.label: Realisation of objectives
11217915.value: Objective 1: To investigate the proper parameters for the titanyl phthalocyanine (TiOPc) plate fabrication and then to develop the microchip for selectively 3D cell patterning. With the support of this project, we developed an easy-to-use chip to realize the rapidly controllable single cell manipulation as well as the flexible fabrication of 3D ca-alginate hydrogel microstructure. This chip is fabricated by coating the titanium oxide phthalocyanine (TiOPc) organic material as optical inducted virtual electrode on ITO glass, by which the gels with cells can be selectively patterned under electrodeposition. The cell viability for either Hek 293 cell or Hela cell was found to be nearly 100% (> 98% ) in 0 h when we applied current density of 3 Am−2 for 150 s. After the cells were cultured for 12 h, although the viability had a slight decrease, the survival rate can still be maintained higher than 85% for both cells. Those results prove that cytotoxicity in fluences on the cells can be ignored in the light-induced electrodeposition approach. Relevant results have been published in Micromachine 2015, IEEE Nanomed 2016. Objective 2: To realize the flexible manipulation of the particular cells based on ODEP manipulation. We mixed the cells with the alginate solution and then used the light projection to control the position of the cell. We have realized the cell trapping in the form of line, circle, tube and even in a capsule. Moreover, by integrating the 3D printing and electrodeposition methods together, we realized the fabrication of gel with cell in 3D space. These results pave a new way for the tissue engineering. Relevant works have been published in Biofabrication 2017, micromachine 2017. Objective 3: To elucidate how the voltage and duration time regulate the height of the hydrogel, and then to achieve the controllable 3D hydrogel generation. To reveal the electrodeposition mechanism and to control the fabrication process precisely, we established the gel formation model by developing the equivalent electric circuit. After that, we analyzed the effect of the applied voltage and time to the growth of the gel. Moreover, we also revealed the key parameters for gel capsule fabrication, including their size, membrane thickness, shrinking and explanation phenomena, etc. Relevant results have been published in Biofabrication 2016, Biofabrication 2017. Objective 4: To automate the cell patterning procedures, and finally to improve the operation accuracy and working efficiency. After developing the system and revealing the electrodeposition system, we further optimized the fabrication parameters and realized the automatic cell patenting by programming. Moreover, we also proposed a method to construct complex higher-order structure by microrobotic manipulation. As demonstration, we fabricated the gel capsule and assembled them to a self-locked structure for the first time. This approach provides an effective and flexible solution for the biocompatible 3D scaffold fabrication, which may find wide applications in biomedical engineering. Relevant results have been published in Biofabrication 2019.

11217915.value: Cell patterning is an essential technique for cell culture at specific environment, which is significant for the study of cell growth, drug test, tissue regeneration and so on. With the support of this project, we proposed a novel 3D cell patterning method to realize the 3D cell culture. This method was based on optically-induced micro manipulation and fabrication, which enables the selective, flexible and productive 3D cell patterning automatically. The main outcomes include: (1) An optically-induced microchip was developed and integrated to the optically-induced dielectrophoresis (ODEP) manipulation system. This chip is fabricated by coating the titanium oxide phthalocyanine (TiOPc) organic material as optical inducted virtual electrode on ITO glass, by which the gels with cells can be selectively patterned under electrodeposition. Moreover, we also revealed the key parameters for gel capsule fabrication, including their size, membrane thickness, shrinking and explanation phenomena, etc. (4) We developed a control system and implement the above 3D cell patterning process automatically. We proposed a method to construct complex higher-order structure by microrobotic manipulation. As demonstration, we fabricated the gel capsule and assembled them to a self-locked structure for the first time, which is expected have long-term impact in biomedical engineering. Relevant achievements have delivered 6 journal paper, 2 conference papers, and 1 US patent.

11217915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217915.value: The development of the optically induced microchip offers a new way for the 3D cell culture, which will benefit many fields in biomedical engineering. As the future work, we intend to improve this technique further and promote it in various application, briefly: (1) To develop the micro capsule robot based on the developed method in this project. (2) To apply the fabricated micro capsule robot in the active drug delivery. (3) To develop the gels or microcapsule with various shape and assembled them to a higher-order structure, and then apply them as the simulator for drug test, tissue regeneration, and so on.

11217915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217915.value: Cell patterning is a method to control the size, shape, location of culture substrate through guiding, manipulating or modifying the physical and chemical properties. It’s an essential technique to study the cells’ growth and functions at various physical and chemical environment. Herein, we developed a novel 3D cell patterning method based on optically-induced micro manipulation and fabrication. This method allows the selectively cell patterning based on ODEP manipulation, which will benefit the in-depth understanding of the single cell growth and the interaction between different types of cells. Moreover, the visible light, rather than UV light or laser, is used to generate the hydrogel, which will provide a more safety fabrication process for cell analysis. Last but not least, the 3D cell patterning process can be performed automatically, which will not only improve the working efficiency, but will also promote the wide application of this method potentially. We believe the outcome of this research will greatly benefit the basic cell biology, tissue engineering, medical development and other related fields.

11218015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11218015.value: 大多数细胞行为和功能都与细胞内的信号通路及传导相关联。研究细胞内信号网络是现代生物学核心议题之一，并且对开发许多疾病治疗试剂至关重要。在此研究计划中，我们的目标是开发一种微创方法用于在原代神经元中原位探测先天免疫反应。该生物传感装置将基于表面修饰特定适配子（aptamer）分子的金刚石纳米针阵列。我们此前已经证明类似形态的纳米结构能够有效的促进向细胞内的物质传递。基于这些初步结果，本项目描述的新型生物传感设备将从四个方面有利于神经元细胞内信号通路的研究。首先，该生物传感装置将被应用来向胞质区域传递生物传感器，这种无载体，金刚石纳米针辅助，良好机械控制的方法将显着减少的毒性问题和潜在的载体引起的干扰元素。其次，基于aptamer的分子传感策略利用了核苷酸 - 蛋白质相互作用的高度特异性，并提供了用于实时检测受激活的信号通路和动态过程的能力。第三，该装置将结合纳米针为基础的细胞内递质方式和分子检测，研究细胞宿主防御对人工引入病原体分子如DNA或RNA的响应。第四，可逆的检测程序将实现从活体神经细胞中分离“蛋白质”等相关的信号元素，尤其是在受激活后释放的许多信号因子，以利于进一步的分析。预计这个项目的成功，不仅为解剖细胞内信号提供了一种全新的工具，而且还有可能对研究神经元细胞的先天免疫反应起到有效的推动作用，以利于脑损伤和神经退化性疾病的治疗。

11218015.label: Realisation of objectives
11218015.value: All the objectives has been successfully addressed in this project, and the results are summarized below: *Fabrication and functionalization of diamond-nanoneedles The diamond-nanoneedles were fabricated using bias-assisted reactive ion etching (RIE) by electron cyclotron resonance microwave plasma chemical vapour deposition (MPCVD), and were characterized by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Most nanoneedles were fabricated to be a tapered cylindrical morphology with a diameter of ~300 nm and a height of ~5 µm. The material, diamond, has been demonstrated with superior biocompatibility due to its inertness, and is safe to use with various types of cells, including fragile primary neurons. To render the diamond-nanoneedles biosensing capability, they were functionalized with the DNA aptamers (5’-GGGGAATCCCC-3’) that were specifically designed to bind NF-κB. A diamond-nanoneedle patch was firstly bathed in heated piranha solution to modify the surface with hydroxyl groups. (3-Aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (APTES) was then crosslinked to the surface, to which NHS-biotin, streptavidin, and biotinylated DNA aptamers was sequentially linked. Due to multiple binding sites on the molecule, streptavidin was used as a bridge for the final functionalization of aptamer DNAs. For visualization purpose, the aptamer sequences were pre-labeled with FITC fluorophore on the 3’ end, so that functionalized diamond-nanoneedles could be readily examined by laser confocal microscopy, as a result of successful crosslinking of FITC-labeled aptamer sequences. *Intracellular “molecular fishing” As we designed, the diamond-nanoneedles were used as “fishing rods”, and the crosslinked aptamers were used as “fishing baits”, which can together be used to retrieve intracellular signaling components from living cells in a minimum invasive format. Meanwhile, the nanoneedles also worked as a delivery tool for cytoplasmic introduction of foreign materials (e.g. dsDNA90 in this study) by temporary disrupting cellular membrane. For proof-of-concept, the functionalized nanoneedles were firstly tested in A549 cells, to see if any NF-κB protein could be isolated from intracellular region after STING activation upon invading of foreign dsDNA90. The whole detection and “molecular fishing” processes were performed in a centrifugation induced supergravity environment (12.8 g), where the nanoneedles were delicately pressed to poke cells for 90 seconds to capture NF-κB molecules. The nanoneedle array was then retrieved and immunnostained to examine the amount of successfully isolated NF-κB. After the “molecular fishing” procedures, NF-κB staining was appeared to be concentrated speckles on the nanoneedle patches. The majority of these NF-κB speckles were colocalized with nanoneedles in a highly consistent manner, whereas no similar NF-κB staining was observed in control patches with diamond-nanoneedles crosslinked with just Alexa Fluor 488, suggesting successful implementation of the diamond-nanoneedle assisted intracellular “molecular fishing”. *Interrogation of cellular innate immunity in living cells The aptamer-functionalized nanoneedles were then used to investigate the dynamics of NF-κB signaling in different types of cells, including cancer cells (A549) and primary neurons, to probe their innate immune response after invasion of pathogen dsDNA. A549 cells were cultured in 4-well plates to ~80% confluence before any experiments. To monitoring the NF-κB translocation process, we repeated the “molecular fishing” in living cells at different time points (0, 7, 15 and 40 mins) after STING activation by intracellularly delivered dsDNA90 at the first (0 min) probing trial. Upon STING activation, the percentage of NF-κB positive nanoneedles gradually decreased from 52.1±6.7% (n = 3, mean±s.e.m., same below) to 8.9±0.6% over 40 minutes, which was likely due to decreased intracellular level of NF-κB as a result of its translocation from cytoplasmic to nuclear regions. In our control groups without the STING activator (dsDNA90), no such reduction of fished NF-κB was observed. The nanoneedle-assisted probing technique was then applied to more fragile cells, primary neurons (9 days in vitro), to test if neuronal cells have a similar NF-κB signaling dynamics as a result of STING activation. The amount of NF-κB isolated from neurons also reduced significantly, as indicated by a reduction of NF-κB positive nanoneedles (from 67.2±4.8% to 30.7±5.9%, n = 3, mean±s.e.m.) within a few minutes after STING activation. These results further proved that our diamond-nanoneedle-assisted probing technique is a capable, versatile and flexible tool for dissecting intracellular signaling.

11218015.label: Major findings and research outcome
11218015.value: Understanding intracellular signaling cascades and network is one of the core topics in modern biology. Novel tools based on nanotechnologies have enabled probing and analyzing intracellular signaling with unprecedented sensitivity and specificity. In this project, we developed a novel tool for probing signal transduction and for in situ isolation of targeted signaling components in living cells using arrays of diamond-nanoneedles functionalized with aptamer-based molecular sensors. Of particular interest, we used the tool to investigate the cell host defense activity, cellular innate immunity, in response to foreign DNA pathogen30, 31, and found that the transcriptional factor, NF-κB, was quickly transferred from cytoplasm to nucleus upon the activation of the STING pathway by a stereotypic pathogen, dsDNA90. Especially for primary neurons, cells from the central nervous system were thought to be immune-privileged in the past due to the existence of blood-brain barrier, our results directly showed that pathogen like foreign DNAs also trigger significant responses in neurons, as they do in other cells. By taking advantage of the repeatable and reversible intracellular probing protocol, we directly isolated NF-κB proteins from cell inside without hurting the cells, and quantified the STING activation level via a straightforward colocalization assay. We showed that dsDNA90 was delivered into A549 and neuron cells within a couple minutes, matching the timescale of STING activation and subsequent NF-κB translocation, which would not be possible if using traditional methods based on cellular endocytosis processes.

11218015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11218015.value: The demonstrated “molecular fishing” based on aptamer-protein interaction, the “fishing baits” (aptamer sequence) can be easily replaced with a large repertoire of molecules targeting other intracellular signaling components, such as microRNAs and enzymes, which opens up new possibility for many downstream analyses that could done on freshly isolated and enriched molecular targets. In addition to molecular sensing and fishing, our method also provides an alternative to quickly deliver various materials into cytoplasm with the attention to activate specific intracellular pathways.

11218015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11218015.value: Most of cellular behaviors and functions are associated with intracellular signal transduction. Understanding the signaling cascades and network is one of the core topics in molecular biology. The invention of novel tools for probing signaling activity in living cells has been part of the major thrust advancing our knowledge about different aspects of cell function. With the convergence of nanotechnology and biomedical research, many nano-devices have been introduced for investigation of intracellular activity. We developed a minimally invasive method for in situ probing of intracellular signaling dynamics in living cells. The biosensing device was based on a diamond-nanoneedle array functionalized with aptamer molecular sensors. The functionalized nanoneedles were used to study cellular immunity targeting the STING pathway, which was identified to be involved in cellular host-defense response to pathogen molecules such as foreign DNAs. Activation of STING leads to translocation of NF-κB from cytoplasmic to nuclear domain. The diamond-nanoneedles were used as “fishing rods” that were inserted into the cytoplasmic region of living cells without damaging them; the aptamer sequences on nanoneedles were used as “fishing baits” that were designed to specifically capture NF-κB, which is released upon STING activation by intracellularly delivered double strand DNAs (dsDNA90).

11300115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300115.value: Random matrix theory has important applications in many different areas of mathematics and physics, such as number theory, combinatorics, statistics, string theory, condense matter physics, classical and quantum optics, etc.. Universality of eigenvalue spacings when the matrix size tends to infinity is one of the central problems in random matrix theory. Universality means that the local eigenvalue statistics are the same for many different random matrix ensembles, or in another word, they do not rely on the exact probability distribution that is put on the matrices, but only on some general characteristics of the ensemble. Classical universality results usually depend on the analyticity of corresponding potentials of the ensemble. When analytic properties of the potentials are changed, some new universality classes are expected to appear. In this project, we will study unitary ensembles whose potential possesses poles. Based on the close relation between unitary ensembles and orthogonal polynomials, we will obtain the new limiting kernels from the uniform asymptotics of related orthogonal polynomials. Note that when the potential has poles, the corresponding weight function for the orthogonal polynomials possesses essential singularities, as a consequence the polynomials belong to the non-Szego class. We will apply the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method for Riemann-Hilbert problems to derive the uniform asymptotics of the polynomials. Near the singularities, new local parametrices will be constructed. The transition properties of the limiting kernel will also be considered when the parameter associated with the poles varies. Some other important quantities, such as Hankel determinants and Fredholm determinants will be studied, too. 隨機矩陣理論在數學和物理的許多領域都具有重要的應用，比如數論、組合學、統計學、弦論、凝聚態物理、經典以及量子光學等。隨機矩陣理論中一個中心的問題是研究在矩陣的階趨於無窮大的情形下，其特徵值的普適性分布。普適性是指對於許多不同的隨機矩陣系綜，其局部的特征值分布是相同的。這也等同於説，局部的特征值分布与具體系綜的概率分布無關，而只是依賴於系綜自身很基本的一些性質。經典的普適性結果對系綜的勢函數的解析性具有一定的要求。當勢函數的解析性質發生變化時，一些新的普適性結果就可能會出現。 在本項目中，我們計划研究勢函數具有極點的酉系綜。基於酉系綜与正交多項式的緊密聯係，我們計划通過對相關正交多項式一致漸進行為的研究來推導酉系綜的極限核。值得注意的是，當勢函數具有極點時，對應的正交多項式的權函數具有本性奇點。這樣的話，這些多項式屬於非Szego類。我們計划從多項式滿足的黎曼-希爾伯特問題出發，運用Deift-Zhou最速下降法來推導相關多項式的一致漸進展開。在奇點附近，解矩陣需要重新構造。我們還計划研究在參數發生變化時，極限核的轉變性質。我們也會考慮其他的一些的重要的量的漸進性質，比如Hankel行列式以及Fredholm行列式。

11300115.label: Realisation of objectives
11300115.value: Random matrix models with singular potentials have attracted a lot of research interests in the literature. In particular, matrix models whose potential possesses poles have important applications in many areas of mathematics and physics, such as statistics for zeros of the Riemann zeta function, finite temperature expectation values in integrable quantum field theory, and the Wigner time delay in quantum transport. Quite a few important results have been achieved in the past a few years. The main objective in the study of random matrix models is their eigenvalue distribution. When the potential possesses poles, the poles will repel eigenvalues away from them. As a consequence, the order and location of the poles have a significant influence on the eigenvalue distributions. The repelling effect changes when the values of parameters vary. In this situation, phase transitions take place under a double (or multiple) scaling limit (depending on the number of the parameters). In the literature, various asymptotic study has been conducted to understand the limiting eigenvalues distributions when the matrix size becomes large. In this project, we investigate the limiting eigenvalue correlation kernel of the unitary matrix ensembles when the pole is close to the soft edge. The pole of general order 2k is considered, where k is an arbitrary natural number. Due to their symmetry properties, it is well-known that unitary ensembles are closely related to orthogonal polynomials. Correspondingly, we first study the uniform asymptotics of orthogonal polynomials whose weight function possess essential singularities. It is natural to expect that properties of the orthogonal polynomials change significantly in the neighbourhood of the pole. Using Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method for Riemann-Hilbert problems, the asymptotic expansions of the orthogonal polynomials are successfully derived in the neighbourhood of the pole. In particular, we have constructed a class of novel parametrix to approximate the polynomials near the pole of general order 2k. Note that new parametrix in the Riemann-Hilbert analysis is crucial to describe new critical situations. It plays a similar role as the canonical forms in the classical steepest descendent analysis of integrals. The novel parametrix in our problem involves the coupled Painleve XXXIV equations, which is the higher order generalization of the classical second order Painleve XXXIV equations. With the uniform asymptotics of the orthogonal polynomials, we obtain the limiting eigenvalue correlation kernel under a multiple scaling limit, which is given in terms of the coupled Painleve XXXIV equations. The coupled Painleve XXXIV kernel generalizes various results obtained in the previous work. This achieves the first objective of the project. Then, we consider the influence when certain parameters vary in matrix models. For the Painleve kernels, the crucial parameters are usually the independent variable in the Painleve equations. Therefore, it is important to investigate the asymptotics of the solutions to the Painleve equations, also known as the Painleve transcendents, as well as their connection formulas. Note that, although the Painleve equations are nonlinear differential equations, they are integrable in the sense that all of the equations possess the Lax pair. From the linear differential system in the Lax pair, one can formulate an associated Riemann-Hilbert problem by studying its direct and inverse problems. It is worth mentioning that the Riemann-Hilbert problem is considered as the nonlinear analogue of the integral representation for solutions of linear differential equations. For integrals, a well-known tool to derive their asymptotic expansions is the classical steepest descent method. For the Riemann-Hilbert problems, we can adopt similar ideas to derive its asymptotics, and finally obtain the asymptotics of the associated Painleve transcendents. These asymptotic results are applied to show how the transition takes place when the parameters vary. For example, one can describe how the Painleve kernels are reduced to the classical Airy kernels or the Bessel kernels via taking different kinds of limits. This achieves the second objective of the project. Last, we turn to the Hankel determinants and Fredholm determinants. Via an improved asymptotic analysis of the orthogonal polynomials, the asymptotics of the corresponding Hankle determinant can be obtained. The Fredholm determinant of the limiting eigenvalue correlation kernels gives us the gap probability, i.e., the probability that there is no eigenvalue in a given interval. Its asymptotic study is more delicate. Because the limiting kernel is integrable in the sense of Its-Izergin-Korepin-Slavnov, its resolvent kernel is integrable as well. By a well-known theorem of Deift, Its and Zhou, the resolvent kernel is related to a Riemann-Hilbert problem. Using the Deift-Zhou nonlinear steepest descent analysis, it is possible to derive the so-called “large gap asymptotics”, which is the probability that there is no eigenvalue in a large interval. Note that, such kind of probability is always exponentially small, and is a nice example in the large deviation theory. Usually, one can only associate the derivatives of the Fredholm determinants with certain entries in the (matrix-valued) Riemann-Hilbert problem. The asymptotics of the Fredholm determinants are obtained after taking an integration. The derivation of the explicit expression of the integration constants is usually a challenging task, which is also referred as the “constant problem/conjecture” in the random matrix theory. These constants also involve some important functions, such as the Riemann zeta function and the Barnes’ G function. In this project, by making use of some important limiting relations and the Hamiltonian structure of the Painleve transcendents, we successfully derived the asymptotics of the Painleve II kernel and the Painleve III kernel (including the important constant). This achieves the last objective of the project. As a summary, all objectives in the present project have been realised successfully.

11300115.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300115.value: We investigate the limiting kernel of the unitary matrix ensembles when the pole is close to the soft edge of the limiting eigenvalue spectrum. To describe the limiting eigenvalue correlation kernel under a multiple scaling limit, we constructed a novel parametrix which involve the coupled Painleve XXXIV equations. In the Riemann-Hilbert analysis, the novel parametrix is of great importance because it can describe new critical phenomenon. This result is contained in the paper published in Annales Henri Poincaré (2019). Then, to investigate transition properties of the limiting Painleve kernels when the parameters vary, we study the asymptotics of the corresponding Painleve transcendents, as well as their connection formulas. Some results have only appeared in the literature formally or numerically. Our work has provided the first rigorous mathematical proof. This is a significant contribution in the study of Special Functions. Our results are contained in papers published in Nonlinearity (2017) and Random Matrices: Theory and Applications (2018). Last, we study the asymptotics of the Hankel determinants and the Fredholm determinants. The Fredholm determinant implies one of the key quantities in the random matrix theory, namely the gap probability. We successfully derived the asymptotics of the Fredholm determinants including the constant terms. Our asymptotic formulas also support the so-called Forrester-Chen-Eriksen-Tracy conjecture. These results are contained in papers published in Journal of Approximation Theory (2016), SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis (2018) and Communications in Mathematical Physics (2019).

11300115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300115.value: In random unitary ensembles, the limiting eigenvalue correlation kernels are always integrable in the sense of Its-Izergin-Korepin-Slavnov. Then, it is possible to associate the corresponding Fredholm determinant with a Riemann-Hilbert problem. Until now, all of the existing results are based on a two-by-two Riemann-Hilbert problem. However, there are some important kernels, such as Pearcey kernel and the tacnode kernel, which are associated with a three-by-three or four-by-four Riemann-Hilbert problem. With our experience in the low dimensional cases, we intend to work on the higher dimensional ones. We may also study the deformed gap probability, where each eigenvalue is removed independently with a given probability. This is a typical example of thinned processes. A few asymptotic results for the deformed gap probability associated with classical kernels have been obtained. We wish to apply Riemann-Hilbert technique to study the asymptotics of the deformed gap probability associated with other kernels.

11300115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300115.value: In this project, we work on asymptotics of random unitary ensembles with singular potentials. The central problem is to understand the eigenvalue distribution when the matrix size becomes large. We have successfully obtain the novel limiting eigenvalue correlation kernel, which suggests a new universality class in the random matrix theory. We also investigate the transition properties of the limiting kernels by studying the asymptotic properties of the related Painleve transcendents. These asymptotic formulas are not only important in random matrix theory, but also valuable in special function theory. Finally, we derive the detailed asymptotics of the gap probability, including the significant constant term. Our results support one of the famous conjectures in this research field.

11300215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300215.value: 消防安全是香港和中國民生所面临的一个主要問題。近年來，香港和中國都經歷了一些毀滅性的火災，并造成了悲劇性的後果，如2009年北京中央電視台辦公樓火災造成2億元的損失和2010年發生在上海高層居民樓火災造成58人死亡以及人民币197萬元的損失。同年，香港旺角嘉禾高層建築火災造成4人死亡，其中包括2名消防員。 玻璃幕牆是現代高層建築采用的主要形式，但其比傳統材料更容易受到強烈火災的影响。火災中幕墙玻璃面完整性的損坏可能會提供一個渠道，让新鮮空氣進入，引起火災的蔓延，從而加速火災發展。玻璃幕墙有许多种不同的安装形式，如點支式，框架式和全玻璃牆，並可以选用各種類型的玻璃，如塗层玻璃，層合玻璃和絕緣玻璃等。因此，非常有必要对玻璃幕牆的各種安裝形式和途徑进行全面的研究，以提高他們的耐火性能。 本項目將建立一套完整的理论体系以預測玻璃幕墙的熱学及力学性能，并提高其耐火性。該項目將探討玻璃幕牆的破壞行為。通过全面的實驗，模拟火灾下玻璃幕墙的性能和評估玻璃幕牆的破壞行為。均勻的热輻射和非均勻的明火加載方式都将被应用到本项目的试验研究当中。一系列彎曲和拉伸等靜態試驗將在各種溫度下進行，以探明不同種玻璃的基本力学特性。此外，本项目将建立一套基於無網格法計算体系，用於預測應力分佈，破損時間，以及裂紋的產生和擴展。数值模擬的结果將通過實驗得到验证。在此基础上，本项目将提出相关设计建議以供工程参考。

11300215.label: Realisation of objectives
11300215.value: In this proposed research project, all objectives have been realized. We have developed a physical model of glass breakage comprising the radiation, conduction, and crack initiation phases. The occurrence of glass breakage depended on the degree of stress in the glazing, therefore, the breakage model was developed from the stress model. Hence, calculating the stress over the glass was the first step in predicting glass breakage. The primary solution of a nonlinear formulation involved linearizing the weak form of the equations and then solving these equations within the discretized domains. This generated an incremental approach in which the solution of each step was based on the results obtained in the previous step. If the temperature in the initial state was known, the associated deformation could then be obtained. As glass is an isotropic material, a rise in temperature induced a uniform strain, which was then determined by the material coefficient of linear expansion. The glass thermal load response was solved using the Newmark integration scheme which was considered as an extension of the linear acceleration method. Cracks were caused by stress accumulating within the glass pane. Two crack criteria were used to predict crack onset; one based on probabilistic theory and the other on the deterministic method. The distribution described as a three-parameter cumulative Weibull function was used for crack prediction in the probabilistic method, and the maximum tensile stress, Coulomb-Mohr, and maximum normal stress criteria were used in the deterministic method. For a crack growth, the stress intensity factors and energy release rates based on the mixed-mode criterion and stress intensity factors based on the maximum circumferential stress criterion were used. The fracture mesh-free method developed for computational and mechanical analyses was incorporated into the glass breakage model to furnish a unique integrated thermal-fracture mechanics model. The mesh-free framework considered the effects of crack propagation on the resulting damage. The glass facade problem domain was discretized by the mesh-free nodes, thermal and displacement information on which was coupled and approximated via an approximation technique. The thermal field and stiffness matrix were solved to obtain the stress and strain under high temperatures. This coupling allows the temperature and pressure fields in the glass facade specimen to be passed interactively to the mesh-free numerical framework, with stress and strain analyses performed simultaneously. Parametric studies were carried out to compare the theoretical and experimental results and to identify credible crack initiation criteria. Finally, the fracture mesh-free method was used to model the crack propagation that took place after crack initiation, ultimately leading to breakage. The equations could be solved numerically using the algorithm in the conventional mesh-free method, which was used to track crack tip progression. We tested the basic mechanical properties of different types of glass at elevated temperatures to inform simulations and predictions of fire resistance of glass facades. The thermal-mechanical model and glass breakage models were coupled with the fracture mesh-free method developed as mentioned previously. During the coupling procedure, the temperature field and stress-strain states were solved simultaneously in the iteration. The structure stiffness found using the mesh-free method was involved in the solution framework for obtaining the deformation of the mesh-free nodes. Crack initiation and progression were predicted in the numerical study. Breakage and damage were considered in the case of a continuous crack separating a portion of the glass from the entire facade body. The simulation system could also be used for simulating heat and mass transfer phenomena in glass facades under fire conditions. The computed thermal-mechanical field, crack, and damage phenomena provided a useful reference for the further design and use of glass facades exposed to fire. We have conducted fire tests and verified the numerical results with experimental results. Experimental data obtained from the following experiments were used to validate the numerical studies. During the experiments, a variety of installation forms and the glass categories were employed to reveal the glass breakage behavior in a real fire and help to develop design guidelines and propose optimal designs of glass facades. Uniform radiation and non-uniform fire loading conditions were considered. A total of 100 samples including clear, ground and coated glass were made, thus the property difference of three kinds of glass were compared and analyzed. Tests for different glass were firstly performed at room temperature, then glass samples were positioned in hot environment which set to 75 °C, 100 °C, 125 °C, 150 °C, 200 °C, 300 °C and 400 °C. Besides, the basic parameters of different types of glass, including maximum strain and stress, coefficient of thermal expansion, and elasticity modulus, were determined using the MTS 810 and Netzsch dilatometer. This research has led to eight high-quality research papers being published in refereed international journals.

11300215.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300215.value: In this research, we have found that the mesh-free framework is a more efficient modeling technique than the conventional computational techniques for predicting the thermal-mechanical behavior of glass building facades and improving their fire resistance. Therefore, the research is of great significance to the scientific fields and has significant potential for improving the fire performance of glass facades in design codes. A glass breakage model has been developed with full consideration given to the thermal loading and crack initiation process. A robust thermal-mechanical model was also developed and validated using the full-scale experimental results and a numerical code was developed to study the structural behavior of glass facades. In addition, a constitutive glass facade model was derived and embedded in the mesh-free method, using an in-house computational code. The mesh-free method incorporated the coupled heat and mass transfer models to facilitate prediction of the first instance of breakage, thermal stress, and crack initiation and propagation. This model only required a modest amount of empirical information on the material properties. The fracture mesh-free method developed for computational and mechanical analyses was incorporated into the glass breakage model to give a unique integrated thermal-fracture mechanical model. The full-scale experiments allowed the in-depth investigation of different installation formats. The results of the proposed project contribute to the fire safety design of the building envelope, the prevention of fire loss and damage, and more economical repair and maintenance works on fire-damaged structures. They also serve as useful references for engineering research and use in Hong Kong, China and internationally. Through the better understanding of glass facade breakage behavior in different installation forms and the improvement method, it is expected safer and more innovative facades can be designed for use in building and construction. The above-mentioned points are the major findings and research outcome of this project.

11300215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300215.value: The developed mesh-free modeling framework and experimental facilities will have the potential to be used for further investigation in fire research of glass facades. The project can help to develop a valuable mesh-free framework for predicting the thermo-mechanical behavior of glass facades and improving their fire resistance. The project has involved full-scale experiments designed to investigate the breakage behavior of glass facades. Real experimental models can be created with the characteristics of a variety of installations to simulate compartment fires and assess the breakage behavior of glass facades. Uniform radiation and non-uniform fire loading conditions can be considered. The effects of different fixing formats on fire resistance can be determined based on the outcome of this research. A series of bending and static stretching tests can be designed and conducted at various temperatures to explore the basic mechanical properties of different kinds of glasses. Moreover, based on this research, an in-house computational code based on the mesh-free method can be further developed to predict stress distribution, coefficient of thermal expansion, elasticity modulus, and crack initiation and propagation. Simulations will lead to the development of effective ways of predicting glass facade breakage.

11300215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300215.value: We have developed a valuable framework for predicting the thermal-mechanical behavior of glass building facades and improving the fire resistance. An in-house computational code based on the mesh-free method developed for computational and mechanical analyses has been incorporated into the glass breakage model to provide a unique integrated thermal-fracture mechanical model and predict stress distribution, breakage time, and crack initiation and propagation. Simulations have been verified by experiments, which have led to the development of effective ways of predicting glass facade breakage. On the basis of the above work, design recommendations and optimal designs have been proposed. The results of the proposed project have contributed to the fire safety design of the building envelope, the prevention of fire loss and damage, and more economical repair and maintenance work on fire-damaged structures.

11300315.label: Project Objectives
11300315.value: To mathematically justify two-dimensional nonlinear shell models of Koiter's type by showing that their asymptotic behavior as the thickness approaches zero matches that of the three-dimensional model, in the sense of Gamma-convergence theory. 11300315.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300315.value: Objectives #2, #3, #4, have been fully achieved: We have been able to construct a nonlinear shell model, whose stored energy is polyconvex and orientation-preserving, and which agree to within the first order with Koiter's nonlinear shell model, with the definite davantage that an existence theorem, in the spirit of the landmark existence theorem of John Ball, holds for our model. The only objective that has only been partially achieved is #1, in the sense that the justification of our model is only formal. We tried very hard to justify our model rigorously from three-dimensional elasticity by means of gamma-convergence theory, but this seems to pose serious mathematical challenges. More specifically, we tried very hard to adapt the pioneering works of H.Le Dret and A. Raoult, and of G. Friesecke, R.D. James, M. G. Mora, and S. Müller. However, in these works, neither polyconvexity nor orientation-preserving "à la John Ball" are assumed properties of the three-dimensional stored energy function, while we were able to incorporate these physically desirable properies in the stored energy function of our model. And it turns out that these two assumptions pose major difficulties when one tries to justify such models via gamma-convergence theory. Actually I have been discussing with some of the above named authors, and they agreed that, at the present time, no one really knows how to successfully incorporate such assumptions in a convergence theory via gamma-convergence. In retrospect, I realize that I was way too "too optimistic" when I proposed Objective #1 in my proposal.

11300315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300315.value: Devise efficient numerical methods for approximating the solution of our model. Fully justify our model by means of gamma-convergence theory, in the manner of Le Dret-Raoult and Friesecke, James, Mora, and Müller.

11300315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300315.value: Our proposed model, which can be used for modeling nonlinearly elastic shell that can undergo large displacements, which are very commonly encountered strutures in engineering, has the definite advantage that it is based on a fully satisfactory mathematical theory.

11300415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300415.value: A decentralized networked coupled system (DNCS) consists of collaborating agents whose behavior is coordinated through wired or wireless communication links. It provides a powerful tool to describe the dynamical behavior of many real-world engineering systems such as sensor networks and cyber-physical systems. Due to limited bandwidth of networks communication channels, it is necessary to save resources among agents in DNCSs. In addition, the demands for sharing resources efficiently in large DNCSs are continuously increasing. In many situations, there is a challenging conflict between the amount of transmitted data and the response time. Hence, efficient communication among agents is one of the key factors for DNCSs to achieve desired performance in a collaborative fashion. It is known that event-triggered control strategies have great potential in many cases to be more efficient than conventional time triggered (or sampled) control. To optimize the use of resource, it is desirable to design an effective event based sampling for DNCSs such that the signals are transmitted only when it is necessary. In addition, the network systems always suffers different types of networked signal transmission constraints. These constraints include limited communication capacity, network induced time delay and random packet loss. When these kinds of constraints occur, the distributed behavior of the event based DNCSs often exhibits highly non-trivial dynamical characteristics. Hence, this will certainly lead to great reliability difficulties in controlling the network performance, and even cause instability of the network system. Our main aims in this proposal are (i) to study the coordination control problem in DNCSs; (ii) to develop a set of distributed event based algorithms that can be used by a group of agents to carry out prescribed tasks efficiently under limited information transmission constraints. The approach will use a set of logical functions described the event-based model and semi-tensor product matrices techniques for performing the analysis and control; (iii) the proposed event-based coordination framework will also be applied to the synchronization and performance analysis of power grid described by Kuramoto-like model. This proposal has set up three new, challenging yet achievable objectives to the theoretical investigation. The results would have both theoretical and practical significance in communication-based autonomous systems, in which actions must be transmitted to ensure a coordination behavior. In particular, the applications in the power grid model will greatly benefit from the improvement of reliability of the proposed distributed event-based scheme. 摘要： 分布式网络耦合系统由交互的多智能体组成，这些多智能体通过有线或者无线网络传输。此类系统为描述大量实际工程系统（如传感器网络，信息－物理系统）提供了有力的工具。由于网络通讯信道带宽有限，因此节约智能体间的传输资源在分布式网络耦合系统中是非常必要的。此外，大规模的分布式网络耦合系统对资源共享的需求日益增加，在数据传输数量和时间响应之间易引起冲突。因此有效通讯策略是智能体间通过协调工作实现分布式网络耦合系统理想特性的关键。 相比于传统的时间驱动策略（如采样控制），时间驱动控制策略具有更高效性。为了实现资源优化配置，设计有效的事情驱动采样策略使得信号仅在需要时传输是一种理想的方法。 此外，网路系统通常受到不同类型的信号传输约束和限制，这些约束包括有限的通信容量、通讯延时和随机丢包。当此类网络约束发生时，基于事件驱动的网络耦合系统的分布式行为会呈现出非平凡的动力学特征。这会较大程度地引起网络性能的不可靠性，甚至促使整个网络系统失去稳定性。 本项目的主要目标包括： （1） 研究分布式网络耦合系统的协同控制问题； （2） 提出一系列分布式事件驱动算法，促使多智能体在有限信息传输的约束下仍能有效地完成事先规定的任务。此方法将采用一系列的逻辑函数来表述事件驱动模型，同时利用矩阵半张量积工具进行分析和控制； （3） 项目所提出的事件驱动协同框架将用于探究Kuramoto模型中描述的电网同步和性能分析。 本项目已经针对三个新的具有挑战性但可实现的目标进行了理论研究。研究结果在通信自治系统中（系统行为须通过信息传输以确保协同行为的实现），具有很大的理论和实践意义。特别是，电网模型中的应用将较大地受益于此项目中提出的分布式事件驱动策略可靠性的改进。

11300415.label: Realisation of objectives
11300415.value: The project is completed smoothly with all the objectives well achieved. (A) Control and filtering design under different imperfect conditions (Realization of Objectives 1 and 3) The problem has been investigated and characterized under communication-delay and event based sampling. (A1) A technical note in [1] addresses the distributed co-variance intersection fusion estimation problem for a class of cyber-physical systems (CPSs), where the raw measurements are pre-processed in each sink node to obtain the local state estimates of a CPS. The main contributions of [1] are summarized as follows: i) a novel communication constraint model with compensation strategy is proposed to describe the limited bandwidth, varying communication delays and packet dropouts, and then the recursive distributed fusion estimator (DFE) is designed based on covariance intersection (CI) fusion criterion; ii) a delay-dependent and probability-dependent condition is derived such that the mean square error (MSE) of the designed DFE is bounded, and it is proved that the estimation performance of the designed DFE is independent of the initial values under certain conditions. This work has partially fulfilled the objectives (1) and (3). The paper was revised several rounds and finally published in [1] in Dec 2016. (A2) Another approach on event-triggered consensus problem with communication delays was investigated in [2]. Two novel event-triggered sampled-data transmission strategies (asynchronous and synchronous), where only local and event-triggering states are utilized to update the broadcasting state of each agent. Under the circumstance of limited information exchanging and distributed communication delays, it is proved that the proposed protocols can realize consensus. More important, Zeno behavior can be excluded under synchronously event-triggered protocol with time delays; and the self-triggered consensus algorithm was given to avoid continuous checking event-triggered condition. The models studied in this paper are close to many realistic network systems, and the derived results would be valuable for the understanding of emergent collective behaviors in these systems. (A3) Distributed recursive filtering problem [3] has been designed for a class of discrete time-delayed stochastic systems subject to both uniform quantization and deception attack effects on the measurement outputs. (B)Event-based control techniques (Realization of Objective 2) (B1) Observer-based control for multiagent system under cyber-attacks: The observer-based event-triggering consensus control problem is investigated for a class of discrete time multiagent systems with lossy sensors and cyber-attacks. The closed-loop multiagent system achieves the prescribed consensus[5]. (B2) An observer-type event-triggered control protocol: This work in [8] is concerned with the finite-horizon H∞ consensus problem for a class of discrete time-varying multiagent systems with external disturbances and missing measurements. To improve the communication reliability, redundant channels are introduced and the corresponding protocol is constructed for the information transmission over redundant channels. An observer-type event-triggered control protocol is proposed based on the latest received neighbors’ information. (B3) Event-triggered control for switched system: The event-triggered control problem for continuous-time switched linear systems is investigated in [9]. It is assumed that only the sampled information of system state and switching signal is available to the controller at each sampling instant. Based on a mode-dependent event-triggered transmission scheme, the closed-loop system is modeled as a switched system with delayed state and augmented switching signal. Then, an exponential stability condition, characterized by the dwell time and average dwell time of the switching signal, is obtained. (C)New event-trigger coordination framework (Realization of Objective 3) (C1) Multilayer framework: Some typical real-world problem of multilayers examples are power grids, bio-systems, social networks, and ground-to-air commanding networks. Motivated by the aforementioned works on analysis and modeling of multilayer networks, we propose a layer event triggered scheme (LETS) for consensus. An event-triggered scheme emphasizes on the communication task that is executed only when it is needed. Thus, the resource of sending necessary information is more efficiently utilized. In addition, it is well known that event-triggered schemes can significantly reduce resource utilization for information transmission and control protocol update at the expense of cost for event detection. Thus, in some cases, a distributed event-triggered scheme may not be the best choice since it may incur high cost for event detection to achieve the required objectives. In [6], an LETS is proposed to cater for the characteristics of multilayer structure, which provides an alternative design to overcome the above-mentioned difficulties in event-triggered schemes. Here, the LETS guides agents in the same layer to update information simultaneously, however, the triggering behavior may not occur simultaneously for different layers. This will reflect the real-life situation that higher levels have various triggering decisions affecting the lower layers. (C2)Edge event-triggered consensus with communication buffer: This work proposes a distributed edge event-triggered (DEET) scheme of multi-agent systems via a communication buffer to reduce unnecessary update of controllers induced by fast information transmission[7]. This edge scheme avoids a synchronous phenomenon in node event-triggered mechanism, in which the triggering of one agent activates information transmission of all edges linked with this agent. Hence, the node event triggered scheme leads to unnecessary update of control protocols while the DEET provides a new approach without constrains on synchronous phenomenon of edge information exchange. That is, the communication on each edge is independent with other edges. In addition, we investigate another case where edge information transmission is subject to quantization and a quantized edge event-triggered control protocol is proposed. both DEET and quantized edge event-triggered schemes have nontrivial properties of excluding Zeno behavior. Furthermore, an algorithm is provided to avoid continuous event detection; hence, the communication traffic of the whole network is reduced significantly. This has fulfilled partially the Objectives (1), (2) and (3). (C3) Cluster Event-triggered Consensus: In this work [4], the receiver can determine: 1) whether the information has to be transmitted to a commander which contains the controller; and 2) the appropriate time for transmission. This idea has been applied to the telemetry system, which is widely used in meteorology, space science, oil/gas industry, and medical/health care. It is known that telemetry is used in many battery-operated wireless systems to inform monitoring personnel when the battery power is reaching a low point and needs fresh batteries. In [4], we propose an event-triggered scheme for information transmission from the receiver to remote commander. This implies that the receiver only sends information to remote commander when it is needed even though the receiver may acquire a great deal of its neighbors’ messages. (C4) Dynamic event-triggered scheme: A centralized event-triggered mechanism (CEM) is first proposed in [10]. Then, a distributed dynamic event-triggered mechanism is developed by introducing an internal variable. In the CEM case, each agent uses global information of the multiagent system, while in the distributed case, each agent only uses local information of its own and its neighbors. The multiagent system can achieve asymptotic consensus as well as exclude the Zeno phenomenon under the designed event-triggered rules in both cases.

11300415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300415.value: A decentralized networked coupled system (DNCS) consists of collaborating agents whose behavior is coordinated through wired or wireless communication links. It provides powerful tool to describe the dynamical behavior of many real-world engineering systems such as sensor networks and cyber-physical systems. Due to limited bandwidth of networks communication channels, it is necessary to save resources among agents in DNCSs. Event-triggered control strategies are known to have great potential to be more efficient than conventional time triggered (or sampled) control. In addition, the network systems always suffers different types of networked signal transmission constraints. When these kinds of constraints occur, the distributed behavior of the event based DNCSs often exhibits highly non-trivial dynamical characteristics. Hence, this will certainly lead to great reliability difficulties in controlling the network performance. The main aims in this project are (i) to design an effective event based sampling for DNCSs such that the signals are transmitted only when it is necessary. (ii) to develop a set of distributed event based algorithms that can be used by a group of agents to carry out prescribed tasks efficiently under limited information transmission constraints. The results from this work have both theoretical and practical significance in communication-based autonomous systems.

11300615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300615.value: 3D models are nowadays of high demand especially by the applications such as virtual reality and 3D printing. However, 3D modeling from scratch is rather difficult for unskilled users and still time-consuming even for professionals. On the other hand, the availability of large collections of 3D models together with various shape segmentation approaches offers a great opportunity for composing new 3D models by recombining the existing model parts. The key challenge is how to properly encode relationships between parts in existing models by shape analysis so that novel but still functionally plausible model variations can be easily created. Existing solutions often regard symmetry as the main semantic cue for encoding part-level relationships. However, such approaches are not applicable to objects or scenes exhibiting little or no symmetry. On the other hand, support with stability is another fundamental relationship between parts of objects in the physical world, especially for man-made objects. This motivates us to perform shape analysis in a support-driven manner, where the symmetry cue if applicable is still useful but becomes supplementary. In this project we will focus on shape analysis of man-made objects and explore a novel support-driven structural organization of their object parts. We are interested in defining and detecting special subsets of object parts with support and stability in existing models. We call such special subsets as support substructures. Using such support substructures instead of semantic parts as building blocks, makes it possible to synthesize both in-class and across-class variations. One of the key challenges in this work is to find a relatively small set of support substructures for easy creation of many novel, non-trivial, and interesting shape variations. We will show that such high-level shape analysis and the resulting support substructures benefit various applications, e.g., part-based shape reshuffling between models, structure rearrangement and synthesis for a single input model. We believe that our work will turn the attention of the research community more towards support and stability, which are very useful but have been largely unexplored for shape analysis and synthesis. 現如今三維模型在眾多應用比如虛擬現實和三維打印中有很高的需求。然而從無到有地模型構建對非專業用戶來說一直是一件很困難的任務。即使對於專業用戶來說創建高質量的三維模型還是一件很費時費力的事情。在另一方面，我們很容易從互聯網獲得大量的三維模型。同時由於這幾年一些高級的三維模型分割方法的提出，使得我們有機會可以通過重新組合已有的模型來產生大量新的三維模型。然而其中一個難點是如何有效地表示模型部件在原始模型中的重要關係，使得新生成的模型是看起來合理的，有意義的。現有的方法主要使用對稱性來表示部件之間的關係。基於對稱性的方法不能被運用到不含有或者沒多少對稱結構的物體或場景。 我們觀察到有穩定的支撐關係廣泛地存在於現實世界物體中，特別是人造物體。這個驅使我們考慮支撐性作為切入點去研究形狀分析。如果對稱性結構存在於物體中，我們仍可使用對稱性來輔助地進行基於支撐的形狀分析。在這個項目中，我們著重於人造物體的形狀分析，探索支撐關係在部件結構關係中所起的作用。支撐關係具有多樣性。我們比較感興趣的只是比較常見的並且有穩定性的支撐關係。我們稱它們為“支撐子結構”。利用這些子結構而不是物體部件本身，我們就有可能同時實現類內和類間的形體合成，生成比較多的形狀變化。這裡面的關鍵問題是如何定義和找到一組個數不多的支撐子結構，但是同時允許我們生成很多新的有意思的形狀變化。我們的支撐子結構有助於多個應用，比如基於部件的形狀重組、對單個模型進行結構重組和合成。穩定支撐還很少被應用到形狀分析和合成的研究中，我們希望通過這個項目會有更多的研究採用支撐關係作為形狀分析的一個新工具。

11300615.label: Realisation of objectives
11300615.value: We have achieved all the objectives. We started the project by using a purely geometric approach ([Journal 3] in Part C) to analyse a single man-made object using support with stability as the primary cue (Objective 1). We defined three commonly seen supporting relations among object parts (Objective 2) and identified such relations in a given man-made object by assuming that the object is under static stability by gravitational force (Objective 1). We then defined and identified subgraphs of the resulting support relation graph as support substructures (Objectives 3 and 4). The support substructures as building blocks can be combined to achieve support in multiple hierarchy, and benefit various applications such as shape reshuffling, structure rearrangement, and structure synthesis (Objective 5). We observed that while the support substructures by the above approach were able to generate many new shape variations, it was not guaranteed all the generated shapes were functionally plausible. One attempt we made to address this issue was to explore human-object relationships ([Journal 6]). We leveraged a human pose to explore object parts with proper affordance from four typical affordance types, which define support relations between different parts of a human body and different object parts (Objective 2). This led to a new structural organization of object parts (Objective 3), establishing a bridge between cross-class objects for composite design and enabling in-class and cross-class shape synthesis and functional hybrid creation (Objectives 4 and 5). We extended this idea to adaptive synthesis of indoor scenes via activity-associated object relation graphs, extracted from a database of 2D floor plans [Journal 5]. We also explored data-driven approaches for part-level shape analysis. Observing that structural relations are not necessarily defined between adjacent parts, we introduced a part-level structure descriptor to learn group-sensitive priors from a database of shapes with the same categories through clustering [Journal 1]. Such priors capture the inherent characteristics and typical variations of shape structures, thus implicitly defining support relations among object parts (Objectives 1 and 2) and benefiting the applications like shape reshuffling among objects from the same class (Objectives 4 and 5). Recently we extended this idea by adopting a deep learning based approach ([Journal 8]). More specifically, we encoded the geometry and associated relationships (including the supporting and supported relations) of a shape part using a representation vector. By concatenating representation vectors for all the parts as input in a consistent order, we jointly learned the part structure of a shape collection and the part geometries (Objectives 2 and 3) by training a structured parts VAE (Variational Autoencoder). This greatly benefited various applications including shape reconstruction, shape generation, and shape interpolation (Objectives 4 and 5). Support-driven shape analysis benefited not only object-level shape synthesis but also many other applications. For example, we presented a new 3D scene synthesis technique [Journal 2] by first extending the support relation graph among object parts [Journal 3] as augmented graphs to capture relations among objects in 3D indoor scenes and then reshuffling objects from different scenes (Objective 5). In [Journal 4], we introduced supporting relations as an additional measurement of the distance between patches in a graph-cut formulation for interactive segmentation of indoor scenes. We also explored the use of supporting relations as contextual cues for improving the performance of sketch classification [Conference 2]. Another application we explored was to exploit structural information in objects [Journal 7] or scenes [Conference 1] to anchor 2D freehand sketches in 3D, thus providing intuitive interfaces for creating 3D conceptual designs. Such ideas were further extended to develop Mobi3DSketch [CHI 2019], which was the first system for creating complex 3D sketches using a single AR-enabled mobile device. In this application, we used 3D proxies either manually specified by users or automatically derived from real-world objects to support 2D strokes and turn them into 3D. A US patent application based on this invention is under processing.

11300615.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300615.value: Support with stability plays an important role in our real world. In this project, we show support relations between object parts or between objects are useful for shape analysis and benefit various applications. Robustly identifying supporting relations from objects or scenes themselves is a challenging problem. A purely geometric approach [Journal 3] is flexible but might lead to insignificant or even wrongly detected supporting relations, which later might cause functionally implausible shape variations for the applications like shape reshuffling. Introducing additional cues, e.g., from a human pose [Journal 6], leads to higher-level object-human relations and thus greatly improves the quality of shape synthesis results. The availability of large-scale shape datasets like ShapeNet enables data-driven approaches for support-driven shape analysis and synthesis. We explored traditional clustering techniques for extracting group-sensitive priors within a small dataset of objects with the same categories [Journal 1] and deep learning techniques for learning support-induced structural information from a large-scale shape dataset based on ShapeNetCore. Such data-driven approaches essentially learn part-level structures from data in a more global perspective and generally perform better than our purely geometric approach [Journal 3]. We have shown that either explicitly extracted or implicitly learned supporting relations benefit various applications, including structure-adaptive shape editing [Journal 1], structure-guided interior scene synthesis [Journals 2 and 5], structure rearrangement [Journal 3], shape reshuffling [Journals 3 and 6], shape generation [Journal 8], shape interpolation [Journal 8], interactive segmentation of indoor scenes [Journal 4], model-guided 3D sketching [Journal 7], sketch-based 3D prototyping [Conference 1], context-based sketch classification [Conference 2], and 3D sketching in mobile AR [Conference 3]. The project led to in total 11 publications, including 8 journal papers and 3 conference papers. See the highlighted papers below (the rankings below are based on Google Scholar Metrics; as of 17 February 2020): - Journals 5 and 8: in ACM Transactions on Graphics (No. 1 in graphics); also presented at SIGGRAPH Asia 2017 and 2019 (SIGGRAPH and SIGGRAPH Asia are the best graphics conferences); - Journals 3, 6, and 7: in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (No. 2 in graphics); - Journal 1: in Computer Graphics Forum (No. 3 in graphics); also presented at Eurographics 2016 (a top graphics conference); - Conference 1: presented as a full conference paper at ACM UIST 2017 (No. 4 in HCI); - Conference 3: presented as a full conference paper at ACM CHI 2019 (No. 1 in HCI).

11300615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300615.value: There are multiple areas to be explored in the future. For example, on top of our purely geometric approach [Journal 3], it is interesting to perform more careful stability analysis, e.g., a systematic treatment of force flow and structural stability with more realistic physical assumptions. Although our data-driven approaches [Journals 1 and 8] achieve good performance for analyzing part-level shape structures, they have to be trained on a dataset of shapes from the same categories. It is interesting to investigate how to extend them to encode shapes of different categories, possibly demanding a more general shape representation. We expect that support-driven shape analysis also benefits applications other than those demonstrated in our publications. For example, supporting relations might be used to parse structural information in primitives in images and thus assist in the task of shape reconstruction from images.

11300615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300615.value: Support with stability plays an important role in the organization of our real-world objects and scenes. This motivated us to revisit the fundamental shape analysis topic from a new perspective of support with stability. We explored support-driven shape analysis solutions by explicitly defining and extracting supporting relations from single 3D models and introducing support substructures. We found that data-driven solutions, particularly based on deep learning technologies, are able to better capture semantic relations between object parts by learning part-level structures from a large-scale dataset of shapes. The extracted supporting relations allow the generation of nontrivial but functionally plausible shape variations via operations such as structure reshuffling, structure rearrangement, shape interpolation, shape generation, and structure-adaptive shape editing. We have also shown that support-driven shape analysis is beneficial to many other applications, including indoor scene segmentation and synthesis, sketch-based prototyping, context-based sketch classification, and 3D sketching in mobile AR. The major findings of this project have been published in top venues of computer graphics and human-computer interaction and led to a US patent application. We believe that we have taken an important step towards support-driven shape analysis and that our findings will be inspiring for the follow-up works in this area.

11300715.label: Project Objectives
11300715.value: Design of feature representation for dataset comparison – We shall consider how to define the notion of similarity between two datasets, such that a query data set can be used to retrieve datasets with compatible cluster structures from an archive. We propose to measure this compatibility using an underlying feature representation based on a set of exemplar clustering views. Transfer of clustering information based on similarity retrieval– Given a query dataset, we retrieve similar datasets from the archive using the new feature representation, and use them to learn a joint latent space with the query, based on which unsupervised transfer learning is applied. The main motivation is to leverage extrinsic information from auxiliary data sources such that the clustering performance could be improved beyond that based on a single dataset. Evaluation of proposed framework – The issue of how to incorporate the retrieved datasets into the transfer clustering process according to their ranked importance in the retrieval list, and how to inject the optimal amount of extrinsic information to maximally improve the clustering performance without disturbing the original query dataset structure, will be comprehensively investigated.
