11300715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300715.value: Clustering is an important stage in the knowledge discovery process for identifying possible groupings of data into different subsets, each of which contains similar entities. Due to the unsupervised nature of the process, the clustering results are sensitive to the presence of noise and outliers, and there is a strong motivation of leveraging extrinsic information and/or auxiliary datasets to enhance the results. To address the challenge of optimizing this cross-dataset clustering process, we propose to adopt an information retrieval perspective, through which a dataset at hand is regarded as a search query. Using this query, multiple auxiliary datasets with similar cluster structures are retrieved from an external archive. The structural information from these external data is then leveraged via an unsupervised transfer learning framework to enhance the clustering results. A critical idea in facilitating the query/auxiliary dataset comparison during retrieval is the association of each dataset with a multi-dimensional feature vector. The vector components represent the conformance of that dataset to multiple exemplar clustering solutions, with each solution summarizing a different structural aspect of the auxiliary datasets in the archive. In this way, the cluster structures of the query/auxiliary datasets can be compared from multiple perspectives corresponding to the different solutions. We propose to search for these exemplar solutions through a multi-objective evolutionary optimization process, which takes into consideration both the criteria of clustering quality and diversity. In this way, a population of representative yet complementary clustering solutions can be discovered. In view of the scarcity of works on cross-dataset clustering, and the lack of a systematic approach for leveraging extrinsic information to enhance clustering results, the proposed framework represents an important step toward automatizing data interpretation/understanding for knowledge discovery. With the exponential rate of data growth in many areas, and the resulting availability of large data archives which contain, e.g. multiple spatiotemporal snapshots of an evolving process, the proposed framework represents a bridge between the previous disparate fields of information retrieval, cross-domain unsupervised learning, and multi-view clustering, such that the potential huge amount of encapsulated information in archived data can be unlocked based on this novel perspective of addressing the clustering problem. In this way, the framework can be applied to a broad range of areas such as crowd movement pattern segmentation in surveillance video understanding, 3D point cloud segmentation in computer graphics, gene expression clustering in bioinformatics, and community detection in social media analysis. 聚類分析是用於甄別一些可能屬於不同類別數據的重要方法。由於非監督學習方法的性質，聚類分析的結果容易受到噪聲和極端值的影響，因此（這些缺點）也促使考慮利用外部信息或者輔助數據集來改進聚類的結果。 為了解決優化這種跨數據聚類方法的問題，我們提出利用信息檢索觀點，通過已有的數據作為搜索的條件。利用這些搜索條件，從外部數據集中抽取具有相似聚類結構的輔助數據。這些來自外部數據的結構信息則可以通過非監督遷移學習的方法用來改進聚類的結果。 在檢索過程中，進行比較檢索及輔助數據的關鍵點在於運用一個特征向量來表示每一個數據集。這些向量的分量可以表示數據集對多個典型聚類結果的相容性，而每一個聚類結果概括了輔助數據不同方面的結構性。通過這種方法，檢索及輔助數據的結構可以通過不同角度來進行比較。 我們提出通過多目標演化優化算法搜索這些典型結果，因這種算法能同時以聚類的質量和多樣性作為優化標準，從而找到具有代表性及互補的聚類結果。由於以往對於跨數據聚類方面的研究工作不多，這裏所提出的框架是對於數據解釋/理解自動化的重要一步。 隨著在不同領域數據的急促增長（例如：隨時間增加的多維序列數據），這裏所提出的框架為各個完全不同的領域如信息檢索，跨域無監督學習和多觀點聚類提供聯系，並能有效地發掘數據中潛在的海量信息，使這種算法框架可以應用到更多方面，如在監測視頻中人群的特征辨別，計算機圖像學中三維點雲的分割，生物信息學中基因表達的聚類及社交媒體分析中的社區發現。

11300715.label: Realisation of objectives
11300715.value: Design of clustering solution representation We have successfully designed a succinct representation of a clustering solution to summarize its main structure, and formulated a proximity measure based on which effective comparison of these solutions can be performed. This representation is developed from the viewpoint of ensemble clustering, which enhances the final clustering performance through the judicious combination of multiple solutions (ensemble). Since not all clustering solutions contribute equally to the enhancement of the clustering process, the proposed representation and its associated proximity measure serves to identify a subset of ensemble members which are more compatible with the data set at hand. Specifically, we summarize each clustering solution using a Gaussian mixture model (GMM), through which the original data distribution is approximated using multiple Gaussian density functions. In this way, the cluster structure can be succinctly represented using the associated parameters of the model. Based on this representation, we formulate a number of proximity measures to quantify the extent to which two clustering solutions are similar to each other. Since each solution is summarized in the form of a set of Gaussian density functions, the proximity of two solutions can be measured through the similarities between their associated Gaussian mixture components. Different variants of this similarity measure have been considered, and it is observed that the adoption of a suitably weighted average distance measure among the pairs of mixture components leads to the best results. Due to the unequal importance of the ensemble members in contributing to the final result, we apply our proposed proximity measure to assign a score to each member, based on its distance from all other members, and use a probabilistic selection mechanism to sample the solutions based on this score. By judiciously integrating the Gaussian mixture components of the resulting sub-ensemble of solutions using a normalized hypergraph cut approach, we obtain a final set of components which succinctly summarize the cluster structure of the data set. Modeling of multiple clustering tasks We have successfully developed a multi-task clustering framework in which multiple related clustering tasks are performed together, such that the performance can be mutually enhanced. Specifically, the set of tasks are partitioned into groups of similar tasks, within which clustering information can be effectively transferred. The proposed framework is evaluated through a number of real-world text and image datasets. We consider various scenarios in which the number of dimensions and the number of clusters can be different across the related tasks. Our main observation is that our proposed framework outperforms previous multi-task clustering approaches, since these approaches have not considered the effect of negative aspects of cross-task information transfer, and unequal contribution of the features to the different clusters in the various tasks. In addition, we also observe that in general the performance improvement is most significant when related tasks have the same number of clusters and different numbers of dimensions. On the other hand, while those tasks with different numbers of clusters cannot attain similar level of performance, they can still benefit from the complementary information introduced through the task diversity. Transfer of clustering information We have successfully developed a framework to transfer information across different clustering solutions. Specifically, we apply a generative adversarial network to synthesize diverse clustering solutions, based on which solution retrieval and fusion can be conducted to improve clustering performance. Building on the foundation of our work in multi-task clustering, in which information is shared across multiple clustering tasks to enhance overall performance, we further develop this framework by considering the scenario in which there are a set of easy tasks and one difficult task. We first perform joint feature extraction for the samples in both the easy tasks and the difficult task using an encoder-decoder deep network, such that each sample can be mapped to a latent low-dimensional representation. Based on the resulting representation, we first apply clustering to obtain pseudo-labels for the samples in the easy tasks. In other words, samples within the same cluster are associated with the pseudo-label. These pseudo-labels are then used as inputs of a conditional generative adversarial network (CGAN) to synthesize new samples belonging to the various clusters. The original and generated samples are then shuffled and combined to form a set of batches. For each batch, we learn a feature projection matrix which, when applied to the samples in the batch, results in the best approximation of the cluster partition matrix. The feature projection matrix serves as a succinct summary of the clustering solution associated with the batch. In this way, we obtain a series of clustering solutions for the batches, in the form of feature projection matrices. To synthesize new clustering solutions, we apply a generative adversarial network to learn the distribution of these projection matrices. After the training process is completed, new projection matrices from the learnt distribution can be sampled from the network. To enhance the clustering performance of the difficult task, we leverage information from the set of easy tasks, by suitably fusing their associated set of learnt and synthesized feature projection matrices. Specifically, the samples in the difficult task are transformed using these projection matrices. By referencing the nearest neighbors of these transformed samples in the easy tasks and their associated degree of similarities in their respective clustering solutions, the resulting similarity matrix of the samples in the difficult task can be estimated. Clustering can then be performed based on these estimated pairwise similarity values which incorporate information from the extrinsic clustering solutions. Evaluation of clustering performance We have successfully evaluated the clustering performance of our proposed framework on different real-world datasets. By measuring the performance using accuracy and normalized mutual information, we observe that our approach is capable of discovering the correct cluster structure for a wide variety of application domains, including social media analysis, image classification, and metabolic network analysis, by leveraging information from external yet related datasets. We have conducted extensive experiments to investigate different aspects of the proposed framework, including sensitivity to parameter values and network architectures, and the relative importance of different stages through ablation studies.

11300715.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300715.value: At the initial stage, we consider a simplified scenario from the perspective of ensemble clustering. In this scenario, the multiple clustering solutions in the ensemble can be considered as the auxiliary retrieved clustering solutions from a repository. The proximity measure between two solutions developed in the context of this task can shed light on how to compare two cluster structures in the similarity retrieval process, and how information can be transferred across different clustering solutions, which serves to enhance the clustering performance through leveraging information from extrinsic solutions. We have also developed a new framework to leverage information from a set of extrinsic clustering solutions to enhance performance. Specifically, the probability distribution of the solutions obtained through a set of easy clustering tasks is modeled using GANs, based on which new solutions can be generated. For a new and possibly difficult clustering problem, a critical task will be to accurately estimate the degree of similarity between samples. By judiciously incorporating the synthesized clustering solutions related to the current problem through a multi-task learning framework, the resulting clustering performance can be enhanced through improved estimation of the similarity matrix. By applying the proposed framework to datasets from different application domains, the main research findings include: -The incorporation of multiple synthetic clustering solutions through generative modeling enables our approach to outperform a broad set of previous approaches, including ensemble clustering and multi-task clustering. This highlights the effectiveness of leveraging information from extrinsic sources to enhance clustering performance. -While the performance of both the current approach and ensemble clustering improves with the incorporation of more solutions, we observe that the improvement gain can be sustained over a larger range of solution numbers for our approach. On the other hand, for ensemble clustering, the performance gain exhibits early saturation when additional clustering solutions are incorporated. -The performance improves with an increase in the depth and width of the generative modeling networks for synthesizing the clustering solutions up to certain values, beyond which diminishing return is observed. This is due to the need of requiring an increasing amount of data to train the network when its architecture becomes more complex.

11300715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300715.value: We shall conduct a more comprehensive evaluation of the proposed framework based on data sets from different application domains. Specifically, we shall consider a number of scenarios, which include the clustering of low dimensional data sets with a large number of samples (e.g. image and video segmentation), and high dimensional data sets with a small number of samples (e.g. clustering of gene expression profiles), in addition to the previous data sets used. In addition, representative data sets from domains corresponding to the above scenarios will be used to build clustering solution repositories, to be applied for clustering new datasets belonging to related domains. The extent to which the incorporation of the extrinsic solutions from the repository can enhance the clustering performance will be determined by comparing the resulting solution with the one estimated using the original data set alone.

11300715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300715.value: In this project, we approach the problem of data clustering from an information retrieval perspective. Specifically, we consider a data set as a query, based on which structurally related auxiliary datasets are retrieved from an archive. In this way, the combined data set will provide additional information to facilitate the attainment of enhanced clustering performance, compared to the case in which only the original data set, with possibly an inadequate number of samples, is used. In view of the rapid rate of data growth in many areas, and the resulting availability of large data archives, the proposed new framework can effectively leverage the information in these archived data to address difficult clustering problems. In this way, the framework can be applied to a broad set of real-world applications, which include image/video understanding, medical information mining, and social media analysis.

11300815.label: Project Objectives
11300815.value: To collect empirical data of passenger/ pedestrian flow characteristics and passengercarried fire load pattern in Hong Kong metro stations. This includes counting of movement speed of different persons, inter-person characteristics, gate-passing pattern, volumetric quantity of passenger-carried items, identification of types of carry-on items and other activities in stations. Data collection may include on-site counting,observations, pursuing walkers’ route choice, extraction of information from video images, questionnaire surveys and etc. To establish a grid-based field survey method to collect the volumetric quantity of passenger-carried items and to identify the types of carry-on items and activities in stations. 11300815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300815.value: 香港以及中国其他许多大城市市区人口密度高，在这样的城市，公共交通服务的需求巨大。地铁是现代城市交通运输体系的重要组成部分，因此铁路和车站构成了人们日常生活中不可或缺的一部分。车站有众多不同的用途，例如商店，银行，快餐店，展览等，因此，车站内的乘客可能在前往乘坐列车期间从事其他活动。在香港，上海或北京等地的地铁系统，日均旅客输运量十分庞大，因此在一天内的大部分时间地铁车站十分拥挤。尽管大多数的现代地铁设施采用不燃材料，但是乘客可能携带行李和其他可燃物，这种情况在终点站更为明显。由于随身携带包裹引起严重的火灾的案例在香港和其他国家都有发生，例如2004年1月在香港地铁发生的火灾事故。但是，尚未有研究关注乘客携带火灾荷载引发的火灾危险。研究乘客携带火灾载荷火灾风险的一个困难是它的动态性。为了研究这种动态的乘客携带的火灾荷载，我们需要详细分析车站内乘客运动模式。能够模拟乘客运动和其他活动的计算机模型将是本研究的一个重要组成部分。在本项目中，我们的目标是建立一个有效的仿真模型用以研究地铁和铁路系统中乘客携带的动态火灾荷载。该模型将是一个微观仿真模型，可以模拟单个个体的运动模式。此外，还将针对乘客携带火灾载荷开展全面的现场调查。本研究将包括3个主要部分：（1）现场收集乘客的运动特征数据和随身携带行李的火灾载荷数据；（2）在基于Agent的客流仿真模型基础上建立乘客携带行李动态火灾荷载仿真模型；（3）发展关联乘客动态分布特征的地铁站火灾风险模型。

11300815.label: Realisation of objectives
11300815.value: (1) Daegu, Korea subway fire (“Daegu subway fire,” 2003), Hong Kong train fire (“At least 18 injured in fire on Hong Kong metro train,” 2017) strongly demonstrated that passengers’ belongings would also bring potential fire risk to metro stations. Therefore, in order to provide a safer and more efficient transportation environment to passengers, it is essential to take the fire risk of passengers’ belongings into consideration when conducting crowd management. Unlike the fire risks caused by the building structures and facilities, the fire risk induced by passengers-carried fire load not merely varies over time but changes spatially with passengers’ motion as well. The research team collected empirical data of passenger/ pedestrian flow characteristics and passenger-carried fire load pattern in Hong Kong metro stations. The information included counting of movement speed of different persons, inter-person characteristics, gate-passing pattern, volumetric quantity of passenger-carried items, identification of types of carry-on items and other activities in stations. The data were used to calibrate the simulation model, as described in (2) below, developed for assessing the dynamic fire risk map in stations. (2) As described in (1) above, the research team has developed a dynamic risk evaluation (DRE) simulation model which can assist crowd management from the perspective of the potential fire risk of passenger-carried fire load. The model combined pedestrian (passenger) movement modeling with fire risk calculation module, which could easily take passengers’ motion into account and be helpful for crowd management in transportation hubs like metro stations. the DRE model could not only display a dynamic graphical demonstration of fire risk distribution within the simulated scenarios but also output some detailed simulation outcomes (including existing duration of fire risks, the trend of fire risks over time, the locomotion time and the trajectory for every pedestrian). (3) The data collection as described above was supported by a grid-based field survey method to collect the volumetric quantity of passenger-carried items and to identify the types of carry-on items and activities in stations. (4) Microscopic simulation model, the DRE, comprises 3 parts. In the first part, vital information is required as inputs of the model, such as the environment information, pedestrian properties, as well as the security demand. The second part is model calculation process, which is established with pedestrian movement module and fire risk calculation module. Pedestrian movement module mainly deals with the movement of passengers at every time step, while fire risk calculation module determines the variation of fire risks induced by passenger-carried fire load. The calculation of spatiotemporal fire risk distribution is executed by the aforementioned two modules with mutual communication. Once pedestrian properties have been provided, the pedestrian movement module will initialize the pedestrians along with their belongings (passenger-carried fire load) in the simulated area. At the same time, fire risk calculation module will rank the fire risk levels of passenger-carried fire load and generate their influencing area. The calculation time interval of the model is predetermined according to security demand in the first part. After that, based on pedestrians’ moving characteristics, a multi-velocity floor field cellular model is incorporated into pedestrian movement module to govern their actual movement and then calculates the moving direction at the next time step through transfer probability. The third part aims to provide fundamental guidance for making decisions for management departments. In part, a spatiotemporal fire risk distribution within the simulated area can be displayed intuitively as a dynamic graphical demonstration, and this will be the primary output for qualitative judgment. The output simulation results can be output as animations which is useful for general facility management. Specifically, our DRE model idealizes every pedestrian and their belongings (passenger-carried fire load) as an integral whole. It is represented by cells with different colors, and numbers are used to simplify the manifestation of fire risks. (5) In this study, two simplified typical scenarios in metro stations were constructed to detail the influence of the initial distribution, the ratio of passengers with high-risk fire load, as well as system scale on the fire risk pattern. Simulation results revealed that the initial distribution of passengers strongly affected their staying time. If passengers with high-risk fire load are distributed in those areas which are close to the exits or other places, fire risk within this area could be reduced rapidly. Conversely, once the passengers who carry high-risk fire load are far away from the exit, the fire risk range would be relatively large and last for a long time. To solve this problem, the critical point is to reduce the staying time of these groups who carry high-risk fire load. To this end, lifts and moving walkways could be applied, also the escalators can speed up properly to avert the crowd together with the potential fire risk staying too long in the platform or concourse. The ratio of passengers with high-risk fire load and entrance flow rate play similar roles in affecting the spatial-temporal distribution of fire risk. Facility management of metro system should adopt more measures to keep them at low levels. It is relatively easy to control the entrance flow rate by adjusting the service time of automatic fare gates, setting up zig-zag channels, and modifying the velocities of escalators. However, it is hard to control the ratio of passengers with high-risk fire load within the station. One possible measure is to set up fences to separate different passenger groups with the help of security machines since it can easily identify the fire risk level of passengers’ belongings. (6) System scale is one of the most important parameters in our simulations, and it reflects the applicability of the DRE model. The outputs of the simulation indicate that smaller system sizes would result in higher volatility in the simulation outcomes. Stable simulation outputs have higher credibility and also helps the management department to take appropriate steps. Therefore, using DRE model to visualize dynamic fire risk distribution within a region is best applied to larger size simulation scenarios.

11300815.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300815.value: To facilitate efficient planning for pedestrian movement and to evaluate the potential fire risk in metro stations, research on the passenger-carried fire load pattern deserves more attention and efforts. In this project, a microscopic simulation model was established, through the combination of pedestrian flow modeling and fire risk assessment, and adopted for mapping fire risk of passenger-carried fire load. Research outputs was published in a top ranked SCI journal [Part C 8.1 refers]. Moreover, a PhD student (graduated in June, 2020), under the supervision of the PI, has been trained. The research title of the PhD student is “Dynamic Risk Evaluation for Passenger-Carried Fire Load in Metro System” [Part C 10.2 refers]. The works have further been developed to evaluate the dynamic fire risk in metro, findings have been consolidated and submitted for publication [Part C 8.4 refers]. While researching in fire risk evaluation for metro station, the research team has also explored the possibility of using visual image to detect the existence of fire. Using remote sensing technology and integrating with an artificial intelligent approach (e.g. Convolutional Neural Network) to evaluate fire risk has also been carried out for wildfire [Part C 8.2, 8.3 and 10.3 refer]. Similar prediction algorithm may be applicable to evaluate dynamic fire risk in metro stations. This may lead to future research works. To extend the monitoring of fire risk for a larger area, including the network connected to the metro system has been studied. We have considered the design and decision making framework for bus-to-metro network system. We have investigated the decision-making required for bus and metro interconnectivity and optimize public transportation networks. Though, it is not the main theme of the project, it is a study evolved from the project and the findings have been published [Part C 8.4 refers].

11300815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300815.value: In a metro station, the passenger-carried fire load intensity and characteristics and the desired movement speed of passengers constitute the dynamic nature of fire risk. In this study, a passenger-carried fire load model has been developed to simulate the risk mapping on passenger with fire load, but not the strategic and tactical level management. The outputs may be used to analyze/ find out high-risk regions and provide information for facility management and design of metro facilities. In future, substantial research efforts can be devoted to the extension and modification of the model and apply it for more dynamic situations. Additional surveys and field studies can also be conducted in metro stations to more explicitly classify the risk levels of passenger-carried fire load, and the experimental study on fire behaviors of all types of passenger-carried fire load should be implemented to estimate the influencing area of different types of passenger-carried fire load. Moreover, it has been demonstrated in a study associated with this project that the use of Convolutional Neural Network or similar artificial intelligent algorithm may be applicable to predict the effect of fire loading if sufficient volume of data can be collected.

11300815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300815.value: Crowd management research in metro stations or other similar transportation terminals often ignores the fire risk generated by the passenger-carried fire load. In this study, we established a dynamic risk evaluation model to assess the fire risk of the passenger-carried fire load. The model can be adopted to analyze spatial settings and crowd movement pattern by focusing on the influence of the initial distribution, the ratio of passengers with high-risk fire load, as well as system scale on the fire risk pattern. Simulation results demonstrated that farther distance to the metro exits would result in a relatively higher fire risk for a relatively long period. Both the ratio of passengers with high-risk fire load and entrance flow rate indicated exponential relationships with the proportion of high-risk regions. The findings of this study could bring new insights for initial spatial design and crowd management of transportation hubs like metro stations as well as the management of facilities.

11301015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301015.value: Over 4 million people a day ride on around 1000 escalators in Hong Kong’s metro system. With approximately 16.8 million escalator rides, around four people persons are injured each day giving a total of approximately 1,400 injuries per year. These accidents resulted in serious delays in metro operation and extremely stressful and heavy burden on the metro operators and engineers causing multi-millions of losses financially to the metro company in particular and the society at large. Due the lack of standardized approach of prediction of accidents, currently, metro engineers could only modified the hardware of escalator systems as much as they could to improve their safety. Safety officers can only post various safety messages, in the form of posters and voice announcements, to raise passengers' safety awareness when using the escalators inside metro stations. However, accidents on escalators remain top of the metro system's accident list. We recently conducted a study in which the passenger throughput rate (PTR) of a station was found to be a major contributing factor to the escalator-related accident rate (EAR). Normally, the EAR is low when the PTR of the station is low. The accident records of a sample of metro stations in Hong Kong were investigated. It was found that a critical PTR exists at which the EAR reaches its maximum. Further increases in the PTR reduce the EAR. It was also found that this critical PTR is not a constant but varies for different stations. Therefore, in addition to the PTR, other station factors must contribute to the determination of the critical PTR. The research team aims to identify these factors for each station and build a model to show the correlation between the PTR and the EAR. Because these factors may be related to the design of the station and other human related activities, and no prior knowledge of the correlation is available, an intelligent approach is proposed to mimic the correlation between them. Following the completion of this project, a real-time intelligent-based monitoring model will be developed to predict the critical PTR at different times for the existing stations or the design of new stations. When the condition of a station becomes unfavourable and approaches the critical PTR, the prediction model will alert the station officers to take appropriate action. This intelligent approach will reduce the accident rate on metro station escalators and hence assisting to alleviate financial and societal losses.

11301015.label: Realisation of objectives
11301015.value: Task 1 – Data collection and processing This task corresponded to objective (i). The outcome of this task was the categorised database of escalator accidents in metro stations ready for development of quantifiable information to support the online learning clustering model for prediction of probability of accident occurrence. The comprehensive data recording system of metro stations had been made available to the research team. It stores the accident records of all 84 metro stations since their opening day. The database included not only escalator-related accidents but also all other types of accidents. The records of all escalator-related accidents for the past 10 years had been retrieved. Each accident record in the metro station database consisting of attributes of the records were categorised into three groups: station information, casualty information, and passenger throughput rate. The categorised database of escalator accidents in metro stations had been established. Task 2 – Development of quantification scheme This task corresponded to objective (ii). The outcome of this task was the quantification scheme for qualitative variables to identify factors attributing to critical throughput rate associated with the maximum rate of escalator-related accidents. Some of the attributes of the accident records are qualitative in nature. For further data mining, it is necessary to quantify the qualitative data. For example, the location of the station provides information on the characteristics of the passengers using the station. If it is located in a shopping area, passengers usually carry shopping bags and use the station leisurely. If it is located in a commercial area, passengers are usually in hurry, which may contribute to the accident rate. To quantify this variable, a vector presentation in the form of {x_1,x_2,x_3 }, where x_1 represents the proportion of commercial buildings to all surrounding buildings within 1 km of the station had been adopted. Similarly, x_2 and x_3 represent the proportion of shopping malls and residential buildings to the surrounding buildings, respectively. The other qualitative attributes had been quantified to establish the joint probability to be used in Task 3. Task 3 – Development of the critical PTR prediction model This task corresponded to objective (iii). The outcome of this task was the ANN model for data clustering in multi-dimensional space (i.e. hyperspace) with online learning capability for probability prediction of escalator accidents. This task was started by utilising the escalator-related accident records of one station collected from Task 1. The accident records collected from Task 1 and processed in Task 2 consisting of multiple attributes were used to establish a hyperspace for locating all accident records by the system information attributes (SI) and the passenger throughput rate (PTR). The probability distribution of the records over this hyperspace p(SI,PTR) was constructed at this stage. A kernel-based artificial neural network model had been proposed. This is a non-parametric model that can approximate the underlying probability distribution by applying a Parzen density estimator to merge the different Gaussian kernels. However, the required number of Gaussian kernels was a critical factor in this approach. Fewer kernels would smooth out the details of the actual distribution. Excessive kernels would treat the noise content of the records as nonlinearity in the system (i.e., over fitting). Also, fixing the number of Gaussian distributions was not realistic as it might change when more accident records were received in the future. The traditional kernel-based artificial neural network model is an offline learning model. When a new escalator-related record had been received, this new record together with all previous records were used to update the kernel-based model to include the information from this new record. This had been a major hurdle for a real-time application because the prediction system would be required to be idle for some time while the kernel-based model is reconstructed. The PENN model developed provided a potential solution to this problem. The pre-processor of the PENN model was a novel clustering approach that utilised probabilistic theories and information entropy. It had been mathematically proven to be capable of working in noisy environments. The PENN model was also an online learning model. Similar to other ANN models, a limitation of the PENN model was that its performance was greatly affected by the initialisation of a new kernel. The initialisation had been carried out manually. Improvements to the PENN model had been investigated. The nearest-neighbour approach had been applied to upgrade the PENN model to a fully autonomous ANN model that would not require any human intervention in the initialisation of a new kernel. Further analysis had been carried out to identify the possible conditions that may trigger an accident. The accident records had been extracted from the escalator-related accident database. Statistical analysis had carried out to determine the possible accident triggering conditions (e.g. upward travel escalator, passenger carrying bags, etc.). The station officers could then take appropriate actions to prevent the occurrence of such accidents.

11301015.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301015.value: In this research, data collection to allow identification of these factors will be a labor-intensive exercise. The research team had collaborated with the metro system and had acquired data for this research project. An artificial neural network (ANN) was proposed to mimic the correlation between the station factors, the critical passenger throughput rate (PTR) and the escalator-related accident rate (EAR). The performance of the ANN depended on the quality of the training samples. Because some of the factors might relate to human activities, the training samples had included fluctuations that might adversely affect the overall performance of the ANN model. The ANN model has been capable of working in a noisy environment. The ANN model was trained on a large batch of samples extracted from the accident records of the metro system. When a new escalator-related accident occurred, a new sample would be created and the ANN model updated. It would be very time consuming if the ANN model needed to be trained on the large batch of training samples together with the new sample. Therefore, the model had been equipped with online learning ability, which only required the new sample to update the ANN model. The PENN model developed in this project has been an online learning model only requiring a new sample to update the model parameters without the presence of the previously used samples. The most significant outcome of this research had been the establishment of the categorized database of escalator accidents in metro stations ready for development of quantifiable information to support the online learning clustering model for prediction of probability of accident occurrence. Also, the real-time intelligent-based prediction model developed by this project can be applied to predict the critical passenger throughput rate of metro stations. It will monitor the actual condition of a station at each time step. When the actual condition approaches the unfavorable condition determined by the model, the monitoring system will alert the station officers to take appropriate action.

11301015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301015.value: Escalator-related accidents are constantly top of the accident list in the metro system. The output of this research will help to alleviate this long-term problem in the metro system. The prediction model can be used not only in existing metro stations but can also be applied during the design stage of a new metro station to minimize the escalator-related accident rate. Further research can be proposed based on the outcomes of this research, in long-term, to address the critical passenger throughput rate of escalators in metro stations and hence improving the escalator system safety correspondingly. Also, one of the proposed course of actions can be the development of a standardized framework for assessment of escalator safety in metro systems.

11301015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301015.value: Our recent study shows the existence of a critical passenger throughput rate (PTR) of a metro station at which the escalator-related accident rate (EAR) reaches its maximum. However, this critical PTR varies for different stations. It is necessary to identify the contributing factors in relation to the critical PTR for each station. These factors may include the time and day when accidents are most likely to occur, the station’s capacity, the number of people using the station, its location (e.g., commercial or residential area), and so forth. The identification of those contributing factors had been the key issue for this project. The overall aim of this proposed research was to develop an intelligent prediction model ready to evaluate the critical passenger throughput rate at which the probability of accident occurrence is maximum, for any existing station. The prediction can provide information to the operators of the station to adjust their strategy accordingly. The developed prediction model can also be used in the design of new stations to optimize the station design and minimize the accident rate. It can be further developed to formulate a standardized framework for assessment of escalator safety in metro systems.

11301215.label: Project Objectives
11301215.value: To incorporate the appropriate amounts of antibacterial agents into surface nano-functionalized titanium alloys to predesigned depths to enhance the antibacterial efficacy and long-term effectiveness To achieve close to 100% antibacterial resistance for at least 28 days and maintain the ability for as long as possible To study the underlying factors affecting bacteria resistance and biocompatibility as well as role played by the plasma-implanted antibacterial agents such as leaching kinetics To design and fabricate temporary surfaces by PIII&D to control the degradation rate on magnesium alloys To study the biodegradation behavior in simulated physiological solutions with emphasis on the corrosion mechanism

11301215.label: Realisation of objectives
11301215.value: The objective of surface design on biodegradable metals is to alter but not change permanently the surface structure and properties. In this project, we aim at fabricating temporary surfaces with a controllable degradation rate on magnesium alloys by PIII&D while allowing osteoblasts to attach, proliferate, migrate, and differentiate. We have achieved the following objectives: (1) The appropriate amounts of various types of antibacterial agents are incorporated into the surface of nano-functionalized titanium and other alloys to predesigned depths to enhance the antibacterial efficacy and long-term effectiveness. (2) Close to 100% antibacterial resistance is achieved and the effectiveness is maintained for a relatively ong time. (3) The mechanism responsible for the bacteria resistance and biocompatibility is investigated and the role played by the plasma-implanted antibacterial agents such as leaching kinetics are revealed. (4) Temporary and dynamic surfaces are designed and prepared by plasma-based and related techniques to control the degradation rate of magnesium and similar alloys. (5) The biodegradation and corrosion behavior of surface-modified biomaterials in simulated physiological solutions and other media are assessed.

11301215.value: We will continue to perform research in this area, including our latest RGC GRF No. CityU 11205617 (Nanostructured Ti-Based and Polymeric Orthopedic Implant Materials with Tailored Mechanobiocidal and Osteogenic Properties).

11301215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301215.value: Plasma-based techniques are widely used in the microelectronics, metallurgical, and biomedical industry and metallic biomaterials are important particularly for the repair and replacement of diseased and damaged bone tissues. In this project, we focus on the following primary tasks: (1) Surface modification and characterization of biomaterials, (2) Investigation and optimization of cells-materials and bacteria-materials interactions, (3) Evaluation of the biological performance of the surface-functionalized materials in vitro and in vivo, and (4) Systematic investigation of the underlying mechanisms responsible for the enhanced biological properties and corrosion resistance. Our results reveal that biomaterials modified by plasma-based and related techniques have enhanced biological, corrosion, as well as mechanical properties. The project has generated a large number of papers and conference presentations and three PhD students have been trained.

11302215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302215.value: 本專案擬研究在由粒子的運動所導致且由Maxwell方程所描述的電磁場外力以及粒子之間二體碰撞兩者相互作用下的稀薄等離子體的外區域問題的性態分析。該問題具有很強的物理背景，在數學上具有挑戰性。本項目基於我們以前關於經典的Boltzmann方程外區域問題的研究以及我們最近關於Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann方程組譜分析的工作，因而是可行的。 雖然對宏觀尺度下的流體力學方程組的外區域問題已經有令熱滿意的數學理論，但是對於介觀尺度下的動理學方程，相應的結論卻很少。例如在宏觀尺度下，Bers，Courant-Friedrichs，Morawetz，Finn-Gilbarg，Gilbarg-Shiffman，Dong，Chen，Chen-Deldman，Liu-Xin-Yin，Elling-Liu等關於亞音速、超音速和跨音速的許多重要工作。另一方面，在介觀尺度下，有Hilbert以及以Chapman-Enskog，Grad，Kogan和Maslova等為代表的哥廷根學派的開創性工作，以及Hamdache和Arkeryd-Cercignani等在DiPerna-Lions重整化解框架下的工作。在擾動框架下，Ukai-Asano給出了在無窮遠Mach數充分小情形下的一個嚴格的適定性理論。這一方法後來被我們加以改進進而用來處理一般的邊界條件的情形。 最近我們關於圍繞一個整體Maxwell分佈線性化的單個粒子和兩個粒子的Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann方程組的精確譜結構工作表明它們與經典的Boltzmann方程有很大的差別。本項目我們擬在這一工作的基礎上，進一步發展由Ukai-Asano提出的方法來研究Vlasov- Maxwell-Boltzmann方程組的外區域問題。為此，我們將應用在散射理論中principle of limiting absorption，解運算元的分解，以及由Golse-Lions-Perthame-Sentis等引入的速度平均引理等。必須要一些新的想法來適當分解解運算元以便保證它們在適當的函數空間中有界性和緊性。 本項目的研究可以應用到其他複雜的動理學方程組，因此將會豐富這方面的數學理論。

11302215.label: Realisation of objectives
11302215.value: The project aims to investigate of the behavior of rarefied plasma outside an obstacle under the influence of the self-induced electro-magnetic field governed by the Maxwell system. The problem has strong physical background and is challenging in mathematics. The feasibility of the proposed project is based on our previous works on the exterior problem study on the Boltzmann equation and also the recent works on the spectrum analysis for the Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system. Note that even though there are satisfactory mathematical theories in the macroscopic level, such as in fluid dynamics, there are very few results on the exterior problem in the mesoscopic level. For example, there are important works and discussions on the subsonic, supersonic and transonic flows by Bers, Courant-Friedrichs, Mowawetz, Finn-Gilbarg, Gilbarg-Shiffman, Dong, etc. However, for kinetic equations, with the pioneer contributions made by Hilbert and the Girttingen school, Chapman and Enskog, Grad, Kogan and Maslova. And for the perturbation of an equilibrium, Ukai-Asano gave a rigorous but technical analysis on the existence and stability for the exterior problem when the far field Mach number is sufficiently small. For the interior and exterior problems for kinetic equations, the typical examples of the kinetic equations under consideration are the Boltzmann equation and the Landau equation. We consider the problem in the mesoscopic level which lies between the macroscopic and miscroscopic descriptions. In this regard, there is no sufficient mathematical theories have been established. Among the works in this direction on the Boltzmann equation, there is a series of important contributions made by Maslova's group where many analytic techniques were developed for treating the boundary value problems. For the exterior problem itself, the work by Ukai-Asano on the existence and stability when the obstacle is convex and the Mach number of the far field is small, requires a detailed and technical analysis on the spectrum of the corresponding linearized operator and the compactness of some reduced operators when the boundary condition is assumed to be in some integral forms. For more general boundary conditions, the analysis of Ukai-Asano was improved in our recent work by crucially using the velocity averaging argument. And there are some works on the interior problem for the Boltzmann equation where a uniform Maxwellian is preserved by the boundary condition. For example, the strong large data L1 convergence under uniform diffuse Maxwellian boundary conditions, the stability of perturbative Couette-Taylor flow with different boundary temperatures on a cylinder, were studied by Arkeryd-Nouri and Arkeryd-Maslova. Moreover, the Rayleigh-Benard problem with external force field was also discussed by Arkeryd and Sone, etc. Guiraud also considered solutions near an absolute Maxwellian for interior and exterior problems. The major outcome of the research on this project consists of the five aspects and the research results were written in five research papers that have been published or accepted by international referred journals. Firstly, we establish the global existence of perturbative classical solutions around a global Maxwellian to the Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system with the whole range of soft potentials by overcoming the difficulties due to the complex structure of the system, in particular, the degenerate dissipation at large velocity, the velocity-growth of the nonlinear term induced by the Lorentz force, and the regularity-loss of the electromagnetic fields. And then we investigate the nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves and rarefaction wave for the bipolar Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (VPB) system. To this end, we first set up a new micro-macro decomposition around the local Maxwellian related to the bipolar VPB system and give a unified framework to study the nonlinear stability of the basic wave patterns to the system. Then, as an application of this new decomposition, the time-asymptotic stability of the two typical nonlinear wave patterns, viscous shock waves and rarefaction wave, are proved for the 1D bipolar Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system. Note that there is no zero macroscopic mass condition on the initial perturbations for the stability of superposition of two viscous shock waves in the first and third characteristic fields by introducing suitable shifts and some diffusion waves. And these are the first results concerned with the nonlinear stability of wave patterns for Boltzmann equation coupled with additional (electric) forces, which together with spectral analysis obtained by Li-Yang-Zhong in our previous work sheds some light on the understanding the complicated dynamic behaviors around the wave patterns in the transportation of charged particles under the binary collisions, mutual interactions, and the effect of the electrostatic potential forces. We also made progress on the global well-posedness of the Boltzmann equation with initial data of large amplitude has remained a long-standing open problem. By developing a new approach, we prove the global existence and uniqueness of mild solutions to the Boltzmann equation in the whole space or torus for a class of initial data with bounded velocity-weighted norm under some smallness condition on L1 norm as well as defect mass, energy and entropy so that the initial data allow large amplitude oscillations. Both the hard and soft potentials with angular cut-off are considered, and the large time behavior of solutions is also studied. Furthermore, we develop a linear theory on a flow under the effect of self-induced electric field past an obstacle governed by the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann equation. The bulk velocity at infinity acts like a driving force on the flow so that some non-trivial stationary solution profile exists. Similar to Ukai-Asano's work on the exterior problem for the Boltzmann equation, the spectrum of the linear operator is used through an approach in the spirit of the limiting absorption in scattering theory. However, to take care of the electric potential that satisfies the coupled Poisson equation, a new decomposition of the solution operator is needed to show the compactness. Finally, the Green's functions and the space-time pointwise behavior of solutions to both the unipolar Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (VPB) system for one carrier and the bipolar Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (bVPB) system for two carriers are studied. Due to the effect of electrostatic potential, it is shown that both the Green's function and the electric field to the unipolar VPB system only admit of a diffusive wave structure whose amplitude decays at an algebraic rate in some space-time region, and exponentially otherwise. This is different from the Botlzmann equation for which the propagation of both the diffusion wave and Huygen's wave are observed in the region of sound wave shown in the works by Liu-Yu. However, due to the combined effects of the electrostatic potential force and the mutual interaction between different charged particles, the Green's function to the bipolar VPB system admits of not only the diffusion wave but also Huygen's wave propagation, in particular, the electric field behaves like a diffusive wave with amplitude decaying exponentially in time. The result justifies the effect of electrostatic potential force and the mutual interaction between two carriers on the transportation of charged particles.

11302215.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302215.value: We first work on the Vlasov-Maxwell Boltzmann and Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann systems about their large time behavior, stability of wave patterns and Green’s functions. These results can be used for the study on the exterior problems for these two systems. The research output was written in five papers with one published in Communications in Mathematical Physics, three in Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis and one in SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis. Some details of the research results are given as follows. How to establish the global existence of perturbative classical solutions around a global Maxwellian to the Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system with the whole range of soft potentials has been an open problem. This is mainly due to the complex structure of the system, in particular, the degenerate dissipation at large velocity, the velocity-growth of the nonlinear term induced by the Lorentz force, and the regularity-loss of the electromagnetic fields. The first paper aims to solve this problem in the whole space provided that initial perturbation has sufficient regularity and velocity-integrability. The main purpose of the second paper is to investigate the nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves and rarefaction wave for the bipolar Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (VPB) system. To this end, we first set up a new micro-macro decomposition around the local Maxwellian related to the bipolar VPB system and give a unified framework to study the nonlinear stability of the basic wave patterns to the system. In third paper, we prove the global existence and uniqueness of mild solutions to the Boltzmann equation in the whole space or torus for a class of initial data with bounded velocity-weighted norm to allow large amplitude oscillations. The fourth paper presents a linear theory on a flow under the effect of self-induced electric field past an obstacle governed by the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann equation. The bulk velocity at infinity acts like a driving force on the flow so that some non-trivial stationary solution profile exists. To take care of the electric potential that satisfies the coupled Poisson equation, a new decomposition of the solution operator is needed to show the compactness. In the fifth paper, the Green's functions and the space-time pointwise behavior of solutions to both the unipolar Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (VPB) system for one carrier and the bipolar Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (bVPB) system for two carriers are studied. The result justifies the effect of electrostatic potential force and the mutual interaction between two carriers on the transportation of charged particles.

11302215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302215.value: How to describe the motion of rarefied gas outside an obstacle with influence of external or self-induced force in mathematics is challenging because of the complexity of the system involved and the lack of existing mathematical theories and analytic techniques. The results of this project give some answer to this question and I believe that there are much more unsolved problems are worthy of being considered in this direction, such as the formation of wave patterns, in particular shock fronts, the hydrodynamic limits and the detailed description of the solution behaviors.

11302215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302215.value: The project aims to investigate of the behavior of rarefied plasma outside an obstacle under the influence of the self-induced electro-magnetic field governed by the Maxwell system. The problem has strong physical background and is challenging in mathematics. The feasibility of the proposed project is based on our previous works on the exterior problem study on the Boltzmann equation and also the recent works on the spectrum analysis for the Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system. Note that even though there are satisfactory mathematical theories in the macroscopic level, such as in fluid dynamics, there are very few results on the exterior problem in the mesoscopic level. In this project, we successfully give some mathematical description of the solutions to these complex systems, such as stability of wave patterns, pointwise estimates based on Green’s function, and the first linear theory to the exterior problem for Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system. We believe the results obtained can be useful for study on the mathematical problems in this direction.

11302415.label: Project Objectives
11302415.value: Construct a phosphopeptide array to profile the substrate specificity of PTPs related to Parkinson’s disease (PD). Through the study, we will gain a better understanding of the mechanism by which these PTPs recognize their substrates. Validate the peptide hits through microplate dephosphorylation assays and verify the biological relevance through affinity pull-down assays. Design and synthesize fluorescent probes to detect specific PTP activity. Apply the probes to monitor target PTP’s activity in living cells. Construct protein-based probes to identify the endogenous PTPs that dephosphorylate α-synuclein. The identified PTP will shed new light on the roles of PTPs in Parkinson’s disease.

11302415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302415.value: 酪氨酸的磷酸化在许多重要的生物进程中起到调控作用，如基因激活、细胞增殖和细胞分化。细胞内的磷酸化水平由蛋白激酶与磷酸酶严格调控，研究表明，磷酸酶在体内发挥着许多重要的生物功能，磷酸酶功能失常将导致许多重要疾病的发生。迄今为止，许多磷酸酶已被鉴定为潜在的药物靶标。 目前科研领域主要集中在研究与癌症相关的磷酸酶，与脑神经疾病相关的磷酸酶的研究则比较稀少。此项研究致力于开发磷酸化多肽芯片，并应用该芯片研究与帕金森病相关的磷酸酶。我们将合成一个磷酸化多肽文库，将它们特异性地固定在经化学修饰的玻璃表面上，由此得到的多肽芯片将用于系统地研究给定磷酸酶的底物选择性。这项研究将增进我们对这些磷酸酶在帕金森病中生物功能的理解，也将有助于发展和设计磷酸酶的有效抑制剂。此外，芯片的检测结果将为荧光探针的设计提供关键信息，我们将在此基础上设计荧光探针并用于研究磷酸酶在活细胞内的生物活性。 帕金森病的形成涉及了α-突触核蛋白的聚集并构成具有细胞毒性的纤维。最近研究表明，α-突触核蛋白中125位点酪氨酸的磷酸化可抑制具细胞毒性纤维的形成，从而降低神经毒性。迄今为止，负责去磷酸化这一位点的酶仍然未知，我们将用表达蛋白连接技术合成基于蛋白的荧光探针，然后用该探针捕获内源性的磷酸酶，该实验结果将有助于揭示磷酸酶在帕金森病中新的生物功能。 我们实验团队在多肽芯片、蛋白质组学、分子生物学及脑神经科学方面拥有丰富经验，我们相信该项研究将有助于推动研究酪氨酸磷酸酶在帕金森病中新的生物机制。

11302415.label: Realisation of objectives
11302415.value: All the objectives of the proposal have been achieved through our study. A phosphor peptide library was synthesized and used to investigate the substrate specificity of various protein tyrosine phosphatases (PTPs) including PTP1B, SHP2 and VHR. Through detailed comparison study, we have gained a better understanding how these PTPs recognize their substrate. For the selected peptide substrates with high dephosphorylation activity, we also performed time-dependent malachite green phosphate assay to study their kinetic activity against the corresponding phosphatase. Furthermore, two fluorescent probes were designed and synthesized to detect the enzymatic activity of alkaline phosphatase, which has been shown to dephosphorylate α-synuclein in vitro. Cell imaging study showed that the probes were capable of real-time monitoring the ALP phosphatase activity in living cells. The probes might provide insight into the roles of ALP phosphatase in Parkinson’s disease.

11302415.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302415.value: Through this work, we have developed a number of useful chemical tools that can help drive the advancement of the protein tyrosine phosphatase field. With our screening strategy, we have identified a number of new peptides that interact with SHP2 phosphatase. The upregulation of SHP2 is found in patients with neurodegenerative diseases. The new peptide substrates identified for SHP2 phosphatase will provide useful information to design potent inhibitors. The SHP2 inhibitors might be developed into drugs for treating neurodegenerative diseases. Furthermore, the two probes developed for detecting alkaline phosphatase may provide useful tools for diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease. A total of 6 scientific papers have been published during the project period. I presented the research work in a number of international conferences. In addition, 3 Ph.D. students were trained during the implementation of the project.

11302415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302415.value: We are conducting further development of the research. We seek to generate SHP2 inhibitors and examine whether they will be useful to alleviate the symptoms of Parkinson’s disease.

11302415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302415.value: A new peptide-based technology has been developed to systematically investigate the substrate specificity of various protein tyrosine phosphatases. The research will advance our understanding of the roles of phosphatases in neurodegenerative diseases.

11302515.label: Project Objectives
11302515.value: Materials fabrication and mechanism study We will fabricate hierarchical metal foams of extraordinarily high specific surface area. Particularly, we will explore the strategy that combines the multi-component electrodeposition and dealloying for fabricating the proposed high surface area metal foams. The formation mechanism of the novel metal foams will be investigated. Application study The fabricated novel hierarchical metal foams of large specific surface area will be studied as supporting frameworks/charge collectors for a number of applications, such as photocatalysts, SERS substrates, and supercapacitor electrodes. The structures and properties of the metal foams will be adjusted and optimized to target the specific applications. Training/Education Another important objective of this work is to provide unique training and educational opportunities for students and post docs. This work will provide them with a wide range of fundamental knowledge and practical skills that will benefit their future development in both academia and industry. The educational strength of this research lies in its multi-disciplinary nature that bridges fundamental investigation in materials electrochemistry and applied research in practical device fabrication and tests. The multi-faceted research plan has tasks at various levels to include undergraduate students, graduate students, and postdoctoral researchers.

11302515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302515.value: Featuring high thermal and electrical conductivities, light weight, attractive mechanical properties and low cost, 3D bulk metal foams hold great promise for various applications. However, the low surface area of current metal foams has largely limited their performance and applications, e.g., as supporting frameworks/charge collectors for electrode materials and photocatalysts. On the other hand, there is a lack of efficient and economical methods to effectively increase the surface area of metal foams. Here we propose a facile method for greatly increasing the surface area of metal foams using low-cost electrochemical treatments (e.g., repetitively alternated electrodeposition and dealloying). Taking Cu foams as an example, high surface area Cu foams will be fabricated using this convenient electrochemical method in a one-pot one-step manner. The roughness or specific surface area of the metal foams will be easily tunable by varying the electrochemical parameters, e.g., the cycle numbers. As charge collectors/supporting substrates, the advanced Cu foams will enable improved performance for various applications, such as surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), biosensing, photocatalysis, and supercapacitors. 3D塊體金屬泡沫以其優良的導電導熱與機械性能、低密度、低成本具有巨大潛力，然而，較低的比表面積大大局限了其功能及應用，尤其在作為電活性或光催化物質的集流體/網絡支架等方面。而現有科技缺乏有效且經濟的技術來提高金屬泡沫的比表面積。這裡我們提出一種價廉、簡便的電化學方法（如使用重複電鍍及其去合金處理）來大幅提高金屬泡沫的比表面積。以泡沫銅為例，高比表面積的泡沫銅可一鍋一步簡便制得，而其表面積及粗糙度可通過電化學參數（如循環次數）來調整。這些高比表面積泡沫銅將會在如表面增強拉曼、生物傳感、光催化、超電容等多種應用領域成就大幅提升的性能。

11302515.label: Realisation of objectives
11302515.value: Using the proposed strategy that combines the multi-component electrodeposition and dealloying, we have successfully fabricated hierarchical metal structure of extraordinarily high specific surface area on Cu- Au- or Ag- based foams, wires, and needles. We have systematically studied the key parameters for fabricating the proposed metal structures and their formation mechanism. By systematically investigation of the key parameters, the optimized electrochemical treatments were as follows: conducted at room temperature using a computer controlled potentiostat, with the metal material to be treated serving as the working electrode, a platinum ring and saturated calomel electrode used as the counter and reference electrode, respectively. A voltage square-wave was applied which periodically modulated between two extreme values for n cycles: a cathodic voltage of V1 for a time duration of t1 for electrodepositing the nano-patches, and an anodic voltage of V2 for a time duration of t2 for selectively etching the treated metal substrate. The etched metals were rinsed with deionized (DI) water and dried under a stream of N2. The precipitates from the reaction electrolyte were collected by repetitively centrifugation followed by water washing for several times. The treated metal substrates displayed hierarchical nanoporous features of greatly enhanced surface areas. The structural features can be easily controlled by tuning the electrolyte recipes and the electrochemical parameters. For example, Au wires of dramatically different surface morphologies of wide-ranging pore size, etching depth, and surface roughness can be achieved by keeping the same electrodeposition voltage, dealloying voltage and cycle number, but in different electrolyte. By studying the different metal systems, the roughening mechanism was confirmed to be generic, rising from a repetitive etching process with in-situ self-masking. First, micro-isles of AB alloy are electrodeposited onto the B ligaments. Second, electrochemical dealloying takes place to selectively etching away the B components from the AB isles and the exposed surface of the B ligaments. The A components in the micro-isles initially serve as micro-masks to shield the underneath B ligaments from etching, and are then detached from the B ligaments due to the under-cutting effect, leaving roughened B ligaments ready for the next electrodeposition/dealloying cycle. The fabricated novel hierarchical metal nanostructures have been studied as supporting frameworks/charge collectors for a number of applications.The structures and properties of the metal nanostructures have been adjusted and optimized to target the specific applications. In particular, they displayed greatly improved performance for SERS substrates, photocatalysis, Plasmon-mediated chemical reactions (PMCRs), and supercapacitor electrodes. For example, the roughened Au wires show great potential as SERS substrates by detecting Rhodamine B (Rb) of extremely low concentration (10-12 M). The two-dimensional point-by-point SERS mapping images clearly show that the roughened Au wire enabled very strong and uniform signal of SERS enhancement. A line mapping of the roughened Au wire showed that over 9% points delivered strong Rb signals. Rb of even lower 10-14 M was detectable, indicating the extremely high SERS sensitivity of the treated Au wires. Furthermore, the roughened Au wire shows very high stability, delivering clear Raman spectra of Rb (10-12 M) after two months storage. It also provide quick and sensitive detection of the different components in vegetable oils, particularly, the trace amount (0.001 % of 2 µl) of peanut ingredients which many people are severely allergic to. For Cu foams treated in the Pt-Cu electrolyte, it was clearly seen that the roughened Cu foam shows much higher photodegradation rate (over 10 times faster) for depolluting methylene blue than the untreated foam. Another key application identified in this project is on the plasmon-mediated chemical reactions (PMCRs). Plasmon relaxation of noble metal nanostructures induce multiple physical processes, such as generating hot carriers and heating the crystal lattice, which can be utilized to improve the rate, selectivity, or yield of chemical reactions at metal surface. In the past decades, plasmon-mediated chemical reactions (PMCRs) are intensively investigated for converting sunlight into useful fuels and chemicals. However, a key question under vigorous debate in this field is on how to disentangle and rank the contributions from hot carrier and photothermal heating. Using the nano-roughened Ag needles as the plasmonic electrode, we have quantitatively unraveled the thermal and “nonthermal” (hot carriers) effects in plasmon-mediated electrochemistry by directly recording their photoelectrochemical behaviors, clearly showing the dominant role of the thermal effect (e.g., it contributed as much as 99% and 83% at -0.31 and -0.70 V, respectively). Furthermore, a new plasmon-induced photoelectric converting mechanism that results in varied surface potential and photocurrent, is discovered on the fabricated novel Ag electrode, which has not been reported on plasmonic Au electrodes in previous studies. One important objective of this work is on education. In this regard, this project has involved undergraduate students, graduate students, and postdoctoral researchers at researches of various levels, offering training on scientific research and a wide range of fundamental knowledge and practical skills that will benefit their future development in both academia and industry. The research work on this project carried out by several FYP students, MSc students, PhD students and postdoc researchers have been included in their dissertations or degree theses, or publications.

11302515.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302515.value: Experimental parameters have been established to fabricate hierarchical metal structures by electrochemical deposition and dealloying techniques. We have successfully fabricated the proposed hierarchical metal structures of high specific surface area on Cu foams, Ag needles, and Au wires. Among them, as reported in the last reporting period study, Cu-Ni systems on Cu foams enabled greatly improved SERS and supercapacitor performance. Regarding other metal systems, we have developed a convenient electrochemical method for effectively nano-roughening commercial Au wires using an electrolyte containing Ag ions, whose surface morphology can be easily controlled by adjusting the electrochemical parameters. The nanoporous byproducts porous silver particles featuring an extraordinarily large surface area. The roughened Au wire shows remarkable SERS performances which delivered uniform signals for detecting Rodamine B dyes of extremely low concentration at 10-12 M, with a detection limit as low as 10-14 M. We also demonstrated that this method not only work on Cu-Ni and Au-Ag system but also worked on Pt-Cu system which produced Pt-decorated nanoroughened Cu foams and nanoporous Pt particles. The roughened Cu foams displayed great promise for greatly improved photocatalytic efficiencies and Raman enhancement. Another important finding based on the nanoroughened Ag needle-based plasmonic electrode is on the plasmon-mediated chemical reactions (PMCRs). A key question under vigorous debate in the field of PMCRs is on how to disentangle and rank the contributions from hot carrier and photothermal heating. Using the nanoetched Ag needles fabricated using the convenient electrochemical method as a novel type of plasmonic electrode, the thermal and non-thermal contributions in PMCRs are quantitatively measured. The dominant role of photothermal effect over hot charge carriers is discovered by investigating the slow and rapid current responses of the Ag electrode in PMCRs. In addition, the plasmoelectric surface potential, a newly discovered plasmon-induced photoelectric converting mechanism, has also been identified to contribute to the rapid current responses, which is absent in previous studies on plasmonic Au electrode. It is further revealed that the contributions of these effects to the overall photocurrent generation are tunable by controlling the applied potential or light intensity, opening a new route to optimal photocatalysis or photothermal performances. In conclusion, this convenient, low-cost and scalable electrochemical method developed in this project is highly attractive for generating a range of metallic nanostructures, leading great improvement and important findings for various applications.

11302515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302515.value: The electrochemical method and fabrication strategy studied here is in principle universal for all types of metal structures (foams, meshes, wires, sheets, etc.) and can be applicable to many different types of metals, such as Cu, Ag, Au, Fe, Ni, and Co, for improving their performance in wide-ranging applications. The nano-etching approach in this project is convenient, low-cost and compatible with large-scale manufacture, opening a new route to surface nano-alloying and nano-roughening, holding great promise for wide-ranging applications such as filtering, sensing, SERS, charge storage, photocatalysis, and electrocatalysis.

11302515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302515.value: We have developed a convenient electrochemical method for effectively roughening metal structures and thus producing a novel kind of hierarchically porous metal frameworks whose surface morphology can be easily controlled by adjusting the electrochemical parameters. Unlike conventional "additive" methods that depend on depositing materials onto the substrate where the adhesion/bonding of the coating materials can be a challenge for maintaining the structural integrity and stability, the electrochemical method reported here is essentially to roughen the material by gradually "carving" its surface. Because the etching takes place by carving the treated metal gradually inwards, the nanoporous surface layer produced is naturally a part of the parent metal material, ensuring a good bonding with the parent substrate. Furthermore, compared with the conventional dealloy method, this approach does not require an alloy system as the starting material, readily applicable to common commercial products made of pure metals (e.g., Au wires or foils). The in situ self-masking strategy completely eliminates the undesired “self-coarsening” effect that is encountered in the conventional dealloy method. The convenient, low-cost and scalable method studied in this project have demonstrated great promises for expanding and improving the various applications of metal foams, in particularly as SERS substrates and supercapacitor electrode materials.

11302615.label: Project Objectives
11302615.value: A model-free variable selection method will be developed, which assumes no distributional model, admits general predictor effects, allows for efficient computation, and attains desirable theoretical properties. The asymptotic estimation and selection consistencies will be established and numeric experiments will be conducted to support its effectiveness against the existing methods in literature. An efficient coordinate descent algorithm will be developed to tackle the large-scale optimization task. The computational cost shall be substantially reduced without sacrificing any accuracy. The algorithm will be adapted to parallel computing nodes to further reduce the computational cost and to handle large-scale real dataset with size up to O(10^7). The proposed method will be extended to scenarios with discrete responses or ultra-high dimensional variables. The extended methods shall deliver superior selection performance and can handle variables with diverging size. The proposed variable selection method will be implemented and disseminated in a publicly available R package.
