11302615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302615.value: 變量選擇在過去二十年吸引了巨大的興趣。它擁有廣泛的應用，包括計算生物學，信息壓縮，文本挖掘，和社交網絡建模。這些應用往往包含大量的變量，從而變量選擇變的更加重要，因為一般認為只有少量的變量是對分析目標真正有用的，而剩下的大多數只是噪聲。本研究項目致力於發展新的不依賴於模型的變量選擇的統計理論，方法，以及算法。它主要的想法是把變量選擇形式化成一個梯度學習的框架，並配以靈活的再生和希爾伯特空間。它不假設任何的分布模型，承認一般的自變量效果，允許有效的計算，並能取得滿意的理論性質。這是與現有變量選擇方法最大的不同，它們在很大程度上依賴於模型假設。我們將研究新方法在大樣本和有限樣本下的理論性質。除此之外，我們也將發展新的有效的算法和平台從而使大規模優化變的可行，它們將包含了高緯參數的估計，以及實時和在線的數據處理。

11302615.label: Realisation of objectives
11302615.value: In this project, the PI and his collaborators propose a novel model-free variable selection method, which requires no explicit model assumptions and allows for general variable effects. The method is based on the idea that a variable is truly informative with respect to the regression function if the gradient of the regression function along the corresponding coordinate is substantially different from zero. As opposed to estimating the gradient functions, the proposed method focuses on identifying the truly informative variables corresponding to the non-zero gradient functions. To attain the sparsity in the estimated gradients, we consider a learning algorithm generated by a coefficient-based regularization scheme, and a group Lasso penalty is enforced on the coefficients so that the proposed method can conduct gradient learning and variable selection. Specifically, the proposed variable selection method is formulated in a regularization form that consists of a pairwise loss function for estimating the gradient functions and a group Lasso penalty. One of the main features of the proposed variable selection method is that it does not require any explicit model assumption and detect informative variables with various effects on the regression function. This is a major advantage over most existing model-based variable selection methods which need to pre-specify a working model. Another interesting feature of the proposed method is the use of coefficient-based representation in estimating the gradient function. It follows directly from the representor theorem in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, and turns out to greatly facilitate variable selection in the gradient learning framework. With the coefficient-based representation, the group Lasso penalty can be naturally enforced on all the coefficients associated with the same variable. More importantly, the asymptotic estimation and selection consistencies of the proposed method are established, showing that it recovers the truly informative variables with probability tending to one, and estimates the true gradient function at a fast convergence rate. The proposed method is also extended to a more general scenario where the truly informative variable is defined as those which are conditional dependent with the response given all other variables. The conditional dependence are characterized through composite quantile regressions functions to fully exploit the underlying distribution. Thus the proposed method is formulated as a gradient learning framework associated with the composite quantile functions on a flexible reproducing kernel Hilbert space. It also equips the gradient learning framework with a group lasso penalty, that can be viewed as an extension of the classical finite-dimensional Lasso penalty in a functional space. The proposed method aims to finding variables that may contribute to not only the conditional mean or quantile function, but the conditional distribution of the response. Thus the identified non-informative variables by the proposed method can be regarded as independent of the response given other variables. Asymptotic variable selection consistency is obtained without assuming any explicit model, a contrast to most existing theoretical results based on model assumptions. Both projects lead to large-scale optimization tasks, due to the fact that the functionals in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space can have a finite-dimensional representation due to the representor theorem. We develop scalable optimization algorithms to tackle the computational challenges. Specifically, a block-wise coordinate descent algorithm is developed for the first project, and an efficient computational algorithm combining the Majorization-Minimization algorithm and the proximal gradient descent algorithm are developed, respectively. Both computational algorithms are implemented in Python, and available upon request. As Dr. Xin HE is busy starting his first tenure-track job at SUFE in the past year, we plan to wrap up all the implementations in both Python and R packages for dissemination in the coming year.

11302615.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302615.value: The major findings of this project is three-folds. First, the PI and this collaborators developed a novel model-free variable selection method (Part C Output 1), which is based on the key idea that a variable is truly informative with respect to the regression function if the gradient of the regression function along the corresponding coordinate is substantially different from zero. The proposed variable selection method is formulated in a classical gradient learning framework equipped with a flexible reproducing kernel Hilbert space. The developed method requires no explicit model assumptions and allows for general variable effects. It is in sharp contrast to the existing variable selection methods, and thus provides an important supplement to the literature on high-dimensional data analysis. Second, the proposed method is also extended to the high-dimensional additive quantile model (Part C Outputs 3 & 4), allowing for both dimension and sparsity to increase with sample size. A new sparsity-smoothness penalty over a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, which includes linear function and spline-based nonlinear function as special cases. The combination of sparsity and smoothness is crucial for the asymptotic theory as well as the computational efficiency. Oracle inequalities on excess risk of the proposed method are established under weaker conditions than most existing results. Third, this project also develops tools to bridge classical machine learning framework to modern unstructured data analysis (Part C Outputs 2 & 6). Particularly, after unstructured data is processed into a standard matrix format with truly informative variables, it can be well fit into the classical machine learning framework. The proposed model-free variable selection method plays an important roles in constructing the informative variables, which eventually lead to superior numerical performance and fast asymptotic convergence rates.

11302615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302615.value: Even though the developed method is attractive in methodology and theory, due to its generality and flexibility, its computational cost can be demanding when the number of noise variables becomes large. This difficulty arises from the fact that the developed method is based on the difference operator, which inevitably boost up the computational cost. A potential further development along this line of research is to consider a global smoothing technique in estimating the gradients functions. Dr. Xin HE and the PI are now working on this extension, by fully utilizing the desirable properties of reproducing kernel Hilbert space. The preliminary numerical experiments are very promising, and the required computational cost can be substantially reduced without any sacrifice of the selection accuracy. Another potential development is to extend the method from mean regression and quantile regression to a general framework of M-estimator. The methodological development is ready, but the asymptotic behavior of a general M-estimator in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space still requires further efforts. The PI also plans to admit another Ph.D. student to join the research team and complete the theoretical guarantees of these extensions.

11302615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302615.value: This proposed research project develops novel statistical theories, methods, and computing algorithms for model-free variable selection. All the objectives are achieved, and an efficient machine learning framework is developed, which is in sharp contrast to most model-dependent methods in literature. The research findings have a wide spectrum of applications in practice, ranging from identifying genes for human diseases to detecting significant driving factors for financial products. The proposed research not only provide a novel perspective of conducting variable selection, but also develop modeling tools to bridge the classical gradient learning framework to the cutting-edge high-dimensional data analysis. With the support of this project, the PI and his collaborators published 8 research articles on leading statistics and machine learning journals, and trained one Ph.D. student Dr. Xin HE, who is now tenure-track Assistant Professor at SUFE. More importantly, this project also opens up a few potential directions for future research on learning complex structure in large-scale data.

11302715.label: Project Objectives
11302715.value: Construction of a smooth path that leads to a perfect stationary point: Every stationary point of a polynomial mapping on a perturbed polytope with the perturbation of ε yields a ε-perfect stationary point. This property together with polynomial form of the mapping will be fully exploited in the construction of the path. For any point of the polytope, we will first introduce an extra variable in between zero and one to formulate an unconstrained optimization problem from an appropriate convex combination of a logarithmic barrier term and the linear objective function with the mapping of the point as its coefficients. This optimization problem deforms from a trivial optimization problem to the original optimization problem when the extra variable varies from one to zero. Then an application of the optimality condition and a fixed-point argument will lead to a system of polynomial equations, all the solutions of which form a semialgebraic set. When the extra variable is positive, the barrier term will enforce every solution of the corresponding optimization problem to stay in the interior of the perturbed polytope. For any given sufficiently small positive value of the extra variable, the corresponding coefficient of the barrier term satisfies that each solution of the system closely approximates some stationary point for the mapping on the perturbed polytope. To ensure the existence of a smooth path that leads to a perfect stationary point, a perturbation term will be subtracted and Mas-Colell’s, Sard’s and implicit function theorems will be applied. The key technical issues to be tackled are the convergence of the path to a perfect stationary point and finiteness of the path length. Development of an efficient predictor-corrector method for numerically following the smooth path: To numerically follow the smooth path to a perfect stationary point, we will first parameterize each point on the path with the corresponding arc-length. A system of differential equations will then be formulated to characterize the path. To solve the system, an efficient predictor-corrector method will be proposed by taking advantage of the special structures of the problem. The emphasis will be on numerical stability and efficiency. The sparsity of the problem will be exploited in the Cholesky factorization. When the value of the extra variable is sufficiently close to zero, the numerical instability may happen. To deal with this problem, we will utilize the preconditioning techniques. The key technical issue to be tackled is the estimation of the step length in the predictor step. Adaption of a simplicial path-following method for computing a perfect stationary point: When a continuous mapping on a polytope is highly nonlinear or nonsmooth, it could be more appropriate to adapt a simplicial method for computing stationary points. By introducing an extra variable in between zero and one and applying a retraction mapping, the stationary point problem can be reformulated as a homotopy system of equations or zeros of a homotopy mapping, which deforms from a trivial system to the original system as the extra variable varies from one to zero. When zero is a regular value of the homotopy mapping, a connected component of zero points of the homotopy mapping forms a piecewise smooth path that starts from the unique solution of the trivial system and leads to a perfect stationary point. To numerically follow this path, a triangulation of continuous refinement of grid sizes will be constructed to define a piecewise linear path and a simplicial method will be adapted for following the path. The key technical issue to be addressed is how to refine the grid size so that the piecewise linear path leads to a perfect stationary point. Numerical implementation of the interior-point path-following method: When the method is successfully developed in the proposed research, we will code it in both MATLAB and C++. To numerically compare the method with a sequential approach to the computation of a perfect stationary point, we will also code the state-of-the-art methods for computing stationary points of the mapping on a sequence of the perturbed polytopes. Extensive numerical experiments will be carried out. A software package of the method will be made available in both MATLAB and C++ for the applications. The key technical issue to be addressed is how to reduce the amount of computation.

11302715.label: Realisation of objectives
11302715.value: An extension of the notion of perfect equilibrium in Selten (1875) to a stationary point problem of a continuous mapping on a polytope leads to the concept of perfect stationary point. To find a perfect stationary point of a continuously differentiable mapping, we have constructed a perturbed polytope and defined an ε -perfect stationary point by exploiting the perturbed polytope. This construction brings us the fact that every stationary point of a continuous mapping on the perturbed polytope with the perturbation of ε yields an ε-perfect stationary point. Given any point in the perturbed polytope, we have introduced a continuously differentiable function of an extra variable ranging between zero and one to incorporate a logarithmic barrier term into the linear objective function with the mapping at the given point as its coefficient and formulated a logarithmic-barrier optimization. This optimization problem deforms from a trivial optimization problem to the original optimization problem when the extra variable varies from one to zero. Especially, the optimization becomes the perturbed stationary point problem before the extra variable vanishes. As a result of this desired property and the optimization problem, we have attained a continuously differentiable homotopy mapping and established the existence of a smooth path to a perfect stationary point. To numerically trace the smooth path to a perfect stationary point, we have first parameterized each point on the path using the corresponding arc-length. A system of differential equations is then formulated to characterize the path. To solve the system, an efficient predictor-corrector method has been adapted by taking advantage of the special structures of the problem such as sparseness and exploiting them in the Cholesky factorization and the estimation of the step-length. For highly nonlinear or nonsmooth continuous mappings on a polytope, a simplicial path-following method has been developed for computing a perfect stationary point. By introducing an extra variable in between zero and one and employing a retraction mapping, we have reformulated the stationary point problem as a system of equations or zeros of a homotopy mapping, which deforms from a trivial system to the original system as the extra variable varies from one to zero. When zero is a regular value of the homotopy mapping, a connected component of zero points of the homotopy mapping forms a piecewise smooth path that starts from the unique solution of the trivial system and leads to a perfect stationary point. To numerically follow this simplicial path, we have adapted a triangulation of continuous refinement of grid sizes for defining a piecewise linear path and utilized a simplicial method to follow the simplicial path to an approximate perfect stationary point. We have coded the methods in MATLAB/C++. Extensive numerical experiments have been carried out in the project. A software package of the methods has been made available in MATLAB/C++ for the applications.

11302715.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302715.value: Many problems in economics and engineering can be formulated as stationary point problems on polytopes. The computation of stationary points plays an important role in these applications. As a refinement of the notion of stationary point, the notion of perfect stationary point significantly reduces the ambiguity of stationary point. In order to apply the notion of perfect stationary point in practice, this project has developed an effective and efficient paradigm to compute a perfect stationary point. The major findings are as follows. Perfect equilibrium in strategic games is a special case of perfect stationary point and has many applications in economic modeling and analysis. To compute a perfect equilibrium in strategic games, this project has successfully established in [1] a smooth path, which starts from an arbitrary totally mixed strategy profile and leads to a perfect equilibrium. By numerically following the smooth path, we have attained a differentiable homotopy method to compute perfect equilibria. The basic idea in this project has been extended to the minimum concave-cost transportation problem and an effective and efficient heuristic method has been proposed in [2] to solve such an NP-hard problem. Calibrating classification probabilities with shape-restricted polynomial regression has many applications in statistical machine learning. Nonetheless, it remained a challenging problem. To tackle the problem, the idea of reformulating a problem as an equivalent optimization problem in [1] and [4] has been exploited in the development of an effective and efficient procedure to solve such a difficult problem in [3]. To compute a perfect stationary point of a continuously differentiable mapping on a polytope, we have reformulated in [4] the problem as zeros of a homotopy mapping and established the existence of a smooth path that leads to a perfect stationary point. The idea can be considered as a generalization of that in [1] and an exploitation of special structures of polytopes. The solution paradigm of the project has many applications in economics and engineering. Some significant applications have been achieved in [5-9]. An effective optimization procedure has been realized in [5] for surface modelling. A more flexible home health care scheduling and routing problem with joint patient and nursing staff selection and an integrated planning approach towards home health care have been derived in [6, 9]. An approximation algorithm for graph partitioning have been realized in [7]. To find a Markov perfect equilibrium for an important application, we have gained an effective and efficient path-following procedure in [8].

11302715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302715.value: Further development of the research will be on stochastic games, to which the concept of perfect stationary equilibrium will be formulated as a strict refinement of stationary equilibrium. The applications will be provided to show the effectiveness of this refinement. The idea in this project will definitely have an application in this further development.

11302715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302715.value: Stationary point problems/variational inequality problems have many applications in areas including economics, finance, game theory and mathematical optimization. Nevertheless, as pointed out in the literature, a variational inequality problem can have many stationary points and some of these stationary points may be undesirable or inconsistent with our intuitive notions about what should be the outcome of a variational inequality problem. To reduce this ambiguity and eliminate some of these counterintuitive stationary points, the notion of perfect equilibrium formulated in game theory has been extended to a variational inequality problem with respect to a continuous mapping and a polytope in the literature. This extension leads to the concept of perfect stationary point. The computation of perfect stationary point plays a fundamental role in its applications. The project has developed an interior-point path-following method to compute perfect stationary points of continuously differentiable mappings on polytopes. A smooth path leading to a perfect stationary point has been established in the project. An efficient predictor-corrector method has been adapted for numerically tracing the path. We have carried out extensive numerical experiments. The developments in this project have significantly advanced the computation of perfect stationary point and will certainly promote further applications of stationary point problems.

11302815.label: Realisation of objectives
11302815.value: Objective 1: To investigate the extent and degree of microplastics pollution on Hong Kong soft shores. Objective 2: To understand the significance of riverine input from the Pearl River in microplastics pollution in Hong Kong. We had collected sediment samples from 10 mudflats and 10 sandy beaches spanning from eastern to western waters. Results have shown that mudflats have 10 times more microplastics than sandy beaches. The western sites have more microplastics than the eastern sites, indicating that Pearl River was a major source of micropastics. Large inter-site differences in microplastic abundance, however, were observed. Local sources, therefore, were also important contributors of microplastics. Polyethylene, polypropylene and PET were the three most dominant types of microplastics found on the shores. The findings were published in “Environmental Pollution” (Lo et al. 2018). The spatial distribution, composition and source of hydrophobic organic compounds (HOCs) including polyaromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) and organchlorinated pesticides (OCPs) of the sedimentary microplastics (0.25–5 mm) in Hong Kong were investigated. The concentrations of ΣPAHs and ΣPCBs (13–1083 ng g–1) varied with both study sites and regions with higher concentrations obtained in the western waters, possibly due to the input from Pearl River. Significantly higher concentrations of OCPs on eastern shores highlighted fishing and aquaculture activities in South China Sea a potential major source of OCPs. Since most of the DDX existed as DDT, this suggested that there was a fresh input of DDT into the microplastics. The findings were published in “Chemosphere” (Lo et al. 2019). We investigated heavy metals (As, Zn, Cd, Ni, Fe, Mn, Cu) contamination of microplastics on six sandy beaches in Hong Kong. The median concentration of Fe was the highest and followed by Zn and Mn. Very low concentrations of Cu, Ni, As and Cd were measured. The western sites have significantly higher concentrations of Ni, Fe, Mn and Cu than the eastern sites, indicating that Pearl River was likely to be a major source of heavy metals on microplastics. The results were presented in the 9th International Conference on Marine Pollution and Ecotoxicology held in Hong Kong between 10 and 14 June 2019, and the manuscript was published in the international journal Marine Pollution Bulletin (Li et al., 2020a). Since distribution and abundance of microplastic undergoes temporal variations, we were interested to know how the weather condition such as typhoons affected microplastics on beaches. The effect of Super Typhoon Mangkhut on marine debris pollution was investigated on two pairs (exposed and protected) of beaches spanning from the eastern to western waters before and after the typhoon. For macro-debris, there was an 11.4-fold increase in the density after the typhoon, with plastic being the most dominant type among all beached debris. Likewise, higher mean microplastic abundances were found in the post-typhoon period. The depositional dynamics for both macro-debris and microplastic were site-specific due to factors such as wind direction and the associated storm surge, topography of the sites and proximity to urban areas. The findings were published in “Science of the Total Environment” (Lo et al. 2020). Objective 3: To compare the extent of microplastics ingestion in field populations of intertidal animals with different feeding modes. Objective 4: To characterize and quantify microplastics in sediments and the associated intertidal animals using various spectroscopic techniques This study investigated the occurrence of MPs in invertebrates collected on 18 mudflats and sandy beaches in Hong Kong and its relationships to biological taxon, feeding mode and habitat. In total 38 species of gastropods, bivalves and crabs were collected and the mean number of suspected microplastics measured. Around 26% of the suspected microplastics were confirmed to be synthetic polymers, including CP (cellophane), PET (polyethylene terephthalate), and PA (polyamide). Microplastic fibres were the most abundant type of MPs, followed by pellets. Significantly higher abundance of suspected microplastics was found in gastropods. Since MP abundance might vary with taxon, it is recommended to include different taxonomic groups in any ecological assessment of the impact of MPs. The findings were published in “Science of the Total Environment” (Xu et al. 2020a). Barnacles is another major group of filter feeders in coastal habitats. The occurrence of microplastics in four species of barnacles at 30 sites in Hong Kong water was investigated. The chemical composition of 152 pieces out of 606 potential microplastics was analyzed. Eight types of polymer were identified with cellophane being the most abundant. There was a positive correlation between MP abundance in Amphibalanus amphitrite and sediments, highlighting the potential of using barnacles as a bioindicator of microplastics. The results were presented in the 9th International Conference on Marine Pollution and Ecotoxicology held in Hong Kong between 10 and 14 June 2019, and the manuscript was published in "Marine Pollution Bulletin" (Xu et al., 2020b). The effect of microplastics was also investigated in another filter feeder bivalve, the Green-lipped mussel Perna viridis, in a field transplantation experiment. The mussels were transplanted to three sites in Sai Kung with different levels of human activities and bioaccumulation of microplastics was determined on Day 7, 19, 33 and 47 post transplantation. The samples in Pak Sha Wan retained the most amount of microplastic in their body. In all study areas, only microplastic fiber and film were found and fiber was the most abundance microplastic (around 90%). Cellophane, polyethylene terephthalate and polyamide were the major chemical forms of plastic in all study areas. Such spatial differences in microplastic abundance and composition might due to differences in human activity at different sites. We proposed to develop a method to identify chemical compositions of microplastics by dissolving them into a uniform film, and quantitatively analyzed by FTIR. Raw pellet (0.5 g, PP, PE or PS) was first dissolved in 5 mL acetone at 40°C. The mixture was evaporated to 1 mL and transferred onto a glass slide. The solvent was evaporated at room temperature and thin film of polymer was produced. The thin film was then characterised by FTIR. The results show that as long as the sample can be dissolved under mild condition (<40°C), this method could be useful. But the weaknesses of this method included 1) long sample handling time (~15 min per sample), 2) the signal is quite weak, and 3) at least 0.2-0.5 g microplastic is needed to generate a detectable signal, therefore, this method could only be applied on larger microplastics. Objective 5: To determine the effect of microplastics on the energy balance of filter feeders and the efficiency of depuration of the ingested microplastics. The effects of microplastic concentrations on the physiological responses of the filter feeder Atactodea striata were investigated. A. striata ingested microplastics and the clearance rate was reduced at high concentration of microplastics. Since the respiration rate and absorption efficiency remained unchanged in exposed A. striata, reduction in the clearance rate would reduce the energy intake. The results were presented in the 8th International Conference on Marine Pollution and Ecotoxicology held at the University of Hong Kong from 20 to 24 June, 2016 and the manuscript was published in "Marine Pollution Bulletin" (Xu et al., 2017).

The Pearl River was a major source of micropastics but local sources were also important contributors of microplastics. Polyethylene, polypropylene and PET were the three most dominant types of microplastics found. 2) Polyaromatic hydrocarbons and polychlorinated biphenyls were found on microplastics, possibly due to the input from Pearl River. For organchlorinated pesticides, fishing and aquaculture activities in South China Sea are potential sources of OCPs. 3) Among the heavy metals (As, Zn, Cd, Ni, Fe, Mn, Cu) found on microplastics on sandy beaches in Hong Kong, the concentration of Fe was the highest and followed by Zn and Mn. The Pearl River was likely to be a major source of heavy metals on microplastics. 4) There was an 11.4-fold increase in the macro-debris density on beaches after the typhoon. Higher microplastic abundances were also found in the post-typhoon period. Wind direction and the associated storm surge, topography of the sites and proximity to urban areas are factors responsible for the depositional dynamics for both macro-debris and microplastics. 5) Around 26% of the suspected microplastics found in marine invertebrates (gastropods, crabs, bivalves) on soft shores were confirmed to be synthetic polymers and most of them were fibres. More microplastics was found in gastropods. 6) Eight types of polymer were found in barnacles collected in Hong Kong waters. There was a positive correlation between MP abundance in Amphibalanus amphitrite and sediments, highlighting the potential of using barnacles as a bioindicator of microplastics. 7) Green-lipped mussels Perna viridis were transplanted to three sites in Sai Kung with different levels of human activities and bioaccumulation of microplastics was determined. Cellophane, polyethylene terephthalate and polyamide were the major chemical forms of plastic. Spatial differences in microplastic abundance and composition might due to differences in human activity at different sites. 8) A method was developed to identify chemical compositions of microplastics and quantify each type of polymer. Raw pellets of PP, PE and PS were dissolved into a uniform film, and quantitatively analyzed by FTIR. The results show that as long as the sample can be dissolved under mild condition (<40°C), this method could be useful for quantifying larger pieces of PP, PE or PS. 9) The clearance rate of the clam Atactodea striata was reduced after ingesting microplastics. Since the respiration rate and absorption efficiency remained unchanged, reduction in the clearance rate would reduce the energy intake.

11302815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302815.value: 1) Since hydrophobic organic pollutants and heavy metals were found on microplastics collected in Hong Kong waters, there is a need to identify the sources of these pollutants. I would suggest deploying virgin microplastics in different regions in Hong Kong and retrieved them in a period of time to study the accumulation of these pollutants for identification of hot spots of these pollutants. 2) Microplastics were found in various groups of shore invertebrates. The routes where microplastics were obtained by these organisms deserve further studies. For example, the significance of trophic transfer in the uptake of microplastics in higher trophic level organisms such as predators. 3) Since one barnacle species was found to be a potential bioindicator of microplastics, further studies should be focused on what types, sizes and forms of microplastics are best represented by this barnacle species.

11302815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302815.value: This is the first study that investigated the extent of microplastic pollution on mudflats and sandy beaches and in their associated animals in Hong Kong. The accumulation of pollutants including organic pollutants and heavy metals was also determined. The results provide clues to the major sources of microplastics in Hong Kong, potential hazards to shore animals, and the possibility of using bioindicators to monitor microplastic pollution.

11302915.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11302915.value: 关于非线性梯度流方程的线性化Galerkin有限元方法及分析

11302915.label: Project Objectives
11302915.value: In this project, we will study more efficient numerical methods for the nonlinear equations of gradient flow, particularly linearized type Galerkin finite element methods. Such methods only require the solution of a linear system at each time step. Efficient iterative algorithms for solving the linear system and some new linearized approaches will also be studied. Efficient preconditioning technique and multigrid methods may be our choices in this direction. Linearized methods have many advantages in computational complexity and implementation. However, analysis for linearized Galerkin FEMs is more challenging, compared with those implicitly nonlinear schemes since the latter may preserve some physical structure exactly and the former only preserves the structure approximately. Due to the gradient-dependent diffusion coefficient in the equation, the key issue to the analysis is the boundedness of numerical solution in $W^{1,infty}$-norm. In this project, we will establish unconditionally optimal error estimates with a temporal-spatial error splitting argument. By introducing an auxiliary iterated time-discrete (elliptic) system corresponding to the given fully discrete scheme and the physical model, the linearized fully discrete method can be viewed as a spatial FE approximation to the iterated elliptic system. The boundedness of numerical solution in $W^{1,infty}$-norm can be proved if we can show (i) the desired regularity of the iterated elliptic system and (ii) the $ tau$-independent error estimates of the FE approximation to the iterated elliptic system. In many physical models, the gradient-dependent diffusion coefficient is defined with a regularization parameter, which is usually small or zero in a part of the physical domain. The latter leads to the degeneracy of the nonlinear parabolic PDE. Numerical methods for the problem with small regularization and the problem with non-regularization are of high interest. Uniform analysis with respect to the regularization parameter for linearized numerical methods will be investigated. In this project, we will also apply proposed linearized Galerkin FEMs and theoretical analysis for some other physical problems, such as an compressible fluid flow in porous textile media with a gradient-dependent diffusion-dispersion tensor and a moving mesh method in which the artificial mesh movement is viewed as a gradient flow. Numerical analysis for the first model with the commonly-used Bear-Scheidegger diffusion-dispersion tensor is incomplete and numerical analysis for the second model is unknown.

11302915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302915.value: The equation of gradient flow is a diffusion type equation in which the diffusion coefficient is gradient-dependent. Applications of this equation can be found in many areas of engineering and science, such as compressible/incompressible flow in porous media, minimal surface/mean curvature flow, moving mesh methods and image denoising. Due to the strong nonlinearity and possible degeneracy of the equation, previous efforts mainly focused on implicit schemes and analyses still require strong restrictions on the time step. Such implicit schemes are not acceptable for the large scale computation in a long time period. The project is to develop efficient and stable Galerkin FEMs and establish optimal and unconditional error analysis. 梯度流体方程是带着梯度相关扩散系数的抛物方程。该类方程在工程及科领城中有着广泛的应用。例如可压及不可压多孔介质流，极小化曲面流，移动网格方法及图像处理。由于强的非线性及可能退化性，之前的数值研究主要集中在全隐格式建立及分析。这样全隐格式在实际计算中往往不可接受。该研究计划旨在发展新的有效的和稳定的有限元方法并提供无条件的误差分析。

11302915.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302915.value: 1. During the period of this project, we have studied the maximal Lp-regularity estimates for fully discrete Galerkin finite element solutions of parabolic equations with time-dependent Lipschitz continuous coefficients. Optimal-order error estimates of fully discrete finite element solutions in the norm of $l^p(L^q)$ are presented here. Analysis for the maximal Lp-regularity of fully discrete solutions is based on a perturbation technique with a duality argument and a more precise estimate of time-discrete solutions. For simplicity, here we focus our attention on the backward Euler scheme for the time discretization. Our techniques can be extended to the Crank–Nicolson and BDF methods once the R-boundedness can be proved. 2. The classical energy approach relies heavily on the strong regularity assumption of the diffusion coefficient, which may not be satisfied in many physical applications. Here we focused our attention on a general nonlinear parabolic equation (or system) in a convex polygon or polyhedron with a nonlinear and Lipschitz continuous diffusion coefficient. Based on the our analysis for linear problems, we further studied the maximal Lp-regularity estimates of semi-discrete Galerkin finite element solutions of nonlinear parabolic equations. With the proved discrete maximal Lp-regularity, we then establish an optimal Lp error estimate and an almost optimal $L-infty$ error estimate of the finite element solution for the nonlinear parabolic equation. 3. Numerical study of incompressible miscible flow in porous media has been investigated extensively in the last several decades. The problem is governed by a system of parabolic/elliptic equations with velocity (gradient of pressure)-dependent diffusion. Of particular interest in practical applications is the lowest-order Galerkin-mixed method, in which a linear Lagrange FE approximation is used for the concentration and the lowest-order Raviart-Thomas FE approximation is used for the velocity/pressure. The previous works only showed the first-order accuracy of the method in L2-norm in spatial direction, which however is not optimal and valid only under certain extra restrictions on both time step and spatial mesh. In this project, we provided new and optimal L2-norm error estimates of linearized Galerkin-mixed FEMs for all three components in a general case. Numerical results for both two and three-dimensional models are presented to confirm our theoretical analysis. More important is that our approach can be extended to the analysis of mixed FEMs for many strongly coupled systems to obtain optimal error estimates for all components. Numerical simulations of the proposed method were also done for some other nonlinear models.

11302915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302915.value: In this project, we mainly focused on unconditional convergence and optimal error estimates of commonly-used linearized Galerkin FEMs and mixed methods for a single nonlinear parabolic equation and a special nonlinear parabolic/elliptic system with gradient-dependent diffusion coefficients from incompressible miscible flow in porous media. Extension of our approach to many other nonlinear physical models is our future plan.

11302915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302915.value: In this project, we mainly focused on the linearized Galerkin and mixed methods for several types of strong nonlinear problems. Linearized methods have many advantages in computational complexity and implementation. However, analysis for linearized Galerkin FEMs is more challenging, compared with those implicitly nonlinear schemes since the latter may preserve some physical structure exactly and the former only preserves the structure approximately. The key issue to the analysis is the boundedness of numerical solution in a strong norm. In this project, we present the $Lp$-estimate of a general nonlinear model, with which we establish unconditionally optimal error estimates in terms of a temporal-spatial error splitting argument. Moreover, for a special incompressible miscible flow model with velocity-dependent diffusion, we studied a class of mixed methods and presented unconditionally optimal error estimates. Our approach can be extended to the analysis of mixed FEMs for many strongly coupled physical systems to obtain optimal error estimates for all components.

11303015.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11303015.value: 软材料板动力渐进模型及其应用

11303015.label: Project Objectives
11303015.value: Deriving the consistent dynamical asymptotic finite-strain plate equations in a differential version together with proper edge boundary conditions. The corresponding weak formulation will also be obtained together with the associated natural boundary conditions. The case of an incompressible material will also be considered. Obtaining the linearized plate equations for small strains. Solving several benchmark problems (for which the exact solutions are avlaible) to demonstrate the accuracy and superiority to some other existing small-strain plate theories. Using the plate model to study crease formation in a gel layer both analytically and numerically to provide a comprehensive understanding of this interesting instability phenomenon. Using the plate model to study wrinkled patterns in an elastic sheet with an aim of providing insights on the effect of finite-strains. Some other applications will be considered, like natural frequecy and critical buckling loads in pre-stressed soft material plates.

11303015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303015.value: 许多天然和人造材料是非常软的，如弹性体、聚合物、 聚合物凝胶和生物组织等。在力学上，这意味着这些软材料可以经受大弹性变形与有限应变。 由于这类材料在工程和科学上的广泛应用，近年来，对这类材料的变形行為进行建模已经吸引了越来越多研究者的兴趣, 其中一个经典的例子是轮胎以及另一个近代的例子是pH敏感凝胶制成的微透镜。并且，目前我们认识到机械力对确定生物对象的形态形成起到非常重要的作用（例如屈曲的黄瓜和褶皱的南瓜）。 此外，板是非常常见的结构（如植物叶，薄凝胶薄膜和生物膜等）。 因此，研究软材料板是非常有必要的。任何物体总是三维的， 然而对于一个板结构来说，其厚度比平面内的长度量级小得多，我们可以通过适当简化的二维板理论着手研究软材料板的变形行为，而不是采用数值和分析上都难以处理的三维理论。目前有许多可用的小应变板理论（如著名的冯·卡门板方程），而相对来说，有限应变变形（软质材料的特质）的板理论却非常少， 特别是尚未有一致的有限应变动力板理论。从数学建模的观点上，软材料的机械行为本构上可以通过应变（自由）能函数来描述。 本项目的其中一个目的是要为具有一般应变能函数的非线性材料获取一个一致的有限应变动力板理论。 为了验证这一新理论的正确性，线性化将用于获取相应的小应变板理论。 此外，该线性板模型将用来求解几个基准问题，得到的解将与精确解以及由其他一些众所周知的小应变板模型得到的解进行比较。 由于我们的板理论与三维构架的一致性，预计这些比较可以体现我们的板理论的优越性。该有限应变板理论的几个应用也将被考虑。其中一个是在实验和数值上被很多人研究过的聚合物凝胶层，其表面上形成的褶皱可以被很好地观察到。我们的目的是基于我们得出的渐近模型，对其进行分析和数值的研究，以了解导致褶皱形成的机制，并对一些关键的实验观察提供解释。 实际上，褶皱是一种广泛分布的现象，例如它也存在于我们的脑和皮肤中，希望我们的结果也能应用于这些方面。 另一个是弹性片的拉伸导致的起皱形态，它与生物组织和太阳帆等应用有关。 近几年来，已经有一些文献通过使用三种不同的板模型（其中有限应变的影响并没有充分考虑到）研究这个问题，我们的渐近模型也将用于研究这种起皱形态以及与其他三个板模型进行比较。关于小应变和大挠度，冯·卡门板理论已被用于研究许多问题，我们得到的有限应变动力板模型预计也可为软材料广泛应用。

11303015.label: Realisation of objectives
11303015.value: Objective 1 is completely achieved. Starting from the three-dimensional field equations for a compressible hyperelastic material and by a series expansion about the bottom surface, we deduce a vector dynamic plate equation with three unknowns, which exhibits the local momentum-balance structure. By performing integrations by parts, we obtain a weak formulation for the dynamic plate equations, from which the suitable boundary conditions are proposed. In a subsequent work, we further impose the incompressibility constraint and derive a plate theory for incompressible materials. The dynamic plate equations are further linearized and the vibration of a rectangular plate is considered and comparisons with the 3D exact solutions confirm the reliability of the linearized plate theory. So, objective 2 is realized. We address objective 3 in another piece of work by developing a consistent finite-strain plate theory for growth-induced large deformations. The three-dimensional (3D) governing system of the plate model is formulated through the variational approach, which is composed of the mechanical equilibrium equation and the constraint equation of incompressibility. Then, series expansions of the unknown functions in terms of the thickness variable are adopted. By using the 3D equilibrium equations and the surface boundary conditions, recursion relations for the expansion coefficients are successfully established. As a result, a 2D vector plate equation with three unknowns is obtained and the associated edge boundary conditions are proposed. It can be verified that the plate equation ensures the required asymptotic order for all the terms in the variations of the total energy functional. The weak formulation of the plate equation has also been derived for future numerical calculations. As applications of the plate theory, two examples regarding the growth-induced deformations and instabilities in thin hyperelastic plates are studied. Some analytical results are obtained in these examples, which can be used to describe the large deformations and reveal the bifurcation properties of the thin plates. Objectives 4 and 5 are addressed in several pieces of works. A uniformly-valid plate theory, independent of the magnitudes of applied loads, is derived based on the two-dimensional plate theory obtained from series expansions about the bottom surface of a plate. For five different magnitudes of surface loads, it is shown by using asymptotic expansions that this unified plate theory recovers five well-known plate models in the literature to leading-order. This demonstrates its uniform validity. More generally, it provides a uniformly-valid plate model provided that two asymptotic conditions are satisfied, which can be checked as a posteriori. The weak formulation of the uniformly-valid plate equations is furnished, which can be used for finite element implementation. Another work studies the planar deformations of a beam composed of a linearly elastic material. Starting from the field equations for the plane-stress problem and adopting a series expansion for the displacement vector about the bottom surface, we deduce the beam equations with two unknowns in a consistent manner. The success relies on using the field equations together with the bottom traction conditions to establish the exact recursion relations, such that all quantities can be represented in terms of the two leading expansion coefficients of the displacements. Another feature is that the remainders of the series can be carried over to the beam equations. Then, based on the general solutions and the error terms of the beam equations, pointwise error estimates for displacement and stress fields are rigorously established. Three benchmark problems are considered, for which the two-dimensional exact solutions are available. It is shown that this new beam theory recovers the exact solutions for these problems. Two cases with boundary layer effects are also discussed. In a different work, we present a general finite-strain shell theory, which is consistent with the principle of stationary three-dimensional (3-D) potential energy. Based on 3-D nonlinear elasticity and by a series expansion about the bottom surface, we deduce a vector shell equation with three unknowns, which preserves the local force-balance structure. The key in developing this consistent theory lies in deriving exact recursion relations for the high-order expansion coefficients from the 3-D system. Appropriate 2-D boundary conditions and associated 2-D weak formulations are also proposed, including various practical cases on the edge. Then, to demonstrate its validity, axisymmetric deformations of spherical and circular cylindrical shells are investigated, and comparisons with the exact solutions are made. It is found that the present shell theory produces second-order correct results for the general dead-load case and internally pressurized case. The advantages of the present shell theory include consistency, high accuracy, incorporating both stretching and bending effects, no involvement of higher-order stress resultants and its applicability to general loadings. We also take the opportunity to use the methodology developed in this project to study some phase-transition problems. In one paper, the stress-induced phase transitions in a shape memory alloy (SMA) tube under torsion and pre-twisted tension are studied analytically. A constitutive model with the specfic forms of Helmholtz free energy and mechanical dissipation rate is employed to formulate the governing system. Exact solution of the tube under pure torsion is first derived and the shear stress-shear strain response is determined, which reveals the hardening effect. For the pre-twisted tube under uniaxial tension, the one-dimensional asymptotic tensile stress-tensile strain relations for the austenite, the phase transitions and the martensite regions are derived by using the asymptotic expansion method. By properly denfing an elastic energy potential, the present system can be viewed as an elastic problem, which can be related to the problem of Ericksen's bar. The analytical formulas for the nucleation and propagation stresses in terms of the pre-shear strain (caused by the pre-twist) are obtained. Tension tests with fixed pre-twists on SMA thin walled tube are conducted, with a focus on the stress-strain response. The measured values and the analytical formula for the propagation stress are used to determine the material parameters, which, in turn, yields the up-down-up response of a shape memory alloy tube under pure tension. The tendency and turning point of the phase transformation in the pre-twisted tube from localization to homogeneous deformation are also determined, which suggests a plausible way to avoid the instability in actuation applications. In another piece of work, we analyze wave propagation in a semi-infinite shape memory alloy (SMA) bar under a rectangular impulsive loading. Different trilinear up–down–up nominal stress–strain curves for loading and unloading processes are adopted to complete the dynamical system. The chord criterion (equivalent to maximally dissipative kinetics) is employed to single out the unique solution for the impact problem. The interactions among discontinuities (loading/unloading elastic shock waves and phase boundaries) can yield some complicated wave structure. In particular, it is found that the encounter of the unloading elastic shock wave and the loading phase boundary can yield three different wave patterns depending on the level of impact stress, which are different from those for a hardening response studied in the literature. Solutions in the whole temporal and spatial domain are obtained, which reveal interesting wave structures induced by two different levels of interesting wave structures induced by two different levels of impact. Phase transformation regions and tension/compression regions are also determined. The results also suggest that the SMAs can be used for impact-protection purpose effectively.

11303015.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303015.value: This project includes the following main results. 1. We develop a consistent dynamic finite-strain plate theory and provide a novel linear plate theory for small deformations. It is consistent with the 3-D weak formulation invloving no high-order stress resultants. The O(h) linear plate theory takes into account both stretching and bending effects, which is manifested by the capability of capturing both symmetric and antisymmetric modes in the free vibration problem. Compared with other linear theories, the present one possesses both simplicity and accuracy (in particular for distributions). 2. A consistent finite-strain plate theory was developed for incompressible hyperelastic materials. The key feature of the current plate theory is that for all external traction and position boundary conditions, each term in the variations of the generalized potential energy functional attains the asymptotic order of O(h4). For the convenience of future numerical calculations, the weak formulation of the 2D vector plate equation together with the position or traction edge boundary conditions are also provided. By considering the pure finite-bending of a plate made of an incompressible neo-Hookean material, it is demonstrated that the plate solutions can achieve an accuracy of O(h2). It seems that no existing plate theory for incompressible materials can achieve the consistency criterion as our current one. Besides that, it is known that finite element calculations always have the difficulty of handling the incompressibility constraint. In many situations, an extra term is added to the strain energy function to make it “nearly incompressible”. For our current plate theory, the incompressibility constraint has been fully utilized to derive the recursion relations, and the final 2D vector plate equation is not subject to any constraint. Thus, such a computation difficulty is also avoided. 3. A consistent finite-strain shell theory for a general shell of arbitrary geometry is developed, with no special restrictions on external loadings. It is also consistent with the 3-D weak formulation with an O(h4) error for each term. The derivation procedure is highly nontrivial due to the complicated effects due to the presence of curvatures. The present shell equation naturally preserves the local force balance. Proper 2-D boundary conditions and associated weak formulations are proposed. The validity of the shell theory is substantiated by the concrete examples regarding axisymmetric deformations of spherical and circular cylindrical shells. The present shell theory may provide a general mathematical framework for studying deformations of thin structures composed of soft materials.

11303015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303015.value: The works done in this project will be extended to establish a plate theory for soft materials with initial/residual stresses.

11303015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303015.value: Many natural and man-made materials are very soft, e.g. polymer, elastomer, polymer gel and biological tissue, etc. On the other hand, plates are very common structures (e.g. plant leaves, thin gel films and biological membranes). Thus, there is a great need to study soft material plates. Any object is always three-dimensional. However, for a plate structure the thickness is much less than the in-plane length scale. As a result, instead of using a three-dimensional theory, which is difficult to tackle both numerically and analytically, one can proceed to investigate the behaviors of soft material plates through proper reduced two-dimensional plate theories. There are many small-strain plate theories available, however, consistent dynamical finite-strain plate theories incorporating both bending and stretching were not available. This project provides such plate theories for compressible and incompressible hyperelastic materials and a shell theory for compressible hyperelastic materials. The works establish a solid theoretical framework for studying general mechanical behaviours of soft-material plates. The methodology developed is also general to some extent and can be used to do dimension-reduction for other problems.

11303515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303515.value: 二氧化碳是一種經濟及可持續的有機化合物的來源，因此，將二氧化碳固定為有用物質及有機化合物受到廣泛關注。現時，使用二氧化碳生產有機化合物的工業十分有限，這是因為大部份二氧化碳的轉化過程都經過相當大的動能屏障，所以發展高效的二氧化碳催化過程特別是以可再生能源推動的催化作用相當重要。 本項目將研究新的光催化作用以轉化二氧化碳為不同的胺基甲酸酯。對比現時使用含劇毒的光氣生產胺基甲酸酯工業方法，這些新的光催化作用是一種十分環境友好的方法。通過機理探究，優化這些光催化過程的反應條件、應用及光催化劑。同時，將探索可循環使用的光催化劑及光催化合成方法。

11303515.label: Realisation of objectives
11303515.value: All objectives have been achieved. The details findings are summarized as follows: 1) Objectives 1 and 2: reaction conditions for the formation of N-carbamates have been elucidated. The results enable us to develop luminescent chemosensors for carbon dioxide and photocatalytic system for organic transformation and carbon dioxide activation. Some of the results are reported in the our publications, such as Dalton Transaction 2016; Inorganic chemistry 2016 and Asian Journal of Organic Chemistry 2018, listed in Part C. 2) Objective 3: the excited state properties, photophysics and electrochemical properties of all the newly-developed luminescent transition metal complexes potentially useful as photocatalysts and activation of carbon dioxide have been investigated in details. Some of the results are reported in publication such as Inorganic Chemistry 2016, European Journal of Inorganic Chemistry 2018, Inorganic Chemistry 2018 and Inorganic Chemistry 2019, listed in Part C. One series of the transition metal complexes also exhibits interesting electrochemical properties, potentially useful as materials for memory devices. Their memory device applications have also been studied and reported in Journal of Materials Chemistry C 2018. 3) Objective 4: solid-supported transition metal complexes for the application in photocatalytic process have also been designed, synthesized and characterized. Although these solid-support photocatalysts are active, their quantum efficiency is much lower than the homogeneous photocatalytic system. A strategy for improving the efficiency has been developed. This is reported in my recent lecture in XXVIII International conference on Organometallic Chemistry.

11303515.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303515.value: The research was conducted in accordance with the proposed research plan and methodology as outlined in the proposal. Various new series of isocyanide/carbene-containing luminescent transition metal complexes with photocatalytic and electrocatalytic activity for reduction and transformation of CO2 have been developed. In the carbene-containing Re(I) complexes, they show improved photocatalytic activity with capability of using low-energy visible light and electrocatalytic activity. On the basis of the reactivity study between amines and carbon dioxide, a new family of acyclic amine-containing carbene transition metal complexes has been developed. All the newly developed metal complexes have been fully-characterized by NMR spectroscopy, IR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry and elemental analysis, and some of them have also been structurally characterized by X-ray crystallography. To gain insights into their photocatalytic applications, the detailed physical properties and excited state properties through photophysical and spectroscopic investigations have been studied. The uses of these transition metal complexes for transforming carbon dioxide to useful products have also been investigated. Unexpectedly, one series of complexes also exhibit interesting electrochemical properties suitable for memory device application. The device application of these complexes have also been examined. For some of these complexes showing promising photocatalytic activity, they were used to prepare the solid-supported photocatalysts through covalent immobilization. In short, these results have led to new design strategy on luminescent transition metal complexes and photocatalysts for CO2 activation and organic transformation. Some of these results have been published in internationally-refereed journals, including Inorganic Chemistry, Dalton Transactions, European Journal of Inorganic Chemistry, Asian Journal of Organic Chemistry and Journal of Materials Chemistry. Apart from publications, the results have also been presented as a number of invited lectures or oral presentations in international conferences, including the XXVI IUPAC Symposium on Photochemistry, Osaka, Japan in April 2016; the 2nd International Symposium on Chemical Energy Conversion Processes, Fukuoka, Japan in May 2016; the 42nd International Conference on Coordination Chemistry, Brest, France in July 2016; the 11th International Conference on Cutting-Edge Organic Chemistry in Asia, Daejeon, Korea in Oct 2016; 6th Asia-Oceania Conference on Sustainable and Green Chemistry, Hong Kong in Nov 2016; the 9th Asian Photochemistry Conference, Singapore in Dec 2016; the 11th International Symposium for Chinese Inorganic Chemists, Singapore in Dec 2016; 22nd International Symposium of Photochemistry and Photophysics of Coordination Compounds, Oxford, UK in July 2017; and XXVIII International Conference on Organometallic Chemistry, Florence, Italy in July 2018; 10th Asian Photochemistry Conference, Taipei in Dec 2018.

11303515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303515.value: As mentioned in 6.1, the results of this project have led to new design strategy on luminescent transition metal complexes and photocatalysts for small molecule activation as well as organic transformation. Three major new directions have been initiated. One direction is the extension of the current work to develop new photocatalytic systems for organic transformations. On the other hand, we discovered novel and unexpected properties, such as memory device application and mechanically-responsive properties, in the new transition metal complexes when new classes of ligands developed in this work are incorporated into other transition metal complex systems. As a result, we have also initiated new research work to develop mechanoresponsive materials and photocatalysis. Of these three directions, the research proposal on the development of the mechanoresponsive materials have been supported by RGC.

11303515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303515.value: The transformation of carbon dioxide to useful products is one of the major challenges and important areas of research. The objectives of this project aimed at contributing to this area through the development of new transition metal complexes to serve as photocatalysts. In this project, a numbers of new transition metal complexes have been designed, synthesized and characterized. The properties and photocatalytic applications of these compounds have been studied in details. The results of our findings showed that some of the newly-developed compounds are excellent photocatalysts to transform carbon dioxide with enhanced performance over the existing and most-commonly used photocatalysts. In short, our results have provided new design strategy on of luminescent materials and photocatalysts. The scientific findings have been published in internationally-refereed journals and presented in a number of invited lectures or oral presentations in international conferences.

11303715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303715.value: Efficient utilization of the solar energy requires materials with electronic band structures that are tuned to absorb a large portion of the sun light and convert it into electrical power. Another important consideration is that these materials have to be earth abundant enough to produce photovoltaics for the global gigawatt scale demand. Moreover, it is highly desirable that these materials are also non-toxic so that their impact on the environment is minimal. Compound semiconductors composed of abundant elements such as oxides and sulfides typically have energy gaps too large for efficient solar power conversion. We have discovered that alloying of distinctly different materials leads to materials whose electronic band structure can differ drastically from the band structure of the component materials. These highly mismatched alloys (HMAs) offer an unprecedented flexibility in controlling not only the band gap but also the location of the conduction and the valence band edges. However, because of the high mismatch in electronegativity and size of the elements, synthesis of these alloys requires techniques that are highly non-equilibrium in nature. In this proposal our goal is to develop highly disruptive future-generation solar energy technologies based on our recently discovered highly mismatched semiconductor alloys. In simple terms we propose to synthesize a semiconductor material with a small energy gap within the solar spectrum by alloying two judiciously selected semiconductors with the large energy gaps outside the solar spectrum. We use the band anticrossing model to identify a class of wide gap compounds of light, abundant elements, namely zinc oxide alloying with zinc sulfide, selenide and telluride that exhibit extreme band gap bowings resulting in a much lower band gaps, well within the range necessary for efficient solar power conversion. Such ZnO-based HMAs are formed of abundant and non-toxic elements and are expected to exhibit high chemical and thermal stabilities as well as a superior tunability in electronic properties. Moreover, we propose to exploit the electronic band tuning capability of ZnO based HMA to fabricate a hybrid ZnO HMA-Si double junction tandem solar cell that is expected to achieve efficiency over 30%. We plan to carry out a 2 phase project—in phase I we focus on material synthesis and characterization of ZnO based HMAs; in phase 2 we will utilize the results obtained in phase 1 to design, fabricate and test prototype single and multijunction solar cells. 高效率太陽能電池要求其吸光層材料具有合適的電子能帶結構，從而可將大部分太陽能轉化成電能。爲了滿足全球吉瓦規模的能耗需求，用於製備太陽能電池的材料須豐富地存在於地球表面。此外，所用材料應儘量無毒，從而降低其對環境的不良影響。由富足元素諸如氧和硫構成的複合半導體通常具有太大的帶隙，因而不能製備出高轉換效率的太陽能電池。我們的研究發現，將大差異的材料結合成的合金材料能呈現出與各組分材料非常不同的電子能帶結構。在調控半導體之帶隙及其導帶與價帶邊緣位置方面，這些高失配半導體合金的製備爲人們提供了前所未有的契機。然而，由於元素間在電負性和原子尺寸上存在極大的差異，製備高失配合金一般需要利用非平衡材料生長技術。本項目旨在以我們近期發現的高失配半導體合金材料為基礎，開發一種極具顛覆性的新世代太陽能電池技術。簡言之，我們倡議, 以通過慎密選取的大帶隙半導體材料製備出寬太陽光譜吸收的較小帶隙的半導體合金材料。運用能帶互斥模型，我們發現一類由輕而富足的寬帶隙半導體構成的高失配合金材料，即氧化鋅與硫化鋅、硒化鋅及碲化鋅之合金半導體；由於其極大的帶隙彎曲現象，這些合金半導體呈現出較小的帶隙，從而適用於製備高轉換效率的太陽能器件。這類由富足而無毒元素構成的基於氧化鋅的高失配半導體合金，不僅在電學特性方面具有優越的調控特性，而且也預期可表現非凡的化學及熱穩定性。此外，我們亦擬充分利用基於氧化鋅的高失配半導體合金在電子能帶方面的可調控能力，製備出基於氧化鋅高失配合金-硅雙節串聯太陽能電池，此等太陽能器件可望實現超30％的光電轉換效率。我們將整個項目分爲兩個階段實施。第一階段，我們將集中基於氧化鋅的高失配合金的合成與表徵；第二階段，我們將利用第一階段所獲得的結果去設計、製備及測試所構建的單結與多節太陽能電池。

11303715.label: Realisation of objectives
11303715.value: 1. Synthesize and characterize highly mismatched O-rich II-VI oxide semiconductors, specifically, ZnO1-xTex, ZnO1-xSex and ZnO1-xSx (with x up to 0.1) using highly non-equilibrium synthesis methods including sputtering and pulsed laser deposition. This objective is fully accomplished for both materials grown by pulsed laser deposition (PLD) and magnetron sputtering. ZnO based highly mismatched alloys (HMAs), including ZnOS, ZnOSe and ZnOTe were synthesized using highly non-equilibrium methods: pulsed laser deposition (PLD) and magnetron sputtering. A wide range of composition of these alloys was explored. The growth parameters for each of the alloy systems were optimized to achieve high quality thin film samples. These studies have established the electrical and optoelectronic properties and also identified the miscibility gap of the respectively HMAs. For example, we grew ZnOTe alloy films over the entire composition range and found that ZnO1-xTex HMAs are in the wurtzite phase with Te composition up to ~15%, while in the Te rich region with x>0.85 they crystallize in the zinc blende structure. More importantly the energy levels of the S, Se and Te substitutional impurities in ZnO were determined to be at ~0.3, 0.9 and 1 eV with respect to the valence band maximum of ZnO, respectively. We have characterized the basic structural and optoelectronic properties of these alloys and found a strong bandgap reduction from 3.3 eV to <2 eV when >2% Te was incorporated in ZnO. This is in good agreement with the band anticrossing model developed for III-V HMAs. 2. Demonstrate the feasibility of an extensive bandgap and band offset engineering in these highly mismatched oxide semiconductors. This objective is fully accomplished for all the ZnO based highly mismatched alloys. Detailed studies on the electronic band structures of the ZnO based HMAs were carried out using spectrophotometry, spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Experimental results were directly compared with a modified band anticrossing (BAC) model for HMAs which takes into account the compositional dependence of the anticrossing coupling parameters. For the ZnO1-xTex HMAs, we found a drastic reduction on the bandgap of the alloy from 3.3 eV (ZnO) to ~ 2.3 eV with the incorporation of only ~1 % of Te. This large decrease in the bandgap is primarily due to the upward shift in the valence band caused by the interaction with the Te states located at ∼1 eV above the valence band maximum (VBM) of ZnO. The upward shift of the valence band is experimentally confirmed by XPS and synchrotron x-ray absorption and emission spectroscopy (XES/XAS) results. A good agreement between experimental conduction band minimum (CBM) and VBM as well as minimum bandgap values with the electronic band structure described by the BAC model was achieved for ZnO1-xTex both for HMAs in the dilute limits and for a composition up to ∼34% Te. ZnO1-xTex alloys with x = 0.2 have a direct energy gap of about 1.8 eV. This provides a good candidate as the top cell material in a Si-based double junction tandem solar cell. In addition to the optimum energy gap, this alloy also has its CBM energy at about ∼4.9 eV below the vacuum level, which provides a good band alignment with the VBM of Si located at 5.1 eV below the vacuum level. 3. Explore the effectiveness of both n- and p-type doping of these alloys by manipulating positions of the conduction and valence bands through changing the composition For this objective, we have accomplished the n-type doping of ZnOTe HMAs, while the pathway for p-type doping was identified and substantiated with preliminary results with N doping. While ZnOTe HMAs were found to be n-type when grown by the PLD method, sputter deposited ZnOTe were rather insulating. Both Al and H were found to be effective donors for ZnOTe HMAs. With Al doping, an electron concentration n as high as 21019 cm-3 with mobility of ~0.3 cm2/Vs can be achieved for ZnOTe with 2% Te. For HMAs grown by PLD, we found that adding Te in ZnO increases the film resistivity, consistent with the upward shift of the VBM. Such upward VBM shift favors the formation of native acceptor defects such as Zn vacancies. When doped with N via increased N2 background pressure during the growth, the electron concentration n for ZnO dropped from ~1020 to ~3 ×1017 cm−3. A much more drastic drop in n from mid-1019 to 1015 cm−3 is observed for ZnO1−xTex with ∼2%–4% of Te. The drop in electron concentration in ZnO due to N incorporation is consistent with compensation due to N acceptors. Such compensation by N acceptors is even more drastic in ZnO1−xTex due to the upward shift of the VBM in ZnOTe. Such upward movement of the VBM reduces the formation energy of native acceptor defects, shifting the balance toward p-type conductivity. Although p-type ZnOTe was not yet achieved with N doping, our observations suggested p-type doping of ZnO with other acceptor species (e.g. Li, Na or K) by manipulating the VBM with the incorporation of Te. In addition to the material synthesis and characterization work performed at CityU, under this project, we also collaborated with several groups internationally to investigate these ZnO-based HMAs as well as other III-V HMAs for various applications. One of the important applications of these II-VI HMAs is for high efficiency solar cells, especially for the novel intermediate band solar cell (IBSC) concept. In collaboration with a Japanese group in Saga University in Japan, we demonstrated the IBSC operation principle using ZnOTe thin films grown by molecular beam epitaxy. The III-V analogue of these ZnO-based HMAs: GaN-based HMAs were also investigated in collaboration with Nottingham University, Strathclyde University, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and the US Army Research Lab. The materials properties of GaNSb HMAs were directly compared to those in ZnO based in terms of the band anticrossing model for HMAs.

11303715.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303715.value: A modified band anticrossing (BAC) model was developed based on detailed studies of the III-V highly mismatched alloys (HMAs) over a wide composition range in order to account for the basic electronic band structure modifications in our ZnO based HMAs [1,3,4]. ZnO based highly mismatched alloys (HMAs), including ZnOS, ZnOSe and ZnOTe were synthesized using both pulsed laser deposition (PLD) and magnetron sputtering. We have established the electrical and optoelectronic properties and also identified the miscibility gaps of the respectively HMAs. For example, we grew ZnOTe alloy films over the entire composition range and found that ZnO1-xTex HMAs are in the wurtzite phase with Te composition up to ~15%, while in the Te rich region with x>0.85 they crystallize in the zinc blende structure [9]. More importantly, the energy levels of the S, Se and Te substitutional impurities in ZnO were determined to be at ~0.3, 0.9 and 1 eV with respect to the valence band maximum (VBM) of ZnO, respectively. Detailed studies on the electronic band structures of the ZnO based HMAs revealed a drastic reduction on the bandgap of ZnO from 3.3 eV to ~ 2.3 eV with the incorporation of only ~1 % of Te. This large decrease in the bandgap is primarily due to the upward shift in the VBM caused by the anticrossing interaction of the extended VB states and localized Te states located at ∼1 eV above the VBM of ZnO. A good agreement between experimental conduction band minimum (CBM) and VBM with the electronic band structures described by the BAC model was achieved for ZnO1-xTex both for HMAs in the dilute limits and for a composition up to ∼34% Te. We further found that ZnO1-xTex alloys with x = 0.2 have a direct energy gap of about 1.8 eV, providing a good candidate as the top cell material in a Si-based double junction tandem solar cell. Electrically, the upward VBM shift with the incorporation of Te in ZnO favors the formation of native acceptor defects and hence reduces the activities of native donors and can be utilized for the p-type doping of the ZnO [9]. Finally, the operational principles of the novel intermediate band solar cells were demonstrated using the Te-rich ZnOTe thin films [5,6,10].

11303715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303715.value: ZnO1-xTex alloys with x = 0.2 was found to have a direct energy gap of about 1.8 eV. This provides a good candidate as the top cell material in a Si-based double junction tandem solar cell. In addition to the optimum energy gap, this alloy also has its CBM energy at about ∼4.9 eV below the vacuum level, which provides a good band alignment with the VBM of Si located at 5.1 eV below the vacuum level. In order to achieved this high efficiency Si-based tandem solar cell structure, a good control of the electrical properties of the ZnO-based HMA is essential. In this work we showed that the n-type doping in ZnOTe can be achieved. However, as in ZnO, the p-type doping of ZnOTe is very challenging. Preliminary results in this project has already established that the incorporation of Te in ZnO modified the VBM, favoring the formation of acceptor defects. Based on this work, another GRF has been funded (CityU11305119) focusing on the p-type doping of ZnO utilizing the concept of electronic band structure engineering in HMAs.

11303715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303715.value: Efficient utilization of the solar energy requires materials with electronic band structures that can absorb a large portion of the sun light and convert it into electrical power. Another important consideration is that these materials have to be nontoxic and earth abundant enough to produce photovoltaics for the global gigawatt scale demand. In this project, based on our prior knowledge on electronic band structure engineering, we developed a semiconductor material with a small energy gap within the solar spectrum by alloying two judiciously selected semiconductors with large energy gaps. These alloys are zinc oxide based formed of abundant and non-toxic elements and are expected to exhibit high chemical and thermal stabilities as well as a superior tunability in electronic properties. We succeeded in synthesizing a series of ZnO based alloys, including ZnOS, ZnOSe and ZnOTe using industrial compatible sputtering techniques. Moreover, the structural, optical and electrical properties as well as electronic band structures of these alloys were characterized. In particular, we found that a ZnO1-xTex alloys with x = 0.2 have a direct energy gap of about 1.8 eV, providing a good candidate as the top cell material in a Si-based high efficiency double junction tandem solar cell design.
