11303815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303815.value: The discovery of cancer stem cells has changed views of carcinogenesis and provided novel targets for cancer therapy. Cancer stem cells have the ability to initiate tumor formation by undergoing self-renewal and differentiation that result in drug resistance, tumor recurrence and metastasis. However, it is not yet fully understood how tumor microenvironments regulate the fate of cancer stem cells and how interactions between cancer stem cells and their niche govern metastatic colonization and enhance tumorigenicity under inflammatory or transforming signals. Quantitative analysis of the behaviors of cancer stem cells in vitro is limited by the conventional co-culturing methods which cannot mimic the microenvironment inside the tumor. In order to monitor and accurately quantify cell-cell interactions in real-time, we propose to develop a microfluidic-based system which will enable the co-culturing of cancer stem cells and cancer cells in vitro while maintaining a microenvironment similar to the in vivo tumor mass. Through the microfluidic networks, we will provide a platform for display of spatial and temporal dynamics of cell-cell communications, and for quantitative measurement of the cellular parameters such as migration distance and areas, and intercellular contacts, for individual and population of cells. By controlling the dimensions of the microchannels and co-culture units, different quantities and ratios of cancer stem cells and cancer cells will be adjusted to mimic different stages of tumor growth, including initiation, progression, regression, and recurrence after chemotherapy. The behavior of lung cancer stem cells and the differentiated lung cancer cells derived from the same lineage will be analyzed, collectively and individually at single cell level, to quantify the cell proliferation, migration, self-renewal, specific differentiation, and cell-cell interactions in the fluctuating microenvironment. The reconstruction of tumor microenvironment in the microfluidic chip can be further exploited to study the biological processes involving cancer stems cells and other cells in tumor, which will be important for the development of novel and therapeutic strategies against cancer.

11303815.label: Realisation of objectives
11303815.value: 1：Migratory behavior of A549 cells in the presence of lung CSCs The behaviors of A549 cells were studied quantitatively, the results showed that A549 cells in the seeding microwells proliferated slowly with the growth rate during the culturing period, indicating the cell proliferation was negligible in the co-culturing systems when compared the cell migration behaviors in the different microenvironments. Contrary to the lung CSCs, there were no markedly increased numbers of A549 cells in the co-culturing chamber when seeded with lung CSCs, indicating that in the presence of the lung CSCs, A549 cells exhibited low motility towards the lung CSCs. We further quantified the distance of the frontiers of the A549 cells island from the edge of the co-culturing chamber, and found that in the co-culturing systems, A549 cells migrated slowly towards the lung CSCs in the co-culturing chamber regardless of the seeding numbers of both types of cells. Of interest, A549 cells cultured alone showed a remarkably increment in the migration distance from the starting point. To investigate the dynamics of the A549 cells, the net migration distances were calculated by subtracting the distance of A549 cells in the mono-culturing system, which showing that A549 cells migrated faster in the first 24 h co-culturing period and dropped back to the seeding microwells at late time points. The above observations indicating different migratory behaviors of lung CSCs and A549 cells in the co-culturing system, suggesting that the soluble factors secreted by lung CSCs and A549 cells might exhibit different regulatory function of cell migration and aggressiveness of the cells. Hypothetically, when limited number of A549 cells seeded in the system, the lack of factors released by the A549 cells act as a rescue signal, which will be recognized by the lung CSCs and promote the migration and proliferation of the lung CSCs. However, even though the A549 cells exhibited favored migration towards the lung CSCs at the early stage, the secret factors from lung CSCs inhibited further migration of the A549 cells. The regulatory behaviors of the cancer stem cells in the tumor have been attracted much more attentions to understand the mechanisms of drug resistance of cancer and metastasis of tumors. 2. Cell growth in the conditioned medium with anti-cancer drugs To further verify the hypothesis, conditioned medium from lung CSCs (LCM) and conditioned medium from A549 cells (ACM) treated with different dosages of cis-platinum (0, 1.5, 12.5, 50, 100, and 150 µM) were collected and used to culture lung CSCs and A549 cells. Three groups of conditioned medium were collected: medium with cis-platinum cultured with cells for 4 h (CM-cisPt-4h), medium with cells cultured for 20 h after the cis-platinum treated for 4h (CM-20h aft cisPt-4h), and medium with cis-platinum cultured with cells for 24 h (CM-cisPt-24h). All the medium were supplemented with 2% FBS. The morphologies of lung CSCs after cultured with the above different compositions of conditioned medium cultured with A549 cells were recorded and compared with the cells cultured in the fresh medium. Lung CSCs viabilities were evaluated by MTT assay and compared with the cells treated with no drug involved ACM in each group. As result, in the ACM without the addition of cis-platinum, most of the lung CSCs maintained their morphologies in the spindle shape and grew in cluster as they were in the normal culture medium. When treated with cis-platinum with low concentration, lung CSCs elongated in shape and grew randomly in the medium rather than formation of cluster. There were no markedly differences in morphology change of lung CSCs cultured with low drug concentration involved ACM in the three groups. However, majority of lung CSCs were detached in rounded shape when exposed to the cis-platinum with high concentration, i. e. 150 µ M, indicating that lung CSCs could not survive in the medium with cis-platinum in high concentration. When cultured with A549 conditioned medium with 150 M cis-platinum for 4 h (CM-cisPt-4h), limited lung CSCs attached to the surface in the elongated shape while in the high concentration of cis-platinum treated A549 cells conditioned medium for 24 h (CM-cisPt-24h), lung CSCs grew healthily and reached the comparable confluence as they were in the low concentration of cis-platinum treated conditioned medium. Cell viability results also indicated the fast proliferation of lung CSCs when cultured with ACM treated with cis-platinum for 24 h. Compared with the composition of CM-cisPt-4h with the same concentration of cis-platinum, CM-cisPt-24h contained lower concentration of cis-platinum which was consumed by the A549 cells for 20 h, and more soluble factors released from the A549 cells. To eliminate the cis-platinum effect, after the drug treatment for 4 h, A549 cells were washed by PBS and cultured in the fresh medium for continues culture, and the medium were collected (CM-20h aft cisPt-4h) after 20 h. It was found that there were no significantly differences in the morphology and cell viabilities of the lung CSCs when treated with CM-20h aft cisPt-4h and CM-cisPt-24h, indicating that the toxicity effect of the cis-platinum in the long time cultured conditioned medium was negligible and the factors responsible for the faster growth rate and the morphology change of the lung CSCs are soluble mediators secreted by A549 cells. To further verify the hypothesis, orthogonal test were performed by collecting the conditioned medium cultured with lung CSCs and A549 cells and then culturing the two types of cells. As result, lung CSCs exhibited the comparable cell viabilities when cultured by lung CSCs conditioned medium for 24 h regardless of the drug treatment or not, while the cells grew faster in the drug treated lung CSCs conditioned medium with the removal of the drugs after 4h. For A549 cells, they also favored the conditioned medium cultured with A549 cells after the drug treatment, and no markedly toxicity effect of cis-platinum presented in the conditioned medium. However, when cultured with drug treated lung CSCs conditioned medium for 24 h, no positive response of the A549 cells with the aspect of proliferation was observed in both drug-included and drug-free CM, respectively. Compared with the pure drug group, the toxicity effect of cis-platinum on the two types of cells were relieved in both A549 CM and lung CSCs after drug treatment for 4 h. These results indicated that both the cancer cells and CSCs were prone to grow faster in the conditioned medium cultured with cancer cells even treated with anti-cancer drug, suggesting that the factors responsible for the different cancer cells growth behaviors are soluble factors released by the dead cancer cells as the death signals, which hypothetically are tumorigenic, thus attracting the aggressiveness of the CSCs.

11303815.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303815.value: Lung cancer stem cells and lung cancer cells were co-cultured in the microfluidic device and the interactions between cells were analyzed by observing the migration at the single cell level. By regulating the number of cells during seeding controlled by the dimensions of the co-culturing unit, it was found that cancer stem cells display enhanced migratory ability towards the small amount of cancer cells. In contrast, cancer cells actively migrate towards the cancer stem cells at the early interaction stage but persist in close proximity to the cancer stem cells after culturing for 66 h. The rapid growth of the cancer stem cells were also verified in the traditional culturing system, in which cancer stem cells exhibited rapid proliferation capability when cultured with the cancer cells conditioned medium with anti-cancer drug treatment. The microfluidic platform enabled to display the spatial and temporal dynamics of the cell-cell interactions, and quantitatively measure the parameters such as migration distance and areas, that are difficult to measure with standard techniques. 11303815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303815.value: In the future, the cell communication model in the tumor mass will be further established and communication between (1) cancer cell-cancer cell, (2) cancer stem cell-cancer stem cell, and (3) cancer stem cell-cancer cell will be quantitatively studied. Modification of the microfluidic device will be conducted to control the distance of the two types of cells, that is, cells could be controlled to direct or indirect contact with each other in the engineered co-culturing chamber. Biophysical model of cell proliferation and motility will be established and verified with the experiment results. Cell behaviors before and after chemotherapy will be real-time monitored, with the quantitative analysis of cell migration, cell interaction time, and gap junctional intracellular communications. In addition, with the integration of the sieving microstructures for the generation of the single layer microbeads array, it is possible to real-time monitor the secret factors released from the cells by functionalization of the microbeads with the probes for the interested cytokines in the co-culturing systems. The reconstruction of tumor microenvironment in the microfluidic chip could be potentially exploited to understand the biological processes and cell interactions of the cancer stems cells with cancer cells in the tumor.

11303815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303815.value: In summary, we have developed a microfluidic platform for cell co-culture to quantitatively study the cell-cell interactions. The feasibility of the microfluidic device was demonstrated by the serum-induced migration of cancer cells, in which A549 cells severely migrated towards the medium containing high concentration of serum. It was also found that lung cancer stem cells favored the conditioned medium cultured with A549 cancer cells in the microfluidic device. LCSC and LCC were co-cultured in the microfluidic device and the interactions between cells were analyzed by observing the migration at the single cell level. By regulating the number of cells during seeding, which was controlled by the dimensions of the co-culturing unit, we demonstrated that cancer stem cells display enhanced migratory ability towards the small amount of cancer cells (<20). In contrast, cancer cells actively migrate towards the cancer stem cells at the early interaction stage but persist in close proximity to the cancer stem cells after culturing for 66 h. The rapid growth of the cancer stem cells were also verified in the traditional culturing system, in which cancer stem cells exhibited rapid proliferation capability when cultured with the cancer cells conditioned medium with anti-cancer drug treatment.

11303915.value: 起源於學習理論和相關課題的一些新的逼近論問題

11303915.label: Project Objectives
11303915.value: Learning with functional data. A general learning theory framework will be introduced to study approximation abilities of functional linear regression algorithms and the role played by the covariance kernel. We shall first consider relations and differences between the best linear functional and a minimizer of the risk among all measurable functions on the input space. We shall then provide estimates for the approximation error of the regularization scheme with functional data in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces in terms of two integral operators induced by the reproducing kernel and the covariance kernel. Multi-scale structures in the topic of learning with functional data will be considered by ideas and methods from wavelet analysis. Approximation theory problems arising from classification and online learning with functional data will be discussed. Estimating covering numbers involving ultra-high dimensions. Covering numbers of a set involving 2-norm and 1-norm arising from one-bit compressed sensing will be estimated by methods from approximation theory and function spaces. Then we shall get asymptotic behaviors of the covering numbers of a function set arising from additive models in ultra-high dimensions with sequence p-norm penalties, and derive minimax rates of convergence and sparsity analysis for the corresponding learning algorithms. Learning theory of one-bit compressed sensing. A learning theory framework will be employed to analyze one-bit compressed sensing algorithms associated with general measurement vectors. Confidence-based bounds will be provided for the excess risk by solving an approximation theory problem for the involved error decomposition. For approximating sparse vectors in a generalized linear model we shall apply ideas from approximation theory to give a comparison relation between the error norm and the excess risk. By the nature with binary classification data of one-bit compressed sensing, we shall study this topic from learning theory viewpoints, and solve the arising approximation theory problems. Some other topics in compressed sensing will also be considered by methods and ideas from learning theory and approximation theory.

11303915.value: 逼近論在學習算法和數據處理的數學分析中起著重要作用. 本項目旨在研究一些起源於學習理論和相關課題的新的逼近論問題,並應用結果分析一些學習算法.首先我們將通过分析學習理论框架下泛函线性回归算法的逼近能力考虑泛函數據學習,其中的协方差核会利用逼近論分析而估计再生核希尔伯特空间中泛函數據正則化算法的逼近誤差. 然後我們將估計一個起源於一彼特壓縮感知的有關1-範數和2-範數的向量集及一個源自超高維p-範數罰值可加模型的函數集的覆蓋數, 並對相關算法進行分析. 我們將發展一個允許一般測度向量的一彼特壓縮感知的學習理論, 對超出風險提供置信度誤差界, 並與比較關係一起給出稀疏向量逼近的範數估計. 最後,對壓縮感知中的一些課題將利用學習理論和逼近論方法和想法進行研究.

11303915.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303915.value: Minimum error entropy (MEE) algorithms, usually implemented by gradient descent have been used for more than one decade in practical applications including signal processing, functional data and compressed sensing, but there has been no consistency or rigorous error analysis. In [1] we give the first rigorous proof for the convergence of the gradient descent method for MEE in a linear regression setting and convergence rates. The topic of pairwise learning is motivated by learning with functional data and data in ultra-high dimensions. In [2] a PhD student and a postdoc supported by this project study the generalization performance of an online pairwise learning algorithm in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space and obtain convergence rates. Deep learning has powerful applications in various domains and has found empirical super performances in dealing functional data, data in ultra-high dimensions, one-bit compressed sensing and some other topics related to this project. In [3] we introduce a deep neural network approach to localized manifold learning, with each hidden layer endowed with a specific learning task. With nets of three hidden layers, for dimensionality reduction, bias reduction, and variance reduction, we derive rates O(m^{2s/(2s+d)}) of approximation of the regression function with regularity s, in terms of the number m of sample points, and the manifold dimension d. In [4], we introduce the boosted kernel ridge regression (BKRR) algorithm by combining L2-Boosting with kernel ridge regression. We show that BKRRprovides a new bias-variance trade-off via tuning the number of boosting iterations. A (semi-)exponential bias-variance trade-off is derived for BKRR, exhibiting a stable relationship between the generalization error and the number of iterations. Deep neural network architectures play the essential role in deep learning for dealing with functional data and data in ultra-high dimensions from various applications. But there lacks a theoretical foundation for understanding the approximation or generalization ability of deep learning methods. In particular, deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown their power in natural images. In [5] we show that a CNN is universal, meaning that it can be used to approximate any continuous function to an arbitrary accuracy when the depth of the neural network is large enough. This answers an open question in learning theory. Our quantitative estimate, given tightly in terms of the number of free parameters to be computed, verifies the efficiency of deep CNNs in dealing with ultra-high dimensional data, and together with covering number estimates provides generalization error bounds.

11303915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303915.value: Approximation theory problems arising from our study and research results and methods developed in this project lead to further questions for deep learning algorithms and distributed learning schemes. These issues will be investigated in our future research activities.

11303915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303915.value: Approximation theory plays an important role in mathematical analysis of learning algorithms and data analysis. In this project, we solved some new approximation theory problems arising from learning theory and related topics, and applied the solutions to analyze some learning algorithms. Our research findings include mathematical analysis of several learning algorithms and some related approximation theory problems: the gradient descent method for the minimum error entropy principle applied in signal processing, functional data and compressed sensing; online pairwise learning for big data; deep neural networks for deep learning with functional data, data in ultra-high dimensions, one-bit compressed sensing; boosted kernel ridge regression; and deep convolutional neural networks for dealing with ultra-high dimensional data. Our research problems and results enhance the interactions among the fields of approximation theory, learning theory, compressed sensing, and data analysis.

11304115.label: Project Objectives
11304115.value: To characterize the effects of transition metal oxide (TMO, e.g. MoO3, ReO3, V2O5) doping on physical properties (optical, dielectric, electronic etc) of selected organic small molecules (e.g . C60, pentacene, rubrene etc) using photoluminescence spectroscopy, optical absorption spectroscopy, capacitance-voltage measurements etc. The main reason for these works is to identify suitable combinations of TMO and small molecule semiconductors with strong interactions and formation of charge transfer complexes (CTC) with widely tunable physical properties. To study the effects of transition metal oxide doping on the energetics (delocalized charge density, energy level offsets, charge interaction etc) and charger transfer (CT) states at selected organic donor/acceptor interfaces (e.g rubrene/C60, SubPc/C60 etc) at both ground and excited states via respectively ultraviolet/ x-ray photoemission spectroscopies (UPS/XPS) and charge-modulated electroabsorption spectroscopy (CMEAS). The main reason for these studies is to establish the correlations between the TMO:organic CTC properties and the D/A junctions’ electronic properties. To develop approaches for controlling charge dissociation/extraction at organic donor/acceptor interfaces via transition metal oxide doping. This objective is included because of the important influences of charge dissociation at D/A junctions on performance of all organic photovoltaic devices.

11304115.label: Realisation of objectives
11304115.value: In this project, physical and electronic properties of TMO and other types of CTC systems have been characterized in details. Their absorption, emission, capacitance-voltage relationship, dielectric effect, electronic structure, etc have been studied. Systems with CT characteristics have been investigated using UPS and CMEAS, respectively. To get a better understanding on our obtained results, theoretical modelling on CT state based on Marcus theory, Gaussian function, open circuit voltage at 0K were also included. The data obtained clarify in detail the charge energetics at D/A interface (i.e. delocalized charge density, energetic broadening of CTS, bimolecular recombination, dielectric effect, charge interaction, etc.) of ground and excited CT states. For example, our UPS results show that some of the D:A blends simply follow vacuum level alignment, but others show strong energy level shifting as a result of Fermi level pinning. CMEAS results further suggested that relaxation processes from “hot” to “relaxed” CT states would not weaken a delocalization feature of CT states in a steady state, which is of crucial importance for the understanding of the role of CTS in photovoltaic processes. Furthermore, studies on dielectric effect on CTC systems show that polarizability of Frenkel excitons has direct correlation with the measured dielectric constant of bulk heterojunction thin films. Based on our studies, guidelines and selection rules are presented to forecast an open circuit voltage (Voc) and investigate its loss in OPV. For example, by controlling a dielectric constant and weight percentage of the system, the Voc of 0, 0.5, 5, 25 and 50 % MoO3 doped OPV devices are 0.8, 0.88, 0.91, 0.95 and 1.02 V respectively. A new approach for stacked structure with more CT excitonic behavior is also demonstrated and the charge dissociation of the new structure is discussed. Besides, we have investigated some bipolar materials (SubNc and SubPc) and found that they exhibit more CT excitonic behavior than traditional OPV materials. These finding point out that exciton formed in these materials are highly delocalized and show strong CT character. With the effort on 1) characterizing the physical and electronic properties of CTC samples, 2) understanding their CT behaviors using UPS and CMEAS, the control of charge dissociation/extraction at organic donor/acceptor interfaces via transition metal oxide doping (i.e. MoO3) are presented. Our model and guidelines supported with examples successfully demonstrated how to improve the device properties (i.e. Voc) of the D:A device. Based on the above results on donor-acceptor charge interaction, we further explore the applications of charge transfer state in perovskite devices e.g. perovskite device and organic light emitting devices (OLED). For example, we studies the in incorporation of dimethylsulfoxide in organic–inorganic halide perovskites with post transitional metal in details. A simple method for controlling the quality of perovskite films by dimethylsulfoxide additives in the precursor solution is presented and their charge transfer process is studied in details. Besides, charge transfer state in white WOLEDs is also studied, and a new device structure is presented.

11304115.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304115.value: In this project, we have examined 1) the effect of transition metal oxide doping on dielectric properties of organic semiconductors; 2) charge interaction at the D/A junctions using CMEAS and UPS studies; and 3) the charge dissociation in OPV device. All the results are published as references 1-7 in part C. Our combined experimental (UPS and CMEAS) and theoretical modelling (Marcus theory, Gaussian function) explain in detail the charge energetics at D/A interface such as delocalized charge density, energy level offsets, energetic broadening of CTS, bimolecular recombination, dielectric effect, charge interaction and charger transfer energy, etc. [J. Phys. Chem. C 26, 14059 (2016)] In particular, the CT energy from each measurement approach exhibit a linear relationship with the measured Voc. This result clearly demonstrates the difference in CMEAS and UPS, and they are both effective technique for measuring the CT energies of the D/A interface. Energy alignment and the correlation on Voc of mixed CT samples are also studied. [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 11, 7283 (2016)] Besides, studies on dielectric effect on CTC systems shows that polarizability of Frenkel excitons has direct correlation with the measured dielectric constant of the bulk heterojunction thin films. [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 33, 21798 (2016), ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 8, 7256 (2018)] All these effort provide important overview to the CT states and its energy loss in various OPV devices. From the understanding on dielectric effect, surface properties and electronic coupling, MoO3 mixing approach is developed. [Chan C. Y., PhD diss. (2017)] The dielectric constants of our devices increased from 9.3 to 21.6 when the MoO3 doping ratio increased from 0 % to 50 %. The corresponding devices shows an increase of Voc from 0.8 to 1.02 V respectively. Also, we have investigated some bipolar materials (SubNc and SubPc) and found that they exhibit more CT excitonic behavior than the traditional OPV materials. [Adv Mater. 29, 1606909 (2017)]These findings point out that exciton formed in these materials are highly delocalized and show strong CT character. Current understanding on the interaction between metal oxide and photoactive materials is also applied to other optoelectronic device. [Adv. Energy Mater. 21, 1800185 (2018), ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 39, 26135 (2016)] Our result clearly show that the control the physical properties of donor and acceptor materials, the overall dielectric properties and device properties of the OPV devices can be tuned and improved.

11304115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304115.value: Current work has successfully characterized the CT complexes and clarified the detailed charge energetics at D/A interface using various system such as MoO3-, fullerene- and bipolar- based system. Our obtained results provide new insight on the charge transfer states properties and their related charge dynamics at organic D/A interfaces; and the results are applied to tune the properties of OPV device. Apart from PV applications, CTCs with many new features and interesting findings have drawn much attention in recent year. For example, with special charge distributions and electronic interactions at the D/A interfaces, unexpected properties such as ultra-long carrier diffusion distance up to 3.5cm (Forrest et al., Nat. Mater.,554,7690 (2018)), abnormally-high electrical conductivities (Kahn et al., Nat. Mater.,16,1209 (2017)), and world’s first organic long-persistent luminescence materials (Adachi et al., Nat. Mater.,550,384 (2017)) have been reported recently. Forrest et al. commented that D:A mixtures are considered as a game-changer in the future development of optoelectronic devices. While all these novel properties clearly open more application possibilities for CTCs, it is important to develop strategic approaches to utilize the new feature of CTCs in various applications.

11304115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304115.value: This project combines the use of a conventional UPS/XPS, a newly developed CMEAS technique and physical characterization techniques to study charge energetics of CT states at organic D/A interfaces in both the excited and the ground states. These techniques are complementary to each other and provides new insights on the interface energetics, charge delocalization and thus carrier extraction efficiency at organic D/A interfaces. Combined with these techniques and theoretical modeling, the PI have examined charge energetics at D/A interface (i.e. delocalized charge density, energy level offsets, the energetic broadening of CTS, bimolecular recombination, dielectric effect, charge interaction and charger transfer energy, etc), and provided important overview to the Voc and its energy loss in various OPV devices. Guidelines and selection rules are presented to forecast the VOC and investigate its loss in OPV. With all these efforts, approaches for controlling the interface energetics are presented. Devices using MoO3 mixing and new structures are studied, and much improved surface properties as well as Voc are presented.

11304415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304415.value: When the dimension of a silicon (Si) structure shrinks to the exciton Bohr radius (4.9nm) of bulk Si, the quantum confinement effect becomes significant, facilitating many interesting and manipulatable physical properties and paving the way for multiple electronic and optoelectronic applications of the material. These low-dimensional Si structures, including quantum dots (0D SiQDs), nanowires (1D SiNWs), and nanosheets (2D SiNSs), share some common properties and functionalities but present different and interesting dimensionality effects. Our recent studies show that the exciton in small SiQDs and SiNSs can be localized at an individual bond, but can also be delocalized in SiNWs. A closer study of these details of all the above mentioned nanostructures, particularly in terms of their exciton geometry and dynamics, is strategically important for their emerging applications. In this project, we will systematically investigate the geometry and dynamics of various possible excitons of these Si nanostructures with different dimensions, sizes, boundaries and symmetries. Using time-dependent density functional theory and its tight binding approximation, we will perform excited-state molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for the Si nanostructures mentioned above. We will explore the formation, trapping, and migration of the exciton in order to understand these ultrafast and dynamic processes. We will also identify the atoms and bonds affected by the excitations and observe the time evolution of the charge density, such as the migration of the excited electron from its initial position to neighboring bonds as well as its localization. The simulation will be conducted at different temperatures including 50K, 100K, and 300K in the MD simulations, in order to examine the phonon effect. These exciton processes may take place at a sub picosecond scale, suitable for the quantum mechanical level simulations. We expect our simulations to reveal the interplay between the material geometric properties (relating to size, boundary, symmetry, defect, passivant and adsorbent) and exciton geometry and dynamics, including the localization and trapping of the exciton as well as the possible transition between the Frenkel and Wannier-Mott types in these highly confined environments. We aim to provide important insights into photoinduced dynamic phenomena and their crucial implications for modulating the exciton transport efficiency in strongly confined low-dimensional systems. The study can advance our understanding of the structure-dependent optoelectronic properties of Si nanostructures and guide their applications in nanoscale optoelectronic devices. 當矽結構的尺寸縮小到體矽材料激子玻爾半徑（4.9nm）時，量子限制效應變得顯著，使許多物理性質變得有趣且可被調控，從而使該材料具有多重電子和光電子應用。這些低維矽結構包括量子點（零維）、納米線（壹維）和納米片（二維）。它們具有壹些共同的特性和功能，但確受維數有不同程度的影響。我們最近的研究表明，激子可以定域在小尺寸量子點 和納米片中某個鍵上，但也可以離域在整個矽納米線中。對上述納米結構中激子的幾何形狀和動力學的詳細研究對促進其新型應用具有重要意義。 本項目將探討這些矽納米結構的各種可能的激子的幾何形狀和動力學以及它們受邊界和對稱性的影響。將使用含時密度泛函理論及其緊束縛近似，對上述矽納米結構進行激發態分子動力學模擬。將探索激子的形成、捕獲和遷移，以了解這些超快動態過程。還將確定受激發的原子和鍵，並觀察電荷密度的時間演化，比如激發電子從其初始位置到相鄰鍵的遷移和局域化。將在不同的溫度下進行分子動力學模擬，包括50K、100K和300K，以研究聲子效應。這些激子過程可能發生在亞皮秒尺度，適於量子力學水平模擬。我們希望，我們的模擬能揭示材料的結構性質（包括大小、邊界、對稱性、缺陷、鈍化和吸附）和激子的幾何形狀和動力學之間的相互關聯，包括激子的局域化和捕獲以及在這些高度受限的環境裏的Frenkel和Wannier-Mott類型激子之間可能的轉化。將為光致動力學現象及調制它們在強約束低維系統中的激子運輸效率提供重要見解。本研究的實施可促進我們對矽納米結構的結構相關的光電性能的理解，並指導其在納米光電器件中的應用。

11304415.label: Realisation of objectives
11304415.value: Since silicon nanostructures with other dimensionalities (SiQDs and SiNWs) have been reasonably well understood soon after we started this project, our work has later largely focused on 2D silicon nanosheets (SiNSs). We calculated the static ground- and excited-state electronic and optical properties of SiNSs as a function of the size(width), followed by the treatment of the self-consistent charge time-dependent density functional tight binding (SCC-TD-DFTB) excited-state dynamics theory to specifically characterize the time evolution of the orbital and geometrical structures. Several previous studies branded the performance of SCC-DFTB and confirmed its ability to produce the DFT level geometries as well as energies. Low dimensional quantum confinement effect is anticipated to control the electronic and optical properties, in particular, the excitons self-trapping during the switch involving the sizing up from a linear geometry to square and rectangular nanosheets. Our systematic structure-property approach regulated the quantum confinement influence on the exciton formation time and the dynamics of SiNSs on the excited- state energy surface. We demonstrated that the exciton localizes along the softer Si-Si bonds due to the structural relaxation, leading to a large Stokes shift. Through excited-state (S1) dynamics, we provided a detailed description of the time evolution of exciton formation, localization, and trapping, as revealed in the static calculations. Time evolution of the excited-state electron charge density, revealing the relocation from the ground-state to the excited-state relaxation and identified the contributions of bond stretching to the excited-state relaxation. The exciton relaxation time for smaller NSs is shorter (~450 fs) as compared to the larger NSs, which takes up to 800 fs, showing a strong interplay between the location of the exciton localization and the quantum confinement of the structure. Our excited-state dynamic observations revealed the mechanism of the size regulated self-trapped exciton formation in SiNSs, suggesting it as center for optical activities and elongated relaxation time for efficient use of carriers in silicon devices at reduced dimensions. More details about this work has been described in publication 3 of Part C-8. We further extended our exciton dynamics study to simulate the reaction of the heptazine−water system to UV excitation. Heptazine-assembled polymeric carbon nitride (CN) materials have fascinated the research community as a photocatalyst for hydrogen evolution while less attention has been devoted to the mechanistic features of the host materials. Our working principle is that the main impact of the solvation is on the excited-state evolution of the hydrogen-bonded heptazine molecule in a water cluster environment. Therefore, we ran excited-state nonadiabatic dynamics simulations of heptazine with one water molecule (heptazine-w1) or a five water molecule (heptazine-w5) cluster using the surface-hopping method within TDDFT-based femtosecond (fs) evolution of the potential energy. The work has been described in detail in publication 3 of Part C-8. At the meantime, we have developed a new method to deal with structure evolution at both ground state and excited state, namely a torque approach (see publication 1 of Part C-8). Rotation-inducing torque is ubiquitous in many molecular systems. We expect the approach would be useful for this project to evaluate the structure changes due to exciton generation and motion. We also explored tunneling lifetimes of electrons escaping from a nanodot or atoms under a static electric field (see publication 2 of Part C-8).

11304415.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304415.value: In publication 3 of Part C-8, we obtained the first excited-state (S1) self-trapped exciton formation in SiNSs by observing the frontier orbital localization relating to the characteristic size of the electronic excitations. We found that the frontier molecular orbitals are highly localized in S1 state on the stretched Si-Si bond due to the photo-excited structural relaxation, leading to a significant Stokes shift. Time domain study of the photo-excited emission gap correlated with the frontier orbital localization properties for exciton formation. Stretched Si-Si softer bonds provide a favorable site for exciton localization, resulting in exciton trapping. The exciton formation time found to be around ~450—850 fs showing the consistency of the initial exciton formation time with a recent measurement (~500 to ~900 fs). Our study reveals that Si-Si bond breaking act as the optical activity center and provides regulation of the self-trapped exciton formation time by quantum confinement effect in SiNSs. In publication 4 of Part C-8, the molecular-level picture of the decomposition of heptazine hydrogen bonded to water molecule(s) (heptazine−water complex) into heptazinyl and hydroxyl biradical products is revealed using excited-state nonadiabatic dynamics simulations. Dynamics simulations show that hydrogen detachment from the water molecule to the heptazine occurs within tens of femtoseconds and suggest that excited-state deactivation via N−H······O−H electron-driven proton transfer (EDPT) is the dominant and most relevant excited-state deactivation process in heptazine−water complexes leading to conical intersection. The observation of photo relaxation-induced water splitting by heptazine is proof of the water-splitting reaction principle, which presents further challenges for computational and experimental investigations of the deactivation of heptazinyl and OH biradical products for efficient hydrogen evolution. In publication 1 of Part C-8, we present a straightforward theoretical method based on forces acting on atoms and obtained from atomistic quantum mechanics calculations to quickly and qualitatively determine whether a molecule or sub-unit thereof has a tendency to rotate and, if so, around which axis and in which sense: clockwise or counterclockwise. The method also indicates which atoms, if any, are predominant in causing the rotation. Our computational approach can eﬃciently provide insights into the internal rotational degrees of freedom of all molecules. In publication 2 of Part C-8, the calculated electron tunneling lifetimes in model systems such as a quantum dot are comparable with other theoretical studies.

11304415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304415.value: As we already started, the methodology we demonstrated in this work for studying the exciton structures and dynamics of silicon nano-structures can be used to explore the exciton dynamics and photocatalytic degradation mechanism of graphitic carbon nitride nanostructures in water splitting. One work needs urgent study is to obtain strategies for reducing photocatalytic degradation, which requires systematic investigation of the exciton dynamics and possible photoinduced chemical reactions of various g-CN nanostructures in water splitting under visible light. Towards the goal, we can use time-dependent density functional theory and its tight-binding approximation to perform the excited-state molecular dynamics simulations for the neutral and charged g-CN nanostructures. The simulation can be conducted at various possible temperatures (ranging from 230K to 320K) likely to be experienced in applications. Systematic simulations of all these possible processes are badly needed in order to identify which is most critical to electrode stability and guide the design of future experiments. We expect that such simulations would help focus experimental efforts and thus reduce the cost and timescale for the commercialization of the technique.

11304415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304415.value: To guide and complement experimental efforts, this project has systematically studied the excited-state properties and resolved the signatures in optical absorption and emission of nanostructures with silicon nanosheets (SiNSs) and graphitic carbon nitride (g-CN) 2D materials as the focused systems, with and without surface modifications or adsorptions. Our study reveals that Si-Si bond breaking act as the optical activity center and provides regulation of the self-trapped exciton formation time by quantum confinement effect in SiNSs. We demonstrated that the exciton localizes along the softer Si-Si bonds due to the structural relaxation, leading to a large Stokes shift. We also demonstrated the photoinduced chemical reaction of 2D nanostructures such as g-CN with molecules from environment. The results provide the needed understanding of the luminescence mechanisms from nanostructures, which will facilitate their applications in optoelectronics and chemical/biological sensings.

11304715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11304715.value: 关于随机相互作用系统经验测度的稀有事件分析

11304715.label: Project Objectives
11304715.value: Develop numerical method for transition pathway when density function exists. We aim to develop various versions of Minimum Action Method (including string method, Maupertuis’ principle) based on the principle of least action. This specific question is to solve the variational problem of the action functional for the weakly interacting diffusion model, under the assumption that the representation of the probability measure for the empirical distribution by using the Lebesque density function is valid. This assumption is validated if the coefficient functions are sufficient smooth. Formulate the large deviation result and develop stable numerical schemes for singular interaction. The task is to solve the challenges of path calculation when singularity happens by first establishing large deviation result with the tools from HJB equation in metric space as well as existing regularity results. The numerical scheme will be developed by using the geometric tangent cone for path interpolation to achieve stability. Applications and Extensions Besides the above two core missions, we also target to solve practical problems and re- lated questions in science briefly mentioned in the proposal. Some of these applications are of their own interests. The generalisation of our results to some similar interacting systems such as multi-level models and jump-diffusion models is also worth additional research work.

11304715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304715.value: 相互作用的粒子系统长期以来一直是统计物理的兴趣之一，并也于近期在金融工程和运筹学出现。本项目考察大量的弱相互作用的扩散粒子。当粒子数趋于无穷大，颗粒的经验测度收敛于一个平均场极限。然而对于有限多个粒子，随机性势必带动该经验测度最终偏离平衡态。这种突然的改变或转变，虽然在非常低的概率发生，可能有整个系统层面的显著影响。他们通常被称为在非常小的频率发生的稀有事件。在实践中，这些稀有事件对应的相变的铁磁性或液晶材料，金融系统性风险，物种群落的灭绝等。 本提案将通过研究概率测度空间上的最佳转移路径来研究稀有事件，其中“最佳”是指基于大偏差原理（LDP）的最小化速率函数（又名作用量泛涵）。 这最优路径提供了稀有事件的最有可能的发生方式，并且和 其他过渡、相变问题紧密相关。该计划的第一个目标是根据拉格朗日形式的速率函数，提供一种有效的数字工具集来计算光滑漂移和扩散系数下的路径， 包括处理莫佩屠斯原则和H-1空间的切空间黎曼几何结构。这里涉及的技术包括最小动作方法及其数值自适应策略。然而，一些重要的物理模型有奇异的相互作用，这可能会导致大规模冷凝效果，即概率测度对勒贝格测度有奇性。我们认为，基于H-1的黎曼几何不足以应付这一挑战。做为这个研究计划的第二个目标，我们将使用度量几何，而不是黎曼几何来处理发生冷凝效果的情况。在一般的度量空间几何切锥的想法将在本内容进行探讨。在这一计划开发的理论与数值格式将是潜在的使用许多应用程序，这计划还涉及如液晶、系统性风险和二维涡动力学等具体实例。

11304715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304715.value: The random interactive particle system is one of the very important tools to describe the nontrivial dynamics of a large population with application in game theory, control theory, economics etc. This project aims for the understanding of the rare transitions for such systems, which may correspond to the drastic change of the macroscopic behaviros of the population, the unexpected and signifcant shift whole public opinions, etc. The research in this project helps to understand the mechanism of how such rare events arise, develop and transit, at the differenet level of scales and noisy pertubation.

11304915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304915.value: Air pollution exerts an important control on the health effects in urban populations. In Hong Kong, the crowded urban environment makes it likely that people receive a significant burden from fine particles and roadside pollutants generated by vehicles. Air pollution is thought to be responsible for the rapid increase in the number of people suffering from non-communicable diseases and presents one of the biggest challenges to the health care systems in Hong Kong with its aging population. The proposed research will examine air pollutant profiles and the potential exposure of people in the roadside environment, most notably sitting out areas and roadside playgrounds. Sensitive individuals such as the elderly and children can spend considerable time at these locations. The project will monitor the concentrations of carbon monoxide/dioxide and fine particles at sufficient detail to map the concentrations in the recreational areas. The concentrations will also be modelled by computer, such that it will be possible to predict ways in which different plantings or walls might lower the air pollution. In parallel we will determine the length of occupancy of people in the areas so we can assess their likely level of exposure to air pollutants. 空氣污染對城市人群的健康曝露有著重要的影響。香港擁擠的城市環境使人們更容易受到道路車輛產生的顆粒物及其他氣體污染物的影響。因此，空氣污染被認為是非傳染性疾病患者的數量迅速增加的主要原因，并且是香港衛生保健系統的最大挑戰之一。本項研究將探討人在路邊環境中的潛在風險，包括敏感人群如老人和小孩有大量停留時間的路邊休憩及游樂場。該項目將監測氣體污染物及顆粒物的濃度在微尺度空間的分布，并通過模型擬合其分布特征。同時，我們將分析人群的時間空間分布來更加完善的評估人群在路邊的空氣污染物曝露水平。

11304915.label: Realisation of objectives
11304915.value: The first objective was only 90% met because a shifting focus to particles rather than gases, but the controlling variable were thoroughly investigated. Objective 1. An original objective of the project was to determine the concentrations and controlling variables on carbon monoxide/dioxide, black carbon and concentration of particulate matter in sitting-out and roadside playgrounds areas with different characteristics. This was met overall, but we increasingly focussed on particulate material as the project progressed, particularly in the published output as this was most relevant to health impacts. The overwhelming importance of road emissions, distance, wind direction and speed studied in this work and treated in some detail in two published papers as attached: Xing, Y., & Brimblecombe, P. (2018). Dispersion of traffic derived air pollutants into urban parks. Science of The Total Environment, 622–623, 576–583. and Xing, Y., & Brimblecombe, P. (2019a). Role of vegetation in deposition and dispersion of air pollution in urban parks. Atmospheric Environment, 73–83. We developed an equation to describe the near-road dispersion of pollutants in the atmosphere with advection-diffusion equation based on the gradient-transport theory, adapted to dispersion processes under weak wind conditions. This required a modified Bessel function of the second kind of order zero to account for eddy dispersion along the direction of the wind. The work suggested that a buffer zone of some 15-25 m was required to dilute the pollutants to half their roadside value, which was in line with the HK government planning standards and guidelines for parks with active users. However, we believe this might readily be extended to parks where the elderly sit or children play (Xing & Brimblecombe, 2018). The most fundamental observations in this project is to reinforce the notion that the interiors of parks less polluted than the surroundings. The cleaner air within parks justifies the metaphor that they are the lungs of cities, but our studies suggest that improvements in air quality in the park core arise through dispersion processes, while deposition to the vegetation plays a minor role. We nevertheless examined the impact of vegetation, especially stands of trees in controlling air pollution in public spaces (Xing & Brimblecombe, 2019a), given the long historical consideration given to their importance. Field measurements provided evidence that trees played little role in decreasing air pollutant along transects in - black carbon (typically from traffic) was measured at pedestrian level along the transects and showed that he concentrations along a leafy avenue, in Tai Hang Tung Recreation Ground, were mostly higher than that in open recreation fields. It is our assertion that we can no longer assume that the presence of trees means air quality in near-road parks will be greatly improved. The role of deposition to foliage often appears overstated in many writings and this notion appears to hinder improved park design and the adoption of horticultural concepts that minimize exposure to air pollutants. A manuscript (Trees and parks as the “lungs of cities”) on this critical issue is under preparation for Urban Forestry & Urban Greening. Wider understanding of the dispersion of air pollutants into parks can contribute to park designs which reduce user exposure. The role of traffic, especially seminal role of nearby bus stops was investigated in the attached paper Xing, Y., Brimblecombe, P., & Ning, Z. (2019a), “Fine-scale spatial structure of air pollutant concentrations along bus routes”, Science of the Total Environment, 658, 1–7 as later as a more general park related process in Xing, Y., & Brimblecombe, P. (2019b) “Traffic derived noise, air pollution and urban park design” Urban Design International. Objective 2. We examined the relationship between pollutant concentrations and temporal variation at fixed monitoring stations and sitting-out areas/roadside playgrounds. There is a strong positive correlation (r = 0.91, p < 0.01) between PM2.5 concentrations within the parks and from EPD stations. It partially supports the statement raised by Lam et al. (2005) that air quality in urban parks is determined by the ambient concentrations. There are differences between measurements from the parks with varied sizes and the regression with observations in the larger parks. This is especially evident in measurements from Mong Kok district, which hints at the effect of park characteristics or local ventilation. Most of the PM2.5 concentrations measured in the larger parks were higher than the corresponding ambient values. This is probably related to the discrepancy in measurement technique; HKEPD adopts gravimetric measurement while the monitor we used here applies light scattering technology to determine real-time concentrations. The increases may also hint at the imprint left by the nearby traffic emissions. Nevertheless, PM2.5 is a typical regional pollutant, therefore it is expected that its concentrations within parks are largely controlled by ambient levels. However, pollutants which mainly arise from local sources, such as black carbon, may have different profiles within urban parks, so there is an improvement of air quality in a number of urban parks as shown in PM2.5 and BC measurements indicating that levels are lower within the parks than roadside values. Objective 3. We undertook extensive modelling using ENVI-MET to assess the spatial and temporal distribution of air pollutants within public spaces that include sitting-out areas and roadside playgrounds in Sha Tin Park and Sham Shui Po Park. The models were tested against mobile measurements made in the parks with the outputs for Sha Tin Park from ENVI-MET under a north wind show a satisfactory agreement with our observations; r = 0.89, FB = 0.19, NMSE = 0.18 and FAC2 = 0.77. This suggests the ENVI-MET simulations to be acceptable in mapping the distribution of air pollutants in the parks. The work is under review in the MS attached (Xing, Y., & Brimblecombe, P. (2019c). Urban park layout and exposure to air pollutants. Landscape and Urban Planning). This work identified differences between air pollutants along the brored and in the park core. Objective 4. We have estimated integrated exposure of occupants of recreational areas to air pollutants in two Hong Kong parks (Xing & Brimblecombe, 2019c). The distribution of park users is strongly influenced by park design, so despite our view that pollutants are not substantially removed by vegetation trees, shrubs and flower beds these define readily accessible regions in the parks. Other facilities (i.e. play equipment, exercises spaces) further determine the spatial and temporal variation in user distribution and their exposure to air pollution. We investigated diurnal and weekly user distribution and showed that in Sha Tin Park, the near-road areas are covered with trees creates a buffer zone. Thus where pollution concentrations are high areas are less accessible. By contrast in Sham Shui Po Park, the trees not only fail to reduce the area with high pollutant concentrations, but also limit the size of the low pollution zone. Over 40% of park users stayed within the high and medium-high pollutant zones in the morning and even more late afternoon. Facilities for intense recreation (i.e. children’s playground, elderly fitness corner and jogging track) bring sensitive population into the highly polluted areas close to the West Kowloon Corridor. The way in which demographic distribution affects exposure has been further explored in a MS (Xing, Y., & Brimblecombe, P. 2019b “Traffic derived noise, air pollution and urban park design”) under review for Urban Design International.

11304915.value: Xing, Y., & Brimblecombe, P. (2018). Dispersion of traffic derived air pollutants into urban parks: Traffic derived air pollutants are readily detected in urban parks. Measurements suggest a rapid decay of pollutants from roadside into parks. Pollutant gradients in parks are explored using an analytical dispersion equation. Traffic derived pollutants halve after ~ 17 m from the road edge. Future park design should emphasise a separation between park interiors and roads. Xing, Y., Brimblecombe, P., & Ning, Z. (2019a). Fine-scale spatial structure of air pollutant concentrations along bus routes: Fourier transforms reveal patterns of air pollutants related to bus stop spacing. Acceleration of buses explains sawtooth concentration profiles. High concentrations just after bus stops may imply optimum siting. Xing, Y., & Brimblecombe, P. (2019a). Role of vegetation in deposition and dispersion of air pollution in urban parks: Pollutant deposition to vegetation plays little role in improving park air quality. Suppression of dispersion by vegetation increases pollutant concentrations in parks. Pollutant decrease from road to park core largely arises from dispersion. Vegetation layout can encourage parks users to avoid polluted boundaries. Only a minimal air purification service is provided by small urban parks. Xing, Y., & Brimblecombe, P. (2019b) Traffic derived noise, air pollution and urban park design: Heterogeneous air pollution in urban parks leads to difference in user exposure and Xing, Y., & Brimblecombe, P. (2019c): Urban park layout and exposure to air pollutants: Heterogeneous pollutant distribution in parks leads to difference in user exposure.. Distribution of occupants observed in parks is strongly influenced by park layouts. Park design affects distribution of pollutants and occupants thus controls exposure A hybrid approach introduced here can be used for optimizing park design. Optimised park design should consider distribution of pollutants and occupants Xing, Y., Brimblecombe, P., Wang, S., & Zhang, A. (2019b). Tree distribution, morphology and modelled air pollution in urban parks: Tall trees tended to have little influence on airflow at the pedestrian level, which means they seem appropriate for small urban parks where wide barriers are not applicable and rapid ventilation should be encouraged. Tee distribution altered the airflow and pollutant dispersion in parks. Our study provides clues for thoughtful planting strategies which can optimise air quality in urban parks.

11304915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304915.value: Improved air quality and noise levels was measured in small urban parks in Hong Kong. This mostly arose from the dilution of traffic derived air pollutants from nearby roads. Despite the commonly held notion that trees filter out the air pollutants the affect is very small and in some cases trees slow down air flow and reduce dispersion of air pollutant. Walls may be more effective in reducing pollutant concentrations close to roads, but trees may constrain areas occupied by park users and could thus encourage users to use the less polluted park core. Typically traffic derived pollutants halve in less than 20 m from the road edge, but some Hong Kong parks are too small to take advantage of this. Future park design should emphasise a separation between park interiors and roads and related bus stops. This work can also be applied to air pollution in school yards close to roads.

11305715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305715.value: After the severe and prolonged snowstorms in South China in January 2008, several extreme cold spells hit different parts of the Northern Hemisphere in the six winters between 2008/09 and 2013/14. Because the intensity and duration of these cold spells were exceptional in the past few decades, more research should be devoted to understanding the underlying physical mechanisms of cold extremes under a changing climate in order to better predict their occurrence in the future. In East Asia, the occurrence and persistence of extreme cold spells are closely related to an anomalous East Asian winter monsoon. These cold spells are preceded by blocking events near the Ural Mountains and the western Pacific. The occurrence of blocking events is linked with low-frequency atmospheric oscillations, such as the North Atlantic Oscillation and the El Niño/Southern Oscillation. Estimations of future Ural and western Pacific blocking frequency and characteristics are crucial for projecting change in the East Asian winter monsoon. Since 1990, a significant winter cooling trend has occurred in the midlatitudes, including western Siberia, where cold air activity in East Asia originates. Simultaneously, a pronounced warming trend has been observed over the polar region accompanying the reduction of Arctic sea ice, which is known as the Arctic amplification. Arctic amplification has thus occurred alongside cold midlatitude winters in recent years, in contrast to cold winters in earlier periods. Under a global warming trend, Arctic amplification may exert an impact on the large-scale teleconnections of the East Asian winter monsoon with blocking in the midlatitudes, but the underlying mechanisms are not yet fully understood. One area of particular concern is the effect that climate change and the substantial reduction of Arctic sea ice might have on the winter monsoon circulation over East Asia. How the East Asian winter monsoon will respond to a warmer planet is not totally clear. One possibility is that anomalous blocking events (frequency, location, intensity, duration) due to Arctic amplification and sea ice loss may enhance extreme cold spells, but the mechanisms potentially involved in such changes are still under discussion. For example, the Hong Kong Observatory recorded 24 consecutive cold days from 24 January to 16 February 2008, which is the longest cold spell since 1968. Due to the huge economic loss this prolonged cold spell caused in South China, it is important to better prepare for the impact of cold extremes under the global warming trend. 自从 中国南方2008 雪灾以后，北半球的不同区域在2008-2013年的6个冬季发生了 许多极端寒冷天气袭击 。由于这些寒冷天气的强度和持续时间在过去的几十年里非常罕见，所以为了更好地预测未来寒潮发生情况，我们应该致力于了解不断变化的极端寒冷物理机制。在东亚，极端寒冷天气的出现和持续性与一个异常东亚冬季风有密切的关系。这些寒冷天气与前期的乌拉尔山脉和西太平洋的阻塞活动有关。阻塞的发生事件与低频大气振荡，如北大西洋联涛动和厄尔尼诺/南方涛动。有效地评估未来乌拉尔山及其以西的阻塞和太平洋阻断频率和特性, 对在东亚冬季风的未来展望是非常关键。 自1990年以来， 中纬度地区经历了显著冬季降温趋势 ，其中包括西伯利亚西部—— 东亚地区冷空气活动起源地。同时，伴随北极海冰减少，极地地区观察明显的变暖趋势，这被称为北极冰放大效应。相比早前寒冷冬季而言，北极冰减少导致 中纬度寒冷冬季发生扩增 。在全球气候变暖的趋势，北极北极冰放大效应可能通过影响阻塞和冬季风环流对东亚寒潮起到遥相关作用， 但物理机制还没有完全理解。特别值得关注的一个领域是 ，气候变化和持续减少北极海冰如何影响东亚冬季风环流。东亚冬季风在全球变暖的背景下如何响应 并不完全清楚。一种可能性是，，由于北极冰放大效应和海冰减少可能增加的异常阻塞事件（频率，位置，强度，持续时间）而导致极端寒冷天气，但机制仍不确定。例如，香港天文台录得从2008年1月24日到2月16 日的24次连续低温日数 ，这是自1968年以来最长时间的寒流。所以由于寒流导致中国南方巨大经济 损失，有必要研究全球气候变暖趋势下极端寒冷事件。

11305715.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305715.value: We have found the remarkable Link between Projected Uncertainties of Arctic Sea-Ice Decline and Winter Eurasian Climate, the direct and indirect ENSO modulation of winter temperature over the Asian–Pacific–American region. We also explained why the global average of surface air temperature in 2015/16 winter broke the warmest record during a strong El Niño event. This was closely related to the remarkable phase transition of the Arctic Oscillation (AO), which can be explained by stratosphere‐troposphere interactions. First, the quasi‐biennial oscillation changed to its westerly phase in summer 2015 and the stratospheric polar vortex was stronger in early to midwinter 2015/2016. As blocking did not occur in December, the associated downward propagation signal resulted in a strongly positive AO in late December 2015. Second, after late December, the positive phase of Pacific‐North America pattern became apparent in El Niño event, which strengthened the Aleutian anticyclone in the stratosphere. In addition, an equivalent barotropic (“blocking”) anticyclone was established in the troposphere over Asia. The coexistence of blocking over Asia and North America characterized the negative AO and a strong zonal wave number 2 pattern. Due to stronger zonal wave number 2 signals from the troposphere, the stronger stratospheric polar vortex was elongated, with two cyclonic centers over Asia and the North Atlantic in January. The resultant southward displacement of polar vortices was followed by rare snowfall in the subtropical region of East Asia and a heavy snowstorm on the East Coast of the United States. We could identify that the projected uncertainty of the pan-Arctic sea-ice concentration (SIC) is strongly coupled with the Eurasian circulation in the boreal winter (December-March; DJFM), based on a singular value decomposition (SVD) analysis of the forced response of 11 CMIP5 models. In the models showing a stronger sea-ice decline, the Polar cell becomes weaker and there is an anomalous increase in the sea level pressure (SLP) along 60°N, including the Urals-Siberia region and the Iceland low region. We have trained 2 undergraduate students (Wang Li kang, Tong Wing yan), published 9 SCI papers and 2 SCIE papers.

11305715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305715.value: It is hypothesized that the long-term variation of the EAWM (East Asian Winter Monsoon) is related to Urals and western Pacific blockings. The occurrence of Urals and western Pacific blockings is affected by the Sea Surface temperature (SST) over the Atlantic Ocean and the Pacific Ocean, respectively. Under Arctic Warming, the meridional temperature gradient between the high- and midlatitudes is reduced and an anticyclonic anomaly forms over the polar region. If it enhances the blocking frequency over the Urals and the western Pacific, it will strengthen the EAWM via blocking–EAWM teleconnections, as opposed to the weakened land–sea thermal contrast under global warming.

11305915.label: Project Objectives
11305915.value: Synthesize a class of shape-persistent aromatic carboxylic acid molecules functionalized with thiol groups. These novel carboxylic acid molecules will serve as building blocks for forming MOFs with metal salts (e.g., the chemically hard Zr(IV) ions), and thus will be designed to have rigid geometries (e.g., as linear, rod-like linkers). Moreover, different substituents can be installed around the thiol group, so as to modify the electronic and steric properties of the thiol function, and to probe the impact on the catalytic activity. Framework syntheses. Crystallization with chemically hard metal ions, e.g., Zr(IV), to construct the targeted porous metal-organic frameworks. The standard and highly effectively solvothermal synthesis and diffusion techniques will be employed. Catalysis studies. Diffuse potentially catalytic metal salts as procatalysts into the channels, and study the catalytic activities within the porous framework. We focus on group VIII elements of Ru, Rh, Pd and Ir, and plan to achieve highly recyclable, broad-scope catalysis in the metallated solid state frameworks. In addition, we will also target enantioselective catalytic processes using framework systems based on the proposed homochiral linkers.

11305915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305915.value: “Too many cooks spoil the soup” captures the issue we aim to address herein concerning the notoriously poisonous effects thiol molecules impose on many transition metal catalysts. Such poisoning primarily arises from the strong and intractable thiol-metal interactions that effectively entrap the metal center and seal off the coordination sphere and suppress the bonding lability that is crucial for the catalytic process. Notice that such entrapment most readily forms in the setting of a solution environment where the thiol groups can freely approach the metal center to fully cut it off from the catalytic cycle. By contrast, such poisoning from the thiol donors can be eliminated in the setting of a rigid framework, where the thiol groups are confined to be too far apart to fully bond around the Pd center—the sulfur atoms therefore would not block off the catalytic steps as in the solution case. On the other hand, the use of such dangling, isolated thiol groups to anchor Pd atoms serves to turn the intractable Pd-S bond on its head, as the very strength of the Pd-S bond would prevent the leaching of Pd species from the host framework, and to create more stable and recyclable solid-state catalysts. Based on this dangling effect recently discovered in our laboratory, we here propose to further explore thiol groups not only as robust anchors for catalytically active metal centers within solid state framework, but also as a potentially effective ligand system for uncovering novel reactivities. Specifically, we propose novel molecules for constructing the host networks, so as to provide the medium in which to improve the catalytic activity. For this we propose to systematically modulate the electronic conditions around as well as the spacing among the thiol groups. We also propose to implant the thiol donors in a chiral environment so as to provide for enantioselective transformations of great relevance to pharmaceutical industries.

11305915.label: Realisation of objectives
11305915.value: The realization of objects 1 and 2, regarding the synthesis of thiol-equipped, shape-persistent aromatic carboxylic acid molecules and the construction of porous metal-organic frameworks, was highlighted by papers No. 2 and No. 5 attached. Therein, we report breakthrough in the synthesis of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) extensively equipped with thiol groups. In line with the stated objectives of this project, the main motivation arises from the versatile reactivity of the thiol function, which imparts to the porous host unique potentials in metal-uptake, catalytic and electronic properties. Thiol-equipped molecules for MOF construction, however, remains challenging to make, because of the lack of efficient, wide-scope synthetic protocols. Utilizing nucleophilic substitution between benzyl thiol and aromatic halides, and AlCl3-promoted deprotection of the resultant benzyl thioether, we succeeded in attaching the thiol groups onto the carboxylate linker backbones in a dense array. The tackling of objective 3, i.e., concerning catalysis applications was explicitly addressed by papers No.2, No. 5 and No. 8. Specifically, the thiol groups as described in papers No. 2 and 5 were used to effectively take up palladium(II) ions from solutions to allow for comparative studies on catalytic activities, and to help elucidate how the spatial configuration of the thiol groups can be engineered to impact the performance of heterogeneous catalysis in the solid state. The system in No.5, due to its dense thiol arrays in this Zr(IV)-based MOF matrix, impart superior palladium(II) uptake capacities, to offer surprisingly high catalytic activities in Suzuki coupling reactions, with the distinct advantages arsing from the leach-free, truly heterogeneous nature of the solid catalyst. In paper 8, we also explore the inexpensive, widely available cobalt as the catalytic agent anchored in one of ours robust Zr-based MOF (Zr-DMBD) functionalized with self-standing thiol (−SH) groups. The catalytic power of this well-defined Co-thiolate solid state catalyst is showcased in the remarkable capability of photocatalytically converting CO2 to CO--with high efficiency and selectivity under visible-light irradiation in a water-containing system.

11305915.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305915.value: As mentioned above, the AlCl3-promoted deprotection of the resultant benzyl thioether, allows for attaching the thiol groups onto the carboxylate linker backbones in a dense array. The widened access of thiol-equipped MOFs facilitates in-depth exploration of open framework sulfur chemistry, allowing for facile oxidative treatment (to form -SO3H functions for acid catalysis; paper 2), and achieving, for instance, fast removal of Hg below the drinking limit of 2 ppb (paper 5). The dense thiol arrays in this Zr(IV)-based MOF matrix also impart superior palladium(II) uptake capacities, offering surprisingly high catalytic activities in Suzuki coupling reactions, with the distinct advantages arsing from the leach-free, truly heterogeneous nature of the solid catalyst. In paper 8, we also explore the inexpensive, widely available cobalt as the catalytic agent anchored in one of ours robust Zr-based MOF (Zr-DMBD) functionalized with self-standing thiol (−SH) groups. The catalytic power of this well-defined Co-thiolate solid state catalyst is showcased in the remarkable capability of photocatalytically converting CO2 to CO--with high efficiency and selectivity under visible-light irradiation in a water-containing system. The turnover number (TON) and selectivity reach as high as 97941 and 98%, respectively. The fundamental exploration of this project has delightfully lent itself to the potential topical application of using solar energy to convert CO2 into valuable fuels or chemicals as a powerful solution to the urgent energy and environmental issues. Alogn hte line of energy applications, Paper 7, in collaboration with Professors Zonglong Zhu and Alex K.-Y. Jen at this University, utilizes the thiol-equipped MOFs developed in this project for simultaneously improving operational stability and minimize lead leakage for efficient perovskite solar cells. In pursuing the catalytic applications of the MOF materials, we have also extensively tackled the two central issues: stability and environmentally friendly, green assembly of MOF solids. Papers No. 3-6 represent significant advances along these directions. For example, paper No. 6 simply uses water as the sole solvent to form a robust microporous metal-organic framework (MOF, CityU-7) featuring metal ions being simultaneously bonded to the carboxyl and thioether donors. The MOF solid is stable in air and can be easily activated by heating, without the need for treatment with organic solvents. Paper No.3 and 9 use thioether groups to flank the carboxyl groups, to achieve MOF priducts found to be exceptionally stable: not only in long-term exposure to air, but also in boiling water and a broad range of pH conditions.

11305915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305915.value: These important advances in stability improvement therefore paves the way for broader application of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as a growing class of porous materials. For example, some of the experimental results point to a new direction of using thiol-equipped MOF materials to anchor various metal ions, so as to generate versatile and economical catalysts for photochemical applications (e.g., reduction of CO2 to CO), and for achieving enantioselective catalytic activity (this latter part is being considered as a new GRF project). We will also explore various spatial configurations of the mercaptan groups within the MOF matrix, in order to further elucidate the catalytic processes, and to optimize the metal-sulfur interaction for better catalytic performances.

11306115.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11306115.value: 噪聲驅動的非彈性粒子系統動態

11306115.label: Project Objectives
11306115.value: Develop a general framework in which discrete particles are driven by noise, experience dissipate collisions with other particles and boundaries and experience spring or body forces. We will develop boundary conditions that include both random and deterministic energy input. Develop an ultra-weak formulation to solve these problems by using the dual of the Fokker-Planck equation. This formulation will be sufficiently general to admit all of the various boundary conditions and forces in our framework. Theoretically analyze various problems using our ultra-weak formulation and determine for what types of systems we can obtain theoretical properties such as existence, uniqueness and boundedness of statistically steady states. Use our ultra-weak approach to develop an efficient numerical method to obtain the solutions to these problems. Then use the numerical method to compute the principal quantities of interest for the problems contained within our framework. The simplest noiseless problem that can exhibit degenerate transitions and can have an unbounded number of multiple stable solutions is that of two freely moving inelastic particles moving between walls that deterministically add energy when a collision occurs. We will analyze how noise affects this systems using our theoretical and numerical tools.

11306115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306115.value: We will investigate the problem of noise-driven particles that experience dissipative collisions with other particles and boundaries. Even in the absence of noise, such systems can exhibit extremely rich dynamics including highly degenerate bifurcation structures and non-uniqueness of solutions. We will formulate a general framework that allows us to study the dynamics in a number of canonical regimes. This will allow us to study systems in which the particles are attached to springs and experience body forces. Moreover, during collisions with boundaries particles experience energy input that can either be deterministic or random. For technical reasons explained in the proposal, we will study these systems by using an ultra-weak formulation involving the dual Fokker-Planck equation. This system presents a number of challenges, because it contains complicated non-local boundary conditions. Nevertheless, by considering sets of local problems we will develop methods that can determine a number of theoretical properties of the problem. This approach will also allow us to develop a particularly efficient numerical method for obtaining the solution. Using these ideas we will analyze particles systems and pay particular attention to determine how noise affects systems with highly degenerate dynamics. 我們將調查噪聲驅動粒子經歷耗散碰撞與其他粒子和邊界問題。即使在沒有噪聲的，這種系統可表現出極其豐富動力學包括高度簡並分叉結構和解決方案的非唯一性。我們將制定一個總體框架，使我們能夠學習的動力在一些規範制度。這將允許我們研究，其中顆粒附著到彈簧和經驗體積力系統。此外，在碰撞粒子邊界經歷能量輸入，它們可以是確定的或隨機的。由於技術原因，在提案中解釋的，我們將通過使用超弱形式涉及雙Fokker-Planck方程研究這些系統。本系統提出了一些挑戰，因為它包含了複雜的非局部邊界條件。不過，考慮套對當地問題，我們將開發一個可確定若干問題的理論性的方法。這種方法也使我們能夠開發獲得解決方案特別有效的數值方法。使用這些想法，我們將分析的粒子系統，並特別注意，以確定如何噪音的影響具有高度退化的動力系統。

11306115.label: Realisation of objectives
11306115.value: The project ran extremely successfully and all of the objectives were achieved. The project was challenging because of the general framework that we were aiming to develop. However, by using an ultra-weak formulation we were able to develop a dual Fokker-Planck system that can treat a broad range of boundary conditions and external forcing. In particular, we were able to study stochastic elasto-plastic problems and obstacle problems with noise. Stochastic elasto-plastic problems are challenging because they involve transitions between elastic and plastic states. On the other hand, the main challenge associated with obstacle problems arise from the discrete nature of the impulses that occur as a result of collisions with the obstacle. The formulation that we adopted involved the use of stochastic processes satisfying variational inequalities. Using this framework, we had to develop numerical techniques to solve equations with non-standard boundary conditions. In considering the optimal stopping and optimal control problem we also had to combine an approach similar to that described above with an algorithm to find the optimal solution. In order to perform the optimisation step robustly and accurately we adopted an approach based on Howard's algorithm. This worked very well and allowed us to compute quantities associated with both optimal stopping and optimal control in an efficient and accurate manner. We were also able to develop some of our ideas related to partial differential equations to obtain results for a special class of coupled reaction-diffusion equations in which the reaction terms are degenerate. We were able to show that there are a surprising number of features that are present in such systems. We were also able to develop simple explicit conditions that ensure various types of solutions. This also allowed us to generate examples that have exact solutions. In a similar vein, we derived and asymptotically analysed mass-action models for disease spread that include transient pair formation and dissociation. This provided a new formulation for effective pairing models that have important theoretical advantages over previous models.
