11504515.label: Major findings and research outcome
11504515.value: (1) Live chat use positively affects the perceived interactivity of consumers, thereby increasing their intention to transact. The influence of live chat use on the perceived interactivity of consumers and its effect on one’s intention to transact online are negatively moderated by the trust of consumers in a seller (Kang et al., 2019). (2) Deep community participation among promotion-focused customers significantly increases purchase frequency; however, deep participation has a very different effect among prevention-focused customers (Wu et al., 2019). (3) Coupon promotions have a positive impact on online review ratings, and the strength of this impact varies in reverse of the time delay between purchase and posting online reviews. And this relationship is enhanced when customers have high deal proneness. (Wu et al., 2016, PACIS) (4) Both offline and online peer influence can affect customer purchase decisions, and there is a substitution effect between them (Wu et al., 2016, ICIS). (5) Shoppers’ cognitive, rather than affective, expressions tend to indicate their purchase intentions. The affective expressions (in positive and negative forms) articulated by retailers have a considerable influence on purchase conversion. However, the same is not true for shoppers (Kang et al., 2019). (6) Joining a firm-sponsored online brand community positively influences customer value in terms of purchase frequency. We found that promotion-focused customers purchased more frequently after they joined online brand community but did not find that the purchase frequency of prevention-focused customers decreased significantly after joining online brand community. Most of the information in OBC relating to product appraisals is relatively positive, thus significantly alleviating the effect of negative bias among prevention-focused customers. (Wu et al., 2019)

11504515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11504515.value: Building upon the MISQ publication in 2019 by Ji Wu, Liqiang Huang, and J. Leon Zhao —"Operationalizing regulatory focus in the digital age: evidence from an e-commerce context", future research directions include focusing on product reviews and individual emotional evaluation, research can extend this study by exploring the possibility of identifying RF via the cognitive dimension. Furthermore, research can be extended to marketing science by joint efforts between information systems researchers and marketing researchers. Based on the Information and Management Publication in 2018 by Ji Wu, Shaokun Fan, J. Leon Zhao. Potential future research directions include (1) studies on better measuring community engagement. Researchers can use text mining to identify the discussion topics among customers and then measure community engagement by counting meaningful postings and replies in two-way conversational relation- ships. (2) Studies can collect data from firms that produce and sell other types of products and examine whether our results are generalized. (3) Future studies can address the concerns related to the endogeneity issue of the community engagement variable by conducting lab experiments and measuring community engagement. (4) Checking for generalizability of our results across different forms of OBCs would be an interesting addition to this study.

11504515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11504515.value: By triangulating information-processing theories, process design and mobile analytics, this project offers managerial insights as well as process customization mechanisms for e-commerce firms to increase sales revenues in an increasingly mobile-centric world. In addition, this project contributes to the accumulation of knowledge and e-commerce practice by finding out the ways in which consumers process product review information in a m-commerce context in ways that differ from web commerce and design a personalized m-commerce processes to facilitate consumer purchase decisions. Also, this research project demonstrates the value of integrating behavioral research, econometric analysis, and design science in order to generate broader and deeper impacts.

11504815.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11504815.value: 线上社交网络中社会关系强度的动态结构

11504815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11504815.value: With the rapid diffusion of online social networking services, human social interactions have not only been augmented but also become digitally documented. With more and more people shifting their primary social networking activities online, companies are eagerly exploiting the unprecedentedly rich social networking data and harnessing the power of online social networks. However, theoretical understanding about online social connections is limited and most existing studies treat online connections as homogenous binary conduits of influence. Recognizing that online social connections are multi-relational, heterogeneous and dynamic, this research sets to uncover the hidden dynamic structure of heterogeneous social influence tie strength embedded in online social networks. In this research, based on a comprehensive review of the theoretical literature on social networks, we will introduce both a static model and a dynamic model of tie strength structure in online social networks that allow individual, category and dyad-level heterogeneity; and we will propose efficient estimation procedures to uncover the hidden social influence tie strength from observed user activities and online social connections. The proposed theoretical models and estimation methods could generate estimates that are used to extend social network theories in the context of online social networks. Further, an analytical application will be built, which is capable of generating real time social network analytics in online social networking service websites. 伴随线上社交网络的快速发展，人们的社会交互活动在内容上变得更加丰富。越来越多的人将线上社交作为日常社会交往的重要方式。与此同时，线上社会交互的各种行为也以数字化的形式被记录下来。这使得研究人员可以观测到更丰富的互动行为，并从中挖掘线上社交网络关系中的细致结构，有效的帮助公司、用户创造价值。但是，理论方面关于线上社会网络结构的讨论仍处于发展阶段，基于传统社会网络研究的理论模型大多假设线上社会关系在传导社会影响的过程中具有同质性。然而，与一般意义线下局部社会网络不同的是，现实中的线上社会网络往往具有多重关系类型，多重关系强度的复杂性，且网络结构会随社交行为发生内生性的动态变化。这一复杂性使既有的线下社交网络中的模型无法有效分析线上网络结构。本项研究将通过严格的理论分析提出多重关系，多重强度的动态网络结构模型，并利用丰富的社交网络行为数据对网络连接的动态结构进行估计。研究中提出的估计算法将考虑到网络体量和数据丰富性给算法的运算效率提出的挑战，从而更有效的利用大数据的丰富信息内容产生及时的估计结果。研究产生的模型和成果可以适用于一般的线上社会网络行为观测，产生动态的网络结构估计和表述，并可以实现对社交网络营销、传播等商业项目效果的模拟。

rows: To empirically evaluate the net effects of cyber-attacks on economies.
To draw inferences concerning cyber-attacks have long term effects on IT innovations.
To provide suggestions that could be helpful in formulating cyber security policies.

11505015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505015.value: We are in the midst of unprecedented changes following the digitization of economies. Owing to the heavy dependence of business transactions and operations on information technology (IT), safeguarding information technology assets is becoming a primary task for many companies and is being recognized increasingly as a critical factor affecting national security interests. However, while the main focus has been on the negative impact of cyber-attacks, one of the less discussed effects of cyber-attacks is its ability to stimulate IT investments and, as a result, IT innovations. The project proposed here is prompted by the observation that previous studies had focused on the former while ignoring the latter. In this study, we seek to collect cyber-attacks data and IT innovation data to study the impact of cyber-attacks on innovation. This question is important because cyber-attacks have so far been viewed mainly in negative terms. A less explored feature concerns their positive social impact by motivating innovations in information systems. For instance, although they have been under constant cyber-threat, online payment systems continue to evolve and become more practical and safe. Hence, we will first study whether cyber-attacks indeed impact IT innovation. Next we will empirically investigate the net economic effects of cyber-attacks on economic indicators such as stock market sector indices, GDP, etc. Literature has traditionally focused on the impact of information technology assets on market values. Our study will take a different route by examining the role of cyber-attacks on IT innovations; thus introducing yet another perspective into research on IT innovation. We plan to make use of sector-level macro-economic figures to further understand how national IT characteristics affect cyber-attack phenomena. The findings are likely to shed new light on aggregate cyber-attack phenomena; this could lead to useful suggestions for national policymakers as they reformulate national IT and cyber-protection policies.

11505015.label: Realisation of objectives
11505015.value: Data breaches inflict severe damage to a firm’s reputation and customer confidence. To prevent data breaches, firms continuously invest in security measures. However, the effectiveness of security investment is questioned by both practitioners and academics. In this study, utilizing data from multiple sources, we illustrate the bidirectional dynamic relationship between information technologies (IT) investment, security vigilance (or a unifying sense of awareness of security threats), and data breaches using a 5-year panel of 80 U.S.-listed firms. We provide empirical evidence to illustrate that investment in security measures alone is not effective in data protection. Rather, firms’ IT investment must be coupled with heightened security vigilance to reduce data breaches. Our results suggest that firms must reconsider the notion that security performance is a direct outcome of security measures and must take a broader perspective when addressing information-security concerns. Objective 1: To empirically evaluate the net effects of cyber-attacks on economies. For research objective 1, our results demonstrate that the impact of cyberattacks is profound. The first impression of that firms react to cyberattacks only with increased IT security may not be how cyber-attacks affect the economies. In reality, the net effects are much more complex. Our results support the notion that firms react to security breaches by going beyond security investment and investing more in IT, and that security-vigilant firms are more inclined to do so. Moreover, the actions taken by firms will affect future cyber-attacks, and that firms also increase IT investment, and security-vigilant firms can effectively rely on IT solutions to combat data breaches. Therefore, in addition to focusing on devoting resources to fight cyber-attacks, being security vigilant is also critical. Objective 2: To draw inferences concerning cyber-attacks have long term effects on IT innovations By using a using a 5-year panel dataset of 80 U.S.-listed firms, we show that cyber-attacks actually stimulates IT investment, i.e., when more data breaches are disclosed to the public, breached firms invest more in IT in the following year. The results is in line with some of the anecdotal evidence that we observed. For example, after the high-profile breach in 2013, Target announced it would undergo a massive upgrade of its in-store payment infrastructure to support the use of the more secure Chip-and-PIN credit cards. Objective 3: To provide suggestions that could be helpful in formulating cyber security policies. Our study provides evidence about the importance of considering both IT investment and security vigilance when fighting cyber threats. Firms must revisit the assumption that security performance is a direct consequence of security investment. Our study further suggests that to achieve a better outcome, firms need to consider their security solutions from a wider context. Second, firms must implement IT solutions with a strong emphasis on the implications of security issues. The insights are especially relevant given that practitioners have stated that firms often do not consider security beyond the context of traditional security functions and that misalignment between IT and security solutions often leaves firms poorly protected. Perhaps most importantly, pertaining to the issues of cyber-attacks, bridging the gaps about variances in perspectives in an organization is perhaps the most critical first step to ensure good security performance. This study findings serve to highlight the importance of implementing such a practice.

11505015.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505015.value: We use the organizational-learning theory (OLT) and resource-based view (RBV) as theoretical lenses to illustrate the bidirectional dynamic relationship between information technologies (IT) investment. We find that data breaches stimulate IT investment. Interestingly, we find no such relationship between data breaches and security investment. The OLT perspective reveals that firms adjust security strategy dynamically and that such effort is critical in addressing the security issues. Facing data breaches, firms reevaluate their IT effort, we also find that security vigilance moderates the interrelationship between data breaches and IT investment. With heightened security vigilance, firms with more IT investment are more effective to curb data breaches. Interestingly, we do not find that security vigilance plays a role between data breaches and security investment. Our work makes several important contributions to the growing list of information security literature. First, by using OLT and RBV, this note provides theoretical explanations of the interrelationship between data breaches and IT investment. Second, our work is the first to show the interrelationship between IT investment and data breaches, revealing that security performance is much more complex than has been acknowledged in the prior literature. Moreover, the finding that security vigilance moderates IT investment and not security investment represents a key novel finding that has not been reported in the literature. In terms of managerial insights. First, we show that it is important not to ignore “IT” when formulating information-security solutions. Although considered as a strategic component in IT governance framework, our results suggest that the consideration of information security must permeate all facets of IT solutions. More importantly, our findings reinforce the notion that security vigilance is critical to the success of information security, but such capability should be anchored in IT planning, not just security planning.

11505015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505015.value: This work provides us many additional ideas to further study the topic. So far, we have started two additional projects. First, we carried out a follow-up study and further scrutinized IT innovations in terms of IT governance and IT material weakness. The eventual objective of this study is to understand the connections between IT governance, IT material weakness, and cyber-attacks. We also have another preliminary study that looks at how regulation (anti-phishing laws) affects IT and security investment for firms.

11505015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505015.value: When addressing cyber-security threats, it is not enough for firms just to consider typical security measures such as firewall, intrusion detection systems. Firms need to consider the overall IT implementation. In addition, maintaining a vigilant mindset is critical. This study finds that investing in security alone is not enough to prevent future attacks. Instead, firms that rely on IT investment and have a vigilant mindset actually perform better.

11505115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505115.value: This proposal seeks to amend the research on both punishment and trust by investigating the dynamic relationship between the two. Trust acts like social glue, binding organizational and interpersonal relationships. Although punishment is an important and common event in a variety of organizational and social contexts, it can create a trust dilemma by pitting mercy against justice (or benevolence against integrity). On the one hand, punishing transgressions or delinquency helps discipline workforce and restore justice, but it has clear negative implications on employees who are punished. In addition, it can also create a cruel and harsh atmosphere for observers. On the other hand, although mercy and forgiveness show sympathy and humanity, letting transgressions go unpunished (or under-punished) can appear both unfair and unjust. Thus, the current proposal investigates an important outcome – interpersonal trust – of different resolutions of the punishment dilemma. In particular, we focus on the effects of punishment on observers to investigate how punishment may enhance or decrease observers’ trust because of their judgments of punishers’ intentions. Because punishers have to choose between two valid moral values (e.g., benevolence vs. integrity), observers often infer punishers’ intentions by judging how they honor or respect these values. We suggest that observers’ trust of punishers is a primarily function of the magnitude of their punishment and transgressors’ deservingness. When a transgression or delinquency deserves to be punished, punishment should occur, and observers are more likely to judge punishers as having integrity and being trustworthy. When a transgression or delinquency does not entirely deserve to be punished, however, observers may trust punishers less because they are more likely to view mercy or forgiveness as benevolent and trustworthy. Thus, whereas severe punishment for more deserving transgressors will increase people’s trust of punishers, inappropriate punishment for less deserving transgressors will reduce their trust. In addition to deservingness and the magnitude of punishment, we also investigate how punishers’ individual characteristics can affect other people’s perceptions of their trustworthiness. In particular, we investigate the effects of punisher’s reputation and (potential) intentions on people’s trust. We suggest that for the same punishing acts, people will trust punishers who have a principled, value-based reputation more than those with pragmatic reputation. In addition, any self-benefitting punishment, even when self-benefits are not intentional, will diminish people’s trust of punishers. We propose three complementary studies to test these propositions and explore the dynamic relationships between punishment and trust. 該研究提案通過研究懲罰和信任的動態關係來補充兩個領域的研究。信任是連接組織以及人際關係的重要因素。儘管處罰是組織和社會中的常見現象，它同時產生了一個信任方面的難題。一方面，雖然懲處違法違規有助於建立組織紀律和公平，它可能會對被懲罰的違規者以及其他的組織成員產生負面影響。另一方面，仁慈和原諒表現了同情心和人道，但是對違法違規不予懲罰或者懲罰過輕會危及到組織的公平和正義。因此，現在的提案研究懲罰和信任之間的難題，特別是不同的懲罰解決方案如何會增強或減弱他人對於懲罰者的信任度。 懲罰者需要在善意和正直之間選擇其一，觀察者通常通過這兩個道德價值觀來推斷懲罰者的意圖。我們認為觀察者對於懲罰者的信任取決於被懲罰者是否應該被懲罰以及懲罰的力度。當被懲罰者應該被懲處，懲罰會增加懲罰者的信任度。當被懲罰者不應當被懲處，懲罰，特別是過度懲罰，會降低懲罰者的信任度。因此，對應當被懲罰者採取大力度的懲罰會增加懲罰者的信任度，但是對於被懲罰者的不當懲罰會降低懲罰者的信任度。 另外，我們同時研究懲罰者的名聲和懲罰意圖會如果影響他人對他們的信任度。我們認為對於同樣的懲罰，他人會更加信任有原則而不是過於務實的懲罰者。此外，自我受益的懲罰，即使收益並非是故意的，會降低懲罰者的信任度。我們提出了三個互補的研究來探索懲罰和信任的動態關係。

11505115.label: Realisation of objectives
11505115.value: We have achieved most of the objectives we planned before. Our original objectives were to 1) theoretically and empirically investigate how resolving the punishment dilemma would influence interpersonal trust; 2) theoretically and empirically investigate how the integrity-benevolence tradeoff in punishment dilemmas may influence people’s trust; and 3) test the effects of contextual factors and punishers’ characteristics on observers’ trust. We conducted three complementary studies to achieve these objectives. Specifically, we suggested that punishment can present a thorny dilemma, pitting mercy against justice (or benevolence against integrity). On the one hand, punishment restores justice and confirms the integrity of a leader and the organization’s system of justice. By not letting transgressions go unpunished (or under-punished), leaders may also appear fair, just, and strong. On the other hand, punishments can create a cruel and harsh atmosphere, one that shuns mercy, forgiveness, sympathy, and humanity. Drawing on this theoretical foundation, we hypothesized that the relationship between punishment and trust would be moderated by punishment severity and perceptions of deservingness. The nature of the interaction is such that either severe punishment for less deserving transgressors or light punishment for more deserving transgressors would reduce observers’ trust of punishers. In addition, we also predicted that punishing a less deserving transgressor would decrease trust with observers’ perceptions of the punisher’s benevolence mediating the effects of over-punishment on trust, and punishing a more deserving transgressor would increase trust with observers’ perceptions of the punisher’s integrity mediating the effects of appropriate punishment on trust. Finally, we also suggested that punishers’ individual characteristics can lead people to judge them as more or less trustworthy. Thus, we predicted that for the same punishing acts, observers would trust altruistic punishers who have a principled, value-based reputation more than self-interested punishers who have a pragmatic reputation. We designed three complementary studies to test our hypotheses. In doing so, our research investigated the important theoretical distinctions between benevolence and integrity and how they influenced post-punishment trust in the punisher. Study 1 used controlled scenarios to show that uninvolved observers trusted leaders who administered large or medium punishment more than leaders who administered no punishment when transgressors deserved punishment. At the same time, large punishment decreased trust more than medium or no punishment for less deserving targets. Study 2’s similar scenarios showed that leaders who administered punishment lost trust when they subsequently received benefits even though it was not clear whether their benefits resulted from their act of punishment. Study 3 provided a behavioral replication of these results. These findings suggest that people trusted punishers more than non-punishers, but only when punishers’ motives were not personal revenge. Although we have achieved most of our original objectives, there are a few remaining issues. First, we assumed in our research that observers who had no direct relationship with either punishers or transgressors. In real organizations, however, observers may have strong relationships with either or both parties. The typical example is punishment within small teams. For example, after a team leader punishes a team member, the leader and the punished member will still likely have to work closely with each other in the same team. In this context, the leader’s punishments can influence both leader-member relations and team culture. One of the reviewers strongly requested that we collect new data to address this issue. Although we finally managed to address it without collecting new data, it remains an important issue for future research. In particular, team-oriented research on punishment and trust would also provide an opportunity to bridge interdisciplinary theories on team dynamics and punishment. Second, although our research suggests that punishment pits benevolence against integrity, our results suggest that people sometimes find it difficult to separate benevolence and integrity (Colquitt et al., 2012). Instead, they may exhibit a halo effect, with highly correlated perceptions of trust, benevolence, and integrity. At the same time, the current studies show that people can distinguish between benevolence and integrity - when transgressors are more deserving of punishment. When punishment was less deserving, however, the effects of integrity and benevolence tended to commingle. This suggests that people do not consistently distinguish these two trusting attributes when they intuitively judge the trustworthiness of leader-punishers. Instead, their perceptions of benevolence and integrity seem more differentially sensitive when punishment is warranted rather than when it is not. This is another important topic worthy of future investigation. Last but not least, the CO-I, Prof. J Keith Murnighan sadly passed away before the project was completed. The PI had to complete the project in the end on his own. As a result, the project might be a little underachieved than originally expected.

11505115.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505115.value: The trade-off between mercy and justice is a classic moral dilemma, particularly for organizational leaders and managers. In three complementary studies, we investigated how resolving the ‘punishment dilemma’ influences interpersonal trust. Study 1's results suggest that the effects of punishment on trust are a joint function of deservingness and punishment magnitude. Although punishing a deserving transgressor increased trust, over-punishing a less deserving transgressor decreased trust. In addition, observers trusted leader-punishers more when transgressors were deserving because they appreciated their integrity. As a result, both moderate and large punishments enhanced trust. For less deserving transgressors, observers trusted leader-punishers less because they questioned both their benevolence and integrity. In particular, they trusted large punishers the least. Study 2’s results suggest that a leader-punisher’s motives affect the relationship between punishment and trust. When a personal benefit followed a punishment, people tended to trust leader-punishers less, even when it was not entirely clear that the benefit resulted from the punishment recommendation. Simply put, people questioned the leader’s integrity when personal benefits subsequently emerged. In contrast, our prediction that a principled reputation would generate more trust than a pragmatic reputation was not supported. Although people tended to rate principled punishers’ benevolence and integrity higher, they did not necessarily trust them more. Finally, Study 3 replicated our previous findings using a behavioral game that allowed participants to enact direct revenge. The results suggest that people who punished were trusted more than people who did not, but only when people punished in a non-self-interested manner (i.e., when revenge was not assured). In other words, people tended to trust altruistic punishers more than self-interested punishers.

11505115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505115.value: First, our investigation focused on observers who had no direct relationship with either punishers or transgressors. In real organizations, however, observers can have strong relationships with either or both parties. For example, after a team leader punishes a team member, the leader and the punished member will still likely have to work closely with each other in the same team. Our current research does not extend to overall trust within a team. However, this is an important topic worthy of future investigation; one reviewer also requested us to collect data to investigate this issue. Second, other organizational factors can also influence employees’ trust toward their leader-punishers. People who have a close relationship with a punished person inside or outside of work are likely to exhibit enhanced sympathy toward the punished person and, as a result, less trust toward the punisher. Similarly, people who have conflicts of interest with a punished person, e.g., direct supervisors or subordinates, are also likely to display biased trust toward either the punisher or the punished person when their interests are affected. Our hope is that future research will investigate additional factors to broaden our understanding of these central team and organizational dynamics.

11505115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505115.value: Our research has important practical implications concerning how managers and leaders can administer punishment without jeopardizing trust in themselves. Punishment is a highly sensitive issue in organizational life. Our research suggests that organizations should carefully consider how, when, and why they administer punishment. In particular, organizations might want to establish clear standards for both deservingness and the magnitude of punishment (e.g., by providing detailed criteria and past examples). In doing so, managers can then rely on objective criteria instead of their intuitive judgments when they decide whether transgressors are deserving of punishment. When they conclude that punishment should be imposed, they should reserve large, harsh punishment only for truly deserving transgressors, as this will not only make other employees view the process as being fair (Treviño, 1992; Treviño & Ball, 1992); they are also likely to increase their trust in their leaders’ integrity. For less deserving transgressors, however, managers might be advised to show more forgiveness and lenience. In particular, they should be warned against using large punishments which can damage other employees’ trust in their benevolence. Instead, punishment for less deserving wrongdoers should tend to be only small or moderate.

11505415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505415.value: Conglomerates (multi-segments firms) have been criticized for diversification discount – conglomerate segments are traded at a discount compared to similar focused firms. However, people still believe that conglomeration can be a solution when firms have difficulty getting outside financing as a new view that conglomerates are ready for a comeback has emerged in the wake of the global financial crisis. Globalization is inevitable and it has significantly increased competitive pressure by facilitating the penetration of foreign rivals into local markets. Understanding how conglomerates behave differently as a response to the intensified competition may provide another chance for conglomerates to be reevaluated. Conglomerate segments should be able to take actions that are not available to single segment firms as a response to intensified competition as they have extra source of inside financing, which is internal capital market in a conglomerate. In other words, some segments can benefit from surplus cash of other divisions in a conglomerate. The project aims to investigate how import competition affects conglomerate segments differently than single segment firms and, hence, to provide a better understanding of comprehensive impact of import competition on domestic markets. While several theories generate predictions on how conglomerate internal capital markets would affect competitive outcomes, the preliminary finding that I obtained suggests further exploration. Additionally, this project will address a related research question: which factors of internal capital markets are indeed important in determining the strategic impact of internal capital markets. As argued by previous studies, relative financial strength of internal capital market should matter. Moreover, the level of diversification and having a financial segment in a conglomerate can generate different competitive outcomes for conglomerate segments. Finally, whether the effect of internal capital markets are derived from efficient resource allocation should be explored. 集团企业（多部門企業）一直因多元化折價 (Diversification Discount) 而受到詬病——相对於類似的專注型企業，集團部門的市場價值往往受到折價。然而，人們仍然認為集团企业的形式解決了公司面臨外部融資困難的問題，從而在全球金融危機復甦階段重新被加以關注和應用。全球化大勢所趨促使海外競爭對手滲入本土市場，加劇了公司的競爭壓力。認識到集團公司如何以不同方式應對日益加劇的市场競爭，将让集团企业有機會進行重新估值。企業集團的額外內部融資，即內部資本市場(Internal Capital Market)，使得集团企业的部門可以採取單一部門的公司所不具備的手段來應對激烈的競爭。換句話而言，集團旗下部門可以受益於其他部门的現金盈餘。 該項目旨在研究相對於單一型企業而言進口導致的競爭如何對企業集團造成不同的影響，並由此有助於更好地理解進口競爭對國內市場造成的全面影響。儘管一些理論推斷集團公司的內部資本市場能夠影響競爭結果，但該項目的基本結果卻顯示這一觀點需要進一步探討。此外，該項目強調了一個相關的研究問題：究竟內部資本市場的什麼因素決定了內部資本市場策略的影響？正如已有文獻的觀點，內部資本市場的相對金融實力對其有影響。除此以外，分散化水平以及在集团企业中擁有一個金融部門會对集团部门产生不同的競爭結果。最後，内部资本市场效应是否源自有效的资源配置值得进一步探讨。

11505515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505515.value: A vector autoregression (VAR) is a simple and common way to model the dynamics of stationary multivariate time series. One can construct VAR models purely based on statistical properties of economic variables without imposing any economic theory, so economists refer to this type of models as the reduced-form VARs. To learn the impacts of a policy change or economic shock on a system of economic variables over time, one has to impose restrictions on the VAR models so that they have economic interpretation. The VARs with economic restrictions are referred to as the structural VARs, and the exogenous policy changes or economic innovations are known as the structural shocks. Usually, structural shocks are not directly observable but are linear transformations of the reduced-from VAR's error terms, which are referred as the reduced-form shocks. Hence, economic restrictions are imposed on VAR models so that the structural shocks can be recovered from the reduced-form shocks. This project focuses on the specification issues of the identification scheme using external instruments developed by Stock and Watson (2012) and Mertens and Ravn (2013). This approach uses variables outside the VAR system as the instruments for the underlying structural shocks. These external instruments have to be correlated with the structural shock of interest but uncorrelated with all other structural shocks. The impacts of the structural shock, known as the impulse response functions, can be then estimated by generalized method of moments (GMM). However, the external instrument approach relies on a crucial normalization assumption, the violation of which can lead to a failure of identification and inconsistent estimators. Also, since the lags of the external instruments are potentially valid instruments, there could be many candidate instruments. If we use many irrelevant instruments in the second stage GMM estimation, then the estimator will have larger finite-sample bias. Moreover, the lag order of the VAR model is also an important parameter. Underestimating the lag order will lead to inconsistent estimates for the impulse response functions, while overestimating the lag order will reduce the estimation efficiency. We propose a unified approach that can test the normalization assumption, select the relevant instruments and determine the lag order simultaneously using a shrinkage estimator. This project will establish the theory for the proposed estimator, investigate the finite-sample properties by simulations, and conduct empirical applications to illustrate the usefulness of the proposed estimator. 向量自回歸模型（VAR）是一種刻畫平穩序列動態變化的簡單常用方法。VAR 模型可以在不施加任何經濟理論的情況下，單憑經濟變數的統計學性質進行構造。經濟學家稱這種模型為簡化形式的VAR。要想瞭解政策變化或經濟衝擊對經濟系統的影響，我們必須在VAR模型上施加約束使其具備經濟解釋，這種VAR被稱為結構VAR，而外生的政策變化或經濟擾動則被稱為結構衝擊。結構衝擊在一般情況下是不能被觀測的，它們是簡化形式衝擊（也就是簡化形式VAR的殘差項）的線性變換。因此，施加經濟約束的目的是為了將結構衝擊從簡化形式衝擊中還原出來。 這個專案主要針對在結構VAR模型中使用外部工具變數（Stock and Watson (2012) and Mertens and Ravn (2013)）的識別問題。這種方法使用VAR系統以外的變數作為識別結構衝擊的工具變數。這些外部工具變數和我們感興趣的目標結構衝擊是相關的，但和其他結構衝擊是不相關的。結構衝擊的影響，也就是所謂的脈衝回應函數，可以通過廣義矩方法（GMM）來估計。但是，這種外部工具變數的方法依賴於一個正規化的假設， 如果這個假設不滿足則會導致模型識別失敗和不一致的估計量。另外，外部工具變數的滯後項也可以作為工具變數，所以可能會有很多被選的工具變數。如果在GMM中使用大量不相干的工具變數，那麼在有限樣本中估計量就會有較大的誤差。還有，VAR模型滯後項的個數也是一個重要的參數。如果這個參數被低估，則脈衝回應函數的估計就是不一致的；如果這個參數被高估，則估計的效率會降低。我們提出了一個統一的框架，這個框架使用壓縮估計的方法可以同時檢驗正規化假設，選擇相關的工具變數，並且決定滯後項的個數。這個項目將為我們提出的估計量構建統計理論，研究其有限樣本中的表現，並運用實證舉例來說明其實用性。

11505515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505515.value: This project develops a new theory for the model selection and statistical inference in analyzing the impacts of an economic shock for a system of time series variables. We consider the estimation of dynamic causal effects using auxiliary variables (i.e., external instruments) and a multivariate time series model (i.e., structural vector-autoregressive model). The model allows the possibility of nonstationary time series, which can complicate the selection and inference problem. We show that the adaptive lasso, a commonly used model selection method, is still able to choose the true model, regardless of the inclusion of nonstationary time series. Also, we provide general conditions under which the statistical inference can be conducted in the standard way without worries about the potential nonstationary time series. We provide an estimator to achieve this objective. We use simulations and empirical applications to justify the usefulness of our method.

11506015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11506015.value: 擬提項目的部分動機是基於最近在中國的一些製造企業的經驗 和學術界的一些最新進展。供應鏈中的不同成員之間的生產，儲存和運送的協調在供應鏈管理中至關重要。在實踐中，供應鏈中的不同階段通常被生產能力約束。通常情況下，產能限制和需求的季節性導致龐大的庫存積壓，這可能會產生過度生產延誤和庫存成本。企業需要實現決策支持系統來協調生產材料流動來減少庫存。 該項目旨在提出新的技術來分析具有能力限制多級供應 鏈，以獲得關於如何實現在企業過程中有效的生產材料的流動的見解。 我們會考慮一個單一產品定期審核具有產能約束的多級庫存系統，其中，從原材料被轉化為最終產品之前要經過多個生產階段。 每個生產階段是受其生產能力的約束，這是由製造機械的產能，人力，其他所需的資源，等等決定的。此外， 兩個連續生產階段之間還有一個固定的生產/運輸提前交貨期。每一個時期最終產品的需求隨機出現。公司的目標是通過優化其庫存補貨/生產的策略儘量減少其期望的總折扣費用，其中包括生產/補貨，庫存和延期交貨成本。 在多級庫存管理的大量文獻中，只有少數文獻考慮能力約束。這些文獻的焦點是對於兩級系統的最優的策略的結構特徵刻畫或者研究對更複雜系統的啟發式算法。由於這個問題的固有的挑戰性， 對於具有能力約束的多級的最優庫存控制/生產的策略結構的刻畫還是未知的。對於這樣一個系統其中最根本的問題是的最優策略的結構是什麼？最優政策的完整描述也可能會減少計算複雜度。然而，即使如果我們有一個完整的刻畫，最優的政策結構可能不容易在現實中實現。因此，制定可實現的啟發式策略和最優策略邊界也是需要的。 不過，最優策略的結構刻畫，不僅提供了評估有效的啟發式和發展一個基準，也有利於我們獲得關於如何開發新的啟發策略和邊界的見解。擬議的項目旨在填補這兩個空白。 這個項目提議包括了初步分析結果連同任務來實現我們的既定 研究目標。在這些初步結果和相關問題技術經驗的基礎上，我們相信能克服所描述的挑戰。

11506215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11506215.value: There is a growing concern about what constitutes a suitable energy source mix for electricity generation. In Hong Kong for example, there is a need to arrive at a new energy mix as the current scheme for the generation of electricity will expire in 2018. The nuclear accident in Fukushima, the need to take steps to combat climate change, and emissions targets are all factors that lend support for an energy transition, and serve as an inducement to countries to reconsider their energy mix for electricity generation. Consequently, there is a need for a general theory on how to design a suitable energy mix. An integrated, interdisciplinary approach is required to properly design such a decision-making framework. Ultimately, the methodology is rooted in economics, in the sense that it requires decision theory. However, a good technical and scientific characterization of each energy source is needed. Notably, it is necessary to consider future characteristics of energy sources since decisions need to be taken in advances, and also because infrastructure decisions are long-term in nature. There is also a lot of uncertainty surrounding issues such as pollution intensity, efficiency of renewables, the cost of natural gas and the reliability of provision. Uncertainty exists with respect to some irreversible environmental thresholds as well, whose crossing would dramatically affect the economies' dynamics: some levels of climate change might reverse ocean currents, some air pollution levels might result in a loss of skilled labor. Therefore, it is a matter of (i) irreversible decisions under (ii) energy source-specific uncertainty and (iii) irreversible environmental thresholds. The objectives of the project are to: • characterize the different sources of energy used for electricity generation in terms of costs (including pollution intensity and the risk of incidents) and benefits. A special emphasis will be placed on the correct way to model the uncertainty surrounding each feature. • properly design irreversible decision theory under energy source-specific uncertainty. • properly account for potentially uncertain environmental thresholds in irreversible decision theory. • provide a general framework that can be used for policy recommendations in the context of energy transition. The general theory could be applied to the specific case of Hong-Kong. Results of this study will be valuable to society in terms of economic policy, and to the scientific community in terms of (i) a new decision theory design that accounts for irreversibility, thresholds and specific uncertainty, and (ii) better understanding and comparisons of the different energy sources using an integrated approach. 如何选择合適的能源組合發電的議題日益受到關注。一個綜合及跨學科性的方法才能正確地設計這樣的決策框架。最終，該方法還是植根於經濟，在這個意義上，它需要決策理論。 然而，我们需要每種能源的良好技術和科學表徵。值得注意的是，有必要考慮能源未來特性，因為需要提前做出決定，而且還因為基礎設施的決定是長期性的。也有不少相关的不確定性問題，如污染強度，可再生能源的效率，天然氣的成本和提供的可靠性。同样對於一些不可逆轉的環境閾值也存在不確定性，其交叉將極大地影響到經濟體的動態：一定程度的氣候變化可能改變洋流，一些空氣污染水平可能會導致熟練勞動力的缺失。因此，它就是一项（ⅰ）不可逆的決定并考虑（ⅱ）能量源特定的不確定性和（iii）不可逆的環境閾值。 該項目的目標是：  表征用於發電的能源不同來源的成本（包括污染強度和事故的風險）和收益。重點是正確模拟相关特征的不確定性。  正確設計在能源特定不確定性下的不可逆轉的決策理論。  正確参考不可逆轉的決策理論中潛在不確定的環境閾值。  提供有关能源转化的總體框架，用於政策性建議。一般的理論可以適用於香港的具體情況。 這項研究的結果在經濟政策方面是有利于社會，在科學领域也是（i）一個新的解释不可逆轉，閾值和特定不確定的決策理論設計，以及（ii）更好地理解和使用綜合方法比較不同能源。

11506415.value: 在营销渠道研究中，由于制造商与经销商之间的相互作用才得以提供产品给终端用户，所以双方的相互依赖是一个非常重要的概念。现有研究表明，相比对称性依赖，不对称性依赖会导致渠道成员关系的非正常非稳定化，也会降低信任度。由于可被强权方压榨剥削以及随时被替换，非对称关系对于渠道中的弱势方尤其不利。 然而，现实中，不对称的渠道关系却大行其道（例如苹果，富士康，沃尔玛与其供应商，丰田与其经销商）， 很难有势均力敌的双方。问题是，身为弱势方，如何去从不平衡关系中获得利益而不是任由强势方摆布？ 本研究致力于关注弱势方的困境，这点在过去的渠道研究中并没有得到太多关注。大多数研究集中于渠道中较强势一方以及他们如何利用权力优势去影响和控制渠道关系。基于权利依赖以及社会网络理论， 本研究致力于探究三个问题：（1）弱势方可以通过自身的网络嵌入作为一种权利的外部来源，进而抵消依赖的不对称性？（2）不同类型的网络嵌入是如何抵消依赖的不对称性？（3）弱势方通过何种策略，才能有效地利用这种由于网络嵌入而带来的潜在权力，并以此影响较强势方？ 这里，我们提出，在新兴市场中弱势方可以通过商业和政府网络嵌入从而获得渠道中的依赖平衡。此外，弱势方如何利用由于网络嵌入带来的潜在权力去平衡渠道依赖性，我们提出了四种可用策略：交易，联盟，替代，上诉，并且比较了它们在不同网络下的作用。为了夯实理论基础，我们同样检验了在不同依赖程度下，商业和政府网络嵌入效果的异变。基于对中国对汽车行业中制造商经销商的问卷调查，本研究不仅加深了对渠道关系中权利依赖的理解，而且对中国中小企业在面对渠道强势方时，如何从长期关系中获得利益提供了重要启示。

11506415.label: Realisation of objectives
11506415.value: 1. To explore the feasible dependence-balancing methods for weaker distributors in channel relationships with dependence asymmetry by extending the dyadic perspective to the network level. For this objective, we conducted extensive literature review and in-depth interviews of managers to explore the feasible dependence-balancing methods for weaker distributors in channel relationships with dependence asymmetry. Prior studies have posited several strategies that can alleviate the disadvantages brought about by their disadvantaged position in the channel relationship. Rossetti and Choi (2005) suggest that disadvantaged players have several options when under pressure from a coercive partner. Taking the dyadic view, prior research has presented several formal mechanisms, such as vertical integration (Palmer et al. 1995; Pennings 1981) and offsetting investments (Heide and John 1988), to balance the dependence between the two partners. These recommended mechanisms are mostly economic arrangements within the relationship to reshape the interdependence structure. However, they may not always be feasible for the dependence-disadvantaged players, because these players usually lack internal resources (e.g., capital and/or human resources) to engage in mergers and large investments. Even a disadvantaged partner with the extra resources to engage in vertical integration or offsetting investments may face the advantaged partner’s counteraction by committing similar investments, which can lead to the ineffectiveness of these solutions. So it is necessary to go beyond the internal economic and polity factors and to consider the interplay between external and internal factors (Stern and Reve, 1980). Researchers working under the network perspective have argued that network resources of interconnected entities can serve as extensions of internal resources (e.g., Lavie 2006; Zhou and Li 2012). As such, the disadvantaged partners may be able to leverage external resources derived from their networks to influence their powerful partners (Bonner et al. 2005). 2. To examine weaker distributors’ embeddedness in (i) business networks and (ii) government networks as power bases to balance the dependence asymmetry with their partners and thereby improve their channel performance and satisfaction. Regarding this object, we theoretically delineate the mechanisms through which the weaker distributors network embeddedness improve their channel performance, and then empirically test the hypotheses. Based on the political economy framework, we posit that a dependence-disadvantaged partner’s embeddedness in business and government networks entices its partner to commit more RSIs, which in turn improve its channel performance; conversely, such an effect is weaker for the dependence-advantaged partner. We collected dyadic survey data of buyer–supplier pairs in consumer product industries in China. In general, the results provide support for our predictions. 3. To delineate the behavioral tactics—exchange, coalition formation, alternatives search, and upward appeal—that mediate the dependence-balancing role of weaker distributors’ embeddedness in (i) business networks and (ii) government networks, respectively. We used the qualitative method to conceptualize the tactics that the weaker distributors use in dependence balancing. We tried using experiments to test the hypotheses, but the results were not very supportive. 4. To investigate the varying role of weaker distributors’ embeddedness in (i) business networks and (ii) government networks under different degrees of dependence asymmetry. We hypothesized and empirically tested the moderating role of dependence asymmetry. We predict that under high dependence asymmetry, a dependence-disadvantaged partner’s embeddedness in the business network will exert a smaller effect, but its embeddedness in the government network will exert a larger effect. We collected dyadic survey data of buyer–supplier pairs in consumer product industries in China. In general, the results provide support for our predictions. 5. To provide important managerial implications for weaker players in marketing channels in China so that they can take advantage of their network connections, to change their disadvantageous position in channel relationships. This research also offers managerial implications. The findings offer special guidance to firms that are more dependent in channel relationships, which are common in developing countries like China. Our findings also offer some guidance to the dependence-advantaged partners in channel relationships.

11506415.label: Major findings and research outcome
11506415.value: Channel relationships with dependence asymmetry, which are especially harmful to partners with dependence disadvantage, abound in developing markets. To help these dependence-disadvantaged parties find feasible solutions for dependence balancing, this project examines network embeddedness and its differential role in enforcing the counterpart's relationship-specific investments (RSIs), thus leading to improved channel performance for both partners. Based on the political economy framework, we posit that a dependence-disadvantaged partner's embeddedness in business and government networks entices its partner to commit more RSIs, which in turn improve its channel performance; conversely, such an effect is weaker for the dependence-advantaged partner. We also predict that under high dependence asymmetry, a dependence-disadvantaged partner's embeddedness in the business network will exert a smaller effect, but its embeddedness in the government network will exert a larger effect. We collected dyadic survey data of buyer–supplier pairs in consumer product industries in China. In general, the results provide support for our predictions. The findings provide theoretical and managerial implications for partners in asymmetric channel relationships in developing markets.

11506415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11506415.value: First, considering the difficulty of collecting dyadic data, we only collected a cross-sectional data of buyer–supplier pairs, which falls short in proving causality and depicting dynamic relationships. Future research are encouraged to use more methods, such as experiments, to establish the causal links among the constructs in our model . Longitudinal data might also be helpful to provide a dynamic perspective on the differential effects of network embeddedness in the imbalanced relationships. Second, we focused on relational embeddedness as a basic description of firms' network embeddedness. Other constructs such as centrality, density, and connectivity also capture the network conditions. Additional research could investigate how these network conditions may affect channel partners' strategies differently in imbalanced relationships. Third, our results also reveal the differential effect of joint dependence on the disadvantaged and advantaged parties. It would be a fruitful direction to investigate the relative effects of joint dependence in asymmetric channel relationships. Fourth, future research may investigate the role of network embeddedness upon other aspects than RSIs .

11506415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11506415.value: Channel relationships with dependence asymmetry, which are especially harmful to partners with dependence disadvantage, abound in developing markets. To help these dependence-disadvantaged parties find feasible solutions for dependence balancing, this project examines network embeddedness and its differential role in enforcing the counterpart's relationship-specific investments (RSIs), thus leading to improved channel performance for both partners. The findings offer special guidance to firms that are more dependent in channel relationships, which are common in developing countries. To avoid being exploited by the less dependent firms, they can actively network with other parties, including business players and government authorities. Compared with other means they may resort to, such as vertical integration and increasing relationship investments, networking does not require many internal resources and thus are more executable. Meanwhile, because of the differential effects of network embeddedness, networking is the strategy useful to the dependence-disadvantaged partner but not the advantaged partner. Moreover, networking with government entities can be more effective when the dependence asymmetry is greater, and thus the more dependent firm can concentrate its resources and efforts more in the government network. However, the effectiveness of business networking is limited, as the effect may be attenuated under high asymmetry.

11506615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11506615.value: Labor has a significant impact on a firm’s financial decisions. Some papers show that firms strategically use more debt to enhance their bargaining position against labor unions, while others argue that strong labor protection increases firms’ operating leverage and leads to a lower debt ratio. In this project, we will extend this literature by recognizing the fact that all these studies treat debt as uniform, ignoring its heterogeneity. Specifically, we will investigate whether and how labor affects a firm’s debt structure choices and how this decision interacts with firms’ leverage choices. We will first examine the relation between labor and a firm’s debt maturity structure. Following the literature, we use unionization as a proxy for labor’s influence. Existing theories suggest different views on the direction of the impact. On the one hand, firms with unionized workers could use short-term debt to strengthen their bargaining power, which suggests a negative relation between unionization and debt maturity. On the other hand, unionization could cause operational inflexibility and increase the likelihood of financial distress. This suggests unionized firms should have incentives to reduce their exposure to liquidity risk by lengthening their debt maturity. Therefore, the net impact of unionization on a firm’s debt maturity structure is a prior uncertain. We will also examine a firm’s choice between private debt and public debt. We hypothesize that unionized firms value the flexibility of debt renegotiation and borrow more privately. Firms could also use strict covenants in private debt contracts as a bargaining tool against labor unions. Moreover, private debt allows firms to maintain information asymmetry with labor unions. We take two approaches to examine the relation between unionization and debt structure. First, we use balance sheet data to construct debt structure measures. With these measures we compare firms that elect to become unionized to those that vote against it. To address the identification concern, we use a regression discontinuity design; we also explore cross-sectional variation in the impact. Our second approach is incremental, focusing on new debt issues. We examine whether a firm starts to rely more on a certain type of debt after firms become unionized. As an extension, we will use the passage of several laws, such as state-level wrongful discharge laws, right-to-work laws, and state repeal of unemployment insurance stoppage provisions, to examine the impact of labor on a firm’s debt structure decision. 勞動力對公司的財務決策有顯著的影響。一些研究顯示，企業會戰略性地使用債務來增加其與工會的談判籌碼。另一些學者則認為，勞動保護會增加企業的經營槓桿，這促使公司選擇較低的負債率。意識到債務結構的多樣性，在這個項目中，我們將調查勞動力如何影響一個公司的債務結構，以及這一選擇與公司資本結構的關聯。 首先，我們將研究勞動力和公司債務期限結構之間的關係。沿用其他學者的方法，我們用工會化程度來衡量勞動力的影響力。現有理論對這一問題有不同的預期。一方面，有工會組織的企業可以使用短期債務來加強他們的談判籌碼，這表明工會化和債務期限應存在負相關關係。另一方面，工會可能導致公司運營的低效率，並提高其財務風險。這表明有工會的企業可能選擇長期債務，以減少他們的流動性風險。因此，工會對一個公司的債務期限結構的淨影響是不確定的。另外，我們也將研究公司如何在私人和公共債務之間選擇。我們推測，有工會的企業會看重債務談判的靈活性，從而選擇更多的私人債務。私人債務合約裏的嚴格契約也可做為公司的有力談判工具。此外，私人債務使公司保持與工會的信息不對稱，而這同樣有利於公司談判。 我們採用兩種方法來檢驗工會和債務結構之間的關係。首先，我們使用資產負債表數據來構建債務結構，然後比較那些同意成立工會的公司和反對成立工會的公司的差別。為了解決內生性的問題，我們使用回歸間斷設計，並探索截面變化。我們的第二個方法著眼於新的債務發行。我們檢查那些成立工會後的企業是否更多地依賴於某種類型的債務。作為一個擴展，我們將會使用一些政策改動來檢查勞動力對企業的債務結構的影響。比如，州立不正當解僱法，勞工就業權保障法，以及失業保險規定等等。

11506615.label: Realisation of objectives
11506615.value: We followed the literature to use unionization as a proxy for labor’s influence. To address the endogeneity issue, we used union elections data and adopt a regression discontinuity design that provides plausibly exogenous variation in unionization. Because election results are not perfectly predictable, close elections that pass or fail by a small margin around the 50% cutoff is a quasi-random event and therefore is unlikely to suffer from confounding selection or omitted variable biases. We collected data from the National labor Relations Board (NLRB) on all union elections that have taken place in the US since 1961. Following Lee and Mas (2012), we merged the NLRB database with COMPUSTAT using company names. This election sample was then matched to financial information from COMPUSTAT and stock returns from CRSP. We obtained debt ownership information from Capital IQ and SEC filings. We found evidence that union election leads to an increase in the use of public debt in the following three years after elections. We then tried to explore the relation between unionization and other corporate policies. We document that in addition to debt structure, unionization also affects firm’s disclosure policies. In particular, unionized firms disclose discretionary news less than other firms do. To establish causality, we employ a regression discontinuity design (RDD) that studies firms experiencing union elections. The evidence suggests that passing union elections causes fewer discretionary news releases. Furthermore, the negative effect of union elections on news releases is only statistically significant for firms in states without right-to-work laws, where unions are arguably more powerful. Moreover, we find that firms increase the amount of negative news releases before union negotiations. Furthermore, this increase is much stronger in states without right-to-work laws. On the other hand, there is no significant change in neutral or positive news releases during the same period. Overall, our results suggest that US managers use a multifaceted news release policy to deal with powerful unions.

11506615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11506615.value: In this project, we examined how labor affects a firm’s debt structure choices and disclosure polices. We found evidence that union election leads to an increase in the use of public debt in the following years after union elections. In addition, we find that US firms use a multifaceted disclosure strategy to deal with strong unions. We find that unionized firms disclose discretionary news less than other firms do, suggesting that they preserve an informational advantage over unions. But shortly before scheduled labor negotiations, firms aggressively promote negative news, presumably to improve their bargaining power and dodge union demands for better employment terms.

11507615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507615.value: Opportunism has been identified as a critical threat to the success of exchange relationships in emerging markets.The massively changing social, political, and economic institutions in emerging markets make opportunistic behaviors pervasive and difficult to detect or punish. Marketing channels literature has paid limited attention to institutional environments that constrain buyer–supplier exchanges, though such institutions are fundamental determinants of transaction costs. Drawing on transaction cost economics and institutional theory, this project examines the confluence of institutional and efficiency views to assess how institutional forces restrain the impact of exchange hazards (i.e., transaction-specific assets and performance ambiguity) on channel opportunism. Legal effectiveness and network importance, two institutional factors, should have differential moderating effects on the relationships between the exchange hazards and opportunism. In particular, this research proposes that the positive effect of TSA on opportunism is attenuated more by legal effectiveness than by network importance. The positive effect of performance ambiguity on opportunism is attenuated more by network importance than by legal effectiveness. In addition, this study proposes that opportunisms has a positive effect on channel disruption and that opportunism has a negative effect on channel members’ knowledge co-creation. This project enriches extant efficiency-based marketing channels literature and demonstrates the importance of integrating macro, legitimacy-based institutional factors with micro features of economic exchanges. The findings of this project will help managers understand how they can leverage macro institutions to suppress partner opportunism in their buyer–supplier relationships in emerging economies.This study also offers valuable implications for public policy makers.

11507615.label: Realisation of objectives
11507615.value: The project has four objectives. Objective 1: To extend previous efficiency-based perspectives on opportunism by taking an institutional view and examining how institutional forces influence partner opportunism. This objective is fully achieved. Studies on marketing channels are conducted largely in developed countries with well-established institutional frameworks. Few have adopted an institutional perspective. However, the profound institutional changes in emerging economies mean that institutions play a critical role in regulating transaction rules and coordinating exchange behaviors. The emerging economies are characterized by massive and rapid changes in their social, political, and economic institutions, as well as pervasive opportunistic behaviors. In this project, we take institutions into account and scrutinize the roles of institutions in curtailing partner opportunism in emerging economies. Using an efficiency-based perspective, such as transaction cost economics (TCE), marketing channels research has devoted great attention to the antecedents of opportunism especially ways to constrain it. However, because interfirm exchanges are embedded in the larger social context, firms must also address their social fitness and institutional legitimacy in emerging economies. This project purposes and empirically tests the main effects and moderating effects of institutions. In particular, the JAMS 2018 paper uncovers the critical influence of formal and informal institutions (i.e., legal effectiveness and networking importance) on the use of governance in deterring opportunism as well as the moderating role of government support on the efficacy of governance mechanism (i.e., contractual and relational governance). The IMM submission examines the effects of institutions and the interaction between institutions and exchange hazards. This institutional view of channel relationship greatly enriches extant efficiency-based channel literature and demonstrates the importance of integrating legitimacy-based institutional factors. Objective 2: To demonstrate the influence of subnational institutions on firm behavior and exchange relationships in China. This objective is fully achieved. In emerging markets, the high costs of obtaining reliable market information, measuring and monitoring a business partner’s performance, and enforcing contracts often lead to opportunistic behaviors. In such markets, an underdeveloped legal system and a pervasive reliance on social networks represent the most salient formal and informal institutional factors respectively. In many emerging countries, even if legal codes and court systems seem well defined, their implementation and enforcement remain problematic. In China for example, despite continuous legal reforms over the past several decades, legal enforceability continues to be a major business hurdle due to intensive government interventions. Emerging economies also possess salient within-country institutional variations, due to their uneven economic development and differential cultural traditions across regions. Therefore, we focus on legal effectiveness and guanxi importance in this project. The findings demonstrate that legal effectiveness mitigates channel members’ opportunism and that guanxi importance was negatively related to buyer opportunism. In addition, legal effectiveness mitigates opportunism through increased use of contractual governance and legal effectiveness mitigates opportunism through increased use of relational governance. Moreover, networking expenditure increases opportunism through reduced use of contractual governance and networking expenditure mitigates opportunism through increased use of relational governance. In summary, this project extends channels literature to the new and challenging context of emerging economies (e.g., China), which offer promising growth opportunities for international marketers. This project exemplifies a way to extend marketing literature into various institutional settings. Objective 3: To examine differential roles of institutional forces in suppressing opportunism due to different exchange hazards. This objective is fully achieved. Given the paucity of institutional research in marketing channels, how legitimacy-based institutional compliance interacts with efficiency-based exchange factors (i.e., transaction specific assets and performance ambiguity) remains unclear. Institutions also interact with efficiency-based factors to affect firm strategies and performance. This project examines the moderating effects of both macro-level institutions (i.e., legal effectiveness and network importance) and micro-level institutions (i.e., contractual and relational governance). The findings of the IMM submission show that supplier TSAs bolster buyer opportunism at low levels of legal effectiveness but inhibit it at high levels of legal effectiveness and that with low legal effectiveness, TSAs are positively related to supplier opportunism. In addition, the positive effect of buyer performance ambiguity on buyer opportunism grows stronger at low levels of guanxi importance and supplier performance ambiguity has a positive effect on supplier opportunism when guanxi importance is low. The finding also show that supplier’s/buyer’s TSAs positively affect buyer/supplier opportunism at low levels of contract binding force but it has a negative effect at high levels. Buyer/supplier performance ambiguity has a stronger positive effect on buyer/supplier opportunism at low levels of contract binding force. Moreover, the supplier’s TSAs has a positive effect on buyer opportunism at low levels of informal agreements. Compared with high levels of informal agreements, when informal agreement levels are low, the positive effect of buyer/supplier performance ambiguity on buyer/supplier opportunism grows stronger. Objective 4: To empirically test the impact of opportunism on channel performance (i.e., channel disruption and knowledge co-creation. This objective is fully achieved. It is well established in the literature that opportunism has a negative effect on firm performance, firm partnership, commitment and satisfaction. Consistent with precious research, this project also finds that opportunism has a negative on knowledge sharing. This finding itself is not particularly interesting. However, this project generates additional thinking about knowledge co-creation (i.e., product co-development) and the opposite side of opportunism (i.e., active collaboration). In inspired by this project, we conducted a study on knowledge-development. The findings of the JOM 2016 paper show that goal compatibility promotes the exchange of ideas and resources, encourages joint problem solving, and engenders harmony of interests. Knowledge commonality initially has a positive effect on product co-development; however, after reaching a threshold, this effect declines.

11507615.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507615.value: Most extant literature on marketing channels overlooks institutional environments that constrain buyer–supplier exchanges. Drawing on transaction cost economics and institutional theory, this project uncovers the critical influence of formal and informal institutions (i.e., legal effectiveness and networking expenditure, contract binding force, and informal agreements) on the use of governance in deterring opportunism, as well as the moderating role of government support on the efficacy of governance mechanism. We identify these four institutions that embed buyer–supplier relationships along with two dimensions: formal–informal and macro–micro. The findings reveal that legal effectiveness mitigates opportunism through increased use of both contractual and relational governance; in contrast, networking expenditure reduces opportunism through relational governance, yet increases opportunism via lowering contractual governance. In addition, our study takes an institutional view and uncovers the effect of contractual and relational governance on the relationship between institutions and opportunism, as well as the moderating role of government support on the efficacy of interfirm governance. Contractual governance is more efficient in constraining opportunism when government support is high, whereas relational governance deters opportunism more when government support is low. The results also reveal that institutional forces not only mitigate channel members’ opportunism but also attenuate the positive effects of transaction-specific assets and performance ambiguity on partner opportunism. Overall, the empirical results support our theoretical propositions, and thus our study contributes to marketing channels literature. This project echoes the call for more research into the role of institutions in marketing decisions, especially in marketing channel management we aim to understand how institutional environments influence opportunism in buyer– supplier relationships.

11507615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507615.value: This project mainly investigates partner opportunism at the firm level and from the senior manager perspective. However, the senior manager perspective cannot fully explain the dynamics of channel partnerships, because boundary spanners at the top and operating levels hold different perspectives. Top-level boundary spanners are primarily responsible for strategic decision making, whereas operating-level boundary spanners are responsible for improving operating efficiency and engaging in exchanges. Therefore, a further development of the research is to study the interaction between top-level and operating-level governance on partner opportunism. The proposed course of action is as follows: (1) to distinguish opportunism occurring at the top-level and operating-level; (2) to conceptually distinguish the governance mechanisms implemented by boundary spanners at different hierarchical levels; (3) to examine whether one type of mechanism is more effective than the other at each management level; and (4) to examine how governance mechanism alignment across different hierarchical levels mitigate two levels of opportunism. From a practitioner’s standpoint, this research development may help top- and operating-level management differentiate the two levels of opportunism and governance mechanisms. By doing so, firms can choose appropriate governance mechanism to suppress opportunism across different management hierarchical levels.

11507615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507615.value: As a response to calls for more attention to the role of institutions in marketing decisions, especially marketing channel management, we examine the impact of institutions on opportunism in buyer–supplier relationships. We identify four institutions that constrain buyer–supplier relationships, along with two dimensions: formal–informal and macro–micro. Extant opportunism literature, mostly rooted in TCE, has focused primarily on the task environment and economic determinants of transaction costs. However, institutions are primary determinants of the size and structure of transaction costs, and they exert regulatory, normative, and cognitive pressures on strategic decisions, including those about opportunistic behaviors. This project extends TCE-based channel literature by explicitly considering the role of institutions. Our findings indicate, both formal and informal institutions constrain opportunistic behaviors in buyer–supplier exchanges. These findings help managers better understand the influence of both macro and micro institutions on opportunism and how to deal with opportunism in emerging economies.

11507815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507815.value: 在多數情況下, 有知識的群體或從廣大專家群體中獲取的信息可以更好的幫助解決複雜的問題。在很多情況下群體智慧是解決這些複雜問題的唯一途徑。 例如, 在2003年非典 (SARS) 病毒突襲香港期間, 最令醫學界感到困解的是“如何確定病患人群” (CDC, 2013)。事情的轉折點出現在非專業醫學人士被引入醫療團隊，他們所表現出的能夠有效辨別“超級傳播者”的能力成為了控制疾病蔓延的重大突破。 到目前為止, 在類似問題上，群體所表現出的優於個體的能力得到了廣泛的認可(e.g., Surowiecki, 2005)。然而, 上述的這種群體智慧優於個體專家的現象並非絕對。有些時候, 群體的智慧被稱讚為“智慧的結晶”, 有時會被批判為“烏合之眾”。因此, 群體智慧這一現象值得我們從以下四個方面進行深入的思考與研究: (1) 群體在共同解決問題時優於個體獨立解決問題的原因。(2) 何種類型的問題最適合應用群裡智來解決。 (3) 如何進一步加強群體智慧的優越性。 (4) 如何將群體智慧應用於更多領域。簡而言之, 我們致力於探求群體智慧的產生機制以及如何使之發揮出其最佳的功效。 於此同時, 我們也著眼於群體智慧所應用的領域以及如何使其更廣泛的應用。 從理論層面上來講, 我們將揭開運用群體智慧解決問題的“神秘面紗”。同時, 我們將確定影響群體表現的非線性因素, 包括群體的大小, 所解決任務的難度 (感受到的難度與真實的難度) 以及群體的智力水平。基於信息技術在重組任務結構與聚集個體智慧方面所表現出的能力，我們將試圖進一步研究任務重組與在信息技術支持下的群體參與機制的影響。我們旨在確定所要解決的問題的呈現方式和解決方案的結構是否可以加強群體在問題處理中的表現。具體而言，複雜的問題可以被分解成許多簡單的問題後被呈現在群體面前。而問題的解決方案也可以被鎖定在指定範圍供群體來參考。 此外, 我們將試圖探索研究結果的可擴展性。這種擴展性可具體表現為可否將運用群體智慧來處理問題的研究成果應用於由群體共同合作完成的項目中去, 例如開放式內容創建 (維基百科)。 除此之外，我們預期通過此項研究對實際應用方面針對如何提高群體解決問題的能力提出指導建議。 潛在的實際應用涉及廣泛, 例如從大局來講, 合理運用群體智慧可以在流行性疾病入侵香港時加強香港的公共安全。 群體智慧的合理應用也適用於十分具體的問題, 例如幫助預測房地產價格.

11507815.label: Realisation of objectives
11507815.value: Collective intelligence describes a phenomenon, whereby non-experts’ aggregate judgments provide higher quality outcomes, than those generated by individuals, even when these individuals are experts. This has been illustrated for instance in the “jellybean jar” experiment where the average estimate for the bean count, drawn from a number of people, exceeds the best individual estimate. Collectives in these settings differ from traditional groups, in a number of characteristics. Most importantly, whereas groups are often described as “social aggregates that involve mutual awareness and potential mutual interaction. … are relatively small and relatively structured or organized”, collectives lack this awareness and interaction. In fact, collectives, which are not ‘normed’ and may not even be aware of each other, but rather represent a “nominal group”. When the collective is not just a nominal group, it must nevertheless meet three requirements for collective wisdom to emerge, namely exhibiting diversity, decentralization of opinion, and independence. Diversity of opinion refers to the availability of multiple viewpoints (ideally many), within the group, as each further viewpoint may help to explain the phenomenon better. Independence means that peoples’ opinions are not determined by the opinions of those around them, which is frequently a biasing factor in groups or teams. Decentralization requires that people draw on their local knowledge and make independent judgments. For collective intelligence to emerge, several task related criteria have to be met as well. First, the outcome which the collective is judging cannot be random. Asking a collective for the expected result of a (random) coin flip, for instance, will not predict the actual outcome, but at best provide a prediction reflecting the probabilistic outcome (e.g., 50/50 percent prediction of heads/tails). Next, individuals have to have some reasoning capability and information concerning the task. The aggregation of random guesses generates no additional information. Needed is the ability to eliminate at least some outcomes, so that multiple processes of elimination of unlikely outcomes, combined, let the best result(s) emerge as most likely, or shift the aggregate estimate towards the true value. Collective intelligence has been applied on a broad range of tasks, including anticipating the outcome of elections, predicting the box office results of motion pictures, identifying mineral fields, or suggesting new product ideas. Among these tasks, we can make two general differentiations, namely between divergence vs. convergence tasks [16], and between interactive and non-interactive tasks. Convergence tasks seek to move toward a unified solution, such as determine a single problem cause, election winner, or such. Divergence tasks seek to find a range of new ideas. Fundamentally, these two are very different, as divergence tasks reward individuality and difference of outcomes, whereas convergence tasks reward finding a single or small set of best solution(s). Task difficulty is another factor that needs to be considered in the exploration of collective intelligence. On a spectrum of difficulty, the high-difficulty endpoint is marked by tasks whose solutions cannot be determined because the underlying problem solving principles are unknown, or are too complicated to apply. We might consider this “objective difficulty”. Problems whose underlying principles are known or can be known in principle, but which aren’t known by the problem solvers involved, are also difficult, but reflect “subjective difficulty”. For either objectively or subjectively difficult problems, problem solvers would have to resort to random judgments, whose aggregation does not improve performance. Thus we would expect a collective to perform about as poorly as individual problem solvers. On the opposite, low-difficulty end of the spectrum, are problems, which are fully understood, and in the grasp of all problem solvers, and thus elementary. Thus, the collective should solve them well, but individual problem solvers also. For either of these extremes, we expect little superiority of the collective over individual problem solvers. Between these two extremes, we expect the existence of a range of appropriate difficulty, which we label the “collective range”. Problems in this range are difficult enough for individuals to perform sub-par, yet the aggregation of collective insights leads to good results. When individuals in the collective are asked to make outcome predictions, one of the key questions is why they should expend the effort to do so. Solution finding is regularly difficult and requires significant effort. Hence the issue of incentivizing the solution finding process has become an important area of study. Frequently, this is done by gamifying collective intelligence tasks. This can take the form of contests, or the creation of markets for predictions, where better predictions result in higher pay-offs. Pay-offs appear to be important for the collective performance can overcome systematic, non-pathological biases, which cause poor individual performance. Whenever individuals make systematically biased judgments, the possible result is less effective resource allocation (e.g., biased risk assessment leading to over-insuring) and thus reduced economic sustainability of the ecosystem. Collective intelligence as an ecosystem can exist void of information and communication technology, yet the availability of technology is usually a vital element in drawing opinions from a large number of widely dispersed individuals and then aggregating them meaningfully. As a result, in recent years numerous such “digital” systems for collective intelligence emerged, for instance as online idea markets, prediction markets, or idea aggregators. Based on the problem structure outlined above, four objectives resulted for the research. Determination of reasons for collective superiority over individual problem solvers, identification of best areas to apply collective intelligence, determination of measures to amplify collective intelligence, and exploration of possible transfer to other domains. All research objectives were achieved. We determined the superiority of collective intelligence over individual task performance in a range of tasks. Noteworthy though, these tasks were not traditional expert tasks were over-learning of highly specialized routines (e.g., flying a plane) were asked for, but instead prediction or estimation tasks of medium difficulty. We also determined that the mechanisms were not simple error reduction routines (regression to the mean), but that collectives were able to behave as if they possessed more complex decision making models, as the overall prediction became an aggregate of numerous individual decision making models taking multiple perspectives on a problem. The search to amplify collective intelligence led to an exploration of gamification as an important incentive mechanism. The exploration of gamification mechanisms revealed significant challenges in design of the gamification so that problem solvers would be sufficiently motivated to provide their best insights. Finally, we explored one transfer domain, namely the use of collective intelligence on producing insights for academic library improvement. Using available information from a large library survey, the usually preference-focused survey was augmented to tap into respondents’ beliefs on how to improve the library, leading to the development of a causal model for library performance.
