11507815.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507815.value: Collectives appear most effective when tasks require access to a wide range of specialized information. In such situations, the collective performed significantly better than the average individual. When tasks become easy, differences between collective and individual problem solving narrow substantially, because of high performance by the average individual, thus leaving little room for improvement. High difficulty, in contrast, leads to random guessing, whereas low difficulty leads to heuristic problem solving, and have improvement potential. We learnt that collective intelligence is not unequivocally better than individual intelligence, even if conditions of diversity, non-randomness of solution, and individual knowledge availability are present. We thus note that collective intelligence as a digital ecosystem has most “survival strength” in situations where task difficulty is moderate. Therefore, if task difficulty can be actively managed, and reduced from high levels down to moderate levels by members of the collective, we should expect increased performance and thus increased sustainability of such collective intelligence digital ecosystems. We learnt that collective intelligence is not based on reduction of random errors (though this can have some impact), but instead on the consideration of more complex prediction models. Lay decision makers use simple heuristics, hence, more sophisticated models require the aggregation of multiple different models. Consequently, decision makers need to operate with some level of independence from each other. Incentives play an important, but also surprising role in extracting collective intelligence. Participants in knowledge elicitation tasks are motivated by incentives and the gamification of the knowledge creation tasks. However, the role of incentives is not straightforward. Some people are willing to participate in tasks when the participation benefits are chance based (winning a prize) or when the pay-off is relatively small. Others appear to be strictly maximizing the “income” from their task performance, seeking to minimize the estimation effort, as a result, they may engage in knowledge withholding or poor estimates, thus leading to a decline in collective performance, where random guessing produces noise that reduces overall outcome quality. As a result, it is important that participants enjoy a meaningful experience, if we want to elicit their best insights. Competition is an important mechanism that facilitates participants’ deep and meaningful engagement within a gamified collective intelligence experience. Greater competition affordance does not mean incorporating leaderboards that let users view the performance of others; instead it means how to develop competition structures that can encourage friendly competition and motivate performance.

11507815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507815.value: The research outlined two promising additional areas of study, namely (1) a further exploration of incentives for the completion of human intelligence tasks, and (2) propagation of knowledge across belief networks. (1) We repeatedly used the Amazon Mechanical Turk to gather collective intelligence information. In doing so, we learnt that the incentive systems for participation were counter-intuitive. Some participants were willing to spend considerable time on low-reward survey responses, demonstrating apparently irrational behaviour. Future research will be needed to understand the motivation of participants in “crowdsourcing tasks”, which appear to be underpaid and void of other significant participation benefits. (2) Our belief elicitation tasks frequently required some interpretation of information from others (belief network), and some understanding how to mathematically use new information to update existing beliefs. Our subjects were not good Bayesians, but relied on simple heuristics that required very little mathematics, so as to produce meaningful answers. Further exploration of this naïve Bayesian updating appears very fruitful in light of growing concerns about misleading news and its impact on people’s beliefs.

11507815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507815.value: Complex problems can often be better solved or only solved by a collective with knowledge or information drawn from a broad pool of expertise. This ability of collectives to perform better than individual experts is by now well recognized. Nevertheless, the results are equivocal, sometimes being better (lauded as wisdom of crowds), sometimes being worse (criticized as madness of the masses). Thus the phenomenon requires a further understanding of (1) why collectives outperform individuals, (2) which problems this strength is best applied to, (3) how this strength can be improved further, and (4) how it might be transferred to other domains. We ventured to investigate the amplifying effects of task shaping and IT--enabled collective aggregation mechanisms. We aimed to also determine whether techniques of problem or solution structuring, whereby the problem is broken down into simpler tasks, or the solution space is narrowed down upfront, can help the collective perform better. Furthermore, we extended the research to understand the role of incentives, especially gamification, to improve task performance. Our findings showed that gamification can be a positive factor in eliciting meaningful responses from members of the collective. However, gamification had to be designed so as to sustain individuals across periods of low motivation, not to keep them indefinitely motivated.

11508415.label: Project Objectives
11508415.value: We attempt to develop a context-specific theory for conducting corporate philanthrophy in a transition economy in that firms may develop a different logic for CP in response to environment uncertainty. We differentiate the distinct effects of two different environment uncertainties on CP behavior, namely regulatory and market uncertainties. We identify the theoretical boundaries for the above relationship between environment uncertainties and a firm’s CP. Specifically, we will investigate whether a firm’s political ties and business ties help alleviate the strategic use of CP for reducing environmental uncertainties.

11508415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11508415.value: This project investigates whether and how corporate philanthropy (CP) is affected by a firm’s perceived degree of environmental uncertainty in the context of a transition economy. Two contrasting perspectives exist regarding the influence of environmental uncertainty on CP. On the one hand, firms may be more likely to contribute when the environment is certain and predictable. Environmental uncertainty may exert a negative impact on firms, forcing them to keep additional resources in hand in order to deal with the possible negative outcomes (Lipshitz & Strauss, 1997). On the other hand, environmental uncertainty may enhance rather than reduce CP such as giving, because CP can help firms build pro-social images and reputations, which invite supports from various stakeholders such as governments, consumers, existing and prospect employees, communities(Brammer et al., 2006). We unravel the above puzzle by developing a theoretical framework that depicts the interplay among environmental uncertainty, political ties, and business ties. In particular, we draw on resource dependence theory to argue that firms’ CP activities are responses to environmental uncertainties, which can be classified as regulatory and market uncertainties. We further argue that a firm’s political ties and business ties alleviate its response to environment pressures. Specifically, both political ties and business ties may reduce the impact of regulatory uncertainty on both giving probability and amount. We plan to examine the above hypotheses in China by collecting both subjective and objective data from a variety of public firms, including state-owned firms, private firms, and joint ventures. This project will illustrate the role of environmental uncertainty in driving corporate social behavior among Chinese firms, and provides valuable insights for CP activities in other transition economies.

11508415.label: Realisation of objectives
11508415.value: We have achieved the above objectives. Specifically, we have found that both regulatory uncertainty and market uncertainty in a transition economy motivate firms to conduct corporate giving. Further, a firm’s political ties and financial performance alleviate its response to environment pressures. Specifically, both political ties and financial performance reduce the impact of regulatory uncertainty on both giving probability and amount, but neither affects market uncertainty's impact.

We differentiate the distinct effects of two different environment uncertainties on CP behavior, namely regulatory and market uncertainties.

We identify the theoretical boundaries for the above relationship between environment uncertainties and a firm’s CP. Specifically, we will investigate whether a firm’s political ties and business ties help alleviate the strategic use of CP for reducing environmental uncertainties.

11508415.label: Major findings and research outcome
11508415.value: We have found that both regulatory uncertainty and market uncertainty in a transition economy motivate firms to conduct corporate giving. Further, a firm’s political ties and financial performance alleviate its response to environment pressures. Specifically, both political ties and financial performance reduce the impact of regulatory uncertainty on both giving probability and amount, but neither affects market uncertainty's impact. In addition, we draw on the behavioral theory to contend that there exists a curvilinear relationship in the above relationship in that the relationship between relative performance and corporate illegality is inverse U-shaped when the firm’s performance is below the social aspirations. However, when the firm’s performance is above its social aspirations, it demonstrates a U-shaped relationship. This project has also enabled research on firm collaboration and competition. We integrate the alliance learning and social network perspectives to examine how different combinations of exploratory and exploitative alliances between a firm and its partner influence the firm’s competition against its partner in product markets. This paper was published at Strategic Management Journal. Also, we conducted research on long-term orientation, and found that top managers’ subjective perception of time, specifically, their long-term orientation, positively affects the comprehensiveness, speed, and creativity of strategic decision-making processes and that industry context moderates these relationships. This paper was published at Journal of Management.

11508415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11508415.value: Further research could explore the simultaneous existence of corporate social responsibility (CSR) and corporate illegality. Firms demonstrate varying degrees of CSR and corporate illegality. It will be interesting to explore why firms are doing good things, i.e., CSR and at the same time, they also engage in bad things, i.e., illegal behaviors. We have made some first attempts in this line of research, and future research could draw on multiple theories to explain this complex phenomenon.

11508415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11508415.value: We examined the effect of environmental uncertainty on corporate giving using a nation-wide survey of private enterprises in China.We divided environmental uncertainty into two categories: regulatory uncertainty and market uncertainty. Our results show that both regulatory and market uncertainty increase both a firm’s giving probability and giving amount to charities. Political ties and ROA weakens the effect of regulatory uncertainty on giving probability and amount, but do not affect market uncertainty’s effect. In the SMJ paper, we examines how different combinations of exploratory and exploitative alliances between two firms affect their competition in the product market. Using a 20-year dataset collected in the U.S. pharmaceutical industry, we find that the proportion of exploratory alliances (i.e., joint development of critical innovations) in the alliance portfolio between a firm and its partner increases the firm’s competition against its partner, up to a tipping point at which such competition starts to decline.

11600315.label: Project Objectives
11600315.value: This research will investigate how readily Chinese courts decree the remedy of specific performance through an empirical study of court decisions in China. rows: This research will investigate how readily Chinese courts decree the remedy of specific performance through an empirical study of court decisions in China.
How often do Chinese courts use SP as a remedy for contractual breaches? We conjecture that SP awards in Chinese courts are less frequent than commonly assumed in the existing literature.
What factors influence a court’s decision whether or not to award SP?

11600315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600315.value: There is a lack of reliable empirical knowledge about contract remedies in China. How did the 1999 Chinese Contract Law affect court-awarded remedies for breach of contract? Specifically, how readily do Chinese courts award specific performance for breach of contract and what factors influence their choice between SP and damages? Normatively, there are arguments favoring either one of the two remedies. For some, specific performance is more efficient than damages while for others damages are superior in other circumstances. Some comparative studies have argued that while the common law world favors money damages, while civil law systems endorse SP as the primary remedy. However, more recent empirical work has shown that, as a matter of practice, both common law and civil law systems tend to reach similar remedial outcomes. This convergence theory requires further verification through country-specific case studies. China is a particularly important yet understudied jurisdiction. Important changes in the last few decades in both PRC contract law and the dynamics of business transactions in China further highlight the importance of the China case study. A gap exists between PRC contract law’s underlying assumptions and the modern reality of how a contract is often experienced and enforced. This research will help us to better understand the choices made between damages and specific performance in China. The research findings will help us assess current Chinese law and consider possible statutory reforms. 关于中国合同的违约实证研究一直或缺。1999年的中国合同法的制定如何影响了法院在合同违约中的判决？具体而言，中国法院多情愿来判决继续履行？什么具体因素来影响在损害赔偿和继续履行之间的选择？在理论上， 两种救济方式各有所长并被推崇。一些学者认为继续履行比损害赔偿更有效率但其他学者却认为损害赔偿更应优先使用。 比较法研究说明，普通法系更倾向于损害赔偿，但民法法域更倾向于继续履行。但是最近的实证研究表明，在实务层面，普通法系和民法罚息其实没有更大的区别 。这种趋同理论需要更多的具体法域实证研究来证实。

rows: This research will investigate how readily Chinese courts decree the remedy of specific performance through an empirical study of court decisions in China.
How often do Chinese courts use SP as a remedy for contractual breaches? We conjecture that SP awards in Chinese courts are less frequent than commonly assumed in the existing literature.
What factors influence a court’s decision whether or not to award SP?

11600315.label: Major findings and research outcome
11600315.value: This project employs an empirical study based on data collected by surveys and follow-up interviews with hundreds of Mainland Chinese judges at various levels of the Chinese court system (related to civil and commercial disputes). Based on the statistical findings of the empirical study, a theoretical inquiry is offered to better understand the relative use or non-use of specific performance as a contractual remedy. The findings show that damages are often favored over specific performance; additionally, judges in the Mainland Chinese courts system take a far more proactive role in the preliminary stages of trials and will actively persuade parties to claim damages over specific performance where expedient. The study also shows that, despite popular belief, that the higher supervision costs associated with specific performance are not a determining factor in the decision to avoid the awarding of SP.

11600315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11600315.value: The study on the use of SP in the Chinese court system provides support for the proposition that the divergence between the civil and common law views of SP as an ordinary or extraordinary remedy is not as wide as depicted in the formal law. It is also the case that Chinese law has been influenced by a common law-like view of case law. The study makes clear that the labeling of SP as an ordinary or extraordinary remedy in the case of SP is not reflected in Chinese court practice. Chinese courts are influenced by a recognized taxonomy of contracts in determining which types of contracts are deserving of SP. In fact, Chinese courts’ frugality in the issuance of SP orders bring them closer to the approach taken in the common law. Therefore, a further study on how to design a statutory provision reform is necessitated.

11600315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11600315.value: This study investigates the values and latent policies, which have shaped the development of Chinese law in the area of the availability of specific performance (SP) as a contractual remedy. The National People’s Congress (Legislature) and Supreme People’s Court in China have addressed the remedial structure of Chinese contract law, namely, the availability of the remedy of SP as opposed to the awarding of damages-only. The law is clear that the remedies of SP and damages are ordinary remedies that a claimant is free to choose between. The question that is confronted in this article is whether in practice the equality of SP and damages as remedies are applied in a neutral, unbiased way by the Chinese courts. Simply put, how often do Chinese courts use SP as a remedy for contract breaches? If SP is found to be seldomly awarded, the question then becomes, what are the underlying reasons or rationales given for its underutilization? This article employs an empirical study based on data collected by surveys and follow-up interviews with hundreds of Mainland Chinese judges at various levels of the Chinese court system (related to civil and commercial disputes). The findings show that damages are often favored over specific performance; additionally, judges in the Mainland Chinese courts system take a far more proactive role in the preliminary stages of trials and will actively persuade parties to claim damages over specific performance where expedient. The study also shows that, despite popular belief, that the higher supervision costs associated with specific performance are not a determining factor in the decision to avoid the awarding of SP.

11600415.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11600415.value: 研製大規模中文閱讀語料庫以從眼動考察無意識分詞

11600415.label: Project Objectives
11600415.value: Identify the optimal ranges of typographic features for Chinese reading; Re-examine word spacing effect in Chinese reading within the optimal ranges; Develop a large scale Chinese reading corpus. Train a machine learning model to learn unconscious word segmentation from eye movement data in the Chinese reading corpus.
rows: Identify the optimal ranges of typographic features for Chinese reading;
Re-examine word spacing effect in Chinese reading within the optimal ranges;
Develop a large scale Chinese reading corpus.
Train a machine learning model to learn unconscious word segmentation from eye movement data in the Chinese reading corpus.

11600415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600415.value: (1) Large scale reading corpora recording readers’ eye movements during reading have rarely been used to study Chinese reading, where two key questions remain unanswered: (2) how words are segmented during reading Chinese texts (without spaces as visually salient word delimiters) and (3) whether eye movements hint an answer to (2); and (4) wordhood remains a notorious long-standing issue unlikely to be resolved by word definition, theoretical argumentation and/or technological advancement in both Chinese linguistics and language processing. Given this background, this project is proposed to develop a large scale corpus of Chinese reading for machine learning to learn from eye movements how native readers segment words. Regarding inconsistent results in Chinese reading research due, to a large extent, to typographic settings (e.g., adequate inter- vs. intra-word spacing), we will first identify their optimal ranges, to ensure the validity, reliability and consistency throughout our reading experiments. Then, we will conduct a pilot study to (re-)examine word spacing effect with spaces/delimiters of various sizes, shapes and colors, to demonstrate the significance of optimal typographic settings, before moving on to developing the reading corpus by recording readers’ eye movements during reading under such settings. The reading materials, presented to readers without word boundary information, are selected from representative segmented Chinese corpora that conform to a Chinese word segmentation standard. The key task to enable the machine learning is the feature engineering to convert eye movements to an optimal set of features (within a predefined feature space defined on characters within the perceptual span of reading with respect to available variables in eye tracking reports) that give the best model for predicting word boundaries after training. Our previous works on machine learning of Chinese word segmentation via character tagging using the conditional random fields model and on large scale feature selection for semantic parsing, that advanced the state of the art in respective areas, provide a strong technical support and plenty practical experience to propel our success in this learning task. As the very first endeavor on (1) in the field, this project will produce not only reliable benchmark data for Chinese reading but also verifiable answers to (2) and (3), by means of modeling how readers’ eye movements reveal their unconscious (vs. subjective) word segmentation, and an objective means to scrutinize how native speakers process controversial cases of Chinese wordhood, for novel insights into this perplexing issue. (1)至今尚無記錄讀者眼動的大規模閱讀語料庫用於中文閱讀研究，而兩大問題仍亟待答案：(2)中文無空格作醒目分隔符，讀者如何分詞？(3)眼動對此有無啟示？(4)什麼是詞，是漢語語言學和中文處理的一個老大難問題，靠詞定義、理論論證和技術進步，似難解決。在此背景下，本項目提出研製大規模中文閱讀語料庫，以從眼動數據學習讀者如何分詞。鑒於過往中文閱讀研究多因文本排印設置（例如字、詞間距大小）不一等導致結果不一，我們將首先測定該等設置的理想區間，以確保實驗有效、可靠和一致，重測不同大小形狀的分隔符對分詞的效用，以驗證該等理想設置，然後選用按分詞標準分詞的代表性漢語語料庫文本，讓母語讀者在理想設置下(無分隔符)自然閱讀，記錄眼動，構建閱讀語料庫。本項目作為領域內對(1)的首試，通過對讀者眼動考察無意識(vs.主觀)分詞，不單為中文閱讀也為(2)(3)問題的求證，提供可靠基準數據，用以客觀檢視母語讀者如何處理有爭議的漢語詞個案，為此難題探求新見解。

11600415.label: Realisation of objectives
11600415.value: 1. This objective to identify the optimal ranges of typographic features for Chinese reading has been successfully achieved. In total, 6 experiments were conducted to test a variety of typographic features. Experiment 1 revealed the optimal range of luminance contrast ratio to be 2.454–7.523:1. Experiment 2, as the very first experiment employing the 2x2 design (font size * character spacing), showed the optimal range of font size to be 0.4°–1° of visual angle and that of character spacing to be 0 between character frames. Experiment 3 further extended the lower and upper bounds of font size in experiment settings and found only 0.3° to be inferior to others, revising the optimal range to 0.4°–1.2°. To further test the validity of these results, we conducted Experiment 4 with a novel idea of introducing various levels of negative character spacing, further re-confirming the optimal spacing 0, plus an extra finding that font sizes >= 0.6° can compensate negative spacing to allow a stable reading performance. Experiment 5 examined the effect of interline spacing on reading and found 200% spacing to be most effective and all other settings to be similar. Further introducing negative interline spacing, Experiment 6 also confirmed the optimal to be 200%, plus an extra finding of a weak trend of attenuated efficiency along more narrow interline spacing. Altogether, these experiments have successfully pinpointed the optimal typographic settings for Chinese reading that guarantee the validity and reliability of future studies to the greatest extent we can. 2. This objective to re-examine word spacing effects on Chinese reading has been successfully fulfilled through 3 experiments. The first, Experiment 7, used exactly the same materials and design as Bai et al. (2008) and successfully replicated most previous results except the good global performance on spaced words in terms of reading time. Experiment 8 adopted word segmentation standards for spaced words with other settings unchanged but still failed to observe this good reading performance. These 2 experiments showed that word spacing facilitates local reading performance on words but prolongs sentence reading time, because of the dual roles of inserted spaces: visually marking word boundaries and also physically extending sentence length. Experiment 9 specifically investigated spacing effects on single-character words (SCWs) as almost all previous studies focused on two-character words. Its result shows that SCWs are easier to process than single-character morphemes while spaced, confirming the psychological reality of the former for the very first time, although spacing effect looks weaker on SCWs than on the latter. Overall, not only have this series of experiments enriched and revised a few key claims regarding word spacing effects on Chinese reading but also discovered many interesting details reflecting the complexity of the effects. 3. This objective has been fully achieved, successfully developing the first large-scale Chinese reading corpus of eye movements up to 2.74M read characters, nearly a triple of the proposed size 1M. It is the largest of its kind in the world. The work to release it is well in progress. Specifically, two independent reading sub-corpora, one for sentence reading and the other for passage reading, have been built through Experiment 10 & 11 respectively, to collect valid data from 98 participants for a total number of read characters exceeding 1.7 million. Also, eye movement data of natural reading (i.e., under conditions with font size in the optimal range and 0 character spacing) from other experiments are also included in the corpus. These natural reading conditions, marked with # in the experiment list below, contribute 1M data of the whole corpus. Next, our work is to release it with proper data formats (other than the raw data as in the eye tracker’s .edf files), including (but not limited to) various kinds of reports (e.g., IA/trial/fixation/saccade/sequence/…) in company with proper documentation of reading materials and experimental settings, in order to make it as useful as possible to different disciplines of language studies. 4. A change request was made to revise this objective before the start of the project for the budget cut equivalent to the proposed senior RA ship for this part. Even without proper manpower, we did try on this part through a BA final year project using a Seq2Seq model, achieving some unpromising results: only eye movements near sentence beginning and end show marginally observable correspondence with true word boundaries. Instead, to illustrate the power of the corpus, a character-based mixed-effects linear regression was conducted at the halfway of data collection, using the sentence sub-corpus of 67 participants’ data to investigate how wordhood influences reading. With other variables (e.g., frequency, char complexity) properly considered, the analysis showed that higher wordhood probability associates with better reading performance on characters as words and morphemes in both foveal and parafoveal vision, confirming “word” to be the default form for activating Chinese characters. It is the very first time to have found that SCWs can be processed in parallel vs two-character words in serial only. This analysis not only sheds light on existing reading models but also showcases the value and the validity of the corpus. Given no comparable corpus of eye movements available at this huge scale, ours is for sure the leading one that can contribute significantly to various interdisciplinary researches in linguistics and psychology that need empirical big data. 11600415.label: Major findings and research outcome
11600415.value: 1. The optimal ranges of typographic features for Chinese reading: (1) Luminance contrast: 2.454:1–7.523:1 A low luminance contrast below the low end of this optimal range was found in to significantly increase both average fixation duration and overall reading time. (Experiment 1) (2) Character size: 0.4° to 1.2° A font size below the low end of this range significantly increased the sentence reading time while those within the range did not elicit remarkable difference. (Experiment 2 & 3) (3) Character spacing: 0 Either increasing or shrinking this default size of character spacing, i.e. 0, significantly prolonged the sentence reading time. (Experiment 2—4) (4) Interline spacing: 200% The average fixation duration and passage reading time showed a downward trend as interline spacing shrink from 200%, and the measures of those conditions over 200% were also numerically worse. (Experiment 5—6) 2. Re-examination of word spacing effect in Chinese reading: (1) Word spacing is facilitative for local but disruptive for global reading performance. The local fixation duration decreased while global reading time increased under word-spaced condition, compare to those under normal unspaced condition. (Experiment 7—8) (2) Word spacing effect is not sensitive to the adjustment of spaced words in experimental materials towards segmentation standards. The findings are highly similar, irrespective of loose or strict word segmentation criteria. (Experiment 7—8) (3) SCWs are processed differently from sublexical morphemes. The total fixation duration increased for a spaced sublexical morpheme, but not for a spaced single-character word. (Experiment 9) (4) SCWs benefit less from word spacing compared to two-character words. While two-character words had both decreased fixation duration and probability under word-spaced condition, single-character words only benefited on fixation probability. (Experiment 9) 3. The development of the large-scale Chinese Reading Corpus of Eye Movements: (1) A reading corpus that contains eye movement data for over 2.74M read characters, from various natural reading conditions. (2) Completion of word segmentation according to segmentation standards and primary word/character annotations for the reading materials. 4. Results of mixed-effects linear regression analysis: (1) Word is the default form for activating Chinese characters in reading. The gaze duration was found to be shorter on characters with higher wordhood probability, regardless of actual wordhood in context. (2) Chinese readers adopt both parallel and serial manners in online word processing, contingent on word length. Lexical characteristics of SCWs (esp. wordhood probability) in parafoveal vision can influence the duration of the current fixation, but those of two-character words (e.g., word frequency) cannot.

11600415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11600415.value: In addition to the ongoing papers below, we have many potential courses for further research. Release the corpus and also invite researchers to upload the natural reading data in their experiments (as we did) for data sharing. Data are everything in this big data area. The larger is the corpus, the better. It can be a huge joint effort towards establishing a Chinese eye tracking data platform. Continue our unfished endeavors on machine learning of word segmentation, the most powerful means to capture invisible patterns or regularities hidden in the intertwined factors in natural reading. Applying mixed-effects linear regression to analyze the data is another possible alternative in this direction. Use the corpus to investigate Chinese reading: detecting general trends and patterns of eye movements in natural reading (for which large scale data have rarely been available because most experiments were conducted via controlled reading); (re)examining existing claims about effects of various character/lexical properties (e.g., frequency, length, complexity, and predictability), especially the “non-existence” of preferred viewing location (PVL) vs. the optimal viewing location (OVP, at word center) in Chinese reading, and exploring the possibility of fitting existing reading models (e.g., E-Z reader and SWIFT) to Chinese natural reading.

11600415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11600415.value: This project was proposed to develop a large scale Chinese reading corpus of eye movements (typically, fixations and saccades) for machine learning of unconscious word segmentation by readers. To ensure the validity, reliability and consistency of collected data, we conducted 6 experiments to pinpoint, for the very first time, the optimal typographical settings for Chinese texts, including luminance contrast ratio (2.454:1–7.523:1, text vs. background), font size (0.4°--1.2° of visual angle), character spacing (0, character frame distance) and interline spacing (200%, vs line height), which are valuable for both normal and disabled readers to achieve the best reading. Using these settings, we achieved the other objectives successfully through 5 experiments as proposed, having (re)examined word spacing effects (e.g., facilitative to local/word but disruptive to global/sentence reading, not sensitive to segmentation standards), obtained new findings (e.g., difference in processing single-/multi-character words), and developed a reading corpus of 2.74M read characters, the first and the largest of its kind in the world. Although the machine learning part has not been successful, we performed the mixed-effects linear regression on available data, finding that word is the default form of activating characters and readers apply parallel/serial strategies to process single-/multi-character words respectively.

11600715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11600715.value: Although Hong Kong budgetary practice has long been regarded as a model of fiscal prudence, surprisingly little research has been conducted on the strains facing the system in the post-1997 period. Yet prima facie evidence suggests that the socio-economic problems of an ageing population, slow economic growth, and demands for more welfare from an increasingly active civil society are placing the traditional model under stress. The government has accordingly begun to modify its long-standing concerns with balanced budgets and low welfare spending and to pay more attention to the problem of selling budget proposals to pressure groups and to the public. This proposal examines a critical dimension of this changing process by analyzing the impact of democratic institutional development on budgeting. The debate on democratic institutional development in Hong Kong has focused on election formats and procedures. Democratization also creates, however, an opportunity to bring budgetary demands to the table and for groups to argue for more spending on community needs. In contrast to the traditional, insulated, top-down budgetary model, democratic institutional development might involve making the process more open and inclusive which in turn might be reflected, quantitatively, in changing patterns of government expenditure. The key research question in this context is: Does institutional development affect spending patterns? More specifically, does it make large-scale budget changes more likely or less likely, and why? We will examine these questions in two related ways. The first will be a quantitative study examining and comparing the spending patterns before and after the democratization, using Punctuated Equilibrium Theory (PET) to develop hypotheses for testing. PET suggests that political dynamics have a significant effect on agenda setting and budgetary changes but such effects have received only limited empirical testing in Western democracies and Hong Kong. The second will involve a qualitative study of the evolution of Hong Kong’s budgetary practices over the period 1990 to the present, examining cases of large spending events in significant details in qualitative reviews of government and public documents to substantiate the spending patterns identified in the quantitative analysis. Employing these methods, the proposal will seek to realise three major objectives: to improve our understanding of Hong Kong’s present budgetary model and the policy process; to provide time series data over the period which will inform analysis of the changing model and should be useful to both scholars and practitioners; and to generate fresh evidence advancing PET budgetary theory. 尽管香港的预算实践长时间以来一直被认为是稳健的财政政策，但是令人惊讶的是很少有研究来关注这一体系在97回归之后所面临的變化。据初步证据显示，人口老龄化所带来的社会—经济问题、经济增长缓慢、积极的公民社会不断要求更多的社会福利都使得这一传统预算模式面临巨大的压力。因此，港府相应的开始以平衡预算、低福利支出以及更多关注如何向压力组织和公民推销预算议案来调整其之前长期所关注的问题。以香港政府预算模式的变化为背景，该研究计划主要检验在这个变化过程中民主制度发展对预算的影响。 关于香港民主政治发展的辩论主要体现在选举的模式和程序。但是，民主化的过程也为预算的公开讨论创造了机会，并且让不同团体有机会为社区需要争取更多的预算支出。与传统的、隔离的以及从上而下的预算模式相反，民主制度发展使得预算过程更加开放和包容，从数量上来讲，可以从政府支出的改变模式反映出来。该研究的主要研究问题是：民主制度发展是否对政府预算支出模式有影响？具体来讲，民主制度发展是否影响大规模的预算变化？ 我们将从两个相关方面来回答以上问题。第一个方面，根据间断平衡理论来形成假设，以量化研究方式来检验和比较民主化过程之前和之后的预算支出模式。间断平衡理论认为政治动态对议程设定和预算变化有重大影响；但是这种影响在西方社会和香港没有得到充分的实证检验；该研究将填补这一空白。第二方面以质化研究的方式来仔细回顾政府和公共文件，从而来探讨从1990年至今以来发生的大规模预算支出案例，以便来证实在量化分析中所确定的支出模式。 通过量化和质化的研究方法，该研究期望达到以下三个主要目标：增进我们对香港当前预算模型和决策制定过程的了解；为民主化过程提供时间序列数据从而有助于学者和实践者分析预算模式的变化；为间断平衡理论提供新的实证证据从而促进理论发展。

11600715.label: Realisation of objectives
11600715.value: Objective 1: To undertake research to help in the construction of new models of the budgetary and policy process in Hong Kong We have achieved this objective. The results of this research indicate that the budgetary decision in Hong Kong has changed, though not all three key factors specified in the proposal have the same impact. In the theoretical development of the proposal, we hypothesized that the colonial-era principle of fiscal prudence and conservatism in Hong Kong has changed as a result of the institutional development, reflecting the (a) changing dynamics in electorate politics in the legislature, (2) change of political power structure inside the executive branch, and (3)a more engaging civic society in the budgetary process. Our results indicate an influence of the legislative politics (the above first factor) on the budgetary decision in Hong Kong spending patterns. We found that, first, from examining the filibuster cases in the legislative process, that legislators have increasingly used filibustering to delay funding and changed spending patterns, and this happens in the capital budgeting process. More specifically, spending on capital projects has followed a much more fluctuated pattern than recurrent spending projects, largely due to legislative maneuvers in the legislative process. Moreover, we also looked into environmental spending as a funding subject for in-depth analysis. Our analysis indicates the potential influence of powers of legislative council members. Using the time-series data going back to the 1980s, we found that the number of elected numbers in the council is negatively associated with environmental spending growth, with all other key variables controlled, providing evidence again showing increasing influence of the legislative branch in Hong Kong budgetary decision making. Third, to further understand how the spending model has changed, we have started to examine the types of strategies used by legislators in the environmental legislations, with a focus on capital spending requests. With a theory that classifies the broad types of strategies used in legislative debates of spending decisions, we are examining different patterns of using the strategies and their potential impact. We hope to further this research by broadening to include non-recurrent spending projects in future with possible new funding. Objective 2: To analyse the fiscal consequences of democratic institutional development in Hong Kong We have achieved this objective. We built a statistical model, with time-series data from the 1980s, to examine the consequences. The results indicate the significant influence of legislative development on spending. A more independent legislature reduces the funding on the environment and infrastructures. Our content analysis of legislative documents suggests that pan-democrat legislators are more likely to support social programmes (social security, healthcare, and community development etc) not infrastructure projects or environmental projects, which partly explains this research outcome. We also examine how such consequences occur. In terms of budgetary strategies adopted by policy makers in budgetary debates, we found that administrators have increasingly framed their funding needs as health urgencies (not just environmental issues), and there is potential influence of budgetary strategies adopted by administrators on legislative budgetary decisions. Moreover, we found legislative impact on spending happens largely in the capital budgeting process of legislation, which is a different process from the legislative process discussing recurrent budgetary projects. Objective 3: To develop a long term time-series fiscal database for studying Hong Kong budgetary patterns and fiscal trends We have achieved this objective. We collected the total spending data and functional spending data in environment, education, healthcare, housing, and several other spending functions. We also collected data measuring three key variables in legislative, bureaucratic, and civic institutional developments. Moreover, we have collected budget filibustering cases and budgetary strategy data from legislative documents. The spending data have been completed and will be sent to the departmental research website. Other databases are being sorted and coded, and will be sent to publication after data cleaning. Objective 4: To help make theoretical advances in the PET theory of budgetary decision making, employing the Hong Kong case as a natural experiment This is the area we have achieved the most in this project. We found evidence that can significantly advance the punctuated equilibrium theory (PET). Adopting a fiscal process-oriented approach, we produced evidence that answers the call of PET scholars for better understanding of the process causing frictions in policy agenda setting and budgetary output patterns (Baumgartner et al, 2009). We have evidence to demonstrate how budgetary output patterns are influenced by fiscal strategic choices made by governments. We found significant deviations of budgetary output patterns in capital projects, restricted funds, and entitlement spending, thus signifying the influence of fiscal management practices on resource allocation decisions. Furthermore, we empirically associate spending punctuation patterns with the growing democratic institutional development in Hong Kong. By examining legislative filibuster cases related to capital projects, we found evidence associating democratization with greater institutional frictions and consequently with larger budgetary output punctuations. Objective 5: To produce high quality academic publications to disseminate the results We have produced several publications from this research. (1) A paper written from this research is under review with a status of revise and resubmit (R/R) by Policy Studies Journal (PSJ), a prestigious journal in public policy studies (ISI Impact Factor 2.83, 18/169 in Political Science, 10/47 in Public Administration). The manuscript was originally submitted in March 2018, and received a letter inviting for R/R in July 2018. We have completed the revision recently, and the final version will be submitted late February 2019. In deciding on the order of authorship, I asked Dr. Hanyu XIAO, a RA of CityU at the time (now assistant professor at the EUHK), to be the first author as he collected the large chunk of fiscal data voluntarily without pay under my supervision as a learning experience, and he has engaged significantly in the data analysis part of the research. (2) Part of spending data has been used for a paper in a symposium sponsored by Public Money & Management (SSCI Impact factor 2017: 0.881) and edited by me and James Chan of University of Illinois, on intergovernmental fiscal relations. The paper was written by Wilson Wong (the CO-I) of this grant and Hanyu Xu with the title “Twenty years of Hong Kong and Macao under Chinese rule: being absorbed under ‘one country, two systems’.” Public Money and Management 36 (6): 411-418. I excluded myself from this research as an editor of the special theme issue. My editorial is James Chan and XiaoHu Wang “Theme: Managing and Financing China’s Intergovernmental Relations” Public Money and Management 38 (6): 407-410. (3) The data have been used to produce a series of high-quality student research projects and outputs including a PhD dissertation by Jingyung Xu (graduated February 2019 and supervised by me) “What makes the government spend more on the environment? The case of Hong Kong”, and a conference paper of the same title presented at International Research Society of Public Management (IRSPM) annual conference in March 2018 in Edinberg Scotland by Jingyung Xu and me.

11600715.label: Major findings and research outcome
11600715.value: First, we have significantly advanced the punctuated equilibrium theory (PET) by providing a fiscal explanation of budgetary output patterns and policy agenda setting. We produce evidence suggesting budgetary outputs and policy agendas can be partly explained by stakeholders' behaviors in various fiscal processes. This is a significant addition to the PET theories which so far are dominated by political explanations. Second, we produce evidence on a major change in budgetary decision making model in Hong Kong, which stresses the significant role of legislature in budgetary decision. This new model is a significant advancement from the traditional budgetary model in Hong Kong understood by academics as an executive-dominated and fiscal conservative decision process. Our research indicates an increasing power struggle between the executive and legislative branches in budget debates, highlighted by the filibuster cases. Third, we also provide some evidence indicating where and how the change of budgetary model has happened. We have evidence that legislative influence over the budgetary output patterns occurs largely in the capital budgeting process, which is a separate decision process from that of recurrent spending budget in Hong Kong. We also have data indicating that various budgetary strategies are used by administrators in budgetary debates, and there is need to understand the potential impact of these strategies on legislative funding decisions and budgetary outputs.

11600715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11600715.value: First, although we demonstrated the importance of various fiscal processes in influencing budgetary outputs, our data are limited in three fiscal processes-- the capital budgeting process, the restricted/non-restricted funding process, and discretionary/mandatory funding process. We need data to validate this influence in other fiscal processes such as debt financing process, investment decision process, and tax rate choices. Perhaps more important in the next step is to understand more on how budgetary strategies adopted by policy makers (both administrators and legislators) influence resource allocation decisions, which will deepen our understanding on how budgetary output patterns, described as punctuated fluctuations in PET, happens. I would very much like to know, for example, if different types of strategies--either stakeholder support or performance-focused-- work differently in various fiscal processes. Do stakeholder prefer a specific type of budgetary strategies during fiscal booming or decline times? Does adoption of a specific type of budgetary strategies lead to funding outcomes?

11600715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11600715.value: Has the institutional development in the democratization process of Hong Kong changed the government spending patterns? Guided by the Punctuated Equilibrium Theory (PET), this research finds that an increasingly independent legislature has led to a decline in environmental spending. Moreover, opposing views in an increasingly confrontational legislature have caused more punctuated spending patterns in capital projects spending. These findings enrich the PET theory by articulating the fiscal influence in policy agenda setting and budgetary outputs. Moreover, we find that various strategies adopted by administrators and legislators in budget debates may cause the change in budgetary outputs.

11601015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11601015.value: 學術研究通常以加勒比與歐洲、美洲和前蘇聯的經濟和地緣政治關係解釋其發展。近年來，中國已經成為一個重要的經濟和政治上的合作夥伴與競爭對手。中國可能對塑造加勒比發展的軌跡上和其4,000萬居民有一個決定性的影響。不斷增長的關係也為加勒比提供一個大型而未被研究的實驗室去研究中國作為一個新的開發合作夥伴的影響和中國在現今主導自由派力量的「後院」向主導全球秩序擺出的姿態所帶出的潛在挑戰。因此，此計劃通過互動：即外交、觀念的影響、援助、貿易、金融和投資的各種渠道研究中國對加勒比的影響。此計劃是一個長期的習題，旨在擺脫之前（雖相對仍有限）的研究，去探討中國與加勒比的關係，以此作為對中國與拉丁美研究的一個註腳 (例如 Lederman et al. 2006, Rosales & Kuwayama 2012)。我們認為，機構的種類、加勒比國家以及他們與中國富於變化的參與是不能完全通過由拉丁美洲的角度去理解；相反，我們提出了一個放在加勒比海國家的具體重點，其中我們已經根據他們與中國的關係初步確定五大非排他性的類型， （一）自然資源到中國的出口國（古巴，圭亞那，牙買加，蘇裡南，特立尼達和多巴哥）; （二）從中國得著顯著直接投資的接受者（巴哈馬，古巴，圭亞那，牙買加，蘇裡南，特立尼達和多巴哥）; （三）已成為中國的援助和商業貸款的重要受益國家（巴哈馬，巴貝多，古巴，多明尼加，牙買加，特立尼達和多巴哥）; （四）位列世界最高中國投資的離岸金融中心（英屬維爾京群島，開曼群島）; 和 （五）一些在世界上少數仍與台灣有全面外交關係的國家（多明尼加共和國，海地，聖基茨和尼維斯，聖盧西亞，聖文森特和格林納丁斯）。 承認本地代理機構和可變性，此計劃將設計一個所有在國家的類型學去分析與中國不同相互作用的後果（或者缺少這些），以及全面的影響。 這類型學將考慮： （一）與中國關係的性質； （二）與其他國家的地緣政治和經濟聯繫； （三）制度的類型； （四）機構能力； （五）經濟政策； （六）個別國家在全球經濟中的地位和 （七）具體的應對政策對中國的影響。 通過二手資料和訪談關鍵知情人士和以上的元素，我們將首次提供一個深入和廣泛的中國與加勒比之間的政治經濟學關係的研究。因此，這計劃不僅有助於衡量中國對加勒比發展的影響，而且還提供了經驗數據和理論論據以回答有關中國是否以及如何對全球自由秩序提出了挑戰這重要問題。這計劃建基於以往的研究經驗，由兩位共富有37年研究經驗的資深研究員負責。他們一直以來都對研究中國的國際關係，並在拉美有豐富的實地考察經驗，亦精通中國和加勒比地區的主要語言，還能貫通與中國和加勒比各地區機關的脈絡。

11601015.label: Realisation of objectives
11601015.value: Our research shows that the PRC has significantly shifted the hierarchies of development in the Caribbean, contributing to the post-unipolar outlook of international relations in the region (Breslin, 2017, 2018). However, this shift has not necessarily altered the region’s broad developmental trajectory (Gonzalez-Vicente, forthcoming 2021). In particular, the PRC has allowed regional economies in search of better financing deals to triangulate beyond a few traditional Western ‘partners’. However, despite broadening the developmental landscape, the PRC’s economic engagement in the Caribbean has also contributed to a narrow developmental horizon. The focus of Chinese businesses on consolidated sectors, natural resources and infrastructure (the latter as part of the Belt and Road Initiative), has done little to reverse the region’s structural dependence on the world market, the unequal postcolonial socioeconomic order within Caribbean societies, or the prevalence of neoliberal business-centric understandings of development among local political elites. Whereas these are issues that can be attributed to the historical preconditions and contemporary political agency within the region, PRC projects have helped to perpetuate these trends by discouraging transparent, accountable, and participatory development approaches. The project has achieved all the objectives listed above, although the relationship between China and the Caribbean is of course in flux and our findings will need to be updated in the future. Objective number 1 was fully accomplished. The work that we have conducted in the Caribbean has allowed us to draw upon previously existing work on the PRC’s relations and apply it to the region, and to contribute our own perspectives on China’s global footprint through a variety of region-focused and globally-oriented research outputs. Four years of research in the Caribbean demonstrate that it is indeed necessary to study this region as a separate entity, as the dynamics of China’s engagement are significantly shaped by pre-existing social, political and economic dynamics. From a Caribbean vantage point we have developed new theories to address China’s global developmental footprint (see especially Gonzalez-Vicente, 2019). Also, we have been able to add insights into China’s Belt and Road Initiative by drawing upon critical Caribbean development thought (see Gonzalez-Vicente & Montoute, 2020). All in all, we have been able to demonstrate the distinctiveness of China-Caribbean links and to develop conceptual thinking that address the particular features of these links. Studying the China-Caribbean nexus has also allowed us to tap into broader debates on Chinese conceptions of the South, investment in developing economies, the spread of soft power agendas, the promotion of Occidentalism, and debt trap diplomacy (Breslin, forthcoming 2021). Objective number 2 has also been accomplished. Through our four year journey of researching China-Caribbean relations we have established important connections with researchers within the region, participating in local debates and publications, and presenting at policy-oriented forums. We are, for example, now members of the University of the West Indies’ Global Belt and Road Research Network. We have also organized an international conference panel at the International Studies Association annual convention, and given seminars and keynote speeches at a number of events within the region and beyond. Objective number 3 has also been achieved, and our research has disaggregated the multiple channels of interaction between China and the Caribbean. Among these, diplomacy, trade, offshore finance, finance and investment stand out. In particular, the upsurge in a combination of Chinese loans with foreign direct investment (FDI) has been one of the most important new economic trends in the region in the last ten years, along with more tenuous offshore financial linkages (Robertson 2019). Objective number 4 has also been realized. Not only have we recorded the agency of different actors within the Caribbean when exploring the links with China, but we have also attempted to promote such agency in our approach by emphasizing the theories and analytical contributions of regional authors in our work (see Gonzalez-Vicente and Montoute, 2020). The research team worked closely together, meeting at international conferences and carrying out significant theoretical/empirical discussions over email and telephone.

11601015.label: Major findings and research outcome
11601015.value: We would like to highlight the following major findings: SPACES OF EXCEPTION In an article in Business and Politics (Gonzalez-Vicente, 2019), we discuss how despite the lack of overarching economic policy conditionalities, Chinese projects require ‘spaces of exception’ to operate profitably. In such spaces, sovereignty is flexibly readapted to accommodate the accumulation rationales of Chinese investors (including levies on custom duties and the ability to hire Chinese workers toiling under Chinese labour regimes). The notion of ‘spaces of exception’ helps to explain how despite the lack of national level conditionalities, Chinese investments require host countries to transform their political geographies to adapt to the profit-making requirements of Chinese businesses. MECHANISMS OF ACCUMULATION The idea of ‘mechanisms of accumulation’ (Gonzalez-Vicente, 2019) adds nuance to Ching Kwan Lee’s argument that some Chinese SOEs operate under a ‘logics of accumulation’ that is not only profit-orientated but responds also to broader state goals. Chinese infrastructural investment in the Caribbean represents a distinct form of capital when compared with local and transnational construction companies in the region. The combination of Chinese state-led ‘predistribution’ through government-to-government arrangements in the Caribbean, and firm-based accumulation, adds up to a distinct mechanism of accumulation that allows Chinese corporations to operate profitably where others could not. THE BRI FROM A CARIBBEAN DEVELOPMENT THOUGHT PERSPECTIVE In this project (Gonzalez-Vicente and Montoute, 2020) we revise a number of critical theories from Caribbean authors (mostly from the 1960s and 1970s, but not only) that have allowed us to gain important insights into the trajectories of Chinese capital in the region and beyond. Some of these theories (e.g. passive incorporation, epistemic dependency) are well suited to characterize the Belt and Road Initiative beyond the region. RECONFIGURATION OF OFFSHORE FINANCIAL NETWORKS AND CHINA-BVI LINKAGES Despite its high profile historically in connecting China to the outside financial world, the British Virgin Islands (BVI) is no longer as central in China-Caribbean relations (Robertson 2019). This case demonstrates a different trajectory than growing FDI ties. Decisions taken in China’s political economy to close down routes for capital exit outweigh the forceful promotion efforts of BVI actors. We would like to point out to the RGC that several journals erred and did not report RGC funding, despite asking for grant details and being reminded at the proofs stage (see attached proofs for Robertson 2019). We will be insistent with forthcoming publications that the RGC be listed as the funding body.

11601015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11601015.value: China’s relations with the Caribbean continue to change. Now, still in the midst of the COVID-19 crisis, questions are being asked about the sustainability of a number of Chinese projects. As the relationship evolved in the last few years, some local governments pushed for economic engagements beyond natural resource extraction and infrastructural development. There are plans for three PRC-financed industrial parks in the region, which could potentially create a significant number of jobs and help to diversify local economies. However, it remains unclear whether these parks could be competitive at a regional or global scale, particularly given the high costs of production in the Caribbean and the impossibility of ‘developmentalist’ policies within the highly open economies of the Caribbean. A new set of questions would be raised if these industrial parks were to develop into ‘Special Economic Zones’ for Chinese corporations to operate in the region, and thus spaces of ‘graduated sovereignty’ where local labour regulations and taxes were waived. From a geopolitical perspective, the United States seems adamant to regain its influence in the region, and judging from a few developments in the last few months this could result in open economic and diplomatic competition with China. From a social perspective, many social groups are still waiting to see tangible development results derived from the high debts acquired with China (up to USD 8.9 billion), and are likely to continue resisting the presence of Chinese businesses if these do not help to raise living standards. All these issues require continued attention, and the researchers in the team will seek funding to investigate these and other questions.

11601015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11601015.value: The People Republic of China’s relationship with the Caribbean has significantly intensified in the last 20 years. This project investigated the multiple channels of interaction between the two regions, with a focus on the developmental dimensions of the relation. The project has unveiled the various reasons that drive Chinese businesses to the Caribbean, and the social, political and economic implications of a large variety of PRC projects in the region. The project has been able to further our understanding of PRC – the contested adaptation of Chinese businesses to local contexts, the deployment of the Belt and Road Initiative in the region, and Taiwan's diplomatic struggles for recognition in the Caribbean. From this vantage point, we have made contributions to global debates on the Belt and Road Initiative, China’s foreign policy, transformations of the global economy, and the changing face of development cooperation. The project has resulted in a range of academic publications in prestigious outlets, and also in contributions to social and policy debates in the Caribbean.

11601315.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11601315.value: 全稱量化及相關概念的跨語言研究及其語義地圖

11601315.label: Project Objectives
11601315.value: To straighten out the inter-relation between universal quantification and other related notions (e.g., distributivity, maximality, exclusiveness, exhaustivity, additivity, focus-sensitivity). To pin down formally the difference among Chinese universal quantifier expressions in a unified conceptual framework and integrate the less-studied phenomenon (e.g., the bound variable use of mei-CL-NPs/ge-NPs and one-CL-NPs) into the picture of quantification. To conduct a comparative study of universal quantification in English and Chinese and project the cross-linguistic variance onto a unified semantic map.

11601315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11601315.value: In the literature of quantification, many studies are directed specifically at universal quantifier expressions which require that something is true with every relevant thing, since the universal quantifier ∀ is one of the two standard quantifiers in first-order predicate logic. Yet, despite the abundant research, the picture of universal quantification in Chinese is still murky and a consensus is not even reached on how universal quantification is instantiated in Chinese. For instance, one of such quantifiers, Chinese dou, conventionally treated as a universal quantifier, is also analyzed as a marker of focus, scalar presupposition, anti-expectation, sum formation, maximality, exhaustification. This project aims to push forward the study of universal quantification by meeting a three-fold objective. First, it seeks to pin down the range of universal quantifier expressions in Chinese and straighten out the relation and difference between universal quantification and the above mentioned notions. The guiding hypothesis is: The basic semantic component of expressions like "dou" is universal quantification and the diverse effects they bring forth are attributed to the sorts of entities they quantify over and the ways of quantificational mapping. Second, it provides an in-depth account of all the expressions related to universal quantification in Chinese. In particular, it aims to fill the gaps of existing theories by tackling universal quantificational phenomena less studied or untouched upon in Chinese, e.g., the co-occurrence of multiple universal quantifiers, and the bound variable interpretations of mei-CL-NPs 'every-NP'/ge-NPs 'each-NP' and one-CL-NPs which may change the conventional views of the former as a generalized quantifier and the latter as an indefinite introducing a new discourse referent. Third, based on the study above, it further draws on cross-linguistic data to complete the semantic map of universal quantification, which may uncover the shared conceptual space of universal quantification across languages. The project will contribute to the study of quantification and indefinites by linking up and sorting out the related notions to universal quantification. Empirically, the study will enrich the picture of universal quantification by unraveling new quantificational patterns in Chinese and other languages and analyzing them in a unified conceptual framework. More importantly, the project is unique in that the theoretical claims will be further verified and strengthened by plotting the semantic map of universal quantification. The outcomes can further deepen the connection among standard logical equipment, the processing of natural language in the human mind, language typology and language acquisition. 全称量词是一阶逻辑中的两个基本量词之一（另一个是存在量词），因此全称量化表达也一直是自然语言形式语义研究的重点。然而，尽管这方面的研究成果颇丰，前人就汉语全称量化表达的范围和意义特点并未达成一致。例如，汉语中的“都”除了被处理成全称量词以外，也被分析成标记焦点、量级预设、反预期、最大化、加合操作或穷尽性的成分。 本项目计划在前人研究的基础上进一步探索汉语及其他语言中的全称量化表达，主要的目标有如下三点：一、重新确定汉语全称量化表达的范围并厘清全称量化与量级预设、最大化、穷尽性等概念之间的关系；二、对汉语全称量化表达进行精确的形式化定义，确保这些定义能凸显不同表达各自的语义特点且符合组合性原则；三、在上述汉语研究的基础上，对其他语言中的全称量化表达进行考察并绘制全称量化语义地图以揭示自然语言普遍涉及的全称量化概念空间。 本项目的理论贡献有三大部分：一、对于全称量化与其它相关概念的关系的考量在学界尚属首次；二、本项目将考查诸多汉语中尚未受到关注的量化表达方式、并为这些语料构建一个统一的解释框架；三、跨语言全称量化语义地图的绘制可为自然语言量化理论的完善提供实证支持。本项目的研究成果还有助于建立逻辑工具与自然语言加工机制之间的联系，对语言类型学研究及语言习得等领域也会有诸多启示。

11601315.label: Realisation of objectives
11601315.value: We carried out the research of this project as planned and achieved all the three objectives, outputting a series of works which appear on or are accepted by journals of high quality. To realize the objectives, we have analyzed theoretical notions with care, explored language facts in depth, and made extensive cross-linguistic comparison. As for Objective 1, we sort out the inter-relation between universal quantification and its related notions, including distributivity, exhaustivity and exclusiveness, based on the language data of Chinese. We conclude that distributivity, exhaustivity and exclusiveness can all be umbrellaed under the notion of universal quantification, and that these meanings are the manifestation of universal quantification and different quantificational mapping mechanisms. We further point out that the mapping of universal quantificational expressions can be regulated by topic-comment structure and background-focus structure. Moreover, we pin down the difference between universal quantification and notions which are often mixed up with universality, i.e., maximality, scalarity and indication of a high degree. In particular, departing from the diverse uses of mandarin ‘dou’ (all), a morpheme that expresses universal quantification, we show that universal quantification involves a component of maximality, that universal quantification when interacting with a contrastive focus can derive the meaning of scalarity, and that universal quantification which expresses that no exception is allowed naturally indicates a high degree on an ordered scale. Hence, in the existing literature, universal quantification and these notions often converge in the analyses of morphemes such as dou. However, through our studies, we have shown that universal quantification is the core semantics of such morphemes and that the other notions are partial manifestation of universal quantification. By straightening out the relations of the above mentioned semantic notions, we believe that the future studies on the diverse use of universal quantificational expressions in different languages can be more precise and more thorough. We present out analysis related with Objective 1 in details in Pan and Feng (2017), Feng and Pan (2018) and Feng and Pan (to appear). As for Objective 2, we tackles a number of less-studied yet important phenomenon of universal quantification in Chinese. First, we discuss extensively the application of the notion of cover on the analysis of the universal dou in Mandarin, pointing out that cover and non-atom-based distribution is not a necessary semantic component of dou; rather, the apparent cases of cover-based distribution can be explained away by assuming an implicit argument in the VP denotation within the scope of dou. Also, we further single out the types of VP predicates which have a slot for an implicit argument, which thus specifies under what conditions dou seems to distribute down to plural sets rather than individual atoms. The analysis of dou and the application of cover is presented in Feng and Pan (2017). Second, we investigate cases where dou does not seem to exert a universal force, and based on the apparent cases where dou allows for exceptions, we generalize that the domain of universal quantification is relativized to various factors, including contextual restriction and speakers’ perspectives. The research findings in this aspect are published in Feng and Pan (2018). Thirdly, we present new data concerning the distribution of mei, a conventionally assumed universal determiner in Mandarin, and investigates its interaction with dou. Multiple studies have raised the issue of double quantification with respect to the co-occurrence of the two morphemes, as it is possible that both morphemes exert their quantificational force on the same nominal domain. To solve this puzzle, we propose to treat mei as a one-place operator over the nominal domain which does not have a complete quantificational structure; therefore, its primary function is to collect entities to contribute to the domain of dou and thus will not cause the predicament of double quantification. This approach to the semantics of mei can shed light on the possible treatment of the co-occurrence of multiple quantificational elements and push forward the exploration of the finer components of quantificational operators in the sense of Generalized Quantifier Theory. The work in this aspect is to be published in Zhang and Pan (to appear). Fourthly, we investigate the interaction between universal quantifiers and polarity sensitive wh-phrases, and approach the distribution of the latter from the perspective of monotonicity and entailment patterns. We are among the first to propose that the distribution of wh-phrases in Chinese is sensitive to decreasing environments and that the restrictor of dou is subsumed under the category of decreasing contexts. The work concerning this issue will be published in Chen and Pan (to appear). Fifthly, we give a systematic review of the problems with the maximality approach to dou, and show that empirically and theoretically the notion of maximality is inadequate to define the semantic contribution of dou. The maximality approach was proposed a dozen years ago and is taken as a primary assumption in many follow-up studies. Our study is the first to sort out the problems with this approach with care, which offers a fair discussion of the more traditional quantificational approach to dou. The work in this aspect is to be published in Feng and Pan (to appear). As for Objective 3, we conduct a careful comparison of universal quantificational expressions in Chinese, including dou, mei and ge. Also, we further single out the similarities and differences between Chinese and English universal quantifier expressions in terms of their monotonicity behavior, quantificational mapping strategies, focus-sensitivity and restrictions on their domain and scope. In particular, departing from the less-studied Chinese data, we manage to show that the mapping between sentential materials and quantificational structures is related to diverse factors, including contextual information, syntactic structure, topic-comment structure and background-focus structure. Some quantificational expressions, e.g., only, allow only one type of strategies, which results in its dedicated use; however, some other ones, e.g., dou, allow multiple strategies to apply, which helps explain its diverse meaning interpretations. The categorization of quantificational morphemes from the perspective of mapping strategies offers a novel way of cross-linguistic comparison; moreover, the perspective can explain why the same logical meaning can have very different manifestation in natural language. The work in this aspect is published in Pan and Feng (2017), Feng and Pan (2017) and Feng and Pan (2018).

11601315.label: Major findings and research outcome
11601315.value: Our major findings pertain to three major aspects, i.e., the theoretical analysis of semantic notions related to universal quantificational logic, the formal analysis of less-studied quantificational phenomenon in Chinese, and a more thorough and extensive comparison of universal quantificational expressions in Chinese and English. Essentially, we argue that due to different quantificational mapping strategies, the logic of universal quantification has two major types of manifestation in natural language, i.e., exclusiveness and exhaustiveness. Furthermore, due to the different makeup of the domain of quantification, the use of exclusiveness can express distributivity, high degree, scalarity and unexpectedness. Similarly, if the domain of quantification contains ordered alternatives, then the use of exhaustiveness can also take on the meaning of scalarity (Feng and Pan 2017, Pan and Feng 2017, Feng and Pan 2018, Feng and Pan (to appear)). In this way, we manage to tease apart the core semantics of quantificational expressions and the related epiphenomena. Also, we give novel analyses of specific quantificational expressions in Chinese, which have important theoretical consequences for the research on co-occurrence of quantifiers, distributive relation, monotonicity and wh-indeterminates (Feng and Pan 2017, Feng and Pan 2018, Chen and Pan to appear, Zhang and Pan to appear). We solve the puzzle of double quantification by dividing the labor of universal quantification between dou and mei in a more reasonable way, explain away the non-atomic distribution of dou by postulating an implicit argument in the VP, and capture the distribution of wh-indeterminates in the restrictor of dou in terms of monotonicity behaviors. Moreover, departing from the Chinese data, we make a more thorough comparison between English and Chinese universal quantifications and capture the cross-linguistic difference in meaning from the perspective of quantificational mapping. Through the cross-linguistic comparison, we show that the apparent diverse use of certain expressions, e.g., dou, is not so special as former studies assume. The items in the stock of universal quantification share the same logical core; and the different meanings in actual use can be attributed to the interaction between quantificational force and information structure, pragmatic information and grammatical factors (Feng and Pan 2017, Feng and Pan 2018, Chen and Pan to appear).

11601315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11601315.value: The research of this project can be furthered in three directions. First, we notice that the research on the dialectal difference of universal quantificational expressions in Chinese is scarce. The research in this aspect is important for the exploration of quantificational logic in natural language, the generation of a semantic map of quantification and the inquiry about the universality of different linguistic varieties. Second, we provide a solution to the co-occurrence of two universal quantificational elements in a single sentence, and plan to further our study on the co-occurrence and meaning composition of three or more quantificational elements in a single sentence. Lastly, aside from quantificational mapping strategies, we plan to take a closer look at the difference between Chinese and English quantifiers in terms of the makeup of their quantificational domain and scope. Such a finer approach to quantificational meanings can uncover the level linguistic diversity in a more exquisite way, which thus sheds light on the universality and specificity of natural language.

11601315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11601315.value: This project investigates the manifestation of universal quantification in natural language and explains why universal quantificational expressions, e.g., all and each in English, and dou(都) and mei(每) in Chinese, can express a variety of meanings, including surprise, unexpectedness, exclusiveness, exhaustivity and high degrees. It shows that the diverse uses result from the interaction of quantificational logical, grammatical structure and contextual information. For different universal quantificational expressions, our research manages to specify the respective restrictions on their distribution and interpretations and derive their meanings in different sentences using formal logic. In particular, we offer a critical review of the diverse approaches to the meaning of the much debated morpheme dou(都), analyzing their respective motivation and problems and offering a fair discussion of the tradition of Chinese semantic research in the international academia. Our research bridges the research on logic with that on natural language meanings and pushes forward the formalization of complex natural language phenomena, which further facilitates the uncovering of universality and specificity of different languages and the realization of more effective interaction between computers and human languages.
