11612715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11612715.value: 本研究将在中美历史关系的框架下探索美国作家项美丽（1905-97）的新闻文学。她一生共出版五十二部著作，发表文章数百篇，可谓事业有成，然而其作品却鲜少受到学界关注。本文重心将放在三十年代末至四十年代初，项美丽在中国内地和香港生活时为《纽约客》杂志撰写的稿件上，并结合日渐增长的新闻文学研究进行论述。 虽然新闻报道的文学价值早已为人所知，过往的学术研究却主要集中在查尔斯·狄更斯、史蒂芬·克萊恩、乔治·奥威尔等著名小说家的作品上。近年来，针对新闻写作的研究开始拓宽自身范围，纳入各色社会背景与批判视角（2009年新成立的新闻文学国际学术组织及期刊即为一例）。当今全球化背景下，大型媒体机构的影响力得到进一步扩大和发挥，个体报道则往往被遗失或淹没。因此，这片学术探索的新领域与现实高度相关，值得关注。 本研究将利用档案资料，采用女权主义及比较文学等不同视角去展现项美丽在现代新闻事业发展中所占据的重要位置，并进一步揭示二十世纪时中国是如何被描述及呈现给美国读者的。

11612715.label: Realisation of objectives
11612715.value: The first aim of the project was “To historically situate Emily Hahn’s oeuvre in relation to other writers of the period and to reveal how notions of national and cultural identity were explored through an engagement with journalistic, literary, and autobiographical discourses.” In the published work that I produced on Hahn, particularly in my book “Literary Encounters in Twentieth-Century China,” I trace the inter-textual links between Hahn and other literary texts of the period while showing that Hahn’s work was influenced by trends in autobiographical writing, cinema and journalism. While showing that Hahn’s descriptions of life in Shanghai and Hong Kong describe political and historical events, I point to the ways that many of her works blur fact and fiction in provocative ways. Through close readings of Hahn’s works I make connections with writers like Ernest Hemingway, Somerset Maugham, and the film maker Josef von Sternberg. These references reveal that the setting of China was an ambivalent location for the Western imagination where ‘modern’ social identities were explored and tested. The second aim of the project was “To narrow a theoretical and methodological gap in knowledge about how ideas of gender were rhetorically constructed in twentieth-century non-fiction, and how such gendered positions influenced the way that China was represented to American readers.” This aim was achieved as I discuss Hahn’s feminist rewriting of fallen-women tropes. While I deal with this topic in my book, a more detailed discussion of Hahn’s engagement with gender will appear in a forthcoming article for the Journal of Modern Literature. This article, entitled “Rising Stars and Fallen Women: Writing Lives in Emily Hahn’s China,” argues that Hahn subverts moralistic discourses around proper female conduct outside of the domestic sphere. In this article I focus mostly on Hahn’s novel “Miss Jill,” a non-fiction novel that depicts the life of a British prostitute in China. Apart from these outputs, the project also supported related research on other popular and middlebrow writers of this period. I wrote and published an article in “The CEA Critic” on James Hilton’s Lost Horizon which argues that popular literature can complicate Orientalist conceptions of the East while also challenging stereotypical notions of imperial masculinity. While this project does not deal with Emily Hahn’s writings specifically, it nevertheless engages with literature of the period broadly and sheds light on the ways in which ideas of gender interact with conceptualizations of the East. The third aim of the project was “To reveal how bifurcated ideas of Chinese and American identity during the twentieth century were challenged in a context of cross-cultural collaboration, cosmopolitanism, and translation.” In my work on Emily Hahn I describe how she was involved with translation projects and bilingual publishing in Shanghai, while at the same time I argue that her works were provocative insofar as Hahn transgressed socially acceptable boundaries that typically divided expatriates from local Chinese residents. Apart from my work on Hahn, however, the article that I wrote on Han Suyin in the journal “Interventions” also reveals similar thematic and theoretical concerns about cross-cultural writing and cosmopolitan identity during the 1920s and 30s. Although the two writers appear to have been unaware of each other, both of them wrote during the same period and published their works for an expanding American readership and provide insights into life in China ‘up-close’. One challenge for this project was utilizing some of the funds that were made available. While the funds for archival research were indispensable, the funds for research support were less useful. While there may have been ways in involve research assistants who could help with some of the work or provide support, I found that it was difficult to find capable research assistants who would be able to contribute to the analysis of the texts or to help locate information through archival research. Much of this work, it turns out, needed to be done by myself. One exception to this was when I involved a research assistant to help with a special issue of Wasafiri Magazine that was co-editing. In this case, the research assistant was very helpful in transcribing some materials for an interview and helping communicate with contributors. This special issue dealt with contemporary Hong Kong writing, a project that does not have an obvious connection with the main objectives of this grant, but which nevertheless addresses several relevant theoretical and thematic concerns including the status of Asia in Western writing, the blurry lines between autobiography and fiction, and the status of gender identity in literary narratives.

11612715.label: Major findings and research outcome
11612715.value: This project revealed that Emily Hahn’s writings have literary and historical importance in the context of British and American representations of China. The main outcome, therefore, is the recognition of Hahn’s work as significant and meaningful in broad historical terms. The main findings of the project are conveyed through the main research output, which is a book that deals with Hahn alongside other British and American authors who travelled in China during this period. This book was published with Routledge in 2019. The findings are also conveyed in an article that deals specifically with Emily Hahn that is forthcoming in the “Journal of Modern Literature” (a top journal in the field of literary studies). These publications will bring more academic attention to Hahn and her writings in the field of early twentieth-century literature and modernist studies. These studies also shed light on the historical evolution of women’s writing during the twentieth century and the convergences between literary, journalistic, and autobiographical modes. A paper on Emily Hahn was delivered at the American Literature Association conference in 2018. Other findings of this project include historical work on other writers of the period, beyond Hahn and her oeuvre. The article “Hygienic Modernity and Han Suyin’s Destination Chungking” describes the historical context of the Sino-Japanese war from an autobiographical perspective and provides another point of view on how writers negotiated the social and political terrain during this period. While the article “Middlebrow Aesthetics in James Hilton’s Lost Horizon” deals with a different context and a different genre of literature, it similarly engages with the context of China and its borderlands as a space for the Western imagination. Both of these studies deal with themes and issues that are relevant to project’s main focus and broaden its impact.

11612715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11612715.value: The project laid the foundations for my current work that continues to deal with China’s representation in Western literature. I am now pursuing a topic that focuses on Harriet Monroe, a writer and editor of the period who maintained a long-time interest in Chinese literature and culture. While this project on Hahn dealt with autobiographical and journalistic writing, this current work focuses more on poetry and the context of modern literary publishing. This project, therefore, can be viewed as a logical continuation of the project on Hahn and is currently being supported by another 3-year GRF. At the same time, I hopeful that I can one day return to some of Hahn’s writings, particularly those she produced while living in Hong Kong during the Japanese occupation. While I allude to her book “Hong Kong Holiday” in my book, I believe there is potential here for a fuller exploration of Hong Kong’s status in American writing during the mid-twentieth century.

11612715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11612715.value: This research project focused on the literary journalism of the American writer Emily Hahn (1905-97), situating her work in relation to mid-twentieth American print culture and in the context of historical relations between America and China. This project revealed how Emily Hahn played an important role in mediating China for Western audiences through a playful and complex negotiation of truth telling and storytelling. Drawing on archival sources, the research explores Hahn’s writings from the critical perspectives of narratology, feminism, and comparative literature, offering original insights into the changing historical circumstances of modern literary journalism and reveal more about how China was brought up-close to American readers during the twentieth century. The main outputs of this project include a book, three journal articles, and a conference paper.

11613315.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11613315.value: 中国法院上访中的话语

11613315.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11613315.value: Dr Ng, Kwaihang Prof Peerenboom, Randall

11613315.label: Project Objectives
11613315.value: Different from previous studies that rely on archival research, textual analyses of legal regulations and published judgments, or drawing from sporadic interviews, media reports, and anecdotal accounts to study the petition system in China, this Project will employ a new method – by directly examining the dynamics of petitioning conferences. It will identify the genres and characteristics of discourses deployed by the petitioners and petition officials, which will form the basis to understand the developing legal consciousness of the petitioners and the operational patterns of the petition system in Chinese courts. Scholars often attribute the increasing number of petitions to the economic compensations provided by the authorities to the petitioners (Yu 2005; Cai 2004). The Project seeks to understand, through studying the interactions in the process of petitioning conferences, how the claims of most petitioners are not seriously addressed, but only diverted into legal or extra-legal institutions. It thus offers a new explanation to the limit of the petition system in dispute resolution. Specifically, it explores how the discourses between the petitioners and the officials are mismatched and how the disputes are reproduced as a result of the channeling strategies of the officials. As a dispute resolution mechanism, the petition system has been hailed for allowing resentful citizens to blow off steam, protecting disadvantaged groups, strengthening central supervision over local administration (Cai 2004; Ying 2004; Peerenboom and He 2009). This Project explores the extent to which the petition system may undermine the rights of petitioners and how the system may steer new petitioners into an endless process. It will shed light on the hidden problems created by a system that values the short-term goal of social harmony over the delivery of justice. It thus raises important questions with regard to China’s policies on the petition system. Policy recommendations will be generated for reforms. Through examining how petitioning complaints are handled in China, this Project will provide a story of dispute transformation in China’s context. It is widely regarded that the dispute transformation is unidirectional (Felstiner el al 1980-1981) and litigation is the final destination. The handling process of petitioning in China, however, suggests that the dispute transformation could be multi-directional, depending on whether or not the petitioners follow the channeling advice of the petition officials and the outcome of the processing. Exploring the social forces underneath the interactions in the petition system of Chinese courts, it enriches the literature of comparative studies on dispute transformation, which has most drawn from the experience of other countries (Felstiner el al 1980-1981; Merry 1990; Comaroff and Roberts 1981; Boyum and Mather eds. 1983).

11613315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11613315.value: The petition system is a vital sector in China’s dispute resolution process. Despite the proliferation of literature on the system, few efforts have been made to understand the trajectories of petitioners' legal consciousness, how they frame their grievances, and what discourses petition officials deploy to respond. To fill the gap, this Project will expand our preliminary study to six courts with their representative profiles of different levels of hierarchy, economic and institutional development, political pressures, and judicial professionalism. Drawing upon petition office ethnography and interviews with relevant petitioners and petition officials/judges, this Project will identify the genres and characteristics of discourses employed by both the petitioners and petition officials in Chinese courts. It examines how the two groups interact during petition meetings and explores how the process influences the formation of further grievances. The findings of this Project are critical to understand how justice is exercised in the petition system of Chinese courts. The Project will not only generate policy recommendations for reforms to the petition system in China, but also provide evidence for broader theoretical debates about dispute transformation and the relationship between law, politics, and perception of justice. 本项目研究法庭中上访当事人的话语。通过对几个法庭上访办公室的访谈，我们试图找到上访当事人及法官的话语的类型及其它意义。它将弥补这一领域的空白。

11613315.label: Major findings and research outcome
11613315.value: It finds that the petitioners fight to frame their disputes in legal terms, while the petition officials use a “channeling discourse” to divert the petitioners to legal or extralegal institutions. The two types of discourse barely confront each other; nor are the substantive issues seriously debated. Since being channeled into other institutions does not resolve their disputes, petitioners start calling their petitioning experiences as injurious, blaming officials, and making new claims. Disputes are thus reproduced. We also analyze how the regime’s political concern for social stability transforms petitioners’ disputes and shapes the evolution of their legal consciousness. Compared with first-time petitioners, who often address their complaints within a legal paradigm, the veteran petitioners take advantage of the judges’ political concern for social stability and present their disputes as potentially threatening social stability.

11613315.value: our research provides futile grounds for quantitative research.

11613315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11613315.value: Drawing on empirical data collected from petitioners in Chinese courts, we analyze the discourse genres and how the regime’s political concern for social stability transforms petitioners’ disputes and shapes the evolution of their legal consciousness. Petitioners hold the judiciary responsible for their plight; they petition courts during “sensitive periods”; they employ innovative tactics to draw official attention; and they seek to secure government stability-maintenance funds as a substitute for legal remedies. However, in framing a legal dispute as a political problem, the veteran petitioners risk retaliation. This article’s analysis provides insights into the operation of the court petition system, howthe legal consciousness ofChinese petitioners evolves, and how in the petitioners’ eyes the legitimacy of the legal system gets eroded.

11614515.label: Project Objectives
11614515.value: To analyze the way identity is constructed in the context of a social network such as Facebook, especially with regard to: - The discursive strategies Facebook-users apply to present their life in public. - The logic employed by the algorithm to present users’ actions on their Facebook-site. - The ‘hidden narrative’ that can be found in the users’ deliberate report and the algorithms automated recording. To determine the different strategies and results of autobiographical writing done in the framework of Facebook and compare them to writing in the setting of a traditional diary. To identify the functions of narrative, non-narrative as well as “numerical-narrative” forms of self-understanding in the age of digitization and datafication To explore how new forms of implicit and automated self-description affect the praxis of explicit and reflective self-understanding and how the subject constitutes identity through the apparatuses of digital and social media.

11614515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11614515.value: The shift from Web 1.0 to Web 2.0 has provided new tools of self-expression which are significantly different from traditional forms of self-presentation and autobiographical writing. Individual statements on personal websites, weblogs, and social networks are publicly accessible and subject the autobiographic self to immediate feedback and permanent evaluation. In social networks explicit forms of self-expression are accompanied and increasingly replaced by automated recording of personal data. The resulting autobiography is an assemblage of deliberate verbal and non-verbal utterances and automated records of the user’s actions and of other users’ interactions (postings, comments, visits, likes, shares etc.). In contrast to traditional autobiographical writing, those reports or records about the self are not the result of self-reflexive identity construction but the datafied mirror of a self that is constructed through its actions in and beyond the social network. Combining the expertise of scholars in literary and media studies and blending close reading of autobiographical writing with the analysis of the technical and social frameworks of such writing, this project aims to understand how the affordances and constraints of digital technology in social networks change autobiographical writing and self-understanding. The primary data will come from a six-week period analysis of twenty Facebook-accounts as well as diaries kept simultaneously during two weeks of that period by ten of the participants. The reported events (status updates and interactions with other sites) and responses (comments, likes, shares) on the Facebook-accounts will be analyzed for keyword patterns and cause and effect trajectories as ‘hidden narratives’. The analysis of the diaries will shed light on the differences between self-description within the interactive constellation of a social network and self-description undertaken without time pressure, space limits, and pending interaction. Data will also include in-depth qualitative interviews with participants about their own retrospective understanding of the time covered on their Facebook-site and in their diary and about their awareness of revealed relations between entries on their Facebook-site. The project will provide an understanding of the role certain techniques of self-expression in digital and social media play in contemporary forms of identity construction. Results of the project will be used to design an undergraduate general education course on autobiographical writing in digital media. 文本作為故事、事件和數據─電子媒體敘事方式的再媒介化

11614515.label: Major findings and research outcome
11614515.value: Our research about the way identity is constructed in the context of a social network leads to the following result: Facebook users favour a passive attitude towards the platform, i.e. to remain in contact with friends and check others’ statuses and to favour, if they do post or share something, “other-related” content, such as news or entertainment. When they do publish about themselves the content tends to be carefully curated, with positive posts dominating over negative ones. The current low frequency of posting, combined with a reduced self-exposure makes it difficult to retrieve even small stories or “to fill the gaps”, as Ruth Page suggests (see research proposal). It is no surprise that not posting, nor sharing, nor commenting, but liking is the most frequent activity on Facebook. However, liking is an almost subliminal act and it lacks even the minimal features of tellability. We therefore can say, that self-narration on Facebook becomes elusive: it is a constantly deferred process, a mirroring game made up of a few posts (only a minority of which about the user) amidst ads and news. Rather than dots whose reconnection would lead to a coherent picture of the self, posts about and by the self are small, rare windows, interspersed throughout the Timeline, and often opening onto lives on which external readers can only speculate. It is, indeed, only by knowing the user intimately or through his/her active cooperation (i.e. keeping a diary within our research project) that it becomes possible to reconstruct small stories about the self. Breaking down the data of our study to detect trends concerning the ways in which Facebook is used and the responses that such uses trigger we were able to advance a six part typology of users according to the kinds of posts published, the type of authorship behind the postings, and the amount of likes and comments received. The fragmentation of the corpus into six types of users suggests a rather skilful and personalized re-appropriation of the platform’s technical features by the participants. Such re-appropriation can be seen as a reaction to the feeling of over-exposure by the participants insofar as each user, far from being merely “played” by the platform, proves able to customize the use s/he makes of Facebook depending on the audience addressed, his/her interests and purposes, as well as the adoption of other SNS alongside Facebook.

11614515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11614515.value: It is not solely a matter of recognizing the posthuman logic of self-narration behind Facebook, but of acknowledging that the self has been eventually evicted from its own story, either by Facebook or due to self-discipline. As a reaction, the writing of the self has been displaced and fragmented through other Social Network Sites such as Instagram, WhatsApp and increasingly Snapchat or delegated altogether to face-to-face communication. The subject of subsequent investigation could be to what extent such development turns Facebook into a mere news-aggregator and a sort of nostalgic database which reminds users of who they were rather than who they are becoming. Central to such investigation is naturally to detect the contribution of those alternative Social Network Sites to the online identity construction of the contemporary individual.

11614915.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11614915.value: 政府機構中的組織目標模糊性: 總統,國會,和正式授權

11614915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11614915.value: Organizations have goals and pursue them. Goals vary in their ambiguity and clarity. Public organizations vary in the ambiguity of their performance goals. Prominent public administration scholars and political scientists have asserted that ambiguous goals can make public managers’ decision-making less effective, dampen employees’ motivation and job satisfaction, and harm individual and organizational performance. These arise because of the lack of clarity about how to achieve unclear goals and the difficulty in evaluating individual and organizational performance while asking for accountability. In this regard, many recent governmental (new public management) reform initiatives have included directives that government agencies state performance goals, clarify them, and measure the accomplishment levels of them. Given the theoretical and practical importance of organizational goal ambiguity, it is valuable to investigate what important independent variables (e.g., President, legislature, interest groups, and managers’ leadership) influence organizational goal ambiguity in government agencies and what contingencies modify the relationships between the independent variables and goal ambiguity. The aim of the proposed study is to contribute to this debate by focusing on the relationships between the two most influential political actors at the central government level (i.e., President and Congress), the ambiguity of formal mandates, and organizational goal ambiguity. This study will examine if stronger political influences lead to greater ambiguity in formal mandates, which in turn increases goal ambiguity. The proposed study team has undertaken extensive research on organizational goal ambiguity, including its measurements and its negative influences, and on political actors’ influence on government agencies’ autonomy, using various statistical methods. This study will develop a unique dataset on all central government agencies in South Korea from the three most recent administrations and implement regression techniques that take account of time. Such data are available in few countries. The findings will contribute to our understanding of goal ambiguity and the improvement of a conceptual framework or an empirical theory of goal ambiguity in public organizations. The findings will also help public managers to devise appropriate strategies and techniques for dealing with mandates and organizational (performance) goals that may need clarification, and thereby improve organizational performance and accountability. 組織都有目標並且追求實現它們。目標的模糊和清晰是變化的。公共組織的績效目標的模糊性也是變化的。傑出的公共行政學者和政治學家指出模糊的目標會降低公共管理者的決策效率，削弱公務員的積極性和工作滿意度，並且對個人和組織的績效有害。這些弊端的出現是因為對於如何達成不清楚的目標不夠明確，並且在問責的時候評估個人和組織績效有困難。關於這點，許多近期的政府（新公共管理）改革的舉措就包括了關於政府機構需要提出績效目標，闡明這些目標，並且衡量目標的實現等級的指示。 鑒於組織目標模糊性的理論和實際意義，探究在政府機構中哪些變量（例如：總統，立法機關，利益集團，和管理者的領導力）會影響組織的目標模糊性，以及什麼意外因素會改變這些變量和目標模糊之間的關係是非常有價值的。本研究旨在通過关注兩個在中央政府中最有影響的政治行為體（總統和國會），正式授權的模糊性和組織目標的模糊性之間的關係對這些爭論做出貢獻。本研究將檢驗是否較強的政治影響會導致更大的正式授權的模糊性，並轉而提高目標的模糊程度。 本研究團隊已經運用各種統計方法，對組織目標的模糊性，包括它的測量和負面影響，以及對政治行為體之于政府機構自主性的影響有了廣泛的研究。本研究將從韓國最近的三屆政府中針對所有中央政府機構建立專門的數據集，並且考慮時間因素運用回歸分析。此類數據只在少數國家可以獲取。本研究的結論將對我們對於公共組織中目標模糊的理解，目標模糊的概念性框架或實證理論的發展做出貢獻。並且會幫助公共管理者發展出處理需要闡明的授權和組織績效目標的合適的策略和技巧，進而提高組織績效和改善問責制。

11615815.value: ＜《三國志演義》及韓国文化認同的形成＞

11615815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11615815.value: ＜《三國志演義》及韓国文化認同的形成＞是一個原創的案例研究項目。《本項目將通過研究《三國志演義》对形成韓国人文化認同的影响去看傳統文學和文化在東亞之間的相互影響。 本項目有五個目標： 1. 弄清《三國志演義》如何在東亞中影響著韓國人對過去五個世紀的文化和歷史認同的構成。 2. 分辨《三國志演義》在韓國朝鮮時代出產的各重要版本及改篇。 3. 通過研究朝鮮女性抄寫的《三國志演義》的手抄本，分析女性作家在朝鮮時代的發展。從而得知當時的女性抄寫員不只是一個抄寫員，更擔當了一個文本批判者和修改者的角色。另外，這也可說明當時的韓國女性曾密切參與到文本閱讀及改寫。 4. 研究現代《三國志演義》的改寫如何反映作者和文本消費者的意識形態觀點。 5. 透過觀察及研究玩家如何在《三國志演義》電腦遊戲中按照他們的意願改寫歷史，我們可以得知作者和讀者的關係在《三國志演義》電腦遊戲是如何發展的。 為了支持我的論點及達到本項目的首要目的：「讓讀者明白《三國志演義》對韓國文化認同構成的重要性」，我將以兩個案例分別闡述。第一個研究重點是朝鮮時代的女性抄寫員是如何在抄寫時對文本進行編輯；另外由於現代互動式媒體持續地對《三國志演義》的歷史作重塑，所以另一研究重點將著眼於《三國志演義》中歷史敘述的轉變。此兩個案例所呈現的內容可能不盡一致，但兩個案例都有關連並旨在幫助了解 (1) 《三國志演義》的主體及內裡的文化材料是如何隨著時間改變 ，和(2) 這些改變在不同的文化環境下可以如何適當地被詮釋和被當地的文化同化。 換句話說，通過研究各朝鮮手稿的傳播及近來電腦遊戲的歷史，我盡力去追溯以下演化過程：《三國志演義》從中國傳入——韓國人透過《三國》互動持續探索及重新呈現改写的《三國志演義》——《三國志演義》成為对韓國很重要的文化產品及現象的一個組成部分。 中韓比較文學及文化研究的領域至今仍然缺乏英文專著專門探究文學交流對韓國文化認同構成的影響。因此這樣的專著將能總結這一個為期三年的研究項目。我計劃先提交三篇國際期刊論文，在項目完成後才開始製作一個完整的專著。

11616015.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11616015.value: 華人作曲家對西方歌劇的挪用、再造、與「創造性誤讀」

11616015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11616015.value: This study looks at how the Western opera—as a set of pre-supposed histories and conditions—has been reconfigured, appropriated, and “creatively misread” by Chinese composers from the Mainland, Hong Kong, Macau, Taiwan, and the Chinese diaspora. This study focuses on music composed after the emergence of the “New Wave” generation in the late 1970s. It will constitute the first cross-generational and comparative analysis of contemporary Chinese music that includes overseas Chinese composers from Australia, Singapore, the Philippines, and beyond. Technical analytical accounts will be integral to this discussion. The intention is to locate an analytical dimension for inter-cultural compositions that “combines broad applicability with local specificity” (Utz 2013), and to put into practice a “relational approach” to the analysis of inter-cultural compositions, which sees music as “a performative process that creates and expresses social relations between its participants” (Cook 2013). By zooming into a single musical approach by a specific group of musicians, this study asks: (1) How do acts of appropriation bring the dynamics of inter-cultural encounter into sharp focus? (2) How is “the East” as well as “the West” productively essentialized in inter-cultural compositions? (3) What do the communicative gestures of appropriation tell us about the “lived-realities” of Chinese composers? （詳見英文版本）這項研究，關注華人作曲家如何挪用、再造、與「創造性誤讀」西方歌劇。西方歌劇作為一種「假定的歷史」與文化條件，如何被來自內地，香港，澳門，台灣，以及海外​​華人社群（包括來自澳大利亞，新加坡，菲律賓等的海外​​華人）的作曲家重置？本研究將著重於 20 世紀 70 年代末、當代音樂「新浪潮」後冒起的年青作曲家們的作品。

11616115.value: 中國與越南勞工行動主義與勞資關係的比較：探索巿場、國家與社會的角色

11616115.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11616115.value: Prof CHAN, Anita Dr CHI, Do Quynh

11616115.label: Project Objectives
11616115.value: To explore how the state, market and civil society impact on workers’ activism, workers’ consciousness and workplace relations in Taiwanese-owned electronic enterprises; To compare China and Vietnam in the terms of objective 1, and to explore the reasons underlying the differences; To identify the limitations of current labour policies and suggest ways of maintaining stable workplace relations for policymakers; To build up a post-socialist perspective to analyse workplace relations and explore the direction in which industrial relations in China and Vietnam may develop.
rows: To explore how the state, market and civil society impact on workers’ activism, workers’ consciousness and workplace relations in Taiwanese-owned electronic enterprises;
To compare China and Vietnam in the terms of objective 1, and to explore the reasons underlying the differences;
To identify the limitations of current labour policies and suggest ways of maintaining stable workplace relations for policymakers;
To build up a post-socialist perspective to analyse workplace relations and explore the direction in which industrial relations in China and Vietnam may develop.

11616115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11616115.value: Since 2003, industrial relations in China and Vietnam have been characterised by strikes mainly staged by migrant workers, leading the governments of both these ‘socialist’ countries to readjust their labour regulatory frameworks and policies (Chan, 2010; 2014; Siu and Chan, 2014). Previous studies have shown that the patterns of workers’ activism in the two countries have diverged in terms of scale, intensity and types of demands (Chan, 2011; Pringle and Clarke, 2011), but there is as yet no systematic research on the factors that have contributed to these differences, and no research on the specific role of migrant workers, their agency and their organisational behaviour prior to the manifestation of protest actions. This research project will identify the similarities and differences in the two countries’ industrial relations, and will isolate the factors that either engender labour activism or deter it from exploding into militancy and social instability. Specifically, it will examine how and why the patterns of workers’ activism and workplace relations differ by exploring the roles and impacts of market, state and civil society, in these two post-socialist countries. We will use Shenzhen in China’s Pearl River Delta (PRD) area and Ho Chi Minh City (HCMC) in Vietnam as our major field sites to conduct this comparative study, as both these places are the cities in their respective countries where strikes are most prevalent. We will also focus on Taiwanese-invested export-oriented electronic factories so as to keep industry and source of capital constant in our comparison of the national/local institutional and cultural factors that affect labour relations, and because most of the strikes in both countries have occurred in the electronic industry. Methods used for data collection include documentary research, semi-formal interviews and observations. Six in-depth factory case studies (three for each country) will be conducted. This research will contribute to the current intellectual debates on workers’ activism, labour policies, industrial relations and social development in China and Vietnam. The research findings will be presented at international sociology, labour and development studies conferences and also conferences on China and Vietnam. 自2003年以來，以移民工為骨幹的罷工已成中國和越南勞資關係的一大特徵。形形色色的罷工都令兩個同是「社會主義國家」的政府不得不重新調整其勞工法規的框架及政策(Chan, 2010; 2014; Siu and Chan, 2014)。至今，文獻中已有不少研究指出兩國的勞工激進主義無論在規模、強度，及訴求上都有明顯差異(Chan, 2011; Pringle and Clarke, 2011)。然而，對於導致這些差異的原因，至今仍未有仔細和系統的分析；另外，對於兩國移民工在抗爭中的角色、能動性，以及他們在抗爭前的組織行為就更尚付闕如。有見及此，本研究計劃將深入分析兩國勞資關係的差異，並探討各種促使或阻礙勞工抗爭演變成勞工激進主義及社會不穩定的主要因素。本研究更會探討兩國巿場、國家和社會的角色，及它們如何影響兩國的勞工行動主義模式與勞資關係。由於中國珠三角的深圳巿及越南的胡志明巿均是兩國罷工最頻繁的城巿，我們會以這兩個城巿作為此比較研究的田野考察地點。此外，為使本比較研究不受國家／地方制度、文化差異的影響，我們會集中研究兩國內的同類產業與資本──台灣投資，並以外銷為主的電子工廠。本研究主要收集數據的方法包括：文獻紀錄研究、半結構化訪談、田野觀察。本研究會深入地對六家工廠（每國三家）作個案分析。本研究將能補足現時文獻中有關中國和越南在勞工行動主義、勞工政策、勞資關係，及社會發展的缺失。研究成果將會在有關國際社會學、勞工及社會發展學，以及中國與越南的國際學術會議中發表。

11616115.label: Realisation of objectives
11616115.value: The objectives of this project has been well achieved. An international research team has been formed, led by the PI, with the following core members: Prof. Anita Chan, Australian National University (Project Co-I); Dr. Do Quynh Chi, Research Center for Employment Relations (Project Co-I) Prof. Jonathan Unger, Australian National University, Prof. Wang Hong-Zen, National Sun-Yat-Sen University, Taiwan, Dr. Elaine Hui, Penn State University, USA (The PI’s former RA), Dr. Kaxton Siu, Hong Kong Polytechnic University. A few rounds of fieldwork have been conducted in China and Vietnam. Based on this project, Kaxton Siu was also awarded an ECS project to extend his research to the aspect of family and migration patterns in China and Vietnam. The team has produced at least four papers to be submitted to Journal of Contemporary Asia, a leading area studies journal. All of these four papers were based on the team’s fieldwork and attempted to compare different aspects of labour activism, working conditions, migration patterns and industrial relations in these two countries. Two of these four papers (Siu and Unger, 2019; Chan, 2019) have been published online, one (by Chris Chan and Elaine Hui) has passed the first round of peer review, and the final one (by Wang Hong-Zen and Chen Chih-jou) is in the process of revision after the team’s internal review. Below are the titles of these four major papers: Dr. Kaxton Siu (Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Prof. Jonathan Unger (Australian National University) " Family and Migration among Factory workers in China and Vietnam". Prof. Anita Chan (Australian National University) "Path Dependency: Vietnam and China’s Diverging Industrial Relations Systems" Dr. Chris Chan (City University of Hong Kong); Dr. Elaine Hui (Penn State University, USA) "Pension Systems and Pension-driven Strikes in Post-Socialist China and Vietnam: A Comparative Study". Prof. Wang Hong Ren (National Sun-Yat-Sen University, Taiwan); Dr. Chen Chih-jou (Academia Sinica, Taiwan) "Comparing Strikes in Vietnam and China：Defensive vs. Aggressive Authoritarian State". Elaine Hui is developing another paper to compare labor NGOs activism in China and Vietnam. Resource in this project has also allowed Chris Chan to publish a few other papers concerning the development of labor activism, trade union reform, and impacts of industrial policies in China. Among others, these major articles have been published or accepted: Xu Yi and Chris Chan (2018). “Conductive activism: Anti-sweatshop campaigns across Hong Kong and mainland China”. Journal of Contemporary Asia. 48(1): 88-112. Xu Wang, Chris Chan and Linchuan Yang (2020) Economic Upgrading, Social Upgrading, and Chinese Rural Migrant Workers: A Study in the Pearl River Delta, China Review. Siqi Luo and Chris Chan (2020) Re-claiming “Territories": Two Case Studies of Trade Union Innovation Projects in South China, China Review.

11616115.label: Major findings and research outcome
11616115.value: Project team members have developed different analysis to compare labor activism, labor market and workplace relations in China and Vietnam which are reflected in the papers listed in 5.3, such as: Anita Chan argues that the path dependency of these two countries' recent histories have set them on different paths vis-à-vis authoritarianism. When external contingencies have prompted institutional change, the industrial relations of Vietnam and China have veered in divergent trajectories. Kaxton and John Unger also found that despite having similar legacies of socialist transformation and similar household registration systems in the past, these two post-socialist countries have developed distinctively different patterns of migration by rural-to-urban migrant populations, and in their access to urban social and welfare services. Chris Chan and Elaine Hui equally emphasized on the similarities and differences of state and labor relationship in these two countries by the cases of pension-driven strikes staged by migrant workers in these two countries.

11616115.value: Based on this project, Kaxton Siu has developed another project to compare family and migration patterns in China and Vietnam. The project has been awarded by the Early Career Scheme of RGC.

To conduct a critical survey of film style, genres, subject matter and conventions that characterize the Cantonese cinematic tradition 3. rows: 1. To conduct a historical study of the development of Cantonese cinema during the ‘missing period’ (1949-1969)
2. To conduct a critical survey of film style, genres, subject matter and conventions that characterize the Cantonese cinematic tradition
3. To create a bilingual digital archive of Cantonese cinema during this period as a resource bank for further research

11616315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11616315.value: This project is a continuation of a special issue series entitled ‘The Missing Period in Chinese cinemas, 1949-1979’, published by the Journal of Chinese Cinemas between 2010 and 2011. The Principal Investigator (Dr. Vivian Lee) of the current project guest-edited the volume on Hong Kong cinema. The series was well-received as it filled an important gap in Chinese cinema research, since existing English-language scholarship predominantly focuses on the early 1980s and beyond. The present study surveys the historical development of Cantonese cinema in Hong Kong during the period 1949-1969, when Cantonese cinema went through cycles of rapid growth and decline before its eventual ‘revival’ in the early seventies. As a regional cinema heavily reliant on overseas revenue, Cantonese cinema during this period was subject to the (trans)national cultural politics in different reception contexts. A working premise of this study is that the twenty years before the dramatic comeback of Cantonese-language films in the 1970s can be considered as the ‘classical period’ of Cantonese cinema, and the films from this period exhibit important stylistic, linguistic, and generic distinctions from later works. The Cantonese cinema during this period therefore constitutes a distinct cinematic tradition that came to an end in around 1969. The generally perceived revival of Hong Kong Cantonese films in the early 1970s, arguably, is a completely different kind of cinema in terms of visual style, genre types, subject matter, and conventions. Another under-researched area in existing scholarship on Cantonese cinema (and Chinese cinema as a whole) during this period is its distinctiveness and importance as an influential cinema in Cantonese as a regional language. The relationship between the transnational circulation of Cantonese-language films and culture across Southeast Asia is another ‘missing link’ that this study aims to recover. The existing literature has been overwhelmingly focused on Chinese cinema as a topic area that presupposes Mandarin as the preeminent screen language. Cantonese cinema as a distinctive cinema in its own right is regarded as a “dialect cinema”, and as an inferior cinema of interest only to local audiences within the dialect community. This project seeks to redress the critical neglect that has resulted from the stereotypical and derogatory view of pre-1970s Cantonese cinema as a topic of research. The main components of this project include a digital archive that will serve as a resource base for future research, and two research articles (details given below). 這個研究計劃針對粵語電影在五十年代和六十年代的發展。到目前爲止，對這個時期的粵語電影的學術研究（尤其以英文發表的論文和專書）仍然不多。過去二十多年，關於香港電影的學術著作大多關注80年代以後的發展，這個研究計劃將通過整理50和60年代的電影和相關資料，建立一個中英雙語並有多種檢索功能的電子資料庫，讓本地和海外的研究者提供研究平台。有關研究亦將以學術論文形式在國際學術期刊發表。

11616315.label: Realisation of objectives
11616315.value: The PI has conducted in-depth research into the history of Hong Kong cinema during the "missing period" over the course of the last three years. The project consists of two parts: an critical/analytical inquiry into the landscape of film production, and data-mining on Cantonese films produced and released between 1949 to 1969. Both initiatives have realised their initial objectives and intended outcomes (see "Research Outcome" for publication details) The critical-analytical part of the project involved a comprehensive review of existing literature on the historical development of the left-wing cinema in Hong Kong since the late 1940s, when the CCP began to set up its cultural united front in Hong Kong alongside other leftist organisations in the business and social sectors. The research into the production and exhibition strategies of the left-wing studios between the 1950s and 1960s has unravelled the intricate connections between the filmmaking world and the contending political forces at work in the ex-British colony after the end of the Second World War. The investigation into the aesthetics and politics of the left-wing cinema seeks to address an imbalance in the current critical discourse on the left-wing as an ethical force imbued with patriotic and social ideals. While this is an important constituent of the left-wing's self-positioning, the left-wing is also understood as an institutionalised cultural agent trying to make an impact in the commercial mainstream; hence, its collaboration with non-left wing partners, including the right-wing studios, is also within the scope of this inquiry. The study also makes a case for the nuanced legacies of the cinematic left in the later decades, when Hong Kong and China were undergoing another phase of economic and social transformation, a subject as yet under-researched in current scholarship. The research team's extensive data-mining has contributed to a more complete filmography of Cantonese cinema in the 1950s and 1960s. The most noteworthy contribution is the discovery of over 300 “missing titles” that are not found in the Hong Kong Film Archive’s database, which is so far the most comprehensive online resource on Hong Kong cinema. These “missing titles” are based on extensive data-mining since the PI obtained an initial start-up grant in 2015. While the HKFA’s database covers both Cantonese and Mandarin cinema, this project has built a more specialised digital archive focusing on Cantonese films based on the primary data collated from various online sources as well as archival research on film advertisements, film reviews, and relevant news reports. Brief summaries of the content of film advertisements, announcements, and film reviews are also included where practicable to shed light on how films and film genres were described in publicity materials. These original findings will contribute to future research on the Cantonese film culture at the time, and how films were branded by industry and received by their contemporary audience and critics. The current database can also be updated continuously with new findings. The findings and research outcomes from this project have laid a solid foundation for further research on Cantonese cinema and the history of the Hong Kong film industry at large. Building on the groundwork in this phase, the PI has obtained funding from the RGC for the next phase (see details below).

11616315.label: Major findings and research outcome
11616315.value: The findings from this project provided valuable historical data for the PI’s on-going research on Hong Kong's film industry during Cold War era and its long-term impact. The major findings and research outcome are given below: 1. An online digital archive of Cantonese films released from 1949 to 1969 has been created and hosted at the CityU Library for access by eligible Library users. The archive is the first online resource dedicated to historical data on Cantonese cinema that includes information on film advertisements and newspaper reviews and news reports. The extensive data-mining has resulted in a more complete filmography of Cantonese-language films produced from 1949 - 1969. Over 300 "missing titles" have been identified and included in the current digital archive. Access link: http://lbprj01.lib.cityu.edu.hk/staff_project/cc1949_69 2. A book manuscript titled "The Other Side of Glamour: Hong Kong’s Left-Wing Studios" has been completed. A research monograph will be published by the Edinburgh University Press in late 2019. 3. A research paper, “Class, Gender, and the Charismatic Female Subject in Hong Kong Cinema during the Cold War era” has been accepted for publication in a collected volume, Liminal Space in a Divided World: Cold War Cities in Europe and Asia during the 1950s, edited by Hon Tsz-ki, Routledge (forthcoming). 4. Presentation on research findings were made at two international conferences: “The Left, Right, and Middle in the Hong Kong Film Industry during the Cold War Era,” International Conference on Global Cities: The Networks of Connectivity in East Asia, Southeast Asia and the Pacific Region, 1850-1950, City University of Hong Kong, April 13 - 14, 2018

11616315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11616315.value: Based on the work done in this phase, the PI applied for a new RGC (GRF) grant for “The Missing Period in Cantonese Cinema, Phase 2”. The new project was approved in 2018 (Project no. 9042742). Initial data collection has begun and the CityU Library will continue to work with the PI on developing the Phase 2 database.

11616315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11616315.value: This project has two major deliverables, a research monograph and a bilingual digital archive of Cantonese films. A book-length study on the historical development of Hong Kong's left-wing studios will be published by the Edinburgh University Press in late 2019. Taking into account existing literature on the subject, this study will bring to light the lesser known aspects of the left-wing film apparatus in Hong Kong and its nuanced legacies in Hong Kong cinema in the subsequent decades. This research project has contributed to a more complete filmography of Cantonese cinema. One noteworthy contribution is the discovery of over 300 “missing titles” that are not recorded in the Hong Kong Film Archive’s database, which is so far the most comprehensive online resource on Hong Kong cinema. These “missing titles” are based on extensive data-mining in the past three years undertaken by the research team. While the HKFA’s database covers both Cantonese and Mandarin cinema, this project has built a more specialised digital archive focusing on Cantonese films based on the primary data collated from various online sources as well as archival research on film advertisements, film reviews, and relevant news reports. Brief summaries of the content of film advertisements, announcements, and film reviews are also included where practicable to shed light on how films and film genres were described in publicity materials. These are original findings that will contribute to future research on the Cantonese film culture at the time, and how films were branded by the film industry and received by their contemporary audience and critics.

12100415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12100415.value: Plants use intricate signaling networks to fine-tune defense pathways in response to attack by different pathogens, leading to broad transcriptional reprogramming. Epigenetic mechanism/chromatin remodeling plays a vital role in regulating expression of defense-related genes; however, the mechanism that control epigenetic modifications associated with defense pathway genes is largely unknown. Nudix proteins, found in all classes of organisms, have diverse substrates but most of them hydrolyze nucleoside diphosphate derivatives. We previously identified two Arabidopsis Nudix proteins, NUDT6 and NUDT7, as negative regulators of the immune response. Our recent findings raise an intriguing possibility that NUDT6 and NUDT7 might function in epigenetic control of the defense pathway to prevent unnecessary or excessive activation of defense mechanism. We and another group have identified two histone acetyltransferases (HAT), HAC5 and GCN5, as putative NUDT7- and NUDT6-interating proteins, respectively. We recently found that the loss-of-function mutations of NUDT6 and NUDT7 make the plants hypersensitive to epigenetic modifications. Many epigenetic suppressors of the nudt6 nudt7 double mutant have been obtained. In this proposal, we will validate the interactions of NUDT7-HAC5 and NUDT6-GCN5. We will examine whether NUDT6 and NUDT7 modulate HAC5 and GCN5 function by hydrolyzing acetyl-CoA, a nucleotide derivative and the acetyl donor in the HAT-catalyzed histone acetylation reaction. Histone acetylation and DNA methylation patterns will be analyzed and compared between wildtype, the nudt mutants, and epigenetic suppressors of the nudt6 nudt7 mutant to reveal the effects of the mutations on epigenetic modifications linked to the defense pathway genes and transgenerational memory of acquired resistance. Besides, genetic analysis will be performed to identify other components in the NUDT6/NUDT7-mediated defense pathway. The proposed study could make a significant contribution toward unraveling the control mechanism of plant immunity.

12100415.label: Realisation of objectives
12100415.value: Two Arabidopsis Nudix proteins, NUDT6 and NUDT7, were previously found to act as negative regulators of the immune response. The nudt6/7 double mutant displays severe autoimmunity. The mutant phenotype is epigenetically unstable, particularly following the treatment of the mutant seeds with EMS. It has been reported by another group that NUDT6 interacts with GCN5 in yeast two hybrid system, raising the possibility that NUDT6/7 might be involved in epigenetic control of disease resistance. The proposed study aims to understand the role of these two Nudix proteins in plant immunity by testing the above hypothesis. 1. Validate the interactions between NUDT7-HAC5 and NUDT6-GCN5 In a report by another group, NUDT6 was identified as a putative interacting protein of GCN5 based on Y2H screen in which GCN5 was used as the bait, although only a single NUDT6-containing colony was identified in the screen. We identified HAC5 among the proteins pulled-down together with NUDT7 in a co-IP assay using the transgenic line expressing tagged NUDT7. We have used Y2H, in planta co-IP assay, and BiFC assay to further determine if these proteins do interact. Our results indicate that the previous report and findings on the NUDT6-GCN5 and NUDT7-HAC5 interactions were not real, likely due to false positive results in the previous essays. Both GCN5 and HAC5 use proteins as their substrates and their peptide-binding domains might be ‘sticky’ which might have caused false positives in the previous protein-protein interaction assays. 2. Examine whether NUDT6 and NUDT7 might be involved in epigenetic control by acting as acetyl-CoA hydrolases To test if NUDT6/7 might mediate epigenetic control by hydrolyzing acetyl-CoA, we expressed NUDT6 and NUDT7 proteins in E. coli and purified them for in vitro enzymatic assay using acetyl-coA as the substrate. It was found that NUDT6 or NUDT7 was not able to hydrolyze intact acetyl CoA. However, if acetyl CoA is dephosphorylated first, NUDT6 and NUDT7 were able to hydrolyze it. It is unknown whether dephosphorylated acetyl CoA is present in plants and has any physiological function, raising a doubt on acetyl CoA being NUDT6/7’s physiological substrate. Besides, we measured cellular levels of acetyl CoA, but did not find a significant difference in its level between wt and the mutant plants. Together, our results argue against acetyl CoA being an in vivo substrate of NUDT6 or NUDT7. 3. Determine global and local DNA methylation and histone acetylation patterns The bisulfite sequencing method was used to generate global methylation patterns of cytosines in the genomes of wt, the nudt6 nudt7double mutant, and two epigenetic suppressors/revertants of nudt6/7 which were identified from the suppressor screen of nudt6/7 by EMS mutagenesis. To determine histone acylation patterns, we used the acetylated-lysine antibody to pull-down peptides that contain acetylated lysine, followed by mass spec identification and quantification. The nudt6/7 double mutation was found to alter DNA methylation patterns and histone acetylation patterns, including changes in methylation patterns of genome regions associated with some known defense-related genes such as Rin4. Recently, we found that NUDT6 and NUDT7 likely act as enzymes that hydrolyze NAD-capped RNAs (see below). We did not further determine any direct role of NUDT6 or NUDT7 in DNA methylation or histone acetylation as our recent data indicate that they are likely indirectly involved in epigenetic control by their function in modulating NAD-capped RNAs. 4. Mutational analysis for understanding the role of NUDT6 and NUDT7 and for identification of additional components in the defense pathway T-DNA insertion mutagenesis was used to identify suppressor mutations in the nudt6 nudt7 background and a total of ten suppressors were identified in the T2 seedlings. One of the suppressor mutation was found to be caused by a T-DNA insertion in a gene encoding for a helper RESISTANCE protein (AtNRG1.1) which partially suppresses the nudt6/7 phenotype. Helper R proteins are not directly involved in recognition of pathogens but acts downstream of of a R protein to activate defense pathways. NRG1.1 is a CC-NBS-LRR protein of the R gene superfamily and it has a close homolog (NRG1.2). Knockout of both NRG1.1 and NRG1.2 was found to completely suppress the nudt6/7 phenotype. The nrg1.1 nrg1.2 mutation was also found to repress the autoimmunity phenotypes of snc1 and pdx3. In addition, we also used a low concentration of EMS (0.1%. Higher concentrations of EMS causes more epigenetic revertants) to treat seeds of the nudt7 single mutant for suppressor screening. One strong suppressor of nudt7 was isolated in the M2 generation. The suppressor phenotype was caused by a dominant mutation. Next generation sequencing is being used to identify the suppressor gene.

12100415.label: Major findings and research outcome
12100415.value: 1. Yeast two hybrid screen, in planta co-IP assay, and BiFC assay were used to examine physical interactions between NUDT6-GCN5 and between NUDT7-HAC5. Our results indicated that these proteins did not interact. 2. In vitro enzymatic assay revealed that NUDT6 or NUDT7 was not able to hydrolyze intact acetyl CoA although they can hydrolyze dephosphorylated acetyl CoA. Besides, we did not find a significant difference in the levels of acetyl CoA between wt and the nudt6/7 mutant. Our results did not support the hypothesis of acetyl CoA being an in vivo substrate of NUDT6 or NUDT7. 3. The nudt6/7 double mutation alters DNA methylation patterns and histone acetylation patterns. Recently, we found that NUDT6 and NUDT7 likely act as enzymes that hydrolyze NAD-capped RNAs. Our recent data suggest that NUDT6/7 are likely indirectly involved in epigenetic control by their function in modulating NAD-capped RNAs. 4. T-DNA insertion mutagenesis was used to generate mutations in the nudt6/7 background and screen for suppressors of nudt6/7. Mutations in two genes encoding for CC-NBS-LRR proteins of the RESISTANCE gene superfamily. These two proteins are considered to be helper R proteins that act downstream of receptor R proteins in activation of the defense pathway. Suppressor screen in the nudt7 background through EMS mutagenesis was also carried out and identification of a putative candidate gene for a nudt7 suppressor mutation is under the way. 5. While carrying out the project, we found that NUDT6 and NUDT7 possess a decapping activity for NAD-capped RNAs. Our focus has then been switched to revealing the role of NUDT6 and NUDT7 in modulating NAD-RNA levels. We have developed a method termed NAD tagSeq for identification of NAD-capped RNAs in Arabidopsis. We found that the nudt7 mutation leads to approximately two-fold increase in the cellular NAD-RNA level.

12100415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12100415.value: We tested the hypotheses on the possible molecular mode of action by NUDT6 and NUDT7 in mediating plant immunity. Rather than directly affecting histone acetylation and DNA methylation, our study showed the role of NUDT6/7 in epigenetic regulation epigenetic regulation of the defense response is indirect. We have found that NUDT7, and perhaps also NUDT6, is apparently a NAD-RNA decapping enzyme. The results raise an intriguing possibility that NAD-RNAs play an important role in mediating plant immunity, and NUDT7 and NUDT6 regulate the immune response by modulating cellular NAD-RNA levels. As the 1st step toward examining functions of NAD-RNAs in plant immunity and other processes, we developed a method (NAD tagSeq) for genome-wide identification and characterization of NAD-RNAs and led to the identification of over two thousand NAD-RNAs in Arabidopsis. We have also compared the NAD-RNA profiles between wildtype and the nudt7 mutant. The realization that NAD-RNAs might mediate plant immunity and the method development open a new avenue for unraveling novel mechanism in regulating plant immunity. Based on these findings, we submitted a CRF proposal which has been shortlisted.

12100415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12100415.value: Plants evolved complex mechanisms to defend against pathogen attack. Understanding the plant defense mechanisms can help to develop strategies for controlling diseases caused by pathogen infection to enhance crop production and environmental sustainability. Arabidopsis Nudix proteins NUDT6 and NUDT7 have long been known to regulate plant immunity; however, for many years, their physiological substrates had remained unknown. We have tested various hypotheses to determine physiological substrates of NUDT6 and NUDT7 and understand their molecular mode of action in controlling plant immunity. Some downstream components involved in NUDT6/7-mediated immunity were identified through genetic analysis. Our study has now led to the finding that NUDT7 and perhaps also NUDT6 are enzymes that remove the NAD cap of RNAs. The NAD cap is a recently discovered cap attached to 5’ ends of some RNAs and its molecular and biological functions remain elusive. Our findings indicate that NAD capping and decapping of RNAs might be a novel mechanism which mediates plant immunity.

12100615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12100615.value: 多糖口服可以被吸收嗎？機理如何？本項目擬通過研究TLRs/Dectin介導的小腸巨噬細胞對靈芝多糖GSP-2的體內外吞噬作用，給出相應的答案。目前鮮有報導口服多糖的代謝研究。普遍認為，口服多糖的生物利用度非常低。雖然有報導螢光標記的多糖口服後可以在血液中檢出，但是還不清楚螢光劑本身對吸收的影響，有關的吸收機理也有待研究。為此，我們建立了一個非螢光標記的檢測方法。已有研究報導，某些腸道淋巴細胞可以識別多糖，其中巨噬細胞表面的Dectin-1受體的表達也會增加。我們前期的研究發現，靈芝多糖GSP-2可以被巨噬細胞表面的多個受體識別。因此我們推測，多糖可以通過這些受體的作用，被巨噬細胞內吞而帶入體內。本項目計畫利用非螢光標記的檢測方法研究巨噬細胞對GSP-2的吞噬作用，並使用特異性的抗體或siRNA來研究某些受體在吞噬中所起的作用。如果成功，本專案將提供確鑿的證據證明口服多糖的吸收，並闡明有關作用機理，從而打破多糖研究的瓶頸，推動口服多糖的研發。

12100615.label: Realisation of objectives
12100615.value: 1. We compared the Flu488-labeled GSP2, FITC-labeled GSP2, and original GSP2 using HPGPC. The results showed that the molecular size of Flu488-labeled GSP2 was much smaller than that of the original, while FITC-labeled GSP2 was much closer to the original. The results of further comparison of cytotoxicity to the caco-2 and RAW 264.7 cell lines showed that GSP2 did not suppress the proliferation of caco-2 and RAW 264.7 cell lines in 24 h, while FITC-GSP2 exhibited cytotoxic effect when its concentration beyond 100 μg/mL (P＜0.0001). These results showed that GSP2 and FITC-GSP2 have comparable properties when its concentration was set below 50 μg/mL. The distribution of FITC-GSP2 in organs after oral dose was tracked by detecting the fluorescence intensity by animal fluorescence imaging system and molecular size by HPGPC. The results showed that FITC-GSP2 could stay in small intestine for 3 hours after oral dose and enter Peyer’s patch to trigger immune response. The results obtained on in vitro human M cell model which is M-like cells derived from Raji B cell induced caco-2 cells, showed that both GSP2 and FITC-GSP2 could be transported through caco-2 cell layer by M cells to induce the production of TNF-α and IL-6 in RAW 264.7 cells. 2. GSP2/FITC-GSP2 could induce the phagocytosis to zymosan by RAW 264.7 cells and they themselvess could be directly internalized by RAW 264.7 cells, which could be suppressed by TLR 2/4 inbitor. 3. GSP-2 induced TNFα secretion in primary macrophages from wild-type, but not TLR4-knockout mice. In addition, GSP-2 upregulated TLR4 protein expression and activated the MAPK pathway in RAW246.7 macrophages. Finally, GSP-2 induced the production of the cytokines TNFα, IL1β, and IL6.

12102415.label: Realisation of objectives
12102415.value: In this project, a systematic investigation was carried out to reveal the relationship between both the identity and amounts of active components and microscopic characteristics in several common but chemically very different CMMs. Through this projects, the chemical profiles of different cells or tissue regions of CMMs was analyzed by means of laser microdissection and ultra-high performance liquid chromatography quadrupole/time of flight-mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS). Several commonly used CMMs containing different chemical types was selected as research targets: Notoginseng Radix et Rhizoma (sanqi) containing saponins, Polygoni Multiflori Radix (heshouwu) containing anthraquinones, Uncariae cum Uncis Ramulus (gouteng) containing alkaloids, Scutellariae Radix (huangqin) containing flavonoids and Angelicae Sinensis Radix (danggui) containing volatile oils. After softening by wrapping with water-soaked non-cellulose paper, the samples was cut into small sections, embedded in cryomatrixTM, and then placed on a cutting platform in the cryobar of a cryostat at−20 ◦C. Serial slices of 40 m in thickness will be cut at −10 ◦C. Each sectioned tissue slice was mounted directly to a non-fluorescent PET microscope steel frame slide and observed with a Leica LMD 7000 microscope system in fluorescence mode with a dichromatic mirror. Microdissection will be conducted by a DPSS laser beam under a Leica LMD-BGR fluorescence filter system. Tissue parts within an area was determined as the investigated size and dissected separately under fluorescence inspection mode. The microdissected tissues was fall into caps of microcentrifuge tubes by gravity. The separated tissue part in each cap was transferred to the bottom of the tube through centrifugation. Then the tube was kept in a desiccator overnight prior to UPLC-QTOFMS analysis. UHPLC–QTOF-MS analysis was performed on an Agilent 6540 ultra-high definition accurate mass quadrupole time-of-flight spectrometer with UHPLC. A UPLC C18 analytical column was used for separation, coupled with a C18 pre-column at room temperature of 20 ◦C. The data analysis will be performed on Agilent MassHunter Workstation software-Qualitative Analysis. The active components of CMM will be used as marker compounds for data analysis. By comparing with the reference compounds, on-line MS data, and UV spectra, as well as data from the literature, most of the chromatographic peaks was identified. The results provide evidences to reveal a consistent correlation between active components and microscopic characteristics of CMMs. And this correlation was further validated by quantity target microscopic characteristics containing active components in CMMs by combining X-ray quantitative phase contrast micro-CT with advanced 3-dimensional imaging processing. The white beam from wiggler radiation is monochromatized via a constant-exit double crystal cryogenic-cooling monochromator. In the monochromator, two sets of crystals with Si (111) orientation crystal and Si (311) orientation can exchange on-line, which enable the X-ray photon output at the energy range of 8–72.5 keV, with the energy resolution of about 0.5%. Four kinds of X-ray CCD detectors with different spatial resolution with the range for different samples will be used. Dynamic imaging experiments with the spatial-temporal resolution of 20frame/s and 9μm/pixel and micro-CT experiments with the spatial resolution of 0.37μm/pixel have been realized. The sample to detector distance will be set at 8m, which should be appropriate for all experiments. An ionization chamber will be employed to monitor the flux during the experiments. Entrance slit system will be used to define the import beam for the monochromator, and the second slit was define the spot size at the sample position. A precision sample stage with 6 axes was installed for micro-tomography. During the experiments, the propagation based XPCMT (X-ray phase contrast micro-tomography) setup was employed and the optimized SDD selected to provide highly edge-enhanced X-ray images. The energy was chosen by compromising factors such as the penetration ability, phase contrast and detecting efficiency, to get the best image. Exposure time was selected to ensure high enough signal-to-noise (S/N) ratio. The CT projection number was selected according to the sample size and the spatial resolution. With some improved reconstruction algorithm, the projection number was as reduced to 1/3 of normal, which could greatly reduce sample dose and data collecting time, while maintaining acceptable S/N ratio and spatial resolution. After optimization, the experiment system was used to investigate the various samples of CMMs directly. Image pixels was segmented according to their gray value, and then the shape of certain microscopic characteristic was obtained. According to the metabolite profiling of various cells and tissue regions, the exact cells and tissue regions containing active components was selected for specific analysis. The quality of CMMs from various sources was evaluated and the correlation of microscopic features and the quality of CMMs established by tissue and cell-specific metabolite profiling, the contents of active components in CMMs was determined by UPLC. The validated relationship between active components and microscopic characteristics was used for evaluating the quality of CMMs by assessing the quantity of the specific cells or tissues where those components are found. The results will enable us to identify the source species and evaluate the quality of CMMs simultaneously by microscopic characteristics. This study will make evaluating the quality of CMM much more practical and provide specific guidelines for a specific number of CMMs—thereby demonstrating how the template is applied, for studies of all other CMMs. A platform was established for assessing all CMMs in a similar way, and to establish the format for reporting results of such assessments.

12102415.label: Major findings and research outcome
12102415.value: (1) The relationship between active components and microscopic characteristics was established and developed as a feasible, fast, and economical way to evaluate the quality of CMMs by microscopic characteristics. (2) The application of X-ray quantitative phase contrast micro-CT and laser microdissection in this study is a powerful scientific and technical platform for correlating microscopic characteristics and biologically active components for quality evaluation of CMMs by microscopic characteristics. Anyone with a microscope can measure the amounts of specific microscopic characteristics for relatively evaluating the quality of CMMs.

12102415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12102415.value: A computer image recognition system of microscopic features could be further established, which is significant for the practical application of microscopic identification. For further study, a systematic investigation will be carried out to identify the same microscopic features from various CMMs by correlating the histochemical distribution by using laser microdissection and ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. First, the same microscopic features from various CMMs will be differentiated by correlating the histochemical distribution using laser microdissection and ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS). We expect the results to identify the same microscopic features from various CMMs according to their respective unique fluorescence microscopic features due to their different chemical components. Then these findings will be used for building up the computer image recognition system. The results will enable us to achieve the identification of the same microscopic features from various CMMs with different chemical components by the computer image recognition system.

12102415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12102415.value: Chinese medicinal materials (CMMs) are becoming popular world-wide, and its quality and efficacy has become an internationally critical issue. Different methods are available to authenticate CMMs, no method to date has been able to both identify the source species and evaluate the quality of a CMM sample. Microscopic identification has been demonstrated to be an effective means for identifying the source species of CMMs. In this study, a systematic investigation will be carried out to reveal the relationship between both the identity and amounts of active components and microscopic characteristics in several common but chemically very different CMMs. Through this study, the amounts of target microscopic characteristics in a CMM was measured by combining X-ray quantitative phase contrast micro-CT with advanced 3-dimensional imaging processing method; the chemical profiles of specific cell- or tissue-types in a CMM can be obtained by tissue-and cell-specific metabolite profiling using laser microdissection; and there is a consistent relationship between active components and microscopic characteristics. The application of X-ray quantitative phase contrast micro-CT and laser microdissection in the proposed study is expected to be a powerful scientific and technical platform for correlating microscopic characteristics and biologically active components for quality evaluation of CMMs by microscopic characteristics.

12104415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12104415.value: 自噬是癌症發展的一個關鍵過程。我們的前期研究表明，來自中藥常山的天然產物常山酮顯示出體內外抗結直腸癌的活性。有趣的是，常山酮可以下調哺乳動物雷帕黴素複合物1的靶點（mTORC1），下調ULK1中ser757位點的磷酸化并上調自噬的標記物LC3-II，且呈劑量依賴關係，提示常山酮在營養豐富條件下可誘導自噬。另一方面，剝奪血清時，常山酮上調mTORC1和ULK1中ser757位點的磷酸化，同時下調LC3-II的表達，提示常山酮可能抑制自噬。因此，我們提出假說，常山酮或通過自噬的一個關鍵環節ULK1磷酸化，在營養豐富條件下誘導自噬或在飢餓條件下抑制自噬，從而達到抗腫瘤的目的。為了驗證這個假說，首先，我們將考察mTORC1調控下的ULK1 ser757位點和AMPK調控下的ULK1 ser317/777位點的磷酸化。其次，為了動態分析自噬，我們擬在營養豐富條件下考察自噬流，包括溶酶體酶活性和溶酶體融合檢測；另外，抑制劑chloroquine and bafilomycin A1也都將用於常山酮誘導自噬的驗證。再次，考慮到營養缺乏可誘導自噬，我們還將考察常山酮在飢餓條件下抑制自噬流。最後，為了模擬體外的營養缺乏條件，我們擬考察常山酮荷瘤裸鼠在限制飲食情況下，常山酮是否增強其抗腫瘤活性，結果將於之前的正常飲食進行對照。基於以上的這些研究，我們將可揭示常山酮通過ULK1磷酸化雙向調節自噬，為常山酮作為自噬調節劑抗結直腸癌提供新證據。

12104415.label: Realisation of objectives
12104415.value: 1.To investigate phosphorylation of ULK1 in CRC cells under nutrient rich and starvation conditions with HF treatment HF was documented to regulate Akt/mTORC1 signaling in CRC, and mTORC1 also inhibits autophagy through phosphorylation and inactivation of the initiating kinase ULK1 in cancer cells, prompting us to ask if and how HF regulates autophagy in CRC cells. Thus, GFP-LC3-II, a fluorescent autophagosomal marker, was conducted to monitor autophagy in CRC cells. As a result, we found that HF induced GFP-LC3-II puncta accumulation detected by a confocal microscope in high glucose medium. To further clarify HF-mediated autophagy, SQSTM1 (p62), which is a putative substrate for evaluating impairment of autophagic degradation, we found that HF significantly reduced SQSTM1 while markedly elevated LC3-II protein levels under nutrient-rich condition. These observations led us to hypothesize that HF induces autophagy in high glucose condition. We further asked how HF initiated autophagy. To validate HF induces autophagy through ULK1, the highly selective inhibitor SBI-0206965 was used to reduce HF-induced autophagy, indicating that HF regulates autophagy at least partially through ULK1. Notably, not only the nutrient-sensing mTORC1, but also AMPK regulates phosphorylation of ULK1 at different sites for autophagic modulation. In this regard, we found AMPK-mediated phosphorylation at Ser317/Ser777 of ULK1 upon HF treatment under nutrient-poor condition. To further uncover the mechanism how HF regulates AMPK for autophagy inhibition, we found that LKB1 rather than CaMKKβ as the upstream event of AMPK, was down-regulated by HF. In conclusion, HF could dually regulate initiation step of autophagy through either Akt-mTORC1-ULK1 or LKB1-AMPK-ULK1 signaling pathways depending on nutritional conditions. 2. To examine the autophagic flux in CRC cells upon HF treatment under nutrient rich condition As mentioned above, HF can dually regulate the initiation step of autophagic flux. We further investigated whether HF could exert a marked impact on later steps including elongation of the double-membrane structure to form the autophagosome under both nutrient-rich and -poor conditions. In this regard, the lysosome inhibitor chloroquine (CQ) that allows the accumulation of the endogenous LC3-II was used to analyze the autophagic flux in CRC cells upon HF treatment. Either HF or CQ caused accumulation of LC3-II puncta and protein expression under nutrient-rich condition. To further provide evidence of autophagosome formation in autophagic flux, we performed tandem fluorescent-tagged LC3 (mRFP-GFP-LC3) puncta formation assay. Because GFP loses its fluorescence from deprotonation in acidic lysosomes, autophagosomes display both green and red fluorescence whereas autolysosomes are red only. Hence, a dramatic increase in the number of red-only indicates maturation of autophagosomes. 3. To investigate how HF inhibits autophagic flux in CRC cells under nutrient starvation conditions In EBSS medium culture, CQ caused accumulation of LC3-II in CRC cells. HF greatly synergized with CQ to cause the most accumulation of the marker LC3-II under nutrient-rich condition. While under nutrient-poor condition, co-treatment of CQ and HF slightly reduced the expression of LC3-II and the decreased the number of GFP-LC3-II puncta. Therefore, we postulated that HF can induce autophagosome formation or inhibit autophagosome membrane elongation, depending on nutrient states.To further provide evidence of autophagosome formation in autophagic flux, we also performed tandem fluorescent-tagged LC3 (mRFP-GFP-LC3) puncta formation assay. As expected, mRFP-GFP-LC3 also aggregated when nutrient-replete medium was replaced with EBSS medium. However, HF treatment caused both red and yellow fluorescence loss, indicating that HF blocked autophagosome formation at an early stage in EBSS medium culture. 4. To further elucidate the anticancer activity of HF in vivo by using caloric restriction in nude mice inoculated with human CRC cells We further determined autophagic regulation for anticancer activity of HF in vivo by using nude mice inoculated with CRC cells. In order to conduct different conditions in vivo, caloric restriction (CR) was performed in mice fed with 70 % of normal food intake. As a result, HF treatment retarded tumor growth in xenograft-bearing nude mice fed with standard chow diet. It is well known that CR is one of the most important physiologic factors to induce autophagy. Therefore, CR is mimicking poor nutrition in vitro with autophagic induction. We also found that HF retarded tumor growth in mice fed with 70 % of normal food intake compared to CR control group. Further assays by western blot and immunofluorescent imaging suggest that HF functions as an autophagic inducer in xenograft-bearing nude mice allowed access to food ad libitum whereas an autophagic inhibitor in CR condition.Together, HF treatment not only dually regulates autophagic flux in cancer cells in vitro, but also retards tumor growth in vivo through dual regulation of autophagy.
