12104415.label: Major findings and research outcome
12104415.value: We found HF inhibits cell proliferation and induces apoptosis through Akt/mTORC1 signaling pathway coupling with metabolic pathways, at least partially due to, the inhibition of Akt/mTORC1. Particularly, GLUT1 and HK-II were found to be markedly inhibited in a dose-dependent manner, which might be associated with metabolic reprogramming modulated by HF treatment. Furthermore, the experiments in nude mice inoculated with human CRC cells validated the therapeutic effect of HF, providing direct evidence to support our notion that HF exerts anticancer activity via Akt/mTORC1 signaling pathway. On the other hand, HF induces autophagy through the Akt-mTORC1-ULK1 signaling pathway, whereas it inhibits autophagy via the LKB1-AMPK-ULK1 signaling pathway, indicating that HF not only impedes tumor initiation but also retards tumor growth through an autophagic pathway depending on nutritional status.

12104415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12104415.value: HF induces or inhibits autophagy through modulation of Akt-mTORC1-ULK1 or LKB1-AMPK-ULK1 signaling pathway presented at the current work. Our investigations on autophagic flux validated the hypothesis that HF can dually regulate elongation stage for autophagosome formation. Moreover, glycolysis or gluconeogenesis is inhibited in cancer cells via the autophagic pathway upon HF treatment, providing a promising approach for anticancer by targeting autophagic pathway. More importantly, HF impairs glycolysis or gluconeogenesis via an Atg7-dependent manner, indicating that autophagy is essential for metabolic regulation of HF treatment. We found Atg7 has a critical role in metabolic regulation in mammalian cells upon HF treatment, but other autophagy-related genes are still need to be investigated in the future.

12104415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12104415.value: According to Hong Kong cancer registry, colorectal cancer (CRC) is the commonest cancer in hong kong in 2017. But there is no effective drug to treat CRC, the patients are waiting novel drugs for selectively killing CRC. In the last two decades, HF has gained attention for its potential therapeutic effects in cancer, especialy CRC. However, our goal is to develop HF to be a anticancer drug candidate. So it is more important to understand the mechanism of HF anticancer effect.

12200415.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12200415.value: 研究对用户隐性反馈的提取以建立他们在复杂决策支持系统中的多属性兴趣模型

12200415.label: Project Objectives
12200415.value: To understand how to stimulate users to perform compensatory decision strategy and establish their multi-attribute preference model correspondingly. To implicitly elicit and construct users’ preferences by analyzing their behavior, that combines clicking actions and eye-movement events at two levels: product-level and attribute level. Particularly, the attribute-level elicitation will be targeted to identify the preferential dependency relationship between attributes. To automatically determine the uncertainty degree of elicited preferences, and develop an adaptive recommendation strategy. Particularly, the suggestion of attributes tradeoff relations will be generated for users to clarify their needs and for the system to address uncertain preferences. To implement a proof-of-concept system for testing the proposed methods through both simulations on real-world data and user studies. Both desktop and mobile versions will be prepared for the evaluation. It is expected that our system will allow users to significantly save involvement efforts, while still being able to make accurate decisions in complex application environments.

12200415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200415.value: 在当前的网络环境中，尤其是电子商务，金融投资，资源管理，在线学习等环境中，决策者经常面临如何处理大量和复杂的数据来快速做出准确决策的问题。在心理学领域，使用互补型策略可以帮助他们做出准确决策，比如加权求和方法，促使用户仔细的审查所有相关选项，并在它们之中做出权衡。但是，由于这种策略在认知或情感上会付出一定代价，用户经常会选取不准确即非互补型的策略。研究难点则是如何即能支持用户做出准确的决策，又将他们所花费的时间和精力控制在可接受的范围之内。个性化的决策支持系统，比如基于用户喜好的推荐系统，被证明可以有效的达到这个目的。尤其是当用户的喜好在刚开始不确定和发生变化的时候，基于批判的推荐系统可以使用户进入一种与系统的通话型交互模式，从而能够不断地完善他们的喜好模型。 但是，当前的系统存在两个普遍问题：一是它们要求用户提供显性的反馈，所以用户需要投入一定的精力；二是很难捕捉用户的互补型决策行为，从而会限制系统有效和准确的创建他们的兴趣模型并生成他们会满意的推荐结果。这个项目的主要创新点在于我们会着力于挖掘用户的隐性行为，比如通过他们的鼠标点击事件和眼部活动，来推测他们的兴趣。更准确来说，我们试图开发一个新式的基于批判的推荐系统。它是主要基于隐式提取的用户反馈，来降低用户所投入的精力，并同时提高他们的决策准确性。这个工作是基于我们最近的试探性研究。我们发现用户的隐性行为，尤其是眼部活动相关变量，可以很好的捕捉用户的兴趣点。 我们期望我们的工作可以从以下几个方面来改进目前的复杂型决策支持系统：1) 分析用户的隐性行为能使我们更深入的理解在哪种情况下用户会做出互补型决策以及如何做；2）隐性的爱好提取可以建立在产品和属性两个级别上，从而更准确的建立用户的多属性兴趣模型。值得提的是，属性级别的提取方式或许能够展现属性间的兴趣相关性；3) 用户喜好的不确定性可以通过系统建议属性间的权衡关系来解决；4) 我们会通过模拟实验和用户学习等方式来评测系统的性能。

12200415.label: Realisation of objectives
12200415.value: In this project, we have basically achieved all of the objectives proposed at the beginning. In particular, we have studied how to infer users' implicit feedback on recommendations through their eye-movement behavior. In recommender systems, critiquing has been popularly applied as an effective approach to obtaining users' feedback on recommended products. In order to reduce users' efforts of creating critiquing criteria on their own, some systems have aimed at suggesting critiques for users to choose. How to accurately match system-suggested critiques to users' intended feedback hence becomes a challenging issue. To address this issue, we have taken into account users' eye movements on recommendations to derive their critiquing feedback. By means of analyzing a collection of real users' eye-gaze data at both product and attribute levels, we have demonstrated the approach's feasibility of implicitly deriving users' critiquing criteria. It hence indicates a promising direction of using eye tracking technique to improve existing critique suggestion methods. (achieved Objectives 1 and 2). Moreover, we have designed a novel explanation interface for recommender systems. To be specific, the explanation interface has been recognized important in recommender systems as it can help users evaluate recommendations in a more informed way for deciding which ones are relevant to their interests. In different decision environments, the specific aim of explanation can be different. In high-investment product domains (e.g., digital cameras, laptops) for which users usually attempt to avoid financial risk, how to support users to construct stable preferences and make better decisions is particularly crucial. Our explanation interface emphasizes explaining the tradeoff properties within a set of recommendations in terms of both their static specifications and feature sentiments extracted from product reviews. The objective is to assist users in more effectively exploring and understanding product space, and being able to better formulate their preferences for products by learning from other customers’ experiences. Through two user studies (in form of both before-after and within-subjects experiments), we empirically identify the practical role of feature sentiments in combination with static specifications in producing tradeoff-oriented explanations. Specifically, we find that our explanation interface can be more effective to increase users’ product knowledge, preference certainty, perceived information usefulness, recommendation transparency and quality, and purchase intention. In order to further identify the reason behind users’ perception improvements on the sentiment-based explanation interface, we performed a follow-up lab controlled eye-tracking experiment that investigated how users viewed information and compared products on the interface. This study shows that incorporating sentiment features into the tradeoff-oriented explanations can significantly affect users’ eye-gaze pattern. They were stimulated to not only notice bottom categories of products, but also, more frequently, to compare products across categories. The results also disclose users’ inherent information needs for sentiment-based explanations, as they allow users to better understand the recommended products and gain more knowledge about static specifications. (achieved Objectives 3 and 4)

12200415.label: Major findings and research outcome
12200415.value: There are four major findings: 1. We have proposed an eye-based feedback elicitation method, so as to reduce users’ self-critiquing efforts. Based on a collection of real users’ eye-gaze data, we have demonstrated the idea’s feasibility. 2. We have compared different recommendation interfaces (the interface that displays a set of recommended products), and found that the category layout performs better than the list structure in terms of stimulating users to view recommended products. As a result, multiple design guidelines are derived from our user experiment. 3. We have developed a novel tradeoff-oriented explanation interface that particularly takes into account sentiment features as extracted from product reviews to generate recommendations and explanations in a category structure. Through both before-after and within-subjects user studies, we found that adding sentiment-based explanations can significantly increase users’ product knowledge, preference certainty, perceived information usefulness, perceived recommendation transparency and quality, and purchase intention. 4. We further performed a follow-up lab controlled eye-tracking experiment that investigated how users viewed information and compared products on the interface. This study shows that incorporating sentiment features into the tradeoff-oriented explanations can significantly affect users’ eye-gaze pattern. They were stimulated to not only notice bottom categories of products, but also, more frequently, to compare products across categories.

12200415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12200415.value: In the future, we will conduct more eye-tracking experiments. One goal is to verify the impact of recommendation layout on users’ fixation behavior in different product domains. For instance, people may make decisions differently when they are searching for a high value product like a laptop, compared to search for a low-value product like a movie. Moreover, users’ personal knowledge background (such as product knowledge and online shopping experiences) may also affect their behavior: Novices may behave differently from expert buyers when they search and evaluate products. We expect that future experiments with the participation of more users would be helpful for clarifying this point. On the other hand, we will continue to collect users’ critiquing data in a more realistic scenario (for example, with a large size of product catalog for users to search), so as to measure the accuracy of our eye-based inference rules. For this goal, we will investigate more fixation metrics, such as fixation spatial density, saccade/fixation ratio, and scanpath. In addition, regarding explanation interface design, we will compare our interface with more variations of the explanatory view based on sentiment features. Considering few related work has emphasized multi-item explanation, we will first investigate the feasibility of extending their single-item explanations for multiple items. Moreover, as inspired by related work that can suggest contexts (e.g., location, time, mood) suitable for the current recommendation, we may extract contextual opinions from reviews to further augment the explanation’s context compatibility. Last but not least, we will study our explanation interface’s effect on enhancing beyond-accuracy user metrics, such as recommendation novelty, diversity, and serendipity, which may help strengthen the role of explanations in improving users’ overall satisfaction with the recommender system.

12200415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12200415.value: In the current online environment, a decision maker often encounters the challenge of how to overcome the overwhelming data for making an efficient and accurate decision, especially in the complex application domains such as e-commerce, financial investment, resource scheduling, trip planning, online learning, and so on. Personalized decision support, such as the preference-based recommender system, has been demonstrated as an effective approach to achieving this objective. Particularly, considering that users’ preferences are usually unstable and incomplete at the beginning of their decision process, the so-called critiquing-based recommender system (CBRS) has been proposed to involve users into a conversational interaction model with the system, with the purpose of incrementally constructing and refining their preferences by eliciting their explicit critiques to the recommended items. The novelty of this project is that we have exploited users’ implicit behavior, by means of combining their clicking actions and eye movements, for eliciting their preferences. We have concretely developed a novel critiquing-based recommender system with sentiment-based explanation interface based on implicitly elicited feedback, so as to reduce users’ involvement efforts while still allowing them to obtain high decision accuracy. We believe this work can contribute to the field of complex decision support from the following aspects. 1) The analysis of users’ implicit behavior enables us to in depth understand in which condition, and how, users perform compensatory decision strategy. 2) The implicit preference elicitation can be conducted at both product and attribute levels for more accurately building users’ multi-attribute preference model. 3) The uncertainty of elicited user preferences can be addressed by suggesting the attributes tradeoff relations for users to consider and choose.

12200915.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12200915.value: 对功能磁共振成像数据的基于张量模型的独立成分学习

12200915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200915.value: 功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）是一種神經影像學技術，對理解人類大腦功能和活動非常重要。然而，fMRI數據是很大的數據，fMRI掃描兩小時內可以產生數千兆字節的數據。如今，越來越多的fMRI數據公開了，使得機器學習研究人員也可以比較容易參與相關研究。因此，在這個項目中，我們的目標是開發和fMRI數據相關的機器學習方法。獨立成分分析（ICA）是一種重要的盲源分離（BSS）方法，並已經用於分析fMRI數據，但是通常取矢量值觀測數據作為輸入。然而，fMRI掃描序列數據本身是多維數據，用張量（多維數組）表示（作為輸入）更加自然。因此，該項目的目標是研究使用張量為基礎的模型和算法來對fMRI做獨立成分分析。我們將提出具有普遍性的模型和算法，並提供新的機學習工具。

12201215.label: Realisation of objectives
12201215.value: The three listed objectives have been realized satisfactorily. Details are discussed as follows. Objective 1: We have developed a new 3D mask attack dataset and an rPPG based face anti-spoofing framework. Details are discussed as follows. Since there was only one 3D mask dataset (3DMAD) publicly available, it is not sufficient for the algorithm development and experiments. As such, we decided to build a new 3D mask anti-spooﬁng database in-house with more variations to simulate the real world scenario. The database contains 12 subjects and 12 masks from two companies (thatsmyface and REALF) with different qualities. Each subject contains 42 (7 cameras x 6 lightings) genuine and 42 mask sequences, and 1008 (42x2x12) videos in total. The dataset, namely HKBU-MARs has been released to public for academic research. 59 universities/research centers have signed the agreement and downloaded the dataset for their research. Details of the dataset can be found at http://rds.comp.hkbu.edu.hk/mars/. To overcome the limitation of generalization ability of traditional appearance-based methods, we have developed an rPPG based face anti-spoofing framework and algorithm. First, we have studied in-depth the theory of rPPG from life science perspective and then developed a rPPG face anti-spoofing framework. We have proposed an anti-spooﬁng method by detecting pulse (heart rate) from face videos. The basic idea is that rPPG signal is available in a real living face but it is too weak to be detected in a masked face. Based on this idea, we have proposed and developed an rPPG-based method for 3D mask face anti-spoofing. The method could be a generalized solution for face liveness detection. This method has been reported and published ICPR 2016. Objective 2: We have proposed and developed two rPPG algorithms which are robust to moving faces under illumination changes. To improve the robustness of the rPPG-based algorithms, we have explored a local rPPG approach. A face image is divided into a number of small image patches and local rPPG signals are estimated from image patches. A correlation model is proposed to determine the cross-correlation of two local rPPG signals so as to enhance the shared heartbeat amplitude on a genuine face while the random noise is attenuated. The rPPG signals extracted from masked face regions will suppress because they are random noise and do not share the same periodic frequency. To further boost the robustness, we have proposed a local rPPG confidence map to emphasize the regions with strong heartbeat signal and weaken unreliable regions which contain weak heartbeat signals. Experimental results on 3DMAD and our HKBU-MARs V1 datasets with both intra and cross dataset evaluation protocols demonstrates the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method. This work has been published in the ECCV 2016. While the robustness of our local rPPG algorithm published in ECCV 2016 is improved, the assumption that the peak of the rPPG signal spectrum reflects the heartbeat signal may not hold in some practical scenarios. How to precisely identify the heartbeat information from the observed noisy rPPG signals is critical. To address this issue, we have proposed and developed a novel rPPG correspondence feature (CFrPPG) which learns the heartbeat verification template from local facial regions and uses the correspondence between the learned template and local rPPG signals as the robust liveness feature. To handle the global (background) noise, we extract rPPG signals from background regions and incorporate them as a constraint into the template estimation. Experimental results on 3DMAD, our HKBU-MARs V1+ and the Replay Attack Datasets show that the proposed CFrPPG not only outperforms the state-of-the-art rPPG based methods on 3D mask attacks but also be able to handle the real environment with poor lighting and head motion. This work has been published in the ECCV 2018. Objective 3: Two versions of completed rPPG-based face anti-spoofing methods are developed. We have also explored other directions and developed deep-learning-based algorithms for face anti-spoofing. Details are described as follows. Most, if not all rPPG-based face anti-spoofing methods are based on the signal spectrum analysis, and required long observation time (~10 seconds) to identify the sufficient number of stable heartbeat cycles. This limits the deployment of the algorithms in real applications. To reduce the observation time, we have proposed the temporal similarity of rPPG (TSrPPG) method by analyzing the rPPG signal waveforms in time domain. Specifically, an rPPG temporal similarity feature operator is proposed to extract both similarity and amplitude information in short observation time. Experimental results on 4 datasets with large number of variations on mask type, lighting condition, camera, and video quality show that the proposed TSrPPG outperforms the state-of-the-art rPPG-based methods with short observation time while maintaining the generalization ability. This work has been published and presented in the WACV 2020. Obtaining quality rPPG signal is one of the key aspects achieving good performance of rPPG-based face anti-spoofing. We have investigated other ways to estimate rPPG and proposed a lightweight rPPG estimation network, namely DeeprPPG. DeeprPPG is based on spatiotemporal convolutions and can be used as a generic module with different types of input skin regions. To further boost the robustness, a spatiotemporal rPPG aggregation strategy is designed to adaptively aggregate rPPG signals from multiple skin regions. We have conducted experiments on three publicly available datasets with facial motion, video compression, and different lighting conditions. The proposed DeeprPPG outperforms state-of-the-art methods and also generalizes well on different skin regions. This work has been published in the FG 2020. Besides rPPG approach, we have also explored deep learning methods. The basic idea is to extract subtle facial spatial and temporal differences between a real face and a masked face. Along this line, we ﬁnd that (i) the subtle facial motion can be captured by multiple deep dynamic textures from a convolutional layer of convolutional neural network, and (ii) not all deep dynamic textures from different spatial regions and different channels of a convolutional layer are useful for the differentiation. Motivated by this observation, we have proposed a new deep learning algorithm to extract those information for face anti-spoofing. This work has been published in IEEE TIFS 2019. The last piece of work in this project is our preliminary study of the generalization of unseen attacks. This work focuses on improving the generalization ability of face anti-spooﬁng methods from the perspective of the domain generalization. We have proposed to learn a generalized feature space via a novel multi-adversarial discriminative deep domain generalization algorithm. In this algorithm, a multi-adversarial deep domain generalization is proposed to learn a generalized feature space which is shared by multiple discriminative source domains. Moreover, the constraint of dual-force triplet mining is imposed on the learning process, which improves the discriminability of the learned feature space. This work has been published in CVPR 2019.

Examine and develop a new face anti-spoofing method based on the methods developed in (1) and (2), and state-of-the art face anti-spoofing techniques.

12201215.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201215.value: 1. Remote photoplethysmograph (rPPG) is a good and feasible approach for 3D mask face anti-spoofing. It is theoretically sound. Comparing with existing appearance-based approach, it could differentiate a real face and fake face by detecting the present of rPPG signals, in particular high-quality masks. This project has successfully developed one global rPPG-based anti-spoofing framework. Experimental results shown that rPPG-based approach has a better generalization ability. The framework and algorithm has been reported in ICPR2016 [C3]. 2. One limitation of global rPPG-based algorithm is that it is sensitive to illumination variations and head motion. To address this issue, we have shown that local rPPG is a good and feasible approach to increase the robustness. This project has demonstrated that correlation model and rPPG signal confident map could improve the performance on extracting the correct heartbeat while suppressing the noise introduced by the illumination and head motion. The proposed rPPG method has been published in ECCV2016 [C2]. 3. The local rPPG algorithm reported in ECCV2016 can be fooled using an external artificial frequency source (e.g. flash light). To overcome this limitation, we found that background information can be used as a verification check. Along this line, this project has proposed a corresponding rPPG features which could compensate/remove this external artificial source frequency. The proposed method has been published in ECCV2018 [C4]. 4. Spectral-based rPPG algorithms requires a long observation time which limits the practicality of the algorithm. As such, time-domain analysis of rPPG signals is important. Along this line, we have developed a time-domain rPPG algorithm which only requires 1-2 seconds to detect the heartbeat. The proposed algorithm has been published in WACV2020 [C5]. Moreover, traditional rPPG signals are extracted using a predefined linear combination of RGB values. It is found that deep learning is more effective in extracting rPPG signals. Along this line, we have proposed a new rPPG signal extraction algorithm which has been reported in FG2020 [C6]. 5. Besides the proposed rPPG approach, we have also explored and demonstrated that deep learning is able to extract subtle spatial and temporal differences between a real face and a mask. The proposed algorithm has been published in IEEE-TIFS2019 [J1]. Moreover, we have suggested that it is important to generalize the anti-spoofing from 3D mask attack to generic and unseen attack. Along this line, we have published our preliminary work in CVPR2019 [C7]. Note: [X#] refers to reference in conference/journal number in Part C.

12201215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201215.value: Face biometrics have been fully employed in many practical applications for person identification such as mobile e-payment. However, it has been shown that face biometrics system can be fooled by different types of attacks, e.g. presenting a face photo to the system. With the advanced 3D technology, high-quality 3D masks can be created with an affordable cost. As such, 3D mask presentation attack becomes an important threat because human cannot be easily tell the differences between a real face and a masked face. Of course, 3D mask can fool the existing face recognition systems. This project addresses the research issues in developing detection methods for the 3D mask attack. In particular, we have developed methods to detect the heartbeat signals from a face video to differentiate a real-face or a fake-face. The basic idea is that the heartbeat signals are too weak to be detected from a masked face video. Experimental results show that our proposed methods could effectively differentiate a real face and a fake face. We have also tested on different types of masks and the results are consistent. The proposed methods can be employed for real face verification before proceeding to the face recognition.

12201315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201315.value: 近年，圖數據被廣泛應用，例如在生物或化學數據庫，社交網絡，相關採購網絡和信息網絡上，等等。這些應用給予了圖數據的研究新的課題，相關的數據庫系統或平台也不斷推出。而參與研發這些系統或平台的單位也很多樣化，有研究實驗室，創業公司和生命科學公司等。 在數據庫研究的自我評估報告中提到，系統可用性一直是數據庫的一個重要課題。不難發現，系統可用性在圖數據上更為重要，原因包括：圖數據模型可能很鬆散，未能幫助編寫查詢或應用程式；圖數據查詢可以很複雜，難以人工編寫，也容易引致人為錯誤。這項目提出以子圖查詢的回饋信息來幫助用戶來搜尋或探索圖數據庫，使圖數據庫更可用。 這項目的第一部份是把（子圖）查詢回饋正式寫成兩個全新的基礎的子圖查詢。用戶可以用這兩個查詢的結果為回饋訊息，幫助他們編輯他們心目中的查詢或調整系統的設定。 這兩個查詢適合被整合於一個視覺介面上(如我們的前期工作)， 提供用戶一個自然的圖查詢的環境。據我們所知，這樣的查詢回饋未被研究過。我們會用數據庫的研究方法來解決這兩個查詢，我們計劃做全面的實驗和小型的用戶測試。

12201315.label: Realisation of objectives
12201315.value: Objective 1 has been investigated in various forms in [1, 7, 8], although they are not exactly formulated as WIFSSQ and WNSSQ. The database system will return the query suggestions (i.e. subgraph feedback) to users. The users may adopt the suggestions, retrieve some answers and repeat this process to explore the graph database. - More specifically, users can provide feedback in the form of a mouse cursor position to the GUI of a graph database [1]. The mouse cursor indicates the position of a graph query that the system requires to provide subgraph feedback. The GUI exploits it to formulate a "query" and retrieve a ranked list of query suggestions as "query answer". User can adopt the suggestions as their next query. - Users can inform the GUI of a graph database their preferences to subgraph feedback [7, 8]. For example, they can either look for queries that return more answers or the queries that are more structurally different. Regarding Objective 2, the algorithms of [1, 7, 8] have been integrated with a GUI (http://www.comp.hkbu.edu.hk/~csppyi/autog/). The system architectures have been reported in [1, 6, 8]. The current prototype runs on a commodity machine and serves one request at a time. We have prepared a virtual machine for interested users to try the prototype on their machines. In addition, the GUI opens up opportunities for research issues. In [2], we constructed and maintained some canned patterns for the GUI from an analysis of the database characteristics. Users can choose those patterns to explore the graph database. In [4], we allow users to analyze why the suggestions not useful, in terms of their preference for the suggestions. Regarding Objective 3, we have investigated the interleaving of query formulation time and query processing time for some advanced graph queries [5, 6]. When the users finished drawing/formulating their queries, the query processing has almost finished. Hence, the time that query answers are delivered to users can be significantly reduced. The suggestions can be delivered interactively. Furthermore, [6] embodies several novel features such as progressive (i.e., iterative) formulation of queries visually and incremental processing, multi-stream results exploration wall to visualize, explore, and analyze search results to identify possible search directions. Regarding Objective 4, [1-8] have been experimentally evaluated. The results show that the query suggestions are useful (saved roughly 40% mouse clicks when using GUI to formulate queries). User tests have been conducted. The users generally agreed the feedbacks are useful. We have also consolidated the findings of this proposal in a book [3]. 12201315.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201315.value: This proposal investigates a wide range of GUI feedback that enables users to explore the data in a graph database. In [1, 7, 8], we propose that graph database systems will return the query suggestions (i.e. subgraph feedback) to users, based on user's current query and the database's characteristics. The users may adopt the suggestions, retrieve some answers and repeat this process to explore the graph database. Users can also provide feedback in the form of a mouse cursor position to the GUI of a graph database [1]. The mouse cursor indicates the position of a graph query that the system requires to provide subgraph feedback. Also, users can inform the GUI of a graph database their preferences to subgraph feedback [7, 8]. For example, they can either look for queries that return more answers or the queries that are more structurally different. We have experimentally evaluated the techniques. The results show that the query suggestions are useful (saved roughly 40% mouse clicks when using GUI to formulate queries). User tests have been conducted. The users generally agreed the feedbacks are useful. The algorithms of [1, 7, 8] have been integrated with a GUI (http://www.comp.hkbu.edu.hk/~csppyi/autog/). The system architectures have been reported in [1, 6, 8]. The current prototype runs on a commodity machine and serves one request at a time. We have prepared a virtual machine for interested users to try the prototype on their machines. We have also consolidated the findings of this proposal in a book [3]. * References are listed in Section 5.3.

12201315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201315.value: Graphs are a powerful tool for a wide range of applications, from biological (such as pfam) and chemical (such as PubChem) databases, social networks, citation networks to information networks. Classical queries, namely subgraph queries, have recently been revisited for performance enhancements. There is an evident and pressing need for informative and user-friendly tools for retrieving graphs. For example, the "Draw a Structure" Graphical User Interface (GUI) is proposed to enable users to drag-and-drop subgraphs, as GUIs facilitate a more natural means of specifying structural queries. However, usable tools mean much more than a decent GUI. This proposal investigates a wide range of GUI feedback that enables users to explore the data in a graph database. Firstly, the GUI can provides a ranked list of query suggestions, given the user's current query. Secondly, if the suggestions are returned are different from users' expected, the GUI analyzes probable ranking perferences of the users. Thirdly, the users can use a mouse to indicate the location of the graph query that query suggestions are needed. Fourthly, GUI can be constructed and maintained by analyzing the data in the graph database. Finally, extensively algorithmic techniques have been studied to allow feedbacks to be delivered interactively.

12201615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201615.value: 隨著智能手機和地理定位裝置的盛行，共乘被認為是一個有效的解決方案，以緩解像香港這樣的大城市中交通運輸相關的問題，如道路擁堵和空氣污染等。最近的研究報告指出，如果用戶願意和出行方式相似的人分享乘車，城市的交通流量可以減少高達31-59％。儘管有這麼多好處，到目前為止共乘並不十分流行。值得注意的障礙包括與陌生人共乘時產生的不適及安全問題。因此，為了克服這些障礙，在這個項目中，我們提出社交感知的共乘服務，除了傳統的時空鄰近性，在共乘參與者分配時特別考慮他們之間的社交關係。研究內容主要包括以下幾個方面：1）對適合共乘服務的社交關係進行建模；2）設計社交感知的高效共乘分配算法；3）對所提出的算法在流量減少和節能方面進行性能評價；4）開發原型系統，以證明我們的建議的可行性。

12201615.label: Realisation of objectives
12201615.value: The project objectives have been successfully realized. To address the issues related to social discomfort and safety concerns, we have proposed social-aware ridesharing services, whereby participants’ social connections are considered besides spatio-temporal proximity in assigning them to shared rides. There are a number of social models that can be employed to measure the social cohesiveness of a ridesharing group, such as star (friend), star (friend of friend), and k-core. We have conducted an online survey with 216 volunteers to compare these social models. We have also examined the potential groups under different social models for the users of New York City in two real datasets (Brightlike and Gollawa). Based on the evaluation results, k-core has been selected as the primary social model to address the social-aware ridesharing problems. We then proceeded to study the ridesharing assignment problem and started by considering the slugging ridesharing model [Journal/1]. We have designed a new type of Social-aware Ridesharing Group (SaRG) queries to retrieve the best riders for a given driver. We have proved that the SaRG query problem is NP-hard, and hence developed an efficient algorithm with a set of powerful pruning techniques to tackle this problem. We have also proposed several incremental strategies to accelerate the search speed by reducing repeated computations. Moreover, we have proposed a novel social-aware index to further speed up query processing. Experimental results on real datasets show that our proposed algorithms achieve desirable performance. In addition, we have studied geo-social k-cover group queries for collaborative spatial computing tasks including ridesharing [Conference/3], geo-social k-core group search to find nearby users with minimum acquaintance constraints [Journal/2], and the trip planning problem for bike-sharing systems [Conference/1]. We have also introduced the social-awareness into realtime taxi ridesharing services [Conference/2]. In particular, upon receiving a user’s trip request, the service ranks feasible taxis in a way that integrates detour in time and passengers’ cohesion in social distance. We have proposed a new system framework to support such a social-aware taxi-sharing service. It provides two methods for selecting candidate taxis for a given trip request. The grid-based method quickly goes through available taxis and returns a relatively larger candidate set, whereas the edge-based method takes more time to obtain a smaller candidate set. Furthermore, we have designed techniques to speed up taxi route scheduling for a given trip request. We have evaluated our proposals using a real taxi dataset from New York City. Experimental results demonstrate the efficiency and scalability of the proposed taxi recommendation solution in real-time social-aware ridesharing services. For batch ridesharing services where ridesharing requests and offers are known in advance, we have formulated a new problem, named Assignment of Requests to Offers (ARO) [Conference/4, Journal/3]. We seek to maximize the number of served riders while satisfying the social comfort constraints as well as spatial-temporal constraints. We have proved that the ARO problem is NP-hard. We then proposed an exact algorithm for a simplified ARO problem. We further proposed three pruning strategies to efficiently narrow down the searching space and speed up the assignment processing. Based on these pruning strategies, we developed two novel heuristic algorithms, the request-oriented approach and offer-oriented approach, to tackle the ARO problem. We have also studied the dynamic ARO problem and presented a novel algorithm to tackle this problem. To better incentivize drivers and riders to participate in ridesharing, we have proposed a new pricing scheme and investigated a novel type of Price-aware Top-k Matching (PTkM) queries [Journal/4].

12201615.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201615.value: We have studied various social models and proposed k-core as the primary model to formulate the social-aware ridesharing problems. Based on that, we have designed a number of efficient ride assignment algorithms, including slugging-based ridesharing [Journal/1], taxi ridesharing [Conference/2], price-aware ridesharing [Journal/4], and batch ridesharing [Conference/4, Journal/3]. In addition, we have studied geo-social k-cover group queries for collaborative spatial computing tasks including ridesharing [Conference/3], geo-social k-core group search to find nearby users with minimum acquaintance constraints [Journal/2], and the trip planning problem for bike-sharing systems [Conference/1]. In all the above studies, we have evaluated the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithms using real datasets. Moreover, a demonstration system has been developed to showcase the proposed techniques and services.

12201615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12201615.value: While ridesharing draws more and more attention from both academia and industries, existing solutions suffer from two major drawbacks. On the one hand, existing techniques often lack of scalability, which make them less practical. On the other hand, only limited types of ridesharing are studied. Therefore, as for future work, we would like to seek distributed solutions to support large-scale systems and study new types of ridesharing queries to improve the service quality. More specifically, first, we plan to design a distributed realtime ridesharing system to deal with high computation workload. We intend to study the distribution strategy to balance the workload and minimize the data to be exchanged between servers. Second, we plan to develop a ridesharing publish/subscribe system, in which riders’ requests keep coming in as a stream and drivers register subscriptions so that the system can push proper ride requests to them. Third, we plan to investigate a novel activity-based ridersharing service, where riders do not have specific destinations but only target activities to complete. As there exists a set of candidate destinations for an activity, this service poses additional challenges in ride assignment and request matching.

12201615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201615.value: With the deep penetration of smartphones and geo-locating devices, ridesharing is envisioned as a promising solution to mitigate transportation-related problems such as congestion and air pollution for metropolitan cities like Hong Kong. As reported in a recent study, the potential reduction of urban traffic can be as high as 31-59% if individuals with similar travel itineraries and schedules are willing to share a ride. However, despite the potential to provide significant societal and environmental benefits, ridesharing has not so far been as popular as expected. Notable barriers include social discomfort and safety concerns about traveling with strangers. To overcome these barriers, this project proposes social-aware ridesharing services, whereby participants’ social connections are considered besides spatio-temporal proximity in assigning them to shared rides. We have developed social models that can improve trust among rideshare participants while keeping rideshare assignments flexible. We have also designed a number of efficient ride assignment algorithms to support social-aware ridesharing services.

12202415.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12202415.value: 基于数据驱动的系统地理学推论揭示疾病时空传播特征

12202415.label: Co - Investigator(s)
12202415.value: Dr Liu, Yang Dr Shi, Benyun Prof Zhou, Xiao-Nong

12202415.label: Project Objectives
12202415.value: To develop an integrated Bayesian inference approach to modeling the real-world geographic diffusion of infectious diseases by incorporating informative priors about both the spatial ecology of the migrant hosts and the viral evolution of the epidemic pathogens.
rows: To develop an integrated Bayesian inference approach to modeling the real-world geographic diffusion of infectious diseases by incorporating informative priors about both the spatial ecology of the migrant hosts and the viral evolution of the epidemic pathogens.

12202415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12202415.value: The geographical spread of infectious diseases has been and will continue to be a serious public health concern in both Hong Kong and mainland China. Typical examples of these diseases include the influenza A(H5N1) outbreak in 1997, the swine flu (H1N1) pandemic in 2009, and the influenza A(H7N9) epidemic in 2013. Computationally, disease diffusion networks can be used to characterize how these diseases spread from one geographic location to another. In these networks, nodes represent locations and edges represent the diffusion dynamics between the locations. From a particular disease diffusion network, we can identify underlying disease hotspots and critical diffusion paths, information that can help public health authorities to achieve active surveillance and efficient control of the disease. However, in practice, such networks are often hidden; we can observe only the locations and times or genome sequences of disease incidences. In this project, we will develop and evaluate an integrated Bayesian inference approach to uncovering real-world disease diffusion networks. The uniqueness of this approach is that it mines and incorporates informative priors from heterogeneous data sources. Examples of such priors include the spatiotemporal distribution of the disease hosts and the evolutionary relationships of the viral sequences. Taking the influenza A(H5N1) viruses in China as a case study, this project contributes to the interdisciplinary field of phylogeographic inference (that is aimed to reveal the geographic spread of disease viruses based on their evolutionary relationships, i.e., phylogenetic trees). Firstly, we propose a Bayesian inference approach to mapping disease diffusion networks based on a reconstructed phylogenetic tree. Secondly, we develop a novel clustering method to characterize spatiotemporal distributions of disease hosts from sparse and biased observation data to avoid the general network inference problem of estimating a large number of free parameters (i.e., n(n-1) unknown diffusion rates for n locations). Thirdly, we design novel Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms to account for the uncertainties in generating phylogenetic trees from the genome sequences of disease viruses and evaluate the proposed methods/algorithms by comparing them with those from existing studies, using both synthetic and real-world datasets. As far as we know, this project is one of the first attempts to incorporate spatial ecology and viral evolution in a phylogeographic inference study. Such computationally obtained results can offer new insights into investigating diffusion networks of other diseases, whose geographic diffusion is caused by host mobility and migration. 在中国大陆和香港，传染性疾病的蔓延都是重要的公共健康问题。典型的例子包括，在香港爆发的H5N1 甲型流感（1997年）和H1N1猪流感（2009年）；在中国东部扩散的H7N9甲型流感（2013年）。在疾病传播网络模型中，每个节点表示一个地区，而其之间的边表示地区之间疾病传播动态。利用这个模型，我们可以对疾病的空间传播进行建模，识别出潜在的疾病传播热点地区和关键的传播路径等对公共健康部门非常有用的信息。然而，在现实中，疾病传播网络往往是隐藏的；我们只能观察到感染案例的患病时间，地点或者病毒基因序列。在此项目中，我们将开发并评估一种集成贝叶斯推理的方法，以揭示现实中疾病传播的网络。这个方法的独特之处在于它可以从异构数据中挖掘并集成有用的先验知识，如疾病宿主的时空分布和病毒基因序列的演化关系等。以中国的H5N1 甲型流感作为个案研究，本次项目将会促进系统地理学的交叉学科研究。首先，我们提出了一个新的基于贝叶斯推理的能根据病毒演化系统树来重构疾病传播网络的算法。然后，我们采用了一种新的聚类方法来通过稀疏的有噪音的观察数据刻画病毒宿主的时空分布。最后，我们设计了一个基于马尔科夫蒙特卡洛的新算法来解释从病毒基因序列构造系统发生树时出现的不确定性。我们提出的算法会与现有算法进行比较，以评估其性能。本项目率先尝试在系统地理推论研究中引入空间生态学和病毒演化，并能够为类似的疾病空间传播研究提供新的视角。

12202415.label: Realisation of objectives
12202415.value: The objective of developing an integrated data-driven inference and modeling approach to understanding the real-world geographic diffusion of infectious diseases while incorporating informative priors about both the spatial ecology of the migrant hosts and the viral evolution of the epidemic pathogens has been successfully achieved through a series of activities in an attempt to answer several important research questions. 1. To characterize the real-world geographic diffusion of infectious diseases, we developed and tested a novel complex-network modeling scheme, in which the nodes represented the host subpopulation in a certain geographic location and the edges corresponded to the spatial interactions between the two connected subpopulation nodes, e.g., the human host spatial mobility between the two locations, as a prior. Based on such a modeling scheme, we further took on the challenge of computing the diffusion dynamics on such a metapopulation network. Having carefully studied the existing centrality metrics as developed and used in the field of network science, we further derived a novel, improved meta-centrality formulation, and tested its diffusion prediction performances through a series of large-scale infectious disease diffusion simulations on various types of real-world social (simulated spatial mobility) networks. Please refer to journal article [1] in Section 8. 2. In addition to modeling the host spatial mobility characteristics and their impacts on disease diffusion, we further considered the complex real-world situations where multiple factors or informative priors are involved that could directly affect the spatiotemporal characteristics of disease spreading. These factors range from the ecological/environmental heterogeneities of the spatial locations, to climate, and to the viral evolution of the epidemic pathogens. Without loss of generality, to address such a complexity issue, we specifically considered the real-world case of Dengue transmissions and outbreak that happened in Guangzhou, China, a few years ago, as our background motivation. And furthermore, we developed a data-driven modeling methodology for performing the essential task of integrated inferences while incorporating various impacting factors. Please refer to journal article [2] in Section 8. 3. Once the inverse problem of estimating the transmission impact factors and their interplays underlying disease diffusion dynamics is solved, a natural extension would be to take one step further, i.e., to make use of the estimated dynamics models, such as the contact patterns of different subpopulations, in planning effective disease control/intervention strategies. As far as such planning (e.g., taking into account subpopulation sizes, contact patterns, infection rates, and infectious risks) is concerned, we formulated and implemented a hybrid SEIR-V model (HSEIR-V), and evaluated its performances under various conditions. Please refer to journal article [3] in Section 8. 4. The above-mentioned studies were aimed to uncover infectious disease diffusion dynamics on a metapopulation-based network, where each node represented a homogeneous subpopulation, such as an age-group. Our next step was to examine the case of an individual-based diffusion network, where each node could correspond to a person/individual, as in social contact-based disease transmission. What makes this problem interesting as well as challenging is that, while modeling the disease diffusion, only can the states of nodes/individuals be empirically observed, whereas the underlying diffusion networks are unknown. Thus, our first research task along this line was to develop and test a probabilistic method for inferring a diffusion network based on node-level observations (cascades). To enhance the inference performance, we proposed to incorporate an important structural prior of networks, i.e., motifs, as they frequently appear in real-world social networks and hence can play a vital role in describing network structures and functionalities. To the best of our knowledge, no existing work had attempted to infer an individual-level diffusion network through exploiting network motif priors. Please refer to journal article [4] in Section 8. 5. Besides the above-mentioned local network structures, another important topological characteristic that could have a critical impact on diffusion dynamics is network community, which is ubiquitous in social networks. Empirical and experimental observations have shown that such an impact is present not only in infectious disease dynamics/outbreaks, but also in information diffusion dynamics in network-based environments. Based on the observations, we aimed to gain a deeper, theoretical understanding of the diffusion processes on networks containing community structures. We focused on the nonlinear crossover of two diffusion processes, i.e., central-user-based and boundary-user based processes as triggered by two opposite initial states of the networks with community structures. We first considered the universality of the crossover phenomenon, and then offered detailed comparisons with respect to the influences of community structures and initial proportions of source nodes on the diffusion processes. Please refer to journal article [5] in Section 8. 6. Last but not the least, in addition to the above-mentioned research tasks, we further studied the research question of how to quantitively model and characterize the phylogeography of an epidemic pathogen. We specifically focused on the case of the influenza A (H7N9) virus in China. First, we conducted a phylogenetic analysis on 626 viral sequences of avian influenza A (H7N9) virus isolated in chicken (based on Global Initiative on Sharing All Influenza Data (GISAID)) to reveal geographical spread and molecular evolution of the virus in China. Next, we adopted the cross correlation function (CCF) to explore the relationship between the identified influenza A (H7N9) cases and the spatiotemporal distribution of migratory birds. Finally, we employed a kernel density estimator to identify geographical hotspots of bird habitat/stopover that could be most relevant to the influenza A (H7N9) infections. Please refer to journal article [6] in Section 8.

12202415.label: Major findings and research outcome
12202415.value: In this project, we examined the dynamic characteristics of disease spatial diffusion in a global metapopulation network, and develop a novel metric for determining the critical nodes, known as “super-spreaders”. A software tool was developed to demonstrate the proposed method. These results could have implications to present/future studies on metapopulation-level disease dynamics, e.g., on the most recent COVID-19 disease pandemic [1]. One of the challenges faced in the real-world modeling is to computationally uncover the underlying transmission networks, as shown in the cases of metapopulation [2][3] and individual-based transmission networks. In this project, we developed a novel method, called motif-aware diffusion network inference (MADNI), for inferring the motif profile from the node-level cascades/observations, and furthermore identifying the underlying network based on the mined motis. We provided two network inference models in our framework for inferring metapopulation-level and individual-level diffusion networks, respectively. Our studies using both synthetic and real-world datasets systematically validated the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Moreover, we showed the generality of MADNI by unveiling the relationships between mesoscale motif priors in our framework and other high-level structural priors, such as community and scale-free properties in the existing work [4]. Concerning individual-based networks, as can be inferred by using the above-developed method [4], it would be most desirable and important for us to be able to further characterize their associated critical diffusion behaviors. In this project, we showed, both empirically and theoretically, that nodes with relatively least centrality could lead to a greater propagation effect in the long term, especially when a network includes more initial source nodes, whereas the ability of nodes with relatively greater centrality tends to dramatically enhance diffusion speed at the initial stage [5]. Another important outcome of this project is that we provided a method for conducting a phylogenetic analysis that helped us reveal the evolutionary and geographical patterns of influenza A (H7N9) infections and enabled us identify possible migratory bird species that were relevant to the influenza A (H7N9) infections in Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Fujian, Jiangxi, and Guangdong in China, where the six municipality/provinces accounted for 91.2% of the total number of isolated H7N9 cases in chicken in GISAID. Based on the spatial distribution of such bird species derived, their geographical hotspots can be further estimated within these typical municipality/provinces. The developed method and the findings could readily help direct the active-surveillance and control efforts [6].

12202415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12202415.value: In our future research, we plan to study not only the impacts of individual factors, such as environmental and behavioral factors, but more importantly their multi-scale dependency in the spatiotemporal modeling of disease transmission, with respect to both metapopulation- and individual-based networks. Thereafter, we plan to develop a more comprehensive framework for data-driven modeling of diffusion dynamics as well as for intervention planning. In addition, we plan to develop a novel method that will enable us to learn a spatiotemporal model of the disease transmission in situations that often involve missing or imbalanced data. Moreover, we aim to put forward an active-surveillance methodology that will allow us to proactively collect data that is most informative and useful for inferring, and hence forecasting, disease transmission risks. This methodology could be especially helpful in situations where time and resource for disease control and prevention are critically limited.

12202415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12202415.value: The geographical spread of infectious diseases has been, and will continue to be, a serious public health concern, both regionally and globally. Typical examples of these diseases include the influenza A (H5N1) outbreak in Hong Kong in 1997, the swine flu (H1N1) pandemic in 2009, the influenza A (H7N9) epidemic in Eastern China in 2013, and the present COVID-19 pandemic. Computationally, disease diffusion networks can be developed to characterize how these diseases spread from one geographic location to another. In these networks, nodes represent locations and edges represent the diffusion dynamics between the locations. From a particular disease diffusion network, we can identify underlying disease hotspots and critical diffusion paths, information that can help public health authorities to achieve active surveillance and efficient control of diseases. However, in practice, such networks are often hidden; we can observe only the locations and times or genome sequences of disease incidences. In this project, we aimed to develop and evaluate novel computational approaches to uncovering real-world disease diffusion networks. The uniqueness of this work is that it mines and incorporates informative priors from heterogeneous data sources.

12300515.label: Project Objectives
12300515.value: To develop a series of efficient numerical algorithms for some special saddle point problems, including linearly constrained convex minimization problems. To develop a series of efficient numerical algorithms for the canonical minmax problem. To develop a series of efficient numerical algorithms for some total variational minimization models that are discretized by such techniques as the finite element discretization. To prove the global convergence of and establish the worst-case convergence rate, measured by the iteration complexity, for each algorithm to be proposed. To apply the new algorithms to various modern applications to gain new insight into their modeling and algorithmic implementation.

12300515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300515.value: Saddle point problems are fundamental mathematical problems that have been widely studied in a variety of contexts. In this project, we will focus on the convex optimization context and further study the algorithmic design aspects of different saddle point problems. We will integrate several up-to-date techniques developed in the contemporary optimization literature into an algorithmic design study of these problems. A series of new algorithms will be proposed for the different saddle point problems, including such special forms as linearly constrained convex minimization problems, the canonical minmax problem, and more general problems such as variational inequalities. For each new algorithm, we will rigorously prove its convergence and estimate its worst-case convergence rate measured by the iteration complexity. We will apply these new algorithms to solve modern applications in several areas. The efficiency of the new algorithms will be verified, and insights into their modeling and algorithmic implementation will be gained through this application. Our aim is a better understanding of the algorithmic design aspect of saddle point problems. We expect the project output to strengthen the current research on this important topic. 鞍點問題是在諸多領域都廣受關注的基本數學問題。本項目將重點研究一些可以化成凸優化模型的鞍點問題，進一步考慮其算法設計問題。我們將結合一些近年來在最優化領域里發展的技術，提出一系列求解鞍點問題的算法。這其中包括諸如帶線性約束的凸最小化模型在內的特殊的鞍點問題、標準的極小極大問題、以及諸如變分不等式等更一般的問題。對於新提出的算法，我們將嚴格地證明其收斂性并估計用迭代步數來度量的最保守的收斂速度。我們也將使用這些新算法來求解一些應用領域里出現的模型從而檢驗這些算法的數值有效性，并試圖更好地理解如何對這些應用問題建立數學模型以及實施數值算法。本項目的主要目的是考慮如何更好地設計求解鞍點問題的算法。我們期望本項目的完成有助於加強有關這一重要課題的研究結果。

12300515.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300515.value: As planned, by completing the project we have developed some efficient primal-dual type algorithms for saddle point problems, optimization problems, minmax problems and some total variational minimization models that are discretized by finite element discretization. Theoretically, we have established the convergence and derived the convergence rates for the proposed algorithms, and empirically we have tested a number of applications. The research outcome includes 9 research papers on high quality journals such as Mathematics of Operations Research, and Inverse Problems; and 1 paper on the top conference NIPS.

12300515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300515.value: The research findings of this project are very encouraging for us to further consider some primal-dual type algorithms for more challenging problems such as extremely ill-conditioned models. Especially, the conditions of the involved parameters should be re-investigated in order to ensure the convergence, and the roadmap established in this project for convergence analysis is potentially useful.

12300515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300515.value: This project was focused on the algorithmic study for saddle point problems. We have particularly concentrated on the so-called primal-type algorithms for some canonical mathematical models which arise in many fields with concrete application backgrounds. We have developed some algorithms whose subproblems can be solved easily, and thus the implementation of these algorithms is generally user-friendly and efficient. Mathematically, we rigorously analyzed the convergence of these algorithms. The efficiency of these algorithms has been verified by various concrete applications. We believe that the results of this project can enhance the algorithmic understanding of saddle point problems, and inspire some new research efforts in the community.

12300815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300815.value: This study will examine rock and sediment outcrops ranging in age from the Miocene to the present (~15–0 million years) in two areas of the northern Kenya Rift Valley. These include the arid Suguta Valley and, to the southwest, the eroded Tugen Hills. Both areas contain well-exposed deposits laid down in a variety of terrestrial and aquatic environments. This investigation will focus on those deposits formed in spring systems and fresh to saline lakes. The research will pursue four major lines of investigation: 1) a study of modern hot and cold springs and their deposits in the Suguta Valley; 2) characterising modern sedimentation in permanent and ephemeral lakes in the Suguta Valley, as well as changes in water chemistry between spring and river sources and modern saline lakes of the Suguta; 3) An investigation of past environments and sediments formed in ancient fresh to saline lakes that date back several million years in both the Suguta Valley and the Tugen Hills; and 4) integrating information on ancient and modern lakes in the northern Kenya Rift in order to determine if their are any systematic changes that can be related to rifting and volcanism in an evolving rift valley. The project will explore these major aims through field studies and systematic analyses of water (modern lake waters, rivers, springs and groundwater inflows) and sediment (outcrops, short cores) samples. We will provide field descriptions of sediment sequences and return samples for geochemical, sedimentological and diatom analyses. The results of this work will allow us to characterise the modern environments and to decipher the past depositional settings in which ancient sediments accumulated. In previous studies of the southern Kenya Rift, two members of the research team have detected many changes in the types of sediment that have accumulated at different times. These changes in deposition partly reflect varying past climates, but also mirror changes in the stage of development of the rift valley. This study will allow the research team to explore if their are similar, or different, long-term variations in deposition that may reflect changes in the evolving northern Kenya Rift and its tectonic setting and volcanic environments. We will then combine models from our earlier studies in the southern Kenya Rift with new models from this investigation in order to develop a broader-based understanding of how sedimentation changes with time in an evolving rift system. 本項目將研究在北肯亞裂谷的乾旱蘇古塔河谷(Sugata Valley)及位於其西南方，已被侵蝕的圖根山(Tugen Hills)的中新世至現代(即約1,500萬年至現時)岩層及沉積物露頭。此兩個地點都有各類型陸相及水相沉積物的良好外露。本項目會針對泉水系統及淡水至鹽水湖相沉積進行研究。 本項目的四個主要研討方向：(一)研究在蘇古塔河谷的現代冷泉及暖泉水系統及其沉積物、(二)描述沉積物在蘇古塔河谷的現代常年河及間歇河的特徵，及在河谷內泉水、河流及現代鹽湖水化學特徵的變化、(三)研究過去數百萬年在蘇古塔河谷及圖根山古淡水湖及古鹽湖的沉積物及古環境、及(四)綜合北肯亞裂谷的現代湖及古湖地質特徵，推斷演化裂谷中的大陸分裂及火山運動有否為其帶來系統性的改變。 本項目將進行野外考察及系統性的水質(包括現代湖水、河流、泉水及地下水流入)及沉積物(包括露頭及短鑽芯)分析，探討上列的調查重點。研究隊伍會提供野外的沉積序列描述，以及采集地球化學、沉積學及矽藻分析的樣本，以描述當地的現代環境特徵，以及推論沉積物形成當時的古沉積環境。 研究隊伍中的兩名研究員曾在南肯亞裂谷找到大量不同時期各類型沉積物相的變化，這些變化部分反映古氣候變化，但亦同時記錄裂谷演化的不同階段。研究員可透過分析南北裂谷在長期沉積記錄中的異同，探討北肯亞裂谷在演化時大地構造及火山運動的變化。 最後，研究隊伍將整合透過本項目所取得新資料建成的新模型，以及現有南肯亞裂谷的構造模型，以對隨時間演化的沉積物相建立更廣泛的認知。

12300815.label: Realisation of objectives
12300815.value: Project delays during the first 18 months were caused by loss of a local affiliate and need for developing a new local relationship as required to obtain research permits. This with eventually done through the University of Nairobi, which also led to an MoU between Nairobi and the Hong Kong Baptist University, Geography Department. In the latter part of the project period, this also led to a new formal relationship with the National Museums of Kenya. Three excursions were carried out to the Suguta and two to the Tugen Hills with samples returned to Hong Kong for detailed sediment and water geochemical analyses. The water analyses allowed characterisation of the hydrothermal activity (Objective 1) and modern hydrochemistry (objective 2) in the basin with the latter supported by sediment sampling in the basin and saline alkaline Lake Logipi (Objective 2). Unfortunately several hydrothermal fields were less active than expected, limiting this aspect of the study to some degree. We were able, however, to carry out analyses of hydrothermal springs at Elboitong and Lake Logipi. In addition, we examined a number of meteoric springs from other parts of the basin. The hydrochemistry and brine evolution (Objective 1) were followed by sampling a number of inflowing streams to the basin for two different seasons. These were also sampled at several points along their lengths as they flowed towards hypersaline Lake Logipi, which was also sampled. Two unusual "maar" lakes (Eight and Red) were also sampled. The results have facilitated the development of a new dataset for trace elements, d13C and d18O for the waters of the Suguta Basin. Microfossil samples were also collected from Mid-Pleistocene and Holocene lake and fluvial sediments from the Suguta to facilitate environmental reconstructions (Objective 3). Samples recovered from the Tugen Hills extend from the Miocene to the present. Analyses involved diatom work, but we also succeeded in developing a high-quality pollen record, something unusual for rift valley sediments. Bulk geochemical data for major and trace elements were also obtained from a variety of fluvial and lacustrine sediments in both areas.

12300815.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300815.value: The various Suguta datasets record multiple lake expansions and contractions between about 0.5 and 1.0 Ma with diatom data indicating that water chemistries ranged from fresh to highly saline. Lake Turkana and the Suguta were connected as a single large lake between about 1–0.9 million years ago with the Suguta occupied by a single large lake during the middle Pleistocene and during the late Pleistocene-early Holocene. Hydrothermal activity related to a humid periods at 800 and 850 ka. Enhanced volcanism at around 500 ka led to the Turkana-Suguta palaeolake being divided into two separate lakes. Pollen data are still being written up, but show multiple transitions between grassland/arid floras and woodland/montane forests, reflecting expansions during wetter intervals. Geochemical analyses of the sediments (combined with additional data from previous research) show four major element groupings for the northern (and southern ) Kenya Rift deposits, reflecting 1) detrital sedimentation (K2O, Al2O3, TiO2, Fe2O3, P2O5 and MnO), 2) the accumulation of lime muds (CaO and loss on ignition), 3) the formation of silica in biogenic and hydrothermal-related deposits (diatomites, chert and opaline silica) and 4) precipitation of sodium carbonate evaporites. Trace elements also show distinct patterns in different basins, reflecting provenance of the deposits and local environmental controls. The major trace element clusters included: (i) Sr, Y, La, Ce, Nd, Sm, Eu and Tb; (ii) Cs, Rb, Ta, Hf and Zn; and (iii) Co, Cr, Cu and V. Sediment REE patterns reflect source lithologies, but depart from these patterns in spring tufas and highly saline, alkaline lake deposits. Neogene major and trace element data for the Tugen Hills (Kamego, Tambach, Ngorora, Lukeino, Chemeron and Kapthurin formations) show temporal variability with a transition from metamorphic sources through mixed metamorphic/basaltic terrains to phonolitic and basalt/trachyte lithologies. Climate factors explain many of the geochemical differences, but the contrasts in geochemistry also reflect faulting histories that led to subsidence and uplift. Temporal geochemical differences also partly reflect changing igneous activity, the movement of non-thermal meteoric and hydrothermal fluids, and the discharge of mantle CO2. Other factors explaining geochemical variability include changes in vegetation related to uplift and subsidence, as well as erosion and weathering rates. Variations in spring to runoff ratios may have significant implications for the dissolved, suspended and bedload inputs. Lakes fed mainly by spring discharge are more likely to have chemical and biochemical sediments than those fed by runoff.

12300815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300815.value: The research provides a broader understanding of rift geochemistry than has been available previously. In particular, it is helping to support another, more recent, GRF funded project on cherts in the Kenya Rift. These appear to also be formed in response to geothermal activity.

12300815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300815.value: The research has helped to enhance our understanding of how waters change as they enter into arid rift basins following evaporative concentration. It is also showing how the geochemistry of hot spring systems contrast with those in river systems, which are derived from rainfall and modified by the sediments over and through which they flow. The work has also reconstructed two environmental records from the north Kenya Rift. These include a one million year record from the Suguta Basin and a fifteen million year, intermittent, record from the Tugen Hills. Together they also enable a better understanding of the relationships between sediment geochemistry and the different stages of rift valley formation.

12301115.label: Project Objectives
12301115.value: To design, synthesize, and conduct lead optimization for a series of novel substitutionally-inert, octahedral rhodium(III) complexes as inhibitors of STAT3 dimerization. To investigate the biological properties of these novel rhodium(III) metal complexes against STAT3 in vitro and in cellulo using biochemical and biological assays. The role of STAT3 as a target in metal complex-induced cytotoxicity will be validated using STAT3 knockdown cells. After biological evaluation, the potencies of the active metal complexes against STAT3 dimerisation will be further optimized by modification of the organic ligands around the metal center. Optimization will be conducted by using a computer-aided and bioassay-guided parallel strategy that aims to furnish more efficacious metal complexes against STAT3 with each successive iteration. To evaluate the in vivo effect of the most promising metal complexes at inhibiting angiogenesis and tumor growth using a mouse xenograft model of melanoma. To build long-term relationships with other local or regional researchers with the aim of developing the candidate rhodium(III) complexes as STAT3 dimerization inhibitors for the potential treatment of skin cancer or other STAT3-related diseases.

12301115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301115.value: 信號轉導及轉錄激活蛋白 (STAT) 是一類響應於細胞因子或生長因子進而調控基因表達的轉錄因子。其中STAT3所調控的基因涵蓋細胞增殖、分化、凋亡、血管生成、新陳代謝、炎症及免疫反應等功能。而異常的STAT3活性在許多癌症的病變中得到印證，其中包括白血病、淋巴癌和皮膚癌。另外，STAT3的活性上調與某些癌症的不良預後有關。STAT3在癌症病變中的異常信號功能使其在癌症治療中成為一個相當受矚目的標靶。然而，仍未有可作為STAT3抑制劑的化合物被批准在臨床中使用。 在我們研究組的近來報道中，非取代性的八面體銠(III)化合物已被證實在STAT3二聚化直接抑制劑的開發中具有胞內外潛在抑制功能，其結構類型十分有前景。本申請的目標為探究大量（大約100個）的非取代性銠(III)化合物用以STAT3蛋白相互作用直接抑制劑的開發。金屬化合物擁有獨特的分子結構，可使其有效的適配那些不適合于純有機分子的蛋白相互作用界面中的化學空間。此外，金屬化合物合成的靈活及模塊化特性使其可通過輔助配體的修飾，輕易地調整其與STAT3中SH2結構域的相互作用，而不需要繁複的合成途徑。同時，對比于會與細胞蛋白或DNA共價結合的金屬基藥物，非動力性的金屬化合物產生不良副作用的幾率較小。 基於我們之前發表的通訊文章 (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2014, 53, 9178)，我們將使用計算機輔助及生物檢測指導的平行型方法，合理設計并合成出一系列新的銠(III)化合物。同時，為確保這些化合物對STAT3有優良的親和及選擇性，我們將在化合物中引入體積更大的芳香族輔配體，使其能夠識別在STAT3中SH2結構域的疏水性亞型口袋空間結構。這些新穎的化合物將會在不同的生物學檢測方法中經受大量的表征及驗證，從而證實它們在胞內外對抗STAT3活性的潛能。另外，通過使用STAT3敲除細胞，將驗證STAT3在金屬介導的細胞毒性測試的標靶角色。此外，計算機輔助對接分析和實驗性的結構與活性關係將被利用于交替地開發具有更好STAT3抑制作用的類似化合物。其中最具有潛力的一類化合物將被用於黑素瘤移植鼠模型的活體檢測中。我們期望銠(III)化合物可最終被開發成具有高潛力及選擇性的STAT3蛋白相互作用前導抑制劑，也期望在本研究中最具抑制作用的化合物可在皮膚癌或其他癌症的治療中發揮潛在作用。由於蛋白相互作用中無特點的大交互界面，使其通常被認為難以作為藥物標靶；同時非取代性金屬化合物在分子標靶治療中的大量使用，使得本項目的結果在科研領域具有很高的學術性，亦可能在增生性疾病的治療中取得重大突破。
