12301215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301215.value: Data in form of point patterns are often encountered in spatial statistics, e.g. locations of a certain species of plants and locations of mines. Point pattern analysis is often carried out by assuming the given pattern as a realisation of some spatial point process model, such as the Poisson process or the Strauss process, and then applying parametric methods for model fitting and testing. Some of these parametric methods are generally applicable but many are for particular classes of models only. Methods for testing goodness-of-fit therefore will be of great practical importance. In the literature the one-sample goodness-of-fit of a given point pattern is usually accessed by deviations of some empirical function from the corresponding function of the hypothesised model and its null distribution is approximated by parametric bootstrap procedure. This approach has been shown to be quite successful for stationary processes. However, for non-stationary processes, the rich flexibility in the parametric forms of such a model means that deviations of an empirical function from the corresponding one of the fitted model may have large variation, resulting in low power bootstrap tests. For two-sample problems, the only available methods require multiple replicates from each process but in applications one often has only a single replicate from each. This project aims at developing asymptotic methods mainly for testing (i) one-sample and two-sample goodness-of-fit hypotheses for non-stationary processes with single replicates and (ii) two-sample goodness-of-fit hypotheses for stationary processes with single replicates. An advantage of asymptotic methods is that the limiting null distribution of a test statistic may be model-free and sometimes is just some standard distribution such as normal or chi-squared. Thus, a fully specified fitted model is then unnecessary and the p-value is approximated by asymptotics rather than estimated by simulation. The proposal starts with mathematical derivations of the limiting distributions of a first-order statistic (which converges weakly to an integral of the difference of two Brownian motions) and a second-order statistic (which is asymptotically chi-squared) for testing whether two independent stationary samples are generated by the same model. Then, based on the mathematics for the stationary case, the proposal outlines the development of analogous statistics for non-stationary processes, in which the distinction between parametric form and nonparametric form of the one-sample goodness-of-fit hypothesis has to be made. For two non-stationary samples, in addition to the equal distribution hypothesis, the problem of testing for a common spatial trend is also briefly mentioned. 空間統計學中會經常遇到點圖案的數據，例如某種特定植物在田野中的位置或礦藏在某特定範圍内的位置便是這種數據。點圖案的統計分析經常是通過假設其為某一空間點過程模型所產生的樣本，例如由泊松過程或施特勞斯過程所產生，然後應用參數方法對模型作擬合和統計檢驗。一些參數方法可應用於所有模型，但還有許多方法只對特定類別的模型可用，因此空間點過程模型的適配度檢定在應用上是具有重大意義的。 在文獻中的單樣本點圖案的適配度一般是量度某經驗函數和在假設模型之下它的相應函數的差異。這種方法應用於平穩過程是相當成功的。然而，對於非平穩過程，參數模型的豐富靈活性意味著經驗函數與擬合模型的相應函數的差異可能有很大的標準差，從而導致統計檢驗力偏低。而對於雙樣本問題，在文獻中唯一可用的方法要求每個點過程模型的樣本有多個複製，但在現實中通常每個點過程模型的樣本只有單一個複製，因此單複製雙樣本問題需要發展出新的適配度檢定方法以配合實際的應用。 這項目旨在為點圖案的統計檢驗開發出漸近方法以應用於（一）非平穩過程的單複製單樣本和單複製雙樣本的適配度檢驗，和（二）平穩過程的單複製雙樣本的適配度檢驗。 漸近方法的優點是一個檢驗統計量的極限分佈可能是無需指定任何模型的，而其極限形式有時甚至只是一些標準的分佈，如正態分佈或卡方分佈。因此，計算p值並不需要完全指明假設的模型的參數形式，而其p值則可以由極限分佈中求取漸近值而不是通過隨機模擬作估計。 這項目的提案由推導一階統計量（弱收斂於兩個布朗運動的差的積分）和二階統計量（弱收斂於卡方統計量）的極限分佈出發，將其用於檢驗兩個獨立樣本由同一模型所產生的假設。然後，以平穩過程的數學為基礎的情況下，這項目的提案概述如何以類似的數學推導為非平穩過程發展出檢驗統計量，而在此課題下參數形式和非參數形式的適配度檢定必須要區分開來。對非平穩過程的雙樣本問題，除了相等分佈假設外，這提案亦簡要地提及如何對兩者的空間趨勢是否相等這種假設作出統計檢驗。

12301215.label: Realisation of objectives
12301215.value: The project successfully developed an asymptotic chi-squared test for the two-sample problem, namely, to test the equal distribution hypothesis for two given independent samples of stationary point patterns. This problem was motivated by the medical application that the patterns of midpoints of capillary profiles in healthy and cancerous tissues have to be compared under the constraint that there is only one realisation from each population. The PI established the asymptotic normality for the empirical second-order product density of a given point pattern at a pre-chosen lag vector, and consequently developed an asymptotic chi-squared statistic to measure the discrepancy between the empirical product densities of two given point patterns at several pre-chosen lag vectors. Simulation studies were carried out, which showed that, when comparing the same class of point processes with different parameters, the newly proposed asymptotic test was more powerful than the permutation test. The test statistic of the latter is based on the K-function, and its null distribution is the permutation distribution obtained by, ignoring expedientially the lack of exchangeability, permuting the empirical K-functions in disjoint quadrats of the observed patterns. In addition to simulated data, the two tests were also applied to the patterns of the ‘on’ and ‘off’ ganglion cells in the retina of a cat, which seem to be two independent patterns from the same kind of stationary hard-core processes, i.e. a situation that the newly proposed test is empirically much more powerful than the permutation test in the simulation studies; no significant difference in the spatial distributions of the ‘on’ cells and ‘off’ cells is detected. The project also proposed a test for one-sample problem, namely, to test whether a given point pattern is a realisation of an isotropic point process model. We proposed a new test statistic to assess the discrepancy between the uniform distribution and the empirical normalised reduced second-order moment measure of a sector of increasing central angle. Anisotropy would result in a large discrepancy. However, our simulation suggested that the limiting null distribution may depend on the underlying model, and this caused difficulty in developing mathematically a model-free test for isotropy. We overcame this difficulty by developing an algorithm to generate stochastic replicates that resemble the spatial structure of the given point pattern of a large number of points, without specifying any underlying model. Consequently, we could approximate the asymptotic p-value by using the empirical distribution of the test statistic in these stochastic replicates. We carried out an extensive simulation study. The highest powers of the asymptotic chi-squared test and our new test are close in all simulated patterns that show attraction between points with large numbers of points. However, the chi-squared test could have much lower powers if we chose bad values (within the recommended range) for its two user-chosen parameters. In contrast, our test would not be very sensitive to its sole user-chosen parameter. Moreover, comparing the two tests in terms of their empirical sizes and powers, we could conclude that our new test would be more capable of detecting anisotropy in patterns showing repulsion between points than the asymptotic chi-squared test, which seems liberal but less powerful. When applied our test to some real data, unlike the inconclusive wide-ranged p-values by the chi-squared test, we got consistently small p-values (with different values in the recommended range for the user-chosen parameter), giving a robust and convincing justification for the rejection of the isotropy hypothesis. We then considered another one-sample goodness-of-fit problem for regression models in which each point of a spatial point pattern has a real-value response. However, the inefficiency in nonparametric estimation of the curve without any dimension reduction of the spatial point pattern would make any local smoothing tests powerless. We developed a projection-based statistic which also enjoys the advantages of global smoothing, because the bandwidth of the Gaussian kernel for smoothing does not play a role in the proposed statistic, which relies on the inter-point Euclidean distances. Asymptotic properties of the proposed statistic were established. Simulation studies were carried out and showed empirically that the proposed statistic possessed the advantages of both local and global smoothing tests. However, not in all applications we could make the smoothing parameter unimportant, and the choice of its value becomes crucial for the success of the applications. We proposed data-driven approaches to choose spatially varying smoothing parameters for Gaussian kernels centred at points of a point pattern. We proved that the interpolation matrix in nonparametric curve estimation is almost surely invertible, when the smoothing parameter is an absolutely continuous random variable independent of the point pattern of the kernel centres, whose inter-centre distances are all distinct. Another approach is to introduce an extra dimension in addition to the dimensions (say d) of the point locations, so that we generate quasi-random point patterns in d+1 dimensions for the d-dimensional locations and the real-valued bandwidths of the kernels, so that nearby kernels are of distinctive shape. We applied this approach to solve PDEs, and numerical examples showed that our proposed approach yielded an efficient (small number of iterations with predictable run-time) solver that could produce cheap but accurate approximations, and it was also robust in the sense that the mean errors were small with small standard deviations among different functions and without bad runs. In spatial point pattern analysis, no matter the one-sample or two-sample problems, when asymptotic null distributions are not tractable, the p-values are often approximately by resampling. We formulated the bootstrap p-value as a Monte Carlo approximation of an integral by taking the average of the integrand values evaluated at the points of a stationary Poisson process in the unit hypercube. When the number of points are fixed, the conditional distribution of the Poisson points is independent uniform. However, the purpose of generating pseudo-random numbers is to simulate randomness, while for the numerical approximation of the integral, what is more important is whether the unit hypercube can be filled uniformly by the point set used to evaluate the integrand values. Using quasi-random methods can achieve this uniformity in space-filling better than using sets of independent pseudo-random points following the uniform distribution can. A quasi-random sequence is deterministic, but we could introduce randomness by e.g. scrambling. Randomisation can lead to improvement of the quality of the resultant point set. Moreover, for numerical examples, randomisation allows replicates so that we can get the bias and mean squared error. Our simulation study suggested empirically that the randomised quasi-Monte Carlo test often results in smaller approximation error in the estimation of the p-value and smaller deviation from the nominal level than the Monte Carlo test. What have not been fully realised in the project are the problems of non-stationary processes. The major difficulty is that all methods considered above were Euclidean distance based and hence if stationarity was not assumed, using Euclidean distances would not be valid. Nevertheless, we were still able to manage to move from distance-based to vector-based statistics that enabled us to not assume isotropy, resulting in models that are not motion-invariant. To overcome this difficulty, the PI started to explore the ideas of applying techniques in topological data analysis to avoid the use of Euclidean distances. Several approaches were formulated and submitted as a GRF proposal in November 2019.

12301215.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301215.value: Six journal articles were resulted from this project. Papers [1] and [6] proposed tests for one-sample and two-sample problems for spatial point processes. The one-sample problem considered in [1] is to test the goodness-of-fit of any isotropic model without specifying the underlying model for a given spatial point pattern. The newly proposed method outperformed the asymptotic chi-squared statistic in simulated and real data. The two-sample problem considered in [6] is to test whether two given independent patterns are realisations of the same point process model. The newly proposed asymptotic chi-squared statistic was shown to be more able than the permutation test approach in the literature to detect the difference in the underlying models when the two patterns are realisations of the same class of models with different parameters. Still considering model checking, paper [4] studies regression model and proposes an approach to bridge the local smoothing and the global smoothing tests so that the proposed kernel estimation based approach can enjoy the advantages of both the local and global tests. Papers [3] and [5] consider spatially varying smoothing parameters for kernels centred at points of a point pattern for nonparametric curve estimation and for solving PDEs. A constant smoothing parameter, which typically is the minimizer of the mean integrated squared error estimated empirically by cross-validation or obtained theoretically by considering asymptotic expressions of bias and variance, is often good enough for the estimation of smoothed curves, but variable smoothing parameters will do a better job when the curves to be estimated have complicated structures. In [3] we introduced an extra dimension in addition to the dimensions of the point locations and proposed to generate a quasi-random point pattern in the higher dimensional space to produce spatially varying smoothing parameters; numerical examples show that the proposed approach has higher efficiency and accuracy in solving PDEs. In [5] we proved the almost sure invertibility of the interpolation matrix for any point pattern for the kernel centres in nonparametric curve estimation. Paper [1] and many other tests in spatial point pattern analysis rely on bootstrap procedures. Paper [2] uses quasi-random points to approximate the bootstrap p-value. The idea is to formulate the bootstrap p-value as a numerical approximation of an integral over the unit hypercube and then generate a quasi-random point pattern in the hypercube to evaluate the integrand at these points to yield an approximate for the true p-value by spatial averaging.

12301215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301215.value: It was observed from this project and from the literature that Euclidean distance based asymptotic methods for spatial point pattern analysis typically require large samples, of order say thousands of points in a single pattern. However, exact distributions are often not mathematically tractable. Therefore, the PI was inspired to develop not further Euclidean distance based methods but new topological methods. Converting a point pattern to a simplicial complex and studying topological properties of the simplicial complex via persistent homology are the starting point of topological data analysis of a given point pattern. A graphical presentation of the persistent homology can be the persistence diagram, and in the last few years quite a number of limit theorems of persistence diagrams of different classes of point process models were established in the literature, and a few statistical methods based on the persistence diagrams were studied. The PI recently submitted a GRF proposal, outlining the ideas of developing some novel topological data analysis approach for spatial point pattern analysis.

12301215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301215.value: The project was successfully completed and resulted in six research articles. In the literature, spatial point pattern analysis is often model-based, and model-free null hypothesis such as isotropy for one-sample or equal distribution for two-sample is seldom addressed. The main obstacle is that the exact null distribution of a test statistic is typically not tractable, and a model-based approach would allow the reader to get the bootstrap p-value by Monte Carlo simulation of stochastic replicates. The beauty of asymptotic methods is that asymptotic distributions often require only mild conditions and hence are generally applicable to most point process models. In this project we studied asymptotic methods for different problems from different point of views. We successfully developed a model-free test for isotropy and compared it with the existing asymptotic chi-squared test, a new asymptotic chi-squared test for the two-sample problem, a model-checking statistic that has the advantages of local and global smoothing, a fully adaptive approach for choosing spatially varying smoothing parameters, an almost sure invertibility theorem for the interpolation matrix with random smoothing parameters, and a quasi-Monte Carlo approximation of the bootstrap p-value. The practicality of all these developments was illustrated by empirical studies of simulated and real data.

12301415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301415.value: Apple snails of the family Ampullariidae exhibit unusually diverse reproductive strategies: while some genera deposit eggs underwater, other genera deposit eggs above-the-water surface. Remarkably, the most derived taxa adopting aerial oviposition, especially Pomacea, display a wide array of egg shape and color among species. The shift from aquatic to aerial egg deposition must have been a difficult one, as evidenced by the dearth of such transitions in evolutionary history. Aerially deposited eggs of Pomacea are brightly colored and filled with nutritious polysaccharides and proteins. However, their eggs have very few predators and the embryos can develop under the strong heat and UV radiation of tropical areas. Our previous studies on the three most abundant lipoglycoprotein complexes from the egg perivitelline fluid (PVF) of the invasive snail Pomacea canaliculata have shown that they play critical roles in the embryonic development: provision of nutrients, protection from UV radiation, and unusual defenses against predation by a neurotoxin and a protease inhibitor. Using transcriptomics and proteomics, we have identified over 50 other proteins from the PVF of P. canaliculata, revealing many other potential roles for these reproductive proteins. We found that gene duplication was involved in the formation of these PVF proteins. Based on these, we propose a transcriptomic and proteomic approach to discover the PVF proteins from key basal and derived ampullariid genera/species exhibiting different traits such as egg colors and oviposition strategies, followed by a structure-function study of candidate proteins. To facilitate protein discovery, the transcriptome of each species will be sequenced and assembled, followed by proteomic analysis to identify and confirm the PVF proteins. Genes encoding PVF proteins will be cloned, and orthologs and paralogs will be analyzed to test alternative hypotheses regarding the mechanisms of their divergence. Functional characterization will then be conducted on selected PVF proteins to establish a link between their sequence divergence and acquisition of cellular function. Our specific aims are to discover the PVF proteins, identify the regions of genes and mechanisms that are responsible for the diversity of these proteins, and ultimately understand the relationship between PVF protein diversification and the contrasting egg-laying strategies of these apple snails. These results will contribute significantly to a better understanding of the evolution of proteins and protein families to facilitate the switch from underwater to aerial egg deposition, a transition that has occurred very rarely in the whole animal kingdom. 福壽螺科的動物具有多種生殖策略：有些在水下產卵，有些在水面以上產卵。其中在演化終端的福壽螺，尤其是Pomacea 的種類，具有多種卵的形狀及顏色。從水中到水面以上產卵是一個很大的生殖行為變化，胚胎必須能夠抵禦強的紫外線以及熱帶的高溫。我們前期關於P. canaliculata的工作表明它的卵週液能提供胚胎營養，保護胚胎不受紫外線破壞，並且具有用於抵抗捕食的神經毒素以及蛋白酶抑制子。本課題將研究福壽螺科卵週液的蛋白組機器相關的的轉錄組，並對若干關鍵蛋白質進行結構功能分析。該研究會增進我們對環境因子如何影響蛋白質進化的了解。

12301415.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301415.value: The family Ampullariidae includes both aquatic and amphibious apple snails. They are an emerging model for evolutionary studies due to the high diversity, ancient history, and wide geographical distribution. Insight into drivers of ampullariid evolution is hampered, however, by the lack of genomic resources. In this study, we provided transcriptome for eight species of apple snails, and genomes of four ampullariids spanning the Old World (Lanistes nyassanus) and New World (Pomacea canaliculata, P. maculata, and Marisa cornuarietis) clades. We used the these resources to support the proteomic application for identification of the egg perivilelline proteins of these snails. Based on data collected from this study, we have published nine peer-reviewed papers. Among them, Sun et al. (2019) published in Molecular Biology and Evolution (impact factor 14) is the culmination of research achievement in this study. It shows that the ampullariid genomes have conserved ancient bilaterial karyotype features and a novel Hox gene cluster rearrangement, making them valuable in comparative genomic studies. They have expanded gene families related to environmental sensing and cellulose digestion, which may have facilitated some ampullarids to become notorious invasive pests. In the amphibious Pomacea, novel acquisition of an egg neurotoxin and a protein for making the calcareous eggshell may have been key adaptations enabling their transition from underwater to terrestrial egg deposition. The publication list of this study is shown in Part C.

12301915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301915.value: Bisphenol A (BPA) is a key industrial chemical used in the manufacture of polycarbonate plastics and other products. The estrogen-like endocrine-disrupting chemical may induce persistent epigenetic changes in the developing uterus. The BPA exposure in utero is also associated with an increased risk of breast cancer in women. However, the mechanism of increasing risk of cancer from the BPA exposure is not clear. A hypothesis that BPA may enhance breast cancer risk through metabolic reprogramming has been proposed. This proposal aims to utilize our strong experience in trace analysis with mass spectrometry for investigating in vitro metabolism of BPA for the potential formation of toxic components, with particular focus on whether the metabolites of BPA could be DNA-reactive. We postulate that BPA may be oxidized to phase I metabolite with a -diOH structure and transformed to BPA-quinones, which could form covalent adducts with DNA. To test this hypothesis, BPA metabolism in rat liver slices under different incubation conditions will be investigated. Metabolite identification will be performed by using liquid chromatography (LC) and gas chromatography (GC) coupled with mass spectrometry (MS). The established metabolic pathway will be confirmed and applied in the investigation of human breast cell (MCF-7) with the comparisons to non-tumorigenic human breast cell (MCF-10A) as well as their controls. Major hydroxylated and oxidized metabolites will be isolated, purified and allowed to react with DNA for the investigation of possible formation of DNA adducts. High resolution mass spectrometry and tandem mass spectrometry as well as other analytical techniques will be applied for the characterization of DNA adducts. We believe that if DNA-adduct formation of BPA could be identified and confirmed, the outcome of this study would provide valuable information for further investigations on whether breast cancer could be attributed from DNA damage with the BPA exposure. The obtained results may also provide useful information for future investigation on BPA toxicities to animals and human.

12301915.label: Realisation of objectives
12301915.value: 1. Method development of the analysis of BPA and it derivatives in biological sample An analytical method for the simultaneous determination of six bisphenols by using UPLC-MS/MS was developed and applied for urine sample analysis. Biological sample preparation procedures for the analysis of BPA and its derivatives were established and validated. Mass spectrometric fragmentation pathways of BPA and other bisphenols were studied by using electrospray ionization Orbitrap mass spectrometry in the presence of rat liver slices. The elemental compositions of the ions were calculated from the accurate mass data. The proposed fragmentation pathways of representative compounds of BPA and BPS were verified from the analysis of isotope-labeled compounds. A chemical isotope-labeling method was developed and applied to describe the effects of BPA on the profiling of cis-diol metabolites. The influence of BPA exposure on cis-diol metabolites was investigated, by comparing different dose administration on rats. It was found that high-dose BPA exposure had strong effects on the cis-diol compound metabolism. The disturbance of the galactose metabolism by BPA is reported and this may have some implications for exploring the toxic effects of BPA exposure. 2. In vitro metabolism study of bisphenol A (BPA) and metabolite identification The proposed fragmentation pathways of representative compounds of BPA and its derivatives were verified from the analysis of isotope-labeled compounds, which provided valuable information for investigating the adsorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion of bisphenols in rat liver slices and cell lines. An UPLC/ESI‐MS/MS method for the determination of BPS and its metabolites as well as its biotransformation capacity in vivo was developed and used to assess the distribution and metabolic pathway of BPS in mice. The results showed that more than 50% of BPS was excreted through phase II metabolism in urine, with BPS‐G as the major metabolite. Due to the biological inactivity of BPS‐G and BPS‐S, rapid metabolism of BPS to BPS‐G and BPS‐S may result in reduced toxicity of BPS in vivo. The possibility of formation DNA adducts through the BPA metabolism was investigated with the identifications of phase-I and phase-II metabolites. To determine the relationship between DNA adduct formation and the genotoxic potential of BPA, the mechanism of the reactions between the reactive electophilic bisphenol A 3,4-quinone (BPAQ) with glutathione (GSH) and ribonucleosides/deoxyribonucleosides were studied. The results showed that BPAQ was capable of binding directly to the nucleophilic site of ribonucleosides/deoxyribonucleosides and GSH in vitro via a Michael addition. 3. The reaction of BPA-quinones and DNA and DNA adduct determination The hypothesis that BPA may enhance breast cancer risk through metabolic reprogramming and DNA damage was examined in vitro. Breast cancer cell MCF-7 was cultured and the cellular DNA was extracted from the cells. The adducts of bisphenol A 3,4-quinone (BPAQ) with 2′-deoxyguanosine (dG), calf thymus DNA and MCF-7 cell DNA were investigated. DNA adducts were characterized by using electrospray ionization Orbitrap high-resolution mass spectrometry and tandem mass spectrometry. The BPA-DNA adducts of BPAQ with dG, calf thymus and MCF-7 cell DNA were identified as 3-hydroxy-bisphenol A-N7-guanine (3-OH-BPA-N7Gua). The MS/MS fragmentation pathway of 3-OH-BPA-N7Gua was proposed based on obtained accurate mass data. BPA quinone metabolites can react with MCF-7 cell DNA in vitro. The findings provide evidence that BPA might covalently bind to DNA in MCF-7 cells mediated by quinone metabolites, which may increase our understanding of health risk associated with BPA exposure. The interaction of hemoglobin (Hb), human serum albumin (HSA) and cytochrome c (Cyt c) with BPAQ by using multiple spectroscopic methods was investigated. The proteins-BPAQ complex formation was confirmed with the hyperchromicity, indicating the adsorption of the biomolecules to the aromatic surface of BPAQ. From fluorescence and CD spectroscopy, it was displayed that BPAQ could strongly quench the intrinsic fluorescence of Hb/HSA/Cyt c and change their second structures with decreasing alpha helical content and increasing beta content. The evaluation of adducts from BPAQ and Hb/HSA/Cyt c might offer valuable information for future researches on BPAQ-protein adducts to give a more thorough insight to the biological implications associated with the chemical toxicological mechanisms of BPA. 4. Mass spectrometry-based method development for toxicological mechanism study of BPS and its derivatives MS-based global metabolomics method was developed and used to estimate the variation of cytokines profiling and metabolism characteristic following BPS exposure. The macrophages cells are used to explore the immunotoxic potential and mechanisms of BPS at environmentally relevant concentrations. It was demonstrated that BPS exposure induced pro-inflammatory phenotype by activating the immuno-related cytokines which include TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-6, modulating metabolic pathways which include glycolytic, GSH, sphingomyelin-ceramide. These toxicological mechanisms are providing us with a deeper understanding of the critical role of metabolites reprogramming of BPS. The effects of BPS exposure on metabolism and spatial distribution of lipids by using lipidomics analysis and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI)-mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) in mouse liver tissues. Lipid metabolites displayed significant up-regulation in phosphatidylethanolamines (PE), lysophosphatidylcholines (LPC), lysophosphatidylethanolamines (LPE) and lysophosphatidylserine (LPS) as well as remarkable down-regulation in phosphatidylcholine (PC) and phosphatidylserine (PS) in mouse liver after the exposure at 100mg BPS/kg body weight/day. The obtained results indicated that the lipidome of liver was perturbed significantly in glycerophospholipid (GP) fatty acid remodeling pathway upon the BPS exposure. To explore the cause of variation of lipid abundance, expression of enzymes that regulate biosynthesis and metabolism of fatty acid in liver tissues were analyzed. Consistent with the results of liver lipidome and spatial distribution, a decrease in hepatic expression of LPC acyltransferase 1 (LPCAT1), LPCAT2 and LPS acyltransferase and an increase expression of LPCAT3, LPCAT4, LPE acyltransferase 1 (LPEAT1), LPEAT2 and phospholipase A2 s were observed in GP fatty acid remodeling pathway. The results indicated that exposure to BPS could induce the GP fatty acid remodeling, which might be useful in toxicity evaluation for bisphenols-induced hepatic diseases. An integrated method involving lipidomics and MALDI-MS) was developed for the study of nephrotoxicity in mice exposed to 10 and 100 μg bisphenol S (BPS)/kg body weight/day. The BPS exposure remarkable perturbed abundances of 91 potential markers that mainly involved in five metabolic pathways. Significant differential signaling lipids such as sphingomyelin (SM) (d22:0/20:4), ceramide (Cer) (d18:2/24:1), and sphingosine (d18:0) related to inflammation were found to be up-regulated and colocalized in the renal cortex, medulla, and pelvis, respectively. The possible epigenetic effects of BPS that might induce in human breast cancer cell line MCF-7 were investigated. The results showed that BPS could change DNA methylation level of transposons and the methylation status in promoter of breast cancer related genes CDH1, SFN, TNFRSF10C were also changed. Gene expression profiling showed that some genes related to breast cancer progression were upregulated, including THBS4, PPARGC1A, CREB5, COL5A3. Gene ontology (GO) analysis of the differentially expressed genes revealed the significantly changes in PI3K-Akt signaling pathway and extracellular matrix, which were related to the proliferation, migration and invasion of breast cancer cells. These results illustrated that BPS exposure might play roles in the progression of breast cancer. An UPLC-MS/MS method was applied to evaluate the oxidative RNA damage induced by BPA exposure. The results demonstrated obvious dose-response relationship between some of nucleosides and doses of BPA. The levels of some modified nucleosides, including 8-oxoG, was significantly higher in high-dose group. The results indicated that a significant relationship existed between BPA exposure and RNA damage.

12301915.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301915.value: Based on the hypothesis that BPA may enhance breast cancer risk through metabolic reprogramming, this study utilized the strong experience and facility of mass spectrometry to investigate in vitro metabolism of BPA for the potential formation of toxic components, with particular focus on whether the metabolites of BPA could be DNA-reactive. BPA was found to be oxidized to phase I metabolite with a -diOH structure and transformed to BPA-quinones, and formed covalent adducts with DNA. BPA metabolism in rat liver slices under different incubation conditions was investigated. Metabolite identification was performed by using LC-MS and GC-MS. The established metabolic pathway was applied in the investigation of human breast cell (MCF-7) with the comparisons to non-tumorigenic human breast cell (MCF-10A) as well as their controls. Major hydroxylated and oxidized metabolites were isolated, purified and allowed to react with DNA for the investigation of possible formation of DNA adducts that were analyzed by using mass spectrometry. The obtained results provided valuable information for toxicological mechanism from BPA exposure.

12301915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301915.value: The protocols and methods developed for BPA from this study have been extended to the investigations on BP-derivatives including BPS and BPF. In addition to DNA adducts formation, we have also investigated other toxicological mechanism on BPA and its derivatives. Moreover, other advanced analytical techniques such as MALDI-imaging were successfully developed and applied for biomarker identification and confirmation. As an important application for further development of the research, the study outcome has also extended to human sample analysis. Exposure assessment of BPA and its derivatives in Chinese women during pregnancy was studied. Health risks using average concentrations of the chemicals in urine samples collected from 941 pregnant women over three trimesters were assessed. BPA and its derivatives were detected in more than 50% of samples, among which BPA was the predominant one. Cashiers, office workers, teachers, and salespersons had elevated urinary BPS concentrations, while healthcare workers had relatively higher BPA concentrations. The obtained results indicated the developed protocols and methods have potential for investigation of environmental pollutant-associated disease and human health.

12301915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301915.value: Bisphenol A (BPA) is a key industrial chemical used in the manufacture of polycarbonate plastics and other products. This chemical may induce persistent epigenetic changes in human. The BPA exposure is also associated with an increased risk of breast cancer in women. This study focuses on BPA metabolism and DNA adducts formation. Metabolism of BPA was obtained and applied for the investigations of cancer cell and animal models. Formation of DNA-adduct of BPA metabolites was investigated. The obtained results were used for examining whether BPA may enhance breast cancer risk through metabolic reprogramming. The results of metabolism study and DNA adduct formation may provide preliminary, but valuable information for better understanding on BPA toxicity. The developed methodologies of biological sample analysis, metabolism study and DNA reaction have been extended to other environmental pollutants. The data from this study provided important information for investigations on toxicological mechanism of BPA. The outcome will provide fundamental knowledge and technical support to studies on BPA toxicity. As BPA contamination in the environment and foods as well as human exposure has been detected in Hong Kong, this study has important significance and local benefit for protection of environment and human health.

12302415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302415.value: This project proposes to continue the PI's research on uniqueness, numerical reconstruction algorithms and invisibility cloaking for inverse acoustic and electromagnetic (EM) scattering problems. Inverse scattering problems concern the recovery of unknown/inaccessible objects by acoustic or electromagnetic wave measurements. They are of central importance to many areas of science and technology, including radar and sonar, geophysical exploration, medical imaging, non-destructive testing and remote sensing. However, there are various challenging problems in this field that are far from well understood. Our proposed studies lie in the core of research on inverse scattering problems. For uniqueness, we propose to establish the unique determination of an isotropic acoustic/EM medium by the fixed-incident-direction far-field data. The inverse problems are formally posed with such measurement data. To our best knowledge, there is no such uniqueness result in the literature. The study is based on showing the discreteness of certain acoustic and electromagnetic interior transmission eigenvalues with generic mediums. The uniqueness result would motivate some new inverse scattering modalities. For the numerical reconstruction algorithm, we propose to investigate a novel multiple-shot method, extending the single-shot method developed by the PI and his collaborators in their recent works for inverse scattering problems. The single-shot method makes use of a single far-field measurement, whereas the multiple-shot method would make use of multiple far-field measurements. The extension is highly non-trivial and the proposed method could produce fine reconstructions for some important inverse scattering problems. Particularly, we shall apply the newly developed method to the reconstruction of buried anomalies in a two-layered medium, and to the ground detection with non-flat/rough background ground. Finally, we consider the approximate invisibility cloaking for acoustic and electromagnetic waves. The transformation-optics invisibility cloaking has been widely investigated in the literature in recent years. However, the cloaking mediums obtained via the transformation-optics approach are usually anisotropic. The anisotropy causes sever difficulties for practical realization of the cloaking devices. We shall develop a general framework of constructing isotropic cloaking devices. The major idea is to investigate the so-called non-scattering potential. 在此項目中，我們主要開展關於反散射問題中的唯一性，數值重構算法以及隱形塗層的研究。反散射主要是關注用聲波或電磁波探測未知物體的研究。它是許多科學技術領域的核心課題，比如雷達和聲納，地質勘探，醫療成像，無損探測，遠程控制等。 關於唯一性的研究，我們在此課題中，會建立用固定入射方向的聲波或電磁波的遠場數據來唯一確定各向同性的非均勻介質。反散射問題在此情景下為正定的。此為一種新型的反散射方法，文獻中還無相關系統研究。我們的研究是基於對一類內特徵值問題的譜的探討來建立相應的唯一性。 關於數值重構算法，我們主要研究一類新型的基於多穩態測量數據的採樣成像方法。此方法推廣了我們之前的單穩態測量數據的採樣成像方法。相關的推廣是非平凡的，所得成像方法在若干實際情景下有重要應用。尤其，我們把所得新方法應用到重構散射體埋在多層介質的情形。 最後，我們關於基於變換光學的隱形塗層的研究，主要是考慮引進正則化近似隱形裝置，從而克服完美隱形裝置中的奇異結構。更進一步，我們通過研究所謂的“非散射”介質，來得到更具實用價值的各向同性的近似隱形裝置。

12302415.label: Realisation of objectives
12302415.value: We have successfully achieved all of the objectives of this project, which are summarised as follows. Objective 1 has been fully achieved in the following two papers: [LL17] H. Liu and X. Liu, Recovery of an embedded obstacle and its surrounding medium by formally-determined scattering data, Inverse Problems, 33 (2017), 065001. [DLL19] Y. Deng, H. Liu and X. Liu, Recovery of an embedded obstacle and the surrounding medium for Maxwell's system, Journal of Differential Equations, 267 (2019), 2192--2209. In these papers, we show that with the fixed-incident-direction far-field data, one can uniquely determine a buried obstacle as well as the surrounding medium from a general class. The uniqueness in this case is challenging to establish since the inverse problem is formally determined with such measurement data. The major strategy that we develop to tackle this challenging issue is as follows: first, we derive a certain integral representation of the wave solutions within which the unknowns are coupled together; second, by making use of the low-frequency asymptotics, we show that the unknowns can be decoupled that are implicitly involved in several integral identities; finally, by using certain harmonic analysis techniques, we could invert those integral identities and thus establish the unique determination results. It is emphasised that for the acoustic and electromagnetic cases, due to the different physical natures, we have to develop different technical ingredients in order to properly incorporate the underlying physics. In addition, we have more developments along this line and following a similar spirit, we have derived moret unique recovery results for thermo and photoacoustic tomography and brain imaging respectively: [LU15] H. Liu and G. Uhlmann, Determining both sound speed and internal source in thermo and photoacoustic tomography, Inverse Problems, 31 (2015), 105005. [DLU19] Y. Deng, H. Liu and G. Uhlmann, On an inverse boundary problem arising in brain imaging, Journal of Differential Equations, 267 (2019), 2471--2502. In [LU15], by the integral identify and low-frequency decoupling approach, we show that in a certain practical scenario, one can recover both the unknown internal source and the surrounding medium by the exterior acoustic wave measurement induced by the unknown source. This is the first result in the literature on recovering both of them. Due to its breakthrough and significance, the paper was selected into the ``Editorial Highlight of the Year 2015" by the journal Inverse Problems. Following a similar spirit, we derive certain results for the electromagnetic scattering in [DLU19], which may have important applications in brain imaging. Furthermore, we obtained some uniqueness and stability results for certain geometrical inverse problems in determining the shape of an obstacle by a minimal number of scattering measurements: [LPRX17] H. Liu, M. Petrini, L. Rondi and J. Xiao, Stable determination of sound-hard polyhedral scatterers by a minimal number of scattering measurements, Journal of Differential Equations, 262 (2017), no. 3, 1631--1670. [LRX19] H. Liu, L. Rondi and J. Xiao, Mosco convergence for H(curl) spaces, higher integrability for Maxwell's equations, and stability in direct and inverse EM scattering problems, Journal of the European Mathematical Society (JEMS), DOI:10.4171/JEMS/895 This is a well-known longstanding open problem in the inverse scattering theory. We have achieved some breakthrough results in solving this challenging issue in the polyhedral case. Objective 2 has been fully achieved and we developed several novel inverse scattering schemes by making use of multiple far-field measurements. The major idea is to develop proper imaging functionals in several practical scenarios. These results are contained in the following papers: [HLW16] G. Hu, J. Li, H. Liu and Q. Wang, A numerical study of complex reconstruction in inverse elastic scattering, Communications in Computational Physics, 19 (2016), 1265--1286. [GHHLL16] Y. Guo, D. H"romberg, G. Hu, J. Li and H. Liu, A time-domain sampling method for inverse acoustic scattering problems, Journal of Computational Physics, 314 (2016), 647--660. [LLW15] J. Li, H. Liu and Q. Wang, Fast imaging of electromagnetic scatterers by a two-stage multilevel sampling method, Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems, Series~S, 8 (2015), 547--561. Objective 3 has been completely obtained in the following papers: [LLLL15] J. Li, P. Li, H. Liu and X. Liu, Recovering multiscale buried anomalies in a two-layered medium, Inverse Problems, 31 (2015), 105006. [WGZL17] X. Wang, Y. Guo, D. Zhang and H. Liu, Fourier method for recovering acoustic sources from multi-frequency far-field data, Inverse Problems, 33 (2017), 035001. The major idea for those works is to make use of the multiple scattering measurements to properly design certain imaging functionals that can be used to identify the unknown scatterers. Furthermore, we have applied the developed reconstruction algorithms to solving some emerging engineering problems: [LWY16] H. Liu, Y. Wang and C. Yang, Mathematical design of a novel gesture-based instruction/input device using wave detection, SIAM J. Imaging Sci., 9 (2016), 822--841. [GLLW19] Y. Guo, J. Li, H. Liu and X. Wang, Two gesture-computing approaches by using electromagnetic waves, Inverse Problems and Imaging, 13 (2019), 879--901. [LLS18] J. Li, H. Liu and H. Sun, On a gesture-computing technique using electromagnetic waves, Inverse Problems and Imaging, 12 (2018), 677--696. In the above papers, we propose and develop several novel gesture instruction/input techniques in the computing technology using the inverse scattering approach. One of the key ingredients in our mathematical design is the effective and efficient reconstruction algorithms. Objective 4 has been fully achieved in the following papers: [LWZ17] H. Liu, Y. Wang and S. Zhong, Nearly non-scattering electromagnetic wave set and its application, Zeitschrift f"ur Angewandte Mathematik und Physik, 68 (2017), 68:35. [JL18] X. Ji and H. Liu, On isotropic cloaking and interior transmission eigenvalue problems, European Journal of Applied Mathematics, 29 (2018), 253--280. [LHW17] J. Li, X. Li, H. Liu and Y. Wang, Electromagnetic interior transmission eigenvalue problem for inhomogeneous media containing obstacles and its applications to near cloaking, IMA Journal of Applied Mathematics, 82 (2017), 1013--1042. In [LWZ17] and [LHW17], the non-scattering electromagnetic waves were considered based on the study of different interior eigenvalue problems in three practically interesting scenarios. The non-scattering waves are obtained by the Maxwell-Herglotz approximations to the interior eigenfunctions. Based on such a study, we develop a novel framework on approximate invisibility cloaking using regular materials. 12302415.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302415.value: The major researching findings are summarised as follows: On the theoretical aspect, we established several novel unique recovery results by making use of "optimal" measurement data including the special case with the fixed-incident-angle far-field data. In particular, we established the unique recovery results on simultaneously identifying an embedded obstacle and its surrounding medium by using the corresponding acoustic or electromagnetic wave measurement. We also considered the non-scattering potential based on the study of different interior eigenvalue problems in three practically interesting scenarios. Based on such a study, we develop a novel framework on approximate invisibility cloaking using regular isotropic materials. On the numerical aspect, based on our theoretical findings, we developed several novel inverse scattering schemes by making use of multiple far-field measurements. On the applied aspect, we applied the numerical reconstruction algorithms mentioned above to develop several novel gesture instruction/input techniques in the computing technology. We also applied the theoretical results on non-scattering potentials to the mathematical and conceptual design of a novel shadowless lamp.

12302415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302415.value: There are two potential directions for further development in our research. First, in this project, we are mainly concerned with the inverse scattering problems associated with acoustic and electromagnetic waves. It would be interesting to investigate similar inverse problems associated with elastic waves. In addition to the mathematical tools developed in this project, one would need to develop more technical ingredients in order to tackle the different physics. Second, in studying the non-scattering potentials in this project, we are led to the study of several interior transmission eigenvalue problems. In fact, the corresponding application to invisibility cloaking heavily relies on the properties of the associated transmission eigenfunctions. In the literature, the properties of the transmission eigenvalues have been intensively and extensively studied, whereas the properties of the transmission eigenfunctions have been less investigated. It would be interesting and of practical importance to investigate the intrinsic properties of transmission eigenfunctions. Indeed, in our recent study, we have been studying the geometric structures of transmission eigenfunctions, which reveal certain intriguing features that are worth of further investigations.

12302415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302415.value: In this project, we study the inverse acoustic and electromagnetic scattering problems. They are concerned with the recovery of unknown/inaccessible objects by the associated wave probing data. The inverse scattering problems lie at the heart of many areas of science and technology including radar and sonar, geophysical exploration, medical imaging and energy science. Due to their practical importance, they have received great attentions in the scientific community. In the first part of our study, we consider a novel type of measurement data in several practical scenarios. Under those measurement data, we established the sufficient conditions, under which the unknown objects can be uniquely recovered. These problems are related to the recovery by "optimal" measurement data, which is a challenging topic in the field of inverse scattering theory. Based on the theoretical findings, we develop several novel numerical reconstruction schemes, and further consider their applications to computing technology. The second part of our study is concerned with the invisibility, which is another side of the inverse scattering problems. Based on the study of several so-called interior transmission eigenvalue problems, we proposal several novel schemes of making objects invisible. Furthermore, we consider their conceptual application to shadowless lamps.

12302615.label: Project Objectives
12302615.value: The generalized likelihood ratio statistic is a profile likelihood statistic. It assumes that the error of the regression model follows a normal distribution or some special distribution. It limits its extension. Without losing the good properties of a generalized likelihood ratio statistic, and acknowledging other nonparametric testing approaches, we will suggest a way to construct a new generalized likelihood ratio test statistic that should indeed be nonparametric and robust to the different distributions of the regression errors. To avoid the bias effect in constructing generalized likelihood ratio test statistics, we must often use the second or quadratic term of the Taylor expansion of the generalized likelihood ratio for complicated statistical models. However, the quadratic test statistic is not sensitive to the local change of the regression function. We will suggest a bias reduction nonparametric regression estimate and apply it to construct the real generalized likelihood ratio test statistic. We will also apply the estimate to construct simultaneously confidence bands for the estimated functions. In practice, prior information or restrictive conditions related to nonparametric functions in the models, such as convex or monotonic conditions are available, As such, in some testing problems, the model under the null hypothesis is not a parametric form, but a nonparametric form with some restrictive conditions, or the alternative space of the model is not a large function space, but a relative small function space. For those testing problems, we will investigate if wilks' phenomenon persists for the generalized likelihood ratio test statistic and apply the results to real case studies. In practice, samples often come from different populations. Studying the properties of the generalized likelihood ratio test statistic for two, or more sample inference problems would have wide applications. This is another objective of this proposal. We will also investigate the bias effect of nonparametric estimates for these two or more sample testing problems on the generalized likelihood ratio test statistic. It is well known that the optimal bandwidth of the nonparametric estimate for testing problem is different from the optimal bandwidth for the estimation problems. We will investigate how to select an efficient bandwidth for the generalized likelihood ratio test statistic based on the power function and how to use the idea of adaptive Neyman test statistics to avoid the bandwidth selection problem for statistical inference. High-dimensional nonparametric or semiparametric models are efficient approaches to making statistical inferences for high-dimensional data without much model bias. However, it is unknown if Wilks' phenomenon remains satisfied for the generalized likelihood ratio test statistics in a high dimensional model setting. We will investigate the properties of generalized likelihood ratio test statistics in high nonparametric/semiparametric regression dimensional modeling.

12302615.label: Realisation of objectives
12302615.value: First of all, for the nonparametric regression model, we remove the normal distribution assumption for the error in the model. Then we could not apply the normal distribution likelihood ratio of residuals to construct test statistics. We proposed to apply the empirical likelihood ratio of the residuals to construct our generalized likelihood ratio test statistics. From theoretical insights, we have shown our proposed generalized likelihood ratio test statistics still keep Wilks' phenomenon, and the power rate under the local alternative is almost optimal. Primarily, it is not dependent on the distribution of the error in the model. Hence such test statistic is more robust than the classical generalized likelihood ratio test statistic for the nonparametric regression model, especially when the distribution of the error is a mixture distribution. From theoretical insight, the first objective is nearly finished. However, because of computational difficulties for the empirical likelihood, the computation of our proposed test statistic meets a problem in its implementation. The numerical results are not as good as our image. We still keep adjusting our algorithm to overcome such a problem. The bias reduction is an essential topic for nonparametric hypothesis testing. We investigate how to reduce the bias of the nonparametric regression model by local polynomial techniques. The method is relatively simple, and the effect is not so bad. Based on the bias reduction estimate, we can construct a new generalized likelihood ratio test statistics so that the power of the test is not sensitive to the bandwidth selection for the nonparametric regression model estimate. Furthermore, we suggested using the local average method to estimate the variance of the error in the nonparametric regression models. It need not to directly estimate the nonparametric regression functions. By numerical investigation, we have shown such variance estimate of the error is more robust and computational efficiency to other estimates. Such an estimate can also be applied to construct a generalized likelihood ratio test statistic without a special assumption about the distribution of the error in the model. So the second objective of this proposal is almost finished. To the third objective, we first considered the transformation regression model. By combining with rank statistics, we construct test statistics to deal with the testing problem, when the nonparametric function is constrained in the monotonic function space. We construction the likelihood ratio test statistic to test parameters and the nonparametric function in the model; the numerical results by bootstrap procedures are not bad. Though the objective is nearly finished, from the theoretical insights, the asymptotic null distribution is difficult to calculate, so does the power function under the local alternative hypothesis. Based on the difference of two nonparametric function estimates, we construct generalized likelihood ratio test statistics for two population testing problems. The performance of the test statistic is not bad, according to our numerical investigation. From theoretical insights, the bias effect of nonparametric function estimates to the test can be reduced under the null hypothesis. So the power function would be more efficient under the local alternative hypothesis. The fourth objective is also almost finished. It is well known optimal bandwidth rate for testing is relatively smaller than the optimal bandwidth for the nonparametric function estimation, We suggested to use cross-validate method to select optimal bandwidth for the generalized likelihood ratio test statistics. Because the cross-validate process is similar to the AIC, relative conservative, hence it would select small bandwidth for the nonparametric regression estimate. So, such bandwidth is more appropriate for the testing problems. However, we have not found any other suitable approach to select optimal bandwidth for the generalized likelihood ratio test statistics, including our original idea of adaptive Neyman test statistics. To high dimensional problem, we found that the bias of the nonparametric function would be accumulated to affect the effectiveness of the generalized likelihood ratio test statistic. Though we can apply our bias reduced method to estimate the nonparametric function, the computation burden is heavy. The final objective is not close to the finish and needs further investigation.

rows: The generalized likelihood ratio statistic is a profile likelihood statistic. It assumes that the error of the regression model follows a normal distribution or some special distribution. It limits its extension. Without losing the good properties of a generalized likelihood ratio statistic, and acknowledging other nonparametric testing approaches, we will suggest a way to construct a new generalized likelihood ratio test statistic that should indeed be nonparametric and robust to the different distributions of the regression errors

To avoid the bias effect in constructing generalized likelihood ratio test statistics, we must often use the second or quadratic term of the Taylor expansion of the generalized likelihood ratio for complicated statistical models. However, the quadratic test statistic is not sensitive to the local change of the regression function. We will suggest a bias reduction nonparametric regression estimate and apply it to construct the real generalized likelihood ratio test statistic. We will also apply the estimate to construct simultaneously confidence bands for the estimated functions.

In practice, prior information or restrictive conditions related to nonparametric functions in the models, such as convex or monotonic conditions are available, As such, in some testing problems, the model under the null hypothesis is not a parametric form, but a nonparametric form with some restrictive conditions, or the alternative space of the model is not a large function space, but a relative small function space. For those testing problems, we will investigate if wilks' phenomenon persists for the generalized likelihood ratio test statistic and apply the results to real case studies.

In practice, samples often come from different populations. Studying the properties of the generalized likelihood ratio test statistic for two, or more sample inference problems would have wide applications. This is another objective of this proposal. We will also investigate the bias effect of nonparametric estimates for these two or more sample testing problems on the generalized likelihood ratio test statistic.

It is well known that the optimal bandwidth of the nonparametric estimate for testing problem is different from the optimal bandwidth for the estimation problems. We will investigate how to select an efficient bandwidth for the generalized likelihood ratio test statistic based on the power function and how to use the idea of adaptive Neyman test statistics to avoid the bandwidth selection problem for statistical inference.

High-dimensional nonparametric or semiparametric models are efficient approaches to making statistical inferences for high-dimensional data without much model bias. However, it is unknown if Wilks' phenomenon remains satisfied for the generalized likelihood ratio test statistics in a high dimensional model setting. We will investigate the properties of generalized likelihood ratio test statistics in high nonparametric/semiparametric regression dimensional modeling.

12302615.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302615.value: By the numerical studies, we found that the classical likelihood ratio test statistic for the regression model is sensitive to the distribution of the error in the model, especially when the mixture regression models are considered and the number of mixture components is unknown, see Huang， Peng, and Zhang(2017), and Xu, Peng, and Huang (2018). Though by constructing the empirical likelihood ratio test statistics based on the residuals can improve the power of the test, the computation is a problem and is not easy to solve. There are more stable approaches to estimate the variance of the error in the semiparametric regression model without directly estimate the nonparametric components in the model. By using such kind variance estimate of the error for testing, the proposed generalized likelihood rato test should be more stable, see Peng, Xie, and Zhao (2018), arXiv preprint arXiv:1810.04448 and Zha, Peng and Huang (2018). The effect of bias of the estimate cannot be ignored when we construct generalized likelihood ratio test statistics for nonparametric or high nonparametric high regression models. Simultaneously testing several nonparametric functions would reduce the power of the test and increase the computational burden. Two-step estimate procedure could be a flexible approach to directly and effectively test every nonparametric function respectively. See Peng, Xie, and Zhao (2018). The concept of partial consistency can be applied to semiparametric regression to reduce the bias of modeling. The global parameters in the model can be estimated directly nearly optimally, and simplify the computation, but without directly estimate the nonparametric component efficiently. For nonparametric components can be also estimated by a two-step procedure, and avoid complex tuning parameter selection procedures to select appropriate tuning parameters for different nonparametric components. Furthermore, the asymptotic null distribution of the generalized likelihood ratio test statistic can be directly applied to make an inference, and also avoid computation burdens of those bootstrap methods. See Zhao, Peng, and Huang (2018) and Peng, Xie, and Zhao (2018). Based on the estimates of nonparametric components with different bandwidth, we could construct a simple regression model to refine and reduce the bias of the estimate of nonparametric components, but without increasing much computation.

12302615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302615.value: The Generalized likelihood ratio test for high dimensional nonparametric regression models needs further investigation. It is well known there exist biases for the nonparametric function estimates in the model. Those biases would be accumulated to affect the power of the generalized likelihood ratio test. Understanding clearly the bias effect of the nonparametric component estimate to the generalized likelihood ratio testing is very important, especially for the high or ultra-high dimensional nonparametric regression models. Then it is possible to find an appropriate approach to reduce the bias effect to the test. Though Wilk's phenomena are held for the generalized likelihood ratio testing. But it is unknown the effect of Redundancy parameters or nonparametric components to the power functions, especially when the high or ultra-high dimensional regression models are considered. When the number of redundancy parameters or nonparametric components is large, how to construct generalized likelihood ratio test statistics to keep the optimal power of the test procedure needs further investigation. Normally we have to use bootstrap procedures to approximate the null distribution of the generalized likelihood ratio test statistics. The computation burden is too heavy. The trade-off of the complexity computation and the testing efficiency is interesting topic needed further study.

12302615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302615.value: The generalized likelihood ratio test is a powerful testing procedure for testing nonlinear relationships among the statistical model. However, it is much dependent on the structure of the model and assumption about the error. In this research project, we generalized the generalized likelihood ratio by relaxing the assumption about the error and reducing the bias of the model estimation. Then the results of the generalized likelihood ratio test could be more stable and robust. It is well known that the computation of the nonparametric test procedure is very heavy, the generalized likelihood ratio test is similar. The byproduct of this research project is that we considered the trade-off between computational complexity and efficiency of testing. By the concept of partial consistency, we could split simultaneous testing problems to individual test problems and much reduce the computation burden. It provides a new approach to the nonparametric testing problems in the regression models. Furthermore, we investigated the relationship of effect of model bias and variance of the model estimates and found that we could nearly optimally estimate global parameters as model bias, especially when those biases of those nonparametric components in the model are close to zero.

12302715.value: 在數據科學，數據通常是由使用一個無向表示圖形頂點和邊緣。這裡 一個頂點表示的實體，和一個邊緣描述的兩個之間的關係實體。在許 多實際應用中,有很多的關係是從不同來源和/或不同類型的模型。例 如,研究不同的疾病基因表達數據或用戶連接在社交網絡中不同的媒 體化下的數據。在該方案中,我們感興趣的是多個圖形聚類在同一組 頂點所在的邊描述實體之間不同的關係。這種關係提供更好的理解方 式，對分類進行分析和應用。現有的方法包括變分貝葉斯估計方法, 張量計算或優化技術矩陣分解。這些技術可以是計算昂貴和/或這些方法假定一個固定的集群結構 對於所有的圖形。 這個項目中,我們要制定切實有效的解決方法的多個圖形的集群。我們的想法是構建塊拉普拉斯矩陣多圖形。主對角線塊是剛拉普拉斯矩陣的每個圖形。因為我們處理的同一組頂點，其非對角塊被設定為負單位矩陣。我們可以識別簇在每幅圖並確定一致的集群中的多個圖形。我們將證明，零特徵值的多重性所構建塊拉普拉斯矩陣等於連接的部件中的數多個圖形。所構建塊拉普拉斯矩陣的本徵向量可被計算有效地用於頂點的聚類。我們將證明徵矢量是多個圖形的鬆弛的解切割的問題。的上限和下限這種多個圖形的最優值切問題可以建立使得所提出的塊譜聚類方法的性能進行評估。此外，我們提出和制定標準化的模塊框架拉普拉斯矩陣多圖形。理論成果和標準化模塊的性能拉普拉斯矩陣將是調查和分析。 另一方面，多個圖形之間的相互關係可以使用，也就是說，在鏈路在 兩個不同的圖形兩個頂點之間的年齡。例如，在社交網絡中，用戶可以分享臉譜的圖片和用戶Instagram的圖片, 反之亦然。相互關係將發現在多個圖形簇結構非常有用。相應地，塊拉普拉斯和塊歸一化拉普拉斯矩陣可以構建自己的理論結果（零特徵的多樣性，多圖的鬆弛割問題，和它們的最佳值的上限和下限)，可以研究和分析。到最好的我們的知識，我們所提出的工作是第一次嘗試，以解決集群這種多重圖形。 在提案中，我們將使用合成和真實數據集（基因表達數據，數據公佈社交網絡數據和萬維網的數據）來測試集群和擬議塊譜聚類算法的多計算性能圖，並與其他現有的方法進行比較。通過使用這些試驗的數據集，我們將研究和評估進一步優化方法塊譜聚類使子空間的解決方案可以最大限度被關聯和簇在各圖可以是一致的優化在不同的圖形。

In research output papers [1,4,5,7], we have established theoretical results for these block Laplacian matrices and block normalized Laplacian matrices by using block matrix eigendecomposition, probability analysis and gradient flow method. In research output papers [1,2], we studies the relationship between block spectral clustering methods and multiple graphs cut problems. The clustering performance of the proposed block spectral clustering methods are also analyzed in research output papers [1,2,4]. Optimization techniques are developed and analyzed in research output papers [1,5,7] such that subspace solutions of block spectral clustering can be correlated maximally and clusters in each graph can be consistent optimally across different graphs. 12302715.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302715.value: In data science, data are often represented by using an undirected graph where vertices represent objects and edges describe a relationship between two objects. In many applications, there can be many relations arising from different sources and/or different types of models. Clustering of multiple undirected graphs over the same set of vertices can be studied. In this project, we proposed and studied block spectral clustering methods for these multiple graphs. On theoretical side, we showed that eigenvectors of the constructed block Laplacian matrix can be shown to be solutions of the relaxation of multiple graphs cut problems, and the lower and upper bounds of the optimal solutions of multiple graphs cut problems can be established. On algorithmic side, we propose block eigenvector decomposition method and gradient flow iterative algorithm to solve such multiple orthogonality constrained optimization problems. The convergence analysis is established in the project. On application side, we make use of the proposed models and algorithms for biological and chemical data sets, and also apply it to image retrieval application. The main idea is to build hypergraphs (multiple and combined graphs) and design a convergent ranking scheme to compute the association scores of images and the relevance scores of visual concepts by employing input query vectors to handle image retrieval. Numerical examples and results are shown that the proposed models and algorithms are efficient and effective compared with existing methods.

12302715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302715.value: Multidomain network classification has attracted significant attention in data integration and machine learning, which can enhance network classification or prediction performance by integrating information from different sources. In many real-world problems, each domain has its specific instance set, and one instance in one domain may correspond to multiple instances in another domain. Moreover, due to the rapid growth of data sources, different domains may not be relevant to each other, which asks for selecting domains relevant to the target/focused domain. A key challenge under this setting is how to achieve accurate prediction by integrating different data representations without losing data information. In the future work, we consider a semisupervised classification approach for a multidomain network based on label propagation, i.e., multidomain classification with domain selection, which can deal with the cross-domain information and different instance sets in domains. In particular, with sparse weight properties, the approach can automatically identify those domains relevant to our target domain by assigning them higher weights than the other irrelevant domains. This not only significantly improves a classification accuracy but also helps to obtain optimal network partition for the target domain. From the theoretical viewpoint, we equivalently decompose the core problem into two simpler subproblems with analytical solutions, which can be efficiently solved by their computational procedures.

12302715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302715.value: In this research project, we have proposed and studied a unsupervised block spectral clustering and domain association for multiple signed/unsigned graphs. We have developed new algorithms to determine the degree of association among different domains, and to achieve accurate clustering results by data integration. With consistency weights calculation, the proposed algorithms identify domains relevant to each other strongly (or weakly) by assigning them larger (or smaller) weights. This approach not only signiﬁcantly improve clustering accuracy but also understand multi-domain networks association. We expect that the proposed models and algorithms can deal with the integration of multiple data sets effectively in biological area.

12302915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302915.value: 人工甜味劑安賽蜜是天然食用糖的一種替代物質，目前已經廣泛並大量地應用於各種食品及其他可消費產品中。安賽蜜本身分子結構極其穩定，現有的污水處理工藝不能將其進行有效處理，因此安賽蜜普遍存在於環境中。基於其環境持久性並大量累積於環境中，安賽蜜已被公認為是一種不可忽視的新型污染物，目前為止，並未有對該類物質的環境規管。在諸多人工甜味劑中，安賽蜜的環境濃度最高；然而更令人擔憂的是，安賽蜜存在於飲用水源、甚至成品飲用水中，因此，對安賽蜜的研究視角應從環境污染提升至全球用水安全問題的高度。鑒於安賽蜜的環境持久性，飲用水消毒處理往往利用高強度的化學消毒工藝，如臭氧化和氯化，其可高效去除安賽蜜，去除效率分別高達60%和85%。前期的實驗資料以及報導指出，該類物質的環境降解過程極有可能會產生毒性更強的產物，由此引發對安賽蜜水消毒過程所涉及的環境健康方面日益劇增的關注。目前為止，安賽蜜氯化過程的化學降解行為以及相關的生物學影響研究仍鮮有報導。我們的初步研究結果表明，氯化過程中安賽蜜的分子結構會發生改變，其氯化產物被證實可誘發突變。因此，詮釋安賽蜜水處理過程的化學行為機制及其環境毒性顯得尤為重要。 本課題的首要目的是追蹤安賽蜜在氯化作用下的化學降解路徑，氯化處理是當今飲用水生產標準中被最為廣泛應用的水消毒技術。利用綜合化學儀器對安賽蜜的水消毒降解產物進行化學結構分析和產物鑒定，進而推導氯化誘發安賽蜜的降解機理，將為飲用水處理工程提供安全、有效的參考資料。 生物學實驗將全面評價安賽蜜水消毒降解產物對飲用水安全的影響，利用哺乳動物細胞分析手段對安賽蜜氯化產物進行急性毒性和去氧核糖核酸損傷測試，從而提供人體健康暴露相關資料。結合現有的關於安賽蜜的環境資料以及本專案關於其氯化處理的化學分析和生物學檢測結果，不僅鞏固了對安賽蜜全面風險評價的科學基礎，而且對飲用水這一重要資源的持續發展將提供更有前景的消毒處理工程參考價值。

12302915.label: Realisation of objectives
12302915.value: The stated project objectives have been completely and satisfactorily achieved. To begin with, the reactivity of ACE in free chlorine-containing water was investigated for the first time. The degradation of ACE was found to follow pseudo-first-order kinetics. The first-order rate increased with decreasing pH from 9.4 to 4.8 with estimated half-lives from 693 min to 2 min. Structural elucidation of the detected transformation products (TPs) was performed by ultra-high performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry. Integration of MS/MS fragments, isotopic pattern and exact mass allowed the characterization of up to five different TPs in the ultrapure water extracts analysed, including two proposed new chlorinated compounds reported for the first time. Unexpectedly, several known and regulated disinfection by-products (DBPs) were present in the ACE chlorinated solution. In addition, two of the six DBPs are proposed as N-DBPs. Time-course profiles of ACE and the identified by-products in tap water and wastewater samples were followed in order to simulate the actual disinfection process. Tap water did not significantly affect degradation, but wastewater did; it reacted with the ACE to produce several brominated-DBPs. A preliminary assessment of chlorinated mixtures by luminescence inhibition of Vibrio fischeri showed that these by-products were up to 1.8-fold more toxic than the parent compound. The generation of these DBPs, both regulated and not, representing enhanced toxicity, make chlorine disinfection a controversial treatment for ACE. Further efforts are urgently needed to both assess the consequences of current water treatment processes on ACE and to develop new processes that will safely treat ACE. Human health and the health of our aquatic ecosystems are at stake.

12302915.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302915.value: Being consistently detected in finished drinking water, marine seawater and effluents of wastewater treatment plants, acesulfame (ACE) has attracted much attention as an environmental emerging contaminants. During the water disinfection process, ACE will come into contact with chlorine. In the present study, the impact of chlorination on ACE transformation and the potential changes in toxicity outcome, were thoroughly studied in order to assess the potential risk of ACE chlorination to both human health and the environment. Laboratory simulation experiments revealed that ACE are degraded by chlorination. Using UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS and GC-MS, transformation products (TPs) and disinfection byproducts (DBPs) of ACE after chlorination were isolated and analyzed. Among the five TPs and six DBPs identified, two of the chlorinated TPs were firstly identified. Moreover, ACE was found to be the precursor of several regulated chlorinated-DBPs and unregulated nitrogenous-DBPs. A batch of brominated-DBPs was also detected upon ACE chlorination in wastewater, which is alarming since brominated-DBPs are reported to be more toxic than their chlorine-analogues. The molecular structures and transformation pathways were proposed. Further bacterial bioluminescence inhibition assessment revealed that the chlorinated mixture of ACE were up to 1.8-fold more toxic than the parent compound (ACE), suggesting that the generation of TPs and DBPs, whether regulated or not, cause enhance toxicity. The elucidated transformation pathway of ACE chlorination, together with the increased toxicity of the chlorinated mixture after chlorination, suggest that ACE accumulation and contamination in our precious water resources is becoming a serious problem. A solution to resolve this issue is urgently needed. A research article addressing all of the above findings was published in Water Research, 2017, 117, 157-166

12302915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302915.value: The present study provided critical information on the transformation fate of ACE upon chlorination in drinking water treatment. As observed, generated TPs were found to elicit higher toxicity than the parent artificial sweetener. Further studies on the environmental distribution, bioavailability and biological effects of the TPs must be conducted to comprehensively assess the risks/influences of these chemicals that may elicit to the environment. Moreover, the impact of chlorination to ACE also inspire relevant studies on the impact of chloramination and other chlor(am)ines based treatments to the transformation and toxicity outcome of ACE. A future study of systematic evaluating the change in role of chlor(am)ine in single chlor(am)ination, pre-UV + post-chlor(am)ination and UV/chlor(am)ination has been planned to comprehensively elucidate how the change of roles of chlor(am)ines, and the sequence of UV irradiation, will affect the transformation fate and ultimately the toxicity outcome of degrading emerging contaminants. Ultimately, these studies will help and serve as a solid foundation for developing satisfactory water treatment technique for safe removal of ACE and its TPs.

12302915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302915.value: Among different kinds of artificial sweeteners, ACE has been one of those with highest occurrence in worldwide environments due to significant input from domestic sewage. The high levels of ACE in finished drinking water has caught the attention to a potential global water crisis. From our present research data, it is revealed that ACE will be transformed in the presence of chlorine, which is commonly used for water disinfection. During the disinfection process, ACE will be transformed into a suite of TPs and DBPs. Alarmingly, according to toxicity assessment results, these products were of higher toxicity than the original artificial sweetener. These findings suggest that chlorine, originally supposed to be used to protect human health through disinfection, may produce more problems when reacting with micropollutants like ACE in our drinking water. The entire set of transformation pathway, mechanism, and toxicity data will guide future studies for a more comprehensive environmental risk assessment, and improve our water treatment techniques to safeguard both our environment and human health.
