12303115.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12303115.value: 混合多元有偏分布下的充分降维

12303115.label: Project Objectives
12303115.value: To generalize Stein Lemma to the cases with mixture skew-elliptical distributions, and to analyse in which cases, the first derivative links to the covariance between the function of the response and the predictors, and the second derivative connects to the Hessian matrix when the model has a dimension reduction structure. After establishing the generalized Stein Lemma, we then apply it to sufficient dimension reduction in regression estimation and investigate the feasibility of the ordinary least squares (OLS) in identifying the directions in the central subspace. We also suggest a method to exhaustively identify all directions in the space via an integrated matrix of all of the OLS directions. Further, when the second derivative is computed, the use of principal Hessian directions (pHd) is investigated. As the class of mixture multivariate skew-elliptical distributions contains mixture elliptical distributions, mixture elliptical distributions, skew-elliptical distributions and elliptical distributions, we then investigate the properties of the generalized Stein lemma in the various scenarios and discuss the necessary and sufficient conditions that respectively make OLS and pHd workable. We study the relevant conditional expectation and variance matrix to explore the availability of sliced inverse regression (SIR) and sliced average variance estimation (SAVE) under mixture multivariate skew-elliptical distribution distributions. In practical applications, the efficacy of the above methods in non-elliptical cases is also examined through extensive simulation studies and real data analyses.

12303115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303115.value: In inverse regression-based methodologies for sufficient dimension reduction, the ellipticity (or slightly more generally, the linearity condition) of the predictor vector, and constant conditional variance assumption are widely used conditions of which researchers however concern its restrictiveness. In this project, Stein Lemma is systematically generalized to the class of mixture multivariate skew-elliptical distributions in different scenarios and to identify and estimate the central subspace. Within this class, necessary and sufficient conditions are explored for ordinary least squares type method (OLS) and principal Hessian directions method (pHd) for identifying the central and central mean subspace. It may also provide a way to do adjustments such that the central subspace can still be identifiable when OLS and pHd fail to work. Further, we also explore the potential of sliced inverse regression (SIR) and sliced average variance estimation (SAVE) under the mixture multivariate skew-elliptical distribution scenarios. Clearly, this research project investigates some important problems in sufficient dimension reduction, and expect the new methodologies and theories developed in the course of the project will have a lasting impact in this field. 在基于逆回归的充分降维方法中，预测变量的椭球性条件（或稍微更一般地，线性性条件）以及常数条件方差的假设被广泛应用。然而这些条件比较强。在这个项目中，我们将Stein引理系统地推广到混合多元有偏分布的情况下去识别和估计中心子空间。我们讨论OLS方法和pHd方法估计中心子空间的充分必要条件，从而给出一个方法去调整OLS 和pHd使之当条件不满足时他们仍可以使用。 进一步，我们也探索在这些分布下，SIR和SAVE使用的可能性。很显然，这个项目研究充分降维的一些重要问题，并期望新的方法和理论在这个领域有一个持久的影响。

12303115.label: Realisation of objectives
12303115.value: In this research, we orignally considered 5 objectives that all are about the sufficient dimension reduction when the underlying distributions of the predictors are even not elliptically symmetric. To this end, we studied a least squres-based method, the classical pHd, and inverse regression based methods and developed their generalizations. The results have been published in statistics journal or have been invited to revise. We have also used the relevant results to investigate the robust estimation. As a summary about our contributions in sufficient dimension reduction, we also contribute a chanter to a book, which is now under review. All the objectives have been achieved.

12303515.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12303515.value: 關於 Hormander 型算子的熱核漸近展開

12303515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303515.value: Hormander 證明了一類具有“向量場之平方和”形式的算子在括號 生成的條件下是次橢圓的。這類算子包含了許多有意思的算子， 比如海森堡群及Engel群上的次拉普拉斯算子、Grushin型算子、 Baouendi-Goulaouic算子以及奇數維球面上的次拉普拉斯算子等。 這些算子很自然地出現在分析、幾何及物理等領域。 熱核是分析黎曼幾何的重要工具之一，很多幾何量可以從熱核的 漸進展開中得出。本研究計劃的目標是得出幾類非常重要的次橢 圓算子的熱核的漸近展開式。我們將首先考察有已知表達式的熱 核，這類熱核一般是由拉普拉斯型積分給出來的，我們將借助於 一些求積分漸近展開的方法，諸如平穩相位法、鞍點法等，來得 出相關熱核的漸進展開式。對於熱核未有已知表達式的算子，我 們將採用WKB逼近及擬微分算子的方法來得出其熱核的短時間 漸進展開。 得到熱核的漸進展開式以後，我們也會建立其跡的展開式，并 研究展開式中係數和算子所誘導的次黎曼幾何的幾何量之間的 關係。這些幾何量包括特征值的漸近、Hausdorff 維數、次黎曼 距離以及數量曲率。這一研究將會對次橢圓算子的指標定理的 研究提供線索。

12304215.value: 香港PM2.5中水溶性含氮有机物的化学表征和来源解析

12304215.label: Project Objectives
12304215.value: Develop and optimize the analytical methods for the characterization of water soluble NOCs using GC-MS and HPLC-MS/MS. Identify and quantify amines, amino acids, nitro-aromatic compounds and organic nitrates in 61 PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong. Investigate the seasonal variations of measured water soluble NOCs in PM2.5 and their contributions to WSON, ONHULIS and WSOC. Assess the influences of origin of air masses, aerosol acidity, meteorological conditions, and major gaseous oxidants on different groups of water soluble NOCs. Apply PMF to apportion the relative contributions of individual primary and secondary sources to WSON and ONHULIS in Hong Kong.

12304215.label: Realisation of objectives
12304215.value: 1. We have developed and optimized a GC-MS based analytical method with prior isobutyl chloroformate (IBCF) derivatization to measure the water-soluble amines in 65 PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong during a 1-yr period. Fourteen amines have been identified and quantified. A GC-MS method with prior BSTFA derivatization and HLB SPE isolation has been applied to determine the water-soluble nitro-aromatic compounds in PM2.5. A number of nitro-aromatic compounds have been identified and quantified in 110 PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong, including 29 samples collected at HKUST, Tsuen Wan, Tung Chung, and Yuen Long, and 81 samples collected at HKBU during a 2-yr period. Since I have got an opportunity to work on a set of 65 PM2.5 samples collected in Beijing through the collaboration with Peking University, nitro-aromatic compounds were also characterized in this batch of BJ samples. Therefore, a larger number of PM2.5 samples with greater diversity have been analyzed than what we originally proposed, which allows us to have a more in-depth understanding and broader view of the spatial and temporal variations, sources, and secondary formation of the nitro-aromatic compounds. Besides the individual WSON species, we’ve also measured WSOC, water-soluble total nitrogen (WSTN), water-soluble organic nitrogen (WSON), EC, OC, HULIS, major inorganic ions, and metals in these PM2.5 samples. The analytical method of water-soluble organic nitrates using HPLC-MS/MS was developed. The main water-soluble organic nitrates that we identified in Hong Kong PM2.5 samples are terpenoid nitrooxy organosulfates, which have been reported in the studies conducted at other locations worldwide, including the PRD region. Identification of “new” organic nitrate species is challenging, which depends on the new findings of smog chamber studies on the speciation and formation of organonitrates from various biogenic and aromatic precursors. This is beyond the scope of this project. As for amino acids, we’ve tried to characterize them using GC-MS with prior IBCF derivatization. Unfortunately, the student working on this project got kidney disease last year. After seeing doctors for several months and taking sick leave for a period of time, she finally dropped out. Before I can hire a RA to take over the work, social movement in Hong Kong started. Soon the lab was closed for about six months due to the intensive social movements and COVID-19 pandemic. That’s why we haven’t measured amino acids in the 65 PM2.5 samples yet. One recent paper reported that amino acids only account for 1.1% to 4.7% of WSON in Hong Kong atmosphere (Ho et al., 2018). Moreover, compared with amines that play an important role in new particle formation and production of aqueous SOA, the scientific merit of detailed speciation and quantification of amino acids in 65 PM2.5 samples may be limited. However, I am still willing to carry out this analysis as proposed in the proposal. Ho, S.S.H., Li, L., Qu, L., Cao, J., Lui, K. H., Niu, X., Lee, S.-C., Ho, K.F., 2018, Air Qualify, Atmosphere & Health, doi:s11869-018-0654-5. 2. We have investigated the temporal variations of water-soluble amines, nitro-aromatic compounds, WSON, and WSTN, and estimated the contributions of measured amines and nitro-aromatic compounds to WSON, WSOC, and HULIS under different meteorological conditions (i.e. local, long regional transport (LRT), and regional pollution days). Pearson’s R analysis was conducted to explore the relations of WSON, WSTN, amines, and nitro-aromatic compounds to selected PM2.5 components (i.e. OC, EC, WSOC, inorganic ions, chemical markers), gaseous oxidants, and environmental parameters (e.g. aerosol acidity and temperature etc.). Information on the possible sources of WSON and nitrogenous species and factors that may influence their distribution and formation in the atmosphere has been obtained. We’ve also compared the species, abundance, and sources of nitro-aromatic compounds in PM2.5 collected in Hong Kong and Beijing. 3. We have applied positive matrix factorization (PMF) to apportion the pollution sources of WSON, WSOC, amines, and nitro-aromatic compounds. Six PM2.5 sources, i.e. secondary formation, secondary nitrate (SN), biomass burning (BB), dust, vehicle emissions, and marine vessels, have been identified to contribute to WSON and WSOC. The relative contributions of individual primary and secondary sources to WSON, and WSOC have been quantitatively assessed. Secondary formation, including both SOA and secondary sulfate, is the leading contributor to WSON, followed by marine vessels, vehicle emissions, and BB. However, for individual WSON species, the source contribution is different from that of total WSON. For example, marine vessels and dust are the two major contributors to amines; secondary formation is an important source just for methylamine. To expand our understanding on WSON species, we also examined the sources of nitro-aromatic compounds in Beijing and compared the results with those obtained in Hong Kong. The source contributions to nitro-aromatic compounds in these two megacities are found to be quite different. Results obtained from this project have been presented in international aerosol conference and written up in research papers. The related publications are listed below. The first one is a poster presentation presented in the 11th Asian Aerosol Conference in 2019. The 2nd one is a manuscript draft on WSON and amines. The 3rd one is currently under preparation. Part of the results on nitro-aromatic compounds were combined with the HULIS analysis (since they share the same sample preparation and analytical method) and published in the last three papers. 12304215.label: Major findings and research outcome
12304215.value: A comprehensive characterization and source apportionment of WSON and water-soluble amines have been conducted for 65 PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong over a 1-year period. Fourteen amines have been identified and quantified using GC-MS with prior IBCF derivatization. The annual mean concentration of total amine was 51.08±23.52 ng m-3, with the highest levels observed on local days and lowest on LRT days. Of the 14 amines, dimethylamine is the most abundant, followed by methylamine, diethylamine, isobutylamine, sec-butylamine, and they accounted for 93% of total amines. WSON ranged from 0.01 to 3.85 μg N m-3, with an annual average of 1.08±0.84 μg N m-3. Similar temporal variations have been observed for WSTN, WSIN, WSON, WSOC, OC, and PM2.5. They all showed the highest levels on regional days and lowest levels on local days, which is different from that of amines. PMF has been applied to apportion the contributions of individual pollution sources to WSON, WSOC, and amines. Six PM2.5 sources, i.e. secondary formation, SN, BB, dust, vehicle emissions, and marine vessels, were identified as the contributors to both WSON and WSOC. Secondary formation, including both SOA and secondary sulfate, is the leading contributor (38.6%) to WSON, followed by marine vessels (23.0%), vehicle emissions (12.6%), BB (11.7%), and so on. However, amines, which only account for 0.7% of WSON, were found to be mainly emitted from marine vessels and dust in HK. Only a fraction of methylamine was resolved into the secondary formation source (Shen et al., 2019; Hu et al., 2020 in Part C). Six nitro-aromatic compounds (NACs) were identified and quantified in Hong Kong PM2.5 samples using GC-MS, including 4-nitrophenol (4NP), 4-nitrocatechol (4NC), 5-nitrosalicylic acid (5NSA), 2-methyl-4-nitrophenol (2M4NP), 4-methyl-5-niraocatechol (4M5NC), and 3-methyl-nitrocatechol (3M6NC). They all showed much higher concentrations on regional days (average: 7.59 μg m-3) than those on local days (2.42 μg m-3). All these six NACs were well correlated with each other, suggesting their common sources in the region, which were SOA and BB followed by industrial exhaust and marine vessels (Ma et al. 2019 and 2020 in Part C). The same six NACs were quantified in Beijing PM2.5 samples, and they showed magnitudes higher concentrations (mean: 64.21 ng m-3) than those measured in Hong Kong (4.63 ng m-3). Vehicle emissions, waste incineration and biomass burning were found to be their major sources (Ma et al. 2018 in Part C).

12304215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12304215.value: Future study will be carried out to explore the aqueous phase SOA formation from the photo-oxidation of several nitro-aromatic compounds identified in this study, with focus on the photo-enhancement/photo-bleaching properties of the formed aqSOA, characterization of aqSOA products, and the possible reaction pathways.

12304215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12304215.value: A comprehensive study on the chemical speciation, temporal variations, and sources of water-soluble organic nitrogen and nitrogenous compounds has been conducted for PM2.5 samples collected in Hong Kong. Fourteen amines have been identified and quantified, with the five most abundant amines (i.e. dimethylamine, methylamine, diethylamine, isobutylamine, and sec-butylamine) accounting for 93% of total mass of amines. The annual mean level of WSON was found to be 1.08±0.84 μg N m-3, which roughly equals to 7.56±5.47 μg m-3 of WSON matter, representing 27±16% of PM2.5 mass. Six PM2.5 sources that contribute to both WSON and WSOC were identified. Secondary formation (SOA and secondary sulfate) is the leading contributor (38.6%) to WSON, followed by marine vessels (23.0%), vehicle emissions (12.6%), biomass burning (11.7%), dust (9.7%), and secondary nitrate (4.4%). However, amines, which only account for 0.7% of WSON, were found to be mainly emitted by marine vessels and dust in HK. Six nitro-aromatic compounds were measured as well. They all showed much higher levels on regional days than those on local days, which is consistent with that of WSON. They mainly originate from SOA and biomass burning, with some contributions from industrial exhaust and marine vessels as well.

12304715.label: Project Objectives
12304715.value: To design, synthesize and characterize a series of new phosphorescent soft salts consisting of a pair of cationic and anionic metal complexes with special molecular functionalities; To study their spectroscopic, redox, thermal, structural and photophysical properties; To investigate the structure-property-function relationships of these phosphorescent soft salts; To develop novel phosphorescent soft salt based ratiometric probes and evaluate their use for ratiometric and lifetime imaging of various analytes in living cells; To develop new optical data recording, storage and security protection systems by utilizing the electrochromic luminescence properties of the soft salts.

12304715.label: Realisation of objectives
12304715.value: The PI has recruited one M.Phil. student and one postdoctoral fellow to work on the project and the student graduated in 2017. So far, the PI has secured 13 publications from this project (including 1 paper in Chem. Sci., 1 paper in Inorg. Chem., one paper in ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 1 paper in Chem. Commun., four papers in J. Mater. Chem. C, 1 paper in Dalton Trans., 1 paper in Organometallics, etc.). These researchers have received good training in several areas of modern science and technology in Hong Kong. A series of phosphorescent transition-metal complex soft salt based probes were prepared and characterized. They can be used for ratiometric and lifetime imaging of various analytes in real time in living cells such as pH and oxygen for the first time. A soft salt complex based photosensitizer was also developed for photodynamic therapy (PDT) of cancer cells. Our findings also suggest that rationally controlled excited states of the Zn(II) complexes by regulating electrostatic interaction have promising applications in various optoelectronic fields, such as light-emitting device, information recording, security protection and so on. As far as the GRF is concerned, the PI considers that he has addressed in full all the issues relevant to the objectives concerned. Since the PI has permanently moved from HKBU to PolyU in June 2018 and the project has proceeded smoothly in the past 3 years, he would like to complete the project earlier such that there is no need for him to transfer this GRF from HKBU to PolyU.

12304715.label: Major findings and research outcome
12304715.value: In contrast to traditional short-lived fluorescent probes, long-lived phosphorescent probes based on transition-metal complexes can effectively eliminate unwanted background interference by using time-resolved luminescence imaging techniques, such as photoluminescence lifetime imaging microscopy. Hence, phosphorescent probes have become one of the most attractive candidates for investigating biological events in living systems. However, most of them are based on single emission intensity changes, which are affected by a variety of intracellular environmental factors. Ratiometric measurement allows simultaneous recording of two separated wavelengths instead of measuring mere intensity changes and thus offers built-in correction for environmental effects. A soft salt based phosphorescent probe was developed for the first time for ratiometric and lifetime imaging of intracellular pH variations in real time. A pH sensitive cationic complex and a pH insensitive anionic complex are directly connected through electrostatic interaction to form a soft salt, which exhibits a ratiometric phosphorescent response to pH with two well-resolved emission peaks separated by about 150 nm (paper 1). Various phosphorescent Ir(III) and Pt(II) complexes were also synthesized and utilized in OLED applications (papers 2-9). Similar ligand systems can later be extended to other phosphorescent soft salts. Some Zn(II)-bis(terpyridine) complexes containing different anionic counterions were reported, which exhibit counterion-dependent emission colors from green-yellow to orange-red in CH2Cl2 solution. More importantly, it is found that the excited states of these Zn(II) complexes can be regulated by changing the electrostatic interaction between Zn2+ and counterions. Based on this controllable excited state, white light emission was achieved by a single molecule, and then white light-emitting device was fabricated. Moreover, a novel type of data decryption system as the optical recording medium was developed by the two-photon excitation technique (paper 10). Another Zn(II) complex containing tetraphenylethene-derived dipyrrin was synthesized and the system served as a “turn-on” fluorescent detector of Zn2+ in aqueous media (paper 11). A Zn-Ir soft salt complex based probe was also exploited for measuring oxygen content changes in living cells. This probe exhibited ratiometric photoluminescence response to different oxygen concentrations with two separated emission bands (paper 12, highlighted as a VIP). A soft salt complex based photosensitizer was developed and it exhibited enhanced singlet oxygen generation rate because of efficient energy transfer between two ionic metal complexes. Furthermore, it was successfully applied in photodynamic therapy (PDT) of cancer cells for the first time (paper 13). The work was highlighted as the inside front cover page.

12304715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12304715.value: The following areas of research work can be further developed in the future: (1) Extension of the work to other phosphorescent soft salts (based on other transition metals) with new functional properties for ratiometric and lifetime imaging of other analytes. (2) Application of external stimuli in self-assembly processes would offer greater degrees of freedom to regulate the supramolecular nanostructures and function of self-assembling molecules. In particular, the utilization of electric field to control molecular self-assembly is of fundamental significance, and it contributes to the development of applications in nanofabrication and optoelectronic fields. It would be promising to develop new classes of soft salt complexes in such self-assembly studies.

12304715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12304715.value: To date, application studies of the phosphorescent soft salts are still limited in the literature. To fill this gap, a series of new phosphorescent soft salts, consisting of a pair of cationic and anionic metal complexes with special molecular functionalities, were synthesized and characterized by various spectroscopic, electrochemical and structural techniques. The structure-property-function relationships of these soft salts were also studied. The present project has investigated the emerging applications of using soft salts as phosphorescent dual-wavelength ratiometric probes for sensing and imaging various analytes in biological systems and also as electrochromic luminescent materials for optical data recording, storage and security protection technologies. The work represents a good opportunity to gain increased knowledge in this area, to position itself to make a significant contribution to the emerging chemosensing and bioimaging technologies which should have a high impact. As a result, this research is relevant to a broad section of the health/biomedical and data recording/storage industries.

12500215.label: Project Objectives
12500215.value: To examine whether lenders charge higher interest rates for and impose more unfavorable non-price contracting terms on loans to borrowers after their board-interlocked firms announce financial restatements; To examine whether lenders’ response to interlocked firms’ restatements, if any, is conditioned upon the type of financial restatements (irregularity versus errors); To examine whether lenders’ response to interlocked firms’ restatements, if any, is conditioned upon the position of interlocked directors (i.e., chairman, CEO, audit committee chair, etc.).

12500215.label: Realisation of objectives
12500215.value: To examine the reputational penalty effect of the borrower’s director association with financial frauds on the cost of bank loan, we specify the following regression model: Loan feature = α0 +α1Post +α2Treat+ α3Post×Treat +α4Borrower-specific Control Variable + α5Loan-specific Control Variables + α6Economy-wide Control Variables + Year Indicators +Industry Indicators +ε In the above model, the dependent variable, Loan Feature, refers to one of the following features of a loan contract for a borrower: Log AIS, Log Maturity, DSecu, FinCovIdx, and GenCovIdx. Log AIS is the natural log of the drawn all-in spread plus the upfront fee and annual fee, in basis points in excess of the London Interbank Borrowing Rate (LIBOR). Log Maturity is the natural logarithm of loan maturity in months. DSecu is an indicator variable that equals one if the loan is secured with collateral, and zero otherwise. FinCovIdx and GenCovIdx are the number of financial covenants and general covenants included in a loan contract, respectively. The variable Post is an indicator variable that takes the value of one for loans borrowed in the period after fraud revelation, and zero otherwise. The variable Treat is an indicator variable that takes the value of one if the borrower shares director(s) with fraudulent firms, and zero if the borrower is a matched firm. Our test variable of interest is the interaction Post×Treat. When Log AIS or Log Maturity is the dependent variable, we estimate Equation (1) using ordinary least squares (OLS) regression; when DSecu is the dependent variable, we estimate Equation (1) using probit regression; and when FinCovIdx or GenCovIdx is the dependent variable, we estimate Equation (1) using Poisson regression. Following prior bank loan literature (e.g., Bharath, Sunder, and Sunder 2008; Graham, Li, and Qiu 2008; Huang et al. 2017), we control for a set of borrower-specific and loan-specific characteristics that are known to influence the cost of bank loans. We also include term spread and credit spread to control for macroeconomic conditions that could affect loan pricing: the variable We finally include year and industry indicators to control for the potential differences in risks and debt cost structures over years and across industries. To test the second research objective, we draw upon the literature to employ three proxies to capture the severity of financial fraud and the damage to a director’s reputation. Our first measure is fraud duration, measured as the natural logarithm of the number of fiscal years for which the financial statements were fraudulently misstated. Frauds with more accounting periods misstated indicate a potentially higher degree of corporate governance failure and more severely damage the reputation of the directors in fraud firms (Palmrose, Richardson, and Scholz 2004; Srinivasan 2005). Our second proxy is based on negative media coverage. Negative media sentiment adversely affects a firm’s contracting with bank lenders by providing incremental information and/or shaping unfavorable perceptions of various stakeholders (Bushman, Williams, and Wittenberg-Moerman 2017). Following prior literature, we obtain media news data from RavenPack News Analytics, and construct the variable Negnews, measured as the number of negative news on the fraud firm in the three months following fraud revelation. Our third proxy is Director replaced, a dummy variable indicating whether shared directors are replaced in fraud firms after fraud revelation. Prior studies imply that the replaced directors are more likely to be held accountable for fraud failure (Brochet and Srinivasan 2014; Marcel and Cowen 2014) and, in turn, suffer greater reputational damage than those who stay. We estimate the regressions by including each of the three proxies and their interaction with the variable Post, respectively, along with control variables using the sample of loans borrowed by interlocked firms. To test the third research objective, we focus on four board positions, that is, board chair, CEO, audit committee chair, and audit committee member, that are believed to wield greater influence on financial reporting issues (e.g., Srinivasan 2005; Fich and Shivdasani 2007; Chiu et al. 2013; Cai et al. 2014). Specifically, we construct three dummy variables to indicate whether the shared director is CEO/board chair (CEOChair), audit committee chair (Auditchair), and audit committee member (Auditmem) in fraud firms and interlocked borrowers, respectively. We then include these three dummies and their interactions with the variable Post in the regressions using the sample of loans borrowed by interlocked firms. Following Beneish, Marshall, and Yang (2017), we draw our sample of financial frauds from a combination of three sources: Accounting and Auditing Enforcement Releases (AAERs), the Government Accountability Office (GAO), and the Audit Analytics database. We keep only the first misconduct event if a firm has multiple frauds. Our initial fraud sample consists of 975 financial frauds from AAERs, the GAO, and the Audit Analytics database during the period 1996-2014. Next, we respectively obtain board director information for fraud firms and bankrupt firms from the Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) database (formerly RiskMetrics). We then identify interlocked firms that share a director(s) with the fraud firms in the ISS database when the financial fraud was made public. We keep only the earliest event if a firm had a board link to two or more fraud cases. We also drop directorate-interlocked firms that made misstatements filings themselves during the sample period. We manually collect detailed director information, such as board positions and directorship terms from the proxy statements filed by sample firms on the SEC EDGAR website because of the incompleteness of the information in the ISS database. We extract bank loan data from the DealScan database. Each deal has either one facility or a package of several facilities with different price and non-price terms. We consider each facility as an independent observation for our sample, since many loan characteristics and loan spreads vary across facilities. We include only bank loans initiated within three years around the fraud revelation/bankruptcy filing date. Financial data are retrieved from the Compustat database. We further exclude interlocked firms if 1) they have loans only in the period before or after the event date, 2) they have no necessary financial data available in the Compustat database, or 3) they belong to financial (SIC codes 6000-6999) or utility industries (SIC codes 4900-4999). We finally obtain a sample of 1,977 loan facilities borrowed by 456 interlocked firms whose director(s) was (were) connected with 164 financial frauds. To rule out the potential effect of time trends in loan contracting, we construct a matched sample for the difference-in-differences analyses. Following Graham, Li, and Qiu (2008), our matched sample consists of firms in the same two-digit SIC industry as a given interlocked firm and with sales within ±10% of the interlocked firm’s sales for the fiscal year prior to the fraud revelation. None of the matched firms either made a misstatement or had any director who ever sit on the board of other fraud firms during the sample period. We apply the same data restrictions to the matched firms and finally obtain 3,260 loan facilities borrowed by the matched firms for the fraud sample within three years around the event date.

12500215.label: Major findings and research outcome
12500215.value: Our analyses show the following main findings. First, lenders charge an additional increase of 8.3% in loan spreads (approximately 8.02 basis points (bps) and $0.58 million of annual interest per average loan) when the reputation of a borrower’s director has been damaged by other firms’ financial fraud, after controlling for borrower-specific, loan-specific, and economy-wide characteristics. These findings suggest that bank lenders tune upward the credit risk and/or information risk of interlocked borrowers in response to damage to the shared director’s reputation, consequently demanding a higher interest premium. Second, the adverse impact of a financial fraud on loan spreads is intensified when its damage to the interlocked director’s reputation tends to be more severe. In more detail, the effect on loan spreads is more pronounced when the financial fraud lasts for more accounting periods, the fraud firm attracts more negative media coverage in the aftermath of the fraud, and the shared director is replaced and perceived as more accountable for the fraud. Third, the increase in loan spreads is indeed larger when the shared directors hold positions of chief executive officer (CEO)/board chair, audit committee chair, and audit committee member in either troubled firms or interlocked borrowers. Our findings suggest that banks devalue those directors’ reputations to a greater degree for their presumably more direct association with financial frauds. Fourth, loans to interlocked borrowers have a significantly higher likelihood to be secured by collaterals and to include interest-decreasing performance pricing provisions and more covenant restrictions following other firms’ financial frauds. Our additional tests reveal that the adverse impact of financial frauds on loan spreads is more pronounced for the interlocked borrowers that perform poorly, are more likely to violate financial covenants, and have no investment grade credit ratings. The evidence suggests that lenders value director reputation to a greater extent when lending to borrowers with higher credit risk. Meanwhile, we find that the adverse impact is mitigated when interlocked borrowers take loans from relationship lenders or reputable banks. A working paper arising from this research project has been presented at 2017 American Accounting Association (AAA) Annual Meeting in San Diego, California, the United States, and the research seminars at Texas Christian University, Hong Kong Baptist University, Chongqing University, Shanghai University, and Central University of Finance and Economics. Currently the working paper is under the second round of review at Journal of Accounting and Economics, a top-tier journal in the accounting area.

12500215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12500215.value: In the journal review process, the referee pointed out that besides financial frauds some other failures happened to firms can damage the reputation of shared board directors and then have impact on the loan contracting terms of the interlocked borrowers. Those failures may include bankruptcy filings, covenant violations, and lawsuits for disclosure violations. Thus, the referee suggested us to examine whether banks take into account other types of corporate failure when lending to directorate-interlocked borrowers. We agree with the referee that bank lenders would be concerned with the effect of damage to the reputation of the directors of their borrowers due to significant negative events such as bankruptcy and covenant default, the two obvious failures in the debt market. When revising our working paper, we have constructed an additional sample based on bankruptcy cases from the UCLA-LoPucki Bankruptcy Research Database and conducted similar tests parallel to those for the fraud sample.

12500215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12500215.value: This research project takes advantage of corporate financial fraud as an exogenous shock to the reputation of directors with multiple directorships and examines whether banks adversely adjust loan spreads in response to the damage to director’s reputation of borrowing firms other than fraud firms. Using a sample of borrowing firms whose director’s reputation was damaged by other firm’s financial fraud, we find that the borrowers face a significantly higher increase in loan spreads after their director’s reputation was damaged by other firm’s financial fraud. The increase in loan spreads is more pronounced if the tainted director holds important financial reporting related board positions in borrowing firms and fraud firms. The adverse impact of damaged reputation of directors on loan spreads also increases with the fraud severity. Further tests show that loans tend to be secured by collateral and include more financial and general covenants after the reputation of borrower’s director was damaged by financial fraud. This study contributes to the growing literature on the impact of individual director’s characteristics on loan contracting and extend the research on the economic consequences of board directors’ involvement in negative events to private debt markets.

12500915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12500915.value: We first plan to extend the work by Bai, Liu, and Wong (2009, 2011), Leung, Ng, and Wong (2012), and others to develop a new portfolio optimization (PO) approach by applying the theory of large dimensional random matrix the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix. We expect our proposed estimate will overcome the over- and under-prediction, allocation, and risk problems in the estimation. We will develop some properties and show the superiority of our proposed estimation. We will conduct simulation and apply our estimation to the S&P data. We then plan to extend the work by Bai, Li, Liu, and Wong (2011), Bai, Li, McAleer , and Wong (2014), and others by using quantile regression to develop a new quantile-regression-based Stochastic Dominance (SD) test. We will develop some properties and show the superiority of our proposed SD test. We will conduct simulation to show the robustness of our test and apply our test to analyze the preferences between internet stocks and traditional stocks. Thereafter, we will extend the work by Chan, Clark, and Wong (2012), Guo, Post, Wong, and Zhu (2014), Huang, Tsetlin, Tzeng, and Winkler (2014), and others to develop new theory of almost SD (ASD) and generalized ASD (GASD) for risk lovers and make comparison between the theory for both risk averters and risk lovers. We then incorporate the idea from Wong and Chan (2008) and Egozcue, Fuentes García, Wong, and Zitikis (2011) to (G)ASD by developing a new (G)ASD theory for investors with S-shaped and reverse S-shaped utility functions. Last, we apply the theories and statistics we have been developed and we plan to develop in this project to some important financial issues. For example, we will study diversification of stock, bond, and other assets including gold so that we will analyze the preference of different types of investors on the portfolios with and without gold. To do so, we first apply the PO approach to construct the efficient frontiers for portfolios with and without gold. Thereafter, we construct different portfolios from each efficient frontier and employ the mean-variance and SD approaches to examine the preference of different types of investors on the portfolios. By doing so, we can investigate several issues, including: could diversification help to reduce risk? What are the preferences between more-diversified portfolios and less-diversified portfolios for different types of investors? Do portfolios in the efficient frontier outperform the equal-weighted portfolio? 首先， 通过应用大维随机矩阵协方差矩阵的特征值，我们首先计划通过Bai, Liu, 和 Wong (2009, 2011), Leung, Ng, 和 Wong (2012) 和其他作者的相关文章， 开发一个新的投资组合优化的方法。我们希望我们提出的估计可以解决过度和不足的预测、分配和估计中的风险问题。我们将扩展一些性质来体现我们提出的估计的优越性。并且我们将应用标准普尔数据来模拟和应用我们的估计。 接下来，我们计划通过延伸Bai, Li, Liu, 和 Wong (2011), Bai, Li, McAleer , 和Wong (2014)和其他相关作者的文章来发现一个新的基于随机占优（SD）检验的分位数回归理论。我们将扩展一些性质来体现我们提出的随机占优检验的优越性。 通过进行数据模拟，我们将表明我们检验的稳健性，并应用我们的检验来分析互联网股票和传统股票之间的偏好。 此後，我們將通過Chan, Clark, and Wong (2012)，Guo, Post, Wong, and Zhu (2014)，Huang, Tsetlin, Tzeng, & Winkler (2014)，和其他的研究開發新的專注於風險愛好者行為的ASD理論和廣義ASD（GASD）理論，比較風險厭惡者和風險愛好者之間的行為。然後，我們加上Wong and Chan (2008) 和Egozcue, Fuentes García, Wong, & Zitikis (2011)）的想法開發一個考慮投資者S形和反S形的功用函数新的（G）ASD理論。 最後，我們應用這些理論和方法在這個項目中研究一些重要的財務問題。例如我們將研究股票，債券和其他資產，包括黃金，我們將分析偏好不同類型的投資者面對有和沒有黃金的投資組合的行為。我們首先將採用PO的方式來構建有和沒有黃金的效率边界。此後，我們從每個效率边界構建不同的投資組合，採用均方差和SD方法來檢查不同類型的投資者對投資組合的偏好。通過這樣做，我們就可以考察幾個問題，包括：多樣化是否有助於降低風險？對於更多元化的組合和較少多樣化的組合不同類型的投資者喜好是什麼？在效率边界的投資組合有否跑贏等權重投資組合？

12500915.label: Realisation of objectives
12500915.value: We have developed a new portfolio optimization approach by applying both the theory of large dimensional random matrix and the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix to improve the estimation and obtained a paper in Li, Bai, McAleer, and Wong (2019). We have also developed a new quantile-regression-based SD test by applying the technique of quantile regression. We have developed some properties for the estimation and conducted a simulation to show the superiority of our proposed SD test and show that our proposed SD test is robust to non-iid samples. We have also applied our proposed test to analyze the performance of internet stocks and traditional stocks and make a comparison. The findings are in Ng, Wong, and Xiao (2017). We have developed the theory of almost SD (ASD) and generalized ASD (GASD) for risk lovers and make a comparison between the theory for both risk averters and risk lovers. We have also developed the theory of ASD and GASD for investors with S-shaped and reverse S-shaped utility functions. The findings are in Guo, Wong, and Zhu (2016). We have applied the theories and statistics we have developed in this project to some important financial issues. For example, we have studied diversification of stock, bond, and other assets including gold so that we will analyze the preference of different types of investors on the portfolios in the efficient frontiers with and without gold. We have also compared the performance between portfolios in the efficient frontiers and the equal-weighted portfolio. We have also applied the Mean-Variance, Mean-VaR, Mean-CVaR models for portfolio selection with background risk. We have developed a bound for ex-post sharpe ratio with application in performance measurement. The findings are in Vieito, Wong, and Zhu (2015), Zhu, Phoon, and Wong (2015), Chan, Kan, and Ma (2017), Hoang, Zhu, Xiao, and Wong (2018), and Chan, Wong and Zhu (2019).

12500915.label: Major findings and research outcome
12500915.value: A new portfolio optimization approach was developed by applying both the theory of large dimensional random matrix and the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix to improve the estimation. A new quantile-regression-based SD test was developed by applying the technique of quantile regression. We showed the superiority and robustness of our proposed SD test, and applied it to analyze the performance of internet stocks and traditional stocks. We have developed the theory of almost SD (ASD) and generalized ASD (GASD) for risk lovers and make comparison between the theory for both risk averters and risk lovers. We have also developed the theory of ASD and GASD for investors with S-shaped and reverse S-shaped utility functions. We have applied the theories and statistics we developed in this project to some important financial issues such as stocks, bonds, and other assets including gold. We have also compared the performance between portfolios in the efficient frontiers and the equal-weighted portfolio. We have developed an integer programming based strategy for Asian-style futures arbitrage over the settlement period and developed an upper bound for the ex-post Sharpe ratio with applications in performance measurement.

12500915.value: We have developed new theories on portfolio optimization, stochastic dominance test, and almost stochastic dominance. There are rooms to extend all the theories we have developed in all the above papers and we are now working on the extension.

12500915.value: We have developed new theories on portfolio optimization, stochastic dominance test, and almost stochastic dominance. We have also applied the theories and statistics that we developed in this project to some important financial issues. For example, we have studied diversification of stock, bond, and other assets including gold so that we could analyze the preference of different types of investors on the portfolios in the efficient frontiers with and without gold. We have also compared the performance between portfolios in the efficient frontiers and the equal-weighted portfolio.

12501215.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12501215.value: 逆向兩地上市後訊息環境有變化嗎?

12501215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12501215.value: With the globalization of financial markets over the past three decades, more and more firms used to choose to cross-list on other financial markets. However, cross-listing in the 2000s was not as hot as it was in the 1990s. Apart from the decline in the number of cross-listings, two trends can be observed in the global financial markets. First, many cross-listed firms choose to delist from developed markets. Second, some firms from emerging markets that were cross-listed on developed markets now choose to reverse dual-list on their emerging home markets. In the proposed research, we aim to address the phenomenon of reverse dual-listing. Normal dual-listing refers to the cases that are first listed on developed/emerging home markets, then dual-listed on developed markets. Reverse dual-listing refers to cases that are first listed on developed host markets, then dual-listed on emerging home markets. Home market refers to the market where a firm’s headquarter located, and other financial markets are regard as host markets to the firm. We will collect a sample of reverse dual-listing firms from the 42 member exchanges of the World Exchange Association. We aim to answer two questions. First, does the stock price synchronicity of these firms change after reverse dual-listing? Second, do home-market analysts make better earnings forecasts than host-market analysts, and do host-market analysts improve their forecasts after reverse dual-listing? Compared with pure home-market listed stocks, reverse dual-listed stocks should disclose more information as they must meet the higher listing and disclosure requirements of developed markets. Therefore, the reverse dual-listing setting allows us to investigate whether the increase in home-market analysts produces further firm-specific information and discover whether the information environment changes after reverse dual-listing. We expect that many cross-listed firms will either delist from the developed markets, or keep their listing status and dual-list on their home markets in the future. Therefore, with the increasing role of emerging markets in the global financial market, the findings from our project will have important implications. We will address whether analysts in emerging markets can produce more firm-specific information and improve the information environment of shares traded in host markets. By examining the long-term stock performance, we will also be able to ascertain whether such reverse dual-listing is at the cost of existing host-market shareholders. 過去三十年，隨著金融市場的全球化，越來越多公司選擇去海外市場異地上市。但是，二千年之後，公司選擇異地上市不像上世紀九十年代那麼火紅。除了異地上市公司數目下降外，全球金融市場另有兩大趨勢。第一，許多已異地上市的公司，選擇從海外發達市場退市。第二，一些已在發達市場異地上市的新興市場公司，選擇了逆向兩地上市，即回到本土市場上市。在本研究建議裡，我們想要研究的就是「逆向兩地上市」這一現象。 一般的兩地雙重上市，是指公司先在自己的市場（發達或新興市場）上市，再去另一發達市場雙重上市。逆向兩地上市，是指公司已在發達的海外市場上市，再回到本土新興市場雙重上市。本土市場指公司總部所在的國家，而其它市場則為海外市場。 我們將從世界交易所聯盟42個成員交易所裡，搜集逆向兩地上市的樣本。我們將探尋兩個問題：一，逆向兩地上市後，公司股價的協同性會否改變？二，本土市場財經分析師的盈利預測會否優處海外市場的分析師？以及逆向兩地上市後，海外市場分析師的預測會否更精準。 相對於只在本土上市的公司，逆向兩地上市的公司應會公開更多訊息，因為他們需要滿足更嚴謹的發達市場的上市和公開要求。所以，逆向兩地上市可以讓我們去研究，因為多了本土上市而多了本土分析師，究竟有否更多公司信息被發掘出來，以及訊息環境是否因此而改變。 我們預期許多異地上市的公司，會選擇從發達市場退市，或擇選擇保留在發達市場上市，但會在本土雙重上市。所以，隨著新興市場在全球金融市場的角色越來越重要，我們的研究結果將會有非常重要的應用價值。我們將會回答，究竟新興市場的分析師能否發掘公司層面的訊息，從而使發達市場交易的股票的訊息環境改善。另外，通過觀察股價的長期表現，我們也可衡量逆向兩地上市，是否以犧牲現有海外市場股東為代價。

12502815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12502815.value: 準確的經濟週期預測，對於按未來經濟狀況的預期而作出決策的 經濟個體來説，是非常重要的。到目前為止，來自經濟學家和工 業從業人員的經濟週期預測，表現並不理想。不令人滿意的預測 表現主要是由於目標變數的定義過於限制、不靈活的模式設定和 有限的數據使用。本方案旨在提高經濟衰退預測的表現。它使用 限制較少的目標變數和一個更加靈活和具有包容性的建模框架， 去同時解決以上問題。擬議的目標變數可以更好地捕捉未來的經 濟衰退和幫助經濟個體作出更好的有關決策。統一的建模框架不 但應用更靈活的模式設定，也從許多的經濟和金融變數提取豐富 的資訊，以及包含混合頻率的數據。本方案研究該擬議的模型是 否比現有的主要模型更能產生較低的預測誤差和更早預測經濟週 期的轉捩點。這些研究結果對於家庭、 企業家、 市場從業人員 和政策制定者有重要的影響。他們可以使用該模型去更好地評估 經濟展望，並因此作出及時的決定和政策。

12502815.label: Major findings and research outcome
12502815.value: This paper develops a flexible and inclusive unified modelling framework to forecast economic recessions. The unified approach improves recession forecasting performance by exploring three channels simultaneously, that is (a) one using a more flexible logit or probit model specification to capture the potential autocorrelation structure of business cycles (e.g., a dynamic mechanism can be introduced by adding the lagged recession probability function as an explanatory variable), (b) one incorporating information embedded in a large number of low-frequency (i.e., monthly or quarterly) economic and financial variables, and (c) one encompassing many relatively high-frequency (i.e., daily and weekly) economic and financial variables, whose information content has seldom been explored in recession forecasting because of data aggregation (e.g., converting weekly data into monthly data). Hence, the unified approach captures the dynamics of business cycles and exploits the predictive content of a large number of variables with mixed sampling frequencies. This paper explores simultaneously the three aforementioned channels to forecast U.S. recessions. The recession forecasting model combines an autoregressive logit specification that captures the autocorrelation of business cycles, a dynamic factor model that extracts monthly and weekly common factors from an extensive set of monthly and weekly variables, and a MIDAS regression model that incorporates common factors with mixed sampling frequencies. The proposed model is found to achieve better in-sample and out-of-sample performance in predicting U.S. recessions. Not only does our model consistently generate more accurate recession forecasts over various time horizons (from one to 12 months), but it also sets off stronger and earlier signals for the turning points of business cycles. Out-of-sample analyses indicate that the proposed model’s forecast error, as measured by quadratic probability score (QPS) or log probability score (LPS), is about 20–50% lower than that of static logit models that do not address any of the three channels. When compared with the existing models that incorporate either channel (a) or (b), the proposed model has relatively about 10⎼40% lower forecast error. Out-of-sample results further show that the model can generate strong recession signals one to four months before the onset of past recessions. Moreover, it predicts an almost-zero recession probability in the month immediately after the end of each recession period, which sends an unambiguous signal of changes in the state of the economy.

12502815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12502815.value: The proposed modelling framework can be extended and used for many forecasting applications. First, it can be applied to forecast macroeconomic variables such as GDP, inflation, and interest rate. Second, it can also be applied to forecast the likelihood of a financial crisis such as a banking crisis or a currency crisis. Third, it can be used to predict the probability of a boom or burst of asset prices like property prices and stock prices. Hence, further research can be extended based on the above-mentioned applications. The findings from these applied research outcomes are very important to decision-making of market participants and policy makers.

12502815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12502815.value: An accurate forecast of economic outlook is important for practitioners such as bankers and fund managers to make timely investment decisions and for policy makers such as central bankers to implement preemptive policies. We develop a more flexible and inclusive unified framework to forecast recessions. The modelling specification combines an autoregressive logit model capturing the autocorrelation of business cycles, a dynamic factor model encompassing many economic and financial variables, and a MIDAS approach incorporating common factors with mixed sampling frequencies. The model generates accurate forecasts for U.S. recessions with relatively small forecast errors and strong early signals for the turning points of business cycles.

12503515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12503515.value: 這個項目的目的是加強我們對於中國B2B供應鏈績效測評系統的理解和使用。在供應商公司，績效測評系統應該可以用於反映客戶重視的各個方面的績效（例如，技術、成本、質量、交付和服務）。為了學習和改善, 供應商通過評估報告, 面對面的會議, 工廠訪問, 測評形式, 電話聯絡從客戶那裏獲得顯式反饋。然而,並不是所有的大客戶都願意與供應商分享他們的績效評估，這常常導致對不同業績重視程度的不平衡。在55個電子產品供應商參與采訪的先導試驗中 (2011), 32%的電子供應商說他們最大的客戶沒有明確地與他們分享績效評估, 另有26%的供應商表示他們最大的客戶每年進行一次。 鑒於電子行業快節奏的增長和新技術的不斷開發, 以及考慮到中國政府推動企業價值鏈的形成，沒有或極少的績效反饋不利於中國供應商的發展。了解供應商如何應對客戶要求以及使用績效測評系統的成果對於中國企業現代管理系統的發展是至關重要的。 在本項目中,我們檢查最大客戶使用隱性合同機制於財務業績的影響以及供應商績效測評系統的校準。在 2010年，為了檢查和精煉采訪工具，我們進行了55個簡短的采訪。2010 - 2012年期間，我們已經對中國電子產業供應商進行了超過1000個面對面的采訪。 這個項目的資金用於購買供應商的金融數據以及中國金融數據庫提供的對於400家供應商互聯網數據的收集和分析。這些金融數據將用於測試供應商對客戶以及交易特征的不同應對的經濟結果, 例如避免貯存成本或獲得的資源部署的收益。 鑒於這個項目是對1000個中國供應商面對面的訪談研究，所以影響廣泛。項目的初步研究已經引起行業關註，獲得了美國商會(2012年11月,2012年8月), 英國商會，香港總商會(2013年6月)的邀請並進行了演講。

12503515.label: Realisation of objectives
12503515.value: Generally the objectives have been achieved with respect to the process of undertaking the research. The process parts including the literature review and the extensive data collection of archival data and subsequent analysis prove to be a great challenge. We were able to codify these processes in a detailed working paper that is undergoing second round review with an international journal (Accounting Organizations and Society). Initially, the working paper was sent to The Accounting Review and the paper was rejected after the first round of review. This paper definitely meets the first objective of understanding the properties of performance measurement systems in inter-organizational relationships. Second, another paper based on the reviewer’s comments was crafted to focus specifically on the issue of Chinese firm’s major challenges and how that affects their strategic response as well as the use of management control systems. This was especially important given the different forces of competition vis a vis foreign domestic competitors and large international customers. The result of this second article writing process has been to gain acceptance with Industrial Marketing Management. This paper speaks directly to the second and third objective of the original application. The biggest challenge faced was the slow and extensive journal review process. For example, the Accounting Organizations and Society reviews normally take 6 months and a thorough revision process takes another 6 months so the average time taken to publish the work is about 2-3 years.

12503515.label: Major findings and research outcome
12503515.value: Research Paper one: Drawing from the resource-based view of the firm, interorganizational relationship theory, and transaction cost economics, coupled with the results from our in-depth interviews, we argue that the type of supplier response strategies depends on the type of challenge faced as well as various transaction and customer characteristics. Our empirical (interview survey) study of 1004 suppliers demonstrated that these driving forces significantly affect suppliers’ strategic responses in different ways. Our study contributes to the literature on brand management in the B2B setting, by investigating how suppliers effectively tackle their biggest challenges from brand name manufacturers to gain competitive advantages. Research Paper two: In this study, we use interview survey data on 339 Chinese supplier-international customer relationships to investigate how location-specific complexity influences the use of performance measurement (output) and monitoring (behavior) control mechanisms by the major customer. The results of our regression analysis demonstrate that the average cultural distance between the customer-supplier is associated with higher levels of the use of output and behavior control mechanisms. In particular, average cultural distance is associated with the use of quality, delivery and service performance measurement, while geographical distance is associated with higher levels of the use of quality performance measurement. In addition, we find the relationship between location-specific complexity and the levels of quality and delivery performance measurement is strengthened when the supplier supplies complex components. We also find that the association between cultural distance and the use of monitoring is strengthened when the supplier has a larger capacity. Our results contribute to the international supply chain management literature.

12503515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12503515.value: Future research should endeavor to build on this and previous studies to construct a more nuanced measure of supplier innovation such as automation, advanced use of technology etc. Second, we focus on traditional approaches taken by MNCs to manage suppliers from a distance such as monitoring and system integration. Future research should examine more recent trends in which MNCs are sending their research and design teams directly to the factory to speed up product development. Research into how these practices and aim and facilitate technology transfer would be beneficial. Third, this study focuses only MNCs that are mainly located in the OECD countries which have advanced technology and management practices compared to MNCs and SMEs located in the Belt and Road economies. Future research could examine how firms from the Belt and road economies take a different path towards supply chain integration and cooperation. Future research could also build on and provide further insights into the internationalization of Chinese manufacturing firms and their role in the global economy.

12503515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12503515.value: From a practical standpoint, our results point to the need for emerging-economy firms to seek ways to innovate without relying on government infrastructure or FDI. The mindset of the manufacturing/ factory owner is key here such that a majority of factory/supplier owners seek to use their business to make money and not focus on making the best product in the world. Sustainable innovation depends on three factors, (i) mindset to make the best, (ii) opportunity costs and investing in property versus investing in new machines, and (iii) the right skillset. Analyses of interviews with managers of Chinese suppliers show that they are responding to various innovation challenges in unsustainable ways, such as controlling costs, recreating their relationships and remarketing their business to customers. The missing piece is to change the processes inside and invest in capital (automation, education and training) that will reap longer term benefits.

12600115.label: Realisation of objectives
12600115.value: The purpose of the experiment was to examine how different types of counterfactual thinking may influence the persuasiveness of the narrative that is meant to foster patients' adherence to aseptic regimen and to increase their understanding of peritonitis. To this end, we developed four animated narratives based on additive/subtractive counterfactuals and positive/negative counterfactuals as the experimental stimuli (One version of the videos: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DiRQ6L6KINk). Through the assistance from eight hospital affiliated renal patients’ self-help groups, we recruited patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD) as the participants for this experiment. However, we experienced unexpected and unprecedented challenges in the patient recruitment process. End-stage renal disease (ESRD) is a chronic, progressive, and debilitating medical condition resulting from impaired kidney function. Because the PD patients are suffering the chronic illness of end-stage renal disease and most of them are elderly (the median age of PD patients in Hong Kong is 60 years old: Ho et al., 2013), their physical health conditions were volatile. As a result, a considerable number of patients could not attend the research sessions even though we scheduled the appointments with their consent because of their deteriorated health conditions. Although we made several attempts to re-schedule the appointments, many of them were no longer capable to participate in the experiment because of hospitalization for complications. One patient who agreed to join our experiment was passed away because of sudden change in his health condition. The renal patients’ self-help groups continued to help us recruiting more patients for the study, but the completion time of recruitment has extended substantially because the availability of the patients for the study was largely restricted by their health conditions. Furthermore, the data collection process was also substantial delayed because the patients were unable to travel to the research venues at the patients’ resource centers in the hospitals, as originally planned, because they easily feel fatigue after long travelling. Because of PD patients have weak immune system and easily get infected during the influenza seasons, some patients were resultant to visit crowded public places such as hospitals. Therefore, we changed our plan to hold the study at the place where the patients found convenient. Although our study can be carried out with an iPad and a headset, we need to find venues that can be comparable to each other without any interruption to prevent any confounding influences on the study. This posed another great challenge to find appropriate venues to conduct the study. Due to the constraints of patients’ health conditions and venues, the participant recruitment and data collection processes were extended substantially from 3 months to 7 months (These two processes was planned to complete by the end of April 2016 and, in the end, these processes were completed by the end of September 2016). In addition, we did not apply for extending the project completion date because we were highly engaged in making up the lost time to recruit new patients and to collect data, and tried our best to complete the whole project within the overall project completion date. We overcame the challenges of recruitment by making individual contact with more than 350 PD patients. As originally planned, the patients’ resource centers in the hospitals provided several meeting rooms to allow us to conduct the experiment simultaneously. Given the patients’ health condition and their preference, we overcame this challenge by conducting the study more than 100 patients on one-on-one basis in different places in Hong Kong. By the end of September 2016, we have collected valid data with 136 patients. We have analyzed the data and finished writing up the manuscript by the mid-June 2017. Currently, we are doing the proofreading and polishing the manuscript. We have strong confident that we can submit the manuscript for journal review in July 2017 and for the next annual conference of the International Communication Association. We will provide the manuscript and the letter of receiving the manuscript for review from the journal (Health Communication) after submission to Research Grant Council as evidence support. Therefore, project objective 1, 2 and 7 have only achieved 80% at this moment because of the challenges in the processes of patient recruitment and data collection. However, the objectives 3 to 6 have achieved 100%. We conducted one focus group research and a survey as the groundwork developed the content of the animated narratives (i.e., experimental stimuli) (See “Other impact” section for further details). Based on the findings of this experiment, we selected one of the four animated narratives to produce DVDs to distribute to the renal patients’ self-help groups for health education. This health promotional animated narrative is based on the empirical evidence (project objectives 3 and 4). Furthermore, this persuasive health narrative in the form of DVD helped the renal patients’ self-help groups to enhance PD patients’ understanding of peritonitis and change their attitude toward aseptic regimen (objectives 5 and 6) (See “Other impact” section for further details). To sum up, in this 9-month project, we faced with unexpected and unprecedented challenges that were out of our control. However, we have overcome the challenges and are going to submit the manuscript in July 2017. Therefore, Project objectives 3 to 6 have fully achieved. Project objectives 1, 2, and 7 have under-achieved at this moment.

12600115.label: Major findings and research outcome
12600115.value: The structural equation modeling was used to examine the hypothesized path model. The measurement model indicated that the data achieved a good fit, CFI = 1.0, SRMR = 0.05, RMSEA = 0.00 (90% CI: .00, .07), χ2 (24, N = 134) = 22.63, p = 0.54, and the structural model achieved a good fit, CFI = .96, RMSEA = 0.05 (90% CI: .01, .08), χ2 (55, N = 134) = 74.30, χ2 /df = 1.35, p = .04, SRMR = 0.06. The findings showed that significant interaction effects on anticipated regret (β= -.42, p < .05) and counterfactual simulation (β= -.29, p < .05) were observed. In the negative condition, additive counterfactuals (M = 5.06) induced greater level of anticipated regret than subtractive counterfactuals (M = 3.88), F(1, 132) = 10.42, p < .01. Additive counterfactuals (M = 5.20) also induced greater level of mental simulation than subtractive counterfactuals (M = 4.13), F(1, 132) = 5.13, p < .05. In the positive condition, subtractive counterfactuals (M = 4.45) induced slight higher level of anticipated regret than additive counterfactuals (M = 4.14), F(1, 132) = .66, p =.42. Subtractive counterfactuals (M = 5.02) induced slight higher level of mental simulation than additive counterfactuals (M = 4.14), F(1, 132) = .66, p =.42. Anticipated regret was positive related to attitude toward adherence to aseptic regimen (β= .28, p < .05) and intention to adhere to aseptic regimen (β= .29, p < .05). Mental simulation was also positively related to anticipated regret (β= .22, p < .05), but it was not significantly related to behavioral intention (β = .03, n.s.). The mediation analyses showed that mental simulation influenced adherence intention via the two indirect paths from anticipated regret and attitude toward the aseptic regimen (β = .09, p < .05). Finally, attitude toward adherence to aseptic regimen and intention to adhere to aseptic regimen are positively related (β= .48, p < .001). These findings suggest that patients who are exposed to narratives with additive-negative counterfactuals are more likely to experience greater level of anticipated regret and mental simulation, leading to more positive attitude and higher intention to adhere to aseptic regimen. This study advanced our theoretical understanding on the process of how narratives with counterfactuals influence the audience’s behavioral intention. This study also offered some practical implications to health communicators when designing narratives to persuade patients’ adherence to treatment regimen.

12600115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12600115.value: This study provided empirical evidence to show that narratives accompanied with counterfactuals have significant influence on the audience’s emotions, cognition, and behavioral intention. Future research can examine whether narratives accompanied with counterfactuals may foster individuals’ confident to perform advocated healthy behavior. Furthermore, this study showed that the effect of narratives with different types of counterfactuals are varied. Therefore, future research can investigate upward/downward counterfactuals. To better understand the psychological mechanism, future research can examine what type of people are more susceptible to narratives with counterfactuals using different health issues. In addition to research development, health communicators and officials can use our animated narratives to develop health interventions or communication campaigns to promote patients’ adherence to aseptic regimen.

12600115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12600115.value: Peritoneal dialysis is the first line treatment of patients with the end-stage renal disease in Hong Kong. Such treatment is associated with great responsibilities and demands on the patients because it involves multifaceted regimens. Failure to do so can potentially cause infectious complications. Peritonitis is the most frequent bacterial infectious complication and is accounted for about 20% of infection-related mortality in Hong Kong. Research has shown that suboptimal adherence to aseptic regimen is an important risk factor of peritonitis. To improve patients’ adherence to aseptic regimen, this experimental study examined the process of how narratives accompanied with counterfactual thinking influence patients’ attitude and intention to adhere aseptic regimen. The results showed that patients who are exposed to narratives with additive/negative counterfactual thoughts are likely to trigger higher levels of anticipated regret and mental simulation, leading to more positive attitude and higher intention to adhere to aseptic regimen. This study advanced our theoretical understanding of the underlying process of narrative persuasion. It also provided practical implication to health communicators and officials to how to design narratives with counterfactual thinking to enhance the message persuasiveness for promoting treatment regimen adherence.

12601115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12601115.value: 這項研究旨在檢視香港青少年的休閒生活體驗，來建立一套休閒自我探索的本土化實質理論。相較其他生活領域，休閒較少受到社會及他人制約，故此被視為青少年發展的重要範疇。青少年自我成長十分重要；年青人需要足夠空間作自我探索和自我認定。不少青少年認真專注參與休閒活動，相較短期以享樂為主的隨意參與，認真休閒活動提供了機會讓參與者獲得知識和技能、表現實踐自我、及提升自我和群組認同。認真休閒活動的好處曾多番在研究中得到確認，但這些研究多以成年參與者為對象。這項研究檢視及比對青少年參與認真休閒和隨意休閒活動，藉此了解自我探索的呈現，希望就此對青少年成長作出啓示。這項在香港進行的研究會把現行青少年休閒學術的理論及研究帶到西方社會以外的文化地域。過往本地青少年休閒研究多關注活動種類、滿意程度及參與態度，甚少觸及休閒作為全人發展的重要環節，亦較少探討休閒體驗對自主、自我成長的重要性。這項研究試圖理解香港青少年的休閒參與感受和意念整構，由此延伸去勾畫有利成長的要素。研究採用現象學方法，與五十名高中學生進行深入訪談，當中認真及隨意參與者各佔一半。選取樣本的程序，包括從香港九所不同學術階別的中學邀請共945名學生進行認真休閒問卷(SLIM)訪查。這項研究有助增進對青少年在休閒體驗中自我探索的理解，亦為學界在促進全人成長和拓展青少年休閒教育活動帶來啟示。
