To determine how identity negotiation is influenced by gender and socioeconomic status while at the same time, capture the complex and shifting nature of identity construction through a mixed methods approach.
To overcome Eurocentric bias and contribute to a contextualized account that highlights the fluid and contradictory nature of (homo)sexual identity construction in China.

12605615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12605615.value: China’s market reform and opening up have resulted in the increased visibility of sexual minorities and enabled them to connect with each other. Discourses of sexual rights and coming out have begun to serve as the building blocks for the construction of sexual identities. While optimism has been expressed over China’s long march to sexual freedom, one must not overlook the intense family pressure faced by the one-child generation. Without siblings to share the burden of parental expectations, they face unprecedented pressure to marry and have a child. Some sexual minorities enter a conventional marriage and establish a heterosexual identity. Others, on the contrary, may pursue an independent sexual identity and lifestyle. There are still others who opt for a cooperative marriage where gays and lesbians marry each other so that they can carve out space for same-sex relationships. This research examines the various ways that Chinese sexual minorities cope with marriage pressure and its impact on identity construction. The work emphasizes that while the discourse of coming out and stabilization of sexual identity has been globally circulated as a dominant model of homosexual identity formation, the experiences of Chinese sexual minorities cast doubt on the universality of such a model. Chinese individuals are subject to the imperative of heterosexual marriage, and hence their sexual identity entails a more hybrid, contradictory and fluid character. We must recognize that sexual minorities in China are heterogeneous rather than homogenous. Men and women can experience marriage pressure in rather different ways. Sons bear the responsibility of having children and carrying on the family bloodline. Daughters experience a relatively disadvantaged position in the job market and may find it difficult to gain financial independence outside marriage. Differences can also be found among men and women rather than between them. This research will examine how Chinese LGB from different social locations experience and cope with marriage pressure. What resources, networks, and discourses do people of different genders and socioeconomic statuses utilize in their negotiations of marriage and sexual identity? Informed by the concept of intersectionality, the understanding in this research is that identities such as sexual orientation, gender and class, are interconnected. An exclusive focus on sexual identity may lead to oversight of the relative privileges, power and opportunities that people can enjoy due to other social identities. This research will utilize a mixed methods approach to capture the qualitative differences among different intersectional positions.

12605615.label: Realisation of objectives
12605615.value: Objective 1: Existing literature has revealed the intense pressure faced by the sexual minorities in China in relation to the imperative of heterosexual marriage. This research contributes to a better understanding of the marriage imperative by focusing on both the symbolic and material aspects, such as the traditional values of filial piety, the culture of face, the materials aspects of care for parents, and the economic costs and benefits of marriage. We have examined the different implications of the marriage institution for sexual minorities of different genders and socioeconomic statuses, as well as their diverse ways of coping with the marriage pressure. The objective has been largely achieved. A major limitation is that since the respondents were mainly recruited through LGB organizations in China, those who would enter or have entered traditional heterosexual marriage tended not to participate in the LGB organizations and thus were underrepresented. Objective 2: A mixed method which combines qualitative and quantitative analyses offers a nuanced account of how identity negotiation is influenced by gender and socioeconomic status. Altogether 1,434 responses were received for the online questionnaire survey and 60 in-depth interviews were conducted. Since some partner organizations provide HIV prevention service for the gay community, we were able to recruit male respondents with diverse socioeconomic backgrounds. However, there was an over-representation of highly educated, high income female urbanites because our partner lesbian organizations mainly work for gender equality. We tried to reach out to the grassroots lesbian community by participating in the activities of an NGO in Shenzhen. Due to the limitations of the sample, we would avoid generalize the findings to the entire LGB population in China. The objective has been largely achieved. Objective 3: This research raises questions regarding the global applicability of the linear progressive model of homosexual identity formation. We use the LGB identity scale developed by Mohr and Kendra (2011) in the questionnaire survey to capture the extent to which sexual minorities in China embrace sexual identity and develop a sense of pride. At the same time, the qualitative data on the identity constructions in different life contexts such as family, school, workplace, and LGB community shed light on the contradictory and fluid character of sexual identification in China. A comparison of the two sets of quantitative and qualitative data enables reflection on the applicability of the out-and-proud model in a family-centered, collectivist society. The objective has been achieved

12605615.label: Major findings and research outcome
12605615.value: Based on the questionnaire survey, an article has been written for publication in a peer-reviewed, international journal. The paper examines gender differences in the identity concerns of sexual minorities in China and the impact of individual and community-level socioeconomic statuses, familial, and cultural factors. The findings show that gender impacts identity concerns. Men indicated a higher level of identity concern than women. Both traditional values and familial pressure to marry positively predict the level of identity concern for men and women. While co-residence with parents is a significant predictor for the men, women are more affected by region of residence. The findings suggest that the identity concerns of men are mainly related to familial and cultural factors while women’s concerns are also influenced by community-related SES factors. A paper on sexual minority women’s negotiation of marriage and identity was presented in an international conference. Specifically, we employed a mixed method approach to examine the interaction of gender and socioeconomic status. The findings show that sexual minority women who attain high education and live in metropolises or provincial capitals tend to develop a more positive sense of sexual identity and resist traditional values. Many prefer to opt out of marriage and remain single, while some may aspire to having same-sex marriage. Sexual minority women who have lower socioeconomic status are more likely to be concerned about whether same-sex relationships can last and find it hard to imagine an alternative form of life. The other conference paper examines how region of residence and internal migration influence negotiation of marriage and identity through a mixed method approach. The findings indicate that compared with people who live in small towns, those who live in large cities are more able to contest the traditional values and embrace sexual identity. Apart from the open atmosphere offered by large cities, factors such as internal migration should be considered. Those who migrate from small towns to large cities can make use of the physical distance to fulfill parental expectation through cooperative marriages between gays and lesbians, whereas those who are local residents in large cities find it hard to perform a performative union and would rather choose to remain single. Yet intense competition and alienation in large cities can influence one’s desire to stay or leave. We argue that identity negotiation of sexual minorities in China cannot be understood in isolation from their migration trajectories.

12605615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12605615.value: We had some preliminary findings on the influence of region of residence and internal migration in sexual minorities’ negotiation of marriage pressure. Future research can explore more systematically how internal and international migrations influence the lived experiences and identity construction of Chinese sexual minorities. I’m exploring with my research partner Prof. Eric Wright the possibility of developing a comparative study of the identity concerns of sexual minorities in US and China. We have been collaborating in a project “Pathways of integration and the health of LGBTQ youth in Hong Kong, Cape Town and Atlanta, and he is a co-author of the forthcoming article. I am writing two journal articles based on the conference papers. In addition, I would write a paper to discuss the global applicability of the out-and-proud model and the linear progressive model of homosexual identity formation (objective 3), focusing specifically on the coming out practices in China.

12605615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12605615.value: Previous work has already validated the influence of cultural values on sexual minority identity in China. The novelty of this study lies in its recognition of the heterogeneity rather than homogeneity of sexual minorities in China. Specifically, it examines what resources, networks, and discourses people of different genders and socioeconomic statuses utilize in their negotiations of marriage and sexual identity. Informed by the concept of intersectionality, the study represents a rare and systematic attempt that explores the interconnection of identities such as sexual orientation, gender and class in China. The research employs a mixed methods approach to capture both the quantitative and qualitative differences among different intersectional positions. Such an approach also offers a nuanced understanding of the fluid and contradictory character of sexual minority identification in China. It raises questions regarding the applicability of the out-and-proud model of sexual identity in a family-oriented, collectivist society. Its attentions to the ethnocentric bias of the model and to both the local and global forces in identity construction enable it to serve as a good reference for sexual minority studies in non-Western contexts.

12605715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12605715.value: The built environment of modern cities is largely shaped by urban planning rather than spontaneous development. While whether planned urban space adequately accommodates human needs remains heatedly debated, the increasing complexity of urban development continues to challenge the competence of planners and policy makers. In Chinese cities, given the rigid control of land use and development, planning generally goes undisputed. However, the distribution of urban activities is increasingly redirected by market forces, leading to unplanned development. Most commonly seen are various commercial establishments that have emerged spontaneously within and around the planned fabric of the urban environment, such as a convenience store popping up at the corner façade, a hair salon opened in the roadside garage and a studio concealed in an apartment building. Despite the downsides of these establishments, they not only meet market demand that is unheeded in city plans, but they also facilitate entrepreneurial endeavors for individuals who cannot afford regular premises. In general, unplanned commercial establishments are distributed sporadically. However, such establishments prevail in urban villages, which are migrant settlements that have been transformed from rural villages engulfed by urban expansion. In a state of quasi-urban jurisdiction where rural collective land ownership remains, the construction and utilization of buildings are beyond the control of planning or building codes. The high level of autonomy allows for excess commercial establishments to emerge in residential buildings and non-residential buildings. Given the large population of migrant tenants in urban villages, the proliferation of various commercial establishments reflects the local demand for cheap and accessible goods and services unavailable in the surrounding planned environment. Urban villages, existing as havens for unplanned commercial establishments, enable us to investigate unplanned commercial establishments in great quantity and diversity. This research will conduct surveys in Shenzhen’s widespread urban villages to examine the spatiality of unplanned commercial establishments. Spatial econometric analytics based on rich building and socioeconomic data will be used to understand the configuration and distribution of unbridled commercial development. The focus on unplanned establishments will offer new insight into retail location studies. In practice, the findings will contribute to urban planning and policy making, in coping with the current state and future development of unregulated commercial activities, and in the effective allocation of commercial facilities. In addition, the analytical methodology developed using highly diverse data will be applicable to suitability analysis of urban development plans and to retail location studies in various settings. 現代城市環境的絕大部分是由城市規劃而非自發建設所塑造。一方面，社會對城市規劃是否能充分解決市民生活中的各種需要尚存疑慮；另一方面，城市發展的複雜性對規劃師和決策者的挑戰越來越大。在中國，政府對城市土地利用和開發的嚴格控制使規劃對城市發展的影響巨大。然而，城市中各種活動的發生不可避免受到市場的支配，形成大量未規劃的設施。這類設施出現在規劃形成的城市空間內部和邊緣，如住宅樓街角部分改建的商業店舖，路邊車庫改造成的髮廊，隱藏在住宅單位內的工作室等等。雖然這些未規劃設施可能存在負面影響，但是它們為無能力支付正規商業舖位較高租金的經營者提供了商業空間，也滿足了部分市民的消費需求。 未規劃的商業設施通常在城市正規街區零星分佈，而它們在城中村中卻大量集中存在。城中村是農村被城市擴張包圍而形成的移民社區。在模糊的城鄉二元管制體系下，城中村的開發建設並未受到城市規劃和建設標準的有效控制，導致大量商業舖位出現在住宅或其它建築。城中村中高密度的低收入人口對廉價商品和服務的需求促進了村內各種商業活動的繁榮。城中村作為未規劃商業設施集中分佈的城市空間，為研究這類商業活動提供了大量的、多樣性豐富的樣本。 本研究將對深圳市廣泛分佈的城中村進行實地調查，以獲取未規劃商業設施的相關數據。對所收集的空間及非空間數據，採用空間計量模型分析非規劃商業設施的空間分佈和組織模式。針對未規劃商業設施的分析，將為零售區位理論提供新的案例和見解。同時，未規劃商業的分佈特徵將為城市規劃和政策制定提供決策支持：未規劃商業的分佈特徵將幫助執法部門有效控制存在社會危害商業設施。同時，對未規劃商業形成原因的探索將為在城市規劃過程中更有效地進行商業及其它設施選址提供規劃建議。此外，本研究採用的計量分析方法將利用調查獲得的大樣本數據做充分檢驗和改進，使該方法能廣泛適用於不同城市環境下的規劃方案適宜性評價、商業選址和零售區位分析。

12606215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12606215.value: Transportation research or more specifically travel behavior research is experiencing a paradigm shift from focusing on the instrumental aspect of travel (such as travel time and monetary costs) to also consider the affective experience of and the cognitive satisfaction with travel. Issues related to daily travel–related subjective wellbeing have recently received great research attention. Pleasure seeking is considered in addition to time and/or money cost minimization as important determinants of travel choices and transport decisions. This new development of academic research has the potential to help broaden the objectives of transport policies from focusing on the provision of efficient and effective transport services (i.e., facilitating the fast movements of people and freight between different places) to also provide pleasant experience of travel. Many studies have been conducted to examine the factors determining individuals’ satisfaction (or dissatisfaction) and affective experience with their daily travel and activities. Existing studies have revealed that travel satisfaction varies significantly between transport models and trip characteristics are important determinants of travel satisfaction. However, the contribution of more policy related variables such as the built environment of individuals’ residential place has rarely been studied. More importantly, notwithstanding the many studies of travel satisfaction in North America and Europe, studies in other parts of the world, where mobility, travel behavior and social norms are quite different, are very scarce. This research project is proposed to fill in these gaps. Based on the Principal Investigator’s long term research on built environment and travel behavior and recent research on subjective wellbeing, this research project is proposed to examine the influence of individuals’ residential environment on their travel satisfaction and travel affective experience, study the effects of travel wellbeing on short-term activity-travel choices, and explore the possible impacts of travel wellbeing in long-term mobility and residential location decisions. The case study is proposed to be conducted in Shanghai, China. This research will fill in an important gap in the travel wellbeing literature with empirical evidences from a city of a developing country and establish important linkages between travel satisfaction, travel behavior and residential environment. The outcomes of this research will be highly relevant for developing transport policies acting on the non-instrumental aspect of travel to manage travel demand and spatial policies to improve individuals’ travel satisfaction and quality of life. 交通研究 ，或更具體地說，出行行為研究正經歷著從關注出行的功能方面（如出行時間和金錢成本）到考量情感經驗和認知滿意度的思考模式的轉換。與日常出行行為相關的主觀幸福感問題近期已受到極大的研究關注。追求愉悅被認為是除時間和／或成本最小化外決定出行選擇和交通選擇的重要決定因素。這一新的學術研究發展有潛力幫助擴大交通政策的目標從重視提供有效和便捷的交通設施（例如幫助加快不同地域間人群和運輸的移動）到提供愉快的出行經驗。許多研究已經對決定個人滿意度（或不滿意度）和他們日常出行和活動之情感經驗的因素進行了調查。現有的研究表明，出行滿意度在不同交通模式之間有顯著差異，出行特徵是出行滿意度的重要決定因素。然而， 更多與政策制定相關的變量，例如個人居住地的建成環境卻很少被研究。更重要的是，儘管北美和歐洲有很多關於出行滿意度的研究，在其他關於移動性、交通行為和社會標準都截然不同的地區卻很少有相關研究。這項研究的提出意在填補這些空白。基於项目负责人對建成環境和出行行為的長期研究，以及關於主觀幸福感的近期研究，本研究項目提出調查個人居住環境對他們出行滿意度和出行情感經驗的影響， 研究出行幸福感對短期活動出行選擇的影響，並探討出行滿意度在長期移動性和住宅選址抉策上可能造成的影響。這個案例研究建議在中國上海進行。本研究將運用一個發展中國家城市的經驗證據填補關於出行幸福感文獻的重要空白，並建立出行滿意度、出行行為和住宅環境之間的重要聯繫。本研究項目的成果有助于制訂管理出行需求和空間政策以提升個人出行滿意度和生活質量。

12606215.label: Realisation of objectives
12606215.value: The objectives of the research project have been achieved through a variety of research activities: 1. Field study and data collection: we have conducted the questionnaire survey in Shanghai. In total, 1031 households from 30 communities, 15 districts in Shanghai successfully participated in the survey. Data on personal and household information, travel wellbeing, physical activities and health conditions, perceived residential environmental attributes, travel attitude and also a two-day activity-travel diary were collected. This database has served to address the research questions concerning travel satisfaction and wellbeing of this research project and offered the opportunities to study issues related to food environment, eating behavior, and health, etc. 2. Exploring the link between residential relocation and changes in travel satisfaction. The research paper was published Transportation Research Part A: Policy and Practice in 2020. 3. Investigating the differences between spouses in well-being changes after residential relocations. The research paper was published in Cities in 2020. 4. Discussing intra-urban differences in travel and residential satisfaction. Preliminary results of the study were presented at the Comparative Urbanism: Global Perspectives Conference in Atlanta in March, 2019. 5. Investigating the issue of residential self-selection in long-term choices including residential location and work place choices. The paper was in Journal of Transport Geography in 2020 6. Exploring the different roles of family members when considering the residential self-selection in the built environment-travel behavior connection. The research paper was published in the journal Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment in 2019. 7. Examining the institutional factors’ role in shaping individuals' mobility and travel behavior. The research paper was published in the journal Transport Policy in 2018. 8. Conduct empirical investigations into the link between car ownership, travel and life satisfaction. The paper is now under review of Transportation Research Part A. 9. Investigating the role of neighborhood food environments in the eating through Online-to-Offline food delivery services? The paper has been submitted to Applied Geography 10. Studying the geographic and socio-economic disparities in accessibility to fresh foods in Shanghai, China. A draft paper has been completed. The paper will be submitted for possible publication in an international journal.

12606215.label: Major findings and research outcome
12606215.value: This research project has so far generated the following research outcomes: 5 research paper publications in top international journals; three papers submitted or under review for possible publication in international journals; one paper (and more) under preparation; and four presentations in international conferences. The major research findings of this project include: Most home movers reported improvement in travel satisfaction after residential relocation, suggesting that residential relocation may serve as an opportunity to enhance travel satisfaction (Wang, Mao, and Wang, 2020, Transportation Research Part A); Residential relocation leads to significant life satisfaction improvements for both male and female household heads and no significant difference in the magnitude of improvements between them (Mao and Wang, 2020, Cities). Residential self-selection exists in all long-term choices including residential location and work place choices, which are found to be mutually dependent and have indirect impacts on travel behavior through the other choice (Guan and Wang, 2020, Journal of Transport Geography); Owning multiple cars increased car users’ life satisfaction, but purchasing a more expensive car and driving cars more frequently could not increase life satisfaction. Car owners who did not use cars often had higher travel satisfaction than those who use often (Li, Wang, and Guan, Transportation Research Part A, under review); Male and female household heads played different roles residential self-selection and should be considered studies on the built environment-travel behavior connection (Guan and Wang, 2019). Hukou status was found to have a significant impact on mobility and travel behavior of Chinese urbanites and local urban residents had better home-work proximity and higher car ownership rate, traveled more by non-motorized modes and spent less time on daily travel (Yao and Wang, 2018)

12606215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12606215.value: The data collected by this project provide the research team new research opportunities and extend our research focus from wellbeing to health. Specifically, our research team is exploring the data collected in Shanghai and study the following issues: 1. Characterize the neighborhood food environment and investigate disparities in access to fresh and healthy foods in Shanghai 2. investigate the link between neighborhood food environments, online-to-offline food delivery service and obesity 3. Investigate the neighborhood environment, physical activities and health outcomes (mental and obesity). Based on research findings of this project, the PI has developed a research proposal to investigate the triangle relationships between neighborhood environment, daily activities, and wellbeing/health outcomes. The proposal has been submitted to RGC to bid for the Senior Research Fellow Scheme 2021/22.

12606215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12606215.value: This research project investigated the importance of residential built environment in travel and life satisfaction. We found that neighborhood built environment influenced travel and life satisfaction and such influence is different for different household members (e.g. husband and wife). We also found that there were connections between car ownership/use and life and travel satisfaction and people owning more cars had higher life satisfaction. The study also revealed that the travel attitudes of male and female household heads influenced residential location choices differently. This project established relationships between mobility and travel/life satisfaction and between neighborhood built environment and travel/life satisfaction. It also discovered that male and female household heads may have different impacts from home relocations. The study improved the existing knowledge on travel satisfaction and contributes to public and urban planning policies aiming to improve travel and life satisfaction.

12606515.value: To examine the news coverage of “Occupy Central” in the media of Hong Kong, Mainland China, Taiwan, compared to those of UK and US. 12606515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12606515.value: “佔領中環”的危機，加上大中華區的三個地區不同的意識形態大背景，為新聞框架研究提供一個非凡的平台，因為它涉及到針對專制政治抱負，這正是不同的媒體系統持有不同價值觀和敏感程度的所在。新聞媒體在處理示威者和統治者之間的衝突時，基於不一致的政治和社會價值採取多種不同的報導及詮釋。本研究探討“佔領中環”是如何在英國，美國，香港，台灣和中國大陸媒體的新聞中被報導及詮釋的，並分析“框架”理念對報導和詮釋的影響， 在意識形態差異的背景下討論這些報導的差異， 以及對造成這些差異和理論意義進行了探討。

12606515.label: Realisation of objectives
12606515.value: Over the course of the project, we conducted relevant literature review, carried out the data collection (news content coding plus in-depth interviews) process, and had data analysis done until all possibilities, capacity, and capability are exhausted. In order to investigate for how the Occupy Central is framed by Hong Kong newspapers, the project team conducted a content analysis concentrating on the whole period from the beginning on September 28 to December 15, 2014, the day of clearance operation on the street. Specifically, the content analysis aimed to code news stories as the following variables: 1. News Perspective: how the story holds a perspective of con-protester or con-government (“clearly anti-protester, probably anti-protester, neutral, probably anti-government, clearly anti-government”); 2. Government Actions: how the news story describes government action as peaceful conciliation or violent suppression (“peaceful conciliation, conciliation, neutral, suppression, violent suppression”); 3. Protester Behavior: How the news story describes the protestors’ behavior (“very violent and negative, violent and negative, neutral, pro-democratic reform or reasonable or positive, very pro-democratic reform or reasonable or positive”); 4. Judgmental headline: how presence of judgmental words in headline is judged (“none at all, mild presence, significant presence”); 5. Conflict frame: how the story behaves in referring to two sides or to more than two sides of the problem or issue (i.e., the story is clearly/slightly inclined to one-side); 6. Human interest: Does the story report the issue by providing a human examples or exemplars or description of individuals and groups who are likely affected by the issue? 7. Economic consequence (1): Is there a mention of financial losses or gains now or in the future? 8. Economic consequence (2): Is there a mention of the costs/degree of expense involved? 9. Causality: Does the news attribute the primary cause/origin to the following conflict? (“internal, external, both”) 10. Solution: Who the story suggests is responsible for solving the problem? (“individual, HK government, China central government, other governments, institutions/corporations”) 11. Relating to Beijing Spring of 1989: Does the story mention the Beijing Spring? 12. Sourcing pattern: Which is the primary source that the news story quotes ? (“HK government/China central government, pro-movement source, anti-movement source, balanced overall”) The study addressed to the following general research question and hypothesis: RQ: How was the Occupy Central movement reported in the news coverage in mainland China, Hong Kong, Taiwan, the U.K., and the U.S., respectively? What is the difference, if any, among them? H: News media of mainland China, Hong Kong and Taiwan exerted different frames on the coverage of Occupy Central that corresponded in each case with their respective prevailing ideologies. A content analysis of the Occupy Central news was conducted involving ten leading newspapers in five different jurisdictions. It was carried out within the period from January 1st to May 30 in 2016. The framing analysis involves seven key variables that are designed to measure the frames used in reporting the Occupy Central protests and crisis. These variables are established in in correspondence to previous studies in literature review, in combination with what the PI has observed and identified from original pilot data – that is, via both deductive and inductive approaches. Media content was obtained through the WiseNews database (for Chinese news) and the Factiva database (for English news). Catering to the needs of academic research, WiseNews is commonly agreed among researchers of the Chinese media to be the best available database that archives Chinese news publications in the Greater China area. The Factiva database is the best available source for English news for the purpose of this research, as it is commonly considered the most established and comprehensive source overall for research related to journalistic documents. The SPSS data file resulted from a rigorous coding process was cleaned and each variable’s descriptive statistics were checked to ensure validity. Statistical procedures, including ANOVA, Chi-Square and cross-tab tests were conducted to analyze the data. A full paper was developed and presented at the AEJMC 2017 Convention as received very position comments. The qualitative part of the study was not without difficulties, however. Initially we planned to use the quantitative results for one conference paper and the qualitative part for another (Objective #6). As it turned out, it was extremely challenging to secure a sufficient number of journalists willing to be interviewed due to their tight and irregular schedules, and probably also due to the politically sensitive topic of this study per se. We tried every possibility to push on for the interviews, including using social media and personal contacts, but in the end, we decided not to far-fetch and resolve the problem by combining the qualitative and quantitative data into one paper (presented at AEJMC 2017 Convention). A journal article was further developed based on the AEJMC paper and has been published in the International Journal of Communication (SSCI) in June 2018. We are in the process of organizing the dataset and working with library colleagues to use a digital platform to share with the research community the data generated from this project via open access online (Objective #5). I am proud to report that all the seven objectives set forth in the original proposal have been largely achieved.

12606515.label: Major findings and research outcome
12606515.value: This study finds that, overall, news media in democratic societies appeared more in favor of the protesters and critical of the actions taken by the Hong Kong government. This offers the hint that a particular dominant ideology can influence media’s framing of politically sensitive issues. One common ground that the Hong Kong, Taiwan, U.K., and U.S. papers share is the anti-communist-ruling attitude. This shared attitude may have contributed to the similarities existing in the Occupy Central coverage among the four. By selecting some aspects of a perceived reality in the Occupy Central protests and excluding others, and describing certain aspects with salience and emphasis, the U.K., U.S., mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan newspapers employed different news frames congruent with their various ideological boundaries. The resulting coverage promoted a particular problem definition, certain causal interpretations, and evaluation of the protesters, the governments’ actions, the responsible parties, the economic consequences, the solution, and even moral judgment of the legitimacy of the democratic movement as a whole. One interesting finding of the study is that the U.K. coverage of the movement seemed to overlap with that of Taiwan more than it does with the U.S. With regard to news perspective, government actions, and protester behavior, there was no significant difference between the Taiwan paper and the U.K. paper. This implies their shared moral judgments on the movement and acknowledgment of the legitimacy of the protests. The New York Times, as an exemplar of a pure liberal press, was found to be the boldest among the free media examined in this study in framing the movement, holding an obvious anti-government stance and a clear positive attitude towards the protesters. The Taiwan paper, though largely enjoying a Libertarian press environment, appeared to have used relatively measured narratives, like those in the U.K. paper, which falls between the liberal model, and the democratic corporatist model and was perhaps more concerned about the economic consequences that the movement may bring to Hong Kong. The Taiwan paper’s behavior may be due to the fact that most Taiwanese media practice self-censorship in reporting sensitive issues about mainland China while the then-incumbent Nationalist Party’s (KMT) government was cementing ties with China. These findings resonate with overall observations on the news from previous framing research. The results of this study are also consistent with those of previous studies in confirming that a particular framing may be made salient not only in press systems where the state imposes strict authoritarian control, but also in systems where press freedom is highly valued, like that of the U.K. and the U.S.

12606515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12606515.value: This research applied framing theory, in combination with the protest paradigm, to the specific context of a significant protest event in Hong Kong’s history. It reveals specifically how the same events and issues were reported by news media of varied ideological backgrounds in different ways. The results provide new empirical evidence to buttress the framing theory. Moreover, the study furthered scholarly understandings of the protest paradigm by integrating framing research with the specific context of political conflicts (anti-government protests in particular) and generating a comprehensive set of concrete measurements that can be used in future research. This article calls for a research agenda that revisits the protest paradigm and contemplates a renewed conception and theoretical framework.

12606515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12606515.value: The Occupy Central crisis, combined with its backdrop of different political climaxes in the three regions of the Greater China, provides an extraordinary platform for a news framing study, as it involves political aspirations against authoritarianism, something that is valued and sensitized to varying degrees among different media systems. Stark contrasts in the news coverage in various media outlets have been observed. This study is not just “another” framing analysis, among others, on an issue covered differently by different media outlets. While studies comparing how different countries’ media frame and present the same story have been done before, this study is unique in that it will assess the phenomenon of news framing by examining how three Chinese-speaking regions, with close geographical and cultural proximity, deal with a political event occurring within their own area, compared to Western coverage on the same matter. While Hong Kong and its Beijing-based central government continue to struggle to achieve political reform, and the three regions (including Taiwan) debate for unification under the principle of “one country, two systems,” this research has great relevance to the political development of contemporary China, and it will also shed light on our understanding of the relationship between media and politics, between global influences and national specificities in the Greater China area.

12606715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12606715.value: 此研究透過分析離婚婦女的敘事檢視香港及廣州的離婚意義。在過去數十年，香港及中國內地均可見離婚數字上升的趨勢。本研究首席研究員曾於1998至2002年期間在香港進行相關研究，發現於上世紀九十年代離婚的中年婦女對離婚賦予的意義非常負面：離婚是不合理、病態的事；離婚女性心理和性格有缺憾。為了避免離婚，婦女會盡力挽救婚姻、長時間忍受及在做離婚決定的過程中付出高昂代價。女性主義分析西方社會中出現的「他」和「她」的離婚，在香港也適用。近廿年有不少研究指出香港的家庭觀念、婚姻價值觀等在轉變，年輕人對離婚的接受程度有所提升。在社會、文化背景的轉變中，此研究旨在更新及擴闊這些方面的知識。在內地，特別是大城市如廣州，離婚率也在上升，但有關離婚婦女的研究非常缺乏。選擇廣州的原因是廣東省是內地經濟發展及社會福利開支增長甚快的省份，廣州在廣東省內廿一個城市中離婚率排行首位。參考三位研究員曾在廣州進行的一項小型有關單親母親的研究結果，本研究旨在檢視在中國急速經濟發展的城市背景中離婚婦女建構的離婚意義，進而比較香港與內地城市離婚意義、離婚後經驗及社會主流論述的相同與差異，透視不同社會、經濟及文化背景如何建構意義。除了社會背景外，年齡、種族、教育、收入因素如何獨立及互動地影響意義建構也是焦點。本研究採用質性研究方法，在香港及廣州進行深入訪談。

12606715.label: Realisation of objectives
12606715.value: All of the six research objectives have been fully achieved. A total number of 96 and 90 Chinese divorced women in Hong Kong and Guangzhou, China were interviewed respectively. The depth interviews of divorced women, each lasted for 1-1.5 hours, have generated very rich qualitative data about the meanings of marriage, family and divorce, the divorce decision-making and post-divorce experiences. Purposive sampling method according to gender, age, income and migrant status was adopted. Regarding the first objective to examine the meanings of marriage, family and divorce evinced by divorced Chinese women in Hong Kong and Guangzhou, it was revealed that meaning making is socially embedded and constantly negotiated in the context of personal situation, family and kin relationships, interpersonal networks at the workplace and/or the community, and the wider culture. There are similarities and differences between meanings ascribed by divorced women in the two cities. For Hong Kong, the predominance of ideas of marriage as lifelong and companionate such as ‘meaning as lifelong’, ‘companionate, equalitarian sharing in marital relationships’ are still evidenced. The modern model of marriage was endorsed by all participants except a few migrant women from mainland China who also expressed utilitarian thinking, such as improving their standard of living, demonstrating the ability to “fly high” by getting married to a Hong Kong man. Regarding the meaning of divorce, there is a mix of traditional and modern ideas with a progression towards the modern. For Guangzhou, while companionate model of marriage is more emphasized among divorced women, utilitarian thinking is evidenced in both the meanings of marriage and divorce. The ideas prescribed by the modern model that ‘divorce is morally neutral’, ‘divorced women are rational’, ‘divorce can be positive’ and there are equal gender rights of divorce have become shared among divorced women of Guangzhou. The second and third research objective is to examine how meanings of divorce have impacted on the divorce decision-making process and post-divorce experiences of divorced women in the two cities. Research findings reveal that the traditional notion of divorce as shameful and a personal failure has been influential in structuring divorce decision-making and post-divorce lives more among Hong Kong than Guangzhou women. Women of Guangzhou have moved towards a more positive stance regarding divorce and have viewed it as more liberating than oppressive as far as personal agency after divorce is concerned. ‘Quick divorce’ has become a pattern of Guangzhou sample with divorce decisions made in a shorter time when compared with the Hong Kong sample. While the inconsistencies between having a modern dominant marriage model and a traditional dominant divorce model explain the dilemmas the women faced in marital troubles and the divorce decision-making process, and their resultant hardships particularly in Hong Kong, divorced women of both cities have reported emotional disturbance. The change in mainland China has far from being completed. The experience of divorce never goes public. Participants of the research study revealed that they have not shared their situation with colleagues in the workplace and neighbours explaining that it is irrelevant. The fear of being known as divorced by people outside of the family has been overwhelming which suggested that divorce is still not treated as a normal form of family and remains a private matter in the context of China. Regarding the fourth objective - to examine how age, ethnicity, education and income by itself and interact to construct the meanings of divorce in both Hong Kong and Guangzhou, it was revealed in the research findings that income in interaction with education and ethnicity (migrant status) has a significant relationship with divorce meanings and experiences. Women of older age and lower education in the two cities have experienced greater struggles and difficulties both during and after divorce. Migrant status in Hong Kong and non-local houkou in Guangzhou are important factors as well. There is a critical factor affecting meaning and experiences as identified among the Guangzhou sample which is the availability of support on childcare. This is closely related to the migrant status/houkou of women. Comparing women who were divorced in the 1990s in Hong Kong (based on the first study conducted by the investigator) in terms of the differences in meanings of marriage and divorce is the fifth research objective. The predominance of ideas of marriage as lifelong and companionate persists as indicated in this study. It reflects the further weakening of utilitarianism and the waning influence of parents in marriage decisions in the context of Hong Kong. Traits of the modern model of divorce, however, emerged as more dominant when the women started to review the meanings of divorce. Certain ideas of the modern model of divorce were endorsed to a larger extent: ‘divorce is an option when love perishes’; ‘divorce is morally neutral and rational’; ‘divorce can bring benefits’; ‘divorce is normal in society’ characterised by more and more divorced women being publicly visible; and divorced couples can continue to relate and be friendly to each other as parents. The research findings of Hong Kong have clearly shown that ideas about divorce have changed enormously in the past two decades. There has been a move towards a more dominant modern stance on divorce, although two powerful obstacles, the welfare of children and social stigmatisation, have persisted. The divorced women in this study have re-negotiated the meanings and experiences of their divorce based on referencing of ideas around modern divorces and through undergoing a dialectical process that includes the personal and social. In doing so, the modern model of divorce has become more conspicuous in the past two decades. Regarding the sixth objective, it was revealed that Hong Kong and Guangzhou has different social, economic and cultural contexts which construct the dominant meanings of divorce. Diversity is evidenced in the ideologies, provision and delivery of social policies related to single parent families, cultural ideas about gender and family, and more, about women’s economic roles in the family and wider society. In Hong Kong, the government adopted the welfare-to-work model in the early 2000s, and has introduced various programs under the Comprehensive Social Security Assistance (CSSA) scheme to make work a condition of receiving welfare. The research findings indicate that although divorced women in Hong Kong mainly interpret welfare as something that is instrumental and transitory, and the experiences with contacting service providers, particularly those who work at social security offices, have been largely negative, they look to social welfare as an important source of support after divorce. A characteristic of the Chinese welfare system is the financing and delivery of community services at grassroots levels through street offices and resident organizations. As these have differing financial resources, there is great local variation in the quantity and quality of services provided. Divorced women in Guangzhou have to rely on various sources of income and mainly from work to survive. Finally, the massive migration of women’s labour from rural to urban and the one-child policy in China, which has weakened the support capacity of families, has no equivalent in Hong Kong. All of these factors testify to the existence of different policy environments, culture and the economic significance for single mothers to work in mainland China.

12606715.label: Major findings and research outcome
12606715.value: The findings revealed that among the different meanings given to marriage, family and divorce by divorced Chinese women in Hong Kong, ideas of companionate marriage have become predominant but are less influenced by ideologies of gender equality in conjugal relationships that are found in the West. The meanings of marriage and divorce are gendered. These women had prioritized marriage which they expected to be a lifelong relationship with exclusive love. Instead, they have internalized the negative meanings of divorce as abnormal, bad, shameful and a personal failure, particularly during the divorce-decision-making which have made the process particularly painful and stressful. Justifications for a modern divorce such as ‘an option when there is no love’, ‘a morally neutral and rational choice’, ‘normal’ and ‘can be positive’ have emerged and become prominent when women started to re-negotiate the meanings after their divorce as a means of reducing distress. Compared to Hong Kong, the meaning of marriage as a lifelong and exclusive love relationship is also dominant in Guangzhou, but utilitarianism prevails in mate selection, particularly with women who migrate from rural to urban areas. Instead of emphasizing morality, there is a pragmatic orientation that sees divorce as a problem solver. The negativities of divorce are more subtle as shown in the narratives which suggest that divorce is normal and understandable; however, the situation is not shared with workplace colleagues, neighbours and extended family members. The findings have also revealed that age, ethnicity, education and income levels independently and together construct the meanings of divorce in both cities. Although the negative meanings of divorce are generally influential, they are more likely to affect the older, less educated or less financially well-off women more. Migrant women particularly suffer from the negative discourses of divorce and are stigmatized as bad, shameful and ill-fated women. In a comparison of Hong Kong women who divorced in the 1990s (the First Study conducted by the PI from 1998 to 2002) versus those in the 2000s, it is evident that ideas around divorce have substantially changed. Although divorce is still considered to be unacceptable and divorced women as failures, particularly in the divorce-decision-making process, there is progression towards a modern view as evidenced in the First Study, and shown in the post divorce narratives in the Second Study, notwithstanding the persistence of two powerful obstacles – the welfare of children and social stigmatization.

12606715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12606715.value: This is an extensive study on Chinese divorce which has interviewed 96 and 90 Chinese divorced women in Hong Kong and Guangzhou respectively. The work has made significant progress in developing knowledge on the meanings of marriage, family and divorce; divorce-decision-making; post-divorce experiences; and the influence of age, ethnicity, education and income levels on the meanings and experiences of divorced Chinese women in Hong Kong and mainland China. Areas related to divorce found during the research process have not been explored in-depth elsewhere, which include post-divorce relationships with paternal and maternal families, co-parenting after divorce, childcare arrangements during marriage and after divorce, divorce experiences of domestic violence victims and experiences with social services. The findings of this study indicate that further research should be conducted to expand and extend knowledge on divorce in Chinese societies. This study provides evidence that meaning making is socially embedded and meanings can be negotiated to enhance post-divorce coping. The findings have implications on social work intervention at the individual, family and community levels. The development of intervention models is recommended to facilitate the negotiation of individual and collective meanings. Moreover, the findings have implications for social policies, social services and community support.

12606715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12606715.value: This is an extensive study on Chinese divorce which has interviewed 96 and 90 Chinese divorced women in Hong Kong and Guangzhou respectively. The work has made significant progress in developing knowledge on the meanings of marriage, family and divorce; divorce-decision-making; post-divorce experiences; and the influence of age, ethnicity, education and income levels on the meanings and experiences of divorced Chinese women in Hong Kong and mainland China. Those in Hong Kong have begun to justify a modern model of divorce as ‘an option when there is no love’, ‘a morally neutral and rational choice’, ‘normal’ and ‘positive’ which have become prominent when women started to re-negotiate the meanings after their divorce as a means of reducing distress. Compared to Hong Kong, in Guangzhou, there is a pragmatic orientation in divorce decisions and after divorce which views divorce as a problem solver as opposed to an emphasis on morality. The negativities of divorce are more subtle which suggest that divorce has been normalized due to its increasing visibility. However, the women hide their situation from workplace colleagues, neighbours and kin. Nevertheless, since the meanings of divorce are socially constructed, changes can be made at the individual and collective levels.

12606815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12606815.value: Background: In Hong Kong, there were around 70, 000 people with neurocognitive disorder in 2006, and the number is expected to escalate to 330, 000 by the year 2050. Among them, about 85% suffered from mild neurocognitive disorder. This continuing increase in the population of people with neurocognitive disorder will be a great burden on both medical and social care systems. At present, pharmacological treatments for mild neurocognitive disorder are found to have small benefits on cognitive decline and symptoms. Recently, cognitive stimulation therapy (CST), which is referred as a cognitive based non-pharmacological interventions that targets cognitive and social functioning, has been developed in UK and internationally. Research evidences have found that people with mild neurocognitive disorder can benefit from CST by improving cognitive functioning, improving quality of life, reducing depression, and reducing behavioural problems. Moreover, CST is also found to be more cost effective than treatment as usual. Objective: This research project thus aims to develop a CST group model which is suitable for local Chinese elderly with mild neurocognitive disorder and to evaluate its effectiveness. Research Design: In this study, a single blind randomized control trial will be adopted. 164 people with mild neurocognitive disorder, recruiting from local district elderly community centres (DECCs), will be randomly assigned to a CST group (i.e. treatment group) or a control group. The CST group will last for fourteen sessions (two sessions a week; each session lasting for 75 minutes), while the control group just receive standard service from local DECCs. Standardized assessment tools will be conducted with all participants at pre-treatment, post-treatment and 4th month follow up periods, so as to investigate the outcomes of the CST group just after treatment as well as its long term effects. Hypothesis: A CST group can improve cognitive ability and reduce depressive mood for Chinese people with mild neurocognitive disorder. Significance: It is anticipated that this indigenized CST group model yields positive outcomes, and that it is easily be implemented at local elderly centres so that thousands of people with mild neurocognitive disorder can benefit from this project. Work done by the Principal Investigator The Principle Investigator (PI) conducted the first pilot study on a CST group for Chinese elderly with mild neurocognitive disorder, and found that after completing CST training, all 55 participants had shown significant improvement in MMSE. These positive findings support the feasibility of this present research project.

12606815.label: Realisation of objectives
12606815.value: The Principle Investigator (PI) conducted the first pilot study on a 14-session cognitive stimulation therapy (CST) group in Hong Kong, funded by the General Research Fund [Reference No.: HKBU_12606815]. In a multi-center, randomized waitlist controlled trial, involving 101 elderly with mild dementia recruiting from local District Elderly Community Centres, results of 2x2 repeated measures of ANCOVA demonstrated that the CST group is significantly more effective than the control group in improving the cognitive ability for participants with a moderate effect size (partial eta square= .11). The present study demonstrates the effectiveness of the CST group on the improvement of cognitive ability of community-dwelling elderly with mild dementia Also, a the program manual of the 14-session CST group, which is adapted from the original program CST manual develop in the Western society, has been produced successfully by this project which are suitable for use with elderly with mild dementia supported by local District Elderly Community Centres. There are five local District Elderly Community Centres joining this research project. Some social workers of these District Elderly Community Centres joined the CTS groups, and provided assistance in running of the CST groups which were primary delivered by the social workers employed by this project. These staff of local DECCs could benefit from this project by observing and learning the knowledge and skills on conducting CST group demonstrated by the social workers employed by this project. Then, these staff of DECCs can then provide CST group in their DECCs for elderly with dementia. PI had a presentation on the research findings on the CST group for elderly with mild dementia recruiting from local elderly centres in Hong Kong at the 2nd International Conference on CST which was successfully held at Hong Kong University on 2-Dec-2017. More than 100 participants, coming from local policymakers, helping professionals in elderly services, local and overseas academics and experts on dementia, attended the conference and my presentation session. In this way, research results has been informed to the local policymakers and other stakeholders in Hong Kong.

12606815.label: Major findings and research outcome
12606815.value: The Principle Investigator (PI) conducted the a multi-center, randomized waitlist controlled trial on a 14-session CST group in Hong Kong, involving 101 elderly with mild dementia recruiting from five local District Elderly Community Centres At baseline, the treatment group (n= 51) and control group (n= 50) did not differ significantly in any demographic or clinical variables. Overall, the participants had a mean baseline MMSE score of 20.67 (SD= 2.30). The 2x2 repeated measures ANCOVA demonstrated that the treatment group was significantly more effective than the control group in improving the MMSE score (F= 12.31, p< .01) with a moderate effect size (partial eta square= .11) after controlling for group difference in age, gender, education, and having a diagnosis of dementia. This demonstrates the effectiveness of the CST group on the improvement of cognitive ability of community-dwelling elderly with mild dementia. In particular, the following research findings are highlighted: 1. elderly with dementia can benefit from the 14-session CST group by having an improvement in MMSE overall score of two points compared with baseline MMSE overall score after completion the CST group over a 7-week period 2. In this study, the social workers who conducted the CST groups adopted a de-stigmatizing approach by promoting the acceptance of illness, valuing the EwMD, and encouraging participants to express their opinions and views. It seems that this de-stigmatizing approach contributes to the effectiveness of the CST group. 3. this study supports the feasibility for EwMD to learn and practice the 8-style tai chi practise, i.e. Baduanjin, which is simple, brief, and popular, and can be self-learned and practised at home and in elderly centres 4. a 14-session CST group is found to be easily conducted by a social worker at a local elderly centre

12606815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12606815.value: PI and Co-Is will continue further develop CST interventions in Hong Kong. In particular, a variety of CST interventions, including: long-term/maintenance CST, individual CST, and internet-delivered CST, have been developed in the Western societies to care for elderly with dementia and caregivers with different needs. For example, those elderly with dementia who cannot attend CST group held at nearby elderly centre due to mobility problems can benefit from the home-based individual CST. The efficacy and effectiveness of these different forms of CST intervention will be investigated by the PI and Co-Is. The benefits and skills of delivering these forms of CST intervention will then be shared with helping professionals in Hong Kong. Also, the PI and Co-Is will initiate advocacy aimed at policy makers to increase resources allocation to further develop different CST interventions, including CST group, in Hong Kong

12606815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12606815.value: In this study, a 14-session CST group is found to be easily conducted by a social worker at a local elderly centre, and that the brief CST is efective on imporving cognitive ability of elderly with mild dementia. These research results suggest that the 14-session CST group is more cost effective than traditional cognitive training programs. With suitable training local helping professionals, such as nurses, occupational therapist, and social workers, can learn the knowledge and skills in conducting CST groups for elderly with dementia in local context. Then, these helping professionals can then provide CST group in their service units for elderly with dementia. In this way, CST groups can be widely implemented in elderly service units Hong Kong. In 2016, there are 216 subvented elderly centre, 73 day care centres/units, and 303 subvented elderly residential homes (Mental Health review, 2017). If all these service units (altogether 592 units) provide 2 CST groups per quarter, with each CST group serving 8 clients with dementia, then about 38,000 elderly with dementia can be served and benefit from the CST groups by improving their cognitive function annually.

12607415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12607415.value: The proposed project will constitute hypermedia anthropological research into an indigenous Hong Kong cultural tradition: the Piu Sik Parade (飄色巡遊) on Cheung Chau Island. Due to urban regeneration, the preservation of local traditions and handicrafts is now in the hands of voluntary organisations within local communities. There is no government-led project or policy related to long-term research on the conservation and inheritance of intangible cultural heritage (ICH) and traditional handicrafts. The proposed project will seek answers to the following questions. Is it possible to preserve a form of ICH such as the Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade and, if so, how can it be preserved? Is there a difference between cultural heritage inheritance and preservation? If so, what is the cause, process and morphology of its inheritance? If the development of an intangible cultural tradition is sustainable, how can it be sustained? Through this project, I wish to generate a research platform for study of the Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade as a form of ICH that includes both material and immaterial cultural ‘living realties’. Moving beyond the parade’s aesthetic qualities, I will seek out links to such important social issues as the island’s identity and memory and cultural preservation. This platform will provide the foundation for wider research on ICH within a Hong Kong-specific academic and intellectual framework. A long-term study will be carried out to observe the ecological environment and developmental trends of Hong Kong’s ICH, with the results serving as an important reference for the preservation and development of ICH and traditional handicrafts and the implementation of related policies and/or advocacy work. Furthermore, an appropriate standard will be established to measure the ecology and value of local traditional industries. The research outcomes will be an academic paper and conference presentation and the online publication of the research results for public access. 此項目將建立以超文本媒體的人類學研究本土長洲香港傳統文化 飄色巡遊。由於城市的重建，現在保全本土傳統工藝大多由本地 社區義務團體進行，香港政府並無主導的相關長遠保全和承傳非 物質文化遺產和傳統工藝研究計劃或政策。這個項目將尋找相關 的提問和答案：保全香港傳統飄色巡遊的非物質遺產(ICH)形態 是否可能？若是，它如何可以被保全？ 非文化遺產的承傳和保 全是否有別？若是，它的成因、過程和非物質的形態是甚麼？若 非物質文化傳統是具可持續的，它能如何被持續？ 透過這研究項目，期望能建構一個研究非物質文化遺產的香港飄 色巡遊的平台，包括其物質的、和其‘當下現實的’非物質文化； 除了巡遊的美學性質，研究將會尋找長洲島嶼身份、記憶I和其 文化保全的重要相關社會事件。這個平台將提供更廣拓香港特殊 的學術和知識框架下非物質文化遺產的基礎。長遠的研究針對觀 察香港非物質文化遺產的生態環境和發展，研究成果可成為非物 質文化遺產保全和發展和厘定相關的政策、建議的重要參考，更 為量度生態和本土傳統工業的借鑑。這項研究的成果將以學術文 章、會議和網上出版展示給公眾。

12607415.label: Realisation of objectives
12607415.value: 1. The Cheung Chau Piu Sik Parade has over seven societies. Through their existing literature and oral history, I was able to organize a comprehensive history of the causes, processes, situations and morphology of the in the heritage of the ICH of the Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade. As one of the societies that have the most historical importance is undergoing reconstruction, we were able to discover many unexposed photos and materials that complement and reinforces the newest part of the research. 2. I photographed and recorded different parts of the three annual Hong Kong Piu Sik Parades in the past years, including the outfits, installations and the design and production of the Piu Sik stands. The order of the parade societies and the design concept of each year's parade complete a horizontal linear depiction of the entire process of the parade, it also consummates and further digs into the structure of the ICH. Though oral description from old masters, there are interesting parts of the process of preparation discovered, such as how to have a child performance emotionally stable during the parade. In addition, answers to questions such as how the old masters were responsible for multiple societies' styling yet they could still adjust the details individually and make each society stand out in its own way. This part of the research constructs and explains a very important and organic partnership in its creative language. The originality of the outfits is based on the regulations and the culture of a co-existing island-society living culture. 3. As a form of ICH, other than being a one-to-one traditional hands craft mode, is also apparent as a communal way of extending the history and culture of such heritage. Although it used to happen only in the Piu Sik Parade on an island, it is constantly being invited to carry into other social communities outside Cheung Chau since 2006. They have been apparent in social performances, school workshops, university-level courses and even in combination with western religious communities. At the same time, Piu Sik has become a crucial cultural heritage and has remained its uniqueness in its method of inheritance even with commercial sponsorships. This is also mentioned in the research. 4. The Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade uses the famous Cheung Chau Bun Festival(打醮 ) medium and successfully became one of the programs in the China ICH. In investigations and research, it is found that other than describing the speciality of Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade, it is more important the Piu Sik Parade can be fit into the application module of Mainland China. An example would be to use the Chinese traditional craftsmanship and put Piu Sik Parade in context to the Chinese Cultural Revolution; the "policy" of The ICH in Mainland China excludes traditional religious and Faith cultural elements, therefore it indicates a difference among the culture and religion of both places. In the ICH application, the cultural context perspective was not heavily implied, such research can serve as a reference for researches in both places. 5. As most of the records and illustrative drawings were more of a literal research outcome, making it easier to present the language details of the technical creation, using hypermedia anthropological research as both a research method and mode of presentation makes sense in this case. It has given related researches a larger and more lively platform to be seen. In addition, the research outcome also includes the interactive power of the multi-media. Overall, the research has reached its researching purposes and is also believed to be able to use a modern media approach to comprehensively and thoroughly connect other researchers to the creators, leading to the traditional craftsmanship a modern way to slice into the knowledge base. The increased understanding of the research knowledge can also be considered as an alternative way of reviving the Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade. During the process of the research, one of the hardest parts is to learn about the complicated social relationships among the masters as the oral description may be deceiving and subjective to understanding. I had to organize well and gather information in a careful manner to make sure the interviewee pool and questions were suitable and clear. In order to gather more insights, there were also conversations recorded with elderlies from the other communities on the island. I believe that the above five research goals have been well accomplished and have also extended more into the difference between the local and regional ICH cultural context. The research can be referred to when searching into the development and history of such context and can also deepen and broaden future research perspectives.

12607415.label: Major findings and research outcome
12607415.value: This research project is to generate a research platform for the study of the Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade as a form of ICH that includes both material and immaterial cultural "living realities". Moving beyond the parade's aesthetic qualities, I seek out the links to such important social issues as the island's identity and memory and cultural preservation. This platform will provide the foundation for wider research on ICH within a Hong Kong -specific academic and intellectual framework. A long-term study will be carried out to observe the ecological environment and development trends of Hong Hong's ICH, with the results serving as an important reference for the perseveration and development of ICH and traditional handicrafts and the implementation of related policies and/or advocacy work. Furthermore, an appropriate standard will be established to measure the ecology and value of local traditional industries. Since this is the first combining academic research and education, knowledge of traditional crafts can be successfully transferred, which is also a platform for continuing education. The refinement of the project output induced a scientific approach of comprehensive documentation of data and images. As a result, a rich database of local traditional handicraft would be built that will continue and supplement the lack of research in this area. The research outcomes mainly a hypermedia anthropologic research approaches: observation (video shooting and photography), and interview (video and audio recording) various masters and their teams of workers, inheritance of ecology, community societies; the organic development of island ecology and culture; audience and government management and conservation; beyond reediting the data, moving images’ research and records are lauded for their ability to bring language and communication to life for web users that make up for what texts lack; and this will empower the interaction amongst intangible cultural heritage and human beings, environments and time.

12607415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12607415.value: More broadly, the results of this research will be made available through the Internet to publicize and share them with an international audience of museum practitioners, students of cultural heritage, an exhibition of Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade at Hong Kong Heritage Museum is planned. The research on Hong Kong Lion Head Dance history, skills and its local influences research also for preparing the following year GRF application. This project will be a hypermedia anthropologic study on the Arts and Crafts of Hong Kong Lion Dance Tradition（香港傳統醒獅藝術和工藝). Lion Dance Tradition: Lion Head Craft and Lion Performance is one of the traditional handicrafts from Foshan, Guangdong in China. In the early 1960s, Hong Kong’s light industrial economy and the community culture of townsmen association boomed. Its Performance is also an intangible aspect of cultural heritage that includes both material and immaterial cultural “living realities”. Beyond aesthetic qualities, Lion Arts are linked with social issues, such as Hong Kong’s identity, memory; and preservation. The research outcome will include visual and textual documentation, academic papers, conference presentation and; an online publication of research findings accessible by the public.

12607415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12607415.value: Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade is intangible cultural research on the Hong Kong traditional craftsmanship. Its history is based on religious performances among local people. Cheung Chau is an island and the annual worship is a Faith activity to protect the fishermen's safety when they go into the sea and also to get illnesses away from islanders. As the geography, time and historical development of the cultural connections are different, the Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade is conducted by local societies with a high attendance rate from the neighbourhood. The narrow landscape of the spaces on the island paves the way for diverse looks and creation that gather outfit designs, weight mechanics, blacksmiths techniques and other combinations to contribute to the development. Since 2006, the annual political reports and hot cultural topics trends have been surrounding the Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade, relating to its design themes and also complementary creations, making the Hong Kong Piu Sik Parade a special annually topic and visual performance that reflects special communities in Hong Kong.

12607815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12607815.value: In responding to the internationalization of higher education, the number of Mainland college students has increased rapidly since the handover of Hong Kong to China in 1997. As a group of international students, they experience a variety of adjustment problems in their adaptation to Hong Kong, which cause acculturative stress and various mental health problems. However, intervention programs aiming at facilitating the psychological adaptation of international students are lacking. Although cognitive behaviour therapy is widely used in university student counselling services in Hong Kong, few studies have examined its effectiveness. This project aims at developing and evaluating a culturally-attuned cognitive behavioural stress management program for Chinese international students, tested with Mainland college students in Hong Kong. A waiting-list control group design will be adopted. A total of 76 participants with a moderate to high level of psychological distress will be recruited and randomly assigned to 4 experimental groups and 4 control groups, respectively. A package of outcome measurements will be developed and administered at pre- and post-test for both experimental and control groups. MANOVA with repeated measures will be conducted to test program effectiveness at both cognitive and affective levels. Theoretical and practical implications for working with Chinese international students, especially in the Hong Kong context, will be proposed. 面對大學教育國際化的發展趨勢，1997年後在香港修讀大學的中國內地學生增加不少。作為國際學生，他們來到香港讀書面對不少適應的問題。這些問題都會對他們做成文化適應及精神的壓力。在香港，專為外地來港的學生的心理適應的服務，實在很少。雖然認知行為介入的方法已經廣泛地應用到大學生的輔導工作上，但卻很少有關於它的應用成效的研究。是次研究旨在評估一個專為中國內地來港學生建立的認知行為壓力管理訓練小組的成效。研究者先把76位有中度至高度心理壓力的參加者作隨機抽樣，安排參加認知行為壓力的實驗組別。候選的參加者則安排作控制組，作為成效對照。研究採用前後實驗設計(pretest-posttest) ， 參加研究者會在小組前和完結時填寫評估問卷。研究者取得前測和後測的資料後會使用MANOVA重複量數測驗，為收回的問卷進行統計分析和比較，評估壓力管理小組的成效。研究者希望從研究結果提供如何幫助中國內地來港學生的心理及文化適應的建議。

12607815.label: Realisation of objectives
12607815.value: All of the two proposed objectives were completed and achieved. A total of 140 participants registered for the study (which is higher than 100 participants in the reseach proposal). Eighteen participants were disqualified (GHQ-12 score < 2) and 22 qualified participants quit the study immediately after the intake interview due to lack of time. Twenty-six qualified participants confirmed to join the study at in-take interview but declined afterwards. As a result, 74 qualified students (as compared to the total sample size calculated as 61 in the research proposal) were randomly allocated to either the experimental group or the waitlist control group. Altogether six experimental groups (n=74)(including participants from waiting-list control groups) and three cohort control groups (n=37) were conducted. The first CBT experimental group was started on 8 October 2016 while the last experimental group was ended on 16 June 2018. In total, 74 and 59 responses from the experimental groups were collected at the pre- and post-tests, respectively. The group prevention program consisted of 8 weekly sessions of 3 hours each, which were run by an experienced social worker and certified cognitive behavioral therapist who was trained at the Beck Institute in the U.S.A., and co-run by a CBT trainee who is a registered social worker in Hong Kong with CBT training. The primary outcome measures were the Chinese version of General Health Questionnaire-12 (GHQ-12; Goldberg & Williams, 1988; Ye, 2009), and Acculturative Stress Scale for Chinese Students (ASSCS, Bai, 2016). The secondary outcome measure included Chinese Automatic Thoughts Questionnaire (CATQ, Pan, Ye, & Ng, 2016), Post-migration Growth Scale (PMGS; Pan, Wong & Ye, 2013), Chinese Making Sense of Adversity Scale (CMSAS; Pan, Wong & Chan, 2008), Chinese version of the Core Belief Inventory (CBI; Cann et al., 2010; Pan, Ye, Chen, & Park, in press), Chinese Affect Scale (CAS, Hamid & Cheng, 1996). Intent-to-treat analysis was performed on all of the data. Prior to the data analysis, missing data were replaced using an expectation-maximization algorithm. The between-group differences in the baseline variables were tested using a Chi-square test and an independent sample t test. A series of 2 (group) x 2 (time) ANOVA with repeated measures were conducted to examine the Group x Time interaction effect on the outcome measures. The partial η2 was calculated as an effect size indicator. Paired sample t test was conducted separately for the two conditions to test the simple main effects of time within each group on the outcome measures with the effect size of Cohen’s d (Cohen, 1988). Clinical significance was examined by Chi-square test to compare the percentages of cases and non-cases on the GHQ-12 scores of the post-test between the experimental group and control group. All of the analyses were conducted with SPSS 25.0.
