14100115.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100115.value: (1) The visible-light-driven (VLD) photocatalytic bacterial disinfection (PBD) ability of three iron-bearing natural magnetic minerals (NMMs), namely, natural magnetic sphalerite (NMS), vanadium titanomagnetite (VTM) and natural pyrrohotite (NP) were determined: The results (Figure 1 in the attached Final Report) indicated that NMS has better photocatalytic disinfection ability toward Escherichia coli than other two NMMs (Figure 2). The physico-chemical properties of three NMMs were also determined (Figures 3-6), the major difference between them is NMS magnetic properties is poorer than those of VTM and NP (Figure 6, Wang et al. 2017, Article 1; Conference Paper 2). (2) The optimized conditions (NMM concentration, visible light (VL) intensity, and initial bacterial cell density) for NMS to photocatalytic disinfect E. coli under VL irradiation were obtained (Figures 8 to 10). The major reactive charged and oxidative species involving in VLD-PBD by the selected NMS and NP under optimized conditions. The results of scavenger study indicated that all charged (e- and h+) and oxidative (•O2-, •OH and H2O2) involved in VLD-PBD, with the h+ and •O2- as the major reactive species (Figure 6). (3) In addition to E. coli, the VLD-PBD activity of NMS toward three more Gram +ve bacteria (Streptococcus aureus, Microbacterium barkeri, and Bacillus subtilis) were determined (Figure 11). The results indicated that B. subtilis was more resistant to photocatalytic disinfection since it produces spore. The bacterial disinfection mechanism of NMS was determined. (4) A 5-liter laboratory-scale photocatalytic disinfection device (Figure 12) was used. The 5-cycel run experiment (Figure 13) indicates the structure and VLD-PBD ability of NMS are stable. Additional Experiments (1) Thermal treatment of NMS (Xia et al., 2018b Article 4) and NP (Xia et al., 2015; Conference article 3) at high temperature significantly enhanced stability and VLD-PBD activity of NMS (Xia et al. 2018b, Article 4). (2) Though NP and VTM did not have good VLD-PBD ability, the presence of persulfate (PS) lead to the production of sulfate radical (•SO42-), which showed excellent bacterial disinfection ability by NP and VTM even in the absence of light (Xia et al., 2017, Article 2 and Xia et al., 2018, Article 3). (3) We also study the possibility of using iron-containing magnetic composite catalysts, Fe@ZnO0.6S0.4 and CoFe2O4/HTCC for VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection, and the very promising results was obtained (Wang et al., 2018, Article 5; Peng et al., 2017, Article 6).

14100115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100115.value: Among three NMMs, NMS shows the best visible-light-driven (VLD) photocatalytic bacterial disinfection ability. Inspired by the study on thermal treatment to increase the stability and photocatalytic activity of NP, thermal treatment of NMS also enhance its stability and VLD-PBD activity. To materialize the large-scale application of VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection, a pilot-scale study with the thermal treated NMS (and even NP) shall be conducted The addition of persulfate (PS) in VTM (and even NP) suspension generates strong oxidant, •SO42-, which show excellent bactericidal performance. Thus, with the low cost and abundant VTM (and even NP), a bacterial disinfection with these two NMMs shall be studied in details for possible large-scale application. Finally, the potential risk of release unknown compounds from the NMMs renders their use in water treatment. The research team developed two types of iron-containing magnetic catalysts, namely, Fe@ZnO0.6S0.4 and CoFe2O4/HTCC for (i) to compare with their VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection performance with those of NMMs tested in this study, and (ii) to study their potential for the large-scale VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection application.

14100115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100115.value: Three natural magnetic minerals, namely natural magnetic sphalerite (NMS), vanadium-titanomagnetite VTM) and natural pyrrhotite (NP) were tested and compared their visible-light-driven (VLD) photocatalytic bacterial disinfection. Among them, NMS has the best VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection. Thermal treatment of NMS and NP further increases the stability and VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection ability. The potential of NMS (and even NP) to be used in large-scale VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection application is excellent and the feasibility of using NMS system for bacterial disinfection shall be further explored by conducting pilot-scale study. Due to the comparatively low VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection ability of VTM (and even NP), the research proposes to use VTM (and even NP) with the addition of persulfate (PS) to generate very strong oxidant, •SO42-, for efficient bacterial disinfection. Additional study is required to access the feasibility of using VTM-PS system for bacterial disinfection. While the potential release of unknown compound(s) from NMMs renders their use in water disinfection, these NMM-photocatalytic or PS- systems are recommend to be used for non-drinking water bacterial disinfection. The research team also design, fabricate and characterize two additional synthetic magnetic catalysts for VLD photocatalytic bacterial disinfection for drinking water.

14100215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100215.value: Abstract Background Ischemic stroke may cause autonomic dysfunction. The presence of autonomic dysfunction may increase the risk of mortality after stroke. A global bihemispheric impairment of dynamic cerebral autoregulation (CA) in acute and subacute stroke has been found. Impaired CA is also correlated with worse clinical outcome after stroke. Autonomic dysfunction and impaired CA may be cross-linked mechanism playing the same role of regulation of cerebral circulation in stroke. This mechanism may be responsible for impaired cerebral perfusion, metabolic and inflammatory reactions after stroke. Modulation of autonomic function and dynamic CA may be an important target in the development of novel therapeutic interventions for stroke treatment and prevention. External counterpulsation (ECP) is a noninvasive treatment used to improve the perfusion of vital organs, which may benefit ischemic stroke patients. ECP provides a new method to improve cerebral perfusion and collateral blood supply via increasing blood pressure and cerebral blood flow of ischemic stroke patients. Objective We aim to investigate fundamental relationship between autonomic function and dynamic CA after acute ischemic stroke, and evaluate the effect of external counterpulsation (ECP) therapies on autonomic dysfunction and impaired CA following stroke. Methods The proposed study is a prospective, randomised, open-label controlled study. A total of 50 in-patients at Prince of Wales Hospital, with recent large-artery atherosclerotic ischemic stroke within 7 days of ictus will be enrolled. Eligible subjects will be randomly assigned to receiving 35 one-hour sessions of ECP or no ECP, in addition to best available evidence-based medical and rehabilitation treatment. All patients will undertake Ewing’s battery test to evaluate autonomic function and transcranial Doppler (TCD) monitoring in bilateral middle cerebral arteries (MCAs) to evaluate dynamic CA at baseline and 7 weeks after the index stroke. Significance (1) We are the first to explore the association between the autonomic function and CA in stroke, which may help to elucidate the mechanism of impaired cerebral perfusion following stroke. (2) Modulation between autonomic function and dynamic CA may be an important target in the development of new therapeutic interventions, such as ECP therapy, for stroke treatment and prevention in the future. 研究背景：缺血性腦卒中可引起自主神經功能紊亂，自主神經功能紊亂會提高卒中后死亡率；研究已發現在卒中后急性期和亞急性期，動態腦血流自動調節機制在全腦雙側半球均受損，而受損的腦血流自動調節與中風不良預後亦密切相關。由此推測自主神經功能和腦血流自動調節機制在卒中后腦循環調節中的作用同等重要并且可能是相互交聯的。這種交聯機制也許可以解釋卒中后受損的腦灌注、代謝和一系列炎症反應。研發新穎的治療干預手段來調節卒中后患者的自主神經功能和動態腦血流自動調節功能是治療和預防腦卒中一個新的靶點。體外反搏是一種非侵入性的、用於提升機體重要器官血液灌注的機械輔助循環裝置，可以使缺血性腦卒中患者從中受益。我們既往研究發現，通過提升血壓和大腦腦血流速度，體外反搏為增強缺血性腦卒中腦灌注和側枝循環提供了一種新的治療方法。 研究目的：研究急性缺血性腦卒中后自主神經功能和動態腦血流自動調節之間的相互關係；評估體外反搏治療對於卒中后自主神經功能和動態腦血流自動調節的效應。 研究方法：這是一項前瞻性、開放性的隨機對照試驗。總共在香港中文大學威爾斯親王醫院入選50例伴有大血管動脈粥樣硬化病變的缺血性腦卒中發病7天內的患者。合適患者除接受常規口服藥物和康復治療之外，隨機分配到體外反搏治療組和無體外反搏治療組，在基線和卒中7周時，分別接受Ewing’s battery測試評估自主神經功能和經顱多普勒超聲監測雙側大腦中動脈腦血流流速評估動態腦血流自動調節。 研究意義：我們首次探索卒中后自主神經功能調節和動態腦血流自動調節之間的聯繫，這有助闡明卒中后腦灌注受損的機制；研發新穎的治療干預手段，如體外反搏治療，來調節卒中后自主神經和動態腦血流自動調節功能是將來治療和預防腦卒中的重要目標。

14100315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100315.value: 摘要 Bag-1是一個在癌細胞中高度表達的抗凋亡基因，小鼠Bag-1基因只轉錄成一種mRNA，並通過選擇性翻譯編碼三種不同的同源体（isoform），稱為BAG-1S、BAG-1M和BAG-1L。BAG-1在細胞增殖、細胞分化、蛋白降解、細胞遷移和細胞存活等重要的細胞活動中發揮多種重要的功能。迄今為止，Bag-1在癌細胞中的作用已被深入研究，已知Bag-1對癌細胞的存活具有重要的作用，因此Bag-1被認為是一個抗癌藥物作用的潛在靶點。相比之下，Bag-1在胚胎正常發育過程中的作用尚不清楚，因為初步的研究發現Bag-1基因敲除小鼠的胚胎在E12.5-13.5左右就會死亡。在前期研究中我們發現，在小鼠胚胎四肢長骨發育過程中在軟骨內成骨的階段Bag-1有表達，並已報導了Bag-1在這一時期的時間及空間表達譜。此外，我們用E12.5的Bag-1基因敲除小鼠胚胎四肢進行微團培養（micromass culture），發現Bag-1的缺失對軟骨發生（chondrogenesis）過程產生了巨大的影響。因此，我們將集中研究Bag-1在骨和軟骨發育過程中的作用。在本研究中，我們將採用Cre-LoxP基因重組系統構建兩種細胞特異性Bag-1基因敲除小鼠，分別是（1）Col2a1-Cre介導的Bag-1條件性敲除小鼠（Col2a1啟動子被激活後表達Cre重组酶，從而將Bag-1基因的外顯子3移除）以及（2）Osx1-Cre介導的Bag-1條件性敲除小鼠（osterix啟動子被激活後，Bag-1基因的外顯子3將被移除），因此在所有類型的細胞中，只有骨或軟骨細胞不表達Bag-1，其他細胞的Bag-1表達則不受干擾。這一策略可以克服非特異性Bag-1基因敲除小鼠在胚胎發育過程中死亡所造成的限制。利用這兩種條件特異性基因敲除小鼠，我們將通過免疫組化、實時定量PCR和微型CT等方法深入研究Bag-1是如何影響和調控小鼠胚胎以及出生後骨和軟骨發育的。另外，我們將對野生型及Bag-1基因敲除的小鼠胚胎四肢進行微陣列（microarray）以及系統生物學分析，從而得到Bag-1基因調控機制方面的信息。

14100315.label: Realisation of objectives
14100315.value: The overall aim of our study is to investigate the effects of deleting the Bag-1 gene on the development of the skeleton in the mouse. To achieve this, we proposed to generate a Runx2-Cre-mediated Bag-1 conditional knockout mouse model. We had encountered a whole series of unforeseen problems with the Runx2-Cre mice, from import license, problem with breeding and the mice had to be destroyed because they were infected by hepatitis. Because of time limitation, we decided the best thing that we could from the stocks of mice we have on hand was to generate Bag1-flox and Rosa26-CreERT2 knockout mouse instead - which was inducible with tamoxifen, to delete the Bag-1 gene. We also generate embryonic stem cells from these mice and their wild-type counterpart. Applying the transgenic mice and embryonic stem cells, we were successful in addressing our aim on how the absence of Bag-1 affected osteogenesis in vivo. We also examine the absence of Bag-1 expression on growth and osteogenesis at the cellular and molecular levels using our embryonic stem cells. The results of our research are summarized and presented below. GENERATION OF Bag1-flox and Rosa26-CreERT2 KNOCKOUT EMBRYOS: Bag1 knockout mice are embryonic lethal which limits our study on the effects of Bag1 on bone development in vivo. In order to overcome this problem, conditional Bag1 knockout mouse with genotype Bag1(f/f)/ Rosa-Cre(+/-) were generated. The mating of these mice will produce offsprings with Bag1-flox and either with or without Cre locus in the same litter. We found Bag1 homologous knockout embryos died at stage E12.5 stage, hence we controlled the Cre recombinase expression at embryonic E13.5 stage by tamoxifen injection. We successfully harvested Bag1 homologous knockout embryos at E21.5 stage. Genotyping confirmed the double mutants by genotyping PCR. A total of 80 embryos were analysed with 40 wide type and 40 mutant embryos from 13 litters. The successful knockout of Bag1 exon 3 was confirmed by PCR (Fig 1A). The ratio of wild-type and mutant embryos is 1:1 which is equals to the expected ratio of Mendel’s principles of inheritance. We did not observe any genotypically preference between wild-type and mutant embryos. GROSS SKELETAL ANALYSIS REVEALED NORMAL SKELETON IN Bag1 KO FOETUS To examine the role of Bag1 in bone formation during embryogenesis, we knockout Bag1 at E13.5 and examine the skeleton by Alcian blue and Alizarin Red staining just before birth. Alcian blue stain cartilage tissue while Alizarin red detected bone by staining mineralization tissues. Whole skeleton staining shows no observable difference between wild-type and knockout embryos(Fig 1B). Both staining showed Bag1 KO mice with the same body sizes and shapes as their WT littermate controls. To further examine the effect of Bag1 knockout in endochondral ossification during embryogenesis. We compare the length of forelimbs and hindlimbs between WT-type and KO mice(Fig 1C). However, the results also shown that no significant difference between KO and WT embryos. Bag1 KO MICE HAVE REDUCED TRABECULAR BONE MASS: From the skeleton analysis, we did not observe growth difference between WT and Bag1 KO embryos. Then we tried to test whether Bag1 KO affect bone mass by analysing the trabecular bone by micro-computer tomographic. We scanned 10 samples from each group and found that all KO mice showed a small reduction in trabecular bone volume and trabecular bone number (Figs 2 A and B). The trabecular bone thickness and space between trabecular bone was increased in the KO mice compared with WT group. We then confirmed these findings by H&E staining to see the individual cells inside trabecular. Consistently, we observed the bone volume and bone number in Bag1 KO mice were slightly reduced. These findings suggest that Bag1 plays a role in regulating bone development. Bag1 KO in mESC DO NOT AFFECT CELL AFFECT CELL GROWTH BUT HAVE REDUCED SOX2 EXPRESSION: We investigated the role of Bag1 in osteogenesis at the cellular and molecular levels. We generated conditional knockout of Bag1 KO mESC. We also created mESC with genotype Bag1(f/f) LoxP (+/-) and used it as a WT control. Then we induced Bag1 gene deletion in mESC by incubating the cells in 5μM 4-Hydroxytamoxifen for different time points to test for the knockout efficiency. From the semi-quantitative RT-PCR result, we confirmed that we successfully knockout Bag1 transcript expression after 5 days 4-OH tamoxifen treatment (Fig 3A). The Bag1 KO mESCs showed the same cellular morphology as their corresponding WT control mESCs. The cells appeared as small and rounded forming a tightly packed colony with clear margins, while individual cells exhibited high nucleus to cytoplasm ratio. Immunofluorescence staining confirmed that Bag1 expression was significantly reduced in the 4-OH tamoxifen treated cells (Fig 3B). We test the effect of Bag1 KO on cell proliferation by cell proliferation assay and the result revealed that the absence of Bag1 did not affect cell grow (Fig 3C). We further examined the effects of Bag1 KO on the expression of pluripotent gene markers. RT-qPCR and western blot analysis revealed that there was no significant difference in Oct4 and Nanog expressions between WT and Bag1 KO mESCs (Fig 3D). However, the expression of Sox2 was found to be significantly reduced in Bag1 KO mESC (p-value=0.02). The change in Sox2 expression was also confirmed by Western blot analysis. Bag1 KO In mESC RETARDS OSTEOGENESIS AND ASSOCIATED BONE GENE MARKERS EXPRESSION: In our embryo studies, Bag1 KO embryos showed a reduced bone mass and bone trabecular number. Therefore, we investigated the effect of Bag1 during osteogenesis in vitro. We cultured the WT and Bag1 KO mESCs in osteogenic-inducing medium. We first examined alkaline phosphatase activity which is the key enzyme involved in the early stages of bone differentiation. The ALP staining result showed no different between WT and Bag1 KO cells, both exhibited similar level of alkaline phosphatase activity 3 days after osteogenic-induced differentiation (Fig 4A). Then we assayed cell calcium accumulation which may affect the bone density by Alizarin Red staining. The WT mESC gave positive Alizarin Red staining from day 7 post differentiation. In contrast, Bag1 KO mESC derived osteoblast shown significantly delayed in bone mineralization which gave positive Alizarin Red staining from day 14 post differentiation (Fig 4B). Since Bag1 KO revealed a significant delay in calcium accumulation and reduced in bone density both in vivo and in vitro, we next examined bone gene markers expression during osteogenesis. As shown in Fig 4B, the key transcription factor Runx2 started to be express in both WT and KO mESCs from day 14 post-differentiation, while Bag1 KO osteoblasts showed reduced Runx2 expression as compared to WT cell on day 28. Both bone sialoprotein (BSP) and osteocalcin play an important role in bone mineralization and calcium binding. These proteins are important markers for bone maturation. Our RT-qPCR results showed that expression of these genes only increased slightly during the differentiation process in Bag1 KO osteoblasts as compared with WT osteoblasts (Fig 4C). Finally, we tested the extracellular matrix protein collagen type 1 expression by mESC derived osteoblasts. The Western blot results revealed that collagen type 1 expression in Bag1 KO derived osteoblasts was reduced when compared with T osteoblasts. We also established Bag1 KO in mESC retards condrogenesis. Unfortunately, this page do not support figures but we are in the process of generating the manuscript.

14100315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100315.value: Bag1 null mutation in the mouse is embryo lethal and the embryo normally dies around day E12 of development. Therefore, we by pass this impediment by creating a Bag1-flox and Rosa26-CreERT2 mouse. The Bag1 gene could be deleted from homologous mice by Cre recombination, we injected tamoxifen into pregnant homologous Bag1-flox and Rosa26-CreERT2 and wild-type (WT) mice at E13.5, E15.5 and E17.5 to induce Bag1 deletion (KO) and the examined its effect on chondrogenesis and osteogenesis. We determined that in the absence of Bag1 expression the hyaline cartilage limb model developed normally and the subsequent endochondral ossification also occur normally at the gross level. At the gross level, there were no obvious observable difference between the skeleton of Bag1 KO and wild-type mice (all genotypes were validated by qPCR). Nevertheless, microCT-scan imaging revealed that all KO mice showed a small reduction in trabecular bone volume and trabecular bone number at the micro level. Embryonic stem cells (mESCs) were generated from the blastocysts of Bag1 KO and wild-type mice. Bag1 KO do not affect mESCs growth but SOX2 expression was significantly repressed. In addition, The absence of Bag1 expression in mESC significantly retarded osteogenesis and associated bone gene markers expression. In conclusion, we propose that Bag1 maintains SOX2 expression during development and that normal expression level of SOX2 is required for normal progression of chondrogenesis and osteogenesis.

14100315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100315.value: To date, we have investigated the effects of Bag-1 knockout on skeletal development in the mouse during E20 – postnatal period. For further development, we will need to extend the period of our investigation until our Bag-1 knockout mice are at least 1 years old and more. This will allow us to elucidate how the absence of BRE effects bone and cartilage from maturity until aged. We hypothesize the effect of Bag-1 KO will be more dramatic during ageing than during skeletogenesis. The course of action will be to conduct a small sample study into how aging affect the skeleton of Bag1 KO mice and compared with their wild-type counterpart. If our hypothesis is proven correct then we will apply for an external grant for a larger and more comprehensive investigation.

14100415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100415.value: 我們的骨骼肌肌肉在受損后擁有很強的再生能力，這要歸功於附著於骨骼肌纖維上的干細胞。這些細胞通常處於靜息狀態，但當肌肉受損時會迅速激活，增殖並分化形成新的肌纖維來修復受損肌肉。這個過程中的每一步都受到精密的轉錄調控，許多轉錄因子起著至關重要的調控作用。在這一課題中我們計劃利用敲除小鼠模型研究轉錄因子YY1對骨骼肌干細胞和骨骼肌再生的調控原理。初步研究結果表明當YY1在胚胎期肌肉干細胞中被敲出后小鼠的胚胎骨骼肌肌肉發育產生嚴重不足。在成鼠肌肉中的進一步誘導性敲除造成了嚴重的再生障礙和干細胞的增殖滯緩。基於這些初步結果，我們認為YY1轉錄因子在骨骼肌干細胞的定向分化中起著重要調控功能。我們將進行三個目標的研究來揭示它的具體功能和調控機理。這一研究將加強我們對骨骼肌干細胞的轉錄調控的認識，並有可能揭示新的調控分子，為未來治療肌肉再生相關疾病提供依據。

14100415.label: Realisation of objectives
14100415.value: In the original proposal we hypothesized that transcription factor and chromatin regulator, YY1 plays a critical role in SC lineage progression and adult skeletal muscle regeneration. To test this hypothesis 3 specific aims/objectives are proposed: We are pleased to report that all 3 aims have been successfully implemented with favorable outcomes. Aim1: To further characterize the YY1 KO phenotype in muscle regeneration. We crossed mice with the Pax7CreERT2/+allele to YY1f/f mice, to generate Pax7CreERT2/+; YY1f/f mice (termed YY1iKO) to permanently disrupt YY1 function in adult Pax7+ SCs upon the administration of tamoxifen (TM). First, we confirmed the efficacy and specificity of TMX-dependent YY1 deletion in Pax7 positive cells. Loss of YY1 in SCs was readily seen with an ablation efficacy of 94%. Then, to study the role for YY1 in muscle regeneration, we employed a commonly used cardiotoxin (CTX)-induced muscle injury-regeneration model. Tibialis anterior (TA) muscles of Ctrl or YY1iKO animals were subjected to a single CTX injury and then allowed to recover for 3–60 days before analysis of the regenerated tissue. We found YY1iKO muscle showed fewer regenerated fiber 5 day after injury compared to Ctrl muscle. If left to 60 days after injury, Ctrl muscle had fully regenerated, and muscle architecture was largely restored. In contrast, YY1iKO muscle nearly failed to regenerate and reconstitute muscle structure, instead it displayed severe atrophy with markedly reduced fiber size and evident fibrosis. Indeed, 3 days after CTX injection, the number of SCs from YY1iKO vs. Ctrl was largely reduced, indicating the expansion of SC pool in YY1iKO mice had been compromised. Collectively, these results suggested that YY1 deletion leads to severe loss of regenerative capacity, and thus, the expression of YY1 in SCs is essential for timely and proper repair of damaged skeletal muscle tissue after acute injury. To further solidify the impact of YY1 deletion on injury-induced muscle regeneration, we next employed a mdx mouse, in which mutation in dystrophin gene leads to continuous degeneration and regeneration of myofibers accompanied by repeated activation and enhanced turnover of SCs, mimicking the phenotype of human DMD. YY1iKO mice were crossed with mdx mice to generate double KO (dKO) mice. The size and weight of limb muscles were markedly reduced. Further histological examination revealed aggravation of dystrophic phenotypes which were characterized with a reduced number of muscle fibers and an exacerbation of fibrosis and impaired tetanus force in muscles. Moreover, a largely reduced number of SCs was observed in dKO mice compared to the Ctrl. (Fig. 1x-x) Altogether, the above findings (Figure1) led us to conclude that YY1 plays an essential role in maintaining SC pool and enables continuous muscle regeneration under chronic injury. Aim2: To elucidate the cell autonomous defect of SCs from YY1 KO mice. To this end, we first examined YY1 expression dynamics in SCs and found it was lowly expressed in FISCs but quickly induced upon SC activation and its level continued to into 48 h as SCs fully activated and proliferated; this pattern was concomitant with a sharp increase in YY1 mRNA level in the acute SC activation/proliferation phase after increase CTX injection. To further study whether YY1 promote the proliferative expansion of SCs, we performed Pax7/MyoD, Pax7/Ki67 and Pax7/Edu staining in SCs sorted out from the Ctrl and YY1iKO mice and found YY1-depleted SCs showed a marked reduction in the number of Pax7+ MyoD+ or Ki67+ or EdU+ cells at 24h and 48 h in culture, reflecting reflecting a activation and proliferative delay. Moreover, we also isolated single myofibers and performed the above staining in SCs associated with the cultured myofibers, the same conclusion was reached. In addition, the number of Myog+MyoD+ cells on YY1iKO myofibers at day 3 in culture was instead largely reduced. Furthermore, TUNNEL assay revealed no evident apoptosis. Altogether, the above results (Figure2) demonstrated that inducible YY1 deletion in Pax7-expressing SCs causes cell-autonomous defect in their activation and proliferation capacity. Aim3: To explore the mechanisms underlying the cell autonomous defect in YY1 KO SCs. To probe into the molecular mechanisms underlying YY1 influence on SCs activation/proliferation, we performed RNA sequencing (RNAseq) to interrogate the transcriptomic changes caused by YY1 loss. A total of 979 genes were up-regulated whereas 924 down-regulated in ASCs of YY1iKO vs. Ctrl. Gene Ontology (GO) analysis revealed terms such as “cell cycle” and “cell division” are prominent among the down-regulated transcripts, consistent with the observed delay in cell activation/ proliferation. Interestingly, the up-regulated genes were dominant by mitochondrion-related GO terms and related with oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) pathway. Furthermore, when total RNAs from freshly isolated SCs (FISCs) were subject to transcriptomic profiling, mitochondrion-related genes were also markedly enriched in the up-regulated panel of genes. To further pinpoint whether YY1 represses the mitochondrial genes through direct binding and transcriptional regulation, genome-wide chromatin immunoprecipitation coupled with massive parallel sequencing (ChIPseq) was performed on chromatins from ASCs isolated from C57B/L wild-type mice. When intersecting with the 979 genes up-regulated from RNAseq, 90 were found to be likely direct targets of YY1 with binding in promoter regions. Strikingly, these genes were extremely enriched for mitochondrion/OXPHOS-related terms, but “cell cycle” or “cell division” related terms no longer appeared. From both the ChIPseq and ChIP–qPCR validation, these mitochondrial genes were bound by YY1 in their transcriptional start site (TSS) regions, suggesting a direct transcriptional regulation. Indeed, we found that co-binding of Ezh2 with YY1 is evident on a list of mitochondrial genes that were up-regulated in YY1iKO cells as well as the enrichment of H3K27me3 on the same loci. Moreover, re-expression of a wild-type (WT) YY1 restored the elevated mitochondrial genes in iKO SCs, but a mutant YY1 (S365D) and YY1(1–394) lacking DNA-binding activity or lacking DNA-binding domain both failed to do so. Altogether, our findings (Figure3) suggested that YY1 and polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) synergistically act to deposit H3K27me3 marks and repress mitochondrial genes upon SC activation. More interesting, a reduced level of glucose uptaking and glycolytic usage were found in YY1iKO vs. Ctrl, as well as an evident decrease of ATP production. To answer what causes the reduced glycolysis in YY1iKO cells, analyses of RNAseq data revealed a striking down-regulation of a panel of glycolytic genes which encode glucose transporters and enzymes involved in virtually every step of glucose metabolism. Moreover, a key regulator of glycolysis genes, Hif1a protein stability significantly decreased in YY1iKO cells vs. Ctrl. Although no direct binding of YY1 was identified on glycolytic genes and Hif1a TSS regions by ChIPseq, we found YY1 physical interacted with Hif1a in normoxic condition by co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP). Indeed, we found that overexpression of a constitutively active form of Hif1a in YY1iKO cells fully rescued the abundance of glycolytic genes and cell proliferation. Supportively, overexpression of a wild-type Hif1a that could not be stabilized failed to rescue the proliferative defect in YY1iKO cells. Altogether, the above results (Figure4) thus suggested that Hif1a protein destabilization upon YY1 loss might lead to comprised glycolysis, which partially mediates the proliferation defect seen in YY1iKO cells.

14100415.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100415.value: Skeletal muscle satellite cells (SCs) are adult muscle stem cells responsible for muscle regeneration after acute or chronic injuries. The lineage progression of quiescent SC toward activation, proliferation, and differentiation during the regeneration is orchestrated by cascades of transcription factors (TFs). Here, we elucidate the function of TF Yin Yang1 (YY1) in muscle regeneration. Muscle specific deletion of YY1 in embryonic muscle progenitors leads to severe deformity of diaphragm muscle formation, thus neonatal death. Inducible deletion of YY1 in SC almost completely blocks the acute damage-induced muscle repair and exacerbates the chronic injury-induced dystrophic phenotype. Examination of SC revealed that YY1 loss results in cell-autonomous defect in activation and proliferation. Mechanistic search revealed that YY1 binds and represses mitochondrial gene expression. Simultaneously, it also stabilizes Hif1a protein and activates Hif1a-mediated glycolytic genes to facilitate a metabolic reprogramming toward glycolysis which is needed for SC proliferation. Altogether, our findings have identified YY1 as a key regulator of SC metabolic reprogramming through its dual roles in modulating both mitochondrial and glycolytic pathways.

14100415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100415.value: Research from our study not only increases our knowledge in the field of transcriptional regulation but also enhances our understanding of molecular regulation in skeletal muscle stem cell behavior and skeletal muscle development. This may eventually lead to the identification of novel therapeutic targets for muscle relevant disease such as muscular dystrophy and sarcopenia. In the future, to further these findings, we plan to continue the investigation of YY1 in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). Our preliminary results indicated that loss of YY1 in satellite cells leads to aggravated dystrophic phenotypes including increased level of fibrosis which may be associated with severe infiltration of immune cells. We will thus continue to examine the mechanisms underlying the observed phenotype in the next chapter of the study, aiming to identify YY1 as a potential treatment target for DMD.

14100415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100415.value: Skeletal muscle is a form of striated muscle tissue which permits basic functions such as breathing and movement, accounting for ~40% of adult human body weight. Failure of skeletal muscle to develop prenatally leads to embryonic lethality, while the inability to repair or maintain skeletal muscle postnatally leads to a diminished quality of life and sometimes even death. Muscular dystrophy, cachexia, and sarcopenia are examples of deleterious muscle wasting conditions that are prevent in our society. Thus, the ability to regenerate diseased muscle has important medical implications. The cell responsible for muscle regeneration is the satellite cells (SC). The molecular mechanisms that integrate various extracellular signals and intrinsic control to establish the character of SCs during the regeneration are a matter of intense research. Here we have studied and for the first time revealed the function of a transcription factor YY1 in promoting the regenerative capacity of SCs; it will thus enhance our knowledge foundation in the regulatory mechanisms underlying muscle regeneration for future therapeutic development of treating muscle damages and diseases.

14101215.label: Realisation of objectives
14101215.value: (1) To determine whether glaucomatous eyes demonstrating progressive lamina cribrosa (LC) deformation randomized to additional intraocular pressure (IOP) lowering treatment (20% IOP reduction) would have a greater absolute risk reduction of visual field (primary outcome measure) and retinal nerve fiber layer (secondary outcome measure) progression compared with those without progressive LC deformation randomized to the same manner. We have completed Objective 1 and compared the absolute risk reduction of visual field progression between the groups with and without ONH deformation, and the rates of RNFL thinning between the treatment arms in the groups with and without ONH deformation. Only main points are summarized below because of word limit. Please refer to reference 1 for detailed description of the finding (uploaded in Part C). We measured optic nerve head (ONH) deformation instead of lamina cribrosa (LC) deformation because we found that analysis of optic nerve head surface depth (ONHSD) change showed less false positive detection (8.6%) than analysis of the anterior lamina cribrosa surface depth (ALCSD) change (17.1%) (Reference 2), which is related to the fact that the ONH surface is more distinctive for segmentation than the LC surface. Furthermore, we showed that the rate of change of ONHSD was similar to the rate of change of ALCSD over the course of glaucoma progression, and that the risk of development of visual field (VF) progression was also similar between the two; the hazard ratios of VF progression were 1.07 and 1.09 for each micrometer per year increase in the rates of change of ALCSD and ONHSD, respectively (Reference 3). For eyes with posterior ONH displacement, the absolute risk reduction of VF progression was 6.7%; for eyes without posterior ONH displacement, the absolute risk reduction of VF progression was 6.3% (Reference 1). There was no significant difference in the ARRs between the groups with and without posterior ONH displacement. In the group without posterior ONH displacement, the greater proportion of VF progression for eyes randomized to receive additional IOP-lowering treatment (12.2%) compared with those randomized to continued treatment (5.9%) is unexpected (of note, both groups had similar IOP measurements in Phase II – Fig.2B, right panel) (Reference 1), rendering the comparison of ARRs between the groups with and without posterior ONH displacement difficult to interpret. Nevertheless, our finding suggests providing additional IOP-lowering treatment may not necessarily slow or prevent VF progression, which aligns with the finding from previous glaucoma treatment trials. Follow-up studies are needed to investigate whether the absence of posterior ONH displacement over time represents a prognostic factor for a poor treatment response (in terms of RNFL thinning and VF progression) of IOP-lowering therapy. For analysis of retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thinning, we measured the rates of RNFL thinning instead of using an event analysis as described in the original protocol (we have shown that trend analysis of RNFL thickness is more sensitive than event analysis of RNFL thickness) (Reference 4). For the group with posterior ONH displacement, progressive RNFL thinning was observed in eyes randomized to continued treatment (-0.29µm/year, 95% CI: -0.07 to -0.51µm/year), but not in those randomized to receive additional IOP-lowering treatment (-0.11µm/year, 95% CI: -0.38 to 0.16µm/year). For the group without posterior ONH displacement, progressive RNFL thinning was insignificant for both treatment arms (continued treatment: -0.20µm/year, 95% CI: -0.42 to 0.008µm/year; additional IOP-lowering treatment: -0.23µm/year, 95% CI: -0.49 to 0.04µm/year). (2) To compare the rates of visual field progression between eyes with and without progressive LC deformation. By the end of Phase II, 5 eyes developed VF progression in the group with posterior ONH displacement (5/90, or 5.6%) among which 4 eyes received continued treatment (4/45, or 8.9%) and 1 eye (1/45, or 2.2%) received additional IOP lowering (p=0.165). 8 eyes developed VF progression by the end of Phase II in the group without ONH displacement (8/92, or 8.7%) among which 3 eyes received continued treatments (3/51, or 5.9%) and 5 eyes received additional IOP lowering (5/41, or 12.2%) (p=0.287). There was no significant difference in the proportions of eyes with VF progression between the groups with and without posterior ONH displacement (5/90 or 5.6% vs. 8/92 or 8.7%) (P=0.418) (Reference 1). (3) To compare the rates of change of LC deformation before and after initiation of additional IOP lowering treatment. Before initiation of additional IOP-lowering treatment, the rate of change of mean ONHSD was 4.14µm/year (95% CI: 3.04 to 5.24µm/year) in the group with evidence of posterior ONH displacement. Providing additional IOP-lowering treatment halted progressive posterior ONH displacement; the rate of change of ONHSD became insignificant (-1.14µm/year, 95% CI: -3.40 to 1.12µm/year) (Fig.5A, left panel) (Reference 1). By contrast, the ONH surface continued to displace posteriorly in the group randomized to continued treatment and the rate of change of mean ONHSD was 3.59µm/year (95% CI: 0.93 to 6.25µm/year, which was comparable to that before initiation of additional IOP-lowering treatment (Fig.5A, right panel) (Reference 1). (4) To identify risk factors for progressive LC deformation We applied logistic regression analysis to investigate risk factors including age, axial length, central cornea thickness, and baseline ONHSD for posterior ONHSD displacement in Phase I. However, none of these factors were associated with posterior ONSHD displacement (P≥0.547). References 1. Leung CK, Wu Z, Lin C, Lam A, Kam A, Yick D. 14101215.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101215.value: Providing additional intraocular pressure (IOP) lowering treatment upon detection of posterior ONH displacement not only halted further posterior ONH displacement but also preserved the retinal nerve fiber layer and the visual field; there was no significant progressive RNFL thinning and only 2.0% of eyes developed VF progression over 5 years. This is in stark contrast to eyes randomized to continued treatment in which the ONH surface continued to displace posteriorly; there was progressive RNFL thinning (rate of change of RNFL thickness: -0.29µm/year, 95% CI: -0.07 to -0.51µm/year) and 6.3% of eyes developed VF progression. Following the same group of patients with the same treatment strategies for another year beyond the 5-year study period confirms the benefit of additional IOP reduction; the proportion of eyes with VF progression remained at 2.0% in those randomized to receive additional IOP-lowering treatment and increased from 6.3% to 16.7% in those randomized to receive continued treatment (2.0% vs. 16.7%, p=0.017). Such differences in the rates of RNFL thinning and the proportions of VF progression between the treatment arms were not observed in the group without posterior ONH displacement. Our study demonstrates monitoring posterior ONH displacement to be informative to guide IOP-lowering treatment decision in staving off disease progression in glaucoma patients. However, with 8.7% of glaucomatous eyes not showing posterior ONH displacement but developing VF progression, monitoring ONHSD alone would not be effective to guide treatment decision in those patients. Please refer to Reference 1 (uploaded in Part C) for additional details.

14101215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101215.value: Our study suggests that monitoring optic nerve head surface depth (ONHSD) may not be informative to guide intraocular pressure (IOP) lowering treatment decision in eyes with a deep ONH surface where further posterior displacement would be difficult to discern. Along with the same line, it remains unclear when to augment IOP-lowering treatment in eyes without posterior ONH displacement as 8.7% of glaucomatous eyes did not show posterior ONH displacement but developed VF progression. In addition to posterior ONH displacement, eyes with progressive RNFL thinning has also been shown to be at risk of VF progression. We will investigate in a follow-up study whether progressive RNFL thinning can serve as a biomarker to inform treatment decision for glaucoma patients without evidence of posterior ONH displacement.

14101215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101215.value: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness with an estimated 76 million patients worldwide in 2020. Although high intraocular pressure (IOP) is a major risk factor for glaucoma progression, management of glaucoma patients has been complicated by the uncertainty of the target IOP levels at which the integrity of the optic nerve can be preserved for an individual eye. When to increase the intensity of IOP-lowering treatment, particularly when the IOP is within the accepted normal levels, remains an open question. Our 5-year randomized clinical trial has provided evidence to support that providing IOP-lowering treatment upon detection of posterior optic nerve head (ONH) displacement as imaged by optical coherence tomography is effective to halt posterior displacement of the ONH, slow progressive retinal nerve fiber layer thinning, and preserve visual function in glaucoma patients. Monitoring posterior ONH displacement is essential to guide treatment decision in the management of glaucoma patients.

14101315.value: To precisely and comprehensively construct a genetic landscape using whole exome sequencing (WES) in the spectrum of adenocarcinoma of the cervix for both early and advanced stage cancers. 14101315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101315.value: In Hong Kong and mainland China, cervical cancer is one of the most common cancers and major causes of cancer deaths in women. The two major types of cervical cancer are squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma. While the incidence of cervical squamous cell carcinoma have been declining, cervical adenocarcinoma appears to be increasing. The prognosis for advanced cervical adenocarcinoma remains especially poor. Cervical cancer is almost always associated with infection from oncogenic types of human papillomavirus (HPV). However, HPV infection alone is insufficient for malignant transformation, thus, other genetic events independent or in conjunction with HPV infection are required. Precision mapping of genetic alterations in cervical adenocarcinoma can aid in the development of new biomarkers and therapeutic targets which may improve treatment outcomes. In a pilot study, we successfully performed whole exome sequencing (WES) on 15 early stage cervical adenocarcinomas with paired normal samples from Hong Kong Chinese women to map their genetic alterations. We found a heterogeneous genomic landscape but identified several frequently altered genes. We also precisely detected a point mutation of the gene PIK3CA in patient’s plasma DNA using a droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR). This project is to seek novel and/or known variants in all functional, protein coding regions of the genome and in turn make clinically useful genomic assays for molecular monitoring of cervical adenocarcinoma in Chinese women. First, we will perform WES of another 35 early and 50 advanced stage cervical adenocarcinomas paired samples. Combining these with the WES datasets of 15 early stage tumors previously sequenced, a comprehensive genomic map of cervical adenocarcinoma can be drawn to discover potential “driver” genes and HPV integration sites in the initiation and progression of this cancer. Second, targeted deep DNA sequencing (TDS) of stringently selected mutated genes will be performed on 50 cervical adenocarcinomas including 25 early and 25 advanced stage tumours to validate the tumour-specific genomic alterations in this cancer. Common somatic alterations chosen from these signature gene aberrations will be used to develop a panel of ddPCRs as novel molecular tracers to detect and quantify tumour-specific sequence changes in cell free DNA extracted from a series of patients’ plasma during the disease course. These cost-effective TDS of tumour DNA and non-invasive genomic ddPCRs using “liquid biopsies” may eventually be clinically applied to monitor tumour status simply and accurately and to choose individualized targeted therapy for cervical adenocarcinoma in Chinese women. 子宮頸癌是一種常見的婦女惡性腫瘤和死亡起因。子宮頸癌的主要病理組織類型為鱗狀細胞癌和腺癌。雖然子宮頸鱗癌的發病率趨於降低, 但是子宮頸腺癌的發病率反顯增加。尤其是晚期的子宮頸腺癌的預後仍然較差。子宮頸癌大多伴同一些致癌型人類乳頭狀瘤病毒(HPV)的感染, 但是研究顯示單是這種病毒的感染, 並不足以致癌, 需有其它遺傳變異或聯同HPV感染導致子宮頸正常上皮的惡性轉化和子宮頸癌瘤的形成和生長。 精確的子宮頸腺癌中遺傳變異的譜圖旨於發展新的子宮頸腺癌的生物標誌和治療靶標, 進一步提高其治療的效果。在初步研究中, 我們已成功地對15例香港婦女早期子宮頸腺癌進行了全外顯子組測序, 發現了一些常見的遺傳變異, 並創用徵滴數字化PCR測及了患者血漿中的與其腫瘤組織中併存的基因點突變。 開展本研究課題的目的是為了尋找中國婦女子宮頸腺癌中臨床相關的基因組變異。首先會加作25例早期和40例晚期中國婦女子宮頸腺癌細胞的全外顯子組測序, 然後仔細分析基因資料, 選擇最有可能為子宮頸腺癌之”驅動”突變基因, 在50例癌例(早期和晚期癌各25例)中進行深度目標基因測序, 以鑑定子宮頸腺癌中特定的基因變異, 進而優選一組最常見的基因變異, 建立液滴數字化PCR, 檢測子宮頸腺癌病人病程中血漿游離DNA的腫瘤特定性基因序列改變。這些低本高效的腫瘤定向基因測序和非侵入性的基因液滴PCR測定最終有可能被用於中國婦女子宮頸癌的臨床監察和個體化靶標定向治療。

14101315.label: Realisation of objectives
14101315.value: This study addresses two key issues relevant to cervical adenocarcinoma: 1) building a precise genomic landscape of tumors using whole exome sequencing (WES), and 2) combining the genomic signatures and patient outcomes to explore clinically meaningful prognostic markers for this specific subtype of cervical cancer with a ddPCR platform. There is great value in comprehensive characterization of the genomic foundations of cervical adenocarcinoma to guide the development of new prognostic markers and targeted therapeutic regimes to improve the outcome of women suffering from cervical adenocarcinoma. To have well achieved the goals, a couple of sophyscated measures were adopted in this project: 1. The hight accuracy of WES is important in building a genomic landscape in human cancer. Therefore, the WES in all samples in this project was carried out in the Center for Cancer Genome Discovery, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Harvard Medical School using WES pipeline well validated previously in multiple successful cancer studies; a tedious but accurate microdissection was performed in all of fresh-frozen tumour tissue samples to enrich tumour cells to reach a purity of 90% or more for high molecular DNA extraction; unmatched pairs of test and control samples were excluded in WES profile analysis by fingerprinting check; WES data were bio-informatically analysed to reliably reveal gene aberrations using advanced programs developed at Broad Institute (Harvard-MIT) and under supervision by an internationally known cancer bio-informatics specialist, Dr. Gad Getz at Broad Institute, Cambridge, MA, USA. 2. For the translational study, sensitive and specific droplet digital PCRs (ddPCRs) for the detection of single nucleotide mutation of human genes as well as HPV virus quantitation in circulating DNA were used in this project. To increase accuracy and comparability of the gene mutation and HPV quantitation particularly in circulating DNA samples, the same quantified amount of DNA (3 ng) was used in the all ddPCRs. Shortage of the project: In this project, clinical samples were collected. However, some study patients missed follow-up and did not provide a complete set of plasma samples (required to be collected prior to any treatment, and 6, 12, and 18 months after treatment) for the ddPCR assays. How to improve patient compliance in the longitudinal study is still a challenge. In the future studies, it may be considered to call and remind the patients to take follow-up one week before the appoint date by research assistant/out-patient clinic nurse.

14101315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101315.value: The precision whole exome sequencing (WES) profiles in cervical adenocarcinoma in Chinese women was achieved. The concised analysed WES data obtained from this project display that most gene aberrations residing in tumours appear as significant intra- and inter-tumor diversity, reflecting their genetic heterogeneity where recurrent gene abnormalities exist, but certain mutations potentially provide statistically significant information to develop precision management of this subtype of cervical cancer. In the listed 61 genes with non-synonymous mutations in the tumor, the majority (67%) are present in Catalogue of Somatic Mutations in Cancer (COSMIC) and many overlap the OncoKB Cancer Gene list (https://oncokb.org/cancerGenes ) also. Notably, 19 genes with mutations are novel. The differences between genomic alterations revealed in our study and those shown in cBioPortal may represent ethnicity and geographic diversities along with individual tumor heterogeneity in the genome of this tumor and the diversity of histologic types of cervical cancer. This is important data to add to contribute to the field to establish the background frequency of mutations within ethnic and geographic groups and assist identification of actionable mutations from background. The most significant finding in the study is that measurement of three missense point substitution mutations in PIK3CA: E542K, E545K and H1047R using ddPCR is to be predictive of recurrence and shorter survival in a subgroup of cervical adenocarcinoma. In the present study, the somatic point mutations of KRAS, OXT and PDE appeared in low frequency either in tumor or in circulating DNA samples in this set of patients. KRAS is a dominant gene with alterations shown in COSMIC and cBioPortal. There are multiple hot spots of KRAS mutation while only one spot p.G12Vwas examined in the present study due to the limited amount of circulating DNA available in sample pool. Therefore, a big technical challenge remains to develop ultrasensitive technologies able to detect very low amounts of tumor cfDNA in the “sea” of normal cfDNA in blood samples. KRT6A point substitution mutation was detected in 50% patients in this study. Though its mutation was not associated with clinico-pathologic features, it may be worthwhile exploring its pathologic functions in cervical adecnocarcinoma and the potential to be a therapeutic target to improve cervical adenocarcinoma treatment.

14101315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101315.value: Though the findings have obtained from the present project are important to improve outcome of patients with cervical adenocarcinoma in Chinese women, further researches are to be conducted. 1. Expand the PIK3CA mutation detection in tumour and circulating DNAs of patients with cervical adenocarcinoma in multiple centers to further confirm the usability of this molecular prognostic marker in this tumour. 2. Further explore the other potential genes with aberration(s) in cervical adenocarcinoma as implicated in the precision genomic landscape from this project to be confirmed as effective prognostic marker and therapeutic target. Together with the PIK3CA mutations, hopefully, a panel of marker and target would specially cover almost all cervical adenocarcinoma. 3. As the yield of circulating DNAs is relatively low, further develop simple, affordable but highly sensitive and specific mutation detection methods are desperately required to be used in liquid biopsy in the disease course. 4. The first PIK3CA inhibitor approved by US FDA used in a sub-group of breast cancer patients may also seek clinical trial of it to be applied in the therapy of cervical adenocarcinoma with PIK3CA mutations to improve outcome: prolong survival time, particularly, in advanced stage tumour.

14101315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101315.value: This project was to exolore genomic aberrations in cervical adenocarcinoma. Using precision whole exome sequencing and high quality DNA obtained from “pure” microdissected cancer cells, a precise genomic landscape in cervical adenocarcinoma that is a clinically important sub-type of cervical cancer in Chinese women was built. These genomic profiles helped reveal mutated genes that might be predictive molecular prognostic markers as well as therapeutic targets in the cervical adenocarcinoma. The translational study at the first time identified that detection of PIK3CA gene mutations combining tumour and circulating DNA assessment using robust droplet digital PCR (polymerase chain reaction) is predictive of recurrence and shorter survival in a sub-group of cervical adenocarcinoma. Stratification of patients with cervical adenocarcinoma regardless of stage based on the PIK3CA gene mutation can be implemented in a clinical setting able to perform ddPCR assay, and may offer the possibility of tailoring the aggressiveness of the regime to the individual patient. In addition, appropriate PIK3CA inhibitor treatment can be tried in the patients with PIK3CA mutations detected in their tumour and/or their circulation to reduce tumour recurrence and patient survival.

14101515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101515.value: 宮頸癌是全世界婦女第四常見癌症，是由高危型人類乳突病毒(HPV)持續性感染引起的。其中，58型雖只在全球少部分宮頸癌中被發現（<3%），但在東亞地區卻與13-29%的宮頸癌相關。 HPV58型在東亞地區呈现出特殊的的種族及地域偏好性的原因未明。我們最近進行了一項國際性的HPV58型流行病學研究，收集了橫跨美洲、非洲、歐洲和亞洲15個地區共401個研究樣本，並發現一個對子宮頸癌及子宮頸皮下腫瘤III級的發展相關的變異株（E7 T20I/G63S）。同時我們也發現這變異株在東亞地區較為常見。此流行病學的觀察結果或可解釋為何HPV58型在東亞地區造成較嚴重的疾病負擔，對診斷和疫苗開發有重要意義。在應用於臨床治療前，我們需通過體外實驗進一步驗證這結果。 具體目標： 我們將透過以下方法研究HPV58 E7 T20I/G63S變異株的致癌性： 1. 闡明并比較HPV58 E7 T20I/G63S變異株與樣本型及其他常見變異株的永生化、惡性轉化和浸潤性的能力﹔ 2. 描述并比較其E7蛋白的亞細胞定位及穩定性﹔ 3. 描述并比較其E7蛋白與關鍵的細胞靶點（包括pRb、p107、p130、Akt、EZH2和MMP）之間的相互作用。 預期結果： 本研究將取得現時未知、與HPV58 E7變異株致癌特色有關的一系列綜合數據。 最終目標： 我們的研究將驗證較早前的流行病學觀察結果，證實一種於東亞地區較常見的HPV58型變異株確實擁有較高的致癌性。本項目不僅有助於我們理解HPV58型在東亞有更高疾病負擔的原因，也對HPV診斷和疫苗開發有重大意義。

14101515.label: Realisation of objectives
14101515.value: Objective 1: Characterize and compare the immortalizing, transforming, pro-invasive and tumourigenic abilities of HPV58 E7 T20I/G63S with prototype and other naturally occurring variants. A. Proposed approaches: We proposed to establish stable cell lines of human keratinocytes expressing HPV58E7 prototype and natural variants, namely V1 (T20I/G63S), V2 (G41R/G63S) and V3 (T74A/D76E), and assess the following oncogenic events: (i) Immortalization – by evaluating the length of time for the cells to reach passage 65 and doubling time. (ii) Transformation – by evaluating the ability of cells to resist anoikis, grow anchorage independently and form tumour in mice. (iii) Cell proliferation and apoptosis – through WST-1 assay, in-situ BrdU and Annexin V-PI staining. (iv) Cell motility and invasiveness – through Matrigel invasion assay. B. Results achieved: (i) HPV58 E7 T20I/G63S variant possesses a higher immortalization and transforming ability than prototype and other variants:- We found that 58E7 prototype and V1 increased the colony-forming ability of primary murine epithelial cells and enhanced the anchorage-independent growth of NIH-3T3 cells, indicating a higher immortalizing and transforming potential, respectively. (ii) Establishment of murine-derived primary HPV58E7-expressing stable cell lines:- We established stable cell lines with HPV58E7 prototype and its variants expressed in primary epithelial cells extracted from baby rat kidney cells (BRK). These cell lines are designated as BRK-HPV58E7P (58E7P), BRK-HPV58E7V1 (V1), BRK-HPV58E7V2 (V2) and BRK-HPV58E7V3 (V3). BRK-pcDNA3.1 cells was served as a negative control. These cells were sub-cultured under continuous antibiotic selection up to 30th passages. We observed no sign of replicative senescence and growth crisis. These immortalized stable cell lines were used for cell proliferation, migration and invasion, and tumour formation assays. (iii) HPV58 E7 prototype and T20I/G63S variant induced high cell proliferation:- We compared the ability of 58E7 prototype and its variants to induce cell proliferation using Cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) or WST assays. As this assay is sufficient to measure cell proliferation, we did not perform in-situ BrdU assay. Our results showed that 58E7P and V1 possessed a higher ability than V2 and V3 to induce cell proliferation. Nonetheless, we observed a slightly higher proliferation ability of 58E7V1 compared to prototype. (iv) HPV58E7 T20I/G63S achieved a greater ability to migrate and invade:- We assessed the ability of HPV58E7 prototype and its variants to induce cell migration and invasion using a transwell Matrigel invasion chamber. We found that cell migration and invasion of V1 was approximately 6-fold higher than 58E7P. On the other hand, migration and invasion ability of V3 was lower than 58E7P. V2 possessed a comparable migration and invasion ability to 58E7P. HeLa (positive), MCF-7 and BRK-pcDNA3.1 (negative) cells were included as controls. (v) HPV58E7 T20I/G63S variant induced larger tumours in mice:- We examined the ability of HPV58E7 prototype and its variants to form tumours in athymic nude mice. We found that V1 formed larger and lobular tumours, with multiple small tumours in the vicinity of the main tumour compared to 58E7P. On the other hand, we observed that 58E7V2, V3 and pcDNA3.1 cells formed smaller tumours compared to 58E7P. C. Problem encountered and solutions: We proposed to use human keratinocytes, however we encountered technical obstacles when expressing HPV58 E7 prototype and its variants in primary human keratinocytes, HeKa (purchased from ATCC). We used various transfection methods, including cationic polymer polyethylenimine (PEI), TransIT (Mirus Bio), and commercially available liposome-mediate reagents, including Lipofectamine® LTX (Thermo Fisher Scientific), Lipofectamine® 3000 (Thermo Fisher Scientific), FuGENE HD and ViaFect (Promega), electroporation using Amaxa® human keratinocyte nucleofector® Kit with the Nucleofector™ 2b Device (Lonza, Switzerland) and retroviral transduction system (kindly provided by Prof. John Doorbar, University of Cambridge). In our hand, all these methods yielded less than 10% transfection efficiency. Due to low transfection efficiency, we were unable to establish stable cell lines to compare oncogenic events mediated by HPV58E7s. In order to overcome this, we used primary cells extracted from 9‐day‐old Wistar Hannover rats. We chose this approach mainly because of the greater transfection efficiency. We believe this is an appropriate method, as it has been well-established and widely used in many laboratories worldwide to study oncogenic events mediated by HPV oncoproteins. Besides, we did not perform study to elucidate the ability of the HPV58E7 stable transformants to resist anoikis and undergoing apoptosis. During the entire experiments, we monitored the cell growth carefully and we did not see any sign of the cells undergoing crisis. In addition, for each passage, we stained cells with trypan blue during cell counting, we did not observe any change in the number of apoptotic cells among the transformants. Objective 2: Elucidate and compare their subcellular localization and stability. A. Proposed approaches: We proposed to exogenously express HA-tagged HPV58E7 prototype and its variants in HPV-null cells, to study: (i) Subcellular localisation in HaCaT cells via immunofluorescence assays (ii) Protein half-life through cyclohexamide-chase assays. B. Results achieved: We found that HPV58E7 prototype and its variants localized predominantly in the nucleus with punctate pattern, and shared a similar protein half-life of approximately 19 mins. Objective 3: Delineate and compare specific E7 key functions by examining their interactions with host cellular targets, including pRb and related pocket proteins (p107, p130), Akt, EZH2 and MMPs. A. Proposed approaches: We proposed to study the ability of HPV58E7 prototype and its variants to degrade pRB, as well as their effect on AKT, EZH2 and MMPs activity, by co-expressing these E7 target proteins with E7 in HPV-null cells. The levels of these E7 target proteins were analysed by Western blotting. B. Results achieved: (i) HPV58E7 T20I/G63S degraded pRB more promptly than other variants, alike prototype HPV58E7 prototype and V1 (T20I/G63S) preferentially induced greater degradation of pRb than other variants. HPV58E7 wild-type and variants degraded p130 and p107 at a similar strength. (ii) HPV58E7 did not affect AKT, EZH2 and MMPs activity. AKT activity: We co-expressed HA-tagged AKT together with either 58E7 prototype or V1 into HEK293 cells. We included HPV16E7 a positive control. We serum-starved the cells for 24 hrs, and then added 20% fetal bovine serum (FBS) for 30 mins to activate AKT in the cells. In our hands, we were unable to reproduce the 16E7-induced increased AKT activity (phospho-AKT or pAKT) as reported by others (Pim et al., 2005; Menges et al., 2006). We also did not observe an effect of 58E7 prototype and V1 on AKT activity. MMP2 and MMP9 activity: We overexpressed 16E7 and 58E7 prototype in HPV-null human osteosarcoma cells, U2-OS. We found that the level of MMP2 and MMP9 in cells transfected with 16E7 and 58E7 were comparable to mock-transfected cells. We also performed the same experiment using HEK293 and HPV-null cervical cancer cells, C33A. We consistently found that 16E7 and 58E7 did not have any effect on MMP2 and MMP9. EZH2 activity: We overexpressed 16E7 and 58E7 prototype in HEK293 cells. From our immunoblots, we found that overexpression of 16E7 or 58E7 did not have any effect on EZH2. C. Problems encountered: This objective was achieved with minimal obstacles. As we found that HPV16E7, 58E7 prototype and V1 have no effect on AKT, EZH2, MMP2 and MMP9 activity, we did not perform further analyses to examine 58E7 V2 and V3, which possess weaker oncogenic property than prototype and V1.

14101515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101515.value: Human papillomavirus (HPV) 58 is the third most commonly detected HPV type in cervical cancers among Eastern Asians. Our previous international epidemiological studies revealed that a HPV58E7 natural variant, T20I/G63S (designated as V1), was associated with a higher risk of cervical cancer. In order to verify our epidemiological findings, we performed a series of phenotypic and molecular assays to compare the oncogenic properties of HPV58E7 prototype with V1, as well as two other commonly found variants, G41R/G63D (V2) and T74A/D76E (V3). V2 and V3 had weaker association with cervical cancer risk. We performed phenotypic assays to compare the ability of HPV58E7 prototype and its variants to induce hallmarks of cancer: immortalization, transformation, proliferation, migration, invasion and tumour formation. We found that, V1 possessed a higher immortalizing and transforming ability. Using 58E7 stable cell lines, we demonstrated that 58E7 prototype and V1 possessed a higher ability to induce cell proliferation compared to V2 and V3. However, 58E7 prototype and V1 showed a different capacity in inducing other hallmarks of cancers. We found that V1 induced 6-fold greater cell migration and invasion, and induced 2-fold larger tumour in mice than that of 58E7 prototype. While V2 and V3 possessed a weaker ability in inducing cell proliferation, invasion and tumour formation than that of 58E7 prototype. From our molecular assays, we observed that amino acid variation within 58E7 variants did not affect the protein stability and their nuclear localisation. We also investigated the ability of 58E7 prototype and its variants to degrade the tumour suppressor retinoblastoma protein (pRB), the most prominent target of E7. We found that V1 possessed an increased ability to degrade pRb, hence, its greater oncogenicity than prototype and other variants. When assessing the effect of 58E7 prototype and its variants to the other E7 target proteins, in our hands, we did not find any effect of 16E7 and 58E7s on AKT activity, nor on the level of EZH2, MMP2 and MMP9 expression. Taken all together, our findings showed the genuine greater oncogenicity of HPV58E7 T20I/G63S (V1) in promoting hallmarks of cancer, partly through perturbation of pRB function, thereby, contributing to its higher association to cancer risk.

14101515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101515.value: Our studies provided experimental evidences to explain our previous epidemiological findings. We found that HPV58E7 T20I/G63S (V1) possessed a higher association to cervical cancer risk. Our experimental data showed the greater ability of V1 in promoting hallmarks of cancers, further shed light to the bona fide oncogenicity of V1. However, during HPV-driven carcinogenesis, E7 often works collaboratively with E6. In addition, the long control region (LCR), which has a role in HPV genome expression, also carry polymorphism. Therefore, the role of polymorphism of long control region (LCR) and E6 should not be neglected. Future studies should put forward the co-operation of HPV58 LCR, E6 and E7 natural variants to gain a full understanding on how these genetic variations affect HPV58 life cycle and the ability of HPV58 variants in promoting hallmarks of cancers in a more physiological setting. Their oncogenic properties can be further validated through a series of phenotypic and molecular assays. Most importantly, the assays should be performed using primary keratinocytes originated from Hong Kong population. This will allow us to have a comprehensive understanding on the role of HPV58 in inducing carcinogenesis under a physiologically relevant condition.

14101515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101515.value: Cancer arise from the uterine cervix is the fourth most common cancer affecting women worldwide. Infection by human papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the major contributors to cervical cancer. There are 15 types of human papillomavirus (HPV) that can cause human cancers. In Eastern Asia, HPV58 is the third most common type detected in cervical tissues. When one is infected by HPV, the virus expresses two major proteins, namely E6 and E7, that can drive cancer progression. From natural observational studies, we found a natural HPV58E7 variant, designated as V1, has a higher association to cervical cancer risk. In order to understand the underlying mechanism on how V1 contributes to higher cancer risk, we performed a series of experiments to assess its ability in altering normal cells to become cancerous. We found that in the presence of V1 expression, the cells gain greater ability to grow uncontrollably and form more aggressive tumour, through suppressing normal function of a tumour suppressor, retinoblastoma (pRB) protein. This study enriches our understanding on why HPV58 poses a higher disease burden in East Asia, which has important implications on the design of preventative and management strategies for cervical cancer in this region.

14102315.label: Realisation of objectives
14102315.value: In the original proposal we proposed to identify and functionally characterize super enhancer associated RNAs (seRNAs) in skeletal myogenesis. Three aims were proposed. We are pleased to report that all aims have now been successfully implemented with favorable outcomes. Aim 1: To identify TFs important for regulating SE activity. In this Aim, we proposed to identify TF assembly and TF hotspots in SEs. All the analyses have been successfully completed with satisfying results. Briefly, we first performed enhancer/SE identification in both C2C12 proliferating MBs and fully differentiated MTs based on H3K27ac, H3K4me1 and p300 signals. As a result, a total of 406 and 759 SEs together with 8389 and 11052 TEs were identified in MB and MT, respectively. In keeping with the notion that SEs are more active than TEs, we noticed histone marks known to be associated with enhancer activity displayed higher occupancy on SEs than TEs. Next, we applied HOMER to predict an array of TFs enriched within SE constituents in MBs and MTs. A large proportion of the top-ranked motifs are previously known key regulators in the respective cell stage. Leveraging a number of ChIP-seq datasets for TFs (14 and 15 from MB and MT, respectively), we observed a large number of the TFs (7 in MB and 12 in MT) exhibit enriched binding in the enhancer regions. To examine the degree of co-association between TFs, a heat map was generated based on the correlation of binding loci between each TF pair within all the SE repertoires. One distinct combinational module was identified in MT by unsupervised clustering involving MyoD, Myogenin, Tcf3, Tcf12, Pbx, Mef2d, and Foxo3. Last, we defined a short genomic region co-bound by no less than 4 or 5 of the above analyzed TFs in MB or MT, respectively as a TF hotspot, which has led to the genome-wide identification of a total of 7790 and 22 827 hotspots in MB and MT with the median size of 428 and 403 bp. Among these, 603 hotspots in MB are located in SEs, with around 75.4% of SEs (306/406) being occupied by at least one hotspot (25.4% for TEs (2134/8389)); 2342 SE hotspots in MT were detected to occupy 94.6% of SEs (718/759) compared to 29.7% for TEs (3281/11 052). These findings are included in our publication, Peng et. al. 2017 Nucleic Acids Research. Aim 2: To identify and characterize seRNAs. In this Aim, we proposed to perform total RNA-seq and GRO-seq and repeat the seRNA identification with the enhanced RNA transcriptome data obtained in this aim. All the experiments and analyses have been successfully completed with satisfying results. First, GRO-seq was performed with proliferating (Myoblast, MB) and differentiating (Myotube, MT, differentiated for 48hr) C2C12 cells in two biological replicates. The generated data were analyzed to define transcription units, which were then overlapped with enhancer repertoire previously classified in C2C12 cells. As a result, a total of 16,835 TE associated RNAs (teRNAs) together with 6,698 SE associated RNAs (seRNAs) were obtained in MB cells; similarly, 14,997 teRNAs and 7,252 seRNAs were defined in MT cells. When examining their expression dynamics during MB differentiation, we found 1,274 were significantly up-regulated in MT vs MB and 1,627 down-regulated, while the majority remain unaltered (n = 24,184). Next, attempting to categorize eRNAs, we applied an integrated analysis leveraging multiple RNA-seq datasets using total or PolyA+ RNAs from C2C12 cells. In brief, RNA transcripts were assembled from total RNA-seq to generate lincRNA catalogue. When overlapped with enhancer repertoire, it yielded a catalogue of 1,746 teRNAs and 1,747 seRNAs in MB, of which 803 teRNAs and 819 seRNAs can be detected in PolyA+ RNA-seq. Similarly, a total of 2,406 teRNAs and 2,275 seRNAs were defined in MT among which 965 and 1,016 are found in PolyA+ RNA-seq. Consistent with the common notion, many of them are divergently transcribed; the transcription start site (TSS) of divergent pairs were further categorized into three classes: Bi-directional (Bi)-stable (both directions yield stable transcripts detected by total RNA-seq), Uni-directional (Uni)-stable (only one direction yields stable transcript) and Unstable (can only be detected by GRO-seq). Expectedly, the majority of eRNAs are unstable; very small fraction are Bi-stable. Our results showed that Bi-stable eRNAs display strongest GRO-seq profiles and Pol II binding compared to Uni-stable and Unstable ones. The distinction is also prominent in histone marks and TF binding. These findings are included in our recent publication, Zhao et. al. Nature Communications, Accepted. AIM 3: To study seRNA regulation and function. In this aim, we proposed to reveal the interplays between key TFs and seRNAs expression and to study the functional roles of the selected seRNAs. All the experiments and analyses have been successfully completed with satisfying results. First, applying HOMER, we predicted potential TF binding motifs enriched within the 2 kb window of TSSs of eRNAs that are highly expressed in MB or MT (log2 (Fold change) > 2 or <-2 with adjusted P value < 0.05). A proportion of the top-ranked motifs are bound by known key regulators in the respective cell stage. In addition, analyzing the available TF ChIP-seq datasets from C2C12, we noticed convergence of multiple TFs at TSSs of eRNAs in both MB and MT. One distinct combinational module unveiled in MT involves MyoD, MyoG, TCF12, TCF3, MEF2D, PBX1 and FoxO3. We next concentrated on MyoD and dissect its regulatory role in eRNA transcription. Our analyses revealed evident signals around MyoD binding sites at enhancers with the read density much higher on SEs than TEs. Moreover, for up-regulated eRNAs in MT vs MB, MyoD binding is sharply enhanced at their cognate TSSs. To strengthen the above findings, GRO-seq was performed in MyoD knockout (MyoD-/-) cells. In response to MyoD loss, the expression of MT eRNAs (both teRNAs and seRNAs) was dramatically diminished, but modestly enhanced for MB eRNAs. Next, to study eRNAs functions, we selected two seRNAs, seRNA-1 and seRNA-2 which were among the highest induced during differentiation. They were originated from two SEs on mouse chromosomes 15 and 3 and bi-directionally transcribed as shown by GRO-seq. PolyA+ RNA-seq however only captured uni-directional transcripts in the SEs respectively; they were barely detectable in MB but highly expressed in MT. To test this functional scenario in seRNAs in myogenesis, we used siRNA to deplete seRNA-1 and seRNA-2 and interrogated the effect on the neighboring genes within ± 150 kb window. Among the nine genes surrounding seRNA-1, knock-down of seRNA-1 resulted in a decrease in levels of two nearest mRNAs, Mb and Apol6. Similarly, silencing of seRNA-2 led to reduction of the neighboring genes, Atp1a1 and Igsf3. Through in vitro and in vivo functional characterization, we demonstrated seRNA-1 and seRNA-2 are pro-myogenic factors. Last, to search for undefined molecular mechanisms underlying seRNAs mediated transcriptional activation of target genes, we sought to identify protein partners of seRNAs through RNA pull-down assay. We proved seRNAs specifically binds to hnRNPL protein and a CAAA tract is pinpointed in seRNA-1 to be crucial in mediating the interaction and function of seRNA-1/hnRNPL, thus modulating neighboring gene expression both in vitro and in vivo. All these findings are included in our recent publication, Zhao et. al. Nature Communications, Accepted.

14102315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14102315.value: Two papers directly from the proposed study have been published. In “MyoD- and FoxO3-mediated hotspot interaction orchestrates super-enhancer activity during myogenic differentiation”, we demonstrated distinct SE landscapes and their progressive decommissioning/assembly during the course of differentiation. Taking advantage of the available ChIP-seq datasets, we identified a myriad of TFs that co-bind with MyoD thus are critical for driving the hotspot formation, among which we showed that FoxO3 represents a previously unknown ancillary TF that is recruited to the MyoD binding sites through their physical association and subsequently stabilizes MyoD binding. We further demonstrated the importance of MyoD and FoxO3 interaction and cooperativity in driving global hotspot formation and SE activation. Furthermore, we dissected hotspot interactions on an SE associated with Myogenin locus as well as the key function of MyoD and FoxO3 in orchestrating the hotspot interaction and hierarchy. In “MyoD induced enhancer RNA interacts with hnRNPL to activate target gene transcription during myogenic differentiation”, we provide the compendium of eRNAs and categorize different eRNA subfamilies through comparing data from global run-on sequencing (GRO-seq), PolyA+ and total RNA-seq in differentiating myoblast cells. We demonstrate the presence of a variety of eRNA species with different features of expression level, Pol II association, histone modifications and TF binding etc. We also show the essential role of MyoD in inducing eRNAs production upon myogenic differentiation. Using two eRNAs generated from SEs, seRNA-1 and seRNA-2 as paradigm, we further show that seRNAs induced upon differentiation function to promote myogenesis in vitro and in vivo. In depth dissection of how seRNA-1 regulates the target gene Mb transcription leads to the revelation that seRNA-1 specifically binds to hnRNPL protein. A CAAA tract is pinpointed to be crucial in mediating the interaction and function of seRNA-1/hnRNPL, thus modulating neighboring gene expression both in vitro and in vivo. In total 15 publications have been generated with this funding acknowledged (PartC8). Our findings were highly received when presented in international and local conferences/seminars (PartC9). One Postdoc Fellow, Dr. Karl K. So was trained under the support of this grant. One PhD students, Dr. Laura X. Peng was also trained under the grant (PartC10). Through this work, we have also developed active collaboration with Prof. John T. Lis at the Cornell University; Prof. Edwin Cheung at University of Macau; Prof. Zhenguo Wu at HKUST; Prof. Huatng Wang, Department of Orthopeadics and Traumatology, CUHK. (PartC11).

14102315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14102315.value: Research from our study not only increases our knowledge in the field of enhancer, enhancer RNAs, but also enhances our understanding of molecular regulation in skeletal muscle stem cell behavior and skeletal muscle development. This may eventually lead to the identification of novel therapeutic targets for muscle relevant disease such as muscular dystrophy and sarcopenia. In the future, to further these findings, we plan to continue the investigation of enhancers, eRNAs, and eRNAs associated RBPs in the muscle cells in the context of normal muscle development, acute and chronic injury induced muscle regeneration and muscle aging. We will also continue to examine the interplay between eRNAs and transcription factors or RNA binding proteins in myogenesis.

14102315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14102315.value: Human genome likely contains hundreds of thousands of enhancers that can stimulate RNA transcription over long-ranges. Unraveling the dynamic communication of remote enhancers with target promoters in the specification of cellular identity is one of the outstanding mysteries of modern biology. Super-Enhancer (SE) is a brand-new concept to define extended regulatory sequences that are characterized by the enriched binding of clusters of key transcription factors and high tissue or cell type specificity. However, many questions remain to be answered regarding SE formation and activation. Of particular interest, high level of RNAs was found to transcribe at SEs but it is completely unknown regarding to their biogenesis and functional roles. Here in this project we defined enhancer/SE as well as enhancer RNA landscapes during the course of muscle differentiation and studied their regulation and functions in muscle cells. In the long run, we hope this will serve as a starting point for the development of new therapeutic approaches for treating muscle related human diseases.
