14107415.label: Major findings and research outcome
14107415.value: In this research project, our major study findings and research outcome point to an unrecognised physiological role of FGF21and/or its analogue (CVX343) in the regulation of islet lipid metabolism and, more importantly, its protective effects against lipotoxicity-mediated beta-cell dysfunction and apoptosis in obese conditions. In this context, our mechanism-driven result data provide a scientific basis for FGF21/analogues being able to reduce the pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction and apoptosis with potentially therapeutic implications (see also attached our major original data from the three published papers in the context of FGF21 and islet functions in Part C). Our significant findings and research impact are summarised as follows: 1. First of all, our project findings indicate that FGF21/analogue downregulates islet cell lipid accumulation, probably via activation of AMPK-ACC and PPARalpha/gamma signalling pathways, while reducing the beta-cell apoptosis under lipotoxic conditions. These in vitro/ex vivo/in vivo data suggest that FGF21 activation is protective against lipotoxicity-induced abnormalities in beta-cell function and survival (see Xie et al. 2019). 2. In addition, our project results indicate that glucotoxicity-induced FGF21 activation modulates islet cell autophagic cell deadth via the inhibition of AMPK signalling, thus underscoring the clinical significance for the potential use of FGF21/analogue as a pharmacological target for the treatment of obesity and its associated diseases, notably T2DM (see Cheng et al. 2019). 3. Furthermore, our project results postulate that alcohol ingestion induces FGF21 resistance and thus leads to pancreatic islet dysfunction and apoptosis that are concomitant with increased risk of T2DM pathogenesis (see Yang et al. 2020).

14107415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107415.value: It has been known that FGF21 and irisin are two of the major myokines, predominantly derived from skeletal-muscle while both of them have critical roles in the homeostasis of glucose and fat metabolism as well as pancreatic cell growth and survival. Against this background, we posit that the potential crosstalk and synergism of these two potent metabolic hormones may have protective effects against pancreatic cell dysfunction and cell death, notably observed in the pancreatic beta-cell and duct/acinar cells, thus implicating its dysreguation/abnormalities in T2DM and pancreatic cancer. As far as the clinical merit and application, it is of great interest to further investigate and develop this research direction in the context of FGF21 and irising-mediated metabolic diseases. If confirmed, physical activity and endurance exercise induced release of myokines may provide a scientific basis for the cost-effective prevention and treatment of metabolic diseases, notably obesity/obesity-related metabolic disorders, such as pancreatic cancer and diabetes.

14107415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107415.value: FGF21 is a potent hormone that positively regulates glucose and lipid homeostasis as well as cell growth and death. Given that abnormalities in islet cell function and survival are the core pathogenesis of type 2 diabetes (T2DM), the protective mechanisms of FGF21 on lipotoxicity-mediated beta-cell dysfunction and apoptosis are of clinical relevance. In light of our study findings, we conclude that FGF21 can reduce high palmitate-induced accumulation of triglyceride and free fatty acids so as to enhance glucose-stimulated insulin secretion via stimulation of AMPK-ACC pathway in mouse islets, INS-1E cells and isolated islets from lipotoxicity-induced obesity mice. Meanwhile, PPARδ/γ signaling is the mediator of FGF21 function. In addition, FGF21 reverses high palmitate-induced cell apoptosis both in islets and INS-1E cells through the regulation of Birc3 expression. In vivo experimental data with FGF21 KO mice and FGF21 analogue further show that FGF21 is key to improving glucose homeostasis and insulin resistance impaired by high-fat-fed diet. Our data provide an unrecognized signaling pathway of FGF21 in lipotoxicity-treated islets and lipotoxicity-induced obese mice. These results provide a mechanistic underpinning of FGF21/analogue-mediated activation of AMPK/PPARδ/γ pathway that may be a novel pharmacotherapeutic target for lipotoxicity-induced β-cell dysfunction and apoptosis in obesity-related metabolic diseases.

14108315.value: 比較內鏡止血粉TC-325與內鏡標準療法於治療非靜脈曲張之急性上消化道出血的功效; 非劣效性的隨機研究 (TC325 study)

14108315.label: Project Objectives
14108315.value: To compare clinical efficacy of the hemostatic powder TC-325 to standard treatment in overall rate of hemostasis in patients with active bleeding from a non-variceal source in the upper gastrointestinal tract. We aim to determine the initial rate of hemostasis and the rate of further bleeding after initial control in both groups. We would like to define role of TC-325 as a mono-therapy when compared to standard treatment. The rate of further bleeding after initial control would also inform us if endoscopic application of TC-325 should be followed by a second look endoscopy with targeted treatment to the bleeding artery. To compare ease of application of hemostatic powder TC-325 to standard treatment.

14108315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108315.value: Acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding is a common medical emergency. Bleeding peptic ulcers and other non-variceal causes constitute to about 95% of all cases of bleeding. Endoscopic treatment stops active bleeding, reduces rate of further bleeding and leads to improved patients outcomes. Endoscopic treatment can be technically demanding especially with lesions in difficult anatomic positions and to endoscopists with less experience. TC-325 is a propriety mineral blend hemostatic powder used to compress external civilian and military traumatic injuries. We reported the first endoscopic application of TC-325 in 20 patients with actively bleeding gastro-duodenal ulcers. We were able to stop bleeding in 19 of them. Subsequent case series from others reported a similar rate in the acute control of bleeding. To further define the role of TC-325 as a mono-therapy, a comparison to the current standard in endoscopic treatment is required. A non-inferiority randomized trial is being proposed to compare endoscopic use of TC-325 as a mono-therapy to current standards (i.e. hemoclips or thermo-coagulation with or without pre-injection with diluted epinephrine) in hemostatic treatment in patients with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding from non-variceal causes. The non-inferiority primary endpoint is control of bleeding over 30 days from randomization. Other outcome endpoints include further endoscopic, angiographic or surgical treatments, hospitalization, blood transfusion and mortality. We also compare ease of therapy measured by procedure time and a 10 cm visual analogue scale rated by endoscopists. Endoscopic application of TC-325 is a simple and less skill dependent technique. It may prove useful in bleeding from anatomically challenging sites of the gastro-duodenal tract. 急性上消化道出血是常見的醫療緊急情況。出血消化性潰瘍和其他非靜脈曲張性原因構成了大約 95%的所有病例的出血。內鏡治療停止活動性出血，減少進一步的出血率並且導致提高的患者的結局。內鏡下治療可以技術要求高，特別是與病變在困難的解剖位置和內鏡經驗較少。TC-325 是得體的礦物摻合料止血粉用於壓縮外部的民用和軍用的創傷。我們報導了內鏡止血粉TC-325 TC 325 積極出血胃十二指腸潰瘍 20 患者的首次內鏡下應用。我們就能夠停止出血的 19 人。隨後從別人的案例系列報導類似在急性出血控制率。要進一步定義的 TC 325 作用作為單一治療，內鏡治療中的當前標準比較是需要的。非劣效性隨機的試驗擬比較 TC 325 作為單一治療當前的標準 (即 止血夾hemoclips 或熱凝有無預注射稀釋腎上腺素) 止血治療非靜脈曲張引起急性上消化道出血患者的內鏡下使用。非劣效主要終點是控制出血超過 30 天從隨機化。其他結果終結點包括進一步內鏡、 血管造影或手術治療、 住院治療、 輸血和死亡率。我們也比較易用性測量過程時間的治療和內鏡由額定的 10 釐米視覺類比評分。內鏡下的應用 TC 325 是一種簡單和較少技能依賴技術。它可能有益於從解剖學上具有挑戰性的胃十二指腸道的出血位置。

14108315.label: Realisation of objectives
14108315.value: We have completed a RCT with a total of 224 patients enrolled. These were patients with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding from documented nonvariceal causes (gastroduodenal ulcers n=130, 58%, upper GI cancers n=32, 14.3% and other causes such as vascular ectasia, Dieulafoy's lesions n-62, 27.7%). With an intention-to-treat analysis, 10.2% in the TC325 group and 18.9 in the standard group reached primary endpoint which was defined as control of bleeding within 30 days ( Difference in two proportions, 95%CI; 8,7%, -1.3 to 8.7%). The RCT was designed as an one sided non-inferiority study with an accepted difference of 10%. We therefore concluded that TC325 was not inferior to standard treatment in the control of bleeding from non- variceal causes of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. The use of TC325 was in fact superior to standard treatment in the control of bleeding at the index endoscopy (TC325 3/111 vs. 11/111, OR 95%CI; 3.88, 1.05 to 14.3, P=0.03) and overall control of bleeding within 30 days (11/111, 9,9% vs. 21/113. 18.6%, adjusted HR, 95%CI; 0.398, 0.185 to 0.857, P=0.02)

14108315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14108315.value: Between September 2015 and December 2018, 224 patients were enrolled from 4 hospitals. These were Prince of Wales Hospital, Hong Kong (n=160), King Chulalongkorn Memorial University Hospital, Thailand (n = 47), Changi General Hospital, Singapore (n = 12) and North District Hospital, Hong Kong (n = 5). These patients were randomized to receive endoscopic application of TC-325 (n=111) or standard endoscopic treatment (n=113). The causes of bleeding were peptic ulcers in 130 (58.0%), tumor in 32 (14.3%) and other lesions in 62 (27.7%) patients respectively. In the TC-325 group, the median number of vials used was 1 (range 1-4). In this group, one patient did not receive the powder. On changing to a dual channel endoscope, bleeding from the ulcer stopped spontaneously. The vessel was then treated with the use of hemo-clips. In the standard treatment group, the combination treatment of injection with diluted epinephrine and thermos-coagulation was used in 41 patients, epinephrine and hemo-clipping in 29 patients. In 10 patients, both hemo-clipping and thermo-coagulation were used after epinephrine injection. Monotherapy with hemo-clips alone was used in 20 patients. Band ligation was used in 2 patients with Dieulafoy’s lesions. In 9 patients with cancers, 8 were treated with the use of argon plasma coagulation and one patient was treated by injection with absolute alcohol. Analysis was by intention-to-treat (TC-325 group n=111, standard treatment group n=113). The baseline characteristics to both groups are provided in Table 1. The two groups were matched in their demographics, severity of bleeding and the proportion of patients with bleeding gastroduodenal ulcers (65 of 111, 58.6% vs. 65 of 113, 57.5%). In the TC-325 group, there were fewer patients with history of alcohol use (3, 3% vs. 11, 9.8%), and were using non-steriodal anti-inflammatory drugs (8.1% vs. 20.4%). In terms of bleeding etiology, there were more bleeding cancers (23, 20.7% vs. 9, 8%), fewer bleeding esophageal lesions (7 vs. 13) and Dieulafoy’s lesions (6 vs. 14) in the TC-325 group. Our analysis was by intention-to-treat; 11 of 111 patients (9.9%) from TC325 group and 21 of 113 patients (16.6%) from the standard treatment group met primary outcomes. After adjusting for the baseline differences, (Hazard ratio 95%CI; 0.398, 0.185, 0.857, p=0.019). TC325 was in fact superior to standard treatment in the control of bleeding over 30 days. This was due to a superior rate in acute hemostasis with the use of tc 325. During initial endoscopy, the use of TC-325 was associated with fewer failures in the control of active bleeding when compared to standard treatment (3 vs. 11, Odds ratio 3.88, 95%CI 1.05 to 14.32, P=0.03).

14108315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108315.value: The finding will change our current practice in the endoscopic management of patients with acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. The hemostatic powder TC325 will become the new standard with its ease of application in non-variceal bleeding from an upper GI source.

14108315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108315.value: Endoscopic application of hemostatic powder has been shown to be similar in efficacy in stopping hemorrhage from a variety of non-variceal causes of acute upper gastrointestinal bleeding. The rate in the control of acute bleeding has in fact been shown to be superior to conventional endoscopic treatment. In bleeding stomach and duodenal cancers, the powder is better. Also as a rescue therapy when other conventional endoscopic treatment, the powder is a useful adjunct.

14108615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108615.value: B-precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) is the most common childhood malignancy and the leading cause of cancer-related death in the pediatric population. Despite the favorable 5-year event-free survival rate (>80%) of childhood B-ALL in Hong Kong and overseas alike, the long-term outcomes of relapsed patients remain poor. Pro-survival signals provided by the bone marrow (BM) stroma could render leukemic cells insensitive to chemotherapy and eventually contribute to disease relapse. Thus, novel agents capable of perturbing leukemia-stroma interaction are of potentials to enhance the efficacy of existing chemotherapeutics. CD9, a tetraspanin protein, is associated with disease progression in various malignancies, including leukemia. Our previous studies have established its role in hematopoietic stem cell homing and mobilization in the NOD/SCID mouse model of xenotransplantation. Our preliminary data on primary B-ALL blasts and cell lines demonstrated: (i) an association of CD9 expression with specific chromosomal translocations; (ii) CD9 regulated B-ALL cell migration and adhesion to BM stroma via modulation of VLA-4/VCAM-1 binding; (iii) CD9-neutralizing antibody (Ab) enhanced sensitivity of B-ALL cells to vincristine in stromal co-cultures; and (iv) CD9-Ab reduced leukemic burden and prolonged survival of NOD/SCID mice xenografted with the B-ALL cell line 697. Our hypothesis is that CD9 promotes binding of B-ALL cells to the BM stroma mediated by adhesion receptors, leading to chemoresistance; and that CD9 antagonist could enhance chemosensitivity by disruption of leukemia-stroma interaction. The objectives of our study are: (1) to investigate the effectiveness and mechanism of CD9-Ab on increasing the sensitivity of primary B-ALL blasts and cell lines (SUP-B15, RS4;11, 697) to vincristine, dexamethasone, L-asparaginase or the combination of these drugs in a stromal co-culture model, in the presence or absence of integrin blocker VLA-4-Ab. The read-out assays will be apoptosis and cell cycle kinetics; and (2) to establish the efficacy of CD9-Ab as an adjunct to chemotherapy for reducing leukemic burden and increasing survival of NOD/SCID mice xenografted with primary B-ALL blasts, and cell lines RS4;11 and 697. The read-out assays will be (a) weekly leukemic load of luciferase-transduced cell lines in NOD/SCID animals by bioluminescent imaging; and (b) survival analysis of animals xenografted with primary B-ALL blasts and cell lines. This novel treatment strategy with CD9-Ab, complementing the established chemotherapeutic regimen, could be applied to treat high-risk B-ALL and relapsed patients. Increased chemosensitivity of leukemia and other CD9+ cancer types might improve treatment outcomes through efficient eradication of malignant cells and minimizing drug toxicity. 急性B淋巴細胞白血病(B-ALL)是最常見的兒童血液系統腫瘤，以及是導致與癌症相關死亡的首要原因。雖然現有的化療藥物在香港和海外都能有效治療大部份患者，復發患者的長期預後仍然很差。由骨髓基質提供的促存活信號可使白血病細胞對化療藥物變得不敏感，並最終導致疾病復發。因此，能夠干擾白血病與基質之間的相互作用的新穎藥物可提高現有化療藥物的功效。CD9，一個四旋蛋白，與各種惡性腫瘤(包括白血病)的疾病進展有關。我們先前的研究確立了其在造血幹細胞歸巢和調動功能上的作用。我們對B-ALL初代細胞和細胞株的初步數據顯示：(1) CD9表達與特定染色體易位有關聯; (2) CD9通過改變VLA-4/VCAM-1的粘接來控制B-ALL細胞遷移和粘附能力; (3) CD9中和抗體增強B-ALL細胞對長春新鹼的敏感性; (4) CD9抗體減少癌細胞數目和延長移植了697 B-ALL細胞株的NOD/SCID小鼠的生存期。我們的假設是，CD9促進B-ALL細胞與骨髓基質之間的粘附，導致產生抗藥性，而CD9拮抗劑可以通過破壞癌細胞與基質之間的相互作用，增強對化療藥物的敏感性。我們研究的目標是：(1) 利用基質共培養模型，調查CD9抗體是否能增加B-ALL初代細胞和細胞株(SUP-B15，RS4;11，697）對長春新鹼，地塞米松，L-門冬酰胺酶或藥物組合的敏感性及相關機制，測定方法將為細胞凋亡和細胞週期; (2) 利用移植了B-ALL初代細胞和細胞株(RS4;11，697)的NOD/SCID小鼠模型，探討CD9抗體作為輔助化療藥物的療效，測定方法為癌細胞數目和小鼠的生存期。這種利用了CD9抗體的新穎治療策略，補充了既定的化療方案，可能適用於治療高風險的B-ALL和復發患者。提高白血病和其他CD9+癌症對化療藥物的反應可能有效消滅腫瘤細胞，並減少藥物毒性，以提高治療效果。

14108615.label: Realisation of objectives
14108615.value: (1) In Objective 1, we proposed to investigate the efficacy of combining CD9 antibody with the standard chemotherapeutic agents vincristine, dexamethasone, L-asparaginase on apoptosis induction and cell cycle regulation of B-ALL cell lines and patient B-ALL blasts in stromal co-cultures. Moreover, we proposed to investigate the mechanism of chemoresistance mediated by the interaction of leukemic cells with stromal cells through CD9 and integrin VLA-4. All proposed experiments have been performed with satisfactory results: (a) To explore the association of CD9 with chemosensitivity, we compared the response of B-ALL cell lines with different degrees of CD9 expression to vincristine, dexamethasone and L-asparaginase in the presence or absence of primary bone marrow stromal cells. Our results showed that stromal co-culture significantly reduced chemotherapy-mediated apoptotic cell death in the CD9high cell lines SUP-B15, RS4;11 and 697 but not in the CD9low Reh cell line. These data suggest a role of CD9 in mediating stroma-dependent chemoresistance. (b) To provide a definitive proof of the above phenomenon, we tested whether the addition of CD9 neutralizing antibody will increase chemotherapy-induced apoptotic cell death in the stromal co-culture model. We have performed co-culture experiments on 4 B-ALL cell lines and 3 pediatric B-ALL patient samples using vincristine, dexamethasone and L-asparaginase as the apoptosis induction agents. Our results consistently showed that co-treatment with CD9 antibody and chemotherapeutic agents significantly enhanced apoptosis of B-ALL cells in stromal co-cultures. In addition, cell cycle arrest at the G0/G1 phase was observed upon CD9 antibody exposure. Drug interaction analyses using the Bliss independence model also revealed synergistic actions of CD9 antibody with vincristine and dexamethasone, therefore confirming our hypothesis that CD9 blockade could enhance chemosensitivity of B-ALL cells. (c) To dissect the mechanisms of CD9 in regulating chemosensitivity, we compared the affinity of integrin VLA-4 (a well-known binding partner of CD9) in B-ALL cells with distinct CD9 expression. Our results showed that CD9high cells preferentially bound to soluble VCAM-1 and adhered to the bone marrow stroma when compared with CD9low cells, and that CD9 blockade diminished the binding level and stromal adhesion. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments revealed that CD9 physically interacted with integrin VLA-4 in CD9high cells. Importantly, dual blockade of CD9 and VLA-4 significantly enhanced chemotherapy-induced apoptosis in stromal co-cultures, when compared to those treated with CD9 antibody alone or VLA-4 antibody alone. These data collectively indicate that binding of CD9 to integrin VLA-4 could enhance leukemia-stroma interaction and mediate drug resistance, which could be largely reversed by antibody treatment. (2) In Objective 2, we proposed to investigate the efficacy of co-administering CD9 antibody with conventional chemotherapy (combination of vincristine, dexamethasone and L-asparaginase) for treatment of pediatric B-ALL using the NOD/SCID mouse xenograft model. All the proposed experiments have been performed with satisfactory results: (a) Single-agent activity of CD9 antibody against pediatric B-ALL was first evaluated in the NOD/SCID mouse xenograft model using the 697 (CD9high), RS4;11 (CD9high) and Reh (CD9low) cell lines. Our results showed that administration of CD9 antibody at day 3 post-transplantation strongly reduced leukemic load by >90% in major hematopoietic organs (bone marrow, spleen, blood and liver) and doubled the survival duration of animals transplanted with the CD9high 697 and RS4;11 cells. In addition, CD9 antibody treatment markedly suppressed infiltration of leukemic cells to the central nervous system and testes, indicating its benefit for controlling extramedullary leukemia. However, such inhibitory effects were not observed in animals transplanted with the CD9low Reh cells. Delayed administration of CD9 antibody also yielded similar leukemia-suppressive activities in 697-transplanted animals, suggesting the antibody is effective at both low and high disease burden. Depletion of NK cells prior to leukemic cell infusion did not reverse the activity of CD9 antibody, suggesting its therapeutic efficacy does not rely on antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity. (b) The efficacy of CD9 antibody for the treatment of primary B-ALL was evaluated using 5 patient bone marrow samples collected at diagnosis or relapse. Four of these patients were refractory to salvage regimens, while the fifth had the high-risk KMT2A-AFF1 rearrangement. Blasts of these patients harbored different cytogenetic abnormalities and expressed high levels of CD9 (>85%). Administration of CD9 antibody significantly and consistently reduced the leukemic burden in bone marrow, spleen, blood and liver by >78.4%, and prolonged the survival duration by >1.8-fold compared with IgG-treated animals. At disease relapse, patient-derived leukemic cells in mice receiving anti-CD9 exhibited lower CD9 expression than animals receiving IgG, suggesting the need to tailor additional therapy for disease eradication. To determine if CD9 antibody was also effective for B-ALL with relatively lower levels of CD9, blasts of 2 KMT2A-AFF1+ patients (CD9 expression 45.4% and 63.2%) were xenografted into NOD/SCID mice. Again, anti-CD9 significantly decreased the multi-organ leukemic load in both cases. (c) To investigate the efficacy of combining CD9 antibody with conventional chemotherapy for treatment of pediatric B-ALL, we administered IgG, anti-CD9, IgG+chemotherapy (combination of vincristine, dexamethasone and L-asparaginase) or anti-CD9+chemotherapy to 697-transplanted mice. At day 14 and day 17, IgG-treated animals had a significantly higher leukemic burden than those in the other groups. Animals receiving chemotherapy or anti-CD9+chemotherapy had a lower leukemic burden than those treated with anti-CD9, suggesting that the inclusion of anti-CD9 into the chemotherapy protocol had no absolute advantage at these early time points. However, as the disease progressed at day 24 or day 31, the leukemic load was significantly lower in animals treated with anti-CD9+chemotherapy than in those receiving anti-CD9 or chemotherapy alone. Consistently, the merit of combination therapy was reflected in the survival statistics. An independent experiment was performed to evaluate the efficacy of anti-CD9 when administered alone or in adjunct to the single chemotherapeutic agent vincristine. Again, treatment with anti-CD9+vincristine resulted in significantly longer survival than treatment with anti-CD9 or with vincristine alone. In a patient-derived xenograft, animals treated with anti-CD9+vincristine survived longer than those receiving anti-CD9 or vincristine alone. These data collectively indicate the feasibility of implementing CD9 antibody into standard or reduced-intensity chemotherapy for controlling B-ALL progression. (d) Lastly, we evaluated the potential toxicity of CD9 antibody on normal hematopoiesis. Measurement of CD9 expression on CD34+ cells from normal bone marrow donors revealed that the early stem and progenitor CD34+CD38- subpopulation expressed low levels of CD9, whereas the lineage committed CD34+CD38+ cells had significantly higher CD9 expression. Administration of anti-CD9 did not affect overall (CD45) and multi-lineage (CD19, CD33, CD71 and CD34) engraftment of cord blood stem cells in primary and secondary NOD/SCID recipients. Similarly, the engraftment kinetics of bone marrow-derived stem cells was not significantly altered by anti-CD9 treatment. These data indicate a favorable toxicity profile of CD9 antibody.

14108615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14108615.value: Major findings of this study: 1. CD9 neutralizing antibody exhibits potent single-agent activity against relapsed/refractory pediatric B-ALL in the preclinical NOD/SCID mouse xenograft model. 2. CD9 neutralizing antibody exerts synergistic activities with standard chemotherapeutic agents for efficient control of leukemia progression. 3. CD9 plays an important role in leukemia-stroma interaction through activation of integrin VLA-4 and mediates chemoresistance, which can be reversed by antibody treatment. Research outcomes: 1. An original research article was published in Leukemia. 2. Four conference abstracts have been published. 3. A patent is filed. 4. A PhD student has been trained.

14108615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108615.value: This study has laid the foundation for future development of CD9-targeted therapies for high-risk and refractory pediatric B-ALL. Planned research agenda includes: (1) Development of humanized and fully human CD9 antibodies for testing in murine and primate models. (2) Further engineering of the prototypic CD9 antibodies into therapeutic forms to improve the efficacy and reduce toxicity. (3) Early phase clinical trials of therapeutic CD9 antibodies for refractory pediatric B-ALL.

14108615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108615.value: CD9 has been implicated in cancer progression but its prognostic relevance and therapeutic potential in B-ALL are largely unknown. This study identified CD9 as a new prognostic marker for predicting survival outcomes in pediatric B-ALL, validated the efficacy of anti-CD9 alone or in combination with chemotherapy for suppressing leukemia progression, and provided evidence linking CD9 to the VLA-4/VCAM-1 axis for regulation of leukemia-stroma interaction and chemosensitivity, in addition to its direct impact on cell growth, survival and signaling. We believe that the inclusion of CD9 into the diagnostic marker panels would allow refinement of clinical risk group stratification. We also propose that CD9 antibody could be developed as an adjunct to standard chemotherapy for treatment of high-risk or refractory pediatric B-ALL. This treatment approach could potentially be extended to adult leukemia and other malignancies that express the CD9 surface antigen.

14109515.label: Realisation of objectives
14109515.value: 1) How and what extent the project objective have been achieved: The aim of this project is to discover the precise mechanisms that underlie ovarian cancer recurrence in tumor microenvironment. We hypothesized that the tumor immunosuppression, which was induced by paclitaxel-mediated antitumor immunity via IFN-γ and PD-L1, contributes to the development of ovarian cancer recurrence. We have published a research article titled “Paclitaxel induces immunogenic cell death in ovarian cancer via TLR4/IKK2/SNARE-dependent exocytosis” in Cancer Immunology Research in 2020. In this study, we showed in ovarian cancer that paclitaxel induced immunogenic cell death-associated DAMPs (i.e. damage-associated molecular patterns, such as CALR exposure, ATP secretion and HMGB1 release) in vitro and elicited significant antitumor responses in tumor vaccination assays in vivo. Paclitaxel-induced TLR4 signaling was essential to the release of DAMPs, which lead to the activation of NF-kB-mediated CCL2 transcription and IKK2-mediated SNARE-dependent vesicle exocytosis, thus exposing CALR on the cell surface. Paclitaxel induced ER stress, which triggered PERK activation and eIF2a phosphorylation independent of TLR4. CALR expression in primary ovarian tumors also correlated with patients’ survival and patient response to chemotherapy. In this published work, we also analyzed T cell infiltration in advanced ovarian tumors from patients receiving NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) followed by interval debulking surgery and high grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) from patients receiving primary debulking surgery by multiplex immunohistochemistry. The number of CD8+ T cells, IFNγ+ cells and IFNγ+CD8+ T cells were significantly higher in post-NACT ovarian tumors compared to those in primary ovarian tumors (Figure 6C in the publication). These results indicated that paclitaxel chemotherapy induced infiltration of cytotoxic T cells in ovarian tumors of the responsive patients. In our follow-up study, we examined the mRNA expression of CD274 (PD-L1), IFN-γ and CD8A in the post-NACT and primary ovarian tumors. Significant higher mRNA levels of CD274 (PD-L1), IFN-γ and CD8A were found in post-NACT tumors compared to those in primary tumors (Figure 1), suggesting PD-L1 was up-regulated in ovarian cancer cells by paclitaxel chemotherapy via CD8+ cytotoxic T cell-derived IFN-γ. Figure 1 Next we investigated the association of defective IFN-γ pathway in primary tumors with tumor recurrence in ovarian cancer patients, which is the Objective 3 “To elucidate the role of defective IFN-γ signaling in tumor cells in the inhibition of CTL-mediated immunosuppression and prevention of ovarian cancer recurrence”. Ovarian cancer patients with recurrence (n=64) and without recurrence (n=86) were be included. Recurrence were defined as disease recurrence or progression after 6 months and before 18 months of completion of initial chemotherapy. Non-recurrence were defined as patients survived more than 18 months of completion of initial chemotherapy without evidence of recurrence. Primary ovarian tumor sections were taken at the time of surgery. We examined mRNA expression levels of 14 IFN-g signaling genes (IFNG, IFNGR1, IFNGR2, JAK1, JAK2, STAT1, STAT3, IRF1, IRF3, CD274 (PD-L1), CXCL9, CXCL10, HLA-DRA and IDO1) in primary ovarian tumor tissues by qRT-PCR, and found that the mRNA expression levels of IFNG, IFNR2, STAT1, STAT3, CXCL9, CXCL10 and HLA-DRA were significantly lower in primary tumors in the patients with non-recurrence when compared to those in the patients with recurrence (Figure 2; NR: non-recurrence; R: recurrence). These results suggested that defects of IFN-γ signaling genes in primary tumors were associated with the prevention of ovarian cancer recurrence. Figure 2 Overall, our publication not only fulfilled the achievement of our previous RGC-funded project titled “Study of immunogenic cell death induced by paclitaxel in high-grade serous ovarian cancer” (GRF 467713), the molecular mechanism of how paclitaxel induces immunogenic cell death through TLR4/IKK2/SNARE-dependent exocytosis as well as the immune profiling in ovarian tumors after chemotherapy were also relevant to the current RGC-funded project (14109515). 2) Give reason for under-achievements and outline attempts to overcome problems: Objective 1 “To characterize IFN-γ- and CD8+ T cell-dependent up-regulation of PD-L1 in ovarian tumor microenvironment after paclitaxel treatment in vivo” To investigate the efficacy of paclitaxel treatment in our syngeneic orthotropic mouse model of ovarian cancer, ID8F3 mouse ovarian cancer cells were inoculated in female C57BL/6 mice (n=10) intraperitoneally. After 14 days of tumor inoculation, mice were treated with paclitaxel (PTX; n=5; 20mg/kg in 300 ul; dissolved in normal saline; intraperitoneally; every 7 days for 4 cycles). Mice with saline (PBS) treatment were served as controls (n=5). Peritoneal ovarian tumors were obtained from the mice with PTX/PBS treatment one day after each drug injection. RNA was extracted and gene expression of Ccl2 and Cxcl10 in the tumors were examined by qRT-PCR. Since Ccl2 and Cxcl10 were up-regulated in ID8F3 cells by paclitaxel treatment via TLR4 signaling in vitro, this is the reason for using Ccl2 and Cxcl10 up-regulation as indicators of the efficacy of paclitaxel treatment in vivo. Our results showed that Ccl2 and Cxcl10 were significantly increased in PTX-treated tumors when compared to those in PBS-treated controls after the 1st and 2nd cycle of drug treatment (i.e. after the 2nd and 3rd injection; Figure 3). In addition, no ovarian tumor in mouse peritoneal cavity was found after the 3rd and 4th cycle of paclitaxel treatment. Our results therefore indicated that the efficacy of paclitaxel treatment in our mouse model was good. Figure 3 Next, we repeated the animal experiment to investigate T cell infiltration and PD-L1 up-regulation in ovarian tumor after paclitaxel treatment in vivo. After 14 days of tumor inoculation, mice were treated with paclitaxel for 2 cycles (n=5). Mice with PBS treatment were served as controls (n=5). Peritoneal ovarian tumors were obtained after 2 cycles of PTX/PBS treatment. Ifng, Cd4, Cd8 and Cd274 mRNA expression were examined by qRT-PCR. Our results showed that Ifng, Cd4 and Cd8 expression were increased in PTX-treated tumors when compared to those in PBS-treated controls, whereas no change of Cd274 expression was found (Figure 4). Figure 4 Those were not ideal results. We therefore planned to isolate immune and cancer cells from peritoneal ovarian tumors after 2 cycles of PTX/PBS treatment in another experiment. We aimed to examine the number of infiltrated T cells and PD-L1 expression levels in cancer cells by FACS analysis. While we were repeating the animal experiments for the FASC analysis, our animal experiments however were terminated by two unexpected events happened in Hong Kong (Hong Kong’s protest 2019 and Covid-19 outbreak). 1) Hong Kong's protests started in June 2019 against plans to allow extradition to mainland China. Anti-government protests rocked Hong Kong for months. In November 2019, protesters occupied the Shatin campus of The Chinese University of Hong Kong for four days. The occupation created chaos and violence in the University campus. All offices (including animal faculties) in the University were closed. Our animal experiment were therefore terminated at the end of November 2019. It took more than a month for the University to recover afterwards. The laboratory research activities was resumed in January 2020. However our research work were paused again by another event happened in February 2020. 2) Covid-19 outbreak. Due to the coronavirus outbreak in Hong Kong, all offices (including animal facilities) in the University were closed and all the research activities were paused from mid-February to early-April 2020. These were the reasons for our under-achievements in Objective 1 and 2 of the project. We attempted to restart our animal experiments in May 2020.

14109515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14109515.value: The findings in our publication suggested that the effectiveness of paclitaxel relied upon the activation of antitumor immunity through ICD via TLR4 and highlighted the importance of CALR expression in cancer cells as an indicator of response to paclitaxel chemotherapy in ovarian cancer. The results obtained from Objective 3 showed the association of IFN-γ signal transduction defects with the prevention of ovarian cancer recurrence. 14109515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14109515.value: Chemotherapy is an effective treatment for advance ovarian cancer. However, generally 70% ovarian cancer patients relapse. This project is aim to study the tumor factor that causes ovarian cancer recurrence. We firstly found that chemotherapeutic drug paclitaxel not only killed cancer cells, but also boosted immune system cells to attack the cancer cells. This phenomenon explained the high initial response rate of chemotherapy of ovarian cancer. However we subsequently found that, during the immune attack, a molecule called IFN-γ activated immune checkpoints in the tumors. These checkpoints helped keep immune responses from being too strong and sometimes could keep T cells from killing cancer cells. Therefore, the activation of checkpoints caused the recurrence of ovarian cancer. Our work therefore suggested to use a combination of paclitaxel chemotherapy and immune checkpoint inhibitor to prevent ovarian cancer recurrence.

14110415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14110415.value: The prevalence of type 2 diabetes has increased markedly over recent decades, and diabetes has become a global public health problem. An increasing proportion of young adults are diagnosed with diabetes, putting them at risk of long-term diabetic complications and increase in healthcare burden. Polycystic ovary syndrome is the commonest endocrine disorder affecting women of reproductive age, and in addition to menstrual irregularity and fertility problems, is associated with increased insulin resistance and marked increase in the risk of type 2 diabetes. In addition to impaired glucose tolerance and diabetes, subjects with PCOS also have increased risk of hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, as well as other cardiometabolic risk factors, when compared to subjects without PCOS. There is much recent debate regarding the cardiovascular risk in women with PCOS, especially in relation to the risk profile as the patients go beyond the reproductive age. It is also not clear which subphenotype of PCOS is most at risk of cardiometabolic problems. Our group has established a registry of over 300 Chinese patients with PCOS, with detailed documentation of baseline characteristics and metabolic evaluation. We aim to conduct a comprehensive follow-up study of these PCOS subjects, in order to address some of the current knowledge gaps. In this study, we aim to evaluate the rate of progression to glucose intolerance/type 2 diabetes, as well as changes in cardiometabolic risk factors, approximately 10 years after the baseline evaluation. We will also assess for evidence of early atherosclerosis by measuring carotid intima media thickness (IMT). All results will be compared to a control group of subjects who have undergone the same metabolic and imaging evaluation at baseline, with recent follow-up evaluation completed approximately 10 years after the baseline assessment. In addition to comparing the incident rate of glucose intolerance/diabetes, we also aim to compare the metabolic risk of the different PCOS subphenotype. Finally, we will evaluate the ability of visceral adiposity and adipokines to predict the risk of incident diabetes among women with PCOS. 14110815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14110815.value: Despite the advance in orthopaedic treatment, the rate of delayed or non-union of fractures reaches about 13%. Further surgery using various fixation devices is still the “gold standard”. However, many complications, morbidity and disadvantages are associated with operative treatment. Enhancement of fracture healing is therefore a desirable objective, in order to reduce or avoid such consequences. Currently, physical intervention, gene therapy, stem cell therapy and growth factor treatments are being developed to enhance bone healing and treat non-union. However various problems have been reported, such as long treatment time, ectopic bone formation, and risk of infection and limited sources of donor bone or stem cells. Delivering effective orthobiologics with low cost and minimal complications remains a great challenge. Recently, natural products derived from medicinal herbs have great potential as biologics in bone healing. Neobavaisoflavone, is reported to ameliorate osteoporosis and stimulate osteoblastic differentiation. In our pilot result, neobavaisoflavone promoted mineralization of chondrocyte dose dependently in cell culture model. Moreover, it promoted bone formation with increasing of collagen type I and bone morphogenetic protein-2 expression in chondrocyte of soft callus in established rat femoral delayed union model. In this project, we hypothesize that neobavaisoflavone promotes bone formation to avoid development of delayed/nonunion of bone fracture and also neobavaisoflavone activates mineralization of chondrocyte through estrogen receptor. The objectives of this study are to investigate: 1) the effect of NBIF on bone formation to avoid the development of delayed/nonunion; and 2) the mechanism of NBIF on mineralization of chondrocyte. The results obtained will help us to develop an alternative therapy for healing delayed/nonunion of fracture. Success of the project leads to a significantly shortened duration, increased success rate of healing of non-union and reduction of related complications and shortened periods of hospital treatment. It may also decrease loss of working ability and low quality of life associated with delayed/nonunion. It also shed light on knowledge and mechanism of natural small molecule on bone formation in nonunion of long bone and its application on other difficult bone healing such as critical sized bone defect and spinal fusion.

14110815.label: Realisation of objectives
14110815.value: 1. Objective 1: To study the effect of NBIF on bone formation to avoid the development of delayed/nonuion. (100% achieved) 1.1. NBIF promoted bone fracture healing in femoral nonunion model in rats After treatment with NBIF (250 and 500 µM) for 1 week (week 4), the bone fracture union was significantly improved, when compared with the vehicle control group. Similarly, the bone fracture union was markedly promoted after treatment with NBIF (250 and 500 µM) for 3 weeks (week 6) and 5 weeks (week 8). The bone fracture healing effects of NBIF were found to have dose- and time-dependent manners. Moreover, under micro CT imaging, NBIF (100, 250, 500 µM) significantly promoted bone union formation after treatment for 5 weeks, when compared with the vehicle control group. 1.2. NBIF augmented the hard callus formation and bone formation rate The hematoxyin & eosin and alcian blue staining results revealed that treatment with NBIF (250 and 500 µM) for 3 weeks (week 6) and 5 weeks (week 8) significantly enhanced the hard callus formation and bone formation rate in femoral nonunion model in rats. 1.3. NBIF increased bone forming protein expression in rats Treatment with NBIF (250 and 500 µM) effectively elevated the bone forming protein markers such as osterix (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, respectively), BMP2 (p < 0.01 and p < 0.001, respectively), osteocalcin (p < 0.01 and p < 0.01, respectively) in the bone tissues of rats, as compared with the vehicle control group. In addition, NBIF (500 µM) markedly increased the protein expressions of SOX9 (p < 0.01), collagen type III (p < 0.01), dickkopf-1 (p < 0.05), ERα (p < 0.01) and ERβ (p < 0.05) in bone tissues of rats, as compared with the vehicle control group. Moreover, NBIF (500 µM) markedly enhanced the protein expressions of CD31 (p < 0.05) and VEGF (p < 0.01) in bone tissues of rats, as compared with the vehicle control group. To sum, NBIF was able to avoid development of delayed/nonunion via enhancing bone healing with augmentation of hard callus formation and faster bone formation rate, and increasing in bone forming protein expression. 2. Objective 2: To study the mechanism of NBIF of mineralization of chondrocyte. (100% achieved) 2.1. The cytotoxicity of NBIF on ATDC5 cells After incubation with NBIF for 24 h, up to 50 µM of NBIF showed no cytotoxicity on ATDC5 cells. Treatment of ATDC5 cells with 100 µM of NBIF for 2 h induced cytotoxicity as the cell viability was reduced to 75.9% of the control value (100%) (p < 0.001). 2.2. NBIF increased mineralization in ATDC5 cells The results of Alizarin Red S assay demonstrated that NBIF (12.5, 25 and 50 µM) could increase mineralization in ATDC5 cells in a dose-dependent manner. Interestingly, at the doses of 12.5 and 25 µM, NBIF generated greater mineralization than treatment with ITS only. 2.3. NBIF induced late phase chondrogenesis in ATDC5 cells After incubation with NBIF (6.25, 12.5, 25 µM) for 7 days, there was insignificant difference between the mRNA expressions of early chondrogenic markers including COL2A2 and ACAN. NBIF (25 µM) also significantly increased the mRNA expressions of COL10A1 by 1.37 folds (p < 0.01) after treatment for 7 days. Treatment with NBIF (12.5 and 25 µM) for 7 days significantly elevated the late chondrogenic marker SOX9 mRNA expression by 1.60 (p < 0.01 for both) and 1.63 (p < 0.01) folds in ATDC5 cells. However, treatment with NBIF (6.25, 12.5, 25 µM) for 14 days significantly decreased the mRNA expressions of COL2A2 and ACAN by more than 3 folds (p < 0.001 for three doses) on ATDC5 cells, when compared with vehicle control group. Similarly, a reduction by 2 folds (p < 0.001 for three does) in COL10A1 mRNA expression was also found after treatment with NBIF (6.25, 12.5, 25 µM) for 14 days in ATDC5 cells. 2.4. NBIF promoted osteogenesis in ATDC5 cells The RUNX2 mRNA expression was significantly upregulated by 1.07 (p < 0.01), 0.84 (p < 0.01), and 0.88 (p < 0.01) folds after treatment with NBIF (6.25, 12.5, and 25 µM, respectively) for 7 days. Treatment with NBIF (25 µM) for 14 days also significantly upregulated the RUNX2 mRNA expression in ATDC5 cells, when compared with the vehicle control group. Similarly, the mRNA expression of BMP2 was markedly upregulated by at least 1 fold (p < 0.05 for three doses) after treatment with NBIF (6.25, 12.5, and 25 µM) for 7 or 14 days, when compared with the vehicle control. When ATDC5 cells were treated with NBIF (6.25, 12.5, and 25 µM), the mRNA expression of COL1A1 was significantly upregulated by 50% (p < 0.05 for three doses) for 7 days and by 1 fold (p < 0.001 for three doses) for 14 days, when compared with the vehicle control. 2.5. NBIF targeted ESR1 The results of silico docking showed that NBIF bound to ESR1 at the binding pocket. Hydrogen bonds were formed at GLU353 and HIS324 with the hydroxyl groups at both ends. After treatment with NBIF (12.5 and 25 µM) for 7 days, the mRNA expression of ESR1 was significantly accentuated by 0.94 (p < 0.05) and 1.80 (p < 0.01) folds respectively, when compared with the vehicle control group. On the other hand, when incubation with fulvestrant (an estrogen receptor antagonist), chondrogenic and osteogenic markers were significantly downregulated. 2.6. Inhibition of Raf-ERK-MAPK abolished NBIF-induced differentiation in ATDC5 cells The effects of NBIF on the chondrogenic and osteogenic markers were abolished by co-treatment of ATDC5 cells with the inhibitors targeting estrogen receptor (Fulvestrant), ERK (FR180204), p38 MAPK (SB203580), and raf (ZM336372). After co-treatment with NBIF (25 μM) for 7 days, the mRNA expression of COL10A1 was significantly decreased by Fulvestrant (p < 0.001), FR180204 (p < 0.001), SB203580 (p < 0.001), and ZM336372 (p < 0.001) in ATDC5 cells, when compared with the NBIF (25 μM) treatment group. The mRNA expression of SOX9 was significantly downregulated after co-treatment NBIF (25 μM) with Fulvestrant (p < 0.001), FR180204 (p < 0.001), SB203580 (p < 0.001), or ZM336372 (p < 0.001) in ATDC5 cells for 7 days, when compared with the NBIF (25 μM) treatment group. In addition, the mRNA expression of RUNX2 was significantly downregulated after treatment with the combination of NBIF (25 μM) and Fulvestrant (p < 0.001), FR180204 (p < 0.001), SB203580 (p < 0.001), or ZM336372 (p < 0.001) in ATDC5 cells for 7 days, when compared with the NBIF (25 μM) treatment group. Similarly, the mRNA expressions of BMP2 and COL1A1 were also significantly reduced after co-treatment with NBIF (25 μM) and Fulvestrant (p < 0.001 for both), FR180204 (p < 0.001 for both), SB203580 (p < 0.001 for both), or ZM336372 (p < 0.001 for both) in ATDC5 cells for 7 days, when compared with the NBIF (25 μM) treatment group. In conclusion, NBIF activated estrogen receptors and BMP2 to stimulate mineralization of chondrocytes in ATDC5 cells.

After co-treatment with NBIF (25 μM), the mRNA expression of COL10A1 was significantly decreased by Fulvestrant, FR180204, SB203580, and ZM336372 in ATDC5 cells, when compared with the NBIF (25 μM) treatment group. The mRNA expression of SOX9 was significantly downregulated after co-treatment NBIF (25 μM) with Fulvestrant, FR180204, SB203580, or ZM336372 in ATDC5 cells for 7 days, when compared with the NBIF (25 μM) treatment group. 14110815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14110815.value: 1. To further confirm the bone formation effect of NBIF on ESR1 knockout mice and mouse model of osteoporosis. The present project has successfully evaluated the bone formation effect of NBIF using femoral nonunion model in rats via modulating the expression of ESR1. We would like to further confirm the bone formation efficacy of NBIF through regulating the ESR1 using ESR1 knockout mice. The mouse model of osteoporosis is induced by ovariectomy (OVX) in female mice to mimic the postmenopausal osteoporosis. Following OVX, the animals display a very rapid loss of trabecular bone, resulting in an osteopenic phenotype. 2. To evaluate the bone formation effect in a pilot clinical trial. The present project is a preclinical study on the bone formation efficacy of NBIF. To develop NBIF into a pharmaceutical agent for fracture healing, it is necessary to test the effectiveness and safety of this promising chemical compound in patients with fracture healing. We propose to initiate a randomized placebo-controlled clinical trial on patients with fracture healing to test the efficacy and safety of NBIF using internationally recognized protocol and assessment tools.

14110815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14110815.value: Bone repairing occurs after bone fractures or bone defects or orthopedic surgery. Ineffective treatment could cause impaired bone formation and, eventually delayed union or nonunion. Effective orthobiologics are urgently needed. The current project aimed to investigate the bone formation efficacy of neobavaisoflavone (NBIF), an isoflavone isolated from the fruit of Psoralea corylifolia, and the underlying mechanisms. Our results indicated that NBIF could promote the bone union healing in the femoral nonunion model in rats via enhancing bone healing with augmentation of hard callus formation and faster bone formation rate, and increasing in bone forming protein expression. NBIF treatment markedly upregulated the mRNA expressions of SOX9, collagen type X A1, collagen type I, BMP2, RUNX2 and ESR1 in ATDC5 cells. The above NBIF-induced mRNA expression changes were abolished when co-treated with the inhibitors of ESR1 or MAPK pathways. Taken together, NBIF could promote bone nonunion healing and mediated osteogenesis via upregulating the chondrogenic and ostrogenic markers. Our results have established NBIF as a promising candidate for fracture healing, and serve as a foundation for future clinical trial to evaluate its efficacy and safety in patients with impaired fracture healing.

14111115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111115.value: Depression is a very common and distressing neuropsychiatric symptom of dementia (Major Neurocognitive Disorder, MND, in DSM-5 classification). It occurs across all stages of the disease, affects quality of life and confers high risk of self-harm and disability. Unfortunately, satisfactory response of pharmacological treatment for Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) has not been demonstrated in depressed people suffering from MND. Major systematic reviews found no superior effects, albeit with more adverse effects, for antidepressant treatments. Due to progressive cognitive impairment of the primary disorder, options for psychotherapy are extremely limited. Recent studies suggested that Depression with MND could not be adequately explained by altered activities of neurotransmitter pathways. More generalized changes in immunological response, and disruption of neuronal activities due to neuro-degeneration may be closely related to clinical presentation of depression in MND. Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) is safe and non-invasive brain stimulation device approved for the treatment of MDD in patients who do not response to at least one course of conventional anti-depressant medication. Studies showed that stimulation of left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex are associated with significant improvement in depressive symptoms with effect sizes comparable to standard medication therapy. The exact mechanisms to explain anti-depressant effects of rTMS are still unknown. It is believed that the magnetic stimulation affects cortical excitability, induces neuroplastic changes through associated chemical and physiological alterations in neuronal activities. The neural modulation in rTMS fits into the hypothesis relating depression with MND. Treatment by rTMS leading to alterations in neuroplastic response may help to optimize neuronal activities in people with depression in the context of neurodegenerative disorders. This proposal aims to study the clinical efficacy of a 3 week intervention of single blind rTMS in Chinese older adults suffering from depression in MND due to Alzheimer’s disease or Major Vascular Neurocognitive Disorder with small vessel disease. We would also evaluate the sensitivity of a peripheral biomarker of generalized neuroplastic response, Brain Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF), in reflecting clinical changes. Primary outcome will be changes in depression scores as measured by Cornell Scale for Depression in Dementia (CSDD). Secondary outcomes will include cognitive function, profiles of neuropsychiatric symptoms, activities of daily living and serum levels of BDNF. The findings of this study will provide important treatment implications for this prevalent condition with no approved treatment available. Associated biomarker assay with BDNF will help to shed light on the physiology of clinical efficacy with this treatment strategy.

14111115.value: 1. The study deadline has been delayed for 9 months. This was mainly attributed to logistic changes in booking arrangement of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain, a mandatory preparation for the neuronavigated TMS treatment. The problem was solved by adopting alternative source for MRI. At the completion of study, the recruitment reached the proposed sample size of the research protocol. 2. We managed to complete clinical assessments on depression, cognitive, neuropsychiatric symptoms and quality of life assessments for most participants. The overall drop out rate is 5%. Therefore, we managed to attain all clinical objectives (objectives 1 to 4) in the study. Major findings and clinical implications are listed in the corresponding sessions below. 3. For the serum assay on Brain Derived Neurotrophic Factors (BDNF) and changes in depressive symptomatology in rTMS and sham TMS intervention, we managed to obtain blood samples in about 60% of all measurements required. Some subjects were reluctant for blood taking at different assessment time points. Group comparisons in BDNF levels are carried out as stated in the objectives, albeit sample size was smaller than the clinical assessments. 4. There were no changes in the study protocol through the intervention. No major adverse events or mortality were identified during the study period.

14111115.label: Major findings and research outcome
14111115.value: 1. 100 subjects were screened for eligibility, 40 were excluded because of not fulfilling diagnostic criteria or defaulted after initial screening. Informed consent was obtained from 60 eligible participants, of which 5 did not complete MRI scanning. Fifty-five participants were randomized (27 in the active and 28 in the sham rTMS groups respectively). Two participants from active and 1 from sham group defaulted intervention. 2. The mean age of active and sham groups is 69.2 (7.3) years and 73.7(7.2) years (t-test, p=0.02). There were no group differences in gender and education, depression and cognitive function at baseline (T1)(p> 0.05). 3. Fifteen active and sham rTMS sessions were conducted. Study outcomes were assessed at T2 (within 1 week post intervention), T3 (3 weeks post intervention) and T4 (6 weeks post intervention). 4. At T2, there was significant reduction in depression scores (CSDD) and improvement in cognitive function test (Montreal Cognitive Assessment, MoCA) in both groups (paired t-test, p<0.005). The improvements persisted in the 6 weeks post-intervention period. Across all observation time points (T2, T3 and T4), there were no group differences in primary outcome of depression raw scores (CSDD). No changes in neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPI) and quality of life (QOL-AD) were found. 5. The proportion of participants achieving clinical remission were evaluated. At T2, 8 (32%) of the active and 3 (11%) of the sham group were classified as in remission (Chi square, p=0.07). The proportion of participants with remission did not differ between active and sham group at T3 and T4. Logistic regression analysis revealed that older age (p=0.016), higher baseline cognitive function (HKMoCA)(p=0.041) and Active group (p=0.025) were associated with remission after intervention at T2 (Nagelkerke R2 0.42). Randomization group is not a significant factor for remission at T3 and T4. 6. Serum levels of Brain Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF) were assessed at baseline, T2, T3 and T4. There were no correlations between baseline BDNF level and depression or cognitive scores. At T2, the BDNF levels of the active group showed a marginally significant increase compared to baseline (paired t-test, p=0.04), a non-significant increase is observed in the Sham group (p> 0.05). There was no group difference in BDNF levels across all assessment time point (T1 to T4).

14111115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14111115.value: 1. The main aim of the study is to examine if rTMS is a safe and effective treatment for depressive symptoms in neurocognitive disorders. 2. In terms of tolerability and safety, our study demonstrated a very low drop out rate of 5%. There were no major adverse events observed through the study (the subjects defaulted mainly because of the noises associated with magnetic stimulation). 3. As for clinical efficacy, while there are no group differences in outcomes for depression and cognitive function raw scores, the proportion of participants achieving clinical remission was higher after 3 weeks of intervention. Our findings also suggested that older participants appeared to exhibit a better response. This gives support for rTMS to be consider as an adjuvant treatment for significant depressive mood in cognitively compromised elderly patients, especially for its rapid antidepressant effects covering the therapeutic gap when antidepressant takes two weeks or longer to take effects on mood, or bridging through the choices of antidepressant when adverse effects occur. 4. For future development, it would be interesting to further explore individual characteristics predicting treatment response. Structural changes such as white matter volume and cerebral atrophy are potential markers for brain reserve affecting responsiveness to brain stimulation. 5. rTMS intervention for a longer period, as well as logistics for regular TMS as maintenance for treatment resonders to prevent relapses of depression should be considered.

14111115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14111115.value: 1. This is a 3 week randomized controlled clinical trial of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for treatment of significant depression in older adults with neurocognitive disorders. Through rTMS, the frontal lobe implicated in the physiological pathway for depression is stimulated. Our findings suggested that rTMS intervention is safe with good tolerability. 2. Both active and controlled groups showed improvements in depression and cognitive function with intervention and post intervention assessments, suggesting significant placebo effects. However, as active treatment showed higher proportion achieving clinical remission at 3 weeks, our study supports the role of rTMS as a relatively safe and effective adjuvant treatment for depression in dementia, especially when a swift reduction of symptom severity is required.

14111515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111515.value: Myopia (short-sightedness) is the most common eye disorder worldwide, especially in Hong Kong. The prevalence of myopia among school children is approximately 30% at 7 years of age and 53% at 12 years of age. High myopia is associated with excessive eyeball growth leading to many sight-threatening complications, including pre-senile cataract, glaucoma, retinal detachment, and choroidal neovascularization. Despite decades of research, a simple and effective intervention to retard the progression of myopia is still not available. We have shown that atropine 1% eye drops are effective in retarding the eyeball growth and thus the myopia progression, but that associated side effects include photophobia due to mydriasis and decreased near vision due to cycloplegia. These ocular side effects have prohibited wide adoption of atropine use internationally. Moreover, the daily regimen of treatment has further deterred acceptance by parents and patients in adopting this treatment. Therefore, a regimen of low dose atropine, which has a much safer ocular profile and is more acceptable to patients, given less frequently, will shed new light on interventions for this potentially blinding disease. In this study we propose to evaluate the efficacy of different dosages and different regimens of low dose atropine in controlling the myopia progression and to determine the phenotypic and genetic factors that are associated with the progression of myopia. Start from September 2015, 800 children aged 6 to 12 years old with documented progression of myopia more than 0.5 diopter in the past year will be recruited and randomized into five groups, with atropine administered as follows: Group 1: 0.1% atropine in both eyes once daily; Group 2: 0.1% atropine in both eyes twice per week; Group 3: 0.01% atropine in both eyes once daily; Group 4: 0.01% atropine in both eyes twice per week; Group 5: 0.9% normal saline in both eyes once daily. All children will be monitored for myopia progression at 4 monthly intervals for 24 months with treatment, and followed by one year wash-out period with treatment stopped. To study the phenotype-genotype correlation, 15 representative single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) that are associated with myopia will be genotyped and compared between children with or without myopia progression to determine the effects of these myopia-associated SNPs on myopia progression. Our results, once proven effective in prevention of myopia progression, will bring a paradigm shift in myopia intervention and will have widespread implications for millions of children worldwide. 題目：評價不同用藥方案和不同劑量的低劑量阿托品局部應用對減緩近視進展的作用 近視（看遠不清）是全世界，特別是香港地區，最常見的眼科疾病。對學齡兒童來說，7歲兒童的近視患病率約為30%，而在12歲兒童中更是高達53%。高度近視與眼球過度增長有關，且會導致許多損害視覺的併發症，包括多白內障、青光眼、視網膜脫離、脈絡膜新生血管的形成等。 雖然經過數十年的研究，到目前為止還沒有一種簡單有效的幹預措施可以減緩近視進展。我們的研究表明，1%阿托品滴眼液可有效減緩眼球生長，進而預防近視進展，但存在阿托品相關的併發症，如散瞳引起的畏光和睫狀肌麻痹引起的視近困難。這些併發症使得阿托品在國際上被禁止廣泛應用。此外，每天都需要用藥的治療方案導致很多患者和家長難以接受阿托品治療。因此，採用低劑量的阿托品，提高用藥安全性，減少用藥頻率，提高患者接受度，可為治療近視這一潛在的致盲性眼病提供新的幹預方案。 本研究中，我們將評價不同劑量和不同用藥方案的低劑量阿托品治療在控制近視進展中的有效性，並找到與近視進展有關的表型和遺傳因素。從2016年1月開始，本實驗將納入800個6-12歲，且在過去一年內近視度數進展大於0.5D的兒童，並將其隨機分為5個組進行阿托品治療：第1組：雙眼應用0.1%阿托品，每天一次；第2組：雙眼應用0.1%阿托品，每週兩次；第3組：雙眼應用0.01%阿托品，每天一次；第4組：雙眼應用0.01%阿托品，每週兩次；第5組：雙眼應用0.9%生理鹽水，每天一次。阿托品持續治療2年後，停止治療，進入1年的洗脫期。在這3年內，每隔4個月對所有兒童進行一次檢查，監測近視進展情況。為研究表現型-基因型關聯性，研究將選取15個有代表性的與近視相關的單核苷酸多態性位點（SNPs）進行基因型測定，並比較有近視進展和沒有近視進展兒童的基因型，以此確定這些近視相關位點對近視進展的作用。 本研究結果一旦證實可有效預防近視進展，將會給近視幹預帶來一種範式轉變，並對全世界數百萬的兒童產生廣泛影響。

14111715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111715.value: The major symptom of Parkinson’s disease is severe movement disability characterized by akinesia, bradykinesia and resting tremor. The main cause of these motor deficits is the degeneration of the nigrostriatal projection, resulting in the depletion of the neuromodulator dopamine in the motor striatum. On the other hand, it is well documented that Parkinson’s disease is often associated with deficits in cognitive functions, some of which are detectable before the appearance of motor symptoms, and could significantly degrade the quality of life of the patients. When compared with the motor symptoms, however, the neurobiological basis of cognitive deficits in Parkinson’s disease is much less clear. Inflexibility in switching one strategy from another to accomplish a task (i.e. task-switching or set-shifting) is common neurocognitive deficit in many Parkinson’s disease patients, and is also found in other neurological problems such as attention deficit and hyperactivity disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, depression and schizophrenia. Impairment in the prefrontal cortex has generally been regarded as an important origin of the problem. In addition, subcortical pathway modulated by dopamine may be involved. In particular, a role of the projection from the prefrontal cortex to the nucleus accumbens, an important integration centre for limbic, sensory and motor functions, has been proposed. However, the mechanism is likely to be complicated and our understanding is currently hampered by the lack of detailed knowledge on the organization and function of this pathway. In this proposal, employing the rodent model and state-of-the-art techniques, we will functionally dissect the prefontral cortex-nucleus accumbens circuitry in mediating the task-switching ability, and the impact of dopamine depletion under Parkinsonism. Optogenetic stimulation combined with in electrophysiological recording and behavioral assessment will be employed. The results will provide significant insight into the causes of neurocognitive deficits in Parkinson’s disease and pave the way for therapeutic strategies against the disturbing non-motor symptoms associated with this disease and other neurological disorders. 帕金森疾病的主要症狀是嚴重的運動障礙，其特徵表現為運動不能，運動遲緩和靜止性震顫。這些運動障礙出現的主要原因是由於黑質紋狀體投射回路的退化而導致運動紋狀體中神經調節物-多巴胺的耗盡。而另一方面，研究發現帕金森病往往與認知功能缺陷相關，而其中一些的認知功能缺陷可以在運功功能症狀出現前所檢測到，並且能夠明顯的降低帕金森病患者的生活品質。然而，與運功功能症狀相比，帕金森病中出現認知功能缺陷症狀的神經生物學機制仍不清楚。 帕金森疾病患者中神經認知功能缺陷主要表現在改變策略來完成任務的靈活性差(如任務轉化，或者設置轉變)，同時帕金森疾病患者還存在著其他的神經學上的問題，如注意力缺陷，多動症，強迫症，抑鬱症和精神分裂症。而前額葉皮層受損已普遍認為是引起這些現象的一個重要的起源。 此外，多巴胺的皮質下通路也可能參與到這一過程。特別是作為邊緣系統，感覺和運動皮層的重要組成部分，前額葉皮層到伏隔核這一投射回路被認為是導致了帕金森疾病患者中神經認知功能缺陷。然而，其具體的機制是比較複雜的，目前對於這一通路中組織和功能上研究的缺乏也阻礙著我們對其正確的認識。 在本課題中，我們採用齧齒動物模型，通過任務切換實驗，分析前額葉皮層到伏隔核投射回路分別在正常狀態以及帕金森疾病中多巴胺耗盡的情況下所起到不同的作用。

14111715.label: Realisation of objectives
14111715.value: Our team has fully realised the objectives of the present proposal, namely, to confirm and elucidate the role of the prefrontal cortex-NAc projection in task-switching flexibility, to determine the contribution of the mesolimbic dopamine pathway in the maintenance of task-switching flexibility, and to decipher the microcircuitry in the nucleus accumbens, with respect to the exact roles of dopamine D1 and D2 receptors, in mediating the observed cognitive flexibility. The results have been presented in an international conference as well as published in a highly respected international journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of USA.

14111715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14111715.value: In this project, we showed that optogenetic excitation and inhibition of the prelimbic cortex-nucleus accumbens (NAc) pathway in the mouse enhances and suppresses respectively strategy-switching ability in a cross-modal spatial-egocentric task, involving a response direction task and a visual cue task. We showed that this ability is dependent on an intact dopaminergic tone in the NAc as local dopamine denervation impaired the performance of the animal in the switching of tasks. In addition, based on a brain-slice preparation obtained from Drd2-eGFP BAC transgenic mice, we demonstrated direct innervation of D2 receptor expressing medium spiny neurons (D2-MSNs) in the NAc by prelimbic cortical neurons, which is under the regulation by presynaptic dopamine receptors. While D1 receptor activation enhances the glutamatergic transmission from the prelimbic cortex to D2-MSNs, D2 receptor activation suppresses this synaptic connection. Furthermore, manipulation of this pathway by optogenetic activation or administration of D1 agonist or D2 antagonist could restore impaired task-switching flexibility in mice with local NAc dopamine depletion, and are consistent with the effects of knocking down the expression of dopamine receptors in the pathway. Together, our results point to a critical role of a specific prelimbic cortex-NAc subpathway in mediating strategy abandoning allowing the switching of one strategy to another in problem solving.

14111715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14111715.value: The ability to abandon old strategies and adopt new ones is essential for survival in a constantly changing environment. While previous studies suggest the importance of the prefrontal cortex and some subcortical areas in the generation of strategy-switching flexibility, the fine neural circuitry and receptor mechanisms involved are not fully understood. We have uncovered a pathway that underlies the ability to abandon an old strategy and adopts a new one. This ability is known to be affected under pathological conditions such as Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease. Therefore, future studies could aim to decipher the changes of this pathway, and other related pathways, in leading to cognitive rigidity found in some brain disorders.

14111715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14111715.value: Strategy-switching flexibility is a critical executive function necessary for living in an ever-evolving environment and this ability is often impaired in attentional deficit and hyperactivity disorder, schizophrenia, and early Parkinson’s disease. To date, the underlying brain circuitry and receptor mechanisms are not entirely clear. The results of the present study suggest the essential role of a specific projection from prelimbic cortex to nucleus accumbens (NAc) D2 medium spiny neurons as well as NAc dopamine and presynaptic dopamine receptors of this projection in controlling the strategy-switching flexibility. These findings promote a better understanding of circuitry and neurobiology of strategy-switching flexibility and could contribute to identify novel therapeutic targets for patients suffering from strategy-switching inflexibility.

14111815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14111815.value: Parkinson’s disease is the second most common neurodegenerative disease, resulting in severe motor disability in patients. Five millions of the Chinese population are expected to suffer Parkinson’s disease in 2030, imposing a great burden to the health care system. Unfortunately, the pathogenic process that leads to the appearance of Parkinsonian symptoms is not clearly understood. As such, there is no cure for the disease and all current treatments only aim to suppress the motor symptoms. Therefore, there is an urgent need to uncover the pathogenic processes in Parkinson’s disease, to enable the development of radically improved treatment or a complete cure. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a common feature in Parkinson’s disease and could represent a key pathogenic pathway in this disorder. At the same time, compelling clinical and experimental evidence suggests that abnormal accumulation of iron in the brain contributes to dopaminergic neuron death in the midbrain substantia nigra of Parkinson’s disease patients. Recently, a novel mitochondrial iron delivery mechanism has been discovered, and such pathway involves a newly identified iron transporter protein, transferrin receptor-2 (TfR2). Here, we hypothesize that the upregulation of TfR2 plays a key role in abnormal iron accumulation in the mitochondria that underlies the selective degeneration of dopaminergic neurons. In this proposal, based on cell and animal models of Parkinson’s disease, experiments are designed 1) to investigate if selective upregulation of TfR2 in the substantia nigra alone can induce dopaminergic neuron loss and cause Parkinsonism; 2) to investigate the pathogenic mechanism involved by studying the relationship between TfR2-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and iron accumulation; and 3) to explore the causes of pathologic TfR2 upregulation in Parkinson’s disease. The results will provide significant insight on the pathogenic mechanism to develop novel therapeutic strategies for treating Parkinson’s disease. 帕金森病是一種能夠導致人類嚴重運動障礙的第二大常見的神經退行性疾​​病。到2030年，預測將有500萬中國人患帕金森病，這將成為醫療保健系統一個很大的負擔。然而，導致帕金森病形成的發病過程還不是很清楚，到目前為止也沒有治愈這種疾病的方法，對於目前所有的治療方式都只能改善其運動障礙。因此，現在急需闡明帕金森病的發病過程，從而從根本上改善治療手段或者找到一種治癒疾病的方法。 線粒體功能障礙是一種能夠代表疾病發病的關鍵的病理特徵，同時，臨床和實驗結果都已經證實鐵異常聚集於帕金森病人中腦黑質區域，從而導致多巴胺神經元的死亡。最近，一種由鐵轉運蛋白-運鐵蛋白受體-2介導的新的線粒體鐵轉運機制被發現，因此，我們預測高表達的運鐵蛋白受體-2介導的線粒體鐵異常聚集，從而導致多巴胺神經元的選擇性退化。 我們的研究計劃書以帕金森病的細胞和動物模型為基礎，實驗設計包括以下三部分：1）探究特異性在黑質區高表達運鐵蛋白受體-2能否引起多巴胺能神經元死亡從而導致帕金森綜合症；2）探究在帕金森病發病機理中關於運鐵蛋白受體-2導致的線粒體障礙和鐵聚集的關係；3）探索在帕金森病中病理性運鐵蛋白受體-2高表達的原因。這些研究結果將讓我們更加了解帕金森病的發病機制，從而研究出新的治療帕金森病的方法。

14111815.label: Realisation of objectives
14111815.value: The team has basically completed fully the 3 major objectives of the proposal. We have answered if TfR2 is sufficient inducing PD-like disease phenotypes by viral construction and administration. There were initial issues with virus expression and behavioural models but have overcome the difficulty. We also probed the pathogenic mechanism of TfR2 in inducing PD-like phenotype and related to iron accumulation in the mitochondria, via different methodologies. We also investigated the involvement of mitochondrial dysfunction as a major mechanism related to the effect of TfR2 over expression. Finally, the binding of Tf/TfR2 involvement in TfR2 up regulation in PD was elucidated. Overall, we have realised the objectives of the proposal. Some preliminary findings related to the proposal were presented in a conference and published in journal articles. A manuscript is also planned for the dissemination of the full results obtained.

14111815.label: Major findings and research outcome
14111815.value: In this project, based on our preliminary observation of the possible involvement of TfR2 in PD pathogenesis, we performed a series of experiments to probe the detailed roles and mechanism of TfR2 in the process. We obtained a number of key findings. We found that in the rotenone model of PD, TfR2 was increased and in particular in the dopaminergic neurons. Also, TfR2 over expression of lentivirus was successfully constructed, and when injected into the midbrain of rats, induced substantial dopaminergic neuronal loss. Concerning the mechanics of action, we found that over expression of TfR2 is associated with increase of iron content in the dopaminergic neurons. We also found evidence of TfR2 colocalization with the mitochondrial marker Grp75 in the rotenone-induced PD model. This was accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction including complex I activity impairment, decreased ATP production and increased ROS level. TfR2 knockdown can improve cell survival. Finally, we obtained evidence that mitochondrial TfR2 can be regulated by Tf level, and that complex I is also be involved in inducing TfR2 changes observed. Together, the results of this project support the notion that TfR2 could be a major player in the pathogenesis in the Parkinsonism.

14111815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14111815.value: This project has discovered a role in the regulation of mitochondrial function by TfR2 and its possible involvement in the pathogenesis of Parkinsonism. These basic findings have strong implications for the treatment of Parkinson's disease. Future development of the research should emphasise on the translational potential of TfR2 in treating Parkinson's disease and other neurodegenerative diseases. Clinically oriented fundings, e.g. from the Health and Medical Research Fund, should be attempted.

14111815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14111815.value: Parkinson’s disease is the second most common neurodegenerative disease, resulting in severe motor disability in patients. There is still no cure for the disease and all current treatments only aim to suppress the motor symptoms. Therefore, there is an urgent need to uncover the pathogenic processes in Parkinson’s disease, to enable the development of radically improved treatment or a complete cure. Mitochondrial dysfunction is a common feature in Parkinson’s disease and could represent a key pathogenic pathway in this disorder. At the same time, compelling clinical and experimental evidence suggests that abnormal accumulation of iron in the brain contributes to dopaminergic neuron death in the midbrain substantia nigra of Parkinson’s disease patients. In this project, we have discovered that the newly identified iron transport protein transferrin receptor 2 could be a key factor in the pathogenesis of Parkinson's disease, by causing abnormal iron increases in the mitochondria leading to cell dysfunction or cell death. The results therefore provide significant insight on the pathogenic mechanism to develop novel therapeutic strategies for treating Parkinson’s disease.
