14112915.label: Realisation of objectives
14112915.value: Three specific aims have been accomplished. For Specific aim 1: To optimize the overexpression efficiency of muscle-specific MAR1 transfer system in aged mice skeletal muscle in terms of dosage and duration. Ninety 18-month-old male C57BL/6 mice were subjected to MAR1 overexpression vector administration for 6 months. There were three different dosages of MAR1 overexpression vector, including low dose (Lo, 2.5x10^8 IU/ml), medium dose (Me, 5.0x10^8 IU/ml) and high dose (Hi, 10.0x10^8 IU/ml). Total 15μl of viral preparation was injected into each muscle. MAR1 overexpression vector was administered based on the following three different approaches. For single injection with three dosages (Lo-Si, Me-Si, Hi-Si), vector was administered only at Month 0 (M0). For double injections with three dosages (Lo-Do, Me-Do, Hi-Do), vector was administered at M0 and M3. For triple injections with three dosages (Lo-Tr, Me-Tr, Hi-Tr), vector was administered at M0, M2 and M4. Thus, there were nine injection groups (n=10 for each group). In addition, ten more 18-month-old male C57BL/6 mice served as age-matched control without any injections for 6 months (Age-matched control). Another ten more mice were sacrificed before the treatment as baseline (Baseline control). MAR1 overexpression vector was injected at the mid-portion of one side gastrocnemius (GA) muscle and tibialis antierior (TA) muscle of each mouse. The contralateral GA and TA muscles served as the control by injecting empty vector (Vector control). After 6 months of administration, both sides of GA and TA muscles were dissected and snap frozen in liquid nitrogen-cooled isopentane and then embedded in OCT medium for subsequent cryosectioning. Muscle cross sections were measured under fluorescence microscope to compare transfection efficiency by quantifying the percentage of GFP-positive fibers. The remaining GA and TA muscles underwent real-time PCR analysis of MAR1 Level to compare the overexpression efficiency of lenti-MSA-MAR1-eGFP vector among different groups. For Specific aim 2: To evaluate the effect of MAR1 overexpression on muscle mass, muscle size, muscle structure and muscle function in aged mice skeletal muscle. Ten 18-month-old male C57BL/6 mice were treated with MAR1 overexpression vector for 6 months with optimized protocol obtained from aim 1 study, which was administered every two months at high dose (10.0x10^8 IU/ml). MAR1 overexpression vector was injected into the mid-portion of left GA and TA muscles of each mouse. Ten more 18-month-old male C57BL/6 mice served as age-matched control without any injections for 6 months (Age-matched control). Another ten more mice was sacrificed before the treatment as baseline (Baseline control). All the mice were sacrificed at the age of 24 months except baseline control. GA and TA muscles were dissected. Before sacrifice, the GA and TA underwent in situ functional testing, including muscle maximal isometric (tetanic and twitch) force, twitch contraction time and half relaxation time. The muscles were collected and muscle weight was recorded. The muscle was processed for cryosectioning as described previously. The muscle cross sections underwent the routine histological staining and histoimmunochemical staining for dystophin for quantifying the fiber CSA. The MAR1 level in all the muscles were examined by real-time PCR at the termination of treatment. For Specific aim 3: To explore the underlying mechanism(s) of MAR1 in regulating SRF- and autophagy-related pathways in aged mice skeletal muscle. The muscle cross sections from aim 2 study underwent the immunohistochemical staining for SRF localization. The total RNA of remaining GA and TA muscles was extracted for real-time PCR analysis of SRF- (SRF, MRTF-A, and STARS) and autophagy- (Beclin1, LC3, and LAMP-2) related signaling markers mRNA levels. The protein level of the above markers and the ratio of LC3-II/I that represented ongoing autophagy was analyzed by western blotting. Furthermore, using bioinformatics technology, the target microRNA of lncRNA, microRNA-487b (miR-487b), and the target protein of microRNA, Wnt5a, were predicted and validated in vitro by luciferase reporter assays and pull-down assay. The research work of the project has been published in two journal publications and reported in two international conferences. Meanwhile, the researcher that supported by the grant also contributed to seven other musculoskeletal research projects which acknowledged the grant in the publications. The information of publications in peer-reviewed journals with impact factor higher than 5 was listed in Part C: Research Output.

14112915.label: Major findings and research outcome
14112915.value: MAR1 expression was dose-dependently overexpressed in aged mice skeletal muscle in the MAR1 transfected groups. In addition, MAR1 expression was higher in the Hi-Tr group than the other groups, suggesting the Hi-Tr (triple injections of MAR1 overexpression vector at the dosage of 10.0 x 10^8 IU/ml for 6 months) treatment of MAR1 as the optimal approach. Using the above administration protocol, 18-month-old mice were intramuscularly injected every two months with muscle-specific MAR1 overexpression vector and sacrificed at 24-month-old. Compared to baseline and age-matched control group, the expression level of MAR1 in MAR1 overexpression group was notably higher. GA muscle mass and mean muscle fiber CSA were both reduced in the age-matched group compared to those in baseline group, while these two parameters were enhanced in MAR1 group. Furthermore, the results of in situ muscle functional testing showed that GA muscle in aged group had weaker strength than baseline group, while MAR1 group generated a higher force than other two groups. A similar trend was also observed in TA muscle. The mRNA and protein levels of myogenic markers (MyoD, MyoG, Mef2c and Myf5), SRF signaling (SRF, MRTF-A, and STARS) and autophagy-related markers (Beclin1, LC3, and LAMP-2) were significantly lower in age-matched group compared to those in baseline group. The myogenic marker was significantly higher in MAR1 overexpression group than those in baseline group. The mRNA and protein levels of SRF, LC3 and LAMP-2 were also elevated in MAR1 overexpression group. The mRNA and protein levels of other markers (MRTF-1, STARS and Beclin1) were comparable between age-matched group and MAR1 overexpression group. The ratio of LC3-II/I was also lower in age-matched group and higher in MAR1 overexpression group compared to that in baseline group, indicating autophagy might be involved in MAR1 function. Furthermore, miR-487b was predicted to be the target of MAR1 by bioinformatics analysis. Pull-down assay and luciferase assay validated the direct binding between miR-487b and MAR1. Wnt5a, an important regulator during myogenesis, served as a target of miR-487b. In vitro study confirmed that miR-487b targeted Wnt5a protein to modulate muscle differentiation. Taken together, the lncRNA MAR1 acts as a miR-487b sponge to regulate Wnt5a protein, resulting in promoting muscle differentiation and regeneration (Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle, 2018). Inspired by the project, our research team has also identified a series of lncRNAs, which have a diversity of functions through various mechanisms in skeletal muscle (Molecular Therapy, 2018).

14112915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14112915.value: The current project established MAR1’s role as an important skeletal muscle anabolic enhancer, which reveal the function of lncRNA and potential mechanisms underlying. The project inspired the extensive studies about lncRNA’s function in muscle homeostasis, especially during skeletal atrophy induced by aging or mechanical unloading. Our research team has identified a series of lncRNAs, which have a diversity of functions through various mechanisms in skeletal muscle. Meanwhile, this project also provided potential therapeutic targets and novel muscle anabolic strategy to prevent or reverse aged-related muscle loss in the elderly population. Our team has started to study the possibility of interfering the interaction between miR-487b and Wnt5a in skeletal muscle during aging, thereby to attenuate the sarcopenia development.

14112915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14112915.value: Sarcopenia, defined as the age-related loss of muscle mass and strength, is associated with serious health consequences. In current project, a newly identified Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs), named MAR1, was studied. MAR1 expression was associated with the expression of myogenic markers and serum response factor (SRF)- and autophagy-related markers in vitro and in vivo. MAR1 dramatically decreased during aging. Enforced MAR1 expression in skeletal muscle by MAR1 overexpression vector could promote muscle mass and strength in aged mice and counteract sarcopenia development. MAR1 overexpression could also enhance SRF and autophagy signaling. Mechanistically, MAR1 could act as a miR-487b sponge to regulate Wnt5a protein, resulting in promoting muscle differentiation and regeneration. The project established MAR1’s role as an important skeletal muscle anabolic enhancer, and also provided a novel lncRNA-based muscle anabolic strategy to prevent or reverse aged-related muscle loss in the elderly population, thereby reducing various adverse health consequences.

14113315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113315.value: Our research question is: Does surgical intervention in children with mild obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) improve neurocognitive outcomes? Childhood OSA is common and it is associated with important morbidities, namely cardiovascular abnormalities as well as neurocognitive and metabolic disturbances. There is accumulating evidence to suggest that these abnormalities and especially neurocognitive deficits are present even in children with mild OSA, defined as an obstructive apnoea hypopnoea index (OAHI) between 1 and 5 events per hour of sleep. The first-line treatment for childhood OSA is adenotonsillectomy. However, there has been no controlled study to evaluate the effectiveness of adenotonsillectomy in ameliorating neurocognitive disturbances in children with mild OSA. Few paediatric cohort studies with methodological concerns provided conflicting findings on whether these abnormalities are potentially reversible following treatment. In this study we will randomly assign pre-pubertal non-obese children, aged 6 to 11 years with mild OSA to surgical intervention or a strategy of watchful waiting. The surgical intervention includes adenotonsillectomy +/- turbinate reduction if latter is deemed necessary according to pre-defined criteria, to be carried out within 4-6 weeks after ENT assessment. Both groups will undergo nocturnal polysomnography, neurocognitive assessment and review by an ENT surgeon before and after a 6-month intervention period. The primary outcome is change in T-scores from Conners’ continuous performance test (CPT) in the two study groups over the intervention period. Secondary outcomes will include changes in indexes of behaviour, functional memory, quality of life and OSA severity (OAHI and respiratory disturbance index [RDI]). We hypothesize that surgical intervention will lead to significant improvements in neurocognitive outcomes. If this study confirms neurocognitive abnormalities in children with mild OSA are amendable following treatment, such novel information will be useful in parents counseling. The result will also be an important catalyst for change in our current management approach for this prevalent and important condition. 我們的研究問題是：手術治療能否改善輕度阻塞性睡眠呼吸暫停（OSA）患兒的神經認知功能？ 兒童OSA是十分常見的睡眠問題，其併發症可能包括心血管異常，神經認知功能受損及代謝紊亂。愈來愈多證據指出這些併發症在輕度OSA（阻塞性睡眠呼吸暫停低通氣指數[OAHI]為每小時1至5次）的患兒也會出現，尤其是神經認知方面的損害。 扁桃體增殖體切除術是兒童OSA的第一線治療。然而，一直沒有任何對照研究以評估該手術對改善輕度OSA患兒的神經認知異常的成效。只有少數群組研究探討OSA患兒的神經認知異常是否可憑藉治療得以回復正常，但始終未有一致的結論。 在這項研究中，研究對象為6至11歲確診患有輕度OSA的青春期前非肥胖兒童，我們將隨機分配參加者至手術干預組或觀察等待組。手術干預組的參加者將接受增殖體扁桃體切除術。如果患兒同時患有過敏性鼻炎，並在耳鼻喉檢查中發現鼻甲肥大，患兒將同時接受鼻甲減容術。手術將在耳鼻喉科檢查後4至6週內進行。兩組的參加者均會在干預前及干預後6個月進行夜間多導睡眠監測、神經認知功能評估及耳鼻喉檢查。此研究的主要結果指標是克氏持續性操作測驗(Conners’ Continuous Performance Test, CPT)中的T-分數干預期前後的改變。次要結果指標包括行為、生活質素及OSA嚴重程度（OAHI和呼吸紊亂指數[RDI]）的改變。 我們假設手術干預可使神經認知功能顯著改善。如果這個研究證實輕度OSA兒童的神經認知功能異常經治療後可改善，此重要信息將可作為說服家長接受子女進行該手術的理據。研究結果也將促使我們改變目前針對這普遍而重要的疾病的管理方法。

14113315.label: Realisation of objectives
14113315.value: A total of 99 children diagnosed to have mild obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) (defined as obstructive apnoea hypopnoea index (OAHI) between 1 and 5/h) were recruited. Five and two of them were excluded because of obesity and reaching puberty, respectively. Ninety-two non-obese prepubertal children were enrolled and randomly allocated to early adenotonsillectomy (AT) or watchful waiting (WW) groups. Subjects allocated to the AT group were arranged for early AT and repeat assessment was conducted 6 months after AT. Those allocated to the WW group were put on the waitlist of AT and reevaluated 9-10 months after the baseline visit. Six of them are still pending for the follow-up visit. Among the remaining 86 subjects, 56 successfully completed the study protocol whereas 30 were excluded or drop-out. Their group allocations were disclosed upon completion or termination of the study. A total of 41 subjects were allocated to the AT group, of whom 26 completed the study protocol. Fifteen (37%) were excluded due to refusal of follow-up (n=7, 17%), refusal of surgery (n=6, 15%), or incomplete primary outcome data (n=2, 5%). Forty-five subjects were allocated to the WW group, of whom 30 completed the study protocol. Fifteen (33%) were excluded due to refusal of follow-up (n=10, 22%) or incomplete primary outcome data (n=5, 11%). According to our initial sample size estimation, a total of 70 subjects are required for this study. Therefore, we need to recruit at least 8 more participants. We are hopeful that this can be done in the coming months. The study has taken a longer time than expected to carry out recruitment and complete all necessary baseline and repeat assessments due to the following reasons: - Our sleep research service was stopped during the peak flu period which lasted from January to April each year, and in 2018 the period was unexpectedly prolonged. - Cases allocated to the treatment group were expected to undergo surgery within a short timeframe, 6-8 weeks after seeing our ENT colleagues but unfortunately in many instances this did not happen as a result of operation list being cancelled, cases with more urgent illnesses taking up the operation slot. This has led to delay in the repeat assessment. - The drop-out and treatment refusal rate was higher than expected. Attempts to overcome problems: - we have offered to carry out sleep study assessment at weekends but once again it depends on bed availability and whether parents / carers are able to accompany their children for hospital admission at weekends. - we have liaised with ward manager and nursing colleagues regarding the use of our day ward for sleep study assessment. Usage of our day ward is less affected by acute emergency admissions. Liaison work involves providing extra manpower to cover for the day ward, generation of a new admission code and approval by hospital hierarchy and our application has recently been approved. This initiative can begin this coming summer. At both baseline and follow-up visits, all participants underwent nocturnal polysomnography (PSG), Conner’s continuous performance test (CPT) and upper airway examination. Their parents completed a set of questionnaires including an OSA symptom questionnaire (HKCSQ), quality of life questionnaire (OSA-18), modified Epworth sleepiness scale (ESS), paediatric daytime sleepiness scale (PDSS), attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) rating scale and child behaviour checklist (CBCL). The complete dataset of 56 subjects who have completed the study is ready for preliminary statistical analysis. General linear models and generalized estimating equations were used to test the group, time and group*time effects on continuous and categorical outcomes, respectively. All statistical analyses were performed on a per-protocol basis.

14113315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113315.value: After AT, OAHI decreased significantly, accompanied by a slight increase in body mass index (BMI). The commission T score obtained from CPT, which is a marker of inattentiveness and impulsivity, was significantly reduced after AT. The WW group did not show any significant change in OSA severity and BMI z score. The Hit reaction time standard error T score, which is marker of inattentiveness, was significantly reduced after the intervention period. On the other hand, the AT group had significant improvements in OSA-related symptoms over the WW group. Prevalence of habitual snoring, nocturnal oral breathing, and morning dry mouth significantly decreased in the AT group but not the WW group. The hyperactivity subscale of the ADHD-rating scale also significantly decreased after AT. Daytime sleepiness scales and the inattention subscale of the ADHD-rating scale did not change significantly, however. OSA-18 quality of life total score also significantly improved only in the AT but not in the WW group. In addition, significant improvements in behavioural problems were demonstrated after AT. The internalizing problem score derived from CBCL was significantly reduced. The anxious/depressed, somatic complaints and thought problems subscales were improved in the AT group. On the other hand, the anxious/depressed and the rule breaking behaviour subscales were improved in the WW group. In summary, the results of this randomised controlled trial supported that AT can significantly reduce OSA severity, accompanied by an improvement in inattention and impulsivity measured by an objective tool. AT can also improve OSA-related symptoms and quality of life, and internalising behavioural problems subjectively reported by parents.

14113315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113315.value: Data of this randomised controlled trial support the causal relationship between mild OSA and inattention and impulsivity in a group of non-obese prepubertal children. However, there are still a number of unanswered questions related to the effectiveness of adenotonsillectomy (AT) on treating mild OSA in children, and to the association between childhood OSA and cognitive and behavioural outcomes. Although OAHI was significantly reduced after AT, most of the subjects still had an OAHI >1/h, indicating a residual disease. We are most interested in knowing which child benefited the most and which did not benefit at all. We may also try to determine if there is any predictor of residual OSA that can be identified before AT. Further analysis will be conducted to compare the resolved group to the residual group. It will also be interesting to investigate the underlying causes of the disordered breathing during sleep despite the removal of tonsils and/or adenoid. Drug-induced sleep endoscopy may be arranged to identify where the obstructions occur. Inattention and hyperactivity may only be found in some of the children with OSA but not the others. We shall try to identify a better outcome predictor in children with OSA by comparing OSA children with and without inattention and hyperactivity problems.

14113315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113315.value: Previous studies investigating the association between childhood OSA and cognitive and behavioural problems provide inconsistent and conflicting results. Our study was the first randomised controlled trial investigating the effects of surgical removal of tonsils and/or adenoid on attention/hyperactivity and other behavioural outcomes specifically in children with mild OSA. The study was based on a group of non-obese prepubertal children with mild OSA with adenotonsillar hypertrophy who are typically seen in clinical settings. The results revealed that the surgical procedure can effectively ameliorate the severity of OSA and improve inattention and impulsivity objectively measured by nocturnal sleep study and a computerized attention test (Conners’ continuous performance test), respectively. Moreover, OSA-related symptoms and internalising behavioural problems subjectively reported by parents were also improved after the surgery. These findings supported that mild OSA in children may induce inattention, impulsivity and internalising behavioural problems, which can be reversed after surgical treatment of OSA.

14113515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113515.value: 背景： 儘管體外衝擊波碎石術（SWL）已有超過30年的應用，治療方案仍在不斷發展。最近在實驗室和動物研究上發現能量水平逐漸提高的治療方案（「遞增」治療方案），比標準的「固定能量」 治療方案 ，能産生更好的碎石效果。然而，目前在這方面的臨床數據仍然沒有定論。此外，「遞增」治療方案對急性腎損傷和病人的耐受並未有得到徹底臨床評估。因此，我們提出了一個前瞻性隨機試驗來研究這兩種治療方案 ，對結石患者在體外沖擊波碎石治療後的影響。 目標 1.比較兩種方案在結石治療十二週後的成功率。 2比較兩種方案在結石治療後引致急性腎損傷的程度，並發症發生率和患者的耐受性的分別。 方法： 300 位患有5至15mm腎結石，並計劃作 SWL 治療的病人，將會被邀請參與這項研究。在獲得知情同意書後，患者將被隨機分配到「遞增」治療方案坡（首1000 衝擊波能量水平為 60％，隨後1000 衝擊波為 70％能量水平，而最後的1000 衝擊波為 80％的能量水平）或「固定能量」 治療方案 （所有3000衝擊波為 80％的能量水平）。我們將利用患者自控鎮痛系統 （PCA）和視覺模擬量表測量，評估患者在治療中痛楚程度。我們亦同時收集術前後的尿液樣本作量度多種急性腎損傷標記，其中包括N-乙酰基 - β-D-葡萄糖苷酶（NAG），中性粒細胞明膠酶相關脂質運載蛋白（NGAL），腎損傷分子-1（KIM-1），白細胞介素18 （IL-18）和尿蛋白，作評估兩種方案對SWL 急性腎損傷的程度比較。 隨後患者會安排在治療後的第二天、第六星期及第十二星期覆診。尿液樣本將會在每次覆診時收集，以量度治療後腎臟損害的程度。在第二天的檢查時，閣下將接受磁力共震或電腦掃瞄，以檢查血腫是否存在。閣下會在治療後的第七天、第四星期及第十二星期接受X-光檢視治療結果，最後患者將接受電腦掃瞄以記錄排石狀況。 結果評價： 本研究的主要成果是評估結石治療成功率，即在 SWL 12週後 結石完全清除或只餘下少於4毫米的碎片。其他評估結果包括兩個方案對腎損傷的影響（包括在尿液標記物腎血腫形成的機會），術後併發症發生率，治療過程中的疼痛，止痛藥的使用量和結石完全清除率。

14113515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113515.value: In this prospective study, 300 patients (150 per group) were recruited between February 2016 and June 2018, and randomized to receive SWL delivered using a ramping (First 1000 shocks at energy level-5, followed by 1000shocks at energy level-6 and 1000 final shocks at energy level-7; Group-1) or fixed-voltage (All 3000 shocks at energy level-7; Group-2) protocols by Modulith SLX-F2. From our results, there was no significant different in the patient and stone characteristics of the two groups. However, Group-1 received significantly lower energy delivered than Group-2 (14.8% less, p<0.001). The treatment success rates for Group-1 and Group-2 were 67.8% and 73.6%, respectively, and were not statistically different (crude odds ratio for Group-1: 0.753; 95% confidence interval 0.456 to 1.244; p=0.268). The stone-free rates for Group-1 and Group-2 were 36.6% and 41.9%, respectively, and did not differ between the groups. However, in Group-1 and Group-2, 23.8% and 43.8% of patients developed perinephric hematoma, respectively, and was statistically significant difference (p<0.001). Otherwise, the pain experienced during treatment, analgesics usage, unplanned hospital admission were similar for the two groups. A multivariate analysis was performed to assess the factors related to the treatment outcomes of SWL and the development of hematoma. Here, stone size was the only identified predictor of treatment success. A larger stone size, higher dose of energy and the use of a fixed voltage protocol were found to predict a greater likelihood of hematoma formation after treatment. Both groups exhibited statistically significant increases in the urinary levels of all markers after SWL and returned to the baseline at 6 weeks after SWL. However, no inter-group differences were observed in any urinary marker level. Therefore, in conclusion, the fixed-voltage SWL and ramping protocols provided similar treatment success rates for renal stones. However, ramping protocol could reduce the incidence of post-SWL perinephric hematoma. Therefore, the ramping protocol should be the recommended protocol to be used for patients suffered from renal stone.

14113515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113515.value: In this study, we have shown that the use of voltage escalation (ramping) protocol could provide similar efficacy and yet less renal injury to kidney during shockwave lithotripsy. Therefore, this will be recommended to be the standard protocol for our patients care. While this treatment protocol could help to decrease the haematoma formation, the acute renal injury markers remain similar to the standard protocol. Therefore, there are still room to further improve the safety of shockwave lithotripsy to patients. Recently, there are some studies to suggest the use of calcium channel blocker or angiotensin receptor blockers might help to decrease the ischemic insult to the kidney and decrease in the change in renal injury markers. However, vasoconstriction is also one of the factors that help to prevent haematoma formation after shockwave lithotripsy. Therefore, it might be an area that could further explore in future research in shockwave lithotripsy.

14113815.label: Project Objectives
14113815.value: Acute inflammation in the iris and ciliary body/processes can be triggered in 24 hrs by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) injection. GHRHR and its downstream molecules are upregulated in these tissues, particularly in the ciliary epithelium and immune cells infiltrated into the aqueous humor. Activation of this signaling axis is possibly triggered by a binding of LPS to Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) on these tissues, which in term triggers production of GHRH. To test this hypothesis, we shall examine TLR4 and GHRH expression in normal ocular tissues, and investigate whether its changes after LPS injection. The specific increases in GHRHR expression in ciliary epithelium and infiltrated immune cells suggest that they may serve as sources of GH and IGF1 during the inflammation process. To test whether ciliary epithelium and one of the major immune cells, macrophages, respond to LPS by synthesizing GH and IGF1, gene expression of GHRH signaling molecules and secretion of GH and IGF1 will be examined in explant culture of iris and ciliary body, and in culture of a macrophage cell line RAW264.7 or a retina derived macrophages. Whether the production of hormones is dependent on GHRHR and TLR-4 will be tested by blocking GHRHR activities with peptide antagonist and knocking down of TLR-4 with siRNA. GHRHR is localized on leukocytes and macrophages in the aqueous humor but not on those in the stroma of iris and ciliary processes, suggesting that GHRHR activation is related to the migration of cells from these tissues to the aqueous humor. This possible action of GHRHR will be tested in a transwell preparation in which motility of RAW264.7 macrophages or retina derived macrophages is investigated after treatment with LPS, and the effects of GHRH antagonist or agonist on this LPS induced macrophage migration will be determined. Preliminary results showed that inflammation develops in posterior segments of the eye after a prolonged survival (2 days) of LPS treatment. This includes activation of macrophages in the retina and infiltration of immune cells in the vitreous humor. Since GHRHR and its downstream molecules are expressed in the retina, inflammatory responses stimulated by LPS in the posterior segments of the eye may also be mediated by GHRHR signaling. To test this hypothesis, we shall examine inflammatory changes in the retina and vitreous body 48 hrs after LPS treatment, and determine the anti-inflammatory effects of inhibiting GHRHR activities with peptide antagonists.

14113815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113815.value: The growth hormone-releasing hormone, growth hormone, insulin-like growth factor-1 (GHRH-GH-IGF1) signaling axis, a classical hormone regulatory pathway, has been shown to exert regulatory functions on immune system. Recent findings in our laboratory have demonstrated that expression of GHRH receptor (GHRHR) is highly increased in the iris and ciliary body in the rat eye one day after stimulation of a bacterial endotoxin lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Genetic analyses confirmed that GHRH signaling genes, which include Pit-1, GHRHR, SV1, GHRH and GH are all elevated specifically in the iris and ciliary body, as well as in the inflammatory cells in the aqueous humor. Blocking GHRHR activity with MIA-609, a highly specific GHRH antagonist, provides significant anti-inflammatory effects to this acute inflammation. A single dose of antagonist reduces accumulation of leukocytes and macrophages and exudation of protein in the aqueous humor. It also suppresses the secretion of factors that induce tissue damage in the eye. These effects are associated with a suppression of production of GH and IGF1, and are not observed in animals treated with an agonist peptide of GHRH. In this proposal, we will further explore mechanisms that underlie anti-inflammatory actions of this signaling axis. We will first investigate whether the LPS receptor toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) and GHRH is expressed in ciliary epithelium and the inflammatory cells, because it may provide a link to how GHRHR activity is regulated by LPS and whether these tissue and cells serve as local source of GHRH. Second, using a culture system we will test whether iris/ciliary body and macrophages are able to produce and secrete GH and IGF1 after stimulation of LPS, and whether this secretion is blocked by GHRH antagonist and suppressing TLR4 expression. Third, as GHRHR is expressed on the inflammatory cells in the aqueous humor but not on those in the stroma of ocular tissues, suggesting a role of GHRHR in this migration process. We will use a migration assay to test whether GHRHR is essential for migration of macrophages upon LPS stimulation. Lastly, LPS induced inflammation is also observed in the posterior segments of the eye 48 hours after LPS stimulation. We plan to test whether GHRH antagonist is an effective anti-inflammatory agent to inflammation in the retina and vitreous body. These findings will provide crucial information on the role of GHRH-GH-IGF1 signaling in acute ocular inflammation, and more importantly, on potential use of GHRH antagonists in treatment of this disease. 生長激素釋放激素，生長激素，胰島素樣生長因子-1 （GHRH-GH-IGF1）信號傳遞軸除了是一個典型激素調節途徑， 亦發揮調節免疫系統的功能。我們最近的實驗研究結果表明， 被細菌內毒素脂多醣（LPS）刺激一天後，在大鼠眼虹膜睫狀體 中，GHRH受體（GHRHR）的表達大大提高。遺傳分析證實， GHRH信號傳遞基因，包括Pit-1，GHRHR，SV1，GHRH和GH 都特別在虹膜睫狀體中，以及在房水的炎性細胞中升高。 MIA-609，一個高特異性的GHRH拮抗劑，能阻斷GHRHR活動 及在這個急性炎症中提供顯著抗炎作用。單劑量的拮抗劑降低 白血球細胞、巨噬細胞和滲出蛋白在房水的積累。它也抑制誘 導眼睛組織損傷的因子分泌。這些作用都與抑制生產GH和IGF-1 相關聯，並且不能在GHRH激動劑肽治療的動物中觀察到。在這 研究提案中，我們將進一步探討這種信號軸的抗炎作用機制。 我們將首先調查脂多醣受體toll like-receptor 4（TLR4）和GHRH 是否表達於睫狀體上皮和炎症細胞，因為它可提示這些組織和 細胞是否調控由LPS引發的GHRHR活性和是否GHRH的來源。 其次，使用一個培養系統，我們將測試虹膜/睫狀體和巨噬細胞 在LPS刺激後，是否能夠產生和分泌GH和IGF-1，和該分泌是否 被GHRH拮抗劑阻止和抑制TLR4表達。第三，隨著炎性細胞從 眼組織滲進房水後GHRHR的表達明顯增加，表明在此遷移過程 GHRHR的可能作用。我們將使用一個遷移測定來測試GHRHR 是否是在LPS刺激的巨噬細胞遷移發揮作用。最後，LPS刺激後 48小時，觀察到眼睛後段產生炎症。我們計劃測試GHRH拮抗劑 在視網膜和玻璃體炎，是否一個有效的抗炎劑。這些研究結果 將對GHRH-GH-IGF1信號在急性眼部炎症的作用提供重要信息， 和GHRH拮抗劑在治療本病的潛在用途。

14113815.label: Realisation of objectives
14113815.value: 1) TLR4 and pro-inflammatory factors production in culture of ciliary body and iris. This objective is fully achieved. To determine whether the ciliary body and iris produce inflammatory cytokines upon stimulation of the lipopolysaccharide (LPS), we developed an explant culture system in which iris and ciliary body from adult Sprague Dawley rats were isolated and grown on a membrane insert without influence of circulating leucocytes during acute inflammation induced by LPS. Using this preparation, we have shown that i) the epithelial cells of the ciliary body and iris were stained strongly with antibody against Toll-like receptor-4 (TLR4), the receptor of LPS, suggesting that these cells are able to respond directly to LPS. ii) RT-PCR and Western blot analysis confirmed GHRHR was highly upregulated in these explants 24 hours after LPS treatment. These increases in GHRHR were observed largely in the epithelial linings of the ciliary body and iris. Exposure to LPS increased expression of IL-1β, IL-6 and iNOS in the ocular explants, which was suppressed by blocking GHRHR activity with MIA-602 (antagonist of GHRHR) but not by MR-409 (potent agonist of GHRHR). ELISA results showed that the surge of IL-6 in the medium after LPS treatment was abolished by MIA-602, but not by MR-409, indicating a specific role of GHRHR activity in the synthesis and secretion of pro-inflammatory factors in the ciliary and iris epithelial cells. These findings were confirmed by immunohistochemistry, which showed the upregulation of IL-6 and IL-1β in these epithelial cells 24 hours after LPS treatment. These results together confirm the ability of ciliary and iris epithelial cells in synthesizing inflammatory cytokines upon stimulation of TLR4 with LPS, and suggest a role of these epithelial cells in immune surveillance in anterior segments of the eye, similar to the function of antigen presenting cells residing in the stroma of these ocular tissues. In another study, we have used a human ciliary epithelial cell line to investigate signaling pathways involved in GHRHR mediated inflammatory processes. The results showed that human ciliary epithelial cells increased dramatically gene expression of inflammation-related cytokines 24 hours post LPS treatment. GHRHR was also upregulated in these cells. Bioinformatics analysis of GHRHR promoter region identified several putative binding sites for NFκb. LPS treatment induced phosphorylation of p65 subunit of NFκb both in vivo and in vitro. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (CHIP) assay showed that NFκb-p65 antibody pulled down DNA fragments containing GHRHR promoter region, indicating NFκb subunit p65 transcriptionally binds to and activates GHRHR expression in human ciliary epithelial cells. To identify signaling molecules involved in the downstream signaling of GHRHR, we used bioinformatics to predict several potential binding partners of GHRHR. Immunoprecipitation (IP) assay showed that among these potential candidates JAK2 was able to pull down GHRHR in the human ciliary epithelial cells and in rat ciliary body/iris tissues. Immunofluorescence staining showed that JAK2 was co-localized with GHRHR in the rat ciliary body and iris epithelium, supporting strongly a physical interaction of GHRHR with JAK-2. We also found that STAT3, a known downstream signaling molecule of JAK2, was phosphorylated 24 hours after LPS treatment, both in ocular tissues and in explant culture of ciliary body and iris. RT-PCR analysis showed that the STAT3 downstream targets, including IL-6, COX-2, IL-17A, iNOS and MMP9, were all upregulated after LPS insults, and were suppressed significantly with GHRHR antagonist (MIA-609). These results indicate that GHRHR regulates production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines through JAK2, which induces phosphorylation of transcription factor STAT3 that switches on the expression of pro-inflammatory factors. 2) Interaction of ciliary epithelium and infiltrated inflammatory cells in regulation of GHRHR expression. This objective is fully achieved. To determine whether the leukocytes in the circulating blood are able to regulate GHRHR expression, ciliary and iris explants were grown together with leukocytes at the lower chamber of a Tranwell culture dish. Flow cytometry analysis indicated that about 65% of the isolated cells were CD11b+ monocytes or granulocytes, whilst 25% were CD3+ T-lymphocytes. While GHRHR was markedly elevated in LPS treated explants, the expression was further increased with increasing number of leukocytes seeded in the coculture. These results showed that the presence of circulating leukocytes, which are observed in abundance in aqueous humor during inflammation, can further enhance the inflammatory responses through upregulating GHRHR in the ciliary and iris epithelia. Moreover, we have shown that the level of IGF-1 was highly reduced, rather than elevated, in both ciliary body/iris explants and the leukocytes after LPS treatment, indicating clearly that the signaling mechanism of GHRHR in production of inflammatory cytokines does not involve the classical signaling of GHRH-GH-IGF1 axis. Protein array analysis has identified a chemokine, CXCL2, produced by the leukocytes that potentiates the expression of GHRHR in the ciliary and iris epithelium. Further experiment has been proposed in a grant proposal to define the role of CXCL2 and its receptor CXCR2 in modulating the inflammatory pathways mediated by GHRHR in LPS induced acute inflammation. 3) GHRHR in motility of macrophages This objective is fully achieved. Motility of RAW264.7 macrophages was investigated in a transwell preparation after treatment with LPS. LPS treatment increased the gene expression of GHRHR and inflammatory cytokines in these cells, which was associated with an increased migration of these cells from the upper to lower surface of the Millipore membrane. However, treatments with GHRHR antagonist MIA-602 or agonist MR-409 both increased the migration of cells after LPS treatment, posing an inconclusive role of GHRHR in this process. Further investigations using various doses of agonist and antagonist showed similar results, leading to the conclusion that GHRHR is not the major regulator in migration of macrophages during LPS stimulation. 4) GHRHR in LPS-induced inflammation in the retina and vitreous body. This objective is fully achieved. The effects of blocking GHRHR activity with MIA-602 were investigated in posterior segments of the eye in rats with acute ocular inflammation 48 hours after LPS injection. Results showed that there was no significant reduction in the levels of pro-inflammatory factors IL-1β, TNG-α and IL-6 in vitreous humor after MIA-602 treatment, when compared with controls. Moreover, no obvious changes were observed in the number of activated microglia and activation of astrocytes and microglia in the retina after MIA-602 treatment, leading to the conclusion that blocking GHRHR function does not produce an anti-inflammatory effect in posterior regions of the eye. Using this animal model, we continued to investigate the protective roles of other molecules on retina during acute ocular inflammation. We have shown that the green tea extract provides potent anti-inflammatory action to the retina 48 hours after LPS injection. Green tea extract also provides potent neuroprotective effect to the degenerative changes in the rat retina induced by treatment with sodium iodate. Furthermore, we have established a mouse model of autoimmune uveitis, and shown that green tea catechins could alleviate effectively the inflammatory responses in the retina induced by the autoimmune disorders. Lastly, with collaboration with colleagues in Guangdong Eye Institute and Zhejiang University we have reported a novel role of GHRHR in the survival and proliferation of pterygium epithelial cells, suggesting a potential therapeutic approach of using GHRHR antagonist in treatment of pterygium.

14113815.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113815.value: 1) TLR4 and pro-inflammatory factors production in culture of ciliary body and iris. The results on expression of TLR4 in explant cultures of ciliary body and iris, and the responses of these explants to LPS by upregulating GHRHR and production of pro-inflammatory factors were published in Experimental Eye research (Ren et al., 2019; Publication No. 6). The signaling mechanisms in LPS induced expression of GHRHR, and the down-stream signaling of GHRHR in production of inflammatory cytokines have been published recently in PNAS (Liang et al., 2020; Publication No. 7). These results were also reported in three local and international meetings (please see Part C, Session 9). 2) Interaction of ciliary epithelium and infiltrated inflammatory cells in regulation of GHRHR expression. The influences of leukocytes in modulating expression of GHRHR in explant cultures of ciliary body and iris were reported in the paper published in Experimental Eye Research (Ren et al., 2019; Publication No. 6). 3) GHRHR in motility of macrophages. Since the results are inconclusive, we did not submit the data for publication. These results were reported in the PhD thesis of Dr. REN Jialin. (Please see Part C, Session 10) 4) GHRHR in LPS-induced inflammation in the retina and vitreous body. The effects of GHRHR analogs on inflammatory responses in posterior segment of the eye after are not significant. However, using the same animal model we showed that the green tea extract provided potent anti-inflammatory actions to the retina 48 hours after LPS injection. These results were reported in Scientific Reports (Ren et al., 2018; Publication No. 4). The neuroprotective effects of green tea extract in ocular inflammation were also explored in other animal models of eye diseases. The neuroprotective effects to degenerative changes in the rat retina induced by sodium iodate was reported in Scientific Reports (Yang et al., 2016; Publication No. 1). Using a mouse model of autoimmune uveitis, the neuroprotective effects of green tea catechins on degenerative changes in the retina were published in two communications (Li et al., 2017, IOVS; Publication No. 2; and Li et al., 2019, Scientific Reports; Publication No. 5). The possible role of GHRHR in development of pterygium was reported in IOVS (Qin et al., 2018; Publication No. 3).

14113815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113815.value: The findings generated from this proposal have led to development of the following projects: 1) Preliminary results using protein arrays suggest that CXCL2 is one of the diffusible molecules released from leukocytes that regulates expression of GHRHR in the ciliary and iris epithelium. Further experiments are proposed in a GRF proposal submitted to RGC to investigate the signaling mechanisms underlying the activation of GHRHR after binding of CXCL2 to its receptor CXCR2 that have been shown to express on ciliary epithelium, and if blockage of its receptor CXCR2 will reduce the production of pro-inflammatory factors from the ciliary and iris epithelium. 2) The reduced level of IGF-1 in this inflammatory process has led to the idea that acute ocular inflammation may be alleviated by replenishing exogenous IGF-1 into the eye. This hypothesis was tested in several experiments and reported in the PhD thesis of Dr. YU Qiuxiao (Part C, Session 10). The findings will be prepared as two manuscripts and submitted to international journals. 3) We have also planned to investigate a local delivery of drugs targeting the signaling pathways reported in these papers in animals with acute ocular inflammation. These drugs include the GHRHR antagonist MIA601 and the JAK inhibitor Ruxolitinib.

14113815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113815.value: Ocular inflammation is a major cause of visual impairment attributed to dysregulation of the immune system. To determine the signaling mechanisms contributing to acute ocular inflammation, we investigated the inflammatory cascades in ciliary body and iris of rat eye medicated by the growth hormone-releasing hormone receptor (GHRHR) after stimulation with lipopolysaccharide (LPS). We showed that the LPS receptor TLR4 is expressed on ciliary and iris epithelial cells. Stimulation of TLR4 results in elevated production of inflammatory factors that cause ocular inflammation. Further study using human ciliary epithelial cells showed that NF-κB subunit p65 is phosphorylated in response to LPS, resulting in transcriptional activation of GHRH-R. Bioinformatics analysis and co-immunoprecipitation showed that GHRH-R interact directly with JAK2, which stimulates phosphorylation of STAT3 and leads to production of pro-inflammatory factors. Inflammatory responses are alleviated by inhibiting GHRHR activity with antagonist MIA-602, and by suppressing phosphorylation of STAT3 using JAK-2 inhibitor Ruxolitinib. These findings indicate a functional role of GHRH-R/JAK2/STAT3 signaling axis in acute ocular inflammation, and suggest a novel therapeutic strategy based on treatment with antagonists targeting this signaling pathway.

14114115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14114115.value: 益生元，作為最近新興的功能食品之一，主要組成為不易消化的碳水化合物（NDCs），其特性為可優先被腸道益生菌（如乳酸桿菌和雙歧桿菌）所利用，而且益生菌的選擇性增長能為宿主帶來各種健康益處。鑒於益生元和益生菌對於人類健康改進非常顯著，故利用二者調節人體腸道微生物種群（腸道微生物組）的研究也越來越多。然而，對於益生菌利用高分子量（HMW）益生元的分子機制以及益生元不通的結構特異性對其被益生菌利用率的變化卻鮮有研究發表。 我們以往的研究表明，從食用菌菌核（菌絲緊密連接交織而成的休眠體）製備而成的β－葡聚醣可以作為一種新型高分子量的益生元，當中包括人類組織選擇性地利用的體外研究和小鼠糞便中雙歧桿菌數量改變的體內研究。為了開發這種具備益生元效能的菌核多醣作為功能性食品／食品補充劑，對其被雙歧桿菌利用機制的理解是至關重要的。 我們建議利用雙歧桿菌（嬰兒長雙歧桿菌），作為研究對象之一，因為這是嬰兒腸道內數量最多的優勢菌種之一；另外，我們會從食用菌之一的菌核側耳（俗稱虎奶菇）菌核提取及純化β－葡聚醣；並通過“組學”（包括轉錄組和蛋白質組）研究雙歧桿菌利用β－葡聚醣的分子機制 。透過對β－葡聚醣進行物理或化學修飾，我們將會獲得一系列結構特異（不同分子大小及支鏈比例）的β葡聚醣，並會將它們作為雙歧桿菌發酵的基質（碳源），找出不同結構的β－葡聚醣對雙歧桿菌發酵效率之間的關聯。除此之外，我們亦會進行人類糞便樣品的體外發酵研究，並使用16S核糖體脫氧核糖核酸(rDNA) 擴增子測序技術，找出不同結構的β－葡聚醣對腸道微生物組的影響，當中包括微生物物種組成及其相對豐度。 這項研究的結果會促進相關科學領域對於腸道益生菌，如雙歧桿菌，利用高分子量益生元背後分子機制的了解。再加上食用菌β—葡聚醣作為新型高分子量益生元的發展，β—葡聚醣將會成為我們人為促進腸道微生物平衡及腸道健康的手段之一，特別是嬰兒的腸道健康（實驗使用嬰兒長雙歧桿菌）。最後，由食用菌提煉的益生元對人類腸道菌群的保健作用仍然存在很大的研究空間，更多的研究將會為我們帶來更多資訊，令我們可以選擇最有效的高分子量益生元於未來進行臨床研究。

14114115.label: Realisation of objectives
14114115.value: Generally, all the four objectives are achieved except objective 2 which is only partially achieved. For objective 1, high molecular weight (HMW) mushroom sclerotial beta-glucans with different molecular weight and degree of branching were prepared by physical (ultrasonication), chemical (partial acid hydrolysis) and enzymatic procedures and structurally characterized. These modified mushroom beta-glucans were then evaluated for their potential as prebiotics by in vitro bacterial fermentation. For objective 2, the molecular mechanism of utilization of these mushroom beta-glucans by bacteria have been investigated by fractional proteomics and transcriptomics. As mentioned in the midterm progress report, due to the problem regarding the retardation of proteins in the first dimension in the two-dimensional gel electrophoresis, proteome approach on pure bacterial culture was explored as an alternative approach. We have only found two annotated proteins after cellular proteomics but they were not predicted to be transporters, implying that there might not be a beta-glucan transporter in the bifidobacteria. We then shifted to meta-proteomics and found some enzymes and pathway of beta-glucan utilization in microbiome (details refer to section 6.1). As for transcriptomics, we also expanded our original work on pure bacteria culture to other microbiome investigation (See section 6.1). For objective 3, the essential structural features of mushroom beta-glucans related to their utilization by bifidobacteria have been established through in vitro fermentation experiments followed by random forest analysis with detailed results to be discussed in section 6.1. For objective 4, changes on the microbial composition and diversity of species in human gut microbiota modulated by mushroom beta-glucans were investigated by ex vivo fermentation of infant faecal inoculum. Beta-glucans with different structural characteristics altered microbial composition and diversity as shown by 16S rDNA amplicon sequencing with detailed results discussed in section 6.1.

14114115.label: Major findings and research outcome
14114115.value: At the completion of this project, the major findings include the followings: The molecular mechanism in the utilization of HMW fungal/mushroom beta-glucans by bifidobacterium was found to involve the upregulation of the transcription of ABC trasnsporter and pullanase genes (Peer-reviewed publication No. 1). The correlations of the structural specificity of native/modified mushroom and other β-glucans with the efficiency of their fermentation by bifidobacteria were found to be related to molecular size, degree of branching, glycosidic linkage, monosaccharide profile, and chemical modification (Peer-reviewed publication No. 4 and 5). The modulation of human gut microbiota in infant (Peer-reviewed publication No. 2 and Recognized international conference No. 4) and in mouse (Recognized international conference No. 2) in terms of the microbial composition and diversity of species by the bifidogenic effect of mushroom prebiotics was proven. The research outcomes of this research project include the followings: The potential of mushroom beta-glucans (non-digestible carbohydrates) as novel prebiotics has been demonstrated ( (Peer-reviewed publication No. 5 and Recognized international conference No. 3). For screening of potential prebiotics, a rapid and high throughput method was established (Peer-reviewed publication No. 3 and Recognized international conference No. 1). Regarding for the development of beta-glucans as personalized prebiotics in infant, a framework using parametric modelling was proposed (Peer-reviewed publication No. 6).

14114115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14114115.value: Both native and modified HMW beta-glucans derived from mushroom sclerotia are potential candidates as novel prebiotics worthy for further studies. In vivo experiments involving germ-free mice inoculated with human fecal samples can be carried out to investigate the prebiotic effect of mushroom and other beta-glucans.

14114115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14114115.value: The research findings in this study advance our knowledge on the utilization of HMW mushroom beta-glucans by gut bacteria and enhance their potential development as novel prebiotics for human health. In particular, it is anticipated that by unraveling the mechanism by which bifidobacteria can ferment beta-glucans would facilitate the development of prebiotics as food ingredients to intervene gut health in humans (infant in particular). Lastly, the health effects of the human gut microbiota mediated by mushroom prebiotics and other beta-glucans can be further investigated for their functional study in future clinical trials.

14114615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14114615.value: 胃癌是人類最常見的惡性腫瘤之一。由於缺乏有效的治療手段，胃癌仍然是一種危害人類生命健康的嚴重疾病。基因的表觀遺傳學修飾是一種不依賴DNA序列改變的基因表達調控方式，其在胃癌的發生發展中起了重大的作用。異常的DNA甲基化修飾是胃癌主要的表觀遺傳學特徵，它能導致抑癌基因失活，從而引發胃癌的進展。 前列腺素E2（PGE2）是一種促炎類花生酸，在炎症和腫瘤中表達水平常增高。我們前期實驗發現PGE2可以通過誘導DNA甲基轉移酶3b（DNMT 3b）表達，從而調節胃癌中DNA甲基化水平。給予胃癌細胞PGE2處理後，能增加DNMT 3b在mRNA和蛋白水平的表達，並且同時增強其在細胞核的活性。我們在胃癌患者的腫瘤組織與癌旁正常組織，發現COX-2（一種PGE2合成酶）和DNMT 3b表達水平同步增高。 DNMT 3b被誘導表達後會提高DNA甲基化水平。我們發現當給予胃癌細胞PGE2藥物處理後，應用亞硫酸氫鹽測序法可以檢測到抑癌基因MGMT的啟動子區相應表現為高甲基化修飾；而經全基因組甲基化分析則發現處理後的胃癌細胞表現為全基因組甲基化修飾，並且這些高甲基化修飾基因與細胞週期調節、DNA修復有關。這些測序結果提示PGE2能誘導甲基化水平提高，並且有顯著的功能作用。 考慮到DNA甲基化在胃癌發生髮展的重要性以及PGE2異常調節的潛在作用。我們提出一種全新的胃癌聯合化療法案: Celecoxib（一種COX-2抑製劑）聯合Decitabine（一種DNMT抑製劑）。在前期研究中我們發現聯合用藥能起協同作用，共同抑制胃癌的生長。因此我們推測PGE2是一種胃癌表觀遺傳學調節不當的重要調節劑；而對於COX-2/PGE2 和DNMT的靶向治療是一項新型胃癌化療方案。 為了評估這一假說，我們提出四個具體目標：1）明確COX-2 / PGE 2軸在體內異常DNA甲基化修飾中的作用; 2）確認PGE 2誘導的DNA甲基化的功能學意義; 3）探索PGE 2誘導DNA甲基化的分子機制和4）評估COX-2/PGE2 和DNMT靶向治療在胃癌防治中的效果。這些具體目標將闡明PGE2在人類胃癌異常DNA甲基化中的作用、功能學重要性和臨床防治意義。

14114615.label: Realisation of objectives
14114615.value: 1. Determine the role of the COX-2/PGE2 axis in aberrant DNA methylation in vivo: To investigate the in vivo relevance of PGE2 in DNMT3B and promoter methylation, we utilized transgenic COX-2 mice. COX-2 transgenic and wild type mice were either treated with vehicle or MNU (for gastric cancer (GC) induction). We first examined expression of Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b in these mice and revealed that Dnmt3b protein, but not Dnmt3a, was induced in COX-2 transgenic mice compared to wildtype in both vehicle- and MNU-treated groups. We next compared overall 5mC levels in COX-2 transgenic mice and wildtype mice by dot blot assay, showing that COX-2 transgenic mice exhibited higher 5mC levels compared to wildtype mice independent of vehicle or MNU treatment. Given that transgenic COX-2 expression in mice induced Dnmt3b, we tested its effect on promoter DNA methylation. BGS analysis of Mgmt promoter demonstrated that COX-2 transgenic expression promoted methylation at multiple promoter CpG sites in vehicle and MNU-treated groups (P<0.05). Correspondingly, MGMT mRNA was suppressed in COX-2 transgenic mice. These data indicate that transgenic COX-2 expression in mice is associated with increased Dnmt3b expression, 5mC and Mgmt promoter hypermethylation, leading to the transcriptional silencing of MGMT, a tumor suppressor. Having established a role of COX-2/PGE2 axis in mice, we next examined the clinical relevance of PGE2 in promoting DNA methylation in humans. We observed a positive positive correlation between DNMT3A (P=0.007) and DNMT3B (P=0.006) with COX-2, but not for DNMT1 (P=0.424) in a Hong Kong cohort of 75 GC cases. The positive correlation between DNMT3A/DNMT3B with PTGS2 was validated in an independent GC cohort (GSE27342). Collectively, these findings indicate that the COX-2-PGE2 axis promotes DNA methylation in vitro and in vivo. To further corroborate our findings in humans, we retrospectively analyze tissue biopsies from a randomized, placebo-controlled trial with long-term treatment with a COX-2 inhibitor in patients with gastric intestinal metaplasia, a precancerous condition. Forty-two age- and gender-matched patients from vehicle (N=21) and rofecoxib (N=21) group. To analyze DNA methylation in tissue biopsies, we performed immunohistochemistry with anti-5mC and determined its nuclear staining score at baseline and two years after the initiation of drug treatment. Comparing the change in 5mC (Δ5mC) at year 2 to baseline, rofecoxib was found to significantly reduce Δ5mC compared to placebo (P=0.009). Thus, COX-2/PGE2 blockade may slow progressive hypermethylation in patients with intestinal metaplasia, further confirming its role in gastric tumorigenesis. 2. Determine the functional significance of PGE2-induced DNA methylation To further evaluate the impact of PGE2-induced DNA methylation on the global scale, we used the Illumina HumanMethylation 450K Array to survey the methylation status of over 485,000 CpG sites in 2 gastric cell lines (HGC27 and MKN1) treated with vehicle or PGE2 (2µM) for 48h. In all cell lines, PGE2 triggered an incremental rise in overall methylation (beta-value) across 485K CpG sites. We identified two candidate genes hypermethylated by PGE2 treatment: CAB39L and POT1. We first validated POT1. BGS analysis confirmed increased POT1 promoter methylation upon PGE2 treatment in both cell lines, with a corresponding decrease in POT1 mRNA. To evaluate the functional significance of COX-2-mediated silencing of POT1, we performed cell viability assays using GC cell lines. POT1 overexpression in HGC27 and MKN1 cells significantly suppressed cell viability and colony formation. Moreover, overexpression of POT1 induced apoptosis, implying that POT1 functions as a tumor suppressor. We have also initiated an independent study focusing on the role of CAB39L, another gene methylated by PGE2, in GC. The silencing of CAB39L in GC prompted us to hypothesize that CAB39L may function as a tumor suppressor. By overexpressing CAB39L in three GC cell lines (AGS, BGC823 and MKN45), we showed that CAB39L inhibited cell viability and colony formation assay. Overexpression of CAB39L in AGS, BGC823 and MKN45 cells also resulted in increased apoptosis. Conversely, CAB39L silencing in MKN74 cells increased cell viability and colony formation, consistent with the function of CAB39L as a tumor suppressor. We determined the effect of CAB39L on cell migration/invasion by wound healing and Matrigel invasion assays, respectively. CAB39L overexpression suppressed cell migration as indicated by the reduced wound closure efficiency in both AGS and BGC823 cells. Conversely, silencing of CAB39L in MKN74 cells significantly increased cell migration and invasion. Taken together, these results indicated that CAB39L suppressed cell phenotypes related to metastasis. Mechanistically, we found that CAB39L activates AMPK tumor suppressive pathway. We performed the Phospho-Kinase Arrays to decipher the phosphorylation profiles of 43 cancer-related kinases. Using BGC823 cells overexpressing CAB39L, we identified AMPKα as top kinase activated by CAB39L. Indeed, CAB39L overexpression induced p-AMPKα; whereas AMPK phosphorylation was inhibited with CAB39L knockdown. AMPKα is the catalytic subunit of AMPK protein complex and its phosphorylation is rate-limiting for AMPK activity. We further identified that CAB39L binds to LKB1 and STRAD, the upstream kinase for AMPK. Co-IP showed direct interaction of CAB39L with LKB1 and STARD. CAB39L promoted LKB1 phosphorylation, suggesting that interaction with LKB1-STRAD complex drives LKB1 activation, which in turn induces AMPK signalling. Finally, we linked effects of CAB39L on AMPK to “Warburg effect”. CAB39L inhibited the glycolytic phenotype in GC and promotes oxidative phosphorylation, thereby contributing to an anti-Warburg effect. Our work on POT1 and CAB39L indicate that COX-2/PGE2-induced silencing of tumor suppressive genes might play a role in gastric carcinogenesis. 3. Decipher the molecular mechanism underlying PGE2-induced DNA methylation To evaluate whether PGE2 induces expression of DNMT3B via EP receptors (surface receptor for PGE2, we performed siRNA mediated knockdown of EP1-4 receptors in HGC27 cells and evaluated PGE2-induced DNMT3B protein expression. Knockdown of EP2 or EP4 reduced PGE2-induced DNMT3B expression, whereas knockdown of EP1 or EP3 had no effect, suggesting that EP2 and EP4 mediate effect of PGE2 on DNMT3B expression. Collectively, COX-2/PGE2 axis mediates EP2/EP4 signalling to induce DNMT3B expression and DNA methylation. 4. Assess the effect of combined targeting of COX-2 and DNMT on gastric cancer prevention We tested whether co-inhibition of COX-2 and DNMT can synergistically impair GC growth. We combined Decitabine (5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine, a DNMT inhibitor) with Celecoxib (COX-2 specific) or Sulindac (nonselective) in HGC27 and MKN1 cells. Co-incubation with a non-cytotoxic dose of Decitabine synergized with either COX inhibitor to reduce cell viability in HGC27 and MKN1 cells, as indicated by MTT and colony formation assays. These data indicate that co-inhibition of COX-2 and DNMT can synergistically inhibit GC growth. To further evaluate their synergism, we determined apoptosis in HGC27 and MKN1 cells. Celecoxib treatment alone (50μM) induced apoptosis by around 2-fold. The combination of Celecoxib with Decitabine induced apoptosis by 4-fold, representing a 2-fold enhancement in their potency in both cell lines. In both cell lines, either Sulindac (75μM) or Decitabine (20μM) alone did not induced apoptosis. However, combination treatment increased the number of annexin V+ cells by ~2-fold. We finally tested the combination of Celecoxib plus Decitabine in HGC27 xenograft model. Mice bearing HGC27 xenografts were treated with Celecoxib (10mg/kg), Decitabine (5mg/kg) or a combination of both, for 21 days. At the end point, neither Celecoxib nor Decitabine alone significantly inhibited HGC27 xenograft growth. The combination treatment, on the other hand, inhibited tumor growth by 68 % (p<0.05), indicating that Celecoxib and decitabine synergize to inhibit tumor growth in vivo. 14114615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14114615.value: In this study, we comprehensively evaluated the role of COX-2/PGE2 axis in promoting DNA methylation in vitro, in COX-2 transgenic mice and in humans, demonstrating that COX-2/PGE2 induced DNMT3B and DNA hypermethylation in vitro and in vivo. (summarized in Wong CC, et al. Theranostics, 2019). In this study, we used PCR array analysis of PGE2-treated GC cells to reveal the up-regulation of DNMT3B, a de novo DNA methyltransferase. In GC cells, PGE2 induced DNMT3B expression and activity, leading to increased methylated cytosine (5mC) and promoter methylation of tumor suppressive genes (MGMT and CNR1). Consistently, Cox-2 transgenic expression in mice significantly induced Dnmt3b expression, increased 5mC content, and promoted Mgmt promoter methylation. We retrospectively analyzed the 5mC content of 42 patients with intestinal metaplasia (a precancerous lesion of GC) treated with a COX-2 specific inhibitor Rofecoxib or placebo for 2 years, revealing that COX-2 inhibitor significantly down-regulated 5mC (N=42, P=0.009). Collectively, these data indicate that PGE2 is closely related to DNA hypermethylation in vitro and in vivo. Using genome-wide 450K methylation array, we identified chromosomal genes (POT1, ATM and HIST1H2AA) and CAB39L were methylated by PGE2. Biofunctional work revealed that POT1 functions as a tumor suppressor. Finally, we demonstrated that combinatorial inhibition of COX-2 and DNMT using Celecoxib and Decitabine synergistically inhibited GC growth in vitro and in vivo. Functional impact of CAB39L, a downstream target of COX-2/PGE2, was reported by Li et al., Oncogene, 2018. Functional studies suggested that CAB39L functions as a tumor suppressor, as overexpression of CAB39L elicited suppression of multiple cancer phenotypes both in GC cells and an orthotopic mouse model; whilst its knockdown promoted tumorigenesis. Mechanistically, CAB39L interacted with LKB1-STRAD complex and induced LKB1, leading to the phosphorylation and activation of AMPKα/β. LKB1-AMPK activation in GC cell lines was tumor suppressive. Moreover, knockdown of LKB1 reversed growth inhibitory effect of CAB39L, indicating that tumor suppression by CAB39L depended on LKB1-AMPK. RNAseq revealed that CAB39L was closely correlated with oxidative phosphorylation and mitochondrial biogenesis. Consistently, CAB39L-induced p-AMPK elicited PGC1α phosphorylation and increased the expression of genes involved in mitochondrial respiration complexes. Accordingly, CAB39L reversed the Warburg effect in GC, as evidenced by enhanced oxygen consumption rate and reduced extracellular acidification rate; inversely, CAB39L knockdown promoted a metabolic shift towards the Warburg phenotype. In GC patients, CAB39L promoter hypermethylation was correlated with poor prognosis. Our data demonstrate that CAB39L is a novel tumor suppressor by promoting LKB1-AMPK-PGC1α axis.

14114615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14114615.value: Our work has comprehensively investigated the association of COX-2/PGE2 axis in the promotion of aberrant DNA methylation in the context of gastric cancer development. However, how exactly COX-2/PGE2 mediated DNA methylation directly contributes to carcinogenesis remains partly understood. We have initially elucidated two potential candidates, CAB39L and POT1, and both function as tumor suppressor genes. In future studies, we aim to uncover the key downstream targets of COX-2/PGE2 that become aberrantly silenced in gastric cancer. Apart from genes, microRNA and lncRNA are also targets of DNA hypermethylation and transcriptional silencing. We plan to expand upon our current observation and evaluate DNA methylation of the promoters of microRNA and lncRNA, in order to uncover potential deregulation of these RNA species mediated by COX-2/PGE2 axis. For the translational part, it will be worthwhile to investigate in multiple cohorts of gastric cancer/precancerous lesions and treated with COX-2 specific or nonselective COX inhibitors, to provide evidence that the intake of COX inhibitors might help to slow or even reverse aberrant DNA methylation in gastric cancer. Given that COX inhibitors are some of the most common medications worldwide, it will have important implications for future of gastric cancer prevention and treatment.

14114615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14114615.value: Gastric cancer is one of the most common human malignancies. It is a devastating disease with few therapeutic options and poor prognosis. Epigenetic mechanisms induced heritable changes in gene expression without a change in their coding sequence, and their dysregulation plays a major role in gastric carcinogenesis. Aberrant DNA methylation is a prominent epigenetic feature of gastric cancer and it contributes to disease progression via silencing of tumor suppressor genes. However, mechanism(s) underlying DNA methylation remain poorly understood. In this study, we have shown that Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), a pro-inflammatory eicosanoid, as a novel molecule that promotes aberrant DNA methylation in gastric cancer progression. Using a series of experimental models, we revealed that PGE2 induces expression of a key enzyme directly involved in DNA methylation, thereby contributing to gene silencing through hypermethylation. Mechanistic studies highlighted the tumor suppressive role of genes targeted by PGE2. We have also demonstrated the translational value of our work by showing that inhibition of COX-2 (rate limiting enzyme for PGE2) could inhibit DNA methylation in a placebo-controlled trial. Finally, we show that combining inhibitors of COX-2 and DNA methylation synergistically blocked gastric cancer. Our work has potential implications for prevention and treatment of gastric cancer.

14115615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115615.value: Peptic ulcer disease is very common worldwide. Life threatening complications associated with peptic ulcers cause enormous hospital admissions and mortality. Aetiological factors leading to peptic ulcers are Helicobacter pylori infection and use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and aspirin. Both of these factors inhibit pathways of natural healing process leading to formation of ulcer. Stem cell-based therapies for tissue repair and regeneration have attracted considerable attention in recent years. There is a growing body of evidence that mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) enhanced wound healing through stimulation of proliferation and differentiation of resident progenitor cells, secretion of growth factors to promote recovery of injured cells and suppression of inflammation and apoptosis. Therefore, in contrast to most pharmacologic agents targeting single pathophysiologic pathway, MSCs function through multiple mechanisms to enhance tissue healing. Stem cell therapy is a potential treatment for peptic ulcer disease. In our recent rodent experiment, single injection of adipose-MSCs (ADMSCs) into submucosal wall significantly enhances the healing of gastric ulcer induced by intraluminal application of acetic acid. Re-epithelialization, regeneration of granulation tissue and angiogenesis are all accelerated on days 10 and 14. The therapeutic effect of a single dose of ADMSCs is comparable to daily administration of pantoprazole, a standard regime for treatment of peptic ulcers. In this small animal experiment, it is impractical to investigate the therapeutic effect of repeated injections of ADMSC. This proposal will investigate the therapeutic effect of repeated endoscopically injection of ADMSCs for treatment of gastric ulcer induced by endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) and Indomethacin. After creation of gastric ulcer, the porcine models will be divided into four treatment groups: 1. endoscopic injection of ADMSC; 2. Oral PPI; 3. Endoscopic injection of ADMSC plus PPI and 4. Control group. The outcomes will be assessed through endoscopy, histopathology as well as molecular aspects to confirm the therapeutic potential of ADMSC for treatment of peptic ulcer disease. The therapeutic potential of ADMSC for endoscopic treatment of peptic ulcer will have major breakthrough impact on clinical management of peptic ulcer disease, as healing of peptic ulcer will be enhance and ulcer complications can be prevented. Moreover, the healing of artificial ulcers induced by ESD will be hastened, and stricture formation can be prevented after circumferential ESD.

14115615.label: Realisation of objectives
14115615.value: (1) We established a porcine model of NSAID-related gastric ulcer in this project. The porcine model was induced by administration of indomethacin before and after creation of artificial ulcers with techniques of endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD); indomethacin (15mg/kg) was given 10 days prior to ESD and was continued after ESD until the end of study. After fasting overnight, two ulcers with a diameter of 5cm in size were created at the body and antrum of the stomach by ESD for each pig. All the ESD procedures were performed by the same endoscopist using Dual knife and IT knife (Olympus) as described in our previous study. Pigs returned to a normal diet on the second day after ESD. Compared with the normal controls in which pigs were not given indomethacin, treatment of pigs with indomethacin preand post-ESD significantly delayed ulcer healing (P=0.018); the healing rate reduced by approximately 30% in the indomethacin group compared with the normal controls at day 7 (P=0.044) and day 14 (P=0.001). This animal model mimics the clinical situation in which patients develop gastric ulcers after long-term NSAIDs ingestion and thus is used for this study. The use of a large animal model also enables the endoscopic injection of stem cells for ulcer therapy which serves as an important simulation to the clinical practice. (2) To evaluate the healing of NSAID-related gastric ulcer, endoscopic surveillance was performed every week until the end of study on day 21 to measure the ulcer size by using an endoscopic ruler. Histology in terms of leukocytes infiltration and mucosal regeneration, as well as the immunohistochemistry for CD31 (marker for endothelial cells) and PCNA (a proliferation marker of G1/S phase), was used to determine the inflammation, re-epithelization, and neovascularization. (3) To track the stem cells in vivo, we labeled the ADMSCs with PKH26 before submucosal injection. Immunofluorescence demonstrated that stem cells engrafted at lamina propria, submucosa, and muscularis externa of the stomach at day 21. Since the function of stem cells for tissue repair may partly rely on the migration of MSCs to injured site and then differentiation into specialized resident cells that subsequently replace the damaged tissues, we also investigated the transdifferentiation of stem cells after transplantation to the stomach. Few engrafted cells were colocalized with the staining for α-smooth muscle actin (α- SMA) and pan-cytokeratin, indicating that these cells did not express vascular smooth muscle cell, myofibroblast and epithelial cell phenotype in vivo. This evidence hence suggests that the role of differentiated MSCs in promoting ulcer healing is minimal. (4) According to the above results, we hypothesized that the effects of stem cells in promoting healing of NSAID-related gastric ulcer might not be mainly due to their differentiation properties but on their paracrine effects. So we firstly investigated the secretome profile of ADMSCs by RT2-Prolifer PCR array. (5) We collected the MSCs-derived conditioned medium (MSC-CM) for the following experiments with the aim to determine the role of ADMSCs-derived effectors in the enhancement of ulcer healing. Both experiments in vitro and in vivo suggested treatment with MSC-CM significantly promoted cell viability, migration, and angiogenesis, thus enhancing the healing of NSAID-related gastric ulcer. (6) Since COX2-PGE2 axis is well known to protect the mucosal integrity in GI tract. In this study, we determined that although ADMSCs transplantation increased the expression of COX2 in ulcer samples, the PGE2 expression at day 21 was not different between the ADMSCs group and the control group, suggesting that ADMSCs treatment did not reverse the NSAID-induced inhibition of COX2-PGE2 axis. We thus turned to investigate other signaling transduction involved in this effect. Since ErK1/2-MAPK and PI3K/Akt are known to be critical for cell survival, migration, and angiogenesis, all of which are involved in the regulation of ulcer healing process, here our results showed that ADMSCs or MSC-CM treatment significantly activated the phosphorylation of ErK and Akt, and the activation of both pathways were related with the enhanced cell viability, migration, and angiogenesis. (7) PPI is commonly prescribed for patients with NSAID-related peptic ulcer, it is not clear whether coadministration of MSC-CM would improve efficacy of PPI treatment. In this study, pigs received not only the submucosal injection of MSC-CM at day 1, 7 and 14 respectively but also the oral pantoprazole (40mg) daily after ESD until euthanasia at day 21. However, results showed that within the course of PPI therapy, additional injection of MSC-CM did not further enhance the healing of NSAID-related gastric ulcer; there was no overall difference in the percentage of ulcer size reduction between two groups. Multivariate test for each time point also showed no difference between groups.

14115615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14115615.value: (1) We found that endoscopic injection of ADMSCs led to accelerated healing of NSAID-related gastric ulcer compared with the controls. The ulcer index in the ADMSCs group reduced to 43.07% of original size by day 7 (vs 85.41% in the control group). (2) ADMSCs treatment stimulated re-epithelization and neovascularization, and alleviated inflammation. The number of PCNA+ (a proliferation marker of G1/S phase) cells per field of view around ulcer margin as well as at granulation tissues was significantly higher in the ADMSCs group than in the control group at day 7. Meanwhile, a significantly higher density of CD31+ capillaries was observed in ulcers treated with ADMSCs than in controls at day 21. Furthermore, ADMSCs injection significantly up-regulated IL-10 expression at day 7 and day 21 and downregulated the MPO activity in ulcer samples obtained at day 21 compared with the controls. (3) The ulcer healing process did not depend on the engraftment and transdifferentiation of stem cells in vivo. Immunofluorescence demonstrated that the engrafted stem cells did not show obvious colocalization with the staining for α- smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) and pan-cytokeratin, indicating that these cells did not express vascular smooth muscle cell, myofibroblast and epithelial cell phenotype in vivo. This evidence hence suggests that the role of differentiated MSCs in promoting ulcer healing is minimal. (4) A series of experiments in vitro demonstrated that the MSC-secreted factors alleviated indomethacin-induced cytotoxicity and enhanced angiogenesis and cell migration in vitro. (5) Further experiments in vivo showed that treatment with MSC-derived conditioned medium (MSC-CM) facilitated healing of NSAID-related gastric ulcer in pigs. The percentage change in ulcer index was reduced in the MSC-CM group compared to control group at day 7 (P=0.012). (6) Submucosal injection of MSC-CM promoted angiogenesis and alleviated inflammation and oxidative stress. MSC-CM treatment also induced proliferation of wound-resident cells including the vascular endothelial cells/vascular smooth muscle cells, mucosal epithelial cells, and the ulcer-associated cell lineage (UACL). (7) Profiling analysis demonstrated upregulation of genes related to the functions of inflammation, re-epithelization, and extracellular matrix remodeling after MSC-CM treatment. (8) Stem cell therapy did not reverse the indomethacin-induced inhibition of COX2- PGE2 axis, but activated the ErK/MAPK and the PI3K/Akt pathways that were crucial for the cell viability, migration, and angiogenesis. (9) Lastly, we found that coadministration of MSC-CM did not enhance the therapeutic efficacy of PPI on NSAID-related gastric ulcer.

14115615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14115615.value: The ultimate goal of the project in the long term is to develop a novel option of using stem cell-based therapy for patients with refractory NSAID-related gastric ulceration, especially for those who suffer side effects from long-term use of PPI. It has been demonstrated that the endoscopically confirmed ulceration may show in approximately 15-30% chronic NSAIDs users, and complications may occur in nearly 2-4% of them. In the United Sates, NSAIDs are thought to cause 3200-165,000 deaths in 1990s. Therefore, the prevention and treatment of NSAID-related GI toxicity has become an important clinical and public health issue. Our proposed work introducing a new strategy may hence produce significant impact on the treatment for this disease in the long term. Current project successfully demonstrated that endoscopic submucosal injection of ADMSCs could significantly promote healing of NSAID-related gastric ulcer in pigs, and this effect was much less dependent on the transdifferentiation of stem cells in vivo but the paracrine activity of stem cells with releasing a wide variety of cytokines, chemokines, and trophic factors might play a more important role in it. Based on these results, we plan to launch a new project that focuses on the investigation of using ADMSCs-derived effectors, especially exosomes, for the treatment of NSAID-related peptic ulcer, as well as on the understanding of potential mechanism. The research proposal has been sent for the consideration of GRF 2020/2021 scheme.

14115615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14115615.value: standard treatment; however, the safety and long term adverse effects of using these drugs are attracting more and more concerns in recent years. Using a porcine model of NSAID-related gastric ulcer, we herein showed that adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ADMSCs) delivered by endoscopic submucosal injection promoted the ulcer healing with less inflammatory infiltration and enhanced reepithelization and neovascularization at day 7 and day 21. However, only few engrafted ADMSCs showed myofibroblast and epithelial cell phenotype in vivo, suggesting the ulcer healing process might be much less dependent on the stem cell transdifferentiation. Further experiment with submucosal injection of MSC-derived secretome revealed a therapeutic efficacy comparable to stem cell transplantation. Profiling analysis showed up-regulation of genes associated with inflammation, granulation formation, and extracellular matrix remodeling at day 7 post-injection of MSC-derived secretome. Our data suggest that endoscopic submucosal injection of ADMSCs serves as a promising approach to promote healing of NSAID-related peptic ulcer, and the paracrine effectors released from stem cells play a crucial role in this process.
