14115915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115915.value: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) rupture is an especially common sports injury resulting in an unstable knee. As a ruptured ACL does not heal, ACL reconstruction (ACLR) surgery utilises a tendon graft to restore the ACL function. However, insufficient self-healing capacity may result in poor graft incorporation, which leads to a high risk of ACLR failure and excessive knee laxity. Attempts to promote graft healing by tissue engineering and regenerative technology offer a greater chance of success, notably with the use of stem cells. However, clinical application of stem cell therapy to promote graft healing in ACLR still awaits further translational research, such as cell source, mode of application and ease of preparation. Our team developed a tendon-derived stem cell (TDSC) sheet which exhibited beneficial effects to promote tendon and ligament healing. Furthermore, we demonstrated that the TDSC sheet is not immunogenic, and pre-clinical animal studies supported the safe use of allogeneic TDSC sheets to promote tendon healing, as well as graft healing in ACLR. A further step to facilitate the clinical use of allogeneic TDSC sheets will be the industrial production of “packaged” TDSC products, which involves the development of preservation techniques for tissue engineered cell constructs. Technical advancement of organ and cell preservation by low temperature treatment, has offered many choices for various applications. As cell preservation techniques tend to be cell type specific, we propose to determine the optimal preservation conditions for TDSC sheets, with respect to duration of preservation, maintenance of physical properties and bioactivities of TDSC sheets. In this proposal, we will optimize the cryopreservation and reactivation procedures to preserve TDSC sheets, and determine the treatment efficacies of preserved TDSC sheets in well-established animal models. This study will facilitate the clinical use of TDSC sheets by devising preservation and reactivation protocols. As there are over 2000 ACLR in Hong Kong, over 200,000 ACLR in US and possibly millions around the world, annually; our study will not only benefit patients in Hong Kong, but also worldwide. 前十字韌帶(ACL)撕裂是常見的運動損傷，令膝關節變得不穩定。由於ACL撕裂後不能復原，ACL重建手術(ACLR) 透過移植肌腱以恢復膝關節功能。不過若移植物自癒力不足而未能與骨癒合，會導致膝關節鬆弛，令重建手術失敗。組織工程和再生技術，尤其是配合幹細胞使用，為促進移植物癒合提供了較大成功機會。然而，幹細胞治療於促進ACLR中移植物癒合的臨床應用，還有待進一步的轉化研究，例如研究細胞來源﹑應用模式和易於製備的方式。我們的團隊所開發的肌腱幹細胞（TDSC）片，能促進肌腱和韌帶的癒合。此外，我們證明了TDSC片不具免疫原性，在動物研究中，同種異體的TDSC片能促進肌腱的癒合，以及ACL重建手術中移植物的癒合，證明TDSC片可安全使用。為促進臨床應用, 同種異體TDSC片需要工業生產化成為TDSC產品，其中涉及組織工程細胞產品的保存技術的發展。器官和細胞的低溫保存處理技術，已經為各種需要提供了多種選擇。由於細胞保存技術往往是因應不同的細胞類型而有所不同，我們建議以TDSC片的保存期限﹑物理性能和生物活性的維持作為TDSC片的保存條件，選取TDSC片最佳的保存方法。在是次提案中，我們將研究TDSC片的冷凍保存和激活程序，並用動物模型研究冷凍後的TDSC片的治療功效。通過研究TDSC片的冷凍保存方法和激活程序，這項研究將有助發展TDSC片的臨床應用。由於現時香港及美國每年均有多於2000 及200,000 宗ACLR進行，全世界甚或有過百萬人需要進行ACLR，我們的研究將會幫助香港以至全世界的病人。

14115915.label: Realisation of objectives
14115915.value: We have completed the work related to the objectives. At 6 months after commencement of the project, there was a change to new PI due to retirement of the former PI. During the study period, there were several unexpected events that affect the progress. These included contamination of cell culture, repair of cell culture hood, and resignation of 2 research personnel in charge. To tackle with the contamination problems, we have cultured other batches of cells in different CO2 incubators so as to reduce the risk of contamination. As there was a change of research assistant-in charge, the progress was inevitably affected. The project was then extended for 6 months. Nethertheless, we were able to complete the work related to the objectives. For objective 1, we isolated and cultured human tendon-derived stem cells (TDSCs), and then induced the formation of TDSC sheet using connective tissue growth factor (CTGF) and ascorbic acid. Cell sheets were detached and then cryopreserved with or without an FDA-approved DMSO-based cryopreservation product “CryoStor-10” in liquid nitrogen at -196°C for 1 month. Before and after cryopreservation, the cell viability was measured using Alamar blue assay, and mechanical strength was tested using tensile test. From tensile test, we found that the ultimate force of fresh TDSC sheet was extremely low (~0.01N). Owing to its elastic, stretchy, and sticky nature, it was difficult to attach the cells sheets to the fixation system. Moreover, the current testing system did not cover the small force range of the cell sheets. These findings were similar to the reports from other studies. Since mechanical strength of TDSC sheets will not contribute to the healing following ACLR, a strong tensile strength is not the most desirable property for TDSC sheet production as long as the cryopreserved TDSC can be handled for subsequent operation. For objective 2, human TDSC sheets cryopreserved for 1 month were reactivated with or without the reactivation media containing magnesium chloride and ascorbic acid for 2 hours. Using qPCR, we examined whether tenogenic and osteogenic properties of the TDSC sheets were retained. For objective 3, using a rat model of anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR), we tested whether wrapping the tendon graft with cryopreserved rat TDSC sheet could improve healing following ACLR. The healing was evaluated using various assessments at 6 week post-operation. The major outcome include mechanical properties by graft pull-out test, as well as examination of the remodeling process by histology. We have also included micro-CT analysis for assessment of bone tunnel healing.

14115915.label: Major findings and research outcome
14115915.value: Tendon-derived stem cell (TDSC) sheets were cryopreserved with or without cryopreservation media CryoStor-10 for 1 month. The cell viability relative to the level before cryopreservation was significantly higher in CryoStor-10-preserved cell sheets compared to control group preserved with phosphate buffered saline (PBS) only (40.47% vs 11.36%, p=0.004). Using a tensile test, we found that the ultimate force of TDSC sheet was extremely low (~0.01N). Nevertheless, cryopreserved TDSC sheets could be handled in subsequent animal operation. After cryopreserving in CryoStor-10 for 1 month, cell sheets were treated with reactivation media (10mM MgCl2 and 25µM ascorbic acid) for 2 hours. Cell sheets were then cultured with osteogenic or tenogenic media for 2 weeks. Compared to PBS control group, cell sheets treated with reactivation media has significantly higher expression of tenogenic marker (scleraxis, p=0.05) and osteogenic markers (osteocalcin and alkaline phosphatase, p=0.008 and 0.05 respectively). During ACLR surgery, we found that wrapping of cryopreserved TDSC sheet around the tendon graft was feasible, however after routing the tendon graft through both bone tunnels, part of the wrapped TDSC sheet could not go into the bone tunnels with graft and was retained in graft mid substance. Thus the distribution of TDSC sheet was uneven on the tendon graft. Following ACLR, at 6 week post-operation, compared to untreated control group, cryopreserved TDSC sheet-treated group did not show significant difference in failure load and stiffness of the femur-graft-tibia complex in pull-out test (p>0.05). From histological assessment, there was high cellularity in graft in all groups. Slightly higher vascularity was observed in cryopreserved TDSC sheet groups. There was no significant difference in bone tunnel healing from µCT measurement (p>0.05 in bone volume ratio, bone mineral density, and connectivity density). In this study, we concluded that the cryopreservation of TDSC sheets with CryoStor-10 enhanced cell viability. Reactivation using MgCl2 and ascorbic acid retained tenogenic and osteogenic activities of TDSC sheets. However, cryopreserved TDSC sheets, after applying in a rat model of ACLR, did not show significant improvement in vivo. This might be due to uneven distribution of cell sheet along the graft. Further modifications on the surgical procedures will be required. Results from objectives 1 and 2 were reported in international conference. Major results from this study was reported in a manuscript to be submitted to peer-reviewed journal. Please refer to the conference paper and manuscript attached in part C.

14115915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14115915.value: Based on the current results, tendon-derived cell (TDSC) sheets could be cryopreserved in commercially available cryopreservation media for at least 1 month. After reactivation, the cell viability and tenogenic and osteogenic activities could still be retained. This suggested that TDSC sheets could be prepared in advance in GMP-grade lab and preserved to facilitate clinical use. Since numerous cell constructs originated from other cell sources are under development, the cryopreservation as well as reactivation protocol developed in this study could possibly be applied to other cell constructs. Apart from ACLR surgery, the use of this type of artificial cell constructs can be extended to other types of tendon and ligament surgeries. Further studies can be conducted to improve retention of cell sheets in situ so as to enhance healing processes.

14115915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14115915.value: Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) rupture is a common sports injury, and ACL reconstruction (ACLR) surgery using tendon graft is currently the standard treatment. Our previous study found that by wrapping the tendon graft with a tendon-derived stem cell (TDSC) sheet, the healing following ACLR could be enhanced. However the preparation of the cell sheets takes around 5 weeks, which did not match the clinical need. In this study, we found that cell sheets could be prepared well before surgery. The cell sheets could be cryopreserved for at least 1 month before reactivation for surgery. After cryopreservation, the desirable biological properties could be retained. Using a rat model of ACLR we found that by applying cryopreserved cell sheet on tendon graft, the mechanical properties of the graft and bone healing did not further improve. We will modify the surgical procedures to ensure this cell sheet could be retained at target site. As many other cell constructs are emerging, the cryopreservation and reactivation techniques in this study may be applicable to other cell constructs. Moreover, this ready-to-use cell sheet with desirable biological activities has a potential in other types of tendon and ligament surgeries.

14116415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116415.value: This project aims to study the ultrastructure and function of the osteocyte-lacuno-canalicular system and the association with bone mineralization and bone microarchitecture in a case-control study on bone biopsies obtained intra-operatively from Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) Vs normal control subjects. AIS is a prevalent three-dimensional spinal deformity that could be associated with serious functional morbidities, cardiopulmonary compromise, early spinal degenerative changes and psychosocial disturbances. Systemic osteopenia affecting multiple skeletal sites, defined as bone mineral density (BMD) of Z-score ≤ -1 with reference to the age and ethnic matched population, was found in over 30% of the AIS patients. The osteopenia could persist into adulthood thus predisposing to osteoporosis and other related complications in later life. Osteopenia in AIS has been shown by our group to be an important prognostic factor for curve deformity progression. Our recent researches have also demonstrated significant alterations in systemic bone microarchitecture, volumetric BMD and mechanical bone strength (finite element analysis) in addition to osteopenia in AIS. From our pilot study, we hypothesize that observed abnormalities in the morphology and function of osteocytes and their lacuno-canalicular system (OLCS) in AIS could result from defects in genetics and environmental factors acting through abnormally reduced dentin matrix protein 1 (Dmp-1), sclerostin (SOST) expression and the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway and manifest phenotypically as abnormal systemic osteopenia, bone mineralization and bone microarchitecture thus affecting the mechanical bone strength and contribute to the initiation/progression and etiopathogenesis of AIS. In this proposed case-control study, volumetric BMD and microarchitectural parameters of the bone biopsy will be evaluated with micro-CT, the ultrastructural and histomorphological evaluation of the OLCS with scanning electron microscopy and immunostaining. Specific osteocytes related markers at the tissue and cellular level will be correlated with bone mineralization and bone microarchitecture in AIS and control subjects. This study will be complementary to our on-going GRF funded study (Project Number 463113 2013/14)) and help to advance our understanding on the possible association between disturbance of bone mineralization, bone microarchitecture and the contributions of key bone cells - osteoblasts, osteoclasts and osteocytes to the etiopathogenesis of AIS. It has the potential to shed light on future development of novel prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic strategies in preventing the occurrence or progression of the scoliosis deformity via targeting on the bone cells and bone mineralization pathway in AIS through timely non-invasive intervention. 本項目旨在病例對照研究中採用青少年特發性脊柱側彎（AIS）患者和正常對照組的術中骨活檢標本，研究骨陷窩-骨小管系統功能和結構，以及與骨礦化和微結構之間的相關性。 AIS是一種常見的3維脊柱畸形。該疾病可導致嚴重功能障礙，心肺並發症，早期的脊柱退行性變和心理障礙。在年齡與人種匹配的人群中，將骨密度（BMD）的Z評分低於1分稱之為骨量減少，而骨量減少可影響全身多處骨骼。骨量減少出現在超過30%的AIS患者中，並且能持續到患者成年並成為骨質疏鬆以及晚年相關並發症的的因素。我們團隊前期研究發現，骨量減少為脊柱側凸進展的重要預測因素之一。我們團隊最新的研究結果表明，除骨量減少外，AIS患者還存在嚴重的全身骨骼微結構異常，容量性BMD和力學方面的變化。 在我們的預實驗中，假設首先是基因的缺陷以及環境因素異常引起牙質基質蛋白-1和硬骨素表達減少以及Wnt/β-catenin信號通路異常，繼而出現可觀察的骨細胞形態學、功能以及骨陷窩-骨小管系統（OLCS）的變化，從而表現為全身性的骨量減少，骨礦化和微結構的異常，進而影響骨的力學特性，最後引起脊柱側凸的發生或加重，並成為AIS的病因之一。 在此病例對照研究中，利用micro-CT檢測活檢骨標本的容量BMD和微結構參數，掃描電鏡和免疫組化檢測OLCS的超微結構和組織形態學變化，並將AIS與對照組的骨礦化和微結構的參數，與組織及細胞水平上骨細胞標記物的參數，進行相關性分析。 該研究將與我們正在進行的GRF基金項目(項目編號463113 2013/14)形成互補，並且在骨礦化及微結構的失衡方面，在關鍵的骨細胞，成骨細胞和破骨細胞對AIS發病作用中的相關性方面，提升了我們對這兩方面相關性的認識。這項研究將在，預測側彎加重的生物標記物方面，以及通過對AIS骨骼中的細胞及礦化通路的影響，及時有效地通過非創傷的方式防止側彎的發生或進展方面。

14116415.label: Realisation of objectives
14116415.value: Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) is a three dimensional spinal deformity occurring during pubertal period. The etiopathogenesis is not clear, but cumulative evidence is suggesting the involvement of abnormal bone metabolism which is clinically an independent prognostic factor for curve progression and risk to reach surgical threshold. With extensive efforts, we have managed to complete subject recruitment of 24 AIS and 12 non-AIS control subjects have been completed (CREC Ref No. 2014-198). Clinical ethical approval in compliance with the Declaration of Helsinki was obtained from the Ethical Committee of the university and hospital. Informed consent was obtained from all subjects or their legal guardians. Basic anthropometric data, the type of curve, time of occurrence and progression pattern were recorded. The trabecular bone biopsies were taken as part of the standard surgical procedure of the operated patients that require bone harvesting. The size of the biopsies varies from batch to batch. In most scenarios, the biopsies were large enough to be used for full set of assessment stated in objectives, but in some scenarios, the biopsies were so small in size that could only be used for few proposed assessment. In order to address the research questions with reasonable sample size and statistical power for analysis, we sub-divided the collected biopsies randomly for us to conduct the proposed assessments. All assays listed in proposal have been conduct according to standard protocol accordingly. This ex vivo study provided direct evidence to define unique bone microstructure, mineralization and defective osteocyte lacuno-canalicular network of AIS. Result of μ CT analysis showed unique trabecular bone parameters of AIS with slightly lower bone volume fraction (− 5.26%, p = 0.405) and specific bone surface (− 8.32%, p = 0.096), higher trabecular separation (18.75%, p = 0.033), lower trabecular number (− 17.03%, p = 0.064), reduced connectivity density (Conn.D; − 49.97%, p = 0.052) and lower structure model index (SMI; − 13.17%, p = 0.711). Additionally, we applied individual trabecula segmentation (ITS)-based morphological analysis to decompose trabecular bone into trabecular rods and plates helped to pinpoint the predominant structural and connectivity changes of trabecular rods in AIS. ITS results revealed a predominate change in rod trabeculae bone volume fraction (− 19.23%, p = 0.459), rod trabecular number (− 11.04%, p = 0.229), and rod-rod junction density (− 56.9%, p = 0.033) when compared with that of plate trabeculae. Osteocyte LCN features of AIS was compared to that of control with SEM and FITC-Imaris technique. The images of backscattered scanning electron microscopy revealed that the cell shape changed from a spindle to a round shape, and a lower mineral content including the loss of a white mineral ring around osteocytes in the AIS osteocytes compared to the control osteocytes. Removal of the superficial layer of mineralized matrix with acid-etched SEM images precisely displayed the structure change of AIS osteocytes, including clusters of roundish osteocytes with shorter, disorganized and poorly interconnected dendrite processes in great contrast to the orderly aligned normal a spindle-shaped osteocytes with abundant perpendicularly radiating interconnected processes in the non-AIS controls. Further analyses with modified confocal laser scanning microscope (CLSM)-based FITC-Imaris images further confirmed these structural changes. The quantitative analysis made by Imaris software showed significant reductions in canalicular number and average length per osteocyte by 25% and 22%, respectively; and increases in lacunar volume and area by 37% and 25%, respectively, in AIS bone tissues. In addition, scatter plot data showed that about 30% of the osteocytes in AIS exhibited these pathological changes. Bone mineral distribution pattern was indicated by local amount of the elements calcium and phosphorus in the bone material in peri-osteocytic region. Figure 1e shows the SEM images with SEM-EDX element spectrum of the controls and AIS (calcium intensity in green; phosphorous intensity in red). SEM-EDX results showed that the Ca/P ratio was significantly lower in peri-osteocytic matrix of the trabecular bone of iliac crest from AIS in comparison with the controls. Structural indices of histomorphometric analyses provide supportive evidence of previous result from μ CT analysis, revealed a thicker layer of non-mineralized bone on the bone surface, and an increase in osteoblast number despite a decrease in osteocyte number in the AIS bones. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to reveal defects of osteoblast and osteocyte functions by determining the transcriptional and protein level of critical markers. The percentage of sclerostin-positive osteocytes in control (76%) was significantly higher than in AIS (p<0.01). Immunohistochemical staining revealed higher active β-catenin level in AIS bone lining cells. DMP1 protein was stained in osteocytes of control and AIS. AIS demonstrated lower expression of DMP1 in osteocytes than controls. A primary osteocytes culture was established by embedding primary osteoblast into three dimensional collagen type I gel to mimic microenvironment for osteoblast to osteocyte differentiation. Features of primary osteocytes was validated by staining of dendritic feature and positive staining of dendrite marker and mature osteocyte marker. qPCR results showed significantly lower expression levels of dentin matrix acidic phosphoprotein (DMP1) (p= 0.017), fibroblast growth factor (FGF 23) (p= 0.014), and SOST (p= 0.024) in AIS bone tissues, whereas matrix extracellular phosphoglycoprotein (p = 0.003) expression was higher when compared with the controls. Reduced expression of DMP1, FGF23 (P = 0.020), and SOST (p = 0.033) were found in AIS primary osteocytes. In addition, AIS osteocytes had a lower level of E11 (p = 0.034) at the mRNA level and CX43 (gap junction protein) at both mRNA (p = 0.027) and protein level. qPCR result showed the CTNNB1 level (p = 0.002) significantly upregulated in AIS bone tissues (Fig. 5a). In AIS, CTNNB1 level was significantly upregulated in both primary osteoblast (p = 0.016) and osteocyte (p = 0.045) cultures. Western blot analysis showed a significant increase in active β -catenin level in the osteoblasts (p = 0.021). Correlation analysis showed association of mRNA level of osteocytes markers to bone mineralization parameters from DXA. mRNA level of CTNNB1 was negatively associated to left and right Femoral neck Bone Mineral Content (BMC) (r=-0.639, p=0.01; r=-0.636, p=0.011). mRNA level of FGF23 was positively associated to left and right Femoral neck Bone Mineral Content (BMC) (r=0.664, p=0.007; r=0.721, p=0.002). Conditioned medium of primary osteocyte culture was collected after 7 days culturing. AIS osteocyte showed less sclerostin protein secretion (p = 0.028) than that in control. To exclude the unknown effect from other exogenous factors in conditioned medium, a commercial available human recombinant sclerostin (rhSOST) was used to address the research question. Primary osteoblast was treated with rhSOST in concentration ranging from (0-50ng/ml). The differentiation ability was determined by assaying expression of representative markers. rhSOST had a consistent dose-dependent effect on level of Alp, E11, CX43, Phex and MMP13. Large individual variance is the possible reason for not reaching statistical significance.

14116415.label: Major findings and research outcome
14116415.value: In the study, we hypothesized that the morphological and functional abnormalities in osteocytes in AIS could be resulting from an abnormal reduction in Dmp-1 and SOST expression acting through the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway and manifest phenotypically as abnormal osteopenia, bone mineralization and bone microarchitecture thus affecting the mechanical bone strength and contribute to the initiation/progression and etiopathogenesis of AIS. Objective 1 of this study is to characterize the ultrastructure of the osteocyte-lacuno-canalicular system (OLCS), microarchitecture and bone mineralization status in AIS Vs normal control bone biopsies through multiple approaches. Apart from conventional immunostaining analysis, we collaborated with Prof. Jerry Feng from Texas A&M College of Dentistry to conduct advanced imaging analysis on OLCS with acid-etched scanning electron microscope (SEM) and fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC)-Imaris technique. We also extended our study to analyze the mineralization and mechanical property at the peri-osteocytic region by energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) and microindentation. The findings showed in general, AIS demonstrated abnormal osteocytes with more rounded and cobblestone in shape, and aligned in irregular clusters with shorter and disorganized canaliculi. Further quantitative analysis with FITC-Imaris technique showed significant reduction in canalicular number and length, and increase in lacunar volume and area in AIS. Three dimensional scatter plot indicated that as much as 30% of osteocytes in AIS exhibited such abnormal structural changes. SEM with EDX analysis demonstrated lower Ca/P ratio at the peri-osteocytic area. Moreover, microindentaion results revealed lower values of Vickers hardness and elastic modulus in AIS when compared with controls. Objective 2 is to investigate the abnormal expression of osteocyte related Dmp-1, SOST, β-catenin and other functional proteins from bone tissue biopsy and primary cell culture of osteoblast and osteocyte in AIS Vs normal controls. We isolated primary osteoblasts from bone biopsies, and developed protocol to induce osteocytogenic differentiation towards osteocytes which allow us to study expression level of target genes and proteins in AIS osteocytes. We also extended our study to explore the possible upstream regulator(s) on the abnormal expression of β-catenin and SOST. By microRNA microarray and gain- or loss-of-function studies with AIS and non-AIS primary osteocytes, we identified and confirmed that microRNA-145 could be one of the potential upstream factor leading the abnormal expression of β-catenin and thus impaired osteocyte activity and SOST secretion.

14116415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14116415.value: This findings of this study has led to the funding of several complementary projects, including three GRF projects (Ref No. 14135016, 14163517 and 14120818), a jointed NSFC/RGC project (Ref No. N_CUHK416/16) and a HMRF project (Ref No. 04152176). With these additional funding support, we are able to continue to study the pathological role of osteocyte and its clinical implication in AIS as a novel biomarker or therapeutic target for curve progression.

14116415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14116415.value: In this project, we have conducted successfully a series of scientific studies based on the objectives we set in the proposal with accepted publication in highly recognized journal in the field and presented in regional and international prestigious professional conferences. The findings of this proposal has opened new research directions to further studies on the cases and mechanism underlying the evidenced abnormal bone quality in AIS through targeting on osteocytes activity and lacuna-canalicular system structure. The findings on the role of microRNA also shed light on the development of novel biomarkers for curve progression and therapeutic strategy via targeting on osteocytes in AIS through timely non-invasive intervention.

14116515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116515.value: Our long-term goal is to understand mushroom development at the molecular level that includes protein-mediated and RNA-medicated regulation. In this proposal we aim to use experimental and computational methods to validate and characterize microRNA-like RNAs (milRNAs) in Coprinopsis cinerea to understand their roles in the development of mushroom-forming fungi. C. cinerea is a mushroom of limited edible value and is extensively used as a model organism to study the development of homobasidiomycete fungi including edible and medicinal mushrooms. Our C. cinerea genomics consortium sequenced its genome. Unraveling the molecular basis of the fungus developmental processes would contribute to evolutionary studies and lead to improvement in the breeding and cultivation of edible and medical mushrooms. MicroRNA (miRNA) is a group of non-coding RNAs of ~22nt that regulate gene expression in various biological processes such as cell differentiation, development regulation and heterochromatin formation. While miRNAs have been extensively studied in animal and plant models for their important roles in controlling developmental processes, miRNAs in fungi are less well studied and in particular their roles in mushroom development are unknown. Emerging evidence suggests that there are milRNAs in fungus. We have sequenced small RNAs from two developmental stages, mycelium and primordium. By computational analysis of these sequences, we predicted and identified milRNAs. We have also identified putative Dicer gene from the C. cinerea genome. Our analyses have revealed 16 highly putative milRNA genes in the C. cinerea genome. Based on our current data and knowledge, we propose this study to (1) experimentally validate the predicted milRNAs in C. cinerea, (2) functionally characterize the validated milRNAs, (3) determine whether Dicer is involved in milRNA biogenesis and regulation of gene expressions in C. cinerea by Dicer gene-knockout and (4) investigate the regulatory networks mediated by those milRNAs by identifying and characterizing target genes. When the study concludes, we will better understand how milRNAs function in mushrooms, adding to the existing knowledge of mushroom development and contributing to future studies on miRNA evolution. 我們的長期目標是從分子水平去了解菇類真菌的生長發育，包括其蛋白質調控和RNA調控。在此方案中，我們的目標是通過實驗與計算生物學的方法，去驗證並分析存在於灰蓋鬼傘（Coprinopsis cinerea）中的microRNA-like RNA（milRNA），進而了解milRNA在菇類真菌中的作用。C. cinerea是一種沒有食用價值的菇，被廣泛用作模式生物以探究同擔子菌亞綱（homobasiomycetes）真菌（包括食用菌與藥用菌）的生長發育。我們的合作夥伴已經測定了C. cinerea的基因組。從分子水平解開菇的生長發育之謎有助於進化研究，並可用於改良食用菌和藥用菌的育種和栽培。微RNA（miRNA）是一組大約長22nt的非編碼RNA。它們調控著基因的表達，進而影響各種生物過程，例如細胞分化、發育控制、染色質形成等。雖然miRNA在動物和植物模型中已被廣泛研究，但它們在真菌生長發育過程中的作用卻是未知的。新出現的證據表明，真菌是含有milRNA的。我們已經測定C. cinerea兩個發展階段（菌絲（mycelium）和原基（primordium））的小RNA。通過對這些小RNA序列的計算與分析，我們在C. cinerea的基因組中預測到了16個的milRNA基因和3個Dicer基因。 根據我們當前的數據和知識，我們提出此次研究來解決以下科學問題：（1）通過實驗來驗證預測到的milRNA，（2）確定這些經過實驗驗證的milRNA的功能，（3）用基因敲除的實驗來確定Dicer是否參與了milRNA的合成，（4）探究C. cinerea內milRNA的調控網絡。當此次研究完成時，我們將能更理解milRNA在菇的生長發育中的功能，完善對菇的生長發育的知識體系，並推動對miRNA的進化研究。

14116515.label: Realisation of objectives
14116515.value: Objective 1. To validate the occurrence and examine the expression patterns of the predicted milRNAs This part was completed. Due to the inconsistent results between 454 sequencing, used for the preliminary data, and Reverse Transcription Real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Another round of high-throughput small RNA sequencing was performed using illumina. As the result, 22 putative milRNAs were computational predicted in mycelium (MYC) and primordium (PRI) samples. Two of these novel putative milRNAs, cci-milR-12c and cci-milR-13e-5p, were validated using both Northern blot and qRT-PCR. Furthermore, in order to advance our understanding on the complex regulation underlying the whole life cycle of model mushroom, C. cinerea, especially for the germination of sexual basidiospore that the molecular mechanisms , either the transcriptomic and post-transcriptomic aspects, of this process remained unknown. Given that the potential roles of milRNAs on cell proliferation and differentiation have been suggested at the early fruiting body development, and the regulatory roles of miRNAs during the transition from gamete production to early embryonic development have been found, the RNA and small RNA profiling in the course of spore germination were investigated. In total, 35 of novel milRNAs were identified in either resting basidiospores or germinating spores. Seven of them were experimentally validated by qRT-PCR and among them, six were differentially expressed in spores. Objective 2. To determine if Dicer takes part in milRNA biogenesis in C. cinerea and characterize the phenotypic and gene expression changes of C. cinerea by knocking out Dicer genes in the mushroom This part is almost completed. Due to unsuccessful gene knockout with traditional methods, we tried to knockdown three putative Dicer-like proteins (DCLs) in C. cinerea by injecting small-interfering RNAs (siRNAs). For example, we tried to add 25uM small interfering RNAs (siRNAs) siRNAs targeting for each DCL to the stipe of primordium, add siRNAs to the YMG broth or spread siRNAs on the 9 mm YMG plates when the mycelial hyphae grow for 3 days. Considering only the expression levels of each DCL were reduced by 60-70% in the first attempt and there is no changes of milRNA expressions can be found. We increased the concentration of siRNAs from 25 uM to 50 uM by triple transfection instead of double transfection and extended the time of incubation from 24h to 48h. Although no milRNA was abolished after increasing the knockdown efficiency to 80%, lighter colour of mature fruiting body was observed. Therefore, the phenotypes controlled by DCLs was identified even the roles of DCLs in milRNA biogenesis cannot be confirmed here. Apart from improving the understanding on milRNA biogenesis in fungi, investigation on the roles of DCL can also provide new insight into the miRNA evolution among fungi and eukaryotic organisms. Even though the interaction between DCLs and the biogenesis of these two validated milRNAs were not confirmed, phylogenetic analysis using the protein sequences of DCL proteins of C. cinerea and that of animals, plants and other fungal species, such as other mushroom forming basidiomycetes and ascomycetes was performed to see if any information related to phylogenetic occurrence of miRNA-mediated regulatory system among fungi or kingdoms can be found. A novel group of DCL with PAZ domain were discovered and an early duplication and diversification of Dicer was suggested. Objective 3. To computationally and experimentally identify the genes targeted by the validated milRNAs and characterize their functions This part was completed. So as to minimize the false positive results, three algorithms, PITA, microTar and miRanda, were used simultaneously to predict the putative milRNA targets. Hundreds of putative targets were predicted for each milRNAs. Based on the GO and KOG enrichment functional analyses, putative targets of cci-milR-12c were related to RNA processing and that of cci-milR-13e-5p were associated with nucleic acid metabolism and protein production. Generally speaking, results from the GO and KOG term annotations of the two validated milRNAs were similar. Since none of the annotated KEGG pathways for milRNA targets were found to be significantly enriched, when using p-value cut-off at 0.05. Therefore, the results of KEGG analysis were not included here Objective 4. To characterize the phenotypic changes and milRNA target gene expression changes of C. cinerea mediated by milRNA inhibitors & Objective 5. To investigate the milRNA regulatory network during the mushroom transition from mycelium to primordium These two parts were completed. cci-milR-12c potentially controls the fungal pheromone, stage-specific hydrophobin and nucleotide metabolic process. Hydrophobin is required for the aerial hyphae in the mycelial stage and pheromone play an essential role in activating septal dissolution and clamp-cell fusion for the vegetative growth. Intriguingly, some genes related to the developmental processes in fungi, including actin, heat shock proteins, and protein kinase binding, were predicted to be the targets of cci-milR-13e-5p. Protein kinases and heat shock proteins were known to be responsible for nutrient depletion and higher incubation temperature at the initiation of fruiting body development. All of these putative targets were validated by milRNA inhibitor transfection and RNA-sequencing that their expressions were significantly downregulated after transfected with milRNA inhibitors. milRNA inhibitor transfections successfully reduced the milRNA expressions (fold change ≤0.5). Therefore, cci-milR-12c is more likely to regulate the growth of vegetative hyphae and cci-milR-13e-5p is more likely to control the dynamic structural changes during the transition from MYC to PRI development under a favourable conditions.

14116515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14116515.value: In this study, we have demonstrated differential post-transcriptional regulatory roles of milRNAs in the early fruiting body developmental transition, from mycelial to primordium stage, in the model mushroom forming fungus C. cinerea. It is also the first study to identify the presence of milRNA in C. cinerea and revealed their regulatory roles in cell proliferation and differentiation, two most critical cellular events occurred at fruiting body initiation, providing new insights into the regulatory mechanisms of fruiting body development and the potential functions of milRNAs in fungi. Moreover, we have found putative two miRNA biogenesis proteins, Dicer-like and AGO proteins, in the C. cinerea genome and investigated on the evolution of miRNA among eukaryotic organisms by phylogenetic analysis. One novel group of Dicer-like protein that was specific for mushroom-forming basidiomycetes, was identified here. Besides, we also make good use of the analysis pipeline established here to complete our understanding on the complex regulatory mechanisms underpin the whole life cycle of C. cinerea. Germination of sexual basidiospore is the beginning of mushroom life and it is another critical developmental stage that was poorly understood. Employing the computation target prediction and milRNA inhibitor transfection, the milRNA-mediating pathways involved in carbon source metabolism during the initiation of spore germination were revealed. To conclude, our findings serve as the foundation for fungal milRNA studies and contribute to further evolutionary developmental studies of fungi and contribute to the phylogenetic occurrence of miRNA-mediated regulatory system among different kingdoms. All the results related to the milRNA in MYC and PRI was published in PLoS One journal and the milRNA study of spore germination is included in the manuscript (under review) as attached.

14116515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14116515.value: Firstly, future experimental work is required to investigate the roles of PAZ-containing DCLs in milRNA biogenesis of other mushrooms and to determine if the milRNA homologs play a regulatory role in other mushroom forming fungi. Laccaria bicolor is the most suitable candidate, considering homologs of cci-milR-12c and the PAZ-domain containing DLC were found in this mushroom, suggesting the biogenesis machinery of milRNA is more likely to be presented in this mushroom. Secondly, a epigenetic enzyme was the potential targets of spore-specific milRNAs in C.cinerea and the regulatory roles of miRNAs in gametes production and embryonic development were extensively studied in animals, Hence, the epigenetic profile during spore germination and outgrowth using the whole genome bisulfide sequencing is needed to performed in order to further evaluate the roles of milRNAs in transgenerational inheritance by contributing to the survival and adaption to the changing environment, which in turns can beneficial to the in vitro cultivation of mushroom in field.

14116515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14116515.value: The morphological changes during fruiting body development is well-known but the molecular mechanism controlling this process is largely unknown. In this study, we aim to fill in this gap by investigating on the changes of gene expression profile at the most critical developmental transition involving the multicellular development in the mushroom-forming fungus, Coprinopsis cinerea. Coprinopsis cinerea is the model organism with well-characterized genome and standardized genetic modification approaches for enormous scope for experimental manipulation. Results of this study contribute to both theoretical and practical aspects. Our findings not only advance the understanding on the complex mechanisms of multicellular development in macroscopic fungi and provide valuable information of comparison to fungal milRNA study in the future, but also highlighted the possible phylogenetic occurrence of milRNA regulatory machinery among kingdoms. Furthermore, identification of milRNA-mediated pathway underlying the spore germination and fruiting body development provide new insight into the improvements of in vitro cultivation of edible mushroom, especially for those are taxonomically closely related to C. cinerea and with economic and biotechnological significance, such as Agaricus bisporus.

14117015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117015.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is common cancer worldwide and in Hong Kong. The incidence of HCC is featured with the gender disparity, as it occurs much more frequent in males than in females. Solid data have indicated a role of β-estradiol (E2) in the protection or prevention of HCC via a number channels, among which the generation of estrogen metabolite 2-methoxyestradiol (2-ME), one of E2 major metabolites, appears to be a key player. Experimental data have demonstrated that 2-ME inhibits HCC through suppression of angiogenesis, cell cycle arrest, and induction of apoptosis. Interestingly, the level of cytochrome P450 1A2 (CYP1A2), the key enzyme in metabolizing E2 to 2-ME, is markedly reduced in HCC. It is therefore postulated that such reduction in the generation of endogenous 2-ME may play a permissive role in proliferation of the HCC cells. But why CYP1A2 is reduced in HCC in the first place? The underlying mechanism leading to the CYP1A2 reduction in HCC is currently unknown. Our preliminary work by analysing the 3’UTR region of human CYP1A2 has identified potential recognition elements for two miR-143 and miR-650, the level of both are known to be increased in HCC. Thus, it appears that there is a reverse relationship between the level of CYP1A2 and the expression of miR-143 and miR-650 in HCC. However, whether these two miRs will bind to the CYP1A2 3’UTR and regulate the expression of CYP1A2 are unknown. In addition to the potential regulation of miRs, the level of CYP1A2 may also be controlled by the methylation as the promoter of human CYP1A2 is rich for CpG contents and its hypermethylation has been shown to reduce the expression of CYP1A2. However, whether this is the case in HCC has not yet been studied. We hypothesize that the reduction of CYP1A2 expression is caused by increased levels of miR-143/miR-650 and the promoter methylation in HCC. This proposal aims to test this hypothesis by examining whether miR-143 and miR-650 will bind to the predicted elements in the 3’UTR and whether the hypermethylation of CYP1A2 promoter occurs in HCC to silence the expression of CYP1A2. We believe, the findings of this study will enable us to understand more about the progression and growth of HCC and may also help explore if metabolites of β-estradiol have a role in treatment of HCC.

14117015.label: Realisation of objectives
14117015.value: The Objective No 1 and No 2 are to verify the levels of CYP1A2, miR-143 and miR-650 in HCC and to determine the regulation of CYP1A2 levels by miR-143 and miR-650 in HCC. The levels of miR-143 and miR-650 were respectively found to be increased in HCC by two publication Diagn Pathol 2014;9:135 (miR-143) and J Surg Oncol 2013;107:105-10 miR-650). We collected 91 HCC tumor tissues and their match non-tumor liver tissues to measure CYP1A2 and both miRs. We found that the expression of CYP1A2 was significantly reduced in the tumor tissue samples compared with non-tumor samples, however, the levels of miR-143 and miR-650 in tumor samples were not different from that in non-tumor samples. At present, we cannot explain these different results. Nevertheless, our negative result indicated that the further study of the regulatory role of both miRs in the expression of CYP1A2 does not make sense. We conclude that though the 3’UTR region of human CYP1A2 contains the recognition elements for two miR-143 and miR-650, these two miRNAs do not appear to involve the regulation of CYP1A2 in HCC. Based on these results, we therefore decided to focus on the significance of CYP1A2 in HCC by 1) correlating its levels with clinicopathological features; 2) studying the impact of CYP1A2 on some key oncogenic features; and 3) exploring the role of CYP1A2 in anti-HCC treatments. The Objective No 3 is to determine the regulation of CYP1A2 expression by methylation in HCC. We have demonstrated that the hypermethylation of CYP1A2 promoter contributes to the reduction of CYP1A2 expression in HCC. Certain HDAC inhibitors including suberoylanilide hydroxamic acid (SAHA), trichostatin A (TSA), sodium butyrate (NaB) and valproic acid (VPA) can significantly induce the CYP1A2 promoter. By analyzing CYP1A2 and clinicopathological features, we have further found that the HCC patients with higher level of CYP1A2 have better disease-free survival than those with the lower CYP1A2. In cultured cell system, we have shown that CYP1A2 overexpression can obviously inhibit the migration and invasion of HCC cells and furthermore it can decrease the sphere formation and the expression of cancer stem cell markers in HCC, whereas CYP1A2 downregulation exerts opposite effects in HCC. To study the therapeutic value of CYP1A2, we have demonstrated that the overexpression can significantly overcome the resistance of HCC cells to sorafenib treatment.

14117015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14117015.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is common cancer worldwide and in Hong Kong. Most patients with HCC are unresectable at the time of diagnosis because of widespread intra- or extra-hepatic involvement or limited hepatic reserves resulting from coexisting advanced cirrhosis. The median survival for these patients with unresectable tumor is very short, less than 3 months. The poor outcome of HCC is mainly due to lack of effective drug treatments for patients, especially for those at advanced stage and not suitable for surgical treatments. Our data have demonstrated that the expression of CYP1A2 is significantly reduced in HCC and that the prognosis of HCC patients with higher level of CYP1A2 are much better than those with the lower CYP1A2. We have further shown that the upregulation of CYP1A2 can significantly reduce oncogenic features of HCC and greatly increase the sensitivity of HCC cells to sorafenib treatment, a common chemotherapeutic agent for the advanced HCC. We conclude that CYP1A2 expression is reduced in HCC and that its upregulation can significantly inhibit the growth of HCC and sensitize the tumor cells to sorafenib.

14117215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117215.value: Selective growth restriction (sIUGR) is a distinct type of fetal growth restriction which describes the discordant growth between the co-twins of a monochorionic (MC) pregnancy. The prognosis of IUGR could be poor because of malnutrition and hypoxia, includes in-utero death, preterm delivery and cerebral palsy. sIUGR-MC twin pregnancy is a unique model for studying placental-related growth disorders, because the other two major factors for growth restriction, namely the intrinsic fetal genetic factor and the maternal environment are controlled (or identical) for the twin pairs. Hence, any differential placental gene expression between the twin pairs can reflect the dysfunctional status of the placenta of sIUGR twins. However, epigenetic research that addresses specifically this issue is limited. Hence, we propose to apply the cutting-edge technology, next-generation sequencing for RNA-sequencing to study the global gene expression in this unique model of sIUGR. The objectives are (1) to investigate any difference in placental gene expression between the sIUGR twin and the normally growing co-twin in MC twin pregnancies; (2) To correlate the changes in placental gene expression with the severity and types of sIUGR. Successful identification of abnormal placental gene expression in sIUGR will not only add knowledge to the path-mechanism of the placental related IUGR applicable to both singleton and twin pregnancies, it may also open further research on non-invasive fetal monitoring, using placental RNA measurable in maternal plasma. This is a collaborative prospective study involving multiple centers with two phases. Women who have sIUGR-MC twin pregnancies, diagnosed by ultrasound with estimated fetal weight < 10th percentile are recruited. Severity and subtypes of sIUGR are also assessed with ultrasound. Exclusion criteria are: dichorionic twin pregnancies, fetuses with chromosomal abnormalities, fetal in-utero death or miscarriage. The clinical management of the recruited subjects is not affected by the study. At time of delivery, placental samples from each of the twin pair are collected and process immediately and properly at delivery to minimize RNA degradation. Special care is also taken to avoid cross-contamination. First Phase: Gene expression of the placental tissue of sIUGR twins will be analyzed by RNA-sequencing, and compared with that of the normally growing co-twins. We plan to recruit 10 cases in 10 months. Second Phase: Any gene expression that has significant variation will be selected for validation using PCR and other technology. 20 cases are to be recruited in 20 months.

14117715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117715.value: Lung nodules of all sizes is a common finding in chest radiograph and computed tomograph (CT) scans in adults, especially with increasing image resolution and the popularity of routine health checks. In general, nodules that are larger, particularly when more than 1 cm have increase chance of being malignant. Traditional ways to obtain diagnosis can be by bronchoscopic biopsy, or CT guided FNA depending on the size and location of the lesion. The former is limited to biopsying more central lesions, sometimes using simple x-ray guidance. The latter is limited to biopsying more larger peripheral lesions with high risk of pneumothorax and lung hemorrhage. Electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopy (ENB) using the advance superDimension (SDS) version 7.0 can achieve biopsy of both central and peripheral lesions accurately, guided by real-time 3-dimension CT image virtual bronchoscopy using electromagnetic positioning. In brief, this bronchoscopy technique allows the clinician to direct the bronchoscope to any lesion within the lungs for biopsy as instructed by the advance navigation software. Apart from doing without the disadvantages of the traditional biopsy methods, an added advantage is that this technique allows biopsy of multiple lung lesions in the same setting. So far, there has been no prospective trials of ENB SDS in the Asian population. Furthermore, the accuracy of the biopsy instrument in “hitting” the target has never been assessed. The proposed study will prospectively investigate the accuracy, diagnostic yield and safety of ENB SDS in the Asian population. The study will use hybrid operating room real-time dynaCT as gold standard to determine the accuracy of the procedure and also subsequent surgical excision biopsy as the gold standard for the diagnostic yield sensitivity and specificity. The detailed follow-up in the peri-procedural period will provide information on any safety issues. Furthermore, case matched comparisons will be made with patients who have undergone the conventional diagnostic procedures for the lung nodules to compare yield and safety. A positive study showing similar or better yield and safety of ENB SDS compared with conventional biopsy approaches will provide supporting evidence for the revision of current guidelines for work-up of small peripheral lung nodules. The study will show that this technology is indeed applicable to the Asian population with more incidence of multiple lung nodules, and more lung ground glass opacities (GGO) type lesions. 14117715.label: Realisation of objectives
14117715.value: During the study period 59 consecutive patients underwent ENB-guided procedures in the hybrid theatre. ENB-guided pathological sampling of lung nodules was performed in 47 patients with lung nodules of average size 2.0 ± 1.1 cm. The accuracy of diagnosis was 86.2%, with 78.2% nodules suspicious or confirmed to be malignant. Incidence of complications was low (pneumothorax 2.1%, minor bleeding 8.5%), and majority of patients were discharged early (length of hospital stay 2.8 ± 1.7 days). There was no perioperative mortality. Thus we can conclude that a hybrid operating theatre can provide unparalleled real-time imaging to guide and confirm successful ENB localization of difficult-to-reach or small lesions, which facilitates accurate biopsy. We were able to assess all 3 objectives set out in the study of success of ENB procedure in providing pathological diagnosis of pulmonary lesion(s); the complications and their frequency; and real-time accurary of ENB biopsy when performed by real-time dynaCT in hybrid operating room. These experiences and achievements have been published in 8 publications, and 2 presentations.

14117715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14117715.value: We were able to publish 9 articles in international indexed peer-reviewed journals and with oral presentation in Asia Pacific Society of Respirology (APSR) annual meeting based on our ENB experience during the study period. We published the world first report of how we used hybrid operating room cone-beam CT scan to improve accuracy of ENB biopsy. In addition, we published how our hybrid operating room ENB approach is useful in marking lesions for uniportal VATS surgery, as well as our technique of triple dye marking. Our biospy data presented in APSR also won the travelling scholarship for the annual meeting that year.

14117715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14117715.value: With the experienced gained duing ENB SuperDimension pulmonary nodule biopsy in the hybrid operating room setting, we can : 1) Investigate workflows that would allow us reduce the number of cone-beam CT scans needed during the procedure , to reduce radiation to the patient while maintaining diagnostic yield. 2) Investigate the use of hybrid operating room CBCT with other navigation bronchoscopy systems, such as Veran , Broncus Lung Point and BodyVision for bronchoscopic biopsy and other procedures. 3) Our development of hybrid operating room cone-beam CT ENB platform and workflow has enable us to be leaders in this area. Thus our recent involvement in international trial for ENB microwave ablation for small lung cancers in the Navablate Study ( ClinicalTrials.gov, Identifier: NCT03569111) and receiving funding from latest RGC grant round.

14117715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14117715.value: During the study period, we have established the technique of using hybrid operating room cone-beam CT scan as a valuable adjunct to electromagnetic navigation bronchoscopic (ENB) biopsy and other related procedures. This technique is associated with low complication rate and a high diagnostic yield, compared with ENB biopsy by other approaches. Development of this high-tech approach has created great opportunities for future development of ENB marking and bronchoscopic ablation, for which we are one of the leaders in the world.

14117815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117815.value: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) has become a major health problem and burdens in our community. Renal fibrosis is a key process to CKD, but treatment remains ineffective due to the lack of clear mechanisms identified. We have previously found that Smad3, a key mediator of TGF-beta signaling, mediates renal fibrosis via a number of microRNAs (miRNAs) and targeting these miRNAs inhibit renal fibrosis but also produce the off-target effect. Therefore, therapy aiming to specifically block fibrosis needs to target precisely the Smad3-dependent genes related to fibrosis. By using the next generation sequencing (RNA-seq), we have identified a number of Smad3-dependent long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) that are associated with renal fibrosis. Of them, an np_5318 is a novel lncRNA that is significantly upregulated in the fibrotic kidney of Smad3 wild-type (WT) mice but not in Smad3 gene knockout (KO) mice where renal fibrosis is absent. We therefore hypothesized that TGF-beta/Smad3 may mediate renal fibrosis via the Smad3-dependent np_5318 lncRNA and that targeting this lncRNA may represent a novel and specific therapy for CKD. We plan to examine this hypothesis in this grant proposal by 3 specific aims. First, we will define the functional role and therapeutic potential of np_5318 in two well-established mouse models of obstructive nephropathy and type-2 diabetic nephropathy in vivo and in kidney tubular epithelial cells and mesangial cells in vitro by knocking down or overexpressing the np_5318. Second, we will investigate the mechanisms whereby np_5318 is regulated by TGF-beta1 via the Smad3-dependent mechanism in Smad3 WT and KO mice and kidney cells. Finally, we will study the underlying mechanism of np_5318-mediated renal fibrosis by identifying the potential target gene the ErbB4 in vivo and in vitro. The ultimate goal of this study is to investigate into the precise mechanism with specific therapeutic potential for CKD by targeting the Smad3-dependent lncRNA related to renal fibrosis. Identification of a novel lncRNA np_5318 that mediates renal fibrosis will be the first step towards the development of the specific therapy for CKD by targeting this lncRNA. Thus, outcomes from this study will be highly significant both scientifically and clinically 慢性腎臟病（CKD）已成為全球的主要健康問題和經濟負擔。 腎臟纖維化是CKD的主要原因，但其機制不清，故治療效果欠 佳。我們發現，Smad3蛋白是轉化生長因子TGF-β信號的重要 介質。Smad3通過微RNA（miRNAs）介導腎纖維化。但針對 這些miRNA治療腎臟纖維化易產生脫靶標效應。因此，特異性 阻斷纖維化需要更精確定位于Smad3纖維化相關基因。通過使 用二代測序（RNA-SEQ），我們發現了一些Smad3依賴性長鏈 非編碼RNA（lncRNAs）與腎纖維化相關聯。其中，np_5318是 一種新型的Smad3腎臟纖維化相關lncRNA。因此，我們假設， TGF-β/ Smad3蛋白可經Smad3依賴性np_5318 lncRNA介導腎纖維 化， 而針對np_5318 lncRNA可能是一種新的抗腎臟纖維化靶向 治療方法。為了驗證這個假設，我們首先通過高或低表達 np_5318，在腎臟細胞系和小鼠梗阻性腎病和2型糖尿病腎病模型 檢測其功能作用。其次，我們將在Smad3基因欠缺小鼠腎細胞研 究np_5318的作用機制。最後，我們將研究抗np_5318治療腎臟 纖維化的臨床治療作用。 因此，這項研究結果將產生非常顯著 的科學理論和臨床價值。

14117815.label: Realisation of objectives
14117815.value: We have successfully conducted and fully addressed all 3 Specific Aims as originally described with three major findings/achievements as described below. First, we found lncRNA np_5318 is a novel lncRNA located within the intron region between the first and second exons of Erbb4 gene on chromosome 1 of the mouse genome. We then named this lncRNA as Erbb4-IR. Erbb4-IR was significantly up-regulated in the diseased kidneys of UUO and type 2 diabetic kidneys in db/db mice, but not in the kidney disease with acute kidney injury induced by cisplatin- and ischemic reperfusion, demonstrating that Erbb4-IR is pro-fibrotic specifically, which was confirmed in vitro by silencing Erbb4-IR to block TGF-beta1, high glucose, and AGEs-induced fibrosis in tubular epithelial cells and glomerular mesangial cells. Importantly, we found that silencing Erbb4-IR is capable of inhibiting progressive renal fibrosis in both mouse models of UUO and in type-2 diabetic nephropathy in db/db mice. All these findings reveal a functional role of Erbb4-IR in the pathogenesis of renal fibrosis in different types of chronic kidney diseases including diabetic nephropathy. More importantly, these findings also provide a clinical evidence that targeting Erbb4-IR may be a novel therapeutic potential for chronic kidney diseases associated with progressive renal fibrosis. Second, we also identified that Erbb4-IR is tightly regulated by Smad3 as Smad3 protein directly binds on the promoter region of Erbb4-IR, indicating that Erbb4-IR is a direct Smad3 target gene. In addition, we also found that Erbb4-IR is upregulated in response to high glucose (HG), advanced glycation end-products (AGEs), or TGF-beta1 in cultured mouse tubular epithelial cells (mTECs) and mesangial cells (MCs) in a Smad3-dependent mechanism as deletion of Smad3 blunted upregulation of renal Erbb4-IR and thus protected against renal fibrosis in both UUO and diabetic nephropathy. The regulatory role of Smad3 in Erbb4-IR expression was further demonstrated in Smad3 or Smad2 knockout mouse embryonic fibroblasts that deletion of Smad3, but not Smad2, was able to block TGF-beta1 or AGE-induced Erbb4-IR expression. Third, we have uncovered the underlying mechanisms by which Erbb4-IR mediates renal fibrosis. Excitingly, we found that Smad7, a negative regulator of TGF-beta/Smad signaling, was a target gene of Erbb4-IR as a binding site of Erbb4-IR is predicted on the 3’UTR of Smad7 gene and overexpression of Erbb4-IR significantly inhibited the reporter activity of Smad7.Thus, knockdown of Erbb4-IR restored the negative feedback of TGF-beta/Smad signaling and protected against the UUO and diabetic kidneys from progressive fibrosis by upregulating Smad7 while inactivating TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling. In addition, we also found a physical binding site of Erbb4-IR in the genomic sequence of miR-29b and silencing Erbb4-IR largely increased expression of miR-29b under diabetic conditions in vivo and in vitro. Taken together, results from this study indicate that Erbb4-IR is a profibrogenic lncRNA responsible for TGF-beta/Smad3-mediated renal fibrosis. LncRNA Erbb4-IR may induce renal fibrosis by targeting Smad7 and miR-29. Thus, targeting Erbb4-IR may represent as a precise therapy for chronic kidney diseases in general. In addition, the research fund was used to partly support a PhD student Dr YOU Yongke for his research in type-2 diabetic nephropathy.

14117815.label: Major findings and research outcome
14117815.value: There are three major findings/achievements from this study. First, lncRNA np_5318 is a novel lncRNA located within the intron region between the first and second exons of Erbb4 gene on chromosome 1 of the mouse genome. We then named this lncRNA as Erbb4-IR (Mol Ther 2018;26:148-161). Erbb4-IR was up-regulated in the diseased kidneys of UUO and diabetic kidneys in db/db mice, but not in those with acute kidney injury , demonstrating that Erbb4-IR is pro-fibrotic specifically. Importantly, silencing Erbb4-IR is capable of inhibiting progressive renal fibrosis in both mouse models of UUO and diabetic nephropathy and in vitro under high levels of TGF-beta1, high glucose, and AGEs, revealing a functional role of Erbb4-IR in the pathogenesis of renal fibrosis and providing a clinical evidence for targeting Erbb4-IR as a novel therapeutic potential for chronic kidney diseases. All these novel findings have been published in top rank journals (Diabetes 2018;67:731-744; Mol Ther 2018;26:148-161; Noncoding RNA Res 2017;2:68-73). Second, Smad3 is a key mediator in renal fibrosis (Kidney Int 2018;93:173-187; Hypertension 2017;70:822-830) and Erbb4-IR is tightly regulated by Smad3 as Smad3 protein directly binds on the promoter region of Erbb4-IR, indicating that Erbb4-IR is a direct Smad3 target gene (Mol Ther 2018;26:148-161). Erbb4-IR is upregulated by high glucose, AGEs, or TGF-beta1via a Smad3-dependent mechanism as deletion of Smad3 inhibited renal Erbb4-IR and thus protected against renal fibrosis in both UUO and diabetic nephropathy (Mol Ther 2018;26:148-161; Diabetes 2018;67731-744). The regulatory role of Smad3 in Erbb4-IR expression was further demonstrated in Smad3 or Smad2 knockout mouse embryonic fibroblasts in which deletion of Smad3, but not Smad2, was able to block TGF-beta1 or AGE-induced Erbb4-IR expression. Third, We have uncovered the underlying mechanisms by which Erbb4-IR mediates renal fibrosis by targeting Smad7, a negative regulator of TGF-beta/Smad signaling (Mol Ther 2018;26:148-161; Clin Sci 2017;131:1955-1969), and miR-29b(Diabetes 2018;67731-744; Noncoding RNA Res 2017;2:68-73). Thus, knockdown of Erbb4-IR restored the renal Smad7 and miR-29b, thereby protecting against the UUO and diabetic kidneys from progressive fibrosis. Taken together, results from this study indicate that Erbb4-IR is a fibrogenic lncRNA responsible for TGF-beta/Smad3-mediated renal fibrosis. LncRNA Erbb4-IR may induce renal fibrosis by targeting Smad7 and miR-29. Thus, targeting Erbb4-IR may represent as a precise therapy for chronic kidney diseases in general. In addition, the research fund was used to partly support a PhD student Dr YOU Yongke for his research in type-2 diabetic nephropathy.

14117815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14117815.value: Compared to miRNAs, lncRNAs are more specific in terms of species, tissues/cells, and disease natures. Thus, the discovery of a Smad3-dependent lncRNA Erbb4-IR in mediating progressive renal fibrosis may provide a strong rationale and evidence for the development of a novel therapy for chronic kidney diseases including diabetic nephropathy clinically.

14117815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14117815.value: In the present study, we first identified that Erbb4-IR is a Smad3-dependent lncRNA responsible for progressive renal fibrosis in mouse models of obstructive and diabetic nephropathy. We found that Erbb4-IR is tightly regulated by Smad3 in response to TGF-beta1, high glocuse, and AGEs under various disease conditions. We also uncovered the underlying mechanisms that lncRNA Erbb4-IR induces renal fibrosis by targeting Smad7 and miR-29. Importantly, inhibition of this lncRNA is capable of blocking progressive renal fibrosis in both obstructive and diabetic kidney diseases. Results from this study suggest that targeting Erbb4-IR may represent a precise therapy for chronic kidney diseases in general.

14117915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117915.value: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a prevalent, serious, and recurrent mental disorder with significant morbidity and mortality. However, MDD is noted to have a marked clinical heterogeneity, suggesting an underlying diversity of different etiologies, which may have contributed to their unsatisfactory treatment response. By delineating the clinical subtypes of MDD and its associated pathophysiology, it might be feasible to develop specific treatment strategies and help understanding of the long-term prognosis of the illness. Recent studies, including ours, suggest that REM sleep behavior disorder (RBD) comorbid with MDD may potentially represent a subgroup of MDD with possible underlying aetiology of dopamine dysfunction and probable future neurodegeneration. RBD is a REM sleep disorder characterized by dream enacting behavior and sleep-related injury. Typically, RBD affects older males (age >60) but it is being increasingly recognized among younger age group (age <50), especially individuals with mental illnesses (predominantly MDD) and usage of psychotropics. Although RBD is regarded as a psychotropic-induced side effect, increasing literature suggested that it is a complex condition. A recent proof-of-concept PET neuroimaging study conducted by our group reported that MDD+RBD subjects showed more dopamine dysfunction compared to those subjects with MDD only. The finding supported that RBD features in MDD may signify the underlying dopamine dysfunction. However, the study was limited by a small sample size without any measurement of specific MDD symptoms related to dopamine dysfunction. By a 2-phase design, this proposed study will fill the gaps in the current understanding of RBD co-morbid MDD in the following aspects. Firstly, by using validated tools and polysomnography, we will be able to provide an accurate estimation of the prevalence of RBD and the associated socio-demographic data in patients with MDD. Secondly, we will document the detailed clinical profiles and severity of MDD that may suggest a dopamine dysfunction, including psychomotor retardation, anhedonia and personality trait of harm avoidance/ lower novelty seeking. Thirdly, we will search for the early neurocognitive and autonomic markers suggestive of any potential signs of early neurodegeneration in MDD+RBD. By having a larger and adequate sample size, we will be able to correlate the neuroimaging findings with clinical subtypes/ profiling of the subjects. By profiling MDD+RBD and its association with dopamine dysfunction and neurodegeneration markers, we may be able to identify a subgroup of MDD for future targeted intervention and exploration of potential neuroprotective treatments.

14117915.label: Realisation of objectives
14117915.value: REM sleep behaviour disorder (RBD) is a REM sleep parasomnia characterised by dream enacting behaviours and sleep-related injury. Ample evidence suggested that RBD is a precursor of synucleinopathy (e.g. Parkinson’s disease) at which dopamine dysfunction is a core pathophysiology. While major depressive disorder (MDD) is regarded as a pre-motor manifestation of Parkinson’s disease, it is also found to increase the risk of developing Parkinson’s disease in typical RBD patients. There is a distinct possibility that the development of the RBD features among MDD patients may represent an early phase of α-synucleinopathy neurodegeneration. From the data of our previous epidemiological studies and case control studies, we found that RBD is much more common in the patients with a mental illness (substantial proportion suffering from MDD) than in the general population (6.4% vs. 0.38%). However, there remains many unanswered questions about the demographic and clinical profiling of patients with co-morbid MDDRBD and their outcomes. We designed the current two-phase study to fill the gaps in the current understanding of RBD with co-morbid MDD. Phase 1 was a clinical epidemiologic study using structural clinical psychiatric interview in a psychiatric out-patient clinic by recruiting a consecutive sample of patients with major depressive disorder. Phase 2 consisted of detailed investigations including video polysomnography(vPSG) and neurological assessment, neurocognitive profiling, and PET neuroimaging for striatal dopamine transmission for selected subjects recruited from phase 1. Through this design, the study aimed to achieve two main objectives: 1. To establish the prevalence of REM sleep behaviour disorder (RBD) in MDD patients using the validated tools and standardized diagnostic criteria, and to characterize the clinical profile of depressive symptoms and personality traits in patients with co-morbid MDD and RBD. 2. To investigate the underlying dopamine dysfunction in patient with co-morbid MDD and RBD by 18F-DOPA, 11C-Raclopride and 18F-FDG PET neuroimaging and its correlations with clinical, polysomnographic and neurocognitive parameters. We also aimed to test two hypotheses in this study: 1. The occurrence of RBD in patients with MDD represents a subgroup of MDD with distinctive clinical, sleep and neuroimaging findings of dopamine dysfunction, including a higher degree of psychomotor retardation, anhedonia, impulsivity, and personality profile of harm avoidance and lower novelty seeking. 2. MDD+ RBD subjects will demonstrate dopamine dysfunction on PET neuroimaging, more olfactory, color vision and other neurocognitive deficits than the subjects with MDD only, which may suggest a distinctive neurodegenerative basis for this subgroup of MDD+RBD. The study was completed as planned and the objectives were achieved. We recruited 504 subjects in total, of which 316 of them were confirmed to be eligible and completed our phase 1 assessment. We screened subjects who completed phase 1 study with RBDQ-HK, a validated, self-reported questionnaire to screen for subjects with high and low likelihood of having co-morbid RBD. 52 screen-positive and 29 screen-negative subjects were recruited into phase 2 of the study. The subjects completed video polysomnographic and neurocognitive assessment. Of the 81 subjects, 12 were vPSG-confirmed RBD, 38 were sub-syndromal RBD, and 31 were labelled as non-case. 55 of the subjects (9 vPSG-confirmed RBD, 26 sub-syndromal RBD and 20 non-cases) underwent 18F-DOPA, 11C-Raclopride and 18F-FDG PET scan. Using this sample, we achieved objective 1 by making an estimation of the prevalence of RBD in our MDD sample. We estimated that RBD has a prevalence of 9.5 % (95% confidence interval=5.0%-18.1%) in patients with MDD. The prevalence of RBD in male and female MDD patients are of 21.1% and 6.3% (95% confidence interval=8.5%-43.3% and 2.5%-15.2%, respectively). These figures are much higher than reported prevalence of idiopathic RBD in the community (about 0.3-1.4% worldwide). We were able to characterise the clinical characteristics of this subgroup and compare it with MDD patients who were without RBD. The MDD patients with co-morbid RBD (n=12) have a mean age of 56.6 and is male dominant (66%). The age of this group of patients is slightly younger than those reported for typical idiopathic RBD patients (mean age of onset in early 60s). The group with sub-syndromal. RBD features, however, are younger (mean age 48.7), female predominant (68% female) and more depressed. We tested our hypothesis 1 using case-control comparison and we did not find distinct clinical characteristics in the vPSG-confirmed RBD group after adjusting for age, gender and severity of depression, except that the diagnosis of RBD in MDD is a significant predictor of constipation. However, we found significant correlation between aggressiveness/impulsiveness/compulsiveness and severity of clinical and polysomnographic features of RBD in patients with MDD with co-morbid RBD spectrum (comprising cases with vPSG-confirmed RBD and sub-syndromal RBD features). This finding indirectly support the notion that RBD interacts with clinical characteristics of MDD. For objective 2, we found negative correlation between level of presynaptic dopaminergic function of putamen and severity of clinical and polysomnographic features of RBD. Our study also found that impulsiveness in this group of patients is correlated with level of presynaptic DOPA uptake of putamen. However, we did not found distinct dopamine dysfunction and neurocognitive deficit in patients with co-morbid MDD and RBD. In summary, our study is the first study that gives an estimation of prevalence of RBD among MDD patients. We confirmed that the prevalence of RBD is high among patients with MDD when compared to reported figures on the prevalence of typical RBD in community worldwide. Our MDD+RBD patients are also younger than typical idiopathic RBD patients. While the result did not demonstrate that MDD patients with comorbid RBD have distinct clinical, neurocognitive and dopaminergic function profile, it suggested that aggressiveness/impulsiveness/compulsiveness, RBD features and striatal dopaminergic dysfunction are interrelated in patients with MDD co-morbid with RBD. We also identified a group of MDD patients with sub-syndromal RBD features. There is a lack of literature in describing the outcome of this type of patients. While the demographics of this group of patients differ from those with confirmed RBD, it would be of interest to observe their progress to see if the group, or a subset of the group, represent prodromal state of RBD.
