14117915.label: Major findings and research outcome
14117915.value: In the phase 1 of the study, we consecutively recruited 504 MDD subjects. 35 of the subjects were excluded. Among the 469 eligible subjects, 316 of them have been clinically interviewed with the confirmation of their disease history as well as potential symptoms of RBD. By a cutoff of RBDQ-HK total score 20/21, those MDD subjects were further divided into screen+ (i.e. RBDQ-HK total score ≥ 21) (n=147) and screen- (n=169). Eventually, 51 screen+ and 31 screen- subjects underwent PSG study and 12 of them were vPSG-confirmed MDD+RBD. The positive and negative predictive value of RBDQ-HK using total score 20/21 as cutoff are 21.1% and 100%, respectively. We estimated a prevalence of RBD of 9.5 % (95% confidence interval=5.0%-18.1%) in MDD population with a post-stratification weighting method. We found a prevalence of 21.1% and 6.3% (95% confidence interval=8.5%-43.3% and 2.5%-15.2%, respectively) for male and female patients with MDD, respectively. In phase 2 study (n=81), we compared vPSG-confirmed RBD(n=12), patients with sub-syndromal (i.e. not meeting clinical or vPSG diagnostic threshold) RBD features(n=38) and MDD only subjects(n=31). With adjustment for age, gender and severity of depression as confounders, we did not find significant difference in symptoms profile and neurocognitive profile among the three groups. The presence of vPSG-confirmed RBD, however, is a significant predictor of constipation (p=0.012). Among the patients with comorbid RBD spectrum (vPSG-confirmed RBD and patients with sub-syndromal RBD features), it was found that the level of punding/hobbyism and non-planning domain of impulsivity are negatively correlated with level of excessive tonic EMG activities during REM sleep after being adjusted for age, gender and severity of depression. Interestingly the level of punding/hobbyism and aggressiveness are positively correlated with self-reported RBD symptoms severity. 55 subjects from phase 2 study underwent PET neuroimaging (9 RBD, 26 prodromal RBD and 20 non-cases) to investigate their striatal dopamine function. There was no significant difference in striatal dopamine transmission among the three groups. For subjects with co-morbid MDD and RBD spectrum, the level of impulsiveness is positively correlated with striatal presynaptic dopamine transmission (BIS non-planning subscale with 18F-DOPA putamen/cerebellum uptake ratio: Spearman’s rho = 0.37, p= 0.036; BIS total score with with 18F-DOPA putamen/cerebellum uptake ratio/putamen K constant/caudate K constant: Spearman’s rho = 0.37, p= 0.037/0.39, p=0.028/0.36 p=0.041, respectively). In this group, the level of excessive tonic EMG during REM sleep and the severity of dream enactment behaviour were negatively correlated with putamen presynaptic dopamine function.

14117915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14117915.value: From this study, patients with depression and co-morbid RBD have a younger onset (mid 50s in our sample), when compared to patients with idiopathic RBD (generally in early-mid 60s). This indirectly support the notion that depression and/or related factor such as antidepressant treatment may hasten the development of synucleinopathic neurodegeneration. The potential for further development would be to follow up on the patients with co-morbid RBD and see if they have an expedited neurodegeneration course. We identified a group of patients with sub-syndromal RBD, and the implication of this status is unclear. This group might represent a prodromal state of RBD or neurodegeneration. We propose a follow-up study to monitor the progression of clinical, neurocognitive, polysomnographic and neuroimaging features of the MDD+RBD and sub-syndromal RBD subjects. The study also revealed the relationship of aggressiveness/impulsiveness/compulsiveness with clinical and polysomnographic feature in patients with RBD or sub-syndromal RBD. This indirectly suggests that RBD interact with MDD’s symptoms profile and it have implication in formulating pharmacological treatment strategies for depressive symptoms in this group of patients. The current study used only self-reported questionnaires to assess the aggressiveness/impulsiveness/compulsiveness dimension. We are planning to follow-up this finding using computerised, task-based assessment tool.

14117915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14117915.value: REM sleep behaviour disorder(RBD) is well recognised as a strong predictor for development of neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease and Dementia of Lewy Bodies. Our study confirmed that the prevalence of RBD is high among patients with depression, at 9.5%. These RBD patients also have a relatively young onset when compared to patients with RBD but without depression. Our study did not find characteristics specific to this group of patients, except for their proneness to have constipation. However, we did find that the level of RBD symptoms and muscle tone during REM sleep (which should be absent in healthy people) are related to some measures of how aggressive and impulsive one is. The level of muscle tone during REM sleep is also related to dopamine function in a part of the midbrain called putamen. This shows that in this group of patients, the severity of RBD is linked to certain aspect of psychiatric presentation and dopamine function of the brain. It would be important to follow up this group of patients to see if they will develop neurodegenerative diseases just like typical RBD without depression, and whether it will happen at an earlier age.

14119115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119115.value: Smad7 has been well demonstrated as a negative regulator of TGF-β signaling, its alteration in expression often results in diseases such as cancer and fibrosis. Recently we have investigated the role of Smad7 in regulating bone remodeling during development using wild type (WT) and Smad7ΔE1 (KO) mice, in which functional Smad7 is disrupted. We demonstrated that partial loss of Smad7 in mice leads to compromised bone quality, with reduced osteogenesis and enhanced osteoclatogensis. In order to further study the underlying mechanisms and downstream targets of Smad7, we have performed RNA Sequencing (RNA-Seq) analysis of the bone tissues from the Smad7 KO and wild type mice. Using bioinformatics tools, we have identified 739 differentially expressed genes, and further selected 16 candidate genes (> 4 folds difference in expression) that possibly relate to osteoblast and osteoclast functions, for further study in this proposal. We also hypothese that Smad7 may be a potential target for the treatment of osteoporosis, and carried out a pilot study administrating Asiatic acid (AA), an activator of Smad7, in overiectomized Smad7ΔE1 (KO) and WT female mice for 2 months. The preliminary results showed that AA treatment could attenuate the osteoporotic bone loss in both the WT and KO group; and we propose to further confirm these findings and study the underlying mechanisms in this proposal. The planned investigations in the current proposal are: (1) To further analyze and confirm the RNA-Seq data of Smad7ΔE1 (KO) and wild type mice; and identify the key Smad7 downstream target genes that may regulate osteogenesis and osteoclastogenesis in vitro and in vivo. (2) To exam the effect of Asiatic acid on bone marrow derived mesenchymal stem cells (BM-MSCs) osteogenic differentiation and bone marrow derived mononuclear cells (BM-MNCs) osteoclastogenesis in vitro. (3) To exam and compare the effects of Asiatic acid, bisphosphate (Alendronate) or combined treatment on bone quality in overiectomized (OVX) mouse model; and to investigate the underlying mechanisms. This study will clarify the novel biological roles of Smad7 in regulating bone quality. The Smad7 may be a new regulator between osteogenesis and osteoclastogenesis; and a potential new therapeutic target for preventing osteoporotic bone loss.

14119115.label: Realisation of objectives
14119115.value: We have completed the projects according to the plans. First, we have investigated the functional roles of two novel genes including Gpnmb and Npy in osteogenesis of MSCs in vitro. Second, we have examined the effect of Asiatic acid on BM-MSCs osteogenic differentiation and BM-MNCs or RAW264.7 cells osteoclastogenesis in vitro. We found Asiatic acid mainly inhibited osteoclastogenesis throught the TGF-β and NF-κb pathways. Third, we have investigated the effects of Asiatic acid, bisphosphate (Alendronate) n bone quality in OVX mouse model and Smad7 partially knock out model. We found that Asiatic acid effectively prevented bone loss and improved bone mechanical properties in OVX mice. We also found that Asiatic acid could partially inhibited bone loss in Smad7 partially knockout mice. More than 9 peer-reviewed papers have been published. In fact, we have produced many exciting new data from this study to support our future investigations.

14119115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119115.value: These findings form the current studies revealed that Asiatic acid may be a potential anti-resorptive agent for postmenopausal osteoporosis. Our data suggested Asiatic acid may be a cost-effective alternative to bisphosphonates for the treatment of postmenopausal osteoporosis. This study also has other implications for the translational potential of bone resorption inhibition, given the fact that clinical situations where decreased bone resorption might be therapeutically useful, such as osteosarcoma. Finally, we have strong pilot data demonstrating the novel effect of Asiatic acid in inhibiting chondrocyte hypertrophy, which form the basis for future research (RGC) proposal to further explore the effect of Asiatic acid in regulating chondrocyte differentiation or cartilage regeneration.

14119115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119115.value: Anti-resorptive agents like bisphosphonates have been widely used for the treatment of postmenopausal osteoporosis. However, their long-term safety and efficacy are still controversial. Our previous study showed that partial loss of Smad7 function leads to enhanced osteoclastogenesis and decreased osteogenesis, leading to rapid bone loss in the Smad7 partially knock out (KO) mice comparing to the wild type mice. As such, our research question is whether Smad7 can be regarded as a therapeutic target of osteoporosis? We hypothesized that Asiatic acid (AA), an activator of Smad7, may be a potential drug for the treatment of osteoporosis by inhibiting osteoclastogenesis. The current study has demonstrated that two novel genes including Gpnmb and Npy are involved in osteogenesis of MSCs in vitro through RNA-seq and further in vitro verification. More importantly, our results showed that Asiatic acid dose-dependently inhibited osteoclastogenesis through TGF-β and NF-κb pathways. We found that Asiatic acid effectively prevented bone loss and improved bone mechanical properties in OVX mice. We also proved that Asiatic acid could partially inhibited bone loss in Smad7 partially knockout mice. This study reveals that Asiatic acid may be a potential anti-resorptive agent for postmenopausal osteoporosis.

14119715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14119715.value: Igf3在斑馬魚性別分化中的功能研究

14119715.label: Project Objectives
14119715.value: To delineate in detail the temporal and spatial expression patterns of Igf3 during zebrafish sex differentiation. To establish the crucial role of Igf3 in zebrafish ovary differentiation. To study the molecular mechanisms of Igf3 action in zebrafish sex differentiation.
rows: To delineate in detail the temporal and spatial expression patterns of Igf3 during zebrafish sex differentiation.
To establish the crucial role of Igf3 in zebrafish ovary differentiation.
To study the molecular mechanisms of Igf3 action in zebrafish sex differentiation.

14119715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119715.value: 動物中普遍存在兩種不同的性別, 但大多數物種的性別如何決定和分化仍不清楚。斑馬魚作為脊椎動物中的重要模式生物之一, 其性別分化機制問題仍懸而未決。到目前為止, 僅鑒定出少數幾個參與魚類性別分化的基因。我們先前的研究發現一種在魚類性腺中特異性表達的新型胰島素類生長因子(Igf3), 已經證明 Igf3 可通過I型 Igf 受體(Igf1r)促進卵母細胞成熟。有趣的是, 我們最近的研究表明, Igf3可能是一個調節斑馬魚性別分化的關鍵因子。該假設基於目前我們得到的三個重要證據: (1) 在成年斑馬魚中, Igf3 mRNA和蛋白的表達在卵巢中遠高於精巢; (2) Igf3 mRNA的表達在性別分化中顯著增加; (3) 敲除Igf3的斑馬魚均發育為可育的雄性。這些初步的結果促使我們擬在本項目中解決以下幾個問題: (1) Igf3在斑馬魚性腺分化期間的時空表達如何? (2) Igf3對於斑馬魚卵巢分化是否扮演一個重要角色? (3) Igf3如何調控斑馬魚的性別分化?

14119715.label: Realisation of objectives
14119715.value: 1. The detailed temporal and spatial expression patterns of Igf3 during zebrafish sex differentiation has been analyzed by real-time PCR and RNA in situ hybridization. 2. Using our established TALENs genome editing platform in zebrafish, we have successfully generated igf3 mutant zebrafish line with the target gene knocked out. The crucial role of Igf3 in zebrafish ovary differentiation has been analyzed using this mutant. 3. The molecular mechanism of Igf3 action on zebrafish sex differentiation was systematically analyzed based on the igf3 mutant.

14119715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14119715.value: Using this grant, we have successfully substantiated our original hypothesis on the importance of Igf3 in regulating sex differentiation in zebrafish. The major findings are: 1. Using quantitative real-time PCR and in situ hybridization, we found the differential expression of igf3 in the critical time-window for sex determination in zebrafish (22 to 26 dpf). The expression level of igf3 appeared to be positively correlated with that of cyp19a1a (mainly expressed in the early ovary) and negatively correlated with that of amh (mainly expressed in the early testis). 2, Using TALENs-mediated gene knockout technique, an igf3 mutant zebrafish was established. We found that disruption of igf3 in zebrafish caused homozygous mutants to develop exclusively as males. Further detailed analysis showed that such phenotype was due to female-to-male sex reversal. 3. We demonstrated that the sex reversal is likely due to decreased germ cell numbers and cell proliferation by inhibiting PI3K/Akt pathway in early ovaries of igf3 mutants. Also, Igf3 may act as a downstream mediator of estrogen signaling proven by the evidence from in vitro treatment assay, study of the cyp19a1a mutant zebrafish and E2 rescue experiment.

14119715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119715.value: Our studies have led us to reveal other interesting findings as described below. First, this gonad-specific growth factor might act as a key factor in other aspects of ovarian development. We found Igf3 is also involved in regulating ovulation in zebrafish. These findings have been successfully published as a research paper on Biology of Reproduction, 2018, 99(6), 1235–1243. Second, inspired by the recent data on Igf3, we hypothesize that Igf3 is involved in ovarian follicle activation by mediating the action of follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) in zebrafish. This hypothesis is based on three lines of evidence: (1) The ovarian phenotype (arrest at the PG stage) of igf3 mutant is similar to fshr mutant zebrafish. (2) igf3 expression is significantly decreased in ovary of fshr mutant zebrafish at 45 dpf. (3) igf3 expression can be up-regulated by FSH signaling in zebrafish testis (demonstrated by Nóbrega et al., Endocrinology, 156 (10), 3804–3817). These have led us to ask the following questions: (1) Whether FSH regulates Igf3 expression in zebrafish ovary? (2) How does FSH regulate Igf3 expression in zebrafish? and (3) Whether Igf3 is important for mediating the role of FSH in early follicle activation? This will constitute another prong of our future research efforts. Third, an effective approach to achieve spatial and temporal gene knockout in zebrafish has not been well established. Therefore, we have developed a new approach, namely bacterial artificial chromosome-rescue-based knockout (BACK), to achieve conditional gene knockout in zebrafish using the Cre/loxP system. We established that Cre/loxP-mediated tissue-/stage- specific gene knockout could be achieved using this BACK strategy. These findings have been published as a research paper on Cellular and Molecular Life Sciences, 74(13), 2503-2511. We will use this newly established method to investigate the function of igf3 gene in the specific stage of ovarian development.

14119715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119715.value: A fundamental question in biology is how sex differentiation occurs. This project focus on the crucial functions and molecular mechanisms of Igf3 in controlling fish sex differentiation. By establishing an igf3 mutant zebrafish, we demonstrated that Igf3 is essential for ovary differentiation in zebrafish. We further found that Igf3 regulates sex differentiation by contolling the germ cell numbers through PI3K/Akt pathway and act as a downstream mediator of estrogen signaling. The information obtained from this study provide a better understanding on vertebrate sex differentiation, through experiments that would otherwise be difficult to conduct in mammals. Furthermore, the present study on zebrafish have potential economic value as this fish species belongs to the family of Cyprinidae representing several important economic fish species commonly cultured around the world.

14119815.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14119815.value: 香港「籠屋」居民社會生態及健康風險的研究

14119815.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14119815.value: Prof Chung, Roger Yat-Nork Prof Goggins, William Prof Tsang, Katrina Wai-kay Dr WONG, Ka Man Carmen Prof WONG, Samuel Yeung-shan

14119815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119815.value: The aim of this study is to understand how the physical and social environments of 'bedspace' dwellings in Hong Kong adversely affect the residents’ health and to determine which factors of individual and collective social capital facilitate the utilization of healthcare and social services in 'bedspace' communities. The 'bedspace,' also known as a 'cage' or 'coffin' dwelling, is one of the unique, urban features of the deprived communities of Hong Kong. The 'cage' is usually described as a tiny cubicle with walls made of steel wire mesh and a floor of wooden planks. ('Coffin' dwellings are very similar to 'cages' except the 'coffin' walls are made of rigid boards instead of wire mesh.) The area of the floor measures 20 square feet. Approximately 12 to 18 cages are piled on top of each other in an area measuring 650-700 square feet. 'Bedspace' dwellings are generally located in historically under-developed and heavily populated urban areas. They lack proper sanitation, health services, security and other infrastructure. The residents, most of whom are impoverished workers, the elderly and migrants, are disproportionately exposed to multiple risk factors resulting in a high prevalence of physical and mental health problems. The proposed innovative, interdisciplinary study will identify variability in types, contexts and patterns of 'bedspace' dwellings, and demonstrate the relationship between the social, environmental and behavioural dimensions of risk and its impact on health outcomes. Based on a social-ecological urban health model, the study will integrate qualitative and quantitative methods to investigate the level of exposure to health risks in the 'bedspace' communities. We will conduct formative, ethnographic research in four districts of Hong Kong in order to investigate the physical and social environments of 'cage' life. We will also conduct a cross-sectional survey, using social networks domains, among 400 'bedspace' residents to examine the interrelationship of individual and collective social capital in the utilization of the health services. By extending the research focus beyond the domain of communicable or non-communicable diseases, the results of this study will not only document the detrimental effect of 'cage' dwelling on health but also identify the protective factors of social capital for health improvement. The study outcomes will lead to the development of appropriate interventions and preventive measures in the communities as well as the promotion of better policies for the improvement of healthcare services in the deprived communities.

14120015.label: Realisation of objectives
14120015.value: The goal of our study is to investigate the involvement of CCR6 in mediating progesterone-induced sperm function. We sought to achieve the goal with three specific aims: 1) to examine the involvement of CCR6 receptor in mediating progesterone-induced, CatSper-dependent Ca2+ influx and sperm functions; 2) to investigate the mechanism underlying the modulation of CatSper channel activity by CCR6 receptor; and 3) to examine the involvement of CCR6/CatSper complex in male infertility. In Aim 1, we have first confirmed the induction of Ca2+ mobilization by progesterone in human sperm. We also showed that blockage of the CCR6 receptor by anti-CCR6 neutralizing antibody treatment or inhibition of the CatSper channel activity by mibefradil treatment each significantly inhibit the progesterone-induced Ca2+ mobilization. These results suggested that CCR6 receptor and CatSper channel are both required for progesterone-induced Ca2+ mobilization in human sperm. Since progesterone has been implicated in sperm hyperactivation and acrosome reaction, we have further set out to examine the involvement of CCR6/CatSper in these sperm functions. Our results showed that progesterone induces a ~2-fold increase in the percentage of sperm with hyperactivated motility. This effect was significantly inhibited by either CCR6 neutralizing antibody or mibefradil treatment and completely abolished by simultaneous treatment of both. Besides, progesterone induces a ~3-fold increase in the acrosome reaction. Similarly, the progesterone-induced acrosome reaction was significantly inhibited by blocking the CCR6 receptor or inhibiting the CatSper channel (Detailed results have been published in Oncotarget, Diao, et al. 2017, see attached paper). Together, these results suggested that CCR6 receptor and CatSper channel are both required for progesterone-induced sperm functions by mediating Ca2+ mobilization. In Aim 2, we have investigated the mechanism underlying the modulation of CatSper channel activity by the CCR6 receptor. We reasoned that CCR6 modulates CatSper channel activity by protein-protein interaction. Using co-immunofluorescence staining, we first showed that the core subunits of CatSper channel, CatSper1, co-localized with CCR6 in the mid-piece and tail region of sperm. The potential interactions between CatSper1 and CCR6 were further supported by the proximity ligation assay result where signals were observed in the mid-piece and tail regions. Moreover, the direct protein interaction on sperm was confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation assay. These results indicate that CCR6 forms a receptor/channel complex with CatSper channel in human sperm. We have further examined the regulation of progesterone-induced CatSper channel activity (ICatSper) by CCR6 receptor using sperm patch-clamp technique. The results showed that CCR6 antibody partially, yet significantly inhibited progesterone-induced ICatSper but not basal CatSper current (Detailed results have been published in Oncotarget, Diao, et al. 2017, see attached paper), suggesting that CCR6 is required for the progesterone-induced CatSper channel activation. In Aim 3, we went on to investigate the involvement of CCR6/CatSper complex in male infertility. We have collected sperm samples from a cohort of asthenozoospermia patients and examined the expression of CCR6 and CatSper1 by Western blot. The results demonstrated a lowered expression of both CCR6 and CatSper1 in sperm obtained from asthenozoospermia patients compared to those obtained from normal men. Furthermore, we compared the progesterone-induced hyperactivation and acrosome reaction in sperm samples collected from normal and asthenozoospermia patients. Our results showed that sperm functions were significantly impaired in patients’ spermatozoa compared to spermatozoa obtained from normal men (Detailed results have been published in Oncotarget, Diao, et al. 2017, see attached paper). These results confirmed the vital roles of the CCR6 and CatSper in sperm functions. Taken together, our results indicate that CCR6 interacts with CatSper channel and the receptor/channel complex mediates progesterone-induced Ca2+ mobilization and sperm functions required for male fertility. Since the CatSper channel is also known to be involved in other motility-related sperm functions such as chemotaxis, we have extended our study to examine the involvement of CCR6/CatSper complex in sperm chemotaxis. Our recent study has identified DEFB119 as a physiological chemoattractant that mediates sperm chemotaxis in vivo. Intriguingly, our results also showed that blocking CCR6 receptor or inhibiting CatSper channel blunt DEFB119-induced sperm chemotaxis in human sperm (Manuscript submitted to Science Translational Medicine). Together, our results suggest that the CCR6-CatSper receptor/channel complex may be involved in multiple sperm functions elicited by different physiological inducers.

14120015.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120015.value: Our study revealed the involvement of CCR6 receptor in mediating the progesterone-induced, CatSper-dependent calcium mobilization and sperm function in human sperm. We have shown that blocking CCR6 receptor blunt progesterone-induced calcium influx. The inhibitory effect was similar to that of CatSper channel inhibition. We have also demonstrated that CCR6 and CatSper are both required for progesterone-induced hyperactivation and acrosome reaction. CCR6 receptor and CatSper forms a receptor/channel complex and this complex mediates the progesterone-induced CatSper channel activation (the results have been published in Oncotarget, Diao, et al. 2017, see attached paper). The involvement of CCR6 receptor and CatSper channel in sperm functions has led us to identify the lowered level of this receptor/channel complex in infertile men that demonstrated lowered sperm motility, i.e. asthenozoospermia. Since the CCR6/CatSper complex is involved in hyperactivation and acrosome reaction, we have also uncovered the defects in these two sperm functions in asthenozoospermia patients. Besides the sperm functions induced by progesterone, we have extended our study and showed that the CCR6/CatSper complex is also involved in sperm chemotaxis elicited by physiological chemoattractant DEFB119 (manuscript submitted to Science Translational Medicine). Together, our study has uncovered the involvement of CCR6/CatSper receptor-channel complex in sperm functions induced by not only progesterone but also other physiological inducers. Our study may shed light on the diagnosis of male infertility by examining the expression and formation of the CCR6/CatSper complex.

14120015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120015.value: CatSper is a principal calcium channel on sperm required for various sperm functions. The presently discovered interaction between CCR6 receptor and CatSper channel suggest that CCR6 receptor may possess multiple ligands other than progesterone. The receptor/channel complex may mediate different sperm functions during the sperm transit through the male and female reproductive tract. Our results have identified another ligand DEFB119 that elicits CCR6/CatSper-dependent calcium mobilization and takes part in sperm chemotaxis in the female reproductive tract. We have started a follow-up study to investigate the mechanism(s) underlying the effects of different ligands in differential sperm functions. The discovery that the level of CCR6 and CatSper1 are lowered in asthenozoospermia patients together with the defective hyperactivation and acrosome reaction in these patients have suggested the involvement of CCR6/CatSper complex in other forms of infertility that stemmed from the defective multiple sperm functions. We are currently exploring the association of this complex and the other ligand DEFB119 in idiopathic infertility.

14120015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120015.value: Progesterone is a pivotal hormone secreted by the female reproductive tract. Recent studies have suggested the involvement of the CatSper channel in mediating the effect of progesterone in sperm. However, the underlying mechanism remains poorly understood. In this study, we have shown that CCR6 receptor interacts and forms a complex with the CatSper channel. The CCR6 receptor is required in mediating the effect of progesterone by activating the CatSper channel. This, in turn, leads to the influx of calcium ion into sperm that elicits hyperactivation and acrosome reaction, both are sperm functions essential for fertilization. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that lowered level of CCR6 and CatSper channel proteins are associated with defective hyperactivation and acrosome reaction in infertile men. Intriguingly, the CCR6/CatSper complex is also involved in mediating the effect of other ligands, e.g. DEFB119 in sperm chemotaxis. Taken together, our results reveal the essential role of CCR6/CatSper receptor-channel complex in mediating sperm functions induced by progesterone and other physiological ligands. Defects of which may underlie various forms of male infertility stemmed from defective sperm functions.

14120215.label: Realisation of objectives
14120215.value: This project explores the phenotypic heterogeneity of Chinese patients with young-onset diabetes (YOD) and assesses the impact of C-peptide levels and anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) autoantibody positivity on risk of developing diabetes-related complications and mortality. Glycaemic response to insulin and whether time to insulin initiation affects clinical outcome in patient subgroups categorised using these biomarkers and body mass index (BMI) are also explored. We proposed to measure C-peptide levels and anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) autoantibodies in stored serum of approximately 1,500 patients with young-onset (defined as age of diabetes diagnosis <40 years) non-type 1 diabetes who were recruited into the Hong Kong Diabetes Registry between 1995 and 2007 and followed longitudinally for clinical outcome and mortality until 2014. To address Objective 1, we have extracted serum from 1,413 patients from this enrolment period, and from additional 91 patients recruited between 2008 and 2012. In total, fasted C-peptide levels and anti-GAD autoantibodies are measured in 1,504 patients, who make up the analysable cohort for this work. C-peptide is measured by Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent Assay using commercial Mercodia C-peptide ELISA kit, and anti-GAD autoantibodies are measured using the RSR GAD autoantibody ELISA kit. Using C-peptide <200pmol/L as an arbitrary cut-off, 49% of the cohort (mean age 43 years, median disease duration 7.0 years) have low C-peptide. Although C-peptide level as a surrogate of pancreatic beta-cell function, may fall with progression of diabetes, we do not observe a correlation of C-peptide with disease duration, suggesting that many patients with YOD have indeed poor beta-cell reserve. Anti-GAD autoantibodies are detected in 8% of the cohort and this group of patients probably have autoimmune diabetes sharing similar disease aetiology to type 1 diabetes. Notably the prevalence of anti-GAD positivity is highest at 17% in normal weight patients with low C-peptide, but even among their overweight counterparts, up to 6% have detectable autoantibodies. Indeed, over half of patients with either low C-peptide or anti-GAD autoantibodies are overweight or obese, suggesting that body weight may not be a reliable predictor of C-peptide levels or autoimmune diabetes.In a related work which is published in Diabetic Medicine, we identify a high rate of conversion to diabetes in people with at least one first degree relatives with YOD, as compare with those with family history of late-onset diabetes or no family history. In particular, we observe impaired beta-cell function even before the onset of diabetes in this group of individuals, which underscore the importance of beta-cell function in patients of YOD and downstream treatment implications. To address Objective 2, we firstly compare the baseline clinical characteristics of patient subgroups stratified by C-peptide levels, anti-GAD positivity and BMI. Next, we estimate the incidence of clinical outcomes including cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, end-stage renal disease (ESRD), severe hypoglycaemia and all-cause mortality in these subgroups. Finally Cox proportionate regression analysis is performed to derive hazard ratios of C-peptide, anti-GAD positivity and BMI for clinical outcomes, adjusted for clinical variables including demographics, disease duration, year of assessment, cardio-metabolic risk factors, renal parameters, comorbidities and medications. The analysis is fully completed. Part of the results generated from these analyses were presented as a poster at the International Diabetes Federation World Diabetes Congress in December 2017, where we showed the possible predictive value of low C-peptide for higher risks of cardiovascular disease and mortality. An abstract on the progression of diabetes-related complications in patients with or without anti-GAD autoantibodies has been accepted for presentation at the upcoming 78th Scientific Sessions, American Diabetes Association, in June 2018, and the abstract will be published in a supplement to the journal Diabetes. Here, we confirm that patients with autoimmune diabetes, who have fewer features of the metabolic syndrome but worse glycaemic control, are less likely to develop cardiovascular disease but more likely to experience severe hypoglycaemia than patients without anti-GAD autoantibodies. A related paper is under preparation, which further compares clinical outcomes to patients with classical type 1 diabetes. For Objective 3, we firstly determine prevalent and incident insulin use in patient subgroups stratified by C-peptide, anti-GAD positivity and BMI. Next, we assess changes in HbA1c before and after insulin initiation by patient subgroups. Lastly, we use Cox regression to examine the interaction of time to insulin with C-peptide, anti-GAD positivity and BMI on incident clinical events. The analysis is fully completed and the paper is under preparation. From the analysis, we confirm the notion that patients with poor beta-cell reserve as evidenced by low C-peptide or low BMI, and those with autoimmune diabetes, have superior glycaemic response to insulin therapy. From the Cox regression analysis, we are not able to detect significant interaction between time to insulin initiation and C-peptide or BMI for risks of new clinical events. However, we identify an interaction between time to insulin and anti-GAD positivity for incident ESRD. We are therefore able to show that patients who harbour anti-GAD autoantibodies are more likely to have ESRD if insulin therapy is delayed. These results are novel and point to the utility of these biomarkers in prediction of glycaemic response to therapy.

14120215.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120215.value: - Of 1,504 patients (mean age at enrolment 43 years, mean age of diagnosis 33 years), 49% have low fasted C-peptide, 8% are positive for anti-GAD autoantibodies, and 71% are overweight/obese. - Patients with low C-peptide at baseline do not differ from their counterparts with high C-peptide with respect to disease duration, but they are thinner and have fewer cardio-metabolic risk factors. Low versus high C-peptide is associated with greater hazard of severe hypoglycaemia, which is amplified in patients with low BMI. - High C-peptide, which may infer either preserved insulin secretion, insulin resistance or both, is linked to higher prevalence of cardio-metabolic risk factors. However, high BMI but not high C-peptide is associated with greater hazard of cardiovascular disease (CVD). - Patients with detectable anti-GAD autoantibodies have fewer cardio-metabolic risk factors but worse glycaemic control, compare to patients without autoantibodies. This group with autoimmune diabetes also have lower hazard of CVD and greater hazard of severe hypoglycaemia, whereas the risks of renal complications and mortality are similar to the group without autoantibodies. - Upon further stratification by C-peptide levels, patients with detectable anti-GAD autoantibodies and low C-peptide have the worst glycaemic control. Up to 47% are prescribed insulin therapy at baseline and estimated mean time to insulin initiation is 1 year. This group has the lowest hazard of CVD and highest hazard of severe hypoglycaemia even when adjusted for insulin use. - Glycaemic response to insulin therapy differs by C-peptide levels, anti-GAD positivity and BMI. Patients with low C-peptide, positive autoantibodies or low BMI achieve significantly greater HbA1c reduction following insulin initiation than their respective counterparts. Whilst insulin use either at baseline or during follow-up is more frequent in patients with anti-GAD autoantibodies, prevalent or incident insulin use do not differ by body weight and patients with low C-peptide in fact have lower usage of insulin, suggesting inappropriate glycaemic management in some patients. - No interaction between C-peptide levels, BMI and time to insulin is detected for any of the analysed clinical outcomes. We confirm a positive interaction between anti-GAD positivity and baseline insulin use with severe hypoglycaemia indicating that the greater hazard of hypoglycaemia conferred by insulin therapy is increased when autoantibodies are present. We further detect a positive interaction between anti-GAD positivity and time to insulin with ESRD, which suggests that patients with anti-GAD autoantibodies who have delayed insulin initiation have heightened risk of incident ESRD.

14120215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120215.value: Our findings suggest that low C-peptide as a marker for poor insulin reserve, high BMI as a marker of insulin resistance and downstream metabolic syndrome, and positive anti-GAD autoantibodies as a signature of autoimmune diabetes, are predictive of cardiovascular disease and severe hypoglycaemia. Furthermore, we detect significant differential in glycaemic response to insulin therapy by these clinical and biological markers. The results from this study call for clinical trials to examine the utility of these markers, which are pointers to underlying pathophysiology, in guiding treatment choices to improve clinical outcome. Current diabetes treatment recommendations do not provide sufficient guidance on the optimal choices of glucose lowering drugs in patients with non-type 1 diabetes. Pending more concrete evidence on the clinical use of genetic markers in directing therapeutic options, algorithms incorporating C-peptide, autoantibodies and BMI may path the way to personalised medicine in diabetes.

14120215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120215.value: Up to one fifth of people with diabetes are diagnosed young before the age of 40 years. Young patients have a very high lifetime risk of progressing to disabling complications from diabetes such as cardiovascular disease and kidney disease as they are exposed to harmful effects of diabetes from an earlier age. Young patients differ from their older counterparts in that the underlying causes of diabetes are diverse and sometimes difficult to establish. The mechanisms which contribute to diabetes may also determine patients' response to therapy and their overall prognosis. In this project, we found that low levels of C-peptide, which is a marker of pancreatic function and insulin reserve, and anti-GAD autoantibodies, which signify an autoimmune basis to diabetes development, predicts severe hypoglycaemia (low blood glucose), whereas high body weight predicts a greater likelihood of cardiovascular events. Furthermore, patients with low C-peptide and positive autoantibodies have better response to insulin therapy. Our results suggest that these simple clinical and biomarkers may be helpful to project outcome and guide management. We propose that algorithms incorporating these markers may be of value in personalising treatment in these high risk patients.

14120915.value: 本申請將研究涉及一種抗腫瘤免疫的小GTP-結合蛋白。腫瘤微環境對腫瘤進展中起關鍵作用。它是由免疫細胞，內皮細胞和間質細胞的複雜組合物的。在腫瘤生長期，腫瘤細胞產生趨化因子和細胞因子賦予一個免疫環境。此外，間質細胞會響應瘤細胞發出的信號會分泌刺激新血管的形成的蛋白質，促進腫瘤擴散。管理在腫瘤微環境不同的細胞類型之間的複雜機制尚未完全確定。 我們發現在RAS基因家族的小GTP-結合蛋白，R-Ras，能在腫瘤微環境的多種細胞類型有不同的作用。 R-Ras能參與細胞粘附和細胞形狀的功能。 它在血管完整性和樹突狀細胞功能很重要的功能。在缺乏R-Ras的小鼠，腫瘤可生長到更大的程度。此外，缺乏R-Ras的小鼠具有小的淋巴結和在T細胞中有多個缺陷。主要理論是，R-Ras 對血管完整性和抗腫瘤免疫有重要的功能。了解 R-Ras基因調控與維持抗腫瘤微環境是這研究項目的長遠目標。 這個項目有三大目標。首先，R-Ras信號通路的表達和激活將在小鼠腫瘤模型和人腫瘤樣品進行評估。第二，使用缺乏R-Ras的小鼠，我們將確定 R-Ras在哪一種免疫細胞能抑制腫瘤的生長。第三，負責介導的R-Ras抗腫瘤的詳細機制將被劃定。此外，我們將嘗試調節該機制，以實現持久的抗腫瘤微環境。 該提案的主要影響是雙重的。從基礎科學的角度來看，它會加深我們對腫瘤微環境的調控機制的理解。從治療的角度來看，這個項目將引導一個治療腫瘤微環境的新模式。

14120915.label: Realisation of objectives
14120915.value: In Objective 1, we have completed the proposed studies investigating the role of R-Ras in both spontaneous mammary tumor model and melanoma models. We encountered two major problems. First, the sensitivity of detecting R-Ras and its activation states from limited immune cells posed a considerable hurdle. We have tried to test the feasibility of four detection methods – qPCR, intracellular staining, immunocytochemistry, and Western blotting analysis. Overall the sensitivity is very low. Therefore, we focused on the measuring the functional consequences of the loss of R-Ras on the tumor growth and tumor microenvironment instead. The second challenge was that subsequent to the importation of the R-Ras mouse line from a previous hosting institution to CUHK, we noticed that some of our mice had developed malocclusion. This inevitably affected food intake and therefore decrease in body weights. This imposed considerable delay to all objectives as the animal facility had to selectively crossed our knockout mice using only animals without these deformities. Despite of these challenges, we have initially investigated the diversity of immune cells in the MMTV-PyMT mammary tumor model by flow cytometry. We then conducted two independent crosses between the MMTV-PyMT and R-Ras knockout mice. Spontaneous tumors were allowed to form over a period of 4 months and significant differences in tumor mass were observed in transgenic mice in R-Ras knockout background. We further investigated the three major populations of immune cells – CD3+ T-cells, CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, and FOXP3+ regulatory T cells (Treg) by immunohistochemical analysis (IHC). We have also completed the analysis of the melanoma model by testing the ability of a melanoma cell lines, B16/F10 in inducing tumors in R-Ras wild-type (WT) and knockout (KO) mice. IHC were then carried out to characterize the infiltrating immune cells including CD3+ T-cells, CD8+ cytotoxic T cells, and FOXP3+ regulatory T cells (Treg). In objective 2, we intended to address two questions. First, are there any differences between WT and R-Ras KO immune cells in the tumor microenvironment and if so, would the lack of R-Ras expression in cells such as Dendritic cells be required for tumor suppression? For this, we proposed to use the B16-OVA melanoma which expressed the chicken ovalbumin protein as a potent “tumor antigen”. We have completed this objective by inducing tumors in R-Ras WT and KO mice. Flow cytometry analysis was carried out to measure the abundance of a host of immune cells and significant changes were observed. Next, to investigate the role of R-Ras in Dendritic cells (DC), we carried out tumor vaccination experiment as proposed in the original application. We completed this set of experiment. We have tested for feasibility and optimized vaccination conditions by adopting a two-week vaccination protocol by isolating bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDC) and differentiated it with GM-CSF. Matured BM-DCs were loaded with OVA 257-264 peptide and immunized naïve C57BL/6 mice. These mice were challenged with B16-OVA tumors vaccinated with either BMDC from R-Ras WT or KO mice. The ability of vaccination in suppressing tumor formation was examined. The major drawback of this objective is that we did not observe a major difference between R-Ras WT and KO BMDC in mediating anti-tumor activity. We speculate that either R-Ras was not involved in mediating the presentation of OVA antigen to T cells, or OVA evokes a strong antigenic response that masks the subtle differences that might have dependent on R-Ras expression. For example, R-Ras knockout BMDC may have only moderate defects in the intracellular transport of OVA peptides to the cell surface. This negative data preclude the need for the conducting the extensive crosses between R-Ras knockout mice to OT1 transgenic mice in order to reduce animal usage. In objective 3, we proposed to investigate the mechanism in how R-Ras in T cells can modulate the tumor microenvironment. Based on the data generated in objective 2, we decided to focus on the last remaining experiment in this objective, which was to investigate the role of R-Ras in Treg in tumor microenvironment. An initial analysis of the Treg population in R-Ras WT, HET, and KO mice was conducted using a cohort of littermates. Spleen and peripheral blood were isolated and the percentage of FOXP3+ cells were analyzed. We have also conducted functional experiments to test the hypothesis that R-Ras may modulate Treg function and thus altering the immunosuppressive environment in selected tumor model. For this, we purchased the FOXP3-DTR mice with the initial plan of depleting FOXP3+ Tregs by injecting mice with diphtheria toxin (DT) for two weeks. We faced yet another 4 months of delay due to the back order of DT from a sole vendor in the United States. Despite of this, we put in considerable efforts in titrating a concentration of the DT without inducing adverse effect on the animals. A dosing schedule of 6.5 ng/g once every three days was selected. Under this condition, we observed considerable enlargement of the spleen following two weeks of DT treatment although all animal were viable. This is unexpected as mouse strain is not known to harbor the receptor for DT. Flow cytometric analysis did not reveal any depletion of depletion of FOXP3+ T cells. We proceeded with the origin proposed plan of isolating CD4+CD25+ Tregs from R-Ras WT and KO cells, and adopted transfer to DT-treated FOXP3-DTR mice. Injection of B16/F10 tumors in these mice did not result in major differences in both tumor mass and volume. Since the phenomenon of splenomegaly following DT exposure in mice is not well-documented. Future plans to repeat this study would need to use alternative strategy such as using antibodies to deplete Treg.

14120915.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120915.value: In objective 1, for the MMTV-PyMT model, there was a significant reduction in tumor mass when compared WT with HET or KO (Fig. 4A&B). This data argue a pro-tumorigenic role of R-Ras in mammary carcinogenesis. By immunohistochemical analysis (IHC), the level of infiltrating CD3+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, and FOXP3+ Treg were analyzed. For the melanoma model, B16/F10 cells were injected in R-Ras WT and KO mice. Overall, there was a slight increase in tumor volume (Fig. 7B). IHC analysis was also conducted to measure the relative proportion of CD3+, CD8+ and FOXP3+ T cells. In both the mammary tumor and melanoma models, we observed increased in CD8+ T cells in RRas knockout genetic background (Fig. 5&7). In objective 2, B16-OVA cells were injected into either WT or KO mice to generate a range of tumors with variable sizes. Early stage tumors of size <0.02 cm^3 and more advanced tumor of size >0.02 cm^3 were separately analyzed. Characterization of infiltrating immune cell populations revealed significant reduction in the % of myeloid Dendritic cells (DCs) in R-Ras KO mice in small size tumors. Furthermore, in larger tumors, the number of CD3+/CD4+ T cells, and myeloid DCs was significantly increased (Fig. 1&2). Next, dendritic cell vaccination experiments were conducted by comparing the growth of B16/F10-OVA tumors in mice vaccinated with either WT or KO bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDC) loaded with ovalbumin. B16-OVA cells were injected into all mice but in both cases, tumors failed to propagate even after one month (Fig. 3). We conclude that R-Ras may not be required for dendritic cells in mediating antigen presentation to T cells in the B16-OVA melanoma model. In objective 3, an initial analysis of the Treg population in R-Ras WT, HET, and KO mice revealed slight increase in FOXP3 population in KO mouse in the spleen but not in the blood. CD4+CD25+ population appeared to be increased in the spleen of KO mouse by 2-fold. We also analyzed the fraction of FOXP3+CD4+ and FOXP3+CD25+ populations but did not uncover differences. FOXP3-DTR mice were depleted of Tregs with diphtheria toxin (DT). Treg from R-Ras WT and KO mice were infused into DT-treated mice and then B16/F10 tumor cells were injected. Tumor induction was monitored for 10 days. This study was cofounded by the appearance of splenomegaly in DT treated mice (Fig 6). A more suitable model is required to pursue the goal of this objective.

14120915.value: Objective 1: We found that the global loss of R-Ras suppresses mammary carcinogenesis. Identifying the critical cell types involved would require the future development of conditional knockout R-Ras mouse lines. In addition, R-Ras plays a critical role in angiogenesis. Whether R-Ras plays a role in both spontaneous or orthotopic tumor model systems needs to be addressed. The role of R-Ras in CD8+ tumor homing capacity should be an exciting future research direction. Objective 2: The failure of R-Ras knockout in BMDC to show any differences than wild-type needs to be investigated further. Additional tumor cell lines lacking a strong antigen needs to be tested. For example, B16-F10 tumor cell line should be tested instead. In this case, BMDC will be pulsed with total tumor lysates. Alternatively, as suggested for objective 1 above, R-Ras can be knockout specifically in DC. Objective 3: The role of R-Ras in tumor-associated Treg is not fully elucidated. The use of FOXP3-DTR mice may not be suitable for long-term assays. The use of neutralizing antibodies to eliminate Tregs may be an alternative. Ex vivo expanding of Tregs isolated from R-Ras WT and KO mice to study its role in regulating T cell functions.

14120915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120915.value: A tumor requires the help from many cell types for its growth and survival. Immune cell types play a critical role in either supporting or destroying the tumor cells. This project aims to test the hypothesis that a single gene, R-Ras, may modulate the immune cell functions and in turn alter the development of tumor progression and dissemination. We found that R-Ras has a protumorigenic effect on mammary tumor growth in general, while its effect on melanoma growth is less drastic. This effect can be explained by the changes in number and composition of immune cells in the tumors.

14121315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14121315.value: Myoglobin is a classical heme protein known for its role in the uptake and storage of dioxygen in muscle tissues. Recent studies have shown that the lentivirus vector-mediated overexpression of myoglobin in A549 lung carcinoma cells suppresses transduction of hypoxia pathways important for cancer survival in vitro, and slows cancer tumour growth in xenograph mouse models. In this proposal, we will study the use of a novel protein delivery system to deliver exogenous myoglobin to A549 cells. We will evaluate whether our protein delivery system can delivery sufficient levels of myoglobin to A549 cells to induce similar anticancer effects. We will also evaluate the impact of this exogenously delivered Cry3Aa-myoglobin on the radiosensitivity of A549 cells and tumour in the presence of ionizing radiation. 癌症是由異常細胞的持續生長導致的，它可能威脅到任何年齡段人群的健康。世界上1/8的死亡是由於癌症，而在香港地區，癌症也是導致死亡的主要因素。癌症的常規治療方法包括化學療法、放射療法、手術療法和免疫療法。由於癌症的多樣性，這些療法經常被綜合運用到癌症治療當中，以期控制和殺死癌細胞。儘管近些年我們已經在癌症治療方面取得了諸多進展，持續的高死亡率迫切地要求一些新的突破，特別是在常規的癌症治療方法失效，並且沒有其他的有效手段可供選擇的時候。 我們知道腫瘤的微環境有別于正常的組織。實體瘤的低氧環境被認為是促進基因組不穩定性、異常基因表達和腫瘤轉移的主要因素之一。低氧氣濃度也被認為是導致腫瘤對放療和抗腫瘤化療耐受的主要原因。克服這種耐受的一個方法就是提高癌症細胞中的氧氣濃度。這會抑制對於腫瘤擴散和轉移非常重要的低氧通路，從而提高腫瘤細胞對電離輻射的敏感性，增強放射導致的細胞凋亡。 在這個研究計劃之中，我們想研究是否可以把經典的血紅素蛋白——肌紅蛋白（Myoglobin）用於癌症治療當中。我們計劃探索一種可以把肌紅蛋白運送進癌細胞的策略，以期研究是否外源性的肌紅蛋白遞入可以增加氧氣濃度並且抑制腫瘤生長。顯然，這樣的方法取得的結果將會與先前在癌症細胞中過表達肌紅蛋白的研究結果一致。我們還計劃研究肌紅蛋白的攝入是否可以增強癌細胞的放射敏感性。如果這些研究都成功的話，這些工作將為一項新的可廣泛運用的治療方法提供基礎。

14121315.label: Realisation of objectives
14121315.value: Each of the key aims was tested, and the outcome led to the first demonstration that delivery of myoglobin to hypoxic cancer cells can be used to enhance their radiosensitivity to radiation. The specific outcomes of the various aims are listed below. Specific Aim 1: To enhance the uptake of Cry3Aa-myoglobin crystals by A549 lung carcinoma cells. This aim is fully completed. We demonstrated that genetic fusion of an A549 targeting peptide to Cry3AD1-myoglobin particles could be used to enhance their uptake into A549 cancer cells. Specific Aim 2: To assess the ability of Cry3Aa-myoglobin crystals to suppress hypoxic responses in A549 lung carcinoma cells. This aim is completed. Though we tried many times, we were unable to observe the changes in HIF-1alpha levels under hypoxia by Western blotting. We were able to confirm, however, that delivery of Cry3AD1-myoglobin particles to A549 cells did affect the level of hypoxia in the cell using a Hypoxia Green Reagent (Thermo Fisher), which releases rhodamine as a result to decreased oxygen levels. These data suggest that myoglobin delivery as Cry3AD1-myoglobin particles can alter the levels of oxygen in the cell. Specific Aim 3: To evaluate whether Cry3Aa-myoglobin crystals can slow A549 lung carcinoma tumor growth in a mouse model. For this aim an endpoint was reached. We prepared A549 tumor xenograph mice and successfully produced tumors. We explored two methods of injection in the mice to treat the tumor, both of which were unsuccessful. We found that tail vein injection of the Cry3AD1-fusion protein crystals resulted in accumulation of the crystals in the liver. Direct injection of Cry3AD1-myoglobin crystals proved difficult since the tumor was unusual hard and so we found that we could not get good injection of crystal into it. Around the same time a manuscript showing that the anti-tumor activity of myoglobin results from its ability to induce mitochodrial fusion, and not by suppressing hypoxic responses. Braganza, A., Quesnelle, K., Bickta, J., Reyes, C., Wang, Y., Jessup, M., Croix, C.S., Arlotti, J., Singh, S.V., and Shiva, S. (2019). Myoglobin induces mitochondrial fusion, thereby inhibiting breast cancer cell proliferation. J. Biol. Chem. 294, 7269–7282. Given our difficulties in delivering our Cry3AD1 myoglobin particles to the tumor, and the fact our particles were not designed to release free myoglobin as needed to promote mitochondrial fusion, we decided to focus on Specific Aim 4 where the increased oxygen levels could make a difference. Specific Aim 4: To explore the use of Cry3Aa-myoglobin crystals to enhance radiation therapy of A549 lung carcinoma cells. This aim is fully completed. With significant effort, we were able to find a suitable colony forming assay to reproducibly monitor the impact of radiation on A549 cells treated with our Cry3AD1-myoglobin particles. Using this assay, we were able to show that myoglobin delivery does serve as a viable approach to enhance the effectiveness of radiation therapy for the treatment of cancer.

14121315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14121315.value: The major findings of the work were reported in the iScience paper published in 2020 and reported in Part C. These findings are: (1) That the N-terminal domain of Cry3Aa can be used to produce Cry3Aa-fusion protein particles that can be delivered to cells. (2) Cry3Aa-fusion particles can be targeted to specific cells by incorporation of C-terminal cell targeting peptides, Here, incorporation a peptide known to bind A549 cells was shown to dramatically increase uptake of Cry3AD1-myoglobin particles by A549 cells. (3) Uptake of Cry3AD1-myoglobin particles by A549 cells under hypoxic conditions can significantly alter the oxygen levels in the cell. (4) Treatment of A549 cells under hypoxic conditions with Cry3AD1-myoglobin particles dramatically increases the effectiveness of radiation therapy.

14121315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14121315.value: The next step in the current study would be to develop a A549 cancer model in the liver, and testing the ability of intravenous injection of Cry3AD1-myoglobin particles followed by radiation therapy to improve the effectiveness of radiation therapy to treat the A549-based liver cancer. Longer term, alternative strategies to specifically deliver myoglobin to cancer cells could be explored. We have recently develop a Cry3Aa-based approach to deliver proteins to cells with high levels of endosomal escape, and the use of this technology to achieve myoglobin delivery could be attempted.

14121315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14121315.value: Cancer is one of the major diseases impacting human mortality. Radiation remains one of the most effective approaches to treat cancer, though the side effects are debilitating. One feature that hinders the ability of radiation to act on cancer cells is the fact the environment around the cancer cell lacks oxygen. Since oxygen is intimately involve in the ability of radiation to kill cancer cells, developing a way to specifically deliver oxygen to cancer cells can potentially improve cancer radiation therapy. In this study we found that the targeted delivery of particles containing myoglobin, an ubiquitous oxygen-storage protein found in mammals, to cancer cells can be used to enhance the effectiveness of radiation therapy. Thus these studies provide a new approach to improve radiation-based treatment of cancer, and potentially reduce treatment times.

14121815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14121815.value: Articular cartilage, a highly organized avascular connective tissue with substantial durability, has a limited intrinsic repair capacity following trauma or degenerative pathology. Hypoxia is a hallmark for articular cartilage development, repair or regeneration and functions as a stimulus for initiation of gene programs regulating cellular growth and metabolism. We reasoned that chondrogenic lineage cells, the cellular component of the healing cartilage, are ideally positioned to sense and respond to fluctuations in oxygen and nutrient supply during the healing process. The hypoxia inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) pathway has emerged as the central pathway responding to hypoxia in a wide variety of organisms. HIF-1α impinges on gene programs which influence stem/progenitor cell proliferation, differentiation and cellular metabolism. HIF-1α levels are controlled by regulated proteolysis through an oxygen sensitive mechanism. Our recent studies have shown that HIF-1α is strongly induced during cartilage repair, and inactivation of HIF-1α in the developing mesenchyme in a mouse model impaired chondrogenesis and joint development. Activation of HIF-1α by small molecule prolyl hydroxylase inhibitor affects chondrogenic cells proliferation, differentiation, and migration. In this proposal, we will test the hypothesis that during articular cartilage repair chondrocytes and their progenitors use the HIF-1α pathway to sense low oxygen tension and transmit signals that regulate the progenitors migration, differentiation and functional engraftment, and targeting the HIF-1α pathway could be designed as a therapy for improving cartilage repair or generation. We propose the following three aims: Aim 1, to examine the effects of inducible conditional deletion of HIF-1α in mesenchymal progenitor cells or chondrocytes on articular cartilage repair. Aim 2, to define molecular signals downstream of HIF-1α that regulate chondrogenic cell migration, differentiation and engraftment during articular cartilage repair. Aim 3, to evaluate the effects of pharmacologic activation of the HIF-1α pathway on articular cartilage repair using a cartilage defect model. 14121815.label: Realisation of objectives
14121815.value: For Aim 1, a circular defect is made in the interchondylar groove of the distal femur with a 27G needle using a circular drilling motion until the subchondral bone was penetrated. A defect 0.6-0.8 mm in diameter is generated. The defect was treated with or without an alginate 3D scaffold. Adenoviruses containing Cre recombinase (Ad-Cre) were injected into the osteochondral defect, with Ad-GFP as control. An efficient deletion of HIF-1α in the repairing cartilage tissues was achieved as indicated by significantly decreased mRNA (70% deletion) and protein levels. HIF-1α target gene expression including VEGF, Glut-1 and PGK-1 was decreased dramatically. This is accompanied by impaired articular cartilage repair in the osteochondral defect model. We next obtained conditional deletion of HIF-1α in chondrocytes (Col2α1-Cre+/-ERT; HIF-1α fl/fl) and confirmed the efficiency of deletion by immunostaining of HIF-1α in chondrocytes of the growth plate of the mutant mouse. The articular cartilage defect model in mice lacking HIF-1α in chondrocytes and the control mice (HIF-1α fl/fl) was performed as indicated above. The articular cartilage defect repair was examined by histological analysis (safranin O staining) and noted that mice lacking HIF-1α in chondrocytes had impaired repair capacity than that of the controls at 12 weeks post-surgery. The cellular proliferation in the defect region of the area in mice lacking HIF-1α in chondrocytes was decreased as indicated by immunostaining of PCNA or BrdU at different time points. The histological and micro-computed tomography analysis also indicated the impaired repair capacity of the articular cartilage defects in mice lacking HIF-1α in chondrocytes than that of the controls. For Aim2, to identify HIF-1α downstream targets that affect ECM synthesis, cell migration and chondrogenesis, we identified the molecular signals that emanated from MSCs or chondrocytes. MSCs carrying HIF-1α floxed allele were plated and infected with Ad-Cre or Ad-GFP, then re-plated and allowed to recover for 48 hours under hypoxia (2% O2) and normoxic condition (20% O2). Cells with or without HIF-1α deletion were cultured in normoxia or hypoxia for another 24h. To characterize the regulatory mechanism of HIF-1α in MSC migration, we examined the expression of migration related genes by quantitative real-time PCR. HIF-1α deletion substantially decreased migration related genes including CD44, CXCR6, CCR1, SDF1, MMP13, and TIMP3. DFO treatment increased the expression of migration related genes including CD44, CXCR4, CXCR6, SDF1, cMet, MMP9, MMP3, and TIMP3. Being dramatically changed in cells with HIF-1α deletion (70% downregulation) or DFO treatment (3 folds upregulation), TIMP3 was considered as an interesting candidate gene downstream of HIF-1α to regulate MSC migration. The upregulation of TIMP3 protein expression was further confirmed by Western blot. A putative HIF-1α consensus binding site located 735 bp upstream of transcriptional start site of the TIMP3 gene was identified. To verify the binding of HIF-1α to the TIMP3 promoter, chromatin immunoprecipitation assay was performed. MSCs were exposed to normoxic, DFO or hypoxic conditions for 12 h. TIMP3 DNA bound with HIF-1α was readily detected in cells cultured under normoxia but dramatically increased under both DFO and hypoxia, demonstrating that HIF-1α binds to TIMP3 promoter region and the binding was enhanced in response to DFO and hypoxia. This indicated that HIF-1α upregulated TIMP3 expression through binding to its promoter region and subsequently increased mRNA transcription and protein expression. To further access whether knockdown of TIMP3 could inhibit MSC migration at indicated checkpoint, siRNAs against TIMP3 was transfected into MSCs. The results showed that siRNA mediated knockdown of TIMP3 was able to decrease MSC migration in both wound healing assays (12 h) and trans-well migration assays (3 h). The quantitative analysis of migration rate showed that the wound healing rate was decreased (30%), while in the trans-well assay the number of migrated cells was lowered (50%) after TIMP3 knockdown. In addition, the effect of DFO on migration was significantly impeded when TIMP3 was knocked down in MSCs. The results reveal that TIMP3 is important for MSCs migration and functions as a target of HIF-1α. In the micro-mass culture (7 or 14 days), we found that hypoxia not only increased the proteoglycan synthesis, but also upregulated the expression of chondrogenic marker genes including SOX5, SOX9, Col2 and Aggrecan. Immunostaining showed up-regulation of HIF-1α, Glut1 and proliferation cell nuclear antigen (PCNA) level in sections of the 3D cultures under hypoxia. Real-time PCR and Western blot analysis showed up-regulation of HIF-1α, PHD2 and Glut1 levels, which were accompanied by enhanced glucose uptake. In addition, the gene microarray analysis showed that hypoxia upregulated PFKL expression, which involved in the regulation of glucose metabolism in chondrocytes. The expression of PFKL mRNA and protein was decreased accompanied with deletion of HIF-1α under hypoxia. The knockdown of PFKL in chondrocytes was obtained using siRNA technique, chondrocyte ECM was dramatically decreased under hypoxia. In mouse osteochondral defect model, alginate/chondrocytes 3D complex under hypoxia were transplanted in the defect area for 3 and 6 weeks, we found that 3D complexes under hypoxia had improved repair of the defect region than that under normoxia indexed with the increased expression of Col2 and sox9, but Col10α1 and MMP13 expressions were decreased in the defect region. These data indicate that hypoxia enhances engineered chondrogenesis through coordinating chondrogenic differentiation and glucose metabolism (Manuscript 1). For Aim 3, mature wild type male mice (8-12 weeks old) were anesthetized by isoflurane inhalation. A sterile preparation was performed. The osteochondral defect was treated with or without an alginate gel 3D scaffold. Alginate gel transplants embedded with DFO was implanted in the defect region. We found that DFO treatment significantly increased cartilage repair outcome as quantified by ICRS scores on the gross examination. For histological assessment, samples from 6- or 12-week post-operation were stained with Safranin O. There were fibrocartilages and organized hyaline cartilages in different groups. The control group showed fibers crossing the boundary in the damaged cartilage and was lack of architecture and subchondral bone formation. Meanwhile, scaffold group showed moderate change in the cluster formation, clefts, focal lesions and Safranin O metachromasia compared with control group. In contrast to control and scaffold groups, osteochondral defect cartilage transplanted with DFO incorporated bioscaffold ameliorated repair outcome with a mature layer of hyaline cartilage in the patellar groove. DFO also dramatically increased cartilage matrix proteoglycan synthesis in neo-cartilage formation over both 6 and 12 weeks. The newly regenerated layers were well-organized and integrated with the host tissues, elucidating a favorable healing microenvironment. The ICRS score revealed that DFO treatment had higher score compared to control and scaffold groups. The data indicate that activation of HIF-1α by DFO-incorporated scaffold enhances cartilage repair (Manuscript 2). To better define a proper bio-scaffold for in vivo transplantation study, we generated a high strength PEG hydrogel. Chondrocytes laden hydrogel was constructed and in vivo subcutaneous transplantation in SCID mice was performed. Histological, immunohistochemistry and gene expression analyses revealed that chondrocytes proliferated and maintained their phenotypes in the scaffold, with the production of abundant extracellular matrix components and the formation of typical chondrocyte lacunae structure over 12 weeks. As a result, the chondrocytes/hydrogel constructs developed into a structure with improved mechanical properties and typical cartilage features. The data provide a guideline for preparation of mechanically strong hydrogel for cartilage tissue engineering (Biomaterials. 2017, 120:11-21).

14121815.label: Major findings and research outcome
14121815.value: In the present study, we established an osteochondral defect model in which an efficient deletion of HIF-1α in the repairing cartilage tissues was achieved by Cre-mediated deletion. HIF-1α target gene expression including VEGF, Glut-1 and PGK-1 was dramatically decreased. This was accompanied by impaired articular cartilage repair in the osteochondral defect model. The cellular proliferation in the defect region of the area in mice lacking HIF-1α in chondrocytes was decreased as indicated by immunostaining of PCNA or BrdU. We next examined the effects of hypoxia environment on chondrogenesis in the three-dimensional (3D) culture system. The chondrogenic differentiation under hypoxia was enhanced indicated by increased proteoglycan synthesis and chondrogenic marker genes expression. 6-phosphofructokinase, liver type (PFKL) mRNA and protein were dramatically up-regulated in chondrocytes under hypoxia than that of normoxia. Deferoxamine (DFO), a prolyl hydroxylase (PHD) inhibitor, was shown to activate HIF-1α and promote the proliferation and differentiation of chondroprogenitor cells and the migration of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). It elevated the expression of tissue inhibitor metalloproteinase-3 (TIMP3) through transcriptional control by HIF-1α. DFO enhanced the initiation of MSC membrane protrusion through regulating the expression and interaction of the key focal adhesion proteins vinculin and paxillin. In an osteochondral defect model, DFO dramatically facilitated the recruitment and functional engraftment of MSCs to the lesion site compared with the controls. Alginate-gelfoam scaffold incorporated with DFO enhanced articular cartilage repair through increasing chondrogenic cell proliferation, differentiation and proteoglycan synthesis. In addition, chondrocytes laden hydrogel was constructed under this condition and in vivo subcutaneous transplantation in SCID mice was performed. Histological, immunohistochemistry and gene expression analyses reveal that chondrocytes proliferate and maintain their phenotypes in the scaffold, with the production of abundant extracellular matrix components and the formation of typical chondrocyte lacunae structure therein over 12 weeks. The study demonstrates that pharmacological activation of HIF-1α enhances articular cartilage repair through coordinating MSC migration, chondrogenic differentiation, proliferation and functional engraftment. The study provides a guideline for preparation of mechanically strong hydrogel for cartilage tissue engineering. Based on the research work of this project, 1 invited lecture, 4 international conference oral or poster presentations were given by the PI and PhD student. One paper was published (Biomaterials. 2017, 120:11-21). Two manuscripts were prepared. The detailed information on the meetings, abstracts, publication and manuscript are enclosed in the research output part.

14121815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14121815.value: Based on the results obtained, it suggests that hypoxia enhances engineered chondrogenesis through coordinating chondrogenic differentiation and glucose metabolism. Targeting the HIF-1α pathway may serve as a potent therapeutic approach for articular cartilage repair. The study also provides a guideline for preparation of mechanically strong hydrogel for cartilage tissue engineering. This novel approach might benefit the patients with articular cartilage degeneration or defects. It can be further developed to test the potential therapeutic effects of the integrative tissue engineering approach for articular cartilage regeneration in the clinical trials.

14121815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14121815.value: Articular cartilage has very limited capacity for repair following injury or degeneration. The reparative stem cells or chondrocytes are readily located in a hypoxic microenvironment during cartilage repair. Hypoxia inducible factor-α (HIF-α) is identified as a key mediator for adaptation to low oxygen tension. However, the molecular mechanisms of hypoxia/HIF-α regulation on articular cartilage tissue repair remain unclear. In this study, we established an osteochondral defect model in which an efficient deletion of HIF-1α in the repairing cartilage tissues was achieved by Cre-mediated deletion, this was accompanied by decreased expression of HIF-1α downstream target genes including VEGF, Glut-1 and PGK-1. Functional analysis showed an impaired repair capacity of the articular cartilage defects in mice lacking HIF-1α in chondrocytes than that of the controls. We next showed that chondrogenic differentiation of chondroprogenitor cells was enhanced under hypoxia indicated by increased proteoglycan synthesis and chondrogenic marker genes expression. Deferoxamine (DFO), a prolyl hydroxylase (PHD) inhibitor, was shown to activate HIF-1α in chondrocytes and promoted the proliferation and differentiation of chondroprogenitor cells. Alginate-gelfoam scaffold incorporated with DFO enhanced articular cartilage repair. The study demonstrates that pharmacological activation of HIF-1α enhances articular cartilage repair through coordinating MSC migration, chondrogenic differentiation, proliferation and functional engraftment.
