14121915.label: Realisation of objectives
14121915.value: The main objective of this project is to characterize a new albino mutant bzs20 and study the gene function causing the mutant phenotype. By far, all objectives have been achieved and below are the highlights for how we have achieved the objectives and what are the major discoveries made relevant to three specific objectives. 1. Research achievements related to Objective 1: “Detailed phenotypic characterization of the bzs20 mutant”. In the original project proposal, we stated that bzs20 was isolated from a T-DNA activation tagging mutant screen in Arabidopsis for bzr1-1D suppressor mutants (bzs). This suppressor mutant screen was expected to identify gain-of-function mutants in the brassinosteroid (BR) signaling, however, a recessive mutant bzs20 was unexpectedly isolated. bzs20 is small and albino in both cotyledons and true leaves and is seedling lethal when grown in the light due to inability to support photoautotrophic growth. In addition, the albinism and lethality of bzs20 could not be rescued by treatments with sucrose or any phytohormones as reported for some other albino mutants. These uniqueness of bzs20 stimulated us to further characterize this mutant and study the mechanisms controlling the mutant phenotype. (1) The chlorophyll biosynthesis and chloroplast development defects in bzs20 greatly affected the photosynthesis performance of the plant As described in our original application, bzs20 has severe defects in chloroplast development and accumulates only about 1/10 chlorophylls of the wild type (WT) plant. During the project implementation period, we further analysed the expression of 28 key chlorophyll biosynthetic genes by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR) and found that the expression of these genes was all reduced, albeit to different extent, in the bzs20 mutant; some of them dropped to nearly zero, such as CHLI2, PORA and PORB. Chlorophyll fluorescence measurements showed that major photosynthesis parameters such as Fv/Fm (an indicator of maximum quantum yield of photosystem II [PSII]), ΦPSⅡ(the effective quantum yield of PSII), and qP (the photochemical quenching) were all significantly decreased in bzs20, indicating severe damage of photochemical activity of PSII and electron transport around PSII and plastoquinone. (2) Chloroplast development defects are formed during seedling greening process but not during embryogenesis Because bzs20 grows albino cotyledons upon seed germination, we wondered that the mutant phenotype might be formed during embryogenesis. Through microscopic embryo dissection we found no differences between the bzs20 and WT embryos at different developmental stages in terms of embryo shape, size and pigmentation, suggesting that bzs20 embryos contain normal chloroplasts and the mutant albinism is likely formed after embryogenesis, such as during the subsequent seedling greening processes. Thus, we compared the chloroplast ultrastructure in the mutant and WT seedlings during dark to light transition and at different seedling greening stages up to 24 hours. No difference was found for etioplasts in dark-grown seedlings or chloroplasts from light-grown seedlings during the first 13 hours of illumination. However, after 24 hours’ illumination, significant differences were found: the bzs20 chloroplasts possess few thylakoid membranes, no grana and starch granules formed as compared with the WT chloroplasts, confirming that the albinism of bzs20 is formed during the seedling greening process. (3) The bzs20 phenotype is independent of brassinosteroid (BR) action Because bzs20 was identified from a BR-related mutant screen, we were interested to know whether bzs20 phenotypes can be rescued by BR treatment and whether the BZS20 protein is BR-regulated and involved in BR-regulated chloroplast development. Based on our studies, the answers to all these questions are negative. 2. Research achievements related to Objective 2: “Identify the mutant gene in bzs20 and study its function in chloroplast development”. (1) BZS20 gene cloning The candidate gene in the mutant was cloned by a PCR-based method -- adaptor-ligation mediated PCR and further confirmed by genome re-sequencing using Illumina DNA sequencing technology. We determined the candidate gene is At2g27290 with a T-DNA insertion in the second intron. In Genbank the gene was annotated as a chloroplast-localized protein with unknown function. To prove that we have cloned the right gene, the At2g27290 cDAN was used to complementbzs20 phenotype. We also performed bzs20 phenotype recapitulation by silencing the At2g27290 gene by CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing. Both experiments confirmed that the At2g27290 gene is the right causing bzs20 phenotypes. (2) BZS20 expression pattern and subcellular localization In silico studies of the BZS20 gene and protein using online tools suggest that it expresses mainly in green tissues and the protein localizes in chloroplast. These predictions were confirmed by gene expression analysis at both RNA and protein levels and by microscopic analysis using the BZS20-GFP transgenic plants. Further, by chloroplast compartments fractionation and washes with different salts, BZS20 was defined as an integral thylakoid protein. We also determined the topology of BZS20 in thylakoid membranes that the C-terminus of BZS20 is integrated in thylakoid membrane and its N terminus faces the chloroplast stroma. (3) BZS20 Is required for accumulation of major thylakoid protein complexes, particularly the Cyt b6f Complex To understand the function of BZS20 protein in chloroplast development, we analyzed the total protein and marker protein levels of major photosynthetic complexes (PSI, PSII, ATPase, Cytochrome b6f and chlorophyll-binding) in the WT (Col-0), bzs20, bzs20-complementation lines, and BZS20-Cas9 mutants by western blot analysis. The results indicated that all the tested proteins were significantly reduced in the two mutants but restored to WT levels in the complemented bzs20 seedlings, suggesting BZS20 is crucial for assembly or accumulation of major thylakoid protein complexes. We also found that among the above protein complexes, PSI, PSII and Cyt b6f are the most severely affected in the bzs20 and BZS20-Cas9 mutants. Also, the Cyt b6f is the earliest complex affected by the bzs20 mutation. Therefore, Cyt b6f might be the primary target of BZS20 protein. A targeted yeast two-hybrid assay revealed that BZS20 is associated with the b6f complex and interacts with 4 subunits of the b6f complex (Cyt b6, PetD, PetG and PetN). 3. Research achievements related to Objective 3: “Identify new regulators for chloroplast development”. (1) Transcriptomic and proteomic study to the bzs20 mutant To identify additional regulators of chloroplast development besides BZS20, we performed a comparative transcriptome study to the bzs20(Col) mutant over WT (Col), and a proteomic study in bzs20(Col), BZS20-Cas9 and their WT (Col). The transcriptome analysis identified 193 differentially expressed genes associated with chloroplast, with 108 genes up-regulated and 85 down-regulated. Most of the down-regulated genes are photosynthesis-related. An iTRAQ-based proteomic study identified 991 differentially expressed proteins from two mutants relative to WT. Among them, 88 were up-regulated in both mutants and are related to stress or transport, whereas the 118 down-regulated proteins were mostly chloroplast (75.4%) or thylakoid (57.6%) proteins involved in photosynthesis. These omics datasets provided useful resource for study of BZS20 function and chloroplast development. (2) Yeast two-hybrid screen for BZS20-interaction partners To further understand the mechanisms by which BZS20 regulates chloroplast development, we performed a BZS20-based yeast two-hybrid screen against an Arabidopsis cDNA library. From this screen, we identified 65 potential BZS20-interacting proteins with high stringency. These proteins will be very helpful for further study of BZS20 function and chloroplast development.

14121915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14121915.value: From a genetic mutant screen in the model plant Arabidopsis, we isolated an albino mutant bzs20, which is small and albino in whole plant. It is also a seedling lethal mutant and cannot grow into an adult plant when grown in the light. Gene cloning from the mutant indicate that the mutant phenotype is caused by a recessive mutation in a gene with unknown function. These uniqueness of bzs20 stimulated us to further characterize this mutant and study the function of the BZS20 gene in controlling chloroplast developemnt. Our results indicated that the mutant phenotype was caused by abnormal chloroplast development during the seedling greening process after germination. Loss of BZS20 function leads to significantly damaged photosynthesis activity and extremely reduced photosynthetic membrane system in chloroplasts, particularly the cytochrome b6f complex. Further, we find that BZS20 has physical interaction with 4 subunits of the b6f complex, suggesting that BZS20 is crucial for assembly or stability of major photosynthetic protein complex in the thylakoids. The identification of BZS20 and other chloroplast genes/proteins identified from our Omics studies and yeast two-hybrid screen for BZS2-interaction partners provide more gene resources for future study of chloroplast development.

14122015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14122015.value: The lateral stalk of ribosome is responsible for domain-specific recognition of translation GTPase such as elongation factors. In eukaryotic ribosomes, the stalk is composed of eL12, P0, P1 and P2. P0 binds two copies of P1/P2 heterodimers to form a pentameric P-complex. Supported by RGC grants, our group has determined the structure of P1/P2 heterodimers by NMR spectroscopy and the structural organization of the P-complex. On the other hand, eL12 and P0, each binds to the 28S rRNA, together constitute the base of the eukaryotic stalk that may provide specific interaction for binding translation GTPases. We have identified that the N-terminal consensus sequence of eL12 and the P0 extended domain (P0ext) are unique features found in eukaryotic ribosomes but not in bacterial ribosomes. The main theme of this proposal is to study how these unique features of eukaryotic stalk proteins eL12 and P0ext domain play a role in protein synthesis. Our work will address the following objectives: (1) How does eL12 interact with P0? One key hypothesis is that the conserved N-terminal sequence of eL12 is essential for binding the P0. We will address this question by mutagenesis and structural studies. (2) Next, we will test if the interaction between eL12 and P0 is essential for protein translation. (3) Finally we will address how eL12 and P0 provide specific interactions for the domain-specific recognition of elongation factors. Through our work, we will provide structural and functional insights into how the eukaryotic stalk base proteins eL12 and P0 plays a role in domain-specific recognition of elongation factors. 真核生物核醣體的外側柄部包含有eL12, P0, P1和P2蛋白，負責識別如延伸因子的特定生物域的翻譯GTP酶。P0與兩個P1/P2異二聚體共同組成了五聚體形式的P蛋白複合物。受惠於RGC基金的支持，我們成功利用NMR技術解析了P1/P2的異二聚體結構，並且推測出P蛋白複合物的結構組成。另外，eL12 和P0分別與28S rRNA結合，共同組成了真核生物核醣體外側柄部的基礎，這個部位可能為結合翻譯GTP酶提供特異的相互作用。我們研究發現，eL12的N端的保守序列和P0的延伸域（P0ext）都是在真核生物的核醣體中所獨有的，而不存在於細菌的核醣體中。這個計劃書的主要目的是研究這些真核生物核醣體中所獨有的eL12和P0ext是如何在蛋白合成中行使功能。我們將會完成以下幾個目標來進行我們的研究：（1）eL12是如何與P0相互作用？一個主要的猜想是eL12中保守的N端序列對於其同P0的結合是必須的。我們將會通過突變實驗和結構研究來解釋這一問題。 （2）接下來，我們將會研究eL12與P0的相互作用對於蛋白質翻譯是否是必須的。 （3）最後，我們將會解釋eL12和P0的相互作用是如何影響不同生物域的延伸因子的識別。通過我們的工作，我們將會從結構和功能上深入了解eL12和P0蛋白是如何在延伸因子特定生物域的識別上行使功能的。

14122015.label: Realisation of objectives
14122015.value: The main theme of this GRF proposal focuses on how the stalk proteins eL12 and P0 interact with each other, and how they play a role in protein synthesis and binding of elongator factor-2 (eEF2). 1. Structure-function studies of P0ext domain • We determined the solution structure of B. mori P0ext domain by NMR spectroscopy (Figure 2, Choi et al). The structure of the P0ext domain consists of three pairs of β-strands wrapping around two helices. Residues 108-184 are well defined while the residues at both N- and C-termini are unstructured. • The solution structure of the P0ext domain was compared to those in eRF1/ABCE1-bound and eEF2-bound ribosomes. We showed that significant structural differences were found in a “hinge” region around a conserved Phe183 residue (Figure 3, Choi et al). A swing motion of Phe183 causes residues around β1/β6 and β2/β5 to move away from the loop connecting to the RNA-binding domain. Interestingly, such a hinge motion facilitates a rigid-body movement of the P0ext domain upon binding of different translation factors (Supplementary Figures, Choi et al). • That the hinge region is intrinsically flexible is supported by 15N relaxation experiments. 15N longitudinal (R1) and transverse (R2) relaxation rates and 1H-15N NOE were measured for the P0ext domain (Figure 4, Choi et al). We showed that residues in the hinge region (Leu119, Leu161, Val167 and Gly168) have significantly faster R2 rate, suggesting chemical exchange contributions in these residues. • To further understand the functional role of the hinge region, using yeast genetics we created a yeast mutant strain expressing a F181A variant of P0 (Phe181 of yeast P0 corresponds to Phe183 in B. mori P0). As the bulky phenylalanine is located at the center of the hinge region making a number of hydrophobic interactions with surrounding residues. The alanine substitution should increase the flexibility of the hinge region, making it easier to change conformational to accommodate binding of different translation factors. 80S yeast ribosomes with the F181A variant of P0 were purified from the yeast mutant strains and assayed for their protein translation activity (Figure 5, Choi et al.). Our results showed that the F181A substitution increased the protein translation activity, supporting the role of flexibility of P0ext domain in protein translation. • Our work on the structural and mutagenesis studies of the P0ext domain has been published (please refer to the attached paper of Choi et al). 2. Structure-function studies of eL12 • We determined the solution structure of human eL12 by NMR spectroscopy. To our surprise, eL12 in solution does not form a single globular structure as in the ribosome-bound form. Instead, it folds into an N-terminal domain (NTD) and a C-terminal domain (CTD) (Figure 1, Yang et al). • Major structural changes are found in the linker region between the NTD and CTD. In the ribosome-bound form of eL12, the linker region forms a helix-3 that form extensive interactions with both the NTD and CTD, linking both domains together to form a globular structure (Figure 1, Yang et al). However, in the free eL12, this linker region is unstructured. • That the linker region is unstructured prompted us to measure the backbone dynamics of human eL12 in solution. 15N longitudinal (R1) and transverse (R2) relaxation rates and 1H-15N NOE were measured (Figure 2, Yang et al). We also performed relaxation dispersion experiment to measure the chemical contributions in human eL12 in solution (Table 1 and Figure 3, Yang et al.) • Intriguingly, residues with significant chemical exchanges are clustered in the linker region and are those interacting with helix-3 in the ribosome-bound form (Figure 3, Yang et al). These results suggest a model where the free form of eL12 is in exchange with a more structured conformation as seen in the ribosome-bound form. • Our results also showed that eL12 in solution contains intrinsically disordered regions. Interestingly, eukaryotic eL12 contains an N-terminal MPPKFDP motif that is conserved only eukaryotic ribosomes but not in bacterial ribosomes. This motif is also unstructured and flexible in the solution structure of eL12. • Interestingly, we showed that this N-terminal motif is important in the eL12-P0 interaction (Figure 4, Yang et al). Pull-down assay showed that eL12 could pull-down the P-complex [P0(P1/P2)2] but not the P1/P2 heterodimer, suggesting eL12 interacts directly with P0. On the other hand, truncation of the MPPKFDP motif in the eL12N7 variant abolished the interaction with P-complex. • Interestingly, eL12 only formed stable complex with the P-complex, but not with the P0ext domain. While this observation precludes structure determination of a eL12/P0ext complex, it suggests that interaction between eL12 and P0 may requires the participation of the RNA binding domain. Given the large conformational changes in eL12 upon ribosome binding, it is essential to confirm the in-vitro binding results with functional assay. • To test if interaction between eL12 and P0 is important to protein translation, we used the hybrid ribosomes to test how the truncation of the MPPKFDP motif affect protein synthesis (Figure 5, Yang et al). The hybrid ribosomes were reconstituted by mixing E. coli 50S core ribosomes with human P-complex and eL12 and assayed for their protein translation activity. Our results showed that hybrid ribosome reconstituted with eL12N7 were lower in translation activity, suggesting the interaction between eL12 and P0. • The results of the hybrid ribosomes were further supported by mutagenesis study in yeast ribosomes. To test the role of the MPPKFDP in a more native environment, we have created a yeast mutant strain expressing a N7 variant of eL12. Similar to what we have described in creating the yeast mutant strain for P0 mutant, we transform a plasmid expressing a wild-type or mutant T7-tagged eL12 to a yeast strain with both copies of eL12 genes in yeast genome (RPL12A and RPL12B) knocked out. • 80S ribosomes were purified from the yeast strains expressing wild-type and N7 of eL12 (Figure 6, Yang et al). After confirming the presence of the truncated eL12 by western blot, the translation activity of the purified ribosomes was assayed. Consistent with our hybrid ribosome data, we showed that yeast ribosome with the eL12N7 variant exhibited a lower translation activity. Taken together, we showed the interaction between eL12 and P0 is important to protein translation. • We are writing up our work on eL12. To facilitate the review of our progress, we have included all the figures in the manuscript in this completion report (Please refer to the figures attached) 3. Mutations that affect eEF2 binding and protein translation • Based on the available structures of ribosomes in complex with eEF-2, we have designed a number of mutants in eL12 and P0ext. Interestingly, we found that rigidifying mutations at Gly33 of eL12 (G33A and G33P) have interesting effect on eEF2 binding and protein translation. • We created yeast mutant strain expressing G33A or G33P variants of eL12. Our initial results suggest that yeast ribosomes with these variants had less tendency to release its eEF2 after GTP hydrolysis, and hence, had lower protein translation activity. In summary, we have combined structure determination, dynamic and mutagenesis studies to understand the role of eL12 and P0 in protein translation. In particular, we showed that the N-terminal motif of eL12 is essential in interacting with P0 and is important in protein translation. Mutagenesis showed that rigidifying mutations of eL12 affect protein translation by alter binding to the eEF2. In our opinion, we have achieved all the objectives.

14122015.label: Major findings and research outcome
14122015.value: 1. P0ext domain has a flexible hinger region that change conformations upon binding of translation factors We determined the solution structure of B. mori P0ext domain. Structural comparison with the structures of P0ext domain in eRF1-bound and eEF2-bound ribosomes reveal significant structure rearrangement in a hinge region, where the swinging motion of a conserved Phe183 may facilitate a rigid-body movement of the P0ext domain upon binding of different translation factors. Our 15N relaxation experiments showed that residues in the hinger region have significantly faster transverse relaxation rate, suggesting conformational exchanges process in the region. 2. Mutagenesis suggests the role of Phe183 in the hinge region is important in protein translation To probe the role of the conserved phenylalanine residue in protein translation, we purified 80S ribosome from a yeast strain expressing a F181A variant of P0 and showed that replacing the bulky phenylalanine with alanine increased the protein translation activity. Our results support the hypothesis that flexibility of the hinge region is important in protein translation 3. eL12 contains an intrinsically disordered linker region that only form structure when bound to the ribosomes We determined the solution of human eL12, which contains a structured N- and C-terminal domains linked together by an unstructured linker region. Structural comparison with ribosome-bound eL12 suggest that the linker region becomes structured with the formation of helix-3 upon binding to the ribosomes. 15N relaxation experiments showed that significant chemical exchange contributions in residues in the linker region. 4. eL12 contains an unstructured N-terminal motif that play essential role in interacting with P-complex and in protein translation The structural and relaxation analyses also suggest that the N-terminal MPPKFDP motif is flexible and unstructured. We showed that this motif is important for eL12-P0 interaction and such interaction is important for protein translation. 5. Mutagenesis studies showed that rigidifying mutations of eL12 affected protein translation By comparing the structures of eL12 in ribosomes bound with different translation factors, we identified structural changes in the helix-2 of eL12. We introduced rigidifying mutations in eL12 and showed that yeast ribosomes with G33A and G33P variants of eL12 were able to retain eEF2 in the presence of GDP. We also showed that the mutant ribosomes had a lower protein translation activity, suggesting the rigidifying mutations may slow down protein translation by altering the binding/release of eEF2 during protein synthesis.

14122015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14122015.value: Through this study, we have identified a number of interesting mutants of eL12 and P0 that affect protein translation. With the recent advances in cryo-electron microscopy, it would be logical to extend our studies to investigate how these mutations may affect the ribosome structures. For example, it would be interesting to understand structurally why the G33A/P mutants have less tendency to release its eEF2 after GTP hydrolysis. Moreover, we have created the P0 and eL12 knock-out yeast strains. While they took us some time to create, the availability of these knock-out strains will greatly facilitate us to introduce further mutations in P0 and eL12 in yeast ribosomes.

14122015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14122015.value: Protein translation by ribosomes is the most fundamental aspects of life. Protein synthesis is driven by GTP hydrolysis with the translation factors, which is recognized by the lateral stalk of ribosomes. In eukaryotic ribosomes, the stalk is constituted by ribosomal protein eL12 and a P-complex with ribosomal protein P0, P1 and P2. In this project, we focus on the roles of the P0ext domain and eL12 in protein translation. We have determined the solution structure of P0ext domain and showed that the hinge region of P0ext domain undergo structural changes to ‘induced-fit’ the binding of translation factors. Dynamics and mutagenesis studies support the role of a conserved residue in the hinge region in protein translation. We also determined the solution structure of eL12. In its free form, eL12 contains intrinsically disordered regions that become structured when bound to the ribosomes. eL12 also contains a highly conserved N-terminal residues that were shown to interact with the P-complex. Truncation of the N-terminal residues in eL12 resulted in reduction in protein translation activity, suggesting that the interaction between eL12 and the P-complex is important in protein translation.

14122215.label: Project Objectives
14122215.value: To evaluate the physiological responses and tolerances of Hong Kong corals to interactive effects of changes in sea water temperature and salinity; To compare such tolerances with those of comparable species from tropical region along a latitudinal gradient along the Philippines and Indonesia.
rows: To evaluate the physiological responses and tolerances of Hong Kong corals to interactive effects of changes in sea water temperature and salinity;
To compare such tolerances with those of comparable species from tropical region along a latitudinal gradient along the Philippines and Indonesia.

14122215.label: Realisation of objectives
14122215.value: Hong Kong is a marginal environment for coral growth with fluctuating levels of annual temperature and rainfall. Hong Kong corals have long been exposed to these environmental stresses so Hong Kong corals are likely to be well adapted to these stresses and are therefore better equipped to cope with global climate change. This hypothesis is addressed in this research project. Interactive effects of lowered salinity and elevated and lowered temperature on different growth stages of the massive coral Platygyra acuta and branching corals Acropora tumida and A. pruinosa were evaluated to address objective 1. Growth stages of these corals were exposed to the temperature range of up to +5oC above ambient, and -3oC below ambient [24, 27 (ambient), 30, 32°C]. The ranges of salinity tested were more extensive [33 psu (ambient), 30, 26, 22, 18, 14 psu]. The results for P. acuta (Chui and Ang 2017a, Research Output (RO) C.8.1) indicate that elevated temperatures (+3ºC and +5ºC above ambient) did not show any significant effects on larval settlement success and post-settlement survival for up to 56 days of prolonged exposure. This thermal tolerance was much higher than that reported in the literature for other coral species. The elevated temperatures also appeared to exhibit a protective effect on the corals by reducing the negative effects of lowered salinity (26 psu) on settlement success. This resulted in an overall positive effect on recruitment success recorded up to 44 and 8 days of exposure under +3ºC and +5ºC ambient respectively. Similar results for Acropora spp. are also found (Chui 2016, RO C.10.1). This enhanced effect on recruitment shown in laboratory experiment, however, is not translated into greater recruitment success of corals in the field. The recruitment pattern of corals in Tung Ping Chau Marine Park (TPCMP) was examined using settlement plates (Chui and Ang, 2017b, RO C.8.2). TPCMP supports one of the best coral covers in Hong Kong. However, the recruitment success of corals in two sites within this marine park is extremely low. This low recruitment rate is partly responsible for low recovery of Hong Kong coral communities, e.g. those in Tolo Harbour and Channel, after a severe disturbance event (Wong 2017 RO C.10.2, Wong et al. 2018 RO C.8.4). Other factors, including predation, could have affected this pattern of recruitment success. However, experiment carried out to examine the possible effect of the corallivorous snail Drupella sp. on coral recruits showed the results to be negative, i.e. this corallivorous snails did not affect the survival of coral recruits (Tsang et al. 2018, RO C.8.5). In the course of checking on the predation effect of corallivorous snails on corals, our team also discovered a hitherto unreported case of a specific predation effect of a nudibranch Tenella sp. on the coral Pavona decussata (Wong et al. 2017, RO C.8.3). The impact of predation appears to be greater on the adult coral colonies. Our earlier studies indicated that lower winter temperature could weaken Acropora, making it more vulnerable to predation. Further experiment conducted on the massive coral P. acuta, which has been observed to be more tolerant to temperature change than the branching corals Acropora spp., showed that this coral is indeed also more tolerant to predation (Tsang and Ang 2019, RO C.8.6). Tolerances of Hong Kong corals to higher or lower temperature and salinity effects may be mediated through symbiosis. Differential acquisition of different symbiont clades by coral larvae was thus examined. Coral larvae of P. acuta and A. valida (= A. tumida) were able to acquire symbionts prior to settlement and form symbiosis with both symbiont types from both homologous and heterologous sources, revealing flexibility of symbiosis establishment. However, no significant difference in infection percentages was found among different sources of Symbiodinium C1, suggesting that host source of the symbiont types was unimportant. Symbiodinium D8-12 resulted in significantly higher infection rates in both species but the the advantage of hosting this to coral larvae is unclear (Ng et al. 2019, RO C.8.7). This ‘opportunistic’ symbiont type was found not as much affected by temperature and salinity stresses as the other clades. While this clade D symbiont was reported to exhibit higher thermal tolerance, it was also shown to be less photosynthetically efficient that leads to lower growth rate in coral juveniles. In the absence of any comparative advantages in settlement success and survivorship in recruits with D8-12 over C1 symbiont, the higher infection success of D8-12 on coral juveniles may simply be due to its greater infectiousness. This implies that global warming may drive the coral recruits to form symbiosis with less favorable symbionts like clade D Symbiodinium and thus affect the growth of future generations of corals under global climate change (Ng 2019, RO C.10.3). While P. acuta may be more tolerant to salinity and temperature changes compared to other corals in Hong Kong, they are nevertheless vulnerable to other impacts, especially those human in origin. Some recent events like red tides could have inflicted extensive damage to colonies of Platygyra acuta, especially in Hoi Ha Wan Marine Park (Ang et al. 2016, RO C.9.1). To further provide evidence on higher tolerances of Hong Kong corals to environmental variabilities than other comparable Tropical species (objective 2), similar experiments to evaluate interactive response of four coral genera / species (Platygyra, Acropora, Porites, Pavona) temperature were carried out in Hong Kong (Marine Science Laboratory, CUHK), the Philippines (Bolinao Marine Laboratory, University of the Philippines, August 2017) and Singapore (St. John Research Station, Singapore, Dec 2017). The original plan to carry the experiment in Indonesia did not materialize because of logistic constraints. Singapore was deemed an appropriate alternative because it shares comparable latitude and other environmental conditions as Indonesia. The factorial experimental designs in all these experiments were the same. Thermal and salinity tolerances of four coral genera: Acropora, Pavona, Platygyra and Porites were compared through a 7-day exposure experiment. The coral fragments of different species were exposed to five temperature levels (23, 26, 29 as ambient, 32 and 35 oC) and three salinity levels (18, 24 and 32-34 psu as ambient). Acropora was consistently found to be the most sensitive coral genus among all. Fragments of this coral were always the first to show different signs of stresses (e.g. pale colour, decrease in photosynthetic activities, and tissue decay). It was also observed that the effects of cold temperature treatment (23 and 26 oC) were weaker than that of the elevated temperature treatment (32 and 35 oC). Regardless of salinity treatments, all the 23oC -treated corals (except the Acropora exposed to 18 psu) were not affected by the cold temperature treatment. On the other hand, all the 35 oC -treated corals were killed by the high temperature. Through these experiments, Hong Kong corals were shown to have a higher tolerance limits than their Tropical counterparts. The final analyses and preparation of the manuscripts from these comparative studies were, unfortunately disrupted when the appointment of the PI was not extended beyond July 2018. The additional six months extension granted initially could not be utilized to complete the project. However, efforts are still being made to find ways to prepare the manuscripts under very difficult situation.

14122215.label: Major findings and research outcome
14122215.value: Experimental evidences were provided to indicate the high tolerance of Hong Kong corals to environmental stresses, particularly higher/lower temperature and lower salinities, compared to their Tropical counterparts. These evidences point to the importance of Hong Kong corals as a possible gene pool for future development of coral reefs, if corals in Tropical areas do succumb to the impact of climate change. Details of these are provided in the papers published, as indicated in Part C and described in Section 5.3.

14122215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14122215.value: With the high tolerance of Hong Kong corals to environmental stresses, physiological mechanisms behind these tolerances should be assessed at the genetic and phenotypical levels. Such tolerances may be due to genetic selection that has gone on over the decades, or may simply be a response to more recent changes through phenotypic plasticity. Such mechanisms, if they could be elucidated, will be of tremendous significance in understanding the responses of corals to environmental stresses and in projecting the future fate of corals and coral reef. These mechanisms will also be of great importance in developing strategies for the restoration of disturbed coral reefs around the world

14122215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14122215.value: Hong Kong, located in southern China, experiences large fluctuation in seawater temperatures as well as in salinity. Hong Kong is a marginal environmental for coral growth and yet at least 90 species of corals could still be found in Hong Kong waters. They form coral communities that serve the same roles as those coral reefs in Tropical seas. With long exposure to these marginal conditions, Hong Kong corals are likely to have developed their tolerances to these environmental tolerances over the years. This study provided evidence to confirm the high tolerance of Hong Kong corals to these environmental stresses, compared to their Tropical counterparts. The implication of these findings is that Hong Kong corals could be very important as gene pool for future expansion of corals and coral reefs, should tropical corals succumb to environmental impact brought about by global climate change in the future.

14122415.value: 水稻雄性不育在杂交育种中具有核心地位，为人们所熟知，但是 对水稻雌性不育材料及雌性不育基因却研究甚少。我们前期从田 间获得了一株水稻温敏型雌性不育种质（命名TGSS），遗传分 析表明此性状受单隐性基因控制（命名TFS1）。本研究拟通过显 微技术观察TGSS材料花器官的发育过程，明确TGSS材料不育的 细胞生物学机理。将TGSS材料与日本晴杂交，构建F2和F3分离 群体，利用SSR、SNP、Indel等分子标记对TFS1进行初步和精确 定位；同时在F2或F3代分离群体中构建Super BSA DNA混合池, 利用基于SLAF-seq技术的Super BSA基因定位方案对TFS1基因进 行定位,从而加快对TFS1基因的克隆。最后将利用反向遗传学技 术对TFS1基因的生物学功能及其作用机理进行研究。本项目研 究不仅对水稻生殖发育、雌性不育机理研究有重要的科学意义， 而且对推动水稻杂交育种也具有十分重要的实践意义。

14122415.label: Realisation of objectives
14122415.value: We found a natural mutation derived from rice cultivar 4266 named as thermo-sensitive female sterility 1 (tfs1), which shows strictly failed seed set during field production. Further observation indicated that double fertilization was blocked in tfs1 plant. The tfs1 displays female sterility accompanied with abnormal hull development under high temperature (>25℃), but the female fertility can be partially restored under low temperature (22-25℃). We first characterized the cytological function of TFS1 in controlling double fertilization. Investigations by confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) and paraffin section demonstrated that tfs1 had normal-appearing pistil and complete 7-cells 8-nuclei embryo sac inner structure. Aniline blue staining showed that after pollen germinating on stigma, pollen tube could reach to the micropyle in tfs1. However, embryo development was not found in ovary of tfs1 even at 4 days after pollination (DAP) or 7 DAP, which was observed in 1 DAP in wild type (cultivar 4266 plants) under high temperatures. These results suggest that double fertilization is blocked in tfs1 mutant after the pollen tube enter the micropyle. We then mapped and cloned the gene. Positional cloning revealed that TFS1 encodes an ARGONAUTE7 (AGO7) protein, the core component of RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC). Furthermore, indica and japonica, introgressed with mutant locus (mTFS1), which created by genetic crosses or genome editing, also displayed thermo-sensitive female sterile phenotype. Increased abundance of miR390 and miR390* loading into mTFS1 was found in tfs1, indicating failure ejection of miR390* from the mTFS1-RISC complex, thus subsequently impair tasi-ARF biogenesis and further weaken the degradation of ARF under high temperature. In addition, the abundance of miR390 and miR390* were partially reduced together with upregulated tasi-ARF in tfs1 under low temperatures, explaining the partial recovery of female fertility under low temperature. These findings indicate that the mutation locus of mTFS1 plays key role in miR390/miR390* duplex unwinding in response to changing temperatures, and eventually maintains female fertility, as well as provide a promising genetic resource for hybrid rice production. Since we have to raise the rice to the final grain filling stage, the experimental cycle is long. In addition, the temperature-sensitive functions of the gene proves very complex, an unconventional epigenetic control, and we had to adopt many new technologies not familiar to us, especially the miRNA analysis methods. Nevertheless, these results have been written up and submitted to Nature finally (Li et al. 2019). Cultivated rice is very different from its wild relatives. Domestication and human selection over the years have harvested many natural mutations such as TSF1. With such thinking and support of this project, we have come up with two reviews to show the rice breeders how to make use of the naturally existing genetic resources. We first analyzed the distribution and population types of drought-and flood-tolerant rice accessions, synthesized recent progresses of flood and drought tolerance research, and proposed a hypothesis that the molecular mechanisms of both drought and flood tolerance may be regulated by cross-talked pathways and coexist in aus subpopulation (Rahman and Zhang 2016). Then we identified a shared geographic distribution pattern for these highly stress-tolerant accessions and pointed out that the majority of these tolerant accessions predominately originated from Southern Asia including Bangladesh, a centralized narrow geographic region (Rahman and Zhang 2018). We believe these reviews will make impact to the rice researchers and breeders. On the molecular side of the rice stress research, we have found that a natural variation in the promoter region of rice calcineurin B-like protein10 (OsCBL10) affects flooding tolerance during seed germination and explains the different flooding tolerance in rice eco-types (Ye et al. 2018). Rice grain filling shows a typical asynchronous pattern with the later-flowering spikelets always poorly filled, the so called inferior spikelets. With the adoption of a very sensitive technology, the SWATH-MS quantitative analysis, we identified 304 proteins differentially expressed between the early and later flowering spikelets, indicating their functional difference during the grain filling period (Zhu et al. 2016). In summary, we have completed the proposed work and exceeded in some aspects for the rice research.

14122415.label: Major findings and research outcome
14122415.value: 1) tfs1 is a thermo-sensitive female sterile mutant tfs1 was identified in the background of an elite cultivar 4266 during field production, which is a strictly sterile germplasm with defective hull and normal vegetative growth under high temperatures (>25℃). However, the fertility of tfs1 was partially recovered, as well as rescued normal hull, when subjected to low temperatures (22-25℃) before panicle primordium formation. Investigations by confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) and paraffin section demonstrated that tfs1 had normal-appearing pistil and complete 7-cells 8-nuclei embryo sac inner structure. Aniline blue staining showed that after pollen germinating on stigma, pollen tube could reach to the micropyle in tfs1. However, embryo development was not found in ovary of tfs1 even at 4 days after pollination (DAP) or 7DAP, suggesting that double fertilization is blocked in tfs1 mutant after the pollen tube enter the micropyle. 2) Positional cloning and identification of TFS1 gene We generated F2 population containing 19848 individuals from the cross between tfs1 and Nipponbare (Nip) (Oryza sativa L. ssp. japonica). F2 population exhibited 3:1 segregation ratio (14836 fertility: 5012 sterility) under high temperatures in paddy field, indicating that female sterility was controlled by a single recessive nuclear locus. Primary mapping revealed that our target phenotype was linked with SSR marker 15295 near the centromere region on chromosome 3. Fine mapping indicated that the target locus was located between 15280 and 15327, a 2.16M region. However, even 4000 more F2 female sterile plants were not able to narrow down the target gene into a smaller region because of the low recombination rate near the centromere region. To solve this problem, modified MutMap method was performed by generating F2 population from the cross between tfs1 and 4266. With the use of SNP markers, we found that the SNP located in AGO7 was the candidate gene. To confirm the identity of this gene, we did the transformation and confirmed the mutation in TFS1 was responsible for the mutant phenotype in tfs1. CRISPR/Cas9 was also used and confirmed the mutation and observed phenotype. 3) Mechanism that leads to female sterility To reveal the molecular mechanism of mutant TFS1 (mTFS1) gene regulates female fertility in response to changing temperatures, expression of TFS1 gene and localization of TFS1 protein were studied. TFS1 showed similar expression level in 4266 and tfs1 both under high and low temperature, suggesting that the mutant site cannot alter the TFS1 expression in transcriptional level. Then, we generated fusion proteins of 35S: GFP-TFS1 and 35S: GFP-mTFS1, which were transformed into rice protoplasts and analyzed by confocal microscopy. Both TFS1 and mTFS1 proteins localized in cytoplasm, revealing that the spontaneous mutation of TFS1 did not affect protein subcellular localization. It has been well documented that the release of miR390* from TFS1 (AGO7), which formed the mature TFS1-RISC complex, was the key step to trigger TAS3 tasi-ARF biogenesis, subsequently regulate ARFs expression. We found there was an increased abundance of miR390 and miR390* loading into mTFS1 in tfs1, indicating failure ejection of miR390* from the mTFS1-RISC complex, thus subsequently impairing tasi-ARF biogenesis and further weakening the degradation of ARF under high temperature. In addition, the abundance of miR390 and miR390* were partially reduced together with upregulated tasi-ARF in tfs1 under low temperatures. These findings indicate that the mutation locus of mTFS1 plays key role in miR390/miR390* duplex unwinding in response to changing temperatures, and eventually maintains female fertility. The above described works have been summarized in a manuscript and submitted to Nature finally (Li et al. 2019).

14122415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14122415.value: Our findings revealed that the site mutation in tfs1 contribute to distinct phenotype from previous ago7 mutants, suggesting that linker2 domain functioned in regulating female fertility and responded to different temperature conditions. To test whether the site mutation of tfs1 can cause the TFS trait in japonica subspecies that may be used for hybrid seed production, we performed introgression experiments by both backcross and genome editing. We firstly used the traditional way to introgress mutant locus into Nip (Oryza sativa L. ssp. japonica) and Minghui63 (MH63) (Oryza sativa L. ssp. indica), after three times backcross followed by selfing, female sterility individuals were isolated from progeny of both backcrosses, indicating that the thermo-sensitive female sterility can be introduced into both indica and japonica varieties. In addition, we developed a convenient one-step way to create thermo-sensitive female sterile lines in indica and japonica rice varieties by genome editing system. A vector was constructed to knockout local TFS1 gene and introduce a mutant TFS1 (mTFS1) gene into other rice cultivars simultaneously and transformed into Nip and MH63 cultivar. Female sterility individuals resembling tfs1 were found in those transgenic lines. Genome editing results showed high transformation efficiency in the T0 generation and revealed that TFS trait was consistent in indica and japonica rice varieties, which is applicable to hybrid seed production in both rice subspecies.

14122415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14122415.value: Rice production has been significantly increased with the adoption of hybrid rice. The genetic background for such success is the utilization of heterosis, a term that defines the increased growth vigor of hybrid, and the discovery of male sterile line that relies on a donor (the restorer line) for fertile pollens. If a donor itself can be female sterile, production of hybrid seeds will be easy because harvest machines can be used without mixing hybrid seeds with seeds from the restorer line. It is well known that cost of hybrid seed production is a limitation to the wide adoption of hybrid rice worldwide. A female sterile restorer line should help reduce the cost. In this study we found a naturally mutated rice line showing female sterility at two temperatures, female sterile at normal high temperature (>25℃) but female fertile at low temperature (22-25℃). We revealed the cytological reasons why the female sterility occurs and found the molecular mechanism about how this gene works. Then we transferred this mutation gene into normal rice cultivars and found it also works. This work certainly has the potential to develop a new way to produce rice hybrid seeds with a reduced labor cost.

14122615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14122615.value: Pre-mRNA splicing in higher eukaryotic cells requires many auxiliary factors and involves complex series of protein-protein, protein-RNA and RNA-RNA interactions. One essential family of splicing factors is the Serine/Arginine-rich proteins (SR proteins). SR proteins are characterized by the presence of multiple continuous stretches of Arg-Ser (RS) dipeptides termed as RS domains at their C-termini. The RS domains undergo reversible phosphorylation and their states affect multiple facets of SR protein activity including their localization and functions in mediating spliceosome assembly, mRNA export and translation. Recent findings suggest that individual SR proteins have different mRNA targets and possibly unique biological roles. Understanding the regulation mechanism of phosphorylation of individual SR protein is therefore critical to the study of their distinct biological functions. One of the kinase families that specifically phosphorylate SR proteins is the SR protein kinases (SRPKs). Extensive efforts have been made on the understanding of the phosphorylation mechanism of the prototypic SR protein SRSF1 by SRPK1, the first identified SRPK. However, there is little information on how other SR protein members are being phosphorylated by SRPKs. In this project, we propose to investigate how different SRPKs phosphorylate individual SR protein using distinct mechanisms. The proposed works are the continuation of two previously supported projects that studied the molecular basis of recognition and phosphorylation of different SR and SR-like substrates by SRPK2, a close homolog of SRPK1. Briefly, we have unveiled that a conserved SRPK-specific docking groove in SRPK2 is critical for its interaction and phosphorylation of different substrates, including the SR protein SRSF1, SRSF3 and SR-like protein acinusS. We showed that SRPK2 phosphorylates SRSF1 using similar mechanism like SRPK1, despite the processivity of phosphorylation is lower. Furthermore, while SRPKs phosphorylate only the N-terminal half of SRSF1 RS domain, SRPK2 phosphorylates nearly the entire RS domain of SRSF3, of which 5 sites are processed processively. In contrast to the C-terminal to N-terminal direction of SRSF1 phosphorylation, SRSF3 is phosphorylated by SRPK2 in an N to C direction. Together our findings strongly suggest that SRPKs utilize vastly different mechanisms in the phosphorylation of different SR protein substrates. Therefore, we hereby propose to study the underlying basis for the difference of catalytic mechanism in SRPK1 and SRPK2 using structural and biochemical approaches. We will also decipher the molecular mechanism of SRSF3 phosphorylation by SRPK2. Our findings may help to define new rules that govern the interaction and phosphorylation of different SR proteins by SRPKs. 在高等真核細胞中，前體信使RNA(mRNA)的剪接需要許多輔助因子的參與，並牽涉到一系列複雜的蛋白-蛋白，蛋白-RNA以及RNA-RNA的相互作用。其中，SR蛋白是參與這一過程的一個關鍵家族。 SR蛋白的特徵是它們的C端都有一個含有多個連續的精氨酸- 絲氨酸多肽的結構域，稱為RS結構域。 RS結構域是SR蛋白進行可逆磷酸化的部位，而它的磷酸化狀態會影響到SR蛋白在許多方面的活動，這些活動包括SR蛋白在細胞內的定位，以及在調控剪接體組裝時，mRNA核輸出時和翻譯時的功能。最近的研究結果表明，不同的SR蛋白會與不同的信使RNA作用，並且可能在特殊的生物過程中扮演不同角色。因此，了解每個特定的SR蛋白的磷酸化調控機制對於研究它們的生物學功能至關重要。 SR蛋白激酶(SRPKs)是特異性磷酸化SR蛋白的其中一個激酶家族。 SRPK1是首個被鑑定的SR蛋白激酶，目前已進行的研究主要集中於揭示原型的SR蛋白-SRSF1被SRPK1磷酸化的機制。然而目前關於其他SR蛋白成員被SR蛋白激酶磷酸化的機制還少有探究。 在這個項目中，我們旨在探究不同的SR蛋白激酶在磷酸化不同的底物SR蛋白時使用的磷酸化機制的區別。這一項目是對已有的兩個研究項目的延續，我們將繼續探究SRPK1的相近同源蛋白SRPK2，對它識別以及磷酸化不同底物SR蛋白的分子基礎進行研究。我們已經揭示了SRPK2的結構中含有一個保守的SR蛋白對接槽，這一結構對於它與不同底物（包括SRSF1，SRSF3和acinusS）的相互作用起到十分關鍵的作用。我們發現，在磷酸化SRSF1的過程中，SRPK2採用與SRPK1相似的磷酸化機制，但SRPK2連續磷酸化的能力不如SRPK1。此外，對於SRSF1，兩種SR蛋白激酶只能夠磷酸化其RS結構域的N端半邊，然而對於SRSF3，SRPK2幾乎能夠磷酸化其整個RS結構域，其中有5個磷酸化位點是被連續地磷酸化的。另外，對於SRSF3，SRPK2是沿著由N端至C端的方向對其進行磷酸化，這與對SRSF1由C端至N端的磷酸化方向相反。總而言之，我們的研究結果有力地說明針對不同的SR蛋白底物，SR蛋白激酶採用迥然相異的磷酸化機制。據此，我們將通過生物化學和結構學的方法繼續尋找SRPK1和SRPK2針對不同底物採用不同催化機理的根本原因。在這一項目中我們還會著重解釋SRPK2磷酸化SRSF3的分子機制。這一項目的研究結果將有助於總結SR蛋白激酶對SR蛋白進行反應和磷酸化採用的規律。

14122615.label: Realisation of objectives
14122615.value: Objective 1: We have performed start-trap kinase assays to compare the processivity of SRPK2wt with SRPK2 mutants which residues H601, G661 or P663 were mutated to the corresponding side-chains in SRPK1. Our results demonstrated that when H601 of SRPK2 was mutated to leucine as in SRPK1, the processivity of SRPK2 increased back to about 8 sites, which is similar to that of SRPK1. This suggests that H601 plays a key role in determining the processivity of SRPK2. This result is published in our 2019 JBC article titled "Distinct mechanisms govern the phosphorylation of different SR protein splicing factors" as listed in part C. To provide the structural basis on how H601 affects the processivity of SRPK2, we have successfully solved the complex crystal structure of the active fragments of SRPK2 and SRSF1 (SRPK2deltaNS3:SRSF1_core) at 2.55 angstrom resolution. In contrast to our hypothesis that the presence of a histidine residue within the acidic docking groove may alter its electrostatic potential and lower the kinase processivity, our structure shows that H601 mediates an extensive network of interaction with other side-chains within the docking groove as well as the RS dipeptides of SRSF1 and thus may stabilize the substrate binding. This network of interaction is absent in the SRPK1:SRSF1 complex structure. To investigate how this network of interaction might affect the processive phosphorylation mechanism of SRSF1, we are now collaborating with Prof. Wang Yi of CUHK, who is an expert in molecular dynamic (MD) simulations, to study the dynamics of the RS domain at the docking groove of SRPK2 and SRPK1 respectively. The new crystal structure and the result of the MD simulations study will be reported in a peer-reviewed journal in the near future. Objective 2: We have successfully generated all the mutant constructs of SRPK2 and SRSF3 for the cross-linking studies. Initial attempts to cross-link full length His-SRPK2(C142S_K648C) mutant and various His-GST-SRSF3 mutants failed due to non-specific proteolytic cleavage of the SRPK2 protein during the experiment. To overcome the problem, we have generated a truncated construct of SRPK2(C142S_K647C) by deleting the non-conserved and flexible N-terminus and spacer domain (His-SRPK2deltaNS_C142S_K647C). This construct exhibits similar kinase activity as the full length kinase yet does not undergo non-specific degradation. However, extensive attempts to cross-link the SRPK2 and SRSF3 mutants using different cross-linkers and conditions remained unsuccessful due to the presence of non-specific cross-linked products. We are continually optimizing the cross-linking conditions. Although we have obtained diffractable crystals from the crystallization screening of SRPK2deltaNS3:SRSF3(1-137) complex, SDS-PAGE analysis of the dissolved crystals revealed that they only contain SRSF3(1-137). Analysis of the diffraction data revealed that there is probability of the presence of 5 or 6 molecules of SRSF3 in each asymmetric unit. Due to the uncertainty of the number of molecules in each asymmetric unit, phasing by the molecular replacement method using the programs Phaser and AMoRe failed to produce clear solution. We are planning to solve the phase problem using MAD by growing selenium-methionine labeled protein-crystals. Meanwhile, we are continually screening for SRPK2:SRSF3 complex crystals. Given the difficulties we have encountered, instead of focusing solely on the identification of the substrate docking motifs that are important for the directionality during phosphorylation of SRSF3, we also studied how the phosphoryl content of SRSF3 is being regulated. We demonstrated that despite the C-terminal RS domain of SRSF3 could be hyperphosphorylated by SRPK2 in vitro, SRSF3 remains hypophosphorylated at steady state in vivo. Through newly designed experiments, we showed that the hypophosphorylation state of SRSF3 was achieved by partial dephosphorylation of the RS domain by phosphatase after the release of SRSF3 from SRPK2. During the course of our investigation, we surprisingly discovered that the previously proposed N to C phosphorylation mechanism of SRSF3 was the result of an artifact caused by the use of Tris-glycine-SDS-PAGE gel, which failed to resolve the C-terminal bands that migrate faster than the 10 kDa protein standard marker. Tris-tricine SDS-PAGE analyses of our foot-printing assays revealed that the phosphorylation of SRSF3 by SRPK2 happens in a C to N direction instead. These new results were obtained after the project was closed, therefore a revision of objective could not be requested. Nonetheless, our new results have successfully elucidated the molecular mechanism of SRSF3 phosphorylation and they are reported in our 2019 JBC publication.

14122615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14122615.value: Serine-arginine (SR) proteins are essential splicing factors that can be classified into two subclasses based on the presence of one or two RNA recognition motif(s) (RRM(s)). All SR proteins contain a C-terminal arginine/serine-rich (RS) domain that undergoes multisite phosphorylation. Phosphorylation regulates the biological functions of SR proteins and therefore detailed studies of their phosphorylation mechanisms may provide insight into their differential biological roles. In this study, we have unveiled the molecular mechanisms of how two members, SRPK1 and SRPK2, of the SR protein kinase family phosphorylate SRSF1, a prototypic SR protein that contains two RRM, with different processivity. We also demonstrated how SRPK2 phosphorylates SRSF3 in a processive manner and proposed a mechanism on how SRSF3 phosphoryl content is maintained in vivo. The results of the study are described in the 2019 JBC publication titled "Distinct mechanisms govern the phosphorylation of different SR protein splicing factors" as listed in part C. In addition to the published results, we have solved the complex crystal structure of SRPK2deltaNS3:SRSF1_core and are currently performing MD simulations study to investigate how the difference of docking groove residue(s) affect the processive phosphorylation mechanisms of SRPK1 and SRPK2. This work will aid the design of SRPK2-specific inhibitor(s) as described in part 6.2 below and provide critical information on understanding the differential roles of the two SRPKs on SR protein phosphorylation.

14122615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14122615.value: Evidence is accumulating that SRPK2 and SRPK1 possess distinct biological functions during pre-mRNA splicing and the misregulation of their expressions result in different forms of cancer, suggesting that SRPKs may be potential targets for anti-cancer therapeutics. Our study has provided the molecular basis on how the two kinases, which kinase core domains are highly homologous, could phosphorylate their substrates in different manners using their slightly different docking grooves. The docking grooves of SRPKs are unique to this family and play critical role in substrate recognition and phosphorylation. Therefore the docking grooves are attractive targets for the development of SRPK inhibitors. In fact, our group has been developing a docking groove inhibitor and our results show that it could inhibit angiogenesis and metastasis of different cancer cells. Information provided by the current study could aid the development of SRPK1- and SRPK2- specific inhibitors for the treatment of different cancer types. Our publication is the first to report how different subclasses of SR proteins are being phosphorylated. The results suggest that there is no conserved mechanism to phosphorylate and maintain the phosphoryl content of SR proteins, thus there is a need to study the regulation of phosphorylation of each SR protein independently.

14122615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14122615.value: This project aimed to study how two closely related enzymes SRPK2 and SRPK1, differentially recognize and modify their substrates SRSF1 and SRSF3. These proteins play important role in the regulation of pre-mRNA splicing and subsequently gene expression and various cellular functions. Accumulating evidence shows that the normal activities of these proteins are critical to the wellness of human cells. Therefore the results from this project not only help scientists to understand how these proteins regulate gene expression and maintain the normal function of cells, but also provide information on how drugs can be developed to treat diseases like cancers that arise from the misregulation of these proteins.

14122715.value: GTP酶都源自同一個祖先蛋白，經過進化，繼而執行各種不同的生理功能。在 G-蛋白（異三聚體G-蛋白，小G蛋白，和非傳統 G蛋白）的三個主要群體中，非傳統G-蛋白可以通過其相對大的尺寸和單體性質區分。對非傳統G-蛋白的功能和調節機理的理解可帶來與GTP酶進化相關的重要資訊。YchF亞科是最後被發現的非傳統G蛋白，有關其功能資訊的資料非常有限。 YchF的同源基因可以在細菌和真核生物中找到，高度保守的特性說明瞭其起源古老。它們包括一個結合了GTP和ATP的G結構域和在翻譯因數中保守的TGS結構域。 我們先前已經從水稻中克隆了一個YchF蛋白（OsYchF1）並證明瞭它是一個在植物抗性和非生物脅逼中的負調節因數。我們也鑑別了幾個OsYchF1的互作夥伴蛋白，包括調節蛋白，以及蛋白翻譯系統和26S蛋白酶體的部件。 此外，我們通過X射線晶體學解構了OsYchF1的結構。基於現有的結構數據和互作夥伴蛋白的資訊，我們建議採用定點誘變來產生個不能與互作夥伴蛋白結合的突變OsYchF1蛋白。利用我們監測植物抗性和非生物脅迫反應的平臺，我們可就缺乏相互作用的突變蛋白在功能上的影響進行調查。因為OsYchF1與蛋白翻譯系統和26S蛋白酶體有相互作用，它可能在整個蛋白代謝中發揮調節作用。因此，我們進一步提出就表達原型OsYchF1蛋白和已失去與蛋白翻譯系統和26S蛋白酶體進行相互作用的突變OsYchF1蛋白的轉基因植物上，進行蛋白質譜比較。 這些研究策略的組合有助於認識這一神秘的GTP酶群。我們的具體研究目標是： （1）在OsYchF1蛋白中保守的表面殘基進行定點誘變； （2）分析突變OsYchF1蛋白與不同互作夥伴的結合能力的變化； （3）在植物抗性和非生物脅迫反應下，比較原型和突變OsYchF1蛋白的生理影響；和 （4） 在表達原型OsYchF1蛋白和已失去與蛋白翻譯系統和26S蛋白酶體進行相互作用的突變OsYchF1蛋白的轉基因植物上，進行蛋白質組學分析 。

14122715.label: Realisation of objectives
14122715.value: Due to the social unrest and COVID-19 pandemics, many of the planned experiments were facing severe delays. We have tried our best to complete the tasks despite all difficulties. Our results indicate OsYchF1 loves to interact with other proteins. It could bind to plant homologs of GAP1, FKBP12, DNJ1, ribosomal protein S7 (a component of 40S ribosomes), ribosomal protein L26 (a component of 60S ribosomes), and the non-ATPase subunit of the 26S proteasome. We employed site-directed mutagenesis to determine the residues that are essential to the binding. With similarity search of close homologs of OsYchF1 using Protein-BLAST. The alignment using thirty homologs was then further analyzed by the Consurf server with our OsYchF1 crystal structure taken into account. Highly conserved amino acid residues exposing at the molecular surface were subjected to mutagenesis. These residues were mutated to alanine to minimize possible effects on the overall protein structure. Finally, eleven OsYchF1 constructs with a total of 17 amino acids mutated were successfully generated. The mutated residues span all three structural domains of OsYchF1: G-domain, helical domain, and TGS domain. The mutated constructs were obtained by PCR mutagenesis with the original OsYchF1 clone via QuikChange method and mutations were confirmed with Sanger DNA sequencing. The mutated OsYchF1 constructs were subcloned into Mini-pRSETA-his SUMO vector to produce His-SUMO-OsYchF1 mutated proteins via bacterial systems. Most of the mutations on OsYchF1 cause loss of bindings to multiple interacting partners. We made use of this information to refine the structural model of OsYchF1. Combining the information on the residues required for binding, the previous crystallographic data by our group, we can build a high-confident docking model for the protein-protein interaction between OsYchF1 and OsGAP1. Since one particular OsYchF1 mutant (OsY104) exhibited a specific loss of binding to OsGAP1, it gives us a tool to perform functional studies. Based on our docking model and other data, we hypothesized that OsYchF1 is a negative regulator of abiotic stress tolerance and plant defense response and OsGAP1 interacts with OsYchF1 to inhibit its activities by activating the ATPase/GTPase activities of OsYchF1. We showed that while OsY104 lost its binding to OsGAP1, its ATPase/GTPase activities were retained but became independent of OsGAP1. By comparing ectopic expression of the native OsYchF1 and OsY104 mutant in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana, we demonstrated that the ability of binding to GAP1 homologs is important to suppress the negative functions of OsYchF1 on stress tolerance and plant defense responses. While OsYchF1 loves to interact with other proteins, it is also important to understand the physiological roles of these interacting partners. We, therefore, performed functional studies on two important regulators that are identified in the same interacting complex involving OsYchF1. We obtained the full-length clone of OsFKBP12, a rice homolog belonging to a subgroup of immunophilins. The family of immunophilins (including FKBP and cyclophilins) was first described as the receptor of an immunosuppressant drug, which was originally applied in clinical operations to prevent graft rejection in transplantation. FKBP proteins exist in all three domains of cellular organisms. FKBP proteins contain a conserved functional domain annotated with peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase (PPIase) activities (EC 5.2.1.8). This domain was thought to catalyze cis/trans isomerization of proline residues in a polypeptide. Such activities were largely proved in vitro and were thought to be linked up with protein folding and maturation. The functions of OsFKBP12 in plant defense and stress responses were characterized by ectopic expression in A. thaliana and inoculation with Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000. Ectopic expression of OsFKBP12 in transgenic lines resulted in more severe disease symptoms, including a larger extent of lesion, higher pathogen titer, and lower expression of defense-responsive genes, e.g. PR1 and PR2. Concerning abiotic stress, 10-day-old seedlings of transgenic lines expressing OsFKBP12 and the untransformed wild-type Col-0 were subjected to salt stress by being transferred onto MS medium supplemented with 150mM sodium chloride. Stress phenotype and chlorophyll content were recorded. Transgenic lines expressing OsFKBP12 exhibited higher sensitivity toward salt treatment compared to wild-type plants. The functional test results were reproducible after repeated tests. We have therefore shown that the functional roles of OsFKBP12 (one of the interacting partners of OsYchF1) are mimicking those of OsYchF1. DNJ1, the OsYchF1 interacting partner, belongs to the type I co-chaperone containing a J-domain (for binding to DnaK and promotes the ATPase activity of DnaK), glycine-phenylalanine (G/F)-rich region with four CXXCXGXG motifs (for enhancing substrate binding by DnaK), and the cysteine-rich (CR) domain (for binding to non-native proteins). It is the co-chaperone conferring substrate specificity for chaperone machinery to work on and thus plays important roles for coupling protein re-folding during stress conditions. There are over 200 J-domain protein-encoding genes in the soybean genome. Yet, only a few of them have been characterized. GmDNJ1 is a typical type-I HSP40 that is localized to both the cytoplasm and the nucleus. The co-chaperone activities of Gm DNJ1 were confirmed by in vitro luciferase refolding assays. A loss-of-function mutation with a stop codon introduced early in the coding sequence was constructed through KeyPoint® Breeding. Using this knockout mutation, we have functionally characterized GmDNJ1, which has a relatively high expression in both normal and stress conditions. Under heat treatments, increased leaf browning and reduced chlorophyll content in Gmdnj1 plants indicated that they are more sensitive to heat stress than the wild type. Besides, Gmdnj1 plants exhibited reduced fresh weights and dry weights compared to the wild type in both normal and heat stress conditions. We observed that there is a number of proteins more readily aggregated in Gmdnj1 mutant lines. In the aggregated protein profiles of the four tissue-treatment combinations, 262 proteins were found in total, sharing 726 GO terms describing diverse but important functions. The proper folding of these protein targets was somehow impacted due to the absence of a fully functional GmDNJ1.

14122715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14122715.value: We performed site-directed mutagenesis on OsYchF1 to successfully construct 11 mutants. Among those mutants, many of them caused the loss of interactions with multiple partners. For instance, only one mutant (OsY104) lost binding toward OsGAP1 specifically while another three mutants also lost binding toward other interacting partners. Making use of these mutants, we performed a structure-function analysis of OsYchF1 and OsGAP1 (Publication #1). Expression of OsY104 in transgenic Arabidopsis thaliana increased the sensitivity of the plants toward salt stress and aggravated the symptoms of bacterial pathogen attack, confirming that the negative function of OsYchF1 is negatively regulated by OsGAP1. Making use of all the site-directed mutagenesis and crystallographic data generated by our group, we are able to generate a docking model of OsYchF1 and OsGAP1 using the data-driven docking server HADDOCK 2.4. Molecular dynamics simulation suggested that the interaction is weak and reversible. Our findings, therefore, provide a working model on the potential regulatory mechanism mediated by a TGS domain, particularly in the class of GTPase of the OBG family. Besides regulated by OsGAP1 via protein-protein interaction, OsYchF1 could also play a central role in stress tolerance and plant defense response by interacting with other protein partners. In this project, we investigated two important regulators that interact with OsYchF1. The first protein partner studied is the plant homolog of FKBP12 (Publication #2). FKBPs (FK506-binding proteins) are members of a sub-family of immunophilins that are involved in human immune responses. Ectopic expression of a rice FKBP12 homolog (OsFKBP12) in transgenic A. thaliana mimicked the effects of expression OsYchF1, to increase sensitivity to salt stress and aggravate disease symptoms after bacterial pathogen inoculation. OsYchF1 also interacts with plant DNJ1 homologs. Since we obtained DNJ1 knockout mutants in soybean, for better agricultural application in the future, we made use of this system to investigate the function of DNJ1 homologs in crops (Publication #3). The soybean DNJ1 homolog GmDNJ1 belongs to the HSP40 sub-groups that are co-chaperones in nature. Gmdnj1-knockout mutants are more sensitive to heat stress, in terms of growth performance, chlorophyll contents, ROS accumulation, etc. The mutant lines accumulated more aggregated proteins in protein catabolism, sugar metabolism, and membrane transportation, in both roots and leaves, with or without heat treatments. Therefore, we provided evidence to prove that at crops like soybean, DNJ1 homologs play significant roles in the surveillance of misfolded proteins for refolding to maintain the full capacity of cellular functions.

14122715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14122715.value: Our finding suggests that the plant YchF1 family (e.g. OsYchF1) plays central roles in both abiotic stress and plant defense response, by interacting with other protein partners such as FKBP12 and DNJ1 homologs in plants which are also important regulators. The functions of OsYchF1 in rice is regulated by binding to ATP and GTP, whereas its ATPase and GTPase activities are controlled by the C2-protein regulator OsGAP1. A structural model of how OsYchF1 and OsGAP1 interact has been proposed based on structural and functional data generated using a site-directed mutagenesis approach. Since YchF1 is also binding to the translational machinery and ribosomes, we will follow up by investigating its roles in translational regulation. Such research will add important knowledge to the central dogma of gene expression. YchF1 is a negative regulator and GAP1 is a positive regulator of the abiotic stress response and plant defense response in plants. In terms of application, they are important candidate genes for genome editing in crop improvement programs in the future.

14122715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14122715.value: We have identified a novel unconventional G-protein OsYchF1 which functions to suppress abiotic stress and plant defense response under normal conditions. The function of this negative regulator is negatively regulated by a C2-domain protein OsGAP1. Using site-directed mutagenesis, we are able the dissect the structural-function relation of OsYchF1 and OsGAP1. We also generated a docking model of the OsYchF1 : OsGAP1 complex to dissect the molecular basis of their interactions. This finding provides important information to make optimal designs for future genome editing to improve stress tolerance and pathogen resistance. We also found that OsYchF1 has multiple interacting partners, including some important regulators, such as the FKBP12 and DNJ1 homologs. We demonstrated that plant FKBP12 homologs are also negative regulators of abiotic stress and plant defense response, mimicking the functions of plant YchF1 homologs. Using a mutant of DNJ1 in soybean, we showed that DNJ1 homologs in plants could be very critical in heat stress response. In summary, our research uncovered an important group of interacting regulators in plants that have not been thoroughly investigated.

14122815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14122815.value: Proteins are essential to the proper execution of diverse cellular activities, ranging from cell growth and survival to cell death. To maintain efficient cell functioning, cells, including neurons, devise multiple protein quality control mechanisms to eliminate misfolded and/or toxic proteins. As one of the principal cellular protein clearance pathways, the activity of the Ubiquitin-Proteasome system (UPS) is tightly regulated to ensure specific and efficient clearance of damaged and toxic proteins. Polyglutamine (polyQ) diseases, including Huntington’s Disease and several types of spinocerebellar ataxias, are caused by the genomic expansion of existing coding CAG triplet repeat sequences. This expansion leads to the production of misfolded polyQ domain-containing disease proteins and an accumulation of these misfolded mutant proteins, and causes neuronal dysfunction and cell death. A growing body of evidence demonstrates that the UPS plays a crucial role in the pathogenesis of polyQ disease. Ubiquitin (Ub) E3 protein ligases (E3), which label proteins for proteasomal clearance, are essential for catalyzing the transfer of the Ub tag to protein substrates. In addition to E3-mediated UPS protein degradation, we now know that E3 ligases also serve other cellular functions. The precursor RNA processing factor 19 (PRPF19) protein is an evolutionarily conserved U-box domain-containing E3 ligase. Recent research has unveiled the non-proteolytic regulatory role of PRPF19, which involves the control of spliceosome function through reversible non-proteolytic protein ubiquitination. We recently identified the Drosophila orthologue of PRPF19, prp19, as a novel genetic modifier of polyQ toxicity. At the biochemical level, Prp19/PRPF19 modulates expanded polyQ protein levels in both Drosophila and mammalian disease models. We further showed that PRPF19 promotes expanded polyQ protein ubiquitination and modulates expanded polyQ-mediated caspase cleavage in mammalian cells. Intriguingly, we found that a Prp19/PRPF19-interacting protein, exocyst complex protein 70 (Exo70/EXOC7), modulates expanded polyQ protein level and toxicity in an opposite manner to that of Prp19/PRPF19 in vitro and in vivo. Interestingly, EXOC7 antagonizes the effect of PRPF19. Our preliminary data suggest that Exo70/EXOC7 exerts, at least in part, its polyQ-modifying effect by regulating the function of Prp19/PRPF19. In the proposed work, we will 1) investigate the effect of Prp19/PRPF19 E3 activity on expanded polyQ protein homeostasis and toxicity, and 2) elucidate the role of Exo70/EXOC7 in the regulation of Prp19/PRPF19 E3 activity. This study will allow us to better define the role of protein ubiquitination in polyQ pathogenesis and understand how Prp19/PRPF19 E3 ligase activity can be regulated by its interacting partner Exo70/EXOC7. 蛋白質對於多種細胞活動的正確執行都至關重要，包括細胞生長，存活到死亡。 用以清除錯誤折疊和/或有毒蛋白的多種蛋白品質控制機制在保持包括神經元在內的細胞中高效的細胞功能起重要作用。 泛素 - 蛋白酶體系統（Ubiquitin-Proteasome system，UPS）是主要的細胞蛋白清除途徑之一，其活性嚴格調節，特異且高效地清除損傷蛋白和毒性蛋白。 聚谷氨醯胺（Polyglutamine，polyQ）疾病，包括亨廷頓氏病和幾種類型的脊髓小腦共濟失調症，皆由編碼的CAG三聯體重複序列的延伸所致。 此延伸導致含有錯誤折疊的polyQ結構域的疾病蛋白產生，這些錯誤折疊的突變蛋白累積導致神經元功能障礙和細胞死亡。 越來越多的證據表明UPS在polyQ疾病的發病機理中起關鍵作用。 泛素（Ubiquitin，Ub）E3連接酶可標記蛋白使其通過蛋白酶體途徑降解，另外也可催化泛素標記的蛋白底物轉移。 這項研究將使我們更好地確定蛋白泛素化在polyQ疾病發病機制中的作用，並瞭解E3連接酶的活性是如何進行調節的。

14122815.label: Major findings and research outcome
14122815.value: In this study, we showed that the E3 ligase pre-mRNA processing factor 19 (Prpf19) modulates expanded polyQ-induced neurodegeneration in both mammalian and Drosophila disease models. We further showed that Prpf19 promotes poly-ubiquitination of expanded polyQ protein as well as its reduction in levels in disease models. Our data further demonstrated that the nuclear compartment is essential for Prpf19 to execute its modulatory role in controlling expanded polyQ protein homeostasis. Intriguingly, we found that the exocyst complex protein 70 (Exo70/EXOC7) modulates expanded polyQ protein level and toxicity in an opposite manner to Prpf19. Our data suggest that Exo70/EXOC7 exerts, at least in part, its polyQ protein toxicity-modifying effect through regulating the E3 ligase function of Prpf19. In summary, this study allows us to better understand how the E3 ligase function of Prpf19 can be regulated by Exo70/EXOC7. In the context of polyQ disease pathogenesis, we showed that targeting Prpf19 function through Exoc7 overexpression resulted in abolished Prpf19’s ability to mitigate expanded polyQ protein toxicity. This highlights the importance of elucidating the complex protein-protein interaction networks of polyQ toxicity modulatory factors, particularly those that are involved in protein exocytosis.

14122815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14122815.value: We will continue to investigate whether the Exo70/EXOC7’s exocytosis function would be involved in its modulatory role of Prpf19. Another important direction of research is to investigate whether Exo70/EXOC7 exerts a direct effect on polyglutamine toxicity which is independent on Prpf19. These studies was conceived by our recent findings which unveiled that other proteins that are involved in exocyst’s function also demonstrate modulatory effects on polyglutamine toxicity. These proposed future studies will shed light on how the exocytosis process modulates polyQ protein toxicity.

14122815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14122815.value: Polyglutamine (polyQ) diseases, including Huntington’s Disease and several types of spinocerebellar ataxias, are caused by the genomic expansion of coding CAG trinucleotide sequences. This expansion leads to the production and accumulation of toxic polyQ domain-containing disease proteins, which causes multiple systems failure and eventually trigger nerve cells to commit programmed cell death. As one of the principal cellular protein clearance pathways, the activity of Ubiquitin-Proteasome system (UPS) is tightly regulated to ensure efficient clearance of damaged and toxic proteins. Emerging evidence demonstrates that UPS plays a crucial role in the pathogenesis of polyQ diseases. The ubiquitin (ub) E3 ligases are a group of enzyme to target damaged and toxic proteins for clearance. Our research identified Prpf19 as one such E3 ligases responsible for promoting poly-ubiquitination of toxic polyQ protein, a crucial step for UPS function. We further found that Prpf19 function is regulated by another protein Exo70/EXOC7. In addition to its well-known role in promoting the transport of different types of materials from one cellular compartment to another through a process terms exocytosis, our study discovered a new role of Exo70/EXOC7 in disease biology.

14200315.label: Project Objectives
