14200315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200315.value: 本項目旨在系統地學習電池儲能系統對於一次調頻的技術和經濟貢獻。我們將特別研究電池儲能系統的最優規劃和操作。 隨著可再生能源的普及，現代電網系統面臨前所未有的挑戰。為了維持電網系統的魯棒性和可靠性，電池儲能系統在全世界範圍內日益普及。截止2013年8月，美国已经安装了24GW的電網儲能系統，包括304MW電池。這個數目在未來幾年裡將再有大幅升高。例如，加州將在2020年前在洛杉磯地區安裝50MW儲能系統，而整個州將安裝1.3GW。在歐洲和亞洲也有類似的趨勢。截至2012年，日本NGK已經安裝了450MW納硫電池。 在電池儲能系統的諸多應用中，一次調頻是最俱有經濟價值的。這是因為電池系統有極快的反應速度，且比其他具有類似反應速度的一次調頻备用负荷要便宜。 然而，利用电池储能系统做一次调频的研究现仍处于初级阶段。现有工作主要基于仿真或实验。业界缺乏对此问题的基本理论认识。为解决此问题，本项目将著重研究電池系統在電網各層，在不同應用場景下的最佳規劃及操作，包括（1）單獨電池系統在一次調頻市場中利潤最大化的規劃及操作，（2）位於同一配电網中不同電池系統的最優協調，（3）在傳輸網中不同配電網上電池系統的相互協調。

14200315.label: Realisation of objectives
14200315.value: The project objectives have all been fulfilled satisfactorily. In particular, we have comprehensively studied the optimal planning and operation of battery energy storage systems (BESS) for primary frequency control provisioning in power systems. The project has led to publications in top venues. Regarding the first objective, we studied a two-level profit-maximizing strategy, including planning and control, for battery energy storage system (BESS) owners that participate in the primary frequency control market. Specifically, the optimal BESS control minimizes the operating cost by keeping the state of charge (SoC) in an optimal range. Through rigorous analysis, we proved that the optimal BESS control is a “state-invariant” strategy in the sense that the optimal SoC range does not vary with the state of the system. As such, the optimal control strategy can be computed offline once and for all with very low complexity. Regarding the BESS planning, we proved that the minimum operating cost is a decreasing convex function of the BESS energy capacity. This leads to the optimal BESS sizing that strikes a balance between the capital investment and operating cost. Regarding the second objective, we studied a battery aggregator that coordinates a number of distributed BESSs to provide primary frequency control service in the ancillary service market. In particular, we proposed a profit-maximizing BESS coordination strategy that is concerned with two operational phases, namely a frequency regulation phase and an SoC recovery phase. Regarding the frequency regulation phase, we minimized the regulation failure penalty by optimally coordinating the operation of multiple BESSs in response to local frequency deviations. The proposed coordination algorithm is “online optimal” in the sense that it does not require any knowledge of the future information, and yet achieves exactly the same optimal performance as if the entire future information is known. On the other hand, during idle periods, the BESSs shall recover their SoCs to a proper range to avoid regulation failure in the next frequency excursion event. We proposed an SoC recovery strategy that is not only optimal, but also state invariant and separable in the sense that the target SoC range of each BESS neither varies with its own SoC nor depends on the operation of other BESSs. As such, the target SoC ranges can be calculated once and for all, resulting in extremely low run-time complexity. Regarding the third objective, we studied the demand response management for profit maximizing energy loads in a electricity market that coordinates the energy supply in a power grid. We showed that the profit-maximizing demand response strategy can be obtained by solving a finite-horizon Markov decision process (MDP) problem. To tackle the high computational complexity, we proposed a dual approximate approach that transforms the MDP problem into a linear programing problem by exploiting the threshold structure of the optimal solution. The work not only maximizes the profit of the energy load, but also alleviates the supply-demand imbalance in the power grid, and even reduces the bills of other market participants. We also considered electric vehicles as a special type of BESS. We study an Internet of Electric Vehicles (IoEV) powered by heterogeneous charging facilities that are distributed in the power network. In particular, we take into account the state-of-the-art vehicle-to-grid (V2G) charging and renewable power generation technologies implemented in the charging stations, such that the charging stations differ from each other in their energy capacities, electricity prices, and service types. We formulated a joint routing and charging scheduling optimization problem for an IoEV network and proposed an approximate algorithm that can achieve affordable computational complexity in large-size IoEV networks.

14200315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200315.value: We found that for both single-BESS (Section C 8-3)and multi-BESS systems (Section C 8-8), the profit-maximizing BESS operation strategies are "state-invariant" strategies, in the sense that it is optimal to adjust the BESS SoC to a target range that is independent of the BESS's current state. When there are multiple BESSs, When there are multiple BESSs, our proof shows that the target SoC range of each BESS neither varies with its own SoC nor depends on the operation of other BESSs, although the BESSs are coupled in the grid system. This finding significantly reduces the complexity of online optimal BESS operation. We also found that in the case of a special type of energy storage device, namely electric vehicles, the optimal charging/discharging decision is also coupled with the EV routing decision. That is, the decision needs to be jointly optimized in the power grid and transportation network. The details are in Section C 8-4.

14200315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200315.value: In the future, we are going to study the application of machine learning in BESS optimization. Our preliminary work in Section C 8-9 and 9-5 demonstrated the effectiveness of reinforcement learning in solving hard optimal energy storage control problems. In our future work, we plan to design deep reinforcement learning methods for energy storage system optimization when the state and action spaces are large. We also plan to explore the use of deep walk to capture the correlation of power flow variables across a power network.

14200315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200315.value: While battery energy storage has a wide spectrum of applications, such as load leveling, peak shaving, price arbitrage, etc., the supply of PFC reserve has been identified as the application with the highest financial value. This project contributes to the fundamental and theoretical understanding of how BESS should be planned and operated to maximize its financial and technical benefits. We developed the optimal BESS planning and control mechanism for individual profit-seeking BESS owners and the optimal operating strategy that coordinates a number of BESSs. The project has led to 8 journal publications, 5 conference publications, and 1 book. 3 Ph.D. students are trained out of this project.

14200515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200515.value: Recently, the PI has formulated the cooperative output regulation problem for uncertain multi-agent systems and shown that the problem includes several cooperative control problems of uncertain multi-agent systems such as consensus, synchronization, and formation as special cases. A distributed internal model approach has been developed to solve the problem for linear multi-agent systems and a few classes of nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems. However, the solvability of the problem for nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems relies on the restrictive assumption that the communication graph of the system is static and connected for all time. In practice, due to the change of environment, or the addition and loss of communication links, communication topologies are usually time-varying. Thus, it is more interesting to study the cooperative output regulation problem for uncertain multi-agent systems under a switching network topology. In this project, we propose to study the cooperative stabilization problem for nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems by a switched feedback control law. The problem is extracted from the cooperative output regulation problem for nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems under a switching network topology. Thus an application of our main result will lead to the solution of the later problem which has been open for several years. It is known that the stability of a switched nonlinear system requires, among other things, that each subsystem admits a Lyapunov function that converges to the origin exponentially. Since the existing control techniques only rely on the existence of a Lyapunov function whose derivative is negative definite, we need to develop a specific technique for finding an exponentially convergent Lyapunov function. For this purpose, we will establish a change supply pair technique for exponentially input-to-state stable (exp-ISS) systems. Also, since a multi-agent system is always multi-input and multi-output (MIMO) and its control law is subject to switched communication constraints , we need to develop a block back-stepping technique for uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems via a distributed switched feedback control law. These techniques will not only be effective in handling the problem in this project, but also have potential to handle other relevant control problems in uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems. The success of this project will break a bottleneck in the cooperative control problems for nonlinear multi-agent systems. Moreover, the applications of our main result will lead to the solution of such problems as consensus, synchronization, and formation of complex nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems in a more practical setting. 最近, 本项目主持人描述了关于不确定多智能体系统的协同输出调节问题并证明了趋同， 同步和编队等问题是协同输出调节问题的特例。在多智能体系统的通讯限制是时不变的假定下， 本项目主持人并提出了分布式内模方法以求解线性不确定多智能体系统及若干类非线性不确定多智能体系统的协同输出调节问题。然而，在实际应用中, 多智能体系统的通讯限制一般是时变的。因此，本项目将进而研究通讯限制为切换网络时的不确定多智能体系统的协同输出调节问题。为此目的， 我们先研究一个基于切换控制的非线性不确定多智能体系统的分布式全局镇定问题。然后证明该问题的解决将导致通讯限制为切换网络时的不确定多智能体系统的协同输出调节问题的解决。必须指出，一个切换系统的稳定性通常要求每个子系统都拥有一个指数收敛的李雅普若夫函数。因此切换系统的稳定性的判据要远比普通系统的稳定性的判据严苛。所以本项目的一大挑战是如何为一个非线性不确定系统寻找一个指数收敛的李雅普若夫函数。本项目的另一挑战是是如何对一个多输入，多输出非线性不确定系统用递归方法设计控制器。 这两样技术不仅将有效解决本项目的问题， 而且也能应用于求解其他多输入，多输出非线性不确定系统的控制问题。 本项目的成功实施将突破非线性多智能体系统协同控制的一个瓶颈。 本项目的主要结果可直接应用于解决通讯限制为切换网络时的非线性不确定多智能体系统的趋同， 同步和编队等问题。

14200515.label: Realisation of objectives
14200515.value: The three original projects are as follows: 1. Develop an approach to handling the cooperative stabilization problem for a class of nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems by a distributed switched feedback control law. 2. Apply the approach to solving the cooperative robust output regulation problem for a few classes of nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems under the switching network topology. 3. Evaluate and validate the general results by specific applications such as the synchronization of multiple Lorenz systems with harmonic systems subject to switching network topology. All three objectives have been successfully achieved. The research has led to eight journal papers, and six conference papers. Three Phd students have been trained through conducting this project and one Phd student has got his PhD degree. The project has also led to collaboration with Prof. Yi Dong of Nanjing University of Science and Technology, and Prof. Jie Chen of Tongji University. Details are referred to Section 6 and Part C.

14200515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200515.value: We have fully accomplished all three objectives. The major findings are summarized as follows: 1. We have solved the cooperative global stabilization problem for nonlinear multi-agent systems in output feedback form with any relative degree subject to directed switching networks via the multiple Lyapunov functions and average dwell time method. We have further shown that the cooperative global robust output regulation problem for nonlinear systems in output feedback form can be converted to the cooperative global stabilization problem via the distributed internal model design. These results have been reported in the journal paper No. 1. 2. We have studied the leaderless and leader-following consensus problems for discrete-time linear multi-agent systems subject to jointly connected switching networks. The problem is solved by converting the problem to the stabilization problem for a class of linear switching systems. The main findings are summarized journal paper No. 8. We have also solved the cooperative output regulation problem of discrete-time linear multi-agent systems by the adaptive distributed observer approach. See journal paper No. 5. 3. We have studied the cooperative global robust output regulation problem for a class of heterogeneous second-order nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems with arbitrarily large uncertainty and arbitrarily large exogenous signals. The result has been reported in journal paper No. 4. 4. Most results on various control problems of multi-agent systems assume that the communication graph satisfies certain connectivity assumption. This assumption is not practical in many applications such as rendezvous, and flocking. We have studied the leader-following rendezvous with connectivity preservation problem for a few classes of mulit-agent systems. The main results are published in conference papers No. 1 and No. 3. 5. Recently, the event-triggered control approach gains popularity because it can more efficiently implement a continuous-time control law in a digital platform than the sampled-data control law. For this reason, we have enlarged the scope of the investigation of our research to consider the event-triggered control for both linear and nonlinear control systems. The main findings are reported in journal papers No. 5 to No. 7. 6. We have also applied our theoretical results to two practical problems, namely, the leader-following adaptive consensus of multiple uncertain rigid body systems over jointly connected networks, and the trajectory tracking and disturbance rejection for quadrotor helicopter. The main findings are reported in conference papers No. 5 and No. 6, respectively. Other relevant work supported by this project includes in conference papers No. 1, No. 2 and No. 4.

14200515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200515.value: Two expansions of the project are summarized as follows: 1. This project has addressed the event-triggered cooperative control of multi- agent systems over static networks. The extension of this project to switching networks is on-going. 2. In this project, we have established a distributed observer for a known leader system. It is more interesting and more practical to establish a distributed observer for an unknown leader system. This generalization is under way.

14200515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200515.value: Many complex engineering tasks are performed by coordinating the efforts of a group of individual systems. Typical examples include the coordination of mobile robots, formation of unmanned flight vehicles, mobile sensor area coverage, containment control of moving bodies, etc. These engineering applications gave rise to the exciting research topic: cooperative control of multi-agent systems. However, so far most rely on the restrictive assumption that the communication graph of the system or, what is the same, the network topology is static and connected for all time. In practice, due to the change of environment, or the addition and loss of communication links, communication topologies are time-varying. Thus, it is imperative to study the cooperative control problem for uncertain multi-agent systems under a switching network topology. In this project, we have proposed to a novel paradigm to handle the cooperative stabilization problem for nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems by a distributed switched feedback control law. The paradigm has successfully accomplished all the objectives of this project. The success of this project has not only significantly advanced control techniques for MIMO nonlinear uncertain systems, but also enhanced our capability to handle various cooperative control problems for practical nonlinear multi-agent systems

14200615.label: Project Objectives
14200615.value: The overall objective of this project is to reveal the working mechanism of peroxide oxidation catalysis in lithium-oxygen batteries and to develop rational catalyst design to improve the charging efficiency and reversibility of lithium-oxygen batteries. The technical objectives that lead to our overall objective are follows: We will investigate the influences of discharge/charge states, operating conditions, and electrolyte properties on the electrochemical efficacy and chemical side-effects of electrocatalysts in lithium-oxygen batteries, which is essential for understanding peroxide oxidation catalysis and identifying the source of disagreement regarding the efficacy of electrocatalysts for lithium-oxygen charging. We will examine three working hypotheses in explaining how electrocatalysts promote the oxidation of solid lithium peroxide. Specifically, we will (i) investigate the role of soluble species in assisting peroxide oxidation catalysis by examining catalyst effects in solid state lithium-oxygen cells, where no (or limited) soluble species are available, (ii) verify the existence and identify the chemical nature of soluble species generated during lithium-oxygen charging in liquid electrolytes and (iii) correlate the lithium-oxygen charging activity with electrolyte oxidation stability, to examine whether the enhancement observed on charging is induced by impurities from electrolyte decomposition. We will develop in situ electrochemical and in situ spectro-electrochemical characterization techniques to examine solids/liquids/gases involved in lithium-oxygen reactions and establish a comprehensive understanding of chemical processes occurring during the cycling of lithium-oxygen batteries. We will apply the fundamental insights generated by this project to identifying the key catalyst properties required for improving lithium-oxygen charging efficiency and reversibility, which will be evaluated by quantitative electron/gas ratio, evolution of chemical/electrochemical reaction products, in addition to the apparent cycle life of the batteries.

14200615.label: Realisation of objectives
14200615.value: To probe the influences of discharge/charge states, operating conditions, and electrolyte properties on the electrochemical efficacy and chemical side-effects of electrocatalysts towards lithium-oxygen recharge, we used ruthenium (Ru) supported on Vulcan Carbon (Ru/VC) as a model electrode to examine the charging overpotential comparing with the pure carbon (VC) electrode under (a) different discharge capacity of 70 – 1000 mAh per gram carbon (mAh/gC), (b) different recharge rate of 20 – 800 mA/gC, and (c) different solvents with varying donicity (or donor number (DN)) i.e. glyme-based solvent tetraglyme (TEGDME, DN = 16.6)/monoglyme (DME, DN = 24)) and high donicity i.e. 1-methylimidazole (Me-Im, DN = 47). Our results demonstrate that the reduced overpotential associated with Ru obtained at low capacity (ΔE = 700 mV at 70 mAh/gC) is larger than that achieved under higher capacity (ΔE = 500 mV at 600 mAh/gC). The efficacy of catalyst is not influenced by the charging rate. Furthermore, the reduced overpotential obtained in high DN solvent (ΔE = 200 mV in Me-Im) is significantly lower than that achieved using low DN solvent (ΔE = 500 mV in TEGDME) with the oxygen release as the major gas evolution evidence by online electrochemical mass spectrometry (OEMS). These results support our hypothesis that apparent efficacy of the lithium-oxygen recharge electrocatalysis is influenced by discharge/charge states and electrolyte properties. To probe the influence of discharge/charge states and operating conditions on the chemical side-effects, we investigate the influence of charging rate ranging from 500 – 2000 mA/gC on the side reaction of the Li-O2 cells via online electrochemical mass spectrometry (OEMS). Interestingly, the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) efficiency of the Li-O2 cell increased from 500 mA/g (OER/ORR = 0.56) to 2000 mA/g (OER/ORR =0.87). In addition, the parasitic CO2 evolution rate of the Li-O2 cell decreased from 500 mA/g (OER/ORR = 0.09) to 2000 mA/g (OER/ORR =0.04). These observations show that charging Li-O2 cells at higher rate improves the O2-evolution rate and reduces parasitic reactions. To examine the three reported hypotheses for the working mechanism of catalyst and elucidate the role of soluble species (i.e. charging intermediate/electrolyte decomposition species/impurities) in enabling the lithium-oxygen recharge catalysis, we examined the role of soluble species in an all solid-state lithium-oxygen cell where no soluble species are available. By combining the OEMS technique, we revealed that the Ru catalyst reduces the overpotential of the Li2O2-oxidation by ~ 500 mV over the entire charge capacity compared with the pure VC electrode with even higher O2 evolution efficiency (87.2% for Ru+VC compared with 65% for pure VC). This shows that the presence of Ru catalyst indeed promotes the decomposition of the solid Li2O2 without the need of soluble intermediates. This result supports our hypothesis that soluble species are not required for lithium-oxygen recharge catalysis. To verify the existence soluble intermediate species (i.e. LiO2) generated during lithium-oxygen charging in liquid electrolytes, we developed thin-film rotating ring disk electrode (RRDE) technique to investigate the LiO2-generation behavior in four model solvents that exhibit distinct LiO2(sol)-stabilizing ability including two high-donicity solvents, Me-Im (DN = 47) / dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO, DN = 29.8) and two low-donicity solvents, tetraglyme (DN = 16.6) / diglyme (DG, DN = 19.5). We revealed that soluble species LiO2 were generated during Li2O2 oxidation and this process is promoted in high-DN solvents. We further developed operando UV-Vis spectroscopy platform and in-house online electrochemical mass spectroscopy (OEMS) to examine the solid/liquid/gas interfaces involved in the Li-O2 reactions. In discharge mode, only a pressure sensor is connected with the cell. They are isolated from the atmosphere by ball valves and purged with Oxygen to 1.1 bar. Then the cell is discharged and the pressure reduction of oxygen is monitored continuously. In charge mode, Argon is introduced continuously via a narrow tube into the head space where gas evolved on the cathode during charge is mixed with Argon before being collected from another tube by the mass spectroscopy. The flow rate is regulated by a mass flow controller to 1 ml/min while the pressure is monitored by a pressure sensor for reference. We coupled OEMS with scanning electron microcopy (SEM), and potentiostatic intermittent titration technique (PITT) technique to investigate the Li2O2-oxidaiton behavior. By in-situ probing the gas evolved upon charging via OEMS, low O2 evolution efficiency (65%) with CO2 evolution over the entire charging process was observed in high donicity Me-Im. In contrast, in low donicity solvent TEGDME, the O2 evolution efficiency was 70% with minor CO2 evolving at the end of charging with the potential beyond than 4.5 V versus Li. By SEM technique, porous/network morphology was observed upon charging Li2O2-prefilled electrode in high donicity DMSO/Me-Im, while gradually shrinking particles without newly formed structure was observed in TEGDME. In PITT, two characteristic mountain peaks with different charging potential were observed in high donicity DMSO/Me-Im, while only one peak was observed in TEGDME/DG which is attributed to the oxidation of original Li2O2. These observations are consistent with the findings obtained with RRDE, confirming that soluble intermediate LiO2 was preferentially generated in high donicity solvent during charging process. Based on these findings, we establish that the role of the solid catalyst for Li2O2-oxidation is to reduce the energy of the reaction intermediate states such as Li2-xO2 by forming a stable intermediate state i.e. Li2-xO2(solid)-Ru, from which to decrease the overpotential needed for Li-extraction from Li2O2. The Ru surfaces can be partially oxidized by the lithium-deficient Li2O2 (or Li2-xO2), forming Li2-xO2(solid)-Ru at the interface. This is supported by the appearance of RuO2-like oxidation state in 50% of charging capacity in Ru L edge spectrum (surface region) and negligible change in the Ru K edge (bulk) upon entire charging. Based on our hypothesis, the key governing factor for non-aqueous OER activity lies in catalyst’s ability to interact/stabilize the solid reaction intermediates, this offers critical insights into the OER catalyst design for Li-O2 batteries. In addition, we revealed that applying soluble catalyst (or redox mediator) not only reduces the charge overpotential of Li-O2 batteries, but also reduces the charging side reactions. We show that by applying soluble catalyst, LiBr, we successfully reduced the charge potential of Li-O2 batteries from average 4.0 V to average 3.6 V. In addition, we use the in-house developed OEMS to study the gas evolution and electron/gas ration and revealed the soluble catalyst was able to improve both the charge voltage efficiency and the chemical stability of the Li-O2 cells as evidenced from the significantly reduced H2/CO evolution and increased O2 evolution.

14200615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200615.value: We resolved the long-debated peroxide oxidation catalysis and developed rational catalyst design to improve the recharge efficiency and reversibility of lithium-oxygen batteries. The galvanostatic charging results from the systematically defined operation condition show that the efficacy of the lithium-oxygen recharge electrocatalysis is influenced by discharge capacity and electrolyte property. We show that catalyst can reduce the overpotential for Li2O2-oxidation in solid-state cell where soluble species are not available and with oxygen release as the major gas evolution. This result unambiguously demonstrates that solid catalyst can promote Li2O2-oxidation kinetics without the help of soluble species which suggests soluble species are not required for lithium-oxygen recharge electrocatalysis. The partial oxidation on the surface of Ru observed in Ru L-edge and K-edge spectrum indicates the formation of strong bonding between the surface of Ru catalyst and the reaction intermediate (i.e. Li2-xO2). Based on our findings, we proposed the role of the solid catalyst for Li2O2-oxidation is to reduce the energy of the reaction intermediate states such as Li2-xO2 by forming a stable intermediate state i.e. Li2-xO2(solid)-Ru, from which to decrease the overpotential needed for Li-extraction from Li2O2. Catalyst with strong ability to stabilize or form stable bonding with the reaction intermediates will show strong OER activity. This understanding provides rational design strategy for Li-O2 OER catalysis. We developed operando UV-Vis spectroscopy platform and in-house online electrochemical mass spectroscopy (OEMS) to examine the solid/liquid/gas interfaces involved in the Li-O2 reactions, which lay critical foundation for future mechanistic understanding for metla-O2 and metal-air batteries. We successfully identified effective soluble catalyst (or redox mediator) to simultaneously improve charging efficiency and reduce charging side reactions, opening promising direction to develop efficient and stable Li-O2 batteries.

14200615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200615.value: Based on the findings developed in this project, we believe that developing soluble catalyst that simultaneously improve charging efficiency and reduce charging side reaction is an important direction. Therefore, it is important to (1) understand the underlying mechanism for the reduced charging side reaction associated with soluble catalyst; (2) develop quantitative metrics and methodologies to evaluate and describe the electrochemical and chemical effectiveness of soluble catalyst for Li-O2 charging, from which to establish the structure-performance relationship between soluble catalyst and charging stability; and (3) develop dual-soluble catalyst for both discharge and charge reactions and control the Li2O2 formation location to be away from carbon electrode. It is also important to apply the in situ electrochemical and in situ spectro-electrochemical characterization techniques developed in this project to probe the reaction mechanisms and side reactions of cells using soluble catalyst. Using quantitative electrochemical and spectroscopic investigations to understand the effects, working mechanism and degradation mechanism of soluble catalyst during Li-O2 cycling. This will help us to develop structure-effectiveness relationship of soluble catalyst, which facilitates the identification of key soluble catalyst properties required for improving the charging efficiency and reversibility of Li-O2 batteries.

14200615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200615.value: Rechargeable lithium-oxygen batteries have received extraordinary research attention and been considered one of the most promising candidates for next-generation energy storage systems owing to their potential to provide gravimetric energy 3–5 times that of conventional lithium-ion batteries. However, the lithium-oxygen technology has been suffering from poor cycle life (< 100 cycles), low rate capability (< 1 mA cm-2) and poor round-trip efficiency (65–70%). These technological challenges are intimately connected to the high OER overpotential (> 1 V) which results in large energy loss and high instability for cell components. Rational catalyst design for enhancing OER has been hindered due to large discrepancies in the efficacy and working mechanism of solid catalysts in decomposing solid Li2O2. Resolving these discrepancies and in-depth understanding the working mechanism of OER electrocatalysis is crucial to address these technological challenges. This project provides mechanistic insights into how solid products decompose and how electrocatalysts promote reaction kinetics upon recharge. These findings provide critical insights into rational catalyst design to improve the recharge efficiency and reversibility of lithium-oxygen batteries.

14200915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200915.value: Understanding hand-drawn sketches is an important step in real-world applications, especially when touch-based portable devices are so widely available nowadays. If machines can better understand the users’ hand-drawing, the user interface can be more natural and intuitive. In other words, sketch analysis is crucial to human-computer interaction. For instance, sketch-based image searching can be more accurate and effective with the better understanding of user sketches. However, semantic understanding of sketches is very challenging as strokes can be very sketchy. While human can intelligently understand that broken strokes or strokes repeatedly drawn are semantically referring to the same line (semantic line), machines lack of such intelligence. Previous works only rely on the proximity and the continuity among strokes in grouping strokes into a semantic line. They do not work in general, unfortunately. In this project, we propose a computational method to analyze the middle-level semantics of hand-drawn sketches. It mimics the gestalt phenomena of human visual perception. Psychologists discover that the gestalt phenomena which describe how humans perceive gestalts (forms) instead of unrelated elements from the visual content. For instance, humans can unconsciously recognize a continuous sequence of dashes as suggesting a line, instead of multiple unrelated line segments. We propose to also model the gestalt law of closure in forming stroke gestalt. This gestalt phenomenon is never utilized in early works. We believe that, by taking into account of this gestalt phenomenon, the computational method can more accurately analyze the semantics of hand-drawn sketches. One major challenge of the project is how to quantify the gestalt phenomena. Existing studies in psychology are mostly qualitative. Besides, we need a computational framework that can simultaneously take into account of complex interaction of multiple gestalt phenomena including closure, proximity, and continuity. By solving these challenges, we believe the outcome (the knowledge, publications, and algorithms) from the proposed project should motivate further study along the direction of sketch analysis in human-computer interaction. Besides, the developed algorithms should be directly applicable to the modern app industry for developing portable devices and smartphones apps with a more intuitive and natural user interface. Via the technology transfer, the proposed method shall provide a technological niche to the app industry in Hong Kong. 隨著觸控便捷式設備的廣泛普及，手繪草稿的語義理解也成為了現實世界應用中的重要一環。如果機器能夠更好地理解用戶的手繪草稿，用戶界面設計就可以更加自然與直接。所以，手繪草稿的理解與分析實為人機交互的關鍵點之一。舉例來說，如果機器可以更好地理解用戶手繪草稿的話，那麼基于手繪草稿的圖像檢索技術與三維模型重建技術將更加準確與有效。但是手繪草稿中的線條可能非常雜亂，這就使得手繪草稿的語義理解變得極為困難。儘管人類可以智能地將多筆雜亂的線條理解為同一筆實際的線條（語義線條），機器卻缺少這種人工智能。為了理解哪些雜亂線條實則為同一語義線條，以往的方法一般會通過分析線條之間的鄰近性與連續性來將線條分組。但是當用戶不擅長繪畫的時候，這種方法往往不能得到很好的分組結果。 在這個項目中，我們提出了一個分析手繪草稿的中層語義的計算方法。我們的方法模擬了人類視覺感知中的格式塔現象。根據心理學家發現的格式塔現象，人類可以從多個視覺元素中感知到其內在聯繫。例如，人類會無意識地將一系列連續的點識別為一條虛線，而不是將其看成多個相互無關聯的點。同樣，我們對格式塔現象建模，并將其應用于手繪草稿的線條分組。格式塔現象從未被用于以往的方法中。我們相信，通過分析格式塔現象，我們可以更加準確地進行手繪草稿的語義分析。 這個項目最大的困難在于如何量化格式塔現象，因為現有的心理學研究大多為定性研究而并定量研究。同時，格式塔現象包括多個法則，如鄰近性法則、連續性法則、閉合性法則等。我們需要一個能夠同時處理多個格式塔法則之間的相互影響的計算框架。在解決了這些困難之后，我們相信這一項目的成果（知識產權、論文、算法等）能夠激發人機交互領域手繪草稿分析這一方向的更多研究。此外，我們開發的算法應能直接應用于移動設備應用產業中，為開發移動設備應用提供更為自然與直接的用戶界面。通過技術轉讓，我們的方法將為香港的移動設備應用產業提供技術定位。

14200915.label: Realisation of objectives
14200915.value: The ultimate goal of this project is to better understand the semantic meaning of the hand-drawn sketches. Unlike the precise engineering drawing (e.g. CAD/CAM drawing), hand-drawn strokes may be carelessly or stylishly laid, and boundaries may not be always close. The drawing could also be rough and sketchy. A semantically meaningful stroke may be broken into multiple strokes and they even overlap with each other. Traditional approaches group them mainly based on the proximity and the orientation continuity. These two cues are traditional gestalt laws being used. However, such approaches usually result in incorrect interpretation. In this project, we propose to design and develop computational method that also takes into account of the closure awareness. That is, the semantic meaning or intention of the strokes is not only accounted by proximity and continuity gestalts, but also influenced by the region (closure) in which the strokes depicting. We found that the proximity and continuity is meaningful in the relative scale to the enclosing region (closure). With this notion, we developed a novel closure-aware stroke analysis framework. Since the interpretation of region is influenced by the interpretation of enclosing strokes and vice versa, we solve this chicken-or-the-egg problem with a cyclic refinement approach. Starting from the initial interpretation of semantic strokes and semantic regions, we adjust the grouping of strokes to optimize an objective function, that accounts for the region completeness, region independence, closure-aware proximity, and closure-aware continuity. The proposed framework can effectively group disjoint strokes into a semantically meaningful stroke with respect to the depicting regions. This allows us to successfully interpret strokes that geometrically the same, but semantically different. We are the first to propose such notion and published the finding in [J01]. The work has been well recognized by the research community, and several following research works are based on our finding. Our first attempt based on the above framework has a significant drawback as it assumes the input must be vector. Vector input simplifies the problem, as each stroke is unambiguously identified. In real world applications, the ability to handle raster image is crucial as users can simply shoot a photo of sketch. In such scenario, there may be unavoidable difficulties in distinguishing each individual stroke. In the second attempt, we adopted the convolutional neural networks (CNN) for handling raster images, due to its demonstrated effectiveness in solving many other real-world problems based on image input. We have designed models to group multiple disjoint strokes into a semantic stroke. But the results are unsatisfactory. Although the neural networks can simplify the sketches, it is not really able to take into account of the closure. Our resultant neural networks can only utilize the local proximity and continuity gestalts, instead of the relative ones. We believe that the local nature of CNN is not very effective in recognizing forms in a global scale. The “blackbox” nature of neural networks makes it very difficult to identify the cause of inability of utilizing the closure gestalt. This is especially true when a single neural network is adopted. In the third attempt, we adopted a divide-and-conquer approach. Instead of solving this gestalt analysis task with a single neural network, we divide the problem into multiple subtasks, and solve each of them with deep learning. We still prefer CNN because its ability in handling noisy/unstable input. The same cyclic refinement framework used in the first attempt is preserved. The major difference is that the identifications of strokes and regions are based on the neural networks. A major bottleneck we faced is the accurate identification of strokes. When two strokes are close to each other, it is difficult to tell whether they are intersecting each other or just touching each other. Such ambiguity is very common in raster image of sketches, especially at the junctions. We proposed a novel CNN approach to decompose the image blocks at junctions into multiple layers, with each layer holding a single stroke. We train the neural networks to restrict the decomposition to always decompose any complex junction into layers of single continuous stroke. This is a novel approach in the area of machine learning. After multiple times of failure, we have successfully trained a CNN to achieve the goal. The major difficulty lies on the carefully designed training procedure. This work is recently accepted for publication in Computer Graphics Forum [J05]. Another subtask is to identify regions. However, regions are usually covered with pattern laid by users to enrich the drawing. An extreme case is manga/comic. To accurately identify regions, we have to first remove the interfering patterns. While human can easily distinguish pattern from outline, machine cannot easily perform that. Although such problem has been tackled by early researchers using multiple image filtering approaches, none of previous work can effectively remove arbitrary patterns, due to the wide variety of patterns used. We are the first to propose to design and develop CNN-based method to remove the arbitrary interfering pattern. Instead of the manual labeling in the traditional supervised training, we are able to synthesize training data for pattern-removal purpose. Our resultant network can remove arbitrary patterns even the pattern never appears in our training data. The work is published in the most prestigious computer graphics journal, ACM Transactions on Graphics, and orally presented in the largest computer graphics conference ACM SIGGRAPH 2017 in Los Angeles. In 2018, a Japanese software company has adopted our technology in their popular software product, Clip Studio Paint, a software dedicated for manga production. With these CNN identified regions and strokes, we can accurately identify individual regions and strokes, which can then be fed to the cyclic refinement framework for semantic interpretation. To evaluate our framework, we have conducted multiple user study at the final stages. Through the user study, we are able to evaluate the reliability and accuracy of the proposed framework. The collected data from user feedback is also used to fine tune the parameters of the cyclic refinement framework. For example, the user data can be used to tune the parameters in multiple terms in the objective function to suit different types of sketches, in order to achieve the best results.

14200915.label: Major findings and research outcome
14200915.value: 1. Traditional approach relies on absolute proximity and continuity for grouping, but we show that proximity and continuity are in relative sense, and hence fail most existing stroke grouping methods. We found that the proximity and continuity gestalts are actually relative to the scale of the enclosing regions (i.e. closure). With this, we are able to formulate the determination of semantic strokes and semantic regions and as the result of a complex interaction between multiple gestalt principles including closure, proximity, and continuity. This approach significantly improves the understanding of rough sketches. Our result is published in the most prestigious computer graphics conference, ACM SIGGRAPH Asia and simultaneously published in the journal ACM Transactions on Graphics [J01] . 2. We extend this semantic analysis to motion gestalts. A sequence of sketches can be better understood if we are able to determine the temporal correspondence (i.e. gestalt in time domain). Existing methods only rely on the appearance of the drawing content and easily fail due to the abrupt changes of appearance over time. We propose to formulate this correspondence determination problem as a network flow problem, and solve this problem by optimization. Satisfactory results are obtained. To demonstrate its effectiveness, we applied the method to the region correspondence determination problem in cartoon. The result is also presented in the most prestigious conference ACM SIGGRAPH and published in the journal ACM Transactions on Graphics [J02] . 3. To accurately identify individual strokes in raster images, we proposed and developed a novel convolutional neural networks to resolve the ambiguity at the junction of strokes. It decomposes strokes at the intersecting junction into multiple layers. Each layer contains only a single continuous stroke. The work is accepted for publication in Computer Graphics Forum [J05] and orally presented in Pacific Graphics 2019. 4. To identify the semantic regions, we have to first remove the interfering patterns usually laid by users. We proposed a texture analysis based method to segment regions. The work is published in Computational Visual Media [J03]. However, the stability of the method is highly sensitive to the quality of input images and the pattern being laid. Hence, we proposed a deep learning method to remove interfering pattern. This learning-based approach can stably remove arbitrary interfering pattern, even the patterns do not exist in our training data. The work is published in ACM Transactions on Graphics [J04] and presented in ACM SIGGRAPH 2017 at Los Angeles.

14200915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14200915.value: Further development: In this project, we attempted to analyze the semantic meaning of sketches based on the awareness of closure. This results in more reliable interpretation of semantic meaning of the drawing. Currently, our approach targets the mid-level semantic meaning. It does not account for the high-level semantic meaning, i.e. the recognition of objects/scenes being drawn. The natural step to proceed forward is to incorporate both high-level and mid-level semantic analysis and their mutual influencing. Course of action: With the success of object classification achieved by modern deep learning methodology, we plan to utilize the convolutional neural networks in high-level object/scene recognition. We believe an integrated learning framework of both high-level and mid-level can push forward the semantic analysis of drawing, and we are currently looking into this direction.

14200915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200915.value: With touch-based display and camera being equipped on almost every smartphone today, sketching and photo shooting of drawing becomes a natural means of communication. However, existing computational methodology may still not reach the level of accurate interpretation of arbitrary user drawing, due to the sketchiness and ambiguity of user sketches. This project serves as a step forward to better understand the semantic meaning of user drawing (both entered via the touch screen and acquired via the camera). The developed method can directly be applied on interpretation of user drawing via the touch screen, as well as the captured drawing from the camera. We have demonstrated the semantic analysis is useful in sketch simplification and the vectorization of user drawing.

14201015.label: Project Objectives
14201015.value: Objective 1. Assuming IID components, we compare the component reliability characteristics based on system lifetimes from multiple data sources. 1.1 Develop parametric and nonparametric testing procedures to test the homogeneity of the components in two different systems. 1.2 Study and compare the power properties of the proposed testing procedures. 1.3 Develop statistical procedures for ranking and selection of the component lifetimes. 1.4 Extend the test of homogeneity of component lifetimes and the ranking and selection procedures to K-system situation. Objective 2. Assuming dependent components, develop statistical inference for the component lifetime distributions based on system lifetime data using copulas and multivariate distributions. 2.1 Develop novel estimation methods for the parameters in parametric models. 2.2 Study the properties of these estimation methods and apply them in statistical inference. 2.3 Study the non-identifiability issue and incorporate the uncertainties of the dependence structure by using Bayesian methods. 2.4 Compare the merits of using copulas and multivariate distributions. Objective 3. For IID components situations, develop statistical inference for censored life-testing experiments and investigate the optimal censoring scheme of the experiments 3.1 Develop point and interval estimation methods, including the use of the EM-algorithm, based on Type-I and Type-II progressively censored data. 3.2 Study the performance of these estimation methods. 3.3 Derive the optimal censoring scheme for censored experiments based exact and asymptotic methods. 3.4 Develop computational algorithm to obtain the optimal censoring schemes and study their performance under small sample sizes.

14201015.label: Realisation of objectives
14201015.value: We have suggested to use the goodness of fit tests to compare the non-parametric and parametric estimates of the component lifetimes distributions based on the system lifetime data. Log-rank type test statistics are therefore can be constructed to test the homogeneity of the components in K-system situation. We proposed to use Bayesian methodology to tackle the dependent components situation. The Gumbel copula is used for modelling the dependency structure. Metropolis-Hastings within Gibbs sampler is proposed to simulate the posterior distributions of the unknown parameters. We have studied two different estimation methods of the parameters of the component lifetime distributions based on the system lifetime data, namely, maximum likelihood estimation and minimum density divergence estimation. We compared these two methods and showed that the minimum density divergence estimation performed better under different contamined models and hence a robust procedure.

14201015.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201015.value: We have proposed two algorithms to compute the system signature. The first algorithm is used for computing the signature when the components lifetimes are exchangeable distributed. The results are reported in the third output in Part C. The next algorithm is used for the computation of system signature where the system can be decomposed into subsystems. The results are reported in the first output in Part C. It is natural that the performances of components vary when they are installed into the system as the working envirnoment changes. We assume that the components are dependent after they are installed into the system. Based on this assumption we proposed to use Bayesian methology to analyse the data. The results are presented in the second output of Part C Before we assume the dependency structure of the conponents, we might want to test if the working envirnoment affecting the lifetimes of components, we proposed goodness-of-fit tests to test if the distribution of the conponent lifetimes are affected. The results are reported in the last item of Part C. We have proposed an alternative estimation method other than the traditional maximum likelihood estimation, namely the minimum density dievrgence method. This estimation method is robust under the contaminated model. We are preparing th manuscript now and will submit to Metrika for publication.

14201015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201015.value: We have studied the problem where the system signature is known. In many situations, the system signature is very difficult to compute. It is a very interesting problem to extend the research to the unknown signature scenario. Treating the unknown signature as the parameter, estimating the component lifetime distribution as well as the system signature based on the system lifetime data is one of the potential study.

14201015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201015.value: Everybody would like to have a reliable product. Signature is one of the measure of reliability of the system. We studied the system signature under difference system set ups. We also provide the estimation methods if the data are avaliable. The results of this research can be used for the deployment of the system.

14201115.label: Project Objectives
14201115.value: To construct a subjective multiple objects segmentation quality database based on the existing single object segmentation database. 14201115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201115.value: 對象分割技術作為許多圖像/視頻應用（例如：基於內容的圖像縮放、檢索、數據壓縮以及安全監控）的預處理步驟發揮著重要的作用。這一技術使得對場景中感興趣的對象進行操作和分析成為可能。而在圖像/視頻處理的過程中，另一項技術，即視覺質量評價技術同樣扮演著重要的角色。該技術能夠控制并最大化地提升輸出結果的視覺質量。因此， 對象分割的視覺質量評估技術作為以上兩種技術結合的產物應運而生。這項技術旨在提供高視覺質量的分割結果以保證後續應用的良好性能。一個好的分割算法應當生成接近手動提取的分割結果。因此，有必要對某一算法生成的分割結果是否達到了與手動提取相近的質量進行評價以便後續應用的使用。儘管對象分割算法已經發展了數十年，對象分割質量評估卻少有研究，特別是以人的視覺感知為基礎的分割質量評價。 圖像中對象分割的視覺質量評價與傳統的圖像質量評價有許多相似之處：1）評價的方法可分為主觀評價與客觀評價兩種。其中，主觀評價更為可靠但耗時過長。因此， 發展符合人的視覺感知的自動的分割視覺質量客觀評價方法成為當務之急。2）根據是否比照手動提取的分割結果，客觀評價方法可分為全參考方法、部份參考方法和無參考方法。3）我們需要建立一個對象分割主觀質量評價數據庫來評估客觀評價方法與人主觀判斷的吻合度。 我們提出的課題研究工作分為三個階段：1）以構建的單一分割對象主觀質量評價數據庫為基礎，擴展至多分割對象的質量評價，即建立相應數據庫。我們將搜集多元化的多對象分割結果，以包含豐富的對象種類并考慮多對象間各自所不同的分割質量。完成主觀評價後，相應的主觀質量評級將被換算為分數以量化分割結果的主觀質量。2）研究基於人的視覺感知特性的全參考客觀評價方法。該方法包含對單一對象分割的質量評價以及將多對象的各自質量融合為全局質量。3）研發一種部份參考客觀評價方法。該方法通過顯著對象檢測來解決對象分割中的二義性問題并通過對面積、似物性、區域數量以及輪廓四個方面的分析來評價分割質量。

14201115.label: Realisation of objectives
14201115.value: To develop the objective measures that can evaluate the visual quality of object segmentation results in agreement with human quality judgments, it is imperative that a platform for evaluating the performance of the objective measures be constructed in order to analyze the factors that influence the visual quality of the segmentation results. To this end, we built a new subjective object segmentation visual quality database, in which a total of 255 segmentation results of diverse contents and different quality combinations of single and multiple objects were collected. The visual quality of each result was evaluated by more than 30 human subjects. The data were then analyzed to obtain the ﬁnal mean opinion score (MOS) and standard deviation value for each segmentation result. In the single object case, it was found that the subjective evaluation of single object segmentation visual quality can be divided into three levels: low, middle and high. However, for multiple objects, the overall quality mainly depends on the worst individual object quality, but it is also inﬂuenced by the area proportion among the individual objects. These observations inspired us to design the objective measure accordingly. A novel full-reference objective measure for object segmentation visual quality evaluation was then proposed for a single object. It incorporates four human visual properties in the formulation. In the proposed objective measure, the compensation term describes the human visual tolerance and saturation; the penalty term mainly reﬂects the perceptual importance of different error positions; and the harmonic mean was used to approximate the subjective pooling method. Moreover, the compensation and penalty terms were also used in the design of the objective measure in terms of the pixel attribute. To evaluate the visual quality involving multiple objects in an image, a pooling method aggregating the qualities of the individual objects was developed to evaluate the overall quality. Finally, our measure was compared with some of the state-of-the-art objective measures on our database. It has been demonstrated that the proposed measure performed better in matching subjective judgments. To aid other researchers in the ﬁeld to evaluate their measures against ours, we have made the database available publicly so that there is a reference dataset for comparison. We extended the full-reference objective measure for object segmentation visual quality evaluation to an unsupervised objective measure for quality evaluation of single object segmentation in images. Here, objectness as an essential attribute of objects is treated as a main feature to measure object segmentation quality. In addition, the prior information about the object quantity is integrated into the proposed measure. Experimental results showed that our measure conforms well to the subjective rating of the object segmentation quality. To study how different factors affect the visual quality of segmentation results, we analyzed the distribution characteristics of gazes when people look at an image. Different cases of the group of candidate regions were then summarized. Based on our analysis and summary, we developed three measures to evaluate the likelihood of a candidate region belonging to the target object and a pooling method to create a likelihood map of this object. Finally, the measures and pooling method were integrated with a proposed iterative strategy for generating the segmentation result. Experimental results showed that our method outperformed the state-of-the-art method. The gaze-based measures were incorporated into the above objective measure for object segmentation visual quality. In order to generate better segmentation results for the subjective object segmentation database, two approaches were studied: (1) interactive object segmentation in two phases; (2) a novel switch scheme and a saliency map binarization method for salient object segmentation. In (1), a coarse-to-fine method from region-level segmentation to pixel-level segmentation was developed. In the region-level segmentation, the best combination of adjacent refined superpixels was selected as the coarse segmentation result by measuring its global contrast and tightness degree. Subsequently, we used the coarse segmentation result to aid the construction of the energy function in the pixel-level segmentation. The result can be further refined with the fusion of region-level and pixel-level segmentations. Experimental results demonstrated that our method can achieve better segmentation performance compared with other state-of-the-art methods. In (2), we proposed a switch scheme, where the saliency map can be segmented by different methods according to its quality, which is evaluated by an existing measure. We also develop a binarization method by integrating three properties of the salient object. This method exclusively derives information from the saliency map (i.e., without referring to the original image). Experimental results have demonstrated that the proposed binarization method can generate better segmentation results and the switch scheme can further improve the segmentation results by fully exploiting the merit of both methods.

14201115.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201115.value: 1. A subjective object segmentation visual quality database has been constructed with 255 segmentation results of diverse contents and different quality combinations of single and multiple objects. The subjective visual quality database can be accessed via the link: http://www.ee.cuhk.edu.hk/~rshi/ 2. A novel full-reference objective measure for object segmentation visual quality evaluation has been proposed for a single object. To evaluate the visual quality involving multiple objects in an image, a pooling method aggregating the qualities of the individual objects has been developed to evaluate the overall quality. A journal paper (Section 8, paper #1) based on the research findings were published. The above work was a preliminary study to develop a novel full-reference objective measure for an object segmentation visual quality evaluation. It commenced soon after the research proposal was submitted to RGC in October 2014. The results obtained were submitted to IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology for publication in January 2015, and the paper was accepted in August 2015 but published in December 2015. 3. An unsupervised objective measure for quality evaluation of single object segmentation in images has been proposed. The measure employs objectness as an essential attribute of objects and integrates the prior information about the object quantity into it. A conference paper (Section 9, paper #3) based on the research findings was published. 4. Three measures to evaluate the likelihood of a candidate region belonging to the target object and a pooling method to create a likelihood map of this object have been developed based the analysis of the distribution characteristics of human gazes when looking at an image. A journal paper (Section 8, paper #2) based on the research findings was published. 5. Two effective object segmentation schemes have been proposed: (1) interactive object segmentation in two phases, which combines the region-level and pixel-level segmentations to deliver better segmentation performance; (2) a novel switch scheme and a saliency map binarization method for salient object segmentation. A journal paper (Section 8, paper #3) and a conference paper (Section 9, paper #2) based on the research findings were published. 5. Prior to the commencement of the project, a review of the current object segmentation subjective assessment methods was carried out to understand the state-of-the-art technology and seek novel research directions in object segmentation quality subjective assessment. A conference paper (Section 9, paper #1) was published on the review findings.

14201115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201115.value: Different objects have different semantic information which is an important factor for object segmentation visual quality assessment. For a speciﬁc application, we can perform the subjective object segmentation visual quality assessment for a special object category, such as portrait, car, ﬂower, etc. To improve the objective object segmentation visual quality evaluation, the semantic information can be integrated into the objective measure. With the development of object recognition techniques, we can ﬁnd rich semantic information about an object. But how to measure its distortion in terms of human perception is very challenging. In the traditional image visual quality assessment, the visual quality of an object affects the visual quality of whole image. If the object is distorted too much, the visual quality of the image would be degraded. Moreover, the segmentation method may be sensitive to the distortion in an image. It means that one segmentation method may generate different result when the image is distorted. Therefore, we use certain object segmentation method to extract this object in the original image and distorted image, respectively. The difference between these two results can be utilized to evaluate the quality of the distorted image.

14201115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201115.value: Object segmentation is a fundamental tool in computer vision and advanced image/video compression applications. For this reason, evaluating the segmentation quality objectively (i.e., without human interaction) is paramount to optimise the performance of these applications. The goal of this research project is the development of a novel objective measure of the visual quality of segmentation algorithms. Comparisons of this new metric with the other quality metrics demonstrate its superior ability to predict empirical (human-based) visual quality evaluation scores.

14201215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201215.value: "Big data analysis", broadly speaking, refers to the mission of solving a computational problem on "big data", namely, datasets at the order of tera bytes or above. In the past few years, the database community has developed several successful systems that can achieve a high degree of parallelism across hundreds of machines. Resorting to these systems has been a predominant approach in doing big data analysis. A drawback of the above approach, however, is the financial commitment it demands: Practitioners must either invest a large amount of money to purchase a cluster of machines, or be prepared to pay a commercial platform (e.g., Amazon EC2) for every single job that they would like to run. This creates a problem for many small- to median-scale companies in Hong Kong---while an increasing number of them are nowadays challenged with big-data analysis, most are either unable or unwilling to afford the aforementioned commitment. This project aims to provide these companies with softwares that help them tackle the big-data challenge with only one commodity machine. With the dwindled computing power, however, comes the need of (i) bringing down the data volume to a manageable level, and (ii) consequently, trading precision away for efficiency. A core concept throughout the project is "massive stream sampling", whose goal is to maintain a large disk-resident sample set on an unbounded data stream. Although stream sampling has been well (relatively) understood under the assumption that the samples fit in internal memory, its investigation has remained at a preliminary stage in the scenario where the assumption does not hold. This project, therefore, is planned to proceed in two phases. In the first phase, we will concentrate on designing optimal algorithms to carry out I/O-efficient massive sampling on different types of streams. In the second phase, we will deploy those algorithms as black boxes to solve data analytic problems I/O-efficiently with precision guarantees. N/A

14201415.label: Realisation of objectives
14201415.value: Objectives 1&2&3. Firstly, we have designed and simulated different metamaterials for a fixed resonant frequency by changing the array structures (slot, bow-tie, bow-tie-slot), dimensions, substrate materials (quartz, silicon and PET), material parameters and resonant frequencies. The corresponding biosensing performances of the designed metamaterials were also simulated and compared. Secondly, based on the simulation results, we fabricated the optimized metamaterial and characterized its biosensing performance for different biological samples by terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) system. In two conference papers, we missed to acknowledgment of the cpationed grant number, due to the time constraint and other factors. Specially, in this part, we fabricated a bow-tie array THz metamaterial biosensor and functionalized it with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) antibody (Ab) for specific EGFR detection. EGFR is a transmembrane protein which plays an important role in the occurrence and development of many kinds of cancers. The schematic diagram of the biosensor and the corresponding EGFR sensing results are given in our conference paper 1. The results demonstrate that the proposed strategy can achieve EGFR detection with high specificity and sensitivity. To further improve the sensitivity, the gold nanparticles (GNPs) were introduced into the biosensing application as a contrast enhanced agent, because the GNPs generally have much larger dielectric constants than the biomolecules. The EGFR sensing results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed sensitivity enhancement method by adopting GNPs. Furthermore, for sensitive THz detection of highly absorptive liquid samples, we proposed a novel multi-microfluidic-channel metamaterial biosensor for highly sensitive THz sensing of small volume liquid samples. The multi-channels are set mostly in the strong electric field enhancement area of the metamaterial, which significantly decreases the liquid amount and enhances interaction between the sensing targets and the THz wave (thus increasing the sensitivity). The schematic diagram of the biosensor and the corresponding liquid sensing results are shown in our paper 1 (IEEE Transactions on Terahertz Science and Technology, 2019, 9(2): 209-214). The liquid sensing results demonstrate the effectiveness of this proposed design. The proposed design provides a strong THz-analyte interaction platform for small volume liquid biosensing. Objective 4. We have designed and simulated the active device and its corresponding biosensing performances with tunable resonant frequencies based on graphene. By changing structure pattern, dimension and the Fermi level of graphene, we compared the resonant properties and the corresponding biosensing performances of the designed active device. For the hybrid graphene structure design to tune the graphene Fermi level and conductivity, we have fabricated the SiO2/Si gated graphene device and the ion-gel gated graphene device for active modulation of terahertz amplitude and phase (based on the total internal reflection and Brewster angel reflection geometries). The experimental results demonstrated that the adopted gating structure can effectively tune the graphene Fermi level and the corresponding conductivity. Objectives 5&6. Based on the simulation results of the graphene device, to achieve tuneable and strong resonance over the terahertz range of interest, the graphene Fermi level is required to be tuneable over a relatively large extent (eg: 0.05 ev-0.9 ev). The present gating structure can usually achieve a tuneable graphene Fermi level range of 0.05 eV-0.5 eV. Additionally, inspired by the active THz amplitude and phase modulation work based on graphene and Brewster reflection (published by our group in Nature Communications, 2018, 9: 4909), we proposed that the active graphene device can also be used as the biosensor by integrating with the sample cell or microfluidic channel. Firstly, we have experimentally measured that the bio-molecules can change the graphene conductivity of the device effectively, which proves the feasibility of our graphene biosensor design. Moreover, recently we have designed a metal-graphene hybrid device by combing the strong resonance of metal metamaterial and the conductivity tunability of graphene. The graphene is placed on top of the metal metamaterial. The sensing bio-molecules will change graphene conductivity effectively and then tune the resonant properties of metamaterial. We still need to further fabricate the device, and then measure the biosensing performance based on the proposed metal-graphene hybrid design. Finally, for sensing different biomedical samples accurately and fast, it is important to minimize the data acquisition time whilst maintaining accurate extraction of the sample properties. To this end, we have also developed several adaptive sampling techniques to significantly increase the sampling rate and keep the accuracy.

14201415.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201415.value: In this project, we have designed and fabricated a bow-tie array metamaterial biosensor and functionalized it by EGFR antibody for specific EGFR detection with high sensitivity. We adopted GNP as a contrast enhanced agent to further improve the biosensing sensitivity based on metamaterial. Furthermore, we proposed a novel multi-microfluidic-channel metamaterial biosensor for THz detection of highly absorptive small volume liquid samples. This design has the advantages of being highly sensitive, label-free, cost-effective, easy to operate and only needing a tiny liquid volume. We proposed novel graphene devices for active modulation of terahertz amplitude and phase (based on the total internal reflection and Brewster angel reflection geometries). The modulation depth is large and the modulation speed is very high. We proposed devices to realize biosensing based on the active graphene modulator and Brewster reflection. We also designed a metal-graphene hybrid device. To accurately sense the samples with high speed, we also developed several adaptive sampling techniques to significantly increase the sampling rate and keep the accuracy. We have finished the fundamental work of this project and have achieved very promising results which will have great impact in the terahertz community as well as the biosensing community. This project so far has an output of 10 journal papers and 6 international conference proceedings. These publications relate to different aspects of the project, such as the antibody functionalized metamaterial sensor for EGFR detection (conference paper 1), multi-microfluidic-channel metamaterial biosensor for small volume liquid sensing (journal paper 1); active terahertz amplitude and phase modulation device based on graphene (journal paper 2 and 8); accurate THz characterisation of thin films (journal paper 3); developing techniques and algorithms for faster and accurate data acquisition (journal papers 4 and 9); and investigation of biomedical THz applications (journal papers 5 and 7).

14201415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201415.value: We plan to further characterise different bio-molecules based on the proposed graphene sensor. The metal nanoparticles will also be introduced as a contrast enhanced agent to increase the sensitivity. The device is basically ready for this application and we will obtain sufficient data to publish another paper on this aspect soon. We will integrate the novel microfuidic design (with multiple input and output ports) into the graphene senor for liquid sensing, which can be used for highly absorptive liquid sensing, especially to simultaneously detect the reaction of different biological liquid samples. The measurement software can also be optimized by using the adaptive sampling techniques to increase the speed.

14201415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201415.value: In this project, we have designed devices to improve the sensitivity of detection of biosamples including antibodies. In particular we designed and fabricated a bow-tie array metamaterial biosensor and functionalized it by EGFR antibody for specific EGFR detection with high sensitivity. We have also proposed a novel multi-microfluidic-channel metamaterial biosensor for THz detection of highly absorptive small volume liquid samples. This design has the advantages of being highly sensitive, label-free, cost-effective, easy to operate and only needing a tiny liquid volume. To accurately sense the samples with high speed, we also developed several adaptive sampling techniques to significantly increase the sampling rate and keep the accuracy. Finally, with a view to speeding up the detection process further and enhancing sensitivity, we have designed and fabricated novel graphene devices for active modulation of terahertz amplitude and phase (based on the total internal reflection and Brewster angel reflection geometries). The modulation depth (MD) is large (99.3%-99.9% MD for 0.3-1.6 THz) and the modulation speed is very high (>90% MD for 5 kHz). We have finished the fundamental work of this project and have achieved very promising results which will have great impact in the terahertz community as well as the biosensing community.

14201515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201515.value: Low-dropout regulator (LDO) plays an important role in power-management IC design since it can provide clean and low-noise supply voltage to the noise-sensitive analog and radio-frequency circuit blocks in IC systems. The performance of the transient response of LDO has strong relationship with both the loop response and large-signal response at the gate of the power transistor. The prior approaches to improve the loop response are not effective to extend the loop bandwidth over 20MHz. In order to enhance the loop response of LDO, a frequency compensation scheme based on multiple pole-zero cancellations is proposed in this project. The scheme will be applied to LDOs with multiple small-gain stages to demonstrate the idea. 14201515.label: Realisation of objectives
14201515.value: The project has been successfully completed. All objectives have been achieved. Several structures of low-dropout regulator to improve both the frequency and transient responses have been developed. The proposed regulator structures have been investigated, and the improvements to the frequency and transient responses have been reviewed. During the project development, we have developed several circuit techniques and structures. We have carried out circuit analyses and optimizations. The developed circuits are 1. A CMOS output-capactorless low-dropout regulator with unity-bandwidth more than 100MHz and response time of 200ps has been developed and experimentally verified. In this design, enhanced multipath nested Miller compensation with embedded feedforward path is proposed to the low-dropout regulator circuit. The loop gain at different loading cases has been investigated. The compensation technique enables a loop bandwidth as high as 100MHz so that the response time can be greatly shortened to less than 200ps. Due to the proposed feedforward path, the performance of power-supply rejection is further enhanced. Moreover, the high-frequency pole-zero cancellation enhances the stability of circuit substantially. This work has been reported in IEEE Transactions on Power Electronics. 2. Another low-dropout regulator design with differentiator-based active zero compensation has been developed and experimentally verified. The regulator is formed by three gain stages with adaptive biasing to improve the transient responses. A differentiator-based active zero is created to cancel pole’s effect such that loop bandwidth can be extended. The generation of zero in this design does not require a larger RC time constant, and thus the chip area for on-chip resistors and capacitors is small. Both the transient response and power-supply rejection have been improved by the proposed circuit methods. This work has been reported in IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems I. 3. Enhanced active-feedback frequency compensation has been developed. The compensation topology has been verified experimentally. The topology makes use of the signal- and transient-boosting structure developed by the PI and an embedded current buffer at the differential input stage to increase the signal-current magnitude significantly. The proposed frequency compensation can be applied to the output-capacitorless low-dropout regulator to improve loop bandwidth. This work has been reported in International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications. 4. Moreover, there are several regulators and circuit techniques developed and they have been reported in some journals and conferences. Upon the completion of this project, it is found that differentiator-based active zero and feedforward path are two effective methods to improve transient response and power-supply rejection of low-dropout regulator.

14201615.label: Project Objectives
14201615.value: Understanding human motions in both normal and pathological patterns through motion modeling and analysis: Conventional gait analyses in gait laboratory are not suitable for online monitoring of patients’ motion patterns during rehabilitation. This project will utilize multiple wearable sensors in AKB to collect patients’ motion data during rehabilitation, construct motion models, and further evaluate individual motion pattern. Patients’ pathological patterns in functional movements will be modeled and analyzed. Determination of user-adaptive assistance in rehabilitation based on motion analysis: In rehabilitation with AKB, patients are encouraged to perform the task-specific exercises, but are assisted as needed. This project will investigate intelligent assistive function to determine customized appropriate assistance to each patient. Motion control of AKB to deliver assistance to patient safely and comfortably: AKB is equipped with a novel multifunctional actuator, which can work in multiple modes for driving and braking functions at the knee joint. This project will develop motion control algorithms for the multifunctional actuator to regulate its output torque/position according to the desired assistance. Stability of the controller under various working conditions will also be studied to ensure a safe and comfortable support in rehabilitation. Validating the effectiveness of robot-assisted lower limbs rehabilitation with AKB: The developed control methods will be implemented in AKB for human trials. Patients with different physical conditions will be recruited, and the effectiveness of AKB-assisted lower limbs rehabilitation will be validated through clinical studies.
