14201615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201615.value: Mobility impaired problems have greatly reduced the life quality of patients suffering from various injuries and diseases. These patients often need to participate into training programs in rehabilitation treatment centers to recover and regain lost functions. In recent years, robotic assistive devices like upper limb rehabilitation systems, exoskeleton suits, and locomotion training machines have been developed for rehabilitation. However, currently wearable lower limb assistive devices to assist in physical therapy still need to be improved in practical implementation. Several wearable lower limb orthoses have been developed, but associated control usually focused on system modeling and human-robot interaction, while considering little about the actual scenario in patients’ rehabilitation. Besides, patients engaged in rehabilitation may have different physical conditions and, thus, need customized exercise programs. Research on assistive functions adaptation of the lower limb assistive devices is still at the early stage. Moreover, there is so far no research on improving the energy efficiency of lower limb assistive devices through energy harvesting. Our group has developed a powered knee orthosis, named Assistive Knee Brace (AKB), for gait assistance of patients with impaired mobility. Based on the AKB prototype, this project aims at developing advanced control methods, so that the AKB can provide patient initiated and customized assistance to patient’s affected leg in task-specific exercise, including functional movements (such as over ground gait, stand up/sit down, and stair walking) and balance exercise, so as to improve the patient’s mobility and balance in neurologic and orthopedic rehabilitation. This project will develop comprehensive gait analysis method based on wearable sensors to recognize patient’s motion intention, analyze motion pattern and quality, and determine proper assistive functions of the AKB for a customized training. Impedance based control of the multifunctional actuator will be studied to ensure stable and safe support from AKB in training tasks considering patient’s intention and human-robot interaction. This project will also explore regenerative braking technology to recover kinetic energy during training, and improve the energy efficiency of the whole device. The scientific knowledge created through this project will facilitate the continuing research on many aspects, including human motion understanding, abnormal gait diagnosis, robot-assisted rehabilitation, and energy harvesting from human motions. The output of this project will benefit the assistive devices development and healthcare of numerous patients. 行動不便問題困擾著為數眾多的罹患疾病或遭受損傷的患者，使他們的生活質量嚴重下降。這些患者往往需要通過參加康復中心的訓練項目來恢復喪失的運動功能。近年來，機器人輔助裝置比如上肢訓練系統、外骨骼套裝及減重步態訓練裝置等被廣泛研究用於康復訓練。然而，目前用以協助開展物理治療的可穿戴下肢輔助裝置還極需通過實際應用研究進一步改進和完善。世界上一些可穿戴下肢矯形器正處於開發當中，但是相應的控制研究目前主要著眼於系統建模和人機交互方面，而缺乏考慮患者實際康復訓練場景。通常在康復訓練中根據患者不同的身體狀況需個性化定制其訓練項目，但是下肢輔助裝置的相關自適應輔助功能研發仍處在早期階段。此外，目前也沒有通過能量回收來改善下肢輔助裝置能量效率的相關研究。本項目組已經開發了一個名為輔助膝架（以下簡稱膝架）的有動力膝關節矯形器裝置，用以輔助行動不便患者開展步態訓練。基於現有膝架樣機，本項目旨在研發先進的控制方法用於在神經和骨骼康復訓練中提供基於患者意圖的個性化的輔助功能，幫助患者完成特定的訓練任務。通過在功能性運動（比如平地行走、站起坐下、上下樓梯）及平衡鍛鍊等康復訓練任務中提供合理有效的輔助功能，改善患者的運動和平衡能力。本項目將基於可穿戴傳感器開發新穎的綜合步態分析方法，用於識別病人運動意圖，分析其運動模式和表現，以及確定膝架在個性化康復訓練中的輔助功能配置。將在考慮病人的意圖和人機交互的基礎上，研究膝架多功能驅動器的阻抗控制方法，確保膝架在訓練中的穩定性和安全性。本項目將同時探索再生制動技術在康復訓練中的應用，通過在運動中回收能量，提高裝置的能量效率。這個項目產生的科學知識將有助於許多方面的後續研究，包括人體運動理解和分析、步態異常診斷、機器人輔助康復訓練，及人體運動中的能量回收。該項目的產出亦將有利於機器人輔助裝置的發展和眾多患者的醫療保健。

14201615.label: Realisation of objectives
14201615.value: Modeling and evaluation of patients’ gait patterns is the basis for both gait assessment and gait rehabilitation. A convenient and real-time gait modeling, analysis, and evaluation method was developed based on ground reaction forces (GRFs) measured by a pair of smart insoles. Gait states were deﬁned based on the foot–ground contact forms of both legs. From the obtained gait state sequence and the duration of each state, the human gait was modeled as a semi-Markov process (SMP). Four groups of gait features derived from the SMP gait model were used for characterizing individual gait patterns. With this model, both the normal gaits of healthy people and the abnormal gaits of patients with impaired mobility were analyzed. Abnormal evaluation indices (AEI) were further proposed for gait abnormality assessment. The results showed that gait patterns were successfully obtained and evaluated for normal, age-related, and pathological gaits. The effectiveness of the proposed AEI for gait assessment was veriﬁed through comparison with a video-based gait abnormality rating scale. A multifunctional magneto-rheological actuator with power regeneration capability, named regenerative magnetorheological actuator (RMRA), was designed for gait assistance in the knee joint. RMRA has motor and magnetorheological (MR) brake parts working in parallel that can harvest energy through regenerative braking. This novel design provides multiple functions with good energy efﬁciency. The conﬁguration and basic design of the RMRA were ﬁrst introduced. Then geometrical optimization of the MR brake was conducted based on a parameterized model, and multiple factors are considered in the design objectives: braking torque, weight, and power consumption. After the optimal design was obtained, an RMRA prototype was fabricated and associated driver circuits were designed. Finally, multiple functions of the RMRA, especially three different braking modes, were modeled and tested. Experimental results of RMRA output performances in all working modes matched the modeling and simulation. Assistive knee braces with the developed RMRA were promising for applications in gait assistance and rehabilitation. In addition, a wearable exoskeleton suit named CUHK-EXO was developed to provide motion assistance for paralyzed patients. The whole system of CUHK-EXO, including the mechanical structure, human-machine interface (HMI), reference trajectories, and control, was designed considering ergonomics, safety, and comfort. Performance of EXO was evaluated by pilot clinical trials with a paralyzed patient. After training the subject to transfer his center of gravity (COG) and use a pair of crutches to keep balance with his upper body strength, the subject can STS and walk with the motion assistance provided by EXO. Testing results validated the effectiveness of the whole system development of the exoskeleton. Control methods developed for Assistive Knee Brace (AKB) with motor and regenerative magnetorheological actuator (RMRA) was implemented and performances were verified via human trials. Clinical trial results of AKB with motor was performed to show that AKB could provide desired assistance to help improve the patient’s effort. On the other hand, control of RMRA for gait assistance was investigated. Considering the energy harvesting capability of RMRA, optimal braking control strategies for torque tracking performance and minimal energy consumption was developed. The developed control methods were implemented in AKB with RMRA. The developed RMRA provided desired assistance with the cooperation of motor and MR brake parts, and the energy consumption was reduced compared to only using motor as actuator.

14201615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201615.value: A multifunctional magneto-rheological actuator with power regeneration capability, named regenerative magnetorheological actuator (RMRA), was designed for gait assistance in the knee joint ([J1] in Part C). RMRA has motor and magnetorheological (MR) brake parts working in parallel that can harvest energy through regenerative braking. This novel design provides multiple function with good energy efficiency. The geometrical optimization of the MR brake was conducted based on a parameterized model, and multiple factors were considered in the design objectives: braking torque, weight, and power consumption. After the optimal design is obtained, an RMRA prototype was fabricated and associated driver circuits were designed. Finally, multiple functions of the RMRA, especially three different braking modes, were modeled and tested. Experimental results of RMRA output performances in all working modes match the modeling and simulation. Assistive knee braces with the developed RMRA were promising for applications in gait assistance and rehabilitation. A lower extremity exoskeleton named CUHK-EXO was developed [J2] with considerations of ergonomics, user-friendly interface, safety, and comfort. An innovative actuator named magneto-rheological series elastic actuator (MRSEA) was designed [J3] for the knee joints of CUHK-EXO. It can also provide large controllable braking torque with low power, and hence improve the system energy efficiency. Analysis of the exoskeleton’s applicability to the sit-to-stand and stand-to-sit (STS) motion assistance was performed [J4]. As nonlinear characteristics are desired in robotic assistive devices in some cases, we have proposed a new convenient design method [J5] to study the cam profile generation in cam-spring mechanism. An off-line design and online modification algorithm was proposed for the exoskeleton to generate reference joint trajectories during walking assistance [J8]. We also published a review article [J6] to discuss the challenges and limitations of the developed ankle-foot orthoses, and provide useful information for researchers to develop robotic assistive devices. We have investigated methods to determine user-adaptive assistance of assistive knee braces (AKBs) in gait rehabilitation [J7]. A fuzzy expert system, which takes a patient’s physical condition and gait analysis results as inputs, was proposed to configure suitable levels of different assistive functions of the AKB. During gait rehabilitation, the AKB generates a reference knee trajectory according to the patient’s individual gait pattern, and the interaction force was controlled through a hybrid impedance controller considering the individual assistive function configuration. Clinical testing results showed that AKB with the proposed control strategies can provide effective assistance to improve the patient’s gait performance during gait rehabilitation.

14201615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201615.value: Significant results (8 journal papers and 4 conference papers, awarded China patent and US/PCT patent applications, Silver Medal in Inventions Geneva, 2 PhD graduates) have been obtained from this completed project. The terrain identification for robotic assistive devices including assistive knee braces and exoskeletons should be further investigated. A suitable pattern recognition algorithm should be developed to process the input signals so as to identify the terrain. The terrain identification system should be implemented in the developed robotic assistive devices, so that they can also work well on different terrains. More clinical trials on patients with mobility impairment problems should be conducted to evaluate the performances. Further commercialization of the developed devices and technologies will be also explored.

The output of this project will benefit the assistive devices development and healthcare of numerous patients.

14202115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202115.value: Latent Variables are random variables that cannot be directly determined from observed data due to various practical reasons, such as unmeasurable nature of variables and missing data of certain types. Notwithstanding that our research was motivated by a specific real-life application, simulation modeling for a hospital emergency department, we plan to conduct a comprehensive study of estimation for latent variables for general systems. In this research, we propose a novel simulation-optimization approach to well utilize the scarce empirical data to infer latent variables. Since the probability-distributions space is huge, we employ variable neighborhood search to guide the search procedure. We have two operators to define the neighborhood structures: change of probability-distribution forms and increment/decrement of parameter values. The change of neighborhood structures enables the search procedure to escape from a local optimum. We also incorporate simulated annealing into our algorithm to further enhance its “hill-climbing” capability. At each iteration, simulations are carried out to evaluate the proximity of a solution to the optimal combination of probability distributions. The integration of simulation and meta-heuristics takes the advantages that (i) the approach is very general where no assumption on the system structure and random variables is needed, (ii) complex systems that analytical models are intractable can be managed, (iii) a large number of enumerations of possible solutions can be avoided, and (iv) the algorithm is derivative-free. With our proposed estimation procedure, we will conduct two computational studies. The first study is to test the performance (effectiveness, efficiency, robustness, etc.) of our solution methodology. The second one is to draw insights into the relationship between latent variables and available observations, for example, conditions for which multiple optimal combinations of probability distributions exist. The design of our computational experiments is original: in reality the latent variables are unknown, while in our study we simulate systems with known random variables to generate empirical data for estimation. This allows us to make comparisons between the actual random variables and our estimates. Our research is significant that (i) this is the first study of latent-variables estimation by integrating simulation and variable neighborhood search, (ii) model developers can implement our approach for any systems, (iii) our algorithm can solve other simulation-optimization problems, and (iv) our computational studies can provide insights into latent-variables estimation. 潛變量是由於各種實際原因，例如變量的不可測量性質或數據不完整性，而不能從觀測數據直接估算的隨機變量。儘管我們的研究是由一特定的實際應用--醫院急症室仿真建模--所啟發，此計劃將會全面研究針對估算通用系統的潛變量。在這項研究中，我們提出了一種新的仿真優化方法並利用有限觀測數據來估算潛變量。由於潛變量的概率分佈可行性組合是極大，我們採用變化鄰域搜尋法引導搜索過程。我們有兩個鄰域結構：概率分佈形式和參數值的遞增/遞減變化。採用變化鄰域結構有助搜索過程逃離局部最優。我們還運入了模擬退火到我們的算法，進一步提升其“逃離局離最優”的能力。在每次迭代中，我們採用仿真方法評估現有概率分佈的組合與最優組會的距離。仿真法和元啟發式的整合的優點是：（一）該方法能應用於任何系統，對於系統的結構和隨機變量沒有假定，（二）可應用於難以計算分析模型的複雜系統，（三）可避免大量的試算，和（四）我們的算法不涉及導數。我們會應用所提出的估算方法進行兩項計算研究。第一項研究是測試我們的搜尋方法的性能（效果，效率，穩定性等）。第二個是潛變量和觀測之間的關係，例如尋找概率分佈最佳組合不唯一性的條件。我們的計算實驗設計是原創的：在現實中的潛變量是未知的，而在我們的研究中，我們模擬與已知的隨機變量系統生成的數據進行估算。這讓我們可以比較實際的隨機變量和我們演算方法提供的估算。我們的研究是重要的：（一）這是第一項研究通過整合仿真方法和變化鄰域搜尋法估算潛變量，（二）建模人員可以應用我們的方法到任何系統，（三）我們的估算法可以應用到其他仿真優化問題，以及（四）我們計算的研究可以提供對潛變量的深入了解。

14202115.label: Realisation of objectives
14202115.value: To achieve the project objectives, we first conducted a literature review of methodologies for the estimation of latent variables in general systems. This gave us a good background as to the effectiveness of the various methodologies. We then developed a simulation-optimization algorithm, which integrates simulation into variable neighborhood search (termed SVNS in our research), to utilize scarce empirical data (e.g., missing data) to infer latent variables. With the support of RGC GRF, we purchased academic licenses of the simulation software ARENA. The algorithm was coded with ARENA and its built-in VBA. Various computational instances of queuing systems were tested. Our computational experiments were original. In each computational instance, the actual system was first fixed (e.g., the logic of the system and the probability distribution functions of the latent variables) and observations were generated from the systems. Thus, the estimated probability distribution functions obtained by SVNS could be compared with the actual ones for the assessment of the effectiveness of our methodology. The computational instances were distinguished by the characteristics of the queueing system (e.g., arrival rates of entities, number of available resources, and probability distribution functions of the service times). Computational experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of SVNS. The results are available in the attached paper titled "Integrating Simulation with Variable Neighborhood Search for Estimating Latent Variables." The paper will be submitted for publication at key international journals. The research findings of our work provide insight into the relationship between latent variables and available observations. We also provide a novel and effective methodology for the problem of latent variable estimation and new knowledge on this topic. In addition to the literature review which focuses on the methodologies for estimating latent variables, we conduct a further literature review on the usage of data, optimization, and simulation for the management of production systems. Our literature review was published at the International Journal of Production Research: • Kuo Y.H. and Kusiak A., “From Data to Big Data in Production Research: The Past and Future Trends." (Selected Surveys on Cutting-edge Problems in Production Research), International Journal of Production Research, 57(15-16): 4828–4853, 2019. The research of the PI and Co-I on optimization was published in the journal Discrete Optimization: • Kuo, Y. H. and Leung, J. M.Y., “On the mixed set covering, packing and partitioning polytope.” Discrete Optimization, 22(A), 162-182, 2016. We also considered the suggestions from two of the reviewers. We studied the application of SVNS to real-world problems. In particular, we investigated the performance of SVNS performs in complex systems. In this aspect of research, we studied three real-world systems – the patient flow of a hospital emergency department, a medical appointment scheduling system, and estimation of hidden health states of patients in a disease control problem – where real-world data were collected for conducting the computational experiments. Our research methodology facilities the investigation into these healthcare management problems. Managerial insights into the operational issues were derived. 14202115.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202115.value: We reviewed papers on the methodologies for estimating latent variables in the system. To better understand the related research, we conducted a more comprehensive literature review of the existing research on data, simulation, and optimization in production systems. Not only the research methodologies and applications were reviewed, but also the future trends and opportunities were identified. The literature review was published in an international journal. We designed the algorithm that integrates simulation into variable neighborhood search (VNS), which we call SVNS, for estimating latent variables in general systems. The integration of simulation and VNS takes the advantages that (i) the approach is very general where no assumption on the system structure and random variables is needed, (ii) complex systems that analytical models are intractable can be managed, (iii) a large number of enumerations of possible solutions can be avoided, and (iv) the algorithm is derivative-free. We successfully developed a computational programme to implement our proposed SVNS with the use of the simulation software ARENA and its built-in VBA tool for latent variable estimation. We developed various queueing models (with known random variables in the system) on ARENA and generated limited observations from these queueing models. These observations were used to train SVNS to estimate the latent variables (that could not be directly estimated from these observations) in the systems. The estimated probability distributions of the latent variables obtained from SVNS were then compared with the actual ones for examining the effectiveness of the algorithm. Our computational results suggest that the algorithm could greatly improve the quality of an initial guess of the distributions and obtain a promising approximation of the distributions in most of the instances. We tested our methodologies with real-world applications: simulation modeling of hospital emergency department operations, medical appointment scheduling, and inference of hidden health sates of patients in a disease control problem. We established collaborations with major hospitals in the region. Real data were provided by the collaborating parties for our computational experiments. Computational results have further demonstrated the effectiveness of our proposed methodology and the practicality and significance of our research. The major findings have been published in key journals in the relevant fields, such as Discrete Optimization, Flexible Services and Manufacturing, International Journal of Production Research, and Journal of Medical Systems. The findings were presented at international conferences and published in the respective conference proceedings.

14202115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202115.value: Due to the complexity of real-world systems and the increasing computational power that enterprises, organizations and research institutes can afford, simhueristic has been commonly adopted in various applications in recent years. Our proposed methodology has advanced the state-of-the-art of the research in this area. Our simulation-optimization framework is not restricted to the use of variable neighborhood search; other meta-heuristics can also serve the purpose, as long as a simulation model can be incorporated into the framework and used to evaluate the goodness-of-fit of the estimated probability distribution functions. Further research can be conducted to study the integration of simulation into other meta-heuristics and examine their effectivenesses and efficiencies. The integration of simulation and meta-heuristic can also be applied to solve stochastic optimization problems where uncertainty in systems is present. As demonstrated by the realistic applications studied in this research, our proposed simulation-optimization framework can be used in numerous real-life problems where latent variables are involved. Further applications can be explored. More research efforts and computational experiments are required.

14202115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202115.value: In this project, we studied the problem of inference of latent variables in general systems. We developed a simulation-optimization framework that incorporates simulation into variable neighborhood search for estimating the probability distribution functions of latent variables. The integration of simulation and variable neighborhood search takes the advantages that (i) the approach is very general where no assumption on the system structure and random variables is needed, (ii) complex systems that analytical models are intractable can be managed, (iii) a large number of enumerations of possible solutions can be avoided, and (iv) the algorithm is derivative-free. Our computational results demonstrate the computational effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed methodology. We collaborated with two major hospitals in the region and studied three real-life problems: simulation modeling of emergency department operations, medical appointment scheduling, and inference of hidden health states of patients in disease control. We utilized actual operational data for the computational experiments. Our computational experiments further demonstrate the benefits of our proposed methodology and the practical significance of our research work.

14202215.label: Project Objectives
14202215.value: Objective 1: to synthesize the guest and host macromers needed for a novel approach of fabricating the guest-host hydrogels. Hyaluronic acid (HA) will be modified with the guest molecules (HA-guest). The host molecules will be modified with one crosslinkable acrylate group (Host monomer). The guest-host hydrogels will be formed by pre-organizing host monomers along the HA-guest backbone via guest-host binding and subsequent crosslinking of the bound host monomers. Objective 2: to characterize the guest-host hydrogel physical properties. Mechanical properties, swelling, and rheological properties will be evaluated. Objective 3: to investigate the efficacy of the guest-host hydrogels as carrier materials of hMSCs for cartilage repair in vitro. hMSCs will be encapsulated in the guest-host hydrogels and evaluated for chondrogenesis under in vitro culture.

14202215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202215.value: 本研究的目的是開發機械堅固，生物相容的，可自我修復，可模塑和注射的賓主型水凝膠作為用於微創軟骨療法所需的細胞及藥物載體材料。 骨關節炎（OA）特徵在於關節軟骨的逐漸退化。一項研究發現，約10％的50歲以上的香港居民從患有這種疾病。也有不少患者因軟骨損傷導致軟骨的全面退化。目前的治療軟骨退變的療法有許多局限性，如壽命有限，缺乏供體組織和疾病傳播的風險。使用治療細胞（包括幹細胞）的軟骨組織工程是一種用於軟骨修復的有前途的方法。但是，細胞在軟骨缺損部位的直接施用通常由於患病關節的惡劣環境導致大量細胞損失，因此療效有限。因此，臨床對能夠為細胞提供一個有利的環境並促進軟骨的癒合的載體生物材料存在著巨大的需求。 水凝膠已被廣泛地作為生物材料的載體應用於的軟骨組織工程。相比化學交聯的水凝膠，通過精心設計的物理鍵結合所形成的水凝膠可具有獨特的性能，如在凝膠狀態下可注射性及破損後的自我修復能力。這些特性都是水凝膠在生物醫學應用中所需的理想性質。然而，物理交聯水凝膠的機械性能一般較弱，並且和很少用於的細胞載體材料。我們建議開發具有良好機械彈性，生物相容性，自我修復能力，通過主客體物理結合交聯的可注射水凝膠，並評價其作為細胞載體材料用於軟骨修復的可行性。這項工作的新穎之處在於在三個方面。首先，相對於傳統的方法中，我們所提出了“主客體大分子單體”的方法是新穎的，它會顯著提高水凝膠的機械性能，同時保持賓主型水凝膠的所需要的特性。其次，所擬水凝膠具有有利於軟骨修復的性能，例如機械彈性，自愈性，成型性和注射性。最後，還沒有研究評估這種主客體水凝膠的用於承載間充質幹細胞和小分子藥物用於軟骨修復。 從該項目的研究成果將有助於指導可用於軟骨再生的注射型生物材料的設計並促進其臨床轉化。在這項研究中開發的水凝膠也將有助於開發新型微創療法修復包括骨頭，韌帶，半月板和椎間盤在內的各類結締組織。

14202215.label: Realisation of objectives
14202215.value: Objective 1: to synthesize the guest and host macromers needed for a novel approach of fabricating the guest-host hydrogels. (100% completion) AD-functionalized guest polymer ADxHA is synthesized by simple esterification reaction. x denotes the modification degree of AD. Guest polymers with low (x=15), medium (x=40) and high (x=80) modification degree are prepared. In order to avoid chemical crosslinking generated from the photo-initiated radical reaction during gelation, we have designed and synthesized the host monomer with exactly one acrylate group. The amine reactive isothiocyanate derivative (HO-NCS) is firstly acrylated by acryloyl chloride to yield Ac-NCS, which is then coupled to the only amine group of 6-monodeoxy-6-monoamino-β-cyclodextrin (βCD-NH2), yielding the mono-Ac-βCD host monomer. By simply dissolving ADxHA and mono-Ac-βCD in the same PBS (pH7.4) solution, the HGMs are formed driven by the specific host-guest complexation as verified by the NMR analysis. Upon complexation, the chemical shift of the ethyl multiplet of AD changes significantly, and the corresponding peak is broadened. The specific host-guest interaction is further confirmed by 2D NOESY NMR, where the AD proton peaks are found correlated with the inner protons (C(3)-H and C(5)-H) of βCD. Our HGM approach produces more efficient and thorough host-guest complexation between the freely diffusing host monomers and guest polymers as evidenced by the ITC (isothermal titration calorimetry) studies. The quick and smooth generation and recovery of the exothermic signal during the titration of guest polymers with host monomers indicates that the host-guest complexation is more efficient and thorough. This efficient host-guest complexation is essential to the formation of the crosslinkable HGMs and the subsequent UV induced hydrogelation. Lastly, freestanding HGM hydrogels are readily created with varied ADxHA concentration (1 wt%, 2 wt% and 4 wt%). The low solid content of the HGM hydrogels (only 1.4 wt% for AD15HA hydrogels) demonstrates the efficacy of the HGM strategy in preparing robust supramolecular hydrogels. Such robustness is attributed to the multivalent host-guest crosslinkers produced by the polymerization of acrylates on the pre-assembled host-guest complexes. The host-guest nano-clusters, rather than the spatially isolated host-guest complexes obtained from the self-assembly of host polymers and guest polymers, act as the multivalent crosslinkers for HA polymer chains. Objective 2: to characterize the guest-host hydrogel physical properties. (100% completion) The reversible nature of the host-guest interactions allows for easy chain rearrangement and re-association upon compression. Therefore, unlike the brittle chemical MeHA hydrogels, the HGM hydrogels are compressible with much faster stress relaxation rate. MeHA hydrogels are brittle and rupture below 50% strain. In contrast, the HGM hydrogels (4 wt% ADxHA) are capable of withstanding a much greater strain, up to at least 80%. In contrast to the irreversible destruction of the static network structure in the chemical hydrogels under compression, the compressive force rearranges the physically associated polymer chains in the dynamic network structure of HGM hydrogels, thereby giving rise to the energy dissipation before breakage of the polymeric networks. Such energy dissipation is revealed by the stress relaxation analysis. For comparison with chemical MeHA hydrogels (modification degree is 37%), AD40HA is used for HGM hydrogel preparation hereafter. We stepwisely increase the compressive strain and study the stress relaxation behavior in the following 5 minutes. Compared to the MeHA hydrogels, which slowly relax about 10% of the peak stress in the first 2 minutes, the HGM hydrogels rapidly relax over 80% of the peak stress during the same time interval at all strain levels. Objective 3: to investigate the efficacy of the guest-host hydrogels as carrier materials of hMSCs for cartilage repair in vitro. (100% completion) To demonstrate that such HGM hydrogels are promising biomaterials for tissue regeneration, we use HGM hydrogels to encapsulate human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs), which are a promising cell source for tissue regeneration due to their potential to differentiate into several mesenchymal lineages including cartilage. The gelation process is found not affected by cells under such conditions, indicating that host-guest complexation is robust enough for cell-related applications. The as-prepared cell-laden hydrogels are then re-molded into rectangle shape by press-fitting into a rectangle mold within two minutes. After compression re-molding of the hydrogels, after 1 day of culture. Even after 21 days of culture, the majority the encapsulated hMSCs remain viable, indicating that the cells are effectively protected by the hydrogel matrix during hydrogel deformation. Moreover, the HGM hydrogels better support the chondrogenesis of the encapsulated hMSCs compared to the MeHA hydrogels likely due to the enhanced retention of growth factors in the HGM hydrogels. Instead of being added continuously to the culture medium, TGFis encapsulated in the hMSC-laden hydrogels during the hydrogel fabrication. After 7 days of culture in the TGF-free medium, the expression levels of chondrogenic marker genes including type II collagen (COL2), aggrecan (AGG), and sex determining region Y-box 9 (SOX9) are significantly elevated in HGM hydrogels. In contrast, the expression levels of these marker genes in the MeHA hydrogels are not significantly different from those of undifferentiated hMSCs (“Undifferentiated”) except that the expression of type II collagen (COL2) is slightly increased. Moreover, after 21 days of culture in the TGF-free medium, the glycosaminoglycan (GAG) content in the HGM hydrogels is around 3 times of that in the MeHA hydrogels. Immunohistochemical staining also shows that much more cartilage specific matrix components, including type II collagen (COL2) and chondroitin sulfate (CS), are deposited in the HGM hydrogels than in the MeHA hydrogels. It is noteworthy that under continuous medium supplementation of TGF-β1, the expression levels of these marker genes in the MeHA hydrogels are also significantly increased, indicating that the fast leakage of TGF-β1 from the MeHA hydrogels is responsible for the poor chondrogenic induction in the TGF-free medium. We postulate that the domains of the host-guest nano-clusters in the HGM hydrogels, which are more hydrophilic than those polyacrylate nano-domains of the MeHA hydrogels, may have contributed to the improved retention of the soluble growth factors within the HGM hydrogels. This speculation is supported by the fact that after a similar initial burst release, which is likely dominated by the release of the protein trapped outside the nano-domains, the HGM hydrogels release the encapsulated model proteins (bovine serum albumin, BSA) more slowly than the MeHA hydrogels. Findings from these in vitro studies suggest that the HGM hydrogels are more promising than the MeHA chemical hydrogels for in vivo applications, where continuous addition of growth factors is impractical.

14202215.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202215.value: We have developed the HGM approach for preparing supramolecular hydrogels reinforced by in situ formed multivalent host-guest nano-clusters as the crosslinking junctions of biopolymers. Such HGM approach combines the efficient host-guest complexation and in situ clustering of the host-guest complexes, thus producing robust HGM hydrogels. Our HGM hydrogels are robust enough as re-swellable freestanding 3D constructs and retain useful supramolecular properties. By virtue of the reversible host-guest interactions, our HGM hydrogels are self-healable and compressible. They can relax the compressive stress rapidly via fast host-guest disassociation and afford effective protection on the encapsulated stem cells during the compression re-molding, making them promising biomaterial that can quickly adapt to and integrate with surrounding tissues of the targeted defects. Furthermore, the HGM hydrogels reduce the fast leakage of the encapsulated growth factors, leading to the enhanced chondrogenesis of hMSCs and neocartilage formation. These results demonstrate that the HGM hydrogels are promising carrier materials of stem cells and therapeutic agents for tissue repair and regeneration.

14202215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202215.value: We are now planning to furhter evaluate the developed hydrogels for 3D culture of stem cells, immune cells and cancer cells. The developed hydrogels will provide a versatile platform to study the behaviors of a wide array of cell types in 3D culutre. We will examine the impact of cellular interactions with dynamic 3D hydrogel network on the proliferation, stemness, mechanotransduction signaling, and differentiation of human embryonic and adult stem cells. We will investigate the molecular mechanism underlying the enhanced mechanosensing and the associated differentiation of stem cells and immune cells in the hydrogels. We will evaluate the efficacy of the hydrogels as the delivery vehicles of stem cells to promote in situ tissue regeneration in an animal model. The findings from these proposed studies will provide valuable guidance for the design of synthetic 3D biomaterials matrix, which not only can assist the basic studies on stem cells and immune cells in the well-controlled biomimetic 3D microenvironment, but will also facilitate the translation of stem cells for a range of clinical applications.

14202215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202215.value: Biopolymer-based supramolecular hydrogels crosslinked by host-guest interactions are usually mechanically weak as shown in “inverted vials” instead of freestanding 3D constructs. Herein, we describe a novel host-guest macromer (HGM) approach for preparation of biopolymer-based freestanding supramolecular hydrogels. Host-guest macromers are formed by molecular self-assembly between adamantane functionalized hyaluronic acid guest polymers and mono-acrylated-cyclodextrins (mono-Ac-CD) host-monomers. Supramolecular hydrogels are readily prepared by UV-induced polymerization of the pre-assembled host-guest macromers. Such hydrogels are soely crosslinked by in situ formed multivalent host-guest nano-clusters, and show significantly reinforced mechanical properties yet still retain desirable supramolecular features. They can self-heal and be re-molded into freestanding 3D constructs which afford effective protection on the encapsulated stem cells during the compression re-molding, making them promising carriers for therapeutic cells that can quickly adapt to and integrate with surrounding tissues of the targeted defects. We demonstrate that such hydrogels not only sustain extended release of encapsulated proteinaceous growth factors (TGF) but also support chondrogenesis of the human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs).

14202815.label: Project Objectives
14202815.value: Develop new parallel laser nanomanufacturing platforms based on temporally focused ultrafast laser that enables direct area patterning with 3-D resolved capability and sub-diffraction resolution. Explore new methods to realize high-speed non-mechanical Z-scanning (along the optical axis) for nanomanufacturing by controlling the linear group velocity dispersion. Develop new methods for precise laser beam shaping based on a digital micromirror device (DMD). Study the optical and thermal effects on patterning with temporally focused light-sheets. Establish quantitative relationships among area material removal rate, threshold fluence, patterning resolution and pulsed laser parameters, e.g. pulse energy, pulse width, and repetition rate. Study and characterize the following material systems using the laser manufacturing platform: Metals, semiconductors, and polymers. Identify optimal processing parameters for each material.

14202815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202815.value: This proposal aims to (1) develop a new parallel manufacturing platform based on ultrashort pulse (~100fs) lasers and (2) study the localized optical and thermal effects for different materials in order to realize nanometer-resolution direct area patterning with the platform. To achieve the goal, an ultrashort pulse laser will be spatially focused to an area of interests and temporally focused to confine the pulse energy within a thin sheet of light (~1µm). Accordingly, 2-D patterns can be directly micro- and nano-machined; large patterning areas can be achieved with higher laser energy within the same amount of time. Ultrashort pulse lasers have been extensively used in micromachining and pulsed laser ablation etc. due to their unique characteristics. For example, they can process practically any material with high precision (300nm) and minimal thermal damage through the control of ablation threshold. However, present manufacturing approach is mainly based on scanning the focal point of a laser, which is sequential and inherently a slow process. In addition, the point-scanning process cannot be expedited by increasing the laser power as the resolution will be compromised with thermal effects, e.g. melting and redeposition. To achieve sub-diffraction direct area patterning, we propose the following new approaches for improving the laser manufacturing system. A digital micromirror device will be used to simultaneously (1) diffract the pulse laser, (2) precisely shape the beam intensity profile and (3) rapidly form 2-D and 3-D patterns for micromachining. To improve the precision (~100 nm) and eliminate unwanted dynamics when moving the sample, a non-mechanical high-speed Z-scanning concept (along the optical axis) can be realized through controlling the linear group velocity dispersion. The laser manufacturing system will then be used to study and characterize the localized optical and thermal effects induced by temporally focused light sheet in both absorptive and transparent materials, including metals, semiconductors, and polymers. The results will guide the establishment of quantitative relationships among area material removal rate, threshold fluence, patterning resolution and ultrashort laser parameters. The result of this work will substantially improve the throughput of ultrashort pulse laser machining, enabling direct area patterning without compromising the resolution. For example, a single pulse (~100fs) with 1mJ energy can now be used to pattern a large area without thermal effect. The results may also be useful in a variety of applications such as laser additive manufacturing, two-photon polymerization, and medical applications such as femtosecond laser cataract surgery or presbyopia treatments. 本項目的研究目標是：（1）開發一種基於超短脈衝激光（約100飛秒）的並行製造平台；（2）研究不同材料的局部光學和熱力學特性，從而在該平台上實現納米精度的直接面成像加工。為了實現此目標，超短脈衝激光會在空間上被聚焦在待加工平面內，同時通過時域聚焦將脈衝能量集中在一個細薄的切層內（切層厚度約1微米）。相應的，二維的圖案可以被直接以微米級或納米級精度作一次性加工。另外，大型的圖案也可以通過提高激光功率來擴大加工面積，在相同的時間內加工出來。 由於超短脈衝激光有一些獨特的特性，它在微納加工和脈衝燒蝕等領域中得到了廣泛應用。舉例來說，在實際應用中通過控制燒蝕閾值，超短脈衝激光幾乎可以以超高精度（約300納米）加工任何材料， 並且幾乎不產生任何熱效應。然而，當前的加工方法絕大多數都通過將激光聚焦成一個點來做逐點加工，這種方法不可避免地極大降低了加工速度。另外，這種點掃描的加工方式不能通過提高激光功率來加快速度，因為隨之而來的熱效應如融化和二次沉積會降低加工精度。 為了實現亞衍射極限精度的面加工，我們提出了以下幾種方法來提高激光加工系統的性能。該方法其中一個核心器件是數字微鏡陣列（DMD）。它將會被用於：（1）衍射入射激光；（2）精確地改變激光的能量密度分佈；（3）高速地產生用於二維和三維加工的圖案。為了在移動工件時消除多餘的振動同時提高精度，我們通過調整線性群速度色散來實現一種非機械的高速縱軸（平行於光軸方向）掃描。接著，該激光加工系統將會被用於研究和歸納時域聚焦對不同材料所產生的局部光學和熱力學效應，包括金屬、半導體和聚合物等吸收型或透明材料。這些相應的結果會被用來定量地確定一系列加工中的參數和其相互關係，例如單位面積材料去除率，閾值選擇，圖案精度和激光參數間的函數關係。 這項工作的成果將極大地提高超短脈衝激光的加工速度和產出，同時使在不降低精度的情況下直接進行面成像加工成為可能。舉例而言，一個擁有1毫焦能量的單一脈衝可在不產生熱效應的情況下加工一個較大的區域。這些成果擁有著廣泛的應用前景，比如激光增量製造，雙光子聚合，以及生物醫藥方面的應用如飛秒激光白內障手術和老花眼矯正等。

14202815.label: Realisation of objectives
14202815.value: We have achieved all project objectives satisfactorily. Specifically, by exploiting the concept of temporal focusing, our team has developed a light sheet-based parallel laser-micromachining system, achieving nanometer level resolution, i.e., 140 nm / 175 nm in lateral / axial directions, and ultra-precise 2-D and 3-D patterning on metals, silicon and polymers. These results have been published in different scientific journals (Publication #1 - #7). For objective 1, 4 and 5, the results of our study are reported in Publication #2 and #4. For objective 3, the results of the study is reported in Publication #2 and #4. For objective 3, the results of the study is reported in Publication #1 and #7. For objective 2 (“explore new methods to realize high-speed non-mechanical Z-scanning for nanomanufacturing by controlling the linear group velocity dispersion”), we have experimentally demonstrated ultrafast axial scanning (10s kHz) via GVD control. One limiting issue of GVD control is that the resolution becomes gradually compromised as the light sheet shifts away from the original focal plane. So we did not include the study in our recent publications. Yet, this high speed scanning method may find important applications in fast 3-D fluorescent imaging and be included in our future microscope systems.

14202815.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202815.value: Based on the concept of temporal focusing, our team has developed a light sheet-based parallel laser-micromachining system; the light sheet, which is generated by a high intensity femtosecond laser amplifier, has a thickness of ~3 microns; arbitrary 2-D patterns can be generated on the light sheet via a digital micromirror device (DMD) [See principles in Publication #2 and #4]. Sub-diffraction limit 3-D nanofabrication has been demonstrated on polymers through point spread function engineering and power-thresholding, achieving the best reported resolution (~140 nm) and speed (~10 mm3/hr) to date, ~ 4 orders of magnitude faster than state-of-the-art systems producing structures of similar / lower resolution [Publication #4]. By combining temporal focusing with electrodeposition, we have realized the most precise and high-throughput 3-D metal printing [See principles in Publication #3]. To address fast axial scanning, binary holograms are applied to the DMD; as such, axial scanning can be realized by switching the designed holograms in a discrete fashion at high speeds, i.e., 22.7 kHz, limited by the DMD pattern rate [Publication #1]. On a 40X objective lens, the scanning range is ~500 micron with a minimum step size of 270 nm, which is sufficiently fine for fabrication applications. Next, the binary axial scanning concept is further extended to perform XYZ random-access scanning; the new scanning method is applied in two-photon microscopy, realizing new functionalities and applications in optogenetics [Publication #7]. We also extend the application of the temporal focusing system to the field of nonlinear imaging. To enhance the resolution, we developed new structured illumination algorithms to substantially enhance the axial resolution and imaging speed, which had been a limiting factor for temporal focusing imaging system. [See principles in Publication #5 and #6.]

14202815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202815.value: All of the proposed tasks have been completed. Currently, we are developing methods to control the curvature and shape of the femtosecond light sheet as well as custom-develop functional two-photon resins to directly fabricate functional devices, e.g. pressure sensors, via the temporal focusing laser fabrication system.

14202815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202815.value: This project creates a new laser fabrication system that uses a programmable depth-resolved light sheet to define 2-D and 3-D structures with a record resolution (~140 nm) and speed (~10 mm3/hr), which is 4 orders of magnitude better than any existing technology. (Note that conventional systems perform fabrication via raster-scanning procedures.) Due to the nature of the femtosecond laser, the light sheet can be used to process any material, e.g., semiconductor, metal, ceramics, and polymers. This new fabrication solution will bring significant impact to the nanotechnology, photonic and semiconductor industries. On the other hand, the concept of temporal focusing is used in nonlinear fluorescent imaging; based on our new imaging processing algorithm, the system demonstrates fast imaging speed (500 frames per second) for in vivo imaging experiments.

14203015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203015.value: Our goal is to develop highly efficient forward- and backward-propagation for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in pixelwise classification and to achieve significant speedup in several orders. It will fundamentally change the training and test process of many CNN-based computer vision applications and will serve as the foundation of many more innovations on CNNs. CNN achieved great success on computer vision. As the foundation of CNN, forward propagation and backpropagation were designed for whole-image classification tasks (i.e. predicting one class label for a whole image). However, it has fundamental problems for pixelwise classification (i.e. predicting a class label for every pixel), which limits its efficiency and effectiveness in many important applications, such as image segmentation, scene labeling and object detection. (1) Naive patch-by-patch scanning adopted by existing approaches has a lot of redundant computation, making training and testing CNNs extremely inefficient. Existing compromised solutions have to sacrifice resolutions or accuracies, and are infeasible for realtime applications. (2) For pixelwise classification, available training samples (i.e. image patches centered around pixels) are more than those in whole-image classification (whose training samples are whole images) in several orders, since each pixel has a class label. However, only a very small portion of image patches were used for training CNN due to the efficiency of forward- and backward-propagation. (3) Existing approaches treat these training patches independently, discarding their spatial information. Our proposed forward- and backward-propagation algorithms can save all the redundant computation, while producing exactly the same results as naive patch-by-patch scanning. Preliminary results show that a speedup of more than 1000 times can be achieved on images of 256 by 256. The speedup could be much larger as the sizes of images and patches increase. It not only makes realtime applications possible, but also can utilize all the training patches by solving the efficiency problem. The fast forward propagation makes it possible to update the error maps constantly to guide training. We will investigate multiple strategies of sampling informative training patches from the error maps by considering their spatial distributions. The proposed technologies will be applied to multiple important computer vision applications including image segmentation, scene labeling and object detection. They will also be generalized to video analysis by incorporating 3D filters and 3D convolution, with even higher speedup. The outcome will have substantial impact because of its fundamental contributions to CNN and breaking the bottleneck for a broad range of CNN-based applications. 本項目的目標是研究卷積網絡中高效的前向和反向傳播算法，將像素級分類任務的速度提高數個量級。它將會從根本上改變許多基於卷積網絡的計算機視覺應用的訓練和測試過程。並為更多的關於卷積網絡的創新提供基礎。 卷積網絡在計算機視覺領域取得了巨大的成功。作為卷積網絡的基礎，前向和反向傳播設計的初衷是用於全圖的分類任務，即為整幅圖像預測一個類別標籤。然而，它在處理像素級分類任務時（即對每個像素預測一個標籤）存在根本性的問題，在諸如圖像分割、場景分割、和物體檢測等重要應用中限制了其效率和有效性。(1) 現有方法簡單採取對圖像小塊逐個掃描，產生了大量冗餘計算，使得訓練和測試卷積網絡效率極低。現有折中的解決方案需要犧牲分辨率或者準確率，不可能用於實時的應用。 (2) 在像素級分類中，每個像素都有一個標籤，訓練樣本（像素周圍的圖像小塊）比整幅圖像分類的訓練樣本（訓練樣本是整幅圖像）多幾個數量級。然而，由於前向和反向傳播的效率低，只有很小部分的圖像小塊被用於訓練卷積網絡。 (3) 現有方法獨立對待訓練圖像小塊，丟棄了他們的空間信息。 我們提出的前向和反向傳播算法可以節省所有的冗餘計算，同時保證輸出和逐個圖像小塊掃描完全一致的結果。初步的試驗結果表明，在256×256的圖像上可以取得上千倍的加速。隨著圖像和圖像小塊尺寸的增加，可以取得更大的加速。它不但使得實時的應用成為可能，而且通過解決效率問題可以利用所有的訓練圖像小塊。快速前向傳播可以在訓練過程中以常數時間複雜度計算錯誤分佈圖。我們將會研究多種策略，根據誤分佈圖對具有信息量的訓練圖像小塊進行採樣，並考慮它們的空間分佈。提出的技術可以用於眾多計算機視覺的應用，包括圖像分割、場景分割、和物體檢測。它們也可以擴展到3D濾波器，用於視頻分析，取得更高的加速比。 本項目的研究成果將會產生巨大的影響力，它不但對於卷積網絡有根本性的貢獻，也解決了很多基於卷積網絡的應用的技術瓶頸。

14203015.label: Realisation of objectives
14203015.value: All the objectives in this project have been realized successfully. (1) We proposed highly efficient algorithms for performing forward and backward propagation of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for pixelwise classification on images. It was one of the first attempts to utilize fully convolutional neural network to generate exactly the same result as patch-by-patch scanning, without sacrificing the resolutions of predicted label maps or early rejecting any patches. Experimental results show that more than 1,500 times speedup was achieved on 256x256 images for both forward and backward propagation. Theoretical analysis shows that compared with patch-by-patch scanning, the complexity of our algorithms is much less sensitive to patch size and the speedup increases with the sizes of images and patches. This is important since image resolutions will become higher and higher in future applications and CNNs prefer large patches which contain more contextual information. The proposed algorithms also have potential impact on CNN training. With fast forward propagation, the prediction errors of all the pixels in an image can be estimated quickly at every backward propagation iteration. The computation complexity of our backward propagation is constant with respect to the number of image patches selected. (2) We proposed an effective sampling strategy to sample online hard negative pixel-level samples to improve the training stability as well as the classification accuracy. In each iteration, all the pixels are first processed by the forward computation of the deep neural network to estimate the classification errors of each pixel. In conventional pixelwise learning systems, when training is close to convergence, most of the pixels would have small training errors and the small number of pixels with large training errors would be overwhelmed by the easy samples (with smaller errors). To alleviate the problem, after forward propagation, the top k1% most difficult pixel samples are chosen as the online negative sample set, and the other k2% randomly sampled pixels from the image are selected as the random sample set. The errors of the two sets of samples are combined and back-propagated to update the network parameters. Such a procedure repeats for each iteration. In this way, the most difficult samples in each iteration consistently contribute to training of the proposed pixel-wise learning system and would not be overwhelmed by the easy samples, which leads to more stable training behavior and more accurate classification performance. (3-4) We applied the proposed efficient forward and backward propagation algorithms to different computer vision applications, including object detection, pose estimation, and video analysis. For object detection, algorithms were proposed for detecting objects in videos. Tubelets in videos are either created by tracking algorithms or by a Tubelet Proposal Network. After ROI-pooling features from feature maps at tubelet locations, 1D CNN or LSTM are then utilized to classify whether the tubelets belong to certain object classes. For pose estimation, we proposed end-to-end learning algorithms that combine traditional probabilistic models, such as Conditional Random Field and mixture of parts, to improve the estimation accuracy. For crowd video analysis, we proposed a novel spatio-temporal CNN, named Slicing CNN, based on the decomposition of 3D feature maps into 2D spatio- and 2D temporal-slices representations. The model is capable of capturing dynamics of different semantic units such as groups and objects. It learns separated appearance and dynamic representations while keeping proper interactions between them and exploits the selectiveness of spatial filters to discard irrelevant background clutter for crowd understanding.

14203015.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203015.value: As research outcomes, 1 journal paper and 20 conference papers were published. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (PAMI) is the best journal on computer vision. 20 papers were published in the top computer vision and machine learning conferences (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, and NIPS). Object detection is a fundamental task in computer vision. State-of-the-art deep learning based methods mostly adopt ROI-pooling operation to extract candidate object information from feature maps, which requires efficient convolution for obtaining high-resolution feature maps. In (Part C.9 No. 8) we propose a cascaded object detection algorithm operating on high-resolution feature maps. In (Part C.9 Nos. 4 & 9), algorithms were proposed for detecting objects in videos. Tubelets in videos are either created by tracking algorithms or by a Tubelet Proposal Network. 1D CNN or LSTM are then utilized to classify whether the tubelets belong to certain object classes. Algorithms with efficient convolution were also proposed for detecting relationships from images. In (Part C.9 No. 10), the relationship detection problem is treated as three inter-connected recognition problems. A Phrase-guided Message Passing Structure was designed to establish the connection among relationship components and to model solving the three problems jointly. State-of-the-art results were achieved on object detection, object detection from videos, and relationship detection. Pose estimation aims to predict human joint locations from 2D input images. Accurate joint location estimation requires using high-resolution feature maps generated from our proposed efficient convolution algorithm. In (Part C.9 No. 1), we proposed an end-to-end framework for human pose estimation that combines deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with the expressive deformable mixture of parts. In (Part C.9 No. 12), we proposed to compose Conditional Random Field (CRF) with CNN to simultaneously model structural information in both output and hidden feature layers in a probabilistic way. In (Part C.9 No. 13), in additional to combine the CRF model into the CNN model, we further combined the holistic attention model, which focuses on the global consistency of the full human body, and the body part attention model for detailed descriptions of different body parts. In (Part C.9 No. 14), we designed a Pyramid Residual Module (PRMs) to enhance the invariance in scales of CNNs. Our proposed efficient algorithms have also been widely applied to person analysis (Part C.9 Nos. 7, 15-20) and crowd analysis (Part C.9 Nos. 3, 5, 6).

14203015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203015.value: In our study, we found that the proposed efficient forward and backward propagation algorithms could significantly accelerate the training of pixel-level classification deep learning systems up to several orders. The proposed online hard negative sampling strategy shows great potential in improving systems' accuracy and performance. We will further investigate different strategies for online sampling training samples to increase the robustness and efficiency of the training procedure. We will also explore to utilize the proposed forward and backward propagation algorithms in more pixel-wise learning applications, such as optical flow, stereo estimation, image super-resolution, to further extend its usability.

14203015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203015.value: The key objective of this project is to investigate efficient forward- and backward-propagation to accelerate the training and evaluation of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in pixelwise classification applications. It can achieve significant speedup in CNN training for several orders. The algorithms results in efficient online hard negative sampling strategies for improving the training stability and classification accuracy. The proposed forward and backward propagation algorithms could be widely applied in various pixel-wise classification systems, such as object detection, pose estimation, video analysis.

14203115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203115.value: The aim of this project is to develop the methodology and a set of enabling technologies for building patient-specific virtual operative models facilitating surgeons to understand the microsurgical anatomy of meningiomas, and implementing virtual environments for the planning and training of microsurgery for meningiomas. In a population-based study, meningiomas account for around 40% of all primary intracranial neoplasms, and the success of the microsurgery requires the surgeon to grasp firm knowledge of complex anatomic landmarks around the lesions and exquisite microsurgical skills of incision and dissection. In this project, we focus on tuberculum sellae (TS) meningiomas but the techniques developed can also be applied to the treatment of other kinds of meningiomas. TS meningiomas arise from the dura of the TS, where the surrounding anatomy is remarkably complex. The goal of microsurgery for TS meningiomas is complete removal of the tumor and preservation of the surrounding neurovascular structures, especially the optic nerves and cerebral arteries. Millimeter-level errors in the surgery may lead to loss of acuity (even blindness), hemorrhage or infarction from vascular injury, oculomotor palsy, and etc. To the end, it is essential for the neurosurgeons to carefully study the individualized anatomic variations of a patient and choose an optimal scheme before performing the surgery. Currently, physicians and surgeons employ MR and CT images to diagnose meningiomas and perform the preoperative planning. Although with the development of neuroradiologic techniques, these images can provide more and more exquisite anatomic details, it is still difficult for surgeons to identify the exact relationship of the meningioma to neighboring structures from these images. On the other hand, current training paradigm using cadavers and plastic models cannot mimic the real surgical environments, making novices difficult to acquire the necessary skills to perform this complicated surgery. We will develop 3D patient-specific virtual microanatomy models with the tumor, the incision path to it and its essential neighboring structures. Based on the models, we will implement a virtual reality based platform for interactive planning and training. The research issues to be addressed include image segmentation, registration and fusion, anatomical model reconstruction, biomechanically-based modeling, realistic visualization, and multi-sensory interaction. To summarize, this is a joint project of a pioneer VR development team, a leading neurosurgery team and an outstanding neuro-radiology team in Hong Kong. The proposed methodology and the set of techniques are anticipated to strengthen and compensate existing meningiomas microsurgical planning and training paradigm and advance related VR research. 本項目的目標是研究構建患者特異性虛擬手術解剖模型的方法論和一系列關鍵技術，促進手術醫生對腦膜瘤顯微解剖知識的理解，並為顯微腦膜瘤手術計劃和訓練提供一個逼真的虛擬環境。一項基於人群的研究表明，腦膜瘤的發病率佔主要顱內腫瘤的40%，並且， 顯微腦膜瘤手術的成功需要醫生清晰地掌握創傷附近的複雜解剖結構知識以及嫻熟的切割剝離等顯微手術技巧。在本專項中，我們集中探討鞍結節腦膜瘤，但專項中開發的技術也適用於其他類型腦膜瘤的治療。 鞍結節腦膜瘤發源與鞍結節的硬腦膜，其附近的解剖結構異常複雜。顯微手術的目的是完全切除腫瘤並保留周圍的腦血管組織，特別是視神經和腦動脈組織。在這一手術中，毫米級的誤差將會導致視力下降（甚至失明）、血管創傷引起的出血梗塞、眼神經麻痺等並發症。因此，神經外科醫師有必要仔細研究每一名患者解剖結構的特異性並為其選擇最優的手術方案。 當前，醫生利用MR和CT圖像診斷腦膜瘤並進行術前規劃。隨著腦放射成像技術的發展，這些圖像可以提供越來越多的精細解剖細節供醫生參考，然而，醫生通過這些圖像精確地確定腦膜瘤與周遭組織的結構關係仍是十分困難的。另一方面，目前的手術訓練模式使用屍體和塑膠模型進行訓練，這些訓練手段不能呈現逼真的術中環境，造成新的醫生不能掌握這一複雜手術所需的必要技能。在本專項中，我們將開發三維患者特異性虛擬顯微解剖模型，包括腫瘤、通往腫瘤的手術路徑及其關鍵的周圍組織。在此模型基礎上，我們還將開發一個基於虛擬現實的可交互腦膜瘤顯微手術計劃與訓練平台。本研究需解決的問題包括：圖像分割、配準與融合、解剖模型重建、生物力學建模、真實感可視化以及多感知人機交互等。 我們的項目聯合了香港頂尖的虛擬現實研發團隊、神經外科手術團隊和神經影像團隊。項目衍生的方法論和一系列技術將加強和補益現有的腦膜瘤顯微手術計劃和訓練模式，同時推動虛擬現實技術的進步。

14203715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14203715.value: 基於鐵磁性納米顆粒的群體螺旋狀微型機械人的體內靶向治療研究

14203715.label: Project Objectives
14203715.value: The overall objective is to understand the collective behavior of magnetic helical microrobots, which are capable of performing in vivo tracking and disassembly to form MNP suspensions, for targeted drug delivery in vivo. The essential technical objectives of this proposed project are listed as follows. To achieve mass-production of helical swimming microrobots using spirulina-templates, and obtain optimized parameters for batch fabrication and magnetic actuation. To understand the interaction of microfluidic and magnetic forces exerted on the adjacent swimming microrobots. The investigation will begin with two micro-agents, and then increase to three and/or multi-agent dynamic systems. To realize controlled disassembly of the helical microrobots for obtaining MNP nanorobotic swarms using ultrasound, and then achieve navigation of the MNP swarm in vitro. To realize functionalized magnetic microrobots which can be tracked using fluorosence for in vivo/in vitro imaging and navigation. To demonstrate in vivo swimming of micro- and nanorobotic swarms, tracked by fluorescence, which are capable of performing swimming inside a mouse peritoneal cavity and/or mouse bladders using magnetic fields for targeted delivery tasks.

14203715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203715.value: 本項目旨在設計和研發基於鐵磁性納米顆粒的微納機械人群體效應以用於體內的主動式靶向藥物輸送。在該項目中，我們將系統性地研究用生物模板法和納米顆粒自組裝加工的螺旋狀微型機械人在旋轉磁場下的群體運動，和找到一種群體控制和視覺捕捉該微型機械人運動的方法以用於體內的追蹤和靶向診療。天然螺旋藻將被用於批量製備該螺旋機械人的生物模板。該加工方法的優勢是可以低成本、大批量的製備殼狀的、由磁性納米顆粒自組裝生成的磁性螺旋結構。在成功製備該螺旋微型結構后，我們將首先研究兩個和多個微型機械人基於流體和磁力的相互間作用。模擬和實驗定量分析將同步展開以理解他們對於機械人群體運動控制的影響。然後，我們將利用低功率的超聲波來機械法分解螺旋狀微型機械人成更小的磁性納米顆粒群體，并研究相關的納米尺度群體運動特點。最後，利用螢光標記的微型機械人，我們也計劃進行動物實驗，以深入瞭解這些磁性微納機械人群體在體內的運動、磁控和追蹤。

14203715.label: Realisation of objectives
14203715.value: The aim of this project is to design and investigate micro- and nanorobotic swarms of magnetic nanoparticle (MNP)-based microrobots for targeted cargo delivery such as cells and drug, for in vivo applications. During the first half period of the project, we have achieved mass-production of helical swimming microrobots using spirulina-templates, and obtained optimized parameters for batch fabrication and magnetic actuation of those robotic microagents. It was discovered that the MNP coating thickness has a tradeoff for fluorescence imaging, degrading and actuation. We have realized a type of biohybrid magnetite microrobot that is imageable, biodegradable, and selectively cytotoxic to cancer cells. The fabrication uses a facile one step-only approach using magnetite NPs, which is cost-effective and suitable for large-scale production. Our results suggest that the fabricated biohybrid microagent is capable of performing robust navigation in various biofluids and being noninvasively tracked by autofluorescence/MR imaging in either superficial tissues or deep organs. Furthermore, it exhibits desired biodegradability, remote diagnostic sensing ability, and anticancer potential. With its features of in vivo monitor via bimodal imaging, tunable degradation via dip-coating control, and inclusiveness of functionality extension/drug loading via surface modification, this biohybrid microagent represents a microbiorobotic vehicle with a high potential for imaging-guided therapy. Furthermore, it may have far-reaching significance as a proof of concept for the development of microrobots and nanorobots with multiple functions. The main discovery of this part has been published in the ranked #1 Robotics journal "Science Robotics", and it was also highlighted in the Science news. During the project period, the PI's lab applied COMSOL and analytical modeling to study the interaction of microfluidic and magnetic forces exerted on the adjacent swimming micro- and nanorobotics agents. Millions of MNP were applied as the building blocks for nanorobotic delivery. We found out that the MNP can be disassembled and gathered into a small dynamic area by applying a programmed magnetic field. The results were shown in our journal paper published in IEEE Transactions on Robotics (T-RO) in 2017. Another discover is that by applying a rotating magnetic field with an optimized pitch angle, the nanorobotic MNP swarm can be transported as an entity in a synchronized manner. The results were presented in the IEEE ICRA2017 conference. It is notable that MNP swarm can be obtained by the disassembly of bio-templated helical microrobots using ultrasound or by chemical synthesis approach. We had investigated pattern generation, reversible merging, and splitting of MNP swarming patterns, and their locomotion properties. navigated locomotion with an intact pattern. The nanoparticle chains inside the MNP swarm perform synchronized motions, making the swarm as a dynamic structure. The generation process, the responses of the MNP swarm to the input frequency of the rotating magnetic fields and the spread state are modeled individually. The corresponding experimental results have good agreement with the models. Through the spread state, the change of the patterns, e.g. merging and splitting of MNP swarms, have been realized for the first time, showing their high controllability and flexibility when actuated by magnetic fields. Furthermore, a VPNS can be navigated as an entity with a stable pattern when the magnetic field has a small pitch angle. The trapping forces that are critical to the synchronized locomotion of the swarm have been investigated by analyzing and simulating the behaviors of non-magnetic spheres. Finally, demonstrations of VPNSs passing through channels with high access rates have been presented. This part of research were also published in a prestigious robotics journal IJRR in 2018. Then, we investigated the generation and remote actuation of the MNP swarms in biological fluids. By analysing and summarising the performances of the swarms in fluids with different physical conditions, the PI's lab proposed a strategy for selecting the optimised swarms in specific bio-fluids. Besides gastric acid, FBS, blood plasma and HA, two types of biofluids that are directly extracted from living bodies are used for validation, i.e. whole blood and vitreous humour. As a result, we validate that magnetic field-induced swarms are not sensitive to ionic strength, and it can be generated in fluids with relatively lower viscosities. Other field-induced swarms actuated by different stimulus may also be sensitive to fluidic viscosity, e.g. the increased viscosity may hinder the formation of the linear collective array of metallic rods actuated by ultrasound. In contrast, medium induced swarms have the potential to be applied in fluids with higher viscosities and fibrous meshes. The experimental validations have good agreements with the prediction. Finally, we demonstrate the ex vivo generation of medium-induced swarms and their targeted deliveries in a bovine eyeball. This work, which was published in Nature Communications in 2019, sheds light on the fundamental understanding of microrobotic swarms, and it is an important step further towards the in vivo targeted delivery.

14203715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203715.value: The major findings and research outcomes from this GRF project is very fruitful. The PI's group has published several key papers in top journals, including Science Robotics, Nature Communications, IJRR (The International Journal of Robotics Research) , and IEEE T-RO (IEEE Transactions on Robotics). We have also promoted the results top robotics conferences, such as ICRA and IROS. Some of the key finding and research outcomes are listed in the following papers: 1. L. Zhang et al., Multifunctional biohybrid magnetite microrobots for imaging-guided therapy, Science Robotics (AAAS), Vol. 2, eaaq1155, 2017. (Impact factor: 19.4, Ranked #1 in the category of “Robotics” in ISI Web of Science) Note: This work has been highlighted in Science News (https://www.sciencemag.org/news/2017/11/robot-made-algae-can-swim-through-your-body-thanks-magnets, by Hong Kong RGC YouTube Channel, https://youtu.be/l2NQfgW8tSQ.) The work is indexed as an ISI Highly Cited Paper. In this paper, a new type of multi-functional helical microrobots has been developed based on the new concept of biohybrid design. We report that the batch fabrication of helical microrobots can be realized using biotemplating approach with ease by using microalgae. Moreover, for the first time, the microrobotic agents are capable of in-vivo tracking using dual imaging modalities, i.e. fluorescent imaging and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and with controlled degradability. The results undoubtedly make an important step towards the use of wirelessly controlled micro-medical robots for image-guided minimally invasive intervention. 2. L. Zhang et al., Ultra-extensible Ribbon-like Magnetic Microswarm, Nature Communications, Vol. 9, 3260, 2018. (Note: this work has been highlighted in Nature News (https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-018-06120-x). 3. L. Zhang et al., Active generation and magnetic actuation of microrobotic swarms in bio-ﬂuids, Nature Communications, Vol. 10, 5631, 2019. 4. L. Zhang et al., Pattern generation and motion control of a vortex-like paramagnetic nanoparticle swarm, International Journal of Robotics Research (IJRR), Vol. 37, Issue 8, 912-930, 2018. In the second half of this project, the PI's lab used applied magnetic fields to trigger the generation of two kinds of MNP swarms. (I) Pattern generation and motion control of a vortex-like paramagnetic nanoparticle swarm are firstly investigated. For the first time, we use rotating magnetic fields to effectively gather dispersed nanoparticles into a dynamically stable entity. Distributed control methods therefore can be converted to a synchronised fashion, which greatly reduces the complexity and increases the efficiency. The major results were published in T-RO(2017) and IJRR(2018). (II). Ultra-extensible ribbon-like magnetic microswarm is investigated. We reported a strategy to reconfigure paramagnetic nanoparticles into ribbon-like swarms (RPNS) using oscillating magnetic fields, and the mechanisms are analysed for their potential application in vivo.

14203715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203715.value: The future development of the research can be focused on both fundamental understanding on microrobotic swarm and the practical applications of microswarms for biomedicine, e.g. localized drug delivery. In nature, various types of swarm behaviors occur, such as a flock of birds and a swarm of ants, which stem from local communications of limited individuals. Through collective pattern formation and reconfiguration, these animals dramatically change their swarming patterns according to the environment they interact with. To date, some large-scale robotic systems can well mimic the complex swarm behaviors of natural creatures through algorithm design and wireless communication (“Programmable self-assembly in a thousand-robot swarm,” Science, vol. 345, no. 6198, pp. 795–799, 2014). However, due to the absence of onboard processers, sensors and actuators, to create a robotic system with functional swarm behaviors at the small scales remains challenging. Therefore, the investigation of magnetic nanoparticles as building blocks to investigate collective behavior of microrobotic swarm in biofluids are highly required if we want to apply them for in vivo applications. For practical applications, on one hand, it is apparent that the animal studies need to be conducted by using the functionalized microrobotic swarm. On the other hand, the delivery strategy of the microrobotic swarm to deep-and-narrow spaces inside the human body need to be further explored.

14203715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203715.value: Remotely actuated microrobots have the potential for numerous applications, ranging from ex-vivo tasks, such as micromanipulation, sorting and microassembly, to in-vivo biomedical applications for minimally invasive medicine, due to their small sizes and accessibility to hard-to-reach regions inside human body. However, in a more practical scenario, the loading capacity is low for a single microrobot, and the small volume challenges the resolution of real-time imaging devices. As a promising way to tackle the problems, to actuate and control a swarm of micro-/nanorobots has emerged as one of the central research topics in microrobotics. The objective of this GRF project is to simultaneously actuate and control thousands or even millions of tiny robotic agents, named microswarm, with synchronised motion, and by adaptively performing pattern reconfiguration and navigated locomotion, the microswarms can realise targeted delivery in complex environments with a high access rate. The PI's lab has successfully demonstrated that a swarm of micro-algae-based helical microrobots can be tracked using MRI and fluorescence signals in vivo, which has high potential for image-guided therapy. Furthermore, the team has reported that a large number of magnetic nanoparticles can be applied for microrobotic swarm for targeted delivery with a high reconfigurability and controllability. The key results were published in Nature Communications, IJRR, TRO, and in many other journals

14203915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203915.value: In the era of Big Data, the Internet and other high-throughput techniques have been constantly producing huge volumes of diversified data in social and economic life, as well as in many research fields. Clustering methods, as one primary data-driven approach to learn the structure of the data, have to face the new challenge that a complicated system is often studied repeatedly from different aspects at different levels. As a result, the same population of objects is described by both their individual characteristics and their pairwise relationship. Therefore, we often have to integrate both vectorial data and network data to better elucidate the group structure among the objects. For example, in E-Commerce, we often need to divide customers into groups of different consumption patterns, so that we can efficiently recommend commodities to a certain customer. In this scenario, the personal information of a customer, such as the age and historical shopping records, is the vectorial data that we can use for clustering. The interrelationship between customers, such as how often two customers shop together and how often they like same Facebook posts, is the network data that we can use for clustering. Traditional clustering methods are incapable here because they can only handle either vectorial data or network data. Naive integration of individual clustering results will lead to serious inefficiency. We propose a probabilistic model for random partitions in the presence of both types of data. Both the number of clusters and the cluster memberships of all objects are modeled as random variables. An MCMC-based Bayesian approach will be designed to fit this hierarchical model to the combined data set. With this new efficient and interpretable clustering technique, the hidden grouping structure under both the multivariate data of individual objects and the weighted network data can be inferred simultaneously within a joint model, thus borrowing strength from both sides. As to our knowledge, this will be the first clustering method which can incorporate both vectorial data and network data in a principled way. Our preliminary studies show that this model-based integrative clustering approach has a great potential to significantly improve the clustering accuracy over naive combining methods. 在大數據時代，互聯網和其他高通量技術在社會經濟生活和許多研究領域中不斷地產生出大量的多樣化數據。聚類方法作為一個主要的數據驅動的結構學習方法，必須面對一個新的挑戰：複雜系統通常被重複地從不同方面做研究；其結果是相同的對象群體既由其個體特性又由其成對關係來描述。因此，我們經常要整合矢量數據和網絡數據，以更好地闡明對象之間的聚類結構。例如，在電子商務中，我們經常需要劃分客戶到不同的消費模式群組，這樣我們就可以有效地推薦商品到對應的客戶群。在這種情況下，一個顧客的年齡和歷史購物記錄等個人信息，是其矢量數據；客戶之間的相互關係，例如兩客戶一起購物的頻度或他們喜歡相同Facebook貼子的次數，是我們可以拿來聚類的網絡數據。 傳統聚類方法不能同時處理矢量數據或網絡數據。分開聚類後整合類標的方法會導致嚴重的低效率。我們提出一個同時聚類兩種數據的概率模型。類的數量和每個對象的類標都被當成隨機變量加以推斷。為了有效的計算該層次模型，我們設計出一個基於馬爾可夫蒙特卡羅算法的貝葉斯方法。有了這個新的高效的、可解釋的聚類技術，隱藏在不同數據中的分組結構將被有效的推斷出來。據我們所知，這將是第一個有機整合矢量數據和網絡數據做聚類的方法。我們的初步研究表明，這種基於模型的綜合聚類方法具有很大的潛力；比分開聚類後整合類標的方法相比，能顯著提高聚類準確性。

14203915.label: Realisation of objectives
14203915.value: All five objectives are fully achieved. For the first objective, we developed the “Shared Clustering” model for combining the vectorial and network data. The two data types share the same underlying cluster labels. For second objective, the Bayesian approach with an MCMC algorithm is used to infer the joint cluster labels. The number of clusters is explored by an advanced Reversible Jump Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm. The third objective is achieved by extensive simulation studies based on synthesized data sets, and comparison with different approaches, including the Vectorial-only clustering, the Network-only clustering, and their consensus clustering. For the fourth objective, our method is applied on real gene expression data sets, real gene network data sets, and real molecular dynamics data sets. The results from real data sets helped us to gain better understanding of the corresponding real problems. The fifth objective is achieved by publishing related methods and their applications, and sharing related software codes online. We not only fulfilled all the above five objectives, but also extended the ideas from this project to other similar clustering problems, such as the spatial clustering on DNA, the movie clustering under high missingness, and the Poisson clustering.
