14203915.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203915.value: (Note: Journal papers listed in Part C/Section 8 are cited here according to their order in the table of Section 8) As planned by the project, we investigated on Bayesian Integrative Clustering for Combining Vectorial Data and Network Data. A “Shared Clustering” model together with its Bayesian inference method is developed as a direct solution to the problem [6]. During the implementation of the project, related clustering problems and their applications are also explored. For a pure network clustering problem, a Poisson clustering method and its application on molecular dynamics data were studied [4]. For a pure vectorial data clustering problem, when high missingness exists, we developed an efficient method based on multivariate multinomial distribution and applied it on movie data [2]. For the spatial clustering of methylated sites on DNA, which is correlated incomplete vectorial data, we developed an HMM method to detect differentially methylated regions [1]. A similar DNA signal detection problem is also investigated [9]. For a special ranking data problem, a method is developed to group correlated ranking lists together and look for the cluster center, which is the consensus ranking [3]. Moreover, related conditional independence testing problem [8] and variable/model selection problem [5] are investigated. Another model selection method is developed for the grouping of nodes on a tree topology [7]. The major findings and research outcomes at the algorithm side include several new or improved clustering methods, including the Shared clustering model [6], the pairwise data clustering method [4], the topic model with high missingness [2], and the DMR detection method [1]. Important general problems of clustering methods are also investigated, including conditional independence [8] and model selection [5]. At the subject side, we not only used the developed methods of this project to solve the gene expression and gene network integration problem [6], but also applied these methods in movie clustering [2], molecular dynamics data analysis [4], and tree path inference [7].

14203915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203915.value: At the application side, the models and computing methods produced by this project can be applied to many heterogeneous data integration problems. In the new era of big data, data are measured for the same group of subjects from different angles, thus producing both individual level data and network data. Our new method can help such cases. At the methodology side, more complex clustering structures can be explored. We will continue developing new joint clustering methods along this line.

14203915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203915.value: In the era of Big Data, the Internet and other high-throughput techniques have been constantly producing huge volumes of data for both individual objects and their interactions. We often need to group these objects according to both individual-level data and network-level data. For example, in E-Commerce, we often need to divide customers into groups of different consumption patterns, so that we can efficiently recommend commodities to a certain customer. We developed a statistical method to efficiently perform such grouping task. It helps elucidate the hidden grouping structure under both the multivariate data of individual objects and the network data. As to our knowledge, this is the first clustering method which can incorporate both vectorial data and network data in a principled way.

14204015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204015.value: Broadband services represent one of the largest economic growth sectors in the world. These services are facilitated by high-speed optical networks, now shifting from 10G to 100/400G to meet the impending traffic demands. That calls for spectrally-efficient modulation and detection schemes. Coherent technology has attracted much interest due to its higher spectral efficiency over greater distance. However, this technology exhibits high cost and high power consumption, thus only suitable for long-metro and long-haul networks. Conventional low-cost solutions with directly modulated lasers (DMLs) and direct detection have been applied to not only simple on-off keying (OOK) format, but also advanced orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals. However, these schemes have fundamental limits. Therefore, there are industry needs and new research challenges to realize high speed and high spectral efficiency at low cost, while extending the transmission reach for applications such as long-reach Ethernet, mobile backbone, and short-metro networks. In this project, we will investigate the realization of advanced modulation formats with extended transmission reach using low-cost DMLs and full-field detection. By carefully designing the amplitude and chirp of DMLs, generation of advanced formats such as differential quadrature phase shift keying (DQPSK) and OFDM is feasible. On the other hand, full-field detection can recover both the amplitude and the phase of optical fields without a local oscillator. The project optimally combines the expertise of the PI gained through works such as generation of DPSK/DQPSK signals using DMLs and the experience of the Co-I on full-field detection to extend the transmission reach of OOK, DQPSK, and OFDM signals. We will investigate characteristics of DMLs, including chirp control and injection locking, and address the challenge to generate high-level formats using low-cost lasers. We will detect these signals using full-field detection with particular care on DML-related signal characteristics. Some disadvantages of DMLs compared to external modulators, such as chirps and low extinction ratio, might provide unique benefits when combined with full-field detection, by avoiding instant phase transitions in the optical field. Both single-carrier and multicarrier formats will be considered. Through the investigations, we target to find out the optimal format design that facilitates signal generation using DMLs and full-field detection to balance performance and cost. This proposal addresses recent academic and industry needs for higher-performance low-cost solutions for the next-generation 100/400G Ethernet. The work also strategically enhances the research collaborations internally and with Tyndall National Institute Ireland, for joint research on high-performance transceivers. 寬帶服務是全球最高經濟增長領域之一。這些服務利用高速光纖網絡，從10G網絡到現今的100/400G網絡，來滿足日益增長的通信需求。這需要高頻譜效率的調制格式和相應的檢測方案。相干技術由於能夠使光纖通信具有更高的頻譜效率和更遠的傳輸距離，因而引起了很大的研究興趣。然而，這項技術需要較高的成本和功率消耗，因此只適用於城域和長途網絡。使用直接調制激光器（DML）和直接檢測技術的低成本傳統解決方案，不僅可以應用簡單的開關鍵控（OOK）格式，而且還能夠應用先進的正交頻分複用（OFDM）格式。但是這些方案也存在缺陷。因此，實現高速、高頻譜效率的低成本通信，並且延伸長距離以太網、移動骨幹網和短距離城域網絡等的傳輸距離，是行業的需要也是值得研究的課題。 在此項目中，我們將研究先進的調制格式，並應用低成本的直接調制激光器和全場檢測方式來延長信號傳輸距離。通過改變直接調制激光器的幅度和啁啾來產生差分正交相移鍵控（DQPSK）和OFDM等先進格式的方法是可行的。另一方面，全場檢測可以在沒有本地振盪器的情況下，恢復光載波的振幅和相位。該項目結合了主研究員在使用直接調制激光器產生DPSK/DQPSK信號格式方面的專長和副研究員在應用全場檢測方式延長OOK，DQPSK和OFDM等信號傳輸距離方面的經驗。我們將研究直接調制激光器的特徵，包括啁啾控制、注入鎖定等，並探索如何使用低成本的激光器來產生高階調制格式。我們將利用全場檢測方式來解調信號，同時關注直接調制激光器對信號的影響。直接調制激光器相比於外部調制器的一些缺點，如啁啾和低消光比等，能避免光域的瞬時相位轉變，反而使其在全場檢測中具有獨特的優勢。單載波和多載波的調製格式都將被考慮。本研究項目的目標是，探索適用於直接調制激光器產生和全場檢測的最優調制格式，以平衡系統的性能和成本。

14204015.label: Realisation of objectives
14204015.value: To achieve the objectives of this project, we have developed several novel techniques to enhance the transmission performance of optical systems. Efficient combinations of these proposed techniques have been extensively investigated in both optical fiber and optical wireless direct-detection systems. All the developed schemes are applicable to the full-field detection applications as complex signals can also be reconstructed in direct-detection optical systems. The summary of the research works carried out during this project is presented as follows, • The first investigation of intensity-modulation/direct-detection (IM/DD) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) using the power-efficient set-partitioned QAM (SP-QAM) format was presented in [J1][C4]. We derived the SP-64QAM for optical IM/DD systems, wherein the SP-64QAM format showed higher power efficiency and enhanced transmission performance than that of the SP-128QAM and 8QAM. Furthermore, we also showed that power-efficient SP formats with fine spectral efficiency granularity can be more effective to maximize the capacity of multi-carrier OFDM based optical systems. We derived an adaptive bit and power loading algorithm for the SP-QAM formats and experimentally investigated the corresponding transmission performance [C4]. It was shown that up to ~17% capacity enhancement (from 36 Gbit/s to 42 Gbit/s) can be attained for 40-km single-mode fiber transmission. Furthermore, the adaptive algorithm also demonstrated improved tolerance to fiber nonlinearity and provided more power budget for the overall system. This work addressed Objective 3 of this project, and the proposed schemes can be beneficial to the Kramer-Kronig receiver based full-field detection systems, wherein direct-detection is also adopted. • In [J2][C2][C5], a channel-independent single-band and multi-band orthogonal circulant matrix transform (OCT) based precoding scheme for the OFDM-based systems was proposed and numerically/experimentally demonstrated. The main idea of this work was to address the inherent bandwidth limitation issue of directly modulated lasers light sources, such as direct modulation lasers (DMLs) or light-emitting diodes (LEDs). The limited bandwidth will severely distort the generated optical signals when higher speed is targeted. We showed that compared to the conventional discrete Fourier transform (DFT) precoding, the proposed OCT precoding exhibits enhanced tolerance of inter-symbol interference (ISI) with the same CP length. The performance was experimentally verified and results indicated that the bit-loaded multi-band OCT precoding [J2], i.e., loading different order of QAM formats to different OCT precoded sub-bands, exhibited comparable BER with the optimal bit and power loading, whilst its implementation complexity was significantly lower. Although demonstrated in the visible LED/LD based visible light communication (VLC) system, the proposed scheme does not have specific requirements on the OFDM format. Hence, these proposed schemes are also feasible in DML-based optical fiber transmission systems to combat the impairments induced by the DMLs when using them to generating high-speed optical signals. This study aligned with Objectives 1 and 2 of this project. • We proposed the joint/individual OCT precoding scheme to boost the capacity of OFDM-based VLC system with multiple transmitters and multiple receivers [C3]. The optimal singular value decomposition (SVD) based adaptive loading scheme has also been proposed and demonstrated for performance evaluations [C6]. The idea of the joint/individual OCT precoding was to jointly/individually pre-code and de-code the multiple channels, such that the severe fading in the multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) can be combated. Differently, the singular value decomposition (SVD) was utilized to decompose the MIMO channel matrix, such that the equivalent channel gains of the system can be extracted for adaptive bit and power loading. Results show that the joint/individual OCT precoding offered significant performance improvement over conventional MIMO-OFDM scheme without prior knowledge of channel state information (CSI). The SVD-based adaptive loading required CSI at transceivers but achieved the optimal system BER performance. Although demonstrated in the VLC system, the proposed schemes are feasible in both IM/DD and coherent systems, including the target DML-based full-field detection systems in this project. The main contribution of this study to the delivery of this project is that it provides solutions to enhance/optimize the performance of DML-based full-field detection systems using OFDM. • In [C6], we proposed the SP-QAM based optical fast-OFDM with a novel real-valued OCT pre-coding scheme for IM/DD optical systems. The proposed scheme demonstrated an enhanced tolerance to narrow-bandwidth filtering and fiber nonlinearity. Experimental results showed that for ~20-Gbit/s transmission over 20-km single-mode fiber, around 3.5-dB receiver sensitivity improvement was attained. Further optimization of the transmission was investigated in [C6], wherein a novel hybrid PAM/two-dimensional-coded PAM (2D-PAM) based optical fast-OFDM was proposed and demonstrated. The data rate of the system was boosted to 43.68 Gbit/s. This study contributed to the realization of Objective 3 of this project. • We have also characterized DML-generated advanced formats under full-field detection and found that the key challenge is that the chirp in DML (in the scale of ~GHz) would enhance the phase noise during full-field recovery. Furthermore, we have developed the phase recovery and dispersion compensation algorithm for full-field detection and tested full-field detected OFDM using external intensity modulation (with a smaller chirp effect). It is found that full-field detection can indeed greatly enhance the transmission reach of conventional DD system and can support more than 500 km at 40 Gbit/s/channel without inline optical dispersion compensation. This work was done, in collaboration with the Co-I, at Tyndall National Institute, and the developed receiver design had been verified in 124-km field-installed British-Telecom fiber link. This study contributed to the realization of Objective 2 of this project.

14204015.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204015.value: Within this project, various digital processing techniques have been developed and extensively investigated to address the objectives of this project. The major findings are listed as follows: (1) the SP-QAM formats based optical OFDM and the corresponding adaptive loading algorithm [J1][C4], with which the SP-64QAM for optical IM/DD systems was developed and showed higher power efficiency and enhanced transmission performance than that of the SP-128QAM and 8QAM; (2) a new precoding scheme, namely, OCT precoding, for both single-band and bit-loaded multi-band to address the system bandwidth limitation issue [J2][C2][C5]; (3) the CSI-free and CSI-dependent precoding techniques for MIMO-OFDM based optical systems [C3][C1]; and (4) the SP-QAM formats based optical fast-OFDM scheme with a novel real-valued OCT pre-coding scheme for IM/DD optical systems, which demonstrated enhanced tolerance to narrow-bandwidth filtering and fiber nonlinearity [C6]. Totally, two journal publications have been published in the top tier journal, Optics Express. We have also published six conference papers in leading international conferences, including the top tier conferences, The Optical Fiber Communication Conference (OFC) and Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics (CLEO). The project also strengthens our collaborations with the oversea researchers, including the Co-I, Dr. Jian Zhao at Tyndall National Institute and University College Cork, Ireland, as well as Prof. Jing Xu at Zhejiang University, China.

14204015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204015.value: This project mainly focuses on the investigations of the advanced modulation formats using DMLs, further development of the research may include the following two aspects, (1) The performance comparison with other commercially available external modulators, such as the single- or dual-drive Mach–Zehnder modulator and the IQ modulator. It is desirable to evaluate the trade-offs of using different optical signal generation methods, especially in terms of transmission performance and implementation costs. (2) Real-time realization of the developed schemes. It is also desirable to verify the feasibility and robustness of the developed schemes in real-time transmission systems, wherein the trade-off between practical system complexity and achievable transmission performance can be identified.

14204015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204015.value: This project addresses the investigations of using advanced modulation formats in direct-modulation based optical full-field detection systems, aiming to develop low-cost and high-performance transmission solutions. This study covers the understanding of fundamental limits, the development of novel digital signal processing (DSP) techniques, and the evaluations of different performance/complexity trade-offs. The topic of this project has been attracting numerous interests from both academia and industry, as it targets using low-cost components to realize high-performance transmission. The outputs of this project provide several DSP-level techniques for performance enhancements, and help identify the trade-off between the transmission performance and cost/complexity. The outputs also lay the foundations to identify optimal solutions for further practical implementations. The outputs of this project have resulted in several publications and they are all published in top tier journal and leading international conferences. This project also helps reinforce the oversea collaborative relationship with the Tyndall National Institute and University College Cork, Ireland, and Zhejiang University, China.

14204315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204315.value: Approximately 60% of people who sustain a stroke have affected hand function at 6 months after stroke. Hand function recovery becomes one of the most important and challenging parts in the rehabilitation program. Hand has a larger representation in the human brain. Brain signal from the Electroencephalography (EEG) is one of the approaches to interpret patient’s movement intentions. The extent of the restoration of motor function after stroke is highly depended on the remapping into the uninjured motor-related areas away from the lesion site in the brain of individual persons. However, how to help lesion brain to re-establish the motor function in the motor-related areas is a key to the successful post-stroke rehabilitation. Mirror Neuron System (MNS) was originally found in the macaque monkeys that the brain can generate signals by observing the others performing the same action, specially in the hand function task. Later researchers also found this in the healthy humans, action observation of another individual performing the same action could increase the cortical excitability of the primary motor cortex(M1) in the brain and supported by neuroimaging and electrophysiology studies using fMRI, TMS, EEG and MEG. The above information open a new potential to use action observation to facilitate the brain to relearn new task or used for neurorehabilitation after brain lesion, like stroke, by engaging similar brain regions to the action execution. Mu-suppression (8-13Hz) in the EEG has been found to be correlated with the action observation. In this proposal, a new neurofeedback system will be designed to capture the mu-suppression during the action observation. Some Brain Computer Interface(BCI) studies used motor imagery with EEG to control robotic system on stroke patients but it did not show significantly better motor function recovery. The main challenge in the motor imagery is that the stroke subject has difficulty to image how to conduct the hand function tasks without visual guide and the previous robotic system was designed for arm and shoulder movement only. Other studies showed that action observation on hand should match with similar execution task to increase the excitability in the MNS. Therefore neurofeedback using mu-suppression and robotic hand are proposed to be investigated in this proposal to facilitate hand recovery. Finally, a randomized controlled trial with a 20-session training will be carried out to compare the effectiveness in motor recovery using neurofeedback from the ipsilesional hemisphere (same side of the lesion after stroke) and neurofeedback from both hemispheres. 大約有60％中風，影響手部功能。手功能的恢復成為最重要的康復。從腦電圖信號是一個方法來解釋患者的運動意圖。如何幫助腦部重新建立運動功能區域是一個關鍵。鏡像神經元系統（MNS）的獼猴最初發現腦可以通過觀察其他執行相同的動作產生的信號，特別是在手功能任務。後來的研究者也發現了這個在健康人，動作觀察另一個人的表演同樣的動作可以增加主運動皮層（M1）在大腦皮質興奮。以上信息打開一個新的潛在使用行動觀察，以促進大腦重新學習新。腦電圖已發現與動作相關聯觀察。因此研究使用神經反饋和機器手，以促進手恢復。

14204315.label: Realisation of objectives
14204315.value: e have successfully realized the aforementioned three objectives. The details are included as the following information. Twenty-four chronic stroke subjects who suffered from first-ever stroke, and with time since stroke more than 6 months, were recruited to receive a 20-session robot-assisted hand training. Subjects were excluded if they had history of epilepsy, serious cognitive deficits, and/or comprehensive aphasia. Consent was obtained from all subjects and the protocol was approved by the local Clinical Research Ethics Committee. All stroke subjects underwent 20- session (~1.5 hours/session, ~3 sessions/week) robot-assisted hand training. In each session, the subjects were asked to sit in a comfortable chair in a radiofrequency-shielded room, facing a 23-in computer screen. Electroencephalography (EEG) signals were acquired for each subject following the international 10-20 system, with 16 active electrodes (C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, Cz, FC1, FC2, FC3, FC4, FCz, CP1, CP2, CP3, CP4) at a sampling frequency of 256 Hz. The electrode impedance was kept under 1 kΩ to maintain a good signal-to-noise ratio. The EEG signals were further real-time processed using a bandpass filter (2~60 Hz) and a notch filter (48~52 Hz) to remove artifacts and power line interference. Subjects were randomly assigned to 1 of 2 groups: action observation therapy-based robot assisted with neurofeedback (AOT) group (n=13) and non-AOT robot-assisted (non-AOT) group (n=11). They were instructed to follow an experimental paradigm. For subjects in AOT group, the trial first started with a focus stage with a ‘+’ sign displayed on the screen for 2 s. It was followed by a 2 s text cue to remind the subject about the next task (hand open or hand grasp). At the action observation stage, a video was displayed on the screen for ~6 s. The video was showing the subject’s unaffected hand either grasping or releasing a cup from one of the three different viewing perspectives (action from the first-person, third-person or overhead perspective was randomly displayed). The video was flipped to pretend that the subject was observing his/her affected hand to do those hand actions. The subject was required to carefully observe the video showing the hand action, and to imagine that he/she was doing the action using his/her affected hand. A hand exoskeleton robot was put on subject’s affected hand to assist hand grasp/open. The robot hand has five individual finger assemblies which can provide two degrees of freedom for each finger, and each finger assembly was powered by linear actuator to provide 55 degrees and 65 degrees range of motion at the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joint and the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint respectively. The robot hand was activated to grasp/open when the subject’s ipsilesional EEG power in mu band (8-12 Hz) was suppressed below a preset threshold during the 6 s video display. Mu suppression has been used as an index of mirror neuron activity since mu oscillations, similar to mirror neurons, respond specifically to self-performed, observed and imagined actions. The degree of mu suppression is related to the extent to which the observer connected with the observed actions. If the mu suppression did not meet the threshold, some encouraging text was shown on the screen and the robot hand was not activated and no hand movement was generated. A mu suppression score was calculated in real time and displayed on the screen to indicate the subject’s performance. Then the subject was asked to rest in the relaxation stage. For subjects in non-AOT group, they followed the same events as in AOT group, except that there was no video display and the subject was instructed to perform motor imagery of his/her affected hand during the 6 s text cue (hand open or hand grasp). A score was randomly generated, and the robot hand was activated only if the score was larger than 40 regardless of the subject’s EEG signals. The robot hand was randomly activated with an activation rate maintained at around 80%, which was similar to the activation rate in AOT group. There were a total of ~100 trials (1 trial refers to a complete run from the focus stage to the relaxation stage) each day. The subject rested for ~5 min every 20 trials to prevent mental fatigue. Two outcome measures: Action Research Arm Test (ARAT) and Fugl-Meyer Assessment for upper-extremity (FMA-UE) were used to evaluate the motor functions of the paretic upper limb. The assessments of each subject were conducted before and after intervention by trained clinical assessors who were blinded to the intervention. Sixteen out of twenty-four subjects who had no magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contraindications were also scanned with a 3T Philips MR scanner using an 8-channel head coil. High-resolution T1-weighted anatomical images, and BOLD functional MRI (fMRI) images were acquired. During each fMRI run, subjects were asked to perform either motor execution (grasp and open their paretic hand) or action observation of hand movement (observe a video of grasping and releasing a cup using the hand same side as their paretic hand from the first-person perspective) task based on event-related task-paradigm design. After an initial rest period (20s), 13 trials (6s per trial) for the execution or observation task were performed with a rest period between each trial (20±4s). Each subject performed two runs for each task for averaging. During rest period, a white crosshair in black background was presented. During activation period, a white character ‘L’ or ‘R’ was presented for motor execution task, and a video of using left or right hand was presented for action observation task corresponding to the side of the subject’s paretic hand. A video-guided training strategy based on mirror neuron system has been developed to guide the stroke subjects to train their brains in motor-related areas for hand open/close function during action observation. A novel neurofeedback system was designed to strengthen the activation in the MNS by combining action observation, EEG signals and robotic hand. The training effects on paretic upper-limb motor function after the intervention, and the induced cortical changes examined using fMRI, were compared to the non-AOT intervention without the input of the subjects’ EEG signals and action observation in order to evaluate the effectiveness.

14204315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14204315.value: Clinical results All chronic stroke subjects had severe-to-moderate upper-limb motor impairment (FMAUE<47), and they were randomly assigned to 1 of 2 groups: BCI-AOT group (n=13; FMA-UE: 23.31±7.71; ARAT: 13.91±9.14) and non-AOT group (n=11; FMA-UE: 24.45±7.92; ARAT: 14.18±4.12). A significant improvement in paretic upper-limb motor functions was observed after interventions for both AOT and non-AOT groups compared to their respective baselines (AOT: FMA-UE change: 3.85±5.51, p=0.033, ARAT change: 6.09±8.08, p=0.045; Non-AOT: FMA-UE change: 2.82±3.97, p=0.036, ARAT change: 5.73±6.34, p=0.009) after the training. Changes in ARAT and FMA-UE were compared against their respective minimal clinically important differences (MCIDs) which are set at 10% of the total range of the scales according to the clinical practice. The proportions of stroke subjects exceeding the MCIDs were higher in the AOT group (ARAT: 54.5%; FMA-UE: 30.8%) compared with the non-AOT group (ARAT: 36.4%; FMA-UE: 18.2%). Besides, a significant long-term training effect [χ2(2) = 7.659, p = 0.022] on the paretic upper-limb motor functional improvement was observed only in AOT group where guided training (AO + EEG feedback) was applied. This suggests that the improvement in the paretic upper-limb motor functions could be more sustainable for the subjects who received AO with neurofeedback training compared to those without AO training. fApEn results Fuzzy approximate entropy (fApEn), a novel entropy-based algorithm designed to evaluate complexity in physiological systems. EEG fApEn in stroke subjects increased considerably in the central area of the contralesional hemisphere after training (p< 0.05). A significant correlation was noted between clinical scales(FMA-UL, ARAT, and WMFT) and EEG fApEn in C3/C4 in the contralesional hemisphere (p < 0.05). This finding suggests that the increase in EEG fApEn could be an estimator of the variance in upper limb motor function improvement. In summary, fApEn can be used to identify abnormal EEG complexity in chronic stroke, when used with BCI-motor observation training. Functional MRI results An index called variability was used to identify the important brain regions that were responsible for the neuroplasticity. Six brain networks were clustered to indicate the higher-level brain changes. Three regions, including right (ipsilesional) anterior cingulate cortex (p = 0.0053), left (contralesional) superior parietal lobule (p = 0.0039) and left (contralesional) middle frontal gyrus (p = 0.009), were found having significant increase in variability after the intervention based on the paired t-test (p < 0.01). The results could suggest that the mirror neuron system could be enhanced and motor relearning could be achieved by AOT with neurofeedback intervention.

14204315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14204315.value: The current findings of action observation (AO) with neurofeedback training could be further explored and developed for potential clinical applications in stroke subjects and patients with other movement disorders. The underlying training mechanism has not been elaborated yet, and the effectiveness of AOT training should be demonstrated in the subsequent analysis. Further studies should verify the neurological changes with other advanced technologies. Modeling efforts like neural mass modeling should be applied to find out the training effectiveness and motion observation mechanisms as well. Moreover, even more effective techniques should be explored to facilitate stroke motor recovery.

14204315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14204315.value: The brain computer interface system with neurofeedback intervention significantly improved upper limb motor functions from clinical results. The fuzzy approximate entropy (fApEn) had been used to identify abnormal brainwave (Electroencephalography, EEG) complexity in chronic stroke, and the fApEn results of EEG signals could expand the existing interpretation of training-induced functional improvement in stroke subjects. The entropy-based analysis might serve as a novel approach to understanding abnormal cortical dynamics in stroke, and the neurological changes induced by rehabilitation training. Moreover, Functional MRI results suggested that the mirror neuron system could be activated and motor relearning could be achieved by the brain computer interface system with neurofeedback intervention, this provided more understanding in the brain networks during the motor function recovery.

14205515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205515.value: Two-dimensional point patterns are hyperuniform if the variance in number of points increases more slowly than the sampling areas containing the points. Regular crystal lattices can trivially satisfy this criterion, but it is less obvious that point patterns which are irregularly spaced, and arranged without any long range order, can also be constrained to be hyperuniform. In 2014, disordered hyperuniform distributions were discovered to have naturally evolved in the position of cones in the retina of chicken eyes. Hyperuniform disordered materials have been described as a new class of materials, which possess the bandgap properties of crystals and the isotropic behavior of liquids. Artificial photonic materials based on hyperuniform disordered structures can thus have broadband isotropic optical properties, unlike traditional photonic crystals which have strong polarization, and directional dependencies. However unlike completely random media, hyperuniform disordered structures can also have complete photonic bandgaps. This surprising behavior presents intriguing new possibilities for enhancing the performance of photonic devices, which is the theme of this proposal. We predict that the strong optical dispersion near the bandedge of hyperuniform disordered structures can dramatically slow light, in a similar fashion to the phenomenon of slow light observed in conventional photonic crystals. Hyperuniform disordered structures thus offer the prospect of producing larger enhancements in the efficiency of photodetectors or solar cells than have been demonstrated with randomly positioned scatterers. We expect slow light and high Q resonators in hyperuniform disordered structures to be useful in enhancing the efficiency of nonlinear optical devices. The existence of photonic bandgaps in isotropic hyperuniform disordered silicon structures was experimentally verified in 2013. Numerical simulations have shown that at short wavelengths near the photonic bandedge, photons are transported in a diffusive manner in a hyperuniform disordered medium. We shall fabricate two-dimensional hyperuniform disordered point patterns and assess their effectiveness for enhancing light extraction from a silicon waveguide. We shall compare the extent of the possible enhancement in the efficiency of a silicon based photodetector with and without hyperuniform disordered structures. We shall also study applications of hyperuniform disordered cavities for enhancing the performance of nonlinear optical devices. The proposed work may pave the way for improved designs of light extraction structures that can ultimately improve the energy efficiency of light emitting diodes used in general lighting. The study on the use of hyperuniform disordered structures in photodetectors may also lead to more efficient structures for thin film photovoltaic cells. 隨機的點分佈圖案中，一定大小區域內包含的點個數的統計方差隨考察區域面積的增加而有更慢的增長速率，可稱為二維超均衡點分佈。普通規則的晶格結構明顯滿足以上定義，而對於無序排列，無任何長程有序性的點分佈仍可通過束縛具有這種超均衡特性。不同于完全無序的光子結構，超均衡的光子晶體具有寬頻和各向同性的光子禁帶特性。這些奇異的光學特性可用於增強光子器件的性能，也是本項目的主題。超均衡的光子晶體結構可能用於進一步提升基於無序散射結構的光電探測器和太陽能電池的光電轉換效率。數值模擬表明波長處於超均衡光子晶體介質帶帶邊處的光子傳播具有擴散的方式。我們將製備二維的超均衡無序光子晶體結構，評估其光子提取效率和矽基光電探測器光電轉換效率的增強。我們也將研究基於超均衡無序光子晶體諧振腔對於光子器件非線性效應的增強。

14205515.label: Realisation of objectives
14205515.value: With the announcement of the funding for this project in July 2015, a PhD student, Wen Zhou was assigned the challenge of developing a method to generate numerically a two dimensional hyperuniform disordered structure (HUDS) in August 2015 when we started the theoretical design simulations ( before the official start date of the project on 1 Jan 2016). We made rapid progress by taking advantage of existing Matlab optimization toolbox to optimize the objective function of a point pattern to satisfy the hyperuniform criteria following the procedure described in the literature by Torquato and Stillinger for the hyperuniform point pattern generation. We carried out the electromagnetic simulations of the photonic bandgap produced by the 2D hyperuniform disordered wall networks generated using the Delauney triangulation procedure developed by M. Florescu et al. The numerical simulations of the hyperuniform disordered wall network revealed a very strong polarization dependence, and using reasonable device dimensions for the silicon-on-insulator wafer thicknesses readily available, it was possible to produce photonic bandgap for TE light but not for TM light . The numerical simulations suggested the possibility of exploiting the photonic bandgap for a very compact and high extinction ratio integrated polarizer using the two dimensional hyperuniform disordered wall network. After a week of calculations, the hyperuniform disordered wall network was numerically optimized to function as a wideband (>160nm optical wavelength range) compact (< 8 microns in length) integrated waveguide polarizer which passed TM polarized light but efficiently scattered (with >30dB extinction) the TE polarized light. The optimized device design had inherent disorder, which gave it the advantage of being very robust to make with much larger fabrication tolerances than conventional photonic crystals. The (at that time very inexperienced) PhD student was able to make the device in first attempt at fabrication. The fabricated integrated hyperuniform disordered wall network polarizer worked almost as predicted with ~98nm optical bandwidth and over 30dB extinction ratio but with less than 2dB insertion loss for TM light . We submitted the preliminary results at the end of November 2015 and updated the paper in the revision of Febrauary 2017. This resulted in the first publication on using hyperunifrom disordered structure for integrated polarizer. [J1, Zhou et al. IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics 2016]. For objectives 2 and 3, we extended to preliminary simulations in the proposal to the more time consuming 3D simulations of the hyperuniform point pattern to evaluate whether there could be enhancements in the out of plane scattered light due to the point hyperuniform point pattern. However unlike the results of the 2D simulations, the 3D simulations revealed that most of the light was scattered in reflections and the total vertically scattered light was not significantly enhanced. Furthermore objective 4 on using the HUDS structure to enhance nonlinear effects by increasing the group index was found to be not feasible because of large optical scattering losses from the diffusive scattering of light and the band edge resonances. Although we fully addressed objectives 2 -4 in the proposal, the negative results from the 3D simulations, particularly the high in plane scattering losses from the disordered structures, were not sufficient for publications, and there were no advantage in using the bandedge dispersion or disordered resonances for nonlinear devices because of the high optical losses from scattering. Therefore we concentrated our efforts on the first objective and continued to develop the novel hyperuniform disordered polarizer by extending the approach to mid infrared polarizers [c5, Milosevic et al, CLEO 2019], and taking advantage of the diffusive scattering and band edge resonances to complement the photonic bandgap to increase the operational bandwidth of the polarizer bandwidth to a theoretical 265nm (30dB extinction ratio) from the 149nm bandwidth achievable from using only the photonics bandgap. Although the device was designed in early 2018, the delivery of the chips fabricated by the foundry at the end of 2018 meant that the experimental results of 210nm bandwidth were only submitted after the official completion date of the project [J2 Zhou et al, Journal of Applied Physics 2019]. Our work on hyperuniform polarizers was also described in an invited review paper [J3 Zhou et al, IEEE J. Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics, 2019]. We further improved the performance experimentally of the hyperuniform disordered waveguide polarizer to a 240nm bandwidth and demonstrated the near isotropic photonic bandgap experimentally at the optical telecom wavelengths [J4, Zhou et al IEEE J. Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics 2020].

14205515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205515.value: The project invented a new type of integrated waveguide polarizer based on the hyperuniform disordered structures (HUDS). We demonstrated experimentally that the HUDS integrated polarizers could be be ultra broadband (240nm optical bandwidth in the near infrared), and be used at different wavelength ranges, extending to the mid infrared. The HUDS polarizers also offer the advantage of being ultracompact and can attain over 50dB extinction ratio [J4, Zhou et al IEEE J. Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics 2020]. These impressive performance has attracted much academic interest and the project led to several invited conference papers and an invited journal paper [J3, Zhou et al, IEEE J. Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics 2019]. A PhD student, Wen ZHOU, worked on the hyperuniform disordered device simulations and experimental characterization of the HUDS polarizers and completed his PhD in 2018. The GRF project also provided research experience to an undergraduate student who was tasked with writing labview instrumentation drivers needed for the project. The undergraduate student worked with another undergraduate student (who was hired under another GRF project because the instrumentation software was needed by both projects). They were able to complete the task assigned and demonstrate the labview drivers for interfacing the optical power meters with the tunable lasers and optical delay lines. However because of time commitments to their final year courses, the students did not continue with other tasks in the second semester and there is a small balance remaining in the earmarked budget for undergraduate research (unfortunately the rules of this earmarked funding stipulated it can be used only for one student and not for different students).

There is also potential to extend this approach to terahertz polarizers.

14205515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205515.value: The project made use of the mathematical definition of hyperuniformity in disordered structures for applications in integrated optical polarizers. We developed a new type of integrated optical polarizer based on the hyperuniform disordered structures and showed experimentally that such polarizers can offer ultra wide optical bandwidth (we demonstrated 240nm experimentally) and high polarization extinction ratio exceeding 50dB in a one of the most compact structures yet reported for high extinction ratio integrated polarizers.. These performance advanced the state of the art for integrated optical polarizers.

14205615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205615.value: The aim of this project is to conduct research on developing deep models for generic object detection. It is able to detect hundreds of object classes from images taken in unconstrained conditions. The proposed technologies have many important applications such as automotive safety, self-driving cars, wearable devices, robotics, content based image retrieval, assistive technology for the visually impaired, advanced human-computer interface, and video surveillance. Object detection is the task of detecting semantic objects of a certain class (such as humans, horses or cars) in images and videos. It is a grand challenge in computer vision and is extremely difficult because objects undergo significant illumination change, nonrigid deformation, rotation, viewpoint change, occlusion, and intra-class appearance variation, and some object classes have large visual similarity. With carefully designed multi-layer architectures, our proposed deep models jointly learn feature representation, deformation invariance, rotation invariance, and context of objects. This is achieved by several major innovations. (1) Novel deformable part layer and rotation part layer are proposed and they fundamentally change the structure of the covolutional neural networks widely used in image-related deep learning tasks. (2) A new pretraining-finetuning scheme is proposed for object detection. It effectively makes use of large extra training data with many object classes to learn generic object feature representations and to avoid overfitting through pretraining. In the meanwhile it well adapts the pre-trained deep models to particular object detection applications, which only involves a small number of object classes and smaller training data, by fine-tuning. (3) It learns robust and discriminative feature representations by simultaneously predicting rich annotations including class labels, bounding box locations, scales, overlaps, aspect ratios and rotation, instead of training detectors with binary classification errors in existing approaches. (4) Realizing that object detection and object recognition are two tasks closely related, a deep learning framework is proposed to jointly learn the models of local objects and global context with shared feature representations. (5) The joint learning of all these components mentioned above creates synergy through close interaction in the training process, and can generate performance far greater than learning individual components separately or sequentially. The outcome of this project will not only significantly improve the effectiveness of deep models for generic object detection, but also have valuable contributions to the architecture design and training of neural networks, which are fundamental problems of deep learning. The largely enhanced detection accuracy will advance many applications which are based on object detection. 該項目的目標是研究如何設計深度模型用於通用物體檢測。它能夠從無約束條件下拍攝的圖像中檢測到數百類物體。所提出的技術有許多重要的應用，如汽車的安全駕駛，自動駕駛，可穿戴設備，機器人，基於內容的圖像檢索，視障人士輔助技術，人機交互和視頻監控。 物體檢測是一種在圖像和視頻中檢測語義對象（例如人，馬或車）的任務。它是計算機視覺的大挑戰。猶豫物體光照變化，非剛性變形，旋轉，視角變化，遮擋和類內變化，以及一些不同類的物體有很大的視覺相似性，物體檢測是非常困難的。 通過精心設計的多層架構，我們提出的深度模型聯合學習特徵表示，形變不變性，旋轉不變性，和對象上下文信息。 這一深度模型通過幾個主要的創新來實現。 （1）新的物體部件變形層和旋轉層，它們從根本上改變廣泛應用於圖像相關的深度學習任務的卷積神經網絡的結構。 （2）新的物體檢測中預訓練-精調方法。它有效地利用了大量額外的訓練數據和物體類型來學習通用物體的特徵表示，並通過預訓練避免過度擬合。同時，它通過精調很好地使得預訓練的模型更適用於相對而言物體種類和訓練數據較少的物體檢測的應用。 （3）通過預測豐富的標註而不是簡單的二元分類來學習具有魯棒性和判別功能的特徵表示。這些標註包括物體類別，物體框的位置，大小，重疊，高寬比和旋轉。 （4）由於物體檢測和物體識別這兩項任務密切相關的，我們提出通過共享的特徵表示來對這兩個任務聯合學習。 （5）通過對上述所有這些組件的聯合學習，這些組件密切互動創造協同效應，並能產生性能遠遠超過單獨或順序學習各個組件的效果。 該項目的成果將對深度學習和物體檢測產生長期影響。新提出的深度模型層，訓練方法以及聯合學習框架對深度學習的關鍵挑戰具有基礎性的貢獻。它們可以推廣到其他基於深度學習的任務。它有望在一般物體檢測中在魯棒性和準確率方面實現大的改善，並以顯著推進基於物體檢測的應用。

14205615.label: Realisation of objectives
14205615.value: All the objectives of this project have been realized successfully. (1) We have developed a deep neural network with deformable part layers and rotatable part layers. Part deformation handling is a key factor for object detection. The proposed deformable part layers are motivated by three important observations. First, deformable visual patterns are usually shared by objects of different categories. For instance, the circular visual pattern is shared by both vehicles and iPod. Second, the regularity of deformation varies for different semantic parts. Third, a deformable part at a higher level is composed of deformable parts at a lower level. Based on those three observations, we designed a new deformation-constrained pooling layer to the shared visual patterns and their deformation properties for multiple object classes at different semantic levels and composition levels. The proposed layer automatically models the deformation of object parts with geometric constraint and penalty. Treating feature response maps as a series of part detection score maps, the deformation layer models the penalties of the relative spatial relations between parts. By summing up the deformable part scores with a specifically designed convolution layer, more accurate detection scores can be obtained via end-to-end training. (2) Previous methods on object detection pretrain on large-scale image classification data and then are finetuned for the target object detection task. However, we observe that there is still a gap between the pretraining task and the finetuning task that makes pretraining less effective. The problem of the pre-training scheme for object detection is the mismatch between pretraining for the image classification task and fine-tuning for the object detection task. For image classification, the input is a whole image and the task is to recognize the object within this image. For object detection, the task is to determine whether a small image patch consists of an object of interest. Because of such mismatch, the image classification task is not an ideal choice to pretrain the deep model for object detection. To tackle this challenge, we propose to pretrain the deep model on a large auxiliary object detection training data instead of the image classification data. Since the ImageNet Cls-Loc data provides object-level bounding boxes for 1000 classes, more diverse in content than the ImageNet Det data with 200 classes, we used the image regions cropped by these bounding boxes to pretrain the baseline deep model. Compared with the training scheme of RCNN, experimental results show that the proposed scheme improves mean AP by 4.5% on ImageNet Det validation set 2. (3) In order to learn discriminative feature representations from large scale dataset with rich annotations, we proposed a large-scale object attribute database that contains rich attribute annotations (over 300 attributes) for ∼180k samples and 494 object classes. Based on the ImageNet object detection dataset, it annotates the rotation, viewpoint, object part location, part occlusion, part existence, common attributes, and class-specific attributes. We use this dataset to train deep representations and extensively evaluate how these attributes are useful on the general object detection task. In order to make better use of the attribute annotations, a deep learning scheme is proposed by modeling the relationship of attributes and hierarchically clustering them into semantically meaningful mixture types. Experimental results show that the attributes are helpful in learning better features and improving the object detection accuracy by 2.6% in mAP on the ILSVRC 2014 object detection dataset and 2.4% in mAP on PASCAL VOC 2007 object detection dataset. Such improvement is well generalized to other datasets. (4) To better integrate local visual features and global context to improve object detection performance, we propose the GBD-Net. The GBD-Net is designed to pass messages between features from different image regions during feature learning. Such message passing can be implemented through convolution in two directions and can be conducted in various layers. Therefore, local and contextual visual patterns can validate the existence of each other by learning their nonlinear relationships and their close interactions are modeled the learning process. It is also shown that message passing is not always helpful depending on individual samples. Gated functions are further introduced to control message transmission and their on-and-off is controlled by extra visual evidence from the input sample. GBD-Net is implemented under the Fast RCNN detection framework. Its effectiveness is shown through experiments on three object detection datasets, ImageNet, Pascal VOC2007 and Microsoft COCO.

14205615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205615.value: As research outcomes, 3 journal papers and 30 conferences papers are published. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (PAMI) is the best journal on computer vision and machine learning. 28 papers were published on top conferences on computer vision and machine learning (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NIPS and AAAI). In this project, we have proposed novel object detection algorithms for still images and videos. In (Part C.8 No. 1), we proposed a deep learning framework with deformable part layer for generic object detection. In (Part C.8 No. 3), a framework that jointly tackles feature extraction, deformation handling, occlusion handling, and classification was proposed for pedestrian detection. The interactions between the components are jointly optimized in this framework. In (Part C.9 No. 7), we analyzed different factors that would affect the performance in finetuning deep neural networks for object detection. In (Part C.9 No. 19), a chained cascade network specifically designed for object detection was proposed. We also proposed different methods for object detection from videos. In (Part C.9 No. 8), we introduced a complete framework for the VID task based on still-image object detection and general object tracking. Their relations and contributions in the VID task are thoroughly studied and evaluated. In (Part C.9 No. 13), we proposed a framework for object detection in videos, which consists of a novel tubelet proposal network to efficiently generate spatiotemporal proposals, and a Long Short-term Memory (LSTM) network that incorporates temporal information from tubelet proposals for achieving high object detection accuracy in videos. Object detection algorithms can also be generalized to assist human pose estimation. In (Part C.9 No. 5), we proposed a novel end-to-end framework for human pose estimation that combines deep neural networks with the expressive deformable mixture of parts. In (Part C.9 No. 6), the relationships between feature maps of different body joints are captured with the introduced geometrical transform kernels, which can be easily implemented with a convolution layer. In (Part C.9 No. 16), we design a Pyramid Residual Module (PRMs) to enhance the invariance in scales of DCNNs. Given input features, the PRMs learn convolutional filters on various scales of input features, which are obtained with different subsampling ratios in a multi-branch network. In (Part C.9 No. 24), we propose a CRF-CNN framework which can simultaneously model structural information in both output and hidden feature layers in a probabilistic way, and it is applied to human pose estimation. We also generalize proposed object detection algorithms to other related applications. In (Part C.9 No. 12), we observe there is a gap between pedestrian detection and person re-identification. To close the gap, we propose a new deep learning framework for jointly handling both aspects in a single convolutional neural network. In (Part C.9 No. 30), we proposed to jointly use the free-form region based and the detection-based visual attention mechanisms for achieving Visual Question Answering.

14205615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205615.value: In this project, we have developed the deformable part layer and a new finetuning training scheme for object detection. We will further investigate how to integrate the deformable part layer and training scheme to tackle other related computer vision problems. Novel deep learning frameworks will be designed to integrate the newly proposed components. In addition, object detection has extensive applications in different computer vision tasks. We will also investigate how to integrate the developed object detection algorithms to assist other computer vision applications. We will also investigate how to extend 2D object detection to 3D object detection and handle point clouds captured by the LIDAR sensors for autonomous driving scenarios.

14205615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205615.value: In this project, we proposed novel algorithms to tackle the generic object detection problem. Object detection is the task of detecting semantic objects of a certain class (such as humans, horses or cars) in images and videos and has extensive applications in different high-level computer vision tasks. However, it is a challenging problem. We proposed carefully designed multi-layer architectures, to jointly learn feature representation, deformation invariance, rotation invariance, and context of objects. A novel deformable part layer and a rotation part layer were proposed for handling the deformation of objects. A new pretraining-finetuning scheme was also introduced for object detection. It effectively makes use of large extra training data with many object classes to learn generic object feature representations and to avoid overfitting through pretraining. We also presented a new large-scale dataset for object attribute that contains rich annotations for learning discriminative feature representations. GBD-Net was the winning method of ImageNet Challenge 2016 on the object detection task, which jointly models local object appearance and global context with shared feature representations.

14206015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206015.value: As the semiconductor process technology scales down to the nanometer era, the gap between the illuminating wavelength and the process node becomes bigger and bigger. Self-Aligned Double Patterning (SADP) is a promising lithography technique for technology node at 10nm or below, because SADP has better overlay control compared with other multiple patterning techniques. In SADP, a layout is decomposed into two masks, a core mask and a trim/cut mask. Compared with Litho-Etch-Litho-Etch (LELE) double patterning, a feature in SADP may not be directly defined by one of the two masks. The decomposition problem for SADP has been studied in a number of previous works. But not many works are on the SADP-aware placement. We need a placement tool that can take into account the SADP induced design rules in order to make possible the decomposition and the manufacturing process. In placement, we want to place the cells and the macro blocks in such a way that routing can be accomplished, timing can be met and the chips can be manufactured. With the rapid technology advancement, designs become more complex and routability is one major concern. Besides, placement is an important step that affects significantly the ultimate circuit performance, but considering timing in placement is non-trivial. One reason is that routing is not done yet at that stage and the routing paths are not known. For another reason, an accurate and fast timing estimator is needed. Moving one single cell can affect the timing of many signal paths and finding the right positions for the cells to fix the timing violations is non-trivial. In this project, we want to tackle all these important problems simultaneously in a placer. We want to study and develop a placement method that can handle routability, timing and manufacturability seamlessly. Continued semiconductor scaling will bring a rapid increase in circuit complexity and the need of advanced lithography technology. The need for a robust placer that can be used with the current technology is becoming pivotal. The success of this project will definitely contribute to the VLSI CAD community and to the design of high performance microprocessors. 隨著半導體工藝的製程縮小到納米級，光刻中使用的光波波長與所需要處理的元件的尺寸之間的鴻溝越來越大。在10納米及以下的製程中，自對準雙重曝光技術 (SADP) 是一種很有希望被採用的光刻技術。這是由於，相對於其他的多重曝光技術，SADP能夠更好地控制疊加錯誤。在SADP中，電路圖形被分解為兩個掩模，即一個核心掩模和一個修剪/切割掩模。不同於刻-蝕-刻-蝕 (LELE) 雙重曝光技術，在SADP中，圖案不一定是由兩個掩模中的一個直接產生。SADP的圖形分解問題已經得到了廣泛的研究。但是目前尚缺少關於SADP導向的佈局算法的研究。我們需要一個能夠考慮因SADP而衍生的設計規則的佈局工具，從而使SADP的分解和製造成為可能。 在電路佈局過程中，我們需要決定如何擺置電路元件和宏模塊，從而使電路繞線可以完成，時序要求可以被滿足，與此同時，芯片可以被製造。隨著技術的快速進步，設計變得更加複雜，而可繞線性又是在設計中被主要關注的問題。另外，電路佈局是一個顯著影響芯片最終性能的重要步驟，但在佈局中考慮時序要求並非易事。其原因之一是，此時尚未進行繞線，所以繞線的的具體路徑也無從得知。另一個原因是，準確及快速的時序估計是必要的。由於移動單個元件即可同時影響多條信號路徑的時序，找到這些元件的正確位置從而修正時序相當困難。 在這個項目中，我們希望在一個電路佈局器中同時處理所有這些重要問題。我們希望研究和開發出一種能夠無縫解決可繞線性，時序和可製造性的佈局方法。半導體尺寸的持續縮小將會帶來芯片複雜性的快速增加和對更先進的光刻技術的強烈需求。本項目若成功，超大規模集成電路自動化設計領域和高性能微處理器設計領域都必將獲益良多。

14206015.label: Realisation of objectives
14206015.value: In this project, we developed a detailed-routability aware placer, which can handle a placement constraint called fence, in which some of the cells are constrained to be placed within some given regions. There are two steps in the placer, global placement and detailed placement. Our global placement is consisted of an upper-bound and a lower-bound optimization framework. The lower-bound process is a wirelength-driven analytical placement solved by an innovative box-constrained conjugate gradient (CG) method. The upper-bound process is a fence-by-fence legalization, to reduce cell overlap and ease routing congestion, a major factor for poor routability. In detailed placement, the wirelength is minimized further with design-rule (e.g., rule for SADP) aware local cell movement. Bin-based target density control is also applied to further enhance the circuit routability. By comparison with the results of the participating teams of the 2015 ISPD Placement Contest [1], our placer shows competitive results in terms of wirelength, routability and design rule satisfaction. For considering of Self-Aligned Double Patterning (SADP) constraints in placement, we have studied applying fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithms to solve the problem. We focus on the layout decomposition problem for different lithography technologies including but not limited to multiple patterning lithography (MPL). The proposed approaches use ideas drastically different from all the previous works for layout decomposition and can obtain optimal solutions in a short running time. We demonstrated the great potential of applying FPT algorithms to solve more NP-hard problems efficiently in EDA. For timing optimization in placement, we studied and developed a tree surgery technique to adjust routing tree topology after global routing to fix timing. A quadratic program (QP) was formulated, which adjusts routing topology of all the nets from a global perspective and takes congestion into consideration to trade off timing and routability. A machine learning-based technique is also applied to accelerate the method. Our performance on public benchmarks show that we can achieve good improvement in timing without significant degradation in routability and wirelength. The same results can be obtained in negligible running time with machine learning-based acceleration.

14206015.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206015.value: In this project, we studied and developed a placer that handles routability and a commonly used placement constraints called fence constraint. We developed a placement engine that considers detailed mutability during placement and incorporate fence constraints in both the global placement and detailed placement stages. In global placement, various design rule issues are modelled and considered. In the detailed placement stage, the rules are handled in details. (This research output is related to the publications of SLIP 2017 and TCAD 37(10) 2018 in Part C.) We have also found that Fixed Parametric Tractable (FPT) algorithms can be applied to solve problems effectively in VLSI CAD, which is a new paradigm to solve NP-hard problems in EDA. Numerous problems in physical synthesis of VLSI circuits can be reduced to the problem of Weighted Odd Cycle Cover (WOCC) which we have developed and implemented an effective FPT method to solve. We have opened source our WOCCP solver for future research. It's shown that our method can be applied to solve the layout decomposition problem for different kinds of manufacturing and lithography technology like e-beam, multiple patterning, etc. effectively. (This research output is related to the publications of TCAD 39(9) 2019, DAC 2017 and ICCAD 2016 in Part C.) Finally, timing is a critical issue to consider for VLSI design and it is hard to improve timing without hurting routability. We formulated and solved a tree surgery problem by quadratic programming, optimizing gate delay and net delay. In order to consider routability simultaneously, congestion is also modelled and optimized in our method. A machine learning-based algorithm is applied to increase efficiency, and features related to timing are extracted and used in the learning model. Results show that our algorithms can achieve good improvement in timing. (This research output is related to the publications of TCAD 2019 (accepted) and GLSVLSI 2018 in Part C.)

14206015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206015.value: For our placer, we can focus more on an accurate congestion estimation in the future especially on the benchmarks with blockages. More investigations are needed to identify the regions that are susceptible to short in detailed routing. Early detection of design rule violations will help the placer to produce easy-to-route result. We can also incorporate a machine learning based predictor into the placer to achieve that. Besides, GPU implementation of the whole placer will speed up the placement process significantly and this will also be a valuable direction to pursuit. More opportunities of applying Fixed Parametric Tractable (FPT) algorithms in CAD can be investigated. Numerous problems in EDA can be solved by FPT algorithms, e.g., many problems can be reduced to the set cover problem, for which highly efficient FPT algorithm exists when the sets are bounded in size. Steiner tree construction problem, which is essential for routing, can also by solved with FPT methods if the edge weights are bounded with the number of terminals as a parameter. More bridging between the theoretical advancement on FPT methods and VLSI CAD can be explored.

14206015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206015.value: Placement is the step to layout the gates and cells on a 2-dimensional chip, given a circuit. In this project, we developed a placement engine that places cells and gates in a manner that can help to improve the connectivity of the wires between the cells and gates in the routing stage, which is usually the next step after placement. The placer can also take into consideration rules and constraints due to design, manufacturing and lithography technologies, e.g., multiple patterning, SADP, etc. To enable different lithography technologies, layout decomposition is very often needed, which will also affect placement. To decompose a layout, we developed a Fixed Parametric Tractable (FPT) based solver to solve a difficult NP-complete problem, called the Weighted Odd Cycle Cover problem, by fixing some of the parameters, optimally but also very efficiently in practice. This solver is now open source and can possibly be useful to solve other related hard combinatorial optimization problems in EDA or other areas. Besides routability and manufacturability, timing is also considered and studied and a routing tree repairing method is developed to improve timing without affecting the routing solution of the other parts of circuit.

14206315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206315.value: 本项目将立足于提出、分析和模拟关于移动群智感知的经济机制设计理论。智能电话与嵌入式传感器的大规模应用导致了新的革命性的移动群智感知模式。在这一模式下，众多移动用户使用他们的移动设备来共同感测和共享与他们感兴趣的现象有关的信息。由于其低部署成本和高感知覆盖的优势，移动群智感知日益在多种基础设施和社区监测方面发挥重要的作用，例如空气质量监测，无线信号强度测量，堵车警报，无线室内定位日益流行和城市层析成像。与此同时，移动群智感知在大规模部署方面遇到的几个关键挑战，如不均衡的覆盖范围，传感质量的不稳定性，用户对隐私的担心，和对用户移动设备资源的过度消耗。解决这些挑战不仅需要创新的技术解决方案和算法设计，而且需要设计有效激励移动用户的经济机制，促使用户积极从事高品质的数据检测和及时地报告数据。在这个项目中，我们计划解决在设计移动群智感知经济机制中得四个关键问题：（1）如何应对不完整的网络信息，并鼓励用户如实分享他们的私人信息？ （2）如何保证最有效的用户能够长期存在于系统中？ （3）如何利用网络动态使得数据报告更划算？ （4）如何利用用户之间的竞争与合作以​​取得良好的检测结果的？本项目的研究团队在网络经济和博弈，无线资源分配，以及网络优化和控制有着卓越的研究背景，并已经在诸如 IEEE INFOCOM 和 IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing 等顶级会议和期刊上发表了多个令人鼓舞的初步研究结果。本项目的研究成果将帮助我们深入了解关于移动群智感知系统的机会和挑战，并显著提高网络性能和用户参与的积极性。

14206315.label: Realisation of objectives
14206315.value: We are pleased to report that the project team has achieved all project objectives, through collaborations with many top researchers around the world. This project is theoretical in nature. we successfully address the following three key questions: (1) How to cope with incomplete network information and encourageusers to truthfully share their private information? (2) How to explore the network dynamics to make the data reporting more cost effective? (3) How explore the impact of the competitive and cooperative user relationship on the MCS performance? Here is a quick summary of our key results: We design an efficient and distributed Nash bargaining algorithm, to encourage users to cooperate with each other in terms of crowdsourcing network resources to improve the system performance. We propose a novel P2P-based MCS architecture, where the sensing data is saved and processed in user devices locally and shared among users in a P2P manner. We propose a multi-dimensional auction mechanism that can effectively crowdsource user resources to support various QoS sensitive and delay stringent applications. We design an optimal joint incentive mechanism and prediction algorithm to deal with the crowdsourced prediction problem with private user information and hidden user efforts. We propose the new framework of data-centric mobile crowdsensing. We propose an algorithm to compute the optimal user’s decisions under the general setting of delay-sensitive mobile crowdsending using dynamic programming. We focus on the energy utilization problem in the tactile Internet under the proposed computation-communication-caching sharing framework. We present a novel contract-based incentive framework to incentivize such a Wi-Fi network crowdsourcing under incomplete information. We propose both the single-object and multi-objectmulti-dimensional auction mechanisms for collabrative video streaming. We provide an overview regarding the design principles of six incentive mechanisms, drawing special attentionto the sustainability issue. We propose a crowd-sourced human mobility prediction model for public regions. We consider a three-layer data-centric crowdsensing model by introducing a new data layer between tasks and users, which allows us to effectively leverage both the task similarity and the user heterogeneity. We consider the important issue of diversity and social impact in mobile crowd sensing. Finally, we consider the crowdsensing problem from the perspective of bounded rationality. Results related to this projects have appeared in 11 top IEEE/ACM journals and magazines, as well as 9 leading international conference papers. This project has helped train 5 Ph.D. students. The detailed summary is given in Part C. A note regarding the unspent funding for "Research Experiences for Undergraduate Students". I was lucky enough to supervise several talented undergraduate students in their final year projects， on topics related to mobile crowd sensing. These projects did not consume any research funding.

We propose both the single-object and multi-objectmulti-dimensional auction mechanisms for collabrative video streaming. This is related to journal paper 10 and conference paper 5. We provide an overview regarding the design principles of six incentive mechanisms, drawing special attentionto the sustainability issue. This is related to journal paper 11. We propose a crowd-sourced human mobility prediction model for public regions. This is related to conference paper 1. We consider a three-layer data-centric crowdsensing model by introducing a new data layer between tasks and users, which allows us to effectively leverage both the task similarity and the user heterogeneity. This is related to conference paper 4. We consider the important issue of diversity and social impact in mobile crowd sensing. This is related to conference paper 7. Finally, we consider the crowdsensing problem from the perspective of bounded rationality. This is related to conference paper 9.

14206315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206315.value: The proliferation of smartphones with rich embedded sensors has led to the new revolutionary mobile crowd sensing (MCS) paradigm, where individuals use their mobile devices to collectively sense and share information related to a certain phenomenon of interest. Due to the low deploying cost and highsensing coverage, MCS becomes increasingly popular for a wide range of applications in environment, infrastructure, and community monitoring, such as air quality monitoring, wirelesssignal strength measurement, traffic jam alerts, wireless indoor localization, and urban tomography. Meanwhile, the large scale deployment of MCS has encountered several key challenges, such as uneven and biased coverages, large variations of sensing quality, user concerns on privacy, and potential excessive consumption of user device resources. Resolving these challenges requires effective economic mechanisms that incentivize mobile users to actively engage in high quality data sensing and timely data reporting. In this project, we successfully address the following three key questions: (1) How to cope with incomplete network information and encourageusers to truthfully share their private information? (2) How to explore the network dynamics to make the data reporting more cost effective? (3) How explore the impact of the competitive and cooperative user relationship on the MCS performance?

14206715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206715.value: The project proposes to design and develop a scalable system for efficient query processing in massive graphs that may be stored in distributed locations. Graph queries such as shortest-path distance queries, reachability queries, pattern matching queries, neighborhood queries, etc., have many important applications and have been extensively studied in the past. However, in recent years, we have witnessed a surge of graph data from various sources such as online social networks, online shopping networks, mobile and communication networks, financial and marketing networks, the WWW and Internet, etc. Most of these graphs are massively large, for example, online social networks have hundreds of millions of vertices (i.e., users) and tens to hundreds of billions of edges (i.e., user-to-user connections), and mobile phone call networks in any big city can easily have billions of connections. For handling such massive graphs, most existing graph query processing techniques are not scalable. Many distributed graph computing systems (e.g., Pregel, Giraph, GraphLab, etc.) have been developed, which provide a general programming framework for processing massive graphs. However, these systems are designed for handling graph analytic workloads, and are hence inefficient for handling graph query workloads due to the different data access patterns in computation. This motivates us to design a new type of distribute system for graph query processing. The proposal is also motivated by real demands arising from applications in Taobao (Alibaba Group), the dominant online shopping platform in China, with whom we collaborate to develop efficient techniques for analyzing massive graphs from Taobao's online shopping platform. While there are analytic tasks for which existing distributed graph computing systems can be used, there are also many other applications in Taobao which require efficient answering of different graph queries. This calls for the development of the proposed system. 這個項目主要提出實現一個圖處理系統，來用於有效處理存在於多個分布式機器上的海量的圖數據查詢任務。圖上的查詢問題，例如最短路，可達性，模式匹配，鄰居查詢等等，都有很多重要的應用，也已經被廣泛地研究。在最近幾年，圖數據變得越來越大，例如社交網絡圖，網上購物網絡圖，電話網絡圖，金融市場網絡圖，萬維網圖。這些圖數據都很大量，例如社交網絡有上億的點（用戶） 和幾千億的邊（兩點之間的聯繫），電話網絡也有上億的邊。去處理這麼大的圖數據，大部分現有的圖處理技術都不可行。現有很多分布式圖處理系統，例如Pregel, Giraph, GraphLab 等等，給我們提供了通用的編程框架來處理海量圖。但是，這些系統適用於處理圖數據分析任務，而不適用於實時查詢任務。這使得我們有必要提出一種新的圖處理分布式系統。這個提案是基於我們的合作夥伴淘寶希望能有效處理淘寶上的數據而提出的。對於他們的購物網絡，淘寶不僅需要圖系統能進行分析任務，也需要系統能處理實時的查詢。

14206715.label: Realisation of objectives
14206715.value: The project has three objectives. For the first objective. We designed and implemented a general programming framework for distributed graph query processing, and designed a user-friendly application programming interface (API) that allows users to easily construct graph indexes and implement various algorithms for processing a broad range of graph queries. The class of queries, as well as the related graph indexes to facilitate their efficient processing, that can be supported by the proposed framework and can be easily implemented using the proposed API consist of all whose algorithms can be expressed using the vertex-centric programming model, by adopting Pregel’s “think like a vertex” programming paradigm. The vertex-centric programming model also naturally supports distributed computing for processing large graphs having over billions of vertices and edges. Currently, we implemented the following types of graph queries: shortest-path distance queries, reachability queries, subgraph matching queries, neighborhood queries, and keyword searches in graphs, together with indexes to speed up their processing. The graph query processing algorithms and graph indexes studied in the project were shown to achieve high efficiency for various types of graph queries in large scale graphs, and the research results were published in top-tier conferences and journals such as the 2016 IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering, the 2016 ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, the 2017 International Conference on Database Systems for Advanced Applications, and the 2018 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data. To achieve the second project objective, a scalable distributed system was designed and implemented to realize the programming framework described in Objective 1. An efficient system prototype was completed in 2016, which exposes a user-friendly API for users to implement various types of distributed algorithms without caring the complicated workload distribution and fault tolerance. The system was then continued to be refined and many optimizations were applied in 2017 and 2018, and the open-source version is now robust and can scale to process billion scale graphs. The system has shown to significantly outperform existing distributed graph systems and able to support a much wider range of graph queries. The results of the research, including both the background studies and findings, performance comparison studies involving related systems, and innovative system designs and implementation details, were published in top-tier conferences and journals such as the 2016 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data, the PVLDB journal (Volume 9, Number 7, 2016), the 2016 IEEE International Conference on Big Data, the PVLDB journal (Volume 9, Number 5, 2016), the 2017 International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval, and a tutorial titled “Big Graph Analytics Systems” that was given at the ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data in San Francisco in 2016. To achieve the third project objective, we actively worked with companies such as Alibaba, Huawei and some start-up companies in Hong Kong. The types of graph queries currently implemented and supported by the system, i.e., shortest-path distance queries, reachability queries, subgraph matching queries, neighborhood queries, and keyword searches in graphs, were in fact used to solve real problems in these companies. For example, shortest-path distance queries and reachability queries are used for the detection of fake reputation enhancement in online shopping applications; neighborhood queries are used for user group clustering and product categorization.
