14206715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206715.value: The project developed a general-purpose programming framework for distributed query processing in massive graphs. The framework provides a user-friendly application programming interface to allow users to easily construct various graph indexes and implement efficient distributed algorithms for processing a broad range of graph queries, including graph reachability queries, graph distance queries, pattern matching queries, and keyword searches in a graph. A scalable distributed system was designed and implemented to realize the proposed programming framework, which has shown to significantly outperform existing distributed graph systems. The system design and some implementation details were published in the 2016 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data and the PVLDB journal (Volume 9, Number 7, 2016). During the project development, we also had other major findings and research outcome as follows. The background studies and literature reviews done in this project, as well as partial research outputs of the proposed system, were compiled into a tutorial, titled “Big Graph Analytics Systems”, which was given at the ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data in San Francisco in 2016. Some comparison studies and performance analysis of related existing systems, from which we drew useful insights to develop our system, were published in the 2016 IEEE International Conference on Big Data. Preliminary studies that inspired the distributed framework and the query processing API of the proposed system were published in the PVLDB journal (Volume 9, Number 5, 2016) and in the 2017 International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval. There are also a number of graph algorithm works that developed the graph indexes and query processing algorithms of various types of queries supported in our framework, which are critical to the efficient processing of graph queries by the system. These graph algorithms and graph indexes were published in top-tier conferences and journals including the 2016 IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering, the 2016 ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, the 2017 International Conference on Database Systems for Advanced Applications, and the 2018 ACM SIGMOD International Conference on Management of Data.

14206715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206715.value: The application programming interface (API) proposed for this project adopts procedural programming. While this is useful to more skilful application developers to allow them to develop more efficient programs, declarative query language may be more attractive to data analysts who care productivity more than performance. One possible solution could be constructing a layer of higher level API on top of the current API. There are also other classes of graph queries, e.g., those supported by Gremlin, Cypher and other declarative query languages, which also have many applications. While the focuses are different, it would be interesting to explore if the two types of systems can be integrated to provide more powerful graph analytics. We will continue to explore the usefulness of such an integration in applications in industry by talking more to our industrial collaborators and understanding their needs. Meanwhile, we will also study various graph query languages and consider whether a new query language is necessary or an existing one can be extended to support a wider range of graph queries.

14206715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206715.value: Graph data are becoming popularly used in companies and today billion-scale graphs are common. Although many distributed graph computing systems have been developed in the past, these systems are designed for handling graph analytic workloads. However, many real-world applications require to process various graph queries such as shortest-path distance queries, reachability queries, pattern matching queries, neighborhood queries, and keyword searches in graphs. For handling such large billion scale graphs, most existing graph query processing techniques are not scalable. This project developed a scalable system for efficient query processing in massive graphs. The system provides a general programming framework and a user-friend application programming interface to allow users to easily implement various distributed graph indexes and graph query processing algorithms, while the system transparently handles the complicated workload distributed and fault tolerance. We tested our system on a wide range of graph queries and showed that it achieves significantly better performance than existing distributed graph systems. The whole software package, including the system codes, application codes and libraries, are open source, which will benefit both researchers and practitioners working on the same topic and on graph data analytics in general.

14206815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206815.value: 脈衝電場（PEF）廣泛應用在食品工業中的非熱滅活機制和DNA轉染電穿孔技術。雖然細胞的電穿孔機制已被廣泛報導，我們目前尚不清楚理解這機制可否源用於不同食物中的細菌孢子，大眾對細菌孢子的PEF失活研究仍然所知不多。這項目旨在通過機電理論和微機電系統，以加強PEF對細菌孢子活力和發芽脈衝機制的理解。我們用模擬數值和實驗來驗證PEF對細菌孢子的影響，並製作一個微流體脈衝電場芯片，以達至高效節能的脈衝電場效果，為將來工業實施借鏡，並以電化學和熒光來研究細菌孢子萌發的過程。我們將表徵和優化PEF參數，研究在液體食物中的需氧芽孢桿菌孢子和厭氧梭狀芽胞桿菌孢子失活情況，以達致食物新鮮度、更長的保質期和更高的成本效益。基於前期的掃描電子顯微鏡結果顯示PEF導致細菌孢子收縮及產生皺紋，我們假設芽孢外殼是一個超彈性材料，並且所述應力-應變的關係可以從應力-應變密度函數計算出來。我們提出一個新的模型，分析細菌孢子在基於Mooney-Rivlin模型電場下的電機應力影響。對於超彈性材料，我們將模擬芽孢外殼與電解質界面表面的電荷。在我們未公開的實驗結果中，電場和孢子殼的厚度變化有著一個非線性的反比例。我們用COMSOL有限元分析，配以SEM，pH值，疏水性和對芽孢桿菌屬和梭狀芽胞桿菌物種電化學測量驗證。初步研究發現，經PEF處理的細菌孢子有著更快的萌發速度和更高程度的同質性。我們也會研究PEF對細菌孢子發芽的其餘影響。細菌孢子主要通過發芽過程導致食品變質和食源性疾病。近年社會推動非熱技術處理食物，以追求更多養份及保存食物之味道和新鮮感。這頂研究從理論分析和實驗兩方面檢討PEF對細菌孢子萌發的影響。

14207315.label: Project Objectives
14207315.value: Devise a methodology for unsupervised generation of second language (L2) phone-like units directly from non-native speech data, with the aim of better modeling the L2 acoustic-phonetic space. These L2 phone-like units will capture similarities and deviations from the native (i.e. L1, or primary language) phone units. The native phone units can originate mainly from the target language and/or the learners’ mother tongue(s). Develop a data-driven approach to derive an annotation scheme for the L2 phone-like units that can capture both categorical and non-categorical deviations from the target canonical phone units. Develop a unified (i.e. single-pass) strategy for mispronunciation detection and diagnosis based on acoustic decoding of L2 speech using the L2 phone-like units. The framework strives for performance improvement by incorporating all available contextual information, including the phone-state transition information to capture co-articulatory effects across L2 phone-like units, as well as phonological information derived from canonical pronunciations of text prompts used for eliciting the learners’ speech.

14207315.value: 計算機輔助發音訓練（CAPT）技術能夠實現自我為導向的，全天候的的語言學習，並能為學習者提供個性化的反饋。它可以彌補教師人數的不足，支持不斷增長的語言學習者。這特別適用於中國學生學習英語。同時，也和香港平民大眾息息相關，因為英語能力是我們香港作為一個國際城市維持競爭力的一個關鍵因素。CAPT主要集中於錯誤發音檢測和診斷（MDD）── 前者对发音作出正確或错误的二元決策，而後者則需要識別錯誤模式，以生成糾正反饋。有別於母語語音，非母語語音通常呈現出一系列的偏差，這些偏差可能来自於學習者母語的影響。音素的缺失，插入或置換，會導致錯誤發音。目標音素可能會被替換成可分類的置換，即一個來自於目標語言或學習者母語的音素。另一個可能性是，目標音素被替換成不可分類的置換，即一個與多個音素相似的“類音素單元”。這兩種類型的置換，在聲學上和正確的音素相類似。這些體現了MDD的挑戰性。以前的工作大多基於這樣的假設，即非母語語音可以由目標語言的音素集來進行標註。然而，那些曾經嘗試這樣標註的語言學家已經明確指出，目標語言的音素集在描述非母語語音時具有嚴重的缺點。這激發了目前提議的項目，該項目旨在開發一種無監督的方法，用於從學習者的語音數據中，直接產生一個第二語言（L2）的類音素單元集。我們將還開發一個數據驅動的方法，以獲取L2類音素單元和母語音素單元的對應關係。這樣就構成了一個描述性框架，它融合了可分類的和不可分類的置換，以達致呈現L2語音的聲學發音特徵。我們將充分利用這一描述性的框架，開發一個統一的（即一次過的）MDD策略。目前，即使最先進的語音識別技術，其性能仍然遠遠不足於開發合適的MDD。因此，我們將開發一種增強版的，由L2類音素單元表示的聲學解碼公式。為了進一步改善性能，我們將利用所有可用的背景信息，包括音素狀態轉換時捕獲到的協同發音信息，和引導學習者發音的提示文本的正確發音。 當聲學解碼器選擇了一個可分類或不可分類的置換，也就意味著一個錯誤發音被檢測到，而相對應的診斷將直接由置換單元和對應母語音素的映射關係中得到。

14207315.label: Realisation of objectives
14207315.value: Objective 1: Devise a methodology for unsupervised generation of second language (L2) phone-like units directly from non-native speech data, with the aim of better modelling the L2 acoustic-phonetic space. These L2 phone-like units will capture similarities and deviations from the native (i.e. L1, or primary language) phone units. The native phone units can originate mainly from the target language and/or the learners’ mother tongue(s). We started out devising a multi-distribution deep neural network (DNN) for mispronunciation detection diagnosis. This approach takes advantage of the new deep learning paradigm in an attempt to excel beyond the extended recognition network approach that our research team has been devising. We proposed an acoustic-graphemic-phonemic model (AGPM) using the multi-distribution, whose input captures the acoustic information, phonemic/phonetic information and also graphemic information. Hence, the AGPM can implicitly model both grapheme-to-likely-pronunciation and phoneme-to-likely-pronunciation conversions, which are integrated into acoustic modeling. The AGPM is applied directly to L2 speech (i.e. non-native speech data). This model is flexible in that we can use only graphemic information, i.e. acoustic-graphemie model (AGM), only phonemic information, i.e. acoustic-phonemic model (APM) and the full AGPM. AGPM gave the best performance. Experiments show that the proposed approach achieves a phone error rate (PER) of 11.1%. In mispronunciation detection and diagnoses, the false rejection rate (FRR), false acceptance rate (FAR), and diagnostic error rate (DER) for MDD are 4.6%, 30.5%, and 13.5%, respectively. This approach outperforms the previous ERN approach using DNNs as acoustic models, whose PER, FRR, FAR, and DER are 16.8%, 11.0%, 43.6%, and 32.3%, respectively. Additionally, since L2 non-native speech pronunciation also includes deviations from the native pronunciation in terms of intonation, stress and pitch accent, we also extended the multi-distribution DNN approach described above to support intonation classification of L2 English speech. If a classified intonation is different from the target one, we consider that mispronunciation is detected and appropriate diagnostic feedback can be provided thereafter. We proposed a new system for transcribing speech data for intonation classification, primarily into the two groups of rising or falling intonation. Based on the annotated data hundreds of Chinese learners of English, we develop an intonation classifier which can determine the intonation of L2 English speech as either rising or falling with an accuracy of 93.0%. We also extended the multi-distribution DNN approach for automatic lexical stress detection and pitch accent detection, Experimental results show that the MD-DNN for lexical stress detection achieves an accuracy of 87.9% in syllable classification (primary/secondary/no stress) for words with three or more syllables. This performance is much better than those of our previous work using Gaussian mixture models and the prominence model (PM), whose accuracies are 72.1% and 76.3% respectively. Approached similarly as the lexical stress detector, the pitch accent detector obtains an accuracy of 90.2%, which is better than the results of using the GMMs and PM by about 9.6% and 6.9% respectively. Objective 2: Develop a data-driven approach to derive an annotation scheme for the L2 phone-like units that can capture both categorical and non-categorical deviations from the target canonical phone units. Articulatory features (AFs) has been a very useful for characterizing and labeling speech. AFs are the positions of articulators when pronouncing phonemes and reflect the pronunciation mechanisms of each phoneme. The use of AFs in MDD is helpful in distinguishing between non-natively and natively produced phonemes. Since articulatory features have direct association with phonemes, three models with articulatory features are proposed based on the acoustic-phonemic model (APM): (1) articulatory-acoustic-phonemic model (AAPM) that embeds articulatory features directly into input features; (2) AAPM with feature representation (R-AAPM) to represent original input features with articulatory features; and (3) articulatory multi-task acoustic-phonemic model (AMT-APM) where phoneme recognizer and articulatory feature classifiers are trained simultaneously in multi-task manner. Compared with baseline phoneme-based APM, the proposed deep learning framework extended with AFs in the new architecture performs better in mispronunciation detection and diagnosis, and gains 5.6% and 7.0% improvement in F1-Measure and diagnostic accuracy respectively. In terms of annotation of L2 phoneme categories, traditional approaches mainly used native phoneme categories. But due to the deviations of non-native productions from native productions, such an annotation tasks is difficulty if not impossible. To better represent L2 speech, this work explores non-native phonetic patterns (NN-PPs) of each native phoneme by an unsupervised approach. We apply an optimized k-means algorithm to cluster state-based phonemic posterior-grams, which are generated with a deep neural network. Then, to discover the NN-PPs related to each native phoneme, we perform forced alignment to divide L2 speech into segments grouped by native phonemes. We use the cluster sequences within segments derived from clustering results to represent different phonetic patterns of each native phoneme. Finally, we apply Cluster Sequence Analysis to discover each phoneme’s potential NN-PPs. We verified experimentally that NN-PPs can extend the native phoneme categories to better describe L2 speech, which can enrich the existing approaches to MDD for better performance. Objective 3: Develop a unified (i.e. single-pass) strategy for mispronunciation detection and diagnosis based on acoustic decoding of L2 speech using the L2 phone-like units. The framework strives for performance improvement by incorporating all available contextual information, including the phone-state transition information to capture co-articulatory effects across L2 phone-like units, as well as phonological information derived from canonical pronunciations of text prompts used for eliciting the learners’ speech. Recent research sees the emergence of the end-to-end approaches using deep learning, which can directly model the inter-relations between an input sequence with an output sequence. Impressive results have been obtained in speech recognition, speech-to-speech translation, text-to-speech synthesis, etc. Hence our investigation took up the challenge of investigating end-to-end approaches for mispronunciation detection and diagnosis. We used Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) to build an end-to-end speech recognition for the mispronunciation detection and diagnosis (MDD) task. Our approach is end-to-end models, while phonemic or graphemic information, or forced alignment between different linguistic units, are implicit. We conduct experiments that compare the proposed CNN-RNNCTC approach with alternative mispronunciation detection and diagnoses approaches. The F-measure of our approach is 74.65%, which significantly outperforms the previous approaches, namely, the Extended Recognition Network (ERN) (S-AM) by 44.75% and State-level Acoustic Model (S-AM) by 32.28% relatively. The relative improvement in F-measure when over Acoustic-Phonemic Model (APM), Acoustic-Graphemic Model (AGM) and Acoustic-Phonemic-Graphemic Model (APGM) are 9.57%, 5.04% and 2.77% respectively.

14207315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207315.value: This research project aims to model non-native learner’s speech for a target language to enable better mispronunciation detection and diagnoses to support self-directed learning through computer-aided pronunciation training systems. The performance of automatic speech recognition technology is often drastically affected by non-native acoustic-phonetic deviations from native productions. To address this problem, we began with the development of a deep learning approach that we refer to as the multi-distribution deep neural network (DNN) that can incorporate acoustic, graphemic and phonemic/phonetic and information (AGPM model) that brought about significant performance improvements in mispronunciation detection and diagnoses (MDD) of non-native learner’s speech, as compared to the convention approaches, e.g. extended recognition networks [Li, Qian & Meng, TASLP 2017]. In addition, we also show that address the suprasegmental issues in non-native speech variations for intonation, stress and pitch [Li, Wu & Meng 2017][Li, Meng et al. 2018]. In order to better capture the articulatory characteristics of non-native speech, we leverage the use of articulatory features (AFs) as a set of compact descriptors. These are also used in multi-task training for the deep learning approach, which shows how articulatory information can improve the performance of mispronunciation detection and diagnoses [ICME 2018][ICASSP 2019]. We also devised an unsupervised approach that can discover the non-native phonetic patterns using Cluster Sequence Analysis – these patterns can be annotated to enrich the phonetic inventory of existing approaches for better performance in MDD [INTERSPEECH 2018]. Finally, we also leverage the rapid advancements in end-to-end neural frameworks, to devise a single-pass approach incorporating Convolutional Neural Network, Recurrent Neural Network, and Connectionist Temporal Classification (CNN-RNN-CTC) to build an end-to-end speech recognition system that can outperform the AGPM approach [ICASSP 2019]. Kindly note: The PI has been pursuing the line of research in Computer-Aided Pronunciation Training for a number of years. Her last GRF project (before the current project) focused on discriminative modeling (and not Deep Neural Networks), and was completed in November 2014. Thereafter, she continued with her PhD student (Kun Li) on the line of research, but focusing on the use of Deep Neural Networks (DNN). By the start date of the current project (i.e. 1 January, 2016), Kun Li has completed his PhD degree and so he is supported by this project as a Postdoctoral Fellow. Based on the research work in the thesis, they have submitted 3 journal papers around November 2015. These papers took a while to go through various revisions before they are eventually accepted in 2017. Hence, the 3 journal papers are listed as research outputs of the current project in Section 8.

14207315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207315.value: Our most recent approach of CNN-RNN-CTC (Leung, Liu and Meng 2019) that uses an end-to-end speech recognition framework for the task of MDD does not require any explicit phonemic and graphemic information input and hence no forced alignment is required. The experiment results show that our approach significantly outperform previously approaches, including those that utilize phonemic and graphemic information input. This work can be used as the baseline of end-to-end approach for the task of MDD. Future work can focus on enriching the end-to-end framework with further linguistic constraints to improve performance.

14207315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207315.value: This research project aims to model non-native learner’s speech for a target language to enable better mispronunciation detection and diagnoses to support self-directed learning through computer-aided pronunciation training systems. The performance of automatic speech recognition technology is often drastically affected by non-native acoustic-phonetic deviations from native productions. To address this problem, we devised a novel deep learning approach that incorporates acoustic, graphemic and phonemic/phonetic information (AGPM) to improve mispronunciation detection and diagnoses (MDD) performance beyond the existing approaches. We have also make use of articulatory features that describe the motions of pronunciation gestures to represent how non-native pronunciations may deviate from native productions. We also used multi-task training of deep neural networks to show how the articulatory features can also help improve MDD performance. We have also devised an unsupervised, data-driven approach to find non-native phonetic patterns to better describe L2 speech to enrich existing approaches to MDD. Finally, we also present a single-pass approach that adopts the novel, end-to-end architecture that can bring further performance MDD improvements above AGPM.

14207515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207515.value: The aim of this project is to conduct a comprehensive study to synthesize and characterize high-quality two-dimensional layered materials and their heterostructures in large area with controllable crystallographic orientations as well as the novel electronic/optoelectronic devices thereof. Graphene is an atomically thin two-dimensional (2D) layered material composed of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice. Its unique and superior properties are widely known. Unfortunately, graphene transistors cannot be effectively used for digital applications due to the absence of bandgap. Recently, electronic devices based on other emerging 2D layered materials, namely MoS2 and WS2, have demonstrated their excellent switching properties with ultralow standby power dissipation, as compared to the state-of-the-art characteristics of silicon based transistors. Combining 2D layered materials vertically and/or laterally is promising for future electronic and photonic applications due to the possibility of stacking the atomically-thin planar layers to produce novel device structures. Moreover, the excellent mechanical bendability, and high optical transparency of these materials enable them for near-term applications in large-area and high-performance electronics that are flexible and transparent. Understanding how these wafer-scale single-crystal 2D materials and their vertical/lateral heterostructures are prepared is crucial to this endeavor. We therefore propose to carry out a systematic investigation, using newly-established synthetic processes as well as well-tested characterization techniques, to elucidate and optimize the growth mechanism for the materials, and to explore new device properties. This study should enable the major proposed large-area single-crystal 2D materials and their heterostructures to be prepared and optimized. Its findings will enable effective fabrication of 2D materials and related devices to be applicable for printed and flexible electronics, and will also provide a fundamental technical background for the future designs of novel electronic and optoelectronic devices, such as wearable energy harvesting devices, self-powered chemical sensors as well as the ultrasensitive “bipolar” photodetectors proposed in this project. 本研究计划旨在深入探讨制备高质量二维层状材料及异质结的新方法，及材料和器件的表征。 石墨烯是一个典型的由单层碳原子组成的二维六角层状材料。它的优异特性已得到充分地展示。遗憾的是它没有带隙，因而无法在数字电子技术中得到广泛应用。近年来，硫化钼和硫化钨等其他二维层状材料异军突起，以其优良性能，譬如优异的开关特性和极低的静态功耗等引起广泛关注。 由二维层状材料组成的纵向异质结及横向异质结在未来的电子学暨光电子学领域具有十分诱人的发展前景。它们可以构筑各种新奇的器件构型，具有优良的力学柔韧性和光学透光性。深入理解其纵向异质结及横向异质结，有利于二维层状材料的进一步发展。 在本研究计划中，我们将深入系统地探讨制备和表征高质量二维层状材料的新方法，并优化材料和器件制备参数，开发新的器件功能。我们期望研究成果在新性电子器件，譬如在穿戴式电子器件和零部件中得到应用。

14207515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207515.value: (1) We developed a method to prepare MX2-MX2 heterostructures. Particularly we find a growth promoter – a salt with alkaline metal and halide element. At present the largest growth area is around 100 micron times 30 microns, which can be transferred to other dielectric or flexible substrate via PVA adhesion technique. See more in Publication Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 13, 16, 17 & PhD theses. (2) We demonstrated that high-quality cm-sized MoS2 sheets can be synthesized on SiO2/Si by CVD technique. An ultra-sensitive photodetector based on vertical graphene/silicon or graphene/MoS2 heterostructure. The mechanisms have been fully interrogated and understood. See more in Publication Nos. 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15, 18, 19 & PhD theses. (3) By utilizing electrically gated graphene, we developed graphene based THz modulators, both experimentally and theoretically. We modified the Fresnel equations to describe a conductive interface in a total internal reflection geometry and revealed a new approach for modulation. To demonstrate this new mechanism, a broadband device achieving a modulation depth greater than 90% between 0.15 and 0.4 THz, and reaching a maximum of 99.3% at 0.24 THz has been designed. The modulation is achieved by applying a gate voltage between -0.1 and 2 V to a graphene layer in a total internal reflection geometry. Compared to conventional designs, the high modulation is realized without assistance from metamaterial structures, resonant cavities, or multi-stacked graphene layers. Thus, the design is efficient and facile-to-fabricate and can be easily retrofitted to most existing THz systems. This work opens up a new avenue of research as the device has verified the theory and demonstrates how it can be used to make practical devices, bringing a promising new paradigm for THz modulation, thin-film sensing, and noninvasive material characterization. See more in Publication Nos. 6, 14, 19, 20 & PhD theses. 14207615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207615.value: This projects aims at intelligent design of new metal filler geometries as well as formulations of polymer matrix in order to achieve high-performance stretchable electrically conductive polymer adhesives (SECAs). Flexible, especially stretchable, electronics are believed to bring about a revolution in the electronics industry by enabling many functions that are impossible for rigid circuits. Among various stretchable conductors, SECAs that consist of conductive fillers in a polymer matrix are a promising candidate because of their good electrical conductivity, reliable adhesion to various substrates, and facile preparation, all of which make them excellent candidates for interconnects in flexible/stretchable electronics. However, current SECAs exhibit significant increase in resistance during stretching due to the increase of the inter-particle distance of the fillers. This largely limits the use of SECAs in the stretchable electronics that demand high conductivity. We propose to address this challenge through a systematic approach consisting of material design, theoretical modeling and experimental characterizations. First, we will develop novel high aspect-ratio silver fillers with 2-D or 3-D structures, including spiky and hairy geometries. This design ensures good contact between individual metal fillers in all directions during stretching, thus reducing variations in the inter-particle distance of the fillers. Both Monte Carlo simulations and experiments will be performed to rationally design the filler shape, size, and aspect ratio to optimize the conductivity and reduce its dependence on mechanical stress. Second, we will generate new formulations for a polymer elastomer, polyurethane (PU), and use it as the SECA polymer matrix. Conductive polymers, such as polyaniline (PANI), will be incorporated into PU by forming PU-PANI interpenetrating polymer network (IPN) structures or cross-linked ladder polymer structures to improve the electrical conductivity of the matrix itself. Lastly, the newly developed SECAs will be systematically examined with theoretical models and chemical, structural and electrical characterizations, and the results will be used to establish microscopic models that describe the correlation between electrical conductivity and mechanical stretchability. The proposed research will dramatically increase the conductivity, elasticity, and reliability required for materials used in stretchable devices, and will therefore accelerate the advent of the flexible electronics era. In addition, the proposed stretchable SECAs are environmentally friendly, bio-compatible, and consume little energy in processing, which together serve to promote the growing trend of green electronics. 本項目旨在通過設計金屬填料的幾何形狀以及聚合物基質材料、實現高性能的拉伸導電性聚合物粘合劑（SECAS）。 賦予傳統的剛性電路以柔性，尤其是伸縮性，可讓現有的電子器件具有許多新的功能，從而引領電子工業的一場革命。在各種伸縮性導體材料之中，SECAS以其良好的導電性、可靠的粘附性、以及方便的使用性，被視為最有希望的柔性/可拉伸電子器件的導電連接材料。然而，目前的SECAS在拉伸過程中由於導電填料的粒子間距離的增加而電阻顯著增加。這在很大程度上限制了可拉伸的電子設備的性能。 在本項目中，我們將通過材料設計，理論建模和實驗表徵的一個系統研究來解決這一挑戰。首先，我們將開發大高寬比、髮狀和刺狀的銀填料結構。這種設計可減少在拉伸過程中填充物因彼此距離變化而失去接觸。通過仿真和實驗並用，我們將設計填料的形狀，大小，和高寬比，以優化導電性和減少其受機械應力的影響。第二，我們將合成新的聚合物彈性體，包括改性的聚氨酯（PU）和聚苯胺（PANI）與PU形成的互穿聚合物網絡（IPN）結構或交聯的梯形聚合物結構。最後，將對新開發的SECAS進行系統的表徵。基於這個結果將建立描述導電性和機械拉伸之間的相關性的微觀模型。 本項目的研究成果將大大增加現有導電膠的導電性和彈性，及其在拉伸裝置中使用的可靠性。這將加速柔性電子時代的到來。此外，本項目研發的SECAS材料具有環保、生物兼容、加工耗能少等優點，將有助於推動綠色電子產品的發展。

14207615.label: Realisation of objectives
14207615.value: We have achieved the technical objectives with modified methodologies. Firstly, for the silver fillers, we have developed a novel emulsion-templated method to fabricate a three-dimensional (3D) interconnected silver nanowire (Ag NW) aerogel, which can then be fully filled with elastomer to achieve high stretchability and conductivity simultaneously. This approach allows for construction of an isotropic porous structure and can be applied to various 1D and 2D conductive fillers. Through characterizations and theoretical modelling we elucidated the mechanisms that enable the high performance of the composite and point out that the unique isotropic micro-pore structure of the composites is beneficial for maintaining the good conductivity of the material within a wide-stretching range. Secondly, for the SECA polymer matrix, we have found an alternative polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)- elastomer combined formula to replace the originally proposed PU-PANI IPN. The advantage of the new system is the fabrication simplicity. In the meantime, it does not compromise the conductivity of the SECA as the new processing method is capable of creating a high-conductivity Ag 3D network. Thirdly, to understand the structure-charge transport property relations, we have performed theoretical simulations on the deformation of a spherical Ag NW architecture under strain and further performed in-situ characterization on the deformed structures. The results reveal that the Ag NW skeleton will change its shape to accommodate external stress and that the stress will concentrate in the middle of the Ag NW sphere. Such deformation reduces the local strain at the Ag NW-formed walls of the pore structure, thus allowing the composite to maintain its conductivity at a high strain value. In this sense, the 3D Ag NW micro-pore structures are generally more desirable for stretchable electronics applications than 2D Ag NW frameworks. We also analysed the variation of the electrical conductivity with different Ag NW density using the tunneling model proposed by Simmons. The result shed light on how the unique geometry of the NW framework allows for high conductivity at relatively low AgNW loading. Finally, we tested the electrical properties of the SECAs and established a parametric model to relate AgNW concentration and network morphology with the electrical performance and the deformation property of the SECAs under mechanical stress.

14207615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207615.value: Through this project, we have conceived and developed several composite designs based on conductive filler/stretchable matrix combinations. The core research findings are summarized below: 1. We have developed an emulsion-templated method to fabricate a porous silver nanowire (Ag NW)-based aerogel. The aerogel displays an isotropic and hierarchical microstructure with good uniformity and processing controllability. To render the aerogel stretchable, the open cells in the aerogel is infiltrated with an elastomer material. The obtained composite exhibits high conductivity (65.7 S/cm) and good stretchability (130% strain) at a remarkably low density (50 mg/cm^3) of Ag NWs. Through characterizations and theoretical modelling we elucidate the mechanisms that enable the high performance of the composite and point out that the unique isotropic micro-pore structure of the composites is beneficial for maintaining the good conductivity of the material within a wide-stretching range. The results highlight the Ag NW/PDMS composites as promising stretchable conductors in the application of soft electronics in the human body. Furthermore, the emulsion-templated method is a versatile strategy for fabrication porous aerogel and it can be easily extended to other highly conductive materials. (Publication #1) 2. We have developed a facile process to utilize natural wood structures to fabricate carbon/silicone composite based flexible pressure sensors. Our method leverages the unique multichannel structure of the composite and introduces variable surface topography with a blade-cutting process. The optimised horizontally-cut composite-based sensors exhibit high sensitivity (10.74 kPa^−1) in a very wide linear region (100 kPa). The overall outstanding sensing properties of the sensors allow for accurate continuous measurement of human pulse and respiration, benefiting the real-time health signal monitoring and disease diagnoses. (Publications #2 ) 3. We have also extended the mechanical - electrical property study to design of strain sensors. We fabricated a stretchable polyurethane grid via near-field electrospinning and decorated the grid with conductive Ag NWs to enable strain sensing. The optimised sensor exhibits a high gauge factor (GF=36) under high strain (100%), representing the best performance combination reported for flexible strain sensors. In good agreement with the theoretical model, the strain sensors are only sensitive to the strain along the electrode direction and are insensitive to perpendicular direction strains. Based on this characteristic response, we demonstrate the excellent capability of the strain sensors in distinguishing hand movement (i.e., bending vs. shaking), suggesting the great application potential of the sensors in robotic vision and prosthesis. (PhD thesis, Huang Yan, a manuscript is also in preparation)

14207615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207615.value: In this project we developed methodologies to fabricate free-standing SECAs. To allow for more efficient integration of such conductive materials with flexible electronic systems, one should further develop ways of direct patterning and connecting the SECAs on functional circuits and devices. This could be done by modifying the fabrication procedure and templating materials of the composite, as well as exploring the use of local reaction to create SECA-device bonding.

14207615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207615.value: Stretchable and conductive composites are an important component of flexible electronics. However, it still remains a challenge to achieve high stretchability and high conductivity simultaneously in the composites to ensure high reliability in use. Through this project we have developed a facile emulsion-templated method to fabricate a porous silver nanowire (Ag NW)-based aerogel and stretchable conductive composites. We performed a comprehensive investigation combining theoretical and experimental approaches on the mechanical and electrical performances of the material system. The results elucidate the key mechanisms that enable the high performance of the composite and point out that the unique isotropic micro-pore structure of the composites is beneficial for maintaining the good conductivity of the material within a wide-stretching range. Our study provides a promising material candidate for soft electronics applications. Furthermore, the emulsion-templated method can be used as a versatile strategy for fabrication porous aerogel and it can be easily extended to other highly conductive materials. Through this project we have also extended our study on the general relations between the mechanical and electrical properties of conductive composites and developed facile processes to fabricate high performance flexible pressure sensors and strain sensors that can be used in various biomedical applications.

14208215.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14208215.value: 偽隨機函數，密碼共享，加密和認證：複雜性和構造

14208215.label: Project Objectives
14208215.value: To determine the implementation complexity of weak pseudorandom functions, secret sharing schemes, encryption and authentication protocols. To design new, fundamentally different kinds of pseudorandom functions and secret sharing schemes. To investigate cryptographic applications of our results in the areas of fully homomorphic encryption and program obfuscation.
rows: To determine the implementation complexity of weak pseudorandom functions, secret sharing schemes, encryption and authentication protocols.
To design new, fundamentally different kinds of pseudorandom functions and secret sharing schemes.
To investigate cryptographic applications of our results in the areas of fully homomorphic encryption and program obfuscation.

14208215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208215.value: We propose to investigate the complexity of implementations of the following cryptographic primitives: Weak and strong pseudorandom functions, secret sharing schemes, encryption and authentication protocols. Besides the direct relevance of this question to the design of cryptographic components, complexity-theoretic measures of efficiency play an important role in applications of fully homomorphic encryption and indistinguishability obfuscation. Unlike their strong counterparts, weak PRFs are not bound by the "natural proofs" limitations of Razborov and Rudich and may thus admit substantially simpler implementations. We consider a specific type of construction in the class AC0 o + and outline approaches for proving security against various types of attacks. While strong PRFs of low complexity have been constructed before, we seek more natural and efficient candidates. We outline a particular proposal that would be especially amenable to obfuscation. We give new evidence for the existence of secret sharing schemes whose sharing and reconstruction algorithms can both be implemented in the class AC0. We view this evidence as surprising: Known schemes make heavy use of linear operations and therefore do not admit AC0 implementations. We believe this line of research may lead to a new paradigm for constructing secret sharing schemes and new fundamental questions regarding the complexity of secret sharing. We also aim to study the complexity of authentication and encryption. As an initial challenge, we ask whether these primitives can be implemented in the class AC0. We discuss connections between this problem and recent work on the complexity of AC0-samplable distributions. 我們提出研究以下幾個密碼原件的實現複雜性：弱和強偽隨機函數，密碼共享方案，加密和認證協議。複雜性理論對效率的度量除了和密碼組件的設計直接相關，還在完全同臺加密和不可分辨混淆的應用中發揮重要作用。 與強偽隨機函數不同，弱偽隨機函數不受Razborov和Rudich的自然證明法限制，因而可能有相當簡單的实现方案。我们考虑一个特定的能在AC0oMOD2 类實現的构造并且概述证明其抵御各种攻击的方法。强伪随机函数雖然以前已经有能在較低複雜度類實現的构造，我們尋求更加自然和有效的候選方案。 我們對分享和重建算法可以在AC0類被實現的密碼分享方案的存在提出了新的證據。這個證據令人吃驚：已知的方案大量使用了線性運算因此不能在AC0類里實現。這方面的研究可能讓我們獲得新的秘密分享方案的範例和關於構造秘密分享方案複雜性的基礎問題。 我們也致力於研究認證以及加密的複雜性。我們首先研究是否這些元件可以在AC0類中實現作為最初的挑戰。我們討論這個問題和最近關於可以被AC0取樣的分佈的工作之間的聯繫。

14208215.label: Realisation of objectives
14208215.value: The complexity of existing pseudorandom functions and secret sharing schemes as well as candidate constructions was thoroughly studied in this project. For secret sharing, the main conclusion is that sharing and reconstruction by highly parallel (bounded-depth AND/OR) circuits is possible. This contrasts with previous constructions that are linear-algebraic in nature. For pseudorandom functions, we argued that weak variants are less complex than strong ones, though we also discovered some new candidate attacks to our proposed constructions. While we did not manage to improve the complexity of encryption and authentication, in ongoing joint work with Yuval Ishai and others we made progress on the related question of designing low-complexity distributions that are hard to learn. Applications to homomorphic encryption and program obfuscation was largely done by other authors (Lin, Vaikutanathan, Sahai, and others). However in joint work with Ishai and Srinivasan we discovered an unexpected application to leakage-resilient computation, solving a 10-year old problem in this area. Overall the objectives of the project have been achieved. The funding was not completely used owing to the award of a HKPFS scholarship to Ph.D. student Christopher Williamson who worked on this project. NOTE: The RGC funding acknowledgment is mistakenly omitted from the conference publication "Approximate bounded indistinguishability". I plan to rectify this omission will be rectified in the full version of the paper which will be made available online.

14208215.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208215.value: This theoretical project led to progress to several questions that have been open for a long time and gave rise to some new ones. Some of the main findings are: 1. The share size in threshold secret sharing schemes must grow linearly with the number of participants, even if the secret is a single bit. This was proved using a new information-theoretic method. (from "Threshold Secret Sharing Requires a Linear-size Alphabet") 2. It is possible to compile any circuit so that an adversary who computes a low-complexity function of the whole set of wires obtains no information about the computation. This was previously known to hold only assuming additional "secure hardware" or unproven assumptions. (from "Unconditionally Secure Computation Against Low-complexity Leakage") 3. Secret-sharing schemes of low complexity (bounded depth AND/OR circuits) can be constructed. Various new tradeoffs between parameters of such schemes (secrecy, reconstruction advantage, information leakage) were obtained, in some cases giving rise to tight results. (from "Bounded Indistinguishability and the Complexity of Recovering Secrets" and "Approximate Bounded Indistinguishability")

14208215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208215.value: After the completion of the project there has been follow-up on several fronts. One direction is to apply insights from the construction of low-complexity secret sharing schemes to obtain new insights about approximate degree, an important measure of boolean functions. Some preliminary results were obtained and a new RGC-funded project on this topic was initiated. Another direction is to extend the leakage-resilience results to a larger, more realistic class of leakage functions. Some preliminary discussions were held, but current methods appear largely inadequate.

14208215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208215.value: Simpler, faster, more parallel implementations of cryptographic functions are important not only because they may speed up crucial secure computations (like e-commerce) but also because they open the door to previously unimaginable ones, like fully private computation on the cloud. The project takes a small step in that direction by rigorously analyzing what is possible and what isn't for some basic cryptographic functions, which serve as the foundation on which others are built.

14208315.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14208315.value: 信息理論上可靠和無法檢測的通訊

14208315.label: Project Objectives
14208315.value: Information theoretic characterization of problem models: The primary goal for each of the models we consider is to understand the fundamental information-theoretic tradeoffs between deniability and throughput. Tools from information theory (among others, hypothesis testing, information-theoretic security, random coding, stochastic encoding, strong converses, and coding theory) seem useful, but a better understanding of their implications in deniable communication is needed. Investigation of interaction of deniability requirement with other communication goals: An important property of many communication systems is modularity. For instance, the fact that in many point-to-point communication systems, compression at the source can be done independently of channel coding (building in redundancy to combat noise) leads to simpler end-to-end design. An important part of our project will be to examine the extent to which existing communication systems that can satisfy varying goals (such as secrecy, robustness to jamming, and network coding) can also be made deniable. Design of computationally efficient schemes for problem models: Information-theoretic results often rely on “random coding” arguments, which argue about the existence of communication schemes with desirable properties, without necessarily providing an explicit design, or computationally tractable encoding/decoding schemes. For our results to have an impact on real-world communication systems, our project will also focus on investigating coding-theoretic techniques for the design of computationally tractable deniable communication systems.

14208315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208315.value: 溝通，說話和聆聽，是人類的基本需求。然而，在日益完善的通訊網絡中，經常有人在監看著我們的通訊。有些情況，即使正在通訊的同時（不單是通訊的內容），也能影響我們的現實生活。舉例來說，假如你是一位在專制的社會里活躍於政治的公民，即使你與外界溝通也可被作為報復的充分理由。這份建議書的目的是研究能夠滿足兩項需求的通訊模型。首先，從源頭（Alice）發出至目的地（Bob）的所有通訊是可靠的，也就是說，通訊協議應該能夠抵抗隨機噪聲，甚至是主動的干擾。第二，假如通訊被第三方（Eve）偷聽，通訊也不能被Eve知道。這也就是說，Eve不單止不能了解源頭的信息是什麼，而且，Eve也不能判斷源頭是否正在通訊。為了實現這種能夠否認的通訊，我們建議Bob和Eve之間可能存在不對稱（例如，Eve的信道噪聲或許會比Bob的信道噪聲要高，或者Eve僅觀測到Bob所了解的一部分）。我們將會使用信息理論的工具去解決這一系列的問題。首先，我們會用假設檢驗來嚴格定義能夠否認的通訊，然後，無論Eve利用何種估計策略，我們的通訊協議是“十分容易否認的”。我們的目標是在各種通訊設置上（有線，無線和量子信道／網絡），證明以上這種能夠否認的通訊的最優率，並且找到一個能夠接近甚至能達到此最優率的可行方案。

14208315.label: Realisation of objectives
14208315.value: 1. Information-theoretic characterization of problem models: In our ISIT 2018 work, we designed codes that simultaneously provide secrecy, stealth, and reliability against adversarial jamming, and simultaneously attain information-theoretic limits. 2. Investigation of interaction of deniability requirement with other communication goals: In our ISIT 2018 works, we designed codes for covertness and stealth that are resilient to adversarial jamming (and also can provide physical layer security). 3. Design of computationally efficient schemes for problem models: We designed the first ever computationally tractable codes for covert communication using concatenated coding schemes, as outlined in our ISIT 2016 paper.

14208315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208315.value: 1. Research output "Computationally efficient deniable communication" designed the first computationally tractable codes that are suitable for covert communications at optimal rates. Due to negligence/lack of communication among authors, this grant was unfortunately not acknowledged in this paper -- the PI apologizes for this! 2. Research output "Multipath Stealth Communication with Jammers" considered a problem where multimodal communication can encode stealthy communication, and simultaneously ensure reliability against adversarial jamming, while also ensuring information-theoretic secrecy, and that is information-theoretically rate-optimal. 3. Research output "Quadratically Constrained Myopic Adversarial Channels" was the first model to demonstrate the impact on attainable throughput of AWGN myopicity on active adversaries with a power constraint, and for a wide range of parameter ranges attained optimal or near-optimal throughputs, via novel achievability and converse arguments.

14208315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208315.value: A new research collaboration with Prof. Matthieu Bloch at Georgia Tech, a world-expert in covert communication, has been established, resulting in a new publication and ongoing work. Summative journal paper versions of the above research outputs (conference papers) are currently in various stages of preparation or review.

14208315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208315.value: This project considered the problem, in a variety of "whispering without being detected by an eavesdropped", even when the eavesdropper may actively be attempting to jam communications. We developed the first communication schemes that can simultaneously ensure non-detectability, and yet be simultaneously reliable to malicious jamming. This work has implications for communications in very adverse situations, where even the fact of communication may have consequences for parties attempting to communicate in the presence of a powerful/oppressive regime (one doesn't have to look too far for examples of such situations).

14208715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14208715.value: 带参数优化问题中的超模保持及其在运营管理中的应用

14208715.label: Project Objectives
14208715.value: Provide necessary and sufficient conditions under which the parametric optimization problems can preserve supermodularity. Provide efficient approaches to check the conditions. With this, we can implement the result from Objective 1 and know whether the supermodularity can be preserved in a given problem. Apply the theoretical results on certain operations management problems where supermodularity plays a key role, such as assemble-to-order problem. Extend the idea on some other important properties, such as submodularity.

Apply the theoretical results on certain operations management problems where supermodularity plays a key role, such as assemble-to-order problem.

14208715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208715.value: The concept of supermodularity has been serving as an important tool in economics and OR literature. It is often a key factor in deriving the monotone structure of the optimal decisions or equilibria. Hence, in many OR problems, one critical concern is whether the supermodularity can be preserved in the parametric optimization problems. In the literature, one of the key results on the preservation of supermodularity is by Topkis (1998), who states that if the feasible region is a lattice, then the supermodularity can be preserved. Nevertheless, the application of this result is rather limited since the lattice requirement is often too restrictive and cannot be satisfied in many problems. In this project, we aim to identify the least requirement, i.e., the necessary and sufficient conditions under which the supermodularity is preserved in certain parametric optimization problems. Specifically, we focus on three classes of optimization problems: the objective function is supermodular, concave supermodular, and linear, respectively. For each class, we intend to identify the corresponding condition on the feasible region such that the supermodularity is preserved. In our preliminary research, we have obtained some results for the first case (objective function being supermodular), and the third case (objective function being linear), and conjectures for the second case (objective function being concave supermodular). However, these conditions might not be easily checkable for a general feasible region. Thereafter, we plan to investigate on the efficient approaches to check whether these conditions can hold for some specific feasible regions. We will first identify several important types of the feasible region, and then develop approaches to check those feasible regions correspondingly. After that, we intend to apply our theoretical results on some OM problems, such as the assemble-to-order (ATO) problem, network flow problem, and coordinated pricing and inventory control problem. Specifically, we want to use the proposed necessary and sufficient conditions to identify the situations where the optimal policy has monotone structure. For the single period ATO problem, we have transformed the general condition to a more specific and intuitive version, which is much easier to check. Finally, we intend to extend this idea to other important properties, such as submodularity, identify the corresponding conditions to preserve those properties in the parametric optimization, and apply on related OM problems. 超模在经济及运筹领域里一直扮演着很重要的角色。它经常会成为推导最优决策或均衡之单调性的关键因素。因此，在许多运筹问题中，一个非常引人关注的问题就是超模特性能否在带参数优化问题中被保持。在过往的文献当中，关于超模之保持的一个重要结论是由Topkis(1998)提出的。他证明了假如可行域是一个格，那么超模之特性就可以在带参数优化中被保持。然而，由于格的要求非常严格而很多实际问题都不能满足此要求，因此，Topkis所提出之结论在应用层面上相当受限。在此项目中，我们希望发掘出对可行域的最低限度之条件，也就是必要充分条件，使得在此条件下超模特性可以在带参数优化问题中得到保持。其中，我们会把注意力集中在三类经典的优化问题当中：目标函数是超模，目标函数是凹且超模，目标函数是线性。对每一种类型的优化问题，我们都计划找到相对应的对可行域之要求，使得超模在对此可行域的优化可以被保持。在我们的前期研究中，我们已经对第一种类型（目标函数是超模）及第三种类型（目标函数是线性）的带参数优化问题得到了一些结果，并对第二种类型（目标函数是凹且超模）的结论做出了有一定依据的推测。然而，在得到这些条件之后，确定任意的可行域是否满足这些条件并不一定是一个容易完成的任务。因此，我们接下来计划研究如何有效检查某些特定的可行域是否满足这些条件。我们首先确定几种重要的可行域类型，然后分别研究检查这些可行域是否满足所提出之充要条件之方法。之后，我们计划把所得理论结果应用到一些运营管理问题上，例如面向订单装配问题，网络流问题，以及定价库存联合控制问题。我们尤其希望可以用所得到的充分必要条件去识别出在具体的运营管理问题中，于何种条件下最优策略会有单调性。对单阶段的面向订单装配问题，我们已经把得到的充要条件转化为一个对于问题结构的一个更直观具体的条件，使得我们可以有效检查问题是否存在超模特性。最后，我们计划把此思路拓展到其他重要的函数特性，例如子模，并找到相对应的使这些特性在带参数优化问题中得到保持的条件，并应用到相对应的运营管理问题。

14208715.value: All the four objectives are completed. The details are as follows. 1. We have stated a series of necessary and sufficient conditions to preserve the supermodularity. The details can be seen in the first research output. 2. In various settings, we provided efficient ways to check whether a given polyhedron can satisfy the conditions we proposed. The details can be seen in the first research output. 3. We have applied our theoretical findings in both the network flow problem and the assemble-to-order system. The details can be seen in the first research output. 4. We extend the idea to log-supermodularity (in the first research output) and the submodularity (in the second research output).

14208715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208715.value: We define a series of new concepts, which include mostly-sublattice and additive mostly sub-lattice. These new concepts generalize the classical concept of lattice in literature. Moreover, unlike the lattice, which is a sufficient condition for preserving supermodularity, our new concepts provide the conditions which are both necessary and sufficient. Moreover, these conditions are less restrictive and hence enhances the applicability in operations management. More specifically, while the lattice condition cannot be satisfied in many operations management applications and therefore we have difficulties in proving the supermodularity, the mostly-sublattice and additive mostly-sublattice conditions are easier to be satisfied and hence can be applied in many applications. We use network flow problem and assemble-to-order system as examples.

14208715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208715.value: In the future, it is of great interest to study the research question of similar flavor, but of different important properties. For example, we can study the conditions for getting submodularity, or supermodularity in some (but not all) components. Moreover, the theoretical tools we provided can be broadly applied in different operations management problems.

14208715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208715.value: In many operations management problems, it is often of interest to obtain insights from some sensitivity analysis, such as the optimal decisions would be increasing in some parameters. However, the existing theoretical tools for conducting the sensitivity analysis is rather restrictive and hence cannot be applied in many important operations management problems. In this project, we improve the theoretical tools, such that its applicability is enhanced and hence can be applied in a much broader class of application.

14208815.label: Project Objectives
14208815.value: The first objective is to investigate how to build a general multi-armed bandit framework for online recommendation. We plan to develop a general multi-armed bandit analysis framework. More specifically, we intend to explore a general convex function for estimating users' rewards. We will derive a general theoretical analysis framework which can provide guarantee for general convex functions for users' reward scores. The second objective is to develop effective algorithms to exploit shared contextual features in multi-armed bandit framework. We plan to develop effective and efficient multi-armed bandit algorithms to improve recommender systems by exploiting users' or arms' information. We first provide an in-depth study on the current state-of-the-art multi-armed bandit analysis methods in recommender systems. Then we will propose novel models to incorporate information among users or arms and share them among users or arms. Moreover, we will develop effective and efficient algorithms to learn the corresponding parameters for reward functions.

14208815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208815.value: 推荐系统，作为一种能够分析用户兴趣，并向用户推送适合的音乐，电影，书籍或新闻等消息的推荐工具，在当今的网络在线服务中已经变得越来越重要。 推荐系统的存在帮助用户过滤掉了大量的无用信息，有效解决了信息过载的问题，并且在新产品推广中也取得了很好的效果,从而提升了市场销售额。传统推荐系统所使用的技术大多基于用户所产生的历史数据间的相似度计算，比如用户浏览历史的相似度，视频网站中的点击和观看相似度，在线购物网站中的购买历史相似度等等。然而，用户的兴趣可能是多样性的，并且可能随时间而变化。对于新用户，由于缺乏足够的历史数据，传统推荐系统所采用的技术也很难学习到新用户的真实兴趣。 为了解决以上的问题，近期的研究将多臂老虎机问题 (Multi-Armed Bandit, MAB) 引入到推荐系统中。在推荐系统场景下，每个商品被建模成老虎机的每个摇臂，将用户对商品的行为建模成该摇臂的收益。在使用多臂老虎机算法的推荐系统中，每一次用户对商品的行为反馈都被记录，并用于更新多臂老虎机算法对用户兴趣的建模。多臂老虎机算法已经被验证能够有效解决推荐系统中的冷启动问题，并且多种基于多臂老虎机的扩展算法已经被提出，例如线性多臂老虎机算法，基于语境的多臂老虎机算法等。但是当前的基于多臂老虎机的推荐算法仍然存在以下一些问题： (1) 当前的MAB算法大多基于一个线性收益假设，即用户对商品的兴趣是基于商品特征的一个线性函数， 但对于非线性收益假设的MAB算法仍然缺乏理论和实际应用的研究。 (2)当前的MAB算法将用户和商品的特征分开对待，认为其互相独立，然而这种假设忽略了用户和商品之间一些共有的特征，也不能完整建模真实环境中的推荐系统。(3)当前MAB算法的理论分析是否仍适用于基于共享特征的非线性收益假设的MAB算法也是未知的，这要求我们找到新的理论分析工具保证基于共享特征的非线性收益假设的MAB推荐算法的应用效果。 为了开发更准确，更实用的推荐系统，在这个项目中，我们提出广义共享语境特征多臂老虎机算法研究。本项目需要解决的核心问题包括：(1) 如何使用基于凸函数的MAB算法动态建模用户对商品的兴趣。(2) 如何使用用户和商品共享的特征提升基于MAB算法的推荐准确性。(3) 如何基于扎实的理论分析框架来平衡探索用户新兴趣和保证推荐准确率，从而确保模型在实际应用中的效果。 本次广义共享语境特征的多臂老虎机算法研究项目包含以下几个重要的组成部分：首先，我们将研究如何使用基于线性（非线性）假设的MAB算法建模用户对商品的兴趣，并研究如何构建基于广义多臂老虎机算法的推荐系统。其次，我们将研究如何利用用户和商品的共享特征，扩展已有的多臂老虎机算法，以便最大程度的使用所有数据信息。最后，我们将在真实数据中进行试验，以验证所提算法的优缺点。 本项目的研究使我们能够开发出有效并且高效的MAB推荐算法，并应用于实际的推荐系统中。我们相信本项目所研究的算法及框架将提供出一些新颖的，有效的方式，对已有推荐系统中的MAB算法进行扩展和改进，包括MAB算法理论上的分析结果和实际应用中的效果，以解决现实世界中不断出现的新的问题。我们在项目中所提到的只是MAB领域研究的冰山一角，我们相信围绕的MAB问题和算法的研究将在未来得到更多的重视。我们相信本项目的研究不仅对于香港会产生很大的价值，对于世界范围内有兴趣探究MAB问题的人们也同样有重大意义。

14208815.label: Realisation of objectives
14208815.value: The objectives of our proposed project on building a general multi-armed bandit framework for online recommendation system and developing effective algorithms to exploit shared contextual features in multi-armed bandit framework have been fully completed based on the research plan. The proposed general multi-armed framework and the effective algorithms which exploits shared contextual features are recorded in multiple published papers. Objective 1: A general multi-armed bandit framework for online recommendation system In this project, we have developed multiple multi-armed bandit frameworks for online recommendation systems under different settings such as contextual multi-armed bandit, best arm identification, and multi-armed bandit with heavy-tailed payoffs. We rigorously derive the theoretical analysis for all the proposed algorithms to provide theoretical guarantees. 1) Contextual multi-armed bandit In the first ICONIP2016 paper [1], we investigated how to leverage social connections to improve online recommendation performance using contextual multi-armed bandit algorithms. In particular, we formulate the online social recommendation task as a contextual bandit problem and propose a Locality-sensitive Linear Bandit (LS.Lin) method to solve it. The proposed model incorporates users’ local social relations into a linear contextual bandit model and is capable to deal with the dynamic changes of user preference and the network structure. We provide a theoretical analysis of the proposed LS.Lin method and then demonstrate its improved performance for the online social recommendation in empirical studies compared with baseline methods. 2) Best arm identification In the ICDM2017 paper [2], we introduced a novel algorithm for best arm identification in multi-armed bandits (MAB), which considers risk control via successive rejects. Best arm identification is an important research problem in stochastic MAB, which can be applied into recommender systems to find the most-likely clicked items for users. Previous work usually selects the arm with the highest expected payoff as the best arm in a given decision-arm set. They ignore the risk of an arm when making a decision. In this work, we investigate the problem of Risk Control of Best Arm Identification (RCBAI) and incorporate the risk of an arm into the best decision via successive rejects. We develop an algorithm named as RCMAN.SR and derive an upper bound for the probability of error for RCBAI in stochastic MAB. The experimental results on synthetic datasets and real-world financial data demonstrate the superiority of our RCMAB.SR. 3) Multi-armed bandit with heavy-tailed payoffs In the UAI2018 paper [3], we investigated the pure exploration problem of MAB with heavy-tailed payoffs. We are inspired by heavy-tailed distributions in practical scenarios e.g., the number of ratings of the items in recommender systems. In this work, we break the assumption of payoffs with sub-Gaussian noises and assume that stochastic payoffs from bandit are with finite p-th moments. Two effective bandit algorithms based on different prior information are proposed. One is based on fixed confidence prior information, and the other is based on fixed budget prior information. We also derive theoretical guarantees for the proposed two bandit algorithms and demonstrate the effectiveness of two algorithms in the pure exploration of MAB with heavy-tailed payoffs in both synthetic data and real-world financial data. In the NeurIPS2018 paper [4], we introduced almost optimal algorithms for linear stochastic bandits with heavy-tailed payoffs problem. In this work, we rigorously analyze the regret lower bound of this problem and demonstrate the state-of-the-art algorithms are far from optimal. Through adopting median of means with a well-designed allocation of decisions and truncation based on historical information, we propose two novel bandit algorithms, where the regret upper bounds match the lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors. This work is the first to solve this problem optimally in the sense of the polynomial order on the total number of rounds to play bandits. Experimental results on synthetic datasets show the effectiveness of our algorithms. Objective 2: Effective algorithms to exploit shared contextual feature in multi-armed bandit framework During the project, we have designed multiple effective and efficient algorithms to exploit shared contextual features in multi-armed bandit framework. Our work focus on three aspects. i.e., improving the reliability of the exploration, handling high dimensional contextual data and generating features of arms. 1) Improve the reliability of the exploration In the CIKM2016 paper [6], we proposed two multi-armed bandit algorithms to improve the reliability of the exploration by constructing robust exploratory directions. The first algorithm is related to contextual information. With the rapid development of information retrieval (IR) systems, online learning to rank (OLR) approaches, which allow retrieval systems to automatically learn best parameters from user interactions, have attracted great research interests in recent years. We propose the Dual-Point Dueling Bandit Gradient Descent (DPDBGD) approach with a Contextual Interleaving (CI) method. In particular, the exploration of DP-DBGD is carefully conducted via two opposite stochastic directions and the proposed CI method constructs a qualified interleaved retrieval result list by taking historical explorations into account. We conduct experiments on several datasets and show that our algorithms improve online learning to rank performance over 10% compared with baseline methods. 2) Handle high dimensional contextual data In the AAAI2017 paper [5], we proposed a contextual multi-armed bandit algorithm in the setting of high-dimensional contextual data. In the era of big data, contextual data usually tend to be high-dimensional, which leads to new challenges for traditional linear bandits mostly designed for the setting of low-dimensional contextual data. Due to the curse of dimensionality, there are two challenges in most of the current bandit algorithms: the first is high time complexity, and the second is extreme large upper regret bounds with high-dimensional data. In this paper, to attack the above two challenges effectively, we develop an algorithm of Contextual Bandits via RAndom Projection (CBRAP) in the setting of linear payoffs, which works especially for high-dimensional contextual data. Besides, we prove an upper regret bound for the proposed algorithm, which is associated with reduced dimensions. We demonstrate improved performance on cumulative payoffs of CBRAP during its sequential decisions on both synthetic and real-world datasets, as well as its superior time-efficiency. 3) Generate features of arms In the second ICONIP2016 paper [7], we focused on the feature generations for arms, which can be used as contextual information for contextual multi-arm bandit algorithm. In this paper, we discover the topological order of skills using students’ exercise performance and using the technique of Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT). We can consider each student as a one-armed bandit and the topological order of skills as the shared features among arms. In future work, we will develop a contextual multi-armed bandit algorithm to recommend personalized learning paths for students using the generated contextual information. References [1]. 2016-ICONIP-Locality-Sensitive Linear Bandit Model for Online Social Recommendation [2]. 2017-ICDM-Risk Control of Best Arm Identification in Multi-Armed Bandits via Successive Rejects [3]. 2018-UAI-Pure Exploration of Multi-Armed Bandits with Heavy-Tailed Payoffs [4]. 2018-NIPs-Almost Optimal Algorithms for Linear Stochastic Bandits with Heavy-Tailed Payoffs [5]. 2017-AAAI-CBRAP-Contextual Bandits with RAndom Projection [6]. 2016-CIKM-Constructing Reliable Gradient Exploration for Online Learning to Rank [7]. 2016-ICONIP-Topological Order Discovery via Deep Knowledge Tracing

14208815.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208815.value: In this project, we focus on developing general multi-armed bandit (MAB) algorithm for online recommendation and also designing multiple effective and efficient algorithms to exploit shared contextual features in MAB framework. The theoretical analysis is rigorously derived for all the proposed algorithms to provide theoretical guarantees. To leverage social connections to improve online recommendation performance, we formulate the online social recommendation task as a contextual bandit problem and propose a Locality-sensitive Linear Bandit (LS.Lin) method to solve it. The proposed method incorporates users’ local social relations into a linear contextual bandit model and is capable to deal with the dynamic changes of user preference and the network structure. Both theoretical analysis and empirical experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method. To consider the risk control in the best arm identification problem, we introduced a novel algorithm which solves this case via successive rejects. We are the first to consider risk control when identifying the best arm. We develop an algorithm named as RCMAN.SR and derive an upper bound for the probability of error for RCBAI in stochastic MAB. The experimental results on synthetic datasets and real-world financial data demonstrate the superiority of our RCMAB.SR. We also proposed multiple algorithms for MAB with heavy-tailed payoffs which are practical in real scenarios. We investigated the pure exploration problem of MAB with heavy-tailed payoffs and designed two novel algorithms based on either fixed confidence or fixed budget prior information. We also introduced almost optimal algorithms for linear stochastic bandits with heavy-tailed payoffs. Through adopting median of means with a well-designed allocation of decisions and truncation based on historical information, we propose two novel bandit algorithms, where the regret upper bounds match the lower bound up to polylogarithmic factors. Both theoretical and empirical experimental results show the power of our proposed methods. We also consider how to design efficient and effective algorithms to exploit shared contextual features in MAB framework. We proposed two algorithms to improve the reliability of the exploration by constructing robust exploratory directions. Besides, we introduced a contextual MAB algorithm in the setting of high-dimensional contextual data. Moreover, we designed a feature generation method for arms, which can be used to generate contextual information for contextual multi-arm bandit algorithm. These models and papers are highly cited by other researchers and have been attracted interests from different research communities. The resulting algorithms and performance have expanded the current MAB research.

14208815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208815.value: One interesting direction is to investigate how to incorporate more complex user behaviors in social networks like collaboration or competition into multi-armed bandit algorithms for the online recommendation. In this project, we have proposed an algorithm to incorporate social connection in MAB framework for the online recommendation. But the social connections can be different types of relations such as collaboration and competition. Therefore, one future direction is to design algorithms to subtly handle different kinds of social connections with different methods. Another potential direction is to extend our almost optimal algorithms for linear stochastic bandits with heavy-tailed payoffs problem. Current algorithms require prior knowledge of the distributional moments, and the experiments are only conducted on synthetic datasets. Therefore, future directions in this line of research include automatic learning of our algorithms without information of distributional moments and evaluation of our proposed algorithms in real-world scenarios.

14208815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208815.value: The online recommendation is an important research problem as well as an essential practical problem, which help users discover new and relevant items like merchandises, music, and movies, making better user experience and simultaneously driving incremental revenue. Therefore, research and industry communities tend to explore more effective and efficient algorithms. In this project, we formulate the online recommendation as a multi-armed bandit problem. We proposed plenty of effective algorithms under different settings including contextual multi-armed bandit, best arm identification, and multi-armed bandit with heavy-tailed payoffs. We also designed several efficient and effective algorithms to exploit shared contextual feature in multi-armed bandit framework by improving the reliability of the exploration, handling high dimensional contextual data, and generating features of arms. Both theoretical analysis and empirical experimental results show the power of our proposed methods.

14209115.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14209115.value: 時延約束網絡信息流：刻画及时路由和编码容量域

14209115.label: Project Objectives
14209115.value: When only routing is allowed, we will develop a hop-expanded graph model to establish equivalence between delay-constrained communication on the original graph and delay-unconstrained communication over the expanded graph. This will allow us to leverage the rich tools and theories available for delay-unconstrained communication to significantly improve the understanding on timely routing capacity. When network coding is allowed, we will develop an algebraic approach built upon two instrumental ones for delay-unconstrained network coding communication and decoding delay of network coding. The approach will allow us to characterize the timely coding capacity for unicast and, if time permitted, multicast/broadcast. We will use results from objectives 1 and 2 to gauge the timely throughput gain of network coding over routing. For unicast, our preliminary result has shown the gain can be as large as 2. This is in contrast to its delay-unconstrained counterpart where coding has no throughput gain. A partial and, if time permitted, full characterization of the gain provide fundamental understanding on benefits of network coding in delay-constrained communication.

14209115.value: 目的：該項目旨在研究在時延約束網絡通信的關鍵問題：確定和實現（完全或近似）流與整個網絡硬盤的最後期限易腐信息的最大吞吐量。 項目背景：延遲約束是在網絡通信系統的設計中一個重要的問題。傳輸信息比特招致網絡延遲，而端至端延遲往往是一個關鍵的網絡通信體驗指標。例如，多媒體通信系統，例如，視頻會議，需要有界延遲上視頻傳輸。同樣，在網絡物理系統，時間關鍵型應用程序強加的等待時間約束要求在其中的數據和控制信息必須在一個有界的時延內到達其目標。 儘管延遲受限通信流量在最近幾年增長迅速，並預計於2013-2018年再提高3倍，下面的根本問題在很大程度上仍然違背解決： 如何確定和實現（精確地或大致）及時容量域，即，在該給定的源節點到目的節點在網絡中傳輸信息的最大速度，在受端至端延遲約束的前提下？ 這個問題有實際應用。例如，在視頻會議，系統設計師可能要最大限度地提高視頻吞吐量，在250ms的視頻延遲約束的前提下，以保證實時的會議體驗。 項目簡介：我們將開展全面研究及時通信容量域的問題，只有路由和網絡編碼允許的前提下。這裡，網絡編碼是指其中在網絡中的節點可以混合接收包並轉發編碼的技術。具體地講，我們的計劃是以下內容。 （i）當只有路由被允許，我們將開發一個新的圖形模型，讓我們不僅重現之前及時只允許路由時單播容量域的結果，而且還可以獲得新鮮的組播/廣播的結果。 （ii）當網絡編碼被允許，我們將開發一個代數模型，使我們能夠確定單播和組播/廣播及時的容量域。 （iii）我們將使用（i）和（ii）的結果以評估網絡的編碼在及時吞吐量方面的增益結果。我們的初步結果表明，相比於即使是單播路由優化網絡編碼能加倍及時吞吐量。與此形成鮮明對比的是延遲不受約束的情況下，這兩種最優路由和編碼實現相同的單播能力。 項目的意義：成功完成該項目將奠定必要的基礎上延遲受限的溝通進一步的調查，並指導實際的系統設計。

14209115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209115.value: Delay constraint is an important concern in the design of network communication systems. Information bits incur transmission delay when traversing links, and it is often critical to constrain the end-to-end delay in information delivery over the network. For example, multimedia communication systems, e.g., video conferencing, require bounded delay on video delivery. This project provides answers to the following open questions: How to characterize and achieve (exactly or approximately) the timely capacity, i.e., the maximum rate at which a given source node can stream perishable information across the network to its receiver nodes, subject to an end-to-end delay constraint? We have carried out a comprehensive study on the timely capacity problem, with routing only and with network coding allowed. Here, network coding refers to the paradigm in which nodes in the network can mix receiving packets and forward coded ones. One of the surprising results from our study shows that network coding can double the timely throughput as compared to optimal routing even for single unicast. This is in sharp contrast to the delay-unconstrained case where both optimal routing and coding achieve the same single-unicast capacity. Results from this project lay down necessary theoretical foundation for further investigation on delay-constrained network communication.
