14209515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209515.value: Digital content generated by people around the world is growing in an explosive rate. Cloud storage business, now hosting petabytes of data, is expected to have double-digit growth in the coming years. As the rate of decrease of bit error rate is much slower than the rate of increase of storage capacity, finding bad sectors or erroneous bits in a hard disk will become more common. The current redundant array of independent disk (RAID6) storage system dedicates two disks to store the parity-check bits, and is designed to tolerate the malfunctioning of any two disks in the system. There are two shortcomings in the employment of RAID6 in future storage systems. Firstly, protection against double disk erasures will soon be inadequate. In the case of solid state drive (SSD), the number of bit errors increases rapidly as the device ages. The risk of permanent loss of data is not negligible. Practitioners in storage technology have already advocated for triple-parity RAID. However, most of the storage codes in the literature are for double-error disk erasures. There are not so many constructions of storage code for three or more disk erasures. The first objective of this proposal is to design new coding schemes for multiple disk-erasures. Secondly, as the capacity of data disk increases, it will be more common to have partial disk failures instead of whole disk failures. This motivates a new kind of model of handling bit errors and sector errors in a hard disk. Indeed, two new classes of coding designs, called partially maximal-separable distance codes and sector-disk codes, were proposed by Plank and Blaum et al. The second objective of this proposal is to construct new coding schemes and devise efficient decoding method for correcting partial disk erasure. The findings of this project will make a fundamental contribution to future distributed storage systems. 在雲端存儲的應用中，以兩個奇偶磁盤為基礎的存儲系統會在不久的將來不敷應用。為了增加存儲系統的可靠性，本項目將建構有三或多於三個奇偶磁盤的編碼方案，以及快捷的除錯功能。其次，當數據磁盤的容量不斷增加，局部磁盤故障將會更為常見。本項目的第二個目標是建構可以同時有效地移除一個儲系統中的整個磁盤錯誤和部分磁盤錯誤的編碼方案。

14209515.label: Realisation of objectives
14209515.value: The main findings in this project are contained in two journal papers. An algebraic framework was developed for encoding and decoding data stored in disk arrays. The encoding and decoding methods can be implemented with low complexity, because only bit-wise shifts and XOR are required. Both of the two types of bit-wise operation are readily available in most computer microprocessors. We call this general methodology "BASIC code", which stands for Binary Addition and Shift Implementable Cyclic-convolutional code. The basic results for BASIC code is summarized in the paper "BASIC Codes: Low-Complexity Regenerating Codes for Distributed Storage Systems." In the second phase of the project, we apply the theory developed in the first phase to some encoding schemes that are used in practical storage systems. In particular, we consider the EVENODD and RDP encoding schemes, which are capable of tolerating multiple disk erasures. New algorithms for decoding and repairing are devised for EVENODD and RDP codes. The algorithms are implemented and the time complexity is compared with existing algorithms. We show that further saving in time is possible using our BASIC approach. The results in the second phase of the project is contained in the journal paper "A Unified Form of EVENODD and RDP Codes and Their Efficient Decoding," which was published in IEEE Trans. on Communication. The research outputs in the papers mentioned in the previous two paragraphs fulfill Objective 1 "Construct encoding schemes for disk arrays which can tolerate multiple disk erasures" and Objective 3 "Devise efficient decoding algorithm for the new encoding method". We address the problem of correcting partial disk errors in an equivalent form. In real-life system, data disks are often divided into groups and each group is put within a rack. This creates a hierarchical structure in the distributed data system. Usually, The speed of data transfer within a rack is much faster than that between two different racks. If we view a rack of hard disks as a "super disk", then the failure of a single hard disk in a rack corresponds to a partial disk error in the "super disk". We investigated the repair problem in this kind of distributed storage systems in the paper "Rack-Aware Regenerating Codes for Data Centers." Some theoretical bound on how well we can implement encoding and repair mechanism was obtained, and an explicit coding scheme was given in the paper. However, we do not have time to implement the encoding algorithms and study them thoroughly. Objective 2 and objective 4 are not completely achieved. The main reason for under-achievements is because of the lack of time. We only have some incipient results, which are mostly on the theoretical side and are subject to further development. We have some fundamental performance bound and preliminary encoding scheme for correcting partial disk errors. However, we do not have a full-fledged and fast decoding algorithm to be evaluated on a test bed. This is why the percentage of achievement for objectives 2 and 4 are only 80%.

14209515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209515.value: A theoretical framework in the paper "BASIC Codes: Low-Complexity Regenerating Codes for Distributed Storage Systems" (journal paper no. 2 in Part C). This framework serves a dual purpose. Firstly, we can build new regenerating codes with very low complexity that is amenable to practical implementation. Secondly, we use this framework to devise efficient decoding algorithms for existing data encoding schemes for disk arrays. The new decoding algorithms are faster than other encoding schemes available in the literature. Application to EVENODD and RDP encoding method can be found in the paper "A Unified Form of EVENODD and RDP Codes and Their Efficient Decoding." (Journal paper no. 3 in Section C) We also have some small result regarding another encoding scheme called the Blaum Bruck and Vardy scheme. This is a new MDS condition condition for this class of codes (Journal paper no. 1 in Section C) The first version of the paper "BASIC Codes: Low-Complexity Regenerating Codes for Distributed Storage Systems" was submitted before the start date of this project, and the initial work was done when the PI was working with the Institute of Network Coding in the Chinese University of Hong Kong, under an Area of Excellence scheme. However, there are significant revision and re-writing before the paper was finally accepted for publication. Part of the funding of this project was used in supporting the PhD student Hanxu HOU, in completing this paper. The research outcome reported in the paper "Rack-Aware Regenerating Codes for Data Centers" (Journal paper no. 1 in Section C) was produced after Hanxu HOU became a faculty member of a university of mainland China. The topic of this paper is directly related to Objective 2 in this project, and is a continuation of his PhD study in the Chinese University of Hong Kong. The conference paper "Storage codes and group representation" was an invited talk. There is no proceeding, and hence there is no acknowledgement to this GRF.

14209515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209515.value: In this project we exploited the bit-wise XOR in implemented regenerating codes and disk array codes. XOR corresponds to binary addition without carry. In all computer system, integer addition (with carry) is highly optimized. We may extend the idea in this project to arithmetic addition, namely, addition with carry. An extension of the theory developed in this project is to consider byte-wise shift and modulo-256 addition (assuming that a byte contains 8 bits), or word-wise shift and modulo-65536 addition (assuming that a word contains 16 bits). The algebraic foundation will be very different. Instead of finite field (Galois field), we need the theory of finite ring (Galois ring).

14209515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209515.value: One method of providing data integrity is to distributed and store the data in a disk arrays, so that part of the disk arrays stores the information bits, and the remaining part stores some redundant parity-check bits. The encoding method is designed so that it can tolerate a pre-defined number of disks failures. EVENODD and RDP are two popular data encoding schemes for disk arrays, and both of them can tolerate two or more disk failures. Due to the large amount of data in modern big-data applications, once a disk failure is detected, one would like to recover the data as quickly as possible. This research project gives efficient algorithm for decoding and repairing a failed disks in a distributed storage system, and thereby provides a building block for the infra-structure for cloud storage.

14300115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300115.value: Mild, catalytic cleavage of aliphatic carbon-carbon and carbon–oxygen bonds with water as the transfer hydrogenating agent will be attempted at low temperatures below 200 degree C to provide energy rich fuels and valuable chemicals from biomaterials and oxygenated wastes. The catalysis couples water splitting and carbon-carbon and/or carbon-oxygen bond cleavages to give hydrogen enriched organic products and energy rich compounds as well as value added chemicals. This proposal aims to provide a new method for biofuels and chemical intermediates in economically more attractive ways. 嘗試在低於攝氏200度及溫和條件下,以水氫化生物材料 和廢物中的脂族碳 - 碳和碳 - 氧化學鍵,以提供在經濟上更有吸引力的生物燃料和有價值的化學品。

14300115.label: Realisation of objectives
14300115.value: The stoichiometric carbon-oxygen cleavages of both strained and unstrained substrates have been investigated and found to be successfully using both rhodium and iridium porphyrin complexes. The alcohol substrates are particularly interesting since they serve as the alkylating agents even though the hydroxyl group is a very poor leaving group in alkaline conditions. The rhodium porphyrin catalyzed, regioselective hydrogenolysis of the carbon-carbon bonds of cyclopropanes with isopropanol have been accomplished to yield mainly the linear alkanes. A rhodium porphyrin radical catalyzed 1,2-rhodium hydride insertion into the carbon-carbon bond mechanism is established. The subsequent hydrogenolysis to the rhodium porphyrin alkyl intermediates goes through an alcoholysis process to form the alkanes and regenerate rhodium porphyrin hydride.

14300115.value: The inert carbon-oxygen and carbon-carbon bonds in organic compounds can be broken to give much more valuable metalloporphyin alkyls, analogues of vitamin B12. The catalytic hydrogenolysis of carbon-carbon bonds can potentially be used to break down high molecular weight compounds into lower ones usable as fuels and value-added chemicals.

14300815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300815.value: 中國青藏高原上多年凍土發育廣泛。在氣候及人為擾動下，高原多年凍土溫度升高、不斷退化。富冰多年凍土融化會在地表形成熱喀斯特（thermokarst）地貌。熱喀斯特在時間和空間的動態變化對水文條件、生態系統、地氣間碳交換、以及基礎設施產生巨大影響。但是針對青藏高原熱喀斯特地貌鮮有研究，仍然有許多未知。 該研究主要利用衛星合成孔徑干涉雷達技術觀測青藏高原三至五個典型熱喀斯特地貌在過去25年的動態形變及變化。另外，我們將實地觀測採集數據和搜集信息，用意檢驗校衛星遙感觀測結果。結合衛星和地表的數據，我們將調查熱喀斯特的觸發機制和控制因素，研究其地貌和氣候方面的影響和重要性。 該研究與當今針對青藏高原多年凍土退化的監測工作高度互補。將填補關於熱喀斯特引起地表變形的研究空白。從這項研究將為評估整個高原上多年凍土穩定性提供重要的數據和信息。

14300815.label: Realisation of objectives
14300815.value: I have completed all the proposed research tasks and realized all three objectives as per the original application. Objective 1: Quantify spatio-temporal changes of individual, non-lake thermokarst landforms using space-borne Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) measurements in the past 25 years. We have collected and analysed multi-sensor InSAR images for the following targets in the following four areas and quantified the spatial-temporal variability in surface elevation changes. (1) Thermo-erosion gullies in Eboling Mountain, Heihe River Upper Basin in northeast Tibet. Data processed: ALOS-1 PALSAR (2006-2011), Sentinel-1A/B (2015-2019), ALOS-2 (2014-2019); (2) Active rock glaciers in the northern Tien Shan of China. Data processed: ALOS-1 PALSAR (2006-2011); (3) Yedoma uplands on Sobo-Sise Island, Lena Delta, Russia. Data processed: Sentinel-1 A/B (2016-2017); (4) Unglaciated Arctic coast, Bayelva catchment, Spitsbergen, Svalbard. Data processed: ERS-2 (1995-2009), Sentinel-1 (2015-2018), and TerraSAR-X (2014-2019). Objective 2: Interpret and investigate key triggering mechanisms and driving factors of thermokarst dynamics at these landforms by combining InSAR and in situ data and information. The landforms we studied are diverse in their locations, topo-climatic conditions, and geomorphological processes, we carried our case-specific investigations of triggering mechanisms and driving factors behind the observed elevation changes. Specifically, (1) We have selected the thermo-erosion gullies in Eboling Mountain as intensive study targets and have used a variety of space-borne, air-borne, and ground-based measurements to investigate their spatial-temporal changes. The remote sensing data/methods include satellite InSAR as detailed above, historical air photos, satellite optical imagery and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV). The ground-based measurements include ground-based InSAR, GPS-RTK, ground penetrating radar and mechanic probing. Synthesizing these comprehensive measurements together, we found that the magnitude and location ground subsidence is controlled by three intertwined processes, including stream-driven thermo-erosion, thaw slumping and rapid melt of ground ice at local sinkholes. (2) We have compiled an inventory that includes 261 active rock glaciers in Tien Shan and quantitative information about their locations, geomorphic parameters, and downslope velocities. We also quantified the geomorphic (including altitude, area, length, shape, slope angle, and aspect angle) and climatic parameters (mean annual air temperature and potential income of solar radiation) of each active rock glacier. Based on these attributes and factors, we found that the latitude and longitude locations have a strong influence on the altitude distribution of the active rock glaciers. We also found distinct altitude distributions of active rock glaciers in the western and eastern parts of the study area divided by 86◦ E, which are due to the influence of distinct climates of these two subregions. (3) Over the Yedoma deposits in Lena Delta, we observed stronger seasonal thaw subsidence on elevated flat Yedoma uplands by comparing to the surrounding Yedoma slopes, which are caused by higher water/ice contents than in lower regions. We also found that delayed thawing associated with air temperature fluctuations affects inter-annual elevation changes. We also observed an uplift in the early season of 2017, which were caused by early summer heave. (4) Supported by field measurements, we inferred that our InSAR-observed surface subsidence is caused by permafrost degradation in Bayelsa, Svalbard. Our high-resolution results also pinpointed strong and sudden subsidence at buildings in Ny-Ålesund and the airport. Objective 3: Assess the feasibility of using InSAR to produce a catalogue of thermokarst landforms and their surface dynamics. Building upon our diverse case studies as summarized above, we assessed and found that InSAR data alone cannot be used to reliably identify thermokarst landforms. The fundamental limitation of InSAR is that reliable phase-based quantification of surface movement requires high coherence between multiple SAR acquisitions, which, however, decreases drastically in case of abrupt thaw subsidence due to thermokarst processes. On a positive note, since InSAR can reveal subtle and gradual subsidence in areas surrounding thermokarst landforms, by combining InSAR and optical imagery, one can identify active thermokarst landforms. In addition to this feasibility assessment of InSAR data, we also developed a deep-learning-based method that can automatically identify and delineate thermokarst landforms from optical imagery. Using this new method, we produced an inventory of thermokarst landforms in central Tibet.

14300815.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300815.value: The project has produced five research papers on InSAR studies of permafrost in Tibet and Arctic, two papers on deep-learning-based delineation of thermokarst landforms in Tibet, and two papers on innovative use of GPS reflected signals for quantifying surface elevation changes in permafrost areas. Please refer to Part C for detailed citation information and the full papers. Below I summarize our major findings as reported in the InSAR papers. Chen et al. (JGR, 2018) developed a permafrost-oriented developed persistent scatterer InSAR approach that incorporates a physics-based piecewise elevation change model. Applying this new algorithm to repeat ALOS-1 SAR acquisitions, we successfully measured gradual surface subsidence at a fine spatial resolution of about 7 m on Eboling Mountain in the northeastern region of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, where thermal erosion gullies are well developed. We found that the gradual permafrost thaw subsidence occurs both inside and around the thermal erosion gullies between 2006 and 2011. Our results revealed that 28% of the study area experiences permafrost thaw processes, which is about 40 times larger than the visible gullies. The spatial pattern of gradual subsidence trends showed correlations between the gullies and their surroundings, suggesting that the permafrost thaws and degrades in a wider region than the gullies. This work demonstrated the potentials of using persistent scatterer interferometry to study permafrost thaw processes and to assess its impacts over vast areas, especially with low vegetation and shallow snow cover. Chen et al. (Remote Sensing, 2018) successfully proved the capability of Sentinel-1 InSAR measurements for quantifying both permafrost thaw subsidence during one thaw season and the inter-annual elevation changes between two thaw seasons in Sobo-Sise Island, Lena River Delta. Compared with X-band InSAR in Yedoma uplands, the C-band Sentinel- 1 InSAR showed higher coherence, even for the interferograms between the years. We also found that the flat tops of Yedoma uplands exhibit the highest seasonal elevation changes. Benefiting from the Sentinel-1 InSAR measurements with short time intervals (12 days in this case), we found that delayed thawing associated with air temperature fluctuations affects inter-annual elevation changes. Wang et al. (The Cryosphere, 2017) proposed a new method that combines SAR interferometry and optical images from Google Earth to map active rock glaciers in the northern Tien Shan of China. We compiled an inventory that includes 261 rock glaciers and quantitative information about their locations, geomorphic parameters, and downslope velocities. Our inventory shows that most of the rock glaciers are moraine-derived and facing northeast. The downslope velocities of the rock glaciers vary significantly in space, with a maximum of about 114 cm/year and a mean of about 37 cm/year. This study provides an important dataset to improve mapping and modeling permafrost occurrence in vast western China.

14300815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300815.value: 1. Further development of multi-sensor investigations of thermokarst development. We have conducted more than 10 types of field-based, air-borne, and space-borne measurements of a few typical thermokarst landforms in Tibet. More work is needed to develop a framework to synthesize and integrate these multi-sensor investigations towards a comprehensive assessment of thermokarst activities and their hydro-ecological impacts. 2. Large-scale mapping of surface elevation changes over permafrost areas. Thanks to the open data policy of the Sentinel-1A/B missions and their regular acquisitions over Tibet, the multi-temporal InSAR technique is mature enough to generate seamless maps of surface elevation changes over large permafrost areas. The challenges would be to validate and interpret InSAR results based on point measurements, expert knowledge, and physical modeling. 3. Automatic delineation of thermokarst landforms. As it has become increasingly labor-intensive and time-consuming to manually identify thermokarst landforms from a large number of remote sensing images taken over decades and over large areas, it is desirable to deep learning to automatically extract these distance features from these big data. Building on our successful case studies (Huang et al., 2018 and 2020), we developed a research proposal and were funded by the RGC to pursue this direction.

14300815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300815.value: Permafrost on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and in the Arctic is thawing rapidly as the climate is warming. Our study focuses on the dramatic, surficial indicators of permafrost degradation, namely thermokarst landforms. Using radar images taken repeatedly from spacecrafts, we are able to remotely measure ground subsidence at unprecedented fine details and accuracies in various thermokarst-affected areas. Our observations reveal that both rapid and graduate thaw subsidence can occur around thermokarst landforms. And our detailed investigations pinpoint the important roles of topo-climatic conditions and ground ice content on the formation and degradation of these landforms. Our studies offer an innovative and unique perspective to advance our understanding of near-surface permafrost dynamics and help to assess permafrost stability in remote and cold regions.

14301015.label: Project Objectives
14301015.value: The solutions of mean field game and mean field type control problems naturally associate with a system of fully coupled Mean Field Type Forward Backward Stochastic Differential Equations (MFT-FBSDEs). We propose to study the well-posedness a wide class of MFT-FBSDEs by its own right. Based on our preliminary calculation, the MFT-FBSDEs induced by a general linear quadratic mean field type control problem satisfied certain monotonicity conditions, and the system always admits a unique solution as shown in our previous work Bensoussan et al.[8]. It is recalled that monotonicity conditions are traditionally critical in establishing the unique existence of classical FBSDEs through the method of continuation first developed by Hu and Peng [19]. It is expected that by enhancing this method subject to a variety of specially designed monotonicity conditions, the unique existence of solution of MFT-FBSDEs could be ensured. We purposely develop a general theory of Mean Field Stackelberg game (MFSG). To be precise, we consider a mean field game in which there is a dominating player (leader) and a large group of inhomogeneous small agents (followers) indexed by a random variable $Delta$, which represents his magnitudes of delay in grasping information from the dominating player; the actual realization of $Delta$ of an individual is only known by himself but not others. We propose to study this game from a rudimentary level on, by first showing that the finite N-player empirical system will converge to the limiting mean field system provided that a non-trivial fixed point property is satisfied; the latter system is highly non-trivial and apparently absent in the existing literature. For MFSG, the optimal control obtained through the stochastic maximum principle for a small agent likely adapts to a non-Brownian filtration, and hence the classical martingale representation theorem fails to be applicable. Nevertheless, the approach is still workable if one readily replaces the Brownian martingale by a general indeterminate martingale, in light of the backward dynamics mentioned in Objective 1. We propose to first consider the problem under LQ setting, as the unique existence of the mean field equilibrium reduces to the solvability of a non-symmetric Riccati equation as argued in Bensoussan et al.[8]. Secondly, for the general setting, in which the coefficient functions are heterogeneous and the model may involve the mean field density function, we aim to derive its master equation (see Bensoussal et al.[7]). We shall elucidate the universal approach of using mean field type theory on resolving portfolio selection problem especially under non-canonical settings. The objective functional of interest is the difference of a convex risk function from the utility functional of the terminal wealth. This new objective functional covers various classical cases in the literature, for example, mean-variance, mean-risk and mean-downside-risk portfolio selection; and it also covers the lasting problem of utility-risk portfolio selection. We anticipate that the optimal terminal wealth is necessary and sufficient to satisfy a static Nonlinear Moment Problem (NMP) represented by a system of non-linear equations, whose solution can be established by hard analysis argument. Numerical approximations of these optimal portfolio selections will also be carried out by considering the same problems but under discrete approximations for the underlying processes as the corresponding NMPs should be explicitly solvable.

14301015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301015.value: 如何模擬動力系統中的群體行為是人類歷史中的一個重要問題，例如：物理學中的相互作用粒子系統，動物的群體行為，經濟學中的集體戰略行為。另外，頻繁的經融危機警示我們不僅要研究獲得豐厚利潤策略，還要理解投資者的集體動態行為。隨機微分博弈是處理這類問題的傳統方法，它對單個體的行為進行直接描述，但缺點是耗費大量的計算成本，以及數學上很難處理。為了解決上述問題，人們藉鑑統計物理學裡的宏觀描述方法，並逐漸發展形成了平均場理論。具體地來說，不同於強調個體間相互作用的傳統方法，平均場理中每個個體都受到一個共同群體量的影響，這個群體量被稱為平均場。當參與者總量趨於無窮時，隨機微分博弈和平均場理論的結合將很大程度上簡化原本問題，最終形成平均場博弈和平均場控制問題，參閱Bensoussan et al. [6]. 當總體數量趨於無窮時，平均場通常是關於總體概率分佈的泛函。雖然平均場博弈有很多有趣的應用，但是目前的文獻缺少一種統一的方法能在廣義的框架中處理這類問題，也沒能和一些現代的博弈論問題形成聯繫，例如Stackelberg博弈；此外我們缺少把平均場理論應用在傳統控制問題的文獻。該項目的目標是沿著這些方向推廣平均場理論。 本項目中，我們首先考慮平均場型正倒向隨機微分方程的解的唯一存在性問題。平均場型正倒向隨機微分方程也被稱為McKean Vlasov型正倒向隨機微分方程，該方程組的係數不僅依賴於解本身還依賴於解的概率分佈；通過運用隨機極大值原理，許多平均場隨機博弈、控制問題都對應為平均場型正倒向隨機微分方程。除了方程係數的李普希茨條件，我們計劃提出幾種不同但相互權衡的單調性條件，保證了平均場型正倒向隨機微分方程解的適定性。我們希望推廣Hu & Peng [19] 中的方法用於處理這個問題。此外，我們計劃把該結果推廣到倒向動力系統，以及運用數值積分和傅里葉-餘弦結合的方法對該問題進行數值逼近研究。 最初的平均場問題僅僅包含同類行為個體，我們將考慮一類更廣泛的平均場博弈問題。該問題中存在一個主導個體和異類行為的參與群體，主導個體能通過改變自身的控制策略來影響平均場，進而影響整個群體；這類似於統治者能夠有權去製定一些讓民眾服從的製度。另外，參與群體間的互異行為是因為主導個體的信息對他們有不同程度的延遲。我們的工作是把Stackelberg [45]中的Stackelberg博弈理念推廣到平均場的框架中。項目的第二部分會詳盡地分析對這類平均場博弈問題。我們希望能夠建立大量的數學工具，例如：任意的過濾概率空間中平均場正倒向隨機微分方程的適定性，以及倒向動力系統在無窮維空間的推廣。 在項目的最後部分，我們的目標是建立平均場型控制理論和資產選擇之間的重要聯繫，特別是在非標準的框架下。一方面，我們希望能夠得到一種統一的方法；另一方面，我們計劃能解決效用-下行風險、失望理論中長期懸而未決的投資選擇問題。 整個研究過程涉及如下課題：隨機分析，偏微分方程，以及平均場理論。我們的預期結果（1）能完全地解決平均場理論和投資選擇中一些重要問題，（2）能顯著地推廣現存的博弈理論，並且拓展平均場理論的應用，（3）建立自成體系的工具和有效的數值逼近方法用於處理平均場型正倒向隨機微分方程。

14301015.label: Realisation of objectives
14301015.value: For Revised Objective 1: The objective is accomplished with more extensions stated as below. a) In [10], we provide a conceptual study on a control problem in a Hilbert space of random variables. Following P.L. Lions, we introduced the Hilbert space of square-integrable random variables as a natural space on which the Master equation arisen from Mean Field theory could be treated effectively via the forward-backward equations, and we also develop the techniques to deal with the latter through a way by combining with some effort developed in our former work "Well-posedness of mean field type forward-backward stochastic differential equations, SPA 125, (2015)". Further general methodology of dealing with some generic MFTFBSDE has been developed in [2]. b) Using the methodology developed in [2,10], we further extend the method to resolve for the solution of a stochastic variational inequality that models an elasto-plastic oscillator excited by a filtered noise in [2]. c) The same methodology as in [2,10] was rephrased in that in discrete setting, and then provided the first systemic study on discrete time partially observable mean field systems in the presence of a common noise in [3]. Both the mean field games and the associated mean field type stochastic control problem are studied. We first solve the mean field type control problem using the classical discrete time Kalman filter with notable modifications. The unique existence of the resulting forward backward stochastic difference system is then established by Separation Principle. For Revised Objective 2: The objective is accomplished, and all results are now published. In [2], we consider a linear-quadratic mean field game between a leader (dominating player) and among a group of followers (agents) under the Stackelberg game setting, so that the evolution of each individual follower is now also subjected to delay effects from both their state and control variables, as well as those of the leader. By invoking a noncanonical fixed point property, we show that for a general class of finite N-player games, each of them converges to the mean field counterpart which may possess an optimal solution that can serve as an epsilon-Nash equilibrium for the corresponding finite N-player game. The overall Stackelberg game is solved by tackling three sub-problems hierarchically. Their resolutions correspond to the establishment of the unique existence of the solutions of three different forward-backward stochastic functional differential equations, with which we manage them by applying the unified continuation method. In particular, by first regarding the mean field term and the delay influence of the leader as exogenous, we use the adjoint equation approach to solve for the optimal control of each follower. Next, we utilize the fixed point property to get the desired mean field equilibrium, with which we propose a time independent sufficient condition that warrants its unique existence. Finally, we solve for the optimal control of the leader and conclude that its presence would not interfere the original existence of the equilibrium of the community. Our present setting induces much different challenge than that in the former work, "Mean Field Stackelberg Games: Aggregation of Delayed Instructions, SICON, 53(4), 2015”, which stems from the delay effects from each follower’s state and control, which result in a more complicated system of infinite dimensional forward-backward stochastic functional differential equations. While to solve for the optimal control of the leader, we develop a thorough understanding of a special linear operator resulting from the delay effects of the leader’s control on the dynamics of each follower, which hinges to the invertibility of another certain functional operator, which has been not considered in any existing literature. For Revised Objective 3: The work as proposed in the present objective is now complete and all related results have been published in top-tier journals in the field and in a book chapter. a) For tackling the related general mean field problem via the use of non-symmetric Riccati equations, the whole programme was laid down in my works of [2, 3, 9]. b) For the construction of general master equations and developing the general methodology, I get it furnished in my works of [6,8,11]. For Revised Objective 4: The work as proposed in the present objective is now accomplished, and most relevant works appeared in top-tier journals in the field. a) In [4], we provide a comprehensive study of the utility-deviation-risk portfolio selection problem. By considering the first-order condition for the corresponding objective function, we first derive the necessary condition that the optimal terminal wealth satisfying two mild regularity conditions solves for a primitive static problem, called Nonlinear Moment Problem. We then illustrate the application of this general necessity result by revisiting the nonexistence of the optimal solution for the mean-semivariance problem. Secondly, we establish an alternative version of the verification theorem serving as the sufficient condition that the solution, which satisfies another mild condition different from that for necessity, of the Nonlinear Moment Problem is the optimal terminal wealth of the original utility-deviation risk portfolio selection problem. We then apply this general sufficiency result to revisit the various well-posed mean-risk problems already known in the literature, and to also establish the existence of the optimal solutions for both utility-downside-risk and utility-strictly convex-risk problems under the assumption that the underlying utility satisfies the Inada Condition. To the best of our knowledge, the positive answers to the latter two problems have long been absent in the literature. In particular, the existence result in the utility-downside risk problem is in contrast to the well-known non-existence of an optimal solution for the mean-downside-risk problem. As a corollary, the existence result in utility-semivariance problem allows us to utilize the semivariance as a proper risk measure in the classical portfolio management paradigm. b) The techniques developed lead us to discover a paradox in the related problem in time inconsistency framework (see [5]), which has been overlooked by the mainstream researchers. c) Finally, the numerical approximations of these optimal portfolio selections have been studied in [7], which is now under review. In particular, we establish the robustness of the optimal solutions for utility-deviation-risk portfolio selection to the changes in the underlying market model. We first consider a generalized market framework for two types utility-deviation-risk problem, namely utility-downside-risk and utility-strictly-convex-risk. Under our generalized market framework, the dynamics of the asset prices can be unspecified, and both the continuous-time Black- Scholes model and the discrete binomial tree model for asset prices can be covered. Under the assumption of complete market, we establish the existence of the optimal solutions for utility-deviation-risk problems under the generalized setting. As a main result, we establish the continuity of the optimal terminal wealth in terminal pricing kernel of the underlying marker model under the weak topology, thus the optimal solution is stable to the changes in market model via the pricing kernel. A subtle application of this robustness result is to provide a numerical algorithm to compute the optimal solution for utility-deviation-risk portfolio selection, which has been absent for the general models in the literature. In particular, the solutions in the binomial tree models can converge to the solution in the continuous- time Black-Scholes model, hence the solution in the continuous-time Black-Scholes model can be computed by approximation. 3 PhD students was trained over the course; particularly, Dr Ying Ying Lai worked under my guidance as an undergraduate before official commencement of PhD study.

14301015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301015.value: Successful accomplishment of all the objectives in our project relies on notable advancements, made by us over the course of study, on the following disciplines: stochastic analysis, partial differential equations and mean field theory. We shall continue to work on some newly formulated problems originated from our own study. In particular, being germinated from this project, my work in mean field games and mean field control theory is now well praised by different scholars in the globe while these recent research outputs of mine also granted me an honorable respect in the community through the award of being a visiting professor of Columbia University in the City of New York. Another GRF research grant, purely based on further study on some common mathematical structures often encountered in mean field theory, has been recently awarded to me in the 2016/17 exercise, which will facilitate to deepen my research in the area. A new research proposal, for GRF grant application, based on mean field theory will be developed in the near future.

14301015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301015.value: Theory of Mean Field Games is to study the collective transient behavior of a continuum of players so that each of them accomplishes his own decision-making by also considering the accumulative effect of marginal impacts from all other players; the problems involved cannot be treated by the standard stochastic control method, and one needs to develop some novel approaches. Through completing this project, we have made a significant advance in mean field theory, which will bring lasting impacts on stochastic analysis, partial differential equations, and economic modeling. Particularly, our work fills a gap in the literature by enriching the study on the well-posedness a wide class of MFT-FBSDEs. Besides, we also obtained the convergence of the finite N-player empirical system to the limiting mean field system under a very general framework, which motivates the relevant numerical scheme. Finally, by using mean field theory, we resolved and developed a numerical approximation scheme for a class of non-conventional portfolio selection problems, including those with an objective functional being the difference of a convex risk function from the mean of terminal wealth; this class covers various classical cases in the literature, for example, mean-variance, mean-risk and mean-downside-risk portfolio selection. Moreover, our obtained result actually resolved some lasting problems in insurance and finance.

14301115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301115.value: The Atlantic meridional overturning circulation (AMOC) has become a major research focus owing to its significant role in the global climate. A central open question in the study of AMOC is how the deepwater goes through the stratified ocean interior and returns to surface. Although there is growing evidence indicating that internal wave breaking is a principal energy source to drive most of the abyssal mixing, but how internal waves break and transfer energy to small dissipative scales is still unclear and poorly quantified so far. Most importantly, how internal wave induced mixing will affect the distribution and transport ability of the overturning circulation in a global context is still unresolved, the answer of which is crucial for climate modeling and prediction. The proposed project aims to investigate the internal wave breaking mechanism and its effects on the flow dynamics and transport properties in horizontal convection in a laboratory experiment that serves as a conceptual model for the AMOC. In the first phase of the project we will investigate internal wave breaking process over topographies with features commonly observed in the deep ocean, in contrast to previous studies that mostly address continental shelf/slope topography. By using particle image velocimetry (PIV) and particle tracking velocimetry (PTV) techniques, we will be able to measure both large-scale dynamics and small-scale turbulent mixing quantitatively with high accuracy, which is one important advantage of the present project compared with previous experiments. In the second phase of the project we will systematically measure the influences of internal waves on stratification, vertical mixing, heat transport efficiency and overturning rate in horizontal convection, which, to the best of our knowledge, will be the first experimental work on this issue. The outcomes of this study will complement field and numerical investigations, and will enrich our existing knowledge of the internal wave breaking mechanism and shed light on the role of abyssal mixing in the AMOC. 大洋環流作為地球氣候系統的一個重要組成部分，對全球氣候變化起到了極為關鍵的作用。因此，大洋環流已成為近年來物理海洋和氣候變化等領域的一個研究熱點。在關於大洋環流的研究中，一個尚未定論的核心問題是：在極地區域下沉到深海中的冷水，是如何獲得能量從而在有密度分層的海洋內部不斷上升並返回海表面的？雖然有越來越多的研究表明海洋中的重力內波提供了大部分所需的能量，但內波如何破碎並將能量傳遞到小尺度（即湍流混合）這一過程並不清楚。更為重要的是，內波破碎所引起的湍流混合會對大洋環流帶來怎樣的影響仍然沒有答案，而這對建立有效的全球氣候模型起著至關重要的作用。 本課題旨在研究內波破碎機制及其對水平對流（一個簡單的大洋環流概念性模型）的動力學特性的影響。我們將首先研究在有複雜地形下的內波破碎過程。通過使用粒子成像測速技術和粒子跟蹤測速技術進行高精度的測量，我們將分別從大尺度動力學和小尺度湍流混合兩個角度去理解探討內波的破碎機制。在本課題的第二階段，我們將系統地研究內波破碎對水平對流系統中的密度分層、垂直混合率、流動強度和傳熱效率等性質的影響。本課題的研究成果將有助於豐富我們對內波破碎機制的認識，並揭示其所引起的湍流混合在大洋環流中的作用。

14301115.label: Realisation of objectives
14301115.value: We have made laboratory experiments to study internal gravity wave generated in a stably thermal stratified fluid layer. All three objectives of the project have been realized. In the first part, we studied the properties of internal wave field at different forcing parameters, i.e., forcing amplitude and forcing frequency. The responses of the flow to the internal wave are measured by the particle image velocimetry (PIV) technique. In the second part, we investigated the breaking process when internal wave is reflected by a continental slope. The wave properties and the influence of internal wave breaking to the flow field generated by horizontal convection are measured by PIV and quantitative analyses are made. In the third part, we produced internal wave beams in a horizontal convection system by periodically disturbing the fluid beneath the hot plate. We measured the changes in the dissipation rate and kinetic energy of the flow field. we also how the heat transport efficiency responds to the internal wave field.

14301115.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301115.value: In the first part of the project, we found that, in all cases, the propagation direction of internal wave is well predicted by the dispersion relation, and the structure of wave beam could be well described by the linear viscous theory. Based on power spectrum analysis, we show that, the nonlinear effect become prominent when the forcing frequency is less than half of the buoyancy frequency, and the nonlinear effect enhances when the forcing amplitude increases. With respect to the second part of the project, we observed an intense boundary flow in the case of critical reflection, the structure of which is found to be analogous to that induced by tide-topography interaction. In the case of subcritical refection, we measured and analyzed the relationship between off-criticality and energy dissipation efficiency. Our results show that, the dissipation efficiency increases monotonically as the off-criticality decreases, and, the dissipation efficiency has no significant dependence on the amplitude of incident wave. During the process of reflection, a near-slope mean flow could be identified, showing strong nonlinearity here, which is further verified by the spectrum analysis. In the third part of the project, our results show that, even though the generated internal wave significantly enhance the dissipation rate and kinetic energy below the hot plate, it has no impact on the strength and the structure of the large-scale flow and the efficiency of heat transport. Presently, we are making detailed analysis of the experimental results and preparing for manuscripts to be submitted to the top journals in the field.

14301115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301115.value: The findings of the present project will be useful in the study of how internal waves influence mixing in the ocean. And we plan to make further and new studies of the influence of internal waves in the presence of surface wind forcing on ocean circulation, via the laboratory model of horizontal convection.

14301115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301115.value: The Atlantic meridional overturning circulation (AMOC) has become a major research focus owing to its significant role in the global climate. A central open question in the study of AMOC is how the deepwater goes through the stratified ocean interior and returns to surface. Although there is growing evidence indicating that internal wave breaking is a principal energy source to drive most of the abyssal mixing, but how internal waves break and transfer energy to small dissipative scales is still unclear and poorly quantified so far. The findings of this project show that internal waves significantly enhance the dissipation rate and kinetic energy in a laboratory model of the ocean circulation --- the horizontal convection, but its impact on the strength and the structure of the large-scale flows, and also on the efficiency of heat transport are insignificant. The outcomes of this study has enriched our existing knowledge of internal waves and their influence on the horizontal convection. This in turn sheds light on the mixing processes of the AMOC.

14301215.value: Dehn手术和有限型不变量问题

14301215.label: Project Objectives
14301215.value: Attain a better understanding of knots and three-manifold invariants and Dehn surgery. Address a few open questions in the field to help achieve this goal. 14301215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301215.value: This project studies three-dimensional topology with emphasis on Dehn surgery. Aiming at a better understanding of Dehn surgery, we address several open problems in the field, including but not limited to the cosmetic surgery conjecture, the cabling conjecture and various classification problems in Seifert fibered surgery. Invariants of knots and three-manifolds are to be studied and applied, particularly on how they behave under Dehn surgery. For this purpose, knot surgery formula of Heegaard Floer homology has proven to be a powerful machinery. We develop techniques to simplify computations involving link surgery formula in concrete examples. In addition, we study finite type invariants. We investigate the extent to which the finite type invariants distinguish knots. In order to achieve this goal, we look for relationships between finite type invariants and knot homology. We then propose a method for categorifying finite type invariants. 此课题研究三维拓扑并着重于其中的Dehn手术方向。 为更好理解Dehn手术理论，我们讨论若干此领域的几个仍未解决的问题，其中包括“整容手术猜想”，“缆结猜想“，以及Seifert丛手术的分类问题。 我们将研究扭结和三维流形不变量的性质，特别是它们在Dehn手术下的变化特性。其中一个非常有用的不变量来自于Heegaard Floer上同调。我们希望发展一套技巧使在某些特定情况下来简化此不变量的计算公式。 我们还将讨论有限型不变量，看它们在多大程度上可以区分不同扭结。为此我们会寻找有限型不变量同扭结上同调的关系，并提出一个范畴化有限型不变量的方案。

14301215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301215.value: Mathematically, the universe that we live can be modeled by a 3-manifold. Dehn surgery on a knot can be viewed as an operation to make a new 3-manifold from a given one. In Layman's language, our results in cosmetic surgery basically claim that the shapes of the new space obtained are all different. This may be viewed as a fundamental unique property of Dehn surgeries. In addition, the PI is so glad that his first Phd student Ran Tao was able to contribute to the project and wrote 2 high-quality paper in the area. Mr. Tao has joined the math department in Sichuan Normal University in 2018 and I am sure he will make further contribution in the new place.

14301315.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14301315.value: 液晶材料在太赫茲器件中的應用

14301315.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14301315.value: Prof Chigrinov, Vladimir Prof Tsang, Hon Ki

14301315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301315.value: The aim of this project is to determine the most suitable liquid crystal (LC) materials for use in terahertz devices. To achieve this goal, we will conduct the first systematic study of the THz terahertz properties of molecular series of LCs. LCs are indispensable materials for the manipulation of light at optical frequencies and have the potential to be similarly useful at terahertz frequencies, however they are seldom used in devices at THz terahertz frequencies due to difficulties in finding LCs with suitable properties in the THz terahertz range such as high birefringence, low absorption and fast reorientation. The most commonly used LCs at optical frequencies are not necessarily good choices for THz terahertz LC devices. LCs exhibit the behaviours of both ordered crystalline materials and disordered liquids i.e. they have some amount of orientational or positional order. Different degrees of order are known as mesophases and LCs have numerous mesophases that are accessed by changing the temperature. The rod-like molecules have the property of dielectric and optical anisotropy, allowing the orientation of the molecules to be controlled by external electric fields, producing LC devices that can control propagation of light, including polarisers, waveplates, and phase modulators. Many LCs have anisotropy at terahertz frequencies, having different refractive indices and absorption coefficients for the ordinary and extraordinary axes. The causes for the anisotropy at terahertz frequency are not fully understood; absorption differences are often attributed to the tails of Poley absorption modes found at higher frequencies, but recent research has shown that vibrational modes alone cannot describe the observed terahertz absorption. This project will conduct the first systematic study to probe the physical origins of the various contributions to the dielectric properties of LCs in the terahertz region. These contributions will likely include both Debye-like relaxational modes and vibrational modes. We will choose series of related LC materials, with a number of mesophases. Precise temperature control of the LC materials will allow us to carefully monitor these contributions with temperature, and in particular to see whether the strength of these contributions is related to mesophase. Molecular Dynamics simulations will be leveraged to help analyse the measurements. This research has applications in future terahertz LC devices: understanding how the various absorption mechanisms alter with mesophase will give insight into the role of order in terahertz optical properties of materials, and this in turn will allow LC materials to be optimised for terahertz LC devices. 本研究課題的主要目的是尋找最適合應用于太赫茲器件中的液晶材料。為達成這一目標，我們將首次系統的研究不同分子類型的液晶材料在太赫茲波段的特性。 對於調製可見光，液晶是一種必不可少的材料。同樣，液晶材料在太赫茲波段也有相似的應用前景。然而，液晶材料在太赫茲器件中卻很少被使用，原因在於很難找到一種在太赫茲波段有合適特性的液晶材料，例如：明顯的雙折射效應，低吸收率，快速的分子轉動等。在可見光波段常用的液晶材料並不一定適合太赫茲器件。 液晶材料同時具備晶體材料分子有序排列和液體材料分子無序排列的特性，也就是說液晶材料是部分有序的。不完全的部分有序排列被稱為中間晶相，通過環境溫度的改變液晶分子可以表現出許多種不同的中間晶相。液晶材料的棒狀分子有介質和光學各項異性的特點，外加電場可以控制液晶分子的各向排列， 從而使液晶器件能夠控制光在其中的通過，由此特性可以製成光學偏振器，波片和相位調製器。許多液晶材料在太赫茲波段同樣具有各項異性的特點，在沿光軸和垂直光軸的方向有不同的折射率和吸收常數。引起液晶分子在太赫茲波段各向異性的原因目前尚不清楚；不同軸向吸收率的不同以前通常認為是由於Poley吸收模式在高頻波段的作用，但是最近的研究顯示，僅有分子震動的吸收並不能完全解釋觀測到的液晶材料在太赫茲波段的吸收。 本研究課題將首次系統的研究影響液晶材料在太赫茲波段介質特性的各種因素以及背後的物理學原理。這些因素包括：Debye-like 弛豫模式和振蕩模式。我們將選擇一系列相關的液晶材料，以及每種材料的多種不同晶相。通過精確的溫度控制，我們能夠仔細的觀察各種影響因素和溫度之間的關係，特別是研究各種因素和液晶中間晶相形成之間的關係。分子動力學仿真將用於幫助分析觀測結果。 這一研究將在未來的太赫茲器件中有應用前景：通過了解液晶材料的晶相變化對其吸收特性的影響，能夠幫助我們深入到分子層面去了解分子排列的有序性對液晶材料在太赫茲波段特性的影響，反過來這又將指導液晶材料的優化，使其更加適合應用于太赫茲器件。

14301515.label: Project Objectives
14301515.value: To construct wave patterns, in particular the rarefaction wave, of the two-fluid Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system with slab symmetry, show the time-asymptotic stability of non-trivial profiles for the Cauchy problem in perturbation framework, and generalize it to the case with the Lorentz force satisfying the Maxwell system. The situation in which we are interested is that the potential function of the electric field is non-constant in large time. The analysis is to be made for the whole range of intermolecular interactions. Special attentions are paid to the effect of distinct masses of a binary gas mixture on the large time behavior. To extend the result to the more physical Landau collision operator for plasma consisting of electrons and ions, particularly focusing on the classical Coulomb interaction.

14301515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301515.value: The project will study collisional kinetic equations with a self-consistent electric field, describing the time evolution of charged ions and electrons in plasma, with special attentions to the dynamical stability of some existing non-trivial profiles. The main goal is to establish the large time asymptotic stability of profiles, in particular the rarefaction wave, for the Cauchy problem on the two-fluid Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system in the whole space with slab symmetry. The study will be focused on the situation where the potential function of the electric field is non-trivial in large time, specifically connecting two distinct constant states at both far fields. We will also take into account the effect on the mathematical analysis from both different masses of two types of particles and different collision operators with general intermolecular interactions, particularly for the classical Landau operator with the Coulomb potential. Boltzmann equation is a fundamental model in the collisional kinetic theory. Due to Boltzmann's H-theorem, an important issue is concerned with the convergence of solutions tending to equilibrium states. Basing on the energy method, the perturbation theory around constant equilibrium states even for the more complex Boltzmann equation with self-consistent electromagnetic fields has recently attracted lots of attentions. On the other hand, it is more important both mathematically and physically to study the stability of non-constant equilibrium states which generally exist under appropriate boundary conditions. Regarding wave patterns, a number of works have been done for the pure Boltzmann equation, but few are known in the appearance of self-consistent forces. In the project we will try to further develop new qualitative and quantitative estimates on solutions in such situation. We also expect the current project to provide some elementary understanding of the two-fluid system structure in the stability study of other kinds of non-trivial profiles besides the rarefaction wave. 本项目将研究带自洽电场的碰撞型动力学方程，这类方程描述的是等离子体中带电的离子和电子随着时间的发展，我们特别关注一些存在的非平凡解的动力稳定性，主要的目标是研究双极Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann系统的柯西问题解的大时间行为。在此研究中，电势函数被假定连接两个不同的常状态，所以它是非平凡的。同时，我们将考虑由于不同的粒子质量以及不同类型的分子间相互作用方式对问题的数学分析产生的影响，特别考虑相应于库伦力的朗道碰撞算子的情况。 在碰撞型动力学理论中，玻尔兹曼方程是一个基本的模型。由于玻尔兹曼的熵定理，一个重要的问题是解趋于平衡态的收敛性。基于能量的方法，即使对于更复杂的带自洽电磁场的玻尔兹曼方程，常平衡态附近的扰动理论已经吸引了很多人的关注。另一方面，研究在适当的边界条件下存在的非常平衡态的稳定性在数学和物理上亦更加重要。虽然对经典的玻尔兹曼方程在不同波的模式附近的稳定性研究已经有相当多的结果，但是在带自洽力的情形认识甚少。本项目中，我们将进一步发展在此种情形下解的定性和定量的估计。 我们期望该项目也可以对具有双极系统结构的除稀疏波以外其它类型的非平凡解的稳定性研究提供一些基本的理解。

14301515.label: Realisation of objectives
14301515.value: Objective 1: We have established the convergence of the two-component VPB system to the quasi-neutral Euler system in the setting of rarefaction waves for well-prepared small and smooth initial data. Thus, the long-term dynamics of the VPB system can be a non-trivial time-asymptotic profile connecting two distinct constant equilibrium states. It should be emphasized that disparate masses and charges of particles also enter into the asymptotic profile and hence they can affect the nontrivial large time behavior of solutions. The obtained result may be regarded as a generalisation of the existing perturbation theory for the VPB system in the cases either for initial data around constant equilibrium states or for the single-component Boltzmann collision. More importantly, although we may only provide a preliminary understanding of the stability of the rarefaction wave profile for the VPB system, it is expected that the analysis developed could be adopted to treat many other relevant problems in connection with those fluid-type systems derived from the kinetic equations. The proof of the main result is based on introducing a new two-component decomposition in order to treat the disparate masses. First of all, H-theorem of the two-component Boltzmann equations implies that the large-time behavior of the VPB system should be in connection with a bi-Maxwellian determined by six local fluid quantities. This motivates us to define the local equilibrium state such that it has the same fluid quantities as the unknown two-component distribution function with respect to all six two-component collision invariants. Therefore, the energy dissipation of the non-fluid part can be obtained by the linearised H-theorem. Moreover, it can not be direct to make the zero-order energy estimate on the kinetic component due to its lower time-decay property. To treat this trouble, we construct a background non-fluid function in terms of the time-asymptotic fluid profile such that the subtraction is integrable in time. The a priori estimates on the fluid part of the two-component solution is much more technical. The key point is to find out the appropriate viscous fluid-type equations of the macroscopic quantities of the bi-Maxwellian such that the energy estimates on the fluid part can be controlled in terms of the non-fluid part in a suitable way. Starting from the two-component moment equations with respect to all collision invariants, we use the original two-component macro-micro decomposition and directly obtain the two-fluid Euler-Poisson type system. To capture the diffusion and heat-conductivity, we further make use of the dissipation effect of like-particle collisions to obtain the two-fluid Navier-Stokes-Poisson type system, because the unlike-particle collisions essentially produce the microscopic corrections. The obtained two-fluid systems are crucial for making the energy estimates on the fluid part. It is also of its independent interest to study the large time behavior of those two-fluid systems in the context of existence and dynamical stability of wave patterns. Besides the stability study of rarefaction wave profiles for the VPB system, we also have explored the following related problems or possible extensions: 1) Since the small perturbation result around rarefaction wave profiles has been established, we expect to extend it to the case of a class of possibly large-amplitude initial data. Note that the similar results are already known for the corresponding fluid dynamic systems, in particular, the Navier-Stokes equations or the Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations. As the first step, we have studied the case when the strength of rarefaction waves is reduced to zero, namely, the background profile is constant. In such case, we have proved the large time stability of the Boltzmann equation for initial data allowed to have large amplitude. The extension to the VPB system can be obtained in a similar functional framework. 2) The energy estimates are essentially based on the analysis of dissipative structure of the complex two-component fluid dynamic equations. In this direction, we also have carried out an independent research in a general way on decay properties with regularity-loss for a class of symmetric hyperbolic systems with non-symmetric relaxations. The relative work may be helpful to treat the coupling kinetic systems that admits more complex dissipative structure than the two-species VPB system, for instance, the VMB system. 3) Since we are concerned with stability of wave patterns for the VPB system with self-consistent forces, it may be also asked what happens to shock waves in addition to rarefaction waves. However, it has been an outstanding open problem to construct the shock wave of the VPB system. As an early step to understand the problem, we have studied the existence, structure in connection with the KdV-Burgers shock wave and dynamical stability of the shock wave profile for the Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations as the corresponding hydrodynamical part of the kinetic VPB system. Objective 2: Although the wave pattern of the Boltzmann equation has been heavily studied, to our knowledge there is no corresponding study of wave patterns on the Landau equation and the Vlasov-Poisson-Landau system so far. Notice that the Boltzmann operator is an integral one while the Landau operator is an integro-differential one, so it is formally much harder to treat the latter case for the stability of non-trivial profiles. Indeed, in this project, we have established the nonlinear stability of rarefaction waves to the VPL system with the physical Coulomb interaction. We also have proved that the rarefaction waves are time asymptotically stable and tend to the rarefaction waves of the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations. As a by-product, the nonlinear stability of the same rarefaction waves to the Landau equation has been also proved. This illustrates that the electric field term does not affect the rarefaction wave propagation to the Landau equation under the assumption of the same masses of two species of particles. We hope that our result serves as a first step to study the nonlinear stability of wave patterns of the Landau equation. The proof of the main result is based on the analysis on the compressible Euler and Navier-Stokes equations and decomposition of solutions to the Landau equation with respect to the local Maxwellian. Since we study the Landau equation around a local Maxwellian and the linearized operator has no a spectral gap, it gives rises to more analytic difficulties than the study on perturbations of a global Maxwellian. As in the Boltzmann case, the source term of the microscopic equation is not integrable in time, then we need to consider the subtraction of the micro part by an asymptotic profile to cancel the slow time decay terms. However, unlike hard potentials, the inverse of the linearized Landau operator with the Coulomb potential is unbounded. To overcome such difficulty, we apply the Burnett functions and analyze the fast decay properties about the velocity of the Burnett functions. Moreover, the nonlinear terms containing the electric field are too hard to control. We introduce a suitable weight function to handle it. To close the energy estimates, we are forced to prove the fast time decay rate of the electric field term. Finally we improve the macro-micro decompositions introduced by Liu-Yang-Yu through combining it to the perturbation with weighted functions of global Maxwellians. Thus we can simplify the related energy estimates and some basic estimates initiated by Yan Guo can be applied to energy estimates conveniently.

14301515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301515.value: 1. We have studied the large time asymptotic stability of rarefaction waves of the two-component Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system in case of disparate masses and charges of particles. The new macro-micro decomposition around local bi-Maxwellians is introduced and the energy estimates basing on such decomposition are developed. The dissipative structure of the complex fluid-type macro systems is analyzed. See the research paper item No. 1 in Section 8, Part C. 2. We have explored the possibility of stability with large initial perturbations and obtained the result on the pure Boltzmann equation in case the strength of rarefaction waves is reduced to zero. The new a priori estimates are developed to treat the difficulty of the appearance of large oscillations of solutions around initial time. See the research paper item No. 2 in Section 8, Part C. 3. We have studied the linear dissipative structure in energy spaces for the fluid-type equations arising from the complex VPB or VMB systems, and established new structural conditions to ensure the time-decay properties of solutions. The obtained result can be applied to the fluid system with much more complicated dissipative structure. See the research paper item No. 3 in Section 8, Part C. 4. We have studied the existence, structure in connection with the KdV-Burgers shock wave and dynamical stability of the shock wave profile for the Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations as the corresponding hydrodynamical approximation of the kinetic VPB system. It is proved that the shock of the NSP system can be approximated by the monotone KdV burgers shock in case when the dispersion by the Debye length is much weaker than the dissipation by the velocity viscosity. See the research paper item No. 5 in Section 8, Part C. 5. We have established the nonlinear stability of rarefaction waves to the Vlasov-Poisson-Landau system as well as the pure Landau system in case of the physical Coulomb interaction. We introduce the refined energy method combining perturbations around both local and global Maxwellians. See the research paper item No. 4 in Section 8, Part C.

14301515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301515.value: 1. To study the asymptotic stability of rarefaction waves for the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system in other cases, for instance, either the wave strength is large or the initial perturbation is large. 2. To study the asymptotic stability of other wave patterns, such as the shock wave, for the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system. 3. From our observations to the study of the Navier-Stokes-Poisson system, there exist a class of non-monotone travelling waves with the stronger dispersion than dissipation. It is certainly interesting to study the dynamical stability of such waves and also extend the result to the more complex kinetic equation.

14301815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301815.value: 近年來，超冷量子氣體逐漸成為了研究多體物理問題的一個越來越重要的載體，這主要是因為它具有傳統固態體系欠缺的極其靈活的可操控性。比如，利用Feshbach共振，粒子間的相互作用可以被改變幾個量級，因而在一套裝置中，我們就可以研究極弱和極強相互作用下的物理問題，浸沒在另一種不同原子池，如玻色愛因斯坦凝聚體，中的單個雜質的動力學，就是這其中最有趣的問題之一。雜質和雜質與池的耦合可以形成一種準粒子，機子，在固態體系中，機子的研究很廣泛而且已經證明它對高溫超導，巨磁阻等材料有重要的影響。 在本課題中，我們計劃利用粒子數不平衡的超冷原子混合物進行玻色機子的實驗研究。這一問題的實驗目前基本沒有，理論方面的工作有很多，但是得到的結果都是模型相關的，特別是在較強相互作用下，需要超越平均場理論處理時，不同理論計算得出的機子的很多基本性質，如穩定性，有效質量和能量等，都有很大出入。 我們的實驗將在一套已經工作的雙凝聚體裝置上開展，其中銣-87作為雜質，鈉-23作為凝聚體池，我們將利用最近發現的銣和鈉之間的Feshbach共振來控制雜質-凝聚體間的相互作用。初步結果顯示，我們已經可以利用這一Feshbach共振來控制銣和鈉凝聚體混合物間的相容性。我們計劃展開一系列的研究，包括在粒子數大失衡情形下的三體複合損耗對機子的影響，利用不同的射頻能譜技術探測不同相互作用下機子的能量及其他參數等。 本課題得到的結果將進一步拓展超冷量子氣體的研究廣度，提高我們對玻色機子的認知，回答理論研究的一些爭議，從而使我們對量子雜質問題有更好的理解。

14301815.label: Realisation of objectives
14301815.value: The main purpose of this project is to investigate a very important many-body problem: the Bose polaron. Although this problem was first encountered in condensed matter system, the unprecedented controllability and tunablity of ultracold atom system make it a very nice platform to study it in the strongly interacting regime. For our system, the basic setup consists of a double BEC machine of Na and Rb atoms and an inter-species Feshbach resonance for tune the interactions between them. There are four objectives in this project. All of them have been successfully addressed. 1. We successfully realized the production of a small amount of Rb impurity immersed in a Na condensate. The density ratio between the impurity and the BEC is more than 20. For detection, we developed a high field imaging system which allowed us to look at the impurity Rb atoms in different hyperfine Zeeman levels. The Feshbach magnetic field stability was improved by a factor of ten, from ~16 mG to ~1.5 mG fluctuation. This was achieved with an improved reference system based on a 20 bit DAC and a redesigned and optimized PID feedback system. We also developed a new RF pulse shaping system for the generation of Gaussion pulse. This eliminated the high frequency rings associated with the squared pulse we used before. As a result, the spectrum resolution was greatly improved now. 2. We investigated the three-body problem for the Na-Rb system near the 347 G Feshbach resonance. Due to the small mass ratio, the first Efimov resonance occurs at scattering length of 20,000a0 and is thus out of reach. Its influence on the polaron spectrum can thus be safely ignored. This conclusion was confirmed by the observed dimer-dimer resonance between NaRb Feshbach molecules which agrees with prediction from the same theoretical framework very well. This result was published in Physical Review A. 3. We spent a rather long time in looking for the polaron signal. Here, the main difficulty is the size mismatch between the impurity and the BEC. This mismatch results in a poor overlap between the impurity and bath. In fact, the thermal impurity has a large size than the BEC bath. Since the polaron signal can only be contributed by the overlapping region but the non-overlapping impurity part also responds to the RF pulse, the mismatched size obscures the signal. To overcome this difficulty, we added in another laser beam to tune the size of the Rb cloud. The wavelength in use is 805 nm which is close to the Rb D lines but far detuned from Na transitions. This allows us to modify the overall trapping potential of Rb without affect that of Na. As a result, the size of the Rb sample is greatly reduced and the overlap with the Na BEC bath is improved. With this improvement, the signal from the polaron and from the background Rb atoms can now be separated. We have been able to observe a clear signal of the Bose polaron. We took inversed rf spectrum of the Rb impurity for both repulsive and attractive Rb-Na interaction with the help of an interspecies Feshbach resonance. The lineshape of the spectrum are far from simple Gaussian. For the data analysis and comparison with theory, we are in collaboration with Prof. Gerog Brunn from University of Aarhus, Denmark. The theoretical curves provided by Prof. Brunn’s group agrees with our data nicely which confirms the observation of the polaron. We are also developing a model in order to extract the polaron energy and residue directly by fitting to the experimental spectrum. This result will be compared with different theories to gauge their validity. A joint experiment and theory paper is currently in preparation. 4. We also studied the influence of the impurity-impurity interaction on the polaron spectrum. In the first effort, we varied the concentration of the Rb impurity and performed the inverse rf spectroscopy to see shift of the polaron signal. However, it was found that the impurity-impurity interaction effect needs time to show up. This time is determined by the polaron formation time and the sound speed of the Na BEC. The inverse rf spectroscopy is thus not suitable for this probe. We then changed to a more complicated method: the polaron is first formed by the inversed rf pulses, it is then probed with the direct rf spectroscopy to give enough time for the impurity-impurity interaction effect to fully manifest. With this method, we observed the initial shift of the polaron signal when the Rb concentration is changed by 50%. However, this shift is rather small so that the signal to noise is not enough to fully quantify the effect. Our theory collaborator is now trying to develop a full theory to account for our experimental parameters. Further investigations will focus on improve the signal to noise ratio by increasing the signal size. This can be achieved by increasing the BEC number and density, as well as the number stability of the impurity.

14301815.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301815.value: 1. We observed a resonance in the scattering between weakly bound NaRb Feshbach molecules. This work was performed by first created a sample of pure NaRb Feshbach molecules and then measure the loss rate at different magnetic fields. This resonance is caused by the crossing of the energy of two NaRb Feshbach molecules with a four-body tetramer. Near this resonance, we also observed the non-Wigner threshold law dependence on temperatures which we attributed to the near resonant effect. This work has been published in Physical Review A 100,042706(2019). 2. We studied the Bose polaron problem by immersing the Rb impurity into a Na condensate. The impurity-BEC interaction is controlled from attractive to repulsive with a Feshbach resonance. We measured the polar spectrum with inverse rf spectroscopy and compared the result with a theoretical model. We also extracted the polar energy and residue vs the interaction strength. A manuscript is in preparation.

14301815.value: 1. To investigate the mass dependence of the polaron spectrum with a Rb BEC and Na as the impurity. A major challenge here is the even larger size mismatch, i.e., the size of the impurity cloud is much larger than the BEC. More advanced data analysis method, such as the inversed Abel transformation, may be necessary for finishing this study. 2. To study Bose polaron in lower dimension by loading the atoms in 2-D and 1-D potentials.

14301815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301815.value: The impurity problem is ubiquitous in condensed matter physics. The dynamics of a single impurity immersed in the bath of a distinguishable atom, such as a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), is one of the primary model systems in understanding this problem. The impurity and its coupling to the bath form a quasiparticle, polaron, has a proved influence on high transition temperature superconductors and colossal magnetoresistance materials. In this work, we investigated the Bose polaron problem with a number imbalanced ultracold atomic mixture. Experimental studies of this problem has been rather incomplete, even though it is in close resemblance to the original polaron problem where the phonon bath is also bosonic, and ultracold Bose-Bose and Bose-Fermi mixtures with tunable interactions have been available for a long time. There are already many theoretical works, but the results are typically model dependent, especially in dealing with the beyond mean-field phenomena found in this problem. Many important properties of the polaron, such as the stability, effective mass and energy are qualitatively different from one theory to another. Our results provide important data to gauge the validity of these theories and shed new light on a deeper understanding in this important impurity problem.

14301915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301915.value: This project will investigate the mechanism of macroscopic self-organization in bacterial swarms as well as the biological significance of this collective phenomenon. Self-organization is ubiquitous in biological systems, such as embryo development, amoebae aggregation, and bacterial biofilm formation. Long-range biological self-organization often arises from intercellular communication via diffusive signals. In contrast, our recent studies with bacterial swarms suggest that macroscopic self-organization over centimeter scale can arise from pure biomechanical interactions between cells and their physical environment, without the necessity of long-range chemical signaling. However, the detailed mechanism and the biological significance of such macroscopic self-organization are still unclear. In this project we aim to make a strong case for the notion that purely local interactions can lead to long-range self-organization in biological systems and in more general active matter systems. We propose to investigate the macroscopic self-organization that we recently observed in bacterial swarming colonies. We will use various imaging techniques to characterize the phenomenon in different aspects, including cellular motion, fluid dynamics and flagellar rotation. We will use genetic engineering and a high-spatiotemporal-resolution cell manipulation technique to perturb the dynamics of macroscopic self-organization, which will help us to understand the mechanism of the phenomenon and allow us to control its dynamics. Further we intend to reveal the connection between the macroscopic self-organization and colony development. The project lies at the interface of physics and biology, and the obtained results will be of great interest to both fields. Bacterial swarming resembles the initial step of bacterial surface colonization and biofilm formation, so understanding the collective behavior during bacterial swarming is of relevance to multicellularity, invasiveness, and pathogenicity. Bacterial swarms provide model systems for the study of self-propelled particles or active matter. The mechanism of macroscopic self-organization to be uncovered here will provide new insights to the control of collective dynamics in active matter systems. 此项目将研究细菌集群运动中的宏观自组织现象及其意义。 自组织显现在生物系统中十分普遍，比如胚胎发育，变形虫聚集，细菌微生物膜的形成。生物系统中长程的自组织行为一般需要通过细胞之间的化学信号通讯来调节。我们最近在细菌集群中观察到长程的自组织行为可以通过短程的生物力学作用来产生，而不需要化学信号来调节。然而这个过程的具体机制尚不清楚。 在此项目中我们计划研究细菌集群运动中的宏观自组织现象的机制，从而为在活性物质系统中短程相互作用可以引致长程自组织行为这一观点提供一个明确的范例。我们会用显微成像技术来清晰刻画细菌集群运动中的宏观自组织现象的各个方面，包括细菌运动，流体运动，以及细菌的鞭毛运动。我们还计划用高分辨率的细菌操纵技术来扰动或者控制细菌集群运动中的宏观自组织行为，以期深入理解这一现象的本质。 此项目涉及物理学和生物学的交叉领域，所得到的结果对相关领域都有重要的意义。细菌集群运动与细菌表面定植和微生物膜的形成初期行为相似，因此对细菌集群运动的研究有助于理解细菌的多细胞状态和致病过程。同时，细菌集群运动可以认为是自驱动或者活性物质体系的典型例子，因此此项目的研究结果会加深我们对活性物质体系的认识。

14301915.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301915.value: One major research output arose from this project: Chen C, Liu S, Shi X, Chaté H, Wu Y (2017) Weak synchronization and large-scale collective oscillation in dense bacterial suspensions. Nature 542: 210–214. We discovered a novel mechanism of biological collective oscillation. Collective oscillatory behavior plays a vital role in many biological processes, such as embryogenesis, organ development, and pace-making in neuron networks. Collective oscillations in multicellular systems studied to date often arise from coupling between individual cells that display inherent oscillations. In stark contrast, we discovered a mechanism of collective oscillation that does not require inherent oscillation of individual cells: We found that millions of motile cells in dense bacterial suspensions can self-organize into highly robust collective oscillatory motion, while individuals remain moving in an erratic manner. This phenomenon presents a fundamentally new mechanism of oscillatory behavior in multicellular systems, and it constitutes a new type of ordered active matter that will advance the field of non-equilibrium physics.

14301915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301915.value: The mechanism of collective oscillation we uncovered may find applications in biomaterial self-assembly and in controlling robotic swarms. We are trying to control the dynamics of self-organization with high spatiotemporal resolution along this line.

14301915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301915.value: Bacteria are the most abundant form of life on the Earth. Contrary to the conventional view that bacteria lead a single-celled life, it is now believed that the majority of bacteria live in surface-associated communities called biofilms. In the natural environment, biofilms play an important role in global carbon and nitrogen cycles. Biofilms found in the human body and on medical devices usually cause chronic infectious diseases, while some of them may benefit human metabolism and immune response. Biofilms have also attracted increasing attention from the physics community because of their relevance to nonequilibrium pattern formation, active matter, and complex fluids. It is therefore important to achieve a comprehensive understanding on the biofilm lifestyle of bacteria. Here we investigated how bacteria cells in viscous fluids perform a unique form of collective motion, namely collective oscillatory motion. The obtained results will provide essential information to understand the surface-associated lifestyle of bacteria. The results may find applications in biomaterial self-assembly and in controlling robotic swarms.
