14302015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302015.value: This project aims at applying Kevin Costello's beautiful and mathematically rigorous construction of perturbative quantum field theories (QFT) to investigate mirror symmetry and other string dualities. The development of mathematics has been largely influenced by the discovery of various string dualities over the last 30 years. Surprising predictions by physicists lead to numerous deep connections among apparently different mathematical subjects, and new subjects were being created. Nevertheless, mathematicians have found it hard to understand these dualities, mainly due to the difficulty in finding a rigorous mathematical foundation to QFT. Recently, the pioneering work of Kevin Costello gave the first complete mathematical foundation for perturbative QFT, which has immediately found numerous applications. One spectacular example is the work of Costello and Si Li on the quantum geometry of BCOV theory which in particular gave the first rigorous mathematical definition of the higher genus B-model for Calabi-Yau manifolds. One main aim of this project is to investigate mirror symmetry at higher genera. The basic idea is that SYZ constructions establish mirror symmetry at genus 0, and the work of Costello-Li indicate that by considering certain symmetries on the classical theory and proving that those are preserved during quantization, the quantum theories can be shown to be equivalent. The PI plans to study how one can make Hori and Vafa's physical proof of mirror symmetry rigorous. The key is to define gauged linear sigma models mathematically by employing Costello's theory. The rigorous definition of these models may also be applied to understand other phenomena such as the crepant transformation conjecture and the LG/CY correspondence. Another part of this project is to extend mirror symmetry to one higher dimension. The PI plans to construct a 3d analogue of the A-model; in a sense this is mirror to his recent work with Leung and Li on the rigorous construction of the Rozansky-Witten model, which is a 3d analogue of the B-model. In this way, we can formulate a 3d version of mirror symmetry which should reproduce the classical 2d version via dimensional reduction. Finally, we would also like to investigate a quantization of the Gross-Siebert program. The PI's recent work with Leung and Ma showed that scattering diagrams appear in the asymptotic expansions of solutions of a certain classical master equation. Its quantization would give a quantum Gross-Siebert program, giving rise to the tropicalization of mirror symmetry at higher genera. 本項目旨在運用Kevin Costello的美麗和嚴格的微擾量子場論 （QFT）的數學構造來調查鏡像對稱等弦論對偶。 在過去30年間，各種弦論對偶的發現影響了數學的整體發展。 物理學家所作出的令人驚訝的預測導致了數學裡眾多明顯不同 的科目之間的深刻聯繫，並正在創建新的數學課題。然而， 數學家們發現很難理解這些弦論對偶，主要原因在於很難尋找到 QFT的一個嚴格的數學描述。 最近，Kevin Costello的開拓性工作給予了微擾QFT的第一個完整 的數學定義，並已立刻度被應用到許多地方。一個典型的例子是 Costello和李思對BCOV理論量子幾何的研究，特別是給了卡拉比 - 丘流形的高虧格的B模型的第一個嚴格的數學定義。 這個項目的一個主要目標是研究高虧格的鏡像對稱。我們的基本 想法是，SYZ構造解釋了虧格0的鏡像對稱現象，而Costello和 李思的工作顯示，通過考慮經典理論上的某些對稱性，然後證明 量化期間他們得以保存，則其量子理論可以證明是等價的。 本項目的PI計劃研究如何能夠將Hori-Vafa對鏡面對稱的物理證明 嚴格化。關鍵是要採用Costello的理論給出GLSM模型在數學上 的定義。這些模型的嚴格定義也可應用於理解其他現象，例如 crepant變換猜想和LG/ CY對應。 本項目的另一部分是關於三維鏡面對稱。本項目的PI擬建立 A模型的三維版本；在某種意義上，這是本項目的PI最近與 梁及李所建立的Rozansky-Witten模型的數學構造的鏡面對偶， 亦是B模型的三維版本。這樣一來，我們就可以制定一個三維版 的鏡像對稱的，而且通過降維應能重現經典的二維版本。 最後，我們還希望調查Gross-Siebert計劃的量化。本項目的PI 最近與梁及馬的工作顯示，從古典主方程解的漸近展開可以看到 散射圖的出現。這個過程的量化應該就是Gross-Siebert計劃的 量子版本，由此將可得出高虧格的鏡面對稱的熱帶化。

14302015.label: Realisation of objectives
14302015.value: The first objective of this project was to study a 3-dimensional analogue of mirror symmetry, and its relation to the classical version. This turned out to be a highly nontrivial task which certainly needs further investigation. In a previous joint work, the PI and his collaborators studied the perturbative aspects of Rozansky-Witten’s 3-dimensional sigma-model by applying Costello's pioneering and mathematically rigorous approach to the Batalin-Vilkovisky (BV) formalism. We proved that the BV quantization (in Costello's sense) of the model can be obtained via the configuration space method of regularization due to Kontsevich and Axelrod-Singer, which therefore produces a mathematical perturbative quantum field theory. We have also applied the more recent foundational work of Costello-Gwilliam to study the factorization algebra structure of quantum observables in this case. In particular, we computed the cohomology of local quantum observables on a genus g handle body and proved that the partition function precisely reproduces the Rozansky-Witten 3-manifold invariants. This laid down the foundation of the 3-dimensional analogue of the B-twisted model (or B-model in short) in mirror symmetry. Indeed, we have also demonstrated in our work that a dimensional reduction of our classical Rozansky-Witten model reproduces exactly the topological B-model studied in a previous closely related work of Qin Li and Si Li. The next natural step would be constructing the 3-dimensional analogue of the A-twisted model (or A-model in short), whose dimensional reduction should reproduce the A-model, or equivalently, the genus 0 Gromov-Witten theory. At the moment, this still seems out of the reach of current technology and methods. (Actually a construction of the A-model in BV formalism is still lacking.) Nevertheless, a former MPhil student of the PI (and currently a PhD student in CUHK), Yu-Tung Yau, has done some preliminary work, which can help paving the way towards constructing such a theory. The second objective of this project was to apply Costello's framework to understand Hori and Vafa's physical proof of mirror symmetry. This turned out to be closely related to the very recent study of gauged linear sigma models. Indeed, it was the original idea in the work of Hori and Vafa that there are intimate relations between models whose targets are linear spaces and those whose targets are the GIT quotient of those linear spaces. As a testing ground, the PI has investigated the relation for toric Calabi-Yau manifolds as GIT quotients of vector spaces. By using instanton corrections coming from Woodward's quasimap Floer theory instead of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono's Lagrangian Floer theory, we showed that the resulting SYZ mirror (which we called the quasimap SYZ mirror) coincides with the one written down via physical means as expected. In particular, the quasimap SYZ mirror coincides with the usual SYZ mirror via the mirror map. Such a result can be regarded as an open-string version of Hori-Vafa's work, and as such, is giving a new perspective to understand their work. The next step would be investigating the quasimap SYZ mirrors for other target spaces such as flag manifolds, which can also be regarded as GIT quotients of vector spaces. The third and most important objective of this project was to incorporate SYZ and Costello's constructions, and apply to understand higher genus mirror geometry. Phrasing in a different way, our aim is to apply Costello's formalism to quantize the Gross-Siebert program, which is a genus 0 theory. In a series of joint works with his collaborators, the PI has been developing a program to achieve this goal. First of all, in a joint work with Leung and Ma, we considered a semi-flat Calabi-Yau manifold equipped with a Lagrangian torus fibration. By applying asymptotic analysis to the Maurer-Cartan equation of the Kodaira-Spencer differential graded Lie algebra (DGLA), we proved that that semi-classical limits (or rather leading order terms in asymptotic expansions) of the Fourier modes of a specific class of Maurer-Cartan solutions naturally give rise to consistent scattering diagrams. The latter are tropical combinatorial objects which encode quantum or instanton corrections (namely, data coming from holomorphic disks with boundary on Lagrangian torus fibers) and have played a crucial role in the important works of Kontsevich-Soibelman and Gross-Siebert on the reconstruction problem in mirror symmetry. On the one hand, our work realized half of the program set forth by Fukaya in 2005 (which in turned has inspired the aforementioned works of Kontsevich-Soibelman and Gross-Siebert). On the other hand, it is well known that scattering diagrams are hard to deal with because combinatorially they are very complicated objects, but our results show that one could work with DGLAs and their Maurer-Cartan equations, in much the same way as classical deformation theory, instead of scattering diagrams as the information they encode are also hidden in the Maurer-Cartan solutions. In a subsequent joint work with Ma, the PI applied asymptotic analysis again to study the extended deformation theory of the Landau-Ginzburg (LG) model mirror to a compact toric surface. We proved that semi-classical limits of Fourier modes of a specific class of solutions to the associated Maurer-Cartan equation naturally give rise to tropical disks in the toric surface with Maslov indices 0 and 2, the latter of which produces a universal unfolding of the superpotential of the LG model. In the case of the complex projective plane, our construction reproduces the perturbed superpotential constructed by Mark Gross, which was proven to be the universal unfolding written in canonical coordinates. We also showed that the extended deformation theory can be used to reinterpret the jumping phenomenon of Gross’ perturbed superpotantial across walls of the scattering diagram formed by Maslov index 0 tropical disks. All these works have laid part of the foundation for formulating the Gross-Siebert program, or genus 0 SYZ mirror symmetry, as a classical field theory under Costello’s framework. The next step, which would require completely new techniques and ideas, would be constructing a propagator of the theory. After this, the ultimate goal is to prove that the resulting classical field theory can be quantized and apply the quantization to investigate higher genus mirror symmetry.

14302015.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302015.value: The first major finding is a relation between the so-called quasimap SYZ mirror, constructed using instanton corrections (i.e., open-string Gromov-Witten—type invariants defined by moduli spaces of open quasimaps) coming from Woodward's quasimap Floer theory and the usual SYZ mirror, constructed using genus 0 open Gromov-Witten invariants coming from Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono's Lagrangian Floer theory, in the case of a toric Calabi-Yau manifold. Such a relation can be regarded as an open-string analogue of Hori-Vafa’s work on a physical proof of mirror symmetry for toric varieties, and as such, gives a new perspective on the understanding of the latter work. The second major finding is the partial realization of the Gross-Siebert program as a classical field theory in the BV quantization framework of Costello. To do so, we have to reinterpret the Gross-Siebert program, in particular the scattering diagrams which have played a crucial role in the program, in terms of the Kodaira-Spencer differential graded Lie algebra and the associated Maurer-Cartan equation. The PI and collaborators have accomplished this in the case of semi-flat Calabi-Yau manifolds; more precisely, we have shown that scattering diagrams near a point of collision of walls naturally appear as semi-classical limits of Fourier modes of Maurer-Cartan solutions. Therefore it makes sense to use the Kodaira-Spencer differential graded Lie algebra as the classical field theory associated to the Gross-Siebert program, and then the associated Maurer-Cartan equation acts as the equation of motion. In view of the fact that scattering diagrams are tropical objects, the above work has indicated that asymptotic analysis of the Maurer-Cartan equation associated to a (sheaf of) differential graded Lie algebra over an integral affine manifold (with singularities) will in general give rise to tropical objects. In a subsequent and closely related work, the PI and Ma applied this philosophy to the mirror symmetry between a toric surface and the mirror Landau-Ginzburg model. We proved that semi-classical limits of the Fourier modes of Maurer-Cartan solutions of the extended deformation theory of the Landau-Ginzburg model indeed naturally give rise to tropical disks of Maslov indices 0 and 2 in the original toric surface. Finally, the PI and his student revisited the construction of SYZ transforms for Lagrangian multisections. We found a new notion of equivalence between objects in the immersed Fukaya category of a general compact symplectic manifold under which the immersed Floer cohomology is invariant and provides an answer to a question of Akaho-Joyce.

14302015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302015.value: Here we have built the foundation for formulating the Gross-Siebert program, which is a genus 0 theory, as a classical field theory under Costello’s framework of BV quantization. The ultimate goal would be constructing a quantization of the Gross-Siebert program or SYZ mirror symmetry, which is expected to exist. The key step is to construct a propagator of the theory, which is essential in constructing a perturbative quantization of the classical theory via Feynman expansions. There are two possible approaches: one is to develop a Dolbeault (or differential-geometric) version of the differential graded BV algebra studied recently by the PI and his collaborators. This would involve defining suitable boundary conditions for differential forms and polyvector fields near the singular fibers in an SYZ fibration. Another possible approach is to apply the configuration space method of regularization due to Kontsevich and Axelrod-Singer as we did in the Rozansky-Witten theory. On the other hand, having initiated the study of SYZ transforms for Lagrangian multisections in this project, we also plan to continue and deepen the study of the geometry of SYZ transforms and apply them to various geometric problems, including those outside the realm of mirror symmetry, in a different future project.

14302015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302015.value: Mirror Symmetry was discovered by String theorists in the early 1990s. It predicts that there is a highly nontrivial and mysterious equivalence between the Symplectic Geometry of a space and the Complex Geometry of a completely different space. This led to numerous surprising and deep mathematical conjectures. Since its discoveory, mathematicians have been striving to understand the geometry of Mirror Symmetry. A breakthrough came in 1996 when Strominger, Yau and Zaslow proposed that Mirror Symmetry should be understood as a geometric Fourier transform. Lying at the heart of the SYZ conjecture is the role played by quantum corrections, which is the key to explain the miraculous power of Mirror Symmetry. Our discovery of the relation between Maurer-Cartan elements and scattering diagrams sheds new light on the understanding of quantum corrections. More significantly, this is an important step towards a quantization of SYZ mirror symmetry or the Gross-Siebert program. Our study of SYZ transforms for Lagrangian multisections also have important applications in mirror symmetry and other geometric problems, which deserve further investigation.

14302215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302215.value: Mirror Symmetry conjecture was originated in the study of String theory in Physics. Mathematically speaking, this is a highly nontrivial identification between two different kinds of Geometry, namely Symplectic Geometry and Complex Geometry. The conjecture was originally stated for pairs of Calabi-Yau manifolds and it has been generalized to other spaces and LG models. Strominger-Yau-Zaslow proposed an explanation of the Mirror Symmetry in terms of a fiberwise Fourier-Mukai type transformation. In this proposal, the PI plans to continue the studies of the SYZ transformation. These include the studies of wall crossing, scattering and quantum moduli space of symplectic structures on the A-side; the description of twin Lagrangian fibration structures and their SYZ transforms; the research on coisotropic A-branes as being SYZ mirror to special Hodge cycles. 鏡對稱源自物理中弦理論的研究。從數學的角度来看，這是兩種不同的幾何的對等關係，它們分别是辛幾何和複幾何。這猜想已從加拉比丘空間推廣至其他空間及LG模型。SYZ提議用 Fourier-Mukai 變換来解析鏡對稱。 在這研究計劃中，研究員計劃繼續SYZ變換的研究。这些研究包括通過牆，散射及辛结構的量子化模空間。描述孿生Lagrangian叢結構及它們的 SYZ 變換。研究 A - 膜作為特殊Hodge周期的 SYZ 鏡象。

14302215.label: Realisation of objectives
14302215.value: The PI has realized all objectives stated in the proposal and also discovered new structures along the way. Quantum corrections has been analyzed in depth for toric orbifolds, relationships with (refined) scattering diagrams, theta functions. Quantum deformation of symplectic structures has been studied and realized using scattering diagrams and also related to our solution of the Fukaya's conjecture. SYZ transformation between A- and B-branes in the large structure limits becomes the same type of scattering diagrams, which has been carefully analyzed. New structures for derived categories are found via homological projective duality. Also three dimensional sigma model, Rozansky-Witten theory, has been established via mathematical approach of Costello.

14302215.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302215.value: In the paper "Scattering diagrams from asymptotic analysis on Maurer-Cartan equations", we investigate SYZ mirror symmetry via asymptotic analysis on Maurer-Cartan equations, following a program set forth by Fukaya. We prove that the semi-classical limits of the Fourier modes of a Maurer-Cartan solution give rise to a consistent scattering diagram. In the paper "Refined scattering diagrams and theta functions from asymptotic analysis of Maurer-Cartan equations", we further develop the asymptotics analytic approach to the study of scattering diagrams. In particular we give a combinatorial description of Hall algebra theta functions for acyclic quivers with nondegenerate Euler forms. In the paper "Fukaya's conjecture on Witten's twisted A_infinity structures", we proved Fukaya's conjecture which says that Witten deformation of higher product structures on cohomology have semiclassical limits as operators defined by counting gradient flow trees with respect to Morse functions. This can be viewed as quantum corrections for cotangent bundles by the work of Fukaya-Oh. In the paper "Pseudotoric structures and special Lagrangian torus fibrations on certain flag varieties", we construct pseudotoric structures on the two-step flag variety Fl(1,n-1,n) which is revelent to the study of SYZ transformation for these spaces. In the paper "A note on disk counting in toric orbifolds", we compute orbi-disk open Gromov-Witten invariants of semi-Fano toric orbifolds and prove convergence in such cases. In the paper "BV quantization of the Rozansky-Witten model", the PI investigate the perturbative aspects of Rozansky-Witten's 3d sigma model using Costello's approach to BV formalism. We produces a perturbative quantum field theory. We also study the factorization algebra structure of quantum observables. In the paper "Categorical Plucker formula and Homological Projective Duality", we give a complete description of derived categories of intersections of HP-dual varieties.

14302215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302215.value: The techniques developed here could be very useful for further understanding of various duality transformations in mathematics and physics.

14302215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302215.value: Mirror symmetry is a deep and mysterious conjectural duality between two different types of geometries. SYZ transformation provides a plausible geometric explanation of it. In this project, the PI had developed important tools in analyzing this transformation using tools from analysis, algebraic geometry and symplectic geometry. The PI also obtained many geometric results along this studies, including the solution of the Fukaya's conjecture.

14302315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302315.value: In this proposal we aim to develop a simple and reliable rehydratable gel-microwell hybrid platform for bioanalysis. The microwell volume ranges from fL to nL, allowing high throughput analysis and single molecule studies. The key feature of the microwell is the rehydratable gel inside each microwell. The dried rehydratable gel can be preloaded with analysis reagent for long-term storage. To perform bioanalysis in the gel-in-well device, analyte solutions will be dispensed into the microwells to rehydrate the gel and to react with the preloaded reagents. To facilitate reliable solution dispensing, the microwell device will present hydrophobic surface while the inner wall of the microwells will be hydrophilic. The rehydration kinetics of the dried gel will be measured in the research. Two models will be used to study the rehydration mechanism and to evaluate the applicability of the dried gel under different experimental conditions. The application of the microwell platform will be illustrated in two aspects: digital PCR and single molecule kinetics. In the first application, the PCR reagents will be preloaded and dried together with the gel in the microwells. The drying procedure will be optimized to preserve the activity of the DNA polymerase in the PCR reagents. Digital PCR will be performed by dispensing solutions of target DNA into arrays of pL microwells. In the second application, the enzyme substrate will be preloaded and dried together with the gel in the microwells. The enzyme solution is then dispensed into arrays of fL microwells to initiate the reaction. The gel-in-well platform obviates the multiple reagent dispensing and mixing in the traditional microwell plate-based bioanalysis. There is no need of sophisticated pumping or valve instruments in the usage of the gel-in-well device, making the platform compatible with point-of-care testing. 我們計劃發展一個簡單可靠的微凝膠-微井系統用於生物分析。微井的體積範圍從飛升到納升，支持高通量或單分子分析。這個系統一個重要特徵是每一個微井有一個幹態的微凝膠粒。幹態的微凝膠預先載有與分析相關的試劑以用於長期儲存。用這個系統進行生物分析時，樣品溶液加入到微井中，幹態的微凝膠吸水成水凝膠溶液，預載的試劑得以與樣品反應。 爲了能夠可靠地把溶液加入到微井中，微井系統的外表面將會處理變疏水，而微井內壁則親水。 我們將表徵幹態的微凝膠吸水的動力學。兩個理論模型將被用於研究吸水的機理，以及評估在不同實驗條件下應用微凝膠的可行性。 我們計劃把微凝膠-微井系統應用於數字化聚合酶鏈式反應（PCR）和單分子動力學兩個方面。 在第一個應用裏，PCR試劑將會預先加入到幹態的微凝膠並儲存於微井中。乾燥的過程需要優化以最大限度地保存聚合酶的活性。數字化PCR的實驗只需將目標DNA溶液加入到皮升的微井中就可以進行。 在第二個應用裏, 酶的底物將會預載於幹態的微凝膠並儲存於微井中。然後酶溶液 加入到飛升微井的陣列以啓動反應。 微凝膠-微井系統避免了傳統生物分析中在多孔板上多次的試劑添加和混合。這個系統也不需要複雜的微泵或閥門，所以適合於在現場進行即時測試。

14302315.label: Realisation of objectives
14302315.value: Objective 1 was successfully achieved. We developed two different strategies for fabricating microwells with heterogeneous surface hydrophobicity. In the first method, we used microfluidic deposition of polydopamine to produce hydrophilic microwells on the flat hydrophobic substrate surfaces. In the second method, we developed a new negative microcontact printing strategy to produce hydrophilic microwells on perfluorinated surfaces. The heterogeneous surfaces facilitated reliable production of rehydratable gel particles in the microwells. Different types of hydrogels were prepared and compared in terms of preparation reliability, mechanical stability, rehydratability, swelling ratio, swelling kinetics, and etc. We found that the best candidates for the applications in bioanalysis are polyacrylamide hydrogel and PEG-DA hydrogel. Objective 2 was successfully achieved. We used polyacrylamide hydrogel as the model to study the rehydration kinetics. We found that the water uptake was by the combination of Fickian diffusion and convection. We also studied the effect of the drying technique on the rehydration of the hydrogel. We observed that the pore size was significantly larger during the rehydration process if the hydrogel was dried directly in air at room temperature, which allowed the hydrogel to absorb large macromolecules such as ribosomes. By contrast, freeze-dried hydrogel did not present such result of enlarged pore size. Through these experiments, we identified the optimal conditions and procedures to use the rehydratable hydrogel as a storage medium of proteins and as a microreactor for applications such as protein crystallization and protein assay. Objective 3 was successfully achieved. In this objective, we further optimized the negative microcontact printing method to produce hydrophilic patterns on perfluorinated surfaces. The patterning resolution reached sub-micron, thus we were able to fabricate fL microwells reliably. Based on this patterning method, we were able to create arrays of one million microwells with the dimension of a few microns. The large number of the microwells allowed us to perform digital PCR with broad dynamic ranges. We also demonstrated single-molecule detection by digital ELISA in such microwells, which is of great interest in clinic diagnosis. Using the droplet microfluidic technique that we used in the surface patterning method, we also developed a new kinetics-based gene detection method. We were able to detect single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) with the abundance as low as 0.2%, which could be useful in early diagnosis of various cancers.

14302315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302315.value: We developed a simple and reliably method of surface patterning with the spatial resolution down to a few microns (H. Wu, L. Wu, X. Zhou, B. Liu, B. Zheng, Small, 2018, 14, 1802128). Recently we optimized the method and improved the resolution to sub-microns (S. Qian, H. Wu, B. Zheng, manuscript in preparation). We investigated the rehydration kinetics of the pre-dried gel particles in microwells and identified the dominating rehydration mechanisms that are responsible for the uptaking of macromolecules into the hydrogel particles (H. Wu, B. Liu, B. Zheng, manuscript in preparation). We developed a new platform using two arrays of microwells for kinetics measurement and for quantitative bioanalysis (X. Zhou, X. Zhou, B. Zheng, Talanta, 2017, 175, 483). We applied the droplet microfluidic method we developed in the surface patterning to the detection of single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) (M. Cui, H. Feng, D. Guo, D. Wang, B. Zheng, Sens. Actuators B Chem., 2017, 253, 731; M. Cui, X. Xiao, M. Zhao, B. Zheng, Analyst, 2018, 143, 116). We also applied the macromolecular conditions to the SNP detection, and found there was a positive crowding effect on the differentiation of SNP from wild type genes using the droplet microfluidic method (M. Cui, X. Zhou, X. Chen, W. Zheng, L. Bian, Z. Li, B. Zheng, Chem. Comm., 2019, 55, 12052). Two students obtained their PhD for their work on this project. Miao Cui developed a kinetics based SNP detection using droplet microfluidics and further investigated the crowding effect on the SNP detection. Han Wu developed the negative microcontact printing method of patterning perfluorinated surfaces, which was used to fabricate millions of microwells with the dimension of a few microns. Research collaboration has been established based on the research works. We are collaborating with Professor Gao Qingyu of the China University of Mining and Technology. Professor Gao is an expert in nonlinear chemical systems. We encapsulated the nonlinear chemical system in microgel particles and plan to investigate the nonlinear biochemical kinetics such as protein expression in the microgel.

14302315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302315.value: The digital PCR using the arrays of gel-in-microwells with fL volume enables the accurate and sensitive measurement of DNA copy numbers, making digital PCR especially useful for rare targets in genetic samples, such as cancer diagnosis, virus detection, and microbes research. To make the digital PCR technology more accessible to the various applications, we need to further improve the instrumentation regarding the device cost and further simplify the operation of the device as well as data analysis. The second important potential application of the arrays of gel-in-microwell is digital ELISA, which allows us to quantitatively detect biomolecules with high sensitivity and specificity. Digital ELISA would dramatically improve the accuracy and sensitivity of many diagnosis, especially for the testing against HIV, HPV and HSV. To make the digital ELISA usable in disease diagnosis, we need to identify the antibody pairs that bind to the target molecules strongly, probably on the level of nM. Similar to digital PCR, we also need to further reduce the device cost and simplify the operation of the device.

14302315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302315.value: In this project we produced arrays of microwells which have the diameter on the scales of a few micrometers. By chemically modify the surface properties, we developed a protocol to reliably filling the microwells with hydrogel. We used the hydrogel in the microwells as a storage medium. We were able to load the molecules of interest into the hydrogel in the microwells for later usage, such as chemical and biochemical analysis, protein crystallization, and etc. We investigated the swelling process of the pre-dried hydrogel in the microwells. We identified the mechanisms that were responsible for the rapid loading of the molecules of interest into the hydrogel. We applied the arrays of microwells containing the hydrogel to bioanalysis. For example, we demonstrated counting the number of nucleic acid molecules in a sample solution, which was partitioned into the microwells for analysis. We also developed a droplet-based technique to detect the nucleic acid mutation in a mixture containing the nucleic acid without mutation.

14302415.value: 分形集合投影和交集的幾何與維數性質

14302415.label: Project Objectives
14302415.value: It is proposed to study the geometric and dynamical structures of intersections of self-similar sets and dynamical invariant sets, so as to analyze the dimension of these intersections. Particular interest will be laid on the intersections of homogenous self-similar sets whose contraction ratios are not logarithmic commensurable. It is proposed to study the dimension of intersections of Moran-like Cantor sets, and characterize the corresponding exceptional set of Marstrand slicing theorem. It is proposed to study the multifractal spectrum of planar random self-similar measures (the so-called Mandelbrot measures) under coordinate projections. Although the fine properties of this family of random measures have been well understood, their projections under specific directions have not yet been studied.

Particular interest will be laid on the intersections of homogenous self-similar sets whose contraction ratios are not logarithmic commensurable.
It is proposed to study the dimension of intersections of Moran-like Cantor sets, and characterize the corresponding exceptional set of Marstrand slicing theorem.

It is proposed to study the multifractal spectrum of planar random self-similar measures (the so-called Mandelbrot measures) under coordinate projections. Although the fine properties of this family of random measures have been well understood, their projections under specific directions have not yet been studied.

14302415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302415.value: The brilliant groundbreaking notion of fractal was coined by Mandelbrot in 1970's to model irregular objects in nature and in mathematics. Since then, the idea of fractal has spread into numerous areas of natural sciences. In mathematics, it has emerged as a new area named fractal geometry. One of the basic subjects in fractal geometry is to study the shape and size of fractal sets under projections and intersections. Unlike smooth geometric objects, even very simple fractal sets may generate extremely complicated structures in their projections and intersections. In mathematics there are some existing fundamental results on dimensional properties of general sets and measures under projections along `typical' directions, and the dimension of `random' intersections of sets. However these results tell nothing about the projections along particular directions, and about deterministic intersections. It arise a natural and important question to study the projections along particular or all directions, as well as the deterministic intersections, for those fractal sets and measures which have strict self-similar structures or dynamical structures. In this project, the proposer plans to focus on several concrete problems, including the study of dimensional properties of intersections of homogeneous self-similar sets, and the study of multifractal structures of a class of planar random Cantor measures under horizontal and vertical projections. These problems are far from being well understood in the literature, there are plenty of rooms for further development. Mandelbrot於上世紀70年代引入了分形的概念，並用它來刻畫數學與自然界中的不規則對象。自此以來，分形的想法已廣泛應用到自然科學的諸多領域。在數學領域裡已產生了名為分形幾何這一學科。 分形幾何的一個基本課題是研究分形集合投影與交集的形狀與大小。和光滑幾何對像不同，對於即便非常簡單的分形集合，它們的投影與交集可能產生十分複雜的結構。儘管數學上目前已有一些關於集合與測度在典型方向上之投影理論，以及關於集合的隨機交集的維數理論， 然而對於確定方向之投影以及確定之交集了解甚少。一個自然且重要的問題是研究具有嚴格自相似結構或動力系統結構的分形集合及測度的確定投影及確定交集。 在該計劃中，申請人擬考慮幾個具體的問題， 包括研究齊次自相似集的確定交集性質，平面隨機康托集在水平或豎直方向上投影的重分形結構。

14302515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302515.value: The aim of this proposal is to investigate asymptotic properties of spin glass models. The disordered spin systems were introduced initially by physicists in the late seventies with the desire of understanding the strange magnetic behaviors of certain alloys. Over the past decades, theoretical physicists have invented a variety of models along with a series of conceptual theories. In recent years, the heuristic methodologies therein have been pushed forward to several applications in various fields such as neural network theory, computer science, theoretical biology and econophysics. This proposal is mainly concerned about two mean-field spin glass models. The first model is the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) model or more generally the mixed p-spin model. The PI and co-PI will focus on three major problems: the structure and the role of the Parisi measure, asymptotic properties of some physical observations and universality of the system. Another mean-field model that will be considered in this project is a bipartite version of the SK model. The PI and co-PI will be concentrated on the computation of its limiting free energy. 本项目旨在研究自旋玻璃（spin glass）模型的渐近性质。 上世纪七十年代，关于合金材料的磁性状态研究，发现了一些 比较奇特的物理现象， 为了更好地解释这些现象，理论物理学 家提出无序自旋系统的概念。据此，几十年来，理论物理学家 发展了一系列关于该系统的模型和理论。最近，这些物理学上 的启发性的探索，也极大地推动了一些其它领域学科的发展， 例如神经网络，计算机科学，理论生物学以及经济物理学等等。 本项目主要关心两类平均场自旋玻璃模型的渐近性质。第一类 模型是 Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) 模型或者是更加一般的 混合p-自旋模型。项目主持人及其合作者将主要考虑以下三个 问题：Parisi 测度的构造和作用，一些物理观测的渐近性质以 及自旋系统的普适性。另一类将考虑的平均场模型是SK模型的 二分版本。项目主持人及其合作者将主要关注该模型的极限 自由能量的计算。

14302515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302515.value: The PI , co-PI with their co-authors have published 19 papers, most of which are in the top journals in the field. Objectives 1 and 3 are completely achieved, while objectives 2 and 4 have been finished 80%. Results we proved include: 1. We show that the Parisi formula of the mixed p-spin model is a concave function of the squared inverse temperature and derive a new expression for the Parisi formula. 2. We show that the limiting ground state energy of the spherical mixed p-spin model can be identified as the infimum of certain variational problem. As an application, we obtain explicit formulas for the limiting ground state energy in replica symmetry breaking phases at zero temperature. 3. We give two types of examples of spherical mixed even-p-spin models for which chaos in temperature holds. These complement some known results for the spherical pure p-spin models and for models with Ising spins. 4. We show that the free energy in the mixed p-spin models of spin glasses does not superconcentrate in the presence of external field, which means that its variance is of the order suggested by the Poincare inequality. This complements the result of Chatterjee who showed that the free energy superconcentrates when there is no external field. For models without odd p-spin interactions, we prove the central limit theorem for the free energy at any temperature and give an explicit formula for the limiting variance. 5. We developed a general approach for identifying the limiting distribution via an exchangeable pair and obtained sharp Berry-Esseen bound for Curie-Weis nmodel. We also developed a general Berry-Esseen type bound in both normal and nonnormal approximation for unbounded exchangeable pairs. The result is successfully applied to various examples including the quadratic forms, general Curie-Weiss model, mean ﬁeld Heisenberg model and colored graph model.

14302715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302715.value: In July 4, 2012, the ATLAS and the CMS experimental collaborations at the European Organization for Nuclear Physics (CERN), announced the discovery of a particle compatible with the Standard Model Higgs boson in the analysis proton-proton collisions produced by the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The discovery was recognized (among other awards) with the High Energy and Particle Physics Prize 2013 of the European Physical Society, awarded to the ATLAS and CMS collaborations, and the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics, awarded to Professors Peter Higgs and Francois Englert. The Large Hadron Collider is now undergoing a shut-down period for maintenance and upgrades; it will resume operations in 2015 with a collision energy of about 14 TeV, which is significantly higher than the energy used to find the Higgs boson (up to 8 TeV), and will collect a much larger data sample. This new data-taking period, customarily called “Run II”, will allow detailed studies of the properties of the Higgs boson, and will make it possible to explore a range of energies previously inaccessible. Hong Kong institutions, building over the solid foundation provided by the success of the Daya Bay Reactor Experiment, have created the Joint Consortium for Fundamental Physics in Hong Kong (JCFP). In June of 2014, the JCFP was accepted as a member of the ATLAS Experimental Collaboration. Hong Kong researchers are already actively involved in the analysis of the Run I data and on the preparation work for Run II of the LHC. To focus our effort, the JCFP will join the ATLAS Muon Spectrometer Project, and will undertake a number of responsibilities within the ATLAS collaboration. The goal of this project is to strengthen the participation of the JCFP in the ATLAS Experiment at CERN through work on the following areas: 1. Measurement of the differential cross-sections of Higgs boson production using Run II data. 2. Search for high-mass di-muon resonances, with particular emphasis on the study of high-momentum muon reconstruction, and of the systematic uncertainties of this search. 3. Contribution to the ATLAS muon identification and reconstruction systems during Run II These areas are designed to avoid overlap with the objectives of the JCFP proposal and, to the maximum extent possible, to complement them to build a complete and solid physics program from Hong Kong institutions, with a significant impact and a long-term contribution to LHC Physics.

14302715.label: Realisation of objectives
14302715.value: All objectives were achieved. Details on each one are given below; research outputs mentioned in PART C are denoted here as RO1, RO2, RO3 and RO4. Objective 1. Measurement of the differential cross-sections of Higgs boson production using Run II data. The Higgs boson, discovered in 2012 at CERN by the ATLAS and CMS collaborations, is a cornerstone of the Standard Model of Particle Physics (SM). Its coupling strengths were measured using the complete dataset from Run I of the LHC by the ATLAS collaboration [ATLASCo14], and these measurements have been extended and updated including additional Higgs decay channels [ATLASCo16]. We made many contributions to these results in close collaboration with other Hong Kong institutions, focusing mainly on selection procedures, the estimation of the background levels, and the study of the systematic uncertainties involved. The results also constituted the basis of a joint ATLAS-CMS measurement of Higgs boson production and couplings [ACCo15]. Our group has contributed consistently to the study of the Higgs boson in the four-leptons decay channel (where the Higgs boson decays into two Z bosons, each of which decays into two leptons). We have developed a solid expertise on this channel and became one of the main groups contributing to the measurement of the differential cross sections for Higgs boson production. A measurement based on the analysis of 36.1 fb-1 (total integrated luminosity) of proton-proton collisions was made public for the 5th Conference on Large Hadron Collider Physics, held in Shanghai, China, on May 15-20, 2017, through a public ATLAS Note [RO1]; the inclusive fiducial cross section in the four-leptons channel was found to be 3.62+-0.50(stat)+0.25-0.20(syst) fb, in agreement with the standard model prediction of 2.91+-0.13 fb. Several differential fiducial cross sections were measured. Results were in good agreement with the SM predictions and were used to set limits on modified Higgs boson interactions [Gon15a, Gon15b]. This work was also published in JHEP [RO2] and is being further developed for the measurement with the full Run II dataset. I would like to clarify here that ATLAS Conference notes do not include an author list; as a result, neither individual ATLAS members, nor funding agencies, are explicitly listed. This is the reason for the lack of an explicit acknowledgement to RGC in [RO1], as entered in section 8 of the Electronic System (Part C: Research Output), but the corresponding publication [RO2] does include the RGC acknowledgement. Objective 2. Search for high-mass di-muon resonances, with particular emphasis on the study of high-momentum muon reconstruction, and of the systematic uncertainties of this search. Our group has been involved in Exotic Physics searches involving leptons since the beginning of our work with the ATLAS collaboration; specifically, on searches for resonances decaying into final states that violate lepton-flavor conservation (electron + muon, electron + tau, muon + tau). Our involvement in those studies has allowed us to develop the techniques and software tools needed for selection, study and analysis of final states resonances with high-momentum muons. In this context, we have developed and refined methods for the data-driven estimation of background processes that can affect searches involving high-momentum leptons. We also work with the ATLAS Group in charge of identification and reconstruction of muons. Building on our experience with muon reconstruction, we contributed to the improvement, upgrade and monitoring of the algorithms used, and studied variations to the analyses carried out so far to take advantage of the large datasets available in run 2, which were used in the search based on 36.1 fb-1 of pp collision data [RO3], and, more recently, further developed in the analysis of the full run 2 dataset, with 139fb-1 of pp collision data [RO4]. With the latter dataset, the 95% CL lower limits on the mass of possible heavy resonance models [Lon86, Lang09] have been extended to 5.1TeV for the combination of the two same-flavor channels (e+e-, mu+mu-). Objective 3. Contribution to the ATLAS muon identification and reconstruction systems during Run II. In collaboration with the ATLAS Muon Combined Performance (MCP) group, we studied and characterized the performance of the two algorithms used in ATLAS to identify muons using only tracking and calorimeter information. Based on those studies, we have been able to modify and improve both algorithms. One algorithm uses selection cuts to determine whether the profile of energy depositions along a reconstructed trajectory is compatible with a muon; upon recognition of large differences in background rejection among different regions of the ATLAS detector, we implemented a selection map that allows a fine-grained tuning of cut values based on a global strategy. Three selection maps were implemented in the ATLAS reconstruction software: a loose selection (aimed at maintaining a large reconstruction efficiency), a tight selection (to minimize non-muon particles wrongly tagged as muons), and a legacy-type selection (to allow fair comparisons with earlier version of the algorithm). The second algorithm uses a multivariate approach, in which energy deposition profiles of muons and non-muon particles passing through the detector are used to build a single discriminating variable. We have already replaced several of the energy deposition profiles with more accurate versions (obtained with full-detector simulation using a more complete description of the detector) with marginal gains in performance. Objective 4. Train Hong Kong students and postdocs for research in the forefront of fundamental physics. One postdoctoral research associate, one PhD student (Tak Shun Lau), one MPhil student (Yun Sang Chow) and one undergraduate student (Heng Fai Chang) contributed to this project. This allowed them to fully benefit from the close interaction with colleagues from other ATLAS institutions (located both in Hong Kong and overseas), from learning several of the tools used for research in High Energy Physics, and from working with recent data and Monte Carlo simulation from the Large Hadron Collider, on searches and measurements at the energy frontier. 14302715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302715.value: 1. Inclusive and differential fiducial cross sections of Higgs boson production are compatible with the corresponding standard model expectations. They were measured in proton-proton collision data from the Large Hadron Collider using the four-lepton decay channel. The collisions, recorded by the ATLAS detector, had a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. With an integrated luminosity of 36.1 fb−1, the inclusive fiducial cross section in this decay channel was measured as 3.62 ± 0.50 (stat) +0.25 (sys) fb, in agreement with the SM prediction (2.91 ± 0.13 fb). Several differential fiducial cross sections were measured for observables sensitive to the Higgs boson production and decay, finding also good agreement with SM predictions. Constraints on anomalous interactions between the Higgs boson and SM particles were obtained. Results are included in publications #1 and #2 listed in PART C.8. 2. A search for high-mass dilepton resonances using up to 139 fb-1 of 13 TeV centre-of-mass pp collision data from the LHC found no significant deviation from the SM expectation. Upper limits were derived at the 95% CL on the fiducial cross section times branching ratio for various hypotheses. These limits, in turn, correspond to lower limits on the mass of benchmark models of physics beyond the SM. Results are included in publications #3 and #4 listed in PART C.8.

14302715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302715.value: There are several areas for potential refinements and improvements. For the Higgs analysis, many developments are currently under way, both on the theory side and in terms of experimental techniques; one example is the use of Machine Learning techniques, which is being actively pursued by our group. For the dilepton searches, Machine Learning techniques can also be used, both when applied at the level of physics objects (specifically in the identification of muons) and at the level of signal extraction.

14302715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302715.value: This research project contributes to our understanding of the fundamental processes of Nature from three fronts: (a) our measuring tools, (b) the characteristics of the Higgs boson, and (c) searching for phenomena that is not expected in our current theories. These objectives are pursued through the analysis of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN in Geneva, Switzerland. There, protons travel almost at the speed of light; when they collide, they can transform into any particle allowed by the laws of Nature. Our current description of these laws (the “Standard Model”, or SM) provides very precise predictions for the possible outcomes of these collisions, but we know that the SM is incomplete, so we are making a systematic search for phenomena not contained in it. We aim specifically to (a) improve the identification of muons, because muons constitute one of the best tools to reconstruct what happened on each particle collision; (b) learn as much as we can about the Higgs boson, whose interactions with other particles may unveil unexpected new phenomena; (c) search for deviations from the predictions of the SM in events containing muon pairs.

14302915.label: Project Objectives
14302915.value: To determine the sequence criteria and environmental conditions for the occurrence of stem-stem interactions between hairpins. The stem regions of hairpins adopted by CAG and CTG repeats contain A•A and T•T mismatches flanked by C-G and G-C Watson-Crick base pairs in a double-helical stem region. These mismatches are expected to have lower thermodynamic stabilities compared to Watson-Crick base pairs and therefore they can open up more frequently. The feasibility of these mismatch openings indeed serve as potential sites to initiate interactions with another hairpin. As a higher thermodynamic stability is expected for a longer repeat length in the stem region, this does not favor the initiation of interactions. Instead, a shorter stem will be more feasible for initiating stem-stem interactions. Therefore, we expect that depending on the sequence context, there will be an optimal repeat length and environmental conditions that favor stem-stem interactions between hairpins. The sequence criteria here refer to the (i) sequence context of repeats, and (ii) repeat length. For the environmental conditions, these include studying the effects of (i) temperature, (ii) type of salt and ionic strength, (iii) pH, and (iv) molecular crowding. To determine the sequence criteria and environmental conditions for the occurrence of loop-loop interactions between hairpins. The dynamics and flexibility of unpaired bases in the loop regions of CAG and CTG repeat hairpins serve as potential initiation sites for loop-loop interactions. Although both CAG and CTG repeats form hairpins with a predominantly 4-nt AGCA and TGCT loops, respectively, the most stable form of these hairpins may not be the best one for initiating loop-loop interactions. It is possible and likely that other sizes of loops can be formed when strand slippage occurs during DNA replication. Therefore, to determine if loop-loop interactions can be present in CAG and CTG repeat hairpins, it is important to determine the effects of sequence context and loop size on initiating loop-loop interactions. Similarly, the environmental conditions for the presence of these interactions will be optimized. To determine the sequence criteria and environmental conditions for the occurrence of stem-loop interactions between hairpins. Topologically, if a long stretch of CAG or CTG repeats form two adjacent hairpins with different sizes, there is a possibility that the unpaired bases in the loop region of the smaller hairpin initiate interactions with the stem region of the larger hairpin. Owing to the dynamic nature and flexibility of the leading and lagging strands during DNA replication, it will not be uncommon that long CAG and CTG repeats can fold into multiple hairpins that are of different sizes. Therefore, stem-loop interactions can also serve as an origin for initiating the formation of MIH, and it will also be important to determine the effect of sequence context, loop size, and stem length on stem-loop interactions. To determine the effect of MIH on the fidelity of DNA replication. After identifying the sequence criteria and environmental conditions for the formation of MIH, we will put an optimized MIH sequence into a primer and template strands to see how DNA polymerase will handle this sequence. In particular, we aim to determine if MIH will lead to polymerase pausing and/or expansion mutations.

14302915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302915.value: This project aims to determine if a long DNA repeating sequence can fold into a higher order structure comprising of multiple interacting hairpins (MIH) instead of a single large hairpin. Specifically, we will determine the sequence criteria and environmental conditions for the presence of interactions between hairpins, which govern the formation of MIH. It is now well known that genetic mutations do not arise randomly in the genome sequences and spontaneous mutagenesis depends on the context of the DNA sequences. Trinucleotide repeats (TNR) is one type of such hypermutational sequences that can affect gene products and gene regulation when they are localized in coding and non-coding regions, respectively. At least 30 genetic disorders have been found to relate to TNR expansions. The formation of non-B form hairpin structures has been proposed to associate with the genetic instability which leads to expansion mutations. Although the exceptionally stable hairpin-forming sequences are abundant in the human genome, they are rarely found in TNR expansions, suggesting the culprit of expansions may be a novel structure rather than simply a hairpin. Recent findings show that the formation of multiple slip-outs in CAG and CTG repeats escapes DNA repair efficiently, leading us to the hypothesis that instead of a single hairpin, a long stretch of CAG and CTG repeats may form multiple smaller hairpins that interact with each other. In this project, we propose to perform native gel electrophoresis and nuclear magnetic resonance investigations on the solution behaviors of the hairpins formed by CAG and CTG repeats through the variations of sequence context and repeat lengths in the stem and loop regions, and under different environmental conditions. Specifically, we will monitor if there will be (i) stem-stem, (ii) loop-loop, and (iii) stem-loop interactions between the hairpins formed by CAG or CTG repeats. The higher order MIH structure may appear to be a novel DNA structural intermediate that leads to DNA expansion during DNA replication, repair and/or recombination, providing an alternative mechanistic pathway for CAG and CTG repeat expansions. The long term impact will improve our understandings of the origin of the diseases that are related to hairpin-forming TNR sequences. More importantly, the identification of interactions between hairpins provides us a structural target for designing therapeutics to inhibit DNA expansion, thereby controlling the chance of genetic mutations and/or the effect on gene regulation and transcription.

14303415.label: Project Objectives
14303415.value: Illustrating the stage and structure prior to nuclei formation such as the precursor structure and probing the new physics brought by the external boundary in heterogeneous nucleation. In the homogeneous nucleation precursors are crucial structures before nuclei formation, and have properties similar to both liquid and solid [40], which facilitate the initial formation of nuclei from liquid via precursors. However, the stage even before precursor remains unknown. Moreover, in heterogeneous nucleation the external boundary induces the nucleation, and poses an entirely new initial condition. For example, the nucleation rates along the boundary and perpendicular to the boundary are totally different and the process is spatially inhomogeneous [33]. We will explore the possible origin of the precursor and the new physics arises from the boundary and spatial inhomogeneity. Clarifying these fundamental questions is crucial for the understanding of heterogeneous nucleation kinetics from the beginning of the process. Elucidating the kinetic pathways of heterogeneous nucleation. Kinetics should evolve continuously as disordered liquid changes into ordered solid. In the homogeneous nucleation this evolution proceeds along multiple pathways, either within the same symmetry or across different symmetries (i.e., BCC, FCC or HCP [40]). However, completely new behaviors arise in the heterogeneous nucleation, including the layering of particles along the boundary, the significant role of boundary effect, and the much lower energy barrier. These new features will undoubtedly produce unique properties in kinetic pathways, whose illustration will uncover fundamental new physics and provide technological guidance to control the crystallization rate with kinetic aspects.

14303415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303415.value: This project aims to build a well-controlled colloidal crystallization system adjustable from homogeneous nucleation to heterogeneous nucleation, directly visualize the distinctive transition kinetics in both symmetry and density for these two fundamental crystallization processes, and clarify the essential difference between the homogeneous and heterogeneous nucleation kinetics at single-particle level. Crystallization is an important process in condensed matter physics and materials science. As liquid changes into solid, evolutions in both symmetry and density take place. The classical nucleation theory describes this process as the nucleation and growth of nuclei: small crystals, which have the same symmetry and density as the stable solid, directly emerge from liquid through thermal fluctuation. However, this description is over-simplified in terms of kinetics, giving little information on how the initially disordered state continuously evolve into the ordered state. Moreover, there are two primary crystallization approaches: the homogeneous and heterogeneous nucleation, which have very different nucleation rates even under the same pressure and temperature. Although this difference has been explained by the energy argument – external boundaries or impurities can typically reduce the energy barrier and cause a much faster crystallization rate in the heterogeneous nucleation – the corresponding kinetics responsible for such a dramatic change remains fundamentally missing. As a result, the kinetics of heterogeneous nucleation and the fundamental kinetic difference between the homogeneous and heterogeneous nucleation require a better understanding. Using density and refractive-index matched colloidal suspensions, we plan to build a well-controlled crystallization system continuously adjustable from homogeneous to heterogeneous nucleation, and clarify this important issue. We will focus on the following three fundamental subjects: (1) What new physics can the external boundary bring to the precursor structure at the very beginning? (2) Which fundamental change in kinetic pathways is responsible for the dramatic speed-up in the heterogeneous nucleation? (3) What is the essential difference in the density-order correlation between these two types of nucleation? The illumination of these fundamental questions will advance our understanding on the exact kinetics for both homogeneous and heterogeneous nucleation, and provide important information for the research of crystallization. As an expert in studying crystallization with colloidal systems, the applicant has successfully revealed the kinetic pathways of homogeneous nucleation (Nature Physics 10, 73-79, 2014). Based on such a strong background, we now propose this three-year project with a total budget of US$207,060 (HK$1,604,720), to further probe the heterogeneous nucleation, and illustrate the fundamental difference between the homogeneous and heterogeneous nucleation kinetics. 本項目旨在創建可控的膠體結晶系統並利用這一系統來研究異質成核與均質成核結晶動力學，以及它們之間的不同之處。眾所周知，結晶是凝聚態與材料物理中的重要課題。在液體轉變為晶體的過程中，物質的結構和密度都發生了急劇的轉變。經典結晶理論（CNT）只是對這一轉變用熱漲落這一簡單圖像描述，而對它的具體動力學過程卻沒有探討。具體來講，共有兩種速率大不相同的結晶方式：異質成核和均質成核結晶，並且前者的發生機率遠大於後者。它們在結晶動力學路徑中的不同之處仍然沒有好的理解。因此，我們需要在實驗體系中詳細觀測並找到這兩種成核過程的動力學路徑以及機制。使用密度及折射率匹配的膠體系統，我們將創建可控的膠體結晶系統並在單顆粒尺度上測量這兩種結晶路徑，以及闡明它們的不同之處。我們的研究將主要集中在以下兩方面：（1）最初的結晶晶核以及前驅體是如何產生的？（2）什麼原因導致異質成核與均質成核在動力學上的不同？對這些基本問題的研究可以大大提高我們對在單顆粒尺度上對結晶動力學的認識與理解。

14303415.label: Realisation of objectives
14303415.value: (1) For the revised objective 1, we have systematically studied the heterogeneous crystallization and the influence from external boundary. We found that at the beginning of crystallization, there is a layering transition, which forms a spatial order in the dimension perpendicular to the boundary first. After this layering transition, it is much easier to realize order in the parallel plane and form crystalline order in 3D. The layering transition in the perpendicular direction followed by ordering in the parallel plane forms a 2-step crystallization process in heterogeneous crystallization, and one major difference from homogeneous crystallization is the layering transition. Because the layering transition is assisted by external boundary, it has a much lower energy barrier and thus much easier to realize. Moreover, the ordering in the parallel plane is mainly driven by collective motion of particles, which is fast and has low energy cost. This two-step crystallization process assisted by boundary differs significantly from the homogeneous crystallization. These findings are shown in details in Mr. Tang, Shixiang's Mphil thesis, "Revealing Enhanced Growth Rate and Kinetic Pathways in Heterogeneous Nucleation by Colloidal Systems". Moreover, in order for the external boundary to assist crystallization, wetting the boundary is the first and important step. Therefore, understanding how the external boundary can get wet by another material is crucial. To address this crucial question, we studied a droplet wetting atomically-smooth boundary at different conditions. We found that when the wetting condition is symmetric, it takes a very long time to realize wetting; however, when the symmetry is broken by gravity or slight motions, the wetting can be realized much faster. This finding is published in Phys. Rev. X. 7, 021036, 2017. (2) For the revised objective 2, we have directly visualized the kinetic pathways from liquid to layered structures, as well as from precursors to solid structures. In the first transition from liquid to layered structures, we discovered a bottle neck in the statistics during transition kinetics, which indicates the existence of an energy barrier. However, in the second transition from layered structure (or precursors) to solid structures there is no bottle neck. Therefore, the major barrier of the kinetics is the layering transition. We have also studied all possible kinetic pathways, both within the same symmetry and across different symmetries, and revealed that the pathway strengths are consistent with the final stable state: the pathway towards the stable state is relatively stronger compared with other pathways. Therefore, the kinetic pathways are of thermodynamic origin. The details of these findings are shown in Mr. Tang, Shixiang's Mphil thesis "Revealing Enhanced Growth Rate and Kinetic Pathways in Heterogeneous Nucleation by Colloidal Systems". In addition to these pathways, the kinetic pathways during the relaxation of crystals are also very important to understand material rigidity and plasticity. To address this important issue, we have studied these pathways in a system with different shaped particles. We found that the relaxation pathways rely predominantly on the 'internal roughness' produced by particle locations and particle shapes. In particular, a novel relaxation mechanism via defect loop, which typically appears in quasicrystals, surprisingly occurs in the crystal structure of triangle particles. These findings are published in Nature Communications 10, 1737, 2019, as well as in Dr. Shen, Hongchuan's PhD thesis “Using Granular Model Systems to Study Structures and Collective Motions of Non-Equilibrium Condensed Matter".

14303415.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303415.value: (1) To systematically study the heterogeneous crystallization and the influence from external boundary, we use confocal microscopy and colloidal systems to probe the kinetics at single-particle level. We found that at the beginning of crystallization, there is a layering transition, which forms a spatial order in the dimension perpendicular to the boundary first. After this layering transition, it is much easier to realize order in the parallel plane and form crystalline order in 3D. The layering transition in the perpendicular direction followed by ordering in the parallel plane forms a unique 2-step crystallization process in heterogeneous crystallization. Moreover, the kinetic pathways are of thermodynamic origin. These findings are shown in details in Mr. Tang, Shixiang's Mphil thesis in 2018: "Revealing Enhanced Growth Rate and Kinetic Pathways in Heterogeneous Nucleation by Colloidal Systems". (2) To understand the kinetic pathways in relaxation, we have studied the relaxation in different shaped particles. We revealed distinct pathways determined by the "internal roughness". Even beyond the thermodynamic systems, we studied the collective motions in non-equilibrium systems and probes the mobility's influence on particle collective motions. We found a high similarity between the mobility disorder and spatial disorder, which suggests a promising possibility of extending the equilibrium analysis to nonequilibrium systems with collective modes. These interesting findings are shown in Dr. Shen, Hongchuan's PhD thesis in 2017: "Using Granular Model Systems to Study Structures and Collective Motions of Non-Equilibrium Condensed Matter". (3) To illustrate how the external boundary can get wet by another material, we studied a droplet wetting atomically-smooth boundary at different conditions. We found that when the wetting condition is symmetric, it takes a very long time to realize wetting; however, when the symmetry is broken by gravity or slight motions, the wetting can be realized much faster. This finding is published in Phys. Rev. X. 7, 021036, 2017. (4) To understand the kinetic pathways in relaxation process, we have studied relaxation pathways in a system with different shaped particles. We found that the relaxation pathways rely predominantly on the 'internal roughness' produced by particle locations and particle shapes. In particular, a novel relaxation mechanism via defect loop, which typically appears in quasicrystals, surprisingly occurs in the crystal structure of triangle particles. These findings are published in Nature Communications 10, 1737, 2019.

14303415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303415.value: By understanding the heterogeneous nucleation especially the boundary's role in the process, we obtain a better idea of layering transition prior to the nucleation. Because this layering transition is induced by the boundary, we may design functional boundary conditions to either facilitate or hinder the layering effect, and thus achieve a controlled heterogeneous nucleation.

14303415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303415.value: Crystallization is an important process in condensed matter physics and materials science. As liquid changes into solid, evolutions in both symmetry and density take place. In particular, there are two primary crystallization approaches: the homogeneous and heterogeneous crystallization, which have very different nucleation rates even under the same pressure and temperature. In our daily life, the most common approach is heterogeneous crystallization. To understand this important process, we have used colloids as a model system to study the heterogeneous crystallization assisted by an external boundary. We experimentally revealed that the layering transition in the perpendicular direction followed by ordering in the parallel plane forms a unique 2-step crystallization process in heterogeneous crystallization. Moreover, the kinetic pathways are of thermodynamic origin. These important findings should advance our understanding on the exact kinetics for heterogeneous nucleation, and provide important information for the research of crystallization.

14303515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303515.value: Stimuli-responsive gelating materials are compounds that can undergo gel-to-sol transitions in the presence of an external stimulus other than the traditional changes of solvent environment or temperature. This type of functional molecules is of special interest as sensing materials or drug delivery agents. This project seeks to design and synthesize a class of oligomeric/polymeric physical gelation compounds that will show restorable, stimuli-responsive properties towards triggering agents such as redox reagents, light irradiation and host-guest decomplexation conditions. The mechanistic basis of the gel-to-sol transition of such materials will be rationalized and the potential advantages of using an oligomeric/polymeric-based gelation system, such as enhanced host-guest binding sensitivity, will also be investigated. 刺激响应型凝胶是在外界刺激而非传统的改变溶剂环境或温度的条件下可以从凝胶转变成溶液状态的一种材料。这种功能材料在传感器或药物缓释方面有非常有趣的应用。本项目旨在设计和合成一系列的寡聚/高分子物理凝胶，这些化合物在氧化还原剂、光照或主客体分离等引发条件下将会显示出还原和刺激响应的性质。我们将对凝胶–溶液状态的转变机制进行解释，并且将对寡聚/高分子凝胶在诸如加强主客体相互作用的灵敏度等方面的应用前景进行探索。

14303515.label: Realisation of objectives
14303515.value: 1. Objectives 1 and 2: Two series of (amide-triazole) receptors 1–4 and 5–7 bearing different spacer length [–(CH2)nAr(CH2)n–, n = 1–4 respectively] between the two receptor sites were prepared (see Appendix Figure 1 for chemical structures). Each of these dimeric compounds possesses two anion binding motifs (shown in red) that are made up of two amide NH protons and two triazole CH protons. These compounds serve as simple models for the study of the anion binding properties of their corresponding polymeric analogs. One important goal of this work is to examine whether there is any cooperativity in the successive binding of the two guest anions. The binding stoichiometries and affinities (K1 and K2) of these host molecules to different halide anions (Cl– and Br–) were determined by 1H-NMR Job plot and titration experiments. The results are summarized below: (a) The Job plot of compounds 1, 3, 4, 5 and 7 indicated a 1:2 (host:anion) binding stoichiometry, while that of 2 and 6 was 1:1. However, poor residual analysis results were obtained when fitting the 1H NMR titration data of compounds 2 and 6 using the 1:1 binding model, suggesting that there was something wrong with the 1:1 binding stoichiometry as suggested by the Job plot. Incidentally, the 1H NMR titration curve of 2 and 6 was also very different from that of the rest. (b) Excellent residual analysis results were obtained when fitting the 1H NMR titration data of all compounds using the full 1:2 binding model (Thordarson. P., Chem. Soc. Rev. 2010, 40. 1305). Hence, the two stepwise association constants (K1 and K2) were determined based on this model. (c) The binding data indicated that negative cooperativity was found in all cases, i.e. binding of the first anion suppressed binding of the second. The interaction parameter (alpha), an indicator of the binding cooperativity (i.e. alpha > 1, = 1, and < 1 mean positive, no and negative cooperativity respectively) for compounds 1, 3, 4, 5 and 7 were in the range of 0.28‒0.91. More strikingly, the figures for compounds 2 and 6 were 0.03‒0.05, suggesting that binding of the first anion drastically suppressed the binding of the second anion in the latter cases. This then explained why the apparent Job plot result of compounds 2 and 6 was 1:1. Incidentally, compounds 2 and 6 both possess ethylene spacers in the structures. We therefore speculated that the observed effect must be due to this unique structural feature. Based on theoretical computation, it was found that the ethylene spacer allowed the central aromatic proton (H8) to orient in a favorable position, in addition to the triazole and amide moieties, to interact with the chloride in compound 6 (see Appendix Figure 2). This wrapped conformation then prevented binding of the second anion as the two binding sites became very close to each other. On the other hand, for the methylene and propylene linkers in compounds 5 and 7, respectively, failed to adopt such a folded conformation and hence the second anion binding was not greatly suppressed. (d) Overall we did not succeed in designing a dimeric (amide-triazole) model compound that can exhibit positive cooperativity binding of anions. Nonetheless, the results indicated that structural factors can significantly affect the host guest properties of multivalent host systems. It is believed that additional designs should be attempted by further changing the structural parameters of the molecules. 2. Objectives 3 and 4: (a) A photoresponsive polymer 8 bearing multiple azobenzene units along the polymer backbone was prepared by click polymerization of a monomer 9 (see Appendix Figure 3). The trans-form polymer was found to be an excellent physical organogelator in a wide variety of aromatic solvents with a minimum gelation concentration (mgc) of <1% w/v. This work represented the first polymer physical gel bearing photoresponsive units along the polymer main chain. Although incorporation of photo-responsive unit(s) within the polymer main chain have been reported, but none of them showed any organogelating properties. It is believed that such a structural design could produce a much more efficient photomechanical effect. As the photo-responsive functionalities are resided on the polymer backbone, thereby the photo-induced isomerization process could lead to significant conformational and molecular packing changes. Hence, the sol-gel reversibility property may become very facile. In fact, the synthesized polymer gel exhibited reversible photoinduced cis-trans isomerization, which was accompanied with reversible sol-gel transition. For example, the polymer gel could be turned into a solution upon UV irradiation after 1 h, and can be reverted back to the gel form after visible light irradiation. The gelation mechanism, gel morphology and the gel strength were also investigated by infra-red spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy and bulk rheology. (b) In another development towards polymer gels with host-guest complexation property, two isomeric polyacylhydrazine-based polymer gels 10 and 11 were prepared by dynamic covalent chemistry. The syntheses were very efficient and the polymers could be obtained in ~90% yield with molecular weights >100 kD. The products were fully characterized by NMR spectroscopy and size exclusion chromatography. Due to the presence of aromatic moieties and intramolecular hydrogen bonds in the polymer backbone, both polymers exhibited very high crystallinity. The polymers were found to be strong physical gelators for aromatic solvents with mgc down to 1% w/v. Upon interacting with metal ions, the two polymers demonstrated different responsive properties such as gel-to-sol transition, gel strength reinforcement, and/or quenching/enhancement of fluorescence intensity. Specifically, polymer gel 11 turned into a sol while the gel strength of polymer gel 10 was significantly enhanced in the presence of Al3+, Fe3+, Fe2+ and Cu2+ ions. Based on solid-state NMR and powder X-ray diffraction studies, the metal ion binding mechanisms were elucidated and a model was proposed to rationalize the difference in their metal ion-responsive properties. This work showed that these crystalline polyacylhydrazone polymers possess very rich supramolecular and stimuli-responsive properties. (c) Finally, we also investigated the use of ferrocene functionality to prepare several redox-responsive polymers bearing ferrocene units on the main chain using click chemistry. Unfortunately, the polymers did not show any gelation ability and therefore no further study was pursued.
