14303515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303515.value: 1. In this research work we aim to develop polymer gelating materials that are capable of sensing various environmental triggers such as metal ions, photons and redox active reagents by embedding the various sensing elements inside the polymer backbone. This structural design possesses one specific advantage in that the sensing units are located in the backbone, thereby any triggering effect could lead to multiple local conformational and molecular packing changes along the polymer backbone and therefore should facilitate the gel-sol transformation than having the sensing units resided on the side chains. More importantly, if the change in the first sensing unit can amplify the effect of the following sensing unit, the overall macroscopic change can be significantly amplified. 2. Two series of oligo(triazole-amide) compounds bearing two anion receptor sites were prepared in order to examine their anion binding cooperativity. As it turned out, for all compounds synthesized, binding of the first anion suppressed binding of the second. Hence no positive allosteric binding effect could be observed. Despite this setback, it was noted that structural factors did produce a very important effect on the binding properties of the resulting host molecules. It was found that the two compounds that bear ethylene linkers in their structure were found to be nearly devoid of binding strength towards the second anion. 3. One photoresponsive polymer gelator was designed and synthesized. The polymer gel showed responsive gel-sol transitions upon UV/visible light irradiation. The result of the work was published in Chem. Commun. 4. Two isomeric polyacylhydrazone-based polymer gels were designed and prepared. Both polymers were shown to be excellent gelators for aromatic solvents. The polymer gels also exhibited metal ion responsive gel-sol transition, modulation of gel strength and photophysical fluroscence enhancement/quenching properties. Despite their structural similarity, they showed very different responsive properties towards Al3+, Fe3+, Fe2+ and Cu2+ ions. The result of this work has been written up and ready for submission for publication. A copy of the manuscript is attached with this report. 5. Attempts to design and prepare redox responsive polymer gelators using the ferrocene functionality failed as the resulting polymers did not show any gelation properties despite several structural modifications. 6. Two PhD students were trained and graduated by working on this project.

14303515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303515.value: In the first part of this research, we planned to develop dimeric host systems that can exhibit positive binding cooperativity towards anions, but negative cooperativity was actually observed. The design of positive cooperativity systems, such as those occurred in nature (binding of oxygen to hemoglobin) is one key area that needs to be further investigated. We believed that the charged nature of the guest molecule also played a role here, as like charges repel each other. Instead of anion binding, we should develop host molecules that bind to electrically neutral molecules and this should give a higher chance of success. In terms of goals achieved, we developed one photoresponsive polymer physical gel and two metal-ion responsive polymer physical gels. Both of them underwent reversible gel-to-sol transitions upon interacting with photons or metal-ions. Nonetheless, the response time was still too slow. For example, the photoresponsive polymer gel reported by us changed to sol after 1 h of UV light irradiation. Ideally this process should be speeded up to within seconds. There are ways to solve this problem. For example, introducing additional electron donating or electron withdrawing groups on the azobenzene units could facilitate a rapid transition.

14303515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303515.value: In this research project we developed two different class of polymer gelators that can freeze aromatic solvents to form gels. In addition, they are capable of sensing photons and metal-ions. Instead of using complicated analytical instrument to analyse the process, the solid like gel polymer material visually turns into a solution upon the trigger effect. Furthermore, when the external trigger is removed, the solution can be reverted back into the solid like gel form. Hence this kind of polymer physical gels are very useful sensing materials for analysis of environmental contaminants such as metal-ions.

14303715.label: Project Objectives
14303715.value: To employ the integration of total internal reflection microscopy (TIRM) with video microscopy (VM) methods to measure how bare particles interact with glass surfaces when they are exposed to a physiological environment of high protein concentration, such as fetal bovine serum (FBS). To synthesise the three most commonly studied anti-fouling polymer coatings: poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG), poly[oligo(ethylene glycol) methyl methacrylate] [poly(OEGMA)], and poly(sulfobetaine methacrylate) [poly(SBMA)]. To characterise the surface properties of these polymer coatings as functions of thickness and grafting density by laser light scattering, zeta potential, water contact angle, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and ellipsometry measurements. 14303715.label: Realisation of objectives
14303715.value: There are five objectives in this project and the details of the realization related to each objective are as follows: 1. To employ the integration of total internal reflection microscopy (TIRM) with video microscopy (VM) methods to measure how bare particles interact with glass surfaces when they are exposed to a physiological environment of high protein concentration, such as fetal bovine serum (FBS). We investigated advancing the technique by integration of TIRM with VM that enabled monitoring single and multi-particles’ simultaneous interaction with the surfaces. We showed that the incorporation of VM resulted in the ensemble average calculation situate in eliminating the heterogeneity of particle size, reducing the measurement time duration and generating more statistical information. More importantly, we have also solved the overlooked blooming problem when applying TIRM-VM in accurate image acquisition. A correction method was developed to deduce the real intensity from the experimental measurement which was further confirmed by the accordance between the corresponding potential energy profiles and the Derjaguin, Landau, Verway, and Overbeek (DLVO) theory. 2. To synthesise the three most commonly studied anti-fouling polymer coatings: poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG), poly[oligo(ethylene glycol) methyl methacrylate] [poly(OEGMA)], and poly(sulfobetaine methacrylate) [poly(SBMA)]. This will be achieved by grafting polymer brushes with different thicknesses and grafting densities on glass substrates using surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerisation (SI-ATRP). We have synthesized more than three most commonly studied anti-fouling polymer brush layers including, hydrophilic PEG and poly(OEGMA), as well as zwitterionic polymers of poly(SBMA) and poly(carboxybetaine methacrylate) poly(CBMA) with different thickness and graft densities by surface-initiated atom transfer radical polymerization (SI-ATRP) to construct functional surfaces and examine protein-surface interactions in a serum environment. We showed that the thickness of the POEGMA brush layers could be well controlled by the polymerization time and density of the immobilized initiators. 3. To characterise the surface properties of these polymer coatings as functions of thickness and grafting density by laser light scattering, zeta potential, water contact angle, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), atomic force microscopy (AFM), and ellipsometry measurements. We have characterized the surface properties of the above four different polymer coatings at the glass surfaces, such as chain length, grafting density and the surface morphology by laser light scattering (DLS), zeta potential, XPS, AFM, and ellipsometry measurements. The results of DLS and ellipsometer measurements indicated that all four different polymer surfaces were adsorbed with a layer of serum protein when they were dispersed in the blood serum. Also, the AFM images indicated that for short POEGMA brush layer or polymer chain with low grafting density, a thick layer of proteins was adsorbed to the surface, but the adsorption of proteins was considerably reduced as the thickness of polymer brush increased. Then, we directly quantified the magnitude and range of the non-specific interaction between the particles/protein-decorated particles and glass surfaces functionalized with the above mentioned antifouling polymer brushes in a serum environment. 4. To quantitatively measure the non-specific interactions of particles, or protein-decorated particles, with these anti-fouling surfaces in FBS so as to understand how surface properties, such as chain length, grafting density, surface charge, and morphology influence the binding of plasma proteins to polymer-functionalised surfaces. TIRM-VM was firstly used to measure the interaction forces between three different kinds of macroscopic surfaces: namely bare polystyrene (PS) particle and bare silica surface (bare-PS/bare-silica), PS particle and silica surfaces both coated with bovine serum albumin (BSA) (BSA-PS/BSA-silica), and PS particle and silica surfaces both modified with polyethylene glycol (PEG) (PEG-PS/PEG-silica) polymers, in a FBS solution. The quantitative measurement by TIRM indicates that serum proteins adsorbed onto surfaces can regulate surface-surface interactions, thus leading to unique moving behavior and stability of colloidal particles in the serum conditions. TIRM-VM was also applied to quantitatively analyzed the dependence of the POEGMA brush layer thickness and grafting density on interaction forces between protein-coated particles and swollen polymer layers formed at the surface in the serum condition. The potential energy profiles analysis revealed that adsorbed protein layer on both surfaces could contribute to mediate the interaction forces between the surfaces by exerting bridging effect caused by heterogeneous patches or steric repulsion caused by a homogeneous coverage. If the surfaces were not fully covered by polymer coating, proteins in serum could directly interact with the material surface to form an adsorbed layer, bridging was likely to occur under this condition. However, for surfaces fully coved by POEGMA brushes, POEGMA surface was effectively against serum proteins. In this condition, the attractive interaction between both surfaces were avoided and the adsorbed protein layer on PS surface could only offer steric repulsions, thus particles underwent freely moving behaviors. We finally studied the interactions between bovine serum albumin (BSA) and two sorts of polymer brushes including zwitterionic poly(carboxybetaine methacrylate) (PCBMA) and hydrophilic POEGMA in NaCl aqueous solutions directly by TIRM-VM. Our results indicated both the surface charge and brushes length can affect protein adsorption through electrostatic and steric repulsions respectively. Both PCBMA- and POEGMA-coated surfaces display negative charge properties due to incomplete coverage. As a result, strong electrostatic repulsions between proteins and negatively charged polymer-coated surfaces could contribute to resist protein-coated particles in solutions with low ionic strength (0.1, 0.5 and 1 mM) and disappear in solutions with high ionic strength (10 mM). The measured interaction profiles demonstrate that PCBMA brushes could only provide apparent steric forces in high ionic strength (10 mM) where zwitterionic brushes exhibit a relatively extended conformation with a lack of electrostatic forces between intra- and inter-polymers. In contrast, the steric repulsion between proteins and POEGMA brushes appears when particles diffuse at low positions in all salt concentrations (0.1-10 mM) with similar steric decay lengths, which results from the unresponsiveness of POEGMA brushes to the salt stimulus. 5. To extend this technique for monitoring the protein-decorated particles interacting with the anti-fouling polymer surfaces that are further coupled with bioactive molecules such as lysine (for plasminogen binding) or collagen (for cell adhesion) in FBS so as to understand the main driving forces occurring between surface-immbilised bioactive molecules and proteins in the physiological environment. We studied the interactions between biomolecules such as fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) and PEG modified monolayer surface (PEG SAM) in solutions with different ionic strengths. We showed that in low ionic strength solution, strong electrostatic attractions between PS-silica-FITC particles and PEG500 SAMs were detected even though both bodies were negatively charged. The origin of the attractive force was the charge correlations between the heterogeneous surfaces. In high ionic strength, the electrostatic attractions were completely screened, only left with the van der Waals attractions between the PS-silica-FITC particles and PEG SAMs. The phenomenon can be explained by the mechanism of biomolecular resistance, including steric repulsion and hydration shell. The energy penalty of small molecule is much less than that of large biomolecule while penetrating into the PEG layers. This work reveals that the PEG SAMs not only fail to prevent the non-specific binding of FITC molecules, but also attract the fluorophores through van der Waals interactions.

14303715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303715.value: This research project has been successfully accomplished by our group. A series of anti-fouling layers were synthesized and characterized so as to construct smart functional surfaces for quantifying protein adsorption and deposition in complicate physiological media. This project has generated a total of 7 high-quality publications in the colloidal and polymer science filed and trained 2 PhD and 1 MPhil students. The main findings are summarized as follows: 1. We showed that when particles and silica surfaces were exposed in the blood serum, all surfaces were adsorbed with a layer of serum protein. The interaction potentials between the particle and surface exhibited both free-diffusing particles and stuck particle profiles, indicating that the adsorbed serum proteins can mediate the particle-surface interactions (Langmuir, 2016). 2. We studied the dependence of the POEGMA brush layer thickness on protein adsorption by measuring the interaction forces between protein-coated particles and polymer layers coated at the surface in the serum condition. We showed that the possibility of protein-coated particles sticking to the polymer brush layer surface greatly decreased as the thickness of the polymer brush increased. The potential energy profiles analysis revealed that such an adsorbed protein layer on both surfaces could contribute to mediate the interaction forces between the surfaces by either exerting a bridging effect or steric repulsion (Colloid and Surfaces: Biointerfaces 2017). 3. We studied the interactions between BSA-coated particles and the surfaces grafted by PCBMA and POEGMA brushes respectively in various ionic strengths by TIRM-VM. The quantitative measurements provided some insights into the protein resistance of polyzwitterionic and nonionic polymers. High ionic strength is necessary for polyzwitterionic polymer to provide adequate steric repulsion, while nonionic polymer is not influenced by the salt concentration of good solution (Langmuir 2018). 4. We have solved the overlooked blooming problem when applying TIRM-VM in accurate image acquisition. A correction method was developed to deduce the real intensity from the experimental measurement (Journal of Colloidal and Interface Science 2017). 5. We also explored measuring the interactions between particles and surfaces in both equilibrium and non-equilibrium systems. We demonstrated that the diffusion coefficient perpendicular to the surface could be obtained, and that this could then be used to determine the interaction forces acting on the Brownian particle (Langmuir 2019). 6. We further developed TIRM incorporated with a magnetic tweezer to study the time-resolved gelation dynamics of 4-arm PEG hydrogels near overlapped concentration via the dynamic scaling theory (Macromolecules, 2019).

14303715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303715.value: In this project, we have demonstrated the successful application of the TIRM-VM technique to measuring the dynamic behavior and stability of particles in a complex biological environment. However, our method continued to rely on sampling the Brownian motion of particles under equilibrium conditions. To overcome this limitation, in future, we need to explore measuring the interactions between particles and functional surfaces in both equilibrium and non-equilibrium systems. In principle, if we can track the real non-equilibrium process of multi-particle deposition onto a polymer-functionalized surface, we can resolve short range particle–surface of particles with diameters down to 100 nm. The quantitative measurements of short particle–surface separation with diameters down to 100 nm is very important, as many colloidal and biomedical products reside in this range. Therefore, the further development of TIRM-VM measurement in the non-equilibrium system not only will establish a powerful technique enabling characterization of nanoparticle–surface interactions, but also will contribute important knowledge concerning the design of functional nanocargoes with optimal cell targeting and drug delivery.

14303715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303715.value: Quite frequently both in vitro and in vivo studies show that non-specific protein adsorption and deposition occurs within seconds on biomedical devices, such as implants. This results in the changes to the surface properties which may subsequently promote undesirable inflammation, anaphylaxis, and thrombosis. Although considerable progress has been made over the last few decades, the ideal surface of which both suppression of non-specific protein adsorption and promotion of specific protein adsorption, has yet to be found. The main reason is that the underlying principles of the protein adsorption to polymer-functionalized surfaces in the biological fluids are poorly understood. This project has successfully demonstrated the combination of total international reflection microscopy (TIRM) with video microscopy (VM) to quantitatively measure the interactions of these functional surfaces with particles or protein-decorated particles in complicate physiological media. We discovered the correlation of protein-coated particles sticking to the polymer brush layer surfaces with the polymer property, thickness and grafting density. The study improves our fundamental understanding of the forces responsible for protein adsorption and deposition in highly complex media, and provides an empirical guideline to the design of the next generation of functionalized membranes and surfaces for the biomedical implants and drug delivery systems.

14303815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303815.value: 天然產物在新藥發現中占有十分重要的地位，天然產物除了可以直接作為藥物使用外，以其相關的先導物為模板，進行結構修飾，最終將其開發成藥效更優良的藥物，是藥物開發的一條捷徑。進化和物種之間的競爭期間，自然選擇已經產生得到更好的效果的藥物，也就是具有良好生物活性的天然產物。化學合成天然產物及其類似物已經為新藥研發的重要工具。不幸的是，自然界，天然化合物僅在非常低量的存在於自然界中，所以它的有限量，不利於對它進行一個完整的生理評估。如果發現這類天然產物是有效的藥物，其缺乏可用的量將是一個顯著阻礙它們在藥物研發中的進一步發展。因此，化學合成可以通過合成適量的天然產物及其類似物去解決這個問題。此外，化學合成可以在天然產物和類似物的研究的基礎上提出發現的特殊的活性結構，然後用於修改相關的結構，最終有利於改善其活性或引導分子的其他物理化學/生物特性的最終目的。 在本項目中，我們的主要集中研究全合成天然產物vindoline（一类臨床抗癌藥物長春鹼 的一部分），以及vandrikine的全合成及其多樣性的合成研究。值得注意的是，vindoline和vandrikine的生物學研究是用於抑制微管的形成和有絲分裂，今天仍然被視為用於治療癌症的非常成功的藥物靶標之一。vindoline和vandrikine並由於其自然稀缺性，加上其特殊的分子結構，重要的生物學特性，使它們作為有非常吸引力的合成目標。 這項研究的長期目標是從vindoline和vandrikine發展高效的抗癌藥物或發現其他線索，以此開展相關藥物分子設計，通過化學合成，進一步研究相關分子的生物學與模仿生物開發新藥。 通過有機合成製備vindoline，發展相關高效策略和方法，可以用於製備多樣性的相關天然產物類似物。通過進行模擬生物合成，挖掘vindoline的其他分子結構和vandrikine的生物活性與結構的關係；實現vindoline和vandrikine及其類似物的全合成研究和相關的醫藥研發。 此外，在本項目中，天然產物或類似結構的天然产物或其他类似物的多樣性也將協助我們發展相關“天然產品医药'庫。 总之，希望本项目能夠通过天然產物的合成研究最終发现更優良的藥物，推動香港的藥物開發與研發。

14303815.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303815.value: Naturally occurring alkaloid molecules have been used medicinally since the 19th century, and many still remain as important drugs nowadays because of their activities against a large variety of diseases. In continuation of our research projects in total syntheses of naturally occurring molecules, we have targeted Aspidosperma and Kopsia alkaloids with intriguing structures and important biological activities. In this project, we have completed the total syntheses of Aspidosperma and Kopsia alkaloids (–)-deoxoapodine, (–)-kopsifoline D and (–)-beninine through a novel domino deprotection-Michael addition-nucleophilic substitution protocol to assemble the core framework in efficient steps. These syntheses involved a cascade reaction to furnish the tricyclic aminoketone, a bio-inspired transannular cyclization to access the bridged carbocycle. Furthermore, Corey-Bakshi-Shibata reduction was employed to afford the crucial intermediate with an enantio-enriched stereocenter for the total synthesis of these molecules. The chirality from Corey-Bakshi-Shibata reduction was shown to completely transfer to the backbone using Johnson-Claisen rearrangement.

14303815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303815.value: Our strategy should open up practical avenues for the total synthesis of structurally similar alkaloids. Application of these synthetic strategies for syntheses of other indole alkaloids and relevant biological evaluation is ongoing in our laboratory.

14303815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303815.value: We accomplished the total syntheses of three structurally diverse alkaloids bearing fused or bridged skeletons, namely, (-)-deoxoapodine (12 steps, 1.8% overall), (-)-kopsifoline D (12 steps, 1.1% overall) and (-)-beninine (13 steps, 2.6% overall), through a domino deprotection-Michael addition-nucleophilic substitution protocol for the assembly of the core framework in efficient steps. These syntheses involved a cascade reaction to furnish the tricyclic aminoketone, a bio-inspired transannular cyclization to access the bridged carbocycle, enantioselective Corey-Bakshi-Shibata reduction to generate enantioenriched common intermediate, and Johnson-Claisen rearrangement to construct the quaternary carbon stereocenter. Application of these synthetic strategies for syntheses of other indole alkaloids and relevant biological evaluation is ongoing in our laboratory.

14303915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303915.value: When the number of securities (p) is larger than the number of observation times (n), the optimal portfolio strategies may fail due to the huge estimation error. While there have been many statistical approaches for such a situation, all of them are constructed for single-period portfolio strategy. In addition, existing framework concentrates on improving the estimation of model parameters. This project aims to propose a novel combined estimation-optimization (CEO) framework which concentrates on estimating effective parameters appearing in the solution of the optimal trading strategy so that the number of estimating parameters is much reduced. The CEO approach is applicable to single-period, multi-period and continuous-time portfolio strategies. The project will establish theories to prove the pitfalls of the plug-in approach which directly substitutes estimated parameters into the optimal portfolio solution. Meanwhile, it shows the advantages of the CEO approach. Simulation and empirical studies will be conducted to examine the practical use and the validity of the proposed approach. 在運用投資組合理論時，現實情況往往遇上參數估計的誤差問題。當投資組合裏的股票數目增加時，情況更為嚴重並大大影響投資收益。現行方法只能改善單一週期的投資。本研究提出嶄新的高維統計方法用作動態（即多週期的）投資組合。我們用數學證明出以往的運作方法所造成的投資損失，並證明這些新方法有效漸近真正的最優投資法。而且這些方法對高維投資組合特別有效。本研究也以模擬和現實數據分析其體驗用處及優勢。

14303915.label: Realisation of objectives
14303915.value: Since we prepared the research proposal, my PhD student and I had already started the investigation. We only got very limit preliminary results until the release of the GRF result in June 2015. Although Objective 1 was realized as a journal article [No.4 research output] published in 2019, the idea and some preliminary results were presented by my PhD student in the INFORM conference in December 2015 for soliciting comments and feedbacks from the academic community. He won the best student paper award (the first place prize). This was the first time that the award went to an Asian Institutions. Past winners were from Stanford, Columbia, CMU, MIT alike. The PhD thesis of my student won the Bruti Liberati Prize for the best PhD thesis in quantitative finance. This prize is conferred by the Bachelier Finance Society, the largest international society in Financial Mathematics and Engineering. Therefore, he got a tenure-track Assistant professorship from Nanyang Technological University immediately after he graduated in mid 2016. This good news however generated difficulty to me because I initially wrote the GRF for hiring him as my postdoc or research associate. As it was really difficult to find a replacement, I then invited my MPhil student and an undergraduate student to participate into this project for computer programming and data cleansing. I have to train them the basic theory and computer programming skills. As the GRF funding is only for two years, I also invited that former PhD student to visit me regularly in Hong Kong. This explains why the publication from Objective 1 appeared after other publications. The undergraduate student became my MPhil student in the following year. Therefore, I hired several undergraduate students to continue her work and develop software for the later development. Objective 2 was realized as three journal articles [No.1 - No.3 research outputs]. These articles came out early because the mathematical proofs based on continuous-time processes were probably more familiar by the literature and the referees. In particular, No.2 output has accumulated 16 citations (Scopus) since its publication in 2017. All these research outputs include comprehensive empirical studies. I also invited my early former PhD student (different from the aforementioned one) to participate in No.3 output. She has been equipped with statistical methods for financial data analysis. The aforementioned publications detailed the numerical algorithm and offered comprehensive empirical studies so that objectives 3 and 5 were achieved. In particular, the numerical algorithm has been converted into software which has been implemented by an asset management firm (non-disclosure of details about the firm). This will be realized as an impact case for RAE2020 to RGC by the end of 2020. More details can be found upon the release of the RAE results. Objective 4 was realized as two research outputs [No.5 and No.6]. While the result in No.5 focuses on the risk calculation, No.6 [the under review (R&R) article] extends our concept to the portfolio selection problem with constraints. The results mentioned above were presented at academic conferences detailed below either by myself or my graduate students.

14303915.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303915.value: Major findings of this project include theory for sparse portfolio selection and the corresponding data-driven computational scheme. The key idea is to combine the estimation into the optimization (CEO) procedure and the norm 1 minimization is found to be a useful approach to realize the CEO procedure and obtain sparse portfolios. We show that our norm-1 minimization, which involves cross-validation (a kind of machine-learning method), can effectively solve the degeneracy problem for high-dimensional portfolios in both continuous-time models (No1-No3 outputs in Part C) and a general discrete-time model with a wide range of distributions (No.4). For portfolios with constraints (No.6) and different risk measures (No. 5), we show how results in this project contribute to simulation algorithms with certain convergence analysis. An important economic implication from this project is a revision to the notion of diversification. Classic understanding of diversification is to include as much as possible risky assets into the portfolio. It is true when the model for risky asset processes is free of estimation error. As estimation error is always there, our result shows that investors should avoid putting all their eggs into a single basket but also not all baskets as well. One should select several good stocks to invest and the selection can be based on a data-driven machine-learning procedure consistent with existing portfolio theories.

14303915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303915.value: Although this project considers a reasonably general asset dynamics, serially-dependent dynamics such as autoregressive and GARCH models are not developed. It is a promising future direction. In addition, the computational procedure considered did not capture some market frictions such as transaction cost and position limits. This is definitely wealth to investigate further. Finally, if the concept is applied to high-frequency data, then it is possibly enhanced with recent deep-learning techniques.

14303915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303915.value: Big-data and machine learning techniques are useful for practical investment. This project shows how these techniques can effectively filter out stocks with too much estimation errors. Therefore, optimal investment portfolio is diversified but does not necessarily include all stocks. This project provides a novel procedure to select stocks through a data-driven procedure that incorporates machine learning advantages. Results from this project have won several awards and been implemented by an asset management firm.

14304015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304015.value: Multi-component bosons may condense in an unconventional fashion, in which any boson needs to form a pair with a partner before the condensation could occur in these pairs. Whereas pair condensates exhibit novel properties absent in ordinary systems and have been studied extensively in theory, they have not been realized in experiments. The main obstacle is the instability of pair condensates against perturbations. It is challenging to access in laboratories extreme experimental parameters, such as degenerate single-particle ground states and sufficiently strong interactions, for stabilizing pair condensates at the ground state. In this project, we will study a new approach for realizing and exploring pair condensates using well-controlled quantum dynamical evolutions in optical lattices. Recent experimental developments have demonstrated an exciting opportunity of populating bosons in two bands of an optical lattice with a long coherence time. Despite the fact that such a state is not an eigenstate of the system, its dynamical evolution is entirely controlled by the pairing tunneling induced by inter-band interaction, which enhances the correlation between pairs of particles, instead of single particles. This provides physicists a unique scheme to dynamically access a pair condensate as a consequence of the quantum evolution so that the unstable issues at the ground state are no longer relevant. By studying the quantum dynamics of a variety of initial states that occupy more than one band in an optical lattice, we will not only search for the optimal parameters for accessing the pair condensates in experiments, but also explore the underlying physics behind the quantum many-body dynamics governed by strong paring tunneling, instead of the conventional single-particle tunneling, a non-trivial theoretical problem that has not been systematically investigated before. The techniques we will adopt, including analytical effective models and numerical methods, such as exact diagonalization and time-evolving block decimation algorithm in one dimension, are suitable for studying such dynamical problems. The outcome of this project is directly relevant to experiments. An experimental group at Peking University has expressed interest in testing our theoretical predictions. Our results will also have impact on current experimental studies of shaken lattices. On the theoretical side, this project will shed light on a number of fundamental questions regarding the dynamical macroscopic quantum phenomena, such as the interplay between the single- and two-particle correlations in quantum many-body dynamics, and the decay and revival of quantum coherence in interacting systems. 多組分玻色子可以通過非常規的方式來實現凝聚。比如，在某些情況下，任何一個波色子都需要先跟一個搭檔形成配對，然後這些波色子對形成“對凝聚體”。儘管“對凝聚體”具有各種特異性能，並已經在理論上被廣泛地研究，它們還沒有在實驗中被實現。這其中主要的障礙是”對凝聚體“作為系統基態的不穩定性。在實驗中很難實現一些極端的參數區間來穩定這些“對凝聚體”，例如簡並的單粒子基態和很強的相互作用。 在這個課題中，我們將研究一種基於光晶格中高度可控的量子動力學演化的新方法來實現”對凝聚體”。在最近的實驗進展里，波色子被佈居在光晶格中的兩個能帶里，並 具有足夠長的相干時間。這樣的狀態不是系統的本征態，它的動力學演化是由相互作用誘導的雙粒子帶間隧穿來控制的。這樣的帶間隧穿會增強雙粒子的關聯，將為物理學​​家提供一種獨特的方案來實現“對凝聚體“。正因為這種方法利用的是動力學過程，基態不穩定性的問題將不再相關。 通過研究佔據雙帶的各種系統初態的量子動力學過程，我們將搜索最佳的參數區間來實現”對凝聚體”，並研究受對隧穿控制的的量子多體動力學背後的物理機制。不同於傳統的單粒子隧穿，這類問題還未被系統地研究。我們將採取包括有效理論，嚴格對角化，時間演化區塊消除法等在內的各種解析和數值的方法。 這個課題跟實驗研究直接相關。北京大學的一個實驗組將測試我們的理論結果。此課題也會幫助對“搖動光晶格”的研究。在理論方面，此課題將提供對宏觀量子動力學現象的理解，例如單粒子和雙粒子關聯的相互作用，以及量子相干性的衰減和復甦。

14304015.label: Realisation of objectives
14304015.value: The original PI of this project was Prof. Qi Zhou, who left for Purdue university in 2016. Before his departure, the investigation was mainly a theoretical one. Later on, the current Hong Kong PI Dajun Wang, an experimentalist, inherited this project. Both PIs are working on ultracold atoms and there are lots of discussion on various possible ways of collaboration before and after Qi Zhou’s departure. The second half of the project is changed to testing some of the theoretical ideas proposed by Prof. Qi Zhou in the CUHK ultracold atom group led by the current PI. Since the start of this grant, we have achieved the following results: 1). For the first part, we have studied theoretically the quantum many-body dynamics for a variety of initial states in an optical lattice, in which the s and p bands (or the s and d bands) are occupied. Both one-body and few-body correlation functions have been explored. We have found out experimental parameter regimes in which a conventional single-particle condensate vanishes, and a pair condensate emerges. A manuscript was prepared on the emergent pair condensate in an optical lattice (arXiv:1711.04105v1). This paper was, however, rejected by a top journal despite a lengthy review process. We are currently trying to improve it for submitting to another journal. The main findings in this work is the role of interaction in the generation of quantum correlations. We find that accompanying the single-particle decoherence, interactions also build up quantum correlations on the two-, three-, and multi-particle levels. Using the quantitative solutions of the quantum dynamics of a condensate occupying two modes, such as two bands of an optical lattice, we find out that such dynamically emergent multi-particle correlations not only reveal how interactions control the quantum coherence of a many-body system in a highly intriguing means, but also evince the rise of exotic fragmented condensates, which are difficult to access at the ground state. We further develop a generic interferometry that can be used in experiments to measure high order correlation functions directly. 2). In the second part, we realized the idea can be tested in a two-species Bose-Einstein condensate mixture with spin degrees of freedom (theoretical work presented in the MPhi thesis of Chan Hon Ming). In such a system, it is possible to make a mixture of heteronuclear spin-1/2 systems, in direct analogous to the two-band system. With the heteronuclear spin-exchange interaction, it was proved that correlation, as well as entanglement between Na and Rb atoms can be generated. It is also possible to realize a fragmentation phase of the heteronuclear system. 3). Such a spinor mixture is uniquely available in the Hong Kong PI’s group. With the previous support from RGC, the Hong Kong PI’s group already demonstrated the coherent spin population oscillation induced by spin exchange interaction between two different atomic species. In a previous experimental work, the Hong Kong PI’s group has demonstrated the spin dynamics induced by the spin-exchange interaction between Na and Rb spinor gases. The starting point of the spin dynamics was a non-equilibrium mixture for of both Rb and Na atoms in their own coherent superposition states . While the spin dynamics is quite fast, the system is not very clear since there are always some atoms from other state left due to the imperfection in the preparation stage, i.e., the system is not really a spin-1/2 mixture. In the new experimental work, to avoid the impurity problem, we decided to start from both Na and Rb atoms in their |F=1, mF=0> state, and explore a different spin exchange process Na|1,0> + Rb|1,0> ↔ Na| 1,1> + Rb| 1,-1>. We note that if not controlled, homonuclear spin dynamics between Rb atoms or Na atoms can also happen. Eventually, this will introduce other states into the system and scramble the purity of the spin mixture. To avoid this, we apply a ~ 1 G magnetic field to suppress the unwanted homonuclear processes while still allow the desired heteronuclear process to happen. We successfully observed the coherent spin oscillation following the selected process. As expected, this process is much slower since the starting point of is a metastable stale. Similar to the previous experiment, the signature of heteronuclear spin exchange is the synchronized population oscillation in different states. We also observe the for short time, the system has only the four states involved and can thus be viewed as a spin-1/2 mixture. 4). According to the theory, correlation and coherence will build up along with the spin dynamics. To extract the correlations, one needs to apply various ways of controlling the spin dynamics and measure the response. These heteronuclear spin control methods were also developed in this work. We successfully realized control of both the amplitude and period of the spin oscillation with DC magnetic fields. In addition, taking advantage of the very different energy levels of Na and Rb, we demonstrated control of the dynamics with microwave and light fields, with both fields acting on Rb only. Especially the method of dynamics control with light field is peculiar to the heteronuclear system. In the future, it should allow us to control the spin dynamics with both fast temporal and high spatial resolutions. The above-mentioned parts of the experimental results were written in a paper which we just submitted to Physical Review A. The heteronuclear spin mixture system still holds great promise, as has been studied in theory. Armed with all the developed experimental capabilities, we are currently working on extracting the correlations and possibly entanglement between Na and Rb atoms following the heteronuclear spin exchange. We are also hoping to realize the fragmentation originally proposed for two-band system in optical lattices. The original PI’s group in Purdue is still pursing some of the theoretical ideas. The collaboration between the Hong Kong PI and the Purdue group will be continued in the coming years. Right now, a main challenge in the experimental project is the small energy scale of the spin-exchange interaction. Under the normal sample condition, it is only on the order of 10 to 20 Hz. As a result, the so generated correlations are easily to be destroyed. Detection of the fragmentation phase requires very stringent experimental parameter control. This may be solved by application of the optical lattice potential which can greatly enhance the onsite interaction. We estimate a factor of 10 improvement on the spin-exchange interaction energy can be easily achieved with a normal 3-D square lattice. Such a technology is already available in another setup of the Hong Kong PI’s group. It should be straight to adapt that to the spinor mixture setup, but more funding is needed for purchasing the narrow linewidth laser for implementing the lattice potential.

14304015.value: Major findings: 1. we have studied theoretically the quantum many-body dynamics for a variety of initial states in an optical lattice, in which the s and p bands (or the s and d bands) are occupied. We worked out the role of interaction in the generation of quantum correlations. The experimental parameter regimes, in which a conventional single-particle condensate vanishes, and a pair condensate emerges, were also figured. 2. We worked out the generation of correlation and entanglement in a two-species Bose-Einstein condensate mixture with spin degrees of freedom, specifically the Na and Rb F = 1 spinor mixture. The heteronuclear spin-exchange interaction can also lead to a heteronuclear fragmented phase. 3. We experimentally investigated the heteronuclear spinor dynamics with the Na and Rb spin-1 mixture and produced a spin-1/2 system with intersperses interaction. 4. We developed two techniques for controlling the heteronuclear spin dynamics with the help of microwave and vector light shift. 14304015.value: 1. Objective 3 was not fully addressed due to the change of PI. Band engineering by shaking optical lattice is still a interest topic. We plan to investigate this in future collaborations between the CUHK experimental group and the Purdue theoretical group. 2. Following the observed spin dynamics, the correlation should already have been built up. We will develop proper ways of reading them out. And try to characterize the so generated entanglement between the two atomic species. 3. Optical lattice can enhance the spin-exchange interaction strength by at least one order of magnitude. This will substantially improve the robustness of the interaction induced dynamics. We will manage to secure more funding to buy a high power and narrow linewidth laser for this purpose. 4. Continue the collaboration between the CUHK experimental group and the Purdue theoretical group.

14304015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304015.value: When a gaseous sample of atoms with high enough density is cooled to ultracold temperatures (T< 10^-6 K), the atoms undergo a phase transition to form a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC). In this exotic state, all atoms occupy the same external state and they behave collective following quantum mechanics. In the last two decades, this kind of ultracold quantum gas has become one of the most popular physical platforms for investigating quantum many-body problems. In this work, we explore the internal and external degrees of freedom of the atoms and take advantage the flexibility in controlling the interaction between atoms to study bosons condensed in unconventional fashions. In the first part, we studied theoretically a new approach for realizing pair condensates using well-controlled quantum dynamical evolutions in optical lattices. We focused on the role of the interaction in the generation of correlation for BEC in two orbits of the external periodical potential. We went beyond the typical two-particle level and found correlations in higher order and multi-particle level. A fragmented condensate phase was also discovered. We also worked out an experimental scheme with which the properties of this exotic phase can be detected and characterized. In the second part, we demonstrated interspecies spin-exchange interaction induced dynamics in a two atomic species mixture of spin-1/2 system. Such dynamics should be another way of generating correlation and entanglement between the two different species. We further developed way of controlling such dynamics with microwave and light field. These flexible control methods will be the key in probing the correlation in future studies.

14304115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304115.value: o-Carboranes can be viewed as three-dimensional relatives of benzenes. They share many features such as aromaticity, high thermal and chemical stability, and facile electrophilic substitution reactions with electrophiles. In sharp contrast to the significant advances in transition metal catalyzed C-H functionalization of benzenes, the corresponding transition metal catalyzed selective cage B-H functionalization of o-carboranes is virtually unexplored, which limits the potential application of carboranes in medicine and materials. It is expected that the selective cage B-H functionalization is much more challenging than that of C-H activation in benzenes since a total of ten B-H vertices are available in three-dimensional o-carborane clusters. We have very recently made significant progress in this research area, achieving Pd(II)-catalyzed selective tetrafluorination of o-carboranes (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2013, 135, 12912) and Ni(0)-promoted intramolecular cage B(7)-C(phenyl) coupling via selective B−H activation (J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2014, 136, 7599). These preliminary results shed some light on transition metal catalyzed selective activation and transformation of cage B-H bonds. In this proposal, we plan to systematically investigate these reactions to develop new methodologies for the synthesis of a variety of functionalized carboranes via transition metal catalyzed selective cage B-H activation. The reaction mechanism is also a subject of this proposal. It is anticipated that this research will result in a new toolbox for the preparation of a new class of B-substituted carborane derivatives and enhance our basic understanding of selective cage B-H activation reactions. It will also be fascinating to discover what lies beyond. 碳硼烷可以被認爲是苯環的一種三維結構類似物。它們和苯環有許多類似的性質，比如芳香性，熱和化學穩定性，以及和親電試劑的反應性。近年來，過渡金屬催化的苯環碳氫鍵活化取得了巨大的成功，但是過渡金屬催化的碳硼烷硼氫鍵的官能團化却少有研究。修飾方法的缺乏限制了碳硼烷在醫學以及材料科學上的應用。相對苯環而言，碳硼烷十個硼氫鍵使得選擇性的活化變得更加困難。我們組最近在這個研究領域取得了重要進展。通過直接的硼氫鍵的活化，我們實現了碳硼烷選擇性的氟化和芳香化。這些結果給過渡金屬催化的選擇性的硼氫活化打開了一個窗口。基于這些基礎，我們計劃發展一系列新的方法學去實現碳硼烷硼氫鍵的不同類型的官能團化。反應機理的研究也是我們的一個重要目標。可以預見的是，這個研究將會爲製備硼取代的碳硼烷衍生物提供一個系統的方法，同時可以提升我們對選擇性硼氫鍵活化反應本質的理解。

14304115.label: Realisation of objectives
14304115.value: Carboranes, a class of carbon-boron molecular clusters, are often viewed as three-dimensional analogues to benzene. They are finding increasing applications as useful functional building blocks in materials science, medicine, organometallic/coordination chemistry and more. Thus, functionalization of carboranes has received considerable attention. In comparison with the weakly acidic cage C-H bonds that can be readily functionalized, selective cage B-H functionalization among ten chemically similar BH vertices in o-carboranes is very challenging. This project focuses on the development of a set of methods for transition metal catalyzed vertex-specific BH functionalization. Differences in electronegativity of carbon and boron elements lead to the electron density of cage B(4,5,7,11) atoms lying between that of B(3,6) and B(8,9,10,12) ones, which makes the selective functionalization of B(4,5,7,11)-H bonds very challenging. We proposed a strategy of directing-group-assisted transition metal catalysis to achieve the selective functionalization of cage B(4,5,7,11)-H vertices. Subsequently, a series of methods has been developed. We developed a Pd-catalyzed carboxylic acid guided regioselective alkynylation of cage B(4)-H bond in o-carboranes. In the presence of 5 mol % Pd(OAc)2 and 3 equiv of AgOAc, reaction of 1-COOH-2-R1-C2B10H10 with R3Si─≡─Br in ClCH2CH2Cl gives 4-(R3SiC≡C)-2-R1-o-C2B10H10 in moderate to high yields. This reaction is compatible with alkynes having sterically bulky silyl groups such as iPr3Si or tBuMe2Si. On the other hand, another catalytic system Pd(OAc)2/AgOAc/K2HPO4 can catalyze the direct B(4)-alkynylation of 1-COOH-2-R1-C2B10H10 with terminal alkynes R2─≡─H in moderate to high yields. The latter has a broader substrate scope from bulky silyl to aromatic to carboranyl substituents. Desilylation of the resultant products affords carboranyl acetylene 4-(HC≡C)-2-R1-o-C2B10H10 that can undergo further transformations such as Sonogashira coupling, dimerization and click reaction. It is suggested that the above two catalytic systems may proceed via Pd(II)-Pd(IV)-Pd(II) and Pd(II)-Pd(0)-Pd(II) catalytic cycles, respectively. In addition, the silver salt is found to promote the decarboxylation reaction and thereby controls the mono-selectivity. This directing group strategy was extended to a rhodium catalyzed hydroxylation of cage B(4)-H bond in o-carboranes with O2 or air as the oxygen source, which serves as a new methodology for the regioselective generation of a series of 4-OH-o-carboranes in a one-pot process. The use of O2 or air as both the oxidant and the oxygen source makes this protocol very environmentally friendly and practical. In the presence of 2.5 mol% [Cp*RhCl2]2 and 2 equiv of KOAc, a toluene solution of 1-COOH-2-CH3-o-C2B10H10 was heated at 95 oC under O2 (1 atom) for 36 h to afford a B(4)-hydroxylated product in 80% yield. After the identification of key intermediates and control experiments, a reaction mechanism was proposed, which offers useful information for the design of new catalytic reactions. We then applied this directing group strategy to transition metal catalyzed regioselective amination of cage B(4)-H bond, leading to the preparation of a series of tertiary and secondary carboranyl amines. Such amination reactions proceeded under mild conditions without the addition of any external oxidants. Hydrogenolysis of the resultant product 4-N(CH2Ph)2-o-carborane afforded primary carboranyl amine, 4-amino-o-carborane, in quantitative yield. We also applied such a directing group strategy to transition metal catalyzed regioselective cage B(4)-H iodination, bromination, and chlorination as well as B(4,5)-H diiodination. The results show that the traceless directing group COOH plays a crucial role not only in controlling site selectivity but also in tuning mono- or di-selectivity. A series of previous inaccessible B(4,5)- and B(4)-halogenated o-carborane derivatives were prepared in a simple one pot process in high yields. The aforementioned methods for the functionalization of carboranes require pre-functionalized coupling partners, which limits the substrate scope and practicability. Inspired by our work on transition metal catalyzed –COOH guided selective cage B-H functionalization, we then combined the activation of cage B-H with aryl C-H for straightforward and site-selective B-H/C-H dehydrogenative cross-coupling. The significance of such catalytic dehydrogenative cross-coupling is three-fold: 1) pre-functionalized reagents are not required, 2) the documented multistep syntheses can be simplified to a simple one-pot process, and 3) various thiophene derivatives with different functional groups are tolerated. Accordingly, we developed Ir-catalyzed –COOH directed site-selective B-H/C-H dehydrogenative cross-coupling of o-carborane with thiophenes. Without any pre-functionalization, carboranyl carboxylic acids and thiophenes can serve as suitable coupling partners, resulting in the preparation of 4-thienyl-o-carboranes in a simple one-pot process for potential applications in materials. In summary, we proposed a strategy of directing-group-assisted transition metal catalysis to achieve the selective functionalization of cage B(4,5,7,11)-H vertices. Accordingly, a large variety of cage B-functionalized carboranes have been prepared.

14304115.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304115.value: (1) Development of several methods for transition metal-catalyzed carboxylic acid guided regioselective cage B-H activation/functionalization of o-carboranes (Pubs. #1, #3, #4, #7, #8, #11 and #12). The methods developed include (a) Pd-catalyzed carboxylic acid guided regioselective alkynylation of cage B(4)-H bond in o-carboranes, (b) Rh-catalyzed hydroxylation of cage B(4)-H bond in o-carboranes with O2 or air as the oxygen source, (c) Ir- or Ru-catalyzed regioselective amination of cage B(4)-H bond, and (d) Pd- or Ir-catalyzed regioselective cage B(4)-H iodination, bromination, and chlorination as well as B(4,5)-H diiodination. (2) Development of two methods for transition metal-catalyzed carboxylic acid guided regioselective B-H/C-H dehydrogenative cross-coupling of o-carborane with arenes (Pubs. #6 and #10). 2a) Ir-catalyzed dehydrocoupling of o-carborane with thiophene derivatives has been realized via –COOH guided cage B-H and aryl C-H activation. This methodology has a broad substrate scope and high functional group tolerance, which provides a straightforward way to incorporate carborane units into various thiophene derivatives including benzothiophenes, thienothiophenes and oligothiophenes for potential applications in photoelectronic materials. 2b) Rh-catalyzed cascade cyclization featuring cage B-H and aryl C-H activation was achieved, leading to the formation of unprecedented C,B-substituted carborane-fused N-polyheterocycles, in which cage B-H and aryl C-H were activated with the construction of three new C-C and B-C bonds. This reaction was well tolerant of halo groups, that could be used for further transformation. (3) Reaction mechanisms were investigated in detail to understand the role of transition metals, ligands, oxidants, solvents and reaction temperatures. Some key intermediates were isolated and structurally characterized. Accordingly, reaction mechanisms were proposed to explain the experimental results. These mechanistic understanding offers very useful information for the design of new catalytic reactions. In summary, this original work has resulted in 12 peer-reviewed articles published in international chemistry journals including Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. (x 3), J. Am. Chem. Soc. (x1), Chem. Sci. (x3), Chem. Eur. J (x 2), Chem. Commun. (x 1), Chem. Soc. Rev. (x1) and Sci. China Chem. (x 1). PI was invited to give two keynote and three invited lectures at international conferences. Three PhD students were trained, of which one was awarded HKPFS.

14304115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304115.value: Chirality is an important issue in life sciences as well as modern organic chemistry. Transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric reaction is a promising strategy to obtain enantiomerically enriched compounds to support the ever-growing needs of pharmaceutical industry. Our further research will be to develop enantioselective synthetic methods for the preparation of chiral-at-cage carboranes via transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric and regioselective cage B−H functionalization.

14304115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304115.value: o-Carboranes can be viewed as three-dimensional relatives to benzene. They share many features such as aromaticity, high thermal and chemical stability, and facile electrophilic substitution reactions with electrophiles. In sharp contrast to the significant advances in transition metal catalyzed C-H functionalization of benzenes, the corresponding transition metal catalyzed selective cage B-H functionalization of o-carboranes is virtually unexplored, which limits the potential application of carboranes in medicine and materials. It is expected that the selective cage B-H functionalization is much more challenging than that of C-H activation in benzenes since a total of ten B-H vertices are available in three-dimensional o-carborane clusters. We took the challenge to develop new methodologies for the synthesis of a variety of functionalized carboranes via transition metal catalyzed selective cage B-H activation and functionalization. The results of this work show that successful applications of directing-group-assisted transition metal catalysis strategy lead to a set of methods for the selective functionalization of cage B(4,5,7,11)-H vertices. Accordingly, a large variety of cage B-functionalized carboranes have been prepared and fully characterized, which may find applications in materials and medicine.

14304315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304315.value: This is a project to address the energy and environmental problems. It starts with the conversion of the abundant and renewable biomass to photocatalysts. The carbon-based photocatalysts can then harvests sunlight to produce clean fuels from water and carbon dioxide. Photocatalysis is an emerging technique that has received much attention. This method is driven by UV or sunlight to split water for hydrogen production, to decompose pollutant molecules for environmental remediation, or to reduce CO2 for valuable fuels. A high efficient and easy-prepared photocatalyst is crucial for the photocatalysis. However conventional metal oxide photocatalysts suffer from narrow-spectrum-photoresponse, poor charge separation efficiency and possible secondary pollution. This proposal aims to prepare carbon-based photocatalysts by hydrothermal carbonation (HTC). HTC is a technique for biomass conversion in a solution under specific temperature and pressure conditions. This proposal describes the use of renewable biomolecules, carbohydrates, as starting materials to make carbon-based photocatalysts. The electronic property of the HTC carbon can be adjusted by doping. Furthermore, these environmentally friendly photocatalysts can be coated on other semiconductor materials. The composite photocatalysts should exhibit enhanced oxidation and reduction power. Applications of the new photocatalysts for hydrogen formation from water splitting as well as reduction of carbon dioxide to chemical fuels will be explored. 本研究主要針對能源和環境問題。眾所周知，地球上存在大量的可再生的生物材料，比如碳水化合物。本研究的主要目的是利用這些生物材料來製備高效的光催化劑。光催化技術是目前越來越被廣泛重視的技術，因為它可以通過利用太陽光能來實現水分解產氫，光解有機污染物和光還原二氧化碳。光催化技術在治理環境污染和生產高附加值的燃料方面都取得了重要進展。對光催化技術來說，生產一種高效，容易合成的光催化劑是其中最為關鍵的一步。但傳統的金屬氧化物光催化劑有窄光譜回應，低電荷分離效率和容易造成二次污染等缺點。本研究計畫主要是通過水熱碳化法合成一系列的碳基催化劑。水熱碳化法主要通過在特定的溶液，溫度和壓力下把碳水化合物這種可再生的生物材料轉化成為高效的碳基催化劑。通過在合成過程中摻雜不同的元素，合成的碳基催化劑還能具有不同的電學性能。而且，這種環境友好的光催化劑還可以覆蓋在傳統的半導體金屬氧化物上來增強他們的光催化氧化或還原能力。合成的碳基光催化劑和碳/金屬氧化物複合物將主要應用于光催化水分解產氫和二氧化碳還原合成化學燃料。

14304315.label: Realisation of objectives
14304315.value: All five objectives were realized. As shown in the 6 publications attached to Part C of this report, a series of Hydro-Thermal Carbonation (HTC) carbon photocatalysts were prepared from abundant starting materials. The HTC could be added to metal oxides such as molybdenum dioxide to form composite materials with enhanced efficiency for photocatalysis. The samples were used for splitting water molecules and degrading pollutants. Photoanodes were also fabricated with the new materials for photoelectrochemical water splitting. Finally, mechanisms were proposed to explain the observed photocatalytic activity.

14304315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304315.value: This project results in the publication of 6 papers in reputable journals. The 1st publication in Part C describes the preparation of HTC carbon material from glucose and its coupling to MoO2. This simple chemical modiﬁcation brings two advantages: (i) an internal electric ﬁeld is formed at the interface between MoO2 and HTC due to their appropriate band alignment; (ii) the nanostructured MoO2 and the HTC matrix are intertwined with each other intimately. Their small size and large contact area promote charge transfer, especially under the internal electric ﬁeld. Therefore, the separation rate of photoexcited charge carrier in MoO2 is greatly enhanced. The activity increases by 2.4, 16.8, and 4.0 times in photocatalytic oxygen evolution, dyes degradation, and photoelectrochemicl cell, respectively. The new approach is helpful for further development of metallic photocatalysts. The 2nd publication shows that HTC Carbon (HTCC) materials can be prepared not only from glucose but also from any hydrocarbons including agricultural and animal wastes. The conversion of carbohydrates to HTCC may be considered as a “Trash to Treasure” approach. We believe this discovery will attract a lot of attention from researchers involved in environmental catalysis, waste recycling, and pollution treatment. The photocatalytic activity of HTCC can be signiﬁcantly enhanced by iodine doping. The enhancement mechanism is investigated by density functional theoretical calculations and electrochemical measurements. The iodine dopants twist and optimize the structures of the sp2-hybridization in HTCC, thereby favoring photon-induced excitation. Moreover, the iodine dopants facilitate the charge transfer between diﬀerent sp2-hybridization structures, thus increasing the conductivity and activity of the HTCC. An added beneﬁt is that the I-doped HTCC exhibits lower cytotoxic eﬀect than the pure HTCC. By using a similar preparation approach but changing the starting material from carbohydrate to thiourea would result in the formation of another non-metal carbon-based polymer, the graphitic carbon nitride. This photocatalyst can be chemically modified with elemental doping (publication 3) or forming composites with red phosphorus (publication 4) and titanium dioxide (publication 5).

14304315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304315.value: Our most recent research output (publication 6) clearly demonstrates the potential for further development of the research. Small naturally occurring biomaterials such as pollen can be converted to carbon-based photocatalysts. These products are particularly effective for photocatalytic water disinfection. This is a sustainable approach for controlling E-coli and other common waterborne species. It offers a new insight into the exploration of other natural substances for economical pollution treatment.

14304715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304715.value: 隨著成像技術的發展，在真實世界中能夠有效地捕捉幾何形像，並構建成為三維圖像。為要分析幾何數據，準確地在兩個幾何形像間獲得一對一逐點對應是非常重要的。形像對準可應用在各個領域上，如計算機視覺，計算機圖形學和醫療成像等。許多現有的對準算法只能處理形狀相似的情況。然而，在實際情況下，任意兩個形狀未必存在一個雙射的對應。例如在來源域上的某些區域可能不符合目標的形狀，反之亦然。這一對形狀的被稱為不一致形狀 。在此情況下，更複雜的對準方式是必要的。在這個項目中，我們的目標是開發一種變分方法來解決不一致形狀的對準問題，並探討其應用。 本研究主要分為兩部分。在第一部份，我們的目標是開發高效率的算法來解決不一致形狀的對準問題。首先，我們將探索使用變分方法來對準不一致曲面的可能性。兩個模型將被考慮:（1）以圖象強度為基礎的對準模式，（2）以圖象特徵和強度為基礎的對準模型。對準的問題可以轉化為優化問題。其中主要的挑戰是，形狀的優化（相應區域）和曲面映射（對準）在優化過程中一同涉及。在這個項目中，我們會考慮不同的數值算法來解決這類具有挑戰性的優化問題。其次，我們感興趣的是開發一種能夠保持拓撲的Beltrami holomorphic flow方法，這使我們同時能夠透過變分模型來調整曲面映射和目標域的幾何形狀。這有利於對準不一致曲面時的優化過程。此外，我們的方法也能夠適用於高維的情況。類似曲面的情況，兩個N維幾何形像數據不一定存在著一個雙射的對應。因此, 我們必需開發一個計算方法來對準高維的不一致幾何數據。我們將設計不同的變分模型來解決不一致N維物體的對準問題。 在研究的第二部分，我們有興趣把對準算法應用在實際情況中：1:計算機視覺，2:計算機圖形學和3:醫療成像。對於計算機視覺，我們將建立一個在不一致形狀空間的度量來衡量形狀間的幾何差異。為了這個目的，我們將考慮選擇合適的能量來設計不一致形狀的對準模型，並以此來定義形狀之間的度量。對於計算機圖形學，我們將運用我們設計出來的算法, 來構建一個完整的動態三維幾何圖像。要構建一個完整的幾何圖像，我們須要將從不同角度拍攝出來的不一致曲面合併起來。對於動態對象，曲面與曲面之間的關係可能要以非剛性變換來表示。由於視線上的遮蔽，曲面也可能具有孔。這啟發我們開發一個能夠同時縫合和修補曲面孔的變分模型。最後，在醫療成像方面，我們計劃應用第一部分的對準算法來解決牙齒數據的對準問題。已對準的牙齒表面將被用於牙齒的形態分析,以研究牙科疾病。

14304715.label: Realisation of objectives
14304715.value: In this project, we have proposed several objectives. The ultimate goal is to develop mathematical models to register and analyze inconsistent shapes. The PI has tackled each proposed problems successfully. Details are as follows. Objective 1: Our first objective is to design and implement a topology-preserving mapping flow method, which allows simultaneous adjustment of the mapping and the geometry of the target domain. This algorithm is crucial to solve the inconsistent shape matching problem. In order to solve the registration problem of inconsistent shapes, optimization models are considered. Our optimization problem is formulated as finding an optimal mapping between two shapes, in which case the source domain and target domain are not fixed. To solve the optimization problem, an effective mathematical algorithm must be developed to iteratively adjust the mapping with free boundary condition, while maintaining the bijectivity throughout the process. We have successfully developed a method to achieve this goal. The basic idea is to obtain mappings with controlled scale distortions, while adjusting the mapping according to the adjustment of Beltrami coefficient without enforcing geometry of the target domain. The scale distortions can be controlled by constraining the singular values of the mapping differential, and can be numerically computed by a simple projection. The mapping is then adjusted without any assumption on the geometry of the target domain, which is according to the adjustment of Beltrami coefficient with controlled magnitude to guarantee bijectivity. The method has shown to be useful to facilitate the optimization model for the inconsistent shape registration problem. Objective 2: Our second objective is to develop mathematical algorithms to register inconsistent shapes. It is a challenging scenario for shape matching, when some regions of the source domain may not correspond to any region of the target domain and vice versa. The PI has successfully develop algorithms to achieve this objective. There are several tasks involved in this objective. Below, we describe in detail what we have achieved for each tasks. Firstly, we have formulated an effective energy functional to solve the inconsistent shape matching problem. The energy functional involves a fidelity and regularization terms. The energy functional is formulated over the spaces of sub-regions on each surface and bijective mappings between them. This is a challenging optimization problem as it involves both the shape optimization and mapping optimization problems. Nevertheless, the PI has developed an efficient and accurate numerical solver to solve this challenging optimization problem. The basic idea is to consider the optimization problem with a special assumption of the maximality property, with which the problem can be simplified and solved on the parameter domains after surface conformal parameterizations. The problem can then be solved via a splitting method and the topology-preserving mapping flow method developed in Objective 1. The corresponding region can be obtained from the range of an optimized map and the registration map is simultaneously outputted. The developed method has shown to be effective in registering inconsistent real dataset, such as the human face and teeth surfaces. Besides, one crucial step in this project is to simplify the shape matching problem by firstly parameterizing the surfaces onto simple domains, so that calculation can be carried out more efficiently. In practice, the surfaces obtained from scanners have very high resolution, in which case existing parameterization methods cannot handle. To tackle this issue, we have developed fast numerical methods for parameterization, which can handle very dense surfaces. Furthermore, to obtain an initial approximation of the inconsistent shape matching, one technique is by closing up the simply-connected surface to become a genus-0 closed surface. As a result, the registration problem can be converted to finding a suitable quasiconformal map between two genus-0 closed surfaces without boundary that matches certain distribution. Fast numerical solver have been developed to compute quasiconformal mapping between genus-0 closed surfaces. The method can also be used to remesh the surfaces, so that the optimization model for inconsistent shape matching can be solved more accurately. Finally, the other intuitive technique to obtain an initial approximation of the inconsistent shape matching is to register two surfaces piece by piece and glue the obtained piecewise registration maps together nicely (conformally). We have successfully developed a welding method to glue registration maps nicely with least distortions. Results show that the method is effective and efficient for glueing maps. Objective 3: Our third objective is to apply the developed algorithms to practical applications in medical imaging, computer graphics and computer visions. The PI has successfully achieved this objective. Firstly, we have built a shape metric for inconsistent surfaces to measure their shape differences. Given two inconsistent surfaces with prescribed landmark constraints, we first apply the method in Objective 2 to find an optimal landmark-matching quasi-conformal mapping between them. This gives a 1-1 correspondence between the common regions of the two surfaces, which are automatically determined by the method. The quantification of the shape variation of two surfaces can then be focused on the common regions without being affected by the inconsistency of the overall shapes. To design a metric for inconsistent shapes, we consider a shape measure defined by the curvature mismatching and conformality distortion for each corresponding region. It can be shown that the shape measure is equal to 0 if and only if each corresponding components are equal up to a rigid motion. Thus, this shape measure can be used to construct a dissimilarity measure between the two shapes. Experimental results show that the shape measure can identify geometric difference between inconsistent shapes. The method has been applied to teeth morphometry problem to analyze a set of mammalian teeth, which yield high classification accuracy compared to other state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, we have applied our inconsistent shape registration method to match human faces captured at different angles, so that they can be stitched together to obtain the whole human face.

14304715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304715.value: In this project, we have developed various mathematical models for the registration and shape analysis of inconsistent shapes, which have resulted in 3 published papers and 1 submitted papers. Details are as follows. (1) Mathematical methods to facilitate inconsistent shape matching problems: a. In [1], we have developed a topology-preserving mapping flow method, which allows us to iteratively adjust the mapping with free boundary condition, while maintaining the bijectivity throughout the process. Using the method, a mapping can be adjusted based on the adjustment of the Beltrami coefficient with controlled scale distortions, without the assumption on the geometry of the target domain. The method becomes one of the fundamental tools for solving the inconsistent shape registration problem. b. The shape matching problem is simplified by firstly parameterizing the surfaces (very high resolution in practice, in which case existing parameterization methods cannot handle) onto simple domains. In [3,4], fast numerical methods have been developed which can handle very dense surfaces. c. To obtain an initial approximation of inconsistent shape matching, one technique is done by closing up the simply-connected surface to become a genus-0 closed surface. The registration problem can be converted to finding a suitable quasiconformal map between two genus-0 closed surfaces. In [4], a fast numerical solver have been developed to compute quasiconformal mapping between genus-0 closed surfaces. The method can also be used to remesh the surfaces, so that the optimization model for inconsistent shape matching can be solved more accurately. d. Another method to obtain an initial approximation of shape matching is done by registering different corresponding regions of the two inconsistent shapes, followed by glueing the piecewise registration maps together with least distortions (conformally). In [3], we have developed a welding technique to glue registration maps conformally with least distortions. (2) Effective optimization model for registering inconsistent shapes: We have developed an energy minimization model to find a meaningful 1-1 correspondence between two inconsistent shapes [1]. The energy functional involves a data fidelity term minimizing the curvature mismatching, together with a regularization term using the Beltrami coefficient. The minimization problem is a challenging one since the energy is formulated over the spaces of sub-regions on each surface and bijective mappings between them. In [1], we have developed an effective numerical algorithm, based on a splitting method, to simultaneously solve the geometry optimization and mapping problems. (3) Development of shape metric for inconsistent surfaces: In order to measure the geometric dissimilarity between two inconsistent surfaces, we have designed a shape metric based on the curvature mismatching and conformality distortion for each corresponding region [2]. (4) Application of the developed models: In [2], our developed inconsistent shape analysis method has been successfully applied to the tooth morphometry problem for the cluster analysis of a set of mammalian teeth, which yield very high classification accuracy. In [1], we have developed our algorithm to match human faces captured by scanner at different angles for facial registration.

14304715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304715.value: There are several areas for further development of the research. Details are described as follows. (1) Inconsistent shape matching for surfaces with arbitrary topologies: Currently, our method can mainly handle simply-connected surfaces. In practice, some surfaces can be of high-genus. We will explore the possibility to extend our method to high-genus cases. (2) Improve the computational time: Currently, solving the optimization model for inconsistent shape matching cannot be done in real-time. In practice, to apply the method to computer graphics (such as stitching), a real-time computation is more desirable. We will explore the possibility to develop a method to solve the model in real time, probably with the combination of deep neural network. (3) Extension to register noisy surfaces: Currently, our method assumes the surfaces to be matched are not noisy. If the surfaces are noisy, our method can be unstable. We are interested to explore the possibility to adjust the models, such that they can handle noisy surfaces. One possible direction is to modify the energy functional in the optimization model with a surface denoising term, so that surface denoising and matching can be carried out simultaneously.

14304715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304715.value: In this project, the main goal is to develop effective mathematical models to register and analyse inconsistent surfaces, which may not bijectively correspond to each others. We have explored three research directions: 1. Develop mathematical techniques, which can facilitate the inconsistent shape matching; 2. Develop optimization model to solve the inconsistent shape matching problem and 3. Develop a shape metric to measure the geometric dissimilarities between inconsistent shapes and explore its applications. We have successfully developed and implemented mathematical models for the above three goals. We have developed several mathematical techniques, which facilitates the process of inconsistent shape matching. An effective energy minimization model for inconsistent shape matching and numerical method to solve the optimization model have also been developed. With the inconsistent shape matching method, we have developed a shape metric for inconsistent shapes, based on curvature mismatching and conformality distortion for each corresponding region. With the developed algorithms, we have developed tools for practical tooth morphometry applications. This method has brought about contributions to biological shape analysis.

14304915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304915.value: 設計共價抑制劑來抑制蛋白-蛋白相互作用是非常有挑戰性的工作。因為蛋白質通常不具備像酶中的活性位點可以參與化學反應。結合誘導的共價反應在這方面具有不可替代的優點：我們設計合成的多肽衍生物可以跟蛋白質形成特異性的共價鍵，從而成為有效的共價抑制劑。然而能夠跟多肽發生共價反應的蛋白質必須要在它的多肽結合位點具有半胱氨酸。在之前發表的兩個例子中，我們通過定點突變的方法在某些特意的位點引入半胱氨酸以實現共價反應。在本計劃書中，我們希望把共價交聯反應進一步拓展到天然蛋白中，從半胱氨酸拓展到酪氨酸的反應，並且探索這個反應的進一步的應用。 我們首先驗證了一個含有半胱氨酸的天然PDZ蛋白的共價反應。我們設計了一個多肽庫，並且觀察到多肽和PDZ蛋白的共價反應可以在細胞內發生。其中的一個共價多肽，可以影響ephrin-B信號通路。這個例子證明（1）在蛋白-蛋白結合位點的確存在可以發生共價反應的半胱氨酸；（2）結合誘導的半胱氨酸巰基的共價反應可以在細胞質裏發生；（3）共價多肽能夠有效抑制蛋白-蛋白相互作用。 結合誘導的共價反應接下來被用到其他模塊化蛋白結合域，比如SH2和SH3。通過SH2和SH3蛋白。在生物信息學和晶體結構信息的指導下，我們表達了一系列的SH2蛋白域，並且合成了一個具有代表性的多肽庫。根據多肽和蛋白的不同反應的模式，我們可以把SH2蛋白質劃分成不同的類別。共價多肽也能夠作爲探針來研究細胞內的處於天然狀態的SH2蛋白。雖然含有半胱氨酸的SH3蛋白相比較而言少很多，但是其中的一些也能夠用作共價結合反應。除了跟半胱氨酸的反應，我們還設計了針對酪氨酸的azo coupling反應。因爲酪氨酸相比半胱氨酸要多得多，這一反應將有更普遍的適用性。這些前期結果爲今後的實驗打下了堅實的基礎。 把結合誘導的共價反應從從後天構造的蛋白拓展到天然蛋白，使得這一反應可以被應用到不同的場合。比如，（1）共價抑制劑，（2）爲含有半胱氨酸的蛋白域分類，（3）從共價多肽到發現新的天然多肽，（4）設計共價探針來研究蛋白組裏的蛋白結合域等。綜上所述，結合誘導的共價反應有望成爲化學生物學工具箱裏的重要一員。

14304915.label: Realisation of objectives
14304915.value: All four objectives have been successfully realized. We systematically explored cysteine containing protein-binding domains, such as SH2, SH3 and PDZ in human cells. In particular, we focused on SH2 domains, and discovered that a large portion of SH2 domains harbour cysteine residues at the peptide-binding sites. This work led to the discovery of a reverse binding mode of the SH2 domains that is almost unreported in the literature. Covalent blockers against Nck peptide-binding domains have been successfully developed. The covalent blocker peptide exhibited much higher inhibitory efficacy than non-covalent blockers, in cell based experiments. The peptide blocker successfully inhibited bacterial infection to the intestine cells, and even exhibited a superior blocking effect in an animal model of bacterial infection. This is to our knowledge the first application of covalent peptide to animal study, and it illustrates a new antimicrobial mechanism that may lead to new antimicrobial therapies. Tyrosine-specific azo coupling reaction has also been developed taking advantage of affinity-guided covalent conjugation reaction. The reaction was used to cyclize a tyrosine containing peptide efficiently and then was applied to inter-molecular reaction between a protein and a peptide. This result showed that tyrosine-specific proximity-induced reaction is feasible. The covalent reactive peptides have been successfully applied to proteomic studies to site-specifically immobilize protein-binding domains on the surface covalently. This technology leads to homogenous, oriented immobilization of proteins, and can be useful for proteomic studies. Specifically, we immobilized methyllysine-binding proteins using this technique and led to discovery of many lysine methylation sites from proteomes for the first time. Taken together, all four objectives have been successfully fulfilled.
