14600215.label: Major findings and research outcome
14600215.value: As indicated by the title, this research focuses on the urban sculpture planning system, its corresponding policies and urban development strategies in Shanghai. Based on extensive and solid empirical work, this project makes a breakthrough contribution by proposing the “cultural elite state” model, which explains the way that cultural development projects are produced using the urban sculpture planning system in Shanghai as an example. This model highlights the importance of “cultural capital” (embedded in individuals’ dispositions and judgmental competencies) in the form of cultural tastes, aesthetic appreciation and cultural participation as a source of cultural elites’ power (Bourdieu, 1979/1987; Katz-Gerro, 2008; Lamont & Lareau, 1988; Bourdieu & Wacquant, 1992), in creating a circle of cultural elites emotionally bonded by the common tastes and behavior patterns, producing urban sculpture plans urban sculpture projects. Two other key features, i.e., the relative autonomy of the cultural development field, and individual-specific qualities versus institutional arrangement, are also critical. From this perspective, this project has explored the way that urban sculpture plans and project decisions are made. It shows that cultural capital serves as a gluing effect which may break the existing hierarchical structure. Also, this research contributes to enriching the literature of Chinese entrepreneurial city by revealing a unique form of public and private partnership in cultural development. Such partnership relations are affected by “cultural” factors, subject to individual cultural projects and being unstable. Actors in partnership with the government can be private enterprises or public corporations or state-owned enterprises. This variation has diversified the nature and form of partnership in the Chinese context. Moreover, this model is also valuable in explaining the way that arts policies and the planning system shape urban sculpture production in Shanghai. The “elite coalition” has created a semi-enclosed system of artist selection and artwork display. As a corollary, commissioning and invitation are the two dominant artist selection methods, being used more often than open competition. The latter is more often foundin democratic political system. In addition, emphasis on technical excellence over true creativity has been found in the urban sculpture production apparatus. Consistent with this, public art plans and related planning documents display an obsession with planning techniques, such as geometric pattern of concept plan and detailed site designs. On the other hand, inadequate public participation is companied by a lack of social planning mechanism.

14600215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14600215.value: Further development of the research can be planned in two aspects. First, the theoretical model proposed by this research project, i.e., “cultural elite state”, can be tested to understand its scope of applicability. For instance, as per this model, stakeholders are bonded together due to the common cultural capital embedded in individuals and thereby create urban sculpture projects. The further research question will be whether other types of cultural development projects in China, such as creative industry parks, museums, theatres, are produced in the same manner? Second, if “cultural elite state” is a model to explain cultural development projects in Shanghai, can it be applied to other cities, such as Beijing, Guangzhou and Shenzhen, or even second and third tiers of Chinese cities? How is the decision-making process of cultural projects like in those Chinese cities? Can the process be explained using the CES model as well? Is Shanghai adequately representative of Chinese cities? How about other countries and cities? I am currently planning to develop a series of key indicators to measure “cultural tastes” and “cultural participation” and test and quantify the correlation between “cultural elite” collation and the consequent projects across 125 cities in China.

14600215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14600215.value: The recent decades have boosted cultural development in China, e.g., museums, theatres and cultural quarters. They are playing a role in producing iconic urban images and boosting local economy. How do the local authorities in China make cultural plans and what is the process of decision making? These were yet to be understood when I put forward the proposal of this research. State-led public art or urban sculpture projects are one type of cultural developments. This research looks at urban sculpture planning in Shanghai. I conducted extensive in-depth interviews with urban planning bureau officers, businesses and artists and art consultants. The major contribution of this project is proposing a new conceptual model to theorize the role of the Chinese local states in creating cultural development projects. It argues that “cultural capital” (e.g., cultural tastes, cultural participation and behavior pattern) is a factor that sparks emotional communications among government officers and other stakeholders in urban sculpture projects. This group of people in coalition makes decisions to produce urban sculpture projects. This model explains how the local states come up with ideas of urban sculpture projects, select developers, artists and other partners for collaboration and the key features of urban sculpture plans.

14600615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14600615.value: Sparse signal reconstruction has become a hot topic in signal processing. A large part of the community has chosen to consider a (non-Euclidean) regularization approach to address these types of problems. We have followed a different path by considering sparsity explicitly. We have developed algorithms that exploit the parametric structure of sparsity (sinusoids, Diracs etc.), resulting in sparse signal modelization theory called “Finite Rate of Innovation” (FRI). In this new project, we would like to develop a new branch of this theory that would deal with approximation of arbitrary signals by FRI signals. In addition we intend to put forward a novel generalization of the FRI framework where the annihilation property is replaced by a masking equation. This framework will allow us to work with discrete sparse signals, allowing a direct comparison of the algorithms with Compressed Sensing algorithms. 稀疏信號重構已經成為一個熱門話題信號處理。很大一部分研究者考慮選（非歐幾里得）通過正則化方法來解決這些類型的問題。我們遵循不同的策略來明確考慮信號的稀疏性 。我們已經證明了利用參數的稀疏結構（例如正弦，Dirac等），可以完全重建稀疏信號。這個理論被稱為“有限創新率”（FRI）。 在這個新的項目，我們想進一步發展這個理論，將考慮的一個新方向是 對任意信號通過FRI信號來近似。此外，我們打算利用全新的FRI框架來描述 湮沒特性方程。湮沒特性方程由蝕刻（masking）方程代替。該框架將允許我們處理離散的稀疏信號，從而可以與壓縮感知算法進行直接比較 。

14600615.label: Realisation of objectives
14600615.value: All the objectives have been addressed and achieved: * 1. Develop FRI approximation algorithms, and in particular, efficient approaches to obtain the FRI model order. We have reformulated the FRI problem as a fitting problem, constrained by a masking equation (see objective 2) that led to: a. Optimally robust algorithms (e.g., -10 dB noise), maximum accuracy (reaching bounds): Thanks to the fitting approach, the iterative algorithm that was proposed in the journal paper #1 behave like a maximum likelihood estimator and so, reaches the Cramér-Rao lower bound, i.e., the smallest error that any (unbiased) estimate of the innovation parameters incurs. b. Significantly more efficient algorithms (no SVD needed anymore, essentially iterative solutions of linear systems of equations), faster: the implementation (in Python and Matlab) requires only to solve linear systems of equations that are further robustified by using a QR decomposition of the matrix involved (fast). c. Determination of the order of the FRI model inside the framework (i.e., the sparsity): as mentioned in the previous report, the fitting approach allows to adopt the fitting error as a criterion by finding the smallest model order that achieves a target fitting quality. This is documented in the conference paper #1. * 2. Develop a novel masking-based framework, which will allow direct comparison with Compressed Sensing results: We have shown that the annihilation-based framework is a special case of a masking-based framework which, additionally, provides an intuitive understanding of sparsity as the parameters of a mask function. More specifically, the algorithm developed: a. Achieves full accuracy (no numerical instabilities) with large sets of data (e.g., tens of thousand samples, compared to a few hundred in older algorithms): the theoretical gains are already shown in the journal paper #1, but we have also been able to demonstrate the superiority of FRI algorithms compared to compressed sensing-based algorithms in a practical radioastronomy application with real radio interferometric data from the LOFAR (LOw-Frequency ARray, http://www.lofar.org/about-lofar/about-lofar) telescope. We showed that it is possible to determine accurate off-grid radio point source locations+intensities in the sky by comparing with existing source catalogs. We achieved angular super-resolution so that very close sources can be reliably distinguished. This achievement is documented in journal paper #2 (which, due to a mistake, does not properly acknowledge the grant, unfortunately). c. Allows relaxation of the uniform sampling constraint: the journal paper #1 showed the theory how to deal with non-uniform samples and, more generally, how to deal with arbitrary linear sample acquisition. This had an immediate application in the radioastronomy paper #2 since the angular, 2D Fourier samples are non-uniformly scattered. d. Generalizes to an efficient multidimensional FRI algorithm (e.g., from quadratic to linear complexity for images): In the radioastronomy paper #2, it became necessary to develop a 2D extension of the 1D algorithms. To avoid cluttering the paper, we developed the multidimensional theory in a new paper (journal paper #3) that was published slightly later. The working principle of this multi-D extension is the mask interpretation of FRI algorithms which, by choosing a multi-D non-separable basis representation leads to huge efficiency gains, even higher as the dimension increases——compared to dealing with the problem in a separable fashion. Typically, in N dimensions, finding K sources requires about K*(D+1) samples with our new method, while using a separable setting, we would need (2*K)^D samples instead. This allows to reach Cramér-Rao lower bound for the estimation the multi-D innovation parameters, as shown in the journal paper #3. The main contributors to this project are: * Dr. Chris Gilliam, post-doc in the PI's group between 2013 and 2017 * Dr. Ayush Bhandari (PhD 2018 from MIT, now Lecturer at Imperial College, London) * Dr. Hanjie Pan (PhD 2018 from EPFL, now at Google, Zürich) The PI was PhD co-supervisor of Hanjie Pan from EPFL (Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne). A new PhD student at CUHK, Ruiming Guo, is using the algorithms developed in a specific application of trajectory retrieval from 1D sensor data.

14600615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14600615.value: Classical FRI algorithms provide the location of sparse 1D “innovations” (typically: location and amplitude of sparse signals, and more generally, of changes in a signal) with very high accuracy (reaching Cramér-Rao lower bound). However, these algorithms lose their accuracy and efficiency when the number of innovations and samples increase. Moreover, the samples are required to be uniformly sampled, which is not always practical, and efficient algorithms work only in 1 dimension. We have solved all these issues by using a new mask-based approach to the algorithms, and by reformulating the FRI problem as a fitting problem, constrained by a masking equation. The original version of this idea is described in the journal paper #1. We have extended this approach in an optimal way to multiple dimensions (journal paper #3) and demonstrated its high accuracy in a very high noise low-frequency array telescope application (radioastronomy, journal paper #2 which, due to a mistake, does not properly acknowledge the grant, unfortunately). See part 5.3 for more details.

14600615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14600615.value: We now plan to deploy these algorithms in practical applications, like time-of-flight imaging (Dr. Bhandari), and TeraHertz imaging (Prof. McPherson), which both require localising pulses with super-resolved accuracy (much better than the width of pulses). Another multi-D FRI application is super-resolution in fluorescence microscopy: FRI algorithms allow to use higher intensities than those used in STORM while still being able to localize individual molecules, making it possible to speed up significantly super-resolution acquisition and hence, to access cell dynamics. The preliminary results obtained by Dr. Hanjie Pan and his collaborators at EPFL are truly remarkable, in particular regarding 3D super-resolution. Finally, a very promising application is the surprising possibility to reconstruct a full image from a one-dimensional sequence of samples, without acquiring any localisation information. We demonstrated that this seemingly impossible problem can be solved using an FRI formulation, by retrieving first the trajectory of the samples. The optimal accuracy and efficiency of the FRI algorithms are crucial to the success of this retrieval. We have published our preliminary findings on this subject at ICASSP 2019 (Brighton, UK)

14600615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14600615.value: Usual data acquisition devices (in particular, microscopes, telescopes) are limited in their acquisition rates and suffer from very large amounts of noise. In classical approaches to deal with these data, this usually means a significant loss of resolution. Finite Rate of Innovation (FRI) theory, on the other hand, is a novel way of processing these data so as to preserve resolution, even achieving significantly higher resolution than predicted by the sampling rate. FRI processing algorithms were previously curbed by many constrains (limited data size, uniform sampling, one-dimensional data etc.). This project has been able to solve and eliminate all these constraints, while improving the robustness and speed of the algorithms. We demonstrate in particular super-resolution in the processing of low-frequency array telescope interferometric measurements (LOFAR), for the location of low-frequency radio sources in the sky.

14600915.label: Project Objectives
14600915.value: APol, the polarimeter - APol has three major components: a half-wave plate (HWP), a rotary table, and a polarizer. We will design/simulate/test two achromatic HWPs, together covering 450-1100 μm, the working band for the ASTE Transition-Edge-Sensor (TES) cameras (Takekoshi et al. 2012). The simulation will be carried out by using Zemax. We will design a torque motor driven rotary table, which avoids the problems that could arise from using gears in locations that are sandy and windy or have a high temperature range (e.g., deserts). Free-stand wire grids are usually used as polarizers for submillimeter instruments. They are, however, fragile and difficult to clean. To circumvent this issue, we will design a photolithographic wire grid for APol. New observing modes and data analysis- As the majority of our targets will be larger than the telescope field of view, the most efficient way to map the targets should be scanning. However, it would be necessary to take account of the response of the detector to the radiation, which is likely to vary during scanning. Scanning while the HWP is rotating is even more challenging. This “scan-rotate” mode of observation is what we want to achieve with APol and new data analysis methods should be developed for it. Student training- Most of the hardware will be designed by the students. For this purpose, we will train them to use software such as Solidworks (for mechanical design; http://www.solidworks.com) and Zemax (for optical design; www.zemax.com), and to use the equipments in the submillimeter laboratory.

14600915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14600915.value: We know much less about the birth of stars than their death (e.g., black holes). One reason is that molecular clouds, the stellar cradles, are so cold (~10K) that their thermal emissions operate at wavelengths in the submillimeter range, which can be effectively absorbed by water vapor in the atmosphere. Since it is still impossible to fly a big telescope to space, dry deserts offer the best alternative locations. The driest, Antarctica, is very difficult to reach, so Atacama in Northern Chile, the second driest desert, has gradually become the world’s capital of submillimeter astronomy. For example, the Atacama Submillimeter Telescope Experiment (ASTE), led by the National Astronomical Observatory of Japan, is a project to operate a high precision 10 m submillimeter telescope at a 4860-m site. Compared to self-gravity and turbulence, the role played by magnetic fields in stellar birth is far less understood. The so-called “magnetic topology problem”, i.e., how the field topology evolves as molecular clouds form and as clouds contract to form stars, has puzzled astronomers for decades. The major way to probe magnetic-field morphology of molecular clouds at various scales is through the polarization of thermal emissions, mainly from dust grains. The thermal emission is polarized perpendicularly to the fields. Making these observations successfully is very challenging: on top of the atmospheric noise/absorption, the degree of polarization is only a few percent. To improve the ability to make successful observations, we propose to build the ASTE polarimeter, APol. Previous surveys of cloud magnetic fields were carried out from Mauna Kea where, due to the atmospherical conditions, only the brightest cloud cores are observable. All these cloud cores have embedded stars already and thus magnetic fields are likely disturbed by stellar feedback. In order to understand the birth of stars, the pre-stellar fields are of course much more important. Given the favourable atmospheric conditions in Atacama, APol will be able to survey pre-stellar clouds and contribute to solving magnetic topology problems. APol can also contribute to studying magnetic fields of extragalactic cloud complexes. We have won financial support on APol hardware and equipments from our home institutions. Here we aim to earn support for postdoctoral and postgraduate researchers to carry out the plan. As Hong Kong’s first submillimeter astronomical instrument (indeed, the Hong Kong’s first instrument in the Atacama desert), APol will open an important and unique window for local astronomers and students to probe the universe. 恆星的誕生仍是個謎。其中一個原因是孕育恆星的分子雲的溫度僅數十K，他們的熱輻射波長在亞毫米範圍內，極易被地球大氣中的水汽所吸收, 故觀測難度高. 全球最乾燥的Atacama沙漠，正逐步發展成為亞毫米波天文學的世界中心。例如，日本國家天文台的Atacama亞毫米波望遠鏡（ASTE）就是在海跋4860米的高精度10米亞毫米波望遠鏡項。 相比於重力和湍流，磁場在恆星誕生所扮演的角色是最神秘的。所謂的“磁場拓撲結構問題”困擾著天文學家數十年。探測分子雲的磁場形態的主要方式是通過熱輻射的偏振。此觀察是非常具有挑戰性的：除了大氣噪聲及吸收，偏振度一般僅為百分之幾。 我們計畫打造ASTE偏振儀，APol。以往的磁場觀測多從夏威夷的Mauna Kea. 該區空氣條件只容許觀察最亮的雲核。這些雲核磁場可能已被恆星反饋干擾。為了了解恆星的誕生，恆星生成前的磁場當然要重要得多。憑藉Atacama優越的大氣條件，APOL就能觀測恆星生成前的磁拓撲結構。APOL將成為香港首個亞毫米波天文儀器和香港部署到Atacama沙漠的第一台儀器。這將打開本地的天文學家和學生探索宇宙的一個重要窗口。

14601015.value: 本計劃的主要目標是透過似然比掃描統計量的方法，去開發一套準確而計算上高效的程序，以應用於時間序列的多變點的統計推論。近數十年來，由於工程學、金融計量經濟學、遺傳學、環境計量學上大數據收集的進步，變點分析受到注目。在上述的應用範疇上，數據通常以一長序列的相依觀察值的形式出現。實驗性證據經常發現，在這些長數據列上會發生多次突然轉變。因此，為了把上述樣本分段以作分離建模，高效而又能簡單應用的長時間序列的變點的推論方法是有需要的。長時間序列的變點的估算是相當困難的。多變點的估算通常是透過優化某一目標函數而去搜尋變點的集合。但是，因為變點的可能組合隨樣本大小而指數地增長，優化過程會耗用非常大量的計算成本。儘管有人提出其他方法，例如遺傳演算法、動態規劃法、LASSO類方法，但是這些方法仍存有一定侷限，優化過程依然是相當困難的。相對於變點的點估算，變點的置信區間更具信息價值。這是因為置信區間囊括了最可能發生轉變的地方。但是，時間序列的變點的置信區間未曾被充份探討。變點估算的漸近分佈只是最近才被發現。儘管如此，其漸近分佈相當依賴於變點前和後的時間序列的結構，因此這一漸近分佈在實際情況中是很難套用的。 為了解決上述的有關計算上及置信區間上的重要問題，本計劃的主要目標是建立一套統計方法去為普遍的時間序列模型的變點進行快速的點估算及置信區間計算。具體來說，我們注意到變點的估算是相當取決於變點的最近鄰域，故此我們提出一套建基於似然比掃描統計量的快速估算程序。似然比掃描統計量的運用可把計算上密集的長時間序列多變點估算的優化問題分割為更簡單的短時間序列單變點估算的問題。假設樣本大小為n，與動態規劃法的傳統的n^2 階相比，新方法的計算複雜性可大大降低為n log⁡(n)階。除了點估算之外，為了應對變點估算其漸近分佈的複雜性，我們將建立一套自助法程序去估算變點估算的漸近分佈。我們將探索各種自助法，例如參數自助法、區塊自助法、原始自助法，的有效性，從而為時間序列的變點提供準確的置信區間。本計劃的成功將會為普遍的時間序列模型的變點其快速的點估算及置信區間計算帶來一套完善的程序。 隨高頻數據分析的急速增長，各個領域的問題需要應用到變點分析。目前的方法不能使分析有效地或準確地進行。本研究將提供有效而準確的變點分析。本研究將為各個科研領域，例如計量經濟學、電機工程學、環境工程學、金融學和物理學，推展重大的進步。

14601015.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601015.value: We have developed a general likelihood ratio scan method for efficient change-point inference in time series. The first step of the method employs a scanning window to efficiently detect possible change-points. The second step of the method utilizes the minimum description length principle to select the number of change point and model in each stationary segment of time series. The final step is a bootstrap procedure to construct confidence interval for each change-point. The consistency, convergence rate and the asymptotic distribution of the number and location of the change-points are established. The validity of the Bootstrap procedures for constructing confidence intervals are also established. Simulation experiments and real data examples are provided to demonstrate the statistical and computational efficiency of the proposed method.

14601115.label: Project Objectives
14601115.value: To propose several joint models for the analysis of the survival data with latent variables. The joint models comprise a CFA model to measure the latent risk factors using multiple observed variables and a MRL regression model to relate potential observed and latent risk factors to the MRLF of interest. Several MRL models including the AMRL model and PMRL model will be considered. To develop sound statistical methods for parameter estimation and establish asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators. Other relevant statistical inferences, such as model/variable selection and model diagnostics, will also be considered. To develop efficient and user-friendly computer programs that produce statistical results and codes that freely accessible to practitioners. To achieve novel applications related to real problems in Hong Kong and elsewhere. This research is motivated by a recent collaboration with colleagues at the Institute of Diabetes, Chinese University of Hong Kong in investigating the MRL for patients with serious diabetic complications (e.g., kidney or heart failure). Many risk factors (e.g., blood pressure, lipid, obesity, and glycemia) are latent, and measured by multiple indicators. Our main purpose is to determine the overall influence of these latent factors on the MRLF of interest. The conventional methods are incapable of revealing such insights. Hence, the joint CFA-MRL models are proposed.

14601115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601115.value: Mean residual life function (MRLF) provides the remaining life expectancy of a subject surviving up to a certain time point. Various studies on mean residual life (MRL) have significantly attracted attention from many fields, such as reliability research, survival analysis, and actuarial study. One of the primary interests in MRLF is to examine the potential risk factors by using regression analysis. Existing MRL regression models assume that risk factors (i.e., covariates) are fully observable and represented by a single observed variable. However, the potential risk factors for many situations in the medical, behavioral, and sociological research settings are latent and should thus be characterized by multiple indicators from different aspects. Conventional regression models manage the latent risk factors by simply incorporating one or more of their surrogates into the regression analysis. Such a separate inclusion of the latent variables' partial surrogates may cause problems, such as the incomplete measurement of latent variables, multicollinearity elicited by highly correlated covariates, and incomprehensible interpretation of the effects of interest. A more comprehensive analysis can be performed by using joint modeling approach, which comprises a factor analysis model for characterizing latent variables using multiple observed variables as well as a MRL regression model for examining the observed and latent risk factors of the MRLF of interest. To the best of our knowledge, this study is the first to introduce latent variables to MRL regression analysis. This study mainly aims to develop a class of joint models for the analysis of survival data with latent variables. The joint models contain two components: a factor analysis model and a MRL model. Several MRL models, including additive MRL model, proportional MRL model, and a class of transformed MRL models, are considered. We develop sound statistical methods for parameter estimation. Furthermore, we establish the asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators. Other relevant statistical inferences, including model/variable selection and model diagnostics, are also considered. Efficient and user-friendly computer programs are developed to produce the statistical results. These computer programs would be made freely available for practitioners. Lastly, the developed methodologies are applied to real problems in Hong Kong and elsewhere. 平均剩余寿命函数描述个体生存到某个时间点的平均剩余寿命。 其相关的研究已受到各个领域包括可靠性研究，生存分析，及 保险业的关注。研究平均剩余寿命函数的主要目的之一是用回归 分析探索影响这个函数变化的风险因子。现有的回归分析假设风 险因子是由单一的观测变量表示。然而在医学，行为学及社会科 学的许多研究中，风险因子可能是由多个观测变量共同刻画的潜 变量。传统的回归模型通常将潜变量的一个或部分观测变量当作 独立的因子进行回归分析。这种分析的局限性包括对潜变量的不 完全刻画，由高度相关的回归因子引起的多重共线性以及对潜变 量的影响效果缺乏整体解释。更合理的分析方法是联合因子分析 模型及生存分析模型，其中因子分析模型通过多元观测变量刻画 潜变量，而剩余寿命模型描述可观测的和潜在的风险因子怎样影 响平均剩余寿命函数。此研究首次将潜变量引入剩余寿命的回归 分析中。 本项目的主要目的是建立一类联合模型来分析含潜变量的生存分 析数据。联合模型由因子分析模型及剩余寿命模型两部分组成， 其中剩余寿命模型包括加性及乘性等模型。我们将研究有效的参 数估计方法，估计量的渐进性质以及相关的模型或变量选择等统 计推断方法。另外，我们将推广相关的统计计算程序以便有需要 者免费使用。最后，我们将运用所提出的方法解决香港或其它地 方的实际问题。

14601115.label: Realisation of objectives
14601115.value: We have fully achieved the project objectives specified in the proposal: 1. We have developed several joint models for the analysis of survival data with latent variables. The joint models comprise a CFA model to measure the latent risk factors using multiple observed variables and a MRL regression model to relate potential observed and latent risk factors to the MRLF of interest. Several MRL models including the AMRL model and PMRL model have been considered. The objective in Item 1 of Section 5.2 (related to model establishment) is fully achieved. 2. We have developed statistical methods for parameter estimation and established asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators. Other relevant statistical inferences, such as variable selection and statistical diagnostics, have also been considered. The objectives in Item 2 of Section 5.2 (related to inference methodology) are fully achieved. 3. We have developed efficient and user-friendly computer programs that produce statistical results and codes that freely accessible to practitioners. The computer codes, many of which were written in freely available software, such as R and Rcpp, have been published along with papers or provided in freely available websites for general use. The objectives in Item 3 of Section 5.2 (related to computer programs) are fully achieved. 4. We have applied the developed methodologies to analyze many real datasets that are relevant to Hong Kong and elsewhere. The real-life applications include, but are not limited to, (1) studies on diabetic complications based on the data collected by the Institute of Diabetes at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, (2) studies of osteoporosis prevention and control for old Chinese men in Hong Kong, (3) studies on different kinds of cancers, (4) studies on the Alzheimer’s disease, (5) studies on the National Longitudinal Surveys of Youth in the US, (6) a multi-center AIDS cohort study, (7) a study on nursing home data, and (8) a study on the determinants of the capital structure of Chinese-listed companies. Important findings and insights have been obtained through these real applications. The objectives in Item 3 of Section 5.2 (related to applications) are fully achieved.

14601115.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601115.value: Our major findings and research outcomes are represented by 13 publications; see "Research Output" in Section 8 of Part C). Specifically, 1. We have developed several joint models for the analysis of survival data with latent variables, such as AMRL models with latent variables, PMRL models with latent variables, additive-proportional MRL models, and semiparametric failure time models with latent variables; please refer to Items 2, 10, and 13 in Section 8. In addition, we have developed other survival models for various time-to-event data, such as additive rate models with recurrent event data, varying coefficient additive hazards models with right censored data, and semiparametric non-mixture cure model with interval-censored failure time data (Items 1, 9, and 11 in Section 8), and other joint models with latent variables (Items 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 12 in Section 8). 2. We have developed statistical methods for parameter estimation and established asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators. Maximum likelihood, estimating equation, and Bayesian methods have been developed for parameter estimation. Other relevant statistical inferences, such as variable selection and statistical diagnostics, have also been considered. Please refer to Items 1 to 13 in Section 8. 3. We have developed efficient and use-friendly computer programs to produce statistical results. All the computer codes have been published or provided on websites that are freely accessible to practitioners (see the corresponding papers in Section 8). 4. We have applied the proposed methodologies to many real studies and obtained important findings. The real applications include (1) studies on diabetic complications based on the data collected by the Institute of Diabetes at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (Items 2, 10, and 13 in Section 8), (2) studies on osteoporosis prevention and control for old Chinese men in Hong Kong (Items 3 and 7 in Section 8), (3) studies on different kinds of cancers (Items 1 and 11 in Section 8), (4) a study on the Alzheimer’s disease (Item 12 in Section 8), (5) studies of the National Longitudinal Surveys of Youth in the US (Items 5 and 8 in Section 8), (6) a multi-center AIDS cohort study (Item 6 in Section 8), (7) a study on nursing home data (Item 8 in Section 8), and (8) a study on the determinants of the capital structure of Chinese-listed companies (Item 4 in Section 8).

14601115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14601115.value: The models considered in this project can be extended to incorporate complex longitudinal and image data. Moreover, dependent censoring, interval censoring and missing data are frequently encountered in substantive research. Hence, joint modeling approaches for simultaneously accommodating these important features are worthy of further investigation and will be considered in the future.

14601415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601415.value: 本項目計劃研究基於金剛石氮-空位缺陷的脈澤和微波放大器。脈澤是微波 波段 (頻率0.3~300 GHz, 波長1000~1 mm)的相干受激輻射。作為激光的前身，脈澤在激光發展史上有重要地位。激光在科研和工業中有廣泛應用，但脈澤的應用則相對較少。這主要是受限於沒有方便的脈澤器。現有的氣態或者自由電子脈澤需要真空環境，而固態脈澤則需要極低溫冷卻。最近有實驗演示基於有機材料磁性雜質的脈澤，它可以工作於室溫。但是該脈澤只能工作於脈衝模式（重複頻率僅～1Hz）。本項目計劃研究用金剛石中的磁性缺陷 - 氮-空位缺陷來實現脈澤及微波放大器。 金剛石中氮-空位色心具有脈澤所需的一系列優良特性 - 室溫極長的自旋壽命、高效的自旋光學泵浦率、 及大樣品體積。現有實驗也已經演示微波腔與金剛石色心的相干耦合。我們的初步預研表明金剛石色心很有希望實現室溫固態脈澤。 本項目中我們將系統地研究室溫金剛石脈澤和微波放大器。我們將設計並數值模擬實際的物理系統 - 包括自旋弛豫、光學泵浦、微波腔等等。 本項目的成功完成會有助於推動微波科技的發展。

14601415.label: Realisation of objectives
14601415.value: (1) We have systematically studied the diamond microwave maser and amplifier system that uses nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond as the gain medium. In the simulation, we studied the conditions for masing and amplification. We show that the diamond maser and microwave amplification are feasible under realistic conditions: cavity Q factor ~50,000, diamond size ~3×3×0.5 mm^3, and NV center concentration ~2 ppm, with the 532 nm optical pump threshold ~3 W for microwave amplifying and ~4 W for masing. For a pump power <10 W, it is possible to achieve masing with an output power >10 nW, a coherence time ~minutes, and a linewidth ~mHz. As a room-temperature microwave amplifier, the noise temperature is as low as ~0.3 K under pump power <10 W. We further studied the effect of temperature fluctuations on the maser coherence. (2) To counteract the effects of the temperature fluctuations on the maser coherence, we studied the scheme of using "bad cavity" and "good spin coherence" for superradiance masing (in which the maser frequency is pinned to the spin frequency which is very stable than to the cavity frequency which is vulnerable to the temperature fluctuation). The conditions for realizing the superradiance maser (including the NV centre concentration, the size of diamond, and the spin decoherence) as well as alternative physical systems (rare-earth spins, e.g.) have been investigated systematically. (3) For applications of masers and microwave amplification in metrology (a most important application of coherence microwave sources), especially near the critical point of masing (where the microwave amplification is just below the masing threshold and is therefore the most sensitive to external parameter perturbation), we have established a general theoretical formalism, namely, the quantum Fisher information theory for non-Hermitian systems (systems that have dissipation and pumping, like the maser system). Using this theory, we show rigorously that the so called "exceptional point" of non-Hermitian systems, which have sub-linear energy dependence on a perturbative parameter and hence diverging susceptibility, have no diverging enhancement of metrology sensitivity, since the susceptibility divergence is counteracted by the vanishing distinguishability of states (due to state coalescence at the exceptional point). This theory provides a systematic tool for analyzing the recent experiments on exceptional point based metrology and future works along the line. (4) We have proposed the importance of many-body correlations in maser systems using good spin coherence time. The potential effects of many-body interactions between spins in the maser systems are unique (unlike the conventional laser systems where the interactions between atoms are negligible). The investigation along this direction is on-going and can be extended to a future project.

14601415.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601415.value: 1. We investigated systematically the realistic conditions for room-temperature diamond maser (with details given in a patent application). We show that under readily accessible conditions a diamond maser with coherence time ~10^5 s is feasible. Also, we predict that the noise temperature can be as low as 140 mK. The study of the realistic conditions for diamond maser laid the foundation for experimental realization of the idea. Recently, the scheme has been demonstrated in experiments and the experimentalists are working along the direction to improve the coherence and efficiency of diamond maser. 2. We established a systematic theory for applying maser and microwave amplifier (and related systems) in realistic metrology. We use the exact formalism of quantum Fisher information to characterize the sensitivity of the parameter estimation of a non-Hermitian system (that has dissipation and gain - such as masers). We find that no dramatic sensitivity enhancement at the so-called expcetional point (where the state coalescence occurs). We show that the susceptibility divergence at the exceptional point is cancelled by the level coalescence (in which the states become indistinguishable). This work provides a solid formalism for analysing sensing schemes based on non-equilibrium systems.

14601415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14601415.value: In the future, it would be interesting to develop diamond maser systems in experiments and explore other possible physical systems (such as rare earth spins). Also, the idea of superradiance maser needs further investigation. Another important direction is the many-body correlations in interaction spins in the maser gain medium (which is absent in usual laser systems). There is also interest in extending the idea of exploring good spin coherence for masers to other wavebands, such as in radio-frequency superradiance amplification with ultralong coherence time.

14601415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14601415.value: Maser is expected to enable enormous applications, including enhanced magnetic resonance spectroscopy, deep-space communication, radar and positioning, high-precision clock, and cosmology observation. The existing maser systems require harsh operating conditions: Gas masers require high vacuum, solid-state masers need liquid-helium temperature, and free-electron masers require large accelerator. Diamond maser is the first solid-state maser system that can work continuously at room temperature. The invention of maser opens up opportunities of a broad range of applications. In this study, we carried out a systematic study for realizing diamond maser and microwave amplification under realistic conditions and the conditions for optimizing the performance. The study facilitates the experimental implementation and the practical applications of diamond maser. For realistic applications of diamond maser and microwave amplification in metrology (a most important applications of coherent microwave sources), we established a general theory, based on the quantum Fisher information formalism, for evaluating the measurement sensitivity near the critical point of masing (the region where the microwave amplificaiton is the most sensitive to external parameter perturbation). This theory provides a useful tool for maser-based metrology.

14601515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601515.value: Impervious surfaces (IS), as the major land surface modification of rapid urbanization in many metropolitans in the past decades, have been widely recognized as imperative indicator for not only urban environmental issues (e.g. water quality, aerosols, urban heat island and climate change) but also socio-economic issues (e.g. population distribution and urban planning) from local, regional to global scales. Pearl River Delta (PRD) is such a typical metropolitan with large area of IS, which have been leading to various environmental and socio-economic problems, and thus urgently require accurate estimation of IS for timely monitoring and understanding its urbanization processes. Given its importance, numerous methods have been developed for IS estimation (ISE) from satellite data. However, most of them were tested in temperate continental areas and with only optical satellite data. Only a few of them considered the case in subtropical humid areas like PRD, where climatology (e.g. rainy and cloudy) and phenology are special and different from temperate regions and thus cause great difficulties for remote sensing studies. To overcome the difficulties, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data has been synergized with optical data in subtropical regions in the past several years, but only single polarization SAR data were employed and the accuracy is far from satisfactory. Multi-polarimetric SAR data have been frequently reported to be able to provide much richer information in urban areas, while its potential application in ISE is still underexplored and many challenging problems remain unaddressed. The general aims of this research are to: 1) Investigate the full potential of multi-polarimetric SAR data, including dual, compact and fully polarimetric SAR data, for improving ISE in subtropical urban areas; and 2) Develop effective fusion methodology for synergizing optical and polarimetric SAR data at both feature and decision levels from city to metropolitan scales. The outcomes of this proposed research will not only provide a comprehensive feature extraction framework for polarimetric SAR data, but also evaluate the effectiveness of these polarimetric SAR features by their contributions to ISE at both feature and decision levels. Additionally, as a validation of the proposed methodology, PRD will be employed for case studies from city scale and metropolitan scale. The implementation of this project can serve as a general model to promote the applications of optical and polarimetric SAR data in accurate ISE of other humid subtropical urban areas in the world. 過去數十年，快速城市化産生了許多城市群，而不透水面作爲城市化在改變地表的主要表現，已逐漸變成了城市環境（如：水質、氣溶膠、城市熱島和氣候變化）及相關社會經濟問題（如：城市人口分布和城市規劃）的重要因素。珠江三角洲正是這樣一個擁有大量城市不透水面覆蓋的典型城市群。珠江三角洲的快速城市化已導致了嚴重的環境和社會經濟問題，因而急需對其不透水面覆蓋進行持續而準確的監測，從而更好理解其城市化過程幷促進城市化管理。 由于其重要性，應用衛星技術對城市不透水面進行估算已有大量的方法。然而，大部分的方法只是針對溫帶地區的城市進行測試，且只使用了光學衛星數據。只有少數研究考慮了氣候（多雲多雨）和物候都較爲特別的亞熱帶濕潤地區的城市，而遙感技術在這些地區的應用面臨更多挑戰。近年來，爲克服相關困難，合成孔徑雷達（SAR）被用于輔助光學遙感進行協同估算不透水面。然而，這些研究大多只采用單極化SAR技術，且估算精度還不能滿足需求。多極化SAR技術已被頻繁報道用于城市區域可提供更爲有用的信息，但其在城市不透水面估算方面還缺乏深入研究，其中許多相關的難題尚待解决。 本項目旨在：1）研究多極化SAR數據，包括雙極化、簡縮極化和全極化SAR數據，在城市不透水面估算方面的潜力和作用；2）在特徵級和决策級上研究開發融合光學和極化SAR數據的方法，幷應用于城市尺度和城市群尺度的不透水面估算。本項目的研究成果將提供一個多極化SAR數據特徵分析的框架以及綜合評估這些極化特徵在不透水面估算中的作用。此外，以珠江三角洲爲例，應用所提出的方法進行城市尺度和城市群尺度的測試。項目所研發的方法可作爲光學遙感與多極化SAR數據融合的一般模型，幷應用于世界其它亞熱帶濕潤地區的城市不透水面估算。

14601515.label: Realisation of objectives
14601515.value: Over the four objectives of the project, all of the scheduled research has been completed. Details of the realisation of the four objectives are summarized as follows. 1) An effective, efficient and automatic co-registration approach was developed between optical and polarimetric SAR data (Zhang et al., 2016, AGIS). Experimental results demonstrate the promising effectiveness of the proposed approach with a significant reduction of RMSE compared with the initial homologous points. The proposed approach is especially applicable in urban areas where the uncertain errors of homologous points in SAR images are higher due to the speckles and foreshortening, layover and shadows from tall buildings. 2) Polarimetric features were extracted comprehensively from polarimetric SAR data including fully polarimetric and dual polarimetric data obtained at various frequencies, various resolutions and various polarizations in different cities of Pearl River Delta (Zhang et al., 2016, LAND; Zhang et al., 2018, PHOTO; Zhang et al., 2018, LAND). We evaluated the effectiveness and contributions of the different polarimetric features by synergizing them with optical data at both feature and decision levels, as well as the evaluation of their scale effects (Xu et al., 2017, JAG; Xu et al., 2017, JSTARS; Zhang et al., 2019, JSTARS). 3) A multi-level optical and SAR remote sensing data fusion technology framework was developed, and a fusion system based on pixel level (data level), feature level, decision level and mixed level was established (Zhang et al., 2018, JAG). The spectral characteristics and spatial characteristics of optical data were established. It is effectively integrated with the backscattering and polarization characteristics of SAR data, thereby improving the accuracy of urban land cover, including urban impervious surfaces. 4) The results were validated in different cities and the whole PRD region from city to metropolitan scales. At the city scale, the results were validated in 11 cities, including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Dongguan, Zhaoqing, Foshan, Huizhou, Jiangmen, Zhongshan, Hong Kong and Zhuhai-Macau. At the metropolitan scale, the annual changes of impervious surface were extracted and validated from 2000 to 2015. Through the analysis of urbanization space and time variation characteristics of PRD, a standardized urban development index (NDUDI) based on urban impervious surface was proposed to evaluate the urbanization patterns of different cities in PRD (Xu et al., 2018, IJRS).

14601515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601515.value: The research team has established a multi-level optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) remote sensing fusion framework, which was applied in the Pearl River Delta (PRD). First, we proposed an effective, efficient and automatic co-registration approach between optical and polarimetric SAR data (Zhang et al., 2016, AGIS). Experimental results demonstrate the promising effectiveness of the proposed approach with a significant reduction of RMSE compared with the initial homologous points. The proposed approach is especially applicable in urban areas where the uncertain errors of homologous points in SAR images are higher due to the speckles and foreshortening, layover and shadows from tall buildings. Second, we extracted polarimetric features comprehensively from polarimetric SAR data including fully polarimetric and dual polarimetric data obtained at various frequencies, various resolutions and various polarizations (Zhang et al., 2016, LAND; Zhang et al., 2018, PHOTO; Zhang et al., 2018, LAND). We also evaluated the effectiveness and contributions of the different polarimetric features by synergizing them with optical data at both feature and decision levels, as well as the evaluation of their scale effects (Xu et al., 2017, JAG; Xu et al., 2017, JSTARS; Zhang et al., 2019, JSTARS). Third, a multi-level optical and SAR remote sensing data fusion technology framework was developed, and a fusion system based on pixel level (data level), feature level, decision level and mixed level was established (Zhang et al., 2018, JAG). The spectral characteristics and spatial characteristics of optical data were established. It is effectively integrated with the backscattering and polarization characteristics of SAR data, thereby improving the accuracy of urban land cover, including urban impervious surfaces. The results were validated in different cities and the whole PRD region from city to metropolitan scales. Fourth, the short-term and long-term changes of urban land cover change are explored (Zhang et al., 2018, Sensors; Fonseka et al., 2019, RS). It was found that in addition to the seasonal changes of natural surface cover such as vegetation and water bodies, the artificial impervious surface in cities also exhibits certain seasonal changes. Seasonal phenomena and their impact on remote sensing monitoring of long-term land changes were analyzed and discussed in depth. In addition, through the analysis of urbanization space and time variation characteristics of PRD, a standardized urban development index (NDUDI) based on urban impervious surface was proposed to evaluate the urbanization patterns of different cities in PRD (Xu et al., 2018, IJRS).

14601515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14601515.value: The general aims of this research are to investigate the full potential of multi-polarimetric SAR data for improving ISE in subtropical urban areas, and to develop effective fusion methodology for synergizing optical and polarimetric SAR data at both feature and decision levels from city to metropolitan scales. All the research objectives have been during the past two and half years’ research. Great potential for further development goes to the applications of the proposed methodology for monitoring other urban land covers and applications of the estimated impervious surfaces in the environmental and ecological impacts of urbanization in and beyond the Pearl River Delta, e.g. urban flood risk assessment, urban heat island and urban ecosystems.

14601515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14601515.value: The research team has established a multi-level optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) remote sensing data fusion technology framework, which was effectively applied to monitor the urban impervious surface in the Pearl River Delta (PRD). Temporal and spatial characteristics of the urban impervious surfaces in the PRD in the past 30 years were analyzed. First, a multi-level optical and SAR remote sensing data fusion technology framework was developed, and a fusion system based on pixel level (data level), feature level, decision level and mixed level was established. It is effectively integrated with the backscattering and polarization characteristics of SAR data, thereby improving the accuracy of urban land cover, including urban impervious surfaces. Second, it was found that in addition to the seasonal changes of natural surface cover such as vegetation and water bodies, the artificial impervious surface in cities also exhibits certain seasonal changes. Seasonal phenomena and their impact on remote sensing monitoring of long-term land changes were analyzed and discussed in depth. In addition, through the analysis of urbanization space and time variation characteristics of PRD, a standardized urban development index (NDUDI) based on urban impervious surface was proposed to evaluate the urbanization patterns of different cities in PRD.

14601715.label: Project Objectives
14601715.value: Improve understanding on the impacts of forward guidance and its unwinding. This is important for central banks to design and conduct optimal monetary policy. It also sheds light on how to exit from existing monetary policy scheme smoothly without disturbing financial market stability and economic growth. The results are also of value to financial institutions. Aware of the possible consequences of unconventional monetary policy, they can actively update investment strategies and portfolio choices to benefit from policy changes. Analyze how different market participants interpret and react to the same policy. The choices of monetary policy convey information relevant to investment outcomes, i.e. asset prices, project returns, economic growth, which affects financial institutions’ investment decisions and portfolio choices. Understand how market participants respond to current unconventional monetary policy can also help policy makers better manage expectations and better forecast impacts of the policy. Keeping expectations consistent with the central banks’ objective is critical because expectations (i.e. deflationary expectations) can be self-fulfilling in driving the actual outcomes and it is difficult to change expectations when they become entrenched. Produce conceptual and methodological advances based on insights of global games and heterogeneous agent models.

14601715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601715.value: In the effort of promoting macroeconomic stabilization and financial market health during the global financial crisis of 2007, major central banks, such as Bank of England, Federal Reserve Bank and European Central bank, have committed to keep the interest rate low for a sufficiently long time. Such unconventional monetary policy, known as forward guidance, has become the predominant tool for central banks to manage market expectations when the interest rate hit the zero lower bound. Due to its unconventional nature, whether and how forward guidance improves financial stability and economic growth remain open questions. The consequences of unwinding such an unconventional policy are also unclear. This proposal seeks to improve understanding on the role of forward guidance by addressing the following questions: 1. What can central banks do to unwind the unconventional policy without generating significant uncertainty and volatility in financial markets? 2. How do financial market participants, in particular institutional investors, respond to forward guidance? How would their aggregate actions affect the financial market conditions and economic fundamentals? 3. Is the central banks’ low interest rate commitment effective in promoting financial market stability and economic growth? 2007年金融危机爆发之后，为了促进宏观环境和金融市场的稳定健康发展，包括英格兰银行，美联储和欧洲中央银行在内的各主要央行纷纷承若维持低利率环境。此类非常规货币政策被称为“前瞻指引”。当利率已经触及零利率下限，该货币工具成为各央行调控市场预期的主要工具。“前瞻指引”能否有效地提高金融稳定性和促进经济增长目前？当时机成熟时，逆向操作会造成什么样的后果？这些问题尚未明确。本方案力求通过解答下列问题来提高对“前瞻指引”这一非常规货币政策的理解。 1．央行应该如何进行逆向操作才能避免造成金融动荡？ 2．机构投资者应该如何应对“前瞻指引”？他们的行动又将如何影响金融环境和经济基本面？ 3．央行的低利率承诺是否能有效提高金融市场稳定性和经济增长？

14601715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601715.value: We propose an asset pricing model with heterogeneous agents allocating capital to the stock and bond markets to optimize their portfolios, utilizing the dynamic interaction between the two markets. While some agents focus on the stock market and have more expertise in it, the others specialize in the bond market. Based on their comparative advantages in a particular market, heterogeneous agents constantly revise their investment portfolios by taking into account the time-varying stock–bond return comovements and the changing market conditions. Agents׳ collective investment behavior shapes the stock–bond interlinkage, which feedbacks on their subsequent capital allocations. Using monthly US stock and bond data from January 1990 to June 2014, we estimate the vector autoregression model with threshold and Markov switching mechanisms. We find evidence in support of flight-to-quality and show that it is mainly driven by the technical traders who actively sell stocks and buy bonds during periods of high market uncertainty.

14601715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14601715.value: Our model can be extended in various dimensions to provide more sophisticated theoretical and numerical results on the stock and bond joint price dynamics. First, one can allow agents to actively switch between different expectation rules and/or market states. Second, one may consider different switching mechanisms and evaluate their profitability in both stock and bond markets. The third extension is to explore the stability conditions for the joint price dynamics in a more complex nonlinear framework. Finally, one may relax the assumptions on comovement expectations by heterogeneous agents and enable more disaggregated trading behavior.

14601715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14601715.value: We find that agents tend to direct new investment flows into both stock and bond markets when the market volatility is low, whereas they tend to move the money out of the stock market and into the bond market when the market volatility is high. Moreover, we find that chartists with comparative advantage in the stock market play a dominant role in driving the flight-to-quality phenomenon. Behavioral heterogeneity that is conditional on the market states thus provides an additional channel to understand the time-varying stock–bond return relations.

14601915.label: Project Objectives
14601915.value: This project will construct a comprehensive database on the parameters of the resource sector in China, such as the geographical distribution of mineral resources, productivity of the mining industries, and the ownership structure and scale of mining enterprises etc. The database will cover all the provinces and selected prefectures for multiple years (at least the recent decade or so when relatively complete systematic statistics are available). This project will understand the strategies of the Chinese state’s intervention in the resource sector by conducting archival and field research on the Chinese government’s policies on the resource sector, with a focus on the policies of privatization and nationalization/consolidation of mining industries. It will analyze and compare the central and local policies to find out how the central directives are translated into concrete local actions and how local practices vary across regions. This project will assess the effects of the Chinese government’s resource policies with regard to the management of resource wealth and the socioeconomic impacts of the resources. It will evaluate if the state intervention in the resource sector can improve the performance of the mining industries and address the adverse effects of resource abundance on economic development and social stability. It will try to explain the impacts of state intervention or the lack of them. This project will produce a series of research articles for publication in major international refereed journals of political science, economics and/or area studies, and eventually a book manuscript. At various stages of the project, the research team will present the research findings at international and regional conferences.

14601915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601915.value: A growing body of comparative studies suggests that countries endowed with rich natural resources such as fuels and minerals tend to suffer sluggish economic development, weak political institutions and frequent social conflicts, which in general are referred to as the curse of natural resources. However, not enough attention has been paid to how the governments of resource-rich countries respond to such adverse effects of their resource endowment and whether the state responses are effective or not. This study mends this gap in the existing literature by conducting a case study on China, a country that hosts abundant mineral resources in many of its localities, and, similar to other resource-rich developing countries, suffers various socioeconomic, political and environmental problems caused by the existence of resources. The Chinese government, aware of some of these problems, has tried to intervene by, for example, consolidating and nationalizing the mining industries, with an underlying assumption that the state can better manage the resource wealth than the private sector can. Against such background, the proposed research will examine the strategies devised by the Chinese government and evaluate their effectiveness in alleviating the adverse effects of the resource wealth. It will adopt a subnational approach by focusing on subnational regions in China and closely examining the local conditions and practices. And it will combine qualitative archival and case studies with large-N statistical analysis. The mixed research methods are expected to not only reveal the correlations between different variables but also identify the causal mechanisms behind the observed patterns. This project makes both practical and theoretical contributions. Practically, it can help us better understand and critically evaluate the Chinese strategies of managing the resource sector and its adverse effects. It can generate valuable policy implications not only for China, but also for other resource-rich developing countries. Theoretically, it can advance the discourse and debate of the resource curse to a new stage by bringing in the state as an active player and examining whether and how it can moderate the impacts of the nature’s endowment. 比较研究发现能源矿产资源丰裕的国家往往经济发展缓慢、政治体制羸弱以及社会冲突频仍，这一系列现象被统称为资源诅咒。但是，现有研究并未充分考察资源丰裕国家的政府如何应对资源诅咒以及这些应对措施是否有效。 通过对中国的实证研究，本项目旨在弥补现有文献的不足。由于中国很多地区拥有大量的矿产资源，这些地区也像其它资源丰裕的发展中国家一样面临着各种经济、政治、社会和环境问题。实际上，中国政府也试图通过如资源整合等手段来解决一些由资源禀赋所带来的负面问题，而这些政府干预措施的一个重要前提假设就是国家能够比市场和私营企业更好地管理矿产资源和它们所带来的问题。 本研究会详细考察中国的资源政策并分析它们应对资源诅咒现象的有效性。与现有大多数以国家为个体的资源诅咒研究不同，本研究会着眼于中国地方层级的政府行为。通过结合定性和定量的研究方法，本研究旨在发现国家干预对于资源诅咒的影响并揭示出内在的因果机制。 本研究兼具理论和现实意义。一方面，它有助于我们了解中国政府的资源管理政策并对其有效性加以批判性分析。研究成果不仅对中国、也对其它资源丰裕的发展中国家的政策制定具有重大的借鉴意义。另一方面，这项研究也会考察和评价国家干预在资源诅咒现象中发挥的作用，从而改变已有的资源诅咒研究普遍忽视国家主观能动性的现状，将这一领域的研究推向新的高度。

14601915.label: Realisation of objectives
14601915.value: Due to the suddenly increased administrative duties on the PI in 2016-17, the project duration was extended from 24 to 35 months. Despite the one-year interruption, the main objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. The research team has collected rich empirical data from various sources and field research and built up a large data set that covers the years of 1999-2015 and more than 200 socioeconomic, political, geographical and demographic variables on China. Based on the rich qualitative and quantitative data collected, the project finds that the Chinese government actively intervenes in the management of the resource sector. Chinese local governments in resource-rich regions adopt diverse policies to address the negative externalities that the mining industries impose on local citizens and to mitigate the adverse socioeconomic impacts of the resource sector, especially with regard to social stability. The Chinese government utilizes a variety of unconventional tools such as political ambiguity and selective corruption control to achieve its policy goals. The project has produced four scholarly articles, two already published in the China Quarterly and Journal of Chinese Governance, and two currently under review by the China Quarterly and Governance respectively. And the PI's book manuscript is near completion. The research findings have been presented at 8 internationally recognized conferences. In addition, the PI has been invited to deliver 9 lectures in academic institutions in Hong Kong, Mainland China and the United States. The research has attracted a fair amount of attention regionally and internationally from not only the academia, but also the media and policy circles.

14601915.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601915.value: This project finds that the Chinese government has actively intervened in the resource sector with a variety of policy tools to ameliorate its adverse socioeconomic effects, especially with regard to the negative impacts on social stability. We find that Chinese local governments in resource-rich regions have adopted reactive and preemptive measures, especially redistributive policies, to address the negative externalities that the mining industries impose on local citizens and to mitigate the tension between the two parties and the widely existing popular grievance. The Chinese government's intervention has largely contained resource-triggered social conflicts to limited scales and isolated cases, and prevented China from suffering major symptoms of the resource curse as seen in other resource-rich developing countries. Specifically, this project has produced four journal articles that have been published or are under review by international refereed journals and one book manuscript: 1. The 2017 China Quarterly article analyzes the various reactive and preemptive strategies that Chinese local governments adopt to resolve or prevent resource-triggered social conflicts, and explains why they are willing and capable to do so. 2. The 2017 Journal of Chinese Governance argues that higher-level Chinese authorities intentionally create political ambiguity to direct subordinate governments towards certain policy goals. This is true in many policy areas including the resource sector. 3. The article that is currently under review by the China Quarterly argues that the Chinese government, instead of heavily relying on forceful repression, actually prefers non-confrontational, redistributive means to address the negative externalities of the mining industries and ease the popular grievance and tension in resource-rich regions. The findings provide useful lessons for other resource-rich countries to handle the socioeconomic problems associated with the resource economy. 4. The article currently under review by Governance discovers that the Chinese Communist party-state strategically uses corruption control to facilitate its broader policy agendas. The findings are highly original and relevant to policy implementation not only in the resource sector but also in other policy areas. They have far-reaching implications for understanding the operation and resilience of single-party authoritarian regimes. 5. The book manuscript analyzes how resource abundance profoundly shapes the triangular relations between the state, the capital and the labor force, the three key stakeholders in the resource economy. It makes novel and nuanced arguments that advance the existing debate on the resource curse as well as the studies on local governance and development in China.

14601915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14601915.value: This project yields interesting findings and valuable data that go far beyond the original objectives and can lead to more stimulating research along different directions. First, some empirical evidence collected during this project suggests that mining companies of different scales and ownership structures may play qualitatively different roles in local development and governance in resource-rich regions. Thus the PI is considering developing another research project to systematically investigate this phenomenon. Second, the PI discovers original empirical evidence suggesting that the Chinese government strategically uses corruption control to achieve its broad policy goals, which deserves thorough examination in future research. If conditions allow, the PI will pursue this research direction to further investigate how selective corruption control affects actual policy implementation. Third, this project has collected a vast amount of statistical data on more than 200 variables during the time span of 1999-2015, which can be extended to longer time series. The wide range of variables can sustain a lot of exciting research on different topics. The PI is exploring opportunities to collaborate with other scholars to fully utilize these data.

14601915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14601915.value: Existing studies find that rich mineral resources often give rise to socioeconomic problems such as economic underdevelopment and social conflicts. However, limited research has been done on how resource-rich states may respond to the so-called resource curse. By studying the case of China, this research finds that the Chinese state has actively intervened in the resource sector and devised various policies, especially redistributive schemes, to address the negative impacts that mining industries generate on the society and local citizens. The findings suggest that resource-rich states, with sufficient awareness and capacity, can well design mechanisms to cope with the resource curse, at least with regard to social stability.

14602015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14602015.value: This research project is an analysis of a large body of ci 詞poetry written during the late Qing period (1840-1911), focusing on the transformation of the practice of cishi 詞史. It argues that the concept and practice of cishi have initiated reflections among poets on the style of ci poetry and changed their form of expression. Understanding the transitional changes of works in this period will help us to reconsider the common impression that late Qing ci poetry is “conservative”, “obscure” and “unrelated to the real world”. There are two objectives of the study. First of these is to define the nature of cishi poetry (ci that reflects or relates to historic events known to or experienced by poets). I will research into different forms of expression and outline a gradual and subtle change in writing practices. The second objective is to explain how the change is related to the “stubbornly traditional” image of ci towards the end of Qing and early Republican era. Reaching its pinnacle in the Song dynasty, ci has formed a unique tradition in form, styles, subject matter and language. It is commonly believed that ci is more suitable for expressing personal feelings than narrating events or casting satire. Despite being an independent genre, ideas from shi 詩poetics have been continuously introduced in order to elevate the status of ci. The notion cishi comes from shishi 詩史, and gained great popularity among the ci poets who experienced the upheavals of late Qing, and felt the need to record current events and voice out their social and political concerns through ci. The term cishi recurs often in the commentary of contemporary critics of the poets. The introduction of cishi to both the theory and practice of ci confronted the poets with the lyrical tradition of ci and the narrative nature of recording shi 史. This research illustrates the tensions between narrative and lyrical, arising both in the discussion of poetics and associated writing practices. By re-evaluating the nature of ci and cishi, poets gradually “return” to a more traditional lyric mode of expression. They are, however, not acted upon by the tradition, but create something new by recapturing the old. The project will review and explain this change in an attempt to shed new light on the nature and development of late Qing ci poetry. 有清一代，詞的創作與理論互相帶動，相輔相成，清詞成就極高，不但可與宋詞媲美，更有突過前人之處。詞復興於清，是現代詞學研究者的共識。但另一方面，晚清民初的詞卻總是給人保守、陳舊、晦澀、脫離現實的印象。這固然與部分詞人的遺老身分相關，但卻不能視之為完滿的解釋。本計劃旨在從「詞史」這個概念入手，考察晚清詞人在敘事與抒情上的選擇取捨及其詞體觀的變化，以重新評價詞在晚清的嬗變發展。 晚清以降，時局變化激烈，「文變染乎世情」在晚清文學中得到了淋漓盡至的演繹，詩、文、小說等體裁均有「革命」之說，但詞似乎特別頑固，故學者對晚清詞的發展有「缺席革命」的提法。不過，「詞史」的概念卻是其來有自。經周濟大力標舉後，更是晚清詞壇上重要的審美價值。晚清詞人在不同程度上都回應了這個概念，探討詞如何反映時事，在創作實踐上也作出了不同形式的試驗。本計劃之目標為：一，詞史概念在創作中的實踐，關注其敘事、記人、抒情的具體形式。二，晚清詞家對詞史概念的探討、實踐與詞體漸予人晦澀印象的關係。

14602015.label: Realisation of objectives
14602015.value: The project has fulfilled the objectives listed out. I have explored the changing concept of cishi and how the concept affected writing of ci poems from late Qing to early Republican era. Based on several pivotal historic events, I have analyzed the related ci poems in terms of how they narrated the historic events, recorded important personages and revealed their critical views and feelings. Since these functions are considered to be that of the shi (history) instead of ci tradition, some ci scholars questioned the appropriateness of adopting the idea of cishi in real writing practice. The tension between narrative and lyrical approach of ci writing was clearly present. Innovative writers deployed different methods to add elements of history while retaining the essence of ci. However, eventually, we can observe a return to the lyrical tradition in ci writing, and historic events and personages are only hinted by using metaphors and allusions. As metaphors and allusions may sometimes be ambiguous in revealing exact events, modern readers find them difficult to understand immediately. Leaders of New Cultural Movement, therefore, criticized it as "conservative" and "unrelated to the real world". My research argues that these comments are a fairly superficial observation. In short, the 5 listed objectives are all covered in the project.

14602015.label: Major findings and research outcome
14602015.value: Research Output: 1 Monograph, 3 Journal Articles 3 Conference paper presentations Major Findings After Zhou Ji advocated the idea of cishi (poet-historian/ poetic history), it became an important and popular notion among poets of late Qing. While the discussion of the concept centered around the essential elements of history, such as narrating and judging important historic/political events, in real writing practices, tensions arose as ci poems had a tradition of writing love and beauties, and its nature mainly being lyrical. Late Qing poets aroused by social and political unrest were eager to vent their frustrations through ci poems. Many ci poems were able to reveal the poets' immediate reactions towards major events. Many poets chose to use direct narration and castigation in order to reveal what they experienced and feel. I have analyzed poems written about the First Opium War, the Taiping Rebellion, the Sino-Japanese War (1894) and the Boxer Uprising and found that there are changed in the way poets wrote poems that they became more aware of the lyrical nature of ci. The tradition of bixing gradually became more preferable to direct narration and castigation. In some exceptional cases, however, a rather direct way of expression can be found in tunes like "man jiang hong". The tune has a tradition of writing war-related subjects and is accepted to have a unrestrained style. Therefore, when poets choose to present in a direct way, finding the appropriate tune can be a solution. The above findings are presented in several articles and combined to form a major chapter of my monograph. By combining and appropriating the articles into the monograph chapter, the trajectory of change can be seen. The monograph then explored on how and why bixing was becoming more significant among poets. It concludes that while the idea of cishi was significant among late Qing poets, they were also increasing concerned in maintaining the lyrical essence of ci. This concern became more and more important in the poets' debates and eventually, ci writing became a more inward-looking activity rather than directly referring to historic events.

14602015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14602015.value: The findings from the project shows the complexity and flexibility in ci poem writing. Poets were innovative in deploying different methods to create a poem that both contain the unique beauty of ci and reveal their life, thought and feelings. For example, there are many emulating poems of that period. While emulation may be considered lacking of originality, but emulating poems of late Qing are far from copying predecessors' works. Poets, using the form, style, tune (tune created by specific poets) to write lyrics for their own time. I have examined "man jiang hong" in the project and believed that much more can be explored.

14602115.value: Prof Tong, Yuying Prof Zhong, Hua

14602115.label: Project Objectives
14602115.value: To explore the extent and pattern of victimization among rural adolescents left behind by migrant parents in the context of rural-to-urban migration in China. To examine the contribution of situational correlates of routine activities and social correlates (social bonds, control balance, delinquent peer association, and social strain) to the victimization of left-behind adolescents in rural China.
