14603115.label: Major findings and research outcome
14603115.value: Preliminary findings relating to one of the key concepts, filial piety, were published in the IR journal Translation and Interpreting Studies (“Consequences of the conflation of xiao and filial piety in English” in section C) by the PI, as well as two papers written by the post-doctoral fellow Chen I-Hsin, whom I hired with additional funds from CUHK. These papers, and the monograph to follow, all demonstrate the validity of the basic premise regarding two-way influence in developing cross-cultural knowledge relating to China. The papers on religion, which were not part of the original grant, were particularly gratifying to the PI, because they demonstrated that the methodology proposed had wider application. In addition, two presentations by the PI and one published paper discuss the use of digital humanities methodologies to conduct research in translation studies on how concepts travel and develop over time. Unfortunately, the footnote with funding information was accidently deleted at printing in the Journal of Translation Studies. Thus although the monograph is not yet complete, there have been substantial outputs both in terms of international conferences attended (four) and IR journal publications (four). One major finding is the close link between historical and social circumstances and how concepts develop. The crisis at the end of the Qing dynasty led to a vast amount of material being translated into Chinese; in this period, the concepts in English had a greater influence on the Chinese ones than vice-versa. Conversely, the rise in importance of the Chinese economy since the 1980s has led to the Chinese concept of guanxi traveling to Anglophone cultures and taking on new meanings. However, other factors besides political or economic power need to be considered, as the development of the concept fengshui teaches us. During the 1960s, when China was politically and economically less influential, the concept still managed to establish itself as part of the American counter-culture. This had perhaps more to do with internal developments in the US and the growth of Chinese-American culture as part of a larger Chinese diaspora than with US-China relations. A second major finding is that, while these concepts changed, sometimes radically, other related concepts were much more stable. While outside the main scope of the study, some attention is paid in the monograph to the fact that fengshui changes greatly while yin-yang proved remarkably stable, perhaps because yin-yang is a more basic concept and therefore less susceptible to change.

14603115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14603115.value: The research can be built upon in the future in at least four ways. First, additional terms between Chinese and English could be studied. As mentioned previously, I decided not to incorporate a chapter on ‘bamboozle’ and ‘copycat’. These terms could be treated in a separate article. Second, other languages besides English could be considered in more detail the history of how concepts relating to China have developed inter-lingually over time, especially in the premodern period. I know French and have a basic reading knowledge of German and Japanese, but this would probably require cooperation with other scholars who have the relevant linguistic expertise. Third, as stated in the fourth objective, the conceptual framework and methodology developed in this project could be used in other, non-Chinese contexts. Finally, the results regarding fengshui and yin-yang are intriguing because they raise the issue of what factors lead either to the stability or flux of concepts.

14603115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14603115.value: This study details how a small set of key concepts relating to China, 孝 (filial piety), 面子 (face), 風水 (fengshui/geomancy), and 關係 (guanxi/social networks), over a period of centuries, have changed and grown through a two-way process of translation and interpretation. Each concept made multiple trips back and forth between English and Chinese, sometimes being equated with different terms. These concepts have sometimes been used by the Chinese and westerners as markers of the uniqueness of Chinese culture, and at other times as part of an argument about universal human traits. Face, for example, starts off as being perceived as uniquely Chinese, only to be re-imagined by sociolinguists in the 1960s and 1970s as a universal of human behavior in all societies, while filial piety begins as a universal human trait but then gradually becomes specific to the Confucian tradition in East Asia. Through a combination of archival research and mining of electronic databases, I show how that translation process has been bound up in the production of new meaning on both sides of the language divide.

14603315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603315.value: 1978年以來中國實行改革開放政策，城市化步伐加快。弗裡德曼認為“儘管同全球化過程交織在一起，中國城市化主要是一個內生過程並產生中國特有的現代化形式”。來自農村沒有城市戶口的暫住移民是“自發城市化”的一部分，得到不少研究的關注。儘管有非農業戶口的人口穩定增長，“國家贊助的城市化” 幾乎被忽略。已提出雙軌城市化的概念描述中國改革時期的城市化過程，同時考慮“自發城市化”與 “國家贊助的城市化”。中國的經濟發展，外資流入與城市化在空間上是不均衡的。不少研究關注區域不平衡發展，省級城市化的空間趨勢也有研究。但是對具有特定地方與區域背景的縣級不平衡城市化缺乏系統研究。 使用最近幾次普查資料，本項目將從雙軌城市化的視角探討福建省不平衡城市化的過程。本項目將從三個空間尺度探討福建省不平衡城市化的過程，包括省級、地級與縣級的城市化。國家贊助的城市化用各地的非農業人口來表示。自發城市化用用各地的暫住人口和鄉鎮企業就業人數來表示。在分析了基於縣級單元的城市化的時空變化之後，將進行統計分析，解釋國家贊助的城市化與自發城市化的不同水準。基於文獻回顧與之前的研究，使用四組變數解釋城市化水平。它們描述各地重要的人口、社會與經濟情況。本研究會檢驗七個假設，以揭示福建省雙軌城市化的動態與決定因素。將與城市決策者、社區領袖與居民訪談，瞭解政府發展規劃、自發城市化以及城市化的結果。 在實證研究的基礎上，可以獲得關於中國不平衡城市化的驅動要素，城市化與發展的關係的理論啟示。

14603315.label: Realisation of objectives

Research activities in 2018: Substantial research activities were conducted in 2018, the analysis of the determinants of uneven dual-track urbanization at county level areas in Fujian was completed. The paper “Spatial patterns and driving forces of uneven dual-track urbanization in Fujian province: An approach based on employment sectors” was revised substantially considering the comments from reviewers and was accepted for publication in Urban Studies (published in 2019). The paper “The different effects of the determinants of urbanization on state-sponsored and spontaneous urbanization in Fujian province of China” was completed in 2018. The revised paper is under review by Population, Space and Place. A conference paper “Analysis of the determinants of state-sponsored and spontaneous urbanization in Fujian province of China“ was presented at the 2018 International Geographical Union Regional Conference in August, 2018, Quebec. Another conference paper “Analysis of urbanization in China from a micro perspective: Social-economic inequality and urbanization impacts on residents” was completed in 2018 and was presented as a Keynote Lecture at 17th Shanghai-Hong Kong Development Institute Annual Conference on City Integration in October 2018 in Fudan University, Shanghai. 14603315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14603315.value: The project examined the spatial patterns and driving forces of state-sponsored and spontaneous urbanization (papers in Cities and Urban Studies). The shift from small towns to large urban areas is found in both tracks of urbanization. Both administrative force, internal market force, and external market force affect the levels of state-sponsored and spontaneous urbanization. First, temporal analysis shows that the administrative force (share of state-owned sector) and the specific internal market force (share of collective-owned sector) had a negative relation with the levels of two urbanization tracks for the province as a whole. The external force affects both tracks of urbanization. Second, a spatial analysis found relatively balanced levels of state-sponsored and spontaneous urbanization in state-led urbanized areas (both are high) and less developed areas (both are low). Coastal developed areas had a large foreign funded employment sector with a low level of state-sponsored urbanization. The Fujian case shows that the two tracks of urbanization have been advancing despite of the relative decline of the state-owned and collective-owned sectors. The project also analyzed different effects of various determinants on the state-sponsored and spontaneous urbanization and re-considered the relation among urbanization, development and modernization (Zhang, 2002; Long, Zou, & Liu, 2009) (revised paper submitted to Population, Space and Place). Firstly, administrative ranks of area units have significant impacts on both state-sponsored and spontaneous urbanization. The administrative rank of county-level cities has a negative impact on the state-sponsored urbanization level. It is noted that county-level cities have been converted from previous counties and they are similar to some extent. The administrative rank of urban areas of central cities has a positive impact on the spontaneous urbanization level. Spontaneous urbanization proceeds with state-sponsored urbanization in such central cities. Secondly, the initial level of urbanization has a great impact on the levels of state-sponsored and spontaneous urbanization. Thirdly, the level of development is the most remarkable determinant of state-sponsored urbanization. Economic growth has some positive impacts on spontaneous urbanization. Fourthly, the share of secondary sector is the most important determinant of the spontaneous urbanization level. But the share of secondary sector does not have a significant impact on state-sponsored urbanization. Based on the fieldwork and semi-structured interviews, it is found that social inequality in employment, children’s education for migrant workers, and housing still exists but some of them have been improved in recent years. Urbanization and migration have positive impact on development in general.

14603315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14603315.value: This project conducted a systematic study on uneven urbanization at county level in Fujian province which has specific local and regional contexts. This is one step further in the study of urbanization at provincial level in China. The findings from the project are insightful to understand the spatial dynamics, determinants and the relationship between the state-sponsored urbanization and spontaneous urbanization. For examples, the administrative rank of urban areas of central cities has a positive impact on the spontaneous urbanization level. Spontaneous urbanization proceeds with state-sponsored urbanization in such central cities. The initial level of urbanization has a great impact on the levels of state-sponsored and spontaneous urbanization. These results can be tested again at other provinces with different development conditions. There are two possible research directions. First, to select representative provinces in the eastern, central and western regions of China to test the hypotheses on uneven dual-track urbanization at county level. Second, to use all county-level units in China to test the hypotheses on uneven dual-track urbanization at county level. Research advancement in these directions will help achieve full understanding of urbanization and development in China. Further research grant will be sought to engage new research in this area.

14603315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14603315.value: The concept of dual-track urbanization has been proposed to describe China’s rapid urbanization in the reform period. But no systematic study on uneven urbanization has been conducted at county level which has specific local and regional contexts. Using data mainly from censuses, this project examined the uneven urbanization process in Fujian. The state-sponsored urbanization was measured by the size of non-agricultural population. The spontaneous urbanization was measured by the size of temporary population. After analysis of the temporal and spatial changes of urbanization based on county level units, statistical analysis was conducted to explain the different levels of state-sponsored urbanization and spontaneous urbanization. Based on literature review and previous studies, five groups of explanatory variables were used to explain the level of urbanization. They described important demographic, social and economic conditions in various areas. The research tested a series of research hypotheses to reveal the dynamics and determinants of dual-track urbanization in Fujian. Interviews with urban policy makers, community leaders and residents was conducted for better understanding of the official planned development, spontaneous urbanization process as well as the consequences of urbanization. Theoretical insights were drawn regarding the driving forces of uneven urbanization and the relation between urbanization and development.

14603615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603615.value: In this project we study the effects of need states on people’s preference in inter-temporal choices and decision making under risk. In the first part we focus on inter-temporal choices. While previous literature finds that need states increase impatience, we propose that such a result is only true when the choice is between an option that is immediately available and an option that is in the future. If both options are in the future but vary in reward timing, we predict that people high in need could be more patient. These results emerge because need states activate two goals simultaneously: the immediacy goal and the quantity goal. When immediacy goal is relevant, people high in need are more likely to make decision based on the immediacy goal and choose an immediately available option, demonstrating lower patience. When immediacy goal is less relevant, for example, when both options are only available in a distant future and thus cannot satisfy the current need anyway, quantity goal dominates to guide their choices. Consequently, people high in need are more likely to choose a larger-later option, demonstrating greater patience. The second part focuses on decision under risk. We distinguish between three types of choices. The first type is a choice between need relevant and need irrelevant options; the second type is a choice between need relevant options; and the third type is a choice between need irrelevant options. We propose that in facing with the first type of choice, people high in need are more likely to choose the need relevant option, no matter the option is the riskier or less risky option. Thus they could be more or less risk seeking, depending on the location of the need relevant option. Alternatively, if consumers face a decision of the second type, we argue that if the less risky option (i.e., the sure option) is too small to be helpful at all in satisfying the current need, consumers high in need will be more risk seeking to choose the option with a potential larger but risky return than those low in need. Whereas if the less risky option is large enough (above “the minimum meaningful quantity”), consumers high in need would be less risk seeking than those low in need. These pattern of results can also be explained by the two-goal framework. We make no predictions for (but can explore) the third type of tradeoffs. 此研究分析了需求狀態對「跨期」及「風險」兩種不同決策的影響。 在第一部分，我研究需求狀態對跨期決策的影響。現存文獻指出人們在高需求狀態下會變得缺乏耐性，並會選擇一個可更快得到的選項。然而，我們認為這只會在其中一個選項是可即時獲得的情況下才發生。如果決策中的選項都只能在將來某個時間實現，我們預測高需求的人會更有耐性。 這是基於我們認為，高需求狀態能同時誘發了兩個動機︰即時動機和數量動機。當要選擇即時得到少量食物，或選擇在將來得到更多食物時，高需求狀態「餓」的人會側重即時目標，而且會比低需求「飽」的人更可能選擇即時得到少量的食物。 若當所有選項都只會在未來的某個時候實現，由於所有選項皆不能滿足即時目標，人便會基於數量目標作決策；此時，高需求的人會傾向選擇一項更遠卻更多的選項，表現得比低需求的人更有耐性。 在第二部分，我們研究需求狀態對風險決策的影響。 我們把風險決策分為三類。 第一類決策是從與需求相關的選項（如︰食物相對於飢餓）及與需求無關的選項（如︰玩具相對於饑餓）作抉擇。 第二類決策的選項都是與需求相關的。 第三類決策的選項都是與需求無關的。根據現有文獻，在作出第一種的決策時，需求高的人總比需求低的人更可能選擇與需求相關的選項。而在作出第二種決策時，若消費者於確定（而足夠）的選項和涉及風險的選項之間進行抉擇，需求越高的人會較偏向選擇確定選項；相反，若所有選項皆涉及風險，需求越高的人則傾向選擇風險較大的選項。 最後，我們預測需求狀態對第三種決策沒有大的影響。

14603615.label: Realisation of objectives
14603615.value: We have conducted a series of studies tested the hypotheses we stated in the proposal. Now we have much better understanding on how need states affect consumer preferences in intertemporal choices and decision making under risk, and what are the underlying processes. Specifically, for the first objective “systematically understand how need states affect consumer preferences in inter-temporal choices,” our experimental results confirmed that: for proximal choice, i.e., choice between an immediately available option and a future option, higher need (e.g., hunger) leads to lower patience in intertemporal choice; alternatively, for distal choice, i.e., choice between two future options varying in time and magnitude, higher need (e.g., hunger) leads to greater patience in intertemporal choice. For the second objective “systematically understand how need state affect consumer preference in decision making under risk,” we used two different risk attitude elicitation methods to test the effect of need on risk preference. We found that when we used that certainty method (a choice between a certain option and an uncertain option), those high (vs. low) in need are more risk averse; however, when we used the uncertainty method (a choice between two uncertain options varying on magnitude and probability), those high (vs. low) in need are more risk seeking. For the other two objectives, we ran a series of studies to confirm that the same two-goal framework can systematically explain the effects of need states on intertemporal choices and decisions under risk. In the project, we used different types of needs and different ways to manipulate needs, and different choice contexts to test robustness and generalizability of the conclusions. In summary, we have achieved all the four objectives stated in the proposal. Overall, this research helps us better understand the impact of need states on intertemporal choices and decision under risk, and the underlying psychological processes, and bringing new research opportunities to the study of judgment and decision making.

14603615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14603615.value: How does need state affect consumer intertemporal choice and decision under risk. In intertemporal choice, we find that need states cause consumers to prefer “now” to “later” options (i.e., impatience; consistent with previous research), but also to prefer a larger-later to a smaller-sooner (but not now) option (i.e., patience). In decision under risk, we find that needs states cause consumers to prefer “sure” to “risky” options, but also to prefer risky option with larger variance to risky option with smaller variance. ? In other words, need states could decrease or increase patience, and need state could increase or decreases risk taking, depending on the type of choice set consumers are facing with. We further proposed and confirmed that the two-goal hypothesis could systematically explain these results and predict under what conditions they happen. Our findings and proposed theoretic framework thus greatly advanced our understanding of the effect of need states on judgment and decision making. The outcome of this proposal is a paper in the review process at the Journal of Consumer Research (invited revision). Meanwhile we also used the fund to support several related projects, some of the papers have already been published (see Part C for details). As stated in the midterm report, we used the grant to support part of data collection for a project with PhD student Canice Kwan and Professor Robert Wyer (research output #1). The initial submission date of this paper was July 2015 and in late rounds (4 rounds in total) of revision we made significant change and collected new data for several studies using fund from this project. The paper is titled “Contextual Influence on Message Persuasion: the Effect of Empty Space.” It was later published in Journal of Consumer Research. Note that this publication was never part of the content of this research proposal, and the content is completely different from the proposal. It was supported by this funding only at its late stage (i.e., the revision process) toward publication.

14603615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14603615.value: We are optimistic that the findings in this project will inspire future research to more systematically study 1) how the need states affect consumer judgment and decisions, and 2) how the proposed dual-goal framework can be adopted to explain other decision phenomenon. We will continue to work in this very field and generate more research outcomes that could contribute to the theories of needs and decision making processes.

14603615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14603615.value: Understanding the impact of needs (e.g., hunger) on decisions is critical to the study of decision making. This project systematically studies the effects of needs on consumers’ patience in intertemporal choices, and consumers’ risk preference in decision making under risk and uncertainty. We further proposed a theoretical framework to explain and make predictions on these effects under different choice situations. A series of studies, involving surveys, lab and field experiments, lent support to the proposed findings and theoretical framework. The research thus advanced our understanding of needs and also its implications for consumer decision making.

14603715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603715.value: Energy consumption and thermal comfort in buildings are important considerations for sustainable and good-quality urban living, especially for high-density cities in the Tropics. Climate change and urbanisation contribute to the rise in urban air temperatures and lead to more heat-stress-related mortality (Chan et al., 2010) as well as to higher energy consumption (Fung et al., 2006; Lam et al., 2010a, 2010b). The Typical Meteorological Year (TMY) for Hong Kong (Chan et al., 2006; Chow et al., 2006; Lam et al., 1996) has been used to evaluate the building energy performance. The impact of climate change on energy consumption in Hong Kong has also lately been incorporated (Chan, 2011). However, TMY data cannot consider the energy performance, and, more importantly, the thermal comfort performance of buildings in urban areas under ‘onerous warm weather conditions’ (CIBSE, 2002). This leads to heat-stress-related problems during the more frequently occurring heat waves. To address the problem, the concept of Design Summer Years (DSYs) derived from a near-extreme summer should be used to assess the overheating risks as well as the energy performance of buildings during summertime. In order to investigate the impact of climate change on thermal comfort and energy use during summertime of subtropical Hong Kong, a set of future weather data of summer conditions is essential. The objectives of this study are: (A) to establish a set of hourly future DSYs of Hong Kong that take into account climate change and the urban climate to assess the overheating risk and energy consumption for a more sustainable urban and building design. The global climate models (GCMs) from the fifth phase of Climate Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP5) will be incorporated into the DSYs of Hong Kong; (B) to evaluate the impact of climate change on the energy and thermal performance of buildings based on the future DSYs by using typical residential and office buildings in Hong Kong; (C) to conduct parametric tests using the identified design parameters so that critical design features may be quantified; and (D) based on this understanding, to develop a set of design guides. This study is a multi-disciplinary research linking meteorology, building physics, architectural design and human comfort. The results will lead designers towards better building designs, especially under critical summer conditions. The framework developed and the experience gained, from climate change considerations to building level designs, will provide a valuable reference for our rapidly urbanising neighbouring cities. 建築物內的能源消耗和熱舒適度是對可持續和優質城市生活的重要考慮，尤其是對於位處熱帶的高密度城市而言。氣候變化和城市化導致城市氣溫上升及更多的熱應力引起的死亡(Chan et al., 2010)，還有更高的能源消耗。 香 港的典型氣象年(Typical Meteorological Year)(Chan et al., 2006; Chow et al., 2006; Lam et al., 1996)被用於評估建築物的能源表現。近來亦加上氣候變化對香港能源消耗的影響。然而，典型氣象年的數據並不能考慮到能源表現，還有是更為重要的，市區內建築物在「麻煩的溫暖天氣」(CIBSE, 2002)的熱舒適表現。在更頻繁發生熱浪的時候，這造成熱應力相關的問題。 為處理此問題，出自近極端夏季中的「設 計夏季年份」(Design Summer Years)的概念應該用以評估建築物在夏季的過熱風險還有能源表現。為了研究氣候變化對亞熱帶香港夏季的熱舒適度和能源使用，一組未來的夏季天氣數據是必要的。 本研究的目的是：(一) 建立一組香 港的每小時未來設計夏季年份，因應氣候變化和城市氣候，評估 過熱風險和能源消耗，達致更具可持續性的城市和建築設計。將第五期耦合模式比較計劃 (Coupled Model Intercomparison Project phase 5)的全球氣候模型 (global climate models)應用於香港的設計夏季年份；(二) 根據未來的設計夏季年份，利用香港典型住宅及辦公室樓 宇，評估氣候變化對建築物的能源和熱能表現；(三) 利用已確認的設計參數進行參數測試，使關鍵的設計特點可以被量化；以及(四) 在此基礎上制定一系列的設計指引。 本研究是結合了氣象學、建築物理、建築設計及人體舒適度的跨學科研究。研究結果可指導設計師達到更好的建築設計，特別針對關鍵的夏季狀況。所發展的研究框架和累積的經驗，由氣候變化的考慮到樓宇層面的設計，將為快速城市化中的鄰近城市提供寶貴的參考。

14603715.label: Realisation of objectives
14603715.value: The first objective is to select the appropriate global climate models (GCMs) from the fifth phase of the Climate Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP5) in Hong Kong, and then establish the future DSYs that take into account climate change. After reviewing the literature, we decided to choose Summer Reference Year (SRY) as the approach to develop a near-extreme summer meteorological data set because it can be applied with data available from various sources, including future climate change. A journal article was published in Building Services Engineering Research and Technology to document the development procedures of the data set. The second and third objectives are to evaluate the impact of climate change and building envelope on the energy performance of buildings and thermal comfort of building occupants. We examined different features of residential buildings and determined the optimal combination of shading panels in order to achieve thermal comfort of building occupants. These findings were documented in three journal articles published in Energy and Buildings and Energy Procedia. The last objective is to develop a set of design guidelines for designers. In the two published papers in Energy and Buildings, design recommendations were formulated based on the scientific findings. This study also contributes to the subsequent Research Impact Fund on understanding the impact of extreme hot weather on the health and well-being of elderly citizens. The concept of SRY is incorporated into the project to provide meteorological inputs for impact assessment in the context of urban design and public health.

14603715.value: Energy consumption and thermal comfort in buildings are important considerations for sustainable and good-quality urban living, especially for high-density cities in the Tropics. Climate change and urbanisation contribute to the rise in urban air temperatures and lead to more heat-stress-related mortality as well as to higher energy consumption. This study uses the approach of Summer Reference Year (SRY) meteorological data set to assess the overheating risks as well as the energy performance of buildings under a near-extreme summer conditions. 14603915.label: Project Objectives
14603915.value: To provide historical background for the Second Amendment to the United States Constitution. To show the linked histories of militias in the Atlantic World. England's 1689 Bill of Rights, The United States' Second Amendment, and France's mass conscription were all different solutions to the problem of how to protect a society from external threats without being threatened by the society's protectors. To place the history of France's Revolutionary and Napoleonic armies in a broader history of citizen soldiers. To show the exclusionary nature of early modern militias, and the importance of race, gender, class, religion and nationality for the role they played in society. To highlight the importance of eighteenth-century codes of masculinity in maintaining the militia system. To use the history of militias to better understand the evolution of categories of citizenship in the modern nation-state.

14603915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603915.value: This project studies the spread and advocacy of militias in the eighteenth-century Atlantic world. During this era, "militias" were armed forces composed of citizen-soldiers, as opposed to permanent standing armies. Starting in the Italian Renaissance writers praised militias' reliability due to the motivations of part-time soldiers with ties to their society. Mercenaries and standing armies were considered threatening to the people and unreliable in times of need. Advocacy of militias became especially strong in seventeenth-century England, before spreading to France and the British colonial world, including America. The fervor with which advocates praised militias surpassed the empirical record of the militias' accomplishments, yet that empirical record could not dampen the enthusiasts' support for citizen-soldiers or their disdain for standing armies - hence the term "militia mania." Militias were valued for their importance in establishing the status and masculinity of their members. Advocates of militias tied participation in the militias to citizenship, claiming that one could not be a citizen unless they were a soldier. But being a "citizen" was far more restrictive than being an inhabitant. Full citizenship required that the person be male, and often also involved racial distinctions, as in North America where Native Americans and Africans were denied citizenship; religious or national distinctions, as in England which gave Protestants the right to bear arms while disarming Scotland; or property restrictions, as in the early militias of the French Revolution. The history of militias helps explain the Janus-faced history of citizenship during the early formation of nation-states. The rhetorical emphasis on inclusion, especially in France and the United States, contrasted with the exclusionary nature of citizenship in those nations. Exclusion from militias was both a cause and a consequence of other exclusionary trends within Atlantic society. The enthusiastic embrace of militias in the Atlantic World also explains two important legacies of eighteenth-century militia mania: the French Revolution's mass conscription that paved the way for the Napoleonic wars, and the Second Amendment to the United States Constitution, which still frames debates about firearm violence there. Militia Mania will show how both of these legacies grew out of the militia mania of the eighteenth century, reflecting both an overvaluation of citizen-soldiers on the battlefield and the exclusionary nature of citizenship. In doing so, it will establish how militias and firearms acted more as tools of domination than of liberation. 民兵狂熱: 近代初期大西洋世界的武器與公民身份 摘要 本研究探討十八世紀民兵制在大西洋區域的散播與提倡。當時「民兵」有別於常備軍，意指由公民-士兵組成的武裝力量。自意大利文藝復興始，作家稱頌民兵的可靠性，認為兼職士兵有心繫社會的積極性。相反，僱傭兵及常備軍對人民具威脅性，並不可靠。 十七世紀英格蘭對民兵制的倡導特強，其後散播至法國和英國殖民地，包括美洲。倡導者對民兵的讚揚熱情超乎民兵成就的實際記錄，然而，這些實際記錄無損熱心人士對公民-士兵的支持，或他們對常備軍的蔑視。「民兵狂熱」一詞於焉出現。 民兵的重要性在於建立其成員的地位及陽剛氣質。民兵制的倡議者將當兵與公民身分掛鈎，聲稱要成爲公民,就非當兵不可。但「公民」比居民更受限制。有完整公民身份者必須是男性：在種族差異方面，例如北美洲的土著和非洲裔人士就被剝奪公民權；在宗教或民族的差異上，例如英格蘭賦予新教徒攜帶武器的權利，卻解除蘇格蘭的武裝；在財產方面，法國大革命的早期民兵就受到有關規限。 民兵歷史有助解釋民族國家形成早期的歷史的雙歧性，如在措辭上對包容的強調，竟與公民身份的排他性成對比，在法國和美國尤其如此。民兵的排他性，既是大西洋社會中其他排他趨勢的原因，也是其結果。大西洋世界對民兵的熱衷，也解釋了十八世紀民兵熱的兩個重要遺風：一是法國大革命的大量徵兵，它為拿破崙戰爭鋪路；二是美國憲法的修訂，它至今仍為有關火器暴力的辯論提供框架。這個對民兵熱的研究，將呈現這兩種遺風如何源自十八世紀的民兵熱，反映了對公民-士兵在戰場上的價值的高估，以及公民身份的排他性本質。在此研究過程中所建立的論述指出民兵和火器如何成爲支配的工具，其對解放所起的工具作用，則相差甚遠。

14603915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14603915.value: This book is about why citizens of the United States shoot each other so often. Historians of the eighteenth-century have a contribution to make on this subject, as American weapons laws are still based in an eighteenth-century framework that emphasizes the importance of citizen-soldiers over professional armies, which required giving average citizens access to weapons. I have found that citizen-soldiers were common throughout the eighteenth-century Atlantic, creating the possibility for comparative studies, especially between the French and American Revolutions. Both show militias playing domestic repressive roles, but the violence of American racial relations went beyond France's class-based animosities. The framework of today's gun violence in American comes from eighteenth-century laws, but the violent legacy comes from the growth of chattel slavery at that time. This research also suggests some reasons why other eighteenth-century rights, such as freedom of speech and freedom of the press, were more easily democratized during the preceding years, while the right to bear arms has traditionally been accorded more freely to American whites than to African-Americans.

14604215.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14604215.value: 香港,中國大陸和韓國獨立手機遊戲製造商的發行策略比較研究

14604215.label: Project Objectives
14604215.value: The first objective seeks to provide an initial understanding of the online distribution network for application game industry in three of the most active mobile gaming markets in Asia. The second objective seeks to complement the existing literature on new media and globalization from the perspective of East Asia. Most studies concentrate on media industry analysis from the national perspective. This project will provide a cross-national comparison in order to examine the dynamics and differences in three East Asian countries. The third objective seeks to add to the current debate on new media and globalization. It will contribute to the literature with a new perspective on mobile games. The project aims to complicate the debate on cultural complexity when mobile technology, popular culture and regionalization intersect in this sub-region of Asia. The fourth objective seeks to understand the potential that independent game developers are able to capitalize on in the emerging application economy. This discussion will promote entrepreneurship for creative individuals and it will also aim to contribute to the discussion of start-up businesses for the cultural economy of East Asia. The fifth objective seeks to understand the changing industry value chain due to the change of distribution channels moving to online. It has the ultimate goal of providing an initial reference to build a distribution model that overcomes the problem of piracy in East Asian markets. This project is based on the belief that innovation in East Asia needs to go beyond the current production and consumption patterns that are heavily regulated by transnational mega-corporations. An overall study of application game distribution will serve to begin the discussion of the new and future game industries in East Asia.

14604215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14604215.value: Aim The aim of this project is to conduct research into the online distribution strategies of independent application game developers in Hong Kong, China and South Korea. Project Background This project will examine the online distribution strategies of application game developers in Hong Kong, China and South Korea. Its purpose is to discover the cultural and economic patterns that exist in the mobile game industry in East Asia. The project's thesis argues that convergence technology supports the emergence of small-scale companies in the mainstream publishing world. Brief Project Description The project will explain the proposed argument with the case of application games. It will focus on independent game developers in the East Asian region of Hong Kong, China and South Korea. The project will also study the platform companies with which the independent game developers in Hong Kong, China and South Korea have chosen to publish their games. The project will examine the publishing conditions in the major platform companies, including Apple iTune, Google Play, Tencent, 360 and Kaokao Game. The project will include the top selling application games in the three markets. Interviews with managers, graphic artists, programmers and market planners will be collected for data collection. The project plans to have carried out a total of 90 interviews in all. This project seeks to accomplish two goals. One is theoretical. By recording the most recent developments in new media culture in East Asia, this study will be able to conceptualize Asia’s regionalization in media cultural studies. The second goal is more practical, in that the project seeks to produce an industry analysis, focusing on interactive entertainment sector. As most Asian content producers face the challenge of finding legal channels in which they can circulate their cultural works, the project can also provide a case of digital content circulation in East Asia's sophisticated mobile markets. Finally, the project aims to create a new literature on East Asian application games for the field of game studies. This contributes to my larger research project on online game development and cultural regionalization in Asia. Significance of Project The proposed research finding will show the continuity of a growing game culture that is contributed by independent game producer and networked technology in East Asia. 研究目的 本研究主要研究香港,中國大陸以及南韓的獨立遊戲開發商在手機遊戲方面的發行策略. 研究背景 本研究的目的是試圖藉著對東亞手機市場的瞭解來發掘香港,中國大陸以及南韓三個手機遊戲產業賦有的特殊文化及經濟特色. 本研究強調, 整合科技在今天的主流發行市場上對小型公司的崛起有相當程度的幫助. 研究簡介 本研究將會通過一些手機遊戲的實例來詮釋所提出的論點，且聚焦於香港，中國大陸，南韓的獨立遊戲開發者，同時也著力於研究這些開發者所選擇的發布平台。本研究將會調查包括蘋果iTunes，Google Play，騰訊，360，Kakao遊戲在內的幾大平台的發布環境。研究將包含香港，中國大陸及南韓手機遊戲市場最暢銷的遊戲。數據收集將會基於對九十人的採訪，這其中包含管理者，設計師，程序開發人員及市場策略人員。 本研究試圖達到兩個目標。第一個是理論。通過記錄東亞新媒體文化的最新發展狀況，本研究將概念化亞洲媒體文化研究中的區域化特徵。第二個目標更為實際，本研究試圖進行行業研究，且著重於交互娛樂部分。基於眾多亞洲內容供應商面臨著尋找合法渠道來發行文化作品的挑戰，本研究為數字內容在東亞複雜的手機市場中的發行問題提供了範例。 最後， 此次研究目的在於為遊戲研究領域中的東亞手機遊戲研究提供新的文獻，且將助力於更龐大的關於線上遊戲發展及亞洲文化區域化研究的項目。 研究意義 擬題出的研究成果將展現出由東亞獨立遊戲製作人和網絡化技術所促成的增長中的遊戲文化的持續性。

14605615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605615.value: 此二年期之專題研究，旨在從訓世建言型文獻與個人年譜等實證性訊息雙方面入手，首次理出近世中國歷史人口上平均壽命值（average life expectancy）減增，人口整體總數走向人口爆炸（demographic explosion）前夕,中國社會內部對“老老之道”之考量與踐履。 計劃第一年，在以清代乾隆朝曹庭棟（1700-1785）《老老恒言》一書為核心，梳理明清江南老人社群人口漸增後，老人在自覺反省下，對其頤養天和，自助助人之道之理念和建議。並舉之與中世之前，以道家“養生”概念為主的看法，如抱樸子《養生論》，陶弘景《養性延命錄》，乃至儒家奉親之道，如《儒門事親》、《養老奉親書新編》等等對照性探究。 計劃第二年，將以過去童年研究中已搜集之近世明清時期大量年譜為基礎， 逐案建立一質性而兼有部分量化意涵之資料庫，以之分析，作為與上階段訓誨性忠誥之對照。質之而考量近世老老之道在“理想面”與“實踐面”兩層次雙面向之發展狀況。 二年計劃間將宣讀一篇國際研討論會論文，出版一篇學審下之期刊論文（或專書章節）。

14605615.label: Realisation of objectives
14605615.value: The main outcome of this two-year project lays in primary research material gathering and analysis. Systematic textual comparison shows that (as listed in 5.1) chapter by chapter and item by item close reading of LLHY reveals a content and outlook of advice literature on “aging” to be quite different from the earlier Taoist “longevity manuals” represented by 抱樸子.養生論 or 陶弘景. 養生延命錄, philosophically and spiritually. In terms of daily practice, a significant turn away from the “老老”(looking after the aging needs of one’s own and those of others by the filial acts of the younger generation), as exemplified by 儒門事親(The Confucian Way of Serving One’s Elders) and 養老奉親書新編(New Compilation on the Way to Serve the Aging and Caring for One’s Elders).instead a novel idea of “自老”(Looking after the Aging process by Oneself) is proposed and clearly laid out. Which carries significant impact in defining the “early modern” prosperity as denoted in the Lower Yangtze Valley region achieved in late imperial China, as well as the conceptual and practical break through of the Confucian China as it generates a new social-cultural-ethical order in response to its economic growth and bio-physical achievements in health and population. Detailed investigation through biographical and autobiographical material and chronologies, as well as clan and genealogical records also verify that a silent personal and familial revolution was in the making in the intimate and private spheres of the Confucian way of life. When this GRF proposal was granted as a 2-year rather than 3-year project (Title: Aging in Late Imperial China Advice and Practice; Project Code: 14605615), in its revised proposal submitted and approved on 1 Sept 2015, the “Expected Outcome” had been adjusted to be: the presentation of one international conference paper and the publication of one refereed journal article or book chapter”. As of the end of this 2-year project, the Final Report submitted in the end of 2018 included one book chapter, 6 conference and meeting presentations, 7 invited lectures. Which far exceeded the original commitment and outcomes expected of this GRF project. Further academic results flowing out of this project related to the subject will continue to be published as part of Chinese monographs and English presentations. Printed evidence of the publication of book chapters and related Chinese book is enclosed for reference.

14605615.value: Major Findings The first historical study and reconstruction of the aging process in Late Imperial China, including both the advice literature and actual practice. In connection with the author’s earlier research on childhood studies, this project completed the historical understanding of the entire life course in traditional China, from beginning to the end. As its publication in Europe demonstrated, the study is done with a comparative perspective and it’s presented as so in academic outcomes. 14605915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605915.value: On 20 February 2012, the European Union (EU) and the People's Republic of China (PRC) decided to launch negotiations on a bilateral treaty addressing the promotion and protection of investment between the two parties. This research anticipates the forthcoming negotiations and examines the legal positions from which the parties will begin their negotiations. In particular, this research aims to investigate and compare the PRC’s fast-evolving investment-treaty-making practice with the emerging position of the EU. In so doing, this research will provide stakeholders, such as policy makers, academics and the general public, with a roadmap to the issues raised in the forthcoming negotiations. The negotiation of a bilateral investment treaty (BIT) between the PRC and the EU is likely to be a watershed event in global investment treaty practice. Because of the size and importance of the PRC-EU bilateral investment relationship , and because of the leading role both parties have played in the global spread of BITs , the issues raised and lessons drawn from the PRC-EU case will have ramifications well beyond China and Europe. 2012年2月20日,歐盟和中華人民共和國決定啟動雙邊條約談判來處理雙方之間的投資的促進和保護。本研究著眼于即將到來的談判，同時研究雙方在即將開始的談判中的法律地位。特別是，本研究旨在調查和將歐盟新興的位置與中國飛速發展的投資協議制定的實踐進行比較。這樣做，本研究将為利益相关者,如政策制定者、学者和公众提供一個關於在即將到來的談判中可能遇到的問題的路線圖。中國與歐盟之間的雙邊投資協議的談判很可能會是全球投資協議實踐的一個分水嶺。基於中國和歐盟雙邊投資的規模和重要性，再加上雙方在雙邊投資協議的領域所起的主導作用，從中國和歐盟這個案例中產生的問題和得到的經驗，其影響將遠遠超出中國和歐盟的範圍。

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14605915.value: This Research Project’s findings also support the idea that although the treaty under negotiation between the EU and China covers only bilateral investments, it can be deemed as the way to success for potential free trade agreements. Furthermore, its relevance has aspects that go beyond the purely economic and legal ones, deriving from the central importance that these two regions have both economically and strategically in their “wider neighbourhood” and worldwide, often in competition with the interests of other world powers. Hence, the CAI is not simply one more of the numerous bi- and multi-lateral agreements forming the “fragmented patchwork” of international investment law, but it is a decisive treaty, and can be considered as a springboard for a closer strategic relationship between China and the EU. This Research Project’s work also suggest that both the degree of liberalization that the CAI will achieve, and its outcome will have a much broader impact than those of an agreement limited to bilateral cooperation. In fact, the destiny of the China-EU BIT will be crucial in taking one of the two following directions: either the two regions will increase their cooperation and enhance mutually beneficial economic relationships, or they will compete against each other for the largest share of the global market, relying on other trade agreements with third States.

14606315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14606315.value: 城市, 作為人類活動的中心, 其土地利用系統及模式隨著人類社會經濟的飛速發展而不斷變化。 尤其是對於快速發展的中國, 其城市土地利用的空間結構更是「日新月異」。 這為精確提取城市土地利用模式與結構帶來了重大挑戰。 遙感技術已被廣泛用於土地覆蓋/利用分類, 為城市規劃和環境管理提供了有效的資料和技術支援。 但由於城市土地利用分類具有典型的社會經濟功能特性,類別具有高度複雜性和易混性, 是遙感分類領域長期難以克服的巨大難題之一。 因而, 本專案旨在利用高級的機器學習技術, 優化詳細的城市土地利用分類演算法, 改善分類精度。 深度學習(Deep Learning)是研究深層結構的有效算法。近年來, 深度學習倍受青睞,其在模式識別和影像解譯領域亦展現出令人滿意的應用效果。 而這一富有潛力的先進方法並未在複雜的城市土地利用分類中大展拳腳, 且在遙感領域亦存在較大的發展空間。 本專案不僅將建立深度學習的詳細的城市土地利用分類框架, 還將高解析度遙感影像(或航空影像)與LiDAR資料結合使用, 以實現高精度的土地利用分類。 而且, 將利用具有典型城市環境的香港作為研究實例, 驗證本分類框架的有效性。

14606315.label: Realisation of objectives
14606315.value: The implementation of this project has adhered closely to the proposed six interrelated objectives. In detail, a theoretical deep learning framework was first proposed for urban land use classification, which integrates different components contained in the project. The components include the deep learning model structure design, multi-source data feature extraction, model parameters training methods, model implementation, and a case study. An effective deep learning model based on optical imagery has been designed and implemented. Traditional deep learning models mainly focus on images with three channels, whereas remote sensing images normally contain more channels. We therefore proposed a semi-transfer deep convolutional neural network (STDCNN) approach to overcome this limitation. First of all, we transferred the pretrained AlexNet model to our model. The AlexNet model has been trained with a large set of natural images, which can be regarded as a powerful feature extractor for our classification task. Then, we also designed a small network with only a few layers, which aimed to interpret multispectral images with more then three channels. Combing two sub-networks in the final step, we have successfully applied this model to optical remote sensing imagery to generate an accurate urban land use classification. In this objective, we explored a suitable method to extract features from optical imagery, which plays an essential role in the following realization of other objectives. Considering multi-source data fusion and the application of land use classification, a two-stage structure model has been designed to accommodate distinct features from different data sources. For the optical imagery, the aforementioned STDCNN has been proved to possess a strong ability in extracting high-level features from optical imagery to the urban land use classification task. The LiDAR sensor as an active sensor can provide elevation and intensity information of different land covers, and can also provide useful information about ground objects which are covered by shadows. As LiDAR data has a distinctive imaging mechanism comparing to optical imagery, we decided to set up an independent branch to extract high-level features of the LiDAR data, rather than directly stacking the LiDAR to optical data as a uniform input for the network. After obtaining high-level features from optical imagery and LiDAR data, a fully connected layer is designed to fuse those features and generate final classification results. Based on a thorough understanding of the urban land use classification task, multi-source data feature extraction, selection and fusion procedures were carefully studied to make the designed framework more task-oriented. It is a normal procedure to decompose large images into small rectangle-like processing units, which chop up the land-use patterns and produce urban land use maps with obvious “blocks”. To obtain an urban land use map, a street block is recommended as the minimum land use mapping unit. However, street blocks are always irregular in shape and are not suitable for input into a deep learning model. Therefore, we proposed a skeleton-based decomposing method using street data is devised to adaptively split every mapping unit (or street block) into processing units with regular shapes. In this way, we can maintain the integrity of the land use patterns. Parameters training strategies and methods were then proposed to accelerate the convergence of the two-stage deep learning structure. The extraction procedures of optical imagery and LiDAR data are distinct from each other. Thus it is necessary to formulate different training strategies to make the training phase more stable. Given the semi-transfer procedure we adopted in the optical imagery training stage, we set the learning rate relatively lower to make sure the transfer learning keep most of pretrained features. In the LiDAR data training stage, we decided to use a higher learning rate comparing to optical imagery training stage to promise an effective feature learning. For the fully connected layer which fuses features from optical imagery and LiDAR data, as well as yields classification results, we also adopted a relatively higher learning rate strategy to bridge the connection between fused features and classification maps. In this project, we presented a deep learning model using both optical imagery and LiDAR data for urban land use classification. In this model, we considered remote sensing optical imagery features extracted from the pretrained model on natural images, features extracted from optical imagery itself, and features from LiDAR data. To facilitate the testing of the proposed deep learning framework, a prototype system was developed. Concerning the final objective of a case study of urban land use classification in Hong Kong, a land use mapping was generated and compared with such mapping with non-deep learning-based as well as single-source data-based methods. Overall, all the proposed objectives have been realized to our satisfaction and more research articles about the proposed methods and applications are being prepared.

14606315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14606315.value: Urban land use classification is a fundamental procedure for understanding the current situation of the urbanization. Optical imagery data as a traditional data source has been widely adopted to achieve this target due to its cost-effectiveness. Based on the optical imagery, we can use convolutional neural networks to extract its features and corresponding transferred features based on a pretrained network. Fusing these two distinct features, as well as combining the city skeleton extraction method, we can effectively perform land-use mapping. Compared to the optical imagery for the urban land-use investigation, the LiDAR sensor as an active sensor not only can acquire the 3D information of the surface and intensity value with respect to the ground objects, but also can avoid the negative effect of shadows. Therefore, it is possible to incorporate the LiDAR data into the urban land-use mapping. We also make full use of the powerful learning ability of deep learning models and proposed a novel deep learning framework that integrates optical imagery and LiDAR data. In the first stage, the proposed deep learning framework learns the high-level features of optical imagery, while the second stage is also made of a deep learning framework to explore the high-level features of the LiDAR data. The classification results are obtained by a fully connected network which inherits features from optical imagery based on features from LiDAR data. In this way, both data sources can provide the necessary information which contributes to generating a more accurate classification result. The proposed deep learning framework was applied to a real-world urban land use classification in Hong Kong and a series of classification results were generated. It was found that combining optical imagery and LiDAR data in the classification procedure will make the classification model more robust. In this research, a prototype system was also developed to facilitate the selection of stride size of overlapping areas, the data source, and the visualization of classification results in Hong Kong. In this way, users can view and compare classification results corresponding to the selected single-source or multi-source data. In summary, this project has delivered successfully an urban land use classification methodology combining optical imagery and LiDAR data in a city or a region.

14606315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14606315.value: Accurate urban land use classification is a vital component in urban environment monitoring and planning. Following the rapid urbanization, the complex diversity of urban landscape makes the urban land use classification extremely challenging. In particular, the problem becomes more complicated when considering the spectral confusion phenomenon with the optical remote sensing imagery. The proposed deep learning framework has successfully fused optical imagery and LiDAR data and obtained satisfactory results. However, in comparison with fully connected networks, a more effective approach should be devised to integrate features from different data sources. The efficiency and robustness are significant factors for the application of designed methods in the real world. Therefore, training a stable deep learning framework which can be directly applied to other cities is also a potential research direction. Parallel computing techniques may also be explored in such cases. Given the methodology which has been studied systematically, it should be scaled up to more cities and regions to demonstrate its values.

14606315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14606315.value: Land use patterns continue to change due to the evolution of human activities and government policies, which poses great challenges to updating urban land use maps. Remote sensing technologies have been widely used for land use/land cover mapping in support of various urban planning and environmental management applications. Typically, most of the urban land use classification methods are based on optical remote sensing images that are widely used. However, the problem of spectral confusion existing in using optical remote sensing imagery as the only source has reduced the classification accuracy. Unlike the optical imagery, the airborne light detection and ranging (LiDAR) sensor provides an active way to capture details of an urban surface in the form of point clouds featuring both elevation and intensity. This project has developed a deep learning framework that capitalizes on distinct high-level features from both optical imagery and LiDAR data to support urban land use classification. A novel framework is also proposed to fuse the two types of high-level features from these two data sources. The effectiveness of the proposed multi-source data fusion within a deep learning framework has been demonstrated through a case study in Hong Kong.

14606715.value: 城市環境感知：面向視覺品質評估的空間要素與心理狀態的相關性分析

14606715.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14606715.value: Prof Fung, Helene Hoi-lam Prof He, Jie Dr Hu, Mingyuan Prof Zhang, Yuanting

14606715.label: Project Objectives
14606715.value: An immersive virtual environment to simulate urban spaces and assess the visual quality in urban design: This project will introduce a virtual geographic environment (VGE) consisting of multi-dimensional representations of building geometry and multi-modal immersive experience. The immersive 3D environment with virtual features and avatar-based participants can provide appropriate solutions for incorporating the personal feelings from visual assessments into the dynamic simulation of complex urban environments. A solution for quantitatively acquiring and classifying emotional changes: This project will provide a quantitative method through EPOC mobile electroencephalographic (EEG) headsets to measure the emotion changes during the visual quality evaluations of surrounding environments. Personal psychological changes will be transferred into legible measurements and classified into a fractal dimension emotion space, supporting the advanced processing and computing with the spatial variables of urban spaces. 14606715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14606715.value: The visual quality of the environment has been identified as a major dimension of the public's perception in urban design. It may evoke strong emotional responses such as the esthetic experience of the urban surroundings. In urban spaces, the visual quality is generated by spatial variables (e.g. openness), and reflected on the psychological state of individuals (e.g. frustration), leaving a gap in between. The majority of empirical studies on the visual quality of the surrounding environment focus on the users’ perceived visual experience of the spatial variables rather than the change of their psychological state. Urban designers often gloss over the psychological state as "subjective" and unquantifiable. In addition, the common methods for collecting urban users’ psychological state and the related emotional changes are confined to qualitative interviews and questionnaires, making the quantitative estimation difficult. These current practices have hindered the urban designers from taking the psychological feelings of urban users into consideration. The connection between the psychological and the spatial dimension in the urban design process has not been fully figured out. This project presents a correlational-analysis method to explore the quantitative relationship between the spatial variables in urban environments and the psychological state of the urban users and to facilitate the visual quality assessment in urban design. It aims at bridging the gap among urban space, visual perception and emotional responses. The proposed methodology will comprise the following four steps: (1) providing a perceivable 3D geographic environment focusing on the multi-dimensional representations of building geometry and the multi-modal immersive experience for human perception through a virtuality-reality mixed way; (2) supporting a semantic and computational process to the visual quality assessment in urban spaces through quantitative spatial variables such as openness, enclosure and permeability; (3) incorporating EPOC mobile electroencephalographic (EEG) headsets to detect and quantitatively measure the users’ physiological states that are related to their emotional reactions (e.g., frustration and excitement) stimulated by spatial-visual perceptions to their spatial surroundings; (4) identifying the quantitative interdependency between the spatial variables of the urban environment and the psychological state of the users to support a close-to-life urban design process. The methodology will be applied in and evaluated by two case studies oriented to the typical urban spaces, one residential area and another open-square space. The results of this project will lead to a better understanding of urban spatial cognition and environmental psychology, and additionally improve the current urban design procedures. 在城市設計研究中，公眾的對於環境的感知很大程度上來源於視覺。城市環境的視覺體驗例如美學體驗，可以誘發人們強烈的情緒反應。同時在城市空間中，視覺品質的高低由一些空間變數（如開放度）所決定，反映在人們的心裡活動（如沮喪）中，但對兩者關係的研究存在著一定程度上的缺失。事實上，針對環境的視覺品質研究的傳統方法多是經驗性的，相關研究更強調於人們對於不同空間變數的視覺體驗，而缺少對於人們更深層次心理變化的關注。同樣的，社區居民的心理層面的評估只能受限於傳統的採訪訪問和問卷調查，而結果被認為是主觀的，不可量化的。這種傳統評估方式的不足也阻礙了在城市設計過程中對人們心理感受的考慮。總的來講，如何將心理因素和空間要素兩個方面相互結合來輔助進行城市設計，仍然是一個亟待解決的問題。 本研究旨在通過一種相關性分析的方法來挖掘城市空間中空間要素和居民心理要素之間的相關關係，建立一種城市設計視覺評估方法，解決在城市空間，視覺感知和情緒體驗交互中出現的問題。 本項目的研究方法將初步按照以下四個步驟進行：（1）通過虛擬實境的方法，提供一個面向多尺度建築幾何表達，多模式沉浸式體驗的可感知三維虛擬地理環境；（2）利用量化的視覺空間參數（諸如開放度，圍合度，通透度）建立一個面向城市設計的支援語義和計算的視覺品質評估方法；（3）結合EPOC移動可擕式腦電採集裝置，監測和量化被試在不同空間場景刺激下的情感狀態；（4）嘗試挖掘不同空間變數組合中的城市環境與被試心理狀態間的相關關係，支持更人性化的城市設計過程。 本研究的方法將常識針對兩個具體的實例開展應用與評估，包括住宅區域和公共開方區域。研究成果期望從城市空間認知，環境心理學的角度為城市空間帶來新的理解，以此優化城市設計過程。

14606715.label: Realisation of objectives
14606715.value: After months of intense investigation at the beginning stage, we found that using EEG as the approach to do human perception evaluation under complex environment is not flexible, considering its presicion and application scope. Hence, we have seek another way to evaluate human perception with high accuracy. However, Understanding the relationship between the two factors quantitatively has been limited by the lack of computational tools and approaches to representing urban physical environment comprehensively. We shift the methodology to achieve the original goal from using EEG device to leverage the urban street-level images and deep learning based computer vision technology. Due to the fast development of web mapping services and mobile internet, street-level imagery is being generated at a rapid speed and densely covers every corner of a city, potentially offering new approaches for researchers to observe, perceive and understand the urban environment. To learn and grasp the high-level visual knowledge of a streetscape automatically and further to facilitate perceiving the urban activity and socioeconomic environment, in this study, we employ a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN). The objective of this study is threefold: (1) Designing a DCNN architecture to represent the urban physical environment comprehensively and quantitatively; (2) Quantifying the relationship between urban built environment and human urban perceptions; (3) Exploring the visual objects that highly correlated with urban spatiotemporal activity patterns. This shifted objective is of significance both scientifically---in shedding light on connections between the physical settings and human perceptions of a place---and practically---in taking advantage of street-level imagery to derive fine-scale socioeconomic information of an urban area and to help urban planners and geographers in urban observation, urban studies, and planning. The whole project has been divided into two stages: First, we propose a framework to quantify the local of a place (urban physical environment); Second, we propose a methodology to quantify the connections between urban physical environments. For the first stage. Locale is one of the basic elements of place, referring to the physical settings and visual appearance of a place. Understanding and representing a locale is of great importance in terms of human perception and human activity. However, taking a quantitative measurement of the visual appearance of urban environment has proven to be challenging because visual information is inherently ambiguous and semantically impoverished. To mitigate this issue, our proposed method employs street-level images as the proxy for urban physical appearance, utilizes the recently developed image semantic segmentation techniques to parse an urban scene into scene elements, and proposes a framework for locale representation using scene elements. The framework is composed of two major components: street scene ontology and street visual descriptor, which are aimed at street scene qualitative understanding and quantitative representation respectively. A case study is developed to demonstrate the application and advantage of the street scene ontology and street visual descriptor. A series of quantitative analyses demonstrates the ability and great potential of the framework for investigating the connections between place and other socioeconomic factors. For the second stage , a data-driven machine learning approach is proposed to measure how people perceive a place in a large-scale urban region. Specifically, a deep learning model, which has been trained on millions of human ratings of street-level imagery, was used to predict human perceptions of a street view image. The model achieved a high accuracy rate in predicting six human perceptual indicators, namely, safe, lively, beautiful, wealthy, depressing, and boring. This model can help to map the distribution of the city-wide human perception for a new urban region. Furthermore, a series of statistical analyses was conducted to determine the visual elements that may cause a place to be perceived as different perceptions. From the 150 object categories segmented from the street view images, various objects were identified as being positively or negatively correlated with each of the six perceptual indicators. The results take researchers and urban planners one step toward understanding the interactions of the place sentiments and semantics.

14606715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14606715.value: Street view imagery is a type of promising and growing big geo-data providing current and historical images in more than 200 countries for urban physical environment representation and audit. Such data not only describe the visual details of urban physical environment, but also contain information about urban functions, socio-economics, and human dynamics. How to extract the rich semantic information from street view imagery efficiently has always been a challenging issue. Also, in the future work, it is promising to explore to what extent the street view imagery is able to reveal not only the physical environments, but also the socio-economic environments. Khosla et al. identified this issue and proposed to “look beyond the visible scene”, where they trained a binary-classification model to predict which image points closer to a grocery or appears safer. We summarized this trend as 'place semantics reasoning', referring to the studies trying to infer and estimate the invisible factors, socio-economics, demographics and human dynamics from street view imagery. More wide and in-depth issues, including how physical environments were involved and whether a universal law exists regarding the distribution of physical elements in the space, are expected to be explored in future works.

14606715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14606715.value: This work provides a method of understanding what kind of urban environment will induce different kinds of emotions of citizens. We use street view images to represent urban environments, collect emotional evaluations of these images from participants and figure out the relationship between urban environments and human perceptions. This project helps urban planners and geographers in urban studies and planning to build a better city.

14606815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14606815.value: Since the early 1980s the Taiwan New Cinema (hereafter TNC) movement had attracted global attention when new directors, signalling a departure from their predecessors, turned to local realities and histories for their cinematic representations. Hou Hsiao-hsien and Edward Yang emerged as key figures as their films won critical acclaim at international film festivals. A second generation, led by Ang Lee and Tsai Ming-liang, followed in the 1990s, heralding a transnational turn in Taiwan cinema through the production and distribution of their films. The new millennium witnessed a return to a more localized as well as popular mode of filmmaking, marking what has been called a post-TNC era. Today, Taiwan cinema is famed as much for its authors of art cinema as it is for recent box-office-smashing hits such as Cape No. 7 (Wei Te-sheng, 2008) and You Are the Apple of My Eye (Giddens Ko, 2011). This project is the first of its kind to critically assess, through notions of authorship, transnationality and historiography, the impact of the TNC movement into the twenty-first century. It will propose, first and foremost, that the currency of Taiwan cinema, especially as it circulates in international film festivals, art-house circuits and academia in the west, is to be found in an auteur cinema that travels transnationally and thereby complicates the historiography of Taiwan cinema as a national cinema. Secondly, it will demonstrate how this transnational turn has taken on a linguistic dimension in the new millennium by looking at, on the one hand, the dual career of Ang Lee, who makes both Chinese-language and English-language films, and, on the other hand, selected non-Chinese-language (including Japanese and French) films made by Hou and Tsai. Finally, the project will engage critically with questions of historiography, specifically on the life and death of the TNC movement, and the sense in which Taiwan cinema can be said to have entered a post-TNC era. This project will advance a methodological approach that combines textual analysis, historical context, and political economy. It will suggest that the measure of a cinema’s success cannot be based on domestic box-office figures alone but must also consider its appeal to filmmakers and audiences across the world. Indeed, cinema can be regarded as a form of soft power that has helped Taiwan break through its diplomatic isolation to gain prominence via global cultural capital. It is living proof that smallness is no hindrance to greatness. 一九八零年代初期，台灣新電影運動的新銳導演與他們的前輩分道揚鑣， 開始著眼於本土現實和歷史，自此吸引了全球的關注。運動的主將侯孝賢和楊德昌的電影在國際影展大放異彩，而一九九零年代竄起的第二代導演如李安和蔡明亮，其電影的製作和發行模式則宣告了台灣電影的跨國轉向。進入新的千禧年的所謂後新電影時期，電影生產回歸本土與通俗的取向。如今，台灣電影不僅以其藝術電影的作者著稱，近期的票房奇蹟如《海角七號》和《那些年，我們一起追的女孩》也備受矚目。 本計劃為第一個檢視台灣新電影運動進入二十一世紀的影響力的研究，將通過作者、跨國性和歷史書寫的角度切入分析。本研究將首先提出，台灣電影的資本，尤其在國際影展、藝術電影院線和西方學術界的流通，取決於作者電影的觀念，使之得以跨國旅行，並衝擊台灣電影作為國族電影的歷史書寫模式。其次，本研究將展示此跨國性的語言層面，一方面審視李安同時拍攝華語電影與英語電影的雙軌事業，另一方面關注侯孝賢和蔡明亮執導的一些非華語（包含日語和法語）影片。最後，本研究將反思歷史書寫的問題，尤其關於台灣新電影運動的生與死，以及台灣電影在什麼意義上可以說是進入了後新電影時期。 在研究方法上，本計劃將採取結合文本分析、歷史脈絡和政治經濟學的路向。研究將指出，一個電影的成功與否不能只是以本地票房數據為準繩，而必須同時考量它對世界各地的電影工作者和觀眾的吸引力。誠然，電影可以被視為一種軟實力，它幫助台灣衝出外交孤立的困局，透過全球文化資本而受到矚目。它證明了小並不足以構成偉大的絆腳石。

14606815.label: Realisation of objectives
14606815.value: Objective 1: To investigate the role of authorship in Taiwan New Cinema (TNC) The project posits that authorship is central to TNC’s ability to cross borders (both national and linguistic) to the extent that the historiographical writing of Taiwan cinema has to be reimagined. It achieves this objective in the following ways: (a) Devoting three chapters (2-4) to key TNC authors, namely Hou Hsiao-hsien, Ang Lee, and Tsai Ming-liang. (b) Highlighting the central role of authorship in Chapter 1 in which a documentary on TNC elicits expressions of admiration for TNC authors from international filmmakers, programmers, and critics. (c) Pointing, in the Epilogue, to a younger generation of directors from Southeast Asia and the People’s Republic of China who have demonstrated their affinity with TNC authors in their filmmaking, generating an afterlife for Taiwan cinema that exists both within and beyond the island’s shores. Objective 2: To delineate the transnational conditions of production and consumption of selected films and filmmakers This project takes the year 2000, when Ang Lee’s Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon was released, as the starting point of TNC’s transnational turn in terms of the conditions of production and consumption. It further refines this transnational turn into the following sub-categories: (a) In Chapter 2, an aural turn for Hou Hsiao-hsien in making films in French and Japanese languages, respectively Flight of the Red Balloon (2009) and Café Lumière (2003). The films are sponsored by French and Japanese institutions, and they privilege aural over visual elements. (b) In Chapter 3, a medial turn for Tsai Ming-liang in his shift from releasing films in the movie theatre to staging them as part of an installation in art galleries and museums in Europe and Taiwan. This turn coincides with Tsai’s use of the digital camera, which facilitates this medial change as well as release of his short films on the World Wide Web. (c) In Chapter 4, an industrial turn for Ang Lee from making Chinese-language films co-produced with a Taiwan studio to making English-language films in England and the United States. The chapter examines The Life of Pi (2012) as a case study as its production brought into collaboration Taiwanese officials (Taichung city government) and a Hollywood studio. (d) In Chapter 5, an affective turn in which local film productions eschew the international soft power of authors (Chapters 2-4) by foregrounding instead a structure of feeling known as “little freshness” that has a regional appeal in China and Hong Kong. Objective 3: To engage critically with questions of historiography, especially as it relates to the periodization of Taiwan New Cinema The question of historiography is dealt with explicitly in the following manner: (a) Chapter 1 provides an alternative historiographical account of the TNC movement by constructing a story about TNC’s reception outside Taiwan, using as its lens the documentary, Flowers of Taipei: Taiwan New Cinema (Hsieh Chin-lin, 2014). (b) The transnational and translingual filmmaking careers of authors laid out in Chapters 2 to 4 illustrate that nation- and language-based historiographies are no longer tenable. (c) Chapter 5 argues that periodization of TNC, in particular the discourse of post-TNC, is a form of “space-clearing gesture” aimed at staking a claim in film historiography but founded on rather shaky ground. (d) The Epilogue suggests that TNC’s resurrection might take place mainly among foreign filmmakers (some of whom based in Taiwan) on whom TNC’s soft power continues to have a lasting impact, thus further complicating the writing of Taiwan’s film history. Objective 4: To contribute to film scholarship by challenging and complicating concepts such as transnational cinema, accented cinema, and Sinophone cinema Whilst the notion of transnational cinema, especially “critical transnationalism” (Higbee and Lim 2010), has been engaged throughout the manuscript, the concept of accented cinema is explicitly challenged in Chapter 4 (on Ang Lee) and that of Sinophone cinema questioned in Chapter 2 (on Hou Hsiao-hsien). The project also mobilizes and reflects upon other film- and media-related theories (from sound studies in Chapter 2 to intermediality in Chapter 3) as well as critical theory such as affect theory (Chapter 5). Most importantly, it is the first single-authored research monograph to employ the notion of soft power for the study of cinema. Objective 5: To advance a methodology that includes qualitative textual analysis and historical context but also considers quantitative conditions of production and consumption The Introduction stages a particular reflection on using soft power as a method for the study of films. More generally, in terms of methodology, three approaches are adopted in the following ways: (a) All chapters typically begin with a contextual discussion, which spells out how each case demonstrates TNC’s soft power and delineates the conditions of production and consumption that have made each case possible. Policy studies is also undertaken to illustrate, for example, the Taiwanese authorities’ efforts in promoting Taiwan film abroad (Introduction) and tourism at home through film production initiatives (Chapter 4). (b) Quantitative tables are included in some chapters (Introduction, Chapters 3 to 5) to provide information on number of films produced each year, box-office figures, market share, awards won, etc. These facts and figures are used to buttress arguments, for example, against the scapegoating of TNC as responsible for the decline of Taiwan’s film industry. (c) Textual analysis is employed where suitable to illuminate more clearly and specifically the examples, such as the privileging of sonic over visual elements in Chapter 2 and affective discursive expressions of youth consumers towards “little freshness” products in Chapter 5. Overall, the objectives have been achieved in a substantive manner, that is, within the discursive construction of the manuscript. The main challenge faced during the development of the project is time, with the completion date of the manuscript delayed by 12 months for two reasons. (a) The adoption of soft power as an overarching framework after the start of the project (as laid out in the mid-term report). Whilst this has given the project greater conceptual coherence, its impact is the devotion of more time to rethink and reframe the materials and arguments to the extent that previously published materials now constitute no more than a quarter to a third of the manuscript (rather than half to two-thirds as initially presumed). (b) An oversight in planning the GRF project, this being my first application soon after I relocated to Hong Kong in 2014. The original schedule did not take into account other research projects that I needed to complete alongside the GRF project. This, however, has resulted in an additional research outcome produced for this GRF (see below). Extra institutional demands (such as overseeing the Research Assessment Exercise submission in my unit of assessment) were also imposed upon me during the grant period. Thanks, however, to teaching relief provided by my institution, I have been able to complete the manuscript by taking up a visiting fellowship at Clare Hall, Cambridge between January and July 2018. The manuscript has now been sent out for consideration at the University of Hawai’i Press, the publisher of my two previous monographs.
