14611015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14611015.value: The 50-year history of new towns and major urban developments in Hong Kong has seen the growth of the city with the highest population density in the world. In the process, it has created unique urban morphological forms that have inevitably changed the local urban climatic conditions (Lam, 2006; Lau & Ng, 2013). Understanding the urban climatic changes of the urban forms in the past allow planners have the perspective for gaining an insight into the future. It also allows decisions on future development to be made in context. This study aims to trace, from a historical perspective, the influences of new towns and major urban developments in Hong Kong on its local urban climatic conditions. It then further aims to investigate the relationship between the urban morphology of the high density city and its urban climatic characteristics in the future. This study firstly collects historical records (1960-2010) on Hong Kong's land-use data from the Lands Department of the Hong Kong Government (LandsD). Major urban growth periods can be time sequenced. Secondly it employs a digitizer to get digitalized land-use data in the Geography Information System (GIS) (Rumsey and Williams, 2002); then, future land use changes (until 2030) can be statistically predicted by using Change Analyst (Huang & Sin, 2010). In the meanwhile, meteorological records (1960-2010) are acquired from the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) and the linear regression method called JMP 0.9 Statistical Package can be adopted to separate urbanization effect and climate change for the past. Furthermore, this will be coupled to the climate change projections of the global climate models (GCMs) from the fifth phase of Climate Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP5) for the future climatic conditions to the year 2030. The urban morphological and climatic data sets are then be entered into the Weather Research and Forecasting with an Urban Canopy Model (WRF-UCM). Based on principle component analysis (PCA), the relatively importance of planning parameters like Frontal Area Density (FAD), Ground Coverage Ratio (GCR), Plot Ratio (PR), of urban forms may be understood. This understanding of the time series and component based relationship between urban forms and urban climatic condition provides a reference for the planners on which planning parameter to optimise for the future. This is important for planners of high density cities in the tropical regions – especially when they are working at the thresholds of heat stress and urban thermal comfort issues. 香港新城鎮和主要城市發展的50年歷史已經見證該市成長為在世界上人口密度最高的城市。在這個過程中，它創造了自己獨特的城市形態形式，也改變了當地的城市氣候（Lam, 2006; Lau & Ng, 2013）。瞭解過往城市形態改變對於城市氣候變化的影響，可使規劃者洞悉未來，也使未來發展決策基於當地的歷史文脈。 這項研究的目的在於從歷史的角度來看，追蹤香港新城鎮和主要城市發展對當地城市氣候的影響。它也旨在探討在未來高密城市形態和的城市氣候特徵之間的關係。 這項研究首先收集香港政府地政總署有關香港土地利用數據的歷史記錄（1960年至2010年）。主要城市成長期可依時間序列選取。其次，將採用了數字化儀在地理資訊系統（GIS）中構建數字化土地利用數據（Rumsey and Williams, 2002）;接著，通過變化分析軟體（Huang & Sin, 2010）預測未來（至2030年）的土地利用變化。同時，（1960至2010年）氣象記錄從香港天文臺獲得，JMP 0.9的統計軟件包將被用來分離過往城市氣候中城市化與氣候變化的影響因素。對於未來2030年的氣候狀況，將利用The 5th Phase of Climate Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP5)的global climate models (GCMs) 預測基於氣候變化下的未來氣候狀況。所得的城市形態和氣候數據將被輸入到WRF-UCM模式中進行類比研究。基於主成分數理統計（PCA）所得，一系列針對城市形態相對重要的規劃參數將被分析和規劃者作設計參考。

14611015.label: Realisation of objectives
14611015.value: Land use land cover data of both Hong Kong and its neighbouring area, the Pearl River Delta region from the 1970s to the 2010s were developed by adopting the level 0 method of World Urban Database and Access Portal Tools (WUDAPT) and local climate zone (LCZ) classification to capture intra-urban morphological variety based on the available Landsat satellite images. Due to the quality of satellite images, one land cover land use data set of every decade was developed to capture major urban growth from 1960-2010. Based on the developed historical land use land cover data, the future land use in 2030 was also predicted and developed. The developed local climate zone data were adopted as input data in the WRF simulations. The implementation of LCZ data in WRF simulation involves uncertainties that arise from various sources. These uncertainties include the following. (1) The supervised classification of different LCZs in the WUDAPT approach by satellite images introduces uncertainty in identifying the correct LCZs. (2) Given that the current WUDAPT approach based on LCZs requires selecting UCPs from a range of values associated with each LCZ, the choices may not accurately represent local conditions, thus introducing some degree of uncertainty into the modeling results. (3) As the WUDAPT approach divides urban grids into classes (LCZs), compared with the continuous UCPs of the NUDAPT approach, this discretization introduces another source of uncertainty. (4) The subsampling of WUDAPT and NUDAPT datasets into the uWRF’s domain also generates uncertainty. In this study, different methods of WUDAPT level 0 prep processing methods are carried out to isolate the source of uncertainties (1) to (4) above. The corresponding WRF result is compared with NUDAPT, which acts as the baseline “reference”; the extent of deviation of the WUDAPT cases vis à vis the NUDAPT case provides the means to quantify different sources of uncertainty. After quantifying those different sources of uncertainty, we offer guidance for implementing WUDAPT in uWRF to possibly minimize uncertainty. Then we evaluate the improvement in the performance of uWRF with NUDAPT, along with the corresponding and suggested WUDAPT approach as input, for comparison with the traditional Noah bulk scheme and local and non-local planetary boundary layer (PBL) schemes, by considering surface observation station data. A series of WRF simulations also provided necessary information about how much local urban growth/urbanization affects urban climate and also how future urban climate looks like under both urbanization and different climate change scenarios. These simulated results were compared and validate by the observed meteorological records. There are several barriers to the development of historical land use data of Hong Kong. Since 80-90% of time in Hong Kong are cloudy or partially cloudy, the satellite images’ quality are not very good and available satellite images are limited. That is why we decided for every ten years, we developed one set of land use land cover data.

14611015.label: Major findings and research outcome
14611015.value: The land use land cover data of both Hong Kong and its Land use land cover data of both Hong Kong and its neighbouring area, the Pearl River Delta region from the 1970s to the 2010s were developed base on the collected Landsat images. Their resolution can reach 100 m. The method was introduced in the journal paper titled ‘Mapping the local climate zones of urban areas by GIS-based and WUDAPT methods: A case study of Hong Kong’ published in Urban Climate (Volume 24, June 2018, Pages 567-576, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.uclim.2017.10.001). The results also were published in the journal paper titled Local Climate Zone Study for Sustainable Megacities Development by Using Improved WUDAPT Methodology – A Case Study in Guangzhou (Procedia Environmental Sciences, Volume 36, 2016, Pages 82–89). Since the developed LCZ data was adopted as input data in the WRF simulations, the corresponding evaluation of uWRF performance and modelling guidance, and the refinement of roughness length Value were tested and introduced firstly in the poster papers published in the 10th International Conference on Urban Climate/ 14th Symposium on the Urban Environment. Two conference papers got the “Poster Honourable Mention Award”. We were invited to develop them into a full paper in the Urban Climate News to share our research experience with the members of the International Association on Urban Climate. A journal paper was published in Urban Climate. A series of WRF simulations for the year of 1988, 1999 and 2009 also provided necessary information about how much local urban growth/urbanization affects urban climate. These simulated results were reported in the journal paper titled ‘Investigation of the meteorological effects of urbanization in recent decades: A case study of major cities in Pearl River Delta’ published in Urban Climate (Volume 26, Pages 174-187, Accepted 12 August 2018, Available online 11 September 2018.) Another paper titled ‘Projecting future urbanization and its impact on local climate under different climate change scenarios in 2030 in the Pearl River Delta Region’ were submitted to the International Journal of Climatology. It is under review now.

14611015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14611015.value: This study has been a part of the global initiative project named ‘World Urban Database and Access Portal Tools (WUDAPT)’, which has drawn a world-wide attention. Our gained research experience in developing land use land cover data and also its applications into urban climate modelling have been summarised and shared in the below two papers: • WUDAPT: An Urban Weather, Climate, and Environmental Modeling Infrastructure for the Anthropocene, Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society (Volume 99, Issue 9, Pages 1907-1924, https://doi.org/10.1175/BAMS-D-16-0236.1) . • Generating WUDAPT Level 0 data – Current status of production and evaluation, Urban Climate (Volume 27, March 2019, Pages 24-45, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.uclim.2018.10.001) WUDAPT method and its LCZ data development also have been recommended by the World Meteorological Organization in the recent Guide for Urban Integrated Hydro-Meteorological, Climate and Environmental Services. https://www.wmo.int/pages/prog/arep/gaw/documents/UrbanIntegratedServicesPart1aConceptandMethodologyEC-70.pdf The developed land use information and simulation results are important for the government to review current urban development and planning’s impact on local climatic conditions. The present study can therefore serve as an useful reference for future urban development under different climate change scenarios.

14611015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14611015.value: This research project has developed a time series of land use land cover data for both Hong Kong and its neighbour area, the Pearl River Delta region from the 1970s to the 2030s. It is found that local urbanization could be the major reason to worse the thermal environment especially in the summer time and also weaken urban wind environment, which potentially would worse our citizens’ door thermal comfort conditions. This study also provide useful land use information and projected future climatic conditions under different climate change scenarios. These research outcomes could serve as reference for local government when they make urban development and planning strategies regarding to climate change.

14611315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14611315.value: 該擬建項目旨在發展一個用於描述聽障學生漢語語法知識的框架。本研究中的“語法知識”意為說話者對於目標語的形式句法和語義特性（例如語序、句法移位操作、功能詞以及轄域理解）的內在语言知识 。很多研究已證實，正常發展的兒童在幼年就已毫不費力地獲得了這些決定了人類語言能力的特性; 調查聽障兒童如何獲得語法知識還待探討。 由於聽力損失，聽障兒童一直面臨難以接觸語言輸入的挑戰，並且不能都達到語言獲得的最終狀態。但是過往研究鮮有從語言獲得角度出發來記錄他們語法發展或解釋其學習困難的系統性研究。 最近在香港有一項研究嘗試開發一套測量聽障學生漢語語法知識發展的評估工具，因為本地的中文書面語以漢語語法為基礎。該評估工具的初始設計參考了中文語言學的語法分析以及中文一語及二語獲得的相關研究。目前，它涵蓋了15個語法結構，多數為句法和形態句法結構，並由4個誘導任務測量。先行研究的結果表明，來自一項設立於常規學校的手語雙語計劃的香港聽障學生在小學四年級時，已達到與健聽常模接近的水平。但他們在掌握存現句、關係子句、被字句和介詞等方面還存在持續性困難。該擬建項目有以下幾大目標：（a）通過增加漢語語法中有代表性的句法和語義特性來完善該描述性工具；（b）建立健聽常模以供比較，從而為臨床應用和聾教育提供更多資訊；（c）比較和考察香港地區和中國內地聽障兒童獲得中文語法知識的情況。 調查聽障學生語法知識的發展至關重要，原因有二：首先，這能讓我們驗證語言獲得理論應用到聽障人群的可行性；其次，從應用角度出發，語法知識被認為是口語讀寫能力發展的一大要素，而讀寫能力發展又能支持聽障學生的學業。

14611315.label: Realisation of objectives
14611315.value: The project represents the first-ever attempt to develop and standardise a tool – Chinese Grammatical Assessment (CGA) – for measuring deaf children’s knowledge of Mandarin Chinese through the written mode. It fills the gap of assessment tools for measuring grammatical knowledge of deaf children in the Chinese context, whose inadequate knowledge of spoken language grammar hampers their literacy development. Regarding Objective 1, the team undertook three tasks: (a) identified relevant simple and complex linguistic structures and contexts of rule application; (b) consulted the literature for some recent grammatical analysis of the structures concerned; and (c) revisited the test items and assessment formats of a preliminary tool based on results of a pilot test. In the end, the team decided to separate the tool into two levels: CGA-KG & CGA-PS. CGA-KG targets children who are in their final year of kindergarten education. The tool, which includes 15 grammatical structures with 60 items all formatted into a word ordering task, assesses knowledge of syntactic word order of some basic grammatical structures such as simple phrase structures as well as declarative and interrogative sentences. The findings offer a baseline upon which one can track how efficiently children process Mandarin Chinese grammar through reading over time. CGA-PS includes 24 grammatical structures with 190 items. These components include word order syntax of more complex grammatical structures, functional morphemes, morphosyntactic categories, other properties of complex grammatical structures such as scope interaction. A variety of tasks were designed to probe specific properties of the grammatical structures included in the tool. After obtaining results from a pilot test in the summer of 2016 based on 1030 hearing children studying from Primary 1 to Primary 6 in schools in Beijing, Nanjing and Tianjin, the research team decided to revise the test design again: (a) replaced the word ordering task and the fill-in-the-blanks task with a multiple-choice task, for the test of word order syntax and functional morphemes; (b) added a grammaticality judgement task for the test of morphosyntactic knowledge, (c) retained the picture selection task for comprehension of complex grammatical structures and interpretation of scope interaction, and (d) retained the truth-value judgement task for the comprehension of aspectual markings and other complex constructions. CGA-KG and CGA-PS were eventually designed to be online assessment so children could engage in the activity using an iPad or a computer that has internet access (CGA-PS: http://www.cslds.org/cga_ps_hk/ & CGA-KG: http://www.cslds.org/cga_kg_hk/). As for Objective 2, a series of norming exercises in Hong Kong and China took place between 2016-2019. In total, 17 kindergartens and 345 children in their third year of KG education participated in the norming exercise for CGA-KG. The team adopted the following criteria in screening data: testees (a) completing all test items, (b) achieving at least 70% in a vocabulary check, (c) having a clear set of biodata and no records of disabilities. Based on these criteria, only data from 272 children were entered for analysis. CGA-KG was not normed on the student population in Mainland China because children there are not encouraged to develop reading or writing skills in kindergarten education. As for CGA-PS, the norming exercise was first conducted in Mainland China in the summer of 2016. Hearing children from the mainstream schools in Beijing, Nanjing and Tianjin, 1030 in total from Primary 1 to Primary 6, participated in the exercise. Unfortunately, since the team discovered some task and item effects in the assessment of some newly incorporated grammatical structures, they decided to suspend the activity and discarded all data. After the elicitation tasks had been further modified and trialled with some hearing students in Hong Kong, the second norming exercise took place in China in 2017. During this exercise, another group of hearing children from mainstream schools in Mainland China, 3175 in total, took part in the exercise. They came from 7 schools in Beijing, Shanghai, Chongqin, Dalian, Suzhou, and PingXiang (in Jiangxi province). Based on the same screening criteria, data from 2440 hearing students were entered for analysis. After China, norming was conducted in Hong Kong in 2018-2019, 2198 students attending 11 mainstream schools in Hong Kong from Primary 1 to Primary 6 participated. In the end, only data from 1052 students were entered for analysis. For all three sets of norming data, Rasch analysis was adopted to look for outfits in items and persons in order to build a unidimensional model of grammatical development based on this assessment tool. As for Objective 3, data collection from deaf students was conducted during 2016-2018. The first set of data, made up of 1100 students from 5 deaf schools in Beijing, Chengdu, Nanjing, Tianjin, and Guangzhou, was collected at the same time as the first norming exercise. They were discarded due to the team’s decision to modify the test design. New data were collected in 2017 with 470 students from a different set of deaf schools in Chongqing, Beijing, Dalian, Pingxiang (in Jiangxi province), Foshan and Zhongshan (in Guangdong province). After applying the screening criteria, data from 357 deaf students were entered for analysis. As for Hong Kong, 61 deaf children studying from Primary 1 to Primary 6 were tested using the tool. The data size of deaf children from China and Hong Kong was small for the following reasons. For China, the size of the deaf schools during the second exercise was relatively smaller than the deaf schools that participated in the first data collection. As for Hong Kong, the only deaf school declined the research team’s invitation for collaboration on the grounds of privacy and confidentiality of deaf students. This school has a size of around 70 deaf students and keeps a database of mainstreamed deaf students for their out-of-class support. In the end, the research team resorted to collecting data from a group of deaf students who enrolled in the sign bilingualism and co-enrollment education programme in the mainstream setting. This unique educational environment created a research opportunity for examining the effect of sign bilingual education on the grammatical development of deaf as well as hearing students. The research team also attempted to create a literacy assessment toolkit by including a vocabulary and a reading comprehension test. Li’s (2000) Pre-school and Primary Chinese Literacy Scale (PPCLS)1 was trailed for the feasibility of adoption. The results revealed that Subscales C & D, which demanded auditory-oral skills posed enormous difficulty to younger deaf students. Nevertheless, a simple vocabulary check was devised based on the vocabulary items used to compose the test sentences in CGA-KG and CGA-PS. A reading comprehension test with 12 passages scaled for difficulty developed by Lin and Qi (2005)2 was also trailed. In the end, only 3 passages were adopted due to the constraint of time for completing all assessment procedures. On the whole, the project has been successful in developing and standardizing an assessment tool to gauge the grammatical development of Mandarin Chinese of deaf children in Hong Kong and China. It has been normed and used to examine the grammatical development of deaf children in both places. 1Li, H. (2000). 14611315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14611315.value: (A) Research findings 1. CGA-KG for Hong Kong: hearing children during the third year of kindergarten education have mastered the word order of most grammatical structures (>70%); however, they showed difficulty in acquiring determiner phrases, sentences with modals, A-not-A questions and wh-questions. 2. Norming CGA-PS on hearing children in Hong Kong and China: The hearing children from Hong Kong have mastered 10 out of 24 grammatical structures in Mandarin Chinese by the end of Primary 1, including aspect, reflexive and pronoun, comparative, negation, quantification, object control sentence, negation of quantifier SUOYOU, and short bei-passive. However, they showed persistent difficulty in localizer, achieving just 61% by Primary 5. The hearing children in China have mastered 15 grammatical structures by Primary 1 and almost all except DEs, relative clauses and interaction between ZHENME and HUI by Primary 2. The acquisition order of the grammatical structures was similar between the two norming populations. However, some differences were observed. The hearing children in China acquired locative constructions, localizers and question particles earlier than the hearing children from Hong Kong. On the other hand, the Hong Kong students were more able to distinguish the functional morpheme DEs (i.e. 的，地，得) than their Chinese counterparts who could only achieve an accuracy level of 66% at Primary 5. 3. CGA-PS by deaf children in China & Hong Kong: deaf children from China generally performed poorly on a majority of grammatical structures throughout their education. At Secondary 2 and 3, they showed a competency level equivalent to hearing students at Primary 1. For the SLCO deaf children in Hong Kong, although they lagged behind their hearing peers initially, they progressed in a pace similar to their hearing peers and almost caught up with them by Primary 5 (deaf accuracy = 84%). (B) Research Outcomes • An online platform for assessing Mandarin Chinese grammar via the written mode was established (CGA-KG (HK): http://www.cslds.org/cga_kg_hk/; CGA-PS(HK): http://www.cslds.org/cga_ps_hk/; CGA-PS(China): http://www.cslds.org/cga_ps_mainland/). Both tools will be open to teachers and clinicians to support them to diagnose deaf children’s development of Mandarin Chinese. • An online platform with resources to support the teaching and learning of Mandarin Chinese grammar was developed (http://www.cslds.org/chinese_grammar/). • Li Qun, postgraduate student trained in this project, has graduated from the PhD programme and joined West China Hospital of Sichuan University. She adapted CGA-PS into an independent measure for her project on autistic children’s acquisition of scalar implicature in Mandarin Chinese.

14611315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14611315.value: Now that CGA-KG and CGA-PS have been normed and tested using data from the hearing and deaf children of Hong Kong and China, it lays the foundation for comparative study between deaf children studying in deaf schools and regular schools, with findings suggesting the effectiveness of different modes of education on the grammatical development and literacy attainment of deaf children. There is ongoing discussion with speech and language therapy professionals on how to package the tool to support their daily practice. In future, a vocabulary test can be designed to supplement CGA-PS/CGA-KG and the reading comprehension test. Future assessment in reading comprehension may adopt the whole test developed by Lin and Qi (2005). There is also talk of establishing equivalent assessment and learning platforms at West China Hospital of Sichuan University to support degree training in audiology and language pathology there. The PhD thesis also shows that CGA can also be adapted to diagnose grammatical knowledge of other atypical populations. Last, more papers reporting on the norming of CGA as well as grammatical development of deaf children in China and Hong Kong are being written up to disseminate the research findings and the availability of the tool of assessment.

14611315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14611315.value: Due to deaf children’s hearing loss, existing language assessment tools, which adopt an auditory-oral mode in examining deaf children’s grammatical knowledge of Mandarin Chinese, may lead to biased results. The project represents the first-ever attempt to develop and standardise a tool – Chinese Grammatical Assessment – which uses a written mode in the assessment. Assessing grammatical knowledge is crucial as previous research has confirmed its relationship with literacy development, an area in which deaf children consistently show poor performance. This tool can gauge their rate and order of acquisition of grammatical structures in Mandarin Chinese. It consists of two sub-tools, one for kindergarten and the other one for primary students. It measures knowledge of syntactic word order, morphosyntax and function words, scope and aspectual markings, and a variety of syntactic constructions. It has been normed on the hearing children populations in Hong Kong and China and applied to analyse the grammatical development of deaf children in both places. Results showed a similar order of acquisition between hearing and deaf children with most grammatical structures, but differences were also observed with some specific ones. With modifications, CGA can be adopted to assess grammatical knowledge of other atypical populations.

14611415.label: Realisation of objectives
14611415.value: The first objective of this project is to develop a tractable model of dynamic legislative bargaining. We first consider a baseline model with symmetric voting weight. A set of n parties bargain over a renewable surplus in each of an infinite number of periods. In each period, there is a status quo policy and a randomly selected party can propose a new policy. If the new policy defeat the status quo via majority voting, it will be implemented in the current period and becomes the status quo for the next period; otherwise the status quo policy will be implemented and remain in force. In a generic situation, various winning coalitions can form to pass different policies. For example, in a three-party case, any two parties can form a minimal winning coalition (MWC henceforth). We further generalize the baseline model to allow a general distribution of voting weight. In this model, each party controls a fraction of the total numbers of parliament seats or votes. If several parties jointly control more than the majority of votes, they can form a winning coalition and implement a policy that they all agree on. Under certain conditions, a given voting weight distribution can be normalized into a unique equivalent homogeneous representation, and then, a party’s contribution to a MWC is measured by its effective voting weight, which is equal to the ratio of its normalized voting weight to the normalized majority fraction. Both the baseline model and the generalized model are highly tractable. We also considered several possible modifications of the model to allow endogenously determined proposers, which worth further investigation. The first objective is thus fully achieved. The second objective is to investigate the properties of Markov perfect equilibria (MPEs) of the dynamic legislative bargaining game. In the theoretical analysis, we are particularly interested in the stationary MPEs with the appealing properties of stable policies and persistent winning coalitions. There are multiple MPEs with such properties and we characterize the MPE that satisfies the size principle, that is, only parties of a MWC receive positive shares. Moreover, the equilibrium outcome is also consistent with the Gamson’s Law. More specifically, in the baseline model with symmetric voting weight, parties in a persistent MWC share the surplus equally; in the model with general voting weight distribution, each party in the MWC receives a share proportional to its effective voting weight. We also spent considerable effort on the modified model with endogenously determined proposer, hoping that we could obtain a sharper theoretical prediction, say, a uniqueness result, but it turned out to be extremely challenging and we have not obtained any clear-cut result. Thus, this objective is only partially achieved (80%). The third objective is to explore a dynamic version of Gamson’s Law and provide a game theoretic foundation for it. We characterize a stationary MPE of the dynamic legislative bargaining game and the equilibrium outcome is consistent with the Gamson’s Law. More specifically, for a given distribution of voting weight, we first normalize it into the unique equivalent homogeneous representation. Then, we characterize a set of stable policies A, each of which is associated with a MWC via a one-to-one mapping. Each stable policy is also consistent with the Gamson’s Law after the normalization of the voting weight distribution. Moreover, each party gets the same positive share of the surplus from any stable policy which is associated with a MWC containing itself. In the MPE, once the status quo policy is in the set A, it can never be defeated by any new proposal, that is, the status quo policy and the corresponding MWC will persist forever. If, in any period, the status quo policy is not in A, the randomly selected proposing party will propose to form a MWC containing itself (with equal-probability randomization when this party belongs to multiple MWCs) to implement the associated stable policy in the set A. The proposal will win the majority voting against the status quo policy. In short, on the equilibrium path, suppose that the initial status quo is inconsistent with the Gamson’s Law, it takes one step to move to a new policy that is consistent; the new policy and the MWC will then persist forever. Therefore, our equilibrium analysis indeed provides a strategic foundation for the Gamson’s Law in a dynamic setting and this objective is fully achieved. The fourth objective is to gain insights into how legislative institutions shape collective choices. As our model admits a large set of equilibria including the ones that have drastically different properties, we design a laboratory experiment to investigate whether our equilibrium will arise naturally in reality. Through such an experiment, we can also investigate how various details of the institution affect participating parties’ behavior, hence to shape collective decisions in the legislative process. The experiment has been carefully designed and is set to be conducted at HKUST in September 2019. We expect to complete the experimental analysis in October 2019. Therefore, right now this objective is only partially (70%) achieved.

14611415.label: Major findings and research outcome
14611415.value: In this project, we develop a dynamic legislative bargaining model with general voting weight distribution, in which the default policy evolves endogenously. We characterize a stationary Markov perfect equilibrium that satisfies several appealing properties. First, the equilibrium leads to the outcome in which the implemented policies are stable over time and winning coalitions are persistent. Second, it satisfies the size principle, according to which only parties of a minimal winning coalition receive positive shares. Third, the equilibrium outcome is consistent with the Gamson’s Law, according to which each party in a wining coalition receives a share proportional to its effective voting weight. As our model admits a large set of equilibria including the ones that have drastically different properties, we decided to conduct a laboratory experiment to investigate whether our equilibrium arises naturally in reality. We invited Professor Wooyoung Lim from HKUST, an expert in experimental economics, to join us on this project. We have carefully designed the experiment, but due to logistic reasons, we were not able to carry out the experiment in April 2019 as originally planned. It is now set to be conducted in September 2019. We expect that we will complete the experimental analysis in October and our paper, Gamson’s Law in Dynamic Legislative Bargaining, should be ready for submission by the end of 2019. While working on the proofs of this project, we gained some new ideas on how to tackle the difficult technical issues in a suspended project on a bargaining model in which players compete for the right to propose. Based on these new ideas, we revived this project. More specifically, we study a bargaining model where players exert costly effort to compete for the right to propose in every period before an agreement is reached. We establish the existence of a stationary subgame perfect equilibrium and characterize the set of all equilibrium payoffs in a general setup. Despite complete information, there exist multiple equilibria, including many with delayed agreements. Additional welfare loss is significant due to competition to gain the first-mover advantage in bargaining. We demonstrate that players’ effort increases as the competition becomes fiercer, up to the point of all expected gain from winning the proposing right. The new working paper (joint with Harold Houba), Characterizing the Extreme Equilibria in Bilateral Bargaining with Endogenous Protocols, is now almost ready for submission.

14611415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14611415.value: The dynamic legislative bargaining model that we develop in this project admits a large set of Markov perfect equilibria (MPEs). We have focused on the MPE that satisfies the size principle and the Gamson’s Law; however, it is desirable in future research to explore the possibility of delivering a sharper theoretical prediction, and hopefully, to single out a unique MPE. We may proceed in two directions. First, we will try to develop a possible equilibrium refinement based on the strategic complexity. Our conjecture along this direction is that the MPE that we characterize in the project is actually the only MPE that can satisfy such a refinement criterion. Second, we will continue to study the modified model with endogenously determined proposers. In many real-life situations, players do compete for the right to propose; hence a model with endogenously determined propose is more realistic, and more importantly, it may lead to a different set of equilibrium outcomes. We hope that such a model can deliver a sharper prediction.

14611415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14611415.value: In a modern democratic society, conflicts of interest are often resolved through some collective decision-making process such as committee voting or dynamic legislative bargaining. In a typical situation, each party controls a certain fraction of votes. In case that a coalition is formed by multiple parties who jointly control more than the majority of votes, a policy that they agree on is implemented. The legislative process then continues and a new winning coalition may form and pass new policy to replace the status quo. We model such legislative process into a dynamic game and characterize an equilibrium, which has the appealing features of stable policies and persistent winning coalitions. Our equilibrium satisfies the size principle, that is, only parties of a minimal winning coalition receive positive shares. Moreover, the equilibrium outcome is consistent with the Gamson’s Law. More specifically, in a baseline model with symmetric voting weight, parties in a persistent minimal wining coalition share the surplus equally; in a model with general voting weight distribution, each party in the wining coalition receives a share proportional to its effective voting weight. We further conduct a laboratory experiment to investigate whether our equilibrium will arise naturally in reality.

14611615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14611615.value: We perceive and comprehend the world by integrating information from multiple sensory modalities. Language, with which we communicate to each other, is conveyed primarily by audition (speech) and vision (articulation/writing/signing). When conflicting information is borne in different modalities, it becomes necessary to orient and maintain attention to relevant information, and to inhibit responses to irrelevant information. As we age, some cognitive abilities decline, e.g., working memory, while others are typically preserved, e.g., semantic memory. However, for individuals who age pathologically, the rates of decline in certain abilities can be substantially greater. Dementia is a set of neuro-degenerative conditions experienced by about 5-7% of people aged 60+. Individuals affected by the most common form of dementia, Alzheimer’s disease, have reduced ability to integrate sensory information from multiple sources, and are less able to inhibit automatic responses to incongruent information. Their linguistic function is also impaired, e.g., semantic memory and lexical access. In this project, we will assess multi-sensory integration and its relationship to linguistic function in the elderly, contrasting the behavioural and electroencephalogram (EEG) responses elicited by a battery of psychological tasks that are characteristic of three cohorts of Cantonese-speaking subjects:- patients with dementia, healthy elderly controls, and healthy young controls. Four tasks will be used—a McGurk task, a Stroop task, a Flanker task, and an auditory attention task—each requiring the participant to integrate sensory and linguistic information across the auditory and visual modalities. The EEG data will be analysed using three complementary methods that have been used previously to discriminate experimental subjects according to age-group and cognitive condition: (1) event-related potentials, i.e., evoked EEG responses to particular stimuli/events; (2) time-frequency analysis, i.e., temporal changes in the EEG oscillations; & (3) microstate analysis, i.e., recurrent, quasi-stable spatial patterns in the EEG time series. For each task, behavioural and EEG indices will be sought that discriminate the three cohorts. Indices that are characteristic of normal ageing will be determined by comparing the data elicited from elderly and young controls, while indices that are characteristic of pathological ageing will be determined by comparing the data elicited from dementia patients and elderly controls. We will also determine the extent to which these indices are correlated across tasks. Collectively, these results will enable us to better understand and contrast the trajectories of multi-sensory integration in normal and pathological ageing. The indices determined here will find potential future clinical application as biomarkers for assessment of dementia. 我們藉著統合多重感官的資訊來感知和理解世界。而語言作為人們溝通的媒介，則是以聽覺（言語）與視覺（文字）傳遞。當不同感官的資訊出現衝突，我們便要對其中重要的資訊集中注意及作出判斷，同時亦需要抑制無關的訊息。隨著年齡增長，一些認知能力會出現明顯衰退（如短期工作記憶），但有些認知能力卻較能有效維持（如語意記憶）。而認知功能出現病態退化的病者，某些認知能力的衰退更是顯著。老年認知障礙症患者會受到各種神經退化症狀的影響，在六十歲以上老年人中，患有老年認知障礙症的約佔五到七個百分比。老年認知障礙症中最普遍的是阿茲海默氏症，病症使患者統合各種感官資訊的能力下降，患者在感官資訊出現衝突時對無關訊息的自主抑制能力亦受到影響。除此之外，患者語言功能亦會受損，當中包括語義記憶和詞彙提取等等。 在本次研究項目中，我們會對長者的多感官統合能力作出評估及探討其與語言功能的關係．研究將會從一系列的心理行為測試中比較受驗者的行為及腦電波反應。本次研究將包括三組粵語受驗者：老年認知障礙症患者組別，認知健全的長者對照組別及認知健全的青年對照組別。實驗將包括四部份：麥格克作業（McGurk Task），史楚普作業（Stroop Task），旁側抑制作業（Flanker Task）及聽覺專注力作業。這些實驗各自都須要受驗者統合感官視覺與聽覺資訊，並作出語言判斷。實驗中所收集的腦電波訊號將從三種方式作出分析，而各種分析亦曾於研究中用於分辨不同年齡及認知狀況的受驗者。三種分析分別為： 1. 事件相關電位分析 － 跟據誘發腦電反應的事件作出分析。 2. 時頻分析 － 腦電頻率隨時間的變化。 3. 微狀態分析 － 隨時間反複出現和類穩定腦電區域分佈。 在每個的實驗部分，我們會跟據行為及腦電波分析尋找能究分辨三個實驗組別的指標：正常老化的指標可由比較認知健全的長者對照組別及認知健全的青年對照組別比較得出；認知功能病態退化的指標則可由比較老年認知障礙症組別及認知健全的長者對照組別得出。我們亦會檢視這些指標在不同實驗部分的關聯性。總合這些實驗的結果，我們將更能了解正常老化與病態認知功能退化者在多感官統合能力上的差別和變化。實驗所得出的結果在未來亦有望能在臨床應用上作為評估老年認知障礙症的生理標記。

14611615.label: Realisation of objectives
14611615.value: The first four objectives of the present study (Objectives 1-4) have been largely achieved. Three cohorts of subjects were recruited: (1) elderly individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), the prodromal stage of dementia, (2) cognitively normal elderly adult controls (EC); and (3) cognitively normal younger adult controls (YC). Following the original proposal, elderly subjects were initially recruited from Prince of Wales Hospital. Those who scored lower than or equal to the sixteenth percentile in the Hong Kong version of Montreal Cognitive Assessment (HK-MoCA) were classified as MCI. However, after several rounds of subject recruitment, only 9 MCI and 23 EC subjects were successfully recruited. Attempts were thus made to recruit potential subjects via Institute for Active Ageing, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, from which 6 MCI and 30 EC subjects were additionally admitted into the study, giving a total of 15 MCI and 53 EC. YC subjects were also recruited to serve as the control group. Behavioural and electroencephalogram (EEG) responses were elicited from these subjects in selected multi-sensory tasks, Stroop, Flanker, and auditory attention tasks (Objective 1). Analysis of variance (ANOVA) was run to examine whether the EEG indices associated with each task carried distinctive information (Objective 2). For example, for the flanker task, the hypothesized biomarker of cognitive decline (N2 magnitude) was found to be larger (i.e., more negative) in the audio-visual flanker task than in the corresponding uni-sensory task (visual flanker task), confirming that the demand for conflict monitoring was enhanced in the multi-sensory task. Despite the increased demand in multi-sensory scenarios, compared with YC subjects, the N2 amplitude was significantly less negative in EC and MCI, with a trend for MCI to be even less negative than EC. In contrast, the P3 amplitude was significantly larger (i.e., more positive) in both EC and MCI. Such general increase in P3 amplitude in elderly adults likely reflected the operation of certain controlled attention mechanisms to compensate for the declining automatic conflict monitoring function, as reflected by the less negative-going N2 amplitude. In addition to N2 and P3 magnitude, MCI was found to have less negative N100 amplitude than both YC and EC. Apart from the ANOVA results, in alignment with Objectives 3 and 4, correlation analyses were run to shed light on the extent to which these EEG indices were associated with the behavioural performance in each task and the behavioural functions that such EEG indices may underlie, including language ability (semantic memory / lexical access) and experience (e.g., second language exposure). Specifically, behavioural indices of inhibition obtained based on the Stroop task were highly associated with both semantic memory and lexical access, operationalized as the performance in semantic fluency and picture naming. The inter-relationship between inhibition and language ability even extended to second language use, with elderly adults with higher proficiency in second language showing better inhibition ability. While these results are in agreement with the growing literature that domain-general mechanisms (including conflict monitoring) may contribute to language ability, EEG results suggest a somewhat more complex picture. Specifically, as expected, N2 amplitude, which has been hypothesized to reflect more domain-general form of inhibition (e.g., response inhibition), was significantly correlated with inhibition ability; however, it was not associated with either language ability. Instead, only the P2 amplitude, often considered as an index for the lexical competition process in the domain of visual word recognition, was found to be significantly associated with both inhibition and language ability across all the subjects in the two elderly cohorts. Taken together, our results suggest that the cognitive processes underlying P2 amplitude may play a role in both lexical and domain-general inhibition, while N2 amplitude was primarily related to domain-general inhibition in elderly adults. Regarding Objective 5 to evaluate the potential use of EEG indices as biomarkers of dementia (specifically mild cognitive impairment), due to limited number of MCI subjects in the present study, classification analyses on the cohort membership (EC or MCI) could not be meaningfully performed. Instead, attempts were made to examine the potential of resting-state EEG spectral characteristics, commonly referred to as quantitative EEG in the clinical literature, by combining the resting-state data obtained in the present project with those collected in our team’s previous studies to yield a dataset comprising 28 MCI and 57 EC subjects. Towards establishing the utility of resting-state biomarkers for detecting early stages of dementia, reliability analyses demonstrated that some of the resting-state measures (e.g., alpha-block measures) achieved good test-retest consistency in elderly adults (> .90), speaking to the promise EEG biomarkers. In addition, classification analyses on eyes-open resting-state spectral power based on linear discriminant showed that significantly above-chance classification of group membership could be obtained based on a combination of theta-, alpha-, and beta band power features (AUC = .76; sensitivity = .68; specificity = .68). This result suggested that the resting-state spectral power is sensitive to MCI vs. EC distinction; with a larger sample size, it is likely that improvement over the current classification performance could be obtained. In summary, through the present project, we obtained further evidence that several components in our EEG, including the N100, P2, N2, and P3 event-related potentials (ERP), as well as resting-state band powers, were sensitive to effects of cognitive ageing. Through an individual-differences perspective, we showed that P2 amplitude was the most significant predictor of language ability in elderly adults. Also, both P2 amplitude and N2 amplitude were significant predictor of inhibition ability. However, our classification analysis on the potential clinical utility of the EEG biomarkers was limited by the small cohort sizes, especially with respect to MCI. Hence, further research remains required to fully determine the extent to which the EEG biomarkers of cognitive functions, such as N100, P2 and N2 amplitudes, are useful for identifying the early stage of dementia (i.e., MCI).

14611615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14611615.value: Major findings 1: The present study contributed to the cognitive ageing literature by providing further evidence about the relationship between inhibition mechanisms and language ability. We showed that the behavioural indices of inhibition, often measured using Stroop task, was highly associated with language performances in semantic fluency (Fong et al., under review; paper submitted to Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology), verbal list learning (Fong et al., under review; paper submitted to Aging, Neuropsychology, and Cognition), or even in second language (Hui, Yuan, Fong, & Wang, under review; paper submitted to International Journal of Bilingualism). In addition, we showed that N2 magnitude, as a neural correlate of conflict monitoring and inhibition ability, would be enhanced by multi-sensory conflicts (Fong et al., 2018). Individual-differences analysis in the elderly suggests that P2 magnitude is associated with both lexical competition (reflected in semantic fluency) and domain-general inhibition mechanisms (Stroop congruency effect), while N2 magnitude is associated primarily with domain-general inhibition mechanisms (Fong et al., under preparation). Major findings 2: This project also aimed to identify the EEG biomarkers for mild cognitive impairment (MCI), a prodromal stage of dementia. By analysing the EEG data collected from elderly adults with MCI, as well as from cognitively normal elderly and younger controls, we found that various event-related potential (ERP) components, including N100, P2, N2, and P3, are sensitive biomarkers of normal ageing. Apart from the findings above, we found that spectral characteristics of resting-state EEG activities often achieved high reliability in cognitively normal controls, speaking to the promise of potentially applying these features in clinical works (Ma, Lee, Fong, Hui, and Wang, 2019; Ma et al., under preparation). The project team has also developed a blind source separation (BSS) algorithm for the purpose of extracting potential EEG biomarkers of cognitive decline, particularly to interpret the time series of EEG signals as a sequence of microstates. This algorithm, which was based on a weak exclusion principle (Ma, Blu, and Wang, 2016; Ma, Blu, and Wang, 2017), compared favourably with other BSS algorithms, and the results have been presented in two conferences (38th International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society, EMBC’16; and The 14th IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging: From Nano to Macro, ISBI’17). Overall, this project contributed to the publication of one book chapter, three journal articles, and several conference papers and abstracts. In addition, four articles are currently under review/preparation.

14611615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14611615.value: The present study shows that several behavioural and ERP indices (e.g., P2 and N2 magnitudes) obtained during conflict processing tasks are related to cognitive ageing and/or language performance. Reliability analysis conducted for a subset of subjects demonstrated that some of these ERP indices have comparable reliability with their behavioural counterparts, many of which such as Stroop inhibition measure were widely used clinically. This speaks to the promise of the clinical value of the ERP indices identified. We envisage to extend the present research by (1) running a longitudinal study to establish the causal relationship between changes in language/inhibition functions and the modulations in P2 and N2 magnitudes; (2) furthering the data collection in order to provide normative data for potential use in clinical diagnosis.

14611615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14611615.value: With the growth in the ageing population worldwide, it is desirable to develop cost-effective and non-invasive technology for accurately detecting mild cognitive impairment (MCI), an early stage of various forms of dementia (e.g., Alzheimer’s disease). Electroencephalography (EEG), popularly referred to as brain waves, is a promising candidate that might have been underutilized. In the present project, we designed three EEG-based tasks on multisensory integration/inhibition and two behavioural tests of language functions, all of which were catered for the local Hong Kong population. The value of the present research is two-fold. First, we showed that the ability to inhibit irrelevant information was highly associated with language performances of elderly adults in semantic fluency, picture naming, verbal list learning, or even in second language. Second, we found that inhibition ability, as reflected by P2 and N2 magnitudes, were sensitive markers of cognitive decline and/or language ability. Taken together, our findings suggest that language functions are significantly determined by inhibition, which in turn is potentially a sensitive biomarker for cognitive decline. The significance of this research is that it lays the foundation for a full-fledged clinical trial for establishing the clinical validity of the EEG biomarkers identified.

14612415.value: Project objectives: 1. Assess how clinical pathways are implemented in physicians’ practice in China’s public hospitals 2. Examine physicians’ attitude toward and use of clinical pathways 3. Investigate factors contributing to physicians’ attitude toward and use of clinical pathways All project objectives have been achieved. To achieve the project objectives, I proposed to carry out a survey of 1,200 physicians in secondary and tertiary hospitals in four large cities in China. At the beginning of the project period, I encountered difficulties in terms of data collection, since the collaborators I intended to work with were unable to implement the survey for a variety of reasons. I was then able to find other collaborators in the field of hospital management and carried out the survey according to the plan in 2018 and early 2019. I surveyed 1,258 physicians in 16 tertiary and 8 secondary hospitals in Beijing, Wuhan, Shanghai and Fuzhou. I also gathered information on the hospitals and clinical departments in which the physicians worked from public sources, such as the size and ranking of the hospitals and whether the departments were treated as key departments in the hospitals. The department- and hospital-level information was merged with the physician-level data. In the areas of medical sociology and health services research, studies on physicians and public hospitals in China typically utilized data from a small number of physicians in a few hospitals. The dataset generated from this project, covering a large number of physicians in many hospitals in geographically diverse cities in China, is rare and very valuable. It promises to produce findings of both empirical and theoretical significance. Three papers have been developed based on the data collected for this project. The first paper explores issues related to all three objectives, albeit with preliminary data. It was based on a pilot survey of physicians in three hospitals and the qualitative data gathered for this project for the purpose of improving the questionnaire. The paper was accepted and published in the September 2017 issue of the journal Sociology of Development. In the mock RAE exercise recently carried out by the Social Science Faculty at the CUHK, the paper was given a very positive review and rated 4 stars (world leading). The second paper addresses the first objective, using data from the physician survey carried out in this project. It examines the implementation of clinical pathways, including the involvement of physicians in the implementation process and the monitoring procedures and incentives. The paper uses the method of cluster analysis to classify the implementation practices and discerns three patterns of implementation practice. It also assesses physician and hospital characteristics that are connected to physicians’ experience of the implementation of clinical pathways. The manuscript is under preparation and I plan to submit the paper to a journal within next two months. Parts of the analysis in the paper were presented in a key note speech on the medical profession in China given at workshop on professions and professionalism in China organized by Nanjing University. The third paper uses data from the physician survey to address the second and third objectives, i.e. physicians’ attitude towards clinical pathways and factors influencing their attitude. It uses the method of latent class analysis to categorize physicians according to their positive and negative ratings of different dimensions of clinical pathways; the analysis again discerns three types of reaction of physicians toward clinical pathways. The paper also develops a theoretical model of predictors of physician attitude and examines the predictors. The manuscript is also under preparation. The findings were presented at the annual meeting of the Hong Kong Sociological Association held in Dec. 2019. The paper was also accepted for presentation at the annual meeting of American Sociological Association, originally scheduled to take place in August this year in San Francisco. But the conference had to be canceled because of the COVID-19 pandemic. Finally, a PhD student of the PI is using the data from the physician survey data to supplement information from qualitative interviews and examine the relationship between physicians and hospitals in China in one of the chapters in her thesis.

14612415.label: Major findings and research outcome
14612415.value: The findings from this project can be grouped into three clusters. First, with regard to the implementation of clinical pathways (CPs), I find that physicians fell into three groups according to their involvement in the implementation process, the largest of which were active participants. The next largest group consisted of indifferent physicians, who stayed away from the implementation process. Finally, a substantial minority wanted to get involved but were left out. Hospitals/ departments used a variety of indicators to monitor pathway usage. But for the majority of the physicians, these indicators were not linked with incentives or sanctions such as income. Taken together, these findings suggest that because of their involvement in pathway implementation and the lack of incentives and sanctions, CPs may not have affected physicians’ discretion in clinical work to a large extent. Second, with regard to physicians’ attitude toward CPs, theories of professions argue that standardization has paradoxical implications for the status of a profession: it adds an aura of science but also threatens to make the practice of the profession more routine and transparent. Consistent with the theoretical prediction, I find that a large group of physicians held ambiguous attitude, agreeing that clinical pathways have both positive and negative effects. But there was also an equally sizable group who regarded CPs as nuisances only, with little other positive or negative impact. Finally, about a quarter of the physicians embraced CPs and saw mostly positive impact. Third, survey findings reveal that physicians’ attitude of CPs was shaped more by organizational factors, such as how the pathways were implemented, than by physicians’ professional orientation or concerns over the status of the profession. The findings suggest that professionals cannot be reduced to their professions and highlight the importance of examining the relationship between physicians and the organizations in which they work. The research outcome of this project includes at least three academic papers, one of which has been published in a reputable journal. Two other papers are under preparation and will be submitted to SSCI journals. I have also presented the findings at international and regional conferences and workshops. Currently, one PhD student is use the survey data in her dissertation. Please refer to Part C for details. Finally, this project also generates a large dataset of physicians practicing in diverse settings, which can be used to address questions going beyond this project.

14612415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14612415.value: The findings from this project highlight the importance of examining the relationship between physicians and the organizations in which they work. I argue that there needs to be a strong focus on the organization in the study of professions. Such research is particularly scarce in China and would be a fertile area of investigation for future studies. Moreover, this project also shows that investigating the actual process of implementation of new initiatives in the ongoing health care reforms provides excellent opportunities to assess professional work and autonomy in organizational contexts. These understandings have already directed me to initiate a project, in collaboration with a PhD student, that examines the implementation of the policy that allows physicians to practice in more than one organization. The project interviewed physicians and administrators in public hospitals and private medical groups to assess the attitude toward and arrangements of multi-site practices. It has shed light on the relationship between physicians and the organizations in which they work. The PhD student is working on her doctoral thesis based on the output from this project. In the future, I will continue to study the relationship between physicians and hospitals in the context of health care reforms.

14612415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14612415.value: China’s public hospitals have been plagued by the problems of rapidly rising costs and sub-optimal quality of care. A key component of the public hospital reform, initiated in early 2011, was to introduce tools to make clinical practice more rational and scientific. The focus has been on clinical pathways, which offer step-by-step guidance on treatments of specific diseases, and the measurement of physician performance according to the specification of the pathways. This project asks three questions: 1) How were clinical pathways implemented in physicians’ practice? 2) What are physicians’ attitude towards and use of the pathways? And 3) what are the determinants of physicians’ attitude and behavior? This project conducted a survey of 1,258 physicians in 24 secondary and tertiary public hospitals in four geographically diverse cities. This project makes both theoretical and empirical contributions. Empirically, this project provides a very timely description of a critical reform measure and physicians’ attitude toward it in China’s public hospitals, about which very little is known. Theoretically, studying the implementations of clinical pathways provides a lens through which issues pertaining to physician autonomy, such as physicians’ relationship with the state, organizations in which they work and patients, can be examined.

14612515.label: Project Objectives
14612515.value: To provide a holistic understanding of Hong Kong's Renjian Huahui through the compilation of a book that includes academic articles, a chronicle of artistic activities, a title list of newspaper articles written by its members, selected documents of the Society, biographies of its artists and related figures, etc. To review the existing narratives of the history of Hong Kong art by complementing the "known" (i.e. the Lingnan School as well as other traditional Chinese and oil painters) with the previously "unknown" (i.e. left-wing artists) through the production of journal papers.

To review the existing narratives of the history of Hong Kong art by complementing the "known" (i.e. the Lingnan School as well as other traditional Chinese and oil painters) with the previously "unknown" (i.e. left-wing artists) through the production of journal papers.

14612515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14612515.value: This project proposes a two-year research to examine left-wing artists and their artistic activities in Hong Kong in the 1930s and 1940s with special reference to the role of Hong Kong in the history of modern Chinese art through the case of Renjian Huahui (The Renjian Art Society, 人間畫會), a left-wing art society which began to germinate in the late 1930s and played an active role in conducting anti-war propaganda in Hong Kong in the 1940s. While no one will argue that the history of Hong Kong art is in need of an overall review, few are aware of the city’s significant role in and profound impact on the development of modern Chinese art as a hub for left-wing artistic propaganda in the 1930s and 1940s. Indeed, the cultural links between Hong Kong and the Mainland has never be severed in the history of Hong Kong art and the decades to be investigated saw extremely active artistic interactions between the two places. At that time, a large number of Mainland artists moved to Hong Kong due to warfare and brought with them their artistic ideas and practices. The left-wing artists among them had great ambition to take advantage of Hong Kong’s location and political conditions to conduct anti-war campaigns through art. As the largest left-wing art society in Hong Kong, Renjian Huahui, which was sympathetic with the Chinese Communist Party, brought together many of the immigrant artists, including printmakers and cartoonists. They held a large number of exhibitions and published their art works in local newspapers almost every day in the latter half of 1940s to promote their artistic and political ideas. It was these artists and their activities that made Hong Kong one of China’s art centres. Yet, there is a serious lack of scholarly attention in the area. This research will study in depth the artistic and political ideals and practices of Renjian Huahui, the complex inter-relationships among its members, their evaluation of the art works of each other, their communication with the Chinese Communist Party, and their interaction with other contemporary artists in both the local and the Mainland art circles. It is expected that a careful investigation of these aspects will provide a clear picture of how Hong Kong contributed to the promotion of left-wing art in the early twentieth century. 此計劃以人間畫會為研究對象，探討20世紀30至40年代的香港左翼藝術家及其活動，從而審視現代中國藝術發展中一段與香港相關的歷史。 到目前為止，香港藝術史的研究並不完整，即如香港如何曾經成為左翼藝術宣傳的中心，如何因此影響現代中國藝術的發展，便一直受到忽視。事實上，香港與中國大陸的文化聯繫從未間斷，而在20世紀30至40年代，兩地的交流及互動更趨頻繁。當時大量藝術家因逃避戰火南下香江，為此彈丸之地注入了新的動力，其中不少左翼藝術家利用香港的地理與政治優勢，致力透過藝術創作，以達到反戰的目的。人間畫會便是其時規模最大的左翼藝術團體，該會南下的畫家，包括版畫家、漫畫家等，為數甚多。他們積極舉辦展覽，於40年代後半葉更幾乎每天於報章刊登作品，為推動其藝術與政治理念而努力。無可否認，此批左翼藝術家及其活動是現代中國藝術史的重要部分，但相關的學術研究卻嚴重不足，殊為可惜。 此計劃將深入探討人間畫會的藝術理念與創作實踐，其畫家的相互交流，與中國共產黨的聯繫，以及與香港及中國大陸藝壇的互動情況。透過此研究，期望可為20世紀前期左翼藝術在香港的發展，填補一段歷史空白。

14612515.label: Realisation of objectives
14612515.value: Objective 1 is the major target of the project, for the book to be compiled would provide a comprehensive understanding of Renjian Huahui, an art body composed of left-wing artists active in Hong Kong in 1946-1950. Since Renjian Huahui was short-lived in Hong Kong and thus did not attract much attention of art historians, it has therefore to a certain extent been ignored in the study of Hong Kong art history. The book under compilation is believed to be able to fill in the gap of the history of Hong Kong art and, particularly, enhance our understanding of the complex ecology of the art circles right after the end of World War II in Hong Kong. The book of Objective 1, tentatively entitled “Renjian Huahui: Hong Kong Left-wing Art Trend in 1946-1950 as Seen in Chinese Newspapers”, includes two main sections, namely, Essay Section and Literature Section. The Essay Section shows an article discussing in detail the formation, members, activities, political ideology, preference of artistic style, etc. of the Renjian Huahui as well as the situation of left-wing art associations in the late 1940s Hong Kong. The Literature Section, which is of more importance, is a compilation of the first-hand materials related to Renjian huahui found in newspapers, including signed declarations, lists of essays written and drawings & paintings produced by Renjian Huahui members, and chronology of activities such as exhibitions, publications, social events, etc. It also includes essays written by art critics on Renjian Huahui as well as memorial articles written by Renjian Huahui members during their late years. An introduction of individual members, a total of 55, is also provided in the form of brief biographies. In addition, an appendix of an interview record with Lu Juchuan, a member of Renjian Huahui, done in 2016 is also placed at the end of the book so as to provide an oral-history perspective for the understanding of Renjian Huahui. For the Essay Section, the article included is the first comprehensive analysis of the Renjian Huahui and should be able to shed light on the understanding of the development of left-wing art movement in Hong Kong short before 1949, and thus fill in the gap of Hong Kong art history and provide a new understanding of the complicated situation of how Hong Kong art and politics are related. An overall review of the writing of Hong Kong art, as enlightened by the research of Renjian Huahui, will be made and presented in the form of a prologue to be placed at the end of the book. This prologue will offer a critical perspective on how Hong Kong, as a British colony, has provided a space for the spreading of political ideology through art in the late 1940s and thus how the art of Hong Kong at that particular time is to be understood. As for the Literature Section, it serves as hitherto the most holistic record of the first-hand materials of the Renjian huahui’s people and activities in Hong Kong. During the compilation process, the research team has spent much time and made huge efforts to collect and collate the textual and visual materials scattered in Chinese newspapers, specifically Huashang bao (China Business News), Wah Kiu Yat Po, Sing Tao Daily, Ta Kung Bao, and Wen Wei Po. These materials include column articles, special essays, art commentaries, comics, drawings, Chinese paintings, oil paintings, Chinese calligraphic works, art inscriptions, wood carvings, etc. A database was thus formed, thus facilitating the classification and sorting out of the textual and visual materials that the book needs. By referring to this section, readers will be able to see a clear picture of how the Renjian Huahui functioned and its members pursued their artistic goals through different kinds of proactive measures. The under-achievements related to Objective 1 is that originally a second essay is to be written to discuss the relationship between artistic style and political propaganda of Renjhian Huahui. However, due to shortage of research materials, this essay has to be given up. In addition, for Objective 2, it is found that members of the Renjian Huahui did not really have much connection with other painters such as those from Lingnan and those who insisted to produce paintings in a traditional modes. Members of the Renjian Huahui seem to represent an art circle in which artists had specific mission of using art for serve for social and political functions. As such, no specific topic for discussion is identified, and thus the reveal of the narratives of the history of Hong Kong art will be discussed in the Prologue of the book mentioned above rather than in the form of journal papers. To fully realize the objectives, the Introduction and Prologue will be written up as soon as possible, and the Literature Section will be carefully reviewed so as to prepare for the publication of the book. In other words, after the completion of the Introduction and Prologue, which might take a few more months, the PI will try to apply for publication funds from the Hong Kong Art Development Council and contact a publication house, most probably in Guangzhou, for publication.

14612515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14612515.value: The book Renjian Huahui: Hong Kong Left-wing Art Trend in 1946-1950 as Seen in Chinese Newspapers is the major research outcome of this project. It includes not only a discussion of the formation and significance of the art group Renjian Huahui in Hong Kong during the 1940s, but also a compilation of the literary materials related to Renjian Huahui. In the past, left-wing artists and their activities in Hong Kong have been very much neglected in the writing of Hong Kong art history. Such a gap in Hong Kong art history was due to the fact that first-hand materials of Renjian Huahui were scattered in old Chinese newspapers and were yet to be collected and collated. As such, the research team has made painstaking efforts to dig out the textual and visual materials from newspapers and compiled them in order as the second section in the proposed book for readers’ easy access. By referring to this section, which includes a chronology of art activities, an index of column and special articles, important documents by Renjian Huahui founders, critical essays on Renjian Huahui, retrospective writings by Renjian Huahui members, and brief biographies of Renjian Huahui members, readers could, for the first time, get a clear picture of the different aspects of the art of Renjian Huahui. It is worth mentioning that this book will be the first publication that offers a holistic understanding of the left-wing art group and the easiest reference for the activities of its members. In addition, the essay “Renjian Huahui: An Examination of a Hong Kong Left-wing Art Group in the 1940s” included in the book is the first comprehensive discussion of the formation, members, structure and propaganda of Renjian Huahui. It also shed new light on how this art group reflects the new art movement of the time as well as how it used art as a means to pursue social advancement. The social and artistic network of the Renjian Huahui members is also examined, through which it is realized that the real picture of the Hong Kong art circles is more complicated than what art historians have expected.

14612515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14612515.value: Most members of the Renjian Huahui returned to the Mainland before 1949 when People’s Republic of China was formed, resulting in bringing this left-wing art group to its end in Hong Kong. As such, further studies would be possible with focus on the life, art, and activities of individual members in New China, though they are beyond the scope of Hong Kong art.

14612515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14612515.value: This research project is a study of Renjian Huahui, a left-wing art group active in Hong Kong during the 1940s. Since most scholars have not paid much attention to this art group, the writing of Hong Kong art has long been left with a gap, particularly with regard to the relationship between art and political ideology. By doing this project, a clearer picture of Hong Kong art during the ten years before the founding of New China in 1949 is worked out, leading to a new understanding of how the ideology of left-wing artists had once been brought into practice in Hong Kong. The major outcome of this project is a book, which is yet to be published, comprising of an academic paper and a compilation of the first-hand documentary records of Renjian Huahui. This book for the first time facilitates the access into the textual and visual materials directly related to Renjian Huahui, and also sheds new light, with its chronology of art activities, on the role played by newspapers in the promotion of left-wing art in Hong Kong.
