14617415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617415.value: 過去，大多數校園暴力研究，主要集中在探討西方國家校園暴力發生的危機因素。反觀三個以華人社會為主的國家或地區(臺灣、香港、大陸)，檢視校園暴力危機因素的實證研究相對鮮少。再者，過去檢視校園暴力危機因素的實證研究，大多數集中在探討學生與學生之間的校園暴力類型，鮮少的實證研究在探討教師與學生之間的暴力類型。此外，Benbenishty與Astor於2005年提出一個以解釋校園暴力的理論模型。此模型認為，學校因素應為學生心理因素、家庭背景因素、社區因素與校園暴力的中介變項。然而，卻鮮少實證研究檢驗此理論模型。至今，我們仍不清楚Benbenishty與Astor (2005)的理論模型，是否適用解釋上述三個華人社會中學生的校園暴力；我們也不清楚理論模型中，學校因素在上述三個華人社會的中介效果是否相異或相同。有些學者認為，因為上述三個華人社會存在著不同的政治、經濟和教育的制度，因此學校因素在這些華人社會的中介效果會有所不同。相反的，有些學者主張，這些華人社會的學校結構非常相似，因此學校因素在這些華人社會的中介效果應該也是相似的。至今，這個理論模型在華人社會的實證研究支持依然缺乏。因此，本研究目標在檢驗Benbenishty 與 Astor (2005)模型是否可以成功運用解釋臺灣、香港與大陸地區學生的校園暴力問題。本研究也將會檢視學校因素在三個華人社會之間的中介效果是否相似與相同。本研究計畫將在這三個華人社會的國民中學以及初級中學以隨機抽樣方式蒐集樣本，並以問卷方式詢問學生以及學生導師。本研究將以結構方程模型為最主要的分析方法。本研究期待能夠對於Benbenishty 與 Astor (2005)的理論模型提供在華人社會的實證研究支持。本研究也期待透過研究結果，提供上述華人社會中的社工人員、學校諮商者、心理學家、以及政策制訂者，對未來校園暴力處遇以及預防方案的參考。

14617415.label: Realisation of objectives
14617415.value: In order to achieve the objectives, we employed a longitudinal methodology drawing on multidimensional perspectives obtained through the use of quantitative surveys. Data was collected from junior high school students and their peers and homeroom teachers in Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Tianjin (Mainland China). A three-stage cluster random sampling was used in this study to obtain a cross-national random sample of junior high school students (Grades 7–9) from Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Tianjin (China). Each society studied comprises four administrative regions. In the first stage, two schools were randomly selected from each region in each society. In the second stage, one to two classes was randomly selected for each grade level (Grades 7, 8, and 9) in the selected schools. In the third stage, all of the students in the selected class were included in the student sample, and the homeroom teachers of each selected class were included in the teacher sample. We adopted multidimensional assessment methods to examine the 1,831 students and their 38 homeroom teachers for both two waves (one-year interval; retention rates for student sample and teacher sample are 70.91% and 52.78%, respectively). The primary method of analysis to be used in this project is Rasch analysis and latent-variable structural equations modeling (SEM) (Objective 1). A bootstrapping approach in SEM (n = 5000 bootstrap samples) was used to assess indirect or mediating effects (Objective 2). Cross-group comparative analyses using SEM were conducted in order to determine whether patterns of relationships and mediating effects were similar or different across three societies (Objective 2 & 3). All objectives have been realized. Further information is provided in Section 6.1: Major findings and research outcomes.

14617415.label: Major findings and research outcome
14617415.value: First, we followed Benbenishty and Astor's model and approach to examine the similarities and differences between three distinct Chinese societies (Taiwan, Hong Kong, and China) regarding the contribution of gender and grade level to school violence, the ranking orders of perpetration and victimization behavior, and the correlates of school nonattendance due to violence. The results of Rasch analyzes revealed that verbal violence is most frequent. Male students are most likely to be aggressive and victimized. Grade-level differences in school violence were shown to be weak or insignificant. School nonattendance is generally associated with being kicked, punched, socially excluded, blackmailed, threatened, or sexually kissed without consent. The results were similar across societies. The findings imply that the contextual differences between Chinese societies may not account for different effects of gender and grade level on school violence, behavioral patterns of school violence, and correlates of school nonattendance. Next, we examined how Benbenishty and Astor’s theoretical model applies to the context of school violence perpetration in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Mainland China, by examining the relationships among students’ negative psychological traits, family functioning, community victimization, school factors (engagement, affiliation with delinquent peers, and teacher-student relations), and school violence (by students against other students and teachers) in these societies. The results of the structural equation modeling analysis based on total sample provides a good fit to the data. Student violence against students is directly influenced by students’ negative personal traits and community victimization. The variable of affiliation with delinquent peers has stronger mediating effects than student–teacher relationships and engagement on student violence against students for negative personal traits and community victimization. By contrast, student violence against teachers is not strongly influenced by negative personal traits, family functioning, and community victimization. Instead, student violence against teachers is indirectly influenced by negative personal traits and community victimization through the strongest mediating variable of affiliation with delinquent peers. Student violence against teachers is also indirectly influenced by negative personal traits, family functions, and community victimization through the mediating variable of poor student–teacher relationships. Poor student–teacher relationship has a small but important mediating impact on student violence against teachers. Together, all of these variables accounted for around one half of the explained variance for student violence against students and around one third for student violence against teachers. The patterns of relationships and the mediating effects of school factors on school violence in the three societies are similar across societies.

14617415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14617415.value: The findings of this study indicated that mediating effects of school variables and patterns of relationships between variables in this model was similar across three diverse Chinese societies. How the findings are relevant to other parts of the world remain questionable. In 2018, PI of this project was invited to participate in an international research team (Children’s Worlds: International Survey of Children’s Well-being), as co-PI in Taiwan and a member in the international team, to further examine how similarities and differences in contribution of personal, family, school, and community factors to school violence across over 40 countries. Furthermore, our findings implied that the school is a unique developmental setting contributing to school violence. Future research should further examine how school characteristics and school contextual effects influence school violence. In 2019, PI of this project was invited to participate in a national-level research team in Taiwan (Taiwan Birth Cohort Study) to conduct research on the topic, using a nationally-representative longitudinal sample of more than 20,000 children in Taiwan. It is expected that the findings derived from this study and the two other projects PI participated could provide strong evidence to further develop international-based intervention and prevention on reducing school violence.

14617415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14617415.value: We examined how Benbenishty and Astor’s theoretical model applies to the context of school violence perpetration in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Mainland China (Tianjin), by examining the behavioral rankings orders as well as the relationships among students’ negative psychological traits, family functioning, community victimization, school factors (engagement, affiliation with delinquent peers, and teacher-student relations), and school violence (by students against other students and teachers) in these societies. Our findings indicated school factors play an important mediating roles in our model. Affiliation with delinquent peers is the most important mediator. The patterns of relationships and school mediating effects are similar across societies. Our findings imply that although prevalence of school violence vary across societies, the contribution of gender and grade level to school violence, the school mediating effects, and the patterns of relationships are similar across societies. These findings support Benbenishty and Astor’s theoretical model that school violence is influenced by a combination of within-school and external-school variables, and within-school variables can mediate the contributions from external contexts. In addition, these mediation findings provide empirical evidence supporting the idea that school environment is a unique and independent developmental setting that contributes directly and indirectly to school violence in high school context.

14617615.value: 視覺注意：被用於選擇的效應

14617615.label: Project Objectives
14617615.value: Exploring the Properties of a Detrimental BUS Effect I plan to systematically measure the properties of this detrimental BUS effect in several ways. First, I will measure the time course of the BUS effect. Second, I will attempt to separate the BUS effects of the different dimensions in order to ascertain whether the BUS effect is general to all dimensions or specific to one of them; this will be accomplished by trying the combinations of each of the two features in the pilot experiment (i.e., color and orientation) with a third feature (e.g., color and texture; orientation and texture). Third, I will try to relate the BUS effect to other important phenomena in the field of visual attention by studying the correlations between the individual differences of the BUS effects and various previous tasks. Distinguishing between the Impairment and Bias of the Feature Representations The BUS effect could potentially occur either because the underlying representation of the information is impaired when it is used for selection or because the underlying representation is biased toward the target feature. I will first try a same/different task which distinguishes between bias and impairment (bias: higher accuracy for the cued feature but a lower accuracy for the slightly different feature; impairment: generally lower accuracies for both cued and slightly different features). Second, I will measure a subjective report on the perceived feature. A bias toward the target feature will manifest as the shift of the mean of a distribution toward the cued feature. Impairment, on the other hand, will manifest as the increase in the standard deviation of a distribution. Generalizing the BUS Effect to the Whole Feature Space The pilot experiment used primary features as cues (e.g., red) and measured the BUS effect on features that are similar to the cues. This design should be generalized in two ways. First, the BUS effect could be different for non-primary features because, for example, only one channel is task relevant for a primary feature but an equal weighting of channels is optimal for a non-primary task. Second, it is potentially important to assess the BUS effect on target features that are dissimilar to the cue; for example, if the BUS effect reflects a bias in a broad range of color space, then following a red (or a green) cue, a yellow object will appear to be slightly reddish (or slightly greenish). Measuring the BUS Effect of Spatial Selection Location plays a unique role in attentional processing, and so we should measure the BUS effect of spatial selection. To achieve this, observers will select an object either by its x-coordinate or y-coordinate, and the exact location of the target could slightly deviate from the cued location on both the x and y dimensions; then, the BUS effect can be established if the discrimination on a dimension is comparatively worse when the selection is driven by the same dimension. On the other hand, we can make comparisons between the tangential and radial components of spatial selection. It would also be potentially interesting to measure these two components on both primary (e.g., vertical & horizontal) and non-primary directions.

14617615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617615.value: 在過去35年間，視覺注意是認知心理學和神經學中非常活躍的研究領域。描述視覺注意的功能的一個通常的概念框架是一扇門，這扇門只讓少量的早期視覺資訊到達意識的層次。這個描述自然的包含了兩個概念上獨立的限制：(a)對資訊的選擇，以及(b)被選擇資訊的通達。基於選擇/通達的區別，顯然同樣的視覺資訊能在視覺注意中扮演兩個不同的角色：(a)用於選擇的資訊，以及(b)被通達的資訊。一個後續問題是：當資訊被用於選擇時，這是否會影響該資訊在視覺中的表徵，然後在該資訊通達意識時顯現出來。為了評測這個“被用於選擇的效應”(簡稱BUS效應)，我測量了測試用於選擇的特徵的任務的績效與測試其他特徵的任務的績效之間的區別。預實驗顯示有一個顯著的負面的BUS效應。 在本申請中，我提出系統的發展這項發現（負面的BUS效應）。該項目有幾個重要的意義。首先，BUS效應的存在就是一個出人意料的發現。這是因為當前視覺注意的理論通常假設用於選擇的特徵並無特別之處。其次，BUS效應的存在為用於選擇的特徵和通達的特徵之間的區別，以及他們之間的交互影響提供了重要的經驗支持。第三，探索BUS效應的屬性能為視覺注意的基礎機制，特別是資訊怎樣被利用來選擇，提供線索。 測試BUS效應將涉及下列幾條線的研究：(1)探索負面BUS效應的屬性，包括它的時間過程，不同維度的BUS效應，以及用個體差異分析來研究BUS效應和以前現象的關係。(2) 在同異任務和主觀報告任務中區分特徵表示的“損害”和“偏向”這兩種可能的BUS效應的機制。(3) 通過嘗試非主要特徵以及與線索不類似的目標特徵將BUS效應推廣到整個特徵空間。(4) 通過比較x和y維度以及測量主要和非主要方向上的徑向和切向分量來測量BUS效應的空間選擇。

14617615.label: Realisation of objectives
14617615.value: The objective 1 was exploring the Properties of a Detrimental BUS Effect. I systematically measured the properties of this detrimental BUS effect in several ways. First, I measured the time course of the BUS effect. Second, I attempted to separate the BUS effects of the different dimensions to ascertain whether the BUS effect is general to all dimensions or specific to one of them. The results of these first and second experiments were repackaged and presented as part of the paper “Unit of Visual Working Memory: A Boolean Map Provides a Better Account Than an Object Does”. Third, I tried to relate the BUS effect to other important phenomena in the field of visual attention by studying the correlations between the individual differences of the BUS effects and various previous tasks. The results of this third experiment were messy and inconsistent across conditions, so no further action is taken. The objective 2 was distinguishing between the Impairment and Bias of the Feature Representations. The BUS effect could potentially occur either because the underlying representation of the information is impaired when it is used for selection or because the underlying representation is biased toward the target feature. I tried the same/different task which distinguishes between bias and impairment and also measured a subjective report on the perceived feature. A bias toward the target feature will manifest as the shift of the mean of distribution toward the cued feature. Impairment, on the other hand, will manifest as the increase in the standard deviation of a distribution. The results were repackaged and presented as part of the paper “Distinguishing target biases and strategic guesses in visual working memory”. The objective 3 was generalizing the BUS Effect to the Whole Feature Space. Here, the initial results were not particularly interesting. But I have made new development concerning feature space, used shape as the exemplar stimulus, and the results are very good. The results were repackaged and presented in the paper “Space of preattentive shape features”. The objective 4 was measuring the BUS Effect of Spatial Selection. Location plays a unique role in attentional processing, and so we should measure the BUS effect of spatial selection. The results turn out to be quite messy and inconsistent across different categories of stimulus items. So no further action is taken.

14617615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14617615.value: Taken together, the planned experiments were completed and some interesting findings have been made. The BUS effect is fairly general but not in all cases. The effect seems mainly to reflect strategic guesses rather than target biases. Although not the focus of the initial research plan, what seems most interesting is the extension to the feature space. The results are published in these following papers. Huang, L. (2020). Space of preattentive shape features. Journal of Vision, 20(4), 10. Huang, L. (2020). Unit of visual working memory: a Boolean map provides a better account than an object does. Journal of Experimental Psychology-General, 149, 1–30. Huang, L. (2019). Distinguishing target biases and strategic guesses in visual working memory. Attention, Perception, & Psychophysics, https://doi.org/10.3758/s13414-019-01913-2.

14617615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14617615.value: The studies on the BUS effect have been completed. However, the studies on feature space may worth further development in future studies.

14617615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14617615.value: Visual features are building blocks of visual processing. When we use a feature in the selection, it has complex effects in the way how they are perceived and used in processing. The present project systematically explored this BUS (being used in selection) effect. Some interesting findings have been made, including the separation of bias and guess, the implication on the unit of processing, as well as the implications on feature space.

14617915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14617915.value: Studies of overseas Chinese and their ancestral hometown have often emphasized on the discontinuation and rebuilding of economic ties through remittance and investment, and social ties through as lineage building and philanthropic contributions. These studies also lead to the discussion of “Chineseness” which stresses the enhancement of cultural identity through practice and performance of claimed traditional Chinese culture. This proposal, with a focus on the communal Hungry ghost festivals organized in three Fujian-Teochew speaking overseas Chinese communities, puts such studies a step further with a hypothesis that traditional Chinese culture, particularly continuously celebrating Chinese communal festivals, are not only serve as a tool for establishing Chinese identity and instrumental to re-establishing connection with their ancestral hometown, they are, more importantly, a cultural façade that the overseas Chinese employ to indigenize, to project themselves as a significant “other” in their adopted country. “Chinese culture” is a survival strategy testing the tolerance of local authorities and, with standardized ritual, mitigates internal differences among the overseas Chinese. The twentieth century was a period when the status of the Chinese overseas changed from sojourners to settlers. It was a period when the overseas Chinese delinked with their ancestral hometown, settled in their host countries, and reconnected with China in the last quarter of the century. The Chinese Hungry ghost festivals serves as a very good example to examine the continuation of Chinese communal festivals as a global phenomenon, exploring, in particular, the interplay of ceremonial structures evolving in overseas Chinese settings and their ancestral hometown. From spiritual salvation, communal charity to intangible cultural heritage, the Hungry festivals studied in this proposed project witness the dynamism and adaptability of traditional Chinese cultural practices. The project proposes to compare the Hungry Ghost Festivals organized by the Fujian-Teochew communities in Hong Kong, Singapore and Kobe, all have records dated back to the late 19th century. It will produce, in addition to individual investigator’s publications, audio-visual databases and three ethnographies each documenting festival details and historical records of the festivals in Hong Kong, Kobe and Singapore. It will also produce a volume comparing the Hungry festivals celebrated by the overseas Chinese and how it helps understanding “cultural China” in the 20th century. It also proposes to bring students to the field, hoping to expose them to festivals in real time, not limited to just sights and sounds as described in books or other reference materials, but as interested participant observers.

14617915.label: Realisation of objectives
14617915.value: This project proposed to understand “cultural China” through the study salvation rituals, particularly the hungry ghost festivals celebrated by the Chinese in Hong Kong, Japan and Singapore. We proposed six objectives: (1) To examine problems of ritual standardization, cultural integration and transnational networking in the 20th century in emigrant communities and overseas Chinese settlements Through in-depth ethnographic studies, we confirmed our hypothesis that “… traditional Chinese culture, particularly continuously celebrating Chinese communal festivals, are not only serve as a tool for establishing Chinese identity and instrumental to reestablishing connection with their ancestral hometown, they are, more importantly, a cultural facade that the overseas Chinese employ to indigenize, to project themselves as a significant “other” in their adopted country. “Chinese culture” is a survival strategy testing the tolerance of local authorities and, with standardized ritual, mitigates internal differences among the overseas Chinese.” We further realized that religious communal festivals, particularly those related to spiritual worship and the deceased have faced many challenges throughout the 20th century in both China and among the Chinese living in overseas communities. These challenges, such as the anti-superstitious campaign since the late 19th century, the global economic crisis in the 1920s and 30s, and the Japanese occupation during the pacific war period provide community members grounds to justify their continuation, modification, reinterpretation or abandonment of the events. Global languages such as the “Intangible cultural heritage” promoted by UNESCO is a conceptual tool implemented by overseas Chinese to indigenized “Chinese culture”. (2) To investigate hungry ghost festivals organized by the Fujian-Teochew Chinese in Hong Kong, Kobe and Singapore We observed twenty-eight salvations rituals, including twenty celebrated in the seventh lunar month, organized in Hong Kong, Japan and Singapore during this research period. We realized that though “Hungry ghost festival” is a term generally used in English literatures to describe spiritual rituals organized in the lunar seventh month, however, comparative ethnographic studies revealed that different Chinese communities employ different names which encompass different ritual meanings and practices. In order to understand the similarities and differences, we organized a conference in 2017 in Osaka, Japan to compare the seventh month festivals celebrated in different East Asian communities. Outcome of this conference will be published in a journal special issue (in Chinese) and will later be published in Japanese. (3) To build a multi-media databank on the hungry ghost festivals for future comparative studies on Chinese communal festivals We have collected more than 2TB of multi-media files including photos, videos and digitized source materials. To established a databank available for public usage, we need institutional support. An initial attempt is the publication of a volume on “photographic ethnography” based on photos taken in the 1980. We are currently discussing with publisher(s) and cultural institutions concerning publications of photographic ethnographies and digitalization of and deposition of these multi-media resources. (4) To produce a monograph comparing hungry ghost festivals in overseas Chinese communities A journal special issue will be published in fall 2019. A Japanese version is now under preparation. (5) To produce three ethnographies detailing the hungry ghost festivals respectively in Hong Kong, Kobe and Singapore We have published four articles based on detailed participant observation. However, we realized that we should move a step forward to understand (1) history of the festival in each specific overseas community, (2) position of the hungry festival in the overseas Chinese cultural activities, and (3) changing meaning and interpretation of the targets of worship in different salvation rituals, particularly when the idea of “intangible cultural heritage” is becoming an unavoidable force for cultural interpretation. We have published one monograph and are now working on three monographs with these concerns in mind. (6) To produce individual papers and ethnographies relating to the subject We have published two monographs, seven articles (including three scheduled to be published in fall 2019), compiled one Journal special issue (expected to be published in fall 2019), and presented findings in eleven conferences.

14617915.label: Major findings and research outcome
14617915.value: We have published two monographs (8.5, 8.6), seven articles including three scheduled to be published in fall 2019 (8.1, 8.9, 8.10, 8.11, 8.12, 8.13, 8.14), edited one Journal special issue expected to be published in fall 2019 (8.7), and presented findings in eleven conferences (9.1-11). The investigators are preparing three book manuscripts respectively on Singapore (8.8), Hong Kong (8.16) and East Asian Chinese communities (8.15). These academic contributions can be divided into two categories: Comparative ethnographies (8.7, 8.14, 8.16, 9.7, 9.11): All contributions are based on detailed ethnographies. We compared different types of salvation rituals, including the hungry ghost festivals, celebrated in different communities. We pointed out that the local government policies as well as changes in the macro-environment determined how the festival was run. In Singapore, for instance, from the late 19th century to mid-20th century, Chinese community leaders avoided participating in religious festivals which were labelled as superstition but in the second half of the 20th century actively taking part in these festivals because of the need to acquire grassroots’ political support. The Singapore government’s policy of religious harmony and rapid urban development also affected the practice of festivals especially those related to the deceased. In Kobe, Japan, the changes of ritual practices were responds relating to immigration and naturalization policies as well as the notion of intangible cultural heritage. In Hong Kong, inscription of the hungry ghost festival as Chinese National Intangible Cultural Heritage played an important role unifying ritual practices of different dialect groups. Methodology and theory (8.5,8.7,8.8,8.15,9.6, 9.7) Besides comparing the hungry ghost festivals celebrated in different communities, we also emphasized on (1) comparing the hungry ghost festivals with other Chinese festivals in order to better understanding the position of the hungry ghost festivals and how “cultural China” is understood by the overseas Chinese, (2) cross-region and cross-nation comparison and cross-thematic comparison: particularly those related to major transnational crises which had significant impacts on the ways of living and the construction of identities among the Chinese population in East Asian communities. These comparisons will implement Arthur Wolf’s “God-Ghost-Ancestor” spectrum by arguing that the salvation rituals such as the hungry ghost festivals are introduced as a “ritual charity” by changing the unattended “wandering ghost” into collective “ancestors” attended by institutions instead of individual families. They also re-examined Okada Ken’s ritual area theory and B.E. Ward’s conscious model by redefining ritual boundaries.

14617915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14617915.value: In 2016 we organized a conference entitled “Coping with transnational crisis: Chinese economic and social lives in East Asian Ports-Cities, 1850-1950” Conference (跨國危機的對應：1850-1950年間東亞港口-城市華人的社會經濟生活) and in 2017 another conference entitled “Recapture “endangering” social life: source materials and ways of living of the East Asian Overseas Chinese during the Pacific War period” 重塑危難中的社會生活：太平洋戰爭時期東亞華僑華人生活方式的史料與研究. Salvation rituals and how a society remember and forget the deceased are themes discussed in these conferences. We are now working towards the publication of selected papers presented in these conferences. To understand how the overseas Chinese re-enact “cultural China”, it is essential to conduct in-depth historical ethnographies as well as comparing the meaning and practices of the rituals and how they are adopted and adjusted according to different times, places and social groups. The PI is working on two monographs in these directions.

14617915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14617915.value: This project applied historical and anthropological methodologies in the study of Chinese rituals and festivals. It studied how they are adjusted and adopted in different overseas Chinese communities. The investigators conducted in-depth ethnographical studies and library research in Hong Kong, Japan and Singapore. They produced two monographs, seven articles, edited one Journal special issue and presented findings in eleven conferences. Their research covered a period mainly from the late 19th century to the 21st century, and a geographic area from Northeast Asia to Southeast Asia. This project is a detailed multi-disciplinary study of traditional festivals celebrated by overseas Chinese. It argued that festivals are not only served as a tool for establishing Chinese identity and instrumental to re-establishing connection with their ancestral hometown, they are, more importantly, a cultural façade that the overseas Chinese employ to indigenize, to project themselves as a significant “other” in their adopted country. “Chinese culture” is a survival strategy and, with standardized ritual, mitigates internal differences among the overseas Chinese. The data collected by the investigators are invaluable and will benefit many scholars who are interested in the study of rituals and festivals in emigrant and overseas Chinese communities.

14618615.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14618615.value: 從圖紙及照片到數字再現：運用三維掃描進行四個蘇州園林的初步研究

14618615.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14618615.value: Prof Girot, Christophe Dr Gu, Kai

14618615.label: Project Objectives
14618615.value: Contribute to a better understanding of Chinese gardens in general and their spatial effects in particular. Test the limitations of 3-D laser scanning for the documentation of Chinese gardens by modeling selected precincts of Suzhou gardens.
rows: Contribute to a better understanding of Chinese gardens in general and their spatial effects in particular.
Test the limitations of 3-D laser scanning for the documentation of Chinese gardens by modeling selected precincts of Suzhou gardens.

14618615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14618615.value: Half a day’s journey from Shanghai, the gardens of Suzhou are among the most popular tourist sites in contemporary China. These gardens are intricate combinations of architectural, landscape and literary elements. Although ideas of Chinese painting are commonly taken to be related to these gardens, visiting gardens seems evidently different from looking at paintings. Chinese paintings are typically non-perspectival while the physicality of a garden engages a consistent sense of spatial depth that can be recorded by photography and Western-style scaled plans and sections. This research project investigates this gap between traditional spatial conception and contemporary experience. Can we refresh our understanding of Suzhou gardens by exploring non-perspectival aspects of them? Can Western techniques of imaging be employed to reverse assumptions of conventional three-dimensional space and, by doing so, re-invigorate the spatial analysis of Suzhou gardens? Using a new configuration of imaging techniques, this research project focuses on four World Heritage-listed gardens in Suzhou: the Garden of the Humble Administrator (Zhuo Zheng Yuan), the Lingering Garden (Liu Yuan), the Garden of the Master of the Nets (Wang Shi Yuan) and the Mountain Villa of Embracing Beauty (Huanxiu shanzhuang). Their range in size enables spatial effects to be studied in the largest as well as the smallest settings. A photographic study will document non-perspectival effects of these gardens. Specific precincts of these gardens will be examined in cut-out views generated from a digital model created by 3-D laser scanning in order to show how non-perspectival effects that prevent the expression of consistent spatial depth depend on specific alignments of irregular landform, plants, rockeries, and architectural elements. Finally, Chinese texts and historical photographs will be correlated with digital images to explore the provenance of non-perspectival effects. This will be the first study of Suzhou gardens that brings together photography, 3-D laser scanning and conventional architectural drawings for an analysis. By aligning Chinese garden studies with new developments in landscape visualization, this project offers new readings of famous cultural sites to invigorate landscape interpretation for visitors, and new material for comparative studies of gardens. 距離上海市約半天路程的蘇州園林是當代中國最受歡迎的旅遊地點之一，這些園林是集建築、景觀及文學元素的複雜綜合體。中國繪畫與園林的關係已有不少闡述，然而實地體驗與讀畫的體驗截然不同。國畫沒有線性透視法，而園林的空間深度卻可以用攝影和西方平面圖及剖面圖記錄。本研究計劃正以傳統空間認知和當代體驗之間的差別作為研究焦點。我們能否探索蘇州園林的非透視體驗，從而更新我們隊蘇州園林的認識呢？我們能否取消西方圖像工具對三維空間的各種前提后，採用它來激活對蘇州園林的空間分析呢？ 本研究計劃提出一個新的圖像運作，并以此研究蘇州世界遺產園林其中四個：拙政園、留園、網師園及環秀山莊。這些園林大小不一，方便我們研究各種空間效果。園林的非透視效果將主要由攝影記錄，之後針對某些特定景區的非透視效果則先以三維掃描製作的數字模型生成剖面圖，考究非規則地形、植物、假山及建築所形成的各種前後高低關係，從而揭示產生非透視效果的具體做法。最後，通過數字圖像與中文文獻和歷史照片的整合研究，說明非透視效果的歷史沿革。 本研究計劃是首個整合攝影、三維掃描及常規性建築圖的蘇州園林研究項目。它將把景觀視覺表現的新發展引進中國園林研究，向遊人提供對著名文化景點新的景觀詮釋，也為園林史的比較研究提供新的素材。

14618615.label: Realisation of objectives
14618615.value: 1. Photographic work Four fieldtrips were made to Suzhou gardens, during 1-5 July 2016 (self-funded), 28 Dec 2016 to 4 Jan 2017 (funded as part of a design studio's site visit), 25 June to 1 July 2017 (funded as fieldtrip of a summer elective), 28 Dec 2017 to 4 Jan 2018 (funded as part of a design studio's site visit). The trips allowed visits to the 4 gardens under study in this project. Visits were made in Summer and in Winter. These visits allowed me to study how aperspectival effects in the larger gardens involved different design techniques compared with the smaller gardens. However, photographic work on the Huanxiu shanzhuang was limited because the authorities had safety concerns and refused public access to the main rockery. (The roots of a tree had made the rockery structurally unsafe.) 2. 3-D scanning This part of the project has not been realized and the funds associated with this work are being returned to the UGC. In the initial application, Mr YANG Hui, a Deputy Director of the Suzhou Gardens Office, provided an in-principle agreement for accessing to the gardens for 3D scanning. Shortly after the GRF project was funded, Mr Yang resigned his position and could no longer be in charge of this matter. Suzhou gardens had not been closed to the public even for CCTV television crews, and the Suzhou administrators declined my request for access to undertake 3-D scanning. (See 2 plans mentioned in the mid-term progress report for the GRF project.) 3. Examining historical photographs and texts A digital archive of published historical photographs of Huanxiu shanzhuang and Wang Shi Yuan involves the collecting and scanning of images. This work is substantially complete. Student helpers were employed instead of an RA for collecting, scanning and sorting. 4. 14618615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14618615.value: Aperspectival effects in three gardens (Zhuo Zheng Yuan, Liu Yuan and Wang Shi Yuan) have been substantially established. The basic understanding developed in this project is that, while aperspectival effects in the larger gardens involved the near and the far as equivocal terms in a non-Cartesian spatiality, in the smaller gardens the main consideration appears to be about relative scaling and setting up surprises about the size and extent of the gardens. In particular, when crossing from one room to another, or one external area to another, the anticipated size of the next are seen through a wall opening or doorway might be larger or smaller than anticipated. In the larger gardens such as the Zhuo Zheng Yuan and Liu Yuan, bridges, embankments and covered walking galleries play important roles in sustaining aperspectival effects. In the smaller gardens such as the Wang Shi Yuan, wall openings, doorways, juxtaposed openings and longer sightlines connected interiors and external areas play important roles in sustaining aperspectival effects. Research Output I have written on 3 of the four gardens studied in this project. Two publications have been appeared so far: one refereed journal paper in Jianzhu xuebao, the top journal for architecture in China and one book chapter in a volume published by Princeton Architectural Press. In addition, a refereed journal paper on the Wang Shi Yuan is under review by the Journal of Chinese Architecture & Planning.

14618615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14618615.value: The expanded vocabulary for analysing Chinese gardens developed in this project might be useful for engaging the new work of emerging Chinese architects. In a public lecture presented at Harvard University in November 2018 (available on YouTube at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZjhM5sIhK8k), I outlined a line of research that would allow us to connect the study of aperspectival effects in Chinese gardens to the study of contemporary Chinese architecture. This work is a part of my current GRF project on two emerging Chinese architects. There is a second line of further development arising from the study of historical texts about Suzhou gardens. Historical information has been commonly used to inform linear chronologies of individual gardens. Yet there is a possibility to engage Chinese literary records and poetry in terms of a shuttling between aspects of memory, direct experience and expectation. In this way, thinking about texts can be parallel to thinking about experience of extant gardens. My intention is to write about this in the next year.

14618615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14618615.value: Four World Heritage-listed gardens in Suzhou have been studied in this project: the Garden of the Humble Administrator (Zhuo Zheng Yuan) and the Lingering Garden (Liu Yuan) are larger gardens, while the Garden of the Master of the Nets (Wang Shi Yuan) and the Mountain Villa of Embracing Beauty (Huanxiu shanzhuang) are smaller ones. Using a newly expanded vocabulary, working both with photographs and historical studies of texts, we showed how bridges, embankments, rockeries, doorways and wall openings participate in landscape settings that are non-perspectival. In this way, the appreciation of gardens is brought closer to the spatial sensibility well-known in traditional Chinese paintings.

14618715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14618715.value: Mangrove found in intertidal zone is well recognized as ecologically important and productive ecosystem. However, limited by accessibility, data availability and cost, no comprehensive survey was conducted, which in turn forbid further understanding of characteristics and function of the ecosystem. Subjected to scarce land resources, development pressures are encroaching natural resources and pose tremendous threats to mangrove habitats in Hong Kong. Besides, the current status of exotic species in Mai Po Ramsar Site, the largest mangrove habitat in Hong Kong is unknown due to lack of distribution information. It urges a quick strategy to collect base data concerning species inventory and their distribution while such method can also be extended to monitor possible adverse impacts in long run. For a number of reasons such as having wide spatial coverage, repeatability and ability to record various parts of electromagnetic energy, remote sensing has long been an effective tool to collect spectral data from satellites or aircrafts for various vegetation applications such as classification, biophysical parameter extraction and monitoring. Among imaging sensors, hyperspectral sensors that are able to collect visible and infrared spectral data in hundreds of narrow spectral bands can detect dynamic changes in the biophysical status or biochemical compounds in vegetation. Besides, vegetation species having subtle differences of reflectance in various bands can be detected by these sensors, which are useful for automatic species differentiation. However, existing hyperspectral satellite-borne or airborne sensing data can hardly fulfill the data demand for geographical and ecological research. Data from satellite sensors limit in spatial details, which only allow identification of large and homogeneous patches. Data obtained from manned aircrafts are rich in spatial details and theoretically, the data can be acquired in regular time intervals for continuous monitoring, but high operational cost prohibited vegetation management application. The development of unmanned airborne system (UAS) and sensor miniaturization overcome such hindrances. Operating at low altitude; UAS can acquire data in ultra-high spatial resolution at centimeter level. Besides, flexibility of data acquisition is largely enhanced as it is not affected by cloud cover and constrained by strict aviation regulation. Additional data product, canopy height can be derived after image mosaicking. And it is evident that integration of optical data (hyperspectral data) and structural data (height profiles) improves the mapping accuracy of vegetation species and biophysical parameter extraction. Given such flexibility, data can be acquired over regular time interval to monitor and understand the changes in these ecosystems.

14618715.label: Realisation of objectives
14618715.value: The research objectives were realized through several stages of data collection, integration and data analysis. (1) Data Collection The following data collection and acquisition methods were performed. UAV Hyperspectral data – This was acquired through an UAV autonomously flying hexacopter Aibot X6 equipped with a pushbroom Headwall Nona-Hyperspec sensor. The hyperspectral sensor acquired 270 spectral bands between 400 – 1000 nm. Two sets of preliminary images were acquired on 08/12/2016 at a flight altitude of 100 m with an equivalent spatial resolution of 0.06m covering a small area of 20,000 m2. This set of data was used for preliminary data analysis to produce Conference Papers 1, 2 and 3 and to achieve objectives 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6. Additional flights were attempted. However, the hexacopter experienced some technical problems and failed to function normally. Thus an extension of the project was applied and approved. It was unfortunate that this UAV sensor could not be fixed at a reasonable cost. Subsequently, the project shifted to acquire data through contracting the service to a vendor. Several rounds of experiment were experimented and a reasonable set of data was acquired in 2018 ultimately. UAV Visible data – To align with the hyperspectral data, a DJI Phantom 4 quadcopter was used to take conventional RGB images from five angles on the same area on 29/03/2017 at a flying altitude of 50 m with a spatial resolution of 0.02 m. This set of images was used to acquire canopy height point cloud data to achieve objectives 2, 4 and 5. LiDAR – Civil Engineering and Development Department of HKSAR acquired LiDAR for the entire HK in 2010, however, Mai Po was not covered. A vendor was contracted to obtain the LiDAR data. A GL-70A survey grade Riegal VUX-1LR laser scanner on a helicopter was used to acquire the data on 21/3/2018 at low flight altitude of approximately 155-270m. This data was used to extract point cloud canopy, height and other structural data to achieve objectives 2 and 4. Worldview-3 Image – As UAV images were small in areal coverage, a Worldview 3 images with 8 multispectral bands at 2 m and 1 panchromatic band at 0.5m acquired on 20/12/2017 was also used for objectives 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6. Field investigation – Mangrove habitat was harsh and accessibility was difficult. Field survey was undertaken in 2017 for species identification and LAI data collection in early 2018 using a hemispherical camera system for LAI regression modeling for objectives 2 and 4. (2) Biophysical, Canopy and terrain modeling Digital surface model (DSM) was first captured using UAV-color images based on photogrammetry. The data was integrated in feature selection and image classification in Conference Paper 1 (2017). LiDAR data captured in a larger area was integrated with WV3 multispectral data for feature selection and species classification in Journal Paper 1. Useful canopy and elevation metrics were selected in image classification. In Journal Paper 2, difference of first return and last return of LiDAR was computed to generate canopy height model (CHM) for further non-parametric regression modeling. Leaf area index (LAI) data was captured using hemispherical digital camera system in the field. LAI was tested against LiDAR, hyperspectral and WV3 data for correlation analysis by the PhD student, Li Qiaosi with results incorporated in her final thesis. (3) Feature Selection Feature selection was conducted to select the important features from remote sensing images and structural data of canopy based on LiDAR and photogrammetry to achieve objectives 1, 5 and 6. In Conference Paper 1 (2017), support vector machine, stepwise discriminant analysis and minimum noise fraction transformation were used for feature selection with the UAV hyperspectral and digital surface model (DSM) derived from UAV-color photos. The most essential 20 selected features were compared in terms of classification accuracy. In Conference Paper 3 (2019), random forest recursive feature elimination (RF-RFE), genetic algorithm with RF fitness function, simulated annealing with RF fitness and stepwise discriminant analysis were used with the 256 hyperspectral bands together with spectral bands plus first spectral derivatives. RF-RFE was better in accuracy and computation efficiency. In Journal Paper 1, RF-RFE was used in feature selection of multispectral data and LiDAR metrics. Most WV3 bands except coastal blue were selected. Among 57 LiDAR metrics, six commonly selected features related to canopy height, elevation variation and canopy stratification played significant role in image classification when combined with multispectral data for mangrove species classification. (4) Mangrove Species Identification, Machine learning classification and object-based classification Machine learning classifiers of support vector machine (SVM) and random forest (RF) were used to test the accuracy of mangrove species with hyperspectral, multispectral and LiDAR data in the 3 conference papers and 2 journal papers. Conference Paper 1 (2017) reported the comparison of SVM with maximum likelihood classifier using six different data sets composed of 20 selected features extracted through different feature selection methods. SVM together with 20 minimum noise fraction features and DSM produced an overall accuracy of 89% and Kappa of 0.88. In Journal Paper 1, SVM and RF were used with spectral and structural data. The highest overall accuracy of 88% was yielded with a combined data using 14 features selected after feature selection. This paper also confirmed the importance of overstory and understory structure in mangrove habitat. Similar result was reported in Journal Paper 2. (5) Objectives not fully realized Related to Objective 6, object based classifier was attempted with the assumption of capturing each tree as an object. This assumption was found too simplistic as the actual canopy structure of mangrove forest was complicated as the forest was dense and canopy was closed and continuous. It was difficult to search through local maxima in CHM to discern individual trees. To test out the use of object based classification, it was found more suitable to use other subtropical forest habitats rather than mangrove. A M.Phil. study by Ivan Kwong was close to completion which made use of UAV LiDAR and RGB airphotos for object based tree delineation. The experience gained will provide a better foundation to pursue future studies in mangrove. Objective 3 on temporal analysis was not performed as earlier LiDAR did not cover Mai Po. The collection of LiDAR and hyperspectral data within the study period was too short of meaningful analysis. The project was conducted with some difficulties. First, the original UAV machines had technical problems after taking several data sets covering a small area. The research needed to shift to vendor of data acquisition which posed some delay in our work. This delay affected data integration as we planned for a closely timed acquisition of UAV hyperspectral data and LiDAR data. Second, doing fieldwork in the mangrove environment was harsh. Student helpers nowadays were difficult to recruit. Third, UAV is an effective means of collecting remote sensing data. It is good particularly for detailed analysis using data collected with very high spatial resolution. The drawback is the small area coverage in data collection. Yet, Journal Paper 2 provided a good attempt to extend the measurement of mangrove canopy height through random forest regression modeling.

14618715.label: Major findings and research outcome
14618715.value: CHM generated showed the terrain elevation was between 2 – 5 m whilst the tallest tree was 10.72m (Journal Paper 2). Variation of canopy height was related to species distribution. A RF based regression model between CHM and spectral data helped generate an overall CHM for the entire Mai Po mangrove. Feature selection studies made use of different methods to extract meaningful features to identify mangrove species. Conference Paper 1 (2017) used SVM, stepwise discriminant analysis and Minimum noise fraction transformation. Conference Paper 2 (2018) used RF-RFE, genetic algorithm with RF fitness function, simulated annealing with recursive feature fitness and stepwise discriminant analysis. Subsequently, RF-RFE was confirmed to the most reliable one and reported in Conference Paper 3 (2019). All these works found that NIR (762, 1003nm), red edge (700-715 and 755 nm), chlorophyll absorption red (650-670nm), blue (427nm) and green (550nm) were important (Conference Paper 3, 2019). Journal Paper 1 found that LiDAR metrics including canopy height model, canopy shape and elevation variation were more effective than spectral features in mangrove species identification. Image classification results confirmed the superiority of machine learning classifiers over conventional maximum likelihood classification in hyperspectral data plus DSM data (Conference Paper 1, 2017). SVM produced an overall accuracy of 89% using 20 minimum noise fraction transformed features plus DSM. In Conference Paper 3 (2019), SVM and RF were used with six sets of data composed of multispectral and LiDAR metrics. Using LiDAR alone worked slightly better than spectral data. The overall accuracy was 79% with LiDAR, versus 72% using multispectral data. However, the most accurate result still came from the combined datasets. Both classifiers were able to generate an OA of 89%. Machine learning classifiers (SVM and RF) were found to be effective and they were less restrictive in assumption and able to handle non-linear data and adaptive fitting capacity. Object-based classifier was found less suitable in the mangrove habitat. At species level, KO, AC, AA and AI were accurately identified with hyperspectral data and DSM (Conference Paper 1, 2017). The producer’s and user’s accuracy were above 90% in some species. However, it was noted that area covered by hyperspectral image was small. Using multispectral WV3 and LiDAR data, AC, AI, KO and KOAI could be effectively identified with 14 input features (Journal Paper 1).

14618715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14618715.value: UAV hyperspectral images provide useful data for feature selection and image classification. However, they suffer from a small areal coverage as they are restricted by battery life and flying height. Studies can only be undertaken in a small area. However, the experiment and conclusion drawn in terms of the importance of features extracted and robustness of classifiers tested, could add value in transferring the technologies to high resolution satellite data for a much larger area coverage so that more meaningful statistics can be generated which was demonstrated in Journal Paper 2. LiDAR derived metrics related to canopy height, variation of elevation and canopy shape were found essential to differentiate mangrove species. More experiments can be undertaken to explore the data dimensions inherent in the LiDAR data. With more advanced LiDAR data available, the full spectrum data could be extended to study the forest structure in more details. With more data being acquired, a meaningful temporal analysis can be conducted.

14618715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14618715.value: Mangroves have significant economic, environmental and ecological values but they are under threat of human activities. An accurate map of mangrove species distribution is important to conserve them. In this study, UAV hyperspectral and satellite multispectral data were integrated with canopy height data from UAV photos and LiDAR. We found spectral bands at red, red edge, near infrared and green essential for mangrove species identification. LiDAR provided important canopy height, canopy shape and variation in elevation information which was found more important than spectral data for mangrove species identification. But the combination of spectral and LiDAR data provided the best result with machine learning classifiers for mangrove species identification. The result of this research will help enrich information for the conservation of mangrove habitat.

14619315.value: 這項研究主要是針對中國農村住宅能源消耗所排放的黑碳的減排。 氣候變化是世界正在面臨的一個前所未有的威脅。愈來愈多的科學證據證明了人類活動排放的溫室氣體需要負主要責任。因為同時存在顯著的氣候和空氣污染影響，短生命週期的氣候污染物正在得到越來越多的關注，在尚未規制的相關污染物中，黑碳是 影響最大的。中國是世界上最大的黑碳排放國，而最主要的貢獻之一來自於農村住宅生物質和煤炭的燃燒。本項目將為如何減排農村住宅能源消耗帶來的黑碳排放提供支持。 通過燃燒更清潔的能源或者提高能源效率，多種技術可以減少黑碳排放，而每減排一噸黑碳的成本在不同技術間有比較大的差異。為了提高減排的費用有效性或者說是在給定預算下減排更多黑碳，成本低的減排機會應該優先得到應用。然而，擁有巨大減排潛力並且以生物質或者煤炭作為主要燃料的地區通常貧困、技術不發達和偏遠。黑碳減排在這些地區有很大的阻礙，技術潛力在某些時候並不能得到充足的發揮而導致實際成本可以遠高於理想情況。因為數據的缺乏，許多現在的政策還是基於潛在減排成本。本項目將會量化實際減排成本，利用世界銀行的現有數據並調查中國主要地理區域內幾個村莊的住宅能源利用技術，針對每種主要的減排技術度量技術潛力和實際情形之間的差距。我們將會計算理想和實際情形下的邊際減排成本曲線。為了縮小它們之間的差距，這項研究將會著重探討政府和市場兩種主要的干預方式。 為了驗證研究計劃的可行性和改進其設計，我們已經在2014年7月和8月開展了第一次探索式的田野調查。技術潛力和實際情形之間的顯著差距確實存在，我們的研究也進行了初步的量化。 這項研究的結果可以提高中國農村住宅黑碳減排的理論理解和戰略實施。作為理論和戰略層面的案例研究，本項目也會對其它行業和其它發展中國家提供可借鑑的建議。

14619315.label: Realisation of objectives
14619315.value: All four research objectives have been achieved. The first research objective aims to improve the understanding and implementation of black carbon mitigation in rural China. A wide gap exists in the application of black carbon mitigation technologies between the ideal situation that fully achieve the technological potential and the actual situation that encounters a variety of technological, social and political challenges. Through our research activities corresponding to the following three research objectives, we have got much insightful knowledge on in-practice black carbon mitigation in rural China. The second research objective was achieved with the performance gaps of black carbon mitigation costs quantified. We quantitatively measured the unit cost gaps of black carbon mitigation technologies in rural China, paying special attention to the lifetimes and annual utilization rates of those technologies. Our first-hand household survey covered three major black carbon emitting provinces (Hebei province in the North and Guizhou and Guangxi provinces in the South with and without systematic winter heating demand), seven counties, 24 villages and 695 households. The observed gaps between the in-theory and in-practice unit costs ranged between 0 and 69.13. The large gaps were found in the biogas digester of glass fiber reinforced plastic (South), improved brick stove (North) and traditional household biogas digester (North), while LPG stove, centralized biogas system (North), and elevated thermal bed had zero gaps. Although caution should be applied in attempting to adopt this study’s results for entire rural China, the newly acquired quantitative knowledge could still produce better estimation than an extrapolation from other countries to China. On the third research objective, our research suggests that the bottom-up incentive, or air pollution control largely for domestic benefits, should be more sustainable than climate change for black carbon mitigation. We examined China’s motivations for active climate mitigation and argued that domestic air pollution concerns, rather than global climate mitigation pressure, could better explain and sustain China’s position reversal in international climate negotiation. A Giant Panda Strategy of climate change was proposed: climate mitigation can become a great opportunity, rather than a heavy burden, to holistically approach domestic goals. For the fourth research objective, our research indicates that the market should be given a more significant role for more effective black carbon mitigation with narrower performance gaps. The deployment of top-down approaches may help remove the barriers to the adoption of mitigation technologies; however, insufficient engagement with rural communities have caused problems such as lack of local incentives, mismatch of resources, and inadequate management capacity to result in wider gaps and poorer technological performance in their operation. A balance should be found between top-down and bottom-up approach to include local communities in political decision-making. In addition, distributed energy production and use such as household biogas digesters have been increasingly advocated as a promising and cheaper solution. However, according to our research, the performance of distributed energy systems failed the expectations largely due to operational challenges. This study illustrates the potential advantage of centralized systems if we take the actual lifetimes and actual annual utilization rates into account. The actual lifetimes of distributed biogas digesters are much shorter than that of centralized ones. Regarding annual utilization rates, since biogas digesters cannot function well in a low-temperature environment (such as in winter), which again undermines the expected performance of this distributed energy system.

14619315.label: Major findings and research outcome
14619315.value: The research project has achieved intended objectives and resulted in several major findings. First, the unit costs of black carbon mitigation in rural China are measured and the performance gaps between in-theory and in-practice unit costs are quantified and explained. We quantitatively examined the unit cost gaps of black carbon mitigation technologies in rural China, paying special attention to the lifetimes and annual utilization rates. In addition, we also analyzed the causes of the performance gaps, especially why some technologies have wider gaps than others. A balance should be found between top-down and bottom-up approach to include local communities in policy making and implementation. Second, our research found that domestic incentives, or air pollution control, should be more sustainable than global climate change for black carbon mitigation. We examined China’s motivations for active climate mitigation and argued that domestic co-benefits could better explain and sustain China’s support of Paris Climate Agreement. This research finding was further extended to more strategically utilize climate change for governing domestic problems. A Giant Panda Strategy of climate change was proposed: climate mitigation can become a great opportunity, rather than a heavy burden, to holistically approach domestic goals. The research has directly resulted in three publications and contributed to the fourth one, all in top academic journals (including Environmental Science and Technology (Impact factor: 6.653; Ranking: 11/242 in Environmental Sciences), Atmospheric Environment (Impact factor: 3.708; Ranking: 16/86 in Meteorology and Atmospheric Sciences), and Climate Policy (Impact factor: 3.832; Ranking: 15/109 in Environmental Studies). Because of its policy implications, especially when President Trump withdrew the United States out of the Paris Agreement, the second research finding has attracted global media interest. We were invited to directly contribute two short papers in Canadian and Australian media: (i) Xu, Y., 4 June 2017. Trump’s climate loss is a huge gain for China, The Globe and Mail, https://www.theglobeandmail.com/opinion/trumps-climate-loss-is-a-huge-gain-for-china/article35198923/; (ii) Xu, Y., 11 August 2016. Understanding China’s climate change commitment, East Asia Forum. http://www.eastasiaforum.org/2016/08/11/understanding-chinas-climate-change-commitment/. Other media that covered our research included: Forbes (United States), El Mercurio (Chile), LA Times (Untied States), News Details (United Kingdom), Science Business (Belgium), Sydney Morning Herald (Australia), and Devex. Directly related to this research project, one Ph.D. student (ZHANG Weishi) successfully graduated in 2017 after defending her thesis, entitled “Measuring and Narrowing the Gaps between Reality and the Ideal: Residential Black Carbon Mitigation in Rural China”.

14619315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14619315.value: We will continue studying the co-benefits of climate change and expand our focus beyond black carbon. This research project led to a hypothesis with two versions. In the strong version, costs for mitigating climate change could be entirely offset by the domestic, non-climate co-benefits, such as air pollution control, energy security, innovation and economic transformation. Accordingly, climate mitigation can be justified by domestic co-benefits alone even without counting those global climate benefits. The weak version states that the domestic co-benefits could partially offset the climate mitigation costs. This hypothesis will be adopted as an analytical framework and empirically tested in our follow-up research. We will select several major countries, tentatively including China, India and the United States, to quantify the domestic, non-climate co-benefits and compare them with the country’s climate mitigation costs. After initial studies in these two years, we plan to submit another proposal under the RGC General Research Fund scheme to carry out the research topic.

14619315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14619315.value: Climate mitigation often has multiple co-benefits. Black carbon not only causes global warming but also is an air pollutant. Its mitigation could thus be justified by both climate change and air pollution concerns. We argue that China’s recent firm support of global climate treaties could be largely explained by domestic, non-climate co-benefits and less by international pressure for climate mitigation. A Giant Panda Strategy of climate change is proposed for China and other countries to actively and strategically utilize climate mitigation for solving multiple domestic governance tasks. Furthermore, black carbon is mainly emitted in inefficient burning of biomass and coal in developing countries, where accurate data are often missing. Current research mainly reluctantly adopts data from developed countries, which may lead to inaccurate or wrong policy recommendations for choosing black carbon mitigation technologies and minimizing costs. This research collects first-hand information on the unit costs of black carbon mitigation technologies in rural China, where various constraints lead to wide performance costs. Nevertheless, some technologies have much wider gaps than others. We conclude that for better black carbon mitigation, a policy mixture between top-down and bottom-up approaches should be applied for technologies’ adoption and more importantly their normal operation.

14620215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14620215.value: 目的 這個計劃旨在探究，相對重溫而言，分散注意力及焦慮情緒如何調節測驗對提昇年青人一般知識記憶的效用。 計劃背景 雖然有證據顯示在練習階段重溫測驗材料有助於其長期記憶的留存，即測驗效應，但是測驗仍然經常被用於量度學習成果，而不是用來促進學習。報告指出採用不同的學習材料、測驗、群體，測驗都對隨後的回憶表現有顯著的好處。不過，在課室內廣泛推廣頻繁測驗以改善學生學習之前，我們需要先驗證各種會影響學生記憶的因素對測驗效應是否有調節作用。 計劃設計 在建議的三項實驗中，我們會在練習階段操縱參與者的注意力（集中／分散），實驗誘發情緒（焦慮／平和），誘發情緒的內容（與測驗相關／與測驗無關）。我們將會在統計上控制個人差異的影響，例如測驗焦慮特質、工作記憶容量、非語言智力、及動機（例：自我效能）。於分散注意操作組，參與者將會透過重溫及／或回想答案以回答用文字顯示的一般知識問題，同時驗證在練習階段中的每個以聲音顯示的概念是否來自預先指定的類別。我們將會在練習階段要求參與者回想一件有關教育（與測驗相關）或家庭（與測驗無關）的事件，以誘發他們特定的情緒。有關的事件會是令他們感到平和或焦慮。我們預計分散注意及焦慮情緒將會起交互作用，減低測驗（相對重溫而言）對參與者在一星期後最後一次線索回憶測驗中的表現的益處。 計劃的重要性 這項研究將會有三個主要貢獻。第一，情緒和注意力對測驗強化記憶的效用將會對一些測驗效應的理論有啟示，例如：注意力是否在焦慮狀態對測驗效應的影響起了中介作用。第二，找出何時測驗強化記憶時最有效可為有意在課室推廣頻繁測驗的老師提供資訊。第三，我們將會探討參與者的個別差異，如：工作記憶容量，如何調節分散注意力及／或焦慮情緒對測驗益處的不利影響。總括而言，此項研究將會填補文獻中的一個重要間隙：找出調節測驗效應的因素。

14620215.label: Realisation of objectives
14620215.value: To achieve Objective 1, we examined how divided attention might affect the testing effect by introducing a secondary verbal task during practice phase. Specifically, participants in the divided attention condition restudied or recalled the missing information in visually presented general knowledge facts, while judging whether auditorily presented items were from a pre-specified category. In contrast, participants in the full attention condition just restudied or recalled the missing information in visually presented general knowledge facts without doing any secondary task. Despite using a high-powered experiment (i.e., with sufficient sample size to achieve high statistical power), we did not obtain any significant effect of divided vs. full attention on the testing effect, whether the general knowledge facts were considered as interesting or boring, and whether the retention interval (between the practice phase and the final test) was immediate or delayed for two days. The preliminary results were reported in our poster (Tse, Chan, Tse, & Wong, 2017, Annual Meeting of the Psychonomic Society) and the full set of findings was reported in our manuscript (Tse, Chan, Tse, & Wong, 2019, Frontiers in Psychology). To achieve Objective 2, we examined how state anxiety might affect the testing effect by introducing an anxious mood induction task before and during practice phase. Specifically, participants in the anxious mood condition viewed and interpreted negative pictures with anxious music background before and during the practice phase. Those in the neutral mood condition went through the same procedure, except that the pictures seen were neutral and the background music was neutral. (The music clips were selected based on previous studies in mood induction literature, whereas the pictures were normed based on the same population as in the current project—i.e., undergraduate students in PI’s institution.) The participants’ mood was measured (via ratings of State-Trait Anxiety Inventory) to make sure the effectiveness of mood induction manipulation. Although the sample size was sufficient to achieve high statistical power, we did not find any significant effect of anxious vs. neutral mood on the testing effect, whether the general knowledge facts were considered as interesting or boring and whether the retention interval was immediate or delayed for two days. The preliminary results were reported in our poster (Tse, Chan, Tse, & Wong, 2017, Annual Meeting of the Psychonomic Society) and the full set of findings was reported in our manuscript (Tse, Chan, Tse, & Wong, 2019, Frontiers in Psychology). It is possible that anxious mood being induced via listening to music and seeing negative pictures was not directly related to the test-failure experience, such that this mood change did not significantly modulate participants’ testing effect. To examine the potential effect of test-relevant anxious mood, we conducted another experiment in which participants performed a phrase arrangement task prior to the restudying/testing practice phase. In this task, participants were given 30 trials, each of which consist of four phrases in Chinese. They needed to rearrange the phrases so as to make a sensible sentence. The contents in all of these sentences were related to test failure experience. These stimuli were found to significantly induce anxious mood relevant to the test failure experience (e.g., Tse, Wu, & Wan, 2005, which also used university students in Hong Kong as their sample). By inducing anxious mood that was directly related to students’ failure experience, we expected to test more precisely whether anxious mood could counteract the benefit of testing on participants’ memory performance. Contrary to our expectation, compared with control participants who did not go through this mood induction procedure, anxious-mood participants showed a stronger testing effect in immediate test, and the two groups showed similar magnitude of the testing effect in the delayed test. Because anxious-mood participants had more difficulty restudying materials in the practice phase than control participants and the presence of test-relevant anxious mood might cause anxious-mood participants to focus more on the fact retrieval, the testing effect could be boosted by test-relevant anxious mood via desirable difficulty. However, this desirable difficulty hypothesis could not explain why the “benefit” of anxious mood disappeared in the delayed test. These findings were reported in our poster (Tse, Chan, Tse, & Wong, 2019, International Convention of Psychological Science). To achieve Objective 3, we combined the divided attention and test-irrelevant anxious mood induction manipulations, as mentioned above, and tested whether the influence of these two factors would undermine participants’ testing effect. Compared with control participants who did not go through these manipulations, participants in this anxious mood + divided attention condition showed about the same magnitude of testing effect, providing further evidence for the possibility that the test-enhanced learning may be immune to the influence of situational factors; that is, divided attention and/or anxious mood during the practice phase. These results were reported in our poster (Tse, Chan, Tse, & Wong, 2017, Annual Meeting of the Psychonomic Society). To achieve Objective 4, in the experiments that involved divided attention manipulation or test-irrelevant anxious mood induction manipulation, we measured participants’ working memory capacity and trait test anxiety as participant-level individual difference variables to examine their influences on the testing effect, and tested whether they might modulate the effect of divided attention or anxious mood on the testing effect. We conducted multiple regression analyses to test whether situational factors (attention being divided or anxious mood being induced) interacted with participants’ individual difference variables (working memory capacity and trait test anxiety) in their influence on the testing effect. The testing effect was not generally predicted by these individual-difference variables. Also, there was no situational factor x individual difference interaction, indicating that the null effects of divided attention or anxious mood were unlikely due to the genuine effects being masked by participants’ individual differences. This suggests the possibility that the test-enhanced learning may be immune to the influence of individual-difference factors; that is, students’ working memory capacity and trait test anxiety. The full set of these findings was reported in our manuscript (Tse, Chan, Tse, & Wong, 2019, Frontiers in Psychology).

14620215.label: Major findings and research outcome
14620215.value: Testing effect refers to the finding that a practice test on study materials leads to better performance in a final test than restudying the materials for the same amount of time. We conducted experiments to test how distraction, as triggered by divided attention or experimentally induced anxious mood in the practice phase, could modulate the benefit of testing (vs. restudying) on the learning of interesting and boring general knowledge facts. Two individual difference factors (trait test anxiety and working memory capacity) were measured. Under divided attention, participants restudied or recalled the missing information in visually presented general knowledge facts, while judging whether auditorily presented items were from a pre-specified category. To experimentally induce anxious mood, we instructed participants to view and interpret negative pictures with anxious music background before and during the practice phase (as test-irrelevant anxious mood) or to rearrange the phrases that are related to test failure experience (as test-relevant anxious mood). Immediate and two-day delayed tests were given. Tse, Chan, Tse, and Wong (2017, Annual Meeting of the Psychonomic Society; 2019, Frontiers in Psychology) showed that regardless of item type (interesting or boring) or retention interval, the testing effect was not significantly affected by divided (vs. full) attention or test-irrelevant anxious (vs. neutral) mood. These results remained unchanged after taking into account the influences of participants’ trait test anxiety and working memory capacity. There was no main effect of working memory capacity and trait test anxiety interaction or their interaction on the overall testing effect. The magnitude of testing effect was not significantly affected even when the divided attention and anxious mood manipulations were combined (Tse, Chan, Tse, & Wong, 2017, Annual Meeting of the Psychonomic Society) or when the anxious mood was induced via triggering participants’ test failure experience (i.e., test-relevant anxious mood) (Tse, Chan, Tse, & Wong, 2019, International Convention of Psychological Science). As far as we know, the current study was the first to obtain evidence that the benefit of testing over restudying on the learning of general knowledge facts was not compromised by situational factors (anxious mood and divided attention) and individual-difference factors (working memory capacity and trait test anxiety) in a laboratory setting.

14620215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14620215.value: In our experiments, we found that the benefit of testing over restudying on the learning of general knowledge facts was not significantly influenced by situational factors (anxious mood and divided attention) and/or individual-difference factors (working memory capacity and trait test anxiety). While this might suggest that students should be encouraged to incorporate retrieval practice as an effective tool toward better learning outcomes, it is important to note that our experiments involved only low-stakes tests, in that we did not impose any evaluative pressure, nor was any monetary compensation given based on participants’ performance. Therefore, it is critical to test whether the current results would be obtained in the situation when students are given high-stakes tests under high-evaluation pressure in classroom settings.

14620215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14620215.value: We examine how divided attention and anxious mood modulate the effectiveness of testing (relative to restudying) on improving young adults’ memory for general knowledge facts. Tests are often used to measure learning, rather than to facilitate it, in spite of the evidence of the advantage in long-term retention for the materials that are tested over the materials that are restudied during the practice phase (i.e., the testing effect). The benefit of testing on subsequent memory performance was robust in previous studies. In the current laboratory experiments, we found that the testing effect was immune to the influence of divided (vs. full) attention and/or anxious (vs. neutral) mood during practice phase. This was so whether anxious mood being induced was relevant or irrelevant to students’ test failure experience, whether final test was given immediately or two days after the practice phase, and whether general knowledge facts were or were not of students’ interest. Individual difference factors, trait test anxiety and working memory capacity also had no influence on the testing effects. While these findings await further replication in the classroom settings, they suggest that students may be encouraged to incorporate retrieval practice as an effective tool toward better learning outcomes.
