14620515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14620515.value: 本研究旨在為数學教師提供支援及培訓課程以協助他們更有效的引導學生參與数學課堂對話，為學生創造更為豐富的数學學習機會。本研究亦將檢視這一教師支援及培訓項目是否改變了教師的相應的教學信念及課堂行為，進而促進了學生的数學學習。本研究含有三個目標如下。首先，研究團队將根据有關教師在引導課堂對話中的作用及教師如何進行有效的專業學習的現有文献知識、他人和参與本研究的教師自身的日常課堂教學實例，設計相關的教師支援及培訓課程。第二，這一支援和培訓課程將在一組數學教師中予以實施。同時，另有一組數學教師作為對照組。第三，本研究將運用量化和貭化分析工具，對两組教師及其學生在課堂中的話語行為表現進行實施教師支援及培訓課程前後的组间及组內的比較，从而對這一教師支援及培訓項目的成效進行評價。評價的指標包括: 教師對進行課堂對話引導的自我成效的觀感，教師的課堂話語行為，學生的課堂話語行為，學生對數學學科、數學課堂學習的興趣和觀感。本研究将填补相关領域的對教師支援及培訓課程的需要, 亦填补對此类教師支援及培訓課程的成效進行系统的、实証的检視的需要, 以协助教育政策的制定、教育實践的改進有据可依。

14620515.label: Realisation of objectives
14620515.value: The research project was conducted to address the apparent lack of the teacher interventions in engaging students with rich classroom discourse for rich learning opportunity, and consequently the apparent lack of the systematic investigations of the links between the teacher interventions to the changes in teachers’ classroom discourse behaviors, and then in turn to student learning. The study has achieved the three proposed objectives to address the needs. The following paragraphs explains how the objectives were achieved. The Design of the Teacher Intervention Programme The goal of the teacher intervention program was to address the need for teachers to develop the conceptual and practical tools for engaging students in dialogical mathematics classroom discourse. Informed by the current research on the core pedagogies of dialogic discourse, five objectives were formulated for the intervention program to achieve. The first objective was to assist teachers in identifying the significant attributes of classroom discourse that affect student learning, such as the attributes of interactive and authoritative dimension of classroom talk, cognitive scaffolding and social scaffolding of teacher questions, ways in which language both promotes and hinders student thinking. The second objective was to assist teachers in applying identified conceptual tools to explore the principles and core practices of engaging students in dialogic discourse. These analytical tools include the principles for disciplined and dialogical classroom engagement, the elements of accountable classroom talk, key aspects for creating favorable conditions for dialogic discourse to take place in mathematics classrooms. The third objective was to apply the learning analytics tool, Classroom Discourse Analyzer (CDA) (Chen, Clark, & Resnick, 2015). to analyze the patterns of classroom discourse at work in the teacher’s own classroom to support reflection on his/her own classroom discourse. CDA is designed to visualize, track, and identify holistic and meaningful classroom talk moves between the teacher and students. The fourth objective was to assist teachers to identify the challenges that they perceive in their daily teaching while orchestrating classroom discourse that supports and expands student thinking and learning. The fifth objective was assisting teachers in mastering and refining repertoire of discourse moves. With these skills, teachers can select strategies that are more likely to create a classroom environment that promotes students’ engagement in dialogic classroom discourse and that are suitable for their classrooms. To support teachers’ professional development through reflecting on their classroom practice, we developed a set of video cases to scaffold teachers to pay attention to the dimensions to analyze classroom discourse and relations of the dimensions to student learning. Also, video cases of the participating teachers were obtained from their classrooms for the teachers to analyze and to reflect upon with assistance of the CDA tool. Further, classroom-embedded intervention activities including structured peer classroom observation, and peer review and discussion were significant component of the intervention program. We designed a total of 28 hours of the intervention activities. For more details about the intervention programme, please refer to Ni & Ho (2017) and Ni, Ho, Chen, Cheung, Cai, & Ng (2017). The Implementation of the Intervention Programme Thirty-two fourth-grade mathematic teachers from16 elementary schools and more than 800 students of the classrooms were recruited for the study. The schools and teachers were selected from 46 teachers from 23 schools who indicated an interest in participating in the study after we contacted 354 public local primary schools. From the total of 16 selected schools and two teachers from each school, half of them were assigned to the intervention group and the other half were assigned to the non-intervention group. The schools in the two groups were paired by taking into consideration the main factors as much as possible: (a) school neighborhood locations, (b) students’ mathematics achievement level based on a territory-wide basic competence test administered by the Hong Kong Examination Authority to monitor the city’s compulsory education system, (c) participating teachers' subject with respect to their professional teaching training, and (d) participating teachers’ experience teaching mathematics. Consent for participating in the study was obtained from the schools, the teachers, and the students’ parents, who were informed of the purpose and procedure of the study before the study commenced. The intervention was implemented over a semester of 4½ months. The intervention programme included 18 hours of 6 workshops that took place in CUHK Faculty of Education and 10 hours of classroom-embedded intervention activities that were peer classroom observations, peer discussions, and review of CDA (Classroom Discourse Analyzer) reports for each pair of teachers in each of the schools. The intervention group participated in the intervention activities during the period of October 2016 to February 2017 when the workshops were conducted during October and the classroom-embedded activities were distributed from November to February. The workshops were provided to the non-intervention group in June 2018 after research data collection for the project was completed. Evaluation of the Efficacy of the Intervention In order to assess the efficacy of the intervention, the study adopted quasi-experimental design. A set of pre- and post-measures of teacher learning were conducted with the intervention group and non-intervention group. These assessments included: 1) teachers’ perceived self-efficacy in teaching mathematics (questionnaire), 2) teachers’ perceived self-efficacy in guiding classroom discourse (questionnaire), and 3) observed features of a teacher’s discourse behaviors in mathematics classrooms (classroom observation). Each teacher of the intervention and non-intervention group had their mathematics lessons videotaped four times, twice before and then twice after the interventions. The pre-classroom-observation was undertaken in September for the intervention group before the intervention commenced in October and it took place in October for the non-intervention group. The post-classroom-observation was conducted in April to May of the following year after all the intervention activities were completed that was mid-February. Building up on the existing literature, we developed a coding scheme including 10 codes to analyze discourse behaviors of the teachers in order to characterize how much a teacher prompts dialogic classroom room discourse to support and extend student learning. All of the 128 videotaped lessons, 64 each from the pre-observation and post-observation respectively, were transcribed into text for coding. Twenty-two percent of 128 videotaped lessons were double coded, 14 lessons each from the pre- and post-observation. After rounds of refining the coding scheme and calibration training for research assistants to code the classroom data, satisfactory inter-rater agreements were achieved, ranging from 72% to 100% agreement for the pre-observation and from 75% to 88% agreement for the post-observation. Three sets of student learning outcomes were also assessed before and after the teacher intervention. These included students’ classroom participation in terms of number of student turns and amounts of words spoken out in classroom discussions (classroom observation), students’ indicated interest and attitude towards learning mathematics (questionnaire), and mathematics achievement (achievement tests). Both quantitative and qualitative analyses have been conducted to establish evidence of efficacy of the teacher intervention in terms of the links between teacher professional development and teacher changes in teachers’ perceived teaching efficacy and classroom practice, and consequently from teacher changes to improved student learning.

14620515.label: Major findings and research outcome
14620515.value: Major Findings Teachers’ experience with the intervention. The intervention teachers were surveyed with a questionnaire to evaluate their experience with the intervention. Their ratings were over 5 point out of a 1-6 point scale across four aspects of the workshops. The teachers also indicated a positive evaluation of the classroom-based intervention activities, rating them from 4. 87 to 5.50 on a 1-6 point scale over the similar four aspects (Ni, Ho, Chen, & Shi, 2017). Teacher learning and changes. The intervention group showed an improved perceived self-efficacy in engaging students in classroom discourse four months after the interventions in comparison with the non-intervention group (Ni, Ho, Shi, & Chen, 2017). More significantly, they demonstrated a reduced tendency to evaluate student responses; they were more likely than the non-intervention group to press students for providing rationale behind their answers and to promote students to engage others' ideas in classroom discussions (Ni, Ho, Shi, Chen, & Cui, 2018; Ni, Shi, Chen, Cheung, Ng, & Cai, under review). Desired teacher changes to influence student learning. Students of the intervention group appeared to respond to the changes in teachers’ discourse behaviors. An intervention effect was found on the amount of student talk in classroom discussions, students’ mathematical reasoning test scores, their perceived interest in learning mathematics, and perceived classroom participation. These results suggest expected changes taking place in the teachers’ discourse practices after the intervention and the changes collectively improved the students’ learning (Ng, Cheng, Ni, & Shi, under review; Ni, Shi, Tam, Cheung, Ng, Cai, under review). Research Outcome Making the field knowledge accessible to local school teachers. The participating teachers including both groups indicated positive influences of the programme on their classroom teaching. Half of the participating teachers were subject panel coordinators in their schools. The coordinators told us that they further disseminated the conceptual and practical tools from the intervention to their school colleagues. Disseminating findings and insights from the project to the research community. One peer-reviewed article was published and three presentations were made at international conferences. Four manuscripts are being submitted to quality journals for consideration. Producing two research tools to the field. A package of booklets for training workshops and a coding scheme to analyze classroom teachers’ discourse behaviors. Providing research training for two undergraduate students. Mr. Chan is now an exchange mathematics teacher in Australia and Ms. Cheung is a Research Assistant in a Hong Kong university.

14620515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14620515.value: It remains a question whether or not the intervention teachers would continuously build ideas on the intervention and improve their classroom discourse practice. It was intended to conduct a following up study with the teachers one year after the intervention to examine a relatively long-term effect of the intervention as it is critical to have such follow-up component in order to produce a high impact intervention study to contribute to the field. Unfortunately, it could not be realized because of resource constraints. To scale up impacts of the research-informed teacher intervention programme, e-learning technologies could be capitalized to make the intervention programme more accessible to schools and teachers. This does not mean merely digitizing the programme but re-designing it with the supports of information technologies to make it pedagogically more powerful. Our study suggests that authority structures in classrooms can be influenced by increased awareness on dialogic classroom discourse. It provides encouraging platform for teacher education programmes and teacher professional development, and complement research on discursive authority. It appears that more research is warranted in exploring the way authority is re-structured by changing teachers' discourse behaviors, across different languages/ cultures.

14620515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14620515.value: To address the central teaching question of how to engage students in dialogical classroom discourse, the current study designed and implemented an intervention programme to assist teachers in developing the conceptual and practical tools required for creating a dialogic classroom for the development of an attitude and skills toward learning and inquiry in children. Results of the study indicate an efficacy of the intervention. The mathematics teachers receiving the intervention of 28 hours over a semester of 4½ months showed an improved self-efficacy in engaging students in classroom four months after the intervention in comparison with the non-intervention group. The intervention teachers were more likely to use the discourse strategies to facilitate students to engage others' ideas during classroom discussions. Also, students of the intervention group showed increased amount of verbal, reasoned contribution in their classroom discourse compared to students of non-intervention group. The changes in students’ contributions suggests a long-term, positive influence of a more dialogic classroom discourse on students’ improved practice in thinking, explaining, and communicating. The findings and outcomes of the study add to the theory and practice on classroom discourse, on effective teacher professional development, and on the assessment of efficacy of a teacher development program.

14621215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14621215.value: In recent years, the internationalization of higher education has become a key policy in Hong Kong. Hong Kong universities have raised their admission quota for non-local undergraduate students to 20%, with the aim of enhancing the internationalization of higher education. Unlike undergraduate programs, there is no quota set for master’s programs. Therefore, master’s programs have emerged as a high potential area for admitting a large number of non-local students. This study aims to investigate the learning experiences of Mainland students enrolled in master’s programs in Hong Kong. This research project will compare the expected and actual learning experiences of Mainland students in the following four areas. First, how Mainland students have adapted to the formal teaching and learning process; Second, how Mainland students have adapted to the informal learning processes involving campus life; Third, how Mainland students have grasped academic conventions as one of their learning outcomes; Fourth, how Mainland students have developed intercultural competence through the process of learning in Hong Kong. Employing a qualitative research method, we will conduct interviews with 60 Mainland students who study in master’s programs at three Hong Kong universities. The three sample universities consist of a first tier comprehensive university, a second tier comprehensive university, and a third tier tertiary institute. The observations of our study will help inform Hong Kong universities how to assist non-local students in adapting to their new environment. This study will have a significant theoretical contribution to the international academic discussion on the learning experiences of non-local students, as well as strong policy implications for the admittance of non-local students and the internationalization of higher education in Hong Kong. 近年來, 高等教育國際化成為香港香港教育發展的主要政策之一. 香港政府計劃把本科生課程招收非本地生的名額提升至20%, 以強化大學教育的國際化水平. 與本科生課程不同的是, 碩士課程並沒有以上的名額限制. 故此, 碩士課程成為一個深具潛質的領域, 可招收更多的非本地生, 其可能面對的問題, 更值得關注. 本研究目的是探討中國內地生入讀香港各大學碩士課程的學習經驗, 志在探討中國內地生在香港就讀碩士課程, 以下四方面的學習經驗: 第一, 內地生如何適應正規教育的教與學過程; 第二, 內地生如何適應大學校園生活的非正式學習過程; 第三, 內地生如何掌握學術基本規範; 第四, 內地生如何透過在香港學習以發展他/她們的多元文化能力. 本研究採質化研究方法, 研究員將訪問共60位在香港就讀碩士課程的內地生. 研究將選取三所香港大學為個案, 其中包括一所第一梯次的知名大學, 一所第二梯次的一般大學, 及一所第三梯次的專上學院. 本研究的觀察, 將有助強化香港各大學了解如何協助非本地生適應新的學習環境. 此外, 本研究將對於非本地生在異地的學習經驗有關的國際學術討論提出相關的理論貢獻, 並就香港高等教育國際化及招收非本地生政策方面, 提出相關的政策建議.

14621215.label: Major findings and research outcome
14621215.value: First, most of our informants perceived that the formal teaching and learning program enlarged their vision. They particularly appreciated that lecturers shared diverse perspectives and cutting edge professional knowledge. Informants from Science and Social Science also emphasized the importance of case studies from various countries to help them have in-depth understanding of academic theories. In the meantime, many students stressed that they learned analytical approaches through the lecturing. However, some who studied Science still did think that, even though they understood teachers were eager to introduce various analytical approaches, their critical thinking was constrained by past learning experiences in Mainland China. Second, due to their previous learning experiences, the very short study period, and the over emphasis on final marks, the mainland Chinese students, no matter whether they studied Science or Social Science, were seldom involved in informal learning through campus activities. Our study observed that receiving high marks was the greatest concern of our informants. They tended to ignore the most precious learning experiences which were those that occur through informal learning in various campus activities because they did not directly lead to receiving a high final grade. However, the activities they ignored may have been the most valuable opportunities to encounter different work norms and approaches in problem solving which would help them develop generic skills. Generic skills are also very important for students’ career development apart from the professional knowledge they learn from their majors. Third, limited interaction with local and foreign students hindered the mainland Chinese students’ development of intercultural competence. Mainland Chinese students in both Science and Social Science chose to stay in small circles that hindered their development of cultural empathy and stifled any tendency to approach social situations in an active way. Instead, they enjoyed the emotional stability of staying with a mainland friend. This could reflect that most students’ open-mindedness and flexibility were not sufficiently developed to reach out in Hong Kong society for new experiences. The exception was the Social Science students, particularly the ones who studied social policy and journalism. They were keen to contact with the local community, as their teachers were very keen to develop students’ attitude to learning more about Hong Kong society. Some teachers even required students to write term assignments using local cases. However, most mainland Chinese students’ limited interaction with the local community led them to have superficial views of Hong Kong society.

14621215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14621215.value: Further studies could investigate the students who stay longer time in Hong Kong. We plan to further our study to investigate the learning experiences of undergraduate students in Hong Kong.

14621215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14621215.value: This study investigated the learning experiences of mainland Chinese students in Master’s degree programmes in Hong Kong. Using a qualitative research approach, 60 mainland Chinese students in Master’s degree programmes in three Hong Kong universities were interviewed. Our study observed that first, mainland Chinese students appreciate the teaching and learning approaches adopted in Hong Kong but they take some time to adapt. The heavy financial support from parents and parental expectations press them to adapt as soon as possible and get high marks in the one-year programmes in Hong Kong. Second, the mainland Chinese students’ previous experiences of participating in campus activities in Mainland China and their instrumental views of learning restrict their involvement in informal learning through campus activities. Third, their limited interaction with local and foreign students constrains the development of their intercultural competence.

14621615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14621615.value: As a major Wu dialect, Shanghainese shares important typological characteristics of Sinitic with other Chinese dialects such as Mandarin and Cantonese, but also exhibits distinctive grammatical features in having a strong degree of topic prominence, characterized by the prevalence of sub-topics; the ability to express definiteness with bare classifier phrases, numeral phrases, as well as bare nouns; and the option of asking yes-no questions with a preverbal interrogative quantifier, in addition to the use of a sentence final question particle and the V-not-V structure. Previous research on Shanghainese grammar has identified some of its salient features when compared to other dialects, but much remains to be understood on how linguistic form maps to meaning and context. Research on the acquisition of Shanghainese has been scanty and has focused exclusively on cross-sectional studies of phonological development. The project will study in further detail the syntax and semantics of topics, nominal structure and interrogatives in Shanghainese from the perspective of parametric variation. It will investigate the early grammatical development of Shanghainese-speaking children, using both longitudinal observations and cross-sectional experiments, aiming to map out the basic milestones in the development of word order and topic structure, classifiers and noun phrases, as well as yes-no questions and wh-questions. It will examine preschoolers’ sensitivity to the markedness status of particular word orders, the (in)definiteness of various types of noun phrases, and the scope of interrogative quantifiers. The study will lead to the construction of the first longitudinal child Shanghainese corpus, and shed light on how distinctive properties of Shanghainese grammar are manifested in early child language, compared with corresponding developments in child Mandarin and child Cantonese. Such a study is urgently called for in view of the fact that research on the acquisition of Shanghainese lags far behind that of other major dialects (for example, Mandarin, Cantonese and Southern Min), and in light of the visible and rapid decline in the vitality of the dialect in recent decades. The study will contribute to our understanding of some general issues in language development, namely, whether topic prominence as a discourse-related property is an early acquired grammatical feature; whether definiteness as encoded by numeral and bare classifier phrases is acquired in a different way than definiteness expressed through determiners; and whether yes-no-questions marked by an adverbial quantifier are more or less accessible than those marked by sentence-final particles or the A-not-A disjunctive form. 作為主要的吳語方言，上海話的語言類型特徵有些與普通話和粵語相同，有些反映本身的特點。其句法結構包括次話題成分，顯示高度的話題優先性；能以量詞-名詞短語、數詞短語和光杆名詞等形式來表達定指；是非問句的形式，除了採用句末疑問助詞和V-否定詞-V外，還使用動詞前疑問量詞。 前人的上海話語法研究，揭示了一些其有別於其他方言的顯著特點，但句法形式如何與語義和語境相聯繫，許多地方仍有待探索。上海話的語言獲得，迄今只有少量關於音系發展的橫向研究。本研究項目從方言參數差異的角度，對上海話的話題結構、名詞短語和疑問形式的句法語義特點作進一步探索。調查上海話兒童的早期語法發展，以追蹤觀察與橫向實驗的方法來探究句子語序、話題結構、量詞、名詞短語、是非問句和特指問句的基本發展里程碑。瞭解學前兒童如何認識不同語序的標記性、各種名詞短語的定指/不定指區別、以及疑問量詞的邏輯轄域。 本研究將建立首個上海早期兒童語言獲得語料庫，揭示上海話語法特徵如何體現在早期兒童語言，並與普通話和粵語的兒童語言發展相比較。上海話近數十年的發展出現急劇衰退，上海話的語言習得研究又落後於其他漢語方言（如普通話、粵語、閩南語），因此本計畫的語言習得調查有一定的迫切性。 研究發現將有助於瞭解兒童語言發展的一些基本問題，例如：與話語有關的話題優先性句型，是否一種早期獲得的語法特徵? 就兒童發展而言，用數詞短語和量詞-名詞組合來表示定指，跟用指示詞來標示定指有何不同？以疑問副詞來進行是非提問，跟用句末助詞或A-否定詞-A形式來作是非問，哪種形式比較容易掌握？

14621615.label: Realisation of objectives
14621615.value: Despite the special circumstances surrounding the final phases of our project (see Attachment #1), we have accomplished our objectives. We have studied the grammar of Shanghainese from the perspective of child language and parametric variation, to understand the extent to which salient properties of the language are reflected in early language development, in an acquisition setting in which the local language is challenged by the standard language. The parametric properties relevant to our inquiry bear on word order, nominal structure, questions and quantification. Word order (Objectives 3 and 4) On the basis of a longitudinal corpus of two male children growing up in Shanghai, consisting of a total of 77 hours of recording, as well as an in-depth cross-dialectal investigation of the acceptability of canonical and non-canonical word orders by adult speakers of Shanghainese, Mandarin and Cantonese, we have arrived at the following conclusions. Our longitudinal data show that before two years of age, Shanghainese-acquiring children show verb argument structures that reflect canonical mappings in line with Universal Grammar, consisting predominantly of the agent role in preverbal position, and the theme role in preverbal or postverbal position; the order is strictly SVO, when both agent and theme are involved. The predominance of SVO order is confirmed in our adult judgment experiment, with subjects favoring SVO order and rejecting SOV order. The distinctiveness of child Shanghainese becomes evident from two years of age, revealed in the use of theme-first sentences with a postverbal resumptive pronoun, and in the diversity of thematic roles permitted in NNV orders, allowing for Agent-Locative, Agent-Theme as well as Theme-Agent sequences for the preverbal nominals. Our data provide psycholinguistic evidence for contexts that are conducive for SOV order, including resultative predicates with aspectual modification, and indefinite objects. On the other hand, the facilitating effect of contrast seems to be minimal. Nominal structure (Objectives 5 and 1) The development of nominals in Shanghainese reveals a pattern that is similar to and different from child Mandarin and child Cantonese in interesting ways. As with child Mandarin and child Cantonese, the earliest nominals in the first few months following the onset of two-word combinations consist exclusively of bare nouns and proper names, with some sporadic use of demonstrative locatives. Classifier-related structures containing demonstratives and numerals, as well as locative particles used singly or in combination with nouns, begin to appear as the child approaches two years of age. Of particular note is the preponderance of a subclass of bare nouns having the structure of [adjective-noun], with the adjective typically the adjectives for ‘small’ or ‘big’, a feature which has not been noted for either child Mandarin or child Cantonese. The use of a demonstrative by itself, or in combination with a noun without the mediation of a classifier, reminds one of child Mandarin but not child Cantonese; on the other hand, the use of [classifier-noun] nominals in subject position aligns child Shanghainese with the latter. The productive use of predicate nominals by Shanghainese-speaking two-year-olds points to yet another distinctive feature of the language. Questions (Objectives 6, 7 and 2) We were interested to see how well Shanghainese-acquiring children understand interrogatives partly because children’s grasp of question forms is an important aspect of their quantificational competence, the question operator being part of the logical apparatus of natural language, and partly because it has been widely reported that some interrogative forms, in particular the prefixal yes-no question has been on the decline and its productivity limited to certain functional verbs. Based on an experiment conducted with Shanghainese-speaking kindergarteners on their understanding of 11 types of questions, we have partially replicated some patterns found in earlier studies, namely, the relative accessibility of who-object questions over who-subject (‘sanin’ 啥人) questions, and the greater difficulty of where-adjunct questions over where-argument questions (‘hhalidak’阿里搭). In addition, how-questions (‘nanen’ 哪能) are found to be much harder than why-questions (‘whesa’ 为啥). Contrary to expectation, all three types of yes-no-questions, namely, the prefixal question (‘ak’-VP, e.g. ), the A-not-A question, and the sentence final particle question (S-‘fha’), proved to be difficult. This may have to do with the decline of the prefixal yes-no question, and the A-not-A questions being less salient than its counterpart in Mandarin, though the poor performance on the sentence final particle question remains a puzzle. It may be conjectured that the availability of three different strategies of questioning for yes-no questions may reduce the salience of any of the interrogative forms. Quantifiers: universal quantifier, additive and restrictive focus (Objectives 7, 6 and 2) As an aspect of linguistic competence relevant to logic and cognition, children’s mastery of quantifiers such as the universal quantifier ‘she’ 侪 (“all”), the additive focus marker ‘hha’ 也 (“also”), and the restrictive focus marker ‘zak’ 只 (“only”) should be an informative indicator of the extent to which children have mastered the functional structure of the language. Our experiment with preschool children demonstrate clearly that they are in perfect command of the universal quantifier even as early as four years of age. Children aged four and five show a strong tendency to use the adverb for “also” in an appropriate context, while six-year-olds readily do so when prompted. In their interpretation of the restrictive focus marker ‘zak’ (“only”), children show considerable difficulty in obtaining the correct interpretation when the focus marker precedes the subject, but have no problem associating ‘zak’ with the correct constituent when it precedes the verb. Our findings corroborate studies of child Mandarin and other child languages in supporting the hypothesis that children associate restrictive focus with the VP by default. The varied pattern of our acquisition findings on interrogatives and quantifiers suggests that children tackle the properties of these logical operators separately, which have individual complexities of their own on top of variation in strategies of quantification in different languages. Code-mixing While code-mixing is not one of the issues addressed, the phenomenon can hardly escape notice in all the data we have collected, in the nominals and clauses used by children, as well as in their responses to questions and instructions in experiments. The hybridity of linguistic structures, evident to different degrees in our two subjects, testifies vividly to the reality of competing grammars when children acquire a local language facing the severe challenge of the standard language, a fact we have ascertained in our sociolinguistic survey of the parents of our experimental subjects.

14621615.label: Major findings and research outcome
14621615.value: Our study on parametric variation in child Shanghainese has produced a longitudinal corpus of two children growing up in Shanghai, observed from around one and a half to two and a half years of age, the first corpus of its kind on a Sinitic language other than Mandarin, Cantonese and Southern Min (P4). The corpus data, along with our experimental findings, have enabled us to clarify a number of issues bearing on the acquisition of word order, question and quantifiers. Our data show that Shanghainese is strictly an SVO language, though it permits of a range of preverbal theme verb-argument structures not commonly found in other child languages. The contexts that facilitate non-canonical SVO order include resultative predicates with aspectual modification and indefinite objects, but not contrast (P1, P5). The early nominal structures in child Shanghainese reveal a common tendency observed for both child Mandarin and child Cantonese, with bare nouns and proper names preceding classifier-related structures. The distinctive aspects of Shanghainese nominals evidenced in child language include the the preponderance of bare nouns having the structure of [adjective-noun], the use of [classifier-noun] nominals in subject position, and the productive use of predicate nominals (P7). With respect to the development of questions, in addition to confirming some well-known patterns of subject-object asymmetry and argument-adjunct differences, our study has demonstrated the marked status of yes-no questions in Shanghainese, possibly arising from the decline of the prefixal yes-no question and the complexity of having three different interrogative structures for this question type (P2). Irrespective of the level of mastery of the language, our subjects show near perfect mastery of the universal quantifier and competent use of the additive focus marker, though their understanding of the domain and scope of the restrictive quantifier reveals a default bias for association with VP, a tendency that has been observed for child Mandarin and other child languages (P6). Our overall findings on children’s mastery of logical operators such as questions and quantifiers suggest that Shanghainese children comprehend the functional core of the language despite the fact that they may exhibit variation in their production of Shanghainese speech (P2, P6). Our study has revealed the complexity of acquiring a major Chinese dialect facing the strong challenge of Standard Mandarin, as reflected in the rich hybrid linguistic structures in child speech due to code-mixing, a natural consequence of language contact (P2, P3).

14621615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14621615.value: Our research has driven home to us the reality of language contact in the context of language acquisition. A challenging topic of research for us would be to probe into the patterns of code mixing and the constraints on it, as well as the status of dialect acquisition in a linguistic milieu dominated by the standard language. In other words, the way we look at acquisition and the issues we address may be different if we look at the acquisition of Shanghainese not as monolingual but as bilingual acquisition, giving due recognition to the reality of ‘universal bilingualism’. Another extension of our project would be to probe into the syntax-phonology interface, given the fact that tone sandhi is subject to highly regular phonological rules in Shanghainese, and the analysis of which parts of an utterance belong to Mandarin, and which parts belong to Shanghainese, often crucially depends on tone sandhi facts. When studying the hybrid linguistic structures of our subjects, we have been attracted to the important interaction between syntax and phonology. An in-depth understanding of Shanghainese phonology would enable us to go further in our research on child Shanghainese.

14621615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14621615.value: In this study of the acquisition of Shanghainese, we examined the command of the language by toddlers and preschool children, with respect to word order, nominal structure, questions and quantifiers, with a view to understanding how child Shanghainese may resemble or differ from child Mandarin and child Cantonese. Our longitudinal and experimental findings show Shanghainese to be a robust Subject-verb-object language, with certain factors facilitating Subject-object-verb order related to aspects of the predicate and object. Early child Shanghainese shows features characteristic of the target language in word order, verb argument frames, and nominal structure. Young children acquiring Shanghainese demonstrate basic competence in their mastery of the logical and quantificational elements of the language, as reflected in their comprehension of various types of wh-questions and yes-no questions, the universal quantifier, the additive focus marker, and the restrictive focus marker. Our study has gained some understanding of the complexity of acquiring a dialect facing the challenge of the standard language, as revealed in children’s exposure to the language, and in the hybrid linguistic structures in child speech due to code-mixing, a natural consequence of language contact.

14630815.label: Project Objectives
14630815.value: We propose a general information propagation model (in which IC and LT models are just special cases) under the CIM problem. This generalization allows researchers and engineers to address wider and more applications. We propose a "Two-phase Competitive Influence Maximization" (TCIM) algorithmic framework which can have a (1-1/e-epsilon)-approximate solution guarantee with probability of at least (1-n^(-l)). More importantly, our framework is computationally efficient and it runs in O(c(l+k)(m+n)log n/epsilon^2), where l is the efficiency control knob of our algorithm, and c depends on specific propagation model, seed-set size k and network G. To validate our solution quality and computational efficiency, we plan to conduct extensive experiments on real-world datasets. For example, on a snapshot of nodes in QQ or WeChat online social networks, which has hundred of million of nodes and trillion of edges. The validation will show the quality of our solution and the scalability of our algorithmic framework.

14630815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14630815.value: 在最近幾年，信息最大化問題越來越大。這個問題是有意義的，因為許多應用可發布的影響最大化框架下，例如，病毒營銷，擴頻，或在因特網或在線社交網絡的流行建模。然而，信息最大化問題本質上是困難的，並應用此框架下，人們必須找到計算上高效的不同算法的應用。本研究的目的是要提供基本原理，以有競爭力的信息最大化（CIM）的問題，其中多個>信息源相互競爭以影響在一個大的網絡用戶。這是比較現實的，但比原來的單一來源問題更具挑戰性。這項研究的目的是發展數學理論和算法框架，競爭信息最大化問題，並運用這個框架進行在大規模網絡病毒式營銷和病毒接種。

Not only we have published some scholarly publications, but more importantly, we had the opportunities to work with some companies and our sponsors, and assisted them to use our framework/algorithms to improve their systems/products.

We were one of the pioneers in carrying out the competitive information modeling and analysis and this creates a wave of follow-up research works by various researchers in the community. It is also interesting that the research is cross-disciplinary for it raises the attention from researchers in the networking, database, and data science communities. 14630915.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14630915.value: 基於信息的“追-逃”博弈中的學習算法

14630915.label: Project Objectives
14630915.value: Single-Pursuer Single-Evader Model under Full or Partial State Observation: Theoretic analysis and simulation study
rows: Single-Pursuer Single-Evader Model under Full or Partial State Observation: Theoretic analysis and simulation study

14630915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14630915.value: Differential games such as pursuit-evasion or automated search have received much interest from the research community since they can be used to model a variety of applications in areas including military operations, economics, finance, robotics and bioengineering. In a pursuit-evasion game, a pursuer tries to capture the evader while the evader tries to evade the pursuer by applying controls on their respective trajectories. These trajectories can be modeled either via a continuous dynamical equation or by means of a connected graph. However, pursuit-evasion games can also be regarded as an information-based control system. This perspective is relevant if the pursuer or evader employs digital electronics to communicate observation data or to actuate control functions. An information-based control model offers a more precise description of such systems, and new research methodologies are required for their solution. It is the objective of this project to develop a methodology for analyzing pursuit-evasion type differential game formulated as multi-agent information-based systems. The new methodology will be developed by merging the powerful learning approach of multi-armed bandit problems with information-based system control techniques. Multi-armed bandit problem was first posed to address sequential resource allocation problems. Indices based on forward induction have proven to be a powerful tool and they can be computed efficiently. A large variety of indices have been proposed in the literature. The bandit problem also provides a natural mechanism via learning for handling uncertainties that arise due to unknown strategies adopted by the opposing agent. To enhance the chance of capturing the evader, it is potentially beneficial to engage a team of cooperating pursuers. Agents organized into swarms, flocks, or platoons have been employed for various applications. Therefore, how to coordinate a team of pursuers in a pursuit-evader game is of theoretical and practical interests. There are two major tasks in this project. The first task is focused on a two-player pursuit-evasion type differential game. We plan to investigate optimal or near-optimal solution for such a game. In the second task, the focus is on games with multiple pursuers and a single evader. For both tasks, we plan to support our analysis with simulations. Results from the project can be applied to search and rescue missions, traffic control, and robotic systems. 微分博弈，例如“追-逃”博弈或自主搜索，廣泛應用於軍事操作、經濟、金融、機器人和生物工程等諸多領域，因此備受研究人員的關注。在“追-逃”博弈中，追捕者試圖捕獲逃逸者，而逃逸者則盡量避免被捕獲。為實現各自的目的， 追逃雙方都利用控制策略來調整自己的運動路徑。通常，這些路徑既可以描述為連續時間的微分方程，也可以表示為一個連通圖。但是，“追-逃”博弈也可以被看作是一個基於信息的控制系統。這樣做的意義在於，如果追捕者或逃逸者利用數字電子設備來傳輸觀測數據或用來執行控制決策，一個基於信息的控制模型可以更精準的描述系統動態，與此同時也需要新的研究方法來解決相關問題。 本項目的主要目標就是要將“追-逃”類型的微分博弈建立為基於信息的多智能體系統，並研究一套新的方法論來對其進行分析。這一新方法論將綜合強大的基於“多臂賭博機”問題的學習算法和基於信息的系統的控制技術。 “多臂賭博機”問題的提出最早是用來解決順序自由分配問題。基於前向歸納的索引已經被證明是一個有效的工具，並且它們可以被高效的計算。對此，文獻中已有大量的研究。當存在對抗智能體採用未知策略時，賭博機問題也提供了通過學習來處理不確定性的自然機制。 在“追-逃”博弈中，追捕者組成一個合作團隊將更有益於增加捕獲機率。多個智能體組成的群組、集群或隊列已經得到了廣泛的應用。因此，如何協調一個追捕者團隊將具有理論和實際上的意義。 本項目擬完成兩個主要任務。第一個任務的重點是二人“追-逃”類型的微分博弈， 我們計劃研究其最優或擬最優解。第二個任務重點研究多追捕者與一個逃逸者的博弈問題。兩個任務都計劃用仿真實驗來支持得到的分析結果。本項目的研究成果可用於搜索或營救任務、交通控制、機器人系統等領域。

14630915.label: Realisation of objectives
14630915.value: This project aims to study how learning algorithms can be applied to a class of differential games as exemplified by the pursuer-evader model with multiple modes of pursuit that is defined in the proposal. Good progress was made in this study over the project duration and we believe all the proposed objectives have been realized. In terms of publication results, five journal papers have been produced, four of which have already been published and one is being under review. Moreover, a PhD candidate from the Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences visited the PI’s research laboratory and participated in the project for over a year. He successfully finished his doctoral degree. At the beginning of the project, we studied the research task using a Gittins Index approach as explained in the proposal. It is well known that optimality of the Gittins Index solution usually does not hold beyond the cases that satisfy the classical assumptions; for example, it usually does not hold for cases where there is dependency among different policy arms. For the pursuer-evader problem, different arms represent different pursuing strategies adopted by the pursuer, so there is obvious dependency among different policy arms. Hence, the task objective focuses on constructing efficient Gittins Index based policies and understanding their performance as a heuristic. This goal has been achieved and we have found that Gittins Index based algorithm can significantly outperform random policies in which the pursuer chooses the mode of pursuit randomly without learning. Due to practical considerations, it is of interest to consider systems in which the pursuit control is subject to communication delays and possibility of packet dropout. In other words, the control decisions are based on prior evader positions and there is a probability that control actions may be absent or modified. A class of linear quadratic control optimization problems with control delays and noisy gain was studied and connection to the pursuit-evasion problem was clarified in this project. Moreover, both discrete time and continuous time models were analyzed. Results obtained for the two cases had been summarized in two separate papers. Both of them have been published, and one of them in the IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics. Due to unknown parameter values, how to derive the optimal control policy for the pursuit-evasion problem with multiple modes of pursuit is unknown. Therefore, in the later part of the project, we searched for other viable solution approaches using techniques from online optimization. We found that regret analysis provides a promising alternative. The regret function provides a measure of how the performance of a control policy differs from optimality. We designed a learning based control policy for the pursuit-evasion problem and carried out a detailed regret analysis of it. We showed that the regret of the accumulated cost has a sublinear growth rate with respect to time. In fact, for the model we studied, the growth rate is bounded by O(ln T), where T is the optimization time duration. This is an interesting result, since among other things, it implies that the learning based algorithm converges to the optimal policy that can be obtained when all system parameters are known. A paper summarizing the new results has been submitted for publication. During the project, one of the PhD students of the PI worked on related online optimization techniques. Interesting results were obtained and a corresponding paper was accepted by a prestigious ACM conference and published in its associated journal venue. The student finished his study and received his PhD degree from the Chinese University of Hong Kong. All these results show that learning based techniques, especially online techniques such as regret analysis, can be well applied to the pursuit-evasion problems we considered. We believe these techniques can be further extended to more general control optimization problems, such as product pricing problems and multi-agent systems. We are convinced the research work investigated in this project is just a beginning. There would be many new exciting ideas built on top of our current results that are worthy of further exploration.

14630915.label: Major findings and research outcome
14630915.value: We studied a Gittins Index based solution to the pursuit-evasion problem and showed that it can outperform random based solutions in which the pursuer chooses the mode of pursuit randomly. Key results obtained for this task are summarized in a journal paper. The original title of the paper was, “Control Policy based on Inductive Learning for a Class of Pursuit- Evasion Problems.” It was subsequently changed to “Gittins Index based Control Policy for a Class of Pursuit-Evasion Problems” and was published. In a second paper, “On Delay-Dependent Algebraic Riccati Equation,” we investigated the linear quadratic optimization and stabilization of a discrete time networked control problem with a fixed control delay and possibility of packet dropouts. General stabilization conditions were obtained in relation to a delay-dependent algebraic Riccati equation. Connection to the pursuit-evasion problem was highlighted as an important application example. We further extended the above study to continuous time models. The paper entitled, “Delay-Dependent Algebraic Riccati Equation to Stabilization of Networked Control Systems: Continuous-Time Case” was published in the IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics. We took a second approach to the pursuit-evasion problem by adopting an online learning technique. By combining learning ideas, dynamic programming and linear mean square biased estimate techniques, we derived a new online feedback control policy. We performed a detailed regret analysis of the new policy and showed that the regret of its accumulated performance has a sublinear growth bounded by O(lnT), where T is the optimization time horizon. Related results were summarized in a paper, “Learning Based Control Policy and Regret Analysis for Online Quadratic Optimization with Asymmetric Information Structure”. The paper has been submitted for publication. As part of our study of online optimization techniques, one of my PhD students published a paper in the associated journal of the ACM SIGMETRICS.

14630915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14630915.value: The analytic techniques obtained in this project can be extended to other dynamic control models other than pursuit-evasion. We believe regret analysis is a promising approach that can introduce learning-algorithm capability to many control optimization problems, such as product pricing, where some of the system parameters are unknown or subject to changes. This provides a promising direction of future research. Another research direction is to generalize the parameter learning ideas in our time-delayed network control model to handle multiple dynamic systems. However, we expect the technical challenges will not be easy to overcome for this research direction.

14630915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14630915.value: Many practical engineering problems contain unknown or time changing parameters. Some examples include the pursuit-evasion games in which a pursuer tries to maximize its chance of capturing the evader by using different pursuit modes and optimal pursue trajectories. As different pursuit mode solicits different types of evader responses, the pursuer needs to learn from the behaviour of the evader. In this study, we analysis how a pursuer can learn from evader responses to design good pursuing strategies to improve the chance of capture. Results obtained in this project are not restricted to this class of problems and can be extended to other application scenarios, such as product pricing.

15100115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15100115.value: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) causes a wide scope of human infections that range from mild skin diseases to potentially fatal pneumonia. Currently, more than two-thirds of clinical Staphylococcus aureus strains are resistant to multiple β-lactam antibiotics, prompting an intense search for alternative therapeutic agents with anti-MRSA effects. On the basis of recent findings reported in the literature and preliminary data generated in our laboratory, we plan to devise a new anti-MRSA approach by generating a novel series of inhibitors that target the bacterial cell division protein FtsZ, with potential synergistic effects on suppression of bacterial cell division activities when orally co-administered with β-lactam antibiotics. This work aims at optimizing the inhibitory functions and bioavailability of FtsZ inhibitors through structural modification of specific lead compounds generated in our preliminary works. The feasibility of administering such inhibitors and β-lactam antibiotics in combination to revitalize the antimicrobial effects of commonly used drug on clinically resistant organisms will be assessed, using MRSA as the test organism, followed by comprehensive evaluation of the cytotoxicity, resistance induction potential and pharmacokinetic properties of selected compounds. Deliverables of this project shall validate the feasibility of a new antimicrobial concept in which new agents that inhibit vital cellular functions in bacteria may restore antimicrobial properties of conventional antibiotics or even confer novel antimicrobial and anti-resistance effects. 耐甲氧西林金黃色葡萄球菌能夠導致人類感染各種皮膚疾病甚至致命性肺炎。近年來，臨床上超過三分之二的金黃色葡糖球菌能夠抵抗絕大多數β-內酰胺類抗生素，從而研發出抑制耐甲氧西林金黃色葡萄球菌的新型抗生素變的越來越來迫切。在近期研究工作的基礎上，我們設計出了一種新型殺死耐甲氧西林金黃色葡萄球菌的方法，通過合成出新型靶向作用於細菌細胞分裂酶FtsZ的抑製劑，並且與β-內酰胺類抗生素聯合口服用藥，從而產生協同作用。這項研究在前期先導化合物的基礎上，進一步結構優化以期能夠增強化合物的抑制FtsZ活性並且提高其生物利用度。我們將化合物與β-內酰胺類抗生素進行聯合用藥來評價其對臨床上耐甲氧西林金黃色葡萄球菌的殺菌作用，並進一步檢測其細胞毒性，潛在的細菌對其耐藥性的誘導以及藥代動力學研究。 此項研究意義在於研製出FtsZ的高效無毒抑製劑，並通過與β-內酰胺類抗生素的聯合用藥，產生協同作用，以期恢復傳統抗生素對耐藥菌的致死作用。

15100115.label: Realisation of objectives
15100115.value: The rapid emergence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) strains has undermined the therapeutic efficacy of existing β-lactam antibiotics (BLAs), prompting an urgent need to discover novel BLAs adjuvants that can potentiate their anti-MRSA activities. In this project, a focused compound library of 3-aminobenzamides and structurally related derivatives has been designed and synthesized for evaluation of their antibacterial and cytotoxic activities against bacterial cells and normal cells. These compounds were easily obtained in 3 to 4 synthetic steps by coupling of various commercially available building blocks with 3-aminobenzamides or 3-aminobenzonitrile, allowing rapid construction of the compound library for SAR analysis. In particular, cytotoxicity and antibacterial screening of a focused compound library enabled us to identify a compound, which exhibited low cytotoxicity against normal cells and robust in vitro bactericidal synergy with different classes of BLAs against a panel of multidrug-resistant clinical MRSA isolates. A series of biochemical assays and microscopic studies have revealed that this compound is likely to interact with the S. aureus FtsZ protein at the T7-loop binding pocket and inhibit polymerization of FtsZ protein without interfering with its GTPase activity, resulting in extensive delocalization of Z-ring and morphological changes characterized by significant enlargement of the bacterial cell. Animal studies demonstrated that this compound had a favorable pharmacokinetic profile and exhibited potent synergistic efficacy with cefuroxime antibiotic in a murine systemic infection model of MRSA. Overall, the lead compound represents a promising lead of FtsZ inhibitor for further development of efficacious BLAs adjuvants to treat the staphylococcal infection.

15100115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15100115.value: Our efforts have yielded a compound, which exhibits low cytotoxicity against normal cells and robust in vitro bactericidal synergy with different classes of BLAs against a panel of multidrug-resistant clinical MRSA isolates with FIC index as low as 0.1. Further target identification and mechanistic studies employing a series of genetic study, computational docking, biochemical assays and microscopic studies have revealed that this compound is likely to interact with the S. aureus FtsZ protein at the T7-loop binding pocket and inhibit the polymerization of FtsZ protein without interfering its GTPase activity, causing the subsequent extensive delocalization of Z-ring and enlarged morphological changes in S. aureus. Animal studies demonstrated that this compound has a favorable PK profile in rat and exhibits potent synergistic efficacy with cefuroxime antibiotic in a murine systemic infection model of MRSA, protecting infected mice with a 100% survival rate. Taken together, our findings indicated that this compound may serve a lead suitable for structural optimization into a BLA combination agent for the treatment of staphylococcal infection.

15101415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15101415.value: Corneal reshaping (also called orthokeratology) is a non-surgical method for temporarily reducing shortsightedness. This treatment requires the patient to wear specially designed rigid contact lenses at night time. Subsequently, if complete myopia reduction is achieved and after stabilization of treatment, wearers will have clear vision at distance during day time without optical correction. Recent studies have found that corneal reshaping is effective in reducing the progression of shortsightedness in children. Most of these lens wearers were children who to their optometrists by their parents. Parents worry that, without intervention, their children would develop substantial shortsightedness, which is associated with serious ocular complications such as retinal degeneration and glaucoma. Corneal reshaping reduces shortsightedness by changing the corneal curvature. The treatment range is limited to moderate shortsightedness and astigmatism. However, some patients may not experience desirable results even if they have less than moderate shortsightedness. Some patients may have a slow treatment response after wearing the lenses. It may be the corneal biomechanical properties hindering the corneal reshaping. Unfortunately, no effective and reliable method for measuring corneal biomechanics exists. A group of biomedical engineers has recently invented a device for measuring corneal biomechanical properties. The effectiveness of the device has been validated. This study is a collaboration between corneal reshaping specialists and biomechanical engineering specialists. The aim of the proposed study is to investigate the predictive value of corneal biomechanical properties in corneal reshaping therapy and the role of these parameters in determining the amount of myopia reduction. This information will be useful to corneal reshaping practitioners for predicting the efficacy of treatment. Patients who have corneas that are difficult to reshape, resulting in poor shortsightedness reduction effect, can be advised to seek other treatment modalities earlier. 角膜塑型術是以非手術方式短暫減低近視。患者需於晚間佩戴特製硬性隱形眼鏡，成功佩戴者於日間無需佩戴眼鏡而能夠享受清澈的視力。最新的研究發現角膜塑型術有効減低兒童近視的增加。基於家長們擔心他們的孩子長遠會患上與深近視有關的眼疾，如視網膜退化及青光眼，現時大多數佩戴者也是兒童。 角膜塑型術以改變角膜曲率用以減低近視，此技術限制於中度近視及散光，但仍有輕度近視患者未能達至理想效果，這可能礙於角膜曲率的改變受制於角膜的生物力學，可惜迄今仍未有可靠及有效的方法測量角膜的生物力學。 我們最近與一群生物力學工程師成功認證了一部新儀器用以測量角膜的生物力學。這研究在於應用此儀器於角膜塑型術上，希望有助探索角膜塑型術如何改變角膜的生物力學。若果發現某些角膜因為其生物力學的參數而未能以角膜塑型術有效減低近視，眼科視光師可及早建議家長採用其它減低近視增加的方法。

15101415.label: Realisation of objectives
15101415.value: This project has three objectives. 1. To measure the changes of corneal biomechanical properties (corneal tangent modulus) from short-term wearing of corneal reshaping lenses (randomized, case-control study) 2. To monitor the changes of corneal biomechanics from long-term (6 months) successful corneal reshaping 3. To determine if corneal biomechanics is predictive of the rate of corneal reshaping Two experiments were conducted, a short-term randomized corneal reshaping study (for objective 1), and a long-term corneal reshaping study (for objectives 2 and 3). A part-time Research Associate was employed in Jan 2016, who changed to be a full-time Research Associate from Sep 2016. This Research Associate worked on the two experiments simultaneously. There is no deviation from the original plan. We finished the short-term study within the first year (objective 1 was 100% achieved). We completed the long-term study and achieved 100% of objectives 2 and 3 upon completion of this project. In the short-term study, 16 subjects with refractive errors between –4D to –5D sphere and astigmatism within –1.50D were recruited. One randomly selected eye wore orthokeratology lens (treatment), and the fellow eye wore conventional rigid gas permeable lens (control). Lenses were worn for 30 and 60 minutes and one night separately with a week of washout period in between. The first two visits were randomly scheduled and before the overnight wear. Eyes were kept closed during all the lens wearing periods. Corneal radius, thickness, and biomechanics (corneal hysteresis (CH), corneal resistance factor (CRF), corneal tangent modulus) were compared between eyes prior to each visit, and then before and after lens wear. Corneal parameters were similar in each visit before lens wear. Significant corneal flattening was observed in the treatment eyes, and corneal flattening increased with wearing time. Control eyes showed no significant corneal curvature changes. CRF reduced by 0.42mmHg (+/- 0.68mmHg) after 30 minutes of orthokeratology treatment. CH reduced by 0.42mmHg (+/- 0.63mmHg) in control eyes from overnight wear. Both eyes showed stable tangent modulus, E, throughout the study. A lower CH (r = 0.51, p = 0.046) and a higher E (r = 0.53, p = 0.037) at baseline was significantly associated with greater corneal flattening along the flattest meridian in treatment eyes. We found that short-term orthokeratology had no significant effect on corneal tangent modulus. Changes in CH and CRF could be related to intrinsic measurement variability of these corneal biomechanics metrics. Corneal tangent modulus provided another measure of corneal biomechanics. In the long-term study, 275 subjects were screened for eligibility to participate in the study. Inclusion criteria were age between 18 and 30 years, myopia between –4D to –5D sphere and with-the-rule astigmatism within –1.50D. In addition, differences in refractive errors for both the sphere and astigmatic components of the two eyes were required to be within 1.00D. With stringent criteria to eliminate confounding factors in corneal biomechanics, such as age and myopia, 55 subjects were eligible and fitted with orthokeratology lenses, of whom 37 completed the 6-month wearing period. Subjects with poor orthokeratology responses (14 subjects who discontinued the study) had lower corneal tangent modulus (mean 0.474MPa) than subjects with good orthokeratology responses (mean 0.536MPa). These two groups shared similar CH, CRF, and corneal stiffness. Subjects who discontinued the study had significantly flatter keratometry results along the steepest and flattest meridians, but had similar asphericity along the steepest and flattest meridians. Subjects who had 6-month successful orthokeratology had CH reduced by 5.8% and CRF reduced by 8.7%. This finding was similar to previous studies. Corneal stiffness was stable, but corneal tangent modulus showed an increasing trend. In subjects who had successful overnight orthokeratology, their baseline corneal stiffness had a weak but significant association with myopia reduction. Corneal biomechanics metrics were also measured one month after cessation of orthokeratology. Although CH and CRF demonstrated significant decrease from overnight orthokeratology, CH returned to baseline level eventually. However, CRF was still lower than baseline one month after cessation of lens wear. Corneal tangent modulus returned to baseline level, and hence, it was a relatively stable corneal biomechanics parameter from overnight orthokeratology. To conclude, intrinsic corneal tissue properties together with corneal curvature contribute to successful overnight orthokeratology. A cornea with a flat corneal curvature together with an unusually low tangent modulus may not respond well to myopic orthokeratology. This finding could be useful to orthokeratology practitioners to decide should orthokeratology be offered. Eye with a higher baseline corneal stiffness may have a greater myopia reduction from orthokeratology.

15101415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15101415.value: We found that short-term orthokeratology had no significant effect on corneal tangent modulus. Although there were reduction in corneal hysteresis (CH) and corneal resistance factor (CRF), their changes could be related to intrinsic measurement variability of these corneal biomechanics metrics. Corneal tangent modulus provided another measure of corneal biomechanics. Corneal biomechanical properties together with corneal curvature contributed to successful overnight orthokeratology. Six-month orthokeratology resulted in CH reduction by 5.8% and CRF reduction by 8.7%. Corneal stiffness was stable, but corneal tangent modulus showed an increasing trend in long-term orthokeratology. After cessation of orthokeratology for one month, CH returned to baseline level but CRF was still at a lower value. Corneal tangent modulus returned to baseline level, and hence, apparently it has not long term effect. A cornea with a flat corneal curvature together with an unusually low tangent modulus may not respond well to myopic orthokeratology. Eye with a higher baseline corneal stiffness may have a greater myopia reduction from orthokeratology. This finding could be useful to orthokeratology practitioners to decide should orthokeratology be offered.

15101415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15101415.value: There are very few clinical methods to measure corneal biomechanics, while each of them accompanies with its specific metrics. This project covered corneal hysteresis, corneal resistance factor, corneal stiffness and tangent modulus. There should be no single parameter which can describe corneal biomechanics comprehensively. Corneal hysteresis and corneal resistance factor have advantages including non-invasive measurement modality and abundant literature support. Corneal stiffness and tangent modulus through corneal indentation might better describe intrinsic physical properties of corneal tissue. Unfortunately, it requires physical contact through topical anesthesia. This may bear concern to eye care practitioners for using it in children. Currently a non-invasive method using ultra-high-speed Scheimpflug camera to capture corneal deformation during air puff deflection becomes popular. An advantage of this technology is its non-invasive nature and hence can be applied in children. Since orthokeratology is a proven intervention to reduce myopia progression. It is commonly applied in children nowadays. Further studies about association between orthokeratology and corneal biomechanics should include this corneal visualization Scheimpflug technology.

15101415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15101415.value: There are limited evidence based interventions to successfully reduce myopia progression. Corneal reshaping therapy, or orthokeratology, is one of them. Subjects are required to wear specially design rigid lenses for sleep to change the corneal shape. Corneal biomechanics may have influence on the effectiveness of corneal shaping through orthokeratology. In this 6-month orthokeratology, we demonstrated a few corneal parameters which might enhance successful myopia reduction in orthokeratology. Adult subjects were involved in this study. Future studies should include children, and other more newly development clinical method, when studying association between corneal biomechanics and orthokeratology. This is important to eye care practitioners so they could offer orthokeratology to subjects who have good potential to successful orthokeratology. Subjects who may not respond well to orthokeratology can be advised to try other evidence based interventions for myopia control.

15102015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15102015.value: Myopia (shortsightedness) is regarded as the most common refractive error. Both the prevalence and severity of myopia are sustainably growing worldwide. Recent research has revealed that myopia now affects almost 33% of adults in the United States, and epidemic proportions of 85% to 90% adults in Asian cities. It is a not just a refractive problem when an eye grows too long for its focus, myopia can actually lead to many sight-threatening ocular complications which are not prevented by optical corrections. In fact, myopic retinal degeneration is one of the leading causes of blindness in Hong Kong. As the myopic population continues to rise, it is feared that the number of visual impairments will escalate drastically. Despite of decades’ clinical and animal studies, evidence–based methods for prevention or arrest of this disorder remain hampered by the lack of clear knowledge of the pathogenesis of this disease. Recent technological revolution in mass spectrometric (MS) based proteomics have paved the way for rapid evaluation of potential biomarkers as well as enhancing our knowledge in many diseases for both diagnostic and therapeutic purposes. By comparing changes between normal and myopic tissues, key biochemical pathways and protein modifications (PTMs) in myopia may be revealed. However, the application of this novel and powerful proteomic approach has not gained popularized in myopia research. Also, there is still no published data on the possible protein phosphorylation involved in myopia. Retina is known as the key ocular tissue which detects and decodes visual cues in the regulation of the myopic eye growth. By applying traditional proteomic technique using top-down two-dimensional gel electrophoresis, we were the first group to profile chick retinal proteome and identified multiple proteins which could be involved in the postnatal eye growth. Using a more advanced DIGE approach, we demonstrated, for the first time, a number of novel candidate proteins which were differentially expressed in the myopic retina in both the classic chick model and a mammalian guinea pig model. The present proposal aims to apply more sensitive ‘Next-generation’ gel-free proteomic approach to investigate the myopic proteome as well as phosphoproteome in the guinea pig retina in response to the myopic growth. The discovery will shed important light in the understanding of robust biochemical pathways that regulate the elongation of eyeball across different species. The candidate proteins and pathways unrevealed in the study could provide novel therapeutic approaches for combating this global epidemic.

15102915.label: Project Objectives
15102915.value: To improve the cognitive functions (attention, memory, executive functions), vocational outcomes (work self-efficacy and employment study) and psychological functions of first-episode schizophrenic patients through an artificial intelligent and virtual reality-based training system (IVR). To investigate if there is any significant differences between IVR and a computer games control group (CG) as indicated by their respective cognitive performance, vocational outcomes and psychological functions during pre-test, post-test, 3-month and 6-month follow up.
rows: To improve the cognitive functions (attention, memory, executive functions), vocational outcomes (work self-efficacy and employment study) and psychological functions of first-episode schizophrenic patients through an artificial intelligent and virtual reality-based training system (IVR).

To investigate if there is any significant differences between IVR and a computer games control group (CG) as indicated by their respective cognitive performance, vocational outcomes and psychological functions during pre-test, post-test, 3-month and 6-month follow up.

15102915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15102915.value: Cognitive impairment has been identified in persons with schizophrenia, apart from widely recognized emotional and behavioural problems. The cognitive deficits might slow down rehabilitation progress including work resettlement. The present study tests an artificial intelligent, virtual reality-based (IVR) training programme in reducing the effect of cognitive impairments in first-episode schizophrenia (FES), and explore its effectiveness to improve specific cognitive skills (attention, memory and executive functions) which are important attributes to work rehabilitation outcomes and ultimately their chance of employability. Thus this project will recruit FES patients to receive a 6-week, 15-session cognitive training programme targets at attention, memory and executive skills. A fast food shop is used as a virtual environment (VE) to serve as both a cognitive and job training scenario. The training components will be loaded with designated cognitive skills training and delivered according to built-in artificial intelligence to fit users’ learning pace and learning needs. It is proposed that such an innovative cognitive training may have added values by customizing training content and pacing to a patient’s cognitive level and learning speed, minimizing sense of failures, fatigue and demotivation. It is also assumed that better cognitive outcomes may lead to better vocational outcomes as reflected by employability. A total of 140 participants will be randomly assigned to one of the two groups, namely IVRG (n=70) for targeted training components, and a computer games control group (CG, n=70) to control for possible computer exposure and contract with research personnel. Participants’ cognitive performances will be evaluated by primary outcome using MATRICS Consensus Cognitive Battery (MCCB) which is an international recognized, standardized assessment for clinical trial in schizophrenia study. Other outcomes include Wisconsin Card Sort Test (WCST), Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS), Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HRSD-24), and self-report instruments (employment status, self-efficacy in work performance). These tests will be completed at baseline, post-training, during 3-, 6-month follow up. It is anticipated that participants in the IVRG will perform better in cognitive abilities and emotional stability, work self-efficacy and employability than those in CG. This study may be the first of this kind in studying artificial intelligence in a VR platform in first-episode schizophrenia. This marks an important step in rehabilitation development and contributing towards theory-building by provision of initial proven evidences for enhancing cognitive strategy and better vocational outcomes in schizophrenia. More low cost, highly effective computerized, cognitive training modules for different job types can thus be deployed.

15102915.label: Realisation of objectives
15102915.value: The project has achieved all the objectives in demonstrating that first-episode schizophrenia is responsive to IVR training. IVR has selective cognitive improvement in attention, working memory, problem solving and executive functions which have been documented to be major limiting factors for successful rehabilitation and functional recovery such as independence and work-ability. Though online computer games applied to OGCG have also therapeutic effects on cognitive processing speed and attention, the effect was not as large as IVR. Moreover, the carryover effect was demonstrated in IVR and not in OGCG.

Further study of its applications to other psychiatric conditions such as bipolar disorder or depression is worthy exploring.

15102915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15102915.value: Artificial intelligent, virtual reality-based cognitive training system (IVR) have been developed to enhance the cognitive abilities in individuals with first-episode schizophrenia (FES). This study evaluated IVR as an intervention tool for enhancing cognitive outcomes in 142 IES randomly assigned to a IVR group and an online cognitive game group (OGCG). IVR adopts a virtual environment using a virtual convenience shop as a training scenario while OGCG played cognitive games through an online platform. Outcome assessments comprised the MATRICS Consensus Cognitive Battery (MCCB), Wisconsin Card Sort Test (WEST), Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS) and self-efficacy scale pre-, posttest and during 3-month follow-up. The IVR exhibited significant improvement in attention, working memory, executive and social cognition. Better carryover effect was found in IVR than OGCG during follow up. IVR training might target cognitive problems in FES.
