15103315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15103315.value: Myopia or shortsightedness is so prevalent that it affects over 80% of our young adult population in Hong Kong and many Asian cities. It is not a trivial matter as high myopia is known to associate with a number of blinding diseases, such as glaucoma and retinal degenerations. With increasing population of high myopia, the number of these blinding diseases will predictably increase dramatically with time. However, exactly how and why myopia can lead to these blinding diseases is not known. Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide. It is frequently characterized by an elevated intra-ocular pressure (IOP) and typical vision loss. The IOP is dynamically maintained by the production and draining of an intraocular fluid called the aqueous humour. The elevated IOP in glaucoma is thought to due to the blockage of drainage system so that the aqueous humour finds it hard to leave the eye. As a result, the pressure inside the eye builds up which causes retinal damages and impairs vision. Clinically, myopes are as much as 8 times more at risk of glaucoma than non-myopes. In addition, the amount of myopia has been positively correlated with the IOP in human. It is hypothesized that as the eye grows excessively large as in myopia, there are pathological changes at the drainage system that slow down the outflow of the aqueous humour. The present study employs guinea pigs as a mammalian myopia model. These animals are made myopic by wearing diffuser lenses which allow only light perception without clear vision. We propose to study the relationship between myopia and outflow facility of the eye. We ask, firstly, if myopia per se causes an increase in outflow resistance of aqueous humour. We will correlate the amount of myopia with outflow facility in young animals where myopia is developing. Secondly, we ask if myopia predisposes the drainage system to blockage in adulthood. We will study the outflow facility in well-established myopic animals with time and examine if its resistance increases with age. The results will shed important light on whether myopia induces glaucomatous changes directly or indirectly or both. It may also help focus future research effort in deciphering the pathogenesis of glaucoma due to myopia, and provide a platform for research that may lead to better treatment for glaucoma. 近視是一種非常普遍的視力問題，在香港及許多亞洲地市超過八成的年輕人患有近視。而高度近視容易引發如青光眼及視網膜退化等可以引致失明的疾病，因此近視並不能輕視。隨著高度近視的人口不斷增長，患有致盲眼疾的病人數目亦會相應地顯著上升。儘管近視問題帶來的後果已是預計之中，近視導致相關疾病的原因及方式卻是未知之數。 青光眼是全球導致永久失明的主要原因，典型病徵包括眼內壓（IOP）上升及視力缺損。眼壓是由一種稱為房水的眼內液體的形成及排水的流動所產生。而青光眼的高眼壓普遍被認為是由於排水系統堵塞，令房水積存眼內所形成的壓力，當眼壓升高，就有可能損害視網膜，並造成視力缺損。臨床研究發現近視人士比非近視人士患上青光眼的風險高達八倍。此外，近視深淺與人的眼壓在數據上呈正比的關係，故有假設指若如近視患者一般，眼球生長過長，有可能引致眼內排水系統病理性改變，減慢房水的排放，令眼壓上升。 本研究利用天竺鼠作為哺乳類動物近視模型，為它們戴上擴散鏡片，使其視力模糊，僅能感光，產生類同近視的效果，從而研究近視與眼睛排水能力的關係。研究首要重點是年幼期動物在近視發展過程中近視加深的程度與眼睛排水能力的相互關係。其次是從近視發展成熟的動物探討其眼睛排水系統的阻力有否隨年歲增長，藉以研究近視導致動物成年期時眼睛排水系統堵塞的傾向性。整個研究所得的結論—近視會否直接或間接引發青光眼性變化，意義重大，不但引領未來近視併發成青光眼的研究，更成為研發成效更佳的青光眼治療的依據。

15103315.label: Realisation of objectives
15103315.value: Objective 1 In order to measure the ocular parameters of guinea pigs, we have set up a high-resolution ultrasound A-scan system, with essential modifications of the measuring probe and software. In our original proposal, we planned to induce myopia in pigmented guinea pigs. However, we have encountered a problem of the supply of pigmented guinea pigs in Hong Kong. Animal facilities of other Hong Kong institutions have no supply of pigmented guinea pigs and the attempt of importing pigmented guinea pigs to Hong Kong from China was unsuccessful due to insurmountable import restrictions. As an alternative plan, we employed albino guinea pigs for myopia model which are readily available in Hong Kong. We successfully induced myopia in albino guinea pigs using form deprivation. A translucent plastic diffuser goggle with visible light transmission of 30% was mounted on Velcro rings and attached to the guinea pigs’ eyes. The diffusers were checked every day to ensure secure attachment during the form deprivation. The diffusers were attached for 2 to 5 weeks in order to generate a developing myopic guinea pigs. We have also set up a perfusion system for measuring the outflow facility of guinea pig’s eyes in Hong Kong, using either constant pressure or constant flow method. The setup was modified and optimized according to similar facility in mice because of the different in the eye size of animals. A system for measuring outflow facilities in guinea pigs was successfully established for the first time. Refractive errors (Rx), ocular parameters and intraocular pressure (IOP) were monitored every two weeks throughout the treatment. Animals were sacrificed at the end of the lens treatment and both eyes were enucleated and perfused immediately for measurement of outflow facility using constant flow method. Moderate myopia was induced in guinea pigs after short-term (2 to 5 weeks) form deprivation (i.e. form deprivation myopia, FDM). The treated eyes were significantly more myopic (change in Rx relative to baseline: treated vs control: -3.64±2.82D vs 0.10±2.08D, P<0.05, n=20) and larger (change in axial length relative to baseline: treated vs control: 0.82±0.18mm vs 0.66±0.17mm, P<0.05, n=20) than the control eyes. The amount of myopia showed no significant correlation with ocular parameters, IOP or outflow facility (C). However, the natural ocular size of treated eye was significantly correlated with outflow facility (axial length vs C: r= -0.45, P= 0.04; anterior chamber depth vs C: r= -0.52, P=0.02, n=20), but not with IOP. A strong and significant correlation between IOP and outflow facility (IOP vs C: r= -0.52, P=0.02, n=20) was also observed in the treated eye with short-term FDM. Natural ocular size of control eye also showed a strong and significant correlation between anterior chamber depth and outflow facility (ACD vs C: r= -0.57, P=0.01, n=20), indicating that outflow facility was related with natural ocular size, rather than myopia. This objective has been achieved completely. Objective 2 In order to study the effect of high myopia on outflow facilities in guinea pigs, we have induced form deprivation for a longer period of time. The diffusers were worn for 6 to 8 weeks in one eye while the other eyes were untreated as control. At protracted (6 to 8 weeks) FDM, moderate myopia (change in Rx: -3.70±4.79D, P<0.05, n=14) was also induced. The treated eyes were significantly more myopic (change in Rx relative to baseline: treated vs control: -6.72±5.01D vs -3.02±2.73D, P<0.05, n=14) and the proportion of guinea pigs (29%) with high myopia (ΔRx<-6D) were higher than those with short-term FDM (15%). However, the refractive errors remained moderate only even after protracted deprivation. The underlying reason could be due to the varied susceptibility towards diffusers in albino guinea pigs. Moreover, yoking effect between two eyes might also be a reason. The interocular yoking effect was more obvious for the protracted period of FDM (Rx: treated for protracted FDM vs. control: -6.72±5.01D vs -3.02±2.73D vs. Rx: treated for shorter period of FDM vs. control: -3.64±2.82D vs 0.10±2.08D, P<0.05, n=20). We tried to protract the duration of FDM for more than 8 weeks so as to induce the higher magnitude of myopia. However, the diffusers were pulled off quite frequently by the guinea pigs as they got bigger and stronger. The amount of myopia showed strong and significant correlations with eye growth (ΔRx vs Δ axial length: r=-0.64, P=0.01; ΔRx vs Δ vitreous chamber depth: r= -0.58, P=0.03, n=14), but not with IOP or outflow facility. Outflow facility showed no significant correlation with natural ocular size of both treated and control eyes while IOP showed a strong and significant correlation with axial length in control eye (axial length vs IOP: r= 0.57, P=0.03, n=14). This objective has also been achieved completely. Attempts to overcome challenges The outcomes of the project have been hampered by a number of unexpected issues and happenings. It sets us back not only in the progress of the experiments but also the publication of the results. The first problem was the availability of pigmented guinea pigs. After we found out that animal facilities of Hong Kong no long provided pigmented guinea pigs, we worked to import pigmented guinea pigs from China which seemed promising in the beginning. However, it took us months to realise that the import policy was extremely complicated and difficult. It proved to be insurmountable in the end. Therefore, we started to look to albino guinea pigs instead as an animal myopia model. However, the responsiveness of the albino animals towards myopia induction was very variable and that many more sets of experiments are required to produce sufficiently sample number for analysis. This issue has not only delayed the setting up of myopia model but also greatly prolonged the time of data collection. The second problem was due to the recent social events in Hong Kong plus the pandemic that have basically halted all our experimental work. All laboratories in the university were closed since mid Nov last year for more than two months. We were not able to have difficulties in carrying on the research activities during that period. Even after reopening, the progress was slow as the whole community gradually recovered and tried to go back to the normal working pace. Shortly after the reopening, the pandemic of coronavirus came and led to the lockdown of the whole city. It has further disrupted our work for the following few months till now. Towards the end of the lockdown, we were able to start some work but again only at a very slow pace. Therefore, due to the unprecedented events, the work has been slowed down and interrupted many times. Months have been wasted and we were not able to complete the experiment on time. Although we have completed all data collection eventually, due to the challenges described above, we are only able to complete the drafting of manuscript recently. The manuscript is attached with this Final report. We plan to publish it within the next six months. I hope to send in update when the paper is accepted for publication to further satisfy the outcome requirement. Therefore, I would be grateful if the review committee of GRF would kindly consider assessing the project in another six months in light of all the experimental hurdles and unexpected happenings.

15103315.label: Major findings and research outcome
15103315.value: An albino guinea pig myopia model was successfully developed and moderate myopia could be induced after 2 to 8 weeks of form-deprivation. The treated eyes was significantly more myopic (ΔRx: -3.73±3.98D, P<0.05, n=34) and larger (ΔAXL: 0.15±0.23mm, P<0.05, n=34) than the control eyes, and the excessive eye growth was significantly correlated with myopia (Rx vs AXL: r=-0.46, P=0.01). However, no direct correlation between myopia and IOP or outflow facility was found. Instead, the natural ocular size of both treated and control eyes showed significant correlations with IOP (AXL vs IOP: treated: r=0.72, P<0.00; control: r=0.80, P<0.00) and outflow facility (AXL vs C: treated: r=-0.47, P<0.00; control: r=-0.48, P=0.00), and the correlations were even stronger in eyes with deepened anterior chamber. It indicated that the over-stretching of eyes might cause the blockage of anterior drainage system, probably through the extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling at trabecular meshwork (TM), which in turn causes an elevation of IOP. Since guinea pig and human are similar in their ocular anatomy, we hypothesize that the present observations in guinea pigs might be generalizable to human. Our results suggested that big eyes with anterior chamber deepening may be more prone to develop glaucoma. Clinically it proposes a new parameter to assess the risk of glaucoma in suspects. This new paradigm provides a platform to further characterize the related molecular changes at the TM that causes the blockage. Eventually, it can help advance our understanding on the mechanism of blockage and devise ways to clear the drainage.

15103315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15103315.value: Our results revealed how natural ocular size might affect the anterior drainage system and lead to IOP elevation. In particular, the deepening of the anterior chamber might disrupt the drainage apparatus, probably through ECM remodelling and cytoskeletal alternations at the TM. It could result in ocular hypertension and glaucoma. It will be important to characterize the related molecular changes at the TM. We propose to study the protein expression profiles of TM tissues in big guinea pig’s eyes with a deep anterior chamber. For example, we can employ both discovery-based proteomic approach (such as the Sequential Windowed data independent Acquisition of the Total High-resolution Mass Spectra, SWATH-MS) and targeted-based approach (high-resolution multiple reaction monitoring, MRM-HR) to study the differential protein changes in these animals. All protein candidates so identified will be validated and their signalling pathways can be extensively studied using various pathway analysis and bioinformatics methods. Ultimately, we will be able to construct a comprehensive or system biology understanding on the mechanism of blockage of anterior drainage system as well as the pathogenesis of glaucoma.

15103315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15103315.value: This project studied the relationship between myopia, or better known as short-sightedness, and glaucoma using a guinea pig animal model. Glaucoma is a sight-threatening disease that is frequently associated with a high intraocular pressure (IOP) which is known to be caused by the blockage of the anterior drainage system. Myopia was successfully induced in guinea pigs by wearing diffuser goggles for 2 to 8 weeks. However, our results showed that myopia has no direct correlation with IOP elevation in guinea pig’s eyes. Interestingly, natural ocular size was found to be significantly correlated with IOP in guinea pig’s eyes, especially those with deepened anterior chamber. Our results revealed that excessive eye elongation, especially in the anterior chamber, can cause the blockage of anterior drainage system and increase the IOP. Furthermore, our result will inform new clinical study to assess the additional risk of developing glaucoma in patients with big eye and deep anterior chamber.

15103915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15103915.value: Unilateral neglect (UN) is a common heterogeneous perceptual disorder which occurs as high as 82% following right-hemisphere stroke (Plummer et al., 2003). UN is a strong predictor of long-term functional impairment and poor rehabilitation outcome in stroke (Jehkonen et al., 2001; Nys et al., 2005). The patient may fail to respond to visual or sensory stimuli presented from the contralateral space, which cannot be accounted for by either sensory or motor deficits. He/she may fail to use the hemiplegic side of the body, attend to objects and people on the affected side, and most severely may deny the left arm belonging to them (Carr & Shepherd, 1998). The reason for UN is best explained by the interhemispheric rivalry model of spatial attention (Corbetta et al., 2005; Hillis, 2006; Milner & McIntosh, 2005). The relatively higher excitability in contralesional hemisphere and lower excitability in ipsilesional side will enhance interhemispheric inhibition and cause more suppression to the affected hemisphere in reverse. There are 2 approaches of behavioral training for UN: recruiting the hemiplegic limbs to reduce spatial preference for the ipsilesional space, or improving awareness of the contralesional space to promote patients’ attention (Paci, Matulli et al., 2010; Pierce & Buxbaum, 2002). Although there are many studies on various kinds of rehabilitation interventions for UN, most of them are still not promising as the effects are transient and could not be generalized to an improvement in daily life (Yang et al., 2013). Mirror Therapy (MT) emerged 10 years ago as a useful rehabilitation intervention for hemiplegic upper extremity following stroke which had already been proven (Toh & Fong, 2012). It is simple and inexpensive. However, no study so far has investigated its effectiveness in treating UN after stroke. The study team has already published few studies in UN, hemiplegic upper extremity and MT respectively. We hypothesized that the mirror illusion of MT serves both purposes of recruiting the hemiplegic limbs to reduce spatial preference for the ipsilesional space, and improving awareness of the contralesional space to promote patients’ attention. If this new treatment being evaluated in this study is found to be effective, it can be widely adopted for stroke rehabilitation both in Hong Kong and overseas. The results of the proposed EEG study would represent a significant contribution to the phenomenology of mirror neuron activity in the field of neuroscience. 偏身忽略是中風病患者中常見的現象, 大約有82% 的左邊偏癱患者都有此症狀(Plummer et al., 2003) 。偏身忽略會嚴重影響患者日常生活(Jehkonen et al., 2001; Nys et al., 2005) 。患者會不注意從患側的視覺或感覺刺激, 但不一定會受患側活動或感覺能力影響。病徵由簡單的不使用患側, 到偏側視覺忽略或目光不注意患側、甚至單側軀體失認 (Carr & Shepherd, 1998) 。 跨半球競爭模型最好被用來解釋偏身空間注意的病理問題(Corbetta et al., 2005; Hillis, 2006; Milner & McIntosh, 2005)。注意網路由於中風的損傷將會導致構成注意網路的皮質區域之間的興奮性失衡。損傷側興奮性降低而損傷對側區域興奮性將會相對增高，不平衡的興奮性反過來進一步強化大腦半球間的競爭抑制作用從而導致對受損半球的抑制加重。偏身忽略的行為治療最主要還是採用治療性訓練將引發患者使用他們忽略側的空間或者肢體,或是重新引導患者注意力到患側(Paci, Matulli et al., 2010; Pierce & Buxbaum, 2002)。雖然有大量治療方法証據被用於臨床，但是目前仍然缺乏公認的滿意治療和能夠轉移到日常生活的有效方法(Yang et al., 2013)。 鏡子治療最近十年研究證據顯示其用於中風患者可以提高偏癱上肢功能(Toh & Fong, 2012)。鏡子治療簡單、低成本，但此療法應用在偏身忽略患者的成效有待證實。 目前, 研究團隊已發表了多份偏身忽略、偏癱上肢、及鏡子治療的研究文章。我們的研究假設鏡像療法可以促進中風患側肢體的近身空間正常化，及影響對側远身空间的注意力。如果此療法証實有效, 將會大大應用在香港及海外中風康復；用腦皮層電波量度中風患者的腦部鏡像神經元活動對腦神經科學定會作出貢獻。

15103915.label: Realisation of objectives
15103915.value: Objective (1): Objective one has been completed, although the actual number of patients recruited in each group was below the predicted number of subjects in each group in sample size estimation. One major reason was that most of the patients with unilateral neglect were severely hemiparetic. The dropout rate was also high in the local hospital in Hong Kong; many resignations from the study were due to instability in medical status, being referred back to acute medical management. We have attempted to overcome the subject recruitment by extending the period of participant recruitment of the study to one and a half years, much longer than expected, and conducted the randomized trial at two trial sites with one site in Guangdong. Although there were more participants, most of the patients were unable to attend follow-up appointments because of their admission to residential institutions or infirmaries after inpatient discharge. With regard to the deliverable, the full paper of the randomized trial has been prepared and submitted for publication earlier. A revised manuscript has been submitted again according to the comments from the reviewers and the editor. Please refer to Point 6.1. Objective (2): We have conducted EEG examination before and after mirror therapy for stroke patients with unilateral neglect who were inpatients in the local hospital. We have successfully completed two cases but the quality of the data was not satisfactory because of too much noises in the hospital environment. We have therefore terminated the investigation on inpatients with stroke in the hospital, and changed to recruit patients with stroke in the community for both the EEG and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) investigation associated with mirror therapy at our laboratory in the university. The outcome of results were satisfactory and the paper has been submitted to a journal which is currently under review. Please refer to Point 6.1. Objective (3) We have already completed the EEG examination, in terms of mirror visual feedback-induced sensorimotor event-related desynchronization (ERD), in healthy adults, however, the investigation could not be carried out in stroke patients with or without unilateral neglect. The major reason was that patients with unilateral neglect were very difficult to recruit in the community, and we found later that it would be a good attempt to find out what our brain is working associated with mirror visual feedback in terms of a translational study before we carried out the EEG examination in stroke patients. Having said that, we did a large scale systematic review of the literature and have already published a review paper on the activation of mirror neuron during mirror visual feedback in stroke. With regard to the deliverable, the full paper of investigating ERD in healthy adults has been prepared and submitted for publication earlier. A revised manuscript has been submitted again according to the comments from the reviewers and the editor. The study has also been presented in an international conference and the abstract has been published already in a renowned journal. Please refer to Point 6.1.

15103915.label: Major findings and research outcome
15103915.value: The project has some important findings. First, in our randomized controlled trial, we found that mirror visual feedback (MVF) of the non-paretic arm was more beneficial than the covered mirror in improving unilateral neglect in stroke patients, particularly in regard to alleviating egocentric rather than allocentric symptoms, but the improvements cannot be associated with arm functions and activities of daily living. However, there was no significant advantage for mirror therapy than viewing the hemiparetic arm through the transparent glass wall viewing the actual arm. This result is consistent with our systematic review paper, which we concluded that both MVF or action observation (AO) may contribute to stroke recovery by revising the interhemispheric imbalance caused by stroke due to the activation of the mirror neuron system, may also promote motor relearning in stroke individuals by activating the motor cortex. Third, there is a change in Laterality Index (LI) between the two hemispheres under mirror view of the hand illusion compared with the direct view of the hand in the EEG mu 8-12 Hz and beta-1 (12-16 Hz) bands in healthy adults. This showed that MVF is likely to activate the contralateral sensorimotor cortex (i.e., contralateral to MVF and ipsilateral to the moving hand). Finally, in our fNIRS study, we found that the activation of the ipsilateral sensorimotor during mirror therapy is likely to be associated with the ipsilateral supplementary motor area in healthy adults and that the precuneus may not be an essential component of the mirror therapy-related neural network. 15103915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15103915.value: To conclude, we suggested both mirror therapy, i.e. the use of mirror visual feedback (MVF), or action observation of both arms is recommended as an adjunct or supplement to conventional physical training targeting motor-impairment of the arm for stroke patients with unilateral neglect. We also suggested that MVF appears to induce higher activation than no mirror visual feedback in the ipsilateral sensorimotor cortex and supplementary motor area. The functional connectivity between these two ipsilateral areas is likely to be strengthened when receiving mirror therapy. Further fNIRS investigation should be done on stroke participants. Our study shows that brain stimulation in terms of transcranial magnetic stimulation appears to have a priming effect on the subject’s brain, making it more receptive to MVF. Further research will be carried out to investigate the clinical efficacy of combining both interventions in the stroke population. We have already submitted a proposal to the GRF on this topic in the year 2019/20, hoping that it can be funded.

15103915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15103915.value: In our project, we confirmed that mirror therapy is able to induce a neurophysiological effect to the lesion hemisphere after stroke to improve unilateral neglect and enhance motor recovery of the hemiparetic arm by shifting the transfer of effect from the non-affected to the affected hemispheres. However, similar therapeutic effect might be substituted by observing and moving two arms - the good arm and the hemiparetic arm, together. The use of brain stimulation appears to have a priming effect on the subject’s brain, making it more receptive to mirror therapy.

15104415.label: Project Objectives
15104415.value: We investigate the roles of N2, P3 and CDA. When compared with the healthy control group, we hypothesize that participants with egocentric neglect will show differences in the anteriorly-distributed P3, suggesting possible modulations to orienting and responding processes; and participants with allocentric neglect will show differences in the posteriorly-distributed N2 and CDA, suggesting possible modulations to discrimination and selection of stimulus and top-down control processes. 15104415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15104415.value: 半側忽略是一種參見的右腦受損導致的障礙。以前的電生理學研究顯示對早期的檢測和反應（即N1a;Russo et al .,2008），最初的回饋（N1p和P2），和注意力的分配（P3）過程進行調節會導致左側視野的忽視。然而，這些研究並沒有運用以自我為中心和非自我為中心的參考框架。這兩個參考框架是並列存在於伴有視覺忽視的患者中的。我們之前關於老年人的研究表明，N2，P3和對側延遲活動（CDA）成分是區分這兩個參考框架的有效標記。該專案旨在探索以自我為中心和非自我為中心的視覺忽視的不同機制。有兩個問題：（1）後N2（鑒別和刺激的選擇），P3（定向和反應）和CDA（自上而下的控制）在以自我為中心和非自我為中心的視覺忽視中的作用；（2）採用ERP源重建的方法來測試，選擇性注意的識別模型能夠在多大程度上解釋自我為中心和非自我為中心的視覺忽視。 方法 研究物件 共40名中風患者參與。依據蘋果測試，其中20名被鑒定為自我為中心的忽視，另20名為非自我為中心的忽視。健康對照組為30名在年齡、性別及教育水平方面相匹配的老年人。 流程 所有參與者要完成三環定位任務，此期間大腦的電信號通過頭皮得以捕獲。 任務設計是為了激發自我為中心和非自我為中心的視覺注意。除了蘋果測試，患者的認知功能、運動功能及自我照顧的獨立能力也要進行測試。 資料分析 採用不同的方差分析模型檢測N2，P3和CDA成分與自我為中心和非自我為中心注意的相關關係的顯著性，以及它們與左/右半球的活動和視覺刺激呈現在左/右側之間的關係。患者的病變部位（基於CT圖像）也將用於重建偶極子源，用以測試與自我為中心和非自我為中心的視覺忽視相關的大腦活動的差異。 意義 我們相信，以自我為中心和非自我為中心的忽視亞型的分化將使我們能夠有效地分離可能被視覺忽視調節的神經加工過程。這一發現將有助於建立自我為中心和非自我為中心忽視的神經加工過程的調節機制。由此產生的知識將充實為伴視覺忽視的中風患者設計的有效干預措施的理論基礎。

15104415.label: Realisation of objectives
15104415.value: Validation of OCS The validation study on OCS was completed. The results were published as a full paper: Hong, W-J., Tao, J., Wong, A. W. K., Yang, S-L., Leung, M-T., Lee, T. M. C., Demeyere, N., Lau, S. C. L., Chien, C-W., Chan, C. C. H., Chen L-D. (2018). Psychometric properties of the Chinese (Putonghua) version of the Oxford Cognitive Screen (OCS-P) in subacute poststroke patients without neglect. BioMed Research International, Article ID 6827854, 12 pages. doi: 10.1155/2018/6827854. This study was aimed to assess the psychometric properties of the Chinese (Putonghua) version of the Oxford Cognitive Screen-Putonghua (OCS-P) for use among post-stroke patients without neglect. Expert review panel evaluated the content validity of Chinese-translated items. One hundred patients and 120 younger (n=60) or older (n=60) healthy counterparts completed OCS-P, Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA-ChiB), and Goldenberg’s test for validity testing. fNIRS Study on Allocentric and Egocentric Attention This part of the study was to collect evidence on the experimental task described in the original proposal for eliciting brain activations characterized allocentric and egocentric spatial coding. Details of the study can be found in Derbie et al. (under review) (journal output #2). The participant were 22 university students recruited through convenience sampling. Participants were told to use a manual visual search during the target phase and to provide responses as instructed. Changes in the oxygenated hemoglobin (O2-Hb) concentration were acquired with a 52-channel configured Hitachi optical topography (ETG-4000, Hitachi™ Medical. Co., Kashiwa, Japan) equipped with laser diodes of two wavelengths (695 nm and 830 nm). Details of the data collection procedure and data analyses can be found in Derbie et al. (under review). Aging Effects on Allocentric and Egocentric Attention This part of the study was to collect evidence on the new spatial coding task for use in the main study. Literature review of this study was written in the form of meta-analysis. Based on the criteria set, 16 experiments (number of subjects = 265, with 203 foci’s) for the task-specific allocentric and 18 experiments (number of subjects = 263, with 219 foci’s) for the task-specific egocentric entered into the meta-analysis. The results of the meta-analysis can be found in Derbie et al. (under preparation 1) (see journal output #3). The research team designed a different spatial coding task for use in the main study. It was a cue-to-target paradigm adapted in a previous study. Each trial began with presentation of three stimuli and a cue for 350 ms. The three stimuli included a pair of empty squares and one empty rectangle. The cue was a Chinese character presented at the centre that indicated the kind of response required later in the trial. The cue was followed by a stimulus-onset asynchrony (SOA) for a fixed duration of 1650 ms, in which the Chinese character was replaced by a dot. Next, a new pair of squares appeared inside the two ends of the empty rectangle. One of the four squares showed a ‘plus’ sign that indicated the target and the other three showed ‘asterisks’ that indicated distracters. In the egocentric condition, the target appeared in one of the squares outside the rectangle and participants was to indicate whether the target was located on the left or right according to their own bodily coordinates. In the allocentric condition, the target appeared in one of the squares inside the rectangle and participants was to indicate whether the target was located on the left or right side of the rectangle, regardless of their own bodily coordinates. In the cue phase at the beginning of the trial, the Chinese character cued the identity of the trial and the position of the target. The font was either in italic or not that indicated egocentric or allocentric condition respectively. The character was either “左” (left) or “右” (right) indicating that the target would appear on the left or right respectively in its corresponding condition. Finally, an inter-trial interval with variable length delay of 500 ms, 2500 ms, or 4500 ms was randomly presented. BOLD signals were captured when the participants performed the task inside MRI scanner. Structural scans were obtained for diffusion tensor imaging (DTI). A total of 71 healthy participants completed both scans. Among them, 27 were younger adults, 20 were middle-aged adults, and 24 were older adults. Details of the data collection procedure and data analysis methods can be found in Derbie et al. (working paper, journal output #4). Post-stroke Patient Dysfunction in Spatial Coding Enormous efforts had been put to recruit post-stroke patients for this brain imaging study. Patient recruitment was conducted in a rehabilitation hospital in which the majority of the patients were three to six months after the onset of stroke. A total of 1837 patients were screened. The majority of the patients were excluded because of secondary stroke and impaired vision (n=554), cognitive dysfunction and not able to complete the task (n=347). Another large proportion of the patients were excluded because they had metal implants and/or claustrophobic (n=674). The final number of patients included in the study was 15 patients without allocentric nor egocentric spatial coding deficits, 8 patients with symptoms of allocentric deficits (as confirmed by OCS and BIT) but able to complete the experimental tasks. There were only two patients who presented with egocentric deficits (as confirmed by OCS and BIT) but able to complete the experimental task. The reason for the very few patients identified as presenting with allocentric or egocentric symptoms because of the high rate of recovery after the onset of stroke. The majority of the patients screened would have been recovered from the deficits at the time when the screening tests were conducted. All participants completed clinical instruments and training on performing the experimental tasks. Each participant completed the experimental task inside the MRI scanner during which BOLD signals were captured. Structural scans were also completed for each participant. The data analyses conducted for the patient groups were contrasts between healthy older participants and post-stroke patients, and between post-stroke patients and allocentric deficit patients. Completion of Project According to Hypotheses Hypothesis 1: Achieved 85% and the explanation can be found below. The research team will continue to recruit patients with egocentric deficits. For this time, the duration of onset from stroke is to be shortened to six weeks to three months. The necessary data collection and analyses for addressing this hypothesis was partially completed. The research team managed to complete the validation of the Chinese version of OCS which is the only cognitive assessment designed for assessing post-stroke patients for Chinese population. The testing of the spatial coding models for healthy younger and older groups was completed. The healthy participant’s model enabled meaningful comparisons with that of the post-stroke patients. Recruitment of post-stroke patients and the subsequent data analyses for constructing the stroke model was completed. Despite fewer than planned, recruitment of post-stroke patients with allocentric deficits was deemed completed. The only part which had not been fully completed in the study was the recruitment of adequate number of patients with egocentric deficits. The two patients who fulfilled the inclusion criteria were not adequate for achieving meaningful analyses for testing the sub-hypothesis set for the egocentric deficits. Hypothesis 2: Achieved 100% based on the healthy younger group, and the healthy younger versus older group.

15104415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15104415.value: fNIRS Study The results demonstrate that the different spatial coding processes are associated with different patterns of cortical activities (see Derbie et al., under review). Despite the positive evidence revealed from this experimental task, the experience gained indicated that the task tended to demand high level of attention and working memory functions for making valid responses. Findings from New Experimental Task This part of the study was to collect evidence of the new spatial coding task for use in the main study. The results supported similar processes mediated by common neural substrates between the two types of spatial codings: superior frontal gyrus, precuneus, post-central gyrus, and superior parietal sulcus (working paper, journal output #4). Egocentric spatial coding was dominated by activations in the medial frontal gyrus and the occipital-related substrates (occipital parietal circuit and middle occipital gyrus). In contrast, for allocentric spatial coding, they were the temporo-parietal junction and the medial temporal lobe. Age-related differences were revealed in both spatial coding processes. In the egocentric condition, the between-group differences included ACC, inferior parietal lobule, IPS, and post-central gyrus. Results obtained for the egocentric and allocentric spatial coding concur with the first and second/third components of SAIM model, respectively. However, our findings did not wholly concur with the neural substrates stipulated in the SAIM model (anterior versus posterior). The inconsistent findings could have been due to the task design. In our study, egocentric spatial coding is characterized with the fronto-parieto-occipital distribution and allocentric spatial coding is fronto-temporo-parietal distribution. Post-stroke Patient Dysfunction When compared with healthy older participants, post-stroke patients showed increases in activations in the superior frontal gyrus and anterior cingulate gyrus in egocentric spatial coding. In contrast, post-stroke patients showed increases in activations in the lingual gyrus and cerebellum than their healthy counterparts in allocentric spatial coding. Patients with allocentric deficits when performing in allocentric condition showed activations in the superior parietal lobule, the pre-central gyrus and the intra-parietal sulcus. When compared with post-stroke patients without neglect, patients with allocentric deficits showed decreases in activations in the superior and medial frontal gyrus in allocentric spatial coding. Allocentric deficits were found to exerted demand on post-stroke patients in maintaining top-down attention and visuospatial working memory, encoding spatial representation, and shifting of task rules in allocentric spatial coding. Findings of this part of the study supported the hypothesis that precentral and medial frontal gyrus would have been the candidates to be affected by the allocentric deficits.

15104415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104415.value: The models built from groups of younger and older participants formed the basis for studying the deficit models among post-stroke patients. Due to the stringent admission criteria set for the patients, the comparisons within the post-stroke patients were based on a small size. The comparisons for patients with egocentric deficits cannot be performed based on the fact that only two patients had been recruited for the study. Future study is to continue recruiting post-stroke patients diagnosed with allocentric or egocentric deficits, particularly the latter. In future recruitment, onset of stroke will be shortened as six weeks to three months. This will increase the chance of identifying patients with the deficits. Understanding of the commonality and differences between the two types of spatial coding benefit design and research of clinical interventions for post-stroke patients who show deficits. First, mental processes of egocentric are likely to precede those of allocentric. Training for patients with allocentric deficits should include both egocentric and allocentric spatial coding. Second, when designing the training, egocentric deficits are to focus on translating visual stimuli to peripersonal spatial landmarks; while allocentric deficits are to focus on attentional control and visuospatial working memory, and shifting across object-to-space relationship.

15104415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104415.value: This study was aimed to gain better understand on the neural processes associated with the two types of spatial coding in attention: egocentric (viewer-centered) and allocentric (object-centered). Results of behavioral and brain imaging measures suggest that the two types of spatial coding are likely to share common neural processes. Besides, the processes involved in egocentric tend to occur at the beginning of those in allocentric spatial coding. Egocentric is characterized with brain activations span from frontal, parietal and occipital regions; while allocentric is characterized with a frontal and temporal distribution. Findings from post-stroke patients with or without allocentric deficits further support these findings. The rate limiting steps of egocentric would be translating visual stimuli into spatial information with respect to one’s person-space and those of allocentric would be navigating among spatial landmarks maintained in working memory and associating objects with space. To clinically differentiate post-stroke patients with spatial coding deficits, the research team also validate the Chinese version of Oxford Cognitive Screen (OCS-P) for use in Chinese population. The knowledge gained will form the basis for improving the competence in diagnosing the deficits as well as designing clinical intervention for rehabilitation of post-stroke patients suffering from these deficits.

15200215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200215.value: Adult acquired flatfoot deformity (AAFD) is a common foot problem that becomes more prevalent with age. Extra-osseous talotarsal stabilization (EOTTS) or subtalar arthroereisis (STA) uses an implant placed into the sinus tarsi via a minimally invasive procedure to stabilize the joint and is one of the most popular surgical treatments for flexible AADF. Different EOTTS devices are used in clinic. Some have higher removal rates, most likely related to the biomechanical function of the device. Also, the specific mechanism in which the sinus tarsi implant functions is still unclear. Surgical interference in the subtalar joint can result in improved biomechanical function of the talotarsal joint, which comprises the interaction of the talus on the calcaneus and navicular bones. It is thus necessary to consider the consequences of surgical treatment and the biomechanical effects over the entire foot and ankle. Unfortunately, direct in-vivo measurements of the internal biomechanical parameters are difficult due to lack of non-invasive measurement techniques. Previous in-vitro studies often used normal cadaver samples and simulated flat foot deformities through sectioning or attenuating the soft-tissue supporting structures. Computational modeling and simulation is a powerful tool in biomechanical analyses, but it has seldom been used for AAFD and related surgeries. Our team has worked on comprehensive computational foot/ankle modeling for over 15 years. The in-house technology and experience can be used to construct an AAFD analytical platform. Integrated with in-vivo experiments, such a computational platform would be useful for understanding AAFD and related surgical operations. The overall objective of this project is to better understand the biomechanical consequences of the EOTTS treatment and how different implant designs with varied shapes, sizes, materials, insertion locations and orientation influence the biomechanical performance of the entire foot and ankle. Representative AAFD patients will participate in this study, with informed consent. The foot and ankle will be scanned before being operated on or implanted. Kinematic and kinetic data during standing and walking can be obtained from a motion analysis capture system and a force platform. Muscle and joint forces can be estimated using a musculoskeletal model. The data obtained will be used to construct and validate the models. Comparisons of stress/strain distribution, plantar pressure distribution, foot arch height, joint stiffness, etc. before and after surgical treatment will be used to understand the biomechanical consequences of treatment. This platform can also be used to study other biomechanical problems associated with AAFD. 成人获得性扁平足是一种常见的足部疾病，随着年龄增长而发病增高。经微创技术在跗骨窦放置稳定器进行距跗关节制动和距下关节融合是治疗可变性扁平足最常用的治疗方法。目前有多种距跗关节稳定器被用于临床，但其中部分稳定器需要二次取出，原因可能与其生物力学特征相关。另外，跗骨窦内植入物的功能特性目前也不明确。 距下关节的手术治疗可导致距跗关节生物力学性能的改善，包括距骨、跟骨和舟骨三者间的互相作用。因此，有必要考虑手术治疗的后果，以及对全足和踝关节的生物力学影响。但不幸的是，由于缺乏无创测量技术，直接测量人体内部的生物力学参数是非常困难的。早期的体外研究往往通过对正常尸体足切断或降低软组织支撑来模拟扁平足，并进行相应研究。 数值建模和仿真是生物力学研究中最有力的手段，但几乎很少被用于成人获得性扁平足研究和手术分析。在过去的15年中，我们研究团队长期从事足踝的综合数值研究。该方面的技术和经验可用于构建成人获得性扁平足分析研究的数字平台。通过与在体实验的结合，该数字平台将对了解成人获得性扁平足的发病机制和手术治疗提供有益的信息。 该项目的总体目标是更好地了解距跗骨制动的生物力学影响，以及植入物外形、尺寸、材料、插入位置和方向对全足生物力学性能的影响。典型扁平足患者同意签署的知情同意书将被纳入本次研究。术前或植入固定材料前将对足踝进行图像扫描。通过运动分析捕捉系统和力平台获得站立和行走时运动学和动力学数据。通过肌骨模型计算足踝部肌肉和关节的力。所获得的数据将被用于构建和验证数值模型。通过比较手术前后的应力应变分布、足底压力分布、足弓高度以及关节僵硬度等参数，了解手术治疗的生物力学影响。该研究平台也可以用于研究与成人获得性扁平足相关联的其它生物力学问题。

15200215.label: Realisation of objectives
15200215.value: In order to understand the differences in foot biomechanics between normal and flat feet, and the biomechanical effects of surgical treatments using subtalar arthroereisis, we have done a series of biomechanical studies as follows to achieve the project objectives. 1) In-vivo experimental studies have been conducted for both eight normal and eight flat foot subjects to measure the gait pattern, plantar foot pressure distribution, forefoot deformation and EMG during standing and walking with different foot supports. The data were used to understand the difference in biomechanical performance between normal subject foot and flat foot. The data would also be used for model input and validation. 2) Musculoskeletal models have been developed using Opensim software to estimate the muscle and joint forces of the lower limb during standing and walking. The data are used for model input for load boundary conditions. 3) MRI scan has been done for one subject who had flat feet for both sides. Three dimensional reconstruction of the images was done to obtained the geometric information for foot surface and bone structures. Based on the geometrical information, finite element model of flat foot has been developed. The FE models developed from our previous experience and in this project are most comprehensive one. The model includes 28 bony segments, connective tissue and muscles, embedded in a volume of soft tissue and skin. The boundary and loading condition were obtained from experimental study. Through compared with our previously developed FE models of normal foot, the internal factors resulted in flat foot (pes planus) was analyzed and attempted to understand etiology of flat foot based on the geometrical different and load transfer mechanism between normal and flat feet. The models have been validated through comparison of pressure distribution over plantar supports between experimental measurements and model prediction 4) Finite element model of flat foot was further extended to simulate surgical treatment with an implant inserted in the sinus tarsi. This model can provide the varies in biomechanical load transfer between flat foot model and surgical treatment model. The comparison can provide the insight on the surgical consequences on the treatment of flat foot. 5) Parametric studies were conducted using the FE models to simulate the different implant types with different material properties, sizes, locations and orientations. Only the implants were changed, while all other conditions were kept the same for well controlled. The same computational output were compared among the different models. These parametric analyses can provide information for better design of implant in terms of type and size, and guidelines for surgical protocols in terms of location and orientation. 6) Computational biomechanical platform for flat foot developed in this project was further used to understand the effect of orthotic treatment on flat foot which are often used in clinics. A series of designs of insoles and functional footwears for children and adults were investigate to understand the treatment consequences. These include experimental study and computational modeling. All objectives proposed in this project have been well addressed. The biomechanical platform developed in this project can be further used for other foot related study.

15200215.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200215.value: To understand the etiology of flat foot, FE model analyses indicated the load transfer of the joints at the proximal medial column of foot was weaken by posterior tibial tendinopathy (PTT). This indicates that PTT changed the load transfer mechanism and the strain of the midfoot plantar ligaments.These changes disturb the load balance of the medial longitudinal arch and possiblely the reason of arch collapse and flat foot. This finding was published in Clinical Biomechanics (Output 1). Subtalar joint arthroereisis (SJA) has been introduced to control the hyperpronation in cases of flatfoot. SJA can partially restore the internal load transfer and midfoot stress, however cannot compensate the salvage of midfoot stability and could be biomechanically insufficient to restore the biomechanical environment. This finding was published (output 2). Our biomechanical platform was further used to understand foot biomechanics, such as bone fracture fusion (output 3), ankle joint arthroplasty (output 5). The foot orthosis significantly reduced the peak ankle eversion angle and ankle eversion moment. The reduction in the patellofemoral joint force and ankle contact force could potentially inhibit flatfoot-induced lower limb joint problems, despite a greater knee adduction moment, which published in journal (output 6).

15200215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200215.value: This project developed a biomechanical platform for the understanding of the flat foot biomechanics, which can be further used in clinical treatment of flat foot and improved design of implants. The implant design should be consider the biomechanical consequences from the treatments. The platform can also be used to understand the conservative methods to treat flat foot such as foot orthosis or functional footwear. More clinical trials can be further studied using the finite element models developed in this project. The project would be benefit to implant design, surgical protocols and orthosis design, through closely collaboration with medical doctors and orthosists.

15200215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200215.value: Adult acquired flatfoot deformity is a common foot problem that becomes more prevalent with age. Subtalar arthroereisis through inserting an implant into the sinus tarsi via a minimally invasive procedure to stabilize the joint and is one of the most popular surgical treatments. This project developed a biomechanical platform with both experimental and computational studies to understand how different implant designs with varied shapes, sizes, materials, insertion locations and orientation influence the biomechanical performance of the entire foot and ankle. The results show the treatment using subtalar joint arthroereisis can partially restore the internal load transfer and stop the arch collapes, however cannot compensate the salvage of midfoot stability. The platform can also be used to understand if the arch supported orthosis can improve the load transfer for flat foot. The findings from this project can provide useful biomechanical information for clinical treatment of flat foot.

15200715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200715.value: 現代處理器通常具有64位的典型字長，即意味着每個處理器核心在每一條指令（每一個時鐘週期）中可以處理64位元的信息。一直以來，這種週期內的並行性並沒有被充分利用。本項目研究如何利用這種週期內的並行性加速內存分析數據庫中的聚合操作。 研究包括針對各種不同的數據庫聚合操作（比如求和、求均值、求最大（小）值、求中位數）設計對應的位元級並行算法。

15200715.label: Realisation of objectives
15200715.value: 1. For each standard aggregation operation: SUM, MIN, MAX, AVG, MEDIAN, COUNT, devise an efficient bit-parallel algorithm that exploits intra-cycle parallelism. (100% achieved) We have developed efficient algorithms for SUM, MIN, MAX, AVG, MEDIAN, and COUNT. The algorithms leverage the bit level parallelism and core parallelism and achieve excellent cache and TLB re-use. 2. Integrate each bit-parallel aggregation algorithm with multi-core and SIMD technologies to achieve extra acceleration. (100% achieved) For each algorithm, we have used AVX2 and AVX256 SIMD to accelerate the processing speed. We have also used multiple-core to parallelize the processing. When using multiple-cores, we are able to reach memory-bound (maximum) performance. 3. Analyze the complexity of the developed algorithms and evaluate the performance (running times) of the algorithms by running experiments and prototyping the algorithms into an open-source main memory analytic database. The complexity of each algorithm is analyzed: The complexity of COUNT is O(n/w), where n is the number of tuples, and w is the word size. The complexity of SUM, MIN, MAX, MEDIAN, AVG are O(nk/w), where k is the column width in terms of bit. Experiments on real data and synthetic are run and those algorithms are implemented in a branch of an open-source prototype.

15200715.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200715.value: In this project, we have successfully developed bit-level algorithms for main-memory analytic databases. We have implemented and tested our algorithms on real data sets and TPC-H datasets. We have also extended our techniques to scan (ICDE18), sort (SIMGOD16), join (DSAA16), and hash table (CIKM19). This project aims to look at the aggregation operations (e.g., SUM, MEDIAN), which are another important class of operations found in main-memory analytic databases. The project has successfully completed. In addition to academic publications, we have also open-sourced the codes such that others can test and integrate them into their systems.

15200815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200815.value: Mud and rock slides happen in many hilly places like Hong Kong. On 31 August 2013, a train derailed in Pingtung of Taiwan due to a mudslide, leaving 12 passengers injured with train service suspended. Solid concrete walls could be used but their cantilever action leads to high cost in foundation and their bucky appearance affects the scene. An alternative and economical method to prevent mudslide is to construct mud and rock flexible barriers made of nets. However, unlike conventional structures made of steel and concrete, the design of a cable net system is more complex and based on the large deflection theory where the tension action in the net and cables is utilized to resist loads. Large deflection nonlinear analysis must be invoked because the stiffness of cables or net develops after deflection. The feature of this structural system is that the structural elements are in contact at their connecting node which is not fixed to these elements, but slide along the elements and this could be named as the curtain effect where rings supporting the curtain cloth slide along the cable wire fixed at its two ends. Conventional finite element packages are generally unable to deal with the design of this structural form practically and efficiently because of the curtain effect. Conventional linear and second order analysis cannot be used here because the structural system behaves highly nonlinearly and the effect of nodes sliding over along element is not accounted for. This project is to develop a computer-based reliable method for design of flexible barrier systems to prevent casualties. New energy and force design criteria will be studied. The force method allows the barrier to resist the impact force and the alternative energy system designs the barrier to possesses sufficient flexibility to absorb dynnamic and static energy from the sliding muds. The origiality of this projects also lies on its modeling of dynamic effect from the impact energy or forces since impacting debris possesses dynamic energy which disappears after a short duration of contact with the net. Previous research findings and development on nonlinear analysis by the proposer has, to a certain extent, generated an impact to the practice of structural engineers. The second-order and advanced analysis was placed in the latest design steel code 2011 published by the Hong Kong SAR government (see web http://www.bd.gov.hk/english/documents/code/SUOS2011.pdf ), in which the applicant was the first principal consultant. . 多丘陵的地方如中國大陸、台灣和香港經常發生山泥傾瀉和岩石滑落。2013年8月31日一列火車經過台灣屏東時遭遇泥石流，導致12乘客受傷，火車服務被迫中斷。用於攔截泥石流和落石的混凝土牆不僅造價昂貴，還損害自然景觀。一種防止泥石流更為經濟的方法是建造由鋼索和鋼絲網製成的柔性防護網。 然而，不像設計傳統鋼和混凝土構成的結構那樣，設計此種承受岩石和其它碎屑的索網系統更為複雜，必須採用大變形理論，充分考慮索網的受拉性能去抵抗外載。設計時必須採用非線性分析，因為鋼索或者鋼絲網的在未變形時其剛度幾乎為零。此種結構系統的特點在於結構單元之間連接方式是一種接觸行為，相接點相對單元而言不是固定的，而是會沿著單元滑移。 此種現象可稱為窗簾效應，即窗簾通過環掛在兩端固定的繩索上，窗簾相對繩索是可自由滑動。傳統有限元分析程序一般不能直接用於設計此種結構形式，因為此類結構的節點是可滑動的，且有大變形效應，在荷載作用下，連接點會沿鋼索滑動、鋼絲網之間也會發生滑動。 此類結構系統通常顯示出高度非線性，而且節點會沿單元滑動（即窗簾效應），傳統的線性分析和二階分析方法因考慮不了這些因素而不能用於設計。本項目旨在延續申請人以前的工作（高效的三維框架分析和一些對索式防護網的二階分析的初步研究），從而可以設計更多更好的柔性防護系統來防止災害和減少人員傷亡。 新的能量和力的設計準則將會加入柔性防護網的設計指南中。能量是基於防護網中的組件失效前該系統所吸收的最大應變能。 申請人以前在非線性分析方面的研究和發展在某種程度上已經對結構工程師產生很大的影響。二階及高等分析方法已經納入香港政府最近出版的鋼結構設計規範2011中，見網頁http://www.bd.gov.hk/english/documents/code/SUOS2011.pdf，而申請人正是該規範的第一起草人。申請人也因將該方法應用於新加坡大跨度空間結構的設計，完全不需要採用傳統的有效長度法，獲得了今年英國-香港聯合結構工程分部香港工程師學會頒發的榮譽大獎。

15200915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200915.value: Wave manipulation is a new emerging concept which starts to draw attention from researchers in many engineering fields. Revealed by relatively recent research and confirmed by our previous work, the phenomenon of the Acoustic Black Hole (ABH) inside a thin-walled structure was shown to exhibit appealing features, which can be further explored for a wide range of applications through structure-borne wave manipulation. Despite the anticipated enthusiasm towards this enabling technology, serious problems still exist, hampering the implementation and application of the ABH phenomenon in the real engineering context. This project attempts to address some of these bottlenecking problems, of both fundamental and applied nature, to deepen the understanding of the underlying physics related to the ABH phenomenon on one hand, and to explore the application feasibility for structure-borne noise control problems on the other hand. The significance of the project lies in its direct applicability to a wide range of engineering problems such as noise and vibration control or energy harvesting, which are of direct benefit to both Hong Kong and beyond. From scientific research viewpoint, the problem under investigation is fundamental and generic in nature, which may have significant scientific value for advancing the state-of-the-art in vibration and noise control engineering. 航空航天飞行器、舰船等大量工程结构中的声振现象的共性本质是波动，而实现这类结构 减振降噪的一个共性基础正是波的操控。声学黑洞是通过薄壁结构厚度或者材料特性的梯度变 化，实现波的减速、聚焦等操控。本项目主要研究基于声学黑洞的工程结构中波操控的力学问 题，此研究是学科前沿，不仅具有重要的科学意义，而且直接与工程中的声振问题和能量回收 技术相结合，具有广阔的应用前景。在前期力学建模和控制等相关研究的基础上，探究结构中 的声学黑洞效应。建立研究此类结构波传播与操控问题的建模和分析方法，重点探索声学黑洞 现象的特征行为和波传播演变过程。揭示声学黑洞现象背后的物理机制，深刻认识声学黑洞结 构在多物理场耦合情况下各参数的影响规律。积极拓展声学黑洞结构在减振降噪、能量回收等 工程领域中的应用，发现声学黑洞的声辐射机制和多物理场耦合能量聚集效应，提出结构优化 设计方法，满足工程实际应用

15200915.label: Realisation of objectives
15200915.value: All objectives of the projects have been systematically addressed and realized. Research activities carried out, in relation to the research objectives are summarized as follows: Objective 1: To achieve a better understanding of the ABH formation process using time domain laser-induced wave visualization technique A laser-based time domain wave propagation visualization technique was established. Analytical expression of the wave reflection coefficient in a modified one-dimensional ABH was derived and the time-domain experimental method based on a laser excitation technique was used to visualize the wave propagation. In the experimental studies, the flexural waves in the ABH were excited by a scanning pulse laser and measured by a Laser Doppler Vibrometer (LDV). The incident wave and reflected wave were separated from the measured original wave field and the decrease of the wave velocity in the ABH was exhibited. Objective 2: To establish semi-analytical and numerical models to analyze structures with embedded ABH feature, and to provide design guidance with the consideration of the coupling between the ABH and damping treatment. Semi-analytical models were established to analyze both beam and plate structures with embedded ABH feature and their full coupling with the damping layers coated over the surface. By decomposing the transverse displacement field of the beam over the basis of a suitably chosen set of series (Mexican hat wavelets, Debauchees or sinusoidal functions with supplementary smoothing terms), the extremalization of the Hamiltonian via Lagrange’s equation yields a set of linear equations, which can be solved for structural responses. Highly consistent with the FEM and experimental results, numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed wavelet-based model is particularly suitable to characterize the ABH-induced drastic wavelength fluctuation phenomenon. The ABH feature as well as the effect of the wedge truncation and that of the damping layers on the vibration response of the structures were analyzed. The developed model was then used to explore means to enhance the acoustic black hole phenomenon in a 1D configuration. The phenomenon of Acoustics Black Hole (ABH) benefits from the bending wave propagating properties inside a thin-walled structure with power-law thickness variation to achieve zero reflection when the structural thickness approaches zero in the ideal scenario. However, manufacturing an ideally tailored power-law profile of a structure with embedded ABH feature can hardly be achieved in practice. Past research showed that the inevitable truncation at the wedge tip of the structure can significantly weaken the expected ABH effect by creating wave reflections. On the premise of the minimum achievable truncation thickness by the current manufacturing technology, exploring ways to ensure and achieve better ABH effect becomes important. In this part of the work, we investigate this issue by using a Euler-Bernoulli beam with a modified power-law profile and an extended platform of constant thickness. Objective 3: To examine vibration and sound radiating structures with ABH features for noise control applications. The above models were extended to sound radiation analyses in both free field and into an acoustic cavity. In particular, ABHs were used to reduce the noise inside a cavity bounded by a flexible plate with multiple two-dimensional (2-D) ABH indentations. The interior sound field was generated by and fully coupled to the vibration of the flexible plate subject to a point force excitation. A semi-analytical model as well as a refined numerical finite element model considering the plate-cavity coupling were established and validated by experiments. In addition, a wavenumber domain method (WNDM) was proposed for the analysis of vibro-acoustic coupling and internal noise reduction mechanism of a pentahedral cavity enclosed by a flexible plate with a two-dimensional ABH indentation, subject to a point force excitation. The relationship between the space-averaged sound energy inside the cavity and the spectra of the structural displacement and the acoustic mode of the cavity was established. This allowed revealing a dual physical mechanism behind the observed noise reduction: amplitude reduction and mismatching between the wavenumber spectra of the plate displacement and the acoustic field, which results in a weakened vibro-acoustic coupling. An additional configuration with an ABH embedded in an irregular pentagonal wall of the cavity was examined. Despite the increasing complexity in the geometry of the coupling interface and its coupling with the cavity, numerical analyses confirm the generality of the observed physical phenomena and the applicability of the proposed WNDM to more complex system configurations. Objective 4: To establish a general design procedure which allow efficient energy absorption and noise insulation. Analyses performed at different stages allows establishing clear design guidelines of the effective conception of ABH structures for different applications. These design principles apply to a). General ABH beam and plate b). Compound ABH structures c). Periodic lattice ABH structures d). Light-weight and highly damped vibrating structures e). Structures with impaired noise radiation capability f). ABH-base dynamic absorbers.

15200915.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200915.value: 1). The feasibility of the laser-based measuring technique for ABH study was demonstrated. Results confirm that there exists an optimal thickness for the damping layer. Based on the laser-induced visualization technique and various signal processing and feature extraction methods, the entire process of the wave propagation in a non-ideal one-dimensional ABH structure can be visualized and scrutinized. This part of work was published in MSSP and ASME Transactions: JAV. 2). The established semi-analytical model showed great efficiency in simulation various ABH-specific phenomena. In particular, the model was extended to design high efficiency vibration isolation lattice, which shows remarkable bandgap properties through effective merge of the ABH-specific local resonances and Bragg scattering effect. This part of work has been published in journals like JSV, JASA, ASME transaction MSSP, APL and JAP as summarized in the outcome Table. 3). The relationship between the space-averaged sound energy inside the cavity and the spectra of the structural displacement and the acoustic mode of the cavity was established. This allowed revealing a dual physical mechanism behind the observed noise reduction: amplitude reduction and mismatching between the wavenumber spectra of the plate displacement and the acoustic field, which results in a weakened vibro-acoustic coupling. This part of the work has been published in JSV. 4). Various means to enhance ABH effects as well as its applications are developed as design guidelines. A modified thickness profile was proposed which brings about a systematic increase in the ABH effect. The use of an extended platform further increases the ABH effect to broader the frequency band. New types of ABH-based dynamic absorbers are proposed. This part of the work was summarized in a publication in the JSV. 5). We observed the loss of the ABH effect in a beam of finite size, which up to now has been reported as a broadband phenomenon above the cut-on frequency in semi-infinite ABH structures. The failure frequencies can be predicted by calculating the local resonance frequencies of the beam portion delimited and pinned by the excitation point, which allows the avoidance of the phenomenon in the targeted application ranges. This part of result was published in APL. 6). Under the invitation of the editor-in-chief of Advances in Mechanics, we carried out a very comprehensive review of the current state-of-the-art in acoustic black hole research. This review paper was also published in early 2017.

15200915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200915.value: Through four years of research on ABH, our group is now regarded as one of the most active research groups in the area. Apart from the academic reputation gained out of this effort, we have successfully attracted strong interest from a number of companies, who decided to support our research through collaborative/consulting projects, which shows the huge application potentials of the technology. Based on our proff-of-concept research and demonstrations, ABH-based technology is entering into a stage where real applications are around the corner. Therefore, the next step is to engage into active R&D with the close collaborations with the industry. Academic-wise, further effort is still needed to solve two problems: 1). Improve the low-frequency performance of the ABH; and 2): realize thin-walled structures which are more appealing to industrial people. We are now looking at these issues, with the great support from Midea Ltd, the biggest domestic product manufacturer in Mainland. Hopefully, a few realistic industrial applications will be materialized in the near future.

15200915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200915.value: The importance of developing advanced structures with good vibration damping and noise insulation capability cannot be overemphasized for a wide variety of engineering applications. Among existing techniques, whilst active control methods show their promises in handling low frequency problems, passive means still remain the most effective and reliable option to tackle mid-to-high frequency range. As one of the important vibration and noise control means, wave manipulation is a new emerging concept which draws attention from researchers in many engineering fields. Revealed by relatively recent research and confirmed by our previous work, the phenomenon of the Acoustic Black Hole (ABH) inside a thin-walled structure was shown to exhibit appealing features, which can be further explored for a wide range of applications through structure-borne wave manipulation. This project has addressed some of the existing problems, which hamper the real applications of the ABH-based technology. The significance of the project lies in its direct applicability to a wide range of engineering problems such as noise and vibration control or energy harvesting, which are of direct benefit to both Hong Kong and beyond.

15201015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201015.value: 對於濕熱地區建築, 常用的冷卻除濕技術存在諸多問題。通過獨 立處理熱濕負荷，溶液除濕空調系統目前被普遍認為是一種節 能環保的解決途徑。若將太陽能或廢熱引入溶液再生，則空調 系統的節能潛力可達30-50%。 我們的近期研究發現溶液除濕空調的性能取決於除濕/再生器內 部溶液與空氣及內冷/熱源的綜合傳熱傳質，而其極大程度上受 溶液膜特性影響，包括氣液接觸面積、液膜波動及界面兩側的 流動等。而該問題未被全面分析和描述。基於上述觀察, 本項目 會從理論和實驗上研究溶液膜的特性和傳熱傳質特性。基於理論 及實驗研究，提出通過加大接觸面和液膜波動以增強系統傳熱傳 質的實際解決措施及方法。

15201015.label: Realisation of objectives
15201015.value: For objective 1, we fully achieved the targets we set in our proposal. In the aspect of 2D CFD simulation, we developed a simulation model for the counter-current flow of liquid desiccant falling film flow. The characteristics of air/solution flow with interfacial waves can be obtained conveniently by the built CFD models. The influences of air velocity and solution flow rate on wave dynamics were investigated. The mechanisms of liquid film waves was also explored by analyzing the interfacial information. It is found that the interfacial pressure and velocity fluctuation are the main mechanisms to induce the liquid film waves. We also developed new theoretical models to descript the simultaneous heat and mass transfer process during dehumidification with the consideration of both shrinkage shape, the variable film thickness of falling film and water vapor condensation on non-wetted area. These models were used to analyze the influences of different factors including the contact angle on the heat and mass transfer performance. In addition, we also developed a novel 3D simulation model to analyze the couple turbulent flow with heat and mass transfer for LDAC system. The mass transfer mechanism ant its influencing factors were detailly investigated. Publication directly arising from this objective: Lu H, Lu L, Luo Y, et al. Specifically, for the 2D CFD simulation model, the film thicknesses and typical interfacial waves obtained by the CFD simulations were validated and in consistent with the experimental results. It indicates that the built numerical model can predict the dynamic characteristics of the counter-current flow very well for falling film liquid desiccant flow. In the aspect of theoretical model, the simulation results were compared with the experimental ones. It was found that the new model was able to predict the film shrinkage accurately with the average relative wetting ratio difference less than 4%. All of the simulation results in terms of absolute moisture removal fell within the ±10% error band of the experimental results with an ARD of 4.04%, which proved that the simulation results were reliable. 15201015.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201015.value: Based on present project, both theoretical, numerical and experimental study were carried out to uncover the 2-D/3-D heat and mass transfer characteristic of dehumidifier/regenerator in LDAC system. Some key findings are summarized as follows: On the aspect of theoretical analysis： (1) A new validated model of heat and mass transfer for the internally cooled/heated LDACS was developed concerning the shrinkage shape of falling film and the variable film thickness along the flow direction. Further, the condensation of water vapor on the non-wetted area in an internal cooling dehumidifier was also considered in another model. These model models both indicates that the important effects of film shrinkage and contact angle on the mass transfer performance. On the aspect of CFD simulation, (2) the CFD models for the counter-current flow of LDD were established successfully based on the VOF model and RNG k-ε turbulence model. The film flow was closely influenced by both the liquid flow rate and air velocity. The interfacial pressure and velocity fluctuation are the main mechanisms to induce the liquid film waves. A novel 3D simulation model based on CFD technology was also developed to study the dehumidification performance of a falling film dehumidifier. The simulation results indicate that falling film of liquid desiccant shrank gradually along the flow direction, leading to an inhomogeneous water vapor absorption process in the dehumidifier. Intense water vapor absorption occurs at the phase interface, resulting in large solution concentration gradient and humidity content in the zone near the air/liquid contact interface. On the aspect of experimental study: (3) A double layer TiO2 superhydrophilic coating was developed and the characterization of the coating was conducted. The coating can remarkably enlargement of wettability and dehumidification performance as well. Other enhancement approaches in terms of surface modification and addition of surfactant were also demonstrated obvious mass transfer improvement. Abundant research outcomes have been directly arisen from the present project. Totally, 18 high-quality journal papers have been published (please refer to Part C for the detailed information of these published papers), which include the journals of Applied Energy, Energy, International journal of Heat and Mass et al. Moreover, one PhD student and several final year projects for MsC and undergraduate students were also supported by this project.

15201015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201015.value: Both the theoretical, numerical and experimental study in present project mainly focused on the single-channel dehumidifier/regeneration, which is not the real case for practical application. As a result, further study can be carried out based on a real component to investigate the real heat and mass transfer process in a LDAC system. Moreover, the distribution of air or liquid desiccant for different channels and the influences of flow distribution on performance can be also explored. In addition, different degrees of metal corrosion were observed during our experiments. Therefore, further study can be also focused on the elimination or alleviation of the metal corrosion problem for the steady and continuous operation of LDAC system.

15201015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201015.value: The waves of liquid desiccant falling film has significant effect on flow, heat and mass transfer of dehumidification/regeneration performance in LDAC system. The present project aimed to theoretically and experimentally identify such influence and change the flow deliberately to enhance the heat and mass performance, which will help significantly to improve the system efficient and save energy as well. During these nearly three years project, the present project proposed both theoretical and CFD model to predict the heat and mass transfer characteristics in the LDAC system, which can provide meaningful guidance for the research and design of real components. Moreover, we also developed a novel nano-TiO2 super-hydrophilic coating to effectively improve the wettability of falling film and performance as well. These outcomes and findings have great application potential in the real industry field.
