15202315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15202315.value: The use of three dimensional (3D)-structured surfaces have become more widespread such as self-adhesive sensors, compound lenses for holography in phonics products, bionic applications, bio-medical areas,etc. Despite there being some research studies of the measurement of different types of 3D-structured surfaces such as grooves, pyramids, grid arrays, tessellates,etc., the research of in-situ or in process measurement of these surfaces is still far from complete. Although significant progress has been made in the development of various precision metrology and measuring instruments for 3D-structured surfaces, most of them focus on traditional off-line measurement processes. With the growing demand for the compensation for the machining errors of the workpiece, it is indispensable to develop in-situ measurement methods and metrology systems for 3D-structured surfaces. As a result, this study aims to develop an encoded-light-based autostereoscopic (ELBAS) measurement method and hence an ELBAS metrology system to perform in-situ measurement of 3D-structured surfaces with sub-micrometre form accuracy. By the incorporation of multiple lenses into the optical system (i.e.Freeform Micro Lens Array), the CCD camera can capture multi-angle information of a workpiece through a single snapshot, which enables the ability to create focal stacks from a single photograph of a workpiece to be recorded through the application of stereo matching. This makes the reconstruction of the 3D information of 3D-structured surfaces feasible. With the encoded light introduced to the ELBAS method as the light source, the efficiency and precision of the stereo matching process can be significantly improved, which can directly enhance the measuring resolution. A novel optical system with multiple optical paths will be developed and incorporated into the ELBAS metrology system to improve the spatial resolution of the measurement and realize multi field-of-view(FOV) of measurement so as to enlarge the measurement range while the measuring resolution can be ensured as well. The technological merits of the proposed ELBAS metrology system include the microsecond level measuring speed, multi-FOV measurement range, and the compact design and setup. This makes the ELBAS metrology system suitable to be integrated into ultra-precision machine tools for conducting in-situ measurement of 3D-structured surfaces. The project if successful will not only contribute to the improvement of the efficiency and accuracy of the precision manufacturing process but also enhance the capability of the measurement and characterization of 3D-structured surfaces. The possible outcome of the proposed study will be the development of a novel in-situ or in-process 3D metrology technology for the precision manufacturing of 3D-structured surfaces.

15202315.label: Realisation of objectives
15202315.value: Key issues of the encoded light-based autostereoscopic (ELBAS) measurement method have been investigated in this project, including the autostereoscopic 3D metrology method, the working principle of the encoded light introduced to the autostereoscopic 3D metrology method as the light source, and the design methodologies of the encoded light pattern based on the theory of information rich measurement (Objective 1) The incorporation of encoded light into the autostereoscopic 3D measurement method can impart more features to the acquired raw 3D information, which can directly enable a matching process with higher accuracy and efficiency. The design basis of the encoded light pattern is the a priori knowledge of the surface profile, such as the design data, machining parameters, or measuring data from other credible measuring systems. Both of the greyscale information and colour information of the light can be encoded with a certain pattern. The target surface profile changes the distribution of these two kinds of encoded information after the reflection of imported encoded light to the system. These changes have a relationship with the surface geometrical information and can be detected by the system. Two different design methods have been developed based on the a priori knowledge for application on different types of surfaces (Objective 2). Contour pattern is an effective method that can be universally applied to different types of surfaces, and can represent all three dimensions of the surface with versatile pixel information distribution (PID) due to the direct relationship between the height information and the lateral information. This contour pattern design method makes use of the Y component of the YCbCr colour space, which represents the luminance that can directly influence the light intensity after the encoded illumination. This can actively control the over exposed part due to the low surface roughness and create features for the matching process due to the featureless continuous surface type. Another encoded pattern design method is also developed based the artificial control over greyscale information regarding different spatial locations of every sample point of the surface profile, which is provided by the a priori information of the structured surfaces. Various schemes can be used to provide versatile PID associated with a specific surface profile, such as sinusoidal distribution, linear distribution, or identical distribution to the design surface profile. These two developed encoded pattern design methods offer competitive performance for providing versatile PID rather than featureless information under normal illumination, especially when faced with special surface features such as high slope, inner reflection caused by low surface roughness, or the over exposed part due to the low surface roughness. The acquired 3D raw information under encoded pattern illumination has a much-diversified distribution of pixel information for the matching process of 3D raw data reconstruction to realize better accuracy and efficiency. Related reconstruction methods of 3D raw data have been studied and developed with the encoded information acquired by the ELBAS system (Objective 1 & Objective 2). In other disparity matching processes of the autostereoscopic 3D system under normal illumination, the determination of matching criterion is groundless conjecture or a post learning process based on the current PID. This generates random errors in the matching process and adversely affects the measuring results. In this project, the matching criterion was predictable according to the a priori knowledge of the encoded light. Different spatial locations of the elemental lenses in a MLA cause small differences in the elemental images (EIs) received on the image sensor (known as disparities). The corresponding points (CPs), which are the image points from different EIs, originate from an identical single object point in the object. CPs need to be accurately chosen among pixels in EIs during the disparity matching process and form the 3D digital reconstruction at corresponding spatial locations in order to reconstruct 3D information. The traditional method first constructs an initial disparity map by the difference of the target and the reference positions, using multi-criteria, including the absolute difference (ABD) and the gradient difference (GRD) of various directions between the to-be-determined point and the referenced point. A refined disparity map which is used to constrain the difference between the initial map and itself is obtained by taking a “winner-takes-all” strategy. Moreover, featured details originating from the encoded light illumination which are captured by the autostereoscopic 3D metrology system as the 3D raw data are processed by Scale-invariant feature transform (SIFT) to become a third matching criterion for the disparity information extraction. The SIFT criterion is used to constrain the difference between the initial map and the one generated by it to maintain the consistency of using different methods. Finally, the final estimated disparity map is obtained after integrating these results together with multipliers. To avoid choosing the multipliers of multiple criteria manually, an artificial intelligence (AI) matching process is used, where the determination of the multiplier of each criterion is finished by a learning model (Objective 2). In addition, the AI matching process is able to learn a complicated non-linear processer to estimate disparity, whereas the traditional matching process only makes use of simple fixed convolutional kernels to process image data. A prototype of the ELBAS metrology system has been developed accordingly (Objective 2), which consists of a main imaging lens and a microlens array for generating multiple 2D images of the target scene from different perspectives, an imaging sensor and a digital projector with full HD resolution used for providing customized encoded light to the system as the light source. The design of the encoded light is customized and generated by Matlab software. Meanwhile, a smart portable projector is used in the development of the proposed metrology system in order to provide an encoded light pattern for the system. The projector is motionless, and the projected encoded light pattern also remains still without any movement for phase shift generation. Experimental studies have been conducted to verify the ELBAS system and the proposed multi-criterion-based disparity information extraction algorithm (Objective 3). Different kinds of freeform surfaces have been measured through the developed system. The features of the measured surface are well reconstructed in 3D space under encoded light illumination while the features are merely detected under normal illumination due to the homogeneous PID. The over-exposure issue has limited influence on the information loss and the accuracy of the experimental results are significantly improved due to the use of patterned illumination and the associated reconstruction method. Both cross reference evaluation and artefact evaluation were conducted to verify the performance of the ELBAS measurement method through uncertainty analysis (Objective 4). A credible offline metrology system was used to provide reference measuring data evaluation. An Iterative Closest Point (ICP) method was adopted to obtain the best surface registration between the reference data and the experimental data for uncertainty analysis. The difference between experimental and reference data shows the minimum value that can be credibly resolved by the experimental system, which is regarded as the system resolution. Moreover, an artefact based on a combination of VDI/VDE and ISO specification standards was also used to conduct uncertainty analysis (Objective 4), which indicates that the developed measurement system achieves standard measurement uncertainties of around 40 μm of probing form, size and sphere spacing when the relative resolution is greater than 1/500 compared to the overall field of view (FOV).

15202315.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202315.value: In this project, the core theories, key issues and science and technology for the encoded light-based autostereoscopic (ELBAS) measurement method have been investigated, including the autostereoscopic 3D metrology method (Conference paper 1, Conference Paper 2 and Conference paper 4), the working principle of the encoded light introduced to the autostereoscopic 3D metrology method as the light source (Journal paper 2 and Journal paper 3) and in-situ measurement method (Journal paper 1 and Conference paper 3). Hence, a novel optical method using encoded light as a motionless light source for purposely manipulating and utilizing the pixel information distribution (PID) of the target surface in both hardware and software manners to enhance the relative resolution as the weakness of this autostereoscopic 3D measurement method (Journal paper 2 and Journal paper 3) was used. The a priori information was incorporated to design the encoded illumination pattern. Two design methods of encoded light information were developed accordingly to artificially control the colour/greyscale pixel information distribution. The use of encoded light is able to provide illumination with dominant features for the matching process even when faced with various freeform surfaces with inconspicuous features, high slopes, inner reflection or low surface roughness. A prototype autostereoscopic system was built and incorporated on ultra-precision machine for in-situ measurement of V-groove microstructure surfaces on a precision roller (Conference paper 3) . Both the traditional and a machine learning-based multi-criterion disparity matching process were developed for high matching accuracy and efficiency. The relative resolution of the proposed system is significantly improved to reach over 1/500, through uncertainty analysis using both the cross reference method and artefact based on international standards (Journal paper 3). Incorporating encoded light information as artificial manipulation of pixel information distribution is a new pioneering attempt to successfully achieve better measuring performance of autostereoscopic 3D measurement systems when the PID under normal illumination is homogeneous. It is also an effective optical metrological approach to apply in the measurement of various freeform and structured surfaces with the solid use of the readily available, interpretable and accessible a priori knowledge. Up to present, one PhD student has been trained. Two refereed journal papers have been published and one refereed journal paper is under review to disseminate the research results of the project. The results of the project have also been presented in four refereed International conferences. One conference paper (Conference Paper 3) has been awarded the best paper award.

15202315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202315.value: Some suggestions for future work are given below: a. In-process ELBAS system for high-performance measurements The ELBAS system developed in this project has potential to be used to perform in-process and on-machine measurements due to its compact system setup and fast data acquisition which will have a wider use in the field of ultra-precision machining technologies. The current measurement data processing time limits the overall in-process measuring time due to the heavy computation. As a result, Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) acceleration will be used to reduce the data processing time which will enable the proposed system to perform in-process measurement with ultra-precision machine tools. b. AI-based colour contour encoded pattern design and adjustments AI techniques will be adopted to learn the colour contour encoded pattern design method when faced with various freeform surfaces. The AI techniques will learn to actively and effectively adjust the encoded illumination status to acquire better PID for the matching process through tuning the colour information and generating masks for the over exposed region. c. Embedded system development for the ELBAS system The ELBAS system will be further developed as a compact and embedded system which will be attached to an ultra-precision machine tool to provide high-performance 3D measurement for various surface profiles.

15202315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202315.value: In this project, an encoded light-based autostereoscopic metrology system (ELBAS) has been developed for the in-situ measurement of three-dimensional (3D) structured surfaces. This system makes use of a novel encoded light-based illumination method by projecting custom-designed patterns onto different freeform and structured surfaces. The pattern is purposely designed based on the prior knowledge of the target freeform and structured surface with developed methodologies. The projected pattern can manipulate the pixel information distribution of the acquired image to enhance the diversity for more accuracy matching and an efficient matching process of 3D raw information. Hence, the resolution of the system is increased and the error due to over exposed regions from the measured surface is reduced. Both the traditional data processing method and an artificial intelligent (AI) based method have been developed for the patterned illumination. Experimental studies of different target surfaces show that the performance of this 3D measuring system is significantly improved. This project leads to the development of a novel 3D metrology technology for possible in-situ measurement of freeform and structured surfaces. The research not only enhances the capability of the in-situ measurement of freeform and structured surfaces but also contributes to the possible improvement of the efficiency and accuracy of the precision manufacturing process.

15202415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15202415.value: Health, safety, and environmental (HSE) disruptions have emerged as a critical aspect of manufacturing firms in China. Based on High Reliability Theory (HRT), this study investigated the key antecedents of the HSE disruptions of listed manufacturing firms in Hong Kong and China. The key antecedents, production complexity, coupling, and capacity were derived and extended from HRT. This study determines the likelihood of HSE disruptions with particular production characteristics after studying the significance of these key antecedents (and other prediction factors). The findings obtained in this study can enable sourcing companies in Hong Kong and China to identify safer suppliers or develop a strategy to prevent HSE disruptions. The findings can also support public policy makers regarding occupational safety and pollution because these findings allow them to develop more specific regulations to minimize HSE problems in production. They can increase the number of inspections of high-risk firms to prevent HSE accidents. In this study, HSE disruption incident data of all the listed manufacturing firms in Hong Kong and China (approximately 2000 companies) are collected from mulitple publically available databases. Their firm performance data are collected from the Thompson Reuters database. A three-step approach is adopted to determine the antecedents of HSE disruption and the association between HSE disruption and firm risk. Finally, the influence of the key antecedents (i.e., production complexity, coupling, and capacity) on abnormal firm risk over multiple years is also evaluated. 健康，安全和環境意外（Health, Safety and Environmental Disruptions –簡稱 HSE Disruptions）對中國製造企業的影響正在成為一個重要的研究方向。基於高可靠性理論（HRT），我們會研究在香港和中國大陸上市的製造業企業的運作中找出導致健康，安全和環境意外的原因, 例如生產的複雜性以, 連接性及生產容量。通過了解這些關鍵的原因（和其他預測因素），我們將揭示健康，安全和環境意外與特定生產特性的關係。這研究會發現會幫助香港和中國大陸採購公司在選擇供應商時，能找出較安全（風險較小）的供應商，或制定一項戰略，以避免健康，安全和環境意外。這項研究還支持職業安全和污染公共政策制定者，因為它允許他們制定更為具體的規定，以盡量減少健康，安全和環境意外問題。他們還可以增加檢查的高風險企業的數量，以避免安全環境事故發生。我們將收集從湯普森路透數據庫中的香港和中國大陸（約2000公司）所有上市製造業企業的業績數據, 以及他們所有健康，安全和環境意外事件的數據。我們採取三步的方式來揭示健康，第一步是找出安全和環境意外的原因，第二步是揭示健康，安全和環境意外和公司風險之間的關係，第三步是研究這些導致意外的原因（即生產的複雜性例如生產的複雜性以, 連接性及生產容量）是否對企業的運作風險有多年並持續的影響。

15202415.label: Realisation of objectives
15202415.value: All the objectives have been completed based on the project plan, and the core manuscript prepared based on the proposal is currently under review in the International Journal of Production Economics, a premier journal focusing on manufacturing and operations management. We collected public manufacturing firms financial data from CSMAR database. We then searched each firm's name in the databases of IPE and SAWS to obtain their HSE incidents. All four objectives are successfully completed, and allow me to explain them below. Objective 1. To reveal the key antecedents of HSE disruptions of Chinese manufacturing firms. Based on the collected the financial data of the manufacturing firms in China, and their occupational safety, and environmental violation data. We constructed a panel database that allows us to predict the propensity of an HSE violation of particular firms using logistics regression. We tested production capacity, return on sales, total assets, firm age, quick ratio, cash on hand, receivable days, working capital, average salary, board size, top management team ownership and percentage of independent directors, and their industry type, as the antecedent. We also tested labor intensity (as a measurement of operational complexity) and reversed inventory days (as a measurement of operational coupling). We found that labor intensity, reversed inventory days, production capacity, return on sales, total assets, firm ages, working capital will increase the likelihood of HSE incidents. While quick ratio will have a negative effect on the HSE incident likelihood. Objective 2 To assist Hong Kong sourcing/buying offices to identify safer suppliers Our findings provide a strong implication for sourcing and buying offices in Hong Kong, as they should look beyond the voluntary management certifications, such as ISO 14001 or OHSAS 18001, in their supplier selection process. The buyers should look at the factory HSE violations, and the key antecedents to evaluate how likely the supplier would commit an HSE violation in the future. Based on the findings, the factory that has more automation would lower the propensity of the HSE incident. Objective 3 To investigate the association between HSE disruptions and firm risk We captured an abnormal increase in systematic risk one year after the HSE incidents. Specifically, the median of systematic risk of sample firms increases 0.27 compared to the control firms from year 0 to year 1 (p < .1). The cumulated abnormal systematic risk from the year -1 to year 1 is also positive (0.042, p < .01), and the positive effects remain significant in the period from the year -1 to 2 (0.024, p < .1). Objective 4. To extend high-reliability theory by investigating the level of production complexity and coupling, and capacity on the relationship between HSE disruptions and firm risk. Based on 198 safety and 458 environmental incident conducted by 318 manufacturing firms in China, we find that reducing operation complexity (measured as labor intensity) and coupling (measured as inventory days) can reduce the likelihood and mitigate the abnormal systematic risk of HSE incidents. We conducted a cross-sectional regression analysis, using the abnormal systematic risk as the dependent variables, the independent variables in the prediction model as control factors, and we tested if labor intensity and reversed inventory days affect the abnormal risk. The coefficient of labor intensity is significantly positive (0.039, p < .05). If we hold other factors in constant, changing the labor intensity from zero to the mean (1.316), the abnormal systematic risk increases by 0.051. The coefficient of reversed inventory days is significantly positive (0.0002, p < .1). Holding other factors in constant, decrease the inventory days the average level (209.27 days) to zero, the abnormal systematic risk increases by 0.042. These findings provide clear implications that reducing production complexity and coupling could help reduce the firm long-term systematic risks.

15202415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202415.value: The major findings of this project revealed the key antecedent of HSE violations in China. We found that production capacity, return on sales, total assets, firm age, quick ratio, working capital, labor intensity (as a measurement of operational complexity) and reversed inventory days (as a measurement of operational coupling) are strong predictors of HSE incidents in China. We also found that the HSE incidents will increase the systematic risk of the violating firms, while this abnormal risk can be minimized by automation and providing more safety inventory. These findings are under review in the International Journal of Production Economics. Second major findings are we revealed the dynamic between innovation, family business and sustainability events in other emerging market. We used a similar research methodology to test the Korea data provided by Dr. Antonio Lau from Kyung Hee University. We found that family business and innovation investment have a positive impact on firms sustainability events, which is a novel perspective to the operations management literature. These findings are submitted to the Journal of Business Ethics and invited for revision (R1).

15202415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202415.value: At the later stage of this project, based on the literature review, the family-controlled business and firm innovativeness could also be good predictors of HSE incidents in other emerging markets. However, the data available in the China market is not readily available and enough for further investigation. We collaborate with Dr. Antonio Lau from Kyung Hee University in Seoul, to investigate the dynamics of HSE events, family business, and innovation. First, we determined a positive relationship between sustainability events and firms’ market value, which indicates that firms in emerging countries can benefit from supporting corporate sustainability. Second, we found that chaebol (family business) has a positive effect on the relationship between sustainability and market value. Thus, chaebol managers should note that they can increase shareholder wealth through sustainability practices. Finally, we found that innovation investment could enhance the positive impact of a firm’s sustainability efforts, which provides an alternative route for nonchaebol firms to enhance the benefits of their sustainability efforts. This study has been submitted to Journal of Business Ethics, and being invited for revision (R1).

15202415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202415.value: This study has revealed the key antecedents of health, safety and environment (HSE) incidents among manufacturing firms in China. We revealed that reducing the level of production complexity and coupling could help reduce the likelihood of HSE disruptions. We need to concern about HSE disruption because we found that it would increase firms’ systematic risks in the long run, showing that investors would view these violating firms are riskier, and thus affect their investment decisions. To reduce the systematic risk, we also found that reducing the level of production complexity and coupling also reduce the abnormal systematic risk for violating firms. It shows a clear strategy for firms that had violation should consider restructure their production process and focus on automation, which will help reduce HSE incident and its risk in future. We further investigate how innovation and family business (not common in China market) could affect the impact of HSE events in Korea, suggesting that HSE incident would have a similar impact on firms in other countries. The findings enriched our understanding of HSE issues in emerging markets.

15203615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203615.value: Textile structures with negative Poisson’s ratio (NPR) are nonconventional structures that can laterally expand when stretched. This unusual behavior makes them very attractive for many applications in different areas. The most important point to the realization of NPR textiles is the proper design of their structures and manufacturing processes. A survey of the literature has shown that NPR textiles so far developed are only based on helical yarn structure and knitted fabric structures, and the study of NPR textiles based on braided structures are still lacking. Therefore, there is a need to conduct a study of NPR braided structures to get a basic understanding on their deformation behavior, mechanical properties and manufacturing process. More specifically, the project will deal with fundamental issues of the structure and mechanical behavior of NPR braided structure that is formed by insertion of stiff yarns into a tubular base braided structure. Based on previous studies done by the PI, a special manufacturing process will be developed to fabricate this kind of nonconventional textile structure. Various NPR braided samples will be produced using different kinds of yarns and structural parameters. Both theoretical and experimental studies will be conducted to investigate their deformation behavior and mechanical properties. The knot strength will be studied as well when two NPR braided cords are tied together.

15203615.label: Realisation of objectives
15203615.value: Objective 1: This objective was totally achieved. A new type of braided structure with negative Poisson’s ratio was designed. In the first design, we suggested to regularly insert stiff yarns into a hollow circular braided structure by passing them from the outside to the inside of the braid wall to produce NPR effect. However, after a series of preliminary studies, we found that as slippage effect of stiff yarns could easily take place under stretch and the wall thickness of circular braided structure was limited, the produced NPR effect was not so high as expected. Therefore, we modified the first design by wrapping a stiff yarn around a circular braided structure inserted with a soft core yarn. At the same time, we also studied the relationships between the modified geometry and its NPR behavior. After the study, we found that the modified design was efficient to produce the braided structure with high NPR. Objective 2: This objective was totally achieved. A special braiding process was first developed to fabricate the NPR braided structure by the modification of a circular braiding process. Based on the process developed, we constructed a prototype with the use of 16 braiding yarns and a core for fabricating NPR braided samples with different types of yarns and geometrical parameters including yarn diameter, braiding angle and wrap angle. However, the first process had some limitations since existing braiding machines could not be used. In order to produce NPR braided samples with more efficiency and lower costs, another process was developed. In the new process, a conventional braiding machine was used to produce NRP braided samples by just replacing one braiding yarn with a stiffer yarn. Using the new process, a series of NPR braids with better quality were easier produced on a 16-yarn carries circular braiding machine for testing. Objective 3: This objective was totally achieved. The deformation behaviors and mechanical properties of the NPR braid samples produced were experimentally studied through uniaxial tensile tests. Based on testing results, the relationships between the Poisson’s ratio and tensile strain, the tensile stress and tensile strain for the NPR braids made with different yarn materials and different structural parameters were generated. Objective 4: This objective was totally achieved. Both the geometrical and finite element analyses of the NPR braided structure developed were conducted in detail. Based on these analyses, the models which can be used to predict the deformation behavior and mechanical properties of the NPR braided structure were successfully established and compared with experiments.

15203615.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203615.value: 1. New NPR braided structures and manufacturing processes developed to produce auextic circular braids by using conventional braiding machine. It is found that auxetic behavior can be achieved into a tubular braided structure by winding a stiff yarn around a conventional circular braid or just replacing a softer braiding yarn with a stiffer yarn in braiding process. The study has provided a new approach to produce NPR braids with a simple way and low costs by using conventional braiding machinery. (Please refer to the publications 1-2 as attached in Part C). 2. Dependency of the auxetic behavior on tensile strain. All the experimental studies have confirmed that the auxetic behavior of NPR braids first increases and then decreases with increase of the tensile strain. It is also found that all the NPR braids with different braiding angles have different auxetic behavior and the NPR braids have low braiding angle have better auxetic behavior when stretched in axial direction. (Please refer to publications 1-2 attached in Part C). 3. The geometrical model developed to theoretically calculate the Poisson’s ratio values of the NPR braided structure formed with winding a stiff yarn around a conventional circular braid. It is found that dividing the deformation process of a NPR tubular braided structure into two stages is not very realistic because the wrap stiff yarn cannot be totally straightened before it is broken under axial tension. It is also found that the geometrical modeling can only predict the deformation behavior of NPR braided structure at low tensile strain level. (Please refer to publication 3 attached in Part C). 4. Finite element model developed to simulate the deformation behavior of the NPR braided structure formed with replacement of a softer braiding yarn by a stiffer yarn during braiding process. It is found that the braided structure could achieve a robust auxetic behavior and its Poisson’s ratio and stiffness are strongly dependent on their initial micro-geometric parameters, especially initial braiding angle and diameter of component yarns. It is also found that a maximum NPR of -9.49 could be achieved by lowering the angle value to 15° and higher NPR effect could be obtained with grosser stiff yarn and finer elastic yarns. (Please refer to publication 4 attached in Part C). 5. Four refereed journal papers, one chapter book and three oral presentations at international conferences.

15203615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203615.value: The proposed project is concerned with a systematic study of braided structure with negative Poisson’s ratio (NPR). The NPR braids are first designed and fabricated based on circular braiding technology. Then, the deformation behavior and mechanical properties of the NPR braids produced under tensile loading conditions are experimentally and theoretically studied. Geometrical and finite element models are finally developed to predict the deformation behavior of this special type of braided structure. The significance and value of the project is to provide a basic understanding on the structure characteristics, formation principle, fabricating method, deformation behavior and mechanical properties of NPR braided structure. The study will provide direct insights into the design and fabrication of NPR braided structure with nonconventional behavior. Thanks to its unusual properties different from conventional braided structure, the newly developed NPR braided structure will be very attractive for medical applications such as smart bandages and surgical sutures with automatic control of drug release. The study will promote the new development of textile products using the latest concept and technologies to increase the competitive capacity of the Hong Kong textile and fashion industry.

15203815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203815.value: Lightning in tropical and sub-tropical areas generates substantial transient electromagnetic fields around buildings, and induces transient voltages and currents in power and communication systems in buildings. These transients can cause faults, malfunction or even physical damage to sensitive equipment. Lightning-generated electromagnetic transients in buildings are greatly affected by the building structures, including reinforcing bars in columns and beams. They are also even more affected by metal decking, raised floor panels and other plates on the floors, walls or ceilings. These planar structures substantially alter the transient electromagnetic environment during a lightning strike. Therefore, it is necessary to develop an effective mean of evaluating and characterizing electromagnetic transients in buildings. Currently there has been little discussion on lightning-generated electromagnetic transients associated with planar structures in buildings. One major difficulty encountered in such transient analysis is that there is no adequate modelling approach available for large planar structures. This project aims at developing an efficient procedure for solving lightning-generated electromagnetic transients in a planar structure using an equivalent circuit method. An extended partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) will be formulated for efficient modeling of planar structures and evaluation of electromagnetic transients. In this formulation the spatial distribution of current density within the plates will be fully taken into account in order to reduce the number of unknowns in a system equation. With the developed procedure, lightning-generated transient electromagnetic fields in buildings can be characterized. Lightning-induced surges in wiring systems can be evaluated as well. The outputs will be used for efficient routing of electrical wires, such as power lines, control wires, communication wires, etc. Guidelines will be made available to tenants, equipment installers, building owners, and developers for better planning and installation of sensitive equipment. 閃電会生成巨大的瞬變電磁場，继而在建筑物中的電力和通信系統誘導出瞬態電壓和電流。這些瞬變過程可以導致电子設備出现故障、甚至物理損壞。 建築物中的金属結構对雷電產生的電磁暫態影响很大。金属結構包括梁和柱中的鋼筋，以及楼面钢承板，高架地板系統和铺在地板、 牆壁或天花板上的其他金属板。在雷擊過程中，這些平面結構大大地改變了瞬變電磁環境。因此，有必要对其開展性能評價和提出表徵建築物電磁暫態過程的有效手段。 目前对閃電電磁暫態與建築平面結構相關议题討論得很少。在閃電瞬態分析中遇到的一個主要困難是没有大型平面結構的有效建模方法。該專案旨在開發用于閃電電磁暫態過程分析的高效求解平面結構的等效電路法。此方法将充分考慮板內的電流密度空間分佈，以达到減少系統方程中未知函數的個數。 本项目的结果可用於评估建築物中由閃電產生的瞬變電磁場以及感應过电压，有助于向設備安裝人员，大廈業主和技术開發人員規劃和安裝的敏感設備提供指引。

15203815.label: Realisation of objectives
15203815.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved generally. (a) Modern buildings are constructed with steel structures, such as reinforced steel bars, and steel beam and columns. In addition to these elements, raised floor panels and metal decking are often adopted for some large buildings. Such buildings can be represented with an interconnected wire-plate structure during a lightning strike. Such a wire-plate structure may carry lightning current, which generates lightning transients in power and signal circuits, and would affect normal operation of electric supply and telecommunication systems. The partial electrical equipment circuit method (PEEC) is an approach for modelling electromagnetic coupling of thin wires. It transforms a field problem into the circuit domain problem, and solve the problem using conventional circuit analysis tool. However, it has not been applied to solve the problem containing large planar structures. In this project, an efficient PEEC formulation for the wire-plate structure has been developed to address lightning transients in the context of a ground structure. The wires in the structures cannot be considered as the filament wires. They may have non-circular cross sections, and both the skin-effect and proximity effect could not be neglected. Different techniques, i.e., unique 2D meshing techniques and analytical functions, have been developed theoretically, and applied for modelling the wires and plates, respectively. With such techniques, it is not necessary to use a 3D meshing scheme for the structure, which may lead to an unsolvable problem. Further improvements have been made subsequently to simplify the PEEC formulation and to speed up numerical computation. For example, a linear and weak magnetic model has been developed experimentally for ferromagnetic materials under a lightning strike. An artificial neutral network trained method has been introduced to extract high-frequency circuit parameters, which is very difficult to obtain because of the strong skin effect. Ground is an important issue in addressing lightning transients on the ground structure. The effect of the ground is fully addressed by using the Green’s functions. The general mixed potential equations were employed to derive the PEEC formulation for the conductors in the lossy ground. The general expressions of dyadic Green’s functions for vector magnetic potential and scalar Green’s functions for electrical potential have been derived. The algorithms have been implemented in the platform of MATLAB to calculate these Green’s functions for the source and field points in the same medium or different media in a two-medium space. Additional work has been performed to develop the quasi-static PEEC formulation for conductors in the presence of a lossy ground, which has not been addressed by others in the literature. In such formulation, the lossy ground can be simplified to be a set of images. This model is similar to the image method, but is not identical to the traditional image method. (b) Both frequency-domain and time-domain solution procedures have been developed in this project. In the frequency-domain procedure, circuit parameters such as resistance, inductance and capacitance are calculated at selected frequencies. To obtain a quick solution, ANN-trained method has been developed, and has been successfully applied to extract high-frequency results for transient analysis. This procedure is the most stable, and accurate. The time-domain procedure can provide the results efficiently in a short time. Several issues were encountered in the development of the time-domain solution, i.e, frequency dependent circuit parameters, retardation among different elements and others. The vector -fitting technique was applied to resolve the frequency-variant problems. These parameters are eventually substituted with frequency-invariant circuit parameters using the rational functions. The full-wave PEEC formulation has been proposed by considering the retardation effect, particularly arising from the ground in the problem. Experimental studies have been performed to validate the simulation models and solution procedures. Tests on the magnetic components such as rebars, flat bars, U-shape channel, and others have been performed to develop the simplified PEEC model. Experiments on scaled models of a tower and others have also been performed in the laboratory to test the accuracy of the models and solutions. (c) The lightning transients in ground structures have been evaluated using the developed solution procedures. These ground structures include the buildings, telecommunication towers, and photovoltaic power plants and others. Different sites, such buildings, one PV power station, two telecommunication towers have been visited, and site parameters required for modelling have been collected. System models for those structures have been developed, and lightning transients in the power supply networks and telecommunication systems were investigated numerically. Typical waveforms and surge current levels were disclosed. Both protective device installation arrangement and equipotential bonding position can greatly influence the lightning transients, and recommendations are provided. Shielding performance of the wire-plate structure was revealed, and effective shielding was found under an indirect lightning trike. These results can be used to design effective lightning protection for the power and telecommunication systems as well as PV systems. The effectiveness of protective devices is evaluated in telecommunication systems, and effective protective measures are provided for PV systems. The PEEC formulation has also been extended for use by other approaches, and hybrid models have been developed for lightning analysis in more complicated simulations. Several PEEC/FDTD hybrid models have been proposed and tested to the good accuracy. In these models, the PEEC formulation was mainly used to deal with skin and proximity effects of the wires in the FDTD simulations. A second PEEC/FDTD hybrid model has been tried to solve lightning transients in a large-scale problem. In this model, the fine structure is represented with the PEEC method, and lightning channel and it generates electromagnetic field is simulated with the FDTD method. In addition, the developed PEEC method has also been applied to derive time-domain wave equations in a vertical conductor, which is similar to the traditional transmission line, but not the same. The concept of transient impedance of the line has been introduced for the first time.

15203815.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203815.value: Fifteen journal papers and four conference papers have been published with the support from this project. Under a lightning strike, a building can be viewed as a wire-plate structure, which may carry direct lightning current and induced lightning current. A complete model of this wire-plate structure under a lightning strike has been developed in this project [J1]. An efficient model of plates using an analytical function was proposed, and its improvement was presented in [J13]. With this semi-analytical model, computation efficiency for 3D problems has been improved significantly [J3,J7,C1,C4], as only 1D or 2D meshing is required. It is found in this project that ferromagnetic structure in buildings can be represented with linear weak magnetism materials, and a simplified model is presented [J5]. A two-level surrogate based optimization process has been proposed to produce optimal design of multi-layer shields using plates [J15]. Modelling of wires of circular and non-circular cross section has been also addressed in this project. Several special meshing techniques including artificial neutral network (ANN) method have been developed to extract circuit parameters of these wires [J4, J6]. This ANN trained method is particularly used for extracting high-frequency results with low-frequency matrices. The ground has a great effect on the lightning transients if the structure is close to the ground surface. In this project, a precise description of the ground effect has been addressed using the Green’s functions [14]. The quasi-static model is first developed for the PEEC formulation in this paper. The model of the wires buried in the ground also was proposed, and was validated experimentally [J9]. A full-wave time-domain PEEC solution procedure has been developed for the structure with the ground effect being considered. The retardation between the structure in air and its image under the ground is fully taken into account [J11]. Some other issues have also been addressed. In [J2,C3], the PEEC approach has been employed to address lightning wave propagation over a vertical conductor. Transient impedance of a vertical conductor has been presented for the first time, is used to discuss the wave propagation, similar to the traditional transmission line. The PEEC approach has been integrated with the FDTD approach to address transient problems on wire strictures. This PEEC approach was particularly useful in addressing skin effects and modelling conductor losses [J8, J12] for wires. A hybrid PEEC/FDTD method has been developed to lightning-induced transients in a large-scale problem [C2]. In this model, the fine structure is represented with the PEEC method, and lightning channel and it generates electromagnetic field is simulated with the FDTD method. An advanced impulse magnetic field sensor has been developed with the size in cm2, the bandwidth up to 1MHz, and the sensitivity in mG [J13,C4]. The developed model and solution procedure have been applied to address lightning transients in buildings, telecommunication towers, photovoltaic power plants [J3,J4,J7,J10,J13]. Lighting currents in power circuits and electronic circuits can then be assessed for risk analysis and protection evaluation.

15203815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203815.value: A PEEC formulation has been developed to model building structure on the ground during a lightning strike. In this project, the lightning is represented with a hard current source with a pre-defined current waveform. In reality, a fixed current waveform for the lightning strikes is not realistic, because of the mutual influence between the lightning channel and ground structure. Given by a fixed amount lightning energy, transient currents on the ground would be different if the mutual coupling is taken into account. A hybrid model for both lightning channel and ground structure would be necessary to address the lightning transient risk and to design effective lightning protection. In the lightning channel, special issues would be investigated further, such as corona sheath, non-linearity of channel core, initial charge deposited on the corona sheath, local breakdown within the corona sheath, etc. Some other issues would also be interesting to engineers for the design of lightning protection, such as the integration of short wires and long wires during a lightning strike. As these wires are modeled with different approaches, the integration techniques need to be investigated further.

15203815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203815.value: Lightning in tropical and sub-tropical areas generates substantial transient electromagnetic fields around buildings, and induces transient voltages and currents in power and telecommunication systems. These transients can cause faults, malfunction or even physical damage to sensitive equipment. Lightning-generated electromagnetic transients in buildings are greatly affected by the building structures. These structures substantially alter the transient electromagnetic environment during a lightning strike. Therefore, it is necessary to develop an effective mean of evaluating and characterizing electromagnetic transients in buildings. The lightning-generated electromagnetic transients associated with wire-plate structures in buildings have been addressed in this project. The challenges have been identified, such as modelling large planar structures and wires with non-circular cross section. An efficient procedure using the extended partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) has been provided. In this formulation the special techniques, such as, adopting an analytical function, ANN trained model, vector fitting method and others were employed to simplify the model and speed up computation. With the developed procedure, lightning-generated transients in buildings, telecommunication towers, photovoltaic power plants, etc. are investigated and characterized. The outputs can be used for efficient routing of electrical wires, such as power lines, control wires, communication wires, and for better planning and installation of sensitive equipment.

The non-homogeneity of underground media will be discussed and analyzed under conditions of groundwater seepage. To find the optimized geometry of foundation pile heat exchangers including both single pile and multi-pile systems. To develop a software package and design guideline enabling engineers to use ground piles as ground heat exchangers in ground coupled heat pumps air-conditioning.

15203915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203915.value: As a form of renewable energy resource and capable of providing better energy efficiency than traditional air-conditioning systems, ground-coupled heat pumps (GCHP) are being developed very rapidly, especially in mainland China, an alternative means of space heating and cooling of buildings with reduced carbon emissions. Borehole ground heat exchangers (GHEs) are the most popular type of heat exchangers found in GCHP systems. U-tubes are installed in the boreholes containing circulating fluid for heat exchange purpose with the ground media. However, the much higher initial costs due to the cost of drilling deep boreholes and the substantial land area needed for installing borehole GHEs are regarded as two most serious problems. Using the building foundation concrete piles, as GHEs, can overcome those two problems. This innovative idea, utilizing what are usually called ‘energy-piles’, has led to notable progress in the field of GCHP applications and has become particularly attractive to developers in urban areas because it offers a lower total cost for a higher heat transfer efficiency and less in spatial requirements. Recently, spiral-coils type is being used instead of long U-tubes because the spiral coil configuration has a greater heat transfer area and a better flow pattern with no air choking in the pipes. This project is to investigate the theoretical quantities of heat and mass transfer occurring between pile foundation GHEs with spiral coils and the surrounding medium when three-dimensional groundwater advection flow is occurring. Different types of soils will be studied in both saturated and unsaturated states. An inverse numerical heat and mass transfer simulation model will be developed using the conjugate gradient method to find optimal spiral coil designs which can minimize overall thermal resistance. Three spiral coil geometric parameters, the radius of the tube, r, the ratio r/R where R is the radius of the coil and the ratio h/R where h is the pitch between rings of the coil, will be simultaneously optimized to obtain the minimal thermal resistance. An experimental lab test rig will be established to validate the theoretical analysis and numerical simulations of the energy piles. The three-dimensional seepage effects will be simulated by an assemblage of thin plastic boards spaced so that water can flow between them. The orientation of the plastic boards can be adjusted to allow the flow direction of groundwater to be changed. An engineering design guideline and associated design software will be developed to assist researchers and engineers. 地源熱泵作為一種可再生能源技術，其發展十分迅速，尤其在中國大陸地區得到了廣泛應用，將其作為實現建築物供熱和製冷的方式之一，能夠減少二氧化碳的排放量。作為系統主要的部分，鑽孔地熱換熱器是目前地源熱泵系統中應用最普及的換熱器，U型管被安裝於鑽孔中，管內部有迴圈液流動，從而實現與地下介質的熱交換。然而，由於鑽孔所導致的非常高的初投資以及佈置鑽孔地熱換熱器所需要的大量土地面積，被認為是兩個嚴重的不利因素，利用建築物的樁基作為地熱換熱器可以克服這兩個問題。這種具有創新性的地熱換熱器被稱為能量樁，為地源熱泵的應用起到了明顯的推動作用。能量樁對於城市的開發商們尤其具有吸引力，因為其既具有較高的換熱效率，又能減少系統的總造價及所需的用於佈置換熱器的土地面積。近年來，螺旋型線圈埋管正逐漸被採用到能量樁技術中，取代了傳統的U-型管，因為螺旋管具有更大的換熱面積，內部迴圈液的流動模式良好從而不宜產生空氣阻塞。本課題將進行這種能量樁的傳熱傳質方面的理論研究，目標是對地下水滲流以三維模式的流動模型類比與螺旋管的樁埋管換熱器時的傳熱，即周圍的地下介質與樁埋管換熱器之間所發生的傳熱過程。含有地下水的不同類型的地下介質，在飽和及不飽和狀態下的影響也將會被研究。一個逆向的傳熱傳質的數值類比模型將會被提出，該模型將用共軛梯度法以實現螺旋管的優化設計，從而使整體的熱阻最小化。螺旋管的三個幾何參數，即換熱管的直徑r, r與螺旋線圈半徑R的比值，以及r與螺旋線圈間距h的比值都將會考慮，這三個參數將會被同時使用以減少熱阻實現優化。一個工程設計指引以及相關的專業軟體將會被研製，可説明研究人員和工程人員更有效的開展工作。

15203915.label: Realisation of objectives
15203915.value: All the objectives of this project have been realized. New heat and mass transfer models have been developed for energy piles with two and three-dimensional groundwater advection. A laboratory rig was set up for validating the simulation results. A design method was proposed for designing ground source heat pumps (GSHP) with energy piles and the heat and mass transfer of energy piles with different underground mediums and different layouts was investigated in detail. Finally, a software package is developed for engineers. The research results can effectively contribute to renewable energy utilization and building energy conservation in Hong Kong as well as other places in the world. The main completed work is listed as follows. (1) Two new simulation models describing the heat and mass transfers surrounding foundation pile ground heat exchangers immersed in two or three-dimensional groundwater advection flows have been developed. The heat and mass transfer of energy piles has a direct effect on system design and operation. Therefore, a fast and accurate model of energy piles should be developed for the design and operation of the systems. Underground water is an important influential factor for the heat and mass transfer of energy piles. Both the velocity values and orientations of groundwater flow should be considered. In this project, the Green function with advection has been deduced to describe the temperature response to an instantaneous point heat source in an infinite homogeneous medium with groundwater flow. As for the model with 2D advection, the energy pile is treated as a solid cylindrical heat source. The dimensionless soil temperature around an energy pile can be calculated by the integration of the Green function over the solid cylinder based on superposition theory, which is shown in Equation 1. As for the model with 3D advection, the spiral coil of an energy pile is regarded as a spiral line heat source. The dimensionless soil temperature around an energy pile is the integration of the Green function over the spiral coil. Using the simulation models with 2D and 3D advection, the soil temperature distribution has been investigated, showing that the new simulation model is more reasonable to study the combined heat transfer including conduction and advection. This is the first time to reveal the temperature distributions in the form of isothermals on the XOY, XOZ and YOZ planes. The influences of orientation and value of groundwater have been studied, and the change of temperature response has been studied. The groundwater orientation and its value affect the temperature response at the same location when an energy pile emits heat to the surrounding medium. In addition, the temperature response along the depth direction of the energy pile with 2D groundwater flow has been explored. The results revealed the real situation of the heat transfer around energy piles, which was helpful to evaluate the ability of heat transfer of the energy pile. (2) A laboratory test rig has been set up for the verification of the model. An experimental rig was set up which was composed of a sandbox, five heat exchanging pipes, a water bath, thermocouples, a glass rotameter, and a data logger. Results showed that the absolute errors of simulated and tested soil temperatures were less than 0.25°C. The developed energy piles group model with 3D groundwater seepage has been validated by the experiment rig. (3) A design method of energy piles and ground source heat pump systems has been proposed based on the above simulations and experiments. This coupled method considered the fluid temperature of energy piles, the COP of the heat pump unit, and the dynamic building load. After the optimal design of the ground source heat pump system, the performance of spiral coil ground heat exchangers has been analyzed in detail. Results show that groundwater reduces the temperatures of upstream soil and outlet fluid and increases the total heat fluxes. The energy pile group with larger pile spacing distance has lower soil temperature, larger total heat fluxes, and lower outlet fluid temperature. (4) An inverse simulation method has been developed to calculate the value and direction of the groundwater flow. The corresponding simulated solutions have been obtained. The inverse method takes into account the points that are distributed around the ground heat exchanger (GHE) and have the same distance to the centerline of GHE. The temperature responses of these points and the established objective function lays a firm foundation for reverse reasoning. Comparisons of temperature responses between theoretical results and the simulative recorded data are made. Differences among the points' temperature responses are respectively used to indicate the direction and value ranges of velocity. The relativity between the points' location and the velocity intensity has been investigated and then some cases have been chosen as the trials to verify the rationality of the reverse calculation method. (5) The heat and mass transfer surrounding pile heat exchangers with different types and conditions of the underground medium have been investigated. The non-homogeneity of underground media including the pile concrete and the underground medium were considered under conditions of groundwater seepage. The concrete of energy piles has a non-negligible influence on the design size because it influences its interior heat transfer performance. Four different underground mediums, including granite, sandstone, concrete, and dry soil, have been investigated. The differences induced by medium types are obvious and thus the acquaintance on the local underground medium of any project is vital, which is favorable to avoid the superabundant length of GHEs, and then the economic investment of the system could be significantly reduced. (6) The optimized geometry of foundation pile heat exchangers including both single pile and multi-pile systems has been studied. As for a single pile, the pile diameter, pile depths, and pile pitches are analyzed to achieve an optimal geometry under the condition of groundwater flow. A short energy pile has relatively low soil temperature, small total heat flux and high outlet fluid temperature due to the heat disperse from the soil surface and shallow depth. As for pile groups, different pile layouts are studied. The energy pile groups with pile layouts 3×2 and 2×3 in the semi-infinite soil nearly had the same soil temperature distribution, total heat flux, and outlet fluid temperature. (7) A software package and design guideline have been developed to enable engineers to use energy piles in GSHP air-conditioning systems. The software package named “The simulation software for predicting the performance of the ground source heat pump using energy piles (EP-Star)” was developed for researchers, designers, and engineers, which can be used to design optimal parameters of energy piles and other components in a GSHP system based on the system performance. In addition, it can also simulate the dynamic system performance after inputting the parameters of building load, underground, and heat pump unit. It was easy for engineers with different academic backgrounds to use accurately and fast. Since there is no commercial software package for designing GSHP with energy piles, this research delivery can promote the application of GHSP.

15203915.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203915.value: The new simulation models for describing the heat transfer of energy piles with 2D and 3D groundwater advection were proposed. The impact that groundwater flow exerts on the pile group was explored and the soil temperature distribution was explained. The influences of orientation and value of groundwater were investigated, and the change of temperature response was studied. In addition, the temperature response along the depth direction of energy pile with 2D and 3D groundwater flow was explored. The heat exchanger utilizing the spiral coils in a ground source heat pump system was designed based on the proposed model. The performance of the spiral coil ground heat exchanger was analyzed under the influence of different factors like groundwater velocity, the pile layout, the pile spacing as well as the pile depth. Results show that the energy piles in the outer layers of the groups, in the upstream along the groundwater ﬂow, with large pile spacing, and arranged in a line shape can exchange more heat with the surrounding soil. The back-calculation method based on the finite heat source seepage model was proposed to obtain the groundwater velocity including value and orientation. It was valuable for investigating the influence that groundwater seepage exerts on heat transfer of energy piles. The project mainly proposed a theoretical method based on reasonable principles, which can provide theoretical guidance for obtaining groundwater velocity while an experiment was completed. For the underground with different hydraulic conditions, the heat transfer surrounding pile heat exchangers and the system performance were investigated. For the pile heat exchangers, the single pile and the piles in a slim layout can exchange more heat with the soil compared to the piles in close layout due to less thermal interaction among piles. The software package for the simulation of the ground source heat pump system using spiral coil energy piles with seepage was developed with the registration of copyright. The software package can be used for predicting soil temperature distribution and system performance. Both the heat transfer around the energy piles and the system heating and cooling effect can be simulated. With this software package, the researcher, designer, and operator can be assisted to achieve the optimum system. This project contributes effectively to the inverse heat transfer optimization of energy pile with three-dimensional groundwater advection.

15203915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203915.value: Compared to the previous two-dimensional groundwater advection model, the improved three-dimensional model can describe the practical groundwater flow more accurately. The orientation and value of groundwater flow are investigated to help engineers design the piles in an appropriate layout and under different hydraulic conditions. The proposed inverse heat transfer model is valuable for investigating the influence that groundwater seepage exerts on heat transfer of energy pile heat exchangers. The groundwater velocity can be predicted based on the inverse model while actual experiments were completed, which could be used for the collection of hydraulic information. The design model of the spiral coil energy pile is proposed to further study the performance of this popular heat exchanger, like the applicability, optimum design, and the technical economy. The different factors, like the different underground mediums, geometries of energy pile heat exchangers, are investigated to optimize the system design, achieving good underground heat transfer and system performance. The developed software package can simulate the soil temperature distribution surrounding the energy piles and predict the system’s heating and cooling performance. This software package could be used for future research on optimizing the system design of different types of buildings in different climate zones.

15203915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203915.value: A ground source heat pump is a clean and efficient technology for hot water supply and air conditioning. Using energy piles as the ground source heat exchangers in this system can save the drilling cost and land occupation on the ground level. The heat transfer surrounding the energy pile is important to design the piles and the system. The developed three-dimensional groundwater advection can play an important rule in calculating the soil heat transfer, which should be accurately described in the simulation. Therefore, the improved inverse heat transfer model of foundation energy piles considering three-dimensional groundwater flow can be used to investigate the influence of three-dimensional groundwater seepage on the soil temperature distribution and the heat transfer surrounding energy piles. Furthermore, under conditions of seepage, different underground mediums and different pile layouts were investigated to optimize the system design in different locations. To help researchers, designers, and operators of ground source heat pump systems to use the proposed model easily, the software package named “Energy Pile-Star” was developed. It can fast and accurately optimize the system parameters during the design process and predict the system performance during the operation process for any ground source heat pump using spiral coil energy piles.

15204315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204315.value: Time series data are abundant in various application domains, e.g., medical analysis, economic analysis, climatology, environmental science. Such data are queried by scientists or data analysts in order to find occurrences of a given trend or discover frequent trends. In the above applications, the length of a time series can reach the billion scale. This renders existing querying methods expensive and prevents users from performing timely analysis. We discover that existing querying methods for time series data spend significant time on CPU rather than on disk accesses. We propose to speedup these methods by fully exploiting the opportunities in modern CPUs (e.g., CPU cache, data-parallel instructions, multi-core processing). Although there exist recent techniques on utilizing modern CPUs to accelerate relational database operations like sorting and joining, those techniques are not applicable to common operations in time series algorithms (e.g., distance computation, pruning techniques). Our problem poses the following three challenges. First, distance computation is a common yet expensive operation in querying algorithms on time series data, as the cost of distance computation is at least linear to the query sequence length. Second, although there exist pruning techniques to reduce the number of distance computations, they still incur considerable CPU time. Third, existing querying methods are sequential algorithms and they underutilize the parallel opportunities in modern CPUs. This project aims at developing efficient techniques that exploit modern CPUs to speedup querying problems on time series data. Our idea is to exploit both the characteristics of time series data (e.g., data changing gradually with the time dimension) and opportunities on modern CPUs (e.g., data-parallel and thread-parallel processing) in order to reduce the query response time. Specifically, we will explore three important research directions in this project: (i) data-parallel distance computation techniques on modern CPUs, (ii) optimizations for pruning distance computation on time series data, and (iii) thread-parallel querying algorithms for time series data on modern CPUs. We will evaluate the query response time of our techniques on real massive time series data. We envision that this project will advance the query processing techniques for time series data. Also, our work will benefit the data analysts in the aforementioned applications, offering faster query response time and supporting timely analysis. 時間序列數據具有各種應用領域，如醫療分析，經濟分析，氣候，環境科學。科學家或數據分析師或對這些數據搜尋趨勢。在上述應用中，時間序列的長度可達到上億規模。這使現有查詢方法緩慢，阻礙用戶及時分析。 現有的時間序列數據查詢方法花費顯著時間於CPU。我們提出利用現代CPU的特性（例如，CPU緩存，數據並行指令，多核處理）以加速查詢方法。雖然最近關係數據庫的技術利用現代CPU加速處理，這些技術並不適用於時間序列算法的算子（例如，距離計算，修剪技術）。我們的問題具有以下挑戰。時間序列的距離計算與現有修剪技術都需要相當大的時間。現有的查詢方法尚未利用現代CPU的特性。 本項目旨在開發高效技術利用現代CPU對時間序列數據的查詢加速。我們構想利用時間序列數據的特徵（例如，數據漸變）和現代CPU的特性（例如，數據並行和線程並行處理）以減少查詢回應時間。我們將探討三個重要的研究方向：（i）以數據並行技術計算距離，（二）改善距離計算的修剪，及（iii）線程並行查詢的算法。我們預計，本項目將推動對時間序列數據的查詢處理技術。此外，我們的工作有助上述的應用，提供更快的查詢回應時間和支持及時分析。

15204315.label: Realisation of objectives
15204315.value: We have carried out research activities on all project objectives. A postdoc fellow and three research assistants have were recruited to investigate these issues. For Objective 1, we have utilized SIMD to speedup distance computation for time series data. Then, we published these techniques in [ADMS/IMDM@VLDB 2016]. For Objective 2, we have developed pruning techniques for time series data and published our results in a journal [VLDBJ 2016]. We have also developed pruning techniques for spatial trajectories, trend insights, and submatrices, and published our results in two conferences [EDBT 2017][SIGMOD 2017] and a journal [TKDE 2017]. For Objective 3, we have developed a thread-parallel algorithm for time series data so that it used both CPU and GPU for processing. We have published this algorithm in a journal [VLDBJ 2016].

15204315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204315.value: Time series data are abundant in various application domains, e.g., medical analysis, economic analysis, climatology, environmental science. Such data are queried by scientists or data analysts in order to find occurrences of a given trend or discover frequent trends. This project aims at developing efficient techniques that exploit modern CPUs to speedup querying problems on time series data. Our idea is to exploit both the characteristics of time series data (e.g., data changing gradually with the time dimension) and opportunities on modern CPUs (e.g., data-parallel and thread-parallel processing) in order to reduce the query response time. Specifically, we will explore three important research directions in this project: (i) data-parallel distance computation techniques on modern CPUs, (ii) optimizations for pruning distance computation on time series data, and (iii) thread-parallel querying algorithms for time series data on modern CPUs. We envision that this project will advance the query processing techniques for time series data. Also, our work will benefit the data analysts in the aforementioned applications, offering faster query response time and supporting timely analysis.

15204515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204515.value: 在本項目書中我們概述了基於CH3NH3PbIxCl3-x的高效鈣鈦礦太陽電池的研究計畫。我們採用熱蒸發技術製備鈣鈦礦材料，這種技術有利於沉積生長高度均勻的薄膜，是發展大面積器件的一個重要特性。 首先，我們會重點研究通過鈣鈦礦薄膜的缺陷工程和晶體工程來提高薄膜的光電特性，這也是本項目的研究重點。專案負責人在之前的研究中闡述了鈣鈦礦材料在乾燥的氧氣中退火後能夠使太陽電池的轉化效率獲得顯著的提高，並利用這種新技術在實驗室裡製備出了高效的鈣鈦礦電池，其中最高的轉換效率達到了15.4%。為了研究這種電池效率提高現象中的基本機制，我們將對鈣鈦礦材料進行氧氛圍的退火處理，同時觀察它對薄膜中的局域態的影響。為此，我們將利用光熱偏轉光譜和低頻噪音技術對材料的帶隙態進行完備的測試。同時我們將對氣相輔助結晶過程促進鈣鈦礦材料晶粒增大進行研究，系統的表徵其對帶隙態，載流子傳輸和複合壽命的影響，這也將作為回饋以優化氣相輔助結晶過程。 第二步是利用這種優化改進的鈣鈦礦材料製備高效率的電池器件。這裡我們將對器件的光學特性進行完備的理論分析，以促進基於CH3NH3PbIxCl3-x的鈣鈦礦太陽電池的器件結構的優化設計。我們也將對二氧化鈦層的摻雜降低器件串聯電阻展開研究。在氧化銦錫（ITO）導電層和二氧化鈦層之間加入一層聚乙烯亞胺（PEIE）能夠在其中引入分子偶極子，可以提高載流子的提取效率。通過對器件的完備表徵，包括電流-電壓測試，外量子效率，低頻噪音，阻抗頻譜測量等，進一步優化器件結構。

15204515.label: Realisation of objectives
15204515.value: We have performed comprehensive study of both thermal evaporation and solution processing of perovskite films and investigated oxygen passivation, as described in the progress report. Furthermore, we have developed optimised processes for the deposition of perovskite thin films, and achieved excellent control of crystallisation. The optimised process (cryogenic process combined with blow drying) has resulted in the champion devices with PCE of 21.4%. In addition to optimising the perovskite deposition, we worked on improving the charge transport and collection. We investigated both undoped and doped charge transport layer. Since we found that devices with TiO2 (objective 4) always exhibited hysteresis, we moved to devices with SnO2 in conventional architecture and NiOx in inverted architecture and investigated doped and undoped oxide charge transport layers. In addition to the doping, we investigated passivation of oxide/perovskite interface, for example by alkali chloride treatments, and the passivation of defects in the perovskite using various organic compounds. All the devices have been comprehensively characterised as stated in objective 5.

15204515.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204515.value: We have found that the perovskite solar cell performance is critically dependent on the properties of the perovskite film, which is affected by the crystallisation control. High quality films have been achieved both by thermal evaporation and solution processing, and various post-deposition treatments and process modifications (ACS Applied Materials and Interfaces, Vol. 8, pp. 32805 - 32814; ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2018, 10, 1, 371-380; Adv. Mater. 30, 1804402, 2018). The presence of chloride ions was generally found to be beneficial for the perovskite properties. The best results achieved were using the cryogenic process combined with blow drying to control the crystallisation of the perovskite film (Adv. Mater. 30, 1804402, 2018), with the efficiency of the champion device as high as 21.4%. In addition to the investigations of the deposition of the perovskite film and its effect on crystallisation and traps and overall properties of the perovskite and its photovoltaic performance, we have investigated the charge transport layers and the effect of their interface with the perovskite. We have used planar films as well as nano rods (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2017,5, 15970-15980), and we worked on cells using TiO2 as well as SnO2 in conventional architecture, and NiOx in inverted architecture. We investigated the effects of doping (Adv. Energy Mater. 2018, 8, 1703519; Adv. Mater. 2019, 31, 1805944), interface passivation (Adv. Energy Mater. 2019, 9, 1803872) as well as additives and passivating molecules (Sol. RRL 2019, 3, 1800290;Adv. Funct. Mater. 2019, 29, 1808855) on the performance of perovskite solar cells. Efficiencies exceeding 20% are routinely obtained in both inverted and conventional architectures, and the devices commonly exhibited improved stability as well. All the prepared devices have been comprehensively characterized to elucidate the relationships between traps and defects and the device performance.

15204515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204515.value: Further development could include detailed investigation of device stability for fully optimised devices in terms of minimisation of defects in perovskite solar cells by crystal engineering and the passivation of traps and interfaces. In addition, further development of cryogenic anti solvent-free process for perovskite precursors dissolved in green solvents can be another possible research direction to further reduce negative environmental impact of perovskite solar cell manufacturing.

15204515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204515.value: Perovskite solar cells are among the most promising next generation photovoltaics technologies, but the properties of perovskite materials, and consequently device performance, are very sensitive to the deposition conditions. In the course of our research, we investigated the optimisation of the perovskite solar cell performance by trap and crystal engineering. We have performed comprehensive investigation of different deposition processes, and developed a novel cryogenic antisolvent free process for high performance perovskite solar cells with efficiency exceeding 21%. Since commonly used antisolvents are highly toxic and environmentally harmful, the development of antisolvent-free technique for the deposition of high quality perovskite film is highly beneficial for the future practical applications. Furthermore, we performed comprehensive investigation of the passivation of defects and interfaces in perovskite solar cells for different device architectures, and we clearly demonstrated how, by careful optimisation of the film deposition and grain boundary and interface passivation, efficiencies exceeding 20% and high device stability could be routinely accomplished for variety of device configurations (both conventional and inverted architectures).
