15204715.label: Project Objectives
15204715.value: To design and fabricate a range of 1-, 2- and 3-dimesional textile architectures with variations in fiber cross-sectional shapes, fiber dimension, thermal and electric conductivity, fiber orientation and packing density with an aim to achieve low thermal conductivity and good adhesion of thermoelectric materials. To measure thermal and electrical conductivity and structural parameters of the constituent fibers. To investigate and select appropriate approaches to fabricate thermoelectric nano-materials with compounds free of tellurium and lead; To characterize the structure and properties of films made from the pure materials by analytical methods including XRD, SEM, TEM, AFM etc. To explore and select appropriate methods to fabricate textile thermoelectric composites via environmental friendly routes including screen printing, sol-gel casting, electrospinning, ink-jet printing, and pressing at moderate temperature, followed by annealing or sintering; To characterize the structure of textile composites by the above mentioned analytical methods to measure the effective thermal and electric conductivity, electric resistivity in the principal directions of the composite samples. To develop multi-physics models and finite element analysis methods for unit cells of intended thermoelectric textile composites with selected fiber architectures, thermoelectric materials and fiber volume fraction distributions. To verify the models and numeric simulation results by comparing with the experimental data obtained from objective 1, 2 and 3. To modify the models if necessary. Using the verified models and FE simulation methods established in objective 4, to reveal the theoretical relationships between the structures and transport properties of fibers/textiles, thermoelectric materials as well as the composites, eventually the figure of merit of the composites.

15204715.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204715.value: We have developed 1D, 2D and 3D fibrous structures for TE generators, that is, in the form of coated fibers, printed fabrics, and spacer fabrics. [1,2,6] We also successfully developed and investigated a range of printable n- and p-type PEDOT/PSS/Bi2Te3 composites with excellent properties and processability at low temperatures via the solution route. The thermoelectric properties of these composites achieve similar Seebeck coefficients of pure Bi2Te3 in addition to good electric conductivity and low thermal conductivity. [3] We also reported our investigation of flexible rGO coated generators. [4] More excitingly, we discovered a gigantic synergy in the MoS2/GO nanocomposites that leads to a huge Seebeck coefficient during the transition between 1T and 2H phases of MoS2. The synergy remains functional even in the pre- and post-transition stage. [5] Atomic-scale molecular dynamic calculations were carried out [5]. Theoretical modeling and numerical calculations of the devices under radiation and conduction were carried out with the 1D fiber and 3D devices in terms of material thermal, electrical, thermoelectrical, and emissive properties; device structural parameters like dimension and packing density; operational temperature. [6]

15204715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204715.value: The mechanisms of thermoelectric nanocomposites and polymer composites is being further investigated via multi-scaled modeling (atomic-, nano-, micro- and meso-scale) and experiments in another funded GRF project. Fiber-based generator device design and fabrication are the topics for further study. Device modeling and visualization of fiber-based thermoelectric generators shall shed new light on the theoretical upper limits of the output of the devices that will be very helpful to speed up the progress in terms of design, optimization and evaluation.

15204715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204715.value: The study of textile thermoelectric composites has resulted in a number of scientific discoveries and technological advances. We have demonstrated a gigantic Seebeck coefficient in hetero-layered MoS2/GO composites for the first time. We have also developed novel printable/coatable polymer composites for textile thermoelectric generators. We have revealed the relationships among the structure and thermal, electric and thermoelectric properties of the composites. Mathematical modeling has provided useful guidance for engineering design, optimization, and evaluation of textile thermoelectric composites as well as fabrication of their thermoelectric generators for wearable applications.

15205515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205515.value: 2010年3月23日,受到中國北部沙塵暴的影響,香港的空氣污染指數超過了500。由我們研究組建立的兩個AERONET監測站得到的數據與MODIS衛星影像相結合的資料顯示,從2006年以來,香港受到了超過30次的沙塵暴影響。然而，由於珠江三角洲的工業污染源, 加上中國南方的潮濕氣候, 以及沙塵氣溶膠本身的時間和空間變換大的特點，致使在香港監測沙塵氣溶膠充滿了挑戰。因此高時間和高空間解析度的沙塵識別和反演演算法是目前急需解決的問題。與太陽同步衛星相比, 日本Himawari-8/9衛星上的高級Himawari成像儀(AHI),韓國衛星的氣象成像儀(MI)和多功能傳輸衛星 (MTSAT)能夠對微小的氣溶膠進行反演並得到高時間解析度的成果。 此研究是通過使用地球同步衛星影像(如MTSAT,MI和AHI),數值氣象預報模型(如WRF)和輔助資料(如數位高程模型,NCEP/FNL資料)來開發一種基於集成與智能知識的沙塵暴監測技術,並利用神經網路和數值反演模型對沙塵氣溶膠進行分析。這一套提出的演算法包括:(i)在大範圍地區內使用神經網路模型進行沙塵暴監測;(ii)使用神經網路模型反演氣溶膠光學厚度;和(iii)使用數值反演模型對氣溶膠的光學特性進行分析,如沙塵高度和有效半徑的沙塵微粒等。本研究創新之處在於集成多個地球觀測衛星和數值模型演算,並且本研究是首次利用AHI衛星影像的高空間、高光譜、高時間解析度的特性(AHI擁有三個可見光波段,解析度為0.5km和1km; 13個紅外波段,解析度為1km和2km)對沙塵暴進行分析研究。 我們研究小組已進行了一項利用MTSAT衛星圖像的試點研究(網站http://158.132.186.221:8080/meteo/),而且這個演算法將被進一步完善以用於MI和AHI衛星影像。項目的成果可用於(i)鑒別氣溶膠的傳輸和污染源地區,幫助政府協調工作;(ii)常規監測,特別是對於機場和港口部門;及(iii)評估氣溶膠對地面輻射平衡和大氣穩定度的研究。

15205515.label: Realisation of objectives
15205515.value: Primary objective - To develop an integrated knowledge-based technique for dust storm monitoring: using geostationary satellite images, numerical weather forecasting model, and ancillary data based on neural network models and an inversion-based model. The primary objective along with the secondary objectives of this project have been well accomplished in approximately 90%. The development of two major tasks: developments of both physical model-based and machine learning model-based method for dust storm detection and retrieval have been accomplished. About 14 SCI journal publications (2 more under preparation), 2 book chapters, 4 conference presentations/abstracts* have been published in this study and several postgraduate students^ have been trained in this project. Secondary objective 1 - To develop comprehensive look-up-tables for MTSAT, MI and AHI satellite images, in order to derive dust aerosol optical properties. The project team has developed the comprehensive look-up tables (LUTs) to derive dust aerosol optical thickness (AOT) and effective radius (EffR) for MTSAT and AHI satellite images. Given that the high similarity between the wavelengths of MI and MTSAT satellite sensors, we consider that the LUTs for MTSAT can be also used by MI satellite images. The project team has developed a physical model-based inversion method by considering non-spherical shape of dust particles for retrieving AOT and EffR, in which previous studies assumed a spherical shape in aerosol retrieval using geostationary satellite images. Natural dust particles are generally in non-spherical shape, thereby such assumptions can lead to large uncertainty of aerosol retrieval. The LUTs were constructed by coupling with both radiative transfer model (SBDART) and single scattering model (T-matrix). The T-matrix code was specifically incorporated to calculate the single scattering optical properties of dust particles by assuming non-spherical shape. Apart from the consideration of the non-spherical shape of dust particles, the complex refractive index (CRI) also plays a significant impact on the retrieval of dust properties. The complex refractive index in previous studies mostly adopted from the Optical Properties of Aerosols and Clouds (OPAC) dataset, in which the dust samples are mainly taken from the Africa or America deserts. This can lead to the discrepancies between the CRIs of OPAC and East Asian dust aerosols. A set of CRIs measured from the dust samples of Taklimakan desert and Gobi deserts, and spanning the whole visible to thermal wavelengths, were utilized to develop a set of empirical dust models for East Asia. In addition, the project team has taken the initiative to utilize both visible and thermal channels from satellite sensors simultaneously for dust retrieval. Previous studies on aerosol retrieval focus on either visible to near-infrared wavelengths or thermal infrared wavelengths. The new generation geostationary satellites provide the new potential for retrieving dust aerosols by utilizing the visible and thermal wavelengths collectively. The LUTs for AHI were also constructed utilizing SBDART and T-matrix, with a new set of dust models for East Asia and incorporated with more wavelengths. The GEOS-Chem dust model was also implemented to assist in identifying the dust transport pathways. The retrieved AOT images were demonstrated to have high consistency with GEOS-Chem simulated products. Secondary objective 2 - To evaluate other machine learning techniques for dust storm detection at broader regional scale, and retrieval of dust AOT. This study has initiated an innovative strategy to retrieve AOT and EffR of dust aerosols with machine learning (ML) models. AOT has been extensively studied with both physical model-based method and machine learning method. However, EffR is also a key indicator of dust aerosols since it largely determines the single scattering albedo, which in turn affects the net radiation. Despite the prevalence of machine learning approaches, there has not been many studies for modeling and retrieving EffR using machine learning methods, especially for geostationary satellite images. With the incorporation of new-generation geostationary satellites, it shows the high potential to derive EffR. In visible to near-infrared (VIR) wavelengths, the new geostationary satellites offer four channels in visible to near-infrared spectrum and at very high temporal resolution. Such information can be used to composite minimum reflectance imagery as surface reflectance. The difference between observed reflectance and surface reflectance (dR) at certain wavelength can be used for retrieving the corresponding AOT. In thermal wavelengths, brightness temperature difference (BTD) at ~8µm and ~11µm, and BTD at ~11µm and ~12 µm can indicate dust particle size based on the rationale that dust particles absorb more radiation at wavelengths ~11µm than ~12 µm, and a typical V-shape is particularly observed for dust aerosols. A series of composited minimum reflectance, maximum brightness temperature, and dust indices has been developed from AHI satellite images, in order to establish more comprehensive training features for machine learning. The machine learning models implemented in this project has also been expanded from the initial Artificial Neural Network (ANN) to more machine learning models. Five single machine learning models were developed in this project for dust aerosol properties inversion. These ML models include ANN, Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boost Tree (XGBoost), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Ridge regression (Ridge) models. Such models were used to model the relationship between satellite observations (along with satellite geometries and land surface elevation) and aerosol properties (AOT and EffR). The project team has also developed the Ensemble models to integrate five machine learning models in order to improve the retrieval accuracy. Secondary objective 3 - To validate and refine the newly developed algorithms using ground station data and satellite-borne Lidar data. The retrieved AOT and EffR results have been thoroughly validated against the ground AERONET data, other ancillary data, as well as the MODIS AOT products. The dust occurrence identified from our dust detection algorithms was also validated against satellite-borne Lidar CALIPSO product. Secondary objective 4 - To simulate the pathways of dust storms using the HYbrid Single Particle Lagrangian Integrated Trajectory (HYSPLIT) forward trajectory model, and visualize the research outputs on Google Earth/Google Map platform. A website has been developed for visualizing the HYSPLIT forward trajectory model using Google Earth/Google Map platform. The research outputs from this project would be further incorporated into the platform for knowledge transfer. * Three conference presentations were invited by the organizing committees (no abstract papers, and they are not included in Section 9) Presentation title: Research Sensing for monitoring and prediction of dust storm events in Hong Kong; Conference name: 测绘遥感大数据：面向能源与环境挑战国际学术研讨会; Oct, 2019, Xuzhou, China Presentation title: Research on aerosol properties from earth observation and its related social impact; Conference name: 2018 ISPRS Workshop on Remote Sensing and Synergic Analysis on Atmospheric Environment; Oct, 2018, Guangzhou, China Presentation title: Spatio-temporal analysis of dust storms events and the related health issues; Conference name: The 1st ISPRS Workshop on Remote Sensing and Synergic Analysis on Atmospheric Environment; Sep, 2017, Changsha, China ^Two MSc students were trained under this project and one of them further pursued the PhD degree under this project Ms. Li Jing, thesis topic: Satellite Detection and Retrieval of Asian Dust Storms using MTSAT Imageries [Apr 13, 2016 to May 26, 2017] (she was continuing the PhD study after her MSc degree) Ms. Ding Ling, thesis topic: Dust Aerosol Optical Thickness retrieval based on Neural Networks using Geostationary satellite images (Himawari-8) [Apr 13, 2016 to May 26, 2017]

15205515.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205515.value: This project has developed an integrated knowledge-based technique for dust storm monitoring: using geostationary satellite images, numerical weather forecasting model, and ancillary data based on neural network models and an inversion-based model. The followings are the three major research achievements. At first, the conventional dust storm detection algorithms were comprehensively reviewed and evaluated. These algorithms could be categorized into spectral indices, anomalous temporal detection, and spatial uniformity test based on the satellite images. An integration of the three types of algorithms with an emphasis on dust indices was proposed for dust storm detection in a more accurate manner. Two types of look-up tables (LUTs) have been developed for MTSAT and AHI satellite sensors. The LUTs for AHI are specifically designed for East Asian dust aerosols. The LUTs with non-spherical shape of dust particles and complex refractive index measured from the East Asian dust samples were developed in this study and the results show higher accuracy in dust retrieval. The AHI satellite provides additional wavelengths, thereby offers a new possibility to retrieve the dust aerosol properties by integrating visible and thermal channels. The models developed by the project team could achieve a higher accuracy in dust aerosol retrieval from geostationary satellite images. A number of machine learning (ML) models have been developed which can be used for retrieving dust aerosol properties. These models include five types of single model and ensemble model (Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Random Forest (RF), Extreme Gradient Boost Tree (XGBoost), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Ridge regression (Ridge)) for both AOT and EffR estimation. The five single ML models achieve high r-square and low RMSE (around 0.9 for r-square and 0.06 for RMSE) in estimating AOT. The five single ML models show moderate r-square and RMSE (around 0.56 for r-square and 0.20 for RMSE) in estimating EffR. It is also found that ANN outperforms other single models with a relatively complex model configuration (four-layer with 512, 256, 128 and 32 neurons in each layer) in both AOT and EffR estimation. The ensemble models indicated that simple configured ANN (two-layer with 32-16 neurons in each layer) and RF models were the optimal models in estimating AOT and EffR respectively with r-squares of 0.94 and 0.63 for AOT and EffR, and RMSE of 0.05 and 0.15 for AOT and EffR.

15205515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205515.value: This project has developed an integrated knowledge-based technique focused on monitoring the East Asian dust storms. The research outcomes can be applied to other geostationary satellites to achieve dust storm monitoring in near real-time and at global scale. The new generation geostationary satellites including FY-4A (China), GEOS 16&17 (America), GK-2A (Korea) and the future MTG-I1-I4 (Europe) have been or will be launched in the recent years carrying satellite sensors with very high spatial and temporal resolutions. The operation of such geostationary satellites together with Himawari AHI can realize continuous spatiotemporal monitoring of meteorological events globally. Monitoring dust storms emanated from the World’s largest deserts including Sahara Desert (in Africa), Arabian Desert (in Arabian), Taklamakan and Gobi Desert (spanning Mongolia and China), Patagonian Desert (in Argentina) by utilizing the synergized observations of geostationary satellites can be of paramount meaning, especially for studying the dust storm effect in global climate. By in coupling the observations from new generation geostationary satellites and the NASA’s AERONET ground station data, it is possible to characterize the dust storms globally and timely. The outcomes and deliverables in this project offer a good showcase which can be applied to other geostationary satellites.

15205515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205515.value: Dust storm is a natural atmospheric phenomenon. The East Asian dust storms emanated from the Taklamakan and Gobi deserts can transport to the downwind populated areas and cause a potential disaster to the populated metropolitans. Geostationary satellites (e.g., MTSAT, MI and AHI) can monitor the dust storms continuously, remotely, and timely. The new generation of geostationary satellites offers more wavelengths and at higher temporal resolution, and they can observe the whole East Asia in near-real-time. Thus, the properties of dust aerosols could be derived from the new geostationary satellites. A new set of look-up-tables based on inversion method has been developed in this study (i) by considering non-spherical shape of dust particles, (ii) incorporating a new set of complex refractive index (CRI) for East Asia, (iii) and in coupling with both visible and thermal channels simultaneously. In addition, a set of machine learning models has also been developed with single and ensemble models. The results show a promising accuracy in retrieving dust aerosol properties, i.e. AOT and EffR. The integrated knowledge-based technique developed in this study provides new research/science achievements, and can be used for monitoring dust storms effectively and accurately.

15205715.label: Project Objectives
15205715.value: To develop efficient algorithms for automatic activity pattern generation based on the collected, filtered and re-identified MAC addresses. Based on (1) to develop a calibration framework and a network equilibrium approach for activity-based travel demand models that take into account the people interactions and time-of-day-dependent activity patterns. 15205715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205715.value: Like many large Asian cities, Hong Kong, owing to its rapid development and high population density, requires frequent refinement of the existing travel demand models to plan for the new railway/highway projects so as to alleviate the urban traffic congestion problems. With the high smartphone penetration rate and increasing WiFi coverage in Hong Kong, media access control (MAC) addresses could serve as a suitable source of data for supporting the frequent and automatic calibration of travel demand models for meeting the needs of this fast-changing metropolitan city. This proposal aims to contribute to the development of an automatic calibration framework of activity-based models (ABMs) for long-term strategic transportation planning, using the re-identified MAC addresses from smartphones and other communication devices. In developing this automatic calibration framework, the automatic generation of activity patterns from collected MAC addresses is one of the key components to be tackled. In this component, the project will first develop efficient algorithms for filtering and matching the collected MAC addresses. Then, based on the observed durations of the detected MAC addresses, activity patterns will be determined. With the generated activity patterns as the potential choice set, this project will then focus on the development of an efficient automatic calibration framework of ABMs with household members’ interactions and time-of-day constraints. Based on the developed calibration framework for the ABMs, focus will then put on the development of simultaneous calibration of ABM and population characteristics with the help from the household-activity-based multi-modal network equilibrium model developed in this study. Lastly, the performance of the developed models and frameworks are examined with the use of field tests and simulation results. The proposed project has the potential to help the transport planners and traffic engineers to collect and prepare the plentiful MAC addresses information for an efficient and accurate calibration of activity-based travel demand models and various population characteristics. The use of MAC addresses in the proposed calibration frameworks holds great promise for reducing the time and resources required for calibrating activity-based travel demand models. Thus, frequent refinement and update of the existing models is possible. This is particularly important for transport planning in Hong Kong, and many other Asian large cities, with rapid development and high population density.

15205715.label: Realisation of objectives
15205715.value: As far as the project objective 1 is concerned, Wi-Fi MAC addresses were collected in the university campus for analysis of the student activity-mobility behavior (see publication nos. (7), (8), (9) and (11)). Data processing and filtering algorithms were proposed for filtering and re-identifying the MAC addresses so as to estimate the individual/joint activity travel patterns of pedestrians within the university campus for facility planning and management purposes. The integration with other data sources was also studied for improving the performance of re-identification and carrying out the in-depth analysis of student mobility and activity behavior. In connection to the project objective 2, an activity-based network equilibrium model was proposed for scheduling two-individual joint activity-travel patterns (JATPs) in congested multi-modal transit networks (see publication no. (4)). The proposed model can be used to comprehensively investigate individuals’ activity choices (e.g. activity start time and duration, activity sequence) and travel choices (e.g. departure time, route and mode) in multi-modal transit networks, including both independent ones and joint ones. In addition, a new household activity-based network equilibrium model was proposed which takes into account the interactions between household members by heterogeneous household type with different size for making choices on daily joint/solo activities and travel in congested road networks (see publication no. (6)). Two new household-oriented network equilibrium principles based on household optimum and household-based system optimum were introduced, together with the formulations of their equivalent mathematical programming problems, and their analytical relationships to the conventional user equilibrium (individual optimum) and individual-based system optimum. A new supernetwork platform was proposed for converting the time-dependent household daily activity-travel scheduling problem into an equivalent static traffic assignment problem within a unified modeling framework. The JATP scheduling problem was further studied in pedestrian networks with use of Wi-Fi MAC address data (see publication no. (7)). A novel activity-based equilibrium model was proposed to schedule the daily activity-travel patterns of pedestrians, hypothesizing that behaviorally heterogeneous pedestrians in the same group may have joint activities and are affected by crowding discomfort while traveling and participating in activities. A pedestrian-joint-activity-time-space (PJATS) supernetwork platform was developed to capture the complex structure of pedestrian networks and interactions on the joint activities of pedestrians. The activity-based models were further extended to investigate transit service scheduling problems in multi-modal transit networks. A new activity-based Stochastic User Equilibrium (SUE) transit assignment model was proposed to capture the interaction between transit timetables and passengers’ activity-travel scheduling behavior over a typical day, as passengers’ activity choices and travel choices (departure time, activity/trip chain, activity duration, transit line and mode) are considered simultaneously under the SUE condition (see publication no. (1)). Step tolling problem for a road bottleneck was also studied using an activity-based modelling framework with time-varying marginal activity utilities (see publication no. (3)). In relation to the project objective 3, the relationships among home-work-home activity durations and travel times of workers were investigated using the household interview survey data from the 2011 Travel Characteristics Survey (TCS2011) conducted in Hong Kong for developing the activity-based models (see publication no. (2)). The utility functions of home-work-home activities of Hong Kong workers were calibrated by time of day. Apart from the home-work-home activities, home-school-home activities were also examined considering both activity duration and travel time uncertainty (see publication no. (10)). A departure time choice model was formulated and calibrated using the TCS2011 data in Hong Kong to better understand the home-school-home travel behavior. In addition, the household characteristics were studied for modelling the individual’s activity choice and intra-household interactions (see publication nos. (5) and (12)). Interdependencies among household member’s choices, social-demographics and travel behavior were considered in the proposed models. In particular, empirical analysis of retired and dual-earner couples was conducted to investigate how retirement would affect their activity time use and patterns using the TCS2011 data (see publication no. (5)). With respect to the project objective 4, case studies were conducted in the university campus to monitor classroom usage and pedestrian facilities using re-identified MAC address data. Based on the proposed data processing and filtering algorithms, the classroom occupancy status was identified over time of day and day of week and the pedestrian activity patterns and walking times were estimated with acceptable accuracy (see publication nos. (8), (9) and (11)). It was also demonstrated that the Wi-Fi MAC address data collected in the study area of the university campus could be used to generate the daily activity pattern of pedestrians and their joint activities from the MAC addresses of the detected pedestrians (see publication no. (7)). To evaluate the performance of the proposed activity-based network equilibrium models, numerical examples were conducted in multi-modal transit networks and pedestrian networks. The results show that both individuals’ independent and joint activity-travel choices can be simultaneously investigated by the proposed models together with their intra-household/intra-group interactions (see publication nos. (4), (6) and (7)).

15205715.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205715.value: As far as the project objective 1 is concerned, data filtering algorithms were proposed for filtering and re-identifying the MAC addresses from smartphones and Wi-Fi enabled devices (see publication nos. (7), (8), (9) and (11)). Activity-travel patterns of pedestrians and walking times were estimated satisfactorily based on these re-identified MAC address data. In respect to the project objective 2, various activity-based network equilibrium models were proposed for modelling activity-travel patterns in congested multi-modal transit networks (see publication nos. (1) and (4)), congested road networks (see publication nos. (3) and (6)) and pedestrian networks (see publication no. (7)). In these activity-based models, independent and/or joint activity-travel choices were modelled on the proposed activity time-space supernetwork platforms. With regard to the project objective 3, population and household characteristics were studied based on the 2011 Travel Characteristics Survey (TCS2011) data in Hong Kong. An activity-based model was calibrated to quantify the utility functions of home-work-home activities of works (see publication no. (2)). In addition, a departure time choice model was calibrated for school-home travel (see publication no. (10)). The time dependence of joint activities between household members was also empirically studied together with the taste heterogeneity in the households. The results show the importance of considering intra-household interactions and group decision mechanism for activity generation and travel demand forecasting (see publication nos. (5) and (12)). In connection to the project objective 4, case studies were conducted in the university campus to demonstrate the use of re-identified Wi-Fi MAC address data to generate the activity-travel patterns for facility planning and management purposes (see publication nos. (7), (8), (9) and (11)) and for calibration of the travel demand models. Numerical examples were also used to illustrate the application of the proposed activity-based travel demand models together with their performances. The results show that the proposed models could reasonable reproduce the activity-travel patterns under different scenarios (see publication nos. (4), (6) and (7)).

15205715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205715.value: In this project, different activity-based travel demand models have been developed for modelling the activity-travel scheduling problems with contributions in both theoretical and methodology development. However, these models may have still omitted some realistic aspects which could be addressed in further studies, such as multimodal transportation networks with interactions between different modes, physical capacity constraints on roads and activity locations, and ridesharing between persons in different households, etc. In addition, behaviors of multi-class households should also be incorporated in the models developed in this project. Non-recurrent joint activity/travel particularly during weekend and/or public holidays can also be considered for further investigation. Furthermore, an activity-based path flow estimator can be developed to simultaneously estimate the time-dependent activity-travel patterns and dynamic multi-modal path flows based on the limited re-identified MAC address data. As we are now merging to the 5G era, multiple types of sensors and fully connected infrastructure will be available in the near future. Therefore, future studies should extend the developed activity-based travel demand models with the use of multiple sources of urban big data for smart city development.

15205715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205715.value: With the high smartphone penetration rate and increasing Wi-Fi coverage in Hong Kong and other cities, media access control (MAC) addresses could be served as a suitable source of data for supporting the calibration of travel demand models for meeting the needs of the fast-changing metropolitan cities. This project contributes the methodology development on calibration framework of activity-based models for long-term strategic transportation planning with use of the re-identified MAC addresses from smartphones and other communication devices. In the project, advanced data processing and filtering algorithms for filtering and re-identifying the MAC addresses were proposed together with various activity-based travel demand models. The results show that use of MAC address data can efficiently generate the activity-travel patterns for calibration of the activity-based travel demand models. The project has great potential to help transport planners and traffic engineers to make use of the plentiful MAC addresses information for efficient and effective calibration of activity-based travel demand models which can be very useful for transportation network design and integrated land-use and transportation optimization problems under the Big Data arena.

15206115.label: Project Objectives
15206115.value: Design and develop functional intimate apparel for preteen and teenage girls in the early stages of scoliosis on the basis of clinical application and material science as well as garment technology, with the aim to improve their posture, reduce the possibility of spinal curve progression, and satisfy the requirements of the patients as well as address their psychological needs. Facilitate finite element (FE) modeling of the spine of a subject with early scoliosis to evaluate the shear and compressive stresses between the spine and the functional intimate apparel. The achievement of this objective would allow us to compare the biomechanical efficiency of different designs for the treatment of patient with early scoliosis by using the developed FE model. Conduct clinical trials and use non-invasive method based on ultrasound imaging to monitor and evaluate whether the intended objectives of the functional intimate apparel can be achieved.

15206115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206115.value: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is a prevalent chronic condition that gradually leads to the three dimensional deformity of the spine. Spine curvature increases in youths as puberty progresses. Generally, only observation is suggested for adolescents with early scoliosis (Cobb’s angle ≤ 20°). Rigid brace treatment is too draconian for them due to the high corrective force which nearly constrains all movements. Flexible brace treatment is an alternative option; however, its efficacy is still controversial. Functional intimate apparel with a specialized design for teenagers with scoliosis is limited and most part of them can only provide some improvement for bad postures, such as hunchback. A scientific approach should be used to design and develop functional intimate apparel as a treatment option for adolescents with early scoliosis. In this study, the design of functional intimate apparel will incorporate different mechanisms, such as a) compression and pulling forces through a close fit of the intimate apparel, b) lumbar flexion by using a supporting belt, c) transverse forces applied by inserting pads inside the pocket lining by using the principle of the 3-point pressure system, d) axial rotation or coupled motion by using a system with uneven straps, and e) an active mechanism that aims to shift the trunk away from areas of pressure. In clinical situations, the way that orthotic loads (from the functional intimate apparel) are transmitted to the spine still is not well understood. Therefore, finite element modeling of the spine of those with AIS to evaluate the shear and compressive stresses between the spine and the functional intimate apparel will be developed. The developed finite element model (FEM) allows the testing of a large number of virtual designs. The numerical simulations allow the comparison of immediate corrections obtained by using different intimate apparel designs or inserting of padding into different locations for the same patient. The FEM also acts as a versatile tool to examine the impact of varying specific design parameters and relative interactions between them. Alternative monitoring strategies will be used to reduce radiation exposure and better quantify the 3D deformity of adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). A non-invasive and safe method for evaluating and monitoring AIS based on a combination of ultrasound imaging, 3D torso profiling and infrared thermography will be used in this study. The achieving of this objective would allow frequent follow-up evaluations and reduce the overall radiation load during the duration of the therapy. 青少年原發性脊柱側彎是一種很普遍、脊柱三維變形的慢性疾病，側彎的弧度會隨著學童的青春期發育成長而增加。非手術治療的患者曲線為25至40度，需要配戴矯形架才有效控制側彎弧度的發展。由於需要長時間配戴並可能引起皮膚敏感和不適， 一般治療順應性偏低。患者曲線為20度以下多會被例為觀察個案，只可以定期覆診評估病童的骨骼發展。有見及此，本項目結合了臨床經驗、纺織工程學以及材料科學去研發一件青少年早期脊柱側彎專用的功能性内衣。 在這項研究中，功能性內衣的設計將結合不同的原理，例如一) 通過貼身剪裁提供壓縮力及拉伸力；二) 支持帶能穩定腰椎前屈；三) 由口袋襯裡內部插入襯墊施加橫向壓力；四) 通過使用不平衡織帶提供軸向轉動；以及五) 使身體主動地避開壓力位置。

15206115.label: Realisation of objectives
15206115.value: Scoliosis is a spinal deformity found in individuals with a lateral curvature of the spine that is over 10 degrees. Bracing is the traditional and universal non-operative treatment. The main correctional mechanism of braces is the application of a three-point pressure system. However, rigid braces are uncomfortable and cause psychological anxiety in adolescents due to their awkward and bulky appearance. In response to the first objective, a functional intimate apparel for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) by using a conceptual framework for apparel design, or the Functional, Expressive and Aesthetic (FEA) model was designed. The design adopted a similar corrective mechanism as rigid brace to control the spinal deformity. A functional intimate apparel consisting of bra top, pants, pelvis belt, hinge bone with a cushion pad and corrective panel was designed and developed to maximise the spinal correction effect of flexible brace and minimise the negative impact such as mobility restriction and discomfort of rigid brace. The corrective panel with a semi-rigid silicon pad is the key component to provide direct pushing force to the convexity of scoliotic spine. The open design in the concavity allows free expansion to promote the correction performance. In response to the second objective, a numerical finite element model (FEM) was developed to simulate the effectiveness of in-brace spinal correction of the proposed functional intimate apparel. There are few studies that have investigated the effectiveness of flexible braces for treating scoliosis by using a biomechanical model. This study therefore develops 3D skeletal, torso, and flexible brace (functional intimate apparel (FIA)) models for FE analysis. A scoliotic female subject was recruited for the development of the FEM and her parents provided consent for her participation. The subject was invited to undergo a radiographic examination, and then 3D body scanning to extract the geometry of her skeletal frame and torso. The simulation model mainly consists of three parts which are the torso body, skeleton and FIA. To build the FEM, first, the geometry models of torso body, skeleton and FIA were created. Secondly, the material properties and element type were defined. After meshing, the numerical processing of the wearing the FIA on the torso was conducted by defining the initial and boundary conditions, displacement condition of the FIA and the loading condition of the torso surface to obtain the numerical solution. Then, the results were pros-processed and validated. The simulation model shown the trend of spinal correction with good accuracy. To response to the third objective, a six-month quasi-experimental pretest-posttest clinical trial has been conducted. The aim of this trial is to assess the ability of a previously developed garment – “posture correction girdle” by PI to control the progression of scoliosis. The corrective effect were compared when the girdle is donned as opposed to when it is doffed. Comparisons of the Cobb’s angle examined by using radiography are carried out to observe pre-intervention versus post-intervention changes as well as pre-intervention versus in-brace correction after 6 months. It is found that the survival rate of the posture correction girdle is up to 90%. More importantly, the results show that there is a significant difference when the girdle is donned as opposed to when it is doffed. These results prove that the use of a pressure garment induces corrective forces onto the spine. After this study, the team modified the design of posture correction girdle and developed another design “functional intimate apparel. A clinical study was conducted to investigate efficacy of the proposed design. Five subjects have been recruited to participate in the 2-hour clinical study to investigate the initial effect of the functional intimate apparel on in-brace correction, contour changes and quality of life and its bio-mechanics. Of these 5 subjects, one subject has been invited to participate in the 3-month clinical study to investigate the short-term changes in spinal deformity, control asymmetry and quality of life. The Cobb’s angle of the subject was improved from 28.1° to 13.3°. The initial spinal correction rate after 3 months was 52.7%. The results are satisfactory and further design modifications will be continued to do.

15206115.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206115.value: The initial in-brace correction rate of the proposed functional intimate apparel was ranged between 9.7% and 87.0%. The subject with single thoracolumbar curve and riser grade 0 obtained the greatest in-brace correction rate. Comparing with other existing braces, the in-brace correction rate of proposed functional intimate apparel for AIS is significantly greater than our previously design - posture correction girdle and other flexible brace in the market - SpineCor. It implicates that the proposed design improves the in-brace correction of existing flexible brace. The result of this preliminary study is also comparable with some of rigid braces from literatures. Regarding the changes of initial in-brace contour asymmetry, there is no correlation between the changes in shoulder asymmetry and in-brace correction. Nevertheless, of 5 recruited subjects, 4 subjects obtained a correction and the symmetry of posterior trunk and correction rate was ranged between 13.1% and 43.2%. Considering the impact of quality of life, questionnaire survey of Bad Sobernheim Stress Questionnaire for Brace (BSSQ) and Brace Questionnaire (BrQ) were conducted. The average score of BSSQ among 5 subjects was 14.0 ± 3.3 which is classified as the moderate stress. Also, the results of BrQ show that the proposed brace almost never induces negative impacts or problems about the general health perception, physical functioning, body pain and social functioning. Regarding to the biomechanics, the interface pressure of thoracic corrective pad and lumbar pad was ranged between 6.0 - 24.4 kPa and 6.1-9.7 kPa respectively. Comparing to literatures, the interface pressure of proposed brace is similar as the rigid braces. It implicates that the use of textile materials also enables to provide similar corrective force as rigid braces did. One subject was recruited to conduct the three-month clinical study. The Cobb’s angle of the subject was improved from 28.1° to 13.3°. The initial spinal correction rate after 3 months was 52.7%. The results show that the proposed brace excels the efficacy of some rigid braces, SpineCor and posture correction girdle. Regarding the change of bodyshape, after wearing the brace for 3 months, the shoulder rotation and posterior trunk symmetry index improved in 29.8% and 13.1% respectively. However, the shoulder obliquity progressed in 1.3˚. Regarding the change in quality of life, after wearing the proposed brace for 3 months, Both SRS-22 score at pre-intervention and after 3 months of intervention are similar, and it implicates that the quality of life did not have a major change after wearing the proposed design.

15206115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206115.value: This study shows the possibility of using textile materials to create direct corrective forces and to push the scoliotic spine for spinal correction. It demonstrates the textile materials enable to provide adequate corrective pressure and results some in-brace correction. However, the sample size of current study was small. A larger sample size is recommended to further investigate the effectiveness of proposed design. More importantly, it is suggested to conduct a clinical study which compare the effectiveness of proposed design and existing rigid brace since rigid brace usually is the universal non-invasive treatment for scoliosis. To enhance the validity of results, a randomised control trial with 90 sample sizes is recommended. Subjects will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: flexible bracing group receiving the treatment of proposed design, rigid bracing group receiving the rigid bracing, and the observation group who do not receive any treatment. After a period, such as 6 months, 12 months and 24 months, the spinal deformity, contour asymmetry, and the quality of life will be assessed.

15206115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206115.value: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is a prevalent chronic condition that gradually leads to the 3D deformity of the spine. Spine curvature increases in youths as puberty progresses. Generally, only observation is suggested for adolescents with early scoliosis. Rigid brace treatment is too draconian for them due to the high corrective force which nearly constrains all movements. Flexible brace treatment is an alternative option; however, its efficacy is still controversial. In this study, a scientific approach is used to design and develop functional intimate apparel as a treatment option for adolescents with early scoliosis. The design includes a bra top, pants, pelvis belt, hinge bone with a cushion pad and corrective panel to maximise the spinal correction effect and minimise the negative impact such as mobility restriction and discomfort of rigid brace. The corrective panel with a semi-rigid silicon pad is the key component to provide direct pushing force to the convexity of scoliotic spine. The developed finite element model allows the testing of a large number of virtual designs. The clinical trial results showed that the proposed design provides 38.5% in-brace correction and 52.7% spinal correction after 3 months of intervention.

15206215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206215.value: An internal fire whirl (IFW) is readily created in a vertical shaft by the burning of a small fire under appropriate ventilation conditions. Electric and magnetic fields are induced by the circular motion of ions and electrons in the IFW. Applying an external electric or magnetic field affects the circular motion of flame ions, and hence the mixing of the fuel radicals with oxygen in an IFW. Creation and attenuation of an IFW can be enhanced or suppressed by applying such an electric or magnetic field. To have a complete understanding of the physical characteristics of an IFW, the electric and magnetic phenomena associated with an IFW will be explored in this project. A scale model of a typical square vertical shaft structure with appropriate widths of sidewall gap for ventilation provision, already constructed as part of an earlier General Research Fund (GRF) project on IFW will be central to the experimental part of the study. Electric and magnetic fields induced by the swirling flame will be studied first. An external electric field will then be applied across the scale model. Air flow patterns through the open roof and sidewall gaps in the shaft model will be studied. Schlieren photography will be applied to study air temperature and flow across the vertical openings in the shaft model. Swirling flame behaviour will be observed by omnidirectional cameras. Flame colour will be studied experimentally to better understand the mixing of fuel with air. All of the above studies on the scale model will then be repeated after also applying an external static constant magnetic field, then a static gradient magnetic field and finally a time-varying magnetic field. A mathematical model integrating Computational Fluid Dynamics air flow simulation, appropriate combustion models for pool fires, and electromagnetic effects induced by swirling flame motion will be developed to study air flow patterns and flame structures of an IFW in a vertical shaft with and without the application of an electric field or a magnetic field. Full-scale burning tests with the shaft model above will be carried out to validate the scale model observations and mathematical modelling results. Results will be applied to fire hazard assessment in relation to the creation or suppression of IFW in the vertical shafts of tall buildings when an electric or magnetic field is applied. 在適當的通風條件下，豎井內一個燃燒的小火源就能形成內部火旋風。火旋風內離子和電子的旋轉運動會引發電磁場。施加一個外部電磁場將會影響火焰離子的旋轉運動，進而影響火旋風內燃料自由基和氧氣的摻混。因此，外部電磁場可以增強或抑制火旋風的生成或衰減。 為了充分理解內部火旋風的物理特性，本專案將開展與內部火旋風相關的電磁現象的研究。在較早前的優配研究基金項目中建成的典型小尺寸方形豎井及其側壁上設有合適寬度的供風縫隙內，首先研究旋轉火焰誘發的電磁場，然後在小尺寸模型上施加一個外來電場。研究頂部開口和側壁縫隙處的氣流流動模式。用紋影攝像技術研究通過豎直開口的氣流溫度和氣流流動。用全景攝像機記錄旋轉火焰的行為。通過實驗研究火焰輪廓及色彩，以便更好理解燃料和空氣的混合。在施加外部靜態恒定磁場、靜態梯度磁場以及隨時間變化的磁場條件下重複上述研究。 結合計算流體動力學氣流類比、池火燃燒模型和旋轉火焰運動引發的電磁場效應建立數學模型，研究有和沒有施加外部電場和磁場條件下豎井內火旋風的氣流流動模式和火焰結構。開展全尺寸燃燒實驗驗證小尺寸模型的觀測結果和數學模擬結果。研究結果將用於對有外部電場或磁場存在的情況下，與高層建築豎井內火旋風的產生和抑制相關的風險評估。

15206215.label: Realisation of objectives
15206215.value: The three objectives listed in the proposal are: 1. To study the electromagnetic effects of an internal fire whirl created by pool fires in a model vertical shaft with various ventilation conditions due to openings in the shaft walls. A 1.45 m tall square scale vertical shaft model was used to study the characteristics of the magnetic field generated by internal fire whirl (IFW) by burning liquid fuel. The induced electromagnetic fields in regions adjacent to the IFW were measured by a DC magnetometer. The flow core structure of IFW was studied to investigate the changes of the fire whirl characteristics under the applied electric field. Flame colour of the IFW was also observed to study the chemical radicals involved. The study was repeated by applying a magnetic field across the IFW generated in the scale shaft model. Air exchange flow through the openings of a vertical shaft model was studied by Schlieren photography at the National Kaohsiung First University of Science and Technology, Taiwan. The neutral plane height was measured across the corner gap. Thermocouples were used to measure smoke temperature and to counter-check results from the BOS technique. An analytical model was developed to explain the magnetic field generated by a fire whirl. As far as the magnetic field around a fire whirl is concerned, the fire whirl is equivalent to a solenoid carrying a current, which is related to the characteristics pertinent to the fire whirl. The vertical component of the magnetic field obtained from this model is compared with experimental results acquired in fire whirls in a shaft model. The gap width of the shaft model was varied to investigate its impact on fire whirl characteristics, such as flame development, swirling intensity, flame height, flame temperature and heat release rate of the gasoline pool fire. Vigorous flame swirling motions were generated when the ratio of the gap width to the shaft section perimeter was within a certain range. From the flame streamline angle, it was observed that the swirling component was much stronger than the buoyancy component near the bottom of the burning region. The swirling component decreased and became roughly the same as buoyancy near the middle. Photographs taken on the IFW using a high-speed camera at critical times of swirling motion development were used to observe the stages for generating the fire whirl. Two flame vortex tubes moving over the horizontal burning surface of the liquid pool were observed. Based on these observations, a set of more detailed schematic diagrams on the swirling motion was constructed. From the observed flame heights under different gap widths and using three assumptions on the variation of air entrainment velocity with height, an empirical expression relating the burning rate with flame height and the corner gap width was derived from the observation with high-speed camera. The correlation expression of the burning rate of the pool fire obtained would be useful in fire safety design in vertical shafts of tall buildings. 2. To study the characteristics of an internal fire whirl in a tall vertical shaft when external electric and magnetic fields are applied. Generation and characteristics of the IFW in a shaft model under external electric and magnetic fields were studied using Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). A simple analytical study on flame height, flame swirling and buoyant plume of the fire whirl was studied based on experimental results and observations on soot particles carried by the gas motion, with solution of the angular velocity equation for circulatory fluid motion. Relative magnitudes of baroclinic force and buoyancy under different magnetic field were investigated. Attenuation of swirling motion of the fire whirl was studied by including variation in vertical velocity and viscous dissipation using the basic equations of vorticity. The relative effects of baroclinic force and buoyancy were found to depend on height and on the heat release rate from the fire pool. Three to five regions were observed from the bottom to the top of a fire whirl, according to the baroclinic force and buoyancy ratio. Vertical variation of Froude number was also investigated. Rotating velocity and attenuation of vorticity from the bottom to the top of the fire whirl were studied by analytical solutions of a simple equation for circulatory fluid flow. Effects of external electric and magnetic fields were studied. Full-scale burning test results on a 9 m tall vertical shaft model were used. A correlation expression of flame height with the width of the single corner gap was studied with three assumptions on variation of air entrainment velocity with height, an expression relating the flame height and the corner gap width was derived for the IFW using the set of compiled experimental data. The correlation expression obtained would be useful for fire safety design in vertical shafts. Numerical simulation indicates that even under low gravity of 0.0125g, circular air motion would still bring fuel to a high level to give a larger flame height in the shaft model, compared with that in free space under the same gravity environment, the ratio in flame height being about 1.5 except at very low gravity value. For IFW generated in the shaft model, the heat release rate, the maximum tangential velocity and the maximum axial velocity decrease slowly as gravity decreases when gravity is above 0.1g. Below 0.1g, these quantities decrease rapidly as gravity decreases. Reduction in gravity also changes the flame shape of IFW. 3. To provide appropriate protection against the generation of internal fire whirls in tall vertical shafts. Based on the above results, applying an external electric or magnetic field or both to protect vertical shaft against IFW fire will be recommended for firefighting guides. Associated fire safety management schemes for the building users were also suggested. Another point, aged structures are now widely repaired by fibre reinforced polymer (FRP). However, flame swirling generated would act on the FRP repairing materials in a vertical shaft to give hazard as a consequence. IFW experiments in the 145 cm tall vertical shaft model clearly illustrated that. Action of swirling flame on FRP installed at the model wall should be further studied.

15206215.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206215.value: An internal fire whirl (IFW) can be generated readily in a tall vertical shaft model under appropriate ventilation provisions. The IFW generated by burning a pool fire in the 145 cm scale vertical shaft model with a single corner gap of appropriate width was studied extensively. The electric and magnetic characteristics of IFW were investigated. Action of external electric and magnetic fields on IFW characteristics under different corridor width and depth were investigated. Schlieren photography was applied to study swirling flame behavior and swirling pattern by high-speed cameras. Experimental studies on a 145 cm scale model with applying magnetic field were compared with some full-scale burning data in a 9 m tall shaft. Further, effect of gravity on IFW characteristics was also investigated. The following were found: • Magnetic field induced by swirling motion of flame ions and electrons in the IFW under different ventilation conditions. • A mathematical model on the magnetic field generated by IFW. • Action of magnetic field on the IFW generation mechanism. • Shape of flame pattern under different conditions. Effects of applying external electric and magnetic field to suppress IFW in different building geometries, in addition to vertical shaft, should be studied in more detail. Results should be justified by more full-scale burning tests to work out workable design guides. Research results compiled can be used to work out new firefighting strategy in IFW suppression in vertical shaft fires. A total of 6 refereed science citation index journal papers and 2 conference papers were presented. One part-time PhD student (who is a practicing building services engineer) working on IFW would submit the thesis by end October 2019 before retirement of the Principal Investigator (PI). The PI is mentoring a team of government fire officers who are updating the local codes for atriums, supertall buildings, cavern structures and residential sprinklers in some special buildings since 2010. Results and recommendations from this project will be integrated with the associated literature and existing overseas fire codes in order to then draft new codes for tall buildings with the Hong Kong Fire Services Department. A special section on the IFW phenomenon will be drafted under the leadership of the PI, with reference to existing local codes, updated overseas codes and associated fire research literature.

15206215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206215.value: There are many buildings with tall vertical shaft, with a fire occurred inside reported before. There, the associated fire safety codes are not yet available in many countries. Physical characteristics including the electric and magnetic effects on an IFW in a vertical shaft aimed at in this project would provide protection against fire hazards for lift shafts and similar types of architectural features such as internal building voids. More full-scale burning tests with the shaft models and other room geometries should be carried out to validate the scale model observations and mathematical modelling results. Results are useful to fire hazard assessment in relation to the creation or suppression of IFW in the vertical shafts of tall buildings when an electric or magnetic field is applied. In fact, the smoke filling process in a room with IFW is studied in another RGC-GRF funded project led by the PI. In addition to the observations and exploration of any new physical flame swirling phenomena under external electric and magnetic fields, long-term and principal benefits likely to result from this research are further development of new theory. Results will be applicable to government and regulatory bodies responsible for building fire safety.

15206215.value: An internal fire whirl (IFW) is readily created in a vertical shaft by the burning of a small fire under appropriate ventilation conditions. Magnetic fields are induced by the circular motion of ions and electrons in the swirling flame. Similarly, applying an actual electric or magnetic field would affect the swirling flame motion. The electric and magnetic phenomena associated with an IFW were explored in this project. A scale model of a typical square vertical shaft structure with appropriate widths of sidewall gap for ventilation provision was used. Effect of applying an external electric or magnetic field on the circular motion of flame ions was studied. A mathematical model was developed to study magnetic field induced by the flame ions integrating Computational Fluid Dynamics air flow simulation and appropriate combustion models for pool fires to study air flow patterns and flame structures of an IFW in a vertical shaft. 15206415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206415.value: With the industrial development and population growth, energy shortage is believed to be one of the emergent problems encountered by the current world. To combat the pressure from energy shortage, people make every endeavor to improve the efficiency of energy usage and storage and at the same time to seek for new energy resources. Lithium-ion battery (LIB) is a electrochemical unit that has been widely used for electrical energy storing and transferring. Developing LIB with high capacity, high charging rate and prolonged life would not only be of great value to the development of the emerging industries, such as portable electronic devices and electrical vehicles, but greatly alleviate the pressure from energy crisis. LIB with high capacity needs high-capacity anode materials such as silicon and SnO2, which have been well recognized as the most promising anode materials for the next-generation LIB. However, accompanying with their high capacity, these anode materials simultaneously exhibit large volume change (300~400%) during the charging/discharging process, giving rise to a series of problems including pulverization, delamination from the current collector and consequent degradation of the electrochemical performance of the LIB. One of the attempts to combat the volume expansion problem is to introduce the core/shell structure – a core of anode material constrained by a hard coating or shell, so that the volume change could be limited to a safe extent. However, intuitive sense implies that if the volume expansion is restricted, it should be more difficult energetically to get the lithium inserted into the active materials. As a consequence, the charging rate and capacity of the LIB would be affected. To date, it is still unclear how the external mechanical constraint affects the insertion of lithium in the anode materials especially in those with large lithiation-induced volume expansion. In this project, we propose a systematic analysis of the effects of mechanical constraint on the electrochemical performance of anode materials with large lithiation-induced volume expansion such as Si and SnO2. The aim of this project is to provide operational guidelines to the design and optimization of the core/shell structured anodes. The outcomes of this project would greatly promote a better application of the core/shell structured anode materials in the next-generation LIBs. 隨著工業發展和人口膨脹，能源短缺成為當今世界面臨的巨大挑戰之一。為了應對能源短缺問題，人們一方面在努力提高能源使用和存儲效率，另一方面也在積極開發新能源。鋰離子電池作為一種廣泛應用的能源存儲和轉化器件，發展高容量、快速充放電、長壽命的鋰離子電池，不僅有助於如移動電子設備和電動車等新興工業產業的發展，也可以極大地緩解能源危機所帶來的壓力。高容量鋰離子電池的發展離不開高容量電極材料，其中矽和二氧化錫是兩種極具潛力的下一代負極電極材料。然而這些高容量負極材料在充放電過程中往往伴隨著巨大的體積變化（300-400%），容易產生電極材料破碎、集流體脫層等問題，從而導致整個鋰離子電池的失效。為了解決這類由體積膨脹所產生的問題，人們引入核殼結構的設計理念來提高鋰離子電池的穩定性：使用一種較硬材質的殼層材料包裹高容量負極材料，從而有效地限制體積膨脹所帶來的影響。然而，值得注意的是，如果嵌鋰過程中的體積膨脹被外部約束所限制住，鋰離子有極大可能將無法繼續嵌入到負極材料中去，從而影響鋰離子電池的充放電速率和容量。到目前為止，仍然不清楚外部約束將如何影響鋰離子的嵌入，尤其是針對諸如矽和二氧化錫這種在嵌鋰過程中伴隨著巨大體積膨脹的電極材料。在本研究課題中，我們提出全面系統的方法來研究外部約束對高容量電極材料電化學嵌鋰過程的影響。通過一系列切實可行的研究，提出核殼結構電極材料的優化設計方案，從而極大地推動核殼結構電極材料在下一代鋰離子電池中的應用。

15206415.label: Realisation of objectives
15206415.value: Objectives 1: To characterize the effect of mechanical constraint on the electrochemical performance of anode materials with large LIVE such as Si and SnO2. To reveal the effect of mechanical constraint on the electrochemical performance of Si, we performed molecular dynamics simulations for the lithiation and delithiation processes of Si nanosheet under mechanical constraint with attention focused on the lithiation rate and specific mass capacity of the Si. The results showed that Si nanosheet under stronger constraint reaches the lower extent of lithiation as compared to the free-standing one, implying that mechanical constraint would reduce the diffusivity of Li ions in Si and therefore reduce the lithiation rate. Meanwhile, our results also showed a strong dependence of the specific capacity on the mechanical constraint. Under weak constraint, full lithiation can be achieved in Si; while under strong constraint, partial lithiation (~20%) is achieved, giving rise to specific capacity around ~800 mA h/g only. To alleviate the negative effects caused by the mechanical constraint, three approaches were proposed: (1) choosing a softer binder material, (2) reducing the thickness of the Si nanosheet, and (3) introducing porous structure. Upon the completion of the above work (published in JPCC, 2018; Nanoscale, 2019), Objective 1 of this project is achieved by 100%. Objectives 2: To formulate the lithiation process in the constrained anode materials such as Si or SnO2 cores encapsulated in carbon shells For the carbon-coated silicon core-shell nanoparticles (designated as Si@C NPs), in-situ lithiation experiments were carried out and showed a counterintuitive fracture phenomenon. That is, Si nanoparticles become easier to fracture upon lithiation if coated with a carbon coating. To shed light on such an unusual fracture of Si@C NPs during lithiation, finite element analysis (FEA) was carried out. The results showed that the mechanical dissimilarity between the carbon coating and lithiated Si exaggerates the driving force pushing a crack pre-existing in the carbon coating to propagate into the Si nanoparticle. Therefore, the crack in the carbon coating, once developed, is quite easy to propagate into the Si core. To prevent the Si@C NP from fracturing, the integrity of the carbon coating should be secured, which can be achieved by optimizing the geometries of the Si@C NP as demonstrated by the follow-up FEA analysis. Moreover, we have also conducted in-situ lithiation experiments with the yolk-shell structured carbon-coated silicon nanoparticles (designated as Si@void@C NPs) and observed the dimension-dependent fracture of Si@void@C NPs during lithiation. To account for such observation, the stress in the carbon shell caused by the lithiation-induced expansion of the Si yolk was analyzed by theoretical modeling based in the framework of elasticity. The analytical solution to the maximum tensile stress in the carbon shell was obtained as a function of the characteristic dimensions of the Si@void@C NP. Upon the completion of the above work (published in Nanoscale, 2016; Composites Communications, 2016), Objective 2 of this project is achieved by 100%. Objectives 3: To provide guidelines for the design of core/shell structured anode materials for high-performance LIBs Our studies on the core/shell structured anode materials such as the Si@C NPs and Si@void@C NPs unveiled the mechanics behind the fracture phenomenon of these anode materials, based on which the guidelines for the design of these nanoparticles were proposed. For example, to ensure the integrity of the carbon coating of the Si@C NPs, the ratio between the core diameter and coating thickness should be less than 0.7. For the Si@void@C NPs, a phase diagram in terms of the core diameter and coating thickness was proposed, by which one can find the best combination of these two parameters for higher capacity and lower risk of rupture. Upon the completion of the above work (published in Nanoscale, 2016; Composites Communications, 2016), Objective 3 of this project is achieved by 100%.

15206415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206415.value: In this project, all the results were obtained from either numerical simulation or experiments with a simplified model and half-cell batteries. For the practical application of our results in the battery industry, experiments based on full-cell batteries should be carried out to verify the feasibility and effectiveness. Given sufficient funding, we can complete this further development within one year.

15206415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206415.value: Silicon (Si) has been deemed as one of the most promising anode materials for the next-generation lithium-ion batteries due to its extremely high specific capacity. Nevertheless, the large volume change of Si during the lithiation and delithiation process limits its application. As one potential solution to this problem, the external coating has been adopted to constrain the volume change of Si. To understand the effect of such a constraint on the electrochemical performance of the LIBs, we have carried out the present studies. The results of our studies confirmed our initial hypothesis that mechanical constraints do affect the lithiation rate and capacity of the Si-based anode materials for LIBs. To alleviate the negative effects caused by the mechanical constraint, we proposed several guidelines for the design of the anode materials such as the structural optimization and introduction of porosity. The results of this project are believed to be of great value to promote the application of Si-based LIBs in industries.

15206815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206815.value: The recent increase in identity theft has drawn the public attention on the potential risk of using remote services. In fact, frauds and identity theft are on the rise in Hong Kong and mainland China because of the popularity of using mobile phones to access remote services. To save operation cost, insurance companies and banks in this region also encourage their customers to use remote services. While remote services bring great convenience and benefit to customers, the services have also attracted criminals to carry out fraudulent activities. Traditionally, authentication of these services relies on usernames and passwords. This authentication method, however, is no longer adequate for safeguarding the security of remote services. The recent advance in speaker recognition technology has demonstrated that voice biometrics could be an important part of the authentication process. For example, using speaker recognition technologies, the identity of a caller can be verified in a live call and financial transactions can be stopped if fraud is detected. Voice biometrics can also help call centers to reduce the risk of leaking customers' information caused by social engineering fraudulence. This project aims to develop a special form of deep neural networks (DNNs) called denoising deep autoencoder for robust text-independent speaker verification. Speaker specific features, referred to as bottleneck features, are extracted from the bottleneck layer of the autoencoder. Unlike conventional autoencoders, our denoising deep autoencoders are able to reconstruct the clean speech signals even if the input signals are contaminated with noise and reverberation effects, which result in robust bottleneck features. Another advantage of our autoencoders is that they are adapted to the characteristics of individual speakers, which enrich the speaker-specific information in the bottleneck features. To make the conventional probabilistic linear discriminant analysis (PLDA) more resilience to varying acoustic environments, two new PLDA models are proposed. These models either make explicit use of SNR information during training and scoring or incorporate the SNR variability into the generative model. The proposed bottleneck features can be readily applied to these new PLDA models. The proposed methods will be evaluated on the latest dataset provided by the NIST. The proposed work will provide insight into deep learning and the extraction of speaker-dependent features from deep neural networks. It will also address the SNR and reverberation variability in speaker verification systems. The proposed framework is also valuable to other problem domains where channel and session variabilities are detrimental to performance. 最近增加的身份盜竊個案引起公眾關注使用遠程服務的潛在風險。事實上，欺詐和身份盜竊在香港和中國大陸的增加是因為使用手機來訪問遠程服務的流行。為節約運營成本，保險公司和銀行也鼓勵他們的客戶使用遠程服務。遠程服務在給客戶帶來巨大的方便和利益的同時，還吸引了罪犯進行欺詐活動。傳統上，這些服務的身份驗證依賴於用戶名和密碼。然而，這種身份驗證方法已經不再適合保障遠程服務的安全。最近在說話人識別技術的進步已經證明語音生物識別技術會是身份驗證過程的一個重要組成部分。例如，使用說話人識別技術，可以通過在線電話驗證使用者的身份，而如果監測到欺詐，金融交易可以被停止。語音生物識別技術還可以幫助呼叫中心減少由社會工程欺詐造成的客戶信息洩漏風險。 這個項目旨在開發一種特殊形式的深度神經網絡(DNN)，被稱為降噪深度自動編碼器，用於穩定的、與文本無關的說話人驗證。說話人的特定特徵，稱為瓶頸特徵，提取於自動編碼器的瓶頸層。與傳統的自動編碼器不同，即使輸入信號含有噪聲和混響效果，我們的去噪深度自動編碼器能夠重建乾淨語音信號，導致了瓶頸特徵的穩定性。我們的降噪深度自動編碼器的另一個優點是，他們適應每個說個人的特點，豐富了瓶頸特徵中說話人的特定信息。為使傳統的概率線性判別分析(PLDA)對不同的聲學環境擁有更多彈性，我們提出了兩個新的PLDA模型。一個模型在訓練和評分中明確地利用信噪比信息；另一個則將信噪比的變異合併到生成模型。我們提出的瓶頸特徵可以方便地應用於這些新的PLDA模型。 我們提出的方法將被評估於由NIST提供的最新數據集。提出的工作將提供深度學習的見解和從深度神經網絡提取的說話人特徵。它還將解決說話人驗證系統的信噪比和混響變化。對於其他會被頻道和會話的變化而影響性能的領域，擬議的框架也是有價值的。

15206815.label: Realisation of objectives
15206815.value: For Objective 1, we have developed a DNN that can (1) denoise the MFCC vectors through a denoising autoencoder, (2) extract noise robust bottleneck (BN) features, and (3) estimate senone posteriors for total-variability matrix training and i-vector extraction. We name the resulting i-vector the senone i-vector. The results have been published in an international conference. For Objective 2, we have developed a new DNN architecture for robust speaker verification. In particular, an SNR-adaptive denoising classifier is constructed by stacking two layers of restricted Boltzmann machines (RBMs) on top of a denoising deep autoencoder, where the top- RBM layer is connected to a soft-max output layer that outputs the posterior probabilities of speakers and the top-RBM layer outputs speaker-dependent bottleneck features. The results have been reported in an international conference and a journal paper in IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech and Language Processing. For Objective 3, we have invented a new method that uses DNN to compute the posterior probabilities of indicator variables in PLDA mixture models. We called it DNN-driven mixture of PLDA. We applied the new method to the NIST 2012 SRE dataset and found that the resulting PLDA mixture models perform significantly better than other existing models. The results have been published in IEEE SLT 2016 Workshop on Spoken Language Technology. We have also wrote a journal version of this conference paper and it has been published by IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech and Language Processing.

15206815.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206815.value: This project has resulted in a number of novel algorithms for robust speaker verification. In particular, the project has developed deep neural network based score calibration algorithms with multi-task learning to make speaker verification systems more practical. The algorithms can make the score shift due to background noise negligible so that the same decision threshold can be used under both clean and noisy environments. The method and its results were published in Ref. 8-1 of Part C. The project has also resulted in a mixture PLDA backend that is robust under a wide range of background noise level. The method is novel in that we are the first group to use DNN to estimate the posterior probabilities of the mixtures in the PLDA mixture model. The method and results have been published in Ref. 8-2 of Part C of this final report. The third contribution of this project is the development of a denoising autoencoder that allows us to extract robust and phonetic-aware bottleneck features for i-vector/PLDA speaker recognition. The project has demonstrated that the phonetic-aware bottleneck features can lead to robust senone i-vectors that outperform the conventional i-vectors. The results are published in Ref. 9-2 and 9-3 of Part C of this report.

15206815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206815.value: Robustness is always a serious issue in speaker verification. The methods developed in this project can be extended to speaker diarization and for far-field speaker verification. It is also interesting to see if the methods could work with elderly speech and children speech, which is a largely unexplored area.
