15206915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206915.value: 正如當今複雜的動態系統依賴於各種控制機制，毫無疑問，控制理論也將極大推動量子工程學技術的發展。這個項目的目的是為量子控制系統開發嚴格的系統分析方法，我們將集中考慮下面三個主題： 主題1：研究量子線性系統的結構分解和實現。更具體地說，我們分析量子線性系統的能控/能觀結構分解，並研究如何通過經典系統設計技術來實現量子線性系統。 主題2：研究量子線性系統對多光子輸入狀的響應。更具體地說，我們推導出量子線性系統對初始糾纏多光子輸入狀態的輸出狀態解析表達式。 主題3：研究兩能級量子系統對單光子輸入狀態的響應。更具體地講，我們得到兩能級量子系統在單光子驅動下傳出光子脈衝形狀的解析表達式。作為應用，我們顯示如何將這個理論應用於單光子開關的模型。 主題1揭示線性量子系統的能控／能觀方面的重要結構信息。這個結構信息在線性量子系統的模型降價的研究中有著直接的應用。線性量子系統的新的實現方法將建立一個從經典控制理論到量子系統設計的橋樑。比如，它允許我們通過研究無損正實經典系統或者J－無損經典系統來設計量子系統。所以說，提議的線性量子系統將有力地豐富線性量子系統與網絡的理論基礎。 主題2提供了量子線性系統對多光子態響應的深入研究。待發展的理論適用於無源和有源量子線性系統。得到的輸出狀態解析表達式可以被用來計算光的各種統計特性，例如，一階和二階相干特性。 主題3研究兩能級（非線性）原子系統如何操作單光子波。我們將給出輸出光場的脈衝波包形狀的解析表達式。此外，提出的方法適用於單光子開關的研究。因此，本研究將有助理解光與原子的相互作用，有助於片上集成的量子網絡的基礎。 擬議的研究將對迅速成長的量子控制工程學科做出貢獻。

15206915.label: Realisation of objectives
15206915.value: All the three research objectives have been accomplished. The details are given below. Objective 1. develop a realisation theory for quantum linear systems. Structure determines property. It is important to analyze the structure of a dynamical system, as witnessed by the great success of the Kalman canonical form for classical linear systems developed in 1960s. Partially financially supported by this project, we developed the Kalman canonical form for quantum-mechanical linear systems; see journal papers (Nos 9 and 15) and the conference paper (No. 3). We have applied the general framework to a few physical experiments for example opto-mechanical quantum systems built on superconducting circuits and the Michelson interferometer. Moreover, in journal paper No 12 we proposed a network synthesis theory for mixed quantum-classical linear systems. Finally, in journal paper No. 18 we proposed a canonical decomposition for quantum two-level systems which is used to demonstrate the decoherence-free subsystems, quantum non-demolition variables and quantum back-action evading measurement. Objective 2. derive analytic expressions for output states of quantum linear systems driven by initially entangled multi-photon input states. In two journal papers (Nos 2 and 5), we conducted a comprehensive investigation of how quantum linear systems respond to single- and multi-photon states. For example, the explicit form of the output photon state has been derived by means of tensor computing. The results have been used to derive many special cases scattered in the Physics literature. As a single- or multi-photon state is essential a non-stationary stochastic process, it is better to view it in both the temporal and spectral domains simultaneously. Motivated by this, we have defined Wigner spectrum for single-photon states and demonstrated how it changes as the photon passes through linear quantum networks. Objective 3. derive analytic expressions for output states of quantum two-level systems driven by single-photon input states. Partially financially supported by this project, we have studied in detail the interaction between quantum two-level systems and single- and multi-photon states. Research results are published in journal papers (Nos 3, 6, 8, 11, 13, 14, 17) and conference papers (1, 2, 4). In the journal paper No. 3, a general framework of quantum filtering for an arbitrary quantum Markovian system derived by a multi-photon state is developed. This result was later applied in journal papers No. 8 and 13 to study the two special cases, namely a two-level atom driven by one or two photons. In journal publications Nos. 6, and 13, we derived the analytic form of the output photon state of a quantum two-level system which is driven by one or two photons. In journal papers Nos. 11 and 17, we proposed reduced quantum filters whose dimension can be significantly smaller than that the original quantum filters. This may find useful applications in filter-based real-time quantum control or quantum information processing.

15206915.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206915.value: (1). Developed a mixed linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) and H-Infinity control theory for coherent feedback control of quantum linear systems in Journal Publication No. 1. (2). Proposed Wigner spectrum for continuous-mode single-photon states in Journal Publication No. 2. (3). Developed filtering theory for single- and multi-photon states in Journal Publication Nos. 3, 8, and 13, and Conference Publication Nos. 1 and 2. (4). Derived the analytical form of the output photon state when a two-level or multi-level system is driven by one-, two- or even three-photons in Journal Publication Nos. 6 and 14. (5). Developed efficient tensor algorithms for computing the geometric measure of entanglement of multipartite quantum systems in Journal Publication Nos. 10 and 16. (6). Derived a necessary and sufficient condition by means of regularly decomposable tensors for classicality of spin states in Journal Publication No. 4. (7). Developed a dynamical analysis theory for linear systems driven by multi-channel multi-photon states in Journal Publication No. 5. (8). Proposed classical and quantum stochastic models for memristive circuits in Journal Publication No. 7. (9). Developed Kalman decomposition theory for quantum linear systems in Journal Publication Nos. 9 and 15 and Conference Publication No. 3. (10). Proposed quantum projection filters for open quantum systems which have much lower dimensions in Journal Publication Nos. 11 and 17, and Conference Publication No. 4. (11). Proposed a network synthesis theory for mixed quantum-classical linear stochastic models in Journal Publication No. 12. (12). Study the structure of quantum two-level system by means of the fundamental concepts of controllability and observability; see Journal Publication No. 18.

15206915.value: (1) Design feedback controllers for quantum linear systems based on their Kalman canonical decomposition. (2) Explore the structure of general finite-level quantum systems beyond the two-level ones. (3) Design tensor-optimization-based quantum algorithms.

15206915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206915.value: Quantum computing is rapidly developing. Quantum computing has the potential of solving many hard problems which are unimaginable for a classical computer, for example factorizing a large integer efficiently. Quantum computing algorithms must be run in a quantum computer; hence building a reliable quantum computer is the Holy Grail for quantum computing. To build a quantum computer which is a hardware, the underlying quantum-mechanical systems must be well controlled. This motives the study of quantum control, in other words, the control and engineering of quantum systems. In this project, we investigated the structure of quantum linear systems such as optical systems, onto-mechanical systems and atomic ensembles. We have obtained their fundamental structure in terms of the Kalman canonical form. We also investigated how a quantum system processes photons which are flying quantum bits (qubits) fundamental to quantum information and quantum computation. Besides quantum linear systems, we also studied the interaction between atoms (stationary qubits) and photons (flying qubits). It is clear that the study done is theoretical, but they are essential for a successful quantum computing.

15207215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15207215.value: 本項目旨在發展一種超分子離子聚合物/碳納米管複合材料，用於設計和和製造電-機械轉換能力增強型的電活性高分子（EAP）致動器。 EAP由於質輕、性質可調、高斷裂韌性及高輸出位移等獨特優點，能用於微納米或大尺寸致動器的製造，可應用於機器人、仿生、航天工程等領域。離子聚合物/金屬複合材料(IPMC)是一種EAP複合材料，被認為是最有前景的智能材料之一。但當前成熟的IPMC致動器輸出機械力非常有限，且運行過程中，反复致動產生的應力造成致動器電極被破壞，對電-機械性能產生不利影響。 為了克服上述缺點，我們基於最新的納米碳技術和IPMC離子交換材料的發展，開發了一種輸出力增強型的新穎離子聚合物及一種無應力損傷電極結構。項目團隊在納米碳及IPMC技術方面擁有相關的研究經歷，曾涉及了納米碳材料的製備、IPMC多場有限元分析、用於IPMC的無氟化離子聚合物製備、碳納米管改性的IPMC製備。 在本項目的方法設計中，性能的提高將由三個相互關聯的途徑實現：（1）超分子主客體相互作用；（2）碳納米結構的修飾；（3）新型致動器結構設計。高分子結構中的β-環糊精（βCD）和二茂鐵（FC）的主客體相互作用將增強致動器的輸出力；單壁碳納米管（SWCNT）既改善離子聚合物的離子傳輸及力學性能，又可用於製造高性能電極；致動器的電極結構被設計成一種無應力結構，在致動器工作時，不至於產生應力破壞作用。 該項目的實施與成功將有助於：（1）多尺度致動器的開發，特別是用於醫療領域的納米致動器開發；（2）發展克服傳統IPMC低輸出力製約的新方法； （3）更好的理解主客體相互作用和離子輸運的雙重致動機制及SWCNT的增強效應。 研究小組以前所做的研究工作為本項目順利實施及取得期望成果奠定了堅實的基礎。

15207215.label: Realisation of objectives
15207215.value: The first revised objective was achieved by the successful synthesis of supramolecular ionic polymer composites. The material compositions and the processing conditions for synthesizing were determined. Synthesis of the supramolecular ionic polymer composites consisted of three phases. Phase One: Synthesis of functional monomers β-CD-grafted acrylamide (β-CD-AAM), and Fc-grafted acrylamide (Fc-AAM) monomers were synthesized as the based materials for the redox responsive supramolecular systems. Proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR) was carried out and indicated that β-CD and Fc moieties were grafted onto the acrylamide monomers. Phase Two: Functionalization of carbon nanotubes with vinyl Multi-wall carbon nanotubes (MWNTs) were used to improve ionic transport and mechanical properties for producing high performance electrodes. To overcome the surface incompatibility and poor solubility of MWNTs, a method combining covalent functionalization and in-situ polymerization were developed. Vinyl grafted-MWNTs were synthesized because the vinyl groups on the MWNTs would take part in alkene involved polymer reactions. The chemical structures of the MWNT samples were detected with a Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectrometer. The FTIR spectrum implied that vinyl groups were successfully induced onto MWNTs by the reaction between the (MWNT–NH2) and acrylic acid. Phase Three: Synthesis of supramolecular ionic polymer composite gels The β-CD gels were synthesized by a homogeneous radical copolymerization of β-CD, acrylamide (AAm), N,N’-methylenebis (acrylamide) (MBAAm), and vinyl modified MWNTs, where ammonium peroxodisulfate (APS)/N,N,N’,N’-tetramethyle-thylenediamine (TEMED) was used as the initiator. Fc monomer (Fc-AAm), MBAAm, AAm and MWNTs were used to prepare guest gels. The homogeneous radical copolymerization was initiated by 2,2’-azobis[2-(2-imidazolin-2-yl)-propane] dihydrochloride. The molar ratio of AAm/CD or Fc/MBAAm/MWNT was set to 4.25/4.25/0.50/0.25. In this project, two kinds of actuator configuration were carried out to fully understand the materials’ sensing and actuating properties: (1) Assembled Janus bilayer hydrogel actuators and (2) Single layered electroactive polymer composite actuators. (1) Assembled Janus bilayer hydrogel actuators Janus bilayer hydrogel actuators with and without CNTs were fabricated by assembling host β-CD and guest Fc hydrogel strips through host-guest interaction. When the β-CD hydrogel film was placed into the water, hydroxy groups on β-CD bonded with water and the interior of the annulus was hydrophobic. Fc acted as the hydrophobic guest and formed host-guest complexes with β-CD. The actuating performance of the bilayer actuators with and without CNTs was evaluated in water. Bending deformation occurred within 1 minute after placing the bilayer hydrogels into water. The bilayer bent towards the Fc and MWCNTs modified Fc (MFc) hydrogels layer due to the higher swelling ratio of CD and MWCNTs modified CD (MCD) gels. The bilayers bent into curvatures. ImageJ, an image analysis software, was used to analyse the mechanical output of the bilayers. The bending strain (ε) and bending stress (σ) and bending moment (M) of the bilayers were calculated. The value of σ and M were, respectively, 1.4 Nm−2 and 9.5×10−3 Nm for the unmodified bilayers. For MCD/MFc bilayers, the value of the elastic modulus of the bilayer was about 20 kPa, doubling that of the unmodified ones. The results suggested that the supramolecular ion assembly between β-CD and Fc was able to improve the mechanical properties of the hydrogels. (2) Single layered electroactive polymer composite actuator The supramolecular ion assembly of a copolymer containing β-CD and Fc moieties showed the redox-switchable properties with conferring voltage controllable assembly and disassembly features. A single layer actuator made of this copolymer was expected to outperform the bilayer actuators by eliminating the delamination of the bilayer actuators. Therefore, single layered supramolecular ionic polymer–carbon nanotube composite (SIPC) hydrogel actuators were fabricated via in situ free radical polymerization based on styrene sulfonic sodium (SSNa), β-CD-grafted acrylamide, and Fc grafted acrylamide. To fabricate the single layered electroactive polymer composite actuator, single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs) were used. Vinyl-functionalized single-wall carbon nanotubes (V-SWCNTs), β-CD-grafted acrylamide (β-CD-AAM), and Fc-grafted acrylamide (Fc-AAM) were synthesized using the similar procedures and parameters in preparing the host and guest gels for the Janus bilayer hydrogel actuators. V-SWCNTs with different weight fractions (0, 0.25, 0.5, and 1 wt%) were incorporated in the supramolecular ionic polymer composites. This arrangement facilitated investigations on the reinforcing effect of CNT inclusion on the electroactive polymer composites. The second revised objective was achieved by the successful fabrication of carbon nanotube reinforced electroactive polymer composites by redox responsive supramolecular assemblies and mechanical testing and electro-mechanical testing of the composites. The effects of carbon nanotube inclusion and redox responsive supramolecular assemblies were also studied. (1) Effects of carbon nanotube inclusion After the electroactive polymer composites were synthesised, tensile tests were conducted with reference to the ASTM D638 standard. The results showed that the tensile properties of the SWCNT-incorporated supramolecular ionic polymer–carbon nanotube (SIPC) hydrogel were improved. Noticeably, as the SWCNT content increased from 0.0 to 1.0 wt%, the tensile strength of the composite hydrogels increased significantly from 12 kPa to 47 kPa. The tensile strength of the SIPC hydrogels was effectively regulated by adjusting the SWCNT content, without compromising the toughness. The enhancement of the tensile property of the SWCNT-containing SIPC hydrogels was due to (i) the well-dispersed SWCNTs in the hydrogel network by means of free radical graft polymerization; (ii) the modified hydrogels by the nano-reinforcement effect of SWCNTs; and (iii) the toughening effect caused by the functionalized SWCNTs. The electro-mechanical response of the hydrogels was studied using a controlled direct current (DC). The deflection response time of the SIPC hydrogels with 0.5 and 1wt% SWCNTs at 10 V were recorded. As the SWCNT content increased, the response time was reduced by over 2 s to reach 55° bending. A faster actuation was achieved by applying a suitable concentration of SWCNT to the SIPC hydrogels. This indicates that the electromechanical properties of the SIPC hydrogel could be enhanced by the proposed SWCNT modification. (2) Effect of redox responsive supramolecular assembly The addition of the host–guest molecules β-CD-AAM and Fc-AAM SIPC exhibited a higher tensile strength of 49 kPa, with an elastic modulus of 36.3 kPa as compared to SIPC without the host-guest molecules. The SIPC with the same CNT content SIPC with host-guest molecules showed higher tensile strength but lower limiting strain. The supramolecular host–guest interaction between the β-CD and Fc moieties served as additional crosslinking sites, thereby enhancing the tensile strength of the nanocomposite but at the same time reducing the limiting strain under tension. The supramolecular ion assembly between the CD and Fc moieties induced a reversible physical crosslinking of non-the monomers due to the covalent host–guest interaction. Moreover, compared with a previously report on Janus bilayer hydrogel actuators, the SIPC hydrogel exhibited an 82% improvement of the elastic modulus. For the electro-mechanical behaviour, when the supramolecular β-CD and Fc moieties were introduced into the hydrogels, the response speed was lowered. This could be attributed to the hardening effect caused by the non-covalent host–guest interaction, which served as the crosslinking sites between the supramolecular moieties within SIPC. The new ideas, knowledge, and findings gave rise to one international conference paper and two journal papers. It could be concluded that the proposed method can be used to prepare the carbon nanotubes modified supramolecular ionic polymer composites with improved mechanical force output.

15207215.label: Major findings and research outcome
15207215.value: The major findings and outcomes are listed below: 1. The material compositions and processing conditions for synthesizing the supramolecular ionic polymer composites with details for preparing β-CD-AAM, and Fc-AAM monomers, vinyl-functionalized carbon nanotubes, CD host composite gels, and Fc guest composite gels. 2. The method to solve the aggregation and surface incompatibility of CNTs when using as nanofillers in polymer composite: Oxidization treatment and vinyl functionalization was developed to overcome these issues. Functionalization with CNTs/host-guest polymer composites and the preparation method demonstrated in this study are environmentally friendly and easy to fabricate on a large scale. 3. The new idea for designing and fabricating bilayer with inhomogeneous structures for electromechanical actuation: Janus bilayer hydrogel actuators with and without CNTs were fabricated by assembling host β-CD and guest Fc hydrogel strips through host-guest interaction. This bilayer actuator showed bending movement in water, which was generated through host-guest interactions between the two hydrogels. Bending behaviour was ascribed to different hydrophilicity of the MWCNTs/host hydrogels and MWCNTs/guest hydrogels. 4. The scheme to prepare single layered supramolecular ionic polymer–carbon nanotube composite (SIPC) hydrogel actuators: Single layered SIPC hydrogel actuators were fabricated via in situ free radical polymerization based on SSNa, β-CD-AAM, and Fc-AAM. Supramolecular ionic polymer composites with different weight fractions of SWCNT were prepared. 5. The findings about effects of carbon nanotube inclusion on SIPC’s mechanical and electro-mechanical performance: The tensile properties of the SWCNT-incorporated SIPC hydrogel were improved over the SWCNT-free hydrogel. The tensile strength of the SIPC hydrogels was effectively regulated without compromising its toughness. For the electro-mechanical performance, quicker actuation response was achieved with the incorporation of SWCNT. 6. The findings about effects of redox responsive supramolecular assembly on SIPC’s mechanical and electro-mechanical performance: The supramolecular host–guest interaction between the β-CD and Fc moieties served as additional crosslinking sites, thereby enhancing the tensile strength of the nanocomposite but reducing the limiting strain under tension. SIPC with host-guest molecules improved the tensile strength but lowered the limiting strain. For the electro-mechanical performance, when the supramolecular β-CD and Fc moieties were introduced into the hydrogels, the response speed was reduced. Referring to Part C of this report, the major findings of Items 1-3 are published in Composites Part B: Engineering and presented in 25th Annual International Conference on Composites and Nano Engineering (ICCE-25) while the rest of them are published in Nanotechnology Reviews.

15207215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15207215.value: An actuator is often designed to carry out specific tasks by satisfying pre-described requirements. 3D printing is one way of realizing such designs. To derive the technologies for printable supramolecular ionic polymer-carbon nanotube actuators is the potential for further development of the research project. With the SIPC, actuators with a new configuration can be designed with two input electrode pairs, an electroactive composite at the middle, and a rigid end effector in a way that mechanical stresses can be minimized. In this connection, a suitable electrode material is required to develop for this design. The electrode material should be highly electroconductive and compatibility with the SIPC. The fatigue strength of the electrode material is also a key concern for the reliability of the actuator under cyclic actuations. The 3D printability of the SIPC is suggested to investigate for the realization of new configurations.

15207215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15207215.value: In this project, a smart material has been developed to produce electroactive polymer actuators for a wide range of potential applications, such as robotics, biomimetics, and aerospace engineering, due to their inherent advantages of lightweight, tunable characteristics, high fracture tolerance, high output displacement and good electromechanical performance. Based on the recent advances in nanocarbon technology, the proposed method can improve the base material to generate better electromechanical performance and produce a new type of electroactive polymer actuator with enhanced features. This study also provides a better understanding of various effects on the electrical and mechanical properties of the nanocomposites, which contributes to future actuator design using this type of nanocomposite.

15208015.label: Project Objectives
15208015.value: To design and synthesize model boron compounds with boronic groups through well controlled reactions of high yields, clarify the contribution of the C-B bond to the boron stability in these compounds against hydrolysis. To apply the stable boron compounds to cellulosic fabrics by mild finishing, investigate the effects of molecular sizes and contents of boron compounds on the FR performance of resultant fabrics through comparative analyses. To improve the washing durability of the above FR finishing with low temperature crosslinking chemistry, investigate the optimal conditions of the cellulose finishing and obtain cost-effective service properties. To identify the burning products of the finished cellulosic fabrics by state-of-art instruments, explore the intrinsic FR mechanism of boron compounds and their possible hazards in fire. To assess the impacts of the optimal FR finishing on environment by life cycle analysis, avoid its adverse effects on sustainability.

15208015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208015.value: Flame retardants (FR’s) are facing a dilemma: more FR’s are demanded because of increasing levels of fire-prevention regulations; at same time, these FR’s are suspected as toxic and not able to meet stricter environmental regulations. As a result, the traditional halogen FR’s have been removed from textile applications in spite of their high efficiency. Currently used phosphorus FR’s also have obvious drawbacks: toxic emissions in fire and low efficiency per unit mass. All these facts are pushing researchers to find more efficient and safer FR’s. Wide range of new materials, such as silica, nano clay and carbon nanotubes, have been explored for the FR application. However, these inorganic materials are not ideal for cellulosic fabrics due to poor durability, impairment of handle and change in color. We propose to explore a new technique to finish cellulosic fabrics with boron compound FR’s, to explore the intrinsic FR mechanism and assess the technique sustainability by a life cycle analysis. Novel boron compounds will be designed and synthesized through solvothermal reactions of high yield. These compounds potentially enable the durable FR finishing of cellulosic fabrics with the lowest mass gain in the literature, which realizes outstanding FR efficiency and retains good service properties of cellulosic fabrics. In addition, these boron finishing systems will be deeply explored in FR mechanism as well as usage safety. This novel FR mechanism is extendable to a variety of boron compounds and applicable to fields beyond textile industry. It can promote the advancement of knowledge in wide areas such as boron polymers, protective textiles and garments, and sustainable FR materials. This research will deliver important information about boron synthesis, crosslink chemistry and FR mechanism, reveal fundamental principles of molecular engineering, green textile finishing and sustainability monitoring technologies. 阻燃劑正面臨一個迷局：它的需求因防火安全的日益嚴格要求而 增長，同時現有的阻燃劑又因為毒性的顧慮而無法滿足嚴格的環 保法規。結果是傳統的鹵素阻燃劑不能再用於紡織領域，儘管它 們的阻燃效率很高。仍在使用的磷系阻燃劑也有明顯的缺點：遇 火釋放有毒氣體，單位質量的阻燃效率較低。所有這些事實都在 推動研究者找出更高效更安全的阻燃劑。好多新材料，例如二氧 化矽，納米粘土和碳納米管，已經包括在阻燃劑的研究範圍。但 是，這些無機材料因為不能提供滿意的耐久性，手感和顏色，不 適用於纖維素織物。 我們計畫開發用於纖維素織物整理的硼系阻燃劑新技術，研究它 內在的阻燃機理並進行全過程分析評估技術的可持續性。將設計 新型硼化合物，並由高產率的溶劑熱反應合成。這些化合物將以 比文獻中更低的使用量達到纖維素織物的耐久阻燃整理，實現卓 越的阻燃效率同時保持纖維素織物較好的服用性能。進而研究這 些硼系阻燃系統的的阻燃機理和使用安全性。這種新型的阻燃機 理可以推廣到更多的硼系化合物以及紡織工業以外的領域。它會 促進硼系聚合物，防護紡織品和服裝，以及綠色阻燃材料的發展 。這項研究將會創造硼系合成，交聯化學和阻燃機理的新知識， 理清分子工程，綠色織物整理和可持續性監管的基本原理。

15208015.label: Realisation of objectives
15208015.value: A series of boron–nitrogen polymers (PEIPAs) were synthesized from 4-bromophenylboronic acid (BPA) and branched polyethylenimine (PEI), to provide a green alternative for flame retardants applicable to cellulosic fabrics. Phenylboronic acid (PA) was successfully linked to the PEI and proved to be stable against hydrolysis, which was confirmed by 1H NMR and FTIR analyses. The polymer with molar ratio 1:1 of ethylenimine:PA (PEIPA 1:1) presented the optimal thermal-oxidative stability in thermogravimetric (TG) analysis. This part of work was published in Cellulose 2018, 25, 843-57. The PA was also linked to (3-aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (ATSi) via a substitute reaction in tetrahydrofuran (THF). The resultant small molecule ATSi-B was converted into organo-silica nanoparticles through a sol-gel reaction in weak alkaline water, where its boronate group was still retained as confirmed by FTIR spectra. This part was summarized in a manuscript too (Efficient Boron-bearing Organosilane Flame Retardants for Cellulosic Fabrics). Additionally, several other small molecules, including azo-boron-BPA (AZA) and ((1E,1’E)‐(sulfonylbis(6-hydroxy-3,1-phenylene)) bis(diazene-2,1-diyl)) bis(3,1-phenylene) diboronic acid (SBDA), were also synthesized and analyzed by NMR and FTIR. A boron-bearing macrocycle molecule (BMC) was synthesized from 4-formylphenylboronic acid, pentaerythritol and tris(2-aminoethyl)amine in ethanol, to explore the effect of molecule size and shape in flame retardancy. Azo-boron grafted graphene oxide (AZOB-RGO) was also synthesized to explore the combinatory effect of boronic acid and graphene. These boron compounds were insoluble in water, so applied to a synthetic biopolymer (PLA) instead of cellulosic fabrics. Thus, the 1st objective was fully achieved. The synthesized PEIPA 1:1 was easily applied on cotton fabrics through a simple dipping-padding method with high uptake. The fabric with 33.8 wt% add-on got self-extinguishing ability. SEM observation revealed the bubble char morphology of the treated fabrics, indicating a intumescent flame retardant mechanism. This part of work was published in Cellulose 2018, 25, 843-57. The small molecule ATSi-B was also absorbed into cotton fibers through aqueous padding process, and in-situ converted into organo-silica nanoparticles via alkaline catalysis. The resultant fabric with 26.5 wt% add-on presented self-extinguishing property. This part was summarized in a manuscript (Efficient Boron-bearing Organosilane Flame Retardants for Cellulosic Fabrics). An inorganic salt, hydrated sodium metaborate (SMB), was facilely crystalized inside and on the surface of cotton fabric via one-pot impregnation approach. TG results confirmed the improvement in thermal stability and char yield of cotton fabrics with SMB, which also had a limiting oxygen index (LOI) value of 28.5% with an afterglow time of less than 1 s in the vertical burning test (UL-94 test, V-0). Considerable reductions in peak heat release rate (PHRR ~91.8%), total heat release (THR ~47.2%), peak carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide produced (PCO ~28.6%, PCO2 ~85.5%) were obtained during the cone calorimeter test, supporting SMB as an effective flame retardant for cotton fabrics. This part of work was published in Cellulose, 2019, 26, 4629-40. Thus, the 2nd objective was fully achieved. The washing durability of PEIPA coating on cotton fabric was improved by a formaldehyde-free cross-linking treatment at room temperature (~ 25 oC). This stable coating with 30 wt% add-on achieved LOI values 29.6% and 23.2% before and after 5 launderings. This part of work was published in Cellulose 2018, 25, 843-57. The small molecule ATSi-B was also applied on cotton together with PEIPA via two-step finishing. The resultant fabric reached LOI values 31.2% and 27.6% before and after 20 launderings, and always passed the UL-94 test. This part was prepared into a manuscript (Efficient Boron-bearing Organosilane Flame Retardants for Cellulosic Fabrics). Several other small molecules containing boron were synthesized and applied in PLA modification. The azo-boron-BPA (AZA) was mixed into PLA together with polydopamine (PDA), presented synergistic effect in producing char at high temperature, reaching V-0 rating in UL-94 test and LOI value of 23.7% at 10 wt% loading, giving obvious reduction in PHRR (~19%) and increment in residue (~17.7%). Another synthesized FR, SBDA, was combined with calcium lignosulfonate (Calig) to modify PLA, which led to important reductions in PHRR (~54%), THR (~28.6%) and average effective heat of combustion (AEHC, ~29.4%), also reached the V-0 rating in UL-94 test and LOI value of 28.8%. These works were published in Polym Degrad Stabil 2018, 152, 64-74; Polymers for Advanced Technologies, 2019, 1-14. The boron-based macrocycle molecule (BMC) was synthesized and incorporated into PLA, which reduced its flammability, improved its tensile properties, and enhanced its ultraviolet (UV) blocking. BMC loading of 3 wt% resulted in significant reductions in PHRR (~23%), THR (~37%), CO release (~71%), CO2 release (~26%), and total smoke release (TSR, ~56%), with an LOI value of 30.5% and a V-0 rating in the UL-94 test. It was summarized into a manuscript too (An Efficient Microporus Boron Based Intumescent Macrocycle Flame Retardant for Poly(lactic acid) with Excellent Ultraviolet Protection). Thus, the 3rd objective was fully achieved. The cotton fabric coated with PEIPA was analyzed by TG-IR, showed significant reduction in the flammable volatiles production. Smoke analysis revealed significant decrement in CO2/CO ratio during the burning of treated fabrics, indicating an effective flame inhibition in gas phase. The novel coatings, simple to synthesize and easy to apply with low waste, are suitable alternative to toxic halogenated flame retardants for cellulosic products. This part of work was published in Cellulose 2018, 25, 843-57. The cotton treated with small molecule ATSi-B and PEIPA together presented higher FR efficiency, with obvious reduction of THR (~53%) and CO release (~75%) in cone calorimetry analysis. TG-IR analysis proved significantly reduction in flammable volatiles. This part was involved in a manuscript (Efficient Boron-bearing Organosilane Flame Retardants for Cellulosic Fabrics). The azo-boron grafted graphene oxide (AZOB-RGO) was added into PLA to reduce its toxic release in burning, together with sodium metaborate (SMB) as intercalant. Considerable reductions in pyrolysis products, mainly hydrocarbons, CO, CO2, and carbonyl compounds were observed in TG-IR analysis. Cone calorimeter test demonstrated substantial reductions in PHRR (~76.5%), THR (~76.9%), TSR (~55.6%), PCO (~25.9%) and PCO2 (~78.6%). The FR mechanism of RGO-AZOB/SMB/PLA nanocomposites is based primarily on the glassy charring from the B-OH groups in AZOB and the inherent lamellar blocking by RGO. This work was published in Carbon, 2019, 150, 8-20. Thus, the 4th objective was fully achieved. Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) was applied to our new FRs, PEIPA and ATSi-B, in comparison to the commercial product Pyrovatex CP. Our new FRs consumed less energy during the synthesis and finishing, resulted in less waste and toxic output during finishing and burning. Considering various test standards available and the recent legislation bans, the LCA results were deeply discussed on its limitations and further recommendations. This part was involved in the manuscript (Developing Life Cycle Assessment Model for Flame Retardants and Flame Retardant Polymer Composites). In order to compare the FR efficiency of boron and phosphorus (P) compounds, a few new P compounds were also synthesized and applied to PLA. These works were published in Polymers 2018, 10, 876; Polym Degrad Stabil, 2019, 163, 76-86; Express Polymer Letters, 2019, 13, 8(697-712); J Hazard Mater 2019, 380, 120856. Thus, the 5th objective was fully achieved.

15208015.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208015.value: In this project, a boronic polymer and a boronic silane were synthesized and applied to cotton by solution finishing with a positive result in vertical burning test. These boronic FRs presented intumescent mechanism and evidently higher washing durability than the previously reported boric FRs. They also displayed less impact on environment than the commercial Pyrovates CP in cotton finishing. Additionally, sodium metaborate was proved as an effective FR on cotton. Several newly synthesized boronic compounds showed satisfying FR performance in PLA and allowed the mixture plates reaching V-0 level in vertical burning test. Among them, boronate functionalized graphene presented outstanding FR performance and mechanical enhancement in PLA. A Chinese patent was applied based on our invention on the A durable post-finishing method for flame retardant and smoke inhibition cellulose fabrics with boron and nitrogen organic compounds (ZL201710063336.6, filed: 24-Jan-2017). Based on our well recognized expertise on flame retardant textiles, we were invited to contribute a chapter to the handbook: Flame Retardant Polymeric Materials: A Handbook, Edited by Yuan Hu and Xin Wang. Taylor & Francis, UK, 2019. ISBN: 978-1-13-829579-7. Page 259 out of 338. Totally, this project has produced 9 published papers, 3 manuscripts in submission, 1 patent, 1 book chapter, 8 conference papers, 1 PhD thesis (refer to Section C).

15208015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208015.value: Besides the proposed cellulosic fabric finishing with boronate compounds, they were also applied to biopolymer PLA via melt blending. More functional boronate compounds of special structures will be explored for the modification of biodegradable polymers.

15208015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208015.value: The research project was a study focusing on a new category of efficient and green flame retardants applicable to wearable fabrics, to improve their fire safety and reduce their environmental impacts. It involved the synthesis of boronic compounds/polymers/hybrids, fabrication of finished cellulosic fabrics and modified biopolymer PLA, and characterization of their flame retardant properties as well as potential flame retardant mechanisms. A comprehensive analysis was taken to see the correlations between different molecular structures and sizes, pairing additives, processing techniques and the resultant flame retardant performances concerned. The commercial products composed of phosphorus compounds may impart high efficiency of fire suppression to celluloses and biopolymers at the expense of polymer strength with abundant smoke release. These shortages were overcome with our new category of boronic compound flame retardants, which also improved their sustainability in expected industrial applications. This new category of compounds can be applied to improve the fire safety of textiles and biopolymers but not limited to this field.

15208615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208615.value: 高解析度高精度月球地形信息對於月球探測任務和科學研究至關重要。月球地形信息通常是利用立體影像之間的匹配通過攝影測量技術來獲得，然而，由於月球影像缺乏紋理，影像匹配可能無法產生密集可靠的匹配結果。而且，高解析度月球立體影像資源稀少。基於明暗恢復形狀的方法在紋理缺乏的影像上效果最好，它可以利用單幅或多幅影像獲取超高解析度的地形信息，然而，僅利用明暗恢復形狀的方法還難以從月球影像上獲取足夠精確的三維地形信息。因此，將明暗恢復形狀的方法與其他方法（影像匹配）或數據(測距數據)集成起來將能夠獲得既高解析度又高精度的月球地形信息。本項目的研究目標如下： (1) 系統地研究并確定适应月球可变表面反射特性的月球表面反射模型，在此基礎上研發一種適應月球影像線陣式幾何成像的多視影像明暗恢復形狀的方法。 (2) 研發一種集成多視影像明暗恢復形狀與立體影像匹配的新方法，以利用立體影像來實現高解析度高精度的月球地形信息獲取。 (3) 研發一種集成影像明暗恢復形狀與測距數據的新方法，以利用單目影像來實現高解析度高精度的月球地形信息獲取。 (4) 利用中國嫦娥二號影像、美國月球軌道勘察器窄角影像以及測距數據來系統地驗證上述方法，獲取月表有關區域高解析度高精度的地形信息以支持未來的月球探測任務。 本項目的研究成果將有助於行星測繪領域的科技進步。將多種方法協同集成將提供更高質量的月球三維地形信息，這對月球探測和科學研究將具有十分重要的意義。本項目也將促進香港科學家對中國的太空探索計劃的貢獻。

15208615.label: Realisation of objectives
15208615.value: (1) For the first objective, we thoroughly investigated different surface reflection models suitable for 3D reconstruction of the lunar surface, including the Lunar-Lambert model and the Hapke model. The systematic experimental analysis found that the performance of the Hapke model and Lunar-Lambert model on 3D reconstruction of the lunar surface is similar. The Hapke model has a clear physical meaning for each of its parameters. The Lunar-Lambert model is relatively simple and can be regarded as an approximate expression of the Hapke model. We also systematically investigated the typical linear-pushbroom sensors, including the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Narrow Angle Camera (LRO NAC) and the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) Context Camera (CTX). Effective methods for recovering the imaging geometry and calibration of these linear-pushbroom sensors have been developed. The related results can be found in our publications (Wu and Liu, 2017, ISPRS J; Hu and Wu, 2018, PSS; Hu and Wu, 2019, PSS). Based on the Lunar-Lambert model, we developed the framework of the multi-image shape-from-shading (SfS) approach incorporating line-sensor geometry. The multi-image SfS approach uses two co-registered images, acquired under different illumination conditions, to generate high-resolution lunar digital elevation models (DEMs). A novel formulation was developed for multi-image SfS to effectively factor out the effects of albedo variations, leading to more robust performance. Notably, we quantitatively investigated the effects of illumination differences on the performance of 3D reconstruction of the multi-image SfS approach. First, the fundamental process of multi-image SfS was mathematically modelled in order to correlate the numeric solution and illumination differences of the images. Then, based on the mathematical model, an error model was derived to investigate the relationships between the azimuthal and zenith angles of illumination of the images and the reconstruction qualities. The developed multi-image SfS approach and the error model were verified with LRO NAC images. The related result has been presented at international conferences (Wu et al., 2016, XXIII ISPRS Congress; Liu and Wu, 2017; PRSM2017) and published by international journals (Liu and Wu, 2018, ISPRS J; Wu et al., 2018, PSS). (2) For the second objective, in circumstances in which images with favorable stereo configuration are available, we developed an innovative approach for integrating multi-image SfS and stereoscopic image matching for pixel-wise lunar topographic modeling, even for images with significant illumination differences. Dense and reliable image matching is a prerequisite for generating DEMs with favorable geometric accuracy and spatial resolution, while it is a challenging task for lunar surface images especially for those collected under different illumination conditions and with subtle textures. A photoclinometry assisted image matching (PAM) algorithm has been developed to integrate multi-image SfS and image matching. PAM is able to generate surface gradients from the candidate matching patches using photometric stereo reconstruction. Given that correct matches usually generate a reasonable surface while incorrect matches do not, PAM finds matches by evaluating the likelihood that they will generate a reasonable surface. In the process, the PAM algorithm finds matches by evaluating the underlying terrain instead of the direct image intensities. As a result, the differences in image intensity caused by the illumination differences do not significantly influence the matching. The output of PAM is disparity maps that can be directly used to generate DEMs through photogrammetric intersection based on the image interior and exterior orientation parameters. The developed approach has been used for high-resolution topographic mapping at the Chang’E-4 and Chang’E-5 landing sites using LRO NAC images acquired under different illumination conditions. The results indicate that the integrated approach is robust to severe inconsistencies in illumination and subtle textures in cases where the conventional image matching approaches fail. The integrated approach is able to achieve geometric accuracies comparable to photogrammetry while having more small-scale topographic details. The related results can be found in our publications (Liu and Wu, 2018, ISPRS TC III Mid-term Symposium; Liu and Wu, 2020, ISPRS J). (3) For the third objective, in circumstances in which only monocular images are available, we developed a new shape-and-albedo-from-shading (SAfS) method for generating pixel-level high-precision lunar DEMs from monocular images with the constraint of a low-resolution DEM interpolated from the range data. The SAfS method refines a lower-resolution DEM to pixel-level resolution given a monocular image with a known light source. In the meantime, it estimates the corresponding pixel-wise albedo map in the process and based on that to regularize the shape reconstruction. A hierarchical architecture was employed for effective shape reconstruction at multiple resolutions. Moreover, an explicit shadow constraint was developed and incorporated into the SAfS approach to overcome image regions with shadows. Experiment validations were carried out using monocular images from the LRO NAC, with a spatial resolution of 0.5 to 1.5 meters per pixel. The integrated Selenological and Engineering Explorer and LRO Elevation Model (SLDEM), with a spatial resolution of 60 m/pixel, was chosen as the initial DEM. The results indicate that local details are well recovered by the SAfS method with plausible albedo estimation. The related results can be found in our publications (Wu et al., 2016, XXIII ISPRS Congress; Wu et al., 2018, ISPRS J). (4) For the forth objective, we have systematically evaluated the developed methods using images collected by the Chang’E-2, LRO NAC, and other planetary cameras. The results indicate that the developed approaches can generate lunar DEMs of favorable spatial resolution and precision even in situations of illumination inconsistencies and subtle textures of the images, which is superior to the conventional technology of photogrammetry. The developed approaches have been used for high-resolution topographic mapping and analysis to support the Chang’E-4 and Chang’E-5 lunar landing missions. We generated a 1.5-m resolution DTM using the SAfS approach based on a single LRO NAC image, which was the best quality DTM available immediately after landing of Chang’E-4. The high-resolution DTM enabled detailed measurement and analysis of the topographic features (surface hazards, slopes, and occlusions) of the area surrounding the Chang’E-4 lander, which was critical for subsequently carrying out the surface operations of the mission. The developed multi-image SfS approach has also been extensively used for high-resolution topographic mapping at the candidate Chang’E-5 landing site to support surface hazard analysis and estimation of the regolith thickness. The related results can be found in our publications (Li and Wu, 2018, JGR-Planets; Wu et al., 2018, JGR-Planets; Hu and Wu, 2019, ISPRS Annals; Liu and Wu, 2020; ISPRS J).

15208615.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208615.value: (1) A theoretical model for error propagation in the multi-image SfS approach has been developed. Experimental analyses reveal that the resulting error in multi-image SfS depends on both the azimuthal and the zenith angles of illumination as well as the general intensity of the images, and the predictions from the proposed error model are consistent with the actual errors obtained by multi-image SfS using LRO NAC images. The error model enriches the theory of multi-image SfS and is of significance for optimized lunar surface reconstruction based on SfS techniques. The related result can be found in our publications (Liu and Wu, 2017; PRSM2017; Liu and Wu, 2018, ISPRS J). (2) A new shape-and-albedo-from-shading (SAfS) method has been developed, which is able to generate pixel-wise high-precision lunar DEMs from a single image with the constraint of an existing low-resolution DEM. Experiments using high-resolution LRO NAC images indicate that the method is able to recover local topographic details with plausible albedo estimation. This is the first time that the shape-from-shading technique can be practically used for 3D reconstruction of large areas on the lunar surface. The related results can be found in our publications (Wu et al., 2016, XXIII ISPRS Congress; Wu et al., 2018, ISPRS J). (3) A photoclinometry assisted image matching (PAM) algorithm has been developed to integrate multi-image SfS and image matching in photogrammetry for pixel-wise lunar topographic mapping, even for images with significant illumination differences. It can exploit the large volume of lunar surface images with inconsistent illumination conditions for high-resolution topographic mapping, which extends the scope and capability of photogrammetry for its applications in lunar mapping. The developed approach can also be referred for high-resolution topographic mapping of other planetary bodies such as Mercury or asteroids. The related results can be found in our publications (Liu and Wu, 2018, ISPRS TC III Mid-term Symposium; Liu and Wu, 2020, ISPRS J). (4) Invited by the China Academy of Space Technology, we have generated high-resolution and high-precision lunar topographic models for the landing sites of the Chang’E-4 and Chang’E-5 lunar landing missions using the developed methods. These topographic mapping and analysis results have been extensively used in the lunar missions for strategic planning and identifying the landing sites. The related results can be found in our publications (Li and Wu, 2018, JGR-Planets; Wu et al., 2018, JGR-Planets; Liu and Wu, 2020; ISPRS J).

15208615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208615.value: Invited by the China Academy of Space Technology, we are currently working on the topographic mapping and analysis of potential landing sites on the South Pole of the Moon for future Chinese lunar missions. We are further developing an integrated software package with better automation and efficiency based on the developments in this project.

15208615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208615.value: In this project, innovative approaches for high-resolution and high-precision lunar topographic mapping have been developed, including (1) a shape-and-albedo-from-shading (SAfS) approach that is able to generate pixel-wise lunar digital elevation models (DEMs) from a monocular image with the constraint of an existing low-resolution DEM, (2) a multiple-image shape-from-shading (SfS) approach that is more robust for generating high-resolution DEMs by factor out the effects of albedo variations, and (3) an approach to integrate multiple-image SfS and image matching for generating high-resolution DEMs that is robust to illumination inconsistencies and subtle textures of images. The research and developments in this project enrich the theory of SfS and extend the scope and capability of the technologies of SfS and photogrammetry for their applications in lunar mapping. The developments and results from this project have been extensively used in the Chinese Chang’E-4 lunar landing mission, for the detailed topographic mapping and analysis of the Chang’E-4 landing site. The developed approaches can also be referred for high-resolution and high-precision topographic mapping of other planetary bodies such as Mercury or asteroids. The results from this project contribute to the advancement of science and technology in the fields of planetary mapping and scientific research.

15208815.label: Realisation of objectives
15208815.value: In this project, we proposed a new class of Quasi-Cyclic Low-Density Parity-Check (QC-LDPC) block codes, namely Cyclically-Coupled QC-LDPC (CC-QC-LDPC) codes. As the name implied, CC-QC-LDPC codes were formed by coupling a number of QC-LDPC block codes (also called sub-codes) cyclically. In general, these cyclically coupled codes need not be identical but having the same codes could simplify the encoder and decoder designs. We successfully completed Objective #2. We designed a low-complexity CC-QC-LDPC decoder architecture and implemented it onto an FPGA board. The decoder consisted of identical sub-decoders and a global controller Moreover, the sub-decoders were connected in a cyclic way, similar to the coupling among the corresponding sub-codes. The components in each sub-decoder were classified into the following three main categories. 1) The first category included the computational logics (and registers for pipelining) consisting of i) check-node processor (CNP), ii) variable-node processor (VNP), and iii) format converters (2's complement to sign-magnitude (C2S) and its inverse (S2C)). The function of these logics was to update the edge messages between the variable nodes (VNs) and check nodes (CNs). We adopted a layered decoding and we called this category of components a layered decoder. 2) The second category included the random access memories (RAMs) which stored the updated messages and channel messages. Each RAM contained memory locations that could be accessed easily based on their independent addresses. 3) The third category included a switch network that connected the layered decoder and RAMs. The switch network was implemented with multiplexers and controlled by a controller. We completed 80% of Objective #1. We first applied our decoder to a rate-5/6 CC-QC-LDPC code with a length 98,304 bits. 4-bit quantization was used together with 10 decoding iterations. Our decoder could achieve a throughput of 3.0 Gbps. Moreover, at Eb/N0 = 3.50 dB, the CC-QC-LDPC decoder can decode all the 1e16 received bits correctly, suggesting that the error floor might be bounded by 1e-16. We also used the same decoder architecture to decode a rate-4/5 code of length 40,960 bits. The potential application of such a code was in SSD storage. A throughput of 1.47 Gbps was achieved and no error floor was observed above 1e-11. To verify the error floor to be lower than 1e-17, at least 1e18 bits needed to be simulated. With a 3.0 Gbps-throughput decoder, the time taken would have been 1e18/3e9/60/60/24/365 = 10.57 years. To shorten the time by a factor of 20, we reduced the number of decoding iterations to 5 for each codeword and the number of simulated bits to 1e17. With this set of parameters, however, an error floor existed above 1e-15. Shortening the code length introduced a higher error floor and the hardware limitation of the FPGA prohibited us from increasing the throughput substantially. We therefore attempted to re-design the LDPC codes, as described below. We proposed a random-permutation-matrix-based cyclically-coupled LDPC (RP-CC-LDPC) code. We compared its performance with the CC-QC-LDPC code, regular and irregular QC-LDPC codes using FPGA simulations. Results shown that the bit error rate (BER) performance of the RP-CC-LDPC code was comparable to and could possibly exceed that of other codes. However, decoder complexity and throughput were major issues of the RP-CC-LDPC code which made use of relatively more complex random permutation matrices instead of simple circulant permutation matrices. We further proposed a new type of LDPC code called tree-permutation-matrix (TPM)-LDPC code. We introduced TPMs, based on which we defined TPM-LDPC codes. We described simple methods for computing the product and transpose of TPMs. According to these basic characteristics of TPMs, we proposed a systematic way of finding large-girth TPM-LDPC codes based on fast hill-climbing algorithm. Using this method, we could easily obtain a girth-8 TPM-LDPC code with a base matrix of size 4 × 24 and a girth-10 TPM-LDPC code with a base matrix of size 3×10. We shown how RAM access conflicts can be avoided when designing parallel TPM-LDPC decoders. We shown simulation results of three TPM-LDPC codes with different parameters. We also compared the BER results and decoder complexity of the proposed TPM-LPDC codes with other LDPC codes under the same code length and code rate. Simulation results shown that TPM-LDPC codes made use of fewer memory resources and had a higher throughput compared with RP-CC-LDPC codes. Compared with QC-LDPC codes, TPM-LDPC codes required more resources in implementation but could provide a slightly better BER performance under a base-matrix size of 4 × 24 and an expansion factor of z = 4096. In summary, we designed a CC-QC-LDPC code of length 98,304 bits and experimentally verified its error floor to be no larger than 1e-16 under an additive white Gaussian noise channel. Verifying its error floor to be 1e-17 was a big challenge because of the enormous amount of time needed.

15208815.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208815.value: We designed a low-complexity CC-QC-LDPC decoder architecture and implemented it onto an FPGA board. We first applied our decoder to a rate-5/6 CC-QC-LDPC code with a length 98,304 bits. 4-bit quantization was used together with 10 decoding iterations. Our decoder could achieve a throughput of 3.0 Gbps. Moreover, at Eb/N0 = 3.50 dB, the CC-QC-LDPC decoder can decode all the 1e16 received bits correctly. We also used the same decoder architecture to decode a rate-4/5 code of length 40,960 bits. The potential application of such a code was in SSD storage. A throughput of 1.47 Gbps was achieved and no error floor was observed above 1e-11. We proposed a random-permutation-matrix-based cyclically-coupled LDPC (RP-CC-LDPC) code. FPGA simulations results shown that the bit error rate (BER) performance of the RP-CC-LDPC code was comparable to and could possibly exceed that of CC-QC-LDPC code, regular and irregular QC-LDPC codes. However, decoder complexity and throughput were major issues of the RP-CC-LDPC code. We proposed a new type of LDPC code called tree-permutation-matrix (TPM)-LDPC code. We proposed a systematic way of finding large-girth TPM-LDPC codes based on fast hill-climbing algorithm. We shown how RAM access conflicts can be avoided when designing parallel TPM-LDPC decoders. We shown simulation results of three TPM-LDPC codes with different parameters. We also compared the BER results and decoder complexity of the proposed TPM-LPDC codes with other LDPC codes under the same code length and code rate. Simulation results shown that TPM-LDPC codes made use of fewer memory resources and had a higher throughput compared with RP-CC-LDPC codes. Compared with QC-LDPC codes, TPM-LDPC codes required more resources in implementation but could provide a slightly better BER performance under a base-matrix size of 4 × 24 and an expansion factor of z = 4096. We proposed a novel method to evaluate the number of closed paths of different lengths in an all-one base matrix. Theoretical results up to closed paths of length 10 were derived and verified by the exhaustive search method. We investigated the hardware design of a turbo-Hadamard encoder/decoder system. The entire system was implemented on an FPGA board. A bit error rate (BER) of 1e-5 was achieved at Eb/N0 = 0.04 dB with a throughput of 3.2 Gbps or at Eb/N0 = -0.45 dB with a throughput of 1.92 Gbps. One US patent was granted and a number of journal/conference papers were published. The work further attracted the interest of the industry and a collaborative research project with the industry began in 2019.

15208815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208815.value: CC-QC-LDPC codes can be applied to higher-modulation systems in addition to BPSK modulation. For example, they can be applied to optical channels with 16/64/256-QAM modulations. When FPGA boards with higher performance become available, the throughput of the proposed CC-QC-LDPC decoder can be substantially increased. When such opportunities arise, it can be verified if the error floor of the proposed code can reach as low as 1e-17.

15208815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208815.value: Error correction codes are embedded in all digital communication systems (e.g., Wifi, Bluetooth, 3G/4G/5G, Internet of Things, space communications and satellite communications) and data storage systems (e.g., solid state drive, hard disk drives, magnetic storage, USB thumb drives, SD cards). The role of error correction codes is to enhance the reliability of data in such systems, ensuring most received/retrieved being free of errors. This project investigated a new type of error correction codes which aim to significantly enhance the reliability of data. In this project, error correction codes with error probability as low as 1-in-1e16 (i.e., one-in-ten quadrillion) were demonstrated. The codes can be applied in further beyond 5G wireless communication systems and optical networks to improve the reliability of data and also the data transmission speed.

15209015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209015.value: 人們有90%的時間都處於室內環境中，並且長期接觸着住宅內空氣中的各種有毒有害物質。研究發現，室內來源使得室內中空氣中的某些污染物濃度甚至高於其室外水平。作為關鍵室內空氣污染物，PM2.5（空氣動力學直徑小於2.5微米的顆粒物）會對人體健康造成負面影響并對人體肺部造成危害。室內PM2.5既會來源於室內直接排放，也會通過滲透或空氣交換來源於室外。因此，精確檢測評估室內PM2.5水平與其化學組分對於曝露研究是至關重要的。然而傳統評估室內顆粒物水平的方法主要依賴於穩態粉塵採樣或短期空氣採樣。穩態粉塵採樣主要針對的是大顆粒物，並且僅僅反映了其空間分佈特點，強烈地依賴於採樣位置/地點。短期空氣採樣則通常指數分鐘至數小時的空气采样，這種採樣方法採集的空氣總量比較小。不同於以上兩種方式，裝置與便攜式空氣淨化器內的HEPA（高效空氣過濾）濾網可以收集人們長期處於的室內空氣環境中的顆粒物，並提供更加全面綜合的居民住宅内的大氣顆粒物樣品。因此，裝置有HEPA濾網的便攜式空氣淨化器可以作為綜合性PM採樣器以用於室內空氣質量研究。本研究中，我們提出用便攜式空氣淨化器作為PM採樣儀來研究香港/西安/上海/廣州四個城市居民住宅內的顆粒物暴露情況，裝置與便攜式空氣淨化器中的HEPA濾網將會被用於採集長期的室內空氣中的顆粒物。此方法將會首次用以確認評估利用石英/特氟龍濾膜採集大氣顆粒物的傳統方法。此外，我們將通過採集香港/西安/上海/廣州四個城市居民住宅內的空氣樣品并分析PM2.5中目標化學污染物組分來探究此方法的適用性。本研究的最大總體優勢在於提出了一個更為經濟的方式來研究室內空氣顆粒物的暴露情況，尤其是在灰霾天氣、工業突發污染事件或其他特殊天氣情況條件下。

15209015.label: Realisation of objectives
15209015.value: Chemical species analysis for traditional air sampling samples (i.e., filter sampling for airborne particles) is a mature technique and is available in numerous book chapters and research articles. HEPA filter, as a key component of the air cleaner, is similar with filter sampling in the aspect of setup. Identical chemical species analysis techniques could be applied for HEPA filter samples. However, due to the conceptual difference between air cleaner and air sampler, that is the air cleaner is to collect particles to lower the indoor air particulate levels (with large flow rate and clean air delivery rate, hence the amount of particles should be much larger), while air sampler is to quantify the particle levels (with relatively small and known flow rate), it is proved that the commercially available air cleaner (which is not controllable, flow rate may be much less stable than ordinary air sampler) may not be capable to quantify the exposure. To overcome these limits, a self-design operation strategy involving multiple PM sensors deployed at different locations in house, a feedback-based control system, a blower with steady flow rate under known power input, and a HEPA filter was developed in this study. The relationship between particle concentrations at certain distance from the deployed air cleaner and the accumulated airborne particles on HEPA filter could be determined by this setup, therefore the total exposure to PM could be further determined. Trial setup is developed and tested under controlled environment and positive results were obtained. Tests in actual indoor environments will be conducted to further evaluate the utility of the self-designed air cleaner setup. Fundamental distribution and primary source contribution of indoor PM2.5 at residential homes in the four cities have been investigated through a sampling campaign in multiple homes. Mass concentration of PM2.5, particle-bound chemical species including organic carbon (OC), elemental carbon (EC), water soluble ions (WSI), heavy metals, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) were determined. And based on chemical species determination, the contributions from different indoor activities and outdoor penetration, as well as the health effect induced by exposure to PM were further studied. Spatial variation of the contributions from different sources was identified. It was found that PM levels at Xi’an households were significantly higher than those of other cities, and the potential of cancer risk may be considerable even for a relatively short-term exposure. There is a need for improving the indoor air quality for the concern of health and well-being, especially for Xi’an household.

15209015.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209015.value: Major findings: During the first round of sampling campaign, the levels of indoor and outdoor PM2.5 and associated chemical species were identified, the exposure and potential health risk were estimated, and the utility of commercially available air cleaner for exposure study was tested incapability. A general trend of Xi’an > Shanghai > Guangzhou > Hong Kong for indoor PM2.5 levels was identified. Spatial variation of attributions to the indoor PM2.5 levels in winter was identified, 1) Hong Kong: both indoor sources and outdoor penetration as of the highest air exchange, 2) Guangzhou: outdoor penetration dominated, 3) Shanghai: indoor sources dominated as of the highest I/O ratio, and 4) Xi’an: outdoor penetration dominated as of the lowest I/O ratio. High OC/EC ratio and apparent difference between indoor and outdoor OC portion suggesting the presence of OC sources and SOC in indoors. Particle-bound polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) is a good indicators of health effects induced by particulate matters. Primarily, Benzo[a]Pyrene (BaP) equivalent exposure (∑BaPeq) was evaluated for both indoor and outdoor PM2.5 at four cities. Only residences in Hong Kong were found exposed to a particle-bound PAHs level lower than WHO recommended limit of 1 ng m-3, and exposure of Xi’an residents was found much higher than other cities (with both indoor and outdoor exposure higher than Chinese national recommended limit of 10 ng m-3, while all compliant for other cities). Potential lung cancer risk due to exposure to PM2.5-bound PAHs, in the form of Incremental Lifetime Cancer Risk (ILCR) based on an 80%/20% of indoor/outdoor exposure basis, was also assessed for residences at four cities. Considered a life expectancy of 70 years, residents in Hong Kong and Shanghai were found with insignificant risk due to exposure to PM2.5 during winter. For Guangzhou residents, this risk may become considerable (cancer risk over 1E-6) after an exposure duration of about 45 years. As for Xi’an residents, this risk would be considerable even for children if there is no adequate control measure, and the mean ILCR for 70 years exposure duration was estimated to be 1.93E-5. In conclusion, there is a need to improve indoor air quality in the aspect of promoting health and well-being, especially for Xi’an residences. Research outcome: More than ten journal papers have been published, and results have been published in three international conferences (two of them have been attached in the report, and another one is invited keynote talk given by Prof. S.C. Lee at AGU JING Meeting at Xi’an in 2018).

15209015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209015.value: This project focused on the investigation of indoor PM2.5 in multiple residential homes in four Chinese cities with a relatively short duration (normally four days sampling) in order to expand the sample size and to make the sample pools more representative. However, on the other hand, it may not be representative enough to reflect the normal activities of a family. For further development of the research, relatively long-term sampling campaign by utilizing non-interfering equipment shall be proposed, to cover different kinds of indoor activities as much as possible. The trial setup of self-designed air cleaner with controllable running mode, steady flowrate, and multiple sensors feedback will be further tested in actual residential indoor environments under short-term and long-term studies.

15209015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209015.value: This project investigated the indoor air quality related to airborne particles simultaneously in residential homes four Chinese cities, and developed a strategy to utilize air cleaner in estimating human exposure to airborne particles. The indoor PM levels and the associated chemical species were determined. The contributions from different sources and the induced health impact were estimated based on the characterization of indoor PM. The commercially available air cleaners were proved not capable for exposure estimation, thus a strategy of self-design air cleaning apparatus to realize the estimation of exposure was proposed. The results of this study indicate that there is a spatial variation on residential indoor air quality and the influencing factors. There is a need to improve indoor air quality for achieving better health and well-being, and the implementation of improvement could be different due to different living habits and contexts of air pollution. Community exposure through media interview on the topic of indoor air pollution and health has also been promoted by our team.
