15209215.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15209215.value: 基於石墨烯之電容式微加工超聲換能器(CMUT)

15209215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209215.value: Capacitive micromachined ultrasonic transducers (CMUT) have been developed for almost two decades. CMUTs have the advantages of broader bandwidth and higher mechanical coupling efficiency when compared with piezoelectric ultrasonic transducers. However, due to the limitation of membrane materials, the operating frequencies that been reported cover a range only from 300kHz to 70MHz in air while piezoelectric transducers have been demonstrated operating at higher than 500MHz or as low as 10kHz when a horn is used. CMUTs are also known to have lower output pressure because the electrostatic force is limited by the gap distance between two parallel electrodes. The device capacitance is also very low at around a few Pico Farads that is very sensitive to parasitic capacitance. To solve these problems, graphene-based materials is proposed to further improve the performance of CMUTs. Graphene has been found to be the thinnest and strongest material for only one-atom thickness of carbon with honey-comb lattice structure and a Young’s modulus of 1 TP still the same as that of the graphite it was originally exfoliated from. It has been used for making high frequency resonators to reach to more than 100 MHz range. Preliminary study has shown graphene has potential to extend the frequency range of CMUTs to be above 100MHz that can still maintain a large bandwidth. For a thin graphene membrane that is one-atom thickness, it was also found that the quality factor has been dramatically improved. It may be due to the extremely thin membrane’s ability to lower the loss to the membrane support and also to the mechanical deformation. This proposal aims to study the properties of CMUT made by a graphene-based membrane, including the change of resonance frequency and its performance in bandwidth broadening when used for ultrasonic imaging in the high-frequency regime, or for ultrasonic range finding in the low-frequency regime. A process that can be used to batch fabricate graphene-based CMUT is also proposed. The graphene film can be transferred from an already CVD-deposited substrate onto another wafer with the cavity by water-transfer technique. A thick PMMA film can provide a good support during the drying process to prevent the membrane stiction problem. After removing the PMMA film, the graphene membrane can stand on the supporting cavity with strong adhesion from the Van-der-Waals force. When drying in vacuum, the graphene film can also provide impermeability for standard gases to provide vacuum seal of the cavity. 電容式微加工超聲換能器（CMUT）已經發展了近二十年，在與壓電式超聲換能器相比之下，CMUT具有更寬的帶寬以及更高的機械耦合效率的優勢，然而，由於薄膜材料的限制，根據已發表的工作頻率，CMUT在空氣中的頻率範圍只能從300kHz至70MHz，而已展示的壓電式換能器的工作頻率可高達500MHz，加上喇叭之後更可低至10kHz，由於靜電力受到平板電容電極間距所限制，CMUT的輸出聲壓較低，器件本身的電容也低至約幾皮法（pF），因此對寄生電容極為敏感，為了解決這些問題，我們提出使用石墨烯作為薄膜材料，以進一步改善CMUT的性能。 石墨烯是已發現最薄與最強的材料，它僅有一個碳原子厚並具有蜂巢狀的晶格結構，而楊氏模量為1 TPa，仍與剝離出它的石墨相同，它已用於製造超過100 MHz的高頻諧振器，初步研究證明，石墨烯有潛力增加CMUT的頻率範圍至100MHz以上，而仍可保持較大的帶寬，對於具單原子厚度的薄石墨烯膜，也有人發現其品質因數有了明顯的改善，這可能是由於極薄的膜厚可降低來自薄膜支撐以及薄膜機械形變的損失。 本提案的目的在於研究基於石墨烯薄膜所製成CMUT的屬性，包括諧振頻率的變化以及用於高頻超聲成像時其帶寬增加的性能，或在低頻率下用於超聲測距，我們還提出了可用於批量生產石墨烯CMUT的製程，由化學氣相沉積(CVD)生產的石墨烯薄膜，可從其襯底經由水轉移技術轉移到已形成空腔的晶片上，在乾燥過程中，較厚的有機玻璃膜(PMMA)可提供石墨烯膜良好的支撐，以防止薄膜粘滯的問題，除去PMMA膜後，石墨烯薄膜可藉由凡得瓦力(Van-der-Waals force)附著於支撐的空腔上，在真空乾燥時，石墨烯薄膜也對標準氣體具有氣密性，使得腔體能長期保持真空密封。

15209515.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15209515.value: 優化運作資源與碳足跡以實現商業樓宇之可持續發展

15209515.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15209515.value: Dr LEE, Wai-ling Prof YIK, Wai-hung

15209515.label: Project Objectives
15209515.value: To obtain statistics on operating resources consumed by and carbon emissions produced from existing commercial buildings in Hong Kong. To establish an appropriate method for normalising the operating resources and carbon emissions into informative benchmarks for evaluation of the economic and environmental performances of the buildings. To reveal inter-relationships between the various operating resources used and carbon emission levels produced by the buildings. To find out cost efficiency and effectiveness of implementing environmental improvement measures for the buildings. To identify criticality levels of the facilities management factors in optimising resources utilisation and environmental impact of the buildings.
rows: To obtain statistics on operating resources consumed by and carbon emissions produced from existing commercial buildings in Hong Kong.

To establish an appropriate method for normalising the operating resources and carbon emissions into informative benchmarks for evaluation of the economic and environmental performances of the buildings.
To reveal inter-relationships between the various operating resources used and carbon emission levels produced by the buildings.
To find out cost efficiency and effectiveness of implementing environmental improvement measures for the buildings.
To identify criticality levels of the facilities management factors in optimising resources utilisation and environmental impact of the buildings.

15209515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209515.value: Central to the global warming problem are the continuously increasing emissions of greenhouse gases (GHGs) such as carbon dioxide, methane etc., especially those associated with the operation of buildings. Over the years, some studies have used simulation/modelling methods to estimate the quantities of GHG emissions (commonly known as ‘carbon emissions’) from buildings while others took an empirical approach to study the emissions. Recently the Investigators completed a pilot carbon audit study on a hotel and a comparative study of the carbon emissions produced by two other hotels, which included investigation into the parameters that affect carbon footprints. Founded upon this groundwork and a carbon footprint assessment (CFA) program that the Investigators have developed, a three-stage comprehensive study, which aims at understanding how to achieve an optimum balance between the operating resources (e.g. energy, manpower) and the carbon footprints of existing commercial buildings in Hong Kong, is proposed. In Stage 1, commercial buildings in which environmental improvement measures have been implemented will be selected with the support of leading organizations of those professionals who manage the operation of numerous existing buildings. The data required for determining carbon emissions from these buildings, to be collected through a self-administered survey, will be processed by the CFA program. In addition to processing the carbon emissions and relevant resources data by categorical and statistical analyses, regression and sensitivity analyses will be carried out to identify suitable factors and an appropriate method for normalising the carbon emissions into informative benchmarks. In Stage 2, the buildings studied in Stage 1 will be classified by their carbon emission levels into three tiers, and a pair of buildings from each tier will be studied using an interpretivist approach. Detailed operational data and physical building parameters will be analysed using correlation and regression analyses to investigate their inter-relationships. Input resources and carbon emissions before and after the implementation of improvement measures will also be computed to identify indicators reflecting their economic and environmental effectiveness. In Stage 3, a focus group comprising representatives of each tier of the buildings will be formed to discuss the practices adopted in managing their buildings’ facilities. Critical facilities management factors, which will be identified and rated by the focus group participants, will be analysed using the analytic hierarchy process to yield importance weights representing the criticality levels of factors involved in optimising operating resources and carbon footprints of commercial buildings.

15209515.label: Realisation of objectives
15209515.value: Following on the literature review completed in preparing the study proposal before, further effort was made to search and review any relevant literature so as to check for any new information that is related to the study. The review found that for commercial buildings, their energy use had been widely studied but research on their carbon emissions had not been common. Moreover, more empirical research using operational data of existing buildings should be carried out in order to obtain real and definite findings. To obtain empirical data of the target buildings, a survey was designed and pilot-tested in the beginning stage of the current study. The finalised survey was distributed with facilitation given by the supporting organisations, including the Building Services Operation and Maintenance Executives Society (BSOMES), the Greater China Institute of Property Management (GCIPM) and the Hong Kong Institute of Facility Management (HKIFM). Based on the survey data, statistics on the improvement works implemented in the sampled buildings were worked out. In addition, the survey respondents were asked to indicate if they would like to participate in a further part of the study where the carbon emissions of their buildings are audited and analysed in detail. After the survey, the study team contacted those who had indicated their interest in joining the carbon audit. To investigate the carbon emissions of their buildings and changes in the emissions associated with any improvement works implemented, the needed data were collected. For this purpose, a meeting was held during which the study team explained to each participant the data needed for the audit. A set of electronic templates, which was devised for collecting the data, was provided to the participants. Quantitative data that can be retrieved from building records (e.g. annual data on input resources, utilities consumptions and operation and maintenance costs) were collected. Following the precautions taken in an earlier carbon audit study, the Investigators tested and verified the validity of the data collected by cross verification of the data from multiple sources (e.g. questionnaires returned, documentary data records, utility bills). Data of 32 buildings were collected and they were processed to give statistics of the operating resources and carbon emissions of the buildings [i.e. Objective 1]. The data needed for calculating carbon emissions under scopes 1 to 3 of the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Protocol were processed by computer software. The calculated emissions together with the relevant cost data were processed by categorical analyses, followed by statistical analyses similar to those the PI made in an earlier study to produce benchmark values (e.g. mean, percentiles). Because a variety of factors such as building area may be used for normalisation purposes, a series of analyses were carried out based on the PI’s experience in an earlier study to identify suitable factors as well as an appropriate method for normalising the operating resources and carbon emissions into informative benchmarks [i.e. Objective 2]. Particularly, the data analysis revealed that carbon emission level is more significantly correlated with total floor area than age or common floor area of the buildings. Based on the above findings, the buildings studied were classified by their carbon emission levels into three groups – low, medium, and high. For each group, a pair of buildings with the largest difference in operating cost levels were selected for detailed case studies. This interpretivist approach enables pair-wise comparisons to be made between peer buildings and hence identification of the factors that give rise to different levels of input resources for the buildings. In order to enable analysis of the effects of variation on the characteristics of and resources input to the buildings, monthly data covering the following aspects were collected: physical characteristics; characteristics of building facilities; operational characteristics; information on the monetary values of the buildings; human and work resources input; energy utilisation; recurrent resources other than the preceding aspects; and indoor environmental quality. A template was tailored to collect the above data. Considering the high level of detail needed and to ensure collection of reliable data, face-to-face interviews with the relevant building managers were conducted, during which the Investigators explained the types and extent of the data needed. Monthly data over a period of six years of the buildings were collected. The carbon emission levels computed based on these data sets were charted to reveal their year-on-year variations and seasonal fluctuations. The emission levels were then grouped into different categories, for instance according to the above-mentioned physical characteristics of the buildings, followed by correlation and regression analyses with respect to different parameters of the buildings. The results inform the inter-relationships between various operating resources and the carbon emissions of the buildings [i.e. Objective 3]. In particular, the finding that small buildings generally produced more carbon emissions than the large ones is important information for policy-makers and facility managers in prioritising environmental conversation measures for implementation in existing buildings. In addition, the buildings’ levels of input resources and carbon emissions before and after implementation of the environmental improvement works were further computed. This, in turn, yielded performance indicators, including cost-benefit ratio and carbon reduction efficiency that can reflect the effectiveness of the work undertaken towards sustainability of the buildings [i.e. Objective 4]. In a particular case study that evaluates the retrofit adopted for the air-conditioning system of a commercial building, the economic performance of the retrofit was evaluated by analysing its net present value and return on investment, and an indicator known as ‘carbon reduction efficiency’ was introduced to assess the environmental-cum-economic performance of the retrofit. That case study illustrated a rigorous, pragmatic approach to evaluating retrofit projects in real-world buildings. In order to investigate factors that determine the level of environmental impact of the buildings, samples were selected from each of the three building tiers (‘low’, ‘medium’ and ‘high’ as identified above) for further in-depth study in the final stage of the study. For this purpose, focus group meetings were held involving representatives of each building tier in order to have fruitful discussions. The Investigators acted as facilitators for the meetings and the participants shared the good practices adopted, and difficulties encountered in implementing environmental improvement measures, as well as the problems they managed to overcome in optimising resources utilisations and carbon emissions. With reference to the analysis methods adopted in relevant past studies and the experience of the study team in analysing information gathered from focus group discussions, the critical factors in facility management (FM) practice that are influential to attaining an optimum balance between the operating resources and carbon emissions of the commercial buildings were identified. The focus group participants were then guided to take part in a further round of discussion, based on their expert opinions, to indicate the levels of relative importance of the identified factors. Using an analytical method similar to that developed by the Investigators for evaluation of FM services before, the perceived importance levels of the factors were processed to yield their importance weights, based on which their criticality levels were determined [i.e. Objective 5].

15209515.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209515.value: Under the study, an extensive literature review was done. It revealed that for commercial buildings, their carbon emissions had not been studied as widely as their energy use. Despite the wide range of efforts made, the growth of carbon emission remains a live issue, to which commercial buildings are among the major contributors. A major conclusion drawn from the outcome of the review is that rather than simulation studies, more empirical research using operational data of existing buildings should be carried out in order to obtain real and definite findings. Detailed data of 32 commercial buildings in Hong Kong were studied. Analysing the data revealed that carbon emission level is more significantly correlated with total floor area than age or common floor area of the buildings. Benchmarking charts, constructed based on the buildings’ normalized carbon emission levels, enable comparisons to be made between the environmental performances of peer buildings in different ranges of age and scale. The finding that small buildings generally produced more carbon emissions than the large ones is important information for policy-makers and facility managers in prioritizing environmental conversation measures for implementation in existing buildings. Many studies have been pursued to evaluate the economic or environmental effectiveness of energy/environmental saving measures; however, the reliability of their results are often uncertain due to the dearth of real data. A case study was conducted to evaluate the retrofit adopted for the air-conditioning system of a commercial building. Using longitudinal energy and cost data of the system, the economic performance of the retrofit was evaluated by analysing its net present value and return on investment, and a novel indicator known as ‘carbon reduction efficiency’ was used to assess the environmental-cum-economic performance of the retrofit. Providing empirical evidence of economic or environmental effectiveness of energy/environmental saving measures, the case study illustrated a rigorous, pragmatic approach to evaluating retrofit projects in real-world buildings. Focus group meetings were held among the representatives of the sampled buildings to discuss the environmental matters of commercial buildings. Found from such meetings include the good facility management (FM) practices adopted, difficulties encountered in implementing environmental improvement measures, and the problems the participants managed to overcome in optimising resources utilisations and carbon emissions. Analysing the focus group findings resulted in the identification of the critical FM factors and their criticality levels towards an optimum balance between the operating resources and carbon emissions of the commercial buildings.

15209515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209515.value: The project found that among the buildings studied, the large buildings produced less carbon emissions per unit floor area than the smaller ones. On this basis, small buildings should be given priority when policy-makers such as authorities and building owners implement environmental conversation measures in future. Following the methodology of this project, further research can be conducted to cover more samples of existing commercial buildings and more types of carbon-intensive buildings (e.g. hospitals). Effects of building characteristics (e.g. building volume) on carbon emissions should also be studied. When more findings of this kind are made available, governments and stakeholders alike will be abler to evaluate the environmental performance of existing buildings. Further to showing how a combined use of indicators (net present value and return on investment) can be taken to evaluate the economic performance of retrofits, a novel indicator known as ‘carbon reduction efficiency’ was introduced for use in evaluating both the environmental and economic performances of retrofits in an integrated manner. Further research can follow this approach to study the environmental-cum-economic performance of building retrofits. More research findings of this kind will be useful for prioritizing energy/environmental saving measures for adoption in buildings.

15209515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209515.value: Commercial buildings, which continue to produce carbon emission, are among the major contributors to the global warming problem. But holistic field investigations into the carbon footprints of commercial buildings and the effectiveness of environmental improvement measures actually taken remain rare. To fill the above knowledge gap, the current project, which is an applied research study that probes into the real-world data, was conducted. In establishing benchmarks for evaluation of the economic and environmental performances of commercial buildings, an appropriate method for normalising the resources used and emissions made was identified. Besides examining the relationships between the resources consumed in commercial buildings and the resulting carbon emissions, the study illustrated a pragmatic approach to evaluating whether, and to what degree, improvement measures adopted for the buildings are effective. Through making investigations on the facility management practices for commercial buildings, factors that are critical to the volumes of operating resources and carbon footprints of the buildings were identified. The outcomes of the project, including the methodology, analysis process and study results provide a good reference for further research locally and elsewhere. This, in turn, will have significant and long-term impacts on the sustainability of commercial buildings across the world.

15209615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209615.value: Electrospark deposition (ESD) can be considered as a pulse arc “micro-welding” process that provides an intense short duration heat input between a lightly contacted consumable electrode and the workpiece substrate. ESD can fabricate metallurgically bonded protective coatings on a wide range of different substrate materials; moreover, due to the extremely rapid cooling characteristic of the process, coatings are normally comprised of nano-structures and homogenous phases, and because of this, good corrosion and tribological properties are obtained. Due to these advantages and the relatively low cost operation, ESD has aroused much research interest in the last decade, in a variety of surface engineering applications in the aeronautical, nuclear, military engineering fields, and in medical industries. About ten years ago, the U.S. Department of Defence sponsored some targeted research programmes to establish ESD as a technically and commercially viable surface coating process for repairing damaged weapons systems components, as well as for gas turbine engines, vehicles and ship components. Notwithstanding the advances that have been made by this research effort, similar to other coating methods, ESD has its limitations. One of these is its difficulty in treating surfaces with intricate profiles. Another difficult-to-solve problem is process instability, which occurs as a result of unstable electrospark discharging. This is largely due to irregular contact conditions between the electrode and the workpiece. With the aim of addressing these two drawbacks, a new ESD method, which employs a magnetised electrode to which fine powder is attracted, is put forward in this proposal (the new process is illustrated in Fig. 1). In this new concept, the electrode tip can be regarded as a “fluidised” deposition head with magnetised coating powders. Now, with the powder assembled head acting like a soft brush, surfaces with complex geometries can be readily coated. Moreover, in this new process, the spark discharge location and the contact condition are no longer dictated by the irregular surface asperities and the applied contact force, but instead, “soft” contacts, which are self-regulating, are established between the magnetised coating powders and the workpiece surface. To prepare for this proposal, a preliminary study on spark stability of the new process has been undertaken, and encouraging initial results have been obtained. This was a small first step towards understanding the discharge behaviour of the process, and much more work, both experimental and theoretical is needed in order to realise the full potential of this new process. 電火花沉積被認為是一種脈衝電弧微焊接過程。其加工過程中，微接觸的工具電極和工件之間產生的暫態熱效應使得工具電極自熔，從而在多種工件基材的表面形成冶金結合的保護性塗層。此外由於電火花沉積過程還具有極速冷卻的特徵，因此沉積的塗層通常具有均勻的納米結構，這使得塗層具有優良的耐腐蝕性能及摩檫學性能。 電火花沉積不僅具有以上的優點而且其加工成本低廉，因此該工藝過程在近年來引起了與航空航太、原子能、軍事工程以及醫療器械等相關的表面工程應用研究領域的關注。 為將電火花沉積成功應用於修復武器系統、渦輪發動機、車輛以及艦船，約十年前美國國防部定向資助了一些相關的研究課題，取得了一定的成效。 然而，與其它的表面塗層工藝一樣，電火花沉積工藝也存在著一些明顯的不足之處，這主要是由於加工過程中工具電極與工件間接觸是不規則的，這一方面導致了該工藝難以用於沉積複雜形狀的表面；另一方面導致了該工藝過程具有極大的不穩定性。為解決這兩大問題，本專案提出了一種新的電火花沉積方法，該方法採用磁性電極吸附微小的磁粉，電極端部吸附的磁粉可看做一種流態化的沉積工具，在加工過程中磁粉具備了像柔軟的刷子一樣的功能和特徵，因此新方法能非常適合於沉積具有複雜形狀的表面，更重要的是，在新方法的沉積過程中，由於磁粉及工件之間具有柔性接觸及自適應調整的特徵，因此火花放電的位置以及工具與工件的接觸狀況將不再像傳統的電火花沉積過程那樣需要受制於工具與工件間不規則的表面特徵及接觸力。本項目申請的相關預實驗結果表明，新方法能獲得極高的加工穩定性，這初步證明了新方法的有效性，然而新方法加工潛能的發揮及其放電機理的揭示則需要在理論及實驗上進行更為深入的研究。

15209815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209815.value: 幾千年的傳統觀念認為，羊毛纖維僅僅是具有優良彈性和保暖性能的紡織材料。直到最近，我們發現羊毛纖維是具有形狀記憶和自修復功能的智能材料，它能夠對熱、水、還原劑和紫外線具有形狀記憶響應。羊毛纖維的這種智能特性是由於其大分子之間及內部具有結晶、二硫鍵和氫鍵。這三種結構成分可以形成雙節點-雙開關結構模型。這種自然界的智能結構特性可以被系統的研究，然後用於開發智能合成材料。另外，多重響應的形狀記憶聚合物需求不斷升級，而目前報導的聚合物材料最多具有三重形狀記憶效應。 基於羊毛雙節點-雙開關的結構模型，本項目的研究目的是發明一種具有四重響應和自修復功能的形狀記憶聚氨酯材料（SMPU）。這類材料和羊毛一樣也能對水、熱、還原劑和紫外線產生形狀記憶響應。 這種SMPU的發明可以彌補應用需求和目前技術之間的差距，同時也為開發其他智能材料提供模型參照。 在本項目中，系統的研究羊毛的結構和其智能性顯得十分必要，這樣將會從分子層面上有效的設計這種新型SMPU。因此我們將會設計化學和物理交聯及二硫鍵的雙節點及二硫鍵和氫鍵的雙開關。氫鍵是由聚氨酯中吡啶環裡的氨酯基間形成，二硫鍵是由大分子間1，5戊二醇-3-巰基形成。本項目中，共混線性物理交聯的SMPU將會製作纖維，氧化生成的二硫鍵用作開關，而化學交聯的SMPU將會製成膜材料。在研究中，傅立葉紅外光譜將表徵氫鍵，拉曼光譜表徵二硫鍵，動態熱分析儀和X射線衍射儀表徵SMPU和羊毛的結晶，動態機械分析儀和萬能機用來分析形狀固定率和恢復率。SMPU的自修復性能將由微裂紋修復效率來探索二硫鍵在其中的作用。

15209815.label: Realisation of objectives
15209815.value: 1. The stress-memory behavior of animal hairs including wools and camel hairs have been investigated and a mechanism model was established. The relevant experiments were conducted and the role of HBs as well as DBs have also been studied, where the energy contribution of bonds in natural materials has been confirmed. Besides, we investigated the feasibility of wools in performing actuating ability through its intrinsic structures and fabrication methods. The diverse modes of contractive forces were obtained in wool materials, including platform-like, double-peak, and slope-like shapes, where a molecular model was also presented to trace the origins of stress evolution. After that, a polymeric blend was created to modify the wool materials and a dissimilar performance of stress production was achieved, a square stress mode with stable manners and maintenances, for broad applications in a more efficient way. It is believed that these actuating properties extracted from natural hairs have a large potential in current smart applications and lay down inspirations in designing actuators. 2. A wool-inspired crosslinked shape memory polyurethane(SMPU), a muscle-like stress-memory material, with controllable DB as a switch in the molecular structure on exposure to Redox was fabricated. Unlike existing artificial muscles, the driving force in this material is mainly from enthalpy change but not entropy elasticity, and the stimulus is pure chemical conditions modulated by Redox, muscles normally live within, but not electricity/heat. The realization of stress memory for muscle isometric contraction is introduced. Besides, HBs as switches incorporated into a PU architecture were also synthesized and relative experiments have been conducted. 3. This redox-responsive material with reversible stress mimics not only the generation of a reversible force but also Redox environment and the specific role of disulfide bond (DB) in real muscles, which could not be found in other artificial muscle materials. The discovery from this work will inspire exploration of the DBs in protein-based materials as well as biological systems and more fascinating smart function of artificial muscles. It is expected that this study could not only extend the boundary of traditional study on reversible movements of artificial muscle but also lead to novel materials with unparalleled characteristics in both robotic and artificial intelligence applications.

15209815.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209815.value: 1. The stimuli-responsible properties of animal hairs have been investigated. It was proved that this kind of natural hair is sensitive to heat, water, and redox. For a water-triggered sample, only one kind of switch exists controlling the memory effect, that is, hydrogen bond. For the reductant-triggered sample, the roles of water and reductant work at the same time in which both HBs and DBs change according to environmental variation. For thermal stimulation, the fabricated structures have a large effect on stimulating behaviors. The successful verification of stress memory in natural hair strengthens our theory and confidence in exploring the smart mechanical functions in numerous natural protein-based materials. It reflects the smart behaviors of biological materials, including natural fibers, and can be applied as enthalpy-driven energy storage for artificial muscles. Meanwhile, it sheds lights on the functions of DBs in biological systems. (Shanshan Zhu and Jinlian Hu*, Multi-Modal Contractive Forces of Wools as Actuator,Polymers, under review) 2. A newly designed cross-linked SMPU with controllable DBs as switches in molecular structures proved the stress storage behavior on exposure to Redox. With increased weight percentage of DBs in materials, the enthalpy change during the transition will also increase, resulting in significant memory stress. The value of memory stress can reach 47% of its original tension stress with 20% DB content, highlighting the capability of this dynamic bond. These Redox-responsive stress release-storage properties and the function of DB are similar to that of titin, which is the key in charge of the passive elasticity of muscle. This work successfully demonstrated the contribution of DBs to stress-memory ability in isometric contraction. (Shanshan Zhu, Jinlian Hu*, A Titin Inspired Stress-Memory Polymer Acts as Muscle, Materials Chemistry Frontiers, 2019, DOI: 10.1039/C9QM00453J) 3. The synthesized single polymer artificial muscle (SPAM) inspired by the crystalline regions in wool structurers and mimicking real muscle structures was proved to have abilities in dual-mode contractions through enthalpy-battery, where spring structure is used as titin and semi-crystal structure as actin. Due to the high sensitivity of crystal phase to temperature, sensing ability to external conditions are reported and energy source from enthalpy change are unprecedentedly explored. Trainability of SPAM was proved by structure evolution of crystal phase through XRD and DSC analysis and the contraction ability were demonstrated to result from selective preloaded and stimulated conditions. (Shanshan Zhu, Jinlian Hu*, Yuanchi Zhang, A Single Polymer Artificial Muscle Having Dual-Mode Contractibility, Temperature Sensibility and Trainability through Enthalpy-Change, Advanced Materials Technologies (2019): 1900017.)

15209815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209815.value: 1. Investigate the potential application of SMP with DBs as switches in biomedical areas. SMPU with DB as switches was proved to act as a muscle in isometric contraction. It mimics not only generation of a reversible force, but also Redox environment and specific role of disulfide bond (DB) in real muscles, which could not be found in other artificial muscle materials. Based on this result, further explore the shape memory effect and isotonic contraction of this material are other good options to improve the overall functions and broaden its applications in biomedical environment, where redox can always be found. At the same time, comprehensive mechanism can be produced according to all-around assessment of SMPU-DB. 2. Improvement of understanding in natural muscles, exploration of natural materials to produce ideal artificial muscles, and broaden the application to intelligent wearable devices. Many fantastic characters of natural muscles have not been explored and the information of corresponding structures has not been unveiled neither. Many natural materials especially plants possess smart functions from innate talents, such as remarkable SME of peacock's tail and reversible movements in mimosa pulvinus. They are sensitive towards temperature, moisture, UV, etc. that proves special structures or bonds inside. Consequently, if natural materials can be explored to be used as artificial muscle, results will be sustainable as well as environmentally-friendly. In the meantime, no matter the natural artificial muscles or the polymeric ones, exploration of their application in smart textile areas especially the intelligent wearable devices would be what we are really after.

15209815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209815.value: For thousands of years, wool has been traditionally considered merely as a natural fiber for textiles for excellent elasticity and thermal insulation. Through our work, wool is discovered to be a very smart material, displaying shape memory effects responsive to heat, water, redox agents and UV-light. These smart functions of wool are due to its three structural components: crystals, hydrogen (HB) and disulfide (DB) bonds among its intra- and inter-macromolecules, thus a twin-switch model is developed. Based on our understanding of wool structure and their smart behavior, we have synthesized wool-inspired shape memory polyurethane (SMPUs). In addition to shape memory, SMPUs with DBs as switches are also found to have stress memory which validates the fundamental platform for materials development in energy, smart devices, artificial muscles, biological and physical massage systems with polymers and beyond. Due to the enthalpy of wool inspired SMPUs change, stress memory is found to be a very useful property for artificial muscles. Unlike existing ones which only provide isotonic contraction, artificial muscles made from wool-inspired SMPUS can provide both isometric (generate force without changing the length of muscle) and isotonic contractions (generate force by changing the length of muscle).

15210515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210515.value: Although optical microscopy is a mature field with many important ideas developed and understood in the 19th Century, it has been an area with burgeoning and exciting developments in the past two decades. As biologists require information on ever finer scales new methods have been developed to look at smaller features than was considered practical even in the recent past. It is interesting that the Nobel prize for Chemistry in 2008 and 2014 was awarded for developments in microscopy. Novel optical microscopy is thus topical and important and plays a key role in experiments for real world applications and research. The present proposal looks at new and practical ways to improve the performance of microscope systems. It develops new surface structures that can be easily incorporated into existing microscopes. These can ensure that we look at very confined regions flare from background light, this will enable us to examine cell membranes rapidly on very fine scale. Cell membranes are particularly important as they are the gatekeepers between the cell and the outside world and thus play a unique role in cell signaling and the development and organization of structures in organisms. In addition to this our methods will allow biologists to look at the dynamics of molecules to gain more detailed information about the local interactions. Despite all the wonderful developments in microscopy over the last few years there are still some serious limitations. The most pressing of these is that looking at living tissue comes at a cost in terms of damage. The two techniques that won the Nobel prize in recent years rely on fluorescence, where light excites a molecule which stores the energy for a short time before giving back the light at a different wavelength (colour), Fluorescence is a crucial and vital technique to either get enhanced resolution or probe the inner workings of the cell. We will use fluorescent methods in this proposal but not exclusively. When fluorophores are excited they become chemically active which over time can poison cells reducing their viability, altering their behaviour and often killing them. We will therefore also examine label free methods which look at direct scattering without the addition of extra chemicals, these will be far kinder and allow long term monitoring of cells. N/A

15210815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210815.value: Hong Kong is becoming an ageing society. The World Health Organization has forecasted that, by 2050, 40% of the population of Hong Kong will be aged 65 or above, and will be fifth-ranked among the cities with the largest proportion of elderly persons in the world. The rapidly ageing population is leading to the strictly increasing age dependency ratio of the population in Hong Kong from 1/10 in the early 1980s, to 1/5 in 2010, to 1/3 in 2021 and to 1/2 in 2041 (Demographic Statistics Section, Census and Statistics Department, 2012). With an increase in the elderly numbers and a shrinking working population, reduction in the number of taxpayers and reduced economic growth, the local public healthcare system is currently encountering a problem in that the health expenditure is growing at a much faster rate than the economic growth (Food and Health Bureau, 2008a). The public healthcare system is experiencing pressure on resources and overloading of the clinical staff. Over the years, despite the ever-increasing healthcare expenditure, the service supply has been always in short supply. According to the Food and Health Bureau (2008b), over 90% of the in-patient services are provided by public hospitals. Also, the elderly population has a much greater demand on healthcare service than the younger population (Food and Health Bureau, 2010).The demand for public healthcare services is increasingly under pressure associated with the ageing population. Given the continuous huge demand of nursing needs and the shortage of clinical staff, the nurse-patient ratio in Hong Kong is far below the international standard of 1:4-6 for the nurse-patient ratio to ensure sufficiency of clinical staff. Although the government has devoted increasing resources to support the recruitment of new clinical staff and has adopted other measures for improving the high turnover of staff, the figures from the Association of Hong Kong Nursing Staff reflects that the number of newly employed nurses is insufficient to fill the vacancies, and cannot meet the projected increasing needs of healthcare services associated with the ageing population. The long-term goal of the proposed research is to develop a model for clinical staff level planning, so as to provide a basis for the local subvented nursing homes to estimate the manpower required to fulfill the service needs while at the same time enhance the flexibility of recruitment and maintain a reasonable staff-patient ratio for the benefit of both residents and clinical staff. 香港現正面對人均壽命延長(人口老齡化)的問題。生育率持續下降，但人均壽命延長，導致長者比例增加，並造成人口結構上的轉變。世界衛生組織預計在2050年，香港將有百分之四十的總人口為65歲或以上的長者。而社區人口迅速老齡化更導致香港人口的老年撫養比率 （65歲及以上人口數目與每千名15至64歲人口的相對比率）由20世紀80年代初期的1/10大幅上升至2010年的1/5。然而，世衛預計此比率在 2021 年將攀升至 1/3，在2041 年甚至將會達到1/2。 社區人口老化為醫療系統帶來重大的挑戰，包括（一）滿足與日俱增的長者醫療服務需求；（二）確保服務質素及安全；及（三）維持足夠具備長者護理技能的工作團隊。 隨著長者數目日增，醫療服務需求因而大增。同時，人口老齡化及就業人口下降為社區及醫療系統帶來了經濟衝擊。本港醫療成本不斷上漲，醫療開支的升幅亦遠高於經濟增長速度。人口老化不但導致醫療服務需求急升，社會對醫療服務質素和安全的期望亦不斷提高。另一方面，公立醫院過去幾年一直面對護士人手不足及護士流失率高企的問題，令前線護理人員面對沉重的工作壓力。而多年來，儘管當局不斷推行新措施以紓解護士壓力及增加服務量，但公立醫療服務供應仍然供不應求， 供求失衡的情況更可能隨著人口老齡化愈趨惡化。 由於醫護人員的短缺和長者醫療服務需求的不斷增加，香港公營醫療體系的平均護士病人比例極不理想，更遠低於國際的護士病人比例標準(1:4-6)，因而無法確保病人得到護理人員的充分照顧。雖然政府已經投入了愈來愈多資源以支持招聘新的護理人員，及採取了其他措施以改善公營體系中護理人力資源問題，但根據香港護士協會的人力資源調查顯示，新聘用護士的數量根本不足以填補人手空缺，更不能滿足醫療服務與老齡化相關的預期需求增長。 因應人口老齡化及安老院舍照顧服務需求增加，各界需要就未來的服務模式提出建議，以加強長者醫療服務的質素和成效。當中，加強人力資源及培訓為其中一項最重要的策略以應付未來的資源需要。 本研究旨在建立一個模型，因應人口老化的影響和長者醫療服務的需求預測進行及改善前線護理人員的人力規劃，為本地資助護養院提供一個基礎，以評估滿足院舍護理服務需求所需的人力，維持合理的護理人員與院友比例。同時，該模型亦用於提升聘用模式的彈性，以吸引新血投身護理行業、挽留護士於公共醫療系統工作，及吸引資歷較深的已離職護士回流，用以紓緩護士人手不足的困境及減低中層護士的工作壓力。

15210815.label: Realisation of objectives
15210815.value: The project was successfully completed, with all the objectives achieved. In which: 1. Systematic literature searches and reviews were conducted to identify the key problems associated with the healthcare resources allocation. At the same time, data from a subvented nursing home in Hong Kong was collected and analyzed. 2. A mixed-integer based optimization model was formulated to deal with the nursing workforce demand modelling problem identified in (1). Aiming at balancing the workload of staff, increasing the flexibility of staff-task assignment and the flexibility of employment terms, as in (3), these factors are taken into consideration in the proposed model either in the objective function or constraints. 3. From the literature study and the feasibility study, it is found that the problem being studied is a Nondeterministic Polynomial Time Complete (NP-complete) problem that cannot be solved by exact algorithms easily in polynomial time. Heuristics was therefore applied to solve the proposed model. Results showed that heuristics can solve the proposed model with reduced staffing costs while enhancing the staff-task flexibility and better sharing the workload among nursing staff.

15210815.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210815.value: A mixed-integer based optimization model for nursing workforce demand projection was formulated. In the model, various important factors, which are commonly discussed but merely modelled in prior literature, were taken into consideration. The model was then solved by heuristics-based method and the performance of the model and algorithm was analyzed using data collected from a selected subvented nursing home in Hong Kong. Results show that the proposed model and algorithm yield perform significantly better than the current approach in terms of reduced total staffing costs, better shared staff workload, and higher staff-task flexibility.

15210815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210815.value: The model may be extended to examine other important problems in the healthcare resources planning, such as the integrated nursing staff demand projection and the scheduling problem, as well as the staff-task assignment problem. By conducting a time study at subvented nursing home that quantifies the properties of nursing staff and healthcare tasks, the proposed model may provide a better and more comprehensive integrated nursing staff demand projection and a scheduling method that is currently discussed in the literature and used in reality.

15210815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210815.value: Demographic change of population ageing is causing social and economic problems. In particular, the demand of residential care services for the elderly is ever increasing. As a result, residential care service providers need to improve the utilization of existing nursing staff and better share the workload of nursing staff. Nursing staff demand modelling (NSDM) plays a critical role. Nevertheless, NSDM relies on human experience and often leads to an ineffective and inefficient planning. In this project, formulation of an optimization model for the planning of optimal size and mixing of nursing teams in nursing homes is described. Critical factors, such as heterogeneous workforce and resident case mix, are considered. A multi-objective evolutionary algorithm is applied to solve the proposed model. A case study of a subvented nursing home in Hong Kong was conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed model and algorithm. The results showed that the total overtime work (in hours) were minimized while the nurse-to-resident ratio was significantly higher within the given budgetary boundary than those based on existing practice. Furthermore, the results suggest that it is cost beneficial to introduce temporary staff in the workforce and to increase the degree of skill mix for NSDM.

15211215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211215.value: Structure-borne sound is the vibrational energy which travels through dynamically loaded mechanical systems. Infra structure-borne sound is inaudible sound of frequency lower than 20 cycles per second (Hertz) which can be excited by low frequency vibrations of flexible structures such as floors, footbridge and even fan blades. Both infra sound and vibration can cause resonances of human organs including eyeball leading to health and safety problems. A common way to solve such problems is to add damping to the vibrating structure if some resonant vibrations of the structure are being excited. Theoretically, increasing damping in a vibrating structure is more effective than increasing its mass or stiffness for the reduction of resonant vibration. Addition of a vibration absorber to a noisy structure can provide an economic solution for vibration suppression and noise radiation attenuation if the absorber is properly designed and located onto the structure. However, there is no easy and systematic way be developed to add the damping wisely. The current design method of adding damping elements to solve the structure-borne noise problem is still by trial and error and case based solutions are reported in literature. The main reason is that there is lack of knowledge to predict the paths of energy which flow from a vibration source to other parts of a structure and engineers just rely on numerical solutions based on the finite element analysis (FEA). The design method based on FEA is a case based approach and provide no insight to the best solution. Since the common viscous damper is ineffective to low frequency vibration, the traditional vibration absorber using viscous damper is not useful to suppress infrasonic vibration. Vibration absorber using viscoelastic material as the resilient and damping element constrained which has potential to be used as a vibration absorber for dampening civil engineering structures. Some preliminary study shows that the fixed-points theory may be applied to optimize the viscoealstic absorber to minimize the resonant vibration amplitude of a single degree-of-freedom vibrating system by adding the viscoelastic vibration absorber. It is proposed in this research to apply fixed-point theory to minimize the resonant vibration amplitudes of both single and multi degree-of-freedom vibrating systems by using one or multiple viscoelastic absorbers each tuned to suppress one vibration mode of the structure in order to suppress infrasonic vibrations in beam or plate structures. The proposed theory will be validated by both numerical simulations and experiments. 次聲波振動抑制用粘彈性動態減震器

15211215.label: Realisation of objectives
15211215.value: The H-infinity optimum parameters of a viscoelastic dynamic vibration absorber (VDVA) using a viscoelastic damper and an elastic spring have been researched analytically for suppressing resonant vibration of a single degree-of-freedom (SDOF) system excited by harmonic forces or due to ground motions. The proposed design of VDVA has an elastic spring and a viscoelastic damper. The stiffness and damping of the proposed VDVA are decoupled such that both of these two characteristics of the absorber can be tuned independently to their optimal values by following a specified procedure. The optimum parameters of the proposed VDVA are derived using the principle of the fixed-points theory. The analytical results show that the optimized viscoelastic vibration absorber can provide similar vibration reduction effect as the optimized traditional dynamic vibration absorber (DVA) at the resonance of a SDOF primary vibrating system. The proposed optimization design of the proposed VDVA is tested numerically using two real commercial viscoelastic damping materials. The proposed VDVA is useful especially for suppressing infrasonic vibrations of large mechanical or civil structures because the traditional DVA using a viscous damper is not effective at low frequency vibrations. A very big viscous damper would be required to generate the damping force required at low frequency. The proposed VDVA may be considered as an alternative design of the traditional DVA for suppressing infrasonic frequency vibrations of massive structures. Research results has been reported in international conference and also published in journal. Design optimization of multiple viscoelastic vibration absorbers for multi-mode vibration suppression has been achieved. Design optimization of multiple vibration absorbers for multi-mode vibration suppression has been researched. It starts with the traditional vibration absorber and the optimization method has been extended to viscoelastic vibration absorbers. In-depth research of the design optimization of multiple viscoelastic vibration absorbers for multi-mode vibration suppression has been addressed in the next reporting period. This research is useful for infrasonic vibration control of multi-degree-of-freedom system such as tall buildings and bridges. Research results has been reported in conference and also published in journal publication. H2 optimization of the viscoelastic vibration absorber for suppression vibrations due to harmonic force excitations has been achieved. H2 optimization of the viscoelastic vibration absorber for suppression vibrations due to support motions has also been addressed. The optimization method are useful to engineers to design vibration absorbers for suppressing broadband vibrations of civil structures such as those due to earthquake or typhoons. Original research results for journal publication is in preparation.

15211215.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211215.value: A viscoelastic dynamic vibration absorber (VDVA) is proposed for suppressing infrasonic vibrations of heavy structures because the traditional dynamic vibration absorber equipped with a viscous damper is not effective in suppressing low frequency vibrations. The proposed VDVA has an elastic spring and a viscoelastic damper with frequency dependent modulus and damping properties. The standard fixed-points theory cannot be applied to derive the optimum design parameters of the VDVA because both its stiffness and damping are frequency dependent. A modified fixed-points theory is therefore proposed to solve this problem. H1 design optimization of the proposed VDVA have been derived for the minimization of resonant vibration amplitude of a single degree-of-freedom system excited by harmonic forces or due to ground motions. The stiffness and damping of the proposed VDVA can be decoupled such that both of these two properties of the absorber can be tuned independently to their optimal values by following a specified procedure. The proposed VDVA with optimized design is tested numerically using two real commercial viscoelastic damping materials. It is found that the proposed viscoelastic absorber can provide much stronger vibration reduction effect than the conventional VDVA without the elastic spring. A beam-based DVA (beam DVA) is proposed and optimized for minimizing the resonant vibration of a continuous or multi degree-of-freedom structure. A constrained damping layer of viscous or viscoelastic damping can be applied in the modeling of the beam DVA. The vibration suppression performance of the proposed beam DVA depends on the mass ratio, the flexural rigidity and length of the beam. In comparison with the traditional sprung mass DVA, the proposed beam DVA shows more flexibility in vibration control design because it has more design parameters. With proper design, the beam DVA's vibration suppression capability can outperform that of the traditional DVA under the same mass constraint. The general approach is illustrated using a benchmark cantilever beam as an example. The receptance theory is introduced to model the compound system consisting of the host beam and the attached beam-based DVA. The model is validated through comparisons with the results from Abaqus as well as the Transfer Matrix method (TMM) method. Fixed-points theory is then employed to derive the analytical expressions for the optimum tuning ratio and damping ratio of the proposed beam absorber. A design guideline is then presented to choose the parameters of the beam absorber.

15211215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211215.value: H2 optimization of the viscoelastic vibration absorber for suppression vibrations due to harmonic force excitations has been achieved. H2 optimization of the viscoelastic vibration absorber for suppression vibrations due to support motions has also been addressed. The optimization method are useful to engineers to design vibration absorbers for suppressing broadband vibrations of civil structures such as those due to earthquake or typhoons. Real earthquake or wind loading data in history can be applied to tall building structures for the test of the proposed viscoelastic dynamic vibration absorber. This further development of the research can help the optimization process of the locations and tuning parameters of the viscoelastic DVAs for vibration suppression of multi degree-of-freedom structures such as tall buildings, bridges and blades, etc.

15211615.label: Project Objectives
15211615.value: Signaling strategies for high capacity NFDM transmission systems: In the NFT framework, the discrete and continuous eigenvalues are all parallel independent channels available for information transmission in a nonlinear fiber governed by NLSE. We will a. derive appropriate signaling strategies using both the continuous and discrete eigenvalues for high capacity transmissions through identifying signal sets with small physical bandwidth, temporal spread, small peak-to-average ratio and other favorable attributes. Practical transmission impairments and their compensation techniques for NFDM signals: Laser phase noise and polarization effects degrade transmission performance and require appropriate compensation in practical long-haul coherent systems. We will a. investigate their performance impact on NFDM systems and derive receiver signal processing algorithms for polarization de-multiplexing, laser phase noise and frequency offset compensation. b. characterize the robustness of NFDM signals against the effects of third-order dispersion and Raman scattering through numerical simulations. Experimental demonstrations of NFDM transmission systems: NFDM transmission experiments are to be conducted with the experimental facilities readily available at PolyU. We will a. conduct proof-of-concept NFDM experiments in transmitting multiple phase and amplitude modulated discrete eigenvalues over long distance. b. experimentally investigate the performance of high capacity signaling sets and DSP algorithms developed in objective 1)

15211615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211615.value: High spectral efficiency modulation formats and electronic digital signal processing(DSP) define the current generation of long-haul optical transceivers supporting 100Gb/s and beyond. Moving forward, emerging dominance of mobile devices, data center, cloud computing, 5G wireless and Internet of Things(IoT) applications impose unprecedented speed requirements that are not met by this generation of technology: even with arbitrarily complex DSP and signaling schemes, transmission performance is limited by fiber Kerr nonlinearity, a fundamental impairment characterizing the nonlinear fiber channel. Recently, Nonlinear Frequency Division Multiplexing(NFDM) based on Nonlinear Fourier Transform(NFT) is proposed as a theoretical framework generalizing soliton and conventional OFDM communication theory. NFDM resembles the commonly-known OFDM philosophy in that independent information streams can be encoded in parallel sub-carriers(called eigenvalues of the Lax operator governing the loseless nonlinear Schrodinger equation) without mutual interference upon nonlinear propagation and is immune to cross-phase modulation(XPM) effects. Also, as NFDM encodes information in the eigenvalues, devastating time-domain effects for traditional soliton systems such as timing jitter may become less damaging. Furthermore, in contrast with soliton transmissions in the 1990s, present-day DSP hardware enable practical realization of true eigenvalue communications for the first time, thus potentially open up tremendous opportunities for fundamental advances in optical communications. A few preliminary NFDM works reported to date have only touched on the surface and a fully developed suite of NFDM communication strategies with practical DSP algorithms and corresponding experimental demonstrations is very far from reality at present. The objectives of the proposed research are to address key issues and elucidate the ultimate potentials for NFDM in long-haul optical communications. In particular, we will 1)derive signaling strategies for high capacity NFDM transmission systems; 2)investigate the effects of practical transmission impairments and their compensation techniques for NFDM signals and 3)conduct proof-of-concept NFDM transmission experiments. We are potentially at the edge of a breakthrough that finally address the decades-old fundamental problem defining optical communications. The successful completion of the proposed research will, for the first time, consolidate the underlying principles of solitons, nonlinear optics, communications and DSP technology into a more general framework guiding communication system designs for the nonlinear fiber channel. The key experimental demonstrations and unique insights developed will be the cornerstone of a new communication philosophy that cleverly embrace the nonlinear nature of the channel and may lead the evolution into a new paradigm in long-haul optical communications. 高階信號調製格式與數字信號處理技術是現階段100Gb/s及以上速率長距離光通信的關鍵技術。然而，隨著移動通信設備數量的劇增，以及數據中心，雲計算，第五代移動通信與物聯網興起，現階段光通信技術所提供的網絡帶寬將會無法滿足需求：即使使用更複雜的數字信號處理技術與信號產生方法，光通信帶寬仍然會受到光纖固有的非線性限制而無法進一步得到提升。最近，一種基於非線性傅里葉變換(NFT)的非線性頻分複用技術（NFDM）被提出并得到越來越多的關注。非線性頻分複用技術（NFDM）的理論框架可以看成是光孤子通信與傳統正交頻分複用技術（OFDM）的融合與在非線性頻率上的擴展，其借鑒了傳統正交頻分複用技術的思想： 將相互獨立的信息流承載到一系列正交的子載波上（在NFDM中則為將信號承載到通過Lax運算符得到的非線性薛定諤方程的特征值上）。承載信號的子載波之間在非線性傳輸過程中沒有相互干擾，而且不受交叉相位調製（XPM）的影響。同時，由於NFDM系統將信息承載到特征值上，傳統光孤子傳輸中在時域中存在的一些破壞性損傷列如定時抖動對於NFDM系統的影響將不再那麼嚴重。並且，與90年代的光孤子傳輸不同的是，現今的數字信號處理技術使真正意義上的特征值通信成為了現實，這將為光通信的進一步發展開闢了新的研究方向。到目前為止，關於NFDM的研究才剛剛開始，NFDM通信完整架構的制定、相關數字信號處理算法的實用化以及NFDM實驗驗證離我們還很遙遠。 此研究計劃的目標是解決NFDM通信中的關鍵問題，發掘 NFDM技術在長距離光通信中的巨大潛力。具體來說，我們將會 1） 推導得到大容量NFDM傳輸系統中信號的產生方法； 2） 研究實際通信中非理想信道對NFDM信號傳輸產生的影響以及補償方法； 3） 進行NFDM傳輸實驗驗證。 我們現在將有可能成功突破幾十年來一直制約光通信進一步發展的瓶頸。該研究計劃的順利完成，將會開創一種融合了光孤子傳輸，非線性光學，通信與數字信號處理的更通用的光通信理論，指導今後基於非線性光纖信道傳輸的通信系統的設計。該研究中所進行的關鍵實驗與之得到的相關研究成果將會為該新通信的理論的產生打下基礎，這種新的通信理論能夠巧妙的解決光纖傳輸中的非線性的影響并引領長距離光通信新的革命。

15211615.label: Realisation of objectives
15211615.value: We have characterized the correlation structure between different signal parameters in the NFT framework such as b-coefficients and eigenvalue noises and developed corresponding signal encoding and receiver detection and signal processing strategies to increase the signal energy, reduce the effects of signal peak-to-average ratio and in turn reduce the bit error ratio, improve transmission speed for both discrete, continuous and polarization multiplexed NFT systems. This include encoding in a-coefficient, detection using b-coefficient, linear minimum mean-square filter to reduce the noise in b-coefficient, signal shaping to improve the signal energy for b-coefficient encoding using signal shaping. We have also investigated the joint encoding of eigenvalues and spectral amplitudes, and also multi-pulse encoding where neighboring pulse collision is absorbed in the design to improve the bit rate-distance product. This sheds light on an extra dimension for signal design in NFT systems. Therefore, objective 1 have fully been achieved. We have also conducted corresponding experiments for all the signal design and detection strategies developed in objective 1) that make use of noise correlation between the b-coefficient and eigenvalue noise, joint discrete eigenvalue-spectral amplitude-spectral phase modulation, multi-pulse encoding, polarization multiplexing and spectral shaping b-coefficient for continuous eigenvalue modulation. The performance of the discrete-eigenvalue experimental demonstrations are leading in the community. Therefore, objective 3 is fully achieved. Furthermore, in both simulations and experiments, the effect of third order dispersion and Raman scattering is shown to be small compared to the performance improvements brought about by the proposed signal design and detection strategies proposed. We also studied and experimentally demonstrated polarization multiplexed NFT transmission and developed polarization demultiplexing using specially designed transmitted symbol sequence, laser phase noise and frequency offset compensation techniques that are necessary for proper signal recovery in both simulations and experiment. Therefore, objective 2 is fully achieved.

15211615.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211615.value: Under the NFT framework, the interaction of signals and noise does not resemble other known systems. We studied statistical structure of noise for NFT systems in Part C8,3 and characterized their correlation structure as a function of distance and other parameters. The statistical structure give rise to new signal design and detection strategy specifically for NFT systems needs to be developed in order to maximize the performance of NFT systems. In Part C8, 1, we show that one can encode information in the a-coefficient as supposed to traditional q-coefficient to improve performance. Also, the noise in b-coefficient are highly correlated with the eigenvalue noise at the receiver. We developed a linear minimum mean square error(LMMSE) filter that make use of such correlation and obtain significant performance improvements. The LMMSE method has since become a standard technique for the community. We further studied joint eigenvalue and spectral amplitude modulation (part C8, 6) using the developed DSP techniques and obtain significant distance reach extension to 1000 km for 24Gb/s transmission. For continuous eigenvalue, we showed in Part 8C.4 that modulation in b-coefficient suffers from a fundamental energy barrier that can be shifted by proper design of the carrier waveform and the modulation alphabet. Simulation and experimental results demonstrated higher received signal quality and longer transmission reach than a conventional b-modulator. We also studied polarization multiplexed NFT transmission using continuous eigenvalue in Part 8C.5. we developed transmitted symbol blocks that includes synchronization symbols (SS), polarization separation symbols (PSS), training symbols (TS) and data symbols so as to train the multi-input-multi-output(MIMO) filter to successfully demultiplex the signals from two polarizations in the NFT framework. 25.6 Gb/s transmission over 1680 km fiber is achieved. Lastly, we show in Part C8,2 that, in contrast to conventional wisdom of avoiding soliton interactions, one can intentionally design the speed of neighboring soliton pulses to interact and collide during propagation and exchange positions to improve transmission performance. This can be achieved by designing neighboring solitons’ eigenvalues to have opposite signs in the real part. 24Gb/s transmission over 1500 km can be achieved under this scheme. We have also studied algorithms to compensate practical impairments such as phase noise and frequency offsets (part C9, 1). This allow all the developed algorithms and research findings aforementioned to be verified experimentally, thus laying out the concrete steps to realize NFT systems and demonstrating the potentials of NFT transmissions for nonlinear fiber systems in the future.

15211615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211615.value: The developed algorithms are preliminary ideas with promising experimental demonstrations. They opened up new ways to encode and decode information for nonlinear fiber transmissions and much more detailed optimizations can be investigated to further improve transmission performance Also, the results show that one can transmit high speed optical signal reliably at 10 to 15 times higher optical power than conventional transmission scheme, which in turn implies that certain optical / electrical amplifiers at conventional receivers can be potentially removed and achieve higher performance and lower cost. These aspects will be investigated in detail as future development of this research project

15211615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211615.value: The worldwide Internet relies on high speed optical communication links and increasing demands of Internet speed and number of connected devices requires better and faster optical communications speed. One of the fundamental limitations of optical communications is fiber Kerr nonlinearity that distort optical signals in complicated manners and hard to analytically studied and eliminated. Nonlinear Fourier Transform(NFT) is a new theoretical framework that attempts to provide a deeper understanding of signal propagation in optical fibers. Based on this new NFT framework, we have developed new signal design strategies at the transmitters and receiver signal processing algorithms. Experimental demonstrations show performance gain in long distance optical transmission links with large amount of nonlineraity effects. The results verify the potentials of this new NFT framework and open up new directions for research in optical communications, which is the foundation to all telecommunication activities in our modern society.

15211815.label: Project Objectives
15211815.value: A 3-dimensional (3-D) electromagnetic field and thermal field coupled finite element method (FEM) for multi-physics performance analysis of nanofluid-filled transformers will be developed. An adjustable DoF method will be developed so that only one FEM mesh is required to achieve the functions of multi-physics coupling, domain decomposition and multi-level modeling, which can significantly reduce the computing time of the multi-physics problems. A multi-objective multi-level optimal design method of the nanofluid-filled transformers will be developed. The performance improvement of the transformers by using the developed design method and the effective design guidelines will be presented.

15211815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211815.value: 隨著電網容量和電壓等級的不斷提高，高絕緣、大容量以及小體積的電力變壓器成為了電力工廠和製造者的追求目標，如何提高變壓器內部的絕緣和散熱性能備受關注。納米改性流體可作為一種新型的概念應用到變壓器油中，它是指將納米顆粒通過一定的分散方法添加到基液后所形成的穩定懸浮液，從而提高了流體的絕緣和散熱性能。由於納米改性變壓器油的絕緣和散熱性能比傳統的變壓器油顯著提高，納米油變壓器的重量、體積以及生產成本等總體性能，相比傳統變壓器，均有很大的提昇。 納米油變壓器有效且可行的設計方法仍是工程師的研究重點和難點。首先，納米顆粒存在磁化問題，其引發的電磁力和電泳現象對變壓器的漏磁場、溫度場以及納米流體都有很大的影響。其次，在設計過程中，電磁場、流體場以及溫度場之間存在著耦合關係，變壓器的損耗以及油流分佈會影響其溫升分佈。相應的溫度大小同樣影響著變壓器的電磁和油流材料特性。最後，由於變壓器結構的複雜性，導致其數值仿真計算有巨大的求解難度。 為此，本項目提出一種基於可調節自由度多物理場數值模型的納米油變壓器優化設計方法。該方法基於有限元法建立及求解電磁場-流體場-溫度場的三維耦合數值計算模型，並且提供了一個方便、準備和有效的方法來增加/降低變量個數、耦合/解耦變量關係，從而顯著的降低了計算時間。在傳統的計算方法中，電磁場、流體場和溫度場計算分別需要不同的網格，這樣大大降低了計算的效率和準確性。而可調節自由度法的主要優點是在實現多物理場耦合、區域分解以及多級優化模型過程中只需要一套網格。因此，在不同的自由度約束條件下，可以很容易實現網格的粗化/細化，大大降低了計算時間。同時，為解決在計算變壓器結構件雜散損耗中的集膚效應問題，本項目提出採用區域分解法去降低計算工作量。並且，應用可調節自由度方法可以方便的處理全域和分域之間的關係。在優化過程中，粗糙模型和逐步細化模型都用於目標函數的計算，這些多級優化計算模型也可以通過可調節自由度控制在一套網格中，增加計算準確性。 綜上所述，為了提高變壓器的電磁、絕緣以及散熱性能，本項目提出一種基於多目標、多物理場以及多級的優化方法應用於納米油變壓器的設計中。最後，本項目將通過試驗樣機去驗證該方法的有效性。

15211815.label: Realisation of objectives
15211815.value: An adaptive degrees-of-freedom (DoFs) finite-element method (FEM) has been developed for the 3-D multi-physics analysis, in which only one FEM mesh is required to meet the different discretization requirements of fields by adjusting the DoFs of each field separately. The mapping algorithms for different meshes are no longer needed, and the resulted mapping errors are avoided. The number of DoFs is increased along with the mesh refinement, while the reduction of DoFs is realized by removing redundant DoFs from the unknown list. Since there is no actual mesh coarsening, the work and time for administrating different meshes between two steps are avoided in the coarsening operation. An accurate and flexible constraint is proposed to adapt the complex 3-D transient field, and the reduction of DoFs is separated from the hierarchical mesh structure. The combination of domain decomposition method and adaptive method has also been studied. A domain decomposition method is used to solve the problem in parallel based on the current mesh, and adaptive method is used to estimate the results and adapt the mesh to the problem. The mesh adaption is conducted globally to avoid the non-conformal mesh between sub domains. Dynamic multi-level optimal design methods have been developed for the oil-immersed transformer design, including the electromagnetic design and the cooling system design. In order to speed up the optimal design process while ensuring the accuracy of the computed optimal solutions, the response surface method is employed in the design process in combination with the numerical method. According to the design objectives and parameters, an initial surrogate model is produced by the response surface method to replace the numerical model in the rough design. Meanwhile, the accuracy of the surrogate model can be gradually improved by adding more design points until meeting the predefined criterion, and a precise design can be realized with the final model readily with almost zero computational cost. The heat transfer performance of nanofluid-filled transformers has been numerically and experimentally investigated. The transformer windings are numerically modelled with the computational fluid dynamics, and the multiphase nanofluid flow is modelled with the mixture model. The changes in temperature profile, mass flow rate distribution and pressure drop after using the nanofluid are evaluated. A further comparison on heat transfer is made after minimizing the oil volume and maximum temperature-rise of these two transformers cooled by nanofluid and conventional transformer oil. An experiment has been conducted to validate the heat transfer performance improvement after using nanofluid.

15211815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211815.value: For the transient magnetic field analysis, the computational efficiency can be further improved by using the domain decomposition methods (DDMs) in combination with the time decomposition methods (TDMs), namely the space-time DDM. The entire time-stepping process is divided into several subdivisions, in which multiple time steps are solved at a time. Meanwhile, the DDM is embedded in the FEM to make the computation of each time step parallel. Other emerging artificial methods, such as deep learning, also can be applied in the rapid field calculation. Dislike the surrogate model, a detailed field distribution can be obtained from the deep neural network. Optimization methods can be developed to fully exploit these fast analysis algorithms. Except the thermal properties, other properties of oil based nanofluids, such as dielectric characteristics, breakdown voltage, can be studied based on the transformer application. Different types of transformers or transformers under different operation status can be investigated. The effect of volume fraction and nanoparticle can be included in the study. To promote the industrial application, efficient nanofluids preparation method can be developed.

15211815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211815.value: An adaptive DoFs FEM solver has been developed for the 3-D nonlinear magnetic field analysis, thermal field analysis, and coupled magneto-thermal field analysis. The coupled analysis is based on the independent solvers for magnetic field and thermal field. The proposed algorithm provides a robust and fast method to reduce the computing time in magnetic field, thermal field and coupled field analysis. The system reduction is realized by eliminating the redundant DoFs from the unknown list rather than removing the corresponding nodes. In the coupled analysis, the different discretization requirements of two fields are met with one set of mesh, and the mapping algorithms for different meshes are no longer needed. Several numerical examples have been solved to showcase the effectiveness of this method in terms of efficiency and accuracy. The heat transfer performance of nanofluid in transformers has been numerically and experimentally investigated. It is concluded from the results that the enhanced thermal conductivity is the main reason for the heat transfer improvement after using nanofluid, and the reduction of coolant volume can be realized along with the reduction of temperature rise after using nanofluid. In addition, efficient design methods based on the response surface method have been presented for the transformer design optimization problems, and the effectiveness has been verified with typical problems.

15212415.label: Project Objectives
15212415.value: To develop consistency based JSA-DL models -- Since both S-DL and A-DL aim to learn dictionaries to represent images sparsely, they have consistency in terms of data approximation and data encoding. In this project, we will propose data consistency and code consistency based integration terms to integrate S-DL and A-DL into a JSA-DL framework. The data consistency terms ensure that the data reconstructed by synthesis and analysis dictionaries are consistent, and the code consistency terms build the correspondence between the coding vectors by the two dictionaries. Alternative minimization algorithms will be developed to optimize the dictionaries and model hyper-parameters. JSA-DL for image reconstruction -- We will apply the proposed JSA-DL models to image reconstruction. Patch-based offline learning and adaptive online learning methods will be firstly developed. Convolution-based method will then be developed to more effectively exploit the correlation of neighboring patches and image global information. The developed image reconstruction methods will achieve state-of-the-art performance in terms of both quantitative measures and visual perception quality. JSA-DL for image classification -- The proposed JSA-DL models will also be applied to image classification tasks. Effective code consistency and code complementarity based integration terms, as well as discriminative regularization terms, will be proposed to promote the model representation capability and discrimination capability. The developed discriminative JSA-DL methods will have not only high classification accuracy, but also high training and testing efficiency.
