15212415.label: Realisation of objectives
15212415.value: 1. Improvements of Synthesis Dictionary Learning (S-DL) and Analysis Dictionary Learning (A-DL) The sparsity prior has been widely studied due to the property of sparse distribution of natural images, and facilitates numerous sparse dictionary learning methods. Existing methods can be generally categorized to the Synthesis Dictionary Learning (S-DL) and Analysis Dictionary Learning (A-DL) models. S-DL based denoising methods show effective performance on additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) removal. However, these approaches are essentially limited by the data-fidelity term described by Frobenius norm, which is not able to characterize the signal dependent and realistic noise. To extend the S-DL model for real-world image denoising, we explored to utilize the channel-wise statistics and signal dependent property of realistic noise and proposed the trilateral weighted sparse coding (TWSC) scheme. We introduced two weight matrices for the data-fidelity term and regularization term, respectively. The data-fidelity term is used to characterize the realistic noise property, and the regularization term is exploited to characterize the sparsity priors of natural images. Experiments on three datasets showed that the proposed TWSC scheme achieves favorable performance with the state-of-the-art denoising methods. This work [C5] was published in ECCV 2018. On the other hand, for denoising task, image priors are generally learned from either external data or the noisy image itself. However, priors learned from external data may not be adaptive to the image to be denoised, while priors learned from the given noisy image may not be accurate due to the interference of corrupted noise. Meanwhile, the noise in real-world noisy images is very complex, making real-world image denoising very challenging. In [J1], we proposed to learn prior by exploiting the information in both external and internal data. The external prior guided the orthogonal dictionary learning of internal patch group to achieve the external-internal hybrid prior models for image denoising. Most A-DL methods learn analysis representation on images from one single modality, which cannot be applied to guided depth image reconstruction. In [C1], we proposed a weighted analysis representation model to extend for guided depth reconstruction. An intensity weighting term and an analysis representation regularization term are combined to model complex relationship between depth image and RGB image. Then, we adopt a task-driven learning method to learn stage-wise parameters for dynamic guidance. [C1] 2. Joint Synthesis and Analysis Dictionary Learning (JSA-DL) To use the complementary property of the S-DL and A-DL models, we investigated the integration of A-DL and S-DL for achieving a JSA-DL framework. S-DL methods investigate signals from a synthesis point of view, and a few coefficients are selected to reconstruct the signal, which facilitates an over-complete dictionary to provide flexible prior. On the other hand, A-DL approaches impose the sparsity prior on the analysis filters on whole images for modeling the local structure of natural images, however, the implicit orthogonal constraints impede it to take benefit from increased redundancy of the analysis dictionary. To address the single image layer separation problem, we integrated the ASR and SSR models into a joint convolutional sparse representation (JCAS) framework. Specifically, the analysis-component is used to approximate image large-scale structures, while the synthesis-component benefits to representing image fine-scale textures. Without external training data, the proposed JCAS model achieves competitive results on different tasks such as rain streak removal, high dynamic range image tone mapping and contrast enhancement. [C3] In discriminative learning, sparsity prior is essentially associated with the regularization term in the MAP-based models. From this perspective, in [J4], we proposed to learn the fidelity term and regularization term simultaneously. By defining the practical image restoration tasks as image restoration with partially known or inaccurate degradation models, we proposed a principled solution by introducing a flexible model, which aims to parameterize the fidelity term for characterizing spatial dependency and complex residual distribution of the residual image. Then, we presented a bi-level optimization model for simultaneously learning the fidelity and regularization terms in a task driven manner. Experiments on rain streak removal and image deconvolution with inaccurate blur kernel demonstrated the effectiveness of our method. This work was published in T-PAMI 2019. [J4] 3. Applications on image reconstruction The ℓ1 sparsity prior has long been adopted in Retinex decomposition to model the structural sparsity of the reflectance layer. Inspired by this, for the task of tone mapping, we adopted the layer decomposition methods, and proposed to impose the ℓ1 sparsity term on the base layer to preserve edges, while its piecewise smoothness nature leads to a weak structural prior. Then, we further applied an ℓ0 sparsity term on detail layer to model the structural prior. Finally, we presented a hybrid ℓ1-ℓ0 layer decomposition model for tone mapping. [C4] Convolutional neural network (CNN) has been successfully applied for denoising due to its large modeling capacity and tremendous advances in network training and design. However, existing discriminative denoising methods are limited in flexibility, and the learned model is usually tailored to a specific noise level. To address this issue, we presented a fast and flexible denoising convolutional neural network, i.e., FFDNet in [J2]. By introducing a tunable noise level map as the input, FFDNet is prone to handling a wide range of noise levels using a single network, and can remove spatially variant noise by specifying a non-uniform noise level map. The experiments showed that it achieves a good trade-off between inference speed and denoising performance. [J2] For demosaicking, most existing hand-crafted prior learning methods exhibit obvious artifacts in the results. In [C2], we trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) in an end-to-end manner to address the color demosaicking. To leverage the demosaicking domain knowledge, a two-phase network architecture is designed to explore the G-guidance prior for R and B channel reconstruction. The intermediate result of the G channel in the first stage is used to guide the reconstruction of final result in the second stage. On the other hand, to facilitate the development of edge-preserving image smoothing, we constructed a benchmark which consists of 500 source images and ground-truth image smoothing results for quantitative performance evaluation. Furthermore, we included various baseline learning models by using representative deep convolutional network architectures and designed novel loss functions to advance the state-of-the-arts. [J3]

15212415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212415.value: 1. To exploit the complementary representation mechanisms of Analysis sparse representation (ASR) and synthesis sparse representation (SSR), we proposed a joint convolutional analysis and synthesis (JCAS) sparse representation model. The proposed JCAS model achieves competitive results on different tasks such as rain streak removal, high dynamic range image tone mapping and contrast enhancement. [C3] 2. In [C5], we proposed a novel trilateral weighted sparse coding (TWSC) scheme to exploit the noise properties across different channels and local patches for real-world image denoising. On the other hand, we explored to learn prior by exploiting the information in both external and internal data in [J1]. The external prior guided the orthogonal dictionary learning of internal patch group to achieve the external-internal hybrid prior models for image denoising. 3. We presented a fast and flexible denoising convolutional neural network, namely, FFDNet. With a tunable noise level map as the input, FFDNet has the ability to handle a wide range of noise levels effectively with a single network, and can remove spatially variant noise by specifying a non-uniform noise level map. It achieves a good trade-off between inference speed and denoising performance. [J2] 4. We developed a principled solution to handle image restoration with partially known or inaccurate degradation. A flexible model is suggested to parameterize the fidelity term for characterizing spatial dependency and complex residual distribution of the residual image. We further develop to learn the fidelity and regularization learning model simultaneously in a task driven manner. [J4] 5. We proposed a benchmark for edge-preserving image smoothing. It consists of 500 paired- smoothing images for quantitative performance evaluation and various baseline learning models. [J3] 6. To exploit color images for guided depth image enhancement, we introduced an intensity weighting term and an analysis representation regularization term to model the dependency between intensity and depth map. Then a task driven training strategy is utilized to learn stage-wise parameters for specific task. [C1]

15212415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212415.value: 1. Improve the generalization ability The proposed methods are mostly proposed for image reconstruction. The JSA-DL framework promotes the model representation capability, and benefits to promising performance. To improve the generalization of the proposed methods for more vision tasks, in the future we will explore the discriminative regularization terms for improving the discrimination capability of JSA-DL models and extend it to some high-level problems, such as image classification. 2. Combination with convolutional neural network Most of existing dictionary learning methods are based on image patches. Recently, convolution-based methods have been developed to more effectively exploit the correlation of neighboring patches and image global information. It inspires us to explore effective and efficient schemes to combine DL with CNN.

15212415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212415.value: In this project, we proposed a series of task-specific methods for image reconstruction. First, the Synthesis Dictionary Learning (S-DL) and Analysis Dictionary Learning (A-DL) models are studied, and improvements are performed by introducing the weighting matrices or the intensity guided weight on data-fidelity and regularization terms. Second, to leverage the complementary advantages, we integrated the A-DL and S-DL models, and proposed a JSA-DL framework for applications involving image layer separation. Furthermore, inspired from the joint S-DL and A-DL scheme, we investigated the discriminative methods for image restoration. We developed the simultaneous fidelity and regularization learning (SFARL) model which provides a principled solution for image restoration with partially known or inaccurate degradation. Third, we applied the S-DL, A-DL, JSA-DL and discriminative methods to image reconstruction, such as image denoising, tone mapping, demosaicking and edge-preserving image smoothing. The developed image reconstruction methods achieve state-of-the-art performance in terms of both quantitative measures and visual perception quality.

15212515.label: Project Objectives
15212515.value: To develop a new moment method aiming at simultaneously tracing agglomerate size and shape factor, i.e. BTEMOMs model, through solving the agglomerate population balance equation(PBE) in terms of bivariates. The closure of fractal moments in BTEMOMs will be achieved with the high performance Taylor expansion technique. To develop a technique for acquiring the reconstruction of particle size distribution(PSD) from the known bivariate statistical moments calculated by solving BTEMOMs equations. The newly proposed BTEMOMs model is expected to solve problems involving not only statistical moment quantities, but also the specific PSD. To establish a novel CFD-BTEMOMs model scheme which truly couples the computational fluid dynamics(CFD) and the agglomerate dynamics within the Eurelian-Eurelian framework. When the specific turbulence model,i.e. the large eddy simulation(LES), is carried out, the influence of turbulent fluctuation due to the filter solution on the dynamics of agglomeration processes shown in BTEMOMs will be quantified and the corresponding closure model for additional unresolved terms will be proposed. This model has potential to be applied to fractal-like agglomerate-laden multiphase flow with multiple dynamic processes and mass & heat transfer. To acquire a better understanding of the fundamentals of transport mechanism of fractal-like aggregates in turbulent and high temperature gradient environments; to capture the governing parameters dominating agglomerate mobility due to the diffusion and thermophoretic force; to acquire the relationship between agglomerate transport and the mass fractal dimension; and to capture the relationship between collision frequency and agglomerate structure & properties. To fully validate this proposed novel CFD-BTEMOMs model through investigating the mechanism of titanium dioxide(TiO2) agglomerate formation and subsequent growth in turbulent combustion flows with the highly reliable existing experimental datasets and sectional method available from the literature. The spatial and temporal evolution of agglomerate size distribution, fractal dimension, turbulence effect on agglomerate dynamics, and competition effect between coagulation & sintering on the final agglomerate properties will be studied.

15212515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212515.value: With the rapid development in nanoparticle synthesis, the physics of agglomerate formation and growth in turbulent combustion flows has become one of the challenging scientific problems. These agglomerates and complicated flow structures influence each other through multiple interactions at temporal and spatial scales that span many orders of magnitude, which make the problem difficult to be investigated by the traditional multiphase flow approach. Today, many suitable numerical methods and the corresponding numerical models involving strong coupling between computational fluid dynamics(CFD), and dynamics of agglomerate formation & reconstruction are still not well established. In order to achieve a much deeper understanding of fundamental mechanism of nanoparticle synthesis thereby enhancement the characteristics of product particles, it is thus necessary to develop an efficient mathematical model by truly combining the flame dynamics with agglomerate dynamics. This newly proposed model is able to investigate the polydispersed and fractal-like agglomerate dynamics influenced by the turbulent combustion flows with strong interphase heat and mass transfer. The Taylor-expansion method of moments(TEMOMs)(which was firstly proposed by the Principal Investigator and Co-Investigator in 2008) will be further developed from "only ONE internal coordinate to TWO internal coordinates" such that "both agglomerate size distribution and agglomerate morphology factors can be simultaneously traced". The approach for accomplishing the reconstruction of particle size distribution(PSD) with respect to bivariates from known statistical moments will be investigated. When coupling this newly proposed “Bivariate TEMOMs”(BTEMOMs) with CFD in turbulent flows, the truly coupled CFD-BTEMOMs model scheme will be established through which the fractal-like agglomerate formation and subsequent growth in turbulent combustion flows can be more reliably described without ignoring the influence of turbulent fluctuation on the agglomerate dynamic processes. It will also focus on acquiring the specific form of CFD-BTEMOMs model when the turbulence model is selected to be the large eddy simulation(LES) approach, and emphasize on acquiring the suitable method to get the closure of additional fluctuation terms once the moments in BTEMOMs are averaged in terms of space. This novel CFD-BTEMOMs model scheme reserves the inherent advantages of our established TEMOMs in computational efficiency and precision,and truly achieves the coupling between CFD and population balance equation(PBE) computation,and therefore is expected to become a very promising method for solving scientific problems related to the multi-scale agglomerate synthesis in turbulent combustion flows. The highly reliable experimental datasets and sectional method available from the literature will also be used as references to validate this new model. 伴隨納米顆粒合成的快速發展，湍流燃燒流中凝並體形成和生長的物理規律已成為一個富有挑戰性的科學問題。 這些凝並體和複雜的流動結構通過多重作用相互影響， 其時間和空間尺度涵蓋多個數量級， 使得傳統的多相流方法難以研究這一難題。 今天，涉及到計算流體力學與凝並體形成-重構動力學之間的強耦合時，許多合適的數值方法和相應的數值模型都尚未成熟地建立起來。 為了獲得對納米顆粒合成的基礎機理的更深刻認識，從而強化產出的納米粒子的特性， 因此有必要通過將火焰動力學和凝並體動力學真正耦合起來， 開發出一種高效的數學模型。 這一新提出的模型能夠用以研究具有多分散性和分形特点的凝並體，在涉及強烈的相間熱與質量傳遞的湍流燃燒流影響下的動力學特性。 泰勒展開矩方法（由本項目首席研究員與合作研究員於2008年首次提出）將從“只有一個內部坐標變量”進一步開發為“具有兩個內部坐標變量， 以便凝並體的尺寸分佈和凝並體的形狀因子可以被同時追蹤。 本項目也將研究從已知的統計矩出發，重新構建出雙變量形式的顆粒尺寸分佈函數的方法。 當這一新提出的“雙變量泰勒展開矩方法”與計算流體力學方法在湍流中實現耦合時， 就可以建立起真正耦合的計算流體力學-雙變量泰勒展開矩方法， 進而通過這個方法可以在不忽略湍流脈動對凝並體動力學的影響的情況下， 對湍流燃燒流中具有分形特性的凝並體的形成和後續生長進行可靠的描述。 本項目也將致力於獲得當選擇大渦模擬作為湍流模型時， 此計算流體力學-雙變量泰勒展開矩方法的具體形式， 並著重於獲得合適的方法， 以便在對雙變量泰勒展開矩方法中的矩進行空間平均后， 多出的脈動項能實現封閉。 這一全新的計算流體力學-雙變量泰勒展開矩方法保留了我們已經建立起的泰勒展開矩方法在計算效率和精度方面的固有優點， 並且真正實現了計算流體力學和顆粒群平衡方程計算的耦合。 因此有望成為一個非常有應用前景的方法， 並能解決與湍流燃燒流中多尺度凝並體合成有關的科學問題。 這個新模型將以文獻中現有的高度可靠的實驗數據及分區方法為參照，進行充分驗證。

15212515.label: Realisation of objectives
15212515.value: In the realization of Objective 5.2.1, our previously well developed Taylor-series expansion method of moments (TEMOMs) model is further extended to solve the bivariate population balance equation (PBE) and formulate the novel Bivariate TEMOM (Biv-TEMOM) model scheme (i.e., the called BTEMOMs model scheme in the proposal). The moments with fractal orders are closed using the well developed Taylor-series expansion method. Since Sheldon K. Friedlander (2000) proposed the general PBE for aerosol dynamics originating from the Smoluchowski discrete coagulation equation, PBE has been the most widely used governing equations for studying mean field simulation of aerosol related problems. Examples include atmospheric and industrial aerosols, colloidal and polymer sciences, powder technology etc. Considerable research studies on aerosol dynamics are carried out to overcome the complexity and difficulty in theoretical and experimental studies on PBE. The main feature of PBE is that it only deals with one variable i.e. particle size is needed to describe the particulate system completely. As far as fractal aggregates are concerned, a modified coagulation kernel including a pre-specified fractal dimension for the entire aggregate population is often used due to the computing limitations. However, the significant progress in computing power has made the solution of bivariate PBE possible so that a more realistic and accurate description of fractal aggregates can be obtained. Among the numerous numerical methods to solve the population balance equation (PBE), the PI's collaborative research team firstly developed a novel Taylor series expansion method of moments (TEMOM) for the solution of PBE. The TEMOM has been widely well-proven and used to be an effective and highly promising method of moments due to its inherent high accuracy and efficiency for univariate PBE. By establishing such a Biv-TEMOM model scheme, it is feasible to simultaneously trace agglomerate size and shape factor of fractal-like aggregates through solving the agglomerate PBE in terms of two variables (known as bivariates). To achieve closure of the ordinary differential equations of moments, the fractal order moments are transformed into linear combinations of integer order moment. By doing so, all the moments including fractal moments are closed within this Biv-TEMOM model scheme. In the realization of Objective 5.2.2, the Bivariate TEMOM (Biv-TEMOM/BTEMOMs) model scheme with consideration of both size and fractal dimension of fractal-like soot aggregates is newly developed and coupled with large eddy simulation (LES) method as well as the detailed combustion chemistry and soot formation model. The influence of turbulent fluctuation due to the filter solution on the dynamics of fractal-like agglomerates is studied when the specific turbulence model (i.e., large eddy simulation (LES) model) is used. By using the LES method, the fluid flow is considered as two parts: the first part is the large-scale structure, which is significantly affected by the turbulence, and the other consists of a small-scale isotropic structure. The sub-grid size is modeled by using the Smagorinsky-Lily model. As a priori step towards the establishment of the novel truly coupled CFD-Biv-TEMOM model scheme, the TEMOM model scheme is coupled with computational fluid dynamics (CFD), which verifies the feasibility of coupling the TEMOM model scheme with different turbulence models including a standard k–ε Reynolds averaged Navier Stokes (RANS) and LES models. In order to realize true coupling between the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and the agglomerate dynamics, the general dynamics equations (GDEs) accounting for characterizing the evolution of particle dynamics is also filtered when coupled with the LES method. On the basis of the Smoluchowski mean-field theory, the transport equation of moments is derived. In the present study, the constitutive law for post-collisional fractal dimension in literature is used to further account for the fractal dimension evolution of fractal-like soot aggregates. This formalism is also used to describe the evolution of size and morphology of flame soot aggregate by other researchers. After some modifications in order to reflect the assumptions and limitations of the measurement technique, the modified constitutive law for post-collisional fractal dimension of soot aggregates is then derived. As a result, the truly coupled CFD-Biv-TEMOM model scheme (i.e., the called CFD-BTEMOMs model scheme in the proposal) is finally developed and established. In realization of Objective 5.2.3, the formulated CFD-Biv-TEMOM/CFD-BTEMOMs model scheme coupled with large eddy simulation (LES) method and soot formation model is used to simulate the effect of high turbulence and large temperature gradient on the transport mechanism of fractal-like soot aggregate dynamics in turbulent premixed flames. The characteristics of multi-scale agglomerate synthesis in turbulent combustion flows including spatial and temporal distribution and transportation profiles of fractal-like soot aggregates are studied with varying Reynolds number and fuel composition, which is aimed to provide flames with different turbulence and temperature gradients. Fuel composition is varied by changing the ratio of hydrogen and methane addition to the premixed fuel-oxidant gas mixture (i.e., ethylene-oxygen). A better understanding of the fundamentals of transport mechanism of fractal-like aggregates in turbulent and high temperature gradient environments are obtained via numerical simulations with the CFD-Biv-TEMOM model scheme and experimental measurements. In realization of Objective 5.2.4, the soot aggregate dynamics of turbulent ethylene-oxygen flame is numerically studied for different equivalence ratios and jet Reynolds numbers. Our well-developed TEMOM model in our previous research studies is further extended to solve the bivariate PBE and formulate the novel Bivariate TEMOM (Biv-TEMOM/BTEMOMs) model scheme. Full numerical validations are performed with the stochastically weighted operator splitting Monte Carlo method and moving sectional method, the Biv-TEMOM model scheme coupled with large eddy simulation (LES) method and soot formation model is used to simulate fractal-like soot aggregate dynamics in turbulent ethylene-oxygen flame. The extended flamelet/progress variable (EFPV) approach is used to simulate gas phase flame model. In order to model soot particles evolving from spherical to fractal shape, the simultaneous nucleation of primary particles, coagulation between primary and fractal particles, and the surface growth processes are considered in the present study. The multi-scale agglomerate synthesis i.e., formation and subsequent growth in turbulent combustion flows is obtained and compared with the highly reliable existing experimental datasets and other numerical method available from the literature with excellent agreement. A deeper insight into the formation and evolution mechanisms of fractal-like aggregates in turbulent combustion flows is provided with the formulated novel CFD-Biv-TEMOM model scheme coupled with large eddy simulation (LES) method and soot formation model. This coupled novel model scheme provides a simple but an accurate and efficient method for studying formation and transport fundamentals of fractal-like aggregates in highly turbulent combustion flows with highly varying temperature gradient. In summary, by establishing the bivariate TEMOM (Biv-TEMOM) model scheme (i.e., the called BTEMOMs model scheme in the proposal) and then couples it with the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) as well as particle and turbulence models, a novel truly coupled CFD-Biv-TEMOM model scheme (i.e., the called CFD-BTEMOMs model scheme in the proposal) is formulated and validated with the highly reliable existing experimental datasets and other numerical method available from the literature. By applying this novel model scheme to studying highly turbulent combustion flows with highly varying temperature gradient, a better and deeper insight into the formation and transport fundamentals of fractal-like aggregates is provided. The developed numerical model also provides highly robust tool for studying complex combustion flows and multi-scale agglomerate synthesis. The listed Revised Objectives in Section 5.2 of this funded project are completely achieved.

15212515.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212515.value: As a priori step towards the establishment of the novel CFD-Bivariate TEMOM model scheme, the Taylor-series expansion method of moments(TEMOM) model scheme is coupled with large eddy simulation(LES) and standard k–ε Reynolds averaged Navier Stokes(RANS) models, respectively. This coupled CFD-TEMOM numerical model provides a simple but an accurate and efficient method, and important coupling strategy between the TEMOM and different turbulence models. This major findings can be referred to the published journal paper in Particuology (2019) in Part C: Research Output. The Bivariate TEMOM model scheme coupled with LES method and soot formation model is used to simulate fractal-like aggregate dynamics in turbulent ethylene-oxygen flame. The increase of equivalence ratio results in more uniform particle size distributions(PSDs) but narrower and higher fractal dimension distributions(FDDs) of soot particles. However, the increase of jet Reynolds number results in higher and broader PSDs but broader and lower FDDs. The results reveal that both coagulation and nucleation rates have similar distribution patterns. Similar distribution patterns can also be observed for the soot surface growth rate and total volume fraction of soot particles. These results show that the mixing of soot precursors and soot particles becomes the dominant factor in the present highly turbulent combustion flows. This novel model scheme can solve bivariate PBE with high robustness and can provide a deeper insight into the formation and evolution mechanisms of fractal-like aggregates in turbulent ethylene-oxygen flame. The above major findings can be referred to the published paper in the top-tier journal of Fuel (2019) in Part C: Research Output. Another journal paper on the consolidated significant research findings is under preparation, the fractal-like soot dynamics of premixed methane-ethylene-oxygen flames is studied experimentally and numerically for different hydrogen addition ratio and volume fraction of methane in the hydrocarbon fuels. The results show that hydrogen addition to the mixed hydrocarbon fuel increases flame temperature. Particle formation and aggregation processes are inhibited by the increasing hydrogen content. The total soot particle concentration is lowered with increasing methane addition while the distribution patterns of soot particle diameter and fractal dimension is only slightly affected. It can also be found that the inhibiting effect of hydrogen addition on soot formation is quickly weakened with increasing methane addition. The results suggest that the addition of both hydrogen and methane to ethylene can reduce soot emissions but the effects of adding hydrogen and methane are not synergetic in the present study.

15212515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212515.value: The major findings and established methodologies obtained from this funded project can be further developed and widely used in the context of multi-scale synthesis and manufacturing technology with great scientific value and the potential of becoming an important method for multi-scale agglomerate synthesis, functional nanoparticles and nano-assemblies (e.g., nano-scale motors or robots). The proposed course of action is as follows: (i) To optimize and extend applications of the developed novel model scheme by establishing multi-scale coupling strategy, which can be used to handle multi-scale systems (e.g., fuel cells, photo-voltaic catalysts); (ii) To increase the computational efficiency by developing parallel computing algorithm under high-performance computing facilities. To achieve this purpose, it is necessary to modify and transform the model scheme into various connected sub-modules; With higher computational efficiency, it is possible to obtain better control and prediction of high-quality particles for potential scientific and industrial applications; and (iii) To further develop a potential commercial software for complex reacting particle-laden flows with multi-scale characteristics based on the developed model schemes and codes. The interface and package are necessary steps for developing such commercial softwares with the developed software, researchers can obtain a better control and design of products (e.g. functional nanoparticles, photovoltaic catalysts).

15212515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212515.value: Basically, this research project is fundamental research and of importance in developing efficient and accurate numerical models to account for complex physical phenomena of combustion flows, nanoparticle technology etc. in both scientific and engineering fields. This novel numerical model scheme can find wide and significant applications in complex reacting systems such as combustion flames, chemical reactors etc. The main significance of this research project lies in three aspects. Firstly, it greatly improves the efficiency of the current moment methods in simulating multi-scale agglomerate synthesis, particularly in the solution of particle transport equations by using a well-established mathematical method, i.e., Taylor-series expansion method, which makes it easier to resolving the moment equations with fractal orders. Secondly, the research method realizes the true coupling between particle method and computational fluid dynamics under different turbulence models. Thirdly, the behavior of fractal-like aggregates under extreme conditions such as high turbulence and high temperature gradient is accurately captured and described. The results provide deeper insight into the formation and evolution of fractal-like aggregates, which is of significance in many areas including the reduction and control of particulate emission, study of multi-phase flow with fractal-like particles and product quality control of functional particle synthesis.

15213215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213215.value: Most high-frequency ground penetrating radar (GPR) applications aim at large-scale positioning and mapping of embedded objects in engineering structures (bridges, buildings, buried pipes, etc). But condition assessment and diagnosis of construction materials and structures are scarce. Such assessment and diagnosis will be attempted by developing GPR as a spectral analyzer to characterize the tale-tell signs of chloride and water seepage in concrete and pipe burst in soil. All these problems contribute to the deterioration of 3000km long water mains, 1977km long roads, 7000 buildings and other infrastructures in Hong Kong, and also worldwide. The proposed methodology will make use of a hybrid GPR and time-frequency spectral measurement to measure the complex dielectric permittivity of dielectric construction materials as a function of GPR frequency. The method will be validated by genuine measurement of the absolute spectral value through small-scale complex dielectric permittivity using coaxial transmission line (CTL). It is necessary because the success of the hybrid method is dependent on hardware, such as types of instrumentation; as well as processing algorithms, such as window size, filter, resolution limits, etc. These uncertainties render relative but not absolute spectral information. Validation by CTL is thus required to reflect the actual polarization and absorption mechanisms which are essential to the understanding of material properties. Concrete and soil, as two important dielectric construction materials, will be the tested media for the method development. Water and chloride will be added to concrete to simulate chloride-induced contamination that causes steel corrosion, and pipe in soil will be burst to simulate underground water leak. Associated changes of peak frequencies, bandwidth and relaxation frequency in both GPR and CTL will be compared. Once empirical relationships between the hybrid and the CTL-based methods are established, signal processing parameters will be optimized and models will be formulated to deduce the genuine polarization and absorption mechanisms using GPR, as a way forward to turn GPR as a large-scale spectral analyzer. The deliverables will have long term scientific and practical impacts. The scientific side refers to (1) optimization of parameters in various time-frequency algorithms; (2) formulation of models between GPR and CTL’s spectral frequency-dependent behavior of dielectric permittivity over 400-2600MHz (as normal GPR frequency range) for large-scale mapping of spectral contents. The practical side will establish the hybrid method as an efficient tool to characterize and diagnose the aging problems of engineering infrastructures. 大多數的高頻率探地雷達 (GPR) 主要應用於對工程結構(如橋樑、 建築物、 地下管道等)中的內嵌物件的大規模定位檢測。但絕少小應用於材料的測量和診斷檢驗施工材料。這種診斷將試圖利用探地雷達作為頻譜分析儀來表徵混凝土和水管爆裂在土壤中的氯和滲水的特徵。所有這些問題都在本港 3000 公里長的水管，1977 公里長的公路、 7000橦建築和其他基礎設施持續惡化, 同樣問題及至世界各地。 擬議的方案將混合使用探地雷達與時頻光譜測量來量度介質建築材料中複數介電常數作為探地雷達頻率的函數。該方法將通過使用小型同軸傳輸線 (CTL)測量真正絕對光譜值的複數介電常數來作驗證。這類驗證是必要的,因為成功的混合方法是依賴于硬體，如儀器的類型;以及處理演算法、如視窗大小、 篩選器濾波方法、 解析度限制等。這些不確定性只呈現相對的而不是絕對的光譜資訊。因此需要以CTL驗證來反映實際極化和吸收機制以研究材料的性質。 為發展擬議的方法, 研究將會以兩個重要的介電建築材料-混凝土和土壤作為測試的媒體。水和氯將添加到混凝土來模擬氯污染引起的鋼筋腐蝕和土壤中的管道破裂來類比地下漏水。研究將比較在探地雷達和 CTL的峰值頻率、 頻寬和張弛頻率的變化。一旦建立了混合方法和基於CTL的方法之間的經驗關係之後，便可以從優化改良信號處理參數和模型來推斷以探地雷達作為一種大型的頻譜分析儀去測量材料真正的兩極分化特性和材料水分的吸收機制。 研究結果將具有長遠的理論和實踐的影響。理論方面指的是 (1) 改良優化在不同的時間-頻率演算法的參數;(2) 制定在400-2600MHz兆之探地雷達 (作為正常一般的探地雷達頻率範圍) 和 CTL之間介電常數的光譜頻率依賴行為的模型以便作大規模檢測光譜內容之間介電常數的光譜特性,以便作大規模建築材料的檢測。在實用層面上，這混合方法將發展成一種高效的工具用以作為分類及診斷基建的老化問題。

15213215.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213215.value: Velocity dispersion of ground penetrating radar wave at different bandwidths is successfully measured via spectral analysis of surface wave (SASW). Effective bandwidths in different cases are successfully recognized with time-frequency analysis (TFA) to limit the upper and lower bound of spectral behaviour. The measurement makes the major aim of the project 'Turning GPR as a spectral analyzer tool' successfully fulfilled. The combination of GPR-SASW and GPR-TFA methodology was then fully validated with a series of plywood and concrete specimens in the labs in both Hong Kong and Germany. Findings can be realized in two focuses: 1. The parameters of the hardware setup of GPR-SASW is confirmed as follows: (a) The two acquired non-stationary GPR direct waves shall include one full wavelength (λ); (2) Distance between the two GPR direct waves is optimized as 3/4 λ. Distance less than this would create false velocity measurement at low frequency regime. Distance more than this would make the second direct waves not recognizable due to large attenuation, 2. In the dispersion curve, the following phenomena are observed in all specimens in general: (a) the wave velocity was largely reduced at all frequencies after increase of moisture content, and vice versa; (b) the velocity at lower frequency part suffered larger reduction than others, 3. The coaxial transmission line (CXL) suggested in the objective is replaced by numerical simulation because the dielectric behaviour of small cells in CXL does not adequately reflect that of the large specimens studied by GPR. Simulation making use of FDTD (finite difference time domain) was used for this purpose to create the dispersion curve in both real and imaginary part of permittivity, 4. Water leakage is clearly observed in four leak points in a test site of buried ductile iron pipe paved with concrete and paving blocks (Cheung and Lai et al. 2019), and 5. GPR E-field, perpendicular to the traverse direction, and the orientation of any linear buried objects, pose a significant effects on the wave velocity measurements, and can be corrected by a correction factor which is a sine of the oblique angle of the E-field and object orientation (Xie et al. 2018).

15213215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213215.value: Material damages evolve at the invisible shallow subsurface and continuously develop and remain un-noticed most of the time. GPR images obtained in common offset GPR imaging give mostly the location of objects rather than evaluation of material properties, especially water content/leakage. Dispersion is used to be regarded as a drawback in GPR data analysis. But it is used in this work to differentiate various phase velocities at different frequencies. It is useful not only for understanding the underlying physics of wave travel in materials, but also evaluating material properties in spatial domain. The development of GPR-WARR and GPR-TFA methodology attempts to solve few problems in next stage of research. For example, at which frequency bandwidth the GPR wave velocity in concrete and pavement structures be decelerated most? Which frequency bandwidth remains unaffected and least affected? How can the result be used as a fingerprint to study material damages like cracks and water seepage? Does the recommended 3/4 λ rule work in other GPR frequency bandwidths? This work paves the way of (1) transforming the GPR physics to applied engineering applications, and (2) building up essential configuration of GPR spectral analyzer for large-scale characterization of material properties in infrastructures.

15213215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213215.value: Majority of ground penetrating radar (GPR) applications aim at “seeing the unseen” or locating objects in engineering structures (bridges, buildings, buried pipes, etc). But GPR diagnosis about material properties and damages of the surface are relatively scarce. These tasks are traditionally conducted by two antennas with fixed distance between one transmitter (Tx) and one receiver (Rx). In this project, these tasks are studied by variable Tx-Rx distance via wide angle reflection and refraction (WARR), and velocity’s dispersive behavior of GPR direct wave. Algorithms of seismic SASW were adopted in GPR to measure the dispersion curve of GPR wave. This project successfully establishes and validate procedures to measure phase velocity dispersion through GPR-WARR and GPR-SASW. Through successfully achieving this aim of the project, dispersion analysis for large-scale material characterization, including water content variation/water leakage in infrastructure is no longer a far-reaching goal in the future.

15213915.value: 基於雲模式和實際雷電觀測的雷暴雲中水凝物動力對雷電形成的影響的研究

15213915.label: Project Objectives
15213915.value: Cloud model modification and coding--: In collaboration with the Chinese Academy of Meteorological Sciences (CAMS), we have established a 3D model dedicated to hydrometeor research in individual thundercloud. Modification and coding of the model will be done so that it is suitable for researches of hydrometeor dynamics and electrification in a particular thundercloud in high spatial and temporal resolutions. Sounding data of air pressure, wind, temperature and dew temperature will be used as the background and boundary conditions of the model. An artificial hot and humid bubble will be assumed to initiate the growth of a convective cloud cell. Electrification scheme setup and its insertion into the cloud model--: The cloud model includes many microphysical processes such as the melting, sublimation and latent heat release and many species of hydrometeors such as the cloud drop, ice, graupel, hail and raindrop. Based on these, the non-inductive charge process due to collision of ice and graupel, the inductive charge process due to collision of cloud drop and graupel, and the charge process in ice multiplication will be added into the cloud model to simulate the cloud electrification process. Moreover, charge transfers in convection, advection and phase changes will be also taken into account. Lightning initiation scheme setup and its implementation in the cloud model--: Experiments show that although the air breakdown electric field under normal air conditions is as high as 750 kV/m for negative and 500 kV/m for positive breakdowns, it may change significantly with the air pressure and moisture. Especially in a convective cloud, the pressure and moisture in different parts of the cloud could be much different and the breakdown electric field in certain parts of the cloud could be low enough to initiate a lightning discharge. Based on this, a new lightning initiation scheme as a function of the air pressure, moisture and temperature will be proposed and inserted into the cloud model to simulate lightning discharges. Modelling validation with observations--: With a properly planned lightning observation system, lightning discharges occurred during a thunderstorm can be well-recorded. Meanwhile, with the sounding data associated to the same thunderstorm and the proposed lightning initiation scheme, the model can output a set of lightning discharges. Comparisons of the signatures of simulated and recorded lightning discharges can help to verify whether the proposed lightning initiation scheme is correct. Understanding of how a lightning discharge occurs in a cloud--: The observations and modeling can be done for various thunderclouds. Once a presumed lightning discharge scheme is proven, the model outputs can be used to analyze the relationships between the air flows, hydrometeors, charges, breakdown electric fields and lightning discharges.

15213915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213915.value: 雷暴雲以及與之相關聯的雷電對地球上的生命財產造成各種損害。研究雷電是如何形成是雷電物理和雷電預警的重要方面。通常雷暴雲中有兩種放電形式：地閃（雲對地放電）和雲閃（雲對雲放電）。最近，一種所謂袖珍雲閃的放電模式也愈發清晰。現有的雷電探測技術可以給出雲內放電的空間時間座標，但如果想要得到每次放電對應的雲內電場還是有困難的。和雷電事件相比，目前的雲遙感技術給出的雷暴雲中氣流和水凝物的時空解析度還偏低。另外，根據僅有的一些觀測和理論模擬，雲內電場強度很少能夠到達實驗室測量到的擊穿強度。所有這些使得理解雷電具體的形成過程存難度。一種較爲普遍的假想的雷電起始過程是所謂的電子逃逸機制，根據這個機制，雷電起始臨界電場可以降低到和觀測相一致的範圍，但並沒有進一步的證據表明這個理論可以適用於所有的雷電放電過程。另一方面，實驗表明，雖然在通常情況下正負擊穿的臨界電場分別高達500 kV/m 和750 kV/m，但當氣壓和濕度改變時，它們卻會有大幅度的變化。尤其在對流雲內，不同位置的氣壓和濕度都有顯著的不同，以至於在特定的區域臨界擊穿電場可以低得引起放電發生。因此，本項目的目標是通過模擬和觀測來研究氣流和水凝物對雷電起始過程的影響。此雲模式可以模擬雲中的氣流，水凝物以及電荷形成情況。對於一個特定的雷暴雲，給定雷電起始條件，該模式可以輸出放電的位置，時間和類型。這些結果可以與真實觀測到的同一塊雷暴雲比對從而驗證之前給出的雷電起始條件。方案成功後，可以解答雷暴雲中雷電是如何，為何以及在哪發生。

15213915.label: Realisation of objectives
15213915.value: The main purpose of this project is to investigate on how the in-cloud air flows and hydro-meteors affect the lightning initiations based on cloud modelling and lightning observations. There are 6 core tasks: (1) To choose a suitable cloud model and make modification of it so that it can reflect the relationship of hydro-meteors dynamics and electrification in a particular thundercloud in high spatial and temporal resolutions; (2) To establish a new lightning initiation scheme as a function of the air pressure, moisture and temperature and to insert it into the cloud model for simulating lightning discharges; (3) To carry out field observations of specific thunderstorms, take records of whole lightning activities as well as the sounding data associated to the same thunderstorms; (4) To implement the cloud model with the associated sounding data and the proposed lightning initiation scheme, compare the signatures of the modeled and recorded lightning activities, which can help to verify whether the proposed lightning initiation scheme is correct; and (5) to understand the relationships between the air flows, hydro-meteors, charges, breakdown electric fields and lightning discharges by analyzing the model and observation results. To achieve these tasks, starting from January of 2016 to the end of June, 2019, we have been carried our continuously field observations and numerous lightning data have been obtained and analyzed with the proposed model. Firstly, for the cloud model, we have selected and established an adequate cloud dynamic and electrification model. We have chosen the cloud model developed by the Chinese Academy of Meteorological Sciences (CAMS) for hydro-meteor research in a single storm. In the model, the vertical space is divided into 40 levels with a resolution of 500 m and the horizontal space is divided into 76×76 grids with a resolution of 1 km, which are adjustable depends on needs. The time step can be set to 1 second or more. Sounding data of air pressure, wind, temperature and dew temperature are used for the original field and boundary conditions of the model. An artificial hot and humid bubble will be used to initiate a convective cell when the simulation starts. A typical value for the turbulent temperature and moisture of the hot and humid bubble is 6℃ and 80% respectively. The model includes 26 various micro-physical processes, such as the melting, sublimation and latent heat release etc. With this effort, we have achieved 80% of Tasks (1) and 20% of Tasks (2) Secondarily, for the hydro-meteor electrification, three charging processes are considered: the inductive charging process of the collisions between cloud drops and graupels /hails, the non-inductive charging process of the collision between ices and graupels/hails, and the charging process in ice multiplication. For lightning initiation, two different lightning initiation schemes have been examined. The first one is the traditional scheme which assume that the critical electric breakdown value is a function of altitude. The second one is a new scheme which assume that the critical electric breakdown value is a function of the air pressure, density and temperature in the cloud. By applying the two schemes to a set of sounding data got before a thunderstorm, the cloud dynamics, electrification and lightning flash occurrence were simulated. The results suggest that the second lightning initiation scheme more reasonable in comparison with observations in literature. With this effort, we have achieved 100% of Tasks (1) and (2), and 50% of Tasks (3) & (4). The above results have been summarized in manuscript titled “Possible impacts of thundercloud dynamics on the lightning initiation based on cloud simulation”, which is ready to submit to a journal. Thirdly, we have investigated the property of inter-event time of lightning flash sequence during the whole life of a severe thunderstorm. By using the data of Lightning Detection and Ranging (LDAR) system at the Kennedy Space Center, the temporal fractal and related correlation behaviors of lightning flash sequences were investigated with the Allan factor (AF) and Fano factor (FF) scaling methods. For the 86 thunderstorms analyzed, all of which involved the stage of rapid increase of 2-minute total flash rate, apparent time-scaling behaviors have been identified. The results suggest that the lightning flash sequences in thunderstorms are possibly a self-organized and cooperative behavior, which may be closely related to the thunderstorm dynamics. The results are published in the paper “Time-correlations of Lightning Flash Sequences in Thunderstorms”, Journal of Geophysical Research - Atmosphere, 123, Jan 2018, https://doi.org/10.1002/2017JD027206. By this effort, we have achieved 100% of Task (3), 80% of Task (4) and 20 % of Task (5). Fourthly, based on a variety of field observation data of inception thresholds and propagation properties of long gap spark discharges, we have found that the step-wise positive leader may be re-strikes due to temporary instability of a continuous positive leader, while the intermittency of negative leader manifests not only a relatively regular stepped leader but also a more erratic negative recoil leader. We further found that the positive leader-streamer may play a unique role in igniting all kinds of intermittent events in lightning, including the initiation of lightning with the fast positive streamer, the formation of space leader in front of a negative stepped leader with the secondary positive streamer, and the reformation of recoil-leader in an instability leader channel due to its low threshold of inception and propagation. We also discussed the self-adjustable ability of a bidirectional leader, suggesting that the potential drop along the streamer channel in front of the leader tip may be an important factor for stabilizing the bidirectional leader. The results were published in the paper “Theory and observation of bidirectional leader of lightning: Polarity asymmetry, instability, and intermittency”, Acta Physica Sinica, Vol.67, No.20, 205201, July 2018, DOI: 10.7498/aps.67.20181079. With this effort, we have achieved 100 % of Task 4 and 50 % of Task 5. Lastly, based on observations with a very high frequency (VHF) broadband interferometer, we found that lightning initiation processes can be generally grouped into two distinct types. One is the previously reported fast positive breakdown (FPB), while the other one started with a kind of isolated short VHF pulses. We have analyzed 31 intra-cloud lightning flash initiation events during three thunderstorms at short range from the interferometer. These events separate into two distinct classes that can be identified based on the time scale and the occurrence contexts of the first detectable VHF emissions from the flash. One class has features completely consistent with previously reported FPB events and is associated with continuous VHF emissions of 10–20 μs duration. But the majority of the lightning flashes analyzed began with ultrashort, sub-microsecond duration, isolated pulses of VHF emission with no identifiable FPB signatures between these pulses and the leader development. The results were presented at the 11th Asia-Pacific International Conference on Lightning, June 12-14, 2019, Hong Kong, China . With this effort, we have achieved 100% of Task 5.

15213915.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213915.value: Firstly, by using the data of Lightning Detection and Ranging (LDAR) system at the Kennedy Space Center, the temporal fractal and related correlation behaviors of lightning flash sequences were investigated with the Allan factor (AF) and Fano factor (FF) scaling methods. The results suggest that the lightning flash sequences in thunderstorms are possibly a self-organized and cooperative behavior, which may be closely related to the thunderstorm dynamics (Ref.: Journal paper No.1 in Part C, doi: 10.1002/2017JD027206). Secondly, based on a variety of field observation data of inception thresholds and propagation properties of long gap spark discharges, we proposed that the step-wise positive leader may be re-strikes due to temporary instability of a continuous positive leader, while the intermittency of negative leader manifests not only a relatively regular stepped leader but also a more erratic negative recoil leader. The positive leader-streamer may play a unique role in igniting all kinds of intermittent events in lightning, including the formation of the fast positive streamer, the space leader in front of a negative leader, and the recoil-leader in an instability leader channel. (Ref.: Journal paper No.2 in part C, doi: 10.7498/aps.67.20181079) Thirdly, based on very high frequency (VHF) broadband interferometer observations, we found that lightning initiation processes can be generally grouped into two distinct types. One is the previously reported fast positive breakdown (FPB), while the other one started with a kind of isolated short VHF pulses. We suggest that the FPB process is responsible for initiating some but not all lightning flashes, and the extremely short pulse - like VHF emissions play a role in initiating those flashes without any FPB process (Ref.: Conference Paper No. 1 in Part C). Fourthly, applying two different lightning initiation schemes (one is the traditional scheme which assume that the critical electric breakdown value is a function of altitude, one is a new scheme which assume that the critical electric breakdown value is a function of the air pressure, density and temperature of the cloud) in the cloud model we established, the cloud dynamics, electrification and lightning flash occurrence were simulated. The results suggested that the new lightning initiation scheme more reasonable in comparison with observations (Ref.: the paper under preparation in Part C).

15213915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213915.value: By this project, we have demonstrated an approach for investigating the relationship between the lightning activity and the thundercloud dynamics via both the theoretical modeling and the field observation. For the modeling, one can theoretically link the preset lightning initiation condition and the resulted lightning activity property with the cloud hydro-meteor and dynamics during the life-cycle of a thundercloud. For the field observation, one can statistically analyze the lightning initiation and activity properties against the thundercloud development. Combination and application of these two methods to a specific thundercloud will be an effective way for understanding the mechanism of the lightning initiation and its association with the cloud dynamics. Therefore, a coordinated modeling and field observation of a specific thunderstorm is a potential research direction that has significant scientific meanings in the area of cloud dynamics and lightning initiation.

15213915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213915.value: Lightning causes huge losses of life and property of human beings on Earth every year. Most lightning discharges start with a so-called preliminary breakdown process inside the cloud due to the strong local electric field established by electrification of cloud hydro-meteors. So it is the hydro-meteor dynamics that results in the lightning discharges. However, we have no mean to observe directly how the cloud hydro-meteors and the lightning discharges evolve inside a cloud. Therefore, we have no mean to understand the lightning initiation condition and its relations to the cloud hydro-meteor dynamics. In this project, we have proposed an approach for investigating the relationship between the lightning activity and the thundercloud dynamics via either a thundercloud model or a field observation. With the model, one can investigate theoretically the relationship between and the lightning activity and the thundercloud hydro-meteors with a preset lightning initiation condition during the life-cycle of a thundercloud. For the field observation, we demonstrated three statistical studies of the lightning initiation and activity properties versus the thundercloud development stages. Application of these two methods to the same thundercloud could be the most effective way for understanding the mechanism of lightning initiation inside a thundercloud.

15214415.label: Realisation of objectives
15214415.value: 1. Fiber laser designs: In this project, we investigated a number of laser configurations starting from those discussed in the project proposal. We simulated the laser operation for each laser configuration studied. We found that the laser performance depends critically on the performance of individual elements in the laser cavity. Thus, we focused on the optimization of individual laser components. (i) Dispersion and nonlinearity varying optical fibers Similaritons preserve their shapes during propagation. Classic chirp-free solitons in uniform anomalous dispersive media is the simplest example of similaritons. In media with slowly varying anomalous dispersion, solitons can still preserve the hyperbolic secant pulse shape while its pulse parameters evolve adiabatically to satisfy the soliton condition. Self-similar propagation of chirped solitons is also found in short tapered media with varying anomalous dispersion or nonlinearity. Our previous work showed that dispersion decreasing fibers are difficult to design and fabricate. We have also shown that nonlinearity varying fiber with large mode area fibers are feasible. Photonic crystal fiber (PCF) is a mature platform. Endless single mode, large mode area, dispersion and nonlinearity engineering can be achieved by controlling the core and cladding structures. Thus in this project, we investigated the design and fabrication of both nonlinearity increasing PCF tapers and dispersion decreasing for self-similar pulse propagation. We tried a number of PCF designs, and fabrications. As a demonstration, we designed a tapered tellurite photonic crystal fiber (TTPCF) with nonlinear coefficient increasing along the propagation direction. Comparatively unchanged dispersion is designed to achieve the self-similar pulse compression of the fundamental soliton. When the variation of group velocity dispersion, high order dispersion, and high order nonlinearity are considered, simulation results show that a 1-ps pulse at wavelength 2.5 μm can be self-similarly compressed to 62.16 fs, along with negligible pedestal. We then designed another uniform tellurite PCF for the supercontinuum generation. We launch the 1-ps pulse and the compressed 62.16 fs pulse into the uniform tellurite PCF, separately. We found that the coherence of the supercontinuum generated with the compressed pulse is enhanced significantly when compared to that generated with the 1-ps pulse, and highly coherent and octave spanning supercontinuum can be obtained. (ii) Chirp reversal elements, mode-locking mechanisms, and gain fibers A readily available chirp reversal element is an optical fiber working in the linear regime. One of the key disadvantages of using optical fibers for chirp reversal is higher order dispersions which will become important when the pulse width narrows. It is also a challenge to keep the optical fibers to function in the linear regime as the pulse peak power increases when the similaritons propagate. Thus we studied the perturbations introduced by the optical fibers during the chirp reversal process by simulations. From prior experience of the investigation team, we have chosen nonlinear polarization as the mode-locking mechanism. For the gain profile, theoretically we have chosen the flat gain in the model and for simplicity. (iii) Impact of spectral filtering on multi-pulsing instability The impact of spectral filtering on mode-locked fiber lasers is well known. When a narrow-band spectral filter is used in a normally dispersive fiber cavity, self-similar pulse propagation in the gain fiber greatly enhances the pulse quality, but with spectral filtering remaining a trigger for the multi-pulsing instability. The pulse evolution in an anomalously dispersive fiber laser cavity is more complex. Periodic and chaotic dynamics are observed in addition to the multi-pulsing transition. In such cavities, the saturable absorber narrows the pulse and hence broadens its spectrum. Thus the spectrally broadened pulse is narrowed by the action of the spectral filter. So in addition to balancing the effects of anomalous dispersion and self-phase modulation, the mode-locked pulse must also balance the physics of saturable absorber and spectral filter. Thus any theoretical model must account for both the balances of the soliton evolution and the dissipative spectral filtering action. 2. Theory and simulation: In this project, we investigated passive similariton propagation in both anomalous and normal dispersion regimes. Normal dispersive media do not support soliton propagation, but chirped parabolic pulses can experience self-similar propagation in amplified or parameters varying media. Unlike the solitons in anomalous dispersion regime which are formed only beyond a certain power threshold, the generation of parabolic similaritons is not sensitive to the power, shape, and phase profile of the initial pulses. In normal dispersive fibers with constant gain coefficients, parabolic similaritons are asymptotic solutions of the systems, which means a pulse propagating in such fibers will eventually evolve to a parabolic similariton. Generation of parabolic pulses based on asymptotic evolutions have been successfully demonstrated in rare-earth doped fiber amplifiers, and nonlinear amplifiers such as Raman amplifiers. One of the main advantages of parabolic similaritons is that they will not experience wave breaking which is the major limitation of high power optical pulses propagating in normal dispersive media. However, the use of amplifiers will increase the system complexity and inevitably introduce amplified spontaneous emission noise into the pulses. Passive parabolic pulse generation has also been demonstrated in dispersion decreasing fibers. Thus, we investigated theoretically the passive generation of parabolic similaritons in nonlinear tapered waveguides. We developed a novel nonlinearity increasing scheme in the normal dispersion regime based on self-similar theory. We studied parabolic pulse generation at the telecom (λ~1550 nm) and mid-IR (λ≥2100 nm) wavelengths. We then compared the pros and cons of dispersion decreasing waveguides (DDWs) and nonlinearity increasing waveguides (NIWs) for parabolic pulse generation. The taper profiles for DDWs and NIWs are designed using the finite element characterization of the waveguides. The dynamics of parabolic pulse generation in both types of tapers are investigated by considering the higher-order effects and loss in the waveguide tapers. To study the effect of spectral filter on mode-locked laser, we extended a geometrical laser model recently developed by the PI to include the pulse shaping effects of chromatic dispersion and self-phase modulation. In particular, we explicitly characterize the filtering action imposed by the bandpass filter in the cavity. We show that the extended geometrical model is well suited for systematically investigating the nonlinear dynamics of the pulse evolution which includes multi-pulsing, periodic and chaotic states and single pulse high-energy transition in mode-locked fiber laser cavities. 3. Connecting it all together: Theory, simulations, fabrication, characterization, and experiments have been utilized throughout the project. We fabricated the nonlinearity increasing PCFs in house. We characterized the fiber tapers fabricated, and constructed a number of similariton lasers. The performance of the lasers were investigated. We studied the individual laser components, particularly the in-house fabricated nonlinear fiber tapers and the chirp reversal elements carefully. We found that it is difficult to optimize the overall laser performance with all the variables involved in the different configurations of the similariton lasers.

15214415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214415.value: i) We investigated theoretically the passive generation of parabolic similaritons in nonlinear tapered waveguides. We developed a novel nonlinearity increasing scheme in the normal dispersion regime based on self-similar theory. We studied parabolic pulse generation at the telecom (λ~1550 nm) and mid-IR (λ≥2100 nm) wavelengths. We then studied both dispersion decreasing waveguides and nonlinearity increasing waveguides for parabolic pulse generation. (Outputs 8.1 and 9.1). ii) We design a simple inversely tapered silicon ridge waveguide with exponentially decreasing dispersion profile along the propagation direction, and numerically investigate self-similar pulse compression within the mid-infrared spectral region. By using the extended nonlinear Schrödinger equation, we demonstrated that a 1-ps input pulse at the wavelength of 2490 nm is successfully compressed to 57.29 fs in only 5.1-cm of propagation, along with a compression factor of 17.46. (Output 8.2) We also designed a tapered tellurite photonic crystal fiber with nonlinear coefficient increasing along the propagation direction, and demonstrate the mid-infrared self-similar pulse compression of the fundamental soliton. We demonstrated that a 1-ps pulse at wavelength 2.5 micron can be compressed to 62.16 fs after a 1.63-m long propagation, along with the negligible pedestal, compression factor of 16.09, and quality factor of 83.16%. The work was carried out by Dr. Li Feng, a Research Fellow supported by this project. (Outputs 8.4 and 9.2) iii) We investigated the impact of spectral filtering in mode-locked fiber lasers by using an extended geometrical model. The iterative model, which includes gain, loss, and the pulse shaping effects of chromatic dispersion and self-phase modulation, is used to model the laser cavity dynamics. We showed that broadband pulses experience large losses from spectral filtering in the cavity, leading to a number of potential laser instabilities and outcomes such as multi-pulsing, periodic and chaotic states, or a single pulse which transits to a higher energy state. For narrow band spectral filtering, the laser dynamics is dominated by the gain-loss dynamics in the cavity which causes multi-pulsing. For broadband spectral filtering, the nonlinearity-induced spectral reshaping of the single pulse can lead to a discontinuous pulse energy transition that circumvents multi-pulsing. (Outputs 8.3, 8.6, 9.4, and 9.5) iv) We numerically demonstrate efficient spectral compression (SPC) of wavelength-shifting soliton in a chalcogenide strip waveguide. We demonstrated that the profiles of group-velocity dispersion and Kerr nonlinearity play key roles in determining SPC. The work was carried out by Dr. Li Feng, a Research Fellow supported by this project. (Outputs 8.5 and 9.3)

15214415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214415.value: In this project, we found that the laser performance depends critically on the performance of individual elements in the laser cavity. A key area of further development is the chirp reversal element. Optical fiber is a readily available chirp reversal element but it only works in the linear regime and for group velocity dispersion, but not with higher order dispersion, which will become important when the pulse width narrows. It is also a challenge to keep the optical fibers to function in the linear regime as the pulse peak power increases when the similaritons propagate. Other means of chirp reversal, such as chirped fiber gratings or even grating pairs are worth investigating. Another key area for further investigation is the mode-locking mechanism. In this project, we have chosen nonlinear polarization as the mode-locker. Other form of mode-locker such as semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors (SESAMs) and nonlinear optical loop mirrors (NOLMs) can be considered.

15214415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15214415.value: Laser is a technological enabler of diverse applications from optical fiber communications to eye surgery. Fiber lasers offer many advantages because of their compactness, ease of alignment, high efficiency, reduced thermal effect, and low cost. This project investigates self-similar propagation for fiber lasers to generate few cycle (duration <10 femtoseconds) pulses. Self-similar pulses (similaritons) undergo significant spectral “breathing” inside the laser cavity making it possible to overcome the bandwidth limitation of the fiber gain. Similariton can propagate in optical fibers if the fiber dispersion and nonlinearity coefficients vary in specifically prescribed manner. Thus the performance of a self-similar laser depends critically on the performance of individual elements in the laser cavity. We investigated theoretically the passive generation of parabolic similaritons in different types of nonlinear tapered waveguides. We studied both dispersion decreasing waveguides and nonlinearity increasing waveguides for parabolic pulse generation. We then investigated the impact of spectral filtering on the laser dynamics of mode-locked fiber lasers. Instabilities such as multi-pulsing and chaos will hamper the lasers to operate in the few cycle regime. We demonstrated that for broadband spectral filtering, the nonlinearity-induced spectral reshaping of the single pulse can lead to a discontinuous pulse energy transition that circumvents multi-pulsing.

15214515.value: To fabricate edge-contact field-effect transistors using 2D layered TMDs, consisting of seamlessly metallic-like and semiconducting phases in one single-crystalline TMD flake. 15214515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214515.value: 矽晶體管的尺寸不斷下降是納米電子學中的一個重要研究課題。這一趨勢要求導電溝道的長度和厚度減少以避免短溝道效應，具體來說厚度應該是長度的一小部分。最近的研究表明二維（2D）層狀過渡金屬硫化物（TMDs）可在大氣室溫的環境下穩定地存在。不像傳統的塊狀材料，這些獨特的二維材料沒有表面態或懸空鍵，有望用在下一代晶體管。此外，二維層狀材料有著很薄的厚度，使得其可以應用在三維集成器件中。 基於TMD的場效應晶體管已被成功地展示，但其測定的遷移率遠低於理論預測，這被歸因於二維TMD和三維金屬電極之間的高接觸電阻。為了使得基於TMD的場效應晶體管超越傳統的晶體管，我們提出通過TMD的相變以增加接觸區域的載流子濃度。基於第六族的（鉬，鎢）TMDs有兩個相：半導體（2H）相和金屬（1T）相。其半導體相可以通過原子層內平面滑行轉變為金屬相，這已經由鋰離子和鉀離子嵌入實驗證明。 在這項工作中，（1）我們將開發與微電子制造兼容的相變方法，將半導體的TMD將通過氫化而不是通過容易汙染的液體處理相變辦法。（2）我們將評估金屬電極和半導體TMD之間的邊緣接觸（共價鍵合）電阻。我們將利用這種辦法建立與n型和p型半導體TMDs低的 接觸電阻。（3）我們將堆疊的半導體TMD層和金屬TMD層一起以形成垂直異質結，並評估其側面接觸（範德瓦爾斯相互作用）電阻。基於TMD的垂直晶體管將被作為三維集成的一個展示，其中半導體和金屬TMDs之間的接觸阻擋將由背柵調制。

15214515.label: Realisation of objectives
15214515.value: 1. By engineering the contact region with copper (Cu)‐doped 2D materials, we demonstrate an n‐tpe carrie transpot in 2D materials field‐effect transistors (FETs). Cu metal atoms are found to severely penetrate into the 2D materials flakes, which forms interstitial Cu (Cuint)‐doped edge contact and facilitates the electron transport in 2D materials. The Schottky barrier height for electrons is relatively low because of the edge contact between Cu interstial dopd 2D materials and pristine 2D materials channel. The contact doping of 2D materials by highly mobile Cu atoms gives rise to n‐type transport property of 2D materials FETs. Furthermore, we demonstrate a p‐n junction on the same 2D materials flake with asymmetric contact. This study provides a stategy on contact engineering of 2D materials. In adition, we also develop a van der Waals contact to 2D materials by transferring metal electrodes to minimize the contact resistance to 2D semiconducting channel. 2. We construct the side-contact configuration between 2D semiconducting channel and metal electrode, which form a Schottky barrier. We can use this Schottky barrier to replace MOS type capacitor to modulate the channel resistance.

15214515.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214515.value: The major findings include (1) We find that highly diffusive Cu atom can penetrate into the body of 2D materials flake. The interstial Cu atom gives rise the transformation from semiconducting characteristics to metallic type, which enables to the seamless formation of metallic edge contact to semiconducting channel. (2) We also develop a technique that allows us to transfer metal electrode on top of the surface of metal electrode to form van der Waals type contact, which can reduce Fermi level pinning effect at contact region and greatly decrease the contact resistance. (3) By using the Schottky barrier between transferred metal electrode and 2D semiconducting material, we can modulate the barrier height and change the channel resistance. The major outputs include (1) We published over 10 journal papers, including Science Advances, Advanced Materials, ACS Nano, etc. We also present our results in conference, e.g., International Electron Device Meeting (IEDM). (2) We trained a MPhil student, Xu Kang. His thesis title is: Controllable doping and anisotropic properties of 2D materials. We also support one PhD student, Lejuan Cai.

15214515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214515.value: We develop a process technique that is compatible with conventional semiconductor processing. By using high diffusive metal electrode, we can realize the phase transformation of 2D materials from semiconducting to metallic characteristcs, which is a result of interstial doping of metal atom. We also develop a technique that allows us to transfer metal electrode on top surface of 2D semiconducting flake and form a van der Waals type contacct to decrease contact resistance.

15214515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15214515.value: Field effect transistor is the building block of the integraded circuit. As the feature size of the transistor continuses to scale down, conventional Si CMOS transistor face a significant challenges, which requires new materials to alleviate the short channel effect existing in Si transistor. Two-dimensional layered semiconductor is a promising semiconductor channel, but it suffers greatly from large contact resistance. In our work, we develop a technique that can transform semiconducting channel to metallic characteristics by doping the semiconductor channel with highly diffusive meatl at contact region, which can significantly decreases the contact resistance.

15214615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214615.value: Warm reclaimed asphalt (WRA) is an emerging green paving material that combines two sustainable paving technologies: warm mix asphalt (WMA) and reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP). The environmental benefits of WRA are significant: WMA reduces fuel consumption and carbon emission during construction, while RAP conserves natural resources during material production. In addition, lower production temperature of WMA facilitates the use of higher RAP contents. Hence, more material and cost savings can be realized. To ensure successful implementation of WRA, its performance shall surpass or at least equal to that of traditional hot mix asphalt (HMA). Therefore, many studies have been conducted to assess the performance of WRA. However, the focuses of these studies have been mainly on the bulk and macroscopic engineering properties of WRA. Unfortunately, the mechanism of the macroscopic properties remains unclear, resulting in inconsistent field performance of WRA. The main objective of this study is to investigate the interaction mechanism amongst the warm mix additive, virgin asphalt binder, and aged asphalt binder in WRA at various production temperatures. To achieve this objective, three common types of WMA additives (i.e., organic, chemical and foaming additives), one common type of virgin asphalt binder and aggregate, and RAP materials from various sources, will be selected to prepare WRA specimens. Both rheological characteristics and microstructures of the virgin asphalt binders with and without WMA additives, aged asphalt binder from RAP, and resultant blended asphalt in WRA will be characterized. Three microanalysis tools, including gel permeation chromatography (GPC), Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and atomic force microscope (AFM), will be used to study the molecular weight distribution, functional groups, and microscopic topography of the test specimens, respectively. Based on the rheological testing and microanalysis results, the effects of WMA additive type and mixing temperature on the microstructure reconstruction and blending efficiency of the new and aged asphalt binders will be investigated. Furthermore, correlation models between rheological and microscopic properties, as well as between the microscopic properties of the new and aged asphalts and those of the final blended asphalt in WRA will be developed. The outcome of this study will significantly improve the knowledge of the working mechanism of WMA additives in WRA at different mixing temperatures. Such knowledge improvement can guide the development and selection of WMA additives for WRA, and promote wider application of sustainable WRA with optimized environmental and engineering performance both locally in Hong Kong and worldwide. 温拌再生沥青（WRA）技术集结了温拌沥青技术（WMA）和再生沥青混合料技术（RAP）的优点。从可持续发展角度而言，温拌技术能大幅减少施工过程中的能源消耗及温室气体排放，再生技术则可有效节约矿物资源，因此温拌再生沥青被认为是一种新兴的环保型路面铺装材料。此外，温拌技术可降低沥青路面施工温度，有利于使用更高比例的再生沥青混合料，从而进一步节约材料成本。从工程角度而言，为了保证路面的正常使用，温拌再生沥青混合料的力学性能需优于或接近传统热拌沥青混合料。针对这一问题，国内外学者们对温拌再生沥青混合料的性能进行了系统的研究。然而，目前大部分研究主要侧重于宏观力学性能。由于欠缺对新旧沥青及温拌剂间作用机理的了解，温拌再生沥青的宏观性能仍不能被较好地控制。 本研究主要侧重于分析不同拌合温度下温拌再生沥青中不同组分间的反应机理。为了实现这一目的，本课题选用三种常用的温拌剂（有机温拌剂，化学温拌剂和发泡温拌剂），一种常见的基质沥青与石料，以及不同来源的再生沥青混合料制备温拌再生沥青及混合料样品。传统流变性能测试和新型微观分析方法将被应用于温拌新沥青，从废料中提取的旧沥青及新旧沥青不同比例下的混合物。其中，新型的微观分析方法包括凝胶渗透色谱分析（GPC），傅里叶光谱分析(FTIR)和原子力显微镜分析(AFM)将分别侧重于分子量分布，官能团组成及表面微观构造的表征。通过上述测试，可得知不同温拌剂及不同拌合温度对老化沥青微观结构的重构情况及新老沥青间混溶效率的影响。此外，本研究将建立模型对新、老沥青和再生沥青微观结构与再生沥青宏观流变性能间的联系进行分析比较。 本研究的结果有助于提高在不同温度下各种温拌剂在再生沥青中作用机理的认识。这方面的认识将指导温拌再生沥青项目中对温拌剂及拌合温度的选择。同时，本研究有助于推动温拌再生沥青这一环保型技术在香港及世界各地的广泛应用。

15214615.label: Realisation of objectives
15214615.value: Objective 1 has been completely achieved. All effects have been evaluated through laboratory Fourier transfer infrared (FTIR) tests on RAP mixtures with glass beads as artificial aggregate. Parameter derived from the FTIR tests have been developed and applied to evaluate the mobilization and blending of aged binders in RAP under different conditions. Objective 2 has been completely achieved. Mircoscopic and chemical tests conducted include FTIR, asphalt binder four fraction (SARA), optical microscope and gel permeation chromatography (GPC) tests. Objective 3 has been completely achieved. The microscopic properties have been correlated with the binder rheological properties obtained from the dynamic shear rheometer tests and viscosity tests. In addition, a three parameter (polarity interaction, hydrogen-bonding interaction, and dispersive interaction) solution-based model has been applied for the first time to successfully analyze the compatibility between the new and aged binders. Objective 4 has been completely achieved. The guidelines were developed based on the outcome of the work for achieving Objectives 1, 2, and 3.
