15214615.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214615.value: • ATR-FTIR can be used to indicate the extent of mobilisation of RAP binders in bituminous mixtures with RAP. • RAP binder mobilisation is greatly dependent on temperature.; Tthe mixtures prepared at 165oC showed on average close to 30% higher binder mobilisation than mixtures prepared at 135oC. • In general, WMA additives can increase the mobilisation of RAP binder when compared with mixtures prepared at the same temperature without WMA additives. From the additives tested, specific foaming and chemical additives showed the highest capability to mobilise RAP binder in mixtures, which were comparable to the levels of HMA mixes. • RAP binder mobilisation considerably varies, depending on the specific RAP used in the mix. However, a considerable amount of RAP binder remains immobilised regardless of the RAP source, under normal mixing conditions. • The RAP binders exhibiting a lower viscosity at the mixing temperature showed higher tendencies to be mobilised. • Chemical and microstructural features of a RAP binder can indicate its potential to be mobilised in a mixture. • Unaged binders and RAP binders can noticeably differ in terms of the extents of relative molecular interactions as per solubility-based parameters. Hence, they are expected to have varying extents of mutual compatibility. • Special mixing requirements such as increased temperature and mixing conditions could improve the relative compatibility between binders, in relation to RAP binder mobilisation and blending. • When considering combined blends of RAP binders and unaged binders, binders blended with low percentages (of up to 15%) of RAP binders showed similar extents of internal stabilities and relative molecular interactions as compared to unaged binders. • Increased concentrations of RAP binders altered the extent of relative molecular interactions in the combined blends, and are subsequently expected to have implications in terms of blend homogeneity. • The oxidative elements in the combined binders were seen to increase with the increase in percentages of RAP binders. It is postulated that these fractions will affect the polydispersity of the molecules through increased molecular agglomerations and associations.

15214615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214615.value: • This work only evaluated some important criteria that may affect RAP binder mobilisation and blending. Other parameters such as the effect of aggregate shapes, use of rejuvenators, clustering of RAP fines should be further investigated. • Specifications could be developed for RAP based on specific rheological parameters such as viscosity. This may help generally improve the blending of binders and improve mixture performance. However, to achieve this, research with a wide database of materials would be required. • RAP binder mobilisation and blending research are suggested to be applied to the asphalt mastic and fine aggregate matrix (FAM) level, as the interaction the binders could be influenced by the presence of filler. • Although the solubility-based tools may be useful for research purposes, its practical use may be limited for practitioners and engineers. It is suggested to develop more directly applicable tools to study the molecular interactions and compatibility between a wide array of binders with different compositions. Molecular dynamic (MD) simulation may be useful in that aspect to generate a broad spectrum of data.

15214615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15214615.value: The use of reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) in new bituminous mixtures has been widely promoted worldwide due to its environmental and economic benefits. However, the extent of aged RAP binder that is mobilised during mixing, and the ensuing blending of aged and unaged binders are still undetermined. This research aims to fill in this gap through fundamental investigation from microscopic perspective. To characterize the mobilization of aged binder in RAP mixtures with and without warm mix additives, glass beads were used as artificial aggregate to trace the virgin aggregate and a mobilization parameter derived from Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) tests was developed and applied. To understand the interaction between the aged and virgin binders, a three-parameter solution-based model was successfully applied. It was concluded that viscosity could be a useful parameter for practitioners to assess and standardize RAP variability. It was also found that some unaged and aged binders could markedly vary in terms of certain molecular interactions. When the concentrations of aged binders are larger than 30%, the internal stability of the blends could be changed. Hence, some consideration of the characteristics of the intermixing binders could be essential to design the most appropriate mix.

15214815.value: To develop new single- and/or multi-criterion optimization models coordinating the time, benefits, and risks of emergency routing. 15215215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215215.value: 隨著化石能源的日漸減少，能源需求的快速增加，以及全球氣候變化，新能源的利用正日益增多。但是，大量新能源的並網會對電網的供需平衡構成很大壓力。智能電網的概念為增強電網的平衡問題提供了新的契機。智能電網增強了電力生產者和消費者相互間的溝通能力，使得他們可以決定電力生產和消費的方式和時間。 鑑於樓宇是電力消費大戶，它們應該在電力需求響應項目中扮演更大的角色（即在峰荷時主動變換他們的負荷曲線）。當獲知電價在幾小時後有變化時，重新安排空調系統的運行以減低電力需求（比如重設定室內溫度）會是一個很好的選擇。但是當電力供應短缺，而增加發電能力又非常昂貴時，一個非常實用的方法是利用突然的電價變化或者其他緊急激勵機制“迫使”需求側做一些快速響應。不幸的是，傳統的樓宇需求側管理策略對於這樣的緊急請求束手無策。 眾所周知，直接關閉一些正在運行的製冷機組可以馬上降低電力需求，但是這一簡單粗暴的做法不僅會使得各空調區域的供冷不平衡，更有可能破壞整個空調系統的穩定運行。在此情況下，能即時降低冷量供應的樓宇需求管理和控制策略顯得尤為重要。它可以快速降低商業樓宇的電力需求以應對智能電網中的短期的電價變化或緊急請求。 由此，該項目的目標是開發一種快速的樓宇需求響應控制策略，使得商業樓宇可以有效地響應智能電網中的短期的電價變化和緊急請求。並且在此過程中恰當地達到犧牲熱舒適性和追求節約成本之間的平衡。 該策略不僅可以提高電網運行和電力生產的穩定性、可靠性和總體的高效性、經濟性，而且可以使得商業樓宇在智能電網所提供的需求響應項目中獲益，最小化電力成本。該項目將同時為樓宇專業人員提供一套方法，使得他們可以積極參與到智能電網的建設中去。

15215215.label: Realisation of objectives
15215215.value: A few innovative methods are developed, which are effective to control the energy use of buildings according to the power supply/demand balance of smart grid, without affecting the service quality to users in buildings. The methods provide the basis for developing smart grid in Hong Kong and developing next generation building automation and management technologies of smart buildings. A new supply-based feedback control strategy of air-conditioning systems for direct load control of buildings is developed to respond to urgent requests of smart grids. A power limiting control strategy based on adaptive utility function is developed for the fast demand response of buildings in smart grids. Experimental study is conducted to investigate the dynamics, quality and impacts of using variable-speed pumps in buildings for frequency regulation of smart power grids. A game theory based interactive demand side management method is developed to respond to dynamic pricing in price-based demand response of smart grids. A model predictive control method is developed for thermal energy storage and thermal comfort optimization of building demand response in smart grids. A game theory-based decentralized control strategy is developed for power demand management of building cluster using thermal mass and energy storage. Optimal and near-optimal indoor temperature and humidity controls is developed for direct load control and proactive building demand response towards smart grids.

A game theory based interactive demand side management method is developed to respond to dynamic pricing in price-based demand response of smart grids. A model predictive control method is developed for thermal energy storage and thermal comfort optimization of building demand response in smart grids. A game theory-based decentralized control strategy is developed for power demand management of building cluster using thermal mass and energy storage. Optimal and near-optimal indoor temperature and humidity controls is developed for direct load control and proactive building demand response towards smart grids. 12 journal papers and few conference papers are published and one PhD student is trained.

15215615.label: Realisation of objectives
15215615.value: The three research objectives were intended for one goal: to understand the cellular mechanisms of sonodynamic therapy. To achieve this goal, we conducted the following experiments: 1. Cell culture and Sonodynamic therapy The human breast adenocarcinoma cell line, MCF-7 cell line was purchased from Cell Bank of Type Culture Collection of Chinese Academy of Sciences (Shanghai, China). MCF-7 cells were maintained in Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium (DMEM, Life Technologies, Carlsbad, CA, USA) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS, Life Technologies), 100 units/mL penicillin, and 100 μg/mL streptomycin. Cells were maintained at 37°C in a humidified chamber containing 95% air and 5% CO2. MCF-7 Cells at a confluence of 80% were digested with 0.25% trypsin for subculture. MCF-7 cells were divided randomly into four groups: (1) control, (2) ultrasound alone (ultrasound), (3) ALA alone, and (4) ALA plus ultrasound (SDT). 5-aminolevulinic acid (ALA) was obtained from Sigma (St Louis, MO, USA). It was dissolved in a PBS to a stock concentration of 1M and was stored in the dark at -20°C. ALA is a kind of classic agent belong to both sonosensitizers and photosensitizers. For the ALA and ALA-SDT groups, the cells were incubated with 1mM ALA for a 4 h drug-loading time in DMEM medium supplemented with 10% FBS. After the treatment, the cells were cultured in fresh medium for further different hours (2h, 4h, 12h) and then prepared for different analyses. 2. Ultrasound System for SDT The cells in the SDT groups were exposed to a 1.0 MHz flat ultrasound transducer with a diameter of 35mm at an average intensity of 0.25W/cm2, burst mode with a pulse repetition frequency of 100Hz and duty cycle of 10% was applied for 10 min. The transducer was driven by a function generator (AFG 3251, Tektronix Company, Oregon, USA) connected to a power amplifier (Model 500A250C, RF Microwave Instrumentation, Souderton, PA, USA). The culture dish with cells was put on the top of a wave guide, 6cm away from the transducer, filled with water to facilitate transmission of ultrasound. 3. Cell viability assay Cell viability at different time points following ALA-SDT was determined using a Cell Counting Kit-8 (Sigma-Aldrich) according to the manufacturer's instructions. Briefly, Cells were plated at a density of 5000 cells per well in a 96-well plate and incubated in 100-μL culture medium for 24h. Cytotoxicity was determined by adding 10 μl CCK-8 reagent per well for 1 h at 37°C in 5% CO2. The absorbance of the treated samples against a blank control was measured at 450 nm as the detection wavelength. The viability of treated cells was determined by comparing to the untreated ones in the control group. 4. Apoptosis assay by flow cytometry Cells were seeded at a density of 5× 105 cells in 6-cm dishes and incubated for 24h. Alexa Fluor 488 Annexin V/Dead Cell Apoptosis Kit (Thermo Fisher Scientific) was used to measure cell apoptosis at the different time point following ALA-SDT according to the manufacturer's instructions. Cells were collected and incubated with 5 µL of the annexin V conjugate and 1 µL of the PI working solution at room temperature for 15 minutes. The cells were analyzed by FACS Calibur flow cytometer and BD Accuri C6 Software (Becton-Dickinson, USA). The flow cytometry excitation wavelength is 488nm, the annexin V fluorescence is detected with a passband filter with a wavelength of 515nm, and a filter with a wavelength greater than 560nm is used to detect PI. 5. Detection of mitochondrial membrane potential Mitochondrial membrane potential was measured using JC-1(Sigma- Aldrich). Briefly, cells were stained with 2.5μM JC-1 in the dark at 37°C for 30min and then washed with FACS buffer. The data was analyzed by FACS Calibur flow cytometer and BD Accuri C6 Software (Becton-Dickinson, USA). Excitation and emission settings were 488nm and 515-545nm (FL1 channel) for JC-1 monomers, 488nm and 564-606nm (FL2 channel) for JC-1 aggregates respectively. 6. Determination of mitochondrial dynamics CellLight Mitochondria-GFP (Thermo Fisher) were used to track mitochondria according to the manufacturer's instructions. Briefly, Cells were incubated with the reagent overnight and mitochondria-GFP behavior can be observed in live cells. After treatment with ALA-SDT, cells were visualized under laser-scanning confocal microscopy with X63 objective (Nikon, Tokyo, Japan). 7. Immunofluorescence microscopy observation of mitophagy Mitophagy was determined by the co-localization of mitochondria with autophagosome and lysosomes following the standard guidelines[41]. 1× 105 cells were seeded per 35mm confocal dishes (SPL Life Sciences, Korea) and incubated for 24h. After treatment, cells were stained with 100nM MitoTracker Deep Red (Thermo Fisher) at 37°C for 15 min. Cells were then washed with PBS and fixed with 4% PFA for 15min at room temperature. The fixed cells were further incubated overnight using antibodies against autophagosome marker LC3 or Lamp2 followed by Alexa Fluor 488- or 594-conjugated secondary antibody. The antibodies were diluted with 5% bovine serum albumin (Sigma). Nuclei were stained with DAPI for 10min at room temperature. Samples were observed by laser-scanning confocal microscopy with X63 objective (Nikon, Tokyo, Japan). 20-30 cells per condition were captured. The number of mitochondria co-localized with LC3 or Lamp2 was quantified. 8. Determination of cellular and mitochondrial ROS production Intracellular ROS production was measured using DCFH-DA(Sigma-Aldrich). Briefly, 10 mM DCFH-DA diluted with DMEM were added to MCF-7 cells at 37°C for 20 min. Cells were then washed with PBS three times. Labeled cells were trypsinized and analyzed by flow cytometry. MitoSOX (Invitrogen, USA) was used to determine mitochondria-derived reactive oxygen species (mROS) production following the manufacturer’s instructions. Cells were incubated with 10μM of mitoSOX at 37°C for 20 min. After washing with PBS three times, labeled cells were visualized by laser-scanning confocal microscopy with X63 objective (Nikon, Tokyo, Japan) and analyzed using Nikon NIS-Elements software. 9. Statistical analysis Statistical analysis was performed with GraphPad Prism software. Image J, Photoshop CS, and Illustrator CS software were used for image processing following the general guidelines. All data, expressed as mean ± SD, were analyzed with a two-tailed student's t-test or by one-way ANOVA. P-values <0.05 were considered statistically significant. The aforementioned experiments fulfilled the 3 research objectives, and we were able to complete 100% of each one of them. Please refer to the publications in Part C Research Output for more details.

15215615.label: Major findings and research outcome
15215615.value: Sonodynamic therapy (SDT), based on the synergistic effect of low-intensity ultrasound and sonosensitizer, is a potential approach for non-invasive treatment of cancers. In SDT, mitochondria played a crucial role in cell fate determination. However, mitochondrial activities and their response to SDT remain elusive. The purpose of this study was to examine the response of mitochondria to SDT in tumor cells. In this study, MCF-7 cells were subjected to 5-aminolevulinic acid (ALA)-SDT, with an average ultrasonic intensity of 0.25W/cm2. Mitochondrial dynamics and redox balance were examined by confocal immunofluorescence microscopy and western blot. The occurrence of mitophagy was determined by confocal immunofluorescence microscopy. Our results showed that ALA-SDT could induce mitochondrial dysfunction through mitochondrial depolarization and fragmentation and lead to mitophagy. The Parkin-dependent signaling pathway was involved and promoted resistance to ALA-SDT induced cell death. Finally, excessive production of ROS was found to be necessary for the initiation of mitophagy. Taken together, we conclude that ROS produced by 5-ALA-SDT could initiate PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy which may exert a protective effect against 5-ALA-SDT-induced cell death in MCF-7 cells. This finding was published in Cellular Physiology and Biochemistry in 2018, which is listed under the “Peer-reviewed publications” in Part C Research Output. During the study, we acknowledged that tumor hypoxic condition, which has low oxygen concentration at the tumor site is a bottleneck for SDT treatment, which requires sufficient oxygen supply to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS). We explored the potential of nano scale biogenic gas vesicles (GVs) as a new kind of oxygen carrier to alleviate tumor hypoxia. GVs, which are naturally formed, gas-filled, protein-shelled compartments, were modified on the surface of their protein shells by a layer of liposome. A substantial improvement of oxygen concentration was observed in hypoxic solution, in hypoxic cells, as well as in subcutaneous tumors when lipid-GVs(O2) were added/tail-injected. Lipid-GVs(O2) alone induced no obvious change in cell viability in vitro or any apparent pathological abnormalities after mice were tail-injected with them. In all, lipid-GVs exhibited promising performance for intravenous gas delivery, a quality that may be applied to alleviate hypoxia in cancers, as well as hypoxia-related clinical treatments. Two publications were made on this study, one in Biomaterials, and the other one in Acta Biomaterialia in 2020. We also participated various conferences and presented our research results, which resulted in 7 conference proceedings. Finally, 2 US patents were filed for the unique design and utility of the technique.

15215615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15215615.value: However, further work is still needed to confirm whether GV have prolonged intravascular retention time, whether they could induce allergic or immunologic reactions during transfusions or whether they could induce potential long term immunotoxicity. Crucially, even where any of these to emerge as issues in further testing, the possibility of alleviating or eliminating these effects through surface modification would still remain, giving such GVs an even greater chance of being successful. Besides being mere oxygen carriers, the shells of GVs are readily linkable with various anti-tumor drugs, GVs have the potential to be an effective carrier for both oxygen and drug delivery into tumor sites with potentially long circulation time and high efficacy. Furthermore, GVs can be used as a contrast agent for ultrasonic imaging due to the echogenicity of gas core. Thus, GVs is a versatile entity that could be used to combine multiple aspects of cancer therapy, potentially achieving the aim of ultrasound-guided oxygen delivery and therapy. Such approaches could help to pave the way for the era of better-targeted cancer therapies with reduced side-effects and greater efficacies.

15215615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15215615.value: Sonodynamic therapy (SDT), based on the synergistic effect of low-intensity ultrasound and sonosensitizer, is a potential noninvasive approach for the treatment of cancers. However, the specific cellular death mechanisms of sonosensitizers with different subcellular localization patterns remains unknown. In the present study, we used ALA to investigate their effects on key cellular activities including autophagy. In the results, we demonstrated that both autophagy existed in ALA-induced PpIX mediated sonodynamic therapy. However, ALA-SDT mainly caused mitochondria-specific autophagy by harming mitochondrial fusion and fission balance. Furthermore, ALA-SDT caused unbalance of mitochondrial redox system by excessive production of mitoROS. Taken together, we conclude that different subcellular localization patterns of PpIX induce different kinds of autophagy, serving as a pro-death function, cooperated with apoptosis to dictate the fate of cell death in sonodynamic therapy.

15216315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216315.value: One-fifth of the world’s economic activities are organized as projects, with an annual value of US$12T, and project management has been identified as a key success factor by many organizations (Project Management Institute 2008; Hall 2012). Work breakdown structure (WBS) is an important tool in project management, and it applies to all kinds of projects. The creation of WBS is an essential preliminary step in project planning. A WBS is a decomposition of a project into smaller components following a hierarchical structure. The top of the hierarchy is the entire project, and the components at the bottom are work packages. A work package may comprise one or more activities. The design of work packages can fundamentally affect project performance. However, the work package design problem has not been formally studied. In this proposed project, we plan to develop optimization models that can help project managers to determine the sizes of work packages in a project and ways to consolidate series activities into work packages. A number of factors should be taken into consideration when making such decision. These include the workload incurred in managing the work packages, accuracy of cost and schedule estimation, responsibility assignment, process control, project network construction, internal cohesion of project activities, cash flow consideration, risk management, resource sharing, activity crashing, and the possibility of concurrent processing. We plan to develop models that can capture the characteristics of most of these factors while ensuring that the models can be efficiently solved. Conceptually, some of these factors justify smaller work packages, while some factors justify larger work packages, and this leads to a tradeoff between two groups of factors. However, some factors such as concurrent processing are more complicated as they involve activities in different parts of the project network. In this case, more sophisticated operations research techniques are required for constructing optimal or near-optimal algorithms for the models developed. We also plan to conduct comprehensive computational analysis to test the performance of the solution methods developed and to perform sensitivity analysis of the model solutions.

15216315.label: Realisation of objectives
15216315.value: Objective 1 has been 100% achieved. We have developed an optimization model for work package sizing decisions in project planning. This model takes into account various factors, including workload of work packages, cost and duration estimation of work packages, monitoring and control of work packages, project cash flow, concurrent processing of project tasks, responsibility assignment of project tasks, internal cohesion of project tasks, and risk management of project tasks. We have also developed other variants of the work package sizing model. Objective 2 has been 100% achieved. We have developed a solution method for each of the above-mentioned work package sizing models. For the main work package sizing optimization model, we have also analyzed its strongly NP-hardness, analyzed the running time of our proposed heuristic solution method, and developed and analyzed lower bounds of the optimal solution value. We have also developed a polynomial-time exact algorithm for the case where the underlying task network is a serial network, as well as a pseudo-polynomial time exact algorithm for the case where the underlying task network is a network with multiple serial paths in parallel. Objective 3 has been 100% achieved. We have performed a comprehensive computational study to test the performance of our proposed heuristic method for the main work package sizing optimization model. We have also performed sensitivity analysis on the model solutions. We have further tested the performance of our proposed heuristic method against the "constant target work package size method." In addition, we have evaluated the benefits obtained by our model, which can be viewed as an integration of work package sizing and scheduling decisions, as opposed to the traditional work breakdown structure planning, which is performed without consideration of the schedulability of the resulting work packages.

15216315.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216315.value: We have studied how tradeoffs in work package sizing decisions affect project performance. Specifically, we have studied the objective of minimizing the total of several costs identified in the project management literature, subject to a project makespan deadline. For serial task networks, we have developed a computationally efficient algorithm. For general acyclic task networks, we have shown that the problem is strongly NP-hard and have developed a heuristic solution method as well as a tight lower bound. Through a comprehensive computational study, we have shown that our heuristic method routinely delivers near-optimal solutions that improve substantially on benchmarks from project management practice. Moreover, our computational results have identified problem characteristics where the benefits from our work package sizing methodology are typically greatest. We have also demonstrated the improvement in project makespan that results from integrating scheduling considerations into decisions about work breakdown structure design. In addition to the above-mentioned analyses, we have considered several extensions and variants of the work package sizing problem. These include a "constant target work package size model" for benchmarking purpose, an extended work package sizing model with task incompatibility, and an extended model with generalized precedence constraints work packages.

15216315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216315.value: There are several future directions for research on work package sizing. First, for particular project management applications, the factors that affect work package sizing may vary from the generic ones considered in this project. It would be useful to identify such factors for those applications. Second, it would be valuable to conduct an empirical study to estimate the relative influence of the various factors on project performance. Third, it would be interesting to generalize our model to allow stochastic task times and study how task uncertainty affects work package sizing decisions. Extensions of our model in such directions would be valuable. Finally, we note that our project focuses on work package sizing, rather than on the sequence of criteria that are used to break the project down. It may be possible to develop a more complicated model that simultaneously optimizes the sequence of criteria used and the work package sizes.

15216315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216315.value: In organizing a project’s tasks into manageable work packages, i.e., forming a work breakdown structure, tradeoffs arise. Defining smaller work packages increases project complexity and workload, and reduces economies of scale. Whereas, defining larger work packages reduces concurrent processing and adversely affects cash flow. In this project, a study of this tradeoff was carried out by developing and analyzing an optimization model for work package formation. The model minimizes total project cost, subject to a deadline constraint on project makespan. A computational study of this model demonstrates high value of deliberately varying work package sizes within a project, in contrast with typical project management practice. This research enables more precise planning of work packages to improve performance, documents the value of integrating the planning of work packages and schedules, and provides insights that guide resource allocation decisions.

15216415.label: Project Objectives
15216415.value: To carry out a detailed full-matrix parametric study on the sound transmission across plenum windows To quantify the effect of acoustical coupling between window cavity and receiver room on the overall plenum window sound transmission loss To formulate a simple, but reliable and scientifically sound prediction scheme for the plenum window sound transmission loss

To quantify the effect of acoustical coupling between window cavity and receiver room on the overall plenum window sound transmission loss
To formulate a simple, but reliable and scientifically sound prediction scheme for the plenum window sound transmission loss

15216415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216415.value: This study is proposed for an in-depth understanding of sound transmission across a special type of window called the plenum window and the prediction of sound transmission losses when the window is applied to buildings. Noise pollution has long been a big problem in the urban areas of a congested high-rise city, where there is usually no space for erecting noise barriers, while the use of extended podia will largely reduce the number of residential units that can be built. Balconies, once thought to be a potential solution, have been shown not to be so effective. Closing windows or using fixed double glazing windows will have an adverse effect on indoor air quality unless sufficient mechanical ventilation is provided (not good for sustainability). A relatively simple device, which can give sound insulation and at the same time allows for a reasonable degree of natural ventilation, is urgently needed. The plenum window is basically an elongated version of the single plenum chamber used in duct noise control. It consists of an air passage. Recent preliminary studies have shown that it can also offer substantial sound insulation and a promising noise mitigation solution. However, its wide adoption is not possible until a reliable design procedure can be developed. It is proposed to carry out a detailed parametric study using scale models because of the many parameters which affect the sound transmission loss and the limited size of the available testing facility. A full-matrix test will be done. It is also planned to carry out 10 to 12 full scale model tests for validation of scale model measurement and also to measure the sound fields in the proximity and inside the plenum windows, and the acoustical coupling between the window cavity and the receiver room. A reliable and scientifically sound prediction scheme for the plenum window sound transmission loss which is simple enough for practitioners’ use will then be developed. Some numerical simulations for low frequency sound transmission across plenum windows will be carried out for a deeper understanding of the underlying wave behaviours, especially when acoustical coupling occurs. The success of this study will not only deepen current fundamental understanding of sound transmission, but help create more residential units in an originally noisy urban high-rise environment.

15216415.label: Realisation of objectives
15216415.value: In this study, a complete parametric study on the sound transmission loss across plenum windows with and without sound absorption has been carried out through laboratory study. Site measurements using mockup flat units as well as a completed high-rise residential building block, have also been conducted with the support of Housing Department to strengthen the database. Room acoustics approach has been adopted to describe the coupling between windows and the indoor space. This simple relationship is shown to practically work. The sound transmission loss of the windows were obtained by removing the indoor reverberation from the measured noise reduction. A simple empirical formula is developed to predict traffic noise transmission losses of the plenum windows and the accuracy is found to be within engineering tolerance for environmental noise study. It is also found that the performance of a plenum window does not depend much on the window's elevation above the sound source in an opened environment. A formulation for estimating the sound transmission across facades installed more than 1 plenum window is also developed and tested at site. Finite element simulations are done in order to understand how the cavity modes are affecting the sound transmission. The effects of installing rigid scatterers on the sound transmission across plenum windows are revealed.

15216415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216415.value: Major findings of the present project are (1) A formula for the prediction of the sound transmission loss of a plenum window (with or without sound absorption in the window cavity) is developed. It has been validated by site measurements. (2) A framework for the prediction of sound transmission loss of a facade installed with more than 1 plenum window is also developed and tested. (3) The performance of the plenum window can be improved by installing rigid scatterer arrays into its cavity. The importance of the cavity acoustic modes in controlling the sound transmission has been revealed.

15216415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216415.value: Part of the results in this study shows that installing rigid scatterers into the window cavity can help improve broadband sound transmission loss across a plenum window. More effective scatterers and how to improve air movement across the plenum windows after installing of scatterers worth further investigation. A new GRF project in this direction is funded in 2019.

15216415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216415.value: Plenum windows are regarded as an important type of natural ventilation-enabling facade noise reduction device for use in a congested high-rise city. It can offer good sound insulation and at the same time allow for acceptable natural ventilation. The prediction frameworks developed in this study as well as the practical experience gained via site measurements will enable easy design of the window and thus wide adoption of the window in practice. The present results also indicate a potential method for improving the sound insulation of plenum window without much reduction in the air movement across the window.

15216715.value: 非线性约束的稀疏优化问题及低阶正则化方法

15216715.label: Project Objectives
15216715.value: We will introduce the extended restricted isometry property and extended restricted eigenvalue condition, investigate their relationships with the classical restricted isometry property and restricted eigenvalue condition, and use them to establish the recovery bound for the constrained nonlinear sparse optimization problem with lower order regularization terms. We will study first and second-order optimality conditions for the lower order regularization problem. We will propose a projected proximal gradient method to solve the lower order regularization problem, and establish the convergence theory by virtue of the projection operator and the Kurdyka-Lojasewicz theory. We will also apply the reweighted scheme to improve the convergence properties and enhance the sparse recovery performance. We will apply our theory and algorithms to solve (group) sparse constrained optimization problems arising in portfolio selection and gene regulatory network.

15216715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216715.value: The sparse solutions of under-determined nonlinear measurements arise in the sparse inverse covariance selection while maximizing the log-likelihood, quadratic compressive sensing in diffraction imaging and sub-wavelength imaging, and nonlinear base pursuit. Nearly, all of the optimization theory and algorithms developed for compressed sensing signal recovery assume that samples are taken using linear measurements and without constraints. Thus it is of great demand to design optimal algorithms to solve constrained sparse optimization problems with nonlinear measurements. In this project, we will address compressed sensing recovery problems in a setting where the observations are nonlinear measurements and there are constraints and develop optimization theory and algorithms by virtue of constrained lower order regularization problems for solving them. We will introduce the extended restricted isometry property and extended restricted eigenvalue condition, and apply them to establish the recovery bound for the lower order regularization problem of the constrained sparse optimization with nonlinear measurements. We will propose a projected proximal gradient method to solve the constrained lower order regularization problem, and establish the convergence theory by virtue of the projection operator and the Kurdyka-Lojasewicz theory. As optimization problems are of a nonconvex structure, it is difficult to establish that our algorithms converge to a global solution. However, we will aim to design algorithms to find a good enough sparse solution and compare their performance with some existing optimization algorithms in terms of computing time, accuracy and successful recovery rate. We will also apply our theory and algorithms to solve (group) sparse constrained optimization problems arising in portfolio selection and gene regulatory network. The practical meaning of the sparcity requirement in the portfolio is that an investor aims to invest in a small number of assets in order to avoid the high cost of transaction fees. The group sparcity structure arises in prediction, dynamic MRI, and gene finding. We will show that exploiting the group sparcity structure can reduce the degrees of freedom in the solution, thereby lead to better recovery performance. 不定非线性系统的稀疏解问题源于稀疏逆协方差选择中的最大似然估計，衍射成像和子波长成像中的二次压缩传感和非线性基追踪问题。然而，几乎所有压缩传感和信号复原方面的优化理论和算法都需要假设样本源于是在线性系统且没有约束限制。因此，设计优化算法来求解带约束的非线性稀疏优化问题具有相当大的需求。 在这个项目中，我们将处理带约束的非线性压缩传感还原问题，通过研究带约束的低阶正则化问题来发展优化理论和算法。我们将引入广义的受限等距性质和广义的受限特征值条件，运用他们来构建出约束非线性稀疏优化的低阶正则化问题的还原界。我们还将提出投影邻近点梯度算法来求解带约束的低阶正则化问题，运用投影算子和Kurdyka-Lojasewicz理论来研究算法的收敛性质。由于优化问题具有非凸结构，很难证明我们的算法收敛到全局最优解。我们会设计算法来寻找足够好的稀疏解并和已有的优化算法在计算时间、精确度和成功还原率等指标进行比较。 我们还将应用我们的理论和算法来求解源于投资组合和基因调控网络的（组）稀疏约束优化问题。投资组合中的稀疏性的意义是投资者希望投资少量的资产从而避免高额的交易费用。组稀疏优化结构源于出生人口预测、动态核磁共振成像和基因识别。我们将展示利用组稀疏结构会降低问题的自由度，进而得到更好的还原表现。

15216715.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216715.value: We showed that infinite-dimensional quadratic programming problems and infinite-dimensional linear fractional vector optimization problems can be studied by using affine variational inequalities. We presented two basic facts about infinite-dimensional affine variational inequalities: the Lagrange multiplier rule and the solution set decomposition. See [1]. We introduced a notion of (p,q)-group restricted eigenvalue condition and applied it to establish a global recovery bound of order O(λ^(2/(2−q))). By virtue of a first-order growth condition, we provided a local recovery bound of order O(λ^2) for a path of local minima. We introduced a group proximal gradient method for solving the ℓp,q regularization problems. We established a second-order growth condition and applied it to obtain a local linear convergence rate of the group proximal gradient method for solving the ℓ1,q regularization problem under the assumption that the limiting point is a local minimum. The numerical results on the simulated data showed that the group proximal gradient method with p = 2 and q = 1/2 is most efficient among the ones with other p’s and q’s and that the group proximal gradient method outperformed many existing algorithms in the literature. The application of the group proximal gradient method to the real data in gene transcriptional regulation revealed that, measured by the biological golden standards, the accuracy of the gene regulation networks forecasting can be improved by exploiting the group structure of transcription factors complexes. See [2]. We introduced a conditional subgradient method to solve a nondifferentiable constrained quasi-convex optimization problem. We established an abstract convergence theorem for a class of sequences, which satisfy a general basic inequality. We proposed a stochastic subgradient method, where a random noisy quasi-subgradient was employed, to approach the saddle value of a quasi-convex and quasi-concave function. Assuming the Holder condition of order p, we obtained convergence properties, in terms of objective values, iterates, and finite convergence respectively by using the constant, diminishing and dynamic stepsize rules. See [3,4,5]. We showed that the distance from the origin to the outer limiting subdifferential of the support function of the subdifferential set is an upper estimate of the local error bound modulus. We illustrated that this upper estimate becomes tight for a convex function under some regularity conditions. We showed that the distance from the origin to the outer limiting subdifferential set of a lower C^1 function is equal to the local error bound modulus. See [6].

15216715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15216715.value: We will investigate a local linear convergence rate of the group proximal gradient method for solving the ℓp,q regularization problem without the assumption that the limiting point is a local minimum. We will explore the quasi-convexity property of the ℓp,q regularization problems and study the application of quasi-convex subgradient methods in solving them. We will apply local error bound properties in the study of the convergence analysis of the group proximal gradient method for solving the ℓp,q regularization problems.

15216715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15216715.value: The global and local recovery bounds guarantee that an optimal solution of the ℓp,q regularization problem is a good approximation of the sparsest solution of a under-determined linear system. The local linear convergence rate result of the group proximal gradient algorithm provides a theoretical support that an optimal solution of the ℓp,q regularization problem can be found efficiently. Our extensive numerical experiments justify that the group proximal gradient algorithm outperforms many existing ones in the literature. The application of the group proximal gradient method to the real data in gene transcriptional regulation reveals that, measured by the biological golden standards, the accuracy of the gene regulation networks forecasting can be improved by exploiting the group structure of transcription factors complexes. Quasi-subgradient methods have a great potential in solving the ℓp,q regularization problems. The outer limiting subdifferential of the support function of the subdifferential set and the end set of the subdifferential set are useful in the analysis of an upper estimate of the local error bound modulus.

15217115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217115.value: Large rupture strain (LRS) fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) composites represent a new category of FRP composites made of new materials such as polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET) fibers. LRS FRPs are economical and environmentally friendly because they have a relatively low elastic modulus and are usually made from recycled materials (e.g., plastic bottles). They exhibit bilinear tensile stress-strain behavior and have a strain capacity greater than 5%, whereas conventional FRPs have linear elastic behavior and an ultimate tensile rupture strain capacity around 1.5% for carbon FRP, 2% for glass FRP, and 3% for aramid FRP. These LRS FRPs are expected to provide a better solution for seismic retrofitting applications, for which increases in ductility and energy absorption are of prime concern. However, relevant experimental and theoretical work is scarce at this stage. Pioneering tests revealed that conventional and LRS FRP-confined reinforced concrete (RC) columns exhibit different behavior under combined constant axial compression/reversed cyclic lateral loading. Conventional FRPs ruptured explosively at the ultimate state, but the LRS FRPs rarely ruptured even after the columns had undergone considerable deformation; instead, the progressive inelastic buckling of the longitudinal bars inside the FRP jackets dominated the ultimate state. This proposed project will investigate in depth the fundamental mechanisms of the interaction between LRS FRPs and RC in LRS FRP-confined RC columns subjected to monotonic and cyclic loading and will accurately predict such behavior. The project scope will be limited to rectangular sections (including square sections as a special case), but FRP-confined plain concrete cylinders and RC columns will both be covered. The specific objectives are as follows: (1) to investigate and model the average stress-strain behavior of LRS FRP-confined concrete in rectangular columns under monotonic/cyclic compression; (2) to investigate and model the behavior of bar buckling in LRS FRP-confined rectangular RC columns subjected to monotonic/cyclic compression; and (3) to investigate and model the behavior of LRS FRP-confined rectangular RC columns subjected to combined constant axial compression/reserved cyclic lateral loading. The proposed project will lead to a sound theoretical basis for the safe and economical use of LRS FRPs for seismic retrofitting of RC columns, thereby facilitating the wider use of this new cost-effective and environmentally friendly strengthening technology for seismic retrofitting and meeting an urgent social need in Hong Kong, the rest of China, and other parts of the world. 大應變FRP是壹種新型的樹脂增強纖維復合材料，因其制造來源於PET廢舊瓶的再生利用，具有很好的經濟及環境友好性。和普通FRP相比，大應變FRP具有雙線性的抗拉應力應變曲線特征，其彈性模量較低，但斷裂應變很大，往往超過5%，因此有優異的能量吸收能力，適合於鋼筋混凝土結構的抗震加固。申請者以前的研究表明：普通FRP和大應變FRP加固鋼筋混凝土柱在軸力和水平低周反復荷載的作用下的破壞形態顯著不同，前者的極限狀態往往是因為纖維的斷裂，而後者的極限狀態往往對應於內部的鋼筋屈曲。鑒於上述不同破壞機理，本項目註重觀察大應變FRP約束矩形截面混凝土和內部鋼筋在大應變FRP抗震加固鋼筋混凝土矩形柱內部的相互作用機理，澄清大應變FRP約束矩形混凝土柱受壓狀態下的平均應力應變本構關系，試驗研究和理論預測大應變FRP約束鋼筋混凝土矩形柱在軸力和水平低周反復荷載共同作用下的強度、延性等力學行為，以實現基於大應變FRP加固鋼筋混凝土矩形柱的經濟、安全的抗震設計。

15217115.label: Realisation of objectives
15217115.value: All three objectives set out for this project have been completely achieved. (1) LRS FRP-confined concrete sections under monotonic and cyclic compression were studied under both monotonic and cyclic loading. The dialation properties of LRS FRP-confined concrete were obtained and an analysis-orientated stiffness-based stress-strain model was established for LRS FRP-confined plain concrete under static loading and then extended to the cyclic loading case. Three-dimensional finite element analysis was conducted to simulate the structural behavior of LRS FRP uniformly and non-uniformly confined concrete to reveal the confinement mechanisms. (2) LRS FRP-confined reinforced concrete (RC) sections were studied under both monotonic and cyclic compressions. The complex interactions between the buckling of steel reinforcement and the external LRS FRP jackets (both uniformly and un-uniformly confined) through the concrete cover were carefully studied firstly through an experimental program, for which the contributions of the steel reinforcement and LRS FRP-confined concrete to the axial-loading capacity were isolated. As a result, a stress-strain model for buckling steel reinforcement considering the confinement effect of LRS FRPs was firstly established for monotonic loading and then extended to cyclic loading cases. Such stress-strain model was implemented to FE modeling to for validation and reproduction of the test results; (3) The seismic performance of LRS FRP-confined RC columns were studied under combined constant axial loads and cyclic lateral loading. The parametric effects of LRS FRP stiffness on the column ductility development were investigated. The FE element modeling was also conducted with implementations of cyclie stress-strain curves of LRS FRP-confined concrete as well as the cyclic stress-strain curves of buckling steel reinforcement considering the LRS FRP confinement effect, to simulate the test results. The valdiated FE model was further used for parametric analyses especially under different axial load ratio to achieve an in-depth understanding of the strength and deformability of LRS FRP seismically retrofitted RC columns.

15217115.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217115.value: (1) An in-depth understanding of the buckling behavior of steel reinforcement in LRS FRP-confined concrete has been achieved through an extensive experimental program (Paper 1 in Part 3) and both monotonic and cyclic stress-strain models for the buckling steel reinforcement considering the LRS FRP-confinement effect have been established and valdiated (Paper 2 and Paper 3 in Part 3). (2) A stiffness-based stress-strain model for LRS FRP-confined concrete was developed and validated through comparison with experimental results.(Paper 4 in Part C) Three dimensional finite elment modeling was established for LRS FRP-confined concrete based on both Drucker-Prager model (Paper 5 in Part C) and Damage-Plasticity Mmodel (Conference Paper 1 in Part C). (3) The above two types of models can incorporatet well the material and confinement properties of LRS FRP materials and the models are proven to be very useful in the finite element modeling for the prediction of the post-peak behavior of LRS FRP confined RC columns under seismic loading (Conference Paper 2 in Part C). Through both the experimental studies and the finite element modeling, the effects of LRS FRP stiffness on the ductility of LRS FRP-confined RC columns have been made clear under different axial load ratios, which can be used in design guides to achieve a most economic seismic retrofit design of RC columns using the LRS FRP materials.

15217115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217115.value: A further development of the LRS FRP technology has been explored through the project, i.e., using LRS FRP to improve the impact resistance of existing structures. The tensile stress-strain curves of LRS FRP materials under different strain rates have been observed (Paper 6 in Part 3) and the results are very encouraging. The PI and his collaborators are exploring new funding opportunities to promote the use of LRS FRP composites for impact resistance strengthening applications by unitlizing their higher energy absorption advantages.

15217115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217115.value: Large rupture strain (LRS) fiber reinforced polymer (FRP) composites refer to a new category of FRP composites made with low elastic modulus fibers. LRS FRPs are economic and environmentally friendly and feature an ultimate rupture strain greater than 5%, which is much larger than that of conventional FRPs. They are expected to provide a better solution for seismic retrofit applications than conventional FRPs, for which ductility and energy absorption are major concerns. This project provided an in-depth investigation into the fundamental issues of LRS FRP –confined RC columns subjected to monotonic and cyclic loading, in terms of (1) the stress-strain behavior of LRS FRP-confined concrete columns; (2) the buckling of longitudinal steel bars in LRS FRP-confined columns subjected to monotonic/cyclic compression; and (3) the strength and deformation capacity of LRS FRP-confined RC columns subjected to combined constant axial/cyclic lateral loading. The project has led to a sound theoretical basis for the safe and economic use of LRS FRPs for seismic retrofit of RC columns, thereby facilitating a wider use of this new cost-effective and environmentally friendly technology for seismic retrofit, meeting this urgent social need in Hong Kong, the rest of China and other parts of the world.

15217415.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15217415.value: 公共交通系統擁堵研究：車輛排隊的動態機理與緩解策略

15217415.label: Project Objectives
15217415.value: Develop simulation models for predicting bus and passenger delays and service reliability in bus corridors/networks that account for queueing dynamics; identify influences of key operating factors on delays and reliability. Unveil the mechanism of bus queue propagation in congested bus systems. Develop and assess innovative and conventional strategies for mitigating bus congestion. Study real-world cases and furnish suggestions on policy changes and control schemes. Formulate general guidelines for practitioners to better manage bus system congestion.

Unveil the mechanism of bus queue propagation in congested bus systems.
Develop and assess innovative and conventional strategies for mitigating bus congestion.
Study real-world cases and furnish suggestions on policy changes and control schemes.
Formulate general guidelines for practitioners to better manage bus system congestion.

15217415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217415.value: Bus systems in densely-populated cities (e.g., Hong Kong and Beijing) often experience severe congestion, which results in large delays and extremely poor service reliability. Apart from exogenous traffic impacts, a busy bus system will naturally get congested because of two reasons: i) bus queueing at busy stops, in part due to the limited number of berths and the mutual blockage between buses; and ii) the inherent instability in bus operations due to the positive correlation between bus headways and dwell times. Worse still, the bus queueing processes and the propagation of inherent instability entangle with each other in a way that further increases bus delays and unreliability. Regrettably, however, the joint effect and the resulting dynamics of bus queues have never been revealed by the literature. We therefore propose to develop parsimonious but realistic simulation models for predicting how bus delays and headway variations accrue temporally and spatially in a busy bus corridor or network. The models will unveil new mechanism of bus queue propagation in a congested bus system, and how key operating factors affect the bus delays and reliability. They will also be extended to examine innovative and conventional strategies that are specifically devised to reduce bus queueing and improve service reliability for congested bus systems. These strategies include: corridor-based bus operating strategies (e.g., bus convoying), unconventional bus control, bus priority schemes, etc. The results and findings will be used to explain prevailing congestion phenomena observed in the real bus systems, and provide better means for mitigating bus congestion. The models will also be calibrated and applied to busy bus systems in the real world. Suggestions of policy change and control schemes will be furnished to transit agencies that manage these systems. General guidelines for better management of congested bus systems will also be formulated. 在人口密度高的大城市（例如香港和北京），公共交通系統的擁堵往往十分嚴重，並導致大量的延誤與極差的公交服務可靠性。除了容易受到外部交通環境的影響之外，繁忙公交系統也會因為以下兩個原因造成擁堵：1）公交車在繁忙站臺的排隊，部分是由於站臺的泊位數量過少以及公交車之間的相互阻擋所導致；2）由公交車輛的車頭時距與停靠時間之間的正相關性所引起的公交系統的內在不穩定性。更壞的情況在於，公交車的隨機排隊過程與系統不穩定性會在站到站、車到車的傳遞過程中相互影響促進，從而在總體上進一步惡化服務可靠性並增加延誤。然而遺憾的是，這種隨機排隊與系統不穩定性的聯合作用及其所引致的動態排隊機理尚未得到研究。 基於以上原因，我們提出研發簡潔但符合實際的繁忙公交走廊或網絡仿真模型，用以預測公交車輛延誤和車頭時距的變異性是如何在時間和空間上進行傳遞的。這些模型將能夠揭示擁堵公交系統中的車輛排隊現象的傳播機理，以及某些關鍵因素如何影響公交車輛的延誤和服務可靠性。模型將被進一步擴展以研究傳統的與創新的策略如何能夠減少公交排隊並提高其可靠性。相關的策略包括：基於走廊的公交運營策略（例如公交編組），非常規的公交控制，公交優先策略，等等。研究的結果與發現將被用於解釋實際公交系統的擁堵現象，並提出更好的緩堵方法。模型也將通過參數校準後應用於實際中的繁忙公交系統。研究得出的關於政策方法和控制策略方面的建議將被提供給公交公司或管理部門。最後我們將利用本研究的結果制訂一般意義上的公交系統緩堵指南。

15217415.label: Realisation of objectives
15217415.value: The following response is organized for all the five original objectives one by one. 1. Develop simulation models for predicting bus and passenger delays and service reliability in bus corridors/networks that account for queueing dynamics; identify influences of key operating factors on delays and reliability. We have expanded the modelling tools from simulation to include analytical models. Our journal paper 1 shows analytically how optimally integrating shared bikes can effectively reduce both the passenger travel costs (e.g. delays) and also the agency’s operating costs for busy bus networks. We showed how key operating factors, e.g., demand rate, city size, wealthy level, can affect the benefits. During the course of studying bus performance in a mixed traffic system (i.e., buses that share lanes with general traffic), we find it is necessary to accurately estimate the impacts of general traffic (e.g. the queue lengths at major intersections). Hence, we deviated a little to study effective ways for estimating the mixed-traffic queue lengths, flow rates, etc., using connected vehicle data. This resulted journal paper 2. Simulation models are developed to manifest that the performance of our method is better than previous ones in the literature. Ways to improve bus operations in the mixed traffic context are also studied; please see the conference paper 1. Simulation models are also developed to study congested FIFO lanes (e.g., for buses or drop-off vehicles); see journal paper 3. This study shows that congestion largely depends on where and how these vehicles dwell (e.g., for picking up or dropping off passengers), and that congestion can be greatly mitigated by strategies that improve the utilization of dwelling area. Last but not least, simulation models are yet again developed to examine how bus delays (and also passenger delays) increase jointly with the service unreliability (in terms of, e.g., the bus headway variation). They are also used to examine conventional strategies like bus convoying and holding, and how the strategies can be used to mitigate bus congestion, reduce bus delays and improve reliability. See journal paper 4. 2. Unveil the mechanism of bus queue propagation in congested bus systems. We have shown: i) How and why vehicles (e.g. buses in congested corridors) operating in a FIFO fashion can be congested, how present-day control in attempt to reduce congestion fails, and what strategies can be effective; see journal paper 3. ii) How bus queueing and service unreliability jointly increase in a vicious cycle in busy bus corridors, how the conventional convoying strategy and its variants actually increases bus delays and degrades reliability, and how a carefully designed holding strategy can jointly improve bus speed and reliability; see journal paper 4. 3. Develop and assess innovative and conventional strategies for mitigating bus congestion. The following strategies have been developed and assessed in the project: i) Integrating optimally deployed shared bikes to feed transit systems. We show that this would greatly reduce the overall system cost and bus frequency (thus reduce the congestion); see journal paper 1. ii) Using connected vehicle data to estimate mixed queue lengths at intersections (see journal paper 2), which can be used to develop better congestion mitigation strategies for buses operating in mixed traffic; e.g., see conference paper 1. iii) Simple policies that can effectively reduce congestion at FIFO lanes (e.g. in bus systems); see journal paper 3. iv) Bus convoying, sorting, and holding strategies that can reduce bus congestion in busy corridors. We show that the conventional convoying strategies only make congestion worse, while the holding strategy, if appropriately designed, can reduce bus congestion and improve service reliability; see journal paper 4. 4. Study real-world cases and furnish suggestions on policy changes and control schemes. Real-world cases studied in the course of this project include: i) A real intersection (in Shenzhen, China) where general traffic and transit vehicles are mixed and congested. Through this we show the capability of using novel data sources to estimate mixed queue lengths (see journal paper 2). This would assist in developing better congestion mitigation strategies for transit vehicles. ii) A real FIFO lane (in the Nanjing South Railway Station, China) where large amount of drop-off vehicles are congested. Through this we show the policy changes and control schemes that can be applied to mitigate congestion (see journal paper 3). Note that the same or similar policies can be applied to bus systems that operate in a FIFO fashion. iii) A real bus corridor in Sau Paulo, Brazil, where large amount of buses congest at many busy stops. Through this we show that the conventional wisdom on bus congestion mitigation strategies is wrong (see journal paper 4). New strategies are proposed and tested via simulation. Unfortunately, due to the lack of sufficient data we are not able to test our strategies in that real case. 5. Formulate general guidelines for practitioners to better manage bus system congestion. The practical guidelines are formulated regarding, e.g., : i) Adding shared bikes to feed busy bus systems can significantly reduce the optimal bus headways needed, and thus relieve the potential congestion (see journal paper 1); ii) General traffic queue lengths can be accurately estimated using novel data sources (see journal paper 2), which can be used to further analyse its impact on bus congestion and delays (e.g,., see conference paper 1); iii) FIFO lanes (e.g. those in bus systems and drop-off areas) can be analysed using vehicle trajectory data and its performance can be improved by increasing the number of berths along the lane (see journal paper 3); and iv) bus delays in busy bus corridors can be significantly reduced, and reliability improved, via carefully designed bus holding strategies (see journal paper 4). These are summarized in the research outputs.

15217415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217415.value: i) Optimally integrating shared bikes with the transit network can largely reduce the passenger travel cost, and under certain conditions can even reduce the overall agency operating cost. This will reshape the optimal design of transit network by increasing the line spacing and reducing the service frequency (thus mitigating congestion). Appropriate pricing on the use of shared bikes is needed to induce the optimal demand assignment. See journal paper 1. ii) A novel Bayesian approach for estimating mixed-traffic (e.g., buses and cars) queue lengths at congested intersections can outperform the existing methods, and is robust to varying traffic conditions. See journal paper 2. iii) Adaptive signal strategies to reduce bus delays without damaging general traffic. See conference paper 1. iv) Regulating vehicle (e.g. bus) entries into FIFO lanes (e.g., large curbside stops for serving passengers) would only aggravate congestion. On the other hand, strategies that improve the utilization of the lane area for serving passengers (e.g. the berthing area) can significantly reduce congestion. See journal paper 3. v) In congested bus corridors where bus queues often occur at a series of stops, bus queues will grow jointly with the service unreliability, and both grow as buses move downstream of the corridor. Conventional bus convoying strategy will only make queueing delays and unreliability worse. An appropriately designed holding strategy, however, can reduce both negative effects. See journal paper 4.

15217415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217415.value: The following further developments are proposed: i) We will extend journal paper 1 to examine how other access means, design methods, and control strategies of bus operations can help reduce congestion. Analytical and simulation models will both be used. ii) We will build upon journal paper 2 to examine advanced congestion mitigation strategies (e.g., smart adaptive traffic signal, or intermittent bus lane) for buses operating in a mixed traffic. We will combine the analytical modelling with the data techniques, and perhaps use advanced optimization skills, e.g., reinforcement learning. iii) We will extend journal paper 3 to examine how the system performs under other queueing disciplines (e.g., what if a passing lane is added). We will mainly resort to simulation for modelling effort. iv) We will build upon journal paper 4 to further examine how refined stop-by-stop control can improve the benefits of holding, for bus corridors that operating under FIFO and other rules. Simulation will be used in this direction.

15217415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217415.value: Bus is a commonly used public transportation mode in the world. Its performance affects a lot of people’s daily life, especially in mega cities. Bus passengers often complain about the delay, unpunctuality, and queueing in busy bus corridors and networks. This project shows that bus queueing and service unpunctuality (and the resulting bus bunching phenomenon, i.e., that two buses of the same line arrive to a stop together) can become worse and worse after congestion occurs. Several strategies are proposed, which can be implemented in the real world to reduce bus congestion, shorten bus queues, and improve the bus service reliability. These strategies include: i) using faster means (e.g. shared bikes or scooters) to enhance the passengers’ access to bus stops; ii) control measures to increase the efficiency of using dwelling areas (e.g., berths at stops); and iii) holding buses appropriately. We have shown that under different operating environments, the above strategies can significantly reduce bus delay, improve service reliability, and reduce passengers’ travel cost. In addition, we also propose a method for estimating mixed-traffic (e.g., buses and cars) queues at busy intersections. This can be used to further improve bus performance by considering the impacts of general traffic.

15217615.label: Project Objectives
15217615.value: To identify the relationship between working pattern and occurrences of site accidents. The impact of working hours on fatal and non-fatal accidents will be singled out from a set of variables also known to be causing accidents. To identify the relationship between working pattern and site work attractiveness to youngsters. The employee perception of the negative effects of working long hours will be singled out from a set of variables including site safety and employment terms, also known to relate to the attractiveness of an industry to youngsters. To examine the viability of adopting five-day work week or similar working pattern, intended to enhance the work-life balance of the construction workers and the attractiveness of the industry to them. Based on the empirical findings, informed choices will be made from competing alternatives, after consultation with the industry.

15217615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217615.value: Two major problems that the Hong Kong construction industry is facing are (1) the dismal site safety record, and (2) difficulty in recruiting young people to join the labour force which is aging and in shortage. The hazardous site conditions have perhaps deterred many youngsters from joining the industry, or many parents from letting their children join. The common thread of the two problems is the working pattern of the industry. A six or even seven day work week is not unusual, and workers are often required to work overtime. This research will seek the evidence to substantiate if: (1) working long hours has resulted in frequent occurrences of site accidents and fatalities, and (2) long working hours and site accidents are the main reasons deterring young people from joining the aging workforce. We have found that there is strong correlation between accident/fatality rates and labour productivity between 1995 and 2013 in Hong Kong. The more the contract value of work that an average worker completes in a year, the higher the accident and fatality rates will be in that year. If labour supply cannot increase swiftly, the only way to complete large volume of construction work at times is by working longer hours. The various statistics collectively suggest that over the years, the safety record has not improved to any significant extent. With both nonparametric statistical inference and linear probability regression models, the relationship between working patterns and occurrences of site accidents will be identified. With similar techniques, the relationship between working patterns and employees’ perception on work-life balance, and their willingness to work on sites, will also be explored. With the set of evidence identified through these quantitative analyses, discussion forums and opinion surveys will be conducted with stakeholders of the industry to validate the results and to examine the viability and strategies of adopting a five-day work or other similar working pattern in the industry. The findings of this project will contribute to the growing body of knowledge on work-life balance in general and working pattern in the construction industry in particular. The nexus between working pattern, site safety and labour recruitment will be identified and quantified; and suggestions to solve the two major problems offered. 香港建造業正面臨著兩個主要問題：1）令人不安的地盤安全記錄；及2）面臨勞動力老化及工人短缺時，仍難以招募年輕人加入行業。地盤的危險性可能妨礙了許多年輕人加入建造業的意願，也使很多家長不希望自己的子女在地盤工作。以上兩個問題的共同癥結在於建造業的工作模式：每週工作六、七天是再尋常不過的，工人經常需要加班。這項研究將尋求證據證實：1）長時間工作會否導致地盤事故及死亡案例的頻繁發生；2）工作時間長及地盤事故會否成為阻礙年輕人加入老齡化勞動力隊伍的主要原因。 我們發現1995年至2013年間，在香港，事故/死亡率與勞動生產率之間有較強的關聯性。工人於一年中完成的工程合約價值越高，這一年的事故率、死亡率也越高。當無法迅速增加勞動力供給，大量的工程也只能通過延長工時才能完成。各種統計數據結果共同表明，多年來，地盤安全問題一直沒有得到顯著的改善。我們將通過非參數統計推論及建立線性概率回歸模型，得出工作模式與地盤事故發生率之間的聯繫。並通過類似分析，探討工作模式與員工對工作/生活均衡看法、和地盤工作意願之間的關係。在得到系列定量分析結果後，將與業界各持份者開展諮詢會及民意調查，以驗證以上分析結果，並探討於建造業實施五天工作制或其他類似工作模式的可行性及策略。 隨著社會對工作生活均衡問題的探討越來越多，這研究將有助於增加社會對該問題的認知(尤其是建造業工作模式方面)。這研究將對工作模式、地盤安全及招工之間的聯繫進行確定和量化，並提出解決建造業面臨的兩個主要問題的建議。

15217615.label: Realisation of objectives
15217615.value: Objective 1 More fatal cases were identified by WiseNews than the data from Labour Department. A total of 256 cases, reported in the press for a ten-year period between 1 January 2006 and 31 December 2015, were collected and analyzed. As for the non-fatal cases, a total of 7497 accident cases between May 2009 and October 2015 collected from the Mass Transit Railway Corporation (MTRC) were analyzed. It was found that eight variables, “accident category”, “place of accident”, “Monday”, “night”, “2 hours after rest”, “environmental factor”, “apprentice”, and “treatment given” were significantly associated with human factor-related accidents when all victims were considered. For millennials, “Monday”, “environmental factor”, “apprentice” and “place of accident” were found to be significant, while “night”, “2 hours after rest”, “environmental factor” and “apprentice” were found to be significant for non-millennials. Most importantly, human factor-related accidents and work patterns were found to be significantly interrelated among all age groups. To reduce accident rates among millennials, it is proposed that constant training and safety reminders be provided, especially after weekend breaks or other vacation breaks. For non-millennials, it is proposed that rest periods should be restructured and training on health and sleep management should be provided regularly to reduce human factor-related accidents. In all, the devastating effects of accidents may actually discourage people from working in the construction industry. Therefore, reduced accident rates in both millennials and non-millennials should encourage both the younger and the older generation to join the construction industry. Objective 2 A contextual study of work hours was conducted. The findings helped interpret the findings of the subsequent work packages. The research team’s former “No-Saturday-Sitework” consultancy study provided the WP1 with some background information and human networking as well. To complement and supplement the findings of the consultancy study, the collection of secondary data was undertaken. The secondary data comprised social-economic data, labor statistics, and construction outputs that are routinely compiled by the Census and Statistics Department of Hong Kong. The findings supported the hypothesis that the younger generation would accord more importance to freedom-related values, and thus would more likely support the “No-Saturday-Site-Work” initiative than the older generation. In contrast, in the cases of employed construction workers and construction trainees, they were placed more emphasis on money value than freedom-related ones. They were concerned with the possible deduction of take-home pay if the initiative were to be implemented because most construction workers are paid daily. In addition, the findings support the emergence of workplace interventions designed to attract and retain younger workers by enhancing their leisure time. Given the long-term potential benefits of the “No-Saturday-Site-Work” initiative, it has generally been suggested that the government is in the best position to implement the initiative through pilot projects as a client requirement. Objective 3 A cross-sectional study of manpower surveys was conducted through the various training boards of the Vocational Training Council. The aim is to find out how serious the problem of construction labor shortage is in comparison with other industries. We compared our finidngs with In each the annualor bi-annual manpower surveys of the 20 Training Boards, which show are the statistics on supply and demand of manpower classified into 5 job levels (technologist, technician, craftsman, operative and unskilled). In particular, the job vacancies (as proxy for labour shortage) at the craftsman and operative levels will bewere compared between the building & civil engineering sector and all the other 19 sectors including automobile, beauty care, metals, plastics, retail trade, security services, textile and clothing and transport logistics … etc. We have finished the manpower survey and found that compared with other these industries, the vacancies on constriction sites were not as large as we had suspected. Interviews with stakeholders from key trade unions were conducted. Based on the findings from the interviews, a questionnaire survey was conducted, covering all types of construction manual workers including building, civil engineering and electrical & mechanical (E&M) workers. A total of 970 valid answers were analyzed through Structural Equation Model (SEM). The findings identified workplace support as the most critical area of concern. Additionally, work-life balance (WLB) was found to have significant effects on perceived health and safety of workers. Method of payment was found not to have a significant effect on WLB. Contrarily, it was discovered that the number of work hours per day has significant effects on WLB when all workers and general workers are considered. Alternatively, perceived workplace support (WPS) was found to have a significant effect on WLB when all workers and only electrical and mechanical workers are considered. In turn, it was established that WLB has positive effects on perceived workplace safety and perceived good health for all workers. Hence, to improve the WLB of construction workers, emphasis should be placed on WPS.
