15217615.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217615.value: Objective 1: It is found that July is the most dangerous month for site works in Hong Kong. Results showed that the two hours after working in the morning and the one hour after the lunch break were most fatality-prone. The age groups of “45-49”, “50-54”, and “55-59” dominated the fatalities. PCA and cluster analysis suggested that safety governance should be focused on RMAA projects from the private sector. Training or retraining programs should be provided to manual works aged 45 and beyond. Improved safety briefs should be introduced on Monday mornings for young workers. More rests and breaks, and avoidance of high-risk work in the afternoons, especially in the hottest months (July and August) should be planned at the beginning of the project to help enhance site safety. A journal paper has been published in the ASCE Journal of Construction Engineering and Management. As for the non-fatal cases, a total of 7497 accident cases between May 2009 and October 2015 collected from the Mass Transit Railway Corporation (MTRC) were analyzed. A journal paper has been published by the ASCE Journal of Construction Engineering and Management. Objective 2: A contextual study of work hours was conducted. The findings helped interpret the findings of the subsequent work packages. Complementary measures can be further implemented to enhance the effectiveness of these pilot projects, including projects to promote cooperation among various stakeholders and more direct labor employment. Two journal papers have been published in the ASCE Journal of Construction Engineering and Management. Objective 3 A cross-sectional study of manpower surveys was conducted through the various training boards of the Vocational Training Council. The aim was to find out how serious the problem of construction labor shortage is in comparison with other industries. The findings identified workplace support as the most critical area of concern. Additionally, work-life balance (WLB) was found to have significant effects on perceived health and safety of workers. It is suggested that organizations should put policies in place that would ensure that workers feel safe and comfortable at work, and that their employers are caring enough. A great WLB would ensure that workers are better able to manage their health and stay safe at work. A journal paper has been submitted to ASCE Journal of Construction Engineering and Management. It has been revised according to reviewers’ comments, and is currently under the second review by the Editor only.

15217615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217615.value: As the study provides insight for the contextual situations and the chain of events that lead to the occurrence of construction accidents, future researches can be a pilot study on the implementation of “No-Saturday-Site-Work” policy. A comparison study can be conducted to assess the advantages and disadvantages of the initiative. In addition, one major limitation of this study is that the data do not include variables such as “number of work hours per week”, “overtime work done per week” and “work shift practice” of each victim that can be used to measure work patterns directly. Thus, more time factors, such as work pattern variables, should be assessed to investigate the direct effects on the occurrence of construction incidents. Moreover, further research can be done to ascertain the direct effect of accidents on the career choices of millennials, e.g. “Monday”, “environmental factor”, “apprentice” and “place of accident”, etc. Furthermore, future studies may target the students, apprentices and the young workers in particular to understand their perceptions of work-life balance (WLB). Studies should also look at different occupations of manual workers from different regions to examine the effects of WLB.

15217615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217615.value: This study provides insight for future research on the contextual situations and the chain of events that lead to the occurrence of both fatal and non-fatal accidents in the construction industry. It identified a number of factors that affect construction safety. It confirmed that work-life balance is essential for manual workers. It surveyed the largest sample size of construction manual labor so far. It demonstrated the working time pattern and the increase of work-life balance would attract more young generations to join the industry, and therefore ease the grim situation of labor shortage and labor aging. In addition, the results of this study provide important evidence supporting the “No-Saturday-Site-Work” policy to address the problems of labor shortages and aging labor. It depicted the picture for implementation of “No-Saturday-Site-Work” initiative for the construction industry in the future.

15218415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218415.value: Highly-populated countries like China have to import huge amount of crops every year, making it urgent to find a scientific solution. The reason behind is that the natural photosynthesis (NP) that plays a major role in the food production using green plants has low energy efficiency (typically <1%). In fact, the NP is naturally a microfluidic system as it occurs in microscale chloroplasts and bacteria filled with fluids, inferring the feasibility to be mimicked by man-made microfluidic structures. This inspires us to propose this project to develop integrated microfluidic chips and large solar reactors for the artificial photosynthesis (AP) of glucose from CO2 using sunlight with much higher efficiency (>10%) and simplicity. This project will be focused mainly on three tasks: (i) synthesis of functional nanomaterials; (ii) development of integrated microfluidic chips for CO2 fixation using RuBP; and (iii) explorations of large photoreactors & cyclic photosynthesis to produce glucose at ~1 kg/h in a self sustaining manner. Compared with the reported AP systems for water splitting and algae/bacteria growth, this project is novel in exploiting the microfluidic structures to streamline the photosynthetic steps with additional functions that are not present in the NP. The unique features include: (1) dividing different functions/steps into different regions and utilizing microchannels to cascade them; (2) immobilizing the photocatalyst, electron mediator and enzymes in different regions, avoiding the complexity of chemical mixture; (3) enabling convenient control of the reaction conditions such as pH value and temperature, exerting the best activity of individual enzymes; (4) exploiting the microstructures to eliminate the adverse effects such as CO2 diffusion limit and O2 inhibition in the NP systems; (5) consuming small volume of solutions (~1 uL) and saving costly chemicals; and (6) having large surface area and fast reaction rate, reducing the reaction time from hours to seconds. We have conducted pilot studies to synthesize the key nanomaterials and have demonstrated the functions of NADPH regeneration, glucose conversion and deoxygenation. Although preliminary, these results give our great confidence to the feasibility of this project. To the PI’s best knowledge, this is the first attempt to build up the full photosynthetic pathway using microfluidic chips and also the first exploration of cyclic production of glucose. If successful, it may find a new route to producing basic food materials like sugar and starch using factory-like production lines, and could be applied equally to the production of biofuel using sunlight. 千百年來，糧食生產一直主要依賴於綠色植物的自然光合作用（NP)，但其能源效率通常低於1%。像中國這樣人口大國，每年都要進口海量的穀物來滿足糧食需求，使得國家長期發展面臨巨大風險。這個問題，迫切需要一種科學的方案，來高效地生產基本食品原料（如糖和澱粉）。事實上，NP天然地就是個微流控系統，這是因為產生NP的微型結構（例如葉綠體和細菌）都充滿了液體，所有的反應都在微流體的環境中實現和轉運，因此有可能由人造微結構來實現光合作用的全部功能。這個想法激發了我們提出本研究項目，來開發微流控集成芯片和大型太陽能反應堆，實現人工光合作用（AP），從二氧化碳直接合成的葡萄糖，而且具有能量利用效率高（大於10%）和技術簡單的優點。 本項目將主要集中研究三個方面的工作：（一）納米功能材料的合成；（二）發展微流控集成芯片，利用RuBP來實現對CO2的固定；（三）製作大型反應器，嘗試利用循環光合作用進行自持式的葡萄糖生產，目標為每小時生產大約1公斤葡萄糖。與已報導的水裂解和藻類/細菌的人工培養等通常所謂的人工光合技術相比，本項目是真正的對光合作用的機理和結構的人工仿製，其新穎性在於利用微流控結構來流水線化光合成的每個反應步驟，簡化和優化反應結構，而且能夠實現NP中不存在的額外功能。本項目的獨創性包括：（1）將不同的功能/步驟分布在微流控芯片的不同區域，利用微通道來進行它們之間的級聯；（2）把光催化劑、電子中介體和生化酶等核心反應物，附着在微流控芯片不同區域的基地上，避免了各種化學物質混合而帶來的複雜性；（3）方便控制反應條件如pH值、溫度，能夠發揮每個生化酶的最佳活性；（4）利用微結構功能模塊來消除NP系統中廣泛存在的問題，如CO2擴散受限問題、O2的抑制作用等；（5）需要消耗的溶液體積小（大約1微升），可省昂貴的生化樣品；（6）比表面積大，反應速度快，可以把反應時間從幾小時减少到幾秒鐘。 為了本項目申請，我們已經進行了準備性的研究，嘗試合成了關鍵的納米材料，證明能夠實現NADPH再生、葡萄糖轉化以及微流控除氧等核心功能。雖然這些結果還很初陋，但是證明了本項目的技術路線是可行的。本項目是第一次嘗試用微流控芯片來仿製光合作用的全部過程，同時也探索了葡萄糖的循環生產。如果成功的話，將為基本食品原料（如糖和澱粉）的工業化流水線生產，摸索出一條全新的技術路線。同時本技術也可應用於利用太陽光進行生物燃料的生產。

15218415.label: Realisation of objectives
15218415.value: In relation to Objective 1, we have successfully developed the photocatalysts rGO/CdS/TiO2, and a one-step synthesis method to synthesize the visible-light photocatalyst C3N4 and the electron mediator [Cp*Rh(bpy)H2O]2+ (M; bpy = bipyridine, Cp* = pentamethylcyclodienyl). In relation to Objective 2, we have successfully immobilized the enzyme RuBisCo on the PDMS wall using Au nanoparticles and polydopamine nanoparticles. In relation to Objective 3, we have successfully developed the deoxygenation microchip using two layers of serpentine microchannels, the top of which is to flow the oxygen-containing flow and the bottom one runs the Na2SO3 solution. In relation to Objective 4, we have completed the experimental studies to capture sunlight, generate active electrons, transfer the electrons to the electron mediator M, regenerate NADP+ to NADPH, and then use the enzyme RuBisCo to capture CO2 and convert RUBP into 3-PGA and finally produce the glucose precursor G3P. Advanced characterization methods such as HPLC, NMR, FTIR have been used to verify and calibrate the intermediate and final products. We have found that the immobilization of enzymes in the microfluidic chips significantly enhances enzyme stabilities (7.2 folds in storage stability, 6.7 folds in thermal stability), and also improves the reusability (90.4% activity retained after 5 cycles of reuse and 78.5% after 10 cycles). In relation to Objective 5, we have studied the details of Calvin cycle and have cascaded three steps of enzymatic reactions using the microfluidic chips. We have found that it is feasible to realize the full Calvin cycle using the microchips but the efficiency and stability need to improve.

15218415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218415.value: The major findings include (1) In the aspect of the fabrication methods, we have synthesized three key materials: (i) the visible-responsive photocatalytic rGO/CdS/TiO2 nanocomposites, (ii) the non-metallic graphene-like C3N4 nanoparticles and the mesoporous C3N4 nanoparticles; and (iii) the electron mediator [Cp*Rh(bpy)H2O]2+ (M; bpy = bipyridine, Cp* = pentamethylcyclodienyl). More importantly, we found a new one-step method that synthesizes the artificial photosystem I (i.e., M on the surface of mesoporous g-C3N4) for highly-efficient photocatalytic regeneration of cofactor NADH. Experimental studies have found that the microreactor immobilized with the artificial photosystem I achieves 63% conversion of NAD+ to NADH using only 13 s, about 23 times faster than the slurry g-C3N4 system. (2) Regarding the immobilization procedures, we have developed (I) a new method to immobilize nanoparticles (e.g., TiO2 nanopowders, Au nanospheres) onto the substrate of microfluidic chip using adhesive types, which show high resistance to the fluidic shear stress and strong SERS signals in experimental verifications; (II) a novel method to immobilize the enzyme RuBisCO onto the sidewalls of PDMS microchannels by using a polydopamine layer as the linker via covalent bonds, which experimentally shows high load amount and enhanced enzyme stabilities and reusability (7.2 folds in storage stability, 6.7 folds in thermal stability, 90.4% activity retained after 5 cycles of reuse and 78.5% after 10 cycles). (3) With respect to the advanced function of deoxygenate using microfluidic structures, we have demonstrated the reduction of oxygen concentration to 1/20 using the deoxygenation microchip. (4) In term of the design of microfluidic chips for artificial photosynthesis of CO2 into glucose, we have immobilized the enzyme RuBisCO into the microchip to convert RUBP into 3-PGA, eventually achieving the continuous production of of glucose precursor at 13.8 μmol/min/g RuBisCO. This is the first time that the artificial synthesis of glucose precursor is demonstrated. (5) In the exploration of the full reaction pathway of Calvin Cycle, we have conducted experimental studies and have found that the full Calvin cycle could be implemented into the microchips by immobilizing the enzymes into different regions and then cascading the reaction. How, the efficiency is low and the enzyme stability needs to improve. Research outputs (1) Published 8 journal articles and 16 conference papers. The one-step synthesis method of artificial photosystem I was published in RSC Advances in 2016. The fabrication of mesoporous g-C3N4 nanoparticles was published in Micromachines in 2017. A review article on microfluidics for artificial photosynthesis was published in Beilstein Journal of Nanotechnology in 2018. (2) Trained one PhD student, Ms. Zhu Yujiao, who got the Ph.D. degree with the thesis title “Microfluidic Reactors for Artificial Photosynthesis of Carbohydrates Using Calvin Cycle” on 27 Jun 2019. (3) Established close research collaboration with researchers of other institutes. For example, we have been working with Professor Aoqun Jian at Taiyuan University of Technology on the device fabrication. We have also collaborated with Professor Xiaowen Huang of Qilu University on the enzyme immobilization. In addition, we have successfully worked with Professor Yanwei Jia of Macau University on the microfluidic biochips. Moreover, we have built up collaborations with Prof. Ning Wang of Wuhan University of Technology on the real-time on-chip monitoring of biochips. (4) Obtained 1 Best Paper Award and 1 Best Poster Award in international conferences.

15218415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218415.value: Further studies will be conducted to integrate the light-dependent part and the light-independent parts into a single microfluidic chip. And new microfluidic reactors will be developed to enhance the enzyme loads and the reaction efficiency/stability. In addition, the microreactors may be scaled up into bulky reactors to increase the production throughput.

15218415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218415.value: Food production relies on the natural photosynthesis (NPS) in green plants but its energy efficiency is typically below 1%. In fact, the NPS is naturally a microfluidic system as it occurs in microscale chloroplasts and bacteria filled with fluids, inferring the feasibility to be mimicked by man-made microfluidic structures. This project has developed an integrated microfluidic chip for the artificial photosynthesis (APS) of glucose precursor from CO2 using sunlight. In this research, we have developed new processes to synthesize the functional nanomaterials (such as the visible-responsive photocatalytic nanoparticles and the electron mediator [Cp*Rh(bpy)H2O]2+) and to immobilize the enzyme RuBisCO into the microchips. We have demonstrated the continuous production of glucose precursor at 13.8 μmol/min/g RuBisCO and have significantly enhanced enzyme stabilities (7.2 folds in storage stability, 6.7 folds in thermal stability) and the reusability (90.4% activity retained after 5 cycles of reuse and 78.5% after 10 cycles). This project mimics the NPS pathway with scalable microreactors for continuous synthesis of glucose precursor using very small amount of RuBisCO and demonstrates artificial synthesis of basic food materials by replicating the NPS, which may hold the key to food crisis relief and future space colonization.

15218915.label: Project Objectives
15218915.value: The objective of this study is to examine the local web buckling strength and behaviour of coped beams with slender webs. In addition, the current design methodology for determining the elastic buckling strength of coped beams with slender web will be reviewed. The existing reinforcing strategies previously developed for hot-rolled coped beams will be revisited, and if necessary, new types of reinforcement details will be developed. Both experimental and analytical investigations will be conducted to achieve these objectives. Specifically, the objectives of this research project will be accomplished by completing the following tasks A full-scale experimental programme will be employed to examine the local web buckling strength and behaviour of coped beams with slender webs. The cope and beam geometry (d/tw > 57.1, dc/D and c/D) and the type of stiffener (longitudinal and transverse stiffeners) will be examined in the programme. The stress-strain behaviour of the materials used for the specimens will be determined by tension coupon tests. The finite element (FE) method will be employed to analyse the structural behaviour of the test specimens. FE models of the specimens will be developed and validated by the test results obtained from this proposed research study. Subsequently, the validated FE models will be used to conduct a parametric study of the strength and behaviour of coped beams with slender web. The nonlinear finite element analysis results will offer a better understanding of the structural behaviour of the test specimens and will facilitate the development of design recommendations. The current design methodology proposed by Cheng et al. [2] and Yam et al. [35] for evaluating the elastic local web buckling strength of coped beams and the corresponding reinforcement strategy will be critically reviewed against the test and numerical results obtained from this proposed study. Where necessary, refinement of the current design methodology or a new design method and reinforcement details will be proposed.

15218915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218915.value: It is very common in structural steel construction to remove part of the flange of secondary beams in order to ensure that they have the same elevation as the main beams at the member junction. The beams with removed top flange, bottom flange, or both flanges near the connection zone are called coped/notched beams. While this is one of the easiest solutions to provide the required clearance, the presence of a cope in a beam inevitably reduces the strength of the beam in the coped region, where local web buckling is one of the most common failure modes. The importance of local web buckling design of coped beams has been identified by several researchers, and relevant investigations have been conducted which have led to the current version of design recommendations (the Cheng method) in the Steel Construction Manual (AISC). Modifications of the existing design methods have also been attempted by the PI (the Yam method) aiming to produce more accurate predictions. However, both design methods were mainly based on research on hot-rolled beam sections with the d/tw ratio (d = clear depth of the web for uncoped section, and tw = web thickness) normally less than 57.1. There is little experimental evidence on the applicability of those design methods to coped beams with slender webs (i.e. d/tw > 57.1). Such cases are common, however, in plate girders and cellular beams, solutions which are often selected by designers in order to accommodate relatively long span demands. As the rationale behind the existing local web buckling design rules for coped beams with slender webs has not been sufficiently proved, further experimental, numerical, and analytical investigations are required. The aim of this study, therefore, is to investigate the local web buckling strength and behaviour of coped beams with slender webs. The possible influence of shear web buckling (which can more easily occur in slender webs) on the local web buckling capacity, will receive attention. Finally, reinforcing strategies for those coped beams will also be explored within the scope of this study, such that a comprehensive set of design rules, which cover both cases of reinforced and unreinforced coped beams with slender webs, will be finally derived. 在鋼結構建築中,為了保證次梁和主樑在連接處位於同一高度,次梁在連接區域的翼緣常常被部分切除。 這些在連接區域被切除上翼緣,或者下翼緣,或者上下雙翼緣的梁被稱為切口梁。 雖然製造切口是提供主、次梁平接所需空間的最簡單方法之一,但是切口的存在會不可避免地降低梁在切口區域的強度,在這種情況下,腹板局部屈曲是最常見的破壞模式之一。 許多學者肯定了切口梁腹板局部屈曲強度設計方法的重要性,並進行了相關研究。 美國鋼結構手冊(美國鋼結構學會)在這些研究的基礎上給出了現有的設計公式。 此外,為了能夠更加準確地預測強度,本專案主要研究者提出了現有設計公式的修改方案。 但是,兩種設計方法都主要基於d/tw值(d=不含切口的梁的腹板高度,tw=腹板厚度)小於57.1的熱軋梁的研究。 很少有試驗研究過兩種設計方法對細長腹板梁(即d/tw > 57.1)的適用性。 然而,當設計板梁和蜂窩梁時,為了滿足較長跨度的要求,設計者常常會採用細長腹板梁。 正因為缺少足夠的研究來證明現有的切口梁腹板局部屈曲設計方法是否能夠適用于細長腹板的切口梁,我們需要更多的試驗、類比以及計算分析研究。 因此,本研究的目的在於研究細長腹板切口梁的腹板局部屈曲強度和受力行為。 而且,腹板剪切屈曲(更容易在細長腹板中發生)對腹板局部屈曲強度可能造成的影響也會被考慮其中。 此外,針對于細長腹板切口梁的加強方案也會在研究範圍之內。 這樣,最後我們可以得到一套詳盡的涵蓋了加強以及未加強的細長腹板切口梁的設計方法。

15218915.label: Realisation of objectives
15218915.value: In general, all the objectives of the study have been achieved. A full-scale experimental programme was conducted to investigate the local web buckling strength and behaviour of coped beams with slender web. The effect of web reinforcements was also included as one of the test parameters. Nonlinear finite element (FE) analysis of the specimens was performed to help explain the test results and to provide further insights into the structural performance of coped beams with slender web. Based on the test and the FE results, a set of design recommendations for the local web buckling strength of single-coped beams with slender web were developed. Reinforcement details for single-coped beams with slender web were also recommended based on the test and numerical results. The experimental programme consisted of 15 full-scale tests of single-coped beam connections with slender web. Of the 15 tests, four of them were tests of specimens reinforced by various types of stiffener. The test parameters of the specimens included the cope length (c), cope depth (dc) and the beam depth (D) to web thickness (tw) ratio. Two types of stiffener detail, namely, full-depth transverse stiffeners and longitudinal stiffeners, and double full-depth transverse stiffeners and longitudinal stiffeners were examined in the experimental programme. For the specimens without stiffeners, the test results showed that the specimens were failed by local web buckling with evident lateral deflection of the coped web. It was found that the local web buckling strength of the specimens decreased with increasing cope length, coped depth, and the web slenderness ratio. In particular, the D/tw ratio, the cope length to beam depth ratio (c/D) and the cope depth to beam depth ratio (dc/D) significantly affected the local web buckling behaviour and the ultimate strength of the specimens with a D/tw ratio greater than 100. For the specimens with large D/tw ratio and cope size (either the cope depth or cope length), the post-buckling behaviour of the specimens was evident as illustrated by the stable ascending branch in the load versus lateral displacement curve of the coped web. For the reinforced specimens, four full-scale tests were conducted covering the two reinforcement types mentioned above. In particular, compared with the unreinforced specimens which were dominated by local web buckling failure mode, it was found that the presence of the proposed reinforcement could effectively increase the load carrying capacity of the connections. Specifically, the longitudinal stiffeners for the cope edge and a pair of single full-depth transverse stiffeners were shown to completely mitigate the lateral deformation of the coped slender web, and the final failure mode of the reinforced specimens was shifted from local web buckling to plate shear buckling of the uncoped region. To further examine the test results, a nonlinear finite element (FE) analysis of the specimens was conducted to capture the structural behaviour of the specimens. The FE results were used to provide further understanding of the test results. In addition, the validated FE models were employed to conduct a parametric study to consider the variables that were not included in the experimental programme. In general, the FE analysis results agreed reasonably well with the test results in terms of failure mode, ultimate strength, and the load versus deflection behaviour of the specimens. The FE results indicated that the ultimate strength of the models with large web slenderness were insensitive to web initial imperfection amplitude, and such trend was more pronounced for cases with large cope length and depth. A comprehensive parametric study using 243 FE models was conducted to further examine the structural behaviour of single-coped beams with slender web. The parameters included the web slenderness ratio, cope geometries, beam depth, and the rotational rigidity of the connection. The analysis results showed that the post-buckling behaviour of the models was observed, however, it is more apparent for the models with increasing web slenderness ratio, cope length and cope depth. Besides, it was found that the ultimate strength of the connection models increases with increasing rotational rigidity of the connection. The FE results also agreed well with the test results of the specimens with stiffeners. Further FE study of the slender coped beams with stiffeners illustrated that the strain distributions, load-deflection responses, failure patterns and resistances of the specimens were well reproduced by the numerical model, confirming the reliability of the test results. The existing design equations for local web buckling strength of coped beams with compact web were re-examined to provide a basis for developing design recommendations for coped-beams with slender web. The current test results were used to assess the applicability of the existing design equations. In general, the predictions of the local web buckling resistance of the coped beam specimens with slender web by the existing design equations were overly conservative. In addition, the conservatism is more pronounced for the specimens with large D/tw ratios, and more intensified in cases with a deeper cope or a longer cope. It is believed that the conservatism was due to the inability of the existing design equations to consider the beneficial effect of post-buckling strength of the specimens. Using the test and the comprehensive FE parametric study results, a design approach based on the shear buckling of plate was adopted for developing a set of new design equations to evaluate the local web buckling of single-coped beams with slender web. Apart from the beam dimensions and the cope geometry, the FE analysis clearly demonstrated the beneficial effect of connection rotational rigidity on the local web buckling strength of coped beams with slender web. Hence, the influence of the connection rotational rigidity, the web slenderness, the cope geometry, and the beam depth were included in the new design equations. It was observed that the proposed new design equations were able to provide satisfactory evaluations of the local web buckling strength of single-coped beams with slender web. The test-to-predicted ranged from 0.91 to 1.20 with a mean of 1.05 and a corresponding coefficient of variation of 0.08. Based on the test and the numerical study results, it can be seen that both reinforcement strategies may improve the load carrying behaviour and resistance of single-coped beam with slender web. However, the reinforcing strategy employing double full-depth transverse stiffeners and longitudinal stiffeners may be more effective in enhancing the resistance of a single-coped beam with slender web.

15218915.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218915.value: Fifteen full-scale tests of single-coped beam with slender web specimens were conducted. Eleven of the specimens were without web reinforcement and 4 with web reinforcements. For the specimens without reinforcement, the main failure mode was local web buckling. The specimens exhibited post-buckling behaviour as illustrated in the load versus web plate lateral displacement curves. The test results showed that the local web buckling strength of the specimens decreased with increasing cope length, coped depth, and the web slenderness ratio. The post-buckling behaviour of the specimens was obvious for the specimens with large D/tw ratio and cope size. The reinforcement strategies examined in the experimental programme were able to increase the ultimate strength of the specimens comparing to those without the reinforcement. The failure mode of the reinforced coped beam specimens was plate shear buckling of the uncoped region. The single full-depth transverse stiffeners with the longitudinal stiffeners were able to prevent local web buckling to occur in the coped region. The nonlinear FE analysis results of the failure mode, ultimate strength, and the load versus deflection behaviour of the specimens compared reasonably well with those from the tests. It was found that for the FE models with large web slenderness, the ultimate strength of the models were not sensitive to web initial imperfection amplitude. Based on a parametric study using 243 FE models, it was found that the post-buckling behaviour of the models was evident for cases with larger web slenderness ratio, cope length and cope depth, and the ultimate strength of the connection models increases with increasing rotational rigidity of the connection. The existing design equations produced very conservative predictions of the ultimate strength of the test specimens. Therefore, a new design approach for local web buckling of single-coped beam with slender web based on plate shear buckling was proposed. The proposed equations consider the effects of web slenderness, beam depth, cope geometry, and connection rotational rigidity. Based on the research findings, the reinforcing strategy employing double full-depth transverse stiffeners and longitudinal stiffeners may be more effective in enhancing the resistance of a single-coped beam with slender web. The research findings have resulted in 2 journal papers. One of them was published in the “Thin-Walled Structures” (Section C, paper 1), and the other one was published in the “Journal of Constructional Steel Research” (Section C, paper 2). Two conference papers were also published as illustrated in Section C.

15218915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218915.value: The structural behaviour and strength of single-coped beams with slender web were studied experimentally and numerically. The test parameters included various cope geometries, beam dimensions, and reinforcement strategies. It would be beneficial to conduct additional tests on coped beams with slender web using different end-plate dimensions in order to consider the effect of connection rotational restraint. More tests on different reinforcement details such as the extension of the length of longitudinal stiffeners beyond the cope end and varied cope details are also valuable since only four tests on reinforced single-coped beams were conducted. The additional test results can complement the parametric study and allow refinement of the proposed design recommendations for assessing the local web buckling strength of coped beams with slender web. In addition, the new test data can help further verify the proposed reinforcement strategies. The design recommendation of the reinforcement details for single-coped beams with slender web can also be enhanced to consider other forms of stiffeners and cope details.

15218915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218915.value: Coped beams are commonly used in buildings and bridges to provide the same elevation of beam/girder flanges at member intersections in order to enable the construction of flooring, decking, and ceiling systems. Since part of the beam flange is notched to provide the cope, the strength and stiffness of the coped beam web are significantly affected. For building structures that require more column free space, a large coped beam depth is required. Hence, the beam web plate may be slender, and local instability of the plate may occur due to the floor loading. A research study including both experimental and numerical investigations was conducted to examine the local web buckling strength and behaviour of single-coped beams with slender web. Reinforcement strategy to strengthen the coped beam specimens was also explored. Designed recommendations to evaluate the local web buckling strength of single-coped beams with slender web were developed based on the results of the test and numerical studies. Reinforcement strategies of using transverse and longitudinal stiffeners were proposed to strengthen single-coped beams with slender web.

15219415.label: Realisation of objectives
15219415.value: Objective 1 To quantify residual stresses due to welding and cold-bending in fabricated box sections of Q690 steel materials. a) An extensive literature review on residual stresses due to welding and cold-bending of steel plates was carried out. It was noted that a large number of experimental investigations were carried out in 1970s, and the method of sectioning was commonly adopted. However, this method was unable to measure residual stresses at the proximity of the welding accurately, owing to physical restrictions. b) An advanced finite element model on welding of steel plates was established, and the model had been carefully calibrated against measured test data of S355 steel plates. It should be noted that temperature distribution history in the vicinity of the welding was measured during welding of the steel plates. These temperature data were incorporated into the finite element model to perform coupled thermomechanical analyses in order to predict residual stresses within the welded sections. c) In order to develop an advanced numerical approach for modelling structural behavior of both S355 and S690 cold-formed tubular sections, the following tasks were undertaken: i. a 2D finite element model was developed to simulate cold-bending, and both longitudinal and transverse residual stresses inside the steel plates were evaluated successfully, and ii. a 3D finite element model was also developed to simulate arc welding, and both longitudinal and transverse residual stresses inside the steel plates obtained above were incorporated into the model. An overall distribution of residual stresses across cross-sections of the tubular sections were successfully obtained. Comparison on predicted stresses with those measured data of S355 sections found in the literature was considered to be satisfactory. d) Calibration of the 3D finite element models was carried out against both experimental and analytical data for S355 and S690 steels. Sensitivity studies against various parameters, such as various sizes and shapes of the tubular sections, and reduction factors to mechanical properties, welding parameters and geometric dimensions of the proposed double ellipsoidal heat sources had been conducted. e) Scientific expressions on maximum residual stresses within the cold-formed tubular sections were also proposed. Objective 2 To establish a scientific mechanism to assess structural penalty owing to residual stresses on fabricated box sections with different combinations of welded and cold-bent corner joints. a) Another 3D finite element model was also developed, and the resulting residual stresses due to i) cold bending, and ii) welding were fully incorporated into the model. Advanced material and geometrical non-linear analyses on the model under compression were completed successfully. Hence, both stocky and slender sections of S355 and S690 cold-formed tubular sections under compression had been examined in details. b) Calibration of the 3D finite element models for cold-formed circular sections was completed. It should be noted that while there were many test data on compression resistances of S355 cold-formed tubular sections in the literature, supplementary data on residual stresses of these sections were few. c) Systematic investigations into the following parameters of interest were also conducted: i. corner radius to plate thickness ratios ii. yield strengths iii. section slenderness, i.e. section dimension to plate thickness ratios iv. member slenderness, i.e. member length to section dimension ratios Objective 3 To develop supplementary design rules to determine the section resistances of fabricated box sections under compression. a) Codified design rules on cross-section and member resistances of cold-formed tubular sections were examined, and technical background on their formulation was studied. b) In general, different interaction curves for various types of cold-formed tubular sections were given in a number of codes of practice and design recommendations. For sections made from different manufacturing processes, different values of the design parameters were assigned for sections under different loadings. c) Based on numerical results obtained from above, codified design rules on cross-section and member resistances of cold-formed tubular sections were examined, and suitability of various design parameters was checked against various numerical results in order to verify applicability of these design rules.

15219415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219415.value: In order to examine effects of various fabrication processes on residual stresses of S690 cold-formed tubular sections (CFTS), a systematic experimental and numerical investigation into thermal and mechanical responses in these S690 CFTS with different cross-sectional dimensions was successfully conducted. Structural implications of both transverse bending and longitudinal welding onto these S690 CFTS had been successfully quantified. A number of cold-formed tubular sections with different geometric dimensions were covered, namely, cold-formed circular hollow sections, and square hollow sections with i) mid-plate welding, and ii) corner welding. These CFTS were manufactured through a transverse bending process using either a press-braking method or three-roller bending method, and then a longitudinal welding process performed by qualified welders. It should be noted that all the welding parameters during the entire welding process were recorded. Consequently, surface temperature history of these CFTS at selected positions were measured with thermocouples during welding while residual stresses of these CFTS were measured with the sectioning method after welding for subsequent calibration of numerical models. Moreover, all these measured residual stresses were compared with existing residual stress patterns available from the literature. Two dimensional finite element models were established to simulate the transverse bending process to predict residual stresses while three dimensional sequentially coupled thermomechanical analyses were then performed to simulate the longitudinal welding process. Key findings of the project are: a) Surface temperature history in S690 CFTS were obtained with thermocouples during welding while the corresponding welding parameters were recorded. This provides an effective means to investigate the welding processes. b) Residual strains of these S690 CFT were accurately measured and predicted, and the residual stresses due to transverse bending were found to be significantly smaller than those design data commonly adopted by researchers and engineers. c) Based on both experimental and numerical results, typical residual stress distributions of these S690 CFTS were proposed. A simplified residual stress pattern was also proposed after comparison with existing patterns available in literature. The proposed residual stress pattern is readily employed for numerical investigation into structural behaviour of various structural members made of S690 CFCHS. Consequently, a scientific mechanism is successfully developed and carefully calibrated to correlate effects of two fabrication processes, namely, transverse bending and longitudinal welding, onto the structural behaviour of CFTS. Residual stresses in these CFTS are accurately predicted, and their effects on both resistance and rigidity of these CFTS are readily assessed through advanced numerical modelling.

15219415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219415.value: Owing to the success of the project, it is proposed to extend the investigation to cover structural behaviour of joints between S690 CFTS, and the following types of joints should be covered: 1. T-joints under axial compression 2. T-joints under lateral forces, and hence, bending under monotonic and cyclic actions 3. K-joints under pull-push forces 4. K-joints under pull-push forces under monotonic and cyclic actions It is also important to calibrate the welding processes between the S690 CFTS at the joints, and both welding procedures and parameters should be carefully monitored during welding. It should be noted that the welding should be properly controlled in order to ensure no changes in microstructures will be resulted. Hence, the advanced finite element models with coupled thermomechanical analyses should be properly extended as well as carefully calibrated. Systematic parametric studies should be carried out to examine structural behaviour of these joints between these S690 CFTS under various practical loading conditions. These experimental ad numerical investigations will enable effective use of S690 steels in building structures, in particular, long span foot bridges and roof structures.

15219415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15219415.value: Owing to their improved strength to self-weight ratios of high strength steels, their applications in tubular structures are considered to be highly favourable by many structural engineers as solutions to heavily loaded members. In general, many engineers believe that adverse effects of various fabrication processes such as transverse bending and longitudinal welding onto cold-formed tubular sections will be proportionally less pronounced. In order to examine effects of various fabrication processes on residual stresses of S690 cold-formed tubular sections (CFTS), a systematic experimental and numerical investigation into thermal and mechanical responses in these S690 CFTS with different cross-sectional dimensions was successfully conducted. Structural implications of both transverse bending and longitudinal welding onto these S690 CFTS had been successfully quantified. Consequently, a scientific mechanism is successfully developed and carefully calibrated to correlate effects of these two fabrication processes onto the structural behaviour of these S690 CFTS. Residual stresses in these CFTS are accurately predicted, and their effects on both resistance and rigidity of these CFTS are readily assessed through advanced numerical modelling. Hence, structural engineers will take full opportunities to exploit benefits offered by high strength S690 steels in construction.

15220215.label: Project Objectives
15220215.value: A general and unified theory of general flux modulated machines (GFMM), which can explain the operating principle of basic flux-modulated motor, vernier motor, doubly-fed magnetic reluctance machine, flux-switching motor, and dual-PM-excited motor, will be developed. Design guidelines of GFMM will be presented. Based on the developed general theory, a computer program which can automatically find possible topologies will be developed. The developed general theory of GFMM will be served as initial fast screening of possible topology combinations. A finite-element model of the proposed machines which couples magnetic field, power electronic circuit, and mechanical motion, will be developed to quantitatively compare the performances of the machines. Their merits and demerits will be comprehensively identified. A multi-objective optimal design method for GFMM will be developed. The design parameters include topology indices, geometric sizes, PM arrangement and windings. The developed method will be applied to design an in-wheel motor for direct-drive of EVs.

15220215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220215.value: 電機的主要功能是實現機械能和電能之間的轉換。由於電機的數量很多，其能量轉換效率的一點點提升便可以節約大量的能源。探索高效率、高轉矩密度、低成本的新型電機一直都是令人關注的研究課題。在最近幾十年，出現了很多類型的新型電機，其中包括用磁阻變化來產生恒定轉矩的基本的磁通調製電機，特殊槽組合的游標電機，定子上有兩套繞組的雙饋磁阻電機，定子上有永磁體的磁通切換電機，定子和轉子上都有永磁體的雙永磁激勵電機。這些電機在一些不同的應用中有他們各自的優勢。基於近幾年的研究，本項目研究者發現所有這些電機都遵循一個基本的運行原理，可以為這種類型的電機建立一個通用的、統一的理論。由於這些電機的運行原理相對較新，不同拓撲結構的變化組合很多，因此有很大的可能可以發明出更多的新型電機。例如，近幾年本項目研究者發明了一種具有高轉矩密度的三層永磁激勵電機，本項目研究者還發明了一種新型雙定子發電機，在轉子的轉速變化情況下可以輸出恒頻恒壓的電力，很適合應用在風力發電系統。 本項目中，通過對基本磁通調製電機、游標電機、雙饋磁阻電機、磁通切換電機和雙永磁激磁電機之間的關係和運行機制進行詳細的研究，發現這些電機都是採用不均勻的磁阻來調製磁通以產生恒定的轉矩，所以所有的這些電機會被歸納為一般磁通調製電機。本項目會提出一個一般性的理論來解釋這些電機的運行原理，同時會為這些電機建立一個通用的設計準則，以便可以快速地確定在不同的繞組極對數組合、永磁體組合、特殊的鐵磁片組合、齒/槽組合以及不同的交流/直流勵磁和轉子轉速下電機的效能。還會提出一種新型的永磁體排列的一般模式，並通過對其尺寸的最優化來自動確定最佳的永磁體排列結構。本項目會建立一個數據結構來表達一般磁通調製電機拓撲變化的多樣性。基於磁通調製電機一般性理論的建立，本項目研究者將會建立一個電腦程式以尋找具有單/雙定子和單/雙轉子的各種可能拓撲結構、不同部分的極對數和磁場旋轉速度的組合及不同繞組中的頻率。對所有可能的拓撲結構都會採用瞬態磁場、電力電子電路、機械運動和溫度場耦合的有限元方法來進行量化研究。基於本項目建立的電腦程式，適用于各種特殊應用的最佳的或新型的電機拓撲結構就可以自動確定。本項目會建立一種多目標優化設計方法以尋找最佳的設計參數，比如各個部分的幾何尺寸和繞組匝數。我們已經完成的初步研究是手動尋找不同的一般磁通調製電機的結構。初步研究結果已經表明與傳統電機相比，新型電機可以輸出多於155%的轉矩。作為一種應用實例，本項目開發的方法將應用於電動汽車用高轉矩密度輪轂直驅電機的設計、樣機製造和測試。

15220215.label: Realisation of objectives
15220215.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. The relationship among the number of pole pairs, the magnitude and rotating speed of main harmonics of the magnetic fields produced by each set of windings and PMs have been analytically expressed according to the mmf and air-gap permeance. Basic conditions for different combinations of various topologies to produce constant electromagnetic torque have been identified. A physical model of general flux modulated machines (GFMM) which can explain the operating principle of basic flux-modulated motor, vernier motor, doubly-fed magnetic reluctance machine, flux-switching motor, dual-PM-excited motor, and some other possible machines with more complicated topologies have been presented. A novel general pattern of PM arrangement has been proposed. The presented pattern includes five types of the most commonly used PM arrangements, which are, traditional surface mounted type, serration type, simplified Halbach type, consequent-pole type, and consequent-pole Halbach type. By optimizing the sizes of the general pattern, the best PM arrangement can be automatically obtained. A time-stepping electromagnetic field - thermal field - power electronic circuit - mechanical motion coupled FEM has been developed to precisely compute the performances of each topology of GFMM. A parameterized geometric model of GFMM has been established. A tree-shaped data structure has been employed to express all possible topologies. In the computer C++ program, a corresponding tree- shaped class sets are used to store all the information of the structures. A multi-objective hybrid optimization method for GFMM topology optimization has been developed. A data structure with a set of topology indices has been developed to represent variable topologies. The design parameters include topology indices, geometric sizes, PM and winding arrangements. To reduce the computing time of optimization, the following techniques have been employed: (1) Based on the developed operating principle of GFMM, basic rules for an initial fast screening of possible topology combinations is developed in order to give a quick assessment whether the sample point automatically produced by the optimization algorithm is reasonable or not. For example, for a brushless structure, if the part has armature windings, it should be stationary. (2) Design parameters are divided into several levels according to the sensitivity analysis. Different optimal strategies are employed based on the levels defined to rapidly search for the optimum design of the machine. An adaptive controlling strategy is used in both level definition and parameter setting in optimization algorithms. (3) A hybrid method combining with both stochastic and deterministic approaches is adopted to speed up the overall optimization procedure. The stochastic methods are improved by introducing the sensitivity factors which guides the local search under the global search background. The merits of both stochastic and deterministic search methods are therefore fully exploited. (4) A surface response method is applied to reduce the number of field computations. The developed GFMM model and its optimization method have been applied to design an in-wheel motor for EV direct drive. The objective functions include high efficiency, high torque density, high power factor and limited temperature-rise over a wide speed range and different operating status. The overall performances of the designed motor are compared with those of conventional PM motors and induction motors. Prototypes of the proposed motor and its converter have been constructed and fully tested.

15220215.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220215.value: (1) A general and unified theory of general flux modulated machines (GFMM), which can explain the operating principle of a basic flux-modulated motor, a vernier motor, a doubly-fed magnetic reluctance machine, a flux-switching motor and a dual-PM-excited motor with PMs on both rotor and stator, has been presented. It is derived from a conventional magnetic gear. A novel general pattern of PM arrangement, which includes five types of the most commonly used PM arrangements, has been proposed. Several physical models of GFMM have been established in which the general pattern of PM arrangements is adopted. Models of GFMM with single/double stators and single/double rotors have also been built for different applications and the corresponding performances are analyzed and compared. (2) A time-stepping electromagnetic field - thermal field - power electronic circuit - mechanical motion coupled FEM has been employed to precisely compute the performances of each topology of GFMM. Parameterized geometric models of GFMM have been established. The computer program which can automatically find possible topologies has been developed preliminarily. A remesh-free method has been adopted to re-generating the FEM mesh and an adaptive time-stepping method according to the excitation dynamics has been used for the transient problem. (3) A multi-objective hybrid optimization method has been developed. An initial fast screening of possible topology combinations is included to give a quick assessment of the sample point. A sensitivity analysis, in which the impacts of the design parameters on the performances of the machine are assessed, is adopted to speed up the converging process of the optimization. Since the sensitivities to design parameters can be obtained fast, the algorithm can save the computing time dynamically. A surface response method is also applied to reduce the number of field computations. (4) The developed GFMM model has been applied to design an in-wheel dual-PM-excited dual-airgap motor with single rotor and improved PMs for EV direct drive. The proposed optimization method has been employed during the optimization process of the geometric parameters and the excitation distribution of the two sets of windings of the motor. The overall performance of the designed motor has been compared with those of conventional PM motors and induction motors. Prototypes of the proposed motor and its converter have been constructed and tested.

15220215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220215.value: The developed GFMM model and its optimal design method can be applied to explore novel topologies of electric machines. Possible topologies may include: brushless field-excited/hybrid-excited machines, high torque density with multi-airgap motors, high-torque-density teeth-coupling machines with small pole pairs but high operating frequency, doubly-fed PM machines for variable-speed constant-frequency wind power generation, and mnemonic motors which can achieve flexible flux controllability by temporarily applying current pulse to magnetize/demagnetize special PM materials.

15220215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220215.value: A general theory to explain the operating principle of the basic flux-modulated motor, vernier motor, doubly-fed reluctance machine, flux-switching motor, and dual-PM-excited motor, has been proposed. Unified design guidelines of these machines, which can quickly identify the efficacy of different combinations of pole pairs of windings, PMs, special ferromagnetic segments and tooth/slots, as well as ac/dc excitations and the rotating speeds of the rotors, have been developed. A novel general pattern of PM arrangement has been presented. By optimizing its sizes, the best PM arrangement can be automatically determined. Based on the developed general theory, a method which can search possible topologies with single/double stators, single/double rotors, the combinations of pole pairs and the magnetic field rotating speeds of different parts, the frequencies in different windings, has been developed. All candidates can be quantitatively investigated using transient magnetic field, power electronic circuit, mechanical motion and thermal field coupled finite-element method (FEM). Based on the developed method, the best/novel topologies of EMs for specific applications can be determined. As an application example, the developed method has been applied to design, construct and test a motor for high-torque-density in-wheel direct-drive in electric vehicles.

15220415.label: Project Objectives
15220415.value: To develop a methodology to efficiently evaluate the three-dimensional soil displacement field around an advancing tunnel. The method will be based on energy minimisation concept, which combines the displacement mechanisms approximated by cylindrical and spherical cavity contraction theories, around the tunnel and in front of its heading, respectively. To evaluate the impacts of tunnelling operations on pile foundations, considering the three-dimensional displacement field around the tunnel. In particular, the effects in the longitudinal direction along the tunnel alignment, such as the induced pile displacements and bending moments will be presented in the form of design charts. To incorporate the building stiffness into foundation model using the matrix condensation method, and to investigate the influence of superstructure stiffness on foundation response near tunnelling operations. A series of sensitivity analyses will be performed to reveal the importance of building stiffness and orientation to pile group performance indicators, including differential settlements, distortions and tilting.

15220415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220415.value: In many major cities, urban population growth and the ensuing infrastructure needs have led to the necessity to explore the use of underground space, with the construction of underground railway systems a very popular means to meet the demands of public transportation. These, together with other infrastructure needs, give rise to the construction of tunnels in close proximity to existing buildings in densely-populated areas, many of which supported by pile foundations. Damage to these foundations can jeopardize the safety and serviceability of the existing structure, and lead to significant economic loss and project delay. Study on piled building response to tunnelling-induced ground movements involves complex interactions among the superstructure, its foundation, and the soil around the tunnelling operations. Therefore, a number of simplifications are often adopted in previous studies, many of which focused only on the foundation response in the transverse direction of the tunnel, and without rigorous consideration of the features of the superstructure. The proposed research project aims to develop an efficient methodology to evaluate the three-dimensional soil displacement field around the tunnel and ahead of its heading, by combining the displacement mechanisms of cylindrical and spherical cavity contraction through the energy minimisation concept. The displacement field thus obtained can be imposed to the analyses of pile response, in an approach usually referred to as the ‘two-stage procedure’ for the evaluation of tunnelling impacts to pile foundations. The significance of the three-dimensional analyses lies on its capability to evaluate pile deflections and bending moments in the longitudinal direction as the tunnel advances, which are often ignored in previous studies that adopt assumptions of plane-strain conditions. In addition, the superstructure stiffness of the building will be coupled to the foundation analysis tool through the matrix condensation method, resulting in holistic simulations of both superstructure and foundation behaviour. These allow more realistic analyses of the building and foundation response, in terms of the foundation differential settlements, and tilting and twisting of the structure as the tunnelling activities approach and pass by the foundation. The outcome of the proposed research will be an analysis approach which lies between approximate methods that assume the buildings as equivalent beams, and detailed three-dimensional numerical simulations that can be too time-consuming for engineering practitioners. Results from sensitivity analyses will illustrate the influence of building stiffness, orientation and structural layout on the foundation performance in both the transverse and longitudinal directions around the tunnelling operations. 隨着主要城市的人口增長，對基建設施的需求亦不斷攀升，地下空間的使用亦愈見重要。不少新建造的地下鐵路系統與管線設施都涉及隧道開挖工程，而在人口稠密的地區，這些工程往往靠近各類現有建築物。若現有建築的地下樁基礎在隧道開挖過程中遭到破壞，即整棟建築物的安全將受到影響，並將導致隧道工程的延誤及經濟損失。因此，研究隧道開挖所造成的地面沉降及鄰近的樁基礎反應至為重要。 基於泥土及結構之間相互作用的複雜性，在目前已發表的研究中，多只考慮隧道橫切面的二維平面應變，亦不充分考慮建築物上部結構的特質。本研究項目的目標是通過土體三維位移運算，建立一套模擬隧道附近的樁基礎反應的方法。三維分析的特點在於能夠在隧道開挖過程中，模擬樁柱的橫向及縱向變形和彎矩。另外，本項目擬利用矩陣凝聚法，結合建築物上部結構與地基作綜合分析，使對隧道附近的沉降及建築物傾斜的評估更為可靠。同時，透過上述的運算方法，本項目將就隧道開挖期間，鄰近建築物的朝向及結構佈置等因素對其縱向及橫向反應進行一系列敏感性分析，藉以闡述隧道工程與建築物地基的相互影響。

15220415.label: Realisation of objectives
15220415.value: The main objective of this research is to develop an efficient approach to evaluate three-dimensional displacement field around tunnels, and to assess the impacts and risks of underground construction to nearby building foundations, taking into account the ground stiffness and superstructure stiffness features. The project objectives have been achieved and the specific works that correspond to the research objectives are listed as follows: 1) A simplified method has been developed to obtain the three-dimensional soil displacement field caused by tunneling, which is subsequently applied to the analyses of piled foundations nearby. In this approach, the soil displacements around the tunnel heading are idealized by the spherical contraction model, while the cylindrical contraction model is adopted to simulate the response far away from the heading. The two deformation mechanisms are combined through a shape function, with the parameters determined using a heuristic algorithm (differential evolution) and comparisons with numerical analyses. To validate the proposed approach, the displacement fields estimated by the simplified solution and the pile group analyses are compared with three-dimensional finite difference simulations, and favorable comparisons are obtained for ground movements, pile deflections, axial forces and bending moments. 2) An analysis and optimization approach for building foundations, such as pile group and piled raft foundations, has been developed, which allows coupling of superstructure stiffness with the foundation model, through a condensed matrix representing the flexural characteristics of the superstructure. This coupled approach is implemented within a multi-objective optimization algorithm, capable of providing a series of optimized foundation designs at various amounts of material. The approach is formulated into a user-friendly program code, which helps to form a link between the structural and geotechnical professionals, as the superstructure and underground features associated with the foundation can be fully incorporated into this code. The approach also facilitates the development of design charts for foundation behavior (which can be various foundation performance indicators such as differential settlements or distortions) under various loading scenarios which can include nearby underground operations. 3) A significant component of risks related to building foundations and tunnelling or underground constructions arises from the uncertainty and spatial variations of geomaterial properties. This project also investigates their impacts on three-dimensional ground displacements and foundation displacements. Geotechnical systems including three-dimensional slopes and underground excavations have been studied, and the characterization and propagation of geotechnical uncertainty in these scenarios are investigated with their effects on foundations also evaluated. For example, using the condensed matrix approach described earlier, an extended approach has been developed to obtain the stiffness matrices for the superstructure and spatially variable subsurface domain individually, which are then coupled with foundation elements for holistic analyses of the system. This allows probabilistic assessments to be performed efficiently using surrogate modeling methods. A number of parametric studies have been performed with design charts showing the impacts of spatial variability patterns onto building foundation response. A similar approach is also applied to study the impacts of uncertain and variable soil properties on the behavior of underground construction and the ground movements nearby, which can be applied to evaluate nearby building foundation behavior.

15220415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220415.value: The study showed that sophisticated three-dimensional numerical analyses on tunnelling-foundation interactions can be reasonably approximated using an efficient and simplified approach, based on combination of cavity contraction theories that obtain the three-dimensional displacement field, and boundary element methods that evaluate the pile group performance. In particular, using five parameters in a shape function to link the cylindrical and spherical cavity contraction solutions, the displacement field can be imposed to the pile group analysis model, and the superstructure stiffness can be easily combined with the matrix condensation method. The favorable comparison with 3D finite difference modelling illustrates the potential of this efficient approach. The simple and quick approach also makes it feasible to conduct various parametric studies to assess and compare different scenarios of tunnel alignments. The matrix condensation method proposed in this study allows coupling of superstructure stiffness, and also ground stiffness with spatially variable properties, into the pile group foundation analysis models. This approach forms a link between the structural and geotechnical engineers, through which accurate global solutions can be obtained without the need for relaxing assumptions on the contribution of superstructure to the foundation system, or assumptions of homogeneous soil and rock profiles which are unrealistic. Considerations of superstructure or building stiffness effects play an important role in the evaluation of foundation behavior or relevant design processes, especially when structural elements such as shear walls contribute significantly to the settlement response of piled foundations. Meanwhile, incorporation of spatial variability in foundation analysis can reveal aspects of system response that cannot be captured by deterministic analyses, such as tilting of the foundation. With the proposed approach and the numerical tool developed in the project, the impacts of underground construction and tunnels on nearby building foundations can be efficiently assessed, where the superstructure stiffness, the underground soil conditions and associated uncertainty can be incorporated in a realistic manner.

15220415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220415.value: This project develops the framework for efficient numerical analyses of building foundations (e.g. pile groups and piled rafts) and their response under the influence of nearby tunnelling and underground constructions. Most of the study involved circular tunnel cross-sections where the cavity contraction solutions are well established. One potential area of further work would involve incorporation of other tunnel geometries or ovalisation effects that may arise during the construction. Also, while the uncertainty associated with soils has been investigated in this project, the uncertainty related to the superstructure, including loading patterns or connection between structural members, can lead to additional variability in foundation performance in the foundation-superstructure system. Another area of further research could involve incorporation of machine learning or other data analytics methods, to analyze the tunnelling measurement data (such as settlements) obtained during the earlier stages of the construction, in order to refine the estimates of future response. These refined estimates can then be used to update estimates of nearby foundation and building response during subsequent construction stages, providing early warnings if necessary. A research proposal is being developed to explore these areas.

15220415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220415.value: Constructions of tunnels and underground openings are increasingly common in major cities, due to the needs to meet the demands of urban population growth and public transportation. The new underground operations can often affect existing nearby buildings, and the assessment of such effects used to involve sophisticated numerical analyses associated with significant computational demands. In this project, a simplified approach has been developed to evaluate, efficiently and accurately, the three-dimensional ground displacement features surrounding tunnel operations. The impact of such ground displacements on nearby foundations can then be assessed, which facilitates implementation of early warning or remedial measures to ensure safety and serviceability of existing structures near the underground construction. The risks and uncertainty related to these ground engineering projects are also investigated, elucidating the effects of uncertain and spatial variable soil properties on the underground construction and building foundation response. Design charts are developed for various scenarios of soil heterogeneity, which allow practitioners to easily assess foundation reliability under such conditions.

15220715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220715.value: The field of disordered photonics is growing at an accelerated rate in recent years. Researchers have been investigating fundamental topics such as Anderson localization of light and other transport phenomena. Light scattering in disordered media has been studied extensively because of its presence in natural, as well as artificial systems. In photonics, the main research focus was on eliminating the effects of scattering, which are often damaging to a light enhancing system. However, intentionally introducing disorder in some applications actually improves device performance. In some photonic materials, it is possible to make use of the intrinsic disorder to create meaningful optical structures. This idea is often implemented in the advancement of micro- and nano-photonics. These man-made disorder structures are used in novel applications such as random laser, imaging, and spectrometry. It is possible to create disordered photonic materials that strongly scatter light at specific wavelengths and angular distributions. They may be useful in solar energy application, in the paint industry or as new light sources such as environmental lighting. Perhaps the most intriguing and revolutionary prospect of light scattering in disordered media is that the required footprint of the associated devices is very small, and can ultimately forming components of part of lab-on-a-chip systems. The understanding of random laser theory will be useful in medical diagnostics, especially in tumour diagnostics. This proposal concerns the development of novel random lasers, more specifically, solid core random fibre lasers, which was recently demonstrated for the first time in our laboratory. Polymer optical fibre will be the primary choice for the investigation, and the work may be possible to extend to the use of silica optical fibre. The flexibility, ease of fabrication and the mode confinement characteristics of an optical fibre provide an excellent platform to experimentally verify some of the published random laser theories, which are still uncertain. The key issues to be addressed in this proposal are firstly to fabricate and to characterise a range of polymer random fibre lasers in order to collect enough experimental data for verification of random laser theories. Secondly, to investigate whether the fabrication of silica random fibre laser is possible, as silica fibre requires a much higher temperature to fabricate and the nanoparticles need to withstand the high temperature. Finally, to investigate the possible devices that can be made out of random laser, and the integration of these devices into existing fibre optics sensor systems. 近年来，无序光子学（Disordered photonics）领域的研究正在加速发展。对此，研究者们已经做了一些相关的基础课题研究，比如光的安德森定域(Anderson Localization)以及其他传导现象。人们之所以对散射于无序介质里的光进行大量的研究，是因为此状态普遍存在于自然界和一些人工系统之中。目前在光子学领域，大部分研究主要集中在理解并尽量减弱光散射的效应，这种效应通常被认为是无益的。然而，对于某些特定的应用，有意引入无序性却能够改善器件的性能。在微纳光子学领域的一些研究已经表明，利用光子材料中的固有无序性来开发有用的光学结构是可能的。这些人造的无序结构被广泛应用在诸如随机激光器，成像，光谱学等领域。同时，制造可以散射特定波长以及角向分布的光的无序光子材料也是可能的。这些相关研究的开发在以太阳能为新光源的环境照明方面也有着潜在的应用。关于无序介质里光的散射最有趣以及最具革命性的前景是，相关器件所需的台面空间很小，并最终能作为光纤实验室(Lab-in-a-fibre)光子系统的组成部分。另外，对随机激光器的理论研究有益于医学诊断，尤其是肿瘤诊断，这是因为癌化人体组织的发射光谱和健康组织的发射光谱是可区分的。此项目提案旨在研发全固态芯的随机光纤激光器(Random fibre laser)，该随机光纤激光器亦是最近于我们实验室第一次展示出来。聚合物光纤将是该

15220715.label: Realisation of objectives
15220715.value: All the objectives have been achieved and the results were published in 4 journals and a patent on a new type of doped polymer optical fibre was filed. The achievements of the four objectives are briefly summarised below. Objective 1: Polymer optical fibre random lasers (POFRLs) were successfully fabricated with the “Teflon technique” by doping TiO2 nanoparticles and Rh640 perchlorate dyes into the core of POFs. The monomeric mixture was composed of methyl methacrylate (MMA) and butyl methacrylate (BMA). The monomeric mixture for the core fabrication was composed of MMA, BMA, and benzyl methacrylate (BzMA). The monomeric mixture contained 800 ppm Rh640 perchlorate dyes and 400 ppm TiO2 nanoparticles (400 nm diameter). The POF preform was heat-drawn into fiber with an outer diameter of ≈1004 µm, and a core diameter of ≈456 µm. The POFRLs were fabricated by cutting as-fabricated POF into 5 cm long pieces. One fiber end-face coated with gold mirror of reflectance 96% acted as a back reflector, and another end-face acted simply as an output coupler. From the concentration and the diameter of the doped TiO2 nanoparticles, the scattering mean free path was determined to be around 600 µm, demonstrating that our POFRLs are in weakly scattering regime. The waveguide effect provided by the POF greatly increase the multi-scattering events for light propagation and results in laser cavity with much shorter length than the scattering mean free path. The large optical gain experienced by the emission light is the root cause for random lasing phenomena. Our POFRL shows a low lasing threshold several times smaller than other reported results [Advanced Optical Materials, 2018]. Objective 2: The emission properties of the POFRL were measured by an in-house setup, which consists of a Nd:YAG pulse laser (wavelength: 532 nm, pulse width: 6 ns), a HR4000 spectrome- ter, an optical power meter, and several optical component. The laser beam was focused into a thin stripe (length: 2.5 cm, width: 1 mm) to side-pump the POFRL, using a beam expander and a cylindrical lens. The emission spectra of the POFRL were collected by a HR4000 spectrometer, which has a wavelength measurement resolution of 0.4 nm. the evolution of emission spectra recorded for the POFRL excited at different pump powers. At low pump powers (subthreshold), a broad spontaneous emission spectrum centered at 625 nm was observed and its full-width-half-max-imum (FWHM) was measured to be ≈37 nm. Several discrete narrow peaks (i.e., lasing modes) started to emerge as the pump power exceeded the laser threshold, which indicated that resonant feedback was generated in the POFRL. With increasing pump powers, the lasing modes disappeared and only one sharp peak (center wavelength: 625 nm, FWHM: 12 nm) was observed in the spectrum. A very large number of the lasing modes with different wavelengths exist in our POFRL system (several thousands) and the spectral distance between each lasing mode is much smaller than the resolution of our spectrometer. The laser threshold was calculated to be around 9.2 mJ cm−2. There are several stable laser cavities in our POFRL. The pump laser excites the fluorescent dyes to generate emission light. Due to the multi-scattering and reflection events provided by the doped TiO2 nanoparticles and waveguide configuration, the light path of the emission light significantly increases. The very large gain experienced by the emission light is the root cause for random lasing phenomena. The laser cavities are formed between several neighboring TiO2 nanoparticles together with the core-cladding interface. Since the structure of our POFRL and the positions of the doped TiO2 nanoparticles are immobile, the established laser cavities are stable, which results in random lasing at fixed wavelengths. However, the intensities of these lasing modes vary as the pump power changes. This can be attributed to the mode competition and the intrinsic statistical fluctuations of the RL. Objective 3: Potential Applications of POFRLs A) Speckle-free optical imaging One major application of RLs is speckle-free optical imaging due to their low spatial coherence. In this project, we measured the spatial coherence of our POFRLs and tested their potential in speckle-free imaging. For spatial coherence measurements, the output of the POFRL was focused by a lens to illuminate and transmit through a frosted glass. The coarse surface of the frosted glass introduced random phase delays to the transmitted light, which would create speckled image using the light sources with a high degree of spatial coherence. A totally spatial coherent light has a speckle contrast of 1, whereas a light without spatial coherence has a speckle contrast of 0. Here, the measured speckle contrast was C = 0.07, showing that the spatial coherence of our ROFRLs is very low. A control experiment realized using a 650 nm commercial laser as the illumination source gave a speckle contrast of C = 0.76. For the speckle-free imaging, a custom-made mask embedded with PolyU logo replaced the frosted glass to work as the imaging object. Under the illumination of the POFRLs, a clear speckle-free imaging was obtained. For comparison, we also tested the imaging using a 650 nm laser to illuminate the mask. Poor-quality image with speckle pattern was observed due to the high spatial coherence of the commercial laser. This suggests that our POFRLs can serve as the illumination source for the speckle-free imaging application. B) Label-free random laser cytometer We have presented a label-free random laser cytometer with the sensing strategies of the diﬀerent lasing properties tuned by the whole cell as well as the subcellular biophysical properties of the single ﬂoating cells. Three key parameters were proposed in the random laser (i.e., lasing threshold, wavelength shift, and optical path length). The lasing threshold was demonstrated strongly relevant to the whole-cell scattering of the bioﬂuids. On the other hand, the peak shift of the lasing spectra was strongly inﬂuenced by the subcellular structure of the cells (i.e., cortical shells and nuclear lamina shells). The PFT analysis further conﬁrms the inﬂuence of the cellular and subcellular structure on the random lasing properties in the random laser, leading to a sensitive and parametrized sensing strategy. By performing more measurements with diﬀerent batches of microﬂuidic devices and cells, the repeatability and reliability of our random laser is veriﬁed. A cell type classiﬁcation strategy is introduced by adapting principle component analysis, and the ﬁrst-order principle component is shown to be a good indicator for detecting cancerous cells in cell mixtures. Our work extends the biological random laser system to integrate with optoﬂuidic devices and reveals the possibility of the random-laser-based cytometer, which opens a new path for cancerous cell diagnostics using the random laser technology. Objective 4: Theoretical Model and Simulation Results We proposed a 2D four-level numerical model based on Monte Carlo dynamic to describe the lasing dynamic in the POFRLs. The numerical model is composed of the waveguide effect, immobile scatterers, and random photons walkers according to the physical configuration of our POFRL system. The simulation results show the random lasing spectra and mode competition phenomenon, which are in a qualitative agreement with the experimental observations. Our work built a preliminary connection between the theoretical models and experimental works performed in POFRL, which will benefit the future research in this field and its applications.
