15220715.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220715.value: A one-dimensional random fiber laser (RFL) based on the polymer optical fiber (POF) was successfully constructed. The core of the POF was doped with TiO2 nanoparticles and Rh640 perchlorate dyes. A multimode and coherent random lasing was successfully obtained. The waveguide effect provided by the POF greatly increased the multi-scattering events for light propagation and resulted in laser cavity with much shorter length than the scattering mean free path, allowing the realization of an efficient random laser with very low threshold power. As an illustration of potential applications, a clear speckle-free imaging was demonstrated using the POFRL as the illumination source. Furthermore, a four-level Monte Carlo method-based numerical model is proposed to describe the lasing dynamic in the POFRL. This outcome was published in the Journal of Advanced Optical Materials, February 2018. In addition, a RL cytometer is demonstrated in an optofluidic device filled with gain medium and human breast normal/cancerous cells. The multiple light scattering induced by the micro-scale human cells promotes the random lasing and influences the lasing properties in term of laser modes, spectral wavelengths, and lasing thresholds. A sensing strategy based on analyzing the lasing properties to determine both the whole-cell and the subcellular biophysical properties of the cells and the malignant alterations of the cell suspensions are successfully detected. The results were published in the Journal of ACS Sensors, March 2019. A patent on a new type of polymer optical fibre using a single dopant to provide enhanced photosensitivity and waveguiding was filed. The new POF allow fibre gratings to be inscribed with low-cost He-Cd laser in just 7 msec was demonstrated. This is several orders of magnitude faster than other reported results. Potential applications of the novel POF for healthcare, including vital sign monitoring were also demonstrated successfully. The findings were reported in LIGHT: Science and Application, 2017.

15220715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220715.value: We proposed a 2D four-level numerical model based on Monte Carlo dynamic to describe the lasing dynamic in the POFRLs. The simulation results show the random lasing spectra and mode competition phenomenon, which are in a qualitative agreement with the experimental observations. Our work built a preliminary connection between the theoretical models and experimental works performed in POFRL, which will benefit the future research in this field and its applications. Further development on quantity description of the laser is necessary to advance the understanding of the POFRL. Another development is the investigation of the potential applications of the POFRLs. We demonstrated that POFRLs can be developed into a light source for speckle-free imaging.

15220715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220715.value: Random lasers (RLs) are unconventional (mirror-less) lasers whose lasing feedbacks are synergistically achieved by multiple light scattering and optical gain amplification. High efficiency, with low-threshold pump power, polymer optical fibre random lasers were successfully constructed by doping laser dyes and nanoparticles in polymer optical fibres. The use of the POFRLs as light sources for speckle-free optical imaging was investigated and the impressive result suggests that the POFRL can serve as the illumination source for speckle-free imaging applications. A new approach to design a label-free biophysical cytometer based on optofluidic random laser devices was successfully demonstrated to detect cancerous cells in cell mixtures. It reveals the possibility of the random-laser-based cytometer, which opens a new path for cancerous cell diagnostics using the random laser technology.

15221315.label: Project Objectives
15221315.value: Aim 1: Synthesis of GQDs with tunable emission spectra. GQDs will be synthesized with a bottom-up approach using citric acid as the starting material via thermal treatment. The tunable emission spectra of GQDs with enhanced quantum yield will be realized by surface modification approaches including varying oxidative groups and grafting amine groups. The emission peak shift and quantum yield of GQDs with various surface chemical groups and molar ratio will be studied. Aim 2: Establishment of GQD-peptide complex based intracellular FRET assay. The peptide substrate will be genetically synthesized with fluorescence protein mKeima-Red sequence as acceptor and caspase-3 cleavage site, with a polyarginine sequence linked on C terminus as cellular penetrating probe, GQDs will then covalently conjugate with synthesized peptide substrate using the EDC/NHS method. The quenching efficiency of GQD-peptide complex will be explored with various pair distance. The optimal pair distance and appropriate molar ratio between GQDs and peptide will be determined. Aim 3: Testing of GQD-peptide based FRET assay for in vitro caspase-3 activity detection. The prepared GQD-peptide based FRET assay will be firstly used for in vitro caspase-3 detection. The sensitivity, detection limit and specificity of this FRET assay for caspase-3 detection will be explored to optimize the performance of this FRET assay. Aim 4: Testing of GQD-peptide based intercellular FRET assay for caspase-3 activity detection in living cells. The cellular uptake process of GQD-peptide complex will be studied using Confocal Fluorescence Microscopy, Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and Mass Spectrometry. The cytotoxicity of GQD-peptide complex will also be studied. The GQD-peptide based FRET assay will then be used for caspase-3 activity detection in cancer cells during the apoptosis process induced by apoptosis stimuli and chemotherapeutic drugs in single cells. Caspase-3 activity will be monitored quantitatively by analyzing fluorescence signal change.

15221315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221315.value: 基於熒光共振現象的檢測儀已經被用於檢測活體細胞內的活動，例如細胞內蛋白-蛋白相互作用，細胞蛋白酶活動以及細胞傳輸活動。然而，傳統的供體熒光分子如有機染料和熒光蛋白有著低光穩定性，較短的熒光壽命以及較快的光致褪色。熒光納米粒子（主要是納米量子點）已經被當作好的熒光分子的替代物，具有高亮度，高光穩定性，狹窄的對稱發射頻譜以及較長的熒光壽命。然而納米量子點仍然有著細胞毒性和熒光閃爍的缺點。石墨烯量子點，作為一種新型的量子點，有著高光穩定性和低細胞毒性的優點，可用於細胞內供體熒光分子。但是基於石墨烯量子點的細胞內熒光共振分析儀還很少被研究。在本項目中，我們將致力於研發一種新型的基於石墨烯量子點的細胞內熒光共振傳感器用於單細胞內細胞雕零過程的實時檢測。這個新型的能量轉移配對以石墨烯量子點為供體及熒光蛋白mKeima-Red為受體，並以特定的肽鏈鏈接。輔助細胞穿透分子連接在肽鏈的C端以幫助FRET系統的細胞內吞。利用這種新型的FRET細胞內檢測系統，由細胞雕亡刺激和抗癌藥物引起的單個癌細胞的caspase-3蛋白酶活動將被實時監測。

15221315.label: Realisation of objectives
15221315.value: During the whole project period, all the 4 objectives have been realized. a) Graphene quantum dots (GQDs) was synthesized with a bottom-up approach using citric acid as the starting material via thermal treatment. The emission spectra of GQDs was tuned by nitrogen and sulfur element doping. It was demonstrated the nitrogen and sulfur element doping could shift the emission spectra from blue emission to green and even red emission. It has been demonstrated that the quantum yield of GQDs could be improved by passivation with PEG. Various surface functional groups including amine and carboxyl groups could be grafted on surface for further functionalization. b) The synthesized GQDs were then used to build fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) probe. The FRET probe is generally composed of donor molecules such as GQDs or fluorescent dyes, and the acceptor molecules can be gold nanoparticle (AuNPs) or molybdenum disulfide (MoS2). The functionalization of donors and acceptors could be performed via EDC/NHS method or pi-pi interactions. To explore the FRET probe performance, FRET efficiency was measured with florescence microscopy. The appropriate molar ratio between donor and acceptor molecules was optimized to achieve the FRET efficiency close to 90%. The donor-acceptor distance effect on FRET efficiency was also performed and 10 nm will be a critical distance for FRET efficiency. c) The established FRET assays have been used for cell-free experiments for both nuclide acid and peptide. FRET nanoprobe based nucleic acid detection is based on nuclide acid hybridization between single stranded DNA and the complimentary DNA conjugated on donor and acceptor molecules respectively. FRET nanoporbe for protein detection is based on aptamer-antigen recognition process. Once the antigen protein binds with aptamer probe sequence, the aptamer probe together with donor molecules would detach from acceptor surface, leading to the fluorescence signal recovery. We have applied our FRET probes for nucleic acid detection in PBS solution and for EpCAM protein detection as a cancer biomarker in PBS solution. The FRET probe for enzymatic activity detection is also explored. The sensitivity, detection limit and specificity of this FRET assays are explored. d) The established FRET probes are also used for intracellular detection. Two FRET probes were designed to monitor anti-cancer drug delivery process in cancer cell and to detect miRNAs in cancer cells in-situ. The FRET probes were functionalized with folic acid to increase cellular uptake efficiency by cancer cells expressed with FA receptors such as MCF-7 cells. The cytotoxicity and hemocompatibility of the nanoprobes were explored and the low cytotoxicity and good hemocompatibility were demonstrated. For the first FRET nanoprobe, the anti-cancer drug molecules release process in cancer cells and the caspase-3 apoptosis degree were successfully monitored. For the second nanoprobe, miRNA-21 expression as a regulator of cancer cell apoptosis was successfully monitored in single cancer cell in-situ.

15221315.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221315.value: During this project, we have successfully synthesized GQDs with good water dispersity, small size, low cytotoxicity and good fluorescence quantum yield. The element doping method could effectively modulate the emission spectra of GQDs. The passivation of GQDs with PEG could largely increase the quantum yield. The low cytotoxicity and good hemocompatibility was also demonstrated. We also designed GQD and other 2D nanomaterials based FRET nanoprobes for various biological applications for solution and intracellular cancer related detections. A novel graphene quantum dot (GQD)@Fe3O4@SiO2 based nanoprobe was reported for targeted drug delivery, sensing, dual-modal imaging and therapy. This nanoprobe has MRI and fluorescence dual imaging capability and also could monitor the drug delivery dynamic process in cancer cell. This luminomagnetic nanoprobe will be a potential platform for cancer accurate diagnosis and therapy ((Su et al., Biosensors and Bioelectronics, 2017, in Part C). We also designed a “turn-on” fluorescence biosensor based on graphene quantum dots (GQDs) and molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) nanosheets for rapid and sensitive detection of epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM). GQD conjugated with aptamer was absorbed on MoS2 surface to form a FRET sensor. The EpCAM protein in buffer solution could be sensitively and selectively detected by monitoring the fluorescence signal change. Finally this FRET sensor was also used to successfully detect cancer cell with high expression of EpCAM protein on the surface (Shi et al, Biosensors and Bioelectronics, 2017, which is mentioned in Part C). We not only want to detect cancer cells via surface protein biomarkers, but also we want to detect intracellular biomarkers of cancer cells such as miRNAs. We further developed in intracellular FRET sensor to detect intracellular miRNA-21 expression in cancer cells. The ability of this nanoprobe for endogenous miRNA-21 detection in single living cancer cells was demonstrated in MCF-7 cells which are highly expressed with miRNA-21. The specificity of this probes was also demonstrated in Hela cells which has low expression of miRNA-21 (Oudeng et al, ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, 2018, in Part C).

15221315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221315.value: The further development of graphene-like 2D nanomaterials based FRET assay include the application new 2D nanomaterials with unique optical properties for solution and intracellular detection. Moreover, another direction of the FRET assay can go to single-molecule and sub-cellular activity detection with high resolution by combining with the modern microscopy technique including super-resolution microcopies. The multiplexed FRET technique can be another direction by spectral or spatial decoding to largely increase the targets number. The functionalization of nanoparticles to establish FRET assay should be based on green chemistry to avoid possible toxicity.

15221315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221315.value: In the past years, fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) assay has been used widely in biological applications. However, traditional FRET assay is based on organic dye or fluorescence protein suffers from photo-bleaching and low sensitivity. Graphene and graphene-like 2D nanomaterials are emerging as potential materials candidate for developing novel FRET assay due to their unique properties. In this project, we develop various graphene quantum dot (GQD) based FRET nanoprobes for cancer related applications for both solution detection and intracellular detection of multiple cancer biomarkers including miRNAs, cancer protein biomarkers and anti-cancer drug delivery and induced apoptosis. Graphene-like 2D nanomaterials based FRET assays are expected to have more applications in bioensing and bioimaging applications.

15221715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221715.value: 钢筋混凝土柱截面通常呈圆形、正方形或矩形。圆形截面对应于正方形截面，适用于截面两个垂直方向所需抗力接近的情形。选择圆形而不是正方形截面通常是出于美观原因。当柱截面两个垂直方向所需抗力有显著差异时，通常选用矩形截面，而与矩形截面对应的椭圆形截面却很少被采用。除美观因素外，对于外部存在钢或FRP套箍以约束混凝土的情况，弧形截面的约束效果要远远好于正方形或矩形截面。较少使用椭圆形截面主要是因为制作及安装椭圆形柱的模板存在困难。 近年来，作为一种新型、美观的柱子形式，椭圆形钢管混凝土柱在实践中逐渐得到认可。申请人最近提出了带纵向钢筋的椭圆形FRP管约束混凝土柱（EFCCC）这一新型组合柱形式，主要用于易受恶劣环境影响而导致钢筋锈蚀的桥梁及其他结构中（例如海港结构）。EFCCC的FRP管纤维接近环向，因此主要在环向提供约束并抵抗剪力；FRP管作为外层可以防止柱内钢筋产生锈蚀，同时FRP管较钢管更易于制造及运输。因此，由于FRP管的存在，EFCCC柱具有出色的耐锈蚀能力以及极好的延性与抗震性能，在恶劣环境下的性能明显优于椭圆形钢管混凝土。 初步的轴压试验显示EFCCC具有优越的性能。该项目旨在对EFCCC在静力及地震荷载作用下的性能进行深入研究。试验研究计划包括EFCCC的单调及循环轴压试验，偏压试验，以及低周往复水平荷载试验。理论研究计划包括有限元模拟及设计方法的建立。 该项目将有力地推进FRP-混凝土-钢组合结构理论的发展，并将促使FRP和椭圆形柱在实际工程中得到更为广泛、安全、经济的应用。该项目的研究工作将会使香港、全中国以及其他地区更好地满足其对对可持续基础设施的巨大需求，并为社会经济发展做出重要的贡献。

15221715.label: Realisation of objectives
15221715.value: Overall Achievement: We have fully addressed Objectives 1 and 2. Realization of Objective 1: (1) Axial compression tests on a series of elliptical FRP tube-confined concrete columns (EFCCCs) with different sectional aspect ratios (i.e., 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5), tube thicknesses (i.e., 6-ply and 10-ply) and fibre angles (i.e., ±45°, ±60°, and ±80° to the longitudinal axis of the tube) were conducted to systematically investigate the stress-strain behaviour of confined concrete in EFCCCs. (2) A large number (more than 40) of curved coupons cut from FRP tubes of different sectional aspect ratios were tested under tension to obtain the FRP tube properties in the hoop direction. (3) A new and robust stiffness-based design-oriented stress-strain model for FRP-confined concrete in elliptical columns was proposed based on the test results of this project. Another design-oriented stress-strain model which is compatible with the relevant equations of the Chinese Technical Code for Infrastructure Application of FRP Composites (GB 50608 2010) was also proposed. (4) The rupture failure process of an elliptical FRP tube in EFCCCs is complex, but the prediction of this ultimate condition is important for understanding the behaviour of elliptical FRP tubes in EFCCCs. A numerical approach aimed at predicting this ultimate condition based on the lattice discrete particle model (LDPM) was studied. (5) In order to understand the behaviour and modelling of FRP-confined concrete in non-circular columns better, the opportunity was taken to study the behaviour of FRP-confined concrete in rectangular columns as well as square columns with section curvilinearzaion as part of the basis of the studies on EFCCCs. Realization of Objective 2: (1) An experimental program of EFCCCs under eccentric loading was completed. The effects of initial load eccentricity, bending direction, column slenderness (i.e., 900 mm, 1500 mm, 2000 mm), and sectional aspect ratio (i.e., 1.5 and 2.0) were investigated. (2) A finite element model for EFCCCs under eccentric loading based on the well-established Modified-Concrete Damaged Plasticity Model (M-CDPM) was established. (3) A theoretical column model modified from Jiang and Teng's (2012) model was developed for the simulation of EFCCCs under eccentric loading. The proposed design-oriented stress-strain models for FRP-confined concrete in elliptical columns were used in the theoretical column model. (4) The design equations for the load-carrying capacity of slender FRP-confined concrete columns in the Second Edition of the Chinese Technical Code (GB 50608 2020, to be published) were evaluated for the calculation of the load-carrying capacity of slender EFCCCs under eccentric loading. A PhD student, Mr. K.C. Liu, has been playing a major role in this research project. He started his PhD study programme on 1 September 2016 and is in his late stage of study. 15221715.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221715.value: Findings Related to Objective 1: (1) Both the ultimate axial stress and ultimate axial strain of concrete can be significantly enhanced by the confinement from an elliptical FRP tube. The sectional aspect ratio has a substantial effect on the FRP confinement effectiveness: the FRP confinement effectiveness decreases as the sectional aspect ratio increases. (2) For the specimens with a sectional aspect ratio of 2.5, the enhancement in ultimate axial stress due to FRP confinement was limited but the ultimate axial strain was still substantially enhanced. (3) The stress-strain curves of FRP coupons cut from FRP tubes with fibres at ±80° to the longitudinal axis of the tube exhibited almost linear behaviour while those of coupons cut from FRP tubes with fibres at ±45° exhibited obvious nonlinear behaviour. (4) The FRP hoop strain distribution around the circumference of an EFCCC with a sectional aspect ratio larger than 1.5 is highly non-uniform. At the ultimate condition, the maximum FRP hoop strain and FRP hoop rupture in the test EFCCCs with a sectional aspect ratio larger than 1.5 generally occurred at or near one of the major vertices (i.e., the ends of the major axis). (5) The fibre angles of the FRP tube have an obvious effect on FRP confinement effectiveness. As the fibres become more vertically oriented, the FRP confinement stiffness in the hoop direction decreases, leading to reduced confinement effectiveness from the FRP tube. Findings Related to Objective 2: (1) The test EFCCCs under eccentric loading possessed great ductility. The failure of these EFCCCs was dominated by the rupture of FRP tube at the compression side. (2) The load-carrying capacity of EFCCCs decreases with an increase in the slenderness ratio or the load eccentricity. (3) The theoretical column model using the proposed stress-strain models for FRP-confined concrete in elliptical columns was shown to predict the load-carrying capacities of the test EFCCCs under eccentric loading reasonably well; however, the ultimate displacements corresponding to FRP rupture were significantly underestimated by the column model. The latter is believed to be mainly caused by the strain gradient effect which was not considered in the proposed stress-strain models. (4) The design equations in the Second Edition of the Chinese Technical Code (GB 50608 2020) using the proposed stress-strain models for FRP-confined concrete in elliptical columns can provide reasonably accurate predictions for the load-carrying capacities of the test EFCCCs.

15221715.value: Objective 3 in the original application (i.e., To develop a theoretical model for EFCCCs subjected to seismic loading) was removed as a result of funding reduction. This objective is important and deserves further research.

15221715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221715.value: In recent years, elliptical columns in the form of concrete-filled steel tubes have gradually gained acceptance in practice as a new form of aesthetically pleasing columns. This project was aimed at understanding and modelling the behaviour of a new form of elliptical columns proposed by the PI, namely elliptical FRP tube-confined concrete columns (EFCCCs) with longitudinal steel reinforcement, mainly for use in bridges and other structures (e.g. costal structures) exposed to a severe environment where steel corrosion is a major concern. The FRP tubes in EFCCCs have fibres oriented close to the hoop direction, and thus have mechanical resistance mainly in the hoop direction for confinement and shear resistance; they also act as an external skin to protect the column from steel corrosion and are easier to fabricate and transport than elliptical steel tubes. A systematic experimental study including both axial compression tests and eccentric compression tests as well as advanced theoretical analysis was carried out in this project. The test results confirmed the excellent ductility and load resistance of EFCCCs due to the presence of the FRP tube. The research has also led to the development of a design method for EFCCCs under static loading.

15221815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221815.value: Many long-span cable-supported bridges with steel box girders have been built in recent years, and some super long-span cable-supported bridges across seas are in the planning stage. When these bridges are constructed in wind-prone regions, they can suffer considerable buffeting-induced vibration. The frequent occurrence of such buffeting-induced vibration, together with traffic-induced vibration, can cause fatigue damage to the bridges. Accurate prediction of buffeting-induced stress responses is, therefore, essential for the long-term safety of these bridges. However, the buffeting analysis methods currently used are not sufficient for this task. The buffeting analysis of long-span box girder bridges has traditionally been performed using finite element (FE) beam models of the bridges with lumped sectional buffeting forces. These sectional buffeting forces are determined primarily through wind tunnel testing of sectional girder models. The FE beam models that reduce box girders to a series of beam elements with equivalent sectional properties are insufficient for performing accurate stress analyses. Their disregard of the cross-sectional distribution of buffeting forces also encumbers the accurate prediction of stress responses. For accurate predictions of buffeting-induced stress responses, multi-scale FE models of long-span box girder bridges and distributed aerodynamic and aeroelastic forces should be taken into account. In this context, this project aims to develop a new framework for buffeting-induced stress analysis in the frequency-domain for long-span cable-supported bridges with steel box girders under distributed aerodynamic and aeroelastic forces. The project involves five major components: (1) developing the multi-scale modelling and model updating methods for long-span cable-supported bridges with box girders; (2) identifying the distributed aerodynamic forces and their spatial correlations over box girders through wind tunnel pressure tests on motionless sectional models; (3) identifying the distributed aeroelastic forces on box girders through wind tunnel pressure tests on aeroelastic sectional models; (4) developing a framework for determining buffeting-induced stress responses based on the multi-scale bridge model and distributed buffeting forces; and (5) examining the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed framework by taking the Stonecutters Bridge in Hong Kong as a case study and examining the field measurement data recorded by a structural health monitoring system (SHMS) installed in the bridge. The success of the project will lay a solid foundation for fatigue damage prognosis calculations for long-span cable-supported bridges under combined wind and traffic loadings. The research assistants involved will be educated to develop the skills of high-quality researchers over the course of the project.

15221815.label: Realisation of objectives
15221815.value: Objective 1. To develop multi-scale modelling and model updating methods for long-span cable-supported bridges with steel box girders. A multi-scale modelling method for long-span cable-supported bridges with steel box girders has been developed. The box girder is modeled with shell elements in detailed geometry while other components of the bridge are modeled using either beam or truss elements. Each segment of the girder is then condensed into a super-element with the sub-structuring method to reduce the number of degrees of freedom (DOFs), thus saving computation time for the subsequent buffeting analysis. The Stonecutters cable-stayed bridge is taken as a case study to demonstrate how to establish a 3D multi-scale finite element (FE) model. A novel model updating strategy has been developed to facilitate the model updating of the multi-scale FE model of a long-span cable-supported bridge. The model updating uses both modal frequencies and multi-scale (displacement and stress) influence lines as updating objectives and adopts response surface method in optimization process to reduce computation time. The proposed model-updating method is applied to the multi-scale FE model of the Stonecutters Bridge. The updated results show that the proposed model-updating method can reduce the differences not only between the measured and computed modal frequencies but also between the measured and computed influence lines. Objective 2. To identify the distributed aerodynamic forces on box girders and their spatial correlations using wind tunnel pressure tests on motionless sectional models. A framework for modelling distributed aerodynamic pressures on the surfaces of a bridge deck section has been proposed in terms of the proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method. The characteristics of distributed aerodynamic pressures, such as pressure coefficients, space functions (pressure modes), principal coordinates, pressure modal coefficients, and pressure modal admittance functions are introduced. Wind tunnel pressure tests of a sectional motionless bridge deck model are conducted to identify the aerodynamic characteristics of distributed aerodynamic pressures on the surfaces of the Stonecutters Bridge. The pressure coefficients, pressure modes, pressure modal coefficients, and principal coordinates are obtained from the measured distributed aerodynamic pressures. The pressure modal admittance functions are identified by using a colligated least-squares method to the auto and cross spectra of the measured wind speeds and pressures. The reconstructed distributed aerodynamic pressures are compared with the measured ones. The results show that the higher-order POD pressure modes provide a very limited contribution and can be truncated without notable loss of accuracy. The aerodynamic pressures distributed over the bridge deck surface can be well represented by a superposition of a limited number of the first few POD pressure modes. The use of pressure modal admittance functions greatly simplifies the identification of many individual aerodynamic pressure admittance functions. The spanwise correlation of wind-induced pressures over the surface of a twin-box bridge deck has been investigated. Each POD pressure mode obtained is likely to be associated with a particular excitation mechanism. Since the spanwise correlation of each pressure component can be quite different from others, the indicial functions are introduced to separate the aeroelastic component from the aerodynamic component. The empirical mode decomposition (EMD) method is applied to the aerodynamic component to further separate the incident turbulence-induced component from the signature turbulence-induced counterpart. The spanwise correlation coefficient and root coherence of each pressure component are investigated by using the pressure data measured from wind tunnel tests on a spring-suspended sectional twin-box deck model. The results show that the spanwise correlation coefficients of the aeroelastic pressures are close to 1. The root coherence of the signature turbulence-induced pressures shows completely different characteristics from incident turbulence-induced pressures. A new coherence fitting scheme for signature turbulence-induced pressures is proposed. With this framework, the root coherence of each component pressures can be obtained, and the root coherence of the pressures at any two points on the surface of the twin-box deck can be reconstructed. Objective 3. To identify distributed aeroelastic forces on box girders and the aeroelastic damping and stiffness matrices using wind tunnel pressure tests on aeroelastic sectional models. Distributed aeroelastic forces on a bridge deck, as well as the associated stiffness and damping matrices, can be obtained from pressure tests on an aeroleastic deck sectional model. The model section represents the typical deck geometry of the Stonecutters Bridge with a length scale of 1:50. The turbulent wind, wind-induced pressures, and displacements are recorded simultaneously during the test. The joint modelling of distributed aerodynamic and aeroelastic pressures on the bridge has been proposed. With the pressure modal coefficients, covariance modes, and principal coordinates calculated from the measured distributed pressures, the pressure modal derivatives are identified. Thereupon, the aerodynamic and aeroelastic components of the pressure modes are separated, and the pressure modal admittance functions are then identified with the isolated aerodynamic components. The results show that the aerodynamic and aeroelastic components of wind-induced pressures can be separated successfully and the distributed pressures on the deck can be well reconstructed with a limited number of POD pressure modes. Objective 4. To develop a framework for determining buffeting-induced stress responses in the frequency domain based on the multi-scale bridge model and distributed buffeting forces. The framework for stress-level buffeting analysis of a long-span cable-stayed bridge with a steel box deck has been developed. The distributed aerodynamic and aeroelastic pressures on the surface of the twin-box deck are modeled in terms of POD pressure modes. The substructure modelling scheme is adopted to construct the FE model of the bridge so that POD pressure modes can be applied and both global (displacement and acceleration) and local (stress) responses of the bridge can be captured accurately and simultaneously. The pseudo-excitation method is used to solve the governing equations for buffeting-induced stress analysis in the frequency domain. Objective 5. To examine the feasibility of the proposed framework by taking the Stonecutters Bridge as a numerical case study. The Stonecutters cable-stayed bridge under Typhoon Hato is selected to examine the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed framework for determining buffeting-induced stress responses. The global and local responses of the bridge under Typhoon Hato are computed using the proposed framework and compared with the measured ones recorded by the wind and structural health monitoring system installed in the bridge. The calculated vertical displacement responses and spectra of the bridge deck at the middle and quarter-span match well with the measured ones. The calculated acceleration responses and spectra agree well with the measured ones. Because the measured and calculated spectra are very close to each other at the natural frequencies of the bridge, one may infer that the aerodynamic parameters identified by wind tunnel tests are quite reliable. The dynamic stress responses are not very large at the measurement points selected. A good agreement can be found at most measurement points between the measured and computed stress responses. It is also found that the stress distribution is not uniform and the stress distribution on the windward box is different from that on the leeward box. However, these areas are not easy to be directly measured by strain gauges due to the narrow space inside the box. This confirms the necessity of the proposed framework for buffeting-induced stress analysis.

15221815.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221815.value: (1) A multi-scale modeling method has been developed for stress-level buffeting analysis of a long-span cable-supported bridge. The bridge deck is modeled in detail with shell elements whereas other components of the bridge are modeled using either beam or truss elements Each deck segment is condensed into a super-element by the sub-structuring method. A multi-scale finite element model has been established for the Stonecutters Bridge (Zhu et al. 2015). (2) A multi-scale model updating method has been developed and applied to the Stonecutters Bridge. The modal frequencies, displacement and stress influence lines measured by the structural health monitoring system are used as updating objectives. The results show that the method can enhance the model accuracy significantly (Xiang et al. 2015). (3) The new framework for modelling distributed aerodynamic pressures on the surfaces of a bridge deck section has been developed in terms of the proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method. The framework has been applied to the motionless twin-box sectional model of the Stonecutters Bridge (Tan, et al. 2018a). (4) The POD based modelling method has been extended for both distributed aerodynamic and aeroelastic pressures over a bridge deck. The indicial functions are used to identify the pressure modal admittances and derivatives. A re-identification process has also been introduced to obtain the accurate pressure modal admittances. The proposed method has been applied to a typical twin-box deck section of the Stonecutters Bridge via free-vibration wind-pressure aeroelastic sectional-model tests (Tan et al. 2018b) (5) The spanwise correlation of wind-induced pressures over the surface of a twin-box bridge deck has been investigated. The spanwise correlation is quantified for aeroelastic and aerodynamic components, in which the aerodynamic component is further separated into both incident and signature turbulence-induced component (Tan et al. 2018c) (6) A new framework for buffeting-induced stress analysis of long-span twin-box-deck bridges has been presented. The characteristic parameters of POD pressure modes are all identified from wind tunnel pressure tests on a spring-suspended sectional deck model (Zhu, et al. 2016; Xu et al. 2019). (7) The Stonecutters Bridge under Typhoon Hato has been selected to examine the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed framework. The comparative results show a good agreement between the computed and measured responses and confirm the necessity of the proposed framework for buffeting-induced stress analysis (Xu et al. 2019). A total of seven peer-reviewed papers have been published in the top international journals.

15221815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221815.value: The linear quasi-steady theory has been adopted in this study to achieve a simplified expression of the wind-induced pressures on the bridge deck, and the unsteady effect was then taken into account by aerodynamic and aeroelastic parameters obtained from wind tunnel tests. To fully consider the fluid-structure interaction, further investigations are required to deal with the nonlinear effects.

15221815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221815.value: Many long-span cable-supported bridges have been built across the world. When these bridges are located in strong wind regions, buffeting-induced stress responses are imperative for the assessment of local failure and fatigue damage. This study thus focuses on the stress-level buffeting analysis of a long-span twin-box-deck bridge considering both aerodynamic and aeroelastic pressures in terms of POD pressure modes. This study proposed an appropriate modelling method for the distributed aerodynamic and aeroelastic pressures on the surface of the twin-box deck of a long-span bridge by introducing a powerful statistical tool named proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), revealed the characteristics of POD pressure modes, determined parameters of POD pressure modes through wind tunnel pressure tests on an aeroelastic sectional model, separated aerodynamic and aeroelastic components, analyzed the spanwise correlation of each pressure component, developed a new framework for buffeting-induced stress analysis of long-span twin-box-deck bridges based on the POD pressure modes and a substructure FE model, applied the proposed framework to the multi-scale FE model of the Stonecutters Bridge, and examined the feasibility and accuracy by comparing with the field measurement data recorded by the SHM system.The project has been successfully completed.

15221915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221915.value: It is well known that life expectancy has been increasing since the end of the Second World War due to fast economic growth, which naturally leads to better nutrition and medical services. However, it is also recognized that quality of life is not necessarily commensurate with economic growth. One obvious example is the unavoidable health deterioration accompanying aging or aging related illness, such as hip joint failure caused by degenerative arthritis. At the advanced stage of the disease, hip joint failure requires surgical replacement with a prosthetic implant, that is, an artificial hip joint. Artificial hip joints consist of two basic components, the hip stem with a femoral head and a metal cup with liner. The femoral head is ball-shaped and fits into the cup liner, forming a ball-and-socket point. CoCrMo alloy is up to now the most popular femoral head material while ultrahigh-molecular-weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) is commonly used for making the liner. Though artificial hip joints have been employed for patients successfully for many years, failure due to various causes is not uncommon, and among these causes is the wear loss of both the liner and the femoral head, which limits the life of total hip replacement to about 15 years. Thus decreasing the wear rate of both the femoral head ball and the socket liner would be an important goal for extending the life of hip replacement, which would consequently reduce the number of remedial surgery. In this respect, developing a coating on the femoral head to reduce friction and wear is an attractive solution in extending the life of total hip replacement as it does not alter the bulk mechanical properties of the components in the artificial hip joint. There are a number of surface treatment techniques for fabricating wear resistant coatings, each with its special features, merits and shortcomings. Among these techniques, the sol-gel method is well known for its versatility in coating composition, ease of application and formation of multilayers, relatively low processing temperature, and suitability for substrates of different geometries. The present project aims at developing a sol-gel coating consisting of zirconia with graphene nanosheets, a composite coating which is expected to be self-lubricating and wear resistant. Laser texturing of the femoral head surface for enhancing coating adhesion will also be thoroughly investigated as coating adhesion is a major difficulty in sol-gel technique.

15221915.label: Realisation of objectives
15221915.value: The present project aims at prolonging the service life of the artificial hip joint via modifying the CoCrMo femoral head and the UHMWPE mating surface. The major objective is to protect the UHMWPE articulating surface during abrasive wear against coated CoCrMo in simulated body fluid. Achievement of the individual objectives are detailed below. Objective 1. To determine the optimal composition of a graphene nanosheets/ magnesia-reinforced-zirconia composite coating (% of GNs). The hip implant consists of a femoral head made of CoCrMo and a cup made of UHMWPE, constituting a ball-and-socket system with the metal and polymer surfaces forming an articulating pair. To reduce friction and wear between these surfaces, a ZrO2 sol-gel coating was prepared on the CoCrMo head, to protect it against wear and release of metallic ions in body fluid. In order to reduce the friction between these articulating surfaces, a solid lubricant is required. In the present project graphene nanosheets were employed to achieve this objective. These nanosheets could be incorporated in the ZrO2 sol-gel coating or in the UHMWPE counter-part. Our experimental results clearly show that addition of graphene nanosheets to UHMWPE is much more effective in reducing friction and protecting both articulating surfaces than graphene incorporation in the sol-gel coating on CoCrMo. To determine the optimal amount of graphene in the UHMWPE-G composite, different amounts of graphene nanosheets (in wt%: 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1 and 2%) were added, aiming at achieving the lowest coefficient of friction and hence wear loss of UHMWPE. When the graphene content was too low, lubrication was inadequate while when it is too high defects were present in UHMWPE. The best wear-resistant composite was obtained at 0.2 wt% of graphene. Objective 2. To optimize the sol-gel coating process parameters and compare the effect of thermal annealing and hydrothermal treatment on the quality of sol-gel coatings. In preparing ZrO2 coatings on CoCrMo substrate, the most important processing parameter in affecting coating quality is the sintering temperature. In the present work CoCrMo plates were coated by dipping in the precursor solution and the coated samples were then sintered at different temperatures (from 300 °C to 700 °C) for 2 h with a heating rate of 10 °C/min, for densification and crystallization of the sol-gel coating. The effect of sintering at such temperatures would not affect the phase and hence the properties of the CoCrMo substrate according to results of previous studies. The quality of the sol-gel coating was evaluated using the scratch test. The critical load values in the scratch test show that sintering at 500 °C (sample designated as T500) would yield the highest adhesion strength. Thus sample T500 was selected for further investigation in other tests. Sol-gel zirconia coating on metals prepared at appropriate sintering temperature has been reported to result is good adhesion because its elastic modulus and thermal expansion coefficient are very close to metals such as steels and CoCr alloys. When the sintering temperature was too low, crystallization was incomplete while when it was too high micro cracks were formed on the surface. An appropriate sintering temperature (500 °C) would yield an intact coating of about 0.5 μm on the substrate. For comparison, ZrO2 coatings on CoCrMo substrate was also prepared using hydrothermal treatment at 200 °C followed by calcination in N2 atmosphere at 600 °C. A thicker coating (more than 10 μm) was obtained, but with cracks present in the coating. Thus it is concluded that sintering at an appropriate temperature would yield coatings of better quality than hydrothermal treatment. Objective 3. To determine the optimal coating thickness or number of coating layers with respect to wear against UHMWPE. The experimental results in the present study show that for high quality ZrO2 coatings the thickness should not exceed 1 μm. At higher thickness the coating adhesion becomes poor and cracks begin to appear. In addition, in the abrasive wear test between the articulating surfaces, UHMWPE is the much less wear resistant part. Thus a thick ZrO2 coating does not contribute to the life of the mating pair. Objective 4. To investigate the effect of laser texturing geometries of the substrate on the adhesion strength of the sol-gel coating. The adhesion strength of ZrO2 sol-gel coating on CoCrMo substrate is expected to be greatly influenced by the surface texture of the substrate. Laser texturing was attempted as previously planned. However, due to the small thickness of the sol-gel coating, the laser treated surface was too rough compared with the thickness of the coating, leading to poor adhesion. To solve the issue of substrate surface morphology wet pretreatment of the substrate was attempted. Two types of pretreatment, namely, electro-etching and electrodeposition of Co, were used to create different surface morphology on the substrate. It is found that electrodeposition under appropriate conditions (current density of 100 mA/cm2 for 150 s) could effectively increase the adhesion strength. The improvement could be attributed to the creation of a densely populated “prolate spheroids”, which provided both increased contact area and better mechanical interlocking.

15221915.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221915.value: 1. System design. The conventional approach of reducing the wear rate of the articulating surfaces in an artificial hip joint involves surface modification of the CoCrMo head, usually hardening the surface or by some kind of coating, with little attention paid to the UHMWPE counter-part. Different from this conventional approach, the present work introduced graphene nanosheets in the UHMWPE liner as a reservoir of solid lubricant. On the CoCrMo head ZrO2 coating was prepared by the sol-gel method. The results of the present work show that such a design is capable of reducing the wear rate of the UHMWPE surface and the rate of release of metallic ions (corrosion products) from CoCrMo. These important research findings are published in W. Zai, M.H. Wong, H.C. Man*. ‘Improving the wear and corrosion resistance of CoCrMo-UHMWPE articulating surfaces in the presence of an electrolyte’, Appl. Surf Sci., 464 (2019). 404-411. [Item 2 in Part C] 2. Optimization. In preparing the ZrO2 coating on CoCrMo via a sol-gel route, processing parameters have to be carefully selected to achieve the best result. A sintering temperature of 500 °C and a coating thickness of around 0.5 µm would yield a smooth and fully crystallized coating, with strong adhesion to the substrate. The amount of graphene nanosheets to be added in UHMWPE is also of critical importance. By varying the graphene content and repeating the wear test, the optimal amount is determined to be around 0.2 wt%. These results are reported in Item 2, Part C. In addition, dip coating with subsequent sintering is found to yield ZrO2 coating of higher quality than that via the hydrothermal route, as reported in. L.J.Zhao, W.Zai, M.H.Wong, H.C.Man*. ‘Hydrothermal synthesis of Ag-ZrO2/r-GO coating on CoCrMo substrate’, Materials Letters Volume 228 (2018) 314-317. [Item 3 of Part C] 3. Surface pretreatment of CoCrMo The surface morphology of the CoCrMo substrate has an important role to play in coating adhesion. Three types of surface pretreatment were attempted in the present study, including polishing, electro-etching and electrodeposition of Co ‘islands’ on the substrate. Scratch testing show that electrodeposition resulted in the highest adhesion strength. These results are reported in W. Zai, C.L.Wu, H.C.Man*. ‘Improving adhesion strength of sol-gel coating on CoCrMo by electrochemical pretreatment’, Materials Letters 270, (2020) 127696. [Item 1 in Part C]

15221915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221915.value: The work in the present project mainly addresses issues related to wear and corrosion, which are major problems in the service life of artificial hip joints. However this is only the first stage in the development of modified hip joints and only preliminary results were obtained. Before the joint can be convincingly implanted in the human body, two classes of research work for further development of project have to be completed. The first class of work would involve in vitro biological tests of the debris and substances released during wear test in simulated body fluid. Such tests should show non-toxic and non-allergic properties of the debris and substances released. The second class of work would involve long-term high-cycle wear test to evaluate the stability and durability of the system.

15221915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221915.value: One very common illness among the elderlies is degeneration of bones and joints, resulting in pains and fractures. At the later stage of the illness, an artificial hip joint is required to restore mobility and normal life style. An artificial hip joint consists of two basic components, a hip stem with femoral head (made of CoCrMo, a metallic material) and a metal cup with liner (made of UHMWPE, a polymeric material). The femoral head and the liner are in constant contact and under abrasive wear. When the degree of damage due to wear is serious, mechanical stability of the joint is compromised, which may result in discomfort or even pain on the part of the patient. In addition, when wear and/or corrosion occurs on CoCrMo, metallic ions are released into the human body, and this is may lead to health issues. To address the wear issue a ceramic coating (ZrO2) was prepared on CoCrMo surface and graphene nanosheets were added to UHMWPE. The hard ceramic coating and the lubricating effect of graphene together greatly reduced the wear rate. In addition, the ceramic coating also prevented the release of metallic ions from CoCrMo.

15222115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222115.value: Soil contamination is a prevalent and costly problem that imposes long-term risks to human health and surrounding ecosystems. Large areas of arable land contaminated by heavy metals are arousing intensive concerns about food safety and water security in many countries, while former industrial areas also require proper remediation before land re-development. In view of this grand challenge, in-situ physicochemical remediation approach has attracted considerable interests, because it is a relatively low-cost and low-impact remediation strategy that addresses widespread contamination in its original place without the need for soil excavation and transportation. This proposal suggests a novel integration of biodegradable chelant-enhanced metal extraction and biochar soil amendment for in-situ remediation of contaminated soils. Biodegradable chelants are environmentally friendly metal extractants that display minimal residual effect of eco-toxicity. Biochars derived from waste biomass are potentially promising soil amendment materials to render the toxic metals immobile and non-bioavailable, which also enable resource recycling and prove effective for improving soil quality and crop yield. Therefore, our approach proposes to accelerate metal extraction from the contaminated soils by using biodegradable chelants in the first place, and then foster subsequent high-affinity metal immobilization by tailored biochars upon facile biodegradation of unrecovered metal-chelant complexes. This proposed strategy aims to prevent unintended metal leaching due to the application of biodegradable chelants while accomplishing tenable and persistent metal immobilization in the biochar-amended soils. The project will establish comprehensive, fundamental understanding of the interactions between heavy metals, biodegradable chelants, and biochar surfaces under varying conditions that are relevant to the environment and land uses. Scientific questions that will be addressed in this study include: roles and tunability of biochar surface chemistry, kinetic interactions of metal-chelant complexes and dissolved metals with tailored biochars, fate and transport of metal-chelant complexes in the biochar-amended soils, as well as mechanisms of metal immobilization at the solid-liquid interface. Multiple lines of evidences will be obtained through specifically designed bench-scale experiments and spectroscopic investigations. Measurable success will be demonstrated using physicochemical and biological endpoints. These findings will provide good science for boosting a low-impact and value-added innovation as well as developing a science-informed remediation strategy. 土壤污染問題日漸普遍，而且處理成本高昂，對人體健康以及周邊的生態系統造成長遠危機。在許多國家，大面積受重金屬污染的耕地已引起人們對糧食安全和水體保護的密切關注，而前工業區的土地再利用亦需預先採取適當的修復措施。鑑於這一重大挑戰，原位物理化學修復方法吸引廣泛興趣，因它無需挖土與運輸，能就地解決廣泛的土壤污染問題，是一種相對低成本和低影響的修復策略。 本項目對原位修復污染土壤提出創新結合可生物降解螯合劑和用作土壤改良劑的生物炭。可生物降解的螯合劑是一種環境友好型金屬萃取劑，其殘餘物對生態的毒性影響最小。由廢棄生物質提取的生物炭是極具潛力的土壤改良劑，不僅能固定有毒金屬使其不可被生物利用，同時有效地改善土壤特性，提高農作物產量，使廢棄資源得以回收利用。我們的方案先利用可生物降解的螯合劑加速金屬從污染土壤中的萃取，隨後利用特定的、具金屬固定高親和力的生物炭促進對殘留金屬的固定。此次研究策略旨在防止因螯合劑的應用帶來意外的金屬遷移，同時在生物炭改善的土壤中實現持久的金屬固定。 此項目將對重金屬、可生物降解螯合劑和生物炭表面在不同環境和土壤條件下的相互作用建立全面和根本的理解。本項目涉及的科學探討包括：生物炭的表面化學作用分析及其可調設性；金屬螯合物、可溶性金屬及特製的生物炭之間的動態作用分析；金屬螯合物在生物炭改良的土壤中的遷移；以及金屬在固液相界面的固定機理。專門設計的實驗室規模試驗和光譜分析將提供不同角度的科學證明。研究的成效將以可量度的物理化學和生物學測試終點表達。這些研究結果將促進以科學依據為基礎，發展低影響及具增值效益的創新土壤修復技術。

15222115.label: Realisation of objectives
15222115.value: While chelant-enhanced soil washing has been widely studied for metal extraction from contaminated soils, there are concerns about destabilization and leaching of residual metals after remediation. This study integrated 2-h soil washing enhanced by biodegradable ethylenediaminedisuccinic acid (EDDS) and 2-month stabilization using agricultural waste product (soybean stover biochar pyrolyzed at 300 and 700 °C), industrial by-product (coal fly ash (CFA)), and their mixture. After integration with 2-month stabilization, the leachability and mobility of residual metals (Cu, Zn, and Pb) in the field-contaminated soil were significantly reduced, especially for Cu, in comparison with 2-h EDDS washing alone. This suggested that the metals destabilized by EDDS-washing could be immobilized by subsequent stabilization with biochar and CFA. Moreover, when the remediation performance was evaluated for phytoavailability and bioaccessibility, prior EDDS washing helped to achieve a greater reduction in the bioavailable fraction of metals than sole stabilization treatment. This was probably because the weakly-bound metals were first removed by EDDS washing before stabilization. Both individual and combined applications of biochar and CFA showed comparable effectiveness regardless of the difference in material properties, possibly due to the high level of amendments (150 ton ha−1). Based on the mobility and bioaccessibility results, the estimated human health risk (primarily resulting from Pb) could be mitigated to an acceptable level in water consumption pathway or reduced by half in soil ingestion pathway. These results suggest that an integration of EDDS washing with soil stabilization can alleviate post-remediation impacts of residual metals in the treated soil. To enhance extraction of strongly bound metals from oxide minerals and organic matter, this study examined the sequential use of reductants, oxidants, alkaline solvents and organic acids followed by a biodegradable chelating agent (EDDS) in a two-stage soil washing. In addition to extraction efficiency, this study also examined the fate of residual metals (e.g., leachability, bioaccessibility, and distribution) and the soil quality parameters (i.e., cytotoxicity, enzyme activities, and available nutrients). The reductants (dithionite-citrate-bicarbonate and hydroxylamine hydrochloride) effectively extracted metals by mineral dissolution, but elevated the leachability and bioaccessibility of metals due to the transformation from Fe/Mn oxides to labile fractions. Subsequent EDDS washing was found necessary to mitigate the residual risks. In comparison, prior washing by oxidants (persulphate, hypochlorite, and hydrogen peroxide) was marginally useful because of limited amount of soil organic matter. Prior washing by alkaline solvents (sodium hydroxide and sodium bicarbonate) was also ineffective due to metal precipitation. In contrast, prior washing by low-molecular-weight organic acids (citrate and oxalate) improved the extraction efficiency. Compared to hydroxylamine hydrochloride, citrate and oxalate induced lower cytotoxicity (Microtox) and allowed higher enzyme activities (dehydrogenase, acid phosphatase, and urease) and soil nutrients (available nitrogen and phosphorus), which would facilitate reuse of the treated soil. Therefore, while sequential washing proved to enhance extraction efficacy, the selection of chemical agents besides EDDS should also include the consideration of effects on metal leachability/bioaccessibility and soil quality. Soil washing and stabilization as a two-step soil remediation strategy was performed to remediate Pb- and Cu-contaminated soils from shooting range and railway sites. Ferric nitrate (Fe(NO3)3) and EDDS were used as washing agents, whereas three types of sludge-derived biochars and phosphogypsum were employed as soil stabilizers. While Fe(NO3)3 extracted larger amounts of metals compared to EDDS (84% Pb and 64% Cu from shooting range soil; 30% Pb and 40% Cu from railway site soil), it caused severe soil acidification. Both Fe(NO3)3 and EDDS washing enhanced the mobility of residual metals in the two soils, which in most cases could be mitigated by subsequent 2-month stabilization by sludge-derived biochars or phosphogypsum. By contrast, the metal bioaccessibility could only be reduced by soil washing. Nutrient-rich sludge-derived biochar replenished available P and K in both soils, whereas Fe(NO3)3 washing provided available nitrogen (N). Soil amendment enhanced acid phosphatase activity but marginally improved soil dehydrogenase and urease activity in the treated soils, possibly due to the influence of residual metals. This study supported the integration of soil washing (by Fe(NO3)3 or EDDS) with soil stabilization (by sludge-derived biochars or phosphogypsum) for accomplishing the reduction of metal mobility and bioaccessibility, while restoring the environmental quality of the treated soils. Ageing is a common phenomenon during biochar storage and its soil application. In this study, we exposed sludge-derived biochar (SDBC) in the air under 4 °C, 22 °C, and 45 °C for 30–120 d to imitate the ageing process after SDBC production. The aged SDBC was characterized and its sorption capacities for Pb(II), Cr(V) and As(III) were compared with the fresh ones in batch sorption experiments. The results showed an increase in acidity, cation exchange capacity, and carboxyl groups of SDBC surface, but a decrease in alkalinity and Fe(III) species during ageing, indicating the oxidation. In addition, ageing for more than 30 d was found to favor the Pb(II) and As(III) sorption, because of higher density of available oxygen-containing groups. The Cr(VI) sorption was found to be compromised by the ageing, because some reducing agents for Cr(VI) reduction was consumed there. Higher temperatures accelerated the above-mentioned ageing effect. Yet, when the SDBC was applied in the heavy-metal contaminated soil, its performance would be affected by both ageing of SDBC itself as well as long-term interactions among soil components, such as colloids and solution, heavy metals, and SDBC, which require further investigation. A novel biochar composite impregnated with α-FeOOH nanorods in hierarchical porous structures (α-FeOOH@PC) was synthesized by molten salt assisted carbonization of corn straws and hydrothermal treatment for crystallization of adsorbed ferric ions within carboxyl functionalized porous carbon. The structures and surface properties of biochar composites were characterized by scanning electron microscopy images (SEM), Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), Raman spectra, and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) analysis. The active α-FeOOH nanocrystals were encapsulated in the gradient porous biochar framework (macropores-mesopores-micropores) via C-O-Fe bonding. The α-FeOOH@PC composites presented excellent performance of both goethite containing a large amount of reactive surface hydroxyl sites and porous carbon consisting of large surface area and huge porous volume. The α-FeOOH@PC composites outperformed other sorbents for copper removal (adsorption capacity of 144.7 mg g−1). The synergistic effects of α-FeOOH and porous carbon in the biochar composite profoundly improved the removal efficiency (71.9%) compared to those of individual porous carbon foam (42.3%) and α-FeOOH nanorods (6.7%). A high adsorption capacity of 124.4 mg g−1 was maintained after three adsorption-desorption cycles. This study suggests that biochar composite is a potentially promising candidate for environmental remediation. This study engineers corn stalk-derived biochar with abundant hydrophilic functional groups as a support material for iron nanoparticles impregnation (nZVI-HCS). Surface chemistry and morphology of nZVI-HCS composites is characterized by SEM, TEM, TG, XRD, FTIR, XPS, and BET techniques, which helps to elucidate the mechanisms of Pb2+, Cu2+ and Zn2+ removal from single and mixed-metal solutions in batch experiments. Equilibrium adsorption capacities can reach 195.1, 161.9 and 109.7 mg·g−1 for Pb2+, Cu2+ and Zn2+ at neutral medium after 6-h process, respectively. The engineered biochar with hierarchical pores can impregnate iron nanoparticles, serve as an adsorbent, and enhance metal reduction/precipitation. Rapid removal and high performance can be maintained after five regeneration/reuse cycles. Multiple interaction mechanisms including adsorption, precipitation, reduction and complexation are responsible for metal removal by nZVI-HCS composites, which can be a novel biowaste-derived material for wastewater treatment.

15222115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222115.value: We explored the use of the corn straw-derived porous biochar loading α-FeOOH nanocrystals with different contents for removal of metal ions. A series of α-FeOOH@biochar composites can be confirmed to contain rich oxygen functional groups, high surface area, and relative excellent slit-shaped pores by different characterization means. Highly efficient performance for metal removal can be realized using corn stalk-derived hydrophilic biochar supported nZVI. The synthesized nZVI-biochar sample was characterized by homogeneous impregnation of iron nanoparticles on the surface of biochar with hierarchical pores. The porous biochar carrier can facilitate the metal sequestration by alleviating aggregation of iron nanoparticles, enhancing metal reduction, and acting as an adsorbent itself. The co-existence of ions exerts notable influence on the removal capacity via competitive adsorption. Regeneration/reuse tests further suggested the potential applicability of engineered biochar composites. Therefore, the combination of porous biochar and nanoscale iron minerals or metal oxides into biochar composites can provide synergistic effects and serve as highly efficient and low-cost materials for environmental remediation, which deserve further studies in the future.

15222115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222115.value: This study integrated chemical-enhanced washing with subsequent soil stabilization using biochar for mitigating the impact of residual metals. The washing results supported that ferric salt was better for metal extraction than EDDS for the shooting range soil. The sludge-derived biochars from different sewage treatment processes showed different pH values, BET surface area, and available nutrients contents, yet the difference in surface functional groups was not obvious. The combined applications significantly reduced the leachability and mobility of metals in the EDDS-washed soil. While the phytoavailability and bioaccessibility were reduced by stabilization, they were more effectively mitigated by prior EDDS washing that removed the weakly bound metals. Soil washing affected the soil dehydrogenase to a limited extent, yet subsequent stabilization with biochars enhanced acid phosphatase activities due to the increase of available P. This study supported that the increased mobility of residual Pb and Cu after soil washing by ferric salt and EDDS should be subsequently stabilized by biochars, which are promising options for replenishing nutrients and restoring soil health. Therefore, the integration of chemical washing with subsequent soil stabilization with engineered biochar can offer a cost-effective measure to alleviate concerns about residual metals in the treated soil.

15222215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222215.value: Hong Kong (HK) requires flexible highway pavements to have a minimum of a 40-year design life. ‘Long-life’ flexible pavement practice commonly focuses on thickness design for the control of critical strains. Recent studies, however, found that asphalt binders throughout the hot-mix asphalt (HMA) layers in some field pavements had aged severely, potentially negatively affecting their long-term performance. To address this critical concern, the proposed study aims to: (1) assess the aging characteristics of asphalt binder in HMA pavements in HK, (2) identify binder aging effects on the performance-related HMA mixture properties, and (3) find effective asphalt binder modifiers for aging control. Pavement sample cores will be obtained from 10, 29 and 36 year-old highways in HK. Asphalt binders will be recovered and tested for chemical and rheological aging indicators. The aging indicators will be converted to be consistent with historical test data. Binder aging levels at different times will be compared to assess aging evolution. The properties of binders recovered from the same sample core but at different depths will be compared pairwisely to identify vertical aging variations. Binder aging effects on the key HMA mixture properties will be investigated. Cylindrical and beam compacted HMA specimens will be subjected to accelerated aging treatments using a custom-made mixture aging vessel. Binder aging effects on the dynamic modulus of HMA mixture will be assessed using both the artificially aged specimens and those extracted from the three roads. Binder aging effects on the endurance limit of HMA mixture will be examined using the artificially aged beam specimens. Based on the physicochemical aging mechanisms of asphalt binder, antioxidants and admixtures will be studied for aging-control effectiveness. Six new asphalts, including four U.S. Strategic Highway Research Program (SHRP) core asphalts, will be modified by the additives and treated in a second type of custom-made binder aging vessel. Models will be developed to bridge the chemical and physical aging indicators for rapid assessment of aging states. The effectiveness of the additives after simulated long-term aging treatments will be compared. The outcomes of the proposed study include: (1) insights into asphalt binder aging characteristics in the field pavements in HK, (2) improved HMA dynamic modulus prediction model by incorporating binder aging effects, (3) insights into the effect of binder aging on the endurance limit of HMA mixture, and (4) effective anti-aging additives for asphalt binders. The outcomes are anticipated to help improve long-life flexible pavement design and durability locally and worldwide. 香港的公路路面需要至少有40年的設計壽命。 “長壽命”柔性路面的通常做法集中在厚度設計。但是，最近的研究發現瀝青結合料在“長壽命”柔性路面中出現嚴重老化的現象，嚴重影響了路面的長期性能。為了解決這個關鍵的問題，本研究的目的是：（1）評估瀝青混合料路面在香港的老化特性，（2）確定瀝青老化的不良效應，和（3）尋找有效的老化控制措施。 本課題將從10、29和36年的香港公路路面獲得芯樣。瀝青將被提取並測試化學和流變老化指標。老化指標將與歷史測試數據進行比較，以評估老化的演變。不同深度的提取的瀝青屬性將被用來進行比較，以確定垂直老化的變化。 本課題將使用特定的混合物老化容器對壓實的混合料試樣進行加速老化處理。經過處理後的試件將被用來做動態模量和疲勞試驗，以檢驗長期老化對瀝青混合料力學性能的影響。。 基於瀝青的物理化學老化機理，本課題將研究抗氧化劑對老化的控制效果。六種新的瀝青，其中包括四種美國戰略公路研究計劃（SHRP）的瀝青，將通過抗氧化劑進行改性。改性後的瀝青將使用特定的瀝青老化容器對其進行加速老化處理。本課題將通過老化狀態的快速評估，比較添加劑的抗氧化效果。 本課題研究成果的包括：（1）香港路面瀝青老化的特性，（2）瀝青混合料動模量隨著老化變化的模型，（3）瀝青混合料疲勞壽命隨著老化變化的模型，（4）有效的抗瀝青老化的添加劑。研究成果預計將有助於提高長壽命柔性路面的設計方法和耐用性。

15222215.label: Realisation of objectives
15222215.value: With generous support from RGC and other stakeholders such as Hong Kong Highways Department, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, and the paving industry in Hong Kong, the project has been satisfactorily completed. The original proposed objectives have been successfully achieved. Fundamental and significant findings have been made based on this project. The realisation of objectives is explained as follows. Objective one: To identify the temporal and spatial asphalt binder aging variations in long-life flexible pavements. With support from Hong Kong Highways Department and the industry, we obtained a large number of samples from the 36 year-old Tuen Mun road, 29 year-old Tolo Highways, and other roads. We also obtained information on the temporal and spatial asphalt binder aging variations on a large number of highway pavements in the United States (from the Long-term Pavement Performance programme and the Minnesota Road Test programme). It is commonly believed that asphalt binder ages very little beneath the surface. Through this study, we found that asphalt binder ages severely throughout the pavements and the actual trends are different than the current prediction models. The results have been published in a book chapter as well as in a conference. Objective two: To quantify the effects of asphalt binder aging on the dynamic modulus of HMA mixture. We developed a piece of equipment and a new method to accelerate the aging process of asphalt binders in asphalt mixtures. We also developed a piece of equipment to accelerate the aging process of pure binder. We analyzed how different aging methods affect the microscopic structure of asphalt mixtures. Based on the analysis results, we created asphalt mixtures of different aging states and systematically evaluated the effects of binder aging on the dynamic modulus of HMA mixture. During the study period, we purchased and commissioned a universal test machine (UTM) for testing the dynamic modulus. A large number of specimens were tested using the UTM. The test results are published in a journal paper and a conference paper. Objective three: To test the effects of asphalt binder aging on HMA mixture fatigue performance. We have prepared a large number of specimens based on two mixture designs. We aged the specimens to different aging conditions and tested the fatigue performance of the specimens using push-pull fatigue test method. We extracted and recovered asphalt binders from asphalt mixtures to determine their aging states and other physicochemical properties. The results provide valuable insights on how aging affects pavement performance life. The results are shared in a keynote speech and are anticipated to be published as a journal paper. Objective four: To identify potentially effective anti-aging modification solutions for asphalt binders, guided by the physicochemical aging mechanisms and assessed by simulated long-term aging treatments. From objective 1-3, we found that asphalt binder aging is the driving mechanism for the performance deterioration of asphalt pavements. Therefore, we spent a large amount of time and effort on developing methods to identify the aging susceptibility of asphalt binders in mixtures and anti-aging evaluation. We developed a new set of methods, including equipment, to evaluate the aging susceptibility of asphalt binders in mixtures. The paper has been published in a conference paper and journal paper. Overall, the research objectives are realised through well-planned experiments, theoretical and methodological developments.

15222215.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222215.value: We have made the following major findings through this study: (1) Severe asphalt aging occurs at all the pavement layers in long-life HMA pavements; (2) Asphalt binder aging is the main driving factor for the property deterioration of long-life pavements; (3) The current pavement-depth-time prediction model used in the Mechanistic-empirical Pavement Design Guide is not appropriate in predicting the long-term aging of asphalt binders in pavements; (4) Different laboratory aging methods affect the microscopic properties of asphalt binders and mixtures; (5) Asphalt mixture design has significant influence on the aging susceptibility of asphalt binders in asphalt mixtures. (6) The diffusion coefficient of compact asphalt mixture can serve as a good indicator to evaluate asphalt mixture’s aging susceptibility. This research has led to the following major research outcomes: (1) Two pieces of equipment were developed for accelerated aging of asphalt binder and asphalt mixture, respectively; (2) New models were developed to predict the long-term aging of asphalt binders in mixtures; (3) New methods were developed to assess the aging susceptibility of asphalt binders in mixtures. (4) Existing models for predicting the dynamic moduli of asphalt mixtures were systematically compared based on aged asphalt mixtures. (5) Strategies to improve the durability of long-life pavements were developed.

15222215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222215.value: The research can be further developed to create greater impact. Long-life pavement is the most sustainable type of pavement because it reduces the consumption of non-renewable resources, energy consumption, greenhouse gas emission, and solid waste generation. In the future, the individual research components could be synthesized to create a more comprehensive pavement design procedure for long-life pavement. In addition, a fatigue performance model could be developed based on viscoelastic continuum damage theory.

15222215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222215.value: Hong Kong has more than 2,000 kilometers of highways and roads. They are the key component of the transport infrastructure systems. It has been found that long-life pavement, with expected structural performance life of more than 40 years, is the most suitable pavement type for Hong Kong. This study evaluated the potential issues of long-life pavement with emphasis on aging-induced durability. The investigation included four components: (1) the actual aging conditions of long-life pavements in Hong Kong, (2) the effects of asphalt aging on asphalt pavement stiffness, (3) the effects of asphalt aging on asphalt pavement fatigue performance, and (4) effective measures for aging control. In the study, we have found the patterns of asphalt aging in asphalt pavements. We have developed new methods and equipment to accelerate the aging process. We have evaluated the effects of aging on asphalt pavement stiffness and fatigue. We have also identified the most effective anti-aging method, which is to improve mixture design by evaluating the diffusion coefficients of the mixture.
