15222315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222315.value: Long I/O latency posts big problems for I/O-intensive big data applications. NVDIMM (Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module) technologies provide a promising direction to solve this problem. By using non-volatile NAND flash memory as storage media and connecting through DIMM (Dual In-line Memory Module) slots, NVDIMM devices go on memory bus so the I/O overhead caused by I/O controllers can be avoided. NVDIMM has been widely supported by industries. However, existing industrial solutions largely focus on NVDIMM design issues. Our preliminary studies show that without system optimization, by mixing I/O and memory traffics, NVDIMM techniques may cause severe performance degradation for memory-intensive applications. Therefore, from a systematic point of view, new memory controller techniques and cross-layer NVDIMM management mechanisms should be investigated. There are several new challenges. First, by migrating I/O traffics to memory bus, I/O-related memory traffics will interfere with original memory traffics. Second, high-speed bursty I/O-memory traffics post new issues in NVDIMM designs. Particularly, we need to carefully manage and coordinate read/write traffics to optimize both read and write latencies while considering slow read/write/erase operations and limited endurance in NAND flash. Third, in NAND flash, when garbage collection occurs, it takes up to several milliseconds to response read/write requests. It becomes more difficult to accomplish the task in light of high-speed bursty I/O-memory traffics. In this project, based on a holistic and systematic approach, we will develop new, enabling mechanisms for NVDIMM techniques to unleash their maximum benefits on big data applications. To address the workload heterogeneity challenge, for memory controller, we will develop scheduling schemes with novel interleaving techniques so as to minimize the interference, explore new internal data forwarding techniques so as to reduce data transfer latency, and study prologue message mechanisms so request information can be passed to NVDIMMs before data transfer. Furthermore, to handle high-speed bursty I/O-memory traffics, in NVDIMM controller, new mechanisms will be studied to coordinate existing one-directional optimization schemes (e.g. prefetch and deduplication) to manage bi-directional traffics for joint optimization of read and write latencies. Finally, in NAND flash controller, we will investigate proactive garbage collection schemes to remove the long garbage collection latency from the critical path of read/write operations. This project will facilitate high-performance computing systems to most effectively utilize NVDIMM technologies to tackle the I/O bottleneck challenges in big data applications, and also contribute to the society through engaging undergraduate student research and research platform dissemination for education/training. 長的I/O訪問延遲嚴重影響I/O密集型應用的性能。NVDIMM (Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module, 雙通道直插式內存) 為解決此問題提供了一種有效的解決方案。NVDIMM方案通過將作為存儲介質的非易失性閃存NAND flash連接到DIMM上，使NVDIMM設備通過內存總線進行數據傳輸，從而避免由I/O控制器引起的延遲損耗。 NVDIMM在工業界得到了廣泛的推廣，然而，目前的工業技術方案主要集中在NVDIMM的設計問題上。NVDIMM將I/O操作和訪存操作混合在一起，利用內存總線進行數據傳輸，通過初步的研究，我們發現如果不採取系統優化策略，NVDIMM可能會導致訪存密集型應用的性能嚴重下降。因此，從系統的角度出發，在利用NVDIMM技術時，需要研究設計新的內存控制技術和跨層NVDIMM管理機制。 NVDIMM技術面臨新的挑戰。首先，NVDIMM技術將I/O引發的數據傳輸移動至內存總線上，I/O相關的內存數據傳輸可能會影響原有的內存數據請求。其次，高速的突發I/O數據傳輸操作成為NVDIMM設計面臨的一大問題。尤其是在設計的過程中，我們不僅要的管理和協調讀寫數據傳輸，從而優化讀寫延遲，同時還需要協調NAND flash本身較慢的讀、寫、擦除操作和及其使用壽命限制的問題。第三，在NAND flash中，當發生垃圾回收時，讀寫操作的延遲可高達幾個微秒，當發生高速的突發I/O數據傳輸時，此問題更加嚴重。 在本項目中，通過全面系統的方法，我們將設計一種新的NVDIMM技術，從而最大程度的發揮出其在大數據應用中的優勢。對內存控制器，針對不同負載，我們將設計新的交叉調度方案從而最小化兩種不同數據傳輸之間的相互影響，探索新的內部數據轉發技術，減少數據傳輸延遲，並研究序幕消息機制，使請求信息在數據傳輸之前首先到達NVDIMM設備。 另外，為了處理高速突發的I/O數據傳輸， 在NVDIMM控制器中，將結合現有的單向優化方案（如預取和數據去重）設計新的機制來管理雙向數據流量從而優化讀寫延遲。最后，在NAND flash控制器中，我們將研究主動垃圾回收策略，從而移除關鍵讀/寫操作路徑中由垃圾回收引發的時間延遲。 本項目將促進高性能計算機系統最有效的利用NVDIMM技術，以應對大數據應用程序中I/O瓶頸的挑戰，同時還可以鼓勵本科生參與學術研究，推廣教學、培訓研究平台的使用。

15222315.label: Realisation of objectives
15222315.value: The project has been going very well, and all objectives have been 100% achieved. With the support of this fund, two PhD students were recruited: one has successfully passed his defense in 2019; the other is expected to graduate in 2021. In total, 6 journal papers and 8 conferences have been published. For the undergraduate research, two undergraduate students, Yuanjing SHI (from HK PolyU) and Zhiqi WANG (from CUHK), have been recruited. Both pursued postgraduate study after they graduated. Objective 1 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 1, we have investigated heterogeneous-memory-workload-aware scheduling and management schemes in memory controller. New scheduling schemes with novel interleaving techniques have been developed to minimize the interference caused by heterogeneous memory traffics; internal data forwarding techniques have been designed to reduce overall memory traffics; and new prologue message mechanisms have been proposed to pass request information to NVDIMMs prior to data transfer. Specifically, in [C1], we propose novel, enabling mechanisms that allow NVDIMM to more effectively bridge the I/O performance gap for big data workloads. To address the workload heterogeneity challenge, we develop a scheduling scheme in memory controller to minimize the interference between the native and the I/O-derived memory trafﬁc by exploiting both data access criticality and resource utilization. For NVDIMM controller, several mechanisms are designed to better orchestrate trafﬁc between the memory controller and NAND ﬂash to alleviate the speed discrepancy issue. To mitigate the lengthy GC period, we propose a proactive GC scheme for the NVDIMM controller and flash controller to intelligently synchronize and transfer data involving in forthcoming garbage collection operations. We present detailed evaluation and analysis to quantify the effectiveness of our techniques with the NVDIMM design. Our experimental results show that overall the proposed techniques yield 10%∼35% performance improvements over the state-of-the-art baseline schemes. Objective 2 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 2, we have developed coordinative mechanisms for managing bi-directional traffics in NVDIMM controller. New mechanisms have been designed to coordinate existing one-directional optimization schemes such as prefetch and deduplication to manage bi-directional traffics for joint optimization of read and write latencies. Specifically, in [C8], we propose a holistic solution to address several important and challenging issues in storage data management in light of emerging NVDIMM-based architecture: namely, new performance modeling, NVDIMM-based migration, and architectural support for NVDIMMs on migration optimization. In particular, a novel NVDIMM-based heterogeneous storage performance model is proposed to effectively address bus contention issues caused by placing NVDIMMs on the memory bus. We also develop an NVDIMM-based lazy migration scheme to effectively minimize adverse effects caused by memory traffic interferences during storage data management processes. Finally, the NVDIMM-based architectural support for migration optimization is proposed to increase channel parallelism in the destination NVDIMMs and bypass buffer caches in the source NVDIMMs, so that the impact of memory traffic can be alleviated. We present detailed evaluation and analysis to quantify how well our techniques can enhance the I/O performances of big workloads via efficient heterogeneous storage hierarchy management. Our experimental results show that overall the proposed techniques yield up to 98% performance improvement over the state-of-the-art techniques. Objective 3 has been 100% achieved. For Objective 3, we have developed various non-volatile-memory optimization techniques for NAND flash and other applications. Our detailed activities are summarized as follows. First, new garbage collection schemes have been developed to remove the long garbage collection latency from the critical path of read/write operations in NAND flash storage systems. Specifically, in [J1], we develop a garbage collection scheme so it can work with CDFTL, an adaptive Caching mechanism for Demand-based Flash Translation Layer, for NAND flash memory storage systems. CDFTL adopts both the fine-grained entry-based caching mechanism to exploit temporal locality and the coarse-grained translation-page-based caching mechanism to exploit spatial locality of workloads. By selectively caching the on-demand address mappings and adaptively changing the space conﬁgurations of two granularities, CDFTL can effectively utilize the RAM space and improve the cache hit ratio. We evaluate CDFTL under a real hardware embedded platform using a variety of I/O traces. Experimental results show that our technique can achieve an 11.13% reduction in average system response time and a 35.21% reduction in translation block erase counts compared with the previous work. In [J6], we develop a special garbage collection mechanism to provide deterministic crash recovery in NAND flash storage systems. NAND flash memory has long been the dominant storage medium in mobile devices. However, power failure may occur at any time and result in loss of important data. Crash recovery therefore becomes vitally important in NAND flash memory storage systems. As flash translation layer (FTL) directly manages flash memory using various metadata, the problem of FTL crash recovery in NAND flash is how to efficiently and effectively maintain and recover the consistency of FTL metadata after system crash. To solve this problem, we propose DCR, a deterministic approach to crash recovery for NAND flash based storage systems. The basic idea is to exploit the determinism of FTL and reproduce events that happened between the last checkpoint and the crash point during crash recovery. Different from existing approaches which have to scan the whole flash memory chip, we show that DCR can recover the system more efficiently by only checking a limited number of blocks based on deterministic FTL operations. Finally, we propose the proactive garbage collection schemes that have been implemented to optimize NVDIMM controllers in [C1, C2, C8]. Second, following our research direction in this project, we have investigated how to exploit non-volatile-memory (NVM) techniques from various aspects such as in optimizing mobile devices [J2, J4, C5], graph computing [J3, C3], SMR storage [J5], blockchains [C4, C7], and SSD flash array [C6]. For instance, in [J2], we propose NVM-Swap by revisiting swapping for smartphones with fast, byte-addressable, non-volatile memory technologies. Instead of using flash, we build the swap area with NVM, to allow high performance without sacrificing user experience. NVM-Swap supports Lazy Swap-in, which can reduce memory copy operations by giving the swapped out pages a second chance to stay in byte-addressable NVM backed swap area. To avoid fast worn-out of certain NVM, we also propose Heap-Wear, a wear leveling algorithm that distributes writes in NVM more evenly. In [C7], we propose Re-Tangle, a novel transaction-based blockchain acceleration architecture that explores the opportunity of performing massive parallel operations by exploiting ReRAM, an emerging non-volatile-memory technique. Re-Tangle consists of a random walking module and a transaction validation module, which transfer Tangle functions into ReRAM-based logic analog computation units. In the random walking module, Re-Tangle maintains an exponentiation translator to reduce its design complexity and improve its computation efficiency for exponentiation. In the transaction validation module, Re-Tangle further utilizes a highly parallel modular unit to accelerate the validation of different tags in a transaction. The experience results show that Re-Tangle distinguishes itself from other architectures, with significant performance improvement and energy saving. In [J3], we propose a new ReRAM-based processing-in-memory architecture called RPBFS, in which graph data can be persistently stored and processed in place. We study the problem of graph traversal, and design an efficient graph traversal algorithm in RPBFS. Benefiting from low data movement overhead and high bank-level parallel computation, RPBFS shows a significant performance improvement compared with both the CPU-based and the GPU-based BFS implementations.

15222315.value: For Objective 1, we have investigated heterogeneous-memory-workload-aware scheduling and management schemes in memory controller [C1, C2]. In [C1], to bridge the I/O performance gap for big data workloads, various mechanisms have been proposed. 15222315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222315.value: Big data applications require high I/O performance as huge amount of data needs to be transferred between memory and storage devices for processing. NVDIMM (Non-Volatile Dual In-line Memory Module) technologies provide a promising direction to alleviate the I/O latency issue. In this project, we have proposed several NVDIMM optimization techniques that have shown promising results. There are several directions for future work. First, how to exploit NVDIMM techniques in the software layer would be an interesting direction. Specifically, with its better read/write performance and non-volatility, NVDIMM techniques open doors for new software design and optimization from applications to operating systems. Second, new non-volatile memory such as ReRAM integrates computation into memory. It should be interesting to exploit this new characteristic in architectural integration and optimization. Third, it can be a new research direction to develop new NVDIMM techniques tailoring for killer applications such as big data analytics or smartphones.

15222815.label: Project Objectives
15222815.value: Development of Exploratory Domain Adaptation Learning Algorithms Our objective is to design a set of exploratory domain adaptation learning (ExpDAL) algorithms that can properly make use of some “hints” to identify a new domain so that data and knowledge from the existing domains can be leveraged to classify the hinted data in the new domain, possibly without any label information. We aim at addressing the challenges of how useful “hints” can be generated and how to carry out domain adaptation based on hinted data in the new domain. Development of a Data Enrichment Analytics Framework The main objective here is to develop an effective data enrichment analytics framework to work with the ExpDAL algorithms. The framework is expected to extend and elaborate the original data space so that a rich space for exploration is prepared. It addresses the challenge of how to generate different representations of the already available and abundant data from existing domains but yet can lead to a new domain that are potentially useful. Extension to Big Exploratory Data Analytics Our third objective is to extend the previous two objectives to a big data analytics context. We aim at bringing in the ExpDAL algorithms and the associated data enrichment analytics framework to a MapReduce-like paradigm that takes into account of the data parallelism in different domains.

15222815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222815.value: In the past several years, there have been strong interests in investigating new data mining or machine learning techniques that allow users to interactively explore their data for something they do not know. In particular, we lack the means to exploratively analyze databases of big scale. This echoes with exploratory data analysis to encourage statisticians to explore the data, and possibly formulate hypotheses that could lead to new data collection and experiments. On the other hand, rigorous research, particularly domain adaptation learning, has been carried out to study the ability of a system to recognize and apply knowledge and skills learned in previous tasks to novel tasks. We hypothesize that domain adaptation learning and exploratory analysis of large datasets have a mutual advantage in both conceptual development and applications. The immediate challenges are (i) how to introduce an exploratory element to the learning process of domain adaptation and (ii) how to develop and guide the exploratory data analysis process through domain adaptation learning so that one can get suggestions from scalable data in the existing domains. In view of the potential synergy of domain adaptation learning and exploratory data analysis, this project is proposed to investigate their integration, develop methods for ingenious domain adaptation learning, and exploit new approaches, frameworks and benefits for advanced analytics. We aim at addressing how to explore and adapt to a new, previously unexplored, and potentially useful domain and how to collect, elaborate and generate a rich space for exploratory domain adaptation learning so that useful suggestions could be obtained from already known domains. With respect to these aims, this project will develop a set of exploratory domain adaptation learning (ExpDAL) algorithms and a data enrichment analytics framework so that the ExpDAL algorithms can be effectively used as a service. We will further investigate how to extend the results to a big exploratory data analytics context so that applications with big data scale can take advantage of the new analytics paradigm. The results of the proposed research are expected to open up a new algorithmic development direction of domain adaptation learning and also initiate the study of innovative analytics. 在過去的幾年中學者們熱衷於研究新穎的數據挖掘或機器學習技術，這些方法旨在幫助用戶交互性地探索一些從未被發現的信息。目前具備大數據探尋性分析能力的手段和方法尤其缺乏，其倡導用戶挖掘數據、提出可能性的假設以便於進一步獲取新的數據和信息。另一方面，已有的研究，特別是領域自適應學習方法，已經達到了利用已有的知識和技能來指導新任務學習的效果。我們認為領域自適應和大數據探索性分析在理論和實踐中具有互補互惠性，但目前它們的融合面臨如下難題：1）如何引入探索性元素到領域自適應學習過程；2）如何在領域自適應學習過程中設計和引導探索性數據分析過程以達到在已有數據中挖掘新的有價值數據和知識發現。 從領域自適應學習和探索性數據分析所潛在的共性問題出發，本項目將主要致力於以下幾個目標，其包含了探究兩種模型的融合形式提出一種更高級且新穎的探索性領域自適應學習方法，進一步地基於所提出的探索性領域自適應學習方法得到具體地學習算法及學習框架，從而對數據做更為高級的分析。具體來說，我們首先要處理的問題是如何構建探索性領域自適應學習方法並使其能夠從一個全新的，未知的，且存在潛在利用價值的領域中獲取有價值的信息。同時，為了保證探索性領域自適應學習方法的性能，如何為該方法收集、提供及創造出豐富的數據儲備。為解決上述的兩大問題，我們發現大量的有價值的信息可從目前已知的領域中得到。至此，依據現有的領域自適應學習方法及所存在的從已知領域中獲取的大量信息，本項目將提出一系列具體的探索性領域適應學習(ExpDAL)算法，並基於所提算法及儲備的豐富數據構建一個具備高級數據分析能力的服務平台。此外，我們還將進一步提出具備大數據分析能力的探索性領域適應學習算法，並針對一些具體的大數據應用實例開發出相應的應用程序。最後，我們希望本項目所獲取的研究成果能夠為領域自適應學習方法開啟一個全新的研發方向，同時也可將其視為領域自適應學習方法在創新學習概念下的一個先驅工作。

15222815.label: Realisation of objectives
15222815.value: We have addressed three key issues of domain adaptation in this project. A major problem is how to get suggestions from existing domains. Based on a large-scale video recommendation application, novel recommendations could be generated by a proposed Bayesian Tensor-Based deep learning model. It takes hints from the already available abundant online multi-relational video information and can effectively exploit these sorts of data and suggest creatively interesting items. Given the dynamic nature of online media, recommendation in this setting is very challenging as it is difficult to capture the users’ dynamic topic distributions in sparse data settings as well as to identify unseen items as candidates of recommendation. Targeting at constructing a recommender system that can encourage more creativity, a deep Bayesian probabilistic tensor framework for tag and item recommendation has been proposed. By using a large-scale Tencent QQ Browser video dataset, the superiority of the proposed model in giving suggestions has been demonstrated, indicating that it can better capture the latent patterns of interactions and generates interesting recommendations based on creative tag combinations. This piece of research work demonstrated the realization of the three objectives by exploiting useful hints in recommendations, learning in rich online multi-relational setting, and addressing a large-scale analytics task. Another application domain we worked on is network learning, particularly, social network analysis, and quite a number of network embedding techniques have been proposed. We have exploited the use of fuzzy labels as hints in cross-network learning to address two problems in network learning, i.e., seed selection and graph sparsification in influence maximization. The proposed methods leverage the greedy seed selection knowledge pre-learned in a smaller source network, to heuristically select the nodes most likely to act as seed for the target networks. On the other hand, the models consider graph sparsification as a cross-network edge prediction problem, by adapting the influence propagation knowledge previously acquired in the source network to remove the edges least likely to contribute to influence propagation in the target networks. This work demonstrates the realization of the first objective particularly. With the advance of deep learning technology, we also continue to study deep network embedding techniques. Network embedding is an effective method to learn a low-dimensional feature vector representation for each node of a given network. We proposed a deep network embedding model with aggregated proximity preserving (DNE-APP). Firstly, an overall network proximity matrix is generated to capture both local and global network structural information, by aggregating different k-th order network proximities between different nodes. Then, a semi-supervised stacked auto-encoder is employed to learn the hidden representations which can best preserve the aggregated proximity in the original network, and also map the node pairs with higher proximity closer to each other in the embedding space. With the hidden representations learned by DNE-APP, we apply vector-based machine learning techniques to conduct node classification and link label prediction tasks on the real-world datasets. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of our proposed DNE-APP model over the state-of-the-art network embedding algorithms. This corresponds to the second objective of this project to extend and elaborate the original data space so that a rich space for exploration can be prepared. In the applications reported above, we have already worked on data with pretty big size, e.g. the QQ Browser dataset has 4071811 samples in total with 137465 unique users, and 9393 unique videos they clicked. As the problem has already made use of tensors to model the data in a data-parallel way, the computational requirement can be handled pretty well. Hence, we have not devised a MapReduce-like implementation for the model. In this regard, we have not fully achieved the third objective (indicated as 80%). If time and resource are available, we can find a big data processing developer to further develop a solution for really big data applications.

15222815.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222815.value: A deep Bayesian probabilistic tensor framework for novel tag and item recommendation has been proposed with encouraging performance in a large-scale video recommendation application. This work has been published in ACM Trans. on Information Systems (ToIS) as reported in Part C. It demonstrates the feasibility to generate new suggestions, particularly novel ones, based on a data rich, multi-relation environment. It contributes to an emerging area of novel recommendation in recommendation systems. Our work in the application area of cross-network learning appears in 2017 ACM SIGIR Conference, 2017 IEEE/ACM International Conference on Advances in Social Networks Analysis and Mining (ASONAM), and IEEE Trans. on Fuzzy Systems. We reported how to leverage cross-network abundant information for graph sparsification in influence maximization and proposed a cross-network graph sparsification model in SIGIR. In ASONAM, we reported a deep network embedding model called deep network embedding model with aggregated proximity preserving (DNE-APP) with the experimental results showing its superiority over several SOTA network embedding models. Based on these two pieces of work, the models have been extended to consider the use of fuzzy labels as hints in cross-network learning to address two problems in network learning, i.e., seed selection and graph sparsification in influence maximization. This latter work has been published in IEEE Trans. on Fuzzy Systems. In the DNE-APP model proposed in ASONAM, a semi-supervised stacked auto-encoder is employed to learn the hidden representations which can best preserve the aggregated proximity in the original network, and also map the node pairs with higher proximity closer to each other in the embedding space. Based on the stacked auto-encoder model, we further studied its use in domain adaptation in general and a deep learning method called Stacked Robust Adaptively Regularized Auto-regressions (SRARAs) is proposed to learn useful representations for domain adaptation problems which has been published in IEEE Trans. on Knowledge and Data Engineering.

15222815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222815.value: We have seen that creativity and novelty have been becoming a focus in different learning task. Our work on novel recommendation should be the first few attempts in recommendation systems and there will have other issues to study in the near future. We will further develop such techniques for possibly other learning tasks and applications.

15222915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222915.value: Laser absorption spectroscopy (LAS) is a powerful technique for trace gas detection. The employment of optical fibre-based technologies enables compact sensors as well as remote detection and sensor networking. However, the sensitivity of the state-of-the-art optical fibre LAS gas sensors is limited to 1-10 ppm (parts-per-million). Recently, we studied photothermal (PT) effect in gas-filled hollow-core photonic bandgap fibres (HC-PBFs) and found it can be used to develop highly sensitive optical fibre gas sensors with good selectivity. With a 10-metre-long HC-PBF as the sensing fibre and using interferometric phase detection, we successfully demonstrated an acetylene sensor with limit of detection down to ppb (parts-per-billion) level. However, the response time is limited by the time needed to fill gas into the hollow-core, and it is impractical to achieve ppb level detection with response time of less than 10 seconds using the long sensing HC-PBF. Here we propose to study cavity-enhanced optical fibre PT spectroscopic sensors and aim to achieve high sensitivity and fast response simultaneously. We plan to build high-finesse HC-PBF Fabry-Perot cavities and propagate a pump and a probe beam simultaneously through the same cavity. The pump and probe beams are tuned respectively to different cavity resonances so that the optical path-lengths of both beams are enhanced by a factor proportional to the cavity finesse. The pump is modulated in wavelength/intensity and is tuned to an absorption line of the target gas to generate phase modulation via PT effect while the probe is tuned to a region with minimal absorption for phase detection. Such an arrangement would enable simultaneous enhancement of PT phase modulation and interferometric phase detection, allowing highly sensitive gas detection with a much shorter length of HC-PBF. The shorter sensing HC-PBF will allow faster response as well as reduced volume of gas consumption. To our knowledge, such a double-cavity-enhanced PT sensor has not been reported previously. The realization of highly-sensitive fibre gas sensors with fast response would enable a range of important applications. One of them is breath analysis in medicine which requires ppb level ammonia detection with response time of less than 10 seconds. Another is condition monitoring of oil-filled electrical power transformers, which requires fast and highly sensitive (ppm level and below) acetylene detection with very small volume of fault gas generated from degraded insulation oil. 激光吸收光譜學在痕量氣體探測領域中是一項非常重要的技術。采用光纖傳感技術有利于傳感器趨向小型化，遠程探測幷且易于組建傳感網絡。然而，基于光纖氣體傳感技術的激光吸收光譜學的靈敏度一直受限在1-10 ppm。 最近，我們研究了注有氣體的空芯光子帶隙光纖中的光熱效應。該研究發現光熱效應有利于實現高靈敏度的光纖氣體傳感技術，幷且具有很好的氣體選擇性。使用10 m長的空芯光子帶隙光纖作爲傳感部件和干涉相位檢測技術，我們成功地實現了靈敏度達到ppb（十億分之一）水平的乙炔氣體傳感器。然而，該傳感器的響應時間受限于注入氣體到空芯光子帶隙光纖中所需要的時間。因此，在使用較長的空芯光子帶隙光纖中很難同時實現ppb水平的靈敏度和快速的響應。 因此，我們提出幷研究基于腔增强的光纖光熱光譜傳感器，該傳感器可以同時實現高靈敏度和快速響應。我們計劃製備出高精細度的空芯光子帶隙光纖法布裏-珀羅腔，幷且使泵浦光和探測光同時經過這個光纖腔。泵浦光和探測光分別調節到光纖腔的不同諧振峰波長處，使得兩束光所經過的光程都可以被正比于光纖腔精細度的因子所增强。我們使用波長/强度調製方式調製泵浦光，調節其波長對準目標探測氣體吸收綫的中心，幷且通過光熱效應産生相位調製，而探測光則被調節到一個沒有吸收的波長處，以此進行相位探測。這樣的方案可以同時實現光熱相位調製信號的增强和干涉相位的測量，幷且可以使用長度較短的空芯光子帶隙光纖來實現高靈敏度的氣體探測。長度較短的空芯光子帶隙光纖意味著更短的響應時間和更少的氣體消耗量。

15222915.label: Realisation of objectives
15222915.value: Objective 1 We designed and fabricated two types of hollow-core photonic bandgap fiber (HC-PBF) based Fabry-Perot gas cells. The first type is low finesse Fabry-Perot gas cells made by fusion splicing a 2 to 5-cm-long HC-PBF to standard single-mode fibers (SMFs) at both ends. The reflectivity at the splice joints is ~ 4%. Multiple micro-channels or side holes with ~1 cm separation between them were drilled from the side of the HC-PBF, with an 800 nm femtosecond laser micro-machining system. Experiments were conducted to test the response time of the gas cells and the time taken for gas to get into the hollow-core by diffusion is less than 10 s. The second type of gas cells is high finesse Fabry-Perot cavity gas cell made by sandwiching a piece of HC-PBF (5 to 10-cm-long) between two dielectric mirrors (>99.5%) made at the ends of two pigtail SMFs. This corresponds to a free spectral range of a few tens of picometers, slightly larger than the linewidth of a typical acetylene absorption line around 1530 nm. The HC-PBF and SMFs were mechanically spliced together. The cavity finesses of these gas cells range from 30 and 130. Side-holes with 1 to 2 cm between them were made along the HC-PBF, allowing diffusion-limited response time of ~10 seconds. For both types of gas cells, the HC-PBF was mounted (glued) onto a PZT stack for cavity tuning by applying an electric voltage. Experimental tests showed that by applying a voltage from 0 to 5 volts, one of the cavity resonant peaks of the Fabry-Perot gas cell can be tuned to the center of a gas absorption line (e.g., the P(13) line of acetylene). Objective 2 The cavity enhancement of phase detection was investigated theoretically and experimentally. The probe wavelength is set to be away from gas absorption lines but can be fine-tuned to different operation points near a cavity-resonance. Theoretical modelling and experiments were conducted to determine the detection sensitivity, i.e., the phase to intensity conversation coefficient, at different operation points. During experiments, a distributed feedback (DFB) laser is used as the pump source and its wavelength is slowly tuned across a cavity resonance (resonance A) which is aligned to the center of the P(13) absorption line of acetylene by tuning the voltage applied to the PZT stack. The pump wavelength is at the same time modulation sinusoidally at a higher frequency to produce the photothermal phase modulation in the Fabry-Perot cavity. The probe beam from an external cavity diode laser (ECDL) is tuned to around a different cavity resonance (resonance B) to detect the photothermal phase modulation. The probe wavelength was tuned to different operation points around resonance B to examine the magnitude of the second harmonic output signal, i.e., to evaluate the phase detection sensitivity. There exists an optimal operation point at which the second harmonic of the Fabry-Perot output is maximized. The probe laser wavelength can be maintained at this optimal point (i.e., the highest slope point) by monitoring the DC component of the transmitted Fabry-Perot output displayed in the oscilloscope and tuning the wavelength of the probe accordingly. By using a HC-PBF Fabry-Perot gas cell with finesse of ~40 and operating near the optimal operation point, the second harmonic signal can be enhanced by ∼20 times over the low-finesse (equivalent of a single-path system) system. Objective 3 Photothermal phase modulation in a high finesse Fabry-Perot was investigated theoretically and experimentally. Theoretical modelling shows that, for the same input pump power and the same gas concentration, the photothermal phase modulation would be enhanced by a factor proportional to the cavity finesse. However, for the high finesse Fabry-Perot cavity gas cells we have made, the losses at the mechanical splice joints are much larger than fusion spliced joints. This results in lower pump power coupled into the Fabry-Perot cavity and hence compromises the photothermal phase modulation. This results in an overall enhancement of photothermal phase modulation of only three to four times the single-path system. We further evaluated the overall systems performance of a 6-cm-long HC-PBF Fabry-Perot cavity with a finesse of ~40. By operating the probe at the optimal phase detection point and by tuning the pump wave across a cavity resonance that is aligned to the gas absorption line. we obtained signal-to-noise ratio of 795 for second harmonic detection for 100 ppm acetylene with a lock-in time constant of 1 second. This corresponding to a detection limit of 126 ppb for a signal-to-noise ratio of unity. In addition to the three objectives listed above, we have also studied the acoustic wave generation due to gas absorption of a pump laser beam. We developed a low-finesse fiber-optic Fabry-Perot cavity interferometric acoustic detector using a thin graphene diagram as one of the reflecting surfaces. With this acoustic detector and operating it at the resonant mode, we demonstrated detection of acetylene gas down to ~120 ppb.

The probe wavelength will be tuned to the highest slope point around a resonant peak of the Fabry-Perot cavity, and detection sensitivity in terms of minimum detectable phase modulation will be evaluated and compared with the single-path phase detection configuration,

To investigate theoretically and experimentally the cavity enhancement of PT phase modulation and to test the performance of the entire system for fast and sensitive gas detection. The pump will be tuned to a cavity resonance of the Fabry-Perot while the probe to the highest-slope point of a different cavity resonance. Enhancement of PT phase modulation over the single-path pumping configuration will be evaluated and the performance of the double-cavity-enhanced system for high sensitivity and fast response trace-gas detection examined.

15222915.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222915.value: We demonstrated a sensitive, compact, and low-cost trace gas sensor based on photothermal effect in a low-finesse HC-PBF cavity gas cell made by fusion splicing HC-PBF to SMF. Experiments with a 2-cm-long HC-PBF with femtosecond laser drilled side-holes demonstrated a response time of less than 19 s and noise equivalent concentration (NEC) of 440 ppb using a 1 s lock-in time constant (Opt. Lett. 41, 3025-3028, 2016). We showed that high finesse HC-PBF resonating Fabry-Perot gas cells can be made by mechanically splicing HC-PBF with SMFs with their ends coated with highly reflective dielectric mirrors. A HC-PBF cavity made with 6.75-cm-long HC-1550-06 fibre has achieved a cavity finesse of 128, corresponding to an effective optical path length of ∼5.5 m. This enables long interaction path (and hence high detection sensitivity based on either direct absorption or photothermal effect) and at the same time fast response because it is much easier to fill the hollw core of a shorter HC-PBF (J. Lightwave Technology, 35, 2887-2893, 2017; OFS-25, Jeju, April 2017) We demonstrated a double-cavity-enhanced photothermal gas sensor with a high finesse HC-PBF Fabry-Perot cavity as the absorption cell. Theoretically, the use of a high finesse cavity simultaneously enhances the intra-cavity build-up for the pump intensity inside the HC-PBF and improves the phase detection sensitivity for the probe beam by a factor proportional to the cavity finesse. The double-cavity-enhanced PT gas sensor allows the use of a shorter HC-PBF to develop highly sensitive and fast all-fibre gas sensors. Experiments with a 6.2-cm long HC-PBF absorption cell with a finesse of 45 for the pump and 41 for the probe demonstrated a detection limit of 126 ppb acetylene. Further improvement is possible (J. Lightwave Technology 37, 4222-4228, 2019). We demonstrated an all-optical fibre photoacoustic gas sensor with a graphene nano-mechanical resonator as the acoustic detector. By operating at one of the mechanical resonances of the diaphragm, the sensitivity for acoustic detection is enhanced and a noise equivalent minimum detectable pressure of 2.11 µPa/Hz1/2 at 10.1 kHz is demonstrated. Under the resonating condition, a lower detection limit for acetylene with the NEC of 119.8 ppb is achieved (IEEE J. of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics, Vol 23, No. 2, 2017).

15222915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222915.value: In the double-cavity-enhanced photothermal gas sensor with a high finesse HC-PBF Fabry-Perot cavity as the absorption cell, the intracavity build-up intensity will be enhanced by a factor of E = t(F/π)2, which is related to the transmission coefficient t of the mirror and the cavity finesse F. For the current HC-PBF resonating waveguide, the cavity enhancement factor E is 3∼8, which is believed due to the loss between the misalignment of mirrored and the HC-PBF. We will work to reduce the loss by using an optimal alignment technique or using concave mirrors to achieve a much higher enhancement factor and hence a much lower detection limit. To realize a stable system for real time application, we will develop a servo control to lock the pump wavelength to a cavity resonance, which is simultaneously locked to the center of a gas absorption line.

15222915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222915.value: Laser absorption spectroscopy is a powerful technique for trace gas detection. The employment of optical fibre-based technologies enables compact sensors. Recently, we studied photothermal (PT) effect in hollow-core photonic bandgap fibres (HC-PBFs) and demonstrated detection of acetylene gas down to ppb level. However, the response time is long due to time taken to fill the long sensing fiber. In this project, we demonstrated a double-cavity-enhanced PT gas sensor with a high finesse HC-PBF cavity as the absorption cell. We built such a cavity and propagated both the pump and the probe beams through the same cavity. The pump and probe wavelengths are tuned to different cavity resonances so that the effective optical paths of both beams are enhanced by a factor proportional to the cavity finesse. Such an arrangement enables simultaneous enhancement of PT phase modulation and detection, which allows highly sensitive gas detection with a much shorter length of HC-PBF and hence faster response. The realization of highly sensitive fibre gas sensors with fast response would enable a range of important applications in environmental monitoring, medicine, as well as petrochemical industry.

15223015.label: Project Objectives
15223015.value: Propose a new method for characterizing temporal dependence at the sub-pixel level The temporal dependence aims to describe the relation between images in TSIs and exploit as many links between images as possible. As widely acknowledged, temporal correlation exists between the TSIs covering the same scene. It is, therefore, favorable to account for temporal correlation. However, SPM further involves scale transformation. To incorporate temporal information into SPM, it is essential to develop a method to characterize temporal dependence at the sub-pixel level. Incorporate fine spatial resolution information in the given period into SPM of TSIs The SPM problem is always ill-posed with multiple plausible solutions. One potential solution is to incorporate further information from auxiliary data and to decrease the uncertainty in SPM. The fine spatial resolution map (FSRM, which can be obtained by, for example, classification of the fine spatial resolution image) is generally convenient to acquire during the period of the TSIs. It is proposed that the FSRM be used to enhance SPM of TSIs in this study. Propose a new method for characterizing spatio-temporal dependence at the sub-pixel level Effective ways to characterize spatial dependence will be identified from existing spatial dependence-based SPM. The spatial and temporal dependences will be combined to further characterize the spatio-temporal dependence. The optimal weights controlling the two dependences will be estimated using a fitting procedure. The process will be fully automatic. Develop optimization algorithms to solve the spatio-temporal SPM problem SPM of coarse TSIs will be formulated as a constrained optimization problem. The objective of SPM is to maximize the spatio-temporal dependence in the TSIs, under the coherence constraint imposed by the coarse LCLU proportions in each image. Effective optimization algorithms will be developed to solve the optimization problem. Conduct case studies The case studies will be conducted to demonstrate the potential of the proposed methods in applications. Two application areas (i.e., an urban redevelopment area and a tropical forest area) will be chosen and a demonstrator will be built for the applications.

15223015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223015.value: Monitoring the spatial distribution of land-cover/ land-use (LCLU) continuously is very important for many studies, including urbanization and global change based on accumulated spatial Big Data of multi-temporal satellite sensor images. The Landsat and MODIS sensors are common sources of imagery used for continuous LCLU monitoring due to their free availability and regular revisit capabilities. However, they provide coarse spatial resolutions relative to the requirements of many applications. Satellites such as IKONOS and WorldView are able to capture ﬁne spatial resolution images with a relatively short revisit time, but the high cost and narrow swath hamper their application for timely monitoring, particularly for large areas. There is, therefore, a great need for technologies that can produce continuous, fine spatial resolution maps from coarse time-series images (TSIs). This project aims to develop a new theoretical framework for sub-pixel mapping (SPM) from TSIs based on spatio-temporal dependence. It has the following objectives: (1) to propose a new method for charactering temporal dependence at the sub-pixel level; (2) to incorporate fine spatial resolution information in the given period into SPM of TSIs to decrease the inherent uncertainty; (3) to propose a new method for characterizing spatio-temporal dependence at the sub-pixel level; (4) to develop optimization algorithms to solve the spatio-temporal SPM problem; (5) to implement the proposed spatio-temporal SPM method and demonstrate its potential in applications using TSIs of selected areas in Hong Kong and Brazil. The research outcomes of this project will be: (1) A new theoretical framework for SPM from TSIs; (2) A technological report of the case studies, from which conclusions can be drawn on the applicability of the newly proposed technology from this project. These findings will be utilized by remote sensing practitioners and policy-makers related to many areas, including urban planning and land utilization. The project will generate several publications in top-rated remote sensing journals, centered upon the newly proposed framework of spatio-temporal SPM and its potential in applications. The new approach will extend conventional spatial dependence-based SPM to spatio-temporal SPM for continuous LCLU mapping. The proposed spatio-temporal SPM approach will offer an excellent opportunity for LCLU dynamic monitoring and change detection at a finer spatial resolution than the available coarse TSIs. This approach has great potential in applications with socio-economic significance, such as monitoring the urbanization process in Hong Kong and deforestation processes in the Amazon rainforest in this project. 15223015.label: Realisation of objectives
15223015.value: (1) Propose a new method for characterizing temporal dependence at the sub-pixel level It is well known that temporal dependence exists between TSIs. However, how best to describe mathematically the temporal dependence at sub-pixel resolution is a key problem. Temporal dependence has been used widely in pixel-level LCLU mapping. These methods, however, involve training information or computationally costly processes. As a simpler alternative and building on the concept of spatial dependence used commonly in SPM, the temporal dependence at sub-pixel resolution is proposed to be characterized by the similarity in LCLU (in terms of class labels) between temporally close images. Based on temporal dependence, the LCLU maps of the TSIs are considered to resemble each other when they are temporally proximate. By maximizing the temporal dependence, the differences in LCLU between the TSIs can be minimized. (2) Incorporate fine spatial resolution information in the given period into SPM of TSIs We assumed access to at least one fine spatial resolution map (FSRM, which can be obtained by, for example, classification of the fine spatial resolution image temporally close to the studied TSIs). The thematic LCLU information from the FSRMs is used in the temporal dependence characterization. The starting image and the manner for propagation of the temporal information are investigated. As for the starting image, an intuitive option is the image at the earliest time. In this way, the starting point is a SPM solution of the earliest image and involves the inevitable uncertainty of the scale transformation (i.e., downscaling). By utilizing the temporal information, the uncertainty in the SPM of the starting image may be propagated to the SPM process of later images. To avoid such uncertainty, we select the FSRM as the starting point. As for Propagation of temporal information, two main approaches have been suggested for propagation of temporal information in multi-temporal image classification (but at pixel-level), that is, the cascade and mutual approaches. The main difference between the two approaches is choice of temporally neighboring images. In contrast to the mutual approach, the cascade approach is a single-pass scheme and, thus, non-iterative. We use the non-iterative cascade approach for propagation of temporal information as it allows a significant simplification of the proposed spatio-temporal SPM for TSIs. (3) Propose a new method for characterizing spatio-temporal dependence at the sub-pixel level In the proposed spatio-temporal dependence-based SPM, the sub-pixel class depends not only on the spatial information in the studied image for SPM, but also the thematic information in the temporally neighboring images of the TSIs. The goal is to maximize the spatial autocorrelation in the image for SPM and at the same time the similarity in LCLU between TSIs, under the coherence constraint imposed by the coarse proportions. That is, the spatial and temporal dependences need to be maximized simultaneously to achieve SPM. It is essential to choose a suitable fusion approach to combine these two types of dependence. Several existing approaches have been summarized for multisource data fusion, including an approach subdividing the data into subsets of sources and then analyzing each subset, an ambiguity reduction approach, a supervised relaxation labeling approach and a stacked-vector approach. They have significant limitations as general approaches for multisource data fusion. We select the consensus fusion approach to fuse spatial and temporal dependences. An appealing advantage of this fusion approach is that flexible weights can be assigned to different types of dependence and, thus, the contributions of different sources of dependence can be controlled according to speciﬁc requirements. As one of the most commonly used consensus rules, the linear opinion pool is employed. Following this rule, the spatial and temporal dependence is combined linearly to characterize the spatio-temporal dependence. (4) Develop optimization algorithms to solve the spatio-temporal SPM problem The proposed SPM method for coarse spatial resolution TSIs is implemented by maximizing the overall spatio-temporal dependence. The coherence constraint is imposed in the SPM of all TSIs. Ideally, the most suitable distribution of all sub-pixel classes within each coarse pixel can be obtained by evaluating all possible conﬁgurations and selecting the one that maximizes the spatio-temporal dependence. This assumption works mainly for cases involving small-size images and a small zoom factor. For a large zoom factor, the number of combinations of possible sub-pixel spatial distributions increases dramatically and the computational load may become unrealistic. This necessitates the application of an effective optimization algorithm to solve the optimization problem. The simulated annealing algorithm is employed in this project. The input is a set of proportion images for all TSIs, and the whole solving process contains two stages: initialization and update. The whole process is performed for each coarse image in turn. (5) Conduct case studies The case studies have been conducted using three application areas: an urban area in Shenzhen, China, an urban area in Georgia, US, and a tropical forest area in Brazil. The main findings are summarized as follows. First, the proposed spatio-temporal SPM approach can provide more accurate TSIs at sub-pixel resolution than conventional spatial-only SPM methods. Second, the FSRM imparts greater benefits for SPM of images temporally close to it. The closer to the FSRM, the greater the SPM accuracy achieved. Third, the reliability of the FSRM is crucial in the proposed approach, and when the error in it was increased to a very large value (above 80%), the proposed method could not increase the SPM accuracy compared to conventional spatial-only methods. Fourth, for remarkably large error values (up to 80%), however, the proposed approach was able to impart benefits compared to conventional spatial-only methods.

15223015.label: Major findings and research outcome
15223015.value: With the high development of the society, the land-cover/ land-use (LCLU) changes faster and it is becoming increasingly important to conduct fine spatio-temporal resolution monitoring. The Landsat and MODIS sensors are common sources of images used for continuous LCLU monitoring at global scale. The main challenge is that they provide coarse spatial resolutions relative to the requirements of many applications. In this project, we develop new approaches to produce continuous, fine spatial resolution maps from multi-resolution time-series images (TSIs). The major findings and outcomes are summarized as follows: 1) Developing new sub-pixel mapping (SPM) methods for fine spatiao-temporal resolution monitoring. The proposed approach considers simultaneously spatial and temporal dependences and provides an excellent opportunity for LCLU dynamic monitoring at a finer spatial resolution. 2) Developing new geostatistical solution, area-to-point regression kriging (ATPRK), to downscaling. ATPRK increases the spatial resolution of images to go to or beyond that of any bands. It has the characteristic of perfect coherence with the original coarse data. 3) ATPRK is extended with a local approach, called adaptive ATPRK (AATPRK). AATPRK can enhance ATPRK in cases where the spatial character varies locally. 4) ATPRK is extended for fast hyperspectral image (HSI) sharpening with an approximate version. The approximate version greatly expedites ATPRK, but also maintains a very similar performance in sharpening. 5) Application of ATPRK for fusion of the data provided by the recently launched Sentinel-2 satellite. We downscaled the six 20 m Sentinel-2 bands to 10 m using the four directly observed 10 m bands, and produce10 Sentinel-2 bands with 10 m spatial resolution. 6) Developing a new method to reduce the point spread function (PSF) effect in SPM. In existing SPM methods, the PSF effect has seldom been considered. A generic SPM method is developed to consider the PSF effect to increase SPM accuracy. 7) Developing a new method to reduce the PSF effect in spectral unmixing. Until now, almost all spectral unmixing methods have ignored the PSF effect. A new method is proposed to account for the PSF effect within spectral unmixing to produce more accurate predictions of land cover proportions. 8) Developing a new image fusion method, called information loss-guided image fusion (ILGIF). Information loss (IL) inevitably exists in all spatial downscaling techniques. The fine spatial resolution images in other wavelengths are used to predict the IL in downscaling and an IL-guided image fusion (ILGIF) approach is proposed.

15223015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15223015.value: Estimation of the point-spread function The point spread function (PSF) effect exists ubiquitously in real remotely sensed data and it can greatly impact the performance of sub-pixel mapping, spectral unmixing, image fusion and downscaling. Although several solutions have been developed to reduce the PSF effect, but the PSF estimation remains an open problem. It is of great significance to seek solutions to PSF estimation for more reliable downscaling. Use of auxiliary data in spatio-temporal sub-pixel mapping Sub-pixel mapping is an ill-posed inverse problem and uncertainty in predicting sub-pixel maps cannot be eliminated. Although various auxiliary data have been investigated for reducing the uncertainty, the challenge is that such data are always not easy to acquire. For the task of sub-pixel mapping of time-series images, there always exist temporally sparse, but spatially fine land cover maps. The value of such fine maps, however, has not been fully explored. In future research, it is important to develop solutions to make fuller use of such fine maps to enhance sub-pixel mapping.

15223015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15223015.value: The research project has developed a number of downscaling methods. These methods can help us to see the remote sensing images more clearly and help to make more reliable decisions based on the products. The outcomes of the projects have great potential in monitoring the land use in urban and rural areas. For example, they can help the planning department to monitor urbanization processes and illegal occupation of public land (e.g., privately expanding ponds).

15223315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223315.value: 普通地圖詳細地描述地面上各種地物，但對許多應用來說，其信息量太多而不好用，特別是在小屏幕顯示的時候。這要求我們對地物內容作出適當的取捨，並對圖形進行簡化，一提高可讀性和可用性。倫敦地鐵圖被認為是簡化地圖的一個絕佳例子，吸引著各領域的專家投入研究，如地圖學、複雜網絡分析、計算幾何、交通、心理學、大規模集成電路、地理信息等。 倫敦地鐵圖是一種拓撲示意圖，它的成功是幾代人的智慧結晶。這種地圖已被廣泛接受而存在巨大的需求。對這樣的需求，而在互聯網時代，大家的共識是要達到“有求即應”。即一有請求，馬上能自動生成。可惜，到目前為止，自動方法生成的結果還未能達到要求。所以，本課題旨在研發一種新的自動生成方法；它不但能保持網絡的主要結構，而且能生成多尺度的地圖。 這一成果將在位置服務、交通、旅遊、導航、大規模集成電路、製圖等領域得到應用。

15223315.label: Realisation of objectives
15223315.value: The objective of this project is to develop techniques for automated generation of display-adaptive multi-scale schematic representations of line networks with proper preservation of line and network structures. With the GRF project, a full-time PhD student has been funded, two MSc students are also partially supported, and one research associate was supported for 6 months. The PhD student, Mr. LAN Tian, is to submit his thesis by end of the August 2020. The title of the thesis is “Automated Generation of Labelled Schematic Network Maps” and an abstract of the thesis (draft) is attached. The first issue tackled in this project is the display-adaptive multi-scale representations. By multi-scale, it means “enlargement/reduction of cartographic ratio”, “coarser/finer resolution”, “variable cartographic ratio” and/or “variable resolution”. Some variable scale representation techniques have been explored to make maps adaptive to small format display. After applying a variable scale transformation to maps (i.e. enlarging interesting areas on maps to larger scales and shrinking other areas), area and direction distortions are created. With such distortions, the clarity of representation for the interesting areas is improved, but effectiveness of map recognition may be reduced. Thus, an optimization method has been developed to correct orientation distortions for variable-scale maps, while preserving the map clarity as much as possible. A paper has been published in the ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing (117: 237–242), which has the highest impact factor (IF=6.38) in the category of remote sensing. The second issue tackled is how to evaluate the quality (or effectiveness) of automatically generated schematic maps. That is, (1) if two different designs of schematic maps are produced, one could be more effective than the other; (2) the schematic maps may be more effective than the original map. The objective evaluation becomes critical issue. In this project, eye-tracking technique has been employed to track the three travel decision-making tasks. Total travel time is used as criterion for effectiveness; completion time and mental work cost are used for efficiency evaluation; subjective scores from questions are used for satisfaction evaluation. A paper has been presented at the 2016 ISPRS Congress held in Prague and the paper is published in International Archives of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing & Spatial Information Sciences, which is now cited by the SCI/SSCI system. The third issue tackled is how to maintain the main structure of the line network so as to produce most promising results. In this project, the four general principles (i.e. preservation of main structure and the topological relations, as well as maintenance of relativity in length and position) proposed by the PI have been used as the constraints for optimization. These general principles are first modelled as constraints and then integrated into mixed-integer programming (MIP) framework for acquiring the optimal solutions of network layouts. Experimental evaluation has been conducted with two sets of real-world transit networks in terms of shape complexity, usability, and computational performance. The network layouts generated by the existing MIP-based method are used as the benchmarks. Experimental results indicate that the proposed automated method can generate network layouts with improved quality. A paper entitled “Integrate general principles into mixed-integer programming to optimize schematic network maps” has been published in International Journal of Geographical Information Science (IJGIS), which is the most prestigious journal in the area of Geographical information Science (see attached). Another paper entitled "Effect of preserving relative position and length on the cognition of schematic network maps" has also been submitted to IJGIS and we have just received editorial request for a revision. (see attached) Most of the schematic maps produced by automated algorithms are without automated labelling. However, labelling is essential for effective and efficiency of recognition. To automatically generate name labels of schematic maps, a two-step strategy is proposed. The rules of labels (i.e. the potential positions and the preferences of these positions) are first acquired by statistics from some existing representative schematic maps. Then, the acquired rules are integrated into a local optimization algorithm. The experimental evaluation is carried out with two real-world metro networks by a 5-grade-marking-system-based questionnaire in terms of “the ease level of finding the corresponding name labels”, “the congestion level” and “the satisfaction level”. The labels on the official schematic maps are employed as the benchmarks. Experimental results indicate that the proposed automated labelling method can generate effective name labels. A paper entitled “Automated Labelling of Schematic Maps by Optimization with Knowledge Acquired from Existing Maps” has just been accepted for publication by Transactions in GIS. As the main objective of this project is to produce schematic maps with proper preservation of line and network structure, we explored the feasibility of using structural fractality of road network as a metric for network structure. The Hong Kong network is used as an example and the relationships between this metric and other socio-economic parameters are also studied. A paper entitled “Urban Allometric Scaling Beneath Structural Fractality of Road Networks” has been published in the AAAG (Annals of the American Association of Geographers).

15223315.label: Major findings and research outcome
15223315.value: It has been found that structural fractality is a good measure to characterize the structural property of a road network and it has high correlation with some geographical parameters. The result has been published in Annals of the American Association of Geographers. Three algorithms have been developed, i.e., to balance area and direction distortions, to produce optimized schematic maps with main structure of a network preserved, and to optimize the lablelling of names (stations/stops). Two algorithms have been published in ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote sensing and International Journal of Geographical Information Science, respectively, and the third resubmitted to Transaction in GIS after a revision. With these algorithms, the resultant schematic maps appear to be more pleasing and easier in interpretation. It has been found that relativity in line length and relation point positions does have effects on the map recognition. A paper based on this result is submitted to and International Journal of Geographical Information Science. A PhD student is to graduate in the coming August!

15223315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15223315.value: For many applications, the usability of maps instead of accuracy is critical. To achieve high usability, simplification must be made to conventional maps. The London Tube map, called a schematic map, has been cited as an excellent example of such possible simplification. It has been a consensus that automation of such a process is a must in order to meet increasing online demands and interactive exploration. However, maps drawn by graphic designers appear still somewhat more pleasing and elegant than the best automatically generated maps. Although continued efforts have been spent on the improvement of such map, yet a lot is still left to be desired. To solve this problem, we have adopted two strategies. The first is to properly preserve the main structure and maintain the relative length of lines and relative position of points. The second is to balance the orientation and shape distortions. Experimental evaluations have been carried out and the results show that, with our algorithms, the elegance and pleasure of schematic maps have been much improved. Such maps will have wide applications such as online and mobile-based navigation, social and Internet complex networks, location-based services, tourism, public transport mapping.

15224015.label: Project Objectives
15224015.value: Video saliency measure for discovering objects-of-interest -- As psychological experiments suggested, human is able to discover and track the objects-of-interest having salient appearance and/or motion in the context of global scene. Driven by this fact, we will propose a video saliency measure with a 3D spatio-temporal representation, which incorporates the complementary color, structure, and motion salience cues. In literature, the research of visual saliency mainly focuses on image-based models, and few of them are associated to visual tracking. The video saliency measure enables us to selectively detect and localize noticeable targets in the scene, and provides evidence (or likelihood) during the online tracking process. Spatio-temporal context online learning -- The existing trackers often ignore the contextual interactions between the targets and the background, mainly because the object models tend to be online maintained while the context model learning demands high computational cost. We will address this issue by proposing a fast learning algorithm, where the spatio-temporal context and video saliency are collaboratively integrated within a short sequence of video frames. Moreover, the framework will be extended to multi-channel and kernelized 3D correlation filter learning, where saliency and image descriptors can be easily integrated for improving tracking performance. A dataset for visual tracking in the wild -- Numerous factors will affect the performance of a tracking algorithm in the unconstrained environments, such as illumination variation, occlusion, camera motion, changing appearance, as well as background clutter. Therefore, it is crucial to evaluate state-of-the-art trackers with different settings to demonstrate their strength and weakness, as well as identify new research directions accordingly. We will collect or capture a number of videos that could explicitly address different real tracking applications. In addition, some new challenges will be included in our dataset, such as automatically localizing objects to be tracked, handling the object-to-object and object-to-scene interactions, and recovering object trajectories under long term occlusion.

15224015.label: Realisation of objectives
15224015.value: 1. Correlation filters for real-time online tracking In this project, much efforts have been made to develop the advanced correlation filter for efficient and accurate online tracking. Robust visual tracking is a challenging problem due to various object appearance changes. Discriminative appearance models have been extensively studied and have achieved promising results. One representative discriminative appearance model is based on the support vector machines (SVMs) to detect objects in visual tracking. SVM-based approaches generally include a sampler for training samples generation and a learner to update the classifier. To reduce the computational load, sampling is required to maintain a small set of samples and budgeting is introduced for online learning of SVM. However, sampling and budgeting improve tracking efficiency with the sacrifice of accuracy. On the contrary, the correlation filter (CF) based methods adopt ridge regression or kernel ridge regression model, which provide limited discriminative ability for accurate target localization despite the high tracking efficiency. Therefore, for efficient and accurate tracking, we propose a novel SVM-based algorithm via support correlation filters. By exploiting the circulant property of the data matrix formed by dense sampling, we formulate a learning problem for support correlation filters and propose an efficient solving algorithm. In an alternative optimization process, the SVM classifier can be efficiently updated by iterative learning of correlation filters with discrete Fourier transform. Furthermore, the proposed algorithm is extended to multi-channel, kernelized and scale-adaptive versions to improve the tracking performance. Substantial experimental results on public tracking benchmark show that he proposed tracker performs favorably against the state-of-the-arts in terms of both accuracy and tracking speed. This work was published in T-PAMI 2019 [J1]. 2. Spatial-temporal regularization in correlation filter for boundary effect We have further investigated the CF and proposed to learn support correlation filters (SCF) in [J1]. The cyclic shifts of the base image for training samples generation makes that the SCF can be efficiently learned via fast Fourier transform (FFT). However, such kind of sampling strategy makes the discriminative correlation filters (DCF) suffer from boundary effects. Specifically, the shifted negative samples will suffer from the boundary discontinuity. Except for the base image, all shifted samples based on the circulant property are not truly negative patches in real images. To resolve the issue of boundary effects, we provide a thorough evaluation on cosine window in [J2]. Despite that boundary discontinuity has been suppressed largely, the shifted images near boundary are still plagued. On the other hand, the cosine window applied on the base image is prone to contaminating negative training samples into unreal image patches. It's worth noting that those spatial regularized approaches still employ cosine window. The contamination of negative samples remains inevitable. It motivates us to consider an interesting problem: when can we remove cosine window from CFs? Through comprehensive comparison, we found that it is possible to remove cosine window from CF trackers when spatial regularization is deployed. Consequently, how to remove cosine window from CF trackers with spatial regularization is concerned. To address this issue, we introduce a binary mask function and a Gaussian shaped mask function to eliminate the effect of boundary discontinuous sample. Experiments are conducted on public tracking benchmarks, and the results indicate that our method can eliminate boundary discontinuity while avoiding sample contamination, and performs favorably against the state-of-the-art trackers. This work was under minor revision in TIP 2019 [J2]. DCF trackers with spatial regularization alleviate the boundary effects and improves the tracking performance but at the expense of increasing complexity. For online updating, recent works formulate models on multiple training images, inevitably introducing large computational cost. In [C3], we introduced the temporal regularization to spatially regularized DCFs based on single sample, and propose the spatial-temporal regularized correlation filters (STRCF) motivated by online passive-aggressive (PA) algorithm. By constraining the adjacent two correlation filters, STRCF provides a more robust appearance model in the case of large appearance variations and can be efficiently solved via the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Our method not only outperforms previous spatially regularized DCFs in target localization accuracy but also satisfy the real-time requirement of online tracking. This work was published in CVPR 2018 [C3]. 3. End-to-end learning for CNN with correlation filter Traditional CNN trackers treat object detection in each frame as a binary classification problem. Positive data sampling usually is performed around the position in previous frame, which is likely to be over-fitting to backgrounds. On the other hand, searching candidates around the location in previous frame for target prediction in the current frame may lead to drifting. In [C4], we propose a simple, flexible yet effective method by decomposing the single tracking task into localization and classification, i.e., Deep Location-Specific Tracking (DLST). A small network is first adopted to provide a specific location of the target coarsely in the current frame, which is then used for candidates sampling. The candidates combined with those sampled from previous frames are feed into the classification network for achieving the final target location. Details can be found in [C4]. In [C1], we explore the integration of temporal information in deep trackers and propose a real-time generic tracker using convolutional neural networks (CNN). Instead of the Siamese-net framework with two branches for template and search area separately, we build a single-stream CNN using frame-pair for training. Specifically, the frame pairs are stacked as the input to learn generic motion patterns of objects with much less annotated videos. To address the prediction tends to the centers of searching windows, we construct pairs by sampling two frames with a random offset, which controls the moving smoothness of objects. Experiments on the VOT challenging datasets show that the proposed tracker performs on par with relevant generic trackers, but runs much faster than most CNN trackers. More recently, the end-to-end learning frameworks combining DCF and CNN further facilitate the performance improvement of visual object tracking. However, all these methods are trained in a supervised fashion, which depends on a large amount of annotated videos. It inspires us to investigate whether we can train a good visual tracking network without using human annotations. In [C2], we propose a novel unsupervised learning pipeline based on the discriminative correlation filter network. Specifically, we utilize an easily obtained single movie to learn the network by iteratively updates the tracker through alternating between target localization and network optimization. Experimental results show that the performance of our unsupervised framework is comparable with those trackers learned with full supervision from large scale databases. This work was published in AAAI 2019 [C2].

15224015.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224015.value: 1. We present a novel SVM-based tracking algorithm in cooperation with the correlation filter for fast and accurate online object tracking. Using the circulant property of training data formed by dense sampling, the SVM classifier can be updated efficiently by learning the correlation filters with discrete Fourier transform. Moreover, the proposed method is extended to the multi-channel and kernelized variants for full use of the multi-channel features and the kernel trick of SVM. [J1] 2. We investigate the correlation filters in depth, especially the boundary effect caused by dense sampling. Through comprehensive analysis, we reveal the relationship between the cosine window and spatial regularization and draw the conclusion that it is possible to remove cosine window from CF trackers when spatial regularization is deployed. Consequently, we further introduce a binary mask function and a Gaussian shaped mask function to eliminate the boundary effect when removing the cosine window. [J2] 3. Based on the spatial regularization, we consider the temporal constraint and present the spatial-temporal regularized correlation filters (STRCF) with an efficient solving algorithm. It not only performs favorably against the state-of-the-arts in target localization accuracy but also satisfy the real-time requirement for online tracking. [C3] 4. We train an individual CNN tracker for both localization and classification, i.e., Deep Location-Specific Tracking (DLST). In particular, we adopt a small network to provide a specific location of the target coarsely in the current frame for candidates sampling. Then these candidates combined with those from previous frames are handled by the classification network for final prediction. [C4] 5. We build a single-stream CNN tracker using frame-pair for training. Frame pairs are stacked as the input to learn generic motion patterns of objects. [C1] 6. We propose an unsupervised learning framework based on the discriminative correlation filter framework. The model is trained using only a single movie and by iteratively alternating between tracking and updating processes. The proposed method achieves comparable performance with those trackers learned with full supervision from very large scale databases. [C2]

15224015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224015.value: There are two potential improvements of the proposed methods in this project. 1. End-to-end correlation filter learning based on CNN The proposed method in [J1][J2][C3][C2] are based on the correlation filters. Despite combining the DCF and CNN to form an end-to-end training framework, integrating the constrained CF into CNN is still a problem and should be improved. In [C2], the unconstrained CF can be easily approximated by a correlation operation, however, the simple CF model inevitably degrades the tracking performance. It is more valuable to integrate the advanced CF with constraint conditions, such as the spatial-temporal regularized CF into the CNN for joint learning. In the future, we will study how to combine the advanced CF with CNN for end-to-end learning. 2. Robust unsupervised learning methods Most existing CNN trackers takes the supervised training scheme which depends on plenty of annotated videos. In [C2], we explore the unsupervised framework by using a single movie video for training and demonstrate its feasibility, but the iterative training process takes too much time, and it cannot be easily scaled to many videos. In the future, we will explore more robust and flexible unsupervised framework and training scheme.

15224015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224015.value: In this project, we investigated the problem of visual object tracking, and developed a series of methods for efficient and accurate online tracking. First, support correlation filters (SCF) were developed to improve the discriminative appearance model with fast solving algorithm for robust tracking. Second, cosine window in CFs was investigated in depth and the results provide more insights on when and how to remove cosine window for further performance improvement. We also explored the spatial-temporal constraint for CF trackers. STRCF introduces temporal regularization to spatially regularized DCF with single sample, which provides a more robust appearance model in the case of large appearance variations and can be efficiently solved by the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Third, we investigated the model learning of CNN trackers. Decomposing tracking process to two stages, i.e., localization and classification, we proposed a Deep Location-Specific Tracking (DLST) model by learning an individual network. Considering the temporal information, we proposed a novel frame-pair based method by using a single stream CNN, which takes the stacked frame pairs as input, to learn generic motion patterns of objects. Finally, we explored the unsupervised tracking framework and demonstrate its feasibility through comparison experiments with those supervised methods.
