15224115.label: Realisation of objectives
15224115.value: Objective 1: To develop a procedure for optimal selection of multivariate mixture models for Bayesian updating of the strain/stress responses with SHM data In-service bridges are normally subjected to multiple loads such as highway traffic, railway traffic, wind and thermal effect, resulting in heterogeneous and multimodal data structure of strain/stress responses. The conventional unimodal distribution models are often inadequate to characterize the multimodal structural responses in that they tend to yield biased model estimation. In this study, a Bayesian mixture modelling approach was developed for characterizing the heterogeneous and multimodal SHM data. The unknown parameters in the Bayesian mixture model are treated as random variables rather than fixed quantities in the conventional probabilistic models, making the model uncertainty be explicitly interpreted. Both aleatory and epistemic uncertainties are thus accounted for. To facilitate the subsequent derivation of an analytical expression of the conditional reliability index, the Gaussian distribution is adopted as component density. The optimal selection of the Bayesian mixture models was pursued by treating it as a model selection problem, which can be addressed by means of Bayes factor in the Bayesian paradigm. Suppose two competing models M(1) and M(2) are concerned, If the observations Y are more likely to come from model M(i), then the associated marginal likelihood p(Y|M(i)) will be larger, and vice versa. Thus, a Bayes factor BF(M(1);M(2))>1 implies that model M(1) is in favor of being more plausible than M(2) in featuring the observation data. In the case of multiple candidate models, e.g., the selection of optimal component number in a mixture model, it is conducted to compare the logarithm of the marginal likelihood lnp(Y|M(i)) (LML) of each model, then optimal model is the one with maximum LML value. The calculation of the marginal likelihood p(Y|M(i)) which involves integration over high dimensional parameter space is analytically untraceable for complex models. In this study, the marginal likelihood was estimated using the Chib’s method which is based on the Gibbs outputs and Monte Carlo estimate. The proposed procedure for optimal selection of the Bayesian mixture models has been applied to real-world SHM data collected from the suspension Tsing Ma Bridge in Hong Kong. The optimal Bayesian mixture models for the top chord, diagonal strut and bottom chord of an instrumented bridge deck cross-section were formulated by the proposed procedure. The optimal mixture model orders for the top chord, diagonal strut and bottom chord are obtained as 4, 3 and 4, respectively, which are highly consistent. Moreover, the reconstructed multimodal probability density functions (PDFs) of the stress responses by the optimal Bayesian mixture models agree well with the stress histograms obtained from the SHM data. Objective 2: To develop a procedure for evaluating the annual predictive distribution of load effects and the time-variant safety index in terms of finite mixture models First, a method for the identification of uncertain parameters in the parametric Bayesian mixture models was formulated. A general mixture distribution model has a parametric probability density function (PDF) which is the form of weighted sum of multiple component densities. The difficulty in estimating the mixture model is the uncertainty of allocating observations to a component. It is therefore necessary to introduce an uncertain component indicator for each observation. In this study, the uncertain component indicator is formulated to conform to a multinomial distribution. By defining conjugate priors for the mixture parameters that are viewed as random variables to interpret the model uncertainty, an analytical form of the full conditional posteriors is derived. Because the direct inference of the joint posterior distribution is computationally intractable, Gibbs sampler is explored to estimate the posterior distributions of the mixture parameters, while quantitative criteria are introduced to diagnose convergence of the Gibbs sampler iteration. Then, a nonparametric Bayesian mixture modelling method was developed in terms of the Dirichlet process prior with the merit of releasing the model order (number of components) assumption. Unlike putting conventional prior distributions on individual parameters in a parametric model, infinite dimensional parameters in a nonparametric Bayesian mixture model usually constitute functions or measures, thus requiring workable prior distributions to be functions or measures rather than random variables. In view of this, the Dirichlet process mixture (DPM) model is adopted to allow that the model complexity automatically adapts to the SHM data with the capability to jointly consider the parametric and model order uncertainties. To avoid low efficiency of direct sampling from the conditional posteriors, the collapsed Gibbs sampler is devised to pursue the posterior mixture density samples. An extended version of the quantitative convergence diagnosis strategy is proposed to assess the convergence of simulations. Given the posterior mixture density samples, quantification of both parametric and model order uncertainties can be achieved through the nonparametric approach. Both parametric and nonparametric Bayesian mixture models have been incorporated into reliability theory to formulate a conditional reliability index for SHM-based bridge condition assessment. The derived conditional reliability index is a function of the uncertain model parameters; thus the estimate of the conditional reliability index reflects both the aleatory uncertainty and epistemic uncertainty depicted in the mixture model. The estimated value of the conditional reliability index, which serves as a quantitative measure of health condition for in-service bridges, can be successively updated with the accumulation of SHM data. The application to the suspension Tsing Ma Bridge in terms of the conditional reliability index concludes that the diagonal strut is in excellent condition with no need of inspection; the top chord is in good condition just needing preventive inspection; and the bottom chord is in satisfactory condition but needs regular inspection. Objective 3: To develop a procedure for formulating adaptive discriminant models for the prognosis of predictive distribution In addition to the conditional reliability index that can be updated with cumulated SHM data to indicate structural health condition, a Bayesian prediction approach incorporating Gaussian processes (GPs) was developed for probabilistic forecasts of structural stress responses. To relieve the computational burden involved in GP-based modelling, a moving window strategy was proposed to elicit a reduced-order GP-based approach for stress response forecasting in the context of Bayesian inference. The predictive (forecasting) stress probability density function (PDF) is then utilized for real-time damage/condition detection in the following way: (i) the predictive PDF model and its alternative model (formulated by shifting the mean value by a prescribed offset) are statistically compared to determine which better fits the actual next observation; (ii) if the comparison results are in favor of the alternative model, it is claimed that a potential change has occurred; (iii) then Bayes factor and cumulative Bayes factor in line with Bayesian hypothesis testing are calculated to accomplish anomaly and damage detection. A structural condition classification approach was further proposed within the time series modelling context. It adopts a computationally efficient binary segmentation approach for change-point detection in order to classify and assess structural health condition. The proposed method was verified using real-world monitoring data acquired from a cable-stayed bridge which experienced structural damage. In addition, a Bayesian optimization method in combination of Gaussian processes (GPs) was developed for evaluating the dynamic response bounds of railway bridges with uncertain-but-bounded parameters; it was verified in regard to a real-world bridge.

15224115.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224115.value: 1. A parametric Bayesian mixture model was developed to accommodate the multimodal structural responses with consideration of parametric uncertainty. An MCMC-based Gibbs sampler was devised to pursue the joint posterior of the mixture parameters. A Bayes factor based method was developed to find the optimal model order of the mixture model. 2. A nonparametric Bayesian mixture model was developed to allow that the model complexity automatically adapts to the monitoring data with joint consideration of the parametric and model order uncertainties. A collapsed Gibbs sampler was devised to pursue the nonparametric estimation of the mixture density samples. Convergence diagnosis of the MCMC simulation was formulated based on a quantitative procedure. 3. In compliance with the developed parametric and nonparametric Bayesian mixture models, an SHM-based bridge reliability assessment procedure was developed. The estimated conditional reliability index allows accounting for both aleatory and epistemic uncertainties arising from resistance and load effect characterization and can be successively updated with the accumulation of monitoring data. The proposed method was applied to the suspension Tsing Ma Bridge in Hong Kong for SHM-based reliability assessment. 4. A Gaussian processes (GPs)-cast Bayesian modelling approach that allows for probabilistic forecasts of structural stress was developed. A moving window strategy was proposed to substantially shrink the size of training data, thus leading to a reduced-order GP model and effectively alleviating the high computational cost. We demonstrate that with the increasing number of the forecasting executions, the time consumption of the full GP-based approach exponentially rises, whereas that of the reduced-order GP-based method is small and quite stable. 5. A structural condition classification approach was proposed within the time series modelling context. It adopts a computationally efficient binary segmentation approach for change-point detection in order to classify and assess structural health condition. The proposed approach does not require knowledge about the structure and is appealing for attaining an automated structural health monitoring (SHM) system. 6. A Bayesian optimization method was developed for evaluating the dynamic response bounds of railway bridges with uncertain-but-bounded parameters. A Bayesian modelling approach adopting Gaussian process prior was proposed to replace the current expensive-to-run original model solver, along with an acquisition function that trades off exploration and exploitation of the search space. By doing so, the optimization of a complex, intractable black-box function is converted to the maximization of a computationally efficiently acquisition function that has a closed-form expression and is differentiable.

15224115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224115.value: 1. In this project, Gaussian component/kernel density was employed in the Bayesian mixture models to realize analytical forms of full conditional posteriors for efficient MCMC execution using Gibbs/collapsed Gibbs samplers. In the future study, the proposed method can be extended to develop other workable kernels such as lognormal, Weibull, Gumbel for mixture models in order to achieve more genetic settings. 2. Deterioration models of structural resistance and the associated uncertainties have not been fully considered in the present monitoring-based reliability assessment scheme. In the future study, in-situ tests or experiments on actual material deterioration behavior of steel or concrete members in the bridge can be conducted to obtain more authentic structural resistance deterioration models.

15224115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224115.value: Monitoring-based reliability assessment of in-service bridges has recently gained massive attention because the integration of reliability principles with site-specific structural and loading information offer a rational way to consider the intrinsic randomness associated with capacity and demand of a structure during the service life. However, the formulation of probability distribution models by making use of structural health monitoring (SHM) data becomes a challenging task when there are multiple loads of highway traffic, railway traffic, and wind acting on the bridge. In such cases, standard distribution models are of inadequacy to characterize the heterogenous monitoring data due to the restrictive assumptions in used, causing high bias in reliability assessment. In this project, a Bayesian framework for multimodal probabilistic modelling and SHM-based reliability assessment is developed. The formulated Bayesian mixture models are then used in conjunction with reliability method to derive the conditional reliability index that is updatable when monitoring data are cumulatively available. The proposed framework is exemplified to reliability evaluation of an instrumented suspension bridge in Hong Kong. In contrast with the conventional frequentist approach, the Bayesian treatment enriches the mixture model by providing not only most plausible parameter estimates but also the associated uncertainty levels.

15224215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224215.value: 最優停時問題在很多領域有許多重要應用, 如科學、工程、經濟、管理、特別是在財務投資。在該領域的傳統研究中, 隨機動態系統由初始狀態隨時間發展。但是, 在研究金融衍生工具如美式回望期權時, 研究人員面臨著隨機系統由終端狀態倒向依賴路徑發展。這就要求研究依賴路徑的正倒向隨機系統以及在評估和優化這類系統的性能。在這一研究項目, 我們計劃檢查依賴路徑的正倒向隨機系統最優停時問題, 以及相應數學工具泛函型伊藤積分。該項目旨在發展新的方法, 其在很大程度上不同於現有文獻中的傳統最優停時問題, 並克服由依賴路徑所引起的困難。此外, 我們亦會將所得理論結果應用到兩個富有挑戰性, 但相對實際和重要的財務投資決策問題。首先我們研究最優銷售問題, 投資者試圖選擇恰當的時間出售其資產, 在有限的時間內實現最大的投資回報。由此所得之結果也將更進一步應用到另一涉及基金經理和客戶的財富管理問題。

15224215.label: Realisation of objectives
15224215.value: In this project, our study adds to the understanding of risk-taking behaviors and investment decision mechanisms of investors in at least three aspects below. First, findings of this project provide important and timely implication practitioners and policy makers by helping them understand their risk-taking behaviors when they encounter consumption cost and non-smooth utility over their investment time horizon. Second, it contributes to the mathematical finance/financial engineering literature by stopping investment at the right time in order to achieve the maximum wealth (path dependency) over a finite time horizon. Third, it is one of the studies addressing investors' decision-making process theoretically according to their historical consumption maximum (path dependency). This running maximum term in the utility function differs significantly from the habit formation preference in the existing literature. The duality approach with the auxiliary dual process is unfortunately not applicable in our setting. This motivates us to seek for other distinctive methods to solve our non-standard control problem with consumption peak and nonnegativity constraint. Therefore, this model sheds light on the cutting-edge development of the financial industry and its corresponding literature. We mainly investigated a variety of dynamic optimization problems featuring both stochastic control and optimal stopping over a finite/infinite time horizon. According to the original proposal, we developed a new methodology by dual transformation, which is significantly different from those of stopping problems mixed with optimal control in the existing literature, to tackle some challenging, yet practically relevant and important, risk-sensitive problems in wealth management to obtain the properties of the optimal strategies and analyse “optimal consumption with reference to past spending maximum (path-dependency)” and “non-smooth and non-concave utility” to achieve a certain level over an infinite time investment horizon (papers 1 and 7 in Part C). In particular, by employing the dual transform of value functions, we obtained the explicit classical solutions of the dual PDE using endogenous boundary conditions and smooth-fit principle. Over a finite time horizon, we considered the stopping investment problem where investors attempt to choose the right time to stop investment in order to achieve the maximum wealth (involved in path-dependency) , further developed the theory and presented the numerical examples (papers 11 in Part C). In paper 12 in Part C, since the original problem can be reformulated into a free boundary problem with a fully nonlinear operator, we further converted it into a new free boundary problem with a linear operator, by means of a dual transformation, which can be tackled by the classical method. Then, using the inverse transformation, we obtained the properties of the optimal trading strategy and the optimal stopping time for the original problem. Besides the above works, we studied the solvability of anticipated backward stochastic differential equations (ABSDEs, for short) with quadratic growth over a finite time horizon (paper 2 in Part C). In fact, ABSDEs are a class of path-dependent stochastic differential equations and an important analysis tool when one deals with delayed stochastic control problems with random coefficients. We will further develop this theoretical result to tackle some stochastic control problems with random coefficients in another research project. During this project period, we also developed weak closed-loop solvability of stochastic linear quadratic optimal control problems of Markovian regime switching system (paper 3 in Part C). The results derived from our work are expected to help readers to have a clear picture on stochastic linear quadratic control based on the modes of Markov chain. In paper 6 in Part C, we analyzed the optimality system using a variational method, which is a linear mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equation with constraint. We derived a complete and explicit representation of the optimal control. In papers 4 and 9 in Part C, we further developed the idea to study a class of mean-field games with control constraints. We represented the decentralized strategies and consistency condition by a class of mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equation with projection operators. Besides these, we also introduced the above methods to study mean-variance portfolio selection in financial investment, which is an important tool and a core concern of rational economic agents (papers 5, 8 and 10 in Part C). In addition to contributing to the academic literature, our study has important yet practical relevance. With the alarm bells the on-going financial crisis rings, risk hedging has drawn much more attention than ever. Among various approaches of hedging and managing risk, consumption cost, non-smooth utility and mean-variance portfolio selections under stochastic system are preferable by institutional investors. Further developing the methods presented by prior research, our approach determines the region in which managers should exit their investee companies based on dynamic stochastic models in financial investment. Moreover, our approach is easily implementable with a standard numerical technique, and therefore it provides managers with a usable way to make decisions.

15224215.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224215.value: The current works of this project deal with a variety of important applications in many fields such as science, engineering, economics, management, and particularly in financial investment. In particular, we mainly revisited some challenging, yet practically important, consumption budget and wealth management models over a finite/infinite time investment horizon, reformulated them as optimal stopping problems and derived their optimal strategies with analytical solution qualities. Also, we studied a class of anticipated backward stochastic differential equations (ABSDEs, for short) with quadratic growth, which is actually a fundamental tool to solve delayed stochastic control problems with random coefficients. Besides these, we further derived the equilibrium strategy and equilibrium value function in a closed-form using backward induction approach within a game theoretic framework during this project period. We published some papers and complete some working papers. 15224215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224215.value: Although the research in this direction has been well developed for path-dependent stochastic control problems, it lacks progress in both theoretical investigation and applications for standard and non-standard time-inconsistent problems within the more general stochastic system framework. We will further study these potential research works in the future. [1] Optimal control techniques proposed in this project can be further employed to study more general portfolio selection models, while one encounters investment problem with reference to the historical consumption maximum over his/her investment time horizon. [2] Our methodologies and techniques on portfolio selection can be adopted to analyze time-inconsistent models within the random exit investment horizon. [3] Our methods developed in this project can be applied to manager's compensation with underlying assets involved in stochastic volatility and interest rates within the random exit investment framework.

15224215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224215.value: As for the theoretical contributions, this study will contribute to the literature on various topics such as optimal policy and consumption cost in portfolio selection (paper 1 in Part C), fund management, incentive compensation and agency theory (papers 7, 11 and 12 in Part C) within the optimal stopping framework. Specific to the literature on portfolio theory and investment, we expect the results to help shed light on the investment strategies on the basis of financial underlying assets over the investment time horizon (papers 1, 7, 8, 11 and 12 in Part C). In addition, the methods adopted in the current research program will also improve the optimal control studied and the implementations developed in the field of stochastic control constraints (papers 4, 5, 6, 9 and 10 in Part C). In particular, one of our findings provides a fundamental tool to further study a class of delayed stochastic control problems with random coefficients in the future. Therefore, this project is believed to be of value and of practical importance with long-term significance.

15224415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224415.value: Mobile Cloud Computing (MCC) offers great opportunities for mobile service industry, allowing mobile devices to utilize the elastic resources offered by the cloud. By using MCC technologies, developers can create advanced applications on mobile devices, such as multimedia applications, and augmented reality, which far more exceed the capability of the devices. In this project, we study computation partitioning, which is to decide whether each part of the application should be offloaded to the cloud or not. There exists new challenges in mobile-cloud computation partitioning. From the mobile side, the partitioning of applications should dynamically change with the user’s mobile environments which may vary due to the user’s mobility. From the cloud side, computation partitioning should support multi-user applications to gain profit through realizing the economic of scale. We aim to provide a systematic approach to support dynamic computation partitioning for multi-user mobile cloud applications. Although a lot of works have been done on computation partitioning, they face two main limitations. First, most works consider static computation partitioning, which assume that the offloading cost does not change during the run time of application. They perform one time static partitioning when the application is initiated, which usually leads to significant application performance degradation. Second, existing works focus on computation partitioning for single user applications. They try to solve the problem from the standpoint of end user, while ignoring the challenges in design of new partitioning methods from the standpoint of cloud providers for multiple users. In this project, we propose to carry out a systematical investigation on the new requirements, and address the issues in dynamic computation partitioning for multi-user mobile cloud applications. In particular, we will develop efficient algorithms to estimate and predict relevant parameters of the dynamic mobile cloud environments, such as the status of network connection and workloads of system, which could affect the partitioning of the application. With the estimated/predicted parameters, we will develop a framework and algorithms to solve the issues in computation partitioning such as environment dynamicity, user scalability and data privacy. This project will make significant contribution towards achieving good performance in next generation multi-user mobile cloud applications. Both application developers and end users will benefit from our research outcome. The project also has high impact on the real operation of industry and society. The contribution of this project is highly relevant and has special significance to Hong Kong scientific and industrial community and society. 移動云計算允許移動設備彈性地利用云上豐富的計算資源，為移動服務的開發和迅速發展提供了機會。由於移動云計算技術，開發者們能在當前移動設備上開發許多對計算資源有著高要求的新興應用程式，例如多媒體應用，移動增強現實等等。 本項目擬研究移動云計算切分問題，即對給定應用程式的計算哪些分配在雲上，以及哪些分配在移動設備上做最優決策。移動云計算切分存在一些新的技術挑戰。首先，從移動端來看，對應用程式計算的切分必須動態隨著用戶環境的變化而變化。其次，從雲端來看，移動云計算切分要求能支持多用戶應用，從而充分利用云資源的規模效益。本項目擬提出一個系統的解決方案以支持多用戶移動云應用的動態切分。 關於計算切分目前已經存在一些已有的研究，但是這些研究工作主要存在兩個不足。其一，大部分工作考慮靜態計算切分，即假設計算遷移的成本在應用執行的過程中保持不變。在應用程序啟動之初，根據當時的環境參數，確定一個計算切分方案。應用程式一直保持該切分方案運行直到結束。這導致應用程式性能在變幻環境下性能較差。其二，已用工作主要考慮單用戶計算切分。它們試圖從用戶端的角度來解決計算切分問題，忽略如何作為云服務商為大量用戶提供計算切分服務所帶來的問題。 本項目將系統系統地研究多用戶移動云應用動態計算切分所面臨的新的要求和一些列研究難點。具體而言，我們首先開發有效的方法來估計或者測量動態移動云環境中，能影響計算切分方案的相關參數，例如網絡帶寬，移動設備和云上負載情況等等。在這些參數估計的基礎上，我們進一步解決計算切分中諸如環境動態性，用戶可擴展性以及數據隱私等一些列研究問題。 該項目將對下一代多用戶移動云計算的性能提升有著重要的幫助。應用開發者以及終端用戶都能從本項目的研究成果中收益。鑒於此，該項目將在工業界以及社會中產生重大影響。該項目的主要貢獻對香港科技領域以及工業的發展帶來很大促進作用。

15224415.label: Realisation of objectives
15224415.value: We have finished the main objectives listed in the proposal. For the 1st objective, i.e., “to investigate and study the new requirements of dynamic computation partitioning for multiple user mobile cloud applications; To design the system models and identify the research issues”, we have proposed an edge mesh system model and focus on the dynamic computation partitioning between the end device and edge clouds. Edge mesh is a system abstraction for us to study the issue for future mobile cloud computation partitioning, where the clouds are distributed across various areas as lightweight micro-clouds. Our resource results for this objective are published in [J2017a]. We have designed the architecture model and functional components, and identify the research issues including resource management and monitoring, computation partitioning, performance optimization and measurement. The 2nd and 3rd objectives are to design algorithms and mechanisms for each specific issues and evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithms and mechanisms through theoretical analysis and simulations. We have studied four specific research problems. The first problem is to multi-user computation partitioning under constraints of multiple types of resources, i.e., the access network bandwidth and the computation resources of the edge cloud [J2018b][J2018c][C2017c] [C2017d]. The second problem is to partition and schedule computation on top of multiple collaborative computing resources [J2019a][J2019b][J2018d]. The third problem is to provide a customized and accurate privacy settings for the cloud augmented mobile applications [J2018a]. The fourth problem is to leverage the SDN technique to reduce the communication latency among the computations in the cloud [J2017b] [C2017a] [C2017b]. The details of the results on these problems are as follows. First, in terms of multi-user multi-types of resources computation partitioning, we have studied network aware mobile edge computation partitioning in multi-user environments, i.e., to decide for each user which parts of the application should be offloaded onto the edge cloud, and which others should be executed locally, and meanwhile to allocate the access bandwidth among the users, such that the average application performance of the users is maximized. This problem is new in that we consider the competition among users for the network bandwidth as well as the computation resources in a multi-user environment. We have transformed the problem into the classic Multi-class Multi-dimensional Knapsack Problem, and develop an effective algorithm, namely Performance Function Matrix based Heuristic (PFM-H), to solve it. We further considered the user mobility and designed effective online algorithms that could be easily deployed in practical systems. Comprehensive trace driven simulations showed that our proposed algorithm outperforms the benchmark algorithms significantly in the average application performance. We have studied joint computation partitioning and resource allocation problem for latency sensitive applications in mobile edge clouds. The problem is novel in that we combine the computation partitioning and the two-dimensional resource allocations in both the computation resources and the network bandwidth. We have developed a new and efficient method, namely Multi-Dimensional Search and Adjust (MDSA), which is an offline algorithm, to solve the problem. We compared MDSA with the classic list scheduling method and the SearchAdjust algorithm via simulations. The results showed that MDSA outperformed the benchmark algorithms in terms of the overall application latency. Moreover, we also design an online method, named by Cooperative Online Scheduling (COS), which can be easily deployed in practical systems. By extensive evaluations, we showed that COS outperforms the benchmark methods by 25% on average. Second, in terms of computation partitioning and scheduling based on multiple collaborative edge/resource nodes, we focus on two typical task models, i.e., independent tasks and dependent tasks. Dependent tasks refers to the application-level tasks which have data dependence among each other. For independent task model, we studied the problem of computation partitioning in future 5G-based edge computing environments. Specially we proposed a new partitioning model, which parallelizes the computations and fully utilizes the computational resources on the edge and end devices. We developed an off-line solution for partitioning and scheduling the computation to the resources. We proved in theory that our off-line solution achieves the optimal performance. Based on the off-line solution, we further developed a set of online algorithms, and conducted extensive simulations to show that our proposed online algorithms significantly outperform the benchmark algorithms. For the dependent task model, we studied the data-aware task allocation problem to jointly schedule task and network flows in collaborative edge computing. We considered the transfer of input data required by different tasks as the data is generated by sensing devices which are located at different geographical places. Besides, existing works solved the problem of task scheduling without considering network flow scheduling which can lead to network congestion and long completion times. We mathematically modeled the joint problem to minimize the overall completion time of the application. We have proposed a multistage greedy adjustment (MSGA) algorithm where the task scheduling is done by considering both placement of tasks and adjustment of network flows. Performance comparison done using simulation showed that MSGA leads to up to 27% improvement in completion time as compared to benchmark solutions. Third, in term of the privacy aware mobile cloud computing, we have studied the privacy issue in the multi-user mobile cloud application. We have addressed the privacy issue by providing proper recommendations about the settings so that the users can preserve their sensitive information and maintain the usability of apps. We proposed an unobtrusive recommendation system, which can crowdsource users’ privacy permission settings and generate the recommendations for them accordingly. Besides, our system allowed users to provide feedback to revise the recommendations for getting better performance and adapting different scenarios. For the evaluation, we collected users’ preferences from 382 participants on Amazon Technical Turks and released our system to users in the real world for 10 days. According to the study, our system can make appropriate recommendations which can meet participants’ privacy expectation apps’ usability. Fourth, in terms of the SDN based mobile-cloud technique, we have studied the SDN based protocols to guarantee the communication latency in the cloud for the multi-user computation partitioning. In specific, we enabled SDN with QoS guaranteed abilities, which could provide end-to-end QoS routing for each cloud service. We implemented an application identiﬁcation technique on SDN controller to determine required QoS levels for each application type. Then, we implemented a queue scheduling technique on SDN switch. It queued the application ﬂows into different queues and schedules the ﬂows out of the queues with different priorities. We evaluated the effectiveness of the proposed SDN-based QoS technique through an experimental analysis. Results showed that when the output interface has sufﬁciently available bandwidth, the delay can be reduced by 28% on average. In addition, for the application ﬂow with the highest priority, our methods can reduce 99.99% delay and increase 90.17% throughput on average when the output interface utilization approaches to the maximum bandwidth limitation. For the 4th objective, i.e., to validate the system with proposed approaches by proto-type implementation and applications demonstrations, we have developed a prototype for dynamic mobile cloud partitioning. We demonstrated the technology using augmented reality application in our campus environment, where the users leverage the mobile phones to recognize the campus building in real time. The demonstration results showed that our proposed technology can speed up the image recognition about 3 times over the application running locally on the mobile device.

15224415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15224415.value: Our major finding includes four aspects. First, we have develop a set of novel algorithms for multi-user multi-types of resources computation partitioning [J2018b][J2018c][C2017c][C2017d]. The research is novel in that we combine the computation partitioning and the two-dimensional resource allocations in both the computation resources and the network bandwidth. Previous works considers multi-user computation partitioning under a single type of resource constraint, either the computation resource constraint on edge cloud or the communication resource constraint. Our problem was more challenging and leveraged a collaborative scheduling method over two types of resources. We designed the collaboration mechanisms between the schedulers aiming to achieving the balanced utilization of the resources. The results showed that the proposed algorithms outperformed the benchmark algorithms in terms of the overall application latency. Moreover, we also design an online method, named by Cooperative Online Scheduling (COS), which can be easily deployed in practical systems. Second, we have developed solutions for partitioning and scheduling computation on top of multiple collaborative computing resources [J2019a] [J2019b][J2018d]. We have designed a new partitioning model, which parallelizes the computations and fully utilizes the computational resources on the edge and end devices in 5G based edge computing[J2019b]. We proved in theory that our off-line solution achieves the optimal performance. Based on the off-line solution, we further developed a set of online algorithms. Moreover, we proposed a data-aware task allocation method in collaborative edge computing. The method can jointly schedule task and network flows to minimize the overall completion time of the application. Existing works solved the problem of task scheduling without considering network flow scheduling which can lead to network congestion and long completion times. Performance results showed that data aware task allocation solution leads to up to 27% improvement in completion time as compared to benchmark solutions. Third, we have developed a customized and accurate privacy settings for the cloud augmented mobile applications [J2018a]. Specially we proposed an unobtrusive recommendation system, which can crowdsource users’ privacy permission settings and generate the recommendations for them accordingly. The experimental study shows that our system can make appropriate recommendations which can meet participants’ privacy expectation apps’ usability. Fourth, we have developed SDN based technique to guarantee the communication latency in the cloud for the multi-user computation partitioning [J2017b] [C2017a] [C2017b]. Our methods can reduce 99.99% delay and increase 90.17% throughput on average when the output interface utilization approaches to the maximum bandwidth limitation.

15224415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15224415.value: On computation partitioning, we will study how to partition a stateful data stream application in a dynamic environment where the network bandwidth from the end device to edge clouds varies frequently with time. Stateful application is an important task. It means the operation/computation on an input data will leave some state which is required by the processing of the next data framework. The partitioning of this type of application has not been studied before, and it is very challenging because the frequent adaption of the partitioning under a varying environment would lead to high state migration cost. The study of this topic would enrich the scheduling theory especially for stateful task. Additionally, in future, we will investigate AI model training as an application domain of the dynamic computation partitioning. We will study how to partition and schedule the model training and aggregation onto the edge devices, aiming to achieve high model accuracy and convergence speed. Moreover, we will study the underlying computing framework to support a portioned execution over the edge devices. Existing container computing is popular due to the features like cross-platform and easy-programming. However, the software framework is still resource-consuming for some edge devices with limited capability.

15224415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15224415.value: The research makes significant contribution towards achieving good performance in next generation multi-user mobile cloud applications. Both application developers and end users obtain benefits from our research outcome. The proposed research saves energy consumption and shorten the latency for the applications running on mobile devices, from the end user standpoint, and as well to achieve operational efficiency and reliability from the system operator standpoint. By incorporating the edge infrastructures in the mobile cloud computing model, our research advanced the technologies for future smart IoT applications that requires real time and low latency data communication, processing and analytics. The efforts to improve the quality of services and IT operational efficiency are the key forces to drive the growth of mobile cloud markets. The project also has high impact on the real operation of industry and society.

15224815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15224815.value: In this project, techniques for realising high capacity short reach optical communication systems will be investigated. According to a recent study by Cisco, global internet traffic has increased by fourfold in the past five years with a compound annual growth rate of 23%. It has been predicated that the trend will be maintained and the global IP traffic will pass the Zettabyte(10 to the power of 21 byte) threshold by the end of 2017. Study has shown that due to the proliferation of cloud computing and multimedia mobile services, more than 70% of the data traffic are within data centres. This requires communication systems that can carry data at very high speed over a short distance of not more than 2km. Such systems should be simple, with small form factor and low power. Although a significant amount of effort has been made in the research of long haul high capacity optical communication systems, the focus have been on increasing overall system capacity and transmission distance. To achieve this, coherent detection technique has been used in most of the recent studies and an extra local oscillator(LO) laser is needed for signal detection. In addition, narrow linewidth transmitter laser is necessary for realizing polarization multiplexed high order modulation scheme with high spectral efficiency. In short reach optical communication systems, to reduce system cost and achieve small form factor, a LO laser has to be avoided. At the same time, low cost transmitter laser with relative wide spectral linewidth has to be employed. Yet it should offer very high data capacity. Techniques developed for long haul optical transmission systems are often not suitable. In the proposed research, a number of possible solutions to address the problems above are proposed and will be investigated. In particular, investigation will be carried out to study the performance of two novel schemes for increasing system capacity through polarisation multiplexing. Detection and equalisation schemes for the proposed schemes will be studied and overall system performance will be verified through simulation and experiments. To further increase system capacity, multiplexing in spatial domain will be explored. Tradeoff between optical fibre design and DSP complexity will be evaluated for multicore fibre based system. The proposed schemes will be compared with performance optimised PAM, CAP and DMT systems in order to design optimum transmission and signal detection schemes for future short reach optical communication systems. 此项目将研究用于实现高容量短距离光通信系统的技术。根据思科系统的研究，全球互联网的流量在过去五年中增加了四倍。在未来的几年中这种趋势将得到保持，全球的互联网流量将在2017年底超过Zettabyte。研究同时显示由于云计算及移动多媒体的快速发展，超过70%的数据流量是在数据中心内。这就需要传输距离在2公里内的简单，小体积，低功耗的高速光通信系统。过去几年科研人员在长距大容量光通信系统上进行了大量的研究。研究重点主要在提高系统容量和传输距离。为达到这个目的必须利用相干检测技术。这需要本振（LO）及窄线宽激光器。在短距传输系统中，基于价格及尺寸的考虑，应尽量避免本振（LO）及窄线宽激光器的使用。为实现高传输速率，我们在此项目中提出一系列解决办法并将进行相关研究。我们将研究直接检测偏振复用技术及相关的解调算法。同时将和其它直检高阶调制技术进行比较结合，以期实现最佳短距传输系统设计。

15224815.label: Realisation of objectives
15224815.value: All the objectives of research project has been achieved successful. With the increase of internet capacity, the demand for higher transmission speed of communication link has also increased significantly. In long haul optical communication systems, this is mainly achieved through the use of coherent detection which allow all the signal dimensions including polarization, phase and amplitude be used. In short reach optical communication especially those used in data centers, the cost concern means direct detected system is a preferred option. A number of approaches can be taken to increase the capacity of a direct modulated and direct detected optical communication system. These include using advanced modulation schemes such as pulse amplitude modulation(PAM), carrierless amplitude and phase modulation(CAP) and discrete multitone modulation(DMT) with the use of various equalization schemes for system performance optimization. At the same time, direct detected polarization multiplexed transmission can also be used to increase system capacity. In this project, a number of innovative schemes in both system hardware configuration and detection algorithm have been explored and very good system performance have been demonstrated through both simulation and experimental verification. The results have been presented in leading conferences including optical fiber communication conference(OFC), the flagship conference in the research area and published in leading journals in the areas. A book chapter has also been published.

15300015.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15300015.value: 求解非凸非光滑約束最小化問題的罰函數法

15300015.label: Project Objectives
15300015.value: We will derive new necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of exact penalty parameters regarding stationary points, local minimizers and global minimizers. We will show how the existence of exact penalty parameters depends on the choice of penalty functions. We will provide necessary and sufficient optimalty conditions for nonconvex, non-Lipschitz constrained minimization problems by using the subdifferential, horizon subdifferential, subspace techniques and smoothing approximations. We will provide a systematic mechanism for selecting the penalty parameters with various penalty functions. We will develop efficient iteratively reweighted convex minimization algorithms for nonconvex nonsmooth constrained minimization problems with intelligent schemes to update the iterative weights and penalty parameters. We will develop efficient proximal quadratic regularization methods for finding sparse solutions of nonconvex non-Lipschitz constrained minimization problems. We will use the gradient sampling techniques or smoothing approximations to build quadratic approximations of the penalty functions. We will extensively test the proposed algorithms and compare them with existing ones on large scale problems in terms of speed, accuracy and robustness. Real data sets will be used to test the efficiency of the new theory and algorithms. We will apply the new theory and algorithms to image restoration, signal reconstruction and variable selection with practical applications in data analytics for intelligent transportation systems.

15300015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300015.value: The penalty methods are standard methods for constrained minimization which represent the constraints as penalty terms added to the objective function and solve a series of unconstrained optimization problems. The penalty term consists of a penalty parameter multiplied by a nonnegative penalty function whose value is positive only when the constraints are violated. How to find the best penalty parameters and penalty functions is an active research area. When the constrained minimization problem is convex and smooth, theory and algorithms for penalty methods are well developed. However, when the objective function is not convex, not differentiable and perhaps not even locally Lipschitz, there is little theory and algorithms for penalty methods. It is well known that nonconvex nonsmooth constrained minimization model can give sparse representation which has important applications in image restoration, signal reconstruction, and variable selection. The aim of this project is to develop effective and innovative penalty methods for nonconvex nonsmooth constrained minimization. In this project, we will derive new necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of penalty parameters with various penalty functions such that any stationary points, and local and global minimizers of the original constrained optimization are stationary points, local and global minimizers of the corresponding unconstrained problems. We will use these conditions to estimate penalty parameters in the algorithms and investigate the sparsity of stationary points, and local and global minimizers. Moreover, we will develop efficient penalty algorithms for solving the unconstrained optimization problems and update the penalty parameters in an intelligent way so that we can find generalized KKT points, and local and global minimizers of the original constrained minimization. Moreover, we will establish new convergence and complexity theorems and compare the new penalty methods with existing methods for solving important problems in image science, signal reconstruction and variable selection. The outcomes of this project will have long-term, high impact, because nonconvex nonsmooth constrained optimization problems arise naturally in numerous important applications in various fields and our penalty methods will provide urgently needed efficient algorithms for solving them. 罰函數法是求解約束最小化問題的一種經典方法。其主要思想是根據約束的特點，構造懲罰項并加到目標函數中去，由此將原約束問題轉化為一系列無約束問題來求解。懲罰項由罰函數乘以一個非負的罰函數組成，若相應的約束條件不滿足，則罰函數的值為正。如何找到最優的罰參數以及罰函數是現今研究中的一大熱點問題。對於凸且光滑的約束最小化問題，其罰函數法理論和算法的發展已經相當成熟。然而，目前對於目標函數非凸且非光滑甚至可能非局部利普希茨連續約束問題的罰函數法理論和算法其發展仍然非常有限。眾所周知，非凸非光滑的約束最小化模型可以用來描述許多實際問題的稀疏表示形式，例如圖像恢復、信號處理以及變量選取等。本項研究的主要目的是，針對非凸非光滑的約束最小化問題，建立高效并具有創新性的罰函數法理論及算法。具體來說，對於多種罰函數的罰參數的存在性，我們將給出新的充分必要性條件，使得原約束問題的任意穩定點、局部和全局極小點都是相應無約束問題的穩定點、局部和全局極小點。通過這些條件我們可以估計出算法中罰參數的大小，以及研究穩定點、局部和全局極小點的稀疏性。與此同時，我們將建立有效的算法來求解導出的無約束問題，并採用合理的方式來更新罰參數，以期找到原約束問題的廣義KKT點、局部和全局極小點。對於新的罰函數法，我們也將給出相應的收斂性分析和複雜度估計。同時，在求解圖像科學、信號重建及變量選取等領域中的一下重要問題上，我們也將此新方法與現存的有效方法進行比較。由於非凸非光滑約束問題在許多重要應用領域中都會出現，這一項目的成果將是長期有效并具有重要影響力的，我們的罰函數法將給這些問題提供一種急需而且高效的算法。

15300315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300315.value: Topological band theory was successful in explaining the properties of electronic edge modes, such as those protected edge states in quantum Hall effects and some newly designed insulating and superconducting materials. Analogous theories are now developing in the field of photonics. Very recently, some designs of photonic topological insulators and one-way topologically protected photonic modes in non-reciprocal photonic crystals have been proposed. These topologically protected non-reciprocal edge modes are novel candidates for realizations of robust optical isolators, which only allow light to pass in one direction but not the opposite. One difficulty in realizing such topologically protected one-way phenomena at optical frequencies is the requirement of large-area extreme static magnetic fields. In this proposal, we plan to use techniques similar to the topological band theory to study the spectral non-reciprocity of photon modes near plasmonic nanostructures. We will focus on non-reciprocal photon modes supported in arrays of strongly coupled plasmonic nano-resonators. This allows us to shrink the structures into the nanoscale such that the requirement of large-area static magnetic field can be reduced. In addition, there can be hybridization among plasmons and free photons in plasmonic crystals, creating additional band gaps. We will study how different hybridizations can create abrupt changes in the band topology so as to create topologically protected edge modes. We will study how those topologically protected modes can be helpful in controlling the flow of light. Last but not least, we will explain how these edge modes couple with external light sources. We expect our research will bring new insights in designing plasmonic nanostructures for non-reciprocal photonics applications. 拓撲能帶理論成功地解釋了一些重要的電子邊緣態的特性，例如量子霍爾效應和一些新材料的絕緣和超導性。此類理論正在光電子領域上發展，例如最近設計出的一些光子拓撲絕緣體及能支持非互逆單向邊緣光子態的光子晶體。這些拓撲保護的非互逆邊緣模式能夠被用於實現只允許光從一個方向通過的光隔離器。大面積的強磁性是在光學頻率實現這種拓撲保護單向現象的困難之一。 我們計劃使用類似於拓撲能帶理論的技術來研究光譜非互逆的等離激元納米結構的光子態。此項研究集中在存於等離激元納米諧振器陣列中的非互逆的光子態。這使我們能夠小縮結構，降低大面積強磁場的要求。此外，等離激元子和自由光子之間會產生雜交，創造更多的帶隙。我們將研究不同的雜交如何引致拓撲能帶結構急劇變化，從而創造拓撲保護的邊緣態。我們將研究這些拓撲保護態如何控制光的走向。最後，我們會解釋這些邊緣態與外部光源的耦合。我們希望此研究將為非互逆的納米光子學應用帶來新的見解。

15300315.label: Realisation of objectives
15300315.value: All objectives have been completely realized. Details are shown in the compiled completion report. The first proposal and the re-submitted proposal of the project were submitted to RGC in Nov 2013 and Nov 2014, respectively. The re-submitted proposal was funded starting Oct 2015. A revision of budget plan and objectives were approved by RGC afterwards according to the reduction of total budget decided by RGC. A preliminary result in the original proposal regarding the formation of non-reciprocal guided plasmon modes in arrays of plasmonc particles have been completed. The final results have led to one publication in Physical Review B [1]. Non-reciprocal bands formed by complex hybridization between free photon and guided plasmon were studied partly (Objectives 1 & 3). We found that such waveguide mode can also well serve as a sub-wavelength isolator (Objective 2). As a result, a theory based on symmetry analysis has been build and the theory suggests that spatial-temporal symmetry plays a crucial role in obtaining non-reciprocal bands [1]. In collaboration with Prof. Nicholas Fang of MIT and Prof. Tony Low of University of Minnesota, we also studied the plasmon modes in 2D materials due to chiral topological bands, in which the results have been published in Physical Review B (Rapid Communications) [2]. The work has suggested that a thin sheet of 2D material could support non-reciprocal transmission enhanced by arrays of plasmonic nanoresonators made of atomically thin materials (Objectives 1 & 2) through a non-magnetic time-reversal symmetry breaking mechanism. The publication has also been reported in multiple famous science/technology news media including MIT news [3]. A final year undergraduate student has also been trained and his study in topological bands in photonic crystals have also led to his first-author publication in Optics Letters [4], which focuses on the Zak phase topological invariant. This work was in collaboration with a PhD student (second author) who spent his final year on the project. The experience they obtained in the work have also led to another work on topological band theory and anomalous asymmetric scattering for lossy plasmonic system (Objective 3 & 4), which has been published in Scientific Reports [5]. Furthermore,we have also studied several more interesting lossy systems as well as gain systems with parity-time (PT) symmetry (Objectives 2 & 4). In Refs. [6,7,8], we have provided compact of PT-symmetric systems with simple layered geometries. We have finished our first attempt to extend the theory to plasmonic systems with nonsymmorphic symmetry [9]. Finally, the nonlinear energy conversion and loss in a hybrid plasmonic systems made of thin plasmonic film sandwiched between topological photonic crystals was studied using a rigorous time-domain approach (Objective 4). 15300315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300315.value: The topological band theory had a great impact on condensed matter physics and material science. Topologically protected photon modes may be used as one-way wave guiding at the interface between non-reciprocal photonic crystals under strong static magnetic field. These pioneer works have led to an emerging field called topological photonics. While dielectrics can be used to make these novel photonic crystals with non-trivial bands and topological edge/interface modes, plasmonic materials can add much more freedoms in designing the bands. Our study of the spectral reciprocity and non-reciprocity in plasmonic nanostructures may have a high impact on nanophotonics and plasmonics for the following reasons. Plasmonic nanostructures have been playing a crucial role in the field of nanophotonics because they offer many opportunities to control light concentration, emission, and propagation at subwavelength scale by enhancing the light-matter interaction at the nanoscale. Typical applications include surface enhanced Raman spectroscopy for detecting small molecules and nanolasers for generation of optical signals. The project also provided new ideas for designing nano-sized optical isolators, which is an essential device for routing signals in photonics and for improving stability of laser operation.

15300615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300615.value: Catalysis plays an important role in modern chemistry by providing structurally diverse functional molecules through selective functionalization and transformation of organic molecules. Given the unique reactivity and selectivity, gold catalysis has contributed to the discovery of novel organic transformation reactions under mild reaction conditions. Recently, visible light photoredox catalysis has emerged as a new research direction in sustainable chemistry development due to the intrinsic green chemistry characteristics including natural abundance, non-pollution, and renewable resource. Synergistic combination of gold and visible light photoredox catalysis will lead to novel synthetic approaches for green and sustainable organic synthesis in excellent efficiency and outstanding selectivity under environmentally friendly reaction conditions. In this proposal, we plan to design and synthesize novel BINOL-oxazoline hybrid gold(III) complexes for catalyzing cyclization of 2-alkynylbenzaldehydes with alcohols. We will fine-tune the product profiles by manipulating the experimental parameters. We aim to study the use of chiral BINOL-oxazoline hybrid gold(III) complexes for asymmetric catalysis. Under visible light irradiation, we plan to develop gold-catalyzed alkynylation of propargylamines. The reaction pathways and the roles of the gold(III) complexes in these novel organic transformation reactions will be investigated by mechanistic studies. Bioconjugation is an important interdisciplinary research area between Chemistry and Biology aiming to investigate complex biological systems. In particular, site-specific modification of biomolecules plays an indispensible role for biopharmaceutical development. On the basis of our track record in catalysis and bioconjugation research, we propose to develop visible light-induced gold-catalyzed multifunctional modification of peptides and proteins in aqueous medium. 15300615.label: Realisation of objectives
15300615.value: (1) In 2017, we have developed unprecedented stable BINOL/gold(III) complexes adopting a novel C,O-chelation mode synthesized by a modular approach through combination of 1,1’-binaphthalene-2,2’-diols (BINOLs) and cyclometalated gold(III) dichloride complexes [(C^N)AuCl2]. By X-ray crystallographic analysis, it was revealed that the bidentate BINOL ligands tautomerized and bonded to the AuIII atom through C,O-chelation to form a five-membered ring instead of the conventional O,O’-chelation giving a seven-membered ring. The crystal structure reveals that the gold(III) atom in (R)-1 adopts a square-planar geometry surrounded by cis-oxygen-nitrogen and cis-carbon-carbon atoms. The complex (R)-1 was light, air, and moisture insensitive and could be isolated and stored at ambient conditions. It is stable upon exposure to air for months. Remarkably, an axial-to-central chirality transfer occurred during the complex formation between (S)-BINOL and [(C^N)AuCl2]. The (S)-BINOL exclusively afforded the gold(III) complex (R)-1 with the quaternary stereogenic carbon center in the R configuration. To our knowledge, we are the first to synthesize chiral BINOL–oxazoline hybrid gold(III) complexes [(R)-1 and (S)-1] with an unusual C,O chelation mode. The scope of using various oxazoline- and pyridine-based cyclometalated gold(III) dichloride complexes [(C^N)AuCl2] for synthesizing chiral C,O-chelated BINOL–gold(III) complexes were studied. Treatment of various ortho-alkynylbenzaldehydes with trialkyl orthoformates in the presence of 2.5 mol% of rac-1 gave the six-membered acetal products in 62–96% yield without the five-membered counterpart as reported in literature. Interestingly, when sulfonic acid (20 mol%) was added to the reaction mixture with 2.5 mol% rac-1, a carboalkoxylation product was exclusively formed in 87% yield, but the tandem acetalization/cycloisomerization product was not obtained. The drastic change in product distribution indicated that the product selectivity of rac-1 towards ortho-alkynylbenzaldehyde is adjusted by addition of acid. This work has been published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2017, 56, 3074 –3079. (2) Along with our continuous effort on asymmetric gold catalysis, in 2019, we have developed catalytic asymmetric carboalkoxylation of alkynes by using novel chiral O,O′-chelated 4,4′-biphenol cyclometalated oxazoline gold(III) complexes with high yield (≤89%) and high enantioselectivity (≤90% ee). The modular synthesis of these chiral gold(III) complexes allows structural fine-tuning for studying their ligand effect and catalytic mechanism. It is interesting to find that enantioselectivity could be significantly improved from 19% to 90% ee by increasing the steric size of the substituent on the chiral oxazoline ligand. Catalysts with O,O′- or C,O-chelated components afforded comparable enantioselectivity (70−75% ee) with a large difference in yields (25−83%). However, reducing the steric bulkiness of the substituents on the chiral oxazoline afforded significantly lower enantioselectivities (19−28% ee). These results suggested that the enantioselectivity was mainly determined by the substituent on the chiral oxazoline ligand. ESI-MS analysis suggested that the sulfonate-coordinated gold(III) cationic species would possibly be the catalytically active species for silver-activated cyclometalated gold(III) dichloride complexes. On the other hand, for O,O′-chelated cyclometalated gold(III) complexes, we noticed that a lower acid loading decreased the intensity of the ESI-MS signal of the sulfonate-coordinated gold(III) species but improved the resulting enantioselectivity. We propose that upon treatment with acid the O,O′-chelated oxazoline cyclometalated gold(III) complexes go through protodeauration on one of the oxygen atoms of biphenol, generating a vacant site for substrate binding. The trans influence in C,N-chelated cyclometalated gold(III) complexes was reported to be the key factor for determining vacant site formation. Thus, due to the stronger trans effect of C than N, protodeauration could be preferred trans to the C of the oxazoline ligand to generate a vacant site for substrate binding that is close to the substituent on the chiral oxazoline. This work has been published in Org. Lett. 2019, 21, 6289−6294. In this connection, we have achieved the objectives of 1. To design and synthesize novel BINOL-oxazoline hybrid gold(III) complexes using a modular approach 2. To develop BINOL-oxazoline hybrid gold(III) complexes as efficient catalysts for organic transformation reactions (3) We have developed a new method for visible light-induced gold(III)-catalyzed alkynylation reaction featuring the synergistic combination of gold and visible light photoredox catalysis. In addition, this newly developed reaction has been employed as a new bioconjugation method of peptides and proteins. For example, N-pheny-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline 1a and phenylacetylene 2a were treated with [Au(pq)2]BF4 3a as the catalyst under irradiation of 5 W white LEDs in 24 h under air at room temperature. Alkynylated product 4a in 22% isolated yield was resulted. Increasing the reaction time to 48 h and 72 h gave higher yields of 60% and 62%, respectively. We have expanded the scope of this reaction by treatment of N-phenyl-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline 1a with various terminal alkynes bearing different substituents. A reaction mechanism supporting our concept of dual visible light gold catalysis was proposed. By treatment of catalyst 3a with terminal alkynes, quinolizinium 5 was generated as the photosensitizer (P) in situ. This visible light-excited in situ generated 5 could oxidize the tetrahydroisoquinoline 1 by single electron transfer (SET) processes and then the reduced photosensitizer was further oxidized by oxygen in air. A hydrogen atom on the oxidized tetrahydroisoquinoline was abstracted by the superoxide formed, resulting in the formation of iminium ion 1’. Then, the iminium ion could react with the terminal alkyne 2 to form the cross-dehydrogenative product. For bioconjugation, the alkyne handle was first incorporated into cysteine-containing peptide, STSSSCNLSK, with alkynoic amide (5 equivalent) to obtain alkyne-linked STSSSCNLSK 2i in 70% isolated yield. Then, N-pheny-1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline 1a and 2i were treated with bis-cyclometallated gold(III) complex 3a in CH3CN/H2O (1:3) under 5 W white LEDs irradiation for 72 h to give product 4l in 37% isolated yield. Treatment of electron-deficient alkyne-modified HSA 4a or BSA 4b with N-phenyl 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline (10 equiv.) and 1 (1 equiv.) in Tris-HCl (pH 8.0) buffer under irradiation (White, LEDs 5 W) for 24 h afforded modified protein 5a (31% conversion) or 5b (34% conversion) by LC-MS. This work has been summarized as a manuscript under preparation. In this connection, we have achieved the objectives of 3. To develop dual catalysis by synergistic combination of gold and visible light photoredox catalysis for alkynylation 4. To develop multifunctional bioconjugation of peptides and proteins by combining gold and visible light photoredox catalysis

15300615.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300615.value: Phosphine/gold(I) and N-heterocyclic carbene/ gold(I) complexes have been developed as efficient catalysts for organic synthesis. However, gold(I) complexes have two coordination sites with a linear geometry, leading to a challenge when arranging ligands around the gold(I) center for tuning catalytic activity and introducing a chiral environment. Gold(III) complexes have a square-planar geometry with four coordination sites, allowing easy fine-tuning through diverse ligand design in a modular approach. However, the development of gold(III) complexes for catalysis remains largely unexplored because of difficult access to the high oxidation state under mild reaction conditions and a lack of suitable non-redox ligands. The great challenge in synthesizing stable gold(III) complexes comes from the facile reduction of gold(III) complexes to either gold(I) or gold(0) species. In this project, we have developed unprecedented stable BINOL/gold(III) complexes, adopting a novel C,O-chelation mode, by a modular approach through combination of 1,1’-binaphthalene- 2,2’-diols (BINOLs) and cyclometalated gold(III) dichloride complexes [(C^N)AuCl2]. Our new approach of synthesizing novel C,O chelated BINOL–gold(III) complexes has opened up a new research direction for gold catalysis based on high-valent gold(III) chemistry. In addition, we have developed novel chiral O,O′-chelated 4,4′-biphenol cyclometalated oxazoline gold(III) complexes that were effective for asymmetric carboalkoxylation of alkynes with high yield (≤89%) and high enantioselectivity (≤90% ee). Interestingly, the enantioselectivity could be significantly improved from 19% to 90% ee by increasing the steric size of the substituent on the chiral oxazoline ligand. It is envisioned that further development of asymmetric gold(III) catalysis will lead to the discovery of novel enantioselective organic transformation reactions which would have significantly different reactivity, selectivity, and substrate scope compared with asymmetric gold(I) catalysis. Our work opens a new direction to explore the unique chiral environment around the AuIII center in asymmetric catalysis. Visible-light photoredox catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy in organic synthesis. Compared to traditional catalytic strategies, photoredox catalysis allows activation of organic substrates under mild reaction conditions with the use of visible-light as a sustainable source of energy, thus offering high biocompatibility with less damage to biomolecules compared to UV light. We have developed a new visible light-induced gold(III)-catalyzed alkynylation reaction and employed it as a new bioconjugation method. It is envisioned that this new bioconjugation reaction would be an important chemical biology tool for manipulating the properties of biomolecules and investigating their functions in complex biological systems.

15300615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300615.value: (1) We have developed unprecedented stable BINOL/gold(III) complexes adopting a novel C,O-chelation mode synthesized by a modular approach through combination of 1,1’-binaphthalene-2,2’-diols (BINOLs) and cyclometalated gold(III) dichloride complexes [(C^N)AuCl2]. In addition, we have developed novel chiral O,O′-chelated 4,4′-biphenol cyclometalated oxazoline gold(III) complexes. Notably, these newly developed chiral gold(III) catalysts are effective to catalyze asymmetric synthesis with high enantioselectivity up to 90% ee leading to chiral synthetic building blocks. We plan to further enhance the chiral environment of the chiral gold(III) catalysts in order to achieve higher enantioselectivity. In addition, effort will be directed towards the application of these useful chiral synthetic building blocks in organic synthesis. (2) We have developed a new approach featuring dual catalysis by synergistic combination of gold and visible light photoredox catalysis for alkynylation. We will further expand the scope of this reaction including more diverse starting materials for the preparation of synthetically useful building blocks for organic synthesis. (3) We have developed a new photoredox bioconjugation reaction by combining gold and visible light photoredox catalysis. Effort will be directed towards strategic incorporation of biophysical probes/affinity tags to bioactive peptides and proteins and investigations of their biological applications.

15300615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300615.value: Chemical synthesis through catalysis plays an important role in the sustainable development of our society by advancing the research and development of new functional materials with high energy efficiency and less toxic product formation. The consumption of fossil fuels for energy production has caused adverse environmental problems leading to an urgent search for new sources of clean and sustainable energy. Visible light photoredox catalysis would offer a new opportunity for the fine chemical industries to revolutionize the industrial chemical production using abundant, inexpensive and non-polluting solar energy to address global energy and environmental issues. In this project, we have developed asymmetric gold catalysis for enantioselective organic transformation reactions that provide structurally diverse chiral synthetic building blocks facilitating the construction of complex molecules. In addition, we have developed a new approach featuring dual catalysis by synergistic combination of gold and visible light photoredox catalysis for alkynylation and conducted application studies on selective modification of peptides and proteins. These newly developed synthetic methodologies would have great applications on fine chemical and pharmaceutical industries. In addition, the new and selective bioconjugation methods would have a significant impact on the fields of Chemical Biology, Biomedical Research, and Biopharmaceuticals Development.
