15304015.label: Realisation of objectives
15304015.value: For this project, the structural and dynamic factors for the large difference in inhibition potency of BLIP towards three Class A β-lactamases, TEM-1, SHV-1 and PC-1, as well as the structural and dynamic factors for the enhanced inhibition potency of three BLIP mutant variants, Y50A, D49N-Y50G and E73M, towards β-lactamases, have been investigated by using hydrogen deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) and ion mobility mass spectrometry (IM-MS), as proposed. Moreover, additional studies with BLIP mutant K74G as well as using molecular dynamics (MD) simulation have been performed. Details of the project implementation are described as below. 1. Study of β-lactamases and their complexes with BLIP by native ESI-MS, IM-MS and global HDX-MS The three Class A β-lactamases, TEM-1, SHV-1 and PC-1, and BLIP wild type and mutants were expressed, purified, characterized and verified by SDS-PAGE and ESI-MS analysis. Native and tandem MS confirmed the inhibitory bindings and stoichiometry between β-lactamases and BLIP. IM- MS was used to study the β-lactamases and their complexes with BLIP, with the results revealing that the three individual β-lactamases showed differentiated conformations while their complexes with BLIP had very similar conformations. Global HDX-MS revealed that the deuterium uptake for TEM1 was higher than that for SHV1 and PC1, indicating that the overall structures of SHV1 and PC1 could be more rigid than that of TEM1. After inhibitory binding by BLIP, all β-lactamases showed similar HDX profiles that corresponded to similar flexibility of the bound states, in consistent with the IM-MS results. 2. Study of β-lactamases and their complexes with BLIP by local HDX-MS More detailed structural and dynamic information was obtained by measuring the local HDX contents of the proteins before and after the binding. For the free β-lactamases, the H10 region showed fast deuterium exchange, reflecting very flexible structures for these three β-lactamases; the deuterium uptake of the N-terminus of protruding loop for TEM1 was significantly less than that for SHV1 and PC1, reflecting a more ordered structure for TEM1; the HDX profiles of SDN loop and C-terminus of Ω loop for TEM1 and SHV1 were similar while those for PC1 were different from TEM1 and SHV1. Upon binding with BLIP, several loop regions showed significant changes, including the protruding loop, H10 region, Ω loop and SDN loop. To validate our findings, three BLIP mutants were used to binding β-lactamases. We confirmed that the protruding loop in SHV1 showed significantly reduced flexibility upon binding to BLIP mutant E73M, while increased flexibility upon binding to wild-type BLIP. It was believed that the reduced flexibility of the protruding loop was due to the restoration of a salt bridge between D104 and K74 from SHV1 and BLIP, respectively. To further validate this hypothesis, another mutant of BLIP, K74G, with enhanced affinity to PC1 was additionally introduced to this project. This mutation eliminates the salt bridge between residue 104 and 74 from PC1 and BLIP, respectively. However, it could also reverse the deprotection effect on the protruding loop caused by wild-type BLIP. By contrast, BLIP mutation Y50A could further enhance the inhibition towards TEM1 by modulating the flexibility of the protruding loop, SDN loop and H10 region. 3. Study of BLIP wild type and mutants and their complexes with β-lactamases by local HDX-MS The conformational changes on the BLIP and three enhanced mutants (Y50A, E73M and K74G) were also investigated in their free and bound states with β-lactamases TEM1, SHV1 and PC1. It was found that the flexibility of the interdomain region was predominantly changed upon binding to TEM1 while showed no significant change upon weak binding to SHV1 or PC1. E73M and K74G on the interdomain region with improved potencies towards SHV1 and PC1, respectively, showed significantly improved flexibility of the interdomain region compared to the wild type. Several other regions, including the β-hairpin loops, helix-loop-helix motifs and termini from both domains of BLIP, also exhibited conformational changes upon binding β-lactamases and after the mutations. 4. MD simulation MD simulation was additionally applied to examine the dynamics of protein molecules at complementary time scale, i.e., ns-μs time scale. The β-lactamases and BLIP were simulated before and after the binding. The BLIP mutants were also simulated to compare with the wild type. Several loop regions, including the β-hairpin loops, were found significantly changed upon the binding and after the mutations. These results provided complementary information to our HDX-MS results. In summary, the conformational dynamics of three β-lactamases and five BLIPs has been studied in the pairwise experiments. The inhibition of TEM1 by BLIP can be enhanced by BLIP mutants Y50A and D49N-Y50G; the inhibition of SHV1 by BLIP can be enhanced by BLIP mutant E73M; the inhibition of PC1 by BLIP can be enhanced by BLIP mutant K74G. The intrinsic differences in conformational dynamics among the three β-lactamases were compared. Similarly, the intrinsic differences between BLIP and its mutants were differentiated. Combining the mass spectrometric approaches and MD simulation, we have obtained further insights into the structural and dynamic factors for the large difference in inhibition potency of BLIP towards three Class A β-lactamases and for the enhanced inhibition potency of four BLIP mutant variants, Y50A, D49N-Y50G, E73M and K74G, towards β-lactamases.

15304015.label: Major findings and research outcome
15304015.value: Our study is the first to provide comprehensive insights into the conformational dynamics of β-lactamases, BLIPs and their interactions, enabling deeper understanding on the binding mechanism and design of the inhibitors with improved potency. 1. Conformational dynamics of helix 10 region and protruding loop in class A β-lactamases for their interactions with BLIP IM-MS, HDX-MS and MD simulation revealed the conformational dynamics of three class A β-lactamases having different binding affinities with BLIP. Local dynamics of several important loop regions, i.e., the protruding loop, H10 loop, Ω loop and SDN loop, were found to be different among the β-lactamases. Upon binding with BLIP, these loops cooperatively rearranged to enhance the binding interface and to inactivate the catalytic sites. The H10 region was revealed as an important allosteric site that could modulate the inhibition of class A β-lactamases. It was suggested that the rigid protruding loop and flexible H10 region might be determinants for the effective inhibition of β-lactamases. (J. Am. Chem. Soc., in revision) 2. The role of the flexibility of the interdomain region in BLIP for the enhanced inhibition potency towards β-lactamases HDX-MS revealed that higher flexibility of the interdomain linker while more rigid interfacial β-hairpin loop 135-145 in BLIP could be desirable for the inhibitory binding. MD simulation showed significant changes in the flexibility of the β-hairpin loop 46-51 and the distant β1’-β2’ loop 115-125 of BLIP after the mutations. These findings provided a general guideline for studying multidomain inhibitory proteins and unique insights into the design of BLIP-derived inhibitors. (Manuscript under preparation for J. Am. Chem. Soc.) 3. The roles of IM-MS, HDX-MS and MD simulation Our studies demonstrated that IM-MS, HDX-MS and MD simulation could be combined to provide complementary and comprehensive information about conformational dynamics of interactions between β-lactamases and BLIP, which could not be obtained by conventional techniques such as X-ray crystallography. These approaches can be extended for studies of other protein systems and for differentiation of conformers and isomers. (Rapid Commun. Mass Spectrom. 2019, 33, 83-89; Trends Anal. Chem. 2020, 123, 11576; Trends Anal. Chem. 2020, 124, 115801.)

15304015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15304015.value: This study explored the structural and dynamic factors in the inhibitory binding between three clinically prevalent class A β-lactamases and BLIPs. The results of this study provided valuable insights into the further design of BLIP mutants with higher inhibition efficiency. For example, we found that several regions of β-lactamases such as the protruding loop, H10 loop, Ω loop and SDN loop were critical for binding with BLIP. These information reveals that BLIP mutants having stronger interactions with these regions could potentially enhance the binding affinity. In addition, the flexibility of the interdomain linker of BLIP, as reflected by the results obtained for various BLIP mutants, is critical for binding with β-lactamases. Therefore, further engineering of this region could be an effective strategy in designing BLIPs with higher inhibition potency. This study indicated that the various approaches adopted in this project, i.e., HDX-MS, IM-MS and MD simulation, could provide important structural and dynamic information on the properties of β-lactamases and BLIP. These approaches could be extended to study of other β-lactamases (e.g., the carbapenem-hydrolyzing class D β-lactamases), other inhibitory proteins, other protein systems, and for differentiation of conformers and isomers.

15304015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15304015.value: β-Lactamase inhibitory protein (BLIP) can effectively inactivate a variety of class A β-lactamases, but with very different degrees of potency. Understanding the roles of BLIP in inhibition of class A β-lactamases can provide insights for novel inhibitor design. However, this problem was poorly solved based on the static structures obtained by X-ray crystallography. In this study, ion mobility mass spectrometry, hydrogen deuterium exchange mass spectrometry and molecular dynamics simulation were employed to reveal the conformational dynamics of interactions between three class A β-lactamases (TEM1, SHV1 and PC1) and BLIPs. Our results indicated that the rigid protruding loop and flexible H10 region might be determinants for the effective inhibition of class A β-lactamases, and that higher flexibility of the interdomain linker while more rigid interfacial β-hairpin loop 135-145 on BLIP could be desirable for enhanced inhibitory binding. Based on these results, engineered BLIPs can be rationally designed to bind β-lactamases with enhanced potency. Our study is the first to provide comprehensive insights into the conformational dynamics of class A β-lactamases upon inhibitory binding with BLIP, which implies alternative and unique strategies for the study of β-lactamases and the design of novel inhibitors.

15304215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304215.value: Ozone in the troposphere ─ a layer of the atmosphere extending from Earth’s surface to about 10 km altitude ─ plays a major role in Earth’s atmospheric chemistry and also acts as an important greenhouse gas. At ground level, ozone is the principal air pollutant in photochemical smog which has haunted many urban areas, including Hong Kong. Therefore, the long-term trend in tropospheric ozone abundance and the underlying mechanisms have been a major concern of environmental science and regulatory communities. Compared to other parts of the northern hemisphere, studies of tropospheric ozone in subtropical Asia have been very limited, despite the fact that this region has undergone tremendous environmental changes due to fast urbanization and industrialization. In this project, we propose to analyze long-term records of ozone measurements obtained at surface and by balloons in Hong Kong during the period of 1994-2017. This data set is the only available long-term (>20 years) record in China. We will analyze emission and meteorological data and apply a sophisticated chemical transport model. The primary objectives are to establish the ozone trend in the lowermost portion of the troposphere from 1994 to 2017 in subtropical south China and to delineate/quantify the roles of changes in emissions of ozone-producing ingredients and climate in the ozone trend. The results of this study will improve our knowledge on tropospheric ozone in rapidly developing Asia (China in particular), which will facilitate a more accurate assessment of the impacts of ozone on the environment and climate, and help to develop strategies to mitigate current ground-level ozone pollution in Hong Kong and other cities in China mainland. 對流層是自地表至高空約10km的地球大氣層，對流層中的臭氧在大氣化學中扮演著一個異常重要的角色，此外它還是一種重要的溫室氣體。在許多城市地區包括香港，光化學煙霧作為一種常見的污染現象困擾已久，而臭氧則是光化學煙霧中最主要的污染物。因此，研究對流層臭氧濃度的長期趨勢及其內在機制一直是環境科學界及監管機構的一個主要問題。 伴隨著快速的城市化和工業化發展，亞熱帶亞洲地區在大氣環境方面經歷了巨大的變遷。然而同北半球其他地區相比，這一地區有關臭氧的研究卻十分有限。因此在本項目中，我們計劃開展1994﹣2017年香港地區地面及探空氣球臭氧觀測長期記錄的分析工作。值得一提的是這一觀測數據集是中國迄今最長的觀測記錄(大於20年)。項目中我們將分析長時期的污染物排放量及氣象數據并會藉用先進的化學傳輸模式等手段。此項目的主要目標是建立1994年至2017年華南地區底層對流層中臭氧的長期變化趨勢，並且區分或量化臭氧前體物的排放量及氣象因素分別在其中所起到的作用。這項研究的成果將有助於增進我們對於快速發展的亞洲地區（特別是中國）的對流層臭氧問題的相關認識，并將有助於更為準確的衡量臭氧對於環境和氣候的影響，從而能為進一步減輕香港及中國其他城市近地面臭氧污染問題出謀劃策。

15304215.label: Realisation of objectives
15304215.value: To achieve objective 1 and 2, we have carried out (1) data analysis of long-term (1994-2018) surface and vertical ozone measurements of (O3) and surface carbon monoxide (CO) in Hong Kong (2) long-term air mass trajectory analysis with the HYSPLIT model (3) data analysis of the large-scale and local scale meteorological parameters, ozone precursors from satellite data and climate indexes and (4) Modelling the effects of weather pattern change on surface O3 in East Asia by a chemical transport model. Detailed descriptions of the activities are as following: 1. Trend analysis of long-term O3 and CO data in Hong Kong Twenty-five years (1994-2018) of hourly O3 and CO measured at a coastal background site (HT) were processed. The annual changes, seasonal variations, and change rates at each percentile of were investigated. Ozonesonde data were obtained from the Hong Kong Observatory for period of 1994-2017. We analyzed the trend at surface and in different heights in the troposphere. To determine the magnitude and sign of the trend, we adopted the nonparametric Theil-Sen (T-S) estimator and the Mann-Kendall (M-K) test, because they do not require prior assumptions of statistical distribution for the data and are resistant to outliers. The T-S estimator was used to compute the rate of change, and the M-K test was used to determine the level of signiﬁcance. We computed the linear trend for annual and seasonal means and according to airmasses. 2. Long-term air mass trajectory analysis with HYSPLIT model Hourly 10-day backwards trajectories arriving at Hong Kong were calculated for 1994-2018 by using the Hybrid Single-Particle Lagrangian Integrated Trajectory model (HYSPLIT, Version 4.9). The model was driven by 6-hourly Air Resources Laboratory FNL archive data with a resolution of 190 km (ftp://arlftp. arlhq.noaa.gov/pub/archives/reanalysis/). All trajectories were then classified into four clusters (“East China”, “Central China+PRD”, “Aged Continental”, and “Marine”) to represent the climatological transport pattern in recent years. The Marine airmass account for 25.8% of the total trajectories, 80% of which are in summer. The East China, Central China+PRD and Aged Continental accounted for 32.9%, 11.2% and 30.1% of the total trajectories, respectively. We also examined the long-term change in the frequency of each type of airmass transported to Hong Kong. To examine the relation between the variation in frequency of each air mass with large-scale transport pattern by the climate index, such as East Asian Summer Monsoon index, South China Sea Monsoon Index, and ENSO index. No distinct relation was found between these indexes with the frequency of airmass and ozone variations. 3. Meteorological data and satellite data We analyzed long-term trend of large-scale meteorological data by using National Center for Atmospheric Prediction and National Center for Atmospheric Research (NCEP/ NCAR) global reanalysis data (https://rda.ucar.edu/datasets/ds090.0/). The yearly variations of specific humidity and precipitation water presented a significant upward trend by k=0.02 g/kg and k=0.14 kg/m2 over the South China coast and Southeast Asia. There was no significant trend in the variation of temperature and solar radiation, with no obvious difference between the two periods. The trend of meteorological parameters (precipitation, solar radiation, temperature, relative humidity) in Hong Kong regions was also analyzed. We also examine the long-term trend of the tropospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2) and formaldehyde (HCHO) column values by satellite. The increasing trend for both land and sea areas indicated an increasing emission in NOx and VOCs in Southeast Asia, including shipping activities in the South China Sea. 4. Chemical transport model simulations A regional chemical transport model WRF-Chem was used to evaluate the effect of changes in weather parameters on the summer ozone level. The model simulations were driven by the NCEP/NCAR reanalysis data in July 1994,1995,1996,2016,2017, and 2018, with the 2016 emission inventory. We also conducted the simulation by global model (Geos-Chem and AM3). Both the two models were overpredicted the observed surface O3 in HT sites, leading to a difficulty in using the global model to simulate ozone at the regional station of HT. 5. Integrate HT data with global ozone database We compared the ozone data in HT site with the HKEPD sites in urban areas. And the HT ozone data from 1995-20015 was also be provided to an international ozone assessment project (TOAR). These combined data have been used to establish long-term trends of both surface O3 and lower tropospheric O3 in a global scale. Our data represented the only data from the tropical region of East Asia.

15304215.label: Major findings and research outcome
15304215.value: • The analysis shows that the surface ozone in the background atmosphere of the southern China has been continuously increasing with an overall 0.35 ppbv/yr. The average ozone mixing ratio from 0 to 1km increased by 0.59 ppbv/year. Compared with the ozone trend in the early years during 1994-2006 (0.62 ppbv/yr, p<0.05), the increase rate of ozone has slowed in recent years (during 2008-2016, 0.1 ppbv/yr, p=0.38). The increase in surface ozone can be seen in all four seasons (0.33 ppbv/year in spring, 0.50 ppbv/year in summer, 0.40 ppbv/year in autumn, and 0.36 ppbv/year in winter). It is interesting that the highest rate of ozone increase was shown in summer, when the south China coast receives the cleanest air of any season. • The increase rate of ozone in marine airmass was 0.36ppbv/year, in “East China” was 0.37ppbv /year in “Central China + PRD” was 0.39 ppbv/year and in “Aged continental” was 0.34 ppbv/year. • The average ozone mixing ratio at 0 to 1km obtained with ozonesonde increased by 0.59 ppbv/year(p<0.01). The ozone peak at 3-4km in springtime indicated the influence of biomass burning from Southeast Asia on the springtime free tropospheric O3 over southern China. • The annual mean CO level at HT appeared to decrease from 1994 to 2000, increased until 2006, and then decreased again over the ﬁnal 4 years. Negative trends were shown in the continent originated air masses (East and Central China; p = 0.02 to 0.10), while no obvious trend was seen in the marine air mass (p = 0.42). • A negative and positive anomaly of specific humidity and precipitation water during 1994-2006 and 2007-2018 indicated a dryer climate in the first period and moister weather in later part of 1994-2018. The weather condition in July 2016-2018 would reduce the ozone level in Southeast Asia and South China compared to July 1994-1996. These results can be attributed to the increase in the dilution of surface-emitted ozone precursors by the enhanced atmospheric conventions in recent years. • The Hong Kong data filled in the data gap in the tropical region of East Asia, and revealed different ozone seasonal pattern compared to the other parts of the world.

15304215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15304215.value: Tropospheric ozone has great inﬂuence on environmental issues ranging from air quality, to ecosystem productivity and to climate warming. Assessing the ozone impacts in fast‐developing Asia has been hindered by lacking long‐term measurements. This project reports and analyses the longest continuous record of surface ozone in nonurban areas of tropical Asia. Using comprehensive tools, we reveal that the measurements on the south China's coast detected different ozone trends in air masses from eastern China (increasing in early years but stabilizing lately) and from Southeast Asia (continuously rising and at the largest rate). The latter ﬁnding is particularly striking, and we show that the recent weather patterns counteracted the expected increase of ozone due to emissions increases from Southeast Asia. Our results ﬁll the gap in the long‐term ozone trends in Asia and highlight the complex interaction of weather and emission in driving the ozone trend.

15304415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304415.value: In recent years, electron spintronic materials have attracted extensive research inter-ests. As conventional ferromagnets fail to meet the requirement of strong spin-dependency for future spintronic devices, cobalt-based half metallic ferromagnets (Co-HMFs) is believed to be a suitable candidate as future spin-injector materials. While most research in the literature has focused on studying the composi-tional effects of these compounds, this project aims to develop thin films of Co-HMFs and to investigate the effect of dynamic lattice tuning on their physical properties. Co2FeAlxSi1-x (CFAS) is chosen as the main system in this study because a large number of studies revealed that the physical properties of this system are sensitive to subtle distortion of the structure. The experimental part of the project will first involve the deposition of CFAS thin films with desired compositions and crystal structures by means of laser molecular beam epitaxy. Structures of the deposited thin films will then be characterized followed by examination of their physical properties (including spin-dependent electron transport behaviors under different conditions, magnetic properties and etc.). Based on the experimental results and optimized processing condition, high-quality thin films could be fabricated. The second part of the project involves developing epitaxial CFAS thin films on piezoelectric single crystal substrates (lead magnesium niobate titanate – PMNT and etc) and examining the impact of lattice symmetry on superconducting behaviors in the thin films. Due to piezoelectric effect, the single crystal substrate should undergo a lattice distortion (up to ~2% for PMNT) upon the application of an external voltage, inducing a symmetrical change in the thin film via mechanical coupling, which in turn, could impact the spintronic properties in CFAS. Through in-situ structural characterization and electrical measurements under different strain levels, direct observation of the structure-property relationship could be made, which could help to gain better understanding of the origin of the HMF band structures in the thin films. Once the above materials have been successfully developed, the research could be extended to the development and characterization of other Co-HMF thin films such as CoMnAlSi, CoFeS and etc. The idea of this project is thought to be original since there is not yet an in-depth and systematic investigation of the kind. We anticipate that the output from this research should benefit the local research in applied physics. N/A

15304715.value: Development of new synthetic strategy to prepare PEI-based IPP dots with high emission efficiency. Two approaches based on self-assembly of chemically modified poly(ethyleneimine) into nanoparticles and crosslinking with hydrophobic or hydrophilic vinylic molecules will be attempted. Once the optimal approach is found, we will aim at enhancing the quantum yield through systematic studies of reaction conditions including temperature, reaction time, and solution pH. The optimal conditions which give the highest quantum yield will be used for subsequent studies. Study of factors which affect the IPP formation and structure-fluorescence relationship with respect to maximum excitation and emission wavelength, quantum yield, lifetime and Stokes shift. These factors include polymer molecular structure and weight, degree of hydrophobic modification, crosslinking method and degree, as well as chemical structure of vinylic molecules. These results are fundamental to understanding the photophysics of the IPP dots. Characterization of the IPP dots including chemical structure and composition, particle size and size distribution as well as particle morphology using various advanced analytical tools. Study of photoluminescent phenomenon of the IPP dots in water. Effect of excitation wavelength on emission peak; pH-dependence of emission intensity at different solution pHs; effect of temperature on emission intensity; concentration-dependence of emission intensity and photostability will be systematically studied. Photoluminescence mechanism will also be elucidated through investigating lifetime and excitation behaviours of the IPP dots using time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy. Exploration of potential applications of the PEI-based IPP dots in cell imaging and intracellular delivery. We will evaluate the potential use of PEI-based IPP dots as a dual fluorescent probe and nanocarrier for imaging-guided drug and gene deliveries.

15304715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304715.value: Multifunctional nanomaterials that can play complementary roles in imaging, diagnostics, and drug therapy will be able to redefine the paradigm in the future. Design and synthesis of nanocarriers that are capable of delivering biologically active compounds at the optimum dose, time and place is a fundamental material challenge. Among various nanomaterials for nanomedicine, only biocompatible polymeric nanocarriers have been approved for clinical application. Therefore, development of polymer-based multifunctional nanoparticles which can function as dual-modular imaging probes and drug carriers for imaging-guided therapy is highly desirable. Intrinsic photoluminescence polymer (IPP) dots, which are macromolecular-based fluorophores in nano-scale diameters, are new class of photoluminescent nanomaterials. Unlike classical photoluminescent materials based on small organic molecules and inorganic nanoparticles, the IPP dots are built through control aggregation of non-conjugated polymer into nano-sized particles, which then can re-emit strong fluorescent light upon light excitation. We have recently discovered that chemical modification of a water-soluble polymer, namely poly(ethyleneimine) (PEI) through varying its hydrophobic/hydrophilic balance could result in the formation of uniform IPP dots with average diameters less than 50 nm in water. These PEI-based water-dispersible IPP dots are not only ultra-bright with quantum yield approaching 0.2 (based on quinine sulphate standard), but also multi-color fluorescence with emission peaks in red window. Furthermore, the IPP dots possess amino functionality, nano-scaled size, inherent fluorescence property, water dispersibility, robustness, and low toxicity. Thus we envision that this type of IPP dots is a new class of multifunctional nanoparticles for cell imaging and image-guided deliveries, and will play a vital role in cancer therapy in the future. There are five main objectives of this project: 1) Development of new synthetic strategy to prepare PEI-based IPP dots with high emission efficiency in water; 2) Systematic studies of factors which affect the particle formation and structure-emission property relationship with respect to maximum excitation and emission wavelengths, quantum yield, lifetime and Stokes shift. Other factors which may change the behaviour of IPP dots such as chemical environment and photoresistance property will also be investigated; 3) Material characterizations including chemical structure and composition, particle size, distribution and morphology using various advanced analytical tools; 4) Study of photoluminescence mechanism of the IPP dots including their lifetimes and excited behaviours; 5) Exploration of their potential applications as multifunctional fluorophores and nanocarriers for cell imaging and image-guided intracellular deliveries. 15304715.label: Major findings and research outcome
15304715.value: Three approaches to synthesize water-dispersible intrinsic photoluminescence polymer (IPP) dots have been developed. The first approach is the modification of a water-soluble polymer, followed by in situ self-assembly of the resulting amphiphilic polymer into nanoparticles. Polyethyleneimine (PEI) was hydrophobically modified with n-butyl acrylate (nBA), followed by self-assembly to form nanoparticles. The resultant PEI-nBA nanoparticles possess strong fluorescent intensity because of “restriction enhanced emission.” An optimal substitution degree for in-situ self-assembly has been carefully determined. The second approach is based on the carbonization of poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) from the PMMA/PEI nanoparticles. This process involved the hydrothermal treatment of the preformed PMMA-PEI nanoparticles in generating carbon dots (CDs) through decomposing the PMMA polymer cores. The newly created CDs were simultaneously encapsulated by the exiting PEI shells, giving stable CDs@PEI nanoparticle. This type of nanoparticles possesses ultra-bright, upconversion PL properties, and excellent pH stability. The third approach is based on the polyion complex formation of methyl acrylic acid (MAA) modified PEI via in situ electrostatic interaction. The PEI/PMAA nanoparticles not only show very bright fluorescence in solution, but also exhibit phosphorescence and ultra-long afterglow phenomenon in the solid-state. Various parameters including the degree of hydrophobic modification, crosslinking method and percentage, as well as other reaction conditions have been investigated to optimize fluorescence properties such as maximum excitation and emission wavelength, quantum yield, lifetime and Stokes shift. The IPP dots have been carefully characterized including their chemical structure and composition, particle size and distribution as well as particle morphology using various advanced analytical tools such as elemental analysis, FTIR, 1H-NMR, Raman spectroscopy, particle size analyzer, zeta-potential measurement, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), photoluminescent spectra measurement, absolute quantum yield, and fluorescent lifetime measurement. Their photoluminescent phenomenon in water including the effect of excitation wavelength on emission peak, pH-dependence of emission intensity at different solution pH, effect of temperature on emission intensity, concentration-dependence of emission intensity and photostability have also been investigated. The potential application of the PEI-nBA nanoparticles as a fluorescent probe for in vitro multicolor cell imaging has been investigated. The ultra-bright CDs@PEI nanogels enabled us to study intracellular trafficking of DNA/nanocarrier complexes in HeLa cells with confocal microscopy, leading to a better understanding of endosomal escape step in gene transfection. Furthermore, in vitro and in vivo cytotoxicity, biodistribution, pharmacokinetic properties, and clearance using 4T1 tumor-bearing BALB/C mice as the animal model have been systematically evaluated for their potential biological application as intrinsic fluorescence nanocarriers.

15304715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15304715.value: We discover that the PEI/PMAA nanoparticles not only show very bright fluorescence in solution, but also exhibit phosphorescence and ultra-long afterglow phenomenon in the solid-state. They also have excellent compatibility with commercial resins such as silicone, epoxy, and poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA), etc. Furthermore, the photoluminescent nanoparticles (PLNPs) are synthesized based on the emulsion polymerization in water, which is environmentally friendly, low cost, and suitable for large-scale production. We have done some preliminary studies on the use of this type of nanoparticles as a nanofiller in epoxy resin for LED light cover. Results demonstrated that blending appropriate amount of the nanoparticles could achieve both high haze and high transmittance with the reduction in blue light. We also found that there was a synergistic effect when mixing the nanoparticles with commercial light diffusers. Therefore, we have successfully obtained ITF Tier-3 funding in 2018 to develop a new generation of light diffusers with both high haze and high light transmittance for LED lenses or covers. The successful development of this kind of nano-scale light diffuser will significantly advance the LED light system and saving of lighting energy.

15304715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15304715.value: The development of polymer-based multifunctional nanoparticles, which can function as dual-modular imaging probes and drug carriers for imaging-guided therapy, is highly desirable. Unlike traditional photoluminescent materials based on small organic molecules and inorganic nanoparticles, intrinsic photoluminescence polymer (IPP) dots are macromolecular-based fluorophores in the nano-scale diameters. They are constructed through the control aggregation of non-conjugated polymer into nano-sized particles, which can emit intense fluorescent light upon light excitation. This project has developed three synthetic strategies to prepare polyethyleneimine (PEI)-based IPP dots with high emission efficiency in the water. Factors that affect the particle formation and structure-emission relationship, including maximum excitation and emission wavelengths, quantum yield and lifetime, have been systematically investigated. Other factors which may change the behavior of IPP dots such as chemical environment and photo-resistance property were also examined. Material characterizations, including chemical structure and composition, particle size, distribution, and morphology, as well as fluorescence lifetimes, were carefully studied using various advanced analytical tools. Potential biological applications as intrinsic fluorescence nanocarriers have been evaluated, including cell imaging, in vitro and in vivo cytotoxicity, biodistribution, pharmacokinetic properties, and clearance using 4T1 tumor-bearing BALB/C mice as the animal model. Results demonstrate promising photoluminescent materials and multifunctional nanocarriers for image-guided therapy.

15500615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500615.value: “So why the f*** doesn't it do that??” on one summer day of 2008, Steve Jobs questioned his team angrily when he found out that MobileMe (an online service provided by Apple) did not meet his expectations (Viticci, 2011). Actually, this IT genius and incredible leader often unleashes his incisive temper on those who fail to meet his incredibly high standards, and surprisingly, his teams can often come up with and share great ideas that shake the world eventually. By contrast, in often times when facing an angry boss, people tend to hide things under the carpet rather than speaking up (see a recent Wall Street Journal article by Shellenbarger, 2012). The above anecdotal discussions suggest that leader’s anger may have complicated effects on employee upward voice, or employees’ expression of constructive work-related ideas to organizational leaders. In many organizations, employees are uniquely positioned to identify emerging problems and opportunities that can critically influence the effectiveness of work processes and outcomes. In this context, upward voice plays a critical role in linking employees' private knowledge and insights with leaders' organizational influence. The purpose of this project is to explore whether, why, and when leader’s display of anger influences employee voice. Based on emotion as social information theory (Van Kleef, De Dreu, & Manstead, 2010), we differentiate two types of anger: anger toward tasks or task-focused anger, and anger toward employees or person-focused anger. We argue that task-focused anger signals leader’s dissatisfaction with tasks or current situation, and it would motivate employees to reflect status-quo, thus leading to upward voice; such an effect would be even stronger when employees have a strong epistemic motivation. By contrast, person-focused anger signals leader’s dominance and status, and it would threats employees’ self-esteem, thus discouraging voice; such an effect would be even stronger when employees have a high power distance orientation. Our initial findings have suggested that it is important to examine voice at the within-individual level and that our hypothesized model makes sense. In order to fully test our model, we propose to conduct (1) a measure-development study to develop scales to measure two types of anger, and (2) an event-based experience sampling study to track interaction episodes between leaders and employees for two weeks. This proposed research would deepen our understanding of the relationship between leader’s emotions and employee voice, and shift voice research to a more dynamic, within-individual perspective. “它他x的为什么不能做这些事？”2008年的某个夏日，乔布斯愤怒地质问苹果公司的MobileMe（苹果公司的一种网络服务）团队，为什么没能达到他的预期 (Viticci, 2011)。事实上，这个IT奇才经常会对不能满足他要求的手下发火，但神奇的是，他领导的团队总是能找到并分享新点子，创造一个又一个的奇迹。相反，在愤怒的老板面前，很多员工通常会缄口不言 (Shellenbarger, 2012)。 上面的讨论告诉我们，领导的愤怒对员工的谏言行为——也就是员工对领导和组织表达和工作相关、有建设性建议的行为，有着复杂的影响。在许多组织中，员工能够辨别存在的问题、鉴别提高组织绩效的方法。因此，员工谏言至关重要。 我们这项研究的主要目的就在于探察领导的愤怒与员工谏言行为之间关系，以及理清这种关系的中介机制和边界条件。基于“情绪社会信息理论” (Van Kleef, De Dreu, & Manstead, 2010)，我们区分两种愤怒：针对任务的愤怒和针对个人的愤怒。我们认为，针对任务的愤怒传达了领导对于任务或者现状的不满，它会激励员工反省现状，从而促使谏言；而且这条路径会在员工具有高认知动机的时候更强。而针对个人的愤怒传达了领导的统治权威，它会威胁到员工的自尊，从而抑制谏言；而这条路径会在员工具有高权力距离价值的时候会更强。 我们之前的研究为我们的研究假设提供了一些初步证据。为了全面地检验我们的假设模型，我们计划（1）做一个量表开发研究，和（2）一个基于事件的经验采样研究，跟踪领导和员工在两周中的互动情况。我们的研究可以加深我们对于领导情绪和员工谏言影响的理解，并且可以为已有谏言研究带来一个更加动态的视角。

15500615.label: Realisation of objectives
15500615.value: We have achieved the three objectives proposed in this project. First, we found that leader's display of anger would influence employee voice, and the effects are contingent upon the characteristics of the anger (displaced vs. direct). Specifically, leader displaced anger expression evoked subordinate work withdraws and discourage voice; while leader direct anger expression triggers employee voice. Second, we found both cognitive and emotional mechanisms to explain why leader's display of anger would influence employee voice behavior. In particular, leader displaced anger expression evoked subordinate work withdraws via increased fear and reduced momentary OBSE, but that leader direct anger expression triggered subordinate voice behaviors via increased guilt and increased momentary OBSE. Finally, we identified the boundary conditions for the effects of leader's display of anger would influence employee voice. That is, subordinate power distance orientation exaggerated the above indirect effects by intensifying subordinates’ emotional and cognitive responses to leader direct and displaced anger expressions. In summary, we have achieved all three proposed objectives.

15500615.label: Major findings and research outcome
15500615.value: Research remains equivocal on the effects of leader anger expression on subordinate work behaviors and outcomes. Drawing upon research on social effects of anger expression and the approach-avoidance framework, we posit that whether employees engage in approach- or avoidance-oriented behavioral responses to leader anger is contingent on the alignment between the target of anger expression and the elicitation of the anger experience (i.e., displaced vs. direct anger). Results from an experience sampling study with 782 time-lagged responses from 82 participants and a randomized experiment involving 163 participants showed that leader displaced anger expression evoked subordinate work withdraws via increased fear and reduced momentary OBSE but that leader direct anger expression triggered subordinate voice behaviors via increased guilt and increased momentary OBSE. Moreover, subordinate power distance orientation exaggerated the above indirect effects by intensifying subordinates’ emotional and cognitive responses to leader direct and displaced anger expressions. Our research sheds lights on the importance of expressing anger in a plausible manner with the appropriate target for achieving constructive effects. These findings have been reported in Liu, Wang, and Liao (In press). In addition, these findings have important implications to how leaders regulate emotions in the team context for better team performance (Wang, Liu, & Chu, 2019), as well as to how leaders manage the interactions with members on the daily base (Liao, LIU, Li, & Song, 2019; Liao, Yam, Johnson, LIU, & Song, 2018). 15500615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15500615.value: This project also stimulate some new ideas for further research in the area of voice behavior and leader-member interactions. For example, we acknowledge that there could be a difference between leader anger expression and leader anger display. Leader anger expression relies on the existence of targets. In another word, there is a specific receiver (or several specific receivers) of leader anger. In comparison, leader anger display may not involve such receivers but only observers. In this case, the social information interpreted by employees might be completely divergent. For instance, Glomb and Hulin (1997) provided some preliminary evidence showing that targets of leader anger expression, compared with observers, might be more likely to legitimize leader anger expression. Future research might explore the distinct effects of leader anger expression on targets and observers. In the future, we will design experiments and collect field data to test these ideas. It would be really interesting to see how emotional display and emotional expression play different role in leader-member interactions.

15500615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15500615.value: Steve Jobs, an IT genius and incredible leader, often unleashed his incisive temper on those who failed to meet his incredibly high standards, and surprisingly, his teams could often come up with and share great ideas that shook the world eventually. Similarly, in the Oscar-winning movie “Whiplash”, the famed conductor (Mr. Fletcher) told his student that “There are no two words in the English language more harmful than "good job".” He felt that it was his responsibility to push people beyond what's expected from them, and he always displayed anger to his students for demanding better performance. In short, anger displayed by the authority seems to motivate members to proactively change the status quo on the way to achieve extraordinary performance. Through field studies and lab experiments, we found that leader's display of anger may hurt the member's self-esteem and create fear if the member is the displaced target of anger, but it may boost the member's self-esteem and create guilt if the member is indeed the correct target of anger. Moreover, we found that all these effects were more salient when the member's power distance orientation was high rather than low.

15500815.label: Project Objectives
15500815.value: Propose and examine controversial efficacies of three relationship governance mechanisms, i.e. idiosyncratic investments, goal congruence, and interpersonal relationships, on resellers' behavioral response within and beyond a relationship dyad. 15500815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500815.value: The research proposes and examines controversial efficacies of three relationship governance mechanisms in marketing channel network: idiosyncratic investments, goal congruence, and interpersonal relationships. All the three mechanisms (or safeguards) come from dominant theoretical perspectives on exchange: transaction cost economics, agency theory, and relationship marketing, and have been widely studied in previous literature on interorganizational exchange. On one hand, previous literature has documented the capability of these relationship safeguards to encourage joint actions, reduce opportunism, and enhance relationship competitiveness. On the other hand, none of the previous research has taken into account the interests and priorities of the recipient party (i.e. the reseller who is the target of a powerful supplier’s governance strategy) beyond a given dyadic relationship. In fact, given today’s hyper competitive marketplace and increasing consolidation of resellers at all levels of distribution, resellers often work with incumbent suppliers and look for new suppliers and opportunities simultaneously to reduce risks and optimize resource allocation. Therefore, it is indeed surprising that few, if any, research in interorganizational exchanges has examined the efficacies of the three dominant relationship safeguards in view of resellers’ both intrachannel and interchannel reactions. In this study, we conceptualize resellers’ intrachannel reaction as relationship strengthening strategy, which refers to their continuous commitment of resources and efforts to strengthen its relationship with incumbent suppliers. In contrast, we term resellers’ interchannel behavior as relationship diversifying strategy, through which the reseller adjusts its resource allocation to consider, contact, and seek potential suppliers for new business opportunities. We develop a theoretical framework to propose that some safeguards are more potent as they can increase the reseller’s efforts to strengthen its current relationship and discourage its diversifying tendency, whereas others exhibit double-edged effects, increasing both relationship strengthening and diversifying behaviors. Our investigation will be based on a longitudinal survey of distributors from multiple industries in China, with three specific research questions: • Are there “dual effects” – relationship safeguards directed towards a particular reseller impact its behavior within and beyond a given relationship as in the forms of relationship strengthening and diversifying strategies? • If so, how does relationship diversifying strategy transpire in the given dyad, affecting the interests of both parties? • Are there ways to enhance the bright side and mitigate the dark side of relationship diversifying behavior? By addressing these questions, the study contributes to a broader understanding of long-term management of interorganizational relationship in distribution channels.

15500815.label: Realisation of objectives
15500815.value: Over the past two decades, marketing scholars have acknowledged that firms are complex entities that often engage in activities that seem contradictory in nature. This realization has been most widely heralded in the organizational ambidexterity literature, which examines the degree to which organizations simultaneously explore new capabilities while exploiting existing capabilities. In our study, we argue that firms can be simultaneously committed to an existing exchange partner while seeking alternative exchange partners. We focus on this apparent controversy and examine its antecedents and consequences. In particular, we conceptualize buyers’ intrachannel reaction as relationship strengthening strategy, which refers to their continuous commitment of resources and efforts to strengthen its relationship with incumbent suppliers. In contrast, we conceptualize their interchannel behavior as relationship diversifying strategy, through which the buyer adjusts its resource allocation to consider, contact, and seek potential suppliers for new business opportunities. We find that the distinction between these two types of channel relationship strategy is meaningful, because certain relationship safeguards that suppliers directed towards a particular buyer can influence its behavior towards other alternative suppliers, which bears consequences to the focal dyad and the buyer’s own performance. We realized our objectives in three ways. First, we bring to light a notion, not yet researched, but highly relevant to the issue of preserving interorganizational relationship outcomes – that is, buyers’ own priorities in balancing current and potential suppliers. We go beyond a dyadic view of buyers’ behavioral response to relationship safeguards to propose the salience of relationship diversifying strategy and contrast it with the frequently mentioned relationship strengthening efforts. We further examine the joint effects, which we term as Relationship Ambidexterity effects on firm-level and dyadic-level outcomes. Second, we challenge the conventional wisdom about the efficacies of relationship safeguards. As we gauge their impacts on both intrachannel strengthening behavior, and more importantly, the interchannel diversifying behavior, we reveal the double-edged effects of some safeguards. Without a critical assessment from the views of the recipient reseller and its priorities beyond a single relationship, we run the risk of naively encouraging a form of governance without knowing its potential “diversifying” effect. In addition, from the buyer’s perspective, we found that in fact, the diversification-focused group have developed relatively strong downstream customer bonds and rich experience in their area of business. These firms tilt toward building more potential links in their supply market in order to gain more business and cater to future changes. Interestingly, these buyers actually perform better than their exclusively committed and larger-sized counterparts do, but worse than the ambidextrous firms, possibly because of the certain cost, yet uncertain returns associated with diversification activities. Third, this research offers suggestions for managing and mitigating the dark side of buyers’ interchannel behaviors. Interestingly, the remedy is also beyond a given supplier-reseller dyad. Using time-lagged data, we test the ability of reseller network cohesiveness – defined as the closeness among resellers – to moderate the effects of relationship diversifying strategy. We measure the reseller’s own competitiveness and its opportunism towards the incumbent supplier one year after the main survey. In doing so, this research provides important managerial implications on the cautious deployment of dyadic relationship safeguards and the usefulness of developing network cohesion to increase joint gains. Finally, we found that when market changes fast and unpredictably, it brings two contrasting requirements on the firm: flexibility and efficiency. If a firm is exclusively committed to existing suppliers, it has insufficient flexibility to face uncertainties, and the threat of obsolescence is particularly salient. Diversification brings increased value to the firm in terms of information for decision-making, access to additional or new suppliers, and an enhanced ability to cater to consumer preference changes. At the same time, the efficiency benefit that commitment adds to diversification increases when market is turbulent. In fact, when the market is uncertain, firms’ ability to ascertain the true value of newly acquired information is reduced, which motivates buyers to stay with existing relationships even after having collected information about new ones. An exclusive focus on diversification will result in inadequate control over cost and supply relationships. An ambidextrous approach combining relationship commitment and diversification thus will generate greater benefit in an uncertain environment.

15500815.label: Major findings and research outcome
15500815.value: The primary outcome is a research paper with Aric Rindfleisch (University of Illinois), Danny Wang (HKBU), and Jeff Wang (Co-I, Monash University) on Relationship Ambidexterity, which was first sent to Journal of Marketing (JM) and was rejected. Then we substantially enriched the study with a new qualitative research, a total reframe of the theory, and a new empirical approach. We presented the paper to Christine Moorman (Editor-in-Chief, JM) in the JM-Research Development Workshop in April 2019. She gave us positive feedbacks and encouraged us to send it to JM as a new submission. Now the paper is in the final stage of proofreading and we aim to submit it by July 2019. In the study, we introduce the concept of Relationship Ambidexterity and propose that it occurs when an organization is simultaneously committed to an existing exchange partner while seeking alternative exchange partners. Our conceptualization outlines the situations under which firms direct their attention to both an existing exchange partner (i.e., commitment) as well as potential new exchange partners (i.e., diversification). Our inquiry begins with a qualitative study among suppliers and then offers an empirical test via a study that blends survey and archival data. The second outcome is research related to customer relationship management, which is from the supplier’s perspective. We presented the paper in American Marketing Association (AMA) Winter Educators, Feb. 22-24, 2019, Austin, Texas. The paper was first sent to JM in 2018 and received a Reject and Resubmit decision. We have thoroughly revised the paper and now have resubmmitted it to JM. In the study, we investigate how suppliers manage customer acquisition and retention simultaneously. Finally, I also explored the idea of conducting exploration and exploitation simultaneously in the context of firms’ outward foreign direct investment. Although the context is different from channel relationship management, the key premise is similar. That is, firms get better off conducting seemingly contradictory activities, which though create tension for firm resources, improve the benefits that each brings to the firm. The research is published in the proceedings of 2018 Academy of International Business (AIB) Annual Conference. An extended version of the paper received a Revise & Resubmit decision from International Business Review in May 2019. We are now working on the revision and aim to resubmit it in August 2019.

15500815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15500815.value: We will continue to develop the research projects resulted from this grant. First, we will finalize the draft of Relationship Ambidexterity and send it to Journal of Marketing in July 2019. Second, upon the notice from JM, we will continue the revision of our paper on Customer Relationship Management at JM if the feedback is positive. If not, we will send it to Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science for review. Finally, we will address reviewers’ comments, revise the paper of Exploratory and Exploitative Foreign Investment, and send it back to International Business Review in August 2019.

15500815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15500815.value: We advance knowledge about how firms engage in activities that seem contradictory in nature. In our supplier relationship management paper, we confirm that firms can be simultaneously committed to an existing exchange partner while seeking alternative exchange partners. They can pursue relationship-strengthening strategy, and at the same time, engage in relationship-diversifying strategy by adjusting its resource allocation to consider, contact, and seek potential suppliers for new business opportunities. An ambidextrous approach combining relationship commitment and diversification will generate greater benefit in an uncertain environment. In our customer relationship management paper, we found firms’ top executives strongly influence firms’ customer orientations. Specifically, executive hubris strengthens firms’ customer acquisition orientation and weakens their customer retention orientation. The hubris effects increase when the market is turbulent and decreases when firms gain experience. Moreover, the joint effect of customer acquisition and retention is beneficial for firms’ long-term development. In our foreign direct investment paper, we found that both exploratory and exploitative investment promote performance and that the positive effect of exploratory investment will last longer than that of exploitative investment. Besides, sequential ambidexterity, that is, the shift between exploratory and exploitative investment, is beneficial for firms’ growth.

15500915.label: Realisation of objectives
15500915.value: The four major objectives of this research have been fully achieved. Through a sample of over 270 manufacturing firms in the U.S. that adopted Business Intelligence (BI) systems from 2005 to 2014, we examine the impact of BI systems on firms’ operational efficiency and firm risks (Objectives 1 & 2). We find that firms improve their operational efficiency and reduce risks in profit returns directly after the adoption of BI systems. We further find that firms with superior employee relationships and higher process institutionalization (i.e., ISO 9000 certified) gain more benefits from the adoption of BI systems. We provide a resource-based view for the competitive advantage derived from the adoption of BI systems, and explore the circumstances under which manufacturers are more likely to obtain benefits from BI adoption (Objectives 3 & 4). Our results show that when a firm adopts a BI system, its operational efficiency is increased and its firm risks are alleviated. Compared with control firms, sample firms obtain significantly higher operational efficiency just after the firms have adopted BI systems and in the year immediately after adoption of BI systems. The median (mean) increase in operational efficiency is 3.2% (3.9%), with nearly 55% of the firms experiencing an improvement in their operational efficiency in the year of BI adoption (i.e., from year t-1 to t). Similarly, the median (mean) of changes in operational efficiency is 2.9% (3.8%), with nearly 54% of the firms experiencing a positive change in operational efficiency in the year after the adoption of BI systems (i.e., from year t to t+1). The median (mean) increase in operational efficiency is 7% (8.4%), with nearly 55% of the firms experiencing an improvement in their operational efficiency from the base year to the year after the adoption of BI systems (i.e., from t-2 to t+1). Similarly, sample firms significantly reduce risks in profit returns in the year of adoption of BI systems and the subsequent year. In the year of BI systems adoption (i.e., from year t-1 to t), the median (mean) abnormal decrease in the firm risks is 0.005 (0.008), with nearly 57% of sample firms experience a reduction in their financial risks. In the year after adoption of BI systems (i.e., from year t to t+1), the median (mean) abnormal decrease in firm risks shrinks to 0.003 (0.004). Nearly 57% of sample firms experience a reduction in their financial risks from the adoption of BI systems. From the base year to the year after the adoption of BI systems (i.e., from t-2 to t+1), the median (mean) abnormal decrease in firm risks is 0.009 (0.011), with nearly 55% of sample firms experience less volatility in profits. Our further analysis suggests that sample firms further enhance operational efficiency and lower firm risks through better stakeholder relationships and higher process institutionalization. The positive impact of BI adoption on risk reduction is stronger among firms with superior stakeholder relationships.This might imply that superior stakeholder relationships help a firm cultivate an open communication environment to acquire more reliable internal and external data, generating more insightful analysis through BI systems. Using ISO 9000 certification as a proxy of process institutionalization, we find that firms adopting BI solutions under an institutionalized process environment leads to stronger improvements in operational efficiency and lowers volatility in profits to a greater extent. Process institutionalization provides a stable work environment with established procedures, streamlining the information collection process and facilitating BI systems assimilation. Superior stakeholder relationships and higher process institutionalization might be helpful to integrating BI systems into business operations, making firms more likely to gain more benefit from BI adoption.

15500915.label: Major findings and research outcome
15500915.value: Although organizations are heavily investing in BI systems and anecdotal evidence suggests that BI systems deliver great values to firms, their actual performance implications need to be examined through rigorous academic research. In this research we explore the business value of BI, and seek to understand the organizational and managerial factors that are critical to the success of BI systems. By selecting control firms through propensity-score matching (PSM) and analyzing the operational efficiency and firm risks of over 270 firms in the U.S. that adopted BI systems from 2005 to 2014, we provide empirical evidence on the potential benefits of BI systems adoption. We further explore the moderating effects of stakeholder relationships and process institutionalization on firms’ adoption of BI systems. Our findings show that BI systems help improve firms’ operational efficiency and mitigate risks simultaneously. In addition, strong stakeholder relationships and high process institutionalization following BI systems adoption can further enhance firms’ operational efficiency and reduce risks. Scholars in OM have long realized the importance of information and knowledge to enhancing organizational routines and capabilities. Yet the effects of BI systems on the risks and returns of firms have not been empirically examined in the literature. In particular, scholars in strategic management traditionally believe that boosting financial returns through any organizational innovations often entails firm risks. There is a tradeoff between firm risks and financial returns. Very little has been known about whether the two outcomes can be improved simultaneously by particular operational initiatives. Our study provides substantial empirical evidence on the positive impact of BI systems on both efficiency improvement and risk reduction of firms.

15500915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15500915.value: Previous research shows that some firms adopt BI systems in a standard way for performance monitoring, while others adopt BI systems in an innovative way for the strategic development. Further research can examine how different attitudes in the BI adoption moderate their benefits to firms. Similarly, we consider operational capability and risks as the two possible outcomes of BI adoption. However, contemporary research in OM also emphasizes on the importance of firm innovativeness additional to profitability and risk control. In addition, this study only considers employee relationships and process institutionalisation as moderating factors. Future studies on the BI adoption could consider other operational contexts such as environmental turbulence and complexity, which might affect the benefits derived from the BI adoption.

15500915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15500915.value: Firms are uncertain about the business value of BI systems. The implementation of BI systems requires large investments in management infrastructure and resources over a few years, and there are many challenges in this process, which have caused more than half of BI projects to fail during the implementation stage. We demonstrate that the benefits of BI systems depend on firms’ social relationships and process formalization, not on the BI systems alone. If firms actively manage their social capital, they could develop strong relationships with their employees and customers for knowledge sharing. Using the timely and reliable data provided by stakeholders might enable firms to obtain more meaningful analysis from BI systems. In addition, if firms effectively adopt the principles and practices of ISO 9000, they might develop a structure with systematic routines to promote information flows, so facilitating BI assimilation throughout their organizations. In the rapid development of “big data” and under knowledge-intensive competition, firms need to consider how the competitive outcomes from the adoption of BI systems can be strengthened and sustained. Our analysis provides evidence on the importance of business analytics in the industry. Firms today need to manage vast amounts of business data available from various internal and external data sources (i.e., big data). They may need to enhance their data management capability by deploying BI systems. Accessing relevant and timely reports for decision-making, firms achieve higher returns with lower risks in operations and supply chain management.

15501415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15501415.value: Of the various economic activities, international tourism is one of the key drivers as well as consequences of globalization. As a result, tourist flows between countries are closely linked. Not only do the economic conditions in a country affect its inbound and outbound tourist flows, they also have spillover effects on tourism demand in the rest of the world. To capture such international linkages of tourist flows, a systematic approach is needed. For instance, to examine the effect of world oil price fluctuations (which affect travel costs) on inbound tourism demand in Hong Kong, a global demand system needs to be developed which includes other key tourist destinations and assesses the effect of oil price changes on all of them simultaneously. Without including Hong Kong and its competing destinations in such a global modeling system, the effect of oil price changes on tourism demand in Hong Kong would be incorrectly estimated, with misleading policy implications. The interactions of tourism demand within a global system can be addressed by an innovative modeling strategy known as the global vector autoregressive (GVAR) model, first developed by Pesaran, Schuermann, and Weiner (2004). This method can model a large vector autoregressive (VAR) system in two stages without estimating a large number of whole-system parameters, hence resolving the over-parameterization issue of the VAR model as suggested by Song and Witt (2003). Song, Cao, Li, and Witt (2013) have made the first attempt to apply the GVAR technique to examine the interrelationships between international tourism demand within a global modeling system of 25 countries, with encouraging results. However, the possibility remains that the GVAR may be over-parameterized if a large number of destination-/origin-related equations and variables are included. One of the natural solutions to this problem is to incorporate Bayesian priors to reduce the number of parameters to be estimated in the GVAR model. To the best of our knowledge, no study has yet attempted to use a Bayesian approach to estimate the GVAR model in either the tourism or the general econometric literature. Therefore, the research proposed here aims to bridge this significant methodological gap by developing a Bayesian GVAR (BGVAR) system for modeling global tourism demand. The BGVAR model is expected to combine the strengths of the GVAR and Bayesian techniques to shrink the number of parameters that require to be estimated in the GVAR system and hence to further improve its efficiency and forecasting accuracy.

15501415.label: Realisation of objectives
15501415.value: All the five objectives are realized, alongside completion of the study. In particular, the study presents the first attempt to examine the interdependencies of tourism demand in multiple destinations based on an advanced and innovative econometric technique: the BGVAR model. Through an empirical case of international tourist flows in nine countries in Southeast Asia (Hong Kong being one of them), this study demonstrates that the BGVAR model is able to capture the inter-linkages between these countries via the impulse response analysis (Objectives 1, 2, and 4). In addition, for the first time the BGVAR model is introduced to the tourism demand forecasting literature. This study presents empirical evidence on the superiority of the BGVAR model in terms of its forecasting accuracy, in comparison to three alternative VAR specifications including the unrestricted VAR, GVAR, and BVAR models, as well as the traditional ARMA model (Objective 3). The findings of the empirical study suggest some important implications on destination management. The proved interdependencies among neighboring countries/ regions require these countries/ regions’ governments and destination management organizations (DMOs) to take account of the external (both global and regional) environment in their own strategic planning and management (Objective 5). Although the study is not necessarily Hong Kong specific, the government of the Hong Kong SAR and NGOs should draw useful policy implications from the study.

15501415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15501415.value: This study presents the first attempt to examine the interdependencies of tourism demand in multiple destinations based on an advanced and innovative econometric technique: the BGVAR model. Through an empirical case of international tourist flows in nine countries in Southeast Asia, this study demonstrates that the BGVAR model is able to capture the inter-linkages between these countries via the impulse response analysis. An external shock to a key economic variable (such as GDP, CPI and the exchange rate) in one destination has spill-over effects on the tourism demand and other variables in some other neighboring countries. In addition, for the first time, the BGVAR model is introduced to the tourism demand forecasting literature. This study presents empirical evidence on the superiority of the BGVAR model in terms of its forecasting accuracy, in comparison to three alternative VAR specifications including the unrestricted VAR, GVAR and BVAR models, as well as the traditional ARMA model. The BGVAR model consistently outperforms its competitors across all forecasting horizons (one- to four-quarter ahead), in all nine countries, based on both sets of forecast error measures. A research paper has been accepted for publication in the Journal of Travel Research, which is a 4 rating journal on the ABS Journal List. Assaf, A., G. Li, H. Song, & E. C. Tsionas (2018). Modeling and Forecasting Regional Tourism Demand Using the Bayesian GVAR Model. Journal of Travel Research. (doi: 10.1177/0047287518759226)

15501415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15501415.value: Given the superior properties of the BGVAR model and empirical evidence of its applicability in tourism studies, further applications of this method are highly recommended. For example, future research may consider a truly global tourism system and investigate the interdependencies of tourist flows on a global scale. In addition, after the UK’s European Union membership referendum, the British pound has fallen significantly. To quantify this effect on tourism demand not only in the UK but also in other European countries and the rest of the world, the BGVAR model can be an effective tool for analysis.

15501415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15501415.value: The research models and forecasts the interactions between countries using Bayesian GVAR approach. Findings of the empirical study suggest the following. Firstly, the interdependencies among neighboring countries require these countries’ governments to take the external (both global and regional) environment into account in their own strategic planning and management. A regional perspective of destination management is necessary. Secondly, given the evidence of different types of response and different degrees of vulnerability that a country is exposed to an external shock provided by impulse response analysis, each destination should identify what type of shocks from which countries they are most vulnerable to, and shock-specific and country-specific contingency plans should be developed. A more general implication is that, an effective risk and crisis management strategy of a tourist destination needs to combine general principles with specific procedures and approaches relevant to particular types and sources of the risk. Thirdly, a systematic approach to tourism demand forecasting is more accurate and useful to support strategic planning. Given the interdependencies among destinations, forecasting of future tourism trends in a destination without accounting for geographical spill-over effects may lead to biased results and further mislead the strategic decision making.

15501515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15501515.value: 學術界對不同會計收益的質素持有相反的觀點。一方面，有些人認為在權責發生制下的收入將不會完全兌現成未來現金流。另一方面，其他人認為會計師應用權責發生制時會令收入和開支有更準確的匹配, 以更好地反映公司的業績。此外，按照標準會計做法, 權責發生制是傾向保守的: 在權責發生制下一元的收入應該預測超過一元的未來現金流。 因此, 投資者也可能對不同會計收益的質素持有不同的觀點。如果投資者認為在權責發生制下的收入化成未來現金流的可能性很低，他們便會不在乎系統性的權責發生制風險。以往的研究並沒有區分這兩種會計收益所可能存在的風險價格差異。 本研究項目的結果可以揭示投資者對不同會計收益的看法。同時，如果在權責發生制下的收入和現金流確實有不同的風險價格，這靈活性便能讓資產可以更準確地定價。

15501515.label: Realisation of objectives
15501515.value: We show that aggregate cash-based operating profitability (as measured by Ball, Gerakos, Linnainmaa, and Nikolaev 2016), but not accruals, displays strong positive predictive power for aggregate stock returns. The predictive power of standalone aggregate profitability for stock returns is weak, and this weakness is due to an omitted variable bias. To extract the predictive content of aggregate cash profits for aggregate stock returns, the omitted variables—the book-to-market ratio and investment—need to be controlled for. We also show that, in the cross section, a portfolio's loading on aggregate cash profits (but not aggregate accruals) helps explain the portfolio's expected returns.

15501515.label: Major findings and research outcome
15501515.value: Key findings of this project have been reported in the paper, "Do Aggregate Profits Forecast Aggregate Stock Returns?", as displayed in Part C below. The paper makes two empirical contributions. The first contribution is related to the finding of Hirshleifer, Hou, and Teoh (2009)—that aggregate cash earnings (accruals) forecast aggregate stock returns negatively (positively)—in sharp contrast to the firm-level evidence of Sloan (1996). By following Ball, Gerakos, Linnainmaa, and Nikolaev (2015), who suggest using consistent deflators (i.e. market equity) on both sides of the predictive regression, we show that Hirshleifer, Hou, and Teoh’s results are driven by the deflators they use—rather than the earnings components per se. Motivated by Fama and French (2006, 2015, 2016), who emphasize the need of jointly using the book-to-market ratio (B/M), profitability, and investment to predict stock returns, our second contribution is to show that omitting B/M and investment from a predictive regression biases the profitability coefficient estimate downwards. Although the predictive power of standalone profitability for aggregate stock returns is weak—consistent with the conclusion of Bali, Demirtas, and Tehranian (2008)—this weakness is due to an omitted variable bias. After controlling for the omitted variables—B/M and investment—aggregate cash-based operating profitability (Ball, Gerakos, Linnainmaa, and Nikolaev 2016), but not accruals, displays strong positive predictive power for aggregate stock returns that are both statistically and economically significant. In sum, the predictive power of the cash and accrual components of profitability at the aggregate level is largely in line with their firm-level counterparts—in contrast to the conclusion of Hirshleifer, Hou, and Teoh (2009).

15501515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15501515.value: The aggregate level findings here can be further linked to the cross-sectional findings of Ball, Gerakos, Linnainmaa, and Nikolaev (2016). These authors show that a long-short cash profit factor (CashRMW) can help explain cross-sectional variations in stock returns. Since we show that aggregate cash profits can forecast aggregate stock returns and can capture aggregate risk premium, it is conceivable that the cross-sectional explanatory power of CashRMW is related to its exposure to aggregate cash profits risks. Thererfore, we propose to further investigate the extent to which the explanatory power of a stock's CashRMW beta can be subsumed by its aggregate cash profits beta. This exercise can potentially provide a fundamentals-based foundation for the explanatory power of the CashRMW factor.

15501515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15501515.value: Previous studies show that aggregate cash earnings (accruals) forecast aggregate stock returns negatively (positively)—in sharp contrast to firm-level results. We find that this apparent inconsistency between the aggregate and firm-level predictive power of cash earnings and accruals can be reconciled in two steps. First, it is important to use consistent deflators (i.e. market equity) on both sides of the predictive regression. Second, although the predictive power of standalone profitability for aggregate stock returns is weak, this weakness is due to an omitted variable bias. After controlling for the omitted variables—B/M and investment—aggregate cash profits, but not accruals, display strong positive predictive power for aggregate stock returns. Having taken these two steps, we find that the predictive power of the cash and accrual components of profitability at the aggregate level is largely in line with their firm-level counterparts.

15501815.value: 國際財務報告準則的強制實施對企業財務決策的影響：動態分析
