15507015.label: Realisation of objectives
15507015.value: All the three objectives have been achieved, as explained below: For Objective (1), i.e., “based on a motivating model with regret preference, construct a regret proxy utilizing a RER measure, and empirically examine the relation between RER and expected stock returns,” we fulfill the task in three steps. First, built on the rationale that it is painful for an investor to observe that an individual stock that she picks performs substantially worse than the market index which represents the overall performance level of all investors, we develop a simple model to highlight this unique perspective of “relative” performance and derive its implications in asset pricing. To emphasize the role of the market index as the benchmark, we develop the theory around the market context of an individual stock’s downside prospect, especially the extreme downside states. For this reason, we change the term “relative extreme risk” (RER) in to “market context” (MKTCON). Also, we base our model on the salience theory of Bordalo, Gennaioli, and Shleifer (2012, 2013) (Bordalo, P., N. Gennaioli, and A. Shleifer. 2012. Salience theory of choice under risk. Quarterly Journal of Economics 127, 1243-1285; Bordalo, P., N. Gennaioli, and A. Shleifer. 2013. Salience and asset prices. American Economic Review: Papers & Proceedings 103, 623-628). The salience effect comes from the comparison of an asset’s payoff in a certain state with the average payoff delivered by all available assets (i.e., market performance) in the same state. Therefore, it shares the same spirit with the regret argument that we originally proposed, but is more general. Specifically, the salience-based model suggests that, holding constant the prospects of an asset’s crash, improvements in market conditions make the crash more salient, rendering the asset more underpriced relative to other assets in the market, and inducing a lower price level and a higher expected return in the cross-section. The model thus generates direct cross-sectional asset pricing implications that can be empirically tested. Moreover, the salience effect is especially strong in a low-probability crash state, in which the asset’s payoff is disastrous and its salience increases the pain. We also discuss in detail the connections between salience theory-based asset pricing and the pricing of alternative context- or reference-dependent preferences, including the regret and “keeping up with the Joneses” (KUJ) models, and highlight the distinctive function of salience theory in differentiating crash states from non-crash states. We believe, and have proved that, the revised theoretical framework fits our study better. The bottom line is that our theoretical argument has always been consistent and never deviates from our original idea of examining the relative benchmark performance against a particular asset’s payoff. Second, we adopt a novel multivariate extreme value approach of Heffernan and Tawn (2004) (Heffernan, J., and J. Tawn. 2004. A Conditional Approach for Multivariate Extreme Values. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B 66: 479-546) to construct the MKTCON measure. Specifically, we estimate the magnitude of the crash loss for an individual stock, as well as the associated market return in the crash states of the stock. The particular extreme value theory model we adopt is able to describe the behavior of one random variable (market return) given that another random variable (stock return) is in its extreme region (lower tail states), and ensures that the estimates are robust to the parent distributions of the stock and market returns. This attribute makes the parametric extreme value approach suitable for our study, which allows us to predict a stock crash level and its associated expected market context in an easy and technically rigorous way. We further show the robustness of our findings, and supplement the extreme value theory-based MKTCON measurement by a nonparametric method in which we select the lowest return data for each stock within a bottom small-probability quantile of its empirical return distribution and use their average to measure the stock’s crash payoff. We use the average of the market returns that are associated with the lowest stock returns to measure MKTCON. We find that these two methods generate remarkably consistent findings with regard to the asset pricing effect of the market context. Third, we find strong and robust evidence that MKTCON is associated with expected stock returns in the cross section. Specifically, we find that a stock crash expected to occur in a better-performing market commands a premium relative to a crash occurring in a worse-performing market, even though both crashes are of the same probability and magnitude. This market context effect is more evident when the potential stock crash is more severe; it becomes weaker as the magnitude of the stock’s expected tail loss declines or as the crash becomes less rare. These findings support the asset pricing implication of the salience-based theory, as well as its prediction that rarer, more severe crashes lead to more overweighting of crash-state payoffs and underpricing of an asset. For Objective (2), i.e., “examine the impact of institutional holdings on the documented RER effect,” we find that the market context effect in the main test is greater for stocks that have fewer institutional holders. This evidence is consistent with the premise that, according to the salience theory, salience arises from narrow framing such that it is shaped by the payoffs of individual assets, and the salience effect comes from people’s limited cognitive resources such that they focus only on sensory/salient prospects. Because institutional investors are less subject to narrow framing and salience distortion, we document that greater institutional investor participation mitigates the asset pricing effects of MKTCON. We further expand this line of inquiry by showing that the market context effect has become stronger in recent decades, suggesting that investors’ cognitive abilities to make investment decisions have declined as the increasing asset population of the market forces investors to concentrate on the salient portions of opportunity sets. For Objective (3), i.e., “check the mutual influences between RER and existing risk measures,” we conduct detailed analysis with this regard. We first show that some commonly used existing risk measures such as beta, size, book-to-market ratio, momentum, liquidity, investment growth, and profitability cannot explain the asset pricing effect of MKTCON. We further find that among stocks with higher risks of crash, an improved market context (i.e., a higher market context return) is associated with smaller beta, larger idiosyncratic volatility (IV), and higher idiosyncratic tail risk. Therefore, the market environment for substantial price drops may thus constitute a significant part of individual stock risk, including systematic and idiosyncratic risks. Consistent with this conjecture, we find that the premium to beta (which is negative, in line with the beta anomaly) and idiosyncratic tail risk can be explained largely by the market context effect, but not vice versa. We document a similar but weaker result for the mutual influences between the effects of market context and the non-extreme IV measure. These findings shed new light on the sources of the beta anomaly and equity premium to idiosyncratic risk, especially when stocks are exposed to crash risks. In sum, we have successfully achieved all the three objectives with strong and clear evidence.

15507015.label: Major findings and research outcome
15507015.value: We first develop a theoretical asset pricing model based on the salience theory of Bordalo, Gennaioli, and Shleifer (2012, 2013). In the model, we derive clear testable prediction that market context matters for expected stock returns. We also discuss the connections of our model with existing salience arguments and models based on context- or reference-dependent preferences. Second, we construct a market context measure for individual stock crash, which utilizes both a nonparametric method and a parametric multivariate extreme value approach. The parametric method is especially novel and has a great potential to be applied to other scenarios. In this sense, our project also has methodological contributions. Third, we document robust evidence that market context of stock crash is priced in the equity market, sending support to investors’ concern of relative performance and motive to avoid underperforming the market (and other investors on average). This is a new aspect to examining asset pricing in the cross section of stock returns and has not been explored in previous studies. Fourth, we find that the market context effect can explain a significant part of the expected returns associated with beta and idiosyncratic extreme risk, which helps solve the longstanding puzzles of beta anomaly and idiosyncratic risk pricing. Fifth, we reveal evidence consistent with behavioral finance premises of narrow framing and limited attention, and incorporate them into a general equilibrium model of market context pricing. Our findings, from the market context perspective, deliver practical suggestions in equity market development and raise serious concerns on the increasing severity of behavioral biases in recent years. Finally, our research supplements studies of the impact of crashes on stock prices, an issue that captures significant attention from practitioners, academicians, and regulators, especially after the recent global financial crisis of 2007-2009. Our novel aspect of examining crash risk speaks to a neglected, but important, consideration in that stock crashes exaggerate investors’ salience concerns which may substantially alter their investment choices. The paper supported by this GRF fund, titled “A Tail of Two Worlds: Stock Crashes, Market Contexts, and Expected Returns,” is currently under review at Review of Finance, which is an A* journal in my institution, sharing the same rank as JF, JFE, RFS, and JFQA. The paper was also presented at the 2018 FMA annual meeting, FMA Asia Pacific conference, FMA European conference, and the 2017 China Finance Annual Meeting (CFAM).

15507015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15507015.value: One potential direction of future development is to further elaborate the market context aspect in asset pricing, which is one of the most important features of our study, both theoretically and empirically. Another way to expand the research is to further differentiate the market context concept from existing systematic measures that also consider risk from the connection between individual stock returns and market returns. We may need to better emphasize the novel feature of considering market context conditioning on the crash prospect of an individual stock, which provides a clear contribution to the asset pricing literature. The third potential development is to highlight the nice asymptotic property of the extreme value method that we adopt in this project. This method is able to assesses inter-variable relations in a two-dimensional setting where only one of the random variables is extreme, providing a suitable statistical framework to estimate a stock crash’s market context.

15507015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15507015.value: Investors often hold equity portfolios different from market index. A particular concern is that stocks selected may perform substantially worse than the market, rendering a painful experience. Such “pain” is especially acute when extreme losses of these stocks are realized. A severe price plunge of an individual stock would be more painful if the market index as a benchmark performs better and less painful if this index also crashes. As a result, the collapses of individual stocks with exactly the same magnitude may give investors varying degrees of pain depending on what happens to the entire market. Not all tails (i.e., large losses) are created equal! We explain the above intuition theoretically in a model, and empirically find that stocks with the potential for crashes in better market conditions are compensated by higher expected returns than stocks with the potential for equally severe crashes in worse market contexts. The impact of market context on returns is more pronounced among stocks with less institutional holdings and when the potential crash is rarer and bigger. The effect also becomes stronger in recent decades. This effect is driven by the market context concern rather than other existing determinants of expected returns.

15600315.label: Project Objectives
15600315.value: Describe, map, and analyze cue-responding behaviors in nurse-patient communication during routine care in oncological settings. Explore the effect of cue-responding behavior of the oncology nurses on patients' informational and emotional needs and satisfaction. Identify any ineffective cue-responding behaviors that may affect the quality of routine care, and/or could post potential risks to the health and safety of cancer patients. Identify and examine the influence of nurses, patients, culture, and the environment on nurse-patient communication. Explore with nurses ways of adjusting their practice through reflective discussion on their cue-responding behaviors and patient experiences of the communication process. Develop guidelines on communication with nurses so that they can integrate their learning into practice.

15600315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15600315.value: For patient-centeredness, the skilled and sensitive use of communication with patients is essential to the practice of nurses and is known to be the core aspect of caring. Patients living with cancer often experience anxiety and depression1. Nurses have the best opportunity to acknowledge and attend to the information and emotional needs of these patients. However, communication with cancer patient is often not ideal. At best, nurses tend not to respond to and/or miss the information and emotional needs of these patients expressed as cues and concerns. At worst, mounting evidence of ineffective communication at all levels of the healthcare system has shown poor patient outcomes, including significant physical and psychological harm2, and patient and clinician dissatisfaction. While time is usually cited as a barrier to nurses communicating with patients, recent findings challenge this belief. This raises the possibility that it is the quality of the nurses’ cue responses to patients’ needs and concerns, rather than the quantity of time spent in communicating, that is important. Related questions that consider patients’ satisfaction with nurses’ cue-responding behaviors also merit attention as an understudied area in communication research. There is a paucity of research on the process of communication, as cue-responding, between nurses and cancer patients within their routine care and the corresponding patient satisfaction and insufficient care/care problem that may have resulted from the under-recognized cues and concerns of patients. The aim of this study is to address this critical gap, thereby giving nurses some guidance in reexamining their nurse-patient communication through cue-responding behaviors, and to explore with them ways of adjusting their practice. It is hoped that the result will be able to improve oncology nurses’ receptivity to patient cues and concerns during brief encounters3 in routine care. A focused ethnographic approach and conversational analysis will be adopted in this study, using observations, a patient’s concern checklist with semi-structured interviews, audio-recordings of nurse-patient interactions, nonverbal observations, nurses’ reflective focus groups, and document reviews. We will analyze, describe the actual conversations, and identify the context (oncology ward environment and the particular situation/encounters) and ways in which communicative practices can be enhanced between nurses and cancer patients within the Chinese culture. Culture is known to have an influence on effective communication in healthcare, and this study is the first of its kind in Hong Kong.

15600315.label: Realisation of objectives
15600315.value: All the objectives have been met. 1. The Medical Interview Aural Rating scale (Heaven & Green 2001) was used to calculate the cue-responding behaviours of nurses during routine care, while the patients’ speech was studied for the expression of cues. Among the 184 cue-responding behaviours exhibited by the patients in 63 conversations, the most common emotional cue was a level 2 cue that was an explicit expression of worry or concern. The nurses responded to more than half of the cues with acknowledgement and exploration (55.98%), followed by adequate acknowledgement but no exploration (23.37%). The presence of positive/negative behaviours manifested by the non-verbal cues during nurse-patient interactions and the determinants affecting the patients’ satisfaction with nurse-patient communication were examined. Among the 110 items of routine care, the two most common positive nonverbal cues that nurses used were visual contact (80.2%) and proximity (75.2%), while for patients the corresponding cues were visual contact (82.2%) and maintaining attention (63.4%). Variables such as nurses’ education level (e.g., having a certificate in palliative/oncology nursing care), nurse’s claim to have a religion, the gender of the patient and the nurse, along with the nurses’ age, influenced the patients’ expression of cues and the nurses’ responses. 2. The nurses’ cue-responding behaviours clearly had positive and negative effects. Interviews with nurses and patients revealed that relationships could be established through the involvement and participation of the patients during the routine transfer of biomedical information. However, relationship building could be hindered by negative experiences arising from inadequate cue-responding behaviours, e.g., through a failure to explore the patient’s cues/concerns, leading to misunderstandings, which shaped the subsequent relationship. Nonetheless, overall, it was revealed that the nurses responded with positive cue-responding behaviours to the concerns raised by the patients. Some patient's perceptions of a negative attitude of the nurses may be attributable to inadequate communication skills and a lack of mindfulness on the part of the nurses, who are compelled to work quickly and efficiently in a busy environment. The results of this study support the view that nurse-patient communication has an impact on the patients’ level of satisfaction of nursing care. Three potential factors were identified affecting the level of satisfaction of cancer patients with nurse-patient communication. They are: having stage 3 cancer, nursing admission procedures, and psychological concern over the impact of the disease on one’s self-care. 3. With staff shortages, colleagues occasionally helped each other to administer medications. Nurses who did not look after the patients but helped with the routine of administering medications did not always attend to patients’ cues and their reasons relating to their refusal to take the medications. They also might not be able to relay to the primary nurses for their follow-up on patients' reasons of refusal. While such occasions seemed to be few, there is the potential for missing information. On the other hand, with an understanding of how busy nurses are with their work, patients prioritized their needs and did not report needs that they perceived to be less urgent. This, however, could pose safety issues. Adequate cue-responding behaviour and building relationships with patients by trying to understand them may help to mitigate any untoward consequences. 4. Patients’ patterns of communication with the nurses seem to be shaped by their understanding of how busy the nurses were and the pattern of their routines. Whether or not they decided to initiate communication depended on whether they thought that their problem should be promptly solved or could be further delayed until nurses came for procedural care. Through their own initial screening and assessment, patients knew when and in what situations they should inform the nurses. In turn, the nurses also provided them with information. Patient empowerment was therefore found to be a feasible way to promote physical self-care through a nurse-patient partnership in a time-constrained oncology setting. For the culture of nursing, there is the need to re-examine the interrelationship between psychosocial care and the physical needs of patients. While physical and psychosocial care could be considered separate entities for cancer patients, the provision of good physical care through effective communication is essential to promoting the psychosocial well-being of patients. Discussions about the case of the nurse’s misunderstanding of the patients’ behaviours revealed that some nurses would choose to apologize and explained their behaviour to the patient, while others would choose to avoid the issue. Yet others justified the responses of the nurse by pointing to the patients’ characteristics. The latter two responses would inadvertently lead to negative feelings that might subsequently affect the patient’s motivation to voice her needs and create potential problems with nurse-patient communication and relationship building. The environment refers not only to situations that evoke emotions in nurses when dealing with the physical and psychosocial issues and concerns of cancer patients, but also to the busy work environment, over which the nurses felt that they sometimes lacked control. 5 &6 The last phase of the study was to explore with the nurses their practice of nurse-patient communication and to share the patients’ experiences through reflective discussions, as well as to develop guidelines on communication based on their views and the findings. A key finding that is particularly important for senior nurses is the need to remind them to appreciate the psychological aspects embedded in providing good physical care to patients. Both nurses and patients focused on physical care as the priority, and both agreed that nurses have no time to offer psychosocial care. From the findings, communication with patients could focus on patient's physical needs for their psychosocial care as well. Since many of the patients were re-admitted, they knew each other. Both the patients and nurses reported that their familiarity with each other allowed them to work in partnership and nurses could communicate with patients through building on their understanding of the patients’ current conditions from their previous admittances. In their responses to the transcripts of patients’ comments and the authentic scenarios that were shared with nurses, it was noted that nurses expressed different beliefs and values arising from their experiences of communicating with patients and their families. Some emphasized the importance of tone and choice of words to express empathy. Others would base their understanding of the situation on the characteristics of the patients and the context, and make the corresponding decision on what tone to use and what to say. Some senior nurses learnt to be more proactive from working with emotionally charged situations. They would spend time providing patients with information, as they anticipated that the patients’ need for information is often at the root of their fear of the unknown, their frustration and, ultimately, their anger about the care that they are receiving. Junior nurses not only need to work with the emotions of the patients and perhaps their families, but also need to have some knowledge of the complexity of the patients’ treatment and cancer conditions. They also need to work with busy doctors, who may not respond to their call to address a patient’s needs in a timely fashion. This, in turn, can lead to misunderstandings and conflicts with patients. Hence, mentoring and reflective practice are key areas that emerged from the discussions and are the foundation for guiding both junior and senior nurses' communication with patients.

15600315.label: Major findings and research outcome
15600315.value: Two main themes identified from patients’ perceptions of their nurse-patient communication. They are 1: Patients' perceptions of the busyness of nurses in relation to communication. 2: Patients’ possible involvement in their own care through their relationship with nurses and their expectations of nurses in meeting their physical and psychosocial needs. While physical and psychosocial care could be considered separate entities for cancer patients, the provision of good physical care through effective communication is the key to promoting the psychosocial well-being of patients. This may be the optimal way to realize the goal of providing holistic care to cancer patients within Hong Kong’s understaffed oncology settings. The results of the potential factors that influence patients’ satisfaction with nurse patient communications are patients, who are at stage 3 cancer, patients receiving admission procedures were significantly more satisfied with their communication with nurses. Those who were more concerned about the impact of the disease on self-care were less satisfied with their communication with nurses. For the cue-responding behaviors of the nurse-patient communication patterns, the oncology nurses used positive or good cue responding behaviors more often than negative or bad responding behaviors. For non-verbal cues, no significant relationship between the number of positive nonverbal cues that nurses and patients used and their satisfaction with communication. The gender of the nurse and the patient along with nurses’ with degree preparation and the certificate training in palliative or oncology nurses demonstrated more positive cue-responding behaviors than the others. Findings from the reflective discussions with nurses have translated into a reminder of them about holistic care and their language involved in addressing the physical and psychosocial aspects within the context of bio-medical dominance and time constraints. This in turn also revealed a pattern of care in nurses’ practice of planned vs ad hoc psychosocial care; pro-active information giving to patients based on experience vs missing patient cues for individual needs; mentoring and coaching needs of nurses for the emotionally charged environment; and for nurses to integrate their learning from the training workshops into their continuous ward practice. It is also clear that nurses' training in communication with patients require post-training supervision and support. Nurses' refinement of practice would be based on their contextual understanding and the various patients' needs. There could also be regular opportunities for nurses to share with each other and with the juniors their reflective experiences on successful and the more challenging communication encounters with patients.

15600315.value: Identify mindfulness communication training workshops for nurses, who work within a busy and emotionally charged environment as part of their professional development. Examine the use of authentic case situations for nurse-patient communication at the regular reflective session as part of mentoring programme for new graduates. Explore nurses’ reflective learning for practice in an emotionally-charged environment for self and professional growth.

15600315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15600315.value: The nature of this study involves an understanding of the ways nurses communicate and work with cancer patients in the busy and emotionally demanding wards. Through working with patients' experiences of their communication with nurses and their perceived busyness of the nurses, a renewed understanding for nurses is to attend to patients' psychosocial needs through physical care, which is significant in a busy environment whereby emotional counselling as psychosocial care is not being expected by the patients and is equally difficult for nurses given the time constraint. Effective nurse-patient communication is based on their building of relationships, nurses' reflective practice and communication training along with patient's trust and the empowerment of patients for quality care. The value of this research is also about its translational in nature that nurses learnt first hand of the patients' perceptions and how best to learn through their continuous reflections, mentorship and training.

15600815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15600815.value: Power relations are inherent in the interaction between experts, referred to here as teachers, and non-experts, referred to as students. In nursing education the teacher-student relationship is still an under-explored area of power dynamics. In this study, nursing students’ perspectives on the power dynamics between themselves and their teachers will be explored, as well as their understanding of the context of the power relations within the campus and in clinical settings. A descriptive qualitative study will be conducted over a period of 18 months using two methods of collecting data (focus group interviews and personal essays). Through convenience sampling, a total of 90 nursing students from one university, with 30 each from Years 1, 3, and 5, will be invited to participate in the study. They will first be asked to write a personal essay using a metaphor of their subjective experience of the teacher-student relationship in the realm of power dynamics. They will then participate in a focus group interview in groups of 6-8. Two semi-structured interview guides exploring the power dynamics within the teacher-student relationship have been designed. Each guide will have a central theme based on the students’ exposure and the relevance of their learning experiences. Year 1 students and final year (Year 5) students will be asked questions about power dynamics in the teacher-student relationship in a campus learning context, while the questions put to Year 3 students and final year students will focus on a clinical learning context. The data will be analysed using a content analysis approach. The PI and RA will separately conduct an initial analysis. A comparison of their findings will then be made. A final thematic analysis will constitute the core themes, which will be authenticated by the nursing students. It is hoped that a power model for teacher-student relationships that is specific to the discipline of nursing can be developed. In addition to publishing the research results, to strengthen the impact of this study, training workshops and seminars for nursing educators will be held to disseminate the meanings of power locally and in Australia, the 2nd Co-I’s home country. A short-term goal is to increase awareness of embedded power relations within teacher-student relationships that will lead to the promotion of active learning and student-centred teaching. A long-term goal is to make students aware of power issues in the nurse-patient relationship after they have graduated and become registered nurses. NA

15600815.label: Major findings and research outcome
15600815.value: The significance of this study was that it showed that the power dynamics varied with an educator's personality, communication skills, ability to effectively monitor large classes, and teaching style. When educators foster a good relationship with their students, their students become motivated and engaged in the learning process. They then become more willing to talk to their educators, and mutual communication results. Originality is seen in the research themes, which have received little attention in the literature, namely: (1) the meanings of power – avoiding doing harm to patients; (2) the desired power dynamics – master vs apprentice; and (3) enhancing the clinical learning experience. The significance of this study was that it debunks the notion that students prefer a teacher-student relationship that resembles a friendship; instead students considered it necessary to patient safety for teachers to have the power to supervise their clinical practice. The most interesting finding was that metaphorical interpretations of the educator-student relationship reveals many faces and possibilities of presentations of analysis of such relationship. Additionally, novel data collection method in the form of a personal essay provides an instructive way of gathering views from students. The second interesting finding was that the campus learning context varied with an educator's personality, communication skills, ability to effectively monitor large classes, and teaching style. When educators foster a good relationship with their students, their students become motivated and engaged in the learning process. They then become more willing to talk to their educators, and mutual communication results. The third interesting finding about the clinical learning context was that it debunks the notion that students prefer a teacher-student relationship that resembles a friendship; instead students considered it necessary to patient safety for teachers to have the power to supervise their clinical practice.

15600815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15600815.value: This research innovation can potentially be employed in the following ways: a) to reveal how the relationship is perceived as metaphors by undergraduate and postgraduate students within nursing and non-nursing disciplines; b) to study students in various stages of development, such as children, adolescents, adults, and the elderly, and to explore any features of age-based metaphors that might affect their perception of power in the educator-student relationship. The present findings about metaphors will enable educators/researchers to learn more about the educator-student relationship from a new angle. The results of this study will have various applications: 1) This study will provide nursing students with a chance to reflect on the relationship between educators and themselves. It is important to let our students voice their views, because they are involved first-hand in the education process and will have experienced relationships that affect their learning outcomes. 2) The results of this study will help nursing educators to understand student perspectives on the relationship. 3) Educators in other healthcare and even non-healthcare disciplines may also refer to metaphorical interpretations of the student experience in various potential research topics.

15600815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15600815.value: Campus and clinical learning are equally important in nurse education. The educator-student relationship is one of the most influential factors in students' learning experiences and outcomes. Many studies have investigated this issue in both campus and clinical settings. However, few have explored students' perceptions of their learning in these two settings from their perspectives. To fill this gap in the knowledge, the research team conducted this research project. An understanding of campus and clinical settings as two contexts for learning can help educators to devise teaching and learning activities that can be delivered in a targeted and effective way, thereby improving the learning environment for students. Some tips for improving the teacher-student relationship have emerged. (1) Nurse educators are encouraged to take the first step by approaching and interacting with students; (2) Nurse educators are encouraged to remember students' names in order to build rapport and reduce distance; and (3) Establishing appropriate relationships with students is critical in order to avoid misunderstanding and conflict. In brief, educators will gain a better understanding of how the power dynamics within the teacher-student relationship affect student learning.

15603715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15603715.value: Child abuse is closely tied up with competence and styles in parenting. It happens when parents knowingly or unknowingly cause harm or potential harm in the course of bringing up their children. Often, parents cause harm to their children when they neglect the developmental needs of their children by being parent-centred, over-demanding, dominating, and harshly disciplinary. In her book Battle Hymn of the Tiger Mother, Amy Chua (2011) suggested, if not glorified that the Chinese way of being strict, demanding, controlling, and punitive in parenting is better than the western permissive way of bringing up for children. She used her daughters as an example and claimed that her way of demanding and disciplinary way of parenting had helped her daughters to be successful academically. She ridiculed herself being a ‘tiger mom’. Since then, the term 'tiger parenting' receives a lot of attention from mass media, parents and social workers as well as academics. As academic achievement is highly emphasized in Hong Kong, some parents also believe that “tiger parenting” is good for their children and endorsed such parenting behaviors. Despite the increasing popularity of tiger parenting among the public, academic attention has hitherto focused more on its relationship with child outcomes, more specifically with academic achievements. There are still many unanswered questions about ‘tiger parenting’, like 'what is its nature?', 'how do Chinese parents view it?', 'what is its relationship with child abuse, and its implications on child protection?'. Not only Hong Kong parents themselves, but also parent education needs to be informed with research evidence on the topic which is so far a virgin land in local research. For these reasons, this proposed study aims to identify the core features of ‘tiger parenting’, to examine the public attitudes towards ‘tiger parenting’ and to identify the relationship between ‘tiger parenting’ and child abuse among Hong Kong parents, and to explore the implications of ‘tiger parenting’ on child protection in Hong Kong. The PI of the research team has been doing research on violence and child protection in Hong Kong for more than two decades, and one of the Co-PI is an international expert in parenting research. With this background, we hope to open a new agenda in parenting research and to generate research findings to better inform Hong Kong and Chinese parents in parenting, and contribute to evidence-based practice in parenting education locally. 虐待兒童與父母的親職方式和能力有著很緊密的關繫。虐兒行為多是發生在親職過程中父母對子女有意或無意的傷害。如果父母過分以自我中心、忽視孩子的成長需要、對他們過分苛求、支配、和懲戒，最終會對孩子造成傷害。Amy Chua（2011）在她的“虎媽的戰歌”一書中，似乎在歌頌中國式的親職，並認為中國父母對子女的嚴格要求和管控、以至帶著懲罰式的育兒方式比西方父母寬容的親職實踐方式更好。她以自己的女兒為例，聲稱她的嚴厲以至帶著懲罰的親職方法幫助了她的女兒在學業上取得成功，並嘲笑自己是一名“虎媽”。此後，“虎式養育”受到了媒體、家長、社會工作者和學者的廣泛關注。由於子女的學業成績受到香港父母的高度重視， 一些家長也認為“虎式養育”有利於自己的孩子，並贊同這樣的養育行為。 儘管“虎式養育”社會上受著一定程度認同，學術界對著課題的關注至今多聚焦在這種養育方式對子女的帶來的成長效果，而且多是與子女學業成績的關係。就目前的研究看來，還有很多有待解答關於“虎式養育”懸而未決的問題：像“虎式養育”的性質是什麼、中國家長怎麼看待“虎式養育”、“虎式養育”與虐待兒童的關係、及其對兒童保護的意義等等。無疑，這都有助香港父母以至香港的親職教育工作者進行循證為本的育兒和親職教育工作，不過有關知識都是目前這個研究課題的處女地。 基於這些原因，本次研究的目的在於確定“虎式養育”的基本特徵、公眾對“虎式養育”的態度、並嘗試探討確定“虎式養育”和虐待兒童之間的關係、和“虎式養育”在保護兒童的含義。研究小組的首席研究員一直至力於香港家庭暴力和兒童保護的研究凡二十年， 而參與的研究員更是親職方式和實踐研究的國際專家。以這個研究組合，我們希望打開香港親職研究的一個新的議程，並將研究成果向香港以至華人的父母和親職教育工作者分享，提升他們的親職實踐以至家長教育工作的能量。

15603815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15603815.value: Many people with recent-onset (≦6 months) psychosis often experience disruptive residual symptoms, impaired psychosocial functioning and high illness relapse rate. A few psychoeducatonal and motivational illness management programs in the U.S. and Europe for early-stage psychosis have reported significant improvements on patients' functioning and relapse. Yet few intervention studies have focused on patients’ mindfulness, changing their negative thoughts towards their symptoms and related suffering, which has been shown to empower patients' self-management of their illness and functioning and distressing thoughts and perception. This proposed research is designed to test the effects of a Mindfulness-Based Psycho-education program (MBPP) for Chinese patients with schizophrenia on their mental state, psychosocial functioning and insight into illness/treatment. A randomized controlled trial will be conducted with 144 Chinese patients diagnosed with psychotic disorders (within the past six months) at two psychiatric outpatient clinics using repeated-measures, three-arm design. They will be randomly selected from the patient lists and after baseline measurement, randomly assigned to either the MBPP, a psycho-education group or usual psychiatric care (n=48 in each group). The MBPP consists of 12 bi-weekly, 2-hour group sessions and is designed to teach patients about illness management skills and help them attain more awareness of, relating differently to and accepting and/or managing their thoughts and perceptions towards their symptoms and make positive changes to their thoughts and behaviors concerning the illness and its symptoms. The psycho-education program also consists of twelve 2-hour group sessions (every two or three weeks) based on the research team’s psycho-education programs for psychosis care in 2008-2010. Patients' symptom severity and re-hospitalization rates (primary outcomes), and their functioning, social support and insight into illness/treatment, will be measured at recruitment and at one week and six and 12 months after the interventions. Based on an intention-to-treat principle, multivariate analyses of variance(or covariance) followed by Helmert contrasts test on individual post-tests will be performed to compare changes in all patient outcomes within-group and between-groups over the 12-month follow-up. Semi-structured interviews will be conducted with 10 MBPP and 10 psycho-education group participants after the first post-test and their contents analyzed to identify their perceived benefits and weaknesses, therapeutic components of the interventions, and major difficulties in their participation. If any significant positive patient outcomes found, this innovative MBPP can be adopted by community mental health teams in Hong Kong and/or Chinese populations to improve early-stage psychosis sufferers’ mental state and functioning and thus their illness relapses. 大多數思覺失調(或精神分裂症)患者在初期(≦6個月)都會出現危害性的後遺病徵、心理社會功能障礙、以及較高的復發率。在歐、美國家一些針對精神分裂症初期患者的綜合性護理研究結果顯示，綜合性護理對心理社會的功能及復發率都有明顯改善。但是，少數干預研究是針對患者的靜觀能力。靜觀訓練是關於改變患者對病徵及相關痛苦的負面思想，有關研究證明可強化患者對病情和自身功能的管理能力，以及改善負面感覺及情緒。本研究建議一項以靜觀訓練為基礎的心理教育計劃(MBPP) ，以改善香港華裔精神分裂症患者的精神狀況和心理社會能力，以及改變其對病患和治療的洞悉能力，並且測試計劃的效果。 研究設計為三組重複測量的隨機對照臨床試驗，計劃在兩個精神科門診部招募144名在過去6個月內確診的思覺失調患者，在基準評估後隨機分到三個組別，包括靜觀為本教育組（MBPP）心理教育組，或常規精神護理組（每組48人）。MBPP組將進行為期6個月的12節小組課程，每兩個星期一次，每節兩小時 ; 主要教導有關管理病症的技巧,增強對自身病徵的意識、對病患的不同看法、接受和控制自我的思想,促使患者對其病患、病徵方面的想法和行為帶來積極正面的改變。心理教育組亦將進行12節，每節兩小時的小組課程，每兩至三星期一次課程內容根據研究團隊於2006 - 2008年的思覺失調心理教育計劃為基礎。 研究的主要成果包括病徵的嚴重程度、及重複入院次數，次要成果包括患者的功能、社會支援、對病患和治療的自我洞悉力。參加者會在招募時作基準評估以記錄這些數據，在干預課程完成後一星期、6個月和12個月時再被評估。根據意向處理分析的原則，所有參加者在進行研究期間12個月的數據都會被分析，包括退出者。數據統計會採用多元方差分析或多元協方差分析，以及赫爾默特(Helmert)對比測試，作組內及組間的變化比較。第一次後測之後，10位 MBPP組及10位名心理教育組的參加者會被邀請參與半結構式訪問，以瞭解他們對課程感受到的益處和缺點、課程中有效的治療元素、以及他們在參與中遇到的困難。若果本研究發現靜觀訓練為基礎的心理教育(MBPP)有顯注的成效，這種創新的護理計劃可被香港及華裔社區精神健康團隊採用，有助提高思覺失調初期患者的精神狀態和功能，並且減低他們的復發率。

15603815.label: Major findings and research outcome
15603815.value: Results of mixed-model MANOVA test indicated that a significant interactive (Group x Time) treatment effects on the whole set of five outcome scores (PANSS, SLOF, ITAQ, and number and duration of re-hospitalizations) between three groups, F(6,223)=10.21, p=0.001 (Wilks’ Lamda=0.92; partial η2 =0.54), showing a large effect size. When the between-group effects for the individual outcomes were considered independently, the Mindfulness-Based Psycho-education Programme (MBPP) participants indicated significant differences with those in the psychoeducation group and/or treatment-as-usual (TAU) on five outcome variables, including: greater improvement in psychotic symptoms [F(2,140)=7.51, p=0.002] and functioning [F(2,140)=8.98, p=0.0008]; more reductions of average length of re-hospitalisations [F(2,139)=6.28, p=0.004]; and more enhanced insight into illness/treatment [F(2,140)=7.01, p=0.003]. The MBPP participants also showed significant improvements in the three subscales of functioning (SLOF; p=0.003-0.0002), and the symptom (PANSS) subscales (p=0.001-0.004), compared with the other two groups over the 12-month follow-up (T2-3: 1 week, 6-month and 12-month post-intervention). There were significant greater improvements in symptom remissions in the MBPP participants at three post-tests (increased from 9 to 25 patients; and % remission also increased from 11.8% to 32.9% across T2-4), using Kruskal-Wallis test (KW value=5.33, p=0.002; moderate effect size of Cohen’s d=0.51), compared to the other two study groups. Results of Helmert’s contrasts test indicated that the MBPP had significantly greater improvements than the psychoeducation and/or TAU at T2-T4 on: (a) Psychotic symptoms significantly reduced (PANSS total score, p=0.01-0.003; Positive Symptoms, p=0.008-0.002; Negative Symptoms, p=0.01-0.05; General Psychopathology, p=0.008-0.001) at T2-T4, when compared with TAU. These symptoms also significantly greater improved than the psychoeducation group at T3 (total score, p=0.01; General Psychopathology, p=0.05), and T4 (total score, p=0.008; Positive Symptoms, p=0.03; General Psychopathology, p=0.01); (b) Average duration of re-hospitalisations significantly much lowered at T3 and T4 [p=0.008 and 0.006], than those in the TAU, and significantly shorter duration than the psycho-education group at T4 (p=0.01); (c) Insight into illness significantly greater increased at T3 and T4 (p=0.05 and 0.01) than the TAU; whereas, their insight also significantly more enhanced than the psycho-education group at T4 (p=0.03); and, (d) Functioning significantly greater increased than the TAU at T3 and T4 (p=0.002 and 0.0008) and also more than the psycho-education group at T4 (p=0.01). In addition, three main categories on participants’ perceived benefits/strengths of the MBPP and another two categories regarding the difficulties/challenges in intervention participation (perceived stigma, concerns about symptoms and long-term treatment required) and hindrances in mindfulness and/or problem-solving practices were identified from the interview data.

15603815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15603815.value: The findings support further research on the MBPP in psychotic disorders with patients from wider socio-demographic and clinical characteristics among Asian/Chinese populations and/or different clinical settings. A larger-scale research may allow investigation of the relationships between perceived benefits, learned skills performance (mediator), and therapeutic mechanisms of the MBPP, using structural modeling technique and/or qualitative interviews/observations. It is also important to have further research on the cost-effectiveness of MBPP in patients with diverse clinical and socio-demographic backgrounds, and/or a longer follow-up period. Another proposal of mindfulness-based programme for schizophrenia spectrum disorders was established and funded by the Health and Medical Research Fund to further investigate the clinical efficacy of this intervention approach for wider psychiatric patient populations.

15603815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15603815.value: Notwithstanding a few limitations on voluntary and sample-sized sample, the findings provide evidence of the effectiveness of a community-based, integrated MBPP for people with recent-onset psychosis on improving their mental state, relapses, insight into the illness, and a few important patient outcomes. This can subsequently lead to reduced relapse and improved recovery, and in turn reduce the medical/social costs. As the MBPP found effective, the community mental health care organisations/services in Hong Kong can corporate this program into their usual care for early-stage psychosis. The content and technique of the MBPP can also be referred to develop psychosocial interventions for other psychiatric patient groups. These results also support the integrated programme aids for relapse prevention and improves the psychosocial health/functioning in the community-based rehabilitation for psychosis in Chinese population, where limited community services are available for these patients.

15604215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15604215.value: The aging population is of concern to policy makers and society because aging is associated with increased prevalence of chronic illnesses and decreased independence, which potentially place a burden on the health and social system. Older people themselves prefer to aging-in-place (AIP) at their own homes rather than receiving institutional care. AIP is a concept that advocates the older people to live with optimal health and a level of independence that enables them to manage daily life in the community. Supporting AIP requires a health-social partnership, since many of the health issues require social interventions (e.g. meals-on-wheels) and likewise some social issues are health-related (e.g. diminished health reduces social activities). Existing disease management programs are delivered by hospital nurses and doctors, with proven outcomes. However, the ownership of health for community-dwelling people should lie with the community itself, not the hospitals. The community-based systematic approach advocates a delivery design that can mobilize resources and involve stakeholders in strengthening supported self-care. This study aims to test the effect of an AIP Health-social Partnership (HSP) program using randomized controlled trial. A sample size of 491 subjects in each arm is required for an effect size of 0.2, a power of 80% and significance level of 5% with self-efficacy as primary outcome. The study will take place in public housing estates in a Hong Kong district with support of the community leaders and geriatric team of the district hospital. The intervention involves a 3-month AIP program coordinated by a nurse case manager with nursing and community background. S/he will initiate a home-based comprehensive assessment based on the Omaha framework that addresses issues in environmental, psychosocial, physiological and health-related behaviors domains and develops a plan of care with contracted goals with the client. The follow-up will happen weekly in the first month and then biweekly in the second and third month with home visits/telephone calls. The design is guided by national guidelines and evidence that aims at enhancing self-care and self-efficacy. The intervention events are protocol-driven to ensure standardization and consistency. The control group will receive routine care and social calls. The outcome measures include perceived well-being, (self-efficacy, QOL, satisfaction), evaluated health outcomes (BP, BMI, ADL, nutritional status, medication adherence) as well as institutionalization and health service utilization. This study is original in building a HSP-AIP program with active participation of the health-social sectors and clients themselves, and subject the program to empirical testing. 老年人隨著年齡的增長，慢性病發生率增加，獨立功能下降，對醫療和社會系統造成潛在的負擔，因此，人口老化是決策者及社會關注的問題。與機構養老相比，老年人更喜歡選擇在自己的家中居家養老 (aging-in-place，AIP)。AIP 的理念提倡使老年人能夠以最佳的健康狀態並盡可能獨立地在社區中生活。支持 AIP 需要醫療界-社會夥伴合作，因為很多的健康問題需要社會干預 (例如，送餐服務)，同樣，一些社會問題與健康相關 (例如，不良的健康狀態降低社交活動能力)。具實效的現行疾病管理計劃是由醫院的護士和醫生提供的。然而，社區居民的健康應由社區本身來主宰，而不是醫院。以社區為本的系統化路徑倡導一項能調動當地資源並由持份者參與的強化支持性自我照顧的實施設計。本研究旨在通過隨機對照試驗測試一項AIP醫療界-社會夥伴合作(Health-social Partnership，HSP) 計畫的效果。以自我效能感作為主要結局指標，要求達到0.2的效應量，檢定力為80%且顯著性水準為5%，計算出所需的樣本數為每組491。這項研究將在社區領導和區域醫院老人科小組的支持下，在香港一個分區的公共屋村邨進行。干預涉及一個為期3個月，由具有護理和社會學背景的個案管理護士協調的AIP計劃。護士將啟動基於奧馬哈框架，強調環境、心理社會、生理和健康相關行為領域問題的居家綜合評估，根據與患者合約的目標制定護理計劃並實施護理。第一個月每週，第二和第三個月每兩週家訪或電話隨訪1次。方案依據國際指引和證據設計，旨在提高自我照顧能力和自我效能感。干預按照議定書執行以確保標準化和一致性。對照組將接受常規社區照顧。效果指標包括感知的健康(自我效能感、生活品質、滿意度)，測量的健康指標 (血壓、體質指數、日常活動能力、營養狀況、服藥依從)以及機構和衛生服務使用。這是一個原創性的研究，醫療界與社會以及患者自身積極參與建立HSP AIP 計畫並進行實證檢驗。

15604215.label: Major findings and research outcome
15604215.value: The health-social partnership model (HSPM) applied among community-dwelling older persons in this randomized control trial has produced evidence to support that the HSPM was effective in promoting health-related self-care behaviors. The intervention group had a significantly higher score in self-efficacy (P =0.049), activities of daily living (ADL) (P =0.012), instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) (P =0.021) and the physical components of quality of life (P <0.001) at the end of the intervention period. The program also significantly improved the mental component of QoL (P <0.001) and medication adherence (P <0.001), as well as reduced the total number of health service attendances of the intervention group compared to the control group (P =0.016). The participants in intervention group had a significant time effect in the reduction of presence of depressive symptoms. Cost-effectiveness analysis revealed that the intervention group had a higher net incremental quality-adjusted life years gain of 0.0014 (3 months) and 0.0033 (6 months) when compared to the control group. The probability of being cost-effective at 6 months was 53.2% and 53.4% respectively based on the cost effectiveness thresholds recommended by the National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence ($200,000/quality-adjusted life years) and the World Health Organization (Hong Kong gross domestic product/capita, HK$381,780). Current health programs introduced at the community level tend to be overly health-focused, neglecting the importance of the social factors that may affect health. On the other hand, the social service provided to the older people dwelling in the community also neglected the health component which contributes to overall quality of life of individuals. This study attempted to address this gap by developing a community based self-care promoting program supported by a health-social partnership framework for community-dwelling older adults and proved to be effective.

15604215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15604215.value: This study has built a health-social partnership model that is proven to be effective in enhancing self-efficacy, activities of daily living, medication adherence, quality of life and reducing the use of healthcare services. The next stage of inquiry is to facilitate the successful update of this evidence-based model in the community. Funding will be sought to support translation of knowledge and the testing of implementation of this evidence-based model. The team has now liaised with more NGOs and General Outpatient Department of the Hospital Authority to facilitate the implementation of this health-social partnership model to sustain health of older people in the community and possible reduction of unnecessary use of health services.

15604215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15604215.value: The health-social partnership model (HSPM) applied among community-dwelling older persons in this randomized control trial has produced evidence to support that the HSPM was effective in promoting health-related self-care behaviors. The intervention group had a significantly higher score in self-efficacy, activities of daily living, instrumental activities of daily living, quality of life in both the physical and mental components. The intervention group also had better medication adherence and reduced total number of health service attendances compared to the control group. In terms of cost-effectiveness, the HSPM had a good probability of being cost-effective, based on both the thresholds recommended by the National Institute for Health and Clinical Excellence and the World Health Organization using the local gross domestic product/capita. Current health programs introduced at the community level tend to be overly health-focused, neglecting the importance of the social factors that may affect health. On the other hand, the social service provided to the older people dwelling in the community also neglected the health component which contributes to overall quality of life of individuals. This study tried to address this gap by developing a community based self-care promoting program supported by a health-social partnership framework for community-dwelling older adults and proved to be effective. This study has provided evidence for policy-makers to consider shaping policies to put resources and efforts in integrating the health and social services. Findings of this study also support further work of the researchers in adopting the implementation science model to translate the evidence into practice and facilitate the success of uptake of this evidence-based health-social partnership model in community-based services.

15604515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15604515.value: Food is closely linked to a nation’s social practices, traditions, and history. A national cuisine reflects a comprehensive range of social, cultural, and artistic values (Chang et al., 2011; Mak et al., 2012a, 2012b). Food also plays an essential role in enhancing a nation’s image and in its competitive advantages as a tourist destination (Cohen & Avieli, 2004; Long, 2010). Food is often regarded as a country’s cultural ambassador, as it has an important role in penetrating foreign cultures and bridging cultural barriers (Kim et al., 2014). Tourism prompted by foreign visitors’ interest in the food or agricultural products of a country is called culinary tourism, food tourism, gastronomic tourism, tasting tourism, or slow food tourism (Cleveland et al., in press; Ignatov & Smith, 2006). The importance of this movement is illustrated by the prominence of Hong Kong food in both print and online promotional materials, which present Hong Kong as an international culinary destination (McKercher et al., 2008). The Hong Kong Tourism Board has organized a number of food festivals, competitions, and trade shows as part of an effort to globalize Hong Kong’s national foods (Lee et al., 2014; Liu & Jang, 2009a, 2009b). Successful globalization leads tourists to the country of the food’s origin and contributes to their tour satisfaction and revisit to Hong Kong (Hong Kong Tourism Board, 2014). This study will analyze the status quo of culinary tourism in Hong Kong and will consider the potential for activating culinary tourism and successfully globalizing Hong Kong food. The study has six objectives: to develop a Hong Kong food consumption value (HKFCV) scale; to develop a HKFCV map using means-end analysis; to segment tourists using the HKFCV scale and traditional segmentation methods; to identify the effects of HKFCV on involvement and behavioral intention; to identify the most preferred culinary tourism program sets; and to compare the findings between three cohorts of foreign tourists. The study will compare three foreign tourist groups that dominate Hong Kong’s inbound tourism market and have high travel expenditures (Hong Kong Tourism Board, 2014): North American, Japanese, and Korean. It will benefit the Hong Kong government, which is struggling to enhance its city brand and promote itself worldwide. Finally, the results of this study will identify strategic approaches for establishing Hong Kong as a global culinary tourism destination. Academically, this study fills a void, as there are limited Hong Kong culinary tourism case studies. 此研究将分析香港美食旅游的现状，考虑美食旅游的潜能以及成功将香港本土美食全球化。大多数美食旅游研究显示美食是一个旅游目的地最重要的属性之一，并且对于游客来说是一种很重要的体验。一些研究已经建议旅游目的地的利益相关者利用美食来打造目的地的品牌并且在地区或者国家层面巩固旅游竞争力。 此研究将比较主导香港入境旅游市场且具有最高旅游消费能力的三大国外旅游市场。 此研究将会使希望努力加强香港的品牌形象以及提升全球知名度的香港政府受益。最后，研究结果将寻找出将香港打造成全球美食旅游胜地的方法。在学术上，此研究将填补美食旅游文献的空缺。

15604515.label: Realisation of objectives
15604515.value: First, Develop a Hong Kong food consumption value (HKFCV) scale using scale development procedures. The measurement items were developed through an extensive literature review, pre-test, and pilot test. Initially, a thorough literature review of food attributes, benefits, values, and behavioral intention was conducted. The items for each construct were then derived and modified to fit the context of local food tourism. The content is reported in a published paper. Second, Develop a HKFCV map using means-end analysis, a qualitative research method. Eight cultural groupings were evident across the 1,593 participants. The researchers adopted a paper-and-pencil questionnaire to survey respondents and supplemented this with the hard laddering technique. The study findings demonstrate the merits of the value map as a hierarchy-based assessment of tourist perceptions of attributes, consequences, and values. It contributes cultural insights into local consumption by food tourists. The comparison of HLFCVMs has potential marketing implications for tourism businesses because different A-C-V linkages facilitate the establishment of customized marketing strategies targeted at homogenous cohorts of international tourists. This study constitutes a scholarly attempt to understand HLFCVMs in international food tourism settings and to undertake a cross-cultural comparison. Third, Segment foreign tourists using both the HKFCV scale and traditional segmentation methods. The segmentation was achieved using IPRA and IAA. The adopted methods used to achieve the objectives were impact-range performance analysis (IRPA) and impact asymmetry analysis (IAA). After undertaking a survey in Hong Kong, a total of 1,184 questionnaires were employed for data analyses. Results of exploratory factor analyses generated three domains of local food attributes and two domains of benefits sought from tasting local foods. Unlike multiple regression analyses, IRPA and IAA produced various results for marketing implications. Fourth, Identify the effects of HKFCV on emotional involvement, behavioral involvement, and behavioral intention. This study was designed to examine an attribute-benefit-value-intention (ABVI) model of local food consumption as perceived by foreign tourists. The model was designed to test the structural relationships between local food attributes, perceived benefits, consumption value, and behavioral intentions. The results are presented in a paper. Fifth, Develop the best culinary tourism program sets using conjoint analysis. The culinary tourism programs were different according to cultural groups. Interestingly, Asian tourists indicated ‘delicious food’ as salient attributes, whereas US and UK tourists addressed ‘traditional food’ and ‘good quality food’ as important attributes. Mainland Chinese and Japanese tourists indicated that their perception of food attributes and benefits are connected to ‘self-satisfaction and achievement’, whereas Western tourists pointed out understanding or learning value by consuming local food in Hong Kong. The study results indicate that tourists have distinct utilities, expectations, experiences, and evaluations when consuming local food in destination settings. One example would be the development of promotional messages about the “flavorful taste” of local cuisine which may be persuasive amongst Chinese and Taiwanese, whereas messages about “learning” benefits help to persuade Western groups to taste local cuisines. Messages relevant to “appreciation of being in original food place” can attract the attention of Japanese, whereas messages including “relationships related with food” will be more persuasive for Thais. Sixth, Compare the outcomes of the three major foreign tourist groups who visit Hong Kong (North American, Japanese, and Korean) and identify the effect of cultural proximity. HLFCVMs were compared across the eight groupings to test the hypothesis that tourist cultural backgrounds influence HLFCVM. The unique maps which were showcased by Japanese and Thai respondents were found to be simpler than those applicable to other cohorts. This study makes a contribution to the development of theory. Firstly the local food consumption values of tourists are introduced in the context of international food tourism using a HLFVM. Second, the researchers have attempted to develop a HLFVM according to six levels of attributes-consequences-values to provide a more exact and detailed interpretation. Third, the study has introduced a new decision rule in determining a cut-off level, which was previously disputed because of the potential for subjective researcher interpretations. Fourth, a comparison of the HLFVMs to identify whether they are similar or dissimilar across cultural cohorts using a large sample, allowed the researchers to overcome the limitations associated with considering a single national group or small samples in an exotic location.

15604515.label: Major findings and research outcome
15604515.value: This study was designed to examine an attribute-benefit-value-intention (ABVI) model of local food consumption as perceived by foreign tourists. The model was designed to test the structural relationships between local food attributes, perceived benefits, consumption value, and behavioral intentions. The structural relationships of foreign tourists’ perceptions of local food consumption were conceptualized and hypotheses were proposed. A main survey was conducted using a large sample of 1,323 tourists in Hong Kong. Regarding major findings, “food quality,” “food novelty,” and “restaurant quality” significantly affected “emotional” and “epistemic benefit.” “Emotional benefit” had a significant effect on “consumption value” and “behavioral intention,” while “epistemic benefit” only influenced “consumption value.” Local food marketers and DMOs need to promote the product features that are relevant to tourists’ benefits. Restaurant marketers need to develop distinctive strategies for tourists from different national backgrounds. This study proposed and empirically tested a new model of tourists’ local food consumption, including two benefits, consumption value and behavioral intention. In addition, the study results show similar or dissimilar A-C-V linages across eight regional groupings. Interestingly, Asian tourists indicated ‘delicious food’ as salient attributes, whereas US and UK tourists addressed ‘traditional food’ and ‘good quality food’ as important attributes. Mainland Chinese and Japanese tourists indicated that their perception of food attributes and benefits are connected to ‘self-satisfaction and achievement’, whereas Western tourists pointed out understanding or learning value by consuming local food in Hong Kong. The study results indicate that tourists have distinct utilities, expectations, experiences, and evaluations when consuming local food in destination settings. The comparison of HLFCVMs has potential marketing implications for tourism businesses because different A-C-V linkages facilitate the establishment of customized marketing strategies targeted at homogenous cohorts of international tourists. This study constitutes a scholarly attempt to understand HLFCVMs in international food tourism settings and to undertake a cross-cultural comparison. Along with its scholarly merit, this study has various implications for practitioners. Local food stakeholders can acquire an enhanced understanding of international tourist perceptions of attributes, benefits, and food consumption value. Furthermore, since the study findings are based on respondents from different cultural backgrounds, this allows for the development of food tourism strategies in different national settings. One example would be the development of promotional messages about the “flavorful taste” of local cuisine which may be persuasive amongst Chinese and Taiwanese, whereas messages about “learning” benefits help to persuade Western groups to taste local cuisines.

15604515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15604515.value: The diverse characteristics of local cuisines in a destination play a crucial role in tourists’ perception of benefits, consumption value, and future intention. This study is valuable because the proposed model manifests the importance of local food in satisfying tourists and increasing their intention to revisit. Structural equation modeling was very effective for understanding foreign tourists’ psychological reactions holistically, compared with previous studies that dealt with the mutual relationships between two constructs. Consequently, not only food stakeholders but also DMOs may gain useful insights into how to enhance tourists’ satisfaction through experiencing the local cuisine and successfully promoting the national brand. The findings may be more helpful to DMOs and food marketers if the moderating effect of tourists’ specific nationality could be examined. Moreover, further research is needed to determine whether the results of this study differ with respect to tourists’ social demographic characteristics such as gender, age, and income.

15604515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15604515.value: In this study, local food is defined as food that is grown or produced in a local area; it can be specialty food or regionally branded food that represents a local identity. This study focuses on Hong Kong food because the sample of this study consists of international tourists to Hong Kong. Since Hong Kong cuisines reflect Cantonese food ingredients, recipes, and dietary culture, they are distinctive from other Chinese foods (Choe and Kim, 2018). This study had three major objectives. The first was to identify the attributes, benefits, and consumption value of local food in a tourism destination. The second was to investigate the structural relationships between local food attributes, benefits, consumption value, and behavioral intention, using structural equation modelling (SEM). Through this study, we expect to improve our current understanding of the meanings decoded in the process of consuming local food in a foreign tourism destination. Local food marketers should consider how to maximize the effects of emotional benefits through their marketing channels. Emphasizing positive feelings such as excitement, relaxation, good memories, and nostalgia can help to create positive intentions.

15604715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15604715.value: To strengthen its environmental governance system, the Chinese government has promulgated many environmental laws and regulations at both the national and local levels. For example, the amended Environment Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China will become effective on 1st January 2015. Although the Chinese government has shown its stronger commitment to environmental protection, how to ensure the effectiveness of environmental law enforcement and policy implementation has remained as a major challenge to the Chinese bureaucracy. Many scholars have identified that goal incongruence between the central and local governments has been a major factor contributing to implementation failures on the ground. However, very few studies have paid attention to street-level bureaucrats, the individual officials who are mandated to carry out environmental laws and regulations passed from upper level governments. Indeed, how do street-level bureaucrats enforce environmental laws and regulations has remained an important issue that has not been well addressed in the existing literature. Based on a theoretical framework we have built in our recent article on environmental policy implementation in Guangzhou, Guangdong Province (Zhan, Lo, and Tang, 2014), this project will conduct a study of street-level bureaucrats in the Environmental Protection Bureaus (EPBs) of Chengdu City and Guangzhou City, which can represent inland and coastal China respectively, with significant differences in the stages of economic development and in the levels of local commitment towards environmental protection. In the proposed research, we aim to examine the relationship between political contexts, work situations, enforcement strategies and self-assessments of street-level bureaucrats in both cities, using data obtained from both in-depth interviews and questionnaire surveys. Our empirical analysis will build on our earlier study of enforcement in the two EPBs of Chengdu and Guangzhou in 2000 and 2010, and we will seek to trace the contextual changes in China’s environmental governance from the Hu Jintao and Wen Jiabao Administration to the Xi Jinping and Li Keqiang Administration, which will enable us to assess how contextual factors have impacted environmental policy implementation by street-level officials on the ground. This research will contribute to a better understanding of the enforcement gap in China’s environmental governance, and whether such enforcement gap may sustain during the Xi Jinping and Li Keqiang Administration. By relating contextual factors to the study of street-level bureaucrats’ implementation work, this research will also contribute to the general literature on public policy implementation. 中国中央政府和地方政府发布了多项环境法律法规来提升环境治理体系。例如，修订后的《中华人民共和国环境保护法》自2015年1月1日起施行。尽管中国政府已经表现出更强的承诺来保护环境，但是对于中国的官僚体系来说，如何保证这些法律和政策能够得到有效的执行仍然是一个挑战。很多学者已经发现，中央政府和地方政府的目标不一致是导致执行失灵的主要原因之一。但是很少有人研究街头官僚，也就是一线的执法者是如何来执行上级政府制定的环境法律法规的。事实上，这一研究问题在现有的文献中没有得到足够的重视。基于我们在近期发表的一篇关于广州市环境政策执行的文章中建立的理论框架(Zhan, Lo, and Tang, 2014), 本研究项目将研究成都市和广州市环境保护局街头执法官僚。两地分别代表中国的内地和沿海地区，在经济发展阶段和地方政府环保承诺上有显著差异。在该项目中，我们将研究政治环境、工作场景、执行战略和两地街头执法官僚的自我评估。我们将采取深度访谈和问卷调查的方式收集数据。我们的研究将给予我们此前在成都和广州两地分别于2000年和2010年执行的研究，我们将试图分析中国在从胡温体系向习李体系的转型过程中环境治理的体系发生了哪些变化，以及这些变化对于街头官僚的执法工作产生了什么样的影响。这一研究对于理解中国环境治理中的执行差距特别是在习李时代这一问题是否持续具有重要意义。通过把情景因素和街头官僚的执法工作联系在一起，这一研究也会对公共政策执行的文献做出贡献。

15605715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15605715.value: 互联网时代下的司法公开：来自网上公开判决书的证据

15605715.label: Project Objectives
15605715.value: What are the institutional determinants of a country’s IPJ performance? We hypothesize a country’s IPJ performance is positively related to the common law legal origin, judicial independence, and press freedom, but negatively related to corruption and judicial bureaucracy. What is the impact of the IPJ on judgment quality? We hypothesize the adoption of the IPJ will cause, on average: (a) lengthier judgments; (b) more legal analysis in judgments; (c) higher plaintiff’s win rate in administrative lawsuits; and (d) less win rate disparity between politically connected and unconnected firms.
