What is the impact of the IPJ on judgment quality? We hypothesize the adoption of the IPJ will cause, on average: (a) lengthier judgments; (b) more legal analysis in judgments; (c) higher plaintiff’s win rate in administrative lawsuits; and (d) less win rate disparity between politically connected and unconnected firms.

15605715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15605715.value: “Justice must be done and must be seen to be done.” (Lord Chief Justice Gordon Hewart 1924) Open justice is a legal principle that requires the court to conduct its business in public as a safeguard against judicial impropriety. The rise of internet enables courts to publish their decisions on the web. Suggested benefits of the Internet Publication of Judgments (hereinafter “IPJ”) include increased judicial transparency, reduced corruption, and enhanced public confidence in the judiciary. However, we know very little about the status of the IPJ around the world, its causes or consequences. This project is an endeavor to address these questions. We propose a novel “IPJ Index” based on a comprehensive survey of the IPJ laws, policies and practices around the world. We empirically test two hypotheses: (1) we conjecture a country’s IPJ performance is positively related to the common law legal origin, judicial independence, and press freedom, but negatively related to corruption and judicial bureaucracy. To test this we run regressions of our IPJ index against country-level institutional variables drawn from prior international studies. (2) We hypothesize the IPJ improves judgment quality because publicity makes judges more accountable to their decisions. We test this by investigating the effect of China’s provincial IPJ experiments at differential times from 2000 to 2013 on judgment quality in a difference-in-differences setup. Using both input (judges’ effort) and output (fairness in the outcome) measures of judgment quality, we posit the adoption of the IPJ causes, on average: (a) lengthier judgments; (b) more legal analysis in judgments; (c) higher plaintiff’s win rate in administrative lawsuits; and (d) less win rate disparity between politically connected and unconnected firms. To make this study impactful, we intend to publicize our IPJ index (with country reports, rankings and related findings) on the web. We intend this website to become an online resources platform for internet-facilitated open justice, and part of our communication channel with government officials, scholars, judges and lawyers world-wide to improve this index. Moreover, using China as an example, our result informs theorists, policy makers and legal scholars on how internet publicity can improve the judiciary in countries of weak legal environment. 司法公开作为一项现代法治社会普遍遵循的法律原则，是促进司法公正、保障司法廉洁、提升司法水平的重要手段。互联网的普及大大提升了司法判决书公开的范围和效率，并显著降低了司法判决书公开的成本。然而我们发现世界上的许多国家在利用互联网进行司法公开的范围和水平方面有着显著的差易。如何度量这些差易，这些差异是否与国家间的制度性因素相关，以及司法公开对于利益相关者的影响是本项目主要关注的研究问题。 本项目拟根据司法公开的基本原则，以及针对各国网络司法公开领域的法律，政策，以及实践，创新性地编制一套“司法公开水平指数”。该指数（及其子项分指数）将有助于我们了解并比较各国司法公开的现状和水平。在此基础上我们将进一步研究造成国家间司法公开水平差异的制度性原因：如法律渊源、司法独立性、言论自由程度、贪腐水平、以及政府效率等。 同时，本项目拟用中国为例，实证地研究网上公开判决书这一实验对于法官行为、判决书质量、以及司法公正的影响。中国大陆从2000年起在不同的省份开始了网络司法公开的试点实践，我们拟用倍差法实证地考察该实验对于（1）判决书的质量；（2）行政诉讼中原告的胜率；以及（3）政治关联方与非政治关联方胜率的差异的影响。

15608415.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15608415.value: 中國農村留守兒童：早期環境與生命史策略

15608415.label: Project Objectives
15608415.value: We will develop a new environmental interaction framework, whereby we regard resource levels (MacArthur & Wilson, 1967) as the controllable environment, the control of which is increased competition to monopolize limited resources, and harshness and unpredictability (Ellis et al., 2009) as the uncontrollable environment because extrinsic mortality and mobility are insensitive to survival effort. The interaction between the two environmental characteristics, or between r-K selection and fast-slow LH strategies, results in new hybrid LH strategies. Left-behind children provide unique data for testing this new theoretical framework. Our major prediction is that left-behind children who are exposed to improved economic resources (from city wages earned by their working parents) and, thus, r selection, but who experience increased harshness and unpredictability because of changes in residence and parental figures (i.e., living with other family members in the absence of their parents), should develop r-fast LH strategies. Control children living with their parents in the same resource-impoverished, high-density, high-competition region who do not have the windfall resources because their parents did not go to cities to work, and who, for the same reason, are spared of the separation-related harshness and unpredictability exposed to their left-behind counterparts, should develop K-slow LH strategies. Within this broad hybrid LH framework, we will test specific hypotheses regarding the effect of the interaction between resource levels (e.g., per capita income, household income, family SES, children’s food provisioning, and competition represented through entrance examination scores,) and environmental harshness and unpredictability (e.g., mainly at the individual level, change in residence, change in parental figures, exposure to death and injury of kin, and harsh parenting) on a set of developmental and behavioral outcomes (e.g., menarche and pubertal onset, sexual behavior and attitude, future orientation, impulsivity, risk taking, externalizing behavior, and academic performance). When testing the specific hypotheses, we will pay close attention to some of the widely reported findings in the literature. One example is the father absence hypothesis and its findings. We will test this hypothesis, likely for the first time, by using Chinese and rural samples. We will include resources as a separate variable so that we can factor out the effect of father absence into that due to reduced resources or earnings and that due to its being a source of environmental unpredictability. An additional example is gender, which, according to the evolutionary (Chisholm, 1996; Del Guidice et al., 2009) and mainstream literature (Voyer & Voyer, 2014), seems to be involved in calibrating or reorganizing LH strategies. The single-child policy has substantially changed gender socialization in China (Shu, 2004) even though the rural population has not closely followed this policy. 15608415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15608415.value: China has 61 million "left-behind" children who have stayed in their rural hometowns while their parents seek employment in cities. The proposed project is a life history (LH) study focusing on the impact of the early environment on the subsequent development of these left-behind children in rural China. Although early life experience has a strong impact on development (Dawson et al., 2000), there is no comprehensive theory for resolving conflicting findings on the extent to which such experience shapes development (Del Giudice & Belsky, 2011). In developed Western countries where most LH research is conducted, similarities in modern day child rearing within nuclear families living above the poverty line preclude the investigation of large environmental variations. The unfortunate experience of the Chinese left-behind children growing up separated from one or both parents in resource-impoverished rural areas provides a unique opportunity to study early environmental harshness and unpredictability as well as resource level and competition, which are the core focuses of human LH studies (Belsky et al., 2012). Based on a longitudinal sample of 500 left-behind children and their counterparts residing with both parents in the same region, the proposed study will focus on two dimensions of the early childhood environment: controllable resource levels, controllable through increased or relaxed intraspecific competition, and the uncontrollable mortality and mobility, also defined as harshness and unpredictability (Ellis et al., 2009). By re-conceptualizing LH strategies, the proposed study will treat the controllable resource levels representing r-K selection separately from environmental harshness and unpredictability representing fast-slow strategies. The main hypothesis is that left-behind children who attain additional resources (because of higher wages sent home by the working parents), but who experience increased harshness and unpredictability because of separation from parents and residence changes should develop r-fast LH strategies, whereas the control-group children living with parents in the same impoverished region who do not have the extra city wages, but are spared of separation-related harshness and unpredictability, should develop K-slow LH strategies. Developmental (e.g., pubertal onset) and behavioral outcomes (e.g., risk taking, externalizing, and academic performance) will be used to test this and other LH hypotheses. The findings from this new conceptual framework will enrich the understanding of LH theory, child and adolescent development, and, more specifically and crucially, the predicament of left-behind children, thereby assisting policy makers and the public in determining means for improving the well-being of these children. 本研究從個體生命史權衡的角度，考察中國鄉鎮留守兒童的早期生活環境對其隨後的社會技能和認知發展的影響。現有的對兒童生命史權衡的研究主要著眼于可控因素，例如環境資源豐富程度對個體的影響，很少考慮不可控因素，例如無法預料的環境改變等。 在西方社會，作爲關於生命史權衡研究的考察對象之一的兒童，主要來自核心家庭，有父母陪伴而且生活無憂。由於社會歷史原因，中國有很多鄉鎮居民移居到城市打工，他們把自己的孩子留在家鄉由其他親人撫養，造就一批數量巨大的留守兒童。這些兒童為人們研究個體的生命史權衡提供了獨特的機會，因爲他們的生活環境，在物質豐富程度與生活穩定程度方面，都不同于西方的兒童，也不同于得到父母照顧的兒童。 本研究擬從童年期到青春期，追蹤500名留守兒童，從資源豐富程度以及生活穩定程度兩個方面，考察早期生活環境對兒童日後發展的影響。由於現有生命史研究主要著重資源方面的影響所導致的有/舞競爭環境，本文結合生活穩定程度導致的快/慢生命史策略，重新定義生命史權衡。留守兒童由於父母在外工作比在家鄉收入更多，相比起同地區父母都留在家鄉的兒童來説，資源更豐富；但他們缺乏父母照顧，生活環境不穩定，因此形成了無競爭-快生命史策略；而同區其他兒童則形成有競爭-慢生命史策略。不同的策略會對青春期到來的時閒、兒童的學習表現、及其在青春期的冒險行爲等等產生不同的影響。 本研究的結果將有利於豐富和完善關於生命史權衡的理論，有助於人們更全面瞭解影響青少年社會行爲發展的因素，並且有助於國家和地區制定關於留守兒童的政策。

15608415.label: Realisation of objectives
15608415.value: Objective 1 was to develop an integrated framework that incorporates both resources or r-K selection (MacArthur & Wilson, 1967) and variability of harshness and unpredictability or fast-slow life-history strategies (Ellis et al., 2009). We have achieved this objective by respectively collecting data regarding resource levels and unpredictability and categorizing participants who scored high or low on both dimensions. We identified four types of participants. Left-behind and non-left-behind children were mapped into those four types to test our theoretical prediction in relationship to life-history strategies. In the proposal, the left-behind children were expected to generally score high on resource levels because their parents earned city wages and score high on unpredictability because parental absence cause unstable family environment and changing residential places, and thus they were hypothesized to be r-fast strategists. By contrast, non-left-behind children were expected to generally score low on resources and low on unpredictability because their family do not have city wages and they are spared of unstable life environment caused by separation from parents, and thus they were hypothesized to be K-slow strategists. Partially different from our hypothesis, we found that some left-behind children had low resources because family impoverishment was the exact reason why their parents left them to seek employment in cities, and that some non-left-behind children had high resources because their parents were returning workers who had amassed their fortune from working in cities (Zhou, Guo, & Lu, 2021). The discrepancy between our hypothesis and the actual findings was consistent with the changing reality of migrant workers in past decades. Around thirty years ago when all rural residents were impoverished, those who had migrated to work in cities earned more for their families (Liang & Morooka 2004), but in recent years those who did not have to leave their hometowns for work were the ones from well-off families or the returning workers who had sufficient capital to run their own business (Xue et al., 2014). With data collected for resource levels and environmental unpredictability, we were able to identify the four types of life-history strategists: r-fast and K-fast, to which most left-behind children belonged, and r-slow and K-slow, to which most non-left-behind children belonged. The categorization of participants was further used to associate with various developmental outcomes. Objective 2 was to examine how childhood environment related to life-history strategies affect a set of developmental and behavioral outcomes. We have achieved this objective by collecting data regarding environmental resources and unpredictability and data regarding children’s sociosexual development to examine the effect of environment on child development. Environmental resources included family capital and income, family SES, and children’s food provisioning and daily living condition, and environmental unpredictability included exposure to mortality and morbidity, unpredictable life events such as change of residence or caring figures, and parental absence. Sociosexual development included pubertal onset, affiliated sociality, future orientation, academic performance, impulsivity, risk-taking propensity, and aggressive and externalizing behavior. Children who have experienced resource scarcity demonstrated fast life history (LH) traits such as early pubertal onset, low prosociality, present orientation, poor academic performance, impulsivity, risk-taking, and externalizing behaviors. Similarly, children who have developed in unpredictable environment demonstrated fast LH traits as well (Chang & Lu, 2018; Lu & Chang, 2019; Lu, Liu, & Chang, 2021; Zhou, Guo, & Lu, 2021). Moreover, environmental resource scarcity and unpredictability worked in the same direction and had ordinal interaction. When they both were present, children would develop the fastest LH traits. More specifically, when the environment was stable and predictable, resource scarcity and abundance did not differ from each other in the effect on LH development. Relatively slow LH traits were developed under these two conditions. By contrast, when the environment was unstable and unpredictable, faster LH traits were developed in the resource-abundance condition and the fastest LH traits were developed in the resource-scarcity condition. These findings also suggest a stronger effect of environmental unpredictability than resource levels on LH development. Objective 3 was to examine the effect of father absence on pubertal onset in the left-behind children and the gender differences of the environmental effect on child development. We have achieved this objective by collecting data on gender composition of the children, status of father absence, and developmental outcomes to examine the differences between genders and between father presence and father absence. We have also reviewed studies and performed a meta-analysis regarding the effect of father absence on daughter’s menarcheal timing and constructed a model in which father absence caused high integrated stress, which in turn altered the pace of physiological and endocrinological development and resulted in advanced menarche in girls (Guo, Lu et al., 2020). The effect of childhood environment on LH related developmental outcomes was the same for both boys and girls, suggesting that the environmental effect was not gender specific. Gender differences were observed in LH traits (Chang & Lu, 2018; Lu & Chang, 2019, Lu, Liu, & Chang, 2021). Compared with girls, boys demonstrated faster LH traits, such as higher impulsivity, more externalizing problems, riskier behaviors in virtual driving, and lower affiliative sociality. These findings were consistent with findings in adults that showed men were more aggressive and more willing to take risks than women because males are faster LH strategists than females in most animals including humans (Hill et al., 1997). The findings suggest a strong evolutionary impact on gender differences, despite the single-child policy that had substantially changed gender socialization in China and had resulted in a roughly identical way to rear boys and girls. Objective 4 was to conduct a longitudinal study on a unique population (i.e., left behind children whose parents left home to seek employment in cities) to investigate how childhood environment influence life-history strategies and their corresponding developmental manifestations. We have achieved this objective by recruiting left-behind children as participants and collecting data regarding early childhood environment and data regarding developmental outcomes. The environmental data were retrospectively reported by the children’s caregivers at the beginning of the children’s middle childhood, and the developmental data were collected from the children’s self-report, their behavioral performance, and teachers’ report on the children, at the end of the children’s middle childhood toward the beginning of their adolescence. These longitudinal data enabled us to better understand the development of the left-behind children and to test the father absence hypothesis in this otherwise unfortunate population. Future study can focus on more variables regarding the psychological and behavioral outcomes in the adolescence of this population. For example, trust toward ingroup and outgroup people (Zhu, Lu, & Chang, 2021), prosocial and anti-social behaviors (Zhu, Lu, & Chang, 2020), and behavioral control under stressful situation (Lu et al., 2021).

15608415.label: Major findings and research outcome
15608415.value: In relation to the objectives, this study aimed at examining how resource levels and environmental unpredictability and their combined effect influenced developmental and behavioral outcomes in rural children, how father absence affected sexual development including menarchial timing in girls, and the gender differences of the environmental effects and life history (LH) manifestations. The first major finding showed that both resource levels and environmental risks predicted LH strategies and subsequent social sexual development. Specifically, low resource level and high environmental unpredictability, respectively, predicted fast LH strategy and corresponding manifestations that include risk-taking propensity, impulsivity, externalizing problems, present orientation, and low affiliative sociality (Chang & Lu, 2018; Lu, Liu, & Chang, 2021). Moreover, environmental unpredictability predicted risk-taking behaviors measured by a virtual driving game and a balloon analog risk task as well as aggressive behaviors reported by the child participants and their teachers (Lu & Chang, 2019). The low resource level and environmental unpredictability ordinally interacted and collectively imposed pressure on the participants to adopt fast LH strategies. More specifically, in predictable environment, LH strategies did not differ across different resource levels, whereas in unpredictable environment, low resource level resulted in faster LH strategy than did high resource level. The second major finding showed that father absence advanced pubertal onset of girls (Chang & Lu, 2018; Guo, Lu et al., 2020). Compared with father presence, father absence and bi-parental absence in the left-behind children resulted in earlier onsets of pubertal signs such as body hair development, growth spurts, and skin changes (e.g., growing pimples) in both genders, breast development and menarche in girls, and facial hair development and voice changes in boys. Father absence resulted in both resources constraint and life routine irregularities that caused increased integrated stress experienced by children, and therefore, altered the pace of physiological and endocrinological development (Guo, Lu et al., 2020; Zhou, Guo, & Lu, 2021). The third major finding was the gender differences of LH development (Chang & Lu, 2018; Lu & Chang, 2019; Lu, Liu, & Chang, 2021). In general, the impact of childhood environment on LH strategies and their corresponding developmental outcomes was the same for both genders. Compared with girls, boys demonstrated a slightly faster LH strategy, higher impulsivity, more externalizing problems, riskier behaviors in virtual driving, and lower affiliative sociality.

15608415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15608415.value: This study revealed how early life environment influenced children’s sociosexual development from the life history (LH) approach. This was a longitudinal study that ended when the children were at their late childhood to early adolescence. Future research can utilize the early childhood data collected in this study to predict the psychological and behavioral development in adolescence and youth. For example, recent studies have reported that environment conceptualized from the LH framework were associated with interpersonal trust towards ingroup and outgroup people (Zhu, Lu, & Chang, 2021), and that LH strategies affected people’s behavioral control of the COVID-19 pandemic (Lu et al., 2021) and adolescents’ prosocial and anti-social behaviors (Zhu, Lu, & Chang, 2020). Future research can include these psychosocial LH manifestations as well as sexual and reproductive behaviors in adolescents and youth as the development outcomes. We will consider applying for continuity grants in the coming years to examine a longer-term impact of early environment on the left-behind children.

15608415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15608415.value: Left Behind Children refer to millions of children left behind in their rural home places by their parents who went to the cities to seek employment. In this study, we took a life history (LH) approach to assess the developmental outcomes of a group of left-behind children selected from rural villages of Henan province. Within the LH framework, we examined resource conditions (e.g., household income, family SES, children’s food provisioning) and unpredictable living conditions (e.g., change of residence, change of caregivers, exposure to negative life events). Supportive of our hypotheses, we found that low resource levels and high environmental unpredictability resulted in these children developing fast LH profiles that include having early pubertal onset, taking reckless risks, and being impulsive and aggressive. According to evolutionary LH theory, these seemingly negative traits and behaviors are adaptive responses to an already harsh and unpredictable living environment imposed on these children (i.e., doing the best out of a bad situation). Parents, teachers, and society as a whole should work together to improve the living environment of rural children. The year of 2021 marks the end of poverty in China. This achievement should fundamentally improve children’s development and hopefully eliminate the “left-behind children” phenomenon.

15609315.label: Project Objectives
15609315.value: Primary outcome objective: Aim 1: To evaluate whether the efficacy of a simplified 5-step hand hygiene program is non-inferior to the conventional 7-step hand hygiene program for schoolchildren with MID in special schools. Hypothesis 1: The cleaning efficacy of 5-step simplified hand washing intervention is not inferior to that of the conventional 7-step hand washing intervention for students with MID in special schools. Secondary outcome objectives: Aim 2: To evaluate the sustainability of the simplified and conventional hand hygiene programs, defined by how well the students with MID can recall the intervention steps 12 months after the intervention programs. Hypothesis 2: The hand hygiene procedures would be retained in the MID students’ memory 12 months after completion of the two intervention programs. Aim 3: To evaluate the cleaning efficacy of the simplified and conventional hand hygiene programs for students with MID in reducing sickness-related school absenteeism. Hypothesis 3: Students with MID's sickness-related absenteeism would decrease significantly after completion of the two intervention programs. Aim 4: To evaluate the acceptability and suitability of implementing hand hygiene programs specifically in special schools in Hong Kong. Evaluation 4: We will evaluate the acceptability and suitability of implementing two hand hygiene programs in special schools in Hong Kong by conducting focus group analysis.

The results for the objective 4 to evaluate the acceptability and suitability of the two hand hygiene programs have been reported and submitted to American Journal of Infection Control. A study report with hand hygiene educational tools for training of trainers has also been published and distributed to the participated schools (ISBN 978-988-13391-8-8).

15609315.label: Major findings and research outcome
15609315.value: A total of 445 students with ID were recruited from six special schools. Schools were randomly assigned to either the simplified 5-step hand hygiene program or the conventional 7-step hand hygiene program as usual practice with video modelling-based intervention package (Handwashing songs, posters, magnetic stickers, matching and video as the multimedia visualization teaching strategies). Measurements included the validated handwashing technique rating, the hand cleanliness rating and the number of sick leave days at different time points. The technique scores in intervention group were significantly higher than the scores in control group after 2nd month although there were significant increases in the scores within both groups. Moreover, the hand cleanliness score in intervention group was significantly higher than the score in control group at post-test, despite improvements in both groups compared with baseline. Furthermore, the mean number of sick days decreased between baseline and 10th month in both groups according to descriptive statistics. The technique scores in intervention group were significantly higher than the scores in control group after 6th month although there were significant increases in the scores within both groups. Moreover, the hand cleanliness score in intervention group was significantly higher than the score in control group at post-intervention, despite improvements in both groups compared with baseline. Furthermore, the mean number of sick days decreased between baseline, 4th month, 7th month and 10th month in both groups according to descriptive statistics. We adopted an exploratory study and conducted 18 focus group discussions with 72 students with intellectual disabilities who experienced the observational hand hygiene video modeling intervention and the 19 school personnel who implemented hand hygiene modeling and provided feedback intervention. Analysis identified five themes of the Observational Modeling Framework: (1) modeling attention: learning handwashing technique if students with ID attended to the model of handwashing behaviours using video-based teaching aids; (2) behavioral retention: remembering the proper handwashing behaviour when they apply it; (3) motor reproduction: students with ID must be able to replicate the proper handwashing technique; (4) display self-motivation: students with ID want to demonstrate proper handwashing technique that they have learned; and (5) routine practice: handwashing modeling was perceived to be the essential domain to facilitate and provide support for the observational modeling process. In this qualitative study, the facilitation of five modeling steps and the provision of environmental and context support for people with ID was a critical component of observational hand hygiene modeling.

15609315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15609315.value: The findings of this innovative study should provide new evidence for the public health sector to explore and consider to adopt the simplified 5-step as the standardized handwashing technique in the school communities, especially for students with ID.

15609315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15609315.value: The results in this study indicate that students with ID who were trained to practice the simplified 5-step handwashing technique with multimedia visualization teaching strategies have experienced significant improvements in the quality of handwashing technique and cleanliness. It has also shown that the school absenteeism rates reduced. The simplified 5-step intervention was shown effective and it is feasible to be adopted as a standardized handwashing technique for students with ID. It is hoped that the findings will encourage the public health sectors to adopt this simplified 5-step handwashing program as a standardized strategy in special schools and ordinal schools.

15609715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609715.value: This study aims to discover expressed meaning in text by focusing on implicit emotions and propose an interactional approach combining linguistic and socio-psychological modelling with computational language processing technology. Since the dawn of the information age, newsworthy facts and trends have spread farther and faster around the globe than previously thought possible. As new information is transmitted to a wider audience, we can observe with greater clarity the kinds of emotions that are triggered in individuals through the implicit nature (and volume) of their response to different events. Previous attempts at emotion analysis have focused mainly on the examination of explicit emotions, in terms of their syntactic and semantic characteristics (in the field of linguistics) or their identification and classification (in the field of natural language processing). Explicit emotion refers to the presence of emotion-related information denoted by emotion keywords, e.g., happy, worried, and sad. This project aims to examine an important yet underdeveloped branch of emotion analysis, i.e. implicit emotion. Implicit emotion refers to the emotion-related information conveyed through inference or connotation instead of emotion keywords. We argue that an in-depth analysis of implicit emotion is a necessary component of emotion analysis; as the majority of emotions expressed are implicit in nature, there is a clear gap in existing emotion research, which this study aims to address. In conducting a comprehensive analysis of implicit emotions, it is important to address the following questions: What kinds of events trigger different implicit emotions? How are such implicit emotions expressed in text? Moreover, what kinds of users are more susceptible to a particular type of implicit emotion? In this research, we will attempt to answer the above questions by exploring implicit emotions in responses to events and trends posted on online social media websites. The overarching goal of this research is to paint a fuller picture of the forms and representations of implicit emotions, and to unveil the mechanism of interactions between event types, implicit emotions, and user profiles. We believe that the current study will shed light on the inference of implicit information as well as the automatic detection and classification of emotion. 本项目旨在通過關注文本中的隱含情緒信息，探討文本表達的含義，並提出一結合語言學、社會心理學模型及計算語言處理技術的互動法。自信息時代的到臨，具報導價值的事實與發展趨勢比往昔更快更遠地傳遍世界各地。由於新資訊正廣泛地傳播予更龐大的受眾群，我們可藉不同個體對不同事件的反應的隱含性（及量），更清晰地觀察在他們身上所引發的各種情緒。過往對情緒分析的研究主要集中於顯性情緒，分別基於其句法及語義特點（在語言學領域）及其識別與分類方法（在自然語言處理領域）作研究重點。顯性情緒是指由具情緒相關信息的關鍵詞所言明的情緒，如高興、憂慮及傷心。本項目致力研究一項雖然重要卻尚有待開發的情緒分析課題的分支——隱含情緒。隱含情緒即在沒有情緒關鍵詞的前提下，透過推論文本中傳達情緒相關信息的內文涵意而識別到的情緒。鑒於情緒多以隱含的方式表達，而過往相關研究卻鮮有提及，我們認為對隱含情緒作深入分析是情緒分析課題中重要的一環，故本研究将重点处理及分析隐含情绪的特质。 在進行隱含情緒的綜合性分析時，以下幾個問題是需要解決的，包括：甚麼類型的事件會誘發不同的情緒？這些隱含的情緒會如何在文本中呈現？哪種用戶更易受某種特定的隱含情緒所影響？本研究將藉探究人們對於網絡社交媒體上提及的事件的情緒反應，試圖就上述問題提出答案。本研究項目的最終目的為更全面地呈現隱含情緒的形態和表述方式，並展示事件類型、隱含情緒及用戶簡介的互動機制。我們深信这次項目將有助加深對隱含信息推論、自動識別以及情緒分類三方面的相關認知。

15609715.label: Realisation of objectives
15609715.value: [The five objectives originally proposed in the GRF submission have been revised to four objectives due to the reduction in budget and project timeline from 3 years to 2 years.] The four objectives proposed in the project have all been achieved. Details are given below: Objective 1: A Chinese event-comment corpus has been constructed. 500 posts have been extracted from Sina Weibo, with each post containing 200 comments. In other words, the corpus contains 500 posts and 100,000 comments in total. We randomly selected 200 posts together with 50 corresponding comments for event and emotion annotation. Event annotation: We adopted TimeML for the annotations of events. Approximately 780 events are identified in the 200 events. We then mapped the annotated events to the WordNet synsets, and classified them into different event types based on their semantic meanings. Since we intend to figure out the interaction between emotion and event type, as well as the interaction between emotion and central figure of an event, we employ FrameNet for the tagging of frame elements of each event. Emotion (and other related information) annotation: Annotators annotated 50 comments of each post with emotion information, including the emotion(s) expressed in a comment, the opinion targets (i.e. what the comment is about), and the use of rhetorical questions. Both explicit emotions and implicit emotions are annotated. For the annotation of explicit emotions, five basic emotions, namely Happiness, Sadness, Anger, Fear and Surprise, are automatically identified based on the taxonomy proposed in Lee (2010), in which the accuracy of the annotation has been checked by annotators. Annotators were also asked to identify implicit emotions, i.e. emotions not expressed by means of emotion keywords or explicitly described. Apart from emotions, rhetorical questions, which is believed to be an emotion-expressing device, are also annotated. Annotators identified the types of rhetorical questions used in the corpus, including series of questions, A-not-A, alternative, echo, etc. In addition, opinion targets were annotated. Opinion targets refer to the argument(s) or topic(s) that a comment is mainly about. Annotators should annotate the opinion target(s) of each comment that is marked with emotion information. Cause events that trigger the emotions were also annotated. Objective 2: Emotions were found to be more frequently expressed in an implicit way (i.e. without emotion keywords). In other words, emotions were often expressed through other emotion-related words or syntactic patterns. We investigated various linguistic characteristics of the annotated implicit emotions and the relevant linguistic cues in terms of semantic, syntactic and pragmatic structure. We found that implicit emotions are expressed by means of various linguistic features, for example emoticons, including verb types, cue words, opinion targets, specific syntactic structures, rhetorical questions, dislocation, punctuations, various figurative devices, cause events, etc. We also examined the interaction between emoticons and explicit emotions. The results showed that the meaning of emotion keywords could be altered with the use of emoticons in a sarcastic way. Objective 3: We mapped different event types to the emotions identified in the corresponding comments. Our observation showed that the provoked emotions often relate to two factors in the event content. The first factor is the event type; for example, 'earthquake' events often provoke sadness and fear emotions. The second factor is that the semantic role of the opinion targets in each post may affect the emotion expressed. For example, the agent and the patient of a 'domestic abuse' event would trigger different emotions in an observer. In that case, if the opinion target is the agent of the event, it is highly likely that an anger emotion is provoked, whereas if the opinion target is the patient of the event, a sadness emotion is provoked. Objective 4: A number of studies have been conducted to simulate and verify the effectiveness of various linguistic findings found in Objective 3 in detecting emotions. We applied a term counting approach to employ linguistic cues such as emotion related words, emotion laden words, adverbs, etc. to predict the occurrence of emotions. Experiment results showed that the linguistic cues prove effective in detecting implicit emotions. We also proposed a neural network approach for emotion classification with the incorporation of emotion cause events. This unified framework allowed simultaneous training of two models for both emotion classification and emotion cause detection, which achieved promising performance in emotion classification. In addition, an adversarial attention model has been proposed to help improve the robustness of emotion classification.

15609715.label: Major findings and research outcome
15609715.value: Major findings 1. A Chinese event-comment emotion corpus was constructed and annotated with emotion-related information such as explicit emotion, implicit emotion, event type, opinion target, rhetorical question, cause events, and post-events. It provides an empirical foundation for linguistic, sociological, and psychological analyses, as well as computational modelling of emotion mechanism. 2. Emotions are often found to be expressed through means other than explicit emotion keywords. This project addressed the gap in existing emotion research – implicit emotion. Various linguistic characteristics of annotated implicit emotions and the relevant linguistic cues in terms of semantic, syntactic and pragmatic structure have been examined. This linguistic account of implicit emotion contributed to a clearer understanding of emotion concepts. 3. The study provides a mechanism for capturing and linking implicit emotions to specific event types. The interaction between event types and opinion targets are found to play an important role in triggering different emotions. This gives a thorough account of the complex nature of emotions. 4. The linguistic findings of implicit emotion have been proven effective through computational modelling, which greatly enhances the robustness of the existing emotion classification systems. Research outcome Publications as a result of this project include four journal articles (#1, #2, #3, #4), and four book chapters (#5, #6, #7, #8). Moreover, the study has been made the topic of nine conference proceedings (#9, #10, #11, #12, #13, #14, #15, #16, #17) and three conference presentations. In addition to the above, two journal articles are currently under review, and two journal articles (one on the linguistic model, and the other on the computational model) are being prepared for publication.

15609715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15609715.value: After completing this study, there are two primary areas around which further ideas can be developed and future research can be based. First, the data set in this study is entirely obtained from a single social media platform, which makes it easier to analyse and derive patterns from. However, in order to strengthen the breadth, depth and predictive power of the model, implicit-emotion posts from other platforms should be assessed and evaluated as well. This will increase the range of the different types of posts and allow for more nuance in emotion detection and classification. Second, in terms of focus, various aspects of implicit emotion can be studied more in-depth. For example, using figurative language devices such as sarcasm and irony, metaphor and simile has an (intended) effect of making otherwise straightforward emotion keywords mean something different from their face value. We have obtained a university grant to conduct research on such language devices, and whether the use of emotion keywords is consistent across different platforms and genres of text.

15609715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15609715.value: The focus of our research in this project has been to uncover the deeper meaning behind what people say and post on social media. While there is often a clear and present emotion to be found within each post, we are aware that there are hidden messages and underlying emotions which are implied by the author. By completing this research, we have developed a way to recognise these implicit emotions in text. From a linguistic perspective, this involves analysing different layers of text - word, lexical and sentential - to find out any hidden or indirect meanings within. In so doing, we improve the accuracy of detecting and classifying emotions - both implicit and explicit - by leaps and bounds. Accounting for implicit emotions as well as explicit ones not only allows for more precise emotion detection and classification, but also provides a broader perspective and framework for collecting and organising data on the subject. This contributes to a wider discussion and analysis of emotions in other contexts and uses, and we hope that efforts can be made to build upon the groundwork laid out in this study.

15609815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15609815.value: How to control environmental pollution has become a pressing policy issue facing by the Chinese government. After more than 30 years of rapid economic development, environmental quality is deteriorating at an increasingly rapid rate, mainly due to China’s poor performance in controlling industrial pollution. Nevertheless, noticeable progress is periodically observed in the control and reduction of specific industrial pollutants. One possible explanation provided in recent studies is that the adoption of campaign-style enforcement of environmental policy has significantly reduced industrial air pollution. Campaign-style enforcement is defined as a type of policy implementation involving extraordinary mobilization of administrative resources under political sponsorship to achieve a specific policy target within a defined period of time. Given the increasingly widespread adoption of this alternative enforcement approach to regulatory control of pollution in China, this proposed research seeks to perform a longitudinal and comparative study of campaign-style enforcement in environmental governance in China. Specifically, it attempts to answer four research questions in environmental regulation within the context of energy conservation and emission reduction (ECER) policy as follows: (1) In what ways does campaign-style enforcement achieve a sustainable and positive impact on regulatory enforcement and compliance? (2) Given the evolving regulatory environment, have there been systematic shifts in the mechanisms through which campaign-style enforcement works? (3) Do regional variations in regulatory and political contexts affect the effectiveness of campaign-style enforcement? (4) In what ways do regulated enterprises with different ownership types respond differently to campaign-style enforcement? These questions will be addressed by conducting: (a) semi-structured interviews with firm managers in campaign-targeted industries in the selected four cities of Guangzhou, Shanghai, Chengdu, and Dalian, (b) in-depth interviews with government officials of environmental protection bureaus and those in bureaus in charge of industrial and economic development in individual cities, and (c) content analysis of local environmental policy archives. The research will build on our earlier exploratory study on the implementation of China’s ECER policy in the power sector as part of that country’s 11th Five-Year Plan. New data to be collected in the proposed research, together with data collected in the previous round, will allow us to study (a) the long-term impact of campaign-style enforcement on regulatory enforcement and corporate compliance in the PRD region, and (b) how different firm-level features and regional variations in regulatory contexts affect the effectiveness of campaign-style enforcement. By drawing on new and current data, the proposed research will provide insights into the dynamics of campaign-style enforcement and its theoretical development. 环境污染已经成为当前中国政府急需解决的政策难题。经过30多年的经济快速发展，对工业污染的忽视已经导致中国的环境质量在急剧恶化。值得注意的是，近些年政府在减少某些特定污染物方面却取得了一定的进展。最近的研究提供了一个可能的解释是，运动式的政策执行策略显著减少了工业废气污染。运动式执法作为一种特殊的政策执行手段通常是指在政治力量的大力支持下通过广泛动员行政和经济资源在规定的时间内去达到一个特定的政策目标。鉴于中国的环境监管越来越广泛地采用这种特定的执行方式，本研究旨在通过纵向和比较研究进一步深化对中国环境治理的运动式执法的理解。具体来说，本研究试图以中国的节能减排政策作为实证研究来回答以下四个问题： 1) 运动式执法如何能够实现环境监管执法和守法的可持续和正面的效能？ 2) 考虑到不断变化的监管环境，运动式执法的作用机制是否出现了系统性的变化？ 3) 环保监管和政治环境的区c域差异是否会影响运动式执法的有效性？ 4) 不同所有制类型的受监管企业是否对运动式执法有不同的应对方式？ 为了回答以上问题，本研究将做以下实证数据收集：（1）在预选的四个中国城市（广州，上海，成都，及大连）挑选运动式执法所涉及的不同行业的企业负责人进行半结构式的访谈；（2）在各个城市与环保局官员以及分管工业和经济发展的部门官员进行深入的访谈；（3）对各个城市在“十一五”和“十二五”期间的地方环保政策实施文件进行分析。本研究将建基于我们之前对中国电力行业在十一五期间节能减排运动式执法的探索性研究。通过收集新的数据并与上一轮的研究数据整合，本研究将深入回答以下两个问题：（1）运动式执法对珠三角地区的环保监管执法和企业守法带来了哪些长期影响；（2）区域监管环境的差异以及企业之间的差异性会如何影响运动式执法的有效性。通过对新的和现有的数据进行分析，本研究试图更加深入地理解运动式执法并将其动态演变理论化。

15609815.label: Realisation of objectives
15609815.value: In the process of implementing this research project, we conducted in-depth interviews with management executives of manufacturing enterprises in Shanghai, Chengdu, Tianjin (replacement of Dalian), and Guangzhou, between 2015 and 2019. Data was collected in the four selected cities to perform a comparative analysis of how campaign-style enforcement (CSE hereafter) of environmental regulations very across contexts and how regulated firms react to CSE initiatives. As this project is built on our study of campaign-style enforcement in the power sector in 2009-2010, we used the same set of interview questions for data collection in individual locations. Regarding data collection efforts in Shanghai, Chengdu, and Tianjin, our interviews cover a boarder industrial sectors that were targeted by various CSE efforts. In particular, we were able to interview both the top manager and environmental manager of each manufacturing company sampled in Chengdu. For data collection in Guangzhou, we focused on the case selection within the power industry. A total of 10 interviews with top exutives of power plants in the city were conducted in 2019. This data collection efforts allows us to perform a longitudinal analysis by comparing the findings with that from the previous data collected in the power sector between 2009-2010. We conducted interviews with environmental enforcement leaders in the Guangzhou EPB and its subordinate offices in all its eleven districts between 2016 and 2017. In these interviews, we asked questions regarding their teams’ major responsibilities, their work situations, their approaches to enforcement, the difficulties they faced in their work, and significant changes in their internal and external environments in the past decade. At least two members of the research team attended each interview, which lasted about one to two hours. The interviews were arranged with the support of the Guangzhou Academy of Environmental Science, which is the research arm of Guangzhou Environmental Protection Bureau. We employed a complementarity mixed methods design in the sense that qualitative interviews were used to illustrate and clarify survey findings. In addition to interviews with regulated enterprises, we also performed content analysis of local environmental policy archives especially policy changes over time in the power sector. We performed a desktop research to examine the evolving mechanisms of CSE and study respective institutional settings of environmental regulations and enterprises’ corporate environmental performance. The later provided us with the contextual basis for the preliminary understanding of cross-cities temporal and regional variations in campaign-style enforcement. An analysis of these data from multiple sources allows us to investigate the long-term impact of CSE on regulatory enforcement and compliance (Objective 1) and whether there have been systematic shifts in the mechanisms through which CSE works (Objectives 2). Moreover, the interviewed enterprises cover a range of industrial sectors and firm types, enabling us to explore whether firms with different ownership types respond differently to CSE (Objective 4). Finally, combining the interview data and secondary information from policy archives collected in the selected four cities, we were able to examine regional variations in terms of regulatory and political contexts that affect the implementation of CSE (Objective 3). Based on the data collected, we were able to publish two papers and one book chapter on regulatory enforcement and environmental governance. The first paper is entitled “Beyond deterrent enforcement styles: Behavioural intuitions of Chinese environmental law enforcement agents in a context of challenging inspections”. It came out in a 2018 issue of the Public Administration. It extends the study of regulatory enforcement by: (1) separating enforcement style elements during inspections and sanction decision-making work, (2) focusing on how these elements function in a context where it is hard in practice to achieve deterrence, and (3) assessing how agents view the effectiveness of combinations of style elements in such a context. The second is a book chapter entitled “Dynamics of Inspectors’ Enforcement Styles”, published in 2019 in Van de Walle, S. and Raaphorst, N. Eds., The Inspectors: Enforcement at the Frontline of Government. The core question addressed is: Why do inspectors subscribe to different enforcement styles in conducting regulatory control in an authoritarian regime? The third paper, entitled “Unpacking the complexity of environmental regulatory governance in a globalizing world: a critical review for research agenda setting”, appeared in a 2020 issue of the Journal of Environmental Policy & Planning, performs a critical review of the existing body of literature on environmental regulatory governance as the basis for a research agenda setting. In addition to the above-mentioned publications, there are two working papers in preparation for submission. The first working paper, entitled “Enforcement Officials’ Coping Strategies in a Changing Regulatory Environment”, is ready for submission to the Public Management Review. Since the recent completion of data collection in the power sector, we have started to develop several papers to investigate the over-time shift of CSE in the power sector in China. In this work, we aim to describe how top-down political pressure and technological advance has generated predictable CSE and the mechanism behind enterprises’ choices of responses to such enforcement based on existing literature on CSE and the axiom of cumulative inertia. In doing so, we will perform more rigorous analysis of the rich interview data with a focus on cross-city and cross-sector comparison in the next few months. The second working paper, entitled “Predictable Campaign-Style Enforcement and Regulatory Compliance” is under preparation for submission to the Public Administration Review. We expect two papers to be prepared in this process for possible conference presentations and journal submissions next year. Taken together, we are confident that findings from these working papers will add novel insights to that from the first three publications from this project, and together to provide significant implications for both regulators and business managers in environmental governance.

15609815.label: Major findings and research outcome
15609815.value: In the process of conducting field research in the respective locations, we have integrated the new data collected in this project with survey data collected in earlier studies. As a result, two journal papers and one book chapter, together with a few conference presentations have been completed. The first major finding is derived from an integration of survey data and interviews among street-level enforcement officials. We found that agents overall see inspection-style elements as more effective than sanction-style elements. They, however, did not consider that more intensive inspections would produce more effective enforcement. Instead, the context agents work matters a lot. In this sense, the effectiveness of CSE by engendering substantive deterrence and sanction is limited. The second major finding addresses the trajectory of regulatory enforcement in an evolving regulatory environment. We summarized a list of working principles for closing the enforcement gap. Four out of the ten principals are closely related to explore the effectiveness and over-time changes of CSE, namely, the principle of “shared priorities”, the “clear objectives” principle, the principle of “resource support”, and that of “adequate enforcement authority”. Our empirical analysis of enforcement styles during a 14-year period provides strong empirical support for the argument that the regulatory behaviors of inspectors is influenced by political leaders and their constituencies. The third major finding emerges from our broad reflection on the complexity of environmental regulatory governance in a globalizing world. Our critical review of the existing literature revealed that in the midst of the doubtful effectiveness of routine enforcement, CSE has become the strongest variant of the state-centered enforcement approach. The last major insights is derived from a working paper based on our preliminary longitudinal analyses. We developed two major argumentations. First, with the technological advances enabling the government to monitor the factories and the spread of “political first” trend making the top political leaders' concerns on the environment produce continuous top-down political pressure, the original CSE may transform into a predictable campaign enforcement which is embedded in routine monitoring with no periodic weakening. Second, in the face of predictable CSE and the possible factory closures, different enterprises have varied responses. This is because their differences in history, operation status, environmental management, ownership type, etc. have caused differences in accumulated inertia. The way that campaign style enforcement finally uses to achieve sustainable impacts on enterprises is to make itself predictable and become the sword of Damocles.

15609815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15609815.value: Given the proven academic contributions of this study, as demonstrated by the papers published in top-ranked journals in public policy and environmental studies, it is strongly desirable to conduct future research in various directions. In particular, a good future direction is to examine why and how regulatees respond to predictable and routinized CSE differently. Perhaps one way is to unpack the dynamic process of CSE and firm responses in regard to the mechanism behind the choices of different responses. Empirically, in addition to the pure qualitative research design as adopted in this project, we acknowledge that recent methodological developments offer opportunities to advance and test the theory of CSE. In particular, the Big Data movements make data utilization for full-cycle studies possible. One obvious extension is to integrate the considerable amount of data from social media, Internet searches, and NGO monitoring data with the increasingly available, government-disclosed data. Such data integration offers strengths in data and measurement sources to explore the breadth and depth of interactions within CSE. With a more rigorous and comprehensive data analysis facilitated by these data collection initiatives, we are confident that we can produce further impactful research outputs in the years to come.

15609815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15609815.value: Campaign-style enforcement is defined as “a type of policy implementation involving extraordinary mobilization of administrative resources under strong political sponsorship to effectively address the decoupling problems in regulatory enforcement and compliance by resource mobilization and power redistribution”. By building on our earlier study on CSE of the profound energy conservation and emission reduction policy under China’s 11th Five-Year Plan, this project has collected rich data in how enforcement officials and regulated enterprises respond to prevalent CSE initiatives in China since then. Adopting a cross-city and cross-sector design, we collected empirical data from in-depth interviews and archival policy documents. Integrating these qualitative data with prior survey data allow us to perform analysis to trace the developmental use of CSE strategies in environmental governance in China’s dynamic and diversified institutional setting. Specifically, we were able to unpack the long-term impact of CSE on environmental governance, and how distinct firm-level factors and regional variations explain the dispersion in CSE effectiveness. We found that the government makes the enterprises know that stricter management is coming and uses the past campaign style enforcement to teach them a lesson. This project hence provide insights into the dynamics of CSE and contribute to its theoretical development.

16100015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100015.value: 氨酰tRNA合成酶是在蛋白质翻译过程中发挥重要作用的古老酶类。特别的是这类酶在进化过程中逐步获得了非催化结构域。我们最近发现了超过200个氨酰tRNA合成酶基因的剪接变体。这些剪接变体大多保留了非催化结构域，而剪切了催化功能域，以获取与其氨酰化功能不同的生物活性。然而，这些剪接变体如何改变结构以获取新功能的分子机制仍知之甚少。 此项研究的目的在于更好地了解氨酰tRNA合成酶如何通过改变四级结构获得新生物功能。本研究主要针对两个酪氨酰-tRNA合成酶的剪接变体。它们在人类和小鼠间具保守性，可能具备重要生物学功能。这些剪接变体剪切了酪氨酰-tRNA合成酶的内部结构域，因此有可能产生新的构象。我们的初步数据表明，在第一个剪接体中，剪接融合了酪氨酰-tRNA合成酶的两个远端序列，形成了卷曲螺旋结构。在第二个剪接体中，因剪接点一个细微的差别显著弱化了卷曲螺旋的形成倾向。这些发现支持氨酰tRNA合成酶基因的剪接变体可重塑构象的假设。有趣的是，该两个新剪接体在不同的组织/细胞类型中特异性表达，很可能行使特定的生物学功能。此外，我们最近的研究发现剪接体在人体骨髓间充质干细胞分化为脂肪细胞的过程中表达上调。 在这个项目中，我们计划进一步研究这两个酪氨酰-tRNA合成酶剪接变体的结构和功能。首先，我们将通过结晶和核磁共振技术解析这些蛋白的高分辨率结构。第二，我们将研究它们在所富含的细胞类型中的生物活性，以及是否被分泌为细胞外信号分子。第三，我们将研究它们在人体骨髓间充质干细胞分化为脂肪细胞过程中的作用，确定其细胞定位及识别与其结合的蛋白质。 通过比较这两个剪接变体的结构、表达，分泌/定位和生物活性，并参照酪氨酰-tRNA合成酶原型，可更深入了解基因剪接如何创造新的结构以行使新的生物功能。此外，氨酰tRNA合成酶已知具备多样的非翻译酶活性，但在细胞分化中的生物学作用从未被报道。这个项目可能会揭示氨酰-tRNA合成酶在干细胞分化为脂肪细胞中的作用，进一步揭示这类蛋白的功能多样性，也可能为未来治疗肥胖相关的疾病奠定基础。

16100015.label: Realisation of objectives
16100015.value: Aminoacyl tRNA synthetases (AARS) are ancient enzymes that play fundamental roles in protein translation. They are exceptional in their progressive and accretive proliferation of noncatalytic domains during evolution. We have recently discovered more than 200 spliced variants (SVs) of AARS genes. A large ensemble of these SVs retains noncatalytic domains while ablating the catalytic domain to create catalytic-nulls (CNs) with biological activities distinct from the canonical aminoacylation function. However, the molecular mechanisms of how the CNs adapt their structures for new functions remain poorly understood. In this project, we have focused on SVs of tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase (TyrRS) to better understand how AARS CNs gain non-canonical activities through transformation of quaternary structures. We have 3 listed objectives: Objective 1: High-resolution structural characterization of TyrRS SVs - 80% completed We performed systematic biochemical and structural characterizations for TyrRS SVs. We first focused on TyrRS-SV7 (the designated protein name of the splice variant TyrRS∆E2-4), whose N-terminus was found to form a distinct alpha-helical structure not present in full-length (FL) TyrRS based on nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) studies. We have employed crystallization and NMR approaches for structural studies, but found the protein sample was not in an optimal homogeneity or stable folding for high resolution structure determination. To address this issue, we expressed the proteins using the mammalian expression system (human 293F cells) to allow native modification of the proteins. Furthermore, we adopted the strategy of co-expression and/or co-crystallization of TyrRS-SV7 with a protein partner (PARP1) that could probably facilitate its folding and stability. PARP1 (Poly [ADP-ribose] polymerase 1) is a protein that we previously found with correlated expressions with TyrRS-SV7 during the differentiating of human mesenchymal stem cells (HMSC) to adipocytes. In this project we showed that PARP1 was associated with the novel function of TyrRS-SV7 in HMSC differentiation, and could be co-immunoprecipitated with TyrRS-SV7 but not the mini-TyrRS (aa1-364). By in vitro GST pull-down assay, we further demonstrated that TyrRS-SV7 directly interacted with PARP1. PARP1 is a large protein with over 1000 amino acids, so we attempted to delineate the PARP1 domains that interact with TyrRS-SV7 for structural studies. Using truncation variants, we found that the C-terminus of TyrRS-SV7 (aa365-528, TyrRS-CT) specifically interacts with the N-terminus of PARP1 (aa1-661), in which the BRCT domain (aa387-486) contributes most to the binding. Next, we evaluated the binding between TyrRS-CT and PARP1-BRCT in vitro by isothermal titration calorimetry, which demonstrated a weak binding with a sub-mM affinity, indicating a transient signaling interaction between TyrRS and PARP1. To facilitate the complex formation, we fused the two proteins with a 10aa-linker. After trying a great number of crystallization conditions, we have recently obtained decent protein crystals, which will be sent to the Shanghai Synchrotron to collect the diffraction data for structure determination. If the data resolution is not ideal, conditions will be further optimized to obtain better crystals. Objective 2: Study of regulated expression, secretion and cytokine-like activity of TyrRS SVs using cell-based assays - 90% completed We investigated the secretion of TyrRS SVs for their potential roles as extracellular signaling molecules, and found that both TyrRS SV7 and SV8 (the designated protein names of the splice variants TyrRS∆E2-4 and TyrRS∆E2-3, respectively) over-expressed in HEK293 cells were released into the culture media, while TyrRS-FL under the same condition was released much less. We also studied the regulation of TyrRS SVs in human cells in response to stimuli. We mainly focused on several human immune cell types including Jurkat T, Raji B and THP-1, and a human lung epithelial cell line A549. We found that in THP-1-differentiated macrophages, lipopolysaccharides induced expressions of proinflammatory cytokines TNFa and IL-8, as well as TyrRS-SV7 (~7-fold), which were significantly inhibited by the anti-inflammatory steroid dexamethasone. In contrast, TyrRS-FL and SV8 were only mildly up-regulated (~2-fold) by lipopolysaccharides stimulation. In THP-1 macrophagic cells, the regulation of TyrRS SV7 was observed upon treatment with tumor necrosis factor alpha or interferon gamma at physiologically relevant concentrations, while the TyrRS-FL or TyrRS-SV8 mRNA expressions remained similar to control. These results suggest that TyrRS SV7 plays cytokine-like roles in THP-1 and A549 cells, and has distinct functions from TyrRS FL or the closely related SV8. Objective 3: Investigation of biological role of TyrRS-SV7 (TyrRSE2-4) in human mesenchymal stem cell (HMSC) differentiation - 100% completed We investigated the biological role of TyrRS-SV7 in the HMSC differentiation, which stems from our previous finding of regulated expression of SV7-like protein during HMSC adipogenesis. In this project, we found that TyrRS-SV7 overexpressed in Hela cells was localized to the nucleus. The cell immunostaining followed with microscopy showed that it was co-localized with PARP1 in the nuclei. The co-IP experiments also demonstrated that TyrRS-SV7 was co-IPed with PARP1 and vice versa. The increase of SV7 overexpression resulted in a progressive decrease of PARP1 and PARP1PAR based on the western blot results. These results suggest that SV7 may interact with PARP1 and function as its negative regulator. Using the more physiologically relevant HMSC differentiation system, we found that endogenous SV7-like protein was specifically detected during the HMSC adipogenesis. Its expression was highest in the early differentiation stage and progressively decreased. To further elucidate the biological activity of TyrRS-SV7 on HMSC adipogenesis, we employed the lentiviral vector system for constitutive, long-term expression of TyrRS-SV7 in HMSC. The HMSC adipogenesis was slowed down by the SV7 overexpression in comparison to the mock-transfected control cells, but was not affected by the overexpression of TyrRS-FL or SV8, indicating a specific activity of TyrRS-SV7 on HMSC adipogenesis. The results also demonstrated that TyrRS-SV7 blocked HMSC adipogenesis by down-regulation of PPARγ2 (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma) and its target gene (FABP4, fatty acid-binding protein 4 and adiponectin) expressions. Based on these results, we hypothesized that TyrRS-SV7 may be induced upon stimulation of the splicing machinery, and interact with PARP1 to inhibit its activation of downstream gene expressions, playing biological roles including the inhibition of adipogenesis. The findings from this project provide new insights into novel functions of AARS CNs, and may demonstrate how TyrRS-SV7 adapts the structure for biological roles distinct from the parent FL TyrRS. Supported by this grant, we presented our results in two conferences (The 16th SCBA International Symposium and the AARS2017 conference). Manuscript(s) for novel structure and functions of TyrRS SVs are under preparation. The postdoc supported by this project (Dr. Liting Zhai) also collaborated with several groups on the AARS and SVs project, which leads to two co-authored papers (Am J Hum Genet. 2018 Jul 5;103(1):100-114.; Nat Commun. 2019 Feb 12;10(1):707).

16100015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16100015.value: We previously found that alternative splicing creates two new architectures for TyrRS endogenously. The early findings with the two TyrRS splice variants (SVs) were published in 2016 (Nucleic Acids Res. 2016, 44(3):1247-55). In this project, we further characterized the structures and functions of these SVs. Both SVs were found to secret to the media from cultured cells, supporting that they may be extracellular signaling molecules. In particular, TyrRS-SV7 was up-regulated by lipopolysaccharides treatment of the lung alveolar epithelial cell line A549, which could be inhibited by the anti-inflammatory steroid dexamethasone. In THP-1 differentiated macrophagic cells, SV7 was induced upon treatment with tumor necrosis factor alpha or interferon gamma at physiologically relevant concentrations. Notably, the expressional regulation was not observed or to a much less extent with TyrRS-FL or SV8, suggesting that SV7 is specifically involved in these immune regulatory processes. Moreover, we extensively investigated the biological role of TyrRS-SV7 in differentiation of HMSC. The endogenous SV7-like protein was specifically detected during the HMSC adipogenesis. Its expression was highest in the early differentiation stage and progressively decreased, in a reverse correlation with the adipogenic markers PPARγ2 and FABP4. Interestingly, the overexpression of TyrRS-SV7 but not TyrRS FL or SV8, down-regulated PPARγ2 and its target genes, as well as inhibited the HMSC adipogenesis. It is known that PARP-1 controls the adipogenic transcriptional program. We were able to demonstrate that overexpressed TyrRS-SV7 was co-localized with PARP1 in the nuclei of Hela cells and co-IPed with PARP1. Their direct interaction was confirmed by in vitro GST-pull down assay. These results suggest that TyrRS-SV7 plays a role in the adipogenesis by interacting with PARP1 and inhibiting its activation of downstream adipogenic gene expressions. To investigate the molecular basis of TyrRS-SV7/PARP-1 interactions, we characterized their binding and prepared protein complex samples for high resolution structure determination. We found that the C-terminus of SV7 interacts with the N-terminus of PARP1, primarily the BRCT domain. They demonstrated a weak binding in vitro, indicating a transient signaling interaction. To facilitate formation of complexes, we linked the two proteins for expression and have recently obtained decent crystals for data collection. The complex structure will elucidate the molecular mechanism of biological roles of SV7, and how the new architecture is created through splicing for functions distinct from the parent TyrRS. The research outcomes from this project have been presented in conferences and manuscript(s) are under preparation.

16100015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16100015.value: First, we will make efforts to obtain high-resolution structure of the TyrRS-SV7/PARP1 complex. If the current crystals cannot provide sufficient resolution, we will further optimize crystallization conditions to obtain better quality data. Once we have the molecular details of the interactions, we will verify the findings by mutational studies using in vitro approaches (e.g. ITC, pull-down assay) as well as cell-based assays (e.g. HMSC adipogenesis assay). Second, TyrRS-SV7 is indicated to function as an extracellular signaling molecule involved in the immune-modulation of A549 and THP-1 macrophages. More studies are needed to elucidate the potential receptor target (e.g. by immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry) and signaling pathways (e.g. gene expression analysis, kinase assays) for this function.

16100015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16100015.value: Aminoacyl tRNA synthetases (AARS) are ancient enzymes known to play fundamental roles in protein translation. Recently, accumulating evidence has demonstrated that AARS also exert important non-translational functions in higher eukaryotes. These novel functions can be gained through alternative splicing of AARS genes to create new protein architectures distinct from the parent AARS. More than 200 splice variants (SVs) of AARS genes have been discovered, however, the molecular mechanisms of how they adapt the structures for new functions remain poorly understood. In this project, we focused on two SVs of tyrosyl-tRNA synthetase (TyrRS), and our results suggest that they can function as extracellular signaling molecules. In particular, one SV was demonstrated with a specific inhibitory effect on adipogenesis of human mesenchymal stem cells (HMSC), a function not observed with the parent TyrRS. We elucidated the interaction partner and signaling pathways for this activity, and also obtained crystals of the protein complex for understanding the molecular mechanism. This study established for the first time an activity of the AARS protein in the HMSC differentiation and/or adipocyte development, expanding the functional diversity of AARS. The findings may also lay a foundation for future development of AARS-related therapeutics for regulation of obesity.

16100115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100115.value: 很多間接證據表明，鈣離子在調節脊椎動物心臟發育的過程中具有重要作用。但現時仍欠缺可靠的活體成像數據來揭示初級「心臟區」指定過程和隨後的「心臟發生」期間鈣離子信號的動態。於是在過去兩年間，我們嘗試開發了新的工具，來實現於原位和更長的時間內斑馬魚心臟發育期間之鈣離子動態的可視化。為了描述正常發育心臟中的鈣信號特征并探索這些鈣信號在心臟發育中的功能，我們建立了心臟組織特異表達的鈣緩衝蛋白parvalbumin-α驅動表達生物熒光鈣信號報告基因 aequorin-GFP和 Nano-lantern (Ca2+)的轉基因斑馬魚。此外，我們還建立了轉基因斑馬魚per3-luc和突變體斑馬魚CLOCK1-DN。我們可以藉助這些轉基因斑馬魚來記錄選擇的生物鐘基因的節律性表達圖像并控制基因的開關。因此，我們可以利用斑馬魚這個光學上透明易於成像的脊椎動物模型來探索鈣離子動態，內源性生物鐘和心臟發育之間的複雜關係。在脊椎動物心臟的發育和發生過程中，其生理特征隨時間呈現出巨大的變化，包括血壓，代謝和心跳速率都體現出節律變化。此外，心臟疾病的症狀在一天中也存在明顯的周期性，例如急性心肌梗塞最常見於早晨。這些節律性的改變都與心臟中內在的生物鐘有關。到目前為止我們對於生物鐘的調節，體內帶動節律的各系統性因素，和鈣信號以及生物鐘功能的中斷所造成的潛在影響等方面的了解還很初步。因此，本計劃旨在研究鈣信號通路和生物鐘內在功能對於心臟發育，細胞週期調節，及其失調引起的心臟病形成，和其在心臟的再生及修復中潛在的作用和影響。此研究結果將有助于我們了解鈣信號和心臟中內在生物鐘於心臟發育的作用，並有助於向心臟研究和醫學界展示心臟研究和治療的重要性。

16100115.label: Realisation of objectives
16100115.value: Visualizing the Ca2+ signals generated from complex, three-dimensional organs in vivo poses significant problems and challenges. This is especially so with regard to the heart. This is because of the multiple, and sometimes overlapping roles that Ca2+ plays during the regulation of the development and function of the heart, and how this changes over time from the earliest stages of development and during maturation into the final form of the adult heart. With regard to our first objective, we initially attempted to image Ca2+ signals from the heart of intact zebrafish over time. Using this experimental approach, were able to visualize Ca2+ transients at low resolution from the whole heart in intact embryos via use of the Ca2+-sensitive bioluminescent protein, aequorin, in conjunction with a custom-designed luminescence imaging detector. This technique was initially selected as it allowed for continuous imaging for up to at least 24 hours, and thus was well-suited to record Ca2+ signals over the extended time window required for the heart to develop. This imaging technique, however, does not offer any resolution in the z-axis, and as a result lacks the resolution required to determine which heart specific tissue or cell type was generating the particular Ca2+ transients observed. This, therefore, restricted our proposed detailed exploration of the development function of specific heart based Ca2+ transients. Application of higher resolution single wavelength fluorescence-based confocal microscopy to image the low level Ca2+ signals also resulted in various problems due to the dynamic nature of heart formation and the structural changes that occur within the body of an intact animal. This problem was overcome when we switched to experimenting with excised hearts in culture. These could be more easily imaged using high resolution confocal microscopy, and this approach proved to be successful. A second strategy to overcome the problem of imaging and manipulating Ca2+ signals at the cellular level during the differentiation of cardiomyocytes in the presumptive heart field in an intact organism, was to utilize the differentiation of cultured stem cells to cardiomyocytes, as a simplified experimental model system. To this end, we generated lines of human embryonic stem cells that expressed aequorin and induced them to differentiate into cardiomyocytes while imaging their Ca2+ signaling signature. In order to explore the developmental function of the Ca2+ signals, we also treated: hearts in intact zebrafish, excised hearts in culture, and differentiating embryonic stem cells, with a variety of drugs to modulate the endogenous Ca2+ transients. Our progress is clearly shown in the talks and posters presented at both local and international meetings. We also currently have two working papers that are nearing completion. The first, titled: “The role Ca2+ signaling on heart looping during the early development of zebrafish embryos”, focuses on the role of Ca2+ signaling during heart looping and the regulation of early heart chamber morphology and orientation, whereas the second, titled: “Ca2+ signaling during the development and function of extracted embryonic zebrafish hearts in culture”, focuses on Ca2+ signaling in hearts excised at just ~26 hpf and grown in culture. All of the experiments we undertook were technically challenging in specific ways, and as a result this pushed our Ca2+ imaging abilities to the limits of what is currently possible with the equipment we have available. We believe that we developed strategies to overcome the challenges we faced during the course of the project, and as a result we have made significant progress with regard to the first of our objectives, and have built a solid foundation to continue this work in the future. We also believe that we have made significant progress with regard to exploring possible interactions between Ca2+ signalling and endogenous circadian clock function during the early development and functioning of the zebrafish embryonic heart. This is displayed in our recent submission of a research article titled: “Investigating the effect of the circadian cycle on heartbeat rate and per3 gene expression in the embryonic zebrafish (Danio rerio) following light entrainment”, to the well-respected peer-reviewed journal PLOS ONE. In this article, which is currently under review, we report the relationship between circadian clock oscillation and the expression of the core clock gene period3 (per3). We also describe the clock-mediated regulation of heartbeat rates under different light entrainment regimes. As well as reporting heartbeat rates from intact embryos, we also recorded them from wounded hearts in intact fish, and also from excised hearts under different light/dark conditions. We believe that our findings from this part of the project make a significant contribution to the chronobiology field. This is especially so, due to our discovery regarding the circadian-related activity of one of the perhaps least understood core clock genes, period 3 (per3). Another key finding, which relates to this project objective and is also reported in our manuscript submitted to PLOS ONE, was that the endogenous circadian clock displayed a regulatory role with regard to two key features of heart development, i.e., per3 expression and heartbeat regulation, so early in development. We regard this to be another key discovery during the project. With regard to the third major objective of this project, we have clearly demonstrated that there are daily changes in critical heart events that are related to the endogenous circadian clock in zebrafish hearts. Our new findings demonstrate one of the earliest functional couplings of the circadian pacemaker to a physiologically relevant output during development. This may reflect the fact that upon hatching, zebrafish larvae exhibit a robust day-night difference in swimming activity and consequently raised heartbeat rates in the day may serve a key physiological role, compared to when larvae “sleep” at night. Furthermore, the novel experiments we carried out to explore the effects of heart-wounding on clock activity showed that although the hypothesized clock-based regulation of heartbeat rate was initially disturbed following wounding, the clock resumed control after recovery. This is an issue of major clinical interest, as disruption of heart-clock physiology following a “heart attack” or invasive surgery, has never previously been considered. The new data that we gathered during this project clearly demonstrate that the endogenous circadian clock in the zebrafish heart is working as a molecular oscillator at the earliest stages of development, and that it is also functionally coupled to two major physiologically relevant clock-output processes, the regulation of heartbeat rate, and the expression of the core clock gene, per3. We also have a working paper nearing completion titled: “Daily rhythms in heart rate are intrinsic to the zebrafish heart”, where we present data to suggest that the larval cardiac clock can drive a daily change in heart rate itself and, as such, must be interacting at a cellular level with the Ca2+ oscillations in the cardiomyocytes to generate this daily rhythm. These results suggest a direct coupling of the cardiac clock to daily heartbeat rate changes and, as such, they open up a wide range of future studies relating to how the clock regulates downstream contractility. In conclusion, considering the time-frame allocated, the manpower employed, and the funding made available, we believe that we have realized the overall objectives of the proposal.
