16100115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16100115.value: Zebrafish serve as an effective model system for studying the development and function of the heart as well as the role of the circadian clock in these processes. We demonstrated that after entrainment in a 12-hour light/12-hours dark (LD) cycle, the expression levels of the clock gene, period3 oscillate with the circadian cycle in intact embryos. In addition, the embryonic heartbeat rate also oscillated in LD lighting conditions with respect to the circadian cycle. Furthermore, after LD entrainment, these oscillations were maintained for at least 3 days under constant darkness (DD), but when kept in constant light (LL) after fertilization, no clear oscillations were recorded. When hearts were wounded in vivo and then maintained under LD conditions, the embryos recovered a circadian oscillation in the heartbeat ~48 h after wounding. These new data indicate that the circadian clock appears to play a role in regulating the function of the embryonic zebrafish heart and has a clear impact on daily changes in the heartbeat rate and period3 expression. A manuscript describing these exciting new findings is currently under review in PLOS One (see Part C/Section 8/#19). While the requirement for Ca2+ during normal heart function is well known, more recent evidence suggests that Ca2+ might also play a key role in heart morphogenesis. Thus, having a better understanding of the role of Ca2+ signalling in normal heart development might help identify novel therapies for congenital and acquired heart diseases, and indicate possible options for pharmacological/genetic intervention to promote heart repair and regeneration. We have identified a series of Ca2+ oscillations generated in in vivo hearts early in development. Embryos were injected with the fluorescent Ca2+ indicator, calcium green-1 dextran, at the 1-cell stage and then the heart was excised at ~26 hpf using well-established protocols. These data are currently being written up into a manuscript (see Part C/Section 8/#20). In addition, to investigate if Ca2+ signaling might play a role in the development of the heart, 1-cell stage cmlc2-GFP transgenic embryos (Tg(gal4)cmlc2:GFP), which specifically express GFP in the cardiac muscle, were injected with the Ca2+ chelator, BAPTA, at different concentrations. Our results suggest that Ca2+ signaling might be important for heart looping and the generation of the heart chamber volume, and thus the overall morphology and function of the developing and maturing heart. These data are currently being written up into a manuscript (see Part C/Section 8/#21).

16100115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16100115.value: It was very exciting to find that the circadian clock acts as a molecular oscillator at the earliest stages of zebrafish development, and that it is functionally coupled to the heartbeat, (a major physiologically relevant clock-output process) at this young age. Another highly relevant finding was that when the heart was wounded in intact embryos, then although the clock-based regulation of heartbeat rate was perturbed immediately after wounding, the rate and some of the rhythmicity resumed within just ~48 hours. This is an issue of major clinical interest, as disruption of heart-clock physiology following a “heart attack” or invasive surgery, has never previously been considered. It would therefore be of intense interest to develop our project further to identify the molecular mechanisms that enable the zebrafish heart to survive significant wounding followed by regeneration and investigate what role the circadian clock might play in regulating these complex processes. Our new data also suggest that the advantages of experimentation using an organ in vitro during the very early stages of development, might in the future be extended to the heart, and thus help us to better understand heart defects that arise during the earliest stages of cardiogenesis.

16100115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16100115.value: Despite recent medical advancements, heart disease remains a leading cause of death worldwide. While the requirement for calcium ions (Ca2+) during normal heart function is well known, more recent evidence suggests that Ca2+ also play a key role in heart morphogenesis. It is also well-established that the circadian rhythm can influence heart function as the chances of having sudden cardiac malfunction are higher in the morning and evening than in the middle of the day. Using zebrafish as our animal model, we demonstrate that Ca2+ signaling plays a role in a key aspect of heart development, called heart looping. We also showed that the circadian clock works as a molecular oscillator at the earliest stages of zebrafish development, and that it is functionally coupled to the heartbeat, (a major physiologically relevant clock-output process) at this young age. Also, when the heart was wounded in intact embryos then some of the rhythmicity resumed within just ~48 hours. Having a better understanding of the role of Ca2+ signaling in normal heart development might help identify novel therapies for congenital and acquired heart diseases. Furthermore, the development of novel chronotherapies might help to alleviate the onset of heart disease.

16100215.label: Project Objectives
16100215.value: Proteomic profiling of the CDK5RAP2-associated pool of the γTuRC To generate a comprehensive map of proteins in the CDK5RAP2-bound γTuRC, we will initiate a systematic search for cellular proteins that interact with the complex. Tandem affinity purification will be used to reduce the background of non-specifically copurified proteins. The γTuRC-binding domain of CDK5RAP2 (i.e., 51–100) will be engineered to contain dual affinity tags for two sequential isolations of the γTuRC and its associating proteins. Following isolation, the complex components will be identified by mass spectrometry. As a complementary approach to map interactions in the CDK5RAP2-bound γTuRC, we will employ proximity-dependent biotin identification (BioID), a method that identifies proximity interactions in living cells. In both methods, a γTuRC-binding deficient mutant (i.e., F75A) of CDK5RAP2 will serve as a control. After identification of the complex components, we will validate the identified interactions and carry out functional characterization to reveal the physiological consequences of the interactions. Characterizing the association of PolD1 with the γTuRC The assays are planned to address the following questions on the association of PolD1 with the γTuRC. First, we will determine whether the smaller subunits of Polδ are involved in the association of PolD1 with the γTuRC. Second, we will delineate the sequence and structural elements involved in association with the γTuRC. Third, we will explore how PolD1 binds to the γTuRC by searching for the complex components that interact with or are in close proximity with PolD1. The interactions will be tested in assays in vitro and in living cells. Fourth, we will investigate the potential role of PolD1 in the binding of the γTuRC to CDK5RAP2 and Nedd1. Based on the data from our preliminary study, we hypothesize that PolD1 may inhibit the binding of Nedd1 to the complex. Results from the above assays will facilitate understanding the function and regulation of the γTuRC. Investigating the function of PolD1 in γTuRC-dependent microtubule organization The experiments are designed to investigate the role of PolD1 in γTuRC-mediated nucleation and organization of microtubules. First, we will test the effect of PolD1 on the γTuRC in an in vitro microtubule nucleation assay. PolD1 may inhibit γTuRC-dependent nucleation even in the presence of CDK5RAP2. Second, we will examine the protein expression, subcellular localization, and localization dynamics of PolD1 throughout the cell cycle. The temporal and spatial patterns will help understand the actions of PolD1 in microtubule-dependent events. Third, we will silence the expression of PolD1 by RNAi or will knockout PolD1 using the CRISPR-Cas9 gene-editing technique in cell cultures. We will then examine the potential effect on cellular microtubules during the cell cycle. In addition, the centrosome-based nucleation of microtubules will be tested in microtubule regrowth assays or by time-lapse microscopy of microtubule growth in an EB1-GFP stable line. The above experiments will reveal how PolD1 in association with the γTuRC functions in the organization of cellular microtubules.

16100215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100215.value: 細胞微管骨架在真核細胞的胞質中起關鍵的組織作用，因此從細胞增殖到形態的形成，其在各種細胞活動中發揮重要功能。在動物細胞中，微管生長的啟動和隨後微管組織成為有序的排列都有賴於γ¬微管蛋白環狀復合體（γTuRC）的參與。γTuRC是一種多分子的大型復合體，其核心成分γ¬微管蛋白是一種於真核生物中的保守蛋白。由γTuRC介導的微管組裝有著嚴格的空間和時間控制。然而，γTuRC功能的調控機制尚不清楚。並且，對γTuRC的組成成分還沒有充分的了解。 本實驗室一直專注於研究微管組織和調控的分子機制，前期工作包括識別CDK5RAP2作為一個中心體蛋白、並鑒定其在γTuRC定位於動物細胞中最主要的微管組織中心—中心體過程中的功能。同時，CDK5RAP2還激發γTuRC的微管成核活性。我們近期的研究發現，與CDK5RAP2結合的γTuRC含有DNA聚合酶δ的催化亞基PolD1，初步的研究結果還顯示PolD1對其結合的γTuRC起到活性抑制的作用。基於這些實驗結果，本研究計劃致力於研究CDK5RAP2結合的γTuRC以及PolD1與γTuRC的相互結合，並設計一系列實驗來達致以下目標：（1）對與CDK5RAP2結合的γTuRC的分子組成進行一個綜合分析，（2）研究PolD1與γTuRC的相互結合，（3）闡明PolD1在γTuRC中的功能以及由此而導致的於微管組織中的作用。我們將應用涉及多學科的實驗方法來解決這些問題。 本研究計劃旨在揭示γTuRC作為微管的主要成核因子的作用機制及其所參與的分子網絡，這項工作還將揭示一種全新的PolD1功能，將不同於其眾所周知的作為一種保守蛋白在DNA復制和修復中的重要作用。另外，該項研究將提供與CDK5RAP2相結合γTuRC的蛋白組分完整圖譜，此圖譜可為研究參與γTuRC功能的分子提供新的視角。總之，這項研究工作所產生的成果將加深我們對於微管組織在各種細胞活動中的分子調控原理的認識。由於微管調控的缺陷已知與很多人類疾病有關，本項研究有可能為新的治療藥物的開發做出貢獻。

16100215.label: Realisation of objectives
16100215.value: Objective #1. Proteomic profiling of the CDK5RAP2-associated pool of the γTuRC We have fulfilled this objective by using mass spectrometry-based approaches to identify proteins that interact with γTuRCs and to reveal post-translational modifications occurred on γTuRC components. To isolate γTuRCs at high purity from mammalian cells, we exploited the specific interaction between γTuRCs and the γTuRC-mediated nucleation activator (γTuNA) domain of CDK5RAP2, and we carried out the isolation by using the tandem affinity purification method that utilized two high affinity tags (i.e. FLAG and streptavidin-binding peptide) fused to the γTuNA. Following isolation, we identified a number of proteins by mass spectrometry, and they include cytoskeletal proteins, adaptor proteins and chaperone proteins, proteins involved in the proteasome-dependent degradation, and proteins of unknown function. These results point to new directions of the research on γTuRCs. In addition, we used mass spectrometry to determine phosphorylation sites on γ-tubulin and revealed γ-tubulin phosphorylation in vivo at three cysteine residues, in addition to the known sites. Using a mutational approach, we found that these site-specific phosphorylations of γ-tubulin exert a control on the following events: γ-tubulin assembly into γTuRCs, γTuRC-induced microtubule nucleation, and centrosome duplication. Collectively, these results establish Cys phosphorylation as a functionally important modification of γ-tubulin. In summary, following the identification of interactions involving γTuRCs and protein phosphorylation of γ-tubulin, the functional characterization revealed new regulatory properties of γTuRCs and several projects have been initiated to study the functional significance of the identified interactions and phosphorylation. Objective #2. Characterizing the association of PolD1 with the γTuRC We have fulfilled this objective by carrying out the following binding characterizations. First, we performed reciprocal immunoprecipitation of γTuRCs and PolD1. Immunoprecipitation of γTuRCs through the γTuRC core component GCP6 or GCP4 co-immunoprecipitated PolD1. Similarly, we detected γTuRCs in the immunoprecipitates of PolD1. Furthermore, we found that PolD1 interacts with intact γTuRCs, but does not bind to its composing subcomplex γTuSC. Disassembly of γTuRCs by RNAi-mediated depletion of GCP4 drastically diminished the co-immunoprecipitation of the γTuSC components γ-tubulin, GCP2, and GCP3 with PolD1. These results revealed that PolD1 specifically recognizes γTuRCs. To verify the direct association of PolD1 and γTuRCs, we conducted a binding test of recombinant PolD1 and isolated γTuRCs. The recombinant PolD1 protein was expressed in HEK293T cells and then purified under a stringent condition to remove all contaminant proteins; γTuRCs were isolated at high purity by tandem affinity purification according to our established protocol. After reconstitution of PolD1 and the γTuRCs, anti-PolD1 immunoprecipitation readily coimmunoprecipitated γTuRCs. This result indicates that PolD1 interacts directly with γTuRCs. PolD1 possesses DNA polymerase and exonuclease activities. To test whether these functions are required for PolD1 association with γTuRCs, we used two PolD1 mutants, the polymerase-deficient mutant S605del (an in-frame deletion of S605 at the polymerase active site) and the exonuclease-deficient mutant D515V, in γTuRC-binding assays; we found that both mutants co-immunoprecipitated γTuRCs at similar activities as wild-type PolD1. Therefore, PolD1 binds to γTuRCs in a manner independent of its enzymatic functions. To test the effect of PolD1 on its associated γTuRCs, we conducted microtubule nucleation assays using recombinant PolD1 and isolated γTuRCs. The purified γTuRCs exhibited a low level of microtubule-nucleating activity, and this activity was stimulated upon binding to the γTuNA of CDK5RAP2. We assayed microtubule nucleation of γTuNA-stimulated γTuRCs in the presence of recombinant PolD1 at various concentrations, and we found that PolD1 inhibited γTuRC-induced microtubule nucleation in a dose-dependent manner, with the IC50 being 98 nM and ~90% of the nucleating activity being inhibited upon adding 356 nM PolD1. We then tested PolD1 inhibition toward CDK5RAP2-free γTuRCs and observed similar potency of PolD1 toward the γTuRCs. In the assays, we also tested the D515V and S605del mutants and another Pol  subunit, PolD2. The proteins of these PolD1 mutants and PolD2 were prepared from expressions in HEK293T in the manner as wild-type PolD1. Both D515V and S605del mutants exhibited similar inhibitory activities as wild-type PolD1, whereas PolD2 did not show any inhibition toward γTuRCs. We conclude that PolD1 specifically inhibits the microtubule-nucleating activity of γTuRCs and that this inhibitory activity is independent of the PolD1 DNA polymerase and exonuclease activities. Objective #3. Investigating the function of PolD1 in γTuRC-dependent microtubule organization We have fulfilled this objective by examining the effects of altering PolD1 expression levels on cellular microtubules. We performed overexpression and RNAi-mediated expression suppression of PolD1 and found that both overexpression and RNAi-mediated depletion did not affect the localization of γTuRCs to centrosomes and the Golgi complex, which are the major microtubule-organizing centers. Next, we examined microtubule regrowth after cold-induced depolymerization. In PolD1-overexpressing cells, Golgi-associated regrowth was potently inhibited and centrosome-based regrowth was reduced at a moderate level, as compared with the regrowth in control cells. We also tested the two PolD1 mutants, S605del and D515V, and observed similar effects as wild-type PolD1 on the regrowth of cellular microtubules. We then effectively suppressed PolD1 expression by RNAi and performed the microtubule regrowth assay. Whereas the PolD1 depletion strongly increased Golgi-associated microtubule nucleation, the depletion did not markedly affect centrosome-based microtubule nucleation. Together, these results indicate that PolD1 controls microtubule nucleation at the Golgi complex by a mechanism that is independent of its exonuclease and polymerase activities. Golgi-associated microtubules play important roles in the assembly and maintenance of the Golgi structure. PolD1 knockdown increased the density of Golgi-derived microtubules, caused an expansion of the Golgi region, and reduced the compactness of the Golgi. Conversely, PolD1 overexpression considerably reduced the size of the Golgi complex and the amount of Golgi-derived microtubules. We evaluated the role of PolD1 in Golgi reassembly after nocodazole-induced disassembly. During the reassembly, Golgi- and centrosome-derived microtubules facilitate the fusion of Golgi ministacks dispersed in the cytoplasm (referred to as the Golgi stage) and the translocation of the fused stacks toward the centrosome (referred to as the centrosome stage), respectively. We found that PolD1 depletion impaired Golgi assembly at the centrosome-stage but not at the Golgi-stage. This observation supports the notion that a balance of the actions produced by Golgi- and centrosome-derived microtubules is essential for proper Golgi reassembly. Because the Golgi complex and its associated microtubules play a pivotal role in cell polarization and directional migration, we performed a scratch-wounding assay to assess the role of PolD1 in cell polarization and directional migration. RNAi-mediated PolD1 depletion reduced cell migration into the wound. To gain insights into the migration defect, we monitored Golgi reorientation in the assay and found that over a few hours after scratch wounding, the PolD1-depleted cells showed drastically lower fractions with their Golgi reoriented toward the leading edge than did the control cells. Our data revealed that the ability of the Golgi to reorganize during reorientation is impaired in the absence of PolD1.

16100215.label: Major findings and research outcome
16100215.value: In this study, we systematically analyzed γTuRCs that were isolated by the γTuRC-mediated nucleation activator (γTuNA) domain of CDK5RAP2. From the isolated γTuRCs, we identified proteins of diverse functions and revealed previously unknown phosphorylation of γ-tubulin. These identified interactions and phosphorylation events provide new insights into the regulation of γTuRCs. Among the identified proteins is the DNA polymerase  catalytic subunit (PolD1). We showed that PolD1 physically associates with γTuRCs and blocks γTuRC-induced microtubule nucleation, and that this PolD1 action is required for the control of microtubule growth at the Golgi complex, but is dispensable for the control of the growth on centrosomes. By manipulating the level of PolD1, we set the experimental conditions required to alter the growth of Golgi-derived microtubules, and we found that the induced changes in Golgi-derived microtubules directly affected the Golgi structure. The suppression of PolD1 expression promoted Golgi-associated microtubule growth and resulted in an increase in the size and a decrease in the compactness of the Golgi complex. By contrast, PolD1 overexpression induced Golgi structural defects that were highly similar to those produced by RNAi-mediated depletion of AKAP450 or CLASPs, which were shown to remove Golgi-derived microtubules. PolD1 depletion caused defects in Golgi assembly and reorientation and cell directional migration. Given that the PolD1 depletion did not markedly affect centrosome-based microtubule growth, the increased growth of Golgi-derived microtubules would have changed the relative proportion of centrosome- and Golgi-derived microtubules. We proposed that the maintenance of a balance between these two microtubule populations is required for proper Golgi assembly and reorientation. Collectively, these findings indicate that PolD1 participates in the organization of the Golgi structure by controlling Golgi-associated microtubule growth. PolD1 is well known for performing housekeeping functions in the nucleus. We showed that PolD1 shuttles between the nucleus and the cytoplasm, and identified the nuclear import and export mechanisms of PolD1. PolD1 harbors two nuclear-localization signals that are known to mediate nuclear import through the classical importin pathway, and PolD1 exits the nucleus through the conserved CRM1-dependent export pathway. Collectively, these findings uncover the nucleocytoplasmic transport mechanisms of PolD1. Overall, this study provides new molecular insights into a wide variety of cellular functions including cell division, movement, and morphogenesis. In addition, this work reveals a new function of PolD1, a protein with well documented functions in DNA replication and repair.

16100215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16100215.value: Our current findings warrant the investigation of the interaction between γTuRCs and identified associating proteins. Now is the time to further explore on their assemblies in model cell systems to define protein associations in the complexes and to understand the function of the assemblies. As a result, it will provide unprecedented insight into various microtubule-dependent cellular events. The findings of this project also warrant further investigation of the identified γ-tubulin phosphorylation at cysteine residues. Protein Cys phosphorylation has only been known in eukaryotes to form a catalytic intermediate of protein tyrosine phosphatases, although Cys phosphorylation plays roles in gene transcription control and cell regulation in bacteria. Our identification of γ-tubulin phosphorylation on Cys shows for the first time that Cys phosphorylation is a mode of stable protein modification in eukaryotes.

16100215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16100215.value: In animal cells, γ-tubulin ring complexes (γTuRCs) mediate microtubule nucleation and anchoring at microtubule-organizing centers such as centrosomes and the Golgi complex. However, the mechanism by which the microtubule-nucleating activity of γTuRCs is controlled has thus far remained unknown. In a systematic search, we identified functionally diverse proteins that associate with γTuRCs and also revealed phosphorylation events occurred on the γTuRC core component γ-tubulin. One of the identified proteins is the DNA polymerase  catalytic subunit (PolD1), a conserved protein that is well recognized for its functions in DNA replication and repair. We demonstrated that PolD1 inhibits the microtubule-nucleating activity of γTuRCs. PolD1 controls microtubule growth at the Golgi complex, a major non-centrosomal microtubule-organizing center that organizes almost half of all cellular microtubules. Further, PolD1 is involved in Golgi assembly and structural organization, and cell polarization and directional migration, all of which involve Golgi-associated microtubules. Collectively, this study revealed a mechanism that is likely to be conserved in eukaryotes to control γTuRC-mediated microtubule nucleation. These findings are not only useful for understanding the mechanisms of various microtubule-dependent cellular activities, but also enhance our knowledge of PolD1, a major enzyme in DNA replication and repair.

16100415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100415.value: The last few decades have seen the rapid emergence and proliferation of antibiotic resistant pathogenic bacteria, so-called “superbugs” that pose enormous danger to public health. Unfortunately, our development of new antibiotics has not kept pace with the bacteria’s ingenuity. The dire situation elicited a recent warning of a “post-antibiotic era” from the World Health Organization. The combined use of multiple antibiotics with synergistic effects is one of the many avenues to prolong the useful lifespan of an antibiotic. However, the lack of knowledge about how such synergistic effects arise at the molecular level makes it difficult to design effective therapies. This project aims to investigate how methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), one of the most prevalent and well-known superbugs, responds to antibiotic stress. In particular, we are interested in the combination of oxacillin, a beta-lactam antibiotic that has lost its effectiveness against MRSA, and a novel candidate drug SIPI-8294, which together exhibit strong synergistic effects against MRSA in vitro. Interestingly, SIPI-8294 has no inhibitory activity itself, and exhibits synergy only with beta-lactams but not other classes of antibiotics. Given that this drug combination has no appreciable synergy against methicillin-susceptible S. aureus, we hypothesize that the synergy arises due to yet-to-be-determined interference of the normal resistance mechanism of MRSA against oxacillin. Following the systems biology paradigm, we believe that such synergistic effects arise from a complex interplay of numerous cellular components and are best studied by high-throughput methods. Building upon our previous work studying the proteome changes of different S. aureus strains against oxacillin, we will employ state-of-the-art mass spectrometry (MS) technology to observe globally the changes in protein expression levels in MRSA cells under various drug treatments, and perform bioinformatics analysis to identify key proteins and pathways that underlie the synergistic effects. Transcriptomic and metabolomic experiments will follow to validate and supplement the findings. By taking a systems approach to testing our hypothesis, we expect to simultaneously unravel the chain of interactions triggered by the drugs, potentially leading to new hypotheses about the action mechanism of our particular drug combination. We also hope to establish an effective strategy of using proteomics to study antibiotic resistance, for which others can use as a model. Given that proteomics has yet to be extensively applied to study antibiotic resistance, we believe that it is timely to take advantage of our expertise in this methodology to address this problem of great impact on human health. 在過去的幾十年裡，多重耐藥的致病菌，即所謂的“超級病菌”，迅速出現，對公眾健康構成巨大危害。不幸的是，人類發展的新抗生素已跟不上細菌的巧思。這嚴峻的形勢令世界衛生組織不得已發出“後抗生素時代”的警告。多種具有協同作用抗生素的組合使用是延長抗生素有用壽命其中一個途徑。然而，我們對於這種協同效應是如何產生的，往往一知半解，使得難以設計有效的治療方法。 該項目旨在研究最普遍的超級病菌之一的耐甲氧西林金黃葡萄球菌（MRSA），如何抵禦抗生素的壓力。我們特別感興趣的是一個抗生素組合：苯唑西林(一種已經失去了對付MRSA的效力的 β-內酰胺)和一種新的候選藥物SIPI-8294。這一抗生素組合表現出對MRSA體外有很強的協同效應。有趣的是，SIPI-8294本身不具有抗活菌性，而協同作用僅限於β-內酰胺類型的抗生素。鑑於這種藥物組合具有針對甲氧西林敏感的金黃葡萄球菌沒有明顯的協同作用，我們推測這種協同作用的產生是基於對MRSA抵禦苯唑西林的機制的干擾。 在系統生物學的思維下，我們認為這樣的協同效應產生於眾多的細胞組分的複雜的相互作用，而該等作用須用高通量方法去闡析。我們將建基於我們蛋白質組學上的研究成果，採用先進設備及最先進的質譜（MS）技術，全面觀察MRSA細胞在各種藥物作用下所有蛋白質的表達水平的變化 ，並進行生物信息學分析，以識別關鍵的蛋白質和其在協同作用中所扮演的角色。我們將用轉錄組學和代謝組學的實驗去驗證和補充調查結果。我們預期此研究項目將揭開抗生素組合引發的連鎖效應，可能提出對此藥物組合的作用機理的新假說。我們也希望建立以蛋白質組學研究抗生素耐藥性的有效策略，成為日後此種研究的楷模。 鑑於蛋白質組學尚未在研究抗生素耐藥性中得到廣泛的應用，我們認為這是利用我們在蛋白質組學上的心得來解決這個對人類健康造成巨大影響問題的大好時機。

16100415.label: Realisation of objectives
16100415.value: The captioned project has been completed with full realization of the objectives. Objective 1 Our first objective is to study the mechanism underlying the synergistic bactericidal effect of SIPI-8294 and oxacillin on MRSA by detecting changes in the MRSA proteome upon individual and combined drug treatments by quantitative proteomics. This includes adapting and optimizing existing methods for studying gram-positive bacteria using shotgun proteomics methods, and particularly to profile membrane- and cell wall-bound proteins efficiently and reproducibly. This objective has been completed and the outcome has been described in the Interim Progress Report. Briefly, we employed label-free quantitative proteomics analysis of methicillin-resistant S. aureus cells’ response to a synergistic drug combination, oxacillin and SIPI-8294. Our results showed that 200 proteins were differentially expressed in SIPI-8294/oxacillin-treated cells, relative to the control. Hierarchical clustering analysis of differentially expressed proteins under different treatments revealed that SIPI-8294/oxacillin elicits very different responses from the individual drugs or the non-synergistic erythromycin/oxacillin combination. Bioinformatic analysis indicated that the synergistic effect can be further traced to a disruption in oxidation-reduction homeostasis and cell wall biosynthesis. These results were published as a full research article in Scientific Report. As the project evolved, we have now shifted gears to study antibiotic persistence by proteomics, which is far less understood compared to resistance, but poses equally daunting challenges in managing chronic bacterial infections. It has been widely conjectured, with preliminary evidence shown in some studies, that persistence plays a critical role in the development of resistance. Another reason is that unlike resistance, persistence is thought of as a phenotypic state, and the mechanism cannot be traced to resistance mutations. Persistence is also likely more general as a bet hedging strategy in bacteria, and if it could be better understood, could lead to interventions that are more universal and not as specific to the antibiotic. Because of the nature of the phenomenon, proteomics has a unique advantage in unraveling the mechanism of persistence, and with our expertise, we are better positioned to create impact than if we had continued in resistance. Indeed we have made excellent progress in a short time, having already published 3 papers on studying antibiotic persistence with proteomics with more to come. We used E. coli as the model system for the persistence study thus far, mainly because it is the system used by other researchers. However, the M. Phil. student trained in the persistence project, Jordy E. Sulaiman, has now begun proteomic investigations on the persistence of MRSA under vancomycin and daptomycin treatment, with and without a co-drug (rifampin), for his Ph. D. thesis, perhaps coming full circle to our original plan to tackle the problem of MRSA infections. Therefore, this original project has also led to high-impact research in a related topic, which is greatly facilitated by the technological platform and know-how we developed in this project for bacterial proteomics. Objective 2 Our second objective is to investigate the upstream transcriptional regulators and the downstream metabolites involved in the synergistic effects of SIPI-8294/oxacillin on MRSA, based on the proteomics results obtained by Objective 1. Our results in Objective 1 did not reveal potential key transcriptional regulators to warrant further study. This may be due to the low abundance of these factors, or that the regulatory responses are mediated by post-translational modifications rather than abundance changes. However, we decided to measure the transcript levels of several proteins relevant to antibiotic resistance by real-time polymerase chain reaction, so as to validate our findings at the protein level. These results are also included in the Scientific Reports paper. To study metabolite changes, we developed an effective protocol to perform metabolic profiling in bacterial cells using the LC-MS platform. To that end, we have purchased (using internal funding) and installed a new LC-MS system, Sciex TripleTOF 4600, in 2016. A postdoctoral researcher and an M.Phil. student, Zichen Yuan, were recruited to develop the method for metabolite profiling from bacterial samples. As Escherichia coli is a more convenient model experimentally and has a more complete metabolomics database (ECMDB), it was used in method development to optimize the sample preparation and LC-MS protocols. The method development work has led to a conference presentation (Yuan, Z. et al., ASMS, 2018). Using the method developed, we proceeded to observe the metabolome changes of MSSA and MRSA under oxacillin treatment. These results were presented in a conference (Liu, J., et al., ASMS 2018) and written up as a manuscript (Liu, J. et al. “Nontargeted metabolomics reveals the global adaptations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus under oxacillin stress,” in preparation). Efforts are still ongoing to find a suitable home for this paper. In brief, it was discovered that consistent with our proteomics data, the MSSA metabolome is more widely dysregulated than the MRSA one under sub-lethal doses of oxacillin treatment. Among the affected metabolites, panthothenate, a precursor to CoA synthesis, was found most up-regulated in MRSA, which also confirms our conclusion from proteomics regarding the importance of this biosynthetic pathway in the resistance mechanism. Overall, the data seems to indicate the antibiotic’s global impact on the metabolism of the cells. A limitation of this study was that a big majority of differentially changed features in the LC-MS profiles remain unidentified in the non-targeted approach that we used. This is primarily due to the limited knowledge about the S. aureus metabolome. Although we made use of metabolite databases for other organisms to aid identification, it is likely that they do not adequately cover the S. aureus metabolome. At this moment, a non-targeted approach for metabolomics for a non-model organism is perhaps still short of what is needed for a truly comprehensive investigation.

16100415.label: Major findings and research outcome
16100415.value: The major research outcome of this project was the method development in bacterial proteomics, and biological insights gained by applying proteomics to study the antibiotic responses of pathogenic bacteria. The synergistic effect of oxacillin and an erythromycin derivative, SIPI-8295, was studied by quantitative proteomics. Hierarchical clustering analysis of differentially expressed proteins under different treatments revealed that SIPI-8294/oxacillin elicits very different responses from the individual drugs or the non-synergistic erythromycin/oxacillin combination. Bioinformatic analysis revealed that SIPI-8295 reduces the expression of key proteins in the resistance mechanism of MRSA against beta-lactams, and additionally disrupts the cells’ oxidation-reduction homeostatis and cell wall biosynthesis. A metabolomics study on oxacillin-treated MRSA cells was also conducted, which provided corroborating data to validate the findings from proteomics. Although the original proposal was more narrow in studying the responses of MRSA towards a specific antibiotic combination, we have since expanded our effort to other systems, in particular in the study of antibiotic persistence. In this case, we were able to use proteomics to show that persisters down-regulated many growth-related processes, including carbohydrate metabolism, fatty acid and amino acid biosynthesis, but up-regulated selected membrane proteins, suggesting that persisters are not merely dormant cells but have active adaptation mechanism to survive prolonged antibiotic treatment. Another study investigated E. coli populations with elevated persister fractions obtained from cyclic antibiotic treatment (mimicking clinical treatment regimes). Several key proteins that appear to affect persistence were identified by proteomics without prior knowledge. Another outcome of the project was the training of one postdoctoral researcher, Dr. Jingjing Liu, and two M.Phil. students, Zichen Yuan and Jordy Sulaiman. Dr. Liu has learned high-throughput profiling skills to accompany her traditional analytical chemistry training, and has now taken up a faculty position in mainland China. Jordy Sulaiman is continuing onto his Ph. D. study with the skills that he learned, on the same topic.

16100415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16100415.value: As described in the Realisation of Objectives section, we believe the project was the first step in an ongoing effort for us to apply proteomics and metabolomics to study the antibiotic responses of pathogenic bacteria, of which antibiotic resistance is only one aspect in the vexing challenges faced by clinicians. Proteomics, despite its promise and relevance to the problem, remain under-utilized in this field, and we are by all accounts among the first researchers to venture into this topic with the proteomic toolkit, especially in the study of persistence. Therefore, we believe the potential for new discovery and clinical impact is high. Our current plan is to continue our study of persistence by proteomics, with more in-depth investigations into the mechanism of persister formation and resuscitation, and how we can disrupt that process by targeting certain proteins. We also have plans to look at the more clinically relevant system of S. aureus, and how S. aureus persisters cope with vancomycin and daptomycin treatment, with or without the co-drug rifampin.

16100415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16100415.value: The last few decades have seen the rapid emergence and proliferation of antibiotic resistant pathogenic bacteria, so-called “superbugs” that pose enormous danger to public health. The combined use of multiple antibiotics with synergistic effects is one of the many avenues to combat such bacterial infections or to slow down the emergence of resistance. However, the lack of knowledge about how such synergistic effects arise at the molecular level makes it difficult to design effective therapies. Proteomics and metabolomics, the systematic and high-throughput identification and quantification of all proteins and all metabolites in a cell, respectively, has advanced rapidly in recently years, but this technology has not been fully utilized to study this complex problem that demands a systems-level view of the system. In this project, we developed the experimental and computational methodology for bacterial proteomics and metabolomics, and applied it to study the responses of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) an important pathogen, against a synergistic drug combination. Insights of how a new candidate drug SIPI-8294 disrupted the normal resistance mechanism of MRSA were obtained. This project has also led to follow-up investigations of a related phenomenon of antibiotic persistence, using the methodology we developed.

16101015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101015.value: 总合草苔虫（Bugula neritina）是一个众所周知的海洋苔藓虫类，因为：1）它是全世界最高丰度的软组织附着生物，2）它是一个有名的具有抗肿瘤和加强记忆活性的药物bryostatins的最初始的来源，3）它是常用的在抗污损实验中检测抗污损化合物活性的模式物种。通过与其它几个常见的污损生物（例如，纹藤壶，华美盘管虫和翡翠贻贝）的幼虫附着变态过程的比较，总合草苔虫的幼虫附着过程有很大的不同。首先，总合草苔虫的幼虫可以在任何的介质上附着，而其他的物种往往只在合适的介质上附着。其次，总合草苔虫的幼虫附着过程不要任何环境化学信号的诱导，而其他的物种往往都需要。第三，在幼虫的附着变态的过程中，其他的物种需要粘合剂的分泌和矿化的辅助，而总合草苔虫的这两个过程都不是特别明显。最后，总合草苔虫的幼虫以卵黄作为主要的营养来源，而且拥有一个很短的浮游幼虫期（1到6小时），而且可以在释放出来30分钟以内就有能力附着；相反其他的物种的浮游幼虫期长达一周甚至一个月。综上所述，总合草苔虫应该具有和其他的污损生物不一样的调控幼虫附着变态的信号通路。所以，这个物种应该是一个研究幼虫附着变态的理想的生物。 我们实验室自从1996年开始一直从事研究有关硬壳污损生物（可形成钙质的壳或者管）和软组织的污损生物（不能形成比较坚硬的结构）的幼虫附着的研究。我们到目前为止取得了一下的一些显著成果：1）我们找到并鉴定到了一些有效的化学信号，来诱导或者抑制纹藤壶，总合草苔虫以及华美盘管虫幼虫附着；2）我们针对以上这三种生物以及其他四种生物构建了蛋白质组学和转录组学的研究方法及对应数据库；3）在这7种物种当中，我们鉴定到了一系列的基因，蛋白和信号通路参与整个幼虫附着的过程；4）我们发现了在纹藤壶里面NO和p38 MAPK 信号通路调控了整个幼虫附着变态过程，并且这两个信号通路可以互相串联影响沟通。我们目前初步的结果表明NO信号通路也会参与到总合草苔虫的幼虫附着过程当中，但是结果却与纹藤壶及华美盘管虫相反。而且，该通路在总合草苔虫当中的具体的分子机理仍然不清楚。由于总合草苔虫展示出来与纹藤壶及华美盘管虫完全不一样的幼虫附着的现象，因此，我们推断在总合草苔虫的幼虫附着变态当中，NO与其上游的HSP90信号通路同时跟其下游的cGMP和PKG信号通路也会相互作用。为了证实这个假设，我们决定进行以下的几方面的研究：1）采用基因特异的抑制剂的方法来看NO信号通路在总合草苔虫幼虫附着过程当中的作用；2）调查NO信号通路的上、下游的信号通路是否也参与总合草苔虫幼虫附着过程；3）NO通路与MAPK通路会串联沟通来调控总合草苔虫幼虫附着过程的机制。我们将通过一系列的基于上述假设的生物学测试实验试图阐明与NO信号通路有关的信号通路网络来调控该幼虫附着的过程，并将得到的结果同其他的2种生物（即藤壶和华美盘管虫）进行对比。我们的这些研究将会为基于靶位点的环境无公害的抗污损涂料的设计带来新的思路和策略。

16101015.label: Realisation of objectives
16101015.value: To realize the objective 1 (to reveal the role of NO signaling pathway in larval settlement of Bugula neritina), we first used the cyprid larvae of the barnacles to study the role of NO pathway in larval settlement because cyprid larval settlement requires chemical cue to be triggered and much easier for us to determine the starting point and end-point, larvae are also much bigger. The purpose of this part of work was to explore the possible role of NO pathways in larval settlement of a hard fouler first and to accumulate experience for working on the soft fouler Bugula neritina. What we found was that when cyprid larvae of the barnacle Amphibalanus amphitrite with a NO donor sodium nitroprusside (SNP), the expression of arginine kinase (AK) were increased. Since AK catalyzes the chemical reaction of L-arginine and ATP into N (omega)-phospho-L-arginine and ADP and L-arginine is also the substrate for NOS to produce NO, the upregulation of AK might be attributed to the elevated level of NO caused by the SNP treatment, which inhibits the activity and expression of NOS and thereby suppressed the consumption of L-arginine. Subsequently, additional L-arginine required more AK for utilization. Alternatively, NO/cGMP pathway activates fatty acid _-oxidation and enhances the production of ROIs (reactive oxygen intermediates). SNP treatments would increase the level of ROIs and further elevate the level of AK due to oxidative stress [28]. In short, it suggested that AK shall be the up-stream regulator of NO pathway. Furthermore, SNP treatment also led to the upregulation of HSPs in A. Amphitrite larvae, suggesting that HSP70 and HSP 90 likely participate in NO-based signal transduction. It was also found that NO can regulate fatty acid degradation (evident by the changes in expression levels of ferritin in response to SNP treatment), modulate the citrate cycle (evident by the elevated expression of four dehydrogenases in response to SNP treatment) and thus, control energy metabolisms in settling larvae of the barnacle. Furthermore, NO repressed the level of myosins and cuticular proteins, which indicated that NO might inhibit larval settlement in A. amphitrite by modulating the process of muscle locomotion and molting (Zhang et al 2015, Proteomics 15:3854-3864). These findings provided very important insight about possible roles of NO pathway in larval settlement in general. To determine the possible role of the NO signaling pathway in larval settlement of B. neritina, we first cloned the NOs isoforms and examined the spatial expression of NOs sGC and PKG and the function of NOs as well as two of the possible inter-connected signaling molecules, namely cGMP and cAMP during B neritina settlement, following the same methodology used in B. amphitrite). We also examined the level of endogenous NO level by using Nos inhibitors and NO donor. We found that 1) the enhanced formation of NO inhibited larval settlement while the reduced production of NO accelerated larval settlement, 2) the exclusive localization of NO specific signal in sensory related organs in the swimming larvae suggested a presumptive signal transduction function of NO. The settlement rate of B. neritina larvae decreased after heat shock treatment. Inhibition of HSP90 induced larval settlement, and attenuated the inhibition of NO donors during larval settlement. In addition, the expression level of both HSP90 and NOS declined upon settlement. These results demonstrate that HSP90 regulates the larval settlement of B. neritina by interacting with the NO pathway (Yang et al 2018 Biofouling, Yang et al 2018, JEB). To realize the objective 2 (to investigate the HSP90-NO pathway interaction and its role in larval settlement), we first cloned HSP90 and HSP70 from Bugula neritina larvae have examined the possible interactions between NO and AK, HSP90 and HSP70 using cloning techniques used in our previous study on barnacle larvae. By using pharmacological bioassays and western blotting, we demonstrated that NO inhibits larval settlement of B. neritina and that NO signals occur mainly in the sensory organ of swimming larvae. The settlement rate of B. neritina larvae decreased after heat shock treatment. Inhibition of HSP90 induced larval settlement, and attenuated the inhibition of NO donors during larval settlement. In addition, the expression level of both HSP90 and NOS declined upon settlement. These results demonstrate that HSP90 regulates the larval settlement of B. neritina by interacting with the NO pathway and that HSP90 are proven to act as upstream regulator of NO pathway (Yang et al 2018, JEB). As hinted by our finding in the study of the barnacle larval settlement, arginine kinase (AK) may serve as upstream regulator of NO signaling pathways during the larval settlement. In the present study, we also examined AK’s involvement in larval settlement of the bryozoan Bugula neritina. Following the same method that we used in Zhang et al (2015), we found that the expression of arginine kinase (AK) were increased and AK was highly expressed in the swimming larvae of B. neritina, while its expression was down-regulated post-attachment. When treated with AK inhibitors, the larval settlement rate was significantly decreased. In addition, the immunostaining results indicated that AK was mainly localized to the neuro-muscular cord in swimming larvae (Zhang et al. 2018 Mar Biol). Also as highlighted in the previous and next section, we found that 1) increase of NO led to enhanced formation of both cGMP and cAMP (downstream molecules of NO pathway), resulting inhibition of larval settlement, indicating that the regulatory function of NO is via cGMP and cAMP dependent pathways, 2) in contrast, reduction of endogenous NO, cAMP and cGMP levels all led to the acceleration of larval settlement of B. neritina, and 3) cGMP and cAMP are the chief mediators of NO signaling during B. neritina settlement, while reduction of these signaling molecules to an appropriate level allowed the initiation of larval attachment and metamorphosis. These results were further validated by quantification of these signaling molecules after different treatments. The NO localization was determined using the NO specific fluorescent probe DAF-FM diacetate. The exclusive localization of NO specific signal in sensory related organs suggested NO’s involvement in sensory functions during larval attachment of the B. neritina. Overall, our study provided comprehensive information on interactive signaling network of NO, cGMP and cAMP regulated larval settlement of B. neritina (Yang XX Mphil thesis 2017, Yang et al 2018, Biofouling). To realize the objective 3 (to investigate the possible cross-talk between the MAPK and No pathways), we treated B. neritina larvae with inhibitors specifically targeting JNK and ERK activity. The spatial and temporal expression pattern of JNK, ERK and p38 MAPKs of B. neritina were visualized by western blot and immunohistochemistry. We found that inhibition of nitric oxide synthase (NOS) led to deactivation of the stress-induced signaling protein p38 MAPK. Exclusive localization of NO and NO signaling-components in sensory-related organs of the larvae is consistent with its signal transduction function, indicating there is crosstalk between the MAPK and NO pathways (Yang et al. 2018, Biofouling, 35). The similar work was carried with the larvae of Amphibalanus amphitrite and the results showed that the interaction between the two pathways was not so clear (Zhang et al. 2015, proteomics). In conclusion, the interaction between the MAPK and NO pathways in different larval species varies consistent, which calls for further investigation (Yang et al. 2018, Biofouling, 35).

16101015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101015.value: Finding 1: NO signaling pathway is directly involved in larval settlement of both the soft fouler Bugula neritina and the hard fouler barnacle Amphibalanus amphitrite since suppression of NO production led to increased larval settlement while increase of NO production led to larval settlement inhibition of both species (Zhang et al 2015, Yang et al 2018, JEB, Biofouling, Zhang et al 2018 Mar Biol). Finding 2: NO regulates fatty acid degradation (evident by the changes in expression levels of ferritin in response to SNP treatment), modulate the citrate cycle (evident by the elevated expression of four dehydrogenases in response to SNP treatment) and thus, control energy metabolisms in settling larvae of the barnacle. Furthermore, NO repressed the level of myosins and cuticular proteins, which indicated that NO might inhibit larval settlement in A. amphitrite by modulating the process of muscle locomotion and molting (Zhang et al 2015, Proteomics 15:3854-3864). Finding 3: Arginine kinase (AK) acts as upstream regulator of NO pathway in mediating larval settlement of both Bugula neritina and Amphibalanus amphitrite since the upregulation of AK led to the elevated level of NO, which inhibits the activity and expression of NOs (Zhang et al 2018 Mar Biol). In addition, the immunostaining results indicated that AK was mainly localized to the neuro-muscular cord in swimming larvae. Overall, AK interacts with NO signaling pathway during the larval settlement of B. neritina and thus acts as upstream regulator of NO pathway (Zhang et al. 2018 Mar Biol). Finding 4: HSP70 and HSP90 also act as upstream regulator of NO pathway in controlling larval settlement of both Bugula neritina and Amphibalanus amphitrite since SNP treatment led to the upregulation of HSP90 and/or HSP70 in both larval species (Zhang et al 2015 Proteomics, Yang et al 2018, JEB). Finding 5: There is clear interaction between of NO, cGMP and cAMP in regulating larval settlement of B. neritina since increase of NO led to enhanced formation of both cGMP and cAMP (downstream molecules of NO pathway), resulting inhibition of larval settlement while reduced levels of NO, cAMP and cGMP led to increased larval settlement of B. neritina (Yang XX Mphil thesis 2017, Yang et al 2018, Biofouling). Finding 6: there is crosstalk between the MAPK and NO pathways (Yang et al. 2018, Biofouling, 35) but interaction of these two pathways in barnacle is not so evident (Zhang et al. 2015, proteomics).

16101015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16101015.value: Information on the role of NO signal pathway in larval settlement of Bugula neritina and well defined up-stream and downstream regulators of NO pathway provides important insight into larval settlement regulation of biofouling organisms. Signal molecules identified in this study can be used as screening targets for antifouling compound research. More importantly, the findings has substantially improved our understanding of signal transduction pathways involved in larval settlement of marine invertebrates, which also help understand evolutionary process of larval development of marine invertebrates. The knowledge gained through this study has been used for studying the molecular mechanisms of antifouling compounds, some of which have been patented in USA and China.

16101015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101015.value: Marine invertebrates are of great importance to both ecosystems and economics. Most of marine invertebrates have a free-living stage and sessile stage. Larval settlement is a transition from pelagic to benthic stages but its molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we examined the roles of NO signaling pathway in regulating larval settlement and identified both the up-stream and down-stream regulators of this particular pathway. We showed that 1) NO pathway indeed mediates larval settlement of a soft fouling organism Bugular neritina; 2) arginine kinase (AK) exerted effect on larval settlement and acted as a upstream regulator of NO pathway; 3) HSP90 inhibitor can attenuate the inhibitory effect of NO donor on B. neritina larval settlement, suggesting that HSP90 acts as a upstream regulator of NO pathway; 4) cAMP and cGMP serve as the downstream regulators of the NO pathways; and 5) the interaction between NO pathway and p38 MARK pathways in B. neritina and the barnacle Amphibalanus amphitrite varies. In conclusion, we uncovered the essential roles of NO pathway in B. neritina larvae settlement and provided substantial insights into the molecular mechanism of larval settlement that might exist among different phyla of marine invertebrates.

16101315.label: Project Objectives
16101315.value: To evaluate the mode of interaction between CDK5, p25 and GSK3β, with the goal of assessing the regulation of this unexpected interaction, and whether such interactions can be exploited in a therapeutically useful way. The Cdk5/GSK3β interactions are also important for the understanding of Alzheimer's disease, and will be pursued to the greatest extent possible given the time and funding constraints. To demonstrate that through its interaction with the Wnt signaling pathway, elevated p25 creates a toxic 'by-stander' effect, destroying neurons in the vicinity even while the affected cell itself remains alive. We will carry out Aim #4 to the fullest extent possible as this bystander mechanism, when validated, will have tremendous implications for the understanding of the pathogenesis and possibly the treatment of Alzheimer's disease.

16101315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101315.value: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a common type of late-onset neurodegenerative disease with a prevalence approaching 50% in the population over 85 years of age. Yet, for millions of individuals who suffer worldwide from this condition, medical science can offer no cure. The root causes of AD are currently unknown, but one persistent association is the presence of tangles of hyperphosphorylated tau. GSK3β and CDK5 are two of the main enzymes that phosphorylate tau in a complementary fashion. By studying them as a pair, this project will offer a new and more nuanced view of Alzheimer's and other diseases where the two related kinases are dysregulated. We have made the unexpected discovery that the p25 protein, known as an activator of CDK5, also binds to and activates GSK3β as well. We propose to evaluate the mode of interaction between all three proteins, and whether such interactions can be used in a therapeutically useful way to alter the kinase activity or substrate specificity of GSK3β, CDK5 or both. We will ask how the interplay of p25:GSK3β and p25:CDK5 dyads affects the function and morphology of neurons. Our analysis will include neuritic branching, synaptic density, levels of transmitter synthesis enzymes and their receptors. GSK3β has two types of actions: unmodified protein substrates can be phosphorylated, but the kinase is more active against phosphorylation sites that have been "primed". A key enzyme that "primes" substrates for enhanced GSK3β action is CDK5. We propose to evaluate the effects of these two types of GSK3β kinase activity on cortical neurons in vitro and in vivo. Finally, we plan to use proteomic techniques, specifically SILAC methodology, to compare the full list of proteins that are phosphorylated in primary neurons after activation of these different forms of GSK3β activity. 16101315.label: Realisation of objectives
16101315.value: The exploration of the GSK/Cdk5/p25 linkage has taken us into unexpected territory. Rather than a story of two kinases, the range of p25 actions led us to senescence which in turn led us to a story of age-related insulin resistance. A linkage between insulin resistance and age-related cognitive decline has been suggested but a mechanistic linkage remains elusive. We found that age related systemic hyperinsulinemia leads to chronic high insulin in brain. This exposure to chronic insulin forces neurons into an insulin resistant state and triggers aberrant pre-synaptic activities. In turn, neuronal insulin resistance showed impaired hexokinase-2 activities and overall glucose metabolism. This consequently leads to a downstream mechanism in which the degradation machinery of p35—the precursor of p25—becomes impaired. The pathway by which this occurs was complex. Insulin resistance leads to reduced glucose uptake. This leads to reduced substrate for, and ultimately down-regulation of, hexokinase-2 (HK2) and thus reduced glucose-6-phosphate (G6P, the product of the reaction of HK2 with glucose). G6P is an activator of MondoA, a transcription factor that drives the expression of salt-inducible kinase (SIK2). SIK2 phosphorylates p35, thus priming it for ubiquitination and degradation. With insulin resistance SIK2 levels are reduced, p35 remains unphosphorylated and thus is not degraded. It has been known for many years that when intracellular calcium levels rise, the calcium-dependent protease, calpain, is activated, allowing it to cleave p35 and produce p25. We have now shown that despite the absence of obvious calpain activation during insulin resistance, there is enough baseline calpain activity that accumulation of non-degraded p35 is sufficient to lead to its calpain-mediated cleavage to p25. The canonical consequence of prolonged p25 accumulation is the binding to and activation of CDK5 a neurotoxic complex that leads to neuronal death. In keeping with this, blocking CDK5 activity with roscovitine or reducing CDK5 level with siRNA reduced the percentage of dying neurons in our cultures by almost four-fold. In contrast, overexpression of CDK5 increased death by almost two-fold. Complicating this picture was the finding that insulin resistant neurons also enter a state of senescence. When the role of CDK5 in cellular senescence was examined, however, a different picture emerged. CDK5 knockdown increased the fraction of senescent cells in the culture by 20% but the CDK5 kinase inhibitor, roscovitine, was without effect. This suggested that physical presence of CDK5, but not its kinase activity was important to prevent senescence. This was further supported by our finding that when CDK5 was overexpressed the level of senescent cells went down. This draws attention to our original data showing that in addition to CDK5, p25 can alternatively bind to GSK3beta, hampering its role in β-catenin degradation, a proto-oncogene that its aberrant presence in normal cells may trigger oncogene-induced senescence. Our finding provides a direct linkage from metabolic abnormality to neuronal death and senescence, and thus has high relevance for neurodegenerative conditions such as Alzheimer's disease. The involvement of insulin resistance in the senescence story has been a complicating factor in our original experimental design, but also a much more valuable insight into the mechanisms behind many age-related neurodegenerative diseases. By linking the p25/CDK5/GSK3beta to the hyperinsulinemia that accompanies normal aging, we have made an unprecedented connection between the known Alzheimer's risk factor, Type II diabetes, and the cell death that accompanies neuronal cell death in dementia. This is therapeutically useful as it clearly suggests that working upstream of both GSK3beta and CDK5 and tackling the neuronal insulin resistance itself will be a far more valuable approach to combatting Alzheimer's.

16101315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101315.value: The major findings of our project are summarized in two important manuscripts, one in revision at Nature Neuroscience and one to be submitted shortly. The first manuscript is the description of the insulin resistance/neuronal senescence story described in item 5.3. The second manuscript is the description of the bystander effect. In this work, which is being revised after the details of the insulin story became clear, we show that the elevated levels of beta-catenin drive neurons to enter a cell cycle which leads to a p53 dependent induction of senescence. After entering this state, they adopt a senescence associated secretory phenotype (SASP) one of whose products is the Wnt inhibitor, DKK1. The local elevation of DKK1 drives neighboring neurons into a cell death program. The net effect is that it is the bystander cells that are most susceptible to the neurotoxic effects of senescence, rather than the senescent cells themselves. Six other associated manuscripts have benefitted enormously from the insights that grew for our studies and these too represent important outcome measures of our work.

16101315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16101315.value: The key question to address right now is to turn the insulin resistance story into a clinically useful intervention. Already our pathway through HK2 has pointed the way to a strong possibility. Typically, a patient with Type II diabetes will receive metformin as a drug. Metformin works through direct activation of the AMP-activated protein kinase cascade, but has the unfortunate consequence of lowering, rather than raising, hexokinase activity. Our data suggest this will only make matters worse and that it would be far better to use a drug like liraglutide, a GLP1 mimetic that increases HK2 activity. As this is the desired outcome, we will begin to test the utility of this class of drugs in Alzheimer's disease models.

16101315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101315.value: Insulin resistance and Alzheimer's disease both increase with age and the former is a risk factor for the latter, but a mechanistic linkage remains elusive. We show that peripheral high insulin levels in blood result in chronic elevation of CSF insulin. Neurons exposed to constant insulin become insulin resistant. We found that in insulin resistant neurons, the most dramatic change in glycolysis is in the first enzyme of the pathway—hexokinase-2 (HK2). The loss of HK2 actions in these cells resulted in remodeling of the stability of a protein called p35. Too much p25 leads to its proteolytic cleavage to p25, and helps the accumulation of Alzheimer's related proteins found in plaques and tangles. We found that loss of HK2 hampered the normal p35 protein degradation pathway of p35, thus the accumulated protein became more vulnerable to be cleaved and form p25. On one hand, p25 causes neuronal cell death by hyper-activating the tau kinase, CDK5. At the same time, it interacts with another kinase partner, GSK3β and induces neuronal senescence, an aging phenomenon. Taken together, our data provide a molecular explanation to how high insulin levels contribute to Alzheimer's disease.

16101415.value: Dinoflagellate chromatins adopt non-nucleosomal mode of compaction into liquid crystalline chromosomes (LCCs), through cation-superhelicity-mediated DNA condensation. The start of the project was substantially affected attributed to a severe Hepatitis A infection during 2015 christmas-2016 new year during which I was hospitalized. Nap1p immunolocalization and post-translational modification studies suggested nuclear-cytoplasmic transport, with increased nuclear localization during G2 phase of the cell cycle, correlated with higher G1 expression level. Given the large-size and permanent of dinokaryons, our observations indicated significant regulatory role of NAP1-mediated transport in gene expression, which have a bearing on their blooming and bleaching. 5. Large-scale recombination of high-copy tandem repeats were reported in dinoflagellates, as well as among amplicons of ciliate macronucleus. Our results have implications to the replication and recombination in dinoflagellate cell cycles. We attempted gene-knockdown studies of Nap1 and other core histones. Results did not give reproducible results, which hindered our publication of our results relating to ubiquitination-deubiquitination of histone H2b and coccoid-swarmer transition. As H2B ubiquitination is an essential mark in many nucleosomal system, this could be relating to lethality caused by the knockdown. 16101415.label: Major findings and research outcome
16101415.value: Motile-to-immotile cell transitions (MITs) are important switches in dinoflagellate life cycles, recognized to contribute to algal blooms and coral bleaching dynamics. Objective 3.Transcriptomes and Histone-enriched Genes during SC-PC Transitions. Comparative analysis suggested relatively little changes in core histone transcripts , unlike genes required for cell wall remodeling(P1, c1, c2) and, proteolipid membrane potential 3 proteins (P2), but similar to condensin SMC4 (P3) during motile-immotile cell transition. The fifteen histone variant genes in C.cohnii stayed at relatively low level during the cell cycle, with overall projected relative abundance two orders of magnitude lower than that of dinoflagellate histone-like proteins(dHlps). A specific H2A variant expression changed with motile-non-motile transitions, but the relative fold of reduction was not as substantial as found in mammalian cell cycle. Objective 1. Characterization of Histone PTMs during Transitions between swarmer cells (SC) and pellicle cysts (PCs); We report several epigenetics marks associated with MITs. Histone H2B ubiquitination and deubiquitination are respectively associated with forward and leeward direction in MITs. Histone H3K9met3 modification was observed to be associated with MIT during S-G2 cell cycle progression, as well as methylation sensitivity in the genomic restriction-enzyme digestion of the H2A encoded loci. H2a.x S139 phosphorylation was observed in response to double-strand DNA breaks in response to topoisomerase inhibitor eclliticine, associated with MITs. Objective 2: Modulation of Epigenetics on SC-PC Transitions Inter-core histone interactions, as well as interactions with nucleosome assembly factor 1 homologues, as well as surprise interactions with histone-like proteins. H2a-knockdown led to increased LCC digestibility , consistent with nucleosomal modulation of gene expression, despite mostly superhelical-mediated DNA-condensation. Inhibitor to H3K9met3 led to reduction of the histone mark and associated G2 arrest. Exogenous Ni2+ ions , an inhibitor of histone deubiquitination, inhibited immotile to motile cell transition, but not in the reverse direction, associated with H2B deubiquitination. Nucleosome assembly protein 1 abundance was associated with nuclear-cytoplasmic transport in G2 (P5); antisense-treatment of which led to mixed in G2 transition, likely related to the histone chaperon mediating multiple histone marks, some likely in the opposite signaling pathways. UV irradiation, an agent reported to modulate MIT, dose-dependently induced cell cycle arrest in dinoflagellates (P6, P7). WE are actively pursuing to continue our track of publishing our results, despite COVID-19, and the delay attributed to my hospitalization due to a severe Hepitatis A in 2015/16.

Future strategic research areas will include the roles of cytoplasmic-nuclear transport, cross-epigenetic signaling, cross-encoding between histones and dHlps, and phase transition. 16101415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16101415.value: Dinoflagellate chromatins adopt non-nucleosomal mode of compaction into liquid crystalline chromosomes (LCCs), through superhelicity-mediated DNA condensation. This raises interesting questions as to the functions of the recently reported variant type non-architectural core histones. Transcriptomic analysis suggested most core histone transcripts were expressed during immotile-motile cell transition (IMC), 2-3 orders of magnitude, associated with abrupt upregulation of the cellulose-synthase (dCesA1), in agreement with the major cell wall remodeling during IMC. Gene knockdown of H2A resulted in increased resistance of dinoflagellate nuclear genome to micrococcal nuclease digestion. Inter-histone association, as well as that with Nucleosome assembly protein 1 (NAP1) homologues, Nap-mediated nucleosomal disassembly, and association of histone post-translation modifications, were consistent with histone-nucleosomal assembly orchestration of sub-domain accessibility in LCCs. Their surprising association with cell-cycle progression will have a bearing on both algal blooms and symbiont-host relationship.

16101515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16101515.value: With an excretion construct, pWKW2, previously constructed by us and the DNA sequence encoding the self-cleavable Sce VMA intein (VMA), we have recently engineered a novel Escherichia coli system and successfully employed it to co-express two valuable human skin proteins: epidermal growth factor (EGF) and basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF). Both polypeptides were not only co-expressed at high levels, but both were also shown to possess their authentic primary structures (Kwong and Wong, 2013; attached diagrams). Other groundbreaking findings reported in our publication include: (1) bFGF is expressed, for the first time, as an extracellular authentic product in E. coli. (2) Both bFGF and EGF, being in their mature authentic forms, were detected at high levels in not only the culture medium, but also in the cell lysate of the host cells. (3) The VMA, despite being a large intracellular protein (~56 kDa), was successfully expressed as an extracellular product in E. coli. (4) Unlike other groups previous findings, the intracellular and extracellular EGF-VMA-bFGF intermediates were found to be selfcleavable; thus the use of a tag/column system to facilitate cleavages in order to free the two growth factors was not required. However, to make the newly-introduced approach suitable for extensive applications, the following issues must first be addressed. First, can the approach be employed to co-express a wide range of proteins, including even non-secretory members? Second, using EGF-VMA-bFGF as a model construct, the amino acids at the borders between EGF-VMA and VMA-bFGF will be studied in detail in order to gain a better understanding of the autocatalytic mechanism(s) between VMA and its exteins. Third, since a combination between the OmpA signal and EGF was shown to help promote secretion/excretion of VMA-bFGF, will the same combination be capable of promoting secretion/excretion of intein-C extein groupings other than VMA-bFGF? Last, it was interesting to note the high solubilities of EGF-VMA-bFGF intermediates, thus circumventing the use of an affinity column for their retrieval. Understanding the high solubilites of EGF-VMA-bFGF intermediates may help resolve the problem of protein aggregate formation, which have been shown to form frequently in protein expression mediated by inteins. The clarification of all these issues may help generate a versatile intein/E. coli expression platform for routine use in the recombinant production of proteins. 結合我們之前構建的外分泌克隆pWKW2以及編碼能自我切除的內含肽VMA 基因序列，近來我們建立了一種新的大腸桿菌系統，運用它成功共表達兩種珍貴的人體皮膚蛋白：表皮生長因子EGF和鹼性成纖維細胞生長因子bFGF。 兩種多肽不僅表達量高，而且都具有與人體自身表達的蛋白相同的初級結構。 在我們發表的文章中其他的重大發現包括： (1)bFGF首次以胞外並且完全與人體自身相同的產物的形式在大腸桿菌中被表達。 (2) 而且，高表達量的成熟並且與人體自身相同的bFGF和EGF不僅能在培養基中被檢測到，在宿主細胞裂解液中也可以被檢測到。 (3)儘管VMA是一個巨大的胞內蛋白(~56 kDa)，但依然成功地在大腸桿菌中作為胞外產物被表達。 (4)與其他研究組之前的發現有所不同的是，我們發現在胞內胞外的EGF-VMA-bFGF過渡產物是可以被自我切除的；因此，就不需要標籤/柱系統去切除以釋放這兩種細胞生長因子。 然而，為了使剛介紹的方法適用於更廣泛的應用，下面的這些問題必須被解決。 首先，這個方法是否能應用於共表達大範圍的蛋白，甚至包括不能分泌的蛋白？ 其次，以EGF-VMA-bFGF作為模型克隆，為了更好地瞭解VMA和外顯肽之間的自催化切除機制，在EGF-VMA和VMA-bFGF分界上的氨基酸需要仔細研究。 第三， 因為OmpA信號肽與EGF的組合證實有助於VMA-bFGF的分泌/外排，那麼相同的組合會不會同樣能促進除了VMA-bFGF以外的其他內含肽-C 外顯肽的分泌/外排？ 最後，一個有趣的發現是EGF-VMA-bFGF過渡產物的高可溶性，避免了利用親和性柱子純化。瞭解EGF-VMA-bFGF高可溶性也許能幫助解決在利用內含肽表達蛋白中經常出現的蛋白質聚集形成的問題。 澄清以上的這些問題也許能有助於建立一個通用的用於表達重組蛋白的內含肽/大腸桿菌表達平台。

16101515.label: Realisation of objectives
16101515.value: The PI’s research team has been working on cost-effective production of cellulases including an endoglucanase, an exoglucanase and various cellobiases, and human skin growth factors including epidermal growth factor (EGF) and basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF) for over 30 years. Currently, his research focuses on engineering of microbial systems to facilitate extracellular expression of heterologous proteins, which are not only biologically active, but may also be produced in high yields. In 2013, his laboratory employed the gene sequence encoding an intein (also known as “protein intron”), a Saccharomyces cerevisiae vascular membrane ATPase (VMA), and DNA sequences comprising the lacUV5 promoter and the ompA leader sequence responsible for protein secretion, to develop an efficient intein-based expression construct, pWK3R (Kwong and Wong, 2013) for high levels co-expression of EGF and bFGF as authentic mature products in E. coli. In pWK3R, the egf and bfgf genes were fused at the 5’ end and 3’ end, respectively, of the vma coding sequence. Subsequent to expression with pWK3R, both EGF and bFGF were detected not only in the culture medium but also, surprisingly, in the cytoplasm (Kwong and Wong, 2013). Based on the successful application of the VMA intein to the expression of EGF and bFGF as authentic products, in conjunction with our experience gained in intein-mediated protein expression in both E. coli and Bacillus subtilis, the objectives listed in this project have all been achieved as described below. Referring to Objective 1, based on our successful engineering and application of pWK3R in mediating co-expression of authentic as well as bioactive EGF and bFGF in E. coli (Kwong and Wong, 2013), the pWK3R was then modified and employed to successfully express two widely different proteins, EGF and an endoglucanase (Eng) of Cellulomonas fimi. Both EGF and Eng were not only shown to be soluble but also auto-cleavable to give rise to properly processed proteins. The results were published in Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology entitled: “Engineering versatile protein expression systems mediated by inteins in Escherichia coli” (Kwong et al. 2016) and reported in Part C “Research Output” of this report. Moreover, the EGF product resulting from the above mentioned expression is fully bioactive, and has been shown to be effective in treating wounds like scalds, of which the results were published in Journal of Analytical & Pharmaceutical Research (2016) entitled: “Application of Recombinant human EGF to effective treatment of scalds”, and reported in the 1st Annual Progress Report as well as in Part C “Research Output” of this report. Referring to Objective 2, our findings demonstrated that the presence of EGF placed at the N-terminal region of VMA-bFGF would facilitate auto-catalytic cleavage of the VMA-bFGF fusion engineered at the C-terminus of VMA, which was shown to take place in both the cytoplasm and culture supernatant (Kwong and Wong, 2013; citation shown below). To study whether EGF might have a beneficial effect on the cleavage of bFGF if it was fused at the C-terminus of VMA instead, the positions of EGF and bFGF with respect to VMA were swapped to result in the expression of the precursor, bFGF-VMA-EGF. In addition, another precursor, EGF-VMA-EGF was also expressed. Results from the comparison of auto-cleavages among the three precursors revealed that a beneficial effect on auto-processing occurred only in precursor EGF-VMA-bFGF, and supported the following conclusions. First, not any target proteins might form a productive pair with the EGF-VMA fusion to achieve auto-catalytic cleavage. Second, it appeared that EGF might only exhibit a beneficial effect on the cleavage of the co-existed target protein, e.g., bFGF, when EGF was fused at the N- but not the C-terminus of VMA. Referring to Objective 3, in investigating the applicability of other inteins, it was found that small inteins such as GyrA was able to mediate co-expression of EGF and endoglucanase effectively (Kwong et al. 2016 and reported in Part C of this report). Further, an OmpA signal peptide-EGF fusion, which was then fused at the N-terminus of GyrA, was shown to be able to facilitate auto-cleavages of target proteins fused at the C-terminus of GyrA (Kwong and Wong, 2013; Kwong et al., 2016). Various point mutations, including (i) S179G, engineered in GyrA of precursor OmpA-EGF-GryA-EGF, and (ii) mimicking the amino acids located in the junction between VMA and bFGF of our formerly engineered model construct: OmpA-EGF-VMA-bFGF (Kwong and Wong, 2013), mutations H197Q in GyrA and N1P in EGF of precursor OmpA-EGF-GyrA-EGF, were introduced, respectively. Although S179G in GryA was reported to promote C-terminal cleavage (J. Mol Biol. 2007, 367:162-173), our results showed that the cleavage of bFGF from GyrA was not observed, an indication that the mutations impose an inhibitory effect on cleavage activities, in the mutant precursors engineered as described in (i) and (ii) above. On the other hand, sequencing data showed that cleavable precursors did not only undergo auto-processing activities, but they were also subjected to proteolysis to give rise to a variety of smaller intermediates (Manuscript describing the results submitted to Journal of Advanced Research in Biotechnology for publication). Investigation of the application of inteins to promoting bFGF expression was also undertaken in another bacterium, B. subtilis, from which inteins has not been identified. In the study, the cellulose-binding domain (CellBD) of an endoglucanase encoded by the cenA gene of Cellulomonas fimi was fused at the N-terminus of a mini intein, Ssp DnaB, (DnaB), of which the C-terminus was fused with bFGF. It was revealed from the work that the precursor, CellBD-DnaB-bFGF, was subjected to auto-processing and authentic bFGF, which was detected in the cytoplasm of B. subtilis. The results, which had not been reported previously, were published in Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology (2018) entitled: “Novel strategy for expression of authentic and bioactive human basic fibroblast growth factor in Bacillus subtilis” and documented in Section C of this report. Referring to objective 4, employing the initial expression construct, pWK3R, we successfully engineered a novel construct, pWK311RompAd, in which the ompA leader sequence was removed, thus possessing two copies of a DNA segment encoding a fusion pair: VMA-bFGF, and resulting in EGF-VMA-bFGF-VMA-bFGF as the precursor product. Applying a refined fed-batch fermentation protocol, a phenomenal yield of 610 mg/L of bFGF was attained from the JM101 [pWK311ROmpAd] transformant, which was 7.5 times higher than that obtained from its JM101 [pWK3R] counterpart. Despite existing in high levels, the bFGF product remained to be soluble and highly bioactive (published in 2016 in Scientific Report; see Part C Section 7 of this report). Moreover, through expression of pWK311RompAd and the application of a newly developed purification protocol, bFGF was purified from both the cytoplasm and culture supernatant (resulting from cell lysis) of the grown transformant, high levels of recovery of 61% and 70% of bFGF were retrieved from the cell lysate and supernatant samples, respectively. The purified bFGF was determined to be authentic and fully potent; the results were published in Internal Journal of Chromatography and Separation Techniques (2018) entitled: “Purification of authentic human basic fibroblast growth factor ex¬pressed in both the cytoplasm and culture medium of Escherichia coli” as listed in Part C “Research Output” of this report. Reference: Kwong K.W.Y. and Wong W.K.R. (2013) A revolutionary approach facilitating co-expression of authentic human EGF and bFGF in both cytoplasm and culture medium of Escherichia coli. Appl. Microbiol. Biotechnol. 97:9071-9080
