16103015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103015.value: The overall project goal was to identify the molecular determinants that define ligand selectivity at the melatonin MT2 receptor and explore potential applications of MT2-selective ligands against type-2 diabetes (T2D). By means of homology modeling and mutagenesis studies, we have successfully identified several residues that are crucial for the binding and function of the MT2-selective isoquinolinones (Abstracts 1, 5 and 6). Ligand selectivity at MT1 and MT2 receptors may be partly determined by two conserved tyrosine residues on TM7 (Tyr281/294 and Tyr285/298), while a conserved histidine (His208 in MT2) may participate in receptor activation (Abstracts 5 and 7). These interesting findings have been compiled for publication but submission of the manuscript (Publication 3 in Part C) was delayed due to the impending publication of the MT1 (Stauch et al., Nature, 2019;569:284) and MT2 crystal structures (Johansson et al., Nature, 2019;569:289) that eventually appeared earlier this year. Prior to submission, we had to painstakingly re-configure our receptor model and re-analyze the data against the published structures (PDB codes 6ME6 and 6ME7). Gratifyingly, the residues predicted to participate in ligand binding largely matched the published structures. Hence, we do not expect any major issue in publishing our work soon. Functional characterization of T2D-associated MT2 receptor mutants have yielded mix results. On one hand, the selected mutations were shown to affect both melatonin and isoquinolinones alike, albeit less so for the latter (Abstracts 2 and 7). On the other hand, functional rescue of a signaling-defective MT2 mutant (R138C) upon coexpression of MT1 suggests possible manipulations through receptor dimerization (Abstracts 3, 6 and 8), a phenomenon known to occur with melatonin receptors. Although there is no strong evidence in support of differential activation of T2D-associated nonsynonymous MTNR1B variants by the isoquinolinones, it remains possible to develop alternative strategies to enhance/rescue the function of MT2 variants. Unexpectedly, despite ample reports of melatonin inhibiting insulin secretion in vivo, robust melatonin suppressive effect could not be demonstrated in three commonly used pancreatic cell lines. Since the functions of several other GPCRs were clearly detected in these cell lines, it implies that melatonin receptors may utilize atypical signaling mechanism. This prompted us to explore melatonin-mediated Gq pathway (Abstract 4), autocrine/paracrine signaling (Publication 1), and protective cellular effects (Publication 2). Please note that although Publication 1 was not directly supported by this grant, the idea of studying GPCR regulation of autocrine/paracrine signaling was conceived through this work.

16103015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103015.value: Our initial idea of visualizing the ligand binding pocket of the MT2 receptor through homology modeling has been vindicated by the recent publication of the crystal structures of MT1 and MT2. Although the published structures do not faithfully reflect native melatonin receptors (because eight mutations had to be introduced to attain protein stability for crystallization), they represent a major advancement in our understanding of this group of receptors. Based on the structural model, functional changes elicited by the isoquinolinones in the different MT2 mutants can be accounted for. Refinement of the model may enable further delineation of the functional implications of mutations that affect MT2 signaling and dimerization. It would be tremendously interesting to unravel how MT2-selective agonists can activate the signaling-defective R138C mutant in the presence of MT1, but not in its absence. Another aspect of melatonin pharmacology which requires further investigation is how melatonin regulates insulin secretion. As demonstrated in the present proposal, the precise mechanism by which melatonin modulates pancreatic β-cells remains elusive. The stark difference between in vivo and in vitro observations tends to suggest complex signaling. It might be worthwhile to characterize the signaling capacity of α-, β-, and δ-pancreatic cells by single cell RNAseq.

16103015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103015.value: Melatonin is often considered as a sleep hormone which is effective against jetlag. Recent studies have extended the function of melatonin and its receptors to the regulation of glucose homeostasis, stem cell differentiation, cancer suppression, and neurodegenerative disorders. There is mounting evidence to link individual melatonin receptor subtypes to the pathophysiology of different diseases such as type-2 diabetes for MT2. The present study has provided several lines of evidence pointing to the molecular basis of ligand selectivity at the MT2 receptor. By visualizing the receptor in 3D structures, it may be possible to develop highly selective ligands that target the melatonin MT2 receptors. Findings from this study also demonstrate that, at some MT2 receptor mutants, isoquinolinone derivatives can produce responses that are different from those of melatonin. Since genetic variations in the MT2 receptor is apparently associated with a higher risk of type-2 diabetes, novel MT2-selective ligands with differential abilities to activate MT2 receptor variants may have potential therapeutic values.

16103215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103215.value: Glaucoma, a worldwide leading cause of blindness, refers to a group of diseases that damage the eye’s optic nerve with associated the loss of vision. It affects one in 200 people below the age of 50, and one in 10 over the age of 80. Primary open-angle glaucoma is the most common glaucoma. It is chronic and dangerous because the visual function loss often develops gradually over a long period of time, and symptoms only occur when the disease is in an advanced stage. The lost visual function cannot normally be recovered and the treatments are only aimed at preventing further loss. Although various risk factors have been investigated, the pathogenesis of glaucoma is still not fully understood. Noninvasive in vivo imaging of biological processes at subcellular resolution represents a new frontier in discovering the biological basis and the impact of disease and therapies. In this proposed research, we aim to develop an advanced imaging technology to visualize the development and progression of glaucoma. Significant advances in the research of glaucoma can be attributed to the introduction of rodent glaucoma models over the past decade. In particular, the mouse model will provide critical advantages for in vivo high-resolution imaging of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and optic nerves at subcellular level, because the mouse eye has exceptionally large optical power and high numerical aperture. This makes high-resolution two-photon excitation fluorescence microscopy practical in the live mouse glaucoma model. We will develop an adaptive optics two-photon excitation fluorescence microscope (AO-TPEFM) system to achieve in vivo structural and functional imaging of RGCs and optic nerves in mouse retina at subcellular resolution. The glaucoma models for fluorescence imaging will be generated using the commercially available transgenic mouse of RGCs labelled with fluorescent protein (FP). The structural imaging channel of the AO-TPEFM system will collect FP signals to form the image of RGCs and optic nerves. The functional information of RGCs will be extracted from the fluorescence of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH), a well-known metabolic coenzyme and endogenous fluorophore. The in vivo structural and functional imaging of live mouse models will provide new biological insights into glaucoma under physiologically relevant conditions. Success of the proposed research will be vital to understanding the mechanism(s) of the disease and developing new therapeutic strategies for its management. The total requested funding for the proposed research over three years are HK$ 1,664,000 (US$213,333). 青光眼是全球範圍內導致永久性失明的頭號殺手，它通過破壞視覺神經進而嚴重地影響視覺。據統計，在年齡50歲以下的人群中，每200人中就有一人受青光眼影響，而在80歲以上人群中，這個比例上升到十分之一。原发性开角型青光眼是青光眼中最常见的一種。它是一種危險的慢性疾病，因为视觉功能損失的過程發展的比較緩慢，當發現症狀時往往已經處於疾病的晚期。青光眼患者失去的视觉功能不能正常恢復，現有的治療手段只能防止進一步的視覺損失。虽然目前有很多對青光眼的各種風險因素的研究，但其發病機制仍然沒有得到充分的理解。無創活體成像技術目前正被廣泛地應用於高分辨地探測生物過程，探索前沿的生物學基礎以及疾病的療法。我們在此提出一種先進的成像技術，可以通過可視化的手段探究青光眼的發展過程。在過去的十年中，嚙齒類動物的青光眼疾病模型的引入對青光眼的研究起了非常巨大的推動作用。具體地來說，由於老鼠的眼球具有較大的光焦度以及較大的數值孔徑，這使得其相比于其他動物來說更適合用於活體高分辨的視網膜成像研究（成像主要包括視網膜神經節細胞以及視神經）。結合老鼠眼球結構的特殊優勢，高分辨雙光子激發熒光顯微鏡可以有效地用於老鼠青光眼模型的研究。我們將開發自適應光學雙光子激發熒光顯微鏡（AOTPEFM）系統以實現在亞細胞分辨率下對視網膜神經節細胞和視神經的結構和功能進行成像研究。我們將採用市售的具有熒光蛋白標記的視網膜神經節細胞的轉基因小鼠來做青光眼模型的視網膜熒光成像研究。其中，AOTPEFM的結構成像通道會收集熒光蛋白的熒光信號來形成神經節細胞以及視神經的結構圖像。同時，視網膜神經節細胞中的NADH（煙酰胺腺嘌呤二核苷酸，一種知名的代謝輔酶和內源性熒光基團）熒光信號會被提取用於分析其生物功能信息。小鼠模型的活體視網膜結構和功能成像研究將有機會發現全新的有關青光眼病理機制的關鍵信息。該研究的成果將會有助於了解青光眼的病理機制以及有針對性地發展新的臨床診斷方法。

16103215.label: Realisation of objectives
16103215.value: The objectives of this project were achieved in two phases of research. First, we have developed a nonlinear optical (NLO) microscopy system integrating a high-resolution stimulated Raman scattering (SRS), multi-channel two-photon excited fluorescence (TPEF) and second-harmonic generation (SHG) to image mouse retina. In particular, the SRS imaging takes advantage of a newly installed picosecond tunable laser system that produces narrow-bandwidth pump and Stokes laser beams to generate high-quality spectral-resolved SRS signals from biological tissue. In the multichannel TPEF imaging, we used multiple hybrid photodetector to enhance the sensitivity, enabling the detection depth in tissue to be increased and photodamage to tissue to be reduced. The morphological and functional details of various retinal layers were revealed by the endogenous NLO and fluorescent protein signals. Particularly, high resolution label-free imaging of retinal neurons and nerve fibers in the ganglion cell and nerve fiber layers was achieved by capturing endogenous SRS and TPEF signals. In addition, the spectral and temporal analysis of TPEF images allowed the visualization of different fluorescent components in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE). Fluorophores with short TPEF lifetimes, such as A2E, can be differentiated from other long lifetime components in the RPE. The NLO imaging method can provide important information for investigation of retinal ganglion cell degeneration and the potential to study the biochemical processes of visual cycle in the RPE. In phase two study, our research efforts were focused on the development of adaptive optics for in vivo high spatial resolution imaging in retina. Direct retinal imaging plays an important role not only in understanding diseased eye and ocular therapeutic discovery, but also study of a variety of well-defined central nervous system (CNS) disorders. In recent years, accumulated evidences have shown that certain neurodegenerative diseases that affect the brain and spinal cord also have manifestations in the retina, and ocular symptoms always precede traditional diagnosis of such diseases, such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease and multiple sclerosis. With the rapid development of mouse models of human diseases, in vivo structural and functional imaging of mouse retina is now considered as an ideal approach to understand ocular diseases and unveil the mechanisms underlying the neurodegenerative disorders in the CNS. However, the limited resolution of prevalent retinal imaging tools makes it inadequate to resolve the subcellular structures and dynamics of retinal neurons, mainly attributed to the large optical aberrations of the mouse eye. Adaptive optics (AO) has recently been employed in microscopy to correct sample-induced aberrations and restore diffraction-limited resolution in biological tissues. However, the commonly used sensorless AO techniques using optimization algorithms are time consuming and thus unable to capture the highly dynamic biological processes. On the other hand, the sensor-based AO technique applied in scanning laser ophthalmoscopy collects the reflectance light from the outer retina as the guide star for AO correction, which has several drawbacks including (1) the multiple back reflections from multiple retinal layers produce superimposed spots patterns on the wavefront sensor; (2) the aberration measured with the reflections from the outer retina may not be applicable for the inner retina; (3) the double-pass measurement loses the information of odd aberrations in the eye, while doubles the even aberrations. All these problems result in inaccurate aberration measurement and thus compromise the performance of AO correction. In this GRF funded project, we advance two-photon microscopy for near-diffraction-limited and functional retinal imaging in living mice. We developed an adaptive optics two-photon excitation fluorescence microscopy (AO-TPEFM) using direct wavefront sensing for high-resolution in vivo fluorescence imaging of mouse retina. In particular, the localized two-photon fluorescence signals were used as nonlinear guide stars to achieve accurate measurement of ocular aberrations at the imaging location. We demonstrate that depth-resolved structures in different retinal layers can be resolved at an unprecedented resolution after full AO correction, allowing for a wide range of studies which are infeasible otherwise. Specifically, it enables simultaneously functional calcium imaging of somas and dendrites of RGCs. In addition, precise axotomy and time-lapse imaging of axonal degeneration were achieved with femtosecond laser induced microsurgery. Moreover, we studied the structural dynamics and alterations of retinal microglia in response to the N-Methyl-D-aspartic acid (NMDA) excitotoxicity. Our work demonstrates that the high-resolution AO-TPEFM is a promising tool to study a host of biological processes in retina, and would also shed new light on the neurodegenerative diseases in the CNS.

16103215.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103215.value: In the first part of this research project, we demonstrated a multimodal label-free NLO microscopy to extract the morphological and biochemical details in different retinal layers. High-quality label-free visualization of the nerve fibers and retinal neurons could be achieved with the SRS imaging. The combination of SRS and TPEF imaging provided unique opportunities to investigate the structure as well as the biochemical characteristics of different retinal layers. The distinct difference in fluorescence lifetime between the two major RPE fluorophores would provide new insights into the functional mechanisms of the visual cycle and the mechanisms of RPE dysfunction. Our findings showed that the label-free capability of SRS and TPEF imaging could make the wild type mouse an inexpensive and easily available model for the retina study. This may even pave the path for retina research in other animals in which transgenicor retrograde-labeling is not applicable. In vivo fundus imaging allows non-invasive access to the neuron structures and biochemical processes in retina. In the second part of this research project, we developed an adaptive optics two-photon excitation fluorescence microscope (AO-TPEFM) system to correct the ocular aberrations based on nonlinear fluorescent guide star and achieve unprecedented resolution for in vivo fluorescence imaging of mouse retina. With accurate wavefront sensing and rapid aberration correction, the AO-TPEFM permits structural and functional imaging of mouse retina with submicron resolution. Specifically, distinct retinal layers could be clearly resolved, and functional calcium imaging of neuronal somas and dendrites was demonstrated. With the recovery of diffraction-limited focus, precise laser axotomy was achieved and degeneration of retinal neurons was studied. Moreover, the dynamics of the microglial processes were finely resolved, and the time-lapse morphological alteration of microglia was monitored in a mouse model of retinal disorder. Our study demonstrated that this high-resolution AO-TPEFM is a promising tool for non-invasive retinal imaging and would facilitate the understanding of a variety of diseases in the central nervous system. 16103215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103215.value: As a window to the brain, the retina is the only part of the central nervous system (CNS) that can be visualized non-invasively with optical imaging approaches. Accumulating evidences have shown that the eye is host to immune responses similar to those in the brain and spinal cord, and ocular symptoms always precede traditional diagnosis of CNS pathologies, such as Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease and multiple sclerosis. Therefore, in vivo morphological and functional imaging of retinal structures provides a non-invasive approach to decipher the mechanisms behind neurodegenerative disorders in the CNS. Our work demonstrates that the high-resolution AO-TPEFM is a promising tool to study a host of biological processes in retina, and would also shed new light on the neurodegenerative diseases in the CNS.

16103315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103315.value: A major obstacle following adult optic nerve injury is the regeneration of retinal ganglion cell (RGC) axons and their reconnection with target neurons. By modulating intrinsic mechanisms, we have shown that RGC axons can regeneration for a long distance within the optic nerve after intraorbital crush. However, only a few axons innervate the brain. Using a pre-chiasm optic nerve injury model, we now demonstrate that lesioned axons can robustly reinnervate the hypothalamus. Some axons form synapses with neurons in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), a central pacemaker for regulating circadian rhythm. The overall goal of this proposal is to examine whether the axons that reach to the SCN form functional connections, and develop strategies to further enhance optic nerve regeneration to the central targets in the brain. 在成年的中樞神經系統中，由於神經元軸突已經失去了它們的自我再生能力，因此一旦有損傷會導致永久的功能性喪失，比如脊髓損傷。如果能促使神經軸突再生並形成連接，就給恢復功能提供了可能性。利用我們實驗室建立了的一個特有的前視交叉損傷模型，最近我們發現通過有針對性地誘導成年小鼠中樞神經系統軸突再生的的分子機制，可以促使損傷的視神經軸突重新生長並與視交叉上核神經元形成有活動的突觸連接。但是這些突觸連接是否有功能並不清楚。 我們將在視神經元同時激活mTOR，Stat3，cAMP通路並結合降低外在的抑制因素，測試是否可以進一步使軸突再生，促進對視交叉上核神經元的支配，並產生有生理功能的突觸連接，甚至影響動物的行為。我們所提出的實驗項目可能產生促進中樞神經系統損傷后軸突再生和功能恢復的新方法。

16103315.label: Realisation of objectives
16103315.value: One of the major goals of studying axon regeneration is to achieve functional recovery after CNS injury. However, it is very challenging to comprehensively demonstrate that axons across the lesion site can reconnect with target neurons with functional synapses, at the levels of ultrastructure, circuitry, electrophysiology especially with the post-synaptic response, and behavior, by using an appropriate injury model. Combining several strategies to boost the intrinsic growth capacity of RGCs leads to robust and long-distance regeneration within the optic nerve after intraorbital crush, a type of lesion close to the eyeball. However, only a few axons innervate the brain, which makes it difficult to assess the potential functional outcome. The limited innervation could be due to the long distance for axons to travel, misguidance along the path, the difficulty for axons to cross the optic chiasm, and continuous neuronal loss months after lesion. To test the hypothesis that regenerated axons can make functional connections, one strategy to bypass the long path is to move the lesion site closer to the target neurons. Such effort has been carried out for sensory axons to reach dorsal nuclei, and also recently optic tract to reach superior colliculi. Our aim was to develop an injury model to examine whether a large number of regenerating retinal axons can reinnervate appropriate target area, and form active connections with appropriate neurons at the synaptic and functional level. We managed to crush the optic nerve at the point right before it enters the chiasm. This model gives us an opportunity to examine the potential recovery of both the visual and non-visual functions after injury. We started the initial experiment by deleting both Pten and Socs3 in retinal ganglion cells, and found that, after prechiasm lesion, retinal axons robustly reinnervate the hypothalamus. Many axons projected ectopically around the core region of the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN), suggesting an abnormal innervation. More axons in the core region were found 4 months after lesion. Some of the regenerated axons reform synapses with neurons in SCN. Both the pre- and post-synaptic markers are co-localized with terminals of regenerated axons by immunofluorescence labeling. To convincingly demonstrate the formation of the new synapses, we overexpressed GFP in regenerated axons using AAV, and performed immunogold electromicroscopy analysis. We found some structures with key features of asymmetric synapses. Through trans-neuronal tracing, we also showed that axons make connections with SCN neurons with the existing circuitry. Furthermore, electric stimulation of the regenerated optic nerve induces excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs) in neurons at SCN. Our results support that boosting the intrinsic growth capacity through inhibiting both Pten and Socs3 in injured neurons promotes axonal reinnervation and rewiring. However both the innervation pattern and evoked responses are not completely restored by the regenerating axons, suggesting combining with other strategies may be necessary. In this proposal, we set up three aims to address these questions. Aim 1: To assess whether combining strategies to enhance the intrinsic growth potentials of RGCs can promote re-innervation into the SCN. In the past year, we have been done the pre-chiasm experiments by combining Pten/Socs3 double knockout with B-Raf activation or cAMP injection. Unfortunately, we found B-Raf overactivation for over 8 weeks will dramatically decrease the RGC survival, and we could not detect regenerating axons in the brain. To our surprise, repeated cAMP did not significantly increase the axon reinnervation into the SCN region. We also tried to inject Chondroitinase ABC (ChABC) into the SCN. We did not find significant difference on the axon re-innervation pattern in Pten/Socs3 KO mice. Recently, we have demonstrated that enhancing neuronal activity by melanopsin overexpression or Gq activation can boost axon regrowth. We did the experiment by overexpressing melanopsin in Pten/Socs3 KO mice. But we did not find significant difference on the axon re-innervation pattern. Aim 2: To assess whether axons can reform active connections with neurons in the SCN. In order to address whether regenerating axons by the combination strategy reform active connections with neurons in the SCN, we assessed this question by trans-synaptic viral tracing. PRV injected into the anterior chamber of the eye retrogradely infects specific retinorecipient nuclei in the brain, namely the OPN, intergeniculate leaflet (IGL) and the SCN, resulting in labeled ganglion cells in the other retina 96 hours after intraocular infection. Through this approach, we showed that regenerating RGC axons reform synaptic connections with SCN neurons. Some RGCs in the ipsilateral lesioned eye were labeled only in the sham and regenerated mice, but not in the injured control, suggesting that regenerating axons connect with part of the brain circuitry by projecting back to the SCN. Aim 3: To examine whether the axons that reach to the SCN form physiologically functional connections and induce recovery of circadian photo entrainment. Our preliminary evidence is suggesting that light can induce activity in SCN neurons by c-Fos staining. 6 months after pre-chiasm lesion, we cut the contralateral optic nerve, place the mice under constant darkness, and monitor each individual’s free-running activity. Then, we examined whether a light pulse during subjective night (CT16-17) can induce c-Fos-positive cells within the SCN in regenerated mice. It has been demonstrated that regenerating axons are lack of myelin and the electrical signal transduction is greatly reduced. We also tested this in our model by giving mice 4-Aminopyridine (4-AP) to enhance axonal transduction. Usually, we could detect c-Fos activation in 1/3 of the regenerated mice at 6 months after injury. After 4-AP, c-Fos can been detected in almost all mice. It suggested that lack of remyelination is another player for the lack of functional recovery in our system. Then we did the running wheel experiment. Although c-Fos could be stimulated by light, indicating the neuronal activity in SCN, we did not find significant difference in the photo entrainment. SCN projecting RGCs are mainly M1 and M2 ipRGCs. To explore the reason of the lack of behavior change, we investigated whether these two cell types actually regenerated their axons into the SCN. By using Ptenf/f;Socs3f/f;Opn4-GFP mice, where GFP mainly labels M1–M3 ipRGCs, we found that although CTB-labeled axons regenerated into SCN, few GFP+ axons regenerated at short distance after the pre-chiasm lesion and none could be detected in the SCN or other brain region. The regeneration was like the intraorbital optic nerve crush we published previously (Li et al., 2016). It indicated that at least the majority of the cell types innervating the SCN were not M1-M3 ipRGCs, even if we cannot exclude the possibility that some M1-M2 ipRGCs may still be able to regenerate their axons due to the sensitivity of Opn4-GFP mice (Bray et al., 2019). Alpha RGCs have been demonstrated to regenerate their axons by Pten KO. We believe that alpha RGCs possibly together with other cell types regenerated in Pten;Socs3 double KO.

16103315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103315.value: A major obstacle following adult optic nerve injury is the regeneration of retinal ganglion cell (RGC) axons and their reconnection with target neurons. By modulating intrinsic mechanisms, we have shown that RGC axons can regeneration for a long distance within the optic nerve after intraorbital crush. However, only a few axons innervate the brain. We demonstrated that after a prechiasm lesion, retinal axons robustly reinnervate the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) region , re-form synapses with neurons in the SCN as shown by electron microscopic evidence, and re-integrate with the existing circuitry as shown by trans-synaptic tracing evidence. We also showed that electric stimulation of the regenerated optic nerve induces post-synaptic excitatory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs) by using brain slice preparation. However, even 6 months after the injury, we did not detect clear functional change by performing the photo entrainment. One of the reasons could be the cell types innervating the nucleus are not the original type.

16103315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103315.value: Our finding supports that axon rewiring can occur after injury in adult CNS. However, in order to achieve detectable behaviour change, many other factors may contribute. One of the factor could be the correct cell types are necessary to mediate functional rewiring. This hypothesis need to be further examined in the future.

16103315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103315.value: Our study illustrated modulating several molecular pathways can promote regeneration of retinal axons after optic nerve injury. We investigated whether the combination of several intrinsic mechanisms can promote axonal reinnervation into SCN and reconnection. Our study has the potential to identify a potential strategy to promote functional recovery after CNS injury.

16103515.label: Realisation of objectives
16103515.value: Microglia, the tissue-resident macrophages in the central nervous system (CNS), are the immune cells responsible for removing infectious agents, damaged cells and plaques in the CNS. Recent studies in animal models and human samples have documented that, in addition to functioning as scavengers to maintain homeostasis of the CNS, microglia also play critical roles in the regulation of neural development, synapse formation and neuronal activity. The important functions of microglia are further supported by the observations that the onset and progression of various neuronal disorders, such as Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis, Multiple Sclerosis, Parkinson's and Alzheimer’s diseases, are often closely associated with the dysregulation of microglia development and microglia function. Hence, a comprehensive understanding of how microglia population is established and maintained in the CNS and how they function under physiological and pathological conditions may offer new therapeutic opportunities for the treatment of these neurodegenerative diseases. Yet, despite extensive effort in the past decades, how microglial precursors - macrophages born in peripheral hematopoietic tissues home to and subsequently colonize the CNS remains largely undefined. In the proposal, we proposed to utilize the unique advantages of in vivo imaging and genetic manipulation of zebrafish to delineate the cellular and molecular basis underlying the brain colonization process by peripheral macrophages. To define the trajectory of microglia homing, we first monitored the temporal and spatial distributions of microglia in the developing zebrafish brain and found that the majority of microglia are localized in the optic tectum of the midbrain. We therefore focused on this region and performed time-lapse imaging on Tg(-2.8elavl3:eGFP;coro1a:DsRedx) double transgenic fish, in which neurons and microglia/microglial precursors are marked by GFP and DsRedx respectively. Our results show that microglial precursors enter the optic tectum of the midbrain predominantly via two routes: the bi-lateral periphery of the midbrain between the eyes and brain along the sheet of meninx, and the ventral periphery of the brain by passing through the ventral part of the midbrain. We next asked whether entry of microglial precursors into the brain depends on circulation or not. By using Tg(kdrl:eGFP;coro1a:DsRedx) double transgenic line, in which the vessels and microglia/microglial precursors are marked by GFP and DsRedx respectively, we showed that microglial precursors enter the brain directly from peripheral tissue without entering the blood circulation. To further support this is indeed the case, we blocked the blood circulation by knocking down the expression of tnnt2a, a gene is required for heartbeat in zebrafish and we documented that the colonization of the developing brain by microglial precursors is not affected in the circulation-defective tnnt2a embryos. Collectively, these data demonstrate that microglial precursors colonize the brain, at least during early development, in a circulation-independent fashion. The next intriguing question was how microglial precursors are attracted into the brain. We notice that the temporal and spatial appearance of neuronal cell death in the developing zebrafish brain correlates remarkably well with the time window and location of microglial colonization. This prompted us to speculate that neuronal cell death may play a critical role in regulating microglia colonization of the brain by generating specific signals. Indeed, when we block neuronal cell death by overexpressing bcl-2 under the neural-specific β-tubulin promoter, the colonization of the optic tectum by microglial precursors are significantly reduced entering. These data indicate that the colonization of the optic tectum by microglial precursors are driven by apoptotic neuronal death. To further define the chemotaxis signals that attract microglial precursors homing to the optic tectum, we used candidate approach. We found that lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC), a phospholipid known to be secreted by apoptotic cells, act as a chemoattractant to promote microglial precursors entering the brain. In contrast, ATP, which has been previously shown to participate in microglia activation and migration, appears to have no significant effect on microglia colonization. These data demonstrate that LPC but not ATP is a potent chemoattractant to promote microglial precursors entering the developing brain. We went on to show that knockdown of the expression of gpr132b, the zebrafish counterpart of the mammalian G-protein-coupled receptors G2A for LPC, reduces the number of microglia colonizing the brain. Taken together, these data demonstrate that microglia colonization in zebrafish utilizes an evolutionarily conserved LPC-G2A pathway. This work has been published in Developmental Cell (38:214-222, 2016). Finally, when we analyzed Tg(Xla.Tubb:bcl-2) transgenic fish, in which neuronal apoptosis is inhibited by the overexpression of an anti-apoptotic regulator Bcl-2 under the control of Xenopus neural-specific b-tubulin (Xla.Tubb) promoter, we noticed that the microglial precursors were able to migrate from their birthplace to the head region prior to the occurrence of extensive neuronal apoptosis, suggesting the existence of alternative signals attracting the migration of microglial precursors to the brain independent of neuronal cell death. In fact, the known “find-me” signals (e.g. nucleotides and lysophosphatidylcholine) released by apoptotic cells to attract phagocytes have been reported to be readily degraded in extracellular regions, therefore unlikely to serve as long-distance signals. Quantification of microglia in different parts of the CNS of Tg(Xla.Tubb:bcl-2) transgenic fish revealed that microglia colonization was not completely blocked in the absence of neuronal apoptosis. These evidences suggest that alternative mechanisms may contribute to the recruitment of microglial precursors to the head region and their subsequent colonization in certain CNS regions independent of neuronal apoptosis. These observations promoted us to propose to another research project for the identification of the second pathway mediating microglia colonization. Indeed, our later study has identified that Il34-Csf1ra pathway plays a critical role in microglia colonization. This work has recently published in Developmental Cell (46:552-563, 2018).

16103515.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103515.value: In sum, our study has defined the major migratory routes and the dynamic behaviors of microglial precursors during their colonization of the developing brain and uncovered the first molecular cue (lysophosphatidylcholine) and its cognate receptor (the G-protein-coupled receptors 132b) mediating microglia colonization of the brain. This work has been published in Developmental Cell (38:214-222, 2016). In addition, we have also uncover that the second molecular cue Il34 and its receptors Csf1ra plays a critical role in microglia colonization. This work has recently published in Developmental Cell (46:552-563, 2018). Our findings have provided the cellular and molecular basis for further in-depth studies of microglia in neural development and neurodegenerative diseases.

16103515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103515.value: Microglia are immune cells in the central nervous system (CNS), and they play important roles in the removal of infectious agents and cellular debris in the CNS as well as in the regulation of neuron development and function. Numerous studies in both animals and human patients have shown that dysregulation of microglia are closely associated with the development of many neurodegenerative diseases. Thus, understanding how microglia are formed and how they function may offer therapeutic strategies for the treatment of these neurodegenerative disorders. Because the precursors of microglia are born in the peripheral hematopoietic tissues, these microglial precursors need to migrate from their birthplace to the head region and then colonize the CNS. The main focus of this study is to dissect the migratory path which microglial precursors travel and the molecules mediating the migration of microglial precursors. Our study shows that microglial precursors migrate to the head region and enter the brain via two specific routes. The migration and colonization processes are circulation-independent and are specifically guided by two sets of molecules, secreted factors lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) and interleukin 34 (Il34) generated by the neurons in the CNS and membrane-bound proteins Gpr132b and Csf1a on the surface of microglial precursors.

16103615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103615.value: The cytoplasmic free calcium is a universal and versatile second messenger in plants. It has become a convergence point for disparate signal transduction pathways. The rise in cytoplasmic free calcium ion concentration, [Ca2+]cyt, is able to specify and transduce signals to downstream post-translational modification, to gene expression and finally to cellular events. A unique internal or external signal is able to induce a corresponding spatiotemporal pattern of calcium spike, which is defined by a unique amplitude, duration, frequency and subcellular locales of the calcium ion in cytoplasm. This signal-specific cellular calcium ion dynamics has been called as “calcium signature or calcium code”. These calcium codes subsequently translate the information of specific developmental and environmental signals into a web of downstream calcium-binding proteins, or calcium sensors, which then influence a subset of gene expression, post-translational modification (PTM, such as protein phosphorylation), enzymatic activity (such as kinase and phosphatase), protein trafficking and other cellular processes to trigger downstream physiological responses. A key question in calcium signaling is therefore how each calcium code is precisely translated into a set of unique and corresponding downstream cellular events, and how these multiple external and internal signals generate a combinatorial calcium signal to specify coordinated physiological responses in plants. To address these important questions of calcium signaling, we select blue light as external inducing signal and three mutants, phot1, phot2 and phot1phot2 double mutant, as experimental material. By systematically performing six pairs of SIML-based differential and quantitative PTM proteomic experiments, i.e. blue light irradiation of three pairs of Arabidopsis plants, wt/phot1, wt/phot2 and wt/phot1phot2 for 40 seconds and 90 seconds, we will unravel photoreceptor PHOT1 and PHOT2-dependent and calcium code-specific PTM profiles. Eventually, through performing protein-protein interactomics and in vitro and in vivo validation, we will couple the PHOT1 and PHOT2-specific calcium codes with the downstream biochemical PTM profile, or the so called PTM code, and further study how the PTM code is translated into downstream transcriptional activities and cellular and physiological responses. This work will represent an example of the multidisciplinary functional proteomics research that starts from large scale mass spectrometry analysis, to protein-protein interaction assays, and finally to in vivo functional substantiation. A close collaboration between PC and all Co-I will allow us to form a coherent research team equipped with all-around molecular and cellular research capabilities to decode these fundamental yet interesting calcium codes that have puzzled plant biologists for decades. 摘要 细胞质游离钙是植物具有普遍性和广泛使用的第二信使。它已成为不同的信号转导通路的一个汇聚点。这些不同细胞信号诱导细胞质游离钙离子浓度［Ca2 +］暂时升高。钙离子浓度短暂地变化可以诱导细胞信号转导至下游的翻译后修饰谱与基因表达，最后转到各种细胞活动。内部或外部的信号诱导的钙离子浓度峰是由一个具有特定的幅度，特定的持续时间，特定的频率和在细胞质中的钙离子的特定的亚细胞区域位置所定义的中间信号。这个信号特异的细胞钙离子浓度峰被称为“钙密码”。各种“钙密码”随后被翻译为特定的发育和环境生物信息，并转换成信号网络下游的钙传感器，钙结合蛋白质， 然后影响一组基因表达，部分的翻译后修饰（PTM，如蛋白质磷酸化），一定的酶活性（如激酶和磷酸酶）与部分的蛋白转运和其他细胞活动过程，最终触发下游生理反应。钙信号的一个关键问题是它如何由每个“钙密码”精确地翻译成一组独特的相应的下游细胞活动。这些外部和内部的多个信号是如何产生一个相应的具有特异性的组合钙信号，诱导协调的生理反应。为了解决“钙信号”的这些重要细胞生物的问题，我们选择蓝光信号和三个蓝光受体的突变体phot1，phot2和phot1phot2双突变体为试验材料。通过系统地在40秒和90秒的光诱导下，进行基于 SIML方法的差减和定量PTM蛋白质组学实验，做三对拟南芥植物野生型与phot1，野生型与 phot2和野生型与phot1phot2材料的差减和定量PTM蛋白质组学比对实验。我们将解开蓝光PHOT1受体和PHOT2受体依赖的，特定的“钙密码” 所调控地PTM 图谱。最终，通过进行蛋白质 - 蛋白质互作组和在体外和体内的进行功能验证。我们将结合下游生化PTM信息， 所谓的“PTM密码”，进一步研究PHOT1和PHOT2特异性“钙密码”如何 被转换为下游的“PTM密码”，导致基因表达和细胞生理反应。这项工作将代表涉及多学科的功能蛋白质组学研究的范例。从大规模质谱分析开始，到蛋白质 - 蛋白质相互 ，最后到体内功能检测。 课题主持者和所有参加者之间的密切合作，将使我们能够形成一个整体的研究团队。课题主持者实验室已配备了齐全的分子和细胞的研究设备，和高效地研究能力用以解码那些困惑植物生物学家数十年的，非常有趣的“钙密码”。

16103815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103815.value: Single cell extrusion from the epithelium is a process important for generation of diverse cell types, organ formation and tissue homeostasis. The cell extrusion process is regulated by signaling pathways. It is also a physical process during which the cells being extruded experience and respond to force, change shape and move out from the epithelium without compromising the epithelial integrity. It is largely unclear how the signaling pathways and mechanical processes are coordinated to drive single cell extrusion. We have established ventral nerve cord (VNC) neural stem cells (neuroblasts) during Drosophila embryogenesis as a model to dissect the molecular and cellular basis of single cell extrusion. This system provides unique opportunities to address this question because of the rich genetic and optical imaging tools available in Drosophila embryos. Here we propose to mechanistically study one key cellular event, apical constriction, during neuroblast delamination. Our preliminary results suggest that the dynamic actin-myosin network on the cell apical surface is critical for the apical constriction process in delaminating neuroblasts. In Objective 1 we will use live imaging and quantitative analysis to establish the relationship between the apical myosin dynamics and the cell apical area change in delaminating neuroblasts. In Objective 2 we will dissect the molecular network that temporally and spatially regulates the myosin dynamics to drive apical constriction in delaminating neuroblasts. 胚胎發育中，單細胞離層對細胞分化和器官形成等過程有重要作用。單細胞離層的分子和細胞機理尚不清楚。我們擬以果蠅胚胎發育過程中神經幹細胞離層為模式，利用該模式中豐富的遺傳學和顯微成像學工具，研究單細胞離層的過程和調控機制。特別地，我們將用定量生物學和活體成像的方法，研究單細胞離層的過程如何被動態的肌動蛋白網絡調控。

16103815.label: Realisation of objectives
16103815.value: Objective 1: Quantitative analysis of apical constriction rate and myosin dynamics in the delaminating neuroblasts. We optimized our imaging setting and established a computational imaging analysis pipeline to quantitatively track the apical constriction processes of delaminating neuroblasts with high spatiotemporal resolution. A neuroblast is initially indistinguishable from its neighbors by their apical shape or area. As a neuroblast initiates the delamination program, we start to see that its apical area steadily decreases while the neighboring cells maintain their apical area with fluctuations. The delaminating neuroblasts decrease their apical area at an average rate of 5 μm2min-1. Moreover, the delaminating neuroblasts also undergo pulses of rapid apical area constriction interrupted by phases of apical area stabilization. During the rapid constriction phase, the area constriction rate exceeds 10μm2min-1. On average, a presumptive neuroblast undergoes about 4.6 pulses in 6 min and reduces its area to 50% of its original value (An et al, 2017). We observed that dynamic myosin foci and fibers are present on the apical cell cortex across the embryo surface. Importantly, the myosin foci and fibers display pulsatile coalescence movements in delaminating neuroblasts similar to those observed in ventral furrow cells, which were defined as medial myosin pulses. It is noteworthy that a dynamic myosin signal is also present at adherens junctions in delaminating neuroblasts, unlike the case in ventral furrow cells where myosin predominantly localizes to the apical cortex. Through quantitative measurements of myosin intensity and correlation analysis of myosin intensity change rate with apical constriction rate, we found that the apical constriction rate is significantly correlated with the medial myosin intensity change rate rather than the junctional myosin intensity change rate (An et al, 2017). Objective 2: Investigation of the molecular regulatory mechanism of myosin dynamics in the delaminating neuroblasts. 1) Spatio-temporal regulation of myosin regulators RhoA and Rok in the delaminating neuroblasts. Using live imaging of the transgenic fly line expressing Rok-GFP, we found that Rok is distributed both in the medioapical cortex region of the cells and on cell junctions. Rok also coalesces into the cell center to form a condensed spot and disperses on the cell apical surface. We quantified the medial Rok intensity and found that the medial Rok has higher intensity in delaminating cells than non-delaminating cells. We then tried to block Rok activity using the widely used Rok inhibitor Y-27632. This inhibitor disrupted Rok activity in both the medial and junctional regions and lead to an overall disruption of epithelial integrity. RhoGEF2, a RhoA activator, is required to organize medial myosin pulses in ventral furrow cells (Mason et al, 2016) and cells in the ectoderm during Drosophila germband extension (Kerridge et al., 2016). We therefore used RhoGEF2 RNAi to examine its effects in neuroblast delamination. In RhoGEF2 RNAi embryos, we observed a significant reduction of the medial myosin intensity but not the junctional myosin intensity, consistent with published results. Consequently, we observed a lower number of cells that undergo delamination in RhoGEF2 RNAi embryos (An et al, 2017). Together, these results suggested that spatiotemporal regulation of RhoA-Rok-Myosin activity is important for neuroblast delamination. 2) Investigation of the planar cell polarity system in the delaminating neuroblasts. We have found that E-cadherin and Bazooka remain enriched at the DV edges during the apical constriction process in delaminating neuroblasts. This result suggested that cell-cell intercalation and apical constriction occur at the same time in the delaminating neuroblasts and it is likely that the junctional myosin dynamics and the radial myosin pulses are mediating two different processes. 3) Investigation of the Snail family protein function in regulating the myosin dynamics of the delaminating neuroblasts. We have found that snail and twist RNAi does not affect the apical constriction process in the delaminating neuroblasts (An et al 2017). 4) Investigation of the Notch signaling function in regulating the myosin dynamics of the delaminating neuroblasts. To understand how differential Notch signaling activity in a proneural cluster affects the delamination process, in particular the apical constriction process, we lowered Notch signaling activity by injecting the embryos with Delta RNAi or Notch RNAi. We observed that clusters of cells, which all adopt neuroblast fate, undergo apical constriction. Individual cells from a delaminating cluster still undergo pulses of apical constriction correlated with the dynamic change of medial myosin intensity. However, on average, these cells in the Delta RNAi embryos reduce their apical area at a rate of 2.5 μm2min-1, slower than the rate of delaminating neuroblasts in water-injected control embryos. These cells in the Delta RNAi embryos exhibit a reduction of medial myosin pulse frequency from 0.8 pulse/min to 0.5 pulse/min in comparison with control. On a close examination of the myosin network, we noticed a strong accumulation of myosin fibers and cables around the junctional region in the delaminating cells in the Delta or Notch RNAi embryos, indicating that differential Notch signaling activity is necessary for sustaining normal myosin pattern in the neuroectoderm. 16103815.label: Major findings and research outcome
16103815.value: Cell delamination is a conserved morphogenetic process important for generation of cell diversity and maintenance of tissue homeostasis. In this project we used Drosophila embryonic neuroblasts as a model to study the apical constriction process during cell delamination. We observe dynamic myosin signals both around the cell adherens junctions and underneath the cell apical surface in the neuroectoderm. The non-junctional myosin forms flows and pulses on the cell apical cortex, which are termed as medial myosin pulses. Quantitative differences in medial myosin pulse intensity and frequency are critical to distinguish delaminating neuroblasts from their neighbors. Inhibition of medial myosin pulses blocks delamination. The fate of neuroblasts is set apart from their neighbors by Notch signaling-mediated lateral inhibition. When we inhibit Notch signaling activity in the embryo, we observe that small clusters of cells undergo apical constriction and display an abnormal apical myosin pattern. Together, we demonstrate that a contractile actomyosin network across the apical cell surface is organized to drive apical constriction in delaminating neuroblasts.

16103815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103815.value: Through quantitative live imaging analysis, we have found that quantitative differences in medial myosin pulse amplitude and frequency are critical to distinguish delaminating neuroblasts from their neighbors. What remains unknown is how differential Notch signaling activities between delaminating neuroblasts and their neighbors is interpreted to set up a highly dynamic and quantitatively refined actomyosin pattern across the epithelial tissue. We are in the process of establishing optogenetic methods to control Notch signaling activity with high spatiotemporal precision in vivo to study how Notch signaling dynamics, including dose and duration, regulates fate determination and morphogenesis processes coordinately and drive orderly single cell delamination.

16103815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103815.value: Single cell delamination is an important morphogenetic event for generating diverse cell types during organogenesis. In this project we successfully established Drosophila embryonic neuroblasts as a new model to study single cell delamination (An et al. 2017). The optical and genetic accessibility of this model provides an ideal system to dissect how cell signaling is coupled with mechanical processes and regulates precise cellular morphogenesis processes.

16104115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104115.value: 真核生物用於識別複製起始序列的六聚体復合物（ORC），在功能和結構上高度保守；但是ORC結合DNA序列的特異性卻比較多樣化，甚至在進化上比較接近而不同種類的酵母之間，其DNA結合的序列也很不相同。ORC的保守結合序列ACS，在釀酒酵母（Saccharomyces cerevisiae，Sc）中為17-bp的序列，而在乳酸克鲁维酵母（Kluyveromyces lactis，Kl）中則為50-bp。相對而言，在裂殖酵母（Schizosaccharomyces pombe）和高等真核生物中，ORC的結合位點在序列上沒有同源性。在此研究計劃中，我們將致力於探究ORC結合DNA序列特異性的決定因素。我們初步的研究結果顯示，由Sc-N端和Kl-C端的ORC4嵌合體可以改變ORC復合体的DNA結合特異性。首先，帶有ORC4嵌合體的Sc菌株會出現HMR位點基因沉默的缺陷；其次，該菌株支持帶有KlARS的質粒的正常複製；第三，ChIPseq分析顯示嵌合的ORC在Sc酵母菌中可以結合KlARS同源序列。這些結果表明Orc4蛋白的C端足以決定ORC復合体的DNA序列特異性的結合。在此基礎上，我們進一步細化Orc4C端在ORC復合体識別DNA序列中的作用，並發現其WH區域非常重要。我們計劃用NMR方法確定該WH的結構，並用突變方法來驗證其關鍵氨基酸的作用。由此研究得出的結果，將會為我們提供有價值的信息，使我們可以更深入理解DNA複製機理，並有助于發現癌症藥物治療和檢測的新靶標。

16104115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16104115.value: The six-subunit eukaryotic Origin Recognition Complex (ORC) is highly conserved in structure and function but diverged in DNA binding specificity even among yeast species. The underlying mechanism for this divergence was largely unknown and remains a long-standing question in the field of DNA replication. In this project, we combined biochemical, structural, and genomic approaches to address the specificity of ORC in origin selection. We discovered that eukaryotic ORC has acquired new elements to augment the cross-kingdom conserved DNA binding modules. We identified three critical motifs from yeast ORC subunits important for sequence-specific recognition of ARS consensus sequence (ACS) DNA. Notably, a basic patch of Orc1 is fully inserted into the minor groove of the ACS DNA for a half turn atop of all the other DNA-binding modules. This insertion is facilitated by Orc2-ISM, which also places its residues deep into the minor groove. These two motifs form three hydrogen bonds with the thymines from the ACS in the minor groove of origin DNA. Another important motif contributing to the sequence-specific interaction is a special insertion α-helix (IH) in the β-hairpin of Orc4-WHD. Orc4-IH is deeply inserted into the major groove of the ACS to contact a stretch of thymine nucleotides. Together, yeast ORC establishes its specific binding with the ACS DNA using these three motifs to contact the bases of the corresponding nucleotides, most of which involve thymine nucleotides. These results perfectly explain why the yeast ACS DNA has to be AT-rich sequence. Interestingly, the special insertion α-helix from Orc4 is completely absent in metazoans. Given the fact that this Orc4-IH is absent in metazoans, Orc1-BP may be the major or sole determinant for DNA recognition and hence the more relaxed sequence specificity for ORC in metazoans. Our further genomic analyses indicate that this short motif is responsible for the divergent specificity of ORC for origin DNA among different species. Our studies provide critical insights into the mechanisms regulating the divergent specificity of ORC in origin recognition. The results of this research produced two publications, one review paper in the journal Molecular Cell and the other one research article in the journal Nature.

16104115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16104115.value: Our discovery of how yeast ORC determines its specific DNA binding allowed us to further investigate the roles of ORC in origin selection and promoting helicase assembly in both yeast and higher eukaryotes.

16104115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16104115.value: How did life begin on this planet? The ability to replicate or propagate is the primordial definition of life. Cells propagate by making copies of themselves through replicating their DNA genome. Aberrant DNA replication is the cause of many cancers and developmental disorders. But where and how to start DNA replication in our human cells are still not clear. Our recent study found that the machine named origin recognition complex (ORC) interplays with DNA to decide the sites where to clamp on. ORC then sits there to serve as a landmark to attract DNA helicase which helps to unzip DNA duplex for initiating genome replication. The results produced from this study has been published in the journal Nature on 12 July 2018. The knowledge derived from this project could potentially be used to devise targets for interfering DNA replication in cancer therapy.

16104315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16104315.value: An essential step in human DNA replication initiation is the assembly of the pre-replication complex (pre-RC) at replication origins. The pre-RC consists of Cdc6, MCM(2-7), ORC(1-6), and Cdt1. For the past eight years, our group has been studying the molecular mechanism of the human DNA pre-replication complex and its relationship with human disease by using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopic techniques, in addition to biophysical and biochemical methods. We focus on the structural basis of interactions among pre-RC proteins and DNA to illustrate the molecular assembly processes, regulations and possible connections with various types of cancer. Our efforts have produced many intriguing results: (a) the NMR structure of Cdt1-Mcm6 complex in solution, providing insight into the mechanism by which MCM is recruited to replication origins by Cdt1 in humans(12), (b) the molecular mechanism underlying geminin inhibition of DNA replication (unpublished data) and its role in cell proliferation/differentiation in humans(23), (c) the structure of Cdc6/G-quadraplex, which may mediate human origin recognition and DNA replication in EBV mediated cancers (unpublished result), and (d) the cell cycle can also be regulated by methyltransferase SET8 (26), adding another level of DNA replication control in human cells. In this proposal, our group is particularly interested in the structural-functional study of human Orc6/DNA complex. Human Orc6, the least conserved component of ORC, is known to be essential in S phase DNA replication and cytokinesis. Knockdown of Orc6 completely halts human DNA replication. It was recently discovered that C-terminal mutations are associated with Meier-Gorlin syndrome(MGS). In addition, it was reported that Orc6 and DNA binding protein HMGa1 form a complex to facilitate human DNA replication origin recognition. Orc6 is also a cancer marker and subsequent anti-cancer drug target as its knock down sensitizes response to chemotherapy. We have determined the initial NMR structure of Orc6/DNA complex in solution as this complex cannot be crystalized. We found that Orc1 and Orc2 interact with Orc6. This initial result warrants the pursuit of further structural-functional studies of Orc6/DNA and other Orc6 complexes to understand the molecular mechanism of Orc6 mediated origin recognition and its related diseases, such as cancer and MGS. The resulting structure of Orc6/DNA complex could be used for computerized lead compound screening for developing therapies against Orc6 related diseases. The results from the proposed research will help elucidate fundamental biological questions of human DNA replication and for the potential treatment of cancer.

16104315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16104315.value: The initiation of cellular DNA replication is tightly controlled event which includes the formation of higher-order nucleoprotein complexes at the chromosomal origins of DNA replication. The eukaryotic initiator, ORC (origin recognition complex), binds to the origins of DNA replication and, working together with the loading factors Cdc6 and Cdt1, it recruits the MCM2-7 (minichromosome maintenance) replicative helicase resulting in a formation of the pre-replicative complex (pre-RC) at replication origins. The MCM complex is loaded onto double-stranded DNA as an inactive double-hexamer, and is activated after origin firing in the S-phase to trigger DNA replication. The exact roles of ORC during the execution of the replication initiation program are long-standing questions in the field. The Orc6 protein is the least conserved and perhaps the most enigmatic of all ORC subunits and amino acid alignments between budding yeast and metazoan proteins do not show statistically significant homologies. In budding yeast, Orc6 is essential for viability but is not required for DNA binding in vitro. In Drosophila, Orc6 is an integral part of whole ORC and is essential for both DNA binding and replication activity both in vitro and in vivo. The isolated Drosophila Orc6 can bind DNA directly with the preference for the poly(dA) sequences. In Xenopus and humans, Orc6 protein does not seem to be tightly associated with other core ORC subunits. Human Orc6 can bind DNA directly with little or no sequence specificity. In both, Drosophila and human cells, Orc6 has been implicated in coordinating cytokinesis with pre-RC formation and chromosome segregation, a role that it performs independently of the rest of the complex. Although the full length human Orc6 structure was not resolved, a conserved C-terminal α helix was found to interact with Orc3. Remarkably, the mutations in this motif disrupt the interaction of Orc6 with Orc3 and the rest of the ORC resulting in defects in pre-RC assembly and reduction of MCM2–7 loading in Drosophila. Specific tyrosine 232 to serine mutation in this region of Orc6 is linked to the Meier-Gorlin syndrome, a form of primordial dwarfism in humans. Despite the functional diversity of Orc6 in different organisms, the protein is required for DNA replication and is critical for ORC function in all studied species. Previous structural analysis showed that human Orc6, HsOrc6, shares the homology with transcription factor TFIIB and is able to bind DNA directly. However, the structure of full length HsOrc6 and the detailed mechanism of Orc6/DNA interaction remain elusive. Here, we present the full length HsOrc6 in apo form which contains three independent domains HsOrc6-N (residues 1–94), HsOrc6-M (residues 95–187) and HsOrc6-C (residues 188–252). Especially, we identified HsOrc6 DNA binding domain, HsOrc6-DBD, spanning residues 95-207. Furthermore, we provide a structural model of HsOrc6-DNA complex based on the experimental NMR data as well as the functional studies that demonstrate the importance of HsOrc6-DBD in DNA replication.

16104315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16104315.value: The molecular mechanism of how the human Orc6 functions in DNA replication and is connected to the human disease remains unclear. In our preliminary study, we found that hOrc6 formed phase-separated droplets only in the presence of DNA both in vitro and in vivo. The propensity of hOrc6 phase separation was directly correlated to the length of DNA. After identifying the DNA binding sites of hOrc6 through NMR structural study of the hOrc6/DNA complex, we showed that hOrc6 mutants with defective DNA binding abrogated the hOrc6-mediated DNA replication and phase separation. The DNA replication regulatory protein Geminin, which was reported to inhibit the activity of DNA replication initiation through direct binding to Cdt1, can readily diffuse into the hOrc6-DNA droplets while the GST protein used as a control cannot. The deeper understanding of this phase transition could explain the new mechanism of pre-RC formation in human which will be different from what we know from yeast. Meanwhile, we have screened a few compounds that could be to block the DNA binding of human Orc6. We hope it could be anti-cancer drugs. We have also studied the binding between Orc6 and G-quadruplex DNAs, single strand DNA and RNA. the results have been reported.

16104315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16104315.value: The six-subunit origin recognition complex (ORC), a DNA replication initiator, defines the localization of the origins of replication in eukaryotes. The Orc6 is the smallest and the least conserved among ORC subunits. It is required for the DNA replication and essential for viability in all species. In metazoans Orc6 binds DNA by itself and is structurally homologous to TFIIB transcription factor suggesting its role in positioning whole ORC complex at the origins. Here we report a solution structure of the full length human Orc6 alone and in a complex with DNA. The detailed analysis of the structure revealed novel amino acid clusters important for DNA binding. Alterations of these amino acids abolish DNA binding ability of Orc6 and result in reduced levels of DNA replication. We propose that Orc6 is a DNA binding subunit of human/metazoan ORC and may play role in targeting, positioning and assembly of the functional ORC at the origins. We also developed new strategy to resolve multiple Orc6 binding sites on DNA to determine final structures.

16200315.label: Project Objectives
16200315.value: To investigate and characterize the properties and structures of surfaces loaded with dust. The effects of surface materials, dust sizes and dust loading mechanisms will be examined. To develop a mathematical model to describe the resuspension process of aerosols on dusty surfaces. The model will consider the effects and dynamics of multi-particles and will be verified by a series of experiments. To study the resuspension of bioaerosols – bacteria, virus, and fungus aerosols - from surfaces loaded with dust and larger particles. The different resuspension behavior between real bioaerosols and simple liquid droplet/ solid particles will also be compared. To investigate the impact of resuspension on the viability of the microorganisms. A procedural method from cultivation of microorganisms to measurement of viability loss after resuspension will be proposed.

16200315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200315.value: When pathogenic airborne microorganisms deposit and settle on indoor surfaces, these surfaces become contaminated. They not only pose risks to occupants who make contact with the surfaces, but also the deposited microorganisms can be resuspended back into the air once the surface is disrupted by airflow or other human activities. Many site measurement studies found significant resuspension of microorganisms in hospital environments during various human activities on the premises. However, well-controlled particle resuspension studies suggested that typical indoor airflow conditions and vibrational force from human activities generally cannot cause resuspension. Such difference could be due to the fact that realistic indoor surfaces are often loaded with dust and other large particles, while other well-controlled studies investigated particle resuspension from clean solid surfaces. When micrometer and submicron airborne microorganisms deposit on surfaces loaded with dust, they may agglomerate to form larger particles, which are easier to be resuspended compared to the original bioaerosols. It is also possible that when the bioaerosols, the dust and the larger particles slip on the surface, the agglomeration is further enhanced by the microscopic airflow current generated. Also, other studies of particle resuspension used simple solid particles instead of realistic bioaerosols containing microorganisms. It is important to understand pathogenic microorganism resuspension under realistic conditions. This project proposes to carry out step-by-step experimental and theoretical analyses to study the resuspension of microorganism particles from surfaces loaded with dust. A number of different surface materials will be loaded with different degrees of test dust particles. The deposited dust structure will not simply be single-layer and will be characterized. In the experiments, freeze-dried bacteria, virus and fungus powder will be used to simulate dried bioaerosols; while bacteria, viruses and funguses droplets will be used to simulate bioaerosols with water content. A set of experiments without the test bioaerosols, but instead using monodisperse particles and droplets, will first be conducted to characterize the force required for resuspension from dusty surfaces. A mathematical model will be developed to describe the physics. The next step will be to investigate the test bioaerosols with microorganisms. Centrifuge and wind tunnel experiments will be conducted to study the bioaerosol resuspension under different conditions. This proposed project will tackle the discrepancy between the site measurement and well-controlled studies on particle resuspension, and enhance our knowledge on the resuspension of pathogenic microorganisms from realistic indoor surfaces as well as the related risk to occupants. 當空氣中致病的微生物沉降在室內的表面上，這些表面便受到污染。這將會對居住者構成風險，因為不僅當居住者接觸到這些表面時，他們有感染的危機；而且當這些已沉積的微生物，被氣流或其他人類活動擾亂時，它們有機會再懸浮回到空氣中。在醫院等環境配合各種人類活動時，許多實地測量的研究發現微生物顯著出現再懸浮的情況。但另一方面，實驗室內顆粒再懸浮的研究結果顯示，一般室內氣流和人類活動引致的振動力並不足夠使顆粒再懸浮。這種差異可能是由於在真實環境下，室內表面通常佈滿灰塵等較大的顆粒；然而在控制良好的實驗室內，研究用的表面通常是經過潔淨或特別的處理程序。當空氣中微米及亞微米級的微生物沉降在佈滿灰塵的表面上，它們有機會和灰塵聚集而形成更大的顆粒，使得其相比原來的微生物，更容易被再懸浮。也有可能的是，當這些生物氣溶膠、粉塵及較大的顆粒，因各種擾亂而在表面上滑行時，它們會因為所產生的氣流而進一步凝聚成更大的顆粒。現時顆粒再懸浮的研究，一般使用簡單的固體顆粒，而不是含有微生物的生物氣溶膠。若能以真實的微生物作研究，這對了解真實環境下致病微生物再懸浮的現象是很重要的。本項目擬以實驗及理論分析逐步研究生物氣溶膠在佈滿灰塵的表面上的再懸浮這課題。若干不同材料的表面將被加載不同程度的試驗粉塵顆粒用以模擬及分析真實環境表面，沉積的灰塵結構不可能簡單的單層形式，不同的結構特徵將被分類及分析。另外，在實驗中，冷凍脫水的細菌、病毒和真菌粉末將被用來模擬固體生物氣溶膠；培養液中的細菌、病毒和真菌將被用於模擬液體生物氣溶膠。在進行生物氣溶膠的實驗之前，首先進行的是使用固定體積的顆粒和液滴的實驗，用以分析氣溶膠在佈滿灰塵的表面上的再懸浮有關的力學。並將會建立一個數學模型用以描述中當的物理現象。下一步便使用存在微生物的氣溶膠的研究。離心機和風洞實驗將分步進行，用以研究不同條件下的生物氣溶膠再懸浮情況，及其對微生物的存活效果。此項目將解釋實地測量及實驗室研究結果之間的差異，並提升我們對病原微生物再懸浮的知識，及對居住者的相關風險。

16200315.label: Realisation of objectives
16200315.value: The overall objectives have been achieved. The characterization of particle deposit by gravitational deposition was investigated first. A comprehensive resuspension investigation on both solid particles and liquid particles was conducted. Different resuspension mechanisms (e.g. by centrifuge and by wind tunnel) were studied. Bioaerosol with bacteria (Escherichia coli, ATCC 11303) and viruses (bacteriophage T3, ATCC 11303-B3) were also investigated. Some key results are shown below. Dusty surfaces with different dust loadings were reproduced by a deposition chamber for characterization and investigation. An optical profiler was employed to measure the surface profile of the dusty surface. After the measurement, arithmetic mean roughness (Ra), root mean square roughness (RMS), area fraction and porosity of dust were determined. The Ra was used to predict the type of deposit such as monolayer, intermediate, and multilayer. The RMS showed the spread of height distribution. A simulation model was also developed to estimate the Ra, RMS, area fraction, and porosity. The simulated characteristics resulted in a good agreement with the experimental result. It is also found that the particle size distribution is important. For example, all characteristics increase with increasing standard deviation of particle size distribution. Equations were also constructed to estimate the characteristics with different standard deviations. It is useful to evaluate the characterization of particle deposit by the simulation method when particle size distribution and dust loading are known. The characterization of particle deposit is important to particle deposition and resuspension analysis. By using centrifugal method, two types of resuspension experiments were carried out: the resuspension of the dust particles (without PE particles) and the resuspension of the targeted PE particles on the dusty surfaces. The results of applying centrifugal force in normal and tangential directions were similar; the remaining dust loading, the Ra and RMS values all started at a dramatic decrease (the first stage), and in the subsequent second stage, the rates of decreases became smaller with increasing rotational speed. In the case of the resuspension of the targeted PE particles, in both normal and tangential directions, the remaining fractions generally decreased with an increasing force field and with increasing dust loading, while a smaller force field is required for tangential direction. Calculated remaining fractions fit well to the experimental data by assuming a log‐normal distributed adhesive force. It was found that the reduction of adhesion increased with increasing dust loading but was independent of the particle size. Regarding the spread of adhesion, no obvious relation to particle size and dust loading was found, but the values were at the same order of magnitude. Finally, it was found that the presence of dust reduces the adhesion of PE particles and the reduction increases with increasing dust loading by one to two orders of magnitude. In an experiment for the resuspension of liquid aerosols, a wind tunnel which can generate a fully developed turbulent flow was employed. The resuspension behaviour of a droplet on different dust loadings, namely 0, 0.3, 0.5, 1, and 2 g/m2 on PMMA surfaces was investigated. The critical friction velocity, critical length, and sliding velocity were also investigated in the experiment. It was found that the critical friction velocity decreased with increasing droplet diameter and the critical friction velocity of 0 g/m2 dust loading was greater than the critical friction velocity of the surfaces with dust particles. The critical friction velocity was fitted to an empirical exponential relation and the corresponding exponents were around 0.5 for all cases of dust loading. With respect to the critical length, this increased with increasing droplet proportionally and the coefficient in the linear relation was about 0.922 for all dust loadings and droplet diameters in the experiment. The presence of the dust particles did not result in a significant effect on the critical length. In the case of sliding velocity, the result was that the sliding velocity was very scattered with different droplet diameters and there was no obvious trend for the sliding velocity. However, there was a range of figures for sliding velocity. Comparing the sliding velocity to the friction velocity of the wind tunnel, the order of the magnitude of the friction velocity was about 1, which was much larger than the sliding velocity. The removal of the droplet was analyzed and the removal force was directly proportional to the droplet diameter and contact angle hysteresis. The relation of the adhesive force was the same as the removal force, and is directly proportional to the droplet diameter and contact angle hysteresis. Then a procedural method to investigate the bacterium and virus survivability in the whole process was developed. A vibrating orifice aerosol generator which generated monodispersed aerosol, or a cough generator which was a custom-built aerosolization system controlled by an Arduino system and able to simulating a cough process, was used for aerosol generation. Mixture of microorganism and artificial saliva solution consisted of 76 g of glycerol and 12 g of Sodium Chloride (NaCl) in 1 litre of sterilized water was used, and the non-volatile material accounted for 6% in volume of the initial droplet volume, which is similar to the actual volume ratio of human respiratory fluid. For the survivability investigation, the substrate surface was cut into two symmetrical pieces by a sterilized scissor. One part was used to count the size-resolved bioaerosol by a microscope. The other part was put into 5 mL sterilized water to extract and enumerate the deposited bacteria or virus by cultivation. Serial dilution and pour plate method were employed. The agar plate containing 30-300 Colony forming units (CFUs) for bacteria or Plaque forming units (PFUs) for viruses were found the best for enumeration In a study of detachment of microorganism-laden droplet from dusty surface by centrifugal method, micrometer-sized droplets with rod-shaped bacteria, Escherichia coli (E.coli), were generated using a vibrating orifice aerosol generator. The droplet was a mixture of glycerol and water to simulate the nucleus of saliva. The droplet was deposited on a dusty substrate and the contact diameter of the droplet was captured by a microscope. After the resuspension experiment, Tryptone soya agar was pour at the cap of a substrate holder. Detached bacteria-laden droplet was deposited on the agar. The E.coli on the agar and the dusty substrate were cultured for 12 hours and the colony forming unit were compared. By comparing the pure droplet with the bacteria-laden droplet, the bacteria-laden droplet was partially detached and E.coli can be found in both the detached portion and the remained portion. There were more bacteria on the detached portion which was about 5 to 10 times of that in the remained portions. Indeed, it is suggested that both the partially detached bacteria-laden droplet and the remained portions on the surface can be a source of bioaerosol. Moreover, it was found that the dust itself does not have effect on the survivability of the E.coli in this study.
