16200315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200315.value: The characterization of the dust deposit for different dust loadings and particle sizes were first investigated. A simulation model was developed to predict the Ra, RMS, area fraction, and porosity in different dust deposit structures: monolayer, intermediate, and multilayer. Then both the resuspension of dust particles and the resuspension of targeted particles on dusty surface were investigated by a centrifugal method (Lee et al. 2019). It was found that dust particles were resuspended by two stages with different rates of resuspension. For the resuspension of the particles on the dusty surface, the remaining fraction of the targeted particles decreased with increasing force field and dust loading. Dust could greatly reduce the adhesion of the particles from one to two orders of magnitude depending on loadings. Similarly, in the investigation of resuspension of a droplet from dusty surfaces in a wind tunnel, it was found that the contact angle hysteresis increased with decreasing dust loading. The critical friction velocity for droplet detachment was found to be fitted well in an exponential equation. In other words, the adhesion of the droplet declined with increasing dust loading (Lee’s PhD thesis). This gives an explanation to the discrepancy between the field and the laboratory studies, because in real situations, dust plays an important role in resuspension which was neglected in most of the laboratory studies. Then we investigated the detachment of microorganism-laden droplets from the dusty surfaces (Leung et al. 2019) and proposed a procedural method from cultivation of microorganisms to the measurement of viability loss (Wang et al. 2020, under review). In a centrifuge experiment, after rotation, the dust showed a pinning effect on the remained portion of droplets giving a ring-shaped of their original diameters. The droplets were partially detached and E.coli can be found in both the detached portion and the remained portion. The remaining droplets with bacteria were found to be smaller than the case without bacteria (i.e. a larger amount of volume of droplet were detached with bacteria inside). Therefore, the resuspension dynamics for bacterium-laden and virus/nanoparticle-laden droplets (Fu et al. 2018) are different. Since the bacteria (E. Coli) were rod-shaped, and about 1.0-2.0 μm long and 0.25–1.0μm in diameter, which is much larger than that of virus/nanoparticles, but not much smaller than that of the droplets (10-50 μm). It is also found that the dust itself didn’t affect the survivability of the E.coli in this study.

16200315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200315.value: During the wind tunnel experiment, it was found that if the substrate sample was not held firmly, it would vibrate when the wind speed exceeds a threshold (this is a flow-induced vibration phenomenon, which was not the focus of this project), but enhanced particle resuspension was observed. Other than the dust effect, this inspired us for another possible reason for the apparently opposite findings between the field and the laboratory studies. Further research efforts can be put into investigating the flow-induced fluttering mechanism. Moreover, bioaerosol particles are not always spherical, and may be irregular in shapes. Shapes have dominant role in particle dynamics, especially the rolling behavior before resuspension. A detailed study of particles of different shapes such as spherical, cylindrical, ellipsoidal shapes are essential in further developing the resuspension model in the future. Furthermore, our result shows that viabilities of the microorganisms didn’t depend on the dust. Since the dust used in this project was sterilized Arizona test dust and its major component is silicon. The same result cannot be applied to other kind of dusts (e.g. household dust) and further investigation into other dusts is recommended, but a proper sterilization process is needed to be carefully examined.

16200315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200315.value: When pathogenic airborne microorganisms deposit and settle on indoor surfaces, these surfaces become contaminated. They not only pose risks to occupants who make contact with the surfaces, but also become a secondary source of indoor air pollution when they are resuspended back into the air once the surface is disrupted. Many site measurement studies found significant resuspension of microorganisms during various human activities. However, well-controlled laboratory studies suggested that typical indoor airflow conditions generally cannot cause resuspension. Such difference could be due to the fact that realistic indoor surfaces are often loaded with dust, while well-controlled studies investigated particle resuspension from clean solid surfaces. This project carry out step-by-step experimental and theoretical analyses to study the resuspension of particles from dusty surfaces. The deposited dust structure with different loadings were characterized first. The resuspension behaviours of both liquid and solid bioaerosol were investigated under different scenarios. It is found that dust could greatly reduce the adhesion of the particles from one to two orders of magnitude depending on loadings and promote resuspension. The findings enhance our knowledge on the resuspension of pathogenic microorganisms from realistic indoor surfaces, including the related risk to the occupants.

16200415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200415.value: A persistent data structure, also known as multiversion data structure in the database literature, is a data structure that preserves all its previous versions as it is updated over time. More precisely, every update (inserting, deleting, or changing a data record) to the data structure creates a new version, while all the versions are kept in the data structure so that any previous version can still be queried. On the other hand, in an ordinary data structure, which is then called an ephemeral data structure to differentiate from a persistent one, once an update has been applied, only the most up-to-date version can be queried while all previous versions are lost. The study of persistent data structures originated in the algorithms community, and has eventually led to system implementations such as Microsoft Immortal DB. Persistent data structures aim at recording every update and all versions accurately, which results in a large space requirement at least linear to the number of updates. In many of today's big data applications, in particular for high-speed streaming data, the volume and velocity of the data are so high that we cannot afford to store everything. Therefore, streaming algorithms have received a lot of attention in the research community, which use only sublinear space and time for processing high-volume high-velocity streaming data, by sacrificing slightly on accuracy. Nevertheless, as a small loss in accuracy can often be tolerated in practice, especially on "big data", data stream algorithms have been considered as providing a nice tradeoff between accuracy and space/time costs, and thus have been studied extensively in the last 20 years, leading to both elegant theories and practical data stream systems. All streaming algorithms work by maintaining a small data structure in memory, which is usually called a sketch, summary, or synopsis. The sketch is updated upon the arrival of every element in the stream, thus is ephemeral, meaning that it can only answer queries about the current status of the stream. In this project, we aim at designing persistent sketches, thereby giving streaming algorithms the ability to answer queries about the stream at any prior time instance. Meanwhile, we will strive to maintain the sublinear space and time costs of ordinary (i.e., ephemeral) streaming algorithms, so as to continue to support high-volume/velocity data streams while "remembering" the entire history. 通常來說，數據結構在發生變化后，只有更新后的版本有效，而以往的版本即丟失，不能再繼續查詢。而持久性數據結構可以記錄一個數據集變化的全部歷史，並且以往的任何一個版本都可以繼續接受查詢。這在很多場景下有應用，微軟公司的Immortal DB系統即是基於此項技術研發出來的。 持久性數據結構能夠記錄全部歷史，但其代價是巨大的存儲空間，這在當今的“大數據”時代下成為其最主要的弊端。“大數據”下的很多數據，特別是流數據，數據本身已經龐大到不能全部存儲，所以學術界近來對只佔用少量存儲空間的數據流算法產生濃厚的興趣，展開了大量的研究。 然而，現有的數據流算法普遍基於數據勾勒技術。現有的數據勾勒技術和通常的數據結構一樣，即當數據流中的數據流過之後，數據勾勒已發生變化，只保存當前版本，而數據流的歷史信息即刻丟失。本項目目標為研究能用在數據流算法中的持久性數據勾勒技術，使現有的數據流算法不但能繼續以小空間代價處理新的流數據，同時可以記錄下數據流的全部歷史，使得我們可以隨時查詢以往任一時刻數據流的信息。

16200415.label: Realisation of objectives
16200415.value: We have successfully achieved both objectives of this project. We have developed persistent sketches for a number of fundamental problems, including online aggregation, range counting, heavy hitters, quantiles, and frequency moments. First, we have designed sketching techniques for online aggregation for joins, a fundamental problem in database systems. Online aggregation over joins was proposed to mitigate the cost of expensive joins, which offers users a nice and flexible tradeoff between query efficiency and accuracy in a continuous, online fashion. However, the state-of-the-art approach is still very expensive and even needs unrealistic assumptions (e.g., tuples in a table are stored in random order). We have proposed a new approach, the wander join algorithm, to the online aggregation problem by performing random walks over the underlying join graph. We also design an optimizer that chooses the optimal plan for conducting the random walks without having to collect any statistics a priori. Compared with ripple join, wander join is particularly efficient for equality joins involving multiple tables, but also supports Theta-joins. Selection predicates and group-by clauses can be handled as well. To demonstrate the usefulness of wander join, we have designed and implemented XDB (approXimate DB) by integrating wander join into various systems including PostgreSQL, Spark, and a stand-alone plug-in version using PL/SQL. The design and implementation of XDB has demonstrated wander join’s practicality in a full-fledged database system. Extensive experiments using the TPC-H benchmark have demonstrated the superior performance of wander join over ripple join. Second, we have also used sketching techniques to solve the problem of two-dimensional orthogonal range counting with additive error. A well-known solution for this problem is obtained by using ε-approximation, which is a subset of points that can estimate the number of points in the range. The ε-approximation is a rather restricted data structure, as we are not allowed to store any information other than the coordinates of the points. Our new sketching-based solution removes this restriction on the data structure, and by doing so, we design a simple data structure that uses less space and answers queries with the same error guarantee. We also prove a matching lower bound. Finally, we have also designed sketching techniques for the join size estimation problem. Join size estimation is a critical step in query optimization, and has been extensively studied in the literature. We have proposed a new sketching algorithm for join size estimation, called two-level sampling. Both analytical and empirical comparisons show that the new algorithm outperforms all the previous algorithms on a variety of joins, including primary key-foreign key joins, many-to-many joins, and multi-table joins. The new algorithm is also very easy to implement, requiring just one pass over the data. It only relies on some basic statistical information about the data, such as the l_k-norms and the heavy hitters.

16200415.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200415.value: We have published the sketching techniques for online aggregation for joins in SIGMOD 2016 (first conference paper listed in Part C). An extended version was published in TODS (second journal paper in Part C). We have published the sketching algorithm for range counting in TALG (the first journal paper in Part C). We have published the join size estimation algorithm in SIGMOD 2017 (the second conference paper in Part C).

16200415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200415.value: The key techniques developed in this project can be potentially useful for many problems on data summarization. We plan to extend them to related problem in other domains, such as data mining and machine learning, where computation is inherently imprecise and summarization techniques can often prove useful.

16200415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200415.value: Data sketching is a fundamental and highly effective approach to dealing with big data sets. It significantly reduces the size of the data, thereby making "big data" small, with the hope that certain properties of the data are still preserved in the sketch. In this project, we have developed a suite of data sketching techniques for a number of fundamental problems, including online aggregation, triangle counting, heavy hitters, etc. Exact methods for these problem can be very expensive on large data sets. By using our techniques, we can return approximate results of these problems on large amounts of data very efficiently. In cases where 100% accuracy is not required, our techniques can be very useful.

16200915.value: 由视觉刺激引发的晕动症（VIMS）的频率响应特点：对恒定振幅、恒定速率的线性及旋转视觉震荡刺激效应的分离探究

16200915.label: Project Objectives
16200915.value: The study will determine the frequency responses of vection, perceived speeds and VIMS with visual oscillations of (a) constant velocities and (b) constant amplitudes along fore-and-aft, lateral, vertical, pitch, yaw and roll axis. In total, 36 sets of frequency responses will be determined using visual oscillations of the same scene complexity. The frequency response data on VIMS will be used to construct ‘equal sickness contour curves’ as functions of (a) frequency and velocity; (b) frequency and amplitude; and (c) velocity and amplitude. The formats of these curves are similar to the ‘equal comfort contour curves’ published in BS6841 and ISO2631 but such comprehensive ‘equal sickness contours’ do not exist for VIMS. The frequency response data on vection will also be used to construct ‘equal vection sensation contour curves’ as functions of (a) frequency and velocity; (b) frequency and amplitude; and (c) velocity and amplitude. The formats of these curves are similar to the ‘equal comfort contour curves’ published in BS6841 and ISO2631 but such comprehensive ‘equal vection sensation contours’ do not exist for VIMS. In addition to the ‘equal sickness contours’ and the ‘equal vection sensation contours’, regression models will be constructed using the data to generate ‘maximum likelihood contours’ for both sickness and vection sensation. Both are new and original and do not exist for such comprehensive combinations of frequency, amplitude and velocity.

16200915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200915.value: Exposure to an oscillating visual scene can cause the illusion of self-motion (vecton) and symptoms of motion sickness (MS). This phenomenon has been referred to as visually induced motion sickness (VIMS). Frequency response of MS with physical oscillations has been the subject of many studies (e.g., Golding and Markey, 1996; Griffin and Mills, 2002). Data has led to models to predict of MS (motion sickness dose value: BS6841, ISO2631). In recent years, frequency responses of VIMS have also been the subject of many studies (e.g., Duh et al., 2004; Lin et al., 2005; Diels and Howarth, 2012; Palmisano et al., 2007; Chen and So (PI) et al., 2012; Yokota et al., 2005; Groen and Bos, 2008; Kiryu et al., 2008). However, VIMS has been reported to peak at different frequencies or to have no peak. Analyses of these studies suggest three reasons for the inconsistent findings: (i) scene complexities varied; (ii) axes of visual motion varied; and (iii) frequency of VOs were confounded with amplitude and velocity in different ways (i.e., some studies kept the amplitude of VOs constant while others kept the velocity of VOs constant). In VOs, frequency of oscillations can be changed by manipulating amplitude, velocity or both. Other than the preliminary work by the PI, a study isolating the effects of keeping amplitude or velocity constant on the frequency responses of VIMS could not be found. The proposed study aims to fill this gap. VOs along all three translational and rotational axes will be studied. In order to increase efficiency of the experiments, Part 1 of the study will examine the frequency responses of vection and perceived speed with many combinations of VO amplitude, VO velocity, repeats, and axes of motion. In Part 2, carefully selected combinations of VO amplitude and VO velocity in all six axes will be studied. The PI conducted two pilot studies with constant amplitude and constant velocity VOs along the fore-and-aft axis. Results indicated that frequency responses of vection, perceived speeds and VIMS are significantly different when amplitude rather than velocity is kept constant, and vice-versa. These preliminary findings need to be confirmed and extended to all six axes. Data will enable the construct of equal vection and sickness contours as well as 50% likelihood vection and sickness sensation curves (Part 3). Findings will fill an important gap in our knowledge of VIMS. 震荡的视觉场景能使人产生一种自身运动的错觉（Vection）以及晕动症（Motion Sickness）症状，这个现象被研究者们称之为由视觉刺激引发的晕动症（Visually Induced Motion Sickness, VIMS）。以往有大量的研究曾探讨了由实物环境震荡(例如，船的摆动) 所引发的晕动症的频率响应特点，并已根据这些数据构建了用来预测晕动(浪)症强度的模型。近来，越来越多的研究者也开始关注VIMS的频率响应特点。然而，这些研究所报告的引起最强VIMS的峰值频率却各不相同，或认为并不存在峰值。对这些研究的进一步分析表明，有三个主要的原因造成了前人研究结果的分歧。第一，这些研究使用的视觉场景复杂度不尽相同；第二，所研究之视觉运动方向是不同的；第三，视觉震荡的频率与刺激频率振幅、速度等诸多因素混淆在一起（在呈现刺激时有些研究维持固定的振幅，也有些研究维持固定的速度）。要改变视觉震荡的频率，我们既可以通过操纵振幅的方式，也可以通过操纵速度的方式，甚至可以同时改变两者；而以往并没有研究将之分离开。 为了填补这一空缺，本研究将试图分离振幅与速度对VIMS频率响应的影响，并单独研究它们在三个平移运动方向与三个旋转运动方向上的效应。

16200915.label: Realisation of objectives
16200915.value: All 4 objectives have been realised. Seven experiments have been completed. Details are summarised as follows: Exp1 – Effects of visual oscillations of constant velocities and constant amplitudes along fore-and-aft axis on perceived vection and speeds (Objective 1) An experiment consists of 37 conditions that have included the exhaustive combinations of 5 oscillation velocities and 5 oscillation frequencies (i.e., 25 conditions) as well as the exhaustive combinations of 5 oscillation frequencies and 5 oscillation amplitudes (i.e., 25 conditions) was conducted. All visual oscillations were along the fore-and-aft axis. Results of the experiment showed that when the velocities were kept constant, the frequency responses of vection were significantly different from those when the amplitudes were kept constant. Results are reported in Fu et al. (2017) and So et al. (2020a). Exp2 – Effects of visual oscillations of constant velocities and constant amplitudes along fore-and-aft axis on perceived vection and visually induced motion sickness (VIMS) (Objective 1) Similar to Exp1, this experiment investigate the exhaustive combination of 5 oscillation velocities and 5 frequencies as well as 5 oscillation amplitudes and 5 frequencies on rated levels of VIMS. All visual oscillations were along the fore-and-aft axis. Subjects were exposed to 20 minutes of visual oscillations. Rated levels of VIMS were taken before and after the exposure. Each exposure was separated by 4 to 7 days to minimize the effects of habituation. Results of the experiment showed that when the velocities were kept constant, the frequency responses of VIMS were significantly different from those when the amplitudes were kept constant. We are excited about this finding. Results are reported in So et al. (2017) and Wei et al. (2017b). Exp3 – Effects of visual oscillations of constant velocities and constant amplitudes along lateral and yaw axes on perceived vection and speeds (Objective 1) An experiment consists of 37 conditions that have included the exhaustive combinations of 5 oscillation velocities and 5 oscillation frequencies (i.e., 25 conditions) as well as the exhaustive combinations of 5 oscillation frequencies and 5 oscillation amplitudes (i.e., 25 conditions) was conducted. All visual oscillations were along the lateral and yaw axes. Results of the experiment showed that when the velocities were kept constant, the frequency responses of vection were significantly different from those when the amplitudes were kept constant. Unlike the findings in Exp 1, the trends in the frequency responses were different but not opposite to each other. Results are reported in So et al. (2017) and Wei et al. (2017b). Exp4 - Effects of visual oscillations of constant velocities and constant amplitudes along lateral and yaw axes on perceived vection and visually induced motion sickness (VIMS) (Objective 1) Similar to Exp3, this experiment investigate the exhaustive combination of 5 oscillation velocities and 5 frequencies as well as 5 oscillation amplitudes and 5 frequencies on rated levels of VIMS. All visual oscillations were along the lateral and yaw axes. Subjects were exposed to 20 minutes of visual oscillations. Rated levels of VIMS were taken before and after the exposure. Each exposure was separated by 4 to 7 days to minimize the effects of habituation. Results of the experiment showed that when the velocities were kept constant, the frequency responses of VIMS were significantly different from those when the amplitudes were kept constant. Although keeping oscillation velocity or amplitude constant has cause the frequency response of VIMS to differ, the effects with yaw axis were different from those reported in Exp2 with fore-and-aft axis oscillations. This suggests that different axis of visual oscillations are influenced differently by keeping velocity or amplitude constant. In other words, two-way interactions are observed. Results are reported in So et al. (2017). Exp5 - Effects of oscillating Virtual Reality (VR)scenes of constant velocities and constant amplitudes along yaw and pitch axes on perceived vection and visually induced motion sickness (VIMS) (Objective 1, 4) Exp5 has two parts. Part I repeated Exp4 using realistic VR scenes presented on a head-tracked HTC Vive VR head set and in yaw and pitch axes. Results were consistent with the findings of Exp4 and the two-frequency hypothesis was supported. As the Vive head set was equipped with eye tracker, individual optokinetic nystagmus (OKN) gains were measured and weak correlations were found between levels of reported sickness and individual OKN gains. A review of literature suggests that a hypothetical relationship between individual after-OKN and levels of motion sickness. Part II of Exp5 was conducted to determine the correlations between after-OKN and levels of sickness. Results indicated that although after-OKN gain did not correlate with levels of sickness, the decay time constants of after-OKN significantly correlated with sickness levels Results are reported in Guo et al. (2017) and So et al. (2017). Exp6&7 – EEG signatures associated with vection induced by scene oscillations in roll axis (Objective 1) Following the findings of Exp5 Part II, a review of literature suggests that those who with higher sickness susceptibility are likely to have larger capacity of neural storage of visual and vestibular signals. During the IEEE conference in Japan, the PI discussed his findings with some Japanese colleagues and we decided to conduct Exp 6&7. Since in our brains, all observable functions are realized in terms of neural connections, Exp6 & 7 were conducted to test the hypotheses that participants with higher sickness susceptibility would have significantly more complex neural connections during vection to support the longer decay time constants of after-OKN. Experimental results indicated that neural connectivity as measured by EEG signals synchronization among participants with high and low sickness susceptibility are significantly different. This finding is of great importance because it suggests sickness susceptibility can be observed as the density of functional neural connectivity (Wei et al., 2017ab, 2018, 2019). Equal vection and sickness contour curves (Objectives 2 and 3) Data collected in Exp1 to Exp4 have been analyzed to produce the ‘equal sickness contour curves’ and ‘equal vection sensation contour curves’. The methodology was adapted from BS6841 (and ISO2631). The traditional ways were to construct the contour curves as functions of (a) frequency and velocity as well as (b) frequency and amplitudes. In this case, because the designers of a Virtual Reality simulation environment can manipulate the velocity and amplitude of visual scene at will, we have constructed the contour curves as functions of velocity and amplitude (So, 2019a) . Maximum likelihood contours for sickness and vection: Part I (Objective 4) Data collected in Exp1 to Exp4 were analyzed using linear regression models. Maximum likelihood models were estimated with visual oscillation frequencies, amplitudes and velocities as factors and predicted levels of vection and sickness (nausea ratings) were the outcomes (Muth et al., 2018). Maximum likelihood contours for sickness and vection: Part II (Objective 4) Data collected in Exp5 part II were added to the regression analyses. Maximum likelihood of sickness and vection were calculated as functions of OKN velocity and scene oscillation velocities. Results indicated the possibility of a “safe” zone in which participants would report strong vection but yet only slight discomfort but no nausea. This is good news to the VR game developers as it supports the possibility for the presence of vection without sickness (So, 2019a).

In total, 36 sets of frequency responses will be determined using visual oscillations of the same scene complexity.

The frequency response data on VIMS will be used to construct ‘equal sickness contour curves’ as functions of (a) frequency and velocity; (b) frequency and amplitude; and (c) velocity and amplitude. The formats of these curves are similar to the ‘equal comfort contour curves’ published in BS6841 and ISO2631 but such comprehensive ‘equal sickness contours’ do not exist for VIMS.

The frequency response data on vection will also be used to construct ‘equal vection sensation contour curves’ as functions of (a) frequency and velocity; (b) frequency and amplitude; and (c) velocity and amplitude. The formats of these curves are similar to the ‘equal comfort contour curves’ published in BS6841 and ISO2631 but such comprehensive ‘equal vection sensation contours’ do not exist for VIMS.

In addition to the ‘equal sickness contours’ and the ‘equal vection sensation contours’, regression models will be constructed using the data to generate ‘maximum likelihood contours’ for both sickness and vection sensation. Both are new and original and do not exist for such comprehensive combinations of frequency, amplitude and velocity.

16200915.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200915.value: Frequencies responses of the vection and visually induced motion sickness (VIMS) have been the subjects of many studies. Theories such as the visual-vestibular mismatch model have been proposed to explain and predict the frequency of visual motion that can cause the most motion sickness. However, oscillating frequencies, amplitudes and velocities are all cofounding with each other. In this study, we found repeated evidence that two frequency responses of vection and VIMS exist depending on whether the amplitudes or the velocities of the oscillating visual scenes are kept constant (Fu et al, 2017, So et al., 2020). This suggests that there would be no single frequency of visual oscillations that will cause the most vection or VIMS. Consequently, our findings not only affect the ways future scientists use frequency responses of visual stimuli to predict vection and VIMS, it also changes our understandings of the neural mechanisms behind vection perception and the associated symptoms of VIMS (Muth et al., 2018, So et al., 2017). Consolidations of the two frequency responses indicate that effects of velocities are more significant than effects of frequencies on vection and VIMS. This led the team to study the neural velocity storage known to be associated with visual perception of stable images during moving visual scenes. Results indicated that individuals with larger capacity of velocity storage as indicated by longer decaying time constant of after-nystagmus also reported significantly higher VIMS (Guo et al., 2017, So et al., 2017, Wei et al., 2017a). We also found supporting evidence that exercising the velocity storage in association with the visual scenes is one of the key correlates with vection (So, 2019a, Wei et al, 2017b, Wei et al, 2018). As all functions in our brains are realized in neural connections, we boldly hypothesized that the density of functional neural connections are different between participants who are more susceptible to VIMS than those who are resistance. Repeated evidence was found and our results are reported in Neuroimage – the most prestige journal in this narrow field with impact factor 5.8 (So, 2019b, Wei et al., 2019).

16200915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200915.value: We are extremely excited to find neural evidence to differentiate participants with higher and lower susceptibility to visually induced motion sickness (VIMS). The significant neural correlations not only suggest an objective differential tool but a window into why human get motion sickness? – the most important question that has been asked repeatedly for decades during the quest for understanding in visual-vestibular interactions. Future studies to continue the successful use of EEG to examine functional neural connectivity are of importance and will continue. This will eventually uncover the truth on the neural mechanisms of motion sickness.

16200915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200915.value: About half of human population experiences some kind of motion sickness. Darwin reported the strange phenomenon of motion sickness 200 years ago. Since then scientists have been searching for the answer to why half of us get motion sickness while the other half do not? The current study found, for the first time, that those who have fewer tendencies to get motion sick are relaying their signals from eyes and ears to the rest of their brain significantly more efficiently than those who have more tendencies to get motion sickness. This new finding is reported in Neuroimage, a famous scientific journal about human brain, and will open up many continuing studies to find out the answer to why some get motion sick while others do not. We also found evidence that those have fewer tendencies to get motion sick can handle changes in eye movement velocities faster. We have also found that it is the velocity of moving scene and not the frequency of movement that is affecting visually induced motion sickness. Results are all published.

16201115.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16201115.value: 基于相对误差的输出估计

16201115.label: Project Objectives
16201115.value: To study the state and output estimation based on relative errors. To study the output feedback networked stabilization with both output uncertainties and input uncertainties.
rows: To study the state and output estimation based on relative errors.
To study the output feedback networked stabilization with both output uncertainties and input uncertainties.

16201115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201115.value: An output estimation problem concerns the use of corrupted measurement of some system variables to estimate some other system variables that are hard or impossible to measure. Recently, the estimation problem in the presence of measurement uncertainties has been attracting more and more attention along with the development of networked control systems, where the measurements are transmitted through a communication network to the controller. Due to information constraints in the communication network, the transmission of the measurements may suffer from various uncertainties such as quantization, packet drop, fading, etc. These uncertainties often come in multiplicative form. It turns out that under these multiplicative uncertainties, both the Luenberger observer and Kalman filter performs badly for unstable systems when the absolute error is concerned. To be specific, the absolute error will explode rather than converge no matter how the estimator is designed. This suggests an urgent need for some new perspective on the estimation problem in the presence of multiplicative measurement noise. As suggested above, the absolute error may no longer serve as an appropriate performance metric in the presence of multiplicative measurement noise. Instead, it is better to gauge the estimation error in a relative manner when the measurement noise takes the relative form. In fact, our previous experience with networked control systems reveals that it is often the relative estimation error that plays an essential role in the stabilization as well as further performance requirement problems. In the proposed project, we will take an unprecedented step to investigate the estimation based on relative error rather than the absolute error when multiplicative measurement uncertainties are present. Our preliminary study shows quite promising results for the special case of an unstable scalar system. In that case, the relative error is shown to be bounded, and the size of the relative error turns out to be proportional to the magnitude of the uncertainty. Our objective is to develop a thorough estimation theory via relative error and further apply the theory to study the output feedback control under information constraints. 输出估计问题致力于研究如何利用一些可测量的系统变量来估计另外一些不易测量的系统变量。最近，随着网络化控制系统的发展，基于失真测量信号的估计问题得到越来越多的关注。在一个网络化控制系统中，测量信号需要通过一个通信网络来传输给控制器。由于通信网络中的种种信息约束，测量信号的传输会受到诸如量化，丢包，衰落等不确定性的影响。这些不确定性常常以乘性的形式出现。在这些乘性不确定性的影响下，基于绝对估计误差的龙伯格观测器和卡尔曼滤波器在不稳定系统上的表现均甚不理想。具体而言，对于一个带有乘性测量噪声的不稳定系统，无论估计器如何设计，绝对估计误差都将发散。在此背景下，提出新的视角来研究在乘性测量噪声情况下的估计问题刻不容缓。 如上所述，当存在乘性测量噪声时，绝对估计误差不再是一个合适的性能指标。针对乘性噪声的情形，我们认为一个更合理的指标是相对误差。事实上，我们对于网络化系统的研究经验表明相对误差常常在系统镇定以及性能控制中起关键作用。 在该拟议项目中，我们将跨出前所未有的一步来研究在乘性噪声情形下的基于相对误差的估计问题。初步研究显示，对于一阶系统的特殊情况，我们可以得到十分积极的结果。具体而言，我们发现相对误差是有界的，并且相对误差的大小和测量不确定性的大小成比例。我们的目标是发展一套深入的基于相对误差的估计理论并进而应用于研究在信息约束下的输出反馈控制问题。

16201115.label: Realisation of objectives
16201115.value: This project has two objectives. The first one is to study the network estimation problem and the second one is to use the solution to the estimation problem to study the output feedback networked stabilization problem. It was hoped that a separation principle exists in networked stabilization in the form of usual output feedback stabilization with ideal signal transmission. During the project, we started to realize that output feedback networked stabilization problem can be tackled in a more direct way, by introducing the two-port channel model. We made remarkable progress towards the second objective, achieving more than what we initially expected, and had quite a few publications. Due to this success, the importance of the first objective became less prominent. Nevertheless, the techniques used to achieve the second objective can now be used to address the estimation issue in the first objective.

16201115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201115.value: By investigating into a special networked control system (NCS) composed of cascaded two-port networks in the communication channel, we obtain a good model of the communication network in a feedback system containing a plant with both input and output uncertainties. The plant and the controller are also assumed to have uncertainties measured by the gap metric. When all the components in the NCS are assumed to be continuous-time linear time-invariant systems, a necessary and sufficient condition for the robust stability of the NCS subject to the previously introduced uncertainties has been obtained in [J1]. Furthermore, a generalization to the case when the uncertainties in two-port networks are nonlinear has been obtained in [J3]. Another generalization is given in [J4] where all the components in the NCS are modeled by discrete-time linear time-varying causal systems. The robust stabilization issue is also studied. We develop an elementary polynomial approach to designing optimally robust controllers in an NCS, see [J2].

16201115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16201115.value: 1. We may utilize stochastic models for systems and uncertainties in analyzing two-port NCSs and try to obtain similar robust stability conditions. 2. We may investigate communication networks involving structured uncertainties that may be more suitable for practical problems.

16201115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201115.value: This research introduces a new perspective to study and analyze noisy communication networks. The theory may help engineers better understand uncertain networks and design optimal controllers that are the most suitable for the noisy environment. Such a controller may be used in many applications, for example, satellite networks, robot networks, remote surgeries, and so on. The elementary design procedures of such a controller may also be valuable in control education and industrial applications.

16201315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201315.value: Creating layouts of graphic elements is vital for many graphics applications. Often, numerous manual operations are needed to create a desired layout, including specifying the spatial properties of individual elements and the spatial relations among them. Command-based arrangement tools are supported by almost all modern graphics editors such as Adobe Illustrator and Microsoft PowerPoint for precise alignment and/or equal spacing of graphics elements. However, their underlying technology has advanced very little since day one. An arrangement command arranges the selected objects by considering the selected elements as one single arrangement group and ignoring the underlying patterns of the objects, therefore may produce undesirable results when the selected elements exhibit a 2D pattern. The first goal of this project is to design group-aware arrangement commands that exploit the underlying patterns of roughly placed objects. The key idea is that an issued arrangement command is in fact very informative, instructing how to automatically decompose a 2D layout into multiple 1D groups, each of which is compatible with the command. We will present a parameter-free, command-driven grouping approach that produce predictable results. We will also design a simple user interface with pushpins to enable explicit grouping control. Creating virtual scenes with 3D objects is common in many applications such as movies and games. Many automatic scene generation procedures have been proposed, but they do not always generate satisfactory results. For example, in a virtual shopping center, the layout of the virtual products should be carefully designed, requiring manual interaction. The second goal of the project is to develop a novel interface to facilitate manual creation of 3D scenes containing numerous objects with less interaction and effort. Following our recent 2D layout beautification framework, we believe that the layout of the objects can be automatically beautified as long as the underlying patterns are extractable. To assist the user in perceiving and editing the layout, the relations among the objects will be visualized. However, visualizing all the relations in 3D scenes would introduce severe visual clutter and confusion. Therefore we will introduce an adaptive visualization scheme that can predict and visualize only the relevant relations. In addition, we will introduce an automatic view transition algorithm capable of predicting the best view for editing based on the user's intended operation. The proposed interaction techniques are expected to greatly reduce user interaction and effort in creating 2D and 3D layouts. Any performance improvement will be validated through user studies. 创建图形元素的布局在很多图形应用程序都起到至关重要的作用。通常，在创建一个图形元素布局时，用户需要进行大量的交互操作。例如，用户需要指明单个元素的空间属性，以及元素之间的空间关系。大部分图形编辑软件如Adobe Illustrator以及Microsoft PowerPoint都会提供基于命令的排列工具。它可以用来对图形元素进行精确的对齐排列，或者等距排列。然而，这个工具所用到的技术一直以来却没有得到改进。当选中一组图形元素并利用这个工具进行排列时，这些选中的元素就被认为仅属于一个排列组，从而忽视了布局自身所具有的模式。当这些元素的布局具有二维的模式时，利用传统的排列命令往往会产生难以预料的结果。根据以上分析，本项目的第一个目标是设计一个群组感知的排列命令工具。它能够利用图形元素初始布局所具有的模式。设计这个工具时主要思想是，排列命令本身提供了额外的信息，从而可以根据图形元素的初始布局将这些元素分解为多个一维的群组。每个群组和发出的排列命令是相容的。我们将会提出一个无参数的、基于命令的分组算法，使得分组结果能够预测。我们还将设计一个简单的图钉工具来提供对分组结果的显式控制。 利用三维物体创建虚拟场景在电影、游戏等应用中是很常见的。人们提出了许多自动的场景创建算法，但在许多情况下这些算法并不能得到令人满意的结果。例如，在创建虚拟购物中心时，虚拟物品的布局需要精心设计，这个时候人工交互往往是必不可少的。本项目的第二个目标是开发一个创新的交互工具，帮助用户利用更少的交互，更容易地创建包含大量物体的三维场景。参照我们最近的二维图形布局美化系统，我们相信能够利用三维场景中物体所具有的模式来对三维物体布局进行优化。为了帮助用户感知和编辑三维布局，物体之间的关系将会被可视化。然而，将三维场景中所有物体间的关系都可视化是不可取的，因为这样将会产生严重的视觉杂乱和混淆。因此，我们将会提出一个新的自适应的可视化方案，能够预测并仅显示适当的关系。另外，我们还将提出一个自动的视角转换算法。这个算法能够根据用户的操作来预测当前情况下的最好视角。 本项目所提出的交互技术预期将会极大的减少用户在创建二维以及三维布局时的交互。我们将会通过用户研究来验证我们的工具所带来的效率上的提升。

16201315.label: Realisation of objectives
16201315.value: Arranging graphics elements into visually appealing layouts is frequently required in applications such as graphics design, slide preparation, and desktop publishing. Such tasks are traditionally accomplished through the users issuing numerous alignment and distribution commands using software such as Illustrator or Powerpoint. Numerous invocation of such arrangement commands is necessary because the commands are oblivious to multiple rows or columns exhibited among the selected elements. The main goal of this project is to reduce user-interactions for designing layouts of graphics elements. We fulfilled the first objective by designing group-aware arrangement commands that can automatically detect the desired groups present in the layout. Our aim is to improve the performance of traditional command-based arrangement tools for achieving 2D layouts, involving multiple rows and/or columns of well aligned and/or distributed elements. The issued command suggests the search for groups perpendicular to the arrangement axis, reducing to a one-dimensional grouping problem. We fulfilled the second objective by designing a pushpin tool for the user to override the automatically determined arrangement groups. A single pushpin can be employed to indicate the reference element for alignment. Multiple pushpins may be used to break a group into two groups. To fulfil the third objective, we conducted a user study to validate that our group-aware arrangement commands are intuitive to use and that they offer performance improvement over traditional group-oblivious arrangement commands. Automatic beautification of layouts of roughly placed graphics 2D or 3D elements can greatly reduce user interaction and effort. We fulfilled the four objective by designing algorithms to automatically detect the underlying patterns in the elements and infer alignment and equal-spacing constraints in a global beautification process. Automatically inferred relationships might not always be wholly desirable. This problem might be indirectly solved by interactive refinement of certain elements’ position and/or size. Alternatively the user may directly add or remove constraints using a gestural interface. We presented a user interface involving a preview window and an input window. While this interface is simple, it has the following benefits. First, the user can focus on the layout design by manipulating individual elements in the input window. Second, the user might refine the beautification results through slightly modifying the input elements. To facilitate more direct control of the beautification results, we designed a gestural interface for editing inferred constraints by directly interacting with the visualized constraints via simple gestures. This fulfilled the fifth objective. Finally, we fulfilled the last objective by conducting a user study to validate that our beautifier system enables faster layout creation than conventional methods. These contributions are elaborated in Section 6.1. In view of these results, we consider that the objectives of the project have been fulfilled.

16201315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201315.value: We designed a set of group-aware alignment commands and distribution commands for fast arrangement of graphics elements into visually appealing 2D layouts. Whenever an arrangement command is issued, the desired groups present in the layout is automatically derived. Our key idea is that an issued command is in fact very informative, instructing how to automatically decompose a 2D layout into multiple 1D groups, each of which is compatible with the issued command. We also designed a simple user interface with pushpins to enable explicit control of grouping and arrangement. Our user study confirms the intuitiveness of our technique and its performance improvement over traditional command-based arranegement tools. A patent for this work has been granted: Group-Aware Command-based Arrangement of Graphic Elements, US10223330B2, March 5, 2019. Specifying precise relationships among graphic elements is often a time-consuming process with alignment commands. Automatic beautification of roughly designed layouts can provide a more efficient solution but often lead to undesired results due to the ambiguity problem. To facilitate ambiguity resolution in layout beautification, we present a novel user interface for visualizing and editing automatic inferred relationships. Our technique is applicable for both 2D and 3D global layout beautification, with an efficient implementation to provide instant feedback. The user study validates that our tool is capable of creating and refining layouts of graphic elements and is significantly faster than the standard snap-dragging or command-based alignment tools in both 2D and 3D layout tasks. A paper reporting this work is under review by IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics [Xu et al. submitted]. We then developed two sketch-based systems involving arrangement of 3D elements, namely model-guided 3D sketching and model-driven sketch reconstruction. Our model-guided 3D sketching system facilitates rapid concept redesign of existing 3D models via 3D sketching. Algorithms are designed to automatically optimize the positions and alignments of 3D components. Our novel solution infers a 3D planar canvas by analyzing structural relations between a guiding 3D model and a group of 2D strokes constrained on the canvas. This work has been accepted by IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics [Xu et al. 2019]. Our model-driven sketch reconstruction system lifts a 2D sketch into a 3D sketch. This problem requires optimizing the 3D positions of sketch strokes, which we solve with the help of models in a shape collection. The key idea is to exploit part structure for retrieving a candidate model that provides plane information for back projection and optimization of sketch strokes. This work was presented as a technical brief at SIGGRAPH Asia conference 2016 [Li et al. 2016]. Finally, the above sketch-based systems further inspire an interesting work. We propose a system, Live Sketch, which allows novice users to interactively bring static drawings to life by applying deformation-based animation effects extracted from video examples. Our system addresses a few major technical challenges, such as motion extraction from video, video-to-sketch alignment, and many-to-one motion driven sketch animation. While each of the sub-problems could be difficult to solve fully automatically, we present reliable solutions by combining new computational algorithms with intuitive user interactions. This work was published in the proceedings of the ACM Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI) 2018 [Su et al. CHI 2018] [Su, PhD Thesis].

16201315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16201315.value: Our layout beautification tool can be integrated with existing graphic editors to examine its interplay with other layout helper features. Our current implementation requires explicit mode switching to activate or deactivate the gesture interface for editing geometric constraints. It would be interesting to explore a mode-less interface where the user could edit both the graphic elements and the constraints without explicit mode switching. Creating 3D scenes containing numerous objects still require much user interaction and effort. Automatic beautification of roughly placed 3D objects through extracting the underlying patterns and enforcing optimized constraints can be an effective solution. Novel interfaces that facilitate editing and refining to resolve ambiguities are needed. The relation constraints can be visualized to assist the user in perceiving and editing the layout. Adaptive visualization that avoids visual clutter and ensures the ease of editing the relevant relations would be desired. Automatic view transition capable of predicting the best view for editing based on the user's intended operation is another interesting research direction.

16201315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201315.value: Creating accurate layouts of graphic elements is vital for many graphic applications. Modern graphic editors such as Adobe Illustrator and Microsoft PowerPoint typically support command-based arrangement operations for precise alignment and/or equal spacing of graphic elements. However, traditional tools are designed to operate on a single group of elements that are distributed consistently with the arrangement axis implied by a command. This often demands a process involving repeated element selections and arrangement commands to achieve 2D layouts with multiple rows and/or columns of well-aligned and/or distributed elements. Our group-aware commands reduce the numbers of selection operation and command invocation. Snapping is a local beautification technique commonly used together with arrangement commands. Each time only a current element is being beautified while all existing elements are kept fixed. Such traditional tools are rather tedious and require a carefully ordered set of manual operations to achieve a desired layout. Our global beautification tool infers perceptually meaningful relationships among a set of roughly placed graphic elements and then refine their positions and sizes to obtain a well-aligned layout that involves only small changes to the inputs. Our tool provides an efficient way for creating and refining layouts of both 2D and 3D elements.

16201615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201615.value: Uncertain (also called probabilistic) graphs, are graphs whose edges are labeled with a probability of existence. They are relevant in a number of applications such as social networks (e.g., an edge between two users denotes the probability that one influences the other) and biological databases (e.g., edges correspond to interactions among genes and proteins observed thorough noisy experiments). Currently, most query and mining tasks on uncertain graphs are based on Monte-Carlo sampling, which (i) draws a large number of possible graphs (samples), (ii) evaluates the task on each of them, and (iii) aggregates the individual answers to generate the final result. However this process is extremely time consuming for the large uncertain graphs commonly found in practice (e.g., social networks). To overcome the high cost we propose the extraction of deterministic representatives that capture well some structural properties of the uncertain graph. The query and mining tasks can then be efficiently processed using conventional (i.e., deterministic) algorithms on these representatives. Specifically, our goals are (i) to investigate which properties of uncertain graphs are relevant and should be preserved by the representatives, (ii) to develop algorithms that efficiently generate representatives capturing accurately the desirable properties, and (iii) to experimentally evaluate the effectiveness of representatives on various graph tasks such as shortest path distance, clustering coefficient and betweenness centrality. 不確定（也稱為概率）圖是其邊緣被標以存在概率的圖。它們是和很多應用有關的，如社交網絡（例如，兩個用戶之間的邊緣表示一個影響其他的可能性）和生物數據庫（例如，在嘈雜實驗的觀察中，邊緣對應於基因和蛋白質之間的相互作用）。現時，大部份在不確定圖查詢和挖掘的任務都是基於蒙特卡羅抽樣:（i）繪製了大量的可能圖（取樣），（ⅱ）評估每個可能圖的任務，和（iii）聚合所有可能圖的個別答案以產生最終結果。但是，在現實生活中常見的大量不確定圖中（如社交網絡），這個過程是非常耗費時間的。 為了克服這樣高的代價，我們提出找出確定性的代表去捕捉好不確定圖的一些結構性質。查詢及挖掘任務就可以對這些代表使用傳統的（即確定性的）算法有高效的處理。具體來說，我們的目標是：（i）研究哪些不確定圖的性質是有關的，從而由代表去保留，（ⅱ）設計一種可以有效地產生代表的算法，去捕捉好所需的性質，和（iii）通過實驗去評估找出來的代表在各種圖的任務(如最短路徑，聚類係數和中介中心 )的有效性。

16201615.label: Realisation of objectives
16201615.value: Graphs constitute an expressive data representation paradigm used to describe entities (vertices) and their relationships (edges) in a wide range of applications. Sometimes the existence of the relationship between two entities is uncertain due to noisy measurements, inference and prediction models, or explicit manipulation. In this case, the data can be modeled as an uncertain graph (also called probabilistic graph), whose edges are labeled with a probability of existence. This probability represents the confidence that the relation corresponding to the edge holds in reality. Query processing on uncertain graphs is extremely expensive because it involves Monte Carlo sampling; i.e., the generation of numerous samples of the uncertain graph, query execution on each sample and aggregation of the results. In this project, we investigated the problem of producing a single representative instance G* (i.e., a deterministic graph) of a given uncertain graph G. Queries can then be processed efficiently on the deterministic instance using conventional graph algorithms. In order to maintain data utility, the representative instance G* should preserve the expected (underlying) structure of the uncertain graph G. Motivated by related work on deterministic graphs, we study the problem of extracting, from an uncertain graph, the representative instance that better preserves the expected degree of each vertex. Going a step further, we generalize the notion of vertex degree to the concept of n-clique cardinality of a vertex u, i.e., the number of cliques of size n that contain u. In particular, the degree of a vertex is equivalent to its 2-clique cardinality, whereas its triangle connectivity corresponds to its 3-clique cardinality. The notion of n-clique is extended naturally to n > 3. Intuitively, this generalization aims at capturing the expected structure in the neighborhood of vertices. For the first problem, extracting representative instances that capture the expected vertex degree sequence, we propose two methods: average degree rewiring (ADR) and approximate B-matching (ABM). ADR involves two phases: first, it generates an instance with the same average vertex degree as the uncertain graph; then, it randomly rewires edges if they more accurately approximate the vertex degrees. ABM applies B-matching to obtain an initial instance, which is then improved using weighted maximum bipartite matching. For the problem of extracting the representative instance that best preserves the expected n-clique cardinality (for n ≥ 2), we develop GREEDY and GAME. GREEDY arranges the edges in a dynamic heap and greedily inserts the one that leads to the best approximation of the expected n-clique cardinality. GAME applies a game theoretic framework that models the edges of the uncertain graph as players of an exact potential game, and uses best response dynamics to generate the representative. In order to evaluate the proposed techniques, we use four uncertain, undirected graphs that capture different real-world scenarios and data characteristics e.g., size, density, edge probability. Our extensive experimental evaluation confirms that the representative instances can indeed be used to efficiently and accurately answer queries based on several metrics such as shortest path distance, clustering coefficient and betweenness centrality. Going on step further, we proposed the related problem of graph sparsification. Specifically, given an uncertain graph G and a parameter α (0 < α < 1), our goal is to create a sparsified probabilistic subgraph G′, which contains a fraction α of the edges, but preserves its structural properties. G′ can be used to approximate the result of any query on G. Since the cost of sampling and query processing is proportional to the number of edges, sparsification yields significant benefits in execution time. In addition, it reduces the storage cost of the graph, and facilitates visualization of complex networks. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work on uncertain graph sparsification. On the other hand, sparsification has received considerable attention in the deterministic graph literature. In that context, most techniques aim at approximating all shortest path distances up to a multiplicative or additive factor, or preserving all cuts up to an arbitrarily small multiplicative error. As we demonstrate experimentally, the adaptation of such methods to uncertain graphs yields poor results. To overcome this problem, our novel algorithms reduce the number of edges and tune the probability of the remaining ones to preserve the expected node degrees, or the expected cut sizes. We experimentally demonstrate that the sparsified graphs are effective for a variety of common tasks including the computation of shortest path distance, betweenness centrality, page rank and clustering coefficient. Since the deterministic representatives have fewer edges than the original uncertain graph, the generation of representative instances could be viewed as a special case of sparsification. However, a representative cannot be used to answer queries whose output is uncertain, e.g., return the probability that the graph consists of a single connected component, or the probability that two vertices are reachable from each other. On the other hand, sparsification techniques generate uncertain graphs that can be used for the same query and mining tasks as the original graph. Moreover, deterministic representative instances do not provide control over the number of edges in the representative graphs.

16201615.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201615.value: In publication J1, we propose extracting representative instances of uncertain graphs. Expensive tasks can then be processed by applying deterministic algorithms on these instances. We focus on two problems: the first aims at minimizing the vertex degree discrepancy between the representative and the uncertain graph, while the second minimizes n-clique discrepancies. For Problem 1, we present ADR a heuristic technique, and ABM that utilizes matching algorithms. For Problem 2, we develop methods based on the greedy and game theoretic frameworks. In order to assess the quality of representatives, we perform extensive experiments on real datasets. Our results confirm that indeed the proposed methods approximate well various structural measures and query metrics. Given the cost savings of our techniques with respect to Monte Carlo sampling, we expect them to have a significant impact on query processing for uncertain graphs. In publications C1 and J2, we introduce a framework for uncertain graph sparsification with entropy reduction. Specifically, we design two methods, GDB (Gradient Descent Backbone) and EMD (Expectation Maximization Degree), which reduce the number of edges and tune the probability of the remaining ones to preserve crucial properties. Both methods start with a backbone deterministic graph Gb. GDB assigns probabilities to the edges of Gb aiming at preserving the expected vertex degrees or cut sizes, while reducing the entropy. In addition to assigning probabilities, EMD also changes the structure of Gb by adding or removing edges. We experimentally demonstrate that the generated sparsified graphs are effective for a variety of common tasks including shortest path distance, reliability, page rank and others.

16201615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16201615.value: Regarding representative graph instances, we will explore additional properties that maybe important for specialized tasks, e.g., graph pattern mining, graph clustering, etc. It will also be interesting to generate and combine multiple representatives for better approximation. We also aim at extending our methods to alternative uncertain settings such as, time dependent or streaming graphs, attributed graphs etc., where the extraction of representatives is even more challenging. Finally, a promising direction is the incorporation of subgraph sampling in the process of representative extraction. The idea is to generalize the problem definitions, so that in addition to preserving the structural properties of the uncertain graph, the representatives also reduce the number of nodes to further facilitate efficiency. Regarding uncertain graph sparsification, we intend to investigate techniques for multigraphs and weighted uncertain graphs.

16201615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201615.value: Data in several applications can be represented as an uncertain graph, whose edges are labeled with a probability of existence. Exact query processing on uncertain graphs is prohibitive for most applications. To facilitate efficiency, we study the problem of extracting a deterministic representative instance from an uncertain graph. Conventional processing techniques can then be applied on this representative to closely approximate the result on the original graph. In order to maintain data utility, the representative instance should preserve structural characteristics of the uncertain graph. We start with representatives that capture the expected vertex degrees, and then generalize the notion of vertex degree to the concept of n-clique cardinality, i.e., the number of cliques of size n that contain a vertex. Our experimental results confirm that indeed the proposed methods approximate well various structural measures and query metrics. In addition, we propose uncertain graph sparsification, where instead of a deterministic representative, the output is an uncertain graph with a subset of the edges. Uncertain graph sparsification also yields significant benefits in execution time and storage cost, while facilitating visualization of complex networks.

16201815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201815.value: The evolution of wireless communication systems like the 4.5G (Advanced LTE) and 5G networks are becoming increasingly data hungry [1] and continue to push the demand for higher bandwidth and throughput of the backhaul networking hardware in the base stations, central offices and data centers. Optical communication technology is the obvious solution to meet such demand and satisfies the form factor and energy consumption requirements. On the other hand, millimeter-wave (mm-wave) wireless communication technique has, in recent years, made significant advancements in system capacity, size and efficiency. State-of-the-art mm-wave technology has demonstrated the capability to handle applications requiring data rate or 20Gb/s [2] utilizing the globally available unlicensed band near 60GHz. As a result, the combination of optical and mm-wave technologies can potentially provide a powerful solution for a flexible, low-cost and high-bandwidth hybrid communication network. Such hybrid networks will offer both wired (optical) and wireless (mm-wave) options for deploying highly configurable and flexible network configuration to cater the different physical constraints of the environment. To address the need of the hybrid fiber-mm-wave communication network, radio-over-fiber (RoF) and baseband-over-fiber (BoF) are two possible configurations to seamlessly mesh the broadband communication technologies. In the RoF architecture, to link up the fiber network with the mm-wave wireless system, the bandwidth of the optical-to-electrical (O/E) and electrical-to-optical (E/O) interface must be pushed to over 60GHz, which is high-cost and low-efficiency. On the other hand, compared with RoF, the BoF architecture requires significantly lower O/E and E/O interface bandwidth for data rate up to 28Gbps. From the perspective of spectrum efficiency and hardware complexity, the BoF architecture offers more advantages and is adopted for investigation in this project. Leveraging our previous experience in system-on-a-chip (SoC) design for high-speed optical links, clock and data recovery (CDR) circuits, and mm-wave communication circuits, we propose to develop an integrated BoF SoC with a 60GHz QPSK transmitter to achieve 10Gb/s data rate. The BoF SoC will perform the optical to wireless conversion needed in the hybrid fiber-mm-wave communication network. Our proposed SoC will utilize integration of the various circuit blocks for both the optical and mm-wave domain to greatly reduce the overall system size and power consumption. Therefore, the successful implementation of this novel SoC can make a disruptive impact on the physical layer design of future 4.5G/5G networks. 无线通信网络如4.5（LTE-A）和5G网络，对数据的需求量正在变得原来越高，因而推动了对应用于基带、中心办公室、数据中心中的具备更高带宽和数据吞吐量的回程网络硬件的迫切需求[1]。光通信方案能够满足上述需求，并且同时能够满足微型化和低能耗的要求。与之同时，毫米波（mm-wave）无线通信技术近年来在系统容量、尺寸和效率等方面得到了显著的进步，当下的毫米波技术利用60GHz的国际免费频带，已可高达实现20Gb/s的数据率[2]。因此，将光通信和毫米波技术相结合，可以为高灵活性、低成本和高带宽的混合通信网络提供更有力的解决方案。这种混合网络可以提供有线（光纤）通信和无线（毫米波）通信两种选择，具有很好的可重构性和灵活性，因为能够适应不同环境的物理限制。 光纤射频传输（RoF）和光纤基带传输(BoF)是两种可能的满足光纤—毫米波混合通信网络需求的架构，它们均能与宽带通信技术无缝衔接。在光纤射频传输中结构中，为了连接光通信网络和毫米波系统，光电转换（O/E）和电光转换（E/O）接口的带宽要到提高到60GHz以上，这样代价太大，效率太低。另一方面，和光纤射频传输相比，光纤基带传输所要求的O/E和E/O接口的带宽即使在高达28Gb/s的数据率时也能得到显著降低。从频谱效率和硬件复杂度方面考虑，光纤基带传输结构更具优越性，因而本项目将探索此种结构。 依靠我们在高速光纤通信、时钟数据恢复电路（CDR）以及毫米波通信电路等片上系统（SoC）的积累，我们提出设计一款集成了60GHz QPSK的发射机的光纤基带传输SoC，设计速率10Gb/s。此款SoC将实现光信号到毫米波的转换，满足光纤—毫米波混合通信网络的需要。本项目设计的SoC将集成光通信和毫米波通信领域的多种电路模块以大大降低系统面积和功率消耗。因此，这款新型SoC的成功实现将对未来4.5G/5G网络的物理层设计产生颠覆性影响。

16201815.label: Realisation of objectives
16201815.value: The five objectives of this project have been successfully achieved with the prototype performance exceeding the projected expectations. We have fulfilled our main objective of designing a prototype baseband-over-fiber (BoF) system-on-a-chip (SoC) by integrating an optical receiver with a millimeter-wave transmitter with integrated power amplifier and frequency synthesizer. We have successfully developed two BoF SoCs to verify our proposed system architecture. The design techniques and measurement results of the first prototype was reported in IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems-I: Regular Papers, vol. 64, no. 3, March 2017, in “A 60-GHz 4-Gb/s Fully Integrated NRZ-to-QPSK Fiber-Wireless Modulator.” In this work, a fully integrated optical-to-wireless (OW) modulator for low-cost fiber-optical backhaul links is designed, fabricated, tested and characterized. The OW modulator directly up-converts and modulates the baseband I/Q NRZ data to a QPSK signal centered at 60 GHz. Realized in 65-nm CMOS, the optical front-end achieves -3-dBm optical input sensitivity at 4 Gb/s with 10−12 BER. The modulator produces -7.2-dBm output power with -12-dB EVM at a bit efficiency of 19.6 pJ/bit. This design demonstrated, for the first time, that a small form factor and low cost optical-to-millimeter-wave modulator can be realized to support future fiber-wireless networks. Building on the success of this first BoF SoC prototype, our second design integrated a complete 28-32 GHz transmitter with on-chip power amplifier (PA) and a 16-Gb/s optical receiver. The SoC directly up-convert broadband optical signals to the lower mm-wave band, with an efficiency of 8.6 pJ/bit, for providing backhaul connectivity in 5G base-stations. The BoF SoC is fabricated in the TSMC 65-nm general-purpose process. The measured TX path conversion gain is 24.7 dB at 32 GHz and larger than 24 dB from 25.3-40.3GHz. The maximum saturated output power of 13.8 dBm is observed at 30 GHz. The 3-dB bandwidth of saturated output power is 15.9 GHz (23.9-39.8 GHz) without any noticeable in-band ripple owing to the effective ripple cancellation scheme. The measured output P1dB and OIP3 are 10.1 and 17.7 dBm, respectively. The peak power added efficiency (PAE) reaches 14.3% at 32 GHz. The entire signal path is measured from the input of optical RX to the output of BIST to obtain the error vector magnitude (EVM) using the BIST. The measured QPSK constellation plot revealed that the EVM of −18.8 dB and −15.6 dB at 6.4 Gb/s and 12.8 Gb/s, respectively. These results are among the best reported to date in literature for 30-GHz mm-wave transmitter with fully integrated CMOS PA. This outstanding performance can be attributed to the high accuracy of the circuit simulation model of the active and passive components (especially the on-chip transformers). These in-housed developed models are based on careful characterization of the active and passive components at mm-wave frequency using on-chip probing and scattering-parameter measurement. Compared to the first BoF SoC prototype, the second design improved to peak data rate to 16 Gbps, which is a 4X improvement. Furthermore, the area and final system form factor is greatly reduced by integrated the PA on chip. To further increase the integration level of the mm-wave transmitter, we investigate the performance of on-chip antenna operating at 60 GHz. We proposed a compact on-chip MIMO antenna design in the paper “Fabrication and Measurement of Millimeter-Wave On-chip MIMO Antenna for CMOS RFIC's” presented at the 2016 IEEE International Wireless Symposium (IWS). The proposed structure consists of one folded monopole antenna operating as main antenna and one IFA antenna serving as the diversity antenna. Antenna ground is formed by connecting the idle space in the pad ring area with the ground pads and the ground plane of the circuit. The proposed antenna is fabricated with standard CMOS process. Measurement results show that the input reflection coefficient of the main antenna is lower than -10dB from 56GHz to 65GHz. The peak broadside gains of the main antenna and diversity antenna at 60GHz are -3.8dB and -6.1dB respectively. The simulated correlation coefficient between the main antenna and diversity antenna is smaller than 0.2 from 56GHz to 64GHz. This work was very well received and was awarded the best student paper at the 2016 IEEE IWS. Another objective of this project is to improve the optical transceiver sensitivity. To address this challenging design problem, we performed comprehensive analysis and prediction of electromagnetic interference-related common-mode (CM) noise sources. Our novel methodology is proposed to systematically analyze and predict the CM noise of an output driver from various dependent parameters, including CMOS process corners, input signal conditions, power supply, and passive interconnections. Analysis reveals that the nonlinear active circuit predominantly produces an asymmetric rise and fall time of the output signal and is an intrinsic source responsible for generating the CM noise. Furthermore, we investigated adopting PAM4 signaling to replace NRZ scheme to improve the speed and sensitivity of this optical receiver as PAM4 has twice the BW efficiency compared to NRZ. However, PAM4 receivers face new design challenges in terms of the decoding scheme, input sensitivity, and linearity requirement. The decoder in an analog PAM4 receiver is one of the most critical blocks in determining the overall receiver power consumption and input sensitivity since it needs to handle different input amplitudes and can be very power hungry if the decoder worked at full rate. A novel decoder architecture utilizing an adaptive variable-gain rectifier (AVGR) in a 1/4-rate receiver is proposed. In our proposed design, only two voltage-mode comparators are needed for decoding to further save power. For different input amplitudes, the AVGR adaptively tunes the gain of its sense amplifier (SA), and correctly performs the decoding function. The 1/4-rate PAM4 receiver achieved a bit efficiency of 1.38 pJ/bit by concurrently performing gain adaptation and amplitude rectification for decoding the least significant bit (LSB). The proposed decoder greatly reduces power consumption compared with the conventional full-rate topology using three comparators. Experimental results verify that the receiver IC, implemented in SMIC 28-nm high-k CMOS process, can receive and decoder a 24-Gb/s 190-mVpp PAM4 signal at a BER of 10^-11. This work was presented at the 2017 IEEE Asian Solid-State Circuits Conference in the paper “A Low-Power PAM4 Receiver Using 1/4-Rate Sampling Decoder with Adaptive Variable-Gain Rectification.” In terms of nurturing post-graduate students, this project also greatly exceeded the original expectation of only training two PGS. As the project progressed, a total of 4 PhD students were involved as they worked as a design team to combine and utilize the outcome of another GRP project, no. 16212114 which developed a quarter-rate re-timer optical receiver based on a novel linear phase detector with embedded data and clock edge equalization. These 4 PGS's have become experts in optical and mm-wave communication IC and system design. More importantly, they have acquired the precious experience of working together as a team to develop a highly sophisticated IC. This experience has prepared them well for the real-world IC design job environment.

16201815.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201815.value: The first-generation fiber-wireless SoC design was first reported in 2015 at the European Solid-State Circuits Conference. The design details and complete measurement results are published in "A 60-GHz 4-Gb/s Fully Integrated NRZ-to-QPSK Fiber-Wireless Modulator," IEEE TCAS-I, March 2017. Next, in the paper “A 16-Gb/s Millimeter-Wave CMOS Transmitter with Integrated Optical Receiver for 5G Baseband-over-Fiber Systems,” presented at the 2017 Optical Society of America (OSA) Summer Topicals Meeting Series, we reported the second-generation CMOS BoF SoC that can support error-free operation up to 16-Gb/s at 8.6 pJ/bit. This work utilized the outcome of the paper "A Full Ka-Band Power Ampliﬁer with 32.9% PAE and 15.3-dBm Power in 65-nm CMOS," which published later in IEEE TCAS-I, April 2018. Under this project, we researched the techniques for enhancing the optical transceiver sensitivity and data rate. In the IEEE Solid-State Circuits Letters, vol. 1, no. 2, Feb 2018 article “A 26-Gb/s 0.31-pJ/bit Receiver With Linear Sampling Phase Detector for Data and Edge Equalization,” we presented a source-synchronous receiver with a quarter-rate linear sampling phase detector (LSPD) using an embedded feed forward equalizer (FFE) and decision feedback equalizer (DFE) for chip-to-chip/module-to-module communication with medium channel loss. The quarter-rate LSPD is proposed to save power and avoid dithering jitter in a nonlinear bang-bang phase detector. The receiver IC is fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process and achieves error-free operation up to 26 Gb/s with a superior bit efficiency of 0.31 pJ/b while tolerating a 14-dB channel loss at 13 GHz. In the 2017 annual report, it was pointed out that more publications with proper acknowledgement are anticipated in the final report. This issue has been fully addressed with a total of 5 journal papers (4 published in 2018) and 7 conference proceeding articles (4 published in 2017) with acknowledgement of the support of this GRF project funding. These 12 publications reported the different components of the proposed BoF system-on-a-chip. They are the outcome of the 4 PhD students’ thesis work trained with support by this GRF project and another related GRF project under project no. 16212114.

16201815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16201815.value: Based on our current success, to further raise the performance and expand the application of the current SoC, the quarter-rate system can to be improved to support both the legacy binary non-return-to-zero (NRZ) signaling and the emerging 4-level pulse-amplitude-modulation (PAM4) scheme. To meet this requirement, the receiver linearity must be enhanced and the PAM4 decoder design must be investigated. To support the up-and-coming 5G applications with hybrid fiber-wireless broadband links, linearization circuit techniques for millimeter-wave power amplifier and transmitter design need to be further researched.

16201815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201815.value: Driven by the ever-growing demand for broadband mobile data traffic, various mm-wave bands ranging from 28-80 GHz are being evaluated for 5G cellular networks to deliver wireless backhaul connectivity over 10Gb/s. To support 5G mm-wave backhaul links, SoC capable of directly converting broadband signals between optical and mm-wave domain is highly desirable. This outcome of this project has demonstrated experimentally for the first time that small form factor and low cost optical-to-millimeter-wave modulator can be realized to support future fiber-wireless networks. This project has successfully trained 4 PhD student and a post-doc fellow. Dr. Yipeng Wang, who designed the first BoF SoC, has graduated in September 2016 and now works for Xilinx Singapore. Dr. Duona Luo and Dr. Qasim Maqbool, who worked together on the noise suppression techniques to improve the transceiver sensitivity, have both graduated in 2017 and now works for Huawei in Shenzhen and Bahria University in Pakistan, respectively. Dr. Guang Zhu who graduated in 2018 and now works for a leading IC design company in Shanghai, has expanded the BoF SoC from the current NRZ scheme to the next-generation PAM4 data format. Our work has laid the foundation for future 5G optical-mm-wave network system design.
