16202215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202215.value: The semantic web data model called the "Resource Description Framework", or RDF, represents data as a collection of triples of the form ⟨subject, property, object⟩. A triple can be naturally seen as a pair of entities connected by a named relationship or an entity associated with a named attribute. RDF is now used to encode data in various applications to expose, share and connect pieces of data on the semantic web. An RDF dataset can also be considered as a graph, where subjects and objects are vertices, and triples are edges with labels between vertices. A standard way to retrieve and manipulate RDF data is to use the SPARQL query language. A SPARQL query can be considered as a combination of some basic graph patterns (BGPs). Such a BGP is a finite set of triple patterns, where each pattern consists of a subject, property and object, and each of these can be a variable. Each BGP can also be considered as a query graph with variables, and evaluating a BGP is equivalent to finding all sub-graphs matching the query graph. There have recently been many proposals for evaluating SPARQL queries on a single machine. However, as the volume of an RDF dataset becomes large, evaluating SPARQL queries goes beyond the capacity of a single machine. For example, Freebase, consisting of data mainly about individuals, contains 1.9billion triples. DBpedia, a project aiming to extract structured content from the Wikipedia works with 2.46billion RDF triples. According to the W3C, the number of triples in some commercial RDF datasets is more than a trillion. In this proposed study we would like to design efficient solutions which can speed up SPARQL queries of distributed RDF databases exploiting the power of cloud computing and the semantic richness of RDF data. To achieve that goal we need to address three key issues: 1) an effective RDF data partition and storage scheme; 2) an efficient in-memory index structure for each computing node in the cloud which indexes both local data and a global view of the whole graph. 3) a cost model-based query decomposition and planning solution together with mechanisms to handle updates. Success in this effort will produce a novel framework for efficient SPARQL query processing of distributed RDF data. The proposed solutions will not only help query processing, but also shed light on semi-structured and structured data processing in the cloud. 作為語義網的數據模型“資源描述框架”，或RDF，是用⟨subject，property，object⟩的三元組來表示。三元組可以用來表示一對基於命名關系的實體鏈接或表示與指定屬性相關聯的實體。 RDF現在用於各種應用的數據表示，在語義網上共享和連接數據。 壹個RDF數據集也可以被看作是一個圖，其中subject和object 是頂點，三元組是用來表示與頂點相連的有標籤的邊。通常我們使用SPARQL查詢語言去查詢RDF數據。SPARQL查詢可以被認為是壹些基本圖模式（BGPS）的組合。這洋的BGP實際上是壹組有限的三元組的模式，其中每個模式包括 subject, property 和 object，這裏的每個元素都可以是變量。每個BGP可以也被認為是基於變的圖查詢，查詢BGP等價於找所有與查詢圖匹配的子圖。 近來的研究對單機上SPARQL查詢提出了許多建議。然而，當壹個RDF數據集變大，SPARQL查詢將超出單個機器的容量。例如，Freebase的，主要包括個人數據，包含了1.9billion RDF 三元組。 DBpedia的，壹個目的是從維基百科上提取結構化數據的項目， 要處理2.46billion RDF三元組。根據W3C的資料，一些商業的RDF數據集三元組的數目超過壹兆。 在此研究中，我們想利用雲計算的強大功能和RDF數據的語義豐富性，設計有效的解抉方案去加快分佈式RDF的SPARQL查詢效率。為了實現這壹目標，我們需要解抉三個關鍵問題：1）有效的RDF數據分割和存儲方案; 2）對雲中的每個計算節點索引本地數據和整個圖的全局視圖的高效的內存索引結構， 3）基於成本模型的查詢分解機制和更新方案。這項研究工作的成功將產生壹個新的分佈式RDF數據的有效SPARQL查詢處理框架。這個新的框架不僅幫助查詢處理RDF數據，還會在雲計算環境中幫助處理半結構化和結構化數據的查詢。

16202215.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202215.value: In this project, we first studied RDF representation format for distributed environment. In order to speed up the query processing, we have designed compressed signatures [12] which is suitable for representing RDF data in a distributed manner, thus, completing our first objective. In addition, we had investigated the multi-truth discovery problem in knowledge graphs (often represented as RDF data) to resolve conflicts, as a consequence, reducing the cost of storage [4]. For our second objective, we had worked on designing several indexing structures to speed up graph query processing, such as path concatenation queries [13] and pattern matching queries [1] . For the third objective, we had investigated query decomposition and planning strategies for SimRank [10] and Event Participation Queries [8, 14]. To achieve the fourth objective to handle update issues, we had proposed novel solutions to handle distributed dynamic graphs [3] and time-aware query processing [7]. Finally, we built a prototype system to demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed solutions and we are in the processing of moving the whole prototype system on distributed mobile platform [2] to increase its flexibility and usability. In addition to fulfilling the objectives listed in the project proposal, we had worked on crowdsourcing and ridesharing and had developed novel solutions for task assignment [5, 6, 9] and worker recommendation [11] . 1. 16202515.label: Project Objectives

rows: Develop a novel method for hierarchical topic detection from big text data based on latent tree analysis, and empirically compare it with the LDA-based methods for the same task.

16202515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202515.value: The past decade has seen extensive research activities on topic detection from a corpus of text documents. The topics obtained provide an overview of the contents of the collection and can be used to guide browsing. They can also be used for dimension reduction and hence are helpful in tasks such as information retrieval and document classification. The predominant methods for topic detection are latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) and its extensions. In LDA, a topic is a probability distribution over a vocabulary. It describes the relative frequency that an author would use each word when writing about the topic. Each document is regarded as a mixture of multiple topics and is characterized by a probability distribution over the topics. The LDA approach has two key drawbacks that have received little attention so far. First, it characterizes a topic using the words which occur with high probabilities under the topic. However, some of those words might also occur with high probabilities under other topics and hence are not suitable for characterizing the topic at hand. Second, when it comes to hierarchical topic detection, the LDA approach is limited in the number of hierarchy levels it can handle, which is typically set at three in practice. Moreover, the number of topics on each level is not determined fully automatically. In this project, we will develop a novel approach to hierarchical topic detection that overcomes the two shortcomings. In the new approach, each word is regarded as a variable that represents the presence/absence or frequency of the word in a document. It produces a hierarchy with the word variables at the bottom and latent variables at the upper levels. The number of levels of the hierarchy and the number of nodes on each level are automatically determined. The number of levels is not limited to three. Each internal node in the hierarchy is associated with a partition of the documents that is obtained based on the word variables in the sub-tree rooted at the node. Each cluster in a document partition is interpreted as a topic. It is characterized using the words that occur with high probabilities in the documents of the cluster and with low probabilities in documents outside the cluster. The topics at high levels of the hierarchy capture “long-range” word co-occurrences and hence are thematically more general, while the topics at low levels capture “short-range” word co-occurrences and hence are thematically more specific. 从文本数据中提取主题是过去十年机器学习领域的一个研究热点。所获得的主题可以使用户对文本集中的内容有一个整体的了解，帮助他们筛选出感兴趣的文本，同时还可以用于数据降维，有益于信息检索和文本分类。 目前占主导地位的是Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA)主题模型，其中主题定义为词汇集上的概率分布, 所刻画的是作者在谈论主题时使用每个词的概率，而文本被认为是一些主题的混合。LDA主题模型有两个弱点： 首先， 它刻画一个主题时使用的是在该主题下出现概率最高的词汇，然而这些词汇在别的主题下出现的概率也可能很高，从而不具特异性。其次，在进行层次化主题提取时，LDA方法只能分三个层次，而且每个层次上的主题个数需要用户给定。 本项目提出一种新的層次化主題提取方法来克服LDA方法的弱点。在新方法中，每个词被视为一个变量，有两个可能的取值，分别代表它在文本中出现和不出现。通过分析得到一个层次化的模型，其中词汇变量在最低层，其它层次由隐变量组成。模型的层数和每层上的隐变量数是自动决定的，层数没有限制。每个隐变量代表对文本数据的一个划分，划分中的每个类（文本的子集合）被视为一个主题。 在刻画一个主题时，选用在该主题中出现概率高并且在其它主题中出现概率低的词汇，这样的词汇特异性高，能更好地刻画出主题的含义。高层的主题反映“远距离”词汇同现，对应抽象概念，而低层的主题反映“近距离”词汇同现，对应含义相对具体的概念。

16202515.label: Realisation of objectives
16202515.value: We started from the following previous work, which laid the foundation for the use of latent tree models for hierarchical topic detection: T. Liu, N.L. Zhang, P. Chen. Hierarchical Latent Tree Analysis for Topic Detection. ECML/PKDD (2) 2014: 256-272. We first addressed the scalability issue of hierarchical latent tree analysis (HLTA) and published C1 (conference paper 1). Whereas we were able to deal with corpora with 1,000 words and 2,000 documents back in 2014, we can now deal with corpora with 10,000 words and 300,000 documents. Then, we spent much time expanding the work into a journal paper. We systematically discussed the novelty of our method w.r.t alternative methods based on LDA; we described the theory and algorithm in more details and addressed two practical issues; we used a new parameter estimation method so that the method can scale up even better; and we conducted extensive empirical evaluations and comparisons. The paper was published on Artificial Intelligence in 2017 [J1, journal paper 1]. In C4, we showed how to use the results of HLTA to index research papers. A system prototype was developed and it was later expanded to aipano.cse.ust.hk. This website covers research papers published since 2000 at major AI and Machine Learning venue. It lets you keep track of the latest developments in AI and offers a fast way to find recent highly cited papers on various topics or published at a certain venue. In C5, we used HLTA to analyze customer reviews on Yelp. HLTA deals with binary data. In C6, we extended it to deal with count data. Although this is a theoretically a natural next step, it did not lead to improvements to the quality of topics, which explains why it took quite some time to get the paper published. The stated objective of the project is: Develop a novel method for hierarchical topic detection from big text data based on latent tree analysis, and empirically compare it with the LDA-based methods for the same task. The objective is achieved 100% with J1, C1, C4, C5 and C6. Not content with achieving the stated objective, we have done extra work to explore the applications of latent tree models in other areas, namely traditional Chinese medicine [J2, J3], clustering [J4], and deep learning [C3]. In C2, we gave an overview of the research on latent tree analysis and various ways it is used in practice

In this project, we have developed a novel approach for hierarchical topic detection called HLTA. It outperforms the previous state-of-the-art methods based on LDA, and is the new state-of-the-art.

16202515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202515.value: We have demonstrated the usefulness of HLTA by creating a topic-based index to the AI literature. The system (aipano.cse.ust.hk) is currently limited in coverage. It would be interesting to expand the coverage, and to update it timely so as to better serve the AI research community. The technology can obviously be applied to other domains. One domain that we are exploring is PubMed (pubmed-pano.cse.ust.hk). We found, for example, that the topic with the fastest growth in the past three years is: “nuclear, nucleus, repress, repression, repressor, transcriptional-regulation”. 16202615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202615.value: 量子光學技術利用單光子作爲量子信息的載體，使得以光子態編碼的信息以量子力學的規律被操控與傳輸。 這爲實現通過糾纏光子態進行量子通信與計算提供了一個有前景的方式，同時有潛力對我們當前依賴傳統信息載體的通信與計算的方式產生一個革命性的轉變。 最近，得益於矽光子技術的迅速發展，將量子光學技術集成於矽晶片上變得可行與有利。矽量子光學不僅有可能與標準的矽互補金屬氧化物半導體（CMOS）工藝流程相兼容，因此可以在未來實現設計緊湊的大規模集成量子光路，用於在矽晶片上進行量子信息操控；而且也有機會利用納米光子學與納米電子學在可重構的固態設備上來操控量子態。但是，當前矽量子光學仍然處於初始階段。該提議的研究中，我們的目的在於革新CMOS兼容的晶片上的單光子源，實現一定功能的用於準備與操控量子態的量子光路，還有研發該單光子源與光路的單片集成。 矽晶片上的處於通信波段（1550nm）的單光子源最近已經被研發出來，該單光子源基於非線性自發四波混頻（SFWM）現象，該現象產生於絕緣體上矽結構（SOI）和氮化矽（SiN）波導與微諧振器裝置。在SOI的單光子源受到雙光子吸收與隨之發生的自由載流子吸收現象的限制，而在SiN的單光子源則不受到這樣的限制，並且可以通過CMOS兼容的沉積技術與SOI平臺進行單片集成。矽晶片上的集成量子光路已經被研發出來，然而該量子光路利用相對較大體積且寬頻帶的基於波導的非諧振器裝置。利用微諧振腔結構的量子光路更加緊湊且具有波長選擇性，可以提供新的量子操控的機會。然而據我們所知，這樣的量子光路還沒有被研發出來。 現在我們提議研發晶片上處於通信波段的，基於在SiN微盤諧振腔的SFWM的單光子源。我們將通過實驗研究在集成微環與微盤諧振器的雙光子量子干涉現象。特別地，我們將探索新的量子光路器件，包括基於波導交叉耦合的微環諧振器的2x2 量子光學交換裝置，基於雙環諧振器的受控非門。我們將對基於SiN的單光子源與基於SOI的量子光路進行單片集成。

16203115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203115.value: 人類的大腦是數十個解剖結構組成的復雜的神經系統。為了研究更深皮層下區域的功能和結構性質，三維圖像分割是腦圖像定量分析和臨床診斷的關鍵步驟。然而，由於皮層下結構都比較小，且具有顯著的形狀變化，對它們進行分割很困難。此外，一些結構的邊界很模糊，甚至會消失在圖像中。盡管人工標註是獲得高品質分割結果的標準過程，但是這個過程非常耗時，而且不同標註者之間甚至同一個標註者的結果都會存在不一致。近年來，研究人員一直專註於開發基於地圖集的自動分割方法，通過結合關於灰度圖譜和組織標簽對應關系的專家先驗知識。 基於地圖集的分割主要包括三部分：地圖集和目標圖像的配準，標簽傳播和標簽融合。無論是在單地圖集還是多地圖集的情況下，在執行了圖像配準後，目標圖像中的每個點都可以從地圖集中收集一個或多個組織標簽， 這使得標簽融合成為了對目標圖像進行可靠標註的至關重要的最後一步。 在這個項目中，我們將致力於為大腦皮質下區域的圖像分割，開發可靠和準確的標簽推斷方法。標簽推斷的框架將基於無向圖，圖中點的連接和邊的權重可以有效地整合信息，各種優化方法也可以被用來尋找目標圖像的最終標簽分配。特別的是，基於區域表達，我們將探索使用稀疏學習對局部灰度信息進行編碼。對於包含有皮層下結構的較大的圖像區塊，深度學習的方法也會被研究用來提取結構的整體特點。我們認為，通過融合局部和整體的先驗信息，分割性能可以被顯著提高。通過公開的數據集與合作醫院的臨床數據，新提出方法的效力和性能將被進行深入的評估。

16203115.label: Realisation of objectives
16203115.value: The main goal of this project is to develop new label inference methods for atlas-based subcortical structure segmentation in magnetic resonance images of the brain. During the method development, we focused on the enhancements of forward deformation and label fusion for atlas-based image segmentation. We believe that these two components are crucial to the segmentation quality. In the initial phase of this project, we have developed and published [1] a novel unified for atlas-based segmentation with new forward deformation and label refinement processes. In this work, we implemented image deformation under the Markov random field framework and meanwhile, we enforced a newly designed distance constraint with contrast sensitivity on mesh edges. Under the new edge distance constraint, the object shapes in the atlas and the target images can be kept similar during the image deformation process. To compensate for the small shape variations around the structural surfaces, we designed a new label refinement process that incorporates both patch registration and label fusion to improve segmentation performance. For this work, we have tested the new method on two publicly available databases IBSR and LPBA40 for method evaluation. From the preliminary evaluation results, the segmentation results are encouraging. We further worked on image label fusion based on the notion of local and global patch priors [2]. The new framework is used for the segmentation of subcortical structures in brain MR images. Because of the significant overlap of intensity patterns among different tissues in brain MR images, the conventional patch prior can be adversely affected because the patch prior is estimated with intensity similarity measurement. Also, the estimated conventional patch prior can become misleading during the final label inference procedure. We proposed a method for providing more discriminative patch representation in the label fusion process. The new method is based on local and global information. The local and low-level patch prior is obtained by using sparse learning. The high-level structural properties of each subcortical structure are also taken into consideration. The proposed global patch prior is extracted with the Convolutional Neural Networks. Intensive experiments have been carried out on two publicly available datasets and results show that the proposed method is able to obtain very good image segmentation performance as compared with the other state-of-the-art, closely related methods. We continued to explore the use of the above two ideas and the new anatomical information. We then proposed a feature sensitive framework for image fusion in atlas-based image segmentation [3,4]. The new label fusion method is formulated on a graph, which combines both label priors from atlases and anatomical priors from target images. There are three kinds of feature vectors are generated in the new framework, intensity, gradient, and structural signature. We believe these three feature vectors can help capture comprehensive information at a voxel. Rather than exact searching, we used a randomized k-d tree with spatial constraint for selecting candidate atlas nodes for fusion. It is an efficient approximation for high-dimensional feature matching. In order to take consideration of both the consistency and variety of different features, we proposed the feature sensitive label prior (FSLP) in order to gather atlas priors. As FSLP is a non-convex problem, one heuristic approach has been designed to solve it efficiently. Also, with the anatomical knowledge, parts of the target pixels are included as the graph seeds to enhance the label fusion process, and an iterative strategy is used to gradually update the label map. Similar to the prior works, intensive experiments have been carried out on the two publicly available databases. The results in segmentation quality are better when the proposed method is utilized. Overall, the two objectives, new label inference method development and its evaluation, have been achieved successfully and related research outputs have been disseminated in journal and conference publications. References can be found in Section 6.1.

16203115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203115.value: The major findings in this project are related to better methods for medical image segmentation. We have improved methods for forward image deformation and image label fusion in atlas-based image segmentation. The new forward image deformation is implemented by using the Markov random fields with a newly designed distance constraint and contrast sensitivity. The image label fusion process is enhanced by using feature sensitive label prior encoding information about the intensity, gradient, and structural signature. The newly developed methods have been applied to the problem of segmenting and detecting subcortical structures in brain magnetic resonance images. Moreover, the methods have been intensively evaluated and quantitatively compared with the other state-of-the-art methods. The research outcome is listed below in the form of journal and conference publications. 16203115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203115.value: The proposed forward deformation and label fusion methods in image registration could be further extended. One possible extension is the large-scale group-wise image registration which is able to map multiple brain image volumes simultaneously and efficiently. Moreover, the idea of using deep learning methods to extract discriminative features has been explored and extended in retinal fundus image analysis [5]. Automatic analysis of retinal fundus images is of vital importance in diagnosis tasks of retinopathy. Segmenting vessels accurately is a fundamental step in analyzing retinal images. We have developed a new method with deep neural networks to solve this problem. The new method utilizes U-net with residual connection to detect vessels. Deep supervision is employed to help convergence. We have evaluated our model on three databases. Experimental results show that our method is able to give a quality performance with AUC of 97.99% on DRIVE and an efficient running time compared to the state-of-the-art methods.

16203115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203115.value: The human brain is a complex neural system composed of several dozen anatomical structures. To study the functional and structural properties of its deeper subcortical regions, three-dimensional image segmentation is a critical step in quantitative brain image analysis and clinical diagnosis. In recent years, researchers have been focusing on developing automatic atlas-based segmentation methods incorporating expert prior knowledge about the correspondences between intensity profiles and tissue labels. Atlas-based segmentation involves three main components, image registration between atlases and a target image, label propagation, and label fusion. After performing image registration, each image position can collect multiple tissue labels from one or more atlases, making label fusion a crucial final aggregation step for reliable labeling of target images. In this research, we focus on developing accurate label inference methods for image segmentation of subcortical regions in the brain. The label inference framework is developed by exploiting an undirected graph that incorporates information effectively via its connectivity and edge weights and helps find the final label assignment of the target image. In this project, with publicly available clinical datasets, we have demonstrated in the experiments that the image segmentation performance can be enhanced.

16203215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203215.value: The Wi-Fi industry has been extremely successful and fundamentally changed our life by enabling us to be connected anytime, anywhere. The popularity of Wi-Fi is largely attributed to the proliferation of Wi-Fi hotspots in public places such as coffee shops, airports and large conventions, where there is a significant number of people accessing the Internet via the Wi-Fi networks. Unfortunately, with the sky-rocketing growth in wireless traffic demands and mobile devices, the performance of Wi-Fi networks in such crowded environment is extremely poor. In this project, we propose to explore two new directions to improve Wi-Fi performance under crowded situations. 1. Higher throughput with less transmission: In a crowded environment, high contention in Wi-Fi networks costs a large amount of overhead. Frame aggregation is proposed in IEEE 802.11n to reduce contention by aggregating multiple frames for the same destination together at the medium access control (MAC) layer. The applications of frame aggregation are limited to bulk transmissions and thus, it is not applicable to real-time applications. The observation we have is that there are concurrent downlink requests for multiple stations, while most of them only have short frames for transmission. This contradiction leads to the design of multi-user aggregation: instead of restricting each downlink transmission to one station, if an access point (AP) can send data for multiple stations concurrently in a single transmission, downlink contention can be significantly reduced. We will propose Carpool, a new PHY/MAC design that enables frame aggregation for multiple receivers in the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) based WLANs. 2. Frame-level flexible channelization: To improve spectrum efficiency, researchers have realized that flexible channelization should be advocated to embrace fine-grained dynamic access over wide spectrum bands. In the context of flexible spectrum access, wireless devices adaptively select proper spectrum bands based on traffic demands, interference, and channel quality. As channel quality and interference change at the frame level, it is desirable to promptly adapt spectrum accordingly. However, the state-of-the-art solutions either focus on spectrum adaptation within the transceiver’s frequency band or require central coordination with substantial overhead that prevents frame-level adaptation. In this project, we will propose SEER, a detailed design for frame-level wideband spectrum adaptation on commodity radios without adding extra hardware. Wi-Fi networks have been widely deployed and evolved aggressively. Efficient solutions resulting from this research will provide new directions for efficient mechanism design for the ever-crowded Wi-Fi networks, and have tremendous technological and social significance. Wi-Fi網絡的成功從根本上改變了我們的生活，使得廣大用戶能夠在隨時隨地享受網絡連接。 Wi-Fi網絡的普及很大程度上是歸功於Wi-Fi熱點在公共場所，如咖啡館、機場和大型會議場所的大量部署。而這些場所往往是使用網絡人數很多的地方。隨著無線流量需求和移動設備數目的增長，Wi-Fi網絡在這種擁擠的環境性能很差。在這個項目中，我們提出探索兩種新的研究方向，以改善Wi-Fi在擁擠環境下的性能情況。 1、以較少的傳輸次數換取更高的吞吐量：在擁擠的環境中，大量的競爭造成了Wi-Fi網絡的控制開銷很大。IEEE 802.11n標準中提出了幀聚合技術， 通過在媒體接入控制（MAC）層將準備發送到同一目的地的多個幀進行聚合來減少競爭。這個技術僅適用於大數據量傳輸，並不適用實時傳輸需求的應用。我們觀察到，在WiFi網絡中有許多對於多個終端並發進行下行傳輸的請求，而且其中大部分只具有短幀的數據傳輸。這種矛盾驅動我們進行“多用戶聚集”的設計：不限制每個下行鏈路傳輸僅目標於某一個終端，而是讓接入點（AP）通過一個單個的數據傳輸為多個終端服務，這樣就能顯著降低 下行鏈路的競爭情況。我們將提出Carpool，一個新的PHY / MAC設計，使多用戶的幀聚合在正交頻分復用（OFDM）的無線局域網中適用。 2、數據幀級別的信道適應：為了提高頻譜效率，研究人員意識到應該提倡更靈活的信道適應，通過這樣可以在寬頻段中進行細粒度的動態訪問。在靈活頻譜接入的背景下，無線設備自適應地根據數據需求、幹擾、和信道質量選擇適當的頻段進行傳輸。因為信道質量和幹擾變化是在數據幀的級別，所以理想情況是能迅速地相應調整頻譜。在這個項目中，我們將提出SEER，將在現有商用無線設備的基礎上，無需增加額外的硬件，進行幀級別寬帶頻譜適應的詳細設計。

16203215.label: Realisation of objectives
16203215.value: As the project title ‘We can Do More for Crowded Wi-Fi Networks‘ indicated, in this project, we tried to explore various directions to achieve better performance under the crowded wireless networks. We have successfully achieved all the objectives of this project via the following directions. 1. Improve the wireless system and spectrum efficiency by proposing new technologies from throughput enhancement, collision reduction, and energy saving aspects. 1.1) Wi-Fi access points (APs) in large audience environments normally serve a crowd of mobile stations (STAs). After carefully investigating the traffic patterns in public WLANs, we proposed Carpool, a practical design that facilitates transmission sharing among multiple receivers, to tackle this problem. The key idea is to reduce contention by feeding frames for multiple destinations into one transmission at physical layer (PHY). As such, each downlink transmission carries payloads for multiple receivers, which reduces contention overhead and enables in-time response to concurrent requests from multiple users. We have implemented the entire PHY of Carpool on the GNURadio/ USRP platform and tested it in various indoor environments. 1.2) Orthogonal multiple access technologies in today’s mobile systems are inefficient in the presence of such massive connectivity and traffic demands. In this regard, non-orthogonal multiple access has been advocated by the research community to embrace unprecedented requirements. We envision that quality of experience awareness is a key pillar for NOMA designs to fulfill versatile user demands in 5G wireless communication systems. We have systematically investigated QoE-aware NOMA designs that translate the physical-layer benefits of NOMA to the improvement of users’ perceived experience in upper layers. We developed a general architecture with a dynamic network scheduling scheme. 1.3) The intense demands for higher data rates and ubiquitous network coverage have raised the stakes on developing new network topologies and architectures. As the deployments are becoming irregular and flexible, inappropriate configurations occur frequently and undermine the network reliability and service quality. We envision that the fine-grained characterization of user traffic is a key pillar to diagnosing inappropriate configurations. In this project, we investigated the fine-grained traffic patterns of mobile users by analysing the network data containing millions of subscribers and covering thousands of cells in a large metropolitan area. We characterize traffic patterns and mobility behaviours of users and geospatial properties of cells, and discuss how the heterogeneity of these characteristics affects network configurations and diagnosis in future ultra-dense small cells. 1.4) Fixed channelization configuration in today’s wireless devices falls inefficient in the presence of growing data traffic and heterogeneous devices. In this project, we have filled the gaps in spectrum adaptation by overcoming these limitations. We proposed SEER, a frame-level wideband spectrum adaptation system which consists of two major components: i) a specially-constructed preamble that can be detected by receivers with arbitrary RF bands, and ii) a spectrum detection algorithm that identifies the intended transmission band in the context of multiple asynchronous senders by exploiting the preamble’s temporal and spectral properties. We have prototyped SEER on the GNURadio/USRP platform and shown that SEER largely improves system throughput over fixed channel configuration and state-of-the-art spectrum adaptation approaches. 1.5) The high sampling rate in Wi-Fi is set to support bandwidth-hungry applications. It becomes energy inefficient in the post-PC era in which the emerging low-end smart devices increase the disparity in workloads. We proposed Sampleless Wi-Fi, a standard compatible solution that allows energy-constrained devices to scale down their sampling rates regardless of channel conditions. Sampleless Wi-Fi recovered under-sampled packets by accumulating redundancy in packet retransmissions. Our evaluation using GNURadio/USRP platform and real Wi-Fi traces has demonstrated that Sampleless Wi-Fi significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art downclocking technique in both decoding performance and energy efficiency. 1.6) Recent years have seen major innovations in developing energy-efficient wireless technologies. Recent advances demonstrate the viability of direct communication among heterogeneous IoT devices with incompatible physical layers. These techniques, however, require modifications in transmission power or time, which may affect the media access control layer behaviors in legacy networks. In this project, we argue that the frequency domain can serve as a free side channel with minimal interruptions to legacy networks. To this end, we propose DopplerFi, a communication framework that enables a two-way communication channel between BLE and Wi-Fi by injecting artificial Doppler shifts, which can be decoded by sensing the patterns in the Gaussian frequency shift keying demodulator and channel state information. 2. Spectrum auction is deemed as an efficient approach for redistributing spectrum and realizing dynamic spectrum access. Improve the wireless spectrum efficiency by secured spectrum auction design. 2.1) So far, the very few existing works on secure spectrum auctions either provide inadequate privacy protection or incur performance loss in terms of spectrum reusability. In this project, for the first time, we proposed PS-TAHES, a privacy-preserving and truthful double auction mechanism for heterogeneous spectrum. We theoretically analysed the security and efficiency of PS-TAHES, which is proved to ensure a full and strong privacy protection for bidders while preserving the allocation efficiency of the original auction mechanism. 2.2) We outlined the framework for privacy-preserving auction mechanism design, which applies cryptographic tools to the original auction and ensures that the private information of bidders is protected, while the basic functionalities of the auction are maintained. Based on the proposed framework, we further constructed a privacy-preserving heterogeneous spectrum double auction, which is shown to uphold the closely similar allocation efficiency with the original auction, and realized privacy preservation with moderate communication and computation overheads. 3. Other issues related to secure communication enabled in crowded wireless system 3.1) The ability to detect which wearables and smartphones are on the same body has the potential to support a wealth of applications, including user authentication, automatic data synchronization, and personalized profile loading. This paper brings this feature to commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) wearables and smartphones, by creating a virtual “on-body detection sensor” based on devices’ inherent wireless capabilities. 3.2) Today’s mobile devices contain sensitive data, which raises concerns about data security. This paper discusses a covert channel threat on existing mobile systems. Through it, malware can wirelessly leak information without making network connections or emitting signals, such as sound, EMR, vibration, etc., that we can feel or are aware of.

16203215.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203215.value: With more and more crowded wireless network taken into consideration, in this project, we tried to explore various directions to achieve better performance under the crowded wireless networks. We have achieved several major findings and research outcome as follows. 1) We investigated the fine-grained traffic patterns of mobile users and characterized traffic patterns and mobility behaviours of users and geospatial properties of wireless cells. We then discussed how the heterogeneity of these characteristics affects network configurations and diagnosis in future ultra-dense small cells. Based on these observations from our measurements, we investigated possible models and corresponding challenges, and proposed a heterogeneity-aware scheme that takes into account the disparity of user mobility behaviors and geospatial properties among small cells. 2) The high sampling rate in Wi-Fi design becomes energy inefficient in the post-PC era in which the emerging low-end smart devices increase the disparity in workloads. Recent advances scale down the receiver’s sampling rates by leveraging the redundancy in the physical layer, which, however, requires packet modifications or very high signal-to-noise ratio. To overcome these limitations, we propose Sampleless Wi-Fi, which allows energy-constrained devices to scale down their sampling rates regardless of channel conditions. Sampleless Wi-Fi recovers under-sampled packets by accumulating redundancy in packet retransmissions so that it can harvest the diversity gain without modifying legacy packets. Sampleless Wi-Fi significantly outperforms the state-of-the-art downclocking technique. 3) Recent years have seen a proliferation in versatile mobile devices and an upsurge in the growth of data-consuming application services. Orthogonal multiple access technologies in today’s mobile systems are inefficient in the presence of such massive connectivity and traffic demands. In this regard, non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) has been advocated by the research community to embrace unprecedented requirements. Current NOMA designs have been demonstrated to largely improve conventional system performance in terms of throughput and latency, while their impact on end users’ perceived experience has not yet been comprehensively understood. We envision that quality of experience (QoE) awareness is a key pillar for NOMA designs to fulfill versatile user demands in 5G wireless communication systems. We have systematically investigated QoE-aware NOMA designs and provided some implications for future QoE-aware NOMA designs by conducting a case study in video streaming applications.

16203215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203215.value: With more and more mobile users and traffic demand, it is no doubt that we will see an even crowded wireless world. Thus, it is very important to continue explore all the possible directions to improve the wireless system and spectrum efficiency by proposing new technologies from throughput enhancement, collision reduction, and energy saving aspects.

There is a significant number of people accessing the Internet via the wireless networks to enjoy mobile applications and services. Unfortunately, with the sky-rocketing growth in wireless traffic demands and mobile devices, the performance of wireless networks in such crowded environment is extremely poor. 16203315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203315.value: Signal processing is entering a revolutionary phase with exciting new applications such as massive multi-antenna communications, large-scale distributed sensing, social networking, and bio-informatics. A defining feature of modern applications is their tendency to produce larger and more complicated data sets than ever before. In practice, such data is often contaminated with various polluting effects (e.g., outliers) that can completely overwhelm conventional statistical techniques. This is particularly true for the fundamental signal processing tasks of covariance estimation and principal component analysis (PCA), and there is an urgent need for robust solutions that can suitably mitigate such effects. The proposed project is focused towards addressing this critical goal. For covariance estimation, a promising strategy is to employ the class of “M-estimators”, which have demonstrated resilience to outliers and other polluting phenomena under classical settings. However, for high dimensional problems of most relevance to contemporary signal processing, the utility of such techniques remains poorly understood. Only very recently, substantial progress was made, first by the Co-I (Couillet) and then collaboratively with the PI. Therein, novel analytical methodologies were proposed which constituted the first successful attempt at clearly capturing the fine statistical properties of certain M-estimators under a suitable high-dimensional statistical paradigm. Current progress has thus far been restricted to ideal non-polluted data models, but nonetheless provides a significant first step towards a more comprehensive investigation. Building upon this recent work, the proposed project will bring together a stellar team with synergistic expertise, comprising both electrical engineers and statisticians, to address two major challenges related to big data and signal processing. The first will be to develop, for the first time, a comprehensive analysis and design framework for robust M-estimation of covariance matrices under high-dimensional data-polluted scenarios. This will provide fundamental insight, describing the utility of M-estimation structures in modern application settings, and will facilitate the development of novel robust methods for specific signal processing problems (e.g., angle-estimation for array processing). The second major challenge will be to develop a novel class of PCA techniques for high-dimensional polluted data models. An innovative approach will be followed, based on suitably integrating ideas from robust M-estimation with promising recent work on high-dimensional sparse PCA, led by the Co-I (Johnstone) and others. This approach can potentially deliver the first robust eigenvector/subspace estimation algorithms that exhibit (provable) statistical consistency under relevant asymptotic regimes, even when faced with data pollution. 信号处理正进入一个革命性的阶段。它有着令人振奋的新应用，比如大规模多天线通信，大规模分散式感知， 社交网络以及生物信息。 一个现代应用的标志性特点是它们相比以往更倾向于处理更大型并且更加复杂的数据集。在实际中，这些数据常常受到各种污染因素 （比如异常值）的影响，导致传统的统计方法完全失效。典型的例子就是信号处理中的协方差估计和主成分分析。 现在我们急需具有鲁棒性的，可以恰当减小数据污染带来不利影响的方法。 被提议的项目正是专注于解决这个重要的问题。 对于协方差估计，一个有潜力的方法就是应用一类“M估计”。 它们在传统的设定中已经展现出了对异常值和其他数据污染现象的抵抗力。但是对于与当今信号处理紧密相关的高维度问题， 这些方法的效用仍旧被了解甚少。 只有到了最近才有了重大的进展。这个进展首先是由合作的研究员（Couillet）， 然后一同由现首要研究员做出。在这方面，创新的分析方法被提出。 这些方法在一个恰当的高维度统计模型下，首次成功的清晰捕捉到了特定M估计方法的精细统计性质。现在的进展限制在理想的未被污染的数据模型，但是这仍旧提供了一个重大的迈向一个更加复杂全面研究的第一步。 建立在近期成果，现提出的项目将会由一个包括电子工程师和统计学家，协同多方面专业知识的明星团队来解决两个关于大数据和信号处理的重要挑战。第一个挑战将是首次在高维度有数据污染的模型下，建立一个对鲁棒M协方差矩阵估计的全面分析和设计的框架。这个将会提供对M估计在现代应用中的效用的深入认识， 并会促进为特定信号处理问题（比如阵列处理的角度估计）设计的创新的鲁棒方法的发展。第二个重要挑战将是研发出一类针对高维度，数据被污染的模型的主成分分析方法。随之而出的一种创新方法将会结合鲁棒M估计和合作研究员（Johnstone）以及其他人的关于高维度稀疏主成分分析的近期研究成果。 这个方法将有希望提供第一个鲁棒的特征向量/子空间估计算法。这个算法在相关的渐进域，甚至在有数据污染下，能展现（可证明） 统计一致性。

16203315.label: Realisation of objectives
16203315.value: All key objectives have been successfully met. The project has produced numerous key contributions, leading to 2 journal and 4 conference publications, all in leading journals or conference proceedings. It has supported 2 Ph.D. students who have successfully defended their Ph.D. and found excellent jobs. Objective 1: Develop an analytical framework for characterizing the statistical properties of robust M-estimators of covariance under high dimensions with data pollution. This first objective was addressed thoroughly, with the main results reported in Journal Paper 1 and Conference Paper 1. We presented a first analytical framework for characterizing the high-dimensional statistical properties of a large class of (regularized) robust M-estimators, of the Maronna type, with and without data pollution. By introducing novel technical tools from random matrix theory, our analysis revealed that in the presence of clean data (i.e., with no outliers or data pollution), the entire class of robust covariance estimators share similar asymptotic statistical properties as more conventional non-robust covariance estimators designed specifically for clean data. This is important, since it implies that there is no cost in performance by using robust methods (that are designed primarily to suppress outliers or data pollution) under idealized conditions. This conclusion is also markedly different to that found with “classical statistics”, which ignore high-dimensional aspects of the data. Novel methods were also introduced to study the effect of data pollution by introducing and computing a robustness measure referred to as the “Infinitesimal Measure of Influence”, or IMI. Analytical methods were presented to evaluate this performance measure, again using random matrix concepts. Methods for performing robust covariance estimation were also presented in Journal Paper 2 and Conference Paper 3. In this case, results were given for a class of low-rank models referred to as “spiked models”, that arise naturally in adaptive array processing. A framework was presented for optimal covariance estimation by introducing non-linear eigenvalue shrinkage techniques. The analytical frameworks put forward in this project are important, and have led to novel insights into classical robust covariance estimation strategies that have been employed for over half a century, and provided a means of developing new solutions. Objective 2: Employ the analytical framework to investigate the performance of existing robust M-estimation methods. This objective was completely addressed. The analytical framework in Journal Paper 1 was applied to present data-driven methods for optimizing regularization parameters, and to quantify the performance analytically in terms of spectral norm loss. The IMI metric was computed analytically for two important M estimators within the specified class – namely, Tyler’s estimator and Maronna’s estimator, and for certain outlier models. This analysis led to quite striking results, demonstrating that commonly employed M estimators within the Maronna class can perform very differently, in terms of their outlier-suppression capabilities. It was shown that one estimator may outperform the other, depending on the nature of the outlier samples. The results were also complemented with a detailed simulation study. Similarly, in Journal Paper 2, analytical methods were used to characterize the performance of adaptive array processing solutions, based on minimum variance distortionless response (MVDR) beamforming, under high-dimensional settings. This analysis was used to develop optimized covariance estimates that were shown to yield significant performance improvements over solutions based on conventional estimators. Objective 3: Propose novel M-estimation solutions relevant for signal processing applications. This objective was completely addressed. In Journal Paper 2 and Conference Paper 3, we proposed novel methods, based on robust high-dimensional covariance estimation, to propose a completely new class of algorithms for MVDR beamforming. These are classical beamforming solutions in signal processing, and their construction relies on accurate inference of (inverse) covariance matrices of received signals. By exploiting our RMT-based design and analysis framework, we proposed methods that were optimized for the MVDR model, which were data-driven, efficient and easy to compute. A comparative study was done with respect to numerous conventional and more recent MVDR techniques, and superior performance was uniformly achieved. This work clearly demonstrated the value of robust high-dimensional covariance estimation in addressing practical signal processing problems. Objective 4: Investigate novel robust sparse PCA methods for noisy high-dimensional data. This final objective was also addressed. The main results were presented in Conference Papers 2 and 4. In Conference Paper 2, robust sparse PCA methods were developed, again by exploiting high dimensional random matrix tools and ideas. This method was applied to study a biological data set comprising sequence data of the NS5B protein, measured from individuals infected with the hepatitis C virus. The method was able to suitably distinguish “signal” from “noise” in this data set, to identify correlated spectral modes representing groups of protein positions that tended to mutate in a correlated way. These groups were shown to have biological significance; having tight connections to different structural domains of NS5B that had been identified experimentally. In a related problem, in Conference Paper 4, robust methods were presented for Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), for data classification. The idea was to introduce robust regularized M-estimators in the conventional LDA framework, to provide resilience against outliers and data pollution. Analytical performance results were developed under high-dimensions, again by appealing to advanced random matrix concepts. The performance of the proposed robust LDA solutions was shown to be superior to conventional non-robust alternatives. It also yielded promising results for classifying numerical digits, when applied on the well-known MNIST data set.

16203315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203315.value: Below is a brief summary of some the major contributions in this project: [Journal Paper 1 and Conference Paper 1]: These papers proposed new analytical methods for studying robust M-estimators under high-dimensions, with and without data pollution/outliers. The significance of these results is that they provided new understanding of classical robust estimation solutions, in a modern high-dimensional context. They introduced new advanced statistical tools for understanding these estimators, and leveraged these to develop new optimally-regularized solutions. Our study also provided new and unexpected insights into the ability of specific robust estimators to suppress outliers and data pollution. The proposed theoretical methods and results will be of interest to researchers and practitioners who seek to apply robust covariance-based methods on high-dimensional data sets. [Journal Paper 2 and Conference Paper 3]: These papers presented fundamental theory and algorithms for robust covariance estimation under high dimensions for a particular class of low-rank (spiked) models arising in adaptive array processing. The contributions led to the proposal of new MVDR filtering strategies. The development of these strategies exploited a low-rank covariance structure in the received signals, that arises naturally from the signal model. The work again leveraged tools from high dimensional random matrix theory. It led to novel optimized non-linear shrinkage algorithms for robust covariance estimation and filter specification. The proposed MVDR filters were easy to implement and, remarkably, were shown to significantly outperform benchmark “diagonal loading” beamformers, even when they were provided with the (unobservable) optimal diagonal loading parameter. Our proposed solutions will be of interest to signal processing engineers working on problems in communications, radar, and other adaptive array processing applications. [Conference Papers 2 and 4]: These papers exploited robust covariance estimation to develop new solutions for machine learning applications; namely, principal component analysis (PCA) and linear discriminant analysis (LDA). Both applications rely heavily on the estimation of covariance matrices or their spectral properties (eigenvectors and eigenvalues). Novel random-matrix based methods and algorithms were proposed for each problem. The proposed solutions were shown to yield superior performance to conventional “non-robust” solutions, and yielded meaningful results when applied to real data sets. This included application of the PCA method to reveal groups of biologically-significant mutationally-coupled sites of the hepatitis C virus based on measured protein sequences, and application of the LDA method to provide robust classification of numerical digits based on the MNIST data set.

16203315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203315.value: There are various avenues for further development. Here we briefly indicate a few such directions. The current LDA analysis has been restricted to 2-class classification problems. An important extension will be to relax this assumption to develop an analysis and design framework for an arbitrary n-class system. This extension is non-trivial and will require the development of additional random-matrix-based tools. Our current work is also restricted to robust estimators of the “Tyler” type. It would be interesting to further extend the framework to a broader class of M-estimators, and to study the pros and cons of different constructions for the LDA problem. We plan to pursue this direction in the near future. The sparse PCA approach may be further developed along similar lines. It currently remains unclear which M-estimators would be most effective for suppressing noise and data pollution for the purposes of reliably estimating covariance matrix eigenvectors, which form the basis of PCA approaches. Again, this extension will require new technical developments that are non-trivial. It is a major challenge and could form the basis of a separate follow-up project.

16203315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203315.value: The project has provided new mathematical theory and tools for studying and optimizing robust covariance estimation solutions under a modern high-dimensional statistical paradigm. We have developed theory and methods for a broad class of robust estimators, including Maronna’s class of M estimators. This provided new understanding of the statistical properties and performance of conventional robust estimators, and led to the discovery of new optimized solutions. The results were applied to address practical problems related to adaptive array processing and machine learning, on simulated and real-world data sets.

16203415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203415.value: 由於石墨烯具有極大的表面積，出色的導電和導熱性能，以及優異的力學性能，它正迅速成為聚合物基複合材料的一種理想納米分散相。為了完全利用石墨烯的潛力，三個關鍵性的問題需要解決，即：（1）為了避免由於分子間π键重叠導致再次團聚，石墨烯應該在聚合物基體中完全剝離而均勻的分散，尤其是在石墨烯含量很高的時候。缺乏足夠的剝離和分散是阻礙複合材料獲得理想的電，熱，機械性能以及其他重要性能的主要因素。（2）氧化石墨烯有著極高的可加工性和極好的分散性，因此被廣泛應用于複合材料的增強和增韌。然而氧化石墨烯對於提高聚合物基體的功能性並不突出，因為含氧官能團極大的改變甚至破壞了石墨烯本身良好的導電，導熱以及機械性能。（3）石墨烯和聚合物基體之間可控而有效的界面結合對於載荷傳遞，電子、熱和能量的傳導起著決定性的作用。由於石墨烯在聚合物基體中的有效分散，複合材料中將形成巨大的界面體積。然而，和其他分散相相比，對於石墨烯/聚合物界面的控制還缺乏基礎性的理解。 為了解決上述問題，本課題提出製備三維石墨烯結構，包括泡沫，氣凝膠和編織物，以及它們的聚合物基複合材料，並把它們用於新興的結構和多功能材料領域。多種技術將用來製備三維多孔超輕的石墨烯結構，例如基於氧化石墨烯的自組裝形成水凝膠的冷凍乾燥法，在鎳或銅基底上進行的化學氣相沉積法。由於這些本身互相連接的蜂窩狀結構，三維石墨烯網絡將會具備極高的導電導熱性，優異的力學性能以及不同尋常的減震降噪性能。當這些結構作為增強相出現在聚合物中時，這些出色的性能將會傳遞到複合材料中去。根據不同的最終用途，將液態聚合物樹脂滲入石墨烯多孔結構中，或者將聚合物納米顆粒電鍍到石墨烯表面，以形成柔性或剛性的複合材料。石墨烯結構的表面積，孔徑，結點結構，各向異性程度和石墨烯含量以及石墨烯-聚合物界面結合等因素都將作為設計對象，以最大限度地提高最終應用中所預期的效果。 總之，本研究旨在研發包含三維石墨烯網絡結構的多功能性納米複合材料，並將它們應用于電子，產能儲能以及結構複合材料等新興領域。

16203415.label: Realisation of objectives
16203415.value: Significant and exceptional progress has been made, producing many original and interesting results that are published in high-impact journals. The major outcomes from the project are discussed in the following. (1) Synthesis of graphene woven fabrics (GWFs), graphene foams (GFs) and 3D graphene aerogels (GAs) (Objective 1) GWFs and GFs are prepared through chemical vapor deposition (CVD) on Ni templates. The freestanding GWFs show unique morphological features consisting of orthogonally interweaved, inherently percolated, hollow graphene tubes (GTs) while GFs consist of a highly porous, cellular structure. A high electrical conductivity of 2.9 S/cm is achieved for freestanding GWF. The composites with 0.62 wt % GWFs deliver a combination of excellent electrical and fracture properties. (J03) 3D GAs with an aligned graphene structure is fabricated through one-step chemical reduction and self-assembly of GO sheets followed by freeze-drying. The unique aligned graphene structure is achieved which shows an ultralow density of ~16mg/cm3 and are highly flexible, capable of recovering 90% compression strain due to the flexible joints, and an extremely high porosity. The anisotropic structure of GAs gives the GA/epoxy composites significant anisotropic properties. (J04) (2) Optimization of dielectric properties of graphene/polymer composites (Objective 2) The effect of chlorination of GO on dielectric properties of Cl-rGO/ poly (vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) composites in comparison with those of the neat PVDF and rGO/PVDF composites without chlorination is studied. The SOCl2 is added into GO dispersion to modify the structure, chemistry, charge carrier density and electrical conductivity of GO, as well as the interfacial interaction and phase of the surrounding matrix in the PVDF composite. The p-type doping improves both the charge carrier density and electrical conductivity of GO. The Cl-rGO/PVDF composites deliver exceptionally high dielectric constants and moderately increased loss tangents. (J01) GO papers are also functionalized with a multifunctional dopant, MgCl2, in an effort to improve the dielectric constant while reducing the dielectric loss. The modification of rGO papers with MgCl2 much enhances the dielectric constant while reducing the dielectric loss through dipolar polarization induced by Mg–O, C–Cl and Cl– molecules. The highly aligned GO sheets constitute a network of numerous nanocapacitors in the paper which leads to charge accumulation, giving rise to an extraordinary high-k over 60000. (J01) A novel two-step route is used to prepare GA/PVA composites with exceptional dielectric performance. The composites possess a highly-aligned, conducting graphene skeleton with an ultralow density, a high porosity and remarkable thermal stability, showing ultrahigh dielectric constants combined with moderate losses. The compaction of barrier-shielded, porous GA/PVA composites yield fully consolidated, solid composites, which deliver both exceptional dielectric constants and very stable, low losses. (J08) (3) Development of GF/CNT/PDMS composites for exceptional microwave shielding (Objective 2) and high sound damping characteristics (Objective 3) Nanocarbon materials, such as CNTs and graphene, have been considered promising alternatives to metal-based microwave shielding materials because of their excellent electrical conductivities, very large specific surface areas and low densities. Highly porous PDMS composites containing 3D cellular-structured microscale GFs and conductive CNTs are fabricated. The GF/CNT/PDMS composite with 2.7 wt % GF, 2.0 wt % CNTs and 90.8% porosity delivers an excellent electrical conductivity of 31.5 S/cm and a remarkable EMI SE of 75 dB in the X-band frequency. The corresponding specific EMI SE per density of the material is 833 dB cm3/g. (J03) GF/poly(3,4ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrenesulfonate (PEDOT: PSS) composites are developed by drop coating of PEDOT:PSS on cellular-structured, freestanding GFs. To enhance the wettability and the interfacial bonds with PEDOT:PSS, GFs are functionalized with 4-dodecylbenzenesulfonic acid. The GF/PEDOT:PSS composites present an ultralow density and a high porosity of 98.8%, as well as an enhanced electrical conductivity from 11.8 to 43.2 S/cm. The composites deliver remarkable EMI SE of 91.9 dB and a speciﬁc SE of 3124 dB·cm3/g through signiﬁcant microwave attenuation by absorption. (J06) The above GF/CNT/PDMS composites are used as the sound damper to achieve a commercially viable absorption coefficient higher than 0.3 over a low frequency range of 100-1000 Hz. The GF/PDMS composites with a porosity of 51.5 % and a thickness of 1.6 mm are capable of shielding a maximum 70 % of the incident sound waves at 100 and 200 Hz. The incorporation of MWCNTs into the PDMS matrix allows the frequency band to be expanded to 1000 Hz. The outstanding sound damping capabilities of GF/CNT/PDMS composites make them excellent candidates for noise shielding. (J07) (4) Enhancement of thermal conductivities (TCs) of graphene/polymer composites (Objective 2) The effect of functionalization on TC of graphene and thermal conduction across the graphene/epoxy interface are studied using molecular dynamics simulation (MDS). Functionalization reduces the TC of graphene while improving the interface thermal conductance. An analytical model is developed to predict TCs of bulk composites containing graphene with different lateral sizes. The improved interface conductance through functionalization dominates the TCs of composites when the graphene size is smaller than a few micrometers, making functionalization necessary. However, when the graphene size exceeds the critical value, functionalization becomes unnecessary. Such critical size theory may explain the discrepancy between different experimental results. The effect of number of graphene sheets, n, on TC of multilayer graphene is studied. With increasing n, the TC of embedded graphene in epoxy increases rapidly first before slowing down when n>5, converging to the asymptotic value of bulk graphite at high n. Similarly, the TC across the graphene/epoxy interface increases with increasing n. The benefits of using large, multilayer graphene sheets are confirmed by experiments. (J02, J05) A high-density 3D multilayer graphene web with interconnected, oriented graphene struts is fabricated based on the CVD technique. The continuous high-quality graphene network within the epoxy composites leads to exceptional electrical and thermal conductivities of 50 S cm-1 and 8.8 Wm-1 K-1, respectively. The high filler loading of 8.3 wt% also gives rise to a remarkable fracture toughness of 2.18 MPam1/2, over 100% enhancement over the neat epoxy. (J09) (5) GAs with highly aligned structure and their polymer composites with anisotropic properties and low percolation (Objective 3) GA with a highly aligned, porous structure are produced through unidirectional freeze casting by generating large temperature gradient in the GO dispersion, enforcing the vertical growth of ice crystals. The GO sheets are expelled by the rapidly advancing ice front to assemble between the aligned ice crystals. After freeze-drying and reduction, the unique graphene orientation is achieved in a preferred direction. Unidirectional graphene aerogels (UGAs) with tunable densities, alignment and electrical conductivities are prepared by varying the average size of precursor GO sheets. UGAs prepared using ultralarge GO (UL-UGA) outperform those made from small GO in these properties. The UL-UGA/epoxy composites exhibit an excellent electrical conductivity of 0.135 S/cm, along with an ultralow percolation threshold of 0.0066 vol%. (J04, J10) A highly conductive and stretchable graphene honeycomb (GHC) sandwich consisting of a porous GHC/PDMS composite core and graphene foam/PDMS composite face sheets is assembled. The GHCs possess an ordered hexagonal porous structure with an ultralow density of 3.25 mgcm-3 and deliver an excellent electrical conductivity of 72 Sm-1. The highly porous GHC core endows the sandwich with an ultralow resistance change over large external strains of 60% with excellent structural durability. A stretchable light-emitting display is demonstrated using the sandwich as the electric circuit and light-emitting diodes. (J11)

16203415.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203415.value: Objective 1: GWFs and GFs are prepared through chemical vapor deposition (CVD) on Ni templates. The freestanding GWFs show unique morphological features consisting of orthogonally interweaved, inherently percolated, hollow graphene tubes (GTs) while GFs consist of a highly porous, cellular structure. (J03). Unidirectional graphene aerogels (UGAs) with a highly aligned, porous structure are produced through unidirectional freeze casting using a custom-made apparatus capable of generating large temperature gradient between the upper and bottom surfaces of the GO dispersion, enforcing the vertical growth of ice crystals. (J04, J10) Objective 2: 3D network graphene/polymer nanocomposites are fabricated by infiltrating liquid polymer resins into the highly porous, cellular graphene with different anisotropic and structural characteristics. These composites present various multi-functional properties, all of which are better than or on par with those of the state-of-the-art similar graphene-based composites reported in the literature. They include excellent electrical conductivities with low percolation thresholds (J04, J09), high thermal conductivities (J02, J05, J09), exceptional dielectric constants with low dielectric losses (J01, J08), high electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness values (J03, J06) and good sound damping capabilities (J07). Objective 3: The graphene structure is tailored using unidirectional freeze casting to form aligned unidirectional graphene aerogels (UGAs) which in turn endow the composites with significant anisotropic characteristics in different directions. (J10) The composites prepared using these UGAs produce exceptional anisotropic mechanical properties and electrical conductivities. (J06) In particular, those prepared using ultralarge graphene oxide sheets present even better electrical conductivities with lower percolation thresholds as well as much better mechanical and fracture properties than those containing small graphene sheets. (J12) A stretchable light-emitting display is also demonstrated using the sandwich consisting of honeycomb-shaped aerogels as the electric circuit and light-emitting diodes presenting reliable lighting performance under different loading conditions. (J13)

16203415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203415.value: The work described in Section 5.3 provides much insight into the mechanisms for achieving excellent dielectric properties, where a highly aligned graphene structure is desired for a high dielectric constant while the conductive path along the transverse direction should be blocked to reduce the dielectric loss. These principles will help future work in further improving the dielectric properties of 3D network graphene/polymer composites. Expanding the highly-aligned graphene structure prepared based on the freeze casting technique may allow the assembly of UGAs with other nanoscale fillers, such as BN nanosheets that possess high thermal conductivities but are electrically insulating, to form micro-sandwich composites with both excellent dielectric constants and high energy densities for high temperature applications.

16203415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203415.value: This project aims to prepare three dimensional graphene architectures in the form of foams, aerogels and woven fabrics, and their polymer-based composites for emerging structural and multi-functional applications. Novel techniques, such as self-assembly of graphene sheets into hydrogel, unidirectional freeze casting followed by freeze drying and chemical vapor deposition of graphene on Ni/Cu templates, have been employed for the fabrication of 3D porous, ultralight and highly-aligned graphene architectures with large surface areas. The graphene structure, like surface area, pore size, junction structure, degree of anisotropy and graphene content, as well as graphene-polymer interfacial adhesion are tailored to maximize the desired effects. Due to the inherently interconnected cellular structure, they deliver exceptional transport properties and excellent mechanical properties as well as high noise damping capabilities, which are translated into the composites made from these nanofillers. The composites produced by infiltrating liquid polymers into the porous graphene structure present unique multi-functional characteristics, such as anisotropic electrical and thermal conductivities with exceptionally low percolation thresholds, exceptional dielectric constants with low dielectric losses, excellent electromagnetic interference shielding capabilities and high sound damping coefficients. These properties ensure potential applications of these 3D graphene/polymer composites as lightweight dielectrics, microwave absorbers, thermal interface materials and sound dampers.

16203515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203515.value: The survival rate of patients suffering from complex ailments such as autoimmune disorders, infectious diseases, cardiovascular diseases, and cancer could immensely benefit from early diagnosis in clinics. Robust diagnosis calls for information on genetic and proteomic profiles of multiple markers simultaneously. Single-marker assays generally fall inadequate due to disease heterogeneity, especially in cancer. Moreover, biomarkers are usually present at minute concentrations during early stages of a disease and unlike nucleic acids there exists no amplification for proteins and peptides. Exacerbating this issue is the sheer complexity of blood serum with more than 10,000 distinct protein species varying over a concentration range of nine orders of magnitude. Methods including enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISA), electrophoretic immunoassays, radioimmunoassays, and mass-spectrometry-based proteomics can reliably measure proteins but have limited use for point-of-care or clinical settings due to long assay time, complicated protocols, and/or difficulty in multiplexing. The challenge of identifying and/or quantifying low-abundance protein markers has been tackled in the past decade by adopting a two-pronged approach. While developing advanced concentration techniques that can enrich target analytes into a smaller volume from a dilute sample, researchers have also come up with a set of label-free ultrasensitive biosensors that can readily detect the presence of target proteins in trace amounts. These approaches have largely benefited from recent advances in miniaturization, in particular from novel structures and materials with critical dimensions in nanometer scales (nanoscales) comparable to those of target species. These nanoscale structures including nanoparticles, nanowires, nanotubes, nanopores/nanoslits, and nanochannels allow us to tap into the physics of the small world for an enhanced signal transduction, thereby empowering us to probe individual molecules. A new addition to this set of nanobiosensors is a nanofluidic diode based on the concept of an ionic current rectification through an asymmetric nanopore or nanochannel configuration. While the nanowire and nanotube biosensors have been extensively studied, the limitations of the nanofluidic diode biosensors for detecting low-abundance proteins have not been explored on integrated platforms. More importantly, the nanofluidic diodes using nanopores/nanoslits are compatible with a new type of electrokinetic concentration technique wherein nanofluidic junctions are leveraged for their ion concentration polarization characteristic. Here, we propose to demonstrate an integrated nanopore diode biosensor for label-free detection of a target protein marker and its subsequent integration with a nanofluidic junction for enrichment-enhanced detection. We also propose to demonstrate a multiplexed label-free detection of target proteins on an array of such biosensors. 身患複雜病癥（例如自身免疫失調，傳染病，心血管疾病，癌症）的病人的生存率的提升很大程度上得益於臨床的早期診斷。然而，一個穩妥的診斷方法往往同時需要不同疾病標誌物的基因和蛋白質組學信息。只能針對單一標誌物的化驗方法很難勝任一些異質性疾病，特別是癌癥的檢測。此外，在疾病的早期，這些標誌物是極其稀少的。其中，與核酸分子不同，蛋白質標誌物還缺少有效的擴增手段。更加嚴重的是，這些蛋白標誌物所存在的血清中還有超過10,000種不同的蛋白質，而且他們的濃度會超過目標蛋白的一億倍以上。現有的蛋白質檢測方法，例如酶聯免疫吸附測定（ELISA），電泳免疫測定，質譜分析，雖然可以可靠地檢測出目標蛋白，但是很難做到臨床線蟲及時檢測，因為他們往往需要很長的時間，複雜的步驟，而且難以檢測多種蛋白。 在過去的十年中，科學家們一直致力於從兩個方面來克服檢測低濃度蛋白標記物的這一挑戰。一方面是開發先進的蛋白濃縮科技來提高目標蛋白的濃度，另一方面則是研究超敏感的生物傳感器，直接檢測出這些極少量的蛋白質。這些方法的研究進程很大程度上得益於最新開發出的一些納米結構，例如納米顆粒，納米線，納米管道，納米孔/縫。這些納米結構允許我們接觸到在納米世界中的一些全新的物理現象，從而大幅提升傳感器的敏感度。其中，納米流體二極管是一種新型的納米生物傳感器。這類傳感器的工作原理是利用不對稱的納米孔縫來起到整流的作用，而蛋白分子的出現會引起整流特性的改變，從而被檢測到。不像納米線之類的傳感器，集成化的納米流體二極管蛋白質傳感器還有很大的開發空間。而且這類基於納米孔縫的傳感器可以直接與最新研究出的納米流體電動學分子濃縮科技相結合 在這裏，我們計劃開發一種集成化的納米流體二極管生物傳感器，並使用這種傳感器來檢測蛋白生物標誌物。此外，我們打算在此類芯片中集成納米流體分子濃縮技術所需要的納米流道來進一步提升傳感器的敏感度和檢測濃度下限。我們還會致力於開發集成化的傳感器陣列用來進行多路高通量的蛋白分子檢測。

16203515.label: Realisation of objectives
16203515.value: This was a fabrication intensive project; the devices proposed featured three-dimensional nanostructures (e.g., cylindrical nanocapillaries and conical nanopores) non-trivial to fabricate via lithography-based and semiconductor processing techniques. A significant portion of our effort went to addressing the issues arising from the fabrication of such structures. A further major effort dealt with demonstrating them for the intended applications for the first time. Despite the hurdles, all the objectives have been met. Objective 1 is concerned with the enrichment of proteins using an electrokinetic preconcentrator based on the ion concentration polarization (ICP) across the nanoslit or nanocapillary junctions. We mainly focused on the nanocapillary junctions and demonstrated the enrichment of ovalbumin protein, achieving an enrichment factor of 105 from a starting concentration of 500 fM (microTAS, Kaohsiung, 2018). Along the process, we discovered that the nanocapillaries exhibit a linear current−voltage characteristic in isolation at low salt concentrations. This is despite the presence of ion-depletion zone, which is associated with the diffusion-limited transport and the consequent nonlinearity in the classical sense. We summarized our findings in a peer-reviewed journal paper (Analytical Chemistry, 2020). This paper is also the first account of ICP characteristics obtained from highly ordered 1D nanochannels. Moreover, we leveraged the ICP across the nanocapillaries and described the very first ICP-based nanofluidic memristor in a communication (Analyst, 2019). We also reported on the ICP characteristics of a single conical nanopore as we developed the integrated nanopore biosensors for the subsequent objectives. (microTAS, Kaohsiung, 2018). Objectives 2 and 3 are concerned with the detection of proteins using an integrated nanopore fluidic diode biosensors based on the nanoslit fabrication process that we previously demonstrated. The nanopores and nanoslits are made of glass on a silicon microchip fabricated in a batch process through low-resolution photolithography and standard semiconductor processing tools. These nanofluidic structures can be transformed into biosensors and provide ultrasensitive, label-free, multiplexed electrical detection of disease markers in real time through charge-dependent ionic current rectification (hence the name diode). This is realized by functionalizing the nanopore and nanoslit sites. That is, respective monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) are immobilized on the nanopore (nanoslit) and surroundings (active site). We successfully fabricated a nanopore fluidic diode as proposed and transformed it into a biosensor by functionalizing it against the target, troponin T (cTnT), which is a cardiac protein known as a disease biomarker for acute myocardial infarction. We achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 1 fg/mL (∼ 30 aM) in buffer, an order of magnitude lower than the level we attained with nanoslit counterparts. This is expected because the target proteins captured around the nanopores can modulate the entire ionic flow unlike the partial modulation observed with the nanoslits. We similarly noted an ultralow LOD for cancer protein markers in a pure buffer: carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA, 1 fg/mL; ∼ 6 aM), α-fetoprotein antigen (AFP, 10 fg/mL; ∼ 150 aM), and human epidermal growth factor receptor-2 (HER2, 0.1 fg/mL; ∼ 1.5 aM), measuring each independently using nanopores functionalized accordingly. We also fabricated an array of nanopores and functionalized each nanopore in the array to a target protein. We then used the array for multiplexed detection of multiple protein targets delivered as a mixture. Specifically, we demonstrated an array of three identical nanopores with each nanopore treated with mAbs for a specific cancer protein among CEA, AFP and HER2. We noted minor cross-reactivity of mAbs for the target antigens through control experiments further establishing the rectification behavior being specific and modulated by the target antigens in the test mixtures. We also performed multiplexed experiments using undiluted and untreated human serum samples spiked with equimolar mixtures of target markers at various concentrations. We recorded an average LOD of 1 pg/mL for HER2 (∼ 7.3 fM) and 10 pg/mL for both CEA (∼ 56 fM) and AFP (∼ 150 fM) when gauged against the response levels to the serum samples that were not spiked. We summarized our results in a peer-reviewed reputable journal publication (ACS Nano, 2018). As for the nanoslits, we enhanced the fabrication yield by revising the original process, specifically, by introducing alumina atomic layer deposition (ALD). By introducing ALD process, we succeeded also precise control of the nanoslit dimension down to 30 nm as opposed to 70 nm achievable through the low-yield process. We functionalized a single nanoslit by surface modification and demonstrated sensitive detection of cardiac biomarker protein, troponin T (cTnT). We presented our results in a prestigious international conference (Transducers, Kaohsiung, 2017). Meanwhile, the structures and fabrication methodologies developed in this project led to other related demonstrations. We demonstrated hydrodynamic chromatography of DNA fragments using long nanocapillaries (Analyst, 2017). Moreover, we demonstrated continuous-flow electrophoresis of DNA and proteins using a novel sieve based on short capillaries (Analytical Chemistry, 2017). We leveraged a part of nanopore process to further demonstrate single-cell point constrictions for reagent-free high-throughput mechanical lysis and intact nuclei isolation (Micromachines, 2019). We also demonstrated continuous-flow separation of nanoparticles in a device based on favorable combination of electrothermal drag and dielectrophoretic forces (microTAS, Basel, 2019).
