16203515.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203515.value: A major outcome of this project concerns the development of a label-free ultrasensitive biosensor for multiplexed electrical detection of disease biomarkers (see Publication 6; Section 8; Part C). The biosensor features a novel nanostructure, which is an integrated array of conical nanopores built into a glass layer on silicon using low-resolution photolithography and standard semiconductor processing tools in a batch process. The biosensor platform allows further integration of upstream functional modules such as sample preparation or sample cleanup for a sample-to-answer testing. The nanopore is fabricated based on the nanoslit process we previously introduced for label-free ultrasensitive detection of protein cTnT. Both nanopores and nanoslits are nanofluidic diodes functioning based on the same physical principle. However, nanopores make a superior sensor as compared to nanoslits owing to their structures. Moreover, a nanopore is more conducive to an array formation for multiplexed detection of target molecules than a nanoslit. We used here, as a proof-of-concept demonstration, three nanopores functionalized against distinct cancer proteins to show multiplexed detection capability. However, this demonstration can be extended to other proteins and nucleic acids by immobilizing corresponding capture probes around the nanopores. The details of our results are given in Section 5.3, Part B. A further project outcome worthy of note here is the ICP characteristics of nanocapillaries. While we found the enrichment factor comparable to those reported for other nanofluidic junctions (see Publication 4; Section 9; Part C), we discovered that the ICP characteristics of a nanocapillary largely deviates from the characteristics of known nanofluidic junctions at low salt concentrations. The latter show the expected nonlinear current-voltage curve due to the presence of the limiting current associated with the ion depletion zone (ICP) whereas the former exhibits a linear behavior. Interestingly, further experiments on single nanocapillaries confirmed the presence of the ion depletion zone. We described these findings based on the interplay between the nanocapillary conductance and the conductance of the neighboring microchannel walls (the so-called surface shunt). Also, we noticed that the nanocapillary transport identifies more closely with the mobility of protons than that of the salt cations. We attributed fast transport to phosphorus-doped silicate glass, the nanocapillary material featuring very fine pores. These pores are likely to be populated with protons as a result of moisture and carbon dioxide adsorption from the air. These outcomes led to the training of two PhD and three MPhil students (see Section 10, Part C).

16203515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203515.value: A major outcome of this project concerns the development of ultrasensitive label-free biosensors for electrical multiplexed detection of disease biomarkers. The proof-of-concept demonstration of a multiplexed detection has been implemented here on a relatively small array which involves only three nanopores, thereby allowing multiplexed detection of only three distinct protein markers. However, a large panel of biomarkers must be detected in a given bodily sample for an accurate disease diagnosis and prognosis. For instance, tens of nanopores can be arranged into a rectangular array where each nanopore is functionalized against a distinct protein target and then measured independently through a row-column addressing. This platform would allow multiplexed detection of tens of biomarkers. The bottleneck, however, lies with the nanopore functionalization which must be done selectively. This step appears to be challenging and likely to limit the array density. Further areas of development may involve nanopore fabrication and functionalization chemistry. Replacing monoclonal antibodies with aptamers as capture probes offers certain advantages. Aptamers are relatively small molecules stable at room temperature and with attractive features including long shelf life and superior affinity and selectivity. Innovations in fabrication are desired for reliability, simplicity, and a possibly reduced cost.

16203515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203515.value: New technologies that can facilitate the detection and analysis of biological macromolecules including proteins and nucleic acids in a bodily sample are of utmost value to accelerate diagnosis and prognosis of diseases. Nanotechnology has delivered modern computer microchips and is among top candidates for fulfilling this task because it can provide microscopic components comparable in size to macromolecules. Using nanotechnology, this research project demonstrated biosensor microchips for ultrasensitive label-free multiplexed detection of disease biomarker proteins. The project also demonstrated analytical microchips for separation of DNA and proteins according to molecular size or electric charge through techniques, mainly including electrophoresis and pressure-driven liquid chromatography. Not only, do these microchips offer performance boost in analysis time and accuracy over traditional techniques but also lead to a considerably shrinkage in the equipment size into portable scales for potential deployment to hospitals, clinics, and check points (e.g. airports for a rapid screening of passengers against infectious diseases). With these microchips the analysis can be performed with a minimal amount of sample requirement, a feature considered precious in some applications such as infant care and forensics.

16203715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16203715.value: 支持大规模数据通信的光交换数据中心网络结构

16203715.label: Project Objectives
16203715.value: MegaSwitch’s data plane design and scaling methodology: To enable MegaSwitch, we first propose optical wavelength switch (OWS) with commercially available optical devices. Then by connecting multiple OWSes on a ring, we design MegaSwitch that readily support 6K+ ports, and 12K+ ports with technology advances. To the best of our knowledge, MegaSwitch is the first optical DCN architecture that supports non-blocking, arbitrary ∗-cast connectivity at such scale. Our key scaling methodology is the combination of Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) and Space Division Multiplexing (SDM). Scalable and distributed control plane of MegaSwitch: Guided by parallel algorithms and graph theory, we propose to design a scalable and distributed control plane for MegaSwitch. Each node measures its own traffic demand to other nodes, and make requests for wavelengths using a distributed wavelength assignment algorithm. Fault-tolerance in both data plane and control plane: We will analyze the possible vulnerabilities in MegaSwitch, and implement necessary redundancy and mechanisms to achieve fault-tolerance in both data plane and control plane. Implementing a fully functional MegaSwitch prototype: We started to investigate MegaSwitch one year ago, and up to now, we have already implemented a small MegaSwitch prototype with 3 OWS-EPS nodes (90 1GbE ports). On this preliminary testbed, we ran a centralized control plane and measured basic data plane metrics such as bisection bandwidth, delay, and switch overhead to validate its control plane performance. We are working towards constructing a larger 10-node, fully functional MegaSwitch prototype running the proposed distributed control plane.

16203715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203715.value: 当今数据中心网络中的大数据和云应用催生了多样化的数据移动模式（一对一（单播），一对多（多播），多对一，以及多对多）。所有模式都在并行数据处理应用中经常出现，例如MapReduce，Spark，Dryad等。当应用程序扩展在越来越多的服务器上时，如何设计一个数据中心网络架构以支持复杂通信模式与越来越多的节点是一个根本的挑战。 传统的多层电数据中心网络架构（例如，Folded Clos或Fattree）不能使成本和复杂性的下降，因为它们需要在每一层的大量交换机，光学收发器和光纤；同时，他们的高功耗也是严重的问题。因此，工业界和学术界最近转向光网络技术，以降低成本，功耗和复杂性，同时提供高网络容量。 然而，大规模数据密集型通信需要光学数据中心网络架构去满足下列额外的挑战： 1, 高端口数（数据层）：大规模的通信需要网络结构提供高端口数量，以支持多个节点间的通信，并需要支持 “* -cast”（单播，组播，多对一，和多对多）与无阻塞的通信。 2, 可扩展的控制层：当拓展至更多节点时，控制层不应该产生显著的开销与延迟。 3, 容错性：在故障情况下的应用提供可靠的服务。 现有的光网络解决方案不能同时满足所有的要求。它们有的端口到端口的连通受到限制，所以不能用于不同的通信模式；另外，有的设计的端口密度受到限制，以至于不能扩展增加节点数（后文详述）。 本项目的总体目标是：设计一个能够满足的上述挑战的光学数据中心网络架构，MegaSwitch，以支持数据中心内部多模式，高带宽，多节点的网络需求。该项目由以下4个部分组成： 1, MegaSwitch的数据层设计：我们首先设计基于市售的光学设备的光波长交换机（OWS）。然后，通过环状连接多个OWSes，MegaSwitch可以支持6K +端口数量，（用更先进的技术可进一步支持至12K +）。目前，MegaSwitch是第一个在如此规模支持无阻塞与* -cast的光学数据中心网络架构。在我们的设计中，关键方法是结合波分复用（WDM）和空分复用（SDM）来扩展端口数量。 2, MegaSwitch可扩展的分布式控制层：基于并行算法理论和图论，我们设计了MegaSwitch可扩展的分布式控制层算法。每个节点测量其自身到其他节点的流量需求，并通过使用分布式波长分配算法（DWA）来实现波长的请求与分配。 3, 数据层和控制层的容错：我们分析MegaSwitch中可能存在的漏洞，并提出实施必要的冗余和机制来实现数据层和控制层的容错。 4, 实现一个功能齐全的MegaSwitch原型：我们开始在一年前进行MegaSwitch这一项目，到现在为止，我们已经实现了一个 小规模的、3 个OWS-EPS节点、90x1G端口的MegaSwitch原型。在此原型上，我们运行了一个集中的控制层，并测得基本数据层指标，如二分带宽，时延，切换开销，以验证其数据层的性能。我们正在努力建设一个更大的10节点、通过分布式控制平层运行、功能齐全MegaSwitch。

16203815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203815.value: The scaling of mainstream CMOS transistor technology has entered the sub-20nm regime. While the performance of the active device is being continually enhanced, the limitation is now shifted to the interconnect technology. The popular interconnect materials such as copper and tungsten have been found to be insufficient due to increasing resistivity with dimension scaling and electromigration concern under high current density. New materials such as carbon nanotube (CNT) and graphene have been extensively studied to extend the scaling roadmap for interconnect. One of the most important applications of the new material is for it to be used as a via filling material. Due to its vertical structure, small dimension and resistance to electro-migration, CNT is the most promising material to achieve a breakthrough as a via filling material with respect to device scaling. However, many barriers have to be overcome before these materials can enter mainstream manufacturing. In this project, we are going to study the integration of CNT as a via filling material into the mainstream CMOS technology. Through our previous studies, we have already developed a number of fundamental techniques to process CNT on silicon substrate. It is a natural extension to integrate these techniques with existing or projected CMOS technologies according to the International Technology Roadmap for Semiconductors (ITRS). A new set of problems in process compatibility have to be overcome in this work. For example, the requirement to have the metal catalyst at the bottom of the via to form CNT via filling is not compatible with the silicide technology in CMOS processing. In addition, the reported vertical CNT forest resistance is still too high for CMOS interconnect application. A systematic study on methodologies to achieve high areal CNT density, small tube diameter, and low CNT-metal contact at a temperature below the melting point of the interconnect metal is required to achieve meaningful integration of CNT technology with mainstream interconnect processes. To address the challenge to integrate CNT as a via filling material into the backend interconnect technology, the project will approach the problem using both experimental demonstration and theoretical formulation. Based on our previously developed process, we are going to perform modifications and optimization to demonstrate a methodology for process integration. In addition, theoretical study based on atomistic simulation will be performed to investigate the approach to reduce the via resistance and form reliable CNT-metal contacts. 主流的CMOS晶体管技术的比例已进入亚20纳米制度。而活性器件的性能正在不断提高，限制现在已经转移到互连技术。流行的互连材料，例如铜和钨已发现不足以由于 增加电阻率在高维缩放和电的关注电流密度。新材料如碳纳米管（CNT）和石墨烯已经 广泛研究延长缩放路线图互连。 其中最...之一这种新材料的重要应用是为它可以通过填充材料用作。由于它的垂直结构，小尺寸和耐电迁移性CNT为最有前途的材料，通过填充材料实现突破作为对于设备的结垢。然而，许多障碍面前，这些被克服材料可以进入主流制造。 在这个项目中，我们将通过填充材料为研究碳纳米管的集成为主流的CMOS技术。通过我们以往的研究中，我们已经开发了一些基本的技术来处理的CNT上硅衬底。之 是一种自然延伸，整合这些技术与现有的或预计的CMOS根据国际半导体技术蓝图技术（ITRS）。一组新的工艺兼容性问题，在这项工作中加以克服。例如，要求具有金属催化剂在通至底部经由填充形成CNT为不与硅化物技术中的CMOS工艺兼容。 此外，所报告的垂直CNT森林阻力仍然太高，在CMOS互联应用。有关方法进行系统的研究，以实现高面CNT密度，小管的直径，并在温度低于低CNT-金属接触 互连金属的熔点来实现有意义整合是必需的碳纳米管技术的主流互连工艺。 为了解决对CNT通过填充材料到后端整合为一个挑战互连技术，该项目将采用两种实验方法的问题论证和理论公式。根据我们以前开发的过程中，我们要进行修改和优化，展示了流程整合的方法。此外，理论研究的基础上原子模拟将进行调查的方法，通过电阻减小并形成可靠CNT-金属接触。

16203815.label: Realisation of objectives
16203815.value: We have gracefully completed all the revised objectives according to the plan and the important results are reported in a number of publications. They are summarized below: (1) For objective 1, we have developed a CMOS compatible carbon nanotube (CNT) synthesis using nickel catalyst instead of iron that cause contamination to the front-end transistors. We have also successfully reduced to the fabrication temparture to around 400 degree Celcius to avoid the interconnect metal from melting. The process has been reported in 2 journal and 1 conference papers, J1, J5, C5 reported in part III of this report. (2) For objective 2, we have developed an oxide plasma tip planarization process to replace the conventional chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) process to remove the excess carbon nanotube over the via. It shows that the process can reduce the damage to the CNTs and lower the contact resistance between the CNT and metal wire. The results are reported in J4 In addition, we have studied the effect of CNT diameter on the density of synthesized CNT to futher reduce the resistance of the contact plug. The results have been reported in C6. (3) For objective 3, we have studied the proper of the CNT-metal contact resistance and identified the cause of high contact resistance is mainly due to the damage to the CNT during the CMP process. In addition, the slurry used in the CMP process has also been shown to cause contamination to the dangling carbon-bonds when they are put in contact with a metal. The understanding led to a new process of planarization using oxygen plasma to avoid the CMP process. The results have been reported in J4. (4) For objective 4, we have successfully isolated the components contributing to the contact resistant of a CNT via. The are the resistance due to chemical bonding between the metal and the CNTs, and the CNT resistance in the via. The model of the chemical resistance between the metal and CNT has been report in J4. The via resistance due to CNT mainly depends on the CNT diameter, CNT density and the size of the via. And its model have been reported in two conference paper C5, C6. (5) For objective 5, we have demonstrated different process to form CNT contact plug on the source and drain region of a MOSFET with Titianium Silicide and Nickel Silicide. MOSFETs withs with the newly developed CNT contact plug technology has been demonstrated and the results have been reported in J3 and a few conference papers C1, C2, C3, C4. In addition to realize the above objectives, we have applied the CNT on the non transistor regions when performing the CNT plug integration. And we found that the CNT technology can be used to reduce the inter-connect capacitance as well. The results have resulted in additional publications J2, J6 and C7. We did not do detail study on the results as they are not the focus of this project even though they are related. It may serve as the foundation for future work to further reduce the interconnect delay.

16203815.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203815.value: As a result of this project, we have arrived at the following results and outcomes: (1) We have developed a process to synthesis CNT on a metalic substrate a very low temperature using a non-contaminating metal catalyst. By modifying the catalyst structure, we can achieve high density CNT synthesis in very small opening. (2) We have modeled the contact between CNT and metal and developed a process by using oxygen plasma to reduce the contact resistance. (3) We have optimized the CNT synthesis process to grow CNT on different substrates, including Titanium Silicide, Nickel Silicide and insulating substrated. This is important for further CNT related technology in the future. (4) We have successfully demonstrated transistors using CNT filled via as part of the interconnect components. It is the first them a CNT process is combined with mainstream transistor process. This mark the feasibility for using CNT in a mainstream manufacturing process to enhance the interconnect performance.

16203815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203815.value: The process in this work is considered at the stage of proof-of-concept. A number of optimization is still necessary for the technology to be used in manufacturing, including the following: 1) Reduce the randomness of the synthesized CNT diameter and position 2) Reduction of CNT diameter to fill very small vias 3) Further reduction of the resistance of CNT via 4) In the project, we have found that the CNT synthesis process can be combined with the interlayer dielectric deposition process to reduce the dielectric constant of the interlayer dielectrics. This can potentially lead to breakthough in reducing interconnect capacitance.

16203815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16203815.value: With the continuous scaling of the mainstream CMOS technology, the current density passing the interconnect wires is getting higher and higher. Some common interconnect metals such as copper (Cu) and tungsten (W) are approaching their current carrying capacity limit due to electromigration and other reliability concerns. Carbon nanotubes (CNT) have been extensively studied as a potential solution to sustain the high current density and further reduce the interconnect resistance. While fully replacing metal interconnect with CNT is still far from reality, the use of CNT to enhance the current interconnect technology is promising. One particular attractive application for CNT is to form the via filling material. However, additional requirements are imposed when it is used in conjunction with the mainstream CMOS technology, including: 1) the catalyst has to be compatible with existing CMOS process and contaminating material such as Fe should be avoided t he catalyst cannot penetrate through the underlying metal or silicide to cause inter-diffusion problem 2) the CNTs have to be synthesized at low temperature 3) the synthesis process should be selective that CNTs are only form inside the via but not other parts of the wafer 4) the process should be scalable to very small via dimension 5) the resulting CNT forest should be dense and uniform 6) low CNT and contact resistance with ohmic behavior Before this project started, a satisfactory process to address the above issues are still yet to be found. In this work we have developed a technology to address all the above issues and for the first time to demonstrate a full integration of the CNT technology to the mainstream CMOS manufacturing process. The work has achieved a proof-of-concept for the first time to verify the feasibility of the proposed methodology

16203915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203915.value: The amount of embedded memory cache is increased to enhance the performance of systems-on-chip such as general purpose microprocessors, digital signal processors, and application-specific integrated circuits in each new Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) technology generation. Static Random-Access Memory (SRAM) cell is the basic building block of the memory banks of systems-on-chip that are employed in all of modern computing systems and popular portable electronic devices such as smartphones and tablet PCs. Further miniaturization, increased performance, lower power consumption, enhanced reliability, and stability are critically important requirements for future computing systems. The achievement of these goals and the realization of future computing products with market-appeal and success depend, to a great extent, upon the advances in memory technology. Reliability of memory circuits is degraded with increasing variability and decreasing power supply voltage in scaled CMOS technologies. Furthermore, a larger memory cache operating at an increased switching frequency consumes higher power, thereby shortening the battery lifetime of portable devices and causing a significant challenge for the cooling of advanced computer systems. Increased power consumption, elevated chip temperature, shorter battery lifetime, and system failures due to insufficient data stability, weak write-ability, and high leakage currents of embedded memory subsystems are primary concerns in modern computers and portable electronic devices. Novel memory technologies are highly desirable for achieving better reliability, stability, and energy-efficiency in future computing platforms. The Fin Field-Effect Transistor (FinFET) is currently recognized as the best candidate to replace the conventional Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor (single-gate/planar/bulk MOSFET) as the basic building block of future giga-scale integrated circuits. New techniques will be developed in this project for enhancing the reliability and energy-efficiency without degrading the integration density or functionality in the memory subsystems of future FinFET microprocessors and mobile computing devices. Various asymmetrical device and circuit structures will be explored for simultaneously satisfying the data access speed, reliability, and stability requirements of future high-performance memory systems. New, superior, and compact memory cells with various novel asymmetrical device and circuit structures will be developed. Substantial enhancement is data stability and reduction in power consumption will be achieved without degrading the performance or increasing the silicon area as compared to the existing memory technologies. Novel FinFET memory intellectual property (IP) will be developed to satisfy these goals that are critically important for the realization of future advanced mobile electronic devices and other high-performance computing platforms.

16203915.label: Realisation of objectives
16203915.value: Several novel SRAM cells with a mix of asymmetric and symmetric transistors have been developed and characterized with the technology computer aided design tools in this project. Objective 1: A 15nm FinFET technology with symmetrical (FinFET-Sym), asymmetrically gate overlap / underlap engineered (FinFET-Asym1), and asymmetrically gate-underlap engineered (FinFET-Asym2) transistors has been developed for this project. FinFET-Sym are designed and optimized to match the International Technology Roadmap for Semiconductors projections for 15nm FinFET technology node. Atlas 2D simulator (purchased using the project fund) is used to characterize the transistors and SRAM cells. The gate length, fin thickness, and fin height of transistors are 15nm, 6nm, and 15nm, respectively. The gate work-functions of the n-type and p-type FinFETs are 4.46eV and 4.88eV, respectively. Equivalent gate-oxide thickness is 0.7nm (1.9nm HfO2 + 0.4nm SiO2). The on-current and off-current that are produced by the minimum size (single-fin) n-type FinFET are 1756µA/µm and 82nA/µm, respectively. The gate overlap length is 10% of the nominal gate length in FinFET-Asym1. The underlap on the right side of the device was increased from 3nm to 10nm for lowering left to right current (ILR) as much as possible while maintaining right to left current (IRL) similar to the on-current of the optimum FinFET-Sym. The IRL is similar to the on-current of the optimum FinFET-Sym when the right underlap and left overlap lengths are 6nm and 1.5nm, respectively. Due to shorter effective channel length in FinFET-Asym1, the off-current that is flowing from right-to-left and left-to-right are however increased by 3.8x and 2.7x, respectively, as compared to FinFET-Sym. ILR that is produced by FinFET-Asym1 is 36.2% lower as compared to FinFET-Sym. This reduction of left to right current provides significant enhancement of data stability during read operations with the asymmetrical bitline access transistors in SRAM cells. Due to shorter effective channel length, however, FinFET-Asym1 produces higher bitline leakage current as compared to symmetrical FinFETs in the idle mode. An alternative asymmetrical FinFET with reduced subthreshold leakage currents was also developed in this project. The underlap on the right side is longer as compared to the left side in an asymmetrical FinFET-Asym2. When the voltage level of the left terminal of FinFET-Asym2 is higher than the right terminal, ILR is reduced due to the increased series resistance of the channel with the longer underlap region on the right side of the device. The underlap length on the left side of FinFET-Asym2 was varied from 0nm to 3nm in this device optimization study. For each underlap length on the left side, the underlap length on the right side was increased from 3nm to 10nm for lowering ILR as much as possible while maintaining IRL similar to the on-current of FinFET-Sym, which is observed when the right and left underlap lengths are 6nm and 2nm, respectively. Due to longer effective channel length, the left-to-right and right-to-left off-currents that are produced by FinFET-Asym2 are 37.8% and 27.9% lower, respectively, as compared to FinFET-Sym. ILR that is produced by FinFET-Asym2 is 37% lower as compared to FinFET-Sym. The project objective has been 100% achieved. Objective 2.1: Symmetrical FinFETs are preferable in cross-coupled inverters for producing lower leakage currents in an SRAM cell. Alternatively, asymmetrical transistors are preferable for bitline access to achieve stronger data stability during read operations. Based on these observations, a novel hybrid SRAM cell (SRAM-Hybrid1) that employs both symmetrical and asymmetrical transistors was developed in this project. Asymmetrically gate overlap / underlap engineered FinFETs (FinFET-Asym1) are employed for bitline access. Alternatively, cross-coupled inverters are implemented with symmetrical FinFETs in order to enhance the read data stability and suppress the subthreshold leakage currents. The project objective has been 100% achieved. Objective 2.2: An alternative hybrid FinFET SRAM cell with asymmetrically gate-underlap engineered bitline access transistors was developed for this project. SRAM-Hybrid2 employs asymmetrically gate-underlap engineered FinFETs (FinFET-Asym2) as the bitline access transistors. The cross-coupled inverters of SRAM-Hybrid2 are implemented with symmetrical FinFETs. SRAM-Hybrid2 suppresses the bitline leakage currents while providing similar read data stability and write ability as compared to SRAM-Hybrid1. The project objective has been 100% achieved. Objective 3: A new single-ended read asymmetrical SRAM cell (SRAM-New1) with underlap engineered tied-gate symmetrical FinFETs was developed for this project. The primary goal of enhancing the read data stability has been achieved as compared to the conventional symmetrical SRAM cells. While the circuity topology of SRAM-New1 is asymmetrical, SRAM-New1 is actually composed of only symmetrical transistors. SRAM-New1 is therefore easier to process and more tolerant to process parameter fluctuations as compared to the other SRAM cells that require asymmetrical transistors that are investigated in this project. The underlap lengths of the transistors in the left inverter are longer as compared to the transistors in the right inverter of the proposed asymmetrical SRAM cell. Furthermore, the transistors in the left inverter of SRAM-New1 are minimum sized (single fin). The bitline access transistors and the pull-down transistor in the right inverter of the proposed SRAM-New1 are identical to the symmetrical SRAM-Tied. The underlap length of the pull-up transistor in the right inverter is identical to the symmetrical SRAM cells. Unlike the symmetrical SRAM cells, however, the pull-up transistor in the right inverter of the proposed asymmetrical SRAM cell consists of two fins. The strengths of the pull-up transistors in the left and right inverters are therefore different. Similarly, the strengths of the pull-down transistors are also different. The voltage transfer characteristics of the left and right inverters in SRAM-New1 are therefore not symmetrical. This provides enhanced static noise margin with the new SRAM cell. The project objective has been 100% achieved. Objective 4: Critical requirements for successful operation of memory circuits at ultra-low voltages are read data stability and write ability. Read and write margin requirements determine the lowest supply voltage that can be applied to a memory cell for minimum power consumption. A new memory cell was developed in this project for enhancing the read data stability, hold data stability, and write ability. Although the circuit structure has been developed, the characterization of this circuit has not been completed yet. FinFET technology will be extremely difficult to scale beyond 5nm technology generation. Gate-all-around (GAA) MOSFET is likely to replace the FinFET technology in sub-5nm CMOS technology nodes. Therefore, the PI has recently shifted focus towards this emerging technology and submitted a new proposal to RGC. Objective 4 will be fulfilled as part of that new memory technology development effort in the future. Objective 5: This objective has not been achieved due to a combination of factors such as the lack of experience of the students assigned to the project, closure of the nanosystem fabrication facility at HKUST for extended periods of time during the turmoil in Hong Kong in 2019 and 2020, the research student’s absence from Hong Kong for more than six months during the coronavirus crisis, and lack of funds that can be used for using the fabrication facilities at HKUST subsequent to the recent return of the research student to Hong Kong from his home country. FinFET technology is rapidly approaching the end of its technology scaling roadmap. Objective 5 will be therefore fulfilled as part of a new GAAFET memory technology development effort in the future provided that the necessary funds for device fabrication could be secured from RGC.

16203915.label: Major findings and research outcome
16203915.value: Objective 1: Asymmetrical transistors with significant skew between left to right and right to left currents have been successfully developed. ILR that is produced by FinFET-Asym1 is 36.2% lower as compared to the on-current that is produced by FinFET-Sym. Objective 2.1: The read current that flows from the bitline to the node that stores a “0” is weakened with FinFET-Asym1 as compared to a symmetrical transistor during read operations. The voltage disturbance on data storage nodes is therefore suppressed and read data stability is thereby enhanced with SRAM-Hybrid1 as compared to conventional memory circuits. Objective 2.2: Due to the higher series resistance of the channel, the bitline access transistor is weakened during read operations in SRAM-Hybrid2. The read data stability is thereby enhanced with the asymmetrically gate-underlap engineered bitline access transistors as compared to the conventional memory cells. During write operations, the write current flows from the node that stores a “1” inside the memory cell to the discharged bitline. The write current is significantly higher than the read current in SRAM-Hybrid2. The transfer of new data into the SRAM cell is thereby facilitated. Furthermore, the bitline leakage current that is produced by the hybrid asymmetrical SRAM-Hybrid2 is suppressed as compared to the conventional memory circuits and SRAM-Hybrid1. Objective 3: The write operation with the proposed SRAM-New1 is dual-ended. Each of the transistors in the left inverter of SRAM-New1 are minimum sized. The gate-underlap lengths of pull-up and pull-down transistors in the left inverter of SRAM-New1 are also elongated to further weaken these transistors. The voltage margin and data transfer speed during write operations are therefore enhanced with SRAM-New1. Furthermore, transistors with longer underlaps produce lower sub-threshold leakage currents. In the idle mode, SRAM-New1 consumes the lowest leakage power among all the memory cells that are considered in this project. The read operation is single ended. The right pull-down transistor in SRAM-New1 consists of two fins for suppressing the data disturbance during read operations. Furthermore, the right pull-up transistor in SRAM-New1 consists of two fins. The voltage transfer characteristics of the right inverter is less skewed as compared to conventional SRAM cells. The underlap lengths of the transistors in the left inverter of SRAM-New1 are tuned to enhance the gain of the voltage transfer characteristics in the transition region. The openings of the butterfly curves of cross-coupled inverters are wider with SRAM-New1, thereby providing significantly stronger data stability as compared to conventional memory circuits.

16203915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16203915.value: The goal of the completed project was to develop novel FinFET memory circuits. FinFET technology, however, will be admittedly difficult to be scaled to sub-5nm gate lengths due to severe process variations, short-channel effects, subthreshold leakage currents, and photolithography/fabrication challenges of (skinny and tall) fin structures that will be required to be able to provide sufficiently high current density in sub-5nm technology nodes. The gate-all-around (GAA) MOSFET is the most promising device to continue the scaling of CMOS technology into sub-5nm gate lengths. Novel memory circuits with stacked nanosheet gate-all-around MOSFETs will be developed by the PI for future computing systems. The ideas that will be explored in this new project will be superior to the technologies that have been developed for the recently completed project. A new proposal with these new ideas and future development plans has been submitted to RGC (currently in review).

16204015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204015.value: Sensors are ubiquitously deployed as the “eyes” and “ears” of modern engineering systems. At home and in appliances, they are used to monitor environmental and physical attributes to improve our quality of life. In automobiles, they are used for engine-control, air-bag deployment and tire-pressure monitoring, etc., to improve fuel efficiency and to enhance safety. In mobile and “wearable” devices, they are used for screen orientation, gaming, navigation and monitoring of biometrics, etc. With time and in a world of the Internet-of-Things, their deployment will become even more prolific. This pervasiveness is fueled also by their affordability, which in turn is predicated on an economy-of-scale made possible by a massively parallel batch manufacturing technology. The redeeming feature of this technology, based on that used to make integrated circuits, is that it costs almost as much to make one billion devices as it does to make a few! In general, signals captured with a sensor must be "processed", typically using a micro-electronic circuit. Since both the sensor and the circuit are fabricated using essentially the same micro-fabrication technology, a possibility exists for their "monolithic" integration. Though potentially more capable and more reliable, such integrated micro-systems are the exceptions rather than the rules in reality. Their realization is hindered mostly by issues of incompatibility between the materials and processes used to fabricate the mechanical "sensing" and electronic "signal processing" devices. The silicon-migration technology (SiMiT) is recently applied to form spontaneously suspended mechanical diaphragms. Capable of greatly reducing the incompatibility issues plaguing the aforementioned integration, its utility has been demonstrated with the monolithic integration of a 16x16 mechanical force-sensing active-matrix diaphragm array with a non-trivial “row-scanning” electronic circuit. While showing great potential as a scheme for device integration, SiMiT could be significantly enhanced by further development that resolves existing issues in yield- or performance-degrading surface roughening and limitations in how the mechanical and electronic devices are isolated. Successful development of the enhancements will result in a "great leap forward" in the integration capability of SiMiT, thus allowing not only the implementation of more demanding applications but also the adaptation of the cost-reducing "foundry" model to the integrated micro-systems industry. The latter has been successfully deployed in the integrated-circuits industry, and bred giant industry icons like Qualcomm and the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company. 傳感器被廣泛地應用為現代工程系統的“眼睛”和“耳朵” 。在家居中，它們被用於監測環境和物理屬性來提高人們的生活質量。在汽車中，它們被用於控制發動機，安全氣囊的釋放和輪胎壓力監測等。最終提高燃料效率和安全性。在移動和穿戴式設備裡，它們被用於控制屏幕方向，遊戲，導航和生物特徵識別技術等。隨著物聯網技術被進一步推廣，可以預測它們的部署將變得更加廣泛。 這種普及來源於它們低廉的價格，而這又取決於一個基本的經濟原則：廉價是通過大規模批量製造技術來實現的。該技術是基於製造集成電路的工藝。兩者的成本幾乎一樣。 在一般情況下，一個用傳感器捕獲的信號通常要先經過微型電子電路的“處理” 。因為傳感器和電路都是用基本相同的微加工技術製造的，這就存在對兩者進行“單片”集成的可能。雖然一體化的集成微系統具有更強和更可靠的潛能，但真正能實現的卻不多。其阻礙來自製造機械的“感測”和電子的“信號處理”器件的材料和工藝都要克服不兼容的問題。 矽遷移技術可用來製造自發形成的懸浮機械隔膜，並大大降低困擾上述一體化的不兼容的問題。矽遷移技術的可行性已通過驗證，並被用來實現機械力傳感16×16有源矩陣膜片陣列與一個“行掃描”電子電路的單片集成。矽遷移技術雖有巨大的潛力，但也有進一步改善的空間：包括解決機械和電子器件的隔離方法，降低表面粗糙的問題等等。 本建議書所提的技術如研製成功，將實現矽遷移技術的集成能力的一個飛躍，並允許更高要求的應用。最終促成低成本的“代工”模式的開展。有助於培育出和集成電路行​​業巨頭一樣的成功範例。

16204315.value: 本項目計劃研究濕磨條件下一種新光學方法在綫測量工件表面形狀誤差所涉及的多相流體相互作用和不透明問題。氣水柱用來推開不透明的冷卻液，從而產生一個透明窗，以便讓測量光綫到達工件表面。這個新方法避免了以前的表面刮傷和冷卻液遮擋問題，從而使高質量加工變成可能。 高質量加工需要冷卻液條件下在綫測量工件表面，以實現閉環精密控制。冷卻液在許多精密加工過程中普遍使用。濕加工中實現在綫測量，其效率要高於先加工后離綫測量的配置。 幾何量中形狀誤差的空間頻率，較粗糙度和波度的低。但形狀誤差對產品質量至關重要。 現有的形狀誤差接觸測量方法使用了觸針，光學方法則需要乾燥條件。接觸方法容易導致表面劃傷和觸針磨損。光學方法所需乾燥條件不適合在綫測量，這是由於冷卻液通常形成一不透明屏障。 由於這些問題，在綫非接觸形狀誤差測量成爲一個難題。 所提新方法使用氣水結合，可以減少水的使用，從而緩解長期使用帶來冷卻液稀釋影響加工性能問題；也可以降低氣流速度，從而避免使用高速氣體影響測量精度問題。僅使用水柱有冷卻液稀釋問題。僅使用氣柱有高速氣流問題。 研究采用實驗方法，研究不同條件下透明窗產生和由於不透明引起測量誤差問題。本項目的新方法的結果將與已有方法的結果進行比較。 本研究是開發一種涉及透明介質新型傳感器的一個基本步驟，這種透明介質用來幫助實現形狀誤差在綫精密測量。這種流體輔助測量系統可用於許多工業，特別是精密加工工業，以實現所需的高精度非接觸在綫形狀誤差測量。

16204715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204715.value: 本項目擬提出兩種新的方法來計算航空應用中由於空氣湍流運動產生的寬頻噪聲以及其他因素引起噪聲的傳播問題。眾所周知，民用飛機在運行過程中排放的氮氧化物（NOx），碳氧化物的和產生的噪聲會嚴重影響到大氣空氣質量和機場附近公眾健康。其中，在起飛和著陸階段噪聲對機場周圍環境的影響尤為顯著。飛機的噪聲特性是衡量其性能的一個重要指標，其也因之成為設計研發過程中必須要加以考慮的重要因素。一般來說，對於噪聲問題的研究主要包括聲的近場產生，遠場輻射以及介於遠場和近場之間的傳播過程。其中傳播特性會對遠場的輻射有重要影響，因此能否準確的模擬和計算該過程對整個飛機噪聲預測結果的可靠性有著決定性的作用。在目前已有的眾多預測方法中，基於線性化的氣體運動方程（歐拉方程或納維-斯托克斯方程）因而具有豐富的物理內涵，並且且可以通過計算氣動聲學（CAA，Computational Aeroacoustics）來進行數值求解的方法非常重要。然而人們在求解目前應用最為廣泛線性化歐拉方程（LEE，linearised Euler equations）時，在很多情況下，不論是通過時域計算還是頻域計算都會發現求解的聲場會被污染從而計算發散從而難以為繼的現象。究其原因，在與時域計算時流動存在所謂的開爾文-亥姆霍茲不穩定性或者瑞利-泰勒不穩定性；在頻域計算時，相關的矩陣是病態的（即矩陣最大特征值和最小特征值相差過大）。在本研究中，我們將會提出一組精確、穩定和可高效計算的聲傳播控制方程。開發一套可以對氣動噪聲進行預測進而能為聲學設計所參考的為數值方法及代碼。首先我們將繼續探索新近提出的針對LEE的梯度項過濾法（GTF，Gradient Term Filtering）。其次，對於入射提到的聲傳播問題中涉及到的線性波中，主要包含了聲波，渦波和熵波幾種成分， 我們將繼續將其中各種成份分離提取出來的線性波控制方程的更深一步研究。最終呈現的數值計算工具將包含一系列常用的計算氣動聲學技術，例如用於空間離散的高階緊緻有限差分格式，低耗散低色散的高階時間積分格式，新的無反射（輻射）邊界條件等。本研究的研究對象是飛機噪聲，然而提出的方法卻並不失一般性。本研究關於噪聲傳播的方法同樣可以應用到其他的領域例如預測風機渦輪，高速列車以及轎車噪聲等。

16204715.label: Realisation of objectives
16204715.value: 1. Develop a class of wave splitting, linearized sound propagation equations for accurate, efficient and stable computation of sound propagation. The linear Euler equations (LEE) describe the behaviors of both vortical and acoustic disturbances. However, numerical solutions of the LEE may suffer from numerical instabilities in the presence of a sheared background mean flow. The numerical instability, which is known as numerical Kelvin-Helmholtz (K-H) instability, grows boundlessly and contaminates the solution eventually. Few methods were developed to suppress the numerical Kelvin-Helmholtz (K-H) instability and improve the accuracy of the stabilized solution. Two types of Gradient Term Suppression (GTS) method and a variant of Gradient Term Filtering (GTF) method were derived to reduce the side effects caused by previous versions. An artificial damping term (ADT) was proposed to damp the vortical components generated during the simulation, and the acoustic component will not be affected directly. It could be expected that a large damping effect can provide a stable result but distortion of the acoustic field would also be indirectly induced at the same time. Considering this, an adaptive technique was developed for the damping term to adjust the artificial viscosity coefficient during the computation. Four test cases were studied: 1) sound refraction by a strong jet flow, 2) sound refraction by a weak jet flow, 3) vortical wave propagation and 4) spinning modes radiation out of a semi-infinite circular duct with a jet. The results of the benchmark cases validate the proposed methods. 2. Develop a suite of computing programs based on advanced CAA algorithms, high performance computer platforms, and methods for modelling broadband noise propagation by turbulence. An in-house computational aeroacoustics (CAA) solver has been developed and improved during the reporting period. The solver was embedded with the multi-block message passing interface (MPI) and compute unified device architecture (CUDA) technology. Therefore, it is able to realize parallel computing on a high-performance GPU or CPU cluster. On a fully structured gird, the spatial gradient terms are computed using a sixth-order prefactored compact spatial scheme [1]. The time marching is solved by a 4-6 stage fourth-order low-dissipation, low-dispersion Range-Kutta (LDDRK) scheme [2]. A tenth-order explicit filter [3] is applied at the end of each time step to remove spurious high-frequency oscillations. Thus, the CAA code is able to simulate propagations of vortical and acoustic waves without significant dispersion and dissipation errors with 8 points per wavelength (PPW). The time step for each case was restricted to a Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) number smaller than 0.5. The implicit buffer zone condition [4] is applied at boundaries of the computation domain to damp incoming waves and achieve a minimized reflection. The far-field acoustic pressure is calculated from an integral solution of the Ffowcs-Williams and Hawkings (FW-H) equation [5]. In the studies of airfoil leading edge noise, the modified digital filter [6] is used to synthesize an isotropic or anisotropic turbulent. 3. Apply the method(s) to model and improve physical understanding of propagation of broadband noise by turbulence, and problems of engineering relevance. Airfoil shaped components have been widely used in aircraft and wind turbines for flow manipulations, and the noise generated by these components is the non-ignorable part of the total aircraft and wind turbine noise. Generally, the noise generated by an isolated airfoil can be separated into two categories: trailing edge noise and leading edge noise. The CAA solver was used together with the proposed instability suppression methods to study the broadband airfoil trailing edge and leading edge noise. Airfoil turbulent boundary layer-trailing edge (TBL-TE) noise is an important broadband noise source for both aircraft and wind turbines. The TBL-TE noise of a single airfoil or a flat plate have been investigated experimentally, theoretically, and numerically. Several methods have been developed. Comparing with the semi-empirical and theoretical methods, which contain more simplifications and assumptions during the derivation, the numerical simulations can provide accurate results for more complex configurations. Numerical studies on the TBL-TE noise were conducted using a developed hybrid methods. The hybrid method was validated with previous experimental and theoretical studies. The effects of airfoil thickness, airfoil camber, angle of attack, and mean flow velocity on the trailing edge noise were studied thoroughly. In addition, the airfoil oscillation is a common phenomenon which closely relates to the aerodynamic flutter, dynamic stall, lift enhancement, and thrust generation. The aerodynamic properties of the oscillating airfoil have been studied in detail by previous scientists. Numerical studies were conducted during the project period to investigate the effects of a heaving airfoil, following a sinusoidal motion, on the turbulence-leading edge interaction noise. Hybrid CAA simulations were performed on a heaving NACA 0012 airfoil encountering synthetic isotropic and anisotropic turbulence. Before the simulations on a heaving airfoil, the numerical methods were validated. The CAA methods and the synthetic were compared with the analytical model. The capacity of the unsteady mean flow solver was demonstrated by the comparison with experimental measurements. The assumption of an inviscid mean flow was also examined for both stationary and heaving airfoil case. References [1] R. Hixon, Prefactored small-stencil compact schemes, Journal of Computational Physics 165 (2) (2000) 522-541. [2] F. Hu, M. Hussaini, J. Manthey, Low-dissipation and low-dispersion Runge-Kutta schemes for computational acoustics, Journal of Computational Physics 124 (1) (1996) 177-191. [3] O. V. Vasilyev, T. S. Lund, P. Moin, A general class of commutative filters for LES in complex geometries, Journal of Computational Physics 146 (1) (1998) 82-104. [4] J. Gill, R. Fattah, X. Zhang, Towards an effective non-reflective boundary condition for computational aeroacoustics, Journal of Sound and Vibration. 392 (2017) 217-231. [5] J. Ffowcs Williams, D. L. Hawkings, Sound generation by turbulence and surfaces in arbitrary motion, Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London A: Mathematical, Physical and Engineering Sciences, 264 (1151) (1969) 321-342. [6] F. Gea-Aguilera, X. Zhang, X. Chen, J. R. Gill, T. Node-Langlois, Synthetic turbulence methods for leading edge noise predictions, AIAA Paper 2015-2670, 2015.

16204715.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204715.value: For the proposed methods, we found that the most accurate near-field sound predictions come from the GTF-2. Compared with methods that modify the gradient terms, the artificial damping term (ADT) affects only the vortical component directly and requires no Poisson solver. For cases with a weak shear layer, the ADT is able to provide the most accurate results since the adaptive method will not be triggered and the damping effect is small. This part of content has been published as one journal paper (No.1 in Section 8 in Part C) and two conference papers (No.1 and No.2 in Section 9 in Part C). For the broadband airfoil trailing edge noise, the research outcomes include: 1) the numerical method for TBL-TE noise simulation is developed and the performance of the proposed method is validated; 2) unsymmetrical behaviors are observed for the TBL-TE noise generated from different sides of the airfoil under angle of attack; 3) more noise is radiated from the thicker airfoil, and the difference is larger at a lower reduced frequency; 4) The effects of the maximum camber and its location on the TBL-TE noise was evaluated. Increasing the airfoil camber and the backward movement of the maximum camber location both enhance the noise level on the suction side and weaken the noise level on the pressure side. This part of content is being prepared to be published as one journal paper (No.3 in Section 8 in Part C). For the leading edge noise of a heaving airfoil, the research outcomes include: 1) the inviscid mean flow assumption was found to be inappropriate for the leading edge noise of the heaving airfoil; 2) for the isotropic turbulence, the effect of the heaving motion on the airfoil leading edge noise is shown to be small; 3) in the studies using anisotropic turbulence with stationary airfoil, the study shows that the effect of angle of attack on the leading edge noise is opposite for turbulence with larger integral length in streamwise and transverse direction; 4) for the leading edge noise of a heaving airfoil, a larger difference can be observed while the incoming turbulence is anisotropic. In addition, the effect is increased with the Strouhal number. This part of content has been published as one journal paper (No.2 in Section 8 in Part C) and two conference papers (No.3 and No.4 in Section 9 in Part C).

16204715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204715.value: In this project, the TBL-TE noise of an isolated airfoil has been studied. The developed method can be further applied to more complex geometries, such as airfoil cascade. The method can also be further developed for 3D simulations of TBL-TE noise of rotors and wind turbines. In the current study, the effects of vortical and acoustic disturbances on the periodic mean flow and the airfoil heaving motion have been ignored in the linear solver. For high-intensity turbulence, the assumption could be invalid. A future study could be performed to investigate the non-linearity of the interaction. Numerical studies were conducted to study the noise generated by an isolated heaving airfoil. In further development of the research, experiments could be performed to validate the findings of the current study and to further explore the noise generation mechanisms. The trailing edge noise of a moving airfoil could be studied through noise measurement in the wind tunnel with an anechoic chamber. In addition, with the design of a controllable turbulence grid, the leading edge noise of a moving airfoil could also be studied with anisotropic turbulence under various length scale ratios.

16204715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204715.value: Airfoil noise is an important part for both aircraft and wind turbine noise. In this project period, a high-order computational aeroacoustics (CAA) solver was developed. Under certain circumstances, pervious CAA solver may suffer from numerical instabilities and produce contaminated solution. During this project period, we have proposed four new numerical instability suppression methods with validated accuracy and improved performance. The new methods were embedded in the CAA solver. We applied the solver to investigate broadband airfoil leading edge and trailing edge noise. The performance of the CAA solver also has been examined by various analytical and experimental studies, including 1) the airfoil geometry effect on the broadband trailing edge noise; 2) the leading edge noise of a heaving airfoil was studied by using an advanced synthesized turbulence method; 3) the effect of the heaving motion on the leading edge noise was studied using various turbulence and heaving parameters.

16204815.label: Project Objectives
16204815.value: To develop experimental protocols for preparing, transferring and device fabrication on graphene nanomesh at lower temperature plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition. Our aim is to obtain a practical bandgap of ~0.5eV for the nanomesh. To quantify experimentally the electron transport properties of field-effect-transistors fabricated with graphene nanomesh. In addition, scanning tunneling microscopy (STM)/ scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS) will be used to study doping effect and the local density of states created by the plasma treatment. To elucidate the structure-property relationship by correlating the structure of graphene nanomesh with their electronic properties from theoretical predictions. The effects of defect states and doping concentration on the graphene’s properties will also be studied.

16204815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204815.value: The aim of this proposed work is to develop a general synthetic protocol for patterned growth of 2D graphene nanostructures at practical temperatures, in particular, for producing graphene nanomesh (GNM, i.e. graphene with 2D periodical nanosize holes) with a sizeable bandgap. Consequently, graphene nanostructures grown by this protocol will be used to elucidate fundamental principles underlying the structure-property correlation that governs electron transport in nanoscale graphene-based devices. Unlike conventional “top-down” post-growth etching methods, our approach is to use block polymer self-assembly techniques, togather with a plasma-enhanced CVD system that we have recently developed to directly synthesis graphene nanostructures at significantly reduced temperatures (~200oC), which enables us to directly grow graphene with patterned structures. Specifically, the creation of graphene bandgap will be realized by the following methods: 1) growth at low temperature avoids drastic variation of metal morphology, which prohibits patterned growth at high temperate (normally >1000oC); 2) the plasma enhanced CVD methods enable facile introduction of dopants in the graphene structure; 3) to avoid disorders that result from post-growth etching. In additions, lower temperature growth significantly reduces cost and is suited for application in industrial processes. The proposed method will provide a new material platform for advances to be made in the fabrication of high-performance functional devices. The controlled graphene nanostructures to be fabricated will be used to develop a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between structure and properties in these materials, which encompass multidisciplinary issues in surface chemistry, device physics and nanoelectronics. Successful completion of this project will lead to the delivery of a state-of-the-art and manufacturable nanoelectronic devices that is suitable for semiconductor applications. This research will provide a platform for the integration of research and education for Hong Kong student, and promote partnership with industry in Hong Kong. 此计划的目的是開發一種实用的，即能够在较低溫度下，采用化学气相沉积法有序合成二维石墨烯纳米结构的技术，特別是用於製造石墨烯納米篩（GNM，即石墨烯的二维週期性納米孔）以取得足够大的帶隙。此外，利用該生長方法合成的石墨烯納米結構可用來检验結構 - 性能關係的基本關係，此关系主导的電子傳輸的主要性能。不同於傳統的“自上而下”的生長後再蝕刻的方法，我們的方法是使用嵌段聚合物的自組裝技術，结合我 們最近開發出等離子體增強CVD系統，在低温下（〜200℃）直接合成石墨烯的納米結構，以实现石墨烯有序生長。具體而言，石墨烯帶隙將通過以下方法來實 現：1）在低溫下生長避免了金屬形貌的大幅度变化，这种变化在高溫下（通常> 1000℃）导致無法實現有序生長; 2）等離子增強化學氣相沉積方法能夠簡單的在石墨烯結構中引入摻雜劑; 3）避免後生長蝕刻所引入的缺陷。另外，較低的生長溫度顯著降低了成本，提高的工業生产的可能性。 本计划所提出的方法將提供一種新的材料平台，推进高性能的功能元件的製造工艺。所合成的可控石墨烯納米結構將有助于我们对納米電子結構和性能之間的關係的全面了解，提高交叉学科如表面化學，器件物理的认识。成功完成該項目將成功研发最先進的，適合於半導體工业的易製造的納米電子器件。本研究將為學生提供用於研究和教育相結合的平台，促進香港科研與產業的合作。

16204815.label: Realisation of objectives
16204815.value: With the financial support from this RGC grant (project number: 16204815), we have successfully accomplished the respective objectives proposed at the beginning. We have reported our research results on 26 peer-reviewed reach articles and has 3 PhD degree awarded from this support. The following includes details of the work performed to fulfill the proposed objectives. Proposed objective #1: To develop experimental protocols for preparing, transferring and device fabrication on graphene nanomesh at lower temperature plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition. Our aim is to obtain a practical bandgap of ~0.5eV for the nanomesh. In the present study, we have demonstrate a new, simple, scalable approach for directly producing graphene nanomesh devices, with a sizable bandgap at low temperature. Initially, we focused on the development of a new concept of edge-epitaxial growth that enables the van der Waals (vdWs) epitaxial graphene growth on different Cu facets. Fundamentally, different from conventional vdWs growth, this new type of epitaxial growth benefits from the strong binding between the graphene edge and a metal step in a hydrogen-absent atmosphere. This work is published as Wu, R.; et al. Chem. Mater., 2019, 31(7), 2555-2562 (J22). Our method allows the graphene to be grown on various substrates and forms various structure. We have also studied the self-assembly of block copolymer on graphene to obtain the desired pattern. We have tested on a variety of block copolymer and or their hybrid on graphene structures, followed by annealing to obtain microphase transition. Once phase separation of the two compositions was obtained, one component is etched away. By varying these parameters, diblock copolymers is organized into a variety of equilibrium structures which allow us to define the structure of graphene for the next step. Our approaches eliminate the need for the post-growth lithography method that usually damages the graphene film. As shown in our published work (Ou, Xuewu et al. ACS Applied Materials and Interfaces, 10(6), 2018, 5534-5542, (J10)), the fabricated structure can be used to suppress the shuttle of lithium polysulfides (LiPS). During the supported period of the this grant, we have developed engineering methods to prepare nanoparticles encapsulated in N,P-doped graphene, and demonstrate the use as electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Our experimental results (Zhuang, M et al. Nano Lett, 2016, 16 (7), 4691–4698, (J1)) show significantly enhanced performance for such engineered nanostructures due to the synergistic effect from nanoparticles encapsulation, along with nitrogen and phosphorus doping. Proposed objective #2: To quantify experimentally the electron transport properties of field-effect-transistors fabricated with graphene nanomesh. In addition, scanning tunneling microscopy (STM)/ scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS) will be used to study doping effect and the local density of states created by the plasma treatment. In the present study, we have fabricated field-effect-transistors (FETs) and measured their electronic properties (I-V and I-Vg characteristics). More specifically, we fabricated FET devices with dual-gate configurations using 40 nm thick Al2O3 dielectric layers deposited by atomic layer deposition as the top-gate dielectric and 250 nm thick thermally grown SiO2 as the bottom-gate dielectric. We measured the resistance of graphene structured channels as a function of the top and bottom gate voltages at a temperature of 1.8 K. From the resistance versus top-gate voltage curves, we observed of a tunable energy bandgap in the material by the increase in the on/off ratio. At 1.8 K, an on/off ratio of more than 3000 is observed, suggesting a narrow gap in the range of 0.2-0.5 eV. . Based on such result, in a recent paper (Gao, Z. et al. ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 2016, 8, 41, 27546-27552, (J2)), we further extend this method for scalable production of DNA biosensors based on gold nanoparticle-decorated graphene field effect transistors (AuNP-Gr-FETs). The FETs are made in a four-probe configuration, using an optimized bilayer photolithography process that yields chemically clean devices, as confirmed by XPS and AFM, with high carrier mobility (3590 ± 710 cm2/V·s) and low unintended doping (Dirac voltages of 9.4 ± 2.7 V). Proposed objectives #3: To elucidate the structure-property relationship by correlating the structure of graphene nanomesh with their electronic properties from theoretical predictions. The effects of defect states and doping concentration on the graphene’s properties will also be studied. We have performed a systematic analysis of the electronic structure with the nanopore lattices and compared with theoretical predictions. We have systematically investigated the structure and property correlation of graphene nanostructures and other similar two dimensional materials for the electronic properties. In a recent work (Hossain, M. D.et al. Adv. Energy Mater. 2019. 9 (10), 1803689, (J20)), we have developed is an activity correlation with the doping , electronic structure, in order to clarify the origin of reactivity for a series of transition metals supported on nitrogen-doped graphene as catalyst by a combination of density functional theory calculations and electrochemical measurements. Similarly, in another work (Abidi, I.H.et al. Advanced Optical Materials (2019), 7(13) (J23)), we have studied luminescent defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and investigated their potential application as single photon emitters (SPEs) at room temperature. Using the gettering technique developed by us, the resulting zero‐phonon line is deterministically placed between the regions 550 and 600 nm or from 600 to 650 nm, paving the way for hBN SPEs with tailored emission properties. This study illustrates beautifully the robustness of the materials preparation method and the device fabrication using our newly-developed techniques, by which the structure of the graphene materials can be controlled. In summary, we have fully accomplished the proposed objectives in the original proposal.

16204815.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204815.value: The present study successfully developed a general synthetic protocol, along with the transferring method, for patterned growth of 2D graphene nanostructures at practical temperatures, and produced the graphene structures with a sizeable bandgap. With the availability of such materials, we have brought light of the fundamental principles underlying the structure-property correlation for the electron transport in graphene. We have developed theoretical framework to predict the graphene properties by tuning the defect, dopant type, dopant concentration, and validate the theoretical results using experimental results. Following the success, we have further validates the structure-properties by fabrications of field effect transistors and demonstrate the practical applications in a variety of scenarios. The major findings of the work can be summarized as follows: 1. We have shown that the large-area graphene is successfully synthesized by tuning the precursor, substrate, crystal plane of the substrates, and is synthesized at the low temperature when microwave plasma treatment is used for carbon deposition. The bandgap of graphene structure produced reaches the range of 0.2-0.5 eV. We further demonstrate that self-assembly of block copolymer enable us to obtain the patterned growth of graphene structures. We have found that N,P-doped graphene have various practical applications, especially in the area of electrochemical energy storage and conversion. 2. From the electron transport measurement, we have shown that graphene synthesized by our method can achieve with high carrier mobility (3590 ± 710 cm2/V·s), and more over graphene-based field effect transistor (GFET) incorporated in a two-dimensional paper network format (2DPNs) can have electron and hole mobilities of ~1256 cm2 V-1 s-1 and ~2298 cm2 V-1 s-1 respectively. 3. Our density functional theory and molecular dynamic simulation results has revealed an activity–electronic structure relationship that allow us to further explore the practical application of graphene nanomesh and other graphene based materials. Our derived relationship provide design principle for designing highly efficient materials. In addition, we have shown that by tuning the defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN), we can tune their emission properties and use it as single photon emitters (SPEs) at room temperature. With the support from this grant, we have published 26 high profile peer reviewed articles and graduated 3 PhD students, and provides lots of training opportunity for undergraduate and high school students.

16204815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204815.value: This study provide deep understand between the materials design and the desired properties. This work elegantly demonstrates the synergy between computational and experimental methods, and allow us to understand and engineer novel graphene-based structures for desired applications. The experimental results and theoretical predictions from this research has built a solid foundation for a full understanding of relationship among graphene structures, structural-dependent physical/chemical/biological properties, and final device performance. With further funding support if possible, the obtained graphene materials can serve as a basis for exploration of other electrical and electronic properties. The graphene fabrication method strategies will have potential for the development of other two-dimensional materials devices, such as hexagonal boron nitride, transition metal dichalcogenides.

16204815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204815.value: Graphene is the next generation materials, with applications ranging from transistors, sensors and structure materials in tissue engineering. However, pristine graphene has no bandgap, therefore limits their application in semiconductor industry. This project has demonstrate that a bandgap can be open by tuning the atomic-scale structure of graphene, and therefore allow us to control graphene properties and eventually to extend their application in many relevant area. We achieved this by making graphene into a patterned structure using plasma enhanced chemical vapor deposition method, which also allow us to produce graphene at low temperature and eliminate the post-growth etching steps. In addition, this method also allow us to incorporate nitrogen, phosphors dopants into graphene lattice, further tuning the graphene properties. This research represent that significant contribution to the field of chemical engineering, device physics and materials chemistry. This research has also trained many undergraduates and postgraduate student on the way to career in science and engineering.

16204915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16204915.value: Near-inertial oscillations (NIOs) and internal tides (ITs) are commonly observed and are the most important high frequency disturbances in the global ocean, contributing to half of the ocean mixing energy to maintain the abyssal ocean stratification, and providing a crucial pathway for energy transfer among different scales of ocean motions. NIOs are generated during the adjustment process after a strong transient forcing and has a frequency set by planetary rotation. ITs are generated through the modulation and conversion of barotropic tides and have a frequency near the tidal frequencies. Although energies from NIOs and ITs are important in channeling the ocean circulation with different spatial and temporal scales, they have been generally ignored in determining ocean circulation and variability in previous studies, which, consequently, leaves a big knowledge gap in understanding dynamics of oceanic circulation. Despite efforts made to study NIOs and ITs in the oceans around the world during the last decades, many of their fundamental characteristics and physics as well as their interactions with ocean general circulation remain unclear. The South China Sea (SCS) is the largest marginal sea in the western Pacific Ocean. It is one of the most energetic NIOs and ITs oceans in the world. The NIOs are generated by local frequent tropical cyclones and ITs are formed by amplified tidal energy over the unique bathymetry and physical conditions in the SCS. However, compared with other oceans in the world, NIOs and ITs study in the SCS is very limited, and we know very little either about NIOs and ITs themselves, or about their response and contribution to the ocean general circulation of SCS. In this proposed study, we will conduct comprehensive investigations to O1) determine the time-dependent, three-dimensional characteristics and the physical controlling mechanisms of the NIOs/ITs and their energy balances and pathways in the SCS and O2) understand the dynamic processes invoked in the interactions between NIOs/ITs and processes in the SCS general circulation and quantify NIOs/ITs contribution to the SCS mean circulation and its variability. An advanced research approach that combines existing time-series mooring current measurements, the state-of-the-art three-dimensional numerical simulations and methods of wave and energy balance analyses will be utilized, for the first time. This study will advance our understanding of NIOs/ITs themselves and their interactive processes with mean circulation, which are applicable not only in the SCS but also in the oceans around the world. 近慣性振蕩及內潮為海洋中十分常見的高頻率擾動現象，其提供用以維持深海密度層結所需一半以上的混合能量，為海洋中不同尺度物理現象間的能量交換提供關鍵的通道，是大洋中最重要的高頻擾動。瞬時的外界強迫所引致的地轉適應過程會激發近慣性振蕩，其頻率受地球旋轉的限制，接近當地的慣性頻率。正壓潮流與海底地形相互作用則產生與天文潮汐頻率相近的內潮。近慣性振蕩及內潮之能量對連接海洋環流不同的時空尺度甚為重要，然而以前的研究中其對於大洋環流變化的作用常被忽略，致使對大洋環流的動力研究留下較大的知識缺口。過往幾十年，全球對近慣性振蕩以及內潮的研究有所增加，但許多基本的特徵、物理過程，以及其同大尺度海洋環流之關係仍不甚清晰。 南中國海為西太平洋中最大的邊緣海，亦是全球內潮以及近慣性震盪能量最大的海區之一。南海中頻密的熱帶氣旋是產生近慣性振蕩的主要因素，而南海獨特的地形及物理條件有助潮汐能量的增強而產生較強的內潮。相較於世界其他區域，有關南中國海慣性振蕩以及內潮的研究仍十分有限，我們對兩者本身的特徵，以及其對南中國海海洋環流的貢獻之認識仍十分匱乏。在此研究計劃中我們將作出一系列綜合的研究以：O1）確定南中國海中近慣性振蕩／內潮的時間演變及三維空間分佈特徵，其控制之動力機制，以及其能量收支、與其他尺度現象的能量交換。O2）釐清近慣性振蕩／內潮與南海環流相互作用之動力過程，量化兩者於南海平均環流、變化中之貢獻。本研究將運用先進的研究方法，在對海流的時間序列分析的基礎上，結合最先進的南海海洋數值模式，對整體的波動能量收支作出綜合分析，是為同類研究中的第一次。本研究將有助於提升我們對近慣性振蕩／內潮本身特徵以及它們與平均洋流之間相互作用的認識，對南中國海甚至是世界海洋研究均具應用價值。

16204915.label: Realisation of objectives
16204915.value: Near-inertial oscillations (NIOs) and internal tides (ITs) are commonly observed and are the most important high frequency disturbances in the global ocean, contributing to half of the ocean mixing energy to maintain the abyssal ocean stratification, and providing a crucial pathway for energy transfer among different scales of ocean motions. They are one of the most important sub-mesoscale processes that governs the ocean circulation, heat and energy transport/transfer and thus the climate variability. Yet, both characteristics of NIOs and ITs and their role on the larger-scale ocean circulation remain unclearing in the global ocean and as well as in the regional seas like South China Sea (SCS). Our research aims to investigate both characteristics of NIOs and ITs and their role on the larger-scale ocean circulation in the SCS to achieve the objectives outlined by this project. The research involved broad scientific investigation of not only NIOs/ITs, but also general circulation in the SCS, since they are inter-connected. The task is challenge and we adopt advanced research methodology of bottom-up, i.e. from circulation to NIOs/ITs, then top-down, i.e. from NIOs/ITs back to the circulation. Because of lack of field measurement due to huge cost of the field work that cannot be afforded by the funding amount of the current project, we first developed a novel three-dimensional ocean circulation, or China Sea Multi-scale Ocean Modeling System (CMOMS) (https://odmp.ust.hk/cmoms/) , and acquired data from remote sensing data and time-series mooring data by collaborating with colleagues in other institutes to validate the model and conduct the investigation of this project. The CMOMS has been rigorously validated with available evidence from observations, previous studies in literature and theoretical justifications (Liu and Gan, 2017JGR). In particular, the model has successfully simulated the coherent transports cross the straits and slope around the China Seas based on the detailed implementations of regional dynamics in both SCS and the adjacent western Pacific Ocean (Li and Gan, 2020). In particular, for resolving tidal forcing and correctly capturing ITs in the SCS, we implemented tidal forcing used as novel tidal-subtidal numerical open boundary condition. As a result, CMOMS is able to generate realistic circulation and tides that most of the existing models in the community cannot achieve. We conduct thorough investigation of the ocean circulation and dynamics in the SCS, to formulate CMOMS and validate the circulation of CMOMS under the forcing of winds, tides, and other external fluxes. We then proceed to investigate the characteristics responses of NIOs and ITs in the SCS (Obj 1), and interactions between NIOs/ITs and ocean general circulation (Obj 2). We have identified the spatial characteristics of NIOs and ITs in the SCS, based on the observation and CMOMS. In particular, we revealed the unique NIO and near-inertial kinetic energy (KEni) variation under influence of the complex velocity and vorticity of the jet stream arising from the larger scale SCS circulation. These unique features in the SCS are different from those in the open Pacific Ocean where the ocean general circulation is relatively organized and weak. We, for the first time, found that the radiating pattern, local dissipation efficiency, and energy field respond differently to the leaping, looping, and leaking Kuroshio paths in Luzon Strait. These new insights into the dynamics and the theoretical clarification of the refraction mechanism that controls internal tide radiation within general ocean circulation provide new understanding of internal tide energetics, tidally-induced mixing, and thus their realistic representation in climate models. We have successfully depicted the three-dimensional pathway of water masses under the wind and tidally induced NIOs and ITs, in addition forcing of larger scale fluxes from the western Pacific Ocean. These results lead to the novel realization of the layered circulation in the SCS. By conducting the full-spectrum investigation following the bottom-up then top-down approach, this project has produced 6 top highly-calibrated papers in the top international journals in physical oceanography, one book chapter and we are submitting additional one to Nature Geoscience and preparing one. The project also trained two PhD students and one MPhi student. Major findings and research outcome are provided in 6.1 below.

16204915.label: Major findings and research outcome
16204915.value: Based on research philosophy of bottom-up (circulation to NIOs/ITs) then top-down (NIOs/ITs to circulation), we have major findings and research outcome on the characteristics responses of NIOs and ITs in the SCS (Obj 1), and interactions with ocean general circulation (Obj 2). 1. NIOs and NIOs energy response in SCS We used a well-validated three-dimensional ocean model to investigate the process of energetic response of near-inertial oscillations (NIOs) to a tropical cyclone (TC) and strong background jet stream in the SCS. We found that the NIO and near-inertial kinetic energy (KEni) varied distinctly during different stages of the TC forcing, and the horizontal and vertical transport of KEni was largely modulated by the velocity and vorticity of the jet stream of the SCS circulation. Kung and Gan (2020) in Part C. 2. Insight into the dynamics of the radiating ITs in the Kuroshio Current We, for the first time, found that the radiating pattern, local dissipation efficiency, and energy field respond differently to the leaping, looping, and leaking Kuroshio paths in Luzon Strait. These new insights into the dynamics and the theoretical clarification of the refraction mechanism that controls ITs radiation within general ocean circulation provide new understanding of internal tide energetics, tidally-induced mixing, and thus their realistic representation in climate models. Xu at al. (2020) in Part C. 3. Circulation dynamics and new numerical model in the SCS To provide the research platform for the NIOs and ITs study, we developed a novel three-dimensional ocean circulation, or China Sea Multi-scale Ocean Modeling System (CMOMS) (https://odmp.ust.hk/cmoms/) driven by winds, tides and other external fluxes. We conducted thorough investigation of the ocean circulation and dynamics in the SCS, to formulate and validate the circulation of CMOMS. We conducted investigations of fundamental circulation dynamics and identify the layered circulation, pathway of waters and the refreshment of deep waters in the SCS, and the oceanic circulation in the western Pacific Ocean that are jointly governed by the external forcing, such as currents and tides. This project formulates a new and over-all understanding of ocean circulation dynamics in the SCS under various forcing, and provides physical insight into the role of diabatic and adiabatic (induced by submeso-scale processes such as NIOs and ITs) processes on the general ocean circulation in the SCS. 16204915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16204915.value: This project built up a strong foundation both in numerical model and ITs/NIOs dynamics for the further development of the research in following directions: (1) Full-spectrum and down-scale/upscale cascading of energy in the ocean circulation of the South China Sea. This topic is one of the critical components that maintains and modulates ocean circulation variability for regional climate variability in term of energy and heat transport in the ocean; (2) Refine the theory of generation of inertial-internal waves and subinertial geostrophic currents in the typhoon-rich SCS. We have set these two future research directions deriving from the current project in action by conducting the relevant research and development of fine-resolution ocean model in the SCS.

16204915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16204915.value: The motion of ocean or ocean circulation is multi-scale, which consists of the interactive motions with different spatial and temporal scales. Near-inertial oscillations (NIOs) and internal tides (ITs) are two of the most energetic and ubiquitous high frequency variability in the ocean. They channel the larger scale ocean circulation and the small-scale turbulence. NIOs and ITs play critical roles in maintaining the three-dimensional ocean circulation through their substantial amount energy transfer, propagation and dissipation, both in horizontal and vertical directions. This study identified unique NIOs and ITs characteristics and responses under complex SCS basin circulation and their interaction with strong western Boundary current Kuroshio. These findings extend our understanding for the NIOs and ITs which were mainly investigated in the open Pacific Ocea with relatively stable and weak background currents. As the result of the project, we developed a new ocean circulation model with inclusion of forcing of ITs and NIOs to realistically depict the layered circulation and water mass transport in the SCS. We also advanced the physics of the circulation such that overall scientific understanding for ocean circulation theory can be advanced.
