16205115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205115.value: 參數辨識是系統辨識的一個重要分支。它在眾多方面都有重要用途。例如：系統建模、儀器標定、依據實驗數據擬合變量間的相關係數、信號處理和改善控制系統性能。在過去的幾十年中，許多參數辨識算法被相繼提出。然而，大部份的算法仍然依賴最小二乘誤差或梯度變化。這導致大多數的算法最終會收縮到局部最小值而非全局最小值。因此，參數的不準確性會影響系統效率和性能。 本計畫書提出兩種不同的算法來解決局部最小值問題。第一種算法是針對一類非線性動力學系統的在線參數辨識，而另一種是面向一類代數系統（非動力學系統）的離線參數辨識。第一種算法可以被視為是對基於線性回歸的投影方法的修正。它由系統狀態反饋信號產生狀態誤差信號，並利用狀態誤差信號的高頻性及頻譜唯一性來降低投影方法辨識系統參數的難度。通過在線迭代計算，最終得到系統參數。第二種算法是針對非動力學系統的參數辨識。它是一種不依賴於梯度的收縮方法，優點是避免了局部極小值的出現。參數被設計成非動力學系統的輸入而非目標，特殊設計的參數更新策略避免了參數之間的相互耦合效應，並同時降低了隨機噪聲對參數辨識的影響，保證參數最終收縮到特定精度閾值內。初步的仿真結果證明了方法的有效性。這使我們需要繼續研究及理解以上兩種算法的內在原理，從而提出嚴格的數學證明並進行實驗驗證。同樣地，以上提議的兩種算法在實際應用中的有效性也需要大量的驗證工作。

16205115.label: Realisation of objectives
16205115.value: A new theoretical framework of the parameters identification in a class of nonlinear systems governed by Lagrange equation is established. This theoretical framework includes two parts: one is a new measurement system to provide the general coordinate, velocity and acceleration with high accuracy based on partial measurements, and the other is an identifier which is a closed-loop system to identify the value of parameters. The linkage between these two parts is the results of the measurement system providing efficient feedback to identifier for parameters identification. In the new measurement system, two approaches are given the accurate values of the general coordinate, velocity and acceleration based on the partial measurement result of sensor. Here, the first approach is utilized when the general coordinate can be measured by position sensor, the second approach is utilized when the general acceleration can be measured by acceleration sensor. These two approaches can adapt to common industrial applications to establish the values of general coordinate, velocity and acceleration with high precision and low cost. The measured values of general coordinate, velocity and acceleration are feedback to the identifier. Then the identification problem can be transformed to a feedback control problem. The estimated parameters together with the designed desired trajectory to formulate the control input to drive the real system. The actual output of the system is captured by the measurement system to compare with the designed desired trajectory. The differences are defined as errors to update the parameters. The newly updated parameters together with the designed desired trajectory will formulate the new control input to drive the real system. After careful designing the update strategy, the parameters will converge to their true values when the differences between the designed trajectory and the actual measure one are infinitely small. The update strategy only allows one parameter to be changed in one update cycle. The variation magnitude and direction of one parameter are determined by the errors generated on the whole trajectory. The desired trajectory will be designed from low frequency to high frequency to excite different parameters. Compared with the conventional bench-marking parameter identification methods, the new identification mechanism do not transform the identification to be an optimization problem. With the carefully designed update strategy and the designed trajectory, the influence of random noise and disturbance can be distinguished from the deterministic behavior of the system. The local minimum phenomenon and the coupling effects between parameters can also be avoided. The simulations conducted on a linear spring-mass-damper system, and nonlinear three degree freedom robotic arm system are verified the new identifier. The experiments conducted on a screw-driven table and a quarter car platform are also verify the efficiency, robust and accuracy of the new identifier.

16205115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205115.value: Instead of defining the identification problem as an optimization problem, this research discloses a new way to transfer the identification problem into a control problem to avoid the local minimum and coupling effects in optimization. A closed-loop system, named identifier, is established to do identification. The identifier is attached to the original system to collect the data from the sensors and to input certain commands to drive the original system. An updated mechanism is designed, which is a step-by-step update based on state feedback and projecting input commands on error of states or their functions. Properly designed desired trajectories for different parameters are used to decouple the parameter from other parameters. A systematic way of updating one parameter at a time in different cycles ensured good convergence of parameters to true value even if absolute decoupling between parameters is not possible for complicate and nonlinear systems. The identifier needs the accurate values of the general coordinate, velocity and acceleration to conduct calculation. Thus, an accurate measurement system is designed, which consists two observers and one accurate time base. One observer collects the signal of general coordinate and provides the general velocity and acceleration. Utilized the causality, the disturbance and unknown in dynamic domain can be avoided. The integral instead of differential is applied in the observer to avoid the sensor’ noise. The other observer gets the signal of general acceleration and gives the general velocity and acceleration. The drift of integral can be inhibited significantly compared with conversional methods. Details can refer to Conference paper No.1, Journal paper No. 1 and 2, and in Dr. Waheed's PhD Thesis. Based on the accurate measurements and the identifier, the parameters of system and the actual values of states can be obtained with high accuracy. Thus, several applications have been achieved. One is the improvement of control performance based on accurate parameters. The experiments were conducted on a motor-driven linear guide and a quarter car platform. Further, the accurate parameters can help robotic arm to better avoid singularity problem in kinematic domain. Details can refer to Conference paper No. 2, Journal paper No.3 and Dr Waheed's PhD Thesis, mainly in chapter 4 and 6. The table of contents of Dr Waheed's thesis is attached with this report.

16205115.value: The outcomes of this researches can further be extended to other applications and tasks. Some of future works are listed which is required to be carried out to further enhance the influence of this research. (1) The accurate parameters are important to improve the control performance in industrial applications, e.g. the robotic arms, automated car, drone, automated vehicle, auto-aligned system, etc. The parameter uncertainty can be decreased to certain level to guarantee the better performance. (2) The accurate parameters can help to diagnose the faults in system. The developed method needs to be packaged at a plug and play device to work with the system simultaneously and to report the abnormal parameters on-line.

16205115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205115.value: Parameter identification is an important field. It plays a vital role in system modeling, device calibration, fault diagnosis, and improving performance of control systems. The difficulties to identify parameter lie in that the number of independent equations is smaller than the numbers of unknown parameters. Existing approaches use excitation method to generate more relation and convert system to an over-determined system. By which problem is converted to an optimization problem. Then the local minimum, coupling effects between parameters, influence of noise and disturbance will deviate the results of identification. The new identifier adopts control theory to parameter identification. Instead of minimizing state variable, the errors of parameters are minimizing in the new identifier. Furthermore, using separately designed periodic trajectory with different frequency play a vital role in avoiding coupling issues. Additionally, projecting inputs on errors of states or state functions help in isolating different signals like state variables, noise, input etc. Thus, the signal to noise ratio (SNR) is increased. By using feedback to decide direction of update ensured that the parameter always converges to its true value and not falling into local minimal.

16205515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205515.value: In recent decades, owing to urbanization and limited space in densely-populated metropolises, high-rise buildings have frequently been built extremely close to each other. Such close proximity has occasionally led to linked building systems (LBSs), i.e., systems comprising buildings connected via links, e.g. skybridges and skygardens, to provide an additional passage and an evacuation route in the event of an emergency. LBSs are usually built tall to achieve a grand appearance. As a result, wind-resistant design of LBSs is a primary concern, particularly in typhoon-prone cities. From a structural point of view, the links in an LBS induce a structural coupling between the two oscillating buildings and alter the structural dynamic properties, such as vibration mode shapes and frequencies. In addition, the links provide a physical path for the transferring of forces between the buildings, promoting spatiotemporal correlation of wind forces on the buildings. This is known as aerodynamic coupling and is particularly important in the design of wind-excited LBSs. Structural and aerodynamic coupling are indeed interrelated and must be considered simultaneously when evaluating the building’s aerodynamic response. In particular, aerodynamic coupling in terms of inter-building wind loading correlations, in the presence of structural coupling, is needed for accurately predicting the building’s response. Until now, however, the two coupling have mostly been dealt with separately. Structural engineering research groups have developed one-dimensional analytical models to represent the dynamic behavior of an LBS subjected to seismic excitation, while wind engineering groups have studied the aerodynamic interference of proximate buildings without taking structural coupling into account. The primary goal of the proposed research will be to investigate both structural and aerodynamic coupling due to structural links and their combined effects on the aerodynamic performance of wind-excited LBSs. This is to be achieved by advancing an analytical model, which was developed by the PI, together with a series of wind tunnel pressure tests to measure the spatiotemporal correlation of wind forces on an LBS. The interrelationship between structural and aerodynamic coupling and the aerodynamic performance of an LBS can be investigated extensively by combining wind load correlation with structural dynamic properties obtained from the advanced analytical model for various building configurations. The benefits of the research will be to advance understanding of the dynamic behavior of wind-excited LBSs and subsequently to improve their aerodynamic performance. 近幾十年來，由於城市化和可用的城市土地空間有限，高層建築間的距離會比較小。 這樣近的距離偶爾造就了連體建築的出現。 所謂連體建築，就是指多個建築物由結構連體如空中橋樑、空中花園等連接起來形成的一個建築系統。 這個結構連體可以提供額外的行人通道或是緊急情況下的疏散路線。 連體建築一般都比較高以達到宏偉的外觀。 因此，連體建築的抗風設計是其設計的一個關鍵程序，尤其是在易受到颱風影響的城市。 從結構上來說，連體建築中的結構連體會造成兩個連接塔樓振動之間的結構耦合，從而改變結構的動態特性，如振動頻率和模態。此外，結構連體可以傳遞連接塔樓之間的內力，所以建築上風荷載的時空相關性更為複雜。 這個相關性也就是氣動耦合，其在連體結構的抗風設計中也尤為重要。 實際上，結構耦合與氣動耦合相互關聯。 所以在評估連體建築的氣動回應時，這兩個耦合必須同時考慮。 尤其是，在有結構耦合的存在下，氣動耦合中的建築間風荷載的相關性對於準確預測系統的回應至關重要。 然而到目前為止，這兩種耦合在大多數情況下都是分開研究的。 結構工程研究組提出了一維的分析模型來研究連體建築在地震作用下的動態行為；風工程研究組則廣泛研究了鄰近建築的氣動干擾，但沒有考慮結構耦合。 本研究主要探索由於結構上的聯繫所產生的結構耦合和氣動耦合，以及這兩者如何影響風致連體建築的氣動性能。 為完成該課題，本研究擬改進一個連體建築的分析模型，並通過一系列風洞測試來測量連體建築風荷載的時空相關性。 繼而通過考慮不同組合的風荷載相關性和結構特性，來全面分析連體建築結構耦合和氣動耦合之間的相互關係。 本研究可進一步瞭解風致連體建築的動態行為，並改善它的氣動特性。

16205515.label: Realisation of objectives
16205515.value: An analytical model applicable for a general linked-building system (LBS) that has an asymmetric structural system (e.g. irregular building forms) and multiple links has firstly been derived to investigate the intra- and inter-building structural coupling among the building towers. The irregularity of building forms and structural systems was considered as eccentricities between the mass center and the stiffness center of each building in the LBS. Expressions for the modal properties of four representative configurations of the eccentricities were derived by solving the associated characteristic equation. The analytical model developed can be used to understand the dynamic behavior of any LBS of its kind. A sequence of wind tunnel tests was subsequently performed to capture the building surface fluctuating loads for the study of aerodynamic coupling. Pressure experiments were carried out in the boundary layer wind tunnel at the CLP Power Wind/Wave Tunnel Facility at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology using a synchronous multi-pressure measurement system (SMPMS) to obtain the wind force information. Models of LBS with a range of gap distances were considered to study the aerodynamic coupling for urban wind condition and full azimuth wind directions. Spatiotemporal wind pressure data was used to investigate the intra- and inter-building aerodynamic correlations of LBSs. Intra-building aerodynamic correlation of the LBSs was examined using correlation coefficients and trajectories. In addition, proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) technique was applied on the spatiotemporal wind pressure data to investigate the systematic structure of the aerodynamic coupling hidden in the fluctuating pressure field. The results were used to uncover the aerodynamic coupling mechanism by mapping the correlation of wind forces between the buildings for each test case. As a result, the critical building configurations with the highest wind load correlations were identified. The flow patterns of the critical building configurations that cause the highest wind load correlations were then further investigated using particle image velocimetry (PIV) at Tokyo Polytechnic University. Aerodynamic and excitation mechanisms, including channeling effects, vortex shedding and asymmetric fluctuations, were successfully identified for each tested building configuration at different modes. Employing the results from the analytical model and wind force data measured from wind tunnel tests, the wind-induced responses of a series of LBSs with different intra- and inter-building structural couplings were calculated to examine the effects of the eccentricity on performance of wind-excited LBSs. The combined effects of structural and aerodynamic coupling were also investigated by analyzing the correlation of wind forces on each building in the presence of structural coupling. Structural optimization was subsequently performed to identify the optimal design of LBSs subjected to various wind excitations.

16205515.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205515.value: An analytical model has been developed to investigate the intra- and inter-building structural coupling for buildings with irregular building forms and structural systems. The irregularity of building forms and structural systems was considered as eccentricities between the mass center and the stiffness center of each building in the LBS. The effects of the eccentricity on the performance of wind-excited LBSs were systematically investigated. The results show that the intra-building structural coupling can cause significantly coupled modes. There are a few favorable configurations of the intra-building structural coupling that can enhance the performance of wind-excited LBS. The results can provide guidance to researchers and engineers on designing a favorable configuration concerning the intra-structural coupling of linked buildings at the initial design stage. The research findings have been published in Journal of Wind Engineering and Industrial Aerodynamics, Engineering Structures, and ASCE, Journal of Structural Engineering. Using a synchronous multi-pressure measurement system, spatiotemporal wind pressure data imposing on the surface of LBSs with a range of gap distance were measured via a series of wind tunnel pressure experiments. The pressure data was used to investigate the intra- and inter-building aerodynamic correlations of LBSs. Results showed that intra-building aerodynamic correlations differ considerably, especially between along-wind and torsional force components. However, although intra-building aerodynamic correlation is significant, its effect on the wind-induced responses of LBs was found to be relatively small. The along-wind inter-building correlation coefficient was found to decrease for 0° wind direction and increase for 90° with increasing gap distance, whereas variation of cross-wind inter-building correlation is complicated. Proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) and particle image velocimetry (PIV) techniques were sequentially applied to reveal the aerodynamic coupling as well as excitation mechanisms. At small building gap, outside shear layers were observed in the evaluation of instantaneous wind flows using PIV for 0° wind direction. At larger gaps, inner shear layers were observed between the two buildings, and their interactions created complex flow patterns. As revealed using the POD analysis technique, channeling effect decreased with the increasing gap, and vortex shedding interactions became more rigorous. The research findings have been published in Journal of Wind Engineering and Industrial Aerodynamics, Engineering Structures, and Building and Environment.

16205515.value: Driven by high land costs, dense population, eagerness of developers to own a landmark tall building, there is a growing trend to design tall buildings in close proximity to each other as a linked building system (LBS), i.e. a system consisting of several buildings horizontally connected by links such as skybridges and skygardens, to provide an additional passage and an evacuation route in the event of a fire or emergency. These LBSs are usually tall therefore wind-resistant design of LBSs is one of the primary concerns, particularly in typhoon-prone cities. The major outcomes of the research project include the successful development a simple mathematical model of LBSs and the identifications of their aerodynamic characteristics and excitation mechanisms. The simple model is particularly useful to understand the coupling mechanism of wind-excited LBSs and subsequently to improve its aerodynamic performance along with the knowledge of excitation mechanisms. The results generated from the project can provide guidance to structural engineers on designing a favorable configuration concerning the effects of structural links on building towers at the initial design stage. A few favorable building configurations that can enhance the performance of wind-excited LBS were identified.

16205715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205715.value: Expanding highway infrastructures might be a common remedy to traffic congestion. However, it is recognized that widened roads spur additional travel and divert users from public transport modes, quickly returning the roads to the original congestion level or even worse. In this sense, highway expansion may increase the travel costs of both auto commuters and public transport users. This phenomenon is referred to as the “Downs-Thomson paradox”; stating that expanding a road system as a remedy to congestion is sometimes counterproductive. One more well-known result in transportation economics is the so called “Mohring effect”, which states that if the service quality of public transport changes with demand, then a rise in demand triggers more frequent service, which shortens passenger’s waiting time at stops and may attract even more passengers. This effect implies increasing returns to scale for scheduled urban transport services and is often referenced in support of transit subsidies under marginal cost pricing. The two noteworthy phenomena have been examined extensively in the literature. Nonetheless, the Mohring effect is often argued in a single, isolated transit system, and most stand-alone analyses do not address the question of where the users go or come from, in response to transit service change. The Downs-Thomson paradox, on the other hand, elucidates on the demand shift between the two modes but often assuming perfect substitutability and separate rights of way. Yet, the two phenomena are evidently interrelated in the context of an integrated bimodal system but their linkage is not always transparent. To seek better joint highway investment and public transit operating strategies, this project proposes to investigate the occurrence of the “Mohring effect” and “Downs-Thomson paradox” and their relation in an integrated bimodal context. The first part of the project will build up the basic model where commuters choose between two imperfect substituted travel modes: automobile and public transit with dedicated right-of-way, under alternative transit operating regimes. The second part will examine how commuters’ heterogeneity in value of time affects transit operator’s responses towards highway expansion. The third part will investigate the Mohring effect and the Downs-Thomson paradox when two substitutive travel modes share the same roadway with direct and cross congestion internalities. The proposed research problem is of great theoretical and practical importance. Apart from enhancing our understanding of intermodal interactions in transportation, the project will provide guidance for the policy makers on integrated transportation services planning and regulation. 關鍵詞: 道路擴建，公共交通，模式間交互，福利效應，交通政策 摘要 擴建道路設施、增加交通供給是治理城市交通擁堵的最常見的手段。然而，近幾十年的實踐證明，由於受城市現有佈局、建設用地、交通出行等諸多因素的限制和影響，道路擴建往往使城市交通陷入“交通擁擠—擴建道路—私人交通增多—公交需求減少—道路更加擁擠”的惡性循環，從而使得個人出行成本不降反升。這個現像被稱為“Downs-Thompson悖論”。 “Mohring效應”是交通經濟學中另一個著名的現象。具體說來，如果公共交通（如地鐵、輕軌、公交巴士等）的服務質量隨著其需求的變化而變化，那麼交通需求的上升會促使線路班次的增加，所有乘客可能都會因候車時間縮短而受益，從而公共交通可以吸引更多的乘客。 “Mohring效應”反映了城市公共交通服務的規模經濟效應。根據“Mohring效應”，當同時考慮運營者和使用者兩方面的成本時，公共交通服務的優化需要政府的補貼來維持。 現有文獻對以上兩個經濟學現象分別進行過廣泛地探討。但是，對“Mohring效應”的研究大多將公共交通系統看作是一個孤立系統，而忽略在公共交通的服務發生變化時，增加的需求從何而來，或者減少的需求到哪裡去等問題。而對“Downs-Thompson悖論”的研究雖然關注不同出行模式(私人小汽車和公共交通)之間的需求轉化，但常常將兩種出行模式看作是完全可替代的，並且假設公共交通有專用道，不會和私人小汽車相互影響。然而在多種出行模式並存的交通系統中，“Downs-Thompson悖論” 和“Mohring效應”之間顯然有著密切的聯繫，有待學者們的探究。 為了更好地統籌規劃和設計城市道路設施和公共交通服務，本研究課題旨在探求“Downs-Thompson悖論” 和“Mohring效應”的產生機制，以及它們在雙出行模式的交通系統中的關係。本課題的第一部分將建立該問題的基本模型。其中，私人小汽車和公共交通這兩種出行模式是不能完全相互替代的。在此基礎上，我們將會在多種公共交通運作管理模式（利潤最大化、維持收支平衡等）下對以上問題進行探討。課題的第二部分將會考慮出行者對“時間”的不同感知程度，以及在道路擴建時公共交通運營者將會如何調整服務的頻次和票價。課題的第三部分將會在私人小汽車和公交車混行的情況下研究“Downs-Thompson悖論” 和“Mohring效應”。在這種情況下，公交服務的改變將會直接影響道路的擁擠程度。 本課題在多模式複雜交通系統的理論和實踐上都具有重大意義。課題的完成將增進對多種出行模式並存的複雜交通系統的理解，從而為城市交通系統的統籌規劃、政策制定提供理論依據。

16205715.label: Realisation of objectives
16205715.value: Throughout the three years of the research period, we were able to investigate all the study issues raised originally in the proposal. All aspects of the Downs-Thompson paradox and the Mohring effects in a bi-modal transportation system in the original proposal were addressed. Traffic congestion is considered one of the most challenging problems in big cities, which recurrently affects commuters’ travel mobility. It is a source of enormous economic costs to both individual travelers and society at large. Many local authorities are aware of this issue and keep thinking of new policies to solve or mitigate the problem. The direct and standard remedy to traffic congestion is building more roads or expanding the existing ones. However, new infrastructure is becoming increasingly expensive and infeasible to construct, especially in densely populated cities with limited land areas such as Hong Kong. Besides of its high construction cost, the arguments towards the effectiveness of highway expansion are also explosive. Experience shows that capacity expansion might fail: more new roads/lanes are built, more severe traffic congestion is observed on the roads. The enlarged road capacity on one hand evokes latent travel demands, and on the other hand it attracts traffic shifts from public transport. Transportation researchers have recognized that highway expansion could reallocate traffic in the transportation system and lead to a new traffic equilibrium where the highway is more congested and the transit service also becomes worse. This phenomenon is called the “Downs-Thomson paradox”, named after Anthony Downs and J. Michael Thomson; it highlights the importance of considering the cross-modal impacts of highway expansion and remains a key issue for effective and sustainable trans-modal integrated transport planning. Apart from commuters’ modal shifts, public transport operations and policy also play important roles in determining the effectiveness of highway expansion. This is particularly true for densely populated metropolises, where scheduled public transport service carries a large proportion of daily commute trips. The “Mohring effect”, named for the well-known economist Herbert Mohring, indicates that more (fewer) passengers lead to more (less) frequent service, which leads to even more (fewer) passengers. This well-known property implies increasing returns to scale for scheduled urban transport services and it is often used as a valid argument for transit subsidies in order to achieve marginal cost pricing for maximizing social welfare. There have been two separate streams of research on the two influential results of the Mohring effect and the Downs-Thomson paradox; their linkage has been, however, largely overlooked in the existing literature. Also, highway planning and transit design problems have often been tackled separately in most previous studies; only very limited efforts have been devoted to the joint investigation of them. The system-wide impact of highway expansion with bimodal interaction is still unclear, especially when the transit service is under different ownership and operation policies (such as self-financing, profit or social welfare maximization with respect to either fare or frequency or both). Moreover, the occurrence of the Mohring effect and the Downs-Thomson paradox and their relation becomes more intriguing but relevant when the two travel modes in an integrated transportation system are imperfectly substitutable, or serve for heterogeneous commuters with idiosyncratic preferences and different value of time, or have congestion interaction when sharing the same roadway. This project examined thoroughly the above issues in the presence of both internal (cross-mode) and external (system-wide) demand elasticity for developing viable highway investment and transit operating strategies. In particular, in-depth analyses were made on the interaction between highway expansion and transit policy, and the relation between the Mohring effect and Downs-Thomson paradox in the integrated bimodal transportation system under more general problem settings of user preferences and modal interactions. The research finding offered interesting insights into the sustainable policy and planning of the integrated transportation system, particularly in the context of the well-known Mohring effect and the Downs-Thomson paradox in transportation economics.

16205715.label: Major findings and research outcome
16205715.value: 1. The bimodal equilibrium problem with imperfect substitutability was formulated. The conditions for the existence of the Mohring effect and Downs-Thomson paradox were established respectively and their relationships in the bimodal context were made clear. It was found that in all regimes the full price of transit declines only if the full price of driving falls as well. The D-T paradox cannot occur in the profit maximization or unconstrained welfare maximization regimes. In the traditional self-financing regime transit service deteriorates, but the D-T paradox is not inevitable. Publications: Zhang, F., Lindsey, R., Yang, H., 2016. A model of public transit service was developed under monopoly when potential users differ in their willingness to pay and value of time. The prevalence of the Mohring Effect and the need for subsidization are investigated. Four types of regulatory policies are considered: fare regulation, frequency regulation, goal or objective function regulation, and fiscal regulation. Furthermore, congestion effect and crowding externalities were incorporated in the model and a unique user equilibrium was found to exist. A cost-recovery formula was also derived. 16205715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16205715.value: Through the course of investigation of the project, we discovered an innovative strategy for managing peak hour transit demand. The strategy is Pareto-improving and revenue-neutral, namely, it can make commuters better while keeping the operator’s revenue intact. This discovery resulted in a new GRF project currently under investigation and one publication: Yang, H., Tang, Y. 2018. Managing rail transit peak-hour congestion with fare-reward schemes. Transportation Research Part B: Methodological, Vol.110, 122–136. Modeling and managing morning commute with both household and individual travels. Transportation Research Part B: Methodological, Vol.103, 227-247.

16205715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16205715.value: Expanding highway might be a common remedy to traffic congestion. However, it is recognized that widened roads spur additional travel and divert users from public transport modes. Thus, highway expansion may increase the travel costs of both auto commuters and public transport users. This phenomenon is referred to as the “Downs-Thomson paradox”; stating that expanding a road system as a remedy to congestion is sometimes counterproductive. One more well-known result in transportation economics is the so called “Mohring effect”, which states that if the service quality of public transport changes with demand, then a rise in demand triggers more frequent service, which shortens passenger’s waiting time at stops and may attract even more passengers. This effect implies increasing returns to scale for scheduled urban transport services. The two phenomena were examined jointly in this project in an integrated bimodal context by taking into account two imperfect substituted travel modes of automobile and public transit under alternative transit operating regimes. Impacts of commuters’ heterogeneity in value of time and congestion internalities on the occurrence of Mohring effect and the Downs-Thomson paradox were fully investigated. The results provided useful guidance for the policy makers on integrated transportation services planning and regulation.

16205915.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16205915.value: 面向3C制造的工业机器人自动化工作站的标定

16205915.label: Project Objectives
16205915.value: Formulate the work cell calibration problem in a unified framework based on the robot calibration, workpiece localization and environmental mapping sub-problems; Develop an algorithm to solve the work cell calibration problem in a computationally efficient and geometrically meaningful manner; Select a proper 3D measurement device and optimize the sampling strategy to improve calibration performance; Implement the calibration technique with a prototype 3C assembly work cell, and evaluate its effectiveness, reliability and usability.

Implement the calibration technique with a prototype 3C assembly work cell, and evaluate its effectiveness, reliability and usability.

16205915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16205915.value: 自2013年以来，中国超越日本成为了世界第一大工业机器人消费国。从中国的制造业总量推断，该地位将在可见的未来继续保持下去。在过去十到十五年里，机器人产业的发展主要由中国爆炸性增长的汽车产业所驱动。然而，随着智能手机、平板电脑的兴起，3C产品（通讯、电脑、消费类电子）的生产制造将成为机器人技术的下一个巨大应用点。我们可以看到：（1）中国拥有超过全世界70%的电子制造产业；（2）电子制造产业的员工数量是汽车产业的4倍；（3）中国3C制造业中的机器人使用率只有汽车产业的1/10，而中国汽车产业的机器人使用率只有日美的1/10，潜力巨大；（4）因劳工价格上涨和劳动力短缺，位于中国的代工公司都大力推进机器人自动化解决方案；（5）地方政府推出一系列刺激措施，如财政补贴、税收优惠等，积极推广机器人的使用。因此，3C制造业中的机器人使用量将在未来十年内快速增长。 3C制造的自动化也面临着巨大挑战，其中的关键问题包括3C制造高达10微米的精度要求与只有4到6周的自动化方案实施周期。典型的工业机器人定位精度约1毫米，而在一个由多机器人、定位模组和辅助设备组成的工作站中，累加定位误差将会更大。通过细致的机器人点位示教，我们可以提高其精度，但这必将延长调试时间。本项目提出的机器人工作站标定，包含了机器人标定、工件定位与工作站环境建模三个子问题，可以在提高精度的同时减少系统调试时间。机器人标定将会有效提高机器人绝对定位精度，而工件定位可以取代繁琐的示教过程。机器人工作站的模型可以进一步用于路径自动规划和机器人防碰撞等。通过同时完成以上几项任务，工作站标定不仅能够提高机器人系统精度，并且可以有效节约系统搭建时间。 在本项目中，我们将研究工作站标定的问题。机器人标定、工件定位与工作站建模之前被认为是三个独立的问题，而这里我们将建立一个统一的框架对他们进行描述。我们将提出一个计算高效并具有几何意义的算法对工作站中的参数进行辨识，并处理观测噪声。在辨识过程中，我们将优化测量方法与采样策略，以提高标定的性能。我们将把所提出的标定技术应用到一个实际的3C装配样机工作站中，测试它的有效性与可靠性。此项目的成果将会为3C制造业中机器人技术的大规模应用铺平道路。

16205915.label: Realisation of objectives
16205915.value: Workpiece assembly is a very common process in assembly and manufacturing industry. In order to improve efficiency, workers will establish a form of work cell to use robots to complete the assembly process. But because of the complexity of robot calibration and work cell calibration, there will be some changes according to the different workpieces. So it is very necessary to formulate the work cell calibration problem in a unified framework based on the robot calibration, workpiece localization and environmental mapping sub-problems; and for this problem, we have to develop an algorithm to solve the work cell calibration problem in a computationally efficient and geometrically meaningful manner;To solve this problem, we summarized the processes that appeared in many factories. For each process, we established corresponding work cell. Firstly, we try to build a general calibration model , which can be applied to many different industrial assembly processes. We summarize several existing processes, including screw-twisting, grinding, dispensing, pick&place, etc. And finally, we build a universal work cell, which can complete any of the above processes, including a 6-axis manipulator, camera, conveyor belt, feeder, etc. For this model, we design as many kinds of models as possible, and test the accuracy of each model, and soften a variety of models, and finally build a very precise work cell model. Secondly, aiming at the model we built, we comprehensively analyzed various calibration problems, including the robot calibration, Workpiece Localization and environmental mapping sub-problems. Thirdly, based on the traditional calibration algorithm, we synthetically analyze and test the effectiveness of each calibration algorithm. For each calibration sub-problem, we adopt the advantages of the corresponding calibration algorithm to deal with it. In this way, we can build a more accurate calibration algorithm for our work cell. Finally, in order to test the accuracy of our calibration algorithm, we use many other calibration algorithms, such as laser calibration and wire-drawing encoder calibration, to test the accuracy of our new calibration algorithm. The experiments show that our new calibration algorithm is indeed an efficient and simple calibration algorithm which can be applied to work cell.

16206015.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16206015.value: 基于AWGR的可扩展数据中心网络

16206015.label: Project Objectives
16206015.value: Identify new scalable AWGR-based optical switch architectures for datacenter networks. The new architecture should expand the port count from N to N^2 and achieve this without using expensive wavelength converters. Since each port can carry up to N wavelengths, the total capacity of the interconnect will be around O(N^3). Explore new crosstalk-constrained scheduling algorithms to further enhance the scalability of AWGR-based switches. NxN AWGRs are the basic building blocks of the proposed switch architecture. The value of N is limited by the worst-case co-channel crosstalk created when N signals of the same wavelength passing through the device simultaneously. But for packet switching, how many same-wavelength signals traverse an AWGR can be controlled by the packet scheduling algorithm of the switch. The objective of this study is to use crosstalk constraint based scheduling to further enhance the scalability of the switching network.

16206015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206015.value: Energy-per-bit efficiency has quickly become the ultimate capacity limiting factor for datacenter networks. People are turning to optics for solutions. If a datacenter network can be implemented with optics, many E/O (electrical to optical) and O/E conversions can be removed and tremendous power saving can be achieved. AWGRs (arrayed waveguide grating router) provide the most promising solution in this regard. But AWGRs have one fundamental limitation: poor scalability. While the realistic port count of an AWGR is likely to be less than fifty, an optical switch for a datacenter network may need to interconnect one thousand racks or more. In this project we intend to address this scalability issue with architectural solutions. We will explore and identify new scalable AWGR-based optical interconnect architectures that can increase the total capacity and the energy-per-bit efficiency of a switch fabric by two orders of magnitude. Furthermore, we intend to achieve this goal without using expensive wavelength converters. The results of this research can have a big impact on how we design routers and datacenter networks in the future. 每比特消耗的能量已经迅速成为数据中心网络的承载能力 的限制因素。如果一个数据中心网络可以用光学实现，许多 E／O（电光)和O / E的转换可以避免，如此可实现巨大的节能。 AWGR(阵列波导光栅路由器）可提供这方面最有前途的解决 方案。但AWGR有一个基本的限制：扩展性差。市面上的AWGR 的端口数量通常低于五十，但一个数据中心网络可能需要互连上 千或更多个端口。在本计划中，我们研究如何解决AWGR扩展性 的各种问题， 并提出不同的解决方案。

More details are given in Sec. 6.1 below.

16206015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206015.value: Both objectives have been achieved. In paper 1 of Part C, we identified an AWGR packet switching architecture that can be scalable to N^2 ports and each port can transmit N wavelengths to different destination ports simultaneously. If we set N = 33 (commercially available) and each wavelength carries 40Gbps, the total bandwidth of the switch is close to 10^15 bps, an unprecedented bandwidth. In paper 3 (Part C), we show how to use constraint based routing to reduce crosstalk and increase the scalability of a signle AWG. Past studies on this issue ignore one important physical characteristic of AWG: channel adjacency has an important impact on the crosstalk level. By exploiting this characteristic, we show that constraint based routing can achieve a much big impact on crosstalk reduction in AWG. Papers 2 and 5 in Part C discuss how to improve the design of an optical space switch, which is a key component of our proposed ASA architecture. Paper 4 deals with performance measurement in SDNs.

16206315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206315.value: Sequences or codes are strings of numbers that have been very carefully designed and possess special properties, almost magical. They are diamonds in disguise that lie at the heart of virtually any digital system commonly used in our daily lives. Examples of such practical systems include the synchronization of everpresent GPS receivers, the separation of users in cellular phone networks, radars, cryptography for secure transactions, and even the watermarking of digital images or videos. Each particular application requires a careful and delicate design of sequences or codes that enjoy some desirable properties. For instance, synchronization sequences need to have very low autocorrelation sidelobes, while cellular codes additionally require small cross-correlations, and radar codes need to pay careful attention to the Doppler effect. Indeed, the topic of sequence design is a fundamental one and has been an active research area since the 1950s. Nevertheless, the traditional approach has mainly been an algebraic one based on a strong mathematical analysis and characterization of properties of sequences with specific length and typically binary elements. This approach has been successful and after the work of many renowned researchers there is a large library of sequences with good properties (e.g., Golomb codes, Hadamard codes, and Barker codes). However, such an algebraic approach only works for specific cases of desired properties and under specific choices of lengths and binary alphabets. In advanced and modern applications, there is a need to consider many new types of constraints (e.g., Doppler constraints and spectral mask constraints) for which the algebraic approach may not necessarily be the best road. An alternative methodology is based on optimization techniques that can provide the desired performance very efficiently. This proposal aims at developing convex optimization methods for the design of advanced sequences in a very systematic way that is theoretically sounded and that produces practical solutions that work well in real systems. Rather than considering heuristic numerical methods, we propose the employment of highly effective successive convex optimization methods that can deal with a variety of constraints, different sequence alphabets, and a plethora of merit functions. Preliminary results are extremely satisfactory and promising. 序列或编码是经过精心设计并具有特殊性质的数字串。它们如钻石一般，处在几乎所有数字系统的核心部分，比如GPS接收机的同步，蜂窝电话网络的用户分离，雷达，安全交易密码系统，以及数字图像或视频的水印。每一个特定的应用程序需要一个精心设计的序列或编码，同时必须具备一些特性。例如，同步序列必须具有很低的自相关旁瓣，而蜂窝码额外需要低互相关旁瓣，雷达编码需要注意Doppler效应。 事实上，序列设计是一个基础的研究课题，并且自从20世纪90年代以来就一直是一个活跃的研究领域。然而，传统设计方法主要是一种基于对序列特性的数学分析和特征提取的代数方法，其中序列需要具有特定长度并且是典型的二进制。这种方法获得了巨大的成功，并且在许多著名学者的努力下，现在已有许多具有良好特性的序列（例如：Golomb编码, Hadamard编码和Barker编码）。但是，特征提取的代数方法要求序列具有特定长度，且为二进制。在一些高级和现代的应用中，有必要去考虑一些新的约束条件类型（例如：Doppler 约束条件和频谱遮罩约束条件），而在这些情形下，代数的方法便不再是一种好的解决方法。而另外一种基于优化技术的方法，则可以十分有效地产生所需特性的序列。 这项提案旨在系统地发展基于凸优化的高级序列设计方法。该方法具有理论指导意义，同时可提供应用于实际系统的解决方案。不同于启发式的数值方法，我们提出一系列基于连续凸优化的高效方法，不仅可以处理各种约束条件和序列字母表，而且兼容不同的评价函数。初步试验结果令人满意，应用前景十分广阔。

16206315.label: Realisation of objectives
16206315.value: The main goal of this project was the development of optimization methods to design sequences that satisfy some constraints on correlation, power, magnitude, peak-to-average ratio, etc., including the theoretical analysis on convergence and the design of practical numerical algorithms. All the objectives have been more than satisfactorily completed (in fact five extra objectives have been accomplished) and the output consists of one book, 14 IEEE top journal papers (including a long overview paper on the mathematical framework majorization-minimization based algorithms), 10 conference papers, and an open-source software package (currently with 3,000 downloads). Objective 1 consisted on designing sequences with controlled autocorrelation needed for modern advanced communication systems via the minimization of the weighted integrated sidelobe levels and, even more interesting, the peak sidelobe levels. The methods are based on optimization techniques and provide the best results in the literature at a very low computational cost. Not only we fulfilled the original objective but we also considered a more general formulation with a wide variety of constraints (including the interesting and difficult peak sidelobe level) and metrics (like the peak-to-average ratio or unit-modulus case). Objective 2 considered the extension of Objective 1 to the case of multiple sequences with cross-correlation properties, necessary in many active sensing and communication systems, e.g., multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) radar systems and code- division multiple-access (CDMA) cellular systems. This objective obtained the best results in the literature with low computational methods. Objective 3 dealt with the extension to the design of ambiguity functions that play an important role in radar systems. We managed to solve the design of a radar sequence subject to the common peak-to-average power ratio (PAR) constraint in radar systems. Objective 4 solved the joint design of transmitted sequences and received filters for radar and communication systems subject to the PAR constraint. Extra objective 5: in the context of multi-antenna wireless communication systems, we considered the design of multiple sequences (one for each transmit antenna) to properly estimate the channel matrix of modern multi-antenna wireless systems subject to PAR or unimodular constraints. The problems turned out to be nonconvex but we developed efficient algorithms based on the majorization-minimization (MM) framework with guaranteed convergence. Extra objective 6: in phase retrieval problems, measurements consist of only the magnitude of several linear measurements of the unknown sequence and the phase has to be recovered. We formulated the recovery of the phase of the sequence as a nonconvex optimization problem and derived low-complexity algorithms with superior performance based on the MM framework. Extra objective 7: we applied the MM optimization framework in the context of a wide variety of applications in communications and signal processing, and achieved the ambitious goal of writing a detailed tutorial of MM in the high-impact journal IEEE Signal Processing Magazine (currently with 150+ citations). Extra objective 8: in the context of signal processing and machine learning, principal component analysis (PCA) and feature selection are key concepts and we combined them into a sparse eigenvector estimation problem, formulated as a nonconvex problem but deriving fast and efficient algorithms. In fact, the obtained algorithms are so practical that we developed an open-source software package under the programming language R (commonly used in statistics and machine learning) which can be found in the official CRAN repository (currently with 3,000 downloads): https://cran.r-project.org/package=sparseEigen. Extra objective 9: in the context of financial portfolio design, it turns out that optimizing the portfolios weights can be seen as designing a sequence which can be formulated as either a convex problem or nonconvex problem. This culminated in writing a monograph on financial engineering problems from a signal processing perspective. On top of that, in the past conferences ICASSP-2016 and ICASSP-2017 (ICASSP if the flagship conference in signal processing) we gave 3-hour tutorials to the whole signal processing community. We are also scheduled to give another 3-hour tutorial in the conference EUSIPCO 2019 (which is the European flagship conference in signal processing).

16206315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206315.value: The major findings of this project were the development of theory and practical algorithms for the design of sequences that satisfy some constraints on autocorrelation, cross-correlation, power, magnitude, peak-to-average ratio, etc. The publication output consists of one book, 14 IEEE top journal papers, and 10 conference papers. Notably, a long tutorial paper was prepared on the optimization framework of majorization-minimization (MM) with applications in communications, signal processing, and machine learning, published in a high-impact factor journal (currently with 150+ citations). Furthermore, a monograph (with 242 pages) was written on the design of portfolio weights in financial engineering from a signal processing perspective. Finally, we developed an open-source software package under the programming language R (commonly used in statistics and machine learning) which can be found in the official CRAN repository (currently with 3,000 downloads): https://cran.r-project.org/package=sparseEigen.

16206315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206315.value: During this project we obtained many results, more than expected. Nevertheless, this only opened the door to many other future problems. Three main directions are foreseen for the future of our research group: i) the detailed exploration of the MM optimization framework is very promising and will be employed for the development of efficient and fast numerical algorithms of a variety of nonconvex problems; ii) the formulation and resolution of complicated portfolio optimization problems is just the beginning for a long-road of exploration in the research group; and iii) the pursue of developing open-source software packages based on our published papers has already started a strong fruitful trend in our research group (currently a total of five software packages have been developed: https://www.danielppalomar.com/software.html).

16206315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206315.value: Convex optimization has significantly advanced in the past three decades as a tool to numerically solve many practical problems in science and engineering. However, most of the real-life problems one typically encounters are nonconvex. So there is a clear divide between the developed theory/tools and the requirements in practice. This project has pushed forward the development and application of a general framework to obtain numerical methods for hard nonconvex problems, the so-called majorization-minimization (MM) method. It has been applied to many sequence design problems in communications, radar, optical imaging, as well as machine learning methods and even portfolio design in finance. Not only papers have been written but also practical software has been produced in the open-source community with a very good acceptance in terms of downloads.

16206415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206415.value: Close linkages between equity derivatives markets and credit derivatives markets have been realized by more and more researchers and practitioners especially after the financial crisis of 2007-2009, during which default events affected both markets profoundly. Consequently, the problem of valuing both equity and credit derivatives associated with a given firm under hybrid equity-credit models has attracted much attention from both industry and academia throughout the world, including Hong Kong - one of the leading international financial centers. However, analytical pricing of equity and credit derivatives under hybrid models, in particular path-dependent ones such as EDS, defaultable barrier and lookback options, is very challenging primarily because the distributions of default times or joint distributions of default times and first passage times may have no analytical solutions. Indeed, most of studies are focused on corporate bonds, CDS and European options, and only a few papers deal with analytical pricing or analytical approximations of path-dependent derivatives such as EDS but only under certain special models. In this project, we propose a unified analytical approximation approach to pricing both path-dependent equity and credit derivatives, including defaultable corporate bonds, CDS, EDS, single- or double-barrier and lookback options, under general one- or two-dimensional jump to default Markov models, which nest not only many celebrated hybrid models such as the jump to default extended Black-Scholes-Merton and CEV models but also jump to default versions of many popular option pricing models, including exponential Levy models, regime switching models, and stochastic volatility models. Specifically, we shall first transform all pricing problems into computations of three building blocks and then take three steps to complete the project. (1) In the one-dimensional case, we intend to apply an "indirect" change of measure to further simplify computations of the three building blocks by removing an intractable factor related to default intensity. (2) We will attempt to derive closed-form expressions for these simplified building blocks under continuous time Markov chains (CTMCs). Then these closed-form building blocks under a CTMC sufficiently close to the original model can serve as analytical approximations to those under the original model, therefore leading to analytical approximation pricing formulas for all derivatives. (3) We plan to extend this approach to two-dimensional Markov models and develop accurate and efficient pricing algorithms for all derivatives under general jump to default Markov models by constructing a CTMC sufficiently close to the underlying model and improving the efficiency of the matrix computations involved. 越来越多的研究人员和从业人员意识到股票衍生品市场和信用衍生品市场之间的紧密联系，尤其是在2007-2009的金融危机之后，在这次金融危机中违约事件对这两个市场都产生了深刻的影响。因此，股票-信用混合模型下一个公司的股票衍生品和信用衍生品的定价问题在全世界范围内，也包括香港--主要的国际金融中心之一，得到了工业界和学术界的共同关注。 然而，混合模型下股票衍生品和信用衍生品的解析定价问题，尤其是路径依赖的股票衍生品和信用衍生品，比如EDS，可违约的障碍期权和可违约的回望期权，它们的解析定价问题非常困难。这主要是因为违约时间的分布以及违约时间和首中时的联合分布可能没有解析的结果。其实，大部分的研究集中在公司债券，CDS和欧式期权上，只有少量的文章研究路径依赖的衍生品的解析定价或解析近似的定价方法，比如EDS，但它们也只是考虑一些特殊的模型。 在这个项目里，我们希望在一般的一维或二维跳违约马氏模型下对路径依赖的股票衍生品和信用衍生品的定价问题，包括可违约公司债券，CDS， EDS，可违约的单边或双边障碍期权和可违约的回望期权，给出一个统一的解析近似的方法。我们考虑的模型不仅包含许多著名的混合模型，比如跳违约Black-Scholes-Merton的扩展模型和跳违约CEV的扩展模型，还包含很多流行的期权定价模型的跳违约版本，这些流行的期权定价模型包括指数Levy模型，体制转换模型，以及随机波动率模型。 具体来说，我们将首先把所有的定价问题转化成三个组成部分的计算问题，然后分以下三步来完成这个项目。(1) 在一维情形下，我们打算采用一种间接的测度变换去掉与违约强度有关的一个难处理的因子，从而使三个组成部分的计算问题得到进一步简化。 (2) 我们将尝试在连续时间马氏链下得到这三个简化的组成部分的显式表达式。如果一个连续时间马氏链与原来我们要研究的模型足够接近，那么对应的这些显式的三个组成部分可以作为原来模型下的三个组成部分的解析近似，从而得到所有我们想研究的衍生品的解析近似的定价公式。(3) 我们计划把上述的方法推广到二维情形，并且通过对原来的模型构造一个足够接近的连续时间马氏链和提高相关矩阵计算的效率来设计一个准确而高效的定价算法对一般的跳违约马氏模型下所有我们想研究的衍生品进行定价。

16206415.label: Realisation of objectives
16206415.value: In this project, we have achieved the project objectives by developing a unified analytical approximation approach to pricing various equity derivatives and credit derivatives under a general class of jump to default Markov process models. More specifically, we have derived closed-form approximation pricing formulas for single- and double-barrier options, equity default swaps (EDSs), credit default swaps (CDSs), European options, and defaultable corporate bonds under the general jump to default extended exponential Levy models with local volatilities (JDEL-LV models), which allow for state-dependent volatilities, state-dependent default intensities and general Levy types with either finite or infinite variation and include many important hybrid equity-credit models as special cases. We first manage to transform all these pricing problems into the computation of two building blocks only in terms of the pre-default stock price process. Then we derive closed-form expressions for the two building blocks under the continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) by assuming that this CTMC well approximates the target pre-default stock price process. Finally, we construct a sequence of CTMCs weakly converging to the target pre-default stock price process and show that the two building blocks under this sequence of CTMCs converge to those corresponding to the target pre-default stock price process. Consequently, all the prices associated with this sequence of CTMCs converge to those under the target JDEL-LV model. Accurate and efficient pricing algorithms based on careful design of state spaces and transition rate matrices of a sequence of weakly converging CTMCs have also been developed. Numerical results indicate that our closed-form approximation methods are accurate and efficient under a broad range of important hybrid equity-credit models. Moreover, by applying the analytical approximations of the related joint distributions, we have also proposed a unified simulation based approach to pricing various derivatives under the popular SABR model with either an absorbing boundary or a reflecting boundary. In addition, to address the issue of model fitting to the real financial data that might be sensitive, we have developed an econometric method to conduct parameter estimation while still preserving privacy. This project has produced three journal papers. Two of them have been published in "Operations Research", a top journal in management science and operations research. The third one is under review in "Mathematics of Operations Research", a top journal in operations research and financial engineering.

16206415.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206415.value: Major findings and research outcome of this project are detailed as follows. We have derived analytical approximations to the prices of various equity derivatives and credit derivatives, including single- and double-barrier options, equity default swaps (EDSs), credit default swaps (CDSs), European options, and defaultable corporate bonds, under a general class of jump to default Markov process models -- the general jump to default extended exponential Levy models with local volatilities. This is made possible mainly because we have transformed all these pricing problems into the computation of two building blocks only in terms of the pre-default stock price process and have also obtained closed-form expressions for these two building blocks under the continuous-time Markov chain that is designed to well approximate the pre-default stock price process. Accurate and efficient pricing methods have been developed to implement the analytical approximation pricing formulas. Moreover, we have also proposed a unified simulation based approach to pricing various derivatives under the SABR model with either an absorbing boundary or a reflecting boundary. In addition, we have also developed a privacy-preserving econometric method to address the parameter estimation issue related to model fitting to real financial data.

16206415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206415.value: In this project, we have derived analytical approximations to continuously monitored single- and double-barrier option prices under a general class of jump to default Markov process models. Potential future research problems might include the study of analytical approximations to discretely monitored single- and double-barrier option prices under jump to default Markov process models. This problem is expected to be more difficult. A potential approach might be to transform the pricing problems into the computation of certain building blocks in the discrete case and to develop recursive pricing algorithms to calculate these building blocks via the CTMC approximation.

16206415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206415.value: Derivatives pricing has been of fundamental importance in both equity derivatives markets and credit derivatives markets. Close linkages between these two derivatives markets have become increasingly noticeable especially during and after the financial crisis of 2007-2008 and therefore motivate the researchers to price equity derivatives and credit derivatives within a unified modeling framework. However, it is very challenging to derive analytical solutions or analytical approximations to path-dependent equity and credit derivatives prices under general jump to default Markov process models. In this project, we have developed a unified closed-form approximation approach to pricing single- and double-barrier options, equity default swaps (EDSs), credit default swaps (CDSs), European options, and defaultable corporate bonds under a general class of jump to default Markov process models. Theoretically, to the best of our knowledge, our project provides one of the first approaches to deriving analytical approximations to single- and double-barrier option prices and EDS rates under a general class of jump to default Markov process models. In practice, our unified approach allows one to price both equity derivatives and credit derivations as well as to investigate both implied volatility and credit spreads within a general unified framework.

16206615.label: Project Objectives
16206615.value: To build a preliminary dc-dc converter grid as the second stage of a two-stage power conversion system for SoCs. The optimal allocation and power distribution of the on-grid dc-dc converters for an efficient chip area usage will also be investigated. To quantify the stability of local dc-dc converter and its effects on neighboring converters on the grid. A solution will be demonstrated provided targeting at eliminating the potential instability due to interferences between multiple converters on the grid. To develop a fast load-sharing scheme that can improve the load transient responses, without sacrificing the global stability. Its effects on the system stability will also be demonstrated in parallel with objective (2). To construct an on-chip distributed power supply demo prototype, which contains the proposed dc-dc converter grid and a simplified load network grid emulating SoC activities. Simulation and prototype chip measurements will be performed for a complete evaluation of the proposed SoC power scheme.

16206615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206615.value: The ever-growing power demands of system-on-a-chip (SoC) designs for portable smart devices have brought up challenges for power management integrated circuits design. SoCs that embed many functional blocks on a single chip require each block to operate in a clean electronic environment, which means supply voltage for each block must be finely regulated regardless of its working status, whether doing extensive power-hungry computing or standing by in an ultra-low-power mode. In a conventional two-stage power scheme for an SoC, a global power bank, which is usually a high-efficiency (over 95%) switching converter, delivers power to multiple second-stage voltage regulators that are located near the loads. However, serious problems arise under this scheme, such as all regulators distributed over the SoC within the same voltage domain will experience disturbances when any block suddenly draws a large amount of current. However, the elimination of any of these disturbances, which depends on the ability of each near-load regulator, is not effective as those near-load regulators are usually not designed to work collaboratively. This proposed research aims to develop a new power distribution scheme which uses a homogeneous dc-dc converter grid or dc-dc regulator grid as the second stage in two-stage power conversion. With the introduction of homogeneous regulator grid, the new power distribution scheme can monitor and direct the dynamic power flow on the grid and enhance the load sharing within the grid. Methods will be developed for this multi-regulator environment that will reduce the complexity in design and allocation of multiple regulators, as well as improve the balanced load sharing within the regulator grid. As a result, it will realize fast transient response and reduce the disturbances on surrounding load characteristics for each regulator. In this project, based on the proposed grid structure, a systematic, fast load-sharing scheme will be developed and its effectiveness in enhancing load transient responses will be evaluated. The new distributed power supply scheme’s ability to adapt to more advanced technologies or upgrading in SoC scale will be explored as well in this project. 近年來快速增長的便攜式智能設備及其全面集成的內部片上系統(SoC)設計，無疑對片上電源管理芯片提出更多挑戰。SoC內部集合的眾多功能性模塊工作模式雖十分複雜，然而不論這些模塊是否處於高功耗的高速計算，抑或是被暫時休眠而只需維持最低電壓或功耗，均需要少擾動甚至無干擾的供電條件。傳統的針對SoC供電策略一般有兩步轉換，例如，先通過放置於SoC周邊的高效率(95%以上)開關式電源提供第一級電壓轉換，隨之鄰近各模塊分別放置線性電壓轉換器，從而為各子電壓域提供更精細的第二級電壓轉換。然而，由於該傳統供電策略中的子電壓域仍包含多個電路模塊，所以在任何一個出現快速負載變化時仍會互相影響。這一缺陷並未在傳統SoC供電策略中得以解決，主要由於鄰近負載放置的第二級轉換器從設計原理上即不能協同應對子電壓域中的快速負載變化。 本項目旨在開發一種新型的可實現快速負載均衡(快速均載)的同質電源分佈式供電技術，以解決傳統SoC供電策略中的諸多缺陷。該供電技術從設計原理上與傳統方案不同，即利用分佈式的轉換器網絡以監控和實現子電壓域內的快速均載。通過該項目，我們不僅能夠為SoC提供一種全新的更易用的供電策略，同時亦可以實現快速的瞬態反應和負載均衡，從而保障SoC的更可靠運行。我們預計該項目不僅從技術上探索該同質電源分佈式供電技術的具體實現方法，更會通過標準的電源性能評估指標來檢測該方案的有效性和可靠性。此外，我們亦會探討該項目中研發的分佈式供電技術如何適用於更精細的工藝，從而使其具有更廣泛的應用。

16206615.label: Realisation of objectives
16206615.value: This project is to develop an on-chip distributed dc-dc power converter grid that can achieve a very fast load transient response with minimum overshoot and undershoot transient voltage (Objective 4). This project has two main components. One component is how to set up an efficient distributed dc-dc power converter grid to allocate non-uniform power distribution within the SoC (Objectives 1 and 2). Another component is how to design a dc-dc converter that can achieve very a fast load transient response and can also communicate with the neighboring converters (Objective 3). Objectives 1 to 3 have to be investigated together in order to achieve the efficient power grid topology that we are targeted for. In order to have a converter with fast response and able to communicate with the neighboring converters, we proposed an analog-assisted digital low-dropout regulator (AADLDO). This kind of hybrid (mixed analog and digital control) LDO can have the advantages of analog LDO with fast transient response and digital LDO with well-defined digital control signals that can easily transmit to neighboring converters. The on-chip distributed power delivery grid was then designed based on this AADLDO architecture to complete the Objective 4. A prototype of a 3×3 power grid with 9 AADLDOs was designed and fabricated with 65-nm CMOS process. Measurement results show the effectiveness of this proposed converter grid for power delivery with the best figure-of-merit.

16206615.label: Major findings and research outcome
16206615.value: Several novel ideas and techniques have been proposed and developed in this project in order to make it success. We have spent lots of time in developing the analog-assisted digital (AAD) LDO particular for our proposed distributed power grid architecture. To have a breakthrough result, first of all, this AADLDO has completely different topology from the other previous hybrid LDO topologies. The conventional hybrid LDOs have one power MOSFET for the digital-part of the hybrid LDO and another power MOSFET for the analog-part of the hybrid LDO. We proposed to share the power MOSFET used in the analog-control part of the LDO and the power MOSFET used in the digital-control part of the LDO. The gate drive signals of the power MOSFET can be switched between digital VDD/GND and analog control voltage. This is not only can save the chip area but can also provide a smooth transition between the digital transition mode and the analog steady status operation of the LDO. The stability of this AADLDO has also been studied and confirmed to be stable during different operation conditions. The architecture of the proposed distributed power grid has been developed using a novel cooperative regulation method. The comparators in the local AADLDO digitize the local voltage and share this droop information to neighboring AADLDOs. Therefore, the proposed power grid has a much-reduced voltage droop and faster recovery speed because the neighboring AADLDOs can adaptively increase the response speed considering the shared information from their neighbors. Finally, we included all these ideas to design and fabricated this distributed power grid with a standard 65-nm CMOS process. Measurement results demonstrated the proposed distributed power grid architecture achieved the fastest 0.28ps figure-of-merits (FOM). These results are published in the most prestige conference for solid-state circuit design [C1], the IEEE International Solid-State Circuits Conference, and the more detail description of the design has been submitted to the most top-tier journal for solid-state circuit design [J1], the Journal of Solid-State Circuits, and now under review.

16206615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16206615.value: In this project, we have developed an analog-assisted digital low-dropout linear regulator (LDO) to break the tie between power and response speed of the LDO, achieving one of the fastest 0.28ps figure-of-merits. We believe this new type of hybrid LDO, either analog-assisted digital LDO or digital-assisted analog LDO, can achieve much better performance than the conventional approach. Therefore, this kind of hybrid LDO, or a modification of this kind of LDO such as digital-assisted analog LDO, should be further developed in other applications.

16206615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16206615.value: This project is to develop a new type of distributed power grid architecture such that the supply voltages of different building blocks inside the system-on-a-chip (SoC) can maintain almost constant even under very large current variations in each individual building block. A prototype of a 3 x 3 power grid has been developed and demonstrated to be effective in achieve good voltage regulation. The same design can be extended to larger m x n grid for bigger SoC devices. Outcomes of this project can lead to a much better voltage regulation and therefore a smaller overhead voltage is needed for the SoC, and thus further reduce the power consumption of the future SoC design.

16206915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16206915.value: Ultrasound imaging is widely used for medical diagnosis of soft tissues such as muscles and internal organs, as well as the blood circulatory system. Taking advantage of novel contrast agents, contrast-enhanced ultrasound has emerged as a promising diagnostic and therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment. The contrast agents are micro/nano-sized particles whose density and compressibility substantially differ from those of blood and tissue, and are detectable in ultrasonography when they adhere and accumulate at specific targets in sufficient quantity. Gas-filled microbubbles, the commercially available contrast media, are largely confined to the intravascular space due to their size of several microns, whereas the smaller nanocapsules are able to enter the extravascular space for targeting extravascular tissues of interest such as tumor cells. Liquid perfluorocarbon (PFC)-filled nanocapsules are being exploited as the most effective contrast agents owing to the enhanced permeability and retention in tumor tissues offered by their unique properties, as well as the enhanced echogenicity of the vaporized forms upon ultrasound activation. As both the trigger frequency for vaporization and resonance frequency for imaging with ultrasound are size-dependent, the monodispersity is a critical measure, and the conventional nanoemulsion methods cannot meet the demand. In this project, we aim to produce PFC nanocapsules with controlled size and narrow size distribution using microfluidic technology. We will perform a combined modeling, simulation, and experimental investigation on the droplet break-up process in our proposed designs. Applying novel fabrication techniques to achieve adjustable and reversible control of nanochannel structures, we will develop a micro/nanofluidic device that allows for precisely control of the size of the nanoemulsions with high monodispersity. Moreover, the stability of the nanocapsules will be improved through the optimization of the surfactants. To demonstrate the feasibility of using such PFC nanocapsules as theranostic agents, we will investigate the conversion of nanodroplets into microbubbles for adequate ultrasound detection, and the encapsulation of drug molecules into the nanocapsules for targeted drug delivery. Through the proposed research, we are developing the core technology for nanoemulsion contrast agents that could lead to improved diagnosis and imaging-guided therapy of tumor cells. The prospect of using novel micro/nanofluidic devices for formulation of mondisperse, multifunctional nanocapsules opens up new possibilities to advance molecular diagnostic tools with superior spatial and temporal resolutions. The new ability to precisely control the synthesis of nanomaterials using fluid dynamics and interfacial science will enable further technology development in the field of nanomanufacturing and molecular imaging. 超聲成像被廣泛用於軟組織如肌肉和內臟以及血液循環系統的醫學診斷。利用新型造影劑，超聲造影已成為有可能实现癌症治療的診斷和治療策略。造影劑是微米/納米尺寸的顆粒，其密度和可壓縮性藓组顯著不同於血液和組織，當它們足量附著和積聚在具體目標时可以被超聲檢測到。现有的用於造影劑的充氣微泡，由於大小有幾微米，在很大程度上局限於血管內空間，而粒径更小的納米膠囊能夠進入血管外空間，从而用於靶向血管外組織如腫瘤細胞。 由於其獨特的性能所提供的滲透性和在腫瘤組織中的滞留性，以及在超聲激活的汽化形式的增強迴聲的能力，液態氟碳（PFC）為核心的納米膠囊目前被认為是最有效的造影劑。由於汽化的觸發頻率和超聲成像的共振頻率都与粒径相关，均一粒径是合成液滴的一个重要指标。而以往的納米乳劑的方法無法滿足这个需求。在本項目中，我們的目標是采用微流控技術產生PFC納米膠囊， 并且控制粒径大小和分佈。我們將对我們提出的設計進行聯合建模，仿真，和實驗研究。應用新的製造技術，實現可控的和可逆的控制納米通道結構。我們將開發一個微/納米流體設備，允許精確控制納米乳劑膠囊的粒径大小和分佈。此外，納米膠囊的穩定性將通過表面活性劑的優化來改進。為了證明使用這樣的PFC納米膠囊作為治療診斷劑的可行性，我們將研究納米液滴轉化為微泡而实现超聲檢測，和藥物分子的封裝而实现靶向藥物传输。 通過擬議的研究，我們正在開發制备納米造影劑的核心技術，从而有望实现用於腫瘤細胞的影像診斷和引導治療。新型微/納流控設備為制备多功能納米膠囊開闢了新的可能性，以推動具有超強的空間和時間分辨率的分子診斷工具。新的能力。能夠精確地控制使用流體動力學和界面科學將進一步推动納米製造和分子成像領域的技術開發。

16206915.label: Realisation of objectives
16206915.value: 1. Objective 1 was fully realized. To investigate the droplet break-up mechanism, we performed numerical simulations using Comsol Multiphysics for self-emulsification in microchannels with a step-like expansion. Through the parametric studies varying the channel geometry, hydrodynamic conditions, and interfacial tension of the two phases, we found that, under a critical capillary number, the droplet generation is driven by the interfacial tension and the resulting droplet size is solely determined by the width of the nozzle and not sensitive to flow fluctuations, fluid and interfacial properties of the two phases. 2. Objective 2 was fully realized. We demonstrated controllable synthesis of PFC nanoemulsions in several micro/nanofluidic devices. The first design is a flame-shaped glass capillary and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) hybrid device that focuses PFC in three dimensions (3D) for droplet breakup. The second design is a rapid mixer that dilute the solvents in PFC stream rapidly and form PFC nanodroplets by spontaneous emulsification effect, known as the Ouzo effect. Various kinds of liquid PFC including Perfluoropentane (PFP, C5F12), Perfluorohexane (PFH, C6F14), Perfluoroheptane (PFHp, C7F16), Perfluorooctane (PFO, C8F18), Perfluorooctylbromide (PFOB, C8F17Br), perfluoro-15-crown-5-ether (PFCE, C10F20O5) were used to produce nanodroplets as small as 200 nm in diameter with polydispersity index (PDI) < 0.04. 3. Objective 3 was fully realized. To enhance the stabilization as well as to render excellent biocompatibility, we used a few types of fluorinated surfactants such as Zonyl FSO-100 and FTAC that are composed of a fluorophilic end and a hydrophilic end, and lipid mixture as nanodroplet coatings. We tested the vaporization and stability of the synthesized PFH, PFHp, PFO, PFOB, and PFCE nanodroplets, in combination with these surfactant/lipid coatings. We have demonstrated enhanced echogenicity of the PFC nanodroplets in an in vitro test after activation to microbubbles by ultrasound, manifesting the feasibility of the PFC nanodroplets can serve as phase-change contrast agents for ultrasound imaging. Perfluorocarbons with low boiling points (e.g., PFH) was relatively easy for vaporization. Other than the boiling point of PFCs, the size of the nanodroplet is another critical factor that influences the acoustic activation thresholds because the Clausius-Clapeyron relation indicates that the phase-transition temperature is inversely proportional to the inner pressure of the droplets, and the Laplace pressure increases as the droplet size reduces. However, the surfactant or lipid coated nanodroplets yield poor stability for in vivo ultrasound imaging. Therefore, we further developed nanobubbles or microbubbles with polymer or lipid-polymer bilaminar shells. These nano/micro capsules demonstrated excellent ultrasound contrast performance and much better stability in both in vitro and in vivo ultrasound imaging experiments, rendering a longer imaging window for ultrasound imaging with animal models. 4. Objective 4 was realized through the conjugation of drug molecules to the polymer shells for drug loading. We did not succeed in the double-emulsification strategy to realize multiplayer coatings for encapsulate both hydrophilic and hydrophobic agents. Drug molecules are difficult to be encapsulated directly in the PFC nanocasuples. Instead, we synthesized polymers that are coupled with the drug agent muelcules as the shell materials for the nanocapsules. We demonstrated chlorin e6 (Ce6) conjugated PFO-PCL-Ce6 as oxygen self-supplement and folate-drug conjugates with Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) for the treatment of cancer in C6 glioma-bearing mice.
