16208115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208115.value: Comparing with the effects of twin tunnelling on an existing circular tunnel above, the existing horseshoe-shaped tunnel experiences approximately 20% more vertical elongation in the mid-plane. The bending strains at the invert of the horseshoe-shaped tunnel can be as much as three times larger than those at the invert of the existing circular tunnel in the transverse direction. However, hoop stress along the tunnel lining in the existing circular tunnel is larger than that in the horseshoe-shaped tunnel. (Ref: 2 – Ng et al., 2016) Considering the effects of the ratio of the breadth of an existing horseshoe-shaped tunnel to the diameter of new circular tunnels (B/D) on the interaction of perpendicularly crossing tunnels, it is found that the induced maximum settlement at the centre of an existing horseshoe-shaped tunnel invert due to twin tunnelling underneath is unaffected by its size for different cover depths. The sagging settlement profile along the existing tunnel crown gradually changes into a hogging shape with increasing B/D ratios for smaller cover depth. The mid-plane deformations of the existing tunnel are vertically elongated but horizontally compressed. (Ref: 3 – Ng et al., 2018) For an existing horseshoe-shaped tunnel without a settlement joint, the settlement at the invert and crown along the longitudinal direction due to new twin tunnel construction underneath showed sagging and hogging curves, respectively. This is caused by the significant vertical elongation of the middle section of the horseshoe-shaped geometry. The presence of a settlement joint can result in an increase in the settlement of the ground surface and the existing tunnel by over 100%. In both cases, larger bending strains are expected in the transverse direction than in the longitudinal direction, particularly around the corners of the horseshoe-shaped tunnel. (Ref: 1 – Jiang et al., 2017)

16208115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208115.value: Only perpendicularly crossing tunnels have been investigated in this study. However, it is inevitably that tunnels will cross each other at an inclined angle in the vertical plane and intersect in the horizontal plane at different angles. These scenarios can result in different stress relief and stress increase leading to different ground responses. Further research is urgently needed.

16208115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208115.value: Major cities such as New York, London, Singapore, Hong Kong and Shanghai around the world are becoming more and more congested due to economic development and urbanization. To efficiently make use of space to relieve traffic congestion, and to protect the environment from excessive energy consumption and emissions due to traffic jams, underground metro systems have become the only viable transportation solution. Due to an increasing demand for underground space, tunnels are constructed closer and closer to each other, particularly at the intersection of different metro lines. Uncontrollable ground movements may cause adverse effects on nearby tunnels. It is not uncommon to encounter existing non-circular tunnels such as horseshoe and oval shaped during the construction of new tunnels. The existing non-circular tunnels often have historical values. The complex interaction of an existing horseshoe-shaped tunnel and new circular twin tunnels has been investigated and understood. Also the influence of the relative size of the horseshoe-shaped tunnel to new circular tunnel and the effects of joint in the existing tunnel are studied. The adverse effects of tunnel shape are identified and illustrated. These findings will be very useful for designers to assess damages to existing tunnels due to the construction of adjacent single and twin tunnels and for politicians to make decision of the risk that may involve in tunnel constructions.

16208215.label: Realisation of objectives
16208215.value: Dura mater, which is the outermost and the toughest meningeal layer, functions to protect the central nervous system through alleviating the brain dynamic response, lowering maximum intracranial pressure as well as shear stress whilst protecting the leakage of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Damages to dura mater can result in CSF leakage, leading to life-threatening complications such as encephalocele, infection, traumatic epilepsy or cerebrospinal fistulas and liquor-rhea. Currently, four different types of dura substitutes are available: autologous, allogeneic, heterogeneous and synthetic materials. Autologous materials have the disadvantages of adhesion between the implant and brain; Allogeneic dura substitutes have the danger of transmitting Creutzfeldt Kakob Disease; Heterogeneous grafts have been linked to the transmission of bovine spongiform encephalopathy. Artificial materials made from synthetic polymers are considered the most promising dura substitute because of their biocompatibility, ease of preparation, low acute body responses and low cost, and Gore PrecludeTM is a commercial dura substitute made of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE). Unfortunately, Gore Preclude exhibit some critical clinical issues such as cell adhesion, meningitis, and inflammatory tissue reactions due to PTFE’s intrinsic low creep resistance, stress-induced high friction coefficient. To address the issues concerning existing artificial dura substitutes, we proposed to develop new dura substitutes based on ultrahigh molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE), a gold standard material for use as implantable biomaterial, for its biochemical inertness, low friction coefficient, self-lubricating and higher mechanical strength in comparison with PTFE. Therefore, the ultimate objectives of this project were to develop a new UHMWPE based dura substitutes that will exhibit no adhesion to brain tissue and hence no tissue reaction, water-tightness, and mechanical properties mimicking to human dura. Besides satisfying these requirements, our newly developed dura substitute is also optically transparent (optical transmittance greater than 80% at wavelengths greater than 200 nm) as well as highly ductile. The optical transparency enables the new dura substitute to attach to the natural dura readily via photo-induced fixations; the high ductility (with recoverable strains>200%) and softness helps to accommodate the posterior swelling effects reducing potential bursting risks. Further, we enhanced functionality of our newly developed dura by transforming it into an e-dura such that it may also function to monitor the intracranial pressure changes under the skull. Specifically, the new dura substitute is a hierarchical composite of UHMWPE with polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), and the e-dura is composite of UHMWPE/graphene/PDMS. The novelty in our new dura design consists principally in our invention of microporous and creep resistant high-strength UHMWPE membrane. Our newly invented UHMWPE membrane itself satisfies most of the property desired for the dura substitute – it has low friction coefficient, strong viscoelasticity endowing it with strong creep resistance, besides, it is hydrophobic and it contains small pore diameters which enable it to be water tight making it highly resistant to Laplace pressures up to 5 bara protecting it from water leakage. To further reduce its stiffness, enhance its ductility and water tightness, we hybridized the membrane with PDMS – PDMS is water vapor permeable but water tight, besides, it has high ductility and is biocompatible but its mechanical strength is significantly weaker than natural dura. Hybridization was achieved by confining PDMS to the micropores bonded by UHMWPE nanofibrils giving strong Haymaker interaction forces at the PDMS/UHMWPE interface. Systematic studies were carried out and so an optimum PDMS loading was determined that enables the formation of PDMS/UHMWPE dura with mechanical properties mimicking natural dura. Further, the new dura shows much higher ductility than nascent UHMWPE membrane which is able to tolerate the local swelling effects upon neural surgery. Besides the successfully development of a new PDMS/UHMWPE, we also prepared a new e-dura by hybridizing with a monolayer graphene. In order to fabricate this new e-dura, we invented a new chemical-free large-area graphene transfer method for the preparation of conductive graphene/UHMWPE in which a monolayer graphene with dimensions up to 36 〖cm〗^2is laminated on its surface. The low out-of-plane bending stiffness of the atomic thin graphene fully conforms to the UHMWPE pore surface giving the laminated UHMWPE surface resistivity as low as 300 Ω/sq. The composite membrane is further hybridized with PDMS by pore confining method similar to the hybridization of PDMS/UHMWPE dura. The newly prepared e-dura exhibits exceptionally high piezo resistivity gauge factors upto 3000 making it a transparent and highly sensitive e-dura. Finally, we systematically investigated cellular level biocompatibility of our new e-dura through cell viability test, cell prefoliation and cell adhesion tests. Two different cells are studied, namely, mouse fibroblasts and mouse neural cells, respectively. No observable cell toxicity was detected, and the neural cells showed no adhesion to UHMWPE surface. An interesting observation is that the PDMS surface showed attachment to fibroblast cells – this means the new dura may form stronger bonding to natural dura after implant.

16208215.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208215.value: Dura mater, which is the outermost meninges under the skull, functions to protect the central nervous system. In this study, we have invented (patented) a number of new material processing methods[1]–[5] and fabricated a soft, compliant, transparent and biocompatible electronic dura mater (e-dura) that matches the mechanical property, mimics the structure of natural dura mater, and monitors the intracranial pressure change via piezo-resistivity sensing[6], [7]. The e-dura[6], [7] is a hierarchical structure consisting of hybridization of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) with nanoporous ultrahigh molecular weight polyethylene (UHMWPE) membrane laminated with an electronically conductive atomically thin graphene. We invented and applied our new hydrophobic, biocompatible and ultra-low-friction coefficient (~0.05) UHMWPE[1], [2], [8] in the new e-dura for the protection against CSF leakage and anti-neural cell attachment functionalities. We coated electrically conductive monolayer graphene using our newly invented large-area graphene transfer method with controlled porosity to impart the new e-dura with high piezo-resistive sensitivity or gauge factor and breathability[5], [9] In addition, we employed rubbery PDMS to impart softness, ductility compliance to the new e-dura. Besides, the new e-dura’s high optical transparency (optical transmittance greater than 80% at wavelengths greater than 200 nm) endows the potential for it to attach the dura mater readily via photo-induced fixations; its high ductility (with recoverable strains>200%) and softness helps to accommodate the posterior swelling effects reducing potential bursting risks; our new e-dura exhibits similar tensile modulus to human dura and thus it will generate no local stress-shielding effects [7]. Besides, the conformability of the monolayer graphene to the porous UHMWPE surface allows the coated surface to retain its porous microstructure. The large surface area associated with the porous structure was observed to act as the mechanical interlocking sites with the PDMS layer[6], [7]. The newly prepared porous UHMWPE membranes derived from this study are platform materials and have been found to lead to breakthroughs in a diverse range of applications including biomedical, environmental and energy; using our newly prepared UHMWPE membrane in membrane distillation technology, we observed record high water desalination flux[3], [4], and its application as a separator in rechargeable lithium-ion batteries enables the new battery to exhibit both higher safety and high-power-density overcoming the critical issues with current safer separators which suffer cause lower power density[2], [8]. This project resulted in two US full patent applications, three Chinese full patent applications, five PCT patent applications. Besides, we have graduated three PhDs and one MPhil students.

16208215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208215.value: The major findings from this project are the development of novel UHMWPE membranes. The new UHMWPE membranes exhibit specific in-plane tensile strengths up to about 25 times that of stainless steel and are highly ductile and possess porous structures ranging from three-dimensional fibrous random pores to 2-dimensional triangulated (Delaunay) random pores. We have for the first time, invented hand-manipulatable porous polymer nanofilms (< 100 nm). Our new nanofilm offer ample scope for new technologies in biomedical, energy, environment and fundamental studies. Examples include but not limited to fully skin-conformable and breathable bacteria resistant wound healing films, fully conformable electronic skins and skin sensors; separators for flexible and transparent batteries, high-capacity dielectric and supercapacitors; high-flux filtration membranes; substrates for the study of nanoconfinement dynamics, etc. We are conducting preliminary experiments on our new nanofilms by exploring their use as sweat sensors, electronic skins, nano-vibration film in high-clarity electrostatic loud speakers. We have also secured new funding from Shenzhen startup fund and Kaisha-HKUST to scale-up our membrane process technologies.

16208415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208415.value: This proposal concerns the design of efficient graph evacuation protocols. Consider a building or campus of buildings that need to be evacuated due to an emergency. This problem is often modelled by a graph with NODES denoting locations, e.g., rooms or campus buildings, and EDGES denoting passageways between nodes, e.g., hallways or roads. Given an input specifying the number of people at each node, the problem is to design a protocol that evacuates everyone out as quickly as possible. Such a protocol would specify the evacuation route from each NODE. More realistically, it could specify a single evacuation edge from each node. Following successive edges would provide the evacuation route. The major constraint in the problem description is on the edges, with each edge being described by a length and a capacity. The length sets the amount of time needed to traverse the edge while the capacity limits the number of people that can traverse the edge at any given time. The major problem when developing evacuation plans is that edges fill up, forcing people to wait to enter them. In the meantime, more people might be evacuated into locations that are already quite full, leading to more congestion, leading to even more delay. An efficient evacuation protocol would try to minimize congestion in order to minimize the time needed to evacuate the entire population. The evacuation protocol design problem comes with different levels of difficulty. In the simplest, the evacuation doors, denoted by SINK NODES, are specified in advance. In addition, each regular node is pre-assigned to evacuate to a specific sink node. In a more complicated variant, the sink nodes are still pre-specified but the assignment of nodes to sink-nodes is part of the protocol design problem. In an even more complicated variant, the protocol design problem needs to specify the sink node locations as well. Finally, in many of these problems, the actual number of people that need to be evacuated from each node is not known in advance. The problem specification only includes a range or distribution from which that population number can be drawn; the protocol will need to work well for all populations within that range. The goal of this proposal is to design good, i.e. minimal evacuation time, graph theoretic algorithms for these abstract problems under a variety of scenarios. The proposal falls within the area of theoretical computer science and, more specifically, graph algorithms. 本研究計劃的主題是在圖形模型上設計有效率的疏散程序和協議。作為例子，可先 假設一座或一群大樓中的人群需要緊急疏散；一般來說，我們以邊與 頂點連結成 的圖形作模型，以個別地點(如房間)為頂點，以通道(如走廊)為邊。 在模型中，各個地點將會有某個數量的人群，而我們要解決的問題是設計一個固定 程序，例如規劃特定地點的人群疏導至逃生出口，以求用最快的方法 完成疏散程 序。相較於不限制路線地為每個點指定逃生出口，更可行的選擇是讓同一個地點的 人向同一個方向逃生，如此串連成一條路線到達指定出 口。 如此設計模型，我們再添加一些規劃上的考慮因素，那就是每個通道都有各自的長 度，按長需要一定的時間通過，而容量有限，在任何時間只能容納一 定數量的通 行者。規劃疏散程序面對的最大的挑戰是通道容量帶來的限制，一旦通道容量用 滿，便會產生擠塞，人群就要等候，增加疏散所需時間。一 個有效率的疏散程序 要盡量避免擠塞，以達到最小的疏散時間。 解決這一類問題將面對多種不同的障礙，可以遂步引入更多因素以調整難度。在最 簡單的模型下，我們可預設「接收點」或「槽點」亦即逃生出口的具 體位置，同 時為各個不同的地點預設一個接收點，然後為此規劃逃生路線。進一步，我們仍會 預設接收點，但是不再為每個地點預設一個接收點；為不 同地點尋找合適的接收 點將是制定疏散程序中的一環。再進一止，我們可以引進更困難的條件，不再預設 接收點的位置，而是將之納入規劃問題之中。 最後，我們可以去除對各地點人群 分佈的假設，只假定各地點人群數目的大致範圍，而疏散程序需要適當應付各種可 能發生的人群分佈情況。 這個研究計劃的目的是設計圖形算法，以有效計算出好的疏散程序，最終達成最短 的疏散時間。這項研究應當分類於計算機科學理論，屬圖形算法的領 域。

16208415.label: Realisation of objectives
16208415.value: The technical objectives of this project were to develop more efficient algorithms for solving dynamic confluent flow problems in various settings Background: The project concerned the design of efficient graph evacuation protocols. The general scenario addressed was a graph in which VERTICES have weights and EDGES have both lengths and capacities. Intuitively, consider a campus of buildings that need to be evacuated due to an emergency. VERTICES denote locations, e.g., rooms, and EDGES denote passageways between nodes, e.g., hallways. A VERTICE's weight is the number of people initially present in the room. An EDGE’s length is the time required to traverse it; its capacity is the number of people that can enter it in one time unit. The problem is to design a protocol to evacuate all the people as quickly as possible to specified emergency exits (special vertices). This requires identifying a path for each evacuee to some emergency exit. Another problem fitting into a similar formulation is having the VERTICES be internet nodes with weights specifying the number of information packets starting at that node and EDGE lengths and capacities being the travel times and bandwidth of links between vertices. The problem is to move packets to destinations as quickly as possible. Such graphs are known as Dynamic Flow networks and have been well studied in the Operations Research literature. The major issue that distinguishes them from normal flow problems is the introduction of CONGESTION. If too much flow tries to enter an edge, it backs up and requires waiting, leading to delays. The design of fast evacuation protocols depends upon the reduction of congestion via clever routing. A further requirement for evacuation protocols that make them harder than standard dynamic flow problems is the CONFLUENCE requirement that all flow entering a vertex must leave along the same path. In evacuation protocols, this corresponds to having all evacuees entering a room (possibly from different doors) henceforth following the same designated evacuation path from that point onward, e.g., a sign stating "this way out". Confluent routing is also standard in (destination based) internet routing as it models “meet and merge” routing protocols. While confluent flow HAS been previously studied in STATIC networks (where it is already known to be difficult) it had not been very well analyzed in dynamic ones. Problem Definitions: The objective results discussed below are for confluent routing in dynamic flow networks. The Quickest Path Evacuation Problem (QPEP) is to find the fastest evacuation time to pre-specified sinks. This is essentially a clustering problem in which the centers of the clusters are known in advance with a very special metric that reflects the evacuation time to that cluster center. The Sink Location Problem (SLP) is to find the location of the sinks that permit fastest evacuation. This is again essentially a clustering problem in which the centers of the clusters need to found. In the “uniform capacity” version of the problem all edges have the same capacity while in the “general capacity” one, different edges can have different capacities. Objectives Realized: The project objectives were to design efficient solutions for the SLP and (easier) QPEP problems for a variety of graph types and scenarios and for both uniform and general capacity problems. In what follows, “n” denotes the number of vertices in the input graph and “k” the number of sinks (evacuation nodes). One main outcome of this project was an extremely strong negative result. More explicitly, it was proven that in a general graph, the QPEP problem (and also the SLP problem) with even one sink cannot be approximated to within a O(log n) factor of optimal time (unless P=NP). This is in contrast to the same problem without the confluence condition, which is known polynomial time solvable. The same techniques also proved that bi-criteria constant-factor approximations can usually also not be constructed. The positive objectives realized, were therefore for special graphs, i.e. paths and trees. The first major positive result was a O(n k^2 poly(log n)) solution to the SLP problem on trees for any number of sinks. Previously, polynomial solutions had only existed for the QPEP. The parametric-search based technique developed was not specific to graph evacuation but was applicable to many other tree-clustering problems as well. These results were for general capacity graphs (running slightly faster on uniform capacity graphs) A second result was an O(n log^3 n) solution to the SLP problem on paths with general capacities (slightly faster on uniform capacity graphs). The focus here was on removing the dependence upon k that had plagued all previous algorithms. A similar result had long been known for the k-center problem on paths but that wasn’t extendable to the more complicated k-sink evacuation problem. This new result required the development of a new suite of data structures. It also provided faster algorithms for the easier QPEP problem. The objective results above all assumed that all vertex weights were fully known. In “robust optimization” the actual input is not known in advance; only constraints on the input are known. The goal is to design a solution that is "least-bad". For the sink-evacuation problems, this translates into only knowing, for each vertex, a RANGE in which the amount of initial flow sited there must fall. Returning to the intuitive motivation previously given, this corresponds to having an upper and lower bound on the number of people initially in each room. The new goal is to find an SLP evacuation protocol that allows a least bad evacuation for all possible allowable inputs (where badness is measured as the difference between the actual time required by the protocol on an input and the time required if the real input was known in advance). Optimizing this is known as a “minmax-regret” problem and is well studied in various other optimization settings. Prior to this project, polynomial time minmax-regret sink-evacuation algorithms had only been known for a few simple cases. More explicitly, they were only known for the path when k=1 or k=2 and for the tree when k=1. The reason for the limitation was that increasing the number of sinks seemed to lead to an exponential explosion in run times. Also, all known results assumed uniform edge capacities. This project solved this minmax regret SLP problem completely for uniform capacity paths and trees. For fixed k, it solved the problem for paths in O(n poly (log n)) time and for trees in O(n^2 poly(log n)) time. Independent of k, it solved the problem in O(n^3 poly(log n)) time for paths and O(n^6 poly(log n)) time for trees. Finally, all previously known results on minmax regret sink evacuation, including the ones listed above, assumed uniform capacity edges. They worked by proving that only a finite (polynomial) number of worst-case solution scenarios could occur and searched in the space of those scenarios. Those techniques failed for general capacity problems and it was unclear whether those problems were even polynomial time solvable. The last result from this project was a new combinatorial understanding of the solution structure of the minmax regret 1-sink evacuation problem on a GENERAL capacity path. It showed that the solution scenario space is infinite, explaining why previous techniques failed. But it then showed that the space still does satisfy some other properties that permit solving the problem with an O(n^4 log n) time algorithm

16208415.label: Major findings and research outcome
16208415.value: In what follows, “n” denotes the number of vertices in the input graph and “k” the number of sinks (evacuation nodes). All works referenced below appear in part (C). (1) The major negative finding was that even the simplest one-sink version of the problem on general graphs could not be approximated to within a factor of O(log n), unless P=NP. This paper appeared in the proceedings of ISAAC 2017 and was a collaboration with a project-supported PhD student and a student intern. (2) The first polynomial time algorithm for solving the general sink location problem on trees. This was published in the proceedings of ISAAC 2016 with a project-supported PhD student and is currently in submission to Algorithmica. (3) Faster algorithms for solving the general sink location problem on paths. This was the first such algorithm that was independent of k, the number of sinks. This appeared in the proceedings of WADS 2017 and is currently in submission to Theoretical Computer Science. (4) The first general algorithm for solving the Minmax-regret sink location problem on paths with uniform capacities. Previous results were only able to solve this for k=1 or k=2 with exponential blowup occurring as k grew. This paper showed how to solve the problem for any k in polynomial time (independent of k). It appeared in Algorithmica in 2019. (5) The first algorithm for solving the Minmax-regret sink location problem on trees with uniform capacities. Previous results were only able to solve this for k=1 with exponential blowup occurring as k grew. This paper showed how to solve the problem for any k in polynomial time (independent of k). A draft of this result has been written (attached to this report) and is currently being revised for publication. This was a collaboration with a project-supported student intern. (6) The first algorithm for solving the Minmax-regret 1-sink location problem on a path with general capacities. This is the first polynomial time minmax-regret sink-location problem for any graph with general capacities. It is currently in submission to Discrete Applied Mathematics. This was a collaboration with a project-supported student intern.

16208415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16208415.value: Three different avenues for further development are being pursued. 1. A draft of the result described in item (5) from Section 6.1 is still being revised and will be submitted for publication soon. 2. Item (6) in Section 6.1 was the first polynomial time Minmax-regret sink location algorithm for any general capacity graph. We are currently examining whether the techniques developed there could be extended to more complicated scenarios. 3. K-center clustering is a standard data-clustering technique and is a special case of k-sink evacuation (with infinite capacities). 1-Dimensional data can be viewed as lying on a path graph. So, k-center clustering of 1-D data is a special case of k-sink evacuation of a path graph. It was recently noted that a variation of the data structure developed for item (4) in Section 6.1, “Faster algorithms for solving the general sink location problem on paths” can be made DYNAMIC, allowing fast insertion or deletion of data items. This should permit being able to find the new cluster centers for the modified data much quicker than re-solving the problem from scratch. The PI with collaborators is currently extending this observation to develop efficient algorithms for dynamic k-center clustering of 1-D data.

16208415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16208415.value: The project concerned the design of efficient graph evacuation protocols. As one example (there are other applications) consider a campus of buildings that need to be evacuated due to an emergency. This problem is often modelled by a graph with NODES denoting locations, e.g., rooms, and EDGES denoting passageways between nodes, e.g., hallways. Edges have defined lengths (travel time) and capacities (number of people that can enter a hallway in a given amount of time.) The problem is to develop protocols (algorithms) for quickly evacuating all people to specified emergency exits as quickly as possible. The problem has multiple variations; sometimes the number of people initially on a node is explicitly known; sometimes it is not. Sometimes, all edges have the same capacity (width); sometimes they do not. The topology (structure) of the graph can be simple or very complicated. A major difficulty that arises in these problems is addressing the CONGESTION caused by multiple people moving along different paths. In this project we designed efficient algorithms for optimally solving some of these problems, often dramatically improving on what was previously known. We also proved that many such problems cannot be optimally solved or even efficiently approximated and developed other solution approaches.

16209015.label: Project Objectives
16209015.value: Develop a framework to study the initiation time of substitute bus services under the uncertainty of disruption duration; Develop a method to determine the fleet size and routing of substitute bus services under the uncertainty of demand redistribution; Develop a deployment plan for substitute buses based on a portfolio of reserve, spare, and retracted buses.

Develop a method to determine the fleet size and routing of substitute bus services under the uncertainty of demand redistribution;
Develop a deployment plan for substitute buses based on a portfolio of reserve, spare, and retracted buses.

16209015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209015.value: As metro systems often serve as the backbone for public transport in metropolitan areas, any major disruption will have a severe impact, affecting tens of thousands of passengers. Even for the most reliable metro systems, such as the Mass Transit Railway in Hong Kong, on average there are hundreds of service disruptions every year, with some lasting for a few hours. It is, therefore, imperative to develop contingency plans for disruption management. This is particularly so for rail systems running on single tracks, without parallel lines, wherein any rail blockage would require substitute buses (SB) for bridging the disrupted railway sections. Despite the importance of bus bridging for rail disruption management, in reviewing the literature, it is surprising that this problem has not attracted the level of efforts it deserves. This project will address three important questions in the development of SB contingency plans. The first regards the initiation time for SB services. As the duration of a disruption varies and cannot be predicted perfectly ahead of time, the response timing is critical. Initiating SB services too early would confuse passengers and have cost implications; initiating too late, on the other hand, would exacerbate the problem as the unsatisfied demand accumulates. The second question pertains to the fleet size and routing of SB services upon their initiation. The analysis should consider demand redistribution due to the disruption, which introduces uncertainty to the problem. The SB routing and fleet size involves a tradeoff between the delay of the affected metro passengers, and that of other passengers affected by road congestion due to the SB services. The third question regards the putting together of a fleet to serve as SB. The analysis will focus on developing cost-effective portfolios to supply the needed SB fleet. Two advancements will be introduced here for the development of SB contingency plans: the first is the proper treatment of uncertainty, including the uncertainty in disruption duration and that of the demand pattern in the aftermath of a disruption; the other is capturing the time-dimension explicitly in the analysis as the disruption unveils itself over time. Both advancements are critical for developing robust contingency plans that adapt to the situation as the disruption continues. We will use Hong Kong and Shanghai case studies to demonstrate this modeling framework. This project will open up theoretically interesting and practically important topics to enhance metro system operations under disruption.

16209015.label: Realisation of objectives
16209015.value: This project has successfully completed all the objectives. Specifically: 1. For Objective 1, we have developed a stochastic model to determine the initiation time of substitute buses services based on probabilistic incident duration according to their types, and applied to the Hong Kong scenarios. 2. For Objective 2, we have formulated the fleet size and routing problem of substitute buses under uncertain incident duration, and applied to a case study in Shanghai. In addition, we have investigated how to regulate the headways of en route buses to make their service more efficient and evenly loaded. 3. For Objective 3, we have developed deployment plans of contracting substitute buses under uncertain incident duration, and investigated the pricing and conditions of acquiring the needed bus fleet from bus operators under market principles.

Based on the stochastic model developed, we identified the optimal substitute bus initiation time, which is basically around 20-30 minutes, depending on the incident duration distribution and types of incidents. Such results are useful to set up guidelines. We have also conducted a comprehensive review of metro disruption management, and identified the future research directions. Part C papers #1 and #5. 2. As part of this project, we have developed a 2-stage stochastic program for designing the fleet size and routing of substitute buses under uncertainty. The plan consists of buses running on regular routes and schedules and ad hoc buses that are added to handle surge in uncertain demand. Once the buses are in operation, we developed a scheme to regulate their headways to avoid bus bunching which will enhance the efficiency of their operations. Part C papers #1 and #4 3. The final part of this project involved composing the fleet to serve substitute buses. We studied various pricing schemes to ensure that such buses will be made available by bus operators according to commercial market principles. We further investigated whether there is benefit to be gained if the metro company jointly operates the bus fleet with a bus company. Part C paper #3

16209115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209115.value: Reinforced concrete wide-beam frame systems are recognised as effective load-resisting structural forms for buildings, since the use of wide and shallow beams provides significant advantages and needs. Seismic performance of wide beam-column connections has received added emphasis due to its importance relating to the design practice of moment-resisting frame structures. However, consistent and general accepted approaches are still not available in the design codes all over the world. The use of wide beam systems in seismically active regions is prohibited because of limited understanding of their seismic performance. The goal of the research project is to investigate the seismic behaviour and failure mechanisms of wide beam-column joints under seismic actions. This is achieved by the experimental, numerical and theoretical investigations. In the studies, wide beam-column joints are tested, followed by a comprehensive finite-element numerical investigation. Based on the test results and computational simulations, a theoretical model is developed for practical design applications. The direct benefit of the research starts in obtaining the relationship between design variables of wide beam-column joints which provide better understanding of the seismic behaviour. The research results and design recommendations from this pioneering research should benefit infrastructure development in the countries and regions that are threatened by earthquakes.

16209415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209415.value: 目前，建築物空間供暖和製冷每年所消耗的能源佔全球能源消耗總量的25%以上。能源樁技術被公認為最有前途的建築節能措施之一，該技術基於地表某個深度（約10米）以下全年溫度相對穩定（在歐洲和熱帶國家分別為10-15和20 -25攝氏度）的自然規律，在冬季提取地熱資源加熱空間，在夏季將室內餘熱轉移到地下。相對於傳統的供暖和製冷系統，利用能源樁技術能夠分別減少能源消耗和二氧化碳排放約60%和50%。儘管能源樁技術有巨大的潛在優勢，但尚未被廣泛使用。這是由於熱能的傳遞使能源樁週邊的土體受到冷熱循環作用，改變土體的材料特性，進而影響能源樁的服役性能，包括承載力和樁頂沉降。國內外對溫度循環作用下土體的材料特性及其理論尚缺乏完善的認知，導致現有的能源樁設計方法主要基於經驗。 本項目將開展室內試驗和理論建模研究兩種代表性土體（即飽和黏土和砂土）在溫度循環作用下的力學性能，重點包括溫度循環引起的變形、應力-應變關係曲線、剪脹性和剪切強度。將考慮與能源樁實踐密切相關的溫度範圍，即4到40攝氏度。依據新的實驗結果，將發展一個狀態相關的本構模型，以更好地反映黏土和砂土複雜的循環熱力學行為。這個項目的成功將毫無疑問提升對溫度循環作用下飽和土力學性質的認知，所獲得的實驗室測試結果和本構模型將幫助研究人員和工程師更準確地分析能源柱的性能，改進能源樁目前的設計方法，並鼓勵業主使用能源樁。

16209415.label: Realisation of objectives
16209415.value: The project objectives have been all achieved through the following activities: (1) Three triaxial apparatuses are modified to heat and cool soils in a wide temperature range of 4 to 60 degrees Celsius. (2) Stress-controlled tests are carried out to investigate the volumetric and deviatoric deformations of both clays and sands subjected to heating and cooling cycles. (3) The influence of temperature and thermal cycles on small strain stiffness, dilatancy and shear strength is investigated through temperature-controlled triaxial shear tests. (4) Three new constitutive models are developed for describing the thermo-mechanical behaviour of clays and sands.

16209415.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209415.value: Key findings related to Objective 1: (1) The thermal strain of sand is affected by its state with reference to the critical state line. A loose specimen above the critical state line contracted in the temperature range from 23 to 35 degrees Celsius and expanded at temperatures between 35 and 50 degrees Celsius. On the contrary, for a denser specimen below the critical state line, only expansion was observed when the temperature changed from 23 to 50 degrees Celsius. (2) Reconstituted, compacted and intact clay specimens all show continuous contraction as the number of thermal cycles increased, albeit at a decreasing rate. After five heating and cooling cycles with temperatures, the accumulated plastic axial strain of the reconstituted specimen was 38% and 68% larger than those of the intact and recompacted specimens, respectively. (References: Journal papers 1, 4, 8, 10) Key findings related to Objective 2: The shear stiffness and dilatancy of recompacted specimens increase with temperature. The shear stiffness and maximum dilatancy increase by as much as 47% and 63% at suctions of 0 and 200 kPa, respectively. On the contrary, thermal effects on the stress–strain behaviour of intact specimens are negligible. (References: Journal paper 7) Key findings related to Objective 3: The mechanical behaviour of soil specimens is only slightly affected by the heating and cooling cycles. For example, the plastic strain induced by cyclic loading and unloading is approximately 20% larger for specimens without thermal cycles than those with thermal cycles. (References: Journal papers 2, 9) Key outcomes related to Objective 4: Theoretical models are developed for describing the thermo-mechanical behaviour of clays and sands. In the model for sands, the concept of state-dependency is newly incorporated to simulate the observed behaviour of sand under cyclic heating and cooling. In the model for clays, two bounding surfaces are constructed to simulate the accumulation of irreversible strain under thermal cycles. These models are well verified using new data from this project as well as existing results in the literature. (References: Journal papers 3, 5, 6)

16209415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209415.value: This project mainly focuses on the thermo-mechanical behaviour of saturated soils. However, soils surrounding energy piles are often unsaturated, particularly in arid and semi-arid regions. To understand the performance of energy piles in these regions, a comprehensive study of the thermo-mechanical behaviour of unsaturated soils is urgently needed.

16209415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209415.value: Energy piles can extract geothermal energy for space heating in buildings in winter and assist in cooling space in summer by dissipating heat into the ground, where the temperature stays fairly constant throughout the year in many parts of the world. Despite their potential benefits, energy piles have not been widely used, because the current design methods are essentially empirical. The empiricism has mainly arisen from the lack of fundamental understanding of cyclic thermo-mechanical behaviour of soils and our incapability of modelling the complex soil behaviour and its interaction with energy piles accurately. The cyclic thermo-mechanical behaviour of both clay and sand have been improved through this project. Different aspects of the thermo-mechanical behaviour are studied using new temperature-controlled triaxial apparatuses, including volumetric and deviatoric thermal strains, stiffness-strain relationship, dilation, and shear strength. Based on experimental results, new theoretical models are developed for simulating the thermo-mechanical behaviour of clay and sands. The experimental and theoretical results will be useful for practical engineers to analyse the performance of energy piles more accurately, and to improve the current design methods of energy piles.

16209715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209715.value: Transfer learning adapts and reuses knowledge from source domains for a target domain. It has attained much popularity in data mining and machine learning, as well as many other areas. A major assumption in many transfer learning algorithms is that the source and target domains are directly related; that is, there exists some overlap between the two domains. However, if two domains are not directly related; that is, few shared factors can be detected, performing knowledge transfer between these domains will not be effective. This source-target domain gap is a serious impediment to the successful application of transfer learning. Inspired by human transitive inference and learning ability, whereby two seemingly unrelated concepts can be connected by a string of intermediate bridges using auxiliary concepts, in this project we study a novel learning problem: transitive transfer learning (abbreviated to TTL). TTL is aimed to break the large domain gaps and transfer knowledge even if the source and target domains share few factors directly. To this end, we propose to leverage a sequence of intermediate domains to connect certain source and target domains. For example, in sentiment classification problems, we may fail to transfer knowledge from a corpus of book reviews to music reviews directly, due to the large word distribution gap, but we can successfully transfer knowledge between them with some movie reviews as a bridge if we apply TTL. As a new learning problem, there are many research issues we have to resolve. First of all, we explore how to transfer knowledge in a chain of domains from a source to a target domain. Second, for any pair of source and target domains, we explore how to build a chain of domains from a set of candidate intermediate domains to enable the best transfer. Third, besides transitively transferred knowledge from the source domain, when the intermediate domains themselves have new knowledge to help the target domain, we explore how to find a chain to achieve best overall transfer. There are many other research issues in TTL, but in this project, we focus on these three and propose effective algorithms to solve them. We expect our solutions to contribute not only to transfer learning research, but also to data mining and machine learning in general, especially when we consider most domains are not directly connected. We will collect extensive real-world data for experimentation and develop and evaluate a prototype system for TTL applications. 迁移学习是机器学习的重要延伸。在迁移学习的模型中， 可以从一个已经建立的模型来推出一个新的模型， 即使在新的领域中， 数据的分布和特征表达和以前不同。我们的研究表示， 迁移学习可以扩展到两个以上的领域，使得即使从原数据不能直接迁移到性的领域， 也可以通过中间领域把知识传递到终点领域。在这一研究项目中，我们将建立 传递迁移学习的模型，探索新的迁移算法，并通过实验验证传递迁移学习的有效性。

16209715.label: Realisation of objectives
16209715.value: We have built a deep learning based transitive transfer learning framework. We have been able to formulate the learning problem in the target domain as one that can learn by transferring both from the source domain and from the intermediate domains, and all the learning is automatically done in the process. In fact, the intermediate domains do not even have labels, and they can still allow transition of transferred knowledge to move from the source to a target domain. We have tested the framework in a number of well known application domains, including the image classification domains and cross domain settings such as going from images to text and vice versa. Our result has been published in top conferences such as KDD and AAAI, and several PhD students are graduated as a result. In particular: 1. We have found several methods to transitively transfer knowledge from a source to a target domain via a number of intermediate domains. One method involves using the intermediate domain data that have partial overlaps with previous domain in features, thus allowing a chain of domains to be connected through to the target domain. Another method assumes that the overlap is not explicit, and thus requires that the subspaces be explored to find common domains. Both methods are shown to perform well, but each have different assumptions. 2 The second step is to find the best path to enable the transitive transfer. For this goal we first tried to use dynamic programming in a graph formed by domains to find the best path to the target domain. Another method is to form a deep learning structure and feed all data in random order to the model. We then designed the middle layer embedding as the output model for classification. This allows us to filter out the intermediate domain samples that are not effective. As a result, only the potentially useful samples are used in enhancing the model, which enables the final transitive transfer. We found that this is most effective when we have multiple cross-media domains to be used as the intermediate domains. 3. Finally, we have found an integrated approach that make use of the deep learning structure for both labelled and unlabelled intermediate domain samples. For labeled samples, the error rate tell us how far they are from the target domain samples, but for unlabelled samples in the intermediate domains, they can also have useful knowledge as they can be used to enhance the embeddings of the final transitive transfer model. We designed an algorithms for efficient speedup to convergence. 4. We have designed a working prototype system for transitive transfer learning. The system has been applied to several cross media application domains. Furthermore, our work has influenced several works in the follow up to our work, including over 100 citations on google scholar.

16209715.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209715.value: Our work is to extend transfer learning to look beyond transferring form a single source to a single target domain. Instead we look at transferring from a source to a series of intermediate domains and finally to a target domain. We have found that the system can work well when we have a fixed path of domains, even when we deal with domains that have a heterogeneous feature representation. When we are not given a path, the best way to enable the transfer is to collectively train a deep learning model, and the training process can itself find out the best samples from the intermediate domains to keep. This finding allows us to optimise the algorithm by simplifying the profess of sample section. The result is a fast-converging algorithm that can transfer knowledge between domains that are far from each other.

16209715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209715.value: The work has been adopted by many researchers. Our top-conference publications (in conferences like KDD and AAA) are well received in the community, with over 100 citations in a short time. We have developed a prototype system that we have made available for others to use and experiment with. We have tested the system on many cross media applications. In the future, we will further extend the framework to allow for more detailed domain-distance measures, and test how the measures affect the final performance.

16209715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209715.value: Transfer learning enables machines to learn by analogy like humans do, by transferring the knowledge from a source domain to a target domain. In the end, the data in the target domain do not have to require extended labelling process which usually make machine learning challenging in practice. Transitive transfer learning allows the source and target domains to be far from each other, by filling the knowledge gaps by data from the intermediate domains. We have designed an algorithm to make this transitive transfer learning process automatic and in an optimised way. The impact to the society would be significant as we apply AI and machine learning in practice, as we often do not have so much labeled data in a domain. Thus, in many situations, transitive transfer learning can be used to alleviate the data lacking problem and enlarge the application range of machine learning.

Event-based estimation strategies for remote state estimation applications have shown good estimation performance despite limited communication bandwidth and sensor transmission energy. The lack of closed-form expressions of the estimation performance, however, has limited the popularity of existing event-based estimation technologies in applications. The closed-form solutions are desirable for almost all the researchers. Compared with their counterparts, e.g., heuristic algorithms, the solutions obtained by approximations and ad hoc solutions, the closed-form solutions enable accurate systematic analysis and application designs with a performance guarantee. In practical applications, the event-based estimation strategies are used in sensor scheduling and power control. The lack of closed-form expressions of the estimation performance makes it impossible to design a good sensor schedule or a good power control policy with guaranteed performance. In short, both theoretical development and practical applications call for a novel design of event-triggering estimation strategies fulfilling the following criteria: 1) the event-based estimation scheme should have a closed-form expression of the estimation performance which is easy to analyze theoretically and will enable the design of a broad class of systems with guaranteed performance; 2) the new scheme should have better estimation performance versus the communication resources tradeoffs than that of the existing event-based strategies; 3) the new scheme must be easy to implement in practical applications. To meet these criteria, we propose to use stochastic event-based estimation in which additional random variables with special distributions are introduced for the triggering event. By properly designing their distributions and the appropriate forms of the triggering events, a closed-form optimal estimator and the associated estimation performance can be expected. The proposed stochastic event-based estimation techniques open new doors to a wide spectrum of potential applications, among which we shall study a few representative ones, specifically, stochastic sensor scheduling, stochastic power control, and stochastic quantization. The overall project will be carried out over three stages sequentially, each of which focuses on one of these research topics. Our initial research results in this direction have enhanced our understanding of the resource limitation vs estimation quality tradeoff of the overall system and have demonstrated that our approach is feasible. Moreover, we expect the deliverable results will enrich the literature as well as provide various tools for practitioners to use. 在本項目中，我們將研究基於事件式狀態估計的方法。在遠程狀態估計的應用中，即使在通信帶寬或傳感器傳輸能源有限的情況下，基於事件式的估計策略依然顯示出優異的性能。然而，由於現有的基於事件式的估計方法缺乏顯式的估計指標表達式，其技術在應用中受到了限制。對絕大多數研究者而言，顯式解具有重要吸引力。與非顯式解——例如啟發性算法解、放松解、特殊解——相比，顯式解可以保證系統性分析的精確性，以及為應用設計提供性能保障。 在實際應用中，基於事件式估計策略被使用於傳感器調度和能源控制領域。由於其估計性能指標沒有顯式表達式，人們尚未利用其設計出具有性能保證的傳感器調度策略或者能源控制方案。 總之，無論是理論發展還是實際應用，都期望壹種新的事件觸發型估計方法。這種新方法需要滿足以下幾點：1）方法中估計性能指標須有顯式表達，從而便於理論分析，保證壹大類系統的設計的性能水平；2）在面對通信資源制約的情況下，新方法的估計性能須勝過已有方案；3）在實際應用中，新方法須易於實現。 為了實現以上要求，我們提出壹種隨機的基於事件式估計方法，它在事件觸發機制中引入了具有特殊分布的新隨機變量。只要適當地設計隨機變量的分布和觸發事件的形式，我們可望得到顯式的最優估計器及相應的估計性能指標。我們提出的隨機型基於事件式的估計技術為壹系列的潛在應用打開了大門。我們將研究其中具有代表性的幾種，如：隨機傳感器調度、隨機能源控制，以及隨機量化。整個項目工作將按三階段展開，每階段各致力於上述壹種應用問題。我們在該方向上的初期研究使我們進壹步掌握了整體系統中資源限制與估計質量的折衷性機制，並顯示了我們所提方法的可行性。最後，我們希望，我們的後續研究結果最終能夠豐富該領域的理論成果，並為實際應用提供更多工具。

16210015.label: Realisation of objectives
16210015.value: We have made excellent progress with this funding. Following the original objectives of the project, we have successfully integrated state estimation and communication via transmission power scheduling. For a number of different application scenarios (e.g., remote estimation with smart sensors/normal sensors), we have constructed novel types of event-based scheduling protocols, derived the corresponding minimum mean-squared error estimate at the remote estimator, analyzed the communication power vs remote estimation quality tradeoffs, etc. In addition to the original objectives, we have successfully applied the developed tools to other areas such as multi-sensor Kalman filtering, nonlinear filtering, etc. The results are fruitful which are summarized and published in 7 leading prestigious international journals (five published in the IEEE-TAC and one in Automatica) and 3 leading international conferences. Two PhD students are trained during the project period.

16210015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210015.value: We have conducted a full-spectrum and thorough study of novel stochastic event-triggered strategies with applications to remote estimation, multi-sensor filtering, nonlinear filtering, etc. We have fully met the original project objectives and achieved more which is beyond our expectation. The major finding is that by properly designing a good stochastic scheduling strategies, greatly enhanced system performance can be achieved with closed-form analytical expressions which allow us to find better system and resource tradeoffs. The main research outcomes include publications in 7 leading international journals and 3 leading international conferences as well as training of 2 PhD students.

16210015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210015.value: The research outcomes are fruitful and paved the way for a number of exciting future research directions including better scheduling of multi-sensor systems, multi-agent consensus, communication and control co-designs, cyber-physical systems security, etc.

16210015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210015.value: This project has conducted a thorough study of stochastic event-triggered strategies and their effect on achieving a better tradeoff between remote estimation quality and the communication resources. We first quantify the importance of different messages based on which, effective event-triggered policies can be designed which significantly reduces the communication resources while meets desired system performance. The developed theoretical tools including state estimation and event-triggering control laws can be used to better analyze and design an important class of networked systems which are seen in a variety of areas in engineering sciences and elsewhere.

16210215.label: Project Objectives
16210215.value: Risk- Aware Optimal Charging Policies for EVs with Fixed Deadlines based on CVaR-Constrained SSP Analysis When given the charging requirement and a fixed deadline, controlling the charging process of an EV with only Type-I uncertainties is usually modeled as a finite horizon Markov decision process problem (thus named as MDP model, hereafter). However, due to the nature of the MDP model, such control policies are often non-stationary and difficult to implement in practice; moreover, the calculation of optimal policies is computationally cumbersome due to the famous “curse of dimensionality”. To tackle these two disadvantages of the MDP model in this fundamental EV charging control problem, the first objective of this project is to propose a unified optimization framework based on the SSP model. Based on this framework, i) we will propose efficient and parallel algorithms to obtain the optimal stationary policy by exploiting the hidden monotonicity of the state transitions; ii) we will further investigate the optimal stationary policy based on the average-deadline constrained SSP analysis and the CVaR-constrained SSP analysis, such that the risk-value tradeoff can be achieved in a computationally tractable way. Risk-Aware Optimal and Robust Charging Policies for EVs with Uncertain Deadlines based on Joint Chance-Constrained SSP Analysis In addition to Type-I uncertainties, the Type-II uncertainty may also substantially influence the design of optimal charging policy. To the best of our knowledge, optimal control of the EV’s charging process while taking into account the two types of uncertainties remains an open yet challenging question. Nevertheless, built upon the chance-constrained SSP framework, the second objective of this project is to propose a joint chance-constrained SSP framework, which is able to guarantee the deadline requirement for every possible deadline realization. Solving the joint chance-constrained SSP, however, is technically challenging by itself. To tackle this difficulty, we will adopt Bonferroni’s inequality from probability theory and decompose the joint chance constraint into multiple individual chance constraints, which will allow us to design computationally tractable algorithms. Moreover, by exploiting the tool of the Kullback-Leibler divergence, we will investigate the robust charging policy that is resilient to the disturbance in the deadline distribution. Robust Bidding and Charging Strategies for Demand-Side Frequency Regulation Using a Fleet of EVs Based on the V2G concept and the above CVaR-constrained SSP framework, the third objective of this project is to propose a robust day-ahead bidding strategy and a charging control algorithm for a fleet of EVs. In particular, multiple Type-I uncertainties will be integrated into the bidding model. To guarantee the regulation service and the charging requirement for all the EVs, we propose to separate the control horizon into two parts the regulation period and the charging period. Specifically, in the regulation period, we aim at designing a methodological framework for an optimal and robust day-ahead bidding strategy; in the charging period, we will further propose an optimal and robust charging algorithm that can guarantee the charging requirement for all EVs. The design in the aforementioned two periods will lead to an online charging-rate allocation algorithm, whose performance will be investigated based on the competitive ratio analysis.

16210215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210215.value: 傳統電網的經濟結構和物理結構正在經歷重塑的過程。在電能供應端，可再生能源日益滲透的現實正逐步推動著系統管理者們去重新思考他們的市場策略，並促使他們重新設計現有的基礎架構，從而使分佈式發電過程中的高度不確定性得到緩解。在電能需求端，不斷增加的電動車數量不僅使電能消耗在時間上產生了顯著的隨機性，同時也在空間位置上出現了相當大的不確定性。然而幸運的是，電動車在其充電功率和充電時間區間上有著顯著的靈活性，因而它也通常被稱為極富弹性的电能负载。如果管理得當，這種弹性负载不僅可以在需求端“消化”電動車充电过程中所帶來的風險和不確定性，而且在供應端還可以“吸收”分佈式發電過程中的間歇性。基於這點，本項目著眼於提出具有風險意識的、鲁棒并且平穩的充電策略，從而去管理電動車充電過程中由多種類型的不確定性所產生的風險。具體來說，我們的項目側重於解決以下三個部分的各種關鍵技術難題。 在第一部分，我們考慮電動車的充電截止時間被提前指定的情況。在這種情況下，根據具體的應用場景，充電控制的主要挑戰源於多種不確定性參數的影響，比如動態電價、間歇性的分佈式發電、可變的非電動車電能需求和隨機調頻信號等等（下文中被統稱為I型不確定性）。對於這種情況，傳統的有限時段馬爾可夫決策過程模型往往只能得到非平穩的充電策略，從而在實踐中很難得到應用; 此外，由於眾所周知的“維數災難”這一問題，該情況下最優策略的計算往往非常複雜。為了解決上述的問題，我們將提出一個新的具有機會約束的隨機最短路模型。基於此模型，我們將證明最優平穩充電策略的存在。同時，我們將會提出一種高效的異步並行迭代算法。 在第二部分，我們考慮一個更為普遍的情況，即電動車的充電截止時間沒有被提前指定（我們稱這種類型的不確定性為II 型不確定性）。這是一個非常具有挑戰性的問題，因為如果不考慮這種II型不確定性，僅僅基於I型不確定性所獲得的最優平穩充電策略可能會被隨機地終止或截斷，從而將極有可能導致前面所得到的最優充電策略變成次優的充電策略。為此，根據所提出的機會約束的隨機最短路模型，我們進一步引進了一個聯合機會約束，從而去保證在截止時間不確定的情況下，電動車的充電需求可以被高概率地滿足。針對這個模型，我們將提出相應的具有風險意識的最優平穩充電策略。此外，更為重要的是，當充電截止時間的概率分佈沒有給定時，我們將進一步研究魯棒的充電策略，從而使得風險和回報達到最優的權衡的同時，去保證該充電策略對充電截止時間分佈的擾動具有魯棒性。 在第三部分，基於上述理論分析，我們將探討一種新型的V2G執行機制。相比於傳統概念的V2G，我們所提出的V2G機制不需要電動車去放電，因此實現起來將會更加的簡單友好。具體而言，該項目旨在提出將多個電動車等價於一個大電池模型之間的條件。在此大電池模型和前面所述的受約束控制的隨機最短路充電模型的基礎上，我們將提出一個魯棒的電網調頻方案，該方案將在電動車聚合器和電力公司之間提前建立一個離線的用電合同。基於此用電合同，我們將進一步提供一個高效的、在線的並且經過嚴格性能分析的電動車充電功率分配策略。

16210215.label: Realisation of objectives
16210215.value: (1) Realization of Objective 1: The Objective 1 of this project is to propose optimal charging policies for electric vehicles (EVs) with fixed (i.e., deterministic) deadlines. Towards this end, we have addressed the following aspects to complete this Objective 1: First, when the charging deadlines and requirements of all the EVs are given, we proposed a novel model for the EV coordinated discrete charging problem. Specifically, most of the existing work optimistically consider the EV charging rate as a continuous variable and implicitly ignore the capacity limitation in distribution transformers, which both have great impact on the efficiency and stability of practical grid operation. Towards a more realistic setting, we proposed to model the EV coordinated discrete charging problem as two successive binary optimization problems. The first one was designed to achieve a desired aggregate load profile (e.g., valley-filling profile) at the distribution grid level while considering the capacity constraints of distribution transformers. Leveraging the properties of separable convex function and total unimodularity, the first problem was transformed into an equivalent linear program, which can be solved efficiently and optimally. The second problem aims to minimize the total number of on-off switchings of all the EVs’ charging profiles while preserving the optimality of the former problem. We proved that the second problem is NP-hard and proposed a heuristic algorithm to approximately achieve our target in an iterative manner. Case studies confirm the validity of our proposed scheduling methods and indicate our algorithm’s potential for real-time implementations. Second, we further extended our above model to account for multiple types of uncertainties and flexibilities associated with elastic loads (e.g., EV charging loads). The uncertainty of renewable energy sources (RES) is traditionally handled by controllable generators to balance the real time wind power deviation. As the demand side management develops, the flexibility of aggregate loads such as the EV charging loads can be leveraged to mitigate the negative impact of the wind power. In view of this, we studied the problem of how to exploit the multi-dimensional flexibility of elastic EV charging loads to balance the trade-off between a low generation cost and a low system risk related to the wind curtailment and the power deficiency. These risks are captured by the Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR). Also, unlike most of the existing studies, the uncertainty set of the wind power output in our model is not fixed. By contrast, it is undetermined and co-optimized based on the available load flexibility. We have successfully transformed the original optimization problem into a convex one using surrogate affine approximation such that it can be solved efficiently. In case studies, we applied our model on a six-bus transmission network and demonstrated that flexible load aggregators can help to determine the optimal admissible region for the wind power deviations. In summary, Objective 1 of this project has been completed. (100%) (2) Realization of Objective 2: The focus of Objective 2 is to study risk-aware optimal and robust energy refueling policies for EVs with both uncertain market price and uncertain deadlines. First, motivated by the urgent demand for EV fast refueling technologies, battery swapping and charging stations (BSCSs) are envisioned as promising solutions. However, inappropriate battery charging operation in BSCSs not only incurs unnecessarily high charging cost but also threatens the reliability of the power grid. Therefore, we investigated optimal charging policies for a single BSCS to minimize its charging cost while ensuring the quality-of-service for EVs. Leveraging the novel queueing network model, we proposed to formulate the charging operation problem as a constrained Markov decision process and derived the optimal policy by the standard Lagrangian method and dynamic programming. To avoid the curse of dimensionality in practical large-scale systems, we further analyzed the structure of the optimal policy and transformed the dynamic programming procedure into an equivalent threshold optimization problem with a discrete separable convex objective function. Numerical results validated our theoretical analysis and the computational efficiency of our proposed algorithms. Second, with the increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources (RESs), it becomes increasingly challenging to maintain the supply-demand balance of power systems by solely relying on the generation side. To combat the volatility led by the uncertain RESs, demand-side management by leveraging the multi-dimensional flexibility (MDF) of EV energy refueling has been recognized as an economic and efficient approach. Thus, it is important to integrate MDF into existing power systems. Towards this end, we proposed an enhanced day-ahead energy market, where the MDFs of aggregate loads are traded to minimize the generation cost and mitigate the volatility of locational marginal prices (LMPs) in the transmission network. In the proposed model, we explicitly captured the negative impact of the uncertainty from RESs on the day-ahead market by a chance-constrained economic dispatch problem (CEDP). Meanwhile, we have proposed a bidding mechanism for the MDF of the aggregate loads and combined this mechanism into the CEDP for the day-ahead market. Through multiple case studies, we demonstrated that MDF from load aggregators (e.g., EV aggregators) can reduce the volatility of LMPs. In addition, we identified the values of the different flexibilities in the MDF bids, which provide useful insights into the design of more complex MDF markets. In summary, Objective 2 of this project has been finished. (100%) (3) Realization of Objective 3: The focus of Objective 3 is on the demand-side frequency regulation using flexible loads such as EVs and thermal systems in buildings. We have addressed the following aspects to complete Objective 3: First, with the successful integration of renewable energy sources into the grid, the volatility of supply in the system will increase. Consequently, the mismatch between the power supply and demand may occur frequently, and lead to frequency deviation from its nominal value. To avoid this scenario, demand-side flexibility has been widely considered to provide frequency regulation services. Towards this end, we focused on the flexibility of thermal systems in buildings and proposed a hierarchical performance-based demand-response market with a three-step algorithm to model the interactions among three entities: the Independent System Operator (ISO), aggregators, and end-users. Numerical results have showed that the performance-based allocation of frequency reserve can be a good scheme to motivate participants to respond accurately to the real-time frequency regulation signal. Second, we proposed a novel EV charging scheduling mechanism by controlling active and reactive charging power of EVs to provide joint voltage and frequency regulation (JVFR) in the distribution network. The objective of the scheduling problem is to minimize the net cost of the distribution system operator (DSO) for operating the distribution grid in the presence of both wind-based renewable generation and EV charging stations. We tested the method on a 34-bus radial distribution network for different levels of VAR requirements of wind DG units to demonstrate the feasibility and performance of the proposed JVFR approach. The simulation results showed that this JVFR greatly reduces the cost of DSO in comparison with Volt-VAR Optimization (VVO) technique, which is traditionally used to optimize voltage and minimize losses of a distribution network. In summary, Objective 3 of this project has been completed. (100%)

16210215.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210215.value: First, we have proposed a realistic model for the coordinated discrete charging of electric vehicles (EVs). The model consists of two successive binary optimization problems. Leveraging the properties of separable convex function and total unimodularity, the first problem was transformed into an equivalent linear program. For the second one, we have proved its NP-hardness and proposed a heuristic algorithm to approximately achieve our target in an iterative manner. Moreover, we further extended the model to exploit the elastic EV charging loads to balance the trade-off between a low generation cost and a low system risk (which is captured by the conditional value-at-risk). The research outcomes of this part have been published in journal papers [1, 8, 9] listed in Part C. Second, we have proposed optimal charging policies for a single battery swapping and charging station (BSCS) to minimize its charging cost while ensuring the quality-of-service for EVs. Leveraging the novel mixed queueing network model, we proposed to formulate the charging operation problem as a constrained Markov Decision Process and derived the optimal policy by the standard Lagrangian method and dynamic programming. To avoid the curse of dimensionality in practical large-scale systems, we further analyzed the structure of the optimal policy and transformed the dynamic programming procedure into an equivalent threshold optimization problem with a discrete separable convex objective function. The research outcomes of this part have been published in journal papers [2, 4, 5, 6, 7] listed in Part C. Third, we have proposed new market mechanisms and control strategies for frequency regulation in smart grids. In particular, we proposed a hierarchical demand-response market with a three-step algorithm to model the interactions among three entities: the Independent System Operator (ISO), aggregators, and end-users (e.g., EVs). The flexibility from the end-users is aggregated in step 1 and a robust optimization approach is examined to improve the user’s decision under the electricity price uncertainty. To model the interaction between the ISO and aggregators in step 2, a bi-level optimization problem was then proposed. In step 3, each aggregator allocates its successful trading reserve among end-users based on their performance score. The research outcomes of this part have been published by journal paper [3] and conference paper [2] listed in Part C.

16210215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210215.value: This project mainly focused on the optimal and robust charging control of electric vehicles, with applications to frequency regulation and voltage regulation in the demand-side of power grids. The problem of how to integrate the demand-side charging strategies with the existing power generation and dispatch strategies in the generation side has not been fully investigated. In practical power systems, when the electricity generation is more relying on renewable energy, the charging strategies of electric vehicles in the demand side should be substantially redesigned. Another problem that needs further development is the situation when electric vehicles are owned by different self-interested agents. In practice, it is not easy to incentivize all the electric vehicles to behave in a certain way such that a desired system-wide objective can be achieved. Therefore, we need to design market mechanisms, with appropriate incentive and pricing schemes, such that all the self-interested agents can act individually for their own benefits, but ultimately lead to a desired system-wide objective, e.g., to minimize the total electricity generation cost or carbon emission, etc.

16210215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210215.value: Currently, charging infrastructures to support electric vehicles are extensively being deployed all over the world. Motivated by this trend, this project primarily concerns how to transfer a certain amount of energy into an electric vehicle’s battery within a fixed or uncertain period; and ii) how to optimize the reward/cost associated with the process of energy transfer by considering the potential impact on the economic operation and stability of power grids. Towards this end, this project has proposed multiple models and algorithms that can be used for controlling and optimizing the charging processes of electric vehicles. Meanwhile, this project has also proposed novel models and market mechanisms to aggregate a large number of electric vehicles to provide services to improve the stability and economic efficiency of the power grid. The outcomes of this project can lead to rich insights into the planning and operation of power grids with and increasing number of electric vehicles.

16210415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210415.value: 物聯網將器件、機器、感測器以及其他的物體連接到網際網路中，這樣它們就能夠稱為我們資訊網路的一部分。物聯網有著巨大的潛力來徹底變革我們監測身體健康、環境、基礎設施的方式並且帶來效率、性能、服務上的提高。物聯網的一個獨特之處在於它有著非常豐富多樣的應用範圍， 包括了各種各樣的環境與專業上的應用。例如，基於無線射頻識別技術的存貨控制就和使用藍牙技術的可穿戴感測器或者海洋參數監測有著很不同的實現方法。因為物聯網的多樣性，沒有任何一個物聯網系統可以被期望能夠涵蓋所有的物聯網應用。因此，隨著應用與環境種類的增加，物聯網的發展需要經歷更多的挑戰。 在本次計畫中，我們考慮物聯網的一個獨特的應用，即自來水公司監測他們的水管網系統。特別地，我們想要探索利用水管無線聲波信號通訊來監測城市水管網路系統狀態的可能性。我們計畫使用水管作為一個聲波波導來傳輸適當地調製的聲波，這樣就能通過水管來提供通訊。這樣的通訊系統可以提高監測和探測例如水洩漏（在全世界大多數供水系統中，20%的水損失是由洩漏引起的） 、水品質和能量效率（城市水管網系統消耗大量的電力）的能力。儘管存在其他可能的通訊技術，比如說無線射頻通訊，但是這些技術不能夠應對某些特定的環境，比如說深埋在地下的金屬水管。所以說水管無線聲波通訊可以提供有效的可供選擇的通訊技術來補充其他的通訊技術。實現該技術將面臨以下挑戰：水管聲波通道模型、雜訊和干擾的特性描述的建立，實體層通訊技術以及適合獨特的水管通道的網路技術的發展。我們將利用無線通訊中高級技術來解決這些挑戰並且決定哪些技術是最適合水管通訊問題的。具體的性能估計，比如說可能的位元速率及其範圍，將會被計算來支援系統的發展。這項研究的長期重要性在於它能夠引導新型通訊技術的發展，使得新穎的物聯網應用得以發展。

16210415.label: Realisation of objectives
16210415.value: All three objectives have been met at the completion of this project. For the first objective (objective 1) we have developed a comprehensive channel model based on simulations and experimental measurements and have published our findings [J1,J3,C1,C2,C3]. We have found that rigid pipe waveguide models are not useful for pipelines filled with water and that an elastic pipe wall model must be used. This is important even for seemingly rigid pipelines made from steel and is due to the high density of water. One of the interesting characteristics of this channel is that its properties vary significantly as a function of frequency and therefore communication methods that can adapt to this are needed. In addition, we have found that the possible communication range in the types of pipeline we have considered is around 50 m. Furthermore, we have developed models for the channel acoustic noise in the pipeline models. These show that in laboratory settings with steady flow the noise is Gaussian distributed. However in transient water flow we have found that the most appropriate noise model follows the alpha-stable distribution with alphas ranging from 1.6 to nearly 2.0. Further details can be found in our published work [J3,C3]. Using the channel model developed from meeting objective 1 we have looked into communication techniques to meet objective 2. We have developed an adaptive OFDM method that allocates power to subcarriers based on the delay spread of each narrowband subcarrier channel. Results have been published [J2]. Significant improvement in performance is shown when the cyclic prefix has limited length. This is important in waveguide applications where delay spread can be very large at the cutoff frequencies. We have also performed experiments to verify the proposed techniques and techniques and meet objective 3. Results from these experimental results have been included in all our publications [J1,J2,J3,C1,C2,C3]. These are used to verify the simulation models that have been developed. In particular we have shown that our adaptive OFDM technique operates satisfactorily for a steel pipeline of inner radius 6.5 cm filled with water [J2]. We have also developed methods to estimate cutoff frequencies and estimate dispersion using a communication configuration and this could also be utilized for channel estimation in adaptive OFDM experimentally [J2,J4]. Furthermore, a particularly interesting and unique finding was obtained through experimental measurements of channel acoustic noise in an operational urban water system pipeline and these are detailed in [J3]. To our knowledge these are some of the first to be published for acoustic noise for operational water supply pipelines. In particular we have found that there is significant transient water flow in urban water systems and these cause significant spikes in noise that can be modeled by alpha-stable distributions for frequencies below 20 kHz [J3]. One area of future research would be to develop acoustic communication systems optimized for alpha-stable noise rather than the conventional Gaussian noise models that are utilized.
