16210415.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210415.value: This research has three major findings. These include: 1) Acoustic communications in pipelines can be performed efficiently using a Subcarrier Delay Spread Based Adaptive OFDM system [J2]. This approach can overcome the large delay spreads of the water pipeline channel near the cutoff frequencies [J2,J4]. 2) That the water pipeline channel model must be based on an elastic pipeline channel model rather than a rigid pipeline approximation. Whereas for an air filled pipeline a rigid pipeline model is appropriate [J1,C1,C2]. 3) That acoustic noise in operational urban water supply systems follows an alpha-stable distribution with alpha ranging from 1.6 to nearly 2.0 [J3,C3]. In addition we have shown that this noise is restricted to less than the 20 kHz acoustic frequency band while for frequencies above this the noise follows a Gaussian distribution.

16210415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210415.value: The techniques we have developed demonstrate that acoustic communication in water pipelines is feasible. Several future research and development issues could be addressed. The first is the extension of the results from acoustic Gaussian noise models to alpha-stable distributed noise models. This is challenging because nearly all communication systems use the Gaussian noise model assumption. The second is to build a complete prototype of the acoustic communication system in an operational pipeline. The results obtained and demonstrated experimentally indicate that a full prototype would perform well.

16210415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210415.value: We have developed techniques that can be used to perform acoustic communication in water filled pipelines. The techniques have been demonstrated experimentally to be feasible and can provide bit rates of up to 20 kbps in a 10 kHz bandwidth channel. The importance of the results is that they can open up applications for the internet of things (IoT) in water pipelines. In particular sensors or robots could be inserted into the water pipelines to monitor water quality or assess pipeline condition, for example, and the data collected could be communicated using the acoustic communication techniques we have developed.

16210615.value: 流體整流器可以實現不同方向上的流量差異。如果流體只允許在一個方向流動, 流體整流器就叫做流體二極體。 流體整流器在微納米流動系統中有著廣泛的應用, 包括醫學, 生命科學, 和工程。目前,在微納米流動系統中, 流體流動可以通過主動或被動微閥來實現。但是主動微閥通常含有運動部件, 並需外部驅動系統。被動微閥也存在諸多問題, 它們只能在高流速下或使用特殊流體才能實現流動的方向性差異, 並且不能實現流動的二極現象。 在這個專案中,我們提出一個新的,基於複合納米通道的,無運動部件的流體整流器/二極體。複合納米通道含有兩部分, 一部分是小些尺寸的親水通道, 另一個部分是大些尺寸的疏水通道。整流的機理是基於流體在納米通道中的浸入壓和通道的尺寸, 表面特性有關。不同部分通道的尺寸和親疏水的差異會產生不同的通道入口能阻, 從而實現流體在不同方向的流動阻力, 達到整流的效果。我們將用分子動力學模擬和實驗的方法研究所提出的流體整流器的整流性能和二極性。 這種新的流體整流器對微納米系統流體流動的控制會有一定的貢獻,對微控晶片技術也會起到推動作用。

16210615.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210615.value: A nanoscale fluidic diode system using a non-uniform nanochannel has been proposed and studied through molecular dynamics simulations. It is showed that the fluidic diode allows water flows in the forward direction and blocks flows in the backward direction in a wide range of pressure drops. The pressure drop range for the fluidic diode can be varied by modifying the surface wettability, channel height, and/or the tilt angle of the channel. The fluidic diode can be used for flow control in integrated micro- and nanofluidic devices. We have also fabricated flow rectifiers using microscale converging-diverging channels. Experiments have been conducted to investigate flow rectification effects. It is found that flow rectification was achieve when the flow rate became sufficient high. The highest diodicity, which is the flow rate ratio between the forward and backward directions, reached 1.77, which is 15-54% higher than previous microfluidic rectifiers for Newtonian fluids. An expression for the diodicity is developed based on two scaling laws for the flow resistances in the forward and backward directions. Numerical simulations are also performed to confirm the experiments. In the project, five journal articles have been published. Most of them are in prestigious journals.

16210615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210615.value: Flow rectifiers using non-uniform channels have been developed. The flow rectification phenomenon observed in micro- and nanochannels can be used to control fluid flows in lap-on-a-chip systems for various applications, such as chemical reactions and bioanalysis. We will continue to study flow rectification, develop new flow rectifiers with better performance.

16210615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210615.value: In this project, micro- and nanoscale flow rectifiers, which generate direction-dependent flow rates, have been developed. These flow rectifiers allow the flow rate in one direction to be higher than that in the opposite direction such that they can be used to regulate fluid flows, especially at small scales.

16211015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211015.value: We propose to develop models for learning of the optokinetic reflex (OKR) and the vestibular ocular reflex (VOR) in vertebrates, and to implement them on a mobile robot platform with an active binocular vision system. These two reflexes ensure image stabilization during relative motion between the environment and the observer. They are adaptive, since they must change in response to changes in the physical configuration of and neural processing performed by the organism as it matures. By developing on-line learning algorithms inspired by this adaptability observed in biological systems, this work will enable robotic systems to exhibit increased robustness to perturbations in their configuration, as well as to improve their performance over time based on their interactions with the environment. While past work in this area has focused on single camera systems, the proposed study will focus on binocular vision systems, since binocular input provides important cues about the absolute distance to objects in the environment. In addition, because the proposed algorithms are based closely upon what is currently known about the neural pathways supporting these reflexes, this study will lead to insight into the factors underlying abnormal development of these reflexes in vertebrates with deficits in binocular vision due to conditions such as strabismus (crossed eyes). In the long term, this work may lead to more adaptive robotic systems, as well as suggestions for effective therapeutic interventions for binocular developmental disorders. 我們提出要開發一個基於脊椎動物的視動反射和前庭眼反射學習的模型，此模型會實現在一個擁有雙目視覺系統的移動機器人平台。在觀察者和周邊環境有相對移動的情況下，這兩種反射確保了圖像的穩定。這兩種反射具有自適應性，會根據物理設定的變化和生物神經處理系統的發育成熟而改變。自適應性是受到觀察生物系統的啟發；通過開發在線學習算法，此系統可以增加機器人受到干擾時的魯棒性，同時也可以使其在與環境互動的過程中改進其性能。此前該領域相關的工作專注於單目視覺系統，因為雙目的輸入提供了關於環境中物體絕對距離的提示，我們提出的方案將專注於雙目視覺系統。此外，因為我們提出的算法是基於現有的關於這兩種反射神經通路的知識，此研究對於兩種反射不正常的發育也可以提供洞見，這其中包含在斜視情況下產生的雙目視覺的缺陷。長遠來看，這項工作會構建一個自適應更強的機器人系統，同時也會對有效治療雙目發育障礙提出建議。

16211015.label: Realisation of objectives
16211015.value: We achieved the first objective by developing a neuromorphic algorithm for learning the optokinetic reflex (OKR) in binocular vision systems. The OKR stabilizes the visual input as an agent moves in space based on visual input. Our model follows the neural pathways known to underlie the OKR in primates. Visual input from the two eyes is combined at the visual cortex. The visual cortex in the left hemisphere processes information from the right visual field and vice versa for the visual cortex in the right hemisphere. The left and right nuclei of the optic track (NOT) combine information from the two hemispheres, and provide input to the contralateral vestibular nuclei (VN). The motor neurons in the left VN control the medial rectus muscle of the left eye and the lateral rectus muscle of the right eye, which drive rightward rotation of the eyes. Similarly, the right VN drives leftward rotation. In the model, input images from the left and right eye at a coarse and fine scale, modelling the peripheral and foveal regions of the retina, are divided into square patches. Corresponding patches from the two eyes are concatenated and passed to sparse coders modelling the processing by the left and right visual cortices. The outputs of the two sparse coders are then concatenated (modelling the NOT) and input to an eye control neural network (modelling the VN). Both the basis vectors of the sparse coder and the weights of the eye control neural network are initialized randomly. They are learned simultaneously as the agent interacts with the environment, through a combination of unsupervised learning (for the sparse coder) and reinforcement learning (for the neural network). The reward maximized by the reinforcement learner is the negative reconstruction error of the sparse coder. We compared the predictions of this OKR model to the results of experiments on biological systems. At birth, the OKR in primates is undeveloped (i.e. its gain is close to zero), but it evolves over time so that the OKR gain is eventually close to one. We observed a similar evolution in our system. We also found that the binocular basis vectors in the sparse coder to be qualitatively similar to the binocular receptive fields of primate visual cortical cells. We achieved the second objective by implementing this OKR learning algorithm on an Adept Mobilerobots Research PatrolBot affixed with a pan-tilt head unit from Directed Perception, which was used to generate head movements. A Point Grey Research Bumblebee stereo camera system mounted on the pan-tilt unit provided the visual input. During training, the motion of the robot was controlled manually using a joystick. We collected sequences of synchronized sensory data, which includes camera images, angular rates of the head and the translational and rotational velocities of the wheels of the robot for training. We found that the gain of the OKR of the real system also evolved from zero at the start to around 0.9 at steady state. This was sufficient to ensure that the image was well stabilized. We achieved the third objective by developing a model of the development of the vestibular ocular reflex (VOR) in binocular vision systems. Like the OKR, the VOR serves to stabilize the visual image as the agent moves in space. However, it uses head movement information as sensed by the vestibular organs, rather than by visual information. The model architecture follows the known neural pathways mediating the VOR. The inputs to the VOR algorithm are a high pass filtered version of the head rotational velocity, as sensed by the vestibular organs. A neural network maps the vestibular input to the rotational acceleration of the two eyes. The network weights are learned during interaction with the environment through reinforcement learning. The reward maximized during learning is the same negative reconstruction error used in the OKR model. The basis vectors of the sparse coder are learned during interaction with the environment, simultaneously with the weights of the eye rotation control neural network. We compared the predictions of the VOR model with the results of experiments on biological systems. In particular, we learned the VOR response assuming different correlations between the visual and vestibular cues, which we controlled by varying the movement of the head and of the visual target. In humans, the gain of the VOR is close to 0.6. We found that the gain of the VOR learned by our system was close to 0.6 when the correlation coefficient was 0.34. We completed the fourth objective by implementing the VOR system on the same mobile robot used for testing the OKR system (the Adept platform described above) using the same joystick for control to collect the training data. Consistent with our simulation experiments, we found that the system was able to learn a successful VOR policy, and that the gain of the VOR policy was 0.59, which is very close to the value of 0.6 reported for humans and found in our simulaton results. These results demonstrate that the system is robust enough to operate in real environments. We completed the final objective by combining the OKN and VOR systems together. In particular, we fed both the vestibular inputs and the visual inputs from the output of the sparse coder into the eye control neural network. This connection pattern is consistent with the neural pathways underlying the OKN and VOR in primate visual systems, where the visual and vestibular inputs are combined in the vestibular nuclei. At the start of training, the neural network weights were initialized so that the VOR gain was close to one and the OKR gain was close to zero, consistent with the gains found in human infants. As the model agent develops through interaction with the environment, the network weights evolve so that at steady state, the OKN gain is close to one and the VOR gain is close to 0.6, as observed in human adults. This suggests that the model captures the developmental nature of the joint evolution of OKN and VOR in humans. We also compared the combined responses of VOR and OKR to those observed by Schweigart et al. in humans, and found our model predictions to be similar to their observations. Our model also generated two testable predictions. First, we predict that the VOR gain in adults is determined by the correlation between visual and vestibular cues. Second, our model predicts how changes in the delays and time constants of neural processing will affect the gain. G. Schweigart, T. Mergner, I. Evdokimidis, S. Morand, W. Becker, Gaze stabilization by optokinetic reflex (OKR) and vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR) during active head rotation in man. Vision Research 37, 1643 (1997).

16211015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211015.value: In this project, we have developed algorithms that enable a robotic agent to learn how to control its camera to stabilize the visual image in the presence of relative motion between the agent and its environment. This relative motion can be caused by motion of the agent, which can be sensed by both vestibular and visual inputs, and/or motion of the environment, which can be detected only by visual input. Disentangling these two sources of motion and their dependency on the vestibular and visual signals is very challenging due to the high dimensionality of the visual signal, ambiguities in the visual signal due to perspective projection, the need to integrate information between different coordinate systems, and the time-varying nature of those coordinate transformations due to behavioral or developmental changes in the state of the agent. As described in [C.9.1], our algorithms enable the agent to learn and to calibrate this stabilization behavior without external supervision, much in the same way that human infants do, by exploiting and modelling sensori-motor contingencies: reliable relationships between actions and consequent changes in sensory signals. Our approach, dubbed Active Efficient Coding, is the first model of the perception-action cycle for human gaze control that can be applied directly to input images and results in predictions of the precise gaze trajectory. Previous models were more high level and abstract. The perception-action cycle is a circular process by which initial sensory inputs lead to hypotheses about the state of the actor and the environment, which lead to actions, which lead to new sensory inputs enabling the refinement of those hypotheses. As described in [C.9.2], integrating initial gaze estimates with information about the 3D environment can lead to improved gaze estimates. As described in [C.8.1] and [C.8.2], accurate models of human gaze can be used to improve robot performance. The work of [C.9.3] and [C.9.4] describes how human gaze models and the extraction of visual motion information can be integrated with environmental context.

16211015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211015.value: The perception-action cycle underlies most goal-directed behavior in biological agents. The model of the perception action cycle developed in this paper can be extended in a number of ways. For example, in the algorithm developed in this proposal, information from coarse and fine scales covering foveal and peripheral regions of the visual field is combined by concatenation. While this is simple, it has the drawback that the periphery may contain multiple objects, which can result in contradictory information. In an ongoing project sponsored by the RGC GRF, we are investigating more complex ways of combining information from the fovea and the periphery. Another direction in which the model developed in this proposal can be extended is to apply it to other sensory modalities besides vision. We have submitted a proposal to the RGC GRF, which is currently under consideration, that seeks to apply the Active Efficient Coding framework to model echolocation in bats. This proposed work would be conducted in collaboration with Prof. Cindy Moss, a neuroscientist at Johns Hopkins University, who has expertise in bat echolocation.

16211015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211015.value: Developmental robotic models of biological systems are open-ended embodied learning systems that mimic the way an infant acquires new skills and knowledge through interaction with the environment. Not only may these models enable robots to be more flexible and adaptive than they are currently, they may also provide scientific insight into the mechanisms of infant development. This project developed a neurally plausible framework modeling the development of the visual-vestibular interaction (VVI) in humans. Visual and vestibular mechanisms help to stabilize retinal images during relative motion between the observer and the environment. The interaction between the two mechanisms adapts during development. Based upon biological findings, our model integrates visual and vestibular inputs and accounts for the co-development of sensory processing and motor action. The properties of our model are both qualitatively and quantitatively consistent with a number of findings on the interaction between visual and vestibular systems. Thus, it provides a unified account that ties together a number of disparate findings. It also generates a number of testable predictions about the effects of the input statistics and the effect of delay on the cue integration between the two systems.

16211615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211615.value: With the popular of smart phones, tablets and digital cameras, numerous pictures are taken by various devices every day. Despite the continuing evolution of advanced sensors, autofocus and anti-shake technologies, photos taken at night are often blurry due to the long exposures. A slight camera shake can induce annoying blur effects since low-speed shutters and long exposures are required under dim lighting conditions. As a result, night image deblurring is in significant demand and an important asset for photography. Image deblurring has been extensively studied in the past decades and has achieved satisfactory results when dealing with blurry images with salient structures. Unfortunately, these schemes often fail to deblur night images. Since the saturated pixels in night images, where the real pixel value is usually large than 255 while cameras fail to record such overlarge value, break the linear convolution formulation that most schemes assume. In addition, night images usually exhibit low contrast, which hinders kernel estimation as it highly relies on salient image structures, and the low signal-to-noise ratio in night images further increases the difficulty of kernel estimation. Consequently, deblurring night images is a challenging problem involving troublesome saturated regions, low contrast as well as heavy noise. In this proposal, we intend to investigate night images deblurring through separable kernel. Specifically, we propose to explore theoretical model for flexible transformation between conventional matrix-form kernel and new separable kernel, utilize the shape of outstanding bright curves in saturated regions for spatially invariant kernel initialization, theoretical analysis of local minimum problem and joint low-level and high-level priors, explore robust depth information for night images deblurring, and heavy noise suppression for night images deblurring using multi-channel color correlations. We hope to deliver a better solution for the deblurring problem in this research plan. The theories and algorithms to be developed can potentially further our understanding of the blur effect and the value of depth image in image processing problems. We believe, with a better solution for the deblurring problem, everyone can shoot and get sharp photos much easier than ever before. Then large swathes of the photographic world would change very rapidly. 伴隨著智能手機，平板電腦和數碼相機等的流行，通過这些手持設備获取的照片日益增长。即使傳感器技术及物理防抖方案在持續發展，在昏暗的光線條件下的低速快門（長時間曝光）拍攝的夜间照片依然无法避免模糊效应，甚至微不可查的相機抖動會誘發惱人的模糊效应。在過去幾十年，圖像去模糊算法在处理具有显著性结构的图像上取得较为滿意的結果。不幸的是，這些算法往往不能处理夜景模糊圖像。具体来说，夜景图片中的过饱和区域打破了传统的去模糊線性卷積假设。此外，夜間圖像通常具有低對比度，破坏了传统算法高度依賴於圖像結構的假设，並且低信噪比進一步增大了模糊核函数估計的難度。因此，夜景照片去模糊是一個颇具挑戰性的問題，涉及到处理过飽和區域，低對比度以及高噪聲。在該申请书中，我們拟研究基于可分离卷积核函数的夜景图片去模糊。具體來說，我們拟探索常規矩陣形式核函数与可分離核函数之间的轉換理論模型，并利用夜景图片过飽和区域中形狀轮廓分明的明亮曲線作为先验，对模糊核函数的估计进行初始化。其次，我们拟探究去模糊算法极易陷入的局部最小值問題，相应的提出低層与高層先验相融合的算法。最后，我们拟探索夜景模式下鲁棒的深度信息对夜間圖像去模糊的辅助，引入多通道顏色互相关性，解决夜間圖像的高噪声问题。

16211615.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211615.value: Deblurring saturated night images are a challenging problem because such images have low contrast combined with heavy noise and saturated regions. Unlike the deblurring schemes that discard saturated regions when estimating blur kernels, this project proposes novel schemes to deduce blur kernels from saturated regions via a novel kernel representation and advanced algorithms. Our key technical contribution is the proposed function-form representation of blur kernels, which regularizes existing matrix-form kernels using three functional components: 1) trajectory; 2) intensity; and 3) expansion. From automatically detected saturated regions, their skeleton, brightness, and width are ﬁtted into the corresponding three functional components of blur kernels. Such regularization signiﬁcantly improves the quality of kernels deduced from saturated regions. Second, we propose an energy minimizing algorithm to select and assign the deduced function-form kernels to partitioned image regions as the initialization for non-uniform deblurring. Finally, we convert the assigned function-form kernels into matrix form for more detailed estimation in a multi-scale deconvolution. Experimental results show that our methods outperform existing schemes on challenging real examples.

As a result, night image deblurring is in signiﬁcant demand and an important asset for photography.

16211715.label: Project Objectives
16211715.value: To design and implement an online measurement mechanism: We plan to capture the workload characteristics in cloud datacenter networks where interactive applications running on top of new data analytic frameworks, e.g., Spark. We aim to design a lightweight monitoring framework that actively probes the resource availability of all the machines in a datacenter, including the response times and traffic patterns for different categories of graph parallel applications. To design a distributed scheduling framework: We propose a bandwidth-aware scheduling framework, which aims to achieve sub-second performance, scalability and fairness. Job-level schedulers directly determine when and where to schedule each task in the DAG of a given job based on the bandwidth on access links and the queue length of CPUs. Coordination among schedulers aims to avoid resource races and unbalanced allocation. To validate our scheduling framework in commercial cloud platforms: we plan to run real applications on top of Spark by writing a scheduling plugin to replace its native centralized scheduler. To guarantee that our experimental observations are convincing, jobs will be produced by running real-world data analytic applications such as personalized web query and iterative machine learning algorithms, in addition to synthetic benchmarks.

16211715.label: Realisation of objectives
16211715.value: With the wide deployment of data-parallel computing frameworks, it has become a norm to run data analytics applications in a large cluster of machines. They accelerate the processing of large datasets by dividing a job into multiple tasks, and by distributing them to different machines across the cluster for parallel execution. Under the data-parallel computing paradigm, a job typically involves multiple computation stages, where tasks in a downstream stage wait for the intermediate results to be produced and transmitted from their upstream stages. Take MapReduce as an example, intermediate results are transferred from mapper tasks to reducer tasks with potentially enormous amount of data. Consequently, the data transfer times have significant impact on the overall performances in terms of both job completion time and system resource utilization. With the proliferation of in-memory data-parallel computing frameworks such as Spark, it enables in-memory sharing across pipelined tasks and mitigating the amount of data transfers. Yet, for tasks dependent upon a large number of other tasks in upstream stages, network transfer time is still one of the main factors affecting the performance. This project focused on the design of bandwidth-aware scheduling and resource allocation strategies for big data processing and analytic applications. The main motivation for this research is the fact that there exist large volume data transfers in the current data-parallel computing frameworks, which can substantially impact the performances. We observe that a typical production cluster hosts multiple types of data-parallel frameworks, running a mix of background batch jobs and interactive query jobs on a common dataset. In such production environments, network transfer times are critical contributing factors to job completion times. For instance, on average, MapReduce jobs spend over 30% of the runtime in data transfer alone. How to incorporate network transfer time into a job scheduler turned out to be a challenging problem, particularly because of two reasons, (1) the existing cluster schedulers either only considered computation resources (such as CPU and memory) when assigning tasks to cluster nodes, or emphasized network transfer time with a sole focus on network bandwidth resources. Without proper coordination, such isolated resource allocation strategies can lead to substantial under-utilized resources, caused by the lack of balance when both computation and network resources are considered. For example, if a network-intensive task is assigned to a CPU core on which no other tasks are running, the CPU core is left mostly idle, since data transfers over the network would be the primary performance bottleneck. (2) The multi-resource scheduling policies in theory have the potential in rectifying such an imbalance in resource utilization across multiple types. However, in production clusters and data-parallel frameworks, there are several practical limitations that make it difficult to apply such multi-resource scheduling policies. Firstly, it is difficult to obtain any prior knowledge of the resource demands in analytics jobs, background or interactive, since resource demands are not specified in job descriptions; even when they can be specified, these are inaccurate estimates that can only provide some hints and guidelines. At the runtime, neither network transfer times nor computation times are deterministic or predictable when co-located tasks share cluster resources. Secondly, the existing multi-resource scheduling strategies are typically designed with a “clean-slate” approach, engineered to replace the current data-parallel frameworks, rather than complementing them. In another word, they cannot directly be applicable in the existing data-parallel frameworks. In this project, we examined the workload characteristics in cloud datacenter networks, where interactive applications are running on top of new data analytic frameworks – Objective 1. We showed that the existing schedulers either only considered computation resources or focused only on the network transfer times. Through rigorous analysis and extensive evaluation, we showed that without proper coordination, such isolated resource allocation strategies can lead to significantly under-utilized resources. In our proposed scheduler, we took a completely different approach by designing a new bandwidth-aware task scheduler that aims to complement and improve, instead of replacing the current scheduling policies in existing data-parallel frameworks, with a coordinated focus on both computation and network resources – Objective 2. Specifically, our approach emphasised on predicting and rectifying the lack of balance in utilizing computation resource and network resource during runtime. The proposed scheduler does not require any prior knowledge or online estimation of the resource demands, while taking into account the requirement of each individual analytic job and the bandwidth across different links. It overcomes the resource imbalance by scheduling computation-intensive tasks (with data locality) on the same CPU core, and network-intensive tasks (without data locality) within the same executor process managed by existing data-parallel frameworks. In addition, it was designed as a plugin to the existing data-parallel frameworks, and so it can co-exist with the existing resource managers in data parallel frameworks. One of the salient features in this design is the transparency to applications, which requires no modifications to the existing programming interfaces. We have fully implemented our proposed bandwidth-aware scheduler in Spark, and extensively evaluated in testbeds with different cluster scale ranging from a few to over a hundred cluster nodes on Linode, and by utilizing a diverse range of workloads – Objective 3. In comparison to Spark, we demonstrate convincing evidence that our proposed bandwidth-aware scheduler improves CPU utilization in the cluster, mitigates the lack of balance when multiple resources are considered, while at the same time reducing the average job completion time.

16211715.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211715.value: We first examined the workload characteristics and showed that the unbalanced utilization of computation and network resources is the key factor leading to a reduced level of overall resource utilization. Scheduling jobs with multiple resource constraints is a classical problem in the operation research, where the primary objective is to ensure equal utilization of all the type of resources. In the context of cluster computing and data-parallel frameworks, however, the resource demands cannot be explicitly quantified. We focused on two types of resources: bandwidth on access links and computing cycles on CPU cores. A cluster node is considered to be resource balanced, if the utilization of all of its resources are the same. However, this requires a runtime resource monitoring mechanism, which is practically inaccessible. In addition, cluster nodes often have heterogeneous resources, in which some nodes have more powerful CPUs, whereas others have faster network access. Given a set of tasks, the resource utilization in the two types of nodes can be very different. This is further complicated that jobs running in a cluster have diversified and dynamic demands for different types of resources. It is thus impractical to impose equal utilization as the standard for a balanced use of multiple resource types. Since the resource imbalance mainly comes from running a network-bound or a computation-bound task alone on a cluster node, the intuition is that a scheduler should co-locate these two types of tasks to correct such imbalance. Given a set of resource unbalanced nodes and a set of candidate tasks, the problem of selecting the best tasks to maximize the aggregated performance can be formulated as a classical Multiple Knapsack Problem, which can be solved through polynomial-time approximation algorithms. We designed our bandwidth-aware scheduler as a plugin to each application in different frameworks, where each application can adopt its own customized scheduling strategies to place tasks onto cluster nodes. Our scheduler aggressively examines these placement decisions to identify if there exists a lack of resource balance, and adjusts these placement decisions by adding tasks to those cluster nodes without resource balance. We conducted extensive experiments on the Linode cluster (running Spark 1.4.0 together with Hadoop 2.6) with different types of workloads, which demonstrated the performance improvement in reducing job completion times and better resource utilization.

16211715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211715.value: This project has focused on scheduling for big data processing and analytic jobs which takes into account the network resource constraint. Through series of studies, we show that this can improve both the cluster resource utilization and individual job performance. Cluster scheduler serves as a critical component to data-parallel frameworks in datacenters. Ideally, a scheduler should provide predictable performance with guarantees on the maximal job completion delay, while at the same time ensuring the minimal mean response time. Practically however, performance predictability and optimality are often conflicting with each other. The results often are a plethora of scheduling policies that either achieve predictable performance at the expense of long response times (e.g., max-min fairness), or run the risk of starving some jobs to obtain the minimal mean response time we are working a set of new schedulers, which aim to minimize the mean job response time while achieving the predictable performance. One of the key ideas is to ensure that jobs are guaranteed to complete within a small constant time of the predictable performance, while obtaining the minimum mean responses time.

16211715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211715.value: The data-parallel computing frameworks such as MapReduce and Spark serve as important foundations for big data processing in cloud datacenters. These accelerate the processing of large datasets by dividing a job into multiple tasks, and by distributing them to different machines across a cluster for parallel execution. One key characteristic in such computing paradigms is the communication in transferring intermediate results between consecutive computing stages. The significance of this project and its outcomes are: (1) we designed and implemented a new network-aware task scheduler that complements and improves the scheduling in existing data-parallel frameworks, with a coordinated emphasis on both computation and network resources; (2) the proposed scheduler predicts and rectifies the lack of balance in utilizing computation and network resources at runtime, without requiring any prior knowledge or online estimation on the demands; (3) it coordinates the resource allocation for both computation-intensive and network-intensive tasks; (4) the scheduler is designed as a plugin and can be readily applied in the existing data-parallel frameworks, while remaining transparent to applications; (5) we implemented the scheduler in Spark, and conducted extensive evaluation using a variety of benchmark to demonstrate its performance improvements.

16211815.label: Realisation of objectives
16211815.value: This project investigated a critical research problem in 5G and beyond wireless networks, namely high-dimensional channel estimation. To accommodate the exponentially growing mobile data traffic, it is expected that next-generation wireless networks need to achieve orders of magnitude increase in the network capacity. With the rapid advancement in coding and modulation techniques, we are already approaching the Shannon limit of the per-link data rate. Thus, disruptive techniques will be needed to further increase the network capacity. Network densification, i.e., to deploy more and more radio access points, is a promising approach, as it can significantly increase the spatial reuse efficiency of the limited radio spectrum, thus increasing the network capacity. While channel estimation has been a fundamental problem in any wireless communication system, it plays a more critical role in wireless dense networks (DenseNets). With densely deployed radio access points, co-channel intercell interference becomes a more prominent problem, which will limit the capacity gain of network densification. This makes interference management to be a key supporting technique in DenseNets, but effective interference management critically depends on accurate channel state information (CSI). Meanwhile, channel estimation in wireless DenseNets becomes more challenging, as the channel dimension in DenseNets will be very large and the number of pilot symbols for estimating the channel will be much smaller than the channel dimension. Thus, it becomes an ill-posed problem. This project developed innovative channel estimation methods to address the above challenge. The essential idea is to exploit prior structure information of wireless channels, so that accurate channel estimation can be achieved with low training overheads. The exploited prior information includes sparsity of the channel in the angular domain, the spatial and temporal correlation of wireless channels, and the partial connectivity of wireless links. Correspondingly, the research objectives of this project covered three key aspects of high-dimensional channel estimation. 1) To propose effective regularizing functions to exploit prior information and develop scalable estimation algorithms; 2) To design optimal training matrices and effective feedback mechanisms; 3) To evaluate the performance of the proposed channel estimation algorithms for different system parameters. Our investigation closely followed the stated research objectives, and focused on two key network architectures, namely massive MIMO systems and cloud radio access networks (Cloud-RANs). Following is the detailed description of the realization of the objectives. • First, we developed compressive sensing (CS) based methods to exploit the channel sparsity structure in the angular domain of massive MIMO systems. While there have been several attempts to reduce the training overhead by exploiting such sparsity structures, they missed some important opportunity. Particularly, there has been little discussion about how to exploit the partial support information of these channels to achieve further overhead reductions. This additional prior information is a set of indices of the significant elements of a channel vector, and we proposed to utilize it to further improve the training efficiency. In particular, we proposed a weighted l1 minimization framework to fully exploit the structure information. Moreover, we provided a sharp estimate of the overhead size, which can be used to guide the pilot design. Extensive simulations demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed method in reducing the training overhead. This investigation addressed Research Objectives 1 to 3. • We next investigated high-dimensional channel estimation in Cloud-RANs, a cost-effective architecture for network densification. Different from massive MIMO systems, there is no sparsity structure in wireless channels of Cloud-RANs, but there exists other exploitable statistical characteristics, namely spatial-temporal correlation. We proposed to convert the available spatial and temporal prior information into appropriate convex regularizers, and developed an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) algorithm to solve the resultant large-scale high-dimensional channel estimation problem. Simulation results demonstrated that exploiting the spatial and temporal dynamics can achieve good estimation performance even with limited training resources. The proposed regularization based framework enjoys modeling flexibility, low training overhead, and computation cost scalability. This investigation was in parallel to the previous one, and it also addressed Research Objectives 1 to 3. • We have also exploited temporal correlation of wireless channels to reduce training overhead in massive MIMO systems with a large number of mobile users. A main difficulty for uplink channel estimation in such systems is that the training overhead is proportional to the number of users, and thus conventional methods can only support a limited number of users. To reduce the training overhead, or equivalently, to increase the number of admitted users, we proposed a selective uplink training method, where in each channel block only part of the users will send uplink pilots for channel training, and the channel states of the remaining users are predicted from the estimates in previous blocks, taking advantage of the channels’ temporal correlation. Based on random matrix theory, we developed an efficient algorithm to dynamically select the users to be trained within each block and determine the optimal uplink training length. This investigation addressed Research Objectives 1 and 2. • Another type of prior information about wireless channels we exploited is the network connectivity information, i.e., the knowledge of the presence of strong communication/interference links. Specifically, we proposed a novel interference management method relying only on the network connectivity information. To acquire such connectivity information incurs significant less overhead than complete CSI, and thus this method is scalable to large network sizes and is a good fit for wireless DenseNets. We formulated the sum rate maximization problem as a rank minimization problem to cancel strong interference and suppress weak interference, and developed a Riemannian trust-region algorithm to solve it. This investigation addressed Research Objectives 1 and 2. Overall, we believe that we have satisfactorily completed this project. By covering all the research objectives in the project (Research Objectives 1 to 3), we are able to produce academically and practically significant research while contributing meaningfully to the training of students in this important area (Research Objective 4). Specifically, as a result of this project, one MPhil student (Changming Li) has been trained and graduated. In addition, with fruitful research outcomes, we were able to publish 2 journal papers, as well as 3 conference papers in IEEE flagship conferences.

16211815.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211815.value: This project focused on high-dimensional channel estimation in massive MIMO and cloud radio access networks (Cloud-RANs), both of which are key technologies for 5G networks. For references, [C1] and [J1] represent conference paper #1 and journal paper #1 in Part C, respectively. • Compressive CSI Acquisition for FDD Massive MIMO: In [J1], we developed a compressive sensing based method for low-overhead channel estimation in frequency-division duplexing (FDD) massive MIMO systems. While massive MIMO is a promising technique for providing unprecedented spectral efficiency, it has been well recognized that the excessive training overhead for estimating channel side information (CSI) is a major handicap, especially for FDD massive MIMO. By incorporating statistical channel knowledge in the form of partial support information, our proposed method significantly reduces the training overhead, which has been verified by both theoretical analysis and extensive simulations. • Selective Uplink Training for Massive MIMO: In massive MIMO systems, conventional uplink training methods incur overhead that is proportional to the number of mobile users (MUs), which makes them inapplicable with dense MUs. In [C1], we proposed an innovative selective uplink training method, where in each channel block only part of the MUs will send uplink pilots for channel training. Meanwhile, the channel states of the remaining MUs are predicted from the estimates in previous blocks. It was demonstrated that the proposed training method provides significant throughput gains compared to existing methods. • CSI Acquisition in Cloud-RANs with Prior Information: In [C3, J2], we developed an effective CSI acquisition scheme for dense Cloud-RANs by exploiting spatial and temporal prior information in wireless channels. In particular, we proposed a composite convex regularizer to exploit the spatial-temporal channel dynamics, and a group-structured regularizer to exploit the temporal sparsity when there are massive devices accessing the network. Furthermore, an efficient estimation algorithm based on the operator splitting method was developed. • Interference Management with Partial CSI in Dense Wireless Networks: In dense wireless networks, interference management plays a critical role, for which the acquisition of the massive CSI becomes a main bottleneck. In [C2], we proposed a novel interference management method which only requires partial CSI, i.e., the knowledge of the presence of strong links, and statistical information of the weak links. The problem was casted as a low rank matrix completion problem, which was then solved by a Riemannian trust-region algorithm.

16211815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211815.value: This project has produced promising results on high-dimensional channel estimation in wireless dense networks (DenseNets). One direction for further research is to improve the computational and statistical efficiency of the estimation methods. Particularly, the methods proposed in this project are based on convex formulations and convex optimization algorithms. Recently, it has been shown that non-convex methods enjoy higher computational efficiency and improved statistical performance on some high-dimensional estimation problems. Thus, it is interesting to develop non-convex methods for high-dimensional channel estimation in DenseNets, to further increase the network capacity. Another important direction is to investigate high-dimensional channel estimation in new communication scenarios, notably UAV communications and vehicular communications. Mobility and the changing network topology will be major challenges in such wireless channels, and thus new methods will be needed. It will be important to exploit temporal correlation, and machine learning based methods (especially recurrent neural networks (RNNs)) will play key roles.

16211815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211815.value: The thriving mobile Internet applications have placed unprecedent pressures on wireless networks, which demand orders of magnitude increase in the network capacity of the upcoming 5G networks. Network densification, i.e., deploying more and more radio access points, stands out as a disruptive way to boost the network capacity. While the spatial reuse efficiency of the scarce radio spectrum has been greatly improved in wireless dense networks (DenseNets), the network capacity is fundamentally limited by the growing intercell interference. Effective interference management thus becomes critical, which seriously relies on accurate channel state information (CSI). Unfortunately, the CSI acquisition in DenseNets leads to a highly challenging high-dimensional estimation problem. This project developed innovate methods for high-dimensional channel estimation in wireless DenseNets. In particular, with massive MIMO and cloud radio access networks (Cloud-RANs) as typical examples, prior structure information of wireless channels, i.e., sparsity in the angular domain, spatial and temporal correlation, has been exploited to enable low-overhead channel estimation. Effective methods based on compressive sensing and regularized high-dimensional estimation have been developed. Overall, the methods developed in this project are capable to provide accurate CSI for interference management and resource allocation in wireless DenseNets, to meet the capacity requirement of 5G networks.

16212115.label: Realisation of objectives
16212115.value: Working closely with the top institutions such as UCSB and Harvard University, we have recently demonstrated high performance 1.3 µm and 1.5 µm InAs QDs lasers directly grown on (001) Si substrate. Miniaturized laser sources can benefit a wide variety of applications ranging from on-chip optical communications and data processing, to biological sensing. There is a tremendous interest in integrating these lasers with rapidly advancing silicon photonics, aiming to provide the combined strength of the optoelectronic integrated circuits and existing large-volume, low-cost silicon-based manufacturing foundries. We developed a strategic method based on the ART concept to form the nano-scale V-grooved Si substrates, by KOH or TMAH wet etching nanopatterned (001) Si substrates. Highly ordered GaAs nanowire arrays with the (111) facet planes were griwb. With an ultrathin low temperature GaAs stress relaxing layer to accommodate the 4% structural mismatch between GaAs/Si, the GaAs bulk layer possesses a very high crystalline quality. Only a few stacking faults in the {111} planes were observed in the ultrathin GaAs nucleation, almost all of which are terminated by the “tiara”-like undercut structure created during the wet-etching process of the Si patterned with SiO2. After the SiO2 dielectric removal, GaAs overgrowth was performed to coalesce the nanowires into 300-nm-thick thin film structures. No planar defects escaped from the top of Si ridge was observed. Threading dislocation density below 107/cm2 has been obtained for device growth, resulting in high performance and reliable lasers in the 1.3 -1.5 µm band. Using III-V quantum dots as the active medium has been proven to lower power consumption and improve device temperature stability. We have investigated such micro/nano-lasers in great extent in the past few years. We demonstrated the first room-temperature InAs/InAlGaAs quantum-dot subwavelength microdisk lasers epitaxially grown on (001) Si, with a lasing wavelength of 1563 nm, an ultralow-threshold of 2.73 μW, and lasing up to 60 °C under pulsed optical pumping. This result unambiguously offers a promising path towards large-scale integration of cost-effective and energy-efficient silicon-based long-wavelength lasers. Fabrication process of the microdisk lasers. We have also reported electrically –pumped microring lasers in the 1.3µm band with sub-mA threshold current. To gain some insight on the device design towards lower threshold and minimized power consumption on Si substrates, the microdisk incorporating two different QD stack numbers were fabricated and compared. An obvious lower threshold together with a higher cold cavity quality factor were achieved with 7-layer QD microdisks, due to a stronger material gain as well as a better overlap of the optical fields with the active elements. Meanwhile, a direct comparison of QDs and QWs as the gain medium in the same laser structure was performed. A lower lasing threshold and a more uniform slope efficiency distribution of QD lasers could be identified, owing to the lower sensitivity of the QDs to defects and surface recombination. Moreover, these quantum dot microdisk lasers on Si compare favorably with the devices simultaneously processed on native InP substrates, with an ultralow average threshold of 8.3 μW, a remarkable temperature stability of To =277 K and red-shift rate = 0.087 nm/K, and the capability of working at chip temperatures over 60 °C. All these results represent an advance towards reliable silicon-based quantum dot lasers at telecom wavelengths. Investigation of electrically injected QD lasers is ongoing to attain efficient and applicable light sources for on-chip photonic circuits and optical fiber communications. Meanwhile, we are also working on the epitaxy of III-V nano-structures on Si using the ART method for nano-scale optoelectronic applications. We patterned and grew well-aligned in-plane InP nano-ridges on (001) Si substrates. The 8% lattice mismatch between InP and Si is accommodated through an unique GaAs stress-reducing buffer and the formation of high density of defects at the III-V/Si interface. The InP buffer layer, where five InGaAs ridge QWs are embedded, has been optimized with much reduced interfacial defects. Figure 2(c) presents a zoomed-in TEM image of one side of the InP nano-ridge, showing five uniform InGaAs ridge QWs. The high resolution TEM image of one InGaAs QW in Figure 2(d) reveals atomic sharp InP/InGaAs interfaces and thus minimized non-radiative recombination via interface states.

16212115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212115.value: We developed high-performance quantum dot (QD) lasers directly grown on exact (001) silicon substrates. First, the optical efficiency and structural property of the quantum dot hetero-structures on various GaAs-on-Si templates was investigated to determine the optimal epitaxial scheme. Next, by combining high-quality whispering gallery modes (WGM) and 3D confinement of injected carriers in quantum dot micro-disk structures, lasing operation from 10 K up to room temperature was achieved under continuous optical pumping on the exact (001) Si substrate. The micro-disk diameters were further miniaturized for dense integration and low power consumption for on-chip laser sources. Subwavelength micro-disk lasers (MDLs) as small as 1 μm in diameter have been demonstrated in the 1.2-μm wavelength range, with low thresholds down to 35 μW at 10 K. A systematic comparison of lasing dynamics shows that the micro-disk lasers on Si substrates compare favorably with devices fabricated on native GaAs substrates and state-of-the-art work reported elsewhere. The optically-pumped microdisk lasers have shown that these quantum dot structures, grown heteroepitaxially on Si substrates, are excellent candidate sources for chip-scale Si-based photonics. The full extension of the optically pumped micro-disk structure towards practical electrically injected laser configurations was further explored. Various types of laser structures have been designed, fabricated, and characterized on native GaAs substrates. These include broad area lasers and ridge lasers with a top-bottom contact geometry and a top-top contact geometry, amorphous Si waveguide laser, microdisk and microring lasers. The fabrication platforms developed here pave the way to fulfilling fully integrated electrically driven lasers on Si, and enable us to demonstrate the world’s first electrically pumped quantum-dot micro-ring lasers epitaxially grown on (001) silicon. Continuous-wave lasing around 1.3 µm was achieved with ultra-low thresholds as small as 0.6 mA and maximum operation temperatures up to 100°C in larger devices. After demonstrating high performance single devices, co-integration of various optoelectronic devices on silicon was designed and explored. This includes laser-photodiode systems through free-space coupling, waveguide coupling, and combination of InAs quantum dots gain elements with index matched amorphous silicon waveguide devices through evanescent coupling. Preliminary on-chip photonic systems have been demonstrated, the feasibility of integrating active and passive devices was analyzed and simulated. We also achieved efficient III-V quantum dot lasers epitaxially grown on Si substrates emitting at the 1.55 μm band. To realize this goal, challenges have to be settled, which mainly lie in achieving good QDs with strong optical emission together with a uniform QD distribution, as well as obtaining a smooth InP buffer grown on Si substrates with minimized defects generation. By utilizing the double-cap procedure, we were able to stack the InAs/InAlGaAs QDs to enhance the optical properties; additionally, these self-assembled QDs were inserted into the InP buffer to serve as dislocation filters. Based on these efforts, low-temperature continuous-wave (CW) operation of QD microdisk lasers (MDLs) grown on (001) Si was realized. To miniaturize the footprints of the microlasers, subwavelength QD MDLs were produced, showing low thresholds, superior characteristic temperatures and above room temperature operation, under pulsed optical pumping. Furthermore, we moved on to grow and fabricate the more practical electrically injected Fabry-Perot lasers. By carefully tuning the growth parameters of QDs and leveraging the V-grooved Si to lower dislocation densities in the QD laser structure, the first 1.55 μm band room temperature electrical QD laser directly grown on Si was demonstrated, with a threshold density as low as 1.8 kA/cm2 under pulsed excitation, and a high operation temperature up to 80°C.

16212115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212115.value: We are the fire group that demonstrated QD communication wavelength lasers on Si by MOCVD, while almost all high-performance QD lasers have been achieved by MBE. This is extremely significant because for volume production of either discrete or integrated devices and circuits, large area epitaxy is needed. MOCVD has been recognized as the production tool of choice for compound semiconductor devices. Further development and perfection of the growth of QD lasers for silicon photonics applications is planned and there are many uncharted territories yet to be explored. We plan to collaborate with Si photonics experts to develop Si photonic integrated circuits with high-performance light sources directly grown on Si.

16212115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212115.value: Behind today's cloud computing and mobile paradigm is a robust network of data center facilities, where information is stored, processed, and transmitted. As the number of connected devices and information handled grows, the power consumed by data centers escalates. The exponential growth of big data traffic, compared with the barely linear improvements in system/equipment energy-efficiency leading to a projected widening of the “energy gap” posts serious challenges. The Global data centers used roughly 416 terawatts (4.16 x 1014 watts) of power in 2017, with a projected annual increase rate of at least 10%. Curbing power consumption of the data-centers requires more energy-efficient, high-capacity communication links and systems in the data center facilities. To fulfill the needs of energy-efficient high-performance computing and data-communication, increasing adoption and integration of optics and electronics using silicon photonics is necessary for such technological advancements. Integrated photonics Similar to silicon semiconductor integrated circuits (ICs), silicon photonics has been exploited in the past decade to extend its applications from telecommunications to data-comm. Photonics is the most energy efficient means we know today to transmit large volumes of data over long distances. In addition to speed, transmission of data using photons instead of electrons can potentially consume much less energy.

16212415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212415.value: GaN (gallium nitride) HEMTs (high electron mobility transistors), which have emerged in recent years, are based on the phenomenon of a high mobility 2DEG (two-dimensional electron gas) generated due to the piezoelectric nature of the hetero-junction structure in III-V compound semiconductor materials. Compared to silicon power MOSFETs, GaN HEMTs have a wider range of breakdown voltages, lower on-resistance, and yet a lower parasitic capacitance per unit area. The improvement over the silicon counterpart is disruptive, resetting many performance benchmarks. A new era of extending this technology to replace the silicon MOSFETs and to take advantage of its new capability has begun. The GaN power electronics market was started by IR and EPC Corp. in 2010. Currently, the maximum commercially available blocking voltage is 200 V for normally-off HEMT from EPC Corp. and 600 V for normally-off hybrid cascode structure from Transphorm [1]. Newcomers (IR, GaN Systems [2], micro GaN [3], Panasonic [4], and so on) are expected to join the market soon. Almost all derive the normally-off function from connecting a normally-on core unit device (GaN HEMT) with a normally-off control unit device (Si MOSFET) in a hybrid cascode configuration. This cascode structure can help to eliminate the gate leakage current and enhance the gate swing, which are big obstacles to designing gate drivers using GaN HEMTs [5]. Furthermore, the cascode structure contains a small Qrr (reverse recovery charge) body-diode from the low-voltage Si MOSFET, which can be used as a freewheeling diode in some rectification circuits. Moreover, the Si low-voltage MOSFET will not degrade the merits of the GaN HEMT. However, the parasitic inductance introduced by the interconnection bonding wires between the discrete Si MOSFET and GaN HEMT increases both the switching loss and the possibility of damaging the GaN HEMT gate by severe internal parasitic ringing [6]. Therefore, novel packaging techniques are demanded to reduce the parasitics caused by assembly. On the other hand, monolithic integration of the GaN HEMT with the Si MOSFET will reduce interconnection parasitics for the cascode structure. In this research, we propose to monolithically integrate the GaN HEMT with the Si MOSFET in a cascode configuration on the same substrate. In this way, normally-off GaN HEMTs with a high gate drive swing and a low pararasitic interconnect inductance can be obtained for optimum system performance. This will also result in a lower switching loss, higher reliability, and lower cost compared to the hybrid counterpart. 氮化镓高电子迁移率晶体管与硅基功率金属氧化物半导体场效应 晶体管相比有更高的击穿电压，更低的导通电阻，和更小的结电 容。这些优点使得氮化镓高电子迁移率晶体管成为了硅基功率器 件的一个有力竞争者。但是，氮化镓功率器件常开的工作特性和 小的栅极驱动摆幅与现有的硅基驱动电路不兼容，这很大程度上 限制了氮化镓晶体管的大规模商业化。一种简单的实现常闭的工 作特性并增大栅极摆幅的方法是用共源共栅拓扑结构将一个高压 、常开的氮化镓高电子迁移率晶体管和一个低压、常闭的硅基金 属氧化物半导体场效应管连接。很多公司（Transphorm，国际整 流器公司，microGaN，等等）利用共源共栅拓扑结构封装分立的 氮化镓和硅基晶体管元件，发布了他们600V/650V产品。但是， 由于分立的氮化镓晶体管和硅基晶体管之间的互联焊线所产生的 寄生电感，不但会导致氮化镓晶体管的开关损耗的增加，也会导 致操作失误率的增加。 本次科研预案的目的是开发一种在同一片硅基衬底上集成氮化镓 高电子迁移率晶体管和硅基场效应晶体管的技术。以共源共栅拓 扑结构连接两种晶体管，可以实现常闭、大栅极驱动摆幅、小寄 生电感的功率器件。而且，这种方式和分立元件封装相比，可以 获得更低的功耗和更高的可靠性。这种单片集成的方法为全面开 发III-V族半导体器件和硅基互补式金属氧化物半导体电路的集成 提供基础，并加速III-V族半导体器件在功率电路领域中的应用。

16212415.label: Realisation of objectives
16212415.value: We began the project by working first on the design of the novel monolithically integrated GaN HEMT-Si MOSFET high-voltage cascode structure. After the structure was designed, a fabrication process which can provide both high performance silicon MOSFET devices and GaN HEMT devices simultaneously was designed. We then proceeded to do the layout design and fabrication of the cascode structure. In the first run, we cannot manage to obtain any working devices due to material non-uniformity and cracking issues. After more subsequent work, we finally got the material issues resolved. However, both silicon and GaN devices in the same integrated structure still cannot work at the same time but with very high leakage current. We then decided to obtain a Si-GaN cascoded diode first because fabricating a GaN compatible silicon diode is considerably easier than fabricating a silicon MOSFET. The Si-GaN cascoded diode is a structure formed by monolithically integrating a silicon pn junction diode and a GaN HEMT. This structure possesses similar advantages as claimed by the GaN HEMT-Si MOSFET cascoded structure. The difference is that the cascoded diode function as a diode and the GaN HEMT-Si MOSFET cascoded structure function as a transistor. The cascoded diode structure was obtained successfully and the results have been published in a journal paper (J1) and an international power semiconductor devices conference (C1). The two-step approach of first integrating the GaN HEMT with the Si diode first and then building a complete GaN HEMT/Si MOSFET cascoded transistor structure allows us to gain more experience for fabricating the more complicated cascoded transistor structure. During the various runs of fabrication for implementing the cascoded diode, we have found out the thermal budget and process sequence needed to prevent the materials cracking, and finally both working GaN HEMT and working Si MOSFET were obtained on the same substrate. The complete GaN HEMT/Si MOSFET cascoded transistor structure was finally obtained and published in a journal publication (J2). We have also fully characterized this monolithically integrated cascoded transistor structure and compared it with the hybrid integration counterpart. The expected function of a normally-off GaN HEMT with a high gate drive swing and a low parasitic interconnect inductance for optimum system performance was obtained, and the results were reported in a conference publication (C2). All the project objectives have been achieved successfully within the project period.

16212515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212515.value: As the semiconductor technology scales further in the deep-submicron domain, the transistor density on modern semiconductor devices like multi-core processors, grows exponentially to provide higher computation and data processing capability. As a result, the power density of the chip also increases exponentially leading to higher heat dissipation which translates into soaring chip temperatures. Studies have shown that thermal failures not only increase cooling and packaging costs but also are a critical threat to the reliability and performance of multi-core processors. Hence, efficient solutions to protect the multi-core processors under a safe temperature are required. However, as transistors continuously shrink in nanometer sizes, fabrication equipment is losing precise control of the manufacturing processes resulting in inter-die and intra-die process variations. Process variations affect the predictability of the system by increasing the variability of power, thermal and performance parameters, turning the effective solutions on power and thermal management ineffective in the presence of unaccounted parameter variations. For example, dynamic frequency and voltage scaling (DVFS) and task scheduling are the commonly used approaches to achieve efficient thermal control in processors. Unfortunately, these solutions become inept under large process variation. Process variation largely degrades the control quality of the DVFS module due to parameter fluctuations in the power/thermal models used for determining the appropriate voltage/frequency levels. Moreover, parameter variations can also result in inefficient task scheduling decisions to processors causing failure to meet temperature or timing requirement. In addressing this issue, previous approaches either required an extra calibration step to measure the variation and amend the power/thermal model in the DVFS module, or considered the process variation from statistical view in the task scheduling algorithm. However, such static approaches suffer from low variation coverage and extra cost also increases with system scale. We propose to address this challenge with a systematic variation-tolerant dynamic thermal management scheme with low cost. First, based on the advantages of fuzzy control on high control quality, low complexity and robustness to parameter variations, we propose to develop an adaptive fuzzy controller as thermal controller which is capable to automatically adjust its control strategies to tolerate thermal parameter variations and maintain the chip temperature within temperature limits. Then based on the adaptive thermal controller, a dynamic thermal management scheme for multi-core processor composed of per-core closed-loop DVFS and a thermal-aware scheduling algorithm will be developed to optimize the system performance while satisfying the temperature constraint under all variations. 隨著半導體技術在深亞微米域的進一步發展，像芯片多處理器一样的現代半導體器件的晶體管密度呈指數增長。其結果是，芯片的功率密度也指數增加， 形成較大的散熱性也意味著芯片溫度飆升。有研究表明，熱故障不僅增加冷卻和包裝成本，而且是对于可靠性和性能的一個重要威脅。此外，由於晶體管縮小到納米尺寸，制卡設備正在失去所需要的製造過程控制，因而產生芯片内外工藝變化。工藝變化会借增加功率，熱和性能參數的變異性而影響系統的可預測性，使得原来有效的電源和溫度管理在參數變化的存在下成為無效的方法。 例如，動態頻率和電壓調節（DVFS）和任務調度是原来兩種有效的方法來實現處理器熱控制。DVFS通過縮減其電壓和頻率水平来控制處理器的功耗從而控制溫度，以適應溫度的約束。任務調度通過智能任務分配來平衡電力消耗達到溫度的控制。不幸的是，這些解決方案当工藝變化存在时失去了能力，面对着頻繁的熱控失效。工藝變化造成了在用於確定合適的電壓/頻率水平功率/熱模型參數的波動，因而在很大程度上降低了DVFS模塊的控制質量。而且，參數變化也可以導致低效任務調度決策而產生定時錯誤。為了解決這個問題，以前的方法需要額外的校準步驟來衡量變化和修改功率/溫度模型。然而，這樣的靜態方法面对覆蓋率小的問題，并且当系統規模增加額外成本也会增加。 我們建議建立一個基於自適應模糊控制的變異容錯自適應溫度管理方法以解決這個問題。模糊控制器提供了較高的控制品質，低複雜性和穩健性參數變化的優點。我們建議以自適應模塊增強基本模糊控制器，並啟用自動調整控制策略来容忍參數的變化和保持芯片的溫度在熱限值以內。此外，我們將進一步開發基於每個處理器核心的自適應模糊控制器的系統級解決方案。这个方案將基於DVFS模塊设计和溫度感知調度算法来實現在穩定的溫度控制下的性能最優化。

16212515.label: Realisation of objectives
16212515.value: In order to resolve the thermal control problem, we have developed the fuzzy control module, and also the power and energy minimization method to minimize the total heat dissipation. We we propose a two-stage thermal-aware task scheduling policy which exploits the application and system architecture characteristics to decouple the mapping of task-graphs for the performance and peak temperature optimization into two stages. At the first stage, the algorithm collects the best mapping of task-graphs exploiting the application and architecture characteristics to minimize the makespan of the task-graphs. At the second stage, a light-weight online algorithm comprised of efficient thermal rank and combined power models is performed to map the task nodes to the real cores for temperature minimization while maintaining the best possible performance achieved in the first stage. Compared to the previous approaches which perform the performance and temperature optimization together, our method can reduce the online mapping algorithm complexity and improve its efficiency. Experiments on real benchmarks show that an average of 6.3 C peak temperature reduction and 6.8% performance improvement can be achieved compared to other existing methods. Furthermore, we observed in most existing energy minimization works using dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS), the overhead of the power delivery system of the multi-core platform has been largely overlooked. Hence, based on previous findings, we propose an overall energy optimization method for the system that minimizes both per-core energy consumption and voltage regulator (VR) energy consumption using DVFS and VR phase scaling by solving a comprehensive convex model. We decompose our proposed convex method into two stages: an off-line stage and an on-line stage. During the off-line stage, we explore the convex model by assuming different numbers of active phases of the VR, various workload pressures and workload characteristics to collect the optimal frequency assignments under different scenarios. During the online stage, the specific frequency assignment for cores and optimal active phase number of the VR are selected and applied based on the actual workload pressure and its characteristics running on the cores . Experiments on real benchmarks show that when compared with state-of-the-art approaches, our method can achieve a significant energy saving of up to 22.4% with negligible on-line overhead. With all our proposed methods, the energy consumption of multi-core systems can be significantly reduced and corresponding thermal issues can be effectively resolved.

16212515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212515.value: With the increasing demands for computation capacity to process large amount of data, the processors require more power and energy to finish the tasks. Accordingly, there will be more heat generated by the power consumption, and cause thermal increase in the processor which may cause threat to the processor reliability or function failure. Hence, it is critical to solve the thermal issue without harming much of the processor performance. We can address the problem through different perspectives including the thermal control, power minimization and energy minimization. The methods we proposed significantly reduced the power and energy consumption around 20% in the multi-core systems and reduce the peak temperature of the system for around 6 C, which effectively mitigate the thermal issues.
