16212815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212815.value: This project is about cooperation between a surgeon and a surgical robot. It is about providing intelligent guidance and necessary warnings during an operation in case of danger. Robotic techniques are coming into our daily life. They provide services, such as guidance, couriering, surveillance and autonomous transportation. The application of robotic systems in medical processes has drawn especial attention, such as the “da Vinci” surgical robot system. In order to achieve reliable robot surgery, a highly-"intelligent" expert system for perception is necessary, by which proper guidance and advice are generated according to the image feedback. We believe that the core of such an expert system is a hybrid cognitive architecture (HCA), which can deal with cognition problems by using medical images. Such an HCA ought to jointly consider the surgeon's requirements and intentions and the real situation. Nature cooperation must balance operational and cooperation demands in a hybrid cognitive architecture which minimises human cognition and attention loads and optimises the joint workflow. Surgical robots can thus serve the operation process more efficiently and reliably. We propose to design the HCA by closely coupling user models to how the surgical robot can interact with the surgeon. Robotic perception (by Deep learning) and decision-making (based on Partial Observable Markov Decision Process) will be combined, providing timely and reliable assistance and especially providing warnings when serious mistakes are about to happen. The HCA bases planning and execution in a cognitive control model. User attention and the characteristics of human behaviour will be jointly considered to guide action in a cooperative context. The surgeon and the robots will have efficient and sufficient interconnection through dedicated modules to assure content awareness. During this process, visual serving will play a role in pose stabilisation. The inter-connectivity will ensure that behavior changes adaptively and coherently system-wide. We propose to focus on cooperation among the surgeons and the surgical robots in an adaptive active/passive manner. Several important modules are to be presented with a real-time integrated system with a robot arm based on pixel-wise image labeling and a decision model. 本項目所研究內容關于手術機器人與手術操作人員的合作。它用于提供在危險情況下的智能的導引與提醒。現今機器人技術日益與生活相關，他們一方面提供各類服務，包括導引、取遞、觀測與自動導航等。它在醫學中的應用得到了廣泛的關注，包括 “達芬奇”系統等等手術機器人。爲了達到更好的可靠性，高智能的專業系統有其必要性，即通過視覺反饋產生合理的導引和建議。我們相信這類系統的核心即建立混雜的認知結構體系(HCA)。這一體系應當同時考慮手術操作人員的實際需求和情況。相對自然化的的交互方式將平衡操作與合作的需求，從而最小化操作人員的認知與關注負擔，優化合作效率。藉此手术機器人可以高效率地服務整個手術過程。 本項目提出應當嚴格結合用戶模型和手术機器人的特性進行HCA的設計。機器人通過深度學習的感知和基於POMDP的決策過程相結合，提出實時且可靠的輔助，特別是在錯誤發生時的及時提醒。基於HCA進行任務規劃與執行。同時考慮用戶的意識與人行爲的特徵，幷將這一特點之用于人機合作框架下運動導引。這一過程中， 手術操作人員和機器人將產生有效且高效的認知效果，而在姿態穩定方面，視覺伺服作爲核心模塊進行機器人的控制。機器人的行爲和決策模型會在人機交互過程中得到全系統範圍的優化。 本項目提出以自適應的方式建立手術機器人與操作人員的合作模型。項目提出的多個模塊將通過基於像素的實時圖像標識(pixelwise labelling)和包括機械手臂在內的機器人系統進行實時驗證。

16212815.label: Realisation of objectives
16212815.value: We have finished all the previously defined research objectives. For each objective, the realization is described as follows: 1 Design and develop a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) framework to model a hybrid cognitive architecture (HCA) to ensure the safety and reliability of human-operating surgical robots. The target HCA will provide the basis for sharing common understandings of the surgical process among robots and operators. We proposed to use a hierarchical structure to realize the cognition of the environment, with emphasis on human-robot interaction and cooperation. We have successfully combined convolutional neural networks (CNN) with fully connected networks, to realize the human-like perception of the environment. The HCA is trained with the input of depth images, and output from manual guidance in the training phase. Afterwards, the robot can move autonomously in the environment with the learned model. As for the experiments, we have tested the model in typical indoor office environments. The general results of decision making are similar to human-decisions based on our evaluation from both time series and confusion matrix. We have applied the learned model to also rehabilitation robots, leading to publication: Weibin Wu, Deli Wang, Tianyunyang Wang, Ming Liu, A Personalized Limb Rehabilitation Training System for Stroke Patients, Proceedings of the IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Biomimetics, ROBIO 2016 We have also studied the data analysis of the high-dimensional feature map of the HCA. In order to demonstrate how the trained network functions as an artificial brain, we try to visualize the feature maps generated from the last layer. The second-last layer represents the feature maps, which are further categorized by the last fully connected layer. The outcome leads to the selection of control commands. However, it is not easy to visualize these feature maps $G := {g_i|g_i=NN(I_i)}$ where $NN$ is the function of the deep-network and $I_i$ is the input depth image with index $i$. $g_i$ is the corresponding feature map of the input $i$. Note that each $g_i$ is with dimension of $g_i in mathbb{R}^19200$. To solve this problem, we adopt a latent variable Gaussian Process model (GPLVM), more specifically, with Spike and Slab Gaussian Process Latent Variable Models (SSGPLVM), which was recently proposed by Dai et al. We project $g_i$ into a lower-dimensional space. After that, a pair of distinguished dimensions can be visualized as $mathbb{R}^2$. We finally visualize the result, from which we can see that the left or right control outputs are slackly distinguished and the straightforward motion is universal under heterogeneous image inputs. More figures and results are referred to our published paper "Tai, Lei, Shaohua Li, and Ming Liu, A deep-network solution towards model-less obstacle avoidance, 2016 IEEE/RSJ international conference on intelligent robots and systems (IROS). IEEE, 2016". We generalized the HCA to robotic arms. The high-level commands are generated from HCA models. A robotic arm controller, trained with Robot Learning from Demonstration (RLfD), further realizes each high-level command. We proposed an effective sequential learning method to realize the high-level commands. The RLfD system can be divided into two phases (learning and reproduction). In the first phase (learning), demonstrations of the task are online collected to sequentially learn the motor skills and impedance parameters (variable stiffness and damping). In the reproduction phase, the learned motion generation and compliant skills (variable impedance parameters) are used for reproducing the robotic compliant behavior. We conducted the stability analysis and derived the corresponding stability constraints for the learned impedance parameters. The detailed analysis and results can be referred to our published paper (Section 4) ”Jianghua Duan, Yongsheng Ou, Sheng Xu, Ming Liu, Sequential learning unification controller from human demonstrations for robotic compliant manipulation, Neurocomputing, Volume 366, 2019”. The results showed that the global asymptotic stability of variable impedance control could be guaranteed through the stability considerations in the learning process, which allows the robot to safely operate in the environments where human beings and robots share the workspace. Besides theoretical analysis, we conducted a realistic task on robotic arms to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method. The task consists of transporting a deformable object over an obstacle and reaching the target point, then the robot drops the object into the target container. Such a sequence of operations can be the analogy of grabbing surgical instruments and handing over to surgeons. The experiment results demonstrated the successful completion of the task. More figures and results are referred to our published paper "Jianghua Duan, Yongsheng Ou, Sheng Xu, Ming Liu, Sequential learning unification controller from human demonstrations for robotic compliant manipulation, Neurocomputing, Volume 366, 2019". 2. Design and implement a novel pixel-wise image labeling system for medical images. We have finished semantic pixel-wise labeling (segmentation) of medical images with the help of Wenzhou Medical School. With provided multiple groups of fMRI data, the semantic regions are correctly labeled. We designed a deep learning model for pixel-wise labeling and used PCA to reduce the complexity in classification to accelerate the forward computing speed. The experiment results demonstrated the precision and effectiveness of our proposed deep network and our PCA-aided method can greatly reduce the inference time. The network structure and results can be referred to our published paper: "Tai, Lei, et al., PCA-aided fully convolutional networks for semantic segmentation of multi-channel fMRI, 2017 18th IEEE International Conference on Advanced Robotics (ICAR), 2017." 3. Design and implement a visual servoing-based algorithm to stabilize the end-point of the surgical robot using the cognitive decisions derived from objective 1. We adopted deep-learning in a typical visual servoing problem, i.e., visual homing, to validate our assumption that the visual servoing control output will lead to a convergent solution. We firstly stretched the images taken from the omnidirectional camera to square size (879x170 pixels). They were separately taken into convolutional neural networks with 4 convolutional layers. Every convolutional layer here was a combination of a convolutional layer, pooling layer and rectified linear unit (ReLU) layer. After the convolutional process, the features extracted from the convolutional layers are concatenated and taken into 4 fully-connected layers. Every fully-connected layer also consists of a ReLU layer. Finally, the relative coordinate between the two images is taken as the output. The loss is the euclidean distance between the label and the prediction. We separately trained two networks for the relative x or y coordinate. The test result showed that the output of the relative distance is very precise based on the target under a similar data distribution to the training dataset. 4. Design and develop an integrated prototype system to mimic the surgical process by using a robotic arm, with the HCA and expert system being embedded. We built a prototype system with a FANUC LR Mate 200iD/7L robot arm, a SONY FLIR BFS-U3-32S4C-C scan camera, and an Nvidia Jetson TX2 embedded computation board for running the HCA and necessary computations. The integrated prototype is a generalized system, which can handle the processes, including but not limited to surgical processes. Here we list some important specifications of the prototype system. Field of view: 140 mm Distance to workplace: 300 mm Camera resolution: 2048 x 1536 Camera frequency: 118 FPS GPU: 256-core NVIDIA Pascal GPU architecture with 256 NVIDIA CUDA cores CPU: Dual-Core NVIDIA Denver 2 64-Bit CPU Quad-Core ARM Cortex-A57 MPCore Memory: 8GB 128-bit LPDDR4 Memory 1866 MHz - 59.7 GB/s Operating Humidity: 20 to 80% Operating Temperature: 0 to 50℃

16212815.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212815.value: As a summary, we have achieved the following facts in the period of this project. - We have published six journal papers, including those in the International Journal of Advanced Robotic Systems (IJARS), Biomaterials, Robotics and Automation System (RAS), IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics (TCYB), and IEEE Robotics and Automation Magazine (RAM). The topics range from medical robot control, localization, image segmentation, exoskeleton, etc. - We have published fifteen international conference papers, including ICRA, IROS, ICAR, RCAR, ICVS, ICIA and ROBIO. The topics range from fMRI image segmentation, rehabilitation robots, etc. - We have been finalized or won four best conference paper awards, including the best conference paper award of CYBER 2015. The paper for fMRI image segmentation won the best paper award from ICAR 2017. - We won the Wu-Wenjun AI Innovation Award 3rd Prize in 2016. - We have graduated one MPhil and two Ph.D. students from Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. - We have supported three international exchange students from Switzerland.

16212815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212815.value: There are several aspects to further develop in the research route: - Socially compliant robots. The current robot arm controller is trained with sequences of data under the RLfD framework. For better cooperation with surgeons, the controller can be customized for each surgeon based on his/her customs. It can base on our recent research on socially compliant mobile robots: "Lei Tai, Jingwei Zhang, Ming Liu, Wolfram Burgard, Socially Compliant Navigation through Raw Depth Inputs with Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning, International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), May 21-25, 2018, Brisbane, Australia". - Multi-robot collaboration. Based on our proposed RLfD method, robots with different training sequences of data can handle a variety of tasks. Such a system can be scaled up to a multi-robot system. Furthermore, a multi-robot collaborative task allocation module can be designed for guiding these surgical robots to cooperate with each other. Besides task allocation, the resource allocation can also be considered if the computation resource and network bandwidth are both limited.

16212815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212815.value: The project completed the necessary know-how and prototype systems for a targeted cognitive expert system for surgical robots, including a hybrid cognitive architecture model to ensure the safety and reliability of surgical robots and a pixel-wise image labeling system to locate and highlight important regions on medical images. The project is defined in the context of surgical robots and could be easily scaled up and extended to other general service robots. The pixel-wise image labeling system led to the best student paper reward in a top international robotics conference. The conducted results may lead to a boost in not only robotics but also analytic research or medical science.

16213015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213015.value: Solid-state optical refrigeration based on anti-Stokes fluorescence is attracting great interest in recent decades due to its great potential applications in cooling optical and microelectronic devices. Compared with other cooling techniques, optical refrigeration offers a solid-state solution that can potentially achieve a low temperature of tens of K without introducing coolants or mechanical vibrations. Up until now, most optical refrigeration research focuses rare-earth-doped glass and crystals, optical refrigeration in semiconductors is still in its infancy, although the latter can potentially provide a much higher cooling power and a much lower achievable temperature. The net cooling of semiconductors was only achieved very recently and the cooling performance in semiconductors is still quite limited. It is highly desirable to improve the performance of optical refrigeration in semiconductors for its potential applications. The cooling power and cooling efficiency of optical refrigeration in semiconductor highly depend on the optical properties of the material and the coupling between the lattice vibration and incident photons. Therefore, by changing the local electromagnetic field and the coupling with the photon modes in free space, the optical performance can be potentially improved. We propose to improve the cooling performance in semiconductor by taking the advantages of surface plasmon near-field plasmon. Micro plasmonic patterns can dramatically increase the photon intensity inside the absorption layer and strengthen the coupling between the lattice and photons, potentially leading to much enhanced absorption coefficient, external quantum efficiency and anti-Stokes to Stokes fluorescence ratio and therefore a much improved optical refrigeration. Using CdS thin films as the targeted material, we will investigate the influence of surface plasmon on the cooling performance in semiconductors through both theoretical modeling and experimental characterization. We will develop a design of micro plasmonic structures that is thermally insulated from the semiconductor but can significantly enhance anti-Stokes emission with minor dissipative loss. High-quality CdS thin films will be fabricated and characterized and their cooling performance with and without the plasmonic patterns will be studied and compared with the theoretical prediction. Based on these studies, the role of surface plasma in the light-matter interaction will be clarified and a general strategy that can be used to enhance the optical refrigeration in semiconductors will be developed.

16213015.label: Realisation of objectives
16213015.value: Mr. Yang Li was admitted as a PhD student to work on the project with the financial support from HKUST. Mr. Li has conducted numerical simulations to design the plasmonic structure, the fabrication and characterization of the plasmonic structure as well as the upconversion tests. He received his PhD degree at HKUST in August, 2019. Meanwhile, Mr. Chongjia Lin also joined the relevant research on plasmonic structures as a PhD student. We have developed theoretical models to predict the antistokes radiation under enhanced electromagnetic field. The light absorption, reflection and emission have been modeled with the enhanced field. It is found that with the enhanced field, the absorption and emission can be significantly enhanced while the reflection will dependent on the incident spectrum. Meanwhile, we have simulated various plasmonic structures to achieve both a high absorption and an extreme field enhancement. It is found that metal-insulator-metal structure can offer a high field enhancement compared with conventional dispersed particles. The influences of various design parameters, such as the metal type, insulator property, thicknesses of metal layers and insulator layer, top pattern shape, and distribution of patterns, on the spectral absorption, transmission and reflection have been explored. We obtained optimized plasmonic structures which can selective absorb infrared light and give high emission in visible light regime. Based on the optimized design, we experimentally exploited equilateral triangular nanodisks and an out-of-plane nanogap of 10 nm, taking advantage of their abilities to confine electromagnetic field components in x-y plane and z direction, respectively. Triangular metal nanoparticles have been proven to be superior building blocks in plasmonic systems because of the expected strong in-plane field enhancement (on the order of 102-103 for an isolated nanoparticle) associated with their sharp tips, and the great potential of coupled triangular particles. Meanwhile, a smooth and ultrathin dielectric spacer can guarantee the extreme out-of-plane coupling, further giving rise to a stronger z-direction field confinement. The obtained PNs realize a maximum absorption of 98% with features of polarization and incident angle independences. A high density of “hot spots” with a maximum local electric field enhancement of 4.5×104 is achieved, confirmed by an ultrasmall point-like mode volume of 3.0×10-6 μm3. Despite the identical disk and gap sizes, this huge enhancement is around twice as large as those for typical in-plane coupled (bowtie-shaped) ones that can only be fabricated by lithographic methods. The film-coupled triangular disks show more potential in large-scale production since the nanoscale spacer and the single triangular disks are more readily available than the tip-to-tip bowties. Moreover, recent breakthrough in the chemical synthesis of triangular nanodisks also paves the way for the mass production of this kind of superior PNs. With the findings on equilateral triangular nanodisks and the out-of-plane plasmonic coupling in a metal-insulator-metal sandwich structure, we developed high-performance spectrally selective plasmonic absorbers with excellent thermal stability. The plasmonic absorber comprises multiple strategies (structure-, material-, and shape-based) and demonstrate full-spectrum sunlight absorption and greatly reduced infrared emission, ultimately boosting the record-high light-thermal efficiency (1000 K) of plasmonic selective absorber from 66.4% to 77.3% under 100‐sun illumination. This superior performance is not only stable at temperatures of 1000 K, but also robust to the variations in the constituent materials of top nanodisks and dielectric spacers. Moreover, the performance of such PMAs is independent of the lateral periodicity or orientations of meta-atoms, paving the way for their large-scale deployment. Using plasmonic TiN layer, we also developed an all-ceramic TiN/TiNO/ZrO2/SiO2 multilayer absorber with highly selective absorption, i.e., a high solar absorptance (92.2%) yet an ultralow thermal emittance (17.0% at 1000 K), producing an unprecedented solar-thermal conversion efficiency (82.6% under 100 suns). Remarkably, the absorber shows great thermal stability even after long-term (150 h) annealing at 1000 K, boosting the operating temperature of conventional multilayer absorbers by at least 227 K. The efficient and stable all-ceramic absorber can be readily produced in quantity via low-cost processes. For large-scale production, we developed solution-processed metamaterial absorbers through assembling colloidal plasmonic TiN nanoparticles into an ultrathin and uniform absorbing nanofilm on reflective substrates with the assistance of solution-processed SiO2 anti-reflection coatings. Near-perfect full-spectrum sunlight absorption (~95%) and ultralow infrared emission (~3% at 100 °C and ~22% at 727 °C) are realized simultaneously in the formed selective absorbers. The all-ceramic structure also endowed them excellent thermal stability up to 727 °C. The solution-processed low-cost plasmonic absorbers even outperform the best-performing vacuum-deposited absorbers in field tests. This work demostrates the great potential of cost-effective solution-processed metamaterials in spectral control and solar energy conversion.

16213015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213015.value: Some materials can emit photons with energy higher than the incident photon energy due to the photon-lattice interactions and this phenomenon can be used to achieve optical refrigeration with light. Compared with other cooling techniques, optical refrigeration offers a solid-state solution that can potentially achieve a very low temperature without introducing coolants or mechanical vibrations. This behavior highly depends on the optical properties of the material and the coupling between the lattice vibration and incident photons. Therefore, by changing the local electromagnetic field and the coupling with the photon modes in free space, the performance of optical refrigeration may be improved by using a plasmonic structure . We have developed theoretical models to predict the optical refrigeration behavior under enhanced electromagnetic field. The light absorption, reflection and emission have been modeled with the enhanced field. It is found that with the enhanced field, the absorption and emission can be significantly enhanced while the reflection will dependent on the incident spectrum. Motivated by this finding, we have designed various plasmonic structures to achieve both a highly selective absorption and an extreme field enhancement, including the metal-insulator-metal sandwich structure with the triangular nanodisks, multilayer structure with plasmonic TiN layers, and low-cost solution-processed film structure with self-assembled colloidal plasmonic TiN nanoparticles. These plasmonic structures show extraordinary absorption/emission selectivity and high performance even under elevated temperatures.

16213115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213115.value: Growths in population and economic prosperity in urban cities drive up the demand for private vehicles which in turn produce the unwelcome effects such as traffic congestion and environmental problems. Sustainability has become a key global transport objective. Upgrading roads and public transportation or smart road pricing are effective ways to reduce private vehicle usage and improve sustainability. However, the implementation of these policies requires a lot of resources and a relative long time period. A more direct and effective way of improving sustainability is to reduce vehicle ownership, the focus of our proposed research. Singapore implemented the world’s first Vehicle Quota System (VQS) which uses Vickrey auction to allocate a fixed number of car license plates every month. Many mega cities in China also start controlling car ownership recently after realizing vehicle emissions are the greatest source of Beijing's air pollution. For example, Shanghai allocates a fixed number of car license plates every month by a limited price auction protocol which restricts the highest bidding price. In contrast to Shanghai's market strategy, Beijing allocates its license plates by a lottery mechanism. As policy makers face an increasing number of options for a possible vehicle ownership control police, to compare their performances in terms of economic efficiency and social fairness, a theoretical framework is needed. The goals of this proposed research are four-fold. (1) To analyze the current vehicle ownership policies and propose possible improvements. (2) To develop a theoretical framework to analyze and compare different vehicle ownership policies in terms of efficiency and fairness. (3) To develop a better vehicle ownership policy. (4) To develop a vehicle ownership policy integrated with usage based charging. The proposed research is the first comprehensive study of vehicle quota control policy targeting the dual objectives of price efficiency and social fairness by game theory approach. In view of the nature of this problem has drawn substantial attention from both practitioners and academic researchers worldwide. The theoretical framework developed in this research will serve an important role in the further development of transportation policies, and has the potential to make a significant contribution to sustainable transport, general auction theory and game theory. The research will also have significant impact on Hong Kong due to its status as one of the big cities with large population and a rapidly increasing percentage of vehicle ownership. 摘要 中国人口的增加和城市经济的繁荣带动了私家车数量的剧增，相应地也带来城市的拥堵和环境问题。可持续发展在全球都是一个重要的目标。升级道路和公共交通或智能道路收费是减少私家车使用量和提高可持续性的有效途径。然而，这些政策的实施需要大量的资源和相对较长的时间周期。一个更直接和有效地提高可持续性的方法是减少车辆的所有权，这也是我们的研究重点。 新加坡是世界上第一个实施车辆配额系统（VQS）的国家。该系统采用Vickrey拍卖来分配每个月固定数量的车牌。在意识到机动车尾气排放是北京空气污染的最大来源之后，中国的许多大型城市也开始控制汽车保有量。例如上海每月按一个限定价格的拍卖来分配固定数量的汽车牌照，这就限制了拍卖中的最高的投标价格。与上海的市场策略相比，北京通过彩票机制分配其车牌。由于政策制定者面临越来越多的有效控制车辆的机制选择，我们非常需要一个理论框架来比较这些机制的经济效率和社会公平性。 该研究有四个目标：（1）分析目前的车辆控制政策，并提出可能的改进。（2）制定一个理论框架，分析和比较不同车牌分配制度在效率和公平方面的不同。（3）制定更好的车牌分配政策。（4）制定以使用为基础的收费机制。 本文提出的研究是通过博弈论的方法来研究车辆配额控制政策，并且是第一个针对价格效率和社会公平双重目标的研究。此问题的重要性得到了全世界的从业者和学术研究人员的关注。这项研究的理论框架，将为交通运输政策的进一步发展起到重要作用，并有可能对可持续运输、一般拍卖理论和博弈论做出重大贡献。香港作为一个人口众多并且私家车增长比例迅速的大城市，这一研究也将对香港的发展产生重大影响。

16213315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213315.value: This project starts with the fabrication of nanotube arrays of Magneli phase titanium oxide, Ti4O7, on a thin foil of aluminum. Titanium coating will be obtained by spattering. TiO2 nanotube arrays will firstly be made by electrochemical anodization. Ti4O7 will then be obtained by controlled reduction of the TiO2 nanotube arrays. The Ti4O7 nanotube arrays will be infiltrated with sulfur. The highly conductive Ti4O7 will act as an electron conductor and the intimate contact between the surface of the nanotubes and the sulfur will eliminate the requirement of binders for the composite in the preparation of the cathode of lithium-sulfur battery. The aluminum will act as the current collector. The top surface of the composite will be coated with ion conductive polymer to further immobilize the polysulfides within the cathode region to decrease the shuttle effect commonly found in conventional Li-S batteries. Suitable interlayers between the cathode and the separator will be tested for interception of polysulfides. The Li-S battery cell so prepared is expected to have high energy capacity, super stability and good rate performance for energy storage. 本課題首先將在鋁薄片上通過濺射的方法塗覆一層鈦金屬膜, 然後通過電化學陽極氧化法制備氧化鈦(TiO2)納米管陣。這些氧化鈦(TiO2)納米管陣在經過適當的還原後可以生成Magneli相氧化鈦 (Ti4O7) 納米管陣。 之後, 研究者將會在這些納米管陣中灌注硫。 高導電性的Ti4O7將扮演電子疏導器的角色。 由於納米管表面與硫的親密結合, 在使用該複合物製備鋰硫電池時可以不需要粘結劑。 鋁薄片將作為集流體使用。 該複合物的表面將塗覆一層導電高分子進一步將多硫化物固定在陰極區域內, 以便降低鋰硫電池使用過程中常見的梭動效應。 我們還會研究在陰極與隔膜之間插入適當的碳膜来截流多硫化物。 使用上述辦法制備的鋰硫電池預計會具有高能量密度、超穩定性以及良好的動力表現。

16213515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213515.value: 過量磷排放造成自然水體富營養化，成為世界上水污染主要難題之一。香港70%以上的處理污水後排放至南部水域，由於無除磷措施南部水域有較高的富營養化風險， 近年來相關水域的赤潮爆發頻率亦呈增加趨勢。因此從本地污水中去除磷正變得越來越重要。強化生物除磷(EBPR) 已成為為一種經濟而有效的除磷方法，其相關技術已在世界一些區域廣泛使用。該技術主要依賴聚磷菌(PAOs) 過量攝取污水中的磷而達到除磷效果。然而，當前的EBPR技術並不適用於像香港這樣的溫熱帶地區，應為較高水溫度只有利於EBPR體系中的聚醣菌(GAOs) 生長，消耗大量有機碳源導致聚磷菌無法取得足夠有機碳生長除磷。這是因為其攝磷過程依賴有機碳源為原料合成作為電子供體的胞內聚羥基烷基酯(PHA)。此外，現有EBPR技術通過聚磷菌快速生長和污泥排放來去實現系統除磷，處理成本往往很高。而香港使用海水沖廁產生高硫酸鹽濃度污水，處理所產生的硫化物以及污水中的高鹽度都對現有EBPR技術中的聚磷菌活性可能產生很強的抑製作用。 在以上背景條件下，我們已成功地將除磷過程結合到了一種利用生物硫循環進行含鹽污水處理的新技術。該係系統可在只產生少量污泥的情況下穩定而高效地除磷，同時其效率不受污水中硫化物含量及鹽度的影響。但是該體系在較高溫度下（30攝氏度）仍然不能排除聚醣菌的影響，因為聚磷菌的除磷過程仍然依賴於胞內聚羥基烷基酯(PHA)合成和轉換來玩成。近期我們通過一些實驗發現， 基於硫轉換的新型聚磷菌(SPAOs)有可能成在。這些細菌在水溫30度顯示較好的除磷效果同時，只伴隨小量甚至沒有PHA的形成和轉換，從而使得聚醣菌在高溫條件下將無法通過碳源競爭來影響SPAOs的除磷功能。這些細菌的存在對研發適用於廣大熱帶，亞熱帶地區的新型EBPR技術具有重要的意義。然而對這些SPAOs所知甚少，對它們的種類，代謝模式以及長期運行時的穩定性等關鍵信息都不清楚。針對這些問題，本研究旨在檢測並鑑定SPAOs，並了解其除磷機制和其群落動態過程，評估建立全新強化生物除磷技術的可行性。科學上本課題開啟生物除磷方面的一個新研究領域；工程技術方面它促進利用可替代型硫酸鹽資源如海水利用，工業廢水，以及由於全球變暖引起的海水倒灌產生的含鹽水源等，在廣大熱帶亞熱帶區域對污水生物除磷處理。

16213515.label: Realisation of objectives
16213515.value: Objective 1 - Establish the BSC-EBPR reactor at 30 °C and conduct long term operation The Biological Sulfur Conversion Enhanced Biological Phosphorus Removal (BSC-EBPR) process has been studied in lab-scale sequencing batch reactors at 30oC over long term operation. Upon the successful completion of this task, the major functional bacteria and their metabolism were investigated; sludge granulation was trialed as a means of improving the process performance; and the effects of pH, temperature and carbon source on anaerobic metabolism and performance of this process were investigated to optimize the process’ operating conditions; the structural dynamics and storage states of internal polymers of BSC-EBPR were investigated. In addition, the BSC-EBPR granular sludge has been developed by manipulating the reactor operational parameters in a sequencing batch pump-lift reactor. The formation of granular sludge for BSC-EBPR, in particular under low organic loading conditions, could realize better biomass retention and treatment capacity. Gradually increasing the superficial up-flow velocity (from 5.1 to 6.8 m/h) while keeping the loading rate at 112.4 mg COD/g volatile suspended solid/day was found to be the most effective technique for promoting granulation while maintaining stable reactor performance. The resulting 375–400 µm granules settled well and the sulfate-reducing and sulfide-oxidizing bacteria were enriched to 17.7% and 15.8%, respectively in the granular sludge. A nearly three-fold improvement in the P removal efficiency and a 25%-cycle time reduction were achieved compared with flocculent sludge. Objective 2 - Examine the biochemical and microbial reactions in the reactor The functional bacteria and their metabolism were explored by manipulating the conditions associated with their deterioration, failure, and restoration. The major functional bacteria, i.e. sulfate-reducing and sulfide-oxidizing bacteria, were shown to both participate synergistically in the process and be crucial for maintaining sulfur conversion at 15–40 mg S/L, corresponding to an optimal sludge concentration of 6.5 g/L. Such sulfur conversion is in favor of the microbial community competition against glycogen-accumulating organisms, various energy flows from internal polymers (i.e. polysulfide or elemental sulfur [poly-S2-/S0] and poly-β-hydroxyalkanoates [PHA]) for phosphorus removal. Adding 25 ± 5 mg S/L of external sulfide at the beginning of the process’s anoxic phase was found efficient restoration of the process after failure. In addition, anaerobic batch experiments were conducted for i) elucidating the fundamental mechanisms of carbon uptake/poly-hydroxyalkanoates formation (1.8–3.8 mg C/(gVSS h)), sulfate reduction/sulfur storage (0.9–1.9 mg S/(gVSS h)), and poly-phosphate degradation/P release (0.6–3.0 mg P/(gVSS h)), and ii) understanding a new anaerobic pathway of simultaneous intracellular uptake of carbon and sulfur (as verified by carbon balance having only 5–10% error). Objective 3 - Investigate the P-uptake and P-release mechanism based on bioprocess stoichiometry Polysulfide or elemental sulfur (poly-S) and associated polyphosphate (poly-P) and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHAs) are systematically investigated through integration of chemical analysis and Raman micro-spectroscopy coupled with multiple microscopic methods (i.e. optical microscopy, confocal laser scanning microscopy, and differential interference contrast microscopy). The chemical analytical results displayed a stable DS-EBPR phenotype in terms of sulfur conversion, P release/uptake and dynamics of relevant polymers. The multiple microscopic images and Raman spectrum profiles further clearly demonstrated the existence of the polymers and their dynamic changes under alternating anaerobic-anoxic conditions, consistent with the chemical analytical results. In particular, Raman analysis for the first time unraveled the co-existence of S0/Sn2− species stored either intracellularly or extracellularly; and the dynamic conversions between S0/Sn2− and other sulfur species suggest that there might be a universal pool of bioavailable sulfur. The results revealed the mechanisms underlying the structural dynamics and changes in storage states of the relevant polymers that are functionally relevant to the carbon/phosphorus/sulfur-cycles during different metabolic phases. These mechanisms would otherwise not be obtained by only using a traditional chemical analysis-based approach. Objective 4 - Identify and characterize the SPAOs enriched in this reactor This research used highthroughput 16S rRNA gene sequencing coupled with principal coordinate analysis and ANOVA with Tukey’s test to unravel the spatiotemporal heterogeneity of functional bacteria and their synergetic and competitive interactions. We did not find any obvious spatial heterogeneity within the bacterial population in different size-fractionated sludge samples, but the main functional bacteria varied significantly with operation time. Thauera was enriched (9.26~13.63%) as the core functional genus in the BSC-EBPR reactors, linking denitrifying phosphorus removal to sulfide oxidation. The other two functional genera were sulfate-reducing Desulfobacter (4.31~12.85%) and nitrate-reducing and sulfide-oxidizing Thiobacillus (4.79~9.92%). These bacteria cooperated in the BSC-EBPR process: Desulfobacter reduce sulfate to sulfide for utilization by Thiobacillus, while Thauera and Thiobacillus competed for nitrate and sulfide as well as Thauera and Desulfobacter competed for acetate. Moreover, the functional populations in the new SEBPR system were identified by a combination of flow cytometry cell sorting, gene footprint separation and 16S DNA high-throughput sequencing - an uncultured genus close to Rhodobacteraceae at the family level is speculated to be the putative sulfur PAO (SPAO). Objective 5 – Evaluation of the BSC-EBPR performance under various operation conditions The effect of different pH levels (6.5, 7.0, 7.5, 8.0 and 8.5), temperatures (20, 25, 30 and 35 oC) and influent acetate to propionate ratios (100–0, 75–25, 50–50, 25–75 and 0–100%, fractions of total organic carbon) on the anaerobic metabolism and performance were further investigated in series of batch tests. A neutral pH (7.0–7.5), relatively warm conditions (25–30 oC) and a mixture of carbon sources (75–25 and 50–50% of acetate to propionate ratios) were found to best support the anaerobic stoichiometry and kinetics conversion of the functional bacteria (i.e. sulfate-reducing (SRB) and sulfide-oxidizing bacteria (SOB)), thus maximizing their ability in competition against glycogen-accumulating organisms. Upon the realization of this task, the know-how of BSC-EBPR under different operating condition was obtained for process design, operation and optimization of this new EPBR.

16213515.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213515.value: The underpinning research on mechanisms and communities of BSC-EBPR were conducted in this research project. The key findings were summarized as follows: • A synergistic relationship exists between anaerobic sulfate reduction and biological P removal, viz. maximum P removal could be achieved at the appropriate values of 15–40 mg S/L sulfate reduced. • Sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB) and sulfide-oxidizing bacteria (SOB) work synergistically for biological P removal in the BSC-EBPR process. At the steady state, SRB and SOB were enriched by 18% and 16% respectively. • Gradually increasing the superficial up-flow velocity from 5.1 to 6.8 m/h and maintaining the OLR at 112.4 mg COD/g VSS/day proved to be an effective strategy for accelerating granulation without jeopardizing the reactor performance. • The optimal values for reactor operation were found to be at neutral pH range of 7.0~7.5, a relatively higher temperature of 25–30 oC and a mixed carbon source of 75–25 and 50–50% of HAc to HPr ratios. • Raman analysis displays the co-existence S0/Sn2− species in bacteria stored either intracellularly or extracellularly, and their dynamic conversions to other sulfur species suggest that there might be a universal pool of bioavailable sulfur. • The conventional PAO of Candidatus Accumulibacter was found at a low abundance of 0.32% only; and an uncultured genus close to Rhodobacteraceae at the family level is speculated to be the putative sulfur PAO (SPAO).

16213515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213515.value: The functional bacteria and their metabolisms remain unclear; hence the recommendation for future studies are as follows: 1) the metagenomic and metatranscriptomic studies are necessary to obtain more detailed information about the microbial community as well as insights into the pathways of S conversion; 2) tests should be conducted to determine the long-term effects of the key factors including pH, temperature, and C source on BSC-EBPR, especially the competition between SRB & SOB and GAOs, and to account for potential microbial shift and adaptations; and 3) different strategies for better control of pH and temperature require further study. It is recommended to build or use activated sludge models or metabolic models describing S and P cycles to simulate the behavior of BSC-EBPR systems and predict performance.

16213515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213515.value: (BSC-EBPR) process has been developed for treating sulfate-rich wastewater. This process has successfully integrated sulfur (S), carbon (C), nitrogen (N) and P cycles for simultaneous metabolism or removal of C, N and P; moreover this new process relies on the synergy among the slow-growing sulfate-reducing bacteria and sulfur-oxidizing bacteria, hence generating little excess sludge. To elucidate this new process, in this research we have investigated the microorganisms proliferated in the system, identified the biochemical pathways and assessed the impact of operational and environmental factors on process performance as well as trials on process optimization.

16213615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213615.value: In performance-based earthquake engineering, a large number of ground-motion time histories are often needed for nonlinear structural and geotechnical analysis. However, actual recorded ground-motion data are often quite limited. Especially, recorded motions at design levels are very rare, and may not be sufficient for characterizing structural responses. As an alternative approach, ground motions can be simulated using numerical methods. This project aims at developing an innovative stochastic simulation technique using wavelet packets for better characterization, generation and modification of ground motion time histories. The new ground-motion simulation and modification technique can be used to reliably estimate the seismic performance of a variety of nonlinear structures and geotechnical systems. Three-interrelated tasks are identified: First, wavelet packet analysis is used to characterize the time- and frequency-varying characteristics (termed as “nonstationarity”) of ground motions. Based on the wavelet-packet characterization, the project will develop a simulation technique to generate spatially distributed three-component ground-motion time histories, which can preserve the natural variability and spatial correlations of ground-motion waveforms. The ground-motion variability and spatial correlations are particularly important for analyzing spatially distributed structures, as well as hazard analysis and loss estimation in a regional scale. The model will be empirically calibrated using a large number of strong motion data from California, Japan, Taiwan and other regions. It will also be systematically validated using empirical relationships and blind tests using historical earthquakes. Second, a new ground-motion simulation and modification technique is developed to generate energy-compatible and spectrum-compatible (ECSC) ground motions through wavelet-packet characterization and optimization. The ECSC method significantly advances traditional ground-motion modification approaches by generating more realistic time series that not only match target response spectra, but also match other important characteristics not well considered in traditional approaches, such as energy build-up and ground-motion duration. Finally, the performance of the proposed ECSC technique will be systematically validated using a variety of structural and geotechnical models, including simple elasto-plastic hysteretic systems, typical low and high-rise buildings, nonlinear liquefiable grounds, as well as sliding masses. By using actual recorded ground motions and modified ones by the ECSC method and other traditional techniques, these extensive numerical simulations will highlight the effects of ground-motion modification on the response of a wide range of nonlinear systems, and provide practical guidelines for using spectrally matched ground motions in nonlinear structural and geotechnical analysis. 基於性能的非線性結構和岩土地震工程設計往往需要大量的地震波時程響應分析。然而，實測地震波數據非常有限，符合設計水準的大震記錄更少，不足以分析結構動力響應的特性。作為一種替代的方法，地震波可以用數值方法來模擬。本研究項目旨在利用小波包分析法開發一種新型的地震波模擬和改造技術，能更好的表徵、模擬和改造地震波時程，以更可靠的預測各種非線性結構和岩土工程系統的地震動力響應。 本研究項目有三個相互關聯的課題：首先，用小波包分析方法來表徵地震波在時域和頻域上的變化特性（稱作“非平穩性”）。基於小波包的表徵方法，本研究將開發空間分佈的三向地震波模擬技術。本技術能保持地震波波形的自然變化性和空間相關性，對空間結構及區域性災害分析和震害評估極其重要。本模型將利用來自加州、日本、台灣等地區的大量實測地震波來標定，並用多個經驗模型和盲測試驗進行驗證。 其次，通過小波包表徵及優化技術，本研究將開發一種能量和反應譜雙重匹配的新型地震波模擬和改造技術（稱為ECSC技術）。 ECSC技術能極大地改進傳統方法的不足，所生成的地震波更加逼真，不但能匹配給定的反應譜，而且能匹配地震波的能量積累過程及時程等重要參數。而後者用傳統技術無法實現。 最後，本研究將應用各種結構和岩土工程模型，系統地驗證ECSC技術。這些驗證模型包括簡單的彈塑性滯回系統、典型的低層和高層結構、可液化土體、以及土坡滑動體等。本研究將通過對比實測地震波、用ECSC技術及其它傳統技術模擬的地震波，重點研究各種地震波模擬與改造技術對非線性體統動力響應的影響，並為在非線性結構和岩土工程中使用模擬地震波提供指引。

16213615.label: Realisation of objectives
16213615.value: Project objective 1 has been fully achieved. The PI and his coworkers have successfully developed an innovative stochastic simulation method using wavelet packets. Spatial correlation model for key wavelet parameters has been calibrated using strong-motion data from California, Japan and Taiwan. Our study demonstrated that the wavelet-based model is successful to stochastically simulate spatially correlated ground-motion waveforms on a regional scale for future earthquakes. As part of this study, two case studies are conducted using the Northridge and Chi-Chi earthquake data. The model capability is verified in blind tests by comparing simulated time histories with the actual recorded data. Success in the objective 1 formed a solid basis for the objectives 2 and 3. Project Objective 2 has been fully achieved. The spectrum-compatible and energy-compatible (ECSC) ground-motion simulation and modification technique have been successfully developed based on the wavelet packet technique developed in objective 1. As expected in the proposal, our study demonstrated that the ECSC algorithm can successfully generate artificial ground motions that match spectral acceleration, cumulative Arias intensity and duration, which is a major advancement over traditional spectral matching methods. A paper [J3] summarizing the ECSC method has been published in Earthquake Engineering & Structural Dynamics, which is a top SCI journal in the field. As ground-motion duration is a key component of the ECSC algorithm, we proposed new prediction equations for ground-motion durations using an updated strong-motion database. The paper published in the flagship journal Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America [J2]. We also proposed prediction equations for effective number of cycles and its correlation with other ground motion intensity measures. Two journal papers were published in Soil Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering [J4, J12]. Project Objective 3 has been fully achieved. We developed extensive numerical models to validate the ECSC technique using a variety of nonlinear structural and geotechnical systems, including seismic slope displacement analysis [J5, J6, J7, J9], nonlinear seismic dynamics of breakwater, pile foundation in liquefied soils [J1, J8, J14], nonlinear site response [J10, J11, J13]. The numerical simulations demonstrate that the ECSC ground motions can predict nonlinear response of these systems rather accurately, and have great potential to be used in performance-based earthquake engineering design. To date, the research findings have been actively disseminated in top international journals, various local, national and international conferences. The research results have been accepted for an oral presentation in The 16th World Conference on Earthquake Engineering in January 2017 in Santiago, Chile, which is the most prestigious earthquake engineering conference held in every four years and attended by 3000 researchers around the world. The research work has also been delivered as a keynote lecture and invited lectures in The 1st International Symposium on Soil Dynamics and Geotechnical Sustainability, The 2nd Huixian International Forum on Earthquake Engineering for Young Researchers, The 3rd International Conference on Performance-based Design in Earthquake Geotechnical Engineering (PBD-III) in Vancouver, Canada, July 2018.

16213615.value: In the near future, we will develop a user-friendly software package for ECSC simulation to be freely accessed by the public. We believe the software can greatly increase the impact of the work and promote its usage among researchers and partitioning engineers around the world.

16213615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213615.value: To design civil infrastructure against earthquakes, a large number of ground motions are needed to perform dynamic analyses. However, actual recorded ground motions are often quite limited, and insufficient for characterizing structural responses. In this research project, we develop a new method to simulate artificial ground motions using numerical methods, which is an important yet challenging task. To generate artificial motions as real as possible, this project successfully developed an innovative method using wavelet packet analysis. Subsequently, ECSC technique based on the wavelet method is developed to modify ground motions in order to achieve targeted properties in terms of time, frequency and energy characteristics. The model is based on analyses of thousands of real ground motions, so it well preserves important characteristics of real ground motions. To demonstrate the performance of the developed model, we directly compare the ECSC artificial ground motions and actual recorded motions in dynamic response of a variety of structures and geotechnical systems. These extensive analyses validated that the proposed method can be reliably used to predict nonlinear seismic responses of structures and geotechnical systems. Therefore, the research outcome can greatly advance the use of artificial ground motions in performance-based earthquake engineering design.

16213715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16213715.value: 用於Li-Fi網絡的可見光通訊發射器晶片系統

16213715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213715.value: Solid-state lighting (SSL), renewable energy and smart power grids are among the major initiatives being deployed worldwide for building a more sustainable environment. In particular, the SSL revolution of replacing conventional lightings by LEDs is projected to cut global electricity consumption by 15% beyond 2020. The ubiquitous deployment of LED lights also provides an opportunity for innovative optical applications other than just simply for lighting. An emerging technology under intense research is the use of LED lights for wireless communication known as visible light communication (VLC). The operating principle is to modulate the LED driver with a data stream at high speed. Since human eyes have “low-pass filter” characteristics, they will not sense the high-speed “flickering” of the light. Compared with traditional radio-frequency (RF) wireless communications, VLC is advantageous in terms of high security, no RF radiation, wide available spectrum and transceiver simplicity. Currently, VLC is being regarded as an effective form of wireless communication supplementing conventional RF communication as well as providing some new wireless applications uniquely achievable with this technology. In particular, the Li-Fi (Light Fidelity) market based on VLC is projected to have a compound annual growth rate of 82% and reach over $6 billion per year by 2018. With great efforts from both academia and industry, the VLC technology has achieved significant progress. As an example, a single VLC link achieving over 100 Mb/s has been demonstrated using commercial LED lamps. However, the power consumption is prohibitively high due to the usage of discrete components. In addition, the estimated energy efficiency of a discrete VLC system is about 20-100 nJ/bit, which is about 100 times lower than the state-of-the-art Wi-Fi's efficiency of 0.2-1 nJ/bit depending on the range. System-on-a-chip (SoC) will be a promising solution to achieving better power efficiency, high reliability, smaller system form factors and lower costs to enable practical Li-Fi applications. Unfortunately, the relevant research is still in the very early stage and no example is available. This project aims to research and develop a fully integrated VLC transmitter SoC in CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor) technology for Li-Fi networks, targeting at a data rate of 5Mb/s over 2 meters. The energy efficiency is expected to reach 10x better than discrete VLC systems. 固態照明，可再生能源和智能電網這三者均為構建可持續發展環境的重要科技。隨著LED逐漸取代傳統照明燈具，預計固態照明技術將於2020年節省15％的全球電力消耗。在提供照明的同時，LED還使一些新穎的應用成為可能。其中，目前學術界深入研究的一個新興技術是利用LED來實現可見光通訊（VLC）。其工作原理是，用高速數據流調製LED驅動器從而使LED發出的可見光包含數據信息。在接收端，則用光傳感器將數據信息檢測並解調出來。由於人眼具有“低通濾波器”的特點從而不會感覺到調製光的高速閃爍，普通的照明功能不受影響。與傳統的RF（射頻）無線通信相比，VLC具有更高的安全性及更寬的可用頻譜，同時具有無RF輻射及收發器結構簡單等優點。目前，VLC已被視為常規RF通信的有效補充，其獨有的特性也使一些新的無線應用成為可能。需要指出的是，預計基於VLC的Li-Fi無線通訊市場將以82％的複合年均增長率增長，並於2018年達到60億美圓。 近年來，通過學術界和工業界的科研和產業化投入，VLC技術取得了顯著的進步。目前，基於普通LED燈具搭建的單個VLC鏈路已經可以實現超過100Mb/s的數據率。然而， 由於廣泛使用分立元件，VLC系統的功率消耗很高。據估算，離散VLC系統的能源效率約為20-100nJ/bit，比當前最先進的Wi-Fi無線通訊系統高約100倍。參照其它商用通訊產品的發展歷史，系統的集成化將是一種有效的解決方案。系統晶片（SoC）可以實現高能源效率，高可靠性，較小的系統體積及更低的成本，為Li-Fi的普及應用鋪平道路。但是，相關的研究還處於剛剛起步階段，沒有實例可以參考。本項目旨在研究和開發一個CMOS（互補金屬氧化物半導體）全集成的VLC發射器系統晶片，目標是實現2米以上的傳輸距離及5Mb/s以上的數據速率。初步估計其能源效率將比離散系統高10倍。

16213915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213915.value: 近年來，隨著進一步縮小半導體器件尺寸的要求仍在繼續，一維半導體器件比如基於納米線的器件因此受到廣泛的關注和研究。由於其自身的極小尺寸及一維特性，納米線可提供與其薄膜材料或體材料完全不同的電學及光學性質。在眾多納米線材料當中，寬禁帶氮化鎵納米線尤為得到研究者的關注，因為氮化鎵納米線具備作為下一代納米電子及納米光電子器件結構單元的潛能。 在過去的十年當中，關於氮化鎵納米線的研究集中在豎直類型或平面外類型上。 然而，利用現代平面製造工藝在這些平面外納米線上做電學金屬接觸是非常困難的。其中一個方法是先收集再散播到另一個新的襯底上以便進行工藝處理。然而用這個方法來處理一些非常長的比如毫米級別長的納米線將會變得十分困難。 更為重要的是，先收集再轉移的方法無法控制納米線的晶向，從而某種程度上限制了納米線的廣泛應用。 橫向或平面內氮化鎵納米線因其與平面製造工藝天然的兼容性而可以進行原位工藝處理。這一點對於納米線器件的製造及集成尤為重要。迄今為止，關於橫向氮化鎵納米線合成的報道僅有少數幾例，並且全都依賴於使用納米金屬顆粒作為催化劑。而金屬催化劑常常會在半導體納米線中成為污染源。與之不同，在無需使用催化劑的條件下，我們成功地在納米多孔的基板上合成了氮化鎵納米線。在此基礎上，本研究計劃將合成及研究兩類重要的氮化鎵納米線器件：1）基於氮化鎵納米線的半極性發光二極管。初步試驗表明橫向氮化鎵納米線存有兩個半極性面（10-11）可供進一步沉積發光二極管外延層。 這種方法無需使用昂貴的半極化氮化鎵襯底，也避免了使用刻蝕方法產生半極性面帶來的損傷。與被廣泛研究的氮化鎵半極性面（11-22）不同，關於氮化鎵（10-11）半極性面的研究仍不完善。本研究計劃對半極性發光二極管的研究將豐富關於氮化鎵（10-11）這一特定半極性面的研究內容。2）基於氮化鎵納米線的高電子遷移率集體管。利用橫向納米線平行排布的特性，由壹， 貳，或者多條納米線組成的晶體管將被研製。考慮到納米線自身巨大的表面積/體積比率，納米線晶體管將被用來研究各類表面處理和鈍化方法，從而為最終實現高效而可靠的高電子遷移率集體管提供依據。

16213915.label: Realisation of objectives
16213915.value: The primary goal of this project is to study horizontal III-Nitride nanowire-based electronic and optoelectronic devices. Currently, there are two major technologies for NW fabrication. One is the bottom-up growth method, in which NW structure is directly grown on plane substrates in association with catalyst or metal-based mask. There are several drawbacks of this method such as Mg incorporation, doping level uncertainty and unexpected sidewall growth. The other method, top-down etching, starting from thin-film structure with well-defined junction location and doping levels, utilizes standard dry etching and wet etching process to form nanorods. In this project, we mainly focused on the top-down etching method to demonstrate horizontal III-N nanowires with controlled doping concentration, including both p-i-n and n-i-n structures. GaN single NW p-i-n diode was fabricated using GaN epi grown on Sapphire by Metal Organic Chemical Vapor Deposition (MOCVD). The p-i-n structure started from a 1.5-µm thick graded AlGaN buffer, followed by a 1-µm thick Si-doped n-GaN layer (~ n= 2×1018 cm-3), a 500-nm thick undoped i-GaN layer, and a 500-nm thick Mg-doped p-type GaN (~ p = 2×1017 cm-3). Using silica spheres 1 um in diameter as etching masks, Nano-wires 200um in diameter were fabricated by dry etching and transferred to a SiO2/Si carrier. The single NW p-i-n diode exhibits reasonable rectifying I-V curves with turn-on voltage of 3.1 V at 1 A/cm2 and leakage as low as 3.2 pA at -10 V, which is comparable with the GaN thin film p-i-n diodes. The ideality factor can be extracted as n =3.9 after the diode was turned on. With UV illumination, repeatable and evident photo current (~ 1.5 pA) of GaN single NW p-i-n diode was observed. The UV light (λ=365 nm) power density was calculated to be 4.5 mW/cm2, according to the photo current of Si PD. So the responsivity can be determined as 0.21 A/W at -2 V, corresponding internal quantum efficiency as high as 70%. Compared to the thin film devices, GaN single NW p-i-n diode presents almost one order higher responsivity due to the defect-free property. Moreover, the visible-blind property of GaN single NW p-i-n diode as a result of intrinsic wide bandgap of GaN. The photo responsivity increases slightly with the rising temperature which indicates thermal stability of the photo response. Using the same method, GaN single NW n-i-n device was also investigated. Under 1 V bias, dark current of 7.71 pA, IUV/Idark of 528 and responsivity of 7069 can be derived. Different from the thin film device, no linear photocurrent was observed in nanowire. It is obvious that under high UV intensity density (larger than 2.88×10-3 W/cm2), the photocurrent has been saturated. The photocurrent can be divided into two part. Under low voltage (< 0.3V), the photocurrent was linear. While under high voltage part (> 0.3V), the photocurrent followed the relation of I~V2.5. We investigated the direct growth of large-area 2D MoS2 film on a SiO2/p-GaN/Si substrate for fabrication of MoS2 top-gated transistors and MoS2/SiO2/p-GaN tunnel diodes. The representative I-V curves of the SIS heterojunction diode which had the same p-contact and n-contact area (0.01 mm2) and inter-pad distance of 5.5 μm. The threshold voltage and series resistance of the diode was extracted to be 5.0 V and 5.3 kΩ. The series resistance was slightly smaller than the SIS tunnel diode made of MoS2/h-BN/p-GaN. The forward current increased rapidly beyond the threshold voltage and at 25 V, the on-state current was measured to be 2.92 mA, which is translated to a current density of 29 A/cm2. To the best of our knowledge, this current is one of the largest currents reported for the 2D material/GaN vertically-stacked diodes, showing the great potential of SIS diodes in this work to be used as a switch. Under reverse bias, the diode showed good current blocking characteristics and the leakage current was measured to be only 30 µA at -10V. Moreover, no breakdown was observed for reverse voltage up to -25 V.

16213915.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213915.value: Horizontal III-N p-i-n and n-i-n nanowires Horizontal GaN single NW p-i-n and n-i-n devices are demonstrated using a top-down method, which presents reasonable I-V and photovoltaic response. For p-i-n devices, the rectifying I-V shows normal turn-on voltage and low leakage level which is corresponding to GaN intrinsic property. The photovoltaic and visible-blind response indicates that GaN single NW p-i-n diode is suitable for application of UV detection or solar cell. For n-i-n devices, the high Iph/Idark ratio and responsivity indicate the potential for high-sensitivity UV detecting applications 2D/3D MoS2/GaN stack devices The direct growth of large-area 2D MoS2 film on a SiO2/p-GaN/Si substrate has been investigated for fabrication of MoS2 top-gated transistors and MoS2/SiO2/p-GaN tunnel diodes. The as-grown MoS2 thin film was characterized by AFM, SEM, and Raman spectroscopy. Fabricated top-gated FETs showed a large on/off current ratio ~105, a subthreshold swing of 74 mV/dec, carrier mobility of ~0.17 cm2/V-s, and current saturation over a wide drain voltage range. A vertically stacked SIS heterojunction diode that consists of a few layers of as-grown MoS2, a thin SiO2, and p-GaN was also fabricated. The I-V characteristics showed a good current rectifying property with a large on-state current of 2.92 mA and small reverse current when reversed biased. The reported device results suggested great opportunities of implementing electronics using the large area 2D/3D material stacks. Advanced device technology for thin film-based p-i-n diodes The growth and fabrication of fully- and quasi-vertical GaN-on-Si p-i-n diodes are demonstrated. Both types of diodes demonstrate low differential specific on-resistance (Ron) and similarly high breakdown voltage (Vbr). Record high Baliga figure-of-merit (FOM) of 0.3 GW/cm2 has been achieved for GaN-on-Si fully-vertical diodes. A detailed comparison has also been made between these two kinds of devices starting from the same epitaxial wafer, regarding forward and reverse I-V characteristics, thermal behaviors, and switching performance. The fully- and quasi-vertical diodes shared nearly-identical but superior recovery performance compared with a commercial Si rectifier. The device characteristics indicate that both kinds of diodes are promising low-cost options for high power applications.

16213915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213915.value: Optimization of top-down etching method There is still much room to improve the etching process. For example, we utilized randomly distributed silica spheres as dry etching mask, which provides poor protection/coverage of the NW top surface, leading to multiple sidewall planes exposed after wet etching. To address this issue, Ni-based metal stack can be adopted as the dry etching mask. Integration of III-N nanowire devices with other optoelectronic devices GaN and its alloy compounds have been applied to a wide scope of electronic and optoelectronic devices. Based on the superior properties of GaN NW devices, it is meaningful to construct an integrated system to include light emitting devices such as LEDs or LDs while the NW device compactly incorporated as photon detecting components.

16213915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213915.value: In this project, we developed a top-down etching method, which starts from thin-film structure with well-defined junction location and doping levels and utilizes standard dry etching and wet etching process to form nanowires. After the etching process, the nanowires were transferred onto another carrier substrate and then metalized on different regions to realize device functions. Horizontal III-N nanowires with controlled doping concentration are demonstrated wtih p-i-n and n-i-n structures. For p-i-n devices, quantum efficiency as high as 70% was achieved. Compared to the thin film devices, GaN single NW p-i-n diode presents almost one order higher responsivity due to their high material quality. It is also experimentally illustrated that GaN single NW p-i-n diode holds good visible-blind property as a result of GaN’s wide energy bandgap. Those results shows that GaN single NW p-i-n diode is suitable for UV detection applications. In addition to nanowires fabrication and study, a platform of 2D/3D MoS2/GaN stack devices were investigated. Moreover, advanced device technology for thin film-based p-i-n diodes and their switching performance have also been well investigated in this project.

To perform theoretical analysis on the obtained systematic data, to explore the different dominant physical mechanisms underlying the observed correlations between grain size and fatigue life, and finally to establish links among grain size, interfaces, hysteresis and fatigue resistance of the material.

16214215.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214215.value: The major findings of the project are the following: Grain size (GS) dependent fatigue crack growth behaviors of nanocrystalline superelastic NiTi shape memory alloys (SMAs) with the average GS of 10 , 30, 60 and 235 nm are investigated by synchronized measurements of the fatigue crack growth, load displacement response and temperature field of the crack tip region of the compact tension specimen. It is found that the fatigue crack growth rate (d a /d N) is monotonically decreased by 10 times when the GS is increased from 10 to 235 nm. The significant increase of fatigue crack growth resistance with GS is also supported by direct observations of fatigue striation spacing on the post mortem fracture surface. It is shown that the increase of GS brings significantly enhanced phase transition and ductility of the material and thus causes an enhanced shielding to the crack tip and a reduction of the effective driving force (ΔKeff) to the fatigue crack growth. Subtracting such crack tip shielding (ΔKsh) due to reversible phase transition and irreversible plastic deformation from the applied ΔKapp, the effective crack tip stress intensity ΔKeff can be obtained. Then the da /dN ∝ ΔKeff curves for different GS specimens become almost GS independent and the intrinsic GS independent and the intrinsic fatigue property of the nanocrystalline NiTi SMAs can be identified. The analysis of the results revealed that the crack-tip shielding effect from the GS dependent phase transition and plastic deformation are responsible for the enhanced fatigue crack growth resistance of superelastic NiTi SMAs. The above major findings are partly summarized in the 4 published papers in the following journals 1. Int. J. of Fatigue 2. Scripta Mater. 3. Acta Mechanica Solida Sinica 4. J. Mater. Research. and will be partly summarized in 2 additional working papers.

16214215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214215.value: The research outcome of this project provides a theoretical and experimental bases for the future development of nanostructured fatigue resistant materials in the environment friendly green solid-state refrigeration technology.

16214215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214215.value: With the fast development of nanotechnology and the race for better material performance, extreme grain refinement of polycrystals and nano-scale phase transition have become active research topics in recent years. This project, through both experimental and theoretical studies, shows that when the GS is reduced down to nano-scale, not only is the phase transition significantly suppressed, but also the fatigue resistance also decreases rapidly. It is revealed that such significant effects of GS reduction on the fatigue responses originate from the GS dependent crack tip shielding effects.

16214315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214315.value: In 25 years of research on statistical machine translation, it is somewhat disturbing that no systems have ever been trained to directly maximize the objective of preserving meaning - which should naturally be the primary aim of translation - until our initial feasibility demonstrations this past year. We aim to significantly advance the meaningfulness of statistical machine translation output via a radical new learning approach: to induce tree-structured translation models driven by semantic objective functions, MEANT and XMEANT, which are our newly developed monolingual and cross-lingual automatic translation evaluation metrics based purely on semantic frames, recently shown to correlate more closely than current metrics against human judgments of translation adequacy. To attack the difficult challenge of bilingual semantic grammar induction we will be leveraging heavy foundations from multiple strands of our previous work, combining for the first time three critical strategies: our (1) semantic objective functions, (2) semantically motivated internal representation structures that can be automatically learned, and (3) bootstrapping induction methods. We will leverage a large new architectural infrastructure platform we have constructed over the past four years for unsupervised induction of stochastic transduction grammars, which supports a wide variety of approaches to learning stochastic finite-state, linear, segmental, preterminalized, and inversion transduction grammars - ideal for experimentation with a large number of alternative bootstrapping training regimens. Our newly developed sets of foundations will now allow us to implement and systematically evaluate SMT performance when MEANT and XMEANT variants are supplied as semantic objective functions for the induction and parameter estimation of stochastic finite-state, linear, and inversion transduction grammars. Our initial feasibility studies have demonstrated the superb robustness characteristics of training using MEANT even for simpler flat phrase-based translation models - and tree-structured models are far better suited for representing semantic frames, strongly suggesting the high promise of our proposed new semantically driven learning approach. 在25年的統計機器翻譯研究，它是有點令人不安的是，沒有系統曾經被訓練直接最大限度地保護意義的目標 - 這自然應該翻譯的主要目的 - 直到我們的初步可行性演示在過去的一年。我們的目標是顯著推進統計機器翻譯輸出的意義，通過一種全新的學習方法：誘使通過語義目標函數，意味著和XMEANT，這是我們新開發的單語和跨語言自動翻譯的評價指標驅動的樹形結構的翻譯模型純粹基於語義框架，最近的研究顯示，以更緊密地相關比對翻譯充足的人力判斷當前度量。攻擊的雙語語義語法歸納，我們將充分利用我們以前的工作中多股重基礎，首次結合三個關鍵戰略的嚴峻挑戰：我們（1）語義的目標函數，（2）語義動機內部表示結構的能自動獲悉，和（3）引導誘導方法。我們將充分利用我們構造了過去四年的無監督歸納隨機傳導語法，它支持各種各樣的方法來學習隨機有限狀態，線性，分段，preterminalized和反轉傳導語法一個新的大型建築的基礎架構平台 - 理想的試驗用大量替代引導訓練方案。我們新開發的集基礎的，現在讓的意思，XMEANT變體提供語義目標函數隨機有限狀態，線性和反演傳導語法歸納和參數估計，當我們執行和系統評價SMT的性能。我們的初步可行性研究已經證實了培訓使用意味著即使是簡單的扁平基於短語的翻譯模型高超的穩健性特徵 - 和樹形結構模型更好的適合表示語義框架，有力地說明我們提出的新的語義驅動學習的高承諾做法。

16214315.label: Realisation of objectives
16214315.value: In this project we have (1) improved the semantic adequacy of statistical machine translation technology, without sacrificing translation fluency, (2) developed new paradigms for automatic induction of cross-lingual lexical semantics abstractions that allow direct optimization of semantic adequacy, rather than merely output language fluency, by directly maximizing the degree to which translation preserves meaning via automatic monolingual semantic objective functions, bilingual semantic objective functions, or both, and (3) advanced our understanding of the cognitive bootstrapping processes in incremental learning of cross-lingual semantic transduction grammars denoting generalizations over cross-lingual semantic frames and semantic dependencies - which integrate context-dependent, compositional semantic relationships between a pair of languages, at varying levels of lexicalization and abstraction. To achieve this we have developed and prototyped new methods for semantically driven transduction grammar induction. Crucially, we have greatly increased the influence of semantics upon SMT (statistical machine translation) training, by successfully shifting the semantic frame based objective functions all the way to the earliest stage of the training pipeline, instead of the last stage of the training pipeline as was done in our initial feasibility studies. Our initial models had applied our semantic frame based MEANT translation accuracy metric as the objective function being optimized by the final phase of (MERT/MIRA based) tuning of a dozen or so parameters in phrase-based SMT loglinear models. Although this was successful at improving translation quality, applying this only at the end of the long training pipeline greatly limited the much greater potential of semantics to influence training of SMT. We have now instead developed a variety of new approaches that strongly inject the semantic frame biases at the very beginning of the SMT training pipeline, namely the EM (expectation maximization) training of ITG word alignments. The IBM word alignment models widely used in phrase-based SMT were replaced instead with our bracketing ITG (inversion transduction grammar) model. Since ITGs have previously been shown to be highly biased toward exactly the kind of cross-lingual semantic frame alternations we would want SMT to learn, this change makes the word alignment model much more absorbent of the semantic frame based signals from MEANT style objective functions. Our new approaches include methods not only for high-resource foreign input languages, but also for low-resource languages. We developed a battery of new methods for ITG induction in the face of low-resource conditions. We have introduced a new approach for category (part-of-speech) induction that leverages heterogenous resources from a variety of resources from the high-resource output language, such as English treebanks, to amplify the utility of the small amount of parallel resources available for the low-resource input language (WMCM @NAACL 2016). For low-resource languages, it has until now been widely assumed that semantic frame based techniques would be challenging, since automatic semantic parsers are not available for low-resource languages. This is indeed true of our new methods for high-resource languages (SML @IJCAI2016, StarSEM 2016, OCOCOSDA 2016, SLT 2016): these techniques employ XMEANT (the cross-lingual version of MEANT) which requires shallow semantic parsers for both the input and output languages, thus ruling out low-resource languages. In addition, however, we have now also developed a family of new methods for low-resource languages: these new techniques employ monolingual MEANT which only requires a readily available shallow semantic parser for the output language (typically English or Chinese). We are very recently beginning to obtain consistent improvement of translation accuracy across different metrics (BLEU, TER, MEANT) even for low-resource languages including Uzbek, Uyghur, and artificially resource-impoverished Chinese as a control condition (Hytra 2016). These new approaches investigated different strategies for incorporating the semantic frame signals. Some of the approaches use the semantic frame signals to penalize word and tree alignment hypotheses within EM training of the ITG when they violate the alignment constraints predicted by the semantic frame based objectives (StarSEM 2016, OCOCOSDA 2016, Hytra 2016, SLT 2016). Others use a more recent strategy that also shows promise, namely to use the semantic frame signals to weight the confidence of individual training instances during expectation-maximization (EM) training of the ITG (SML @IJCAI2016). These strategies are independent, and therefore potentially complementary. In the process of improving the expectation-maximization (EM) training methods, we discovered and fixed a longstanding issue in the Viterbi variant of EM training. The handling of ties between equiprobable derivations during Viterbi training, which occur frequently, was historically glossed over in research papers. Whether they are broken randomly when they occur, or on an ad-hoc basis decided by the algorithm or implementation, or whether all equiprobable derivations are enumerated with the counts uniformly distributed among them was left to the readers imagination. The first hurts rarely occurring rules, which run the risk of being randomly eliminated, the second suffers from algorithmic biases, and the last is correct but potentially very inefficient. We have shown that it is possible to Viterbi train correctly without enumerating all equiprobable best derivations. The method is analogous to expectation maximization, given that the automatic differentiation view is chosen over the reverse value/outside probability view, as the latter calculates the wrong quantity for reestimation under the Viterbi semiring. To get the automatic differentiation to work we devised an unbiased subderivative for the max function (LATA 2018). In the later stages of the project, large amounts of implementation work was done in order to improve translation accuracy, by designing much larger scale experiments employing further new methods that combine and extend the successful models among our new techniques for automatically inducing cross-lingual abstractions driven by semantic adequacy objectives. The results were significantly improved and greatly scaled up. Work has successfully been extended across many more challenging low-resource languages including Amharic, Uyghur, Tigrinya and Oromo. Results show that our model influences the learning towards more semantically correct alignments, leading to better translation quality than both the standard ITG or GIZA++ based SMT training models on different datasets (EAMT 2018, and in Meriem Beloucif's PhD thesis). We have also engineered a much improved version of the semantic objective function and translation evaluation metric, MEANT, that we developed for use in this work (Chi-kiu Lo's PhD thesis, with the assistance of Karteek Addanki in the course of his PhD thesis). Three PhD theses have been produced during the course of this work, contributing to various aspects of the project: those of Meriem Beloucif, Chi-kiu Lo, and Karteek Addanki.

16214315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214315.value: We have developed the first known techniques to inject semantic frame influence into early stages of machine translation training. This family of new methods inject semantic structure biases at the earliest stages of the training pipeline, which are the expectation-maximization based word alignment models. No previous machine translation models have ever done this. The new training methods directly maximize the degree to which translation preserves semantic measures of accuracy, and reflect a significant step toward a more cognitively plausible translation training approach. Moreover, we developed new variants of this model to tackle translation from low-resource languages for which there are very limited sources of training data of the sort typically used for training translation for common high-resource language pairs such as Chinese-English or between European languages. Unlike earlier versions of our models, these new techniques do not require semantic parsers for the input low-resource language, which are typically not available. Along with improvements in semantic translation adequacy, We have shown that our techniques influence the machine learning toward more semantically correct alignments. This explains why the new models obtain higher translation accuracy compared with standard machine training models, given the same amounts of training data.

16214315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214315.value: One of the most exciting further developments of this research, which we are currently exploring, is to extend the approach of injecting semantic frame information into training not only symbolic inversion transduction grammar models, but instead also our neural deep learning transduction grammar models. Our TRAAM (transduction recursive auto-associative memory) family of deep learning models is particularly well suited to absorbing frame based constraints, both hard and soft, as well as objective functions. This will attack the problem that current deep learning models still do not have good internal semantic structure models.

16214315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214315.value: Machine translation based on machine learning has made tremendous progress in the past quarter century since we helped pioneer it, yet current systems still have only the most rudimentary understanding of the meaning of sentences they are translating. Instead of learning the right generalizations about how meaning is interpreted/translated, current systems rely on memorizing huge amounts of data and playing fancy word games. This project focused on new approaches that allow semantic structure to strongly influence generalizations made by machine learning when training translation systems. This allows much smaller amounts of training data to be used, with both scientific and practical benefits. Scientifically speaking, children learn to interpret/translate language from tiny amounts of training data in comparison to current translation systems, and our directions will be much more cognitively plausible. Practically speaking, this will allow translation systems to be trained even for low-resource languages where very limited amounts of training data are available.
