16303415.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303415.value: We regard the outcome of this research project to be a singular experimental and theoretical achievement in a classic field of electrophoresis. In particular, we note the following items. (1) We have obtained the first full numerical solution of the relevant governing equations of electrophoresis—the Poisson-Nernst-Planck equations coupled with the Navier-Stokes equation, in the context of electrophoresis. Where prior researchers used linearization of the equations, here the full nonlinearity of the equations within the Debye layer was taken into account. As a result, we found that the electrophoretic flow is divided into two regimes: an inner regime and an outer regime. Whereas the outer flow regime coincided with the Smoluchowski solution extremely well, the inner flow region is a new finding. In particular, the inner flow region is characterized by a belt of vortices (in the laboratory frame), with a well-defined interface separating it from the outer flow regime. (2) The source of vorticity in the inner flow regime, arising from the net charge density within the Debye layer and the consequent large local electric field, represents something new that, to our knowledge, has never before been published. (3) We have carried out the first measurement of the electrophoretic drag coefficient by using an AC scheme, in which an optical tweezer was used to hold the single electrophoretic particle in a harmonic trap, and an AC electric field was used to drive the particle motion. A simple analysis of the AC experimental approach shows that the in-phase component of motion is driven only by the electric field, and this point is crucial in ensuring the experimental accuracy of obtaining the electrophoretic drag coefficient. (4) The measured electrophoretic drag coefficient is definitely non-Stokes, which is new. (5) The measured electrophoretic drag coefficient and the associated effective charge can be quantitatively explained theoretically by their values on the inner/outer interface, not on the surface of the solid particle. (6) The new elements of our findings constitute the missing element in the traditional theoretical framework that enables a consistent correlation between the theory and experiment on the inner/outer interface, as opposed to the solid sphere’s surface. (7) The distance of the inner/outer interface from the solid surface has an excellent power law dependence on the salt ion concentration, which is still un-explained mathematically and therefore can be an excellent problem for applied mathematicians.

16303415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303415.value: The electrophoretic drag coefficient is a central quantity of our research investigation; and we have found it to be non-Stokes in character. To further substantiate this finding, work is currently underway to measure the electrical dissipation as a function of concentration of the charged colloidal particles. This should represent an alternative approach to measure the drag coefficient. In theory, one of the authors, XU Shixin, is currently using mathematical analysis to obtain some rigorous result on the inner flow field, especially its width. However, since this can be a very difficult mathematical problem, it is not known if the goal can be achieved.

16303415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303415.value: Charge separation can occur at certain material’s interface with water (e.g., silica/water) in which the positive charge is dissociated from the interface, leaving behind a negatively charged surface charge. Such charge dissociation leads to an electrical double layer comprising the mobile positive charges and the negative surface charges. When an electric field is applied to this system, the net force on the system is zero, since the electrical double layer is charge neutral overall. In accordance with Newton’s laws, the center of mass momentum therefore must be zero. However, since the mobile positive charges will be moved by the electric field, it follows that the solid particle must move in the opposite direction in order to maintain zero overall momentum. Such solid particle motion is denoted electrophoresis. In this research project, we have focused on the hydrodynamic force experienced by the moving particle. By carrying out experiments as well as theoretical studies, we have uncovered something new—that the flow field around an electrophoretic particle can have an inner flow field that is carried along by the solid particle, whose interface with the well-known outer flow field is the key to understanding the drag force of an electrophoretic particle.

16303515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303515.value: Tilings appear in many natural structures such as honeycomb, crystals, molecular structures. Such natural structures also inspire man-made structures in engineering. Tiling is also an integral part of the human civilization. For example, it is an essential part of the islamic art and is also a recurring theme in the paintings of M. C. Escher. Mathematicians have studied tilings for more than 100 years, due to its beauty and wide applications in chemistry, biology, crystallography, architecture, and many other scientific and engineering fields. The major achievements in the tiling theory include the solution to Hilbert's 18th problem, the classification of wallpaper groups and crystallographic groups, and the classification of isohedral tilings of the plane. Compared with the abundance of literature on tilings of the plane, not much research has been done for the tilings of the sphere. The only major work in the field is the classification of tilings of the 2-sphere by congruent triangles, started in 1923 and completed in 2002. Our initial investigation of tilings of the 2-sphere by congruent pentagons revealed some very interesting properties, and we have obtained partial classifications in some relatively easy cases. We are confident that the complete classification is within our grasp. The primary aim of this proposal is to completely classify edge-to-edge tilings of the sphere by congruent pentagons. The secondary aim is to further study interesting phenomena we encounter in such an endeavor, such as the combinatorial aspects of the pentagonal tilings. Even if we cannot completely classify such tilings, the knowledge and technique we gain from such investigation would be very useful and have potential applications to other science and engineering fields. 拼圖的數學研究已有100多年的歷史，並廣泛應用於化學、生物學、晶體學、建築學等科學和工程領域。關於拼圖的主要數學結果有希爾伯特18問題的解決，牆紙群和晶體群的分類，和平面的等面（isohedral）拼圖的分類。 相比於平面拼圖的大量研究結果，關於球面拼圖的研究相當稀少。球面拼圖的唯一主要結果是三角形拼圖的分類，起始於1923年，直到2002年才全部完成。我們開始研究球面的五邊形拼圖，已經對一些簡單情況得到分類結果。根據已得到的結果，我們對球面五邊形拼圖的完全分類具有信心。 此研究項目的主要目的是球面五邊形（邊對邊）拼圖的完全分類，同時也希望在研究過程中發現一些相關的組合結果。就算我們得不到完全分類，我們仍舊預計得到的經驗和部分結果會在其它科學和工程領域找到應用。

16303615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303615.value: The proposed research is to study the spectral distribution of random matrices from some families of discrete sequences. In a recent joint work, the PI proved the "randomness" of matrices formed from binary linear codes with dual distance at least 5 with respect to the empirical spectral distribution. This improves the remarkable results of Babadi and Tarokh on several fronts and in particular confirms a "group randomness" property for sequences based on the Gold codes, a mysterious phenomenon observed and investigated by Babadi and Tarokh. Building on this success, the PI plans to employ various mathematical tools from number theory, graph theory and random matrix theory to investigate much further the concept of "group randomness". More precisely, for each of the interesting families of sequences such as sequences from binary linear codes, mutually unbiased bases, approximately mutually unbiased bases and more generally from near-orthogonal systems and from finite geometry all of which have important applications in compressed sensing, the PI plans to study the empirical spectral distribution of large random matrices arising from the sequences in two different ways and to compare the results with the random matrix theory. Other sequences and other statistics in the spirit of "group randomness" may also be considered. 本课题研究的是一些离散序列的随机矩阵的谱分布。在近期合作的文章里，相对于经验普分布而言，作者证明了对于从对偶距离至少为5的二元线性码产生的随机矩阵的随机性。这个结果改进了Babadi 和Tarokh之前的结果，特别的，验证了基于Gold码的序列的“群体随机性”。建立在这个结果之上，作者计划使用各种数学工具，继续深入研究“群体随机性”的概念。明确来说，对于一些意义重大的的序列，比如说由线性码，由相互无偏差正交基，以及更一般的由近似正交系和由有限几何产生的序列，这些序列在实际中都有很重要的应用，作者计划研究他们的随机矩阵的普分布。作者计划研究两种不同的普分布，普分布的结果将与随机矩阵理论作比较。

16303615.label: Realisation of objectives
16303615.value: Objective 1 is achieved in the finished preprint, titled "Spectral distribution of random matrices from Mutually Unbiased Bases" (see https://arxiv.org/submit/2978925). This paper is joint with Ch. Chan. It was submitted and is currently under journal review. Objective 2 is achieved: in the paper, titled "Random matrices from linear codes and Wigner's semicircle law", joint with C. Chan and E. Kung, IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory vol. 65, no. 10, page 6001-6009, 2019, we studied the empirical spectral distribution of matrices from linear codes normalized differently and proved the convergence to the Wigner's semicircle law. Objective 3 is achieved: in the paper, titled "On the complete weight distribution of subfield subcodes of algebraic-geometric codes", joint with C. Chan, which will appear in IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, we studied a new statistics, the so-called "complete weight distribution" and found randomness in subfield subcodes of general algebraic-geometric codes. Related to Objective 3, we also studied much further the empirical spectral distribution of matrices from linear codes, which resulted in two finished preprints, titled "Convergence rate of empirical spectral distribution of random matrices from linear codes" (https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.08428) and "Random matrices from linear codes and the convergence to Wigner's semicircle Law" (https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00323) respectively, joint with C. Chan and V. Tarokh. Currently these papers were under journal review, hopefully to be accepted for publication in the near future. In these two papers, we used advanced tools related to Stieltjes transform in random matrix theory to obtain a strong convergence rate of the empirical spectral distribution to the expected distribution laws.

16303615.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303615.value: In the published paper 1, joint with his two former students, the PI showed that the empirical spectral distribution of matrices from linear codes, normalized slightly differently, converges to Wigner's semicircle law, if the linear codes satisfy some natural conditions. This is another group randomness property for sequences from linar codes. In the published paper 2, joint with C. Chan, the PI showed that the so-called complete weight distribution function for subfield subcodes of general algebraic-geometric codes satisfy some randomness properties. This partially explain partly why such codes are good for applications in general. In preprints 3 and 4 which were submitted, joint with coauthors, the PI obtained strong convergence of the empirical spectral distribution of matrices formed from linear codes of dual distance 5 to the expected distribution. In preprint 5 which was submitted very recently, joint with C. Chan, the PI studied the spectral distribution of random matrices from mutually unbiased bases and found the convergence of the limiting distribution to the expected distribution laws.

16303615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303615.value: Given the strong convergence of the empirical spectral distribution of matrices from linear codes to the expected distribution laws, the PI also plans to study further, for example, the linear eigenvalue statistics of such matrices from linear codes, and hope to prove the Gaussian law under suitable conditions.

16303615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303615.value: In this project the PI mainly studied "group randomness" properties for linear codes. More precisely, for matrices formed by choosing codewords at random from linear codes, it was proved that the empirical spectral distribution of such matrices converges to the expected distribution laws when the code length goes to infinity and the code satisfies some natural algebraic conditions. The PI also obtained a strong convergence rate by using advanced tools in random matrix theory. The PI also studied a different statistics, the complete weight distribution of linear codes and show that with this respect, subfield subcodes of general algebraic-geometric codes are very similar to random codes. Such study was also carried out to mutually unbiased bases and the convergence of the empirical spectral distribution to the expected laws was also established. Group randomness properties can be considered as new pseudo-random test for sequences in a family and may have many potential applications.

16303815.label: Realisation of objectives
16303815.value: The objectives of this proposal are to (a) design and synthesize new functional monomers, (b) develop new polymerization routes based on organic reactions of (halo)alkynes, (c) search for new catalysts and optimum polymerization conditions, and (d) investigate the properties of the obtained polymers and explore their high-technology applications. Through elaborate efforts in the past three years, we believe we have completed all the objectives. Functional stereoregular polymers with 1,5-dihalo-(Z,Z)-1,4-pentadiene as dominated segments are prepared through the metal-free multicomponent polymerizations of diyne, aldehyde and boron trihalide. The stereoselectivity of the polymerization was demonstrated to be highly dependent on the employed boron trihalide species as well as the reaction conditions. The polymerization of diyne, aldehyde and BCl3 that proceeds at 0 °C for 1 h followed by stirring at room temperature for another 1 h affords poly(dichloropentadiene)s with a predominant (E,Z)-configuration. When diyne and BCl3 are allowed to react at 45 °C for 1 h prior to further coupling with aldehyde at 0 °C and room temperature, a high molecular weight polymer with the same composition but mainly (Z,Z)-configuration was obtained in a satisfactory yield. Replacement of the mediator from BCl3 to BBr3 also results in polymers with a predominant (Z,Z)-1,4-pentadiene unit in a good yield with a high molecular weight. All the obtained polymers possess high thermal stability and good film-forming ability. Their thin films show high refractive index of 1.9007–1.6462 in a wide wavelength region of 380–890 nm with low optical dispersion. The polymers are weakly emissive in dilute solutions but become highly emissive upon aggregated, demonstrating a unique phenomenon of aggregation-enhanced emission. Their nanoaggregates in aqueous media can serve as sensitive fluorescent chemosensors for the detection of explosives with a superamplification effect and a low detection limit. A transition metal-free polymerization route to functional polydiynes from a haloalkyne-based organic reaction was also developed. Mediated by an inexpensive additive of KI under nitrogen at 120 °C, the polymerizations of 1,2-bis[4-(iodoethynyl)phenyl]-1,2-diphenylethene (1), 1,4-bis(2-iodoethynyl)benzene (2) and 4,4’-bis(2-iodoethynyl)-1,1’-biphenyl (3) proceed smoothly in N,N-dimethylformamide at 120 °C under nitrogen, producing P1–3 consisting of alternate aromatic and 1,3-diyne moieties in moderate to satisfactory yields. All the polymers are thermally stable, losing 5% of their weight at elevated temperature of up to 352 °C. While P1 possesses good solubility in common organic solvents, P2 and P3 are insoluble due to their rigid structures. P1 can form a tough thin film which shows high, UV-tunable refractive indices (n = 2.1125–1.7747) in a wide wavelength range (400–900 nm). A well-defined fluorescent photopattern can be generated by UV irradiation of a polymer film of P1 through a copper mask. A facile one-pot multicomponent polymerization route to functional polymers with unique multisubstituted four-membered heterocyclic structures was also successfully developed. This synthetic strategy enjoys the advantages of readily available monomers, simple operation, high efficiency, mild condition, environmental friendliness, and high atom economy. The four-membered azetidine rings in the polymer skeletons can be easily transformed into amide and amidine moieties via a fast and efficient acid-mediated ring-opening reaction, producing brand-new polymeric materials with distinctive properties. The obtained azetidine-containing polymers show obvious solid-state luminescence despite of the absence of large π-conjugated structures. Experimental results and theoretical analyses demonstrate that the clustering of heteroatoms and conformational rigidification-induced formation of efficient through-space conjugation plays an important role in such an unconventional luminescence phenomenon. All the obtained polymers show excellent optical transparency, high and tunable refractive indices, low optical dispersions and good photopatternability, which make them promising materials in various advanced electronic and optoelectronic devices. The ring-opened polymers can also function as a lysosome-specific fluorescent probe in biological imaging. A novel synthetic strategy to conjugated poly(p-arylene dihalodiene)s (PADs) with high regio- and stereoselectivity was developed. In the presence of PdBr2 and CuBr2, the polymerization of terminal alkynes proceeded smoothly without heating to generate PADs with high molecular weight and high thermal stability. An excessive amount of CuBr2 could be used for the polymerization without strict control on the monomer stoichiometric balance as required in traditional two-component polycondensation and polyaddition. Monomers with twisted structures endowed the resulting polymers with good solubility and processability. The thin films of PADs showed high refractive indices and could be utilized for fabricating well-resolved fluorescent photopatterns by photolithography. The vinyl bromine functionality of PADs enables them to undergo postfunctionalization to afford materials with more sophisticated structures and applications. A new monomer stoichiometry imbalance-promoted polymerization method toward multisubstituted polynaphthalenes (PNs) has been successfully developed. The palladium-catalyzed oxidative polycoupling of aryl iodides and internal diynes proceeded efficiently in o-xylene at 80 °C under monomer non-stoichiometric conditions, furnishing 1,2,3,4-tetrasubstituted naphthalene-containing polymers with high molecular weights in high yields. Compared with previously reported synthetic routes for PNs, widely available and less expensive Pd(OAc)2 was used as the catalyst in this method and highly conjugated PNs can be facilely generated. The non-stoichiometric effect of this polymerization further supports our recently proposed “reactive intermediate” mechanism. That is the stoichiometric balance between the reactive intermediate and internal diyne is more crucial than the monomer feed ratio for the improvement of polymerization efficiency. All the obtained polymers exhibited excellent solubility in common organic solvents and good film-forming ability. Their thin films possessed high refractive indices. Fluorescent conjugated PNs were formed when tetraphenylethylene-containing diynes were used. Taking advantage of their efficient solid-state emission and photosensitivity, well-resolved photopatterns with green emission can be generated by irradiating their thin films under UV light through copper masks. A new facile multicomponent polymerization route to afford luminescent polymers using natural resources as monomers was developed. The polymerizations of 1,2-bis(4-ethynylphenyl)-1,2-diphenylethene, disulfonyl azide, and water together with ethanol were catalyzed by copper(I) iodide and triethylamine, generating soluble polymers with high molecular weights in satisfactory isolation yields. This polymerization route exhibits fascinating features such as high atom utilization, high synthetic efficiency, simple operation, mild reaction conditions, and cheap monomers, which ideally meets the demand of green chemistry. By controlling the adding amount of water and ethanol, the ratio of amide and imidate units in the polymer chain could be readily modulated. Due to the tetraphenylethene moieties embedded in the polymer chains, the polymer solutions emit faintly, but their aggregates fluoresce intensely, demonstrating a characteristic of aggregation-induced emission.

16303815.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303815.value: Development of organic reactions into useful tools for the synthesis of polymers is one of the important subjects in polymer research. Olefins have been the main monomers for the construction of electronically non-conjugated polymers that are commonly used as commodity materials. On the other hand, acetylenes possess one more π-bond than olefin monomers. This makes them attractive as monomers because their polymerization gives electronically unsaturated polymers that are difficult to produce through the conventional vinyl polymerization. In this proposal, we have developed new synthetic methodologies for their synthesis. They are (i) metal-free multicomponent polymerizations of diyne, aldehyde and boron trihalide to stereoregular poly(dichloropentadiene)s, (ii) KI-mediated polymerization to functional polydiynes, (iii) one-pot multicomponent alkyne-based polymerization to azetidine-containing polymers, (iv) PdBr2 and CuBr2-catalyzed polymerization of alkynes to stereoregular and regioregular poly(p-arylene dihalodiene)s, (v) monomer stoichiometry imbalance-promoted polymerization method toward multisubstituted polynaphthalenes, etc. These methods enjoy the advantages of readily available monomers, simple operation, high efficiency, mild condition, environmental friendliness, high atom economy and high tolerance to functional groups and monomer stoichiometric imbalance. The resulting polymers are often synthesized in high yields with high molecular weights. They are soluble and show high thermal stability, good-filming ability and high refractive index. All these properties make them to find high-technological applications such as high refractive materials, photopatterning and fluorescent chemosensors. The strained rings of azetidine-containing polymers enable them to efficiently undergo ring-opening post-modification under simple acidic conditions to transform into new polymers with amide and amidine units. This feature not only enriches the polymer structures but also greatly tunes the polymer properties and broadens their application scopes. XPS technique was innovatively employed to provide direct experimental evidence for their clusteroluminescence mechanism, which could be further extended for the mechanistic study of other unconventional luminescent systems. The proposed “reactive intermediate” mechanism of monomer stoichiometry imbalance-promoted polymerization is expected to be instructive for further development of transition-metal-catalyzed non-stoichimetric polycouplings of mono-functionalized aromatic substrates with diynes to benefit the preparation of functional polymers with diverse structures. As you can see in part C of this report, 15 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in journal articles with high impact factors. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful result.

16303815.value: The development of polymeric materials with novel structures and unique properties and functionalities is of both academic and industrial significance. Olefins have been the main monomers for the construction of electronically non-conjugated polymers that are commonly used as commodity materials. The polymerizations acetylene reactions, however, yield polymers with conjugated backbones that have been found to show an array of novel functional properties and promising high-technological applications. 16304015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304015.value: 晶界是研究歷史最長，但了解最少的晶體缺陷。晶界是多晶材料中兩晶疇之間的界面。它們對金屬，合金，礦物質和陶瓷材料的機械，熱，光，電，磁特性都有顯著影響。晶界表現出豐富的行為，比如粗糙化和預熔化。實驗上可測量固體表面的晶界，但難測量三維固體內部的晶界。此外，單個原子運動很快，在晶界上的動態難以觀測。這些難點導致對晶界行為有許多懸而未決的問題和爭議。 膠體是研究相變的優秀模型系統，因為微米大小的單個膠體粒子的軌跡可在光學顯微鏡下直接看到並測量。過去二十年間，利用膠體粒子作為“大原子”研究結晶，熔化和玻璃化轉變已取得很多重要成果。與這些體相變相比，界面本身也可以有相變，但幾乎還沒在膠體中研究過。這裡，我們提出使用新型的可調膠體晶體首次在單粒子尺度上對晶體內部晶界的形態和運動直接成像，並研究其相變。 隨著溫度升高，一個平直的晶界面往往會先長出許多小的階梯，再變得粗糙並強烈波動（即粗糙化相變），最終在低於熔點處發生預熔化。我們初步的實驗已經在膠體晶體中首次觀察到了上述的豐富行為，從而使許多重要問題可以被研究，包括粗糙化相變的屬性，機制，動力學，以及它對晶界遷移率，硬度，附近的應變場和振動模的影響。我們計劃在較大的參數空間中進一步探索晶界的運動，包括研究在單層和多層晶體中的小角度和大角度晶界，對稱和非對稱晶界，三晶界交界線的運動。另外晶體可由排斥或吸引粒子組成。此外，我們將用相場法進行計算機模擬來更好地理解實驗結果。 這些試驗使我們能夠首次直接觀察固體內部界面的相變。通過單粒子尺度上的觀測，可以有助於澄清當前關於晶界的爭論，幫助完善關於晶界的理論，這些對材料科學，冶金，納米技術和凝聚態物理有重要的基礎意義。

16304015.label: Realisation of objectives
16304015.value: Objective 1: To study grain-boundary roughening transition at the single particle level and understand the related dynamics under different conditions. We successfully fulfilled this objective by comprehensively studies of the grain-boundary roughening in both experiment and simulation. We achieved the single particle resolution by using novel colloidal systems under optical microscopy. We further compared the results with the existing theories and our new analysis methods, and found that the roughening transition follows an unexpected critical behavior. N-isopropylacrylamide (NIPA) spheres are self-assembled into a face-centred cubic (fcc) crystal confined between two parallel glass plates. We use thin-film crystals with a thickness of 15–20 layers, and thus all grain boundaries were ribbon-like with a uniform shape along the z direction and perpendicular to the parallel plates. Therefore we can monitor one layer in the bulk to capture the full dynamics of the grain boundary. Increasing the temperature reduces the particles’ diameter and decreases the volume fraction, which drives the roughening and melting transitions. We observed the colloidal polycrystals at the mesoscopic scale using Bragg diffraction microscopy and at the microscopic level using bright-field microscopy. We measured the morphology and dynamic fluctuations of various types of grain boundaries, including the spatial and time correlations of height functions and their fluctuations. We found that the correlation lengths and times diverge at the same point before the melting, which signatures the roughening transition. The fittings of the curves show that the high-angle grain boundaries can be described reasonably well by the capillary wave theory, and their roughening exhibits both static and dynamic critical behaviors. Similar critical behaviors have been observed in the shape fluctuations of biological membranes. Our results not only provide the first observation of the roughening of buried grain boundaries, but also reveal an unexpected critical behavior which has not been predicted in any roughening theories. The unusual decreases in fluctuation amplitude and grain-boundary mobility after the roughening could be attributed to the widening of the grain boundary, which has not been considered in roughening theories. Since there is no theory about high-angle grain boundary roughening, we fit the data with the conventional capillary-wave theory about liquid-air interfaces. The fitting results are very good, indicating that the anisotropy in grain boundaries and the stress effects are not important. Our theoretical collaborator, Prof. Tsui, proposed a theoretical model which can fit the experimental data almost equally well. Combining with our simulation results, our data better supports the capillary-wave theory. Objective 2: To study grain-boundary premelting transition. For low-angle grain boundaries, we found that their roughening is not complete. As the temperature increases, the low-angle grain boundaries premelt before reaching the roughening transition. This is the first experimentally observation of the melting of low-angle grain boundaries, which is distinct from the previously studied melting of high-angle grain boundaries. The initial melted regions are isolated lakes at some of the dislocations, and then expand and coalesce. At high temperatures, the melted grain boundary form a band of liquid. We quantified the morphology and the shape correlation of two crystal-liquid interfaces of such liquid band, and discovered non-trivial correlations. Such measurements are difficult to achieve in atomic crystals due to the blurry electron-microscopy images near the melting point. As the temperature further increases, the liquid band expands and eventually melt the whole crystal. Objective 3: To perform simulations for the experimental results. We performed phase-field simulations which confirmed the experimental observations, including the non-monotonic correlation length and time and the roughening point approaching the melting point as the mismatch angle of the grain boundary decreases. Details are in the supplementary information of our paper published in Physical Review X. We further performed simulations beyond the experimental results, including the surface roughening and premelting of low-dimensional crystals (monolayer and bilayer crystals). We found that monolayer crystals have very rough surfaces, and premelt into liquids before reaching the roughening transition. The premelted liquid on the surface have crystallite patches and strong fluctuations in thickness, which are distinct from the normal surface liquids observed in the bilayer premelting. These results demonstrate that monolayer and bilayer crystals have distinct surface behaviors, which provide very interesting challenges in theory.

16304015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304015.value: We directly visualize the roughening dynamics of grain boundaries buried inside crystals for the first time. In particular, the novel colloidal crystals we used provide the single-particle resolution under the video microscopy, which is not available in atomic crystals using electron microscopy. We systematically measured the morphologies and thermal fluctuations of low-angle and high-angle grain boundaries, and discovered that their roughening exhibit both static and dynamic critical behaviors, in contrast to the Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in typical free surface roughening. The roughening point shifts towards the melting point as the grain boundary’s mismatch angle decreases and is preempted by melting when the mismatch angle is less than 18°. We found that the roughening transition is preempted by melting for grain boundaries with a mismatch angle less than 18°. Counterintuitively, the amplitude of grain-boundary fluctuations decreases above the roughening point. We attributed this to the observed widening of the grain boundary. The roughening strongly affects the mobility of the grain boundary but not the stiffness. These results provide new guidance for the control of microstructures in polycrystals and the development of roughening theory. We further confirmed the results by our phase-field simulations. These results were published in a top physics journal Phys. Rev. X 8, 021045 (2018) “Grain-boundary roughening in colloidal crystals” by Maijia Liao, Xiao Xiao, Siu Tat Chui, and Yilong Han. In addition, we recently studied the surface roughening of thin-film crystals by simulation, which is an extension of the proposed research. The surface roughening of such low-dimensional crystals have rarely been explored. Interestingly, we found that monolayer and bilayer crystals have different surface roughening behaviors, and their roughening transitions are preempted by the surface premelting. We will submit the manuscript about this work soon. The melting and solid-solid transitions can also involve grain boundary dynamics such as roughening. We applied some of the analysis methods in roughening to the studies of the melting and solid-solid transitions of the hard-sphere system, which is one of the simplest models for the study of phase transitions. These results cast light on the melting and solid-solid transformations of atomic body-centered cubic crystals, which exist widely in nature. The results are published in “Transformations of body-centered cubic crystals composed of hard or soft spheres to liquids or face-centered cubic crystals” Feng Wang and Yilong Han, Journal of Chemical Physics 150, 014504 (2019).

16304015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304015.value: Any interface can have a roughening transition, but theories are available only for the crystals’ surfaces. The theory of grain boundary roughening is more complicated and has only been proposed for simple low-angle grain boundaries. Our novel experimental results show that the grain boundary roughening is different from surface roughening, which casts light on developing the theory of grain boundary roughening. The future development of the related theory is badly needed. Another direction is to explore the grain boundary roughing in low dimensions. A grain boundary or surface of a 2D crystal should always be rough, but our preliminary simulation does show flat grain boundaries. More studies are needed to understand the roughening in 2D.

16304015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304015.value: A grain boundary is the interface between two grains, or crystallites, in polycrystalline materials such as metals, alloys, minerals and ceramics. They dominate material properties, but are poorly understood because electron microscopy cannot observe grain boundaries buried inside the bulk and track the fast motions of atoms. As temperature increases, a flat grain boundary become rough and curved with strong shape fluctuations, a phenomenon known as roughening. We experimentally observed such grain boundary roughening for the first time using a colloidal model system. It represents the first study of interfacial phase transition inside the bulk of a solid with the single-particle dynamics. Micrometer sized colloidal particles can be viewed as “big atoms” which are excellent model systems for grain boundary studies because the trajectories of individual micro-particles are measurable by optical video microscopy even when they are inside the colloidal crystal. We measured the grain-boundary dynamics for various types of grain boundaries and found that they follow a critical behavior, which is distinct from the predicted behavior in the roughening theories about crystal’s surfaces. We further confirmed this result by phase-field simulations. The results are of fundamental importance in condensed matter physics, material science, metallurgy, nanotechnology and related industries.

16304115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304115.value: Due to the increasingly important applications of chiral molecules in everyday life, including pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and materials, the development of new useful catalytic asymmetric processes for the efficient synthesis of chiral building blocks remains in high demand. With the recent advances in asymmetric catalysis, new tools and concepts have been made available. In the new context, there are new opportunities and challenges regarding the development of previously underdeveloped or unmet challenges in chiral building block synthesis. Here we propose to further advance the synthesis of chiral building blocks employing Brønsted acids, N-heterocyclic carbenes (NHCs), and chiral counter anions, etc. With these tools, we will address challenges in four different subareas, including the asymmetric synthesis and opening of four-membered strained rings, merging NHC catalysis with radical chemistry, asymmetric reactions isobenzopyryliums for dihydronaphthalene synthesis, and asymmetric reactions of disubstituted quinone methides. The development of these asymmetric reactions will not only provide fundamental understanding of new reactivity and stereocontrol methods in challenging organic species, such as isobenzopyryliums and quinone methides, but also provide rapid access to a range of useful chiral building blocks with applications in medicines, materials, other aspects of daily life. 由於手性分子在日常生活中包括藥物、農業化學品和材料等领域越來越重要的應用，新的不對稱催化過程的發展也越来越重要。最近，不對稱催化领域出现了新的方法和概念，它们给手性砌塊的新型高效合成提供了新的機遇和挑戰。這裡我們進一步推進这方面的研究。我们将利用手性質子酸、氮雜環卡賓、手性陰​​離子等作为手性诱导单元对四個不同的子课题进行研究。它们包括四元環的不對稱开环反应、氮杂环卡宾與自由基化學的结合、isobenzopyryliums的不對稱反應、以及亚甲基苯醌的不對稱反應。這些不對稱反應的發展將不僅对重要中间体isobenzopyryliums和亚甲基苯醌的反应性提供新的认识，而且還提供快速合成一系列有用的手性砌塊與的新方法。这将在醫藥、材料及人类生活其它方面的进一步发展具有深远的意义。

16304115.label: Realisation of objectives
16304115.value: In this project, we have successfully developed a range of new strategies for the synthesis of useful chiral building blocks with organocatalysis. The process has been achieved within the following four areas: (1) asymmetric synthesis and opening of four-membered strained rings, (2) merging NHC catalysis with radical chemistry, (3) asymmetric reactions isobenzopyryliums for dihydronaphthalene synthesis, and (4) asymmetric reactions of quinone methides. The objectives of this proposal have been realized as expected. (1) We have developed a range of new asymmetric opening reactions of strained four-membered rings for the synthesis of chiral small building blocks. Specifically, the first asymmetric oxetane opening by chloride has been achieved. We also employed chiral anion to induce chirality in the asymmetric opening of azetidiniums. (2) We also developed new catalytic asymmetric processes involving NHC catalysis and radical chemistry. We have developed an NHC-catalyzed efficient dihalomethylenation process employing the concept of merging NHC catalysis with single-electron chemistry, a new and rare example. Later on, the important trifluoromethylation reaction was also achieved by NHC catalysis (3) We have developed a new catalytic asymmetric reaction of isobenzopyryliums for the synthesis of chiral dihydronaphthalenes. In this project, we did mechanistic studies on this reaction. (4) We developed a range of catalytic asymmetric reactions of quinone methides, including ortho-, para-quinone methides, aza-quinone methides. With chiral Bronsted acid catalysis, these reactions all led to highly enanthioenriched useful chiral building blocks.

16304115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304115.value: In this project, we have developed the following new organocatalytic processes leading to the synthesis of useful chiral building blocks and synthetically important structural units. (1) We have developed an efficient organocatalytic enantioselective intermolecular addition of naphthols to in-situ generated para-quinone methides. (2) Asymmetric opening of oxetanes is a challenging topic. Following our previous effort, in this project we achieved the first asymmetric chloride opening of oxetanes, providing expedient access of highly functionalized three-carbon chiral building blocks with excellent efficiency and stereocontrol. (3) The first intermolecular aza-Piancatelli reaction with excellent chemo-, enantio-, and diastereoselectivity under mild conditions was achieved. It provides expedient access to a wide range of highly enantioenriched 4-amino-cyclopentenone products from readily available 2-furfurylcarbinols. (4) We developed an NHC-catalyzed efficient dihalomethylenation process employing the concept of merging NHC catalysis with single-electron chemistry. (5) We achieved the first catalytic asymmetric reaction of aza-para-quinone methides. (6) We developed an enantioselective [4 + 2] cycloaddition of o-quinone methides and vinyl sulfides for indirect access to generally substituted chiral chromanes. (7) We developed an organocatalytic synthesis of chiral tetrasubstituted allenes from racemic propargylic alcohols via 1,8-conjugate addition to para-quinone methides. (8) In our effort to develop organocatalytic synthesis of chiral diarylmethyl alkynes, we demonstrated a rare exmple of improving synthetic procedure by understanding the role of additive. (9) We developed the first catalytic enantioselective desymmetrization of azetidiniums. (10) We developed the first organocatalytic approach for direct conversion of racemic diarylmethanols to valuable chiral diarylmethylamines. (11) We developed a new organocatalytic addition of azlactones to quinone methides for the efficient synthesis of chiral β,β-diaryl-α-amino acid derivatives. (12) We have developed the first general trifluoromethylation at the γ position of carbonyl compounds by NHC-catalysis.

16304115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304115.value: As an extension of this project, the development of additional useful organocatalytic asymmetric processes will continue to be our topic of pursuit in this area. In particular, we will continue to expand the utility of chiral Bronsted acids in asymmetric catalysis. Our effort in asymmetric strained ring opening, such as oxetanes and azetidines, and the asymmetric addition of quinone methides will still be a topic for further research.

16304115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304115.value: In this project, we have discovered a range of new organic processes with excellent efficiency and selectivity. These processes utilized organocatalysts that do not involve metals, which are environmentally friendly. These reactions provide new approaches to build carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom bonds, which are important in our daily life as demonstrated by their potential utility in medicinal chemistry and pharmaceutical industry. These findings will contribute to the advances in drug discovery and environmental protection.

16304215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304215.value: Self-assembly provides a powerful tool to fabricate advanced materials through the bottom-up approach. Understanding the kinetics of self-assembly would thus greatly help to achieve precise control in designing elegant structures for advanced materials. However, it is difficult to elucidate kinetic details of self-assembly at molecular level because these processes are often heterogeneous. Transition Path Theory (TPT) applied on computer simulations has the potential to elucidate the full ensemble of self-assembly pathways that would be difficult to obtain experimentally. However, applying TPT to self-assembly may result in numerous parallel pathways with comparable probabilities that make it difficult to understand major mechanisms of self-assembly. To better understand the self-assembly processes, we propose a novel algorithm, Path Lumping, that can efficiently group numerous transition pathways obtained from TPT into metastable path channels according to their kinetic similarity. This is achieved by defining the similarity of a pair of transition pathways by accumulated fluxes that intercross them. Preliminary results show that the Path Lumping algorithm can effectively identify metastable channels of transition pathways for a 2D-potential as well as the aggregation of two hydrophobic organic molecules in water. We will employ the Path Lumping algorithm to elucidate major mechanisms for the self-assembly of star-like blocked co-polymers. Since the self-assembly process of this type of co-polymers are sensitive to various parameters such as solvent condition, monomer structure and concentration, we aim to reveal the key factors that control the dominant aggregation pathways and further manipulate self-assembly pathways by tuning these factors. An important emphasis of our theoretical work will be to generate hypotheses that will be tested by our experimental collaborator, and these experiments will further help refine our theoretical models. 自組裝為通過從底層向上的方法來製造先進材料提供了一個有力的工具。掌握自組裝的動力學將極大地有助於在設計先進的材料時實現精確控制其結構。然而，由於自組裝過程的多樣性，在分子水平上闡明其的動力學細節具有很大的挑戰性。雖然基於計算機模擬的過渡路徑理論（TPT）可以提供實驗上很難觀測到的自組裝途徑的完整集合，但是該理論運用到自組裝過程中往往產生大量平行的路徑，從而難以理解自組裝的主要機制。 為了更好地理解自組裝的過程，我們提出了一種叫做路徑聚合的新算法，該算法可以基於路徑之間的動力學相似性有效地找到主要路徑的通道。我們的算法是通過加和路徑之間交叉的通量來定義兩個路徑之間的相似性的。我們的初步結果表明，該路徑聚合算法在二維勢能面和兩個疏水有機分子在水中聚集的體系中都能有效的發現主要的路徑通道。 我們將採用提出的路徑聚合算法闡明星形高分子自組裝的主要機制。因為這種類型的高分子自組裝過程對包括溶劑條件，單體的結構和濃度敏感等各種參數的依賴。我們的目標是找到控制主導自組裝途徑的關鍵因素，並進一步通過調節這些因素來調控自組裝的過程。我們的理論工作的一個重要的重點將是產生可以通過我們的實驗合作者進行測試的假設，而這些實驗將有助於進一步完善我們的理論模型。

16304215.label: Realisation of objectives
16304215.value: All three objectives of the proposal have been well achieved. For objective 1: We have successfully completed this objective by developing a new algorithm for identifying major pathways from computer simulations to investigate mechanisms of self-assembly. Specifically, we have developed the Path Lumping algorithm to group parallel pathways into metastable path channels to investigate the kinetics of self-assembly processes (J. Chem. Phys., 147, 044112, (2017)). Self-assembly of a large number of designed molecules is regarded a powerful bottom-up approach to fabricate advanced materials in nanotechnology. Insights into the conformational dynamics of self-assembly processes would greatly advance our understanding in this important field. Constructing kinetic network models on top of large-scale molecular dynamics (MD) simulation trajectories is a promising approach to dissect the kinetic mechanisms of complex chemical and biological processes. Combined with the Transition Path Theory, kinetic network models can be applied to identify all pathways connecting any conformational states of interest. However, the identified pathways can be too complex to comprehend, especially for self-assembly processes where numerous parallel pathways with comparable flux probability coexist. To address the above-mentioned challenge, we have developed the Path Lumping algorithm to group these parallel pathways into metastable path channels for analysis (J. Chem. Phys., 147, 044112, (2017)). In this algorithm, we define the similarity between two pathways as the intercrossing flux between them, and then apply the spectral clustering algorithm to lump these pathways into groups. We demonstrate the power of our method by applying it to two systems: a 2D-potential consisting of four metastable energy channels and the hydrophobic collapse process of two hydrophobic molecules. In both systems, we show that the Path Lumping algorithm can successfully group thousands of pathways into several path channels that are consistent with the underlying kinetic mechanisms of the two systems. In addition, we have also developed a new weighting scheme in simulated tempering algorithm that could be combined with Path Lumping algorithm to enhance conformational sampling and facilitate the construction of the kinetic network models (J. Chem. Phys., 144, 154107, (2016)). As the clustering is an important step in our Path Lumping algorithm, we have also compared common clustering algorithms adopted to analyze MD simulation trajectories (Chin. J. Chem. Phys., 31, 404 (2018)). Furthermore, we have developed an efficient Bayesian kinetic clustering algorithm, which could be applied to lump kinetic pathways (J. Chem. Phys.,149, 072337, (2018)). In addition, the Path Lumping algorithm could become a useful step in our suggested protocol to investigate functional conformational changes of complex biological and chemical systems (WIREs Comput Mol Sci, 8:e1343, (2018)). We expect that our Path Lumping algorithm to be a promising tool for revealing unprecedented insights into the kinetic mechanisms of complex self-assembly processes. For objective 2: We have successfully realized this objective to elucidate the detailed mechanisms of self-assembly for a series of star-like block co-polymers. In particular, we have elucidated the dominant self-assembly pathways of the star-like block copolymers by constructing kinetic network models from extensive coarse-grained Brownian Dynamics simulations. We found that an aggregate mostly grows upon colliding with other aggregates, and meanwhile each aggregate also undergoes structural rearrangement to change its morphology from rod to sphere. We further identified two competing kinetic parameters that control these dominant pathways: the frequency of collision, and the rate for the aggregate morphology change. Strikingly, our results showed that without altering the experimental conditions, two distinct self-assembly mechanisms (diffusion of individual copolymer into the aggregate core and membrane closure) can coexist at different stages of a single self-assembly process. Furthermore, by rational design that tunes the rate for the aggregate morphology change, we successfully altered the dominant self-assembly pathways. We believe that such rational design opens a window of opportunities for developing desired self-assembled co-polymer structures via the kinetic control of the self-assembly processes (Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 20:6767, (2018); Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 18:23494, (2016)). By constructing kinetic network models, we have also elucidated the mechanisms of the self-assembly of an intrinsically disordered peptide: hIAPP (Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 18, 29892, (2016)). In addition, we have elucidated kinetic mechanisms for the aggregation of hydrophobic molecules by tightly coupling the theoretical and experimental studies (Nature Communications, 8, 15639, (2017)). Finally, we have applied a simplified version of the Path Lumping algorithm to identify major self-assembly pathways of two amphiphilic molecules with very similar chemical structures but distinct self-assembled structures (J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 8, 1798, (2017), see the next section for more details). For objective 3: To address this objective, we have successfully revealed key structural features and external conditions that can determine their self-assembly pathways. In particular, we have revealed how two largely similar amphiphilic molecules that differ in a single functional group: 1-[11-oxo-11-(pyren-1-ylmethoxy)-undecyl] pyridinium bromide (PYR), and 1-(11-((5a1,8a-dihydropyren-1-yl)-methylamino)-11-oxoundecyl) pyridinium bromide (PYN), prefer distinct kinetic assembly pathways (J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 8, 1798, (2017)). While PYR prefers an incremental growth mechanism, whereby planar disk-like aggregates were formed and further assemble into a nanotube, PYN favors a hopping growth pathway, whereby curved disk-like aggregates were formed that tend to further assemble into a vesicle. Importantly, we found that such preference for kinetic assembly pathways originates from differences in their amphiphilicity and adhesion rate during the fusion of micelles. Consistent with existing experiments, our results clearly elucidate the role of kinetics in the rational design of amphiphiles self-assembly. To achieve the above results, we constructed kinetic network models on top of large-scale molecular dynamics simulations, and applied the Path Lumping algorithm to identify major self-assembly path channels. Unlike conventional simulation methods that rely on inspection and analysis of individual simulation trajectories, kinetic network models provide a statistical depiction that identifies dominant transition pathways among all conformational states during the assembly process. By investigating the self-assembly process of patchy particles, we have explored key structural features and external conditions that can significantly impact the kinetics of self-assembly pathways (Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 20, 10030, (2018)). In particular, by constructing the kinetic network models from extensive coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, we successfully elucidated the formation mechanism of the dodecahedral cage from the self-assembly of patchy particles. We found that the dodecahedral cage is formed through increasing the aggregate size followed by structure rearrangement. Based on this mechanistic understanding, we performed the rational design by modifying the patch arrangement of patchy particles, and this design indeed greatly improved the productivity of the dodecahedral cage. Our results demonstrate the feasibility to achieve the rational design of the desired self-assembled structures via the kinetic analysis.

16304215.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304215.value: Self-assembly provides a powerful approach to fabricate functional materials in nanotechnology. Experimentally probing the molecular details of this kinetic process is challenging. Computer simulations may complement experimental techniques to provide dynamic information at molecular level. However, it remains challenging for simulations to obtain a statistical picture of kinetic pathways for the self-assembly process. With the support of this grant, we have developed a novel Path Lumping algorithm that can identify major kinetic pathways of the self-assembly process (J. Chem. Phys., 147, 044112, (2017)). The path lumping algorithm addresses the challenge that heterogeneous self-assembly process often involves a large number of comparably probable pathways. These parallel pathways can be identified by transition path theory based on kinetic network model constructed from computer simulations. Our Path Lumping can efficiently group these pathways into metastable families according to their kinetic connectivity. We have successfully applied the Path Lumping algorithm to identify major self-assembly pathways of two amphiphilic molecules with very similar chemical structures but distinct self-assembled structures (J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 8, 1798, (2017)). Moreover, we elucidate detailed mechanisms of self-assembly for star-like block co-polymers. Interestingly, we found that two distinct self-assembly mechanisms (diffusion of individual copolymer into the aggregate core and membrane closure) coexist at different stages of a single self-assembly process (Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 20:6767, (2018); Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 18:23494, (2016)). By investigating the self-assembly process of patchy particles, we have explored key structural features and external conditions that can significantly impact the kinetics of self-assembly pathways (Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys., 20, 10030, (2018)). Our understanding of these key factors further facilitated our designs of patch arrangement of patchy particles to improve productivity of the dodecahedral caged structures. These results demonstrate the feasibility to achieve desired self-assembled structures via rational design based on kinetic analysis. Due to the above findings, the PI has been invited to give talks in prestigious international conferences. Two Ph. D students partially supported by this grant have successfully obtained their degrees. In 2018, the PI was elected as a founding member of the Young Academy of Sciences of Hong Kong.

16304215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304215.value: We expect that our Path Lumping algorithm can be widely applied to reveal kinetic mechanism of many chemical and biological processes. For example, in addition to self-assembly, our novel Path Lumping algorithm holds promise in understanding molecular mechanisms of peptide aggregation, protein-protein interaction and hydrophobic collapse. Supported by this grant, we have demonstrated the feasibility to achieve desired self-assembled structures (i.e. the improved productivity of dodecahedral cages via re-designing patch arrangements of patchy particles) based on mechanistic understanding of kinetic pathways. In the future, we anticipate that the kinetic analysis of self-assembly process may greatly facilitate the rational design of self-assembled materials by manipulating their kinetic pathways.

16304215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304215.value: Self-assembly provides a powerful tool to fabricate advanced materials through the bottom-up approach. Understanding the kinetics of self-assembly would thus greatly help to achieve precise control in designing elegant structures for advanced materials. However, it is difficult to elucidate kinetic details of self-assembly at molecular level because these processes are often heterogeneous. To address this challenge, we have developed a novel algorithm, Path Lumping, that can efficiently group numerous transition pathways into metastable path channels according to their kinetic similarity. Using the Path Lumping algorithm and kinetic network models, we have elucidated mechanisms for the self-assembly of star-like blocked co-polymers, self-assembly of amphiphilic molecules, and self-assembly of patchy particles. For patchy particles, we have further achieved desired self-assembled structures (i.e. improved productivity of dodecahedral cages) by altering kinetic pathways of self-assembly. Our studies open a window of opportunity for the rational design of self-assembled materials by manipulating their kinetic pathways.

16304315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304315.value: 类似于一幢建筑，宇宙中的物质是由“砖块” - 基本粒子，如电子，上夸克，下夸克，光子等组成的。超对称是具有不同自旋的两类基本粒子，费米子和玻色子，之间的一种对称性。它有可能是构建粒子物理终极理论的一个基本方针。超对称预测，每一个基本玻色子（例如，光子）具有一个费米超对称伴随子，并且每个基本费米子（例如，电子）具有一个玻色超对称伴随子。目前没有任何费米或者玻色超对称伴随子被发现。 令人惊讶的是，超对称为一些自然界中最根本的难题提供了优雅的解决方案。超对称解释了为什么电弱相变，在该过程中W，Z玻色子（弱相互作用力的载体）获得了质量，并因此和光子区分开来，发生在一个比基本能标－普朗克标度，低大约16个数量级的能标上。此外，超对称可以在一个高能标上把强，弱，电磁三种相互作用统一起来。换句话说，这些相互作​​用在该能标上具有相同的作用强度，只是同一种力的不同表现形式。 加速器是研究粒子物理的一种基本工具。它可以通过粒子碰撞创造出新的粒子，例如希格斯粒子和可能存在的超对称粒子。大型强子对撞机（LHC）是世界上最大的加速器。它在探索微观世界非常成功：只用了1％的预计在LHC上的数据采集量，我们发现了大约半个世纪前预言的希格斯粒子。为了升级，LHC在2012年年底被关闭，预计在2015年四月（正好在提出的资助期开始之前）将再次开始采集数据。预计到资助结束时，将会有3-4倍的现有数据量在更高的对撞能标上被采集。 作为LHC项目的首要任务之一，探索超对称非常具有挑战性，因为我们对超对称的理论和实验两方面都理解有限。到目前为止，没有任何超对称物理的信号被观测到。为了应对这些挑战，PI提出了两个主要的研究方向： 数据驱动的超对称理论和唯像学研究，以及理论驱动的超对称对撞机物理的研究。如果这个科研项目获得批准，粒子物理的研究及其在香港的发展将会极大的受益。

16304315.label: Realisation of objectives
16304315.value: There are two objectives in this project, both of which are mainly based on or strongly motivated by the Run II data at LHC. Additionally, we planed to involve PhD students in this project, to provide them opportunities to learn how to conduct research and how to do it well. All of these objectives have been successfully achieved. The first objective is on supersymmetric phenomenology. The goal is to improve our understanding on supersymmetric models, with Run II data. If signals were observed, we would understand if it origins from supersymmetry. If null results were obtained in the search, we would extract their implications for supersymmetry and properly adjust the strategies for its collider searches. In December 2015, after analyzing the early data of Run II, the ATLAS and CMS collaborations at CERN both announced the observation of a potential 750 GeV di-photon resonance. If this observation is confirmed, it will be an unambiguous signal for physics beyond the Standard Model (SM). We explored if this observation could be explained in supersymmetric theory. It turned out that, if the 750 GeV di-photon resonance is a CP-even or CP-odd heavy Higgs boson in the Higgs sector of the Minimal-Supersymmetric-Standard-Model (MSSM), an efficient mechanism to yield the measured signal rate is absent. So we extended the MSSM by introducing an extra U(1)′ gauge symmetry, where the extended particle spectrum provides a parameter space to accommodate this observation. The research outputs were formulated as a publication “750 GeV Resonance in the Gauged U(1)′-Extended MSSM”, Phys. Lett. B759 (2016) 354-360. The second objective is on collider physics of supersymmetry. We targeted on the Higgs sector of supersymmetric models. Different from the SM, anomaly cancellation in supersymmetric models generically defines an extended Higgs sector. Therefore, the search for the siblings of the SM-like Higgs boson provides an avenue to test supersymmetric models. Our goal is to explore the decoupling limits of these theories where the Higgs siblings are heavy. Explicitly, we designed strategies to search for neutral Higgs bosons in the decoupling limit of the MSSM, where these Higgs bosons are typically heavy and may dominantly decay into top-quark pair. Usually such Higgs bosons are searched for via their gluon fusion production. Yet, this is unsatisfactory due to a strong interference between the signal and its QCD background. To address this problem, we proposed to conduct this search via the Higgs production accompanied by one or two top quarks, using the same-sign di-lepton signature. With this new strategy we found that the sensitivity can be greatly improved at high-luminosity LHC. The research outputs were formulated as a publication “Heavy Higgs bosons at low tan β: from the LHC to 100TeV”; JHEP 1701 (2017) 018. Despite the excitement in the community with this potential 750 GeV di-photon resonance, the significance of this observation stopped increasing with more data being analyzed. Actually, so far no convincing signal about physics beyond the SM including supersymmetry has been observed with Run II data. This means that, if the BSM physics like supersymmetry exists, the relevant parameter values or the correct scenario might be untypical or even unexpected. Given that most collider analyses at LHC are exclusive, we need to develop strategies which are relatively model-independent, to improve the efficiency. This will allow supersymmetry and other BSM physics to be searched for in a broader way. Motivated by this, we applied the machine-learning techniques of novelty detection, based on Deep-Neural-Network (DNN), to search for supersymmetry and Higgs boson. In this study we collaborated with ATLAS experimentalist. We explicitly showed how the supersymmetric scenarios and the Higgs production with a pair of top quarks can be simultaneously probed if they share similar signature. The research outputs were formulated as an article “Detecting New Physics as Novelty”. This study involves both objectives of this project: with better understanding on supersymmetric physics (mainly based on Run II data), we are proposing new collider strategies for supersymmetry search. As was highlighted in the ``education plan'' of this project, the PI always views ``student development is integral to any successful research plan, and is one of the most rewarding aspects of a research project.'' In this project, two PhD students (Xuhui JIANG and Yingying LI) under the PI's supervision were involved. Yingying LI played a major role in the first two papers, and Xuhui JIANG plays a major role in the third one. Yingying LI graduated in 2019 Summer and joined the theory devision of the world-famous Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory in USA for her first postdoc position in 2019 October.

16304315.value: After analyzing the early data of LHC Run II, the ATLAS and CMS collaborations at CERN both announced the observation of a potential 750 GeV di-photon resonance in December 2015. We explored if this observation could be explained in supersymmetric theory. Considering that an efficient mechanism to yield the measured signal rate is typically absent in the Minimal-Supersymmetric-Standard-Model (MSSM), we extended it by introducing an extra U(1)′ gauge symmetry. Here vector-like supermultiplets and singlet supermultiplets are introduced for anomaly cancellation and U(1)′ symmetry breaking, respectively. Then we illustrated that this 750 GeV resonance could be a singlet-like scalar or pseudo-scalar, with a di-photon decay rate enhanced by the vector-like supermultiplets. The research outputs were formulated as a publication “750 GeV Resonance in the Gauged U(1)′-Extended MSSM”, Phys. Lett. B759 (2016) 354-360. Additionally, we designed strategies to search for neutral Higgs bosons in the decoupling limit of the MSSM, where these Higgs bosons are typically heavy and may dominantly decay into top-quark pair. Usually such Higgs bosons are searched for via their gluon fusion production. Yet, this is unsatisfactory due to a strong interference between the signal and its QCD background. To address this problem, we proposed to conduct this search via the Higgs production accompanied by one or two top quarks, using the same-sign di-lepton signature. With this new strategy we found that the sensitivity can be greatly improved at high-luminosity LHC. The research outputs were formulated as a publication “Heavy Higgs bosons at low tan β: from the LHC to 100TeV”; JHEP 1701 (2017) 018. Yet, the null results of searching for beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) physics, including supersymmetry, at LHC Run II so far post new challenges to particle physicists. The probe of supersymmetric scenarios and other BSM physics in a broader way calls for a strategy which is more model-dependent. Motivated by this, we applied the machine-learning techniques of novelty detection, based on Deep-Neural-Network (DNN), to search for supersymmetry and Higgs boson. We explicitly showed how supersymmetric scenarios and the Higgs production with a pair of top quarks can be simultaneously probed. The research outputs were formulated as an article “Detecting New Physics as Novelty”. It is in finalization for submission to arXiv and peer-reviewed journal.

16304315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304315.value: With the data collected in Run II program at LHC, the experimental particle physicists have not observed any unambiguous signal on physics beyond the Standard Model. The Run III program at LHC is expected to be operated during 2021-2023, and then a high-luminosity run will follow around 2025. If everything is smooth, one order more data will be collected during the whole program. As the collected data become bigger and the detection is extended to more challenging physics scenarios, the data mining strategies and techniques with higher efficiency and sensitivity are strongly called for. Therefore the endeavor in this direction will be highly valuable. Yet, there exists a big uncertainty on the experimental outcomes. If any anomalous signal is observed, we need to take a further analysis on the underlying physics. If the signal turns out to be supersymmetric or supersymmetry-like, it implies that there exists a landscape above electroweak scale yet to be explored. Notably, the search results, if being null, never mean that they are negative. It simply means that we need new inputs or theories to understand the fundamental puzzles in nature, such as hierarchy problem, dark matter, etc.

16304315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304315.value: Supersymmetry is one of the presumed fundamental guidelines for organizing the spectrum of fundamental particles and describe their interactions. Supersymmetry predicts that there exists an extended Higgs sector, and meanwhile, each boson (e..g, photon) has a fermionic superpartner, and each fermion (e.g., electron) has bosonic superpartner. It provides an elegant solution to some of the most challenging puzzles in nature, such as dynamical origin of electroweak symmetry breaking, the unification of non-gravitational interactions, dark matter existence in the universe, etc. In this project, we completed three academic articles (two publications, and one in finalization for submission). In the first stage, we have proposed strategies to search for the Higgs sector in decoupling limit of supersymmetry. These strategies have been adopted by both the ATLAS and the CMS experiment at the LHC. We have also explored supersymmetric interpretation of the ATLAS and CMS observation of a potential 750 GeV di-photon resonance, based on the early data of LHC Run II. In the second stage, in response to the null results of supersymmetry searches at LHC, we have proposed a strategy to probe supersymmetric scenarios and other unexpected ones in a broader way, using deep learning techniques for novelty detection.

16304515.label: Realisation of objectives
16304515.value: In the early period of this project, we have performed collaborative research with colleagues in HKUST and researchers in other institutions to further explore the novel properties about the 2D superconductivities of the Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure. These include the robustness of the 2D superconductivity, the 2D vortex dynamics, the current driven vortex-antivortex pair breaking and vortex explosion in this heterostructure. We have also used the point-contact technique to study the detailed superconducting characteristics of the Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure. In this work, we reported a pronounced twin gap structure with a large gap of unconventional pairing symmetry, corresponding to the interfacial superconductivity, and a smaller gap which opens below the characteristic BKT temperature and is associated with proximity-induced superconductivity in the topologically insulating Bi2Te3 layer. We also studied the electrical resistivity on the novel interfacial superconductor Bi2Te3/FeTe under the influence of hydrostatic pressure. The observed pressure-induced increase in Tc is attributed to an enhancement of the electronic-coupling between the FeTe interface region and the topological Bi2Te3 surface state. A local suppression of the antiferromagnetic SDW order that makes way to a superconducting ground state at the interface may represent a good candidate. These research studies resulted in the publication of four journal papers [Part C: 8 (1-4)] and two conference papers [Part C: 9 (1-2)]. After the above studies, we focused our effort on studying the underlying mechanism of the observed 2D superconductivity of the topological insulator/FeTe heterosturcture system. In one study, we fabricated a Bi2Te3:Fe sample with varying Fe concentration along the growth direction so as to study if a certain Fe doping concentration in Bi2Te3 could make it superconducting, which is based on the thought that Fe diffusion from the FeTe layer to the Bi2Te3 layer may occur. The temperature dependent resistance of this sample displays a superconductivity transition at about 12.3 K. Detailed structural and chemical analysis reveal that this layer consists of two types of unexpected Fe-Te nanostructures: one is FeTe thin layer formed near the surface, and the other is FeTe2 nanorod embedded in the Bi2Te3 layer. Based on the results of further electrical and magnetotransport studies, it is likely that the observed superconductivity originates from the interface between the FeTe nanostructure and the neighboring Bi2Te3 layer. We have addressed the formation mechanisms of the observed nanostructures. This work resulted in the publication of one journal paper [Part C: 8(5)]. After the success of fabricating another TI/FeTe heterostructure that also displays 2D superconductivity, the Sb2Te3/FeTe heterostructure, we have focused most of our effort and time to study the origin of its 2D superconductivity. The results of our transport measurements support that reduction of the excess Fe concentration of the Fe1+yTe layer not only increases the fluctuation of its antiferromagnetic (AFM) order but also enhances the quality of the SC of this heterostructure system. On the other hand, the interfacial SC of this heterostructure was found to have a wider-ranging TI-layer thickness dependence than that of the Bi2Te3/Fe1+yTe heterostructure, which is believed to be attributed to the much higher bulk conductivity of Sb2Te3 that enhances indirect coupling between its top and bottom topological surface states (TSSs). The fact that 2D SC of a Fe1+yTe layer occurs only when it is covered with either Bi2Te3 or Sb2Te3 implies that a property of TI is likely involved in the induction of this SC. Since the TI layer in these heterostructures provides a source of itinerant carriers confined at the interface through the TSSs, it is possible that these itinerant carriers exhibit an unconventional pairing at the interface, leading to the observed interfacial SC. In this work, we address the possible pairing mechanism of the 2D SC at the Sb2Te3/Fe1+yTe interface. We believe the 2 key ingredients at the Sb2Te3/Fe1+yTe interface are 1) 2D itinerant electrons induced by the TSSs of Sb2Te3 and 2) local spin moments with AFM ordering in Fe1+yTe. Our experimental results suggest that at the Sb2Te3/Fe1+yTe interface, the fluctuation of the local moments of the AFM ordering in Fe1+yTe is enhanced due to the hybridization with the itinerant electrons in TSSs. On the other hand, the enhanced fluctuating spin moments provide a driving force for the superconducting pairing of the itinerant electrons at the interface. The fact that SC transition temperature increases upon the increase of the fluctuation of the AFM order, as observed in this study, also implies that superconducting pairing benefits from the fluctuation of AFM order. Consequently, we propose that the superconducting pairing mediated by spin fluctuation enhanced by the hybridization of local spin moments in Fe1+yTe and 2D itinerant electrons in the TSSs of Sb2Te3 is a possible mechanism of the SC observed in the Sb2Te3/Fe1+yTe heterostructures, which could be extended to apply to the topological insulator/FeTe system in general. This work resulted in the publication of one paper published in a prestigious journal [Part C: 8(6)]. Through a close collaboration with a non-local university, the proposed objectives of performing scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy (STM & STS) and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) characterizations of the TI/FeTe heterostructures to better understand the mechanism of their superconductivity were successfully realized. In this work, a Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure with higher crystalline quality was fabricated as the FeTe layer was grown on a closely lattice-matched SrTiO3 (001) substrate. Our results show that the superconductivity in the Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure originates at the interface and does not enhance or weaken with the increase of the Bi2Te3 thickness. The UPS study has revealed the thickness dependent work function evolution of Bi2Te3, which indicates that an electron transfer occurs at the interface due to the misalignment of the Fermi surface between Bi2Te3 and FeTe, leading to a hole doping effect on the FeTe layer next to Bi2Te3. Based on the above results, a mechanism of the interfacial gating induced suppression of magnetic ordering in the FeTe layer was proposed to explain the emergence of interfacial superconductivity. Our ARPES measurements indicate that the topological surface states are preserved in the Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure that has a thick Bi2Te3 layer, suggesting that this interfacial superconductivity system can potentially host Majorana zero modes. It is fair to say that this work gives other aspects of the origin of the 2D SC in addition to what we found in our work on the Sb2Te3/FeTe heterostructures, but they both point out that the magnetic ordering in the FeTe layer is related to the superconductivity mechanism. This work resulted in the publication of another paper published in a prestigious journal [Part C: 8(7)]. It is worth mentioning that some of the original objectives such as aiming to tune the TI layer to be intrinsic, gate-bias experiments and investigating of the biaxial stress effect have not been explored detailed enough. These proposed studies are indeed quite challenging either they are very time consuming or requiring major modification on the existing instruments. In fact, the new approaches used for studying the superconductivity mechanism as reported in the last three publications in Part C proved to be more fruitful toward the understanding of the key objective of this project.
