16304515.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304515.value: 1) We have carried out field-cooled and zero-field cooled magnetic response and M-H hysteresis studies in details. Strong anisotropic magnetic responses was found. The observed strong magnetic anisotropy provides further evidence that the induced superconductivity in the Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure has a 2D nature (J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 27, 345701 (2015), which is not listed in the research output since it was published before the project starting date). 2) We have studied the robustness of the 2D superconductivity, the 2D vortex dynamics, the current driven vortex-antivortex pair breaking and vortex explosion in the Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure. We reported a pronounced twin gap structure with a large gap of unconventional pairing symmetry, corresponding to the interfacial superconductivity, and a smaller gap which opens below the characteristic BKT temperature and is associated with proximity-induced superconductivity in the Bi2Te3 layer. We revealed a pressure-induced increase in Tc is attributed to an enhancement of the electronic-coupling between the FeTe interface region and the topological Bi2Te3 surface state. [Part C: 8 (1-4)] and [Part C: 9 (1-2)]. 3) We have addressed the formation mechanisms of the nanostructures formed in heaving Fe doping of Bi2Te3, which is attributed to the strong reaction between Fe and Te atoms during the growth process. [Part C: 8(5)]. 4) Interfacial superconductivity (SC) is found in the Sb2Te3/FeTe heterostructure system as well. We have systematically studied some factors that are responsible for inducing the 2-dimensional SC, including the spin fluctuation of antiferromagnetic ordering in Fe1+yTe layer and the thickness of Sb2Te3. we propose that the superconducting pairing mediated by spin fluctuation enhanced by the hybridization of local spin moments in Fe1+yTe and 2D itinerant electrons in the TSSs of Sb2Te3 is a possible mechanism of the SC observed in the Sb2Te3/Fe1+yTe heterostructures. [Part C: 8(6)]. 5) We have also studied other aspects of the origin of the mechanism of the SC in the Bi2Te3/FeTe system via STM, UPS and ARPES experiments. It was found that an electron transfer occurs at the interface due to the misalignment of the Fermi surface between Bi2Te3 and FeTe, leading to a hole doping effect on the FeTe layer next to Bi2Te3. A mechanism of the interfacial gating induced suppression of magnetic ordering in the FeTe layer was proposed to explain the emergence of interfacial superconductivity, which echoes our previous claim that the magnetic ordering in the FeTe layer is related to the superconductivity mechanism. [Part C: 8(7)].

16304515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304515.value: Our recent discovery of a novel two-dimensional superconductivity (2D SC) at the interface of a Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure of which the two components are both non-superconducting. In this project, we have also revealed that Sb2Te3/FeTe heterostructure also enjoys such a 2D SC. Due to the possible unconventional pairing symmetry of Fe-based superconductor, these topological insulator/FeTe heterostructures could provide new platforms for creating and studying Majorana fermions in a quasi-1D template. The successful manipulation of Majorana fermions would facilitate a quantum leap in our computational and data storage abilities as these quasi-particles are ideal basic calculation units for a topological quantum computer. The PI of this project, Prof. IK SOU will join the research team led by his colleague, Prof. Vic KT Law in a recently funded CRF project (HK$5.9 M) to explore these proposed works focusing on the Bi2Te3/FeTe heterostructure. Prof. SOU has also submitted a GRF proposal targeting to fabricate both Bi-bilayer/FeTe and Sb2Te3/FeTe heterostructures followed by studying their possible quasi-1D topological SC by applying suitable sample geometry or nanowire fabrication. Our research aims to generate and detect Majorana fermions in the proposed quasi-1D systems that hold promise for realizing a topological quantum computation unit.

16304515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304515.value: This project targets to study if the deposition of other topological insulator thin films rather than Bi2Te3 on a FeTe layer also could induce a two-dimensional superconductivity (2D SC) at the interface of the heterostructure system. Most importantly, it aims to study the underlying mechanism of this novel 2D SC. A better understanding of this superconductivity could help to realize the generation and controlling of the quasi-particles, Majorana fermions, which are suitable qubits of a novel quantum computation approach. The values of this project can be summarized as followed: 1) Sb2Te3/FeTe indeed also enjoys the 2D SC and the superconducting pairing mediated by the interaction of the magnetic ordering of the FeTe layer and the interface charge carriers of the Sb2Te3 layer is a possible mechanism of the 2D SC of this heterostructure; and 2) an electron transfer occurs at the interface due to the misalignment of the Fermi surface between Bi2Te3 and FeTe, leading to a hole doping effect on the FeTe layer next to Bi2Te3. The emergence of the interfacial superconductivity may come from the suppression of the magnetic ordering. These results together have offered a better understanding of the underlying mechanism of the observed 2D SC.

16305015.label: Realisation of objectives
16305015.value: Research on materials with pure organic room temperature phosphorescence (RTP) and their application as organic single-molecular white light emitters is a hot area. Herein, a facile strategy of heavy atom-participated anion–π+ interactions is proposed to construct RTP-active organic salts. These compounds with heavy-atom counterions (bromide and iodide ions) exhibit outstanding RTP due to the external heavy atom effect via anion–π+ interactions, evidently supported by the single crystal X-ray diffraction analysis and theoretical calculation. Their single-molecular white light emission is realized by tuning the degree of crystallization. White light emission was also realized in polymer matrices and the use of the present molecules in 3D printing is demonstrated by white light lampshades. Pure organic materials with ultralong room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) are attractive alternatives to inorganic phosphors. However, they generally show inefficient intersystem crossing (ISC) owing to weak spin–orbit coupling (SOC). A novel design principle based on the combination of a small ΔEST and pure π-π* configuration of T1 to obtain efficient and ultralong RTP materials via structural isomerism. The meta isomer exhibits an ultralong lifetime of 795.0 ms with a quantum yield of 2.1%, which is among the best RTP materials reported so far. Theoretical investigations reveal that the small ΔEST is crucial to promote ISC while pure π-π* configuration of T1 enables ultralong phosphorescent emission. Systematic investigations on the structure–property relationship demonstrate that the steric hindrance and conjugation effect of the ester substituent at different positions causes large spatial separation of HOMO and LUMO and minimal electron distribution around the carbonyl group to lead to small ΔEST and pure π-π* configuration of T1. The development of single molecule white light emitters is extremely challenging for pure phosphorescent metal-free system at room temperature. In this project, five pure organic room temperature phosphors with dual RTP emission are synthesized. Experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that the dual RTP arises from the low- and high-lying triplet states. Based on this, a design strategy to achieve metal-free, pure phosphorescent and single molecular white light emitters by intrasystem mixing dual room temperature phosphorescence arising from the low- and high-lying triplet states was demonstrated. A single pure organic phosphor, namely 4-chlorobenzoyldibenzothiophene, emitting white room temperature phosphorescence with Commission Internationale de l’Éclair-age coordinates of (0.33, 0.35). Manipulation of the emission properties of pure organic room-temperature phosphors through molecular design is attractive but challenging. Tremendous efforts have been made to modulate their aggregation behaviors to suppress nonradiative decay to achieve efficient light emission and long lifetimes. However, success has been limited. In this reporting period, we present a clear picture for comprehensive understanding of the phosphorescence process of pure organic materials. We proposed a rational design principle, which involves adjusting the characteristics of molecular orbitals and the exciton configuration in the excited state by varying the molecular structure, to modulate the intrinsic RTP performance. Theoretical calculations reveal that the electronic configuration of the exciton is crucial to ISC and the phosphorescence decay. Comprehensive investigations on the molecular orbitals show that an excited state with hybrid configurations of (n,π*) and (π,π*) in appreciable proportion is desired to obtain efficient persistent RTP materials. By tuning the features of the molecular orbital and the energy level of the excited state through tailoring the aromatic subunits in arylphenones, we obtained a series of full-color pure organic phosphors with an efficiency of up to 36.0% and a long lifetime of 0.23 s under ambient conditions. The key issue is the synergistic effect of aromatic subunits and ketones, which realizes remarkably fast kISC and slow kP to afford balanced performance. Stress exists ubiquitously and is critically important for the manufacturing industry. Due to the ultrasensitive mechanoresponse of the emission of 1,1,2,2,-tetrakis(4-nitrophenyl)ethane (TPE-4N), a luminogen with aggregation-induced emission characteristics, the visualization of stress/strain distributions on metal specimens with a pure organic fluorescent material is achieved. The invisible information of mechanical strain on metal specimens was transformed to fluorescence signal for directly observation by naked eyes. Compared with traditional methods, stress/strain fluorescence mapping using TPE-4N demonstrated excellent performance and enjoyed the merits of real-time, full-field, and on-site visualization. More inspiringly, TPE-4N is the first success of pure organic material for such study on metal specimen, which opens numerous opportunities for real applications of pure organic MRL materials. It is envisioned that stress/strain visualization of complicated and practical objects, such as pivots and wheels in high-speed railway could also be achieved by TPE-4N. The development of intelligent materials, in particular those showing the highly sensitive mechanoresponsive luminescence (MRL), is desirable but challenging. In this project, a new design strategy for high performance On–Off MRL materials by controlling the intersystem crossing (ISC) process is developed. Nitro groups are incorporated into twisted AIEgens to facilitate the efficient ISC process. Experimental and theoretical investigations reveal that the nitrophenyl group effectively opens the nonradiative ISC channel to impart the high sensitivity and contrast On–Off behavior. Mechanical stimulus modulates the molecular conformations to give varied solid-state morphology with luminescence On–Off switching. Experiments demonstrate the high contrast and sensitive On–Off MRL performance as well as reversibility and fast responding behaviors.

16305015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305015.value: Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) has rarely been observed in pure organic systems due to their ease of nonradiative relaxation via molecular vibrations and rotations and oxygen-mediated quenching under ambient conditions. Thus, it is challenging to develop efficient pure organic RTP systems. There is still no clear structural design. In this project, we found that the introduction of carbonyl group and heavy atom helps promote spin-orbital coupling to increase the RTP efficiency. And an excited state with hybrid configurations of (n, π*) and (π,π*) in appreciable proportion is desired to obtain RTP materials with balanced performance in terms of efficiency and lifetime. On the other hand, the small energy band gap between the singlet and triplet excited states is beneficial to promote intersystem crossing, whereas the pure π-π* configuration of T1 helps to prolong the lifetime. Both effects work cooperatively together to result in efficient and ultralong RTP materials. We also developed a facile strategy of heavy atom-participated anion–π+ interaction to construct RTP-active materials. Single-molecule white light emission can be achieved by tuning their degree of crystallization. Additionally, metal-free, pure phosphorescent and single molecular white light emitters can be obtained by intrasystem mixing dual room temperature phosphorescence arising from the low- and high-lying triplet states. As you can see in part C of this report, 21 publications have arisen from this research project. Most of the papers are published in journal articles with high impact factors. We are confident that further research in this field will lead to more fruitful result.

16305015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305015.value: Materials with phosphorescent emission, particularly the organic ones, have attracted much attention owing to their potential applications in electronics, optics and biology. Unfortunately, efficient phosphorescence from pure organic molecules has been observed only under stringent conditions, typically at cryogenic temperatures (e.g., 77 K) and in the absence of oxygen, which significantly hampers their application. Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) has rarely been observed in pure organic systems and thus the development of efficient pure organic RTP systems is challenging but is of academic importance and practical importance. In this investigation, we have proposed few strategies to obtain efficient and persistent RTP materials such as the small energy band gap between the singlet and triplet excited states, pure π-π* configuration of T1 and the introduction of carbonyl group and halogen atom. However, what we have done is just a beginning and there are many ways awaiting us to explore. Thus, although the project completion date has passed, we are still working on the exploration of new systems and new strategies to obtain efficient and ultralong RTP materials. If we can get further support from RGC, we will hire experts to get detail study on the RTP mechanism and meanwhile explore the high-technological applications of RTP materials in various fields.

16305015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305015.value: The development of efficient pure organic systems with room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) is challenging but is of academic importance and practical importance. In this investigation, new synthetic strategies to efficient persistent RTP materials are developed, through which a series of full-color pure organic phosphors with an efficiency of up to 36.0% and a ultralong lifetime of 0.795 s under ambient conditions are obtained. White light emission was obtained from a single-molecular phosphor, which allows it to find high-technological applications such as 3D printing.

16305115.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16305115.value: 通過Copula來建立貝葉斯多變量時空分佈模型

16305115.label: Project Objectives
16305115.value: To develop multivariate spatial-temporal models via copulas. Two classes of models, observation-driven and parameter-driven, will be considered. Statistical properties of the two classes of models will be studied. To introduce Bayesian methods for estimating and analyzing the proposed models. Bayesian shrinkage analysis will also be investigated for handling potentially large numbers of variables simultaneously. To determine suitable copula functions and spatial correlation functions in copula modeling. To evaluate the proposed multivariate models using forecasting errors, statistical information criteria and Bayesian tests. The evaluation will be based on real environmental data. To consider extensions of the multivariate models to deal with count and binomial/binary spatial data.

16305115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305115.value: Variables observed over space and time are commonly used in research in areas such as environmental science, economics and biology. For example, multiple pollutant data from different locations are modeled and their health-related impacts are studied. Different weather and meteorological variables are analyzed to gain knowledge about the effects of climate changes. In spatial econometrics, relationships of economic indicators from different regions are quantified to understand interactions of economic changes in nearby regions. The spatial pattern of biological variables can also provide hints on the transmission of infectious disease and the setup of preventive measures against transmission. All of these tasks require the effective modeling of multivariate spatial-temporal data and their spatial relationships. The multivariate modeling of spatial data over time has been challenging because the dimension of the problem is a multiple of the number of variables analyzed and the number of locations of measurements, which is typically large. In addition, dealing with spatial dependence between variables is also crucial for understanding interactions between them and the implications of those interactions. The proposed study will develop parsimonious multivariate spatial-temporal models using copulas. With the help of copula theories, we will be able to capture nonlinear spatial dependence between variables. Statistical computation of the proposed models via Bayesian analysis will be investigated. It is expected that the findings will not only provide viable models for analyzing multivariate spatial-temporal variables but also lead to various applications in environmental science, economics, and biological and medical studies.

16305215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305215.value: Following the remarkable progress made in understanding and controlling the electronic properties of graphene, researchers have turned their attention to finding other atomically thin two dimensional crystals obtainable from layered materials. Among them, layered transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) have attracted great attention due to their remarkable properties. In addition to monolayer or few layers semiconducting TMDs, ultra-thin metallic TMDs have also started to emerge. Recently, it has been shown that few-layers metallic TMDs can also be obtained by mechanical exfoliation of bulk crystals. The three-dimensional (3D) bulk metallic TMDs such as MX2 (M = Nb, or Ta; X = S or Se) exhibit an interplay of charge density waves and superconductivity. Monolayer or few-layers metallic TMDs allow us to investigate the effects of dimensionality on the interplay between ordered charge and superconductivity. In this project we will first obtain monolayer and few-layers metallic TMD samples by mechanical exfoliation and then use electron-beam lithography to fabricate two-dimensional (2D) and one-dimensional (1D) devices. We will investigate the influence of going from the bulk to lower-dimensionalities on the electrical and magneto-electrical transport properties and the Raman spectra of metallic TMDs. We will focus on the occurrence of charge order and superconductivity in going from 3D to 2D to 1D. We aim to obtain insight about the various fascinating properties of these metallic TMDs. 繼在理解和控制石墨烯的電子特性取得了顯著的進步，研究人員已經把注意力轉向尋找其他原子層薄的二維晶體材料。其中，層狀過渡金屬二硫屬化物（TMDS）由於其顯著的特性已經引起了極大的關注。除了單層或數層半導體TMDS，超薄的金屬TMDS也開始出現。最近，實驗已經顯示單層或數層金屬TMDS也可通過的塊狀晶體機械剝離獲得。三維（3D）體金屬TMDS如MX2（M = Nb或Ta; X = S或Se）表現出電荷密度波和超導的相互作用。單層或數層金屬TMDS可以讓我們來研究維度對電荷有序和超導性之間的相互作用的影響。在這個項目中，我們將首先由機械剝離得到的單層和數層金屬TMD樣本，然后用電子束光刻來制造二維（ 2D）和一維（ 1D）的器件。我們將研究的從三維到較低維度對金屬TMDS的電子輸運特性和拉曼光譜的影響。我們將專注於從3D到2D到1D對於電荷有序和超導產生的影響。我們的目標是洞察有關這些金屬TMDS的各種引人入勝的性能。

16305215.label: Realisation of objectives
16305215.value: We have successfully exfoliated metallic 2D TMDCs NbS2, NbSe2, TaS2, and TaSe2. We have characterized these samples by AFM and Raman spectroscopy. We have fabricated devices with different atomic layer numbers and nanoribbon widths using e-beam lithography techniques. The nanoribbon devices are obtained by dry etching the exfoliated thin layers using RIE method, in which etching conditions are optimized to achieve smooth ribbon edges. We have measured temperature dependent resistance of these samples and identified CDW and superconducting transition temperatures. The enhanced superconductivity in few layer 2H-TaS2 and suppressed CDW transition of nanoribbon 1T-TaS2 have been investigated. Transport properties of different thickness 2H-TaS2 reveal the suppression of CDW transition signature in 2D region and at the same time the strong enhancement of superconductivity with the critical temperature of a 2D trilayer sample can be up to 2.6 K compared with 0.8 K in 3D bulk crystals. The superconducting gap is measured by four-probe differential resistance method. 1T- TaS2 demonstrates its unique three CDW evolutions with changing temperature. The decreased width of nanoribbon like channels behave similar to the decreased layer thickness samples, showing a suppressed CDW transition signature in the measurements. In addition, we have studied SPE in a Bi2Se3/NbSe2 junction fabricated with an all-dry transfer method. We have observed two sharp resistance drops at 7 K and 2 K, respectively, corresponding to the superconducting transition of NbSe2 flake and the SPE induced superconductivity in Bi2Se3 flake. We have also studied the magnetotransport properties of the topological insulator Bi2Se3 flakes grown by chemical vapor deposition. We observe the non-saturating linear transverse MR and the negative linear longitudinal MR at high magnetic fields (B>8 T). Furthermore, we have investigated experimentally the giant anisotropic magnetoresistance and its transverse version, called the planar Hall effect observed in the Dirac semimetal Cd3As2 micro-ribbons.

16305215.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305215.value: The enhanced superconductivity in few layer 2H-TaS2 and suppressed CDW transition of nanoribbon 1T-TaS2 have been investigated. Transport properties of different thickness 2H-TaS2 reveal the suppression of CDW transition and enhanced superconductivity in 2D limit of atomically thin 2H-TaS2. The critical temperature of a 2D trilayer sample is up to 2.6 K in comparison with 0.8 K in 3D bulk crystals. The measured superconducting gap fits well with BCS model. The enhanced superconductivity may be a consequence of suppression of CDW transition and the enhancement of DOS at Fermi level. Moreover, the transport characterization of bulk crystal 1T- TaS2 demonstrates its unique three CDW evolutions with temperature. However, nanoribbon devices with decreased width show a suppressed CDW transition signature similar to the decreased layer thickness samples. This may be due to higher and more stable barrier between CDW transitions induced lower dimensionality. These results are presented in an MPhil thesis. In the study of SPE in a Bi2Se3/NbSe2 junction fabricated with an all-dry transfer method, we have observed a bias-independent conductance plateau (BICP) near zero bias below 7 K and a zero bias conductance peak (ZBCP) emerging from the plateau below 2 K, which can be reproduced in our numerically simulated differential conductance spectra and show that the SPE in topological surface states in Bi2Se3 gives rise to the observed BICP below 7 K and the SPE in bulk states in Bi2Se3 give rise to the ZBCP below 2 K. A paper based on these results is published in PRB. In the magnetoresistance measurements of Bi2Se3 flakes with different thicknesses grown by CVD a non-saturating positive MR is observed in the perpendicular fields, while an evident negative MR is observed in the parallel fields. Both the positive MR and negative MR show a linear magnetic field dependence at high magnetic fields (B>8 T). These are attributed to the conductivity fluctuations in the electron accumulation layer at the surface or Bi2Se3/SiO2 interface. These results are published in APL and presented in a PhD thesis. We experimentally observe in the Dirac semimetal Cd3As2 of giant anisotropic magnetoresistance and its transverse version, called the planar Hall effect. The high anisotropy and the minus sign in this isotropic and nonmagnetic material are attributed to a field-dependent current along the magnetic field, which may be induced by the Berry curvature of the band structure. The result is published in PRB.

16305215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305215.value: What we have achieved so far indicate that fabricates the VdW heterojunction of 1T-TaS2 and 2H-NbSe2 may lead to interesting observations of the proximity effect and allow to further study the interplay of superconductivity and CDW in low temperature region. In addition, many interesting phenomena observed in the newly discovered twisted bilayer graphene imply that twisted fewer layer 2D TMDCs may also lead to many interesting findings. Further exploration in these two directions should be the future actions to take.

16305315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305315.value: Modern portfolio management often involves a large number of assets, and effectively managing large portfolios is of great importance. In this project, we aim to develop methodologies that use the increasingly available financial data to aid large portfolio management. A central object of research is the dependence structure among returns of different assets. Many investors implicitly assume that the dependence structures are similar over consecutive time periods. We will examine this assumption, to better model and predict dependence structure, and consequently improve the reliability of risk analysis and make portfolio optimization more trustworthy. Furthermore, motivated by the growing popularity of minimum variance portfolios (MVP), we will investigate the high-dimensional MVP optimization problem. 現代投資組合往往涉及到很多資產，如何有效管理大型的投資組合應此變得日益重要。在這個項目中，我們旨在發展新的方法，利用越來越多的金融數據來幫助管理投資組合。這其中一個中心的研究對象是投資組合裡各個資產之間的相關性。一個常常默認的假設是相鄰時間段內相關性是類似的。這個假設有多合理？我們會提出方法來檢驗這樣的假設，並在此基礎上更好的建模及預測，以提高風險管理及組合優化的可靠性。另一方面，對於日益受到重視的最小方差投資組合，我們也會利用高維統計的方法來研究如何優化。

16305615.label: Project Objectives
16305615.value: To construct a cold-atom-cavity experimental apparatus. Unlike previous systems, we will create a cold atomic ensemble with high optical depth (>50) inside the cavity using a two-dimensional magneto-optical trap. To excite two-level atoms inside the cavity with a single photon. We will investigate how to efficiently excite two-level atoms inside cavity with a single photon, by carefully shaping the single photon waveform and making use of our recently demonstrated photon-cavity loading technique. We will also study the differences as we increase the number of atom inside the cavity. To explore quantum interaction between photon and atoms inside the cavity. To generate ultra-narrowband biphotons with coherence time >3 us. Using cavity resonance enhancement and frequency filtering, the SFWM biphoton generation can be enhanced while the unpaired off-cavity-resonance Raman and Raleigh scattering noise photons are suppressed.

16305615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305615.value: Cavity quantum electrodynamics (CQED) studies quantum interactions between photons and atoms inside an optical cavity. Its potential applications in quantum information processing and quantum computation have attracted much research interests, especially since the 2012 Nobel physics prize. In the past, most experimental work with single photons has focused on the frequency domain, while the work in time domain took weak coherent light. Here, we propose an experimental program to explore CQED with a single photon in the time domain. We will construct a CQED apparatus able to maintain an atomic cloud with high optical depth inside an optical cavity. We will study the quantum interactions of such an atomic ensemble inside a cavity with an injected heralded single photon with controllable temporal waveform. Our target is to demonstrate a highly efficient CQED-based quantum interface between a true single photon and many atoms. Success will pave the way toward applications in quantum communication and quantum computation. 腔量子電動力學研究光子和原子在光學諧振腔裡面的量子相互作用。自從2012年的諾貝爾物理學獎之後，由於其在量子信息處理和量子計算方面的潛在應用，腔量子電動力學吸引了世界各地巨大的研究熱情。在過去，大多數此類涉及單光子的實驗研究局限於頻域，而在時域的研究工作均採用弱相干光源。在本研究計劃裡，我們提出了一個研究在時域裡的單光子腔量子電動力學的方案。通過控制單光子的時域量子波函數，我們將研究單個光子如何同位於光學腔內的一大團原子相互作用。我們的目標是建立連接單光子和原子的基於腔量子電動力學的高效量子接口。該項目的成功將為腔量子電動力學在量子通訊和量子計算的廣泛應用奠定基礎。

16305615.label: Realisation of objectives
16305615.value: All the objectives have been successfully realized and fully achieved: (1) We have successfully constructed a cold-atom-cavity experimental apparatus. Loading laser-cooled atoms to a two-dimensional magneto-optical trap inside the cavity, we obtained a cavity-enhanced optical depth up to 7600. [Rev. Sci. Instrum. 90, 013105 (2019).] (2) We studied the excitation of two-level atoms inside the cavity. Coupling photons to the two-level cold atoms inside the cavity, we observed vacuum Rabi splitting (VRS). As we increase the number of atoms inside the cavity, we observed that the VRS is proportional to square root of the atomic optical depth. [Rev. Sci. Instrum. 90, 013105 (2019).] (3) We have explored quantum interaction between photons and atoms inside the cavity. Making use of the light-induced quantum coherence, we successfully demonstrated a photonic quantum heat engine using cold atoms with electromagnetically induced transparency. We further demonstrated optical parametric oscillation with tunable threshold in cold atoms. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 119, 050602 (2017); Phys. Rev. Lett. 119, 150406 (2017).] (4) We produced narrowband time-frequency entangled photon pairs (biphotons) and test the Bell inequality using time-resolved detection. [Optica 4, 388 (2017).] Summary: Realization of the objectives has leaded to a series of publications [Phys. Rev. Lett. 119, 050602 (2017); Phys. Rev. 16305615.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305615.value: We have achieved the following major findings and research outcomes: (1) Intracavity cold atomic ensemble with high optical depth. We developed a cold-atom-cavity experimental apparatus loaded with cold Rb85 atoms of high optical depth (OD) in the weak coupling regime. We obtained a cavity enhanced OD up to 7600 – this is the highest value record in the world - with an enhancement factor of about 188. This system will have many applicaiotns in studying collective atom-light interaction inside cavity. Our result was published in Review of Scientific Instruments [Rev. Sci. Instrum. 90, 013105 (2019)]. Representative Publications: [1] Rev. Sci. Instrum. 90, 013105 (2019) (2) Quantum heat engine with electromagnetically induced transparency We demonstrated a photonic quantum heat engine using cold atoms with electromagnetically induced transparency. Making use of light induced atomic coherence, we produce a directional thermal radiation with a spectral brightness 9 times greater than the reservoir. Our results violate detailed balance principle and Kirchhoff’s law. It is considered as an early demonstration of a nontraditional coherence-based quantum heat engine. It provides insight for developing future generation heat engines with higher efficiency and performances which cannot be reached by traditional heat engines. The work was published in Physical Review Letters. Representative Publications: [1] Phys. Rev. Lett. 119, 150406 (2017) (3) Optical parametric oscillation with tunable threshold With our cold atom apparatus, we demonstrated an optical parametric oscillation with tunable threshold with four-wave mixing using electromagnetically induced transparency. In presence two classical laser beams, we produce a pair of counterpropagating photons which build up intrinsic nonlinear feedback for the parametric oscillation. The pump threshold can be controlled by the system parameters, with the lowest threshold pump power of 15 uW. The narrow spectral width is 16 kHz. This is the world first-kind of such experiment. The work was published in Physical Review Letters. Representative Publications: [1] Phys. Rev. Lett. 119, 150406 (2017). (4) Violation of Bell inequality with frequency-bin entanglement In all previous Bell test experiments, the photon coherence time is much shorter than the detection time. Making use of the long coherence time of our produced narrowband time-frequency entangled biphotons, for the first time we tested the Bell inequality on frequency-bin entanglement using time-resolved detection. Our result violates the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) Bell inequality |S|<=2 with the measured |S|=2.52. Our result will have applications in quantum information processing involving time-frequency entanglement. Representative Publications: [1] Optica 4, 388 (2017).

16305615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305615.value: Potential for further development of the research and proposed course of action may include: (1) To reduce the ground-state dephasing rate of cold atoms in cavity. (2) To explore applications in quantum information processing. (3) To explore applications in quantum network.

16305615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305615.value: Cavity quantum electrodynamics (CQED) studies quantum interaction between photons and atoms confined inside an optical cavity. Its potential applications in quantum information processing have attracted much research interests, especially since the 2012 Nobel Prize in Physics. In this research project, we have developed a cold-atom-cavity experimental apparatus in weak coupling regime. We obtained a cavity enhanced OD up to 7600 – this is a new world record. With this unique cold atom system, we demonstrated a nontraditional quantum heat engine and realized an optical parametric oscillation with tunable threshold. For the narrowband photon pairs generated from this system, we made the first test of the Bell inequality of frequency-bin entanglement with time-resolved detection. Our results, making a new case of CQED in weak coupling regime, will have impact on the development of future quantum technology based on precisely controlling individual quantum systems.

16305715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16305715.value: 格顶点算子代数和 Siegel-Weil 公式

16305715.label: Project Objectives
16305715.value: The Siegel mass formula for theta functions is an identity of a certain sum of theta functions for lattices and Eisenstein series. We will find a generalization of the identity, in which one side is a sum of genus one correlation functions of lattice vertex algebras, and the other side is a chiral generalization of Eisenstein series. We will study vertex algebras for hyperbolic lattices. The Siegel's definition of theta series for non-definite lattices suggests that it is possible to define the character of these vertex algebras. We study the character and n-point correlation functions on torus. We will study the vertex algebra of a beta-gamma system from the loop group representation point of view. And we will look for possible connections between our earlier work on Weil representation of loop groups and beta-gamma system.

We will find a generalization of the identity, in which one side is a sum of genus one correlation functions of lattice vertex algebras, and the other side is a chiral generalization of Eisenstein series.

We will study vertex algebras for hyperbolic lattices. The Siegel's definition of theta series for non-definite lattices suggests that it is possible to define the character of these vertex algebras. We study the character and n-point correlation functions on torus.

We will study the vertex algebra of a beta-gamma system from the loop group representation point of view. And we will look for possible connections between our earlier work on Weil representation of loop groups and beta-gamma system.

16305715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305715.value: The mathematical concept of a group captures the essence of symmetry in abstract terms. The representation theory is a branch of mathematics that studies the groups and their representations. The vertex algebra is a mathematical structure that appeared in the study of mathematical physics. The theory has been rapidly developing in the recent 20 years and has emerged as an active area in representation theory. In this project, we propose to study the connections of lattice vertex algebras with the more classical area of representation theory, the theory of automorphic forms. We will start from the Siegel mass formula for theta functions of even unimodular lattices. The formula can be interpreted as a formula for the characters of lattice vertex algebras. This interpretation suggests the generalization of Siegel's formula to correlation functions of lattice vertex algebras on torus. We plan to find this generalization and further explore the connections between lattice vertex algebras and automorphic forms. It is important to find relations of seemingly unrelated fields. 群的概念產生於對稱性的研究。表示論是數學中關於群及其表 示理論的一個分支。頂點算子代數是數學物理中自然產生的概 念， 和物理中的對稱性緊密相關。過去20 多年，對頂點算子代 數的研究發展很快，它已經成為表示論中一個重要研究方向。 本項目將研究格頂點算子代數和表示論中一些傳統領域的關係。 如自守型。 我們的出發點是著名的Siegel Mass 公式。我們對此公式的新理 解是它和頂點算子代數特徵的關係。這種新解釋指明了進一步 研究的方向。這個項目的順利完成將使我們對圈群， Siegel Mass 公式， 和Chiral De Rham Complex 的關係加深理解。

16305715.label: Realisation of objectives
16305715.value: We have achieved most of the research objectives. However the results we have obtained are not quite the same as we planed in this proposal. In the work to achieve the first and second objective, we found new constructions of representations of loop groups and the affine Kac-Moody algebras, and this new construction leads us to introduce the concept of topological modules over vertex algebras. These results deviate from our original plan to generalize the Seigel-Weil representation using vertex algebras. The third objective is completely achieved and much more have been done. My student Hongbo Zhao, who was partially funded by this project, published two papers related to this part of project.

16305715.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305715.value: In this project, we studied vertex algebras and the related objects such as loop groups and Kac-Moody algebras. We obtained the following results. (1) We obtained a new construction of representation of loop groups using certain function function spaces on certain infinite dimensional spaces. (2) We gave a new type of free field realization of representations of affine Kac-Moody algebras. (3). We introduced the concept of topological modules over vertex algebras, this extends the usual module theory over vertex algebras and gave some interesting examples of topological modules. (4). My student Hongbo Zhao studied the theta correspondence of vertex algebras and his work was published.

16305715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305715.value: We introduced the new concept "topological modules over algebras". This extends the representation theory of vertex algebras to include more interesting examples. The new construction of representations of loop groups and affine Kac-Moody algebras can been further generalized to p-adic loop groups.

16305715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305715.value: Our research enriches the representation theory of vertex algebras, loop group and affine Kac-Moody algebras. It has potential applications to other subjects.

16305815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305815.value: Our lab has developed structural mimics of viruses by the spontaneous co-assembly of short designer peptide and DNA. The peptides adopting a beta-sheet structure wrap around plasmid DNA in an orderly manner. Unlike most nano-complexes containing DNA and polycations, unique and sophisticated nanostructures are obtained from this simple system, appearing as nano-sized cocoons with uniformly striped surfaces. We will illustrate the elegance of self-assembly in this project --- by using a bottom-up approach to engineer virus-like functions into the newly-discovered nanostructures. Control of structural properties, which then impart functions, will be enabled by the design of peptide sequences. The peptide template consist of 4 segments: 1) an N-terminal DNA-binding oligolysine, 2) a central short hydrophobic β-sheet forming segment, 3) an alkyl inker to bridge segment, and 4) a C-terminal hydrophilic segment. Through systematically altering the sequence in each segment, we can modulate the driving force for self-assembly. This understanding will allow us to balance the assembly and disassembly properties, thereby constructing a robust nanostructure capable of timely disintegration to release the encapsulated cargoes. We will render stimuli-responsiveness to the nano-cocoon by incorporating acid- or UV-sensitive residues in the peptide. We plan to use the C-terminal segment to expose signal sequences for modulating the interaction of nano-cocoons with cells. The structured peptide self-assemblies provide a tunable platform to change the spatial arrangement of these signal sequences on the nano-cocoon surface, optimizing the display to achieve biological effects. The morphology and structural details will be thoroughly examined by physical techniques (TEM, AFM, circualr dichroism, FTIR, X-ray powder diffraction, and dynamic light scattering, etc.) In proof-of-concept experiments on cultured cells, we will evaluate specific cellular uptake and gene transfection efficiency of nano-cocoons engineered with desirable properties. Based on the knowledge of the nanostructure, we will also evaluate the possibility of expanding the types of cargoes to include DNA and RNA of different lengths, as well as small hydrophobic molecules. This project will enrich the design of a new category of self-assembling nanomaterials. It paves way to the development of new therapeutics and medical applications based on virus-mimicking functional materials.

16305815.label: Realisation of objectives
16305815.value: We have completed more than 95% of our proposed objectives. We successfully developed peptide-DNA co-assembled artificial virus. Through sequence variation, we understood the co-assembling mechanism. By incorporation of stimulus-responsive units into the system, the transgene expression efficiency was significantly improved. For objective 4, we encountered some realistic issues: 1) since the self-assembling peptide (SAP) strand is short, the addition of a long peptide ligand to the SAP significantly altered the peptide assembly propensity. To overcome this problem, we changed to a new strategy that was through the post-conjugation of peptide ligands on the surface of peptide assemblies. This strategy is currently still under exploration.

16305815.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305815.value: In this project, we discovered a general rule for peptide-DNA co-assemblies, which is independent on peptide sequence and the size of encapsulated plasmid DNA. By introducing stimulus-responsive units into the peptide strands, the co-assembled artificial virus displays not only virus-like structure/morphology, but also virus-like function (transgene expression). These research findings have been presented on several international conferences and published on highly impacted scientific journals.

16305815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305815.value: This peptide-DNA co-assembly system is a good example of nature-inspired biomimetics. The research findings have paved the way for further development of non-viral gene delivery vectors. In addition, the discovered peptide self-assemblies and peptide-DNA co-assemblies display significantly different surface patterns, which inspires the further exploration of the peptide-based vaccine delivery.

16305815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305815.value: The best way to cure a disease is to treat its origin. The origin of some life-threatening diseases such as cancer is due to the malfunctioned genes. The goal of this project is to make an artificial virus, which could deliver therapeutic genetic drugs into the disease part to cure the disease.

16305915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16305915.value: Polymer solar cell (PSC) technology is low cost and environmentally friendly, allowing solar panels to be produced using high throughput printing methods. A PSC device consists of the blend film of a polymer donor and a fullerene acceptor. The donor polymer has been the main driving force for the development of the PSC field. To date, most donor polymers in PSCs have intermediate (1.5 - 1.8 eV) optical bandgaps. There are limited choices of high-performance large (>1.9 eV) or small (< 1.4 eV) bandgap polymers that are essential components for the construction of tandem PSCs, which could reach over 20% efficiency in theory. One goal of this project is to develop donor polymers with large or small optical bandgaps for tandem PSCs. Another application of large and small bandgap polymers is “cosmetic solar cells” for building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV). In contrast to inorganic solar cells that exhibit poor color tunability, donor polymers with various bandgaps will provide better-looking solar panels with various colors such as blue, red or green. In general, the development of donor polymers (with large, small or intermediate bandgaps) faces similar challenges. Firstly, PSC material design has been carried out in a trial-and-error approach and has low success rates, which can be partially attributed to the sensitive polymer:fullerene blend morphology that is difficult to predict or control. Secondly, the majority of high-efficiency PSCs are based on relatively thin (100 nm) active layers. When the thickness of the active layer is increased to 300 nm, the fill factor typically suffers a dramatic decrease that leads to poor cell efficiencies. Lastly, best PSC performances can only be achieved with a specific fullerene, PC71BM, which, however, is highly expensive. Recently, we reported a material design rationale that had led to three different donor polymers and ten polymer:fullerene combinations which all exhibit higher efficiencies (up to 10.8%) than the previous best devices. These high efficiencies were achieved with very thick (~ 300 nm) active layers and can be obtained with many non-conventional fullerenes under a well controllable polymer:fullerene morphology. The key feature of our three 10% efficiency polymers is a structural motif called 2OD-T4, which enabled a highly temperature dependent aggregation property for the polymers and thus great PSC performances. In this project, we will apply our successful material design rationale by combining the 2OD-T4 motif with several electron-poor or -rich building blocks to develop high-performance donor polymers with large or small optical bandgaps. 高分子太阳能电池（PSC）技术成本低且具有环境友好型的特点，使得太阳能电池面板可以使用高产量的印刷技术制备而成。高分子太阳能电池的活性层由高分子供体和富勒烯受体的共混物组成。而且供体高分子是高分子太阳能电池领域发展的主要驱动力。 当前，高分子太阳能电池中的大多数供体高分子的光学能隙都比较适中(1.5-1.8 eV)，高性能的大光学能隙以及小光学能隙比较少，而这些高分子是串联高分子电池的重要组成部分。串联太阳能电池理论上可获得20%的光电转换效率。我们此项目的目标就是研发适合串联高分子太阳能电池的较大光学能隙或较小光学能隙的供体高分子。另一个大光学能隙和小光学能隙的高分子的应用是作为光伏建筑一体化的表面太阳能电池。无机太阳能电池具有较差的色彩可调性，相比之下，具有不同光学能隙的供体高分子使得太阳能电池面板更好看，更多彩。 总体来说，供体高分子（较大，较小或是适中的光学能隙）的发展面临着相同的挑战。首先，高分子太阳能电池材料的设计总是有着相似的历程：尝试然后失败，成功率极低。部分原因可能是高分子：富勒烯共混层的形貌比较敏感，且难以预测和控制。第二，大多数高性能的高分子太阳能电池的活性层相对较薄（100 nm）,当活性层的厚度增加到300 nm,填充因子会急剧下降，导致电池效率较低。最后，最好性能的高分子太阳能电池的获得只能使用一种特定的受体PC71BM, 然而PC71BM非常昂贵。 最近，我们报道了一个材料设计的基本原理使得基于三种不同的高分子和十个高分子：富勒烯组合的太阳能电池的光电转换效率达10.8%，比之前报道过的最好效率都要高。在可控性较好的高分子：富勒烯形貌下，较厚的活性层（~300 nm）以及和非常规的富勒烯工作都能取得较高效率。三个可获得~10 %光电转换效率的高分子的关键特称是它们都具有2OD-T4的结构基元，这个特殊的结构基元使得高分子具有基于温度变化聚集的性质以及较好的高分子太阳能电池的性能。 在此项目中，我们将应用我们成功的材料设计原理，把2OD-T4基元和几个缺电子或富电子的结构单元相结合，从而研发出高性能的具有较大或较小光学能隙的受体高分子。

16305915.label: Realisation of objectives
16305915.value: In this project, the objectives have been achieved. We have successfully developed a range of high-performance donor polymer, especially a series of Temperature-dependent Aggregation (TDA) polymers that have been processed with non-fullerene acceptors to make high-performance Organic solar cells (OSCs). First, on order to achieve efficient organic solar cells, the design of suitable donor–acceptor couples is crucially important. State-of-the-art donor polymers used in fullerene cells may not perform well when they are combined with non-fullerene acceptors, thus new donor polymers need to be developed. Here we developed non-fullerene organic solar cells with efficiencies up to 10.9%, enabled by a novel donor polymer that exhibits strong temperature-dependent aggregation but with intentionally reduced polymer crystallinity due to the introduction of a less symmetric monomer unit. Our comparative study shows that an analogue polymer with a C2 symmetric monomer unit yields highly crystalline polymer films but less efficient non-fullerene cells. Based on a monomer with a mirror symmetry, our best donor polymer exhibits reduced crystallinity, yet such a polymer matches better with small molecular acceptors. This study provides important insights to the design of donor polymers for non-fullerene organic solar cells. Furthermore, it is important to reduce the voltage loss from the optical bandgap to the open-circuit voltage of the cell in order to achieve efficient non-fullerene organic solar cells, Hence, we designed a highly efficient non-fullerene organic solar cell with a high open-circuit voltage of 1.08 V and a small voltage loss of 0.55 V. The high performance was enabled by a novel wide-bandgap (2.05 eV) donor polymer paired with a narrow-bandgap (1.63 eV) small molecular acceptor (SMA). Our morphology characterizations show that both the polymer and the SMA can maintain high crystallinity in the blend film, resulting in crystalline and small domains. As a result, our nonfullerene organic solar cells realize an efficiency of 11.6%, which is the best performance for a non-fullerene organic solar cell with such a small voltage loss. To maximize the VOC of PSCs, it is important to fine-tune the energy level offset between the donor and acceptor materials, but in a way not negatively affecting the morphology of the donor: acceptor (D: A) blends. an effective material design rationale based on a family of D–A1–D–A2 terthiophene (T3) donor polymers is reported, which allows for the effective tuning of energy levels but without any negative impacts on the morphology of the blend. Based on a T3 donor unit combined with difluorobenzothiadiazole (ffBT) and difluorobenzoxadiazole (ffBX) acceptor units, three donor polymers are developed with highly similar morphological properties. This is particularly surprising considering that the corresponding quarter-thiophene polymers based on ffBT and ffBX exhibit dramatic differences in their solubility and morphological properties. With the fine-tuning of energy levels, the T3 polymers yield non-fullerene PSCs with a high efficiency of 9.0% for one case and with a remarkably low energy loss (0.53 V) for another polymer. This work will facilitate the development of efficient non-fullerene PSCs with optimal energy levels and favorable morphology properties.

16305915.label: Major findings and research outcome
16305915.value: First, we study the influence of donor polymer’s crystallinity on device performance and we find that one polymer with a C2 symmetric monomer unit yields highly crystalline polymer films but less efficient non-fullerene cells while a novel donor polymer with intentionally reduced polymer crystallinity due to the introduction of a less symmetric monomer unit shows higher device performance. This study provides important insights to the design of donor polymers for non-fullerene organic solar cells. (Nature communications 2016, 7, 13094.) Second, in order to reduce the voltage loss from the optical bandgap to the open-circuit voltage of the cell to further improve efficiency of organic solar cells, we designed a highly efficient non-fullerene organic solar cell with a high open-circuit voltage of 1.08 V and a small voltage loss of 0.55 V. The high performance was enabled by a novel wide-bandgap (2.05 eV) donor polymer paired with a narrow-bandgap (1.63 eV) small molecular acceptor (SMA). As a result, our nonfullerene organic solar cells realize an efficiency of 11.6%. (Journal of the American Chemical Society 2017, 139 (18), 6298-6301.) Third, we reported an effective material design rationale based on a family of D–A1–D–A2 terthiophene (T3) donor polymers, which allows for the effective tuning of energy levels but without any negative impacts on the morphology of the blend. Based on a T3 donor unit combined with difluorobenzothiadiazole (ffBT) and difluorobenzoxadiazole (ffBX) acceptor units, three donor polymers are developed with highly similar morphological properties. This is particularly surprising considering that the corresponding quarter-thiophene polymers based on ffBT and ffBX exhibit dramatic differences in their solubility and morphological properties. With the fine-tuning of energy levels, the T3 polymers yield non-fullerene PSCs with a high efficiency of 9.0% for one case and with a remarkably low energy loss (0.53 V) for another polymer. This work will facilitate the development of efficient non-fullerene PSCs with optimal energy levels and favorable morphology properties. (Advanced Energy Materials 2017, 7 (15).)

16305915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16305915.value: Recently, Y6-derivatives small molecule acceptors show a potential to make high performance organic solar cells. Therefore, it is significant to find suitable donor polymer to match with Y6-derivatives small molecule acceptors since the design of suitable donor–acceptor couples is crucially important. What's more, tandem solar cell architecture is efficient way to reduce the energy loss. We still have to develpment new type of donor polymers for making high-performace fornt cells and back cells of tandem solar cell.

16305915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16305915.value: In this project, we have designed several efficient polymer donors for making non-fullerene based organic solar cells, and devices based on these polymers showed high performance with maintaining good stability. The success of this project not only provide an excellent platform to study the influence of polymer structures on device performance, but also establish fundamental knowledge of aggregation behaviors of these polymers among the photovoltaic devices. Moreover, these functional materials can also be used for broad electronic devices with diode structures, such as photodiodes, light-emitting diodes, and sensors in the future.

16306115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306115.value: 单细胞的蛋白组研究比基因组或者转基因组研究能提供更多关于细胞功能（如信号传导）的直接信息。然而，细胞体积很小，而且许多重要的蛋白质在细胞里数目非常少。因为没有蛋白质扩增技术，单细胞的蛋白研究非常困难。尽管传统的细胞流式仪对单细胞蛋白分析比较有效，但是它的缺点是价格高，单次需要大量细胞，并且一般实验室没有这样的仪器。近期微流控技术被开始用于单细胞蛋白研究，但是现在它还有诸如低通量，可研究的蛋白质比较少，以及细胞物质被大量稀释等不足。 这里我们将发展一种新技术，结合高密度微阵列、微流控技术和免疫分析技术来对单细胞内的蛋白质进行高通量分析。微坑阵列可以极大地简化细胞操作并减少把单细胞相互分离的时间。我们的设计也不需要其他微流控芯片必须的辅助部件，这样不仅可以大大地提高微阵列密度还能简化芯片的操作。我们的方法只需要使用离心技术来分离单细胞。球形微坑能有助于细胞装入以及随后把多余的细胞除去。该芯片能处理微量溶液进行细胞内蛋白质的免疫分析，也能研究单细胞分泌的蛋白质；此外，也能研究细胞之间相互作用所参与的蛋白。 我们提出的技术将能够在10分钟内同时分析一百万个单细胞，并且原则上对可研究（取决于可用的抗体）的蛋白质的数量没有局限。因为对细胞物质的稀释非常低（仅1-2倍），免疫测定的灵敏度将大大提高。此外，该技术对于各种细胞类型都使用而且操作（主要涉及一般的离心和免疫测定步骤）非常简单。该工作将提供一种新型的强大工具用于高通量和多用型单细胞蛋白质组研究。该技术将允许我们更好地理解细胞信号转导途径，细胞间相互作用，干细胞分化和各种疾病（如癌症）。此外，我们的单细胞蛋白质组研究技术具有很大的潜力，可以开辟在疾病诊断和预测（例如，以确定稀有细胞）的新技术。

16306115.label: Realisation of objectives
16306115.value: We show the realization of objectives one by one below: 1. To develop a convenient technique for arraying single cells in extremely high-density microwells (up to 1 million cells/square inch). We have developed a facile centrifugation-assisted single-cell trapping (CAScT) approach based on a truncated cone-shaped microwell array (TCMA) chip for both arraying single cells and performing real-time observations of cellular apoptosis. Our method requires neither a pump nor a pressure-controlling system, and it greatly reduces the complexity of other cell-trapping devices. This method is so fast and efficient that single-cell occupancy could reach approximately 90% within a few seconds. Combined with modern fluorescence microscopy, CAScT makes the highly ordered and addressable TCMA an extremely high-throughput platform (more than 1 million cells per square inch) for single-cell analysis (refer to #1 and #10 papers in Part C). This Objective is successfully completed. 2. To establish a method for immunoassay of individual cells in the array; Cells trapped in the array could be exposed to various chemicals by directly immersing it in bulk solutions without the significant loss of cells due to the truncated cone shape of the microwells. As a proof of concept, we demonstrated the ability of our chip for the real-time observation of the apoptosis of single HeLa cells induced by the common anticancer drug doxorubicin. We also established a method for immunoassay of individual cells in the array. Further, we integrated our arraying method with time-of-ﬂight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) for the study of drug-induced cellular phenotypic alterations. Micropatterned poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) stencil ﬁlm and centrifugation-assisted cell trapping were combined for the preparation of on-surface single-cell microarrays, which exhibited both high site occupancy (>90%) and single-cell resolution (>97%). TOF-SIMS is a surface-sensitive mass spectrometry and is increasingly utilized in biological studies. We demonstrated, for the ﬁrst time, its successful application in high-throughput single-cell analysis. Drug-induced phenotypic alterations of HeLa cells in the early stage of apoptosis were investigated using TOF-SIMS. The major molecular sources of variations were analyzed by principle component analysis (PCA). This simple, robust, and efficient approach possesses great potential in diverse applications, such as drug screening, bio-sensing, and fundamental biological research (refer to #1, #6, #9 and #10 papers in Part C). This Objective is successfully completed. 3. To analyze multiple proteins in single cells in the array. Our technology of centrifugation-assisted single-cell trapping (CAScT) integrated with time-of-ﬂight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS) can be used to study various types of molecules, including multiple proteins in single cells in the array (refer to #1, #6, #9 and #10 papers in Part C). This Objective is successfully completed. 4. To explore the developed technique for other types of assays of single cells. We explore our developed single-cell technology for other types of assays of single cells. For example, we studied cell apoptosis under anti-cancer drugs, paired individual cells followed with induced cell fusion, and paired individual cells for cell-cell interactions studies (refer to #1, #6, #9 and #10 papers in Part C). Furthermore, we extended our exploration to develop other cell-related techniques. For example, we fabricated a circulatory system microchip to simulate human circulatory systems (refer to #2 in Part C), developed a new method for forming microporous chitosan hydrogel for 3D cell culture (refer to #7 in Part C), invented a new technology for generating 3D hydrogel networks for 3D tissue engineering (refer to #5 in Part C), and others (refer to #3, #4, #8, and #11-13 papers in Part C). This Objective is successfully completed.

16306115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306115.value: Our major findings and research outcome are the following: 1. We developed a new, convenient method for arraying single cells in extremely high-density microwells (more than 1 million cells/square inch), which we name centrifugation-assisted single-cell trapping (CAScT) technique. 2. We developed a new method for analyzing single-cell molecular contents, including lipids and peptides, with mass spectrometry by combining CAScT with time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (TOF-SIMS). 3. With the CAScT technique, we developed a convenient method for cell pairing and subsequent cell fusion. 4. By modifying the CAScT technique, we developed a controllable, centrifugal-based hydrodynamic microchip for cell-pairing and subsequent long-term cell-cell communications at the single-cell level. 5. We invented a microfluidic chip for mimicking human circulatory systems. 6. We developed a few methods for 3D cell culturing and tissue engineering, including macroporous hydrogel and fabricating 3D cell-encapsulated complex hydrogel networks. 7. We also developed a one-step strategy for ultra-fast and low-cost mass production of plastic microfluidic chips, which will be useful in the fabrication of cell microchips.

16306115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306115.value: Potential for further development of this research will be: 1. To apply our developed CAScT method for various single-cell studies, e.g., differentiations of stem cells, cell-cell interactions and drug screening. 2. To optimize the integration of CAScT with TOF-SIMS, e.g., to have a wider spectrum of molecules of study, to enable easy interpretation of MS data, and to increase the throughput of the overall analysis. 3. We will use our developed single-cell study techniques to collaborate with researchers in biology, biochemistry, and medical fields to solve particular biological questions at the single-cell level.

16306115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306115.value: Here we have developed a facile centrifugation-assisted single-cell trapping (CAScT) approach based on a truncated cone-shaped microwell array chip for both arraying single cells and various subsequent single-cell studies. It required neither pumps nor pressure-controlling systems, and it greatly reduced the complexity of other cell-trapping devices. This method is so fast and efficient that single-cell occupancy could reach approximately 90% within a few seconds. Combined with fluorescence microscopy, CAScT offered an extremely high-throughput platform (over 1 million cells per square inch) for single-cell analysis. It also allowed long-term study of individual cells in high throughputs. Further, we integrated this method with time-of-ﬂight secondary ion mass spectrometry for the study of drug-induced cellular phenotypic alterations, which showed outstanding performances compared with other methods. We demonstrated, for the ﬁrst time, its successful application in high-throughput single-cell analysis of drug-induced phenotypic alterations of HeLa cells in the early stage of apoptosis. Moreover, we extended our technique for more cell studies such as pairing individual cells, cell fusion of single cells, and studying cell-cell interactions. The developed technique here will allow us to better understand cell signal transduction pathways, cell-cell interactions, stem cell differentiations and various diseases such as cancers.

16306315.label: Project Objectives
16306315.value: To build a proper function theoretic foundation for the finite difference calculus with reference to interpolatory aspects of difference operators in general, and the Askey-Wilson operator and Wilson operator in particular. The first aim is to build relevant difference Nevanlinna theories with respect to the interpolatory aspects that are natural for the corresponding difference operators. The second aim is to understand the implication of the study of values distibution of meromorphic functions in relation to the study of the interpolatory aspects of difference operators. In particular, one would like to understand the singularity structures at singular points revealed by the first objective. This leads natually to understanding analogous concepts of residue calculus and their interpretation at a more abstract level.

16306315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306315.value: Interpolation theories have theoretical interests in both pure mathematics and numerical computations of finite difference schemes which have numerous applications in a wide variety of scientific research. This proposal aims to provide a function theoretic understanding for this important branch of mathematics. In fact, mathematicians have used complex analytic methods to find and to study solutions of difference equations even before the 1930s. The main interest and development of finite difference theories are biased naturally toward solving real-life problems with the advances of computational tools in the twentieth century. However, in recent years researchers of special functions, non-linear discrete integrable systems and complex functions have gradually noticed a strong and deep connection between finite difference schemes and complex analytic structures that require further study. Some initial successes have been made in recent years by applying classical Nevanlinna’s complex analytic values distribution theories to study both linear and non-linear difference equations for which I have played a part. We have discovered deep analytic structures behind many finite difference operators arising from current special functions research, thus giving novel interpretations to phenomena that were not noticed before. For example, We have found that in one of the special cases of interpolation polynomial sequence (Wilson basis) that plays an important role in recent special function theory development were originally used by Newton and further developed by Stirling around 1730 extensively in numerical computation. In particular, we have found that there they have deep complex analytic structure not known before. In short, one can conclude that what appears to hold for differential operators defined on the complex plane in the past in fact also hold for difference operators, but with the need to find novel ways to see and comprehend new structures. This project aims to widen earlier works which are heavily Nevanlinna theoretic to include finding new ways to understand a residue calculus with respect to difference operators. We also aim to consolidate our earlier difference Nevanlinna theories research with proper interpolation polynomials as base instead of the usual Laurent series.

16306315.label: Realisation of objectives
16306315.value: The essence of this project is to make a comprehensive study of complex function theory/value distribution theory with interpolation series and corresponding finite difference operators instead of the classical power series approach. We have achieved in finding explicit results relating the growth of entire functions concerning the properties of their interpolating series expansions with analog theories of Wiman-Valiron. This results in one published paper (J. Approx. Thy. 2019) and one submitted paper (2019). The publication (Ann. Acad. Sci. Fenn. (2017)) was partially supported with this grant and its main theme is related to this proposal. However, the project encountered an impasse while we tried to interpret the meaning of multiplicities when two interpolation series for two functions are multiplied, a difficulty that was not anticipated since the corresponding issue for Taylor/Laurent expansions is well-known and straightforward. This is an issue every mathematician working on this issue would have to deal with. It took us over a year to find a possible remedy after numerous trials and errors. The potential remedy draws on ideas from operator algebra combined with non-commutative algebra. We discarded this idea initially since it appeared too radically different from our original goal. It took us almost another year to recognise that the non-commutative approach is our only way forward. The operator approach also recovers the well-known multiplicity rules of operations for classical Taylor/Laurent expansions. By that time, we had already passed the project completion deadline. However, our new approach allows us to develop a radically different approach to the classical function theory with respect to interpolation bases and difference operators. This results in a manuscript to be completed in the next six months. We tried to tackle another issue related to the value distribution of values of a complex analytic function at an essential singularity with respect to a difference operator (depending on Laurent expansion analog of an interpolation basis). In order to develop analogs of Weiestrass type theorem (i.e., the image of the neighbourhood of the ``essential singularity” is dense in the complex plane), we encountered another difficulty to formulate a correct version of Liouville-type theorem for difference operators. The classical Liouville theorem states that a bounded entire function is a constant. We interpret constants being members of the kernel of differential operators. Thus our question becomes: what does it mean to have a ``bounded entire function” so that it must belong to the kernel of a difference operator? This would be a natural first step to investigate the value distribution of a meromorphic function in an interpolation sense. Unfortunately, we spent a long period of time on this issue. Only recently, and beyond the completion date that we have made some definite progress. We have introduced unconventional set up that amount to have a special factorization (not to be confused with the Hadamard factorization) of the finite order entire/meromorphic function concerned with factors in different function spaces. We have also found another approach that is independent of growth order. This results in a manuscript also to be completed in the next six months. We have given more details of the above investigations in Part C (section11). Although we have not reached a version of Nevanlinna theory with respect to interpolation bases as originally intended in the technical sense, we have taken a path that is unavoidable in the sense that these are fundamental issues that one must tackle in order to proceed to answer more difficult fundamental questions in value distribution theory. We have underestimated the difficulty of these more “elementary problems” which are the “intermediate steps” toward our goal. They turned out to be much harder that is not at the technical level but at the conceptual level. It took us a period of time that is out of proportion from our original plan. But we are pleased to report that we have found a remedy when we thought the difficulties mentioned above were insurmountable even if it is beyond the project completion period. The remedy is rooted from a non-commutative algebra approach which is completely out of expectation. We have gained insights into these centuries old interpolation problems have unnoticed algebraic structures which must be combined with the function theoretic approach (our original expertise) in order to achieve the original goal of this project (details to be found in the Part C (section 11)). Thus we could claim a success in finding a right direction towards our original goals in the holistic sense. It is clear that we must also adjust the original goal with respect to our latest findings of the new algebraic structures. Two more papers are outcomes from these new discoveries in additional to two published papers and one submitted paper.

rows: To build a proper function theoretic foundation for the finite difference calculus with reference to interpolatory aspects of difference operators in general, and the Askey-Wilson operator and Wilson operator in particular. The first aim is to build relevant difference Nevanlinna theories with respect to the interpolatory aspects that are natural for the corresponding difference operators.

The second aim is to understand the implication of the study of values distibution of meromorphic functions in relation to the study of the interpolatory aspects of difference operators. In particular, one would like to understand the singularity structures at singular points revealed by the first objective. This leads natually to understanding analogous concepts of residue calculus and their interpretation at a more abstract level.

16306315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306315.value: We have discovered previously unnoticed operator and algebraic structures/interpretation of interpolation series expansion of entire/meromorphic functions. This results in two papers to be completed even beyond the project completion date. This also points to a way in building theories in modified forms from the original goals. Moreover, these findings also point to potential new development where the operator and algebraic structures aspects would become an indispensable part in dealing with finite difference calculus.

16306315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306315.value: Interpolation is amongst the oldest mathematical disciplines. Given a set of discrete data in relation to another set of discrete data. How do we interpolate the relationship in coordinates that “falls between the discrete values”? This project investigates some fundamental issues of such possible relations and rigidity of such relations from a complex analytic theory viewpoint. Complex analytic structures are abundant in the nature. For example, the most basic trigonometric functions (or ratios such as sine/cosine/tangent) that we all learnt at schools are known to have complex analytic structures since the eighteen century. Alost all important mathematical models derived from prominent physical models are known to possess complex analytic structures. This project carries this viewpoint more further in order to discover deeper new structures. A number of new results have been discovered.

16306415.label: Project Objectives
16306415.value: Develop techniques for fast and robust phase retrieval. We will focus on constructing special classes of linear measurements for this purpose. Answer the minimality problem in phase retrieval: what is the minimum number of linear measurements needed to allow for phase retrieval. We hope to develop new ideas to answer this fundamental question. Solve other type of phase retrieval problems include fusion frames and non-homogeneous linear measurements (which arises in holography).
