16306415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306415.value: The traditional framework for solving unknowns through linear measurements is ubiquitous in science and engineering, and it is no exaggeration to view solving Ax=b as the foundation of computational mathematics and engineering. Under this framework techniques have been well developed to handle measurement noise, redundancy of measurements (over-determined systems) and insufficiency of measurements (under-determined systems). In recent years a new class of problems has emerged where we no longer have the luxury of the linear measurements. Instead we can measure only the amplitude of the entries of Ax, namely |b| where the absolute value is taken entry-wise. In other words we have the amplitudes of the linear measurements but have no phase information, and need to solve |Ax|=|b|. Known as the phase retrieval problem, the goal is to recover the signal x by recovering the phase information. Phase retrieval has important applications in a number of fields. In fact the classic phase retrieval problem is to recover a function from the magnitude of its Fourier transform, which comes naturally from X-ray diffraction imaging. Of particular interest also is the case when the coefficients are obtained from a windowed Fourier transform (also known as a short-time Fourier transform), or an undecimated wavelet transform (in audio and image signal processing). A similar problem appears in quantum information (QI) theory. Other applications are found in wavefront reconstruction, terahertz imaging, holography, communication, and more. Phase retrieval is now a significant and fast growing area of applied and computational harmonic analysis. It has seen significant progress especially in the past few years, both theoretically and computationally. We shall discuss some of it in the main body of the proposal. But many challenges and unanswered questions remain. In this proposed research we shall focus on a selected set of concrete challenges in phase retrieval, particularly its more theoretical aspects. The questions to be addressed include the minimality of measurements needed for phase retrieval, measurements designs that allow for fast and robust phase retrieval, sparse signal phase retrieval, and non-homogeneous systems. We will discuss some preliminary results and ideas for further tackling the problems. 在科學和工程中可以毫不誇張地说解线性方程Ax = b是一个基础。在傳統的框架下，我们可以把Ax看成为線性測量，而通过線性測量解方程未知是無處不在的，這個理論與技術已經很發達，在信號處理方面已經有了很健全的發展。 近年來一類新的問題又出現了，在這裡我們不再有線性測量Ax = b的奢侈。相反，我們僅僅可以測量到Ax=b的幅度，即我們可以取得|Ax|=|b|，這裡|.|是絕對值。換句話說，我們具有線性測量的幅度，但沒有相位信息。這類問題被稱為相位恢復問題，其目標是通過恢復相位信息來恢復信號x。 相位恢復問題 有在若干領域的重要應用。事實上經典相位恢復問題的方法是從它的傅立葉變換的幅度變換，這是很自然的X射線衍射成像恢復的功能。特別感興趣的也就是當係數從一個加窗傅立葉變換獲得的情況下（也稱為短時傅里葉變換），或一個抽樣小波變換（在音頻和圖像信號處理）。類似的問題也出現在量子信息（QI）中。其它應用存在於波前重構，太赫茲成像，全息，通信，等等。 已經出現了對相位恢復顯著進展，特別是在過去的幾年裡，在理論和計算。我們應在提案的主體討論許多進步的。儘管如此，仍有許多挑戰，懸而未決的問題。在這項研究中建議，我們將專注於在相位恢復的具體挑戰選定的一組課題，其中包括理論和應用方面的問題。這些問題考慮相位恢復的充分必要條件，同時也考慮怎麼測量，設計才能允許快速和穩定的相位恢復，稀疏信號相位恢復，和非均質系統測量極少個數。我們還將討論這個問題上的一些初步成果和想法。

16306415.label: Realisation of objectives
16306415.value: I have essentially achieved all the objectives I had set for this project, and more. In terms of fast and robust phase retrieval, I have developed a novel technique that is based on a smoothed version of the Amplitude Flow method. Using this technique we can show that our method leads to linear convergence for complex phase retrieval. This is the first time that such a "provable" algorithm is developed for complex phase retrieval (previous results either requires O(n log(n)) measurements or only work for real phase retrieval). We have also developed a new algorithm that allows us to do fast and robust phase retrieval for measurements that are non-Gaussian. All previous results are only for Gaussian measurements. Additionally we have developed a method called "splitting variable". It works very well for general phase retrieval. The basic idea is to take a regular quadratic function and introduce a second variable to split x^2 into xy. This has the advantage of allowing the use of alternating projection technique. We have shown that it leads to fast convergence for Gaussian phase retrieval. For the minimality problem (Objective 2), we have made strong stride. In many aspects we have made the biggest progress on this program. Here we have developed a technique using algebraic geometry, by introducing a notion called "admissible projective variety". This is a very checkable condition and holds for most of the projective varieties arising in my study. We are able to answer questions on how many measurements are needed in order to reconstruct a signal (such as with phase retrieval). It turns out that phase retrieval can be viewed as just a special case of a far broader class of problems, which seeks to recover a signal on a manifold from a "small" number of linear measurements. Here "small" means the number is far smaller than the ambient dimension. Our technique essentially covers virtually all well-known cases (such as compressive sensing, low rank matrix recovery and phase retrieval). As a special application, we have settled the open question concerning the number of projections are needed for fusion frame phase retrieval in the complex case. In fact our study is set in the form of "generalized phase retrieval", which covers regular phase retrieval as well as fusion frame phase retrieval as special cases, and sharp results have been obtained under this general setting. For objective 3, we have already mentioned the theoretical side on the fusion frame phase retrieval. Algorithms that are provable to give linear convergence have also been developed. The non-homogeneous linear measurement recovery problem arises from holography. Here we have made a complete analysis as to the number of measurements needed, the Lipschitz property of recovery (related to the stability and robustness of recovery algorithms), as well as algorithms. One problem we can are still trying to improve is for structured measurements in phase retrieval. Currently all results are for random measurements, but structured measurements are extremely useful in real applications. Unfortunately there have been very few good results here, especially on the computational side. This is a difficult problem, still, we wish to tackle it heads on.

16306415.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306415.value: We have pioneered a technique using projective varieties in algebraic geometry to study the minimality question in phase retrieval, which asks how many measurements are needed to recover a signal in phase retrieval. This is done by introducing a notion called "admissible projective variety". This is a very checkable condition and holds for most of the projective varieties arising in my study. Using this new technique we have settled several questions on the minimal number of measurements needed to recover a signal, under settings broader than phase retrieval. For example, for low rank matrix recovery and nonhomogeneous measurements that arise from holography. We have also made significant gains on the algorithmic side. First we have developed a splitting variable approach. Here we introduce a second variable to split x^2 into xy, but adding penalty term |x-y|^2. We prove it is the same as the original model for phase retrieval. Alternating projection method can then be used for fast recovery in phase retrieval. One standard algorithm is the Amplitude Flow model for phase retrieval. This however can be proved to work only in the real cases. We have developed a novel technique that is based on a smoothed version of the Amplitude Flow method. Using this technique we can show that our method leads to linear convergence for complex phase retrieval using only O(n) measurements. This is the first time that such a "provable" algorithm is developed for complex phase retrieval. Interestingly all previous algorithms focus on Gaussian measurements. We have for the first time looked into phase retrieval using non-Gaussian random measurements. We develop a new algorithm that allows us to do fast and robust phase retrieval for measurements that are non-Gaussian.

16306415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306415.value: The theoretical analysis for robustness phase retrieval with non-Gaussian measurements is still not sharp. Right now we show that one can achieve robust recovery with linear convergence using O( n log^2(n)) measurements. But we hope to improve it to first order. We don't know whether this is true, however.

16306415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306415.value: Phase retrieval has many applications. For example, we cannot see directly of the structure of molecules or crystals. To do so we need to use X-ray, electron microscope, or other instruments. These instruments do not measure the structure directly, but indirectly. In general, one only measures the amplitude of Fourier transforms. The process to reconstruct the structure from such measurements is exactly phase retrieval. In other words, we try to retrieve lost phase information from amplitude measurements only. The question is: how can one do this? If there is a way to do it, how do we know it always works, and it does give us a wild answer if our data has some corruption. The project is focused on addressing these questions for phase retrieval, in a more general setting. Beside the applications, the project also studies the theoretical side of phase retrieval. For example, how many measurements are needed to do phase retrieval? We have made progress on many important questions in this area.

16306515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306515.value: High temperature crystallization offers a useful means of preparing a variety of crystalline materials that cannot be produced at ambient temperature. Traditionally this has required the use of expensive pressure vessels. Since optimal high temperature preparation of crystalline polymers such as Metal-organic Frameworks (MOFs) requires variation of many conditions, the application of a high throughput screening procedure is desirable. This is technically challenging using a steel-autoclave approach. The recent application of 3D printing technology to produce reaction chambers for solvothermal crystallization of MOFs using polypropylene for the vessel construction offers hope of a breakthrough for this approach. However a number of features need to be improved for the method to find wide usage which will be addressed in this proposal. First the advantages and limitations of various thermoplastics, such as polycarbonate (PC), polyetherimide (PEI) or Nylon-12 for the 3D printing will be investigated. The possibility of using composites (glass fiber, carbon etc) with greater high temperature rigidity will also be explored. Secondly the possible scope of the technique will be explored through its application to four test systems; 1. The addition of organic templates to several systems of MOF synthesis in order to investigate possible 'structure- directing' effects. 2. The application to the preparation of pharmaceutical co-crystals, for example in the case of oleanic acid and artemisinin based anti-malarial drugs. 3. The screening for high temperature polymorphs of organic crystals from a wide range of solvents, especially for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs). 4. The suppression of crystalline solvate or hydrate phases by high temperature crystallization. The applicability of the 3D printing technology to these fields of synthesis and crystallization screening will be more firmly established by this work, with applications ranging from preparation of porous solids to pharmaceutical formulation. In particular the engineering materials appropriate for specific applications of the technique will be identified, and compatibilities with solvent, pH and temperature determined. Given the popularity and importance of these fields it is expected that the work will receive prominent attention and be a timely contribution to their further development.

16306515.label: Realisation of objectives
16306515.value: Objective 1. 3D Printed Pressure Vessels There are many advantages and limitations regarding 3D printing. 3D models in different shapes with various capacities can be directly produced, the highly customized products can be used for different kinds of research, especially for high throughput screening. Low-cost 3D printer and filaments is more economic in comparison to traditional Teflon-lined stainless steel autoclave. By adjusting the printing conditions, defects can be minimized. The 3D printed reactors were investigated to be used for hydrothermal or even solvothermal synthesis of MOFs after the thermal and chemical resistance analysis was done. To employ 3D printing technology in my research, [Co(2-EtIm)2] was synthesized successfully from different 3D printed reactors made by ABS and PC (polycarbonate) and the product yields obtained were found to be 64.2% and 40.1% respectively. Two filament types of Nylon were attempted but some difficulties found with compatibility of vessel design. Objective 2. The first system we have explored in depth is [Cd(BzIm)2] which we have found can make a surprisingly wide range of product phases depending on solvent and /or involving addition of organic solute molecules. our first publication in this area on 2-D ‘honeycomb’ polymers with encapsulated aromatic solvent/ guest molecules. Selective sorption/desorption studies on these are being carried out for completion of this work.Three other papers will address the novel effect of organo-templating giving solvated MOF products with the same framework topology, but different 3D structures arising from conformational isomerism. The first one on [Cd(BzIm)2] Sodalite frameworks of varying symmetry, based on guest-templating effects of cyclic amines and ketones, the next is on solvated ABW frameworks of [Cd(BzIm)2] with different non-interconverting structures. In this case the solvates for example from dioxane and from dimethylformamide can be desolvated and the framework structures are still inequivalent due to conformational arrangement of bridging benzimidazole groups. Ms Wentao Zhou has shown a third ABW framework type (Zhou, AsCA18, Auckland Dec 2018) Finally a third paper on cag-topology structures derived from ketones, will show how an aldol condensation product molecule once again templates a modified cag framework different and non-convertible with that derived from cyclic ketones. Some of these results have been communicated (by IDW) at the Nano S&T conference Singapore, October 2016. However screening of crystallization conditions from a wide range of solvents in the related [Cd(2-EtIm)2] system gave the helpful finding that improved crystallization could be obtained for the unsolvated quartz-like MOF framework of this composition. These conditions could also be successfully applied to related Zn and Co compounds and single crystals of 0.5mm could be readily grown. This has allowed the successful single crystal study of the phase transition from low to high quartz for [Zn(2-EtIm)2] phase which occurs at around 300oC. The analogous transition for Cd is just above 400oC and remains elusive for crystals in air due to decomposition. This work was carried out in collaboration with Prof Michele Zema (U. Pavia) and other colleagues in Italy (U. Bari) and both preliminary findings and detailed studies have been presented in conferences in 2016 (Yim, Hobart Mar 2016, Zema Hanoi Dec 2016). Objective 3 Pharmaceutical Cocrystals 11-azaartemsinin is a far more potent and less neurotoxic antimalarial than its parent compound and crucially the change to a lactam amide (NH-C=O) from a lactone ester (O-C=O) helps co-crystal formation. Ms. Nisar has prepared a range of new co-crystals for 11-azaartemisinin, some of which were presented (Nisar, Hanoi, Dec 2016). In following through with GRAS (safe) carboxylic acids as coformers we found that roughly 50% of them could form cocrystals, with a highly conserved R8 heterosynthon ring between acid COOH and lactam CONH functionalities. Apart from solvothermal preparation we found that LAG was a successful high throughput method of screening and checking via P-XRD that new product phases had been formed. Two papers on this work have already appeared (Nisar et al CrystEngComm, 2018 and Nisar et al Acta Cryst C, 2018). A further publication with Prof Aviva Chow, HKU will be made on these findings. Screening cocrystallization with sugars and sugar alcohols has proved more difficult but Ms Nisar found two new cocrystal phase types with sorbitol and arabitol. (PhD thesis, 2019). One challenge we sought to overcome by cocrystal formation was the separation of regioisomers with similar solubilities. Wogonin and Oroxylin A are isomeric methoxy derivatives of Chrysin. Nicotinamide forms new cocrystals with only Wogonin (De Grano, PhD 2020) have different solubility from the parent phases allowing a facile separation for the first time. Objective 4 Organic Polymorph Screening Several pharmaceuticals were investigated in depth and new polymorphic forms were discovered. One system we have looked at is the Traditional Chinese Medicinal compound canadine, which was synthesized by us as a racemate. We wished to undertake a single crystal analysis, but the low solubility and low crystal quality of the compound prompted us to try solvothermal screening of crystallization. We have since obtained two polymorphic forms and studied their relative stability. Solvothermal crystallization from various solvents was attempted in a decoquinate system which had proven extremely challenging to crystallize due to the long alkyl side-chain. This was finally obtained from less than 5mg of sample in a high temperature polymorphic form which a single crystal was isolated and which allowed structure determination. The structure of the compound which is highly active against drug resistant tuberculosis strains is reported in Beteck et al, Communications Chemistry (Nature Publishing Group, 2018) Another approach to polymorph formation (Nisar, ACA meeting 2018) has been to use seed crystals of a molecular analogue to access a new packing arrangements. This was found by our group for arylsulfonyl-11-azaartemisinin compounds first by forming solid solutions from related compounds which have different packings. These 'quasi-polymorphs' can be used to structure direct a pharmaceutical into a new solid state structure. Objective 5 This Objective has now been extensively explored for crystals in the Oleanic Acid system by Ms. Yip and this work will be readied for publication and form one chapter of her Ph.D. thesis to be submitted in summer 2017. In this more than 10 different [OA-H] solvate systems have been studied, mostly alcohols and it is shown that in each case judicious use of crystallization conditions can either result in crystalline solvated or unsolvated phases. In a very few cases a mixture of phase types is found. The varying of temperature, concentration or solvent composition effects the product phases found and can be explained by a model in which the temperature of the initial crystallization is the key variable. This is then sensible to understand Apart from OA-H we have also examined the hydrated forms of anti-cancer drug Wogonin, which we have prepared as a monoclinic sesquihydrate (1.5H2O) phase from DCM. It appears this crystalline form was seen before, but incorrectly reported as a methanolate, whilst alternative mono-hydrated orthorhombic phase was also previously published. The unit cells and structures are related, but clearly distinct in their packing, one being a chiral arrangement and the other centric. Wogonin is an achiral planar molecule, but in the solid one phenol OH can form H-bonds directed up or down from the molecular plane causing a local chirality. In all crystals molecular stacks are formed with homochiral arrangements, but in our sesquihydrate neighboring stacks are of opposite chirality.

16306515.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306515.value: Objective 1 Based on these approaches a study was made by high throughput screening of mixed Cd(2-MeIm)/(2-EtIm) polymers. This has led to novel type of Ice framework MOFs as well as double Quartz topology MOF solids. Solvothermal temperatures to 140oC are realisable. Objective 2 We have demonstrated that topologically identical MOF framework compounds can be prepared from different solvents (or guests) in several structurally distinct forms due to hindered rotation of ligand bridges. This can lead to tailoring of porous solids by specific guests, which could have highly selective sorption properties. Templating of chiral MOF frameworks by chiral organic templates has not been successful to-date, but chiral organic network solids have been prepared by self aggregation of chiral anions through varying solvent T and time. We have similarly looked at the use of solvothermal screening methods applied to chiral resolutions using diastereomeric salt formation and found an improved resolution of trifluorolactic acid. Objective 3 In addition to traditional coformers we also attempted to use other anti-malarial drugs, and the detailed structure of one of these with mefloquine hydrochloride has been carried out. (Nisar, New Orleans, 2017). We have carried out further studies on the properties of these cocrystals and importantly found both superior thermal stability as well as aqueous dissolution are possible, emphasising the potential advantages of drug cocrystal formation. We have successfully used seeds of a tolyl derivative (monoclinic P21) to redirect crystallization of the phenyl parent compound (orthorhombic P212121) to its structure. Importantly the tolyl seed compound redissolves leaving phase-pure phenyl compound in the modified polymorphic form. Price (UCL, London) has recently reported that carbamazepine system can show similar behaviour. We believe an important new strategy to make new polymorphic forms will emerge from this work via forming a range of crystalline molecular analogues and using them as structural templates. Success in this approach may have profound implications for the pharmaceutical industry. Objective 5 In the OA system we have found ways of controlling crystallite size and morphology through solvate formation, which may be beneficial for inhalant aerosol formulation of the drug. (De Grano, PhD thesis 2020). The wogonin anti-cancer agent forms a variety of hydrates and solvates and control of these can be effected by high temperature crystallization. The ethylacetate (EA) solvate of Wogonin can be desolvated to an anhydrous form with empty pockets, but these are hydrophobic in nature and so the anhydrous solid formed is porous but not hygroscopic.

16306515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306515.value: Objective 1/2 Formation of the new MOF materials with modified composition and channel properties is highly desirable. We are currently looking to engineer the hydrophilic/ hydrophobic nature of MOF channels for dehumidifier applications which may have significant commercial value. Objective 3/4 The new 11-aza sulphonyl derivatives are being thoroughly explored as a strategy for new routes to stable polymorphs that are otherwise not readily accessible by traditional screening methods. A number of other more basic systems such as salicylic acids and acetaminophens are also being evaluated in a similar manner by our group. Objective 5 In the Wogonin system so we have shown an important example of the crystal engineering of drug compositional stability with respect to humidity. By contrast the channel hydrate forms of Wogonin that can be isolated from alcohols and other solvents such as DCM are likely be more subject to variable dehydration/ rehydration issues and these parameters will be studied in depth using controlled humidity chamber experiments.

16306515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306515.value: Our project has explored various aspects of high temperature crystallizations. The first aspect which had some success was the use of new 3D printing technology to make cheap disposable vessels for the high temperature crystallizations. This approach does work but has some limitations at high temperature and using organic solvents. Polycarbonate (PC) was shown to be a possible engineering plastic for this application for the first time. By these and other screening methodologies we have looked at varying many crystallization parameters such as solvent, temperature, time and reagents to facilitate new crystalline forms of network solids that can help in new selective separations, including handed (or chiral) compounds. Higher temperature crystallizations have also been successfully applied to making new solid forms of drugs that incorporate other molecules in their crystals that may improve properties such as drug solubility and thermal stability in the solid state, which can help shelf-life Finally we have found new approach to make new crystalline forms of drugs which are called polymorphs. These have different physiochemical properties and so may have considerable intellectual property value. The new approach uses crystal seeds of molecules that are similar in size and shape to a drug, but have a different crystal packing.

16500315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500315.value: In this project, we examine how the nature of a choice set from which a consumer selects a brand can influence whether the consumer persists with the chosen brand on future choice occasions. The psychological literature and marketing literature have examined the nature of consumer preferences. During last three decades, behavioral decision theory researchers have established that preferences are often constructed. That is, instead of using prior preferences, often people construct their preferences based on the available inputs. This type of construction is very common in marketing. For example, while I may use my prior preferences and decide on a brand in frequently purchased product categories, if I am not sure about what constitutes a good product, I'll examine information provided on the package and construct preferences accordingly. An important question is whether preferences constructed in this manner persist over time and what factors account for such persistence. However, these issues have received very little attention in marketing. We examine the stability of preferences with no intervention from competitors, preference persistence under a competitor's challenges of different kinds, and the consistency between attitudes toward brands and choices. In all these investigations, the effect of the choice sets will be our focus. It's an important theme in marketing and we intend to study this issue with rigor. In seven experiments, we intend to examine the issues outlined above. In addition to examining the outcomes, our research will also examine the processes involved. It is hoped that the findings will strengthen psychological theories of persistence of preference specifically in a marketing context. In addition, it is hoped that the findings will be useful for marketers who want to create persistent preferences for their brands and lessen preference persistence for the competing brands. 在這個研究項目裏，我們研究消費者於選擇一個品牌時所面對的選擇組合的性質，會如何影響該消費者於將來持續作出相同的選擇。心理學文獻和市場學文獻研究了消費者喜好的性質。在過去的三十年中，行為決策理論的研究人員已經確定，喜好通常是構建的。也就是說，人們並非依從既有的喜好，而通常是基於現有的選擇去構建自己的喜好。這種構建在市場學中是很常見的。例如：於一些經常購買的產品類別中，我可以用以前的喜好去選擇一個品牌；但對於一些我不肯定怎樣才算是一件好產品的類別，我會審視包裝上的資料，從而構建我的喜好。一個重要的問題是：在這種情況下構建的喜好會否持續一段時間，以及哪些因素會影響這持續性。然而，在市場學中，這些問題獲得的關注很少。我們將會研究在沒有競爭者介入的情況下，消費者喜好的穩定性；在有競爭者的各種挑戰下，消費者喜好的持續性；以及消費者對不同品牌和不同選擇的看法的一致性。在所有這些研究中，我們關注的焦點是選擇組合的影響。這是市場學中一個重要課題，我們打算嚴謹地研究這個課題。我們打算在七個實驗中，研究上述問題。除了審視結果，我們的研究也將會審視當中所涉及的過程。我們希望，這些發現能加強特別是在市場營銷的情境當中，有關喜好持續性的心理學理論。此外，我們也希望這些研究結果能幫助市場營銷人員，為自己的品牌建立持久的喜好，並減低消費者對競爭品牌的喜好的持久性。

16500315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16500315.value: In this research, we examined the effects of choice sets of different types on the strength of preferences. The choice set types included efficient frontier sets, compromise sets, asymmetrically dominated options set, and symmetrically dominated options sets. The dimensions of preference included confidence in choice, choice satisfaction, stability in choice and resistance to competitors' challenges. We found that several factors interact with choice sets to produce higher or lower strength in terms of each of these dimensions that induce or indicate preference persistence. In eight experiments we collected ample data to test each of the propositions. This research will make substantial contribution to research on persistent preferences. In addition the findings will be quite useful for marketers as these findings have implications for building consumer brand loyalty.

16500315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16500315.value: As discussed in the manuscript, there are several issues worth investigating further. The two key directions for future research are the role of type of challenges in determining the effects of choice sets on preference persistence and the moderating role of separate versus joint evaluation in the effect of choice sets on attitude-behavior consistency.

16500315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16500315.value: In this research, we investigated the role of initial choices on subsequent choices, specifically whether a consumer stays with a previously chosen brand or switch to another brand. The factor of options in the choice set during the initial choice can be easily manipulated by marketers. Based on our research findings, we specify the conditions under which certain types of choice sets yield greater or lesser strength in preferences.

16500615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500615.value: 無線電頻譜是指適合用作無線通信的電磁波段。一直以來，包括美國聯邦通信委員會（FCC）和歐洲電信標準協會（ETSI）在內的頻譜管理機構都是將頻譜段以獨占的方式劃分給某一服務提供者使用。我們把以此方式獲得使用權的用戶稱作是主要用戶或許可用戶。這種靜態的頻譜分配方式雖然能減輕重要通信服務受到的干擾，但也導致已分配頻譜的利用率偏低。即使在繁忙時間段，某些區域的頻譜利用率仍低於百分之二十。另一方面，由無線電和互聯網技術融合發展所引起的無線語音與數據通信需求導致了無線數據傳輸量的激增。現有的在用無線數據頻譜正接近其容量極限。 要緩解這種因靜態分配而造成的人為頻譜短缺問題，一個自然而然的方法是允許次要用戶或非許可用戶去使用臨時空閒的頻譜，以提高已分配頻譜的利用率。此類頻譜使用方式被稱作機會頻譜接入。然而，允許非許可用戶接入也可能對現有的許可用戶產生干擾。因此，此類系統的運作需要：（1）掌握各頻譜段的實時狀態，如：信道的空閒與否、排隊等候的用戶數量等；及（2）一個有效的控制機制去管理非許可用戶的頻譜使用行為。這些要求導致了認知無線電的發展。認知無線電是一種可以智能感測頻譜環境並依照指定控制方式反應的基於軟件的無線電系統。 配備認知無線電的共享網絡的實施顯然涉及到技術上和運營上的課題。眾多電子工程領域中的研究者已經在此方向上進行研究並專注在前者上。在本計劃中，我們將研究運營上的課題，並揭示定量及定性的管理見解以回答如何有效共享頻譜及如何根據不同頻譜用戶定價的問題。儘管此類網絡可用多類型多服務器排隊模型模擬，它們和傳統服務及製造業系統中產生的模型有着顯著的區別。我們期望能揭露出此類網絡複雜的系統動態，並從中獲得與現有成熟服務系統不同的管理見解。據我們所知，本研究是運籌學/運營管理學領域中第一個關於無線通信共享網絡的綜合研究。我們所提出的研究工作不僅會為現有運籌學/運營管理學知識的應用打開一扇新大門，更會促進本領域新研究方法的發展。

16500615.label: Realisation of objectives
16500615.value: We have successfully fulfilled all five objectives and beyond. We were surprised to learn that, despite of the vast research on wireless communications, little is known about the operational issues and there is little study in the literature. We held numerous meetings with scholars in electrical engineering and computer science, and practitioners at the forefront, and read academic books to gain basic knowledge in wireless communications. After gaining some understanding of the advantages and disadvantages of various spectrum sharing protocols to different users, we identified key performance indicators relevant to industry practice, i.e., sensing frequency of unlicensed users, the length of the service session allowed to unlicensed users, the probability that licensed users will be interrupted, the probability an unlicensed user has to release a channel, etc. We then build a complex many server queueing model to describe the dynamics of communication systems. We conduct performance analysis and optimize the performances by dynamically controlling protocol parameters. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first com- prehensive study of a shared network in wireless com- munications. Although there have been some attempts by researchers in electrical engineering using relatively simple queueing models, our model captures many more of the features of such a system. We are able to uncover complicated system dynamics and obtain managerial insights different from those drawn from the many well-studied service systems. Our work not only opens the door for new applications of existing queueing theory in wireless communications but also may stimulate the development of new methodologies.

16500615.label: Major findings and research outcome
16500615.value: We show that the sensing frequency of the unli- censed users waiting in the queue does not affect sys- tem performance from the operational perspective, and its decision should be based on technological concerns. When the system is underloaded or critically loaded, there is no need to restrict the service session of unli- censed users. Otherwise, limiting the transmission of the unlicensed users is necessary only when the system load is above a threshold. Thus, it is possible to improve spectrum utilization while guaranteeing a very high service level, as expected by licensed users in practice, and spectrum sharing can potentially be a socially opti- mal solution to alleviating spectrum scarcity. Spectrum sharing, if feasible, is especially beneficial for systems with a smaller portion or a large num- ber of licensed users with shorter service times. Our study sheds light on the implementation of spectrum sharing and opens the door for new applications of existing queueing theory in wireless communication networks, which may lead to the development of new methodologies. Our study also provides some rich research oppor- tunities. For instance, the arrival rates of the users may be uncertain in practice. Our preliminary result shows that higher variance will always hurt system perfor- mance if the system is expected to be underloaded or critically loaded. However, if the system is expected to be overloaded, it seems that increasing the variability up to a certain level will actually improve the throughput rate.

16500615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16500615.value: In reality, users’ behavior in data transmission can be more complicated than what we described in the paper. For instance, unlicensed users who have to abandon the system earlier may reenter the system later while licensed users may abandon the system if no idle channel is available upon arrival. Also, sensing may not be perfect (e.g., a false alarm can occur), in which case a spectrum opportunity is overlooked by an unli- censed user. It will be interesting to incorporate these elements into the model and examine how they change the system performance and operational decisions. The insights revealed in this research may also pave the way for studying other important business issues in wireless communications, such as contract design and pricing in shared networks. For instance, how should a spectrum owner set the prices and decide the ser- vice quality to both licensed and unlicensed users in a shared network? Should unlicensed users be charged a fixed and/or usage-based fee? Since unlicensed users may belong to different service providers, should a spectrum owner run an auction to select the service providers and settle the prices?

16500615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16500615.value: Opportunistic access of licensed spectrum by unlicensed users is widely considered a way to alleviate artificial scarcity of radio spectrum by increasing the spectrum utilization. However, it may reduce the service quality for licensed users because of poten- tial interference from unlicensed users. While much research on spectrum sharing has been conducted by researchers in electrical engineering, with the main focus on technological issues, the operational aspects have not been adequately addressed through analytical work. In this project, we model a shared network consisting of both licensed users and unlicensed users as a multiclass, many-server queueing system. The distinctive features of our model are that the service requirement of an unlicensed user can be fulfilled even after multiple interruptions and the unlicensed users wait- ing in the queue are required to sense channel avail- ability periodically while waiting. These features complicate system dynamics and lead to quite different insights from those derived from most service systems. Our analysis reveals a number of distinctive properties of the system. For example, sharing does not affect the level of service provided to the licensed users in an asymptotic sense even when the system is critically loaded.

16500715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16500715.value: Cybercrime poses a significant threat to the world economy. The Council of Europe's international law, called the Convention on Cybercrime (COC), criminalizes malicious activities on the Internet. However, the effectiveness of the COC has not been tested empirically. If it does not facilitate marginal deterrence, i.e., punishing criminals according to the extent of offense committed, then it could motivate more serious offenses. This project proposes to empirically study the deterrence effect of the COC. We plan to study distributed denial of service (DDOS) attacks, which are unambiguously criminalized under the COC. We shall collect worldwide, longitudinal DDOS attack data at the Internet protocol (IP) address level. Based on the victim computers' IP addresses, we identify the countries in which the DDOS attacks occurred, and then match the attacks to the respective countries' legal frameworks, specifically whether they had adopted the COC. We then identify the impact of the COC on DDOS attacks using a difference (COC versus non-COC countries)-in-differences (before/after COC enforcement) design. We plan to study two measures of DDOS attacks: the number of unique victim IP addresses ("victim IP") and the number of packets used to attack each victim IP address ("packets/IP"). Studying the victim IP allows us to assess whether COC enforcement reduced the crime rate, whereas studying packets/IP helps assess whether the intensity of the crime changed. The COC is effective in deterring DDOS attacks if it decreases both victim IP and packets/IP more than when and where it is not enforced. If it decreases victim IP but not packets/IP it may have failed to deter major offenders. If it decreases victim IP but increases packets/IP it may have failed to achieve marginal deterrence, meaning the determined offenders may have escalated their offenses. This is a pioneering attempt to provide empirical evidence on cybercrime deterrence, and the importance of marginal deterrence, in a field setting. The study of cybercrime has been impeded by a lack of quality data and empirical insights. The results from this project will inform policymakers about optimal approaches to tackling cybercrime, particularly whether deterrence through legislation is advisable and whether it produces any unintended consequences, such as escalated offenses. Based on insights from this project, the government could design the optimal mix of preventive and deterrence measures against cybercrime, which are on the rise. 網絡犯罪已發展成對世界經濟的一個重大威脅。歐洲理事會的一部名為《網絡犯罪公約》（以下簡稱《公約》）的國際法已將互聯網上的惡意行為定義為違法活動。然而，《公約》的效用目前還未得到實證驗證。如果這部法律不能促進邊際威懾，即無法根據罪行的嚴重程度來懲罰，那麼它有可能會刺激更加嚴重的攻擊。 本項目意圖從實證角度去探究《公約》的威懾效用。我們計劃研究一個被《公約》毫無爭議地定性為犯罪行為的活動 -- 分佈式阻斷服務攻擊。我們將縱向地收集全球在互聯網協議地址層面上的分佈式阻斷服務攻擊的數據。根據受攻擊電腦的網絡地址，我們首先識別出攻擊發生在哪個國家，然後將這些攻擊對應到相關國家的法律構架，即這個國家是否已經實施了《公約》。據此我們採用雙重差分模型（實施國與未實施國間的差別以及實施國實施前後的差別），從而鑑別出《公約》對分佈式阻斷服務攻擊的影響。 我們計劃研究分佈式阻斷服務攻擊的兩個測量指標：非重複的受攻擊的網絡地址數量以及用來攻擊每個受害網路地址的數據封包數量。研究前者有助於評測《公约》是否減少了犯罪率，而研究後者有助於評測攻擊的強度是否有所改變。相較於實施前以及未實施國，如果《公約》的執行在實施國同時減少了受害網絡地址數量和攻擊每個地址所用封包數量，那麼《公約》是能夠有效地威懾住分佈式阻斷服務攻擊；如果《公約》僅減少了前者，那麼它很有可能沒能夠威懾住主要的攻擊者；如果《公約》減少了前者但提高了後者，那麼它很可能未能實現邊際威懾，意味著頑固的攻擊者加強了他們的攻擊強度。 本研究可被視為一個從實際中為威懾網絡犯罪以及邊際威懾重要性提供實證證據的創舉。關於網絡犯罪的研究長期受限於缺少有質量的數據以及有實證證據支撐的洞見。本項目得到的結果能夠幫助政府更加優化地應對網絡犯罪，特別是通過法規進行威懾是否可取以及法規是否會產生意料之外的影響，例如犯罪強度的增加。本研究得到的觀察也能幫助政府更佳地綜合利用預防和威懾手段來應對日益加劇的網絡犯罪。

16500715.label: Realisation of objectives
16500715.value: All stated objectives are achieved. We compiled a comprehensive set of distributed denial of service (DDOS) attack data for each country/region from 2004 to 2014. We analyzed the DDOS attack trends across countries/regions and over time, and related such trends with national characteristics such as Internet infrastructure, socio-economic factors, demographics, and governance quality. We found that the national characteristics are variously correlated with the observed DDOS attacks, indicating attackers do not choose targets randomly. Instead, they rationally launched attacks based on the target profiles as exhibited in the national characteristics. This completes Objective 1. For Objective 2, we developed a difference-in-differences (DID) model that exploits the staggering enforcement of the Convention on Cybercrime (COC) across countries, taking into account the level of domestic enforcement against cybercrimes and the national characteristics analyzed in Objective 1. Our empirical framework accounts for unobserved but persistent national characteristics such as culture, and time-invariant characteristics such as the evolution of DDOS attack techniques and tools. More importantly, we developed multiple identification and falsification strategies utilizing additional information such as the enforcement of other international conventions in the studied countries and their signing (instead of enforcement) of the COC. These strategies allow us to unambiguously pin down the effect of COC enforcement on DDOS attacks. This completes Objective 2. We then took the empirical framework to the DDOS attack data and studied the general deterrence effect of COC enforcement. In particular, we used the number of DDOS attack victims as the dependent variable in this analysis as it gives us a good indication about the frequency of attacks to each country/region. We found that both domestic law enforcement and COC enforcement decreased the number of DDOS attack victims in the studied countries/regions. Importantly, our empirical framework allows us to isolate the nuanced effect of the enforcement. We found that the deterrence effect of COC is largely caused by its provision of mutual assistance across countries. This suggests that international cooperation can help deter cybercrimes, a novel result that has not been advocated in previous research. Based on this insight, we took one extra step by compiling additional data on the autonomous systems (AS) connections between the studied countries/regions. Using AS connection as a precise and specific measure for network connectivity, we found strong network and displacement effects in COC enforcement. Neighboring countries' enforcement of the COC increases the DDOS attacks recorded in the focal country when the focal country has not enforced the COC. However, it decreases DDOS attacks when the focal country has enforced the COC. This implies COC enforcement is complementary among the enforcing countries and drives attacks towards non-enforcing countries/regions. This is a pioneering empirical evidence on the effectiveness of international law enforcement. It fully completes what we intended to achieve in Objective 3. Our next analysis utilized the same empirical model but inspected the attack intensity, by studying the maximum number of packets per minute and packets per day used in the recorded DDOS attacks. Contrary to what we have found using the number of victims as the dependent variable, here we found that the attack intensity actually increased among the enforcing countries. Because we measured attack intensity on a per-IP basis and our model controlled for IP-level and time fixed effects and rich country-time heterogeneities, we have high confidence that the average attack intensity has increased. Essentially, the enforcement has changed the mix of the DDOS attacks. Although it decreased the attack rate measured by number of victims, it did not deter the committed attackers. To our knowledge, this is the first large-scale empirical study to contrast the difference between attack rate and intensity in an international setting with more than 10 years of data. It completes Objective 4 of the project. Finally, based on the empirical findings and insights obtained from the analysis of the DDOS attack data, we drew managerial insights on the impact of deterrence measures and how it can be used to complement preventive measures in addressing the growing cybercrimes. This completes the last objective of the project. Overall, we have completed all objectives as specified in the project. With millions of DDOS attacks recorded in more than one hundred countries/regions and over a period of 11 years, this project provides perhaps the first empirical evidence on the deterrence effect of law enforcement in such a large scale. It generates valuable knowledge for and support to the use of law enforcement and especially international cooperation against globalized cybercrimes.

16500715.label: Major findings and research outcome
16500715.value: We have two major sets of findings. The first set is about the general deterrence effect measured by attack rate in terms of number of DDOS attack victims. The key finding is that COC enforcement has an incremental deterrence effect on top of domestic enforcement against cybercrimes. This deterrence effect is largely driven by the COC's provision of international cooperation, viz. the participating countries are supposed to preserve stored computer data to assist in crime investigation and extradite suspected criminals to each other. In addition, we find that the enforcement benefits from network effect, but it displaces DDOS attacks to non-enforcing regions. These findings provide useful insights to cybersecurity strategies. We report these findings and implications in the first paper listed in Part C, which was published in MIS Quarterly. The second set of findings zooms into the attack patterns recorded in each specific IP address. We find that among the attacked IP addresses, the intensity as measured by maximum packets per minute and number of packets per day actually increased after COC enforcement. This implies that there is a limit on how much law enforcement can deter crimes. This finding suggests that we must combine deterrence and preventive measures in tackling cyber criminals, which could comprise amateur and committed offenders, the latter may not be deterred by heightened law enforcement. We report these findings in a working paper, which will be submitted for journal publication in due course Based on these findings, the investigators have tried to provide informed advice and guidance on the efficacy of regulatory measures in tackling crimes in the mass media. Specifically, we have contributed various opinion pieces on the ongoing discussion about the role of law enforcement in crime deterrence based on the findings from this research. These opinion pieces are listed in the Other Impact Section in Part C.

16500715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16500715.value: One potential development of this research is to examine whether the deterrence effect of law enforcement differs across target organization types. For example, if the DDOS attacks are financially motivated, then the deterrence effect should be more visible in commercial organizations but not non-profit organizations. By contrast, if the attacks are motivated by defiance or stigmatization, then we expect more pronounced attacks against government organizations. To explore the underlying attack motivation and whether law enforcement produces differentiated deterrence, we plan to categorize the DDOS attack victims into different types (government, mass media, e-commerce firms, etc.). This requires tedious efforts as we need to trace the IP address of each victim and locate their website. Nevertheless, it will be a meaningful exercise as differentiated deterrence, if established, can provide further guidance to firms’ strategic planning and preparation against potential cyber attacks. The investigators plan to embark on this data compilation and expand the IP-level analysis as outlined in Section 6.1 above.

16500715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16500715.value: This research shows that law enforcement can help deter cybercrimes especially when it facilitates cooperation between the enforcing countries/regions. There is network effect in law enforcement in that the deterrence effect is stronger when more countries work together. On the other hand, the enforcement drives attacks to non-enforcing countries/regions, meaning we should encourage more countries to join the same international convention. There is a caveat in this deterrence effect, however, as the law cannot deter motivated attackers. Hence, law enforcement is not the panacea to cybercrimes. The findings of this research are significant because cybercrimes are on the rise globally and governments in many countries are planning to step up their measures against cybercrimes. However, little is known about the efficacy of cybercrime laws. Our empirical analysis provides robust evidence to support setting up cybercrime laws. More importantly, we advocate international cooperation and warn governments and firms about potential crime displacements if the cybercrime law is not extended to their jurisdictions. We also inform governments and firms about the limitation of cybercrime laws, viz. the law may not be effective against determined criminals. We must combine a mix of prevention and deterrence measures in tackling cybercrimes.

16500915.label: Realisation of objectives
16500915.value: We first developed a systematic procedure of statistical inference for the heavy-tailed TAR model. It is shown that the self-weighted least absolute deviation estimator of slope parameters are root-n consistent and asymptotically normal. In particular, we showed that the estimated thresholds are n-consistent, each of which converges weakly to the smallest minimizer of a compound Poisson process. Based on this theory, the Wald test statistic is considered for testing the linear restriction of slope parameters and a procedure is given for inference of threshold parameters. We finally constructed a sign-based portmanteau test for model checking. Simulations were carried out to assess the performance of our procedure and to make a comparison with LSE. We then studied the theory and methodology for statistical inferences of threshold and change-point in the threshold autoregressive models with i.i.d errors. It is shown that the LSE of the threshold and change-point are n-consistent, and converge weakly to the minimizer of a compound Poisson process and the location of minima of a two-sided random walk, respectively. When the magnitude of change in the parameters of the state regimes or the time horizon is small, it is further shown that these limiting distributions can be approximated by a class of known distributions. The LSE of slope parameters are root-n consistent and asymptotically normal. Furthermore, a likelihood-ratio based confidence set is given for the threshold and change-point, respectively. Simulation study is carried out to assess the performance of our procedure. The proposed theory and methodology are further illustrated by a tree-ring data set. We further investigated the quasi-maximum likelihood estimator (QMLE) of the structure-changed and two-regime threshold double autoregressive model. It is shown that both the estimated threshold and change-point are n-consistent, and they converge weakly to the smallest minimizer of a compound Poisson process and the location of minima of a two-sided random walk, respectively. Other estimated parameters are root-n consistent and asymptotically normal. The performance of the QMLE are assessed via simulation studies and a real example was given to illustrate our procedure. To explore the possibility of extending our new theory and methodology to GARCH models, we proposed a first-order zero-drift GARCH model to study conditional heteroscedasticity and heteroscedasticity together. Unlike the classical GARCH model, the model is always non-stationary regardless of the sign of the Lyapunov exponent, but interestingly it is stable with its sample path oscillating randomly between zero and infinity over time when the exponent is zero. Furthermore, we studied the generalized QMLE of the model, and established its strong consistency and asymptotic normality. Based on the general QMLE, a t-test for stability, a unit root test for the absence of the drift term, and a portmanteau test for model checking are constructed. Simulation studies are carried out to assess the finite sample performance of the proposed estimators and tests. Applications demonstrate that a stable model is more appropriate than a non-stationary GARCH model in fitting the KV-A stock returns. To distinguish TAR model and the smooth STAR model, we proposed a test statistic. Under a STAR model, it is shown to follow asymptotically a chi-squared distribution, and under a TAR model, it can be expressed as a functional of a chi-squared process. We presented numerical results with both simulated and real data to assess the performance of our procedure. To explore the possibility of extending our new theory and methodology to heavy tailed time series, we studied the heavy-tailed vector error correction models and established the asymptotic theory of the full rank least squares estimator (FLSE). It is shown that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the long-run parameters is n (sample size) and its limiting distribution is a stochastic integral in terms of two stable random processes when the tail index is in (0,2). Furthermore, we showed that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the short-term parameters is not root-n and its limiting distribution is a functional of two stable processes when the tail index is in (1, 2). However, when the tailed index is in (0, 1), we showed that the rate of convergence of the FLSE related to the short-term parameters is n and its limiting distribution not only depends on the stationary component itself but also depends on the unit root component. Based on the FLSE, the limiting distribution of the reduced rank LSE (RLSE) is derived. We finally explore the possibility of using Lasso method the change-point problem. The Lasso-based approach for variable selection of ARMA models was studied. We showed that the Lasso estimator has the Knight-Fu's limit distribution under a general tuning parameter assumption. With a special restriction on tuning parameters, we showed that the Lasso estimator can achieve the oracle" properties { zero parameters are estimated to be zero exactly and other estimators are as efficient as those under the true model.

16500915.value: Yang and Ling (2017) investigated the self-weighted least absolute deviation estimation for the model and used the Wald test statistic for testing the linear restriction of slope parameters . We constructed a sign-based portmanteau test for model checking. Simulations were carried out to assess the performance of our procedure and the NASDAQ daily volume was studied. Li, Zhang, Zhu and Ling (2018) proposed a first-order zero-drift GARCH model. Unlike the classical GARCH model, this model is always non-stationary regardless of the sign of the Lyapunov exponent. We studied the generalized QMLE of this model, and established its strong consistency and asymptotic normality. Based on the GQMLE, a t-test for stability, a unit root test for the absence of the drift term, and a portmanteau test for model checking were constructed. Simulation studies were carried out to assess the finite sample performance of the proposed estimators and tests. Applications demonstrate that a stable model is more appropriate to capture heteroscedasticity than a non-stationary GARCH model for the stock returns. Gao, Ling and Tong (2018) proposed a test statistic for TAR model against STAR model. Under a STAR model, the test is shown to follow asymptotically a chi-squared distribution, and under a TAR model, it can be expressed as a functional of a chi-squared process. We re-examined the monthly seasonally unadjusted unemployment rate for U.S. based our procedure. Gao and Ling (2018) investigated the LSE of the structurally changed TAR models. It is shown that both estimated threshold and change-point are n-consistent, and they converge weakly to the smallest minimizer of a compound Poisson process and the location of minima of a two-sided random walk, respectively. The result is further applied to study the growth of tree rings in China, from which we get the evidence of climate change during the year 1642-1669. Chan, Ling and Yau (2018) proposed the Lasso-based approach for variable selection of ARMA models. Guo and Ling (2018) investigated the QMLE of the structure-changed and two-regime threshold DAR model. It is shown that both the estimated threshold and change-point are n-consistent, and converge weakly to the smallest minimizer of a compound Poisson process and the location of minima of a two-sided random walk, respectively. She and Ling (2018) established asymptotic theory of heavy tailed vector error correction models. Li, Ling, Tong and Yang (2018) gave a Brownian motion approximation of compound Poisson processes with applications to threshold models.

16500915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16500915.value: It is well known that the structures of financial and economic variables may change from one period to another because of a new policy or a new event such as the oil crisis, financial crisis or fiscal quantitative easing, among many others. To locate the time of change, the change-point in various models has been studied for a long history. Because of difficulty in non-linearity, the research on change-points in nonlinear time series models has had just a little progress. This project established an asymptotic theory for change-points and thresholds in a class of structurally changed DTAR models. We showed the consistency of the quasi-MLE and its rate of convergence. Furthermore, we derived the limiting distributions of the estimated change-point and the estimated threshold. They do not have a closed form for the purpose of statistical inference. We obtained an approximating distribution to approximate percentiles under a general setting. Our results will help researchers and practitioners to understand the structural change of economic and financial data in a new way. The research outputs from this project should be important both theoretically and empirically, and have been published in leading international econometric and statistical journals.

16501015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16501015.value: 医院的救护中心，信用卡中心的服务热线，提供服务的实体店（比如苹果店）等等都可以被看成是大型服务系统。在这些系统中，大量的需求被“服务器” （比如，医生，电话热线专员，实体店专员等）服务。管理这些系统的一大难点来源于顾客的分类，否则就可以直接使用先进先出的服务规则。促使顾客分类的原因有很多，比如，病人病况的紧急程度不同，顾客有vip 顾客和普通顾客的区别，实体店的顾客中有的有预定，而有的没有。一方面，我们希望给某些顾客，像紧急情况的病人或者vip 顾客，优先享受服务的权利，使得他们有更短的等待时间。另一方面，我们也不想完全忽视那些优先级比较低的顾客。管理这种系统的目标就是通过优化服务策略使得关于等待时间的效用函数最大化。 不同的顾客类别不仅仅意味着他们服务的优先级不一样，他们所需要的服务时间或者要求的服务技能也可能不同。这些会使得整个系统的运作变得非常复杂，也使得对不同的服务策略进行分析变得很难。除此之外，这些服务系统还包含了很多随机因素。比如，有些有预定的顾客会迟到，有些手术会比预期的时间长或者短，顾客的光顾在周末或者有新品发布的时候也会很不一样。这些因素使得管理与优化这些系统变得非常有挑战性。 我们用排队网络模型对这些系统进行建模，并通过分析这些模型来发现不同的因素（顾客的到达模式，服务时间的概率模型等）会如何影响系统。我们会利用系统比较大型的这个特点来分析系统复杂的动态表现下所隐含的规律。管理系统的方案多种多样，不可能一一列举出来进行分析。通过我们所建立的模型与方法，我们可以设计出一种最优的方法使得系统达到最好的表现。

16501015.label: Realisation of objectives
16501015.value: The objectives have been achieved with success. In paper #4 (see Section 8 of the report), we developed an analytical framework for analyzing fluid models of many-server system with time varying arrival. Paper #3 provide a theoretical framework for optimal control with Brownian input. In this way, Objectives 1 and 2 are achieved. Paper #1 provided a nice policy for solving the routing and staffing of a multi-class service networks with different customer classes. The optimality of the policy is proved. Papers #5 and #7 developed nice policies for handling multi-class customers in a many-server queueing setting by theoretically analyzing the asymptotic behavior of fluid models for many-server queues. The analytical framework we developed is both mature in theory and applicable. In this way, objectives 3 and 4 are achieved. Move over, to demonstrate the applicability of our method, we also apply our analytical framework to study a model motivated by spectrum allocation in wireless communication in paper #2. Paper #6 also study and extended model online demand fulfillment in a class of networks with limited flexibility. So objective 5 is achieved. Extensive numerical experiments are carried in most of these papers, thus objective 6 is achieved. Achieving the objectives was not an easy task. It took tremendous effort from myself and four of my PhD students. All of them have already graduated. One became an assistant professor at Nanjing University School of Business upon completing a post-doc with me, one was placed as an assistant professor at Shanghai Maritime University after a year of visiting professor at HKUST, another also became an assistant professor at Institute of Data and Decision Analytics at CUHK(Shenzhen). The last one is doing a post-doc at Columbia University, and is on the job market this year. The papers produced in this project were much improved by hiring research assistants and communicating with top researchers in the field. The grant allowed me to have English editors improve the exposition of all my papers. The travels made possible by this grant also enable me to collaborate extensively with my collaborators and consultant around the world, and present the research outcomes in major conferences and workshops.

16501015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16501015.value: This project lead to significant development in both theory and application. Papers 3, 4, and 5 developed a framework and necessary theory to support it. All papers are motivated by practical applications such as service centers, and applied the framework to obtain insightful results as well as practically implantable near-optimal policies. The major findings of this project are as follows: Paper #1 provided a nice policy for solving the routing and staffing of a multi-class service networks with different customer classes. Paper #2 demonstrated the effectiveness of our methodology by applying it to a spectrum allocation problem with different customer classes. Paper #3 provide a theoretical framework for optimal control with Brownian input. Paper #4 unify two mainstream methods of analyzing fluid models with time varying input. Paper #6 extend a well know nice property from the classical long chain model to more general network structure. It shows that a little bit flexibility goes a long way. Papers #5 and #7 developed nice policies for handling multi-class customers in a many-server queueing setting by theoretically analyzing the asymptotic behavior of fluid models for many-server queues. The analytical framework we developed is both mature in theory and applicable.

16501015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16501015.value: In this project, we have solved several major problem completely. For example, we develop a framework of fluid analysis to address a class of important application models with multiple customer classes. We also applied our method to some closely models. So in the main theme, there should not be much left to do in the scope of proposed research. This project has great potential for future research in applications. We only demonstrate the application of the theory we develop in several application in the scope of this project. The method we develop can surely be applied to other types of model. For example, bike sharing (or more generally business models in the emerging sharing economy such as Didi Chuing) systems can be modeled as a multi-server system. The proposed course of action would be to study what are the important factor in those applications, and the modify the model (sometimes with slight adaptation of the method) to obtain insights and results in those applications.

16501015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16501015.value: This project demonstrated both theoretical and application significance. On the theoretical side, we advanced the state of art of analyzing the difficult yet widely used multi-server queueing network model by developing a framework for fluid analysis and approximation. Our research has been driven by real application in emerging areas, which leads to some innovative models such as the online web chat system, and spectrum sharing in wireless communication. These models are new in the research literature and have their own distinctive features, thus we need to develop new method to analyze them. Based on the theory we developed, we are able to obtain operational insights to the applications. For example, we propose easy-to-implement and optimal staffing and control policies for service centers with multiple customer classes, an important application in the modern society. We also reveal important insights into the spectrum management problem, and propose optimal control policy to maximize throughput while control the delay probability. Also, we provide insights in the flexibility of a service network, and shows that a sparse structure, which is often the case or needed, is near optimal.

16501315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16501315.value: QR codes (abbreviated from Quick Response Codes) have been growing dramatically in mobile marketing but are understudied. This research investigates the effect of QR codes in the context of mail coupon: how does the presence of a QR code on a consumer coupon affect redemption. Using two large-scale field experiments on restaurant coupons with about 60 thousand real consumers, we document a mere exposure effect of QR codes: merely showing a QR code on a coupon increases redemption when the coupon is offered by a restaurant that is close to consumers, but may backfire when the coupon is from a distant restaurant. A series of follow-up eye-tracking studies and lab experiments showed that the underlining mechanism for such an effect is that the natural correlation between QR codes and “Quick Response” activates a low construal, concrete thinking such that consumers focus on feasibility of closing a deal rather than desirability of the deal itself. This research is among the first studies on how consumers respond to QR codes, a powerful but yet understudied new marketing tool. Our findings also add to the research on location-based targeting.

16501615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16501615.value: An important topic in accounting research is whether and to what extent the reporting of a firm’s business performance per se (as opposed to business performance itself) has consequences for stock prices. Publicly reported accounting information serves as a basis for investors to forecast a firm’s future cash flows and assess the associated risk. Regulators and academic researchers widely believe that high-quality information helps to reduce uncertainty for market participants and thus lower the investment risk. However, gathering empirical evidence to support this notion has been a challenge for accounting researchers. One of the challenges pertains to accurate measurement of the (unobservable) discount rate that investors apply (that is commensurate with the investment risk). Another involves how to disentangle the two components of the discount rate (risk) attributable, respectively, to fundamental business uncertainty and accounting information quality. While both are important in their own right, only the latter component is of special interest to this line of research. Perhaps because of these (and other) difficulties in research design, empirical findings documented in the literature have been mixed, and we have not been able to draw unambiguous conclusions. In this project, we aim to provide more clear evidence by exploiting a unique setting in mainland China where two classes of a firm’s shares are traded in segmented markets: the A-class shares traded by Chinese investors and the B-class shares for foreigners. Although A- and B-shares have the same cash flow and voting rights, the prices of A- and B-shares diverge, with B-shares typically traded at deep discounts to A-shares. Because future cash flows accrued to them are the same, the differential prices should in theory be attributable to the respective risks facing domestic and foreign investors. Within this setting, we will examine theoretically and empirically how the quality of publicly reported accounting information influences the relative risks for domestic and foreign investors who otherwise have different accesses to company information through private channels, and consequently affects relative share prices. Taking advantage of the unique market setting, we will develop empirical tests that circumvent the aforementioned issues in research design. The study will contribute to the literature by identifying more clearly the pricing effect of accounting quality through the channel of information risk (the discount factor). 16501615.label: Major findings and research outcome
16501615.value: This study provides evidence of a link between accruals-based earnings quality (EQ) and cost of capital by examining two classes of shares traded in China’s segregated markets prior to 2001. The A- and B-shares introduced respectively for domestic and foreign investors carry identical cash flow rights, but B-shares are traded at deep discounts relative to A-shares. We predict that whereas the differential informedness of domestic versus foreign investors causes A- and B-share prices to diverge, high-quality public reporting serves to narrow the information and hence price gaps. Consistent with our predictions, we find that EQ is negatively related to the A-B share price differential and that the negative effect is more pronounced for firms with large disparities in informedness between the markets. We further find that this EQ effect vanishes after the new policy in 2001, which permits domestic investors also to trade B-shares and consequently reduces the inter-market information gap. By employing this unique setting, the study circumvents some of the research design limitations in prior studies, which enables us to better identify the pricing effect of accruals quality.

16501615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16501615.value: This line of research can be further developed to better understand the role of accounting quality on the cost of capital in the two segments of the market. The Chinese stock market has gradually been opened up to foreign investors over the years and the information gap between the two segments of the market has changed in general. There have been major developments such as the Hong Kong – Shanghai and Hong Kong – Shenzhen stock connects that initially started in 2014. The changes in the general market conditions and in the relative informedness of the two market segments provide more varied settings for further testing the role of accounting quality and related issues.

16501615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16501615.value: While financial reporting regulators and standard setters believe that high quality accounting information lowers investment risk, business managers and investors are interested in whether accounting quality indeed affects the risk that investors face in the capital market and the cost of capital. This study provides empirical evidence confirming that accounting quality has a beneficial effect on a firm’s cost of capital. In the two segregated parts of the Chinese stock market where two types of shares are being traded, the study shows that improving the quality of publicly reported accounting information helps to reduce the information gap and hence the price gap between the two market segments, and the effect of accounting is more pronounced when the information gap is particularly large. By employing this unique setting, the study circumvents some of the research design limitations in prior studies, which enables us to better identify the beneficial effect of accounting quality.

16502015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502015.value: In this project, we experimentally investigate the models of legislative rules in Gilligan and Krehbiel ("Asymmetric Information and Legislative Rules with a Heterogeneous Committee," American Journal of Political Science, 1989, 33:459-490) and Krishna and Morgan ("Asymmetric Information and Legislative Rules: Some Amendments," American Political Science Review, 2001, 95: 435-452). We hope to design experimental games that allow us to provide empirical data to be used to draw some meaningful conclusion on the informational efficiency of open and closed rules. More precisely, we address the following three questions. First, we explore whether one rule performs better than the other in terms of informational efficiency. Second, we investigate to what extent the information transmission is conducted with strategies consistent with the logic of either Gilligan and Krehbiel (1989) or Krishna and Morgan (2001). Finally, we explore how the empirical performance of an equilibrium may depend on the specification of out-of-equilibrium beliefs. 在這個項目中，我們通過實驗研究Gilligan和Krehbiel立法規則的模型（“在異質委員會情況下，信息不對稱與立法規則”，美國政治學雜誌，1989年）和Krishna和Morgan的模型（“信息不對稱和立法規則：一些修正“，美國政治科學評論，2001年）。 我們的目標是設計實驗性博弈，使我們能夠提供對 “開放和封閉的規則下信息效率”的問題有意義的實證數據。更確切地說，我們解決以下三個問題。首先，在信息效率方面 , 我們探討是否一個規則比其他的表現得更好。第二，我們研究信息發送策略是否與 Gilligan和Krehbiel（1989）或Krishna和Morgan（2001）的邏輯一致。最後，我們探討均衡點如何取決於均衡外猜測。

16502015.label: Realisation of objectives
16502015.value: In this project, I and my coauthors experimentally investigate the informational theory of legislative committees (Gilligan and Krehbiel 1989). Two committee members provide policy-relevant information to a legislature under alternative legislative rules. Under the open rule, the legislature is free to make any decision; under the closed rule, the legislature chooses between a member’s proposal and a status quo. We find that even in the presence of biases the committee members improve the legislature’s decision by providing useful information. We obtain evidence for two additional predictions: the outlier principle, according to which more extreme biases reduce the extent of information transmission; and the distributional principle, according to which the open rule is more distributionally efficient than the closed rule. (This finding addresses the first part of Objective 1.) When biases are less extreme, we find that the distributional principle dominates the restrictive-rule principle, according to which the closed rule is more informationally efficient. (This finding addresses the second part of Objective 1.) In addition, we find that data patterns are consistent with the out-of-equilibrium behavior specified by Gilligan and Krehbiel. In particular, when the two messages from the senders do not coincide, the receiver tended to take the action that corresponds to the ex-ante ideal one. (This finding addresses Objective 3.) Overall, our findings provide experimental support for Gilligan and Krehbiel’s informational theory. (This finding addresses Objective 2.)
