16502015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16502015.value: The first prediction of the informational theory that our data speak to is the outlier principle, which involves comparisons within each legislative rule: under both the open and the closed rules, more extreme preferences of the committee members reduce the extent of information transmission. While this principle appears intuitive and has been highlighted in the literature (Krehbiel 1991), it is controversial from a theoretical point of view. The existence of equilibria featuring the outlier principle is first proved by Gilligan and Krehbiel (1989). With different selections of equilibria, Krishna and Morgan (2001) show that more informative equilibria exist: for the open rule, they construct a fully revealing equilibrium under which the outlier principle does not hold. Our data support Gilligan and Krehbiel (1989): under both legislative rules, we find that an increase in the committee members’ biases results in a statistically significant decrease in the legislature’s payoff. The second set of predictions that our data speak to involves comparisons between the legislative rules, what we may call the restrictive-rule principle and the distributional principle. Gilligan and Krehbiel (1989) define two measures of inefficiency: informational inefficiency, which is measured by the residual variance in the equilibrium outcome, and the distributional inefficiency, which is measured by the divergence between the expected outcome and the legislature’s ideal policy.3 A key finding in Gilligan and Krehbiel (1989) is that, compared to the open rule, the closed rule is more informationally efficient (the restrictive-rule principle) but less distributionally efficient (the distributional principle). Krishna and Morgan (2001) have questioned this finding too, highlighting that these results are not a feature of all equilibria: there exists at least one equilibrium under the open rule that is more informationally efficient than any equilibrium under the closed rule, and there are equilibria under the closed rule that achieve the maximal possible distributional efficiency. Our experimental evidence clearly supports Gilligan and Krehbiel’s (1989) distributional principle. Regarding the restrictive-rule principle, however, we do not find evidence that the closed rule is more informationally efficient than the open rule. Overall, we find that the distributional principle dominates the restrictive-rule principle and so the legislature’s payoff is higher under the open rule than under the closed rule.

16502015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16502015.value: Our data can be explained reasonably well by the theory proposed by Gilligan and Krehbiel (1989). However, there are a few behavioral patterns that deviate from the theoretical predictions. Thus, it is important to consider some behavioral models that could potentially explain the experimental data better than the theory based on the assumption that agents are fully rational.

16502015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16502015.value: We experimentally investigate the informational theory of legislative committees (Gilligan and Krehbiel 1989). Two committee members provide policy-relevant information to a legislature under alternative legislative rules. Under the open rule, the legislature is free to make any decision; under the closed rule, the legislature chooses between a member’s proposal and a status quo. We find that even in the presence of biases the committee members improve the legislature’s decision by providing useful information. We obtain evidence for two additional predictions: the outlier principle, according to which more extreme biases reduce the extent of information transmission; and the distributional principle, according to which the open rule is more distributionally efficient than the closed rule. When biases are less extreme, we find that the distributional principle dominates the restrictive-rule principle, according to which the closed rule is more informationally efficient. Overall, our findings provide experimental support for Gilligan and Krehbiel’s informational theory.

16502315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502315.value: Hong Kong has one of the most active derivative warrant markets in the world. A derivate warrant entitles the holder to buy or sell an underlying stock at a preset price on or before a preset date. Derivative warrants in Hong Kong are issued by third-party financial institutions, usually investment banks, and sold to the public. At the same time, analysts of these warrant issuers write reports on the future prospects of the underlying stock. This situation generates a potential conflict of interest: an analyst should always try to provide accurate predictions, but if he changes his predictions more frequently, the underlying stock price may become more volatile and the warrant price may increase, generating higher revenue for the investment bank. Previous studies have identified two reasons for analysts to write more favorable but less accurate reports: to attract more securities underwriting business from companies and to maintain relationships with firm managers. In contrast, this new source of conflict of interest stemming from warrant issuance does not depend on other firms, and is therefore more direct. It may also apply to other countries with active warrant markets, such as Germany and Italy, but not the US. Warrant issuance provides a potential explanation for the international evidence of analyst recommendations. Recommendations are more accurate in the US than in some other developed countries. Using the data on analysts and warrants in Hong Kong, we will first examine whether analysts of warrant issuers are more likely to change their earnings forecasts and stock recommendations on the underlying stock before the warrant issuance. Then we will link two determinants of the warrant issuance price, volatility and returns of the underlying stock, to the revisions made prior to issuance. These revisions should also be less accurate and less informative, since the primary objective is to influence the warrant price. Analysts may even give inconsistent predictions before successive warrant issuance dates to further increase the volatility of the underlying stock. 香港是全世界衍生權證產品最活躍的市場之一。衍生權證賦予權證持有人在預先規定的時間或之前以預先設定的價格買入或賣出相關的股票的權利。在香港，衍生權證是由第三方金融機構，例如投資銀行，向公眾發行。同時，這些權證發行方的分析師將會對權證的相關股票的未來走勢撰寫分析報告。這種情形會導致潛在的利益衝突：一方面分析師應該盡可能提供關於該股票的準確預測，但另一方面如果他頻繁的更改預測結果將會導致相關的股票價格波動增大，這會提高了該股票權證的價格，從而為權證的發行方帶來更高的收益。 以往的研究確認了股票分析師撰寫關於公司股票樂觀但不精準報告的兩個原因：一，吸引更多的證券承銷業務；二，與公司經理維護良好的關係。然而，我們以上提出的利益衝突並不取決于除發行方以外的公司，因此更加直接。這個利益衝突的現象或許對其他擁有活躍權證交易的市場同樣適用：例如德國和意大利，但並不包括美國。權證發行對於全球的分析師推薦的行為特點提供了一個可能的解釋。美國的分析師推薦相比其他發達國家更加準確。 通過使用香港的關於分析師和權證合約的數據，我們首先會檢驗權證發行方的分析師是否更有可能在權證發行前更改對相關股票的盈利預測以及推薦。接著我們會將權證發行價的兩個決定性因素：股價波動率以及相關股票的回報率，與權證發行前的相關股票的修改意見聯繫在一起。由於分析師的目標是影響權證的發行價格，這些修改意見應該缺乏準確性並包含較少的公司信息。分析師在成功發行權證前甚至會發出與之前不一致的分析預測，以進一步增加相關股票的價格波動率從而提高權證的發行價格。

16502315.label: Realisation of objectives
16502315.value: All the objectives were achieved. In this study, we examine the discretionally short sale program on HKEx from 2006 to 2010. Specifically, we establish a baseline selection model for shortability and identify stocks based on Type I and Type II errors as misclassified (i.e., shortable stocks but should not be shortable) or protected stocks (i.e., not shortable stocks but should be shortable). We show that there are important asset pricing implications for deviating from the prediction model: protected stocks, especially if they are small, are associated with significantly higher future returns. To understand the misclassification and protection, we find that institutional ownership by Chinese banks, companies, and funds and/or the firm’s market exposure play a role. Chinese institutional ownership may capture some unobserved factors that are economically relevant to HKEx’s definition of "liquid stocks," or regulators have some preferences for protecting these companies from short sellers.

16502315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16502315.value: We examine the efficacy of short sale regulations in Hong Kong, where the list of shortable stocks is managed by regulators and is updated quarterly. While regulators generally cautiously restrict short selling to larger stocks, we form our predictions and examine two types of deviations: (1) misclassification, shortable stocks that should not be shortable; and (2) protection, non-shortable stocks that should be shortable. Misclassification is not associated with systematic mispricing, but protected stocks earn significantly higher future returns than other non-shortable stocks, implying a 0.56% annual welfare loss on the Hong Kong Exchange. We also establish that the likelihood of being protected is positively associated with Chinese institutional ownership. Overall, our findings suggest that increased transparency about regulatory interventions should be encouraged to promote price efficiency.

16502315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16502315.value: Many short sale bans were imposed on an ad-hoc basis, providing little cross-sectional and time-series variations to tease out other effects coming from general market conditions; their implications may also not be applicable to normal times. On the other hand, regulators in Hong Kong actively manage a designated list of “shortable” stocks: short selling a stock is allowed only if the stock is on the list, and the list is updated periodically. This style of active, frequent intervention is relevant for some emerging markets, which are in the process of adopting securities lending and short selling with regulatory oversight. There is also a wide range of new regulatory interventions even in developed countries recently: for example, the newly implemented disclosure requirements and circuit breakers in Europe, Japan, and the U.S. Therefore, the effectiveness of the regulators in Hong Kong is of major economic interest, beyond a particular type of intervention in a specific exchange.

16502315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16502315.value: Regulators claim that the short sale system in Hong Kong is “robust.” Hong Kong is one of the few markets that did not impose additional short sale bans and restrictions during the global financial crisis. Our paper presents some asset pricing implications of HKEx’s choice of shortable stocks, as well as highlights the challenges faced by regulators. They need to carefully pick the list of stocks that the rules apply to (with both Type I and Type II errors in mind) and the updating frequency of the rules. An adequate frequency should avoid outdated regulations between updates, but at the same time should not over-interrupt the market. Alternatively, exchanges may consider a system where short sale or other restrictions are applied equally to all stocks, supplement with ad-hoc rules during crisis periods. We understand that there are no perfect interventions, but we document evidence that current rules incur costs, which is related to the benefit-cost analysis of financial regulation that the recent literature proposes (Cochrane, 2014; Posner and Weyl, 2014).

16502815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502815.value: Agriculture is the most important economic sector in many developing countries, and China currently has the world’s largest population of farmers. An important obstacle they face is lack of information for making informed planting, harvesting, and selling decisions to improve their earnings. This significant information asymmetry between market participants in farming leads to poor price discovery in the value chain, which often results in economic losses for the farmers. To overcome the information gap, governments, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), and the business sector are leveraging information and communication technologies (ICT). In this proposed study we seek to investigate two main questions: As more information becomes accessible by farmers, will that create value for them and for society as a whole? Should information be widely distributed among farmers in a competitive environment? The answers to these fundamental questions are socially influential, because farmers are crucial stakeholders of the entire value chain. They are not only society’s primary producers, but also are the largest group of consumers of household products. We propose to apply game theory to uncover the salient drivers of information provision. If successful, this research is expected to identify the most important economic forces and provide equilibrium production strategies for the farmers. Information, competition, and the interactions among farmers all play crucial roles of this market equilibrium. Studying the agricultural sectors of developing countries is important because they are dominant trading partners and collaborators for Hong Kong and China. We propose to characterize the optimal information provision policy from the social welfare perspective. Our analysis will address the accessibility of information and the information’s precision. These instruments have broader impacts. Reducing the information’s precision may backfire despite its good intention. It may constitute a form of discrimination against some farmers, which would generate societal anxiety raise fairness concerns. Beyond agriculture, this study’s approach can be adapted to devise policy recommendations for traffic control, service system design, and aggregate industrial planning. Disseminating information to facilitate national central planning has been a long-standing goal for some developing (and even developed) countries. For example, Singapore implemented such a mechanism in its taxi system. Information regarding the profitability of specific industries or occupation choices can help the government to achieve socially efficient allocation of human capital. 為了消除開發中國家面臨的極度貧窮困境，許多政府以及非營利組織致力於提供給農民即時的市場資訊。這個項目研究以下兩個主要問題: 第一，當農民獲得較多的市場資訊時, 整個社會是否因此得到更多的價值? 第二， 在有市場競爭的環境中， 政府以及非營利組織是否應該廣泛地提供農民市場資訊? 由於農民是整個價值鏈的大宗， 這些問題的答案有極大的社會影響。本研究使用賽局分析來了解資訊提供以及市場均衡的重要因子，並且對於運輸控制，服務系統設計以及產業規劃提出方針建議。

16502815.label: Realisation of objectives
16502815.value: In the midterm report, we have stated that two activities were conducted for the project. Activity 1: “Information provision policies for improving farmer welfare in developing countries: Heterogeneous farmers and market selection” has been accepted by M&SOM, and the link was provided in the midterm report. Activity 2: “Providing Information to Fewer Farmers can Improve Farmers' Welfare in Developing Economies” was in the process of preparing a working paper for submission. Activity 1: Information provision policies for improving farmer welfare in developing countries: Heterogeneous farmers and market selection As mentioned, this addresses both Objectives 2 and 3 and has resulted in a paper accepted by M&SOM. Activity 2: Providing Information to Fewer Farmers can Improve Farmers' Welfare in Developing Economies This activity addresses both Objectives 1 and 4. After the midterm report, we completed the paper and submitted it to the journal MSOM in 2018 June. We are happy to report that the paper has recently been accepted by MSOM, and we acknowledged the RGC funding.

16502815.label: Major findings and research outcome
16502815.value: In Activity 1, we observe that when key market uncertainties are involved, information provision can help farmers to achieve better outcomes. However, the best provision policy should be targeted: since the information value is the highest for farmers that are not very close to either end of the market, these farmers “in the middle” should be offered information. Information provision is justified by the value creation to its receivers. The utilitarian objective therefore favors these natural beneficiaries. We also find that information provision may be implemented by simple pricing. In terms of measurable research outcomes, this activity results in a top journal publication in MSOM. In Activity 2, we instead consider homogeneous farmers ex ante. Thus, there is no targeting issue, because farmers are identical at the beginning. Nonetheless, our insights continue to carry over, in the sense that it is not optimal to provide information to all farmers. Therefore, fairness is compromised if the government intends to facilitate the best market outcome. Indeed, this insight differs from that in Activity 1: information provision has nothing to do with the value creation to a specific farmer type. Rather, it comes from the macro perspective. We have completed a paper that has been accepted by M&SOM.

16502815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16502815.value: We anticipate that the project leads to some follow-up work on the information provision policies, especially in the context of socially responsible operations. The two settings described in the two activities are stylized. Consequently, there are various dimensions that one can think of when extending them: information structure, market composition, time and space configurations, and etc.

16502815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16502815.value: Governments and non-governmental organizations in developing countries have devoted tremendous efforts in providing market information to farmers for alleviating extreme poverty. In this proposed study, we seek to investigate two main questions: First, as more information becomes accessible by farmers, will that create value for them and for society as a whole? Second, should information be widely distributed among farmers in a competitive environment? The answers to these fundamental questions are socially influential, because farmers are crucial stakeholders of the entire value chain. We propose to apply game theory to uncover the salient drivers of information provision and market equilibrium. Our analysis addresses the accessibility of information and the information’s precision. These instruments have broader impacts. Reducing the information’s precision may backfire despite its good intention. It may constitute a form of discrimination against some farmers, which would generate societal anxiety raise fairness concerns. Beyond agriculture, this study’s approach can be adapted to devise policy recommendations for traffic control, service system design, and aggregate industrial planning. Disseminating information to facilitate national central planning has been a long-standing goal for some developing (and even developed) countries.

16502915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502915.value: Relational demographers propose that demographic dissimilarity is interpreted through the lens of organizational status hierarchies such that members of high- and low- status demographic categories (such as whites and men, and women and non-whites respectively) respond differentially to demographic dissimilarity. Dissimilarity, they argue, lowers the extent to which individuals build a positive social identity through group membership. Three questions remain unaddressed: (i) why do individuals sometimes react positively and sometimes negatively to demographic dissimilarity, (ii) how does dissimilarity affect cognition and affect, and (iii) how do affect and cognition influence employee outcomes such as coworker relations. We draw on regulatory focus theory to build a relational demography model where we predict the impact of demographic dissimilarity on individuals’ cognitions and emotions and subsequently coworker relationships. 关系人口学家提出，人口差异性，通过解释 组织地位等级的镜头，这样的高和低的成员 状态人口统计类别（如白人和男人，妇女和非白人 分别）响应差异人口结构差异性。相异，他们 认为，降低到个人通过建立积极的社会认同程度 组成员身份。三个问题仍未得到解决： （一）为什么个人 有时候人口差异性做出积极反应，有时负， （二） 如何相异影响认知和影响，以及（iii ）如何影响和认知 影响员工的成果，如同事关系。我们借鉴监管重点 理论建立关系人口统计学模型，我们预测的影响 对个人的认知和情感，并随后人口统计异性 同事关系

16503015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503015.value: In empirical research quantile regression techniques have been widely used and are particularly well suited to the analysis of censored data. So far quantile regression techniques have focused more on cross-section data and less on panel data, with linear specifications. Partial linear quantile regression allows for flexible model specification and quantile regression in a panel setting with fixed effects allows for both unobserved individual observed heterogeneity and varying covariate effects. In this project, we consider sequential instrumental variable partial linear quantile regression with censoring and sequential censored quantile regression for panel data with fixed effects. The new estimation procedures to be developed in this project are expected to provide the applied researchers useful tools in empirical applications. 分位數回歸方法在當代實證研究中頗為流行。尤其在處理刪失數據方面，分位數回歸技術獨具優勢。然而迄今為止，分位數回歸的研究與應用主要針對線性模型設定下的截面數據模型，對於非線性模型與面板數據模型涉足較少。在計量經濟學與實證研究中，一方面部分線性分位數回歸模型在方程設定上更加靈活，另一方面，運用固定效應面板數據模型便於控制刻畫不可觀測的個體異質性與協變元的變動性。在本課題的研究中，我們系統地考慮研究工具變量部分線性刪失數據分位數回歸模型（sequential instrumental variable partial linear quantile regression with censoring ）與固定效應面板數據分位數回歸模型（censored quantile regression for panel data with fixed effects）的序貫估計與統計推斷技術。分位數回歸的序貫估計方法簡潔實用，相信能成為實證研究人員手中的利器。

16503015.label: Realisation of objectives
16503015.value: In the paper “Sequential Estimation of Censored Quantile Regression for Panel Data with Fixed Effects“ we proposed a sequential estimation procedure which applies standard panel QR method to observations in informative subsets selected sequentially. The proposed estimator is computationally convenient and achieves the same asymptotic efficiency as Powell's estimator. In order to establish asymptotic normality, the number of time periods T is required to grow much faster than the number of individuals N. This requirement is more restrictive than that in nonlinear panel data literature where T increases at a rate up to N. Under this weaker condition, we consider a smoothed sequential estimator which is consistent and asymptotically normal with a bias in mean. Based on the expression of the bias term, we also consider an analytic bias correction procedure. A small Monte Carlo simulation is conducted to assess the finite sample performance of our estimators and the results show that they have stable and good performance. In the paper “Semiparametric Estimation of a Censored Regression Model with Endogeneity”, we proposed a new semiparametric estimator that overcomes drawbacks associated with existing semiparametric estimation methods for the censored regression model with endogeneity. We derive conditional quantile moment conditions for all the conditional quantiles and propose a moment-based estimator. In particular, we construct two types of moment conditions and develop a computationally attractive estimator. We show that our estimator is consistent and asymptotic normal. A Monte Carlo study indicates that our estimator performs well in finite samples and compares favorably with existing methods. In the paper “Quantile Regression for Duration Models with Time-Varying Regressors”, partly motivated by the approaches in the previous two papers, using the Study of Unemployment Insurance Exhaustees public use data, which was designed to examine the characteristics, labor market experiences, unemployment insurance (UI) program experiences and reemployment service receipt of UI recipients. Using a two-step method, I studied how various characteristics affect the unemployment duration.

16503015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16503015.value: Under certain regularity conditions, the proposed estimators are consistent and asymptotic normal. Monte Carlo studies indicates that they are easy to implement and perform well in finite samples and compares favorably with existing methods. In the study of how various characteristics affect the unemployment duration, the coefficients of the replacement rate and the unemployment rate exhibit a clear trend, declining steadily when moving to the tail area. Furthermore, we have also computed the marginal effects at the sample averages for the continuous variables (replacement rate and the state unemployment rate) and different combinations for the discrete variables (race and age). For the replacement rate, any increase in the unemployment rate has less impact on the short-term unemployment than on the longer-term unemployment.

16503015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16503015.value: The estimation approaches I have proposed could potentially be extended to cases with double censoring and sample selection. I will look into these issues in a future project.

16503015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16503015.value: Missing data due to data censoring or top-coding is common in economics. In this project, I have developed econometric procedures in two different settings. These procedure should prove to useful to applied researchers, for example, for the evaluation of policy initiatives or program evaluation and how various labor market characteristics affect unemployment duration. For example, I have found that the increase in replacement rate of unemployment benefits has less impact on the short-term unemployment than on the longer-term unemployment.

16503115.label: Project Objectives
16503115.value: To examine the psychological benefits of product anthropomorphism. To examine how anthropomorphization influences consumer reactions to brand transgressions. To examine cultural influences on product anthropomorphism.

16503115.label: Realisation of objectives
16503115.value: Objective 1 was fully achieved. The project provided a well-rounded understanding of how anthropomorphism can alleviate the antecedents motives of need for connection and need for competence. Further, our findings showed that this process, in turn, increases consumers' feeling of subjective well-being -- which then produces better self-control in subsequent tasks. Finally, building off the idea of brand connection, we also found that different ways of communicating about a brand yield different levels of connection: speaking about a liked brand connects the consumer more to it than writing about that brand. Objective 2 was partly addressed. A full literature review was conducted, and a theoretical framework was used to formulate systematic predictions. However, initial empirical investigations failed to confirm these predictions. We are working further on this aspect of the project, including making changes to our theorizing and exploring other ways of empirical assessment. Objective 3 was almost fully addressed. We found that the basic antecedents and consequences of anthropomorphism were similar across two different cultures (Hong Kong and US). We would like to explore this issue further by examining contingency situations under which cultural differences can manifest in different reactions to anthropomorphized products.

16503115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16503115.value: While most research in the area of product anthropomorphism examines how the act of humanizing products influences subsequent consumer reactions to those products, the present research examines how such anthropomorphism influences consumers themselves. We propose that for consumers with a insufficient sense of sociality or competence, engaging in product anthropomorphism satisfies these deficiencies, which in turn leads to an increase in experienced vitality. Furthermore, enhanced vitality has positive implications for individuals’ capacity to subsequently exert self-control in unrelated domains. A set of studies provides support for these hypotheses, across both HK and US consumers. By demonstrating the positive effect of anthropomorphism on consumer vitality and self-control, this research illuminates the nature of anthropomorphism. In doing so, we also connect two streams of literature: one on anthropomorphism and the other on vitality, in a way that has not been explicated by past research. Building off the idea of brand connection, another key finding from our project is that speaking (vs. writing) about a liked brand increases consumers' sense of connection to that brand, which again has implications for consumer wellbeing.

16503115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16503115.value: As part of the unaccomplished objectives of the current project, we are currently further exploring how anthropomorphism influences consumer reactions to brand transgressions, by refining our current theorizing on this issue. In addition, building off the ideas and findings generated by this project, we have started another project which examines the idea that consumers tend to speak more favorably of an anthropomorphized brand than its non-anthropomorphized counterpart, even when the two brands are otherwise identical and equally liked. This research has received a favorable review and revision request from our premier journal, Journal of Consumer Research.

16503115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16503115.value: Our research speaks to the growing importance of products and possessions for our feeling of wellbeing. We find that people who are lonely, or who feel helpless, tend to endow their products with more humanlike characteristics -- thinking of it like a person (a process called anthropomorphization). Doing so helps them to feel less lonely, and more in control. In turn, this increases their ability to perform better at subsequent, unrelated tasks. Thus, especially in an increasingly materialistic world -- and also a world in which human-human interactions seem to be decreasing -- our research provides cross-cultural evidence for a broad societal implication: products seem to be replacing humans in providing key emotional benefits. This notion of brand connection also comes through in our findings regarding speaking vs. writing about a liked brand: the former leads to greater feelings of connection.

16503715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16503715.value: 主管为何对员工产生敌意并苛待员工：员工的偏差行为，主管的权力和地位三者之间的交互作用。

16503715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503715.value: Supervisor mistreatment or harmful behaviors directed by supervisors towards subordinates is a prevalent and costly problem to organizations. Survey data has shown that while 37% of American workers have been mistreated at work, 72% of mistreatments came from supervisors (Workplace Bullying Institute & Zogby International, 2007), and significantly more employees identified supervisors (58%) rather than coworkers (38%) or subordinates (5%) as perpetrators of mistreatment (Keashley, Trott, & MacLean, 1994). Mistreatment from supervisors results in huge costs to organizations by decreasing employee performance and health, and increasing legal costs (Tepper et al., 2006). It has been estimated that supervisor mistreatment may cost organizations at least US$23.8 billion annually (Tepper et al., 2006). The more frequent occurrence of supervisor-to-subordinate mistreatment compared to other kinds, such as coworker-to-coworker or subordinate-to-supervisor mistreatment, suggests that the power and status advantages of supervisors over subordinates may explain the enactment of mistreatment. However, despite theoretical speculations that powerful individuals are more likely to mistreat low-status individuals (Cortina, Magley, Williams, & Langhout, 2001), researchers have also suggested that powerful and high-status individuals are more likely to conform to norms and not abuse their power (Aquino, Tripp, & Bies, 2006) because those who abuse their power can provoke reprisals and challenges from subordinates (Boehm, 1993). Corresponding to these contradictory theoretical suggestions are conflicting empirical findings on the relation between power, status and workplace mistreatment, with some showing that high-power individuals were more likely to mistreat low-power offenders (Kim, Smith & Brigham, 1998), while some showing that high-power individuals were less likely to do so (Aquino et al., 2006). The purpose of the current proposal is to develop a theoretical model to explain these conflicting views on the relation between power, status and supervisor mistreatment. Consistent with the argument that individuals do not usually harm others unless otherwise provoked (Berkowitz, 1989), we examine the effects of power and status in the context of supervisors perceiving threats from subordinates who engage in organization- or supervisor-directed deviance. Furthermore, we distinguish power from status and integrate the ego-threat theory perspective and the power-dependence theory perspective to further our understanding of the role of power and status in the relation between subordinate deviance and supervisor mistreatment. In addition to theoretical contributions, the proposed project will provide practical implications on how to eliminate supervisor mistreatment and its related human and organizational costs. 主管对员工的苛待或者伤害行为在组织中是很常见的，且对组织带来巨大的损失。调查数据表明虽然37%的美国员工都遭遇过被苛待的经历，72%的苛待经历来自于主管，而只有28%的苛待经历来自于同事或者下属 (Workplace Bullying Institute & Zogby International, 2007)。来自于主管的苛待大大地降低了员工的工作绩效，损害了员工的身心健康，并给组织带来很多法律诉讼方面的开销(Tepper et al., 2006)。据估计，主管苛待所带来的损失每年至少高达238亿美金 (Tepper et al., 2006)。 来自于主管的苛待远远高于来自同事或者下属的苛待这一事实表明主管高于下属员工的权力和地位可能可以解释主管为何苛待下属。然而虽然有一些研究者提出权力会促使人们苛待地位低的人群(Cortina, Magley, Williams, & Langhout, 2001)，也有另外一些研究者提出权力和地位会让人们更多地服从规范而不是滥用权力(Aquino, Tripp, & Bies, 2006)因为滥用权力会引起下属的反抗从而使他们最终丧失权力(Boehm, 1993)。实证研究的结果也往往互相矛盾：有一些研究表明高权力的人更有可能苛待低权力的人(Kim, Smith & Brigham, 1998)，而另一些研究表明高权力的人更不可能苛待低权力的人(Aquino et al., 2006)。 本研究的目的在于提出一个理论模型来解释为何这些既有的关于权力、地位和苛待之间关系的观点彼此矛盾。由于人们一般都是因为自己受到挑战才会去伤害他人(Berkowitz, 1989)，我们提出要探讨权力和地位是否让主管更容易苛待下属必须考虑的背景条件是主管是否受到了来自员工的挑战（比如员工是否做出了一些偏差行为来挑战主管）。另外，我们区分了权力和地位这两个概念，并结合了自我威胁理论和权力依靠理论的观点来进一步理解权力和地位在员工偏差行为和主管苛待行为这两者关系中所起的作用。除了理论贡献之外，本研究还将对如何减少组织中主管苛待员工的现象以及该现象所造成的各种人本和经济损失提出实践指导意义。

16504015.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16504015.value: 流動性衝擊和股票回報率在世界各地：是反應不足或者放大的效果?

16504015.label: Project Objectives
16504015.value: To comprehensively examine whether the liquidity shock effect is pervasive around the world; To test which hypothesis is better in explaining the cross-country differences in the liquidity shock effects: the underreaction hypothesis versus the amplification hypothesis.
rows: To comprehensively examine whether the liquidity shock effect is pervasive around the world;
To test which hypothesis is better in explaining the cross-country differences in the liquidity shock effects: the underreaction hypothesis versus the amplification hypothesis.

16504015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504015.value: Many studies have shown that investors demand higher average returns for stocks with less liquidity (or high liquidity risk). The financial crisis of 2007–2009 further exemplifies the importance of liquidity on asset prices. When stock prices decline substantially, the collateral-based model of Brunnermeier and Pedersen (2009) suggests that the tightened margin constraints force investors to liquidate their positions, resulting in further price drops and an illiquidity spiral. Thus, illiquidity occurs simultaneously across stocks. This phenomenon is referred to as the liquidity commonality or comovement. Empirical evidence appears to support the idea that market declines cause asset illiquidity. While the theory of illiquidity implies a positive relation between the level of stock illiquidity and expected returns, Bali, Peng, Shen and Tang (2014) find that shocks of illiquidity (liquidity) significantly and negatively (positively) predict future stock returns for up to six months. They interpret the return continuation as stock market underreaction attributed by limited investor attention and illiquidity. However, if initial illiquidity or liquidity shocks are accompanied by sufficiently large contemporaneous price changes, price changes can be amplified through the cash-flow feedback channel (Subrahmanyam and Titman, 2001), wealth contagion channel (Kyle and Xiong, 2001) or illiquidity spiral channel (Brunnermeier and Pedersen, 2009). This proposal uses a global approach to examine the dgree to which the liquidity shock effect is generated by investor behavioral bias or the collateral-induced illiquidity spiral. In particular, we first examine whether the liquidity shock effect is pervasive around the world. We then distinguish between the underreaction hypothesis (investor inattention and illiquidity) and the amplification hypothesis (correlated trading and liquidity commonality) in explaining the liquidity shock effect. We take advantage of the substantial variation in trading activities across countries to uncover the determinants of return continuation caused by liquidity shocks. This international strategy allows us to examine not only which features of trading activities help explain the liquidity shock effect across countries, but also whether the relative ability of the underreaction hypothesis and the amplification hypothesis explain their cross-sectional and time-series variations. The results of the project will contribute to the literature on how market frictions and margin constraints affect the association between liquidity shocks and stock returns in the international setting. The findings should be useful and important for investors and governments in Hong Kong and around the world. 許多研究表明，投資者對流動性較差（或高流動性風險）的股票要求較高的平均收益率。 2007 - 2009年的金融危機進一步體現了流動性對資產價格的重要性。當股票價格大幅下降，Brunnermeier和Pedersen（2009年）以抵押品為基礎的模型表明，收緊保證金約束迫使投資者清倉離場，導致價格進一步下降和流動性變差的惡性循環。因此，流動性不足可同時發生在所有的股票上。這種現象被稱為流動性共同性或聯動。實際證據似乎支持這一想法，市場下跌導致資產流動性不足。 雖然流動性不足的理論意味著股票流動性不足的水平和預期收益成正相關，但是Bali, Peng, Shen, 和 Tang (2014年）卻發現流動性不足（流動性）的衝擊可顯著負（正）的預測未來股票收益達六個月之久。他們的解釋是股票回報的延續性是歸因於投資者有限關注和流動性不足所引起的股市反應不足。但是，如果最初的流動性不足或流動性衝擊同時伴隨著足夠大的同期股票價格變化，價格的變化可以通過現金流反饋管道（Subrahmanyam和Titman，2001年），財富蔓延管道（Kyle和Xiong, 2001) 或者流動性不足惡性循環管道 (Brunnermeier 和 Pedersen, 2009)。 這項研究計劃使用全球性的方法來檢驗流動性衝擊效果是否由於投資者行為偏差或抵押品價值下降所引起的流動性不足的惡性循環所產生。特別是，我們首先檢驗了流動性衝擊的影響是否在世界各地普遍存在。然後，我們區別流動性衝擊效果是否由反應不足假說（投資者注意力不集中和流動性不足）或者放大假說（相關交易和流動性共性）所引起。 我們利用在各國交易活動的大量變異來揭開流動性衝擊所造成回報延續的決定因素。這種國際化策略使我們不僅檢驗交易活動的哪些功能有助於解釋不同國家的流動性衝擊的影響，而且檢驗反應不足假說和放大假說何者比較能講釋它們的橫截面和時間序列的差異。 這項研究計劃的結果將有助於理解市場摩擦和保證金限制如何影響國際環境流動性衝擊和股票回報率之間的關聯。研究驗結果對香港及世界各地投資者和政府應該是有用的和重要的。

16504015.label: Realisation of objectives
16504015.value: The major objectives of this project are (i) to comprehensively examine whether the liquidity shock effect is pervasive around the world, and (ii) to test which hypothesis is better in explaining the cross-country differences in the liquidity shock effects: the underreaction hypothesis versus the amplification hypothesis. We have extensively investigated the liquidity shock effect around the world. We find that the liquidity shock effect is not only exists in the U.S. with our extended period, but also very pervasive outside the U.S. More importantly, we show that both the underreaction hypothesis and the amplification hypothesis can explain the liquidity shock effect. More specifically, the underreaction channel works quite well in stocks with positive liquidity shocks, while the illiquidity spiral channel is strongly supported in stocks with negative liquidity shocks. We also find that both positive and negative liquidity shocks are positively associated with the degree of capital constraints. The results are summarized in a paper, which has been presented in many international academic conferences (the 2016 Conference on the Theories and Practices of Securities and Financial Markets (SFM) in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, the 2017 FMA Asia/Pacific Conference in Taipei, Taiwan, the 2017 China Finance Annual Meeting (CFAM) in Shanghai, China, the 2018 Asian Finance Association conference in Tokyo, Japan, and the 27th (2019) Conference on Pacific Basin Finance, Economics, Accounting, and Management (PBFEAM) in Taipei, and the 2019 Annual Conference of Multinational Finance Society in Israel (scheduled)) as well as many universities. The paper with a focus on the U.S. market is currently under review at Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis. The outcomes of the project have clearly demonstrated that the project objectives have been successfully achieved.

16504015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16504015.value: This project has generated the following paper. The paper was presented at many international conferences. 1. Chen, Te-Feng, and K.C. John Wei, 2019, “Illiquidity shocks and asymmetric stock market reactions around the world: Is underreaction or illiquidity spiral the culprit?” Summary: Illiquidity shocks are negatively associated with future returns. There are two potential explanations: underreaction and illiquidity spiral. We find that negative illiquidity shocks generate upward price continuation, but positive illiquidity shocks lead to initial downward price continuation quickly followed by price reversal. Further analysis shows that the underreaction channel proxied by institutional ownership works well only in stocks with negative illiquidity shocks, whereas the illiquidity spiral channel proxied by short-term versus long-term institutional ownerships is strongly supported in stocks with positive illiquidity shocks. Moreover, our results are not subsumed by the numerator component (i.e., volatility shocks) or denominator component (i.e., volatility shocks) of the illiquidity shocks. Throughout the presentations at conferences and universities, we learn that the paper is too long for a journal publication. We now divide the paper into two separate papers. The first paper focuses on the U.S. market, while the second paper on the international markets outside the U.S. The summary of the first paper is currently under review at Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis and is summarized as follows: 2. Chen, Te-Feng, and K.C. John Wei, 2019, “Liquidity shocks and asymmetric stock market reactions: Is underreaction or illiquidity spiral the culprit?” under review at Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis Summary: We extend the previous research on the effect of liquidity shocks on future stock returns to understand the underlying mechanisms that drive the liquidity shock effect. We propose two potential explanations: underreaction and illiquidity spiral. We find that positive liquidity shocks generate upward price continuation, while negative liquidity shocks lead to initial downward price continuation but quickly followed by price reversal. Moreover, we find that the underreaction channel works well only in stocks with positive liquidity shocks, whereas the illiquidity spiral channel is strongly supported in stocks with negative liquidity shocks.

16504015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16504015.value: Liquidity is very important for the functioning of financial markets. The liquidity dry-up due to the illiquidity spiral effect is blamed for the meltdown of the financial markets in the 2008-09 global financial crisis. The potential for further development of this project is to investigate whether there is a spillover effect of the illiquidity shocks across countries and if yes, whether the centrality of a financial market plays any role. This is in our future research agenda.

16504015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16504015.value: The apparent spiral or amplifying effect of liquidity dry-up on the meltdown of the global financial markets is witnessed during the 2008-09 global financial crisis. In this project, we study the spiral effect of liquidity dry-up and the helping-hand effect of liquidity supply or positive liquidity shocks on the equity market. We find that the stock market appears to underreact to the positive liquidity shock, while the negative liquidity shock (or the liquidity dry-up) induces the spiral effect. More specifically, the positive effect of positive liquidity shocks on future stock returns is caused by investors’ underreaction, while the negative effect of negative liquidity shocks on future stock returns is mainly driven by illiquidity spiral. Our research outcomes clearly help us to understand the mechanisms that drive the liquidity shock effect on future stock returns.

16504115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504115.value: The goal of this study is to investigate a new channel through which analysts collect information, namely information sharing among colleagues covering economically related industries. It aims to provide new insights into their information acquisition process. The extant research has largely ignored such analyst activity. Specifically, I propose to measure cross-industry information sharing as the interdependence between an analyst’s industry and her colleagues’ industries using the data from the Benchmark Input-Output Surveys of the Bureau of Economic Analysis. Using brokerage mergers as an exogenous shock, I will investigate whether information sharing benefits analysts’ research along multiple dimensions, including earnings forecast accuracy, forecast timeliness, and All-Star ranking. I will also investigate cross-sectional variations in the effect of information sharing on analysts’ research quality and productivity along two dimensions – quality of colleagues and the length of the colleague relationship. The central contribution of this study will be that it identifies a new channel through which analysts collect information and provides new insights into their information acquisition costs. It will have several implications for the literature on financial analysts and practitioners such as brokerage houses and investors. First, the prior literature has mostly focused on analysts’ role as industry specialists. The main conclusion that they produce information that is highly specialized along industry lines leaves the impression that analysts contribute to the informational segmentation in the market (Menzly and Ozbas 2010). This study will show evidence that information sharing exists among analysts covering economically related industries. Second, the prior literature has often assumed that an analyst works in solitude (including working with her own team) and has studied analysts’ decisions under this assumption. This study has the implication that future research on analysts’ decision process needs to take into account their information sharing activities. Third, it will extend the literature by identifying a specific type of brokerage resource useful to improving analyst performance – information sharing with colleagues. Information sharing, measured based on supply chain relationship, captures the interdependence among industries, thus the benefit an analyst can extract from her colleagues. Therefore, the results will have a practical implication for brokerage houses that providing coverage along the supply chain and promoting collaboration among analysts covering the supply chain industries can improve their research quality and productivity. Finally, this study will have implications for investors in terms of making better investment decisions by identifying analysts with better cross-industry knowledge and superior research quality. 摘要： 这项研究的目的是研究一个分析师收集信息的新的渠道，即覆盖有经济相关产业的同事之间的信息交流，并提供了他们的信息采集过程的新的见解。现存的研究在很大程度上忽视了这种分析师的活动。具体来说，我建议利用经济分析局的基准投入产出调查数据来衡量产业之间的相互依存关系,然后用它来测量分析师和她的同事们之间的跨行业信息共享。使用券商并购作为一种外生冲击，我将调查信息共享是否有利于分析师的研究，包括盈利预测的准确性，预测的时效性，和全明星的选拔。我也将探讨在信息分析师的研究质量和效率两个维度共享的效果截面变化 - 同事的质量和同事的关系长度。 拟议的项目将有几个贡献。首先，也是最重要的是，它会指出一个新的分析师收集信息的渠道，并提供他们信息获取成本的新的见解。其次，它对未来的分析师的决策过程的研究有寓意：需要考虑到他们的信息共享活动。第三，将扩展分析师的研究文献，因为确定了与同事信息分享，一种券商资源，有助于提高分析师的效率。最后，它将对投资者的影响在于他们可以通过识别有更好的跨行业的知识和卓越的研究质量的分析师来做出更好的投资决策。

16504115.label: Realisation of objectives
16504115.value: We have achieved all objectives listed in the original grant proposal. The first objective in the grant proposal is to investigate whether analysts’ forecasting performance improves substantially when their colleagues cover industries that are economically related to their own. We find that analyst forecasting performance does improve substantially when their colleagues cover industries that are economically related to their own. In our proposal, we argue that an analyst can benefit from information sharing if two conditions are met: the interdependence between her sector and its upstream/downstream sectors is high; and these sectors are covered by her colleagues. Using the data from Benchmark Input-Output Surveys of the Bureau of Economic Analysis, we construct the following measure that takes into account both conditions: For every sector (sector i), we measure the importance of another sector (sector j) to it as the ratio of the sum of sector i’s input commodities made by sector j (i.e., j’s importance to i as its upstream sector) and sector i’s output commodities used by sector j (i.e., j’s importance to i as its downstream sector) to sector i’s total output. The sum of the importance of all the sectors covered by an analyst’s colleagues captures the total benefit she could exploit by obtaining information from her colleagues covering economically related sectors. We call this variable of interest information sharing. For an average analyst in I/B/E/S during our sample period, we find that the level of information sharing amounts to 61.1% of the total output of her sector, which is economically significant. After controlling for other factors that prior literature has shown to explain forecast accuracy, we find that analyst earnings forecast accuracy is positively correlated with information sharing. The incremental effect of information sharing on forecast accuracy is both statistically and economically significant: a one standard deviation increase in information sharing is equivalent to working for a brokerage house that employs 37 more analysts or gaining five more years of sector experience. This result suggests that the information obtained from colleagues covering economically related sectors is useful in predicting the future fundamentals of the companies covered by an analyst. Second, we document that information sharing has a favorable incremental effect on analysts’ forecast timeliness that is also statistically and economically significant. The result is consistent with the explanations that continual interaction with colleagues supplies analysts with more frequent and timely information signals and that the information signals from upstream and downstream sectors provide analysts with an edge in anticipating changes in their own sectors. The second objective in the grant proposal is to investigate whether analysts’ All-Star ranking improves substantially when their colleagues cover industries that are economically related to their own. Using the information sharing variable described above, we find evidence that supports our prediction. Prior research has documented that analysts’ All-Star ranking is associated with analyst forecasting performance, such as the accuracy, timeliness of earnings forecasts and analyst productivity, analyst experience, analyst coverage, and broker size and reputation. We find that, after controlling for analyst and broker characteristics from prior literature, analysts are more likely to be ranked as Institutional Investor All-Stars if the level of information sharing is higher. The marginal effect of information sharing is 2.06%, or 18.9% of the unconditional probability of getting ranked (10.9%), indicating economic significance. It is important to note that we already control for analyst forecasting performance such as earnings forecast accuracy and timeliness in this regression. Therefore, this result captures information sharing’s impact on analysts’ overall research quality beyond the dimensions of forecast accuracy and timeliness, and implies that other attributes desired by institutional investors, such as industry knowledge, written reports, and idea generation, also likely benefit from information sharing among analysts. Our third objective is to investigate whether analysts’ forecasting productivity improves substantially when their colleagues cover industries that are economically related to their own. We posit that a likely consequence of information sharing is increased research productivity. This is because having colleagues as a source of value-relevant information greatly lowers an analyst’s overall cost of information acquisition. All else being equal, lower information acquisition cost enables an analyst to increase research outputs more easily without being stretched too thin. We examine two measures of research productivity: total market cap covered in the industry and total number of forecasts issued for the industry. Prior research suggests that an analyst has incentives to increase the market cap covered in her industry because it gains her visibility and generates more trading commissions (Hong and Kubik 2003). A recent paper by Groysberg et al. (2011) shows that market cap covered is positively related with analysts’ compensation. Similar to the measure for forecast accuracy discussed earlier, we use the normalized ranking of market cap covered in the industry to control for task difficulty and the differences in company size across industries. Specifically, the analyst covering the highest total market cap in the industry receives a rank of 100 and the one covering the lowest total market cap receives a rank of zero. The second measure of research productivity we examine is the frequency of earnings forecasts issued for a industry, measured based on the normalized ranking similar to the last measure. An analyst has incentives to increase forecast frequency because it is widely used as an action-based performance measure by brokerage houses in evaluating analysts (Groysberg et al. 2011). Prior research also suggests that more frequent revisions may generate more commission revenues and investment banking revenues (Juergens and Lindsey 2009; Krigman, Shaw and Womack 2001). We use the information sharing variable defined above and find empirical results consistent with a positive relation between an analyst’s research productivity within the sector, based on the market cap covered and forecast frequency, and information sharing, after controlling for other observable analyst and broker characteristics. Last, our fourth objective is to examine if information sharing has a greater positive impact on an analyst’s research quality and productivity if her colleagues covering related industries are have All-Stars or have a long relationship with the analyst. Our results confirm our intuition and show that information sharing does have a greater positive impact on an analyst’s research quality and productivity if her colleagues covering related sectors are All-Stars or if the colleague relationship is longer than two years.

16504115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16504115.value: There is anecdotal evidence that analysts at the same brokerage covering related industries share information and that brokerage houses promote research collaboration among analysts. The extant literature on financial analysts, however, mostly focuses on their role as industry specialists and often makes an implicit assumption that they work in solitude. So far, little knowledge has been accumulated on analysts’ cross-industry information sharing. Our study fills a void in the literature by documenting evidence consistent with analysts sharing information with colleagues covering economically related industries. We measure the potential benefit of cross-industry information sharing as the interdependence between an analyst’s industry and her colleagues’ industries based on industry inputs and outputs data prepared by BEA. Our results indicate that information sharing benefits analysts’ research along multiple dimensions. After controlling for other factors that explain analyst performance, we find that analysts’ earnings forecast accuracy, forecast timeliness, and All-Star ranking improve with information sharing. We also document a positive relation between analyst productivity and information sharing. Moreover, we show that the impact of information sharing on analysts’ research quality and productivity is economically significant. Lastly, we investigate the cross-sectional variations in the benefit of information sharing and find that such activity is particularly helpful to an analyst’s research quality and productivity when her colleagues are All-Stars or have had a long relationship with her. Our study contributes to the literature by identifying a new channel through which analysts collect information and providing new insights into their information acquisition costs. Specifically, it provides several important implications. First, it is widely believed that analysts produce information that is highly specialized along industry lines. Such a belief can leave the impression that analysts contribute to the informational segmentation of markets. Our study reveals that analysts actually facilitate information flow across economically related industries in the market by sharing information with colleagues. Second, our findings imply that a potential cost of industry specialization -- forgoing complementary information from diversified coverage -- can largely be mitigated by sharing information with colleagues covering economically related industries. Finally, our findings have practical implications. For brokerage houses, they suggest that promoting cross-industry collaboration improves analyst research. For investors, our findings help them identify analysts with better cross-industry knowledge and superior research quality. Our working paper was accepted in the 2017 American Accounting Association annual meeting conference in San Diego. We received positive feedback and are currently revising the paper for submission.

16504115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16504115.value: Although the paper is not published, we are optimistic for the following reasons. First, the most important feedback we receive is that we need to control for brokerage resources (in addition to broker size), and endogeneity (better analysts choose to work for brokers with better colleagues and colleagues who cover related industries). To mitigate these concerns, we conduct new empirical tests (not yet tabulated) to control for broker and analyst fixed effects alternately in the model, and use change regressions instead of level regressions and continue to find results. We were not able to use these analyses because, until recently, I/O Tables were released every five years and thus information sharing variable did not have sufficient time-series variations and power. Since annual I/O data became available, we have re-done all analyses and find consistent results. Second, we have collected location and work/education history data from analysts’ LinkedIn profiles and conducted a series of new cross-sectional tests and find that information sharing is more beneficial if analysts work in the same location, if they have prior working or educational ties. We are writing up these new results and will submit the new manuscript to a top accounting or finance journal.

Our study fills a void in the literature by documenting evidence consistent with analysts sharing information with colleagues covering economically related sectors. 16504315.value: Investigate whether bank analysts informed the market about the underlying risk exposure of banking firms prior to the 2008 financial crisis.
rows: Investigate whether bank analysts informed the market about the underlying risk exposure of banking firms prior to the 2008 financial crisis.

16504315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504315.value: This study examines bank analysts’ role as information intermediary in the period leading up to the 2008 financial crisis. Financial analysts are financial experts, and sophisticated users of financial data. The severe consequences of the financial crisis naturally raise the question of their role as information intermediary in informing the market about the underlying fundamentals and risk exposure of banking firms. To understand bank analysts’ role during the financial crisis, it is important to consider all the major research outputs from analysts – not only the stock recommendations and earnings forecasts, but also, more importantly, the textual content in their research reports. We hypothesize that because of bank opacity and analysts’ asymmetric incentives of releasing good and bad news, combined with the different levels of the information precision conveyed by different research outputs, bank analysts’ forecast behavior exhibits certain pattern: they give banks the benefit of the doubts in their earnings forecasts and stock recommendations, but spoke their doubts in their written reports. Therefore, we argue that without looking into bank analysts’ report texts, prior literature fails to evaluate what analysts knew about the financial institutions before the financial crisis, and whether they had informed the market about the evolving risk in banks. Excessive risk-taking by banking firms is commonly identified as a culprit in the financial crisis. Understanding the risk exposure faced by banking firms face and its implications is critical in analyzing banking firms. Therefore, we propose to investigate the role of bank analysts in informing the market about banks’ fundamentals and risk exposure in the period leading up to the financial crisis. Specifically, we investigate the following three categories of banks’ risk exposure discussed in analyst reports: asset quality, capital, and real estate/housing exposure. Our project makes two contributions. First, it sheds light on the role of bank analysts in the 2008 financial crisis. We predict that bank analysts were able to provide early warnings about banks’ mounting risk in their written reports in the period leading up to the financial crisis, but failed to incorporate such signals in their earnings forecasts and stock recommendations. Second, to the best of our knowledge, our paper is the first to provide evidence on bank analysts’ research. Prior research on analysts’ research fails to consider the fundamental differences between financial institutions and industrial firms. Thus our paper provides direct empirical evidence on the nature and quality of bank analysts’ services. 本研究探討銀行業的金融分析師在2008年金融危機期間的信息中介角色。金融分析師是金融專家也是財務數據的專業使用者。2008金融危機的嚴重後果，讓人們質疑他們作為信息中介的角色 ，即他們是否通知了市場有關銀行公司的基本面和潛在風險。 本項目認為，為了解金融危機期間銀行業分析師的角色，考慮分析師的所有主要研究成果是很重要的 - 不僅是股票推薦和盈利預測，而且，更重要的是，他們的研究報告的文本內容。我們推測，由於銀行的不透明度，和分析師釋放好消息和壞消息的非對稱的激勵，結合不同的研究成果具有不同層次的信息精確度，銀行業分析師的預測行為表現出一定的規律：他們給銀行的盈利預測和股票推薦更加傾向樂觀，但在他們的書面報告中表露他們的疑慮。因此，我們認為，如果沒有考慮到銀行業分析師的報告文本，以往文獻無法評估分析家對金融機構的全面評價，和回答他們是否在金融危機之前已通知市場在銀行不斷發展的潛在風險。 銀行公司過度承擔風險通常被認為是金融危機的罪魁禍首。了解判斷銀行公司所面對的風險和其影響是分析銀行公司的關鍵。因此，我們建議，調查銀行業的分析師在2008金融危機前期，通知市場銀行業的基本面和風險的角色。具體來說，我們研究以下三類銀行的風險項目在分析報告中的討論：資產質量，資本，房地產/住宅投資曝光。 我們的項目有兩個貢獻。首先，它揭示了銀行的分析師在2008年金融危機中的作用。我們預計，在金融危機前期，銀行業的分析師在他們的書面報告中，有能力預警銀行業越來越高的風險，但未能將這些信號反映在其盈利預測和股票推薦中。第二，盡我們所知，我們的論文是第一個關於銀行業分析師的研究證據。在此之前的關於分析師的研究沒有考慮到金融機構和工業企業之間的根本區別。因此，我們的文件提供了銀行業分析師的研究的本質和質量的直接經驗證據。

16504715.label: Project Objectives
16504715.value: We evaluate the SEZ’s impact on the investment, employment and output of firms located in the zone. We identify the underlying mechanism: the zone’s effect on incumbents, relocated firms and new firms. Thus we can evaluate the distributional effects of the policy. By assessing relative magnitude of benefits and distortions, we derive the program's welfare implications at the local level. Our analyses will shed light on the heterogeneous effect of zones depending on the characteristics of the targeted localities and industries. Therefore, we aim to provide insightful policy implications for designing more efficient SEZ programs.

16504715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504715.value: The proposed project will compile and analyze data to examine the micro-impact of a prominent place-based program in China - the Economic Zone. Economic Zones have been widely adopted by the Chinese government: implementing special policies in an area within a jurisdiction, the goals of the zones are to increase foreign direct investment (FDI), domestic investment, international trade, technological cooperation and innovation, and employment. We plan to exploit a natural experiment in the establishment of China’s economic zone. Using firms as the unit of analyses, the project sheds light on the incidence and effectiveness of spatially targeted policies in developing countries. This greatly complements the existing literature, which has focused on the impact of such policies in the United States and in Europe. In particular, we are interested in elucidating the mechanisms underlying the effects of Economic Zones. There are two questions that we aim to answer. First, who gains and who loses from zone policies? Second, what characteristics of targeted localities make the policies more effective or less effective? In investigating these issues, we examine how the economic zone policy impacts newly created firms, relocated firms and incumbents respectively; how it influences firms differently depending on whether they are in capital-intensive sectors or labor-intensive sectors; how factors such as a zone’s pre-existing agglomeration economies and transportation accessibility play a role in determining the effectiveness of the program. To address these questions we propose to construct a novel dataset based on the following sources: first, a unique dataset of China’s economic zones including their boundary, location, establishment year, type and area; and second, a comprehensive dataset of Chinese firms spanning the periods before and after the zones’ establishment, which reports each firm’s sector, address, inputs and performance. Methodologically, we overcome the identification challenges prevailing in the evaluation of place-based policies by pairing firms across zone boundaries before and after the zones' establishment – a geographical discontinuity design. 本研究将系统地收集及分析数据，以检验中国一项影响深远的地域针对性政策的微观层面效应——开发区。开发区这项政策被中国政府广泛使用，其主要内涵如下：在一个有限的地理区域实行特定的政策，目标是为了吸引外国直接投资和内资，推动贸易，促进技术合作和创新，以及增加就业。 我们将利用中国开发区成立这一自然政策试验。该项研究以企业作为分析的基础单位，为理解发展中国家地域针对性的政策的影响和有效性提供借鉴意义。现有的文献主要关注此类政策在美国和欧洲的影响，本文将触角转移到了中国，对相关研究起到了重要的补充作用。 具体而言，我们着重想要厘清开发区政策产生影响的渠道，致力于回答两个问题： 第一，谁从该项政策中获益，而谁又因此承受了损失。第二，对于该项政策所针对的区域，哪些区域特征使开发区效应更为有效？在探讨这些问题时，首先，我们将所在区域的企业分为新创立的企业，搬迁的企业和之前就存在的企业这三类，分析开发区政策如何分别影响他们。 其次，我们将企业区分为劳动密集型和资本密集型两类，研究开发区政策如何因企业资本密集程度而产生不同的效应。最后， 我们关注开发区所在的地理因素（如交通便利程度、市场潜力等）如何影响政策的效率。 为了分析这些问题，我们计划基于以下的来源构造一个全新的数据库：一，中国开发区数据库，包括了各开发区的边界、地理位置、建立时间、类型和面积；二，详细的中国企业数据库，其时间跨度包括了开发区成立前后的年份，指标方面涵盖企业的行业、地址、投入和产出等。在计量方法方面，我们将使用地理断点回归，比较开发区边界两侧的企业在开发区成立前后的表现，用以克服分析地域针对性的政策时经常会遇到的内生性问题。

16504715.label: Realisation of objectives
16504715.value: The analyses of the paper proceed in three stages. The first examines the local effects of an SEZ on the targeted area using a reduced-form approach. Structural welfare analysis is then applied to evaluate the aggregate effects of SEZs, shedding light on their overall costs and benefits. Finally, the extent to which the effects of the zones depend on program features and the characteristics of the targeted localities is studied. A key innovation has been to construct a novel data set which merges comprehensive data on China's economic zones with two geocoded economic censuses in 2004 and 2008 covering all manufacturing firms. The zone data include the year in which each zone was established, the type of zone, and the villages located within its boundaries. The merged data set contains information on firms' ages, sectors, addresses, investment, employment, and output. That is supplemented, more importantly, with information on the firm's dynamics (entry, exit and continuing firms) and its geographical proximity to a zone. In all, 3,143,445 firms are covered. The individual firm data are then aggregated to construct a panel data set by area and year. The data series cover two periods–two years before a zone's establishment and two years after–allowing an assessment of any effects of the SEZs on the targeted areas and providing interesting evidence about how various margins contribute to the impacts. Other important outcomes such as productivity and wages are analyzed using data from China's Annual Surveys of Industrial Firms (ASIFs) from 2004 to 2008. They cover all state-owned enterprises (SOEs) and non-SOEs with annual sales of more than five million yuan. This is the first time that the outcomes of interest for SEZs have been precisely measured on such a disaggregated level. It is also the first time that comprehensive geocoded information on Chinese firms has been compiled and analyzed in relation to SEZs, something which has not previously been possible in such studies. Only with very fine-grained geographical data can empirical analyses detect whether an SEZ has had a positive incremental effect on economic activity or simply displaced activity from an untreated area to an adjacent treated one. The key challenge in identifying any causal effects of zone programs is selecting appropriate control groups, given the possible presence of spillovers. This study starts with a difference-in-differences (DD) analysis at the village level (the most disaggregated geographic unit and smaller than an SEZ) and then the county level. It compares the changes in performance among SEZ villages and counties with the changes among non-SEZ counterparts during the same period, conditional on a rich set of control variables. The village-and county-level estimates are then further utilized to separately uncover the true SEZ effects and spillovers within an inclusive econometric framework. As an alternative approach, the techniques of Neumark and Kolko (2010) and Briant, Lafourcade, and Schmutz (2015) are applied making use of the detailed information on firm location and zone boundaries. Specifically, the discontinuity in treatment at the zone boundaries is exploited to combine a boundary discontinuity (BD) design with the DD setting (constituting a BD-DD analysis). A series of analyses is used to investigate the robustness of the findings, including a concentric ring analysis (which progressively drops villages close to the SEZs from the control group) to examine potential estimation biases caused by the spillovers, and a check for parallel pre-trends between targeted and control areas using the ASIF data. Moving beyond local effects, to address the important issue of whether or not local gains from SEZs cancel out at the national level, the study builds upon the spatial general equilibrium framework developed by Kline and Moretti (2014b). In particular, the importance of the agglomeration elasticities across regions which Kline and Moretti highlighted is central to the welfare analyses of SEZs in this study. There will be national efficiency gains when the elasticity of agglomeration with respect to economic density is larger in the SEZs than in other non-SEZ areas. Following their lead, the SEZ program is allowed to influence local productivity in two ways: a direct effect through investments in infrastructure, and an indirect effect through agglomeration economies. A dynamic estimation approach is applied to distinguishing and estimating the direct and indirect productivity effects of the SEZs, on which basis their short-run aggregate effect could be evaluated. The structural approach imposes certain assumptions which might not be fully applicable to China, so a flexible estimation alternative is applied. Following the lead of Busso, Gregory, and Kline (2013) and Chaurey (2016), a back-of-the-envelope cost-benefit analysis is conducted. The distributional effects of the SEZ programs are considered, among which the main benefits include potential increases in firms' profits, workers' wages, and landlords' rental income. Meanwhile, the corporate tax concessions that firms in SEZs typically enjoy are regarded as the main costs of the program. The analyses yield three classes of results. First, the evidence shows that the SEZ program has had a significant and positive impact on the areas targeted. After two years, the SEZ areas have 58 percent more capital invested, 35 percent greater employment, and 49 percent larger output than the non-SEZ areas. The number of firms in the SEZs has increased by 29 percent. Productivity has increased by 1.5 percent on average, and wage rates by 2.9 percent, indicating agglomeration economies. There are relatively limited spillovers in industrial activity between SEZs and non-SEZ areas. The effects of SEZs mostly come from firm entry and exit (the extensive margin), with very limited effects from the existing firms (the intensive margin). Second, the direct effect of an SEZ is sizable. Improvement in a zone's infrastructure generates a 2.3% increase in local productivity in the first year, and a 18.1% increase in the second year. There are also indirect effects on agglomeration economies. In the short-run, the agglomeration elasticity in the Chinese counties seems to exhibit threshold effects. Productivity increases more rapidly in the low- and medium-density range than in the high-density range. If such non-linear relationship of agglomeration effects persists in the long run, it would provide an efficiency rationale for targeting lagging counties in addition to the equity considerations. There would be net national welfare gains because the economic gains in the targeted counties would exceed the losses in other regions. Using the estimates from the structural approach, the net present value of the benefits of the SEZ program during the period of 2007 to 2008 is roughly US$21.38 billion. Comparing it with the total tax cost of US$9.53 billion, there are net benefits of US$11.85 billion from the zone program. The alternative back-of-the-envelope cost-benefit analysis generates a very similar estimate of US$11.62 billion in net benefits, which is reassurance that the results are not sensitive to particular assumptions or methods used. Finally, the zones exhibit larger positive impacts on firms in capital-intensive industries, while zones with greater market potential and more accessible infrastructure do not demonstrate significantly larger effects. These findings are in line with the features of the SEZ programs, which typically subsidize capital investment.

16504715.label: Major findings and research outcome
16504715.value: Combining rich firm and administrative data, this paper examines the incidence and effectiveness of a prominent place-based policy in China: Special Economic Zones. Establishing zones is found to have had a positive effect on capital investment, employment, output, productivity and wages, and to have increased the number of firms in the designated area. Net entry plays a larger role in explaining the effects than incumbents. A structural analysis suggests that the program yielded net benefits of about US$11.85 billion over two years. Capital-intensive industries benefit more than labor-intensive ones from the zone programs.

16504715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16504715.value: This study has been a first step toward understanding the micro-foundations of place-based policies in developing countries. Much remains to be done. This study evaluates only short-term effects (two years after the zones' establishment) due to data limitations. Further efforts should be extended to investigating the long-term impacts of the zones, including whether or not the non-linear agglomeration elasticity persists. It would be interesting, in particular, to uncover any links between local political, economic, and social institutions and the effects of zones. Such analyses would undoubtedly be of great benefit in defining how SEZ policy interventions should best be implemented in specific contexts.

16504715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16504715.value: Place-based programs – economic development policies aimed at fostering the economic growth of a specific area within a larger jurisdiction – have grown popular and been pursued by many governments around the world over the past several decades. Although there has been much research focused on such programs in the United States and Europe, there have been few attempts to evaluate interventions in developing countries. Several questions loom especially large: Who benefits and who loses from place-based programs? Do local economic gains cancel out when aggregated nationally? Which factors determine the effectiveness of such interventions? Since developing countries usually suffer from poorly-developed institutions and markets, would the assumptions and conceptual approaches of the place-based policies in the United States and Europe still hold for them? This study constitutes a novel step in that direction. A primary contribution of this work is that it provides some of the first compelling evidence about the local and aggregate effects of zones, their welfare implications, and several determinants of program effectiveness, at least in China. Given the large number of developing countries implementing similar zone programs, the findings have important implications for policy (World Bank, 2008) and the design of more effective SEZs.
