16504815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16504815.value: The financial sector plays a critical role in affecting the aggregate economy. The Great Recession of 2007-2009, triggered by the recent financial crisis, was a fresh reminder that a small shock to the financial sector can cause a large business cycle fluctuation. In the medium and long run, underdevelopment of financial markets can also be an important reason for poor performance in economic growth (see Shleifer and Vishny (1997) and Levine (2005)). What is less well understood are the channels through which the financial sector impacts the aggregate economy. Substantial progress in our understanding has been made by studying the financing channel. See, for example, the seminal work by Bernanke and Gertler (1989), Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) and Holmstrom and Tirole (1997), and the more recent survey by Brunnermeier et al. (2013). However, there are puzzles that cannot be explained by the financing channel. For example, the evidence documented by Adrian, Colla and Shin (2012) shows that the aggregate financing provided by the financial sector to the real economy did not decline much in the recent financial crisis. Also, the segment within the financial industry that was hit hardest was broker dealers and hedge funds whose main activities have been in secondary market trading, while commercial banks, the main source of corporate financing, were relatively intact (He et al. (2010) and Greenwood and Scharfstein (2013)). Our project aims to explain the puzzles by studying a different channel - the information channel. We propose a theory of information amplification and spillover that explains the propagation effect of the financial sector, and will formally confront the theory with data. The key insight of our theory is that there exists mutual learning between firms and financial markets. When this insight is embed into a macroeconomic model with a financial sector, our preliminary result shows that our theory delivers a number of new important implications about amplification, contagion and the welfare of the macroeconomy and financial markets. The scope of investigation undertaken As we planned in the application of the grant, we proceeded with our project in three steps: Step 1: Provide a theory for the information role of financial markets to the aggregate economy Step 2: Confront the theory with data by both calibration and empirical tests Step 3: Extend the theory along several dimensions We have finished all the three steps. 1. In our two published papers, we build a theoretical model in each paper. Those models are very novel, which makes our paper published in top journals. 2. We have asked RAs to collect data and empirical evidence to test the key implications of our theoretical models. The empirical findings support our theoretical predictions. Moreover, we have calibrate our model to confront with the real data in our second publication. 3. We have extended the theory along several dimensions and derived new implications including amplification effects, real uncertainty and financial uncertainty, contagion and spillover, and cross-sectional implications (see the details in our second published paper entitled: "Financial Markets, the Real Economy, and Self-fulfilling Uncertainties").

In the first published paper, we introduce endogenous information acquisition into an otherwise standard business cycle model. In our framework information is a productive input, which is essentially specialized labor, so information acquisition is linked to the labor market and thereby to macroeconomic conditions. We show that when firms acquire information optimally, information acquisition is endogenously procyclical, and therefore economic uncertainty faced by the firms is countercyclical. Two-way feedback exists between economic uncertainty and macroeconomic activities, resulting in an amplification effect of TFP shocks, and possibly generating multiple equilibria. Our basic model can also be extended to explain countercyclical aggregate volatility. On the theoretical side, our model demonstrates that strategic complementarity (substitutability) in information acquisition coincides with strategic complementarity (substitutability) in production, and that reducing uncertainty through information acquisition improves resource allocation. In the second published paper, we develop a model of informational interdependence between financial markets and the real economy, linking uncertainty to information production and aggregate economic activities. We argue that there exists mutual learning between financial markets and the real economy. Their joint information productions determine both the allocative efficiency in the real sector and the market efficiency in the financial sector. The mutual learning creates a strategic complementarity between information production in the financial sector and that in the real sector. A self-fulfilling surge in financial uncertainty and real uncertainty can naturally arise when both sectors produce little information in anticipation of the other producing little information. At the same time, aggregate output falls as the real allocative efficiency deteriorates. In the extension to an OLG dynamic setting, our model characterizes self-fulfilling uncertainty traps with two steady-state equilibria and a two-stage economic crisis in transitional dynamics.

16504815.value: We are doing some further research along the line of our existing researches. We expect the new research will also lead to top publications. 1. We plan to study both the financing channel and the information channel in explaining how financial markets affect the real economy. 2. We plan to use our model framework to explain the yields of risk bonds across business cycles.

16504815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16504815.value: It is extremely hard to publish theory papers in top finance journals. Our researches, which greatly expanded the frontier of the human knowledge on the role of information in macroeconomy, lead to two publications in top journals (Journal of Economic Theory and Journal of Finance). Specifically, our researches show how information interacts with macroeconomy in the following ways. 1. There exist mutual learning between financial markets and the real economy. This creates a strategic complementarity in their information production. 2. In general equilibrium, information in financial market, information in the real economy, and aggregate economic activities are linked. That is, the amount of information in the economy is endogenous and interplays with the aggregate economy. 3. In a dynamic setting, we characterize self-fulfilling uncertainty traps with two steady-state equilibria and a two-stage economic crisis in transitional dynamics.

16505315.label: Project Objectives
16505315.value: Examine the interactive effects of perceived identity, and positive and negative leader and team member behaviors on the motivational process of proactive behaviors. Analyze the motivational spillover effects of leader and team member behaviors experienced in one cross-functional team (Team A) on change-oriented proactive behaviors exhibited in another cross-functional team (Team B). 16505315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16505315.value: In today’s competitive business environment, employee change-focused proactivity “has swiftly become an organizational necessity” (Chen, Farh, Campbell-Bush, Wu, & Wu, 2013, p. 1026; Parker & Collins, 2010). To enhance productivity, more firms are embracing team-based work. With limited employees and numerous projects, a common practice is to assign employees to work on multiple teams (Mathieu & Chen, 2011). Consequently, employee motivation and proactivity likely emanate from social stimuli employees are exposed to across different team leaders and coworkers. Despite these trends, previous team research has typically simplified these dynamics by focusing on one team context at a time (Mathieu & Chen, 2011). To better understand modern-day teaming, we deviate from prior approaches and propose a longitudinal investigation of employees’ simultaneous participation in multiple teams. Our purpose is to explore how leadership, team characteristics, and motivation in one team (Team A) can spillover to influence employee change-oriented proactive behaviors in another (Team B). In addition, we explore the boundary conditions that might influence motivational between-team spillover. The proposed research will enrich our understanding of how complex, multi-team dynamics influence individual employee proactivity within and across teams. We will also provide practical insights about how to manage employees in multiple teams and maximize the transfer of employee contributions across teams.

16505315.label: Realisation of objectives
16505315.value: The objectives of the project have been achieved successfully. For the first three objectives, we conducted three studies including one experiment and two field studies to examine leadership and team member proactive behaviors in the multiple team membership context. In the first experiment, we found that empowering leadership emanating from leaders of two distinct teams could influence (uniquely and interactively) an employee’s overall psychological empowerment and, subsequently, the employee’s overall proactivity. A strength of the study is the experimental manipulation of two leaders’ empowering leadership (while holding differences in employee, teams, and leader attributes constant), though the artificial (i.e., scenariobased) setting of the study, coupled with focus on proactivity intentions rather than actual behaviors, represent limitations. In addition, this study focused on overall (across teams) psychological empowerment and proactivity versus the extent to which empowering leadership of a leader in one team can spillover to affect an employee’s psychological empowerment and proactivity in a different team. In the second study, we constructively replicated the first study in a number of ways. First, using a multisource and time-lagged survey design, employees assessed individual-referent empowering leadership of their two leaders in two distinct teams, as well as their psychological empowerment in each team, whereas each of the two leaders rated employee proactivity in their teams. Second, we wished to examine whether the effects detected in Study 1 in a U.S.-based sample generalizes to employees and leaders from a different cultural background (i.e., a sample in the People’s Republic of China [PRC]). Third, to account for alternative explanations for the findings, we also statistically controlled for the total number of teams to which employees were assigned as well as the number of hours per week employees worked in each of the two teams. These are important controls because employees arguably have greater exposure to leader influences and more opportunities to be proactive in their teams when (a) they are members of fewer teams (and hence also work under fewer leaders) overall, and (b) spend more time working in any given team. Results from the second study constructively replicated and extended results from Study 1 to team-specific forms of psychological empowerment and proactivity. First, we found that empowering leadership from two different leaders of two distinct teams positively and uniquely related to an employee’s team-specific psychological empowerment, and that the nonfocal team leader’s empowering leadership more strongly and positively related to an employee’s psychological empowerment in a focal team when the leader of that focal team exhibited lower empowering leadership. In addition, we also found that an employee’s team-specific psychological empowerment mediated between empowering leadership of two different team leaders and that employee’s team-specific proactivity. Importantly, findings were consistent in this study (with team specific measures of psychological empowerment and proactivity) with those reported in Study 1 (with measures of overall psychological empowerment and proactivity). This occurred despite the different study designs and measurement approaches in the two studies and using a sample of employees and their leaders from the PRC (vs. U.S.-based participants). The first two studies relied on either overall or team-specific psychological empowerment, and both relied only on individual-level (i.e., individual-referent) operationalizations of empowering leadership. To further support and extend our hypotheses, in the third study, we included measures capturing (a) both individual-referent and team-referent empowering leadership, and (b) both team-specific and overall psychological empowerment in the same study using different perationalizations of empowering leadership experienced by members in two distinct teams). We also included a sample of U.S.-based employees and their teams’ leaders and a different set of controls than Study 2. In particular, we controlled for (a) whether each team leader was also an employee’s formal supervisor (because formal supervisors have more formal power, and hence may influence employees more strongly than others serving only as team leaders), and (b) whether the two teams’ leaders were colocated or not (given colocated leaders may suggest the teams—and leader influences—are less distinct than teams whose leaders work in distinct offices/locations). The results of the third study fully replicated Study 2’s findings on the spillover relationships involving team-specific psychological empowerment and proactivity. With individual-referent measures of empowering leadership, the results also fully replicated Study 1 finding on the spillover relationships involving overall psychological empowerment. The results also showed that team-specific psychological empowerment from the same focal team—but not team-specific psychological empowerment from another team or overall psychological empowerment—uniquely and positively related to team-specific proactivity and mediated the influences of two distinct leaders’ empowering leadership on team-specific proactivity. The three studies allowed us to achieve the first three objectives listed above. We chose not to examine the perceived identity mentioned in objective #1, due to the already very complex model we are testing, and the realization that adding something more like this may hurt our ability to deliver a clear and coherent story and ultimately, our chance of publishing it in the top-tier journal. That being said, all other elements stated in objective #1 are examined and thus the objective is still very well achieved (99%). The overall findings across the three studies also provide insight into and practical knowledge of effectively motivating professional workers that participate in multiple teams to engage in proactive behaviors, achieving the fourth objective. Specially, our finds suggest that employees’ psychological empowerment is important for the successful implementation of multiple team membership designs in organizations. Specifically, enhancing employees’ psychological empowerment can motivate employees in multiple team membership settings to contribute their talents to their teams and transfer knowledge across teams (e.g., by proactively offering innovative suggestions and initiating positive changes in their teams). Our findings are especially insightful for organizations that heavily adopt team-based operations, such as an employee-owned public benefit organization with a strong focus on effective team-based work and human capital utilization.

16505315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16505315.value: Using a scenario-based experiment and 2 field studies of leaders and their employees in the People’s Republic of China and the United States, we examined how empowering leadership exhibited by 2 different team leaders toward a single employee working on 2 different teams can spillover to affect that employee’s psychological empowerment and subsequent proactivity across teams. Consistent across all 3 studies, we found that each of the team leaders’ empowering leadership uniquely and positively influenced an employee’s psychological empowerment and subsequent proactive behaviors. In the field studies, we further found that empowering leadership exhibited by one team leader influenced the psychological empowerment and proactive behaviors of their team member not only in that leader’s team but also in the other team outside of that leader’s stewardship. Finally, across studies, we found that empowering leadership exhibited on one team can substitute for lower levels of empowering leadership experienced in a different team led by a distinct leader. The research contributes to the motivation, teams, and leadership literatures in significant ways, and provide practical guidance for leaders charged with managing employees that have multiple team memberships. The article that came out of this project has just been published in one of the flagship journals of the management field: Chen, Smith, Kirkman, Zhang, et al., (2019). Multiple Team Membership and Empowerment Spillover Effects: Can Empowerment Processes Cross Team Boundaries? Journal of Applied Psychology, Vol. 104, 321-340.

16505315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16505315.value: 1. Our research only focuses on two teams for the multi-team phenomenon. As many employees work on more than two teams simultaneously and, it is important to examine whether our findings generalize beyond two teams. 2. We chose to examine empowerment and proactivity process among members who are working on multiple teams simultaneously. It would also be interesting to study "spill-over effects" of other social influences--both positive (such as positive affect tone, or psychological safety), and negative (such as negative affective tone or abusive supervision in teams)--across teams. 3. It may be interesting to examine other potential moderators of spillover effects of leader influences in multiple team membership contexts. For example, how strongly team members identify with the roles they hold in the teams, similarities across teams' social contexts (e.g., similar team goals), and how similar leaders are to employees (e.g., in terms of demographic or functional attributes) can also strengthen or weakens the spill over effects.

16505315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16505315.value: In today’s organizations, employees are often assigned as members of multiple teams simultaneously (i.e., multiple team membership). We set out to examine the leadership and employee phenomena in such settings. We conducted three studies with one experiment and two field studies, and found that leadership of one leader in one team can affect members of another team that is outside of that leader's supervision. This research project not only contributes to the advancement of several liteatures in management field academically, but also provides valuable insights to practitioners in the society. Our results show that employees’ psychological empowerment is important for the successful implementation of multiple team membership designs in organizations. Specifically, enhancing employees’ psychological empowerment can motivate employees in multiple team membership settings to contribute their talents to their teams and transfer knowledge across teams (e.g., by proactively offering innovative suggestions and initiating positive changes in their teams). Our findings are especially insightful for organizations that heavily adopt team-based operations, such as an employee-owned public benefit organization with a strong focus on effective team-based work and human capital utilization.

16505715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16505715.value: The notion that investors prefer returns with higher positive skewness and are ready to pay a premium for it has been widely discussed, and appears to be well-established in the literature, and even if various aspects of this phenomenon are still intensely debated. Yet, some recent evidence from the currency markets seems to contradict this established view on investors' attitudes, and a few recent studies have found evidence inconsistent with the skewness premia, or even outright contradicted it. This evidence comes from currency carry trades and may apparently extend to carry trades in the commodity markets. The goal of the proposed study is, first, to verify and document this puzzling evidence and, second, to begin the enquiry into its nature and possible resolution. 投资者偏好于有正向偏斜度的收益率并且愿意为之支付一 定溢价的概念在文献中已经有成熟的讨论， 即便对于是这种现象的有些方面仍然存在激烈的争论。 然而，一些来自货币市场的新近的实证证据似乎跟投资者的这种偏好观念是相违背的。其中，有一些新近的研究发现和偏斜度溢价不一致，甚至是完全相反的证据。这些证据来自于货币市场中的利差交易，很明显，也能拓展到商品市场的利差交易。此项研究计划的主要目的是：其一，再次确认这一项令人费解的实证证据的存在；其二， 开始寻找这个谜底的性质和可能的解释。

16505715.label: Realisation of objectives
16505715.value: The project envisioned the study of four global markets - currency, equity, commodity and bonds. The specific focus of interest was the POSITIVE cross-sectional relation between average returns and return skewness, as per our preliminary observation in the data, which is in contrast to theories that attempt to explain returns with the magnitude of a NEGATIVE skewness. In particular, such a relations is at odds with a long research tradition that investigates the investors' preference for (positive) skewness, and aversion to negative skewness, and the associated premia. Objective 1 involved an in-depth empirical investigation of the relation at hand, across the four markets. It was found that the relation is the strongest in the currency and commodity markets, marginally significant in the global equity market, and non-existent in the global bond market. Furthermore, it was found that the relation in the commodity market is highly sensitive to the presence (or absence) of one particular commodity in the set used for constructing the carry trade. The results for the equity futures data were also found to be sensitive to the inclusion or exclusion of two specific country indexes, and were impacted by the different length of the respective returns series across different countries. Overall, the investigated relation is the strongest in the currency market, and at beast marginal in two of the other three markets. Pursuing Objective 2, a number of robustness checks were implemented. Importantly, one of these involved subsamples of different length, which revealed that the investigated relation is strongly time varying, for currencies, commodities and equities. Furthermore, in some subsamples it switched sign, conforming to a standard skewness preference. The commonality in results across these markets is consistent with the original conjecture Objective 3 was pursued most rigorously for the currency and commodity markets, since the relation was found to be the strongest there. Besides, the quality of the respective option data for these two markets is most suitable for our purposes (commodity option data were obtained as part of this project). The equity index futures options data are more sparse and uneven, for different countries, similar to the equity futures data. The results for Objective 3 are mixed. First, comparing the investigated relation across option-hedged and unhedged trades did not deliver clear-cut new insights, as it was unstable and sensitive to the way that various carry trades were constructed. Second, option-based measures of skewness were compared with the statistical counterparts, which showed that the difference strongly varies over time, both in sign and magnitude, and for both currencies and commodities. This finding agrees with that for Objective 2, both pointing to a major role of certain time variation that operates across markets. Therefore, Objective 4 was naturally focused on possible rationalizations that rely on time varying state variables. While an extensive search for common driver(s) across the markets was performed, no particularly strong joint results were found. The time variation in the investigated relation appeared to be related to different candidate state variables and with a different strength for the different markets. It remains an open question to identify the common drivers of returns across markets that can account for the specific time variation in the relation between average returns and skewness that we observe in the data. In this sense, Objective 4 was not fully achieved. Still, pursuing Objective 4 brought the conclusion that our setup can fruitfully address important questions specifically for the currency market (where our results are typically most significant). Importantly, we realized in the course of this investigation that certain type of carry cross sections (i.e., numeraire invariant ones) are the PERFECT tool for studying global risks in the currency market, where the currency perspective plays a key role, and this ultimately underpinned the decision to focus exclusively on the currency market. The study evolved towards the search of an explicit time-varying relation that can explain the returns of (invariant) currency carry trade cross sections, and thus throw light on the economic nature of global risks, which are an integral part of recently developed models of the currency market. My paper "Global risks in the currency market" is the direct outcome, so far, of the investigation based on carry cross sections. The key state variable that is suggested is the average return of the US dollar against a number of currencies of developed economies, as discussed in particular in a recent paper by Lustig, Roussanov and Verdelhan. I add to their model a time-varying dispersion in the exposure to global risk, with and treating the relative US interest rate as a global state variable. A number of interesting new empirical results are found, and a test for global risk factors is designed, based on the model. Empirically, the test rejects a number of risk factors used in prior studies, indicating that global risks still present a challenge to empirical research in the currency market.

16505715.label: Major findings and research outcome
16505715.value: The main finding is that the investigated cross sectional relation between average returns and return skewness of carry trades does NOT hold uniformly in different markets. In this aspect, we did not find confirmation for the original conjecture about a new common phenomenon across markets. This conclusion is somewhat unexpected, given, for example, the strong commonality between carry trades constructed in different markets and instruments in Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen and Vrugt (JFE'2018). One interpretation of this finding is that the causes for such commonality, which are still not clear, are not likely to be related to return skewness. This interpretation also strengthens the evidence against a skewness premium and/or skewness aversion explanations of carry trade returns (unconditionally), which in itself is an important finding, in light of the influential works of Brunnermeier, Nagel and Pedersen (NBER'2009), and Farhi and Gabaix (QJE'2016), among others. However, an alternative interpretation that we favor is that the relation is in fact more involved, and exhibits clear time variation, with some subsamples where it conforms to a standard skewness preference, and other subsamples where it switches sign and poses a major puzzle. My paper "Global risks in the currency market" is the direct outcome of the investigation based on carry cross sections. It adds to the model of Lustig, Roussanov and Verdelhan (JFE'2014) a time-varying dispersion in the exposure to global risk, treating the relative US interest rate as a global state variable. A test for global risk factors is designed, based on the model, which, as we find, rejects a number of risk factors used in prior studies, indicating that global risks still present a challenge to empirical research in the currency market. A second work to which the investigation in this project has contributed is the paper "Good Carry, Bad Carry", with Geert Bekaert. While this work was started earlier, and provided some motivation for this project, it also benefited to an extend from the project. This refers in particular to the notion of "invariant carry trades" that was developed as a direct outcome of the project, and also to the examination of cross sections of option-hedged vs. unhedged carry trades. The latter results formed a separate section in the paper until the very last round of revisions.

16505715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16505715.value: Related to Objective 4, it remains an open question to identify the common drivers/factors of returns across markets that can account for the time variation in the relation between average returns and skewness that is observed in the data. The results obtained so far indicate that key global financial variables, like the (relative) US interest rate could play the role of global state variables that can explain the observed relations.

16505715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16505715.value: The project envisioned the study of the relation between average returns and skewness of carry trades constructed in four major global markets (currencies, commodities, equities and bonds). The motivation for this study comes from the observation that for some cross sections of carry trades the relations is in fact positive, and thus at odds with theories that postulate a negative relation, and thus investors' preference for (positive) skewness, and aversion to negative skewness in general, for any type of assets. This observation is also at odds with theories that attempt to explain specifically the carry trade returns as a premium compensating investors for negative skewness. The main finding of the study is that the investigated cross sectional relation does not hold uniformly in different markets. At the same time, the relation exhibits clear time variation, with some subsamples where it conforms to a standard skewness preference, and other subsamples where it switches sign and generates the puzzle that motivates the study. Further research should strive to identify the common drivers/factors of returns across markets that can account for the time variation in the relation between average returns and skewness that is observed in the data. Candidates for such drivers are key global financial variables, as for example the (relative) US interest rate.

16505815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16505815.value: Financial disclosures are important means of communication with stakeholders. Given that product markets fundamentally determine a firm’s survival and growth, voluntary disclosure in product markets is of great interest. To date, the stream of literature has largely focused on the proprietary costs of disclosure (see Healy and Palepu, 2001, for a review), i.e., voluntary disclosures reveal company secrets to its competitors. To the best of my knowledge, there is no study investigating the role of sales and marketing executives in deciding disclosure policies. Sales executives are front-line executives who possess strong incentives and superior knowledge in revenue generation. The study is aimed to provide evidence regarding whether or not sales executives matter to voluntary disclosures. Specifically, motivated by recent studies examining whether CEOs’ and CFOs’ personal styles matter to disclosure policies (e.g., Bamber et al., 2010; Ge, Matsumoto, & Zhang, 2011), I examine whether the individual style of sales executives influences financial and non-financial disclosures, and the associated factors. In this project, I expect that sales executives matter for three reasons. First, sales executives are responsible for revenue generation and possess superior knowledge in predicting future revenue. Second, the theory of proprietary costs of disclosures suggests that public disclosures reveal company secrets to its competitors (e.g., Verrecchia, 1983). As sales executives’ job security and pay is closely linked to sales performance, they have a strong incentive to minimize the proprietary costs of disclosure. Third, there is evidence that sales executives are directly involved in the disclosure events, e.g., in earnings conference calls. However, it is also possible that the effects of sales executives on disclosures may be subsumed by CEOs and CFOs. In such cases, the behavior of subordinates indicates only an execution of the CEOs’ decisions rather than a reflection of their own viewpoint. Any effect of subordinate managers on disclosure decisions may thus be overridden and even disappear entirely. I plan to acquire financial disclosures, including management forecasts, and non-financial disclosures, including product releases and business expansion. To identify the individual styles of managers, I will follow prior literature and utilize the fixed effects of sales executives and their turnover. I also propose to investigate the associated factors using the executive’s incentives, ability, and background. Overall, the proposal provides academic insight by identifying the role of operation managers in setting disclosure policies. It also offers practical value in terms of internal corporate governance and public disclosure regulations. 財務信息披露是與利益相關方溝通的重要手段。鑑於產品市場根本上決定了企業的生存和發展，文獻對產品市場自願性信息披露的有很大的興趣。迄今為止，文獻主要集中在信息披露向它的競爭對手揭示公司的秘密，自願披露損害企業的競爭力。沒有研究銷售和營銷經理在決定披露政策中的作用。銷售人員是一線主管, 擁有強大的創收知識。我們的研究旨在提供銷售主管是否自願披露的證據。具體而言，出於最近的研究認為CEO們和CFO的個人風格的重要披露政策，本文研究銷售人員的個人風格是否會影響金融和非財務披露，以及相關的因素。 在這個項目中，我預期銷售人員重要的原因有三。首先，銷售人員負責創收，並有預測未來的收入卓越的知識。二，信息披露的專利成本的理論認為，公開披露洩露公司機密給它的競爭對手。銷售業績和銷售管理人員的工作保障，工資是密切相關的，他們有強烈的動機，以盡量減少公開的專利成本。第三，有證據表明，銷售主管直接參與本發明的事件，例如在財報電話會議。然而，在另一邊，也有可能是銷售人員對信息披露的影響可能由CEO和CFO被納入。在這種情況下，對下屬的行為是一個單純的執行CEO的決策，而不是他們自己的觀點的反映。下屬經理披露決策有什麼影響因此被CEO們的覆蓋，甚至可能完全消失。 我計劃收集財務披露，包括管理層預測，以及非財務信息披露，包括產品發布和業務擴張。為了確定這些經理的個人風格，我會按照之前的文獻和使用銷售人員和他們的營業額的固定效應。我建議研究利用高管的激勵機制，能力和背景相關的因素。總體而言，該提案通過識別操作管理人員在制定信息披露政策中的作用提供了學術見解。它也有內部的公司治理和公開披露的規定方面的實用價值。

16505815.label: Realisation of objectives
16505815.value: The research objectives of the project have been fully achieved. In particular, we use a fixed effects model and estimate the individual styles of sales executives to empirically test their influence on revenue forecasts (e.g., Bertrand and Schoar 2003; Bamber et al. 2010b; Ge et al. 2011). To control for omitted variables, we separate the fixed effects of sales executives from known economic determinants of disclosures, including ﬁrm, time, and CEO/CFO fixed effects. This design provides us with a powerful model to identify the effects of sales executives and to control for correlated economic factors. Our findings show that after we control for other determinants of voluntary disclosures, the fixed effects of sales executive styles are significant in predicting the issuance, accuracy, bias, and precision of revenue forecasts. In terms of disclosure quality, we also find evidence that sales executives on average reduce forecast bias and improve forecast accuracy, although they do not have a directional impact on the frequency and precision of revenue disclosures. We conduct two additional tests to provide further insights. First, we compare the incremental explanatory power of sales executive styles over those of CEOs and CFOs in determining disclosure decisions. Our evidence shows that sales executive styles have double the incremental power of CEO and CFO styles in explaining revenue forecasts, suggesting their overall influences are greater than that of CEOs and CFOs. Second, we perform cross-sectional tests by identifying circumstances in which sales executives are more important. We expect that sales executives have a stronger incentive to influence a disclosure when the proprietary cost of disclosure is higher. We also expect that their expertise in future revenue generation is more valuable when revenue forecasting is more difficult, i.e., when there is greater operating complexity. We find evidence consistent with our expectations. To ensure the robustness of our main findings, we conduct several additional tests. First, as Execucomp only reports the top five executives in each firm year, our tests are conditional on having sales executives ranked within top five. To address the selection problem, we use a Heckman two-stage selection model to control for the endogeneity of sales executives in Execucomp. In the first stage, we model the likelihood of a firm having sales executives in the top management team. In the second stage, we use the inverse Mills ratio based on the first-stage regression as a control variable in our estimation. We find consistent evidence that reinforces our main results. Second, to refine the F-statistics test in the fixed effect model, we conduct a placebo test, in which we randomly assign sales executives to different firms 1,000 times and then compare the F-statistics from the simulated sample with those from the actual sample. The F-statistics from the simulated sample are significantly smaller than those from the actual sample, which further validates our conjecture that sales executives affect a firm’s voluntary disclosure policy. Third, as previous studies demonstrate that analyst forecasts are largely driven by voluntary disclosure information, we conduct a test that uses analyst revenue forecasts as an alternative measure of sales executives’ influence on revenue disclosures (Baginski and Hassell 1990; Donelson et al. 2012). We find that sales executive styles are significantly associated with the properties of the analyst revenue forecasts issued for a firm. Finally, we find that, using an indicator variable equal to one when sales executives are in top-5 executives to capture the sales executives’ influences on disclosures is subject to an endogeneity bias. The significance of the indicator variables in predicting disclosure properties disappears after we control for endogeneity using the Heckman two-stage selection model. This result supports the benefits of using fixed effects models in the tests. Our project provides several contributions to the literature. First, our findings extend the results from the literature related to the determinants of revenue-related disclosures. Studies of revenue-related disclosures mainly examine the information-related consequences of revenue forecasts in capital markets (Han and Wild 1991). Most voluntary disclosure studies focus on the economic determinants of earnings-related disclosure (e.g., Hutton, Miller and Skinner 2003) or the effects of CEOs/CFOs (e.g., Bamber et al. 2010b). They ignore the managers of frontline operations, who have superior knowledge and incentives to generate revenue and are directly in charge of communicating with customers. Our project examines the determinants of revenue forecasts, in particular, whether sales executives, who have strong concerns of product market competitiveness, affect a firm’s decision to reveal plans for revenue generation. The findings thus fills this research gap and provides both academics and regulators with a better understanding of management team composition in revenue-related disclosure decisions. Second, our project makes methodological contributions by reconciling the empirical methodologies used to estimate the presence and magnitude of the influence of top managers’ styles in relation to firms’ decisions. Although previous studies use either fixed effects models (e.g., Bertrand and Schoar 2003; Bamber et al. 2010b; Ge et al. 2011) or turnover tests (e.g., Brochet et al. 2011; Fee et al. 2013), these two approaches produce inconsistent results in some settings (Fee et al. 2013). Therefore, we use both a fixed effects model and turnover tests in our project and find that both sets of results are generally consistent with the notion that sales executives imprint their styles on issuances of forward-looking information. Our project thus suggests that the combination of alternative methodologies used to test managers’ individual styles can provide more robust and convincing evidence for the influence of executive style on firms’ voluntary disclosure decisions.

16505815.label: Major findings and research outcome
16505815.value: This project extends previous studies on firm disclosure decisions by examining the influence of sales executives on revenue-related voluntary disclosures. It finds that sales executives’ individual styles affect firms’ disclosures beyond the effects of CEO and CFO styles. Sales executives have a greater overall incremental power to explain disclosure decisions that is double than that of CEOs and CFOs. Furthermore, the effect of a sales executive’s style on a firm’s disclosure decisions is related to proprietary costs and operating complexity of the firms. The results are robust after controlling for the endogeneity of sales executive presence on top management teams, and are extendable to analyst revenue forecasts.

16505815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16505815.value: The project can be further developed to study the importance of sales executives in firm valuations. For instance, sales is a key measure of firm performance. As such, the characteristics of sales executives and their importance may be important consideration for financing decisions and merger and acquisitions. How sales executives are accounted for in those senarios may thus provide further insights to quantify the value of sales executvies to the firm.

16505815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16505815.value: The project examines the importance of sales executives’ individual style in firms’ voluntary disclosure decisions. Using both fixed effects and exogenous executive turnovers, the findings show that the style of sales executives are significant in explaining the properties of revenue forecasts, after controlling for economic determinants and the effects of CEOs and CFOs. We also find that sales executives are more important than CEOs and CFOs in deciding revenue forecasts, and when firms have higher proprietary costs and operating complexity. Finally, our findings are robust after controlling for the endogeneity of whether firms’ sales executives are in top-five management teams. In summary, our study contributes to the literature by documenting that sales executives are an important determinant of voluntary disclosures.

16505915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16505915.value: In supply chains, it is quite common for manufacturers and retailers to use rebates to stimulate demand. For example, according to a report by Parago in 2011, the US market for corporate-funded rebates is estimated at more than US$8 billion, with an average saving of US$150 per year for a typical household. It is well known that rebate programs can allow firms to achieve price discrimination. Rebates can also be more cost effective than price markdowns because consumers may fail to redeem their rebates after making purchases. Although a rebate program can be an effective promotion tool, it usually leads to a higher advertising and distribution costs. In a supply chain setting, a manufacturer who offers such a program has to incur the cost, even though the program also benefits the retailer. With the advance of information technology, large retailers routinely acquire market data to obtain information about product demand. Many of these retailers have started to offer data-sharing programs to provide such information to the manufacturers to facilitate collaboration. With better information, a manufacturer can make better decisions to improve supply chain performance. However, the manufacturer may abuse the information to gain an advantage in future business transactions. Therefore, in offering a data-sharing program, a retailer typically faces the tradeoff of improving the overall supply chain profit with more information transparency and claiming a smaller share of the profit due to the loss of private information. Manufacturer rebate is an area that could greatly benefit from information sharing by a retailer, but the retailer may not have an incentive to do so due to concerns about information abuse. In the literature on supply chain management, most of the work on manufacturer rebate focuses on a one-manufacturer-one-retailer relationship under complete information. The issues of asymmetric information and manufacturer competition have been largely ignored. Moreover, besides the wholesale price, the issue of how information sharing impacts other channel policies such as manufacturer rebate has not been much explored. We hope to fill these gaps by developing analytical models to study (1) the incentive for manufacturers to offer rebate program under competition, and (2) the incentive for a retailer to share private demand information with competing manufacturers who offer consumer rebates. Our investigation will contribute to supply chain management theory and provide managerial insights to practitioners who are involved in manufacturer rebate programs and retailer data-sharing programs. 供应链中，零售商与制造商常常采用返现折扣来刺激需求。 例如，Parago公司的2001报告估计就美国市场每年商家提供800亿美金的返现折扣，相当于平均每个家庭可以每年节省150美金。众所周知返现折扣帮助商家实现价格歧视。不仅如此，返现相比直接降价更具有成本效益，这是因为消费者往往在购买时候忘记申请返现。虽然返现是一种有效的促销手段，但是也意味着更高的广告和发行成本。在供应链中，制造商发行返现折扣需承担有关成本，尽管零售商也从中获益。 随着信息技术的发展，大型零售商会常规地购买市场数据来提取产品需求信息，并且开始向制造商提供此类信息，以促进协作。制造商有了更好的信息后就能改进决策，从而改善供应链效率。然而，制造商也有可能会滥用信息来获得未来交易的有利条件。 因此，零售商在决定是否与制造商共享数据时面临着两种利弊的权衡——是否要通过失去独享信息和增加自己利益的机会来改善供应链的整体效益。尽管共享信息能很大程度地促进制造商折扣，但出于信息滥用的担心，零售商仍可能不愿意这么做。 绝大多数的供应链管理的文献关注于完全信息下单个零售商和单个制造商的供应关系，而忽视了信息不对称和制造商间竞争的问题。并且，除了批发价格外，共享信息如何影响其他渠道政策，比如制造商返现折扣，很少被研究探索。我们希望通过分析模型研究如下方面从而填补这些空缺：（1）制造商在竞争条件下发行返现折扣的动机，和 （2）零售商与发行返现折扣的制造商分享私有需求信息的动机。 我们的研究可以为完善供应链管理理论有所贡献，并为供应链管理者在零售商数据共享及制造商返现折扣相关实务方面提供指引。

16505915.label: Major findings and research outcome
16505915.value: I analyse a base model with two competing manufacturers selling substitutable products through a common retailer and obtain the following results. Without competition, a manufacturer offers rebate if the fixed cost of a rebate program is low, market size is large, rebate redemption rate is low, or the proportion of rebate-sensitive consumers is large. With competition, both manufacturers offer rebate when their fixed costs are low, and none of them offers rebate when their fixed costs are high. Otherwise the manufacturer with a low fixed cost offers rebate whereas the one with a high fixed cost does not. When competition is less intense, it is more likely for the manufacturers to offer rebate. Without rebate, more intense competition hurts the manufacturers and benefits the retailer, whereas a smaller market size generally hurts all the firms. With rebate, however, when more intense competition or a smaller market size induces a manufacturer to cease offering rebate, it hurts the retailer, benefits a non-rebate-offering rival manufacturer, and benefits a rebate-offering rival manufacturer if competition is intense and hurts her otherwise. I extend the base model to the case when the retailer has private demand information and obtain the following results. When there is information sharing, the manufacturer's wholesale price and rebate decision respond positively to the demand information. Without competition, information sharing benefits a manufacturer but hurts a retailer. When there is no side payment, a retailer does not voluntarily share information with a manufacturer. When there is side payment, however, information sharing can occur when the proportion of the rebate-sensitive consumers is large. With competition, when the proportion of the rebate-sensitive consumers is low, the retailer does not share information with either manufacturer. As such a proportion increases, the retailer starts to share with both manufacturers, and then shares with only one manufacturer. This is true regardless of whether the retailer can charge a side payment for information sharing or not. When there is side payment, the retailer prefers to offer information sharing concurrently to both manufacturers instead of sequentially to one manufacturer before the other. Some of the above findings are reported in the paper entitled "Manufacturer Rebate Competition in a Supply Chain with a Common Retailer" published at Production and Operations Management in 2017.

16505915.value: In supply chains, it is quite common for manufacturers and retailers to use rebates to stimulate demand. Although a rebate program can be an effective promotion tool, it usually leads to a higher advertising and distribution costs. A manufacturer who offers such a program has to incur the cost, even though the program also benefits the retailer. Our research findings offers useful insights about the incentive for a manufacturer to offer rebate, and how this depends on the business environment such as competition and asymmetric information. Moreover, such an incentive can be enhanced via collaboration with a retailer. Our results contribute to supply chain management theory and provide guidance to practitioners who are involved in manufacturer rebate programs and retailer data-sharing programs.

16506015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16506015.value: Aggregation of preferences and information in elections are fundamental questions in political economy. How elections aggregate preferences has long been of interest to researchers. Given the incentives of rational voters to vote strategically, how voter preferences map into election outcomes is an important but difficult question. More recently, researchers have also studied the aggregation of information in elections. When voters do not have perfect information about candidates, information of voters affects their voting behavior in complex ways. Despite the fact that how actual elections aggregate preferences and information are two key questions, empirical work that tries to address these questions is scarce. This project seeks to identify and quantify the extent to which information and preferences are aggregated using data from U.S. presidential primaries. This proposal considers how elections aggregate preferences and information in the context of U.S. presidential primaries. The sequential nature of the presidential primaries provides a suitable environment for studying information aggregation because it naturally gives rise to heterogeneity in what voters who vote at different dates know about candidate quality: voters in later states can learn from the votes of earlier states as well as from new events that occur after earlier primaries. This makes it possible to examine the extent to which information is aggregated through elections. Another feature of the U.S. presidential primaries is that voters in the same state vote simultaneously, while elections are sequential at the state level. Together with the fact that municipality-level breakdowns of votes for each primary are available, these features help identify strategic voting and strategic turnout and isolate the effects of strategic voting and strategic turnout from the outcome of the election. This makes it possible to examine the extent to which preferences are aggregated through elections. More broadly, the identification and estimation strategy considered in this proposal can be applied to many settings in which decisions are made collectively and aggregation of information is important. Examples are not limited to applications in political economy (e.g., decision making in legislatures and elections), but also include other important applications such as corporate governance (corporate board and/or share holder meetings), monetary policy (Federal Open Market Committee meetings), and judicial decision making (judges and juries). 選擇傾和聚集和選舉信息是政治經濟學的基本問題。選舉如何聚合偏向一直令研究人員感興趣。理性選民有策略地投票，如何將投票的偏向切合選舉結果是重要而困難的問題。最近，研究人員還研究了在選舉中的信息聚合。當選民沒有關於候選人完善的信息，選民既有的信息以影響他們的投票行為便比較複雜。儘管選舉聚集偏好和信息是兩個關鍵問題，試圖用實證研究解決這些問題卻很少被涉及。這研究項目旨在用美國總統初選的數據 , 來確定和量化信息和偏向怎樣匯集。 這提案檢視美國總統初選中, 選舉如何聚集偏向性和信息。美國總統初選的有序性 , 提供了一個合適的條件去研究信息的聚合，因為選民在不同日期投票 , 以後的選民可以穿參考早期的選舉結果以及初選之後發生的新事件 , 這異質性引令選民更了解候選人的品質。這令人能檢查信息如何聚集。美國總統初選的另一個特點是，在同一個州的選民投票同時進行，而選舉在國家連續迎進行。加上投票的每個直轄市級的分項數字，這些可幫助了解戰略投票和投票率 , 及從選舉結果中分析策略投票和投票率。令人可檢視偏向怎樣透過選舉而聚集。

16506015.label: Major findings and research outcome
16506015.value: We made two types of finding in this project which studies the effect of voter turnout on preference aggregation in large election. The first is a methodological one. We found how to separately identify cost of voting, voter preference, and perception on efficacy of voting from data of voting outcome. The second is an empirical one. We find young, less-educated, low-income, and religious voters have high voting costs, as do African Americans, Hispanics, and other minorities. Moreover, young voters have low perception of voting efficacy, which further depresses turnout among this group. Overall, young, less-educated, and low-income voters are particularly underrepresented. In terms of preferences, minority, young, highly educated, low-income, and non-religious voters are more likely to prefer Democrats. Our results show that, overall, there is a positive correlation between voting cost and preference for Democrats that can be accounted for through observable characteristics. Except for two voter characteristics--years of schooling and being religious--we find that demographic characteristics that are associated with a higher cost of voting are also associated with preferring Democrats. We also find that unobservable cost shocks are positively correlated with unobservable preference shocks for Democrats. These correlations result in fewer Democratic votes relative to the preferences of the underlying population. Our estimate of turnout is significantly lower among the electorate who prefer Democrats to Republicans, at 55.7%, compared with turnout among those who prefer Republicans to Democrats, at 64.5%. Finally, in our counterfactual experiment, we simulate the voting outcome when all voters vote. We find that the vote share of the Democrats increases in all states. Overall, the increase in the Democrats' two-party vote share is about 3.7%. We also find that the increase in the Democratic vote share would overturn the election results in nine states, including key states such as Florida and Ohio, resulting in the Democrats winning a plurality of the electoral votes.

16506015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16506015.value: The project found a way to identify a basic voting model with participation only based on aggregate level actual voting data. The methodology can be extended to many elections, particularly the ones for which polls and surveys are not reliable, such as Brexit and 2016 U.S. presidential election, to understand how voting outcome and voter turnout are related.

16506015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16506015.value: We study how voter turnout affects the election outcome. Under voluntary voting, election outcomes disproportionately aggregate the preferences of those voters with low voting cost and high preference intensity. We show how to statistically measure the relationship between preferences, costs, and perceptions of voting efficacy, and explore how the relationship affects preference aggregation. Using county-level data from the 2004 U.S. presidential election, we find that young, low-income, less-educated, and minority voters are underrepresented. All of these groups tend to prefer Democrats, except for the less-educated. Democrats would have won the majority of the popular and the electoral votes if all eligible voters had turned out.

16506415.value: 国有企业改革对中国经济的量化分析

16506415.label: Project Objectives
16506415.value: Develop a general equilibirum model with SOEs so that we can undertake quantitative policy analysis. Apply quantitative analysis to the Chinese economy so as to asses different types of policies on SOE reform.
rows: Develop a general equilibirum model with SOEs so that we can undertake quantitative policy analysis.
Apply quantitative analysis to the Chinese economy so as to asses different types of policies on SOE reform.

16506415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16506415.value: One of the most important economic developments in Chinese economy in the past 30 years is the transition from State-Owned Enterprises (henceforth, SOE) sector to the non-SOE sector. During this transition process, China undertook dramatic and persistent reforms in SOEs, which helps the efficient reallocation of resources and substantially contributes to the growth of the Chinese economy, as shown in Brandt, Hsieh and Zhu (2008). However, even after more than three decades’ of reform, SOEs still have more advantages than non-SOEs, such as easier access to the credit market as emphasized in Song, Storesletten, and Zilibotti (2011) and the monopolistic position of SOEs in upstream industries discussed in Li, Liu and Wang (2014). This has led to some deep structural problems in the Chinese economy, such as financial repression, more investment-driven than consumption-driven growth and inefficient allocation of resources. The Chinese economy has started to slow down recently. External demand has weakened because of the financial crisis in 2008 and the slow recovery of developed economies, especially the Eurozone. Therefore, looking for new driving forces for growth for the Chinese economy has become one of the most important tasks for the Chinese government. In 2014, China began another wave of economic reforms, and the SOE sector plays a very important role in these reforms. Reducing the market power of upstream SOE firms and financial market reforms have been discussed widely. How to reform the SOE sector? What are the welfare consequences of these potential policies? This paper plans to evaluate different types of policies on SOE reform and conduct quantitative welfare analysis in a general equilibrium model with the SOE sector. Our model is based on Peng, Shi and Xu (2014), but considers two more important components, endogenous entry of firms and the active role of government. The policies to be investigated in the paper include: lowering of entry barrier to upstream industries, the reallocation of credit resources and the reduction of government investment through SOEs.

16506415.label: Realisation of objectives
16506415.value: During this report period, I have worked on two papers to fulfill the objectives of the project. Both papers focus on the vertical production structure and resource misallocation in China. As emphasized in Li, Liu and Wang (2014), the industrial structure in Chinese economy is characterized by a vertical structure where SOEs monopolize key industries and markets in the upstream industries and provide intermediate goods to the non-SOE downstream manufacturing sector. Due to policy distortion and regulation, there exist severe resource misallocation between SOE and non-SOE firms as well as upstream and downstream sectors. First, Chinese government subsidize SOEs heavily, especially in the upstream sector. Second, private firms are subject to severe credit constraint and financial friction. Third, the upstream service sector such as financial service, energy, education, health care are highly regulated industries and not fully open to non-SOE firms. The entry barrier to service sectors or some upstream industries for private sector lead to lack of competition in the upstream and excessive competition in the downstream manufacturing sector. Recently, policies that reduce the entry barriers to the upstream sectors are being discussed and considered extensively by the government and the policy makers. Also, policies that target the financial frictions and credit constraint in the non-SOEs sectors are the focus of financial structural reform of the next stage. These policies will lead to more efficient resource allocation between SOEs and non-SOEs, as well as between upstream and downstream sectors. Hence, these policies will have important welfare implication for China’s growth and business cycles. In the first paper, we focus on the role of capital misallocation between the upstream and downstream sectors in driving trade imbalance between China and US. Global current account imbalances have remained persistently large over the last decade. Recently, the trade dispute between China and the US is getting out of control and leads to a trade war. There is growing literature that studies the global current account imbalance, especially the bilateral US-China trade. However, most of existing literature focus on the overall trade imbalance. If we decompose the trade imbalance between the US and China, there exist sector- levels of trade imbalance. On the one side, China runs huge trade surplus in the manufacturing sector; on the other side, China has large trade deficit in the service sector. From the view of traditional trade theory, the substantial divergence of trade balance in these two sectors is simply due to comparative advantage or technology differentials in two countries. In this paper, we argue that this is because of the mismatch between the supply and demand for both service goods and manufacture goods. With economic development, demand for service and manufacturing goods by Chinese households increase unevenly; the former grows much faster than the latter. Chinese consumers continue to shift their demand towards service goods and away from manufacturing goods and food. They will upgrade their consumption, on items such as education, health-care, travel and entertainment. In a market economy, firms will respond to the change of consumption pattern by shifting resource to service sector from manufacturing sector. However, the resource misallocation between upstream and downstream sectors due to regulation inhibits the supply of service goods. Consequently, China becomes the world factory and the major exporter of manufacturing goods, and most are low-end manufacturing products. Therefore, the structural change in demand and the misallocation in the supply side generate substantial mismatch of consumption and production in Chinese economy, which enlarge the divergence of trade balance in both sectors. Motivated by these evidence, we build a two-country, multiple-period overlapping generation model to study the dynamic of trade imbalance and economic dynamic transition. In this model, we consider a vertical production structure in Chinese economy. There is an upstream SOE who produce intermediate goods to the downstream manufacturing and service sector. There are two types of firms in the downstream: SOE and PE. Three frictions are investigated in the supply side, the subsidy to upstream SOEs, the credit constraint for private firms, and the entry barrier for private firms. For the household side, we introduce subsistence of consumption on service goods so as to generate uneven demand elasticity for service goods and manufacturing goods. We calibrate the model to match Chinese trade data and show that the structure change in consumption and the resource misallocation driven by policy distortions can help explain the rising of trade imbalance from 1998 to 2016. Furthermore, our calibration results show that polices that remove the subsidy on SOE sector and alleviate the credit constraint on private firms in China will speed the economic transition up and reduce the trade imbalance by 39.3 %, which increase welfare by 14.7%. In the second paper, policy distortion and regulation imply that lack of competition in the upstream and excessive competition in the downstream manufacturing sector leads to a severe relative price distortion between the upstream and downstream goods. For private firms subject to financial constraint, variation in the relative price between inputs and output will amplify the financial distortions. So we try to explore how the interaction of relative price distortion between upstream goods and downstream goods and the financial friction in the non-SOE sector will affect the capital misallocation in China. We will develop a dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model with SOEs and non-SOEs with two key features. First, a vertical production structure, where SOEs monopolize key industries and markets in the upstream industries and provide intermediate goods to the non-SOE downstream manufacturing sector. The non-SOE firms in the downstream sector are subject to financial constraint while firms in the upstream sectors are not. Second, the markup in the upstream sector is higher than that in the downstream sector due to different market structure in the two sectors. Since the upstream sector goods will be used as intermediate inputs in the downstream sector, the higher relative of upstream (SOE) sector goods to downstream (non-SOE) sector goods create a relative price distortion which will interact with the credit constraint in the downstream sector and amplify the capital misallocation due to asymmetric financial access. To show that the markup in the upstream sector is higher than that in the downstream sector, we first match the custom level data and the Chinese firm level data to collect the price and cost information at the sector and firm level. The current empirical evidence support this conclusion. Moreover, we plan to empirically investigate if fluctuation in the intermediate input price can explain the time-variation of capital misallocation of Chinese firms using panel data. To do that, we also follow Hsieh and Klenow (2010) to measure the TFPR based resource misallocation. These empirical finding will guide our quantitative analysis. Currently we are working on the quantitative exercise. The purpose is to show a) The importance of interaction of vertical structure, relative price distortion and the financial friction in resource misallocation; b) If entry barrier to the upstream sector is reduced, so that relative price distortion is mitigated, how much misallocation can be reduced, and what is the welfare implication? c) If the degree financial friction in the non-SOE firms in the downstream sectors is reduced, what will be the welfare improvement. This paper is still in progress.

16506515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16506515.value: Extensive empirical evidence demonstrates there is a positive relationship between return volatility and trading volume. While trading volume is an indirect measure of investor participation, we are not aware of any study that examines how the level of investor participation affects the return volatility. In this project, we make use of a unique database provided by the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE) that contains the trades by all investors. The database allows us to calculate, for each stock, the number of traders on any particular day. We use the number of traders and the number of shareholders as the measures of the level of investor participation, and examine how they affect the stock’s volatility. There are two hypotheses. The investor sentiment hypothesis predicts a positive relationship between volatility and number of traders (a proxy for the investor sentiment). The liquidity provision hypothesis predicts a negative relationship between volatility and number of traders (a proxy for liquidity provision). Despite a lot of studies conjecturing that a more diverse ownership structure will improve the liquidity, we are not aware of any studies that provide direct evidence. We will provide direct evidence for how the number of traders and the number of shareholders are related to the stock’s liquidity. 大量的實證證據表明股票回报波動率和交易量之間存在正相關關係。雖然交易量是投資者參與的間接措施，我們不知道有任何研究探討如何投資者的參與程度影響了股票波動。在這個項目中，我們利用上海證券交易所（上證所），包含交易所有投資者提供一個獨特的數據庫。該數據庫可以讓我們來計算，每隻股票，交易者在某一天的數量。我們用交易者的數量和股東的投資者參與程度的數量，檢查它們如何影響股票的波動性。有兩種假設。一是投資者情緒假說, 它預測波動性和交易者的數目之間的正相關關係。二是提供流動性假說, 它預測波動性和交易商的數量之間的負相關關係。這個項目將提供直接證據, 探討如何交易者的數量和股東人數影響到股票的流動性。

16506515.label: Realisation of objectives
16506515.value: There are two objectives in the initial proposal. - Examine the relationship between stock's price volatility and the number of investors trading in the market; - Examine the relationship between the degree of investor participation (measured by either the breadth of shareholders of or the number of investors trading in the stock) and the stock's liquidity (as proxied by the price impact measure) Following the objectives, we retrieve the following data. The first dataset is directly extracted from the information center in the Shanghai Stock Exchange (SSE). We focus on A-share common stocks that are listed on the SSE throughout 2007‒2013. For each stock, the dataset contains the daily numbers of retail accounts and institutional accounts that participate in trading the stock and the daily opening numbers of the retail and institutional accounts that hold long positions in the stock. The second dataset consists of daily data provided by the RESSET Data Inc. For each stock, the daily data include the stock return (adjusted for dividends), closing price (adjusted for dividends), share trading volume, yuan trading volume, and the number of all shares outstanding. The third dataset is RESSET level-I intraday data, which provides time-series snapshots of the consolidated open limit order book (COLOB) for each SSE stock’s continuous trading session. A snapshot is recorded on average every 3-6 seconds, and shows the five best quoted bid prices, ask prices, and volumes as well as the most recent transaction price and trading volume. We estimate time-series regressions of daily volatility on the daily number of shareholders, controlling for either daily turnover ratio or daily number of traders. We confirm a positive relationship between the price volatility and trading activity, whether we use the turnover ratio or the number of traders in the market. On the other hand, the price volatility is negatively related to the number of shareholders. The results are both economically and statistically significant, and robust across both retail and institutional investor subsamples. We find that the relationships of order imbalance and depth imbalance to the number of shareholders are both negative, while their relationships to turnover ratio or the number of traders are both positive. This suggests that a wider shareholder base will lead to more-offsetting trades and promote liquidity provision, while a higher turnover ratio or a larger number of investors trading in the market can lead to larger order imbalance and less-balanced liquidity provision. We further show that the numbers of traders and shareholders affect price volatility by affecting order imbalance and depth imbalance, we regress daily volatility on the order imbalance predicted or the depth imbalance predicted by the numbers of traders and shareholders. We find that daily volatility has positive relationships to the predicted order imbalance and the predicted depth imbalance. We conduct additional tests using exogenous shocks to the number of shareholders and number of traders, respectively, based on changes in the security transaction tax (STT) on May 30, 2007 and April 24, 2008 in the Chinese stock market. For each of the two STT changes, we run cross-sectional regressions of change in volatility (or change in depth imbalance) on change in the number of traders and change in the number of shareholders. These cross-sectional results are consistent with the time-series results: change in number of traders (shareholders) has positive (negative) relations with change in volatility and with change in depth imbalance.

16506515.label: Major findings and research outcome
16506515.value: The main results in the paper are summarized as follows. Conventional wisdom would suggest that the large shareholder base enhances liquidity provision and mitigates volatility. As a result, many companies, stock exchanges, and policymakers try to increase the ownership breadth, or the number of shareholders for each stock, as they believe that an increase in the number of investors holding a stock will have a positive effect on its liquidity and therefore on the company’s value as well. However, there are very empirical studies. In this project, we make use of a unique database in the Chinese stock market that keeps track of the number of shareholders for a cross-section of stocks as well as on a daily basis. The database also keeps track of the number of traders on a daily basis, so that we can compare the impact of the number of shareholders versus number of traders on the market’s volatility. We have the major findings as the following: 1. We estimate time-series regressions of daily volatility on the daily number of shareholders, controlling for either daily turnover ratio or daily number of traders. We confirm a positive relationship between the price volatility and trading activity, whether we use the turnover ratio or the number of traders in the market. On the other hand, the price volatility is negatively related to the number of shareholders. 2. We also study effects of number of traders and number of shareholders on order imbalance (the difference between buyer-initiated and seller-initiated trades) and depth imbalance (the difference between market depths on the two sides of the limit order book). We find that the relationships of order imbalance and depth imbalance to the number of shareholders are both negative, while their relationships to turnover ratio or the number of traders are both positive. This suggests that a wider shareholder base will lead to more-offsetting trades and promote liquidity provision, while a higher turnover ratio or a larger number of investors trading in the market can lead to larger order imbalance and less-balanced liquidity provision. 3. To further show that the numbers of traders and shareholders affect price volatility by affecting order imbalance and depth imbalance, we regress daily volatility on the order imbalance predicted or the depth imbalance predicted by the numbers of traders and shareholders. We find that daily volatility has positive relationships to the predicted order imbalance and the predicted depth imbalance.

16506515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16506515.value: Conventional wisdom suggest that the large shareholder base enhances liquidity provision and mitigates volatility. If a stock is widely held by a lot of shareholders, the large shareholder base can enhance the liquidity provision on both sides of the market. We make use of a unique database provided by the Shanghai Stock Exchange to study the roles of investor participation in the volatility-volume relation. We find that number of shareholders and number of traders participating in the market can have different effects on stock price volatility -- the daily stock price volatility is negatively related to the daily opening number of shareholders, but positively related to the daily turnover ratio and number of traders. Further, the number of shareholders and number of traders also have different relationships with the daily order imbalance and daily depth imbalance. These findings suggest that a bigger shareholder base tends to supply liquidity and reduce volatility, while a larger number of traders lead to larger order imbalance and higher volatility. We thus contribute to the volatility-volume literature from a new perspective, by differentiating the effects of two types of investor participation measures (shareholders and traders). .

16600215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16600215.value: 從漢語方言語法研究，我們看到方言在語序上存在著明顯的差異：(1) 粵語傾向把賓語置於動詞後 (我買咗書 ‘我買了書了’)，而官話和吳語則經常用處置式 (我把書買了) 和次話題化 (我書買了) 把賓語置於動詞前；(2) 在有些情況下，當北京話和吳語使用後置詞時 (擱桌上)，粵語和閩語可以不用後置詞，而用前置詞 (放喺枱 ‘放在桌上’)；(3) 在差比式中，官話和吳語的基準出現在形容詞前 (張三比我高)，而粵語和閩語的基準出現在形容詞後 (張三高過我)；(4) 官話把副詞置於動詞前 (我先走)，粵語和吳語則可以使用“動詞+副詞”的語序 (我走先)。 方言在語序上的差異也反映在方言歷史材料中。初步觀察發現方言在語序上經歷了重大的變化。在方言歷史材料中，我們有以下的發現：(1) 粵語和吳語都經常使用“動+賓”語序，但後者現在更傾向把賓語置於動詞前；(2) 官話和吳語的處所詞往往是前置詞和後置詞並用的，但它們現在更多的只使用後置詞；(3) 現代粵語表示比較的“形容詞 + 基準”語序，在方言歷史材料中的分佈更廣泛；(4) “動詞 + 副詞”的語序只見於粵語的歷史材料。上述方言在語序上的變化值得進一步考察。 本研究以十六世紀後編寫的方言材料為基礎，探討官話、吳語、閩語、粵語在以下語序上的變化：(1) 動詞和賓語；(2) 名詞和前後置詞；(3) 形容詞和基準；(4) 副詞和動詞，並找出導致上述語序變化的動因。最後，我們會在不同性質的材料中，包括教科書、小說、聖經翻譯，考察語序變化的速度。 以往研究主要是對個別方言的歷史材料進行描述，本研究則把不同方言的歷史材料放在一起比較，試圖在統計資料的基礎上為觀察到的語序變化提供一個解釋。研究結果將會幫助我們對漢語方言歷史、語序類型、歷史語言學等範疇有進一步的認識。
