16600215.label: Major findings and research outcome
16600215.value: 1. Early Cantonese and Southern Min texts show that in terms of the frequency of use, the guo-comparative is the dominant comparative construction, whereas the bi-comparative is borrowed from the standard language. Evidence from the wide distribution of the guo-comparative in contemporary Chinese dialects further suggests that the guo-comparative is native to these dialects and the marker guo has independently developed through metaphorical extension from a directional verb (cf. Output 8.1). 2. Early Wu, Mandarin and Cantonese all use topicalization and the disposal construction to place the patient preverbally, with early Wu preferring the use of topicalization, early Mandarin the use of the disposal construction and early Cantonese neither. Nevertheless, the frequency of the two constructions is low, in comparison with the use of VO sentences, thus showing that VO is the basic word order. Factors that trigger patient-preposing include the animacy of the agent and patient, the referentiality and the number of syllables of the patient and ease of processing (cf. Outputs 8.3 and 8.4). 3. Cantonese preverbal and postverbal dak express the meaning of “only”, a meaning that neither dak conveys in early Cantonese. The frequent co-occurrence of both daks and a restrictive element enables daks to acquire a restrictive meaning. On the other hand, the extreme low frequency of the use of postverbal dak to express “only” suggests that the two daks are not derivationally related (cf. Output 8.2). 4. Me is a question marker in early Cantonese, which has significantly picked up a discourse marker function since 1960s. On the other hand, the pronunciation mi found in some early Cantonese texts for this sentence-final particle sheds light on its origin, i.e. VP-m ‘negative’ + ni ‘sentence-final particle’ > mi > me (cf. Output 8.5) 5. In contemporary Cantonese and Hakka, the adverb xian ‘first’ is used both preverbally and postverbally. However, preverbal xian is found in both early dialects but postverbal xian is observed only in early Cantonese. The distribution of postverbal xian in contemporary Hakka dialects illustrates that it is not widely used, thus suggesting that such usage might have been borrowed from Cantonese (cf. Output 9.2). 6. The disposal construction, which characterizes Mandarin, is more frequently used in Bible translations than pedagogical materials in early Cantonese, Shantou and Shanghainese, a phenomenon which suggests that the former, under the influence of Mandarin, is less colloquial than the latter (cf. Outputs 8.3, 8.4 and 9.1).

16600215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16600215.value: This study focuses on one of the many facets of early Chinese dialects, namely, word order. To have a complete picture of how the early dialects have evolved into their contemporary counterparts, more work is yet to be done to reconstruct the history of each dialect. Moreover, the importance of a comparative approach should not be neglected as it allows us to identify changes induced by internal factors and those caused by external factors. Also, only two types of materials, i.e. Bible translations and pedagogical materials, are involved in the present study. Historical materials such as novels, short stories, newspaper, etc., however, have not been studied. A comparison of a single phenomenon across different types of historical materials will not only provide us with a more comprehensive picture of the early dialects. It will also enlighten us on the nature these different materials.

16600215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16600215.value: This study investigates issues pertinent to word order in Chinese dialects spoken between the 16th and early 20th centuries including the word order of the adjective and standard in the comparative construction, the verb and the object, and the verb and the adverb. While the change from adjective-standard to standard-adjective in Cantonese and Chaoshan Minnan and the change from adverb-verb to verb-adverb in Hakka are triggered by the influence of the dominant dialect, namely, Mandarin and Cantonese respectively, the change from verb-object to object-verb is triggered by multiple factors including the animacy of the agent and patient, the referentiality and the number of syllables of the patient and ease of processing. Moreover, grammaticalization and subjectification are responsible for the development of the directional verb guo ‘pass’ to the comparative marker and the development of the question marker me in Cantonese to a discourse marker. In Cantonese, while the frequent co-occurrence of the postverbal dak and a restrictive element has given rise to the expression of the “only” meaning of dak, that of the question marker me and a negative has led to the expression of a negative presupposition of me. Findings of the study are of great relevance to areas such as Chinese historical grammar, contact linguistics, the theory of grammaticalization and the typology of word order. This study also hopes to demonstrate how the historical materials help us reconstruct the history of Chinese dialects, which split from their parental language at different points of time, and the trajectory that they have travelled before they have taken shape.

16600515.label: Realisation of objectives
16600515.value: With GRF's generous support, all of my project objectives have been achieved. Through the case study of Gao Xingjian, I have delineated the impact of the philosophy of Daoism on modern and contemporary Chinese literature. In my article "Women and Dao in Gao Xingjian's Works," I have examined the interrelationship between women and Daoism in fictional representation by adding a feminist insight that inextricably connects the Daoist conception of nature with literary criticism. The reason I want to talk about women and Dao in Gao Xingjian’s works is that many studies are inclined to label Gao a misogynist writer. In his review of Soul Mountain, Kam Louie asserts that his “misogynist fantasies are resonant with traditional prejudices that saw young women as only one step from being swept away by the flood of sexual desire.” Less critically, some scholars respond that Gao’s representation of women is problematic because he focuses more on his own social and cultural identity, merely using women as the projection of his own anxiety and desire rather than truly sympathizing with women’s problems and fate. However, in the eyes of other scholars and critics, Gao Xingjian’s treatment of women’s images in his plays and fiction shed the didacticism of his aesthetic and philosophical models, allowing him to delve into female thinking and unconsciousness. Mabel Lee, for example, challenges the notion of Gao Xingjian’s perceived misogyny and provides alternative perspectives on his multilayered theatrical depictions of the female psyche. Drawing on the existing scholarly studies that have gone beyond the misogynist paradigm, I intend to explore the connection between the Zen Buddhist comprehension of Dao and the representation of women in Gao Xingjian’s novels and plays. As desire and sexual relationships play a very crucial part in the realm of Zen, the role of women is inevitably bound up with self-awareness and self-reflection, which are enshrined by Gao Xingjian as necessary on the path toward individual enlightenment. According to Gao, even if women’s roles are socially and culturally constructed or sometimes become a privileged trope of defying social convention, the truth that emerges from secular life often incorporates the spirituality into women’s unique biological and psychological construction, immune to men’s full understanding but inexorably furnishing a way leading to the state of Zen. In this article, I have achieved the objective of rewriting modern and contemporary Chinese literary history from the perspective of gender and Daoism. In addition, my article "Women and Dao in Gao Xingjian's Works" was included in my co-edited book with Mabel Lee. The new book's title is Gao Xingjian and Transmedia Aesthetics, published by Cambria Press in 2018. In this book, Mabel and I have reexamined some of the assumptions that underlie current cultural and literary studies. Previous studies on Gao Xingjian usually focus on particular areas of his fiction, plays, painting, film or poetry, or used his essays to explore his ideas on literature and creative aesthetics. This new book, which I have coedited with Mabel Lee, aims to cross the boundaries of these media, and to provide a comprehensive investigation of Gao Xingjian’s creations and ideas. The purpose of this is to showcase his transcultural, transdisciplinary, and transmedia explorations, and examine how he has persistently projected the struggles and agonies of the individual’s inner landscape into vivid images on stage, in films, in black-and-white paintings, and in the multilayered narrative expressions in fiction and poetry, and even in dance and music. Furthermore, this volume crosses the boundaries of traditional academic writing and takes the reader to the in-between spaces of different styles of writing, research, and commentary, which help us better understand Gao’s endeavors in literary, theatrical, and pictorial creation and their accompanying philosophical insights. The chapters in this book transgress the boundaries of different media and genres—fiction, drama, poetry, painting, film—in their deliberations, and these diverse approaches serve to broaden the scope of Gao Xingjian research through what can be described as a dimension of heightened freedom, that is suggestive of Chan Buddhist comprehension. Gao Xingjian often states that for him creative innovations emerge at boundaries and in-between space. The aim of this collection thus seeks to explore such boundaries and in-between spaces in academic research on Gao Xingjian. This new book is derived from this GRF project and has a very positive impact on the field of modern Chinese studies. Taking Gao Xingjian's multidisciplinary writing as a common thread, I not only reexamined the existing paradigm from the perspective of gender and Daoism but also extended my research to the field of transmedia studies.

16600515.value: The major research outcome of this project has resulted in my academic article "Women and Dao in Gao Xingjian's Works," which was published in both English and Chinese academic journals. The Chinese version of this article was published by Huawen wenxue, one of the refereed journals in China. The English version of this article was accepted for publication by Journal of Modern Literature in Chinese, which is one of the refereed journals in the field of Chinese Literature studies. In addition, this article was also included in my newly published book, Gao Xingjian and Transmedia Aesthetics, co-edited with Mable Lee and published by Cambria Press in 2018. This new book is derived from this GRF project and has a very positive impact on the field of modern Chinese studies. According to Professor Michel Hockx from the University of Notre Dame, this book "offers a valuable mixture of critical appreciations and scholarly essays dealing with the work of Gao Xingjian, the winner of the 2000 Nobel Prize for Literature. It adds significantly to our knowledge of Gao's oeuvre in all its complexity." According to Professor Carlos Rojas, "this exuberantly interdisciplinary volume examines Gao Xingjian's eclectic oeuvre from a variety of different perspectives, ranging from the aesthetic to the philosophy." Professor Song Weijie from Rutgers University states: "This fascinating, comprehensive, and important volume about Gao Xingjian forcefully presents the multilayered dimensions of Gao's diversified, contested, and connected literary and artistic world, and impressively covers a great range of different genres and styles from dramatic creations to fictional representations, ink painting to dance and music, and art exhibitions to cinematic poetry." Professor Song Mingwei praised the book as such: "The unique strength of this book lies in the variety of expertise and the wide range of disciplinary approaches that the authors bring to the study of Gao Xingjian, the playwright, the novelist, the poet, the painter, and the philosopher. It provides a panoramic view on Gao Xingjian's many talents through a well-orchestrated effort to examine the transmedia aesthetics that connect these talents." According to Professor Christopher Lupke from the University of Alberta, "Completed with an interview of the author, the broad range of subjects and intellectual approaches ensures this book will be of great interest to modern scholars of Chinese and comparative literature as well as those studying Gao Xingjian for generations to come."

16600515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16600515.value: I plan to further develop my research on the modern Chinese writer Jia Pingwa, who has written a novel Daideng, which can also be analyzed from the perspective of the interrelationship between women and Dao in fictional representation. I have published a Chinese essay on this topic, which was published by the famous Chinese intellectual journal, Dushu. Since this article was written as a scholarly essay, it is fine for me to develop it into an English academic article in the future based on my research of this GRF project.

16600515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16600515.value: With GRF's generous help, I have achieved all of my objectives and successfully reexamined the interrelationship between women and Daoism in fictional representation. The research has resulted in a refereed journal article entitled "Women and Dao in Gao Xingjian's Works." More importantly, it generated my edited English book with Mabel Lee, Gao Xingjian and Transmedia Aesthetics, which has already been published by Cambria Press in March 2018. In this book, not only did I focus on the topic of gender and Daoism, but I also extended my research to the transdisciplinary, transcultural, and transmedia studies of Gao Xingjian. It has significantly broadened the scope of my research. This book has received many praises in the field of modern Chinese literature.

16600615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16600615.value: The dramatic economic and social changes in China have inspired many social scientists to assess the impact of these changes on the welfare of different social groups. Most of the literature, however, tends to focus on the changing effects of political capital and human capital on economic inequality, and more recently, on the role played by specific institutional arrangements such as the household registration system and the work unit system. Despite the fact that China’s 55 ethnic minorities have historically trailed the Han majority in terms of a variety of socioeconomic indicators, scholars of Chinese stratification, with a few exceptions, have rarely paid attention to how ethnic minorities fare in a rapidly changing society. This project aims to provide a comprehensive study of ethnic socioeconomic stratification in contemporary China, based on data from a series of population censuses and a mini-census. Specifically, the project plans: (1) to examine the temporal trend in spatial and occupational segregation of ethnic minorities relative to the Han in China from 1982 to 2010, and their association with other macro-level social forces, such as regional development and population migration, etc; (2) to analyze socioeconomic disparities between ethnic minorities and the Han and to evaluate the effectiveness of China's ethnic autonomous policy in reducing ethnic inequality; and (3) to investigate the trend in inter-group marriage between ethnic minorities and the Han Chinese and the implications for ethnic assimilation and stratification. The project will provide a solid analysis of the changing patterns of ethnic inequality and an in-depth understanding of the mechanism of the changes, especially the roles played by the state/government ethnic policies. Such a comprehensive study will not only fill an important gap in the literature on Chinese social stratification in particular and comparative studies of ethnic stratification in general, but also will help to develop evidence-based policies to address ethnic issues that have been posing great challenges to China's social stability in recent years. 中國急劇的經濟和社會轉變，已經激發了許多社會科學家去評估這些轉變對不同社會群體在生活福利上的影響。可是，大多數文獻往往把重點放在政治資本和人力資本如何改變經濟不平等，以及較近期的是，特定制度安排（如戶籍制度系統和單位制度系統）所發揮的作用。儘管國內55個少數民族在各項社會經濟指標上長久以來一直落後於漢族，但研究中國分層的學者卻甚少關注少數民族在這樣一個瞬息萬變的社會的境遇如何。 本項目依據一系列的全國人口普查和小型普查數據，針對民族社會經濟分層作全面的研究。具體計劃如下： (1) 研究從1982至2010年間，少數民族相對於漢族的空間和職業隔離趨勢，以及與其他宏觀社會力量，如地區發展和人口遷移等的關聯；(2) 分析少數民族與漢族之間在社會經濟上的差距，評估中國民族自治政策對減低民族不平等的效果；(3) 探討少數民族與漢族之間跨民族婚姻的趨勢，以及其對民族同化和分層的含意。 本項目將對種族不平等的轉變模式進行扎實的分析並深入理解其轉變機制，特別是國家／政府的民族政策所扮演的角色。這一全面的研究不僅能够填補中國社會分層文獻和民族分層比較研究上的一個重大缺口；亦有助於制定以實證爲基礎的政策，解決近年來一直挑戰中國社會穩定的民族問題。

16600615.value: With the funding support from the project, I hire a research assistant/post-doc to assist me in managing the large-scales census data. I have published two papers in Journal of Contemporary China and China Review, respectively, and have addressed the first tow objectives to a large extent. The third objective is delayed because the access to census database was disrupted (online submission of SAS program to run the data). The PI has managed to gain access to the data but need on-site tabulation in Beijing, which have caused much inconvenience. Moreover, the geo-code information in the new census data has been removed and some research plans cannot be carried out, as originally planned. Nevertheless, the PI has been exploring alternative way to achieve the final objective through on-site tabulation at a data center at Tsinghua University, Beijing. It will take more time than expected. Meanwhile, with the support from the project, I also published several papers on social stratification in China based on the census data, though they are not directly related to the ethnic stratification (e.g. gender stratification during China's market transition). All together, the studies have help me theorize the stratification dynamics in post-socialist China.

16600615.label: Major findings and research outcome
16600615.value: In the article "Changing Ethnic Stratification in Contemporary China," we investigate the temporal trend in the socioeconomic differentials between ethnic minorities and the Han majority in China. Data from a series of population censuses and a mini-census show that, while the regional distribution of ethnic minorities remained stable from 1982 to 2005, occupational segregation and educational disparities between minorities and the Han increased over time. Multivariate analysis of data from the 2005 mini-census further reveals that ethnic minorities were disadvantaged in earnings in urban labor markets compared to the Han, especially those minorities in the private sector and in self-employment. we show substantial heterogeneity among ethnic minorities in their socioeconomic relationship with the Han and presents a comprehensive picture of how various ethnic minorities have fared in the course of China’s economic transition. In the article "Ethnic Autonomy and Ethnic Inequality: An Empirical Assessment of Ethnic Policy in Urban China", we examined socioeconomic disparities between ethnic minorities and the Han majority in China, focusing on the role played by regional ethnic autonomy. Based on a large sample of China’s mini-census data collected in 2005, we found that among nonfarm working populations, minorities are more likely than the Han to become managers/professionals or obtain high-status occupation, regardless of whether they are living in their own autonomous jurisdiction or other places. Minorities are paid lower wages, however, even after controlling for other characteristics, and the gap is even wider in autonomous jurisdictions than elsewhere. Finally, children of mixed Han-minority marriages in ethnic autonomous jurisdictions are more likely to identify themselves as minorities, especially those holding urban registration status (hukou) whose parents have received more schooling. Our findings bear important implications for the current debate on ethnic policy in China.

16600615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16600615.value: Based on the studies that have been carried out and the ongoing analysis and inter-marriage between ethnic minorities and the Han Chinese, future work may need to focus on specific regional/local context to understand the ethnic relationship and ethnic inequalities with survey data beyond census data currently used. The studies of ethnic stratification, together with gender stratification, have contributed to further theorization of the post-socialist stratification dynamics in China (see the 2019 article in the Annual Review of Sociology).

16600615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16600615.value: The project is the first of its kind to describe ethnic stratification with large scale census data with detail geocode information, and evaluate the ethnic policy and findings can be engaged in the debate on policy towards ethnic regions in China.

16600715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16600715.value: 通過客戶的拒絕來建立信任

16600715.label: Project Objectives
16600715.value: Introduce a novel mechanism for the client to monitor the credence-good seller and for the credence-good seller to build his reputation. According to this mechanism, the clients monitor the expert’s honesty by rejecting his service. Fully characterize the optimal equilibria, namely equilibria that yield the credence-good seller the highest profit, and identify precisely the conditions under which the credence-good seller is monitored by the clients’ rejection of his service. We analyze how the efficiency of the most profitable equilibrium changes in the extent to which expert values his reputation and the relative likelihood that the client’s problem is serious instead of minor. Analyze how reputation concern shapes the expert’s optimal pricing and recommendation strategies. Generate interest among economists in more closely examining the reputation-building of credence-goods sellers. Our model is relatively simple and additional elements can be easily added to enrich the model either by us or others. We also hope that the validity of our model will be verified by experiments.

16600715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16600715.value: Services by experts such as doctors, lawyers and car mechanics are considered credence goods because a client has to rely on experts for diagnosis and treatment, and once her problem is successfully treated, the client cannot tell whether she really needed the service. Experts have a natural incentive to prescribe expensive treatment whose cost exceeds its benefit to the client. Sellers of experience goods build their reputation through their customers’ satisfactory consumption of their products or services. However, this reputation mechanism is ineffective for credence goods sellers. The client can no longer find out whether an expert has made an honest recommendation once she accepts the expert’s recommended services and has her problem treated. Instead, reputation can be built through clients’ rejection of experts’ recommendation of an expensive treatment. Only through rejecting the expensive treatment recommendation and suffering the consequence, the client can verify whether her problem is as serious as the expert has stated. In this project we build a fully dynamic game of expert services in which a long-lived expert serves a sequence of short-lived clients. In each period, a client arrives in the marketplace and needs the expert to diagnose and fix her problem. The expert chooses prices for his services and a recommendation policy which specifies the type of treatment recommended to the client conditional on her problem. The client decides whether or not to accept the expert’s recommendation. We characterize the optimal equilibrium, i.e., equilibrium which yields the expert the highest profit. The optimal equilibrium is one of two classes: the one-price-fix-all equilibrium in which all problems are treated at a single price, and the monitoring-by-rejection equilibrium in which the client rejects the expert’s recommendation of the expensive treatment with a positive probability. Our objective is to fully characterize the optimal equilibria for all interesting parameter cases and then precisely identify the conditions under which the monitoring-by-rejection equilibrium is optimal. We show that when the expert is sufficiently concerned about his future profits, the monitoring-by-rejection equilibrium approximates the first-best profit and dominates the one-price-fix-all equilibrium in profitability. Our preliminary analysis strongly suggests that there is a wide range of parameter cases in which monitoring-by-rejection is optimal. 由例如醫生，律師，汽車修理工等專家提供的服務被認為是信任商品，因為客戶必須依靠專家進行診斷和治療，而且一旦客戶的問題給解決了，她就無法知道她是否真的需要該服務。專家們自然有動機建議昂貴的治療，即使治療成本超過其對客戶好處。體驗商品的賣家，通過客戶消費他們的產品或服務的滿意度來建立他們的聲譽。然而，這種信譽機制對於信任商品賣家是無效的。客戶一旦接受了專家推薦的服務，並把她的問題解決了，她就不再能判斷專家是否已作出了誠實的建議。相反，專家可以通過客戶拒絕其昂貴的治療建議來建立信譽。這是因為通過拒絕昂貴的治療建議及承擔不解決問題的後果，客戶可以驗證她的問題是否如專家說的那麼嚴重。 在這個研究項目中，我們建立了一個完全動態的模型，一個長壽命的專家給一序列短暫的客戶端提供服務。在每一期，一個客戶到達的市場，需要專家來診斷和修復她的問題。專家選擇服務的價格，以及一個推薦政策。這推薦政策決定了專家在客戶有不同的問題之下所推薦的治療。在專家提出建議後客戶決定是否接受該專家的建議。我們刻畫了最佳的均衡，即給與專家最高利潤的均衡。最佳的均衡是兩類之一：（一）"一價全修復"均衡，及（ii）"通過拒絕來監控"均衡。在第一類均衡裡，專家訂下一個價格並以這個價格來解決所有顧客的問題。在第二類均衡裡，客戶以某個概率來拒絕專家所提出昂貴的治療建議。我們的目標是在所有感興趣的參數的情況下找出最佳的均衡點，然後準確地識別在什麼條件下，"通過拒絕來監控"均衡是最佳。我們指出，當專家足夠關注他的未來利潤，"通過拒絕來監控"均衡讓專家獲得接近最優的利潤和比"一價全修復"均衡裡獲得的利潤高。我們的初步分析有力地表明，存在一個寬範圍的參數的情況，"通過拒絕來監控"均衡是最佳的。

16600715.label: Realisation of objectives
16600715.value: Regarding Objective 1, we have successfully introduced a novel mechanism for the client to monitor the credence-good seller and for the credence-good seller to build his reputation. Exactly as stated in the objective, the clients monitor the expert’s honesty by rejecting his service. We demonstrated this mechanism both in a monopoly and competitive setting. In a monopoly setting, rejection leaders to undertreatment and in the competitive setting, rejection leaders to costly search for second opinions. Regarding Objective 2, in our fully dynamic game, the set of equilibria is large and possible equilibria can be very complex. Yet, we are able to fully characterize the set of optimal equilibria, or equilibria in which the expert earn the highest profit. Applying the method pioneered by Abreu, Dilip, David Pearce, and Ennio Stacchetti (1990), we are able to show that one of two equilibria maximizes the expert's payoff: one-price-fix-all equilibrium or monitoring-by-rejection equilibrium. This finding is reported as Proposition 3 in our paper. In Proposition 4, we fully characterize the respective conditions under which these equilibria are optimal. Following the tradition of applied repeated games, we focus on analyze on the optimal equilibria stated in Objective 2. With that, we are able to fully predict of the expert's pricing and recommendation strategies for all possible discount factors. Therefore, we have also fully achieved Objective 3. We also extend our analysis to a competitive setting and characterize a natural class of equilibrium for the case when the search cost is not large. As it is clear from the statement of Objective 4, it is a long-term goal of generating interesting among economists for our novel mechanism of reputation building in credence goods market. Therefore, it is not realistic fully achieve that within the project period. On the other hand, we have already presented out work in several high-quality international conferences in front of leading scholars and raised many people's interest. Under the guidance of PI, his PhD student Xiaoxiao Hu has also written a high quality paper in a dynamic-game credence good setting. So, our assessment is that we have completed 60% of our objective, and given the long-term nature of this objective, we hope this progress is reasonable.

16600715.label: Major findings and research outcome
16600715.value: We study trust building in credence goods markets in a dynamic setting. An extreme lemon problem arises in the one-shot game and results in no trade. In the repeated game, an expert’s honesty is monitored through consumers’ rejection of his recommendations. The expert’s proﬁt in the optimal equilibrium weakly increases in the discount factor but cannot achieve the ﬁrst best, which contrasts sharply with the optimal equilibrium in experience goods markets. Competition enhances eﬃciency by allowing consumers to search for second opinions after rejecting the ﬁrst treatment recommendation, but the eﬃciency gain comes at the cost of less honesty. --- We have presented our research in many high-quality international conferences and academic institutions, including (i) 2017 European Econometric Society Meeting, (ii) 2018 Canadian Economic Theory Conference, (iii) Annual Columbia-Duke-MIT-Northwestern IO Theory Conference 2018, (iv) 2018 HKUST IO Conference, (v) 2018 International Conference of Industrial Economics at Zhejiang University. The paper is also currently under review of leading general interest journal American Economic Journal: Microeconomics

16600715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16600715.value: There is clear potential for future research on dynamic models of credence goods. We can extend our analysis in many dimensions in the future. For instance, we can consider imperfect diagnosis or costly diagnosis. We can allow the expert to charge a fee for diagnosis. We only study a setting under the assumption of Liability. We can also study a setting under the assumption of Verifiability. The PI is also supervising his PhD student Xiaoxiao Hu on the project "Verifiability and Fraud in a Dynamic Credence Goods Market". The PI and Co-I would continue to make contribution to the credence goods literature predominantly conducting research using dynamic settings.

16600715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16600715.value: We study how sellers of credence goods, such as experts and professional services providers, build their reputation for honesty in a repeat-purchase setting. Often time, credence good sellers or experts may exaggerate the severity of their clients' problems to overcharge them. If the clients always follow an expert's advice, even if their problem gets fixed every time, they are not able to tell whether the expert's treatment was excessive and a cheaper treatment could have fixed their problems. As a result, it could be difficult for experts to gain consumers' trust. In our study, we show that under certain conditions, an expert can more effectively build his reputation by inducing his clients to reject his services sometimes, even though doing so leave some problems untreated. The reason is that only after the client rejects the expert's recommended treatment and suffers the consequence, the client can really tell the the expert was honest and that she should have listened to the expert. The significance of our finding is that, unlike experience goods, full efficiency in credence good markets cannot be achieved even if credence good sellers care their reputation and future payoffs.

16601615.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16601615.value: 詩與照：現代中國的圖文互動、情感地圖

16601615.label: Project Objectives
16601615.value: To reconstruct the history and significance of the practices of writing about and inscribing poems on photographs, as well as the interaction between photos and poetic texts, thereby significantly enriching our knowledge of the literature and visual culture of the late Qing and Republican eras. To address issues of how portrait photography was understood and utilized in China’s flourishing urban culture, and how traditional aesthetics and concepts were employed in adopting and indigenizing this new visual technology. To explore the theoretical implications with regard to image and text, and to contextualize these practices and writing in their places in modern culture as well as the world history of photography.

16601615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16601615.value: Conceived as an interdisciplinary study in literature and visual culture, this book-length project will examine the complex interactions between poetry and photography beginning with the early reception of photographic technology in China at the end of the nineteenth century up to the Republican era. The project will investigate the intriguing artistic practice of inscribing poems on photographs or composing poems about photographic images. This newly forged relationship between image and text, and the subsequent dissemination of photographs with poems throughout literati and artistic communities, created a common public platform as well as a new route for communication and empathetic resonances. Through a survey of pictorial magazines, photo albums, and poetry anthologies, the project will delve into fundamental conceptual issues regarding sight, consciousness, and the social life of emotion, all of which were brought into play at this very moment of visual and verbal encounter. The critical questions that I intend to address include: how visual images and texts became sites where issues of the real and the disguised were conflated, and the tropes of visual truth and illusion were interlocked; in what ways photography—as distinct from traditional painting—challenged and altered the viewing/writing subject’s mode of thinking about and experiencing the world; how classical poetry negotiated a variety of intermedia and intercultural exchanges so as to accommodate this “realistic” vogue as instigated by photographic and print technology; when poets confronted these photographs, how did they understand and conceptualize the self and the body; and how photos and poems were circulated and exchanged as gifts, which may provide insight into the changing cultural norms and emotional life of the era. Further, this book project will also examine fascinating practices of photographic culture, i.e., using the new visual technology to experiment with different representations of the multiple or idealistic self, the real and the spectral, and of nudity, all of which helped to further blur the boundaries between truth and artifice, and fantasy and reality. Poetic sources offer us an advantageous position to gain insights into these cultural practices. By detailing the various ways in which traditional ideas and forms were negotiated or set in conflict with the new visual culture, this project will demonstrate that the dynamics of image and text, mediating a range of emotions (romantic love, eroticism, empathy and friendship), were deeply implicated in the cross-cultural exchanges of technologies and power in the formation of Chinese literary and visual modernities. 本項目研究現代語境中的古典詩歌與照片之間的互動關系，關注新的視覺觀念、看與被看的行爲是怎樣跨過畋域滲透到傳統的詩歌寫作中去的；而已然典律化的本土文化實踐模式（吟詩、題畫、扮相等）又是如何與技術化的視覺景觀相結合來呈現或制約現代性的生命體驗；凝望的視野、複制的行爲背後, 隱含著怎樣的性別與文化的政治意義；世紀之初的文化人又是如何來理解真、幻、變等觀念。逾越東西方的界域、傳統與現代的時序,詩歌與視覺的結緣, 進以證成這一獨特的現代性經驗,以及新的文學、圖像與情感生産方式的開拓。這兩種截然不同的視覺與文字之媒，在錯亂的時序中的互動交鋒，在相擊相撞中激發出的層次豐富的美學與文化的意涵。

16601615.label: Realisation of objectives
16601615.value: This project commenced on September 1, 2015 and it was completed at the end of February, 2019. During the first half of this period, I made research trips to Shanghai Library, Fudan Library, National Library in Beijing, the British Library in London, the Library of Congress in Washington DC, Harvard Yenching Library, as well as other libraries to locate scattered materials and engage in the intensive archival research necessary for my bringing my project to completion. After exploring a significant number of pictorial magazines and photograph albums, I have gained a good grasp of urban culture, the image and text relationship of the eras, as well as photographic practices in comparative perspectives. These materials include, in particular, Victorian photography, Western manipulated photography, and Western spirit photography. During the latter half of the grant period, I devoted myself to researching the materials and, most importantly, to writing about my findings. A full book manuscript, as the fruitful result of this research project, comprised of 125,000 words and 100 image inserts, will be published by Columbia University Press. First of all, this book offers a coherent history of the practices of inscriptions and writing about photographs in modern China. By providing a historical account of the dynamics of word-image, this project has extensively investigated the interactions of verbal discourse and visual culture, which led to a new kind of representation, creativity, and aesthetic experience. In addition to the dynamics of image and text that were presented in the original proposal, I have also examined photo poetics in the light of media analysis to highlight its status as a between and intermediary space. Photo poetics is one such arena to investigate these intermedial configurations and cross-genre movements, with the special qualification that the diverse signification of intra- or inter-medium relations and dynamics remains open-ended. The concept of intermediality has guided me to situate the image/word in a specific historical context and to enact relational thinking between different media and the multiple levels of mediations among communities and their cultural spaces. By addressing the complexity among image, text, and (inter-)media, this project has investigated intermedial configurations, cross-genre movements, and multiple levels of mediation, all of which have contributed to the configuration of new visual perception, innovative forms of emotive communication, and literary and visual modernities. Secondly, this book addresses critical issues of how portrait photography was understood and utilized in China’s urban culture and how traditional aesthetic concepts and practices were employed in indigenizing this new visual technology. In the original proposal, I only noticed the fact that photography was referred to as shadow, illusion, and dream and the circulation of the emotions and friendships through photographs. These critical issues have been explored in great depth in various way in my subsequent work. As I mentioned in the mid-term report, the threads of the ideas about how religious ideas (those of Buddhism in particular) affected Chinese understandings of photographic images has been significantly developed in my research. I have argued that religious ideas about images substantially underpinned Chinese understanding of photographic images, which on many occasions were taken as manifestations of bodily images, icons, or traces. The Chinese lyric vision (revealed in lyrical inscriptions and Chinese lyrical understanding about the mind and the world) is materialized or remediated in images. Chinese practitioners, imbrued with lyricism, often defy the representational mode of artistic creation and the limits of the technical medium. Thirdly, I have further explored theoretical implications of image and text dynamics and offered a unique perspective and intervention into the world history of photography. When Chinese photographers dress up in costumes, use scissors to cut and combine images, or use blush to beautify an image, the contrived images and lyrical comments demonstrate the roles of subjectivity in the era of technological reproduction. While republican China is the primary focus, this study employs a comparative perspective. These delimited comparative discussions include the Western conceptualization of photography, the manipulations of portrait photographs and spirit photography, and the photograph and the text practice in the Victorian and post-Victorian eras. While the understanding of photography from Meiji Japan displays some similarity with their Chinese counterparts, Chinese practices of pictorialism and spirit photography were distinctive in many of their aspects. The project originally conceived of six chapters, but it has been expanded into seven chapters with broader scopes. Below is a brief summary of the final version of the book manuscript. Part I (Chapters 1 and 2) explores fundamental questions relating to the conceptualization of these new photographic visual images, i.e., the issue of illusion versus truth claims and the rise of self-consciousness in the practice of portrait photography. Practitioners, drawing upon crucial ideas of lyricism and Buddhist concepts to understand the medium’s representational power, continually challenged and negotiated the myth of transparency and objectivity in photography. Set free by imagination and aided by technology, they achieved creativity and a heightened modern self-consciousness through a refashioning of an array of self-images, which displayed a delicate balance between the pursuit of novelty and an adherence to convention. Part II (Chapters 3 and 4) offers a fresh understanding of the significance of affective objects and the gendered configurations in image/text dynamics. It charts the itinerary of the exchange of photographs among literati groups, the constant recycling of poetic tropes, and the circulation of stylized images of the beautiful woman, the skull, and the nude to reveal realms of affective response and social networking. Tracing the circulation of these photographs among friends and disciples casts new light on social networking and the topography of the emotions. These chapters explore issues surrounding the politics of the representation of the body to reveal unresolved tensions and conflicts between traditional gender ideology, the male gaze, and modern progressive ideas. Part III (Chapters 5, 6 and 7) elucidates the issue of illusion and the creative practices of photography through a portrayal of the outer world (e.g. landscapes) and its relation to the otherworld (e.g. spirits). It offers a previously unexamined way to understand Chinese intellectuals’ manipulation of and innovation with vision, illusion, and memory with an emphasis on composite photography and spirit photography. The General Research grant has greatly assisted me for my research trips, providing additional time for writing, and supporting the use of research assistants and publication subsidies, all of which have been essential for the successful completion of the project. I am tremendously grateful for the support that I have received. The RGC’s support has been acknowledged in the publication of two journal articles (in English and Chinese) and will be prominently acknowledged in the book Photo Poetics upon its publication.

16601615.label: Major findings and research outcome
16601615.value: This project has systematically documented the various ways in which traditional ideas, forms, and esteemed textual traditions were integrated, negotiated, or set in conflict with the new visual culture. The study demonstrates that a preeminent poetic tradition still exerted a strong hold in the modern era. In so doing, it reveals the roles of Chinese tradition in the formation of Chinese literary and visual modernities, an aspect often neglected in contemporary studies. Further, while late Qing Chinese were in awe of visual verisimilitude and began to embrace the camera’s evidentiary character in social uses, this study has shown how many Chinese practitioners used human agency and lyrical sensibility to overcome the constraints of the medium and its putatively transparent replication of reality. They exhibited a consistent proclivity to impose lyricism and aesthetics onto mechanical objectivity, transgressing the new media’s material limitations. These fascinating Chinese stories that I have told not only show the different reception and practices of photography, but they also shed light on the innovations and the conceptualization behind such innovations, thus contributing to the history of world photography. I have published two peer-reviewed articles in English and Chinese and will publish one single-authored monograph in English. The article “A Paper Mirror: Autobiographical Moments in Modern Chinese Poetry” has been published by the Journal of Chinese Literature and Culture from Duke University Press. I have also published one expanded version of Chinese article “重層的自我影像：抒情傳統與現代媒介” (Mirroring the Self: Chinese Lyrical Tradition and Modern Photography). It has appeared in Bulletin of the Department of Chinese Literature National Chengchi University in Taiwan. Most fruitfully, the book manuscript titled Photo Poetics: Chinese Lyricism and Modern Media, with the total word count of 125,000 and 100 image inserts, will be published by Columbia University Press.The Table of Content and the publishing agreement have been attached to this report in section 8. In addition, I presented my chapters and papers at the conferences, including the Association for Asian Studies Annual Meeting in March 2016, International Convention of Asia Scholars (ICAS) in June, 2017 in Chiang Mai, Thailand, the Image Conference in October, 2017 in Venice and American Comparative Literature Association Conference in March 2018 at UCLA. I was also invited to give the lectures relating to this project at the National University of Singapore in March 2016, Harvard University in November 2016, and Society of Fellows Lecture Series in March, 2018 at Hong Kong University.

16601615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16601615.value: I have started to prepare the Chinese edition of English monograph Photo Poetics. In order to reach a broader readership, I am planning to publish a Chinese edition in a style accessible to general readers, soon after the publication of the English edition, through recognized presses in mainland China and Taiwan. This will further disseminate and share my research findings with the general public, and help educate readers to more greatly appreciate the photographical practices and poetic culture of modern China. I have already given four well-received public lectures (two at the History Museum in Hong Kong, one at Harvard Chinese Culture Workshop, organized by Chinese Writers’ Association in North America, and one at the Boston Chinese Photography Association). Audience responses were enthusiastic and highly encouraging. This is a project that has larger social relevance and impact. I plan to continue to give public lectures at a variety of venues such as universities, museums, libraries, and local communities, and cater to the general public’s revived fascination with old photographs. After spending many hours for archival research, I have also collected some visual materials in late Qing and Republican eras that might be useful for my future research projects.

16601615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16601615.value: This is an interdisciplinary study in literature and visual culture in modern China. This GRF project, realized in a single-authored monograph in English titled Photo Poetics, presents the first comprehensive examination of the complex interactions between poetry and photography from the end of the nineteenth century to the Republican era. Through an extensive examination of pictorial magazines, photo albums, and poetry anthologies, this book delves into fundamental conceptual issues regarding vision, intermediality, and the social life of emotion, all of which were brought into play at the very moment of China’s new visual encounter. The book offers a coherent narrative of the history and significance of the practices involved in the interaction between photographic images and poetic texts, thereby significantly enriching our knowledge of the literature and visual culture of the late Qing and Republican eras. This investigation of a significant number of original sources and previously neglected cultural practices, the very first monograph of its kind, will not only fill a critical lacuna in the studies of modern Chinese literature and the history of Chinese photography, but will also contribute to ongoing theoretical discussions regarding the relations and tensions between image and text, intermediation and visual poetics.

16602015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602015.value: Through the use of an optimal scaling method to calibrate a set of internationally comparable occupational categories, the proposed study will attempt to determine to what extent that there is indeed a universal occupational hierarchy that does not differ much over time and/or location. The methodology to be applied was developed by the PI and it is extremely versatile and has a number of desirable properties preferable to those of previous measures. It provides standard errors for the rankings of individual occupations, the ability to test formally whether specific sets of occupations have equal rankings, and, most importantly, the provision that permits these estimated scores can vary and thereby the ability to conduct a formal test as to whether a universal ranking hierarchy indeed exists. Drawn largely from data collected from the Integrated Public Use Microdata Series (IPUMS) International Project at the Minnesota Population Center and other publicly available census or census-like data, this project proposes to study 10 countries, providing 25 data points between 1990 and 2010. The study will also compare and examine the relative importance of economic development, political and cultural development, and individual idiosyncrasies in accounting for country-specific and temporal differences. The proposed project is a continuation of another RGC-funded project on the temporal changes in the occupational structure of the United States. Together, the findings from both studies will address an important topic in social stratification research regarding the invariance of socioeconomic hierarchy, commonly known as the Treiman constant in stratification literature. 本研究將使用最完善的量度方法，設定一套客觀並具國際適調性的職業類別系統， 以探討職業排名是否如傳統理解般，具有跨國和跨時空的穩定性，普世不變。本研 究用以計算和比較的統計模式，由首席研究員開發，極為靈活，優點甚多，除包括 取締採用主觀聲望方法來釐定排名、提供個別職業排名的標準誤差以便評審個別職 業是否具有同等排名以外，最重要的是，允許個別地方和時空數據存有差異，從而 正式測試職業排名是否普世不變。透過正式統計模式，這測試能確定和評估其中差 異的真確性，更有助瞭解背後成因。本研究的數據來自美國明尼蘇達州人口中心的 國際普查資料庫，研究將採用共十個國家提供的廿五個數據點作分析，數據取自約 一九九零至二零一零年間。研究也將比較和分析經濟、政治和文化發展可否解釋職 業排名的差異。本硏究可說是另一個由教資會資助首席研究員進行、關於美國職業 排名變化的研究的延伸。總括而言，兩個研究累積的成果，將對社會分層研究作出 重大貢獻，徹底釐清職業排名的不變性，加深我們對被稱為特雷曼常數的了解及分 析。

16602115.value: 流失創新的企業家人才是新興市場需面對的問題。因此發展中國家必須尋求重獲流失的人才和技術的辦法。本研究著眼於三個國家 --- 土耳其、印度和中國的兩個主要回流群體：學者和企業家。 很少國家能於這兩個領域同時取得成功：印度成功鼓勵海外企業家回來開店，土耳其則有較多學者回國。借鑒崔大偉教授比較熟悉的中國經驗，本研究將探討這三個國家的成功和失敗因由。 何以中國能成功拉回許多頂尖企業家回國工作？通過帶回國內匱乏的海外的技術，，中國的企業家們賺取了國外這無法給予的巨額利潤。與此同時擴大了中國的技術前景。 在海外學習生活的印度裔技術人才是否出於同樣原因回流？如果是的話，他們可能會大大改進印度的技術水平。抑或他們是為了聘請印度本土高水平的科技工作者們，去開發出口電腦軟件？ 中國仍未能吸引特高水平的中國海外研究專才回流。於２００７年，中國博士生逗留美國的比率是91％，為全球最高。原因之一是中國的「政治化」研究文化──院校通常給予人事網絡夠廣的學者較多獎勵，而非因工作質量。為了深入了解中國，我們將研究成功吸引有才華學者回國的土耳其。他們大多數湧向已建立西方式的研究文化的私立大學。事實上，民辦高校只招受過海外教育的學者。然而土耳其的海歸學者也回到更為「政治化」的公立大學，因此我們反思，大學的地位會否影響海歸的工作質量？對海歸來說，回不回國是否取決於學術機構的研究文化？如果是的話，“政治”文化是否決定性的不利？我們希望在研究土耳其的研究風氣對回流學者的影響的同時，明白同樣在影響中國回流學者的要素。

16602115.label: Realisation of objectives
16602115.value: While we were unable to truly gauge the nation-wide return rate of entrepreneurs to India, my Turkish team and I were able to find many academic returnees and able to better gauge that number for Turkey. We carried out detailed surveys in three cities in India, as promised, using the questionnaire used in China in 2004. We also interviewed Turkish returnees and were able to understand their motives for returning and their overall disappointment at having returned in light of the political changes in the country. We did discover that technology does play a role in reverse migration in India, but the situation is different than in China, as much of the focus of India's reverse migration of technology is to use the Indian skilled labour force to work on new technologies that can be exported. According to our interviews, the domestic market in India was simply not developed enough to need all this foreign technology. We have already done all the statistical analysis of the data set from India, and have supplemented our observations with the field research of Dr. Kellee Tsai, who has also done research on India and its Diaspora. We have submitted a joint paper entitled “State Absenteeism in India’s Reverse Migration? A Comparison with the Chinese Experience,” to the journal, World Development. We are waiting to hear back from them. Problems publishing Turkish findings.

16602115.label: Major findings and research outcome
16602115.value: On Turkey, we found that many people returned in the mid-2000s, when the political system was undergoing a liberalization, and academics felt positively about Turkey's future. Many also returned because their family members had been forced to post a bond on their behalf which would have been confiscated by the state if they had not returned. Unlike in China, many returnees to Turkey only received an MA overseas before returning to Turkey to get their PhD. No one in China ever did this. Many may return after just getting an MA, but if they want a PhD, they would stay abroad. This pattern is unheard of in the China case and may reflect why Turkish academia and science has not progressed as far as Chinese despite the fact that so many Turks have studied abroad. Simply too many Turks get local PhDs. The reverse migration of Turks with overseas MAs may have been because families had to post financial bonds on behalf of their relatives to facilitate their overseas education. After the current president cracked down after the failed coup of 2016--we can document the impact of the coup on returnees’ views--many people wanted to leave the country, either in the short- or long-term. But most academics were not good enough to find spots overseas. We discovered nepotism in Turkish universities, as many returnees were hired by the university where they received their undergraduate degrees. Our research on India became less focused on technology transfer as a motivation for reverse migration; instead, we illuminated the comparative role of the Chinese versus the Indian state in facilitating reverse migration. While the Indian state was either predatory or absent, the Chinese "developmental" state helped returnees succeed. Also, returnees’ attitudes in the two countries towards the state varied in line with the actions of the respective state. The differences in the roles of the two states affected how they dealt with their Diasporic entrepreneurs. While Chinese officials in the consulates actively recruited Chinese entrepreneurs to help China, the Indian entrepreneurs were left on their own, but developed their own associations overseas.

16602115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16602115.value: The data from India can still be used for another paper on regional variations and reverse entrepreneurship. We have submitted a paper comparing the role of the state in India and China and, while we have not heard back from the journal as yet, we intend to publish this paper. The entire issue with Turkey is whether there will be a political thaw that will allow us to publish our findings. I am currently worried that the negative nature of our findings--that people want to leave, that academics oppose the President--can all create serious problems for Dr. Akman, should we publish our findings. One question I would like to pursue is whether Turks who received overseas PhDs, as compared to those who received local PhDs, were better scholars, as they received the most significant part of their academic training abroad.

16602115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16602115.value: Many Turks returned to take up academic posts in the mid-2000s, when the political system was liberalizing and academics felt positively about Turkey's future. Many also returned because family members had been forced to post a bond on their behalf which would be confiscated by the state if they did not return. In this sense, Turkey is much more authoritarian than China. However, after the intense crackdown that followed the failed political coup in 2016--we did interviews before and after the coup--many people began looking to leave the country, either in the short- or long-term. But because many academics could not easily find spots overseas, they were trapped. We also discovered serious nepotism in the hiring of faculty; most academics returned to the university where they received their undergraduate degrees. Such a policy creates internal fighting within universities and undermines academic development. Our research on India became less focused on technology transfer as a motivator for reverse migration, but instead the research illuminated comparative role of the Chinese versus the Indian state in facilitating reverse migration. Thus we found that the Indian state was largely absent, with the local government being largely predatory, while the Chinese state was developmentalist at both levels.

16602315.label: Project Objectives
16602315.value: Compile and analyze a ‘big’ database of individual and household wealth, events, and categories from village and county archives in Shanxi and Heilongjiang Provinces. Locate and transcribe county archival data from the three main revolutionary base areas of Shanxi Province, to compare with the data already transcribed from Shuangcheng. The RCCSH has already partially collected similar data from as many as eight counties, and can provide resources for more systematic collection. Transcribe household class registers from the Four Clean-ups Movement into coded databases. The RCCSH collection already includes such registers for over 350 production teams and roughly 10,000 households from 60+ administrative village archives. Examine the social and political processes involved in the redistributions of wealth and social leveling that took place in Heilongjiang and Shanxi during the 1945-1965 period through land reform and rural collectivization. Answer such basic questions as who got what, and why. In addition to an eventual book monograph comparing the processes of land reform and rural collectivization in North and Northeast China, write several articles in both Chinese and English peer-reviewed journals summarizing our preliminary findings.

16602315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602315.value: 本项目拟以1945-1965年 黑龙江、山西两省的经验为基础， 探讨建国初期农村社会革命的模式与实践。这二十年内的 土地改革与农村集体化不仅是二十世纪最伟大的社会实验 之一，而且还是历史上最大规模的财富再分配实践之一。 尽管如此，半个世纪后的今天，我们对这一重大事件的理 解仍基于特定目击者的叙述和官方挑选出的少数地点的调 查报告等有限资料。通过近些年在东北地区开展的档案收 集工作，我们发现就这场宏大的农村社会革命的微观过程 来说，更系统、更全面的资料是存在的，依托这些资料， 学者们可以深入探究对这一时期的更多历史问题，形成新 的历史理解和认识。本项目拟在东北资料收集的基础上， 从黑龙江省扩大到华北的山西省，收集并分析相关的地方 档案和历史资料，经过对土改与集体化微观过程的客观分 析，对重新认识现代中国的社会发展与财富分配打基础。 以前关于土地改革与农村集体化的研究基于高度选择性的 资料。与此相比，本项目拟利用华北、东北几百个村庄的 系统性个人、家庭资料进行分析。研究人员已在黑龙江省 双城县县档案馆发现类似的资料，包括土改时期全县90个 行政村的8,000个人登记表及80,000户的划分阶级成份档案 。这种覆盖全县的资料能够分析空间和时间上的土改运动 模式，而比较各村的土改运动实践。本项目试图在山西省 收集、量化、分析及比较类似的县级档案资料。 与此同时，本项目也拟以山西大学中国社会史研究中心已 收集的山西省200村庄在40个县的村级档案资料与黑龙江省 的县级资料（Noellert 2014）进行农村社会革命的比较研究 。我们已开始将60个村庄200多个生产队四清时期阶级成份 登记表进行量化。这些登记表详细地记载着各家 的家庭历 史，描述每个家庭二十世纪上半期各个阶段的社会经济状 况。这种资料能够补充双城县县档案所记载较为广泛的农 村社会革命模式，以加 上山西农村集体化前20年的个人、 家庭的微观社会经济变迁。

16602315.label: Major findings and research outcome
16602315.value: The CSSCD series’ systematic records of individual and household experiences of communist land reform and rural collectivization will revolutionize our understanding of this transformative period of Chinese history. Previous understandings of this history have been based on national-level policy statements and select personal anecdotal accounts. The CSSCD is one of the first available sources of micro-level data on complete communities from mid-twentieth century China. Preliminary analysis of the CSSCD has yielded new findings on the social, economic, and political dynamics of life in a revolutionary society. Socially, our research has explored marriage patterns and kin relations to reveal complex social networks that challenge mainstream narratives of state regimentation and social revolution. Previous studies debate whether or not the Revolution was successful in restructuring patterns of marriage and family, but our research makes it possible to go further in exploring not just whether or not patterns changed, but how and why. Our study of marriage, for example, found that who people married in revolutionary China did not change as much as previously believed. Economically, our research has focused on changing patterns of personal wealth and its distribution, to suggest that the collectivization of agricultural wealth in particular encouraged the majority of the population to find new avenues for wealth accumulation and facilitated a rapid transformation to a more industrial economy. By equalizing the distribution of certain forms of wealth, this wealth could no longer be used as a means of distinction between households, which led to the emergence of other means of distinction like wage incomes, consumer goods, place of residence, and political status. Politically, our research has explored the institutionalization of class labels and changing processes of social inequality to complicate previous understandings of communist and authoritarian politics. China’s communist revolution emphasized socioeconomic equality, but this within-group equality only intensified political inequalities between groups of Party and non-Party, good and bad classes, and urban and rural populations.

16602315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16602315.value: Analysis of the CSSCD series is just beginning, and both the data and its analysis will continue to inspire further research for many years to come. The origins of twenty-first century China lay in the mid-twentieth century, and the CSSCD demonstrates that many rich sources of data from this period remain unexplored. We plan to both continue researching the CSSCD and promote the construction and expansion of similar databases to provide a more comprehensive understanding of this important stage of Chinese history.

16602315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16602315.value: This research project looks at the everyday experiences of people living in rural China during China’s communist revolution. What kinds of property people owned, where they worked, who they married, who were their relatives, and what was their political status are all central parts of people’s lives. In the mid-1960s, the state recorded how all of these parts changed over the course of the revolution for every single household and individual in multiple provinces. This information helps us understand not just what happened to the majority of people in communist China, but also what happens more generally to human societies that try to eliminate socioeconomic inequalities between different groups of people. Today in the twenty-first century many people around the world still condemn social inequalities and call for a more equal world, but mid-twentieth century communist China is one of the only historical examples of a society that has tried to make this equality a reality on a large scale. The goal of this research project is to learn from both the successes and failures of China’s communist social experiment.

17100015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100015.value: Habitat integrity, including size, quality and connectivity is essential for ensuring survival of free-ranging wildlife populations. It also provides a quantitative baseline for classifying the risk of extinction of a threatened species. However, facing many present-day anthropogenic impacts, this integrity is increasingly degraded at scales seldom anticipated and even less measured or monitored. In this project, we focus on the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin, a species with highly restricted inshore shallow-water distribution and narrow habitat selectivity; hence highly susceptible to adverse effects of human activities and the degradation of inshore habitats. Equipped with GIS techniques and long-term satellite imagery data, we will quantify the extent of habitat destruction, the scale of degradation of prominent physiographic features and the loss of dolphins' preferred habitats due to land reclamation and coast modification that took place in the Pearl River Estuary and off Taiwan west coast in the past four decades. We will compare this findings with historic, recent, and current sightings of humpback dolphins; and with their known behavioural preference of certain habitats. This will allow us to investigate the extent at which the coastal degradation and habitat destruction may have compromised the ecological requirements of humpback dolphins. This project will contribute new valuable insights into the population ecology of coastal delphinids in areas suffering from rapid habitat deterioration and major anthropogenic impacts. Few such studies have previously been attempted. Apart from advancing the science of biodiversity conservation, this project will provide valuable tools to quantifiably determine the effectiveness of past management practices and - especially valuable - will provide empirical bases for the delineation of future management strategies, which represents a central point in present-day applied conservation ecology. We anticipate that the data will reveal both large-scale and small gradual processes that may lead to alteration or even disappearance of prominent physiographic features, and will have a great value for any future research or monitoring programs involving humpback dolphins in Hong Kong and elsewhere in the region. We anticipate that this work will provide a valuable referential data source for other species of coastal delphinids elsewhere. Locally, in Hong Kong, the significance of this project has another important dimension, a direct applicability in the current (and future) efforts of implementing the Convention of Biological Diversity (CBD), especially as it pertains to constructing models of habitat protection and/or restoration and the preservation of a threatened population of coastal seas' iconic species.

17100015.label: Realisation of objectives
17100015.value: All objectives of the project have been fully achieved and in fact some of our work and findings extended beyond what has been initially proposed. Three peer-reviewed papers have been already published, another one is currently submitted (under peer-review) and two other are in an advanced stage of preparation for journal submission (submission intended for late-2019/early-2020). The paragraphs below summarise the realisation of our objectives and project outcome: • For the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin, an obligatory shallow water inshore species, the degradation of coastal habitats have major consequences for population persistence and distribution. Off Taiwan’s west coast (TWC), these animals are predominantly seen in two areas separated by a stretch of coast with only sporadic sightings. We quantified the extent of habitat destruction off TWC since 1972 using satellite images a habitat integrity index (HII). While early Landsat data reveal extensive continuity and diversity of coastal habitats, by 2013 over 23% of dolphin habitat and 40% of dolphin foraging habitat was lost to land reclamation. General linear model (GLM) analysis show a significant relationship between HII and sightings of dolphins per unit effort (SPUE), indicating that off TWC the current discontinuous distribution of humpback dolphins is due to a different extent of habitat degradation rather than natural patchiness of the environment. Our findings indicate that a recent environmental change off TWC limits the population connectivity. • In Hong Kong, using Landsat data, we quantified the scale and rate of land reclamation and coastal infrastructure projects since 1970s. Habitat Selection Function (HSF) of Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins was constructed to identify their habitat preference. Occurrence probabilities in the past (before major alterations) and future (when all currently planned projects are completed) were modelled to confirm the current impacts and identify potential future impacts. Since 1970, >4000 hectares of coastal humpback dolphin habitat were lost to land reclamation; the length of artificial shoreline has increased by 300%, reducing the proportion of natural shore from 90% to less than 65%. GLM analyses show that humpback dolphins prefer inshore areas <30m deep and they display strong affinity to natural shores (and, across larger spatial-scales, avoidance of artificial shores). The modelled projections of occurrence probability indicate that there has been a major drop of habitat usage near previous reclamation areas, and there will likely be a major decline in usage of current Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) in Hong Kong and the Pearl River Estuary (PRE) due to intended and soon-upcoming construction projects and alterations of coastal habitats. • In the PRE, humpback dolphins form multiple, closely interacting social clusters that have different core areas but overlapping ranges. The socio-spatial differences between individuals and clusters are most likely driven by fine-scale differences in the individual pattern of habitat choice and range use. Recently, two large-scale anthropogenic events, a massive construction project and change in coastal fisheries practices, had a notable impact on humpback dolphins in Hong Kong waters. During the construction of the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge, the dolphin range use pattern and their core areas in Hong Kong have shifted southwards, away from the construction zone. Their pattern of movement and social grouping has also changed. This environmental change and fine-scale dolphin response correspond closely to the projected long-term response indicated by our Habitat Selection Function models described above. In response to changes in fishery practices (the territory-wide ban on trawling), trawler-associating dolphins changed their residency pattern, and the associations between trawler-associating and non-trawler-associating dolphins increased. Both these anthropogenically-driven impacts affect the distribution and abundance of dolphin prey, supporting the hypothesis of habitat/resource-driven population structure of coastal/inshore dolphins, as recently quantified by our another recently completed study (by Stephen C.Y. Chan, a recent Ph.D. graduate under the PI's direct supervision, partially-supported by the PI's another RGC grant). • In Hong Kong, ~50% of the dolphins suffer from at least one type of epidermal lesions, likely related to anthropogenically degraded habitat. One in every ten dolphins has physical injuries indicative of vessel collisions, propeller cuts and fishing-gear entanglements. As obligatory inshore species and top predators with long lifespan, humpback dolphins are good ‘‘barometers’’ of marine environment and their compromised health conditions are symptomatic of increasingly degraded ecological conditions of coastal seas, especially in rapidly developing regions of fast-growing economies. • In coastal waters of the Pearl River Delta region, fishing pressure has been intense since at least late 1980s, which warrants concerns of the potential fishery-related impacts on the food resources and foraging ecology of humpback dolphins, the apex marine predator in this region. While the dolphins appear to be opportunistic foragers, our findings suggest a dietary shift in recent years, from demersal (as previously reported) to neritic fish. Furthermore, dolphin foraging group size has decreased in recent years, which corresponds to the decreasing size and number of primary prey species found during analyses of dolphin stomachs (the largest dolphin diet dataset anywhere in this species range). We suggest that these are indicators of declining food resources. Faced with a shortage of preferred prey, humpback dolphins have broadened their dietary spectrum to maintain their daily energy intake, while their foraging group size decreased in response to the altered tradeoff between the costs and benefits of group foraging. • In addition to the scope of work described in the original proposal, we conducted also eco-toxicological analyzes and assessed the spatiotemporal trends of the concentrations of 11 heavy metals in the liver and kidney of humpback dolphins across the PRE. The hepatic levels of Cr, As, and Cu in these dolphins were among the highest reported for cetaceans globally, and the levels of Zn, Cu, and Hg were sufficiently high to cause toxicological effects in some of the animals. Between same age-sex groups, dolphins from eastern PRE were significantly more contaminated with Hg, Se, and V than those from the western reaches of the PRE, while the opposite was true for Cd. The concentrations of Cu and Zn increased significantly in recent years, corresponding to the high input of these metals in the region. In contrast to the significant decrease in heavy metal levels in the dolphins in Hong Kong waters, the elevated metal exposure in the western PRE raises serious concerns. • Our findings indicate a severe inadequacy of current protection measures and insufficiency of environmental management in Hong Kong waters and the PRE. Furthermore, this project highlights the importance of the understanding of animal behaviour in spatial conservation zoning. The Incorporation of behavioural data into spatial modelling of animal movement helps in the understanding of the daily habitat use by the dolphins. In Hong Kong, foraging is the key determinant of the dolphins’ overall distribution pattern. With the application of Local Convex Hull (LoCoH) models, we identified dolphin core areas based on the frequency of visitations and their behavioural significance. Using this spatio-behavioural pattern quantified for humpback dolphins in Hong Kong waters, we developed a two-tier framework of Marine Protected Area (MPA) designation, with spatially-restricted strict marine reserves placed within a larger envelope of a coastal management zone. This approach is well-applicable to identify critical habitats and prioritise areas for conservation for humpback dolphins and other coastal cetaceans elsewhere.

17100015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17100015.value: Current findings provide an excellent basis for the development of conservation management strategy for this coastal flag-ship species in Hong Kong waters and more broadly in the Pearl River Delta region. A need for such scientifically-guided initiative has been voiced since late 1990s but up until recently sufficient scientific evidence was lacking. This successfully completed project (and previous RGC-funded projects by this same PI) carries a great potential for direct applicability and incorporation of its findings into current and future coastal management strategies in the region. However, as the PI's position at HKU was sabotaged in mid-2017 and he had to leave HKU in early 2018, this potential is unlikely to be realised.

17100015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100015.value: Habitat selection allows free-ranging animals to optimize prey and resource acquisition and reduce predation risk that ultimately enhances their fitness. This behavior facilitates also essential responses to short-term disturbances and long-term habitat deterioration. Coastal species such as the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin (known locally as the Chinese white dolphin) depend on shallow-water inshore habitats, which makes them susceptible to the changes in coastal environment, especially in areas such as Hong Kong and the Pearl River Delta (PRD) region where urbanization process is immense and rapid. Our findings indicate that immediate and focused responses are needed to restrict habitat deterioration. It also demonstrates the vulnerability of humpback dolphins to future developments and the urgent need to revise current conservation management strategies in Hong Kong and the PRD. We emphasize that the history of coastal habitat alteration must be considered when interpreting cetacean distribution from survey data and formulating habitat management decisions, especially in areas experiencing extensive anthropogenic coastal change. Furthermore, our data highlights the susceptibility of humpback dolphins to anthropogenic pressure. With their high-specificity to shallow-water inshore habitats and not yet fully understood but likely restricted degree of socio-behavioural plasticity, their ecological adaptability to environmental change is limited.
