17100715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100715.value: Staging of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients differs significantly from other cancers as the underlying liver disease has a significant impact on the prognosis. Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) staging classification is widely used in North America and Europe to guide the prognosis and treatment of HCC patients. Nonetheless, it is not commonly used in Asia as BCLC staging was developed mainly based on cohorts of predominantly hepatitis C infected patients, whereas in most Asia countries, HCC is mostly associated with endemic hepatitis B virus infection. Moreover, more aggressive treatment approaches for HCC is usually adopted in most Asia centres. Recently, our centre has developed a new prognostic staging system--Hong Kong Liver Cancer (HKLC) prognostic classification scheme. The scheme was constructed based on a large cohort of almost 4,000 consecutively diagnosed and treated patients. It classified patients into five main stages with distinct survival outcomes. When HKLC prognostic classification was compared with BCLC classification for performance, HKLC staging showed significantly better discriminatory ability than BCLC staging. More importantly, HKLC identified subsets from BCLC intermediate- and advanced-stage patients for more aggressive treatments than what were recommended in BCLC and led to better survival outcomes. Despite these provocative findings, the study was limited by its retrospective nature and was only a single-center study. We thus propose to conduct a prospective multicenter study to validate and compare the performance of HKLC staging classification with BCLC classification in an independent Chinese cohort. This study shall be conducted at three public hospitals in Hong Kong. All new consecutive HCC patients seen at the joint HCC clinic in these three centres will be enrolled. The recruitment will start in January, 2016 and lasts for three years. All patients will be followed up prospectively and their study parameters will be entered into a database for analysis. All the recruited patients will be staged with both HKLC and BCLC prior to treatment. Survival is the only measure of the performance of both HKLC and BCLC and will be compared at different survival endpoints (1, 3 and 5 years). . We believe the results of this prospective multicenter study will provides a fresh look at HCC staging and might address the key limitations of the BCLC staging system. It would be of major clinical impact in improving the treatment stratification and ultimately the survival outcome of HCC patients.

17100715.label: Realisation of objectives
17100715.value: The project was initially started at Queen Mary Hospital, Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital and Tuen Mun Hospital in 2016. We closed down the recruitment at Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern (PYNEH) Hospital as the site investigator Dr Cheung Foon Yiu had left the hospital for private practice by the end of 2016. Between January 2016 and December 2018, we had screened about 684 potentially eligible patients for enrolment into this study. About 429 consecutive eligible patients with completed follow-up dataset were analysed finally. About 66% of patients underwent potential curative procedures and 11% of patients received transarterial chemoembolization as the first treatment for HCC. 38% of patients had died at the time of analysis (31 October 2019). The median overall survival was 43.2 months. The median follow-up time was 22.3 months. Despite the difference in patient composition, HKLC staging again showed significantly better discriminatory ability vis-à-vis BCLC staging (area under receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] at 12- month 0.84 vs 0.71; concordance index 0.66 vs 0.61). BCLC-B (intermediate) and BCLC-C (advanced) are two heterogeneous groups with a mix of patients of a range of HKLC stages. Most of the patients did not get BCLC recommended treatment, therefore a reliable subset comparison is not available at the moment, notwithstanding that the subsets of patients getting the HKLC recommended treatments had apparently better survival outcomes. Thus, HKLC classification scheme is said to be prospectively validated and compared with BCLC scheme according to our initial planned objectives.

17100715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100715.value: Between 2016 and 2018, 429 consecutive patients were recruited in this prospective study. The majority of patients were hepatitis B carriers (80%). About 66% of patients underwent potential curative procedures (i.e., resection, LT, and ablation) and 11% of patients received transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) as the first treatment for HCC. 38% of patients had died at the time of analysis (31 October 2019). The median overall survival was 43.2 (95% confidence interval: 39.7-not reached) months. The median follow-up time was 22.3 (interquartile range: 11.0-33.3) months. Compared to the original cohort, the prospective cohort tended to have less advanced tumour status and receive more aggressive therapies, and much higher proportion of patients received curative therapies as first treatment (66% vs 38%). Despite the difference in patient composition, HKLC staging again showed significantly better discriminatory ability vis-à-vis BCLC staging (area under receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC] at 12- month 0.84 vs 0.71; concordance index 0.66 vs 0.61). BCLC-B (intermediate) and BCLC-C (advanced) are two heterogeneous groups with a mix of patients of a range of HKLC stages. Most of the patients did not get BCLC recommended treatment, therefore a reliable subset comparison is not available at the moment, notwithstanding that the subsets of patients getting the HKLC recommended treatments had apparently better survival outcomes. HKLC classification scheme is said to be prospectively validated. More patient data are desirable to obtain a more reliable subset comparison and longer follow-up is required to obtain fair inference on the survival outcomes of the patients.

17100715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17100715.value: More patient data are desirable to obtain a more reliable subset comparison and longer follow-up is required to obtain fair inference on the survival outcomes of the patients. We will continue the project for another 3 years to recruit more patients for analysis and have a longer follow-up time for the recruited patients for survival analysis. We believe the final results of this prospective study will provides a new look at HCC staging and might address the key limitations of the BCLC staging system.

17100715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100715.value: Our centre developed the Hong Kong Liver Cancer (HKLC) prognostic classification scheme. The scheme classifies patients into stages with distinct survival outcomes. Compared with BCLC staging, HKLC staging showed significantly better discriminatory ability, and was able to identify subsets from BCLC intermediate- and advanced-stage patients for more aggressive treatments and led to better survival outcomes. This project aimed to prospectively validate and compare the performance of HKLC classification with BCLC classification in an independent cohort of Chinese patients Between 2016 and 2018, 429 consecutive patients were recruited in this prospective study. The majority of patients were hepatitis B carriers. Compared to the original cohort, the prospective cohort tended to have less advanced tumour status and receive more aggressive therapies, and much higher proportion of patients received curative therapies as first treatment. Despite the difference in patient composition, HKLC staging again showed significantly better discriminatory ability vis-à-vis BCLC staging. We believe the HCC community will benefit from this prospective validation of HKLC vs BCLC. Hopefully, HKLC will replace BCLC and become the staging scheme for HCC patients. We believe the results of this prospective study will be of major clinical impact in advancing the staging and treatment guideline for HCC patients worldwide.

17101715.label: Realisation of objectives
17101715.value: Objective 1. Examine the clinical significance of MIPOL1 and its downstream signaling targets in NPC clinical samples A panel of 119 pairs of NPC tumor samples representing different clinical stages was used to investigate the expression level of MIPOL1, during the course of tumor progression. MIPOL1 was confirmed to be overall down-regulated in 75% of the NPC tumor tissues for the different cancer stages. Also, the results from the protein array assays showed that the angiogenic factors (e.g. IL6, IL8, and MCP1) and phosphorylation level of important proteins related to metastasis (e.g. FAK, ERK, AKT, and Paxillin) are down-regulated, when MIPOL1 was re-expressed in HONE1 cells, as compared to the control. Objective 2. Provide mechanistic insight into MIPOL1 regulation of the cancer-related defective signaling pathways in NPC cells and functionally validate its role utilizing different in vivo and in vitro functional assays. MIPOL1 was shown to interact with RhoB by co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and yeast-2 hybrid (Y2H) assays. The NPC cell lines with re-expression of wild-type MIPOL1 and two MIPOL1 deletion constructs were established for downstream studies. The results of real-time qPCR and western blot suggested that re-expression of wild-type MIPOL1, but not the truncation form of MIPOL1, could suppress the expression of the angiogenic factors (IL6, IL8, and MCP1) and metastatic-related targets (pAKT, pFAK, and p65). Furthermore, in vitro functional assays including colony formation assay, wound healing assay, migration and invasion assays confirmed that only the wild-type MIPOL1 could suppress the colony formation, migration, and invasion in NPC. The inhibition of metastatic ability by the wild-type MIPOL1 was further confirmed by a nude mice intrasplenic injection assay. In addition to inhibition of metastatic ability, re-expression of wild-type MIPOL1 could also suppress the NPC tumor growth in the in vivo subcutaneous injection tumorigenicity assay. The other defective signaling pathways identified from the protein array assays are under investigation. Objective 3. Identify MIPOL1 DNA binding target(s) and investigate the abilities of MIPOL1 in regulating their gene expression in NPC Our data show that MIPOL1 is able to bind to the CDKN1A promoter regions. MIPOL1 re-expression was confirmed to up-regulate expression of p21 protein in our previous study. This further confirmed the ability of MIPOL1 in regulating p21 expression and can be a new area for investigating the function of MIPOL1 in the DNA damage pathways members.

17101715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17101715.value: This current study provides strong evidence that MIPOL1 plays an important tumor suppressive and metastatic suppressive role in NPC. Significant down-regulation of MIPOL1 was detected in a majority of tumor samples in a panel of NPC biopsies with different clinical outcomes, suggesting some clinical significance in NPC. This led us to further investigate the tumor suppressive ability of MIPOL1 in both in vitro and in vivo levels. A panel of wild-type (WT) and truncation MIPOL1 constructs was established for downstream assays. Functionally, re-expression of WT MIPOL1 was shown to suppress in vivo tumor growth and tumor cell metastasis in the nude mouse assay, but interestingly, the truncation constructs showed loss of suppressive ability, as WT MIPOL1 inhibited both in vivo tumor growth and metastasis. The WT MIPOL1 also inhibited in vitro cell migration and invasion; this further supported the tumor suppressive function of MIPOL1. At the molecular pathway levels, WT MIPOL1 co-immunoprecipitated with a well-studied tumor suppressor, RhoB, and enhanced its activities. Interestingly, this RhoB was confirmed to regulate different metastasis-associated pathways. Re-expression of WT MIPOL1, but not the truncation constructs, is associated with down-regulation of a panel of key metastatic factors, including the angiogenin, IL6, IL8, MCP1, PDGFFBB, and TIMP-2, which are closely related to the tumor cell metastasis. In addition, only WT MIPOL1 showed the ability to reduce phosphorylation levels of metastasis-related signaling pathway members, including the pAKT, pp65, and pFAK. This provided strong evidence that the WT MIPOL1 is associated with the suppression of metastasis. Our previous study confirmed that MIPOL1 could up-regulate p21(CDKN1A) expression. In this current study, MIPOL1 was further confirmed to bind to the CDKN1A promoter region, as well as in the other cancer-related pathway members, although the mechanism still remains to be further confirmed. These results support a role of MIPOL1 in the regulation of expression of these potential candidates.

17101715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17101715.value: This study showed that MIPOL1 could suppress in vivo tumor growth and metastasis. Down-regulation of MIPOL1 was detected in a panel of NPC clinical biopsies with different clinical outcomes, suggesting the potential of MIPOL1 to serve as a biomarker for prognostic or diagnostic usage. This can be further substantiated by examining its expression in more clinical tumor samples. In addition, MIPOL1 re-expression down-regulated the factors important for metastasis, suggesting that these targets, including IL6, IL8, pAKT, and pP65, could be the new therapeutic targets for NPC. Novel inhibitors for these targets could be tested to validate the current findings. Also, the downstream signaling pathways regulated by the interaction of MIPOL1 and RhoB can be investigated, as RhoB is a well-studied tumor suppressor and it would be useful to know more about the function of MIPOL1 by investigating the RhoB-associating pathways. In addition, the defective signaling pathways contributed by the re-expression of MIPOL1 need further functional assays for validation. The comprehensive mechanism to determine how binding of MIPOL1 to the CDKN1A promoter regulates the expression of p21 would be of interest to further explored in the future.

17101715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17101715.value: Mirror Image Polydactyl 1 (MIPOL1) was initially known to be associated with developmental diseases. Patients with a defective MIPOL1 gene can present with a rare syndrome characterized by having abnormal numbers of fingers and toes. In our current study, we provides strong evidence to support that this development-related gene, MIPOL1, could also play a critical role as a tumor suppressor gene in a nasal cancer, namely nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), which is highly prevalent in Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. The high mortality rate of NPC is largely attributed to late stage disease characterized by distant metastasis. Identification of the markers and factors contributing to NPC growth and metastasis is necessary in future NPC research. Our study showed that MIPOL1 usually shows a low expression level in NPC tumors and MIPOL1 inhibits NPC tumor cell growth and metastasis in a mouse animal model. MIPOL1 can also reduce the expression and activities of factors and proteins, which can regulate tumor growth and metastasis. MIPOL1 can also interact with a well-studied tumor suppressor, RhoB. This further confirmed the critical role of MIPOL1 in NPC development. MIPOL1 and its associated downstream signaling partners can be potential therapeutic targets for suppression of NPC.

17101815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17101815.value: Obesity-induced adipose tissue inflammation, characterized by massive accumulation and phenotypic changes of immune cells, contributes to the development of glucose dysregulation and insulin resistance. Macrophage has been identified as a key effector cell in the initiation and progression of these metabolic disorders. Autophagy is a conserved adaptive mechanism responsible for maintaining cellular homeostasis via recycling cellular components and damaged organelles under stress conditions. Dysregulation of autophagy causes inflammation, glucose intolerance and peripheral insulin resistance. However, little is known about the regulation of inflammation by autophagy in adipose tissue macrophages in obesity. Accumulating evidence suggests that the endosomal protein APPL1 acts as a signaling adaptor regulating multiple fundamental processes. In particular, we and others found that APPL1 is the converging regulator of adiponectin and insulin pathways which maintain metabolic and vascular homeostasis. Recently we showed that expression of APPL1 is dramatically decreased in stromal vascular fraction of obese adipose tissues with inflammation. Transgenic overexpression of APPL1 counteracts obesity-induced insulin resistance and glucose dysregulation, at least in part, by ameliorating adipose tissue inflammation in mice. Such an improvement is associated with enhanced autophagy activity in macrophages. Overexpression of APPL1 attenuates both endotoxin- and toxic lipid-induced inflammatory program in primary macrophages, whereas APPL1 deficiency results in opposite effects. Further analysis indicated that APPL1 diminishes inflammatory response by promoting autophagy in macrophages. These salutary actions of APPL1 are largely abolished when its interaction with the small GTPase Rab5 is disrupted. APPL1 forms a complex with Rab5 and the class III phosphatidylinositol-3 kinase Vps34 upon endotoxin stimulation. Noticeably, the Rab5-Vps34 protein complex has been shown to promote autophagy activity under stress condition. Based on these preliminary data, we propose that APPL1 is a key signaling regulator in mediating the cross-talk between autophagy and inflammation in macrophages. Obesity reduces expression of APPL1 in macrophages, leading to defective autophagy and elevated inflammation, thereby resulting in adipose tissue inflammation and glucose dysregulation. In this project, we will test whether hematopoietic overexpression of APPL1 protects against obesity-induced adipose tissue inflammation and glucose dysregulation through promoting autophagy, and will elucidate the detailed molecular mechanisms involved in the process. The findings are expected to provide new insight into the fundamental mechanisms regulating adipose tissue inflammation, and to shed new light on the pathogenesis of glucose dysregulation in obesity. In addition, such information will contribute to the development of therapeutic strategies against obesity related complications by alleviating inflammation in adipose tissues.

17101815.label: Realisation of objectives
17101815.value: Overall, we have proved that APPL1 restricts inflammation in macrophage via mitochondrial specific autophagy through the Rab5 signaling on the early endosome. In addition, we also provided solid in vivo evidencing showing the importance of hematopoietic APPL1 in preventing dietary-induced adipose tissue inflammation and insulin resistance. Realisation of each objectives are listed as following. Due to word limitation, only key findings are described. Objective-1: To investigate whether hematopoietic overexpression of APPL1 alleviates high-fat diet induced adipose tissue inflammation and insulin resistance using adoptive transfer approach. We generated a mouse model with specific overexpression of APPL1 in hematopoietic cells by transferring the bone marrow cells from APPL1 transgenic mice and its wild-type littermates into lethally irradiated 6-week-old male C57BL6/N mice (so-called BMT-WT and BMT-APPL1-TG mice). Both high-fat-diet (HFD)-fed BMT-WT and BMT-APPL1-TG mice developed displayed comparable adiposity, food consumption and energy metabolism. BMT-WT mice developed glucose intolerance and insulin resistance upon HFD feeding for 6 weeks, whereas hematopoietic overexpression of APPL1 modestly alleviated obesity-induced insulin resistance and glucose intolerance. Such improvements were associated with reduced systemic inflammation. M1 macrophage polarization and adipose tissue inflammation was increased in BMT-WT mice fed with HFD when compared to their corresponding standard chow (STC) controls, but these changes did not occur in BMT-APPL1-TG mice We also determined whether hematopoietic deletion of APPL1 aggravates dietary-induced adipose tissue inflammation and glycose dysregulation. The bone marrow cells from APPL1 knockout (KO) mice and their WT littermates were transferred to lethally irradiated C57BL/6N mice, followed by HFD feeding and metabolic characterization. The mice were so-called “BMT-APPL1-KO” and “BMT-WT-littermates”. Consistent to our hypothesis, BMT-APPL1-KO mice were prone to HFD-induced adipose tissue inflammation, glucose intolerance and insulin resistance. More macrophages were infiltrated into visceral fat in mice without APPL1 in hematopoietic cells. Circulating levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines including IL-1β and MCP1 and anti-inflammatory adipokine adiponectin were increased and decreased in BMT-APPL1-KO mice. Consistently, expression of IL-1β in adipose tissue and the liver were increased in BMD-APPL1-KO, accompanied with reduced insulin signaling cascade. Objective-2: To examine whether APPL1 prevents obesity-induced inflammation by promoting autophagy in macrophages. To investigate how APPL1 regulates inflammatory response in macrophages, we isolated bone marrow derived macrophages from 1) APPL1 Tg mice and their WT littermates and 2) APPL1 KO mice and their littermates. To our surprise, overexpression or knockout of APPL1 had no obvious effect M1 macrophage polarization but modulated activity of nucleotide binding domain leucine-rich repeat-containing receptor, pyrin domain-containing-3 (NLRP3) inflammasome, a protein complex that regulates production of IL-1β and IL-18. Indeed, we found that APPL1 deficiency augmented ATP or palmitic acid-induced IL-1β and IL-18 in LPS-primed BMDM in a time- and dose-dependent manner, whereas APPL1 overexpression exerted opposite effect. Further analysis indicate that APPL1 did not regulate the priming step since APPL1 deficient BMDM displayed normal response to LPS-induced upregulation of NLRP3 and pro-IL-1β mRNA and NF-kβ activity. On the contrary, APPL1 deficiency led to an upregulation of capase-1 activity. Treatment with capase-1 inhibitor abolished the elevate IL-1β and caspase-1 activity. On the other hand, APPL1 deficiency did not control NLRC4 and NLRP1 inflammasome activity. Consistent with these in vitro findings, we observed that expression of caspase-1 is augmented in adipose tissue resident macrophage in epipdymal white adipose tissue of BMT-APPL1-KO mice fed with HFD when compared to those from BMT-WT-littermates mice. Recent studies indicated that danger signals from damaged mitochondria mediates NLRP3 inflammasome activation and APPL1 has been documented to maintain mitochondrial homeostasis, we hypothesized that APPL1 regulates NLRP3 inflammasome activation via mitochondria. BMDM lack of APPL1 displayed increased production of mitochondrial ROS, reduced mitochondrial member potential and increased amount of damaged mitochondria when compared to WT control under basal and inflammasome activation condition. In addition, amount of cytosolic mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) in APPL1 KO BMDM was significantly higher than in that in WT BMDM upon inflammasome activation. Previous studies suggested that these danger signals from damaged mitochondria trigger NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Indeed, we found that genetic deletion of APPL1 pronounced NLRP3 inflammasome induced by the mitochondrial complex I inhibitor retenone, the complex III inhibitor antimycin and respiratory chain uncoupler FCCP. The degree of mitochondrial membrane potential loss induced by retenone and antimycin was significantly larger in APPL1 KO BMDM than that in WT controls. Furthermore, APPL1 also limited palmitic acid induced mitochondrial dysfunction in LPS-primed BMDM. Next we investigated whether removal of mitochondrial ROS and DNA is able to alleviate APPL1 deficiency-induced elevated inflammasome activation. Treatment with the general ROS scavenger N-acetyl cysteine (NAC) or the mitochondrial specific ROS scavenger Mito-TEMPO significantly reduced LPS+ATP-induced mitochondrial ROS production in both APPL1 KO and WT BMDM, accompanied with a reduction of IL-1β and cleaved caspase 1 secretion in the culture medium. Noticeably, the increased mitochondrial damage in APPL1 KO BMDM could not be rescued by treatment with NAC nor MitoTEMPO, indicating mitochondrial damage is upstream to mitochondrial ROS production. In addition, removal of mtDNA also abolished the elevated NLRP3 inflammasome activation. These data collectively suggest that APPL1 deficiency induces mitochondrial damage, leading to increased production of mitochondrial ROS and cytosolic mtDNA, which in turn promotes NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Autophagy is responsible for removal of damaged organelle to maintain cellular homeostasis. We found that APPL1 deficiency impairs LPS-induced LC3-II expression in BMDM, whereas APPL1 overexpression exerts opposite effects. In addition, we demonstrated that APPL1 controls p62 recruitment to mitochondria and promotes mitophagosome trafficking to the lysosome for degradation in macrophage upon NLRP3 agonist stimulation Taken together, these data suggest that APPL1 is crucial to maintain proper mitochondria function and restrict inflammation in macrophages, perhaps via induction of mitophagy (a specific form of mitochondrial autophagy) Objective-3: To elucidate whether APPL1 potentiates autophagy via the Rab5-Vps34 signaling axis. In this objective, we focused to delineate how APPL1 controls mitophagy. Co-immunprecipiation assay revealed that APPL1 interacts with Rab5 and Vps34. We found that APPL1 and its interaction partner Rab5 were co-localized and recruited to mitochondria upon NLRP3 inflammasome activation in BMDM. Co-localization of Rab5+ early endosomes with mitochondrial was increased by FCCP/ATP treatment in LPS-primed WT BMDM, and such a change was controlled by APPL1. The APPL1 mutant without Rab5 binding ability or endosomal localization was unable to be recruited to mitochondria in response to NLRP3 agonist. In addition, APPL1 also controlled the recruitment of the autophagy receptor p62 to the mitophagy in response to NLRP3 agonist, which in turn regulated formation of mitophagasome and subsequent mitochondrial autolysosomes. Abrogating the interaction between APPL1 and Rab5 diminished the promoting and suppressive effect of APPL1 on mitophagy and inflammasome activation, respectively in BMDM. Next, we investigated whether activation of Rab5 rescues the APPL1 deficiency phenotypes. To this end, APPL1 KO BMDM and WT BMDM were infected with adenovirus encoding constitutively active form Rab5 (Q79L) or empty control. Activation of Rab5 restored mitophagy and prevented excessive NLRP3 inflammasome activation in APPL1 deficient BMDM. These data collectively indicated that APPL1 deficiency leads to defective Rab5-mediated mitophagy, which results in elevated inflammasome activation upon ATP/FCCP stimulation. Finally, we demonstrated the endosomal localization of APPL1 is required for its inhibitory effect on inflammasome activation and its promoting effect on mitophagy. Taken together, our data indicated that the APPL1-Rab5 signaling axis on endosome is reduced to mediate mitophagy and restricts NLRP3 inflammasome activation.

17101815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17101815.value: Mitophagy removes damaged mitochondria, and its defect has recently been shown to induce overactivation of NLRP3 inflammasome and subsequent interleukin (IL)-1β production, yet the detailed underlying mechanism remains poorly understood. The endosomal protein APPL1 dynamically transmits signals among different organelles including early endosomes in response to extracellular hormonal and stress stimulation. In this project, we show that APPL1 promotes endosomal-mediated mitophagy, which in turn restricts NLRP3 inflammasome activation in macrophages. The major findings are summarized below: 1. APPL1 selectively inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome and IL-1β production in macrophages. 2. APPL1 facilitates the removal of damaged mitochondria, thereby preventing generation of mitochondrial ROS production and cytosolic mtDNA. 3. Endosomal APPL1 is recruited to the damaged mitochondria, where it interacts with the small GTPase Rab5 to promote mitophagy, thereby restricting NLRP3 inflammasome activation in BMDM. 4. Hematopoietic APPL1 is essential to restrict obesity-induced adipose tissue inflammation and insulin resistance in mice. Research outcomes: 1. Presentation in three international conferences: a) 79 th Scientific Sessions-America Diabetes Association b) International Conference on Molecular Mechanisms of Inflammation-2019 c) 14th International Symposium on Healthy Aging 2019 2. Training of five undergraduate students (Bachelor of Science-PolyU) and one PhD student (PolyU). 3. We have published two reviews about the role of adipose tissue dysfunction in obesity and its metabolic complication in Clinical Science (2020 Jan 31;134(2):315-330) and International Journal of Molecular Science (2020, 21(11), 4184) 4. We have sent the manuscript entitled “An early endosomal-dependent mitophagy mediated by APPL1-Rab5 axis restricts NLRP3 inflammasome activation in macrophages” to Nature Cell Biology on 23 June 2020. We originally planned to submit this earlier and get it published before final report submission. However, due to outbreak of COVID19 and campus closure (Nov-Dec 2019; protester occupied the campus), the progress has been heavily delayed. But the PhD student trained in this GRF and I have published two reviews during the aforementioned period. Nevertheless, we will update Research Grant Council once the manuscript is accepted for publication. 5. We also found that APPL2 (the close homolog of APPL1) controls browning of adipose tissue and glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in pancreatic beta cells. The study about APPL2 and browning was published in EMBO Reports (2018 Apr;19(4):e44977.), while the study about APPL2 and insulin secretion was submitted to PNAS. We are now revising the manuscript and plan to resubmit around in near future. 6. Award: Young investigator award (Poster) in 14th International Symposium on Healthy Aging.

17101815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17101815.value: 1. Our study revealed that APPL1 controls mitophagy via Rab5, but the precise mechanism remains elusive. In addition, how APPL1 senses the activation of NLRP3 inflammasome and damaged mitochondria is also unknown. 2. Future studies should identify a mean of manipulation of APPL1-Rab5 signaling axis for the treatment of obesity-associated adipose tissue macrophage inflammation. 3. To validate whether the APPL1-mediated mitophagic response is reduced in human obesity and its associated metabolic diseases. 4. To investigate whether APPL2 (the close homolog of APPL1) also plays a role in regulating endosome-mediated mitophagy and inflammasome activation in macrophages.

17101815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17101815.value: Macrophage-mediated chronic inflammation links obesity and multiple metabolic disorders, yet the underlying mechanism remain poorly understood. Autophagy removes damaged mitochondria, and its defect has recently been shown to induce chronic macrophage inflammation. The endosomal protein APPL1 dynamically transmits signals among different organelles including early endosomes in response to extracellular hormonal and stress stimulation. In addition, we and others demonstrated that APPL1 is an insulin and adiponectin sensitizer, but its role in autophagy and macrophage inflammation has never been explored. In this project, we show that APPL1 promotes endosomal-mediated autophagy via the small GTPase Rab5, which in turn restricts activation of NLRP3 inflammasome (a multimeric protein complex that initiates secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines interleukin-1β) in macrophages. APPL1 prevents production of interleukin-1β and hence alleviates obesity related adipose tissue inflammation and type 2 diabetes. Our finding uncover how the interaction between autophagy and inflammatory pathways controls adipose tissue function in obesity, and indicate that targeting APPL1 might be a promising approach for treatment of metabolic diseases related to macrophage inflammation .

17102115.label: Realisation of objectives
17102115.value: 1. To characterize the functional effect of Cav1-mediated S100P in HCC under hypoxic stress (The study of this objective was fully completed) To answer whether Cav1-regulated HCC cell migration and invasion is mediated by S100P, S100P was reintroduced in MHCC97L Cav1 knockdown cells. Expression of S100P in Cav1 knockdown cells significantly restored the cell migration and invasiveness. Treatment of recombinant S100P also restored the cell migration and invasiveness of Cav1 knockdown cells and such restoration was abolished when S100P neutralizing antibody was added. To further examine the involvement of Cav1-mediated S100P downregulation in HCC tumorigenesis and metastasis, stable clones of non-target control cells, Cav1 knockdown cells and Cav1 knockdown cells with S100P, were subcutaneously injected into nude mice. Expression of S100P in Cav1 knockdown clones formed bigger tumors when compared to tumors developed from Cav1 knockdown cells. To determine whether S100P can restore metastasis in vivo, orthotopic liver implantation was performed. Restoration of S100P also enhanced tumor development in liver and incidence of distant metastasis to lungs. Taken together, our findings show that S100P is a functional component in promoting HCC aggressive phenotype. To test whether S100P could be a potential therapeutic target for HCC, we functionally characterize metastatic MHCC97L cells after the suppression of endogenous S100P by lentiviral based knockdown. S100P expression was stably silenced by two different shRNA targeting S100P. Diminution of S100P significantly inhibited anchorage independent growth, migration and invasiveness of MHCC97L cells. More importantly, suppression of S100P expression largely inhibited tumorigenesis through subcutaneous injection. Smaller tumors were formed when S100P was knocked down when compared to the control cells. We next tested if silencing S100P could reduce metastasis using an orthotopic liver implantation model. It was revealed that mice implanted with S100P-knockdown tumor cells had significantly smaller tumor formation in the liver and significant reduction in lung metastasis when compared to mice implanted with the non-target control cells. Subsequently, we further demonstrated the role of Cav1/S100P in HCC metastasis under hypoxia in cell culture and in animal model. Hep3B and MHCC97L Cav1 knockdown stable clones were established. Both migration and invasion of Cav1 knockdown stable clones were significantly reduced under normoxia. Hypoxia significantly enhanced the cell migration and invasion of the control non-target cells when compared to cells cultured in normoxic condition. However, such enhancement in migration and invasion was not prominent when Cav1 expression was suppressed in Cav1 knockdown cells. To study the effect of hypoxia on HCC metastasis, hepatic artery ligation was employed to obstruct hepatic artery blood flow to promote intratumoral hypoxic environment in the liver. Tumor seeds derived from MHCC97L non-target control and Cav1 knockdown cells were implanted into liver of mice with or without receiving HAL. HAL increased both expressions of Cav1 and carbonic anhydrase IX, a marker of hypoxia. Functionally, HAL treatment enhanced the tumor growth and lung metastasis in control cells. Largest amount of metastatic tumor focus was observed in the lung tissues of animals subjected to HAL. However, this enhancement was suppressed in mice implanted with Cav1 knockdown tumor cells. These results suggest that Cav1 contributes significantly to the cell motility and metastasis of HCC cells under hypoxic stress. 2. To delineate the molecular basis of Cav1 and S100P signaling in HCC cells (The study of this objective was fully completed) Based on the apparent coregulation of Cav1 and S100P in HCC cell lines, we examined how Cav1 upregulates S100P. Transient expression of Cav1 upregulated S100P and phospho-p65 (S276) in cells. Addition of NF-kB inhibitor, IMD-0354, abolished the upregulation of S100P by Cav1 and this inhibition of NF-kB was verified by the abrogation of phospho-p65 (Ser276) level. Consistently, the expression level of phospho-p65 (Ser276) was suppressed in MHCC97L Cav1 stable knockdown cells when compared to the non-target control cells. Our data therefore suggests that Cav1 upregulates S100P via the activation of NF-kB pathway. Functionally, activation of NF-kB pathway rescued the migration and invasion of Cav1 knockdown cells. Knockdown of S100P recapitulated the effect of Cav1 knockdown in HCC cells. Diminution of S100P significantly inhibited anchorage independent growth, migration and invasiveness of cells. Moreover, suppression of S100P expression largely inhibited tumorigenesis and metastasis in an orthotopic liver implantation model. 3. To evaluate the clinical relevance and prognostic significance of Cav1 and S100P expressions in HCC clinical tissues (The study of this objective was fully completed) Western blot analysis revealed that S100P expression was well correlated with Cav1 expression in a panel of HCC cell lines. S100P expression was studied in 36 sets of clinical samples, comprising of non-tumorous liver tissues, primary HCCs and extrahepatic metastatic tissues. The result showed that S100P staining was not detected in non-tumorous tissues while moderate or strong staining of S100P in cytoplasm was detected in 14/36 (39%) paired tumorous and extrahepatic metastatic tissues of the same patient. To determine the clinical relevance of S100P in HCC, S100P expression was revealed in 87 cases of paired tumorous and non-tumorous liver tissues. S100P was overexpressed in 34% (30/87) of the cases. Clinicopathological correlation revealed that overexpression of S100P was significantly associated with venous invasion, tumor microsatellite, direct liver invasion and the absence of tumor encapsulation.

17102115.label: Major findings and research outcome
17102115.value: Hypoxia in solid tumors has been attributed to the aberrant vascular formation and the enhanced proliferation of tumor cells. Intratumoral hypoxia is an indicator of poor prognosis and correlates with an increased risk to develop metastasis. Our recent data revealed that caveolin-1 (Cav1) is dramatically increased in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) metastatic tissues and cell lines, suggesting a role of Cav1 in HCC metastasis. However, its role and molecular mechanism under hypoxia in HCC remains unknown. In this study, we found that hypoxia elevated Cav1 expression in HCC cell lines. In addition, hypoxic region of HCC xenograft displayed elevated expression level of Cav1. Hypoxia promoted HCC cell migration and invasion and distant metastasis to lungs in nude mice in in vitro and in vivo experiments, respectively. However, such promoting effect was abolished in Cav1 knockdown cells. Gene expression profiling revealed that hypoxia-induced Cav1 functioned as a positive regulator of S100P through the activation of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) pathway. The elevation of S100P under hypoxia was abrogated when Cav1 or NF-κB was knocked down. Restoration of S100P in Cav1 knockdown cells rescued the migratory potentials of HCC cells as well as tumor formation and lung metastasis. Clinically, overexpression of S100P was significantly correlated with venous invasion, microsatellite, direct liver invasion and absence of tumor encapsulation in HCC. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that enhanced Cav1 expression under hypoxia leads to upregulation of S100P via the activation of NF-κB pathway; promoting the migratory, invasive and metastatic potentials of HCC cells. This study has been published in Cancer Research 2016, 76(24):7242-7253 by Mao et al.

17102115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17102115.value: The current study has provided a comprehensive understanding regarding the clinical significance and oncogenic role of S100P as a metastasis driver in HCC. Based on the secretory nature of S100P, the secretory form and in the form of exosomes suggest the potential of S100P in pre-metastatic niche formation in distant organs. Our continual study revealed the presence of S100P in the exosomes derived from metastatic HCC cells. Encouragingly, the expression of S100P in circulating exosomes was detected and was well correlated with the tumor stage of HCC patients. This physiological evidence strongly supports the pivotal role of S100P in HCC particularly at the advanced stage. Thus, targeting exo-S100P, likely by neutralizing the functions of oncogenic exosomes, may be envisioned as a combined treatment with TACE for HCC patients. HCC is a prevalent cancer in our country. High incidence and mortality have led to the attention of major public health problem. Exosome research will potentially avail the clinical management of cancer patients and ease the burden on health care system in our country.

17102115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17102115.value: Most of the liver cancer patients are diagnosed at the late stage and no treatment has been proven successful. For patients with unresectable liver cancer, trans-arterial chemoembolization (TACE) is considered to be one of the most effective palliative measures. TACE involves the occlusion of hepatic arterial blood supply and focused administration of chemotoxins to the tumorous tissues. Despite the effectiveness of TACE, intratumoral hypoxia and metastasis are observed after treatment. Several studies have shown that TACE inevitably induces hypoxia. Although intratumoral hypoxia is originally thought to kill cancer cells, it provides selective pressure for the most aggressive cancer cells to adapt and survive under hypoxic stress. Our findings revealed that caveolin-1 is a promising regulator of liver cancer metastasis and its promoting effect under hypoxia, suggesting underlying basis how hypoxia counteracts the therapeutic efficacy of TACE for patients. This study also provides insights into the development of combined treatment with TACE to overcome the effect of hypoxic stress.

17102915.label: Project Objectives
17102915.value: To test the roles of HMGB1 signaling in promoting cytokines and MMPs activation, and mediating BBB disruption and HT induction in ischemic brains with delayed thrombolysis. To elucidate the roles of peroxynitrite in the activating HMGB1 signaling and inducing BBB disruption and hemorrhagic transformation during thrombolysis. To test the hypothesis that preventing peroxynitrite-mediated HMGB1 release can be an adjunct therapeutic strategy to reduce t-PA-induced BBB disruption and HT in ischemic stroke treatment: Using Baicalin as an example.

To elucidate the roles of peroxynitrite in the activating HMGB1 signaling and inducing BBB disruption and hemorrhagic transformation during thrombolysis.

To test the hypothesis that preventing peroxynitrite-mediated HMGB1 release can be an adjunct therapeutic strategy to reduce t-PA-induced BBB disruption and HT in ischemic stroke treatment: Using Baicalin as an example.

17102915.label: Realisation of objectives
17102915.value: We conducted a series of experiments and have achieved all of the goals designed in our original proposal. Objective 1. (1) We conducted in vivo animal experiments by using rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model with delayed tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) treatment at 5 hours after MCAO. We observed the increased production of HMGB1 and its receptor 2 in the ischemic brains with delayed t-PA treatment, which was associated with the increased expression and activity of MMP-9, and disruption of tight junction protein claudin-5 and extracellular matrix collagen-4. HMGB1 inhibitor glycyrrhizin decreased the expression of HMGB1 and its receptor 2, inhibited MMP-9 activity, protected the blood-brain barrier integrity, reduced brain edema and inhibited the hemorrhagic transformation, decreased the brain edema, attenuated the brain cell apoptosis, and eventually improved the neurological outcomes and survival rate. Interestingly, we found that treatment of glycyrrhizin, a HMGB1 inhibitor, could mitigate the nitrosative stress in the ischemic brains as indicated by the reduction of 3-nitrotyrosine (3-NT). Consistently, HMGB1-binding heptamer peptide HBHP decreased the cytokines in the ischemic brains, including IL-6, TNF-a, IL-1β and COX-2, and showed to protect blood-brain barrier, reduce hemorrhagic transformation and improve the survival rate in rat MCAO model with delayed t-PA treatment. (2) We used cultured brain microvascular endothelial b.End3 cells in vitro, and found that HMGB1 inhibitor glycyrrhizin could protect the cell viability and reduce the para-cellular permeability of b.End3 cells under oxygen and glucose deprivation model. Objective 2. (1) We investigated the mechanisms of how HMGB1 was triggered to mediate the ischemic brains injury with delayed t-PA treatment. By using our newly developed probe HKYellow-AM, we observed the significant increase of peroxynitrite, a representative reactive nitrogen species, in the ischemic brains with delayed t-PA treatment. Peroxynitrite decomposition catalyst (PDC) FeTmPyP significantly decreased the peroxynitrite level, down-regulate the expression of HMGB1 and its receptor 2, inhibited MMP-9 activity and protected the tight junction proteins, subsequently protected BBB and HT. Consistently, we found that intracerebral injection of peroxynitrite donor SIN-1 increased the expression of HMGB1 and its receptor 2 in the naïve rat brains. (2) To further understand the role of peroxynitrite in inducing HMGB1, we conducted in vitro study and showed that peroxynitrite donor SIN-1 increased the expression of HMGB1, and the increased HMGB1 was abolished by the peroxynitrite decomposition catalyst. Objective 3 (1) We screened the natural compounds from Chinese medicinal herbs, and identified that baicalin could directly scavenge peroxynitrite as indicate by HPLC-Mass spectrum analysis. We further demonstrated that baicalin inhibited peroxynitrite production and directly scavenged peroxynitrite in cultured neurons and brain microvascular endothelial cells under oxygen glucose deprivation (OGD) for mimicking ischemia-reperfusion in vitro and in the ischemic brain areas of cerebral cerebral reperfusion injury animal models in vivo. The production of peroxynitrite and related molecular targets was detected by using HK-Yellow AM and western blot analysis for the formation of 3-nitrotyrosine (3-NT, a footprint of peroxynitrite). We further found that baicalin inhibited the expression of HMGB1, MMP-9, preserved the tight junction protein ZO-1, protected the BBB damage, brain edema, brain cell apoptosis and hemorrhagic transformation. Furthermore, baicalin did not affect the thrombolytic activity of t-PA. (2) In vitro, we found that baicalin inhibited peroxynitrite in cultured neurons and brain microvascular endothelial cells under oxygen and glucose deprivation model with t-PA treatment. Furthermore, baicalin protected the cultured neurons and the brain microvascular endothelial cells against t-PA induced injury.

17102915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17102915.value: 1. HMGB1 plays a crucial role in the blood-brain-barrier (BBB) disruption, hemorrhagic transformation (HT) via activating MMP-9 in ischemic brain injury with delayed t-PA treatment. We conducted animal experiments of ischemic stroke with delayed t-PA treatment beyond 4.5 hours and performed clinical trials to test serum HMGB1 level in acute ischemic stroke patients. Major discoveries include (1) Serum HMGB1 level were elevated in acute ischemic stroke patients and ischemic stroke rats with delayed t-PA treatment. Delayed t-PA treatment increased the expressions of HMGB1, 2 and MMP-9 in the ischemic brains. Blocking HMGB1 by using HMGB1-binding heptamer peptide (HBHP) at 4.5h after brain ischemia significantly attenuated mortality rate, hemorrhage, brain swelling, neurological deficits, BBB impairment, microglia activation, and the expressions of inflammatory cytokines. The work has been published in Journal of Neuroinflammation (2018: 15:237); (2) Both glycyrrhizin and HBHP inhibited HMGB1 and MMP-9, protected the BBB, reduced brain edema and prevented HT. Inhibition of HMGB1 reduced the para-cellular permeability of brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMECs) in vitro under OGD condition. The manuscript is under reversion for Translational Stroke Research, and was partially published in a conference abstract. Free Radical Biology and Medicine Volume 100, Supplement, November 2016, Page S167. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2016.10.440 2. Peroxynitrite mediates HMGB1 signaling for activating MMP-9, leading the BBB damage and HT. We found that peroxynitrite production induced the expressions of HMGB1 and its receptor 2 in the ischemic brains with delayed t-PA treatment, and the naïve rat brains in vivo, and cultured BMECs in vitro. FeTmPyP down-regulated HMGB1, 2 and MMP-9, protected the BBB and reduced HT. Part of the results has been published in Translational Stroke Research. (2018, 9, 515-529). 3. Baicalin could be a potential adjunct agent with t-PA to reducing hemorrhagic transformation. A natural compound baicalin was found to directly scavenge peroxynitrite, inhibited MMP-9 activation, protected the BBB integrity and reduced HT. The results have been published in Translational Stroke Research. 2018, 9(5), 515-529. 4. Plasma 3-nitrotyrosine and HMGB1 could be potential biomarkers for predicting HT Clinical study was conducted to investigate the values of plasma 3-nitrotyrosine (3-NT) and HMGB1 as biomarkers for ischemic stroke patients. Seventy-two patients with ischemic stroke were included. Pearson analysis showed that plasma 3-NT level could be a biomarker for predicting the hemorrhagic transformation of ischemic stroke patients. Plasma HMGB1 level was also increased in ischemic patients with hemorrhagic transformation. We will use the pilot study for further clinical investigation.

17102915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17102915.value: Based on the achievement of our studies, we expect following potential directions for further studies: (1) to explore the molecular mechanisms of HMGB1 in regulating the hemorrhagic transformation of ischemic stroke with delayed t-PA treatment. In particular, how HMGB1 regulates MMP-9 activation and contributing to blood-brain barrier damage are valuable to be further studied. (2) Using HMGB1 as a molecular target for drug screening to prevent hemorrhagic transformation (HT) of ischemic stroke, not only for HT associated with thrombolytic therapy, but also HT developed after mechanical reperfusion, or induced by hyperglycemia. More extensive studies can be conducted in this aspect. (3) To further investigate the relationship between plasma HMGB1 level and hemorrhagic transformation, neurological dysfunction in both stroke animal model and stroke human subjects. Due to the limitation of funding and research period, we could not achieve the goals. We plan to seek for more funds from RGC GRF grants or other funding sources to continue our studies in this direction.

17102915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17102915.value: Stroke is a leading cause of disability in human diseases. The prevalence of stroke becomes one of the major disease burdens worldwide. The only FDA approved drug for ischemic stroke is the tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA), which has a limited treatment time window of 4.5 hours. Treatment beyond this time window increased the risk of hemorrhagic transformation (HT). Therefore, understanding the mechanisms of HT and develop a therapeutic strategy for overcoming HT is timely important. With the support of RGC GRF grant, we conducted a series of experiments to test our hypothesis that HMGB1, a pro-inflammatory signaling molecule, plays important roles in the regulation of hemorrhagic transformation of ischemic stroke with delayed t-PA treatment. We demonstrate that HMGB1 plays a crucial role in including the activation of MMP-9, subsequently contributing to the disruption of the blood-brain barrier and hemorrhagic transformation. We further demonstrated that peroxynitrite, a reactive nitrogen species generated from cerebral ischemia-reperfusion, plays an important role in HMGB1 induction in the ischemic brains. Blocking peroxynitrite could reduce the expression of HMGB1, subsequently reduced HT and improved the neurological outcomes. Targeting HMGB1 with HMGB1-binding heptamer peptide HBHP showed similar protective effects against hemorrhagic transformation induced by delayed t-PA treatment. Therefore, peroxynitrite-HMGB1 signaling is important for drug discovery in preventing HT for stroke treatment. We further found that natural compounds glycyrrhizin and baicalin, derived from Chinese Medicinal herbs Glycyrrhiza uralensis Fisch. and Scutellaria baicalnsis Geprgi respectively could target the peroxynitrite-HMGB1 signaling, subsequently prevent hemorrhagic transformation induced by delayed t-PA treatment. This project yields 2 original articles, 1 article in preparation, 3 review article and trained 5 postgraduate students.

17103015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17103015.value: 此項目將開發一種嶄新的方法-結合光遺傳刺激及聽覺功能磁力共振成像（fMRI）的技術- 研究神經科學的一個基本問題：大腦皮層如何調節中腦的聽覺處理？在中樞聽覺系統中，聽覺皮層（AC）中含有大量的突觸連結至中腦的聽覺子核，稱為下丘（IC）。 我們提出的這個研究項目不但對了解正常腦幹的聽覺處理十分重要，對於了解聽力障礙，包括聽力功能喪失，也非常有幫助。目前我們對皮層下行調控中腦的聽覺處理只有有限的認識。原因之一是現有的電生理技術僅可以檢測下丘神經元的一小部分；此外，我們只能依賴比較簡單的手段來激活或抑制下行皮質突觸以影響下丘（例如，電刺激和組織冷卻）；最後，目前已有的研究僅測試了聽覺皮層對下丘 的反饋作用。要進一步了解聽覺皮層，和其他感覺皮層可能產生的對中腦聽覺處理的下行調節作用，主要的研究障礙在于缺乏大範圍測試及刺激技術。我們提出的研究方法可以解決這些問題。基於血氧水平（BOLD）的功能磁力共振成像可以大範圍地、非侵入性地檢測局部大批神經元的活動。我們的研究項目將利用光遺傳聽覺功能磁力共振成像（o-afMRI）的方法來研究下行突觸對下丘聽覺處理功能的影響。我們假設整個下丘的聽覺處理會受到來自聽覺皮層和視覺皮層的下行突觸的調控。我們進一步假設，如果利用光遺傳學方法對聽覺或視覺皮層區域內的錐體神經元進行操縱，其產生的下行調控作用將可被聽覺功能磁力共振成像檢測到。具體而言，我們將首先開發一套光遺傳聽覺功能磁力共振（o-afMRI）技術規程。這項規程將（i）利用光遺傳學方法對皮質錐體神經元進行刺激，(ii) 利用聽覺刺激并透過7T磁力共振成像掃描儀進行功能磁力共振成像，從而分析囓齒動物下丘的四個基本聽覺處理功能。然後，我們將通過光遺傳學操縱特定聽覺皮層或視覺皮層區域中的錐體神經元，研究其如何調節下丘的聽覺處理功能，以此來系統地測試我們前述的假設。這個項目的結果將使我們進一步了解中腦聽覺子核如何綜合由聽覺和視覺皮層下行輸入的信息。它們也將指導今後對整個聽覺網絡中多個區域的協調活動及功能障礙的研究。當設計新的聽力障礙的治療方法和輔助設備時，這項研究也會提供重要的參考。

17103015.label: Realisation of objectives
17103015.value: The proposed objectives have been mostly achieved. 1. We have successfully implemented optogenetic fMRI technology platform at PI's laboratory, which is now one of the few such laboratories in the world. 2. We have innovated a number of MRI methods to advance fMRI technology, particularly in terms of improving EPI image quality. 3. Scientifically, we have conducted most of the proposed optogenetic fMRI experiments. The results are in general agreement with the original hypothesis. 4. These experimental results and technical capability have directly led to a new round of experiments that are presently funded by a RGC CRF project. 17103015.label: Major findings and research outcome
17103015.value: 1. We have developed a number of image reconstruction methods that enabled us to acquire and reconstruction high quality EPI images, which are the template images for fMRI. 2. Scientifically, to investigate whether and how visual cortical inputs affect IC auditory responses, we have combined auditory blood-oxygenation-level-dependent (BOLD) functional MRI (fMRI) with cell-type specific optogenetic manipulation of visual cortex. The results showed that predominant optogenetic excitation of the excitatory pyramidal neurons in the infragranular layers of the primary VC enhances the noise-evoked BOLD fMRI responses within the IC. This finding reveals that inputs from VC influence and facilitate basic sound processing in the auditory midbrain. Such combined optogenetic and auditory fMRI approach can shed light on the large-scale modulatory effects of corticofugal pathways and guide detailed electrophysiological studies in the future. 3. In addition, we have studied the patterns of large-scale brain-wide interactions mediated by thalamo-cortical networks through optogenetics and functional MRI. We found that the thalamus can recruit long-range cortical and subcortical networks and initiate their interactions in a spatiotemporally specific manner.

17103015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17103015.value: We have successfully implemented optogenetic fMRI technology platform at PI's laboratory, which is now one of the few such laboratories in the world; Our MRI research laboratory is one of the few laboratories in the world that can perform highly complex optogenetic fMRI experiments at this point.

17103015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17103015.value: Sensory cortices contain extensive descending pathways, yet their impact on brainstem processing - particularly across sensory systems - remains poorly understood. In the auditory system, the inferior colliculus (IC) in the midbrain receives cross-modal inputs from the visual cortex (VC). However, the influences from VC on auditory midbrain processing are unclear. In this project, we have advanced optogenetic fMRI technology. To investigate whether and how visual cortical inputs affect IC auditory responses, we have combined auditory BOLD fMRI with cell-type specific optogenetic manipulation of visual cortex. The results show that predominant optogenetic excitation of the excitatory pyramidal neurons in the infragranular layers of the primary VC enhances the noise-evoked BOLD fMRI responses within the IC. This finding reveals that inputs from VC influence and facilitate basic sound processing in the auditory midbrain. Such combined optogenetic and auditory fMRI approach can shed light on the large-scale modulatory effects of corticofugal pathways and guide detailed electrophysiological studies in the future. In addition, our thalamocortical optogenetic fMRI results demonstrated that low-frequency activity governs large-scale brain-wideinteractions through long-range excitatory projections to coordinate the functional integration of remote brain regions.

17103215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17103215.value: 引言: 鼻咽癌（ NPC ）在香港常見的癌症中排名第七，治療的主要方法是放射治療，隨著放射治療的進步，早期癌症存活率，現在超過80％ 。不幸的是，放療仍然引發長期副作用，而其中最主要的副作用之一是吞嚥困難和氣管吸入食物或飲料。吞嚥困難和氣管吸入食物或飲料不單影響生活質素，亦可以導致危及生命的肺部感染。研究顯示超過60%的鼻咽癌存活者患上潛在性吸入，5%鼻咽癌存活者需要入醫院接受吸入性肺炎治療。放射治療涉及頭頸部區域吞嚥結構會引致功能障礙以致造成吞嚥困難，但那些吞嚥結構較容易因放射治療而受損傷則仍然未知。而導致吞嚥困難和引起吸入性肺炎的放射臨界劑量也未明。 研究目標: 1. 識別引致鼻咽癌病人在放射治療後吞嚥困難的結構 2. 識別導致吞嚥困難的輻射臨界劑量 研究設計: 這項研究是評估鼻咽癌存活者的吞嚥功能的橫斷面研究，與輻射劑量吞嚥的各種結構之相互關聯，用吞嚥相關的生活質素問卷作主觀評估症狀，而X光吞嚥造影錄像檢查（Videofluoroscopic Swallow Study; VFSS) 和高分辨率測壓（High-Resolution Manometry; HRM)將被用於客觀吞嚥評估。本硏究會收集了放射治療規劃和吞嚥評估中大型數據集。為了利用這些“大數據”，本研究將利用“Oncospace®” - 一個關係數據庫，用作發掘放療劑量體積直方圖的數據和結果關係。各個數據集的輻射劑量和吞嚥評估結果將被匿名化，並上傳到數據挖掘和統計分析的Oncospace®數據庫。 研究對象: 邀請接受了調強放射治療3年或以上的鼻咽癌病人參與研究，研究計劃在兩年內招募最少74名病人。 預期成果和未來的研究方向：本研究將確定那些關鍵吞嚥結構會較容易受放療損害，並導致長期的吞嚥困難的發展，以及確定放射臨界劑量。該信息在將來會用作設計前瞻性臨床試驗，以保留吞嚥功能，並限制在已識別的吞嚥結構的放射劑量，最終的目標是提高鼻咽癌存活者的吞嚥功能及生活質素。

17103215.label: Realisation of objectives
17103215.value: A total of 80 NPC survivors who underwent radiation therapy at least 3 years prior were recruited from Queen Mary Hospital; 2 participants did not have radiation data available, therefore a total of 78 participants were included in the analysis. Objective 1: Radiation dosage to 12 structures in the head and neck were obtained from hospital records, these were: 1) oral cavity, 2) ipsilateral parotid, 3) contralateral parotid, 4) base of tongue, 5) superior pharyngeal constrictor, 6) middle pharyngeal constrictor, 7) inferior pharyngeal constrictor, 8) pharyngeal constrictors, 9) cricopharyngeus, 10) glottic larynx, 11) supraglottic larynx, 12) whole larynx. Each structure was identified by the oncologist in the computer tomography scan of the participants, then delineated using tissue contouring via computer software. The median dosage to each contoured structure was then extracted. Based on initial analysis of participants, 4 structures were correlated with significant differences in swallowing function as measured by kinematic measures of swallowing structures. These were the inferior pharyngeal constrictors, glottic larynx, cricopharyngeus, and base of tongue. Dosage information is incomplete and being collected currently. Additional swallowing function measures are in paper form (participant completed questionnaires etc) and require more time to be reviewed and converted into electronic form for analysis. Dosage data is anticipated to be completed collected by the end of February 2020. Swallowing measures will require manual review of hard copies of data and will commence in January 2020. Analysis will then be conducted using additional measures of swallowing function, including participant-completed swallowing-related questionnaires, to identify structures that may be responsible for subjective and objective standards of dysphagia. Objective 2: Correlation of dosage to swallowing dysfunction has not yet been achieved. Gathering dosage information for each participant is highly time consuming, as each structure being investigated need to be manually identified and extracted by hand on whole-body CT scans. We are in the process of completing this, with 68 out of 78 participants' dosimetry information extracted. This is an ongoing process and is estimated to be completed by the end of February 202. The complete dosage data will then be sent to Dr. Harry Quon of John Hopkins University, a co-investigator of the study, for analysis to achieve this objective.

17103215.label: Major findings and research outcome
17103215.value: This study identified four structures related to swallowing that are correlated to longterm altered swallowing function following radiation therapy in a group of nasopharyngeal cancer survivors. During early analysis of a portion of the participants (n=20), pressures at the tongue base, upper esophageal opening, and throughout the esophagus were found to be associated with patient self-reported difficulties with swallowing and mealtimes. These findings offer insight into the biomechanical behaviours represented by subjective reports from patients, and therefore allows clinicians to make the appropriate corresponding intervention decisions. This was presented as a poster at the 8th European Society for Swallowing Disorders Congress in 2018 (please see part C of reports). In regards to our primary research objectives, several structures were identified as related to late stage dysphagia, including the inferior pharyngeal constrictors, glottic larynx, cricopharyngeus, and base of tongue. Of particular note is the finding of inferior pharyngeal constrictor (IPC): in contrast to the finding of the other structures having negative impacts on swallowing kinematics, radiation to the IPC seemed to better maintain swallowing kinematics. This points towards the need for further investigation into the relationship between the various structures of swallowing and their interactions. This has been submitted as a conference abstract to the American Head and Neck Society's 10th International Conference on Head and Neck Cancer, awaiting reviewer feedback.

17103215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17103215.value: Given the current findings, there is a need to further explore the dosage amount to the various structures investigated and how they interact to affect swallowing overall. Analyses of radiation dosage will be commencing soon, as describe din 5.3. Further statistical modelling will be conducted to elucidate the finding of IPC as a variable that seemed to have a positive correlation with swallowing kinematics. Investigation into other types of head and neck cancer will also be able to provide data to shed light on this novel finding. The PI currently has one GRF funded study examing NPC survivors, and another application awaiting review for non-NPC survivors. These studies and their findings will have clinical and theoretical value in the field of head and neck cancer.

17103215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17103215.value: Nasopharyngeal cancer is a highly prevalent form of cancer that affects a large number of people in Hong Kong. Survival rate has been improving, but the toxic side effects of radiation therapy can seriously compromise the quality of life of survivors. One major example is swallowing difficulties that result from radiation damage to the muscles of the mouth and neck areas. Swallowing difficulties reduce the individual's ability to safely and enjoyably eat and drink in daily life, leading to malnutrition and weight loss, and at its worst can lead to life threatening aspiration pneumonia. It is therefore highly important that swallowing difficulties are avoided. One method is to avoid structures that will later affect swallowing during radiation treatment, which the current study aimed to achieve. Our findings have identified structures that confirm some of the existing findings in this field. With confirmation of these findings, current practice in the treatment of nasopharyngeal cancer (and potentially other head and neck cancers) can be optimised to ensure best treatment outcomes with minimal side effects.

17104215.label: Realisation of objectives
17104215.value: We have successfully completed the project, and have published 2 research articles in J Biol Chem. Guo Y, An L, Ng HM, Sy SM, Huen MS. An E2-guided E3 screen identifies the RNF17-UBE2U pair as regulator of the RIDDLE syndrome protein RNF168. J Biol Chem 2017; 292(3):967-978. Ng HM, Wei L, Lan L, Huen MS. The K63-Deubiquitylating enzyme BRCC36 limits DNA break processing and repair. J Biol Chem 2016; 291(31):16197-207. Briefly, we have delineated how UBE2U participates in the DNA damage signal transduction pathway, and showed that UBE2U promotes cell survival in response to ionising radiation-induced DNA damage. By analysing the UBE2U interactome we found that UBE2U encodes a bona fide E2 enzyme with the Ring Finger protein RNF17 to promote RNF168-dependent DNA double-strand break responses. Moreover, we have also uncovered mechanistically how the deubiquitinase BRCC36 promotes BRCA1-dependent DNA damage responses, and found that BRCC36 deficiency is coupled with hyperactive DNA repair. Together, these findings highlight important roles of ubiquitin machineries in driving cellular responses to genotoxic stress.

17104215.label: Major findings and research outcome
17104215.value: By conducting a genetic screen for ubiquitin machineries that promote DNA double-strand break responses, we have identified the E2 enzyme UBE2U as a novel component of the mammalian cell responses to genotoxic stress. Following our analysis of the UBE2U interactome we have further delineated how UBE2U, in concert with its cognate E3 enzyme RNF17, enforces RNF168-dependent loading of DNA repair proteins 53BP1 and BRCA1 onto the damaged chromatin. Deficiency of UBE2U hyper-sensitise cells to DNA damage, highlighting UBE2U as a important component in the protection of genome integrity.

17104215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17104215.value: Intrigued by how the human ubiquitin machineries promote cell responses to DNA damage, we are now taking a lead to perform a genome wide screen to identify additional important players of the mammalian DNA damage responses using the platform we have established in this project. This undertaking will provide an important resource to further delineate how post-translational modifiers serve as molecular switches to dynamically regulate DNA repair processes.

17104215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17104215.value: Human ubiquitin machineries have emerged as important components of the mammalian DNA damage response. In this project we performed genetic screens to isolate novel factors that drive DNA repair processes, and have identified UBE2U as an important ubiquitin machinery that promotes cell responses to DNA double-strand breaks. Our findings not only highlight a pivotal role of UBE2U in genome integrity protection, but also implicates UBE2U dysregulation in fueling human tumourigenesis.

17104815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17104815.value: 基質金屬蛋白酶12在椎間盤纖維化中的作用和機理研究 後腰痛是世界範圍內的常見病，影響80%的人口。椎間盤退變與後腰痛密切相關。此外，退變會導致椎間盤脫出，並導致脊髓和神經根受壓，以及脊髓病和坐骨神經痛。病情嚴重者需要脊柱融合手術治療。然而手術會使該運動節段運動能力消失，並且可能誘發相鄰椎間盤退變。了解椎間盤退變將有助於本病的治療和預防，以及減少其造成的社會經濟負擔。 我們前期研究顯示，椎間盤退變與纖維化進程有關。然而，迄今為止，纖維化進程的分子機制仍不清楚。在其他組織和器官中，巨噬細胞和成肌纖維細胞為纖維化進程的主要效應細胞，兩者均表達基質金屬蛋白酶12（MMP12）。MMP12不僅是基質降解酶，它還能誘導巨噬細胞向炎症部位遷移，並被認為能協同調節其他基質金屬酶，包括MMP2和MMP3的表達。最新的研究表明MMP12也是一種新型轉錄因子，能夠調節細胞免疫相關蛋白的表達。這提示MMP12在炎症和纖維化中起重要調節作用。 我們最近的研究表明，在人體退變椎間盤細胞中，MMP12基因表達發生上調。同時，我們發現在纖維化的大鼠和人體退變椎間盤中MMP12陽性率增加。而且MMP12與肌成纖維細胞標記物α平滑肌肌動蛋白（α-SMA）和成纖維細胞特異性蛋白1（FSP1）存在共表達，提示退變椎間盤內的MMP12可能來源於肌成纖維細胞。我們進一步研究顯示，椎間盤內注射間質干細胞可以降低椎間盤纖維化水平，並通過旁分泌功能下調髓核內MMP12的表達。以上綜合表明，MMP12在椎間盤纖維化中起重要作用。 我們推測MMP12對椎間盤細胞穩態具有重要影響，可能是通過促進炎症信號以及與其他蛋白酶相互作用，例如促進促纖維化基質酶（如MMP3）的表達而抑制抗纖維化基質酶（如MMP2，MMP13）的表達，來導致椎間盤纖維化，然而具體影響仍不明。 我們有三個研究目標：1）闡明在人類椎間盤髓核纖維化和嚙齒類動物的椎間盤退變進程中MMP12的表達圖譜，以及MMP12的細胞來源; 2）通過體內外MMP12的敲除，驗証MMP12對椎間盤穩態及纖維化進程的影響; 3）研究在椎間盤退變過程中，MMP12是否能夠以及如何調節炎症信號。 據我們所知，這將是首次對MMP12在椎間盤退變過程中的表達和功能進行系統調查。從科學角度，這項研究將有助於我們解開椎間盤退變過程中所發生的生物學改變。揭示MMP12在椎間盤纖維化中的作用將有助於我們理解與椎間盤退變相關的關鍵生物學機理，從而進一步界定椎間盤退變的發病機制。從臨床角度，本研究將有助於推進治療椎間盤退變的生物學方案的設計和開發，以造福數百萬倍受腰痛折磨的患者。

17104815.label: Realisation of objectives
17104815.value: Intervertebral disc (IVD) degeneration is one of the major contributors of low back pain, a common chronic disorder that causes disability and tremendous socioeconomic burden worldwide. Nucleus pulposus (NP), the gelatinous core of IVD, losses its matrix content and undergoes fibrotic changes during the degeneration. This leads to compromised mechanical function of the IVD and hence motion segment instability under load. Matrix metalloproteinase 12 (MMP12) has an important role in myofibroblast activation in fibrosis disorders. MMP12 is markedly upregulated in myofibroblast differentiation. Moreover, MMP12 can regulate myofibroblast differentiation and enhance collagen deposition via limiting anti-fibrotic MMPs, including MMP2 and MMP13. In addition, IVD degeneration has been linked to an increase of MMP12 . In this study, we hypothesize that MMP12 expression in NP is associated with myofibroblast recruitment and bears a role in pro-inflammatory cascade signaling in IVD fibrosis progression. Objective 1: To elucidate the expression profile and cellular origin of MMP12 during fibrosis of nucleus pulposus in human and rodent IVD degeneration. We postulated that MMP12 expression is associated with fibrotic changes in NP during the disc degeneration. We collected the clinical IVDs from patients recruited in Queen Mary Hospital or in the collaboration with Prof. Zheng from The First Affiliated Hospital, Sun Yat-sen University. In isolated NP cells from degenerative and non-degenerative IVD samples, we studied the gene expression profile and determined MMP12 as the top differentially expressed fibrotic mediators. Histochemistry confirmed fibrotic changes in human degenerative NP tissues. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was performed in the paraffin sections of human NP specimens to identify MMP12+ cells in disc fibrosis. We also examined the expression in degenerative rat tail IVDs induced by puncture injury using immunostaining. Furthermore, we attempted to understand the identity of MMP12-expressing NP cells. We explored the myofibroblast phenotype of MMP12-expressing NP cells by immunofluorescence in both human and rat tail IVDs and quantitatively assessed their accumulation in disc degeneration by cell counting. Altogether, we gathered evidence that support an association of NP fibrosis in IVD degeneration with an increase of MMP12+ myofibroblastic cells. We have published the data as conference papers (2016, OARSI word congress; 2016, ORS annual meeting; 2016, MBSAZ annual meeting) and a research article in peer reviewed journal (2016, Osteoarthritis Cartilage). Objective 2: To validate the contribution of MMP12 to disc homeostasis through MMP12 depletion in vitro and in vivo. We postulated that MMP12 has a role in disc integrity and degeneration and investigated the consequence of MMP12 ablation. We imported MMP12-/- mice (B6.129X-Mmp12tm1Sds/J) from Jackson Laboratory and examined the disc structure and the progression of disc fibrosis and degeneration in punctured tail IVDs by histological and radiographical analysis. On the other hand, we knocked down MMP12 in human degenerative NP cells by siRNA transfection, verified by western blot and RT-qPCR, and examined the impact on myofibroblast markers expression. Overall we obtained evidence that supports a function of MMP12 in regulating myofibroblast-like phenotype in vitro and in vivo. Objective 3: To investigate if and how MMP12 regulates the inflammatory signaling in IVD fibrosis. We originally proposed to investigate the function of MMP12 in the inflammatory responses of NP cells. However, because our results indicated a distinct regulatory function of MMP12 in the myofibroblast phenotype of NP cells, we decided to continue this line of investigation and addressed how MMP12 may mediate myofibroblast differentiation of NP cells. TGF-β1 is a key cytokine to master myofibroblast differentiation in mesenchymal cells/fibroblast and epithelial-mesenchymal transition by activating Smad2/3 or p38 signaling. Excessive TGF-β1 activation is linked to IVD degeneration in mouse and bovine. Hence, we established an in-vitro model of myofibroblast differentiation of human non-degenerative and degenerative NP cells and described the expression pattern of MMP12. Contractile capacity of myofibroblastic NP cells were further examined by collagen contraction assay. On the other hand, loss of function study by MMP12 siRNA transfection was performed and myofibroblast differentiation was investigated by immunoblotting and qPCR. Overall, we gathered evidence to implicate a function of MMP12 in TGFb-mediated myofibroblastic differentiation of NP cells.

17104815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17104815.value: 1. Human degenerative NP showed significantly higher MMP12 expression along with lower KRT19 expression. Higher MMP12 positivity was found in peripheral NP and AF of the degenerative rat discs and in NP of the aged mice. In addition, human degenerative NP and AF showed increased α-SMA(+) cells, indicating enhanced myofibroblast activity. MMP12 was found co-expressed with α-SMA, FSP1 and FAP-α in human and rat degenerative IVDs. Dual positivity of MMP12/FSP1 or MMP12/αSMA (~13%) was markedly elevated in degenerated NP compared to non-degenerated specimens (~2%). These results implicate the association of MMP12 with myofibroblast markers in disc fibrosis and degeneration. (Data published in Lv F et al Osteoarthritis Cartilage, 2016) 2. Both human non-degenerative and degenerative NP cells showed markedly enhanced myofibroblast-like phenotype and contractile capacity in response to TGF-β1 via smad1/5/9 phosphorylation. While degenerative NP cells showed a higher endogenous level of MMP12 than non-degenerative NP cells, MMP12 expression could be significantly up-regulated by TGF-β1. Loss-of-function of MMP12 in dNP cells via siRNA transfection could abolish the myofibroblast markers expression in human degenerative NP cells. MMP12 knockout mice showed suppressed collagen deposition and myofibroblast phenotype compared to wild type in annulus puncture-induced disc degeneration. Notably, more disc height loss was found in punctured Mmp12-/- mice. Altogether this suggested an important role of MMP12 in the myofibroblast activation of NP cells and disc fibrosis. (Abstract accepted by ORS annual meeting and ISSLS meeting, 2019)

17104815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17104815.value: It has been suggested that fibrosis may involve fibrocyte differentiation into myofibroblasts. Function of MMP12 in fibrocyte-to-myofibroblast transition therefore warrant further investigation. We will use the MMP12-/- mice to study the fibrocyte-to-myofibroblast transition in annulus puncture-induced disc degeneration including immunostaining and flow cytometry analysis of relevant markers. NP cells from MMP12-/- discs will be isolated and nuclei transportation of MMP12 in myofibroblast transition will be further determined. ¬¬Accumulation of cells with macrophage-like phenotype in disc degeneration has been suggested. We will attempt to study MMP12 expression in these macrophage-like cells in NP fibrosis. After completion of project, we have been collecting further data related to the Mmp12 knockout mice and knockdown culture study to substantiate the findings. We are preparing a manuscript for submission to Osteoarthritis Cartilage or other equivalent journals. Grant application is also under preparation for the work proposed above.

17104815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17104815.value: Intervertebral disc (IVD) degeneration is common and linked to low back pain, a leading cause of disability and healthcare burden worldwide. Nucleus pulposus (NP) is the central jelly-like core of IVD which undergoes fibrotic changes during disc degeneration. MMP12 is a profibrogenic mediator in fibrotic disorders. In this study, we found MMP12 highly expressed in both human degenerative NP tissues and puncture-induced rat/mouse disc degeneration, and majorly localized in myofibroblast-like NP cells. TGF-β1 could induce myofibroblast-like phenotype in NP cells, and MMP12 deficiency could abolish such induction. Moreover, MMP12 depletion in transgenic mice resulted in a decreased number of myofibroblast-like cells and reduced disc fibrosis in puncture-induced disc degeneration. In conclusion, our study has indicated a function of MMP12 in IVD degeneration and mediating fibroblastic activity in NP cells.
