17105115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105115.value: Background Severe periodontal diseases such as periodontitis affect an estimated 1-2 billion people. They are one of the main causes of tooth-loss in adults. These infectious-inflammatory diseases result from chronic multi-species bacterial infections of the gums and tooth-supporting tissues. Bacteria known as ‘treponemes’ (genus Treponema) constitute a significant proportion of the human oral microbiota. More than 75 oral treponeme species or as-yet uncultivated species (phylotypes) have been identified. One species, Treponema denticola, is strongly associated with periodontal diseases. However, the roles of other treponeme species/phylotypes remain obscure; largely due to our ignorance of their respective genomic composition and biological activities. This greatly hinders our understanding of the etiology (causation) of periodontal diseases, and the identification of key disease-promoting pathways. Approach Here, we directly address this problem using a comparative bacterial genomics approach. In part 1, we will determine the complete genome sequences for 24 carefully-selected oral treponeme strains, which encompass multiple species and newly-proposed ‘species’. This includes isolates previously classified as ‘Treponema vincentii’ and Treponema medium, which our preliminary results show should be re-classified as novel species. A set of ‘Treponema denticola-like’ strains of canine origin will also be genome-sequenced. Dogs develop periodontal diseases analogous to humans, but have notable differences in their oral ‘microbiome’ composition. Specifically, we will analyze the genomic data to identify putative ‘virulence’ genes; and to establish inter-strain phylogenetic relationships (genetic ancestry) and genetic ‘signatures’ indicative of host specificity. In part 2, guided by our genomic data, we will establish the activities of three families of protein-degrading enzymes, which are highly-conserved within treponemes. These cell-surface proteases are implicated in several disease-promoting processes. Our initial analysis indicates there are key inter-species differences in their distributions, composition and predicted activities. Significance and Impact Key areas of oral treponeme taxonomy (species definition) remain confusing and very poorly defined. By delineating the genetic boundaries between various oral treponeme species, we will greatly improve our ability to accurately-establish the etiology of periodontal disease in different patient groups. To the best of our knowledge, there are no genome sequences for any oral treponeme species of animal origin. Through elucidating the genome sequences for canine oral treponeme isolates, we will gain a unique window into the similarities and differences between dog and human microbiota. Furthermore, by defining the activities of a diverse, and poorly-studied set of cell-surface proteases, we will establish how certain oral treponeme species may promote periodontal diseases more actively than others.

17105315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105315.value: 为改善乳制品结构和粘性，防止缩水作用及机械损伤，从食品级微生物获取的胞外多糖作为天然稳定剂，被广泛应用于奶制品行业用以替代化学合成稳定剂。胞外多糖产量与细菌菌种相关，温度、酸碱性及培养基组分也会影响胞外多糖产量。Shah教授在之前澳大利亚的实验室及现在香港大学实验室做了大量关于嗜热链球菌ASCC1275的研究工作并报告了这株菌最高的胞外多糖产量结果。这株菌被用于制造酸奶及马苏里拉奶酪，然而，在优化条件下其胞外多糖高产量的机理依然不明确。由于这株菌有较低的半乳糖利用活性，导致用添加了其胞外多糖的马苏里拉奶酪制作披萨时会产生严重的褐变。香港大学刚刚完成了这株菌的基因测序及生物信息学分析。我们计划对该菌进行不同酸碱性、温度及培养基组分条件下转录组学及蛋白组学的相关分析，以找到影响其胞外多糖分泌的关键基因。我们计划研究通过调节关键基因来增加其胞外多糖产量从而增强其对半乳糖的代谢。此项研究成果对发酵引物及发酵工业将有重要影响。

17105315.label: Realisation of objectives
17105315.value: This project aimed at carrying out transcriptomic and proteomic analyses to understand the genetic basis of EPS production and metabolic pathways of S. thermophilus 1275. The genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis had given insight into (i) biosynthesis pathway of EPS and its structural assembly from the eps gene cluster in this organism; and metabolic networks of amino acids (proteinase, dipeptidase) and carbohydrates (glucose, lactose, galactose). This helped discover genes responsible for regulation of EPS and their pathways for metabolism of galactose. The project also planned to carry out transcriptomic and proteomic analyses of this organism grown under various pH, temperature and nutrients to understand the basis of EPS production. Transcriptomic and proteomic analysis was able to identify differential expressed proteins during various growth conditions, thus we were able to identify key genes in nutrient metabolism networks during the stimulation processes. Additionally, amino acids and sugar metabolism in S. thermophilus ASCC 1275 have been revealed from its genome. Lack of essential amino acids biosynthesis in this strain affected the production of EPS and metabolism of galactose. From this study, knowledge of various genes regulating EPS production was achieved, and mechanisms of gene regulatory networks in EPS production in S. thermophilus 1275 under optimized conditions was for the first time be systematically revealed. All the objectives of this project are successfully completed.

17105315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17105315.value: A novel eps gene cluster for EPS assembly containing two-pair epsC-epsD genes for determining the chain length of EPS was found; S. thermophilus 1275 (ST1275) produces two types of EPSs. Additionally, ST 1275 exhibited effective proteolytic system, and the highest number of four separate CRISPR/Cas loci allowing this organism to adapt to milk. Functional genomic analyses of S. thermophilus ASCC 1275 for EPS production: pH decrease induced most differentially expressed proteins that are involved in stress responses, glutamate catabolism, arginine biosynthesis, cysteine catabolism, purine metabolism, and lactose uptake. Concordance analysis for DEPs demonstrated glutamate catabolism and purine metabolism at pH 5.5. Down-regulation of EpsB involved in EPS assembly was observed at both mRNA and protein level at pH 5.5. The mRNA-seq analysis and targeted pathway analysis indicated that genes associated with lactose catabolism, EPS assembly, proteolytic activity, and arginine/methionine/cysteine synthesis and transport in ST1275 were significantly up-regulated under the optimized conditions of pH 5.5, 40°C or WPI supplementation compared to that of pH 6.5 and 37°C, respectively. This indicates that genes involved in above metabolisms co-operate together for improving EPS yield from ST1275. We investigated the influence of glucose, sucrose and lactose, at log phase (5 h) and stationary phase (10 h), on the global proteomics of S. thermophilus 1275 to understand the differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) during EPS production using isobaric tags for relative and absolute quantitation (iTRAQ)-based proteomic analysis. Among 98 DEPs in sucrose medium, most of them were mapped into epS biosynthesis pathway and other related metabolisms. There was upregulation of several proteins involved in sugar transport (phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) phosphotransferase system), EPS assembly (epsG1D) and amino acid metabolism (methionine, cysteine/arginine metabolism) in sucrose medium. This study showed that increased EPS production requires a well-co-ordinated regulation of pathway involved in both EPS assembly and amino acid metabolism along with the availability of sugars. Differential gene expression analysis revealed the involvement of phosphoenolpyruvate phosphotransferase system (PEP-PTS) for glucose and sucrose uptake, and lacS gene for lactose uptake. The pathways for the formation of UDP-glucose and UDP-galactose were highly upregulated in all the three sugars. In the presence of sucrose, eps1C1D2C2D were found to be highly expressed which refers to high EPS production. Protein homology study suggested the presence of Wzx/Wzy-dependent EPS synthesis and transport pathway in this bacterium. KEGG pathway and COG functional enrichment analysis were also performed to support the result. Structural characterization of exopolysaccharide: Three fractions (F) obtained from gel permeation chromatography were termed F1 (2.6%), F2 (45.8%), and F3 (51.6%) with average molecular weights of approximately 511, 40, and 5 kDa, respectively. Monosaccharide composition analysis revealed the dominance of glucose, galactose, and mannose in all 3 fractions. A possible structure of EPS in F2 and F3 was proposed.

17105315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17105315.value: Knowledge of various genes regulating EPS production, and mechanisms of gene regulatory networks in EPS production in S. thermophilus 1275 under optimized conditions have been for the first time systematically revealed. This will enable yogurt or starter and cheese manufacturers to predict the quality of the product and minimize the variations in EPS production and browning due to galactose in Mozzarella cheese during pizza making. Understanding the genetic basis of role of sugars particularly galactose as a substrate in the production/synthesis of EPS and their role in improving texture and stability of a product will provide vital information. This discovery from this study will be vital for starter culture and dairy industry. A follow up project is already underway to improve quality of yogurt and Mozzarella cheese and is likely to be taken up by the manufacturer of yogurt and Mozzarella cheese.

17105315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17105315.value: EPS-producing dairy starter cultures improve the quality of dairy products, such as improving viscosity, and preventing syneresis in fermented milks and yoghurt. The amount of EPS synthesized is highly variable and is influenced by the starter culture used and growth conditions (temperature, pH and composition). The project aimed at examining ways to increase EPS production and structure of eps gene cluster responsible for the production of EPS in S. thermophilus (ST) and elucidating the mechanism of EPS production. Functional genomic analyses of ST for EPS production were carried out in this project. A novel eps gene cluster for EPS assembly containing two-pair epsC-epsD genes for determining the chain length of EPS was found. Proteomic analysis reveals potential factors associated with enhanced epS production in ST. Differential gene expression analysis revealed the involvement of phosphoenolpyruvate phosphotransferase system (PEP-PTS) for glucose and sucrose uptake, and lacS gene for lactose uptake. The pathways for the formation of UDP-glucose and UDP-galactose were highly upregulated in three sugars (glucose, sucrose and lactose). Transcriptomic insights into the growth phase- and sugar-associated changes in the exopolysaccharide production and mechanism of a high EPS-producing ST were revealed. Structural characterization of exopolysaccharide in ST was carried out.

17105615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105615.value: 酰基輔酶Ａ結合蛋白（ＡＣＢＰ）是一個參與酰基與脂類間新陳代謝的蛋白家族。家族成員共有一個能結合長鏈酰基酶Ａ的保守結構域，這個結構域可以促進對脂類的結合。在哺乳動物，線蟲以及植物中，ＡＣＢＰ被發現參與早期發育和脅迫反應，並且這些功能是保守的。植物ＡＣＢＰ分為四類：第一類（１０ｋＤ小分子量ＡＣＢＰ），第二類（具有ａｎｋｙｒｉｎ重複序列的ＡＣＢＰ），第三類（在Ｃ末端具有酰基輔酶Ａ結合域的ＡＣＢＰ）以及第四類（具有Ｋｅｌｃｈ基序的ＡＣＢＰ）。在這份研究企劃中，我們將比較在單子葉植物和雙子葉植物之中的第一類和第二類ＡＣＢＰ。我們選擇單子葉植物水稻（Oryza Sativa）源於其為支持超過全球半數人口的重要糧食作物。對於調控水稻早期發育和脅迫反應的基因的研究將會與農業與糧食生產休戚相關。這份研究企劃來源於對單子葉植物（水稻）和雙子葉植物（擬南芥，Arabidopsis thaliana）中第一類與第二類ＡＣＢＰ觀測中發現的的一些有趣的變化。雖然在水稻與擬南芥中存在六個ＡＣＢＰ，但是它們在各個類別中的分佈是不同的。水稻第一類ＡＣＢＰ包括三個成員，我們定義其為水稻酰基輔酶Ａ結合蛋白１（ＯｓＡＣＢＰ１），水稻酰基輔酶Ａ結合蛋白２（ＯｓＡＣＢＰ２）以及水稻酰基輔酶Ａ結合蛋白３（ＯｓＡＣＢＰ３），與之相較，擬南芥中只有一個第一類ＡＣＢＰ，擬南芥酰基輔酶Ａ結合蛋白６（ＡｔＡＣＢＰ６）。並且，水稻中僅有一個第二類ＡＣＢＰ，酰基輔酶Ａ結合蛋白４（ＯｓＡＣＢＰ４），相比之下，擬南芥中有兩個，擬南芥酰基輔酶Ａ結合蛋白１（ＡｔＡＣＢＰ１）和擬南芥酰基輔酶Ａ結合蛋白２（ＡｔＡＣＢＰ２）。這份企劃的目標是解釋第一類與第二類ＡＣＢＰ在兩種植物中的差異，並且特別關注他們在早期發育和脅迫反應中可能存在的非冗餘功能。另外，水稻酰基輔酶Ａ結合蛋白３（ＯｓＡＣＢＰ３）是一種特別的第一類ＡＣＢＰ，它不僅被定位於細胞液中，還存在於細胞內其他位置。ＯｓＡＣＢＰ３有一個Ｃ末端延伸，它被定位於不同的亞細胞結構中。因此，另一個研究目標是解釋Ｃ末端延伸的作用，這或許可以揭示ＯｓＡＣＢＰ３的特別功能。我們將使用自發熒光來標記ＯｓＡＣＢＰ３的Ｃ末端，用以研究ＯｓＡＣＢＰ３的亞細胞定位。此外，在這項研究中，我們將使用反向遺傳學，生物化學，分子生物學，顯微技術和報告基因融合技術。我們預期可以揭示１）第一類ＯｓＡＣＢＰ是否存在功能上的冗餘；２）ＯｓＡＣＢＰ３的Ｃ末端延伸的意義以及３）ＯｓＡＣＢＰ４（第二類ＯｓＡＣＢＰ）的功能。

17105915.label: Realisation of objectives
17105915.value: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is the principal dialysis modality used in Hong Kong. The success of PD is dependent on the structural and functional integrity of the peritoneal membrane. The normal peritoneal membrane is lined by a monolayer of mesothelial cells, which provides the first line of defence against chemical and bacterial injury and plays an important role in reparative as well as fibrotic processes. Peritoneal fibrosis and subsequent loss of peritoneal transport function is a common complication that affects all PD patients and may contribute to PD cessation. The mechanisms that initiates peritoneal fibrosis remains to fully defined. MicroRNAs are endogenous short non-coding RNA molecules that regulate gene expression at the post-transcriptional level, either through mRNA degradation or inhibiting protein translation of their specific targets. The role of microRNA-200c (miR-200c) in cancer and metastasis has been extensively studied, and is reported to repress epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and maintain epithelial phenotype. This study aimed to investigate the role of miR-200c in peritoneal dialysis (PD)-associated peritoneal fibrosis and included animal, in vitro and ex vivo studies. We have fully completed Objectives 1, 2 and 4, and Objective 3 will be completed within the next 4-6 months. Objective 1: miR-200c was constitutively expressed in cultured human peritoneal mesothelial cells. Incubation of cells with glucose-based conventional PD fluid for 24 h decreased miR-200c expression by 21.83 +/- 4.52% compared to cells incubated with serum free medium (P<0.001). We and others have previously reported that glucose-based PD fluids mediate their detrimental effect on mesothelial cell fibrogenesis through TGF-beta1 activation. Incubation of mesothelial cells with exogenous TGF-beta1 (0.1, 1.0 and 10 ng/ml) decreased miR-200c expression in a dose-dependent manner, with a 41% reduction at 10 ng/ml TGF-beta1 compared to serum-free medium (P<0.001). Repression of miR-200c was accompanied by a significant decrease in E-cadherin expression and increased gene and protein expression of the mesenchymal markers ZEB2, Notch1, Jagged2, SNAIL, fibroblast specific protein-1, alpha-smooth muscle actin, collagen I and fibronectin. Whereas the induction of the aforementioned mesenchymal markers was apparent after 24 h incubation with TGFbeta1, phenotypic changes in mesothelial cells was observed after 48 h. To confirm that miR-200c regulated epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in mesothelial cells, lentivector-based miR precursor constructs (lenti-miR-200c) were used to over-express miR-200c in Met-5A cells (an immortalized cell line of human mesothelial cells). Lenti-miR-200c increased miR-200c expression in Met-5A cells by 414.7 +/- 65.6 and 419.8 +/- 74.5 -fold compared with non-transfected and lenti-scramble-transfected cells respectively. miR-200c over-expression had no effect on cell viability, attachment, proliferation or morphology, or constitutive gene and protein expression of E-cadherin, transcription factors relating to EMT or fibronectin, but significantly decreased collagen I and collagen III expression. In cells stimulated with TGF-beta1 for 24 h, miR-200c over-expression attenuated TGF-beta1-induced SNAIL, ZEB2, Notch1, Jagged2, fibronectin, collagen I and collagen III expression, and partially increased E-cadherin gene expression. To identify putative direct targets of miR-200c, we searched the TargetScan database for miR-200c target sites in mRNA sequences of known repressors of E-cadherin, and TargetScan predicted that ZEB2, Jagged2 and Notch1 were likely candidates, with their 3-UTR containing 6, 1 and 1 binding sites respectively for miR-200c. Mutation studies and luciferase reporter assays were undertaken, and identified ZEB2 and Notch1 as direct targets of miR-200c in mesothelial cells, whereas the interaction of miR-200c with Jagged2 in mesothelial cells was indirect. Objectives 2 & 3: miR-200c was constitutively expressed in the peritoneal membrane of saline-treated mice, and quantitative miR-200c expression did not differ with time. In our experimental model of PD, administration of conventional glucose-based PD fluid to C57BL/6 mice by twice daily intra-peritoneal injection reduced peritoneal miR-200c expression by ~80% after 3 days of PD compared to control mice and this decrease was sustained until study’s end. Decreased peritoneal miR-200c expression preceded induction of fibrogenic markers by at least 1 month, with an increase in fibronectin expression in the mesothelium, and an increase in the number of alpha-smooth muscle actin-positive elongated cells in a collagen-enriched submesothelium. Peritoneal membrane thickening was not apparent until after 2 months of PD, and was accompanied by denudation of the mesothelium and loss of tight junctions, increased expression of collagen I, collagen III and fibronectin and increased infiltration of immune cells. Studies to over-express miR-200c in the peritoneal membrane are currently ongoing and we have now optimized the dose of lenti-miR-200c and frequency of administration. Our studies have shown that miR-200c over-expression in the peritoneum resulted in ~60-70% reduction in peritoneal membrane thickening. Staining of EMT transcription factors, mesothelial cell activation and identifying sub-populations of infiltrating cells that contribute to peritoneal fibrosis are currently ongoing and we plan to complete all animal studies within 4-6 months. Objective 4: Denudation of mesothelial cells from the peritoneum and their isolation from dialysate was not apparent until 6 months after initiation of PD. Mesothelial cells isolated from PD fluid initially yielded a homogenous population of epithelial, polygonal cells. After 12 months of PD, senescent mesothelial cells were observed in culture and these cells showed a low proliferative capacity, decreased E-cadherin expression and increased fibronectin expression. Dialysate miR-200c level increased with time on PD and this was accompanied by a concomitant decrease in dialysate CA125 (marker of mesothelial cell mass), and decorin (marker of anti-fibrosis) levels and increased dialysate hyaluronan level (marker of inflammation and fibrosis). Taken together, our findings suggest that miR-200c plays an important role in regulating epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and fibrogenesis in mesothelial cells. With increasing time on PD, peritoneal membrane miR-200c expression is reduced and is accompanied by an increase in dialysate miR-200c level. Whether the measurement of dialysate miR-200c may serve as a surrogate marker of mesothelial cell denudation and peritoneal fibrosis warrants further investigation.

17105915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17105915.value: microRNAs (miRs) are a family of endogenous short non-coding RNAs that regulate gene expression at the post-translational level. Dysregulated miR expression has been detected in pathological conditions such as cancer and tissue fibrosis and several miRs have been implicated in the regulation of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) resulting in the repression or promotion of EMT and fibrosis. miR-200c has been reported to repress EMT transcription factors and preserve epithelial cell-cell contacts, but its role in mesothelial cells remains to be defined. The study aimed to investigate the role of miR-200c in peritoneal fibrosis and peritoneal mesothelial cell EMT and to identify its target genes in the context of PD. PD fluid-treated mice showed ~80% reduction in miR-200c expression after 3 days when compared to saline-treated mice, and a reduction in peritoneal miR-200c expression was accompanied by increased peritoneal alpha-smooth muscle actin, fibronectin and collagen expression, increased infiltration of immune cells, and mesothelial denudation. Lentivirus-mediated miR-200c over-expression administered by intraperitoneal injection markedly reduced peritoneal membrane thickening and infiltration of immune cells. In cultured mesothelial cells, glucose-based PD fluid significantly reduced miR-200c compared to serum-free medium and this was mediated, at least in part, through TGF-beta1. Incubation of mesothelial cells with exogenous TGF-beta1 reduced miR-200c in a dose-dependent manner and this was accompanied by down-regulation of E-cadherin expression, and increased ZEB2, Jagged2, Notch1, SNAIL, FSP-1, fibronectin and collagen gene and protein expression. Lentivirus-mediated miR-200c over-expression attenuated TGF-beta1-induced markers of EMT and fibrosis in mesothelial cells. Mutation studies and luciferase reporter assays showed that miR-200c directly targeted Notch1 and ZEB2 and indirectly targeted Jagged2. In PD patients, dialysate miR-200c level increased with PD duration, and showed a negative correlation with dialysate CA125 level, a marker of mesothelial cell mass. Taken together, our results suggest an important role of miR-200c in PD-associated peritoneal fibrosis. Part of the data have been presented at 3 international conferences including the American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week 2016, which is the top-ranked international nephrology meeting. Part of the data generated from this study have also been included in an invited lecture given at the 17th Congress of the International Society for Peritoneal Dialysis, in Vancouver.

17105915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17105915.value: In our ex vivo studies, we demonstrated a negative correlation between dialysate miR-200c and CA125 levels suggesting that as mesothelial cell mass is reduced with increasing PD duration, miR-200c may be released from mesothelial cells and may serve as a surrogate marker of mesothelial cell injury. Since this study used dialysate from 30 PD patients collected over the course of 1 year, further studies are warranted to determine the long-term effect of PD on dialysate miR-200c level and whether it can be used as a surrogate marker of mesothelial cell injury. The miR-200 family comprises 5 members, namely miR-200a, miR-200b, miR-200c, miR-141 and miR-429. Potential for further development of this research would be to investigate whether changes in miR-200c expression is accompanied by changes in the other 4 members and whether any of the other miR-200 members may compensate for miR-200c deficiency in mesothelial cells. If preliminary data are encouraging, we will apply for funding support from the RGC General Research Fund or Food and Health Bureau to further elucidate the role of miR-200 family in peritoneal inflammation and fibrosis.

17105915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17105915.value: Peritoneal dialysis (PD) is the primary dialysis modality used in Hong Kong. Although PD has greatly improved the quality of life in renal patients, progressive peritoneal fibrosis affect all patients on long-term PD and results in increased morbidity and mortality. Presently there is no effective means to prevent or treat peritoneal fibrosis in PD, which is essential in order to preserve the structural and functional integrity of the peritoneal membrane. There is evidence that microRNA-200c (miR-200c) may repress transition of epithelial cells to an elongated fibroblastic phenotype, a process termed epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT), which precedes tissue fibrosis. In this study, we demonstrated in a mouse PD model that peritoneal miR-200c expression is significantly decreased compared to control mice and this reduction precedes submesothelial thickening and onset of peritoneal fibrosis. In cultured mesothelial cells, miR-200c over-expression suppressed mediators of EMT and fibrosis induced by TGF-beta1, whereas miR-200c deficiency promoted mesothelial cell fibrogenesis. In PD patients, a loss of mesothelial cell mass was accompanied by the release of miR-200c from mesothelial cells into the dialysate, which may serve as a potential marker of peritoneal membrane injury. Our data provide novel insight into the pathogenesis of PD-associated peritoneal fibrosis.

17106015.label: Project Objectives
17106015.value: We will measure the levels of LPS, LBP and sCD14 in sera obtained from patients with lupus nephritis to ascertain whether these proteins may be considered biomarkers of disease activity. We will measure serum levels and intra-renal expression of LPS, LBP and sCD14 during progressive lupus nephritis in NZBWF1/J mice and delineate their correlation with clinical, serological and histological parameters of disease, with particular focus on apoptotic, inflammatory and fibrotic processes. Age- and sex-matched BALB/c mice will be used as controls. We will investigate the structural integrity of the intestinal epithelium with progressive disease, its permeability to FITC-dextran and FITC-LPS, and whether these molecules can translocate from the gastrointestinal tract to the kidney and circulation. We will determine the underlying mechanisms through which anti-dsDNA antibodies increase LBP and CD14 synthesis in HMC and PTEC and the involvement of cytokines and growth factors. We will determine the functional roles of LBP and CD14 in HMC and PTEC. We will over-express LBP and CD14 in both cell types and determine their roles in mesangial and tubular epithelial cell activation, proliferation, viability, apoptosis, and in the synthesis of pro-inflammatory cytokines and matrix proteins. Since monocytes/macrophages play important roles in tubular injury, we will isolate CD14+ monocytes from lupus nephritis patients and co-culture them with PTEC to ascertain whether overexpression of CD14 in PTEC will increase PTEC-monocyte interactions and inflammatory processes.

17106015.label: Realisation of objectives
17106015.value: We have completed Objectives 1, 2, 3 and 4, and Objective 5 will be completed within the next 4-6 months. Objective 1: Paired serum samples, one collected during renal relapse and the other during remission, were obtained from adult patients with kidney biopsy-proven class III/IV+/-V lupus nephritis (LN) (n=50). Control groups included healthy subjects and patients with non-proliferative chronic kidney disease (n=50 for both groups). Serum LPS, LBP, and sCD14 levels were determined and results were correlated with serological and clinical parameters of disease and cytokine levels. Serum LPS level was significantly higher in LN patients when compared to healthy subjects and patients with non-lupus renal disease (P<0.001, for both), and the level was comparable between LN patients with renal relapse and remission (P=0.34). Serum LBP and sCD14 levels were significantly higher in LN patients with active disease compared to LN patients in remission, healthy subjects and patients with non-lupus renal diseases. LPS level inversely correlated with IgG level (P=0.029), whereas LBP level correlated with that of anti-dsDNA antibody (P=0.003), sCD14 (P<0.001), IL-6 (P<0.05), and IL-8 (P=0.014) levels. CD14 level correlated with that of anti-dsDNA antibody (P<0.001), IL-6 (P=0.013), and IL-8 (P=0.039) levels, and inversely with C3 level (P=0.024). ROC analysis showed that serum LPS, LBP and sCD14 levels distinguished patients with active LN from healthy subjects and patients with non-lupus renal disease (P<0.001, for all), but they could not distinguish between active LN and remission (P = 0.56, 0.63 and 0.57 respectively). Objectives 2 and 3: NZBWF1/J mice spontaneously develop features of LN such as deposition of immune complexes in the kidney parenchyma, anti-dsDNA antibody production, increased tubulo-interstitial infiltration of immune cells, and proteinuria. We bred NZB mice with NZW mice to generate NZBWF1/J mice. Female NZBWF1/J mice were sacrificed at different stages of disease at 8, 16, 25 and 35 weeks of age, which represented pre-disease, production of anti-dsDNA antibodies, onset of nephritis and tubulo-interstitial fibrosis respectively. Age- and sex-matched BALB/c mice served as controls. Blood, kidneys and colons were collected for analysis. In a proportion of mice, FITC-LPS was administered by oral gavage 4 h before sacrifice to investigate whether FITC-LPS could be detected in the kidney, which would indicate increased permeability of the gut. Renal histology in NZBWF1/J mice with active disease showed increased mesangial proliferation, glomerular expansion, glomerular basement membrane thickening and increased collagen and fibronectin deposition in both the glomerular and tubulo-interstitial compartments. IgG deposition was predominantly localized to the glomeruli, with IgG staining also detected along the tubular basement membrane although to a lesser extent. Mononuclear cell infiltration was noted in the periglomerular, perivascular and interstitial space in mice at 25 weeks of age. As disease progressed, tubulo-interstitial infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells and CD19+ B cells and tubulitis became apparent, with glomerulosclerosis and tubulo-interstitial inflammation and tubular atrophy occurring at 30-35 weeks of age. LBP and CD14 expression increased in NZBWF1/J mice with progressive lupus nephritis, and was more pronounced in proximal tubular epithelial cells especially in tubules that had undergone atrophy, and within the interstitium with prominent immune cell infiltration. Circulating anti-dsDNA antibody and LPS levels increased with progressive disease. FITC-LPS was detected in sera and urine samples in NZBWF1/J mice with active disease, and this was accompanied by positive LPS-FITC staining in proximal tubular epithelial cells in NZBWF1/J mice. FITC-LPS could not be detected in the serum, urine or kidneys of age-matched BALB/c mice. To investigate whether circulating LPS level and its detection in the kidney was associated with a leaky intestinal epithelium, we next investigated structural changes in the colon of NZBWF1/J and BALB/c mice. H&E staining of colon specimens from 8-week old NZBWF1/J and BALB/c mice were comparable, with numerous mucosal folds comprising a well-defined mucosal epithelium, and crypts of Lieberkuhn containing numerous goblet cells. Although inter-group comparison showed no apparent histological changes in the colon, mucosal epithelial expression of ZO-1, claudin, LBP and CD14 was markedly reduced in the colon of pre-nephritic NZBWF1/J mice. As disease progressed, colonic expression of ZO-1 and claudin became negligible with reduced LBP and CD14 expression. 16S rRNA analysis revealed that active LN in NZBWF1/J mice was associated with increased Gram-negative bacteria including Proteobacteria and Bacteroides, and a decrease in Gram-positive bacteria. Objectives 4 and 5: Given that LBP and CD14 expression was predominantly increased in proximal tubular epithelial cells in the kidney, we next investigated the functional role of LBP and CD14 in HK-2 cells. These cells are normal human proximal tubular epithelial cells immortalized by transduction with the human papilloma virus 16 E6/E7 genes. We demonstrated that under basal conditions, HK-2 cells weakly expressed LBP and CD14, whereas incubation of HK-2 cells with human polyclonal anti-dsDNA antibodies increased the expression of both proteins (P<0.05, for both), mediated at least in part, through IFN-alpha, IFN-gamma, IGF and EGF. Exogenous LPS increased LBP and sCD14 in HK-2 cells in a time- and dose-dependent manner and this was accompanied by increased IL-6 and IL-8 secretion, and increased fibronectin expression. Increased fibronectin expression is considered an early event in tubulo-interstitial fibrosis, which serves as a temporary scaffold for the deposition of other matrix proteins such as collagen and laminin. Since LBP and CD14 expression was increased in proximal tubular epithelial cells in NZBWF1/J mice, we generated HK-2 cells that overexpressed LBP and CD14. Both cell lines showed no changed in cell viability or proliferation compared to non-transfected HK-2 cells. We demonstrated that in the absence of any stimulation, HK-2 cells overexpressing CD14, but not LBP, was accompanied by increased IL-6 and IL-8 secretion, and fibronectin expression, and the addition of LPS further increased inflammatory and fibrotic processes, mediated in part, through increased activation of ERK, p38 MAPK, JNK and PI3K signaling pathways. We further demonstrated that CD14 overexpression in HK-2 cells further increased fibrotic processes induced by TGF-beta1, a key mediator of kidney fibrosis. The role of CD14 in inflammatory and fibrotic processes was validated in HK-2 cells deficient in CD14. Studies are currently ongoing to investigate whether increased CD14 expression in HK-2 cells can increase macrophage binding and subsequent inflammatory responses. We envisage that these studies will be completed within 4 to 6 months. Conclusion In this study, we demonstrated that serum LPS, LBP and sCD14 levels are increased in LN patients, especially during active disease when compared to healthy subjects and patients with non-lupus renal diseases. Serum LPS, LBP and sCD14 levels correlated with serological markers of immunological activity and cytokine levels. LBP and CD14 expression was increased in lupus-prone mice with active nephritis and was predominantly localized to the proximal tubular epithelial cells. Increased LBP and CD14 expression contributed to inflammatory and fibrotic processes in the tubulo-interstitium and may also mediate increased LPS binding to the kidney parenchyma to exacerbate kidney inflammation and fibrosis. Increased circulating LPS level may originate from the gut microbiota since active nephritis was associated with dysbiosis (imbalance of the gut microbiota), with increased abundance of Gram-negative bacteria phyla and a decrease in Gram-positive bacteria. We further demonstrated increased permeability of the intestinal mucosa in NZBWF1/J mice, which permitted gut microbial components to enter the circulation and distribute in organs distant from the gastrointestinal tract, e.g. kidney, and contribute to pathogenesis of disease.

17106015.label: Major findings and research outcome
17106015.value: LN is one of the most severe manifestations in SLE as reflected by its detrimental effect on patient and kidney survival. Insight into the underlying mechanisms that contribute to disease pathogenesis may offer novel targets for therapeutic intervention. In this study, we observed increased serum LPS level in LN patients compared to control groups, which correlated with immunological activity. We demonstrated that active nephritis in NZBWF1/J mice was associated with a leaky gut characterized by a loss of tight junctions including ZO-1 and claudin. Further analysis of colon specimens showed a reduction in goblet cells - cells that secrete mucin, which forms a protective mucus layer. Active nephritis was accompanied by an increase in the abundance in Gram-negative bacteria such as Proteobacteria species, with a reduction in Gram-positive bacteria. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) is a major component of the outer wall of Gram-negative bacteria and it is one of the most potent activators of the mammalian innate immune system. We demonstrated that serum LPS level was increased in NZBWF1/J mice with active disease compared to age- and sex-matched non-autoimmune BALB/c mice, and it originated, at least in part, from the gut microbiota. A leaky gut permitted FITC-LPS to translocate from the gastrointestinal tract to the circulation and kidney in NZBWF1/J mice, and FITC-LPS was predominantly localized to proximal tubular epithelial cells, and also to infiltrating cells, although to a lesser extent. Examination of kidney specimens from NZBWF1/J mice demonstrated that LBP and CD14 expression was increased in proximal tubular epithelial cells, induced by anti-dsDNA antibodies, and which may enhance LPS binding in the kidney to exert subsequent downstream inflammatory and fibrotic processes. We next generated HK-2 cells that overexpressed LBP and CD14, and demonstrated that in the absence of any stimuli, CD14, but not LBP contributed to increased IL-6 and IL-8 secretion, and fibronectin expression, and these inflammatory and fibrogenic processes were exacerbated in the presence of LPS and TGF-beta1, mediated through increased activation of MAPK and PI3K signaling pathways. Taken together, our findings demonstrated that there is an abundance of Gram-negative bacteria in lupus-prone mice with active nephritis, and LPS translocated from the gut to the circulation and kidney in LN, and this may contribute to tubulo-interstitial inflammation and fibrosis. Part of these findings have been presented at international conferences such as the American Society of Nephrology Kidney Week (top-ranked nephrology conference), and the ISN World Congress of Nephrology.

17106015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17106015.value: Based on our findings from this project, we demonstrated that there is an increased abundance of Gram-negative bacteria in lupus-prone mice with active nephritis. We have conducted preliminary studies and have confirmed that the abundance of Gram-negative bacteria is also increased in LN patients with renal relapse compared to disease quiescence. We will apply for funding support to further this study using clinical samples from LN patients. In this study, we have identified a novel function of CD14 in contributing to kidney inflammation and fibrosis independent of its role as a ligand for LPS. We were awarded a grant from RGC General Research Fund 2020/21 to further investigate the role of CD14 in chronic kidney disease.

17106015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17106015.value: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a common cause of kidney injury in this locality. A greater understanding of the mechanisms that contribute to kidney disease may offer novel therapeutic options. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) is a component of the outer wall of Gram-negative bacteria and is one of the most potent activators of the innate immune system. In this study, we demonstrated that circulating LPS level was higher in patients and mice with active LN compared to controls, that LPS originated from the gut microbiota, and it translocated from the gut to the circulation and kidney since the expression of tight junctions - proteins that prevent leakage of gut microbial components, were absent. LBP and CD14 bind LPS and permit LPS to exert its damaging effect. LBP and CD14 expression were increased in the kidneys of lupus-prone mice, and was induced by anti-dsDNA antibodies. Further studies revealed that CD14 overexpression contributed to inflammatory and fibrotic processes in the kidney through activation of signaling pathways, and increased cytokine secretion and extracellular matrix proteins. Our studies highlight the contribution of LPS in LN pathogenesis. Improving the balance between good and bad bacteria in the gut may be beneficial to LN patients.

17106315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106315.value: The cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) is an anion channel that conducts chloride and bicarbonate ions for regulating electrolyte transport and pH homeostasis in epithelial cells. Dysfunction of CFTR by genetic mutations disrupts the normal epithelial function leading to a life-threatening disease cystic fibrosis (CF). The most common CF mutation ΔF508, deleting a phenylalanine residue at position 508, is carried by about 90% of patients with CF. ΔF508 mutation heavily impairs the protein processing and channel activity of CFTR, resulting in a profound reduction in transepithelial chloride and bicarbonate transport. Since CFTR conducts chloride ions better than bicarbonate ions, early studies mainly focus on how to restore chloride transport in the CF epithelia. Recent studies demonstrate that CFTR-mediated bicarbonate secretion is associated with the severity of CF diseases, mucus properties, bacterial killing and innate defense system such as superoxide formation in the airway surface fluid. Moreover, partially restoring the airway chloride transport of CFTR(ΔF508/ΔF508) pigs fails to prevent CF-like lung diseases. These studies suggest that defective bicarbonate secretion may be a leading cause of CF diseases. Since our recent study shows that acidic intracellular pH (pHi) directly stimulates CFTR activity, bicarbonate secretion by CFTR or anion exchangers may possibly cause proton retention intracellularly leading to localized acidosis, which may further stimulate CFTR activity for more bicarbonate secretion. This mechanism forms positive feedback provoking epithelial bicarbonate secretion. Our preliminary data demonstrate that bicarbonate efflux stimulated the channel activity of wild-type CFTR, supporting this mechanism. In addition, acidic pHi-induced stimulation on channel gating was altered in ΔF508-CFTR. Thus, we hypothesize that this positive-feedback mechanism of bicarbonate secretion is defective in ΔF508-CFTR. To test this hypothesis, we firstly want to know the origin of CFTR pHi sensitivity for further exploring the mechanism how the pHi sensitivity of ΔF508-CFTR is altered. Several pH-sensitive amino acid residues close to the ATP binding sites in CFTR will be studied for understanding their roles in generating the pHi sensitivity. Second, the effects of bicarbonate efflux and influx on the channel activity of ΔF508-CFTR will be tested. Finally, the amount of bicarbonate and chloride secretion will be compared in the cultured epithelia expressing wild-type or ΔF508-CFTR. Our study would elucidate the mechanisms of CFTR-mediated bicarbonate secretion in the epithelial cells and how it is defective in ΔF508-CFTR.

17107415.label: Realisation of objectives
17107415.value: For objective 1, 13 complete genomes from samples of four different wild rodent species (chestnut spiny rat, Coxing’s white-bellied rat, roof rat and Indochinese forest rat) positive for “Rosavirus C” and one street rodent species (Norway rat) positive for “Rosavirus B” were sequenced. Phylogenetic trees were constructed using the aa sequences of P1, P2 (excluding 2A) and P3 (excluding 3A) of rosavirus B and C. The results suggested the presence of two novel picornavirus species, proposed to be named “Rosavirus B” and “Rosavirus C”. We have also detected other potentially novel picornaviruses from new rodent samples and will continue to characterize them in future studies. For objective 2, “Rosavirus B” was found to infect street rodent species, Norway rat (Rattus norvegicus), whereas “Rosavirus C” infects five different wild rodent species, suggesting interspecies transmission. No major distinct genome features were identified between strains from different rodent species or geographical locations, although geographically distinct strains tend to be genetically diverse. Two rosavirus C strains from mainland China possessed a total of 432 unique nucleotide substitutions over the entire genomes compared to eight rosavirus C strains from Hong Kong. The Ka/Ks ratios for most coding regions were low, supporting purifying selection. Further studies are required to better understand the mechanism of cross-species transmission. For objective 3, samples from >1000 rodents of different species were obtained. RT-PCR using specific primers targeting these potential novel picornaviruses was positive in 62 respiratory and 70 alimentary samples from 92 rodents. Viral sequences belonging to “Rosavirus B” were only detected from the street rodent species, Norway rat (Rattus norvegicus), whereas sequences belonging to “Rosavirus C” were detected from five different wild rodent species, greater bandicoot rat (Bandicota indica), chestnut spiny rat (Niviventer fulvescens), roof rat (Rattus rattus) and Indochinese forest rat (Rattus andamanensis) from Hong Kong, and Coxing’s white-bellied rat (Niviventer coxingi) from Hunan and Guangxi. Anti-rosavirus B antibodies were detected in two (3.3%) of 61 Norway rats from Hong Kong whereas anti-rosavirus C antibodies were detected in three (4.3%) of 70 Indochinese forest rats from Hong Kong and three (7.5%) of 40 Coxing's white-bellied rats from Hunan Province. No cross reactivities were observed between rosavirus B and C. Neutralization assays showed that five of the six rats with anti-rosavirus C antibodies by western blot analyses were positive for neutralizing antibodies against rosavirus C RASM14A with titer 1:10 to 1:40. For objective 4, we studied the pathogenicity in mice challenged with rosavirus C RASM14A isolated from infected 3T3 cells. Rosavirus C can cause multisystemic disease in infected mice, with histological pathologies in organs including lung and liver sections. Immunohistochemical staining with guinea pig anti-serum against rosavirus C VP1 protein antibody revealed viral antigen expression in bronchiolar and bronchial epithelial cells in lung sections, and hepatocytes in liver sections. These results have been published in PLoS Pathogens. All our objectives have been achieved.

17107415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17107415.value: In this project, we identified two novel picornaviruses, rosavirus B from the street rat, Norway rat, and rosavirus C from five different wild rat species (chestnut spiny rat, greater bandicoot rat, Indochinese forest rat, roof rat and Coxing's white-bellied rat) in China. Analysis of 13 complete genome sequences showed that “Rosavirus B” and “Rosavirus C” represent two potentially novel picornavirus species infecting different rodents. Though being most closely related to rosavirus A, rosavirus B and C possessed distinct protease cleavage sites and variations in Yn-Xm-AUG sequence in 5’UTR and myristylation site in VP4. Anti-rosavirus B VP1 antibodies were detected in Norway rats, whereas anti-rosavirus C VP1 and neutralizing antibodies were detected in Indochinese forest rats and Coxing's white-bellied rats. While the highest prevalence was observed in Coxing's white-bellied rats by RT-PCR, the detection of rosavirus C from different rat species suggests potential interspecies transmission. Rosavirus C isolated from 3T3 cells causes multisystemic diseases in a mouse model, with high viral loads and positive viral antigen expression in organs of infected mice after oral or intracerebral inoculation. Histological examination revealed alveolar fluid exudation, interstitial infiltration, alveolar fluid exudate and wall thickening in lungs, and hepatocyte degeneration and lymphocytic/monocytic inflammatory infiltrates with giant cell formation in liver sections of sacrificed mice. Our findings support the potential of rosaviruses for interspecies transmission, and extend our knowledge on the diversity and host range of picornaviruses in rodents. Since rosavirus A2 has been detected in fecal samples of children, further studies should elucidate the pathogenicity and emergence potential of different rosaviruses. Our works also establish a new platform and animal model for studying the pathogenicity of picornaviruses. The work has been published in PLoS Pathogens.

17107415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17107415.value: The ability of rosavirus C in causing multisystemic infection in mice with high viral loads in infected organs suggested that rosaviruses may cause severe infections in their host. Further experimental studies using other rosaviruses and rodent species may help better understand the pathogenicity of members of the genus Rosavirus in different rodents and human. Rodents are the largest order of mammals on earth, accounting for 43% of the approximately 4,800 living mammalian species. They are widely distributed, being found in all habitats except the oceans. Urban rodents may pose particular risk to human health, as in the case of Hantavirus and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus infections. Our findings also suggest that more epidemiological studies should be performed to explore the diversity of rodent picornaviruses and their potential risks to human.

17107415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17107415.value: We identified two novel picornaviruses, rosavirus B and C, infecting street and wild rats respectively in China. While rosavirus B was detected from Norway rats, rosavirus C was detected from five different wild rat species (chestnut spiny rat, greater bandicoot rat, Indochinese forest rat, roof rat and Coxing's white-bellied rat) by RT-PCR. Anti-rosavirus B antibodies were detected in Norway rats, whereas anti-rosavirus C antibodies were detected in Indochinese forest rats and Coxing's white-bellied rats, supporting potential interspecies transmission of rosavirus C. Genome analysis supported the classification of rosavirus B and C as two novel picornavirus species, with genome features distinct from rosavirus A. Rosavirus C isolated from 3T3 cells causes multisystemic diseases in a mouse model, with viruses and pathologies detected in various organs of infected mice after oral or intracerebral inoculation. Our results extend our knowledge on the host range and pathogenicity of rodent picornaviruses.

17107915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107915.value: Implantation and diapause are two important processes with opposite consequences in reproduction. Implantation is tightly regulated leading to attachment of the embryos onto the endometrium and subsequent growth of the fetuses. Diapause refers to a temporary and reversible arrest of embryonic development at the blastocyst stage before implantation. Diapause occurs in over 130 mammalian species. It allows the young to be born in a favorable environment. During diapause, the embryos become dormant but can implant and develop normally when activated. A recent study suggests that the potential for diapause may be present in all mammals. How diapause and subsequent implantation are regulated is not fully known. Mature microRNAs are small RNAs suppressing gene expression. In mice, the expression of a family of microRNAs, termed let-7, is high in blastocysts during diapause, but diminishes to low levels at implantation. Forced expression of let-7 in the mouse blastocysts induces diapause. Polyamines are small molecules essential in cell growth and development. Two sets of observations suggest that a high level of polyamines activates dormant blastocysts: (1) The synthesis of polyamine increases in the uterus of mink and mice upon activation from diapause; and (2) Polyamine deprivation suppresses activation of, while polyamine treatment activates dormant mink embryos, Evidence shows that uterine fluid contains polyamines and let-7-containing small vesicles. Their roles in implantation and diapause are mostly unknown. We hypothesize that the blastocysts implant when the polyamine concentration in the uterine fluid is high but become dormant when the let-7 concentration is high. The hypothesis will be tested in this project using mice as a study model. In addition, we will investigate the applicability of the hypothesis in a human implantation model, looking into the actions of polyamines and let-7 on attachment of clumps of human placental cells (embryo surrogates) onto human endometrial cells. Knowledge of implantation and diapause is not only of academic interest, it will open new ways of manipulating reproduction at the implantation level. Approximately 15% of couples at reproductive age suffer from infertility. Results of the project provide the scientific basis for studying endometrial polyamine insufficiency or microRNA dysregulation as causes of infertility. Trophectoderm biopsy is increasingly used in preimplantation genetic diagnosis, during which part of the trophectoderm of blastocysts is biopsied for genetic diagnosis followed by cryopreservation of the biopsied embryos waiting for the diagnostic result. In depth understanding of diapause could simplify the procedure by inducing diapause to replace cryopreservation.

17107915.label: Realisation of objectives
17107915.value: Implantation and diapause are two important processes with opposite consequences in reproduction. Implantation is tightly regulated leading to attachment of the embryos onto the endometrium and subsequent growth of the fetuses. Diapause refers to a temporary and reversible arrest of embryonic development at the blastocyst stage before implantation. Diapause occurs in over 130 mammalian species. It allows the young to be born in a favorable environment. During diapause, the embryos become dormant but can implant and develop normally when activated. A study suggests that the potential for diapause may be present in all mammals. How diapause and subsequent implantation are regulated is not fully known. Mature microRNAs are small non-coding RNAs suppressing gene expression. In mice, the expression of a family of microRNAs, termed let-7, is high in blastocysts during diapause, but diminishes to low levels at implantation. Forced expression of let-7 in the mouse blastocysts induces diapause. Polyamines are small molecules essential in cell growth and development. Two sets of observations suggest that a high level of polyamines activates dormant blastocysts: (1) The synthesis of polyamine increases in the uterus of mink and mice upon activation from diapause; and (2) Polyamine deprivation suppresses activation of, while polyamine treatment activates dormant mink embryos. The hypothesis of the project is that the occurrence of endometrial polyamines and microRNA let-7 determines whether the blastocysts should implant or become dormant. Specifically, the blastocysts implant when the uterine content of polyamines is high but become dormant when that of let-7 is high. To test the hypothesis, the project studied the actions of polyamines/let-7 signaling in embryo implantation and diapause. We had fully addressed and achieved all the objectives as stated in the proposal. Objective 1: To study the action of polyamines on implantation/diapause. The expression of polyamine biosynthesis enzymes including ornithine decarboxylase (ODC1) in Day 4 (D4), dormant and estradiol (E2)-activated mouse embryos was compared by western blot, immunostaining. The actions of polyamines and ODC1 inhibitor (DMFO) on D4 blastocysts in terms of attachment and spreading on culture dishes, and EGF-binding (a blastocyst activation marker) were determined. The roles of polyamines in activation of dormant embryos was studied by treating dormant blastocysts with DFMO in vitro, transfer the treated embryos into delayed implanting mice followed by E2 induced activation. The EGF-binding and implantation potential of the polyamine treated dormant blastocysts in 2-fluoroestradial-17β (2-Fl-E2)-treated mice was determined. 2-Fl-E2 treatment induces a receptive endometrium but does not the dormant blastocysts. The relationship between polyamine and let-7 in mouse blastocysts was studied by determining the (1) expression of c-myc, lin28, eIF5, ODC in D4 blastocysts  forced expression of let-7a; (2) in vitro survival of let-7 forced expressed dormant blastocysts in the presence of polyamines or DFMO; and (3) expression of let-7 in polyamine-treated blastocysts  knockdown of eIF5 or lin28. Objective 2: To determine the roles of steroids in the production of polyamines and let-7/let-7 containing exosomes in mouse endometrial cells. Polyamines production in uterine fluid of non-pregnant, pregnant and pseudopregnant mice, E2, progesterone (P4) and combined treated ovariectomy mice, delayed implanting and E2-activated mice was determined. The contents of let-7 in exosomes isolated from the spent media after culture of primary epithelial and stromal cells from uteri of D4 pregnant or D7 delayed implanting mice in the presence of polyamine or DFMO were compared. The exosomal let-7 levels in uterine fluid of D3 and D4 pregnant mice injected with DFMO were determined. The actions of E2 and P4 and combined on production of let-7, let-7-containing exosomes, ODC1 and LIN28 in primary mouse endometrial epithelial cells and stromal cells from different stages of the estrus cycle and pregnancy were studied. In addition, the experiments were repeated in the presence of DMFO or after knockdown of lin28 and eIF5. Objective 3: To study the roles of uterine polyamines and let-7 in implantation/diapause in vivo. The roles of polyamines and let-7 in implantation/diapause in vivo was studied by determining the levels of let-7 in endometrial cells and their exosomes from LIN28 transgenic mice. This objective aimed to generate a uterus-specific Odc1 knockout (KO) mouse model but encountered difficulty. We obtained heterozygous Odc1tm1a/+ mice from the European Conditional Mouse Mutagenesis Program (KOMP). The mice carry a LacZ and neo cassette with FRT and LoxP sites as KO genotype. Crossing of Odc1tm1a/+with Cre-expressing mice was expected to generate Odc1tm1b/+ KO mice with LacZ expression. However, homozygous Odc1tm1b/tm1b KO mice were not viable, and no pup was produced. An alternative approach was used by first crossing the Odc1tm1a/+ with Flipper mice obtained from HKU to generate the Odc1tm1c/+ mice carrying the floxed Odc1 allele. Intercrossing of Odc1tm1c/+ generated Odc1tm1c/tm1c homozygous floxed mice, which were then crossed with the PR-Cre mice from Jackson Lab (USA) carrying Odc1tm1b/+ to obtain Odc1tm1b/tm1c (carrying one knockout and one floxed Odc1 allele) with tissue-specific Cre-recombinase. Finally, a number of Odc1tm1b/tm1c:PR-Cre female mice were obtained, and mating experiments were setup to study the fecundity of the females with normal males. The endometrial receptivity, expression of ODC1, polyamine and let-7 in these mice were determined. The attachment rates of their blastocysts was determined in the presence of polyamines. Objective 4: To study the roles of hCG on polyamines and let-7 expression and function in human endometrial cells in vitro Let-7 expression and production of Let-7 containing exosomes of human endometrial cells with or without prior E2 and P4 treatment were determined. The expression of polyamine biosynthesis enzymes, eIF5 and LIN28 in the endometrial cells and trophoblast spheroids were also studied. The attachment of Jeg-3 trophoblast spheroids with or without DFMO treatment onto endometrial cells in the presence or absence of hCG were compared.

17107915.value: a. Endometrial-derived polyamines and miRNAs affect implantation. Further research should be on (1) if dysregulation of miRNAs and/or polyamines is a cause of infertility in humans; and (2) if supplementation of polyamines to embryo culture medium could improve the implantation rate of embryos in clinical assisted reproduction. b. Exosomal let-7 induce diapause. Further research should be on (1) roles of other exosomal miRNAs on diapause and implantation; and (2) mechanism by which exosomes induce diapause of the inner cell mass. The endometrial-derived exosomes act on the trophectoderm. Uncovering the mechanism will enable us to understand intra-embryonic communication between the trophectoderm and the inner cell mass. c. Exosomes can efficiently transfer miRNAs into embryos. The method is the gentlest way of manipulating gene expression in preimplantation embryos. Further development of the method may allow us to rescue poor quality embryos in assisted reproduction. d. Inhibition of polyamines biosynthesis suppresses decidualization. Defective decidualization causes pregnancy complications. 17107915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17107915.value: Endometrial factor is a cause of infertility. Implantation and diapause have opposite consequences in mammalian reproduction. Implantation leads to development of fetuses in the uterus. In diapause, the embryos cease to develop in the uterus, but can be activated to resume development upon receiving appropriate stimulation. Diapause is a strategy commonly used in wildlife to avoid birth of the young in an unfavorable environment. Results of this project show that the mouse endometrium secretes polyamines and a microRNA known as let-7. The balance of polyamines and let-7 in the uterus determines whether the embryos should implant or undergo diapause. Specifically, the embryos implant when the uterine content of polyamines is high but become dormant when that of let-7 is high. Sex steroids controlled the balance; progesterone required for maintenance of diapause increases the production of let-7, while estrogen required for activation of dormant embryos increases production of polyamines and decreases that of let-7 in endometrium with prior exposure to progesterone. Similar actions of polyamines and let-7 were found in a human implantation model. The knowledge gained in the project prompts to identification of endometrial polyamines insufficiency or microRNA dysregulation as causes of endometrial infertility.

17108315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108315.value: 現今，人類平均壽命的增長對於人口結構產生了重大的影響。許多城市正面臨著人口的老齡化。在香港，預計年齡在65歲以上的人口比例將從2011年的13%增長到2040年的30%。統計研究發現有6%的70歲以上老年人患有癡呆症，65%的則患有阿爾茨海默病(AD)，因此探索人類老化的神經生理學機制就顯得尤為重要，該機制能為與衰老相關的神經退化性疾病的提早診斷提供線索。 有研究發現通過功能性核磁共振成像(fMRI)，在認知任務中健康老年人的雙邊前額葉皮層的啟動程度要高於健康成人組。一些研究者推斷這種大腦活動的增強可能是對衰老導致的神經缺失的反應，並稱之為“補償假說”。這種現象已經在基因有患AD風險的受試者身上觀察到，但是產生這種變化的生物化學基礎並不能僅僅通過fMRI來闡明。 磁共振質子波譜成像技術（1H-MRS）是一項非常有前景的技術，該技術的能夠通過測量活體腦內代謝物濃度的優點可以彌補上述的不足。它已經被廣泛應用於研究老化以及多種神經退行性疾病。該技術得到的主要代謝產物如谷氨酸鹽(Glu)和N-乙醯天冬氨酸(NAA)能夠反映能量代謝、神經元的功能與結構的完整性，可以充當神經過程的生化標記物。我們最近發表的一項研究發現在前扣帶回(ACC)，後扣帶回(PCC)和左海馬的NAA濃度會隨著年齡的增長而升高，此外，我們未發表的實驗資料也揭示了相似的與年齡成正比的ACC和PCC區域的Glu絕對濃度的提升。因為Glu被認為是神經血管耦合的主要介質，Glu濃度的增加可能可以等價為fMRI中的大腦啟動程度的增強。fMRI的信號絕大部分取決於血氧水準的改變，所以fMRI作為一種間接的測量大腦活動的方法與神經活動耦合相關。鑒於這種耦合作用，Glu濃度的變化可能最終影響fMRI的啟動程度。 我們後續的研究將通過在認知任務中ACC和海馬區的MRS代謝物濃度變化與fMRI信號的關聯，進一步探索在正常衰老過程中一些代謝物濃度變化的功能意義。本研究的中心假說：通過結合施加任務的fMRI和1H-MRS這兩種方法，來闡明認知過程和相關的生物化學變化之間的複雜關聯。 該研究的順利完成能夠幫助我們增強對與年齡相關腦活動變化的神經化學基礎的理解。

17109215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109215.value: 髓母細胞瘤（MB）是最常見的兒童惡性腦腫瘤， 發病率和死亡率是兒科癌症中最高。嬰兒和成人的MB大部分是由於刺猬（SHH）信令異常，並歸類為 SHH-MB。嬰兒SHH MB同時帶有SUFU突變是最難根治，因為需要針對Smo的下游，不能使用Smo拮抗劑治療法。因此，需要究發出新藥物，從而針對在Hh通路中Smo下游的信號。同時，SUFU對MB的影嚮也需進一步研究。 要為最難根治的惡性嬰兒SHH MB建立研究模型，我們把小鼠神經幹細胞（NSC）或小腦顆粒神經元前體（GNP）的Sufu 敲除（SufuKO）。引人注目的是，我們的初步數據表明，Sufu的缺失不能引發MB。此外，我們發現SufuKO小鼠沒有激活Hh 信號。 同時如我們把Sufu 從PtcKO小鼠中敲除，也能減慢MB的形成。另一方面，當SufuKO小鼠的SPOP E3泛素減少，Gli活性就能恢復，小鼠很早就長出類似人類的高侵略性嬰兒SHH MB 。這些結果表明，MB的形成是需要同時失去Sufu及穩定Gli蛋白 。與此相符，在MB 病人一並失去SUFU基因及雜合性丟失（LOH）BTRC基因 也是非常常見。其中BTRCβ編碼TrCP，是一種F-box蛋白，負責Gli蛋白的SCF介導的泛素化。這些數據引申出一個有趣的可能性，有賴於GLI蛋白的泛素化, SUFU可作為抗癌或致癌基因。我們推測，高GLI活動能加速SHH MB腫瘤發生； 而失去SUFU能導致GLI蛋白不穩定，減弱小腦腫瘤形成。而失去SUFU及減少GLI泛素化就能引發MB。因此，我們建議1) 使用條件SufuKO; PtcKO小鼠去了解失去SUFU是如何抑制SHH-MB腫瘤發生; 2）劃定SUFU引致MB的分子機制，以挑選出新治療靶點;和3）了解BTRC和SUFU基因缺失而引致MB的主因，以建立最佳的模型，用於將來研發治療嬰兒MB之用。總括而言，這項研究將有助理解人類生物學，及病理學，並以開發治療SHH MB新標靶藥物為長期目標。

17109215.label: Realisation of objectives
17109215.value: Objective 1: To decipher how loss of Sufu suppresses SHH-MB tumorigenesis using conditional Sufu;PtcKO mice Using various mouse mutant lines, we have demonstrated that (1) elevated Gli2 activity causes disorganized cerebella in Sufu KO mice but is insufficient to induce MB formation; (2) gene dosages of Spop and Gli2 are critical for MB formation in Sufu KO background; (3) Sufu is required for maintaining robust Gli activity in SHH MB with Smo activation. Objective 2: To delineate the molecular mechanism underlying the oncogenic functions of Sufu in MB tumorigenesis to identify potential new therapeutic targets To further delineate the underlying mechanism, we analysed the transcriptomes and epigomes of Sufu;Spop DKO MB to identify the key Gli2 targets in MB tumorigenesis (e.g., GLI1, PTCH1, HHIP, and CCND1). Among the 116 GLI2 targets identified in MB, we revealed that 95 of them have previously been implicated in cancer (36 in MB tumorigenesis), and 22 being transcription factors. Gene ontology analysis revealed enrichment in terms such as Smo signaling, neurogenesis, extracellular matrix (ECM) organization, angiogenesis, DNA replication, etc., suggesting a central role of Gli2 in these processes. To characterize the mechanisms underlying the transcriptional regulation of Gli2 target genes, we performed motif analysis of Gli2 peak regions and found that bHLH and NFI transcription factor (TF) motifs are significantly enriched in Gli2 peak regions compared with background sequences. RNA-seq data revealed that, among the neural bHLH TFs, only Atoh1 was uniquely upregulated in MBs. To determine whether Atoh1 can directly activate transcription of Gli2 target regions, we performed a luciferase reporter assay using Gli2/Atoh1-bound regions from two candidate genes: intron 2 of Ptch1 and an element 26 kb downstream of Cxcr4. Our data showed that Atoh1 activates these two Gli2 target genes via the Gli2/Atoh1 binding element. Importantly, co-expression of Atoh1 and Gli2 resulted in a drastic upregulation of the two reporters in a synergistic manner, suggesting these two factors act synergistically to activate Gli2 target genes to promote MB tumorigenesis. Objective 3: To determine whether loss of both Btrc and Sufu alleles induces MB in order to establish a model of the most aggressive infant MB for future therapeutic interventions With the support from the co-I, Prof. C.C. Hui, the above two objectives have been finished and the work has been published in Developmental Cell. The remaining resources were used to address the objective 3 in the original proposal. BTRC LOH is frequently found in SHH MB patients carrying SUFU mutation and that βTrCP encoded by BTRC mediates GliA degradation. We found that Btrc null mice do not show any sign of tumor, so it is unlikely that loss of Btrc alone leads to MB tumorigenesis in vivo. Thus, we generated Sufu;Btrc double knock-out mice to examine whether Btrc would favour the formation of MB in Sufu KO. Again, we found that loss of both Sufu and Btrc alleles is still insufficient to induce MB in mice and only hyperplasia was observed. In summary, our work establishes the dual role of SUFU in SHH MB and provides mechanistic insights into transcriptional regulation underlying Gli2-mediated SHH MB tumorigenesis.

17109215.label: Major findings and research outcome
17109215.value: SUFU alterations are common in human Sonic Hedgehog (SHH) subgroup medulloblastoma (MB). However, its tumorigenic mechanisms have remained elusive. Here, we report that loss of Sufu alone is unable to induce MB formation in mice, due to insufficient Gli2 activation. Simultaneous loss of Spop, an E3 ubiquitin ligase targeting Gli2, restores robust Gli2 activation and induces rapid MB formation in Sufu knockout background. We also demonstrated a tumor-promoting role of Sufu in Smo-activated MB (~60% of human SHH MB) by maintaining robust Gli activity. Having established Gli2 activation as a key driver of SHH MB, we report a comprehensive analysis of its targetome. Furthermore, we identified Atoh1 as a target and molecular accomplice of Gli2 that activates core SHH MB signature genes in a synergistic manner. Overall, our work establishes the dual role of SUFU in SHH MB and provides mechanistic insights into transcriptional regulation underlying Gli2-mediated SHH MB tumorigenesis. The major findings were published in Developmental Cell 48, 167–183, January 28, 2019.

17109515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109515.value: TP53是在人類癌症中最常見的突變基因之一，該基因所編碼的關鍵抑癌蛋白質p53有調節DNA修復、細胞週期進程、和細胞凋亡等功能。P53在腫瘤發病中起著重要的核心作用。食道鱗狀細胞癌（以下稱食道癌）有著極高的p53突變率，約60%至90%的患者擁有p53突變。喪失野生型抑癌功能的p53功能失去性突變已得到充分研究。然而，不依賴於其野生型功能的致癌性p53功能獲得性突變存在的證據正不斷湧現。P53功能獲得性突變被認為是腫瘤發病的重要驅動力。P53功能獲得性突變與早發疾病、增強的細胞侵襲與轉移、和異常的組織特異性細胞信號傳導相關聯。此種突變可能為具有特別侵襲性的腫瘤細胞亞群體提供選擇性生長優勢。這些腫瘤細胞也可能表現出較強的化療抗性。 我們對癌症中p53突變有著長期的興趣。於早期食道癌研究中，我們利用聚合酶鏈式反應-單鏈構象多態性分析技術與直接測序技術在42%的來自中國大陸和香港的樣本中發現p53突變。然而，免疫組織化學染色技術顯示出更高的p53突變率為78%。隨著新一代測序方法的進步與可實用性的發展，在最近我們對香港食道癌樣本所進行的前期研究中，超過90%的樣本檢測到了遺傳變異。其中約36%為於別種癌症中確認的有作用的功能獲得性突變。P53的功能獲得性突變之前並沒有在食道癌中研究過。由於p53功能獲得性突變其作用所具有的組織特異性特性，確定其於食道癌這種有著所有癌症中最高之一的p53突變率的癌症當中所起的致癌性作用，將對瞭解該種致命癌症的遺傳基礎與潛在的治療應用提供新穎的寶貴資料。 我們推測p53功能獲得性突變與臨床結果相關聯，這將有助於香港食道癌患者的預後判斷。我們的目標是確定直接於食道癌腫瘤中所觀察到的幾個潛在復發性的p53功能獲得性突變的功能性作用、進行機理研究、確定其於臨床標本發生的頻率，並確定其於預後及治療策略選擇中的功用。抑制其致癌性作用及（或）恢復其野生型的腫瘤抑制作用等治療策略預計將發揮臨床效益。本研究計畫預計將闡明p53功能獲得性突變在細胞信號傳導、癌症發展、及癌症轉移中的關鍵作用；並確定此些作用是否可作為有效的預後指標；並研究在食道癌中p53靶向抗癌劑功效的有效性。這些研究將有助於我們增進對該種致命癌症的瞭解以及其臨床管理。

17109515.label: Realisation of objectives
17109515.value: AIM1. Elucidate the function of key ESCC gain-of-function p53 mutants To elucidate the function of key ESCC gain-of-function (GoF) p53 mutants, we first sequenced the TP53 coding sequences in a panel of eight ESCC cell lines and examined the corresponding p53 protein expression. By applying various biochemical assays, we concluded that the differences on PAGE gel migration rates between different mutants are due to the intrinsic biochemical properties of the mutant proteins. We examined the phosphorylation patterns of the endogenous p53 mutant proteins and also exogenously-expressed p53 mutant constructs in various of ESCC cell lines and other cell lines including HeLa and HEK293T. We consistently observed a specific phosphorylation pattern for potential GoF mutants including R248Q and several hotspot mutants (R248S and R273C), as compared to other p53 mutants. Ser9 and Ser46 of potential GoF mutants are always strongly hyperphosphorylated. By subcellular fractionation we showed that R248Q p53 mutant resides more frequently in the endomembranous structures compared to other p53 mutants. We then utilized clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-mediated functional knockout (fKO) to deplete endogenous p53 protein in four ESCC cell lines, followed by nude mouse subcutaneous xenograft tumorigenicity assays to examine in vivo the functional consequences of depleting p53 mutant protein expression. Multiple CRISPR guide RNA oligos were designed to target p53 tested in various ESCC cell lines. Three oligos that greatly eliminate p53 protein expression in all cell lines tested were chosen for further study, together with control oligos that target non-coding regions of the p53 locus. We found that only depletion of the endogenous R248Q p53 mutant in KYSE150 cell lines resulted in suppressed tumor growth, but not depletion of p53 mutants in KYSE180, KYSE450, and SLMT cell lines. Therefore, we functionally validated the GoF of R248Q mutant. The other three p53 mutants including I195T, H179R and R273L do not show GoF oncogenic properties. We also concluded that there is no correlation between endogenous p53 protein expression and GoF properties. We also utilized the experimental metastasis model by tail-vein injection to examine the effect of R248Q depletion on lung metastasis formation. However, we did not observe metastasis suppression by R248Q depletion. We evaluated various in vitro functional assays including 2D and 3D cell culturing techniques and analyzed the functional consequences of depletion of GoF mutants. We specifically constructed a bioluminescence-based quantitative 3D Matrigel embedded culture model. We found that only the 3D Matrigel-embedded culture model shows growth-suppression of R248Q depletion in KYSE150 cells, mimicking the tumor suppression seen in vivo. Results of 3D colony growth of depletion of other endogenous mutant were also consistent with the in vivo data. AIM 2. Perform mechanistic and signaling studies of gain-of-function p53 mutants in ESCC To analyze the GoF mechanism of p53 mutants in ESCC, we performed signaling analysis. Since the 3D Matrigel embedded culture model elicits functional consequences of R248Q depletion, we continued to perform mechanistic and signaling studies of GoF p53 using this culture model. We did not see growth/proliferation suppression by R248Q depletion in 2D culture or in 3D culture without extracellular matrix (ECM). Therefore, we focused on signaling pathways that mediate communication with the ECM compartments/substrates. We found that the focal adhesion kinase (FAK) is hypophosphorylated in R248Q-fKO KYSE150 cells, along with hypophosphorylation and reduced activities of its downstream targets SRC/ERK, suggesting that GoF p53 R248Q mutant regulates ECM/integrin/FAK signaling. We showed that expression of a constitutively active MEK, the kinase and activator of ERK, rescues proliferation and colony growth of R248Q-fKO KYSE150 cells. These data suggest that ERK acts as the effector downstream of FAK in R248Q-fKO induced cancer cell growth suppression. We found that the RHOA/ROCK pathway regulates FAK activation in ESCC cells under 3D Matrigel culturing conditions by performing a ROCK inhibitor (ROCKi) assay. We further demonstrated that ROCKi diminishes the suppression of FAK phosphorylation by R248Q-fKO in KYSE150 cells, suggesting that R248Q regulates FAK activation through the RHOA/ROCK pathway.

17109515.label: Major findings and research outcome
17109515.value: The current study verified the oncogenic role of the p53 R248Q mutant in ESCC using both well-controlled in vivo and in vitro functional and molecular assays. Only depletion of the endogenous R248Q mutant, but not the other mutants (including I195T, H179R, R273L), was able to suppress tumor growth and induce anti-cancer effects. In an in vitro 3D Matrigel embedded culture model, R248Q depletion leads to reduced colony formation. The molecular mechanism of tumor suppression associated with R248Q depletion was also analyzed. R248Q depletion leads to suppressed FAK/SRC/ERK signaling; expression of a constitutively active MEK mutant construct rescues the reduced colony formation in 3D Matrigel culture. RHOA/ROCK inhibition diminished the suppression of FAK/SRC/ERK signaling by R248Q depletion. R248Q re-expression in cell lines depleted of endogenous p53 mutants enhances 3D colony formation. Expression of p53R248Q in an ESCC patient-derived organoid culture depleted of endogenous p53 expression also enhances in vitro organoid colony formation. We found that the WNT1-inducible-signaling pathway protein 2 (WISP2) is down-regulated by R248Q expression. We found that the R248Q mutant exhibits distinct molecular properties including hyperphosphorylation on ser9/ser46 and endomembranous-localized protein expression. A manuscript based on this research project is under preparation for submission soon and aims for a high impact journal. The results of this project have been presented in the form of poster presentation in a renowned international cancer research conference, the American Association for Cancer Research Annual Meeting 2018, held in the United States

17109515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17109515.value: The current results suggest a critical oncogenic gain-of-function role of a certain p53 mutant in ESCC development. Mutations of p53 are the most frequent events in cancer biology. Identification of p53 mutants possessing gain-of-function may provide significant therapeutic advances. We showed that the ROCK/FAK/ERK signaling pathway plays a critical role in R248Q-mediated GoF properties. Targeting this pathway may offer therapeutic benefit in certain ESCC patients harboring the R248Q p53 mutant. Whether other p53 mutants possess similar GoF properties prompts more detailed analysis of a collection of ESCC patient-derived mutations in a well-controlled cell line and patient-derived tissue culture model. Detailed mechanistic analysis in a preclinical drug testing platform and large-scale ESCC patient tissue sample analyses using methods such as immunohistochemical staining are needed to further verify this possible utility of the findings from this project.

17109515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17109515.value: We studied the tumor promoting effect of specific mutants of the gene TP53 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, a deadly form of esophageal cancer highly prevalent in the Chinese population. TP53 is a master tumor suppressor; it is the most frequently mutated gene in cancer. We found that one specific mutant of the gene, R248Q mutant, possesses pro-cancer function, independent of any wild-type function of TP53. We performed various assays to analyze how this TP53 mutant promotes tumor development. We found that the R248Q mutant regulates the activities of critical cell growth-promoting molecular players that are involved in communication with extracellular components. These findings enhance our understanding of esophageal cancer progression and assist future development of biomarker and therapeutic applications to ultimately improve clinical outcomes.
