17110315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110315.value: 摘要 與EB病毒（EBV）相關的鼻咽癌是一種在中國南方地區（包括香港）高發的頭頸部癌症，具有極高的轉移性。基於臨床上可在癌前病變的鼻咽上皮組織中檢測到克隆EBV感染的研究結果，EBV感染被視作鼻咽癌發病過程中的先決條件。據推測，EBV感染的鼻咽細胞和炎症基質之間的持續相互作用與鼻咽癌的發生發展密切相關，特別是腫瘤相關巨噬細胞（TAM）對於炎症相關癌症的發病與轉移有重要的促進作用。但是，TAM對EBV感染的鼻咽細胞的轉移活性有何調節作用尚未明確。 我們的前期實驗結果表明，腫瘤生長因子（TGF）-β1作為一種TAM分泌最多的細胞因子，可上調鼻咽細胞中JAG-1（Notch配體）的表達。更為有趣的是，與非EBV感染的鼻咽細胞相比，EBV感染的鼻咽細胞中Notch3信號在與TAM相互作用之後進一步激活增強。並且，與非EBV感染的鼻咽細胞相比，TGF-β1介導的腫瘤細胞轉移在EBV感染的鼻咽細胞中更為明顯， EBV感染的鼻咽細胞在經過TGF-β1處理後，可更有效地在三維膠原蛋白基質中形成侵襲性偽足和變形浸潤。 TGF-β1也可以上調LMP1的表達，以進一步提高JAG-1的轉錄水平。 我們建議研究TAM對EBV感染的鼻咽上皮細胞的影響，主要關注TGF-β1在介導JAG-1/Notch3信號軸的激活以及提高EBV感染的鼻咽細胞的侵襲能力方面的功能。我們將使用多光子活體成像進一步驗證TAM和EBV感染的鼻咽細胞的相互作用，及其在體內促進鼻咽細胞侵襲能力的機理。本課題結合體外與體內實驗研究方法，可更好的闡明炎症基質在與EBV相關的鼻咽癌侵襲過程中的作用。

17110315.label: Realisation of objectives
17110315.value: Aim 1: To elucidate the roles of TAM-induced TGF-beta1/JAG-1/Notch3 signaling in governing the invasiveness of EBV-associated NPC in vitro. Increased macrophage density in the stroma of carcinomas, including nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), has been correlated with poor patient survival. Tumor associated macrophages (TAMs) can produce large quantity of TGF-beta1 which is known as potent inducer for invasion and metastatic spread. In particular, macrophages appear to be critical for tumorigenesis and invasiveness in several types of inflammation-induced cancer. Undifferentiated NPC is almost 100% associated with EBV infection and highly metastatic in nature. We showed that treatment of TGF-beta1 or co-culturing with TAMs (constrained within 4 µm pore-sized chamber) could activate the JAG-1/Notch3 signaling in our premalignant NP cells and is a critical oncogenic event in NPC tumorigenesis. Interestingly, the coculturing of TAMs induced the expression of an EBV-encoded gene, latent membrane protein 1 (LMP1). Overexpression of LMP1 could also enhance the expression level of JAG-1. TGF-beta1 was also found to induce cell scattering in 2-D culture and amoeboid invasion to the 3-D matrix. Moreover, it enhanced the formation of invadopodia, which are matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-secretory microdomains that can focally interact with and digest the extracellular matrix (ECM). We have further investigated the TGF-beta1-induced invadopodia formation on 3D bioplatforms. We studied the topographic guidance of invadopodia formation in invasive nasopharyngeal cells under the stimulation of TGF-beta1, using engineered gratings with different width and depth. We reported that TGF-beta1 could act as an external signal to upregulate the formation of invadopodia with a random distribution on a plane 2D surface. However, when the cells were seeded on parallel 3D gratings of 0.1 to 1 μm depth, invadopodia aligned to the edges of the gratings, indicating a topographic cue to the control of invadopodia localization. This suggests that nasopharyngeal cells, when invading in tissues, can sense the topology of individual ECM ﬁbers or bundles, which vary in size between 30 and 300 nm, and concentrate invadopodia at hotspots of high curvature of the plasma membrane. All our findings demonstrated that TGF-beta1-mediated properties may contribute to the intravasation of NPC cells through an invadopodia-dependent process. Aim2: To investigate the dependency of EBV infection in potentiating the cancer cells’ invasiveness induced by TAMs. In the pathogenesis or development of NPC, continuous interaction between the EBV-infected premalignant/malignant NP cells and TAMs may contribute to the gain of invasiveness, possibly through the release of different cytokines (e.g. TGF-beta1, TNF-alpha and others) from the TAMs. In this part of the study, we confirmed that the supernatant of the M2-like macrophages could upregulate the expression of LMP1, and LMP1 could induce invadopodia to facilitate NPC invasion. Knockdown of LMP1 in the EBV-infected NPC cells partially suppressed the formation of M2-induced invadopodia, suggesting the involvement of this viral protein to the activation of invadopodia generation in NPC cells. Through transient transfection and stable expression of LMP1 in NPC cells, the LMP1 was shown to promote formation of invadopodia. The LMP1 was found to induce invadopodia formation through the Cdc42/N-WASP signaling axis. By using the wildtype and truncated mutants of LMP1 with deletion of different domains, the C-terminal of LMP1 was shown to be responsible for the activation of Cdc42/N-WASP signaling axis. To further confirm the involvement of LMP1 in invadopodia formation in nasopharyngeal cells, the expression of LMP1 in transfected cells was visually observed using LMP1 conjugated with a fluorescent tag (EBFP). Activation of invadopodia formation was observed in cells expressing LMP1 as indicated by the expression of EBFP. All these results support the ability of LMP1 to induce invadopodia formation and degrade gelatin in nasopharyngeal epithelial cells. Surprisingly, the LMP1-expressing cells were more responsive to TNF-alpha treatment and generated more invadopodia than the control cells transfected with empty vector. TNF-alpha is one of the cytokines highly released by macrophages in tumors. The synergistic effect of LMP1 and TNFα to induce invadopodia formation in NPC cells suggests the interplay of EBV-infected cancer cells with the inflammatory tumor microenvironment in enforcing the invasiveness of NPC cells and their ability to degrade extra-cellular matrix. Aim 3: To examine the in vivo cellular motility of EBV-infected and non-infected NP cells under the interaction with TAMs using multi-photon intravital imaging TAMs may affect the invasive movement and invadopodia-dependent extravasation of NPC cells, possibly through the release of TGF-beta1 and TNF-alpha. Our discovery that 3D topography could affect the localization of invadopodia also suggests that invadopodia is required in invasive cells for intravasation into blood vessel. In this project, we have developed intravital 2-photon microscopy to understand the invasive cellular movement of EBV-infected and non-infected NP cells with the interaction of TAMs in vivo. We have implanted window chambers on the dorsal skinfold of anesthetized mice. To visualize the NPC cells, we have transduced them by retro-virus for stable expression of GFP. The tumor was allowed to grow and reach 2 – 3 mm diameter and was observed under the window chamber. Collagen was visualized through second harmonic generation. To visualize the vasculature and the perivascular macrophages, Texas-red labelled dextran was tail vein injected to the mice 3 hrs before the microscopic imaging. We adopted the use of lower-molecular-weight dextrans (~70 kDa range) which allows for escape of some of the dye from the blood stream and then being picked up by perivascular macrophages. Intravital imaging was taken by LSM 710 (quipped with tunable 2-photon 690 – 1040 nm, Carl Zeiss). The Spectra Physics MaiTai HP laser was tuned to 800 for exciting GFP and second harmonic generation; and tuned to 900 for exciting Texas-red. The emission filters are 385 – 425 nm, 500-550 nm and 604 – 644 nm for second harmonic generation, GFP and Texas Red respectively. A heating mat was placed under the sedated mice to maintain physiological temperature of the animal during all experimental procedures. Typically, in each tumor, four different areas with blood vessel supply were imaged 10 µm steps for 500 µm Z-stack was taken. We observed that some tumor cells could detached form the tumor mass and migrate to the matrix areas with the presence of macrophages.

17110315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17110315.value: In this study, we aimed to gain a more comprehensive understanding of cell invasion and formation of invadopodia of nasopharyngeal cells under biomimetic in vivo environments. We have demonstrated the TAMs could secret cytokines including TGF-beta1 and TNF-alpha to simulate the NPC cells to be much more invasive. Moreover, it is interesting to note that cells are sensitive to topographical pattern accompanied with spatial re-organization of invadopodia. The integration of biological and geometric signals for initiating the formation of invadopodia and their spatial regulation in invasive nasopharyngeal cells was reported in Research Output 1 (Tsang CM et al, Acta Biomaterialia, 2019.) This is also the first study showing that macrophages stimulated invadopodia formation in NPC through secretion of TNFα and induction of expression of LMP1 in EBV-infected NPC cells. In Research Output 2 (Zhang J et al, Oncogene, 2019), we have demonstrated a pathological role of EBV and its encoded LMP1, in driving cell motility through metabolic reprogramming. The detail signaling pathways of LMP1 and TNFα had also been further defined with some of the essential molecules involved in invadopodia were examined. The phosphorylation of the signaling proteins including EGFR, Src, ERK, Cdc42, N-WASP and cortactin were examined in LMP1 and TNFα mediated invadopodia formation. In Research Output 3 (Tang WC et al, manuscript prepared), it will report the secretion of cytokines such as TNFα from infiltrating macrophages and EBV infection could act synergistically in invadopodia formation to facilitate invasion and metastasis in NPC. These studies give insights of the roles of EBV in the development of NPC and provide translational opportunities to treat NPC (Research Output 4: Tsang CM et al, Semin Cancer Biol. 2019. Research Output 5: Lin W et al, Nat Commun. 2018.). Heavy inﬁltration of macrophages is a common characteristic of EBV-associated NPC. Together with the other stromal cells, they form a unique tumor microenvironment which has been postulated to play an important role to support growth and progression of NPC cells in patients. The interplay of EBV-infected cells with the tumor microenvironment in the pathogenesis of NPC has been reviewed and published in Research Output 5 (Huang SCM et al, Cancers, 2018), Output 6 (Zhang J et al, Adv Exp Med Biol. 20170 and Output 7 (Tsao et al, Philos Trans R Soc Lond B Biol Sci. 2017).

17110315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17110315.value: The microenvironment has strong influence on the behavior of premalignant and tumor cells and plays crucial role in driving the tumor development and progression. Elucidating the complex interplay of TAMs and EBV-infected premalignant/tumor cells is critical for understanding the pathogenesis and invasiveness of NPC. The delineation of signaling pathways and mechanisms involved in the invasion of EBV-associated NPC cells will open new avenues for effective treatment therapies to prevent spread of NPC cells in patients. Our study indicates a dual inactivation of both the tumor and TAMs is necessary to potently inhibit the migratory or invasive properties of NPC cells. Furthermore, our study also hints the important roles of several signaling pathways in promoting the invadopodia formation in NPC cells. Preclinical assessment of inhibitors which can target these pathways will provide important information for enhancing the efficacy of current chemotherapy in controlling the metastasis of NPC patients. Our findings also indicate a synergistic upregulation of invasiveness of NPC cells through the paracrine induction of EBV gene by the neighboring macrophages. It again suggests any approach that can eliminate the EBV in the NPC cells may be a promising therapeutic intervention for NPC.

17110315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17110315.value: Metastasis is common in NPC and is the major cause of treatment failure in patients. Association with EBV infection and inﬁltration of macrophages are commonly observed in NPC. It has long been suggested that substantial and interactive impacts between cancer and stromal cells create a tumor microenvironment to promote tumorigenesis and progression. This study has delineated some of the essential events involved in governing the invasiveness of NPC cells which provide research background for future investigations aiming to target the pathogenic actions of NPC, particularly in invasion and metastasis. Careful molecular and mechanistic studies of biological and physical stimulations encountered by invasive cells give insights on disrupting the functions of invadopodia for controlling the metastatic spread of cancer cells. The synergistic integration of paracrine signals from macrophages (e.g. TGF-beta1 and TNF-alpha) and viral oncogenes (e.g. LMP1) to activate invadopodia formation is clinically relevant to the invasive behaviors of NPC cells in patients as these cytokines are common in human tumor microenvironment. Effective and deliverable vehicles or drugs which can abrogate the interaction of EBV-infected cells and stromal macrophages will be essential to inhibit the metastasis of NPC cells.

17110715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17110715.value: 在多细胞器官发育过程中，多潜能前体细胞如何建立并维持多能性，获得细胞命运以及分化为特定功能细胞是发育生物学领域长期困扰生物学家的问题。尽管大量研究已经发现存在控制这些发育过程的关键的分子，然而其机制仍未完全阐明。未决定分化方向的神经脊祖细胞在背根神经节处能够分化为感觉神经元和卫星胶质细胞，因而是研究神经系统参与调控细胞命运获得分子的理想模型。我们既往证实Sox9是神经脊细胞的早期标志分子之一，在迁移前和迁移中的神经脊细胞中一过性表达。通过鸡胚电穿孔和突变小鼠模型，我们发现Sox9是背根神经节中神经脊祖细胞多能性维持所必需，以及诱导细胞分化为卫星胶质细胞。然而因胚胎发育阶段细胞凋亡清除掉Sox9突变的小鼠神经脊祖细胞以及电穿孔转基因技术的随机性限制了对Sox9 功能的研究，包括对未决定分化方向神经脊祖细胞维持以及对特定细胞命运获得。此外，我们发现Sox9的下游分子Sox10可以通过扰动感觉神经元的重要蛋白——neurogenin2蛋白的表达，部分的调控Sox9 特化胶质细胞系的功能。因此，我们假设 sox9在神经脊祖细胞多能性维持以及特化为胶质细胞的命运中扮演不同角色，后者通过 sox10 扰动ngn2蛋白的表达抑制神经脊祖细胞向感觉神经元系方向分化。为此，我们将通过体内细胞谱系示踪，遗传修饰细胞神经脊细胞sox9表达，胚胎电穿孔，生化研究以及基因组学技术，（1）鉴定sox9来源的神经脊细胞在神经节背根的分化的衍生物；（2）评估获得和失去sox9功能对神经脊祖细胞在神经节被根中多能性维持和细胞系分离的影响；（3）阐明sox9调控神经脊祖细胞获得感觉神经元和卫星胶质细胞命运中的分子机制。 我们的研究，在了解sox9在神经脊细胞特化和剥离中的功能之外， 将进一步深入了解sox9在未决定分化方向神经脊祖细胞多能性维持中的作用，以及在神经节背根发育过程中感觉神经元与卫星胶质细胞分离的分子机制。通过理解分子参与维持神经脊祖细胞未分化状态和决定多潜能细胞分化方向的调控机制，我们可采用操控多潜能细胞分化的方法治疗疾病。

17110715.label: Realisation of objectives
17110715.value: Objective 1: Determine the fate of Sox9-expressing neural crest cells (NCCs) by lineage analyses We have employed a “pulse and chase” genetic marking approach using the Cre-LoxP system in mice in conjunction with a Cre-reporter to determine cell fate and lineage of Sox9+ neural crest cells. We have obtained a stable germ-line transmission of 70kb-Sox9-CreERT2-2A-H2B-EGFP transgenic line which had been crossed with Rosa26-floxed stop tdTomato reporter mice. Upon 4-OHT induction in double transgenic mice at E8.5-E9.0 when initiation of Sox9 expression has just begun, we analyzed mouse embryos at E10-E12.5. At E10.5, we found most of the tdTomato+ cells were located in the periphery of the DRG which are marked by Sox2 and Sox10, indicating that cells remained undifferentiated or bipotent. By E11.5-E12.5, some tdTomato+ cells were detected in the dorsal root ganglia core where they expressed satellite glial markers Sox10 and BFABP instead of sensory neuron markers HuC/D and Islet1/2. We also compared the number of Sox9-derived cells to the number of Wnt1-cre;tdTomato-derved cells in the DRG. The results show that Sox9 descendants exhibit preferential differentiation into satellite glial cells in the DRG compared to the bulk neural crest population (Wnt1-Cre;tdTomato+) which appears to be equipotential to differentiate into both sensory neurons and glial. Together, these lineage studies suggest that cells expressing endogenous Sox9 represent a subpopulation of neural crest progenitors bias toward glial lineage in the DRG. We are in the process of scaling up the number of transgenic lines to demonstrate consistent observations between lines. Objective 2- Assess the impact of gain- and loss-of-function Sox9 function on neural crest progenitor maintenance and lineage determination To investigate the effects of Sox9 overexpression in bulk neural crest population on lineage determination in the dorsal root ganglia, we have collected and analyzed E10-E12.5 embryos from the mating cross between Wnt1-CreERT2 and another Z/Sox9 transgenic line (suspected to have low ectopic Sox9 expression from previous transgenic line) following 4-OHT treatment at E8.75-E9.0. Analysis of embryos at E10 revealed the co-expression of ectopic GFP and Sox9 protein in neural crest progenitors marked by p75, whereas no ectopic expression of both proteins was detected in Z/Sox9 control embryos. When embryos were examined at E11.5 and E12.5, the time when endogenous Sox9 expression was downregulated, we could detect co-expression of ectopic GFP and Sox9 in the periphery of the DRG with some GFP+Sox9+ cells expressing BFABP but not Islet1/2 and HuC/D, suggesting that overexpression of Sox9 tends to drive bulk neural crest progenitors to differentiate into glial lineage. To further evaluate the effects of sustained Sox9 activity limited to Sox9+ neural crest cells, we treated embryos with 4-OHT at E8.5 and E9.0 from 70kb-Sox9-CreERT2-2A-H2B-EGFP x Z/Sox9 intercrosses and analyzed at E9.5-E10.5 and E10.5-E12.5, respectively. Although we could detect co-expression of Sox9 and GFP in migratory neural crest cells at E9.5 and E10.5, we did not observe significant differences in the number of sensory neurons and glial cells formed in the DRG at E11.5 and E12.5. The lack of effects on lineage differentiation could be due to the level of Sox9 overexpression not high enough or over the threshold to impact on progenitor maintenance and lineage determination. It is also possible that the compensatory effects of bulk neural crest population override the impact on lineage determination caused by a subset of Sox9 overexpressing cells. We also crossed 70kb-Sox9-CreERT2-2A-H2B-EGFP transgenic with Sox9flox/fox mice in an attempt to delete Sox9 beyond the stage of delamination to determine its role in lineage determination because previous studies showed that germ-line-specific-Cre- or Wnt1-Cre-mediated deletion of Sox9 gene resulted in apoptosis of neural crest progenitors. Following 4-OHT treatment at E8.5 mouse embryos which were then analyzed at E9.5, we detected loss of Sox9 protein and apoptosis as shown by Caspase 3 immunofluorescence in a subset of neural crest cells. However, we did not observe significant impact on lineage differentiation in the DRG probably due to only a small portion of Sox9 mutant cells undergoing apoptosis which might not exert dramatic impact to the differentiation potential of bulk neural crest population. Nevertheless, these data indicate that Sox9 is crucial for neural crest survival beyond the stage of delamination. Objective 3: Elucidating the molecular events regulated by Sox9 in determining sensory neurons versus satellite glial cells (i) Genetic analysis of Sox10 in regulating neurogenin 2 (neurog2) expression We have purified the monoclonal neurog2 antibody from David Anderson’s lab and repeated immunofluorescence on transverse sections of Sox10+/N-EGFP and Sox10N-EGFP/N-EGFP mutants at E9.5. The results showed increased number of neurog2+ migratory neural crest cells in Sox10N-EGFP/Sox10N-EGFP mutants compared to Sox10+/N-EGFP. Similar results were obtained in chick embryos treated with Sox10 morpholino. These results suggest that Sox10 is required for neurog2 protein stability. (ii) Functional studies of Foxd3 in regulating neurog2 expression We did not investigate this issue further as we put more resources in characterizing the function of transcriptional targets of Sox10 in regulating lineage choice between sensory neurons versus satellite glial cells in the DRG of chick embryos (see iv). (iii) Biochemical analysis of neurog2 protein stability in ovo To further determine whether Sox10 could promote ubiquitination of ectopic ngn2-GFP in vivo, immunoprecipitation for anti-GFP was conducted in lysates from 10 well-transfected embryos at 9 h post-transfection (hpt) with each group being electroporated with neurog2-GFP+Sox10, neurog2-GFP+Sox10+Myc-Ub (ubiquitin) and neurog2-GFP+Myc-Ub. Addition of exogenous amount of Ub is to enhance the sensitivity of detection for the ubiquitinated form of neurog2 on Western blot. The results showed that overexpression of Sox10 with exogenous Ub enhanced the level of Ub-conjugated neurog2 to a greater extent than treatment without Ub and neurog2+Ub, suggesting that Sox10 promotes destabilization of neurog2 through ubiquitination. (iv) Genes regulated by Sox10 in lineage determination of satellite glial cells versus sensory neurons Gene expression profiling using RNA-sequencing revealed that overexpression of Sox10 upregulated expression of several F-box family members expression including Fbxo2 and Fbxo25 but they showed barely detectable expression in the DRG. Fbxw11 is expressed in the DRG neurons that does not appear to coincide with the role of Sox10 in specifying glial lineage. We thus selected Fbxo9 gene for further studies because it showed overlapping expression with Sox10 in migrating neural crest cells at HH16 but not with Islet1/2+ sensory neurons in the DRG at HH18. Consistent with the RNA-seq data, ectopic Fbxo9 mRNA was detected in most of the Sox10 overexpressing cells at 6 and 24 hpt, indicating the effect was cell-autonomous. In contrast, the ability of Sox9 overexpression to induce ectopic Fbxo9 expression was less pronounced at 6 hpt whereas no induction was detected at 24 hpt. These results suggest that Sox10 is sufficient to induce Fbxo9 expression. Gain- and loss-of-function studies demonstrate that Fbxo9 destabilizes neurog2 protein and determines glial cell fate. Co-immunoprecipitation experiment shows the ability of Fbxo9 to interact with neurog2 through the F-box motif. Epistasis analysis further demonstrate that Fbxo9 and probably other F-box members mediate the role of Sox10 in governing neurog2 protein destabilization and lineage bias of neural crest progenitors toward glial cell rather than sensory neurons. Altogether these findings unravel a new Sox10-Fbxo9 regulatory axis to promote glial fate of neural crest progenitors through neurog2 destabilization.

17110715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17110715.value: In this project, we found by lineage analysis that cells expressing endogenous Sox9 represent a subpopulation of neural crest progenitors bias toward glial lineage in the DRG. Consistently, overexpression of Sox9 tends to drive neural crest progenitor population to acquire glial cell fate instead of sensory lineage in the DRG. Genetic deletion of Sox9 beyond the stage of neural crest delamination shows that Sox9 is required for the survival of early migratory neural crest cells. Sox10 functions downstream of Sox9 to specify glial cell fate in the DRG through activation of Fbxo9 expression which destabilizes neurog2 protein. A manuscript entitled “Fbxo9 functions downstream of Sox10 to determine neuron-glial fate choice in the dorsal root ganglia through neurog2 destabilization” is currently under revision (due by 17 Dec 2019) in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (PNAS). In addition, we also published a review on ‘Neural crest stem cells and their potential therapeutic applications’ in Developmental Biology 2016 Nov 15; 419 (2): 199-216.

17110715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17110715.value: Further development of the two research projects are ongoing: (1) It has been shown that phosphorylation regulates neurog2 protein stability and proneural transcriptional activity. We are currently investigating whether neurog2 is subjected to phosphorylation in migratory neural crest by phosphoproteomics and western blot for anti-phosphoserine/threonine in immunoprecipitated neurog2 protein lysate. If neurog2 could be phosphorylated, we will further investigate whether phosphorylation of neurog2 leads to its destabilization mediated by Fbxo9. (2) Since Fbxw11 is expressed in the DRG neurons, we are currently investigating the role of Fbxw11 in sensory neurogenesis by gain- and loss-of-function studies in developing chick embryos.

17110715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17110715.value: Neuron-glial lineage segregation from neural crest progenitors to form the dorsal root ganglia is essential for the formation of the peripheral nervous system. However, our current understanding of hierarchical transcriptional control does not fully explain how this lineage bifurcation occurs. Here, we provide in vivo evidence for a glial lineage specifier Sox10 to inhibit sensory neurogenesis via a degradation mechanism. A ubiquitin-ligase Fbxo9 acting downstream of Sox10 destabilizes proneural neurog2 protein that results in loss of neurogenic capacity while maintaining glial potency of neural crest progenitors. Functional inhibition of Fbxo9 and possibly related members lead to prolonged expressioin of neurog2 protein that causes both expansion of bipotent neural crest progenitors and precocious neuronal differentiation. Our results unravel a previously unrecognized mechanism in neuronal-glial cell fate decision. In addition, recent studies show that glial cells in the DRG play active roles in chronic pain. Therefore, understanding how protein degradation contributes to the formation of glial cells will lead to a better understanding of the aetiology of this disorder.

17111015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111015.value: Liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC) is one of the most prevalent cancer worldwide as well as in Hong Kong. Ascribed to the high incidence of metastasis of HCC, prognosis of the disease is poor. Despite the well characterization of the etiological factors of HCC, including hepatitis B and C virus infection, liver cirrhosis and aflatoxin B1 intake, the involvement of genetic alterations in hepatocarcinogenesis remains poorly defined. The centrosome is a specific cellular structure that is important for a wide variety of cellular functions, including cell movement, adhesion, polarity and cell cycle progression. Compelling evidences have shown that amplification of centrosome number, i.e. supernumerary centrosome, is frequently observed in cancer cells, suggesting that aberrant centrosome function is intimately linked to carcinogenesis. Recently, the PI has identified a novel centrosomal protein, TAX1BP2 that suppresses centrosome amplification. Further studies showed that TAX1BP2 is a putative tumor suppressor in HCC and is involved in regulating the chemo-sensitivity of HCC cells. Polo-like kinase (PLK) is a signaling molecule that catalyzes the addition of phosphate to a serine or threonine residue on protein substrates. PLK4, a member of PLK family, localizes specifically to centrosome and plays a critical role in regulating cell cycle progression via maintaining normal number of centrosome in cells. The role of PLK4 in cancer development remains controversial. Interestingly recent data demonstrates that inhibitor of PLK4 is potentially applicable in treating a subset of breast cancer. To corroborate the involvement of PLK4 in hepatocarcinogenesis, we examined the mRNA expression of PLK4 in clinical HCC samples. Surprisingly, the PLK4 mRNA expression was increased in 45% of HCC as compared to their adjacent non-tumorous liver tissues. By immunohistochemical staining, PLK4 protein was shown to be highly expressed in tumor cells. Furthermore, expression of PLK4 could also promote the proliferation of HCC cells. Strikingly, our data reveals that TAX1BP2, a centrosomal protein that inhibits hepatocarcinogenesis, is indeed a good substrate of PLK4, suggesting that PLK4 may target TAX1BP2 to favor HCC formation. In this proposal, we will confirm the tumorigenic activity of PLK4 in HCC cells and examine whether PLK4 inactivates TAX1BP2 to promote hepatocarcinogenesis. Furthermore, we will explore if PLK4 plays a role in HCC chemo-resistance and metastasis. Thus our work will definitely gain novel insight into the pathogenesis and metastasis of HCC, and might reveal novel molecular targets for therapeutic intervention. 肝癌 (肝細胞癌，HCC) 是全世界及香港最普遍的癌症之一。由於肝細胞癌的轉移率很高，疾病預後往往較差。現時已知肝癌有幾種明顯的發病因素，包括乙型和丙型肝炎病毒感染、 肝硬化及攝入黃麴黴毒素B1，但在肝癌基因變異這方面，醫學上的了解還欠深入。 細胞中有一種特定的結構體叫中心體，它對於細胞內各種各樣的運作十分重要，包括控制細胞運動、細胞粘付、細胞極性與細胞週期。現時已有大量證據顯明癌細胞的中心體數目比正常細胞多，此現象稱為中心體擴增，這表示中心體異常與癌症的發生有極大關係。最近，此申請項目的首席研究员發現了一個新的中心體蛋白叫TAX1BP2可抑制中心體擴增。進一步的研究表明TAX1BP2屬於一種腫瘤抑制基因，可以抑制肝癌的發生，而且其表達可調控肝癌細胞在化療中的敏感性。 Polo樣蛋白激酶4 (PLK4)是一個信號分子，其作用是催化絲氨酸或蘇氨酸磷酸化。PLK4作為Polo样蛋白激酶家族作員之一，其位置就在細胞中心體裏面，能通過維持正常數目的中心體來調控細胞週期進程。目前對於PLK4 在癌症發展的作用仍存在爭議。有趣的是，最近有研究表明PLK4的抑制劑可能適用於治療其中一部份的乳腺癌。為了證實 PLK4 在肝癌中的功能，我們檢查了PLK4 在臨床肝癌樣本的mRNA表達量。出人意料的是，在45%的肝癌組織中PLK4 mRNA 表達量明顯增加。免疫組織化學染色結果表明 PLK4 蛋白在腫瘤細胞中高度表達。此外，PLK4 的表達還可以促進肝癌細胞的增長。值得注意的是，我們的資料揭示了中心體蛋白及肝癌抑制因子TAX1BP2是PLK4一個極好的底物分子，這表明 PLK4 可能針對 TAX1BP2 而導致肝癌形成。在這申請項目中，我們將確認 PLK4是否透過滅活 TAX1BP2蛋白而促進肝癌發生。此外，我們將進一步探討PLK4 在肝癌化療耐藥和癌轉移方面的作用。我們的工作定將為肝癌發病機制及肝細胞癌的轉移帶來新的觀點和知識，為將來提出新的分子治療靶點奠下基礎。

17111015.label: Realisation of objectives
17111015.value: For objective 1, we have successfully carried out all the objectives and characterized the functional role of PLK4 in HCC tumorigenesis. To gain a better understanding of PLK4 function in hepatocarcinogenesis, PLK4 transcript level in human HCC clinical samples was examined. Forty pairs of HCC sample with adjacent nontumorous tissues were analyzed using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. After normalization with beta-actin, PLK4 transcripts were upregulated in 47.5% of cases. The median PLK4 transcript level was significantly higher in HCC than the nontumorous counterpart. However, there was a lack of correlation with clinicopathological features and survival significance probably due to small sample size. Further examination of TCGA-LIHC datasets showed that the high expression level of PLK4 transcripts correlated with higher tumour grading, tumour stage, overall pathological stage, TP53 mutation, and poor prognosis in overall and disease-free survival. To examine the tumorigenic activity of PLK4, we established stable PLK4 knockdown clones in HCC cell lines, HLE and MHCC97L. To examine whether PLK4 possesses tumour-promoting ability, colony formation, proliferation, soft agar growth and nude mouse xenograft assays were performed using stable PLK4 knockdown cells. The result showed that silence of PLK4 significantly reduced the proliferation rate, anchorage-independent growth and in vivo tumour growth when compared to scrambled-control. Furthermore, transwell migration and matrigel invasion assay were performed to examine the effect of PLK4 on HCC metastasis. The results showed that loss of PLK4 inhibited the HCC cell migration and invasion. Conversely, overexpression of PLK4 promotes HCC cell invasion but reduced HCC cell growth rate. To identify the region of PLK4 important for growth control, colony formation assay was carried out using truncation fragments that covered different domains of PLK4. However, there was no significant difference in the colony formation rates using the truncation mutant or vector control. We attempted to overcome these problems using fragments consist of different combinations of PLK4 domains rather than a single domain but in vain. These results suggested that only full-length PLK4 exerted its effect on cell growth. To search for the PLK4 centrosome targeting region, transient transfection of different PLK4 fragments into HCC cells for co-immunofluorescent staining with centrosome markers, pericentrin and -tubulin. Immunofluorescent staining showed that the cryptic polo-box in PLK4 is essential for its centrosome targeting function. Apart from that, we also examined the activities of signalling proteins, including PAK1, LIMK1/2, Erk1/2, c-Myc, and CD44 in PLK4 overexpressing cell, but no changes were detected. For objective 2, we have completed all of the experiments. To identify the PLK4 phosphorylation site on TAX1BP2, we employed two different approaches. First, we predicted the phosphorylation site using an online program (GPS3.0) and identified six potential PLK4 phosphorylation sites on TAX1BP2 (S1044, T1048, S1089, T1096, S1195, S1301). We mutated all the potential serine or threonine residue into alanine and performed the in vitro kinase assay. In vitro kinase assay result suggested that S1044, T1048, S1195, and S1301 were potential PLK4 phosphorylation sites on TAX1BP2. However, when we further tested the effect of these mutants on HCC cell growth, they showed no remarkable difference in the colony formation assay, indicating that the phosphorylation site may not have an impact on TAX1BP2 tumour suppressive function. Thus, the mass spectrometry approach was adapted. The result suggested that residues S1271, S1274, S1300, S1301 and S1308 were potential PLK4 phosphorylation sites. However, using in vitro kinase assay, we could not confirm the phosphorylation sites identified by mass spectrometry analysis Interestingly, when we tried to understand the role of TAX1BP2 in PLK4 oncogenic activity, we found that Hepatitis B virus oncoprotein HBX interacted with TAX1BP2 and suppressed TAX1BP2 to promote microtubule dynamic and aneuploidy (data published in Cancer Letters). Consistently, in stable inducible PLK4 expressing clones, aneuploidy is one of the phenotypes. This raises the possibility that PLK4 regulates, possibly by phosphorylation, TAX1BP2 to enhance aneuploidy in HCC cells. Therefore, a better understanding of how PLK4 regulates TAX1BP2 will be of interest, interfering such regulation might be envisioned as a potential therapeutic approach against HCC progression and metastasis. Since we failed in identifying the putative phosphorylation site of PLK4 on TAX1BP2, we attempted to overcome the problems by searching for mechanisms other than TAX1BP2 phosphorylation to explain the oncogenic effect of PLK4. By literature search and co-immunoprecipitation assay, we confirmed that PLK4 interacted with two other kinases, i.e. Tyrosine Kinase expressed in Hepatocellular Carcinoma (TEC) and Aurora A kinase (AurkA) that may be important for HCC formation and centrosome duplication. To investigate the role of TEC on the regulation of PLK4, we examined the phosphorylation of PLK4 by TEC. Using in vitro kinase assay and truncation mutants, we identified a novel TEC phosphorylation site, i.e. tyrosine 86 (Y86) residue, on PLK4. Our data suggested that Y86 phosphorylation was crucial for PLK4 stability and invasion ability. Mutation of Y86 to a phosphorylation defective mutant (Y86F) was sufficient to revert the PLK4 induced invasiveness in HCC cells. Besides, we showed that stable TEC expressing cells had a significant increase in growth, migration, and invasion rates; whereas knockdown of TEC reversed the effects and suppressed the in vivo tumour growth using nude mouse xenograft assay. Using in vitro kinase assay, we showed that AurkA phosphorylated at the cryptic polo-box domain of PLK4, a region characterized to be important for PLK4 dimerization that is critical for PLK4 activity. We hypothesized that the AurkA phosphorylation blocked the dimerization before PLK4 self-activated. Using the wound healing assay, we also revealed that PLK4-mediated cell migration could be blocked by treatment of AurkA pharmacological inhibitor. To understand how PLK4 expression promotes HCC invasion, we performed genome-wide RNA-sequencing using stable inducible PLK4 expressing and knockdown clones. Hierarchical clustering analysis based on Euclidean distance was performed on the transcriptomics data. The resulting heatmap exhibited 2-branched partition of two systems, but treatment groups were well separated from control groups. Gene Ontology terms and pathways analysis on the differentially expressed genes (p values < 0.05) were performed and the result indicated that most of the terms were related to tumorigenesis, such as cell adhesion, migration, differentiation, inflammatory response, growth. Four potential pathways were identified to be regulated in the opposite direction in the two systems, including regulation of Actin cytoskeleton, ECM-Receptor Interaction, focal adhesion and PI3K-Akt signalling pathway. To confirm the results obtained from the RNA-Seq, we examined the phosphorylation of Met receptor tyrosine kinase and central mediator of focal adhesion signalling – the Focal Adhesion Kinase (FAK), by Western blotting. The result showed that the MET receptor and FAK were activated in the PLK4 overexpressing clones as revealed by the phospho-antibodies targeting the activation form of the proteins. For objective 3, all the objectives have been achieved. The stable PLK4 knockdown and inducible PLK4 expressing clones were treated with different doses of cisplatin, doxorubicin or 5-Fluorouracil (5-Fu), for 24 and 48 hours, respectively. Cells were subjected to foci-forming assay to check for their sensitivity. Unexpectedly, the results showed that knockdown of PLK4 did not seem to have a big impact on HCC cell chemosensitivity toward chemotherapeutic drugs. The same experiments were performed using parental HLE and MHCC97L co-treated with PLK4 inhibitor and doxorubicin or 5-Fu. However, similar results were obtained and inhibition of PLK4 activity did not seem to affect the chemosensitivity of HCC cells.

17111015.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111015.value: In this study, PLK4 was found to be an oncogene in HCC. PLK4 was frequently overexpressed in clinical HCC samples and a high level of PLK4 predicted poorer overall and disease-free survival of patients. Functionally, we demonstrated that overexpression of PLK4 promoted the invasiveness of HCC cells by upregulating focal adhesion pathways. Whereas knockdown of PLK4 or treatment of PLK4 inhibitor suppressed the growth and migration of HCC cells. Importantly, HCC cells treated with PLK4 chemical inhibitor suppressed drastically the proliferation of HCC cells. Thus, our data provide evidence that PLK4 is a potential druggable-kinase and its function is related to HCC metastasis. By transcriptome analysis, a novel candidate pathway by which PLK4 induces cell migration was identified to be focal adhesion (FA). FA pathway is important for connecting the cytoskeleton to the ECM through integrins and connects multiple intracellular signalling cascades for the cell migration and invasion. In addition, we showed that PLK4 was regulated by two kinases, i.e. TEC and AurkA. Our interest in investigating TEC as a potential PLK4 regulator was prompted by the fact that TEC was overexpressed in HCC cells and its role in HCC is less characterized. We demonstrated that TEC is a putative PLK4 kinase and overexpression of TEC was oncogenic in HCC cells. Our result indicated that stable knockdown of TEC inhibited the invasion of HCC cells, whereas stable overexpression of TEC promoted HCC cell invasion. Interestingly, TEC expression was found to stabilize PLK4 resulting in an enhancement of cell invasiveness. Mechanistically, we showed that TEC phosphorylated endogenous PLK4 and the TEC phosphorylation site was mapped to Y86 residue of PLK4. The mutation of Y86 to phenylalanine significantly repress the invasion of HCC cells, suggesting that TEC is a regulatory kinase of PLK4. Furthermore, the invasiveness of stable TEC expressing cells could be inhibited by treatment of PLK4 inhibitor or knockdown of PLK4, strongly indicating that PLK4 plays a role in TEC-medicated HCC cell migration. Taken together these results argue that PLK4 is important for TEC tumour-promoting activity, especially in cell invasion (manuscript under preparation).

17111015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111015.value: As TEC acts as a positive regulator of PLK4, this raises the possibility that TEC expression may act as a surrogate marker in predicting responses towards PLK4 inhibitors. Data from current study established the functional relationship between TEC and PLK4 on promoting cancer cell invasion. However, the significance of this interaction has not yet been fully studied. For instance, both TEC and PLK4 were shown to be transcriptionally activated by NF-κB, a key transcriptional factor for inflammatory responses. As the majority of HCC progresses from chronic liver inflammation, the possibility that proinflammatory environment contributes to cancer metastasis through the TEC-PLK4 axis warrants further investigation. We observed that inducible PLK4 overexpressing cell with multiple centrosomes showed bulk TAX1BP2 staining. Since the mechanism by which centrosome linker in centrosome clustering, a strategy employed by cancer cells to prevent multipolar division, remains elusive, PLK4 induces centrosome overamplification could serve as a model to address this issue. With this system, the effect of PLK4 phosphorylation on TAX1BP2 can be examined. AurkA overexpression has suggested generating tetraploid cells and pharmacological inhibition of PLK4 causes cytokinesis failure. Thus, it is interesting to examine whether AurkA inhibits PLK4 to produce tetraploid progenies through inducing cytokinesis failure.

17111015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111015.value: Cancer is a global health problem that causes thousands and thousands of lives. In Hong Kong, liver cancer is one of the most common cancers and the number three killer of all cancers. Although surgery, radiotherapy ablation and liver transplantation are curative treatments for early HCC patients, these therapies will not be viable for advanced-stage patients. Therefore, it is critical for developing new drugs for HCC treatment. Cancer is mainly caused by the alteration of genes that lead to abnormal production of proteins. Here, we showed that one of these proteins is called PLK4, which is an enzyme that is responsible for the control of centrosome number. The centrosome is a small cellular structure that is critical for the cell division, whose abnormality results in cancer growth. We found that the PLK4 protein was frequently elevated in liver cancer. Furthermore, we demonstrated that by reducing the level of PLK4 in cancer cells, it slowed down the growth and migration of cancer to other organs. Therefore, our study suggests that aberrant increased in PLK4 protein is a causative factor for liver cancer progression and future strategy for HCC treatment can be designed to repress the PLK4 protein level.

17111315.label: Realisation of objectives
17111315.value: All the 4 objective have been fully realized. We investigated the effect and mechanism of hypoxic microenvironment and hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs) on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cancer stemness. In this study, HCC cancer stemness was analysed by self-renewal ability, chemoresistance, expression of stemness-related genes and cancer stem cell (CSC) marker-positive cell population. Specific small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) proteases 1 (SENP1) mRNA level was examined with quantitative PCR in human paired HCCs. Immunoprecipitation was used to examine the binding of proteins and chromatin immunoprecipitation assay to detect the binding of HIFs with hypoxia response element sequence. In vivo characterisation was performed in immunocompromised mice and stem cell frequency was analysed. We showed that hypoxia enhanced the stemness of HCC cells and hepatocarcinogenesis through enhancing HIF-1α deSUMOylation by SENP1 and increasing stabilisation and transcriptional activity of HIF-1α. Furthermore, we demonstrated that SENP1 is a direct target of HIF-1/2α and a previously unrecognised positive feedback loop exists between SENP1 and HIF-1α. Taken together, our findings suggest the significance of this positive feedback loop between HIF-1α and SENP1 in contributing to the increased cancer stemness in HCC and hepatocarcinogenesis under hypoxia. Drugs that specifically target SENP1 may offer a potential novel therapeutic approach for HCC.

17111315.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a common cancer and leading cause of death worldwide. Hypoxia is common in solid cancers and particularly in HCC, which is a fast growing cancer. Specific SUMO proteases 1 (SENP1) is able to deSUMOylate hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1α and increase its stability in hypoxia. 17111615.value: 急性燥動（acute agitation）是一種急性行為精神症候群。病人的燥動行為可對其個人、醫護人員及其他病人的安全均構成潛在威脅，應需介入治療。而急性燥動病人常見於醫院急症室內。急性燥動的病徵包括煩亂不安 (restlessness)、易怒 (irritability)、對刺激物有過激反應 (excessive responses to stimuli) 及言語行為不當 (inappropriate verbal/physical activity)。而急性燥動可由精神疾病、酒精或藥物中毒引起。 如不及時採取醫療措施去控制急性燥動，患者可能會有傷害他人的機會。一般初步急性燥動管理所採取的方法包括舒緩激動情緒、進行轉移注意的活動及回應病人需求。不成功的話可能需用藥物鎮靜及/或身體約束。以注射鎮靜治療前，應先考慮使用口服鎮靜治療。而是次研究主要調查在使用較侵略性治療措施前，口服藥物鎮靜治療能否有效管理急性燥動。 現時文獻建議口服鎮靜治療可有效地管理約一半患有急性燥動的病人。尤其當資源不足的情況下去監察病人，或應對病人身體機能產生的不良反應時（包括立即復甦），口服鎮靜治療能提供一個更安全的方法去管理急性燥動病人。現時只有少量高品質的臨床試驗提供在醫院急症室環境使用口服鎮靜治療的資訊。很多有關使用口服鎮靜治療的研究都在精神科中進行，由於病人的種類、治療時間及對臨床結果的期望有所不同，因此其研究結果並不適合應用於急症室。基於病人的知情權、疾病管理的緊迫性及足夠程度的盲性（blinding）各方面的考慮，一般較困難在急症室進行大規模的隨機臨床試驗（randomised clinical trials）。雖然如此，本研究團隊已成功完成兩次隨機臨床試驗，另外兩個臨床試驗也在進行中。 是次研究計劃是探討近期成為非專利藥物olanzapine 於急症室的國際性應用。以三種藥物作對照組的隨機臨床試驗，比較口溶錠olanzapine與傳統口服鎮靜藥物（haloperidol/diazepam）。 olanzapine價格的下降以及其良好的心血管系統評估能替代其他傳統抗精神病藥物（如haloperidol）。從試驗數據中可看到是次研究的重要性： haloperidol是香港最常用的傳統抗精神病藥物，但由於其帶來的不良反應（adverse events），haloperidol於國際的使用其實並不多。本研究將尋找及解決管理急性燥動的不足，從而為病人找出一種能快速溶解的合適劑型，及比傳統口服鎮靜藥物更安全又有效的替代藥物。

17111615.label: Realisation of objectives
17111615.value: We are pleased to report that all the requirements of the study has been completed. To achieve the revised study objective, we collected clinical data of over 136 thousand patients prescribed any antipsychotic from 2004 to 2014 in Hong Kong, to conduct a propensity score-matched population-based cohort study. Study goal To determine the risk of mortality by all-cause, cardiovascular diseases, or pneumonia; and the risk of cardiovascular diseases and pneumonia in patients with mental illness prescribed haloperidol versus other antipsychotics. Methods Data sources Data were retrieved from the Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS), a clinical database managed by the Hong Kong Hospital Authority which provides primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare to 7.5 million Hong Kong residents (representing 5.5-6.2 million adults between 2004-2014) through 41 public hospitals and institutions, 47 specialist outpatient clinics and 73 general outpatient clinics. Patient demographic information and clinical data (records of diagnosis, prescriptions, pharmacy dispensing, admission/discharge information, emergency attendance, laboratory test results) from all in-patient, out-patient and emergency settings since 1995 are available in CDARS for audit and research proposes. In CDARS, the British National Formulary (BNF) is used to categorise medication details, including prescription period, dosage and dosage form. The International Classification of Diseases, 9th Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-9-CM) is used to record diagnosis. The death records and cause of death were obtained from regional death registries of the Hong Kong Immigration Department. Data on cause of death is classified using the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM). Anonymous patient identifiers are generated to protect confidentiality. Cohort study design To investigate a delayed and rare outcome such as mortality with long-term treatment, a cohort study design is preferred due to the long follow-up period and large sample size. We identified all patients aged 18 or above who were prescribed an antipsychotic drug (BNF 4.2.1 and 4.2.2) from 1 January 2004 to 31 December 2014. We included incident antipsychotic users, defined as individuals who did not receive an antipsychotic prescription at least 180 days prior to the index date (start date of the incident prescription). We excluded patients with terminal illnesses including malignant neoplasm, patients with a recent diagnosis of delirium (180 days before index date), or patients receiving palliative care as the inclusion of these patients may introduce confounding. We excluded patients whose first antipsychotic prescription was a short-acting injection (i.e. non-depot formulation) as this is typically prescribed for acute symptoms. Antipsychotics used for acute behavioural disturbance in emergency settings (mainly single doses or short-acting injections for acute disorder or undifferentiated agitation) were not included. A similar exclusion criterion was applied in previous studies investigating mortality risk of older patients on antipsychotics. The follow-up started from the incident antipsychotic prescription start date (Day 1) and ended at the earliest occurrence of any of the following: death, end of study (31 December 2016), switching to another antipsychotic or starting concurrent prescription of another antipsychotic. We censored the follow-up at drug switching/concurrent prescription to prevent the potential effect of drug-drug interactions. The exposure of interest was any incident prescription of antipsychotic with haloperidol as the reference group. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes were cardiovascular-related and pneumonia-related death. In the original study protocol, we also explored suicidal death and rheumatoid arthritis as secondary outcome and negative control outcome, respectively. However, due to low incidence of events, both outcomes were not included due to lack of power. To study the duration of effect, follow-up was sub-divided into short-term (Day 1-30), mid-term (Day 31-180) and long-term (Day 181 to the end of follow-up). To study the dosage effect, we conducted a subgroup analysis on relative levels of cumulative dosage, which was derived using the defined daily dose (DDD) as low dose (<0.5 DDD/day), moderate dose (0.5 to <1.5 DDD/day), high dose (≥1.5 DDD/day) or missing dosage. A similar categorisation was applied in a study investigating mortality risk in patients on psychotropic drugs, including antipsychotics. Propensity score matching Propensity score is the conditional probability of receiving treatment. By matching patients in different treatment groups with the estimated propensity score, confounding due to non-random treatment allocation can be controlled. In this study, the propensity score estimated patients’ probability of receiving haloperidol over other antipsychotics, derived from a logistic regression model. In this model, the dependent variable was the prescription of antipsychotics (haloperidol or other) and covariates were sex, age, comorbidities (diagnostic record before Day 1 of the following: schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, other psychoses, major depressive disorder, dementia, anxiety disorder, delusional disorder, personality disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, sleep disorder, behavioural problem, myocardial infarction, arrhythmia, other ischaemic heart disease, congestive heart disease, hypertension, cerebrovascular disease, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, hypothyroidism, Parkinson’s disease, hepatic disease and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), recent medication (antidepressant, hypnotic, anxiolytic, antiepileptic, antidiabetic, drugs used in hypertension and heart failure, antiplatelet, calcium channel blocker, diuretic, beta blocker, antiarrhythmic, digoxin, nitrate, anticoagulant, peripheral vasodilator, lipid-regulating drug, antimanic, oral corticosteroid, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug [NSAID], proton pump inhibitor [PPI], histamine-2 receptor blocker [H2 blocker], antibacterial, antifungal and antiviral prescribed in the 365 days before Day 1, and the total number of prescriptions in the 365 days before Day 1), and recent healthcare service usage (number of inpatient admissions, outpatient clinic appointments and emergency attendances in the 365 days before Day 1). After trimming 5% of patients with extreme propensity scores, patient(s) prescribed with haloperidol were matched to each patient on non-haloperidol antipsychotics on the propensity score within a stratum of sex and 5-year age band using a parallel, variable-matching-ratio (up to 2:1) nearest neighbour algorithm. This matching method has been demonstrated to improve matching precision and allow a similar distribution of observed baseline characteristics among matched subjects. The propensity score calculation, trimming and matching were conducted for each non-haloperidol antipsychotic. To examine the matching performance, we calculated weighted standardised differences of each covariate between haloperidol and other antipsychotic groups before and after matching. Those with a value less than 0.1 after matching were considered to have negligible imbalance in the covariates. Statistical and sensitivity analyses The hazard ratio (HR) of each outcome with 95% confidence intervals (95% CI) was estimated using the Cox proportional hazards model in the matched cohorts for each antipsychotic drug versus haloperidol. HRs for each outcome were estimated for the short-term, mid-term and long-term, also in the low-dose, moderate-dose and high-dose subgroups. More commonly prescribed first-generation antipsychotics (haloperidol, chlorpromazine, sulpiride, and trifluoperazine) and second-generation antipsychotics (risperidone, quetiapine, clozapine, olanzapine, amisulpride, and aripiprazole) in Hong Kong were reported in this study. Since mental illness requiring antipsychotic treatment is usually a chronic condition, we assumed that antipsychotic treatment was continuous once the incident prescription started. To verify this assumption, we conducted a sensitivity analysis which censored follow-up at the cessation of antipsychotic prescription. Two prescriptions with a gap of no more than 28 days apart were considered continuous. Analyses were independently conducted by KSJL and AYSW and results were crosschecked using R (version 3.33; R core team) and SAS (version 9.3; SAS Institute, Inc) for quality assurance. A two-sided p-value of 0.05 was considered statistically significant. We also reported the survival curves by all-cause mortality for each propensity-score-matched cohort.

17111615.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111615.value: A total of 136 593 new antipsychotic users were identified during the study period after application of the exclusion criteria. Haloperidol was the most commonly prescribed antipsychotic, followed by quetiapine, risperidone and sulpiride. The total follow-up was 438 333 person-years (mean 3.2 person-years). Successfully matched subjects showed similar baseline characteristics with a weighted standardised difference less than 0.1, except for hypertension, ischaemic heart diseases, cerebrovascular diseases, antiplatelet, calcium channel blocker, beta-blocker, nitrate, lipid-regulating drugs, NSAID, PPI/H2 blocker and antibacterial drugs in aripiprazole-haloperidol matches, and PPI/H2 blockers in olanzapine-haloperidol matches. Risk of mortality During the follow-up, there were 44 400 deaths, of which 6 841 were cardiovascular-related, and 16 141 were pneumonia-related. Patients aged over 65 had the highest mortality rate (205.0 per 1000 person-years) among all subgroups. Patients on haloperidol presented with the highest mortality rate (186.8 per 1000 person-years) among all antipsychotics. The results of primary analysis showed that non-haloperidol antipsychotics were associated with a statistically significantly lower risk of mortality versus haloperidol with HRs ranging from 0.43 for trifluoperazine (95% CI 0.36-0.53) to 0.68 for chlorpromazine (95% CI 0.64-0.72). Cardiovascular-related mortality was significantly lower for risperidone (HR 0.79 [95% CI 0.66-0.93]), sulpiride (HR 0.78 [95% CI 0.64-0.96]), chlorpromazine (HR 0.76 [95% CI 0.65-0.90]) and quetiapine (HR 0.67 [95% CI 0.57-78]) compared with haloperidol. Significantly lower pneumonia-related mortality risk was observed for all non-haloperidol antipsychotics, except amisulpride and olanzapine, with HRs varying from 0.38 (95% CI 0.24-0.61) for trifluoperazine to 0.76 (95% CI 0.68-0.85) for risperidone. For duration of effect, a lower risk of all-cause mortality was observed for non-haloperidol antipsychotics. This association occurred consistently throughout follow-up except for the short-term prescription of aripiprazole. For cardiovascular-related mortality, lower HRs were observed for quetiapine for all time periods, risperidone for short-term period and chlorpromazine for long-term period. For pneumonia-related mortality, a lower risk was observed in all time periods for chlorpromazine, quetiapine and risperidone, the short-term period for sulpiride, the mid-term period for trifluoperazine, and the long-term period for aripiprazole, sulpiride and trifluoperazine. Dosage level analysis suggested a lower risk of all-cause mortality in the low-dose and moderate-dose groups for chlorpromazine, risperidone, quetiapine, olanzapine and aripiprazole, which was similar to the primary analysis. A lower risk of mortality from cardiovascular diseases and pneumonia was observed to be associated with low-dose prescriptions of risperidone, quetiapine, and chlorpromazine. Moderate-dose prescriptions of quetiapine and chlorpromazine were associated with lower risk of pneumonia-related death.

17111615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111615.value: For future research direction, larger sample size and longer follow-up period are required for relatively new marketed antipsychotics (such as aripiprazole) and subgroup analyses. Other important modifying factors including exercise, dietary pattern, genetics may be considered in the mortality risk evaluation model where data could be accessed and linked using additional datasets. Furthermore, in addition to mortality risk as more a comprehensive health outcome, future research could focus on other important clinical outcomes that impact quality of life and resource utilisation. Outcomes of clinical interest include (but not limited to) metabolic syndrome and neurodegenerative diseases. This study was accepted for publication (CNS Drugs) in December 2019. It is anticipated that the study results will be disseminated to broad international readership including psychiatrists, emergency clinicians, mental healthcare workers. Our research findings may be included and cited in local Hospital Authority clinical guidelines on the use of haloperidol in different clinical settings. We have commenced discussion with emergency clinicians at the Hong Kong College of Emergency Medicine regarding the place of haloperidol in the emergency setting. It is anticipated that our results will contribute to a change in practice and optimise the way antipsychotic drugs are monitored and used.

17111615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111615.value: Haloperidol is among the most commonly used first-generation antipsychotic medication in Hong Kong and globally. In the current literature, it is unclear how the risk of death of long-term users of haloperidol compare with other antipsychotics including the newer, second-generation antipsychotic medications. In this study, we found that haloperidol was associated with an increased risk of death compared with several other common antipsychotics, regardless of cause of death. This was found to occur consistently throughout follow-up. Haloperidol was also associated with an increased risk of death due to heart disease or pneumonia compared with risperidone, quetiapine, sulpiride, and chlorpromazine. A higher risk of death due to any cause was observed for haloperidol (whether low or moderate dose) compared with other antipsychotic medications (chlorpromazine, risperidone, quetiapine, olanzapine and aripiprazole). While haloperidol continues to be commonly used in different clinical settings globally and locally, our research broadens our understanding of the potential risks involved compared to other antipsychotics and guides clinical decisions on the choice of medication. Treatment with haloperidol, especially in older patients and patients at risk of heart disease or pneumonia, should be carefully monitored while the preferred option of other antipsychotics with lower risk may be considered.

17111715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111715.value: 蛋白糖基化可以導致細胞內外蛋白的故障。該反應的產物， 高級糖化終產物（AGEs）在血管病變，腎病變，神經病變和視網膜病變的糖尿病患者的發病機制中發揮着重要作用。因此抑製AGEs的形成被公認為是最有希望的預防糖尿病並發症的方法之一。清除活性羰基化合物（尤其是二羰基化合物）是一種有效抑制AGEs形成的方法。目前一些合成的活性羰基清除劑已進入臨床試驗並取得了一些成功，證實該類類方法的可行性。由於合成藥物的毒副作用，近年來該類研究更專注於天然產物作為AGEs形成的抑制劑的研究。我們最近的研究表明具有獨特的2,4,6- trihydroxybenzyl多酚類物質是有效的活性羰基清除劑；這些多酚類物質可以迅速和活性羰基化合物發生化學反應以形成穩定的加合物。但是由於多酚類物質只是最近才被確認為活性羰基清除劑，而且前期的測試主要在非細胞體系中進行，有待於進一步研究在真正的生物體系中它們是否也能清掃活性羰基化合物及抑制AGEs的形成。另外多酚類化合物可以通過其他途徑來抑制AGEs的形成及降低AGEs誘導的毒性，例如與AGEs 的受體（RAGE）的相互作用，減少活性氧和氮物資的形成，進而導致NFκB的失活，抑制促炎細胞因子，生長因子和粘附分子的釋放，或通過直接調節葡萄糖的动态平衡。这些方面都有待于进一步的研究。 本研究將針對上述問題，精选三类具有相似的抗氧化活性，但是不同的活性羰基清除能力多酚纯物质，芹菜素，cyanomaclurin和根皮素在細胞和動物體系中進行研究。同时也精选富含芹菜素，cyanomaclurin和根皮素的三種植物提取物，甘菊，菠蘿蜜和蘋果来评估其它與多酚共存的植物化學物質與我們精選的多酚物質是否有協同的抗糖基化作用。我們的研究結果將有助於澄清具有雙重屬性，即抗氧化和羰基清除能力的天然酚類物質是否會更有效的抑制AGEs的形成，和降低AGEs誘導的細胞毒性以及改善糖尿病小鼠血管功能和調節葡萄糖的動態平衡的作用。我們也將確定純化的多酚抑或是富含多酚的植物提取物是否是對糖尿病血管並發症治療的更好選擇。

17111715.label: Realisation of objectives
17111715.value: Objective 1. Establishing human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) as the cell model to evaluate the methylglyoxal-scavenging capacity of some selected phenolics and phenolic-enriched extracts; We have established human umbilical vein endothelial cells as cell model to evaluate the direct trapping of methylglyoxal by different phenolic compounds and extracts. The following compounds including carnosic acid, rosmarinic acid, phloretin (a dihydrochalcone), apigenin (a flavone), and cyanomaclurin, plus probucol and AG and the following extracts including Rooibos tea, Dark tea, Peppermint, Yerba mate and Hong Dou Shan leaves were tested. We also tried to identify the active methylglyoxal-scavenging agents in Hong Dou Shan leaves. We demonstrate that three flavonoids can scavenge/trap MGO in cell model (HUVECs) with a MGO concentration ranging from a low concentration (25 μM) to high concentration (500 μM), sharing the same efficiency as in chemical model. In addition, in cells, the MGO-scavenging capacity of phloretin is similar with AG, which is a well-known anti-AGEs drug candidate. Furthermore, both phloretin and apigenin show a significantly higher trapping ability of MGO compared to a famous antioxidant probucol, suggesting their potential as inhibitors against AGEs formation. It also partially proves our hypothesis that flavonoids with dual effects are better inhibitors against AGEs formation. Among the plant extracts, Hong Dou Shan extract shows the strongest trapping capacity of methylglyoxal with a group of catechins identified as active components. A manuscript titled as “Antiglycative capability and effective components of Taxus chinensis” is under writing and will be sent to Food Chemistry for review. Objective 2. Investigating the protective effects of some selected phenolics/extracts on the direct formation of AGEs, induced oxidative stress, and endothelial dysfunction in HUVECs; and objective 3. Investigating the inhibitory effect of selected phenolics on AGEs-induced endothelial cell apoptosis and inflammation and the underlying mechanisms; As phloretin and apigenin were discovered to be the most active methylglyoxal trapping agents. We further selected phloretin and apigenin to evaluate their impacts on oxidative stress, inflammation and cell apoptosis in HUVECs. Results showed that apigenin could directly trap methylglyoxal (MGO) to form apigenin-MGO adducts, thus inhibiting AGEs formation. Apigenin and di-MGO apigenin adduct (DMA) were found to inhibit AGEs-induced oxidative stress and inflammation in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) by significantly suppressing ROS production (30% relative to control) and decreasing the protein expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and adhesion molecules (MCP1, IL6, TGF-β1 and ICAM1) by 30–70 %. Further mechanistic investigation revealed that the protective effect was likely mediated via suppression of the ERK/NF-κB signalling pathway initiated by AGEs-RAGE interaction and induction of ERK/Nrf2 pathway with subsequent up-regulation of antioxidant defense molecules NQO1, GCLC, GCLM and HO1. In summary, our results suggest that apigenin possesses great potential to protect against AGEs-associated health disorders by modulating cellular inflammatory and antioxidant defense signalling pathways. This part of research is summarized into one manuscript “Inhibitory effect and mechanism of apigenin and its methylglyoxal-adduct on advanced glycation end products induced oxidative stress and inflammation in human umbilical vein endothelial cells” and currently the manuscript is under review by Free Radical Biology & Medicine. In addition, we examined the inhibitory eﬀect of pterostilbene on AGEs-induced damage. Pterostilbene was found to signiﬁcantly suppress ROS production, mRNA expression of NADPH oxidase, and carbonyl levels of proteins and AOPP, which are related to oxidative stress. In addition, pterostilbene signiﬁcantly reduced gene expression of inﬂammatory mediators, including TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-6. Further analysis showed that pterostilbene inhibited AGEs-induced RAGE up-regulation, but showed no eﬀect on CD36. Moreover, it reduced NF-κB phosphorylation and MAPKs activation, including p38 and ERK1/2 induced by AGEs. Thus our results indicated that pterostilbene might act as a promising agent to alleviate AGEs-induced oxidative stress and inﬂammation via RAGE/MAPK/NF-κB pathway. This part of research work has been published in Journal of Functional Foods. Furthermore, we investigated the inhibitory effect of DMA (di-MGO apigenin adduct) on advanced glycation end products (AGEs)-induced inflammation in macrophages and macrophage-endothelial co-cultures. Results showed that DMA remarkably inhibited the mRNA and protein expression of RAGE, thereby inhibiting the production of ROS and pro-inflammatory cytokines, including TNF-α, IL 1, IL 6, and MCP 1 in RAW 264.7 cells. In the co-culture system which was performed in Boyden chamber, macrophages filtration and adhesion to endothelial cells was significantly suppressed by DMA. Further study indicated that DMA decreased AGEs-evoked IL 6 and MCP 1 secretion, which might be achieved through RAGE and its downstream regulated TGF-β1 and ICAM 1 expression. In conclusion, our study demonstrates that DMA has anti-inflammatory activity in both macrophages and macrophage-endothelial co-cultures, offering a promising approach for slowing down the development of chronic diseases. This part of research work is summarized into one manuscript and is under review by Food Chemistry. Objective 4. Investigate the protective effects of these selected phenolics/extracts against AGEs formation, oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction in arteries from db/db mice and their direct impact on glucose homeostasis. We selected two rosemary components, rosmarinic acid (RA) and carno-sic acid (CA), to study their activity against hypoglycemia, hyperlipidemia, oxidative stress and an imbalanced gut microbiota architecture in diabetic rats. Treatment with RA and CA (30 mg kg−1) decreased the levels of fasting plasma glucose (23.7%, 15.6%), total cholesterol (30.4%, 14.1%) and triglyceride (65.7%, 47.8%) at 15 weeks. RA and CA also exhibited an anti-oxidative and anti-glycative eﬀect by lowering the formation of malondialdehyde and advanced glycation end products. In addition, they showed protective eﬀects against tissue damage and inﬂammation in the abdominal aorta, based on microscopic observations and the analysis of protein expression. Finally, the prebiotic eﬀects of RA and CA on gut microbiota were demonstrated by increasing the population of diabetes-resistant bacteria and decreasing the amounts of diabetes-sensitive bacteria. Overall, RA showed a stronger protective eﬀect than CA in mitigating diabetic symptoms in rats. This part of research work was published in Food & Function.

17111715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111715.value: Protein glycation can lead to the malfunction of intracellular and extracellular proteins. Products from such a reaction, generally termed as advanced glycation end products (AGEs), play important roles in the pathogenesis of vasculopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy and retinopathy in diabetic patients. Therefore, the inhibition of AGEs formation has been recognized as one of the most promising strategies for the prevention of these devastating complications. An effective therapeutic approach is by scavenging the reactive carbonyl intermediates (particularly dicarbonyls) of AGEs. In this project, we evaluated the bioactivity/action mechanism of phenolic-type carbonyl scavengers by chemical/molecular biological approaches. Several representative phenolic compounds including apigenin, cyanomaclurin phloretin, carnosic acid, rosmarinic acid and pterostilbene and several extracts were evaluated of their effects on the formation of AGEs, oxidative stress, and AGEs-induced apoptosis and inflammation (some of the results were published in Journal of Functional Foods, Food & Function, Food Chemistry, three top journals in the field of food science and technology ), evaluated their carbonyl scavenging potentiality in cells and whether their carbonyl scavenging capacity/antioxidant activity is responsible for their health benefit, plus their action mechanism against inflammation, oxidative stress. We discovered apigenin and phloretin can scavenge reactive carbonyls in vitro with better antiglycative effects, more interestingly, the flavonoid-reactive carbonyl adducts also showed beneficial effects, as an example, apigenin and di-MGO apigenin adduct (DMA) were found to inhibit AGEs-induced oxidative stress and inflammation in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) by significantly suppressing ROS production (30% relative to control) and decreasing the protein expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and adhesion molecules (MCP1, IL6, TGF-β1 and ICAM1) by 30–70 %. Further mechanistic investigation revealed that the protective effect was likely mediated via suppression of the ERK/NF-κB signalling pathway initiated by AGEs-RAGE interaction and induction of ERK/Nrf2 pathway with subsequent up-regulation of antioxidant defense molecules NQO1, GCLC, GCLM and HO1 (the manuscript is under review by Free Radical Biology & Medicine, impact factor: 6.002). Furthermore, in animal study, some of these phenolics exhibited an anti-oxidative and anti-glycative eﬀect by lowering the formation of malondialdehyde and advanced glycation end products. In addition, they showed protective eﬀects against tissue damage and inﬂammation in the abdominal aorta, based on microscopic observations and the analysis of protein expression (published in Food and Function). Our findings helped to clarify that natural phenolics possessing dual properties, namely antioxidant and carbonyl-scavenging activities, would inhibit the formation of AGEs, and AGEs-induced cytotoxicity with better efficacy.

17111715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111715.value: The accumulation of reactive carbonyl species (RCS) and their subsequently induced protein modifications are proposed to constitute a state of “carbonyl stress”. These RCS are responsible for the formation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs), linked with diabetic complication. A very few chemical agents have been found to suppress/prevent excessive generation and accumulation of cellular RCS. Our study demonstrated that certain types of phenolics could directly scavenge RCS in a cell culture system and these phenolic derivatives could protect the cells from RCS-induced carbonyl stress. Furthermore, our study suggested these phenolics compounds could play multiple roles against diabetic complications ameliorating different pathological conditions such as elevated AGEs formation, increased oxidative stress, inflammation, cell apoptosis and endothelial dysfunction through different action mechanisms. This study provided a pharmacological foundation for phenolics as a new class of RCS scavengers and contributed to drug discovery regimes and prevention of RCS-associated chronic diseases.
