17112615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112615.value: Schizophrenia is a severe mental illness with enormous burden to patients and society. Our understanding of its nature is still rudimentary. Though the illness is likely to be heritable, the knowledge of specific genes involved is limited by the complexity of syndromic behavior in schizophrenia. Therefore, symptom-specific approaches and identifying elementary phenotypes of the disorder such as the endophenotype, may be crucial to further our understanding of schizophrenia. Delusion of reference is among the most common psychotic symptoms. Visual signals referring to oneself (being looking at) is one of the key themes of reference delusion. Perception of visual signal, particularly other’s gaze, is essential in social interaction. When attention is specifically targeting to oneself, it usually signifies important implications for the individual. Literature suggests that patients with schizophrenia are more likely to judge averted gaze as self-referential. A pilot study conducted by our group confirmed and replicated the results of previous studies. A similar tendency has been reported in patients with Turner’s syndrome, a congenital condition which is three-fold more prevalent in patients with schizophrenia. Imaging studies suggest the possible involvement of neural networks specifically related to self-referential processing. Hypersensitivity of self-referential gaze perception (SRGP) could be a part of the basic mechanism for the generation of self-referential delusions. It could also be a potential content-dependent endophenotype of schizophrenia. However there has not been any longitudinal study looking into detailed mechanisms of this phenomenon and its potential as an endophenotype of schizophrenia. We proposed a longitudinal prospective study of patients with first-episode psychosis (FEP), subjects with at-risk-mental state and healthy control to study the state dependent nature of SRGP and its relationship with psychopathology. We will also conduct a cross sectional study of patients with (FEP), autistic spectrum condition and healthy control to study the specific mechanism of SRGP abnormality. Patients with FEP, their healthy full siblings and healthy controls will be recruited to test the hypothesis that SRGP hypersensitivity is present at higher rate in non-affected siblings of patients. Finally the neural basis of SRGP specific to the illness process using functional MRI will be explored. Understanding of the mechanisms of SRGP abnormality in patients may facilitate our understanding of the evolution of the delusional believe. This symptom-specific approach may help to delineate the underlying mechanisms of this complex and heterogeneous illness. The exploration of its potential as an endophenotype of schizophrenia could support future genetic studies.

17112615.label: Realisation of objectives
17112615.value: We explored the hypothesis one with two studies. In study one, we tried to understand the difference of SRGP between patients (N=75) and controls (N=25) and its relationship with symptomatology and cognitive functions. We found a significant group differences for ambiguous-SRGP (10° and 15°) (Wald χ2 = 19.199, p < 0.001) and unambiguous-SRGP (20°, 25° and 30°) rates (Wald χ2 = 15.546, p < 0.001) between patients and healthy controls where patients were divided into three groups: high reference group (HRef group), low reference group (LRef group) and clinical remission group (Rem group). The ambiguous-SRGP pairwise comparisons showed significant difference between HRef group and Rem group, HRef and HC group, LRef group and Rem Group, and LRef group and HC group. But no difference was found between HRef and LRef groups and Rem and HC groups. For unambiguous-SRGP, pairwise comparisons only found significant difference between HRef group and all other groups. Cognitive function composite score, SAPS and SANS total scores were found to be significantly associated with ambiguous-SRGP and unambiguous-SRGP rates. PDI score was associated with ambiguous-SRGP rate. IRIS score as associated with unambiguous-SRGP rate. The overall linear regression model with transformed ambiguous-SRGP rate as dependent variable, and cognitive function composite score, SAPS and SANS total scores as independent variables was significant (F=4.226, p=0.008). Only cognitive function composite score was significant in the model (B=-0.253, p=0.044) and SAPS total score showed a trend significance (B=0.21, p=0.065). Results of this study suggested that patients with psychotic symptoms had hypermentalization of gaze direction as towards oneself and it was positively related to psychotic symptoms and negatively associated with cognitive functions. Therefore, SRGP is likely to be a state phenomenon. The misperception of self-referential gaze may reinforce the existing delusional belief of patients and contribute to the persistence of psychotic symptoms. Improving general cognitive functions in symptomatic patients with schizophrenia may help to reduce SRGP and hence reduce the reconsolidation of the delusional belief. A manuscript of this study has been submitted for publication and is currently under review by Schizophrenia research. In study two, we have included ARMS and siblings’ groups for further study and eye tracker and intentional judgement assessments were also conducted. We found that intentional judgement measured with Comic Strip task were significantly related to both ambiguous SRGP (r=-0.496, P<0.001) and unambiguous SRGP (r=-0.365, P<0.001) in the first episode psychosis (FEP) patients but not among the ARMS or other groups. For the eye tracker data analysis, we adopted Hidden Markov Model (HMM, a time-series model in machine learning) based approach, which considers the individual differences in temporal and spatial dimensions of eye movements. With that approach, two common eye movement strategies were found among participants: eyes-focused strategy and nose-focused strategy. Eyes-focused strategy is consisted of more compact regions of interest around the eyes area, while nose-focused strategy has wider regions of interest across the face center. Significant differences were found between patients and healthy controls on the eye movement strategies they adopted, χ2(1) = 9.93, p = .003. Healthy controls were more likely to use the eyes-focused strategy than patients. Such differences were observed across angles (center: χ2(1) = 5.079, p = .047; ambiguous angles: χ2(1) = 11.329, p = .002; and unambiguous angles: χ2(1) = 5.079, p = .047). In addition to eyes-nose scale, each HMM’s entropy H was calculated. Entropy is a measure of predictability: higher entropy indicates a less predictable or more random eye movement pattern, and a lower entropy value reflects higher predictability. A 2 x 3 ANOVA revealed a significant interaction effect between gaze angle and group, F(1.72, 99.51) = 3.36, p = .046, partial Eta2 = .055 (Mauchly’s test of sphericity was violated, and the Huynh-Feldt correction was used). Main effect of gaze angle (p = .39) and of group (p = .80) were not significant. When we examined the gaze angle effect in the two groups separately using a one-way repeated-measures ANOVA, patients’ overall eye movement entropy across the three angle categories showed a significant gaze angle effect, F(1.67) = 3.52, p = .045, partial Eta2 = .11 (Mauchly’s test of sphericity was violated, and the Huynh-Feldt correction was used): patients’ eye movement patterns showed higher inconsistency in the center and ambiguous angle than unambiguous angle conditions. In contrast, controls did not show a significant gaze angle effect (p = .604). A 2 x 3 ANOVA on marginal entropy of the first fixation showed a similar significant interaction effect between gaze angle and group, F(1.72, 99.99) = 3.85, p = .030, partial Eta2 = .062. Again, one-way repeated-measures ANOVAs on marginal entropy of the first fixation revealed that patients’ overall entropies differed significantly across the angles, F(2, 1.658) = 5.26, p = .012, partial Eta2 = .15, while controls’ overall entropies did not (p = .76; Mauchly’s test of sphericity was violated and the Huynh-Feldt correction was used). The main effect of gaze angle (p = .19) or group (p = .85) were not significant. A manuscript on these results of eye movements measured with eye tracker compared between patients and controls are in preparation for submission. For research question two, the study one reported difference of the SRPG of patients at difference stage of the illness (remission and acute stage) and significant relationship between positive psychotic symptoms and SRPG suggesting the SRPG is likely to be a state phenomenon. Kruskal-Wallis H tests revealed significant group differences on ambiguous-SRGP (χ2(2) = 18.242, p <0.001) and unambiguous-SRPG (χ2(2) = 15.326, p <0.001). Post-hoc pairwise comparisons showed that ambiguous-SRGP was significantly different between patients with FEP and healthy controls (p = 0.023), and between participants with ARMS and healthy controls (p < 0.001), while there was no difference between patients with FEP and participants with ARMS (p = 0.126). Such observations hold true for unambiguous-SRGP (patients with FEP – healthy controls: p = 0.002; participants with ARMs – healthy controls: p =0.005; patients with FEP – participants with ARMS: p = 1). Both ambiguous SRPG and unambiguous SRPG of ARMS was significantly related with social anxiety symptoms measured with LSAS (p<0.001) and the unambiguous SRGP of ARMS was also significantly related with depression symptoms measured with BDI (r = 0.422, p = 0.028) but not with other psychotic symptoms. This suggested the SRPG of ARMS is related with the affective symptoms. No significant difference on SRGP between siblings of patients and healthy controls. These results suggested that SRPG is likely to be a state phenomenon. Preliminary analysis of the task fMRI suggested that patients have more activation at the middle frontal gyrus, prefrontal gyrus, medial prefrontal gyrus than the health controls while healthy controls have more activation at insula than patients when exposed to the ambiguous gaze stimulus. When exposed to the unambiguous gaze stimulus, healthy controls were more activated at the interior parietal gyrus and postcentral gyrus while patients were more activated at the middle occipital gyrus and precentral gyrus. This suggested possibility of presence of specific brain activity related to different types of gaze stimulus among patients and control groups.

17112615.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112615.value: Self-referential gaze perception (SRGP)—the perception that others’ gaze is towards oneself—is a core experience in patients with schizophrenia, and may be related to common delusional themes such as delusions of reference. Studies exploring SRGP bias in schizophrenia are limited and results have been inconsistent, particularly regarding its relationship with symptomatology and cognition. We found symptomatic patient displayed higher ambiguous SRGP rate, and the group with high reference delusions showed more unambiguous SRGP bias. Cognitive functions, positive and negative symptoms were associated with SRGP rate. Cognitive function was the only significant predictor for ambiguous-SRGP rate. Patients with psychotic symptoms have hypermentalization of gaze perception as towards oneself, whereas patients with delusions of reference have more profound bias in gaze perception. General cognition is implicated in SRGP rate. Results of this study has been written up as manuscript and submitted to schizophrenia research journal, currently under review. Eye movement assessment using Hidden Markov Model suggest that there are two eye movement strategies in judging the gaze perception: eye-focused and nose-focused. Significantly more patients adopted nose-focused strategy than healthy controls. This nose-focused strategy is also related with the positive symptoms. Furthermore, patient’s eye movement patterns show higher inconsistency in the center and ambiguous gaze angle than the unambiguous angle, whereas controls did not show such inconsistence. This suggest that patients and health controls have different eye movement patterns in viewing the eye gaze stimulus and determining the SRGP. Manuscript on these results of eye movement analysis is in preparation for submission. We found SRGP of ARMS is significantly different compared with the healthy controls but is not with the FEP. SRGP of patients is associated with psychotic symptomatology and SRGP of ARMS is associated with affective symptoms. We did not find significant difference of SRGP between siblings and healthy controls. These suggested that SRGP is likely to be state dependent. The fMRI of the gaze stimulus suggested that patients have more activation at the middle frontal gyrus, prefrontal gyrus, medial prefrontal gyrus than the health controls when exposed to the ambiguous gaze stimulus. When exposed to the unambiguous gaze stimulus, healthy controls were more activated at the interior parietal gyrus and postcentral gyrus while patients were more activated at the middle occipital gyrus and precentral gyrus. These results suggested that different neurobiological pathway may be activated in expose to the gaze stimulus between patients and controls.

17112615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112615.value: Future studies could investigate interventions with targeted psychopathological profiles using strategies to improve non-social cognitive functions to test the hypothesis that cognitive functioning is related to SRGP bias and delusional beliefs. Further study can explore the psychotic-experiences and schizotypal characters in the general population may have different eye movement pattern. A collaborative grant with one of the key collaborators of this project is in preparation. Furthermore, current study used 2-D photo as stimuli, further study on the ecological assessment of the SRGP could be development. The difference in the behavioral outcomes and eye movement patterns suggesting a difference in attentional pattern between groups. In collaboration with another research group at the University of Minnesota, we have piloted a mouse tracker study where subjects were asked to view standardized picture with details only be seen by moving mouse cursor to the locations of interest. All movements of the mouse cursor were collected online. Random Forest classifier found the patient classification accuracy can reach about 85%. Results has been submitted for poster presentation at the Conference of Society of Biological Psychiatry 2020 and grant application based on this pilot result is in preparation.

17112615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112615.value: Many people with psychosis often feel like they are being looked at. We are interested to see if this sense of “being looked at” is related to psychosis. We want to use this as a marker for spotting psychosis. We compared the sense of “being looked at” between patients with psychosis, people who are at risk for psychosis, healthy participants and healthy siblings of patients with psychosis. We found that both patients and people who are at risk for psychosis were more likely to feel like “being looked at”. Patients who are more psychotic and had poorer cognitive functions are more likely to have a stronger sense of “being looked at”. People who are at risk for psychosis had a stronger sense of “being looked at” when they are depressed or socially anxious. We also tracked participants’ eye movement when looking at faces and found that patients were more likely to look across the face while healthy participants were more likely to focus on the eyes. Our study showed that the sense of “being looked at” is related to the state of having psychosis and patients have distingue eye movement patterns.

17113315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113315.value: Psychotic disorder is a condition associated with staggering societal cost, and often lifelong disability. Cognitive impairment is at the core of the disorder, and if accurately assessed can provide critical information for outcome and treatment. A key disturbance is the organization in patients’ thoughts, which is related to how ideas are represented in the brain and how their meanings are retrieved (semantic networks). These disturbances are linked to many symptoms such as delusions and disordered thinking. Most theories assume words (and their corresponding ideas/concepts) are arranged in a network which may be disturbed in psychotic disorder due to a difference in their representations or activations. Despite considerable work using word association paradigms, the relationship between semantic abnormalities and psychopathology (subjective experiences of delusions, though disorder) remain unclear, possibly because of methodological limitations of only testing small parts of the mental lexicon. We propose a solution using recent computational linguistics methods, through which we can accurately access the structure and content of how concepts are organized in the mind for individual patients. By conducting a 6-month longitudinal study of patients and healthy participants, we will develop longitudinal semantic network models for both groups and relate these to psychopathology. Our network-based proposal offers an alternative to the restricted view of the mental lexicon as a hierarchical taxonomic knowledge repository, but rather assumes the structuring force is primarily thematic and retrieval is a process of integration, namely finding a context of word use. Such an account offers new data on semantic organization in patients at macro, meso- and microscopic levels according to modern methods in network analysis. At a macroscopic level, we can examine the degree of organization and efficiency of information. At a mesoscopic level, the network informs us about what the flow of information between a subset of ‘nodes’. At the microscopic level, the local density of connectivity for a node allows an evaluation of how accessible words/ideas in the lexicon are. 17113315.label: Realisation of objectives
17113315.value: All project objectives have been met. The project developed a novel methodology of studying large-scale semantic networks in psychotic disorders. This new network analysis approach, an undirected cue-by-cue networks constructed based on similarity of responses between cues, was applied to the semantic association data collected through the continued word association task (Objective 1). To study the psychopathology of psychosis, 40 adult schizophrenia spectrum patients and 40 matched healthy controls have been recruited, assessed at baseline and at 6-month follow-up. The global network parameters this study used to investigate the semantic network include network density, clustering coefficient, average shortest path length, modularity. The following analyses have been conducted (Objective 2, 3, 4): 1) Response characteristics, semantic distance and global network parameters of the patient group and that of healthy control group were compared to identify the differences in semantic network; 2) Global network parameters of patients’ network at baseline and at follow-up were compared to identify the change of semantic network across time; 3) Subgroup analyses of the patient group were also conducted, the global network parameters between patients whose symptoms have improved significantly over time and those who have not were compared. The patients were split into subgroups based on symptom severity (positive, negative, formal thought disorder, affective symptoms and cognitive functioning).

17113315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113315.value: Across time comparisons of patients between baseline and 6-month follow-up have been conducted, where generally patients experienced positive symptoms at baseline with poor cognitive and social-occupational functioning. Then at follow-up, positive symptoms (p< 0.001) and general psychopathological (p=0.004) symptoms have significantly improved with 59.52% of the patient subjects experiencing at least 20% improvement in overall PANSS scores across time. The patients also significantly improved in terms of social-occupational functioning (p= 0.002), whereas most of the cognitive functioning parameters remain unchanged across time. Firstly, a general characterisation of responses was looked at through comparing response valence, concreteness and semantic distance. Patients’ response valence were lower at baseline, and significantly increased at follow-up (p=0.033). This may be reflecting the decrease in positive and general psychopathology symptoms in patients across time. There were no changes in patients’ response concreteness overtime (p= 0.577). In addition, there was a significant interaction between group and time point on semantic distance (F = 6.865, p= 0.009), where semantic distance of patients’ responses were significantly greater than controls at both time-points (p< 0.001). There is a significant time effect: the semantic distance reduced significantly over time (p< 0.001). Within the patient group, a change in semantic distance was correlated with symptom change over time, specifically with general psychopathology (p=0.024), depressive (p= 0.046) and manic symptoms (p< 0.01). Global network parameters were also compared. In patient and control network comparisons, the patients’ network differed from control’s network in which their association network is denser, more clustered, with shorter average shortest path length, but is less modular. Furthermore, the network structure changes across time when patient’s mental states changed was also found. The baseline network is denser and more clustered than follow-up network. This may indicate that part of the anomalies noted in patients’ network at baseline has changed across time with the reduction of positive and general psychopathological symptoms. Change in semantic network from baseline to follow-up in patients were also looked at through sub-group analyses. The key findings are as follows. Patients with more severe positive symptoms have flatter semantic structure. Patients with higher FTD symptoms and those with more cognitive impairments are found to have more clustered networks. Patients with more severe negative, depressive and FTD symptoms are shown to have networks with higher average shortest path lengths. Patients with more severe positive and FTD symptoms, less symptom improvement and more severe cognitive impairment have higher network density.

17113315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113315.value: Potential further development of the research project would be the application of semantic network analyses in At-Risk Mental States (ARMS) individuals for prediction of clinical onset of psychosis. Moreover, this study demonstrated the use of semantic network parameters as both a state and trait measure, in which to some extent improves but does not normalize with symptom reduction. Thus, we can hypothesize that this may be a potential predictor for relapse. Abnormalities in the semantic network could be an indicator towards the latent vulnerability to relapse. Future studies could investigate the use of semantic network analyses as a predictor for relapse.

17113315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113315.value: The current study is the first to develop a novel methodology to investigate how ideas are organized in the mind using a large-scale network model. Using this method, we can detect disruptions to the organization of ideas when patients suffer from a psychotic episode (with delusions and hallucinations). There is an increase of shared responses to cues at baseline, shown through a denser and more clustered semantic network, then when symptoms subsided at follow up, the semantic network normalized. Therefore, we demonstrated with this new method that the disorganization of ideas associated with the psychotic state can be reversed to a certain extent. Even in the remission state, there are still some residual abnormalities in the network structure, namely network modularity and average shortest path length. We also successfully developed a new method to assess the semantic distance between two ideas. This suggested that some of the semantic anomalies noted may be state-dependent measures, which change along with patient’s symptom change, while other anomalies may be trait measures that remain unchanged despite change in patient’s symptoms.

17113415.label: Realisation of objectives
17113415.value: Objective 1. Investigation of the role of Eya1 in the ectodermal epithelium during branchial arch segmentation We examined the Eya1-/- mutants from E8.5 to E10.5 and identified a series of phenotypes that were previously unknown. Firstly, Eya1-/- embryos displayed pharyngeal arch (PA) segmentation defect. There were no contact points between the pharyngeal ectoderm and endoderm-derived epithelia, such that the pharyngeal clefts and pouches could not form properly and the pharyngeal mesenchyme in adjacent PA never separated. Secondly, scanning electron microscopy analysis demonstrated that in E10 Eya1-/- embryos, PA2 was shortened with an apparent reduction of the proximal portion. Using specific markers Dlx1, Dlx5 and Brn1, we confirmed that the proximal arches were lost in Eya1-/- embryos. The Eya1-/- specific phenotypes prompted us to further investigate the epibranchial placodes and their possible roles in pharyngeal segmentation and arch morphogenesis. We discovered that the epibranchial placodal cells underwent a stepwise differentiation and segregation into two cell types: the previously characterized Neurog2+ delaminating neurons as well as Sox2+ /Fgf3+ cells, which formed the non-neuronal epibranchial placodes. To further analyze the novel Fgf3+/Sox2+/Ngn2- cells in the non-neuronal epibranchial placode, we used a Sox2 cell lineage tracing system (Sox2-CreER; R26REYFP mice) in which tamoxifen induction at E7.5 would label the Sox2-expressing cells after this stage. Our results showed that cells expressing Sox2 at E7.5 segregated to delaminating neurons as well as to cells in the novel non-neurogenic epibranchial placode. In this study, we had achieved Objective 1 fully. We established a new model for epibranchial placode differentiation, suggesting that the epibranchial placodes are more similar to cranial placodes which seed both neuronal and supporting non-neuronal cells. Objective 2. Investigation of the molecular interactions between Eya1 and NICD and the role of Eya1 phosphatase in modulating Notch signaling activity To address the link between Eya1 and Notch1 receptor, we first assessed the interactions between Eya1 and Notch1 ICD proteins in transfected 293T cells. Co-immunoprecipitation experiments revealed an interaction between Flag-Eya1 and Myc-Notch1 ICD, and the C-terminal domain of Eya1 showed a strong interaction with Myc-Notch1 ICD while the N-terminal domain exhibited a very weak or no interaction. To assess the half-life of Notch1 ICD, we blocked protein synthesis by cycloheximide treatment, and the short half-life of Notch1 ICD (approximately 5 hours) was significantly extended (more than 10 hours) when Eya1 was co-transfected. By in vitro phosphatase experiments, using purified Flag-Eya1 and Flag-Notch1 ICD, we showed that in the presence of Eya1 the amount of threonine-phosphorylated Notch1 ICD was reduced. To identify the target dephosphorylated threonine residue on Notch1 ICD, we noted that there was a sequence similarity between the region around T2122 in Notch1 ICD and the region neighboring T58 in c-Myc. To test the importance of T2122 in relation to Eya1 phosphatase activity and Notch1 ICD stability, we generated phospho-mimetic (T2122D) and phospho-dead (T2122A) versions of Notch1 ICD, i.e. mutant versions that mimic the phosphorylated form and which cannot be phosphorylated, respectively. The phospho-dead Notch1 ICDT2122A mutant could interact with Eya1, and its threonine phosphorylation status was not altered by Eya1, indicating that T2122 is the phosphorylation site targeted by Eya1. As the stability of Notch1 ICD is regulated by phosphorylation and ubiquitination, in particular by the E3 ubiquitin ligase Fbw7, we examined the impact of Eya1 on the turnover of Notch1 ICD. By immunoprecipitation experiments, we demonstrated that the ubiquitinated-Notch1 1ICD level was enhanced by Fbw7, but reduced significantly in the presence of Eya1. The level of ubiquitination was also reduced by Eya1. In conclusion, our results show that Eya1 interacts with Notch1 ICD via its C-terminal domain and that Eya1 acts as a threonine phosphatase on Notch1 ICD, controlling its stability. Therefore, we have fully achieved Objective 2. Objective 3. Investigation of the cooperation between Notch signaling and Eya1 in branchial arch development by gain-of-function and loss-of-function analyses To investigate the roles of Notch signaling in epibranchial placode and branchial arch development, the spatiotemporal expressions of Notch signaling factors including Jag1, Jag2, Dll1, Lfng, Mfng, Hes1, Hes6, and Hey1 were examined. Our results showed that components of Notch signaling pathway were differentially expressed and might be dynamically involved during regional specification of the epibranchial placodes. Based on our gene expression, Pax2-Cre; Rosa26N1-IC gain-of-function and Actin-cre;Rbpjf/f loss-of-function analyses, we showed that Notch signalling is required for epibranchial placode patterning into rostral and caudal regions. High levels of Notch signalling expand the caudal domain at the expense of the rostral domain, whereas loss of Notch signalling produces the converse phenotype. To address the significance of Notch signaling in normal branchial epithelial function, we knocked out the transcriptional coactivator Rbpj and investigated the requirement of Notch mediated transcriptional activities in pharyngeal segmentation. We found that the posterior placodal area and the pharyngeal arches of the Actin-cre;Rbpjf/f embryos were much reduced compared with wildtype embryos, suggesting a requirement of Notch signaling for the maintenance, but not for the initiation, of the epibranchial placodes and PA development. As loss of Eya1 resulted in reduced levels of the Notch1 receptor and lower expression of Notch downstream genes in the pharyngeal ectoderm, we tested whether restoring Notch signaling could override the phenotypic consequences of Eya1-deficiency. In a genetic rescue experiment, we activated Notch1 ICD in the pharyngeal ectoderm from the Rosa26N1-IC mouse by Pax2-Cre activation. A definitive first pharyngeal cleft could be found in the Pax2-Cre; Rosa26N1-IC; Eya1-/- embryos. Our results indicated that induced Notch signaling could restore the expression of Fgf3 and rescued the morphological and functional defects of pharyngeal epithelium caused by loss of Eya1. Moreover, activation of Notch signaling was sufficient to promote the formation of the non-neurogenic epibranchial placodes. In this study, we have fully achieved Objective 3.

17113415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113415.value: In this study, we have made the following novel discoveries: 1. We found that the posterior placodal cells are multipotent progenitors. During pharyngeal development, the epibranchial placodal region is patterned into molecularly distinct rostral and caudal domains. Furthermore, the caudal domains give rise to both neurons and non-neuronal structures. 2. We showed that Notch signaling regulates the rostral-caudal patterning of epibranchial placodes. 3. We discovered that the intracellular domain of Notch1 receptor (N1 ICD) is a novel substrate of Eya1 phosphatase. Eya1 could dephosphorylate N1ICD and modulate Notch signaling activity in the pharyngeal epithelium. 4. We showed that an Eya1-Notch regulatory axis controls the neuronal and non-neuronal epibranchial placode cell fates, and is required for the formation of proximal pharyngeal arches. Placode derived ganglia and pharyngeal epithelia collectively coordinate pharyngeal arch development during mouse craniofacial morphogenesis. The results of this study have been reported in the following research articles attached to this report: 1. Zhang, H., Wang, L., Wong, E.Y.M., Tsang, S.L., Xu, P.X., Lendahl, U. and Sham, M.H. (2017) An Eya1-Notch axis specifies bipotential epibranchial differentiation in mammalian craniofacial morphogenesis. eLife, 2017;6: e30126. 2. Wang, L., Xie, J.J., Zhang, H., Tsang, L.H., Tsang, S.L., Braune, E.-B., Lendahl, U. and Sham, M.H. (2020) Notch signalling regulates epibranchial placode patterning and segregation. Development, in revision.

17113415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113415.value: To characterize the molecular signatures of the rostral, caudal, and caudal neuronal progenitor domains of epibranchial placodes, and to decipher the developmental trajectory of these progenitor cells in craniofacial morphogenesis, we plan to perform single cell RNA-Seq experiments using wildtype and Notch mutant mouse embryos. We will seek research funding from the RGC and other research grant sources to support these further studies.

17113415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113415.value: Craniofacial morphogenesis requires proper development of pharyngeal arches and epibranchial placodes. We show that the epibranchial placodes not only give rise to cranial sensory neurons, but also generate a novel non-neuronal cell population. We identify an Eya1-Notch regulatory axis that specifies both the neuronal and non-neuronal commitment of the epibranchial placode, where Notch acts downstream of Eya1 and promotes the non-neuronal cell fate. Notch is regulated by the threonine phosphatase activity of Eya1. Eya1 dephosphorylates p-threonine-2122 of the Notch1 intracellular domain (Notch1 ICD), which increases the stability of Notch1 ICD and maintains Notch signaling activity in the non-neuronal epibranchial placodal cells. Furthermore, we reveal that the broad posterior placode area is patterned into a Vgll2+/Irx5+ rostral domain and a Sox2+/Fgf3+/Etv5+ caudal domain relative to each pharyngeal cleft. The caudal domains give rise to the neuronal and non-neuronal cells in the placode. We show that high levels of Notch signalling expand the caudal domain at the expense of the rostral domain, whereas loss of Notch signalling produces the converse phenotype. Collectively, these data unravel a new patterning principle for the early phases of epibranchial placode development, and an important role for the Eya1-Notch axis in craniofacial morphogenesis.

17113915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113915.value: The overarching goal of this proposal is to study interactions of influenza virus with its host in ways not previously possible, using a set of tools we have recently developed for the purpose. A comprehensive atlas of host factors exploited by viruses is crucial not only to provide novel insights into physiological pathways, but also for development of effective antimicrobials against emerging and re-emerging viruses. Identification of non-essential host genes that can be targeted for developing novel anti-viral compounds has the additional benefit of avoiding potential resistance acquired in viruses by mutation and selection. Enveloped viruses pose a particular challenge: genome-wide screens aimed at identifying essential host factors have yielded widely divergent results. The complexity of the assembly and release of enveloped viruses provides a potentially rich source of host targets for interference. We aim to understand the intracellular mechanisms of influenza virus biogenesis. Two main goals underlie this approach: (1) to discover new factors that control intracellular trafficking and assembly of the virus, and (2) to explore how these host factors contribute to infection mechanistically. Since viruses have evolved to exploit host machinery for entry and infection, such studies will reveal basic aspects of host cell biology too. We tackle this fundamental question of the process of influenza virus biogenesis using new genetic and biochemical approaches. We previously established a role for Tsg101 in transport of influenza HA to the cell surface. Tsg101 is known to be a component of the endosomal-sorting complex required for transport (ESCRT) machinery and had not been implicated earlier in influenza trafficking and release. We have started dissecting the function of Tsg101 in the process of virus egress. We aim to determine the mechanism of Tsg101 mediated flu transport and what other associated factors (e.g Nedd4/Nedd4L, ESCRT II and III proteins) of the ESCRT complex are involved. Post-translational modification of Tsg101 through phosphorylation and ISGylation appears to play a significant role in regulating its function in the context of influenza infection. 17113915.label: Realisation of objectives
17113915.value: Specific objective 1: Examine whether Tsg101 plays a role as a general host factor in the intracellular transport of influenza viruses. We completed this section and provided a summary in the previous progress report. Using a combination of pulse-chase assays and flow cytometry, we had identified Tsg101 as a critical component for transport of influenza virus glycoproteins (A/WSN/33, H1N1) through the secretory pathway to the cell surface. Absence of Tsg101 arrested hemagglutinin and neuraminidase transport in intracellular compartments and attenuated budding of infectious viral particles. We extended this finding to test whether this was a strain specific effect or a universal phenomenon with all influenza viruses. To do so, we tested H3N2, H7N9, H9N2, as well as H5N1 viruses. All viral strains displayed a similar defect in intracellular transport of their glycoproteins in Tsg101 deficient cells. This defect could be rescued by influenza NS1, depending on its pathogenicity. Specific objective 2: Mechanism of Tsg101 regulation by post-translational modification during virus infection To elucidate the function of Tsg101 and the role of its modification through phosphorylation, ISGylation and ubiquitylation, we generated CRISPR/Cas9 mediated knock-out of Tsg101 or MGRN1 – its E3 ubiquitin ligase – in A549 cells. In addition, we generated constructs of Tsg101 with mutants in their phosphorylation as well as Isg15/ubiquitylation modification sites. Infection with different strains of live influenza virus was performed in these Tsg101 knock-out cells reconstituted with the mutant variants of Tsg101 in conjunction with pulse-chase and confocal microscopy to identify the function of these post translational modifications that regulate its function. Our results suggest that during a productive virus infection Tsg101 is hyperphosphorylated at the Y390 residue, whereas upon IFN-I induction it is Isgylated. Influenza NS1 is the primary antagonist of the host immune response and appears to block the Isg15 modification. Upon infection with a recombinant deltaNS1 influenza strain, which fails to suppress the IFN-I response, we could isolate Isgylated but not phosphorylated Tsg101. These data suggest that phosphorylation and Isgylation are mutually exclusive modifications regulating the function of Tsg101. Similar analyses performed for Vesicular Stomatitis Virus (VSV) infection show hyper phosphorylation of Tsg101 at Y390 (unpublished data). We hypothesize that Tsg101 is hyperphosphorylated, most likely by the activity of an upstream kinase whose activity is modulated by viruses and facilitates virus release. On the other hand, under conditions of robust interferon response or exogenous IFN treatment, Tsg101 is modified by Isg15 and subsequently blocks viral protein transport from the Golgi to the PM. Specific objective 3: Large scale proteomic analyses of Tsg101 positive vesicles to identify host factors that follow the same route. We analyzed the interactome of Tsg101 in mock and virus infected cells to chart out the pathways that are activated under conditions of infection, using a proximity based labeling assay. We generated a BirA fused construct of Tsg101 as well as for Mgrn1 – its cognate E3-ligase that was reintroduced into cells deficient in either Tsg101 or Mgrn1 respectively. These cells were either mock infected or challenged with H1N1 influenza virus and all interactors (isolated through biotin modification) were identified using mass spectrometry and further validated by immunoblotting. Tsg101 was found to interact predominantly with the cytosolic proteins in mock-infection, but shifted to interacting with a specific set of exosomal vesicles and viral HA and NA upon influenza infection. Our results indicate that the post-translationally modified form of Tsg101 (such as ubiquitylation and/or phosphorylation versus Isgylation) determines its interaction with influenza virus HA and NA, which in turn recruits other cofactors necessary for transport of viral glycoproteins to the cell surface. Interestingly, loss of Mgrn1 not only blocked ubiquitylation of Tsg101, but also inhibited viral polymerase activity as measured by a mini-replicon assay, suggesting a potential role of ubiquitylation on the PB2 polymerase function during infection. Data obtained in this proposal (specifically for aims 1 and 2) on characterization of Tsg101/Mgrn1 in the context of influenza virus infection has been submitted and is under consideration in PNAS (for minor revision). Amongst the various interactors of Tsg101 in the context of influenza infection, we identified Annexin 6 (which had been previously described to play a role in influenza budding). In addition, cyclin D3 emerged as a prominent hit in our mass spectrometry dataset, which we had independently identified using a yeast two hybrid-based screening of influenza M2 interactors. We characterized the role of Cyclin D3, in greater detail, which turned out to play a significant role in restriction of virus release. We analyzed its mechanistic function in both A549 cells as well as in human bronchial epithelial cells (where it is expressed to significant levels). In the context of influenza A release Cyclin D3 was found to play a crucial role in interfering with influenza M1 and M2 interactions that are necessary to assemble progeny infectious virions. Data obtained for this section was published in Journal of Biological Chemistry (Fan et al, 2017) and has been further summarized in a review article accepted in Frontiers.

17113915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17113915.value: Specific objective 1: Examine whether Tsg101 plays a role as a general host factor in the intracellular transport of influenza viruses This aim has been successfully completed. Using a combination of pulse chase assays and flow cytometry to measure transport of viral proteins to the cell surface, we determined that Tsg101 is universally utilized by all strains of influenza viruses tested. Specific objective 2: Mechanism of Tsg101 regulation by post-translational modification during virus infection. We have successfully completed this aim. Tsg101 and Mgrn1 knock-out cells were defective in assembly and release of virus particles. In addition Mgrn1 deficient cells were also defective in the PB2 polymerase activity, suggesting that ubiquitylation is necessary not only for Tsg101 but also for PB2 function during infection. We generated several mutants of Tsg101 with defective phosphorylation/ubiquitylation/Isgylation and reconstituted them in the Tsg101-deficient background. Interaction of Tsg101 with viral hemagglutinin and neuraminidase required phosphorylation of Tsg101, which was positively correlated with its ubiquitylation and negatively with its Isgylation. Phosphorylated Tsg101 facilitated viral protein transport to the cell surface, whereas Isg15-modified Tsg101 inhibited viral transport. NS1 from more pathogenic viruses were able to hijack cellular kinases to phosphorylate Tsg101; however, with NS1 from WSN lab strain of flu, this effect was lost. These findings underscore the importance of a single post translational modification on a protein, which can determine its function in the context of infection versus innate immune response. Data obtained in aims 1 and 2 were submitted for publication in PNAS (in revision) and requires minor revision for acceptance. In addition, most of the data generated were presented in various international conferences such as Keystone and EMBO/EMBL symposiums. Specific objective 3: Large scale proteomic analyses of Tsg101 positive vesicles to identify host factors that follow the same route Proteomic analyses on the interaction of Tsg101 and its E3-ligase Mgrn1 was successfully completed in virus-infected and interferon treated cells. It supported a role of Tsg101 in transport of exosomal vesicles to the plasma membrane upon influenza infection, whereas in interferon treated cells, this shifted to a Golgi localization, indicating that Isg15 inhibits Tsg101 function by arresting it at the Golgi compartment. Amongst the interactors of Tsg101, we also identified Annexin 6 and cyclin D3, which emerged as prominent hits in our mass spectrometry dataset with infection. We characterized Cyclin D3, in greater detail, which turned out to play a role in restricting virus release. Data obtained for this section was published in Journal of Biological Chemistry (Fan et al, 2017) and summarized in a review article in Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology (accepted).

17113915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113915.value: In this proposal we investigated the role of Tsg101 and Mgrn1 in influenza virus assembly and release. We have started unravelling the involvement of the endosomal sorting complex in virus infections, especially how post-translational modifications can determine the outcome of their utilization by viruses. Apart from providing important insights into viral glycoprotein transport, this has significant therapeutic potential, because of the availability of small molecule inhibitors that are already available for targeting this pathway, especially the kinases which function to phosphorylate Tsg101 and appear to facilitate infection. These kinases and their inhibitors will be tested in future studies.

17113915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113915.value: Through this proposal we identified a crucial link between the endosomal sorting complexes in mediating assembly and release of influenza virus for facilitating budding. We determined that upon infection, influenza HA and NA proteins interact with Tsg101, which is phosphorylated by a cellular kinase that is hijacked by the virus. This interaction results in transport of the viral glycoproteins to the cell surface to enable production of more progeny virions. Loss of Tsg101 or expression of mutant variants in cells that do not associate with HA become resistant to influenza production. This appears to be largely due to the arrest in viral glycoprotein transport in the absence of Tsg101. This finding is particularly significant in terms of defining perturbations in the host secretory pathway which affects virus production, but perhaps more importantly, in emphasizing the possibility of pharmacological interventions by repurposing available drugs such as kinase inhibitors that are in clinical use. Data generated in the course of this project resulted in 1 manuscript that has been published in JBC and one in revision in PNAS. In addition, an invited review has been accepted in Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology.

17114515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114515.value: 乾燥綜合徵（Sjogren's syndrome，SS）是一種常見的系統性自身免疫性疾病。該疾病在臨床上以口乾、眼乾為主要症狀，病理上主要表現為外分泌腺組織，如淚腺和唾液腺（SG）中淋巴細胞浸潤及程度不等的組織結構破壞。雖然大量淋巴細胞浸潤唾液腺形成灶狀聚集，但是其腺體破壞的生理病理學的機制還並不完全清楚。現階段的研究主要關注並揭示了T細胞在SS的進展中的致病作用，而對B細胞在疾病發展過程中的致病機理還知之甚少。近期的研究通過在小鼠上建立人類SS模型取得了在致病機理研究上的重要突破。我們的前期工作成功建立了實驗性乾燥綜合徵（ESS）小鼠模型。該模型很好地模擬了人類SS的主要臨床症狀，我們也通過研究該模型揭示了Th17細胞在SS發病過程中的重要作用。雖然有研究報導提示了邊緣區（MZ）B細胞（一種成熟B細胞亞群）可能參與了SS的發病機理，但是MZ B細胞如何參與疾病進展的機制還不清楚。在前期的探索性研究中，我們觀察到ESS小鼠的臨床症狀出現前MZ B細胞就有極顯著的擴增。並且，我們發現了一群高分泌IL-6 的MZ B細胞亞群並以過繼性轉輸的方式證明其促進疾病進展的致病作用。在此課題中，我們將對MZ B細胞亞群在ESS進展過程中的動態變化以及其功能特徵進行深入研究，並檢測MZ B細胞亞群是否以及如何調節T細胞的激活以及功能。最後，我們將以MZ B細胞作為可能的治療靶標並觀察其對ESS疾病進展的影響。

17114515.label: Realisation of objectives
17114515.value: 1) Kinetic changes and functional features of MZ B cells in ESS development Using the mouse model of experimental Sjogren’s syndrome (ESS), we first identified significantly increased CD19+CD1dhiCD21+CD23- marginal zone (MZ) B cells, but not follicular (FO) B cells during the disease development. Moreover, CD21+ MZ-like B cells were also detected in the lymphocytic foci of salivary glands (SG) of ESS mice, indicating that MZ B cells were closely involved in the disease pathogenesis. Moreover, we characterized the cytokine production by MZ B cells and detected increased IL-6-producing MZ B cells at disease early onset stage, but reduced IL-10-producing capacity by MZ B cells at disease acute and chronic stages. Current studies, including our previous finding showed that IL-10-producing regulatory B cells were enriched in the MZ B cell compartment. To further investigate whether reduced IL-10-producing B cells contribute to ESS development, we generated ESS mice deficient for IL-10+ B cells by using adoptive transfer technique. Notably, IL-10+ B cells were found critically involved in regulating effector T cell responses including T follicular helper (Tfh) cells and Th17 cells. Transfer of wildtype (WT) B cells, but not IL-10-/- regulatory B cells, significantly ameliorated ESS pathology in diseased mice, as revealed by attenuated salivary hypofunction, decreased Tfh and Th17 cell responses (Lin X et al. Cell Mol Immunol, 2019; attached in this report). Importantly, we further demonstrated the functional importance of IL-10-producing regulatory B cells in patients with primary Sjogren’s syndrome (pSS). To determine the functional importance of MZ B cells at disease early onset stage, we first transfer MZ B cells into immunized mice upon ESS induction, showing accelerated disease progression and severe lymphocytic infiltration compared with age-matched ESS mice with FO B cell transfer or PBS vehicle treatment. We further depleted MZ B cells in mice by splenectomy, followed by ESS induction. Interestingly, splenectomized mice showed significantly reduced disease incidence, delayed ESS development and ameliorated salivary pathology compared with sham controls. Consistently, transfer of MZ B cells, but not FO B cells, fully restored the ESS development in splenectomized mice. Thus, these results suggested that MZ B cells play a crucial role in the development of ESS at early onset stage. Our previous studies identified an essential role of Th17 cells during ESS development, as IL-17-/- mice were resistant to ESS induction, regardless of absence of presence of MZ B cells. Notably, targeting Th17 cells with proteasome inhibitor, Bortezomib, significantly suppressed Th17 cell response ESS development in mice. In the present study, transfer of MZ B cells significantly promoted Th17 cell response in the draining cervical lymph nodes (CLNs) of splenectomized mice, leading to the restored disease pathology in WT, but not IL-17-/- mice with ESS induction. Thus, these results suggested that MZ B cells may contribute to ESS pathogenesis by promoting Th17 cells in the CLNs. Moreover, we detected the migration of a small MZ B cell subset into draining CLNs and effectively promoted Th17 cell response in vivo, which was further supported by the findings from in vitro co-culture studies. Using adoptive transfer technique and RNA-sequencing analysis, we have for the first time demonstrated that very late antigen-4 (VLA-4, or alpha4beta7 integrin) + MZ B cells could produce IL-6 and migrate to CLNs with potent function in promoting Th17 cells during ESS development. Together, we demonstrated that MZ B cells regulate T cell responses and contribute to the ESS pathogenesis. 2) To identify key molecular signals involved in the induction of cytokine-producing MZ B cells. Previous studies showed that B cell-activating factor (BAFF) significantly promoted MZ B cells during autoimmune diseases. In this study, we first revealed that ESS mice with BAFF treatment displayed exacerbated disease pathology with increased MZ B cells and Th17 cells, which could be ameliorated by anti-BAFF treatment. Moreover, MZ B cells exhibited potent IL-6-producing capacity upon BAFF treatment. Upon RNA-seq analysis of transcriptome signature between VLA-4+ B cells and BAFF-treated B cells, we identified that interferon regulatory factor (IRF)-4 was critically involved in BAFF-mediated IL-6 transcription, which was confirmed in cultures of WT or IRF4-/- MZ B cells. Importantly, IRF4 was found mainly expressed by VLA-4+, but not VLA-4- MZ B cell subsets, which were markedly upregulated by BAFF treatment. Using adoptive transfer technique, we generated ESS mice with WT or IRF4-/- MZ B cells, in which Th17 cells were found increased by WT, but not IRF4-/- donor MZ B cells, demonstrating a critical role of IRF4 in regulating MZ B cell function. 3) To determine the therapeutic effects of targeting MZ B cells in the treatment of ESS. Based on our current findings on the effector function of VLA-4+ MZ B cells in ESS development, we first treated ESS mice with anti-alpha4 integrin neutralizing antibody. ESS mice treated with anti-alpha4 antibodies showed significantly ameliorated salivary hypofunction and Th17 cell response, while anti-alpha 4 antibodies did not directly affect Th17 cell differentiation in culture. Thus, we further explore the therapeutic effect of firategrast, a VLA-4 inhibitor approved by FDA for patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. Indeed, firategrast treatment resulted in reduced VLA-4+ B cells in the CLNs of ESS mice. Moreover, firategrast significantly attenuated salivary hypofunction in ESS mice, with decreased serum autoantibodies and ameliorated histopathological changes in the salivary glands. Phenotype analysis revealed that ESS mice with firategrast treatment showed markedly reduced effector T cell subsets including Th17 cells and Tfh cells, as well as germinal center B cells in the draining CLNs. Thus, our results suggest that VLA-4 may serve as a promising candidate for targeting MZ B cells as novel strategy of treating human pSS (manuscript under review).

17114515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114515.value: Primary Sjogren’s syndrome (pSS) is a progressive autoimmune disease characterized by exocrinopathy involving the lacrimal and salivary glands (SG) and manifested with severe dry-eye and dry-mouth symptoms. pSS patients suffered from a lack of effective treatments in clinical management due to poor understanding of immunopathology of this disease. Current studies have suggested dysregulated B cell responses during SS development. However, the role of marginal zone (MZ) B cells, one of B cell subsets, in the pathogenesis of SS is not fully understood. In the present study, we aim to characterize the function of MZ B cells using our recently established mouse model of experimental Sjogren’s syndrome (ESS). We first observed increased numbers of MZ B cells during ESS development. Moreover, CD1dhiCD5+ MZ B cell subset exhibited impaired immunosuppressive function with reduced IL-10 production, which contributed to enhanced T follicular helper (Tfh) cell response during ESS progression. Furthermore, we demonstrated that VLA-4+ MZ B cell subset significantly promoted Th17 cell response via IL-6 production. Importantly, both adoptive transfer of functional CD1dhiCD5+ B cells and targeting VLA-4 with an inhibitor effectively ameliorated ESS development in mice. Our findings may facilitate the development of new therapeutic strategies for treating human pSS.

17114715.value: Background: Bisphosphonates (BPs) are commonly used for management of bone diseases with pathologically high resorption. Despite the great clinical benefits, a severe complication known as bisphosphonate related osteonecrosis of the jaw (BRONJ) has been reported. The large number of patients under BPs treatment for various medical indications and the poorly understood etiology and pathophysiology of BRONJ render a serious concern of clinicians and society. Key issues: 1) around 60-70% BRONJ were associated with tooth extraction, and periapical diseases is one of the major causes resulting in the extraction. Recent clinical data showed potential relevance between periodontal/periapical diseases and BRONJ, which may lead to the rest 30-40% spontaneous BRONJ. Some recent studies including our own research have elaborated the relevance between periodontal disease and BRONJ, however, the role of periapical disease in the induction and progression of BRONJ has not been fully investigated. 2) The high prevalence of isolation from BRONJ suggests a critical involvement of Actinomyces in the etiopathological process of BRONJ. However, there are no clear data so far demonstrating the role of these factors as well as the subtle correlations among dental diseases, Actinomyces infection and BRONJ. Objectives: 1) to investigate the role of periapical disease in induction and progression of BRONJ using a modified rat model with intracortical remodeling; 2) to assess the significance of oral Actinomyces infection in the etiopathological process of BRONJ; 3) to study the influence of immune status on the development of BRONJ. Methods: All the rats receive bilateral ovariectomy to induce intercorticol remodeling. Zoledronic acid (a high potent BP), and/or dexamethasone (a high potent corticosteroid), or saline vehicle are administrated depending on treatment group. Pulpal exposure is performed at the first molar of lower jaw to induce periapical disease. Actinomyces is then inoculated into the dental pulp of the rats. Micro-CT, quantitative PCR, histology and immunohistochemistry examinations are used to investigate morphological and histopathologic changes of jawbones under various experimental conditions. Significance: For the first time this modified rat model with intracortical remodeling will provide comprehensive data both to assess the impact of periapical conditions and Actinomyces infection on the etiopathological process of BRONJ under varied immune statue, and to elaborate the correlations among these factors. Any further understanding of BRONJ is of crucial clinical significance for the prevention and management of this disease. 背景: 双磷酸盐类药物被广泛应用于治疗各种不同类型的病理性骨吸收疾病并表现出优异的临床疗效, 但与此同时, 一种被称为双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死的严重并发症亦被发现. 一方面是由于种种原因需要接受双磷酸盐治疗的大量患者的迫切医疗需求; 另一方面是对双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死这一并发症的病因及其病理生理学机制认知的不足; 因此该现象已引起临床医生及社会的极大关注. 关键问题: 1) 据统计, 约60-70%的双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死患者的发病与拔牙史有关, 而根尖周病正是拔牙的一个主要原因. 近来亦有临床研究指出牙周病/根尖周病与双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死具有潜在相关性, 前者可能与另外30-40%的自发性双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死有关. 此外还有其它研究包括我们自己的研究成果均显示牙周病与该病的相关性. 然而对于根尖周病在双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死的发生发展中的作用还未有研究探明. 2) 双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死患者的标本中大量检测出放线菌提示其可能在该病的发病过程中发挥了特定的作用. 然而, 目前并没有数据显示牙源性疾病, 放线菌感染等因素及其相互作用对双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死发病的影响. 研究目的: 1) 使用具皮质骨改建的改良动物模型研究根尖周病在双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死发病及进展中的作用; 2) 评估放线菌感染在双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死发病机制中的作用; 3) 研究机体自身免疫状况对双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死的影响. 研究方法: 所有实验动物均接受双侧卵巢摘除术以诱导其发生皮质骨内改建, 然后实验动物将根据所在实验组别分别接受唑来磷酸(一种高效能双磷酸盐药物)及/或地塞米松(一种高效皮质激素)或生理盐水注射. 接下来将在下颌第一磨牙施行开髓术诱导该牙根尖周病, 同时将放线菌接种至开放的牙髓组织中. Micro-CT, 定量PCR分析, 组织学和免疫组化分析将用于对动物骨标本进行形态学及组织病理学改变的观察分析. 研究意义: 本研究使用具皮质骨内骨改建的改良动物模型, 该动物模型为双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死发病机制的研究, 对根尖周病及放线菌在不同免疫状态下作用下在该病发病机理的作用及其相互间的关系研究提供了全面的数据; 双磷酸盐药物性颌骨坏死的任何研究进展对于该病的预防与治疗都具有重要的临床意义.

17114715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17114715.value: In the first study, animals received oncologic dose of zoledronic acid (ZA) or vehicle administration. A pulpal exposure (PE) operation was performed to induce periapical disease. Micro-CT analysis demonstrated that periapical diseases significantly increased alveolar bone resorption and the resorption was greatly attenuated by ZA treatment. The results also showed that concurrent ZA therapy and periapical lesions significantly increased bone density and histological osteocyte necrosis. It suggests that periapical infectious diseases could be a risk factor for BRONJ development. Based on these findings, the influence of periapical disease in the development of BRONJ in an immunocompromised status was investigated. Micro-CT observations illustrated that concomitant ZA and steroids produced a considerably elevated BMD and strengthened microstructure. Histological results displayed an aggravated severity of osteocyte necrosis in animals under both ZA and steroid administration. The results indicate that BRONJ is a multifactorial disorder of Bps therapy and periapical diseases may increase the predisposition of having BRONJ in an immunocompromised condition. To further understand the role of oral bacteria in the progression of BRONJ, Actinomycesnaeslundii (An), a notorious pathogenic microorganism for bone invasion and frequently isolated from BRONJ lesions, were inoculated into the oral cavity of OVX animal with exposed pulp cavity. Real-time polymerase chain reaction assay demonstrated that large amount of bacterial were detected in their oral cavity but An were not routinely found in the oral cavity. The results showed that Aninoculation significantly aggravated alveolar bone resorption and changed bone microstructure in the presence of periapical diseases. Moreover, it substantially increased the incidence of subclinical osteonecrosis. In conclusion, BRONJ is a multifactorial disorder of long-term BPs therapy. Periapical disease is a risk factor involved in its development and suppressant immunological status may increase the predisposition of having BRONJ. In addition, An infection may play a critical role in the initiation of BRONJ. The presence of odontogenic infectious diseases combined with immunocompromised condition might be the prerequisite of An infection of the jaws and promote the risk for or persistence and progression of BRONJ.

17114715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17114715.value: For the first time this modified animal model with intracortical remodeling provides comprehensive data both to assess the impact of periapical conditions and Actinomyces infection on the etiopathological process of BRONJ under varied immune statue, and elaborates the correlations among these factors. The present study provide solid base for future study on the prevention and management of this disease .

17114715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114715.value: The large number of patients under BPs for various medical indications and the unknown underlying pathophysiology of BRONJ render a serious concern of patients, clinicians and society. Data derived from this study provides invaluable insight into the pathogenic mechanism of BRONJ and provide clear information of the impact of dental disease and oral bacteria on the induction and unmasking of BRONJ. The new understanding of BRONJ is of crucial significance to manage this disease, and will eventually benefit the patients, clinicians and society.

17114915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114915.value: Liver resection remains an important curative treatment for malignant liver tumors. However, liver failure (PLF) remains the commonest cause of death after resection despite advances in operative techniques and perioperative care during the last decade. A small future liver remnant (FLR) is known to be associated with PLF. For instance, removal of the right liver is necessary for clearance of a right lobe tumor. However, a small left liver (i.e. FLR) < 30% of the total liver volume will not be able to sustain the metabolic need. A right liver resection in this setting will inevitably result into PLF, and ultimately death. To avoid this life-threatening complication, the conventional approach was to occlude the right portal vein by embolization (PVE) so as to augment the left portal flow to induce FLR hypertrophy. By this approach, the left liver will grow in size by 30% over 4-6 weeks. However, 30% of the patients will suffer from inadequate liver hypertrophy or tumor progression during the waiting period that precluded them from resection. Hence, there is a genuine need to explore new approach that would optimize the chance for FLR hypertrophy and subsequent resection. In March 2012, Schnitzbauer et al. reported a novel strategy to induce FLR hypertrophy by right portal vein ligation and in-situ liver split in 25 patients with malignant liver tumors. A procedure that was later termed as Associating Liver Partition and Portal Vein Ligation for Staged Hepatectomy (ALPPS). In this landmark study, FLR volume could be rapidly increased by 74% over an interval of 9 days, and a 100% feasibility rate for staged liver resection. However, all these patients had normal livers that could explain for the significant and rapid liver hypertrophy within a short period of time. In Hong Kong where hepatitis B infection is endemic, it accounts for 80% of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) with background liver cirrhosis. Our challenge is to achieve oncological cure by resection while minimizing the risk of PLF due to insufficient and diseased liver remnant. ALPPS offers a new dimension to the management of small-for-size FLR. Our study will evaluate its efficacy as well as its safety profile in patients with chronic liver disease. To our knowledge, this will be the first prospective ALPPS study in the literature solely designated for HCC patients. 一直以來，肝切除手術都是根治惡性肝腫瘤的重要療法。過去十年，肝切除技術以及圍手術期間護理都進步不少，但術後肝衰竭依然是最常見的肝切除後死因。術後肝衰竭與過小的剩餘肝臟（剩肝）息息相關。舉例來說，要清除肝右葉中的腫瘤，就需要切除右半肝，若然左半肝體積小於全肝的30%，將不能應付代謝需要，在這情況下，切除右半肝必定會導致術後肝衰竭，最終引致死亡。為了避免這個致命的併發症，傳統的做法是以栓塞術來阻斷右門脈同時增加左門脈的血流，誘使未來剩肝的細胞增大，從而令未來剩肝整體增大。栓塞術可以使未來剩肝在四至六星期內增大30%。然而，30%的病人會因增生不足或腫瘤在這期間的進展而不能接受肝切除手術，因此必需探討如何令未來剩肝快速增大以符合肝切除的需要。 2012年3月，德國Schnitzbauer教授等報告在25位有惡性肝腫瘤的病人身上進行的創新術式，以原位斷肝暨右門靜脈結紮來誘使未來剩肝增大。這項嶄新術式後來稱為「聯合肝臟離斷和門靜脈結紮的二步肝切除術」，一般簡稱ALPPS。在那25位病人中，未來剩肝在9天內增大了74%，全部病人都可接受其後的肝切除手術。然而，這25位病人的肝臟都正常，他們的未來剩肝能在短時間內顯著而快速增大，不難理解。 乙肝感染是香港的風土病。在本港，80%伴有肝硬化的肝细胞癌起於乙肝感染。我們的挑戰是以肝切除術根治惡性肝腫瘤的同時，盡量減低因剩肝過小或帶病而出現的術後肝衰竭的風險。ALPPS正正是這挑戰的應對良方。我們的這項研究會評估ALPPS應用於慢性肝病的效用與安全性。就我們所知，這是首個單一以肝细胞癌為治療目標的ALPPS前瞻性研究。

17114915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17114915.value: ALPPS induced a much greater FLR volume gain and FLR hypertrophy rate than PVE . ALPPS induced a much greater FLR hypertrophy rate (FLR volume gain by 48.8%, or an increment of FLR/ESLV from 24.6% to 37.6% i.e. an additional 12.8% over 6 days) than PVE. The percentage of FLR volume gain was more pronounced in chronic hepatitis than cirrhosis (52.7% vs. 32.5%, p=0.025) but the speed of liver regeneration as expressed by the daily rate of hypertrophy (24.6 vs. 20.7ml/day, p=0.205), or daily FLR/ESLV ratio increment (2.1% vs. 1.6%, p=0.07) showed no significant difference. No significant independent risk factors for mortality after ALPPS was found on multivariable analysis. Right portal vein ligation in stage I operation substantially increased FLR flow from 70.2 (35.6-272.0) to 197.0 (65.3-1179.6) ml/min/100gm (p<0.001) and remained elevated at 183.2 (46.7-464.0) ml/min/100gm after parenchymal split (p<0.001). The flow then decreased to 87.4 (36.0-195.7) ml/min/100gm after stage I operation during the waiting period to stage II operation (p<0.001)(Figure 1A). Portal pressure increased from 9.0 (2.0-25.0) mmHg to 14.5 (2.0-36.0) mmHg (p<0.001) after stage I operation. All patients proceeded to staged II operation except one patient (No. 48) who had a substantial portal flow increment from 272ml/min/100gm to 1179.6ml/min/100gm after right portal vein ligation. For this patient, the portal pressure also increased from 16 to 21mmHg with occurrence of ascites after stage I operation but the FLR volume only marginally increased (FLR/ESLV increased from 19.0% to 20.5%). As a result, stage II operation was not performed due to insufficient FLR with evidence of portal hypertension. He was subsequently discharged home and later received radiotherapy for tumor control. The median preoperative ICG value was 10.1% (3.8%-30.2%), and increased to 39.5% (15.4% - 54.4%) during stage I operation (P<0.001) and 33.7% (9.7% - 66.4%)after hepatectomy in stage II operation (p=0.001) . Perioperative outcomes ALPPS was associated with more total perioperative blood loss than PVE group. Postoperative complication rate after stage I was 21.7% and after stage II was 19.6%. All post-ALPPS stage I-related complications were either grade 1 or 2 (Table 3). No difference in overall postoperative complication rates (20.7% vs. 30.4%, p=0.614) and hospital mortality rate (6.5% vs. 5.8%, P=1.000) between ALPPS and PVE was observed. The length of hospital stay for ALPPS group and PVE group were 18 and 8 days respectively (p<0.001).

17114915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17114915.value: The findings from this study which was derived from the largest series on HCC in the literature showed it for the first time the superiority of ALPPS over PVE with regard to the effectiveness in inducing liver hypertrophy without compromising the short-term outcomes of the patients. As such, ALPPS should be incorporated into the standard management algorithm of patients requiring modulation of future liver remnant before major hepatectomy. Future development should promote the application of ALPPS globally.

17114915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17114915.value: For the first time in the literature, our study showed the superiority of ALPPS over the standard treatment in the form of portal vein embolisation with respect to induction of liver regeneration without compromising the safety of the patients. Our research results which has just been accepted in Annals of Surgery (the highest impact factor in the field of surgery) has been commended by the reviewers to be innovative due to the fact that it derived from the largest single centre experience of ALPPS on hepatocellular carcinoma in the world.

17115015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115015.value: Influenza virus continues to threaten global human health with significant morbidity and mortality. Although strategies including vaccine and antiviral drugs have achieved a great advance to control influenza virus infection, the efficacy of these strategies is still limited by the highly frequent mutations in the viruses and the emergence of drug-resistance strains. Human gammadelta-T cells, as the innate-like T lymphocytes, play an indispensible role in the host immune defense systems against virus infection. Our previous studies have demonstrated phosphoantigen pamidronate can control influenza virus infection in humanized mice by enhancing human gammadelta-T cell immunity, suggesting a novel therapeutic strategy for treating influenza by targeting human gammadelta-T cells than the virus, thereby reducing the opportunity for the emergence of drug resistant viruses. However, one notable drawback of gammadelta-T cell-based immunotherapy is the rapid exhaustion of proliferation and effector responses by these cells after repeated treatments with phosphoantigen. CD137 is a costimulatory molecule expressed on T cells. CD137 signal can stimulate CD3 T cell expansion, increase cytokine induction and prevent activation-induced cell death. However, little is known about the role of CD137 signal in human gammadelta-T cells. Our preliminary study showed that human CD137+ gammadelta-T cells displayed more potent cytotoxic activity against influenza virus-infected cells than their CD137- counterpart, and this superior cytotoxic effect was mediated by CD137 engagement. Here, we will test our hypothesis that CD137 signal can stimulate the activation and expansion of human gammadelta-T cells, and enhance their antiviral activity against influenza virus in vitro and in vivo. This study will improve our understanding of the role of CD137 in the antiviral activity of human gammadelta-T cells. 17115515.label: Realisation of objectives
17115515.value: The success of liver transplantation has led to an ever-increasing demand for liver grafts. The development of living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) has substantially relived the crisis of liver graft shortage. However, the hepatic ischemia/reperfusion (IR) injury is an inevitable consequence during liver transplantation. Hepatic IR injury will be deteriorated when the graft is small-for-size, such as a partial liver graft from a living donor. The distinct inflammatory signaling pathway up-regulated in LDLT may play crucial roles for acute and chronic graft injury. Therefore, understanding the precise molecular mechanism regulating liver graft injury will be essential not only for the treatments of early graft non-function, but also for developing the new therapeutics for late phase consequences. IN current project, we aimed to explored the role and mechanism of repressor and activator protein1 (Rap1) on marginal liver graft injury during transplantation. In this GRF project, we have successfully achieved following research objectives: 1. We have investigated the impact of Rap1 on liver graft injury after transplantation both in clinical series and animal models. We have demonstrated that over expression of Rap1 was associated with severe liver graft inflammatory response, especially in small-for-size liver graft both in clinical study and rat transplantation models. 2. We have elucidated the direct role of Rap1 promoting hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury of small liver remnant in Rap1 gene knockout mice models. In mice model, the knockout of Rap1 attenuated hepatic IRI damage. 3. We have explored the regulating mechanism of Rap1 on inflammatory signaling in neutrophils and macrophages using primary cells from Rap1 gene knockout mice. The knockout of Rap1 attenuated neutrophil induced-inflammatory response and suppressed the activations of inflammation-associated NF-κB and MAPK pathway in both mouse hepatic IRI model and primary neutrophils. The knockout of Rap1 also suppressed neutrophil migration activity and adhesion in response to liver sinusoidal endothelial cells through down-regulating neutrophil F-Actin expression and CXCL2/CXCR2 pathway. In summary, Rap1 may induce hepatic IRI through promoting neutrophil inflammatory response. Rap1 may be the potential therapeutic target of attenuating hepatic IRI. All the original objectives have been fully achieved (Li CX et al, 2016). In addition to the original objectives, we have also achieved following data for publications related to acute phase liver graft injury and late phase consequences: 1. NLRP inflammasome induced liver graft injury through activation of telomere-independent RAP1/KC axis. (Liu H et al, 2017) 2. Glutathione Peroxidase 3 Delivered by hiPSC-MSCs Ameliorated Hepatic IR Injury via Inhibition of Hepatic Senescence. (Qi X, et al, 2018)

17115515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115515.value: Elucidating the precise molecular mechanism of RAP1 on liver graft injury will lay the foundation for further development of therapeutic strategies to prevent graft non-function and late phase consequences. It will also open a new window for the Research & Development for local and overseas pharmaceutical companies. Therefore, there will be potential commercial benefit for local R&D industries. We are currently developing the new treatments to attenuate liver graft injury at early phase and prevent late phase consequences including cancer recurrence for the liver transplantation recipients. Targeting RAP1 will be the potential therapeutic strategy. It will not only attenuate acute phase liver graft inflammatory injury, but also prevent late phase tumor recurrence for the liver cancer patients receiving transplantation.

17115515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115515.value: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury of liver graft is an inevitable consequence during liver transplantation. It contributes to primary liver graft non-function and/or late dysfunction, and even leads to a higher incidence of acute or chronic rejection. The acute phase inflammatory response, which is induced by hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury, also plays in important role in late phase tumor recurrence for liver cancer patient after transplantation. Therefore, identification of the key molecule orchestrating this complex web of hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury will be essential to develop novel therapy for the attenuation of liver graft injury after transplantation. In current project, we have investigated the role and mechanism of repressor and activator protein1 (Rap1) on liver graft injury during transplantation. Clinical analysis and animal models suggested that over expression of intragraft Rap1 is significantly associated with liver graft injury. Knockout of Rap1could attenuate hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury in a mouse model. Representing the efforts for basic, translational and clinical research, we have tackled the basic issues of molecular mechanism for Rap1 regulating liver graft injury after transplantation. The precise molecular mechanism explored will lay the foundation for further development of therapeutic strategies to prevent graft non-function and late phase consequences.
