17115815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17115815.value: 肝細胞癌(HCC)是最主要的一種原發性肝癌，在世界上最為常見的癌症中排名第五，也是癌症致死的主要原因。在過去幾十年裡，對肝癌的研究主要側重於基因層面上的變化。最近幾年，越來越多證據表明，表觀遺傳學變化在癌症發展中也起著重要作用。表觀遺傳學變化多種多樣，過去的研究大部分集中在DNA甲基化和組蛋白修飾。然而，染色質重塑在肝癌發生中的病理學意義卻基本未知。我們轉錄組測序(RNA-Seq)的初步結果表明，淋巴特異性解旋酶(HELLS)在肝癌中表達顯著上調。 HELLS是一種染色質重塑蛋白，是SNF2家族蛋白中的一員，包含有一個進化上保守的N-端腺苷三磷酸酶以及C-端解旋酶結構域。在功能上，HELLS控制核小體定位，局部染色質結構以調節基因表達。儘管HELLS是一個重要的表觀遺傳調節因子，其在人肝癌中的臨床病理學意義仍有待探究。初步數據顯示HELLS的表達在人肝癌中普遍上調，且與惡性的腫瘤表型緊密相關。 HELLS頻繁的表達上調可能是由SP1轉錄因子的過度激活以及miR-7水平降低造成。穩定敲低HELLS可以顯著抑制肝癌細胞體外增殖以及原位裸鼠模型的致瘤性。此外，敲低HELLS還可以顯著恢復線粒體呼吸活性，降低肝癌細胞有氧糖酵解。我們進一步確定了PTEN誘導激酶（PINK1）為HELLS潛在的下游靶標。 PINK1的表觀遺傳失活可能是HELLS介導的代謝重組的原因之一。這些初步結果讓我們推測HELLS在人肝癌中可能是一個致癌基因，通過改變代謝機制來促進癌細胞生長。此研究計劃旨在通過以下幾個方面詳細研究HELLS在人肝癌中的病理意義及分子功能：1) 確定HELLS在人肝癌中的表達變化及其臨床病理學意義；2) 研究導致人肝癌中HELLS表達頻繁上調的分子機制；3) 在體外及體內模型中表徵HELLS的致瘤性；以及4) 描繪HELLS介導的肝癌發生和腫瘤代謝重組的基本機制。我們相信，這項研究將增進我們對肝癌發生發展分子基礎的理解，並促進新的診斷和治療方法的發展。

17115815.label: Realisation of objectives
17115815.value: Objective 1 (completed): The frequent up-regulation of HELLS in human HCC has been confirmed at mRNA and protein level by RNA-Seq, qRT-PCR, and Immunohistochemistry. Objective 2 (completed): Through exome-seq and qPCR, we detected frequent amplification of HELLS gene in human HCC. Using in silico analysis we identified SP1 as an up-stream regulation of HELLS. Using shRNA and small molecular inhibitor, we demonstrated that inactivation of SP1 significantly suppressed HELLS gene expression. Objective 3 (Completed): We generated HELLS knockout cells by CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system. We demonstrated that knockout of HELLS suppressed HCC proliferation and cell migration in tissue culture. In addition, by using orthotopic liver implantation model, we demonstrated that HELLS was essential for HCC tumorigenicity and metastasis in nude mice. Objective 4 (Completed): We demonstrated that inactivation of HELLS elevated mitochondria membrane potential and ROS production, indicating that an increase of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. Inactivation of HELLS also decreased lactate production, an indication of glycolysis repression. Therefore, depleting HELLS led to HCC metabolic reprogramming and reversion of the phenotypes of the Warburg effect.

17115815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17115815.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third lethal cancer worldwide. Increasing evidence showed that epigenetic alterations play an important role in human carcinogenesis. Deregulation of DNA methylation and histone modifications have recently been characterized in HCC, but the significance of chromatin remodeling in liver carcinogenesis remains to be explored. In this study, by systematically analyzing the expression of chromatin remodeling genes in human HCCs, we found that HELicase, Lymphoid-Specific (HELLS), a SWI2/SNF2 chromatin remodeling enzyme, was remarkably overexpressed in HCC. Overexpression of HELLS correlated with more aggressive clinicopathological features and poorer patient prognosis, compared to those patients with lower HELLS expression. We further showed that up-regulation of HELLS in HCC was conferred by hyperactivation of transcription factor SP1. To investigate the functions of HELLS in HCC, we generated both gain- and loss-of-function models by CRISPR activation system, lentiviral shRNA, and CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing system. We demonstrated that overexpression of HELLS augmented HCC cell proliferation and migration. In contrast, depletion of HELLS reduced HCC growth and metastasis both in vitro and in vivo. Moreover, inactivation of HELLS led metabolic reprogramming and reversed Warburg effect in HCC cells. Mechanistically, by integrating analysis of RNA-seq and MNase-seq, we revealed that overexpression of HELLS increased nucleosome occupancy that obstructed the accessibility of enhancers and hindered the formation of nucleosome-free region (NFR) at transcription start site (TSS). Though this mechanism, up-regulation of HELLS mediated epigenetic silencing of multiple tumor suppressor genes including E-Cadherin, FBP1, IGFBP3, XAF1 and CREB3L3 in HCC. In summary, our data unravel that HELLS is a key epigenetic driver of HCC. By altering the nucleosome occupancy at NFR and enhancer, HELLS epigenetically suppresses multiple tumor suppressor genes to promote HCC progression.

17115815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17115815.value: This study demonstrated that deregulation of chromatin remodeling factors may contribute to the aberrant gene expression and liver cancer progression. Our finding also demonstrated that inactivation of HELLS can suppress liver cancer formation and metastasis both in vitro and in vivo. Further research should test the potential of using small molecular inhibitors to target HELLS or other members of SWI/SNF2 chromatin remodeling complex as a novel strategy for cancer therapy.

17115815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17115815.value: Chromatin structure controls DNA packaging and gene expression. Chromatin remodeling factors are enzymes that control the chromatin structure. In this study, we found that a chromatin remodeling factors, namely HELLS was frequently deregulated in liver cancer. Activation of HELLS lead to inactivation of key tumor suppressor genes and thereby contribute to liver cancer formation and metastasis, On the other hand, inactivation of HELLS inhibited liver cancer growth in mouse model. Our findings demonstrated that HELLS is a key oncogene in liver cancer..

17116715.label: Realisation of objectives
17116715.value: Our study objectives were realized using a genetic association study with a candidate gene approach based on a a Household Transmission Study (HTS) examining disease transmission and secondary infection of seasonal influenza virus infection in households. The HTS was conducted from 2007 to 2017, including a total of 1088 families. Influenza index cases (IC) was confirmed by a rapid diagnostic test when presenting within 48 hours of symptoms onset in a primary care clinic, their asymptomatic household contacts (HC) were recruited in a home visit. All participants maintained a daily symptom diary for 7 days, and with nose and throat swabs (NTS) collected on day 0, 3, 6, and 10 for for ascertainment of study outcomes, including laboratory confirmed influenza virus infection and viral shedding pattern. Secondary cases of clinical acute respiratory infection (ARI) in HCs was defined by the reporting of ≥2 out of 7 ARI symptoms (including fever, headache, sore throat, cough, pains in muscles, runny nose, phlegm). Laboratory-confirmed secondary influenza infection in HCs was defined as a positive RT-PCR result for influenza A or B on any NTS collected on subsequent days. Individuals reporting fever plus ≥4 other symptoms in any illness episode were classified as having a more serious clinical picture. Viral shedding in index case was quantified by RT-PCR on the NTS. A higher amount of viral shedding was defined by > 6 log10(copies/ ml) in any NTS specimen. The duration of viral shedding was estimated by the mean between the home visit days with the last positive and the first negative NTS. This study examined the genotype of 2,342 participants from 679 households participated in the HTS, including 679 index cases and 1663 household contacts. Genotyping was performed using Sequenom MassARRAY for the following 23 single nucleotide polymorphisms in 15 candidate genes: CCR2 190G/A (rs1799864), NLRP3 -2107C/A (rs35829419), NLRP3 (3_UTR) (rs10754558), IL-1B -511G>A (rs16944), IL-6 -5843A/G (rs1818879), IL-8 -251T/A (rs4073), IL-10 -1082A/G (rs1800896), IL-10 -819T/C (rs1800871), IL-10 -592A/C (rs1800872), MBL-2 -34C/T (rs5030737), MBL-2 -221C/G (rs7096206), MxA-88G/T (rs2071430), OSA1 Intron 5 (rs1077467), RIG1 G/C (rs9695310), TLR3 -1377T/G (rs3755290), TLR3 -7G/T (rs3775296), TLR4 -G/A (rs5030718), TLR4 -Asp299Gly (rs4986790), TLR7 Gln11Leu (rs179008), TLR8 -129G/C (rs3764879), TLR8 Met1Val (rs3764880), TLR8 G/T (rs11003131), CD55 T/T (rs2564978). Mixed effect logistic regression and mixed effect linear regression models were used to evaluate the relationship of polymorphisms with various binary and continuous outcomes respectively in relation to secondary infection, illness severity and viral shedding. Potential confounders including age, gender, chronic co-morbidity, vaccination history were adjusted with a fixed effect, and within-household correlation and familial relationship with a random effect. The corresponding adjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for difference SNPs were estimated, using the wild type of the SNPs as the reference category. The heterozygous genotype was also grouped with either of the two homozygous genotypes to analyse in a dominant or recessive model. Two-sided P values were reported and p≤0.05 was considered to indicate statistical significance.

17116715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17116715.value: Among all household contacts, 30.23% were classified as secondary cases of ARI (reporting ≥2 symptoms during follow-up). Polymorphism OSA1 rs1077467 GT (OR=1.42, CI=1.09,1.85), and combined GT/TT (OR=1.37, CI=1.06,1.77) in a dominant model, and CCR2 rs1799864 combined AA/AG (OR=1.47, CI=1.11,1.95) in a recessive model were associated with higher odds of clinical ARI infection. Among all household contacts, 10.91% were classified as secondary influenza infection (having a positive RT-PCR on NTS). NLRP3 rs10754558 GC (OR=1.60, CI=1.05, 2.45), and combined GC/GG (OR=1.57, CI=1.04,2.36), in a dominant model, were associated with higher odds of RT-PCR confirmed influenza infection. CCR2 rs1799864 AG (OR=0.36, CI=0.13,0.98), GG (OR=0.38, CI=0.14,1.0), and combined AG/GG (OR=0.35, CI=0.13,0.91); IL-8 rs4073 AA (OR=0.52, CI=0.28,0.95), and combined AA/TA (OR=0.68, CI=0.46,0.99) both in a dominant model, and CD55 rs2564978 TT (OR=0.53, CI=0.29, 0.96) were associated with lower odds of RT-PCR confirmed influenza infection. Clinical illness duration and severity is a proxy of viral shedding, and carried a potential impact on disease transmission. Mean illness duration was 6.99 (SD 1.96) days. MxA rs2071430 GT was associated with a shorter illness duration of 0.36 (CI=0.03,0.69) days. Mean number of symptoms reported was 4.8 (SD 1.4). Some SNPs were associated with a lesser number of symptoms. MxA rs2071430 GG and combined GG/GT were respectively associated with a mean of 0.49 (CI=0.04,0.94) and 0.45 (CI=0.02,0.89) fewer symptom. IL-1B rs16944 combined AA/GA was associated with 0.33 (CI=0.07,0.58) fewer symptoms. A more severe clinical picture (fever plus ≥4 other symptoms) was present in 60.4% of index cases. TLR8 rs3764879 CG (OR=0.39, CI=0.17,0.87), GG (OR=0.51, CI=0.28,0.94), combined CG/GG (OR=0.50, CI=0.27,0.93); TLR8 rs3764880 AG (OR=0.38, CI=0.17, 0.85), GG (OR=0.50, CI=0.27,0.93), and combined AG/GG (OR=0.50, CI=0.27,0.92), both in a dominant model; and IL-1B rs16944 combined AA/AG (OR=0.59, CI=0.40,0.87) in a recessive model, were associated with lower odds of a more serious clinical picture. IL-8 rs4073 combined AA/AT (OR=1.45, CI=1.02,2.06) in a recessive model was associated with higher odds of a more serious clinical picture. Runny nose and cough were regarded as potentially facilitating transmission. TLR3 rs3755290 CA, comparing with AA was associated with a higher odds of runny nose (OR=3.32, CI1.15,9.63). No significant associated was detected for cough. Infectivity is positively related to the duration and amount of viral shedding. Mean duration of viral shedding was 5.49 (SD 1.98) days. RIG1 rs9695310 CC and CC/CG were associated with longer shedding duration of 0.58 (CI=0.02,1.13) and 0.41 (CI=0.05, 0.77) days respectively, while TLR8 rs3764879 CC/CG and TLR8 rs3764880 AA/AG were associated with a shorter shedding duration of 0.40 (CI=0.03,0.78) and 0.40 (CI=0.03,0.77) days respectively. Mean maximum amount of shedding was 6.45 (SD 1.45) log10(copies/ml). MBL-2 rs7096206 CC and CC/CG were associated with a higher amount of viral shedding by 0.64 (CI=0.13,1.15) and 0.58 (CI=0.08, 1.08) log10(copies/ ml) respectively. IL-8 rs4073 TA (compared to AA) was associated with higher shedding by 0.37 (CI=0.00, 0.74) log10(copies/ml), IL-1B rs16944 GG/GA with lower shedding by 0.29 (CI=0.00,0.59) log10(copies/ml). A higher amount of viral shedding (>6 log10 (copies/ml) was present in 68.6% of index cases. IL-1B rs16944 GA compared with AA (OR=0.61, CI=0.38, 0.99), and CD55 rs2564978 TT compared with CC (OR=0.55, CI=0.30, 1.01), were associated with decreased odds for a higher viral shedding amount, with marginal statistical significance.

17116715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17116715.value: Our study examined the impact of host genetic polymorphisms that may affect the transmission of seasonal influenza infection in the household setting. Our result identified a number of SNPs that may be important in modifying the risk of disease transmission in a household setting, including the effects on host susceptibility of he exposed and infectivity of the infectious individual. All these polymorphisms identified in relation to susceptibility or viral shedding pattern are compatible to the current understanding regarding the role played by those genes in either the pathogenesis or immunological response to influenza infection. Manuscripts for publication are currently in preparation and should be of interest to high impact general scientific journals. SNPs affecting host susceptibility in the current study are quite different from those reported previously in the general community setting. This may be explained by the better standardization of the exposure by the presence of a laboratory-confirmed index case in the same household, which helped to eliminate the potential confounding effect of differential exposure rather than a true genetic effect as reported in previous studies. Alternatively, this may reflect potential differences of the predominant transmission pathway in the two setting, which may be affected by different sets of relevant SNPs. This is an area important for further study and clarification, which is under planning as riding on our influenza field studies in other community settings. Further exploration of SNPs that had been reported to be affecting disease outcomes (e.g. rs12252-C IFITM3) but can’t be accommodated in the Sequonom assay design, by other genotyping approach, is currently under planning as a next step. Exploration of other SNPs currently not examined in the IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TLR3, TLR4, TLR7, TLR8, MBL-2, RIG1, CCL1 and OSA1 genes will also allow for the study of different haplotypes and potential interacting effects of different SNPs.

17116715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17116715.value: The susceptibility to influenza infection in an individual has been reported to be dependent on the interplay of host immunity and viral pathogenicity. This study further examined the relationship between genetic variation and disease transmission of seasonal influenza virus infection, basing on 2,342 subjects from 679 households participated in a Household Transmission Study (HTS) conducted from 2007 to 2017. A number of different SNPs potentially affecting the transmission of influenza infection, when a member of the family is infected, were identified. The result from this study has demonstrated the importance of host genetic variation in affecting the susceptibility to influenza infection when being exposed. For an infected individual, our result also showed the importance of genetic variation in affecting the pattern and severity of clinical symptoms, and the duration and amount of viral shedding, thus one’s potential of further infecting other susceptible individuals. Our findings may help to explain the great variability in the susceptibility to influenza infection upon exposure in different individuals. These identified genetic variations affecting transmission risk are important in improving our understanding on the mechanism of disease transmission, and ultimately contribute to improved consideration for enhancing different approaches of public health control measures for influenza infection in different community settings.

17117015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117015.value: Hepatocellular Carcinoma (HCC) is a common malignancy which approximately impacts 1, 000,000 people and claims 600,000 lives annually; however, only one FDA-approved drug is available for HCC treatment. This high magnitude of unmet clinical need strongly reflects the urgency for the development of novel HCC therapies. Therefore, knowledge on the biology of HCC is warranted. HCC is composed of cancer and stromal cells. A population of stromal cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), are present in tumors yet the molecular mechanisms guiding MDSC recruitment remain elusive. MDSCs are myeloid progenitors that rapidly expand during cancer development and possess immune-suppressive and pro-angiogenic functions. Mouse and human MDSCs are phenotyped as CD11b+Gr1+ and CD11b+CD33+HLA-DR-, respectively. Hypoxia, oxygen (O2) deprivation, frequently occurs in HCC due to abnormal tumor vasculature. Hypoxia stabilizes hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs) that transcriptionally activate genes essential for cancer growth. Our preliminary data revealed that MDSCs are detected in human and mouse HCC. In vivo co-inoculation experiment showed that MDSCs promoted angiogenesis and growth of tumors. Intriguingly, MDSCs preferentially infiltrated into hypoxic regions in HCC. We found that chemokine, CCL26, was induced by hypoxia in HCC cells and significantly over-expressed in HCC tissues. In silico analysis suggested that CCL26 promoter encompasses three putative hypoxia responsive elements. Hypoxia-induced CCL26 expression was abrogated when HIFs were knocked down or pharmacologically inhibited in a HCC cell line, MHCC97L. Flow cytometry analysis showed that tumor-associated MDSCs expressed cognate receptor, CX3CR1, for CCL26. Importantly, recombinant CCL26 protein attracted MDSCs in vitro which could be inhibited by anti-CX3CR1 neutralizing antibody. Knockdown of CCL26 in MHCC97L cells suppressed MDSC recruitment and growth in vivo. These preliminary data led us to hypothesize that hypoxia, through HIFs in HCC cells, induces CCL26 which recruits CX3CR1 expressing MDSCs to HCC, thereby facilitating the growth of HCC. In this proposal, we will first investigate the clinical relevance of MDSC recruitment and CCL26 in human HCC. Second, we will detail the regulatory pathway that leads to over-expression of CCL26 in HCC. Third, we will comprehensively investigate the roles of the HIFs/CCL26 pathway in MDSC recruitment and HCC growth. Fourth, we will explore the therapeutic potentials of targeting MDSC recruitment in HCC. Taken together, our study will provide valuable information on the biology of HCC and the molecular mechanisms involved in MDSC recruitment. Our study will be beneficial to the development of therapeutic approaches to inhibit MDSC recruitment and subsequently HCC progression.

17117015.label: Realisation of objectives
17117015.value: All the objectives of the proposal have been addressed and hypothesis has been proven with data. Objective 1: To investigate the clinical relevance of MDSC recruitment and CCL26 expression in human HCC. We confirmed that CCL26 was over-expressed in human HCC. Both CCL26 and MDSC co-localized with HIF-1 markers in same tissue regions suggesting a link between hypoxia, CCL26, and MDSC infiltration. Intriguingly, we found that CCL26 was significantly over-expressed in HCC as compared to corresponding non-tumorous (NT) liver tissues. Over-expression of CCL26 mRNA (> 2 fold) was found in 49% of HCC patients and significantly associated with poorer differentiation by Edmonson’s Grading. IHC staining confirmed that CCL26 was also over-expressed at the protein level in human HCC relative to NT liver tissues. CCL26 and CA9 staining patterns significantly overlapped. Furthermore, CCL26 expression was particularly abundant near peri-necrotic regions and staining intensity gradually weakened in regions distant from peri-necrotic regions, suggesting that CCL26 expression is tightly related to hypoxia in human HCC. Hypoxia is an important micro-environmental component in solid cancers. We therefore explored the roles of hypoxia in MDSC recruitment. We stained consecutive sections of human HCCs with MDSC marker CD11b, hypoxia markers including glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) and carbonic anhydrase IX (CA9), and observed a significant overlapping staining pattern. Objective 2: To examine the regulation of CCL26 in human HCC We confirmed that CCL26 is induced by hypoxia and overexpressed in HCC. The MDSC invasion assay showed that CM from hypoxic cells possesses chemotactic ability for MDSCs. To search for the responsible chemokines or cytokines, we interrogated the mRNA expression of chemokines and cytokines from our transcriptome sequencing database consisting the expression profiles of genes in a human HCC cell line, MHCC97L, exposed to 20% and 1% O2. The absolute expressions are reflected by the FPKM (fragments per kilobase of exon per million fragments mapped) values. Two chemokines, chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 26 (CCL26) and CCL28, were particularly abundant as compared to any others (17.457 FPKM in 20%O2 and 501.377 FPKM in 1%O2; 1.824 FPKM in 20% O2 and 48.106 FPKM in 1%O2) and induced by hypoxia for 28.721 and 26.374 fold respectively. Of note, CCL28 has been previously reported as central regulator of Treg cell recruitment, whereas roles of CCL26 remain to be elucidated. Data were confirmed in individual quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR) in additional human HCC cell lines, BEL7402 and PLC/PRF/5 (PLC). To investigate whether CCL26 is directly regulated by HIFs, we examined CCL26 expression in our HIFs knockdown HCC cells. In addition, we further established HIF-1 knockout cells by Transcription Activator-like Effector Nuclease (TALEN) approach. Q-PCR and ELISA assay indicated that hypoxia induced CCL26 mRNA and protein expressions through both HIF-1α and HIF-2α. CCL26 expression was elevated in PLC cells that stably expressed constitutively active HIF-1α (CA5) construct as compared to the empty vector (EV) control under 20% O2. Pharmacologic inhibition of HIF suppressed CCL26 expression. Putative hypoxia responsive element (HRE) containing HIF binding consensus sequence –A/GCGTG- was found in the promoter region of CCL26. Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) assay demonstrated that enrichment of hypoxia-inducible binding of HIF-1α to the putative HRE of CCL26. Hypoxia also induced the luciferase activity in HCC cells expressing the wild-type (WT) but not the mutated (Mut) HRE of CCL26. These data converged to show that CCL26 is a direct transcriptional target of HIFs. Objective 3: To elucidate the roles of the HIFs/CCL26 pathway in MDSC recruitment in human HCC To further provide evidence on the mechanistic link of hypoxia and MDSC recruitment, we first established HIFs knockdown cells in MHCC97L cells that stably expressed short hairpin RNAs against HIF-1α and HIF-2α. We placed the conditioned medium (CM) generated from different MHCC97L subclones (EV, shHIF-1α, or shHIF-2α) that were exposed to 20% O2 (normoxia) and 1% O2 (hypoxia) in the bottom wells of the matrigel-coated Boyden chambers as chemoattractants. Top chambers were seeded with freshly isolated splenic MDSCs from HCC-entrained mice. Flow cytometry confirmed the purity of our isolated MDSCs. CM from hypoxic HCC cells significantly induced the motility of MDSCs and this effect was abrogated upon the knockdown of HIF1α or HIF2α. Digoxin inhibits HIF synthesis. Pharmacologic inhibition of HIF by HIF inhibitor, digoxin, in HCC cells mirrored the effect of HIFs knockdown. To further delineate the possible cross-talk between MDSC and HCC cells, we asked if the T-MDSCs express the cognate receptors for CCL26, CCR3 or CX3CR1. Both splenic MDSCs and T-MDSCs showed negative expression for CCR3; however, 7.5 ± 3.8% of splenic MDSCs expressed CX3CR1 and importantly, this subset significantly increased to 26 ± 5.3% in T-MDSCs. We further investigated the chemotactic ability of CCL26 for MDSCs by transwell invasion assay. We placed recombinant CCL26 protein or mock control in the bottom chamber while splenic MDSCs in the upper chamber. CCL26 was able to attract MDSCs but the chemotactic ability was drastically abolished when MDSCs were treated with CX3CR1 neutralizing antibody (CX3CR1 Ab). This demonstrated that CCL26 contributes to the recruitment of CX3CR1-positive MDSCs. We next sought to confirm whether the CCL26 secreted by HCC cells was able to attract MDSCs. To test this notion, we established CCL26 stable knockdown clones in MHCC97L by expressing two independent shRNA sequences against CCL26 (sh26-1 and sh26-2). We collected the CM generated by these subclones that were exposed to 20% and 1% O2 for 24 hr for MDSC invasion assay. Knockdown of CCL26 profoundly suppressed hypoxia-induced invasion of MDSC. Addition of recombinant CCL26 rescued the suppression. These data led us to suggest that CCL26 is a major chemokine responsible for MDSC recruitment under hypoxia. To provide in vivo evidence regarding the roles of CCL26 in MDSC recruitment, we orthotopically implanted 1x106 luciferase-labelled MHCC97L-NTC and –shCCL26 cells into the left lobes of the livers of mice. Percentage of CD11b+Gr1+ MDSCs, tumor volume, and endothelial cell density were significantly reduced in tumors derived from the MHCC97L-shCCL26 subclones relative to –NTC subclone. It is noted that human and mouse CCL26 proteins both contain 94 amino acids and share approximately 50% homology. To further consolidate our in vivo observation, we established mouse Ccl26 stable knockdown subclones in MM189. Consistently, recruitment of MDSC and tumor growth were significantly repressed upon knockdown of mouse Ccl26. Objective 4: To evaluate the effect of pharmacologic inhibition of HIFs and CX3CR1 in MDSC recruitment and HCC progression. Targeting MDSC recruitment is an attractive therapeutic approach to treat HCC. MDSC recruitment can theoretically be blocked by at least two approaches: (1) Inhibition of HIFs in HCC to suppress production of CCL26, (2) Inhibition of cognate receptor for CCL26, CX3CR1, in MDSCs. To test our notions, we evaluated the efficiency of HIF inhibitor, digoxin, and CX3CR1 Ab in MDSC recruitment and HCC growth. We orthotopically implanted 1x106 luciferase-labelled MM189 cells to BALB/c nude mice and daily treated the mice with either digoxin (1.2 mg/kg) to inhibit HIF synthesis or CX3CR1 Ab (0.2 mg/kg) to suppress the CCL26-CX3CR1-cross-talk between cancer cells and MDSCs. Both approaches significantly reduced CD11b+ Gr1+ MDSCs in tumors and suppressed tumor growth.

17117015.label: Major findings and research outcome
17117015.value: A population of stromal cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), are present in tumors. As studies have gradually revealed the pro-tumorigenic functions of MDSCs, the molecular mechanisms guiding MDSC recruitment remain largely elusive. Hypoxia, O2 deprivation, is an important factor in the tumor microenvironment of solid cancers whose growth often exceeds that of the functional blood vessels. Here, using hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as the cancer model, we show that hypoxia is an important driver of MDSC recruitment. We observe that MDSCs preferentially infiltrate into hypoxic regions in human HCC tissues and hypoxia-induced MDSC invasion is dependent on hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs). We further find that hypoxia-inducible factors (HIFs) activate the transcription of chemokine (C-C motif) ligand 26 (CCL26) in cancer cells to recruit chemokine (C-X3-C motif) receptor 1 (CX3CR1)-expressing MDSCs to the primary tumor. Knockdown of CCL26 in cancer cells profoundly reduces MDSC recruitment, angiogenesis, and tumor growth. Therapeutically, blockade of CCL26 production in cancer cells by HIF inhibitor, digoxin, or blockade of CX3CR1 in MDSCs by CX3CR1 neutralizing antibody could substantially suppress MDSC recruitment and tumor growth. This study unprecedentedly reveals a novel molecular mechanism by which cancer cells direct MDSC homing to primary tumor and shows that targeting MDSC recruitment represents a novel therapeutic approach for solid cancers.

17117015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17117015.value: This study has greatly advanced our understanding on the importance of hypoxia in creating the immunosuppressive microenvironment of liver cancer. Many further studies have stemmed from this funded work. We are investigating the roles of hypoxia-induced metabolites (AMP and adenosine) on MDSCs and HCC development. We have gone beyond MDSCs and are now studying other populations of immunosuppressive cells such as Tregs in HCC.

17117015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17117015.value: Cancer cells recruit alliance to assist them evading immune surveillance. Our work has revealed the molecular mechanisms by which liver cancer cells recruit immunosuppressive cells, MDSCs, to counteract T cells which are the major immune cells that eradicate cancer cells. This mechanism is induced by low oxygen due to poor blood diffusion into the tumor. Therapeutically, we identified the molecular targets to block this important step in liver cancer development.

17117715.value: 先天性心臟缺陷（CHD）是香港和世界上最常見的出生缺陷。最常見的是室間隔缺損（VSD; 62.7％）。單基因缺陷已報導引起CHD。這些基因突變引起的缺陷包括15個轉錄因子基因（例如，NKX2-5和GATA4），17個受體或配體基因，以及其他信號分子基因（例如，ACVR2B和NOTCH1）和5個結構蛋白基因（例如，ACTC和ELN）。然而，這些基因仍無法解釋CHD在人群中的發病率。在小鼠中進行CHD的遺傳研究讓我們能檢測出新的缺陷基因。在之前的一個RGC研究基金的支持下，我們建立了一個CHD小鼠家系，進行了全基因組分析，在hnrnpa1基因中檢測到一個突變。在家系的遺傳分析分析中，这兩個鹼基對“CT”缺失的突變純合子能解釋了心臟缺陷的表型。突變純合子小鼠在出生時有房室間隔缺損（AVSD）和大動脈換位（TGA）。在胚胎E9.5，突變純合子有心臟動脈管的問題，而雜合正常。在突變純合子的胚胎，hnrnpa1 mRNA表達幾乎失去，這可能是由無義介導的mRNA降解（NMD）造成。胚胎整體原位雜交（ WISH）證明hnrnpa1廣泛地在野生型E9.5胚胎表達。 hnrnpa1在三對咽弓和第二心臟發育區前端（aSHF）表達是非常強的，這表明了hnrnpa1在SHF有重要的作用。 WISH的分析發現，hnrnpa1突變導致了Nkx2.5 mRNA在aSHF的顯著下調。在SHF的擾動可導致心臟動脈管伸長缺陷和動脈極取向缺陷。此外，我們測序了273 CHD患者的HNRNPA1基因，發現2個VSD患者帶有雜合突變。所有的結果支持Hnrnpa1基因突變會導緻小鼠和人的CHD假說。這是第一次，我們提供了確鑿的證據，hnrnpa1參與SHF發育。本研究項目，我們將進入下一個步。我們將研究Hnrnpa1引起先天性心臟缺陷的發病機制從而發現新靶標/代謝途徑，並解釋這種基因突變如何改變來自胚胎幹細胞的心肌細胞的分化。該項目可能提供深入了解發育和生理過程的機制，以及為未來的藥物研發，提高我們目前對天性心臟缺陷的認識。

17117715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17117715.value: In conclusion, our project is the first to detect mutations in the Hnrnpa1 gene cause Congenital Heart Defects (CHDs) in both humans and mice. Hnrnpa1 is critical for both the First Heart Field (FHF) and Second Heart Field (SHF) during early cardiac development. However, in later stages, Hnrnpa1 only has a major role in the SHF. Loss of Hnrnpa1 in the SHF leads to dysregulation of cardiac transcription factors, including Isl1, Nkx2.5, and Tbx1, as well as signaling pathways, such as the BMP, FGF, and Notch pathways. Thus, CHDs can be caused by impaired development of both the FHF and SHF lineages. This study provides insights into the mechanism by which Hnrnpa1 becomes involved in the cardiac development. The detail results are available in our paper published in JCI Insight attached with this report.

17117715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17117715.value: Our preliminary phenotypic analysis has shown that hnRNPA1 null mutants display severe defects in the central nervous system. The expression of the progenitor markers Sox2 and Sox9 and the postmiitotic neuronal marker HuC/D in the ventricular zone of the dorsal region of the neural tube are severely affected in our mutant mice. Our expression analysis has identified that HNRNPA1 protein is predominantly expressed in the PH3, which marks the M phase cells, positive cells in the ventricular zone of neural tube and telencephalon. Our mutant mice showed reduced proliferation of the neuronal progenitors in the ventricular zone. We thus hypothesize that HNRNPA1 regulates the proliferation of the neural progenitors probably via the regulation of mRNA splicing during the M phase in the cell cycle. We will test this by knocking down hnrnpa1 in the H2B-GFP cell lines. A recent study has discovered that hnrnpa1 expression is lost in the ALS patients. This may suggest that the complete removal of hnrnpa1in the mouse is essential for phenocopying the human ALS phenotype. We have obtained an internal Seed Fund for Basic Research from HKU to conduct this study and will apply RGC or HMRF grants in future

17117715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17117715.value: Incomplete penetrance of congenital heart defects (CHDs) was observed in a mouse model. We hypothesized that the contribution of a major genetic locus modulates the manifestation of the CHDs. After genome-wide linkage mapping, fine mapping, and high-throughput targeted sequencing, a recessive frameshift mutation of the heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein A1 (Hnrnpa1) gene was confirmed (Hnrnpa1ct). Hnrnpa1 was expressed in both the first heart field (FHF) and second heart field (SHF) at the cardiac crescent stage but was only maintained in SHF progenitors after heart tube formation. Hnrnpa1ct/ct homozygous mutants displayed complete CHD penetrance, including truncated and incomplete looped heart tube at E9.5, ventricular septal defect (VSD) and persistent truncus arteriosus (PTA) at E13.5, and VSD and double outlet right ventricle at P0. Impaired development of the dorsal mesocardium and sinoatrial node progenitors was also observed. Loss of Hnrnpa1 expression leads to dysregulation of cardiac transcription networks and multiple signaling pathways, including BMP, FGF, and Notch in the SHF. Finally, two rare heterozygous mutations of HNRNPA1 were detected in human CHDs. These findings suggest a role of Hnrnpa1 in embryonic heart development in mice and humans.

17118515.label: Project Objectives
17118515.value: To investigate the general infectivity of aquatic avian H10 viruses in chickens. H10 viruses from migratory waterfowl have been repeatedly introduced to domestic ducks. However, only a single introduction to chickens was observed across six provinces in southern China in our surveillance network over the past 12 years (Table 1, unpublished). Evaluation of the general infectivity of aquatic avian H10 viruses in chickens will help delineate the host range restriction of this subtype. To investigate the general infectivity of aquatic bird H10 viruses in mammals. H10 is one of the few subtypes that can directly infect humans or other mammals without prior adaptation in aberrant hosts [6-12]. Viruses isolated in the past decades through our surveillance network show the genetic diversity of H10 viruses in the AIV gene pool (Table 2, unpublished). Whether the H10 viruses are generally infectious to mammals, or only specific strains are, needs to be investigated. To compare the mammalian infectivity of different chicken reassortant variants and investigate if the internal genes from the enzootic H9N2 virus lineage contribute to mammalian infectivity. After the H10N8 virus was introduced into chickens, reassortments between gene pool-like and enzootic H9N2 viruses were observed (Ma et al, submitted). Among these variants some acquired human infectivity leading to three human cases [8, 13]. Phenotypic differences in the mammalian models of infection will help to identify the genetic determinants associated with their infectivity. To evaluate the changes of mammalian infectivity as the H10 virus continues to evolve in chickens. Since the emergence of the novel H10N8 reassortants, H10 viruses appear to be becoming established in chickens and are continuing to evolve in poultry, leading to the accumulation of amino acid changes and further reassortment to obtain an N6 gene. Studies of these altered viruses will determine whether the infectivity of the viruses for mammals has changed.

17118515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118515.value: Similar to the ecological distribution of H2 subtype that caused the 1957 pandemic, H10 influenza viruses are not commonly seen in their primary hosts, aquatic birds. However, this subtype has sporadically infected several mammalian species, including humans. In 2013, three H10N8 human infections were identified in Jiangxi, reinforcing the pandemic potential of this subtype. Our phylogenetic analyses have revealed that the human H10N8 virus was generated by sequential reassortments between duck-origin H10 and N8 viruses, and then with enzootic chicken H9N2 viruses. Introductions of H10 viruses from migratory birds to domestic ducks repeatedly occurred in last decade at Poyang Lake, Jiangxi, and these viruses were amplified and maintained in this species. Emergence of the novel reassortant H10N8 in chickens and then in humans was a direct consequence of the increased activity of H10 viruses in the region. The novel reassortant H10N8 viruses, first detected in chickens in mid-2013, now show a tendency to become established in this new host. Genetic analyses indicate that molecular changes are continuing to occur while the H10 viruses remain prevalent. With humans being constantly exposed to poultry H10 viruses, questions and mechanisms relating to the pandemic potential of these viruses that remain to be explored include: 1) whether H10 viruses from aquatic birds are generally infective in chickens and mammals, 2) whether incorporating internal gene complex of enzootic H9N2 viruses increases their infectivity to mammals, and 3) whether the mammalian infectivity and transmissibility of H10 virus will change while it prevails and evolves in chickens. Our long-term influenza surveillance in southern China, especially in Jiangxi (the source of the H10N8 virus), has provided the most comprehensive repository of viral strains, enabling us to trace each step associated with reassortments, generation of genetic variants and adaptation in different host species. Here, we propose to 1) investigate the general infectivity of duck H10 viruses in chicken and mammalian models; 2) compare the mammalian infectivity of different chicken reassortant variants and confirm the impact of incorporating different internal genes from the enzootic H9N2 virus lineage, by using prototype isolates and reverse-genetically generated reassortants; and 3) evaluate the infectivity changes occurring as the H10 virus continuous to evolve in chickens. Findings generated in this proposal will enhance our understanding of the emergence pathways of zoonotic influenza viruses, provide insights into their adaptation in domestic birds that may be associated with human infectivity, and allow better pandemic preparedness plans. 盡管H10亞型禽流感病毒在其自然宿主水禽中的陽性分離率並不高，但它們的生態分布與引起1957年大流感爆發的H2亞型病毒很相似，並且還能夠偶爾感染不同種類的哺乳動物，包括人類。2013年，在中國江西省出現了三例人感染H10N8流感病毒的新病例，引起了公眾對這個亞型的註意。 我們從系統進化分析中發現，這種人H10N8病毒是由鴨源H10及N8亞型病毒和已經在地化的雞H9N2病毒經過多次重組而產生的。在過去十年間，H10亞型病毒不時從江西鄱陽湖候鳥中被引入到家鴨中，並在家鴨中繁殖擴增和維持，繼而進入家雞群體並發生重組。H10病毒在該地區的活動增強，直接導致了H10N8重組新變種病毒在家雞中的爆發，以及随后的人類感染個案。這種新型的H10N8變種，最早於2013年年中開始出現在雞中，目前有在該宿主中發生在地化的可能。遺傳分析結果表明，隨著H10病毒的流行，其基因組中不斷出現各種突變。 鑒於人類經常暴露在家禽H10病毒中的現狀，不排除這類病毒可能會有機會直接或間接地引發未來的流感大流行。值得註意的幾個問題是：1）水禽H10病毒對雞和哺乳動物是否存在普遍的感染性；2）獲得H9N2內部基因是否會提高H10亞型病毒對哺乳動物的感染性；3）隨著H10病毒在雞中的流行和進化，該病毒對哺乳動物的感染和傳播能力是否會有相應的變化。 我們在華南地區尤其是在H10N8起源地江西長期開展的流感調查，為本研究提供了極為豐富的病毒庫存資源，也令我們得以深入了解病毒在不同宿主間適應、重組、產生新型遺傳變種的詳細過程。在本研究中，我們計劃：1）了解鴨H10亞型病毒在雞和哺乳動物模型中的普遍感染性；2）比較各種家雞重組病毒在哺乳動物模型中的感染情況，並通過反向遺傳學構建不同重組型病毒，將它們和原型病毒相比較，確認H9N2內部基因的作用；3）評估H10亞型流感病毒在不斷進化過程中出現的感染能力改變。 本項目的開展和執行，有利於加深我們對人畜共患性流感病毒發生途徑的理解，並能幫助我們掌握病毒在家禽中的適應情況。病毒在家禽中的長期適應，有可能導致病毒感染人的能力發生改變。對這個問題進行深入研究，有助於為大流感產生提供有效的防範措施。

17118515.label: Realisation of objectives
17118515.value: < Objective 1 > To understand the general infectivity and transmissibility of H10 subtype of influenza viruses in chickens, viruses with different genotypes and isolated from different hosts were intranasally inoculated into specific pathogen-free (SPF) chickens. We found that duck H10 viruses replicated very poorly in chickens, with peak shedding titers lower than 10^4 TCID50 and none of the physical contact or airborne exposed chickens was infected, indicating a relatively low risk for direct interspecies transmission of the wildtype H10 viruses from aquatic birds to chickens. Adaptation or reassortment may be needed for an aquatic avian H10 viruses from the Eurasian gene pool to become established in chickens. Comparatively, chicken H10 isolates with five or six internal genes derived from the enzootic Asian H9N2 viruses replicated efficiently in chickens, reaching peak shedding titers of around 10^6 TCID50 in the oropharyngeal swabs. These chicken H10 viruses could transmit to contact birds, with some strains even showing airborne transmissibility. The human isolate also shown limited physical contact transmission in chickens. Acquisition of the H9N2-like internal genes and/or other adaptations in chickens seemed to confer H10 virus better replication and transmission in this host. < Objective 2> To systematically evaluate the risk posed by the different genotypes of H10 subtype of influenza viruses in mammals and to investigate difference in their infectivity and pathogenicity in the mammalian hosts, we have selected a human H10N8 isolate, a few H10N8 (n=8), H10N6 (n=4) and H10N3 (n=1) subtypes of avian isolates and the genetically closely related human H7N9 (n=1) and avian H9N2 (n=2) viruses for the infection experiment, based on phylogenetic and evolutionary analyses. These 17 viruses were intranasally inoculated into the C57BL/6 mice, together with the mock infected controls inoculated with phosphate buffer solution (PBS). It was found that all tested H10 viruses were readily infectious and six out of the 14 H10 viruses were lethal in mice at an inoculation dose of 10^5 TCID50. Amongst them, the human H10N8 isolate shown the highest pathogenicity and fatality. One chicken H10N8 isolate also shown 100% fatality and efficient virus replication. These two viruses were even more virulent than the prototype human H7N9 virus, while the others were less pathogenic. Contemporary chicken H9N2 viruses were not infectious; and the duck H10N3 virus caused the least infection in mice, when compared with the duck or chicken H10N8 and H10N6 viruses. Infection of these 17 viruses in the ex vivo swine lung tissue showed that different genotypes of the H10 subtype of avian influenza virus could all replicate in the ex vivo swine lungs, indicating that the H10 subtype was generally infectious to the mammalian species without prior adaptation. Moreover, we selected six H10 viruses (one human H10N8, one duck H10N8, one duck H10N3, two chicken H10N8 and one chicken H10N6) for infection and transmission tests in a ferret model. All six viruses could efficiently replicate and transmit among ferrets. The three avian H10N8 viruses even shown airborne transmissibility from ferrets to ferrets. Therefore, risk posed by the H10 subtype to humans and other mammals can go beyond the human H10N8 virus. Various genotypes or NA combinations of H10 viruses can also be a potential threat to the public. However, variations exist between strains in the viral infectivity and pathogenicity in mice, in the transmissibility in ferrets, and also in the replication ability in the swine lung tissues. < Objective 3 > As described above, infection with the different genotypes of H10 isolates indicated that acquisition of the H9N2-like internal genes not only enhanced the virus infection and pathogenicity in mice, but also increased the virus replication in swine lung tissues. Obtaining five to six internal gene segments from the H9N2 virus lineage also significantly improved the H10 virus replication and transmission in chickens. The internal genes deriving from the H9N2 viruses seemed to play an important role in expanding the H10 virus replication in many animal species. It was noticed that infection of H10 in ferrets was usually not lethal, but the virus could replicate efficiently in the upper respiratory tract and shed to peak titers of around 10^6 TCID50/ml. Some strains shown significant transmissibility among ferrets. However, these were not necessarily associated with the presence of the internal genes from the H9N2 lineage. Those with higher pathogenicity and virus replication in mice were not necessarily more transmissible in ferrets either. Obtaining the H9N2 virus genes did not appear to be a prerequisite for the efficient transmission from ferrets to ferrets. Other mechanisms need to be further explored to understand the virus transmissibility in mammals. Apart from comparing the phenotypes of wildtype H10 virus strains which possessed various genotypes, we have also reconstructed viruses with different genotypic compositions or mutations. Infections in mice suggested that PB1 and PB2 genes may be key contributors for the mammalian infectivity and pathogenicity of this subtype. PB2-627 served as one of the key amino acids for the viral virulence in mice, but not for the virus transmissions either in ferrets or chickens. < objective 4 > Our surveillance in China has found that after the emergence of H10N8 in chickens in August 2013, it has caused a few cases of human infections in November 2013 to February 2014. The H10N8 virus was then replaced by the genesis of a new H10N6 reassortant virus in the spring of 2013. However, both H10N8 and H10N6 disappeared after the closure of live poultry markets in the southern and eastern China in 2014, and no more H10 subtype of viruses could be detected since then. Establishment and long-term adaptation of the H10 lineage did not occur in China due to the prompt intervention and disease control measures. However, as there were seven reassortant genotypes of H10N8 and four genotypes of H10N6 viruses co-circulating in chickens during 2013-2014, before they were completely eliminated from the local farms and live poultry markets, representative viruses from each genotype were tested for their infectivity and pathogenicity in different animal models. In comparison to the duck-borne H10N8 and H10N3 which had no genes deriving from the enzootic H9N2 lineage, all the chicken H10N8 and H10N6 viruses had 4 to 6 internal gene segments from the A/Chicken/Zhejiang/HJ/2007-like H9N2 clade. These reassortant chicken viruses shown significant growth advantage both in chickens and swine ex vivo lung tissues over the duck viruses. Furthermore, viruses possessing the N8 NA genes replicated to a much higher titer in mice and pig lung tissues than those with N6 or N3 genes. The H10N8 viruses also shown better transmissibility in ferrets and more pathogenicity in mice than the H10N3 and H10N6 viruses. Acquisition of N6 or N8 genes appeared to be a risk factor for enhancing the H10 virulence in mammals, though N6 tended to have less effects than N8 gene did. This might partially contribute to the emergence of H10N8 in humans but not the H10N3 or H10N6 viruses.

17118515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17118515.value: We have identified the viral gene segments and some residues that may contribute to the emergence of H10N8 infections in humans and the enhanced mammalian infectivity, pathogenicity and transmissibility of the avian H10 viruses. 17118515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118515.value: Interspecies transmission of avian influenza viruses (AIVs) poses a continuous threat to agriculture and public health. To systematically evaluate the risk of H10 subtype of AIVs and to investigate how it emerged to infect humans in 2013, we selected 14 contemporary strains representative of different genotypes and host origins. We found that all were readily infectious in chickens, mice, ferrets and ex vivo swine lungs, with some fatal in mice and airborne transmissible in ferrets. The human H10N8 isolate was the most virulent in C57BL/6 mice, while the duck H10N3 was the least. N8 NA gene appeared to confer a growth advantage over the N6 and N3 genes in mice, ferrets and pig lungs. Acquisition of the H9N2 internal genes significantly enhanced the H10 virus replication and transmission in chickens. It also improved the virus replication and pathogenicity in ex vivo swine lungs and mice. Of note, PB1 and PB2 genes played an important role for the mammalian infectivity and pathogenicity. PB2-627 served as one of the key amino acids for the viral virulence in mice, but not for the virus transmissions either in ferrets or chickens.

17118815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118815.value: 腦腫瘤是兒童最常見腫瘤之一。在香港每年約20-30個孩子被診斷有腦腫瘤。生殖細胞腦腫瘤在西方是罕見的，但於亞洲比較常見;佔達15％的亞洲兒童腦腫瘤。 生殖細胞腦腫瘤的生存率是高的;然而，因為生殖細胞腦腫瘤需要高劑量的電療，有人擔心會影響兒童神經認知和功能結果。 在大腦中，有白質和灰質。最近的證據證明在使用擴散張量磁共振成像（DTI），白質定量損失以及相關的兒童髓母細胞瘤的神經認知成果倖存者。白質損傷通常反映神經系統/功能障礙。傷害灰質會導致認知功能障礙，但沒有研究於相關灰質損失與腦腫瘤存活者的認知結果。 DTI很少用於評估灰質的變化。然而，新的方法叫做擴散峭度成像（MR-DKI）可以顯示出在白質和灰質的變化, 有用於成人神經系統疾病，如中風，創傷性腦損傷或阿爾茨海默氏疾病。 我們的試點研究也提供了初步證據表明大多數生殖細胞腦腫瘤倖存者有認知障礙,MR-DKI指標均能反映有認知和功能障礙的嚴重性。 我們推測，MR-DKI指標可以反映白質和灰質損失,這些指標可以作為預測生殖細胞瘤倖存者的功能和神經損傷。這項假設將通過以下具體目標進行測試： （1）為了測定生殖細胞瘤倖存者在認知和功能障礙的程度。 （2）研究MR-DKI指標，成功完成該項目將提供白質和灰質損害為神經認知功能損害的原因。通過MR-DKI, 白質和灰質損失可能是作為預測神經認知和功能性成果。這可以指導臨床醫生更加謹慎給予電療，及考慮神經保護藥物和及早提供復康服務。

17118815.label: Realisation of objectives
17118815.value: Total of 25 intra-cranial germ cell tumour (GCT) survivors were recruited. Comprehensive evaluation of physical disability, cognitive function, performance status and quality of life in GCT survivors were performed. 5 of them did not complete the MR-DKI examinations due to claustrophobia or technical problems. 14 age and gender-matched healthy control subjects were recruited. We have achieved all of the objectives stated in the project proposal. Realisation of objectives: 1. To determine the degree of cognitive and functional impairment in intracranial germinoma survivors. The average IQ scores of patients was 92 and six patients (24%) had borderline intelligence or worse (IQ < 80). For physical impairment, only one patient was free from any physical disability or long-term complications. For functional impairment measured by the Karnofsky/ Lannsky performance scales (KPS), four patients (16%) had KPS scores < 70. GCT survivors were found to have significantly lower scores in the physical related quality of life compared with healthy age and gender-matched control subjects. 2. To investigate the association between MR-DKI metrics, neurocognitive and functional outcomes in childhood intracranial germinoma survivors. In GCT survivors, white matter microstructural changes with higher mean diffusivity (MD) values in the anterior limb of the internal capsule, superior fronto-occipital fasciculus, anterior corona radiata, uncinated fasciculus, cerebral peduncle, superior corona radiata, cingulate cinulum and the fornix were associated with lower IQ scores. Lower FA values in the cerebral peduncle, anterior and posterior limb of internal capsule, external capsule, cinguluate cinulum, superior fronto-occipital fasciculus, uncinated fasciculus and superior corona radiate were associated with lower IQ values. For gray matter changes, higher MD values in the olfactory, insula, caudate, thalamus, Heschl gyrus, parahippocampal gyrus, hippocampus, anterior cinulum, frontal inferior trangularis, middle and superior temporal gyrus, rolandic operculum, middle occipital gyrus, angular, precentral and postcentral gyrus were associated with lower IQ scores. The gray matter MK values showed positive association with the IQ scores in the superior frontal gyrus, frontal gyrus, postcentral gyrus, supra-marginal gyrus, cuneus, heschl gyrus, frontal inferior triangularis, caudate and the thalamus. 3. To compare the degree of white and gray matter loss, neurocognitive and functional outcomes in intracranial germinoma affecting different regions of the brain e.g. pineal vs. suprasellar vs. basal ganglia. For the degree of white matter loss, compared to healthy age-matched controls (n= 14), GCT survivors (n= 20) had significantly higher mean diffusivity (MD) values in the cingulum, fornix, uncinated fasciculus, superior fronto-occipital fasciculus, anterior limb of internal capsule, superior corona radiate and the cerebral peduncle regions. GCT survivors had significantly lower mean kurtosis (MK) values in the cingulum, fornix, superior longitudinal fasciculus, anterior and superior corona radiate and the anterior limb of the internal capsule. Furthermore, they had significantly lower FA values in the cingulum, fornix, anterior and posterior corona radiate, posterior thalamic radiation as well as the anterior limb of the internal capsule. For the degree of grey matter loss, compared to healthy age-matched controls (n= 14), GCT survivors (n= 20) had significantly higher MD values in the anterior, mid posterior cingulum, amygdala, frontal inferior triangularis, heschl gyrus, supramarginal gyrus, calcarine sulcus, superior, mid & inferior temporal gyrus, precentral and postcentral gyrus, insula, fusiform, rolandic operculum, lingual gyrus and the cuneus.

17118815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17118815.value: 25 intracranial GCT survivors were recruited into our study. Longer length of time since treatment was associated with lower IQ scores. Larger tumour size was associated with lower KPS scores indicating poorer function. Hemiparesis, poor manual dexterity and complications with milti-organ involvement were associated with significantly lower KPS scores. Higher irradiation dosage was associated with lower PedsQL physical scores. In terms of cognitive and physical functions, the majority of GCT survivors had average intellectual functioning, satisfactory performance status and relatively good quality of life, except in the physical aspects. Using MR diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), our study is the first study to provide evidence of significantly reduced white matter integrity as well as extensive decrease in gray matter integrity in GCT survivors. The microstructural brain changes might lead to wide range of functional deficits in cognition, motor as well as problems with sensory processing. Our study also shows significant associations between the diffusion kurtosis metrics (mean diffusivity MD, mean kurtosis MK and fractional anisotropy FA) with the cognitive function (measured by IQ scores) as well as physical function (measured by KPS scores) of GCT survivors. Similar to previous studies, multiple brain regions with white matter microstructural changes were found to associate with poorer cognitive function. However, our study is the first to identify significant gray matter microstructural changes with associated poor cognitive function in specific brain regions which include: the caudate, thalamus, heschl gyrus, frontal inferior triangularis and the postcentral gyrus. Most of the brain regions with associated functional impairment as indicated by poorer KPS scores are white matter regions such as the internal capsule or the corona radiata. Only limited regions of the brain showed significant gray matter microstructural changes with associated functional impairment. Our study showed that in GCT survivors, cognitive deficits are likely due to microstructural changes in both white and gray matter. In contrary, the functional deficits are mostly due to the white matter microstructural changes.

17118815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17118815.value: Although the majority of GCT survivors have average intellectual functioning, satisfactory performance status, and relatively good quality of life, they are prone to poorer physical health and well-being. We recommend longitudinal follow-up of GCT survivors comprising holistic and comprehensive assessments of physical health, neurocognitive function, performance status, and quality of life to ensure timely support and improve long-term outcomes. Diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI) can provide prognostic indications on which patients are at high risk of cognitive or functional impairment. This can help rehabilitation specialists to provide timely intervention and training for GCT survivors at high risk of intellectual or physical disabilities. We have applied the knowledge gained from this study to the development of the brain tumour survivorship follow-up program at the Hong Kong Children's Hospital where paediatric brain tumour survivors will have regular follow-up by a developmental paediatrician on their neurocognitive, physical functions, performance status as well as quality of life. We are currently performing MR-DKI on survivors with other types of brain tumours e.g. medulloblastoma. We plan to follow-up brain tumor survivors longitudinally so that we can follow the developmental trajectory, longer term neurocognitive outcomes as well as microstructural white and gray matter changes in brain tumor survivors.

17118815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118815.value: We have completed a comprehensive evaluation of the impact of tumor characteristics, treatment modalities and medical complications related to the tumor and its treatment on the neurocognitive function, performance status, and quality of life of GCT survivors. Longer length of time since treatment was associated with lower IQ scores. Location and size of tumor and the presence of physical disability were found to affect performance status. Higher irradiation dosage was associated with poorer physical health related quality of life. The majority of GCT survivors had average intellectual functioning, satisfactory performance status, and relatively good quality of life, except in the physical domain. Using advance neuroimaging with MR diffusion kurtosis, we have identified brain regions with significant white and gray matter microstructural changes that are associated with impaired cognitive function or functional deficits. These can be used as prognostic indicators to identify patients at high risk of cognitive or functional impairment so timely intervention and training can be provided for high risk patients.

17120415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120415.value: 雙酚A(BPA)是一種內分泌干擾物，大量證據顯示雙酚A可引起多種副作用，包括生殖力下降，出生體重減少，男性生殖器發育異常，糖尿病，肥胖和腫瘤。BPA通常被用來製造聚碳酸脂塑料，食物容器和牙齒密封劑。每年BPA的生產量約為360萬吨。社會公眾很擔心BPA的有害作用，這促使製造商在一些產品中更換BPA。2011年，歐盟禁止在奶瓶中使用BPA，一年後美國也頒布這一禁令。在一些工業應用中，雙酚A已經被雙酚類似物取代，這些類似物在結構上與BPA相似，例如BPS，BPF和BPB都包含兩個酚環，由橋接碳或其它化學結構連接。 雙酚S(BPS)首次出現於1869年，但在2006年起才被引進到消費品中。目前，BPA的年產量達到了一萬噸，並且BPS的生產比率正在逐年遞增。越來越多的研究顯示BPS，BPB和BPF含有的雌激素活性與BPA的雌激素活性相似。事實上，一些雙酚化學物的生物降解能力明顯弱於BPA，這可能會讓它們對人類的影響更具危險性。激素水平的改變影響生殖過程，尤其在子宮內膜發育和胚胎種植過程中。然而，我們並不完全了解這些雙酚類似物是如何影響生殖的。 我們假設雙酚類似物(BPB, BPF, BPS)可影響人類生殖，通過改變雌激素受體和Wnt信號通路抑制胚胎種植和出生後發育。本研究計劃中，目標(1)研究雙酚物(BPA,BPB,BPS和BPF)對胚胎發育和種植的影響，(2)揭示雙酚物對種植影響的潛在分子機制，(3)檢測20種香港常見的淡水魚和鹹水魚中雙酚物的水平，並檢測香港人群血清中雙酚物的含量，(4)探討IVF病人血清中雙酚物濃度與其臨床結局的關係。本研究將闡明雙酚物是如何影響球體(胚胎替代物)與子宮內膜相互作用，胚胎種植和IVF病人生殖能力，及其基本分子機制。公眾和IVF病人血清中雙酚物的濃度將為雙酚物的長期累積，及可能存在的健康及生殖力相關問題提供重要的證據，也可為食物中雙酚物的安全水平提供建議。

17120415.label: Realisation of objectives
17120415.value: 1. To investigate the effect of bisphenols on embryo development and implantation We first investigated the effect of bisphenols (BPA, BPF and BPS) at 1, 10 and 100M on the development of mouse embryo from zygote to blastocyst in vitro. We found BPA and BPF at 10uM significantly induced blastocyst size, but not blastulation rate when compared to Kaa medium group (control). When BPA and BPF at 1uM were used together, similar suppressive effect on blastulation was seen (He X, MMedSc thesis, 2019). Using in vitro attachment assay, BPA and BPA+F treated embryos had reduced attachment rate to endometrial epithelial Ishikawa cells (Jiang, PhD thesis 2020). We further investigate the implantation rate of bisphenol treated blastocyst transferred on day 4 in pseudo-pregnant mice on day 8 of pregnancy. It was found that the number of implantation site was significantly lower in the BPA, BPF and BPA+BPF group at 10uM, but not 1uM than the control group (He X, MMedSc thesis, 2019). We then investigated the effect of bisphenols on the attachment of trophoblastic spheroid (blastocyst surrogate) on endometrial cells in a co-culture model. The effect of acute (24 h) and chronic (1 month) BPA treatment were investigated. Acute high-dose bisphenols (1, 10 and 100uM) were used to treat human endometrial epithelial Ishikawa and trophoblastic Jeg-3 cells for 24 hours. We found BPA and BPF at 10 and 100uM, and BPS at 100uM significantly suppressed (p<0.05) the attachment rate of trophoblastic spheroid onto endometrial cells. Chronic low-dose Bisphenols (1, 10 and 100nM) were used to treat Ishikawa cells for 1 month. BPA at 100nM significantly suppressed (p<0.05) spheroid attachment when compared to BPS, BPF and DMSO control. The MTX was used as positive control in the assay (Fan, PhD thesis 2017). Then, we studied if bisphenols affected stromal cell decidualization and trophoblastic cells invasion and outgrowth. By using both direct and indirect co-culture assay using culture insert, we found BPA, BPF and BPF did not affect stromal cell decidualization, but BPA and BPF treated decidualized stromal cells affected trophoblastic cell invasion, partly by up-regulating invasion-related molecules including LIF; and down-regulating anti-invasion molecules including PAI-1 and TNFa (Fan et al., 2020). We further investigated the effect in utero bisphenol exposure on post-natal development of mice. Low dose bisphenol treatment (BPA, BPS, BPF and BPA/F, 500ug/Kg/day) were used to feed adult female for 30 days before mating and during the whole gestational period to study their effects on reproductive function and fertility of offspring at F1, F2 and F3 generations. We found bisphenols treatment did not affect the length of estrus cycle of the adult mice, as well as the number of implantation site on day 7 of pregnancy. However, the female F1 generation from the BPA, but not BPS, BPF or BPA/F group has delayed time to puberty and prolonged estrus cycle length. Interestingly, BPA treatment induced follicle activation of the female offspring, and a larger number of pups was found in BPA group. However, the weaning body weight of F1 and F2 generation in BPA or BPF group was decreased, indication bisphenol might affect their pre-weaning development. But this phenomenon was did not found in F3 generation. (Jiang, PhD thesis 2020). 2. To study the molecular mechanism of bisphenols on implantation We studied the effect of bisphenols on the expression of estrogen receptors, membrane receptors and Wnt-signaling molecules in human endometrial cells. Acute high-dose bisphenols (BPA, BPF and BPS, at 1, 10 and 100uM) were used to study the expression of ERa, ERb and GPR30 expression in human endometrial Ishikawa cells. BPA, but not BPF and BPS at 100uM could significantly suppress ERa and ERb expression; while all bisphenols could suppress the expression of GPR30. We further tested the effect of chronic low-dose bisphenols (BPA, BPF and BPS, at 1, 10 and 100nM) on the expression of ERs, GPR30, ERRg and Wnt-signaling molecules in human endometrial Ishikawa cells. It was found BPA and BPF at 100nM induced the expression of ERa, but BPA suppressed the expression of ERb in Ishikawa cells. All bisphenol molecules did not induce any change of Wnt-signaling molecules including the expression of active b-catenin or GSK-3b. However, BPA but not BPF and BPS suppressed the expression of Wnt-signaling inhibitor Axin2, but induced the expression of phospho-ERK (Fan, PhD thesis, 2017). We further investigate the effect of bisphenols on the changes in transcriptomic profile in human endometrial Ishikawa cells. Human transcriptome array 2.0 was used to compare the transcriptomic changes in Ishikawa cells by bisphenols (BPA, BPF and BPS, 10uM) treatment. GeneSpring analysis identified 24 up-regulated, and 3 down-regulated genes commonly expressed in the three treatment groups when compared to the DMSO control. Clustering analysis demonstrated that the bisphenol treatments shared similar transcriptomic changes and clustered together. Six commonly up-regulated genes (TGFA, THBS1, ANO1, PGR, NPPC and OLFM1) were confirmed by quantitative-PCR, in which PGR protein was found to be significantly up-regulated by Western blot analysis of the treated Ishikawa cells. The result was confirmed when PR siRNA was used to down-regulated bisphenol-treated Ishikawa cells for co-culture studies. We also tested the effect of chronic low-dose BPA (100nM) on the transcriptome profile of the Ishikawa cell, and identified a number of up- and down-regulated gene upon long-term BPA treatment. The identity of these genes (e.g. CTGF, FosB, EGR1, Jun, SEMA3A, SPON1, FGFBP1) could be used to study the underlying molecular mechanism of chronic low-dose BPA effect on endometrial cells (Fan, PhD thesis, 2017). 3. To determine the concentration of bisphenols in fishes in Hong Kong We have tested the levels of bisphenol compounds (BPA, BPB, BPF and BPS) in 20 commercial (10 marine water and 10 freshwater species) available Hong Kong species of fishes by mass spectrometry. BPA was detected in all fish samples. BPF was detected in some marine and freshwater fishes; while BPS and BPB could only be identified in 2 marine species. On the basis of the measured concentrations of bisphenols, BPs (BPA, BPB, BPF, BPS), the average daily intake will be 20.5-31.5ng/kg bw/day which was found to be lower than values of tolerable daily intake established in Europe (Wong et al., 2017). When compared to the BPA data published in 2011, the current study showed an approximate 10-fold increase in the concentration of BPA in samples from freshwater and marine fishes (Wong et al., 2017). 4. To determine the concentration of bisphenols in human follicular fluid in patients receiving IVF treatment We collected 210 patient serum and follicular fluid samples from patients who visited out IVF clinics. Patient’s demographical data were collected from the IVF clinic, follicular fluid samples and pregnancy outcome in the first and subsequent cycles were completed. We have tested the levels of bisphenol compounds (BPA, BPB, BPF and BPS) by mass spectrometry in both the follicular and serum samples (>100). Similar to the fish sample bisphenol levels, BPA and BPF, but not BPB and BPS were detected (detection limit is 5 ppb) in some of the patient samples. Importantly, serum BPA level is negatively correlated to pregnancy outcome in IVF patient (p=0.02, Fan, PhD thesis, 2017).

17120415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17120415.value: Bisphenol A and its analogs (BPA, BPF and BPS) on human reproductive functions were investigated by using in vitro and in vivo models. We found 10uM BPA and BPF affect mouse embryo development and implantation. Mice feed with BPA (500ug/Kg/day) at the peri-gestational stage affects the number of offspring born at F1, but not in F2 and F3 generations. This is associated with aberrant activation of ovarian follicles during postnatal development. BPA treatment affects the receptivity of human endometrial epithelial cells to spheroid (blastocyst surrogate) attachment, but not decidualization of endometrial stromal cells. However, BPA and BPF treated decidualized stromal cells affected trophoblastic cell invasion, partly due to changes in the expression of invasion- and anti-invasion molecules. Acute (24h) high dose BPA, but not BPF and BPS at 100uM could significantly suppress ERa, ERb, active b-catenin and E-Cadherin expression; while all bisphenols could suppress the expression of GPR30 in endometrial epithelial cells. Chronic (1 mo) low-dose bisphenols BPA and BPF (100nM) induced the expression of ERa, but BPA suppressed the expression of ERb, Wnt-signaling inhibitor Axin2, but induced the expression of phospho-ERK. Using human transcriptome array 2.0, we identified 24 up-regulated and 3 down-regulated genes in Ishikawa cells treated with 10uM BPA, BPF or BPS when compared with DMSO control; while chronic low-dose BPA (100nM) treatment identified several up- and down-regulated gene including CTGF, FosB, EGR1, Jun, SEMA3A, SPON1, FGFBP1 which could be used to study the underlying molecular mechanism on how chronic low-dose BPA affects endometrial receptivity. We tested the levels of bisphenol compounds (BPA, BPB, BPF and BPS) in 20 (10 marine water and 10 freshwater species) species of fishes in Hong Kong. BPA was detected in all fish samples. BPF was detected in some marine and freshwater fishes; while BPS and BPB could only be identified in 2 marine species. When compared to the BPA data published in 2011, the current study showed an approximate 10-fold increase in the concentration of BPA in samples from freshwater and marine fishes. We also tested the levels of bisphenol compounds (BPA, BPB, BPF and BPS) from 210 IVF patient serum and follicular fluid samples from patients by mass spectrometry. We found similar result that BPA and BPF, but not BPB and BPS were detected (>5 ppb) in some of the patient samples. Importantly, serum BPA level is negatively correlated to pregnancy outcome in IVF patient (p=0.02).

17120415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17120415.value: This study provided important information on how bisphenol A (BPA) and its analogs (e.g. BPF, BPS) affecting human reproductive functions including the risk of BPA and BPF on embryo implantation, endometrial receptivity, the number of offspring produced, suppression of estrogen- but activation of ERK-signaling pathways. The identification of transcriptomic markers upon acute and chronic bisphenol exposure provided fundamental information for the detection of endometrial receptivity upon bisphenol exposure. Importantly, we are at the risk of increasing bisphenols exposure, and a 10-fold increase in fish BPA level in 10 yr time alerted us to have a more stringent screening and monitoring program for bisphenols detection in the future. This study highlighted the fact that BPA and BPF were detected in human serum and follicular fluid, and BPA level is associated with poor pregnancy outcome. Although the effect of other endocrine factors including steroid hormone and receptor expression levels on pregnancy outcome cannot be underestimated, the risk of how bisphenols interact these endocrine factors should be investigated in the future.

17120415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17120415.value: Bisphenol A (BPA) and its family member (e.g. BPF and BPS) are hormone-related chemical and their effect on human reproductive functions remain largely unknown. Here, we found BPA and BPF affect mouse embryo development and attachment to the uterus. Mice feed with BPA before and during pregnancy affected the number of mice produced and is associated with changes in the number of egg produced in the ovary. BPA treatment also affect human uteri epithelial and stromal cell functions and subsequent spheroid (embryo surrogate) attachment. Acute and chronic bisphenol exposure affect various cellular signaling pathways including hormone receptor and invasion molecules expression. In Hong Kong, BPA was detected in 20 (10 marine water and 10 freshwater species) fishes and BPF was detected in some marine and freshwater fishes. When compared to the BPA data published in 2011, there was an approximate 10-fold increase in the concentration of BPA in these samples. The levels of bisphenol compounds (BPA, BPB, BPF and BPS) collected from 210 IVF patient serum and follicular fluid samples shared similar findings that BPA and BPF, but not BPB and BPS were detected (>5 ppb). Importantly, serum BPA level is negatively correlated to pregnancy outcome in IVF patient (p=0.02).

17120715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120715.value: 主動脈瓣狹窄(AS)是一種常見的瓣膜疾病，對成年人的影響高達4%。這種疾病的特點是長期處於無症狀階段，一旦症狀發展將帶來不良預後。根據現有的推薦，一旦病人出現症狀或者左心室功能障礙或者左心室擴張，主動脈瓣置換(AVR)將是唯一的治療方法。對於還不需要主動脈瓣置換手術治療的無症狀患者，目前還沒有已經證實的醫學治療可以有效的預防不良左心室重構，延緩症狀的出現或改善其臨床預後。 腎素-血管緊張素系統（RAS）在需要手術治療的有症狀的嚴重主動脈瓣狹窄病人中已被激活，並且已證明它與左心室肥厚及心肌纖維化有關。此外，動脈硬化，一個常見的並存問題，獨立作用于增加心臟後負荷，將進一步增加左心室肥厚和左心室功能障礙的風險。動脈硬化已經證實與腎素-血管緊張素系統活動密切相關。對需要做主動脈瓣置換手術之前的無症狀主動脈瓣狹窄患者，腎素-血管緊張素系統激活與心肌結構改變，心肌力學以及動脈硬化的關係仍然未知。因此我們建議調查研究無症狀主動脈瓣狹窄患者腎素-血管緊張素系統活動與心肌結構改變，心肌收縮力及動脈硬化的關係以及它們之間的相互作用。 在動物模型中，血管緊張素轉換酶抑製劑(ACEI)作用於腎素-血管緊張素系統（RAS）可延遲左心室肥厚的發展并改善心肌收縮性。最近的一項回顧性觀察研究顯示，ACEI或血管緊張素受體阻滯劑(ARB)與提高主動脈瓣狹窄患者生存率并降低心血管疾病的風險相關。由於這是一次回顧性研究，對於觀察可能存在偏見的潛在混雜因素不能夠排除。到目前為止，沒有隨機對照試驗已經證實ACEI/ARB治療是否能夠預防主動脈瓣狹窄患者左心室重構。我們提議ARB對於RAS的阻礙作用將減慢無症狀主動脈瓣狹窄患者左室不良重構，從而延遲他們主動脈瓣置換的需要

17120715.label: Realisation of objectives
17120715.value: For objective one, we have included 205 patients with aortic stenosis who are asymptomatic (age 63, male 55%). Detailed echocardiography including conventional parameters, E/E` ratio and global longitudinal strain (GLS) were performed. Further, plasma matrix metalloproteinase-1, TIMP-1, amino-terminal propeptide of type I and type III procollagen and renin angiotensin system activity were measured. We have found that patients with asymptomatic moderate to severe AS had a higher plasma level of TIMP-1 and propeptide of type III procollagen than patients with mild AS. After multivariate adjustment, TIMP-1 associated with E/E' and GLS. Based on this result, we can conclude that TIMP-1 is independently associated with myocardial diastolic dysfunction and GLS in patients with asymptomatic AS. The results of this objective has prepared for abstract presentation in international conferences. For objective 2, we have randomized a total of 42 patients to received losartan and placebo (1:1 ratio). Following one year of randomization, there was no significant difference in terms of echocardigoraphy parameters (LV mass, diastolic function of GLS). Nonetheless, no significant/serious adverse events was detected in both group of patients.

17120915.label: Project Objectives
17120915.value: The first objective is to identify the actions of PACA on the phenotypes and functions of macrophages. Our pilot results suggest that PACA is the least toxic and most active compound for regulating the phenotypes and functions of macrophages. We will examine the effect of PACA on the expression of several additional biomarkers (i.g., IL-1β, TNF-α, CD68, CD206) and the functions of macrophages such as phagocytosis and chemotactic potential. We will verify the effect of PACA on phenotypes and functions of primary mouse peritoneal macrophages. The second objective is to discover the mechanisms by which PACA regulates the phenotypic and functional switch of macrophages. iNOS is a useful biomarker for monitoring the phenotypes and functions of macrophages. We recently found that PACA activated Nrf2 pathway and induced antioxidant HO-1 via direct modification of Keap1. We also found that HO-1 inhibitor could attenuate the inhibitory effect of PACA on iNOS induction. Thus, this study will focus on the effect of PACA on iNOS as an indicator. We will employ siRNA, ChIP, promoter cloning and promoter-reporter system to address how different transcription factos and signaling pathways (i.g., PKC, PKA, COCS-1 and -3) regulate the expression of iNOS in response to PACA. The third objective is to explore the in vivo efficacy of PACA in modulating pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory macrophages in rodent MI models. We found that PACA attenuated isoproterenol-induced myocardial injury by reducing NO production and increasing GSH levels. On the other hand, PACA effectively stimulated macrophages to secret chemotactic mediators for bone marrow-derived hematopoietic stem cells. Thus, we will verify whether PACA exhibits cardioprotective activity in rodent MI models by targeting macrophages. We will focus on the in vivo effects of PACA on phenotypes and functions of macrophages with a special regard to resolution of inflammation and cardiac repair.
