17120915.label: Realisation of objectives
17120915.value: Macrophages are known to exhibit different phenotypes and diverse functions in tissue remodeling, repair and fibrosis after myocardial infarction (MI) [1]. M1 macrophages are pro-inflammatory and promote cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis [2]. M2 macrophages are anti-inflammatory and help the resolution of inflammation and tissue repair [2]. Both M1 and M2 macrophages play active roles in removing damaged tissues [3]. Importantly, M2 macrophages not only exhibit anti-inflammatory activities but also directly support the formation of new tissue [3]. M2 macrophages support the proliferation and differentiation of stem cells and progenitors within damaged myocardium [4, 5]. Cardiac macrophages inhibit the infiltration of inflammatory cells and attenuate cardiac dysfunction in hypertensive rats [6]. However, macrophages may exhibit different phenotypes and functions with time and the pathological contexts [7]. For example, M1 macrophages are predominant phenotype in MI patients with atherosclerosis. Thus, pharmacological activation of macrophage polarization towards a M2-like phenotype should be a novel therapeutic strategy for the treatment of myocardial infarction. The long-term goal of our research is to discover the protective and restorative activities of traditional herbal medicines and the underlying mechanisms for the treatment of ischemia reperfusion injury [8-13]. In our preliminary experiments, we synthesized and discovered n-propargyl caffeamide (PACA) as the promising candidate for regulating the phenotypes and functions of macrophages. We hypothesized that PACA might induce phenotypic and functional switch of macrophages towards the resolution of inflammation and cardiac regeneration via Nrf2/HO-1–dependent and –independent mechanisms. We have extensively tested this hypothesis through accomplishing three specific aims: 1) to identify the actions of PACA on the phenotypes and functions of macrophages; 2) to discover the mechanisms by which PACA regulates the phenotypic and functional switch of macrophages; 3) to explore the in vivo efficacy of PACA in modulating pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory macrophages in murine MI models. For Specific Aim 1, we investigated the actions of PACA on the phenotypes and functions of macrophages. We treated macrophage RAW264.7 cells with LPS in combination with PACA (2, 10, 50 μM). For macrophage phenotypes, we determined the protein levels of iNOS and COX-2 by Western blot, CD80 and CD163 by flow cytometry and the mRNAs of arginase-1, CCL2, CXCL10, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-10, iNOS, TNF-α by qRT-PCR. For the effects of PACA on the functions of macrophages, we assayed the chemotactic potential of macrophages in Transwells and phagocytosis towards latex beads and apoptotic cardiomyocytes. These results suggested that PACA promoted macrophage M2 polarization, chemotaxis and phagocytosis. The results have been published in Cheng Y et al Cell Physiol Biochem. 2018;47(6):2544-2557. Overall, we have addressed the studies proposed under Specific Aim 1 by 100%. For Specific Aim 2, we investigated the mechanisms by which PACA regulated the phenotypic and functional switch of macrophages. We conducted a small scale of virtual screening by docking oxidized PACA into various signaling molecules. As result, we discovered that oxidized PACA could effectively bind to PPAR-γ at the previously unidentified site involving amino acid residues (i.e., ARG288, SER289, CYS285, LEU330, LEU333 and ALA292). By introducing PPRE-Luc reporter system into RAW264.7, we confirmed that PACA increased luciferase activity in a concentration dependent manner. By analyzing the expression of iNOS and arginase with Western blot, we found that PACA increased arginase-1 and reduced iNOS in a PPAR-γ-dependent manner. We also found that siRNA-mediated silencing of PPAR-γ could attenuate the effects of PACA on the expression of iNOS. These results have been described in the manuscript that was under major revision for publication in Aging-US. In addition, we also performed CHIP assay and promoter cloning although no new information was obtained. Overall, we have addressed the studies proposed under Specific Aim 2 by 100%. For Specific Aim 3, we have explored the in vivo efficacy of PACA in modulating pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory macrophages in two mouse MI models. By using isoproterenol-induced model of myocardial infarction, we examine the effects of PACA on the body weight, safety, cardiac fibrosis and the kinetics of macrophage M1/M2 polarization over a period of 35 days. We did not observe the signs of toxicity in animals after PACA treatment. However, we found that PACA effectively suppressed cardiac fibrosis, promoted macrophage M2 polarization. We verified the in vivo cardioprotective efficacy of PACA in a mouse model of acute myocardial infarction by ligating coronary artery. In addition, we examined the effects of PACA on the activity of macrophages to induce the chemotaxis of bone marrow-derived hematopoietic stem cells. These results have been described in the manuscript that was under major revision for publication in Aging-US. In addition, we also investigated the in vivo cardioprotective effects and pharmacokinetic profile of N-propyl caffeamide against ischemia reperfusion injury and published the results in Cheng Y et al Arch Immunol Ther Exp (Warsz). 2017 Apr;65(2):145-156. Overall, we have addressed the studies proposed under Specific Aim 3 by 100%. References 1) Mosser, D.M. and J.P. Edwards, Nat Rev Immunol, 2008. 8(12): 958-69. 2) Usher, M.G., S.Z. Duan, C.Y. 17120915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17120915.value: The first important finding was that PACA could effectively suppress pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization, promote pro-inflammatory M2 macrophage polarization and enhance the phagocytosis and chemoattractant activity of macrophages. Several key macrophage biomarkers were determined by Western blot and RT-PCR techniques in macrophage cell culture and primary mouse peritoneal macrophages in response to PACA treatment. The phagocytosis and chemoattractant activity of macrophages were evaluated by well-recognized methods. These results were published in Cheng Y et al Cell Physiol Biochem. 2018;47(6):2544-2557. The second important finding was that PACA regulated the phenotypic and functional switch of macrophages via coordinated activation of two key mechanisms, Nrf2/HO-1 pathway and PPAR-γ pathway, respectively. We initially found that PACA could activate Nrf2/HO-1 pathway via covalent modification of Keap1. These results were published in Cheng Y et al Cell Physiol Biochem. 2018;47(6):2544-2557. In the course of work in the present project, we found that PACA could also activate PPAR-γ pathway through direct and covalent interaction. These results suggest that PACA may regulate the cross-talks between Nrf2/HO-1 pathway and PPAR-γ pathway. The activation of Nrf2/HO-1 pathway is important for the resolution of inflammation whereas the activation of PPAR-γ pathway may help the suppression of cardiac fibrosis. These results will be published in Cheng Y et al Aging-US, under review. The third important finding was that PACA could effectively suppress pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization and promote anti-inflammatory M2 macrophage polarization towards the resolution of inflammation and cardiac repair in rodent models of myocardial infarction. These results will be published in Cheng Y et al Aging-US, under review. In addition, we also investigated the in vivo cardioprotective effects and pharmacokinetic profile of N-propyl caffeamide against ischemia reperfusion injury and published the results in Cheng Y et al Arch Immunol Ther Exp (Warsz). 2017 Apr;65(2):145-156. The results from the present study served as the important preliminary results for a successful HMRF grant #16171751. We will develop novel specific PPAR-γ agonists for inducing pro-resolving macrophages and suppressing cardiac fibrosis in experimental myocardial infarction. The grant supported the academic training of three PhD students and one post-doctoral fellow.

17120915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17120915.value: The existing drugs for treating myocardial infarction mainly treat blood coagulation, cardiac inflammation and pain. Timely recovery of cardiac functions is an ongoing challenge. We initially synthesized and patented PACA as a novel neuroprotective and neurotrophic compound for the treatment of neurodegenerative diseases. The present project was designed to investigate the in vivo efficacy of PACA against inflammation and cardiac fibrosis in experimental myocardial infarction. As result, we demonstrated that PACA not only promoted the phenotypic switch of macrophages from pro-inflammatory M1 to anti-inflammatory and resolving M2 but also enhanced the phagocytosis of macrophages towards the resolution and cardiac repair. The present study also demonstrated that PACA might help resolution of inflammation and suppress cardiac fibrosis through activating two important mechanisms, Nrf2/HO-1 pathway and PPAR-γ pathway, respectively. Thus, the present study provided molecular insights to support PACA as a drug candidate for the treatment of myocardial infarction. Nevertheless, the present study only evaluated the cardioprotective potential of PACA in two common models of experimental myocardial infarction. We will further investigate the therapeutic potential of PACA in future preclinical and clinical studies. Ultimately, we are confident that novel PACA analogs will be developed as therapies against myocardial infarction.

17120915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17120915.value: Myocardial infarction is a highly prevalent and life-threatening disease. Many survivors suffer from the incomplete recovery of cardiac functions. The long-term goal of the present study is to discover the protective and restorative activities of traditional herbal medicines and the underlying mechanisms for the treatment of ischemia reperfusion injury. We previously synthesized and patented caffeic acid derivative PACA as a neuroprotective and neurotrophic drug candidate. In the present project, we continued to study whether PACA could induce phenotypic and functional switch of macrophages towards the resolution of inflammation and cardiac regeneration via Nrf2/HO-1–dependent and –independent mechanisms. As results, we have achieved three specific aims and consequently discovered three important properties of PACA as follows: 1) PACA effectively promoted the phenotypic switch of macrophages from proinflammatory M1 to anti-inflammatory and resolving M2 while enhanced the phagocytosis of macrophages; 2) PACA might promote the phenotypic switch and phagocytosis of macrophages through activating two important mechanisms, Nrf2/HO-1 pathway and PPAR-γ pathway, respectively; 3) PACA effectively promoted macrophage polarization towards anti-inflammatory and resolving M2-like phenotype in animal models of myocardial infarction. Thus, the results from the present study provided molecular insights for the development of novel PACA analogs as therapies against myocardial infarction.

17121315.label: Realisation of objectives
17121315.value: We have performed series of in vivo and in vitro experiments and demonstrated that N-Acetylcysteine restores Sevoflurane Postconditioning Cardioprotection against Myocardial Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Diabetic Rats which is associated with enhancement of cardiac Brg1. Furthermore, we explored the role of STAT3 activation in Brg1-mediated restoration of the sensitivity of the diabetic heart to volatile anesthetic isoflurane (which has similar structure as sevoflurane) conditioning cardioprotection, and that STAT3 activation is key for Brg1-mediated cardioprotection in both diabetic and non-diabetic subjects. Therefore, the objectives 1, 2 and 3 are fulfilled. Moreover, we have extended the study to demonstrated that STAT3 activation mediated the attenuated diabetic heart I/R injury offered by Repeated Non-Invasive Limb Ischemic Preconditioning, and we also proposed h-HABP as a sensitive indicator and predictor of post-ischemic myocardial recovery.

17121315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121315.value: We have found that SevoPC attenuates post-ischemic infarction and facilitates autophagosome clearance, and enhanced myocardial Brg1 and p-STAT3 in non-diabetic and diabetic subjects. Brg1 is critical for SevoPC cardioprotection through facilitating STAT3 signaling that involves the modulation of cardiac autophagy. Reduced level of cardiac Brg1 is the underlying mechanism that causes the diabetic heart to lose responsiveness to SevoPC cardioprotection, and that activation of STAT3 signalling is the key pathway in Brg1-mediated restoration of diabetic heart sensitivity to SevoPC.

17121315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121315.value: The findings grained from the current study will provide a rationale for more informed pharmacotherapies during reperfusion in diabetic patients and can be extended to clinical trials testing the effect of SevoPC cardioprotection in cardiac patients with diabetes.

17121315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121315.value: We have found that SevoPC confers cardioprotection in myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury with non-diabetes and diabetes, and the underlying mechanisms involve Brg1, STAT3 and autophagy. Information gained from this study will lead to the identification of new therapeutic targets to increase diabetic cardiac Brg1 level by either genetic or pharmacological approaches.

17121915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121915.value: 颌骨错位可能导致功能和面部形态的异常。一些严重的病例，牙齿位置的治疗甚至需要结合手术方法，即正颌手术。在此类型的手术中，上下颌骨其中软组织附着于咽腔气道的这一部分骨组织被连接起来、改变位置。这样的改变将导致气道形状和大小的变化。部分文献报道了正颌手术后阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停（OSA）的发生发展。了解咽腔气道在常见骨性错颌（牙合）中的基线特征，对于避免术后发生呼吸紊乱（如OSA）有着无可估量的价值。通过比较患者测量值与参考值之间的差异，可预先确定可能导致潜在气道阻塞的区域并列入手术设计。 目前，常见面部畸形的咽腔气道在正颌手术后，它们3D特征的数据资料或维度变化都无法得知。锥形束CT（CBCT）出现后，以小剂量辐射获取颌骨组织的3D影像成为可能。尽管CBCT在软组织与空气交界处有着很高的空间分辨率，但在做气道评估时，它仍然常常是一个被忽视的方法。 该课题的目的是建立常见面部畸形中咽腔气道的3D特征，并量化在正颌手术后骨移动导致的气道变化情况。从46位患有常见面部畸形（如骨性II类、III类畸形）的患者中获取手术前后的CBCT扫描，手术造成的气道变化用专用软件量化，构造3D预测算法从而用于正颌手术设计中。 这将会对术者有着极大的帮助——设计出使正颌手术达到最佳功能和美学结果所需的骨移动的量和方向，且不损害气道的开放。不同的手术方案在术前都可进行评估，使术前准备更完善并缩短了手术时间。患者易并发严重术后气道并发症（如OSA）的风险也能预先确定。具体病例中充分的治疗设计方案将因此减少修正手术的需求。此外，3D预测可用于在术前向患者告知手术步骤，从而建立更好的医患交流。

17122415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122415.value: 妊娠期母體螺旋動脈的重塑是形成胎盤並成功妊娠的必要條件，重塑失敗可導致多種妊娠並發症，危及孕婦和胎兒生命。子癇前期是常見的妊娠並發症之一，主要認為與滋養細胞侵入過淺，子宮螺旋動脈重塑障礙有關。子癇前期影響著2-5%的妊娠產婦，是產前發病率和死亡率的首要原因。目前尚無可靠的預測或早期診斷的方法。 蛻膜自然殺傷(dNK)細胞是孕早期蛻膜組織中最豐富的淋巴細胞群，妊娠第三月末期其數量約佔蛻膜淋巴細胞總量的70%。與外周血自然殺傷(pNK)細胞不同，dNK細胞具有極低的細胞殺傷活性，並能分泌各種大量的細胞因子，直接和間接作用於子宮螺旋動脈與滋養細胞，最終促進胎盤血管重塑。 Glycodelin-A（GdA)主要由蛻膜間質細胞分泌，是妊娠早期蛻膜中最豐富的糖蛋白。它對調節蛻膜內不同免疫細胞的細胞活性至關重要。我們未公開的數據表明GdA能特異性地與dNK細胞結合，促進其血管重塑功能。 因此我們提出假設：蛻膜內GdA通過影響孕早期dNK細胞的活性從而調節胎盤血管重塑；GdA表達下調會參與子癇前期的病理生理髮生機制。此假設將通過研究以下五個方面來驗證：(1) GdA對dNK細胞直接調節血管重塑的影響；(2) GdA對dNK細胞通過作用於滋養細胞而間接調節血管重塑的影響；(3) GdA對dNK細胞表面活化受體表達的影響；(4) GdA對dNK細胞的作用機制；(5) 子癇前期GdA及其受體的表達。 此研究有助於更深入理解人類早期胎盤形成的機制。在臨床方面，其結果或預示著可以使用GdA及/或其受體的表達水平作為預測或早期診斷子癇前期的指標之一。

17122415.label: Realisation of objectives
17122415.value: Glycodelin-A (GdA) is an abundant glycoprotein in the decidua during early pregnancy. It plays an important role in regulating the cellular activity of different immune cells that reside in the decidua. In this study, we hypothesize that decidual GdA regulates the placental vascular remodeling in human by modulating the activities of dNK cells during early pregnancy and the down-regulation of GdA contributes to the pathophysiology of preeclampsia. There were 4 objectives in this project, and they had all been achieved. Objective 1. To study the effect of glycodelin-A on decidual natural killer cell-mediated vascular remodeling GdA was purified from amniotic fluid by affinity chromatography. Its identity was confirmed by tandem mass spectrometry. Insoluble particles and endotoxin were removed by a 0.22 μm filter and endotoxin removing kit, respectively. Buffy coats were obtained from Hong Kong Red Cross Blood Transfusion Service. Peripheral blood CD16-56bright NK cells, the suggested tissue-specific NK cells precursors, were isolated by fluorescence-activated cell sorting or by CD56 MicroBeads after negative immuno-magnetic NK cell isolation steps. Decidual natural killer (dNK) cells were isolated from first trimester termination of pregnancy tissues. The tissue was minced, digested with DNase I and collagenase and passed through a 70 μm cell filter to obtain single-cell suspension. dNK cells were obtained by Ficoll-Plaque followed by CD56+ positive immuno-magnetic isolation. GdA was purified from amniotic fluid by anti-glycodelin affinity chromatography. In addition, primary trophoblast was isolated from tissues obtained from patients undergoing surgical termination of first trimester pregnancy. NK cells (1x106) were cultured in the Roswell Park Memorial Institute (RPMI-1640) medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 500 IU/mL of recombinant human interleukin (IL)-2, 5 ng/mL of recombinant human IL-15, and 5 μg/mL of GdA for 5 days. NK cells cultured under the same condition without GdA were used as control. GdA treatment significantly enhanced the expression of dNK cell markers CD9 and CD49a and the production of the dNK pro-angiogenic factor VEGF in the peripheral blood CD16-CD56bright NK cells. The spent media of GdA-treated CD16-CD56bright NK cells promoted tube formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC). Supplementation by anti-VEGF antibody reduced the tube formation induction by GdA-treated peripheral blood CD16-56bright NK cell medium. Objective 2. To study the regulatory role of decidual natural killer cells on the vascular remodeling activity of trophoblast and its association with glycodelin-A The vascular remodeling activity of trophoblast was determined by the ability of the trophoblast to migrate/invade and then integrate into the endothelial cells network. Spent medium derived from GdA-treated peripheral blood CD16-56bright NK cell induced the invasion of primary extravillous trophoblast and JEG-3 cells. In contrast, the medium did not affect the migration of the trophoblast. Anti-IGFBP-1 antibody supplementation nullified the biological activity of GdA-treated peripheral blood CD16-56bright NK cell culture medium, i.e. down-regulated the invasiveness of JEG-3 cells when compared to GdA-treated NK cell medium group. On the other hand, anti-VEGF antibody has no such effect. Besides, spent medium derived from GdA-treated CD16-56bright NK cell has no effect on trophoblast integration to the endothelial cell network. Objective 3. To study the effect of glycodelin-A on the expression of activating receptors in decidual natural killer cell Flow cytometry was used to determine the surface markers of decidual NK cell markers (CD9, CD151 and L-selectin). GdA treatment significantly induced the expression of CD9 in peripheral blood CD16-CD56bright NK and the tissue-specific NK cells precursors subset, but not CD16+CD56dim NK cells. GdA has no effect on the expression of activating receptor, including LILRB1, NKp44 and KIR2DS1 in all NK cell subsets. Objective 4. To investigate the mechanism of glycodelin-A action on decidual natural killer cell GdA had a stronger binding affinity to the CD16-CD56bright NK cells when compared to the CD16+CD56dim NK cells. This GdA-NK cell interaction was reduced by de-sialylation. The involvement of L-selectin on GdA-NK cells interaction was confirmed by (1) immuno-precipitation with the recombinant L-selectin; (2) L-selectin expression on monocyte and macrophage surface; and (3) the ability of anti-L-selectin antibody to block the GdA binding to the monocytes and macrophage. The intracellular signaling pathways induced by GdA treatment was also analyzed. The biological activities of GdA were demonstrated to be mediated by the activation of ERK signaling pathways in NK cells. Objective 5. To determine the expression of glycodelin-A and its receptor in pregnancy complicated by preeclampsia Chorionic villus sampling (CVS) is used to obtained placental tissues in early pregnancy for prenatal diagnosis. In this study, CVS surplus to diagnostic needs (~1 mg) was collected. As there is no reliable marker in predicting PE in early pregnancy, spare CVS samples from all women consented to participate in the study were stored until delivery. The expressions of glycodelin-A and L-selectin in CVS was determined by immunohistochemistry using specific antibodies followed by fluorescent-labelled secondary antibody. Results from samples diagnosed to have PE at delivery was compared with that of the matched controls. PE is defined as maternal hypertension >140/90 mmHg without previous hypertensive history and 300 mg/l proteinuria without any history of renal disease. A total of 163 CVS samples have obtained during the study period and 5 of them were obtained from PE pregnancy. Our results showed that there was no difference on the expressions of glycodelin-A and L-selectin between first trimester CVS samples from PE patients and normal pregnancy control.

17122415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17122415.value: - GdA treatment enhanced the expression of dNK cell markers CD9 and CD49a and the production of the functional dNK secretory product VEGF in the peripheral blood CD16-CD56bright NK cells. - The spent media of GdA-treated CD16-CD56bright NK cells promoted tube formation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells and invasiveness of trophoblasts. - The stimulatory effect of GdA on angiogenesis and trophoblast invasion were mediated by the up-regulation of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 1 (IGFBP-1), respectively (Lee et al., 2019). GdA is involved in angiogenesis during embryogenesis as well as in endometrial cancer (Lee et al., 2016). -The stimulatory effect of GdA on angiogenesis and trophoblast invasion were mediated by the stimulatory activities of GdA on the extracellular signal-regulated protein kinases (ERK) signaling pathways activation (Lee et al., 2019). - Glycosylation is important in the biological activities of GdA. Only native GdA, but not deglycosylated or desialylated GdA, binds to NK cells (Lee et al., 2019). Deglycosylation also abolishes the regulatory activities of GdA on trophoblasts, monocyte and spermatozoa (Lee et al., 2016). - GdA interacted with L-selectin, expressed only in the CD16-CD56bright NK cells, but not in the CD16+CD56dim NK cells (Lee et al., 2019).

17122415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122415.value: There are two important areas for further development: 1. Based on the important role of GdA in regulating immune cell and trophoblast functions during early pregnancy, it is reasonable to speculate that deficiency in the normal functions of GdA may contribute to the pathophysiology of various pregnancy-associated complications. We are planning to determine the expression of GdA and its receptors in the placenta complicated by intrauterine growth restriction and gestational trophoblastic disease. 2. We have shown that GdA binding to L-selectina to monocyte and macrophage via carbohydrate recognition. Removal of sialic acid, the outmost sugar residue of the glycan chain, has lost the binding the GdA-mediated biological functions. In a recent study on its molecular structure using x-ray crystallography indicated a unique structure of glycodelin in presenting its glycan chains. Further study of glycodelin with homogeneous glycan structure is required to define the mechanistic aspects of these glycans.

17122415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122415.value: The vascular remodeling of maternal spiral artery is crucial to placentation and successful pregnancy. Decidual natural killer (dNK) cells are the most abundant (~70%) leukocyte population at the maternal-fetal interface in early pregnancy. dNK cells secrete immunomodulatory factors that contributes to vascular remodeling. Dysregulation of vascular remodeling and aberrant levels of dNK cells are associated with various pregnancy complications leading to significant maternal and fetal death. Glycodelin-A (GdA) is a decidua-abundant glycoprotein regulators immune cell function. The project tested the hypothesis that GdA regulates the placental vascular remodeling in human by modulating the activities of dNK cells during early pregnancy. The results demonstrated a role of GdA in driving the NK cell differentiation into a dNK cells, which promotes vascular remodeling and placental development via secretion of cytokine IGFBP-1 and angiogenic factor VEGF. The project also identified the mechanism of GdA by binding to the surface receptors L-selectin and activate ERK signaling pathway. The outcome of this project gives a better understanding on the role of dNK cells in pregnancy. In long term, the present findings enhance our understanding of the cause of pregnancy loses and provide the basis for development of new treatment strategies.

17122915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122915.value: 一型人類免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV-1) 是引發獲得性免疫缺陷綜合症 (俗稱: 愛滋病, acquired immunodeficiency disease syndrome, AIDS) 的病原體。 不安全的性行為是愛滋病不斷傳播的主要途徑。傳統疫苗對防止HIV-1感染成效不顯著, 因此為了對抗HIV-1/AIDS, 新型疫苗的研發有著急切性, 最終解決方案仍靠發展有效疫苗及治愈方法。基於研資局資助的研究(RGC762209), 我們透過調查免疫系統中“細胞程式死亡-因子1” (Programmed death-1, PD-1) 和細“胞程式死亡-配體” (Programmed death-Ligand, PD-L) 信號途徑, 來研究AIDS疫苗的設計。我們的疫苗稱“PD-1-based vaccine”, 通過PD-L的結合將HIV抗原靶向樹狀細胞 (Dendritic Cells, DC) 來誘發高頻率的特異性免疫反應。這種疫苗能引發的高頻率多功能性CD8+ T細胞, 是其他靶向DC誘導方法不能產生的。 由於以T細胞為基礎疫苗的效能, 取決於誘發高頻率的效應和記憶性T細胞, 我們的發現提供了一個簡單, 可重複, 且有效的方法, 來誘導長久的CD8+ T細胞免疫，對疫苗及治愈方法發展有重要影響。 最近有研究指示, 骨髓來源的抑制性細胞(Myeloid-derived suppressor cells, MDSCs) 誘發針對HIV的CD8+ T細胞功能衰竭。 而且HIV-1 甚至AIDS 疫苗也能引發MDSCs。 MDSCs抑制保護性CD8+ T細胞的反應, 因此克制MDSC反應是研發AIDS疫苗的重要步驟。 我們最近發現PD-1-based vaccine能從克制MDSC相關反應, 進而將表達HIV-1 抗原GAG的惡性間皮瘤治愈。所以本研究的兩個主旨是: 一, 探討PD-1-based vaccine引發的 CD8+ T 細胞如何缓和MDSC相關的免疫抑制 ; 二, 從減低MDSC反應, 來提升疫苗引發的 CD8+ T細胞消除被HIV-1感染細胞的效能。

17123315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123315.value: The cultivation of genetically uniform crops over large areas of farmland is frequently associated with severe disease outbreaks which could result in huge economic losses. In addition, the use of agrochemicals to control plant pathogens often leads to serious pollution problems and increases the cost of production significantly. Understanding the intrinsic pathways involved in plant defense responses remains the key to the development of durable disease control strategies. Phytoalexins are low-molecular-weight antimicrobial compounds produced by plants in response to infection or stress. In sorghum, 3-deoxyanthocyanidins and flavones are flavonoid phytoalexins essential for defense against Colletotrichum sublineolum which causes severe foliar damages and substantial yield loss. Both metabolites are classified as 3-deoxyflavonoids because of the absence of C3-hydroxylation. Over the years, a number of sorghum pathogen-specific structural genes encoding enzymes in the central pathways for flavonoid biosynthesis have been identified and characterized in our laboratory. However, the reaction steps in the 3-deoxyanthocyanidin branch pathway which is inducible during defense responses are not completely established. On the other hand, several phylogenetically related cytochrome P450 sequences are potentially involved in the formation of different flavone-derived phytoalexins. In this study, we will continue our ongoing efforts to elucidate the biosynthetic routes for 3-deoxyflavonoid phytoalexins in sorghum following fungal inoculation. The available sorghum genome sequence has allowed us to identify new candidate genes for biochemical characterization through recombinant enzyme assays and transgenic plant analysis. We will also implement a virus-induced gene silencing system to evaluate the effects of targeted gene suppression on the metabolite and infection phenotypes in fungal-infected sorghum seedlings. A quantitative proteomics approach will be employed to discover novel metabolic enzymes and regulatory proteins potentially involved in phytoalexin accumulation in sorghum. Complete understanding of the molecular biology of 3-deoxyflavonoid biosynthesis will provide insights for biotechnological improvement of disease resistance in plants. Because of their potential for chronic disease prevention, the 3-deoxyflavonoids can also be engineered transgenically in edible tissues of food crops for functional food development. Finally, results from this work may advance our knowledge on how distinct flavonoid branch pathways with defense functions are evolved in sorghum but not in other related cereals. 大面積種植同一種農作物往往引起病害爆發，從而造成巨大的經濟損失。化學農藥的使用不僅增加了經濟投入，同時還會帶來嚴重的環境污染。瞭解植物防禦病害的機理是可持續性控制植物病害發生的關鍵所在。植物干擾素是植物響應真菌感染而產生的低分子量抗菌劑。炭疽病侵染高粱，引起高粱葉片嚴重損傷，從而造成大面積減產。高粱體內合成3-deoxyanthocyanidins和黃酮類，用於防禦其病原真菌Colletotrichum sublineolum的侵染。因缺少C3-羥基，這兩種代謝產物被分類為3-deoxyflavonoids。本實驗室近幾年來已發現多個在此病程相關信號途徑中重要的基因，並對其功能進行了詳細研究。然而，高粱響應真菌侵染合成3-deoxyanthocyanidin的通路還不甚明瞭。另一方面，許多細胞色素酶P450（cytochrome P450）家族的基因可能參與了不同黃酮類植物抗毒素的合成。在本研究中，我們將繼續探明高粱響應真菌侵染合成3-deoxyanthocyanidin的途徑。我們將充分利用高粱基因庫，並通過分析體外重組酶活性，利用轉基因植物，及病毒誘導的基因沉默系統來研究目的基因的功能。數量蛋白組學的方法將用於挖掘在高粱抗菌劑合成途徑中的新的代謝酶及調節蛋白。深入瞭解3-deoxyanthocyanidin合成的分子生物學將有助於通過生物技術途徑提高植物對病害的抗性。除此之外，3-deoxyflavonoid對慢性疾病有預防作用，通過轉基因技術，將食用作物發展為功能作物將產生一定的醫學和經濟價值。最後，此研究將有助於加深我們對高粱特有的不同類黃酮響應病害進化途徑的瞭解。

17123315.label: Realisation of objectives
17123315.value: Objective 1 Recombinant enzyme assays and transgenic Arabidopsis analyses were used to characterize the biochemical functions of the candidate metabolic enzymes in this study. Most of the work was done by a PhD student (Wang Lanxiang), unless specified otherwise. Sb06g029550, which was proposed to be a flavanone reductase (FNR), was not able to convert naringenin/eriodictyol to flavan-4-ols in recombinant enzyme assays. Consistently, transgenic plant does not produce flavan-4-ol and its derivatives. Hence it is unlikely to function as an FNR enzyme. Three new members of the CYP93G subfamily (FNSII and F2H enzymes) were also studied. Previously we demonstrated that CYP93G3 was a pathogen-inducible flavanone 2-hydroxylase (Du et al. 2010). Results from this project confirmed that Sb06g000260 and Sb04g008860 are flavone synthase II (FNII) while Sb01g034930 is a flavanone 2-hydroxylase. These tasks were performed by an undergraduate student (Tse Lap Hang) for her final year project. A member of the CYP75B family, Sb01g034460 (CYP75B97), was included this study because of its high homology to our previously reported a novel enzyme (CYP75B4) in rice (Plant Physiol 175:1527). Our data demonstrated that Sb01g034460, like CYP75B4, is a dual apigenin 3’-hydroxylase and chrysoeriol 5’-hydroxylase. The dual enzyme activities are highly conserved in the grass family, including sorghum, switchgrass, and rice, for tricin production. As tricin is a lignin monomer, this enzyme represents a novel target to manipulate lignin content to improve cell wall digestibility in grass biomass (e.g. for biofuel production). These tasks were performed by an undergraduate student (Lui Cheuk Woon) for his final year project. The CYP75B97 enzyme assay data were included in our publication in New Phytologist. Chalcone isomerase is the enzyme that generates the first flavonoid structure (flavanones). Its involvement in 3-deoxyanthocyanidin biosynthesis has never been investigated. We have assayed crude enzyme extracts from infected sorghum and detected pathogen-inducible CHI activities, which are stronger in a resistant line than a susceptible line. Recombinant enzyme assays showed that the putative CHI converts chalcones to flavanones, hence confirming its CHI activities. The CHI data were presented at the 12th Congress of the International Plant Molecular Biology (IPMB). Several glucoyltrasferase genes (CGTs and OGTs) were proposed to be investigated. However, it was found that they were not induced following pathogen inoculation. Hence, we decided to focus on the above genes/enzymes in this project. Objective 2 The Brome Mosaic Virus (BMV) system was originally proposed to be used for inducing transient silencing of different target genes in sorghum. We had acquired the BMV vectors from the Samuel Noble Foundation (USA) as soon as the project started. Unfortunately, after repeated attempts and numerous trouble-shootings, the BMV gene silencing could not be successfully implemented. As an alternative strategy, we decided to generate CIRSPR/cas9 sorghum mutant lines for our target genes since this approach was applied successfully to generate rice mutants in our lab. We quickly constructed CRISPR/Cas9 vectors for 9 target genes and also teamed up with Professor Ian Godwin at University of Queensland (UQ) whose lab has established an efficient gene gun platform for sorghum transformation. Two PhD students (Wang Lanxiang and Lui Cheuk Woon) were deployed to perform sorghum transformation at UQ, each for six months. Unfortunately, we were not able to generate enough transformation events for each construct to identify gene editing mutants because of delays in visa issuance, unavailability of immature embryos in a timely manner, and other unforeseen circumstances. In addition, we were probably too ambitious by shooting too many constructs (9), instead of focusing on just 2-3 constructs, considering the time limitation and the students’ lack of experiences in sorghum transformation. Afterall, CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing is still not widely applicable to sorghum. Nonetheless, the students also transformed some over-expression constructs simultaneously, and stable transgenic lines over-expressing SbF3H1 which encode flavanone 3-hydroxylase (F3H) were successfully generated. After their return to HKU, the transgenic lines were propagated to T3 generation for characterizations. As F3H is not active constitutively, SbF3H1 overexpression resulted in flavonoid profiles enriched with 3-hydroxylated flavonoids which do not normally accumulate in wild-type vegetative tissues. The transgenic SbF3H1 plants also showed reduced susceptibility to Colletotrichum sublineolum (a major sorghum pathogen). Furthermore, infection-induced production of reactive oxygen species was alleviated in the transgenic plants. The enriched flavonoid profile may enhance defense responses and also represent a novel source of nutraceuticals. We have submitted a manuscript on the SbF3H1 transgenic plants to Plant Biotechnology Journal. In addition, we had generated transgenic CHI-overexpressing sorghum but only one line was successfully propagated. Nonetheless, this line showed stronger 3-deoxyanthocyanidin production than wild-type plants. The data were presented at the IPMB congress together with the CHI enzyme activity data described above. Although we were not able to generate useful mutants for characterization, our enduring efforts had resulted in positive outcomes including the SbF3H1 manuscript, exchange research experiences for the PhD students, successful collaboration with UQ, and the acquisition of sorghum transformation skills by our lab. Objective 3 The label-free SWATH-MS proteomics platform established in our lab (J Proteome Res 2016, 3528-3539) was used to investigate differential protein profiles between seedlings of two sorghum cultivars, SC748-5 (resistant and produces 3-deoxyanthocyanidins) and DK77 (susceptible with no 3-deoxyanthocyanidins). Soluble proteins were extracted from infected plants 48 h after C. sublineolum inoculation, then trypsinized and purified. The digested peptides were then subjected to SWATH-MS-based quantitative proteomic analysis. A total of 870 proteins were exclusively identified in the resistant cultivar. These proteins, with a fold change of >1.2 or <0.70 at a significance level of 0.05, were considered to be up- or down-regulated respectively. Under such definition, 168 proteins were up-regulated and 134 proteins were down-regulated 48 hours after the fungal inoculation. These proteins were then categorized according to their biological functions by Gene Ontology analysis of Biological Processes (GOSLIM). Most of the up-regulated proteins were involved in different metabolic processes, for instance, organic acids and secondary metabolites. Similarly, most down-regulated proteins were also involved in various metabolic processes like carbohydrates. According to the GOSLIM classification, 10.7% of the up-regulated proteins were involved in eliciting responses to stimulus, including allene oxide synthase involved in jasmonate biosynthesis and two pathogenesis-related proteins (PR-4). Meanwhile, proteins involved in photosynthesis were also down-regulated after the fungal treatment. The number of differentially expressed proteins detected were relatively small. Also, there were no obvious novel targets that merit further investigation. Hence, we decided to employ next-generation sequencing technology to C. sublineolum-inoculated sorghum seedlings compared with mock-inoculated control. Interestingly, the data revealed that alternative splicing (AS) regulation may function as important as traditional transcriptional control during defense responses. In particular, several genes involved in flavonoid and phenylpropanoid biosynthesis pathways undergo multiple AS modifications. In addition, non-conventional of both 5’ and 3’ splice sites were alternatively used in response to C. sublineolum infection. Furthermore, splicing factors were also affected at both transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels in infected sorghum seedlings. As a first transcriptome report on C. sublineolum-infected sorghum, this study suggested that AS functions in parallel with transcriptional control and participates in defense responses. A manuscript reporting these data is now under revision after review by Frontiers in Plant Sciences.

17123315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17123315.value: This project has trained two undergraduate students (10: nos. 3 and 4) who worked on their Final Year (Part C 10: nos. 1 and 2) and two current PhD students who participate actively in different experiments including sorghum transformation at University of Queensland (UQ). We demonstrated that sorghum CYP75B97 is a flavonoid B-ring hydroxylase with dual apigenin 3’- and chrysoeriol 5’-hydroxylase activities which are specific to biosynthesis pathway for extractable tricin and cell wall lignin-bound tricin. These findings constitute part of the data published in New Phytologist (Part C 8: no. 4). Sorghum normally accumulate 3-deoxyflavonoids (mainly flavone derivatives) as predominant flavonoids. Transgenic SbF3H1 overexpression sorghum lines were generated and shown to have altered flavonoid profiles containing flavonol and anthocyanidin derivatives. They showed reduced susceptibility to Colletotrichum sublineolum (anthracnose pathogen) with alleviated reactive oxygen species production. A manuscript was submitted for review by Plant Biotechnology Journal (Part C 8: no. 3). We also present the first transcriptome report on sorghum infected by C. sublineolum. Alternative splicing (AS) was identified as an important component of defense responses. AS modifications were confirmed for several genes involved in flavonoid and phenylpropanoid pathways as well as splicing machinery. Non-conventional splice sites are also selectively recognized during fungal infection. A manuscript submitted to Frontiers in Plant Sciences (Part C 8: no. 2) is now under revision. Using the flavonoid profiling methodologies developed in this study, we have demonstrated that transgenic sorghum over-expressing Lr34 produced higher levels of 3-deoxyflavonoid phytoalexins and showed enhanced resistance to C. sublineolum. This work was done in collaboration with CSIRO scientists and our data constitute a portion of a publication in Plant Biotechnology Journal (Part C 8: no. 1) We also presented our data on chalcone isomerase (CHI) at the 12th Congress of the International Plant Molecular Biology in Montpellier in August 2018 (Part C 9: no. 1). Following fungal infection, a resistant sorghum line showed stronger CHI gene expression level and enzymatic activities as well as higher amounts of 3-deoxyflavonoid phytoalexins. Transgenic CHI over-expressing sorghum lines were generated and demonstrated to synthesize more 3-deoyanthocyanidins upon infection. This project has resulted in successful collaborations with Dr Evans Lagudah of CSIRO Agriculture and Food (Australia) and Professor Ian Godwin of UQ. We have published a paper with the CSIRO group (8: no. 1). Two PhD students have learned sorghum transformation at UQ. A manuscript with Godwin lab is now under review (8: no. 3).

17123315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17123315.value: The collaborations established with the Australian scientists have continued despite completion of this project. For example, we have recently published another paper with CSIRO scientists on the characterization of a transgenic barley expression the wheat Lr67 resistant gene (Plant Physiol 179:1285). We were analyzing the flavonoid profiles in the transgenic lines following fungal infection. For a long time, transformation is a hurdle for molecular research in sorghum. Following the collaboration with the Godwin lab at UQ, we have acquired the transformation skills and implemented the gene gun at HKU. We will start doing sorghum transformation for the new genes discovered in this project as soon as new funding becomes available. In fact, we submitted a GRF proposal (2019-2020) to investigate alternative splicing in sorghum during infection using transgenic sorghum lines. Meanwhile, we will continue to collaborate with the Godwin lab on the generation of sorghum CRISPR/Cas9 mutants. Recently, they have successfully achieved gene editing by CRISPR/Cas9 in the sorghum genotype Tx430 (Methods Mol Biol 1931:169-183).

17123315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17123315.value: Sorghum is ranked 5th among cereals in terms of total world production. It is well known that sorghum produces 3-deoxyflavonoids as defense compounds against fungal infection which could cause severe yield loss in the field. This study aims to understand what factors would influence the production of 3deoxyflavonoids, which may in turn affect the disease outcome in sorghum. We established the catalytic functions of flavonoid enzymes including chalcone isomerase (CHI), flavone synthase II, flavanone 2-hydroxylase, and chrysoeriol 5’-hydroxylase (C5’H). In particular, CHI activities, which are required for 3-deoxyanthocyanidin formation, are strongly induced in a resistant sorghum line. Meanwhile, C5’H is involved in production of tricin for cell wall lignin. In collaboration with University of Queensland (UQ), we generated genetically modified sorghum with flavanone 3-hydroxylase activities, resulting in enriched flavonoid profiles and reduced disease severity. We also worked with CSIRO Agriculture and Food (Australia) and demonstrated that 3-deoxyflavonoids are important defense metabolites in transgenic Lr34 sorghum. Furthermore, we identified alternative splicing as a potential regulatory mechanism for flavonoid biosynthesis genes during fungal infection. Finally, this project had resulted in continuing collaborations with CSIRO and UQ scientists. It also provided valuable exchange experiences for two PhD students to conduct research at UQ.

17123915.label: Realisation of objectives
17123915.value: We have performed series of in vivo, ex vivo and in vitro experiments and demonstrated that PKCβ2 over-activation exacerbates myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury in diabetes which is associated with reduced expression of cardiac caveolin-3 and impaired autophagic influx. Furthermore, we explored the role of caveolin-3 in the detrimental effect of PKCβ2 over-activation by using wildtype and cardiac specific caveolin-3 gene knockout mouse in the absence or presence of PKCβ2 inhibition with PKCβ2-siRNA and/or caveolin-3 enhancement with Adv- caveolin-3. We found that PKCβ2 over-activation is the major mechanism that renders the diabetic heart prone myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury; and it does so via downregulating caveolin-3 and involves the modulation of cardiomyocyte autophagy. Therefore, the objectives 1, 2 and 3 are fulfilled. Moreover, we have extended the study to demonstrate that propofol counteracts cardiomyocyte H/R injury by attenuating mitochondrial damage and improving mitochondrial biogenesis through upregulating Cav-3 during hyperglycemia. Additionally, we proposed several potential targets, including repressor activator protein 1 (Rap1), prostaglandin E receptor subtype 4 (EP4), forkhead box transcription factor 1 (Foxo1). Their roles in the myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury in diabetes are worth further investigation.

17123915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17123915.value: We have found that inhibition of over-activation of PKCβ2 significantly down-regulated myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury in diabetes with concomitantly enhanced expression of caveolin-3 and improved autophagic influx, as evidenced by reduced cardiac LC3-II/LC3-I accumulation and increased level of p62. The caveolin-3 is the downstream of PKCβ2. Reduced level of cardiac caveolin-3 is the underlying mechanism of PKCβ2 over-activation that causes the diabetic heart prone to aggravate myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury. Cardiac specific knockout of caveolin-3 block the cardioprotective effect of the inhibition of PKCβ2 in ischemia/reperfusion injury in diabetes, indicating that PKCβ2 over-activation is the key mechanism that renders the diabetic heart prone myocardial ischemia/reperfusion injury, and it does so via downregulating caveolin-3 and involves the modulation of cardiomyocyte autophagy.

17123915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17123915.value: The findings grained from the current study will support the long-term development of a new class of therapeutics to treat ischemic heart disease and provide a rationale for more informed pharmacotherapies during reperfusion in diabetic patients. Mechanistic studies can be extend to pre-clinical and clinical trials testing the effect of PKCβ2 and caveolin-3 and yield novel insights into unexplored physiology, which may open a new avenue for treatment of ischemic heart disease in diabetes.

17123915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17123915.value: We have found that inhibition of PKCβ2 over-activation confers cardioprotection in myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury with non-diabetes and diabetes, and the underlying mechanisms involve caveolin-3 and autophagy. Information gained from this study will lead to the identification of new therapeutic targets to inhibit diabetic cardiac PKCβ2 level by either genetic or pharmacological approaches.

17124115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124115.value: 視網膜色素變疾病（RP) 是一組因為感光細胞死亡而造成失明的遺傳性疾病。每年全球超過150萬人因 RP疾病喪失了視力。 導致感光細胞死亡的分子機制仍然不完全清楚。我們以前研究發現小膠質細胞參與了RP的病理過程。 然而， 目前還不清楚是視網膜中小膠質細胞增殖還是外週巨噬細胞浸入參與了RP的病理過程。 我們主要假設是：視網膜中小膠質細胞增殖參與了RP的病理過; 抑制了CSF1R-C/EBPα-PU.1通路可以阻止視網膜中小膠質細胞增殖，進而延遲了視網膜色素變性疾病的進展。基於小膠質細胞增殖對CSF1R的依賴性，我們採用CSF1R抑製劑PLX3397在RP的小鼠模型（RD10）上調節小膠質細胞水平。我們的初步結果表明PLX3397可以迅速而明顯減少視網膜小膠質細胞。此外，鉴于PLX3397可以造成中樞及外圍的巨噬細胞死亡，我們因而又採用RD10/CX3CR1CreER/+/R26iDTR/+小鼠，用白喉毒素有選擇地誘導大腦和視網膜小膠質細胞死亡， 而保持外週巨噬細胞完整。這樣我們就可以確定視網膜小膠質細胞增殖对RP的進展的具體貢獻。 這項研究將有助於建立採用CSF1R抑製劑在臨床治療RP病人的可行性。

17124115.label: Realisation of objectives
17124115.value: The main goal of this proposal was to investigate the role of microglial proliferation in the expansion of the microglial population during the pathogenesis of retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and the molecular mechanisms underlying the microglial expansion to the progression of RP. To investigate the temporal dynamics of microglial proliferation in the rd10 mouse model of RP (Aim 1), we backcrossed transgenic CX3CR1GFP/GFP mice, in which microglia are fluorescently labeled after replacing the Cx3cr1 gene with the gene encoding enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP), with rd10 mice and generated a new line of rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP mice. In wild-type (WT) mice, microglial cells primarily distribute to the outer plexiform layer (OPL), inner plexiform layer (IPL) and the ganglion cell layer (GCL) of the retina. However, we observed some microglial cells in the outer nuclear layer (ONL) of rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP mice, which is not the normal distribution site of microglial cells, and incorporation of BrdU in these microglia cells at all the three time points (P16, P19 and P21). The regional and temporal distribution of BrdU-positive microglial cells in the ONL of the retina indicated the proliferative activity of the microglial population during the course of RP disease. We then examined the molecular mechanisms underlying microglial proliferation (Aim 1). Colony-stimulating factor receptor 1 (CSF1R) plays a key role in microglial proliferation and survival. CSF1 and interleukin-34 (IL34) are two ligands for CSF1R. We thus performed quantitative RT-PCR and western blot to analyze the expression levels of CSF1R, IL-34, CSF1 and transcription factors PU.1 and C/EBPα. We found that the mRNA and protein expression levels of CSF1R, CSF1, IL34 and the transcription factor PU.1 and C/EBPα were progressively increased during RP disease compared with WT controls. Similarly, we observed that CSF1R was upregulated at the mRNA level in sorted populations of microglia from rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP mice. Altogether, our results indicated the signaling through the CSF1R and the activation of PU.1 and C/EBPα as the possible pathways underlying microglial proliferation. To examine the role of CSF1R in controlling microglial proliferation, we inhibited its activity by using a blocking antibody for CSF1R. We found that the CSF1R antibody efficiently blocked microglial proliferation in the ONL of rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP mice, as evidenced by the reduced levels of incorporation of BrdU in microglial cells compared with rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP injected with a control antibody. In addition, blocking the CSF1R reduced the expansion of microglial population in the retina of rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP mice. Similarly, we found a significantly higher number of proliferating microglial cells (BrdU+GFP+ microglial cells), and total microglial cells (GFP+ microglial cells) in the retina of rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP mice administered with CSF1 or IL34, when compared with the saline injected rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP mouse controls. Our results suggested the important role of signaling through CSF1R driven by CSF1 or IL34 or both for microglial proliferation. We then treated rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP mice with PLX3397, a small-molecule compound that inhibits CSF1R, to block the expansion of proliferating microglia (Aim 2). PLX3397 treatment caused a significant reduction in microglial proliferation and led to the elimination of virtually all microglia from rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP mouse retinas. We found a downregulation of CSF1R, PU.1 and C/EBPα in the rd10 retina treated with PLX3397. PLX3397 treatment caused the reduction of the expression of inflammatory mediators in microglial cells, including interleukin-1β (IL-1β), tumor necrosis factor-a (TNF-a) and nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) in rd10 retinas, using qPCR and western blot analysis. We found that PLX3397 treatment had beneficial effects over the progression of retinal degeneration, evidenced as a decreased number of degenerating retinal photoreceptor cells (TUNEL-positive photoreceptor cells, and TUNEL is an apoptotic marker) in the rd10 retina. Similarly, we observed preservation of rod and cone photoreceptor cells in the rd10 retina treated with PLX3397 at P30, P40, and P50. Similarly, visual function was rescued by PLX3397 treatment, evidenced as higher electroretinograms (ERG) responses and better behavioral performance on motion perception at optokinetic tracking test. Together, our results demonstrated a clear beneficial effect of PLX3397 in slowing RP progression and highlighted the detrimental contribution of microglial proliferation to the progression of RP disease. Withdrawal of the CSF1R inhibitor PLX3397 leads to rapid repopulation of microglia in the brain. To explore repopulated microglia homeostasis in rd10 mice, we treated rd10/CX3CR1+/GFP mice with PLX3397 for 10 days from P7 and the mice were then switched to vehicle (Aim 4). We observed a rapid repopulation of retinal microglia at the 3-day recovery time point after drug removal. Surprisingly, we found no difference between repopulating microglial cells and original proliferated microglial cells based on the release levels of inflammatory mediators and their neurotoxicity to photoreceptor cells. Our results showed that repopulated microglial cells did not alter their ability and contributed to disease progression in RP. To eliminate the possible contribution of peripheral macrophages from blood circulation, we took advantage of CX3CR1CreER/+/R26iDTR/+ mouse line, in which microglial cells could be specifically depleted from the brain with diphtheria toxin administration, while leaving peripheral macrophages intact. We backcrossed CX3CR1CreER/+/R26iDTR/+ mice into rd10 background and generated a new line of CX3CR1CreER/+/R26iDTR/+/rd10 mice (Aim 3). Consistent with previous studies, we found that CX3CR1CreER/+/R26iDTR/+/rd10 mice had a marked reduction of retinal microglial cells (99.5% ± 0.6%) within 1 day after administration of diphtheria toxin (DT). We found that microglial depletion largely recapitulated beneficial effects observed in rd10 mice with PLX3397 treatment, suggesting the local proliferation of resident microglial cells as the major mechanism for population expansion in the evolution of chronic RP disease. To conclude, we presented the evidence of the regulation of microglial proliferation during the progression of chronic neurodegeneration in a RP animal model. Our results supported the hypothesis of local proliferation of resident microglial cells as the major mechanism for population expansion during the pathological course of RP disease and provided a potent tool to target the innate immune response during chronic neurodegeneration for RP patients Please kindly note that this project heavily depended on animal models. I changed my job and moved to PolyU from HKU in mid 2016. Unexpectedly, it took us more than 6 months to relocate our animals including rd10 mice, the important mouse line for this project, from my HKU to PolyU, because of paper work related to material transfer agreement (MTA) for the animals. Moreover, our animals were accidently affected by pinworms in late 2018. These affected mice were treated for more than 3 months by PolyU Centralised Animal Facilities. During that period time, we were not allowed to perform any experiments on these mice. These sudden interruptions interrupted our experiments and subsequently delayed the project. Even with these difficulties, we managed to complete all our four proposed aims within 3.6 years. Furthermore, the PolyU campus siege that took place in November 2019 caused disruptions and inaccessibility to the campus laboratories and animal facility for 3 months. Immediately after the campus reopen, COVID-19 pandemic erupts. Consequently, a lot of our laboratory work and research activities were virtually suspended until mid-June 2020. As such, our research progress on the project has been negatively affected. Manuscript from this project is currently under preparation.

17124115.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124115.value: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is a group of eye diseases. The phenotype is characterized by an initial loss of night vision as a result of the death of rod photoreceptors followed by a progressive loss of cones, the photoreceptors that are responsible for color and high-acuity vision. To date, RP patients have had few possibilities for therapy. Microglia have a central role in the central nervous system (CNS) inflammation. Previous studies have reported that microglial activation and expansion make detrimental contribution to the progression of RP. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying the microglial expansion to the progression of RP are not completely understood. To address this issue, we initially treated the rd10 mouse model of RP with PLX3397, a small-molecule compound that inhibits colony-stimulating factor receptor 1 (CSF1R). We found that PLX3397 treatment caused a significant reduction in microglial proliferation and led to the elimination of virtually all microglia from rd10 mouse retinas. Blocking microglial proliferation by PLX3397 treatment had beneficial effects over the progression of retinal degeneration, evidenced as the reduction of the expression of inflammatory mediators, preservation of rod and cone photoreceptor cells, higher electroretinograms (ERG) responses and better behavioral performance on motion perception at optokinetic tracking test, etc. Moreover, we identified the important regulatory pathway regulated by the activation of CSF1R and the transcription factors PU.1 and C/EBPα, which was driven by CSF1 or interleukin-34 (IL34), two ligands for CSF1R, for the molecular regulators of the microglial proliferation during the course of RP disease. To eliminate the possible contribution of peripheral macrophages from blood circulation, we took advantage of CX3CR1CreER/+/R26iDTR/+ mouse line, in which microglial cells could be specifically depleted from the brain with diphtheria toxin administration, while leaving peripheral macrophages intact. We found that microglial depletion largely recapitulated beneficial effects observed in rd10 mice with PLX3397 treatment, suggesting the local proliferation of resident microglial cells as the major mechanism for population expansion in the evolution of chronic RP disease. In conclusion, we demonstrated that microglial proliferation is a major component in the evolution of chronic neuroinflammation during the development of RP disease. Targeting the activity of CSF1R inhibits microglial proliferation and significantly delays retinal degeneration and RP progression. Therefore, our findings could establish the translational potential of CSF1R inhibition for RP treatment.

17124115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124115.value: The results from this project might help in creating new therapeutic modalities to treat neuroinflammation for retinitis pigmentosa (RP) patients, which will slow down vision loss and eventually help improve health and wellbeing for RP patients. RP is a group of diseases caused by mutations in a wide variety of rod photoreceptor specific genes. Rd10 mice we used in this study carry a mutation in the beta subunit of rod-specific phosphodiesterase gene 6 (PDE6β), a common gene that has been identified in RP patients. It will be interesting to investigate whether colony-stimulating factor receptor 1 (CSF1R) plays a similar role in RP mouse model carrying a different gene mutation, such as rhodopsin (RHO) gene, another common gene in RP patients. Based on the findings from this project on CSF1R function in microglial proliferation and survival, we have expanded our research to investigate the functional role of microglia in the programmed apoptosis of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) in the developing mouse retina. We treated new-born C57BL/6J and Cx3cr1GFP/+ mouse pups with PLX3397 and examined RGC apoptosis in the absence of local microglia in the retina. We have completed the study and submitted our manuscript to a peer-reviewed journal (Part C).

17124115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124115.value: Neuroinflammation is an important component of chronic neurodegenerative diseases within the central nervous system (CNS). Microglial cells play a key role in the maintenance of inflammatory responses and show enhanced proliferation and activation in neurodegenerative diseases. In this project, we examined the time course and regulation of microglial proliferation, using a mouse model of human retinitis pigmentosa (RP), a group of untreatable eye diseases. Our results show that that microglial proliferation contributes to the expansion of the retinal microglial population during RP progression. Moreover, we identify the CSF1R-C/EBPα-PU.1 pathway as the molecular regulator of the microglial proliferation. Inhibition of the pathway blocks retinal microglial proliferation and significantly delays the pathological course of RP, indicating an overall harmful contribution by microglial proliferation and a potential route to further delaying RP progression in RP patients.

17124415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124415.value: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV) is a novel coronavirus capable of inducing acute respiratory distress syndrome. The virus is closely related to another deadly virus, severe acute respiratory syndrome-associated coronavirus (SARS-CoV), which infected ~ 8000 and killed 750 people in Hong Kong, in 2003. Despite their resemblance in clinical presentation, replication kinetics and cytokine responses, the human-to-human spreading rate and mortality rate are different. Patients infected with MERS-CoV has a much higher mortality rate (~ 30%) than that of SARS-CoV (~ 10%). It should be noted that organ failure, especially renal failure, is frequently associated with MERS-CoV-infected cases. Pathogenesis of MERS-CoV-associated renal failure is largely unknown despite the fact that increasing evidences suggest that renal cells are natural targets for some coronaviruses. More importantly, some studies reported that MERS-CoV RNAs can be detected in the urine of infected patients suggesting the possibility of renal infection. Our previous cell line susceptibility study revealed that renal cells are permissive to MERS-CoV infection; however, detail examination of individual renal cell type after MERS-CoV infection remains unknown. To address the above question, we have conducted some pilot studies in which an ex vivo human kidney organ culture model has been successfully established. We propose to use such model to first address which renal cell types can be infected by MERS-CoV under close to physiological conditions. Next, we will examine the effect of MERS-CoV on various renal cell types. Finally, we will generate a humanized mouse model to study the pathogenesis of MERS-CoV in vivo. Such studies not only can advance our understanding on the pathogenesis of MERS-CoV in renal cells, but also provide platforms for future drug treatment against MERS-CoV infection. 中东呼吸综合征冠状病毒是一种新型冠状病毒，其可导致急性呼吸窘迫综合征。中东呼吸综合征冠状病毒（MERS-CoV）与2003年香港爆发的严重急性呼吸器官综合征冠状病毒（SARS-CoV）密切相关，而SARS-CoV在2003年香港爆发期间共感染约8000人，致死750人。尽管MERS-CoV和SARS-CoV所致临床症状，复制动力学，细胞因子反应方面具有相似性，但在人际间传播速度和致死率却不尽相同。MERS-CoV致死率(~ 30%)远远高于SARS-CoV (~ 10%)。更值得注意的是，在MERS-CoV所致器官衰竭的感染病例中，肾功能衰竭频频发生。 尽管目前越来越多研究发现某些冠状病毒感染肾脏细胞，但中东呼吸综合征冠状病毒（MERS-CoV）所致肾功能衰竭的病机尚未明确。然而研究发现MERS-CoV感染患者的尿液中可以检测到MERS-CoV的RNA，该研究表明MERS-CoV极可能感染到肾脏细胞。我们团队前期研究发现肾脏细胞对于MERS-CoV具有易感性，但肾脏细胞各个亚型对MERS-CoV感染性的具体研究尚未开展。为阐述上述问题，我们团队初步研究成功构建了人体肾脏器官体外感染模型。因此，我们首先建议采用相似模型研究接近生理状态下各个肾脏细胞亚型对于MERS-CoV的易感性；其次，我们将研究MERS-CoV对于不同肾脏细胞亚型的影响；最后我们通过采用人源化小鼠模型进行MERS-CoV病理机制的体内研究。上述科学研究不仅可以增进我们对MERS-CoV所致肾功能衰竭病理机制的了解，更可以对日后MERS-CoV感染的治疗提供宝贵科学依据。

17124715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17124715.value: Psychotic disorders are severe mental illnesses causing enormous burden to patients and society. Early intervention for psychosis has been the major focus in mental health care development worldwide in the last decade with particular emphasis on using operationalized clinical criteria in identifying individuals at high-risk for psychosis. It is suggested that intervention in this pre-psychotic period may prevent progression to full-blown psychosis. However, the major challenge is to accurately differentiate those who will become psychotic from those who will not before illness onset. Thus far, no robust predictors of psychosis transition have been identified and sensitivity of these clinical criteria remained low. Furthermore, a significant proportion of at-risk individuals exhibit enduring functional impairment. Despite extensive research, neurobiological basis underlying psychosis development remains unknown. Neuroimaging, in particular magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) which has been increasingly applied in clinical high-risk research in recent years, represents a promising biomarker in predicting psychosis and functional disability. First, established psychotic disorders are associated with brain structural and functional abnormalities. Second, these brain alterations have also been found, to a lesser degree, in clinical high-risk individuals. Third, emerging evidence revealed that there are progressive brain changes occurring during the period of transition to psychosis. Despite these promising results, previous studies are hampered by several major methodological limitations. Most studies used cross-sectional baseline MRI measures for psychosis prediction without taking into consideration longitudinal brain changes across clinical high-risk transition period. Majority only focused on a single neuroimaging modality. Among those very few longitudinal neuroimaging studies, almost all had inter-scan interval beyond one year after presentation when a substantial proportion of at-risk subjects had already developed psychosis before follow-up scanning with results likely being confounded by medication effects. Predictive value of neuroimaging measures on functional outcome has rarely been investigated. In this project, we will conduct a prospective 2-year follow-up study on clinical high-risk subjects to examine whether longitudinal multimodal MRI measurements independently predict psychosis transition and functional outcome. To improve risk prediction and to better capture dynamic brain changes underlying psychosis development, MRI assessment will be conducted at baseline, at 6 and 12 months of follow-up. We hypothesized that applying longitudinal multimodal MRI examinations with 6-month inter-scan interval across the first year after presentation in at-risk sample will enhance psychosis prediction and functional outcome estimation which may facilitate pre-emptive intervention for psychosis in the future. Additionally, our findings will provide insights in neurobiological underpinnings of psychosis development. 思覺失調疾病是一種對患者及社會帶來沉重負擔的嚴重精神病。思覺失調疾病的早期治療已成為近十年全球精神健康服務發展的重點，其中特別強調使用各種臨床標準去辨識思覺失調高風險人士。有研究指出在高風險時期作出介入治療可阻止病情發展至全面的思覺失調疾病。然而，如何有效地判斷哪些人會患上思覺失調疾病是一個重大的挑戰。到目前為止，醫學界仍然未能完全辨識哪些高風險人士將會患上思覺失調，而現有臨床標準的準確度仍有不足。再者，大部份高風險人士有長期的功能受損。儘管世界各地都有很多的研究，我們對思覺失調演變過程中的神經生物學成因機制仍然未有透切的了解。 磁力共震腦掃描已被廣泛應用在臨床研究上，並為其中一個預測思覺失調病發及功能受損的重要因子。首先，思覺失調疾病跟腦部結構及功能上的缺陷有顯著關係；其次，這些腦部的轉變也在思覺失調高風險人士上出現；最後，有研究指出高風險人士在演變成思覺失調患者期間，其腦部亦有相應的轉變。 儘管過往的思覺失調高風險研究已獲得不少成果，但過去的研究方法亦有不足的地方。首先，大部分研究使用橫向磁力共振掃描方法去預測思覺失調，卻沒有探討高風險時期腦部結構的變化。還有，大多數的研究只着重單一神經影像模式。而在少數的縱向神經影像研究中，幾乎所有初次和跟進腦掃描都相隔超過一年時間，因而不少參與者在接受跟進腦掃描前已全面病發，而藥物治療亦可能影響腦掃描的結果。此外，很少研究使用腦掃描去驗證和預測功能結果。 在這個項目中，我們將進行為期兩年針對臨床高風險人士的跟進研究，以驗證縱向多模式磁力共振掃描能否預測那些高風險人士會病發及他們的功能表現。為了更準確地捕捉腦結構變化及思覺失調的演變，此掃描會在首次評估，第6和第12個月進行。我們推論腦掃描可提高對思覺失調病發和功能結果的預測，從而有助研發出更有效的早期介入治療。最後，此研究為釐清日後有關思覺失調神經生物學成因機制提供更清楚的認識。

17124715.label: Realisation of objectives
17124715.value: 1. Objective 1 -This was successfully achieved. We recruited 112 clinical-high-risk (CHR) subjects and 45 demographically-matched healthy controls. Prospective 2-year follow-up for CHR sample was completed. Clinical, cognitive, functional and MRI measures were successfully conducted. Among CHR sample, all completed baseline MRI scan, 101 completed 6-month scan and 76 completed 1-year scan. All subjects were traced for 2-year clinical data supplemented with medical-record review. Psychosis transition rate was 18% (n=20) over 2 years, largely comparable to most recent findings of meta-analysis. Regarding MRI assessment, voxel-based morphometry and cortical thickness analysis were conducted, and CHR subjects showed volume reduction in hippocampal/parahippocampal areas, anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), and medial frontal cortex relative to controls at baseline, but no group difference in cortical thickness. Tract-based spatial statistical (TBSS) analysis found that CHR subjects had reduced mode of anisotropy (MO) in bilateral anterior thalamic radiation (ATR) than controls, and trendwise significant difference in radial diffusivity (RD) in ATR at baseline. No difference in fractional anisotropy or axial diffusivity. Theory-driven seed-based (esp. default-mode network, DMN; salience network, SN; fronto-parietal network, FPN; central executive network, CEN; thalamus network, TN) and data-driven independent-component-analysis (ICA) approaches were applied in resting-state fMRI for functional connectivity assessment. Overall, CHR subjects exhibited significantly altered functional connectivity in DMN and SN, which are also implicated in established schizophrenia. Longitudinal analyses concerning differentiation between CHR-T (transition) and CHR-NT (non-transition) revealed that CHR-T showed steeper rate of gray matter loss in right superior temporal regions than CHR-NT, with antipsychotic exposure status adjusted, but no significant difference in cortical thickness changes over time. Significant improvement in RD in ATR over time was observed in CHR-NT but not CHR-T. Significant group-by-time interaction in DMN was noted, indicating that CHR-T, but CHR-NT, displayed reduced DMN connectivity over follow-up. We failed to replicate recent findings that thalamic dysconnectivity was significantly associated with psychosis transition. Taken together, although this study is still likely hampered by modest sample size (taken into consideration subtler neuroanatomical abnormalities in CHR compared to psychotic disorder, modest transition rate, and dropout rate on repeated MRI measurements but not on 2-year clinical FU), given substantial MRI data and the need to correct for multiple comparisons in analysis, our results suggest that multimodal longitudinal MRI can predict psychosis transition in CHR. To take full advantage of our multimodal MRI and clinical dataset for psychosis prediction, further advanced MRI analyses will be conducted including surface-based analysis such as gyrification index and surface area, deterministic tractography and structural connectome (whole-brain structural covariance patterns) for white matter connectivity, as well as graph-theory based analysis for global and local networks and dynamic functional connectivity analysis for resting-state fMRI. Adoption of neuroanatomical-based age prediction analysis to detect deviant patterns in neurodevelopmental maturity associated with CHR-T versus CHR-NT would further enhance psychosis prediction. 2. Objective 2 -This was successfully achieved. We specifically focused on CHR sample with completed dataset over 1-year including MRI data for functional outcome analysis. CHR subjects were classified into good (n=35) and poor (n=41) functional outcome based on GF:role and social scale cutoff scores. Results showed that more severe amotivational negative symptoms, male sex, worse premorbid adjustment, as well as poorer processing speed and working memory significantly predicted poor functional outcome at follow-up. Increased RD in ATR and decreased cortical thickness in left ACC at baseline were significantly associated with poor functional outcome status. No other baseline MRI parameters or longitudinal changes in MRI measures were found to be significantly related to functional outcome, after correction for multiple comparisons. Addition of DTI RD and cortical thickness measures into multivariate model significantly improved performance of prediction model for functional outcome. This indicates that incorporation of MRI data further enhances functional outcome prediction in CHR. Given the encouraging results, similar prediction analyses will be conducted to further evaluate predictive value of MRI data on 2-year functional outcome in CHR subjects, as well as restricting our analysis to CHR-NT subsample who contributes to the majority of CHR population and still displays markedly impaired functioning. 3. Objective 3 -This was successfully achieved. We have examined relationships between various MRI parameters in CHR sample. Results revealed no significant correlations of gray matter volume and cortical thickness with white matter alterations or functional connectivity measures. On the other hand, our seed-based between-network analyses revealed several significant findings, specifically in relation to DMN with the other networks, including decreased functional connectivity between DMN and striatum, DMN and salience network, as well as DMN and FPN. These findings are largely in keeping with the functional connectivity abnormalities observed in schizophrenia, though in a much smaller scale (less widespread deficits than in schizophrenia), thereby suggesting potential critical role of aberrant DMN in neurobiological underpinnings of psychosis progression. Notably, our results in this respect should be treated with caution owing to the fact that our sample size is modest, MRI abnormalities in general are much subtler than those of established psychotic disorders, and clinical heterogeneity of the nature of CHR, which comprises both true-positive (CHR-T) and false-positive (CHR-NT, though still experience psychiatric symptoms and functional impairment). As mentioned in Objective 1, other advanced MRI analytic strategies will be applied to further clarify, and hopefully unravel potential complex inter-relationships among various MRI parameters in CHR. 4. Objective 4 -This was successfully achieved. Our results found that in general white matter alterations and disrupted functional connectivity were more likely to be associated with symptomatology and cognitive impairment in CHR sample than structural brain abnormalities, as measured by volume deficits and cortical thickness, after correction for multiple comparisons to correct for type I error. For instance, decreased MO in ATR (DTI measures) was significantly correlated with higher levels of positive symptoms, poorer verbal fluency and verbal memory, while elevated RD in ART (DTI measures) were significantly related to more severe negative symptoms and poorer role functioning. Hypo-connectivity in DMN and SN were also associated with more severe positive symptoms in CHR sample. Overall, certain MRI measures are found to be significantly linked to the core symptoms of CHR including positive symptoms, negative symptoms and cognitive dysfunction. 5. Objective 5 -This was successfully achieved. We first developed our psychosis prediction model using machine-learning approach with the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) for Cox proportional hazards model. Four a priori candidate clinical predictor variables were selected, comprising age at presentation, positive symptom severity, global functioning, and psychiatric comorbidity, based on literature. The model was then internally validated using 5-fold cross-validation method with 500 stratified bootstrap resamples. The prognostic scores were generated which were then used to stratify CHR sample into three distinct risk-level classes, with high-risk class demonstrating a markedly higher transition rate (54.5%) than the remaining two risk-level classes (13% and 5.6%) at 2 years. The model predicted psychosis transition with an AUC of 0.790 (p<0.001), and c-index of 0.703, indicating satisfactory prediction accuracy, and was adequately validated by as revealed by internal validation analysis suggesting sufficient calibration. Combined clinical-neuroimaging model (primarily gray matter abnormalities) yielded further improved performance in psychosis prediction relative to clinical-only prediction model. This indicates that multivariate model incorporating both clinical and neuroimaging parameters would further enhance psychosis prediction in CHR samples.
