17124715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124715.value: Major findings of the project are summarized as follows: In a representative cohort of Chinese individuals at clinical high-risk (CHR) for psychosis, 18% converted to full-blown psychotic disorders over 2 years. Compared to healthy controls, CHR subjects displayed significant brain structural and functional abnormalities including reduced gray matter volume in hippocampal / parahippocampal areas, anterior cingulate cortex, and medial frontal cortex, decreased mode of anisotropy in bilateral anterior thalamic radiation, altered functional connectivity in default-mode and salience networks, and hypo-connectivity between default-mode, salience, and fronto-parietal networks. Longitudinal MRI analyses further suggested that steeper changes in right superior temporal regions, less improved in radial diffusivity in anterior thalamic radiation, and more marked default-mode network abnormalities were associated with psychosis transition status. Altered MRI measures were also linked to poorer clinical (positive and negative symptoms) and functional outcomes, in particular white matter (esp. radial diffusivity and mode of anisotropy in anterior thalamic radiation) and functional connectivity abnormalities (esp. default-mode and salience networks). Multivariate prediction model including key clinical variables of age at presentation, attenuated positive symptom severity, psychosocial functioning, and psychiatric comorbidity significantly predicted psychosis transition with satisfactory model performance and accuracy. Model-generated prognostic score successfully stratified CHR sample into three risk-level categories, with the high risk-level class demonstrating markedly elevated risk of psychosis transition over 2 years, relative to the remaining two lower risk-level classes. Importantly, incorporation of neuroimaging parameters associated with transition status further improved the performance of clinical prediction model for progression to full-blown psychotic disorders in CHR sample.

17124715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124715.value: To further build on our study findings, several course of action should be implemented: First, continuous follow-up with clinical and neuroimaging reassessment in this CHR cohort can be conducted to capture MRI prediction and longitudinal trajectories of neuroanatomical abnormalities over longer-term period as non-converted CHR subjects still carry high-risk for psychosis transition; Second, adoption of advanced MRI analytic methods in our data likely further enhances prediction model accuracy; Third, we can combine MRI data with proton-MRS data collected in our ongoing CHR study (which also collects MRI data) for outcome prediction, as accumulating evidence indicating potential role of proton-MRS parameters, indexing brain glutamate alterations, in psychosis prediction; Fifth, our MRI findings were only internally-validated. We can apply external validation to verify our results using data of our ongoing CHR proton-MRS study. Sixth, given modest sample size and transition rate, and subtler MRI abnormalities in CHR, collaboration with participation in CHR consortium for neuroimaging including our MRI dataset will facilitate generation of novel MRI markers and validation of existing significant findings to enhance psychosis risk stratification. Such collaboration will also facilitate development of future larger-scale CHR research project for both psychosis and non-psychosis outcome evaluation.

17124715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124715.value: Psychotic disorders are a group of severe mental disorders associated with significant functional disability and huge societal costs. Early intervention specifically focusing on individuals at imminent clinical high-risk (CHR) for psychosis development is of critical clinical significance. Neuroimaging is proposed to enhance current clinical prediction model for psychosis transition in CHR sample. This 2-year follow-up study aimed to examine potential role of multimodal neuroimaging measures for psychosis prediction. Our results showed that CHR individuals exhibited brain abnormalities across gray matter, white matter and functional connectivity relative to healthy volunteers. Importantly, several baseline and longitudinal neuroimaging parameters, measured by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) techniques, were significantly associated with psychosis transition over 2 years including regional gray matter volume reduction, altered white matter integrity index, and disrupted functional connectivity in specific networks implicated in human’s internal mentation and self-referential processing. Furthermore, MRI abnormalities were found to be associated with worse attenuated positive symptom and negative symptom outcomes, as well as poorer psychosocial functional levels in CHR individuals. Combined risk-stratification model incorporating both clinical variables and neuroimaging parameters further enhanced psychosis prediction relative to clinical-only model, highlighting potential utility of multimodal longitudinal MRI measures in predicting psychosis transition from CHR populations.

17125115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125115.value: Our goal is to find keys to structural and functional plasticity of sensory pathways in early postnatal life. Our study of the central vestibular circuitry for graviception found a postnatal stage when inhibitory (GABAergic) transmission as regulated by chondroitin sulfates of perineuronal nets (PN) in the vestibular nucleus (VN) is sensitive to labyrinthine inputs to the VN. Our search for plasticity-inducing factors found semaphorin 3A in colocalization with PN-chondroitin sulfates in the postnatal VN. Cultures of postnatal VN explants treated with semaphorin 3A effected dendritic remodelling among the VN neurons, implicating structural plasticity that delays synapse formation. We therefore hypothesize that PN-chondroitin sulfates regulate the pool of Sema3A available for triggering structural/synaptic plasticity at GABAegic interneurons in the postnatal establishment of the vestibular circuit for graviception. We aim (1) to study the effects of semaphorin 3A on synaptic transmission at vestibular interneurons before, and after the formation of perineuronal nets; (2) to find effects of remodeling chondroitin sulfation on the gradient of semaphorin 3A as presented to signaling receptor complexes for the maturation of negative geotaxis. Results will indicate how perineuronal chondroitin sulfates are remodeled to reset synaptic plasticity for expression of the gravity detection behavior during postnatal development. We expect findings to apply across sensory systems and thus to inform therapeutic and training paradigms with prospects for improvements in learning and memory as well as posttraumatic recovery and rehabilitation.

17125115.label: Realisation of objectives
17125115.value: Objective 1: To study the effects of semaphorin 3A on synaptic transmission at vestibular interneurons before, and after the formation of perineuronal nets. 1.1. As early as postnatal day 9 (P9), lectin-histochemistry revealed condensation of WFA-positive perineuronal nets (PN) around interneurons in the different vestibular subnuclei. Combination with immunofluorescence for semaphorin 3A (sema3A) revealed progressive PN-sema3A colocalization as from P9. The co-localization persisted into adulthood. 1.2. Sequestration of Sema3A by PN reduced its effect on excitatory transmission. Significant increase in frequency of mEPSC as observed at P7 required co-treatment of “chondroitinase + exogenous sema3A” but not sema3A alone. By contrast, significant increase in mEPSC as observed at P9 was detectable following chondroitinase treatment, irrespective of inclusion of exogenous sema3A. Chondroitinase and sema3A treatment had synergistic effect in promoting neurite growth and branching in VN explant neurons. 1.3. The results support the hypothesis that PN limited action of endogenous sema3A to increase excitatory synapses onto interneurons in the vestibular circuit. 1.4. Digestion of PN CS by chondroitinase increased excitatory transmission (EPSC, as stated in 1.2.) but reduced inhibitory transmission. This indicates differential modulation of excitation and inhibition by PN. Objective 2 To find effects of remodeling chondroitin sulfation on the gradient of semaphorin 3A as presented to signaling receptor complexes for the maturation of negative geotaxis. 2.1. Rats naturally displayed negative geotaxis by P9, coincident with PN condensation around vestibular interneurons. Following treatment of the vestibular nuclei of rats with (i) chondroitinase, (ii) sema3A (iii) chondroitinase + sema3A, or (iii) PBS (control) at P6, we observed delayed display of negative geotaxis to P12 in the case of co-treatment with (chondroitinase + sema3A) but delay was not significant in the other test cases nor in the control. The observations were reproducible for rats placed initially head-down or side-down. 2.2. Loss of WFA-positive PN around vestibular neurons was observed following chondroitinase treatment at P6. By P13, we detected return of WFA-positive PN and this lasted into adulthood. 2.3. The behavioral evidence supports the hypothesis that PN-sema3A impacts on postnatal establishment of the vestibular circuit for graviception. 2.4. A novel method for identification of PN CS sulfation pattern by HPLC has been developed. It was found that sema3A binding CS-type E increases with age. This supports specific regulation of neuronal plasticity and activity by modification of PN CS sulfation pattern.

17125115.label: Major findings and research outcome
17125115.value: 1. Condensation of PN around vestibular nucleus (VN) neurons is coincident with and essential for emergence of negative geotaxis reflex. 2. PN sequesters the plasticity molecule semaphorin 3A (sema3A) due to developmental increase in CS-type E sulfation. This prevents excessive plasticity in developing VN neurons. 3. PN has differential effect on excitatory and inhibitory neurotransmission.

17125115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125115.value: 1. We revealed the effect of sema3A on excitatory transmission (mEPSC) is in part mediated by sequestration of sema3A, but the mechanism by which PN regulates inhibitory transmission remains unclear. 2. Developmental change in PN sulfation has been characterized. Future studies will focus on how sulfation is modified in neural trauma or neurodegenerative disease.

17125115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125115.value: The surface of a subset of neurons becomes enwrapped by polysaccharide structure known as perineuronal net (PN) during developmental maturation. PN sequesters growth-promoting molecules in the brain to limit excessive growth of neurons, thereby promoting maturation of brain circuits. We demonstrate the effect of one of these molecules semaphorin 3A on maturation of vestibular circuits and resultant emergence of a vestibular reflex. This provides clues for strategies that tune plasticity of the mature brain for therapy following brain trauma or neurodegenerative disease.

17125315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125315.value: The incidence of rotator cuff tear (RCT) is more than 50% in asymptomatic individuals of older than 60 years. The mainstay of treatment is repair of the torn tendon back to bone in symptomatic patients. Despite an improvement in symptoms, it is common to find “failed healing” or “re-tear” in the rotator cuff repair site during reassessment MRI (from 25% to over 90%). The healing of rotator cuff is considered to be a significant issue to address because of this high “re-tear” rate and the natural history of continual progression of tear with time. The normal tendon-bone junction of rotator cuff insertion is a “direct enthesis”. It is composed of a transition of tissues, including bone, calcified fibrocartilage, uncalcified fibrocartilage and tendon. This direct enthesis is strong and allows gradual transition of stress during loading. This minimizes the chance of tendon rupture during activities involving rotator cuff muscle contraction. However, it was shown in majority of animal models studying rotator cuff repair that the healing in the repaired tendon-bone junction was an indirect type, i.e. mainly by formation of fibrous scar or “Sharpey-like” fiber in the interface between bone and repaired tendon. This fibrous healing is much weaker and may be a possible cause for the “re-tear” observed in clinical scenario. We developed a novel strontium enriched calcium phosphate cement (Sr-CPC) by incorporating 5% strontium into the CPC system. By applying this Sr-CPC on the surface of tendon graft, we were successful in accelerating the healing of tendon graft within the bone tunnel and reproducing the direct enthesis type of ligament-bone junction in a rabbit anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction model. The healing of graft within bone tunnel in ACL reconstruction was similar to the healing of repaired tendon in rotator cuff repair. With the success in reproducing the direct enthesis type of tendon-bone insertion in ACL reconstruction, we proceed to study the effect of local application of strontium in other surgery involving healing in the tendon-bone interface (i.e. rotator cuff repair) by augmenting the repair site with Sr-CPC. We hypothesize that local release of strontium lead to an accelerated healing of rotator cuff in the tendon-bone interface. We further hypothesis that local release of strontium results in formation of direct enthesis type of tendon-bone junction. This hypothesis is tested in a rabbit rotator cuff repair model comparing tested group (treated with Sr-CPC augmentation) and control group. Histological and biomechanical experiments are conducted. 60歲以上的患者，肩袖撕裂的發病率 約為50％以上。治療的主要方法是以外科手術修補撕裂的肌腱。儘管大部份患者的病徵得到改善，在手術後進行的磁力共振掃描中，肩袖修復部位“癒合失敗”或“再撕裂”的情況非常普遍（25％到90％）。因此，怎樣提高肩袖癒合的比率是一個重要的課題。 正常肌腱和骨骼的連接點是一種 “Direct enthesis”。它包括骨、鈣化纖維軟骨、纖維軟骨和肌腱。“Direct enthesis” 的組織減少肌腱在和骨骼的連接點斷裂的機會。 可是，在大多數肩袖修復的動物研究中，肌腱和骨骼連接點只是靠纖維瘢痕 - “Sharpey Fiber” 來癒合。這種Indirect enthesis可能就是導致肩袖修補後“再撕裂” 的主要原因。 我們通過將5％的鍶放進磷酸鈣骨水泥系統(calcium phosphate cement, CPC) 開發出一種新的含鍶磷酸鈣骨水泥（Strontium enriched calcium phosphate cement, SR-CPC）。通過使用這種含鍶磷酸鈣骨水泥，我們成功地在兔子研究中，加速前十字韌帶 (ACL)移植物在骨隧道內的癒合，並成功地重建前十字韌帶和骨連接的Direct enthesis。 前十字韌帶 (ACL)移植物在骨隧道內的癒合和肩袖修復術後肩袖在骨骼表面上的癒合是非常相似的。因此，我們決定將這種含鍶磷酸鈣骨水泥使用在肩袖修補術中。我們假設，鍶的局部釋放將會加速肩袖肌腱 - 骨界面的癒合。我們進一步假設，這種含鍶磷酸鈣骨水泥會成功地重建肩袖和骨骼連接點的的Direct enthesis。我們計劃在兔子進行這種含鍶磷酸鈣骨水泥的肩袖修補手術，術後進行組織學實驗，從而驗證我們的假設。

17125315.label: Realisation of objectives
17125315.value: The first objective was achieved. It was found that histomorphometric score was significantly higher in the experimented group (6.2 +/- 1.6) when compared with control group (3.2 +/- 1) at 12-week after index operation (p=0.03, Mann-Whitney U test). The hypothesis that local application of strontium leads to acceleration of healing of tendon-bone junction in a rabbit rotator cuff repair model when compared with a negative control was confirmed at 12-week after operation. The second objective was achieved, despite the hypothesis was rejected. At 24-week after operation, it was observed that the repaired tendon-bone junction was filled with sharpey fiber in both experiment group and control group. Tendon-fibrocartilage-calcified fibrocartilage-bone type of direct enthesis was not observed. The hypothesis that local application of strontium leads to the reproduction of direct enthesis at the tendon-bone junction of repaired rotator cuff at 24-week after index operation was rejected. A total funding of HK$ 860,722 was obtained to carry out an animal experiment on rabbit rotator cuff repair model in 60 animals to investigate the effect of local application of Strontium on tendon-bone healing in rotator cuff repair. Before starting the animal experiment, revision of project was applied and later approved for (i) reduction of number of animal used from 120 to 60 and (ii) amendment of objectives. The project was started in January 2016. Application of extension of project for six months was made before the end of 2017 and was subsequently approved. The project completion date was June 30th 2018. Rotator cuff repair was carried out in a total of 62 animals (103% of the planned number) from February 2016 to December 2017. There were six unexpected animal deaths before the time of sacrifice. The wastage due to unexpected animal death was 10%. All the other animals were sacrificed at the planned time point. However, gross dehiscence of the repair site was noted in six specimens. This dehiscence was believed to be a result of surgical error. Hence, these six specimen were excluded. The wastage due to surgical error was 10%. The total wastage of animal in this project was 20%. The remaining 50 specimens were available for analysis to compare the difference in healing of repaired rotator cuff tendon between experiment group (repair augmented with strontium enriched calcium phosphate bioactive cement) and control group (unaugmented repair) at the time point 3-week, 6-week, 12-week, 18-week and 24-week. For the control group, the average histomorphometric score were 3, 4.1, 3.2, 5.3 and 5.8 at 3-week, 6-week, 12-week, 18-week and 24-week respectively. The mode of healing was by sharpey fiber formation between the repaired tendon and the bone. For the study group, the average histomorphometric score were 2.9, 4.8, 6.2, 6.5 and 7 at 3-week, 6-week, 12-week, 18-week and 24-week respectively. The mode of healing was by sharpey fiber formation between the repaired tendon and the bone. Direct enthesis type of tendon-bone junction was not observed at the final time-point of 24-week. 3-WEEK AFTER OPERATION For the 3-week specimens, there was a gap in the tendon-bone interface. The gap was filled with fibrous connective tissue in both the control and experiment group. Sharpey fiber-like structure was only occasionally observed in some specimen. Fibrocartilage started to appear in this gap in the region near proximal humerus, indicating that new bone was formed by endochondral ossification. This observation was more obvious in the experiment group. This was postulated to be due to the osteogenesis effect of Strontium in the experiment group. The average histomorphometic scores were 3.0 +/- 1.0 and 2.9 +/- 1.8 in the control group and experiment group respectively. There was no difference between the two groups at 3-week after index surgery (p>0.05, Mann-Whitney U test). 6-WEEK AFTER OPERATION For the 6-week specimens, it was observed that there was more fibrocartilage formation. New bone formation was active in both groups. The gap became smaller. Much more sharpey fiber-like tissue could be found when compared with the 3-week group. This indicated that tendon-bone healing was in a more active stage in both groups, when compared with the 3-week specimen. The average histomorphometic scores were 4.1 +/- 2.5 and 4.8 +/- 1.5 in the control group and experiment group respectively. There was no difference between the two groups at 6-week after index surgery (p>0.05, Mann-Whitney U test). 12-WEEK AFTER OPERATION When comparing experiment group and control group, there was much more new bone and fibrocartilage formation in the experiment group at 12-week after operation. There was more osteoid deposition around the newly-formed bone. Osteoclastic resorption was also found in the region of osteoid. The gap previously filled with inflammatory cells, fibrous scar tissues were replaced by Sharpey fiber, which acted as a bridge connecting the tendon and bone. The average histomorphometric scores were 3.2 +/- 1 and 6.2 +/- 1.6 in the control group and experiment group respectively. The histolomorphometric score was significantly better in the experiment group, indicating a better healing of tendon to bone surface (p=0.03, Mann-Whitney U test). 18-WEEK AFTER OPERATION When comparing specimen taken at 18-week after operation with that at the time point of week 12, the observed difference in the repaired tendon-bone junction between the two groups decreased. The amount of fibrocartilage and new bone formation appeared to be more comparable. At 18-week after operation, evidence of direct enthesis could not be found in both groups. The repaired tendon-bone interface was filled with sharpey fiber in both groups. It demonstrated that the healing of rotator cuff to bone was by fibrous healing. The average histomorphometic scores were 5.3 +/- 0.9 and 6.5 +/- 2 in the control group and experiment group respectively. There was no difference between the two groups at 18-week after index surgery (p>0.05, Mann-Whitney U test). 24-WEEK AFTER OPERATION Remodelling was noted in the tendon-bone connection. Sharpey fiber between the healed tendon and bone were well-organized in regular array. The difference between the control and experiment group was further reduced. The average histomorphometic scores were 5.8 +/- 2 and 7 +/- 0.9 in the control group and experiment group respectively. There was no difference between the two groups at 24-week after index surgery (p>0.05, Mann-Whitney U test). HEALING OF REPAIRED TENDON AT DIFFERENT TIME POINTS When comparing histomorphometric scores of the specimens in the experiment group at different time points, significant progressive improvement in the histomorphometric scores was observed (3-week vs 12-week, p＜0.05; 3-week vs 18-week, p＜0.01; 3-week vs 24-week, p＜0.001; t-test). It showed that the rotator cuff repair augmented with local strontium healed in a more steady and efficient manner. Similar trend was not found in the control group. Considering both the time and treatment method, using two-way ANOVA statistical analysis, there was no interaction between the factors of time and treatments (p＞0.05, ANOVA) . The difference between treatments existed across the healing period indicated that the presence of Sr-CPC indeed accelerated the healing progress of rotator cuff tear (p＜0.001).

17125315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17125315.value: Local application of strontium in the form of strontium-enriched calcium phosphate cement led to acceleration of healing of tendon-bone junction in a rabbit rotator cuff repair model at 12-week after operation. The rotator cuff repair augmented by local strontium healed in a more steady and efficient manner. However, the healing was still by fibrous healing. Remodelling to direct enthesis was not observed at 24-weeks after surgery in the current rabbit rotator cuff repair model. One post-graduate student (Mr Chen Bo) was under training.

17125315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125315.value: The current research confirmed the hypothesis that local application of Strontium in the form of strontium-enriched calcium phosphate cement led to an accelerated and repeatable healing in a rabbit rotator cuff repair model, when compared with a negative control model. To ascertain the beneficial effect was due to local strontium, the experiment should be repeated by comparing the experiment group (rotator cuff repair augmented by strontium enriched calcium phosphate cement) and positive control group (rotator cuff repair augmented by calcium phosphate cement). On top of histological proof, biomechanical study should be carried out to confirm that acceleration in tendon healing by applying local strontium is associated with improvement in mechanical strength of the construct.

17125315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125315.value: The incidence of rotator cuff tear is more than 50% in subjects older than 60 years old. Rehabilitation after successful rotator cuff repair is notorious to be difficult, partly due to the fact that healing of the repaired tendon to bone takes a long period of time. Besides, the result of healing can be unpredictable. The observed rate of “failed healing” is around 15 – 20%. The result of current experiment showed that augmentation of rotator cuff repair by applying local strontium can lead to a faster and more reproducible healing of the repaired rotator cuff to bone. This may lead to a faster rehabilitation and lower rate of rotator cuff re-tear after rotator cuff repair.

17125815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125815.value: The lining of uterine cavity (endometrium) is a highly regenerative tissue which sheds and regenerates at each menstrual cycle throughout the reproductive life of women. Our group was the first to identify stem cells in human and mouse endometrium. These cells are rare cells in the endometrium and are believed to be responsible for the endometrial regeneration. It is well-accepted that the microenvironment surrounding the endometrial stem cells (stem cell niche) decides whether they should divide to replicate themselves or differentiate into mature endometrial cells that form the bulk of the endometrium. The actions of the niche on the stem cells can be mediated by direct contact between the endometrial stem cells and their neighbouring niche cells, and by components of the microenvironment, including soluble factors presented by the niche cells. The details of the regulatory process of the endometrial niche on stem cell fate remain unclear. We and others have localized the endometrial stem cells to the lower basalis layer of the endometrium, which is next to the uterine muscle termed myometrium. Our preliminary data showed that the myometrial cells stimulated proliferation of the endometrial stem cells and their ability to form colonies in low cell density culture. Furthermore, the observed actions are mediated by soluble secretory factors from the myometrial cells. We have provisionally identified a few myometrial cells derived candidate molecules that could be responsible for the observations. It is logical that the intimate interaction between the endometrial stem cells at the basal endometrial layer and the myometrium regulates the behaviour of the endometrial stem cells. The hypothesis of this project is that secretory factors from the myometrial cells modulate the activities of the endometrial stem cells. The aim of the project is to identify and characterize the myometrial cells derived molecules involved in regulating the endometrial stem cell activities. The results of the project will enable us to better understand the niche composition and the signals within the uterine microenvironment regulating the functions of the endometrial stem cells. The research will open new avenues for recreating or stimulating the uterine microenvironment for proper expansion of the endometrial stem cells and control of their biological activities in vitro and in vivo. The results will be useful for both basic biological study and endometrial tissue engineering. 子宮腔內層（子宮內膜）是一種具備高度更新能力的組織，子宮內膜在女性育齡期的每個月經週期都會發生脫落和更新。我們研究組最先在人類和小鼠子宮內膜中發現幹細胞的存在。子宮內膜幹細胞的數目雖少，但被認為是主導內膜更新的因素。 通常認為子宮內膜幹細胞周圍的微環境決定了幹細胞是進行細胞分裂以自我複製或者分化到成熟內膜細胞以組成內膜的基本成分。幹細胞微環境對幹細胞的作用是通過內膜幹細胞與微環境細胞直接調控，包括微環境細胞釋放的可溶性因子而進行的。子宮內膜幹細胞的微環境如何調控幹細胞的命運仍然未知。 我們和其他研究組的研究發現子宮內膜幹細胞位於內膜的基底層，接近子宮肌層。我們的前期研究也顯示子宮肌層細胞促進內膜幹細胞的增殖和在低密度培養條件下形成克隆的能力。並且這些特點是由子宮肌層細胞釋放的可溶性因子來介導的。目前我們已經從子宮肌層細胞中發現一些可溶性因子可能在介導內膜幹細胞的活性中有作用。 因此，我們認為子宮內膜基底層的幹細胞和肌層細胞之間的相互作用可以調節內膜幹細胞的生物學行為。本課題的設想是肌層細胞釋放的可溶性因子能調節內膜幹細胞的生物學活性。本課題的目標是確定並研究肌層細胞釋放的具備調節內膜幹細胞活性作用的可溶性因子的特點。 本課題的研究結果能幫助我們更佳地瞭解調節內膜幹細胞功能的微環境的組成和分子信號的信息。本研究將為通过體內和體外提供和刺激子宫微环境而調控內膜干细胞增殖方面的研究开创新途径。本課題的結果將有益於基礎生物學研究和子宮內膜組織工程學的研究。

17125815.label: Realisation of objectives
17125815.value: Adult stem cells are rare cells in the adult tissue. They undergo self-renewal and differentiation into tissue-specific mature cells important in tissue repair. It is generally accepted that the fate of the adult stem cells is strongly influenced by their surrounding microenvironment known as stem cell niche. The governing principle is that stem cell fate decisions are primarily affected by direct interaction between the adult stem cells and their neighbouring niche cells and by components of the niche microenvironment, including soluble factors and signals presented by the niche cells. However, the details of the regulatory process of the niche microenvironment on adult stem cell fate are unclear In humans, a subpopulation of endometrial mesenchymal-like stem cells (eMSCs), which co-express CD140b and CD146, are located in perivascular regions and mainly in the lower layer of the endometrium next to the muscle layer of the uterus (myometrium). In this project, we propose that the myometrial cells are one of the niche components regulating eMSC activities. Objective 1: To determine the role of myometrial cells on the clonogenicity and proliferation of endometrial mesenchymal stem-like cells. To determine if myometrial cells can regulate eMSC, co-culture experiments using both cell types were conducted (direct and indirect contact). Using various functional assays, it was found that some of the stem cell properties of eMSCs (i.e. proliferation and self-renewal activity) were enhanced after co-culture with myometrial cells. Coculture of eMSCs with human myometrial cells at different ratios revealed that myometrial cells stimulated the clonogenicity of eMSCs at a cell-density-dependent manner. Coculture with myometrial cells significantly increased the proportion of CD140b+CD146+ cells in eMSCs using flow cytometry. eMSCs co-cultured with human myometrial cells displayed similar multipotency as mono-cultured cells. They were able to differentiate the four mesenchymal lineages: myogenic, osteogenic, adipogenic and chondrogenic lineages when cultured under specific induction medium. Our data demonstrated that direct contact of eMSCs and myometrial cells was not essential and that secretory soluble factors alone can sufficiently maintain eMSCs. Using time lapse microscopy to study the cell cycle of eMSCs, it was found that soluble factors derived from myometrial cells can increase the frequency and rate of division. The cell type specificity of the observed effect on eMSCs was assessed by using cell lines derived from human skeletal muscle cells, human cardiomyocytes, mouse skeletal muscle cells and human endometrial stromal cells. Unexpectedly, skeletal muscle cell and cardiac muscle cells have similar effect in stimulating self-renewal of eMSCs. It is possible that these muscle cells secrete common factor(s) for eMSC maintenance. An alternate possibility is that different factors from various muscle cells exert the same effect on eMSCs. Since the human myometrium is the physiological eMSC niche component, the search for the candidate secretory factor(s) focused on myometrial cells. The temporal effect of myometrial cells on the clonogenicity and proportion of eMSCs was also evaluated. It was found that the effect was stronger in the second week of culture for the formation of colonies and self-renewal of eMSCs when compare to the first week alone. Objective 2: To determine the role of Wnt signaling in the myometrial cells-induced increase in clonogenicity and proliferation of endometrial mesenchymal stem-like cells. To determine the role of Wnt signaling in the observed phenomena, we firstly evaluated the expression of active β-catenin with western blotting and immunofluorescence. The expression of active β-catenin in eMSCs was significantly higher than that of the monoculture. Consistently, treatment of myometrial CCM increased the TCF/LEF transcriptional activity of eMSCs. Loss-of-function using XAV939 or IWP-2 decreased the clonogenicity and phenotypic expression of eMSCs. Whereby, gain-of-function using Wnt3A CM or recombinant Wnt3A protein supported the proliferation and self-renewal of eMSCs. Next, we determined the expression of a comprehensive panel of Wnt/β-catenin signaling-related genes in myometrial cells using real-time PCR Taqman Array. Wnt5A was found to be the highest expressing ligand in myometrial cells. To determine whether Wnt5A was responsible for the stimulatory action, we functionally neutralized the effect with the antibody against Wnt5A and found to reduce the cloning efficiency, percentage of eMSCs and the TCF/LEF luciferase activity. The expression of active β-catenin was also decreased. Using immunofluorescent staining, coexpression of frizzled 4 (FZD4) and low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 5 (LRP5) was found to be expressed in eMSCs. The LRP component was biologically active, as eMSCs responded to DKK-1, a secreted Wnt antagonist that binds to LRP5/6 Wnt co-receptor. DKK-1 reduced the number of colonies and the proportion of eMSCs. The role of FZD4 in Wnt5A induced Wnt signal was assessed by knock down of FZD4-siRNA. The treatment reduced the myometrial CCM induction of TCF/LEF luciferase activity when compared to the siRNA. Similarly, the recombinant Wnt5A induced increase in TCF/LEF luciferase activity was abolished upon treatment of eMSCs with FZD4-siRNA. Furthermore, the contribution of the non-canonical Wnt pathway was investigated. Our finding demonstrate that the non-canonical Wnt/planar cell polarity (PCP) and the Wnt/calcium pathway were not involved in the observed activities of myometrial cell coculture by using western blot and inhibition of the Wnt/PCP pathway using SP600125. Objective 3: To study the actions of myometrial cell-derived matrix metalloproteinase 3 (MMP3) on clonogenicity and proliferation of the endometrial mesenchymal stem-like cells. Beside Wnt/β-catenin signaling, other molecules may also contribute to the observed effect in myometrial CCM. MMP3 was identified as a secretory molecule of the myometrial cells. We postulate the observed action of MMP3 is via the interaction with Wnt5b, hence the action of these molecules on eMSCs were examined. We found there was no change in the formation of colonies or phenotypic expression of eMSCs markers after the addition of MMP3 recombinant protein. Neutralization of MMP3 using antibody or siRNA significantly suppressed colony formation but not able to reduce the eMSC population suggesting a role of MMP3 in proliferation activity. We also examined the effect of cytokines on MMP3 secretion and found pro-inflammatory cytokines (i.e. IL-1β and TNF-α) could significantly increase the MMP3 secretion, protein and mRNA expression in myometrial cells. Therefore, certain cytokines can act directly on myometrial cells to regulate the MMP3 secretion. Wnt5b protein expression was detected in the cell lysate and conditioned medium of myometrial cells. Exogenous Wnt5b did not increase the expression of eMSC markers. However, neutralization of Wnt5b could suppress the eMSC population in vitro, implying the involvement of myometrial derived Wnt5b in stem cell self-renewal. This finding further strengthens the role of Wnt signaling in regulating stem cells in the human endometrium.

17125815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17125815.value: Understanding the regulation of stem cell niche is challenging due to rarity of adult stem cells within the tissue. In this proposal, the following outcome was achieved: In vitro co-culture of myometrial cells with eMSCs enhanced the colony forming and self-renewal abilities of eMSCs when compared with culture of eMSC alone. The coculture effects were observed even when there was no direct contact between the myometrial cells and the eMSCs, indicating that the myometrial cells derived secretory factor(s) were responsible for maintaining the stem cell properties of eMSCs in vitro, including expression of endometrial mesenchymal stem cell phenotypic markers, short and long-term expansion and multipotency (Abstract 2019). The temporal effect of myometrial cells on the clonogenicity and proportion of eMSCs were evaluated. Our data show the effect was stronger in the second week of culture for the formation of colonies and self-renewal of eMSCs when compared to that in the first week alone. Hence, stem cell replication occurs in the second week of culture. Secretory factors associated with the activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling promoted eMSC proliferation and self-renewal. Wnt5A was found to be the candidate molecule based on: (a) Wnt5A was among the highly expressed Wnt ligands in primary human myometrial cells; (b) anti-Wnt5A antibody reduced the stimulatory action of myometrial CCM on colony formation, self-renewal, and TCF/LEF transcriptional activities of eMSCs; and (c) recombinant Wnt5A protein increased the formation of colonies and phenotypic expression of eMSCs (Cao et al., Stem Cells, 2019). We further demonstrated expression of Wnt receptor - FZD4 and co-receptor - LRP5 in eMSCs (Li T, Master of Medical Science dissertation). Thus, Wnt5A can activate the Wnt canonical depending on the receptor context. Wnt5b could stimulate the proliferation and self-renewal of eMSCs - this may also be a potential stem cell regulator (Cheng C, MPhil Thesis). Using centrifugal filter devices, liquid chromatography, SDS-PAGE and mass spectrometry analysis, MMP3 was one of the proteins identified in the spent medium of myometrial cells. Neutralization of MMP3 suppressed for the formation of colonies, implying this molecule may play a role in stem cell proliferation (Abstract 2016, 2017). During inflammatory events, cytokines such as IL-1β and TNF-α may modulate the MMP3 secretion in myometrial cells to enable eMSCs for the regeneration of the human endometrium (Abstract 2016, 2017).

17125815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17125815.value: Currently there are no good methods for eMSCs expansion without differentiation in vitro because we are unclear about the regulation of their proliferation, self-renewal and differentiation. The secretory factors produced from the myometrial cells offer a specialized microenvironment for human eMSCs. By gaining a better understanding of the niche composition and the signals within the uterine microenvironment, it will be possible to recreate a milieu for stem cell expansion and control their in vitro biological activities. Since we now have supporting evidence that Wnt/β-catenin signaling is a prominent candidate for stem cell regulation in human endometrium. Besides Wnt5A and Wnt5b, we propose other Wnt ligands or Wnt agonist may also participate in stem cell regulation. The Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway was mainly focused in this project. However, the interplay between adult stem cell and their niche are highly dynamic and complex in vivo. Therefore, future studies should explore other signaling pathways (i.e. Notch signaling, TGF-β signaling) which may also modulate the stem cell fate in human endometrium.

17125815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125815.value: Little is known about the local niche signals of endometrial stem cells self-renewal. The microenvironment surrounding the endometrial stem cells decides whether they should divide to replicate themselves or differentiate into mature endometrial cells that form the bulk of the endometrium. Aside from niche cells, local paracrine signals within the microenvironment are important in maintaining stem cells. Our findings showed that secretory soluble factors from myometrial-cells modulate the activities of endometrial stem cells. The biological actions of Wnt activators and inhibitors together with the presence of appropriate receptors are in line with a functional role of Wnt signaling on eMSCs proliferation and self-renewal.

17126115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126115.value: 背景：根據牙列所處的發育階段可估計個體成熟度和年齡。在此基礎上，倫敦牙齡研究資訊組近期建立了有效可靠的年齡估計方法。該方法根據已建立的參考數據庫，應用數學模型和定義清晰的牙龄發育標準估計個體年齡，其可靠性和有效性已經過驗證。多個研究中心已經成立並致力於建立國際各人種的牙龄參考數據庫，以供研究者和相關機構使用。本研究組致力於在亞洲首次建立中國南方人種牙齡參考數據庫。目前，該數據庫已經過驗證並被證明適用於中國北方人群和日本東南地區人群。 關鍵問題：近年來關於牙龄分析的研究越來越多，這是因為需要估計年齡的法醫學案件增多。在香港，每年超過1000例的非法移民（多來自東南亞和中國大陸）僞造身份文件。對於類似案件，香港尚無系統化的年齡分析方法來證明移民年齡。東南亞地區接近地球板塊交界處，頻繁發生的地震和火山災害對當地人民造成了影響。自然災害時期的身份認證問題及東南亞國家獨特的社會經濟因素造成很多兒童無出生記錄。這些問題造成了人權侵害事件頻發，包括童工，兒童新娘，人口販賣等。牙龄分析（DAA）有助於證明兒童的年齡，使這些兒童獲得正式身份認證并獲得相應國家的社會和法律保護。然而，牙龄分析在東南亞地區實施困難，因爲在每個國家建立民族特異性參考數據庫需納入大量具有代表性樣本，並使用標準的方法學。近期基因研究表明東亞地區多數人種是由中國南方人種發展而來，東南亞人群表現了中國南方人種的常見表型。因此，中國南方人種牙齡參考數據庫對於東南亞人群的適用性具有研究價值，並且該研究對於國内外東南亞人群具有普遍意義。 目的：中國南方人種參考數據庫及牙龄分析方法對於東南亞五個不同地理位置人群的適用性。 研究計畫：從東南亞地區的合作機構選取2160例牙科放射線片，根據中國南方人種參考數據庫估算參試者個體年齡（5至22嵗）。應用具備靈敏檢驗能力的統計方法比較各年齡/性別參試者的牙龄和實際年齡（金標准），以確定中國南方人種牙齡參考數據庫對於東南亞人種的適用性。 研究意義：關於東南亞人種恆牙列成熟度分析較少，本研究所得牙齒發育數據有助於東南亞人種恆牙列成熟度的研究和分析。數據庫得到驗證后可用于臨床治療參考。該牙龄分析法可用於人類學及考古學研究，也可廣泛應用於民事，法律，刑事和法醫學鑒定上，並可推薦應用于香港入境事務處和律政司，以及聯合國人道主義事務協調辦公室。

17126115.label: Realisation of objectives
17126115.value: # How the project objectives have been achieved: 1. Preparation for realization of the objective The accuracy of estimated age depends on the reference data sets (RDS) from which the maturity scores or ages of attainment were obtained. We therefore tested the accuracy of age estimation from three different population specific dental RDS first (Paper 2). Two hundred and sixty six dental panoramic radiographs of subjects belonging to southern Chinese ethnicity were scored and dental age (DA) was estimated from three RDS: French-Canadian, United Kingdom (UK) Caucasian and southern Chinese. The difference between the chronological age (CA) and DA using the French Canadian RDS was -0.62 years for males and -0.36 years for females. For the UK Caucasian RDS, the age difference was 0.25 years for males and 0.23 years for females. The difference observed using the southern Chinese RDS was -0.02 years for both genders and the difference was not statistically significant (p>0.05). The southern Chinese RDS estimated the age of 80% of subjects within ± 12 months range, and 90% of subjects within ± 18 months range (p<0.05) showing it to be more accurate than other datasets (Paper 2). To further examine the accuracy of the Chinese RDS, 320 subjects with and without supernumerary teeth (ST) (Paper 4), and 668 subject with various growth trajectories and growth rates (Paper 3) were recruited in this project, respectively. The estimated age difference (CA-DA) was 0.10 years for boys and 0.19 years for girls with ST, whilst 0.01 years and 0.05 years for boys and girls without ST (p>0.05). Since no significant difference was observed in the dental development of children with and without ST, we concluded that the presence of ST does not affect the accuracy of the southern Chinese RDS (Paper 4). However, we found that growth had a continuous impact on dental development (p < 0.01) (Paper 3). We thus adjusted the Chinese RDS for use in the following procedures. 2. Sample selection We have conducted blind studies to test the applicability of the southern Chinese RDS in samples from Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, the Philippines, and Indonesia. The most recent dental panoramic tomographs (DPTs) of subjects in the age range from 5 to 22 years were used. For each age and gender group, 12 subjects were randomly selected from the archives of the local dental hospitals. Good-quality DPTs with the full set of dental health-related information, including date of birth, gender, ethnicity, medical and dental histories, radiographs, diagnoses and treatments were obtained. Written consent were obtained from every patient before his/her treatment in these dental hospitals. The subjects were selected from the most recent patient list (within five years) using a systematic random sampling method. Starting with the highest patient code number (the most recently registered patient), this patient and then every other patient were sequentially selected until the desired sample size was obtained. The patient’s records were examined for the inclusion and exclusion criteria. The DPTs that were taken previously for diagnostic purposes were re-used in this study. In order to cover the developmental stages of all the permanent teeth, 18 age groups of patients aged from 5 to 22 years were selected (5 years ≤ age group 1 < 6 years; 6 years ≤ age group 2 < 7 years;…; 22 years ≤ age group 18 < 23 years). For each age group, 12 females and 12 males were recruited, yielding a total of 432 subjects from each country. Inclusion criteria • Healthy subjects of the target ethnic group, with both parents belonging to the same ethnicity • Subjects in the target age range with proper age documentation Exclusion criteria • Systemic diseases or syndromes that would affect the skeletal and dental growth • Localised oral pathology, anomalies or impacted teeth that would affect the dental growth • Severe malocclusion • Congenitally missing permanent teeth • Premature loss of permanent teeth • Previous or current orthodontic treatment • DPT of a poor quality, in which one or more targeted teeth cannot be scored Ethical approval for this study was obtained from the Institutional Review Board of the University of Hong Kong - West cluster Hospital authority (IRB No.UW 12-280). 3. Data collection Participants’ DPTs and their personal information related to age (date of birth and date when the DPT was taken) and ethnicity were collected from the existing records by a research assistant using the same protocol. The DPTs were assigned a code, scanned at a resolution of 300 dpi in grey-scale format, and stored as a JPEG image with dimensions of 2440 x 1280 pixels (Epson scanner 1000XL, Epson Inc, USA). The CA and ethnicity data were stored separately from the DPT data. The digitised DPTs and the participants’ ages and ethnic information collected were brought to the Hong Kong centre for scoring and analysis. Two trained and calibrated examiners evaluated the DPTs. 4. Data processing All the left maxillary and mandibular permanent teeth plus the 2 third molars on the right side (18 teeth per subject) were scored based on Demirjian’s classification of tooth developmental stages. The DA of each subject was then estimated using the established southern Chinese reference data set for age estimation. For each subject, based on the gender, the mean age and standard error were obtained for the corresponding stage of development for each specific tooth from the southern Chinese RDS. The mean and standard error values obtained from the database were transported to STATA (Stata Corp, Version 9.0, 2005) and the weighted average was calculated using the meta-analysis command. Ten percent of the DPTs were randomly selected using the random numbers generated electronically, and the tooth developmental stages were re-evaluated to test the inter-examiner and intra-examiner reliabilities. 5. Statistical analysis The distribution of the differences between the estimated dental age and chronological age were tested for normality using the Shapiro-Wilk. The two-tailed paired t-test, Pearson’s correlation coefficient, and the agreement assessment technique described by Bland and Altman were used to compare the estimated dental age and the chronological age (gold standard) for each subject in each age/gender group of the Southeast Asian sample to examine the applicability of the southern Chinese RDS and the age estimation method developed by the Dental Age Research London Information Group. The method is regarded as valid (within the range of accuracy) if the p value is greater than 0.05 in the paired t-test, the r value of Pearson’s correlation coefficient is between ±0.9 and ±1.0 (p<0.001), and at least 95% of the points on the Bland and Altman scatterplot are within difference magnitudes of ±0.5 years. The inter-examiner and intra-examiner reliabilities for assessing a developmental stage of each tooth on the DPT were tested using the weighted Kappa, with Cicchetti-Allison weights. # To what extent the project objectives have been achieved: The project objective has been completely achieved. # Give reason for under-achievements and outline attempts to overcome problems, if any: Nil.

17126115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126115.value: # Potential for further development of the research: Results from this study show that the DA estimation method based on southern Chinese RDS had different performances across the different samples tested. The method consistently overestimated the age of the five East Asian population groups. It is unclear whether population differences in dental maturity amongst global populations are due to genetic, environmental or methodological factors. A better understanding of variation in dental maturation patterns would require a finer level of analysis and consideration of other factors, such as socioeconomic status, other potential sources of variation in tooth formation timing, sample composition, as well as a more diverse set of test samples. # Proposed course of action: This study aimed to test the applicability of the southern Chinese dental maturation RDS on five East Asian population groups. If it is found applicable, the southern Chinese RDS can be recommended for use in the respective population groups. In the event that the southern Chinese RDS is unsuitable, a RDS for specific population groups would need to be developed. Based on our results we recommended that the southern Chinese RDS can be use in the five East Asian population groups with minor adjustments.

17126115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126115.value: Southeast Asian is one of the most disaster-prone areas in the world. Southeast Asian people are frequently affected by various forms of natural disasters including volcanic eruption, earthquake, typhoon, landslide and flood. Moreover, latest statistics from the United Nations Children’s Fund states that not all children in the area have their births registered. Dental age estimation can assist in the identification of victims following natural disasters and it can also help to solve birth date disputes in individuals involved in criminal activities. A reference dataset has been developed in Hong Kong from the dental development of thousands of subjects of southern Han Chinese origin and subsequently validated. This study sought to test the applicability of this reference data set for age estimation in five other East Asian populations, namely Vietnam, Thailand, Cambodia, the Philippines, and Indonesia. Based on the results of this study, it is recommended that this reference data set can be use in the five East Asian population groups with minor adjustments. This study provides much needed test of the cross-population applicability of dental age estimation methods and significant information to aid experts in making decisions about the methods they should employ in forensic and legal circumstances.

17126615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126615.value: Intervertebral discs (IVD) are the major skeletal joints of the spinal column that provides motion function and acts as shock absorbers for the body. IVDs can undergo degeneration, and consequently structural deformity, which may lead to back pain and sciatica. This causes a significant loss of work hours and disability. IVD degeneration is associated with a loss of function of its gelatinous core, the nucleus pulposus (NP). Regeneration of the NP with native biological properties is therefore important for the re-establishment of IVD function, and may reduce the clinical impact of the degeneration and pain incidence. To date, however, it is still not clear how the recovery of the NP cells can be effectively promoted in the degenerated disc or how they can be properly bioengineered. We have recently demonstrated the existence of NP progenitors from human and monkey IVDs, and found that a loss of their activities is associated with IVD degeneration in humans. By profiling of the transcriptome of the NP cells and subsequent validation in vivo, we identified a putative marker panel for the NP progenitors. Our data further suggest that inhibiting MAP-kinase activity during chondrogenic induction can direct adult mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) towards a lineage with upregulated expression of these markers. We propose that this platform, which we term MICCI (MAP-kinase Interference Coupled Chondrogenic Induction), may provide unique insights into future programming of NP progenitors to facilitate IVD regeneration or engineering. In this proposal, we hypothesize that MICCI may induce adult MSCs into an NP progenitor-like state. To address this hypothesis, we will examine the properties of MICCI-derived cells and test their function in IVD repair. Moreover, we will investigate how different MSC sub-populations respond to MICCI for a better understanding of the differentiation platform. Overall, this investigation may promote our understanding of NP cell biology and facilitate stem cell-based engineering of NP progenitors and consequently the mature forms of NP cells. The findings will aid in the future development of IVD bioengineering or regeneration strategies. 17126615.label: Realisation of objectives
17126615.value: The mechanical function of the intervertebral disc is attributed to the integrity of the nucleus pulposus (NP). However, bioengineering of authentic NP cells remains a challenge. Our previous transcriptome analysis implied that primitive rat NP tissue has a lower activity of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAP kinase) components and TGF-β signaling relative to cartilage (data unpublished). Expression study in methylcellulose cultured NP cell colony suggested CDH2 and GALNT3 are novel markers of disc progenitors in addition to collagen II, aggrecan, and Tie2. Our pilot study further suggested that inhibiting MEK1/2 activity during TGF-β-based chondrogenic induction of bone marrow mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) may have a potential to induce a phenotype resembling NP cells. We termed this process “MAP-kinase Interference Coupled Chondrogenic Induction” or MICCI. In this project, we aimed to consolidate and gain more understanding of this process so as to seek its implications in disc engineering and regeneration. We completed Objective 1 and examined the properties of the MICCI process and its derived cells. To validate if MSCs undergo an NP cell-like differentiation process under MICCI, we isolated bone marrow MSCs from 13 human subjects receiving scoliosis correction and characterized their differentiation potential. We conducted a chondropellet culture study with these MSCs in presence of 10ng/ml TGF-β1 with or without 10uM MEK1/2 inhibitor. Inhibition of MEK1/2 phosphorylation induced by TGF-β1 was confirmed by Western blot analysis. We examined the gene expression of matrix and committed NP cell markers (both published and deduced from transcriptome study in-house) at day 0, 1, 7, 14, and 21. Consistent with the hypothesis, we observed an upregulation of disc matrix collagen II (COL2A1) and aggrecan (ACAN) gene expression in the MEK inhibition group. However, significant variation of modulation among the different lines of MSCs was observed. We speculated this may be due to genetic variation among subjects, or the MSC lines contain various amounts of certain cell subpopulations responsive to the differentiation. Otherwise it may be related to suboptimal TGF-β1 dosage. Growth factors are known to exert distinct regulation at different concentrations. We tested the effects of MEK inhibitor under low (1ng/ml) and high (10ng/ml) dosages of TGF-β1. At both dosages, we observed a significant induction of COL2A1 and ACAN in MICCI induced differentiation, compared to TGF-β1 alone. Committed NP cell marker genes CD24 and KRT19 were induced at late stage of MICCI induced differentiation (Day 14 and Day 21). Putative progenitor markers CDH2 and GALNT3 were upregulated in MICCI-induced differentiation at early stage (Day 1 and Day 7) when compared to the TGF-β1 group. NP progenitor marker TEK (encoded for Tie2) was progressively reduced with time during MICCI induced differentiation. Taken together, MICCI may promote NP-cell like differentiation and the time-course results implied gradual enrichment of disc progenitors to committed cells. There appeared no significant difference in overall differentiation performance at high or low TGF-β1 dosage. Because MEK1/2 inhibition regulated the putative progenitor markers in MICCI induced differentiation process, we tested if TGF-β1 can promote the formation of colony formation unit-spheroid (CFU-S) in methylcellulose culture which is indicative of progenitor activity. Interestingly, TGF-β1 could increase CFU-S formation in both degenerative and non-degenerative human NP cells. The increase was inhibited in the presence of MEK inhibitor. No significant changes of CFU-S formation with MEK inhibition alone. On the other hand, TGF-β inhibitor could abolish CFU-S formation. These findings therefore suggested that TGF-β signaling is critical to promote an activation of dormant progenitors to proliferate, and the activation depends on MEK1/2 activity. Based on the course of gene expression changes, we propose a hierarchy of differentiation, in which dormant stem/progenitor cells (Tie2+) were activated as proliferative progenitors (positive for GD2, CDH2, GALNT3) and eventually differentiated into a committed phenotype (positive for COL2A1, ACAN, CD24, KRT19). Overall, our findings implied that enrichment of progenitors and differentiation into NP-like cells are coupled to MEK kinase signaling. To gain a more understanding of the progenitor-like phenotype of human NP cell subpopulations, we also attempted to fractionate the different cell units in the methylcellulose. Marker expression in three cell populations isolated from the methylcellulose cultured adult human NP cells at day 14 by their size and plastic adhering capacity was profiled. These include floating sphere-like units (FSP), attached fibroblast-like cells (AFP) and floating single cells (SP). The expression level of various markers related to stem cells (Nanog and Grem1), disc progenitors (Tie2) and mature NP cells (COL2A1) signatures was investigated in these three subpopulations by RT-PCR. The expression profile implicated that FSP is more progenitor-like compared to the AFP or SP, supporting the progenitor activity of NP cell-derived CFU-S. In the original plan, we aimed to identify the potential MSC subpopulations involved in the MICCI differentiation by testing the effect of cell sorting using selected surface markers (CD146, CD49f, CD271) (Objective 2). The identification is considered an important step for enrichment of target cells to be used in disc repair evaluation (Objective 3). However, because of the observed significant variation of MSC lines in MICCI differentiation efficiency and that treatment with a different dosage of TGF-β1 showed no significant difference in expression of the markers, we considered a necessity of understanding and optimizing the differentiation in a more robust manner. Rushing into an in vivo functional test with yet to be defined or unenriched cells would also be inappropriate. With the recent acquisition of 10X Genomic platform in our institution, we determined that studying single cell transcriptome is a more effective and comprehensive strategy than the proposed cell sorting method, which is based on educated guess, to identify the involved cell subpopulations. Moreover, single cell transcriptomics enables deduction of differentiation pathway through analysis of lineage trajectory. We therefore reallocated the resource of cell sorting and animal study to single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) as a follow-up investigation. Based on the gene expression findings from the MICCI-derived chondropellet study and remained budget, we selected two timepoints of the differentiation for scRNA-seq: Day 1 timepoint as an enrichment stage of active NP-like progenitors based on an increased expression of putative progenitor markers CDH2 and GALNT3, and Day 14 timepoint as late differentiation stage with an increased expression of NP-committed markers COL2A1, ACAN, CD24, and KRT19. We adopted a cell release protocol by enzymatic digestion which enabled retrieval of >80% viable single cells. Gene expression profiling of the released cells confirmed an expression pattern similar to that of findings from previous MICCI-derived pellet study. We observed a lower cell yield from chondropellets at Day 14, possibly due to incomplete digestions of cell-cell contact or extracellular matrix, particularly in disassembly of collagen II-positive progenitor cell clusters in the pellet. We tested a range of incubation time for pronase and collagenase digestion to optimize the single cell isolation from the pellets. scRNA-seq data will be obtained from the submitted samples and analysis is expected to complete in coming 3 months. Focus of analysis will be put on pseudotime analysis to study cell state transition and identifying which MSC subpopulations are related to the differentiation.

17126615.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126615.value: 1. Primitive nucleus pulposus (NP) showed a lower MAP kinase activity and TGF-β signaling relative to cartilage. In a TGF-β induced MSC chondropellet system, nucleopulpogenic differentiation process was observed under MEK inhibition. Expression profiling implicated an induction of NP progenitor-like markers at early stage (Day1), and committed markers at late stage (Day14). Differentiation efficiency showed significant variation among different MSC lines and appeared independent on TGF-β dosage. 2. In a methylcellulose culture system, TGF-β1 promoted activation of dormant NP progenitor cells proliferation to form CFU-S, whereas MEK inhibition could attenuate the TGF-β induced CFU-S formation. This suggested that NP progenitor proliferation or activity is coupled to TGF-β1 mediated MEK kinase signaling. 3. NP cells cultured in methylcellulose displayed at least three distinct populations: floating sphere-like, attached fibroblast-like, and single cell populations. The floating sphere-like population express the highest levels of progenitor markers. 4. Single cell release from the MICCI derived chondropellets could be achieved by enzymatic digestion for scRNA-seq study. Using 300U of collagenase II digestion per chondropellet (2x105 cells), ~ 9x104 single cells/pellet could be harvested at Day 1 and ~2.4 x104 cells/pellet at Day 14. Induction of progenitor markers as early as Day 1 and committed NP markers at Day 14 was confirmed by bulk expression analysis. 5. Findings have been published in form of abstracts, posters and podium talks in a number of major international conferences. We aim to publish the work in refereed scientific journals upon completion of scRNA-seq analysis. Altogether, our study indicates that activity of human NP progenitor cells is dependent on TGF-β via MEK kinase signaling, while MEK kinase inhibition can on the other hand promote TGF-β mediated differentiation into a committed phenotype. Forthcoming scRNA-seq analysis in the MICCI-derived MSCs chondropellets will further provide important insights into the control of the differentiation.

17126615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126615.value: Our study showed that, by manipulating TGF-β1/ MEK kinase activity, dormant cells may be activated to proliferate and that MSCs can differentiate into NP-like cells. It has been proposed that an ERK-dependent feedback mechanism prevents haematopoietic stem cell exhaustion via AKT/mTOR signaling to balance quiescence and differentiation. (Baumgartner, C. et al. 2018 Cell Stem Cell 22, 879,892) By further in silico analysis of the time-series scRNA-seq data in MICCI-mediated differentiation, the responsible subpopulations into NP-like cells, and the phenotypes of the differentiated cells in the process can be characterized in detail. In addition, a cross-comparison with a recently established transcriptome dataset of native human NP cells and pluripotent stem cells derived NP-like cells (by collaborator Prof. K Cheah and Dr. Q Lian, HKU) can be performed to define the influential transcriptional programs involved. To gain insight into the underlying mechanism, we can utilize gene editing tools to create mutants of the influential components in human NP cells and investigate their function in regulating the differentiation program. These findings also implicate a possibility of modifying disc degeneration using small molecule inhibitors to regulate TGF-β and MEK signaling.

17126615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126615.value: Intervertebral disc (IVD) degeneration is an age-related disorder resulting in low back pain and disability. The core of IVD, the nucleus pulposus (NP), plays critical roles in the health and maintenance of the disc. This study aims to investigate the feasibility of deriving progenitors and mature form of NP cells from adult stem cells via manipulating TGF-β1/MEK kinase signaling. Conventional management is limited to pain-relief, in particular by surgery where disc excision and intervertebral fusion is performed to immobilize the degenerated spinal segment. Disc repair via stem cell therapy or stimulation by trophic factors has been investigated with limited efficacy. In this study, we tested the function of TGF-β1/ MEK kinase in activation of progenitors and directing adult stem cells into NP-like cells and examined the property of the differentiated products. The findings should facilitate not only the generation of effective strategy for NP engineering, but also understanding of the underlying biology of renewal and propagation of disc progenitors. Ultimately the understanding of such molecular cues may be harnessed for IVD regeneration or engineering to benefit low back pain patients.

17127015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127015.value: Stroke is one of the leading causes of death and disability in Hong Kong and worldwide. Ischemic stroke is caused by the blockage of the cerebral artery resulting in an insufficient supply of glucose and oxygen to brain, which initiates a cascade of cellular events leading to cell death. The cellular responses to brain injury are critical for the fate of neurons. Treatments for ischemic stroke, especially those that confer neuroprotection to delay cell death, are still lacking. Previous studies to identify neuronal responses to ischemic insult identified intracellular transport as a potential target for neuroprotection, but the underlying mechanisms are still unknown. N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR)-mediated excitotoxicity is a critical factor in ischemic provoked neurodegeneration. Our preliminary work showed that decreased levels of Kinesin-1, a microtubule-dependent molecular motor, conferred neuroprotection by altering extrasynaptic distribution of NMDAR and its functioning during ischemic stroke. We found that Kif5b, the heavy chain of Kinesin-1, was down-regulated by ischemic preconditioning. A 50% reduction of the Kif5b level protected the neurons against ischemic provoked neurodegeneration through extrasynaptic NMDAR hypofunction. Furthermore, we have shown that Kinesin-1 forms a complex with NMDAR. Decreasing the Kinesin-1 level reduced the formation of this Kinesin-1/NMDAR complex in vivo. This prevented NMDAR from concentrating at extrasynaptic sites, which inhibited calcium influx mediated by extrasynaptic NMDAR activation to confer neuroprotection. These results strongly suggest that Kinesin-1/NMDAR interaction is important in neurodegeneration and that specific disruption of the Kinesin-1/NMDAR interaction may postpone or halt neurodegeneration. In this proposed project, we plan to characterize in detail the Kinesin-1/NMDAR interaction, with the aim to lay the foundations for specific modulation of the Kinesin-1/NMDAR interaction for novel neuroprotective strategies. 在香港和世界各地，中風是死亡和殘疾的的主要原因之一。缺血性中風是由腦動脈從而導致供給葡萄糖和氧的不足，进而啟動細胞事件導致細胞死亡。腦損傷中細胞反應性的决定了神經元的命運。治療缺血性中風，尤其是保護神經元延緩細胞死亡的方法仍然缺乏。以往的研究確定了細胞內轉運為神經保護的潛在目標，但背後的機制仍不清楚。 N-甲基-D-天冬氨酸受體（NMDAR）介導的興奮性毒性是缺血性神經變性一個關鍵因素。我們的初步工作表明，降低驅動蛋白1，一個微管依賴性的分子馬達，可以提高神經保護的水平。其机理在于改變缺血性中風過程中NMDA受體的分佈。我們發現，KIF5B，驅動蛋白1的重鏈，会被缺血預處理下調。把KIF5B的水平降低50％，即可減少神經變性。此外，我們已經阐明，驅動蛋白1与NMDA受體形成複合物。這些結果表明，驅動蛋白1 / NMDA受體相互作用在神經變性中的起著重要的作用。阻斷驅動蛋白1 / NMDAR的相互作用可以推遲或阻止神經變性。在本項目中，我們計劃詳細阐述驅動蛋白1 / NMDA受體的相互作用，以建立新的神經保護策略。

17127215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127215.value: 肺動脈高壓（PAH）是一種罕見的漸進式疾病，其表徵為平滑肌細胞增殖和肺動脈血管壁增厚，導致肺部高壓進而引起右心增大和衰竭。儘管近年來已有多種針對性的治療手段，PAH的發病率和死亡率仍居高不下，治療后五年內患者死亡率高達50%。胰泌素（SCT）是一種傳統的胃腸多肽激素。本實驗室近來已證明SCT在水平衡調控中起作用，這一發現連同SCT及其受體在心臟中的表達促使我們提出SCT也可以調節心臟功能的假設。我們詳盡分析了六月齡SCT基因敲除小鼠（SCT-/-）的心臟發育和生理機能，發現此種鼠的右心極度纖維化和肥大，對右心室/（左心室+心室隔膜）比率（右心室肥大的一種指標）的檢測進一步肯定了這一發現。在四月齡SCT-/-小鼠體內則無以上發現，因此PAH很可能是一種漸進式疾病。由於右心病變通常與肺部疾病有關，因此我們也分析了肺動脈的結構。SCT-/-小鼠的肺中動脈和肺大動脈呈現動脈血管壁增厚和纖維化。這些發現表明敲除小鼠的SCT基因可誘導與PAH 有關的病理漸進發展。在此提案中，我們將首先確認進而歸納在不同年齡組SCT-/-小鼠中PAH漸進發展的特徵。本項研究的第二個目標旨在厘清SCT-/-小鼠中PAH形成的分子機制，這一目標的重要性是顯而易見的。儘管研究人員爲了開發新的PAH療法做出了多種努力，但目前尚無可治愈的療法。許多患者雖持續治療但仍不可避免地經受病變漸進之苦，因此，進一步的創新療法亟待研發。本提案是首次將SCT與PAH相關聯的直接證據，研究的最終目標是檢驗SCT在SCT-/-小鼠和藥物誘導的小鼠PAH模型中防止和/或逆轉PAH癥狀的功效。此項研究將更新我們對PAH治療方法的認知，尤其是針對與SCT-/-小鼠有相同病因——SCT缺失的PAH患者的療法。

Loss of SCT results in systemic hypertension and cardiac remodelling To detect hypertension in SCT-/- mice, cardiovascular parameters were measured in SCT-/- mice by implantable telemetry. SBP, DBP and MAP were found to be significantly higher in 6-month-old SCT-/- mice compared with the same age of wild-type mice (SBP: 138.91±7.36 vs. 117.42±2.96 mmHg, p=0.0283; DBP: 110.25±7.71 vs. 88.16±1.89 mmHg, p=0.0247, MAP: 122.81±7.14 vs. 102.37±2.31 mmHg, p=0.0275; n=12/group). Heart pathologies in SCT-/- mice were also identified by heart weight ratio measurements, gross morphology and histology analysis, as well as cardiac functional analysis by echocardiography. First, [RV/ (LV+S)] ratio, heart to body weight and heart to tibia length ratios were significantly increased in 3-month-old SCT-/- mice. However, these ratios were not relevant at 6 months or older ages of SCT-/- mice because they have already developed RV deformation and fibrosis with myocardial tissue loss and hypertrophy. Second, the upper part of RV of SCT-/- mice was dilated and fibrotic, the lower portion of the RV was also hypertrophied. LV mass was found to be smaller in SCT-/- mice by high frequency echocardiographic examination. Collectively, these measurements indicated that SCT-/- mice have myocardial tissue loss in the LV and RV hypertrophy and fibrosis. 2. Loss of SCT also leads to pulmonary arterial hypertension and histopathological changes in the lungs Apart from SHT, we also studied the BP parameters in the pulmonary circulation and echocardiographic parameters related to pulmonary circulation and right ventricular function to examine whether SCT-/- mice exhibit PAH. RVSP was significantly increased in SCT-/- mice of all age groups [3 months: 26.74±0.81 (n=8) vs. 58.84±8.03 (n=7) mmHg, p=0.0009; 6 months: 30.37±1.65 (n=7) vs. 58.42±6.83 (n=7) mmHg, p=0.0031; 9 months: 25.63±0.86 (n=6) vs. 53.26±5.13 (n=8) mmHg, p=0.0011; 12 months: 26.2±1.62 (n=6) vs. 53.65±7.23 (n=6) mmHg, p=0.0070] at 350 bpm heart rate. In echocardiography, thickened RV walls were observed in 3-month-old SCT-/- mice denoting early hypertrophy, while dilated RVs with thin free walls and thickened IVS were observed in SCT-/- mice at 6 months of age and older. The indices of pulmonary hypertension, i.e., PAT/PET and PAT, RV stroke volume and cardiac output were reduced in SCT-/- mice. These data suggested that during the progression of PAH in SCT-/- mice, 3-month-old SCT-/- mice exhibited the initial stage of PAH with compensatory RV hypertrophy, but while the SCT-/- mice progressed to RV dilation by 6 months, overall RV function, including SV and cardiac output, was still maintained until 12 months of age. Collectively, these data showed that SCT deficiency causes moderate PAH along the developmental state of the animal. Next, from the H&E staining of all experimental ages of SCT-/- mice, the walls of the pulmonary arteries and medial width in lung arteries were thickened significantly compared to wild-type mice. The medial to total area ratio (0.67±0.02 vs. 0.39±0.03; p<0.001) and medial to luminal area ratio (2.35±0.25 vs. 0.74±0.11; p<0.001) were significantly elevated in SCT-/- mice, indicating arterial wall thickening in the lungs of SCT-/- mice. In CD31 staining, it showed thickened walls and narrowed lumens in the lungs of SCT-/- mice, revealing severe vascular remodelling of the arteries in the lungs of SCT-/- mice. Next, the inflammatory score of SCT-/- mice was markedly higher than that of control, and a large number of eosinophils were found inside the lumen of pulmonary arteries and surrounding the respiratory ducts and alveoli from the H&E staining but were absent in wild-type mice. From the picrosirius red collagen staining, increased perivascular fibrosis was also observed in 6-month-old SCT-/- mice compared with same age control mice. In addition, the fibrosis to lumen area ratio was increased in 6-month-old SCT-/- mice compared to that in control mice. In H&E staining, the perivascular space in all experimental ages of SCT-/- mice was much larger than that in control mice, demonstrating that perivascular adventitial expansion was present in the lungs of SCT-/- mice. Small airway remodelling was also found in SCT-/- mice. From H&E staining, thinner bronchiolar epithelium with the loss or deformation of the shape of native club cells was observed in SCT-/- mice compared to control mice. Meanwhile, immunostaining revealed a reduction in VEGF and COX-2 expression in the lung tissue and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) of SCT-/- mice at 6, 9 and 12 months of age. To further examine the apoptosis in the lungs of SCT-/- mice, both TUNEL staining and double staining of TUNEL/CD31 were carried out and showed an increased apoptosis and apoptotic ECs. Taken together, the changes in lung morphology and increased apoptosis in the lungs of SCT-/- mice suggested that SCT-/- mice exhibit small airway remodelling. Objective 2) To examine the molecular mechanisms for SCT in the advancement of PAH in SCT-/- mice 1. Molecular changes in cardiac tissue hormones and protein in SCT-/- mice To identify the underlying mechanisms of SCT, NO, VEGF, aldosterone and other molecules affecting blood pressure and related to SCT were measured. In plasma, NO (1.26±0.14 vs. 2.4±0.17 nmol nitrate; p<0.001) and VEGF (69.69±1.96 vs. 79.7±2.48; p<0.05) levels were significantly reduced in SCT-/- mice. The plasma aldosterone level (652.53±92.74 vs. 376.68±34.51 pg/ml; p<0.05) and aldosterone to renin ratio (36.34±4.44 vs. 22.68±1.66 pg/ng; p<0.05) were significantly higher. ). Furthermore, cardiac tissue aldosterone (1.05±0.11 vs. 1.95±0.35 pg/mg; n=8/group; p=0.0372) and cardiac VEGF (0.06 ± 0.00 vs. 0.07 ± 0.00 pg/mg; n=8-9/group; p=0.0085) were also significantly increased in SCT-/- mice. In gene expression analysis in the heart of SCT-/- mice, ET-1 transcript was observed together with a significant fold increase in AT1aR, AT-1bR), and MHC genes. However, eNOS expression was reduced. 2. Molecular changes in lung tissue hormones and protein in SCT-/- mice Apart from the observed deteriorated lung tissues in SCT-/- mice, related lung tissue hormones and proteins were analysed. Significantly elevated transcript levels of TNF-α, ET-1 and ETAR (3.55-fold, 3.21-fold, and 2.3-fold vs. control). Meanwhile, VEGF, PTGS-2, VPAC1R and TGF-β were downregulated in the lung tissues of SCT-/- mice. Objective 3: To test the potential therapeutic usage of SCT for protecting and/or reversing PAH symptoms in SCT-/- mice as well as a drug-induced PAH animal model 1. Long-term SCT treatment can prevent heart and lung pathologies Effect of long-term SCT treatment was tested in 3-month-old SCT-/- mice using a mini-osmotic pump. After long-term SCT treatment in SCT-/- mice, the medial width (standard medial thickness), medial area to total area ratio, medial area to luminal area ratio and inflammatory score in the lungs were significantly reduced in the SCT-replacement group. In the histomorphology analysis of the heart and lungs, arterial wall thickening, endothelial cell proliferation, perivascular inflammation and adventitial expansion, and cardiac fibrosis were all reduced in the SCT-treated group. In the lungs of SCT-treated SCT-/- mice, ET-1 and ETAR transcript levels were significantly downregulated (0.37±0.08-fold and 0.68±0.07-fold vs. control), while VEGF transcript levels were upregulated (2.27±0.35-fold). As for the heart of SCT-treated SCT-/- mice, ET-1 and alpha-MHC transcript levels were downregulated (0.64±0.03-fold and 0.54±0.08-fold vs. control), while the eNOS transcript level was upregulated (1.65±0.23-fold vs. control). These results collectively suggest that long-term SCT treatment can improve heart and lung conditions due to hypertension, correction of related gene expression changes.
