17127215.label: Major findings and research outcome
17127215.value: This research has revealed that deficiency of SCT in mice would exhibit both systemic and pulmonary hypertension with damage in the heart and lungs. The systemic hypertension in SCT-/- mice was due to dysregulation of the RAAS with lowered VEGF and NO levels and higher aldosterone levels because of SCT deficiency. These significant decrease in VEGF and NO in SCT-/- mice could avoid vasodilation and result in continuous vasoconstriction, which then increased SBP, DBP and MAP and led to LV and RV pathologies. The damage to cardiac tissue can be due to the pressure overload in the pulmonary and systemic circulations or from the heart itself. As a result, cardiac fibrosis was due to the continual increase in blood pressure and heavy workload in cardiac muscles. Moreover, these pathologies are mainly localized in the RV and IVS of the heart of SCT-/- mice, likely due to high pulmonary arterial blood pressure. Meanwhile, the genes related to myocardial fibrosis, namely, ET-1, ET-1, AT1AR and AT1BR expression, were significantly increased with the augmented cardiac aldosterone. In contrast, eNOS expression was significantly decreased in the hearts of SCT-/- mice, which may induce and enhance myocardial fibrosis. The increased cardiac VEGF level was the result of ET-1 overexpression and increased cardiac aldosterone. All of these may be the combined cause of cardiac fibrosis and apoptosis in SCT-/- mice. Furthermore, expression of cardiac hypertrophic marker genes including beta-MHC, alpha-MHC, and alpha-SKA are all found to be high in the heart of SCT-/- mice. Robust arterial remodelling, perivascular inflammation, and adventitial expansion in the lungs of SCT-/- mice were observed, which are associated with pulmonary hypertension. Small airway remodelling found in SCT-/- mice can also be the reason for the inflammation reaction in the lungs. The disruption of the pulmonary bronchiolar epithelium with the loss or deformation of the shape of native club cells observed in SCT-/- mice may be due to the consequences of SCT deficiency on Cl- and HCO3- secretion in the lungs. This epithelium defect also contributes to the reduction of TGF-beta, iNOS, and VEGF expression in bronchiolar epithelium found in SCT-/- mice. One-week-long SCT treatment can reduce plasma aldosterone, renin and the aldosterone to renin ratio, while the 3-month-long SCT treatment can prevent the development of heart and lung pathologies in SCT-/- mice. In the long-term SCT-treated SCT-/- mice, arterial wall thickening, perivascular adventitial expansion and inflammatory cell proliferation were all reduced.

17127215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17127215.value: It would be interesting to study the potential use of secretin as an anti-hypertensive drug in treating pulmonary hypertension or improving the damaging effect on heart and lungs associated with long term hypertension. Using secretin and secretin receptor as target we have recently tested and developed a small molecule secretin receptor modulator (i.e. KSD179019). Our lab has already filled for US provisional patent for this compound as potential anti-hypertensive drug via HKU TTO office. Additionally, we has registered a HKU spin off biotech company to further develop this compound as novel drug for the treatment of resistant hypertension (RA). RA effect 10% of total hypertensive population. The 30% of world adult population is known to be suffering from hypertension.

17127215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127215.value: In this project, we have successfully identified that SCT-/- mice would suffer from systemic and pulmonary hypertension with increased fibrosis in the lungs and heart. Small airway remodelling and pulmonary inflammation were also found in SCT-/- mice. Serum nitric oxide and VEGF levels were reduced and plasma aldosterone levels were increased in SCT-/- mice. Elevated cardiac aldosterone and decreased VEGF in the lungs were observed in the SCT-/- mice. More interestingly, SCT replacement in SCT-/- mice could prevent the development of heart and lung pathologies compared to the untreated group. Taken together, we comprehensively demonstrated that the critical role of SCT in the cardiovascular and pulmonary systems and provide new insight into the potential role of SCT in the pathological development of cardiopulmonary and cardiovascular diseases.

17127515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127515.value: 綠色螢光蛋白（GFP）在過去二十年為分子生物學帶來革命性的影響，而發現、改造和應用這項技術於活細胞成像的日本科學家下村脩、美國科學家馬丁·查爾菲和錢永健更因而獲得了2008年的諾貝爾化學獎。最近的研究提出核糖核酸(RNA)的錯誤定位嚴重關係到生物過程, 然而對於疾病機理方面的了解甚少。因應現時用於RNA活細胞成像的技術主要是應用於蛋白質活細胞成像方面, 發展針對RNA的活細胞成像的技術是必需的。 雖然Jaffrey的實驗團隊於2011年於“科學”中發表的研究文章裡描述了開創性的RNA擬態綠色螢光蛋白“Spinach”，但是發展出更多、更小、更亮和更寬闊光譜的RNA螢光適體對用於多重顏色成像技術肯定是有迫切需要的。在此，我們提出一個用於選擇RNA螢光適體的新穎方法, 名為脫氧核糖核酸顯示配體指數增強系統進化技術 (DNA Display SELEX)，使我們能直接使用螢光的參數作為適體進化的參考而挑選出合適的RNA螢光適體。這個方法比傳統的配體指數增強系統進化技術 (SELEX)更能直接從適體的螢光度反映適體的進化，從而進化出更優化和“度身訂造”的螢光。 作為一個多方面協作的專業團隊，我們的研究團隊包括具有豐富適體研究及應用相關經驗和往績，在醫學院的首席研究員及在工程學院，擅長於微流體的聯合研究員。 我們將匯合各方面的專業知識來解決於的研究過程遇到的挑戰及實現挑選出合適的RNA螢光適體的目的。在此項研究，我們有四個目標: 一，利用我們新穎的DNA Display 方法為顆粒塗上RNA塗層，再運用螢光激活細胞分選 (FACS) 驗證這新穎的方法。二，利用以上方法挑選出具有我們所期望的螢光特性的RNA螢光適體。三，運用生物物理技術去所挑選的RNA螢光適體的特性。四，探討所挑選的RNA螢光適體如何用於標記和踪融細菌和人類細胞的RNA。 總括以上，此研究將不僅提供更好的螢光試劑用顯示RNA於活細胞成像中，更加提供應用在分子生物學之上的革新的新分子進化方法。

17127515.label: Realisation of objectives
17127515.value: The first objective, “Establish the DNA display technique on beads and investigate integration with emulsion PCR using previously discovered aptamers as a proof-of-principal”, has been completed. Our intent with the DNA display system was to link genotype with phenotype. We found another method to achieve this that has advantages in terms of assay formats and cross reactivity of clonal species. That is microfluidic water-in-oil emulsion droplet based selection. We developed a microfluidic water-in-oil emulsion droplet based system and the assays required for selection of light-up upon binding RNA aptamers. This system includes: 1) Droplet generation to form distinct PCR reaction vessels, each populated with a single DNA template sequence that is amplifies to create clonal droplets. 2) Picoinjection of transcription mixture and fluorogen to generate RNA aptamers and fluorescent signal. 3) microfluidic sorting of fluorescent droplets. We demonstrated this system with known fluorescent RNA aptamers and optimised the PCR droplet mix formulation and generation, picoinjection transcription mix formulation and fluorescent sorting gates. Deliverables from objective one: 1. One patent on DNA display. 2. Related methodology journal papers (see Complexity 2017 and Int J Mol Sci 2017) 3. Three PhD students trained The second objective, “Evolve new fluorophore-RNA aptamers with a range of selected fluorescent properties using fluorescence activated cell sorting coupled to deep sequencing”, has been completed. We performed five rounds of microfluidic selection to evolve light-up upon binding RNA aptamers against the DFHBI-1T fluorogen. Each selection round consisted of PCR droplet generation, PCR amplification, picoinjection, transcription, microfluidic sorting, emulsion breaking, ethanol precipitation, PCR amplification and purification of DNA template. Between selection rounds we performed mutagenic PCR to diversify the aptamer libraries. We used PCR to add barcode flanking regions to all of our aptamer pools before performing deep sequencing to characterise the microfluidic selection. Deliverables from Objective 2: 1. Related methodology papers (see Genes 2018, Chembiochem, 2018) 2. Conference presentations at internationally leading conferences 3. Main paper still in preparation for JACS for submission late 2020. 4. Three PhD students trained The third objective, “Characterize newly selected fluorophore-RNA aptamers in vitro for biophysical properties, stability, environmental impact on fluorescence, and potential for fusion with longer RNAs”, is currently ongoing. We have sequenced the aptamer selection rounds and are currently characterising the aptamers. The characterisations we are performing are sequence diversity, evolutionary pedigree, fluorescence activation, binding constant determination and thermal stability. Deliverables from Objective three: 1. Related methodology papers 2. Three PhD students trained The fourth objective, “Observe newly selected fluorophore-RNA aptamers expressed in cells using E. coli and human cell culture as two independent model cell systems” is completed. We have used light-up upon binding fluorogen/RNA aptamer pairs for the visualisation and monitoring of transcription within cell-like assemblies. This work relates to the origins of life on the Earth and is one of the most fundamental challenges facing modern science. Compartmentalization of biomolecules was likely an essential stage in the genesis of the first living cells. We developed a system that underwent liquid-liquid phase separation driven by evaporation. Using our light-up upon binding fluorogen/RNA aptamer tools, we demonstrated the flow of genetic information in these phase-separated compartments via in vitro transcription. Our work could help answer the longstanding question of how compartmentalization of necessary biomolecules may have occurred in the earliest living cells. We submitted a manuscript comprising of this work to the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America (PNAS) titled “Prebiotically plausible pathways for liquid-liquid phase separation and cell-like assemblies in an evaporating droplet”. This paper has passed editorial review and is currently under referee review. Deliverables related to objective 4: 1. High impact paper under review at PNAS. 2. 3 PhD students trained - highly interdisciplinary between medicine and engineering. Overall, we have realised the objectives for the most-part as demonstrated by patents, publications and students trained. There are some shortfalls/experiments which we are completing relating to fluorophore selections and applications in cellular context. We will bring this together in latter half of 2020 with our publication planned for JACS.

17127515.label: Major findings and research outcome
17127515.value: The original intentions of our research were to develop the methodologies of DNA display, integrating this with emulsion PCR, and use these approaches to develop fluorophore-RNA aptamers. We report the major finding that we have indeed developed DNA display as a new technology for molecular evolution experiments. This is demonstrated in a patent "DNA display and methods thereof" which is filed in EU, USA, China. Several journal publications were also published aligned with this in Complexity, Int J Mol Sci, coupled to reviews in Chembiochem and Genes. We also report fluorophore-RNA aptamer selections after developing methodologies for droplet based selections. This has delivered a new set of RNA tools which will be highly useful for molecular biology. We have reported this in several conference presentations, with the methodologies published in 2019 in Advanced Biossytems, and the major paper relating to this is in preparation for JACS in late 2020. The research also links into more fundamental research where we used such fluorophore-RNA aptamers. This has provided some insight into mechanisms of phase separation. This research is under review at PNAS. Three PhD students were trained in the course of this research, and several journal publications are published (or in process of being published). A patent is filed relating to DNA display. There have been significant outcomes/deliverables from this research.

17127515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17127515.value: Other directions in my laboratory are developing new chemistries in nucleic acids: Cheung, Y.W.*, Rothlisberger, P.*, Mechaly, A.E., Weber, P.P.W., Levi-Acobas, F., Lo, Y., Wong, A.W.C., Kinghorn, A.B., Haouz, A., Savage, G.P., Hollenstein, M.*, & Tanner, J.A.* Evolution of abiotic cubane chemistries in a nucleic acid aptamer allows selective recognition of a malaria biomarker. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA, accepted in press (2020). No group internationally has yet coupled diverse chemistries to droplet based aptamer selections. Doing so will open new vistas particularly in droplet-based evolution of catalytic activities. Our research team is planning for this direction in future.

17127515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127515.value: It is possible to use evolution techniques outside living organisms as an approach to develop new molecular tools which can be used in biomedical sciences, or more translationally for therapeutics or diagnostics. One can evolve nucleic acids such as DNA and RNA by these evolution techniques to carry out tasks that would not occur naturally. One example is to evolve RNA so that it fluoresces in the presence of other small molecules. This is useful as one would then have a technique to observe where RNA is in the cell by fluorescence microscopy. This is important as there are many unanswered questions regarding how RNA moves around the cell and how this is linked to disease mechanisms for example. In this research we developed the methodologies which enable such evolution experiments termed "DNA display". We then integrated this with a novel droplet based selection method as our molecular evolution selection approach. We were successful in using these approaches to identify new functional RNA molecules then apply them in model systems. This research provides a new toolbox for discovery of functional molecules that can aid biomedical research, and could be applied in future for the development of new therapeutics and diagnostics.

17127715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127715.value: The BAF (BRG1/BRM-associated factors) complex, as the first identified chromatin remodeling complex, can utilize the energy of ATP hydrolysis to alter chromatin structure, thereby spatiotemporally controls genomic DNA accessibility to nuclear machinery. BAF complexes are generally comprised of both core factors BRG1/BRM, BAF47, BAF155/170 and lineage-specific subunits BAF250a/b, BAF60a/b/c, BAF57, BAF45a/b/c/d, BAF180 and etc. The core factors of the BAF complex together with variant subunits can assemble into different combinations. It is well documented that distinct combinatorial assembly of the BAF complex produces functional diversity. Through interacting with the chromatin, transcriptional factors and other epigenetic regulators, the BAF complex regulates the transcription of a large number of target genes, thus plays an essential role in development, differentiation, maintaining pluripotency in embryonic stem cells and promoting somatic cell reprogramming. Given the fact that the BAF complex plays an instructive role in cell lineage specification, it is conceivable that misregulation of subunits in the BAF complex could lead to human cancers and neurodevelopmental disorders. Indeed, recent cancer genome sequencing studies have revealed that mutations in components of human BAF complex are quite common, with a frequency of 19% across a wide spectrum of human cancers, close to the mutation rate of p53, the most frequently mutated tumor suppressor. The BAF complex is increasingly being recognized as a therapeutic target for cancer development. However, the molecular mechanism underlying the contribution of high frequency BAF subunit mutations to human cancers remains largely unknown. Even though being extensively studied over the past two decades, the structural information of the BAF complex is very limited, which has seriously hampered our mechanistic understanding of the BAF complex. In this project, based on the preliminary results, we propose to further pursue the molecular mechanism of BAF core factors including the following aims: (i) To determine the molecular basis of epigenetic recognition by BAF155; (ii) To explore combinatorial recognition of methyl histone and DNA by BAF155; (iii) To characterize the molecular interaction between BAF155 and BAF47. The results from our proposed studies will provide important insights into the mechanism by which BAF155 facilitates the BAF complex to target at specific genomic loci, and will provide the first-line of evidence how BAF155 serves as a scaffold protein to interact with other BAF core subunits for the BAF complex formation. The completed study will contribute to furthering our understanding of mutations in the BAF complex drive tumor formation. 17127915.label: Project Objectives
17127915.value: Aim 1: To develop a method and optimize procedures for identification of molecular targets using MS-based proteomics expression data. To understand the molecular target and thus the mechanism-of-action of a drug is crucial for drug development. In preliminary studies, we used camptothecin, an alkaloid with known target, as a model for development and optimization of methods and procedures for drug target identification. With the help of bioinformatics tools and high through-put MS-based proteomics techniques, the target identification procedure has been optimized. And the known target of camptothecin, topoisomerase I, is identified as the main target from the proteome profiles of camptothecin treated cancer cells. The procedures has been applied to study capsaicin, an alkaloid found in chili peppers to confirm that the methods applicable to compounds other than camptothecin and to refine the developed procedures. The results will be compared with the findings on studies of capsaicin in literature. And in turn the procedures will be refined to improve the accuracy and significance of the hypothetic molecular target prediction. Aim 2. To apply the optimized procedure to search for novel molecular targets of selected bioactive TCM components. The same procedure has been applied to another bioactive component in herbs, corydaline, an alkaloid found in corydalis rhizome. Our preliminary study with corydaline hypothesized the proto-oncogene c-fos as one of the potential targets. Other than corydaline, a few bioactive TCM components will be selected based on their cytotoxcities, and the target identification procedure will be applied subsequently. Several TCM has been targeted based on their pharmacological effects stated in traditional Chinese medicinal literature. The selected TCM including: Dendrobium nobile (Shihu), Juncus effusus (Dengxincao), Lithospermum erythrorhizon (Zicao), Houttuynia cordata (Yuxingcao) and dandelion (Pugongying), their major bioactive components will be used in the proposed research. Aim 3. To validate the potential targets of the selected bioactive TCM components and to elucidate their mechanism-of-action. A potential targets generation method is helpful in providing research direction to study the mechanism-of-action of a drug. The proposed potential molecular targets found in Aim 2 will be validated through orthogonal biological assays. And the mechanism-of-action of the bioactive TCM components will be elucidated through the identified targets. We are validating the proto-oncogene c-fos as a target of corydaline. Our preliminary results showed that corydaline inhibits a c-fos related transcriptional activity.

17127915.label: Realisation of objectives
17127915.value: Objective 1: To develop a method and optimize procedures for identification of molecular targets using MS-based proteomics expression data. This objective has been fully achieved. (100%) In order to develop a method for target identification, a model molecule with known target is needed. Camptothecin serves as a good model for this purpose. Camptothecin is an alkaloid isolated from camptotheca (Xishu) and it is well-known as a specific inhibitor of the DNA enzyme topoisomerase I (topo I). The development of method for identification of molecular targets was started using the MS-based proteomics expression data of camptothecin treated cancer cell lines. Sample Preparation for proteomics analysis. The 72 hours half maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) of camptothecin on HepG2 cell line were determined by MTT (3-(4,5-Dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide) assay. HepG2 cells were treated with camptothecin at its IC50 for 1h, 6h and 48 h, the cells were then harvested and lysed with urea lysis buffer. The protein amount in the lysates were then determined with Bradford protein assay. A known amount of proteins was purified by acetone precipitation, digested with trypsin and desalted prior to high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)-MS/MS proteomics analysis using the Orbitrap MS. Target identification with proteomics data and bioinformatics tool. The camptothecin-treated cell lysate digest was analysed with Orbitrap MS connected with HPLC. The resulting MS raw data was then submitted to MaxQuant for database searching to identify proteins. Relative quantification of identified proteins was done on a label-free basis. The protein expression data were then uploaded on to ExPlainTM (a bioinformatics tool developed by BioBase, Germany). The target identification procedure described in a publication by Zubarev (J Proteome Res. 2011 10: 2679-83) was tested with the obtained proteomics data. In brief, a list of identified proteins from control and treated samples, with accession number and abundance, was loaded on to ExPlainTM, then keynode molecules (keynodes are molecules found at the intersections of the molecular network in the database) were deduced through upstream searching in the network from the input protein list. A score was assigned to each keynode molecule depending on its connectivity with the input proteins. The differences in keynode scores (SK) between treated sample and control were calculated as: SK = (SS – SC) × log(SS/SC) The keynode molecule with the highest SK between treated sample and control for each time point was identified as cIAP-2, proCaspase-3: Hsp10: Hsp60 and ERK1 respectively for 1h, 6h and 48h time point. Then a downstream search was performed from each top-scoring keynode molecule, the common downstream molecules from the three top-scoring keynode molecules of the three time points are the potential molecular targets. However, the target identification result was not satisfactory. Although topo I was identified as one the potential targets of camptothecin, there are a large number (993) of potential targets; which makes this approach not helpful and further optimization was performed. Optimization of procedures for identification of molecular targets. As the common downstream molecules are the potential targets, the number of common molecules could be lowered when downstream searching from more top-scoring keynode molecules. Two more cell lines were selected: AGS and SKOV3. The same experiments of camptothecin were repeated for AGS and SKOV3 as those performed with HepG2. The resulting top-scoring keynode molecules for the three different cell lines are: Mos, integrins and Beta-D-fructose respectively for 1h, 6h and 48h time point on AGS cell line; proCaspase-3, cGKI-beta and ERK2 respectively for 1h, 6h and 48h time point on HepG2 cell line; Mos, 7,8-dihydrofolate and 3-phosphohydrox-pyruvate respectively for 1h, 6h and 48h time point on SKOV3 cell line. The number of common downstream molecules was reduced and topo I was identified as the top-scoring potential target among a handful number of molecules. A keynode molecule network can be constructed which connects topo I and the top-scoring molecules. Objective 2. To apply the optimized procedure to search for novel molecular targets of selected bioactive TCM components. This objective has been fully achieved. (100%) Application of the target identification procedure to Dehydroeﬀusol (DHE). The target identification procedure has been applied to another bioactive component in herbs, dehydroeﬀusol (DHE), a phenanthrene isolated from the Chinese medicinal plant Juncus effusus. Biological evaluation of DHE reveals in vitro and in vivo anticancer eﬀects. HeLa cells were treated with 20 μM DHE or DMSO vehicle for 6, 10, and 24 h. The optimized procedure described in objective 1 was applied to the proteomics data obtained with the DHE-treated cell lysate digest samples. Two top-scoring keynode molecules per time point are PKC and MKK4 for 6h, Cdk1 and ABL1 for 10h, Granzyme B and procaspase-3 for 24h time points. A keynode molecule network can be constructed which connecting the top-scoring molecules, JNK and ATF2. The results revealed that activating transcription factor 2 (ATF2) may be a key signaling molecule inﬂuenced by DHE. The ATF2 transcription factor is a member of the ATF/CREB family of leucine zipper proteins that bind to both AP-1 (Jun) and CRE DNA response elements.27 ATF-2 interacts with a variety of oncoproteins and cellular tumor suppressors and regulates growth, survival, or apoptosis, depending on the cellular context and the composition of the dimeric complexes. Cellular stress imposed by anticancer compounds activate c-Jun kinase (JNK) that phosphorylate ATF-2, thereby mediating a tumor-suppressive eﬀect through a transcriptional program that is frequently down-regulated in human tumors. Objective 3. To validate the potential targets of the selected active TCM components and to elucidate their mechanism-of-action. This objective has been fully achieved. (100%) Validation of the mechanism-of-action of Dehydroeﬀusol (DHE). Activation of JNK and ATF2 is closely associated with induction of apoptosis. In this study, it was found that phosphorylation of JNK and ATF2 were induced at 10 and 24 h in the presence of DHE. Thus, the possibility exists that DHE-induced apoptosis may be linked to activation of the JNK-ATF2 pathway. Furthermore, DHE treatment also inhibited the tumor promoter, phorbol myristate acetate (PMA)-induced transcriptional activity, which is mediated through the AP-1 responsive element of a reporter gene as examined with a luciferase reporter assay. The connections within the JNK-ATF2-AP1 axis are not yet fully understood but it is nonetheless a likely part of DHE’s mechanism of action. Details with figures can be found in the resulting publication in J. Proteome Research stated in Part C.

17127915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17127915.value: The major findings of our projects are the identification of molecular targets of several natural products including corydaline, dehydroeffusol and erianin through novel proteomic approaches. The key results are as follows: (1) Dehydroeffusol (DHE) is a phenanthrene isolated from the Chinese medicinal plant Juncus effuses (燈心草). Biological evaluation of DHE reveals in vitro and in vivo anticancer effects. We have performed a shotgun proteomic analysis using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry to investigate the changes in the protein profiles in cancer cells upon DHE treatment. DHE affected cancer-associated signaling pathways, including NF-κB, β-catenin, and endoplasmic reticulum stress. Through quantitative pathway and key node analysis of the proteomics data, activating transcription factor 2 (ATF-2) and c-Jun kinase (JNK) were found to be the key components in DHE's modulated biological pathways. Based on the pathway analysis as well as chemical similarity to estradiol, DHE is proposed to be a phytoestrogen. The proteomic, bioinformatic, and chemoinformatic analyses were further verified with individual cell-based experiments. Our study demonstrates a workflow for identifying multiple mechanisms of action of DHE through shotgun proteomic analysis. (2) Erianin is a natural stilbenoid compounds found in a Dendrobium species (Shihu石斛) which is a common material in Chinese herbal medicines. Erianin at submolar concentrations could inhibit a variety of cancer cell line growth in vitro. In addition, treatment of mice bearing human lung cancer xenograft with erianin could reduce the tumor volume without adverse effect. Through quantitative pathway and key node analysis of the proteomics data, EGFR was deduced as one of the potential targets. Furthermore, a chemical probe of Erianin was synthesized in order to further identify the molecular targets. Affinity labeling and Click chemistry with biotin using the erianin probe followed by proteomic analysis identify tubulin and tubulin interacting proteins End binding protein 1 (EB1) as the possible targets. Accordingly, erianin was also shown to induce cell cycle arrest at G2/M stage and stimulate phosphorylation of histone H3 which is indicative of the cancer cell mitotic arrest. Research outcome: The proteomic analysis of mechanisms of action of dehydroeffusol has been published in J. Proteome Research, 2018 17:2470-2479 The identification of molecular targets of erianin has provided supporting information for a patent application on the use of erianin and derivatives as anticancer compounds (PCT/CN2018/097183).

17127915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127915.value: This project is directed to elucidate how bioactive natural products work for treating diseases by using integrated chemistry and biology approaches. The significance of the project has two fold: (1) It has successfully established several novel proteomic technologies for identification of the molecular targets of bioactive compounds. These technologies include quantitative pathway and key node analysis of the expression proteomic data, chemical probes conjugated to the bioactive compounds for direct isolation of binding protein targets (photoaffinity and click chemistry) and the use of thermal stability of proteins to identify the direct or proximal proteins engaged by the targeting compounds. (2) Through these approach, we have elucidated the mechanisms of actions and molecular targets of anticancer active compounds from Chinese medicinal herbs such as dehydroeffusol from Juncus effuses and erianin from Dendrobium species. While Chinese medicine or other natural products is inevitably an untapped source for drug discovery and development, their pharmacological properties are complex. It is anticipated that the proteomic approaches developed herein should provide a streamlined and effective platform for exploring the bioactive compounds from Chinese medicines for therapeutic applications.

17128115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128115.value: The global incidence of type 1 diabetes (T1D), an autoimmune disease caused by a complex interaction of genetic, environmental and immunological factors, has more than doubled in the past two decades. Although T1D accounts for only 5-10% of all diagnosed cases of diabetes, it is one of the most common chronic diseases in children and adolescents and the most severe type of diabetes. There is currently no cure available for T1D, and the diabetic patients have to rely on the life-long medication with insulin. Despite enormous research efforts in the past decades, the mechanism underlying β-cell destruction in autoimmune diabetes remains poorly understood. Neutrophils, which are the most abundant type of white blood cells, have recently been implicated in both the onset and progression of T1D. Our recent clinical studies have demonstrated that a decreased neutrophil number in patients with newly-diagnosed T1D is accompanied by a marked elevation in circulating protein levels and enzymatic activities of both neutrophil elastase (NE) and proteinase 3 (PR3), the two major neutrophil serine proteases that play a key role in tissue inflammation and damage. Furthermore, we observed a close association of increased NE and PR3 levels with β-cell autoimmunity in T1D patients. In NOD mice with spontaneous development of autoimmune diabetes, increased neutrophil infiltration and elevated NE/PR3 activities occur at the very early prediabetic stage, prior to insulitis and islet β-cell destruction. Chronic administration of the pharmacological inhibitors of NE and PR3 leads to a marked attenuation of islet inflammation and subsequent development of hyperglycemia in NOD mice. In this project, we will use our unique NE and PR3 double deficient mouse model to comprehensively investigate how neutrophils, via releasing NE and PR3, participates in the initiation and perpetuation of islet inflammation and β-cell self-destruction, and will also interrogate the roles of these two serine proteases in mediating the crosstalk between different immune cells to elicit β-cell autoimmunity. Furthermore, we will evaluate whether adeno-associated virus-mediated islet-specific delivery of human elafin, a potent protease inhibitor specific to NE and PR3, can prevent or reverse insulitis and autoimmune diabetes in NOD mice. The findings from this study will shed new light on the novel function of neutrophils in regulating immunometabolism, and will also provide scientific evidence to support the use of the two neutrophil serine proteases as a diagnostic marker and/or drug target for risk prediction and early therapeutic intervention of autoimmune diabetes.

17128115.label: Realisation of objectives
17128115.value: Objective-1: We have performed four sets of independent experiments demonstrating that neutrophil elastase (NE) and proteinase-3 (PR3), two major neutrophil serine proteases, are the early mediators of autoimmune diabetes in NOD mice. Firstly, we generated NE- and PR3- double knockout NOD mice (named as NE-/-PR3-/- NOD) by crossing NE-/-PR3-/- mice with NOD mice for at least ten generations, and monitored the spontaneous development of insulitis, beta cell destruction and diabetes in both NE-/-PR3-/- NOD and NE+/+PR3+/+ NOD mice from birth to 35 weeks of age. Our results showed that NE-/-PR3-/- NOD mice exhibited much less insulitis and immune cell infiltration in pancreatic islets, delayed onset time and obviously-reduced incidence of diabetes. Secondly, we generated recombinant elafin (a ~6 Kda endogenous inhibitor of NE/PR3), and treated NOD mice with recombinant elafin by intraperitoneal injection from 12 days to 7 weeks after birth, followed by monitoring the incidence of diabetes. Our result showed that treatment with elafin significantly delayed the onset time and dampened the progression of autoimmune diabetes in NOD mice, accompanied with a marked alleviation of insulitis, suggesting that inhibition of early increases in pancreatic NE activity of NOD mice is sufficient to alleviate T1D. Thirdly, we expressed elafin directly in pancreatic islet by adenovirus-associated viruses(AAV) delivery system (driven by the rat insulin promoter), and observed a similar therapeutic benefit in alleviation of T1D. Fourthly, we treated NOD mice with sivelestat (a chemical inhibitor of NE) from 12 days to 7 weeks of age by daily intraperitoneal injection and confirmed that such treatments can block pancreatic NE activity using fluorescent imaging analysis. The results showed that treatment with sivelestat from 12 days to 7 weeks of age delayed the onset time to 20-week-old and reduced the diabetes incidence of 30-week-old mice from 90.45% to 53.82% in NOD mice. Objective-2: To evaluate the contribution of NE and PR3 to dynamic changes on infiltration of various immune cells and production of pro-inflammatory cytokines in NOD mice, we measured the dynamic changes of NE and PR3 activities in the islets during the development of insulitis in NOD mice at different ages, by intraperitoneal injection with NE680 FAST (a NE- activatable agent that is optically silent upon injection and produces fluorescent signal after cleavage by NE), followed by noninvasive fluorescent imaging analysis to determine the activity of NE in different organs of NOD mice. Our results showed that NE and PR3 activities significantly elevated at the very early stage of insulitis (3 week-old), and elevated NE and PR3 occurred specifically in the islets but not in other tissues of NOD mice examined. Additionally, we performed flow cytometry analysis for the frequency of different immune cells in the spleens, pancreatic islets and lymph nodes of NE-/-PR3-/- NOD and NE+/+PR3+/+ NOD mice using the antibodies against surface markers [macrophages (F4/80+), M1 (F4/80+CD11c+), M2 (F4/80+CD206+), helper T cells (CD3+CD4+), cytotoxic T cells (CD3+CD8+), neutrophils (LY-6G+), pDCs (m927+CD11cmed), cDCs(CD11b+CD11c+), B cells (CD20+). Our results showed that double deficiency of NE and PR3 significantly decreased the number of total macrophages (F4/80+), and reduced the percentage of M1 macrophage (F4/80+CD11c+)and the number of cytotoxic T cells (CD3+CD8+), but increased the percentage of M2 macrophage (F4/80+CD206+) in NOD mice. Similar results were also observed in NOD mice treated with sivelestat, suggesting islet macrophages are an important target cells for pro-inflammatory actions of NE/PR3. Objective-3: To elucidate the molecular mechanisms whereby NE/PR3 triggers insulitis and pancreatic β cell destruction, we investigated the roles of NE and PR3 for neutrophils-mediated activation and migration of macrophages. To this end, neutrophils isolated from bone marrow of NE-/-/PR3-/- mice or wild-type littermates were seeded into the bottom chamber of a transwell plate and were activated with irradiated Min6 β-cells or endotoxin (LPS), and macrophages isolated from the spleens of NOD mice were seeded onto the upper chamber, followed by counting the number of macrophages migrated into the lower chamber, and analyzing the expression profiles of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNFα, IL1β, MCP-1) with real-time PCR. Our results showed that neutrophil-mediated transmigration and activation of macrophages was reduced by NE and PR3 deficiency, and replenishment with recombinant NE or PR3 in the co-culture system reversed these changes. We also generated recombinant NE and PR3 using a mammalian cell expression system, and tested their direct effects on production of several pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemokines in macrophages. The results showed that treatment with recombinant NE or PR3 protein significantly up-regulated the gene expression of Tnf-ɑ, Il-1β and Mcp-1, and also elevated the protein concentration of these pro-inflammatory factors in the conditioned medium and RAW264.7 macrophages, which were largely abolished by co-incubation with the NE/PR3 endogenous inhibitor elafin or sivelestat. By using cell migration assays in a co-culture system, we found that conditional medium from NE/PR3-treated min6 beta cells significantly promoted the migration of RAW264.7 macrophages, suggesting that NE/PR3 can directly induce the inflammatory response in both beta cells and macrophages, exacerbating microphage migration triggered by beta cells. Furthermore, we found that treatment with recombinant NE resulted in a significant increase of phosphorylated IκBα (p-IκBα) and phosphorylated NFκB (p-NFκB p65) in RAW264.7 macrophages, accompanied with an obvious decrease in t-IκBα, suggesting that NE causes a phosphorylation-dependent degradation of total IκBα in macrophages. However, pre-incubation with CLI-095 (a selective antagonist of toll-like receptor-4(TLR4)) drastically reduced NE-induced elevation in p-IκBα and p-NFκB p65 as well as prevented the degradation of t-IκBα, and also blocked the effect of NE on exacerbation of microphage migration by conditioned medium of min6 beta cells, suggesting that TLR4 is a crucial mediator in NE-mediated inflammatory responses in macrophages and beta cells. Due to the difficulties in obtaining sufficient number of NE-/-PR3-/- NOD and NE+/+PR3+/+ NOD mice for the study, excessively-long duration of each round of animal study (almost 52 years from generation to characterization of mice), repletion of experiments to obtain reproducible data and shortage of animal holding space, the completion of this project was delayed, which led to late submission of our manuscript. Nevertheless, all the objectives proposed in the proposal have now been realized.

17128115.label: Major findings and research outcome
17128115.value: We have obtained a series of genetic, pharmacological and clinical evidence demonstrating that transient elevation of neutrophils and neutrophil-secreted two major neutrophil proteases (NSPs, including NE and PR3) in the pancreas of neonatal NOD mice as an obligatory driver for the onset of type-1 diabetes (T1D) by facilitating the crosstalk between two major types of innate immune cells (neutrophils and macrophages). Furthermore, we discovered the therapeutic potential of NE/ inhibitors for early invention of autoimmune diabetes. The major findings are summarized below: 1. There is a transient infiltration of neutrophils into pancreatic islets of neonatal NOD mice, peaking at 17 days of age and then declining gradually to a baseline level prior to development of overt diabetes. This change is mirrored by a transient elevation of NE and PR3 protein levels and enzymatic activities in both pancreatic islets and bloodstream of NOD mice; 2. Genetic ablation of NE and PR3 in NOD mice leads to a marked delay in onset time and a significant reduction in the incidence of T1D, accompanied with alleviation of insulitis and β-cell destruction. 3. Treatment with either recombinant elafin (a ~6 Kda endogenous inhibitor of NE and PR3 selective) or a highly-selective chemical inhibitor of NE (sivelestat) at the neonatal stage is sufficient to ameliorate the late development of immune cell infiltration, insulitis, β-cell loss and diabetes in NOD mice; 4. Sivelestat treatment decreases cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and compromises pathogenic T helper cells (Th1 and Th17 cells) in spleen, pancreatic islets and lymph nodes of NOD mice, but has no obvious effect on the frequencies of Th2 (CD4+IL4+) and Treg (CD4+foxp3+) cells. Importantly, the frequency and absolute cell numbers of pancreas-resident CD11b+F4/80+ macrophages of NOD are substantially attenuated by treatment with sivelestat, accompanied by reduced expression of a panel of pro-inflammatory cytokines. 5. Mechanistically, sivelestat suppresses the effects of NE and PR3 on activation of NF-κB signaling pathway and production of proinflammatory cytokines in both pancreatic β-cells and macrophages, and also blocks NE-stimulated macrophage migration through inhibition of NE-induced activation of Toll-like receptor4 (TLR4). The pro-inflammatory effect of NE and PR3 are largely blocked by the TLR4 antagonist CLI-095 (see part C, c8 item#1; C10, C11). Additionally, with the partial support of this grant, we have conducted a well-controlled exercise intervention study in the Chinese population, and discovered gut microbiota and its metabolic as key molecular transducer in mediating the benefits of exercise in diabetes prevention (see part C, 8 iem#2, C11). We have also obtained solid evidence that dysbiosis of gut microbiota is a culprit for the transient neutrophil infiltration and release of NSPs, thereby leading to T1D.

17128115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17128115.value: The findings from the present study have firmly established the role of neutrophil elastase (NE) and proteinase-3 (PR3) as obligatory molecules for driving autoimmune attack of insulin-producing beta cells in the pathogenesis of type-1 diabetes. Additionally, this project enabled us to establish a comprehensive range of unique research tools for both basic and translational research on these two major neutrophil serine proteases, including NE/PR3 double knockout mice, high throughput NE/PR3immunoassays and enzymatic assays for screening and optimization of their inhibitors for possible therapeutic applications. We will take advantage of these unique platforms to further explore the roles of NE and PR3 in other inflammatory diseases in which neutrophils have been implicated, such as atherosclerosis. A grant from Health and Medical Research Fund of 1,159,010 $HK has been secured to work on this project. Furthermore, based on the findings from this project and our previous study (Wang Y, Diabetes, 2014), we have been granted with a US patent (US9625460B2, see part C, section 11), and this patent has been licensed to Immunodiagnostics Ltd through HKU Technology Transfer Office to develop NE and PR3-related products for diagnostic and/or therapeutic applications. We will also seek support from Innovation & Technology Council to develop humanized monoclonal antibodies against NE/PR3 for therapeutic applications.

17128115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17128115.value: Type 1 diabetes (T1D), also known as juvenile diabetes, is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system is activated to destroy beta cells in the pancreas which produce insulin. There is currently no cure for T1D, and daily injection with insulin is the only medication. To develop more effective strategy for prevention and treatment of T1D, it is of paramount importance to uncover the early pathogenic event which initiate the autoimmune attack of islet beta cells. In this project, we have identified a transient elevation of neutrophil serine proteases (NSPs), which occurs in the early neonatal age, as an obligatory driver for the initiation of autoimmune destruction of beta cells in pancreatic islets, Furthermore, we demonstrated that inhibition of NSPs activities with either the pharmacological or biological inhibitors at an early age is sufficient to reduce the onset and incidence of T1D. These findings provide solid scientific evidence supporting the key pathogenic role of dysfunctional neutrophils, which are the most abundant type of innate immune cells in our body, in triggering the onset of autoimmune diabetes, and also raise the possibilities to use neutrophil elastases and proteinase-3 as novel biomarkers for risk stratification, early diagnosis and therapeutic intervention of this chronic disease. Given that NE inhibitors (such as Sivelestate and Elafin) have already been developed for treatment of various inflammatory diseases, our results may help to expand the therapeutic applications of these drug candidates to autoimmune diabetes

17128215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128215.value: TAC3是速激肽成员之一，它的成熟肽神经激肽B（NKB）最近被发现能够通过调控下丘脑中kisspeptin和GnRH的水平引致哺乳动物垂体分泌促黄体生成素（LH）。然而在哺乳动物中关于NKB在垂体中的直接作用尚不清楚。与哺乳动物不同，鱼类TAC3基因除了NKB编码外还有一个在高等脊椎动物中没有被发现的短肽，我们将其命名为NKB相关肽(NKBRP)，目前关于NKBRP的功能仍所知甚少。最近，通过体内实验发现斑马鱼TAC3成熟肽NKB與NKBRP也能够促进体内LH分泌，并且在高浓度时这些鱼类速激肽还可激活人类的速激肽受体NK3R。以草鱼这种中国养殖规模最大的商品鱼作为研究对象，我们首先克隆并取得草鱼TAC3a和TAC3b两个TAC3基因亚型。利用蛋白质组分析技术我们也在草鱼的下丘脑-垂体轴中检测到了这两个基因的产物，它们分别是TAC3a成熟肽NKBa和NKBRPa以及TAC3b成熟肽NKBb和NKBRPb。利用草鱼原代培养细胞作为研究模型，我们发现上述四个TAC3成熟肽并不能改变垂体中LH的分泌和基因表达量，不过他们却能提升垂体中生长泌乳素α（SLα）的蛋白分泌和mRNA水平。SLα是鱼类垂体分泌的一种主要激素，它能够调控鱼类体色、生殖、生长以及免疫等重要功能。在近期的研究中，我们有如下几个新发现：（i）TAC3成熟肽NKB與NKBRP对SLα蛋白分泌和mRNA表达量的调控是通过结合垂体中的NK3R受体及其偶聯之cAMP/PKA、PLC/PKC和Ca2+/CaMK-II信号通路完成的;（ii）NKBb可以作为NK3R受体的拮抗剂进而阻断另外三个TAC3成熟肽对NK3R的受體結合和激活，这种拮抗作用来源于其序列中FXGLM保守区最后一个蛋氨酸（M）突变为亮氨酸（L）；（iii）胰岛素样生长因子（IGF-I和-II）能够显著提升TAC3成熟肽对SLα mRNA表达水平的上行调控作用，而这种增強效應可能是由於IGF对NK3R表达的诱导以及IGF-I受体与NK3R受体之间通过PI3K/Akt信号通路串联引起的。在本课题中，我们将进一步探明TAC3成熟肽在草鱼垂体细胞中对SLα调控的機理，其具体研究目标如下：（i）阐明TAC3成熟肽诱导SLα基因表达过程中受体后信号通路与转录调节因子或顺式元件之间的耦合作用；（ii）阐明NKBb中FXGLM保守区结构改变导致其对SLα诱导的拮抗作用产生的分子机制；（iii）揭开NK3R上行调控与NK3R和IGF-I受体信号通路串联在IGF诱导SLα表达增势作用产生的功能角色。我们的研究将为TAC3/NK3R系统在鱼类垂体中的功能提供新观点與发展方向，并能提升我们对速激肽在垂体中功能进化的理解。由于鱼类NKB和NKBRP也能激活人类NK3R受体并且速激肽激动剂已被用于人类疾病的治疗，我们关于NKBb结构变化而形成拮抗作用的研究也将为新型NK3R拮抗剂的研制提供指导方向。

17128215.label: Realisation of objectives
17128215.value: The project on somatolactin α (SLα) regulation in fish model by TAC3 gene products, namely neurokinin B (NKB) and NKB-related peptide (NKBRP), was started in 2014 and the funding support was granted in 2015. The major findings based on the project since 2014 can be summarized as follows: (I) Receptor specificity & signal transduction for pituitary actions by TAC1/3 gene products in grass carp Using grass carp as a model for fish species, two forms of carp TAC3, TAC3a & TAC3b, and three subtypes of neurokinin (NK) receptors, NK1R, NK2R & NK3R, were cloned and confirmed to be expressed in the carp pituitary by RT-PCR. Using in situ hybridization and RT-PCR coupled to LCM isolation of different types of pituitary cells, TAC3a & 3b expression were located in somatotrophs, gonadotrophs & lactotrophs while NK1R, NK2R & NK3R signals could be detected in gonadotrophs, lactotrophs and somatolactotrophs, respectively. In grass carp pituitary cell culture, the gene products of TAC3a (NKBa & NKBRPa) and TAC3b (NKBb & NKPRPb) were all effective in triggering SLα secretion, SL production and SLα mRNA expression via NK3R activation with parallel rises in prolactin (PRL) release, PRL production and PRL transcript level via NK2R activation. For the TAC3 gene products tested, the efficacy of NKBb on SLα and PRL induction was much lower than that of NKBa, NKBRPa & NKBRPb. Apparently, SLα signals induced by TAC3 gene products were mediated by cAMP/PKA, PLC/IP3/PKC and Ca2+/ CaM/CaMK-II cascades coupled with NK3R activation. The post-receptor signaling for PRL responses was found to be similar except for the absence of PKC component with functional coupling to NK2R activation. These results indicate that TAC3 gene products can act as novel stimulators for SLα and PRL in carp species through overlapping mechanisms for signal transduction coupled to NK2R & NK3R expressed in the respective cell types within the carp pituitary. Since TAC1 & TAC3 are members of tachykinin gene family and their gene products are known to have cross-reactivity at receptor level, grass carp TAC1 coding for substance P (SP) and neurokinin A (NKA) was also cloned and confirmed to be expressed in lactotrophs in the carp pituitary. Consistent with the cell-type specific expression of NK1R, NK2R & NK3R, the TAC1 gene products were shown to have regulatory actions on luteinizing hormone (LH), PRL and SLα in carp pituitary cells. In this case, carp SP & NKA could induce LH, PRL & SLα secretion with parallel rises in PRL & SLα transcript levels. Interestingly, short-term incubation (3 hr) with SP but not NKA was effective in inducing LH release while prolong treatment of SP (24 hr) could reduce LH mRNA expression. At pituitary cell level, LH, PRL and SLα regulation by TAC1 gene products were shown to be mediated by NK1R, NK2R & NK3R, respectively. Apparently, SP- and NKA-induced LH and SLα secretion & transcript expression were mediated by AC/cAMP/PKA, PLC/IP3/PKC, and Ca2+/CaM/CaMK-II cascades. The signal transduction for PRL responses was similar despite the lack of a PKC component. For LH mRNA responses, the cAMP/PKA- and PLC/PKC-dependent mechanisms but not the Ca2+-dependent cascades were involved in the inhibitory effect by SP. These results, taken together, suggest that TAC1 & TAC3 gene products in grass carp can play a role in LH, PRL & SLα regulation through different subtypes of NK receptors expressed at the pituitary level. (Results published in Endocrinology 155:3582-3596 and 158:1776-1797.) (II) NK3R expression in SLα induction by the synergistic effect of IGF-I, SLα and TAC3 gene products In our previous studies with carp pituitary cells, IGF-I was shown to be a potent stimulator for SLα synthesis & secretion and SLα released at pituitary level can also exert a local stimulation on its own production. For pituitary interactions of IGF-I & SLα with TAC3 gene products, we have the novel findings that co-treatment of TAC3 gene products with IGF-I and SLα respectively could lead to potentiation of SLα mRNA expression (up to 4-6 fold basal) and these potentiating effects were mediated by NK3R activation and cAMP/PKA-, PLC/PKC-, and Ca2+-dependent mechanisms. Of note, the stimulatory effect on SLα gene expression could be further enhanced (up 14-fold basal) by co-treatment of IGF-I, SLα & individual TAC3 gene products. In our studies, IGF-I and SLα were both effective in elevating NK3R mRNA level in carp pituitary cells via PI3K/Akt and MAPK cascades. Besides, JAK2/STAT5 pathway was shown to be involved for the NK3R responses by SLα but not IGF-I. In the case of IGF-I potentiation, additivity of IGF-I stimulation with cAMP/PKA- & Ca2+-dependent mechanisms and potentiation of NKB/NKBRP on IGF-induced Akt activation were also observed. These results, as a whole, suggest that TAC3 gene products may act in a synergistic manner with IGF-I and SLα produced locally in carp pituitary to stimulate SLα gene expression by NK3R up-regulation & functional crosstalk in post-receptor signalling. (Results published in Sci Rep 6:36102 and Cells 8:887.) (III) NKBb as a novel antagonist for NK3R activation and SLα regulation in carp pituitary cells In our cloning study, NKBb encoded by carp TAC3b was found to be structurally distinct from the other TAC3 gene products with an M to L substitution in the C-terminal signature motif “FXGLM” of the tachykinin family. In addition, the bioactivity of NKBb in stimulating SLα release, SLα production & SLα mRNA expression was much weaker than that of NKBa, NKBRPa & NKBRPb. The same is also true for its stimulatory effects on cAMP level & Ca2+ signals in carp pituitary cells. In HEK293 cells with carp NK3R expression, unlike the high affinity binding of other TAC3 gene products, NKBb was found to have a low binding affinity for NK3R. In carp pituitary cells, co-treatment with high dose of NKBb was effective in reducing/blocking the stimulatory effects of NKBa, NKBRPa & NKBRPb on SLα synthesis & secretion, implying that NKBb, besides its weak agonistic effect, can also act as an antagonist for other TAC3 gene products. Using NMR spectroscopy, the solution structures of other TAC3 gene product with an intact FXGLM motif was confirmed to be a helical peptide, which is not the case for the random coil structure of NKBb with a mutated FXGLL motif. Interestingly, an L to M mutation in NKBb to restore the signature motif, which can also resume the helical structure based on NMR analysis, was shown to notably enhance its binding to NK3R expressed in HEK293 cells and elevate its stimulation on SLα release/gene expression in carp pituitary cells. In contrast, an M to L mutation in other TAC3 gene products in the same motif was all effective in reducing their binding affinity for NK3R & efficacy in SLα regulation at pituitary cell level. These findings suggest that the M to L substitution in the signature motif of NKBb can disrupt its helical structure and turn it into a competitive antagonist at NK3R level for other TAC3 gene products in the carp pituitary. (Our collaborator is in the process of constructing the docking models for NK3R binding with the NMR structures of the wild type & mutated forms of NKBb to complete the manuscript for submission.)

17128215.label: Major findings and research outcome
17128215.value: (I) Demonstration for the first time for the direct pituitary actions of the gene products of TAC1 (SP & NKA) and TAC3 (NKBa/b & NKBRPa/b) on LH, PRL and SLα regulation in grass carp through overlapping post-receptor signaling mechanisms (including cAMP/PKA, PLC/IP3/PKC & Ca2+/CaM/CaMK-II cascades) functionally coupled to NK1R, NK2R & NK3R expressed in gonadotrophs, lactotrophs and somatolactotrophs, respectively. (Objective #1 of our proposal) (II) Unveil the signal transduction mechanisms for pituitary expression of NK3R induced by IGF-I (via PI3K/Akt & MAPK cascades) and SLα (via PI3K/Akt, MAPK & JAK2/STAT5 pathways) and elucidate the role of NK3R up-regulation and functional crosstalk in post-receptor signaling (especially for Akt activation) in the synergistic action of TAC3 gene products with IGF-I and SLα in stimulating SLα gene expression in carp pituitary cells. (Objective #3 of our proposal) (III) Discovery of the novel action of NKBb encoded by TAC3b as a competitive antagonist for NK3R binding and activation against the stimulatory effects of NKBa, NKBRPa & NKBRPb on SLα secretion & gene expression in carp pituitary cells and confirming that the antagonistic property of NKBb (in terms of NK3R binding, cAMP/Ca2+ signaling and SLb responses) could be traced back to the M to L substitution in the signature motif of the tachykinin family, which could disrupt the helical structure of NKBb peptide for receptor binding/activation. (Objective #2 of our proposal)

17128215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17128215.value: In our studies with carp pituitary cells, we have found that TAC3 gene products, especially NKBa, NKBRPa & NKBRPb, could also elevate CREB, c-Fos and c-Jun mRNA levels with parallel rises in SLα primary transcript & mature mRNA. Our preliminary studies also revealed that the stimulatory actions on gene expression of the three transcription factors & SLα primary transcript were mediated through activation of cAMP/PKA- and PLC/PKC-dependent mechanisms coupled with NK3R activation. Consistent with the presence of CRE & AP-1 binding sites in the proximal promoter of grass carp SLα promoter, over-expression of CREB and c-Fos in HEK293 cells after transfection with a Luc reporter carrying a carp SLα promoter could also increase SLα promoter activity. These results, taken together, suggest that SLα mRNA expression induced by TAC3 gene products may also involve SLα gene transcription via promoter activation through increased production of CREB and AP-1 transcription factors. These findings for sure can serve as the basis for our follow-up studies in carp model for transcriptional regulation of SLα gene expression by TAC3 gene products via up-regulation of CREB & AP-1 signals at the pituitary level.

17128215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17128215.value: Somatolactin (SL) is a pituitary hormone in fish models with regulatory functions in background adaptation, growth & adipogenicity, osmoregulation, reproduction & immune responses and its manipulation is known to have potential implications for fish farming, especially related to induced spawning & growth performance in commercial species and spreading of diseases in high density fish culture. Our findings of TAC1 & 3 gene products as novel regulators for LH, PRL & SLα secretion & gene expression as well as the mechanisms & post-receptor signaling involved in the synergistic effect of IGF-I with TAC3 gene products, namely NKB & NKBRP, on SLα gene expression have provided new information on SL regulation at the pituitary level in fish model. Our study on the antagonistic effect of NKBb with a single a.a. substitution in the tachykinin signature motif also provides new insight on the structure-activity relationship of NKB & NKBRP for receptor binding & activation. The information will have a significant impact on the design of new analogs for NK receptors, which could be useful not only for fish farming but also for clinical studies on human diseases associated with dysregulation of tachykinins/their receptors.

17128315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128315.value: Cells are able to respond to mechanical signals. Engineering the mechanical microenvironment of stem cells by controlling substrate rigidity or applying external force impacts cell survival, orientation, proliferation and differentiation. Nevertheless, our understanding of how stem cells sense and respond to mechanical signals is still poor, preventing us from optimizing the loading regimes for functional tissue engineering. We and others have used 3D matrix models to demonstrate that human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) respond to mechanical loading (including tension, compression and torsion) by becoming aligned in a specific direction. Cell alignment is an important property enabling proper functioning of many tissues and is hence a critical parameter in functional tissue engineering. Nevertheless, the loading-induced cell alignment that occurs in a matrix with a randomly-oriented meshwork challenges our traditional understanding regarding the necessity of having aligned substrates. By encapsulating hMSCs in 3D collagen matrix and delivering dynamic compression, we recently identified the omni-directional formation of finger-like pericellular matrix-degrading actin protrusions immediately after loading. Well-known actin protrusions of the cell membrane include lamellipodia, filopodia, podosomes and invadopodia. These compression-induced actin protrusions (CAPs) are morphologically different from lamellipodia and podosomes but similar to filopodia and invadopodia although they differ from filopodia in their prolonged stability and resistance to cdc42 signaling. They are compositionally most similar to invadopodia as they exhibit pericellular matrix degradation, however, they differ from invadopodia in their abundance and cdc42-independent signaling. Interestingly, a few hours after the removal of compression loading, these protrusions and indeed the entire actin meshwork disassemble to form actin patches throughout the cell and the actin meshwork recovers fully within 24 hours. These novel findings prompt us to hypothesize that the CAPs might be important mediators of the compression-induced formation of cell alignment. Specifically, we would like to investigate: (1) the molecular signature and hence the identity of the CAPs; (2) the major signaling pathways involved in regulating the formation of the CAPs; (3) the functional significance of the CAPs in mediating loading-induced cell alignment. Our recent discovery of CAPs has already made an impact in the mechanobiology field due to the novel nature of these mechano-sensitive subcellular structures. The long-term impact of this project will be its contribution to the development of optimal loading regimes that control cell alignment when engineering functional tissues in bioreactors. 壓縮引起的肌動蛋白突起（CAPS）在人類間充質幹細胞 - 了解機械調節機制 细胞能够以机械信号做出响应。通过控制基片的刚性或施加外力影响细胞存活，取向，增殖和分化工程干细胞的机械微环境。尽管如此，我们对干细胞如何感知和机械信号作出反应的认识仍然较差，阻止我们优化装载制度的功能性组织工程。 我们和其他人已经使用3D矩阵模型证明人类间质干细胞（hMSC）的培养通过在特定方向上变得对齐响应机械负荷（包括拉伸，压缩和扭转）。细胞对齐是有利的许多组织的适当运作的一个重要特性，因此是在功能性组织工程的关键参数。然而，发生在同一个随机取向小梁矩阵装载诱导的细胞排列挑战我们对具有对准基板的必要性传统认识。 通过在3D胶原基质包封的hMSCs和提供动态压缩，我们最近发现的全向形成的指状细胞外基质降解的肌动蛋白的突起装入后立即使用。细胞膜的知名肌动蛋白突起包括伪足，丝状伪足，足体和侵袭伪足。这些压缩诱导肌动突起（CAPS）是从伪足和足体形态不同，但相似的丝状伪足和侵袭伪足尽管它们从丝状伪足不同在其长期稳定性和抗CDC42信令。它们是组成上最相似的侵袭伪足，因为它们表现出细胞外基质降解，然而，他们从侵袭伪足不同的丰度和Cdc42无关信令。有趣的是，在除去压缩负载之后的几个小时中，这些突出部乃至整个肌动蛋白小梁拆机而形成的肌动蛋白斑块整个细胞和肌动蛋白网状组织恢复完全的24小时内。 这些新的发现促使我们推测这种的CAP可能是压缩诱导形成细胞对准的重要介质。具体地，我们想研究：（1）分子組成; （2）参与调节的CAP的形成主要的信号通路; （3）在介导装载诱导的细胞对准的通行证的功能意义。 该项目的长期影响将是其在生物反应器工程的功能组织的发展作出贡献。

17128315.label: Realisation of objectives
17128315.value: Aim 1 – To study the molecular signature of the CAPs; We have fully realized Aim 1 by identifying a number of molecular markers which are highly expressed and co-localized with the F-actin in the compression-induced CAPs. CAPs are compression-induced actin protrusions. We have firstly induced the formation of CAPs by mechanically loading hMSCs encapsulated in collagen meshwork using cyclic compression. We have identified the optimal protocol to stimulate the formation of CAPs. In order to define the molecular signatures of these CAPs, two approaches have been used. The first one is a systemic approach to study protein markers of CAPs by micro-dissecting CAPs from the stained sections of the microtissues exposed to compression loading and then conducting proteomics analysis using mass spectroscopy. However, this approach has some technical challenges. In particular, fixing and processing of the sample sections were necessary for immunofluorescence staining of the CAPs markers before micro-dissecting the tiny CAP structures at the cell-matrix interface of the hMSCs microencapsulated in collagen micro-tissues under compression loading using the fluorescence channel of the laser microdissection instrumentation. However, the fixing and processing of the samples ections with specific immunofluorescence staining inevitably and chemically crosslinked the protein components of the CAPs, adversely affecting the amount and the identity, and hence the validity of proteins detected during the mass spectroscopy proteomics analysis. As a result, we focused on using the targeted approach to study the expression of different actin cytoskeleton and molecules associated with cell-matrix interactions, using immunofluorescence staining, western blotting and real time PCR, etc, and hence identifying the molecular markers of the CAPs by assessing the level of expression, the localization and the extent of co-localization of individual marker with the F-actin staining of the actin protrusions. There are many types of actin protrusions and the well-known ones are filopodia, lamellipodia, invadopodia and podosomes. We have conducted a comparison in the characteristics and molecular markers of the CAPs with that of the other well-known actin protrusions. The molecular markers with high expression and at least partially co-localize with the CAPs have been identified and these markers have been used to identify CAPs in the subsequent studies. Aim 2 - To study the major signaling pathways regulating the CAPs; We have fully realized Aim 2 by demonstration of the critical significance of a particular type of RhoGTPases in regulating the formation of CAPs among the three major ones we have investigated. Three major RhoGTPases signaling pathways regulating actin cytoskeleton organization and dynamics including CDC42, Rac1 and RhoA and their associated molecules have been investigated, using immunofluorescence staining, western blotting, GTPase activity assays and real time PCR. The significant role of these signaling pathways particularly the upstream master regulators and selected downstream effectors have also been investigated using two approaches, chemical inhibition of the activities of the GTPases and knock-down of the GTPase using specific siRNAs. In particular, specific chemical inhibitors of the GTPases were supplemented to the culture medium before and during compression prior to subsequent evaluation of the CAPs structures and the associated molecules of the three major types of RhoGTPase (CDC42, Rac1 and RhoA). The cell morphology, the immunopositivity and level of expression of the major molecular markers identified from Aim 1, the presence and the number of CAPs formed upon compression loading, the expression level of the major GTPase regulators and their activities have been evaluated to determine the significance of the these signaling pathways in CAPs formation. Aim 3 - To study the functional significance of the CAPs and associated structures. We have fully realized Aim 3 by verifying the function of the identified CAPs and associated structures. After identifying the major RhoGTPase regulatory signaling pathway from Aim 2, the identity of the CAPs could be revealed, in conjunction with the positive expression of various molecular markers identified from Aim 1. We then verified the functional significance of the CAPs by conducting a few functional assays related to the identified actin protrusions, specifically, the matrix digestion assay and the cell motility assay. Moreover, the CAPs were formed at the cell-matrix interface upon compression and hence cell-matrix interactions should reveal important functional significance of the CAPs. Therefore, we have also studied a few signaling pathways related to cell-matrix interactions including integrin alpha v and alpha 5 as well as the mechanosensing YAP signaling, using immunofluorescence staining, western blotting, proximity binding assay, etc. Mature cell-matrix adhesion structures named 3D matrix adhesions (3DMA) have been identified for the first time in hMSCs upon mechanical loading and upon incorporation of fibronectin matrix in the scaffold materials, and a few functional assays of these structures, in particular, proliferation and differentiation of hMSCs under compression loading have been conducted.

17128315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17128315.value: Aim 1 – We have characterized the CAPs and identified molecular markers which are highly expressed and co-localized with F-actin. CAPs are compression-induced, slender and branched actin protrusions with a diameter of several hundred nanometers and a length of several microns and are stable for >1 hour. CAPs are omni-directional to the long axis of hMSCs upon compression loading, and are F-actin positive, co-localized extensively with cortactin and MMP14, partially with Arp2/3 and integrin beta 1. CAPs exhibit characteristics similar to those of invadopodia and lamellipodia (Paper 1). Aim 2 - We have demonstrated the critical significance of Rac1 GTPase in enabling compression-induced CAP formation. Chemical inhibitor of Rac1, but not that of CDC42 and RhoA, significantly reduced the CAPs formed upon compression induction. Silencing a downstream effector of Rac1, namely CTTN, also significantly reduced the number of CAPs. Moreover, from the fact that compensatory upregulation of Rac1 and downstream effectors upon siCTTN treatment did not lead to CAP formation, we concluded that Rac1 plays a supporting or enabling role in the compression-induced CAP formation while it is the compression loading that is the necessary inducer of CAPs (Paper 1). Aim 3 - We have revealed the functional significance of the identified CAPs and associated cell-matrix adhesion structures. From Aims 1 & 2, the identity of CAPs should be lamellipodia, which are known to facilitate cell migration and matrix degradation. Monitoring cell movement in 3D did not reveal any global movement of cells. The matrix degradation function of CAPs was demonstrated by the presence of two most extensively expressed markers CTTN and MMP14, which are both associated with matrix degradation, and the identification of an immediate digestion zone at the proximity of CAPs, through immunofluorescence staining of Col 2 3/4Cshort. Another associated cell-matrix interface structure induced by compression is mature and elongated 3D matrix adhesions (3DMA), with high aspect ratio and molecular composition of integrin alpha 5, fibronectin and paxillin, aligning well with the main axis of hMSCs, suggesting that after creating a digestion zone, cells adapted to long term compression by formation of mature 3DMAs, revealing the functional significance of 3DMA in mechanical adaptation associated cell alignment. Another function of 3DMA is to potentiate osteogenesis of hMSCs (Paper 2). Furthermore, these 3DMAs are also inducible by incorporating fibronectin into collagen scaffolds (Paper 3) and other culture substrates (Other output 1).

17128315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17128315.value: This study discovered for the first time, two novel structures at the cell-matrix interface, namely CAPs and 3DMAs, in hMSCs upon compression loading. Both structures exhibited significant functions in determining the fate of hMSCs in mechanical loading-induced cell alignment and mechanical loading-potentiated osteogenesis. The knowledge generated contributed to better understanding of the molecular mechanisms of mechanoregulation of hMSCs in 3D context. Whether these structures could be induced by mechanical loading in cells other than hMSCs such as chondrocytes, osteoblasts, tenoblasts and intervertebral disc cells, and whether other modes of mechanical loading such as tension and torsion also alter cell fate via the formation of these novel structures, are interesting questions to explore before we can generalizing the conclusion about the compression loading-induced CAPs and 3DMAs formation as a common molecular mechanism for mechanoregulation. The immediate impact is the derivation of a loading regime for (1) functional tissue engineering for tissues where cell alignment is important such as osteochondral tissue; and (2) stem cell-based osteochondral tissue engineering where osteogenesis is critical. One immediate research project to follow is to study the role of mechanical loading in engineering complex osteochondral tissues with biomimetic zonal organization and the underlying mechanisms involved.

17128315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17128315.value: Our group has established a series of mechanical loading-based bioreactors with the aim to engineer functional tissues. Our earlier studies have demonstrated the effects of mechanical loading in altering the cell fate of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) including cell alignment. Here, we delineated the molecular mechanism of loading-induced alignment formation by discovering for the first time, two novel structures at the cell-matrix interface, namely compression-induced actin protrusions (CAPs) and 3D matrix adhesions (3DMAs), in hMSCs upon compression loading. By characterizing the molecular composition, identifying their identities, delineating the regulatory signaling pathways and verifying the functional significances of these structures, we concluded that these structures exhibited important functions of mechanical loading-induced cell alignment and mechanical loading-potentiated osteogenesis, respectively. This work explained our previous observation of mechanical loading induced changes in hMSCs and contributed to better understanding of the mechanoregulation mechanism of hMSCs in 3D context. The immediate impact is the derivation of a loading regime or protocol for functional tissue engineering for tissues where cell alignment and/or differentiation are important and one illustrating example is osteochondral (cartilage-bone) tissue engineering. In the long run, this work contributes to development of bioreactor-based functional tissue engineering and associated therapeutic strategies.

17128515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17128515.value: Recent genome-wide association studies have contributed important insights into the genetic architecture of common human diseases. The findings indicate that these diseases are typically under the influence of a very large number (at least hundreds) of sequence variants. Both common and rare variants are involved, with a wide range of effect sizes. The majority of the genetic factors for complex diseases discovered to date appear to have very small effect size, with allelic odds ratio of less than 1.5. These sequence variants collectively explain only a modest proportion, typically less than 25%, of the overall heritability, even for the best-studied diseases. The two alternative explanations of missing heritability: rare variants not captured by GWAS or common variants with effect sizes too small for current GWAS, have important implications for future research strategy. If missing heritability is due largely to rare variants, then one should abandon GWAS and move on to whole-genome sequencing (WGS), which is able to capture rare as well as common variants. On the other hand, if hidden heritability is due largely to common variants of very small effect size, then GWAS with very large sample size would be the most efficient strategy, since WGS remains much more expensive than GWAS on a per-subject basis. Thus, estimating the overall contribution of common variants to complex diseases is important for determining the future strategy of genetic research. The proposed method aims to estimate the variance (of a quantitative phenotype or of the liability to a binary disease phenotype) explained by a set of corrected genetic variants, using only GWAS summary statistics (p-values). It aggregates estimated variant-specific contributions to variance explained, with appropriate discount for pairwise linkage disequilibrium. The method produces a standard error for the estimated variance explained, and can be extended to bivariate analysis of two phenotypes. In addition to application to real data, we will also develop a website to update the estimated variance explained from GWAS of quantitative traits and complex disorders. This will help to monitor progress in explaining the genetics of complex traits and disorders. 17128515.label: Realisation of objectives
17128515.value: A method for estimating the contribution of common variants was developed in the PhD thesis of Sam Choi. This model was applied to the problem of prediction of polygenic traits from genome-wide SNP information by post-doctoral Timothy Mak, who developed two methods of individual disease risk prediction using GWAS data, one based on local true discovery rate weighting, and the other based on a modification of LASSO for summary GWAS statistics. GWAS methods were applied to the study of the genetics of lipid levels in East Asians, resulting in 2 major papers reporting the discovery of novel or population-specific genetic variants for blood lipid levels, variants which also influenced the risk of cardiovascular disease. Finally, we developed a power statistical test to map from GWAS data the genes that are most likely to be causally related to a disease, and applied it to schizophrenia, detecting 185 genes, which implicate gene networks important in post-natal brain development. The software of this method is freely available to the community.
