17128515.label: Major findings and research outcome
17128515.value: The genetics of schizophrenia – the contribution of common variants and genes implicated in a maternal immune activation model (SW Choi, PhD thesis, 2016). A method was developed for estimating the contribution of common genetic variants to the heritability of a complex disease from GWAS summary statistics, which gave an estimate of 0.185 for schizophrenia. Genes associated with schizophrenia are enriched in differentially expressed genes in an maternal immune activation mouse model of schizophrenia, and SGK1 may be a mediator of the beneficial effect of n-3 PUFA rich diet in this model. Local true discovery rate weighted polygenic scores using GWAS summary data (Mak et al. 2016, Behavior Genetics). We developed a method of improving the predictive accuracy of polygenic risk scores, by weighting the estimated effect sizes of SNPs by their local true discovery rates, obtained from the empirical distribution of the p-values of the association tests of the SNPs. Polygenic scores via penalised regression on summary statistics. (Mak et al. 2017 Genetic Epidemiology; Awarded Robert Elston Prize). We developed an improved method of polygenic risk score calculation which takes account of linkage disequilbrium between SNPs). The method can be applied to summary statistics for the association between disease and SNPs, so that individual phenotype and genotype data are not needed. Exome-wide association analysis reveals novel coding sequence variants associated with lipid traits in Chinese. (Tang et al. 2015 Nature Communications). This is the first large-scale GWAS of blood lipid levels in Chinese. We discovered 3 novel Chinese-specific risk variants, and showed that the effect sizes of SNPs on blood lipids (in particular LDL cholesterol) are linearly related to their effect sizes on coronary heart dieases, confirming a causal relationship between blood lipid levels and coronary heart disease. Exome chip meta-analysis identifies novel loci and East Asian-specific coding variants that contribute to lipid levels and coronary heart disease. (Lu et al. 2017 Nature Genetics) This is the largest East Asian GWAS to date on blood lipids, and discovered 14 novel East Asian-specific risk variants. A powerful conditional gene-based association approach implicated functionally important genes for schizophrenia. (Li et al. 2018 Bioinformatics). We developed a conditional gene-based test to identify genes that are truly causal to a disease, and used to to identify 185 probable causal genes for schizophrenia. These genes are enriched in gene networks active in post-natal brain development.

17128515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17128515.value: Our work has contributed to the methodology and understanding in the field of common disease genetics, which is now entering an exciting new phase. A new international consortium - the ICDA (International Common Disease Alliance) was launched in September 2019, which aims to accelerate the progress of this field, from genetic mapping to biological mechanisms to clinical applications (Maps to Mechanisms to Medicine, M2M2M). We have joined the mapping working group of this international effort. In Hong Kong, genomics is also gaining recognition, with the government's decision to build a new Hong Kong Genomics Institute. We will participate in this exciting initiative, and offer our expertise to facilitate research and translation which will benefit the local community.

17128515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17128515.value: Common diseases are caused by a combination of genetic and environmental factors, where the relative importance of genetic factors is measured by an index called heritability. We developed a new method to estimate of heritability from the results of genetic association studies comparing patients and controls on a genome-wide scale. and showed that the heritability of schizophrenia due to common genetic variation is 0.185. We also showed that genes associated with schizophrenia are enriched in a mouse model of schizophrenia. The results from genome-wide studies can also be used to make prediction of individual risk of developing common disease. We developed 2 new mw methods of calculation predicted risk that have important advantages over existing methods, in terms of accuracy and ease of calculation. Finally, only some of the results from a genome-wide study represent true causal effects. We developed a new statistical method for identifying these effects and applied it to discover 185 probably causal genes for schizophrenia. Interestingly, these genes are particularly involved in brain development after birth.

17128615.value: 磷酸化修飾是生物體內最重要的蛋白質翻譯後修飾之一,同時也是細胞生長,存活和凋亡的調控手段。 隨著質譜的分析最近的技術進步, 全景式的揭示細胞中蛋白質組的磷酸化狀態在接受藥物治療後的變化-磷酸化蛋白質組學-已經成為可能。 天然小分子,特別是傳統中藥(TCM)的提取物,已經作為先導化合物用於研發治療疾病的藥物。 故而瞭解天然小分子的表型特徵和靶點對於開發有效和低毒藥物用於人類疾病的治療具有重大意義。 通過磷酸化蛋白質組學研究天然小分子及其衍生物在活細胞內的快速和暫態的效應,可以解釋其在不同類型的細胞中的作用機制,並可能説明我們理解中藥的多組分和多靶點的效應。 雷公藤是一種具有高毒性的中藥,並在過去數百年中被用於治療類風濕關節炎,系統性紅斑狼瘡,慢性腎炎和牛皮癬。 在本課題中,我們計畫利用目前最先進的磷酸化蛋白質組學技術對兩種從雷公藤中提取的小分子-雷公藤內酯醇(TL)和雷公藤紅素(CEL)在癌細胞中的作用進行差異性研究並嘗試描繪其靶向信號網路。 CEL和TL同樣具有抗癌, 抗炎和免疫抑制活性的特性, 這意味著它們同時影響多個信號通路, 完全適用磷酸化蛋白質組學進行差異分析。 本專案的另一個目的在於通過生物化學,分子生物學和細胞生物學技術等多種技術手段來研究新發現的磷酸化蛋白在細胞週期和凋亡的調控功能及其後繼效應。 儘管TL和CEL同樣體現出雷公藤對於多種癌症的抗腫瘤活性,相對而言TL為更有效及毒性更強。 因此,剖析TL和CEL作用機制在不同類別的腫瘤細胞的異同將有機會闡明導致其差異的分子機制。 本專案將提供TL和CEL分子層面上作用機理的異同,為理解它們在不同類型的癌症的作用機制和「脫靶」效應提供線索。

17128615.label: Realisation of objectives
17128615.value: To perform differential phosphoproteomic analysis in cancer cells treated with TL or CEL and dissect common and distinct TL and CEL regulated signaling pathways We used a SILAC-based MS approach to identify and quantify the global change of phosphorylation events in HeLa S3 cells in response to TL treatment. HeLa S3 cells labeled with heavy arginine (L-Arginine-HCl, 13C6, 15N4) and lysine (L-Lysine, 13C6, 15N2) were treated with 100 nM TL in DMSO for 30 minutes, and cells labeled with light lysine and arginine were treated with DMSO as control. Equal amount of extracted total cellular proteins from both control and treatment group were then mixed for downstream phosphoproteomics analysis. The protein sample was first digested following the standard in-solution digestion protocol. Then the phosphopeptides were enriched by two-step SIMAC protocol and subjected to Orbitrap MS analysis. Identification of the phosphopeptides and measurement of the relative abundance of particular site between two labeled group (i.e. the control and treatment group) were performed using the MaxQuant software (Version 1.6.2.3) against Uniprot human database (2018_09). The whole experiments were then repeated for three times to increase data confidence and distinguish the technique differences brought up in the experimental procedure, and two reciprocal labeling between control and treatment group were employed to remove the potential bias introduced during the labeling process. All the data from six biological repeats were then searched individually for analysis. Phosphoproteomics analysis to compare the effect of TL and CEL in HCT116 and HeLa cell was also performed. Search for pathways and potential candidates that CEL regulates in both cell lines were carried out. For CEL, we found phosphorylation of Hsp90β was only marginally increased in HCT116 cells, but not induced at all in HeLa cells. Both S6 and HSP27 (Hsp beta-1) were significant induced in HeLa but not in HCT116 cells. Due to the detection limit of our Orbitrap mass spectrometry, the numbers phosphopeptides identified were not very high (below 2000), compared to the state-of-the-art high-resolution MS (nowadays phosphopeptide number can reach 5000-10000). The absence of adequate mass spectrometry service at HKU significantly hampered the progress of this project. Efforts were made to establish collaboration with MS experts in other institutions but some of the experiments need to be repeated to obtain higher phosphopeptide numbers. Nevertheless, given the existing MS data sets, we chose several proteins to perform further validations. To validate those newly identified phosphorylated proteins and to determine their functional consequences in regulation of cell cycle and apoptosis We chose five phosphosites of our interest for validation their TL-regulating pattern by western blot analysis, including Ser255 of Hsp90β, Ser235/Ser236 of ribosomal protein S6, Ser82 of Hsp27, Ser132/Ser133 double phosphorylation sites of HDGF, and T170 of CDK7. We performed western blot to analyze the regulatory pattern of the five phosphorylation sites upon TL treatment. For three selected phosphorylation sites, we performed site-directed mutagenesis and explored the relationship between phosphorylation events and TL-induced cell apoptosis. In particular, we focused on the mechanism of TL interaction with Hsp90β on the cell apoptosis.

17128615.label: Major findings and research outcome
17128615.value: In this study, our phosphoproteomics data on the short time response to TL treatment in a cancer cell lines provides a unique angle for studying the molecular mechanism of TL, as it is the first time to see TL simultaneously regulates the phosphorylation level of multiple signaling proteins from different signaling pathways within a short period of time. While kinases known to be regulated by TL such as CDKs are also found in the list, it is delighted to see signaling molecules like WNK1 or regulators of PP1 that are previously unknown to be associated with TL mechanism. The regulation over multiple kinases and phosphatase regulators suggested that TL induces an instant yet significant change over the whole signaling networks via manipulating activities of kinases / phosphatases simultaneously. More importantly, we observed a significant enrichment in the RNA splicing function in the ‘TL centric’ phosphoproteome, suggesting that TL might initiate a quick post-transcriptional regulation within 30 minutes of drug administration. TL-induced apoptosis occurs by release of cytochrome c and activation of caspase 3, and it is also known that TL inhibits expression of heat shock proteins (HSPs) during the process. However, it is currently unknown if TL regulate HSPs at PTM level. It is therefore particularly interesting to look into the two important HSP proteins, Hsp90β and Hsp27, phosphorylation status of which are found to be upregulated by TL in our study. Phosphorylation on both serine sites (Ser225 and Ser255) of Hsp90β are found to be up-regulated by TL and involved in TL-mediated cell death. Caspase markers and viability assay showed that TL-mediated cell apoptosis event is significantly reduced in de-phosphorylation mimic mutant of Hsp90β (Ser225Ala/Ser255Ala), which is probably a consequence of Hsp90β-Apaf1 complex stabilization as reported. In the case of Hsp27, our data show that TL probably also induces cell apoptosis via up-regulating the phosphorylation level of Hsp27, which consequently activates the caspase 9 and PARP cleavage. Thus TL up-regulates phosphorylation level of both Hsp90β and Hsp27 to activate the caspase-PARP pathway for apoptosis induction. Phosphoproteomics tools also enable us to discover some novel candidates that seem unrelated to TL function, such as HDGF. The double phosphorylation at residues Ser132/Ser133 has been identified to be the major (if not sole) phosphorylation event in response to TL treatment in HDGF. More interestingly, the phosphorylation status of HDGF is directly associated with TL-induced apoptosis, probably via activating PARP cleavage.

17128615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17128615.value: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of a large scale phosphoproteomics analysis on the drug mechanism of TL. We believe this study suggests that phosphoproteomics could be used as a powerful tool in studying drug mechanism, particular for multi-target drugs such as TL. The technology platform developed for ‘TL centric’ phosphoproteomics could be applied to the investigation of other bioactive natural products isolated from TCM, dissecting the multi-component and multi-target effects of TCM in modern drug discovery.

17128615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17128615.value: Protein phosphorylation, as one of the major post-translational modifications, serves critical roles in regulation of cell growth, survival, and apoptosis. Triptolide is one of the major active components from Tripterygium wilfordii Hook F, a traditional Chinese medicine widely used for centuries to treat a wide range of diseases. Triptolide has triggered tremendous interest due to its broad range of bioactivities including anti-cancer, anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive activities, while its analogues are widely utilized in clinical trials for various cancers. However, most of the studies focused on the long-term (treatment time in hours’ range) effects of TL, while studies on the rapid responses (within 30 minutes) are very limited. In this study we describe the first non-biased, quantitative phosphoproteomics analysis for the short-time response of triptolide in cancer cell line. Multiple novel phosphorylation sites that are responsive to triptolide treatment were identified. Regulatory pattern of five phosphorylation sites were confirmed by western blot. Most importantly, by using site-directed mutagenesis of three selected phosphorylation sites, these novel triptolide-regulated phosphorylation events were found of crucial importance to triptolide’s cell-killing effects, via caspase-PARP pathway.

17200415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200415.value: Stability analysis of electrical engineering systems has a history of over 100 years initially for power networks and subsequently motivated by problems in circuits, control, communications and larger power systems. The advances can be interpreted as dealing with increasing complexity from linear time-invariant systems to time-varying, time-delayed, nonlinear, large-scale and recently different types of hybrid systems including switching and impulsive effects. Most results tend to deal with these complexities separately or maybe in limited combinations. Also many fundamental results have been given but sometimes without clear useable criteria for checking stability of a given system. In fact, it can be argued that stability criteria for complex systems is a subject requiring continued serious effort. Nevertheless, powerful methodologies have arisen including those based on Lyapunov theory and variants (such as Razumikhin theory for time-delayed systems), input-output theory, dissipativity theory, input-to-state stability (ISS), hybrid-time ideas and related ideas for particular classes of systems such as dynamic networks, where the role of structure represented by a system graph has been highlighted. In the last area, there has been recent interest from communities outside of stability theory and control. This project builds on the CI’s participation in these developments to consider some remaining problems in 1) providing constructive stability tests for combinations of complexities and 2) to further develop theories which more closely relate the major methodologies. In particular, combinations of complexities integrated with system graph structure will be explored, connections between dissipativity and ISS approaches developed and use of Razumikhin ideas to provide a new approach to study hybrid systems will be studied. Finally, the application of the new stability criteria to specific classes of dynamical networks will be considered. 從最初的由電路、控制、通訊以及大型電力系統產生的電力網絡開始，電力工程系統的穩定性分析問題已經有一百多年的歷史。對於該問題的研究經久不衰，並取得了很多重大的成果，其主要原因在於系統持續增長的複雜性：從線性時不變系統到時變系統，時滯系統，非線性系統，大型系統，再到最近的包含切換和脈衝現象的混雜系統。目前針對複雜系統的研究已經取得了很多有效的處理方法並建立起相應的理論體系。這包括基於Lyapunov理論及其拓展理論（例如針對時滯系統的Razumikhin理論）的理論成果、輸入到輸出理論、耗散性理論、輸入到狀態穩定性理論、混雜時間思想以及針對特定系統的相關理論，例如：動態網絡。在動態網絡的研究中，網絡的拓撲結構對穩定性的影響得到了充分的重視。目前已經有很多穩定性和控制理論以外的研究機構對該研究領域產生了濃厚的興趣，並逐漸重視起來。然而，大多數的現有成果在處理各種複雜性時都傾向於將它們分開處理；很少有結果綜合考慮這些複雜性對系統穩定性的影響。並且許多成熟的基本結論有時很難用來判斷特定系統的穩定性。因此，複雜系統的穩定性問題是一個需要持續關注的課題。 本項目基於主要參與者多年來從事這些領域的研究經驗，致力於那些尚未解決的問題：1）通過綜合考慮各種複雜性，建立具有構造性的穩定性判斷準則；2）進一步發展與健全與主流方法密切相關的理論體系。特別地，注重揭示各種複雜性與系統拓撲結構之間的相互作用關係；建立系統耗散性方法與輸入到狀態穩定性方法之間的聯繫；以及利用Razumikin思想建立一種新的針對混雜系統的研究方法。最終將所建立的穩定性判斷準則應用到特定的動態網絡中去。

17200415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200415.value: 1. Constructive criteria [J3, J8] For stability analysis of hybrid dynamical systems (HDS), prior methods, including the common (smooth) Lyapunov function (LF) and common (average) dwell time are often hard to test. In this project, new criteria give a constructive approach for testing stability and event-stability for HDS with unstable subsystems. Moreover, instead of constructing a hybrid-event-time LF as in our prior work SIAM, 2014, the criteria can be directly used to derive global uniform asymptotic stability (UAS) under events (event-GUES). The results are also showed how the events (switching and jump) drive an HDS with all unstable subsystems to achieve stability. Also we improved the conditions of dwell time including the common (average) dwell-time condition for subsystems. 2. ISS approach [J2, J4, C1] The input-to-state stability (ISS) analysis aims to relate how external inputs affect the UAS of systems. In the literature, most results on ISS are based on the UAS of dynamical systems. Moreover, ISS analysis for time-varying systems was still relatively undeveloped. Our work on ISS in this project takes a different line from the methods used in the literature. We took factors such as more general dynamical behaviors (not just UAS) of systems under zero inputs, time-varying dynamics, and time-delays (not limited to finite time-delay), into considerations. 3. Razumikhin theory [J1, J9] Recently, by integrating with small-gain arguments, the Razumikhin method as well as the Krasovskii-Lyapunov functional approach were adopted to develop ISS and small-gain ISS theorems for dynamical networks with time-delays. They are usually based on assumptions that every subsystem has an ISS-type Lyapunov function(al) and the couplings are required to satisfy the small-gain condition. In this project, our work on stability and ISS for hybrid dynamical networks (HDN) with time-delays extends these results by establishing Halanay-type ISS Lemmas, and the small-gain condition can be relaxed. Two more journal papers are in preparation, which will be submitted to SIAM and IEEE TAC. 4. Application classes [J5, J6, J7] The notions proposed in this project (Parts 1-3), including stability under events reflected specific effects on stability. These notions and related stability results provided a necessary base to design hybrid control (impulsive control, switching control) and event based control for stabilization of unstable complex and networked systems. In this project, by taking these event focused stability results as a theoretical base, we proposed event based impulsive control design. Note - Jx and Cy refer to journal and conference papers respectively.

17200415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200415.value: A research monograph on the body of work for this project is in preparation. This involves many extensions. It is also planned to deal with the above-mentioned unsolved problems, namely: - The connection between ISS and dissipativity methods remains unsolved; - The study of specific networks including power networks.

17200415.value: Stability analysis of electrical engineering systems has a history of over 100 years motivated by problems in circuits, control, communications and larger power systems. The advances can be interpreted as dealing with increasing complexity from linear time-invariant systems to time-varying, time-delayed, nonlinear, large-scale and recently different types of hybrid systems including switching and impulsive effects. Most results tend to deal with these complexities separately or maybe in limited combinations. Also many fundamental results have been given, but often not allowing important aspects like unstable subsystems and/or without clear constructive criteria for checking stability of a given system. Nevertheless, powerful methodologies have arisen including those based on Lyapunov theory and variants, input-output theory, dissipativity theory, input-to-state stability (ISS), hybrid-time ideas and related ideas for particular classes of systems such as dynamic networks. This project builds on the CI’s prior participation in these method developments to solve some remaining problems in: 1) providing constructive stability tests for combinations of complexities; 2) to further develop theories which more closely relate the major methodologies, and 3) the application of the new stability criteria to specific classes of dynamical networks will be considered.

17200815.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17200815.value: 耦合波導系統的極端波

17200815.label: Project Objectives
17200815.value: To study rogue waves using a combination of theoretical and computational approaches - Rogue waves of one component NLSE have been observed experimentally in hydrodynamic wave tanks and optical fibers. Analytical information for coupled waveguides can potentially be tested in a laboratory. Discovering conditions to 'tame' rogue waves will be a great intellectual challenge. To investigate the rich dynamics in systems with coupled waveguides - The properties of localized modes in any waveguide may be dramatically affected by the presence of modes in the other waveguide. Illustrative examples: (a) Coupled nonlinear Schrodinger equations - applicable to surface waves in fluid mechanics and optical fibers with carrier waves of distinct frequencies; (b) Coupled long wave-short wave resonance model - applicable to systems where the phase velocity of the long wave matches the group velocity of two (or more) short waves. To recognize a quantitative indicator for rogue waves - Modulation instability, exponential growth of small disturbances resulting from the interplay of dispersive and nonlinear effects, has been closely identified with the onset of rogue waves. This correlation will be tested quantitatively in several systems of coupled waveguides. To incorporate the effects of shear currents and realistic oceanic conditions - In practice oceanic free surface waves evolve under the influence of a huge variety of environmental factors and agents. We shall concentrate on the effect of shear currents. A linear shear permits analytical advances but may suffer from discontinuity in other properties of fluid dynamics. We shall study parabolic and exponential shear profiles fitted to realistic conditions, which might produce more desirable outcomes. The additional efforts are numerical computations of the vertical structure of the eigenfunctions. To conduct computational studies of stability - Although there have been many derivations of the fundamental and higher order rogue wave modes in the past few years, their stability properties have received comparatively little attention. We shall address this issue. A computer simulation on the evolution of a perturbed wave profile will be conducted. It might be difficult to observe those modes with significantly distorted growth phase, as they are masked by the background modulation instability. To extend the considerations to other models of dynamics - (a) 'Nonlocal' evolution equations, where the nonlinearity depends on properties of a medium not confined to the immediate spatial neighborhood of the observer: A nonlocal nonlinear Schrodinger equation solvable by the inverse scattering transform will be investigated by the present formulation. (b) Evolution systems consisting of a slowly varying complex envelope coupled to a scalar potential: We shall choose examples with bilinear forms and elucidate the dynamics of the rogue waves.

Analytical information for coupled waveguides can potentially be tested in a laboratory. Discovering conditions to 'tame' rogue waves will be a great intellectual challenge.

To investigate the rich dynamics in systems with coupled waveguides - The properties of localized modes in any waveguide may be dramatically affected by the presence of modes in the other waveguide. Illustrative examples: (a) Coupled nonlinear Schrodinger equations - applicable to surface waves in fluid mechanics and optical fibers with carrier waves of distinct frequencies; (b) Coupled long wave-short wave resonance model - applicable to systems where the phase velocity of the long wave matches the group velocity of two (or more) short waves.

To recognize a quantitative indicator for rogue waves - Modulation instability, exponential growth of small disturbances resulting from the interplay of dispersive and nonlinear effects, has been closely identified with the onset of rogue waves. This correlation will be tested quantitatively in several systems of coupled waveguides.

To incorporate the effects of shear currents and realistic oceanic conditions - In practice oceanic free surface waves evolve under the influence of a huge variety of environmental factors and agents. We shall concentrate on the effect of shear currents. A linear shear permits analytical advances but may suffer from discontinuity in other properties of fluid dynamics. We shall study parabolic and exponential shear profiles fitted to realistic conditions, which might produce more desirable outcomes. The additional efforts are numerical computations of the vertical structure of the eigenfunctions.

To conduct computational studies of stability - Although there have been many derivations of the fundamental and higher order rogue wave modes in the past few years, their stability properties have received comparatively little attention. We shall address this issue. A computer simulation on the evolution of a perturbed wave profile will be conducted. It might be difficult to observe those modes with significantly distorted growth phase, as they are masked by the background modulation instability.

To extend the considerations to other models of dynamics - (a) 'Nonlocal' evolution equations, where the nonlinearity depends on properties of a medium not confined to the immediate spatial neighborhood of the observer: A nonlocal nonlinear Schrodinger equation solvable by the inverse scattering transform will be investigated by the present formulation. (b) Evolution systems consisting of a slowly varying complex envelope coupled to a scalar potential: We shall choose examples with bilinear forms and elucidate the dynamics of the rogue waves.

17200815.label: Realisation of objectives
17200815.value: Objective (1): The Hirota bilinear method was demonstrated to be a feasible alternative for the widely used Darboux transformation in finding the lowest order rogue wave of nonlinear systems. Objectives (2) and (3): (a) Modulation instability of plane waves in nonlinear systems was shown to be closely related to the existence condition of rogue waves. (b) In particular, multiple waveguides tended to induce new regimes of modulation instability and hence new sets of rogue waves. (c) The split-step Fourier schemes were used in the numerical simulations of instability and onset of rogue waves. Objectives (4) and (5) (a) These ideas were applied to the fluid flows in oceanic configurations. Effects of shear currents and layered density stratification were assessed. Amplitudes of possible rogue waves were estimated. (b) Long wave-short wave resonances, where the group velocity of short waves matched the phase velocity of long waves, were studied both in a theoretical setting as well as realistic oceanic applications. Objective (6) One typical example of nonlocal Hirota equation was investigated. The results were published in Applied Mathematics Letters in 2016. This paper had received 47 citations as of 2020 and was rated as a 'Highly Cited Paper'.

17200815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200815.value: (a) In many nonlinear systems, the existence condition of modulation instability and the onset of rogue waves are closely related and actually identical in several simple cases. (b) For multiple waveguides, coupling generally produces new regimes of modulation instability and hence new modes of rogue waves. (c) In realistic oceanic situations, the presence of currents will change the stability condition of Stokes waves and hence will affect the likelihood of surprisingly large waves.

17200815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200815.value: (a) Theoretically, higher order modulation instability will involve concepts of enslavement of modes, cascading instability and triangular spectra for the nonlinear Schrodinger equation. Whether these features will hold for other nonlinear dynamical systems, e.g. derivative nonlinear Schrodinger equation with self-steepening nonlinearity, should be investigated. (b) Multiple wave-trains satisfying resonance conditions, e.g. sum of wave numbers and frequencies of two trains equal to those of the third train, will lead to faster time scale of interactions. The dynamics of rogue waves in an oceanic setting is still not properly investigated.

17200815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200815.value: Surprisingly large amplitude oceanic waves obviously pose immense danger to marine shipping and coastal operation. Currently scientists are not able to produce accurate and reliable indicators for the occurrence of such 'rogue' waves. One attempt to understand these oceanic waves using a deterministic approach is to study nonlinear waves system theoretically. Concepts like localized modes and robustness will be critical. We elucidate the connection between modulation instability of plane waves and the onset of rogue modes in nonlinear wave systems. One restriction of this approach is the assumption of unidirectional wave propagation. On a realistic stormy sea surface, waves can propagate in all directions. Incorporating theoretical knowledge, wave spectrum data from field studies and stochastic analysis will constitute tremendous challenges in the future.

17201215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201215.value: Mismanagement of multi-storey residential building is common in Hong Kong, leading to accelerated ageing and building dilapidation. While property management agents (PMAs) can be employed to manage buildings on residents’ behalf, there is a lack of a simple and consistent measure to evaluate the performance of PMAs. PMA’s performance was commonly measured by key building performance indicators, which could lead to wrongly ascribe a dilapidated building to the inferior performance of the PMA. This study aims to develop a standard method to assess and compare the performance of PMAs. The performance of a PMA is defined as its achievement in managing the building to the satisfaction of the residents and its endeavor to maintain the building in a good condition. In this study, the performance of a PMA is divided into a) tangible dimension-PMA efforts to building condition, and b) intangible dimension-the way PMA service is delivered. A total of 300 multi-storey residential buildings in Hong Kong will be sampled for building condition assessment. Demographic characteristics of residents in the sample buildings and PMA’s service delivery will be collected. Using those data, tangible dimension scores will be computed with reference to building conditions. Other exogenous factors, including building’s inborn attributes, residents’ characteristics, and coordination mechanisms will be controlled. Intangible dimension scores will be computed using Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Combining tangible dimension scores and intangible scores, performance scores for PMAs in those sampled buildings will be computed. These performance scores will be tested against the level of management fees charged by the PMAs to determine whether the residents are receiving value for money services from their PMAs. The practical and research implications of the proposed study are: 1) a like-with-like framework for comparing PMA’s performance, and 2) a potential extension to evaluate other facility management services and for different building types. 香港多層住宅樓管理不善很常見，引致樓宇失修及加速老化。住戶一般會聘請物業管理公司來管理大厦，但現時欠缺一個簡單及统一的評估機制來衡量及比較物業管理公司的表現。以往物業管理公司的評估只着重業績指標，而且一般人都將引致大厦破舊的原因歸咎於物業管理公司，這會導致不能對症下藥及改善失修樓宇的狀况。 這項研究其中一個目的是制定一個標準的方法來評估和比較物業管理公司的表現。物業管理公司的表現除了反映在住戶的滿意度，還須要看公司致力维持大厦安全及狀况的努力及成效。在這項研究中，物業管理公司的表現會被劃分成 (一) 有形的狀况評估，和 (二) 無形的服務效果。研究計劃包括對三百楝多層住宅樓宇的狀況評估，收集住戶的人口特徵和物業管理公司的服務選項及水平。運用和分析這些數據，有形的整體狀况會得到評分。其他外在因素，包括建築物的原有設計，住戶特性，和溝通機制等將被置於一致水平上。無形的服務水平將採用主成分分析法 (PCA) 來計算。物業管理公司的總績效評分是結合有形和無形的得分。我們將測試這些表現的得分會否反映在物業管理公司收取的管理費上，以確定住戶是否得到他們付出的物業管理酬金之等值服務。 擬議研究的實踐和理論研究的影響將是：(一) 落實一個一致的平台框架，可用於比較物業管理公司管理住宅的成效，以及 (二) 有機會擴展至評估其他用途的設施管理服務。

17201215.label: Realisation of objectives
17201215.value: To realize the project objectives, the research team has undertaken or completed the following activities: (1) Overviewing the frameworks and processes of property management of multi-storey buildings in Hong Kong and other Asian cities through a background study. Problems and difficulties encountered in property management were studied; (2) Conducting a comprehensive literature review on the concepts and methods of performance evaluation of property management agents (PMAs). Based on the findings of the literature review, a conceptual model which adopts William Sharpe’s residual concept of management performance was constructed; (3) Compiling rosters of private residential developments with not less than 350 domestic units in Sham Shui Po and Tsuen Wan, Hong Kong based on the information from the governmental sources and publicly accessible geographical information systems. These rosters formed the sampling frameworks for the building assessment and questionnaire survey in the two study districts; (4) Inspecting and evaluating the actual physical condition of 117 residential developments in Sham Shui Po and 100 in Tsuen Wan using the protocol of Building Condition Index; (5) Designing, pretesting and fine-tuning a questionnaire set for residents’ satisfaction survey; (6) Carrying out questionnaire survey in the 217 private residential developments assessed; (7) Computing the Property Management Performance Indices (PMPIs) for the PMAs managing these 217 private residential developments by integrating the findings in the building condition assessment and residents' satisfaction survey. Those indices indicate the performance of PMAs in managing the respective residential developments; (8) Validating of the PMPI, using the SERVQUAL findings obtained from the residents’ satisfaction survey; (9) Carrying out analyses to identify exogenous factors affecting the management performance of a PMA; and (10) Drawing practical and policy implications and recommendations regarding how to improve the performance of PMAs in Hong Kong. Overall speaking, the three project objectives as per original application have been substantially achieved.

17201215.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201215.value: A model for measuring and benchmarking property management agents’ performance in managing residential developments in Hong Kong was developed. The performance indicator generated as an output of the model was called the property management performance index (PMPI). The PMPI scores of the PMAs derived from the residual series when regressing the physical condition scores and residential satisfaction scores against different sets of variables. A PMPI score bears a positive value or negative value, depending on whether a property management agent (PMA) outperforms or underperforms the peers, ceteris paribus. Using the PMPI, the performance of PMAs in 217 private residential developments were evaluated and compared. As a whole, while 107 PMAs (49.3%) received a positive PMPI score, only 50 PMAs got positive residuals in both aspects of physical condition and residential satisfaction. In other words, less than one quarter of the PMAs under investigation outperformed their peers when physical condition and residential satisfaction of the residential developments were taken as the performance outcomes. The PMPI was validated using the SERVQUAL-based PMA’s service quality perceived by the residents in the subject residential developments. Details of the construction and validation of the PMPI framework can be referred to the book chapter in "Strategic Management". Besides, exploratory analyses were carried out to identify factors affecting PMPI. Interestingly, no significant relationship is found between the level of management fee and PMPI score. The scale of property management company to which the PMA belonged (in terms of floor area of residential properties being managed by the company) did not exert any significant impact on the PMPI score. On the other hand, PMPI score for a PMA was found to be higher if the PMA had obtained an ISO10002 certification and the residential development concerned had a more homogeneous mix of residents. Moreover, even for the same PMA, the management performance could be very dissimilar across different residential developments. Apart from main research outlined above, some “secondary” research was made possible using the dataset of the current project. For example, drawing on the data collected in different stages of the project, a two-stage data envelopment analysis (DEA) model was developed for the evaluation of PMA performance. The PMAs of a total of 37 private residential developments in Hong Kong were evaluated using the DEA model. For the design and findings of the secondary research, one can refer to the article published in the "International Journal of Development and Sustainability".

17201215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201215.value: Currently, the team is writing two papers, one on the socio-economic and contextual determinants of the PMA’s performance in managing multi-owned housing (MOH) developments in Hong Kong (targeting at the “International Journal of Strategic Property Management”) and the other on how a PMA’s inputs and organizational settings affect the PMA’s performance (targeting at “Property Management”). Moreover, the team plans to study the responses of the private housing residents when experiencing poor services provided by their PMAs. The exit-voice-loyalty-neglect model will be employed to build up our analytical model which will then be tested using the data collected in the satisfaction survey. A manuscript targeting at "Le Travail Humain" will be prepared and submitted. The current research can be further extended in several ways. First, using the PMPI developed and validated, we can test the relationship between property price or rent and PMPI. Second, the empirical study can be rolled out to other parts of Hong Kong and other Asian cities with many multi-storey residential developments. Third, when a critical mass of PMAs in a city have been evaluated using the PMPI and the evaluation results are released to the public, we can see if any signaling effect can be created.

17201215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201215.value: Mismanagement of multi-storey residential building is common in Hong Kong, leading to accelerated ageing and building dilapidation. While property management agents (PMAs) can be employed to manage buildings on residents’ behalf, there is a lack of a simple and consistent measure to evaluate the performance of PMAs. PMA’s performance was commonly measured by key building performance indicators, which could lead to wrongly ascribe a dilapidated building to the inferior performance of the PMA. To fill the extant research gaps, this study aims to develop a novel model to assess and compare the performance of PMAs. The research has significant practical and research implications. The research findings provide property management practitioners, residents and public administrators with valuable insights into the property management performance in Hong Kong. The model developed in this study can serve as a protocol for benchmarking the performance of PMAs in managing residential buildings in Hong Kong. It can help a culture of quality property or MOH management to foster in Hong Kong in the long run. Besides, using the model, we can quantify a PMA’s performance in a scientific way. This promotes future studies on the correlates of PMA’s performance (e.g. property value and management fee level).

To evaluate the effectiveness of the developed system in improving learning from evidence-based problem-solving practice

17201415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201415.value: The aim of this project is to conduct research to add learning facilities into a diagnostic decision support system. Diagnostic decision-making, the process of diagnosing a clinical problem, plays a crucial role in clinical practice. In the face of incomplete information and uncertain situations, diagnostic decision-making involves complex, dynamic processes in which situations evolve and decisions and actions influence one another. A number of computer-based diagnostic decision support systems have been developed to help physicians and other health professionals to make diagnoses based on expert knowledge and clinical evidence. These systems have been shown to improve clinical practice and support evidence-based medicine. They have also had an impact on medical education by supporting senior students and junior physicians in applying medical science knowledge to problem-solving practice. However, the educational application of such systems has been limited, and achieved mixed success, because existing systems have been developed primarily to help individuals to diagnose problems rather than to teach diagnostic problem-solving. The aim of the proposed project is to add learning facilities into a diagnostic decision support system to address the need for effective learning from diagnostic problem-solving practice. The main outcomes will be development of a computer-assisted decision-making and learning (CADML) system. Different from traditional diagnostic decision support systems, the CADML system will request that the learner complete a diagnostic task on his/her own, the process of which will be captured and visualized. The learner can then reflect upon and refine the process with the support of individual feedback from the system. After completing a number of cases, the learner will be asked to articulate the knowledge underlying the diagnostic processes as a knowledge map, based on which the system will help the learner to identify gaps in his/her knowledge. To achieve the project’s aim, a set of ontology- and visualization-based functionalities, including simulating clinical problems, visualizing diagnostic processes, representing expert knowledge as ontologies, advising on individual diagnosis and learning processes, will be developed using intelligent agent technology. By integrating the proposed learning facilities into a diagnostic decision support system, the project will enhance such systems’ capability to fulfill the need for effective learning from evidence-based problem-solving practice. 本研究旨在探討如何借助智能代理為診斷決策支持系統建立學習功能。診斷決策在臨床實踐中起著關鍵作用。在信息不完全和不確定的情況下，診斷決策大多涉及到複雜動態的過程。一些計算機輔助診斷決策支持系統已用來幫助醫生和相關人員根據臨床證據和專家知識作出診斷。這些系統不僅有助於提高臨床實踐和循證醫學，也對醫學教育產生影響，用來幫助高年級醫學生和初中及醫師練習運用醫學知識來解決臨床問題。然而，這種系統的教育應用不太成功，因為現有系統主要功能是輔助診斷，而並非教會人如何診斷。該研究的目的是探討如何為診斷決策支持系統建立學習功能。主要手段是研發一個計算機輔助決策和學習（CADML）系統。與傳統的診斷決策支持系統不同，該CADML系統首先要求學習者獨立完成診斷任務，其診斷過程將記錄在系統並可視化。然後，學習者可以對其診斷過程進行反省，並藉助系統反饋以改善診斷過程。完成了一些任務後，學生將對診斷過程以及相關知識加以總結，找出收穫或存在的問題。為了幫助學習者達到這些目的，智能代理技術系統將被用來建立相關學習功能包括模擬臨床問題，可視化診斷過程，建立專家知識，提供個性化反饋。該項目將加強傳統診斷決策支持系統的學習能力，幫助學習者通過練習、反饋、與反省來提高臨床診斷能力。

17201415.label: Realisation of objectives
17201415.value: We have fully achieved the two objectives of the project. Below are the detailed activities we have performed to complete the project and achieve the objectives. 1) Theoretical Research: January – February 2016 In the first phase, we established a theoretical framework by investigating the key characteristics of computer-assisted diagnostic decision-making and learning processes. Relevant educational theories such as situated learning, problem-based learning, and cognitive apprenticeship have been used as foundations of the learning environment design. The frame includes the following elements to facilitate learning through problem-solving practice. · Exploration – push learners to solve problems on their own · Modelling – provide learners with examples to demonstrate desired performance · Reflection – ask learners to reflect on their diagnostic processes and knowledge maps, and compare their solutions with those of experts · Articulation – ask learners to articulate the knowledge underlying diagnostic processes · Scaffolding – provide help on tasks that learners are unable to complete autonomously · Coaching – observe learners’ performance, and provide personalized feedback 2) Conceptual Design: March – April 2016 The theoretical framework established in the first phase has been mapped onto a system architecture. The architecture is outlined as a set of intelligent agents, each equipped with adaptive mechanisms as well as relevant knowledge. The system was designed to allow learners to interact with simulated clinical cases, perform diagnostic tasks, progressively articulate the underlying knowledge, and receive personalized feedback. 3) System Development: May 2016 - February 2017 Based upon the system architecture designed during the second phase, a prototype system has been developed. The system is developed using Java programming tools and delivered on the Web via Windows Server. SQL Server will be used to manage the databases. Moreover, ontology- and visualization-based functionalities are developed for effective learning from evidence-based problem-solving practice. Glaucoma diagnosis is selected as the study domain owing to its complexity. A number of learning cases is developed based on academic and practical references with the support of domain experts. The knowledge needed to diagnose glaucoma is collected from academic journals and references, assorted databases, protocols, practice guidelines, consensus statements, and domain experts. An expert solution to each case as well as the expert knowledge map is being developed on the basis of expert knowledge. Pedagogical principles and learning strategies are determined and incorporated into the system for the provision of personalized feedback. 4) Pilot evaluation: March – May 2017 After the proposed system was developed, a pilot evaluation of the system was conducted with students in order to ensure students’ acceptance of the system. 5) System refinement: June – August 2017 Based on pilot evaluation result, we made some adjustment of the system (functions & interfaces) to meet necessary requirement. 6) Formal evaluation – first round: September - December 2017 Using the refined system, a formal evaluation was arranged with students to examine the system’s effectiveness in improving learning through diagnostic problem-solving practice. Students’ task performance, knowledge achievements, and learning activities were collected. Also, the participants’ perceptions of the system (including usefulness, ease of use, and user satisfaction) and its relevance to cognitive apprenticeship strategies were collected through a survey and interviews. 7) Refinement of the system and the evaluation method: January – March 2018 Based on the evaluation result of the first round, we made some further adjustment of the system interfaces. In addition, we improve the data collection and analysis methods for the next round of evaluation. 8) Formal evaluation – second round: April - August 2018 Using the further refined system and improved data collection and analysis methods, the second round of evaluation was arranged with students to examine the system’s effectiveness in multiple aspects. More data were collected from interviews with participants. 9) Integrated analysis and report: September - December 2018 Based on the data from the two rounds of evaluation, we made an integrated analysis of the effectiveness of the proposed approach and system. Meanwhile, we presented the findings in written reports and academic publications in international journals and conferences proceedings.

17201415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201415.value: Diagnostic decision-making, the process of diagnosing a clinical problem, plays a crucial role in clinical practice. In the face of incomplete information and uncertain situations, diagnostic decision-making involves complex, dynamic processes in which situations evolve and decisions and actions influence one another. It is important to make the complex process visible to novices and provide them with necessary support throughout the diagnostic tasks. This study proposed and implemented a computer-based clinical decision-making and learning environment that allows learners to perform simulated diagnostic tasks and capture their task process in a visual format for effective thinking and reﬂection. Moreover, expert support is incorporated to improve self-reﬂection by allowing learners to identify the difference between their performance and that of the expert. The evaluation results have demonstrated the effectiveness of the approach in improving students’ task performance and knowledge achievement. The results also showed that the inclusion of expert support made the visualization-based reﬂective learning environment more effective in improving learners’ task performance, supporting their construction of knowledge from tasks, and improving their conﬁdence in solving complex problems. The findings of the project have been published 4 articles in high-impact journals (e.g., BMC Medical Education, Computers in Human Behavior, Educational Technology & Society) and presented at two prestigious international conferences (Annual Meetings of The American Educational Research Association, The International Conference of the Learning Sciences).

17201415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201415.value: The findings have shown promising effects of the developed system and proposed approach. We have introduced the developed approach to some medical schools in mainland and received positive comments. If additional fund is secured, we plan to further explore this project through more close collaboration with domain experts and practitioners. We will also consider integrate more artificial intelligence technologies to improve learner performance in multiple aspects.

17201415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201415.value: In Hong Kong, public hospitals suffer from a shortage of doctors. At the same time, it is difficult for senior medical students and junior physicians to transit more quickly from preclinical study to clinical practice. The transition process requires extensive guided practice, and is therefore time-consuming and expensive. This study proposed and implemented a computer-based clinical decision-making and learning environment that allows learners to perform simulated diagnostic tasks, reflect on their performance, and identify the gasp between their performance and that of the expert. The proposed approach has shown its promising effects on improving learners’ task performance, supporting their construction of knowledge from tasks, and improving their conﬁdence in solving complex problems.

17201515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201515.value: The first-hand property market in Hong Kong is dominated by a small number of developers (sellers) with almost no new entrants over the past two decades. This market structure, especially the major developers, is often blamed to be the culprit of high property prices. However, since property is a durable good, the first-hand market is arguably competing with the second-hand market characterized by many individual sellers. In light of this, this study aims to empirically identify the conditions under which developers have market power to charge a price higher than the more competitive second-hand market. There are two contributions to the methodology. First, with the abundance of repeat property sales in Hong Kong, a difference-in-differences approach will be developed so that any variation due to property quality or market conditions can be eliminated when comparing the prices of the two markets. Second, different measures of product substitutability will be developed so as to test the prediction from monopoly theory that a high degree of substitutability between the two markets should weaken any market power. The methodology so developed can help the court decide if there is any abuse of market power, which is a key objective of the forthcoming competition (anti-trust) law. 香港一手物業市場由少數房地產發展商主導，過去二十年幾乎沒有新的發展商打入市場。這種市場結構經常被視為香港樓價高企的罪魁禍首。然而，房地產作為耐用品，一手市場不能完全避開由大量個別業主組成的二手市場競爭，發展商並非必然具有壟斷優勢。有鑒於此，本實證研究旨在透過比較一、二手價格來分析一手市場的壟斷性。本研究的貢獻主要有二。 其一，利用香港物業市場的高流通量，本研究得以建立「雙重差分模型」來剔除一手和二手市場之間因物業質量所導致的價格差異，從而準確地比較兩個市場定價上的不同。 其二，本研究會建立一系列的產品可替代性比率以檢驗壟斷理論中的可替代性假說，即二手產品跟一手產品愈相似，一手市場的壟斷性會愈低。 本研究的方法和結論可以為日後法庭審理競爭法（反壟斷法）案件提供有用的參考。

17201915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201915.value: Traffic congestion and vehicle emissions are major problems in urban areas worldwide, and Hong Kong is no exception. Traffic congestion has such negative impacts as time and productivity losses, whereas vehicle emissions deteriorate air quality, have adverse effects on human health, and contribute to global warming. It is therefore a matter of urgency that we manage both congestion and vehicle emissions to reduce their impacts and achieve a more sustainable urban environment. Road pricing is one means of achieving these objectives, but it was focused primarily on managing traffic congestion. Such pricing has also been used to mitigate vehicle emission problems recently and examined using static traffic assignment modeling frameworks. The static models are unable to capture the time-varying nature of traffic or the effects of such spatial queues as junction blockages and queue spillback. Hence, these models are unable to predict the spatial and temporal distributions of vehicle emissions accurately. To address some of these limitations, dynamic traffic assignment models have been proposed to predict dynamic traffic patterns. For example, cell-based dynamic system optimum (DSO) models have been proposed to derive and set time-varying tolls while capturing the effects of spatial queues. They often incorporate the cell transmission model, which is relatively computationally inefficient compared with the link transmission model (LTM). The LTM is based on Newell’s simplified theory of kinematic waves. Its fundamental diagram is triangular, meaning it may not be suitable for urban street applications. In addition, existing DSO models often fail to consider multiple destinations, first-in-first-out, vehicle emissions, and different vehicle types and their interactions, and hence cannot be applied to deriving and setting time-varying tolls accurately for general road network applications. This project will develop a methodology for determining time-varying congestion and emission tolls based on a DSO model incorporating a proposed link-based multiclass traffic flow model. This traffic flow model will consider a more general fundamental diagram and more vehicle types than the LTM. All models developed will be analyzed numerically and analytically, and an efficient and convergent solution method will be proposed. The proposed methodology and analyses are anticipated to be very useful in determining sustainable time-varying congestion and emission tolls for managing traffic and improving roadside air quality in congested cities. 交通擁堵和車輛廢氣排放是全球城市地區普遍面臨的重大問題，香港也不例外。交通擁堵產生的負面影響主要為在時間和生產力上的損失，而車輛廢氣排放問題則使空氣質量進一步惡化、影響公眾健康並且也是導致全球變暖的重要因素。因此，對交通擁堵和車輛廢氣排放同時進行管理以減少交通系統帶來的負面影響便成為了我們營造更加可持續的城市環境的當務之急。道路擁堵費是實現這些目標的手段之一，但它更側重於對交通擁堵的管理，此類收費方式近期也被用於減輕車輛廢氣排放問題。同時，研究者們也在靜態交通分配模型的框架下對此類收費進行了研究。然而，靜態模型無法描繪交通流量在時間變化上的性質、交叉口堵塞和車輛排隊後溢。因此，這些模型都無法準確預測車輛廢氣排放的時間和空間分佈。 為了解決上述缺陷，研究者們提出動態交通分配模型用以預測動態交通模式。例如，通過基於單元的動態系統最佳（Dynamic system optimum, DSO）模型來推導和確定隨時間變化的道路收費，並同時考慮交叉口堵塞和車輛排隊後溢的影響。這類模型通常包含了單元傳輸模型，而相比於路段傳輸模型（Link transmission model, LTM），這些模型計算效率相對較低。 LTM是基於紐維爾（Newell）的簡化運動波理論，其基本圖像為三角形，這也意味著該模型或許不適用於城市道路結構。此外，現有的DSO模型常常没有考慮到多目的地、先入先出、車輛廢氣排放以及不同車輛類型和它們之間的相互作用，並因此不能被用於準確推導和確定一般道路系統的時變道路收費方案。 本研究將提出一個包含基於路段的多類別交通流模型的DSO模型，並開發一個基於此DSO模型用於確定時變擁堵及車輛廢氣排放收費方案的一套方法。該交通流模型將考慮比LTM更普遍適用於城市道路結構的基本圖像，並囊括更多的車輛類型。我們將對本研究提出的所有模型進行數學分析和解析分析，並提出一個高效且收斂的解決方法。我們認為，本研究提出的方法及分析非常有益於幫助受交通擁堵困擾的城市確定可持續的時變擁堵及排放收費方案以更好地進行交通管理並改善路邊空氣質量。

17201915.label: Realisation of objectives
17201915.value: To achieve objective (1), a comprehensive literature review was first conducted [J1, J4]. A methodology for setting dynamic emission tolls for single-destination road networks was then proposed [J1]. This methodology involves developing an emission pricing model and using a solution method to solve optimal control problems. The traffic propagation is based on hydrodynamic theory. The model contains two sub-models derived from the corresponding two subproblems: a dynamic system optimum (DSO) traffic assignment problem and a first-best dynamic emission pricing subproblem. The first subproblem, which is formulated as an optimal control problem, determines an optimal free-flow solution that minimizes the generalized system cost including the costs of total travel times and total emissions (or fuel consumption). The second sub-problem determines the optimal emission prices of all links in the network, which was formulated as an optimal control problem to minimize the total tolls. Wardrop’s route choice principle was integrated into the model as part of the constraints. The free-flow optimal solution obtained from the first sub-problem was used as an input to the second sub-problem. The optimal first-best emission pricing can then be determined by first solving the optimal control problem for the first subproblem and then solving the optimal control problem for the second subproblem. The DSO model for the first subproblem had been extended for general networks [J3] with the consideration of both route and departure time choice [J6]. Different DSO formulation approaches were discussed [J6]. To capture multiple user classes and determine a dynamic congestion and emission toll, a bi-level programming model was developed [J5]. The upper-level program is used to determine the optimal toll whereas the lower level model is used to depict the route and departure time choice of users of each class. The bi-level model was solved by a double Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno (BFGS) method, which uses a classical BFGS method to solve the upper-level model and the proposed BFGS method to solve the lower-level model. To achieve objective (2), two branch and bound algorithms were developed to solve the DSO models with the FIFO consideration for a general road network with multiple destinations [J3, J6]. One considers the non-vehicle holding property while the other one does not. The efficiency of the algorithms was illustrated [J3, J6]. To achieve objective (3), the properties of the DSO and pricing models were analyzed and discussed, including the non-vehicle holding property of DSO [J1, J2, J3, J6] and the existence of free flow solutions [J1], solution uniqueness [J2], the monotonicity property of the emission (or fuel consumption) functions [J1], and first-in-first-out [J3, J6]. Numerical results are presented to illustrate the tradeoff between total emissions and total travel time minimization [J1, J2]. A comparison between congestion and emission pricing, congestion pricing, and no-toll strategies was also conducted [J5].

17201915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201915.value: The research outcomes (in forms of the modeling framework, submodels, solution method, and properties of studied problems/models) and major findings were published in six journal papers [J1-J6] and was presented in an international conference [C1]. The following summarizes the major findings. [J3] reveals that the proposed link-based system-optimal dynamic traffic assignment (SO-DTA) models are consistent with the traditional cell-based counterparts in terms of yielding an identical optimal total system travel time (TSTT). However, the link-based models outperform the cell-based counterparts in terms of computational efficiency. [J6] illustrates the following: (1) link-based non-vehicle holding constraints cannot completely eliminate vehicle holding phenomena, and the first-in-first-out (FIFO) conditions for link-based, intersection-movement-based, and path-based dynamic system optimum simultaneous route and departure time choice (DSO-SRDTC) problems (i.e, SO-DTA problems with the extra consideration of departure time choice) are not equivalent. (2) The three formulations of the DSO-SRDTC problems are equivalent in terms of obtaining the same optimal total system travel cost (TSTC) if FIFO constraints are not considered. However, they can give different TSTCs if FIFO constraints are considered. (3) Cyclic flows can help to reduce the TSTC in cyclic networks under time-varying capacities. Because it is difficult to enumerate cyclic paths in a cyclic time-dependent network, it is concluded that complete path-based formulations for DSO-SRDTC problems may not be able to be available for these networks. (4) Link-based and intersection-movement-based models can be solved more efficiently than path-based models. [J2] shows that the proposed SO-DTA models with the consideration of total system emissions are more accurate than existing counterparts; the SO-DTA models can have multiple optimal solutions, and the proposed bi-objective version can capture the trade-off between emissions and travel time. [J5] demonstrates that at congestion and environmental toll equilibrium (CETE), the arrival of each group of commuters at the destination in the whole studied period does not follow a predetermined order, and the CETE traffic assignment problem cannot be formulated and solved using the traditional approach i.e., reformulating the problem as a static traffic assignment problem using a variational inequality and solving it by the Gauss-Seidel decomposition (GSD) method. [J5] also shows that the BFGS-based method outperforms the GSD method in terms of solving the no-toll equilibrium and congestion toll equilibrium problems. The optimal congestion and environmental toll scheme outperforms the optimal congestion toll scheme in terms of total system cost (TSC), i.e., the sum of TSTC and total system environmental cost (TSEC).

17201915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201915.value: The proposed framework in [J5] assumes fixed travel demand and homogeneous desirable arrival time for different classes of travelers. To improve the realism, the framework can be extended to consider elastic demand and heterogeneous desirable arrival times in the future.

17201915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201915.value: Traffic congestion and vehicle emissions are major problems in urban areas worldwide, and Hong Kong is no exception. Traffic congestion has such negative impacts as time and productivity losses, whereas vehicle emissions deteriorate air quality, have adverse effects on human health, and contribute to global warming. It is, therefore, a matter of urgency that we manage both congestion and vehicle emissions to reduce their impacts and achieve a more sustainable urban environment. Road pricing is one means of achieving these objectives, but it was focused primarily on managing traffic congestion and existing road pricing models are unable to account for vehicle emissions accurately. This project developed a new methodology for determining time-varying congestion and emission tolls. All models developed were analyzed numerically and analytically, and efficient and convergent solution methods were proposed. The proposed methodology and analyses are anticipated to be very useful in determining sustainable time-varying congestion and emission tolls for managing traffic and improving roadside air quality in congested cities.

17202115.label: Project Objectives
17202115.value: Online Primal Dual with Convex Programs - Case Studies: We will use online primal dual and convex programs to design and analyze online algorithms for three representative cases -- online scheduling on speed-scalable machines, online combinatorial auctions with production costs, and online facility location with scalable capacities. We will complement the algorithmic results with lower bounds on the competitive ratios of these problems to justify the optimality of our algorithms. Online Primal Dual with Convex Programs - General Framework: We will develop a recipe for using online primal dual to solve a large family of convex programs online, including convex extensions of packing and covering linear programs, and convex programs with mixed packing and covering constraints. Limitations of the Canonical Approach: We will explain why online primal dual failed on some problems using a novel theory of canonical online primal dual and online duality gap that we developed in our preliminary studies. We will further develop the theory of online duality gap and study how it depends on the competitive ratios of the primal and dual problems. Beyond the Canonical Approach: We will explore potential approaches beyond the canonical one to circumvent the online duality gap, and use such approaches to design better algorithms for problems on which the canonical approach failed.

17202115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202115.value: 本项目主要研究在线组合优化问题以及在线对偶算法。我们将探索以下两个方向： 1. 凸规划 我们会把已有的针对线性规划的在线对偶算法拓展到凸规划。凸规划及其对偶性质是对线性规划及其对偶性质的重要拓展。凸规划能刻画许多线性规划无法刻画的问题，比如目标函数为凹函数的在线匹配问题以及一些在线调度问题。最近几年有一些研究设计了针对特定问题的凸规划的在线对偶算法，然而到目前为止还没有一个一般性的算法框架。在这个项目里我们会发展一个一般性的针对凸规划设计在线对偶算法的框架。 2. 传统在线对偶算法的限制 虽然在线对偶算法在近年来成功的解决了许多在线组合优化问题，然后仍然有一些问题无法用这个方法解决，比如说一些在线调度问题以及k-Server问题等等。因此，我们将着力研究导致传统在线对偶算法无法解决这些问题的一些限制，并提出解决方案。

17202115.value: All 4 objectives have been achieved. 1. We have obtained matching upper and lower bounds for the proposed special cases. 2. We have developed as general framework for a large family of covering and packing problems with convex objectives. 3. We have identified obstacles for the k-server problem, a variant of online scheduling with speed-scaling, an online matching problem with stochastic rewards, if we use the canonical approach. 4. We have found a way to reinterpret the recent non-primal-dual algorithm for k-server as lifting the naive linear program. Such lifting techniques also help us resolve the online matching problem with stochastic rewards.

17202115.label: Major findings and research outcome
17202115.value: 1. Fenchel duality is the key to generalize the online primal dual technique to handle problems with convex objectives. 2. Lifting the linear program to accommodate more information of the integral problem may result in i) an amortization in the charging argument and/or ii) a delay of dual online decisions, both of which enhance the power of the online primal dual technique. 3. With our new understanding of the technique, we can now use online primal dual to solve a much wider family of online matching problems.

17202115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17202115.value: 1. The technique of lifting the linear program in online primal dual is worth further investigations. I will seek further rounding to support this research. 2. Some pieces are still missing in the research direction of online primal dual and online problems with convex objectives. These smaller research problems are suitable for undergraduate students who want to get some exposure to research.

17202115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17202115.value: This project investigates an important technique in the design online algorithms called online primal dual. It advances the state-of-the-art in two folds: 1. We now have a systematic approach to apply the techniques to problems whose objectives are convex functions; examples include scaling server speeds to achieve a balance of job efficiency and energy consumption, allocating resources which have marginally increasing production costs, etc. 2. We now have a much deeper understanding on why the online primal dual technique has failed to tackle certain problems thus far and have a method to fix it.

17202215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202215.value: Social infrastructure facilities (SIFs), such as utilities and transport systems, are indispensable to a society. To maintain the best service quality, infrastructure asset management (IAM) systems are deployed to monitor and report the condition of SIFs. While IAM systems serve well in individual SIFs, they fail to address the complex interrelationship and interdependence of a coalesced infrastructure network. As well as the health of SIF being influenced by other facilities in vicinity, its breakdown could also induce a knock-on effect to the entire infrastructure network and result in catastrophic consequences. Consolidating up-to-date data from various SIF owners and operators for joint decision support at strategic, tactical and operational levels can radically streamline the decision process and improve the accuracy and timeliness of IAM decisions. The emerging big data concept may open up new ways to improve information sharing and collaboration between different SIF owners. While big data has been successfully applied in various domains, its significant potential in enhancing the efficiency, reliability and safety of the entire social infrastructure model is yet to be explored. The proposed research aims to develop an agile big data centered inter-network IAM (ABIN-IAM) platform to facilitate owners and operators of different SIFs to capture, transform and exchange relevant real-time asset information for simultaneous inter-network inventory and asset location tracking, condition appraisal, failure detection and reporting, maintenance planning, resilience prediction and reaction, post-incident reconciliation and message dissemination. The different components of the proposed research – literature review, interviews, case studies, a focus group meeting and a Delphi study – will unveil the existing IAM practices and formulate the information and analytical framework for a joint IAM. A suitable unified data regime will then be identified to allow data to be captured, transformed and exchanged between different IAM systems. Finally, the system architecture will be designed and a prototype ABIN-IAM platform will be developed for validation. The findings of this research will contribute to the research community by unfolding the information and analytical framework required for joint IAM decisions, the considerations behinds the unified data regime, the essential features of the big data centered IAM platform, and the potentials of an ABIN-IAM. These would pave the way for the development of a national IAM big data center to continuously uplift service quality and stability, improve the predictability and manageability of resilience, and ultimately chart out a sustainable smart city master plan. 社會基建設施（SIFs）是每一個社會不可或缺的。為確保維持SIFs的最佳服務質素，應考慮引進基建設施資產管理（IAM）系統作為幫助監視、記錄、和報告SIFs的狀態以制定及時預防和補救措施。雖然現時IAM系統是可以應付獨立的SIF，他們卻未能解決跨網絡基礎設施的複雜關係。一個SIF的狀態不僅影響在周邊的其他設施，其故障也可能引發對整個基礎設施網絡的連鎖反應。沒有意識到其他基建設施的位置和最新狀況，有可能導致災難性後果，就如在2014年高雄天然氣管道爆炸這樣。整合來自不同SIFs擁有者和運營商的實時數據作共同戰略、戰術、和操作層面的決策支援可大大簡化決策過程及提高IAM決策的準確性和及時性。 嶄新的大數據概念可為提高不同SIFs之間的信息共享和協作開闢新的前路。大數據包括一系列的技術，從物聯網、雲計算、和智能作業平台，至更快速更高效的數據庫、邏輯數據倉庫、和大數據分析數組。鑑於大數據已成功地被應用在各個科學領域中，當務之急是要探索發展大數據為本的IAM系統是否能提高整個基礎設施網絡的集體運行效率、可靠性、和安全性。本研究項目旨於建立一個大數據為本的IAM系統，以協助不同SIFs擁有者和運營商充分利用實時資產信息進行聯合資產清查和位置追踪、狀態評估、故障檢測和報告、維修規劃、應變能力預測和預防、及發生事故後的管理和公佈。 研究始於文獻綜述，訪談，案例分析，專題小組會議和Delphi研習，以了解目前IAM的實踐慣例，並制定實時協作IAM的信息和分析框架。繼而設計一個統一平臺以採集、整理、和交換不同的IAM系統中之數據。基於大數據的概念，一個合適的系統結構將被建立。最後就是開發原型大數據為本的實時協作IAM系統作為驗證和意見採集用途。 這項研究的結果將有助學術界剖釋協同IAM決策時的資料和分析框架之要求、建立統一數據平台時之考慮因素、以及大數據為本實時協作IAM系統的基本特徵。這將為未來發展現實世界大數據IAM樞紐打好根基，從而提升SIFs之服務質量和穩定性、預測和管理應變能力、和勾劃出未來可持續發展的智能城市的總體規劃藍圖。

17202315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202315.value: Many metropolitan cites, including Hong Kong, Shanghai, Melbourne and New York, are located in regions of low-to-moderate seismicity. Due to land scarcity in these areas, modern reinforced concrete buildings taller than 30 stories high are widely constructed, with a range of functional uses on different levels. Transfer structures are commonly used in these buildings to distribute vertical loads from shear walls above to widely spaced columns below the transfer level. Recent studies conducted by the PI [1,2] have revealed that critical shear and flexural stresses on shear walls can arise from out-of-plane deformations of transfer structures under gravity and seismic loads. Such deformations can cause severe shear loads on walls just above the transfer structure. The structural response of these walls is similar to that of concrete squat walls subjected to high shear and gravity loads. During a major earthquake, these walls could suffer brittle shear or axial failure, accompanied by a rapid degradation of strength and stiffness. However, research on the seismic behavior of squat walls under high axial loads is extremely rare. The actual failure mode and collapse mechanism are unclear. The seismic design of squat shear walls is not covered in any design code or standard. The proposed study is a comprehensive experimental assessment of the seismic performance of reinforced concrete squat walls. Twenty squat wall specimens with different axial load ratios, shear-span-to-depth ratios and reinforcement arrangements will be subjected to axial failure under reversed cyclic lateral loads and a constant axial load to investigate the change in axial stiffness and the axial load effect on the failure mode and failure mechanism. The seismic response, including hysteretic behavior, drift capacity, energy dissipation capacity and strength and stiffness degradation, will be quantified. Benchmark experimental results will be provided for the development of analytical models and the calibration of numerical models for the analysis of squat shear wall collapse under seismic and other extreme events. A better understanding of the collapse mechanisms of squat walls could help relax the drift limit for collapse prevention checks of existing buildings and lead to a reduction in seismic retrofit costs without jeopardizing structural safety. The axial load limit and reinforcement arrangements evaluated by this study will directly contribute to the development of rational design models and design provisions for squat walls in Hong Kong and other regions of low-to-moderate seismicity. 許多大都市，例如香港、上海、墨爾本和紐約，都位於低和中等抗震設防區。由於土地空間稀缺，在這些大都市常常需要建造超過30層的現代鋼筋混凝土建築。很多高層建築因上部與下部平面使用功能不同，通常設置轉換層結構，可將上部剪力牆承受的豎向荷載分攤給下部大空間的鋼筋混凝土柱。課題申請人最近的研究表明[1,2]，對於帶轉換層的高層建築，在地震和重力荷載作用下，剪力牆、柱和轉換層之間的相互作用以及轉換層的平面外變形，會引起轉換層上方剪力牆產生“剪力集中效應”，轉換層上方剪力牆在自重和較高剪力作用下，其力學行為與低矮剪力牆較為接近。在罕遇地震作用下，這些剪力牆可能會產生剪切或受壓破壞，同時其強度和剛度迅速下降。目前對低矮剪力牆的研究較少，特別是對低矮剪力牆在高軸壓比下的抗震性能研究很少，對低矮鋼筋混凝土剪力牆的受力性能尚未完全認清。目前混凝土結構相關規範和標準中，涉及低矮剪力牆抗震設計的條文較少。 擬研究項目是對鋼筋混凝土低矮剪力牆的抗震性能進行綜合試驗評估，開展不同參數的低矮剪力牆試件的擬靜力試驗，這些試件加載直至受壓破壞，研究軸壓比、剪跨比和配筋率等參數對其抗震性能的影響，重點研究軸壓比對破壞模式和破壞機理的影響，量化分析低矮剪力牆的抗震性能，包括滯回性能、變形能力、耗能能力、強度和剛度退化等。本項目將為低矮剪力牆分析模型的發展，數值模擬方法的驗證等提供基礎數據。對低矮剪力牆破壞機理的揭示，有助於改進現有規範中關於防倒塌的設計，以及節約抗震加固成本（同時不影響結構安全性）。項目研究得到的低矮剪力牆軸壓比限值和鋼筋佈置方法，可直接應用於香港和其他低和中等抗震設防區的低矮剪力牆設計規範的編制和改進。

17202315.label: Realisation of objectives
17202315.value: The project objectives stated above have been fully achieved. For Objectives 1 and 2: Seven large-scale short shear span reinforced concrete (RC) wall specimens have been prepared to investigate the influence of the axial load level, concrete strength, steel arrangement on the seismic performance until gravity collapse. Digital image correlation (DIC) method has been used to capture the full field deformation and collapse response of the wall. Results including the hysteresis loop, energy dissipation, lateral stiffness degradation, vertical stiffness degradation, collapse mode and DIC vertical strain history have been obtained. For Objective 3: Non-linear finite element analysis based on the modified compression field theory was conducted. The numerical models have been validated by our test results. The purpose of the numerical study is to determine the maximum residual tensile strain of the reinforcement at the wall edge which is an important parameter in determining the instability of out-of-plane buckling. For Objective 4: Based on our test results together with the relevant test results from others, a theoretical study on short shear span RC walls was conducted. Two empirical models have been proposed to estimate the shear capacity and ultimate drift ratios of rectangular RC shear walls under the effects of different axial load levels. For Objective 5: Through the numerical and experimental results, a modified Mohr's axial capacity model for RC walls with short shear span subjected to cyclic tension-compression excursions has been developed.

17202315.value: The drift capacity for RC walls designed and detailed based on the old concrete design code in Hong Kong could be extremely low (< 0.4%). 17202315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17202315.value: Hong Kong is located in a low-to-moderate seismicity region. Buildings in Hong Kong do not require to conduct seismic design. Reinforced concrete (RC) walls often feature high steel content and high axial load level. This study found that those walls only have limited drift capacity. The problem can be exaggerated by the shear concentration effects above transfer structure. Those walls might experience gravity load collapse after shear failure during a major earthquake attack. In this study, through a series of experimental and numerical studies, empirical models have been developed to predict the drift ratio and shear capacities of short RC wall under a high axial load level. Furthermore, a new axial capacity model has been proposed for checking gravity load collapse during earthquake attacks. Design recommendations for limiting the axial load level and proportioning appropriate ductile details have been proposed. It is concluded that axial load should be controlled during the design stage. The findings from this study can help improve the seismic resilience of RC buildings in Hong Kong.
