17202415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202415.value: 繪畫是藝術的一種主要形式，並進行交流的共同平台。 然而，它也是出了名的富有挑戰性的學習和掌握。 因此，顯著的研究工作一直致力於創建和部署的數字化工具，幫助人們更好地畫。 這些工具應該滿足兩個同時進行的，往往相互衝突的目標：（1）提高用戶的能力，以創造更好的輸出，而（2）保持它們的自然行為以最小的中斷。 為了實現這些目標，這項研究的目的是設計和構建交互式繪圖系統，可以預測哪些用戶可能需要根據他們以往的工作流程，在未來的繪製。 類似的自動校正的短信和自動完成的編程工具，我們的圖紙的預測可以提高輸出質量，同時減少了人工工作量。 用戶可以使用一個簡單的手勢接受的預測（如按一個熱鍵）而不破壞其流，修改預測的定制，或者乾脆不理它保持完全控制。 我們的主要假設是圖中，類似的許多其他人類活動，含有大量的重複，如點畫，艙口，和中風過1D輪廓和二維區域，或物體出現在多個動畫幀。 因此，什麼樣的用戶在過去所做的那樣可能會透露很多關於他們計劃在未來做。 我們採用數據驅動的方法：記錄和分析過去的繪圖工作流程，方便的互動創作和未來的合成重複。 我們把工作流重複紋理的一種形式，並擴展為交互式數字抽選紋理分析和合成方法。 儘管在各種常見的現象，如表面圖案，幾何結構，並且在圖形和交互動態運動現有方法的成功，它們主要集中於目標的物理現象。 我們延續這樣的分析和綜合的範圍人類活動，這往往是互動的，主觀的，和特質。 我們對單幀素描初步結果，並移動到（1）總圖的內容和繪畫媒介和（2）多幀連環畫風格的動畫。

17202715.label: Project Objectives
17202715.value: To design and analyze algorithms for the problem with general constraints at the offline and online nodes via mathematical programming methods. For instance, the chosen edges incident to a node should respect the node capacity or form an independent set in some underlying matroid. To design and analyze algorithms for the problem with arbitrary arrival order and also random arrival order. For arbitrary arrival order, free disposal is performed at the end to enforce the node constraints. Even for unit capacity, achieving a ratio better than 0.5 would be non-trivial. To design and analyze algorithms that can observe only the relative merits of edge weights. For example, we will consider privacy-sensitive applications, in which users may want to keep their actual weights secret, revealing only the relative merits of those weights.

17202715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202715.value: This project will investigate online matching problems in various settings. The underlying graph is bipartite, with the offline nodes constituting one side. In each step, an online node arrives and the weights of its incident edges connecting to the offline nodes are revealed. The algorithm then immediately decides whether any of the newly arriving edges are included in the matching, subject to certain constraints at the online node and offline nodes. The goal is to maximize the total weight of the edges in the matching, in which the performance ratio compares its weight with that of the offline optimal matching. The problem has wide applications in areas such as online advertising, resource allocation and logistics. For instance, in online advertising, an online node corresponds to a homepage request, for which a number of advertisements will be shown. In addition to budget constraints, the system should ensure that no competing advertisements are displayed together on the requested homepage. When the online nodes arrive in random order with only one offline node, the problem becomes the classical secretary problem. In preliminary work, we use a primal-dual continuous linear program (LP) framework to derive an asymptotically optimal algorithm for a generalized secretary problem in which the offline node can have capacity greater than one. In an upcoming SODA 2015 paper, we extend this algorithm to the online matching problem in which the offline nodes can have non-uniform capacities. Together with the continuous LP techniques developed in our previous SODA 2014 paper, we have a collection of powerful techniques for tackling new variants of the online matching problem: (1) General node constraints. For instance, the chosen edges incident to a node form an independent set in some underlying matroid, which forbids certain edges from being selected together, as in the foregoing online advertising example. (2) Arbitrary arrival order with free disposal. In the literature, this scenario means that the arrival order can be chosen adversarially, and that the constraints at the offline nodes are enforced at the end by disposing of certain edges. (3) Algorithms considering only relative merits. In privacy-sensitive applications, the algorithm cannot observe the actual edge weights, but only their relative merits. This project will unify and make important technical contributions to a number of research areas such as online matching, secretary problems and matroid theory. Moreover, our results will have significant impacts on the related practical applications. 本項目將探討多種設定下的在線匹配問題。基礎圖為二分圖，其中一邊由離線節點組成。在每一步，一個在線節點到達並顯示其與離線節點之間邊上的權值。在滿足基於在線節點和離線節點的特定約束的情況下，算法將立即決定是否將某些新到達的邊納入匹配中。目標是最大化該匹配中的邊權值之和，且這種情況下的性能比將對該匹配的權值和離線最優匹配的權值進行比較。該問題在在線廣告、資源分配和物流等領域具有廣泛應用。例如，於在線廣告中，一個在線節點對應一個網頁請求，針對該請求的一些廣告將會顯示。除預算約束外，系統應確保相互競爭的廣告不同時出現在請求的網頁中。當在線節點以隨機順序到達且只有一個離線節點時，該問題即為經典秘書問題。在初步工作中，我們用一個原對偶連續線性規劃框架導出了一個針對廣泛秘書問題的漸進最優算法；在該問題中離線節點可具有大於一的容量。在一篇SODA 2015論文中，我們將該算法擴展到離線節點可具有非均勻容量的在線匹配問題上。加上我們SODA 2014論文所開發的連續線性規劃技術，我們有強大的技術庫來應對在線匹配問題的新變種：（1）廣泛節點約束。例如，連接同一個節點的所選中的邊應形成某個擬陣中的獨立集；如在線廣告例子中所述，該約束禁止某些邊被同時選中。（2）任意到達順序並可自由處置。在文獻中，該情境意味着到達順序可被對抗性地決定，並且最終算法將處置某些邊以確保服從離線節點的約束。（3）只考慮相對價值的算法。在對隱私敏感的應用中，算法不能觀測真實的邊權值，而只能獲得它們的相對價值。本項目將針對在線匹配、秘書問題和擬陣理論等諸多研究領域進行整合並作出重要的技術貢獻。此外，我們的結果將對相關的實際應用產生重大影響。

17202715.label: Realisation of objectives
17202715.value: Objective 1 As a first step to employ mathematical programming in the project, we have considered a max-min allocation problem in which items are assigned to users such that the minimum utility of a user is maximized. Even the special case in which the utility of an item for a user is either 1 or some small epsilon is interesting, as we have shown that it is NP-hard to obtain an approximation ratio better than 2. Using a configuration linear program (CLP), we have expressed the bound on the minimum user utility as constraints on all the user nodes. As opposed to existing approaches, our algorithms and analysis do not directly use the feasibility of CLP. Instead we use integrality gap analysis and local search technique to show that our algorithms terminate with the claimed approximation ratios if the CLP is feasible. We have designed approximation algorithms based on the approach of hypergraph matching augmentation. In quasi-polynomial-time, our approach can achieve approximation ratio arbitrarily close to 3, and in polynomial-time, our approach gives 9-approximation. The results have appeared in ISAAC 2016 and Algorithmica 2018. Next, to develop a theoretical foundation for online optimization with matroid constraint, we have studied the problem of online submodular maximization under the special case of uniform matroid. The best previous performance ratio is 0.25 for general matroids by Chakrabarti and Kale (IPCO 2014), Buchbinder et al. (SODA 2015), and Chekuri et al. (ICALP 2015). The uniform matroid is the special case in which a solution is feasible if its size is at most some pre-determined budget k. We have designed a deterministic algorithm with competitive ratio at least 0.2959, and the ratio approaches 0.3178 as the budget k approaches infinity. We have also shown that our algorithm is optimal among a class of deterministic monotone algorithms that accept a new arriving element only if the objective is strictly increased. Further, we prove that no deterministic monotone algorithm can be strictly better than 0.25-competitive even for partition matroids. Interestingly, we show that randomized algorithms are strictly more powerful by giving a (non-monotone) randomized algorithm for partition matroids with ratio 0.3178. The results have appeared in SODA 2017/TALG 2018. The above results have inspired us to consider other budgeted optimization problems. For instance, given a graph, the goal is to find which k edges would have the largest impact on maximum flow queries on a network. This problem has important applications in areas like social network and network planning. We have shown the inapproximability of the problems and presented several heuristic algorithms. The results have appeared in Information Systems 2017. Objective 2 Using techniques in convex program, we have considered online optimization problems with covering or packing constraints with arbitrary arrival order. For instance, the capacity of a node can be expressed as a packing constraint. In the online covering problem, the variables are offline, and each constraint arrives at every time step. In the online packing problem, the number of constraints is fixed, and each variable arrives at every time step. By analyzing the Frenchel dual of the objective function, we have developed a primal-dual approach to give online algorithms for these generic problems. As our framework is very general, we can use it to simplify, unify, and improve upon previous results for several applications such as mixed covering and packing LPs, social welfare maximization with production costs, unrelated machine scheduling with startup costs, capacity constrained facility location, capacitated multicast problem, online set cover with set requests, etc. Our main idea is to increase the values of the primal variables exponentially proportional both to their current value and their coefficient in the constraint, but divided by the gradient of the objective function at the current solution. The dual is increased at a carefully chosen linear rate. Moreover, we use “shadow duals” to bound the primal cost more tightly. These dual variables are non-monotone and may be decreased at certain times. However, doing this carefully and maintaining such “non-monotone” duals is crucial in obtaining a sharp competitive ratio. The results have appeared in FOCS 2016. To illustrate the difference between arbitrary arrival order and random arrival order, we have studied the online problem with vector knapsack constraint, in which each item has a weight and a node has a capacity vector such that the items collected have to satisfy the capacity constraint in every dimension. The results are typically parameterized by the sparsity k, which is an upper bound on the number of non-zero coordinates of each weight vector. We have developed an O(k)-competitive algorithm for the slacked variant in which no single item can totally saturate any dimension. Even though our algorithm is deterministic, the techniques are inspired by randomized rounding. Specifically, our algorithm maintains a fractional solution, which is rounded at every step to achieve an integer solution. Even when each coordinate of the weight vector is arbitrarily small, we have shown that there is no algorithm with competitive ratio o(log k/ log log k). This is in contrast with the random arrival order scenario, in which competitive ratio close to 1 is possible. Our results have appeared in ESA 2017. Objective 3 We have also investigated the scenario in which the weight of an edge represents a user’s evaluation on a certain item, which can be considered private information. Hence, the goal is to develop a truthful allocation mechanism such that a user has no incentive to lie about his information. We have applied mechanism design techniques on a double auction problem between buyer and seller nodes. Using the technique of reserve price, we design a mechanism such that the subset of users that actually participate in the final allocation depends on the relative merits of their evaluations. Moreover, the party running the double auction aims to maximize the total weight of matched edges which represents the social welfare. Together with the Co-I, we have evaluated our mechanisms using real-world data and compare the experimental results with the theoretical analysis. The results have appeared in CLOSER 2017. Finally, as we have observed that the aforementioned mechanism depends on the relative merits of users’ private evaluations, comparison-based oblivious sorting is an important subroutine to filter out some buyers or sellers. As these applications involve a huge number of users, these mechanisms are often run in the cloud, and hence, the I/O costs under the external-memory paradigm will have an impact on the practical performance. We have made a significant step forward in understanding external-memory oblivious sorting algorithms. Specifically, we have constructed such an algorithm that is optimal in I/O-cost; moreover, our algorithm is also cache-agnostic in the sense that the algorithm does not need to know the storage hierarchy's internal parameters such as the cache and cache-line sizes. Our results have appeared in SODA 2018.

17202715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17202715.value: We have investigated various mathematical programs to tackle different optimization problems. As a starting point, we have used a configuration linear program to design and analyze algorithms for a max-min allocation problem in which the utility of an item for a user is either 1 or some small epsilon. Our constant approximation algorithms have appeared in ISAAC 2016/Algorithmica 2018. We have studied the problem of online submodular maximization under the special case of uniform matroid. While the best previous performance ratio is 0.25 for general matroids, we have improved the ratio to 0.2959, and the ratio approaches 0.3178 as the rank of the uniform matroid approaches infinity, where the ratio is optimal for a class of deterministic monotone algorithms. The results have appeared in SODA 2017/TALG 2018. Using techniques in convex program, we have considered online optimization problems with covering or packing constraints with arbitrary arrival order. By analyzing the Frenchel dual of the objective function, we have designed primal-dual online algorithms for these generic problems. Our framework is very general, and we have used it to simplify, unify, and improve upon previous results for several applications. The results have appeared in FOCS 2016. To illustrate the difference between arbitrary arrival order and random arrival order, we have studied the online problem with vector knapsack constraint, in which each item has a weight vector with sparsity at most k. We have developed an O(k)-competitive algorithm for the slacked variant in which no single item can totally saturate any dimension. We have proved that when each coordinate of the weight vector is arbitrarily small, there is no algorithm with competitive ratio o(log k/ log log k). This is in contrast with the random arrival order scenario, in which competitive ratio close to 1 is possible. Our results have appeared in ESA 2017. We have also investigated the scenario in which the weight of an edge represents a user’s evaluation on a certain item, which can be considered private information. We have developed a truthful allocation mechanism such that a user has no incentive to lie about his information via a double auction problem between buyer and seller nodes. The results have appeared in CLOSER 2017. Inspired by the aforementioned mechanism, we have constructed a comparison-based oblivious and cache-agnostic sorting algorithm that has optimal I/O cost in the external memory model. The results have appeared in SODA 2018.

17202715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17202715.value: We have developed online allocation algorithms under various settings. A common theme in the design of these algorithms is that only partial information is known at the moment an algorithm needs to make a decision. Towards the end of the project, we have seen that this algorithm design paradigm can lead to privacy preserving mechanisms, which can make decisions without complete knowledge of sensitive user data. In addition to performance ratio, future work should investigate other practical aspects such as I/O efficiency in real-world applications such has cloud platforms. While the decisions of the online algorithms in this project are made centrally, in modern peer-to-peer networks, it is also relevant to consider these problems in a distributed setting. Besides protecting its own privacy, each node might also behave arbitrarily. Hence, an interesting direction is to consider game theoretic and security notions in online allocation problems in a Byzantine environment. In addition to maintaining utility and security, desirable protocols should have good practical performance such as low round and communication complexity.

17202715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17202715.value: The results of this project have applications in online advertising, resource allocation and logistics. We have developed online primal-dual algorithms that make irrevocable decisions based on incomplete information and maintain feasible solutions. For instance, using the theory of matroids, we can capture the constraint that no competing advertisements are displayed together on a requested homepage. Although random arrival order provides mathematical beauty in some analysis, we have designed algorithms for the online submodular maximization problem (for instance, with vector packing constraint) for the more practical scenario in which online requests may arrive in some adversarial order. We have achieved a better theoretical understanding by showing that performance ratios achieved under random arrival order may be impossible under adversarial arrival order. In privacy-sensitive applications such as resource allocation in cloud computing, we have designed mechanisms that do not make decisions based on users’ actual evaluations, but only their relative merits. This has inspired us to develop oblivious algorithms for the sorting abstraction that has optimal I/O-efficiency in the external memory model. The techniques developed in this project will foster further research in online distributed mechanisms that can achieve both utility and security.

17203815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203815.value: The hyporheic zone (HZ) is the interstitial space immediately below or adjacent to a stream that contains some proportion of stream water. Stream water actively moves into and out of the HZ together with dissolved materials, supporting various important ecological and biogeochemical processes. The HZ also directly benefits humans by purifying stream water and mitigating floods. However, worldwide urbanization has significantly degraded many stream ecosystems. Streams are often turned into traditional drainage channels which completely remove the HZ. In recent decades, there has been increasing interest in restoring streams and channels to more natural states. However, stream restoration or rehabilitation projects rarely explicitly consider the HZ, despite its significance. This project will derive insights that will facilitate the incorporation of HZs during stream rehabilitation in highly urbanized areas. Residence time (RT) is the duration that a water molecule or a solute remains within the HZ, and directly relates to the proper functioning of the HZ. Thus, in this project, we will first evaluate the RTs of HZs under various conditions through laboratory experiments and numerical simulations, and then derive relationships between the RTs and their various governing factors. Using these derived relationships, researchers will be able to efficiently approximate the RTs, and thus the HZ’s functional level, of any stream segment. We will further apply scientific understanding of RTs at the small scale to larger-scale engineering stream network analysis, specifically linking the RT relationships with modeling tools to result in a framework that can predict the flow and water quality of a stream network. Such an integrated evaluation will allow HZs to be incorporated without affecting the conveyance capacity and the structural integrity of drainage channels, which are the main concerns in urban drainage systems. Finally, we will evaluate the effectiveness of different stream rehabilitation designs using case studies in Hong Kong, a task that is particularly challenging due to Hong Kong’s high level of urbanization. This project will facilitate the incorporation of HZs in future drainage systems, which is an important step in striking the balance between mitigating floods and conserving the environment. In combination with work from other researchers on stream and HZ restoration, this will lead, in the longer term, to changes in the practices of governments and agencies that strive for the sustainable stormwater management in the face of numerous challenges in highly urbanized cities. 潛流帶處於河溪兩岸及河床，溪水以及溶解物質不斷進出潛流帶，支援不同生態及生物化學作用。而潛流帶亦有助人類，如過濾溪水及舒緩水浸。但世界各地的城市發展嚴重影響河溪的生態系統，河溪已常被改造成沒有潛流帶的人工排水道。近幾十年來，多國已著手修復河溪及興建較自然的排水道，但仍極少顧及潛流帶和其重要性。這項目主要研究修復大城市河溪之潛流帶。水分子和溶質在潛流帶的停留時間直接影響潛流帶的運作，因此，這項目先以模擬程式來判斷不同情況下潛流帶的停留時間，然後再引申出停留時間與其因素的關系，而從這關系能有效地估計不同潛流帶的停留時間及運作情況。這項目亦進一步分析河溪網絡，引入停留時間的關系至模擬程式來估計河溪網絡的流速及水質。這全面的分析能在不影響河道的排水和結構的前提下修復河溪之潛流帶。最後，這項目會以香港為例子，來評估各種修復潛流帶的設計。總括而言，這項目重點研究修復河溪之潛流帶，對舒緩水浸及環境保護有極大幫助。再配合其他修復河溪的研究和工作，這項目能長遠地改變各政府機構的傳統做法，在大城市中亦能達到可持續的排水管理。

17203815.label: Realisation of objectives
17203815.value: 1. Examine the influence of heterogeneity and anisotropy on the residence times (RTs) of hyporheic zones (HZs) The first part of the project developed numerical models in MODFLOW to examine the influence of heterogeneity and anisotropy, and that of the natural K distribution in a streambed, on the RTs of the HZ. The general design of the model followed the study of Stonedahl et al. (2010) except the stream was straight instead of meandering, and the model parameters were derived from the studies of Stonedahl et al. and Zhou et al. (2014). The influence of heterogeneity and anisotropy on the RTs of HZ has been identified and 100% of this objective has been achieved. 2. Develop mathematical functions to link the RTs with various governing factors The second part of the project developed mathematical functions to link the RTs of a single pool-riffle sequence to various governing factors (e.g., discharge, bedform geometry, streambed hydraulic conductivity and groundwater flow), based on previously published data. The governing factors were first transformed into dimensionless parameters using Buckingham π theorem and the equations were developed using exponential and multiple linear regressions. Overall, 80% of the data from the Trauth et al. (2013) dataset were used to derive the equations, and the remaining 20% were used for validation. Besides, the data from Tonina (2005), Tonina and Buffington (2011) were also used for validation. The coefficients of the proposed functions have been obtained and results of validation showed that the predicted values of the derived equations generally agreed well with the original data. 100% of this objective has been achieved. 3. Coupling stream and groundwater modeling to examine the RTs The third part of the project built coupled stream and groundwater models to more accurately examine the RTs of HZ in a straight pool-riffle channel with floodplain. Flume model was firstly built and the impacts of discharge and groundwater flow on the HZ flux were investigated using tracer experiments. Then numerical model was built and calibrated with experimental data, and parameters were changed to further investigate impacts of more governing factors on the RTs of HZ, including stream discharge, streambed amplitudes and groundwater flow. Flume experiments have been completed and numerical models have been calibrated. The influence of governing factors on the RTs in a straight pool-riffle channel with floodplain has been derived. 100 % of this objective has been achieved. 4. Evaluate effectiveness of different stream rehabilitation designs in restoring hyporheic zone The final part of the project examined the effectiveness of different stream rehabilitation designs in restoring the HZ, including a straight pool-riffle channel with floodplain, a straight channel with baffles and a sinuous pool-riffle channel. Similar to the third part, both flume and numerical models coupling stream and groundwater were built for each design. Factors, such as stream discharge, streambed amplitudes, groundwater flow, sinuosity, slope and etc., were examined for their influence of the HZ flux. Finally, the optimal designs of morphological and hydraulic conditions that generate the maximum flux, largest scale and longest RTs of the HZ flux were found. 100 % of this objective has been achieved.

17203815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203815.value: 1. Examine the influence of heterogeneity and anisotropy on the residence times (RTs) of hyporheic zones (HZs) Heterogeneity and anisotropy were both found to shorten the mean and median RTs while increasing the range of the RTs. Moreover, heterogeneous K fields arranged in a more orderly pattern had longer RTs than those with random K distributions. These results could facilitate the design of streambed K values and distributions to achieve the desired RT during river restoration. They could also assist the translation of results from the more commonly considered homogeneous and/or isotropic conditions into heterogeneous and anisotropic field situations. Please refer to the paper named Impacts of Streambed Heterogeneity and Anisotropy on Residence Time of Hyporheic Zone in part C for reference. 2. Develop mathematical functions to link the RTs with various governing factors Mathematical functions were derived to predict the RTs in a single pool-riffle sequence by considering all various governing factors, including stream discharge, bedform amplitudes, streambed hydraulic conductivity and groundwater flow. The coefficients of the proposed functions have been obtained and results of validation showed that the predicted values of the derived equations generally agreed well with the original data. The derived equations require inputs that can be readily determined, and thus provide a very convenient and efficient way to approximate the median RTs of HZ. They can therefore be used to quickly generate insights into the physicochemical and biological effects of HZ, which should be beneficial for processes such as water quality prediction and HZ restoration through pool-riffle sequences in stream rehabilitation. Please refer to the paper named Empirical Equations to Predict the Characteristics of Hyporheic Exchange in a Pool-Riffle Sequence in part C for reference. 3. Coupling stream and groundwater modeling to examine the RTs A flume model of a straight pool-riffle channel with floodplain was built. And a numerical model coupling stream and groundwater was further developed and successfully calibrated using experiment data. It was found that in a straight pool-riffle channel with floodplain, the median RTs significantly reduced as groundwater flow increased and impacts of gaining conditions were more significant than that of losing conditions. Besides, a threshold was observed regarding the impacts of streambed amplitudes on the median RTs while median RTs were not sensitive to stream discharge. Finally, the median RTs of bank-induced HZ flux were generally larger than that of bed-induced HZ flux. These findings provided insights to the RTs of bed- and bank induced HZ flux and promoted the development of stream restoration techniques. 4. Evaluate effectiveness of different stream rehabilitation designs in restoring hyporheic zone The impacts of governing factors such as stream discharge, streambed amplitude, slope and groundwater flow on the HZ flux in a straight pool-riffle channel, a straight channel with baffles and a sinuous pool-riffle channel were determined. By combination of all the results, the optimal designs of morphological and hydraulic conditions that generate maximum HZ flux, largest scale and longest RTs of the flux could be derived. Results would directly provide practical guidance to different stream rehabilitation designs according to various objectives.

17203815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203815.value: This study so far has focused on steady state of stream and groundwater flow. However, the stream flow changes temporarily during a rainfall event or permanently when there is a change in land use, climate, etc. Therefore, the potential development of the research would be to investigate impacts of changing streamflow on the HZ flux. Stream discharge scenarios, including flow regimes of various hydrographs during rainfall events, and flow regimes that represent the typical hydrographs of stream flooding before and after urbanization can be investigated in a straight pool-riffle channel using tracer experiments in a flume. The concentration curves of tracer under different hydrograph patterns would be compared. Numerical model coupling stream and groundwater model would be built to investigate the HZ flux, RT distribution and flow path of the HZ flux under various hydrograph patterns. The results will provide a better understanding on the impacts of rainfall events, flood events on the HZ flux, as well as impacts of urbanization and climate change on the HZ flux in a pool-riffle channel.

17203815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203815.value: The hyporheic zone (HZ) is the interstitial space surrounding a stream where stream water actively moves into and out of with dissolved materials, supporting various important ecological and biogeochemical processes. Thus the HZs play an essential role in stream ecosystem functions. However, worldwide urbanization commonly removes the HZ while recent stream restoration projects rarely explicitly consider the HZ, despite its significance. This project has derived insights that would facilitate the incorporation of HZs during stream rehabilitation in highly urbanized areas. Residence time (RT) is the duration that a water molecule or a solute remains within the HZ, and directly relates to the proper functioning of the HZ. Thus, in this project, we first determined the RTs under various conditions through numerical simulations, and then derived mathematical functions to predict the RTs using various governing factors. 17204115.label: Project Objectives
17204115.value: Data-set collection: We plan to collect, and publicly share, a large set of demonstrations for a wide range of manipulation tasks, using both parallel jaws grippers and multi-finger hands, and incorporating rich sensor readings. The tasks we have in mind include knot-tying, laundry organizing and folding, box or furniture assembly, coil winding, bag filling, and surgical suturing. Learning grasp policies from demonstrations: We aim to study how to recover the deformable objects' geometry, dynamics, and physical properties from large amounts of demonstrations. We will also show how to leverage the learned knowledge about the deformable objects to achieve high quality grasp policies. Learning manipulation policies from demonstrations: We will improve the state-of-the-art techniques by incorporating rich sensor readings, including visual priors, inertial profiles and haptic feedbacks. We will also investigate how to manipulate deformable objects at robots' extreme speed by incorporating objects' dynamics during manipulation. Moreover, we would like to study the way to accurately place a deformable object like a rope at a goal configuration, which will involve quasi-static manipulation and underactuated systems. Deep-learned visual and tactile features for learning from demonstrations: We would utilize the recent advances in deep learning to help robots directly learn grasp and manipulation policies from RGB and tactile sensors, rather than relying on high precision depth sensors, which are not applicable in the small workspace of surgical robots.

Learning grasp policies from demonstrations: We aim to study how to recover the deformable objects' geometry, dynamics, and physical properties from large amounts of demonstrations. We will also show how to leverage the learned knowledge about the deformable objects to achieve high quality grasp policies.

Learning manipulation policies from demonstrations: We will improve the state-of-the-art techniques by incorporating rich sensor readings, including visual priors, inertial profiles and haptic feedbacks. We will also investigate how to manipulate deformable objects at robots' extreme speed by incorporating objects' dynamics during manipulation. Moreover, we would like to study the way to accurately place a deformable object like a rope at a goal configuration, which will involve quasi-static manipulation and underactuated systems.

Deep-learned visual and tactile features for learning from demonstrations: We would utilize the recent advances in deep learning to help robots directly learn grasp and manipulation policies from RGB and tactile sensors, rather than relying on high precision depth sensors, which are not applicable in the small workspace of surgical robots.

17204115.label: Realisation of objectives
17204115.value: 1. We have successfully collected a large number of data allowing robots to learn advanced grasping and manipulation policies by themselves. In addition, we also explore how to use reinforcement learning to enable robots to collect data by themselves by exploring by themselves how to interact with the surrounding work and to achieve tasks. 2. We have successfully enable a robot to autonomously learn how to grab deformable objects by itself. 3. We have successfully enable a robot to autonomously learn how to manipulate deformable objects to a specific target configuration in terms of a set of localization points and/or features. 4. We have allowed the learned controller to deal with rich image, point cloud features and tactile by using deep learning.

17204115.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204115.value: During this three-year project, we have successfully accomplished our target: designing an autonomous robot grasping and manipulation system that can learn from demonstrated data. Besides that, we also enable a robot to not only depend on manual demonstrations but also can autonomously interact with environments to collect sufficient data for its learning. This extension actually greatly increases the intelligence of our manipulation system. The main results are presented in our papers: "3-D Deformable Object Manipulation Using Deep Neural Networks" and "Deep-Learned Collision Avoidance Policy for Distributed Multiagent Navigation". We also find that it is not enough to just design advanced algorithms. For efficient grasping and manipulation and making them useful for real industrial applications, we need to develop advanced hardware systems. In particular, we have developed a fragile hand with new mechanical designs to simplify the algorithm requirement for grasping and manipulation. For this part of work, the result is in "Design of Anthropomorphic Fingers With Biomimetic Actuation Mechanism". We also investigated the low-level dynamics algorithm accelerated using GPU, which is critical for the learning from demonstration and reinforcement learning algorithms to be efficient. This part is in our paper "Parallel Dynamics Computation Using Preﬁx Sum Operations".

17204115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204115.value: For further development, 1. We will investigate developing advanced reinforcement learning algorithm to allow robots to learn advanced manipulation skills completely by themselves from scratch, rather then relying on a large number of human demonstrations. 2. We will extend the techniques developed in this project to other force- and torque-related tasks. For instance, we have learned from our industrial partners that our learning from demonstration technique has great potential to be applied in the robotic polishing task -- which is one of the open industrial problems in robotics. 3. We will continue working with our industrial partners to reduce the gap of applying our techniques in cloth-related industry.

17204115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204115.value: This project allows a robot to learn how to accomplish complicated deformable object grasping and manipulation tasks by learning from examples provided by human experts. In this way, the robot can mimic human's capability to learn how to perform a task by learning from a teacher. The resulting autonomous grasping and manipulation system for deformable objects has great potential in cloth industry and other related applications.

Carry out a systematic test programme to design, fabricate and test the rock-like solids so that they can have micro-fluid inclusions with high pressures and show the abnormally delayed deformation and/or fracture phenomenon. 17204415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204415.value: Both intact rocks and cement concrete are construction materials and can be used to function as structures of buildings and infrastructures, because both have similar high rigidity against deformation and, tensile, shear and compressive strengths against fractures. In-situ intact rocks are excavated for tunnels, caverns and slopes in ground. As part of structures, their mechanical behaviour plays an important role to the safety and serviceability of the engineered openings and facilities in the ground. However, the in-situ intact rocks after their excavation do have some abnormally delayed mechanical behaviour. One of the most peculiar behaviour is the so-called rockburst. The rockburst involves the implosion of the intact rock into the excavated tunnel with the release of significant amounts of energy, which often causes disasters. Although numerous investigations have been carried out over the past 50 years around the world, the rockburst is still an unexpected, unpredicted and undescribed phenomenon with the current theories of applied mechanics and rock mechanics. Cement concrete does not have any such abnormally delayed behaviour. The mechanical behaviour of concrete can be predicted and described using the current theories of applied mechanics and concrete mechanics. The lithification process of rocks is similar to that of concrete. But their ambient pressure and temperature are substantially different. Intact rocks are any lithified solid material of sedimentary, igneous, or metamorphic origin. They are normally lithified at very deep ground, where the compressive stresses such as the overburden stress can be tens to hundreds mega-pascal (MPa) and the temperature can be many hundreds °C. Their micro-voids can be infilled by fluid (gas or liquid) inclusions with high pressures. Concrete is a man-made rock-like material formed by mixing cement, rock aggregates and water together. The lithification process of the man-made fluid mixture to form concrete is taken place at zero to ten kPa compressive stress and tens °C temperature conditions. Therefore, their micro-voids may be infilled by fluid inclusions but with almost zero pressure. The fluid inclusions with high pressure in the micro-voids can be the cause and energy source of the abnormally delayed mechanical behaviour of the in-situ intact rocks after excavation, which has been theoretically shown and validated. This GRF project aims to test and validate whether or not the cement concrete can similarly have such abnormally delayed mechanical behaviour if its lithification process from the initial fluid mixture is undertaken at high compressive stresses in laboratory experiments. 岩石和混凝土拥有相类似抵抗变形的刚度和抵抗破坏的抗拉、抗剪和抗压强度。因此，它们都是建筑材料，都能被用于建筑和基础设施的结构。隧道、硐室和斜坡的工程建设常常要开挖地下完整岩石。作为地下工程结构的一部分，完整岩石的力学行为对地下工程开挖空间和设施的安全与使用起到重要的作用。 但是，在工程开挖后，依然留在原地的附近完整岩石的确存在一些异常滞后的力学行为。最为奇特的行为就是所谓的岩爆。岩爆是硐壁完整岩石向已经被开挖好的硐室内部空间喷射现象。它同时伴有大量动能的释放。它时常造成灾害。虽然在过去50多年中，世界各地的研究人员都做了大量的研究，但是，岩爆依然是一种不能用现有应用力学和岩石力学理论来预期、预测和描述的现象。在另一方面，混凝土没有这种异常滞后力学行为。它的力学行为可以用现有应用力学和混凝土力学理论来预测和描述。 岩石成岩过程同混凝土的胶结凝固过程相似。但是，它们形成过程中的温度和压强具巨大的差异。完整岩石具火成、沉积和变质作用来源。它们一般在地下深部成岩。四周围压可达到数百兆帕，温度可达数百度。它们的微细孔隙可能被具有高压强的流体（液体或气体）包裹体所充填。混凝土是人们用水泥、砂粒和水混合在一起而胶结形成的一种类似岩石的材料。它们的凝固过程一般在零到数十千帕和几十度温度条件下进行的。因此，它们的孔隙可能也被流体冲填，但是流体的压强应该几乎等于零。 完整岩石微细孔隙内部的、拥有高压强的流体包裹体能够是，开挖后，留在原地、作为硐壁的完整岩石的异常滞后力学行为的原因和能源。这个假说已经被理论所证明和验证。因此，本研究计划目的就是要用实验室的试验，来测试和验证，在高压下胶结形成的混凝土能否具有岩石的异常滞后力学行为。

17204415.label: Realisation of objectives
17204415.value: The four objectives are realized via the following research activities and results. 1) A fabrication method is a set of laboratory apparatus that is invented and used for fabricating samples of the rock-like solid with micro-gas inclusion of high pressure. It consists of a sealed cylinder jacket, two pistons, a hydraulic pump, a load cell, LVDT, and data logger. Sample fabrication and test procedure is developed and established. It has three main steps: (a) mix cement, water and gas entraining liquid (i.e., hydrogen peroxide); (b) cast and pressurize the cement paste mixed with hydrogen peroxide liquid until hardened; (c) take out of the hardened solids by jacking. A series of tests are carried out to fabricate many cylindrical samples of rock-like solids with micro-gas inclusions of small to large pressure by varying the amount of hydrogen peroxide liquid and the compaction pressure and different cementing materials such as Portland cement and epoxy resin. A series of laboratory physical and mechanical tests are conducted to measure and examine the density, uniaxial compressive strength, Brazilian tensile strength, Young’s modulus, SEM images and CT scanning images of the fabricated samples. Furthermore, the phenomenon of disc fracturing in the fabricated cylindrical samples is discovered and examined in detail. The dividing curve for the automatic occurrence of the disc fractures in the fabricated cylindrical samples after releasing the applied hardening pressure is examined in terms of the applied hardening pressure and the amount of the added hydrogen peroxide liquid. 2) An ejection method is a set of laboratory apparatus that is invented and used to examine the rockburst due to micro-gas inclusions. It can burst or eject a solid (rock or steel) piston from a completed sealed (rock or steel) cylinder infilled with cement paste. Portland cement, water and hydrogen peroxide liquid are mixed to form the cement paste with suitable weight ratios of the three materials. The piston is tightly inserted into the steel cylinder and seal the cement paste. The chemical reactions among the three materials generate the micro-oxygen gas inclusions in the cement paste. The cement paste in the sealed and compacted cylinder would expand. The expansion can push upward the solid piston and can further burst and/or eject the piston with part of the cement paste to fly into the air. A video camera is used to record the ejection process in real time. Many tests are carried out to examine the ejections with a series of weight ratios of the three materials. The friction between the piston and cylinder is also tested. A theoretical model is developed and used for analyses and prediction of the ejection phenomena in terms of the three materials. The experimental results and the theoretical results are well compared. The ejection heights and velocities of the piston and the cement paste have certain positive correlations with the amount of the added hydrogen peroxide liquid. Both results demonstrate that a tiny amount of the hydrogen peroxide liquid can generate a suitable amount of micro-gas inclusions of high pressure in the cement paste to burst and eject the heavy piston that is tightly inserted into the cylinder. Both the laboratory test method and the theoretical equations can provide quantitative tools to examine the rockburst in rock excavation and the magma eruption of volcanoes. 3) A cell method is invented and used to examine the bursting of rock and coal samples due to highly pressurized micro-gas inclusions in laboratory. This set of apparatus consists of a transparent triaxial cell, a coal or rock sample, a gas decompression device, a gas tank, a gas pressure sensor, strain gauges, and a data logger. It can have a thin tempered glass plate. The sample is located within the sealed cell. After vacuuming the air in the cell, the mass of highly pressurized carbon dioxide gas is filled into the cell via a pipe from the gas tank until the gas pressures in the cell and the tank are balanced. The highly pressurized gas can further penetrate into the micro-voids of the solid sample for about 12 hours. Subsequently, different applied gas pressures and different gas release rates are tested for coal samples with different water contents. During the gas releasing process, the coal sample in the cell can have different responses and behavior in terms of the applied maximum gas pressure, the gas release rate, and the water content. The response and behavior change from remaining intact, to occurrence of dominate fractures and to bursting of the sample into various sizes of fragments. The tests are further used to examine the energy releases of both the pressurized free micro-gas inclusions and the desorbed gas by the solids, as well as the energy dissipation of solid fragmentation quantitatively. 4) A pipe method is designed and used to examine the shock-wave, flying distance and deposition of rock/coal bursting by highly pressurized micro-gas inclusions. It is a laboratory apparatus that consists of a coal or sand chamber, a long and horizontally placed plastic pipe, gas pressure sensors, gas tank and a gate of thin tempered glass plate. The air in the cell fully filled with coal particles of less than 2 mm is vacuumed by pump. Then, the gas with pressure values of 0.2 to 0.6 MPa from the tank is slowly injected into the coal or sand particles within the chamber via a pipe of 4 mm in diameter. The glass gate is suddenly broken to initiate bursting and flying of the coal particles along the pipe due to their pressurized micro-gas inclusions. The bursting process is videoed and the gas pressures at different pipe locations are measured. After each test, particle sizes of coal depositions along each meter within the 11 m long pipe are tested and compared among themselves and the original particle size distribution. The gas pressure sensors can measure a sudden and rapid pressure increase in milliseconds during the rapid flowing of the gas-particle mixture within the pipe. The peak value of the measured pressure can be two times of the applied gas pressure in the tank. They indicate the presence of shock waves of the mixture flowing in the pipe. Segregation of coal particle deposition is found from the particle size measurement. 5) A numerical method is developed with the finite-discrete element method for simulation of the rock or coal burst induced by the micro-gas inclusions with high pressure. The solids are represented with deformable triangular discrete elements. Interfaces of the solid elements are infilled with compressed gas. The gas can only flows through the interfaces. The interface aperture determines the gas flow permeability. The absorbed gas in solid element can be desorbed if the interface free gas pressure decreases. The numerical method is used to examine the effect of micro-gas inclusion release rate and pressure on the fracture and fragmentation of rock/coal samples. 6) Analytical and boundary element methods are further developed and used to examine the elastic stress and displacement fields in rocks and other solid materials due to internal and/or external loading. These capabilities and results can quantify and predict the effect of micro-gas inclusions in the rocks due to excavations. 7) The above physical, numerical and analytical results are further compared with current rock engineering practice.

17204415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204415.value: 1) Four new laboratory methods (i.e., fabrication, ejection, cell and pipe methods) are invented and used for examining rockburst and coal-burst. 2) The fabrication method can successfully fabricate and form the high strength and rigid rock-like material with micro-fluid/gas inclusions of high pressure. The presence of the highly pressurized micro-gas inclusions can automatically make the cylindrical rock-like materials to form disc fractures similar to those occurring in deep rock coring. (see Part C: Research Output 9.1, 10.1, 10.2, 10.3, 10.4, 10. 6, 10.7). 3) The ejection method demonstrates that a very small weight of oxygen gas generated by chemical reaction in a sealed steel cylinder with cement paste can eject its tight and heavy steel piston, which shows that the micro-gas inclusion can have high pressure and be the power source to cause ejection and/or burst of a sealed intact rock. Such ejection result can elaborate the mechanisms of rock burst and volcano eruption. (see Part C: Research Output 10.5, 10.8). 4) The cell method demonstrates that the gas pressure and gas release rate of micro-gas inclusions in coal samples in the pressurized gas cell dominate the occurrence and intensity of coal fragmentation and coal-burst. The low gas pressure and/or decompression rate induce only the deformation of coal samples. The increase in both the pressure and release rate can lead to fracturing and fragmentation. The major energy of the fragmentation and/or coal-burst is the expansion energy of the free-state micro-gas inclusions inside the coal sample. The adsorbed micro-gas inclusions in the coal sample plays a minor role. Water content can affect the coal burst. (see Part C: Research Output 8.3, 8.8, 10.1). 5) The pipe method demonstrates that strong shock waves during coal-burst along long plastic pipe can occur in coal samples with micro-gas of high pressures. The pure gas eruption of the similar gas volume and pressure shows only weak or little shock waves in the pipe. This peak pressure is about 2 times higher than the applied gas pressure. The deposition of the coal fragments have segregation. The coal fragment size has a positive correlation with deposition distance along the pipe. Larger sizes deposit far distance. (see Part C: Research Output 8.9, 10.1). 6) The numerical method with FDEM code can simulate the interaction of pressured micro-gas inclusion and rock/coal. The proposed algorithm for the micro-gas inclusion and solid interaction can model the phenomena of rock and coal fractures and bursts due to internal micro-gas inclusions with high pressure. (see Part C: Research Output 10.1). 7) Many new solutions of related elastic fields in rocks due to internal and external loadings are derived and examined using both analytical and BEM methods, which offers a theoretical foundation for rockburst. (see Part C: Research Output 8.4, 8.5, 8.6, 8.7, 10.9, 10.10). 8) The above results are consistent with the observations of rockbursts at field and current engineering practice for preventing rockburst. (see Part C: Research Output 8.1, 8.2, 9.2, 9.3).

17204415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204415.value: 1) The fabrication method can be further developed and used to design and produce new rock-like materials of high strength and rigidity and with or without micro-fluid/gas inclusions of high pressure in small to large sizes. 2) The ejection method can be further developed and used to examine the mechanism of rockbursts in rock excavation and the mechanism of volcano eruptions and to calibrate the related theoretical prediction methods and results. 3) The cell method can be further developed and used to examine the effect of the pressure and release rate of micro-gas inclusions in various rocks for cracking and fragmentation and bursting. 4) The pipe method can be further developed and used to examine the effect of the pressure and release rate of micro-gas inclusions in various rocks for their shock waves and deposition distance and segregations along the long pipe. 5) The numerical method with FDEM code can be further developed and used to simulate the interaction between the micro-gas inclusions and various rocks and predict their fractures and bursts due to the internal micro-gas inclusions of high pressures. 6) The new solutions of related elastic fields in rocks due to internal and external loadings can be further developed and used to examine the global and local stress and strain fields in underground rocks due to internal and/or external loading induced by various engineering activities.

17204415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204415.value: Rockburst is the phenomenon involving implosion of the rock into the tunnel with the release of significant amounts of energy. It can suddenly occur in surrounding intact rocks at many minutes, hours, days, and months after rock excavation or tunneling. It can cause severe damage and disasters. However, no credible means are available to explain or predict the delayed behaviour of rockburst, because its cause and mechanism are incorrect. This project examines the cause hypothesis of originality proposed by this project team. The micro-gas inclusions can have high pressure and enough active energy to induce rockburst after excavation. Four laboratory methods are invented and used for examining and testing the mechanical behaviour of rock-like solids with micro-gas inclusions of small to high pressure. The physical results demonstrate that the micro-gas inclusions can be several microns in diameter and have high pressure of several MPa. The micro-gas inclusions can induce fractures and bursts after the intact rocks are disturbed. The occurrences of fractures and bursts depend upon the volume and pressure of micro-gas inclusions. Furthermore, new numerical, analytical and boundary element methods are developed and used to examine the response and behavior of rocks due to internal and external loadings. Findings of this project can provide a credible means to explain and predict the rockburst and prevent its damage.

17204715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204715.value: This project studies efficient auction-based mechanisms for pricing dynamic cloud provisioning and resource scaling in IaaS cloud platforms. Cloud computing services are proliferating in today's Internet, aiming to meet users' resource demands at any time using virtualization technologies, which pack resources (CPU, RAM, disk and bandwidth) into virtual machines (VMs). While most of the major clouds provide fixed types of pre-configured VMs (e.g., Amazon EC2, Microsoft Azure), a latest emerging trend is to offer customized bundles of resources in the form of tailor-made VMs to best meet a user's need (e.g., Gridspot, ProfitBricks). Although the granularity of resource provisioning keeps improving, fixed pricing policies are still dominant, charging customers a fixed amount for each pre-configured VM or each unit of resources. Such a pricing method inherently lacks market agility and efficiency, jeopardizing both the provider's revenue and customers' utility. In addition, current clouds allow scaling of a user's resources by launching and terminating extra VMs (e.g., AWS Auto Scaling), but not ''hot'' resource addition or release to/from a running VM (except for the disk). In many cases, users may wish to adjust resources on VMs where their jobs have already started to run with the variation of their workload, to eliminate the need for copying data to new VMs. Virtualization technologies are in fact ready for real-time, on-demand VM partitioning and resource addition/removal, e.g., utilizing CPU hotplug and memory ballooning techniques. The major obstacle that prevents practical deployment of dynamic resource scaling lies in the lack of an effective pricing mechanism to charge the increased/released resources, according to their current availability and scarcity. This project proposes a set of dynamic pricing mechanisms for customized VMs and dynamically scaled resources, based on truthful, computationally-efficient auctions. The mechanisms allocate cloud resources according to real-time user demand, and price the resources on the spot, such that the social welfare, including both the cloud provider's and the users' benefits, is maximized over the long run. We start from the basic case of customized VM assembly and pricing in an offline setting, and then extend our study to online VM provisioning, resource scaling and pricing over time. We focus on computational resource (CPU, RAM, disk) provisioning first, and then involve bandwidth allocation in the setting of virtual cluster provisioning and pricing, with data traffic between VMs. We seek rigorous theoretical analysis to our mechanisms, as well as real-world implementation and evaluation in practical settings.

17204715.label: Realisation of objectives
17204715.value: We have achieved Objectives 1-3 in this project to 100%, and achieved Objective 4 to 80%. For object 1, Goals a) and b) have been achieved. We designed an efficient randomized auction mechanism based on a novel application of smoothed analysis and randomized reduction, for dynamic VM provisioning and pricing in geo-distributed cloud data centers. An exact algorithm to solve the perturbed instances of the offline optimization problem in polynomial time in expectation was proposed, and an MIDR allocation algorithm and payment scheme were designed for the auction. This auction achieves (i) truthfulness and individual rationality in expectation, (ii) polynomial running time in expectation, and (iii) (1 ε)-optimal social welfare in expectation for resource allocation, where ε can be arbitrarily close to 0. The result was reported in publication 9 in Part C-8. For Objective 2, towards Goals a) and b), we designed online VM auctions where each bidder requests a bundle of resources with desired occupation durations in possibly different data centers. We consider convex running costs of servers which depend on the resource usage on the servers. We designed an online algorithm based on the primal-dual optimization framework for dynamic resource allocation, which can handle various convex server cost functions, and reveal the payments through the dual variables. We hence designed truthful, polynomial-time auctions to achieve social welfare maximization with good competitive ratios. We then used a randomized reduction algorithm to convert the social welfare maximizing auctions to profit maximizing auctions, with competitive ratios comparable to those for social welfare. The results were reported in the publication 1 in Part C-8. For the case that a user has some flexibility in her resource usage time with different willingness-to-pay, we designed an online auction mechanism where each user bids (i) a utility, reflecting the amount that the user is willing to pay for executing its job, and (ii) a soft deadline, specifying the preferred finish time of the job, as well as a penalty function specifying the cost when the deadline is violated at different levels. The auction runs in polynomial time, provides truthfulness guarantee, and achieves optimal social welfare for the cloud ecosystem. The results were reported in Publication 2 in Part C-8. For Goal c), in the context of VM allocation for running NFV (network function virtualization) service chains, we design an online stochastic auction mechanism for on-demand resource provisioning and pricing at the NFV provider. Our auction takes in buy bids for service chains from multiple customers and sell bids from various resource suppliers (possibly previous buyers with superfluous resources) to supplement the providers geo-distributed resource pool. Instead of using the classical double auction, we extended online primal-dual optimization framework to handle both buyers and sellers, with a new competitive analysis. The online mechanism maximizes the expected social welfare of the system with a good competitive ratio, while guaranteeing truthfulness in bidding, individual rationality for both buyers and sellers, and polynomial time for computation. The results were published in publication 3 in Part C-8. For Goal d), we explored the optimal pricing function forms to produce the optimal resource prices in an auction like mechanism. Especially, we design optimal pricing functions based on current resource utilization ratios in a wide array of demand-supply relationships and resource occupation durations, and proved worst-case competitive ratios in social welfare. The results were reported in publication 1 in Part C-9. In addition, we have found that the auction mechanism design techniques studied in the project can be applied to incentive design for emergency demand response in colocation data centers, where the colocation operator offers awards to tenants (following an auction mechanism) for their voluntary power reduction during power emergencies. The results were reported in publications 4, 5, 6 in Part c-8 and publication 2 in Part c-9. For Objective 3, towards Goals a) and b), we studied online virtual cluster auctions where each user bids for a cluster of tailor-made VMs at (possibly) different data centers with a specified usage duration and bandwidth demand between VMs, or multiple optional bundles of VMs with different valuations. We designed novel online algorithms for dynamic VC provisioning, inter-VM traffic routing and resource pricing, achieving truthfulness, individual rationality, computation efficiency, and a good competitive ratio in social welfare. The results were reported in publication 7 in Part c-8 and publication 3 in Part c-9. For Goal c), we proposed online and offline dynamic pricing mechanism for inter-datacenter bandwidth resources, via Shapley value based auctions. The Shapley value based payment in the auctions addresses ISP’s bandwidth charges. Our auctions are truthful, individually rational, budget balanced and approximately efficient in social welfare. The results have been included in publication 12 in Part c-8. For Goal d), we designed efficient, truthful online auctions for resource provisioning and pricing in the practical cases of dynamic VM scaling, where: (i) users bid for customized VMs to use in future durations, and can bid again in the following time to increase resources, indicating both scale-up and scale-out options; (ii) the cloud provider packs the demanded VMs on heterogeneous servers for energy cost minimization on the go. We design resource prices maintained for each type of resource on each server to achieve threshold-based online allocation and charging, as well as a novel competitive analysis technique based on submodularity of the offline objective, to show that a good competitive ratio is achieved. The results were included in publications 8, 10, 11 in Part c-8 and publications 4, 5 in Part c-9. For Objective 4, we developed the cloud management toolkit, which implements our mechanisms and algorithms designed. We evaluated our algorithms in publications reported in simulated/emulated systems on our own testbed with workloads produced following the Google cluster-usage data and and other real-world traces, and reported evaluation results in terms of social welfare, profit, etc. We have made efforts on constructing a cross-institutional cloud testbed, but have found it very difficult due to different policy/security regulations of different institutes and lack of management and technical support in different institutes. On the other hand, we realized that the main contributions in the project can be reasonably well evaluated using emulated systems following real-world traces. So we have largely resorted to evaluations on our own testbed.

17204715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204715.value: In publication 1 in Part C-8, we designed an online algorithm based on the primal-dual optimization framework for dynamic resource allocation, which can handle various convex server cost functions, and reveal the payments through the dual variables. We hence designed truthful, polynomial-time auctions to achieve social welfare maximization with good competitive ratios. We then used a randomized reduction algorithm to convert the social welfare maximizing auctions to profit maximizing auctions, with competitive ratios comparable to those for social welfare. In 2 in Part C-8, we designed an online auction mechanism where each user bids (i) a utility, reflecting the amount that the user is willing to pay for executing its job, and (ii) a soft deadline, specifying the preferred finish time of the job, as well as a penalty function specifying the cost when the deadline is violated at different levels. The auction runs in polynomial time, provides truthfulness guarantee, and achieves optimal social welfare for the cloud ecosystem. In 3 in Part C-8, we designed an online stochastic auction mechanism for on-demand resource provisioning and pricing. Our auction takes in buy bids for service chains from multiple customers and sell bids from various resource suppliers (possibly previous buyers with superfluous resources) to supplement the providers geo-distributed resource pool. The online mechanism maximizes the expected social welfare of the system with a good competitive ratio, while guaranteeing truthfulness in bidding, individual rationality for both buyers and sellers, and polynomial time for computation. In 4-6 in Part C-8 and 2 in Part c-9, we applied our auction mechanism design for incentive design for emergency demand response in colocation data centers. In 7 in Part C-8 and 3 in Part c-9, we designed novel online algorithms for dynamic VC provisioning, inter-VM traffic routing and resource pricing, achieving truthfulness, individual rationality, computation efficiency, and a good competitive ratio in social welfare. In 8, 10, 11 in Part C-8 and 4, 5 in Part C-9, we designed efficient, truthful online auctions for resource provisioning and pricing in the practical cases of dynamic VM scaling. In 12 in Part C-8, we proposed online and offline dynamic pricing mechanism for inter-datacenter bandwidth resources, via Shapley value based auctions; our auctions are truthful, individually rational, budget balanced and approximately efficient in social welfare. 17204715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204715.value: A cross-institutional cloud testbed would still be good for evaluating cloud-based systems and algorithms, with a set of unified equipment for researchers to experiment on. It will be very nice if such a platform can be built across different institutes in Hong Kong. We have experienced difficulty to build such a platform during the course of this project, due mainly to lack of management and technical support from different institutes, as well as the lack of funding. We look forward to an initiative from the RGC on building such a cross-institutional cloud testbed in Hong Kong.

17204715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204715.value: This project designed mechanisms and algorithms for VM resource allocation and pricing in cloud platforms, to optimize profits obtained by the cloud provider or the social welfare. We designed auction-based mechanisms in various settings, including offline and online VM resource provisioning, scaling and pricing, online virtual cluster provisioning and pricing, and a number of other relevant scenarios. Our mechanisms and algorithms were proven to be truthful, individually rational, budget balanced and approximately efficient in social welfare or profit. No known efficient, market-driven pricing schemes were available for tailor-made VMs or resources at finer granularity (e.g., units of CPU cycles) in the real-world IaaS clouds. Our study is the first to systematically examine near-optimal online VM/VC packing solutions and pricing mechanisms.

17205015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205015.value: Query Suggestion for Geo-Textual Data The recent advances in telecommunications has brought to availability big amounts of spatial data that carry textual information. Geo-textual objects include points of interest on a map tagged with textual descriptions, GPS-tagged pictures in photo-sharing applications (such as Flickr) that have descriptive tags, and web documents that refer to locations. Mobile users can search for geo-textual data using keyword queries, with objects that are close to them ranked higher. For example, a mobile user searching for a "Chinese restaurant" is most probably interested in documents about restaurants near her current location. Location-based keyword search does not always return satisfactory results to a user. One reason is that there are not enough geo-spatial objects that contain the query keywords and are near the user's location. Another reason is that the user has difficulty to express her information needs precisely. A proposed solution is to suggest to the user a number of alternative keyword queries. However, the location of the user has not been considered by existing query suggestion methods, mainly because these approaches target web search users and location-independent objects (e.g., keyword queries from desktop computers for general web pages). We argue that especially for mobile users their locations should not be disregarded in query suggestion. Therefore, query suggestion should provide to a user keyword queries that (i) are semantically relevant to the user's original query (ii) produce results that are near the user's location. In this project, we will study in depth the problem of location-aware keyword query suggestion (LAKQS). Our first objective is to define and evaluate appropriate LAKQS models, which suggest to users alternative keyword queries that meet their search needs and also return nearby objects. A good LAKQS model will greatly enhance the experience of the mobile user who routinely uses her smartphone to search for services or information. Our second objective is to develop effective data indexing and preprocessing methods paired with efficient search algorithms, in order to achieve real-time LAKQS that scales well with the size of the searched data and the query logs. There is a growing interest by the research community and the industry in enhancing the search experience of users; at the same time, the number of searches from mobile devices is also growing. Therefore, we believe that LAKQS is an important and timely research subject, especially to Hong Kong which has a huge amount of geo-textual objects. 近年來，隨著電訊的快速發展，人們得以獲取大量帶有文本信息的空間數據。常見的空間-文本對象包括地圖上帶有文字描述的地點、照片分享應用（如Flickr）上帶有GPS信息和文字標籤的圖片，以及涉及位置信息的網頁等。手機用戶可以輸入關鍵詞來查詢空間-文本數據，並期望距離自己更近的對象排序更加靠前。例如，一個用移動設備查詢“中國餐館”的用戶很有可能對於距離她更近的中國餐館信息更加感興趣。 基於位置的關鍵詞查詢並不總能返回令用戶滿意的結果。其中一個原因是數據 庫中沒有足夠的既包含用戶搜索關鍵詞又離用戶較近的數據；另一個原因則是用戶並不總能準確地用關鍵詞來表達她所想要的信息。一種可行的解決方法是推薦給用 戶一些替代性的關鍵詞（即關鍵詞推薦）。但是，現有的關鍵詞推薦技術主要是為傳統的基於桌面電腦的網頁搜索而設計，因此其中並沒有考慮到用戶的位置信息。 我們認為，在當前的搜索和關鍵詞推薦中，尤其是在移動設備（如手機）上，用戶的位置信息不應該忽略。因此，搜索引擎所推薦的關鍵詞應該同時符合以下兩種需 求：（1）推薦詞需要與用戶的起始輸入語義相關；（2）推薦詞應當能搜索到離用戶更近的結果。 在這個項目中，我們將深入研究位置相關的關鍵詞推薦（LAKQS）技術。我們的第一個目標是定義並設計合適的LAKQS模 型，使之可以推薦給用戶既符合其信息需求，又能找到較近對象的替代性搜索關鍵詞。這樣一個模型可以極大地提高移動設備用戶搜索服務或信息時的體驗。我們的 第二個目標則是開發有效的數據處理、索引技術，以及高效的搜索算法，從而能夠實時處理位置相關的關鍵詞推薦，並且能夠適應大規模的搜索數據和搜索記錄。近 來，如何有效提高用戶的搜索體驗成為了科研界和工業界都十分關注的興趣點；於此同時，移動設備上提交的搜索次數也在快速增加。因此，我們相信位置相關的關 鍵詞推薦技術是一個重要並切時的的研究課題，而且因香港有大量空間-文本對象，該課題對香港而言尤為如此。

17205015.label: Realisation of objectives
17205015.value: The project is completed. We have published 4 journal papers and 7 conference papers. Moreover, besides on-going students, four PhD student have been trained and graduated. We have achieved the project objectives described in the proposal, as detailed below: 1) In the IEEE TKDE journal paper titled "Location Aware Keyword Query Suggestion Based on Document Proximity", we presented our first results on this project. We designed, implemented and tested a LAKQS technique, which is based on creating a document-keyword graph as described in the proposal. We tested the model on public datasets and found that the model has satisfactory accuracy. This result addresses to a high degree objectives 1 & 2. 2) In ACM TKDD journal paper titled “Entity-based query recommendation for long -tail queries”. We examine how to suggest queries for long-tail queries, which are queries that are rare but also occupy a large percentage of queries asked. This problem has not been handled very well by existing approaches, which often depend on the use of user logs. The main idea of our work is to use a knowledge graph (KG), containing nodes representing various entities (e.g., persons, places, items etc.), in order to produce an external source of recommendation. Our results show that the use of KG in query recommendation solutions can improve recommendation quality. This results addresses to a high degree objectives 1, 2, and 3. 3) In Geoinformatica journal paper titled “location-aware query reformulation for search engines”, we study how to reformulate a query, i.e., performing query recommendation and auto-completion, based on the physical locations of the query issuers. We extend the bookmark coloring algorithm for graph proximity search to support our proposed query recommendation approaches online. Experiments using a real query log shows that our proposed approaches significantly outperform previous work in terms of quality. The running times are also fast for recommendation purposes. This result addresses to a high degree objectives 1, 2, 3. 4) Conference publication “DSANLS: Accelerating Distributed Nonnegative Matrix Factorization via Sketching”, published in WSDM 2018, proposed an efficient parallel and distributed algorithm for non-negative matrix factorization, which can be used to perform scalable recommendation. It is highly related to Objective 3. 5) Conference publication "Location-Aware Query Recommendation for Search Engines at Scale" extends this work to incorporate an effective spatial proximity measure between a query issuer and a query with a location distribution obtained from its clicked URLs in the query history. Based on this, two popular query recommendation approaches based on query flow graphs are extended to our location-aware setting. Finally, we speed up the bookmark coloring algorithm for graph proximity search to support online location-aware query recommendation. We use a spatial partitioning based approximation that accelerates the computation of our proposed spatial proximity. We conduct experiments using a real query log, which show that our query recommendation approaches significantly outperform previous work in terms of quality, and they can be efficiently applied online. This result addresses to a high degree objectives 1, 2, and 3. In the remaining conference publications are by-products of this project which are related to graph search and recommender systems: 1) In publication "Reverse k-Ranks Queries on Large Graphs" we studied algorithms that find for a given node other nodes in the graph that rank it highly according to a graph distance measure. The results of this work can be used to improve the efficiency of query suggestion, since it can be used to accelerate proximity-based ranking between queries (Objective 3). 2) Publication "HBGG: a Hierarchical Bayesian Geographical Model for Group Recommendation" improves the quality of location-aware recommendation for groups of users. The results of this work can be used to improve location-aware query recommendation for groups of users (Objective 1). 3) Publication "P-LAG: Location- aware Group Recommendation for Passive Users" has a similar goal and it is also related to Objective 4) Publication "Efficient Fault-Tolerant Group Recommendation Using alpha-beta-core" targets the efficiency of group recommendation and it is directly related to Objective 3. 5) Publication "FEXIPRO: Fast and Exact Inner Product Retrieval in Recommender Systems" accelerates ranking of vectors based on inner product similarity. If queries are modeled as latent vectors based on their results and their spatial distributions, this technique can be used to accelerate query suggestion (Objective 3). 6) Publication “Recommending Packages with Validity Constraints to Groups of Users” examines the recommendation of a package (e.g., vacation packages) to a group of users (e.g., tourist groups). A special case of this problem, where recommended items are places and recommendation should consider the current locations of the users in the group, has been studied. It is thus related to Objectives 2 and 3.

17205015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205015.value: The recent advances in telecommunications has brought to availability big amounts of spatial data that carry textual information. Geo-textual objects include points of interest on a map tagged with textual descriptions, GPS-tagged pictures in photo-sharing applications (such as Flickr) that have descriptive tags, and web documents referring to locations. Mobile users can search for geo-textual data using keyword queries, with objects that are close to them ranked higher. We study location-aware keyword query suggestion (LAKQS). We have defined and evaluate appropriate LAKQS models, which suggest to users alternative keyword queries that meet their search needs and also return nearby objects. A good LAKQS model will greatly enhance the experience of the mobile user who routinely uses her smartphone to search for services or information. We also develop efficient search algorithms, to achieve real-time LAKQS that scales well with the size of the searched data and the query logs. There is a growing interest by the research community and the industry in enhancing the search experience of users; at the same time, the number of searches from mobile devices is also growing. Therefore, LAKQS is an important subject, especially to Hong Kong which has a huge amount of geo-textual objects.

17205115.label: Project Objectives
17205115.value: [To develop query solutions for uncertain graphs.] We will invent novel techniques enabling the execution of two common classes of queries on uncertain graphs. Specifically, the “Q-index”, a data structure derived from a given uncertain graph G and query q, produces a “query-dependent i-graph” G(q), such that the answer to q when executed on G(q) is the same as the result of running q on G. We will examine how the Q-index enables efficient and effective query evaluation. We will also explore approximate solutions for building the Q-index, as well as graph queries that return path information. [To study the graph event model.] We will investigate the handling of events that occur on one or more edges of an uncertain graph. For example, consider a train route that connects several nodes of an uncertain graph and has stopped because of a strike. The occurrence of this strike affects the travel times on one or more roads. More generally, the probability distributions among the edges are inter-related or correlated. We propose a graph event model to capture this information. Because this makes uncertain graphs more difficult to query, we will investigate efficient and effective solutions. We will also explore situations in which events are given at query time, and we will develop methods that can handle update, insertion, and removal of events efficiently.
