17205115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205115.value: Graph data, which are prevalent in important applications, are often large and uncertain. Consider a navigation system that manages traffic data (e.g., travel times) in a road network. These data can be extremely large; in Shanghai, the traffic information recorded on a single day is about 1TB in size. Also, because drivers move at different speeds, the travel time on each road segment may not be an exact number, but a probability distribution. As another example, to study social interactions among authors of Wikipedia entries, a graph can be constructed by analyzing the authors’ text inputs. In this graph, the nodes are the authors, and an edge between two nodes describes the corresponding authors’ relationship (e.g., they have the same political opinion). This graph can have millions of edges, whose existence is not definite. Applications such as the above call for a system that can manage uncertain graph data. However, the issues of managing and querying such data are not well understood. In this project, we will examine this topic extensively. We will consider two common kinds of uncertain graphs, which assign probability information to graph edges in different ways. For these models, we will study the evaluation of fundamental queries that return answers with probability guarantees. For example, a k-nearest neighbor query returns k nodes, along with their probabilities, such that the distances of these nodes from a user-specified node are the shortest. Owing to the sizes of real-world graphs and complexity of probabilistic information, query processing can be very costly. Therefore, we propose to develop a data structure called the Q-index. Moreover, we will study the graph event model, which enriches the semantics of uncertain graphs by capturing the interplay among the graph edges (e.g., the traffic on one road is affected by an accident on another road). We will perform extensive experimental evaluations to validate the efficiency and accuracy of our methods. We will prototype a system that supports the management and querying of uncertain graph data, and implement a road navigation system on top of it. This system, based on 1TB real traffic data from Shanghai, will provide navigation services to mobile users. Existing solutions for managing uncertain graph data are inadequate, and our work will advance the state-of-the-art. Moreover, navigation services are central to urban computing (e.g., smart driving and gas consumption control). Our solutions are therefore highly relevant to the Hong Kong SAR and China. 大規模不確定圖數據廣泛存在於新型應用中。例如，在上海市，單日的交通信息流量便逹到1TB。此外，由於交通狀況不斷變化，行駛某一路徑所需的時間 是不確定的。圖數據也可用來表示維基百科條目作者的關係 （例如，它們是否具有相同的政治觀點）。在這個包含上百萬邊的圖，一條邊的存在便帶有不確定性。 本項目以設計大規模不確定圖數據庫系統為目標，研究支持高效存儲與快速查詢的算法和數據結構，從而為用戶提供高質量的服務。針對一個重要的概率圖模型，研究一些基本查詢，如最短距離查詢，使其返回有概率和統計保證的結果。我們也擴展到包含邊相關關係的複雜i-圖，並通過大量實驗驗證這些方法的性能。本項目的研究成果預期會對概率數據庫管理和相關實際應用提供借鑒。

17205115.label: Realisation of objectives
17205115.value: 1) We study the problem of enabling the execution of probabilistic queries on uncertain graphs. We have developed the Q-index for source-target queries, which return distance information between given source s and target nodes t (e.g., finding the shortest distance between s and t). The Q-index is essentially a graph decomposition, called PTree, of a given probabilistic graph. Given a source s and target t, the solution will find from the PTree an “equivalent subgraph”, which compresses distance information among nodes. Our result shows that PTree significantly improves the performance of probabilistic graph queries. An approximation solution has been developed, which is highly accurate. The results have been published in ACM TODS 2017, a top database journal. 2) We extend PTree to support source-only queries (e.g., retrieving the k closest nodes of a given node s). We study different types of distance functions (e.g., reliability) for measuring the closeness of nodes in a probabilistic graph. We investigate efficient algorithms for evaluation of queries that return probabilities (e.g., there is a 60% chance that node x is the closest to node y). Extensive experiments were published about this work, and we have published the work in EDBT 2018, a top database conference. We have extended the paper which considers more advanced techniques, and recently submitted it to VLDB Journal for consideration. 3) To support large graph analytics and mining (e.g., graph clustering and classification) on uncertain graphs, we have developed an embedding solution. Essentially, in an embedding, each graph node was converted to a d-dimensional vector for a given value of d. Our solution considers common types of similarity measures between node pairs on uncertain graphs (e.g., Jacquard and cosine similarity). Existing vector-based analytics solutions can then be applied to the embedding. Our results show that our embedding solution is better than both existing uncertain graph mining algorithms and embedding solutions that are designed for general graphs. The results were published in CIKM 2017, which has an acceptance rate of 21% (171/820). 4) We have studied how the uncertain graph model can be used to maximize social influence. In particular, we study influence graphs, where each node (a social network user) has a probability of influencing another node to do something (e.g., purchase). An edge with a direction and probability between two users indicates the influence. In the paper published in DASFAA 2018, we examine how to consider the decay of influence with time should be considered in finding the “seed nodes” (i.e., nodes that advertisement should be first targeted). With detailed experiments, we show that the influence can be maximized with consideration of our proposed time-decaying influence model (called awareness threshold model in our paper). 5) We studying the problem of evaluating complex probabilistic queries with different conditions on uncertain graphs. An important problem is the study of motif counting on uncertain graphs. A motif, essentially a small graph of around 3 to 7 nodes, is a fundamental building block of a graph, and it can be considered as a more expressive and semantic building block than an edge. A fundamental issue about motif-based graph analysis is the collection of statistics through counting the number of motif instances in a graph. Because the counting problem, which involves searching a subgraph from an uncertain graph, is computationally challenging, we have developed an advanced solution, which encodes the uncertain information into bits for efficient counting. Our solution, which returns the probability distribution of counts of motif instances efficiently, can be useful in deriving statistics of counts such as mean and variance). It is also more effective than existing motif counting approaches on uncertain graphs. The paper has been recently submitted to VLDB, and we have received a “revision” notification. We are currently revising the paper based on the reviewers’ requests. 6) We have studied the issues of evaluating other kinds of complex queries with different constraints on graphs, including trajectory joins on road networks (TKDE 2016), handling k-NN query workload in road networks (VLDB 2018, ICDE 2019), community search on social networks (VLDB 2016, VLDB 2017), and motif-clique discovery on heterogeneous information networks (ICDE 2019). We have studied the evaluation of SimRank on a large graph in a parallel cloud environment (VLDB 2016). Please refer to Part C for more details.

17205215.label: Project Objectives
17205215.value: To design a high-performance BLISS prototype for a time-stretch imaging system The proposed continuously-sweeping BLISS leverages MHz-repetition rate to achieve ultrafast frame rate or scan rate, and use a fiber-based optical parametric amplifier (OPA) that enhances sweeping bandwidth and sensitivity. In this stage of the project, we will design a BLISS prototype in the 1.55-µm wavelength window for a time-stretch optical imaging system, together with the fiber OPA, for implementation and optimization in the later stages of the research. To implement a BLISS prototype for a SPAT system A discretely-sweeping BLISS prototype in the 1.0-µm wavelength window for a SPAT system will be implemented and its performance thoroughly characterized in a number of respects, including wavelength-sweeping range, pulse energy and pulse width, repetition rate, and synchronization. This stage of the research provides a well-characterized 1.0-µm BLISS prototype for SPAT application and a development platform for the last phase of the research. To explore application of the synchronized 1.0-µm and 1.55-µm BLISS in a hyperspectral SRS system Leveraging the previous two phases, we will explore application of the synchronized 1.0-µm and 1.55-µm BLISS in a hyperspectral SRS system. In particular, one BLISS oscillating at 1.55 µm (or 1.0 µm) will be externally driven by another stable source (another BLISS) oscillating at 1.0 µm (or 1.55 µm), which can be used as the Stokes and pump wavelengths, respectively in a hyperspectral SRS imaging system. Thorough study of this aspect of BLISS performance will lay the foundation for its use in capturing hyperspectral SRS images towards the end of the research.

17205215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205215.value: Growing demand for healthcare solutions has necessitated substantial advancements in optical bio-imaging technologies over the past decade. Availability of high-speed photonics technologies in telecommunications has invigorated the biomedical imaging arena through various optical imaging modalities. Time-stretch microscopy, photoacoustic tomography (PAT), and non-linear optical spectroscopy (e.g. stimulated Raman scattering (SRS)), to name a few, have proven to be promising in their respective applications. Microscopy, tomography, and spectroscopy (MTS), apparently orthogonal arenas, can together strategically formulate an unprecedented data set for exploiting next-generation optical imaging applications. However, a versatile laser source providing MTS information with agile-wavelength tunability and high-speed, high-sensitivity capabilities for practical applications is yet to be achieved. The proposed breathing laser as inertia-free swept source (BLISS) offers a versatile platform for various promising imaging modalities. In a three-phase approach, we will demonstrate BLISS as a core technology to meet some of the critical challenges of next-generation optical imaging systems. First, we plan to demonstrate a scheme leveraging the positive- and negative-dispersive fibers inside a highly compact all-fiber ring cavity with the all-optical (inertia-free) wavelength-swept (continuous) mechanism in a 1.55-µm wavelength window. Sweeping wavelength and sensitivity are expected to be further enhanced through use of a fiber-based optical parametric amplifier (OPA) together with BLISS in time-stretch microscopy. Second, we propose to deploy BLISS in the regime of discrete sweeping. BLISS can provide a swept source for spectroscopic PAT (SPAT) with wide wavelength sweep range and fast tuning speed (i.e. high-speed imaging capabilities) around a 1.0-µm window, surpassing the conventional SPAT system in which speed is limited by mechanical tuning of the bulky optical parametric oscillator (OPO). As a result, BLISS realizes a robust and agile swept source for the SPAT system. Third, we will explore the possibility of external synchronization of one BLISS with another at different wavelength and its application in the hyperspectral SRS system. The proposed project thus constitutes advancement in multi-modal optical imaging technology in the context of agile, robust fiber-based wavelength-swept sources, and thereby in high-speed imaging capabilities over versatile wavelength windows with improvement in sensitivity through optical amplification. The wide spectrum of knowledge generated in the project will thus contribute to both the research community and industry. 近十年來，對醫療保健解決方案的需求推動了相關光學生物成像技術的顯著進步。高速光電通信技術的實用化促進了生物醫學各個光學成像模式的發展。新興醫學成像技術，包括時間拉伸顯微鏡，光聲斷層掃描（PAT）和非線性光學光譜分析（例如受激拉曼散射（SRS）），在各自的領域獲得了同行的青睞，並被證明是有前途的成像模式。顯微技術，斷層掃描技術和光譜學顯然是正交的成像方式（簡稱為MTS）。它們可以被策略性地溶合在一起，為下一代醫學成像提供制空前的分析數據流和解決方案。但是，實現這一目標的前提是研發一種能夠為MTS提供靈活而高速的波長掃描，并且能夠在實用環境中提供高靈敏度的多樣化激光光源。 本項目擬研究的無慣性伸縮脈衝掃頻光源（BLISS）將為MTS中各個顯像模式提供優良的工作平台。在項目的三個研究階段中，我們將展示BLISS作為一種核心技術如何解決下一代光學成像系統所面對的關鍵挑戰。首先，我們將在1.55微米窗口展示採用正負色散光纖杠桿原理的解決方案，它是一種高度緊湊的全光環形結構的連續波長掃描光源。它的波長掃描範圍和靈敏度將通過光纖光參量放大器進一步提高，並在時間拉伸顯微鏡中進行表徵。然後，我們將研發離散波長掃描模式的BLISS。它將為1.0微米窗口的頻譜分析光聲斷層掃描（SPAT）提供寬波長掃描範圍和快調諧速度（即高速成像能力）。這將使基於大體積固體光學參量振盪器的傳統SPAT系統帶來速度的極大提升。所以，BLISS將為SPAT系統提供健壯而敏捷的掃頻光源。最後，我們將研究多個（不同波長窗口）BLISS之間的外部同步可行性，並將其應用到超光譜非線性受激拉曼散射系統中。 擬研究的課題將推動多模式光學成像技術的發展，這些包括敏捷而健壯的光纖技術波長掃頻，多波長窗口高速成像和基於光纖光學參量的靈敏度提高技術。因此，本項目中所獲得的豐富知識將會對研究領域以及工業界作出突出的貢獻。

17205215.label: Realisation of objectives
17205215.value: 1. To design a high-performance BLISS prototype for a time-stretch imaging system We demonstrated a continuously-sweeping BLISS leverages MHz-repetition rate to achieve ultrafast frame rate, and used a fiber-based optical parametric amplifier (OPA) that enhanced sweeping bandwidth and sensitivity in the 1.55-μm wavelength window. 2. To implement a BLISS prototype for a SPAT system We have investigated the possibility of leveraging a BLISS for spectroscopic PAT (SPAT). Specifically we have extended that beyond 1.55-μm wavelength window to realize micro-joule laser pulses with a shot-to- shot intensity variation of 1.6% and a pulse duration of 150 ns were obtained for spectroscopic PA detection. 3. To explore application of the synchronized 1.0-µm and 1.55-µm BLISS in a hyperspectral SRS system We developed a two-color self-synchronized fiber laser source for SRS applications. It consists of a directly generated laser covering 1000-1060 nm wavelength based on ytterbium-doped fiber, and a synchronized laser covering 770-785 nm wavelength which is frequency-doubled from an erbium-doped fiber laser. In combination, the wavelengths of these two lasers are ideal as Stokes and pump pairs in CRS imaging, which can cover a broad range of Raman resonances in the high wavenumber region from 2700 to 3550 cm-1, which includes the CH2 stretching resonance at 2845 cm-1 predominantly associated with lipids as well as the resonance of cellular proteins at 2920 cm-1.

17205215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205215.value: In this project, we proposed and demonstrated a breathing laser as inertia-free swept source (BLISS) that offers a versatile platform for various promising imaging modalities. First, we demonstrated a scheme leveraging the positive- and negative-dispersive fibers inside a highly compact all-fiber ring cavity with the all-optical (inertia-free) wavelength-swept (continuous) mechanism in a 1.55-µm wavelength window. Sweeping wavelength and sensitivity were further enhanced through use of a fiber-based optical parametric amplifier (OPA) together with BLISS in time-stretch microscopy. Second, we demonstrated a spectroscopic PAT (SPAT) with wide wavelength sweep range and fast tuning speed (i.e. high-speed imaging capabilities) beyond 1.55-µm wavelength window, surpassing the conventional SPAT system in which speed is limited by mechanical tuning of the bulky optical parametric oscillator (OPO). Third, we explored the possibility of deploying a two-color self-synchronized fiber laser source for SRS applications. With these efforts, this project thus constitutes advancement in multi-modal optical imaging technology in the context of agile, robust fiber-based wavelength-swept sources, and thereby in high-speed imaging capabilities over versatile wavelength windows with improvement in sensitivity through optical amplification. The wide spectrum of knowledge generated in the project will thus contribute to both the research community and industry.

17205715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205715.value: Removing and recovering phosphorus (P) from wastewater are receiving a lot of attentions in these years. Enhanced biological phosphorus removal (EBPR) process, has been widely applied in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) to remove P from wastewater by enriching polyphosphate-accumulating organisms (PAOs), and benefits the possible further recovery of P from the discharged sludge containing high P contents. The roles of different PAOs populations are always interesting scientific questions and useful engineering knowledge in the wastewater treatment field. In the past two decades, molecular techniques have significantly advanced our understanding of PAOs, but mainly in the laboratory reactors. With the fast development of next generation sequencing and the relevant bioinformatics tools, researchers have good expectations on the new insights of PAOs revealed using the combined “omics” approaches. Some preliminary studies conducted by other researchers and PI in the past few years showed promising progresses on this aspect and also offered many clues for further genomics studies of PAOs in EBPR process. For this project, a three-year experimental program is proposed to achieve the following objectives: 1) to study the profiles of different Accumulibacter clades in laboratory reactors fed with different substrates and operated under different conditions; 2) to extract the draft genomes of different Accumulibacter clades based on metagenomic data sets of activated sludge collected from these reactors; 3) to uncover the conserved and unique metabolic characteristics of the Accumulibacter clades by conducting comparative genomic analysis; 4) to examine the gene expression profiles of these clades in the two phases of EBPR process when fed with different substrates and operated under different conditions; 5) to explore the novel PAOs in these reactors and a few local full-scale WWTPs by high-flow capacity flowcytometer sorting and metagenomic sequencing after specific staining of polyphosphate granules in PAOs cells; 6) to investigate the correlations between PAOs and other bacteria populations in activated sludge using network analysis based on high-resolution taxonomy profile obtained by high-throughput sequencing of 16S rRNA genes. 以強化生物除磷（EBPR）除去和回收廢水中的磷（P）的工藝已被廣泛應用於污水處理廠， 不同的聚磷微生物群體的相互作用始終是備受關注的科學問題。在過去的二十年中，分子生物學技術已經顯著提高了我們對聚磷微生物的認識。隨著新一代測序和生物信息學相關工具的快速發展，研究人員對聚磷菌的研究更多地採用組合“組學”的方法。在本項目這個為期三年的實驗計劃中， 主要針對以下目標：1）研究在不同條件下Accumulibacter分支的分佈; 2）獲取不同分支Accumulibacter的基因組草圖; 3）通過開展比較基因組分析揭示Accumulibacter的代謝特點; 4）檢查這些分支在EBPR兩個階段的基因表達圖譜。

17205715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205715.value: In this project, we designed novel quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) primers for the polyphosphate kinase 1 (ppk1) gene, targeting eight individual “Candidatus Accumulibacter” (referred to as Accumulibacter) clades in the Enhanced Biological Phosphorus Removal (EBPR) reactors. With the primers designed by other research groups, a highly selective and sensitive qPCR-based method was developed to quantify all Accumulibacter clades. The applicability to environmental samples was demonstrated by profiling the Accumulibacter clades in activated sludge samples of nine full-scale wastewater treatment plants (Please refer to Research Output No. 1). Using the two dimensional binning approach based on metagenomic sequencing of different EBPR microbial communities under different conditions, we recovered a draft genome of Accumulibacter Clade IIC from a laboratory reactor under the shift of the microbial populations due to pH change in the operation period, supplementing the current collection of genomes of this not-yet-cultivated microorganism. Comparative genomic analysis demonstrated that Accumulibacter clades had different abilities in nitrogen metabolism and carbon fixation, which shed light on enriching different Accumulibacter populations selectively (Please refer to Research Output No. 3). Following that, we further did a comprehensive pan-genome analysis of all available Accumulibacter and developed a method to infer the hidden traits for the enrichment of not-yet-cultured populations using Candidatus Accumulibacter as the model. Our method constructed a whole picture of the carbon, electron, and energy flows in the not-yet-cultured populations from the genomic datasets and the coordination across three flows was decoded from the transcriptional datasets. Based on it, our method diagnosed the status of the not-yet-cultured populations and provided the strategy to optimize the enrichment systems, and shed light to the exploration into Accumulibacter and other bacterial dark matter in the environments (Please refer to Research Output No. 6). Additionally, based on the metagenomic datasets, we explored the bacterial phage which are related to different bacterial populations (including Accumulibacter and other PAOs), and these bacterial phages could be used as a control strategy to shape microbial community of activated sludge of EBPR (Please refer to Research Output No. 5). In this project, we also applied metagenomic approach to conduct some additional studies related to the microbial populations of activated sludge (Please refer to Research Outputs No. 2 and 4).

17205715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205715.value: In this project, we designed novel quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) primers for the polyphosphate kinase 1 (ppk1) gene. Further validation of these primers and design of new primers of the ppk1 gene are needed. Using the two dimensional binning approach based on metagenomic sequencing of different EBPR microbial communities under different conditions, we recovered a draft genome of Accumulibacter Clade IIC from a laboratory reactor. Further studies on new genome of other lineage of “Candidatus Accumulibacter” in different EBPR reactors are needed in order to have complete understanding of the genomic diversity of these phosphate-accumulating bacteria. We did a comprehensive pan-genome analysis of all available Accumulibacter and developed a method to infer the hidden traits for the enrichment of not-yet-cultured populations using Candidatus Accumulibacter as the model. However, no experimental validation has yet been conducted to test this method. Further tests are needed to validate the model and the method. Based on the metagenomic datasets, we explored the bacterial phage which are related to different bacterial populations. Further researches should be conducted to isolate the specific bacteria phages of Accumulibacter and apply these phages in phages therapy of the EBPR reactors by shaping the microbial communities in the reactors.

17205715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205715.value: Phosphorus in sewage is one of the main reasons for eutrophication of water bodies. Generally, enhanced biological treatment processes are applied to remove phosphorus in sewage plants to control pollution. However, the knowledge of polyphosphate-accumulating organisms (PAOs) that play a major role in the phosphorus removal process is still very limited. In this project, we designed a new detection method for different groups of polyphosphate-accumulating organisms, and investigated the distribution of polyphosphate-accumulating organisms in the sewage treatment plants all over the world, providing basic data for understanding the ecological niches of different groups of polyphosphate-accumulating organisms. In addition, we used metagenomic sequencing technology to assemble a draft genome of polyphosphate-accumulating organisms in an enhanced biological phosphorus removal reactor, which supplemented its genome resources. We also performed a whole-genome analysis on all the genomes of polyphosphate-accumulating organisms, and used it as a model to develop methods to infer the hidden characteristics of difficult-to-cultivate bacteria to enrich and cultivate these bacteria, including PAOs.

17205815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205815.value: Dynamic systems that exhibit switching behavior are ubiquitous in real-world settings. The switching may originate from changes in the intrinsic structures of the systems or from the responses to external stimuli. Models that describe such switching characteristics can be found, for example, in the packet delivery of networked servo control, gain-scheduling of time-varying and parameter-varying plants, production processes involving failure and recovery, interactions of gene networks, probabilistic changes in age-structured populations, HVAC control of mixed-mode buildings, or control of wheeled robots. Although these switched systems have attracted considerable attention in recent years, commonly used control techniques for them with uncontrolled switching are often conservative, while research on controlled switching remains limited. Hybrid control refers to using a family of continuous control laws together with discrete logic-based or event-based switching among them to achieve desirable stability and performance objectives. This control architecture has the potential to provide improved closed-loop stability, beyond what can be achieved by using either classical linear or smooth nonlinear controllers, and gives additional performance benefits. However, no comprehensive theory or systematic approach on the design of hybrid control systems currently exists, and most hybrid control applications are based on an empirical approach. In this project, hybrid control design and related robustness will be investigated for switched systems. The nature of the switching signals governing the switched systems may have deterministic or stochastic descriptions. Theoretical design conditions for the existence of desirable hybrid stabilizing controllers with guaranteed performance will be established for both continuous control and discrete mode switching. To this end, novel techniques based on extended observation, input-state/output partition, for instance, will be developed to cater for off-line and on-line syntheses. As a fundamental issue for engineering systems, the robustness of the closed-loop systems with hybrid controllers against uncertainties in both continuous state evolution and discrete mode switching will be analyzed. Situations with an uncertain dwell time, an imprecise switching boundary, uncertain or partially known probability descriptions, and asynchronous switching will be considered. Focusing on the applicability of the design methods, extension to structurally constrained hybrid control will be pursued as a step towards ensuring greater reliability and cost reduction in real engineering applications. The expected performance improvements due to hybrid control design will not only reduce undesirable conservatism in current system synthesis approaches, but will also considerably narrow the gap between engineering practice and design theory, and offer more effective control systems with higher robustness and reliability. 在現實世界中，表現出切換行為的動態系統無處不在。切換可能來自系統內在結構的變化或者對外部激勵的回應。描述這種切換特徵的模型在許多控制系統中普遍存在，如網路化伺服控制的資料包傳輸、時變與變參數系統的增益調度、涉及故障與恢復的生產過程、基因網路的相互作用、不同年齡結構種群的概率變化、混合式建築的暖通空調控制、輪式機器人的控制。儘管近年來這些切換系統受到廣泛關注，但通常對其使用的控制方法中切換不受控，從而控制策略保守性高。目前對於受控的切換控制策略的研究還很有限。混雜控制是指使用連續控制規則及其之間離散的基於邏輯和事件的切換，以達到理想的穩定性和系統性能目標。這種控制架構與傳統線性或者光滑非線性控制器相比，有望提高閉環系統穩定性，以及提供額外的性能優勢。然而，混雜控制系統的設計至今尚未建立綜合的理論或系統的方法。大多數混雜系統的應用都基於經驗方法。 本專案主要致力於切換系統的混雜控制設計和相關的魯棒性分析。切換系統的切換信號可能具有確定性或者隨機的描述。對於連續控制與離散模態切換，我們將建立滿足給定性能指標的混雜鎮定控制器存在的理論設計條件。為此，我們將建立基於擴展觀測、輸入到狀態/輸出的分割等的新技術，以達到離線或者線上綜合的要求。 作為工程系統的一個基本問題，我們將分析帶有混雜控制器的閉環系統對連續狀態演化及離散模態切換中不確定性的魯棒性。對於具有不確定駐留時間的情況，可以考慮不精確的切換邊界、不確定或者部分已知概率的描述以及非同步切換。為提高設計方法的適用性，我們欲將其拓展到帶有結構限制的混雜控制，以確保更高的可靠性和降低工程應用的成本。混雜控制設計帶來的預期性能提高將大大降低現有系統綜合方法的保守性，並且將大大縮小工程實踐和設計理論之間的差距，並提供具有更高魯棒性和可靠性的高效控制系統。

17205815.label: Realisation of objectives
17205815.value: All the objectives have been achieved. The details are listed below. The project has established theoretical design conditions for the existence of desirable hybrid stabilizing controllers with guaranteed performance. For continuous control, state-feedback and observer-based output-feedback have been considered. For discrete mode switching, both the deterministic and stochastic cases have been considered. The switching of the controller with the deterministic scheme can be either time-dependent or state-dependent. The case with periodic switched has been considered extensively in which a general class of continuous-time periodic piecewise linear systems have been addressed. In this connection, the finite-time stability, stabilisation, L2-gain and H-infinity control problems have been considered. The characterizations of stability and performance have been carried out using a piecewise time-varying Lyapunov-like function so that sufficient conditions for stability and performance level can be obtained with their corresponding time-varying controllers constructed using the linear matrix inequality approach. Under actuator saturation, H-infinity state-feedback active vibration controllers are proposed in matrix inequality form. To reduce the conservatism, new conditions of stability and stabilization have been proposed using continuous Lyapunov function with a time-dependent homogeneous Lyapunov matrix polynomial. The exponential stability problem has been studied first using square matricial representation and sum of squares form of homogeneous matrix polynomial. Constraints on the exponential order of each subsystem used in previous work have been relaxed. State-feedback controllers with time-varying polynomial controller gain have been. A further improvement has been obtained for the stability, stabilization, and L2-gain problems for periodic piecewise systems with time-varying subsystems. Continuous Lyapunov function with time-varying Lyapunov matrix has adopted. A condition guaranteeing the negative definiteness of a matrix polynomial, deriving from the Lyapunov derivative, has been first obtained. Moreover, a state feedback controller with time-varying gain has been developed for stabilization. The L2-gain criterion for eriodic piecewise time-varying system has also been studied. Along this direction, the design problem of periodic piecewise guaranteed cost controllers for uncertain periodic piecewise linear systems using a time-weighted quadratic cost function. By developing Lyapunov functions with quadratic cost matrices to a time-varying form, sufficient conditions are proposed to ensure the exponential stability of the closed-loop system and a guaranteed upper bound of the cost function. To minimize the upper bound in the controller design process, an iterative algorithm is developed to solve the problem via convex optimization. For periodic piecewise continuous-time linear systems with time delay, H-infinity control problem based on exponential stability and weighted L2-gain analyses have been investigated. A periodic piecewise Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional has been developed by integrating a discontinuous time-varying matrix function with two global terms. By applying the improved constraints to the stability and L2-gain analyses, sufficient delay-dependent exponential stability and weighted L2-gain criteria are proposed for the periodic piecewise time-delay system. Based on these analyses, an H-infinity control scheme has been designed under the consideration of periodic state feedback control input and iterative optimisation. On the other hand, the guaranteed cost control problem has been studied with sufficient delay-dependent conditions of closed-loop asymptotic stability presented based on an improved formulation, which involves a novel Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional with relaxed requirement in positive definiteness of the decision symmetric matrix variables. The corresponding optimization problems aiming at the mixed performance involving an upper bound of H2 guaranteed cost and an H-infinity performance index for disturbance attenuation have been established. The problems of stability analysis and L1-gain characterization for continuous-time switched systems consisting of positive subsystems. With the aid of a discretized copositive Lyapunov function, a sufficient condition ensuring the asymptotic stability of continuous-time switched positive systems under dwell-time constraint is obtained. Furthermore, the conservatism of the proposed approach has studied and the result with least conservatism in the framework of discretized copositive Lyapunov function has been obtained. The result has then been extended to L1-gain characterization for switched positive systems. With a prescribed dwell time, an unweighted L1-gain can be computed via solving a linear programming problem. Apart from dealing with control problems, the peak-to-peak filtering problem has also been tackled. Attention has been focused on designing of robust peak-to-peak filters that guarantee the robust asymptotic stability of periodic piecewise filtering error system and satisfy a prescribed peak-to-peak disturbance attenuation level for all admissible uncertainties in a polytope. A sufficient condition has been proposed for robust stability and peak-to-peak performance by employing the constructed time-varying Lyapunov function. Two design approaches based on the Lyapunov function with parameter-dependent matrices and parameter-independent matrices have been utilised to solve this problem. In the discrete-time case, the stabilization and L1-gain of linear periodic piecewise positive systems has been considered. The monotonicity of linear periodic piecewise positive systems has been studied and a time-varying co-positive Lyapunov function for periodic piecewise positive systems has been. a state-feedback periodic piecewise controller to stabilize the system is formed and an upper bound of L1-gain of the system has been given. In the discrete-time setting, the exponential stabilization problem of Markovian jump systems via a hybrid control strategy, in which the transition probability matrix and static output-feedback controller have been designed simultaneously. A necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of an exponential stabilizing transition probability matrix has been derived by means of a mode-dependent parametric approach. Furthermore, a sufficient condition has been established for the hybrid design with a specified lower bound on the decay rate. The proposed design approaches can be applied to solve two kinds of control design problems with practical constraints imposed on the hybrid design. Besides, an estimation approach has been proposed on the decay rate and decay coefficient of the jump systems. Also, two optimization problems have been formulated to obtain the hybrid control strategy. The approach has been illustrated numerically based on a network-on-chip (NoC) application to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed results. A stochastic scheme composes of a Markovian transition after a fixed dwell time has been studied. A new stability criterion, which is equivalent to an earlier necessary and sufficient condition, has been established first, and then reformulated in terms of linear matrix inequalities. Based on the stability analysis result, L2-gain performance analysis and H-infinity control problems have been studied. The stability and stabilization issues for a family of discrete-time stochastic switching systems with bounded sojourn time have also been addressed. The stochastic switching systems are modeled by semi-Markov jump linear systems and the semi-Markov kernel approach has been employed to handle the stability and stabilization problems. The sojourn time of each system mode is considered to have both upper and lower bounds. The concept of sigma-error mean square stability has been put forward in a new form by taking into account the lower bounds of sojourn time for all system modes. Numerically testable stability and stabilization criteria in the sense of the proposed sigma-error mean square stability have been obtained for the closed-loop stochastic switching system. The project has also provided the stability and ℓ1-gain for discrete-time positive 2-D Markov jump systems. The mathematical model of 2-D Markov jump systems has been established based on the Roesser model. Necessary and sufficient condition for stability and sufficient condition for ℓ1-gain computation have been derived. Furthermore, the stability and ℓ1-gain conditions have been extended to Markov jump systems with partially known transition probabilities.

17205815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205815.value: For the stability and stabilization problems of switched systems, a number of switching scenarios have been considered, namely, periodic switching, arbitrary switching, and stochastic switching. Hybrid and uncertain switching cases have also been tackled. The H∞ performance and controller designed have been considered with periodic parameter variations modeled as piecewise linear time functions in the system matrices. The performance-based stabilization problem involving actuator saturation has been solved in [1]. The approach has been extended to finite-time stability in [2] with new technical lemmas/techniques to reduce the conservatism. The basic idea has been employed to the peak-to-peak filtering of linear polytopic systems [8]. A significant extension from the piecewise linear case to polynomial case has been carried out [9, 14]. For the case with a mixed fixed dwell time followed by a Markov jump process, a new stability criterion which is equivalent to an earlier necessary and sufficient condition has been established [4]. Then a more general stochastic switching framework with bounded sojourn time has been considered. The stochastic switching systems are modeled by semi-Markov jump linear systems and the semi-Markov kernel approach is employed to handle the stability and stabilization problems [7]. For discrete-time Markov jump linear systems under output feedback such that the transition probabilities as part of the design parameters, a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of an exponential stabilizing transition probability matrix has been derived [6]. When time delays are presence, a periodic piecewise Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional is developed by integrating a discontinuous time-varying matrix function with two global terms. The stability and L2-gain analyses, sufficient delay-dependent exponential stability and weighted L2-gain criteria have been proposed [5]. The guarantee cost control problem with exponential stability is then tackled based on an improved formulation aiming at minimizing a mixed performance involving an upper bound of H2 guaranteed cost and an H∞ performance index [10]. A time-weighted version has been treated in [11]. Special consideration to the important class of positive systems has been made. Arbitrarily switched positive systems with dwell time constraints are examined in [3]. Their stability analysis and the unweighted L1-gain characterization can be checked based using linear programs. The case with periodic piecewise characteristic is considered and a state-feedback periodic piecewise controller to stabilize the system with a guaranteed L1-gain has been provided [12]. Moreover, the extension to discrete-time in a 2D setting has been dealt with in the 2D setting [13].

17205815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205815.value: Amongst the many potential applications and extensions of the results developed in the project, there are three possible areas for further development of results: (a) The periodically switched systems with polynomial-type system matrices can be considered as agents in some multi-agent systems. This will enrich the dynamic behavior of the multi-agent system. Moreover, such periodic switching can also be considered in the communication topology. (b) In the development of time-varying matrices in periodic switched systems, polynomials have used in each subsystem. Another more general formulation that can be considered is to use a Fourier-type description. New bounding tools will be required for establishing entirely novel results for both next continuous- and discrete- periodic systems. (c) The problems of reachable set estimation and synthesis for periodic positive systems with different exogenous disturbances may be considered. The lifting method and the pseudo-periodic Lyapunov function method can be adopted for the estimation problem. Optimization methods can be used to minimize the bounding hyper-pyramids of the reachable set. The state-feedback controller design conditions may then be designed for making the reachable set of closed-loop systems lie within a given hyper-pyramid.

17205815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205815.value: Dynamic systems that exhibit switching behavior are ubiquitous in real-world settings. The switching may originate from changes in the intrinsic structures of the systems or from the responses to external stimuli. Models that describe such switching characteristics can be found, for example, in gain-scheduling of time-varying and parameter-varying plants, and production processes involving failure and recovery. In this project, hybrid control design and related robustness have been investigated for switched systems. The switching signals governing the switched systems may have periodic, arbitrary with dwell time constraints, or Markov chain descriptions. Theoretical design conditions for the existence of stabilizing controllers with guaranteed performance have been established for both continuous control and discrete mode switching. New formulations and improved bounding techniques for technical developments have been employed to arrive at results of reduced conservatism. The case with and with time delays have been treated. A variety of stability analysis and synthesis problems have been covered, including guaranteed cost control with H2 and H-infinity performance indices, L2-gain analyses, and designing of transition probabilities, and filtering with polytopic uncertainty. Moreover, the results have been extended for positive systems. The techniques and results developed will narrow the gap between engineering practice and control design theory.

17205915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205915.value: Mitigation for slope protection from rainfall is usually costly, intrusive and based in heavy engineering solutions. More sustainable alternatives that require fewer raw materials are urged. The primary goal of this 3-year project is to develop a new approach for slope protection based on reducing the affinity of soils for water. Soil water repellency occurs in nature, after wildfires and in some forest soils, and is known to generate a sealing effect that reduces water infiltration. Our pilot studies in model granular materials with water repellent treatment show that the method is effective in reducing infiltration and relatively low cost. However, evidence from soils after wildfires show that if there is complete sealing, surface runoff and sediment discharge is likely. The specific goal of this project is to determine the conditions under which infiltration is reduced in water repellent materials without significantly enhancing erosion. Carefully constructed experiments will test the response of induced water-repellent soils under different scenarios. The influence of the soil properties and soil treatment in relation to the environmental conditions and vegetation and, crucially, the lifespan of the water-repellent condition will be investigated. Extreme rainfall events urge solutions for remediating infrastructure slopes, in particular for Hong Kong’s fill slopes prone to static liquefaction. Long term stable, water-repellent soils are a contribution in that direction. 针对降雨而采取的传统边坡防护措施通常具有造价高昂、扰动过大、工程量多等不足，因而工程界对一种可持续的、原料需求小的替代方法有很大需求。本项目为期3年，其主要目标是通过降低土颗粒对水的亲和性，提出一个边坡防护的新方法。在自然界中，斥水性土通常存在于部分森林土中及经历过野火的地区，通过产生密封效果来阻止水的渗入。试验研究证实了此方法可以通过对颗粒材料进行斥水性处理来有效减少水的渗入，并具有成本低廉的特点。然而，有关野火导致的斥水性土的研究表明：完全的密封效果在阻止水流渗入的同时会形成表面径流并进一步导致边坡表面的侵蚀。因此本项目具体的目标是探究在何种情况下斥水性材料能有效阻止水流的渗入，同时不会显著地增加表面侵蚀。试验将会测试人工斥水性土在不同方案下的反应，土的性质及其处理对周围环境和植被的影响，以及人工斥水性土的使用寿命。尤其在香港地区，存在着大量容易发生静态液化的填土边坡，而经常发生的特大暴雨也对极端情况下边坡的防护提出了要求，因此具有长期稳定性的斥水性土能够为这个问题的解决提供新的思路。

17205915.label: Realisation of objectives
17205915.value: All three objectives have been achieved as detailed next. ENGINEERING WATER REPELLENCY The project initiated by seeking the most effective compounds to hydrophobise soils. Dimethyldichlorosilane was used as a hydrophobising agent for the treatment of soils. We examined the effect of dimethyldichlorosilane concentration on the soil type and time-dependent effects by means of contact angles measurements using the sessile drop method. The results revealed that the presence of organic matter, residual water and other non-mineral matter hinders the effectiveness of the treatment. Treated clean soil particle surfaces from crushed rocks achieve an immediate and high degree of water repellency. OUTPUT 1 Another two silane compounds were tested on medium-sized sand: octadecyltrichlorosilane and trimethylchlorosilane which were compared to dichlorodimethylsilane. From the findings, it was concluded that the combination of OTS treatment in air-dried clean sand provides the highest and most stable water-repellent behaviour, paving the way for future research in cover applications where water tightness is of paramount importance. OUTPUT 2 Objective (1) was delivered through outputs 1 and 2 HYDROLOGIC OPTIMUM Delivering objectives (2) and (3) implied conducting physical model tests with the measurement of water content. Within this context, the performance of soil moisture sensors in synthetic water-repellent soils needed to be evaluated. Two soil moisture sensors (ECH2O EC-5 and ThetaProbe ML2x) were tested in three dimethyldichlorosilane -treated granular materials (Fujian sand, crushed silica and completely decomposed granite), by obtaining the soil-specific calibration equations using a two-step calibration approach. Differences in the calibration equations were documented and linked to the changes in the pore-water chemistry. OUTPUT 6 In the built environment, soil water repellency offers the opportunity to develop granular materials with controllable wettability for slope stabilization. Twenty-four flume tests were carried out in model slopes under artificial rainfall; soils with various wettability levels were tested, including wettable, subcritical water repellent and water repellent. Various rainfall intensities, slope angles and relative compactions were applied to model the response of natural and man-made slopes to rainfall. Overall, an increase in soil water repellency reduced infiltration and shortened the time for runoff generation, with the effects amplified for high rainfall intensity. Comparatively, the slope angle and relative compaction had only a minor contribution to the slope hydrology. The main finding was that the subcritical water-repellent soils sustained infiltration for longer than both the wettable and water repellent soils, which presents an added advantage if they are to be used in the built environment as barriers. OUTPUT 3 THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK AND NUMERICAL MODEL In order to develop a theoretical framework for synthetic water-repellent soils, there was a need to account for the erosional processes. Erosional variables, including splash erosion rate, average sediment concentration, peak sediment concentration and time to peak sediment were measured to quantitatively analyze the behaviour of twenty-four flume tests. The results revealed that: (1) synthetic water repellency does not necessarily lead to increased soil erosion yield; its impact is dependent on grain size; (2) splash erosion was positively correlated to soil water repellency and high rainfall intensity, regardless of grain size; (3) the erosion processes for sand/silt mixtures are particle size selective and not affected by soil water repellency, whereas this phenomenon is not observed in the coarser with Fujian sand. OUTPUT 4 Finally, we explored the use of capillary barriers with synthetic water-repellent soils. By monitoring the surface runoff, lateral diversion and basal percolation, and conducting water balance analysis, the performance of monolithic cover, conventional capillary barrier and water-repellent capillary barrier cover systems were evaluated, with the results currently under review. OUTPUT 5 A particle-scale numerical model was also delivered. We investigated the interaction between an inclined hydrophobic granular surface and a millimetre-sized droplet. The droplet impact and sliding was investigated by the Lattice- Boltzmann method. Different droplet dynamics modes were found: (1) droplet sticks to surface, (2) droplet moves by pinning and depinning, (3) droplet partially detached from the surface, (4) droplet fully detached from the surface. Among other findings, the results revealed a dependence of the terminal velocity on the impacting velocity. These findings are available as Chapter 5 ‘Droplet sliding on inclined hydrophobic granular surfaces’ of the PhD thesis ‘Lattice Boltzmann simulation of fluid-particle interaction in hydrophobic granular materials’ by the PI’s former PhD student Dr Kang Hengyi.

17205915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205915.value: SYNTHESISED WATER REPELLENT GRANULAR MATERIALS Initial research identified compounds able to induce water repellency in various granular materials: from clean industrial sands to natural soils from Hong Kong. Among various compounds tested, dimethyldichlorosilane was found to induce high and persistent water repellency. Testing protocols were established and were since used in all our subsequent research. HYDROLOGICAL BEHAVIOR From a series of flume tests, an increase in soil water repellency reduced infiltration and shortened the time for runoff generation, with the effects amplified for high rainfall intensity. Comparatively, the slope angle and relative compaction had only a minor contribution to the slope hydrology. The subcritical water-repellent soils sustained infiltration for longer than both the wettable and water repellent soils, which presents an added advantage if they are to be used in the built environment. This study revealed substantial impacts of man-made or synthetically induced soil water repellency on the hydrological behavior of model slopes in controlled conditions. EROSIONAL BEHAVIOR From a second set of flume tests, synthetic water repellency did not necessarily lead to increased soil erosion yield. Its impact was dependent on grain size with the soil erosion loss increasing for Fujian sand, but decreasing for sand/silt mixtures. Splash erosion was positively correlated to soil water repellency and high rainfall intensity, regardless of grain size. The erosion processes for sand/silt mixtures were reported to be particle size selective and not affected by soil water repellency, whereas this phenomenon was not observed with Fujian sand. This study revealed that an optimum condition that inhibits the infiltration while controlling the increase in erosion can be achieved. WATER REPELLENT CAPILLARY BARRIERS From a third set of physical model tests conducted on inclined model slopes to evaluate the performance of a monolithic cover, a conventional capillary barrier and two proposed water-repellent capillary barrier cover systems, by monitoring the surface runoff, lateral diversion and basal percolation, and conducting a water balance analysis. The capillary barrier effect was significantly strengthened by the induced soil water repellency, including increased surface runoff, promoted lateral diversion, decreased basal percolation and delayed breakthrough. Particularly, the release of accumulated water into the underlying layer is still inhibited even after breakthrough. Note that most of our outputs were published in high-quality journals with demanding review processes, among them we would highlight Géotechnique, Journal of Hydrology and Science of the Total Environment.

17205915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205915.value: FIELD-SCALE TEST In the current study, laboratory scale experiments were conducted. However, an extrapolation from the behavior of the physical model to the behavior of the prototype is required. By performing full-scale field testing that uses soils under real environmental conditions, the scale effects can be avoided. Since water repellent soils are proposed as promising geomaterials, full-scale field testing would offer a validation of its applicability in engineering applications. It is therefore recommended to construct full-scale models to further investigate the hydrological and erosional behaviors of water-repellent soils, and thereby evaluating their performance as slope stabilization measures or landfill cover systems. Long-term monitoring should be carried out with a number of variables measured, e.g. surface runoff, infiltration, soil moisture content and sediment concentration. PARTICLE-SCALE MECHANISMS This study has presented distinctive hydrological and erosional behaviors of synthetic water repellent soils. However, mechanistic understanding of these processes is still needed, which could help to apply these interesting materials for practical problems, and further assist the design of engineers.

17205915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205915.value: Water repellent soils are granular materials that show a low affinity for water, with delayed water infiltration. Due to their distinctive hydraulic properties, interest has been growing in their potential as infiltration barriers. The current research aims to explore the hydrological and erosional behavior of synthetic water repellent soils, with a view to facilitating their utilization in the built environment. Overall, an increase in soil water repellency reduced infiltration and shortened the time for runoff generation, with the effects amplified for high rainfall intensity. The results revealed that water repellency did not necessarily lead to increased soil erosion yield. Its impact was dependent on grain size. This study indicated that an optimum condition that inhibited the infiltration while controlling the increase in erosion can be achieved. The capillary barrier effect was significantly strengthened by soil water repellency. Particularly, the release of accumulated water into the underlying layer is still inhibited even after breakthrough. This research provided a new insight on the understanding of the hydrological and erosional behavior of synthetic water repellent soils under rainfall, and therefore provides a basis for using these novel materials in the built environment.

17206615.label: Project Objectives
17206615.value: To conduct a theoretical study to look into the interplay between various driving mechanisms on the microscale of a SLIPS, and hence the interaction between the working fluid and the lubricating fluid, when the working fluid is under an applied pressure gradient or shear force on the macroscale. To investigate, through mathematical modeling or numerical simulation, effective or macroscopic slip arising from flow of a viscous fluid over a SLIPS as a function of the microtexture, properties of fluids, deformation of the fluid interface, and hydrodynamics of the bulk flow. To investigate drag reduction for pressure-driven flow through channels of various geometries with SLIPS walls. To investigate the self-healing capability and the draining loss of lubricant as a function of the microtexture, properties of the fluids, and hydrodynamics of the bulk flow.

17206615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206615.value: A novel non-wetting surface known as slippery liquid-infused porous surface (SLIPS) or lubricant impregnated surface (LIS) has been reported very recently. Experimental evidences revealed that SLIPS may have distinct liquid-repellency characteristics, such as a small contact angle hysteresis, capability to repel both aqueous and oily liquids, stability under high pressure, ability to self-repair when damaged, and so on. Being multifunctional, robust and inexpensive, SLIPS is considered to have great potential as a slippery surface to be widely used in the future. Much basic research being carried out in recent years, the current interests are to look into aspects like ice-phobicity and anti-fouling capability of SLIPS. Nonetheless, SLIPS is still in its early stage of development. Many aspects in terms of fluid mechanics about SLIPS are yet to be fully understood. In particular, how SLIPS may help reduce flow resistance in an internal flow remains a largely unaddressed issue to date. The present project aims to investigate effective slip or drag reduction arising from pressure-driven flow through a microchannel bounded by SLIPS. The slip can depend on many parameters, including geometry of the microtexture, properties of the fluids, the hydrodynamic and interfacial forcings, channel confinement, thermal effect, and so on. An in-depth and systematic theoretical modelling study will be pursued in this project. Efforts will be devoted to the development of a three-dimensional multi-phase numerical model that can simulate the flow of both lubricating and working fluids inside and immediately outside the microtextured surface. It is of interest to determine the optimum configuration for different geometries (such as grooves or pillars) of the microtexture. It is also of fundamental interest to look into the detailed hydrodynamics involved in the process. The aim is to address issues such as the stability of the interface between the lubricant and the working liquid when under the combined action of hydrodynamic and interfacial forcings, and also the flow of the lubricant in the process of self-healing. More advanced effects such as nonlinear fluid rheology and thermocapillary action will also be examined. The findings of this project may help develop phenomenological relationships between the effective slip and the controlling parameters. These relationships will enable one to estimate the drag reduction that can be obtained by using SLIPS walls in an internal flow. 本項目旨在探討當流體通過有「潤滑液注入多孔表面」(SLIPS) 的微通道時的有效滑移或減阻問題。這個滑移取決於許多參數， 包括微觀結構的幾何形狀、流體特性、流體動力和界面應力、 管壁束縛、熱效應等的屬性。本項目將在深入和系統的理論層面 開展。包括發展一個三維多相數值模型，可以模擬工作流體和 潤滑液在微結構表面外內的流動。目的為確定不同的幾何形狀 （諸如凹槽或支柱）的微觀結構的最優配置。也探討這一進程 的詳細流體力學。這樣可幫助瞭解多個問題，如在流體動力和 界面力的聯合作用下，工作液體和潤滑液之間的界面的穩定性， 和潤滑液的自愈流程中的流動。更深入的問題，如非線性流體 流變和熱毛細作用也將進行研究。這項目的研究結果可有助於 開發SLIPS管壁和控制參數之間的關係。這些關係將使人能估 算可以通過使用SLIPS壁中的內部流而獲得的減阻作用。

17206715.value: 無線電力傳送：全方位負載偵察及高效率方向性電力輸送

17206715.label: Project Objectives
17206715.value: To study and evaluate 2-dimensional and 3-dimensional load position detection methods for Omni-directional WPT systems. To examine directional power flow control methods in a 2-dimensional and 3-dimensional manner with the optimal energy efficiency. To combine the "Omni-directional" load detection method and the "Directional" power flow control method in 2-D and 3-D WPT systems.

17206715.label: Realisation of objectives
17206715.value: (1) We have conducted analyses on 2-D and 3-D wireless charging systems. We discovered that true omni-directional wireless power transfer (WPT) can only be achieved by using non-identical current control. Based on the use of the 3 current magnitudes, the overall resultant magnetic vector can be created and controlled in all directions. By scanning this resultant magnetic vector over a 3-D sruface and registering the amount of power delivered in each position, we can detect the load positions. This important discovery and proposed non-identical current control method has been patented. (2) After detecting the load positions based on the method developed in Objective 1, we futher studied the optimal directional power flow. We have developed the full analyses for the 2-D and 3-D WPT systems in capturing the power profiles. Based on such information, we can zoom energy directionally towards the loads in an energy-efficient manner. (3) To achieve objective 3, we combine the load-detection method based on the results in objective 1 and the directional power flow method in objective 2 to form a “scanning for load positions” and “power flow to loads” process. The success of this process has confirmed the practicality of the 2-D and 3-D WPT systrem analyses. All these theories have been practically verified with experimental prototype.

17206715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206715.value: The outcomes of this project include the first sets of full theoretical analyses on 2-dimensional and 3-dimensional wireless charging systems. We have laid down the mathematical foundations for these systems in a 2-part IEEE Transactions Papers. The theories have been practically verified with measurements. These outcomes have fulfilled the first two objectives of the project. For the third objective, we have developed the control principle of omnidirectional wireless power transfer systems. By scanning the magnetic vectors and registering the power consumption in a 3D manner, the power information allow the users to locate the load positions. Then we zoom the wireless power towards these loads in a directional manner in order to achieve high efficiency.

17206715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206715.value: The theory and control principles of omnidirectional wireless power transfer systems have been successfully developed in this project. These result open a new area of research, as reflected by the high citations of the 3 IEEE Transactions papers arising from this project. We are aware that some companies have plans to develop 2-D and 3-D wireless charging systems. A US patent on this omnidirectional wireless charging system was granted in April 2019. The Technology Transfer Office of HKU will handle the negotiation with potential industrial users.

17206715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206715.value: In the past, most of the wireless charging systems are of 1-dimensional nature. This project has successfully laid down the theoretical foundation and the control principles for wireless charging in a 3-dimensional manner. Besides publishing the outcomes in 3 top-tier journals, a US patent on this omnidirectional wireless charging system was granted in April 2019. The Ph.D student trained in this project is now an Assistant Professor at the University of Manchester, U.K.

17207115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207115.value: Buildings in Hong Kong consume 90% of electricity and contribute 60% of carbon emissions. Due to the scarce developable land in Hong Kong, high-rise residential buildings are almost the norm. The prefabrication approach has been integrated into the building design and construction of public housing in Hong Kong. Prefabrication will help not only reduce the carbon footprint of materials and products, but improve the efficiency of construction processes and quality of constructed facilities which should lead to substantial carbon reductions over the life cycle of the building. However, prefabrication is not yet a recognised life cycle stage, and there is no consistent method of estimating life cycle carbon emissions from prefabricated buildings. Previous research has also overlooked the indirect effects of prefabrication use, which may also play a significant role in reducing carbon emissions. The aim of this project is to examine the implications of prefabrication use for building life cycle carbon emissions and develop solutions for achieving maximum life cycle carbon emission reduction in high-rise public residential buildings in Hong Kong through optimal such use. The project will be carried out over a 36-month period in three interrelated stages: (1) develop a building life cycle carbon emission model; (2) estimate the carbon emissions of buildings in different prefabrication scenarios; and (3) conduct sensitivity analyses and develop solutions. The model will be contextualised and validated using a typical high-rise public residential building project in Hong Kong. Adopting the life cycle assessment approach, cradle-to-gate and after-use embodied carbon will be calculated using the SimaPro tool, prefabrication- and construction-related carbon emissions calculated using the process analysis method, and operational carbon emissions estimated using EnergyPlus software. A building information model (BIM) of the reference building will be created using Revit software. The BIM output will be converted into input for SimaPro and EnergyPlus using the application program interfaces provided by the tools/software to form a systemic model for the sensitivity analysis of building carbon emissions in different prefabrication scenarios. These scenarios will integrate low-carbon materials and innovative design features. The solutions developed in this project will help to achieve maximum life cycle carbon emission reduction in high-rise residential buildings, and the systemic model will provide a useful way of quantifying the relationship between prefabrication use and carbon emissions. The optimal prefabrication scenarios will be critical to exploring the future of buildings in Hong Kong. 香港建築消耗全港90%的電力資源, 對應60%的碳排放。由於可開發用地的缺乏，高層住宅建築在香港成為常態。預製吊裝方法已經被廣泛應用於香港公屋的設計與施工。該方法不僅有利於減少建築材料和產品生產過程中的碳足跡，還可提高施工效率及建築物質量，從而在根本上降低建築全壽命週期碳排放。然而，預製吊裝過程並未被考慮為建築全壽命週期的一環。當前並無統一的方法對採用預製吊裝技術的建築物的全壽命週期碳排放進行評估。諸多研究也忽視了預製吊裝技術可以有效減少建築碳排放的間接效應。 本研究旨在評估預製吊裝技術的應用對於建築全壽命週期碳排放的影響，並且通過優化該技術的應用，最大程度地減少香港高層公共住宅建築全壽命週期碳排放。本研究項目為期36個月，包括三個相關聯的階段: (1)建立建築的全壽命週期碳排放模型; (2)測算採用不同預製吊裝技術方案下的建築碳排放; (3)進行敏感性分析并提供解決方案。 該建築碳排放模型將使用典型的香港高層公共住宅項目實例進行檢驗。建築的全壽命週期評估，包括從開發到交付及後續階段的能耗計算將通過SimaPro軟件進行, 施工階段碳排放將使用過程分析方法計算, 建築運行階段碳排放將使用EnergyPlus軟件進行模擬。參考項目的建築信息模型 (BIM) 模型將通過Revit系列軟件建立，並且通過程序接口實現向SimaPro及EnergyPlus的數據傳遞，從而提供一套系統的計算模型以對多種預製吊裝方案進行建築碳排放的敏感性分析。這些方案將考慮低碳建築材料以及其它新型建築設計特征。 本研究所得出的解決方案將有助於最大程度降低香港高層住宅建築的全壽命週期碳排放。建立的系統性模型將提供一套有效的方法，以量化分析預製吊裝技術與建築碳排放之間的關係。優化的預製吊裝技術方案將對香港建築的未來發展具有重要意義。

17207115.label: Realisation of objectives
17207115.value: All of the three objectives have been achieved. For achieving Objective 1, a critical review of development and methods of building life cycle carbon assessment (LCCa) was conducted to identify the knowledge gaps. A fundamental framework to rethink the boundaries of buildings’ LCCa for achieving meaningful benchmarking and learning was developed. A total of four semi-structured interviews and two surveys were conducted with different stakeholders, including the representatives from the Hong Kong Housing Authority, the main contractor, prefabrication experts, as well as industry practitioners, to understand the latest development of the construction project using prefabrication techniques and methods of building life cycle assessment used in Hong Kong. A five-level framework for assessing the embodied carbon of prefabricated buildings was established in Teng and Pan (2019) to calculate and report the embodied carbon of prefabricated buildings in Hong Kong during the cradle-to-end of construction stages. It denotes that the embodied carbon is analysed at the levels of material (e.g. concrete, steel), component (e.g. a precast slab and a staircase), assembly (e.g. a non-volumetric precast facade panel completed with window and a volumetric precast bathroom/ kitchen pod), flat (a residential unit) and building (the entire building). The assessment of the operational carbon of high-rise prefabricated buildings was conducted based on energy consumption calculated using DesignBuilder software. A framework of the BIM-integrated embodied carbon assessment was developed to reduce the time for inventory data acquisition and to improve the details of the LCA study for a specific building. The framework is comprised of three essential steps: data input, data analysis, and solution. For achieving Objective 2, a systematic examination of the evidence for reducing building LCCa through prefabrication was conducted in Teng et al. (2018). The relevant published empirical studies were examined using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses method, based on the fundamental framework developed before. A systems framework was developed from the ontology, epistemology, methodology and axiology aspects to have identified seven gaps in existing knowledge. A typical high-rise public rental housing (PRH) block in Hong Kong was used as case study to validate the model application. For achieving Objective 3, a detailed literature review on carbon reduction measures was first conducted. Then a scenario analysis followed by a sensitivity analysis was used to investigate possible embodied carbon reduction measures in Hong Kong. Scenarios were designed to a case building, and included (1) adopting low carbon materials (S1a replacing 25% of the cement with pulverized fly ash (PFA) and S1b replacing ordinary Portland cement with blast furnace slag cement), (2) increasing the prefabrication rate of the case building from 35.2% to 44.8%, (3) decreasing the thickness of non-structural concrete block walls from 150 mm to 125 mm and the thickness of load-bearing reinforced concrete walls from 200 to 175 mm. For operational carbon, a quick-win and the optimization scenarios were developed, followed by sensitivity analysis.

17207115.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207115.value: This research leads to publication of 6 journal articles (with 2 more in writing) and 4 conference papers and training of 2 PhD students. The current challenges of buildings’ LCCa are examined in Pan et al. (2018) as: implicit system boundaries of prefabrication and LCCa; inconsistent methods, models and units of analysis of estimating buildings’ life cycle carbon; and labour-intensive process with limited accountability. To address these challenges, the solutions are: a regression model of relating buildings’ LCCa to system boundaries; a five-level framework of units of analysis consisting of material, component, assembly, flat and building; and a smart technology integrated approach for automatic LCCa. The review conducted in Teng et al. (2018) shows that the embodied and operational carbon of prefabricated cases vary signiﬁcantly from 105 to 864 kg CO2/m2, and from 11 to 76kg CO2/m2/yr, respectively. The results also indicate that, on average, 15.6% of embodied and 3.2% of operational carbon reductions are achievable through prefabrication compared with their traditional base cases. The embodied carbon of the case building is calculated at the five levels of unit of analysis in the paper by Teng and Pan (2019). At material level, more than 75% of the material embodied carbon is contributed by the production of cast-in-situ concrete (39.8%), steel (20.1%), and precast concrete (19.4%). At the component and assembly levels, more than 85% of the embodied carbon was generated from material consumption. At flat level, the ‘1B’ type of flats was found to be least embodied carbon intensive among all four types (1B, 1P2P, 2P3P, and 2B). At building level, the embodied carbon of a typical floor is estimated to be 561 kg CO2/m2. The operational carbon emissions intensity (CEI) is calculated as 55.5kg/ (m2-yr). For the embodied carbon reduction measures, the scenario analysis is concluded in Teng and Pan (2019). It indicates that replacing 25% of the cement with PFA for concrete can result in a 9.8% reduction of the embodied carbon. A maximum 22.8% embodied carbon reduction can be achieved by replacing ordinary Portland cement with blast furnace slag cement. For the operational carbon reduction measures, the quick-win and optimization scenarios can help to achieve 28.5% and 58.3% carbon reduction. Measures such as renewable energy technologies (particularly PV) with standard efficiency, cooling set point, shower time have greater influence.

17207115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207115.value: The estimation of prefabricated buildings’ embodied carbon has been a labour-intensive process with limited accountability. Traditionally, data are collected and analysed manually, rendering a very low-efficiency process prone to human error. Further study could be conducted on smart-techs integrated analysis for achieving automated embodied carbon assessment of prefabricated buildings. Smart meters and sensors can be used for data collection. Necessary APIs can be adopted for data transfer and conversion from BIM to carbon estimation software.

17207115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207115.value: The reconstructed system boundaries of buildings’ life cycle carbon assessment help to achieve a better understanding of the factors that influence buildings’ life cycle carbon emissions in a systems integrative manner and thus facilitate cross-case comparisons. The developed building information modelling integrated carbon assessment framework provides a working example of linking a building information model with a carbon assessment tool, which facilitates the integration of carbon assessment into a more efficient process. The developed five-level analytical framework paves the foundation for future standardization and benchmarking of prefabricated buildings’ embodied carbon and the findings provide a useful way of quantifying the relationship between prefabrication use and buildings’ carbon emissions. The low carbon solutions developed will help to achieve maximum carbon emission reduction in Hong Kong’s high-rise residential buildings, thereby will inform future research and practice in the area of innovative prefabricated building design and construction.
