17207415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207415.value: Most existing facility location models assume that the facility cost is either a fixed setup cost or comprised of a fixed setup and a problem-specific concave or submodular cost term. This structural property plays a critical role in developing efficient column generation, Lagrangian relaxation, constant ratio approximation algorithms, and conic IP reformulation approaches for these NP-hard problems. Many practical considerations and complicating factors, however, can make the facility cost no longer concave or submodular. By removing this restrictive assumption, we study two facility location frameworks with an arbitrarily number of general nondecreasing facility cost functions, which are referred to as the basic and compound models, respectively. These general frameworks have many important applications, such as joint location-inventory model with capacity and/or congestion cost, multi-commodity facility location and production model with economies and diseconomies of scale, and multi-commodity facility location and capacity planning model with service level constraints. The general models do not even admit any approximation algorithms unless P=NP. In response to this, we consider the column generation approach and focus on the solution procedure of the pricing problem, which must be solved in each iteration of the column generation scheme. Although our preliminary result shows that the pricing problem is NP-hard, we have effectively analyzed the structural properties of the pricing problem arisen from the basic model with one or two general facility cost functions. These results lead to efficient algorithms to solve the pricing problem. Our numerical experiments have validated that for the basic model with two general facility costs, the proposed column generation approach is capable of solving practically-sized model instances within moderate computational time. This project will further study the pricing problem for the basic model with more than two general facility cost functions as well as that for the compound model. We have obtained sufficient insights from the preliminary studies, which will guide us to characterize the structural properties of the corresponding optimal solutions. Based on these theoretical properties, we will develop efficient algorithms to solve the pricing problems and build the column generation schemes using these components. Various column generation and parallel computation strategies will be employed to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed approaches. In addition, we will study the extensions of the basic and compound models in supply chains consisting of manufacturing plants, warehouses, and customers. 大多數現有的設施選址模型中，設施運營成本通常被假定為單一的固定成本，或由固定成本及一項針對特定問題的凹性或子模性函數構成。這種結構特性對開發高效列生成算法、拉格朗日鬆弛算法、恆定比例近似算法、及錐整數規劃，從而對這些NP困難的問題進行求解起至關重要的作用。然而，許多實際問題中的複雜因素會破壞設施運營成本的凹性或子模性。通過去除這種限制性假設，我們得到兩種框架性模型，即基本模型和符合模型。它們均包含任意項的一般非減性設施運營成本函數，在實際中有很多重要的應用，如包括容量約束及/或阻塞費用的聯合庫存選址模型，規模經濟及不經濟下多商品的選址和生產模型，以及服務水準制約下多商品的選址和容量規劃模型。 除非P = NP，這兩種一般性的模型甚至不能通過近似算法求解。為此，我們採用列生成算法。由於列生成算法每一次迭代都要對定價問題求解，我們將著重於對定價問題的研究。在基本模型只包含一項或兩項一般性設施運營成本函數時，雖然我們的初步結果證明該定價問題是NP困難問題，我們已經通過有效地分析其結構特性，從而對其進行快速求解。我們的數值實驗已證實，就包含兩項一般性設施運營成本函數的基本模型，我們所提出的列生成算法能夠在適度的計算時間內解決實際大小的模型實例。 本項目將進一步研究有兩項以上一般性設施運營成本函數的基本模型以及複合模型的定價問題。通過初步研究，我們已經對這些定價問題的最優解得到充分的瞭解，這將指導我們全面地刻畫最優解的結構特徵。基於這些理論特性，我們將開發高效算法以解決定價問題，並在此基礎上構建設施選址問題的列生成算法。我們還將運用多種列生成及並行計算的策略以增強該算法的效率和效能。此外，我們將對基本和複合模型進行擴展，從而研究包括製造工廠、分銷中心、和客戶的多級供應鏈。

17207415.label: Realisation of objectives
17207415.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. The details are provided as follows: In both the basic and compound models, we are given a set of retail outlets and a set of potential facility locations. Each retailer must be served by exactly one facility to be set up at a potential location. There are three types of costs incurred in this system: (i) fixed cost for opening facilities, (ii) transportation cost, which is a variable cost incurred each time a unit is sent from a facility to a retailer, (iii) facility cost, representing the operating cost of a facility that depends on the set of retailers served by the facility. The objective is to determine the location of facilities and the assignment of facilities to retailers (assuming single-sourcing) so as to minimize the total systemwide location, transportation, and facility costs. In order to model the facility costs, we introduce a set of attributes for each retailer i if it is served by each facility j. For example, an attribute could represent the demand mean, the demand variance, the constant demand rate, or the weighted shipping distance of product k from facility j to retailer i via routing. The facility cost for facility j is then defined as a general nondecreasing function of the aggregated attributes of all the retailers served by facility j. The basic and compound models differ in the general function form that determines the facility cost. The basic model considers the case that the facility cost at any facility j is the sum of some single-variate functions. The input for each of the single-variate functions is the sum of a single attribute for each retailer served by facility j. For example, we can use a single-variate function to represent the cost to serve the aggregated demand mean of a given product from all retailers assigned to facility j. In the compound model, we consider the facility cost at any facility j as a sum of multi-variate functions. For any of the multi-variate functions, each input argument corresponds to the sum of a single attribute for each retailer served by facility j. For example, if the facilities are manufacturing plants, we can consider the facility cost at any facility j as the total cost of building sufficient capacities for multiple products. For any specific product, under the assumption that demands for all retailers are independent normal random variables, the corresponding capacity cost can be represented as a function that depends on the aggregated demand mean and the aggregated demand variance for all retailers served by facility j. Both the basic and compound models are then generalized to supply chain network design problems. In particular, we consider two types of supply chain networks. First, we consider a supply chain network consisting of manufacturing plants, warehouses, and retailers. The products are produced by the manufacturing plants and then distributed to the retailers through the warehouses. The locations of both manufacturing plants and warehouses, the assignments of warehouses to manufacturing plants, as well as the assignments of retailers to warehouses are jointly optimized to minimize the sum of the location costs of manufacturing plants and warehouses, the transportation costs from manufacturing plants to retailers via warehouses, and the general facility costs at warehouses. A supply chain network of the second type consists of suppliers, manufacturing plants, and retailers. The manufacturing plants obtain raw materials from the suppliers, produce the products, and ship the products to the retailers. We would like to determine where to locate the manufacturing plants, how to source the raw materials, and how to assign each retailer to the manufacturing plants so that the total cost of location, sourcing, transportation, and operating the manufacturing plants can be minimized. In this project, we have first formulated each of the aforementioned facility location and supply chain network design problems as a set partitioning model, which has an exponential number of binary decision variables. Therefore, the branch-and-price approach is adopted to solve the set partitioning model to optimality. The branch-and-price approach solves the set partitioning model based on the branch-and-bound procedure, in which the linear programs to be solved at each node of the branch-and-bound tree are solved by the column generation method. Consequently, for each node of the branch-and-bound tree, a pricing problem must be solved in each column generation iteration so as to check whether the current solution is optimal to the linear program at this node. Through branching on whether a retailer is served by a facility, we can ensure that the pricing problems for all the branch-and-bound nodes have the same structure. The pricing problems turn out to be binary integer problems with nonlinear objective functions, which are proved to be NP-hard. Nevertheless, after carefully analyzing the structural properties of the pricing problems, we have developed efficient algorithms to solve the pricing problems to optimality. As a result, the branch-and-price algorithm is also capable of solving the corresponding facility location or supply chain network design model in a reasonable time. We have conducted extensive numerical studies to verify the efficiency of the branch-and-price algorithms. It is also revealed that the systemwide cost can be reduced significantly by incorporating the facility costs when making strategic decisions of supply chain network configuration.

17207415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207415.value: This project has led to 2 papers published in INFORMS Journal on Computing (Li et al. 2017 and Ni et al. 2020), 1 PhD thesis (Li, 2016), 4 presentations in international conferences, and 1 seminar talk at Jinan University. Through this project, we have successfully developed efficient branch-and-price algorithms for the facility location and supply chain network design problems with general facility cost functions. Our numerical studies also show the importance of considering the general facility costs, which can substantially reduce the systemwide total cost. Please refer to Ni et al. (2020) for more details. A major theoretical contribution is to study the structural properties of the pricing problems derived from the branch-and-price algorithms, which is briefly introduced as follows. - For the basic model, without loss of generality, suppose that the facility cost for each facility can be represented as the sum of n single-variate functions. (i) There exists an optimal solution to the relaxation of the pricing problem that contains at most n fractional components. If the total facility cost, i.e., the sum of the n single-variate functions, can be represented as a multi-variate quasi-concave function, then there exists an optimal solution to the relaxation that contains at most one fractional component. These properties suggest that a simple branch-and-bound algorithm can be employed to solve the pricing problem as long as its relaxation can be solved rapidly. (ii) For any optimal solution to the relaxation, there exists a hyperplane in the n-dimensional space such that the components corresponding to points on one side of the hyperplane are ones and those corresponding to points on the other side of the hyperplane are zeros. Furthermore, there exists a systematic approach to construct an optimal solution with at most n fractional components by solving optimization problems with n decision variables corresponding to points on the hyperplane. Therefore, the relaxation can be decomposed into at most C(m,n) problems with n decision variables, where m denotes the number of customers in the facility location problem. - For the compound model and the network design problems, if the facility costs are defined based on n attributes of the retailers, the pricing problems have the same properties as that for the basic model whose facility cost is the sum of n single-variate functions. Hence, the pricing problems can be solved by algorithms similar to that for the basic model.

17207415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207415.value: An important contribution of this project is to develop efficient algorithms for the pricing problems arising from the branch-and-price procedure. These pricing problems are likely to have important applications in other areas as well. Many problems, such as the performance achievability checking problem for multiclass queueing systems, the market selection problem, and the operating room scheduling problem, are also special cases of the pricing problem. Although all the aforementioned models possess a submodular structure, a simple practical consideration, e.g., capacity, may destroy the property. Therefore, there are potentially many important applications of our results on the pricing problems that go well beyond location and network design modeling. It would be interesting to explore these applications in the future. Another possible way to further this research is to develop efficient heuristics for the proposed models. For strategic decisions such as supply chain network configuration, minimizing the systemwide cost may not be the sole objective of the decision makers. Compared with the exact solution approaches proposed in this project, the heuristics may be able to generate multiple solutions with closed-to-optimal costs. The decision makers can then choose among these heuristic solutions the one that most suits other needs.

17207415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207415.value: Most existing facility location models assume that the facility cost is either a fixed setup cost or comprised of a fixed setup and a problem-specific concave or submodular cost term. This structural property plays a critical role in developing fast solution approaches for these NP-hard problems. Many practical considerations and complicating factors, however, can make the facility cost no longer concave or submodular. By removing this restrictive assumption, we study new location models that consider general nonlinear costs to operate facilities in the facility location framework. The general models do not even admit any approximation algorithms unless P=NP because it takes the unsplittable hard-capacitated metric facility location problem as a special case. We first formulate these general problems as set-partitioning models and then propose branch-and-price approaches to solve the resulting binary integer programs with an exponential number of decision variables. Although the corresponding pricing problems are NP-hard, we effectively analyze their structural properties and design algorithms to solve them efficiently. Extensive numerical studies verify the efficiency of the proposed algorithms. They also demonstrate that significant cost reductions can be achieved if we consider the general facility costs at the network design stage.

17207715.label: Project Objectives
17207715.value: Develop the prototypes of the ACED cavity operating in VIS-sNIR – ACED cavity is essentially a free-space Fabry-Perot cavity with two non-parallel (i.e. angle-misaligned) mirrors, which is the key feature enabling enormous (also dynamically tunable) GDD, yet with low optical loss, within a reasonable footprint. In contrast to the standard dispersive-fiber-based OTS, this is a new concept of OTS. We will thus first devise the optimal ACED-cavity design rules, which can be done adequately based on geometric optics, i.e. ray-tracing, for efficient OTS operation in VIS-sNIR. Design considerations include the achievable GDD, optical loss, spectral and spectral/temporal resolutions. According to the optimal designs, the prototypes will be constructed by the commercially-available optics, e.g. high-reflectivity plane mirrors and diffraction grating. Its OTS performance will be characterized and optimized in two selected wavelength ranges: ~500 nm and ~800 nm – the windows to be adopted in the OTS-based imaging systems. Establish two OTS bioimaging modalities in VIS-SNIR based on ACED cavity – Leveraging on our current expertise in varies modalities of OTS-related imaging, we will then exemplify the utility of the new ACED-cavity concept for OTS bioimaging in the unexploited VIS-sNIR range by developing two imaging modalities based on our prior work – (i) optofluidic cellular quantitative phase OTS imaging at ~500nm: To demonstrate its better compatibility with standard tools used in biomedicine (e.g. bioassays), this quantitative phase OTS imaging system will also be integrated with a non-imaging single-cell fluorescence detection module for multiparametric quantitative cellular imaging in ultrafast microfluidic flow (>1 m/s), particularly valuable for highly multiplexed cellular assays; (ii) OTS-based swept-source OCT (SS-OCT) at ~800nm with an A-scan rate of multi-MHz: OTS-based OCT has been restricted in 1500–1600nm while many successful OCT applications, e.g. retinal imaging in ophthalmologic diagnosis, demand the operation window of 800–1000nm. . Exploit a new modality: “spectral-encoding-free” OTS imaging in VIS-sNIR – Spectral-encoding of image has long been the pre-requisite in OTS imaging. However, it is this feature making OTS imaging generally incompatible with fluorescence imaging – the workhorse in life sciences and biomedicine. Intriguingly, ACED cavity also works with non-spatially-dispersed light for efficient OTS in VIS-sNIR. It implies that broadband spectral encoding is no longer necessary. Together with its giant stretched-time and low-loss operation, ACED cavity represents a unique concept enabling ultrafast OTS fluorescence imaging. We will exploit this entirely new approach, i.e. spectral-encoding-free OTS imaging, using a narrowband source in VIS-sNIR. Specifically, the prototype development will be focused on demonstrating fluorescence OTS imaging.

17207715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207715.value: 光學時間伸延 (OTS)技術早期是被應用在高速光纖通訊, 而近年來, 它被轉化成為全新的高速光學成像技術 (達到每秒超過一百萬幀), 應用到生物醫學領域上. 此技術主要成像概念是 把影像資訊實時及高級地轉化成時間連續數據, 當中物理原理是透過光色散現象去連續地編碼影像資訊數據到光波中. 但此光色散現象往往令至光強度嚴重損耗, 大大影響成像之敏感度. 而OTS 成像技術成功之處在於它利用低損耗玻璃光纖作為傳送被編碼之影像資訊, 這既能夠做出強大光色散現象之餘, 並保持光強度. 可惜, 礙於現今製造光纖的技術, 此功能只限於近紅外線波段 (NIR) 操作範圍. 所以OTS 成像技術至今仍然未能適用在短波段. 而廣泛光學生物成像技術就正正需要利用短波段光源去操作. 為克服上述有關難題, 此研究項目會開發一個全新OTS 技術平台, 名為ACED cavity. 此技術能夠在短波至長波段 (即由可見光至紅外)中產生低損耗極大光色散現象. 當中原理是利用一對輕鬆不平衡的平鏡去 製造光色散現象. 由於ACED cavity 完全可以的真空或空氣中操作, 不需要倚靠任何物料作為傳送光的介面, 因此光強度損耗在 ACED cavity 中非常低 (物料, 例如玻璃光纖,會導致光強度損耗). 此研究項目目標利用ACED cavity去發展全新可用於可見光至紅外的OTS 成像技術. 此技術可應用不用光學生物成像診斷, 例如高速高通量光流體細胞成像檢測, 高速光學相干斷層掃瞄, 以及甚至有利開發OTS 螢光成像技術.

17207715.label: Realisation of objectives
17207715.value: 1. We have developed the ACED cavity operating in VIS-sNIR – ACED cavity that enables enormous (also dynamically tunable) GDD, yet with low optical loss, within a reasonable footprint. We also demonstrated that this techniique outperforms conventional fiber-based time-stretch in generating large GDD and lower optical loss. 2. We have successfully demonstrated optofluidic cellular quantitative phase OTS imaging at ~500nm (based on the concept similar to phase-graident encoding) by using ACED and allow multiparametric quantitative cellular imaging in ultrafast microfluidic flow (>1 m/s). Combined with our experience in microfluidic fabrication, we applied this imaging technology to realize fluorescence + bright-field imaging flow cytometry (in the format of microfluidic platform) for cancer cell detection in blood as well as other functional cell-based assays (nutrient starvation assay, as well as drug-response assay). 3. We have developed the spectral-encoding-free approach that only relies on simple focuing lens to generate largely flexible delay between the virtual sources, which are projected onto the imaging plane as ultrafast laser-scanning beam. This imaging technique has successfully applied to different imaging modalities, from bright-field, phase-contrast, fluorescence, and even multiphoton contrasts. We have also demonstrated the use of ACED for high-speed 2D dynamical fluorescence imaging at a 2D frame rate as high as 3000 fps.

17207715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207715.value: We have developed the ACED cavity operating in VIS-sNIR – ACED cavity that enables enormous (also dynamically tunable) GDD, yet with low optical loss, within a reasonable footprint. We demonstrated that this techniique outperforms conventional fiber-based time-stretch in generating large GDD and lower optical loss. We have successfully demonstrated optofluidic cellular quantitative phase OTS imaging at ~500nm by using ACED and allow multiparametric quantitative cellular imaging in ultrafast microfluidic flow (>1 m/s). We applied it for fluorescence + bright-field imaging flow cytometry for cancer cell detection in blood as well as other functional cell-based assays. We have also demonstrated the use of ACED for high-speed 2D dynamical fluorescence imaging at a 2D frame rate as high as 3000 fps. We have generated at least 10 journal publications and 24 conference presentations. 1 US patent was filed and granted. PI have co-found a spin-off company commercializing the ACED (now known as FACED) technology for cancer screening application.

17207715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207715.value: The system will be further expanded to other optical imaging modalities, especially, nonlinear optical microscopy (e.g. second harmonic generation (SHG), and two-photon excitation fluorescence imaging). This could open up a new direction of high-speed multi-photon microscopy development, for high-speed 2D or even 3D dynamical imaging, as well as high-throughput screening applications (e.g. flow cytometry).

17207715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207715.value: We have successfully developed a new type of optical microscopy technique that high-speed laser-scanning imaging at the rate 100x faster than the existing microscopes (notably fluorescence microscopes). This technology allows a new paradigm in opticial microscopy in a wide range of new applications that have not been achieved by the existing technologies, such as high-throughput fluorescence imaging flow cytometry (at the IMAGING throughout of > 10,000 cells/sec) used in clinical diagnosis (e.g. immunology), dynamical fluoresence microscopy (e.g. monitoring neuronal firing) at the 2D frame rate of 1000 fps (e.g. neuroscience research).

17208515.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17208515.value: 基於激光檢測技術（LIF和LDA）對錯流式膜分離過程中濃差極化的研究

17208515.label: Project Objectives
17208515.value: To use LIF to visualize the CP layer near the membrane in the crossflow environment and to characterize the CP dynamics under different hydrodynamic conditions; To use LDA to detect the shear flow and micro-turbulence in the boundary layer over the membrane surface and to study their impact on the material transport and CP formation; To validate and modify the CP models based on the laboratory findings and to develop effective CP control strategies.

17208515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208515.value: Membrane filtration, including nanofiltration (NF) and ultrafiltration (UF), has been increasingly used in water purification and wastewater treatment and reclamation. However, membrane fouling is still a major problem for the membrane filtration process. It has been well recognized that membrane fouling is inherently connected with the phenomenon of concentration polarization (CP) that occurs in the boundary layer near the membrane surface. During membrane filtration, rejection of the impurities by the membrane gives rise to the material accumulation near the membrane surface, forming a CP layer. The CP formation not only increases the resistance of membrane filtration but also forces the foulant deposition on the membrane, leading to irreversible membrane fouling. However, due to the highly dynamic and instable feature of the CP in a small (<0.1 mm thin) scale, there are few experimental studies conducted directly on the CP dynamics. Lacking of the experimental means for CP detection also makes it difficult to validate the CP models and to study the CP formation behavior during membrane filtration. Laser-based imaging or detection techniques are powerful tools for studies of fluid phenomena. In recent years, we have developed the techniques and capability to use laser-based imaging and detection methods for investigation of small-scale fluid structures or dynamics, including laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) for flow visualization and chemical detection and laser Doppler anemometry (LDA) for point-measurement of the velocity details. In this proposed project, the LIF and LDA techniques will be utilized in the membrane study to investigate the CP dynamics in micro-scale during the crossflow ultrafiltration in a flat-sheet membrane cell. The LIF system will be used with the fluorescent proteins for direct visualization of CP layers at different crossflow velocities and filtration fluxes. The LDA technique will be applied with titania nanoparticles to measure the velocity details in the boundary layer and to detect the micro-turbulences near the membrane surface. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) also will be performed to simulate the CP dynamics. Based on experimental and simulation results, a more comprehensive CP model will be formulated for membrane filtration accounting for the effect of flow instability on the material transport near the membrane surface. Accordingly, effective strategies, such as optimization of the hydrodynamic conditions and modification of the membrane surface morphology, will be developed for CP control. The research findings will make significant contributions to the development and application of membrane technologies in the field of water purification and wastewater reclamation. 膜分離技術（納濾（NF）、超濾（UF））越來越廣泛地應用在飲用水深度處理、污水深度處理和回用等方面。然而，膜污染仍然是膜分離過程中需解決的一個主要問題。膜污染與在膜表面的邊界層發生的濃差極化（CP）現象有著密切的內在關聯，已被人們所認知。在膜分離過程中，隨著過濾的持續，膜截留物質在膜表面累積而形成濃差極化層。濃差極化層的形成不僅會增大膜過濾的阻力，還會促使膜表面被截留物質的沉積，進而形成不可恢復的膜污染。由於濃差極化具有高度動態化、不穩定、厚度較小（小於0.1毫米）等特徵，故鮮有實驗直接對濃差極化的動態過程進行相關研究。缺少適宜的實驗手段來觀測濃差極化現象，使對濃差極化模型的驗證以及對在過濾過程中濃差極化層的形成方式的研究變得十分困難。 基於激光的成像或檢測技術是研究流體現象的有力工具。近年來，我們建立了利用激光成像檢測方法研究小型流場結構或其動態過程的技術，包括：利用激光誘導熒光（LIF）將流體可視化、進行化學檢測的技術，利用激光多普勒測速儀（LDA）對流速細節進行點測量的技術。在本次立項中，LIF與LDA技術將聯用於平板膜組件裡錯流式超濾過程中微型濃差極化動態過程的研究。其中，將LIF系統和熒光蛋白用於在不同錯流流速和過濾通量運行條件下，濃差極化層的可視化表徵的研究。將LDA技術和二氧化鈦納米粒子共用於測定邊界層裡的流速細節、檢測膜表面附近的微紊流特徵的研究。同時，將計算流體力學（CFD）用於濃差極化動態過程的模擬研究上。基於實驗和模擬的結果，將建立一個能夠用於解釋膜表面附近流體的不穩定性對於傳質的影響的更加綜合的膜分離的濃差極化形成模型。據此可以提出諸如優化水力條件、修整膜表面形態學等策略，對濃差極化進行有效控制。本研究結果將為膜技術在飲用水淨化及污水回用領域的發展與應用做出重要貢獻。

17208515.label: Realisation of objectives
17208515.value: All of the research objectives have been well achieved. Following the proposal, the experimental setup consisting of a typical cross-flow membrane filtration chamber and a micro-LIF system was developed. The permeate was collected and measured by a balance that was connected to a computer for data recording, and the concentrate was returned to the feed tank. During the filtration experiment, the transmembrane pressure (TMP) was read from a pressure gauge, and the cross-flow velocity through the membrane chamber was calculated from the water flowrate, measured by a flowmeter. The flat-sheet membrane chamber with internal dimensions of 120 × 10 × 5 mm3 was fabricated from polymethyl methacrylate to satisfy the optical transparency requirement. A 30 × 5 mm2 observatory window in the side wall of the membrane chamber reduced the wall thickness from 15 to 5 mm to satisfy the LIF micro-lens focal length requirement. The micro-LIF system (Dantec Dynamics, Denmark) consisted of a laser source (high-power Nd:YAG lasers) emitting 532 nm laser light, a HiSense Zyla sCMOS Camera with a long-pass cut-off filter and a 5× microscopic objective lens, and a computer equipped with the Dynamic Studio software package for image acquisition. A laser generator was used to form a 1 mm thick laser light sheet to illuminate the membrane chamber. The laser sheet plane cut perpendicularly along the center of the membrane surface in the flow chamber, and the flow field near the membrane surface could be captured from the side view. The fluorescent light signals were captured by the CCD camera through the optical filter and recorded in a gray-scale image. The images had a resolution of 2,560 × 2,160 pixels for a size of 2.45 × 2.07 mm, corresponding to a high resolution of <1 μm/pixel. Dynamic Studio software (version 6.2) was used for the preliminary image processing and analysis. As concentration polarization (CP) is a dynamic process affected by various hydraulic factors during filtration, the effects of cross-flow velocity and TMP on the CP dynamics were investigated. Three crossflow velocities, 0.03, 0.10, and 0.14 m/s (Re = 220, 660, and 950, respectively), were tested and changed in a sequence of 0.14-0.10-0.03-0.10-0.14 m/s at the fixed TMP of 1 bar. Similarly, three TMP values, 0.5, 1.0, and 1.5 bar, were applied and varied in a sequence of 0.5-1.0-1.5-1.0-0.5 bar for a fixed cross-flow velocity of 0.14 m/s. Three particle concentrations, 20, 70, and 100 ppm, were used for the different crossflow and TMP conditions, giving a combination of six experimental tests. For the filtration experiment, each condition was maintained for 5 min and the LIF images were captured every minute. The results show that the exact CP profile can be influenced by the crossflow velocity, TMP, and particle concentration. When changing the filtration conditions, such as the crossflow velocity or TMP, the CP profile changes immediately and reaches a new steady state in a short period. The CP profile appears to be reproducible under the same operating conditions. Therefore, the reversibility of the CP layer is validated by its visualization and CP dynamics under different hydrodynamic conditions were well characterized. By applying the film theory model to further quantify the experimental results, the concentration at the membrane surface, the thickness of the CP layer, and the mass transfer coefficient can be determined. However, the deficiency of the film theory model based on merely Brownian diffusion in describing CP dynamics is also revealed, and the CP model is shown to require improvement. As shear-induced diffusion needs to be taken into consideration during the crossflow membrane filtration process, the effect of the fluid shear rate on the shear-induced diffusion of particles of different sizes, and its impact on the particle deposition and membrane fouling was investigated with the application of micro-LIF and micro-PIV. The particle concentration distribution and profile near the membrane surface were well depicted by micro-LIF for the filtration of 100, 600 and 800 nm particles under the low shear rate and high shear rate conditions. The local shear rate at the interface was obtained from the vector map determined by the micro-PIV detection. Results showed that membrane fouling by particle deposition could be mitigated by shear-induced diffusion that is affected by the shear rate and particle size. A high shear rate and large particle size resulted in a greater shear-induced diffusion, leading to less fouling. By further calculation of Brownian diffusion coefficient and shear-induced coefficient, the dominant mechanism of particle back-transport was revealed. Shear-induced diffusion was much stronger than Brownian diffusion for most cases. Brownian diffusion was found to be important to small particles, while shear-induced diffusion was significant for large particles. Therefore, enhancing the shear-induced diffusion by increasing the fluid shear rate can be an effective approach to mitigate the membrane fouling problem. As membrane surface modification has been recognized as an effective approach for membrane fouling mitigation and reduction, for the first time, particle deposition on the surface of micro-patterned membranes was investigated by using micro-LIF and micro-PIV. Micro-patterned membrane was successfully fabricated by the modified immersion precipitation method from the PDMS replica mold with parallel line and space micro-patterns. Experiments were conducted to determine the different flow patterns near the surface of both the patterned and non-patterned membranes. Filtration tests were carried out to visualize the nanoparticle depositions on the patterned and non-patterned membrane surface. The results showed that the growth of the particle deposition layer, or fouling layer, on the micro-patterned membrane was much slower than that on the non-patterned membrane. Further analysis of the shear rate distribution obtained from the velocity vector map confirmed that there was a high shear rate region in the upper region of the patterned membrane surface, which explained the mechanism of fouling mitigation by the membrane surface patterning. This high shear rate in the micro-turbulence region was effective in disturbing the accumulation and attachment of particles on the membrane surface and facilitating the detachment of the particles from the membrane surface, resulting in much less fouling on the patterned membrane surface than the non-patterned one. Therefore, membrane modification with the surface patterning was shown to be a promising approach for membrane fouling control. In addition, the flow and fouling behaviors of two different types of patterned membrane were also studied by micro-LIF and micro-PIV. The size ratio of the pattern on the membrane surface was 1:2 and 3:2 respectively. Filtration tests of 800 nm fluorescent particles were conducted with these two types of patterned membranes under two different crossflow velocities. Results found that under the same crossflow velocity, fouling was less severe for the patterned membrane with big size ratio than the one with small size ratio, especially when the crossflow velocity was small. For the same membrane pattern type, fouling was less severe when the crossflow velocity was high, especially for the one with a small size ratio. As the vortex formed varied with the pattern size ratio and crossflow velocity, the hydraulic behavior of the flow near the patterned membrane played an important role in the anti-fouling performance of the patterned membrane. Thus, membrane fouling can be mitigated even without the need of increasing crossflow velocities, as long as the vortex formed between patterns were large enough to take effect.

17208515.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208515.value: • A non-invasive micro-LIF technique was successfully applied to realize real-time investigation of the CP phenomenon during crossflow ultrafiltration. Images of the CP layer and its dynamic changes under different filtration conditions were captured at a high resolution and the reversibility of the CP layer was validated. The results show that the thickness of the CP layer was approximately in the range of 30-50 μm. When changing the filtration conditions, such as the crossflow velocity or TMP, the CP profile changed rapidly and reached a new steady state in a short period. The CP profile appeared to be reproducible under the same operating conditions. By applying the film theory model to further quantify the experimental results, the concentration at the membrane surface, the thickness of the CP layer, and the mass transfer coefficient were determined. (Sun et al., 2016; Meng and Li, 2019) • Micro-LIF and micro-PIV were applied collectively for the first time in research on membrane filtration to provide detailed and comprehensive information of the flow and materials in the boundary layer of the membrane surface. The effect of the fluid shear rate on shear-induced diffusion of particles sizing 100, 600 and 800 nm and related particle deposition and membrane fouling was characterized. The results showed that membrane fouling by particle deposition could be mitigated by shear-induced diffusion that is affected by the shear rate and particle size. A high shear rate and large particle size resulted in a greater shear-induced diffusion, leading to less fouling (Sun et al., 2018; Hu et al., 2018; Wei et al., 2018; Meng and Li, 2019, 2020). • In addition, micro-LIF and micro-PIV were applied to investigate particle deposition on the patterned membrane surface. For the first time, fluid vortexes introduced by the surface patterns were directly visualized, which validated the prediction from the CFD simulations. The results showed that the growth of the particle deposition layer onto the micro-patterned membrane was much slower than that on the non-patterned membrane. This high shear rate in the micro-turbulence region was effective in disturbing the accumulation and attachment of particles on the membrane surface and facilitating the detachment of the particles from the membrane surface, resulting in much less fouling on the patterned membrane surface than the non-patterned one. Therefore, membrane modification with the surface patterning is shown to be a promising approach for membrane fouling control (Hu et al., 2018; Meng and Li, 2019, 2020).

17208515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208515.value: • As the deficiency of the conventional film theory model has been revealed and shear-induced diffusion also plays an important role in back diffusion of the materials, a more comprehensive model may be developed that incorporates various transport mechanisms and takes into account local hydrodynamic conditions. The functions and relevant parameters in the model can be determined from the experimental tests with the assistance of micro-LIF and micro-PIV. • As particle deposition is affected by the patterned membrane surface, variation of the surface patterns (e.g., pattern shape and configuration) and the resulting local hydraulic conditions can be further determined. The effect of various membrane surface patterning on the CP formation and membrane fouling control can be evaluated in great details by the micro-LIF and micro-PIV systems. • The optimization of the pattern features of the membrane and hydraulic conditions may be determined to eliminate particle deposition and the resulting membrane fouling. In addition, chemical surface coating can also be incorporated with membrane surface patterning to achieve a better fouling mitigation result.

17208515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208515.value: Concentration polarization (CP) and membrane fouling remain to be a major problem for the application of membrane filtration in water industry. The formation and development of CP and membrane fouling is closely related to the hydraulic conditions in crossflow filtration. However, a lack of real-time detection tools makes it difficult to characterize the CP and fouling dynamics near the membrane surface. In this study, non-invasive laser-based techniques, i.e., micro-LIF and micro-PIV, were applied for the first time to investigate the CP details and initial membrane fouling during crossflow ultrafiltration. The reversible, highly dynamic nature of CP and its sensitive response to the filtration conditions were investigated and validated. The effect of the fluid shear on shear-induced diffusion of particles of different sizes and its impact on the particle deposition were further studied. The mechanism of the patterned membrane surface on the CP control and fouling mitigation was also validated. The collective use of the advanced visualization techniques is proven to be a powerful tool to provide detailed information for investigation of the dynamic membrane filtration process. The findings will help develop more effective membrane strategies for effective membrane fouling control.

17209815.label: Project Objectives
17209815.value: Develop an efficient method for processing and classifying sketched boundary curves. Study the existence of surfaces interpolating given boundary curves as curvature lines. Develop a new surfacing method based on matching the curvature tensor of a surface to a guiding cross field derived from user-sketched curves.

17209815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209815.value: Sketch-based surface modeling is an important technology for shape design in computer graphics. Here the designer uses a computer interface to sketch curves as boundary curves or other guiding features, such as silhouettes, and then has the computer generate a surface shape to interpolate or follow the sketched curves. In this project we focus on the problem of generating surfaces from user-provided sketched curves in 3D. The motivation for our research is the observation that a designer often wishes to sketch the lines of curvatures to convey the surface shape. None of the existing methods are capable of creating surfaces from sketched curves with the required control on the curvature lines. We will develop theory and efficient methods for supporting sketch-based surface modeling with the unique ability of accommodating the designer's control on curvature lines of the surface to be designed. Specifically, we will develop two surface generation methods, using the triangle mesh surface representation to allow desired generality. Our methods will be the first to allow explicit and intuitive control on the lines of curvatures in interactive surface design, thus greatly enhancing the capability of design tools for surface modeling. 基于草图的曲面造型是计算机图形学中一项重要的造型技术。在建模过程中，设计人员先利用交互式界面绘制出曲线作为目标模型的边界曲线或是模型的外形特征，如物体的轮廓，再应用相关的算法依照草图上的曲线簇或是对这些曲线进行插值生成曲面形状。本项目主要研究如何利用用户提供的三维草图曲线生成相应的曲面模型。我们进行这一研究的动机是在建模过程中观察到，设计者在表达曲面形状时绘制的曲线通常含有曲面的曲率信息，而目前尚没有成熟的方法可以从草图中的曲线提取出曲率信息来生成相应的曲面。 我们将研究基于草图的曲面造型理论和有效方法，该建模过程将以设计者给出的曲面曲率线作为依据和引导。具体来讲，我们将开发两种曲面造型算法，并使用三角网格表示曲面以满足所需的普适性。在交互曲面设计中，我们的算法将是首个使用在曲率线进行直观建模的方法。这将成为曲面造型中强有力的设计工具。

17209815.value: All the three objectives have been accomplished successfully, and published in a series of three SIGGRAPH papers, based on the main idea of using curvature lines for sketch-based modeling of free-form surface. Note: The first paper was done after the submission of the proposal and was accepted before the proposal was funded (which is a span of 10 months), so the funding information could not be contained on the paper. The GRF funding is acknowledged in the next two papers.

Improve the current modeling practice for dispersion and source apportionment of vehicular pollutants in the policy innovation perspective.

17210115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210115.value: Urbanization substantially modifies surface features that changes the source nature and dispersion mechanism of ground-level pollutants. Vehicles are major pollutant sources in cities. Apart from primary pollutants, tailpipe exhaust includes a range of chemically reactive species and semi-volatile organic compounds (SVOCs) that evolve into (often more harmful) secondary pollutants once emitted into the urban atmospheric boundary layer (ABL). Early-stage pollutant dispersion from a tailpipe can be explained by the free-shear turbulent jet flows (micro scale). Afterward, the motions of pollutant jet plume are governed by the prevailing ABL flows, leading to the subsequent mixing and removal in a longer timescale. The current industrial practice of dispersion modeling, which assumes line-source vehicular exhaust and inert tracer, likely overlooks the key micro-scale jet-plume dynamics. Besides, pollution chemistry and SVOC microphysics are rarely addressed that could impose uncertainties into the air quality studies at pedestrian level and even in other scales. To bridge the aforementioned knowledge gap, this project is conceived to elucidate the physics and chemistry of vehicular exhaust in urban areas. Unlike most of the existing studies, we will specifically look into the micro-scale processes in the tailpipe jet plume (near-field) and their implication to the subsequent pollutant dispersion over urban areas in larger length scales (far-field). As a pilot attempt, idealized sources, hypothetical street-canyon urban morphology, generalized chemistry mechanism of gaseous pollutants and simplified SVOC vapor/aerosol microphysics will be employed to address the core scientific question: “How the configurations of tailpipe, vehicular exhaust and urban buildings collectively affect the dispersion, secondary pollutant production and street-level air quality at micro scale”. In particular, we attempt to innovate the current empirical parameterization of vehicular pollutant dispersion in order to handle the tight coupling among dynamics, physics and chemistry in the complicated near- and far-field processes. A complementary solution approach consisting of experiments and computer modeling will be sought for a fundamental knowledge base. Sensitivity tests will be conducted using the large-eddy simulation (LES) codes, LESChem and LES-SVOC, to constitute an in-depth understanding. Measurements for jets and in wind tunnels will be conducted, facilitating data verification and interpretation. Source apportionment will also be performed, initiating our research effort in source recovering. Street-level air quality is a key component for the life quality of urban inhabitants. This project will serve the scientific community by knowledge advancement and modeling innovation. It will also help society by effectuate source-level environmental management for improved air quality. 城市化進程顯著改變地面表面特徵繼而影響污染物的來源性質和分散機制。車輛是城市主要的污染源。除了初級污染物，汽車尾氣排氣包括一系列化學反應性物種和半揮發性有機化合物（SVOCs），其演變成次級污染物（通常更有害的）排放到城市大氣邊界層（ABL）。尾氣排氣早期污染物擴散可由自由剪切湍流噴流（微觀尺度）來解釋。之後，污染物射流卷流的運動由大氣邊界層管轄，導致隨後的一個較長的時間尺度的污染物混合和除去機制。目前的工業實踐擴散模型，即假設線源汽車廢氣和惰性示踪劑，可能會忽視關鍵性的微觀噴射羽動態。此外，較少涉及的污染化學和半揮發性有機化合物的微觀，會增加空氣質量的研究在人行的水平，甚至在其他的尺度伽不確定性。 為了彌補上述的知識差距，這個項目的初衷是闡明車輛尾氣的物理和化學在城市地區。與大多數現有的研究中，我們將具體考慮在排氣管噴射羽（近場）和它們的含義，以市區上空隨後的污染物擴散在更大的尺度（遠場）的微觀過程。作為試點嘗試，理想化的來源，假設街道峽谷城市形態，氣態污染物和簡化半揮發性有機化合物蒸汽廣義化學機理/氣溶膠微將被用來解決核心科學問題：“尾氣，機動車尾氣和城市建築如何配置共同影響分散，二次污染物的生產和路旁的空氣質量在微觀尺度“。特別是，我們試圖創新車輛污染物擴散的當前經驗參數，以處理好動態，物理和化學的緊密結合，在複雜的近場和遠場的進程。互補的解決方案的方法包括實驗和計算機模擬將尋求一個基本的知識基礎。敏感性測試將採用大渦模擬（LES）的代碼，LESChem和LES-半揮發性有機化合物，構成一個深入的了解進行。測量飛機和在風洞中會進行，便於數據驗證和數據解釋。源分配也將完成，開始我們的研究工作在源代碼中恢復過來。 路邊空氣質量是城市居民的生活質量的重要組成部分。該項目將有助於科學界通過知識進步和建模創新。這也將有助於社會所招致的源代碼級的環境管理，改善空氣質量。

17210115.label: Realisation of objectives
17210115.value: The project objectives are addressed to different extent. The methodology and the difficulties encountered are detailed below: Objective #1 - Use LES and laboratory experiments to study the nonlinear coupling among flow dynamics, pollution chemistry and SVOC microphysics in jet plume. 90% achieved Mathematical modeling (large-eddy simulation; LES) and laboratory experiments (wind tunnel measurements) were used to examine the flows, pollutant chemistry and semi-volatile organic compounds (SVOCs) microphysics. Flows and dispersion in urban areas were focused so pollutant dispersion from point/line sources in hypothetical urban areas (fabricated by ribs or cubes) were employed in both LES and wind tunnel measurements. The aerodynamic resistance over the hypothetical urban areas was controlled by the density of the roughness elements. Only isothermal conditions were considered because of the near-surface dynamics and the short time/length scales (compared with those in the atmosphere). The advantage of mathematical modelling is the full control of all the parameters. Finite volume (FV) method was used to discretize the spatial domain of different configurations of roughness elements. Tens millions of FV cells were used so the near-wall dynamics was well-resolved. The time domain was integrated implicitly with a small Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy (CFL) for numerical stability. The small-time increment facilitates the use of fast Fourier transform (FFT) to study the dynamics in the frequency domain. The refined spatio-temporal resolution collectively helps understand how wind shear modifies the transport processes over rough surfaces (urban areas). A range of surface roughness was tested by control the separation of ribs in crossflows in which the drag coefficient was comparable to that of real urban areas (measured in wind tunnel experiments elsewhere). Transport models of passive tracer, gaseous chemistry (NOx-O3 and NOx-O3-VOCs; where NOx , O3 and VOCs, are nitrogen oxides, ozone and volatile organic compounds, respectively) and particle were integrated into the LES as well. The wind tunnel experiments mainly served to validate the LES. The wind tunnel (3,000 mm (length) x 550 mm (width) x 550 mm (height)) in the Department of Mechanical Engineering, The University of Hong Kong was used. It is an open-loop, isothermal unit and the wind speed was up to 15 m/sec. In addition to ribs in crossflows, cubes were used in the wind tunnel experiments (to determine whether there are any differences induced by the roughness element types). Apart from flow visualization, the wind speeds were measured by constant-temperature (CT) hot-wire anemometry (HWA) so the signal data were recorded at 2,000 Hz. In addition to the gases and particles, laboratory-scale tracer dispersion using water vapor was developed in this project that can mimic gas dispersion provided that the tracer concentration is not too high (E-03 by volume) and the wind speeds are not too slow (around 10 m/sec). The results of LES and wind tunnel measurements agree well. This objective is not fully achieved. From the research team’s point of view, more comprehensive laboratory experiments, in particular the combinations of reactive gases and particles, should be employed to complement the LES findings as well as strengthen the basis for conclusion. The extensive sensitivity tests will take a long time. Objective #2 - Elucidate the characteristic street-level air quality and pollutant removal mechanism in urban environment at micro scale. 100% achieved The results obtained in this project help formulate the removal mechanism of aged air and pollutants from urban areas. Apart from the conventional understanding of street-level air quality and pollutant characteristics (e.g. higher wind speeds improve air quality and higher building density weakens pollutant removal). Generally, it was found that street-level air quality improves with increasing urban roughness. It is noteworthy that high building density does not necessarily mean high urban roughness. Roughness increases wind shear together wind turbulence kinetic energy (TKE) that in turn augment the pollutant dilution and improve street-level the air quality. Mathematically, the turbulence intensity at the roof-level of roughness elements is proportional to the root of drag coefficient. In fact the above characteristics can be explained in details by turbulent transport so as to formulate the fundamental pollutant removal mechanism. From the fluid mechanics point of view, the flows decelerate and simultaneously the updrafts carry the aged air with pollutants away from the street level. This is the event of ejection (Q2) in quadrant analysis. The flows cannot decelerate all the times, otherwise the winds stop. The winds accelerate to resume the speeds and kinetic energy. At the same time, the free-stream fresh air entrains into the street level, diluting the pollutants. This is the event of sweep (Q4) in quadrant analysis. The flows switch back and forth between ejection and sweep that constitutes the pollutant removal mechanism from street level in urban areas. The transport processes described above also help develop the pollutant plume dispersion. Taking the tracer dispersion after a ground-level line source as an example, it largely follows the Gaussian shape. Interestingly, the dispersion is a function of the surface roughness. Mathematically, it was found that the (vertical) dispersion coefficient is proportional to the fourth root of draft coefficient and the root of streamwise distance. It offers a quantitative estimate to the pollutant dilution over urban areas. Dispersion of reactive pollutant after a line source in crossflows was attempted by the LES as well. The case of ozone titration was investigated by setting up the dispersion of nitric oxide (NO) from a ground-level line source in the flow stream with background ozone (O3). The reactive plume dispersion generally follows the Gaussian form except adjacent to the ground surface. Besides, the plume coverage and the reaction rate increase with increasing surface roughness. It was also found that the vertical profiles of reactive pollutant concentrations can be represented well by the Gamma distribution. Objective #3 - Improve the current modeling practice for dispersion and source apportionment of vehicular pollutants in the policy innovation perspective. 100% achieved Objectives #1 and #2 offer scientific evidence to improve the current modelling practice of pollutant dispersion over urban areas. Drag or drag coefficient are commonly measured in wind engineering and wind load assessment for property development projects. It can then be used with the mathematical formulae newly proposed in this project to estimate the performance of street-level ventilation and pollutant removal. The solution can improve the prediction reliability by modifying mildly the current practice so that the interruption is minimal. The new mathematical equations are handy methods that can be easily interpreted by non-engineering professionals.

17210115.label: Major findings and research outcome
17210115.value: Both mathematical modelling and laboratory experiments were used to examine the dispersion of vehicular pollutant (jet plume) in urban environment (rough surfaces). Major findings included how the flows and transport processes in response to the urban roughness and pollutant source configuration. Rougher surfaces favor street-level ventilation as well as pollutant removal. It was found that the street-level ventilation can be measured indirectly in terms of the drag coefficient of urban areas. Mathematically, the roof-level ventilation is proportional to the root of drag coefficient [1]. Analogously, plume (from a line source in crossflows) coverage enlarges such that the dispersion coefficient is proportional to the fourth root of drag coefficient [4]. Similar to passive, inert pollutants, reactive pollutant plume dispersion (nitric oxide by ozone titration) follows largely the Gaussian form. Its plume coverage and chemical reaction rate increase with increasing surface roughness [2]. Increasing TKE enhances the mixing of NO and O3 near the ground surface that produces more nitrogen dioxide (NO2) [3]. The reactive plume no long follows the Gaussian form. Instead, the Gamma distribution represents well the NO distribution that serves a handily model for reactive plume dispersion [5]. From the turbulent transport point of view, the aforementioned pollutant transport in response to rough surfaces can be explained by quadrant analysis. Flow acceleration (entrainments) and deceleration (updrafts) are, respectively, the events of ejection (Q2) and sweep (Q4). Accelerating flows suppresses turbulence that drive fresh air downward to the street level. On the other hand, decelerating flows augments turbulence that purge aged air upward to the atmospheric boundary layer aloft. The switching back and forth between flow acceleration and deceleration suggests the basic mechanism for the pollutant removal from urban areas. The key question is how to optimize the performance of street-level ventilation and pollutant removal of urban areas. Flow deceleration purges street-level pollutants to higher level that eventually leads to stagnant air (calm wind). The slow flows should accelerate to resume the kinetic energy. Under this circumstance, building design that could promote frequent flow deceleration/acceleration, such as variation in building density and height, could be the measures to improve street-level ventilation and pollutant removal.

17210115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17210115.value: There are three major areas worthy to further develop and develop, as follows: #1. Continue the wind tunnel experiments to widen the scope of sensitivity tests. #2. Integrate chemistry mechanism other than NOx-O3 and NOx-O3-VOCs into the LES. #3. Instead of idealized urban areas, use the real urban morphology to test whether the theory formulated in this project is equally applicable.

17210115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17210115.value: Street-level ventilation and urban air quality are major concern nowadays because of the large number of inhabitants in dense built environment. Whereas, the fundamental understanding of the mechanism is rather limited. In this project, a complementation solution consisting of mathematical modeling and laboratory experiments showed that urban roughness generally enhances the removal of aged air and pollutants. Wind shear induced by urban areas extracts the energy needed from mean flows to turbulence, improving the pollutant mixing and dilution. Quantitatively, the roof-level ventilation and dispersion coefficient are proportional to the root and fourth root of the drag coefficient of urban areas. Proper building design, which encompasses the elements of urban roughness, thus could help improve street-level air quality in dense built environment. Drag coefficient is available from the wind engineering assessment of property development projects. The two proportionalities above are handy rules for architectural design. It is noteworthy that urban roughness eventually leads to stagnant flows. Instead, environmental design should be composed of diversified rough and smooth urban surfaces, such as building density and height variability, so the winds could exhibit a ranges of turbulence scales in addition to favorable wind breeze and speeds, promoting street-level ventilation and urban air quality.

17210615.value: 使用混合非易失性內存的多核容錯系統軟件

17210615.label: Project Objectives
17210615.value: Propose a new fault-tolerant multicore architecture fabricated from the next-generation non-volatile memory (e.g., STT-RAM) used as last level cache (LLC), on-chip programmable scratchpad memory, and off-chip memory. Revamp the Linux operating system to exploit such special hybridized memory hierarchy with both caches and programmable scratchpads SRAM and STT-MRAM. A novel persistent process model and a persistent page table design are proposed to help provide native fault tolerance for program execution against transient and crash failures. Explore new data affinity techniques tailored to big data computing along the abovementioned memory hierarchy. In particular, we propose anti-caching of datasets whose access via the conventional cacheable datapath could cause serious cache pollution. The anti-caching mechanism exploits the on-chip programmable memory. 17210615.label: Realisation of objectives
17210615.value: Objective (1), 100% achieved. We have modified Gem5, a full‐system time‐accurate simulator to add the STT‐RAM main memory and programmable on‐chip memory into hardware architecture. The simulated chip consists of 2GB DRAM, 2GB STT‐RAM and 1MB programmable on‐chip memory. The programmable on‐chip memory is added next to L3 cache, and is shared by all cores. To simulate the STT‐RAM main memory, we add a new STT‐RAM memory class similar to DRAM in Gem5. Gem5 stores a copy of STT‐RAM memory as a file into a ram disk of host OS. For every modification of STT‐RAM memory, Gem5 writes the modification into the ram disk copy. Hence, even if we inject a hardware failure in Gem5, the content of STT‐RAM memory is still stored in the ram disk of the host machine. When Gem5 starts, it will check the ram disk and recover the content of the last‐time execution. In this way, we simulate the non‐volatile behavior of STT‐RAM. To simulate the programmable on‐chip memory, we add a new STT‐RAM memory class. Besides the non‐volatile feature, we provide hardware interfaces for programmable on‐chip memory to operating system. Simulation results show little overhead for runtime logging (mostly less than 5%) and short recovery time (mostly less than 25%). These measurements on various levels of memory hierarchy are useful for us to design the proposed software in the later stages. Objective (2), 100% achieved. Based on the simulation results, we revamp the Linux operating system with emulated scratchpads SRAM and STT‐MRAM on a 64‐core AMD machine. SIMPO consists of kernel‐ and user‐space components, namely Persistent Object Manager (POM) and SIMPO Library. POM extends the Linux kernel to drive and manage the hybrid memory. SIMPO Lib provides the API for users to interface with the POM for building fault‐tolerant programs. The SIMPO Manager is essentially an extension of the existing Linux virtual memory system. SIMPO Manager uses the existing Linux page allocator. In Linux, physical memory pages are managed through the zone mechanism and every zone is composed of page frames. A page frame is allocated from a particular memory zone in kernel space called “NVM” zone with a new flag “GFP NVM” to indicate that pages should be allocated from NVM zone. SIMPO Manager maintains a three‐level page table in NVM. Each NVM directory entry records the page table entry address. SIMPO Manager encapsulates PO operations as POMalloc, PORealloc and POFree. SIMPO Lib provides a way for user to create Persistent Objects from the POBase class or from a class extended from POBase. Every PO is stored in NVM and provides a root pointer for programmers to access all data within that PO. To protect a PO from common failures like power loss, all access to POs should be done within a Persistent Function (PF) defined using the SIMPO Lib’s API. The library runs every PF with a redo log maintained internally to guarantee ACID semantics. Objective (3), 100% achieved. We have designed and implemented a software‐controlled on‐chip memory (PSM) based on the Gem5 simulator. PSM has a memory controller which is similar to the DRAM controller. The controller connects to L2 cache bus which is a cache‐coherent bus. Via this new memory controller, PSM could operate memory requests from the CPU cores. Currently, both bus‐based and directory‐based MESI protocols are supported. Data allocated on PSM is exclusive to L2 cache, and is only cached in L1 cache. As PSM is programmable and can be controlled by the user, the anti‐caching is realized in software. Simulation result on Linpack benchmark has shown a 37% improvement using PSM. We further evaluate PSM and anti‐caching on real Linux machines with a wide range of micro‐benchmarks and application benchmarks comprising machine learning, compute‐intensive and database workloads. Performance results on a 64‐core AMD machine with an emulated programmable STT‐RAM on DRAM show that SIMPO incurs negligible overheads, mostly lower than 5%. For highly‐threaded big data applications, SIMPO improves data locality and concurrency and can achieve up to 2.35x speedup than the native execution without SIMPO. When tested with Berkeley DB, SIMPO even improves the performance by up to 2.03x over the application’s native transactional persistence implementation. The results are very encouraging. Objective (4), 100% achieved. SIMPO also features a novel double‐copy RCU (read‐copy‐update) logging technique based on a new checkpoint technique, called “buffered‐double‐copy” (BDC). Based on the value logging, we design a fine-grained differential logging scheme which is able to flush non-continuous dirty cache-line granularity data to NVRAM to guarantee persistence. Unlike previous work that persistent updated data in block-granularity, we effectively reduce the size of log data written in NVRAM. We show that BDC checkpointing achieves up to 1.4x speedup than copy‐on‐write (COW) checkpointing. To improve the scalability of SIMPO upon performing the recovery operations, we designed a lightweight read‐copy‐update (RCU) lock in Linux kernel. The new NUMA-aware lock can achieve 3.7 times faster than RCL lock and 17 times faster than POSIX mutex on 64-core AMD machine, especially under high contentions situations. The detailed design and performance results were reported in our IEEE TPDC 2017 paper “Scalable Adaptive NUMA-aware Lock”. Objective (5), 100% achieved. We design a programming model that classifies functions to be applied on the persistent objects (POs) into “deferrable” type and “instant” type. Deferrable functions can only modify data of the persistent object or local variables without returning values, e.g. mutator methods. Instant functions are operations (e.g. print()) that expose or output values (to a storage system) and will be executed in SIMPO immediately. Instant function will activate a system thread to inspect the pending logs, wake up slave threads of SIMPO and assign parallel Deferred functions to different slave threads to maximize the execution concurrency. We provide a user library consisting of a C++ library with the POBase class, an automatic deferrable function classification tool and a code refactoring tool. The classification tool distinguishes Deferrable and Instant functions by checking whether a function only modifies data of the persistent object or function local variables without returning values. The refactoring tool performs source‐to‐source code transformation to ease the programming effort. In our recent NVSM 2018 paper “NVCL: Exploiting NVRAM in Cache-Line Granularity Differential Logging”, we ported SIMPO on the FUSE ﬁle system on a Linux machine with NVDIMM to build a new in-memory data persistence system. Our log recording and checkpointing scheme can be effectively optimized towards NVRAM, mitigating its long write latency through write-combining and consolidated flushing techniques. NVCL can save up to 127× NVRAM writes and achieve 84% speedup comparing to Redis append-only-ﬁle logging mechanism. NVCL can also reduce up to 50% NVRAM writes and achieves 15% speedup over state-of-the-art logging mechanisms.

17210615.label: Major findings and research outcome
17210615.value: To achieve data persistence, state-of-the-art techniques apply logging and checkpointing mechanisms. Log-based systems can be further classified into two types, namely value logging and function logging. For every function or transaction of the persistent data, systems with value logging record the updated data, while other systems utilize function logging (a.k.a. operation logging) and checkpointing. In this work, we propose the design of in-memory object persistence frameworks leveraging the new memory architecture embedded with hybrid DRAM/STT-MRAM main memory and programmable on-chip STT-MRAM. Our results validated the idea of the new memory system design using on-chip STT-MRAM for both types of log-based systems. We conclude our work with two major findings and outcomes: (1) Scalable in-memory persistent object framework with function logging. We have presented the design and implementation of SIMPO, a scalable in-memory object persistence framework with function logging. Our approach is different from traditional persistence frameworks that adopted data replication schemes for fault tolerance. SIMPO supports in-memory persistence with streamlined function logging to exploit the byte-addressable NVRAM for fast persistence and recovery in a user-transparent manner. We design a deferrable execution model to make the best use of function logging. In particular, our programming model enables a novel Transactionized Function Grouping (XFG) technique, which coalesces a group of functions as a transaction. The deferrable execution model provides better opportunities for optimization, e.g., maximize the execution concurrency and exploit optimal data locality. Persistent objects are made more durable through a buffered-double-copy checkpointing mechanism that effectively masks the slow writes of NVRAM. The results have been published in our TACO 2018 paper: “SIMPO: A Scalable In-Memory Persistent Object Framework Using NVRAM for Reliable Big Data Computing”. (2) In-memory data persistence system with cache-line granularity differential logging. We find that value logging is more suitable than function logging for Redis (an in-memory NoSQL database). NVCL generates only the dirty cache-line bytes of updated persistent data. Due to the minimum unit of NVRAM flush is a cache-line, NVCL minimizes the value logging size. We evaluated NVCL on real Linux machines with a wide range of micro‐benchmarks and application benchmarks (PostMark) comprising machine learning, compute‐intensive and database workloads. The experiments show that NVCL can only record 0.7% log size of Redis AOF mechanism and 50% log size of state-of-the-art logging mechanism NVWAL. Key results were reported in our NVSM 2018 paper “NVCL: Exploiting NVRAM in Cache-Line Granularity Differential Logging”.

17210615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17210615.value: STT-MRAM has the potential to become a leading storage technology due to its higher densities, low power consumption and reduced cost as compared to conventional NVRAM technologies. The recent STT-MRAM chips (e.g., Everspin’s pilot production of 28nm 1 Gb STT-MRAM memory in 2019) demonstrated interface speeds comparable to DRAM, with DDR4 interfaces. With volume production, it could soon bring advanced persistent memory capability to modern data center storage and computing applications. In our future work, we plan to enhance the code refactoring tool to automatically detect and classify functions into defer and instance functions, thus relieve programmers’ effort. We will extend SIMPO and integrate it to large-scale big data computing platforms, such as Spark or Flink, to support high-speed recovery with the use of the STT-MRAM enabled memory systems. We will also consider to extend our work to IoT devices with embedded STT-MRAM as the replacement for flash and embedded SRAM. Our new design should address the energy-efficiency issues. Particularly, we will design low-overhead checkpointing and recovery, rapid transition between different power modes, and recovery from a wide range of fault conditions.

17210615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17210615.value: Emerging non-volatile memory (NVRAM) technologies pose revolutionary impacts on today’s operating system and system software tool-chain design. Our work investigated the new design of operating system and programming model which could effectively exploit memory hardware innovations for better support of reliable big data applications. We proposed a new multicore architecture with a two-level memory hierarchy (on-chip and off-chip) containing both non-volatile SST-MRAM and volatile SRAM/DRAM. We store data in STT-MRAM for fault tolerance and fast recovery, while DRAM as a unified buffer for caching working memory. We proposed a novel double‐copy RCU (read‐copy‐update) logging technique based on a new checkpoint technique, called “buffered‐double‐copy” (BDC). With BDC, we could reduce the number of memory operations and hide NVRAM’s slow writes. Simulation results based on Gem5 demonstrated the feasibility of proposed solutions. Experimental results on a 64-core Linux server also outperformed several state-of-the-art persistence solutions. Our work redefined the programming interfaces for supporting fault tolerance for big data computing and suggested new operating system primitives while considering the non-volatility, byte-addressability of the next-generation NVRAM with choices of memory technologies applied at all levels: SRAM vs. MRAM, on-chip vs. off-chip, and cache vs. scratchpad.
