17210815.label: Realisation of objectives
17210815.value: For the 1st objective, a hybrid electromagnetic (EM) circuit simulator is proposed for incorporating multiport lumped circuit networks through their admittance matrices into the discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method. The admittance matrix in the Laplace domain can be derived analytically or obtained from network parameters such as s-parameters in the frequency domain. To convert frequency-dependent network parameters into the admittance matrix in the Laplace domain, the vector-fitting technique is employed to facilitate the mapping process. The computational domain of interest is split into two subdomains. One is the EM part solved by the DGTD, and another is the circuit part modeled by the basic I–V relationships in the time domain. The couplings between the EM and circuit parts happen at lumped ports where the port voltages and currents are solved via these coupled systems. Due to the local properties of DGTD operations, only small coupling matrix equation systems are involved. To further improve the efficiency, local time-stepping strategy is included. Both linear and nonlinear lumped devices, and subsystems could be analyzed through this method. For the 2nd objective, to study the EM wave propagations in the general materials, a scheme hybridizing discontinuous Galerkin time-domain and time-domain boundary integral (TDBI) methods for accurately analyzing transient electromagnetic scattering is proposed. Radiation condition is enforced using the numerical flux on the truncation boundary. The fields required by the flux are computed using the TDBI from equivalent currents introduced on a Huygens' surface enclosing the scatterer. The hybrid DGTDBI ensures that the radiation condition is mathematically exact and the resulting computation domain is as small as possible since the truncation boundary conforms to scatterer's shape and is located very close to its surface. Locally truncated domains can also be defined around each disconnected scatterer additionally reducing the size of the overall computation domain. Our nonlinear benchmarks demonstrated the accuracy and versatility of the proposed method are presented. We further studied the second-harmonic (SH) generation of nano particles, which is tremendously important for nonlinear sensing, microscopy, and communication systems. One of the great challenges of current designs is to enhance the SH signal and simultaneously tune its radiation direction with a high directivity. In this work, we harness a plasmonic hybridization mechanism together with a special selection rule governing the SH radiation to achieve the high-intensity and tunable-direction emission by a metallic particle-in-cavity nanoantenna (PIC-NA). The nanoantenna is modelled using our self-consistent nonlinear PMCHWT method, which considers the depletion of pump waves. The proposed PIC-NA results in a significantly larger SH conversion efficiency compared to existing literature. The main beam of the radiation pattern can be steered over a wide angle by tuning the particle’s position. For the 3rd objective, with the purpose of avoiding very fine mesh cells in the proximity of a thin wire loaded with nonlinear components, the modified telegrapher’s equations (MTEs) are employed to describe the thin wire voltage and current distributions, which consequently results in reduced number of unknowns and augmented Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy (CFL) number. As hyperbolic systems, both the MTEs and the Maxwell’s equations are solved by the discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD)method. In realistic situations, the thin wires could be either driven or loaded by circuit networks. The thin wire–circuit interface performs as a boundary condition for the thin wire solver, where the thin wire voltage and current used for the incoming flux evaluation involved in the DGTD-analyzed MTEs are not available. To obtain this voltage and current, an auxiliary current flowing through the thin wire–circuit interface is introduced at each interface. Corresponding auxiliary equations derived from the invariable property of characteristic variable for hyperbolic systems are developed and solved together with the circuit equations established by the modified nodal analysis (MNA) modality. Furthermore, in order to characterize the field and thin wire interactions, a weighted electric field and a volume current density are added into the MTEs and Maxwell–Ampere’s law equation, respectively. And in the 2-D/3-D hybrid discontinuous Galerkin timedomain (DGTD) method, it is efficient to deal with structures that contain elements capable of 2-D simplification. To separate 2-D elements from 3-D ones, a criterion for approximation error manipulation is required. However, in the latest reported technique, this kind of criterion is derived from the causality principle and the Courant–Freidrichs–Lewy constraint, and thus is indirect and inessential to 2-D simplification. As a result, some elements capable of 2-D simplification are unnecessarily flagged as 3-D ones, deteriorating efficiency dramatically. Moreover, controlling absolute error, the traditional criterion is not flexible for structures with complex mode distribution. In this work, a novel criterion is proposed. Compared with the traditional one, this new criterion controls comparative error instead of absolute error, thus enhancing accuracy and flexibility. Besides, for the time adaptive updating algorithm, the proposed criterion is derived directly from the discretized matrix equations of the DGTD method, rendering it straightforward and efficient. For the 4th objective, a novel hybrid field-circuit simulation method is proposed for transient heterogeneous electromagnetic simulations. It adopts the discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method and behavioral macromodel trained by artificial neural network to analyze the electromagnetic structure and circuit network, respectively. Due to the feature of DGTD method and behavioral macromodel, the proposed method can handle not only electromagnetic structures with complex geometries and materials but also manage circuits with unknown internal details. It provides a new approach that has the trainable accuracy to meet today’s IP projection requests. It is also the first time for DGTD algorithm to work with the behavior model based on our literature searches. It is well known that the graphene material demonstrates spatial dispersion properties, i.e., its conductivity is nonlocal and a function of spectral wavenumber (momentum operator) q. To account for effects of spatial dispersion on transmission of high-speed signals along graphene nanoribbon (GNR) interconnects, a new discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) algorithm is proposed. The atomically thick GNR is modeled using a nonlocal transparent surface impedance boundary condition (SIBC) incorporated into the DGTD scheme. Since the conductivity is a complicated function of q (and one cannot find an analytical Fourier transform pair between q and spatial differential operators), an exact time-domain SIBC model cannot be derived. To overcome this problem, the conductivity is approximated by its Taylor series in spectral domain under low-q assumption. This approach permits expressing the time domain SIBC in the form of a second-order partial differential equation (PDE) in current density and electric field intensity. Regarding to the temporal dispersion effects, the auxiliary differential equation method is utilized to eliminate the expensive temporal convolutions. Volterra series (VS) representation is a powerful mathematical model for nonlinear systems. We proposed a new systematic approach that enables a convenient extraction of Volterra kernels from nonlinear X-parameters. A concise and general representation of the output response due to arbitrary number of input tones is given. The relationship between Volterra kernels and X-parameters is explicitly formulated. An efficient frequency sweep scheme and an output frequency indexing scheme are provided. The least square linear regression method is employed to separate different orders of Volterra kernels at the same frequency, which leads to the obtained Volterra kernels complete. The proposed method is systematic and general-purpose.

17210815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17210815.value: A new hybrid electromagnetic (EM) circuit simulation method is proposed for incorporating multiport lumped circuit networks for the discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method. It takes the modified nodal analysis into the parasitic DGTD solving process to handle complex linear and nonlinear problems. The admittance matrix in the Laplace domain can be derived analytically or obtained from network parameters in the frequency domain. Due to the local properties of DGTD operations, only small coupling matrix equation systems are involved. To further improve the efficiency, local time-stepping strategy is included. Both linear and nonlinear subsystems and new materials could be analyzed through the proposed DGTD methods and a series new algorithms we developed for DGTD. We developed a new a novel neural network based behavior model for for transient heterogeneous electromagnetic simulations that commonly have a mix of linearities and nonlinearities. It adopts the discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method and behavioral macromodel trained by artificial neural network to analyze the electromagnetic structure and circuit network, respectively. Due to the feature of DGTD method and behavioral macromodel, the proposed method can handle not only electromagnetic structures with complex geometries and materials but also manage circuits with unknown internal details. It provides a new approach that has the trainable accuracy to meet today’s IP projection requests. It is also the first time for DGTD algorithm to work with the behavior model based on our literature searches. To enhance the nonlinear second-harmonic signal in nano materials and simultaneously tune its radiation direction with a high directivity, we harnessed a plasmonic hybridization mechanism together with a special selection rule governing the SH radiation to achieve the high-intensity and tunable-direction emission by a metallic particle-in-cavity nanoantenna (PIC-NA). The nanoantenna is modelled with a first-principle, self-consistent boundary element method, which considers the depletion of pump waves. The giant second-harmonic enhancement arises from a hybridized gap plasmon resonance between the small particle and the large cavity that functions as a concentrator and reflector. Centrosymmetry breaking of the PIC-NA not only modifies the gap plasmon mode boosting the SH signal, but also redirects the SH wave with a unidirectional emission. The PIC-NA has a significantly larger SH conversion efficiency compared to existing literature. The main beam of the radiation pattern can be steered over a wide angle by tuning the particle’s position.

17210815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17210815.value: Considering modern electronic vehicles (EV) are more electromagnetic complex compared to before, their electromagnetic environment characterization becomes more challenging. The heterogeneous linearity and nonlinearity are fundamental features that have to be properly handled to balance the accuracy and cost in the analysis. The research outputs from this project are great foundations for studies along this direction. Meanwhile, a teamwork with EV research teams will be a fruitful collaboration to make the future steps more effective and efficient. PI would pursue this direction at the proper time in the future.

17210815.value: The novel discontinuous Galerkin’s time domain methods and relevant computational electromagnetics algorithms have been proposed to enable the characterization of the electromagnetic coupling and scattering characterization when the nonlinearity presents. It is applicable to highs speed integrated circuits analysis such as signal integrity and power integrity, scientific exploration such as nonlinear optics and spintronics, etc.

17211115.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17211115.value: 基于微流控技术制备形貌、尺寸均一的栓塞微粒

17211115.label: Project Objectives
17211115.value: To develop an effective microfluidic approach for a direct on-chip precision fabrication of uniform embolic microspheres; the polydispersity index of fabricated particles, defined as the standard deviation of the particle diameter divided by the mean diameter, is less than 2%; To reliably correlate processing parameters and particle morphology; To develop and characterize three kinds of uniform embolic particles using polyvinyl alcohol, gelatin, and sodium alginate.
rows: To develop an effective microfluidic approach for a direct on-chip precision fabrication of uniform embolic microspheres; the polydispersity index of fabricated particles, defined as the standard deviation of the particle diameter divided by the mean diameter, is less than 2%;
To reliably correlate processing parameters and particle morphology;
To develop and characterize three kinds of uniform embolic particles using polyvinyl alcohol, gelatin, and sodium alginate.

17211115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17211115.value: 栓塞疗法是一种通过有目的性的引进栓塞药剂，选择性地堵塞血管来达到治疗目的的非外科手术性的、创伤小的治疗方法，目前已经成为现代介入疗法的一个重要分支。这种方法被广泛应用于器质性疾病的治疗，包括肿瘤，出血和血管异常的治疗等。为了获得良好的临床效果和减少并发症，临床上亟需形状、尺寸均一的栓塞微粒。迄今为止，由于传统制造技术在设计栓塞微粒的形状、尺寸和微结构上的缺陷，商品化的栓塞微粒的功效远远不能达到令人满意的效果。 本项目拟采用一种精准的技术来制备形状、尺寸均一的栓塞微粒。 其关键在于用基于高分子交联聚合反应的“自下而上”的微流控系统来代替传统制造加工的“自上而下”的宏观、粗放的大体系。该技术利用玻璃毛细管微流控装置来制备可固化为微粒的微液滴，充分利用了微流控技术对微小体积流体的精确操控和对液滴形成的精准控制的能力。通过添加交联剂来实现液滴的固化，交联剂是在液滴形成时被精准的加到每一个液滴中，从而确保每一个液滴都能单独固化。上述方法能够高度可控地制备微粒，从而保证得到非常均一的微粒。毛细管微流控装置圆形的管道横截面，以及根据热力学的最小表面能原理，都确保能形成完美球形形状的液滴和尺寸均一的微粒。因此，所制备出的微粒的形状和尺寸都非常均一。 本项目的目标是将这一具有潜在发展前景的微流控技术应用于栓塞微粒的制造加工，来实现微粒形貌的精准可控并找出过程参数和微粒形貌之间的关系。本项目将针对聚乙烯醇,明胶和海藻酸钠这三种已商品化的具有生物兼容性的材料，来开发和表征相关制备方法。 本项目将提供一种可制备和开发高品质微粒的方法，以此改变栓塞微粒的传统制备技术，使之能更有效地用于靶向栓塞。同时，也将为根据临床需求设计、定制特殊形貌的栓塞微粒提供一种新思路。此外，本项目所制备的创新型栓塞微粒，在治疗诸如子宫平滑肌瘤和肝癌等疾病时，其操作方式可控、精准、方便，也必将成为栓塞疗法的全新标准。

17211115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17211115.value: Embolization therapy is a nonsurgical, minimally invasive procedure that involves the selective occlusion of blood vessels by purposely introducing embolic agents. It has become a major branch of modern interventional therapy, its applications fundamental in treating a wide variety of conditions affecting different organs of the human body. To obtain good clinical outcomes and minimize complications, embolic particles uniform in shape and size are essential. To date, the functional outcomes of existing embolic particles have not been satisfactory due to the inadequacies of conventional fabrication approaches in engineering their shape, size and microstructures. An approach was developed for precise fabrication of embolic microparticles that are uniform in shape and size. The key is to replace the “top-down” bulk process used in conventional approaches with a “bottom-up” microfluidic process of polymer cross-linking. The approach uses a microfluidic device to generate droplets containing the particle material, exploiting the capability offered by microfluidics to precisely handle small fluid volumes and accurately control formation of droplets. Cross-linker solution is used for droplet solidification, and is injected into each individual droplet to ensure solidification at individual droplet level. These methods enable the generation of highly uniform particles overall.

17211215.label: Project Objectives
17211215.value: To develop methods allowing us to control the cell volume in a precise and programmable manner. To carefully examine the transmembrane ion transport in various cells under imposed volume regulation. To systematically explore the possibility of using imposed volume changes to selectively kill different cancer cells. To model the size evolution of cells induced by different volume-changing cues.
rows: To develop methods allowing us to control the cell volume in a precise and programmable manner.
To carefully examine the transmembrane ion transport in various cells under imposed volume regulation.
To systematically explore the possibility of using imposed volume changes to selectively kill different cancer cells.
To model the size evolution of cells induced by different volume-changing cues.

17211215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17211215.value: Cells must maintain their volume in order to perform biological duties and survive. Changes in the concentration of intracellular contents can profoundly affect protein functions, cause cell cycle delay and eventually lead to cell death. As such, it is conceivable that the behavior and fate of live cells can all be directed if we are able to control their size in a precise and programmable manner. Unfortunately, a method allowing us to do so is still lacking. Interestingly, our pilot studies have demonstrated that variations in the surrounding hydrostatic pressure and osmolarity can both induce volumetric deformation of cells. However, whether these initial clues can indeed lead to techniques we are looking for remains to be further explored. Our preliminary observations also suggested that a much higher death rate among nasopharyngeal cancer cells, compared to their normal counterparts, will be triggered by imposed volume changes. Furthermore, the activation of cross-membrane transport of sodium and potassium ions in cells appears to depend more on how (e.g., gradually or suddenly) the volume-changing cues are applied, rather than their amplitudes. Despite these interesting findings, it is unclear whether similar results will be obtained in other cell types or ion species, which clearly is a question of both fundamental and clinical importance. In this project, we plan to conduct a combined experimental and modeling study to address these unsettled issues. Specifically, on the basis of our preliminary investigations, methods enabling us to precisely control the size evolution of cells will be developed and optimized, in conjunction with simultaneous theoretical modeling taking into account realistic features of the problem. After that, the possibility of using these techniques to selectively kill different, including leukemia, nasopharyngeal, lung and colorectal, cancer cells as well as direct their transmembrane ion exchanges will be carefully and systematically explored. If successful, results from this project will unambiguously confirm or refute our primary hypothesis that the ion transport activity and death of living cells can all be regulated by imposed volume changes, and hence greatly enhance our basic understanding of the activation mechanisms of various ion channels. Findings here could also provide critical information for the development of new treatments for different cancers. Finally, the volume regulation methods to be developed in this study can serve as powerful tools for examining issues like the influence of molecular crowding on various cellular processes in the future. 細胞必須維持其體積，以便行使生物職責及生存。胞內物质濃度的變化可以深刻改变蛋白質的功能，引起細胞週期的延遲，並最終導致細胞死亡。因此，如果我們能夠对細胞體積进行精確和可編程的控制， 那对活細胞的行為和命運的引導就将成为可能。不幸的是，我們仍然缺乏一個這樣的方法。我們的試驗性研究表明，周圍环境的靜水壓或滲透壓的变化都可以改变細胞的體積。然而，這些初步的線索是否確實能夠变成我們正在尋找的技術還有待進一步确认。我們初步的觀察也表明，同正常细胞相比，體積的变化会在鼻咽癌細胞中导致高得多的死亡率。此外，鈉離子和鉀離子的細胞跨膜轉運的改变似乎更多地取決引起细胞體積變化的信号是如何被施加的 （逐步的或是突然的），而不是它們的幅度。儘管有這些有趣的發現，是否相似的結果也会在其他細胞或離子類型中被观测到这一對基礎和臨床都极其重要的問題仍然尚待解答。 在這個項目中，我們計劃進行實驗与模擬相结合的研究来解決這些懸而未決的問題。具體而言，在我們的初步研究的基礎上，使我們能夠精確控制細胞大小的方法将会被開發并優化。在此之後，使用這些技術来選擇性殺死不同癌细胞（包括白血病，鼻咽癌，肺癌和結腸直腸癌细胞）以及控制其跨膜離子交換的可行性將会被仔細和系統地探討。如果成功的話，從這個項目的結果將明確證實或證伪活細胞的離子運輸和死亡可以通過对其體積的調控来加以实现这一假設，從而大大提升了我們对不同離子通道的激活機制的理解。同时，可能的發現還可以为癌症治療新方法的發展提供重要的信息。最後，本研究所建立的方法也可为将来对各種細胞過程的深入研究提供有力的工具。

17211215.label: Realisation of objectives
17211215.value: 1. We have developed a technique to introduce precise changes in the cellular volume by varying the medium osmolarity via electroosmotic manipulation. 2. The active transmembrane ion transport in different cells under a suddenly applied osmotic shock or a gradual change in the extracellular osmolarity have all be carefully examined. 3. We have systematically measured the death rate of different lung and nasopharyngeal epithelial cancer cells, along with their normal counterparts, under imposed volume changes. 4. By taking into account the exchange of water/ion molecules across the cell membrane, as well as the as the elastic response of the membrane, a theoretical model has also been proposed to describe the size evolution of cells, induced by different volume-changing cues.

17211215.label: Major findings and research outcome
17211215.value: 1. An electro-osmotic manipulation device has been developed to introduce precise volume change to cells introduced by varying the voltage applied across a Naﬁon membrane that separates the culture medium from a reservoir (refer to items 8-1 and 8-5 in Part C). Interestingly, it was found that, unlike sudden osmotic shocks, active ion transport across the membrane of leukemia K562 cells will not be triggered by a gradual change in the extracellular osmolarity. Furthermore, such system has also been used to investigate the migration of more than 20 different types of cancer cells in a confined environment which revealed a linear positive correlation between the water channel protein concentration and the cell migration speed (item 8-8 in Part C). 2. We showed that, when subjected to the same volume changing cue, different lung and nasopharyngeal epithelial cancer cells will undergo larger volumetric changes and have a 5–10% higher death rate compared to their normal counterparts, demonstrating the potential of achieving selective killing of cancer cells via controlling the cellular volume. We further demonstrated that such distinct response is largely caused by the overexpression of aquaporin-4 in tumor cells, with knockout of this water channel protein resulting in a markedly reduced change in the cellular volume as well as death rate (refer to item 8-1 in Part C). 3. Theoretical models were developed to describe the voltage-induced size changes as well as migration of cells (observed in our experiments) where factor like the exchange of water/ion molecules across the Naﬁon film/cell membrane, the elastic resistance of the deformed membrane and possible cell-outside interaction have all been taken into account (item 8-1 and item 8-8 in Part C). Furthermore, by considering the possibility of a locally weakened cortex during cellular deformation, a boundary integral method-based model has also been developed to describe the formation and growth of cellular blebs. The predicted shape evolution of blebs and the critical size of the weakened cortex region for blebbing to occur all agree well with our observations (refer to items 8-3 and 8-6 in Part C).

17211215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17211215.value: 1. Our devices for regulating the cellular volume and triggering the motility of cancer cells may lead to new strategies in achieving selective killing and sorting of tumor cells which could have great clinical implications. 2. The models developed could be extended to examine other interesting phenomena such as the volume changing or blebbing-assisted migration and homeostasis regulation of cells.

17211215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17211215.value: We have developed novel methods to introduce precise changes in the volume of cells via electro-osmotic manipulation. Using this setups, it was found that, unlike sudden osmotic shocks, active ion transport across the membrane of cells will not be triggered by a gradual change in the extracellular osmolarity. Furthermore, when subjected to the same applied voltage, different lung and nasopharyngeal epithelial cancer cells will undergo larger volumetric changes and have a higher death rate compared to their normal counterparts, due to the overexpression of water channel proteins in tumor cells. Findings from this study will enhance our understanding of cancer and could provide valuable information for the development of new interventions.

17211415.label: Realisation of objectives
17211415.value: In order to optimize the design of micro-cavities on the thin-film platform, extensive simulations based on Finite-different time-domain (FDTD) simulations have been carried out. In the first instance, simulations were carried out on micro-cavities on different substrates, including sapphire and Si, and compared to micro-cavities on thin-film substrates. The superiority of the thin-film platform is thus established. Subsequently, simulations were carried out to determine the optimal dimensions for both the Fabry-Perot vertical cavities and the whispering gallery lateral microdisk cavities. Optical design for the mirrors were also carried out for the vertical cavities. Instead of using conventional oxide based distributed Bragg reflectors, conductive GaN gratings were successfully designed. Having determined the optimal cavity designs, the methods of realizing the cavities must be developed. As such, the fabrication processes are developed and optimized. This includes the choice of patterning (using optical lithography, electron beam lithography, microsphere/ nanosphere lithography etc), optimization of the laser lift-off process, the choice of eutectic bonding layer as well as the etch processes. These are crucial for the fabrication of high-quality micro-cavities with low lasing thresholds and high quality factors. For the grating reflectors, different patterning methods have been explored, including laser interference lithography, scanning near-field optical microscopy (SNOM) lithography, nanowire lithography and electron beam lithography. Although the first 3 methods are attractive, it was difficult to control the patterns over the larger regions required for device fabrication. Etching of the patterns are carried out by inductive-coupled power (ICP) plasma etching. The structures must be etched with precision control of etch rates, as well as the formation of vertical and smooth sidewalls. Optimization of the etch processes have been carried out, including optimization of the choices of etch gases, chamber pressures, as well as the process powers (including ICP and plate powers). With the optimized designs and processes, fabrication of the microdisks are carried out in the cleanrooms. The microdisks are patterned by microsphere lithography due to the high sphericity of the particles, as well as the high etch selectivites of the oxide materials. A bonding layer with high reflectivities as well as adhesion was developed that improves optical confinement within the micro-cavities. The fabricated micro-cavities are characterized using photoluminescence spectroscopy to determine the lasing thresholds and quality factors. Using our home-built scanning near-field optical microscopy set-up, we attempted to characterize the fabricated microdisk cavities. Compared to conventional macro-beam or micro-beam spectroscopy, SNOM spectroscopy enables the characterization of the optical structure with sub-micron spatial resolution.

17211415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17211415.value: The simulations found that that micro-cavities formed on thin-films perform much better than those on original substrates. This is because the ideal microdisk should be optically isolated by a material/ambient with a lower refractive index, with air being the ideal choice. Since the fabricated structures have to be supported by a substrate in reality, that interface layer has to be carefully chosen. Since the GaN-on-sapphire microdisk is optically-coupled to its transparent substrate, significant portions of light leak out of the cavity reducing its ability to confine light. Such leakages are effectively suppressed with the thin-film structure, where the optical-coupling pathway is completely eliminated. Consequently, a more than twofold increase in field intensities is observed from the simulated data, highlighting the effectiveness of the thin-film design. Different forms of nano-patterning, including optical lithography, electron beam lithography, microsphere/ nanosphere lithography have been explored. In our study, the thin-film GaN microdisks with diameters of 7 µm were realized by adopting a combination of microsphere lithography (MSL) [and laser lift-off (LLO) techniques. In contrast to conventional photolithographic processes based on the patterning of soft resist materials, MSL relies on spherical microspheres as hard masks to produce microdisks with smooth and vertical sidewalls with excellent circularities due to the high etch selectivity between GaN and microsphere material, typically SiO2. On the other hand electron-beam lithography patterning of the grating for the vertical cavities was preferred over the other techniques explored. The microdisks with thicknesses of 150 nm has been fabricated and the WGM lasing through optically pumping at room temperature has been obtained. Three lasing peaks, centered at 427.1, 430.0, and 433.3 nm, show a nonlinear enhancement with different transition durations. The frequencies are consistent with those predicted with FDTD simulations. The threshold and Q-factor for this system is 8.82 mJ/cm2 and 1673 respectively.

17211415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17211415.value: The work laid down the foundation for continuing work in the area. For instance, the GaN thin-film platform being used for current projects on electroluminescent microdisk lasers, as well as photonic systems for communications. There are great potentials for further development of work in this area, including extending the platform to GaN electronic devices and systems to enhance their performances and robustnesses.

17211415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17211415.value: An optical cavity is the basic and essential structure of a laser diode, which plays the all-important role of confining light to achieve population inversion. For the GaN materials and their alloys, which enable emission across the UV-VIS bands, optical confinement is not trivial due to the transparent substrates, sapphire, on which they are grown on. In this project the concept of the GaN thin-film platform is explored. The sapphire substrates are removed from the GaN-on-sapphire wafers by laser lift-off processes, and transferred to a secondary substrate via a bonding layer. The bonding layer is chosen to not just provide adhesion but also reflectivity, thus offering optical confinement. The results of the project demonstrated the feasibility of the approach, successfully demonstrating optical-pumped lasing from thin-film microdisk optical cavities. The GaN thin-film platform can readily be extended to other devices and systems in the GaN family.

17211515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17211515.value: 現代社會越來越迫切地需要高效率，高靈活度的配電系統。特別是在鉆井/采礦工業，海底和外太空探測等領域，塵土，潮濕，油汙和泥汙使得電力供應和電力線纜、 設備的安裝鋪設非常復雜甚至不可能。在一些格外危險的環境，例如化工廠和核化應堆，人力會被自動機械或機器人代替。在這些危險的環境裏，可以利用無線輸電技術實現一個無線高頻交流的配電網絡，從而可以不間斷地傳送電力給各種設備或給它們的電池充電。在上述場合，無線輸電的好處是顯然易見的。它為上述應用提供了一個可靠，靈活和高效益的解決方案。 在2008年，無線充電聯盟(WPC)發布了“Qi”標準，標誌著可攜帶電子設備的近距離無線充電技術已經到了商業化的階段。為電動車或混合動力車設計的無線充電系統開發工具已經出現了。 它展示了未來電動車或混合動力車的泊車-充電系統。 現在，很多前沿的科研人員已經加入了對中距離無線輸電技術的研究。主要的研究方向包括同時增加傳電的距離和提高系統的效率。 為了應對不斷增加的對靈活而高效的無線配電系統的需求，這個研究提議開發一系列的無線輸電接收器和相應的控制方法，為未來無線高頻交流配電系統的發展鋪設道路。為了實現這個目的，這裏提出兩個主要的研究目標： 1）為無線輸電接收器的新電路的研發，提出一套有系統的電路合成流程。通過一個有系統的分析方法，新電路的穩態和暫態電氣特性可以被表達出來。 2）為無線輸電接收器開發控制辦法和提供完整的方案。我們會整理設計和制作接收器電路所需要的所有實際知識。 這個2年研究項目的順利完成，會加快無線輸電技術的研究和開發。這樣又會激發更多創新的方法和有用的應用。這個項目的研究成果是雙重的: 1）這個研究會訓練有知識的學生和研究員，為無線輸電領域作出貢獻。新開發的電路結構和理論會毫無疑問激發技術上的創新，同時為這個領域的研究人員提供無價的知識。 2）建造的硬件模型會展示一個實際的方案，向工業界和從業人員推廣這個新的無線輸電的模型，從而使這個技術走向市場化。大量的應用會進一步刺激這個技術給社會帶來經濟效益。

17211515.label: Realisation of objectives
17211515.value: This project is proceeding well. New converter topologies for high frequency-fed AC-DC conversion are developed. PI leads his team investigated into the possibilities of new converter structures. A topological analysis to explore the variation of the circuit configuration has been performed. Commonly used converter topologies such as buck, boost, buck-boost, ZETA, Cuk and SEPIC are evaluated. The performance and limitations of the new converters are summarized. Key equations are derived to explain the limitation of the converters. The financial support from RGC also enables PI to conduct further development in the related research topic. A three-winding common mode inductor has been developed by PI and his team. 17211615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17211615.value: Surfaces and objects surround us in the built environment, and touching them is integral to everyday life. But hand touching can contaminate surfaces, and contaminated surfaces (fomites) are known to transmit diseases. However, unlike airborne and close contact routes, our understanding of the fomite route remains at an empirical level. Little is known about the ways and speed at which the surfaces become contaminated. In a crowded environment, a surface (root surface) contaminated by a source patient can be touched by a number of people, and each of these individuals subsequently touch other surfaces as they move around. Each of these contaminated surfaces can be touched again by other people, and such touching sequences progress. At the end, all touched surfaces can be traced back to the root surface. Here this is referred to as the surface touch/contamination network. Understanding this network and its growth is fundamental to understanding the fomite route. We hypothesize, as found in our preliminary study, that under certain conditions, the number of contaminated surfaces grows logistically in an environment, corresponding to a possible rapid transmission of infection. Such a surface network can transmit the virus to remote distances—i.e. as far as people move—thus sharing the same long distance transmission potential as the airborne route. We aim to develop a basic theory of the surface touch/contamination network. The research will include constructing the network and analysing its static and dynamic properties; carrying out a multi-scale field study; and applying the new findings to understand the effectiveness and strategies of hand and surface hygiene. Our surface network construction will enable the spatial pattern of exposure and infection risk due to fomite route to be predicted and analysed. We have identified/developed three complementary approaches: observational (or empirical), laboratory experimental and analytical. Unlike existing work, our observation studies will identify how the number of “contaminated” surfaces/hands change over time, and how this is affected by factors such as crowdedness and job nature. The new laboratory/computer modelling approaches will enable us to study how different prescribed or simplified human behaviours and “standard” surfaces impact on the network dynamics. Using the mass action law, our new analytical approach can shed light on how major parameters such as touch rates and cleaning rates impact on the network growth, and thus the disease spread. This new theory will guide us to develop effective strategies for surface cleaning and hand hygiene. 研究摘要 建築環境中，我們周邊有著各色表面和物件，觸碰它們是日常生活中必然的事。但是，用手觸摸表面可能引發表面汙染，而眾所周知，被汙染的表面（汙染物）又可以傳播疾病。然而，與空氣傳播和近距離觸摸傳播不同，我們對汙染物傳播路徑的理解還停留在經驗階段。關於表面以何種方式以及速率被感染，我們知之甚少。 在擁擠的環境中，一個被源病人汙染過的表面（源表面）可以被一大群人觸摸，並且隨後當這些人四處走動時，每個人都可能觸摸別的表面。每個被感染的表面可以被他人再次觸摸。這種觸摸模式還將繼續發展。最後，所有被觸摸過的表面可以被追溯到源表面。這就是表面觸摸/汙染網絡。了解這個網絡和它的增長模式是理解表面觸摸傳播路徑的基石。 正如我們初步研究中所發現的一樣，我們假設在某些情況下，對應著疾病快速傳播，環境中被汙染的表面數目將呈現logistic增長。這樣的表面網絡可以將病毒傳播到遠處，延伸到人們活動範圍，因此與空氣傳播路徑一樣，具有將疾病傳播到很遠的距離的潛力。 我們致力於為表面觸摸/汙染網絡構建一個基本理論。這項研究將包括建設網絡，分析它的統計學以及動力學性質；展開一項多尺度的研究；將新的發現應用於研究手部和表面清潔的有效性和制定相關策略。表面觸摸網絡的構建將使得我們可以有效的預測和分析疾病通過表面觸摸傳播所導致的感染概率的空間分布的特征。 我們已經識別/發展了三條互相補充的研究手段：觀察性研究（或者經驗性研究），實驗室試驗，以及理論分析性研究。與現有工作不同，我們的觀察性研究將確定感染表面和手的數目如何隨時間變化，及其是如何被擁擠程度和工作性質所影響。新的實驗和電腦模擬手段將使我們能夠研究不同的規定或簡化的個人行為和標準化表面對網絡動態的影響。使用了質量作用定律，我們新的分析手段將能解釋觸摸速率以及清潔速率等主要參數如何影響網絡增長以及疾病傳播。新的理論將引導我們構建一個有效的表面和手部清潔策略。

17211615.label: Realisation of objectives
17211615.value: The objectives are brief; hence I shall report our progress for each individual tasks as in the original proposal. Phase 1 – Developing basic understanding through experiments and simple theory Task 1.1 Laboratory bench-top model study (Objective 1) We have created two bench-top models in our lab (Yam Pak Building third floor). One is for an air cabin and the other is for the hospital ward 8A in the former Prince of Wales Hospital. The planned fluorescence method worked well. Our surfaces were characterized by AFM, and SEM. The work is published in a journal publication; see Xiao et al (2018b). Task 1.2 Surface touch/contamination network model development (Objective 1) We have completed a surface touch/contamination network model as planned. The expected logistic growth behaviour was observed. The surface touch network model has been analysed in detail for an air cabin environment. Though we have completed the network model development and also the network property development, the use of the existing Network theory for analysis of the network properties is not ideal. The work continues in a new CRF project including using constructal theory. The work is published in a journal paper; see Lei et al (2017c). Task 1.3 Understanding the surface touch network in a multi-scale field study (Objective 2) The original plan of the project was very difficult, due to the difficulties in developing or identifying a suitable surface measurement method in the field tests. It turned out that the field detection of surface contamination is extremely difficult. We have now finally developed a new method using Lactobacillus bulgaricus, which has been demonstrated in a student office. For this project, we have explored in detail the multi-scale network properties in an air-cabin. The logistic growth was again observed. The work was used to study the spread of SARS, influenza and norovirus. The wok was published in a journal; see Lei et al (2017b). Task 1.4 Mathematical description of the network growth (Objective 2) The proposed mass action law model worked very well. The paper on the hygiene equation is being written. Also, we applied the developed model for analysing surface cleaning strategies in a hospital for controlling Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and other healthcare-associated infections transmitted through the contact route. Our study reproduces the observations in a field study in the literature with room cleaning intervention, providing support for validity of our findings. The work has been accepted in a journal publication; see Lei et al (2017a). Phase 2 – Application to studying roles of cleaning and disease spread Task 2.1 Understanding the surface hygiene criterion (Objective 3) Our surface hygiene criterion has been found to work well in ideal conditions. We have also done partially a literature review on natural decay of commonly found respiratory and enteric viruses on different surfaces. A paper has been drafted for publication, but recently we found one major assumption in this surface hygiene criterion, i.e. homogenous mixing, which is not ideal. The work may be improved in the near future by removing the assumption, and be published later. Part of the work is included in Lei et al (2017a). Task 2.2 Fomite route modelling and analyses of disease outbreaks (Objective 3) We have applied the model developed Task 1.2 to two air cabin outbreaks of norovirus as planned. The results are amazing to us. Aisle passengers were more likely to be infected. The reported case distribution agrees well with simulations as in Lei et al (2017c). We also re-examined a previously described norovirus outbreak in a restaurant using our model, where airborne transmission was originally inferred. The results show that, with some reasonable assumptions of human behavior patterns, the distribution of attack rates corresponded well with that of the infection risk via the fomite route. This offers an alternative interpretation of the transmission routes for this particular norovirus outbreak, which is an important consideration when developing infection control guidance and when investigating other similar future norovirus outbreaks. Additionally, we also analysed a hypothetical influenza outbreak, and found that the influenza virus was likely to have spread via a combined long-range airborne and fomite routes, with the former predominant and the latter negligible. Most importantly, we also use our developed new model to analyse the well-known MERS outbreak in Seoul, which was timely and offered new insights into the possible transmission routes for MERS. The work is published in three journal papers; see Xiao et al (2017, 2018a and 2018c). Research output Journal publications 1. 17211615.label: Major findings and research outcome
17211615.value: Surfaces and objects surround us in the built environment, and touching them is integral to everyday life. But hand touching can contaminate surfaces, and contaminated surfaces (fomites) are known to transmit diseases. However, unlike airborne and close contact routes, our understanding of the fomite route remains at an empirical level. Little is known about the ways and speed at which the surfaces become contaminated. For the first time, we established the new concept of surface touch/contamination network, and understanding this network and its growth is fundamental to understanding the fomite route. We found that under certain conditions, the number of contaminated surfaces grows logistically in an environment, corresponding to a possible rapid transmission of infection. Such a surface network can transmit the virus to remote distances—i.e. as far as people move—thus sharing the same long distance transmission potential as the airborne route. Thus, we developed a basic theory of the surface touch/contamination network. We constructed the network using bench-top experiments, field measurement and computer modelling, and analysed its static and dynamic properties. We applied the new findings to understand the effectiveness and strategies of hand and surface hygiene. The surface cleaning strategies in a hospital is developed for controlling Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). For the first time, we construct a surface network that enables the spatial pattern of exposure and infection risk due to fomite route to be predicted and analysed. The new model was used to analyse the outbreaks of influenza, SARS and norovirus in air cabins. The reported case distribution agrees well with simulations with new insights on the transmission routes with this unique comparative approach. We also re-examined a previously described norovirus outbreak in a restaurant, where airborne transmission was originally inferred. The results show that the distribution of attack rates corresponded well with that of the infection risk via the fomite route. We also analysed a hypothetical influenza outbreak, and found that the influenza virus was likely to have spread via a combined long-range airborne and fomite routes, with the former predominant and the latter negligible. Most importantly, we also use our developed new model to analyse the well-known MERS outbreak in Seoul, which was timely and offered new insights into the possible transmission routes for MERS. Our data offers new interpretation of the transmission routes, which is an important consideration when developing infection control guidance and when investigating other similar future outbreaks.

17211615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17211615.value: Our work first shows clearly the importance of the need to study human touch behavior. The network of surfaces that allows the transfer of viruses and bacteria by hands is known in our study as the surface touch network. Understanding the surface touch network and its growth is fundamental to understanding the fomite route. The PI has already secured a new CRF project in studying the human touch behavior in building following this finding. The work is also relevant to understanding of the distribution of the general microbial community on surfaces. Little is known about the mechanisms underlying identified patterns of microbiome distribution. For example, it remains unclear how every human maintains a specific microbial “fingerprint” despite regularly touching various kinds of surfaces. Further research is needed. The hygiene equation that we identified showed that it is not the hand hygiene alone that matters in the fomite route, but the product of the hand cleaning efficiency and surface cleaning efficiency matters. This implies that those intervention studies focusing the hand hygiene alone might not be too meaningful, if the surface cleaning data lacked. The PI plans to carry out some relevant studies in this direction.

Here this is referred to as the surface touch/contamination network, a new concept that we have developed to find the ways and speed at which the surfaces become contaminated, and how the diseases are transmitted. 17212015.label: Project Objectives
17212015.value: The main project purpose is to develop an economical method to thermally incorporate Zn and Pb in MSWI residues, as a safer and more reliable alternative of current cementation methods. The key challenge is on promoting the formation of glass-ceramic matrices with the aluminates and aluminosilicates for hosting Zn and Pb. The metal reaction pathways will be clearly identified by X-ray diffraction and electron diffraction results. The evolutionary processes of different Zn and Pb hosting phases will be portrayed across different precursor compositions and treatment schemes. Our very unique quantitative X-ray diffraction analysis skill (Rietveld refinement method using the fundamental parameter approach and amorphous content quantification through internal standards) will then report the quantities of Zn and Pb hosting phases in products through high resolution X-ray diffraction data. An amorphous content quantification protocol employing commonly available calcium fluoride and silicon carbide internal standards will be also conducted to assist in the development of a reliable quantification method for the amorphous content. Crystalline characteristics (lattice parameters, cation distribution, crystal size, etc.) of Zn- and Pb-containing phases generated from thermally reacting with the precursors will be quantified by Rietveld refinement on X-ray diffraction data to evaluate the quality of metal stabilization. The influences of different metal oxide additives on the structures of Zn- and Pb-hosting phases will also be assessed by monitoring the responses of these crystalline characteristics to provide direct evidence of the changes in the metal coordination environment. Metal stabilization effects will be investigated by leaching experiments to quantify the metal leachability and by surface-sensitive characterization tools, e.g. atomic force microscopy (AFM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), to elucidate the metal leaching behavior on the surface. Our strong expertise in high resolution electron microscopy (SEM and TEM) will assist the characterizations of glass-ceramic microstructures and the identification of metal-hosting phase nanostructures, such as grain boundary features, to facilitate the development of a reliable metal incorporation strategy. Based on the mechanistic understanding of Zn and Pb phase transformations initiated by reactive glass-ceramic matrix incorporation, techniques will be elaborated for fabricating desired nano- and micro-structural features for MSWI residue-containing products. Overall, the implementation of this project will facilitate the goal of safely and reliably stabilizing the hazardous metals in MSWI residues through a scientifically sound and economically feasible treatment strategy.

Metal stabilization effects will be investigated by leaching experiments to quantify the metal leachability and by surface-sensitive characterization tools, e.g. atomic force microscopy (AFM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), to elucidate the metal leaching behavior on the surface. Our strong expertise in high resolution electron microscopy (SEM and TEM) will assist the characterizations of glass-ceramic microstructures and the identification of metal-hosting phase nanostructures, such as grain boundary features, to facilitate the development of a reliable metal incorporation strategy.

Based on the mechanistic understanding of Zn and Pb phase transformations initiated by reactive glass-ceramic matrix incorporation, techniques will be elaborated for fabricating desired nano- and micro-structural features for MSWI residue-containing products. Overall, the implementation of this project will facilitate the goal of safely and reliably stabilizing the hazardous metals in MSWI residues through a scientifically sound and economically feasible treatment strategy.

17212015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17212015.value: Significant amounts of municipal solid waste (MSW) were generated everyday creating significant environmental impacts in many regions of the world. Hong Kong currently uses landfill to dispose of the nearly 9000 tons/day of MSW and has chosen incineration to resolve this problem in the future. Incineration provides an effective way to reduce waste organics but results in municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) residues. MSWI residues are generally enriched with silicon and aluminum oxides, together with certain hazardous metals needed to be properly treated prior to disposal or any beneficial uses. Zinc (Zn) and lead (Pb) are commonly found with the highest concentrations among the other hazardous metals in MSWI residues. Conventional treatment methods rely on cementitious materials to encapsulate the MSWI residues. Thermal treatments can employ crystalline (ceramic) or non-crystalline (glass) matrix to further incorporate hazardous metals into the atomic- and nano-scale structures, but usually require an energy-intensive high-temperature (>1300C) condition. This project aims to develop the glass-ceramic matrices that can both react with and encapsulate hazardous metals at a much lower temperature range (several hundreds to 1000C). The key development is to facilitate the formation of aluminates and aluminosilicates in alkali metal oxide modified solid systems to produce the glass-ceramic products at the targeted temperature range. Most metal speciation studies of solids focus on the reaction mechanisms in either crystalline phases or glass form, but recent reports have suggested a new strategy of synergistically using glass-ceramic matrices to create different metal hosting sites and stabilization mechanisms. This project will identify and control the key mechanisms of incorporating Zn and Pb into the glass-ceramic matrix. Experimental activities will start by calcining bottom ash and fly ash materials to observe the Zn and Pb phase transformations, following by supplying different metal oxides to reduce the formation temperature of glass-ceramics in the system. The high resolution X-ray diffraction technique will then be performed on the calcined samples, and a state-of-the-art Rietveld refinement analysis with amorphous content quantification will be implemented to quantify different metal phases and crystalline parameters of the metal hosting phases. By identifying the grain boundary features and evaluating the metal leachabilities of product phases, the hosting characteristics of Zn and Pb in glass-ceramic matrices can be further examined. Finally, the flexibility to design a variety of nano- and micro-structure features for MSWI residue-containing products will be explored for developing the safe and reliable waste disposal and beneficial use strategies. 都市固體廢物（固廢）產量日益增加，對全球環境造成重大影響。香港當前以堆填方式每日處理約9000噸固體廢物，並計劃發展焚化技術來進一步解決固體廢物問題。焚化可有效減少固廢中的有機物，但同時產生富含矽、鋁氧化物以及有害重金屬的固體廢物焚燒灰渣，灰渣中的有害重金屬在棄置或重新利用前，需要進行進一步處理。鋅(Zn)和鉛(Pb)作為焚燒灰渣中含量最高的有害重金屬，傳統的處理方式以水泥固化包裹為主。熱處理技術則利用晶體(陶瓷)或非晶體(玻璃)基質進一步將目標金屬固定在原子或納米微結構中，但熱處理能耗成本過高，反應需要較高溫度(>1300C)。本研究旨在於低溫條件下(幾百到1000度)以陶瓷玻璃體系與廢灰渣中的鉛和鋅發生結合反應從而達到固化效果。研究的重點在於促進鋁酸鹽及矽鋁酸鹽化合物在鹼性金屬氧化物修飾的固體體系中的結晶，從而在目標溫度下形成相關陶瓷玻璃產物。大多數關於固體中金屬形態的研究側重於結晶相或者玻璃態的單一反應機理，最新的科研成果則提出新的協同固化策略，綜合應用穩定化原理，使用陶瓷玻璃給有害重金屬提供不同的固化位置。本研究將對陶瓷玻璃中鋅/鉛主要固化機理進行深入探討。實驗設計包括：燒結焚化底灰和飛塵混合物，觀察其中鋅/鉛相的變化；嘗試摻入不同金屬氧化物以降低反應溫度，高分辨X-射線衍射技術將被運用於表徵燒結產物；Rietveld精修分析方法則對不同金屬相及非晶相進行定量研究並給出相關金屬固化相的晶格參數。通過分析陶瓷玻璃產物中的顆粒邊界性質及有害金屬在結晶相中的浸出性能，可進一步瞭解鋅/鉛在陶瓷玻璃中的固化特性。本研究還將探討製作不同微觀結構特徵的廢灰渣固化產品的可行性，為危險固體廢物的安全有效處理及再利用提供更多想法和建議。

17212015.label: Realisation of objectives
17212015.value: The municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) ash has gone through high-temperature oxidization processing, and thus the residual metals, including Zn and Pb, are predominantly in their oxide forms. To study the behavior of Zn and Pb in the subsequent stabilization treatments, Zn and Pb oxides were used in our thermal treatment experiments. Moreover, it is known that the MSWI ash is also largely in glassy form, likely incorporating the hazardous metals in its glassy network. Thus, some of our experiments also used the Pb-containing glass (can be obtained from waste cathode ray tubes) as the precursor to test whether the treatment scheme can be effective, even if the hazardous metals were encapsulated in the glassy network. In this setting, the thermal reactions of Zn and Pb with the other commonly seen inorganic components in waste, such as Si, Fe and Al, were studied in this project. The formations of glass-ceramic products for Zn and Pb were observed in the thermal treatment experiments with the product properties reported. The metal reaction pathways were identified by X-ray diffraction and electron microscopic tools to illustrate the evolutionary processes of Zn and Pb hosting phases with different precursor compositions and treatment conditions. The Pb-Fe oxides (PbFe12O19, PbFe4O7, Pb2Fe2O5), Pb aluminosilicate (PbAl2Si2O8), Pb-Fe silicate (Pb2Fe2Si2O9), Zn aluminate (ZnAl2O4), and Zn ferrite (ZnFe2O4) were observed in the treatment products with their properties discussed in this project. Our unique quantitative X-ray diffraction analyses were widely used in this study to report the quantities of Zn and Pb hosting phases in products. High-resolution X-ray diffraction data were collected from our X-ray diffractometer, and the Rietveld refinement analysis scheme was successfully established and used for reliable quantification outcomes, including the quantification for amorphous content. We had also studied the crystal structures of metal hosting phases with their relevant structural parameters. The lattice sizes of the product phases after different levels of thermal treatments were presented in the high-resolution X-ray diffraction data, and the influence of crystal size affecting the metal stabilization reactions was also evaluated. With the metal hosting phases and their crystalline characteristics, the Zn and Pb coordination environments and their mobility tendencies can be compared. The performance of metal stabilization outcomes was widely investigated by leaching experiments and assisted by surface characterization techniques including small-area SEM-EDS, FTIR, and selected-area TEM, when needed. Our high-resolution electron microscopic (SEM and TEM) work also assisted the characterizations of glass-ceramic structures in the products in reflecting the reliability of the planned metal incorporation strategies. After understanding the Zn and Pb phase transformation mechanisms, it can be concluded that the glass-ceramic matrix was widely found in the thermally treated products and different thermal treatment schemes were found to generated different nano- and micro-structural features. The goal of using different precursors commonly found in MSWI (such as Si, Fe, Al) to control the mobilities of Zn and Pb is achievable. The comparison of the chosen reaction mechanisms for hazardous metals (Zn and Pb) could also be reliably realized by our developed leaching experiments. An invention of low-temperature glass-ceramic sintering strategy through forming the melanotekite crystal phase for Pb was particularly highlighted in the study to fulfill the project goal.

17212015.label: Major findings and research outcome
17212015.value: The hazardous metals are commonly found and further concentrated in the municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) ash. Among those concerned hazardous metals in MSWI ash, Zn and Pb often play major roles in the compositions. This project used the oxide forms of Zn and Pb, together with the glassy form, to observe their behavior in the subsequent thermal treatment processes. By thermally reacting with the widely available inorganic components in waste (such as Si, Fe, and Al), the formations of glass-ceramic products for Zn and Pb were observed in the products. The potential product phases that may exist are found to be Pb-Fe oxides (PbFe12O19, PbFe4O7, Pb2Fe2O5), Pb aluminosilicate (PbAl2Si2O8), Pb-Fe silicate (Pb2Fe2Si2O9), Zn aluminate (ZnAl2O4), and Zn ferrite (ZnFe2O4). This study used the high-resolution X-ray diffraction and electron microscopic tools to illustrate the evolutionary processes of those Zn and Pb hosting phases with different precursor compositions and treatment conditions. The quantitative X-ray diffraction analyses were widely used in this study to report the quantities of Zn and Pb hosting phases in products, together with the quantification for amorphous content. The crystal structures of metal hosting phases were also studied, and it was found the metal transformation efficiency can be increased when the reactant crystal size is reduced. The performance of metal stabilization outcomes was widely investigated by leaching experiments and assisted by surface characterization techniques including small-area SEM-EDS, FTIR, and selected-area TEM, when needed. Our high-resolution electron microscopic (SEM and TEM) work also assisted the characterizations of glass-ceramic structures in the products to reflect the reliability of the planned metal incorporation strategies. Among the Zn hosting phases, Zn ferrite was found to possess good resistance to metal leaching in acidic aqueous solution. Among the Pb hosting phases, the magnetoplumbite structure (PbFe12O19) showed the highest acidic attack resistance. However, in view of the concern of treatment cost, this project had discovered that using the melanotekite (Pb2Fe2Si2O9) crystal phase can stabilize Pb with a low-temperature sintering scheme (crystal structure initiated at 500-600C) to form the glass-ceramic matrix achieving a safe and economically beneficial treatment.

17212015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17212015.value: The implementation of this project has sufficiently used the experimental resources in a laboratory scale facility. Further scientific research development can be planned with the synchrotron-based tools to further understand the changes of atomic coordination and occupancy when the targeted metals were going through the leaching processes. Another development direction is to conduct theoretical thermodynamic calculation to model the behavior of metals when subjected to acidic attack. Both developments can further verify the product phase stability results presented in this project outcomes. Another direction of development is to refine the parameters and processing procedure generated from our laboratory-scale experiments with the industrial scale operation to fully realize the actual application of research outcomes.

17212015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17212015.value: The zinc (Zn) and lead (Pb) are hazardous commonly found in the municipal solid waste incineration (MSWI) ash. This project thus investigated the potential thermal treatment methods capable of effectively stabilize these two metals. With the unique quantitative X-ray diffraction technique, the results showed many commonly available inorganic components in waste (such as silicon, iron, and aluminum) can react with Zn and Pb to efficiently benefit the goal of stabilizing these hazardous metals. The projects also tested the stability of metals in the treated products through acid leaching method. It was found a Pb ferrite phase (PbFe12O19) can be particularly stable than the other Pb-containing phases, and a Zn ferrite phase (ZnFe2O4) also performed very well in resisting the attack of the acidic solution. Moreover, a new strategy of using the melanotekite (Pb2Fe2Si2O9) phase to stabilize Pb in the glass-ceramic matrix was invented, and it can stabilize Pb at a much lower temperature range (attainable at 500-600C) comparing to the traditional thermal treatment scheme to achieve a safe and economically beneficial treatment.

17212115.label: Project Objectives
17212115.value: Conduct a series of material tensile coupon tests to examine the material properties of very high strength steel with the nominal 0.2% proof stress between 700 MPa and 1100 MPa. Conduct a series of beam-column tests on very high strength steel with the nominal 0.2% proof stresses of 700, 900 and 1100 MPa. Furthermore, concentric compression and pure bending tests will be conducted in order to obtain the full interaction curves. Develop finite element model for beam-columns, and validate the model against the newly generated test results. Perform an extensive parametric study for beam-columns, with variation of cross-section slenderness, column lengths and loading eccentricities. Revisit the current section classification framework in Eurocode 3 (EC3, 2006) and propose new class limits for cold-formed high strength steel with the nominal 0.2% proof stress greater than 700 MPa. Assess the existing design rules and propose new design methods for very high strength steel beam-columns of circular, square and rectangular hollow sections. Beam-column interaction curves will also be derived.

17212115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17212115.value: Nowadays, cold-formed high strength steel structural members have become more and more popular for structural applications. Owning to the rapid development in cold-forming technology and material advancement, the strength of the steel material can be enhanced, so that the member size and the number of members in steel structures can be reduced by using very high strength steel. This may be favoured by the architects and more importantly, it will reduce the weight of the structure and construction costs. Therefore, the society will benefit from the very high strength steel materials in terms of energy efficiency and sustainable development. However, structural design of the very high strength steel with the nominal 0.2% proof stress (i.e. the yield stress) beyond 700 MPa is not currently covered by the existing international design specifications, such as the American Specification (AISC, 2010), the Australian Standard (AS, 1998), the Australian/New Zealand Standard (AS/NZS, 2005), the North American Specification (AISI, 2012) and the European Code (EC3, 2006). This restricted the use of such material in construction. Therefore, there is a need to investigate very high strength steel materials and structural members. Beam-column is one of the basic and essential structural components in a structure. However, cold-formed high strength steel beam-columns with the nominal 0.2% proof stress higher than 700 MPa has not been reported in the literature. Circular, square and rectangular tubular sections (CHS, SHS and RHS) are commonly used in structural applications owning to its advanced aesthetic and structural benefits. Therefore, it is proposed in this research project to conduct experimental and numerical investigations on very high strength steel beam-columns of CHS, SHS and RHS. Furthermore, the effects of welds on high strength steel are also lack of research. Therefore, the material properties of welds as well as the material properties in the heat affected zone will be investigated in this project. The objectives of this research project are to generate experimental and numerical data on material properties, beam-column capacities and welding strengths of cold-formed high strength steel with the nominal 0.2% proof stress greater than 700 MPa, and thereafter, design recommendations for cold-formed high strength steel tubular beam-columns will be proposed. 现今，冷弯高强钢构件在建筑结构中的应用越来越普遍。由于冷成型工艺技术和高等材料的快速发展，钢的材料强度得到加强，通过使用超高强钢使得钢结构中构件的尺寸和构件的数量得到减少。这可能非常受建筑师欢迎，更重要的是，它也将会相应减少结构的重量和建设成本。因此，从有效利用能源和可持续发展的角度看，整个社会都会从应用超高强钢材料中受益。然而，当今国际上钢结构设计规范中，0.2%名义应力（屈服强度）超过700MPa的超高强钢材料的设计并无涉及，例如，美国设计规范(AISC, 2010)，澳大利亚设计规范(AS, 1998)，澳大利亚/新西兰设计规范(AS/NZS, 2005)，北美设计规范(AISI, 2012)以及欧洲设计规范(EC3, 2006)。这些因素阻碍了这种超高强材料在建筑工业中的使用。因此，有必要研究超高强钢材料和超高强钢构件的性能。 梁柱是建筑结构中基本且非常重要的组成部分之一。然而，目前文献中并没有涉及0.2%名义应力超过700MPa的冷弯高强钢梁柱的研究报告。基于建筑美观和结构优点，圆形，方形和矩形截面(CHS, SHS and RHS)在建筑结构应用中比较普遍。因此，本研究项目计划对圆形，方形和矩形截面的超高强梁柱进行试验和数值研究。另外，由于缺少焊接对高强钢的影响方面研究，本项目也会对焊接的材料性能以及热影响区的材料性能进行研究。本研究项目的目标是得到0.2%名义应力超过700MPa的冷弯高强钢的材料性能，梁柱结构承载力以及焊接性能的试验和数值数据，然后提出冷弯高强钢管的梁柱设计建议。

17212115.label: Realisation of objectives
17212115.value: A series of material tensile coupon tests on very high strength steel with the nominal 0.2% proof stress between 700 MPa and 1100 MPa was conducted. The material properties of the very high strength steel was carefully examined. Furthermore, a series of beam-column tests on very high strength steel was also conducted. The behavior of the beam-column structural members was investigated. In addition, concentric compression and pure bending tests were also conducted in order to obtain the full interaction curves. These tests were successfully carried out. The objectives of the experimental investigation have been achieved. Numerical investigation on cold-formed steel members of very high steel grades subjected to combined axial load and bending was performed. Finite element model for very high strength steel beam-columns was developed. The numerical model was verified against the test results. Furthermore, an extensive parametric study for beam-columns with variation of cross-section slenderness, column lengths and loading eccentricities was also performed. Therefore, the numerical results together with the experimental results were used for the development of new design rules for very high strength steel beam-columns. The objectives of the numerical investigation have been achieved. The current section classification framework in Eurocode 3 has been revisited. New classification limits for cold-formed high strength steel with the nominal 0.2% proof stress greater than 700 MPa have been proposed. Furthermore, the existing design rules for very high strength steel beam-columns of circular, square and rectangular hollow sections were assessed. New design methods for very high strength steel beam-columns have been proposed. In addition, beam-column interaction curves have been derived. The objectives of the design rules development have been achieved.

17212215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17212215.value: Recovery of 3D shape and motion from 2D image sequences or video is a fundamental problem with applications in human-computer interaction, security, autonomous robots, etc. Although traditional structure from motion (SFM) for static scenes is well studied, research to extend SFM to dynamic scenes has a long way to go, with current development focused in two areas. On the one hand, some methods exploit properties of structures supporting special kind of motions, such as human skeleton and articulated objects. On the other hand, the rigidity assumption of SFM has been completely relaxed, allowing non-rigid structures to deform in any arbitrary manner, leading to the general non-rigid structure from motion (NRSFM) problem. The methods for articulated and other special structures are obviously restricted only to their specific problem areas, whereas NRSFM remains an ill-posed problem with no good solution to date. To our knowledge, there is no existing methodology that can perform shape and motion recovery for a complex dynamic scene featuring a static background, articulated objects undergoing motion (such as human) and other deforming objects, with occlusion occurring as well. In this project, we propose to take a stratified approach to recover shape and motion from a complex dynamic scene using a strategy consisting of four stages. First, motion segmentation is performed to classify feature points in a scene as background, rigid parts of articulated structures or general deformable shapes. Secondly, the identified rigid parts are linked to build articulated structures such as humans. Third, feature points belonging to deformable shapes are described by means of a characterization of all possible solutions using a free parameter, which addresses the ill-posedness of the NRSFM problem. Finally, the ambiguity in the solution to NRSFM is resolved by determining the free parameter using additional constraints such as physical modeling of the deformable shape. The proposed stratified approach cannot be achieved by an integration of existing methodologies which are developed for specific paradigms with idealized assumptions making them not readily applicable to realistic scenes. For the different stages of the proposed approach to fit together in a unified framework, novel methods have to be developed in key areas including robust motion segmentation with occlusion handling, construction of kinematic chains, and a new approach to resolve ill-posedness of NRSFM. Our proposal represents a coordinated effort to develop a range of methods that work together to tackle a complex realistic scene. 從二維圖像列或視頻恢復三維形狀和運動是一個基礎問題，其應用領域包括人機交互、安保、自主機器人等。雖然傳統的從運動恢復結構(SFM)對靜態的場景已得到充分的研究，把從運動恢復結構延伸至動態場景的研究還有很長的路要走，目前的發展主要集中在兩個方面。一方面，一些方法是建基於結構本身的特性及其特殊運動方式，比如人體骨骼和鉸接式物體。另一方面，另一些方法把從運動恢復結構的剛性假設完全放鬆，從而允許非剛性結構以任意的方式變形，衍生出更普遍適用的從運動恢復非剛性結構(NRSFM)問題。解決鉸接式及其他結構的方法顯然受限於其特定的問題領域，而另一方面從運動恢復非剛性結構迄今仍然是一個不適定問題並沒有很好的解決方法。據我們所知，對於一個包含靜態背景、運動中的鉸接物體（如人體）和其他變形物體，並有遮擋情況發生的複雜的動態場景，沒有現行方法可以做到結構與運動恢復。 在此項目中，我們提出一個包含四個階段的分層方法以對複雜動態場景進行結構與運動恢復。首先，我們執行運動分割把場景中的特徵點分類為背景、鉸接結構的剛性部件、和一般變形物體。其次，識別出的剛性部件被連接以構成鉸接式物體如人體。其三，屬於變形物體的特徵點會通過一個表達所有可能解的自由參數來描述，以應對從運動恢復非剛性結構的不適定性。最後，附加的約束條件如變形物體的物理模型可用來確定此自由參數從而解決從運動恢復非剛性結構的解的不確定性。 我們所提出的分層方法不能通過集成現有的方法來實現，這是因為現有方法是為具有理想化的假設的特定情況設計的，故不能直接應用於現實場景。為要把上述方案的不同階段整合在一個統一框架內，必須在關鍵領域開發新的方法，包括可處理遮擋的可靠的運動分割、運動鏈的構建、以及解決從運動恢復非剛性結構的不適定性的新方法。我們的方案是通過協調開發一系列可以互相配合的方法來處理複雜的現實場景。

17212215.label: Realisation of objectives
17212215.value: [Objective 1] Two different complementary methods have been developed to perform motion segmentation of a complex dynamic scene into articulated structure and deformable shapes against a static background, namely, rigid subset detection (by ellipsoid fitting [C1] or metric rigidity constraint [J1]) and non-rigid shape detection (by tensor factorization [C3]). The ellipsoid fitting or rigidity constraint incorporate metric conditions into the motion segmentation and are therefore more robust than existing subspace detection methods based on a low-rank condition. The rigid subset detection is however, sensitive to the choice of a fitting threshold. To overcome this problem, we have developed a statistical analysis procedure for setting the threshold, as reported in [J1]. The statistical analysis is important as it holds the key to fully automate the motion segmentation process without any need of manual tuning of the threshold. [Objective 2] We have developed a new method for linking rigid subsets (as identified by the method described under Objective 1) into articulated structures based on physically meaningful properties of joint motion between two rigid subsets. As a result, joints and their positions are identified with joint costs that can be used to construct a graph. Minimum spanning tree search is then applied to link the rigid subsets into kinematic chains. Since our approach does not require the joint positions of adjacent links to be coincident, it is particularly suitable for modeling imperfect articulation of the human joint, as illustrated by examples provided in [J1]. [Objective 3] We have adopted the blend shape method for characterizing solutions to the non-rigid structure from motion (NRSFM) problem, with the novelty of imposing an additional constraint generated by a pseudo camera to resolve the ambiguity of NRSFM (see [C2]). Then, we develop a solution platform that combines ASFM (articulated structure from motion) and NRSFM into an integrated framework (see [J1]), whereby articulated structures of approximately rigid subsets are first recovered (using methods described under Objectives 1 and 2), and then the blend shape technique is used to model the deformations of individual subsets. This represents a first attempt to combine ASFM for modeling global motion and NRSFM for describing local deformations in an integrated approach. As examples of application, we have applied the integrated method to perform motion segmentation and 3D shape recovery of different kinds of human body motion.

17212215.label: Major findings and research outcome
17212215.value: In this project, we consider recovering 3D structure from a dynamic scene by combining articulated structure from motion (ASFM) and non-rigid structure from motion (NRSFM). Our ASFM method employs a seed-growing strategy based on rigidity metric constraints to perform motion segmentation of the scene into approximately rigid subsets (see [C1] and [J1]). The rigid subsets are then linked into articulated kinematic chains (e.g. a human skeleton) by minimum spanning tree search in a graph of joint costs. Our method is robust due to the use of metric conditions, and computationally efficient being linearly related to the number of feature points. For NRSFM, we have adopted blend shape techniques for modeling deformations, with characteristics of physically meaningful shape basis and the generation of a pseudo view for regularization (see [C2]). We have also developed tensor factorization as a complementary method for detecting non-rigid shapes in a dynamic scene (see [C3]). We have applied our method to the recovery of human body motion, which is one the most studied problems in 3D structure from motion. We note that human body motion generally consists of large articulations between different body parts and small local deformations within each body part. Based on this, we propose an integrated framework that combines the above ASFM and NRSFM methodologies to estimate human body motion and shape as an articulated deformable structure (see [J1]). This represents a first attempt to combine ASFM and NRSFM in an integrated approach that exploits both the global and local characteristics of human body motion. The proposed method has been applied to a range of public datasets sets. Experimental results show that our method provides better performance for human motion segmentation and 3D shape recovery compared to existing methods [J1].

17212215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17212215.value: The integrated framework described in [J1] provides a general solution platform for combining NRSFM techniques with ASFM, which can be further developed in two directions. First, although the blend-shape method adopted in this project has good physical meaning, it can be substituted by different NRSFM techniques to take advantage of the specific nature of non-rigid deformations under consideration. Secondly, the stratified procedure in the proposed method can be made into an iterative process, whereby the motion segmentation and non-rigid structure recovery can be refined alternately to reap the maximum benefits of the integrated approach.

17212215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17212215.value: In this project, we considered recovering 3D structures in a dynamic scene from a sequence of 2D images or video, which is a fundamental problem with many applications. We adopt two basic approaches, namely articulated structure from motion (ASFM) and non-rigid structure from motion (NRSFM) for recovering moving and/or deforming 3D structures in a dynamic scene. We have developed an integrated framework that combines ASFM and NRSFM in a stratified procedure. In our method, first, motion segmentation is performed to partition the scene into approximately rigid subsets which may be undergoing motion relative to the background or others entities in the scene. Then, links between individual subsets are established to connect them into articulated kinematic chains, such as a human body. Finally, the individual approximately rigid subsets are described as deformable shapes by means of parameterized blend-shape models. The proposed method is particularly suitable for motion segmentation and 3D structure recovery of human body motion, which generally consists of large articulations between different body parts and small local deformations within each body part. Experimental results show that the proposed method provides better performance for human motion segmentation and shape recovery compared to existing methods.
