17212315.label: Project Objectives
17212315.value: New theory with fast and robust algorithms for tensor decomposition and analysis ---- a prominent yet intriguing property of tensors is that they allow various decompositions into finite low-rank terms, in contrast to the singular value decomposition (SVD) of matrices that is unique up to signs of singular vectors. This translates into the quest for tensor analysis and synthesis algorithms that strike the balance between numerical efficiency, accuracy and robustness. Expedited tensor-based circuit modeling and simulation ---- many circuit modeling exercises naturally give rise to multi-dimensional data representation which are unnecessarily "flattened" into matrix/vector format only to fit into existing computing platforms and linear algebra routines. In fact, preservation of the intrinsic tensor structures and direct computation in tensor formats often lead to significant speedup. Open-source computer codes and benchmarks for generic tensor operations and specialized EDA routines ---- appreciation of the benefits of tensor-based algorithms is best achieved by making them available in the public domain. This permits promulgation of the tensor framework, as well as verification and improvement of tensor algorithms through collective talents and efforts. Long-Term Impact: The long-term impact of this project is echoed by the recent flurry of research on tensor decompositions and applications. Our initiative to introduce tensors to the EDA field can also address the need for an efficient tool in handling nonlinear circuit design problems that are naturally captured in the tensor format. The success of the above goals and their streamlined integration into the EDA flow will lead to a revolution in the data structure and numerical routines for performing circuit modeling and simulation. Elements in this project can also provide students, researchers and practitioners with the breadth (general tensor knowledge) and depth (specialization to EDA algorithms) of knowledge necessary to contribute to the academia and industry. The contemporary content of the project can be readily merged into postgraduate courses at HKU to provide an interdisciplinary training in advanced multi-linear tensor algebra, numerical algorithms, nonlinear theory and circuit modeling.

17212315.value: 線性代數是幾乎所有電路模擬和仿真程序的基礎。在模型降階，系統辨識等一系列應用中，電子設計自動化（EDA）工具中的許多高效的數值實現都是建立在矩陣運算和存儲的基礎上。如果我們認爲標量和矩陣分別代表了一階和二階的數據結構，那麽張量就是在任意高階的多線性延伸，並出現在無數工程課題中。盡管對張量的研究早在幾十年前就開始了，但近年來其在數據挖掘，信號處理和計量化學領域的成功應用使得科學界對其産生極大的興趣。在矩陣代數領域，有很多非常成功和廣泛應用的分析和分解算法，例如本征值和奇異值分解，但這些算法在張量領域的延伸卻並不容易，也特別引人入勝。此外，在電路模擬和仿真領域對張量的研究還比較少，因此對其在EDA應用中的潛在益處是本項目要發掘的主要目標。 本項目有兩個主題：擴展張量的分析和分解算法，以及應用張量格式來加速電路模擬和仿真。爲了實現這兩個主題，本項目制定了三個主要目標： 1. 發展新的高效的張量分解的理論和算法； 2. 應用張量運算來加速電路模擬和仿真； 3. 爲通用張量操作和基于張量的專有EDA應用開發優化的計算機代碼和實例。 本項目的成果無疑會促進張量在EDA領域中的應用。張量的多線性性質使其尤其適合處理高階非線性問題，有助解決長期困擾當代研究者的非線性混合信號芯片的模擬和仿真。因此，對張量算法的理論研究和數值實現有望將電路設計效率提升到一個新的層次，同時鼓勵更創新和高效的設計工具的發展。本項目將用流行的Matlab/Octave語言來作爲開發語言，並將算法和實例公開發布，以方便其他研究者驗證他們的發現，以及芯片設計者將張量工具嵌入到傳統EDA設計流程來提升設計速度。

The long-term impact of this project is echoed by the recent flurry of research on tensor decompositions and applications. Our initiative to introduce tensors to the EDA field can also address the need for an efficient tool in handling nonlinear circuit design problems that are naturally captured in the tensor format. The success of the above goals and their streamlined integration into the EDA flow will lead to a revolution in the data structure and numerical routines for performing circuit modeling and simulation. Elements in this project can also provide students, researchers and practitioners with the breadth (general tensor knowledge) and depth (specialization to EDA algorithms) of knowledge necessary to contribute to the academia and industry. The contemporary content of the project can be readily merged into postgraduate courses at HKU to provide an interdisciplinary training in advanced multi-linear tensor algebra, numerical algorithms, nonlinear theory and circuit modeling.

17212315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17212315.value: This GRF project has been completed very successfully, both in terms of the quantity and quality of research publications, as well as in its subsequent influence on the PI's research directions. To be concise, this project has proceeded in two main directions: one is on the theory and algorithms of fast tensor decomposition, another is on the application of these algorithms to practical circuit modeling and simulations. The first part targets the numerical linear algebra community, while the second part addresses the interest of the electronic design automation (EDA) community. Among the many publications generated from this GRF project, the PI would like to highlight that an IEEE Keynote paper has been published that covers the tensor basics, presents latest tensor-based EDA algorithms from the PI's team, and provides outlook for more tensor application in the field. Other outputs on tensor-based modeling and simulation also appear in the prestigious journals such as Automatica etc. Consequently, the first two project objectives: 1) New theory with fast and robust algorithms for tensor decomposition and analysis; 2) Expedited tensor-based circuit modeling and simulation; are accomplished with high standards. Moreover, Matlab and Octave codes are archived and provided for many test cases in nonlinear circuit modeling and simulation. The list of available codes are available from under: https://www.eee.hku.hk/~kimb/software.html These publicized codes therefore fulfills the third project objective: 3) Open-source computer codes and benchmarks for generic tensor operations and specialized EDA routines. The successes of the above three objectives then directly contributes to the fourth project objective which is an integration of aforementioned techniques and results. Even more, the tensor techniques arising from this GRF project have further been extended to generic nonlinear system identification framework based on the given multi-input multi-output data. Such tensor-driven nonlinear system identification approach is the first of its kind in the literature. It is highly scalable and general, with application not only in EDA topics, but also in the latest development in neural network design and image completion, where the networks or images are regarded as systems to be identified.

17212315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17212315.value: The results and findings from this GRF project has successfully inspired the PI's next GRF project entitled "A New Tensor-Based Volterra Series for Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Nonlinear System Modeling" which was funded. Specifically, tensor algebra has been further enhanced and deployed into the regime of nonlinear circuit modeling and simulation based on tensor extension of the traditional Volterra series framework for modeling nonlinear responses. Such tensor formulation totally overcomes the curse of dimensionality in traditional Volterra series (previously limited to second or third order kernels), and allows arbitrary high order kernels to be incorporated at essentially linear complexity. Further generic development of the tensor techniques is in nonlinear system identification based on input-output dataset. Such system identification approach can even be extended to other engineering topics including neural network design and image completion, as reflected in the PI's publications after completion of this GRF project.

17212315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17212315.value: This GRF project has been completed very successfully, as is reflected from the quantity and quality of research outputs. The project has produced important results both in the theory for fast tensor decomposition, as well as their practical application enabling the speedup of electronic design automation (EDA) algorithms. In fact, tensors are generalization of 2d matrices to their higher dimensional counterparts, and constitute the most natural form of capturing the inherently high-dimensional data existing in nature and most engineering problems. The PI's developed tensor-based algorithms have resulted in a keynote paper in IEEE transactions, which is in fact the pioneering work to promote tensor algebra in the EDA field. Besides, the tensor techniques have further been extended to generic nonlinear system identification based on the given multi-input multi-output data. Such nonlinear system identification approach is highly scalable and general, with application not only in EDA topics, but also in the latest development in neural network design and image completion, where the networks or images are regarded as systems to be identified. Last but not least, codes and softwares arising from the project have also been released, thus facilitating practitioners to freely make use of these versatile tensor algorithms.

17212415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17212415.value: Learning good priors from motion capture data is an important problem in human motion modelling. Prior models provide crucial additional information for under-constrained problems. For example, solving for human motion data from video inputs can be central for applications ranging for security to game UI, but data from 2D inputs alone are insufficient to recover 3D movements. A model of natural human motion captures our prior belief on whether a movement is natural, and can be used to guide solutions to regions of the motion space corresponding to natural motions. While there has been a large volume of work on fitting probabilistic models to motion data, these models have exhibited limited ability to generalize away from data. For example, a prior model learned from walking data is not in general useful for tracking running or other activities. Depending on the type of model used, even generalizing to different walking styles or individual subjects can be challenging. Fundamentally, these models measure the naturalness of new motions based their proximity to training data, motions not close to training data are often treated as equally unlikely. Alternatively, physical models can differentiate motions more finely based on physical plausibility or effort levels, but are difficult to construct by hand or learn from data. The goal of this research is to show that an effective and generalizable physics-based prior model can be constructed using an energy-based learning framework, where an parameterized energy function is defined for the entire space of motions, with low energy regions corresponding to more preferable motions. Through a parameterized energy surface, learning in these models entail lowering energy for regions near training data while raising energy for other regions. Physical constraints are incorporated in a straightforward fashion by defining terms penalizing residual forces and contact inconsistencies. Furthermore, weighted terms corresponding to movement styles such as relative center of mass possition, angular momentum, and contact force levels are introduced with weights used as model parameters. The outcome of the proposed project is a hybrid physics-based and data-driven method for learning models of human motion that can significantly improve the generalization ability of state-of-the-art motion models. Applications of the motion model include detection of suspicious activity from video and motion synthesis from consumer grade cameras, as well as motion synthesis for entertainment. N/A

17300015.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17300015.value: 关于新特提斯海消失的研究: 印度－欧亚板块碰撞体系模型的改良

17300015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300015.value: * Carry out a paleomagnetism-focused investigation of various ophiolite suites scattered along the Indus River-Yarlung Tsangpo (I-Y) suture in northern India and southern Tibet. * Aim to test several disparate hypotheses that have recently been proposed to explain the configuration of the Neotethys Ocean at key times in the Late Jurassic-Early Eocene, prior to its closure coinciding with India's collision with Asia. * Critically, the various scenarios are all testable with same methodology. * We might also be able to garner insights into how subduction initiates in intra-ocean settings. With regards to "plate tectonics", this process is the one aspect of the theory in which the Earth-Science community acknowledges considerable uncertainty. The 2500-km-long I-Y suture along which the Indian sub-continent accreted to Asia contains numerous remnants of an intra-oceanic arc. Hence, the older view of a simple two-continent/one-ocean convergence system is no longer valid. As a consequence, many researchers incorporate into their regional tectonic models an additional oceanic plate, and at least one more plate boundary. Interestingly, a number of diverse scenarios have been proposed to account for the intra-oceanic arc’s development prior to its collision with northern India around 55 million years ago (Ma; about the time of the Paleocene-Eocene boundary). This ambiguity stems largely from the fact that the paleomagnetic data-base used to deduce the latitude and orientation of the arc at key times in the past is extremely limited. The proposed research project aims to rectify this by carrying out a comprehensive paleomagnetic investigation of numerous arc terranes that are scattered along the I-Y suture, from NE India to NW India via southern Tibet. In parallel, support age-dating (biostratigraphy and radiometric) and geochemical studies will also be undertaken. The data produced will be incorporated into a regional plate reconstruction spanning the Late Jurassic-Early Eocene (160–50 Ma). Such a model will be of considerable value to the numerous researcher investigating the geological development of the Himalayas-Tibet, as well as orogenic systems elsewhere. Furthermore, under favourable circumstances, there is a possibility that we can address the issue of how subduction initiates in intra-oceanic settings. Much debate surrounds this fundamental geotectonic process, and there is a chance that a number of the arc-ophiolite suites we sample were generated when this event took place. Hence, the derived plate model would contribute significantly to our understanding of this high-order geotectonic phenomenon. 长达2500 km的雅鲁藏布江缝合带是由印度板块与欧亚板块碰撞产生的。在此缝合带内，许多海洋内岛弧残迹相继被发现。因此，一个简单的两洲／一洋融合系统的旧观点已不再成立。随后，不少学者开始在他们的区域构造模型中引入附加海洋板块，以及至少一个板块边界。有趣的是，多种不同的可能情景被相继提出，以解释这海洋内弧的发展，但欧亚板块与北印度板块的碰撞早于五千五百万年前开始（Ma, 介于古新世－始新世), 其间却未见足够的数据以支持他们的解释。原因在于目前可以用来确定该岛弧在此期间所处的纬度及方位的古地磁数据极为有限。因此，本项目旨在对聚集在雅鲁藏布江缝合带的多个岛弧区（从印度板块的东北部经由西藏板块南侧直到印度板块的西北部）进行系统的古地磁研究。生物地层和放射性物质的定年以及地球化学的研究也会同时开展。得出的数据将重现该区域板块从晚三叠世到早始新世阶段的发展历史。而得出的模型将会对在喜马拉雅－印度，以及其他的造山系的地质的研究起到不可或缺的指引作用。除此之外， 在有利的条件下，我们还有可能解释岛弧潜没是如何在洋内环境中产生的。由于该基础地质构造过程仍存着很多争议，倘若我们采样中的蛇绿岩属于洋内岛弧产物的话，将会帮助我们进一步了解这一地质现象。

17300215.value: Prof Cumming, Andrew Prof Kaspi, Victoria M. Dr Takata, Jumpei Dr Wang, Zhongxiang

17300215.label: Project Objectives
17300215.value: Comparing the surface temperature of magnetars and high-B RPPs: one major prediction of the magneto-thermal evolution model is that objects possess strong B-fields should show significant crustal heating resulting from field decay. This effect is expected to keep magnetars hotter for longer. We plan to test this with new X-ray observations of magnetars and RPPs. We will measure their surface temperature and compare quantitatively with theory predictions. The results will significantly expand the sample, as only a few strongly magnetized pulsars have temperature measurements so far. Determining the physical conditions of magnetars and high-B RPPs from timing: the physical distinction between different pulsar classes could lie on the toroidal B-field component, which is not directly observable from spin down, but can give rise to complex pulse profiles. In order to test this theory, we will analyse the magnetars and high-B RPPs pulse profiles and quantify their complexity using a Fourier or wavelet technique. We will identify any correlations between the complexity and the surface temperature, field strength, and other physical parameters. Moreover, we will compile a database of magnetar glitches and carry out a statistical comparison with those of radio pulsars. The results will reveal effects of strong magnetic fields on pulsar interior structure. Detecting magnetar emission at long wavelengths: four magnetars have radio pulsations detected, but the emission mechanism remains unclear. We propose new observations to measure the magnetar spectra at high radio frequency. This will fill in the gap between radio and infrared data and indicate any spectral turnover. The results will provide essential inputs for building a physical model. Also, detecting any correlated flux variabilities with emission at other wavelengths will localize the emission site to unveil the emission mechanism. Measuring the hard X-ray spectra of MSPs: the strong magnetic fields at the light cylinders of MSPs result in short plasma instability timescales, which could lead to coherent radio emission in phase with gamma-ray pulsations. The radio waves would inverse-Compton scatter with energetic particles in the magnetosphere to produce X-rays. To test this idea, we propose new observations to measure the hard X-ray spectra of several MSPs. We will search for signatures of inverse-Compton emission. The results will make predictions to the low-frequency radio spectra, which can be tested with the on-going radio studies.

17300215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300215.value: 脈衝星為大質量恒星演化最後期之超新星爆炸所留下之核心。有極强磁場，為研究極端磁力現象之最佳實驗室,在地球上沒法複製。目前已知有超過２千顆脈衝星，大多數周期為１秒及磁場為1e12G。他們越轉越慢,將旋轉動能轉化成寬帶輻射,從無線電到X光到伽瑪射綫,所以又名為自轉驅動脈衝星(RPP)。 近十年間發現了數種跟RPP不同之脈衝星。 此研究計劃將集中於磁星和毫秒脈衝星(MSP)。 磁星為宇宙中最强磁力之物體,可達1e15G。他們由磁場衰减驅動, 表面極高溫, 偶爾有强烈爆炸。 MSP自轉極快, 周期只有數毫秒, 是很老的脈衝星, 從吸積獲取新的角動量。 他們在光速柱面的磁場是所有脈衝星之中最强的。 我們提出一系列觀測去研究磁場對脈衝星之影嚮。 磁星跟毫秒脈衝星非一般的特性使他們成為理想研究對象。 我們已有新觀測數據去量度磁星和強磁場RPP的表面溫度。 目標是判斷磁場對脈衝星溫度演化之影嚮, 及各類不同脈衝星在物理上之區別。 我們亦會研究這些星體的時序特性去估計磁場排列和內部結構。 最後, 我們會提出毫米波磁星觀測和X光MSP觀測去驗証輻射理論。 總括而言, 此研究將揭示磁場在脈衝星內部結構、 演化、和輻射之中所扮演之角式, 結果將提供重要數據去優化脈衝星群族模型, 從而進一步了解超新星物理。

17300215.label: Realisation of objectives
17300215.value: The main goal of this project is to understand effects of magnetic fields on pulsars. We have successfully measured the surface temperature of a magnetar and a high magnetic field pulsar. The results established a clear correlation between temperature and magnetic field strength. This directly confirms the magneto-thermal evolution model that suggests internal heating of the star due to magnetic field decay. We also compiled a comprehensive database of magnetar and high B pulsar temperature and their timing properties. These set an important stage for further theoretical modeling. To detect magnetars at lower frequency, we have awarded observing time with ALMA through a competitive proposal. The source however was not detected. We are proposing new observations of two other magnetars.

We have measured the surface temperature evolution of a magnetar SGR 0501+4516 after outburst (Mong & Ng 2018). 3. 17300215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300215.value: Our study shows clear effect of magnetic field on the surface temperature, which well agrees with theory predictions. On the other hand, magnetic effects on timing properties are less clear. Further theoretical and simulation studies can provide more detailed investigation in this aspect.

17300215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300215.value: Neutron stars are ideal laboratories for testing extreme magnetism. This project aims to determine effects of a strong mangetic field on a star. We found that neutron stars with stronger fields show higher surface temperature, while the effect on their rotational properties is less clear.

17300315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300315.value: Molecular recognition is central to life. It is involved not only in fundamental biological processes such as protein folding, DNA replication, enzyme-substrate interactions, cellular compartmentalization, cellular communications, signaling, etc., but also is important in health technologies such as drug design, targeting and delivery, and diagnostics. By manipulating how molecules can recognize and interact with each other, synthetic systems that can detect and intercept a molecule of interest in a biological sample can be created for the study of their basic chemical biology, physiology and pathology, as well as for the development of potential drugs and diagnostic tools for diseases associated with these molecules. Catecholamines are an important class of neurotransmitters and hormones that play vital roles in many physiological and pathological processes, from cognition and physical responses to neurological disorders and drug addiction. These small organic molecules have no distinct shape and are electrically neutral, and they share the same functional groups (diol and amine) with other common biomolecules, and therefore disentangling catecholamine from a complex biological mixture is a very difficult task. Creating a specific host for a neutral molecule is not trivial and could involve huge design and synthetic efforts. Current bioanalytical techniques for the detection of catecholamines are largely based on chromatographic and electrochemical methods, which are applicable mainly for isolated specimens such as blood or urine, but not in biological environments such as cells, tissues or the whole organism. In this proposal, we will develop a new biocompatible, bioorthogonal and selective recognition strategy for catecholamines. A “binding-induced chemical reaction” approach that includes chemical reactivity as part of the recognition process is proposed for the selective detection of catecholamines in biological environments. The recognition motif will be coupled with different luminophores to selectively recognize and report levels of catecholamine by luminescence. Results from this work will provide not only valuable bioanalytical tools for detecting and imaging catecholamines in various biological samples including blood, urine, living cells and tissues, but also a general recognition strategy for the detection of different bioorganic molecules. The recognition strategy and luminescent catecholamine probes developed in this project will find applications across different chemical and biomedical disciplines including neuroscience, drug design and delivery, chemical sensing, and diagnostics. 兒茶酚胺(包括去甲腎上腺素，腎上腺素和多巴胺)是一類具有兒茶酚的胺類化合物。在生物學上，兒茶酚胺是重要的神經傳遞物質和激素。過高或過低的兒茶酚胺水平均可引致不良徵狀和疾病，例如高血壓和柏金遜症等。故此，兒茶酚胺的辨識和偵測對於研究兒茶酚胺的生理功能和相關疾病的檢測是十分重要的。 這研究項目旨在開發一種與生物體系相容且正交的新型兒茶酚胺辨識策略。作為一種電中性而且細小的有機分子， 選擇性地辨識兒茶酚胺是有著相當的困難。有別於一般單靠主客結合的分子辨識方法，化學活性將在這研究項目中被加進為分子識別的其中一個元素。透過主客結合所誘導的化學反應，我們期望能開發出一種對兒茶酚胺具高度選擇性的辨識策略。通過這方法得到的兒茶酚胺辨識系統將會與各式的發光體耦合，從而得出一系列對兒茶酚胺有著高度選擇性且敏感的化學探針。

17300315.label: Realisation of objectives
17300315.value: The two objects have been successfully realized. For objective 1, a panel of transition metal complexes of iron, copper, manganese and other 3d transition metals supported by tridentate and tetredentate ligands of systematically varied N, O, and S donors have been synthesized and evaluated for their oxidative reactivity towards catecholamines and a range of related compounds. About 20 ligands and 8 transition metal complexes for each ligand with a few different fluorophores (over 200 new compounds) have been synthesized and characterized. An N3S-Cu(II) complex has been identified as a selective catecholamine triggers that upon reaction with catecholamine will lead to an oxidative ether bond cleavage to release a fluorescent reporter. The corresponding N3S-Cu(II) complex-fluorophore conjugates have been subsequently developed into a set of catecholamine probes for imaging the neurotransmitter in different biological samples. These catecholamine probes showed very good selectivity towards the neurotransmitter against a broad range of chemically similar compounds including diols (sugars), amines (e.g. amino acids), glucosamine, biological redox agents (e.g. vitamins, quinones, ascorbate ...etc.) and also metal ions and reactive oxygen and nitrogen species. The photophysical properties of the catecholamine probes can be easily tuned by using fluorescent reporters of different absorption, emission and other properties without compromising the catecholamine reactivity and selectivity, and catecholamine probes of a whole range of emission colour including red, orange, yellow, green, cyan and blue have been developed for multichannel imaging. In addition, ratiometric and bioluminescent probes have also been developed by attaching the catecholamine trigger onto respective luminescent reporters possessing these properties. For objective 2, the catecholamine-induced oxidative ether cleavage was first studied in detail by an integrative approach using a range of physical characterization techniques including fluorescence measurement, HPLC, LCMS, ESI-MS-MS, NMR, UV-Vis, CV, and IR and also kinetics studies. One of the probes (CAP-cyan) has been further evaluated in various biological samples including human plasma, live neurons and also brain slices from mice. CAP-cyan showed a good sensitivity and selectivity in these samples, suggesting that the probe can be applied in the study of the neurotransmitters under biologically relevant conditions. In particular, we have demonstrated that CAP-cyan can successfully visualise an increase in intracellular dopamine level in a cellular model of neuron differentiation. In addition, CAP-cyan has also been applied in imaging the decrease in dopamine in a cellular Parkinson's Disease model.

17300315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300315.value: The major findings from this project are 1) the identification of an N3S-Cu(II) complex as a catecholamine selective trigger and its development into fluorescent catecholamine probes for biological imaging of the neurotransmitter in different biological samples; 2) the development of the metal-based oxidation strategy as a new activity-based recognition of reactive species and small organic molecules that are otherwise difficult to be recognized by conventional host-guest chemistry. In addition to the catecholamine recognition and sensing, we have additionally discovered two other copper complexes that display good selectivity and reactivity towards superoxide and ascorbate, and fluorescent probes for these two species have also been developed. By studying the large library of metal complex-fluorophore conjugates towards a range of biologically relevant species including metal ions, reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, biological redox agents, sugars, amino acids and vitamins, an understanding on the structure-activity relationship of the oxidative reactivity of the metal complexes is also resulted. Findings from this project have been published in international, peer-reviewed journals including one in Chem. Sci. (IF = 9.556) and one in Chem. Commun. (IF = 6.164), and the Chem. Sci. has been selected as a Hot Article by the Editorial Broad and featured by a journal cover art. Another two other manuscripts are under preparation and will be submitted for journal publication soon. The results have also been presented in international conferences in related areas in the form of invited oral presentations and also student poster presentations. In addition, our work has been recognized by the award of Graeme Hanson Early Career Researcher Award in the 8th Asian Biological Inorganic Chemistry Conference, and this project is also part of the Croucher Innovation Award. A US patent based on the metal-mediated oxidation method has also been granted. One graduated MPhil student, and two PhD students (one has submitted his thesis in Aug 2019 and one will submit her thesis in Aug 2020) have been trained on this project.

17300315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300315.value: After identifying the N3S-Cu(II) complex as a selective catecholamine trigger, catecholamine probes of other properties such as localization in a particular organelle, probes for other imaging modality (e.g. MRI, photoacoustic imaging) could also be developed. These different catecholamine selective probes will form an important imaging toolbox for studying the neurotransmitter in different experimental settings. The catecholamine trigger can also be developed into other triggered-release system for the stimulated release of other substances such as drug or active ingredients. On the other hand, by further understanding the mechanistic picture of the copper-based oxidation, new catalytic systems that is triggered by an external co-factor could also be developed. In general, the metal-mediated oxidation triggered by a small external molecule could be developed into a new recognition strategy that complements the conventional host-guest chemistry in the development of new hosts, sensors, and responsive systems.

17300315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300315.value: Catecholamines (i.e. dopamine, adrenaline and noradrenaline) are small molecule neurotransmitter and hormone that play many important physiological roles such as memory, learning, motor control, regulation of heart rate ... etc. An imbalance of catecholamine level is associated with different diseases including ADHD and Parkinson's disease. Bioanalytical methods that can efficiently detect catecholamine in biological samples is therefore of critical importance but current methods are only applicable in extracted sample. In this project, new fluorescent probes that show an enhanced light emission in the presence of catecholamines are developed. The sensing strategy is based on a copper-mediated oxidative release of a non-emissive, caged fluorescent reporter in its emissive state. By fluorescent and microscopic techniques, levels of catecholamine in plasma, cells and tissues can be monitored by using these new catecholamine probes. The structure-activity relationship of the catecholamine trigger, bond cleavage mechanism, and applications of the probes in visualizing changes of dopamine level in cellular models of neuron differentiation and Parkinson's disease were studied. These selective catecholamine probes are important for further unveiling the physiological roles of the small molecule as well as developing new therapeutic and diagnostic strategies for related diseases.

17300415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300415.value: Atomically thin layers of group VI transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDC) have been recognized as a promising material for ultimately thin electronic devices and emerging electronics, particularly the conceptual valley based electronics (Valleytronics). It is widely believed that this family of dichalcogenides MX2 (M=Mo,W; X=S,Se) have similar band structures as well as physical properties. Recent advances reveal intriguing properties arising in monolayers, for example direct band gap, nonzero but contrasting Berry curvature at K(K’) valleys in their Brillouin zone, and spin-valley coupling, etc. These exotic properties make atomically thin TMDC crystals an unprecedented platform for physics study as well as emerging electronics. In this application, we propose to experimentally study the physics properties in 2D TMDCs MX2 (M=Mo,W; X=S,Se) by optical spectroscopy and electric transport including photocurrent, photoluminescence at nonlinear regime, ultrafast absorption/reflection spectroscopy, and nonlinear spectroscopy. The study will experimentally probe electron-electron interactions, intervalley scattering, spin-orbit coupling and the interplay of spin, valley and layer degrees of freedom in monolayer and multilayer TMDCs. Besides, the potential applications of 2D TMDCs in spintronics will be explored with the spin-resolved photocurrent spectroscopy and the electric transport study. The proposed study will be of interest both in fundamental science and in application-oriented researches. 伴随着体系维度的降低所带来的新奇特性以及丰富的物理现象极大的推动了人们对类似层状二维材料的探索。如今，已发现的可稳定存在的超薄二维过渡金属硫化物多达百种，根据不同的化学组分和结构，它们展示着多样的电子态结构以及电学性质，包括半导体、拓扑半金属、金属乃至超导体。而当中作为研究能谷物理的平台，主要集中于半导体型六族过渡金属二硫化物. 此半导体二维层状材料是最具有代表性的类石墨烯二维层状材料，其能带宽度在1.0 电子伏特以上，并且单层存在明显的反演对称性破缺。 本项目计划采用光学探测及电输运的方法对二维六族过渡金属二硫化物的物理性质进行试验研究。研究重点集中于对其能谷自由度， 电子自旋的调控及二维体系中电子间相互作用。研究手段包含偏振分辨荧光光谱，时间分辨的反射光谱及克尔光谱，及电子输运。

17300415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300415.value: 1. Experimental study of the dynamics of spin relaxation in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs). Monolayer TMDs feature a valley degree of freedom, giant spin-orbit coupling, and spin-valley locking. These exotic natures have stimulated efforts of exploring potential applications in conceptual spintronics, valleytronics, and quantum computing. Among all the exotic directions, a long relaxation time of spin and/or valley polarization is critical. The present valley dynamics studies concentrate on the band edge excitons which predominate the optical response due to an enhanced Coulomb interaction in two dimensions. The valley relaxation time of free carriers remains ambiguous. In this Rapid Communication, we use time-resolved Kerr rotation spectroscopy to probe the valley dynamics of excitons and free carriers in monolayer tungsten diselenide. The valley relaxation time of free carriers is found around 2 ns at 70 K, about three orders of magnitude longer than the excitons of about 2 ps, and 15 times larger than that of trions (130 ps). The extended valley relaxation time of free carriers evidences that an exchange interaction dominates the valley relaxation in optical excitations. The pump-probe spectroscopy also reveals an exciton binding energy of 0.60 eV in monolayer WSe2. 2. Realization of spin polarization in monolayer TMDs. Manipulating spin polarization of electrons in nonmagnetic semiconductors by means of electric fields or optical fields is an essential theme of the conceptual nonmagnetic semiconductor-based spintronics. Here we experimentally demonstrate an electric method of detecting spin polarization in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) generated by circularly polarized optical pumping. The spin-polarized photocurrent is achieved through the valley-dependent optical selection rules and the spin–valley locking in monolayer WS2, and electrically detected by a lateral spin–valve structure with ferromagnetic contacts. The demonstrated long spin–valley lifetime, the unique valley-contrasted physics, and the spin–valley locking make monolayer WS2 an unprecedented candidate for semiconductor-based spintronics.

17300515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300515.value: Terrestrial invertebrate and vertebrate fossils, mainly including insects, dinosaurs, pterosaurs, turtles and fish have been discovered from the Cretaceous Laiyang, Qingshan and Wangshi Groups in the eastern part of the Shandong Peninsula since the 1950s. Although most fossils are yet to be well studied, the discoveries from this region have great potential to improve our understanding of the Mesozoic ecosystems in general. In addition to the body fossils, abundant dinosaur and pterosaur tracks are found from these formations. Extensive body fossils and trace fossils from the Laiyang, Qingshan and Wangshi Groups indicate that the paleoecosystem in the eastern part of the Shandong Peninsula thrived during middle-late Mesozoic. Determining the age and duration of these fossil-rich groups using abundant tuffaceous sandstones and interbedded volcanic rocks is critical to understanding several fundamental questions: 1) Were the Laiyang fauna and the Jehol Biota contemporaneous? If not, how to reappraise the hypothesis of the Jehol radiation? 2) When did Psittacosaurus first appear and thrive in the Shandong Peninsula? 3) Was Tsintaosaurus appear in the Late Cretaceous? 4) When did the hadrosaurs first migrate to North China? Reliable radioisotopic ages for these fossil-bearing formations will allow us to address all of these questions. 自1950年起，大量脊椎和無脊椎化石在山東半島的中生代地層中被挖掘出土，儘管這些保存良好、形態各異的化石提供研究中生代環境和物種演化的重要依據，但截止目前為止，化石層的確切年代仍有爭議。本研究旨在調查山東半島東部萊陽組、青山組和王室組的地層對比，期望建立這些含化石地層的高精確年代。

17300515.label: Realisation of objectives
17300515.value: 1. During the first part of the project duration, we obtained more than 10 datable samples from the dinosaur-bearing strata in the Shandong Peninsula and successfully established robust ages for all samples. Our age data indicated that the Laiyang, Qingshan and Wangshi Groups are ~ 125- 100 Ma. Our results enabled to understand Cretaceous ecosystems in this region. 2. Our study reported detrital zircon age distributions from eight sandstones collected from the eastern part of the Shandong Peninsula. Age distributions exhibited four major populations of Paleoproterozoic (2.5-2.4 Ga), Paleoproterozoic (1.9-1.8 Ga), Neoproterozoic (850-700 Ma) and Jurassic to Early Cretaceous (171-107 Ma) ages. We interpreted a maximum depositional age of 107 Ma for the Wangshi Group and a depositional age of 121-120 Ma for the upper Laiyang Group. Age distributions indicated that the Sulu orogenic belt of the East Shandong complex served as the primary source area. Detrital zircon age data also indicate major changes in the types of source material contributed to the Laiyang and Wangshi groups. Based on these shifts, we propose a four stage model for Early Cretaceous evolution of the Jiaolai basin. In this model, subduction of the Pacific plate and associated transform motion on the Tanlu fault influenced the transition from a transpressional to an extensional tectonic setting. 3. In this study the youngest zircon ages analysed from upper Wangshi Group sandstones, date at 107 ± 3 Ma and 111 ± 2 Ma. Age distributions from Lower Wangshi Group sandstones gave minimum ages of 110 ± 3 Ma. No Late Cretaceous zircon ages were detected in the dinosaur-rich Wangshi Group. Given the degree of age overlap among these samples (within 1-sigma error envelopes), as well as their major populations of Early Cretaceous zircons, we interpret the youngest age, 107 ± 3 Ma, as the maximum depositional age for this Group. This 107 Ma constraint on the Wangshi Group is noteworthy, given the relatively wide range of Qingshan Group magmatic ages (125-89 Ma). It is interesting that igneous rocks that younger than 110 are rarely reported in East Shandong, thus these rocks may no attributed to the Wangshi Group. The age gap between maximum depositional and biostratigraphic age estimates demonstrates the need for further radiometric and paleontological analysis of the study area. This analysis can also inform paleontological interpretations of hadrosauroid evolution. Previous studies have specifically suggested that the Hadrosauroidea originated in Asia during the late Early Cretaceous and then migrated to other continents during the Late Cretaceous. Our better geochronological constraints for hadrosaurid-bearing units in the Wangshi Group have offered supporting evidence for (or revision of) the timing of this event. 4. This project supported two PhD students, Jun Wang and Daran Zheng. During their PhD studies, they were both trained to be geochronologists and now are both able to interpret geochronologic data well. Now Dr. Jun Wang is an associate professor at Yunnan University while Dr. Daran Zheng is a postdoc at HKU. This project also provided opportunity for undergraduate students in EASC3417 "Earth Through Time" to learn Mesozoic ecosystems, tectonic history and geochronology. In the Module 1 of EASC3417, students calculated age of rocks by using data provided. After the lab activity, they fully understand the concept and applications of radiometric dating.

17300515.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300515.value: This project has provided robust age determinations for the fossil-rich sediments from the Shandong Peninsula. We interpret a maximum depositional age of 107 Ma for the Wangshi Group and a depositional age of 121-120 Ma for the upper Laiyang Group (Wang et al., International Geology Review, 2016). Our age suggested that the Wangshi and Laying Groups should be correlated with the third and second phases of the Jehol radiation, respectively. This result has refuted widely accepted hypothesis related to the Jehol Biota and allowed to understand the paleobiography in Mesozoic (Wang et al., International Geology Review, 2016). Our age data, furthermore, enabled us to correlate several dinosaur-bearing strata in Central China and has greatly improved our understanding of dinosaurian evolutionary history (Wang et al., GSA Bulletin, 2018). In addition to paleontological implications, this study contributed to tectonic history of East Asia as well. For example, our detrital zircon age data provided critical information reconstructing tectonic background in the Central Sulu orogenic belt (Wang et al., Tectonophysics, 2016). We reported the tectonic history of late Mesozoic post-collisional exhumation in East Asia (Wang et al., Geoscience Frontiers, 2019). Our study provided detailed surface evidence for Paleo-Pacific subduction and associated effects. Furthermore, our geochronologic and geochemical data helped to reconstruct sedimentological and tectonic history in vicinity of the Sulu Orogenic Belt.

17300515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300515.value: This project is successful as we established robust ages for the Cretaceous fossil-bearing beds in East China. Based on the results, we aim to correlate other fossil-rich strata in Central and South Asia. Our ultimate goal is to establish a model for dinosaur migrations during late Mesozoic. To make it possible, we have started field works in Sichuan, Xinjiang of China, and in Mongolia, Myanmar, India and Malaysia. At least 30 datable samples have been collected and processed. We will use suitable dating methods for our samples. In the next 10 years we will provide reliable age determinations for most dinosaur-bearing strata in these regions.

17300515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300515.value: Abundant and well-preserved Cretaceous terrestrial fossils, including insects, various vertebrates, turtles, dinosaurs , dinosaurs eggs and footprints, continue to be discovered from the Laiyang, Qingshan and Wangshi Groups in the eastern part of the Shandong Peninsula since the early 1950s. In this study we established radiometric ages for these fossil-rich strata. Our data indicated that the Shandong Peninsula was a biological hotspot during middle-late Cretaceous. This study has allowed to improve our understanding of Mesozoic ecosystems and paleobiogeography. Furthermore, we provided a new model for the tectonic setting during this critical interval. Our research enabled to re-think the link between life and the natural environment.

17301115.label: Project Objectives
17301115.value: For the three term Fermat type functional equations, try to settle at least one or two of the cases n=6 (for entire solutions), 7 and 8 (meromorphic solutions) with some growth restriction on the functions and hence partially solve the long-standing problem(s) asked by Hayman as well as Gundersen. Try to study the three term Waring-type equations or some sharing sets problems using jet differentials.

17301115.label: Realisation of objectives
17301115.value: For the general Fermat-type functional equation $f^n+g^m+h^l=1$, in a joint paper with Sai-Kee Yeung, applying the method of holomorphic jet differentials, we give a geometric proof on the non-existence of non-trivial meromorphic solutions when $1/n+1/m+1/l le 3/8$. This is the strongest result for the general Fermat-type functional equation so far. For the original Fermat-type functional equation $f^n+g^n+h^n=1$, it turns out that the method of holomorphic jet differentials cannot tackle the case of %n=6$ for entirte solutions and $n=7,8$ for meromorphic solutions. We only prove that no non-trivial meromorphic solutions of order less than $1$ exist for $n=8$, and that no non-trivial entire solutions of order less than $119/117$ exist for $n=6$ by using the Wiman-Valiron theory for vector valued entire functions. These are the strongest results for n=6 and n=8 so far. In a joint paper with my PhD student Jiaxing Huang, we applied the same method of jet differentials to study some problems of unique range sets for functions meromorphic or holomorphic not only on the complex plane but also (with some growth restriction) on parabolic Riemann surfaces. In particular, we obtain sufficient conditions for the equivalence of the unique range set (URS), the uniqueness polynomial (UP) and the strong uniqueness polynomial (SUP) for meromorphic and holomorphic functions. We also give a simpler criteria for the zero set of a polynomial to be a unique range set which is not covered by Fujimoto's work (2000,2003). In this project, the PI also contained some results on other functional and complex differential equations. In a JMAA paper, a characterization on the entire admissible solutions of Pell type functional equation were obtained. In another JMAA paper with Jiaxing Huang, we obtained a partial solution to the Bank's Conjecture (1977) on the hypertranscendence of $Gamma e^h$.

17301115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301115.value: Recently, the PI and Sai-Kee Yeung were able to apply the result that no non-trivial entire solutions of order less than $119/117$ exist for $n=6$ to show that no non-trivial entire solutions exist for $n=6$ when the solution [1,f,g,h] is a Brody curve. 17301115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301115.value: The investigation of the Fermat type functional equation f^n+g^m+h^l=1 in function theory, was motivated by the corresponding equation in number theory. By studying the solutions of this interesting functional equation, one try to develop new methods and results in function theory. These new methods and results in function theory may allow one to tackle other research problems in mathematics (for example the unique range set problems considered in this project).

17301215.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301215.value: (1) My two papers on tournament ranking are devoted to the study of the classical feedback arc set problem on tournaments, which arises in a rich variety of applications and has been a subject of extensive research. In this series of two papers, we have successfully characterized all tournaments with the min-max relation on packing and covering cycles. (This characterization problem was posed as an open problem in the 1980s by two research groups in Europe, even when the tournaments have only five vertices.) Our proof of the main theorem is highly sophisticated and difficult, which takes more than 100 pages in total. So we split this work into two papers: "Ranking Tournaments with No Errors I: Structural Description" and "Ranking Tournaments with No Errors II: Minimax Relation", which have already been published online in J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (JCTB) and is to appear in JCTB in 2020. (Note: JCTB is one of the most influential journals in discrete mathematics. Proofs of some lemmas are given in an online appendix.) (2) In the paper "When is the Matching Polytope Box-Totally Dual Integral" (Math. Oper. Res. 43 (2018), 64-99, with G. Ding and L. Tan), we have successfully characterized all graphs for which the matching polytope is box-totally dual integral, thereby resolving one research problem proposed by Edmonds and Giles in 1984. (Note: The whole proof takes more than 70 pages, part of which is given in an online appendix. Besides, Math. Oper. Res. is a flagship international journal in operations research.) (3) In the paper "Packing Feedback Arc Sets in Tournaments" (in preparation, with G. Ding and Q. Zhao), we obtained a complete characterization of all tournaments with the min-max relation on packing and covering feedback arc sets, which yields a beautiful and deep theorem in combinatorial optimization.

17301215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301215.value: A complete solution to the problem addressed in Objective 4.

17301215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301215.value: The present project has both theoretical interest and practical value. First, the proposed problems are all fundamental and attractive; solution to any of them will yield not only a beautiful mathematical theorem but also a polynomial-time algorithm for the corresponding feedback set or graph bipartization problem on a large class of graphs. The origin of these problems could be traced back to the 1960s, and the study of them has inspired a number of celebrated results in combinatorial optimization, including the Lucchesi-Younger theorem on packing dicuts. A successful completion of this project will also lead to complete solutions to some well-studied and difficult problems in this research direction, such as “which tournaments can be ranked with no errors?” Second, since the proposed research covers a wide spectrum of combinatorics and optimization, in our investigation we have to develop various new solution techniques and exhibit a wealth of new structural properties. As feedback arc set and dijoin are dual concepts when restricted to plane digraphs, our proposed proof of the approximate min-max relation on planar digraph relies heavily on the existence of short cycles, and the graphs with the min-max relation on packing odd cycles have intimate connection with t-perfect graph (as observed by the PI), the techniques and structural properties obtained in this project can certainly be further employed or developed to tackle the well-known Woodall’s conjecture on dijoins, Caccetta-Haggkvist conjecture on cycles, and Schrijver’s problem on t-perfect graphs. Finally, since the feedback set and graph bipartization problems arise in a rich variety of applications, the results obtained in this project can be applied to solve many important real-world problems.

17301415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301415.value: A new class of materials, viz. ion exchange polymers threaded in metal organic framework, will be synthesized and studied for their performance. Combinations of polymers and metal organic frameworks will be selected for the investigations. They include anionic polymers with an amine group, cationic polymers with a sulfate group, and metal organic frameworks of ZIF-8, MIL-101 and others. In addition to different choices of polymer and metal organic frameworks, loadings and molecular weights of polymers will be varied to provide a large set of materials. This provides different chemical and structural variations for determination of structure-performance relationship and identification of optimized materials for enhanced ion exchange applications. The materials will be carefully characterized by a list of analytical instruments including electron microscopes (SEM, TEM), chemical identification (FTIR, NMR, EDX), structural determination (XRD, TEM, EDX mapping), polymer characterizations (GPC), nitrogen sorption porosimetry, and thermal analysis (TGA, DSC). Preliminary results of an anionic PVBTAH~ZIF-8 and a cationic PSS~MIL-101 are excellent with high selectivity and fast kinetics of ion exchange. The key advantages of this class of materials arise from the extra free volume of the linear polymer chain residing in a highly porous matrix, allowing rapid and full interaction with solvent and dissolved ions. 本研究將致力於合成一類新型的穿載於金屬有機框架空間內部的離子交換聚合物；並且探究该類材料的離子交換性能 本研究方案將選擇不同的離子交換聚合物和金屬有機框架進行複合，包括具有銨基團的陰離子交換樹脂，具有磺酸基團的陽離子交換樹脂，以及ZIF-8和MIL-101等金屬有機框架。 用不同的金屬有機框架和聚合物組合，不同聚合物的負載量以及分子量， 可以形成豐富的物質材料。在化學組分與結構方面，這些材料提供了充分的差異性，以供建立起結構-性能之間的聯繫，從而進一步優化離子交換性能。 這些材料將被一系列的儀器進行表徵，包括：電子掃描顯微鏡SEM，電子透射顯微鏡TEM，物質結構測定（X-射線粉末衍射XRD，TEM，X-射線能量彌散譜圖EDX mapping），聚合物表徵（凝膠滲透色譜法GPC），氮氣吸附孔結構测定，熱重分析TGA，差示掃描量熱法DSC。 陰離子PVBTAH~ZIF-8，以及陽離子PSS~MIL-101的初步結果，皆顯示了很高的離子選擇性以及快速的離子交換動力學。這類材料的核心優勢來自於線性聚合物鏈在多孔材料內的額外自由體積,令聚合物與溶劑或離子的快速及充分接觸。

17301415.label: Realisation of objectives
17301415.value: We achieved a one step synthesis of anion exchange polymer threaded in a metal organic framework (MOF) via in situ polymerization of an ionic liquid (IL) monomer. The ionic liquid 3-methyl-1-vinylimidazolium iodide (3MVIm-I) is water miscible and can be easily impregnated into hydrophilic UiO-66 before triggering in situ polymerization to produce the composite. This simple synthesis does not involve an amination step, which was previously required to incorporate anion-exchange function of a polymer threaded into ZIF-8. This method also avoids difficult impregnation of hydrophobic precursors into hydrophilic MOF for in situ ionic liquid formation and their removal. The synthesized P3MVIm-I~UiO-66 composite is tested for anion exchange and cation rejection in aqueous solvent. P3MVIm-I~UiO-66 demonstrates outstanding ion selectivity over pristine UiO-66 and commercial anion exchange resin (Amberlyst A26). Aside the high OH- exchange capacity (6.05 meq g-1), more than 95 % of inorganic anions (AuCl4-) and 90 % of anionic organic dye (Acid Blue 9) are exchanged by P3MVIm-I~UiO-66 within 30 minutes. In addition, there is complete rejection of standalone cationic dye (Rhodamine B) by P3MVIm-I~UiO-66 while the pristine UiO-66 exhibits no such rejection. Crystallinity of the UiO-66 host is retained after impregnation and ion exchange. To correlate performance to structure, we applied molecular dynamics simulations to study the effects of MOF geometry on threaded polymers' behavior. Canonical molecular dynamics simulations are performed to investigate behavior of single-chain and multiple-chain polyethylene glycol (PEG) contained within a cubic framework spanned by polyethylene (PE) chains. This simple model is first of its kind to study the chemical physics of polymer threaded organic frameworks which are materials with potential applications in catalysis and separation processes. For a single chain 9-mer, 14-mer, and 18-mer in a small framework, the PEG will interact strongly with the framework and assume a more linear geometry chain with an increased radius of gyration Rg, compared to a large framework. Interaction between PEG and the framework decreases with increasing mesh size in both vacuum and water. In the limit of an framework with infinitely large cavity (infinitely long linkers), PEG behavior approaches simulations results without a framework. Solvation of PEG is simulated by adding explicit TIP3P water molecules to a 6-chain PEG 14-mer aggregate confined in a framework. The 14-mer chains readily solvated and leach out of a large 2.6 nm mesh framework. There are less water-PEG interactions in a small 1.0 nm mesh framework, as indicated by a smaller number of hydrogen bonds. The PEG aggregate, however, still partially dissolves but is retained within the 1.0 nm framework. The preliminary results illustrate effectiveness of the simple model to study polymer threaded framework materials and to optimize polymer or framework parameters for high performance. We report for the first time a non-biological highly selective MOF membrane with particles of polyelectrolyte threaded in the nanochannel of metal organic framework (polyelectrolyte~MOF) and its selective transport of alkali metal cations. Poly(sodium vinyl sulfonated-co-acrylic acid)~MIL-53(Al) is prepared on anodic aluminium oxide substrate via steps of MOF MIL-53(Al) growth followed by in-situ polymerization. The poly(VS-co-AA)~MIL-53(Al) membrane demonstrates highly specific selectivity in transport of alkali metal cations. Rate of ion transport correlates inversely with the hydrated diameter of the ion reaching a low limiting rate near 0.7 nm hydrated diameter. Charge exclusion is demonstrated with blockage of anion transport under a concentration gradient. The highly uniform porous nanostructure of MOF and ionic function of polyelectrolyte offers the MOF membrane with synergistic selectivity based on exclusion forces of the framework and Coulomb forces from fixed charges of polyelectrolytes in nanochannels.

17301415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301415.value: Syntheses of various pairings of MOF and polyelectrolytes were attempted. A new strategy of synthesizing an anion exchange polymer in a metal organic framework (MOF) without amination was developed via in situ polymerization of an ionic liquid (IL) monomer. The ionic liquid 3-methyl-1-vinylimidazolium iodide (3MVIm-I) is water miscible and can be easily impregnated into hydrophilic UiO-66 before triggering in situ polymerization to produce the composite. The synthesized P3MVIm-I~UiO-66 composite is tested for anion exchange and cation rejection in aqueous solvent. P3MVIm-I~UiO-66 demonstrates outstanding ion selectivity over pristine UiO-66 and commercial anion exchange resin (Amberlyst A26). This work has been published in the journal Microporous and Mesoporous Materials with a manuscript title "Direct Synthesis of Anion-Exchange Polymer Threaded in a Metal Organic Framework through in situ Polymerization of an Ionic Liquid" Other pairs of polyeletrolyte~MOF were synthesized. The MOFs include ZIF-8, UIO-67, MIL- 101, MIL-53 and the polymers include polyynyl sulfonate, polystrene sufonate, polyvynyl carbonxylic acid. Molecular dynamic simulations of a hydrophilic polymer in a simplified model of open framework were performed to investigate the structure-property relationship. A manuscript "Polyethylene oxide in a polyethylene framework: a simple model for simulation studies of a soluble polymer in an open framework" has been published in ACS Langmuir. MIL-53 was successfully grown onto anodized aluminum oxide membrane and threaded with a polyelectrolyte for ion selective membrane applications. The membrane showed high selectivity base on charge and size of hydrated ion. A manuscript has been published in NanoLetts.

17301415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301415.value: Ion exchange materials have been used in water purification, chromatography, metals recovery, and other separation processes. Their performance is critical in technologies related to environmental, biotechnology, and energy. In addition, ion exchange membranes formed from these materials are used in batteries, fuel cells, electrodialysis, and other electrochemical technologies. High selectivity is demanded for these materials so that specific ion can be allowed to be adsorbed or transported. Further examples and extensions have been achieved in this propjectto a new class of materials recently developed in our group. These ion exchange polymers threaded in metal organic framework are synthesized and studied for their performance. This provides different chemical and structural variations for determination of structure-performance relationship and identification of optimized materials for enhanced ion exchange applications. The key advantages of this class of materials arise from the extra free volume of the linear polymer chain residing in a highly porous matrix, allowing rapid and full interaction with solvent and dissolved ions. A special ion-selective membrane we synthesized NaPSS~MIL~53 has achieved transport of alkaline metal cations with very high selectivity that are only achieved with biological ion channels.

17301715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301715.value: Parent-of-origin effect, also known as genomic imprinting, is an important epigenetic factor. More and more genes are found to show parent-of-origin effects. It is believed that more than 1% of all mammalian genes are imprinted. Imprinting effects have been demonstrated in diseases such as Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome, Prader-Willi Syndrome and Angelman Syndrome, and mental disorders. Statistical tests for imprinting have been proposed in the literature. However, these methods either are nonparametric which are often not as powerful as the parametric likelihood approach, or treat extended pedigrees as multiple nuclear families and so information is not fully utilized. In this project, we will employ the conditional logistic regression model and use the parametric likelihood approach to construct the score tests to test for association and imprinting for qualitative (binary) traits using extended pedigrees. The test statistics include the popular transmission disequilibrium test (TDT) for association and the parental-asymmetry test (PAT) for imprinting as special cases. The score tests evaluate the differences in genotype scores and imprinting scores for all discordant pairs (cases versus controls) in an extended pedigree, thus fully utilizing information beyond first-degree relative pairs. This is an improvement over other association and imprinting testing methods where extended pedigrees are treated as multiple nuclear families, and so information is not fully utilized. Furthermore, we plan to include maternal effects, and we will deal with quantitative traits and the X-chromosome in the analysis. Our aim is to establish a theoretical and empirical foundation for using the likelihood approach to test for association, imprinting and maternal effects. Finally, we will apply the proposed methods to analyze real data sets including the Genetic Analysis Workshop 15 (GAW15) data of rheumatoid arthritis in which significant imprinting effects have been observed. 親源效應，又稱為基因印記，是一個重要的後生因素。越來越多的有親源效應的基因被發現，相信哺乳動物的基因至少有1%被印記。很多疾病已經驗證了印記效應的存在，例如貝克威思-威德曼(Beckwith-Wiedemann) 綜合症，普拉德-威利(Prader-Willi) 綜合症和天使人(Angelman)綜合症，精神障礙等。在相關文獻中已經提出了印記效應檢驗的統計方法。然而，這些方法要麼是功效低於參數似然方法的非參數檢驗，要麼把拓展家系當做多個核心家庭，導致很多家系資訊沒有被充分利用。 在本項目中，我們將會在拓展家系的品質（二分類）性狀上運用條件logistic回歸和參數似然法來構建得分檢驗，檢驗關聯和印記效應。檢驗統計量包括檢驗關聯通用的TDT和對於某些特殊病例印記檢驗的PAT方法。在某拓展家系所有的患病和非患病同胞對（病例-對照）中，得分檢驗利用基因型得分和印記得分在其中的差異來進行檢驗，這樣就充分利用了除一級親屬對以外的其它資訊。此方法有效改善了先前方法把拓展家系當做多個核心家庭，導致很多資訊沒有被充分利用的缺陷。進一步，我們計畫在分析中納入母體效應，並處理數量性狀和X染色體。本專案旨在構建一種基於理論和實踐的似然方法來檢驗關聯、印記和母體效應。最後，將提出的方法應用於來自GAW15的類風濕關節炎真實資料，該資料已被發現具有顯著印記效應的位點。

17301715.label: Realisation of objectives
17301715.value: Genomic imprinting, also known as “parent-of-origin” effects, is an important epigenetic factor which can lead to complete or partial deactivation of the maternally or paternally inherited copy of a gene. In this project, we aim to construct powerful tests for association and parent-of-origin effects on autosomes and X chromosomes. For objective 1, we have completely achieved it. We have successfully constructed tests for association for qualitative traits based on extended pedigrees, and for parent-of-origin effects on X chromosome using data from nuclear families and general pedigrees. Note that tests for parent-of-origin effects on autosomes have been constructed for about 20 years, yet no tests have been suggested for the X chromosome. We are the first group of researchers who have successfully tackled this problem. For objective 2, we have also fully achieved it. Statistical methods for the identification of parent-of-origin effects for quantitative traits on the X-chromosome have been proposed. They perform well in real data analysis and in simulation even when Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is violated. For objective 3, we have applied our methods to analyse real data of rheumatoid arthritis from the North American Rheumatoid Arthritis Consortium in which significant imprinting effects on autosomes have been observed. As for the X-chromosome, we analyse the data set of Turner’s Syndrome and satisfactorily findings are obtained. In general, the project was conducted smoothly.

17301715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301715.value: In this project, we have written five paper (see Part C). The first four have appeared, while the fifth one is under “Minor revision”. The major findings and research outcome are given as follows: The conditional likelihood ratio test based on extended pedigrees having the cases (affected by the disease of interest) and controls (unaffected) have been shown to be powerful for testing for association in qualitative traits. However, the test is not applicable when there are parent-of-origin effects. In paper 1, based on a novel decomposition of the genotype score of an individual according to the paternal or maternal allele, we developed a novel statistic to test for association incorporating parent-of-origin effects. The test is found to perform well in simulation studies. In papers 2 and 3, we are aiming at the test for parent-of-origin effects for qualitative traits on the X-chromosome. In paper 2, we proposed the parental-asymmetry test on the X-chromosome (XPAT) based on complete nuclear families. Then we extended the method to deal with incomplete families (one parent is missing) and multiple affected offsprings. These methods were extended to handle general pedigree data (Paper 3). The Monte Carlo pedigree parental-asymmetry test on the X-chromosome was proposed. The proposed methods were investigated through simulation studies and their performance were satisfactory. For practical use, the proposed methods were applied to analyse the rheumatoid data and Turner’s syndrome data. Papers 4 and 5 are on the detection of parent-of-origin effects for quantitative traits on the X-chromosome. In paper 4, the parental-asymmetry test on the X-chromosome (XPAT) was extended to analyse quantitative traits (QXPAT). A class of XPAT-type tests have been developed. Thus, paper 4 unifies the theory of the XPAT method in the analysis of both qualitative and quantitative traits. Recently, we have developed two simple but powerful methods for the identification of parent-of-origin effects for quantitative traits on the X-chromosome (Paper 5). The new methods outperform the QXPAT in almost all the scenarios that we have investigated by simulation.

17301715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301715.value: In this project, we have constructed various tests for parent-of-origin effects on the X-chromosome. In future research, we shall work on test for genetic association on the X-chromosome accounting for parent-of-origin effects and X-chromosome inactivation. Gene-based tests will also be considered.

17301715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301715.value: Genomic imprinting, also known as “parent-of-origin” effects, is an important factor in the study of genetic traits. More than 1% of mammalian genes are believed to show parent-of-origin effects. In this project, we have constructed statistical tests for detecting genetic association accounting for imprinting effects based on extended pedigrees. Empirical studies show that our methods can outperform existing approaches. Although imprinting tests on autosomes have been developed for about 20 years, yet no statistical tests for imprinting effects on the X-chromosome are available in the literature. In this project, we proposed powerful statistical methods for the identification of imprinting effects for qualitative and quantitative traits on the X-chromosome.

17301815.label: Project Objectives
17301815.value: Time-resolved absorption (fs-TA and ns-TA) and TR3 spectroscopy experiments will be performed to investigate the photoredox and/or photodeprotection reactions of derivatives of selected benzophenone (BP) and anthraquinone (AQ) compounds so as to characterize the excited states and reactive intermediates and reaction mechanisms for the compounds of interest. Time-resolved absorption (fs-TA and ns-TA) and TR3 spectroscopy experiments will be done to investigate how the substituent and leaving group properties influence the deprotection reactions of ketoprofen (KP) based phototrigger compounds in aqueous solutions of varying pH. This will help better understand how substituents with varying properties and located at different positions will affect the behavior and outcome for the photodeprotection reactions of interest. Time-resolved absorption (fs-TA and ns-TA) and TR3 spectroscopy experiments will be performed to investigate benzophenone alcohols like 2-(3’-benzoyl)phenethyl alcohol that undergo a base catalyzed elimination of formaldehyde and form a 3-methylbenzophenone side product. Experiments will also be done in aqueous solutions of varying pH values in order to better understand why this reaction only appears to be appreciable in strongly basic and acidic solutions but only trace amounts of the reaction were observed in neutral and slightly basic aqueous solutions. Time-resolved absorption (fs-TA and ns-TA) and TR3 spectroscopy experiments will be done to study photoenolization based photorelease reactions for selected ortho-alkyl substituted aromatic carbonyl compounds that have a good leaving group on the ortho-alkyl substituent or the -position next to the aromatic carbonyl in aqueous solutions of varying pH values. This work aims to develop an improved understanding of the reaction mechanisms, and what role the water and pH conditions play in the photoenolization reactions and the release mechanism(s) of interest. Time-resolved absorption (fs-TA and ns-TA) and TR3 spectroscopy experiments will be performed to examine photoenolization based photorelease reactions for selected ortho-alkyl substituted aromatic carbonyl compounds in which the cleavage of the leaving group occurs by intramolecular relactonization of the photoenol alcohol group with an ester moiety. This work will help gain a better understanding of the reaction mechanisms and the role water and pH conditions play in the photoenolization and intramolecular relactonization of the photoenol alcohol group with an ester moiety. The accumulated experimental and computational results gained in objectives 1-5 will be compared to each other in order to help determine similarities and differences in their excited states, intermediates, substituent effects and pH dependence for their associated photochemistry. This may be helpful to determine promising trends and/or properties that may be useful to explore in the design of improved photoredox and photodeprotection compounds for use in particular applications with certain aqueous pH conditions.

17301815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301815.value: Several classes of aromatic carbonyl compounds have been observed to undergo unusual photoredox and/or photodeprotection reactions in aqueous solutions and water appears to play a crucial role in enabling these kinds of reactions since they do not occur appreciably in non-protic organic solvents. In a number of these photoredox and photodeprotection reactions for the aromatic carbonyl compounds of interest, the reactions may occur within a limited pH range which further indicate that the form of the ground state molecule and/or protonation and/or deprotonation in the excited states may also play important roles in enabling these novel reactions to occur to an appreciable extent. The photoredox redox reactions of interest involve distal functional groups where water facilitates the photoreox to occur over a noticeable distance and this may be useful in some organic synthesis applications. The variety of photodeprotection reactions of interest here may find utility in applications like initiating protein folding and unfolding, drug delivery and phototriggers to study biological processes. In order to be able to better utilize the potential applications for these kinds of aromatic carbonyl compounds, it is important to have a much better understanding for how they work. Most of the research done on the compounds of interest has involved mainly product analysis studies and in some cases nanosecond time resolved transient absorption to observe some intermediate species. However, the ultrafast (eg femtosecond and picosecond time scales) processes have not been explored experimentally and almost all of the intermediates have not been clearly identified using structural information from time-resolved vibrational spectroscopy techniques (like time-resolved resonance Raman or time-resolved infrared spectroscopy). To obtain this missing information, we propose to use a combination of femtoseond and nanosecond time resolved transient absorption and time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy methods to directly observe, characterize and identify the excited states and intermediates from femtoseconds to final products. This new data combined with results from quantum mechanical calculations for the structure and properties of these species as well as reaction pathways connecting them can be employed to better interpret the experimental results and develop an improved and more comprehensive understanding of the reactive intermediates and reaction mechanisms for the photoredox and photodeprotection reactions of interest. This new information will also help develop a much better understanding of the role water plays in enabling these reactions to take place and in the design and development of improved photodeprotection compounds for particular applications. 芳香羰基化合物的光化學反應是光化學研究的一個重要的領域，目前，有幾類芳香羰基化合物已經被觀察到能夠在水溶液裡發生異常的光氧化還原反應和光去保護反應，水在這些反應中起到了非常關鍵的作用。如果在非水的有機溶劑中，就不能明顯地發生這些反應。並且，許多重要的芳香羰基化合物的光氧化還原反應和光去保護反應只能在一定的pH範圍時才會可以發生，這進一步表明基态分子的存在的形式和/或激發态的質子化和/或去質子化也是使這些新型的光氧化還原和光去保護反應高效發生的重要因素。有趣的是有些遠距離的官能團也能參與了芳香羰基光氧化還原反應，水分子能夠促使光氧化還原反應在遠距離發生，這對於一些有機合成來說非常有用。各種類型的光去保護反應也具有非常廣闊的應用前景，如誘導蛋白的折疊和展開，藥物的運輸，光控開關研究生物的過程等。為了更好地開發芳香羰基化合物的作為光去保護反應的潛在應用，非常有必要探索和理解這些反應的機理。目前絕大部分對芳香羰基化合物的光化學研究都僅限於光照後的產物分析，有一些研究也僅利用納秒瞬态吸收光譜探測到一些反應中間體。然而，在實驗上，還從來沒有探索過芳香羰基化合物的光氧化還原反應和光去保護反應的超快過程，並且也未用時間分辨振動光譜技術（如時間分辨共振拉曼光譜或時間分辨紅外光譜）獲得全部瞬态中間體的結構信息並歸屬它們。為了獲得這些信息，我們計劃結合飛秒和納秒瞬态吸收光譜和時間分辨共振拉曼光譜技術直接考察，表徵和鑑別從飛秒時間範圍到最後產物全過程的激發态和瞬态中間體。並結合量子化學模擬計算可以提供瞬态物種的結構信息和反應性質以及獲得光化學反應的路徑，這使我們能更好地解釋和理解實驗結果，使我們能夠對光氧化還原反應和光去保護反應中的反應中間體和反應機理有更深和更全面的認識。同時，這些新的信息和結果也能幫助我們更好地理解水在促進這些反應的作用，並設計和發展出能應用於特殊領域的更好的光去保護化合物。

17301815.label: Realisation of objectives
17301815.value: We have essentially achieved and attempted to achieve all of the objectives of this project and have accumulated a lot of new spectroscopic and computational data that has enabled an increased understanding of the excited states, intermediates and reactions of interest for this project for a range of different aromatic carbonyl and related molecules. The research results from this project include a large amount of time-resolved transient absorption (TA) and time-resolved emission (TRE) spectroscopy data that were employed to directly observe and characterize the electronic state character of the electronic excited states and reactive intermediates associated with the photochemistry of the aromatic carbonyl and related molecules investigated in this project. These time-resolved electronic methods were also employed to examine the growth and decay kinetics of the species observed for the photochemical reactions studied. In order to gain a deeper characterization and understanding of the structures and properties of the species seen in the time-resolved electronic spectra (TA and TRE), time-resolved resonance Raman (TR3) spectroscopy was utilized to obtain vibrational spectra which can be used to more clearly identify and structurally characterize the reactive intermediates observed in the time-resolved spectroscopy experiments. Density functional theory (DFT) computations were also employed to investigate and estimate the structures, vibrational frequencies and spectra, electronic absorption energies. DFT calculations were also employed to explore the reaction pathways and energy barriers to reactions of interest. Comparison of the DFT results to the experimental time-resolved spectroscopic data was used to aid in the interpretation of the experimental data and in deducing the reaction mechanisms and gain more insight into the reactive pathways and properties of the reactive intermediates and their chemical reactivity. This work addressed and essentially achieved all six objectives of this project. Time-resolved spectroscopic investigations and correlated DFT computational studies on the photochemistry and reaction intermediates were performed for a variety of aromatic carbonyl compounds like selected benzophenone (BP), anthraquionone (AQ) ketoprofen (KP) derivatives as well as selected related heterocyclic molecules like hydroxyquinolinyl derivatives in varying solutions and pH conditions. This work fully addressed objectives 1, 2, 3 (eg selected benzophenone (BP), anthraquionone (AQ) ketoprofen (KP) derivatives) respectively. Some of the BP and AQ derivatives along with selected related heterocyclic molecules like hydroxyquinolinyl derivatives addressed the objectives 4,5 and 6. The research for this project resulted in 10 publications in international referred journals, presentations at 2 international conferences and three PhD students being trained. The details of the project results and findings are presented in part C of this report.
