17301815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301815.value: First, work was done to directly observe the excited states that then produced the unusual triplet states and biradical intermediates involved in the water assisted photoredox reactions of selected BP and AQ systems in aqueous solutions. The experimental and theoretical results in neutral aqueous solutions determined that a proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) taking place from an alcohol C−H bond to the para-carbonyl is the important step for the photoredox reaction of 2-(1-hydroxyethyl)-anthraquinone (HEAQ) to take place whereas the correlated 3-(hydroxymethyl)-benzophenone (3-BPOH) compound undergoes a different PCET from an alcohol O−H bond to its carbonyl as its important step that is followed by an intersystem crossing process that does not lead to the analogous photoredox. These different behaviors by the BP AQ derivatives appears to be due to an interesting charge-radical coupled effect. This work addressed Objectives 1, 4, 5 and 6, reported in publications 1 and 5 and the first PhD thesis given in Part C of this report. Further time-resolved spectroscopy and DFT computations were done to examine selected BP and AQ derivatives that lead to photocleavage reactions in aqueous solutions that are of interest for the development for various potential applications. This work lead to direct observation of triplet states and biradical intermediates with varying properties due to substituent effects and/or solvent effects that gave rise to the photocleavage and/or photosubstitution reactions of the BP and AQ derivatives examined. This research addressed objectives 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 and reported in publications 2, 3, 4 and 9, two international conference presentations and the second PhD thesis. Additional time-resolved spectroscopy experiments and DFT calculations were done to directly observe and characterize excited states and intermediates involved in the photodeprotection reactions of selected HQ derivatives. This work found that some tertiary amines attached to the 8-cyano-7-hydroxyquinolinyl (CyHQ) could make photoactivatable forms appropriate for employment in investigating cell physiology with an example being the photoactivation of tamoxifen and 4-hydroxytamoxifen could be utilized to activate Cre recombinase and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing. These new photoactivatable compounds were found to be highly efficient in their release from a singlet excited state of CyHQ on the 70 ps time scale of biological effectors via both one- and two-photon excitation (1PE and 2PE). This research addressed objectives 2, 5 and 6, reported in publications 6, 7 and 10, international conference 2 and the third PhD thesis. Further publications are in preparation.

17301815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301815.value: There is a great deal of potential for further development that can emerge from this projects results. Time-resolved spectroscopy methods allowed the direct observation and characterization of the electronic excited states and reactive intermediates for the photochemical reactions. This new knowledge has potential to be utilized to develop new chemistry. Selected benzopehenone and anthraquinone compounds (publications 1 and 5 in part C of this report) were determined to undergo very efficient photoredox reactions with quantum yields of up to 0.6 for distal functional groups. Additional research can be performed in collaboration with synthetic groups new work can be done to optimize new molecules for particular applications like in the synthesis of selected target compounds. Other selected benzophenone, anthraquinone and ketoprofen molecules (publications 2, 3, 4 and 9 in part C) and also selected hydoxyquinonline derivatives (publications 6, 7 and 10 in part C) have potential for being developed for use as photoremovable protecting groups in important applications as phototrigger compounds. Similarly, further research can be done in collaboration with synthetic groups to synthesize new related molecules to optimize them for particular applications in photolithography, to study some chemical biology processes, drug release and/or some physiology processes.

17301815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301815.value: Photocleavage reactions can be important tools in the release of biological effectors in chemical biology, in physiology experiments and in drug release. In order to better apply and make improved versions of these kinds of molecules for photocleavage reactions, it is important to ascertain the identity, structure and properties of the reaction intermediates and the reaction mechanism(s) associated with the photocleavage reactions and these are not yet clear for many new molecules being designed and synthesized for different applications. This project employed time-resolved transient absorption, time-resolved emission and/or time-resolved resonance Raman spectroscopy to directly investigate and characterize the reactions of selected benzophenone, anthraquionone, ketoprofen derivatives and hydroxyquinolinyl derivatives in varying solutions and pH conditions to obtain this missing information regarding excited states, intermediates and reaction mechanisms for their photocleavage reactions. These results have led to a deeper and improved understanding of the properties and chemical reactivity of important reaction intermediates. This project has gained a better understanding of solvent and hydrogen bonding effects on the reaction intermediates and reaction mechanisms of interest. This new information can help in improving the utilization and development of improved aromatic carbonyl and hydroquinoline molecules for photocleavage reactions for particular applications in the future.

17301915.label: Project Objectives
17301915.value: To determine the spatial distribution and relationships of Paleozoic plutons and volcanic rocks in the Bayan Obo, Chengde and Yitong areas, which are located in the western, middle and eastern parts of the northern margin of the North China Craton, respectively; To carry out extensive field-based structural investigations on Paleozoic complexes at the northern margin of the North China Block and determine the nature of major structural episodes through detailed structural analysis, especially on the early deformation phases which are critical to determining the polarity of the subduciton if the Paleo-Asian Ocean was indeed subducted beneath the northern margin of the North China Block; To probe the geochemical characteristics of Paleozoic plutons and volcanic rocks in the Bayan Obo, Chengde and Yitong areas in order to investigate whether they have affinities to continental margin arcs; To utilize LA-ICP-MS/ SHRIMP U–Pb zircon geochronology combined with cathodoluminescence (CL) imaging to determine the rock-forming ages of Paleozoic plutons and volcanic rocks in the Bayan Obo, Chengde and Yitong areas in order to determine when the southward subduction of the Paleo-Asian Ocean beneath the northern margin of the North China Block started if such subduction did exist; On the basis of the above studies, to establish a comprehensive tectonic model for the Paleozoic evolution of the northern margin of the North China Block in association with expansion and closure of the Paleo-Asian Ocean.

17301915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301915.value: The Paleo-Asian Ocean was a long-lived Neoproterozoic to Paleozoic ocean, whose opening was related to the breakup of Rodinia and whose expansion and closure led to the development of the Central Asian Orogenic Belt and the collision of Tarim-North China and East Europe-Siberia, respectively. In the last two decades, researchers have carried out extensive investigations on the Paleo-Asian Ocean/Central Asian Orogenic Belt and produced large amounts of new data and competing models. However, a number of geological issues are still unresolved and remain controversial, which has significantly hampered further understanding the history of the Paleo-Asian Ocean and the formation and evolution of the Central Asian Orogenic Belt. One of such important issues is whether or not the eastern segment of the Paleo-Asian Ocean underwent southward subduction beneath the northern margin of the North China Craton before its final closure, and if such southward subduction did happen, when did it start and how long it lasted? This proposed project aims to resolve these controversial issues through an integrated geological and seismic imaging study on the northern margin of the North China Craton. Specifically, we will carry out extensive field-based structural, petrological, geochemical and geochronological investigations on Paleozoic plutonic and volcanic rocks from three key areas (Bayan Obo, Chengde and Yitong) in the western, middle and eastern segments of the northern margin of the North China Craton in order to determine when these rocks formed and whether or not they were arc-related, developing on a subduction zone. We will also combine our geological results with seismic reflection data recently collected through the SinoProbe Program (Deep Exploration in China) for the northern margin of the North China Cratona and the Soloker-Xar Moron Suture Zone, which is considered to have resulted from the closure of the eastern sector of the Paleo-Asian Ocean between North China and Siberia. The outcomes of this project will not only determine whether or not and when the Paleo-Asian Ocean was subducted beneath the northern margin of the North China Craton, but will also provide important insights into understanding of Phanerozoic crustal growth in East Asia. 古亚洲洋是一个长期活动的晚元古代至古生代大洋；它的开启与Rodinia超大陆裂解有关，而它的扩张和闭合分别导致中亚造山带的形成和塔里木-华北与东欧-西伯利亚的拼合。在过去20年里，研究者对古亚洲洋/中亚造山带开展了广泛研究并取得大量的新数据和有说服力的模式。尽管如此，仍然有若干地质问题没有得到解决并存争议，这极大地限制了对古亚洲洋演化历史和中亚造山带形成与演化的进一步认识。其中一个重要问题就是古亚洲洋的东段在闭合前究竟是否向南俯冲到华北克拉通之下；如果存在这样的向南俯冲，俯冲是何时开始及持续多长时间？本项目是想通过对华北克拉通北缘的地质和地震图像解译研究来解决这些地质问题。具体来说，我们是想通过对华北克拉通西段、中段和东段三个关键地区（白云鄂博、承德和伊通）的古生代深成岩和火山岩的构造学、岩石学、地球化学和同位素年代学研究，以确定这些岩石何时形成以及是否形成于俯冲带上的岩浆弧环境，并将这些地质研究结果与最近通过“中国深部探测计划”项目获得的华北北缘和华北与西伯利亚之间的索伦克-西拉木伦缝合带（古亚洲洋东段闭合带）的地震反射数据进行对比，这些研究结果不仅有助于确定古亚洲洋是否和何时向华北克拉通北缘下面俯冲，而且对于理解东亚大陆显生宙地壳生长提供新的窗口。

17301915.label: Realisation of objectives
17301915.value: We have successfully completed all parts of the five objectives designed for this project as follows: Objective 1 is to determine the spatial distribution and relationships of Paleozoic plutons and volcanic rocks in the western, middle and eastern parts of the northern margin of the North China Craton (NCC). This objective was completed through four times of fieldwork (May 12-June 3, 2016; October 13-21, 2016; April 13-20, 2017; and June 13-July 1, 2018). In the field, the Principal Investigator (Guochun Zhao), three CIs (Yanhong He, Jian Zhang and Shihong Zhang) and their postgraduates carried out extensive reconnaissance of Paleozoic plutons and volcanic rocks in the western, middle and eastern parts of the northern margin of the North China Craton, where we mapped out the spatial distribution of Paleozoic plutons and volcanic rocks. Such large-scale mapping has led to important discovery of adakites and high-Mg andesite that are typical arc-related rocks. During the fieldwork, we collected ~800 samples for further petrographic, structural and geochronological studies. Objective 2 is to carry out extensive field-based structural investigations on Paleozoic complexes at the northern margin of the North China Craton in order to determine the nature of major structural episodes and the polarity of the subduciton. This objective was completed by detailed structural investigations along the northern margin of the North China Craton. During the four times of fieldwork, we identified three episodes of deformation (D1 to D3) in the western, middle and eastern parts of the North China Craton, of which D1 is represented by small isoclinal and recumbent folds, D2 produced large-scale asymmetric folds and an associated penetrative axial planar foliation, and D3 is indicated by open to tight folds of varying scales, axial crenulation cleavages and thrust faults. A paper entitled “Double-sided divergent subduction of the Paleo-Asian Ocean subduction: Insights from thrusting structures at the northern margin of the North China Craton” by Jian Zhang, Guochun Zhao and Yanhong He has just submitted to Journal of Structural Geology. Objective 3 is to probe the geochemical characteristics of Paleozoic plutons and volcanic rocks in the western, middle and eastern parts of the North China Craton in order to investigate whether they have affinities to continental margin arcs. This objective has been completed through detailed major, trace and REE analysis and isotopic studies on Paleozoic plutonic and volcanic samples collected from the western, middle and eastern parts of the North China Craton during the four times of fieldwork. The results of our geochemical studies show that these Paleozoic plutonic and volcanic rocks from the western, middle and eastern parts of the North China Craton have affinities to modern magmatic arc rocks, which indicates that the Paleo-Asian Ocean was indeed subjected to southward subduction beneath the northern margin of the North China Craton, and thus supports the divergent double-sided subduction model for the Paleo-Asian Ocean. Totally 10 papers reflecting the research outcomes of this objective have been published (see Research Outputs No1, No.3, No. 4, No. 6, No. 7, No. 9, No. 11, No. 12, No.18, No. 22 in the next section). Objective 4 is to utilize LA-ICP-MS/ SHRIMP U–Pb zircon geochronology combined with cathodoluminescence (CL) imaging to determine the rock-forming ages of Paleozoic plutons and volcanic rocks on the northern margin of the NCC in order to determine when the southward subduction of the Paleo-Asian Ocean beneath the northern margin of the North China Craton started and when the closure of the Paleo-Asian Ocean occurred. Our dating results demonstrate that the southward subduction of the Paleo-Asian Ocean beneath the northern margin of the North China Block was mainly operative during Late Paleozoic time, whereas the final closure of the ocean occurred at 280-265 Ma in its western segment and 260-245 Ma in its eastern segment. The research outcomes of this objective have led to publication of three papers (see Research Outputs Nos. 1-4, Nos. 11-12, Nos. 17-18). Objective 5 is to establish a comprehensive tectonic model for the Paleozoic evolution of the northern margin of the North China Block in association with expansion and closure of the Paleo-Asian Ocean. This objective was successfully completed with a scissor-like closure model we proposed for the Paleo-Asian Ocean in which the closure of the western, central and eastern segments of the ocean occurred along the Tianshan, Beishan and Solonker suture zones at 310-280 Ma, 285-265 Ma and 260-245 Ma, respectively (see Research Outputs No. 3, No. 11, No. 15, No.23, No. 24, No. 25). Two comprehensive review papers on when the southward subduction of the Paleo-Asian Ocean beneath the northern margin of the North China Craton started and when the closure of the Paleo-Asian Ocean occurred have been published in Earth-Science Reviews (see No. 15 and No. 16 in Research Output in next section).

17301915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301915.value: In the last three years, the PI and his research group have carried out extensive and comprehensive investigations on Paleozoic plutons and volcanic rocks in the western, middle and eastern segments of the northern margin of the North China Craton (NCC) and produced large amounts of new data and interpretations which are reflected in 25 refereed papers published in leading international journals including Geology, Tectonics, GSA Bulletin, Earth-Science Reviews, etc (see Publications listed in Part C). We summarize our major findings and research outcomes as follows: 1. The eastern segment of the Paleo-Asian Ocean was subducted beneath both the northern margin of the North China Craton and the southern margin of the Mongolian Terrane bordering the Siberia Craton, and was finally closed along the Solonker Suture Zone, leading to the collision of North China with Mongolian Terrane (Siberia) at about 260-245 Ma (see Research Outputs No. 16). 2. The central segment of the Paleo-Asian Ocean was subducted beneath both the northern margin of the Alxa Terrane and the southern margin of the Mongolian Terrane, and was finally closed along the Beishan Suture Zone, leading to the collision of the Alxa Terrane with the Mongolian Terrane at about 280-265 Ma (see Research Outputs No. 3, No. 4, No. 11, No. 12 and No. 22). 3. The closure of the western segment of the Paleo-Asian Ocean (Junggar and South Tianshan oceans) occurred along the Western and Eastern Tianshan orogens at 310-285 Ma, leading to the collision of the Tarim Craton with the Central Tianshan-Yili-Hasakstan Block (See Research Outputs No. 8, No.15, Nos. 23-25). 4. Based on new data produced in this project and previous data, we proposed the scissor-like closure of the Paleo-Asian Ocean from west to east during the period of 310-245 Ma, leading to collision of Tarim with the Kazakhstan-Yili-Central Tianshan Block at 310-285 Ma, Alex (plus Central Qilian and Qaidam) with the Mongolia Terrane (Siberia) at 280-265 Ma , and North China with the Mongolia Terrane (Siberia) at 260-245 Ma (see Research Outputs Nos. 14-16).

17301915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301915.value: Our results from this project confirm the scissor-like closure of the Paleo-Asian Ocean from west to east during the period of 310-245 Ma, leading to the amalgamation of the North China and Tarim blocks in the south and the Siberia and East European blocks in the north. In the same period, Gondwana in the south amalgamated with Laurasia in the north to form the Pangea supercontinent. This demonstrates that North China and Tarim blocks were involved in the assembly of Pangea, contrasting with previous models that placed all East Asian blocks out of Pangea, existing as isolated blocks surrounding the Paleo-Tethyan Ocean. Whether or not the model proposed from this project is correct can be tested by paleomagnetic data for North China and Tarim blocks. This forms a justification for a potential RGC GRF project entitled ““Paleomagnetic study on the Neoproterozoic and Paleozoic rocks at the northern margin of the North China and Tarim cratons, which will be submitted to RGC in future.

17301915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301915.value: The Paleo-Asian Ocean was a long-lived ocean once existing between the East European and Siberian blocks in the north and the Tarim and North China blocks in the south, with its opening related to the breakup of Rodinia in the mid-Neoproterozoic and its expansion and final closure leading to the formation of the Central Asian Orogenic Belt and collision between Tarim-North China and East Europe-Siberia, Respectively. However, controversy has long surrounded the timing of collision of North China-Tarim and Siberia-East Europe. In this Hong Kong RGC GRF project (17301915), by carrying out extensive field-based structural, petrological, geochemical and geochronological investigations on Paleozoic plutonic and volcanic rocks in the western, middle and eastern segments of the northern margin of the North China Craton, we determined the middle and eastern sectors of the Paleo-Asian Ocean underwent southward subduction, finally leading the northern margins of the Alxa and North China blocks to collide with the Mongolian Terane (boarding Siberia). The results of this project lead us to propose a new model for the scissor-like closure of the Paleo-Asian Ocean from the west (310-280 Ma), through the middle (280-265 Ma), to east (270-240 Ma) segments.

17302115.value: Fabricate the Cu-doped ZnO by the PLD method, and characterize the structural and magnetic properties. Study for all the origins contributed for the FM. 17302115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302115.value: High Curie temperature (TC) dilute magnetic semiconductor (DMS) has received intensive attention because of its potential in spintronic applications. After the theoretical prediction of room temperature ferromagnetism (RTFM) in transition metal (TM) doped ZnO, extensive effort has been devoted to realize the genuine carrier mediated DMS exhibiting intrinsic RTFM. Despite of the observation of RTFM in TM-doped ZnO reported, the origin of the RTFM has been questioned to be coming from the extrinsic origins like the clustering of the magnetic dopant TM metal or the formation of secondary phase. Cu-doped ZnO is an interesting candidate for DMS. Cu metal and its oxides are not magnetic. There have been theoretical and experimental studies reporting for the RTFM for Cu-doped ZnO. The understanding of the RTFM in Cu-doped ZnO is far from complete. It is known that defects play important role in influencing the RTFM, but the detail is still missing. In some preliminary study, we have already achieved fabricated Cu-doped ZnO exhibiting RTFM. Adopting both the experimental and theoretical approach, the present project aims to study the physics behind observed RTFM in Cu-doped ZnO. Attention will be given to identifying the secondary phase and spinodal decomposition, exploring the origins of the FM, and understanding the relevant exchange mechanism. We also aim to produce a genuine Cu-doped ZnO based DMS exhibiting carrier mediating RTFM. 高居里温度稀磁半导体由于其在自旋电子领域的潜在应用受到了广泛关注，理论推测过渡金属掺杂ZnO具有室温铁磁性，因此实验研究一直致力于实现载体介导稀磁半导体的室温铁磁性。迄今为止，实验中已经实现了通过掺杂过度金属制备出具有室温铁磁性的ZnO，但是室温铁磁性的磁性机理一直存在疑问，例如过渡金属形成团簇或者第二相的存在。Cu掺杂ZnO一直是稀磁半导体的候选体系之一。 虽然Cu及其氧化物不具有磁性，但是实验和理论研究发现Cu掺杂ZnO体系可以实现室温铁磁性，对CuZnO体系铁磁性起源机理的解释在不断发展但一直不够完善。众所周知，缺陷对室温铁磁性有很大的影响，但是细节方面却一直不得而知。我们已经初步实现了Cu掺杂ZnO的室温铁磁性，现在的研究致力于这种铁磁性的物理解释，例如确定材料中第二相及其转变分解，和探索交互作用机制。除此之外，我们还致力于制备具有载体介导室温铁磁性的Cu掺杂ZnO。

17302115.label: Realisation of objectives
17302115.value: We have systematically study the Cu-doped ZnO using PLD with different Cu composition of ceramic target (Cu=1, 2 and 4 wt%) and different oxygen abundance (oxygen pressures PO2=0-0.05Pa). A comprehensive spectroscopic approach including SQUID, XRD, HRTEM, XPS, XANES and Hall effect measurement was adopted to reveal the samples’ magnetic properties, structural properties, oxygen vacancy VO abundance, Cu_{2+}:Cu_{+} oxidation state occupancy ratio, and electron concentration. For the room temperature ferromagnetic (RTFM) ZnO:Cu samples grown with Cu=4 wt%, CuO nanocrystal (~4 nm) was identified by the XRD peak and the HRTEM Morie fringe. Moreover, bifurcation of the zero field cooled and field cooled (ZFC/FC) magnetic data below the superparamagnetic blocking temperature of ~210 K indicated the presence of nanocrystal with size of ~7 nm. These works started in May 2014 before the GRF application submission. Some data were included in the application proposal as preliminary results. After submitting the application, the work continued and resulted in a paper submitted in May 2015 and accepted in June 2015 (before the GRF awarded), and thus the GRF grant was not acknowledged. For the samples grown with Cu=1 and 2 wt%, no secondary-phase XRD peak, Morie fringe in TEM image was found. For the Cu=2wt% and 4wt% samples, influences of PO2 (0-0.05 Pa) on the electron concentration, VO abundance, relative Cu_{2+} occupancy and magnetic properties were studied. The electron concentration, VO abundance and relative Cu_{2+} occupancy decreased with increasing PO2. However, the magnetization did not show monotonic change with PO2. The sample grown with PO2=0.025Pa had clear RTFM with saturation magnetization MS~1.1 μ_B/Cu. For the samples grown with other PO2’s (0, 0.015 and 0.05), the magnetization were very small (~0-0.1 μ_B/Cu). It is surprising that the MS does not increase with the Cu_{2+} abundance which has incompletely filled 3d^{9} orbital. The Al/ZnO:Cu/ZnL:Ga/c-sapphire cell structure array sample was fabricated by PLD with Cu=4wt%. The ZnO:Ga film was used as the transparent electrode. The cell sample exhibited reversible non-volatile resistive switching between low resistance state (LRS) and high resistance state (HRS) by applying +4V and -4V respectively. Non-volatility cycling test showed the non-volatile resistance state maintained at least 2 hours after the resistance state was set and then with the electric bias removed. SQUID, XPS, XANES and PL measurements were performed while the cell structure array sample was sequentially set as HRS, LRS and then HRS to investigate the magnetic property, V_{O} abundance and relative Cu_{2+} occupancy. The MS (measured by SQUID), the relative Cu_{2+} intensity (measured by Cu L3/2 XPS and Cu L3/2 XANES), and the green luminescence GL and near band edge emission NBE of the PL spectra were found to be reversibly modulated by the non-volatile resistance switching. The MS reduced by ~30% while the sample was set from HRS to LRS, and then restored the original value while switched back to HRS. The GL and the NBE intensities demonstrated clear enhancement while set from HRS to LRS, and then restore the original intensities while reset back to HRS. The relative Cu_{2+} revealed by Cu L3/2 edge XANES reduced by ~50% from HRS to LRS (reduced by 40% measured by XPS) and then restored the original value while reset back to HRS. The V_{O} abundance measured by XPS did not change while the resistance state changed. The cell structure sample fabricated by the ZnO:Cu film with a lower Cu=2wt% also had its MS modulated by the resistive switching though the magnitude of change is smaller. The MS modulation by electrical resistive switching indicates that at least part of the RTFM was associated with an intrinsic origin rather than completely from the extrinsic secondary phase CuO nanocrystal, which was not expected to be modulated by the external electric bias. The decrease in MS while switched from HRS to LRS were associated with the reduction in the relative intensity of ferromagnetic Cu_{2+} which had unpaired 3d^{9} electron. The increase in Cu_{2+} occupancy in the Cu_{2+}/Cu_{+} transition (corresponding to a deep acceptor level in the band gap) implied the shift-up of the Fermi level towards the CBM, which was compatible with the increase of electron concentration while set from HRS to LRS. Magnetic properties of intrinsic isolated defects (interstitial, antisite and monovacancy) and vacancy clusters (V_{O}V_{Zn}, V_{Zn}-2V_{O} and 2V_{Zn}-V_{O}) were studied experimentally and theoretically. Undoped Zn-polar and O-polar ZnO films were fabricated by PLD. Both polarities of undoped ZnO were RTFM, though the hysteresis was small. Positron annihilation spectroscopy (PAS) study, which was selectively sensitive to vacancy-type defect containing V_{Zn}, showed that single type of vacancy defect V_{Zn}-2V_{O} existed in the O-polar sample but different types of vacancy defects existed in the Zn-polar samples. Systematic study was thus performed on the O-polar samples. The irreversibility between ZFC/FC curves persisted well above room temperature would be due to the ferromagnetic component. The temperature dependent magnetization was measured under 10000 Oe which insures the saturation. The saturation magnetization shows a fast drop below 50 K, which might be due to a small paramagnetic component. Above 50 K, the saturation magnetization shows mild decrease with increasing temperature, indicating the Curie temperature for the ferromagnetic component is well above room temperature. O-polar samples fabricated with different PO2 were studied by PAS, XRD and SQUID. Correlations between the MS, the surface to volume ratio of the grain sGB, and the V_{Zn}-2V_{O} concentration were observed, indicating the ferromagnetism was associated with the V_{Zn}-V_{O} in the vicinity of the grain surface. First principle calculation was performed to study the relaxed atomic geometry, formation energies and magnetic properties of the isolated intrinsic defects (monovacancy, antisite and interstitial) and vacancy clusters (V_{Zn}V_{O}, V_{Zn}-2V_{O} and 2V_{Zn}-V_{O}) in ZnO. The studies included both the octahedral (oct) and tetrahedral (tet) configurations of the antisites, and the V_{Zn}-2V_{O} and 2V_{Zn}-V_{O} laying on the ab-plan and along the c-axis. Neutral and 1- charged V_{Zn}; neutral and 1- charged O_{i} (oct); and neutral and 1- charged 2V_{Zn}-V{O} were found to carry non-zero magnetic moment and energetically favoured ferromagnetic state comparing with anti-ferromagnetic state. It was also found that for these ferromagnetic defects the localized O-p electron and the Zn-d electron were the principle contributor for the spin density. As mentioned in the Mid-term Progress Report for the period ending 31-10-2016 (i.e. 15 months after the project commenced), the theoretical study was delayed as the in-charged researcher belonged to the CoI Javerd’s group left. A postdoc was recruited at HKU to perform the work with the collaboration with Dr Chi-Hang Lam (HKPolyU). The experimental works were also delayed as we need the theoretical results for analysing and drawing conclusions on the experimental data.

17302115.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302115.value: It has been reported that the RTFM in Cu-doped ZnO was due to the bound magnetic polaron and Cu3d-O2p exchange [Coey et al, Nat. Mater. 173 (2005); Tian et al [APL 98, 162503 (2011)]. The reduction in MS in the cell structure sample while set from HRS to LRS could be explained by the decrease in the relative Cu_{2+} abundance [P2,P5,P9,P10,C1,C3,C4]. The modulation of MS by external electric bias and Fermi level movement offers evidence for the presence of intrinsic origin for the observed RT FM [P2]. The simultaneous modulations of MS and luminescence intensity of the cell structure sample would imply new potential for opto magneto memistor device [P5,P10]. The MS of the Cu-doped ZnO samples changed abruptly and does not follow simple dependence on electron concentration, relative Cu2+ occupancy nor VO abundance [P1]. This seems surprising as the MS does not increase with the Cu2+ abundance. O-polar and Zn-polar undoped ZnO grown by PLD [P4] were RT FM [P8,C5]. Many literatures attributed RT FM of ZnO to monovacancy type defects, like Yong et al [J. Alloy Compounds 739, 1080 (2018)] and Khalid et al [Phys. Rev. B 80 (2009)]. Single type of V_{Zn}-2V_{O} defect was unambiguously identified in the O-polar samples [P3,C5]. Correlations between MS, sGB and V_{Zn}-2V_{O} clearly showed that the RT FM was associated with the vacancy cluster nearby the grain boundary surface in the O-polar sample [P7,P8,C5]. Theoretical study showed that some charge states and configuration of V_¬{Zn}, O_{i} and 2V_{Zn}-V_{O} carried non-zero magnetic moment and energetically favoured the ferromagnetic state [P6]. Our studies showed that intrinsic defects were crucial factor influencing the room temperature ferromagnetism of ZnO. Coey et al [Nat Phys 12, 694 (2016)] recently suggested that the M-H curves with small hysteresis observed in the d-zero oxides was originated from a giant orbital paramagnetism in coherent mesoscopic domain. However, our current data [P8] did not coincide with the temperature independent MS data predicted by this theory.

17302115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302115.value: - The saturated magnetization of the Cu-doped ZnO sample does not increase with the increase of the relative Cu2+ intensity. XMCD studies on the Cu-doped ZnO samples fabricated with different PO2 and the cell structure array sample in different resistance states would yield valuable information on the exact origin of the ferromagnetism. - The resistive switching modulations of luminescence intensity and saturation magnetization with the tuning of the Fermi level of the cell structure array sample would have potential for new opto-magneto-memristor devices. We plan to fabricate the LED/memristor device to have its luminescence intensity reversibly tuned by the non-volatile resistance state. - The origin of room temperature magnetism in oxides of metals with no d nor f electrons is still in debate. Coey et al [Nat Phys 12, 694 (2016)] attributed the magnetism observed in CeO_{2} to the giant orbital paramagnetism in coherent mesoscopic domain. However, Paidi et al [Phys. Rev. B 99, 180403 (2019)] reported the RT FM in CeO_{2} was supported by the data of XAS and XMCD and result of first principle calculation. XMCD study in ZnO and comprehensive study in ZnO in different material forms (like nanoparticles) may clarify the uncertainty.

17302115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302115.value: Room temperature ferromagnetism, luminescence and resistive switching are the basic physical phenomenon for the spintronic devices (devices working with the manipulation of the electron spin), optoelectronic devices and memory devices. Material having multi-functionalities in a single phase would be an advantage of developing new devices with integrated applications. The present study demonstrated that Cu-doped ZnO (ZnO:Cu) film fabricated by pulsed laser deposition with appropriate condition is ferromagnetic at room temperatures. Comprehensive experimental and theoretical study suggested that defects are crucial for determining the room temperature ferromagnetism observed in undoped and Cu-doped ZnO. A ZnO:Cu cell structure sample exhibited reversible switching between non-volatile low and high resistance states respectively by applying external bias of +4V and -4V. Moreover, the saturation magnetization and photoluminescence intensity was found to be dependent on the non-volatile resistance state, and reversibly modulated by the resistive switching. This revealed the potential for developing new devices for optical-magnetic-memristor applications.

17302315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302315.value: The gamma-ray satellite, Fermi, has detected GeV photons from some binary systems, which we call gamma-ray binaries. These binaries can be roughly classified into two classes. The first class consists a compact star and a high mass companion, which is usually a O/B massive star with strong stellar wind. They also have long orbital periods ranging from several days to several years with highly elliptical orbits. The nature of the compact star for most high mass gamma-ray binaries is not known except PSR B1259-63/LS 2883, whose compact star is known as a pulsar. We call this class as high-mass gamma-ray binaries. The second class also consists a compact object, which is already known as a pulsar, and a low mass companion, which is usually either low mass G-type star or a very low mass degenerate white dwarf with a circular orbit and very short orbital period about several hours to less than a day. We call this class as low mass gamma-ray binaries. In addition to GeV energy band the high-mass gamma-ray binaries have also been detected in other energy bands including X-rays and TeV. All these multi-wavelength emissions exhibit orbital periodicity. Low-mass gamma-ray binaries have also been detected in wide range of energy spectrum but not all these emissions exhibit orbital periodicity. Furthermore TeV emission has not yet been found from low-mass gamma-ray binaries. In this project we shall assume that the compact star in high-mass gamma-ray binaries with unknown nature is a pulsar. We study the particle acceleration mechanisms in the termination shocks, which are formed due to the interactions between stellar wind from the companion star and the pulsar wind. We will consider the synchrotron and inverse Compton processes for the shocked particles as well as the inverse Compton processes between the cold pulsar wind and low energy photons from the companion star. The Doppler boosting effect may play an important role in producing the orbital modulated signals. Other important factors, which may also produce orbital modulated signals include position dependent pulsar wind energy conversion into particle kinetic energy, anisotropic wind emission, pair creation, viewing angle effect, stellar disk, time dependent stellar wind effect etc., will be considered in our calculations. 伽瑪射線衛星，費米，已檢測到 GeV 光子從一些雙星系統， 我們稱之為伽瑪射線的雙星系統。 這些伽瑪射線的雙星系統可以大致分為兩種類。 第一類包括一個大質量的伴星，通常是 O/B 恒星。 他們有長軌道週期從幾天到幾年與高橢圓軌道。 除了 PSR B1259-63/LS 2883，其緻密星為脈衝星。 伽瑪射線雙星系統之緻密星的性質一般而言是不明的。 我們稱此類為高質量 伽瑪射線雙星系統。除了 GeV 能帶， 高質量伽瑪射線雙星系也發現包括 x 光和 TeV 其他能帶。 所有這些波長也表現出軌道週期。第二類伽瑪射線的雙星系統， 是脈衝星和低質量的伴星，通常是低質量的G-型星或很低質量的 白矮星。其軌道是圓形軌道和很短週期從幾個小時到少於一天的 軌道週期。我們稱此類為低質量伽瑪射線雙星系統。 低質量伽瑪射線的雙星系統也發現範圍廣泛的能譜， 但並沒有表現出軌道週期,TeV 排放也尚未被找到。 在這個專案中，我們將研究這兩類伽瑪射線雙星系輻射特性之 異同。我們將假設伽瑪射線的雙星系統包括一顆脈衝星， 由於形成的粒子加速機制從脈衝星和伴星的恒星風或低質量的 白矮星風之間的相互作用。我們將考慮同步和逆康普頓作為 輻射過程，逆康普頓是由於冷脈衝星風和低能量伴星的光子作用 產生。多普勒效應亦可能發揮重要作用在生產軌道的週期信號的 作用。其他重要的因素，也可能產生軌道信號包括位置取決於 脈衝星風能源轉換成粒子動能、各向異性風排放、觀測角效應 、 恒星盤，軌道特性、時間依賴的恒星風效應等， 將考慮在我們計算中。

17302315.label: Realisation of objectives
17302315.value: Our research strategy is first using the existing observational results to summarize the key differences and similarities between the high mass and low mass gamma-ray binaries. Secondly we develop theoretical models to explain the existing properties of these systems. Thirdly from the theoretical understanding we try to identify new low mass and high gamma-ray binaries. We found that in the low mass gamma-ray binaries the X-ray orbital modulation is stronger than that of gamma-ray orbital modulation. It is interesting to note that X-ray peak positions in the orbital phase in black widow systems and red back systems (they are two major sub-classes of low mass gamma-ray binaries) are opposite whereas the gamma-ray peak is the same. These two classes of low mass gamma-ray binaries both consist of a millisecond pulsar but their companion star is different. One is low white dwarf and another one is main sequence star, which implies that the stellar wind from these two systems is different. In fact the red back is stronger than the black widow. This can explain by the fact that the shock cone which is determined by the ratio between the pulsar wind and stellar is opposite in these two classes. The X-ray intensity is enhanced by Doppler Boosting effect so that the cone direction is the peak position of the X-rays. We also found that the gamma-ray peak is always in the orbital phase when the pulsar is behind the companion star and its spectrum can be modelled by a simple gaussian component. We argue that this is because the orbital independent emission comes from the magnetospheric emission of the millisecond pulsar which can be described by a power law with exponential cut-off whereas the orbital dependent component comes from the inverse Compton scattering between the companion star photons and the relativistic pulsar wind. Therefore when the collision is head-on, namely when the pulsar is behind the companion star, the inverse Compton efficiency is highest. Since the pulsar wind is nearly mono-energetic so that the spectrum of inverse Compton scattering can be described by a gaussian spectrum. In case of high mass gamma-ray binaries the orbital modulated signals do not come from either the inferior conjunction or superior conjunction instead it closes to the orbital phase where the stellar disk of high mass companion star is located, for example PSR B1259 -63. The X-ray and gamma-ray emissions in this orbital phase cannot be described by a simple gaussian. The X-ray spectrum can be described by a power law, which implies non-thermal synchrotron radiation emission and the gamma-ray spectrum can be described by a power-law plus a cut-off from 200MeV to a few GeV. We model this behaviour by the fact that when pulsar enters the stellar disk the shock is enhanced and the synchrotron radiation from the shock in X-rays increase. However the synchrotron emission by the shocked accelerated electrons due to the balance between the synchrotron loss time and acceleration time is restricted to have emission energy less than several tens MeV. The GeV emission must come from different mechanism. We notice that when the pulsar enters the stellar disk the pulsar can accrete matter and form a transient accretion disk surrounding the neutron star. It is the soft disk photons which interact with the pulsar wind which produces the observed gamma-rays. If the temperature of the accretion disk is constant then the spectrum should be gaussian like spectrum. However this is a transient disk so its temperature is function of time. In gamma-ray observations the photons are not many so it needs to integrate over a long time to get a spectrum therefore we are observing the time average spectrum and consequently a power-law like spectrum is observed. In fact we have noticed that a similar phenomenon has also been found in low mass gamma-ray binary, a red back called PSR J2021, has been observed under a transition from non-accretion phase to accretion phase. During the accretion phase its gamma-ray emission is also enhanced due to the inverse Compton scattering between the soft photons from the disk and the pulsar. Since the disk in this system can be maintained by the injection of mass from its companion star so a broad gaussian spectrum in gamma-ray is detected. We are quite sure that the orbital dependent gamma-ray from low mass gamma-ray binaries are produced by the inverse Component scattering between the companion star soft photons and the pulsar wind so that its peak always occur when the pulsar is behind the companion star. We use this fact to search for orbital dependent emission from the redback candidate 3FGL J2039.6-5618 and successfully identify an orbital dependent gamma-ray component in this system. In this study it is very important to have accurate orbital period information. We use the optical data from three different observations to find the orbital period and use the optical orbital timing data to identify when the pulsar is located behind the companion star. This requires nearly 9 years of gamma-ray data and we obtained a nearly 5-sigma significant. We have also used similar technique in another Redback system 3FGL J0954.8-3948. We have tried to search new high mass gamma-ray binaries from the Fermi data base. But it is very difficult because of two reasons. Unlike in the case of low mass gamma-ray binaries their millisecond pulsars can be identified so that very accurate timing data can come from radio. Also these systems usually have optical and X-ray orbital modulated signals so that their orbital information is more or less known. Their positions can also be identified accurately by optical and X-ray data. On the other hand in the high mass gamma-ray binaries according to the population synthesis in our Milky Way there are less than 30 so on average they are very far away from us so that X-ray observations become difficult. We have used several blind search techniques but not successful. However there is one advantage of these systems their companion stars are O or B stars which mean they are very luminous in optical. So we plan a searching method in future is to look for X-ray counter parts of some O/B binaries within the Fermi unidentified sources and hopefully the X-ray counter part provides better location of the source which plays an important in blind search process.

17302315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302315.value: In pub. 1 and 10, we speculate a Fermi unidentified source called 3FGL J2039.6-5618 is a redback low mass gamma-ray binary. In pub. 1 we have done a preliminary search for the orbital modulated gamma-ray signal in Fermi data base. We can only get very low significant signal due to two reasons, inaccurate orbital period and insufficient gamma-ray photons. In pub. 2 we make use the new optical observation data to obtain better orbital period and we have two more years gamma-ray data, so that we can identify an orbital dependent gamma-ray signal in a nearly 5 sigma significant. We also model the observed spectrum by the inverse Compton scattering between pulsar wind and companion star soft photons. In Pub. 9, we study the multiwavelength properties of a New Redback Millisecond Pulsar Candidate: 3FGL J0954.8--3948". In pub. 2 and 7, in the early 2017 we first predict the multi-wavelength emission of a very long orbital gamma-ray binary called PSR J2032+4127/MT91 213 nearly its periastron passage, which occurs at the end of 2017. Our predictions are published in Pub. 2. At the end of 2017 we collect data in X-rays, GeV and TeV and try to compare with our predictions. We find that our X-ray prediction match the observed feature very well. In TeV the observed data is qualitatively agreed with our predictions. In GeV, Fermi data did not show any significant change. However our prediction show that the enhancement in GeV is at most comparable with steady component. In order to identify the enhancement, we have to remove the steady component from pulsar magnetosphere which requires very good timing solution. We hope that the Fermi team can release the most updated timing solution so that we can check our predictions. The pub. 2 has attracted a lot attention for researchers studying this system. In pub. 3,4, 5 and 8, we study interaction between the pulsar and the companion stellar disk in the high mass gamma-ray binaries by using two high mass gamma-ray binaries, i.e. PSR B1259-63 and HESS J0632+057. We calculate how a transient accretion disk can be formed when the pulsar enter the stellar disk and then we calculate the inverse Compton scattering between the disk soft photons and the pulsar wind. We then use this model to fit the observed gamma-ray data of PSR B1259-63 and HESS J0632+057. We are able to obtain a good agreement between the observed data and the model predictions in pub. 3,4, 5 and 7. In pub. 8 since PSR B1259-63 is also a radio data which contains very accurate timing information when the pulsar passing through the disk. We study what is the interaction torque between the transient accretion disk and pulsar during this period. We find that the coupling is weaker than that predicted by standard model. Our study is able to put some constraint on the coupling parameter between the disk and pulsar. In pub. 6, we use the binary pulsar system to study the pulsar wind properties.

17302315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302315.value: We have identified what are the main differences in multi-wavelength emission from low mass and high mass gamma-ray binaries. We can make use these key features to search for new low mass and high mass gamma-ray binaries in future. In studying the orbital dependent gamma-ray emission from low mass companion we still do not know how the intensity depends on other parameters, e.g. inclination angle, properties of companion star etc. More detailed spectroscopic observations will be helpful to identify these properties and hence tell us how they affect the actual gamma-ray intensity. In high mass gamma-ray binaries we are sure that the X-ray, 100Mev-10GeV and TeV flares are related to the interaction between pulsar wind and the stellar disk. But it appears that there are two way to cause these emissions. One is forming a transient accretion disk after accreting matter from the stellar disk, e.g. HESS0632 +057. Another one could be forming a hot cocoon inside the stellar and somehow this cocoon will be dispersed immediately and will persistent after leaving the stellar disk. This situation seems to be very important in PSR B1259-63. Furthermore PSR J2032+4127 did not show any GeV flaring after passing the disk. More observations in future may provide important hints to explain all these differences.

17302315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302315.value: In this study we have studied the multi-wavelength emission from low-mass and high-mass gamma-ray binaries in terms of theoretical modelling and data analysis of various X-ray and gamma-ray satellites. We found that some high mass gamma-ray binaries exhibit pulsar magnetosphere emission similar to those in the low mass gamma-ray binaries. On the other hand the low mass gamma-ray binaries exhibit weak orbital modulated emission in both X-ray and gamma-rays in the comparing with the high mass gamma-ray binaries. The main reason for this difference is that the orbital modulation in low mass binaries come from the inverse Compton scattering (IC) interaction between the relativistic pulsar wind and the soft photons from the companion star. This IC intensity is lower than the overall magnetospheric emission component. But it appears in GeV region as gaussian distribution which can be distinguished from the power law magnetospheric emission. The orbital modulation emission in high mass component mainly come from the pulsar wind and stellar disk interaction which is much stronger. The emission from this interaction actually dominated in X-ray, 100MeV-10GeV and even up to TeV range. In these properties allow us to search and identify new high mass and low mass gamma-ray binaries respectively.

17302415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302415.value: Boronic acids and acid esters are important compounds, both as intermediates that play versatile roles in the synthesis of target molecules, and as targets themselves for biological and therapeutic applications. Therefore, the ability to synthesize a variety of boronate esters bearing different functional groups is a significant goal for expanding the utility of these compounds. This research project aims to develop a novel method to generate C-boron enolates, ie. boronate esters functionalized by alpha carbonyl groups. The synthesis starts from O-boron enolates, which are readily obtained by copper-catalyzed conjugate reduction of unsaturated esters, and induces their rearrangement to C-boron enolates via phosphine catalysis. This reagent-controlled synthesis employs readily available starting materials, and the use of chiral phosphines to catalyzed the rearrangement could yield enantiomerically enriched C-boron enolates. The utility of these unstabilized C-boron enolates has been successfully demonstrated in an application by oxidation to yield lactic acid derivatives, constituting a one-pot bis-functionalization of enoates and an overall alpha-hydroxylation of esters. This proposed study aims to investigate the detailed mechanism of the rearrangement of the O-boron enolate to the C-bound enolate, and to examine the range of nucleophiles and the scope of the substrates to develop a general method to furnish these compounds. The research will also be focused on the applications of the C-boron enolates to expand the reaction repertoire of these functionalized boronate esters and establish them as versatile building blocks for organic synthesis. 硼酸和硼酸酯是重要的化合物，它們不但是合成藥物目標分子的重要中間體，本身也是醫藥藥物的目標分子。因而，為了拓展這類化合物的應用範圍，如何合成含各種官能團的硼酸和硼酸酯是急需解决的關鍵問題。 本研究課題旨在發展製備碳硼烯醇鹽的一類新的方法，就是通過硼酸酯化羰基的α-位。我們的合成策略以氧硼烯醇鹽為起始原料，通過膦試劑催化，使其重排成碳硼烯醇鹽。氧硼烯醇鹽可以由銅催化的不飽和酯的共軛還原制得。該方法通過試劑控制，並使用易得的起始原料，用手性膦試劑催化，可以得到手性的碳硼烯醇鹽。我們已經成功地將這一方法應用在乳酸衍生物的合成當中，通過氧化這些沒有採用官能團而稳定的碳硼烯醇鹽，一鍋法實現雙官能團轉化，最後得到α-羥基化的酯。 本研究課題將探究氧硼烯醇鹽重排成碳硼烯醇鹽的詳細機理，同時考察親核試劑和底物的適用範圍，進而發展一種通用的方法去制備這一類化合物。我們也將致力於拓展碳硼烯醇鹽的應用範圍，使這類含豐富官能團的硼酸酯作爲廣泛應用于有机合成當中的合成砌塊。

17302415.label: Realisation of objectives
17302415.value: The objectives to study the generation of C-boron enolates and their potential for synthesis, have been largely achieved. We have studied the O-to-C isomerization of O-boron enolates obtained upon reduction of unsaturated esters and amides. We have isolated and purified the novel unquaternized C-boron enolates, and have even obtained the x-ray crystal structure of these sensitive compounds for the first time. This was a special feat because the C-boron enolates are moisture-sensitive molecules. The scope of the unsaturated esters and amides have been investigated and found to be quite general. Thus we prepared a series of these compounds and studied their chemistry. We were able to convert the C-boron enolates to form new C-O and C-C bonds, but we were unable to convert them to C-N bonds in high yields--this is an aspect that require further study. We have also studied the mechanism and found that the isomerization is dependent on both Cu and the phosphine. Beside phosphines, NHC carbenes are also effective additives to increase the rate of formation of C-boron enolates. Asymmetric reduction products are able rearrange to provide lactic acid derivatives with good ee. All these results culminated in a communication published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society (Impact factor 14.695) Unfortunately, although the addition of B2pin2 was studied, the Cu-O and B-B metathesis was too slow and no isomerization to C-boron enolates occurred.

17302415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302415.value: In this study we found that, contrary to the general concept, quaternization of the boron is not necessary for stable C-boron enolates. Such species have now been synthesized reliably, isolated, purified and fully characterized for the first time to show that the boron is trigonal planar. We have devised a general method for the generation of these species. The reductive copper hydride-mediated reduction first provides O-boron enolates, and with the addition of a catalytic amount of a more nucleophilic ligand, an O-to-C isomerization will occur to produce C-boron enolates. Upon investigating the scope of this reaction, it was found that O-boron enolates such as those of amides, convert to C-boron enolates more rapidly. This is one of the major reasons why the reductive aldol reactions of unsaturated amides occur with lower yields, as the C-boron enolates that are formed irreversibly cannot then engage in aldol reactions with aldehydes. The synthesis of C-boron enolates allowed the systematic investigation of their reactivity. Optimizations found conditions that allow the C-B bond to be transformed to C-C and C-O bonds, but they do not undergo typical O-boron enolate reactions such as Claisen rearrangements or aldol reactions. Most of these findings have been reported as a communication in J. Am. Chem. Soc. in 2018. Additional findings related to the aldol reaction, and the further scope of enolborate isomerization will be submitted shortly as two publications.

17302415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302415.value: Further investigations on the synthetic potential of C-boron enolates can be pursued. The conversion of the C-B bond to a C-N bond occurs but the yields are not high--additional investigations are needed. This will be followed up by a postdoctoral fellow. Additional studies on the mechanism of the O-to-C isomerization should also be pursued.

17302415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302415.value: C-Boron enolates were thought to be species that are unstable unless the boron is saturated. We have found however, that even when they are unsaturated, they are stable, and we have synthesized a series of these elusive compounds. Moreover, for the first time, we have isolated and purified them, and full characterization proves unequivocably that the boron atoms of these C-boron enolates are trigonal and coordinatively unsaturated. Having found a reliable way to synthesize C-boron enolates, we have also been able to investigate their reactions. They behave very differently from their better known, O-boron enolate cousins. Whereas O-boron enolates are well known to undergo the highly important classical aldol reaction, C-boron enolates do not. Instead they undergo coupling reactions to generate new C-C bonds and C-O bonds. Their full synthetic potential can be further mined and exploited.

17302515.label: Project Objectives
17302515.value: In a broad stroke, the classification of almost universal ternary quadratic polynomials which are sums of n-gonal numbers is the main goal. A secondary goal is to apply the technique developed for the first objective for representations by a quadratic form related to elliptic curves. In particular, the goal is to prove than an algorithm for constructing supersingular elliptic curves given their endomorphism ring actually terminates successfully, by resolving a conjecture about quadratic forms. The first step along the process of classifying almost universal quadratic polynomials is to establish a criterion which determines local obstructions to representability. In individual cases this is a straightforward calculation, but may become complicated in the generality needed for this project. After establishing local representability, the next goal is to determine when the coefficients of certain unary theta functions cancel the main asymptotic growth of the number of representations expected by local conditions. This should involve an array of techniques and long calculations arising from lattice theory (and in particular cosets thereof). Given the output from Objectives 3 and 4, establish a guess for the classification of almost universal quadratic polynomials Prove a generalization of the infinitude of sign changes of Fourier coefficients of cusp forms which are orthogonal to unary theta functions. Use Objective 6 to prove that the guess from Objective 5 is indeed correct, establishing the first goal, a classification.

17302515.label: Realisation of objectives
17302515.value: The application of sign changes to representations of integers by sums of polygonal numbers was first realized in a paper describing its application to show the halting of an algorithm to construct a supersingular elliptic curve. This successfully achieved objective 2. Local obstructions were investigated through representation masses of spinor genera. A study of the more general definition of spinor genera of shifted lattices was necessary in order to investigate these these representation masses. Objectives 3-4 were successfully completed by working on this. Staring with the work of Anna Haensch and the PI, a study of the theta functions for spinor genera of shifted lattices was undertaken. A very special case was considered in this first investigation; this was continued and expanded upon in continued research, where a condition was discovered in the joint work of the PI with Siu Hang Man. This successfully attained Objective 5. Objective 6 has been achieved by successfully generalizing a theorem of Kohnen, Lau, and Wu. We have shown in particular that there are sign changes in arithmetic progressions of square classes. This is joint work between the PI, the co-PI, and a Ph.D. student Zilong He. Objective 7 has not been fully achieved. This was dependent upon the success of Objectives 3-6, and these ran a bit more in series than expected, with objective 6 only being achieved much later. It thus took a bit longer to begin working on this part of the project. A more careful analysis of previous work of Rainier Schulze-Pillot is necessary to attain this objective. This has been slowed down a bit by the fact that the work is written in a slightly different language, both mathematically and in the fact that the papers are written in German.

17302515.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302515.value: There have been three major outcomes from the research undertaken in this project. The first was the usage of sign changes to prove a conjecture about the halting of an algorithm to construct a supersingular elliptic curve. This led a paper in Mathematics of Computation in 2017, joint with King Cheong Fung. The second outcome was a deeper understanding of the theta functions for shifted lattices and their connection with almost universal ternary sums of polygonal numbers. This led to a paper with Siu Hang Man appearing in L-functions and automorphic forms within the Contributions in Mathematical and Computational Sciences Springer series. The third outcome is the proof of sign changes in arithmetic progressions in order to obtain almost universality under certain conditions. The sign changes in arithmetic progressions result has been completed, but the paper is still in preparation.

17302515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302515.value: The final steps for using the sign changes in order to obtain a precise statement for the almost universality is the next step in continued research in this area. It was shown within the research of the project that almost universality or non-almost universality can be proven by investigating sign changes, as proposed in the project, but numerical information is needed in order to obtain the local densities for spinor genera of shifted lattices. This requires generalizing a series of papers from Rainier Schulze-Pillot which are more algebraic in nature (most of the research in this project was analytic), and hence requires a slightly different approach in order to unify the analytic and algebraic results.

17302515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302515.value: The representations of integers as sums of polygonal numbers (the number of dots contained in a regular polygon is called a polygonal number) has a long history going back at least to Fermat. By considering the sums of polygonal numbers as what is known as a quadratic polynomial, one can think of these as the distances of certain points that occur regularly throughout higher dimensional space (the distance being defined in a slightly more general way than our usual "Euclidean" distance) from a fixed point in the space. The question investigated in this project was whether there is always a point of a given integral distance from the fixed point. Many of the questions have been thoroughly investigated when the beginning fixed point is one of the regularly-spaced points; our knowledge of the case when the point is another random point is now better understood from this investigation.

17302815.label: Realisation of objectives
17302815.value: 1. Porous carriers for inhalation was successfully produced by spray freeze drying. In general, the spray freezing step controls the overall size of the particles by adjusting the atomization gas flow rate, whereas the freeze drying step controls the porosity of the particle by adjusting the solute concentration. With the use of mannitol as excipient, the size and porosity of the spray freeze dried particles could be optimized. It is found that spray freeze dried particles prepared with solute concentration between 1% to 4% (w/v) are suitable for inhalation as the porosity is high enough to promote aerosolization without compromising the robustness of the particles. In addition, the high surface area due to the highly porous structure of the particles results in improved dissolution rate. 2. Blank porous particles were produced by spray drying. Ammonium bicarbonate was employed as pyrogen as it decomposed at elevated temperature of around 36 C. Since mannitol and ammonium bicarbonate have similar solubility, it is expected that mannitol will stay on the surface during spray drying due to its higher molecular weight, leaving pores in the internal structure of the particles when ammonium bicarbonate decomposed. To produce large porous particles suitable for aerosolisation, it was found that at least 85% (w/w) of ammonium bicarbonate is required, with a lower atomization rate of around 450 L/h and inlet temperature of around 100 C. These conditions can avoid ammonium bicarbonate to decompose too early while preventing the formation of residual ammonium salts. Unfortunately, such a narrow operation window has severely limited the formulation flexibility for pulmonary delivery, and the drug loading capacity is significantly reduced. After considering the applicability of the formulation, it is determined to focus on the use of spray freeze drying technique to produce porous carrier instead. 3. Voriconazole, a triazole antifungal agent, was employed as a drug model to develop a porous particle delivery system. Due to the poor solubility of voriconazole, t-butyl alcohol (TBA) was used as a co-solvent. TBA was selected because of its relatively high boiling point, so that it can undergo sublimation process during freeze drying temperature relatively easily for pore formation. Mannitol was used as bulking agent. Factorial design approach was employed to investigate how different formulation and operation parameters, including drug content, co-solvent composition, solute concentration, liquid feed rate and drying temperature, may affect the resultant properties of the spray freeze dried particles, including particle size distribution, surface morphology, porosity, aerosol performance and dissolution properties. It was found that increasing hydrophobic drug content could increase powder dispersion and hence aerosol performance. High solute concentration could provide more robust yet porous particles. The aerosol performance was significantly affected by primary freezing temperature, with higher the temperature (at -10 C), the better the aerosolization. Moreover, the biodistribution study in mice suggested that such formulation can achieve high local drug concentration following intratracheal administration while minimizing its distribution in the systemic circulation and other organs as compared with the intravenous route of administration, thereby reducing the potential risk of side effects. 4. The feasibility of using spray freeze particles as porous carrier for pulmonary delivery was further investigated on other therapeutic agents, including small interfering RNA (siRNA). The atomization gas flow rate has a major impact on the aerosol properties of the particles. The higher the atomization gas flow rate (up to 600 L/h), the smaller the particle size, the higher the respirable fraction. The stability of the powder, as reflected by the crystalline properties, was achieved. Overall, it was found that spray freeze drying method was able to produce porous powder with good aerosol performance while maintaining the structure integrity and biological activity of the nucleic acids.

17302815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302815.value: 1. With suitable spray drying condition, ammonium bicarbonate can be used as pyrogen to produce large porous particles for inhalation. However, due to the relatively high content of ammonium bicarbonate required (over 80% w/w), the drug loading capability is significantly reduced, limiting its application as carrier for pulmonary drug delivery system. For this reason, the spray freeze drying is focused for the production of porous particle for pulmonary drug delivery. 2. Using mannitol as excipient, porous particles can be prepared by spray freeze drying. A solute concentration of 1% to 4% is suitable to produce porous particles with good aerosol performance, dissolution rate and structural integrity. 3. Voriconazole was investigated as drug model for the preparation of porous, inhalable dry powder formulation by spray freeze drying. It was found that high hydrophobic drug content could promote powder dispersion, while high primary freezing temperature could produce smaller particles upon dispersion to enhance aerosol properties. (Liao et al 2019 International Journal of Pharmaceutics; Liao et al 2020 International Journal of Pharmaceutics). 4. The use of spray freeze drying technology was further investigated to produce porous particles of biomacromolecules for inhalation. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) was studied. It was found that increasing atomization gas flow rate can effectively decrease particle size, thereby improving aerosol properties. The structural integrity as well as the biological activity of the siRNA molecules were also successfully preserved. (Liang et al 2018 International Journal of Pharmaceutics).

17302815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302815.value: The objectives of future study is to develop this delivery system as a platform technology so that it can be applied to a wide range of therapeutic agents (especially those with low aqueous solubility) for different therapeutic indications such as respiratory infections, lung inflammatory diseases, acute lung injury/ pulmonary fibrosis and lung cancer. In addition, the formulations will be evaluated with different inhaler systems and different inspiratory flow rate in order to assess their suitability for use in patients with different pulmonary function/ disease conditions. Pharmacokinetic studies will also be performed to gain a better understanding on the performance of the inhaled dry powder formulations as compared to other routes of administration.

17302815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302815.value: In this study, we demonstrated that ammonium bicarbonate can be used as a pyrogen, with the use of mannitol as bulking excipient, in spray drying to produce porous carrier for inhalation. However, the requirement of high pyrogen content (at least 85% by mass) has limited its application for pulmonary drug delivery. Alternatively, spray freeze drying is another particle engineering technique that can be used to produce porous particles with good aerosol properties for inhalation. We have investigated this technique to prepare porous particles of two different therapeutic agents, voriconazole (which is an antifungal agent for the treatment of pulmonary fungal infection) and small interfering RNA (siRNA, which can be used to manipulate expression of disease-associated gene). We have successfully produced spray freeze dried particles with high porosity that is suitable for inhalation. In the future, this technology will be applied to different therapeutic agents for evaluation on a wide range of therapeutic indications.

17303015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303015.value: 分子在納米通道的傳遞與在體相中是截然不同的。在納米通道中，分子傳遞總是靠近與通道表面的。使用新發展的納米加工手段，我們可以更精確的控制納米通道的尺寸並研究分子傳送的性質。當納米通道尺寸接近分子尺度時，表面的作用力將會起到決定性的作用。這個性質可能可以被用於高靈敏度的化學或生物分子的分析和檢測。已有的研究表明，納米孔可以被用於單個DNA分子的檢測和分析，並有希望用於DNA測序。 本研究著重研究納米管表面對DNA或蛋白分子在納米管內的傳送的影響。通過設計納米管表面，以達到可以對單鹼基的分子的不同作用，最終可以成為單鹼基一種鑑別方法。這項研究可以用於單分子DNA測序以及蛋白分子的分析。

17303015.label: Realisation of objectives
17303015.value: The single-molecule sensor has been successfully created and the signals are detected. The nanotube coating method also successfully developed and peptides and DNA molecules are coated inside and verification of the method are completed with the fluorescent images. The single-molecule translocation behaviour is studied with the surface coating. Several coating materials such as SiO2, Al2O3, and ZnO are used. However, the result data shows insignificant distinguishability over different deoxynucleoside monophosphates translocation event. The high noise in the translocation event prevented confident identification. In regard to the result, additional research is shifted towards the study of the surface electrophoresis control and fluidic physics study. The size effect of the electrophoresis is studied. Instead of directly using single-molecule, the nanoparticles and microparticles are used as a model system to evaluate the flow stability and explore the control mechanism. With better understanding and control of the electrophoresis and electroosmosis, the noise suppression is expected. The identification of deoxynucleoside monophosphates will be revisited upon completion of the noise suppression study. With the study of electrophoresis and osmosis, several research papers are published with the direct support of this project for highly controllable microparticle migration, including 1 Nature Nanotechnology, 1 Advanced Materials, 1 Nature Communications.

17303015.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303015.value: The Brownian motion is highly important in the mass transport of molecules and nanoparticles. In order to identify the molecules/nanoparticles, the molecules and particles must be properly controlled or labelled. The surface charge state will be the key control parameters for mass transport, which must be carefully designed. The control of mass transport is the process of fighting against the Brownian motion, which will be easier for micro/nanoparticles over the single molecules. Several method including site selective modification and electrode modification is the effective method to suppress the Brownian motion. Research output including: 1. 17303015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303015.value: Additional research is needed to further suppress the size of controlled particles to single molecular level. One potential method is the high viscosity liquid dynamics and light field confinement. The nanofluidic dynamics need to be firstly studied, and the spectroscopy measurement should be used to elucidate the mechanism.

17303015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303015.value: In this research, a nanofluidic system is developed to control the electrophoresis motion of single molecule. We developed a strategy to suppress the Brownian motion of nanoparticles which is useful for biological analysis. Through coating the surface of inorganic materials with polymers and molecules, we demonstrated that the mass transport at nanoscopic scale can be confined and controlled. The finding will be useful to build the nanorobot and nanomedicine.

17303115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303115.value: The Northwestern Pacific Ocean is characterized by the highest biodiversity on Earth. In spite of this obvious importance, our understanding of shallow marine biota in this region is relatively poor compared with well-studied North American and European margins. Here, as a step towards a holistic understanding of northwestern Pacific biodiversity dynamics, we propose to use a microscopic-sized fossil (known as microfossil) group of Ostracoda (small bivalved crustacean) preserved in surface sediments as a model system to investigate detailed present-day shallow-marine biodiversity and biogeographic patterns throughout the northwestern Pacific Ocean as far south as the Indonesian Archipelago and as far north as the Bering Sea and Arctic Ocean. The results will give us a better understanding of large-scale biodiversity and biogeographic patterns in this region. More specifically one of our main goals is elucidating details of latitudinal species diversity gradient, which is one of the most important diversity patterns on Earth characterized by tropical high and polar low diversity. Secondly, we aim to understand biogeographic divisions in the northwestern Pacific Ocean. Thirdly, we plan to investigate the differences of these diversity and biogeographic patterns between taxa, e.g., poor disperser ostracodes vs good dispersers including molluscs. Furthermore, this present-day dataset will enable us to conduct statistical modeling with environmental data to elucidate important factors controlling biodiversity and biogeographic distribution. This detailed investigation of present-day diversity patterns using a taxon with excellent fossil record (i.e., Ostracoda) will help four dimensional (i.e., both spatial and temporal) understanding of large-scale biodiversity dynamics in the future. 西北太平洋是全球最高生物多樣性的地方，其重要性無庸置疑。儘管如此，相對於獲充分研究的北美和歐洲沿海地域，我們對西北太平洋淺水海洋生物的認識只是冰山一角。在這裡，我們提出利用一種保存在海底泥土稱介型蟲(細小而具備一對殼的甲殼類動物)的微型化石(又稱微化石) 作一個模型系統來詳細地探究現今西北太平洋的淺水海洋生物多樣性和生物地理的模式，向全面理解西北太平洋生物多樣性動態踏出一步。這研究結果會讓我們更了解南至印尼多島海；北至白令海及北冰洋的大範圍生物多樣性和生物地理的模式。更準確來說，我們其中一個主要目標是闡明物種多樣性的緯度梯度性，其特點是熱帶地區的生物多樣性較高；極地的生物多樣性則較低，是地球其中一種最重要的生物多樣性模式。第二，我們會致力了解西北太平洋生物地理的劃分。第三，我們計劃探究不同生物類別(例如散布能力弱的介形蟲和散布能力高的軟體動物)的生物多樣性和生物地理的模式之差異。此外，我們將可利用得出的現代生物數據和環境資料作統計分析以找出控制生物多樣性和生物地理分佈的重要因素。透過運用擁有絕佳化石記錄的生物(介形蟲)，這項探討現代生物多樣性模式的詳盡研究將有助我們從四維角度(包括時間和空間上) 理解大範圍的生物多樣性動態。

17303115.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303115.value: Through this project, we substantially expanded our knowledge on northwestern Pacific biodiversity. We produced a lot of new data on regional biodiversity (e.g., Hong et al 2019; Cheung et al 2019) and also compiled existing data (Yasuhara et al 2017). We found northwestern Pacific fauna is controlled by eutrophication, damming of major rivers, pollution, among others. Water depth is also an important factor. Latitudinal diversity pattern is unimodal showing the peak at the mid latitude (Yasuhara et al. 2017). This may be because subtropical region has both tropical and temperate species, resulting higher diversity (Hong et al. 2019). These findings will help to compare northwestern Pacific biodiversity with those of other regions to put northwestern Pacific biodiversity in a global context. 17303115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303115.value: We are interested in comparing our northwestern Pacific biodiversity results with northwestern Atlantic data to see the difference of regional biodiversity patterns between the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans. Also by integrating Arctic biodiversity data, we can see marine migration between the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans via the Arctic. In addition, we are going to use our large ostracod census datasets developed through this project to reconstruct Holocene sea-level changes in Hong Kong using Modern Analogue Technique . These are our plan of future development of this line of research.

17303115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303115.value: We studied northwestern Pacific Ocean to better understand its biodiversity patterns. We found that changes in continental positions, complicate coast line and long-term climatic changes as well as organic and metal pollution and damming of major rivers affect northwestern Pacific animals and their biodiversity. This project gives important baseline information on biological diversity and geographic distributions of animals in the northwestern Pacific Ocean including Hong Kong.

17303215.label: Project Objectives
17303215.value: We will construct the hydrodynamic equations for spin dynamics in large spin Fermi gases based on the extension of traditional Landau Fermi liquid theory. Special attentions will be paid to SU(N) Fermi gases. We will discuss and extend the concept of contact to large spin Fermi systems. Connections of the contact to other important physical quantities (e.g., momentum tail, radio-frequency shift) in large spin Fermi gases will be established and their experimental consequences will be discussed. We will also make some efforts to discuss the implication of the correlations embodied in contact to spin dynamics.
