17303215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303215.value: Cold Fermi atoms with large internal spin offer a unique opportunity to study spin dynamics in a degenerate quantum many-body system with a much-enlarged internal structure, as compared with the traditional quantum liquids, like helium three. As a result, the spin dynamics in these large spin systems become very rich. For example, the description and nature of spin diffusion and relaxation require both the extension of traditional spin dynamics equations and more physical understanding. Furthermore, the possibility of optical Feshbach resonance in alkaline-earth elements provides a unique way of modifying the inter-atomic interactions and open new vista to investigate the interaction effects in these large spin systems that have no analogue in condensed matter physics. In this proposal, we will study two aspects of these high spin systems: (1) Spin dynamics and spin diffusion behavior and (2) The interaction effects and in particular, the definition and extension of the concept of contact to a large spin Fermi system. It has been suggested that the connection between contact and spin diffusion provides a unique angle in understanding the effects of interaction in spin dynamics and provides a nature link between the two. In the first part of the proposal, we shall base our discussion on a generalized Fermi liquid theory as applied to large spin Fermi system and derive the appropriate hydrodynamic equations for the spin dynamics. In particular, we will apply the derived equations to the standard spin-echo type experiment and extract the spin diffusion properties of the system. In the second part, we shall first concentrate on extending the concept of contact to a large spin Fermi system and establish various exact relations, as in the case of two-component Fermi gas. Possible connection of contact dynamics to spin dynamics will be discussed whenever possible. In both parts of the proposal, particular attention will be paid to the so-called SU(N) Fermi gases, as exemplified by the Ytterbium elements. 具有高自旋的冷原子给我们提供了一个很好的机会来研究简并气体中的自旋动力学过程。相比较于传统的量子多体体系，由于其多重内部自由度，高自旋体系的自旋动力学变得十分丰富，譬如自旋扩散过程。最近由于光学共振方法的提出，使得我们同时有可能研究这个系统的相互作用性质。这个在传统凝聚态体系中是没有先例的。在这个项目中，我们将研究高自旋体系的以下两个方面。（1）自旋动力学以及扩散过程，以及（2）如何利用“接触”来刻画多体的相互作用，以及自旋扩散过程中的接触时间演化。在第一部分，我们会建立自旋演化的流体力学模型并将其应用到自旋演化中。第二部分我们将着力研究高自旋体系中的接触定义以及性质。在这两个研究中，我们还会对所谓的SU(N) 气体做特别关注。

17303215.label: Realisation of objectives
17303215.value: Overall, both objectives have been achieved with relevant publications listed in Part C. Several related problems are also considered with the support of the GRF fund. Details are given below. Objective 1. We will construct the hydrodynamic equations for spin dynamics in large spin Fermi gases based on the extension of traditional Landau Fermi liquid theory. Special attentions will be paid to SU(N) Fermi gases. This objective is achieved in the manuscript currently being considered for PRL, Collective excitations in two-dimensional SU(N) Fermi gases with tunable spin, arXiv:1905.10815 (2019) Objective 2. We will discuss and extend the concept of contact to large spin Fermi systems. Connections of the contact to other important physical quantities (e.g., momentum tail, radio-frequency shift) in large spin Fermi gases will be established and their experimental consequences will be discussed. We will also make some efforts to discuss the implication of the correlations embodied in contact to spin dynamics. For transport, theoretical discussions are given in Transport phenomena in dilute quantum gases, Acta Phys. Sin. 68 040302 (2019). A related work on the spin dynamics in spinor system is also given in our recent work, Manipulation of heteronuclear spin dynamics with microwave and vector light shift, currently in review in PRA (ref number AF12035 Li). The general concept of contact has been generalized to large spin system and experimental work on the related issue is now carried out in Jo’s lab at HKUST. The theoretical aspects has been worked out in the research note attached.

17303215.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303215.value: The major findings of this proposal include the following: 1. A theoretical framework for the dynamics of su(N) gas in the harmonic trap is given based on the equation of motion for the Wigner functions in phase space. Including the mean field interaction effect in the time-dependent equation (essentially random phase approximation) and showed how various different modes behave as one changes the number of components of N. 2. Related work on the spin dynamics of a mixture of two Bose particles (Na and Rb) and show how the variation of external magnetic field, light field change the spin dynamics of spin mixture. The dynamical equations bear strong analog to the equations derived for su(N) system, but with more complicated Wigner functions (due to two component gases). The agreement between theory and experiments are in general very good. 3. Some general discussions on the spin dynamics in dilute Fermi gas was given and the role of interaction is particularly emphasized. In this paper, the effects of so-called identical spin rotation effect were discussed. Interaction effects related to contact are discussed in the research note attached. It still awaits experimental confirmation. 4. A related work on the spin dynamics in spin-orbit coupled Bose system is given and the persistent helical structure and its decay is investigated.

17303215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303215.value: There are a few directions that is worth studying regarding transport in high spin systems. (1) Recent experiments on large spin system on optical lattices (Yb) and the investigation of spin dynamics in the Mott regime is quite worthwhile. (2) 2D transport in large spin systems is still an open issue that requires further investigation. With the realization of flat trap, this might be a good opportunity to renew its study especially experimentally.

17303215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303215.value: Spin is a new quantum degree of freedom and its dynamics obey quite different equations than that of the usual charge transport. Spin transport is supposed to play an important role in the next generation of modern technology. Our understanding of transport of either charge and spin is not very well understood, especially when interaction is involved. Our research effort in the proposal is to use a particular example of high spin dynamics in ultracold gases. Due to its well-controlled and clean nature, our study in the ultracold gases could shed new light in this area. For strong interaction limit, the problem is even more challenging and the close collaboration with experimentalists could make substantial progress in this direction.

17303315.label: Project Objectives
17303315.value: The basic generalized conditional autoregressive Wishart (GCAW) model and some of its useful extensions that are parsimonious in terms of the number of parameters will be defined. The probabilistic structure, estimation procedures and their asymptotic properties, model selection and model diagnostic methods as well as the effect of large dimension on statistical inferences of these models will be studied. Nonlinear extensions of the GCAW family defined by introducing a threshold structure will be considered. This will help study the non-linear dynamics of the RCOV under different market conditions. Again, the probabilistic structure, estimation procedure, identification and model diagnostic methods as well as the effect of large dimension on statistical inferences of these models will be studied. Applications to financial return data will be considered during the process of model development. Softwares that will be useful to researchers and practitioners will be developed. Possible future extensions of the GCAW models will be considered if time allows.

17303315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303315.value: In recent years there have been a lot of attentions on the realized covariance (RCOV) matrix obtained from high frequency returns of financial assets. The dynamics of the RCOV is of great interest to both practitioners and researchers of the financial market. Amid many proposals to model RCOV is the Wishart autoregressive process (WAR) and the conditional autoregressive Wishart model(CAW). The former models the noncentral parameter of the conditional Wishart distribtuion of the RCOV while the latter models its matrix scale parameter. This project proposes to combine both approaches resulting in a generalized conditional Wishart processes (GCAW). This results in a versatile description of the RCOV dynamics. With regard to this basic GCAW model more flexible and parsimonious model specifications are developed and considered. These extensions will allow for more efficient statistical inference, modelling and forecasting. In other words, we will study a broad family of models under the GCAW framework. Statistical properties and estimation procedures will be studied with applications in mind. The results should be of interest to practitioners, researchers in finance and time series analysts.

17303315.label: Realisation of objectives
17303315.value: Objective 1. (1)As reported in the progress report, the basic generalized autoregressive Wishart (GCAW) model for realized covariance matrices (RCOV) has been defined and studied to some extent. A complete statistical modelling was proposed and applications to some real financial time series have been considered. The results are reported in a paper appeared in the Journal of Business and Economic Statistics (paper 1 in this report). (2) We next consider how to reduce the dimension (which results in a large number of parameters) of the model. It turns out that an effective and natural way to achieve dimension reduction is by means of a matrix factor model. Positive definiteness of the estimated realized covariance matrix is assured by the proposed approach and asymptotic results are derived for the estimated parameters. The results are reported in a paper to appear in Quantitative Finance (paper 6). (3) Using the large-dimensional random matrix theory, it is well known that the eigenvalue distribution of the RCOV matrix is intimately linked to that of the Integrated Covariance Matrix (ICV) through the Marčenko–Pastur equation. Consequently, the spectrum of the ICV can be inferred from that of the RCOV. However, extensive data analyses demonstrate that the spectrum of the RCOV is spiked, that is, a few large eigenvalues (spikes) stay away from the others which form a rather continuous distribution with a density function (bulk). Therefore, any inference on the ICVs must take into account this spiked structure. As a methodological contribution, a spiked model is proposed in paper 2 for the ICVs where spikes can be inferred from those of the available RCOV matrices. The consistency of the inference procedure is established. The result can clearly be applied to the estimated (predicted) RCOVs of the GCAW family of models. Objective 2. (1) Nonlinear extension of the model is achieved by using the threshold approach. The non-centrality matrix and scale matrix of the Wishart distribution are piecewise linear driven by the lagged values of RCOV matrices and retain two different sources of dynamics. We call this new nonlinear model the generalized threshold conditional autoregressive Wishart (GTCAW) model. The model is defined, statistical inference procedure and applications to real data are reported in paper 3 which appeared this year. Objective 3 Applications to financial time series of RCOVs have been considered in all the papers reported. We have also considered extension of the GCAW model under the more general matrix-F distribution. The relation between the matrix-F and the Wishart is analogical to the relation between the univariate F distribution and the Chi-square. Consequently, asymptotic results of this paper can also be adapted naturally to the Wishart case. This new model is coined the CBF model in paper 5 which is still under review. Paper 5 also considers a matrix factor CBF model for dimensional reduction. The mathematics in developing the inference procedure have been very challenging. In addition to properties of the model and asymptotic results for the estimated parameters a new portmanteau goodness of fit test is developed for the CBF model. We believe that this result is the first of its kind for time series models for matrix data and can be generalized to other matrix time series models. In addition to the CBF model above we also consider other applications and extensions of the GCAW model. Paper 4 constructs a new generalized Hausman test for detecting the presence of structural change in a multiplicative form of covariance matrix time series model. This generalized Hausman test is asymptotically pivotal, and it has non-trivial power in detecting a broad class of abrupt and smooth change alternatives. Moreover, paper 4 proposes a new semi-parametric covariance matrix time series model, which has a time-varying long run component to take the structural change into account, and a BEKK-type short run component to capture the temporal dependence. A two-step estimation procedure is derived to estimate this semi-parametric model, and the asymptotics of the related estimators are established. Like paper 5 the mathematics are pretty challenging. This paper is under review.

17303315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303315.value: Objective 1. The GCAW model for RCOVs has been studied to some details. The model structure and the statistical modelling methodology are reported in the paper appeared in Journal of Business and Economic Statistics (paper 1 in this report). Dimensional reduction is achieved effectively by defining a matrix factor model. The new model has about one tenth of the number of parameters of the full model yet producing comparable estimates of RCOVs. The results are reported in a paper to appear in Quantitative Finance (paper 6). In a related development a spiked model that can predict the spiked eigenvalues of a high dimensional RCOV is developed in a paper (paper 2) that appeared in Computational Statistics and Data Analysis. The methodology is applied to real financial data from the US and Hong Kong markets. It is found that the model clearly outperforms the existing one in predicting the existence of spikes and in mimicking the empirical RCOV matrices. Objective 2. The linear setups in both the scale and the non-central parameters of GCAW are extended to nonlinear ones using the threshold principle. In the forecasting experiment for out of sample data the generalized threshold conditional auto-regressive Wishart (GTCAW) model outperforms all those using the linear setup . This is reported in paper (3) recently published in Statistics and Its Interface this year. This paper has been indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection, Objective 3. All the new models have been successfully applied to model time series of RCOVs. In addition, we consider new models by replacing the Wishart distribution by the matrix-F distribution in paper 5 (analogical to replacing the chi square by the F distribution in classical statistics). A portmanteau goodness of fit test is derived for the new CBF model which can be extended to other situations. Testing and modelling for structural change for time series of RCOVs are also considered successfully under the framework of the GCAW family of models (paper 4).

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303315.value: The generalized conditional auto-regressive Wishart (GCAW) model for time series of realized covariance matrices (RCOV) of financial returns are developed and studied to some extent. An effective way to reduce the dimension of the GCAW model is proposed via a matrix factor approach. A spiked model is developed to predict the spiked eigenvalues of RCOVs. Nonlinear extension is successfully developed using the threshold (piece-wise linear) principle. The more general matrix-F distribution is suggested in replacing the Wishart distribution resulting in more flexibility in modelling. The problems of testing and modelling for structural change in the RCOV matrix time series are also investigated. These models are useful in the modelling of realized covariance matrices (RCOV) of returns of financial assets. They can find applications in risk management such as value at risk calculations and portfolio allocation.

17303415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303415.value: The Central Asian Orogenic Belt (CAOB) is the largest Phanerozoic orogenic collage in the world. It was developed during a prolonged history of orogenesis, from ~1000 to ~250 Ma (million years before present), giving rise to an enormous amount of mineral resources. Tectonic reconstructions of the CAOB are poorly constrained, but it is generally agreed that a major process associated with its tectonic history involved a progressive accretion of continental and oceanic materials along the convergent plate margins, and the collision and amalgamation of multiple plates and/or arc systems. How exactly these accretionary and collisional processes occurred is a matter of ongoing investigation that attracts major international research collaborations, such as UNESCO’s funded projects (IGCP 592, 480 and 420). Research on the geology of the CAOB is currently positioned at the forefront of geoscience research (ranked first in Web of Science, 2013), making this project, on collisional processes in northwestern China (Xinjiang), particularly timely and relevant. This project will focus on collisional processes between the Chinese Altai and the East Junggar, which records the amalgamation history of the peri-Siberian orogenic system and the Kazakhstan-South Mongolian orogenic system in the Late Paleozoic. According to detailed structural analysis complemented by petrological and geochronological investigations, this project will constrain spatial and temporal variations in deformation, metamorphism and magmatism in the southern Chinese Altai, with the aim of unraveling the timing and geodynamic processes associated with this amalgamation. The project will specifically evaluate the role of thrust tectonics, strike-slip deformation, and post-collisional extension in the amalgamation processes. The research outcome will build a geodynamic framework of the Chinese Altai in the Late Paleozoic, which will make an important contribution to tectonic studies and mineral exploration. 中亞造山帶是世界上最大的顯生宙造山帶，是在距今1000到250百萬年前長期的歷史過程中形成的，並帶來巨量的礦產資源。中亞造山帶的大地構造重塑工作很初步，但一般認為其構造歷史中沿著匯聚板塊邊緣大陸和大洋物質的不斷增生，伴隨眾多板塊或者島弧體系碰撞拼合是很重要的過程。到底這些增生碰撞如何發生是目前研究的熱點，吸引了好多國際合作，例如IGCP592, 480和420等項目。中亞造山帶的地質研究目前被列為地球科學的前沿課題（2013年被Web of Science列為第一）。因而這一開展中國西北新疆地區碰撞歷史的課題在時間上和意義上都十分重要。 此課題將專注中國阿爾泰和東準噶爾碰撞的過程，記錄了環西伯利亞與哈薩克斯坦-南蒙古造山系統在晚古生代的拼合歷史。依據詳細的構造分析和岩石學、地質年代學研究，此課題將對中國阿爾泰南部變形、變質和岩漿作用進行時空限制，以揭示這一拼合過程的時間和地球動力學過程。 此課題將研究在拼合過程中逆衝構造、走向錯動變形、以及碰撞後的拉張。研究結果將有助於建立古生代中國阿爾泰的地球動力學格局，這對中亞大地構造的整體研究和礦產勘探都有貢獻。

17303415.label: Realisation of objectives
17303415.value: Objective 1: In the beginning of the project, we mapped macroscopic fold structures in the southern Chinese Altai and analyzed their relationships with the development of the adjacent Irtysh Shear Zone, four generations of folding and associated fabrics were identified and published: The earlier fabric (S1), is locally recognized in low strain areas, and is commonly isoclinally folded by F2 folds that have an axial plane orientation parallel to the dominant fabric (S2). S2 is associated with a shallowly plunging stretching lineation (L2), and defines ~NW-SE tight-close upright macroscopic folds (F3) with the doubly plunging geometry. F3 folds are superimposed by ~NNW-SSE gentle F4 folds. The F3 and F4 folds are kinematically compatible with sinistral transpressional deformation along the Irtysh Shear Zone and may represent strain partitioning during deformation. The sub-parallelism of F3 fold axis with the Irtysh Shear Zone may have resulted from strain partitioning associated with simple shear deformation along narrow mylonite zones and pure shear-dominant deformation (F3) in fold zones. The strain partitioning may have become less efficient in the later stage of transpressional deformation, so that a fraction of trans- current components was partitioned into F4 folds (Publication 1). Objective 2: Our data show four major geological events for the Chinese Altai: (1) emplacement of Early Devonian magmas (ca. 410–400) associated with formation of a volcano-sedimentary cover, which was transposed by sub-horizontal Barrovian metamorphic fabric associated with variable metamorphic degrees in different areas, correlating with upper, middle and lower orogenic crust that developed during important vertical shortening and horizontal flow. (2) major Middle Devonian (ca. 390–374 Ma) tectono-metamorphic event (Buchan type), related to intrusions of the syn-subduction granitoids in an extensional setting. (3) Late Devonian-Early Carboniferous NE-SW trending upright folding and crustal scale doming without apparent metamorphism, responsible for the exhumation of the hot lower crust. (4) Early Permian regional NW-SE trending regional upright folding with localized Buchan type high- to ultrahigh-temperature reworking (ca. 300–280 Ma), related to massive perturbation of thermal structure of the mantle lithosphere due to the collision of the Junggar arc with the Chinese Altai terrane (Publications 3 and 4). Objective 3: Our data constrained that the above four structural and metamorphic events occurred at Early Devonian (ca. 410–400 Ma), Middle Devonian (ca. 390–374 Ma), Late Devonian-Early Carboniferous, and Early Permian (ca. 300–280 Ma) (Publication 3). Objective 4: The available data suggest that the Irtysh Complex probably represents an accretionary complex built along the southern Chinese Altai (part of the peri-Siberian orogenic system), incorporating crustal relicts from both the Ob-Zaisan Ocean and the Dulate arc. Metamorphic investigation shows that the amphibolite facies metamorphism occurred at ca. 284 Ma, recording a high geothermal gradient (307– 457C/km) along the Irtysh shear zone. Data compilation suggests that East Junggar probably collided with Chinese Altai between ca. 313 and 299 Ma, which was followed by an episode of high- to ultrahigh-temperature metamorphism possibly related to syn-/postcollisional extension in the early Permian (Publication 2 and 5).

17303415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303415.value: The Siberian marginal arc system (Altai) was separated from an intra-oceanic arc system (Junggar) by the Ob-Zaisan ocean in the Paleozoic. The Chinese Altai represents a ca. 520–460 Ma accretionary wedge, which experienced a lithospheric-scale extensional event in the Devonian, resulting in massive heat influx, emplacement of juvenile magmas, and occurrence of bimodal volcanism (Publication 3, 4, 9 and 10). The orthogneissic rocks formed at ca. 411–398 Ma (Publication 6), and the bimodal volcanic sequences erupted at ca. 380 Ma (Publication 7). We propose an evolving tectonic scenario from a magmatic arc to arc rifting, and finally back-arc opening in the southern Chinese Altai, which corresponds to an extensional regime and resultant asthenosphere upwelling during the Devonian, probably in response to the trench retreat (Publication 6, 7 and 9). This trench retreat was followed by the subduction of a series of back-arc basins, which contributed to the development of multiple arc systems in the CAOB (Publication 9). We further propose that the trench migration is likely a critical mechanism to control the evolution of accretionary systems worldwide (Publications 6 and 7). Our work makes a significant contribution to understand the timing and the processes of the collision between the Chinese Altai and the East Junggar (Publication 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8). The Ob-Zaisan Ocean began to close in the late Carboniferous (<323 Ma), and the collisional zone (Irtysh) was initially subjected to crustal thickening at ca. 323–295 Ma, followed by orogen-parallel extension (ca. 295 Ma) and transpressional deformation (ca. 286–253 Ma) (Publication 2). We consider that the syn-collisional extension was responsible for the Permian elevated thermal gradient, and the subsequent transpressional deformation contributed to the exhumation of high-temperature metamorphic rocks (Publication 2, 3 and 5). The closure of the Ob-Zaisan Ocean post-dates the initial phase of oroclinal bending in the western CAOB, thus indicating that oroclinal bending initiated during subduction. We suggest that the early stage of oroclinal bending was likely driven by slab rollback (Publication 2 and 8). Available data further suggest that alternating contraction and extension operated on the Chinese Altai in the Early-Middle Paleozoic, which is possibly critical for the evolution of accretionary systems worldwide (Publications 6 and 7). We further suggest that the formation of multiple island arcs within marginal sea basins in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, is a possible analogue for the Late Paleozoic development of the East Junggar island arc system (Publication 9).

17303415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303415.value: 1）This project makes a significant contribution for us to understand the arc-arc collisional processes between the Chinese Altai and the East Junggar in northwestern China. Both the Chinese Altai and the East Junggar extend farther east into western Mongolia. It is worth investigating when and how the Mongolian segment of these two arc systems evolved in the late Paleozoic, and whether they behaved in a similar way as in NW China. 2) This project comes out a conceptional model for the arc-arc collision in accretionary orogens. A numerical-modeling study would be helpful to understand how strain evolves in different structural levels in response to ongoing collision.

17303415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303415.value: The lithosphere of the Earth is composed of several rigid plates, the boundaries of which are convergent, divergent or transform faulting. The convergent boundary is a major site of earthquake and volcano, and records the key information how plates interact. This study investigated an ancient plate boundary between the Altai and Junggar plates in Central Asia. An ocean existed between the two plates in the Palaeozoic, called Ob-Zaisan Ocean, and the boundary is now a shear zone, called Irtysh zone. This study aimed to understand when the ocean was closed and what happened along the plate boundary following the ocean closure. Based on field studies and state-of-the art geochemical analysis, the deformation and thermal evolution were depicted. Our results show that the Paleo-Asian Oceanic was consumed ~320 Ma ago, and the lithosphere behaved in a way of episodic thickening and thinning that resulted in contrast metamorphism and a serious of regional magmatism, which is possibly critical for the evolution of accretionary systems worldwide. Our results provide a classic case study for how the collision of two arc systems evolved in an accretionary orogen.

17303515.label: Realisation of objectives
17303515.value: In 1937, Neyman introduced the notion of smooth tests of the null hypothesis that the sample data come from a uniform distribution on the interval (0,1) against alternatives in a smooth parametric family. This idea can be used to embed various nonparametric inference problems in a parametric family. Motivated by Neyman’s work, we proposed in this project an entirely new class of parametric models for the analysis of ranking data which provides a unified framework for analyzing ranking data. We first developed a new class of ranking models based on two rank score functions, Spearman and Kendall. We considered both the Spearman and Kendall score functions in the one or two sample design problems. When the number of items to be ranked is large, we can add a penalty term in the log-likelihood function. The extension to the multi-sample problems was documented in our research monograph published by Springer. It can be seen that the locally most powerful tests can be obtained from this framework. Collaborating with Prof. T.L. Lai, a renowned professor at Stanford University, we further extended the parametric embedding approach to the case of censored data. (Objectives 1 and 3: Alvo (co-I) and Xu (visited Mayer Alvo before his PhD study under me starting from September 2015) (2017), Alvo and Yu (2018) [A Parametric Approach to Nonparametric Statistics. Springer. 279 pages. A review of the monograph: “The book is interesting and well written. Theoretical results and formulas derived are illustrated by various numerical examples. The majority of chapters are equipped with interesting exercises for the readers.” (Jonas Šiaulys, zbMath 1416.62006, 2019)], Alvo, Lai and Yu (2018) and Yu, Gu and Xu (2019)). Note that Dr. Hang Xu is now working as a Data Scientist at Huawei Noah Ark Lab in Hong Kong and Mr. Jiaqi Gu is now studying PhD under my supervision. Motivated from our new formulation, we discovered that the framework can also be applied to detect multiple change points via the embedding of the nonparametric problem into a parametric framework. Under some mild conditions, we showed the consistency and asymptotic properties of the procedure to locate the change points. The proposed method successfully applied to identify chromosomes with DNA copy number alternations, to detect economic recessions on an interest rate time series, and to identify the changes in probability of market backwardation based on the spot and futures price data of the WTI crude oil contracts. (Objectives 1 and 3: Xu, Yu and Alvo (2018) and Alvo and Yu (2018)). Notice that a distance-based ranking model can be viewed as a special case of a score-based model with one-dimensional rank score X(π_j )= d(π_j, π_0) and θ= -λ for modal ranking π_0: for k=1,…,n, p(π_k;λ)=exp{-λd(π_k, π_0)}/C(λ). Here, λ represents the quality of rankers. However, rankers with different backgrounds may have different cognitive levels of examining the items. This motivated us to develop two new distance-based models by allowing different weights for different rankers. One approach is to consider a weighted version of Kendall distance. We also developed the R package “rankdist” which provides a framework for fitting and evaluating finite mixture of distance-based models for complete and incomplete ranking data. Another approach is to assume that ranker k has his/her own λ_k to account for the heterogeneity in the expertise among the rankers. We also proposed a new class of general exponential ranking models called angle-based models which covers the Spearman distance-based model as a special case. A fast variational Bayesian algorithm was developed for determining the posterior predictive density. This approach exhibited a great computational advantage compared to traditional MCMC methods. Model extensions to incomplete rankings and mixture models were also developed. We also considered an extension of angle-based models to incorporate the presence of covariates. Real-world applications demonstrated that the above-mentioned models and their extensions outperform existing rank aggregation methods. (Objectives 1, 2 and 3: Yu and Xu (2019), Qian (my former UG project student) and Yu (2019), and Xu, Alvo and Yu (2018)). I am very glad to know that Mr. Qian is now studying PhD in Mathematics at the Cambridge University in the UK.

17303515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303515.value: In this project, we successfully adopted the notion of Neyman’s smooth tests to construct a new class of parametric models for ranking data in the one-sample, two-sample or multi-sample design problems or in the problem with censored data. The new class of ranking models is considered a breakthrough in the field to formulate nonparametric statistics systematically within a framework of parametric modeling. Under the new models, the locally most powerful tests were developed. We also focused on the generalization of distance-based models, a special class under the general framework. Various computational problems were tackled including optimal parameter tuning, developing efficient parameter estimation procedures and predicting the ranks of the unranked items. The new models were applied successfully to analyze real-world problems, such as aggregating people’s rankings on various sets of items, analysis of incomplete ranking data of NBA teams, classification of disease subtypes of breast cancer patients based on their gene expressions, confirming that the new models outperform existing ones. We also demonstrated that the new framework can be applied to study the multiple change-point problems and the results are promising. We believe the new class of models has made practical and theoretical contributions to the analysis of ranking data.

17303615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303615.value: Geochemical investigations of the aragonite skeletons of stony corals have been critically important in expanding our understanding of past ocean conditions. Within the crystalline structure of the coral skeletal organic matrix (CSOM) remains multiple environmental records, formed at the moment of calcification and well-preserved even after fossilization. Like tree rings, corals form bands that can be dated and analyzed in time-series. Thus, isotopic and elemental records of past ocean temperature and pollution have revealed the impacts of global change and human development on the coastal oceans from modern to ancient timescales. Recently, a new record of stable nitrogen isotopes from CSOM has been achieved through methodological advances. The emergence and utility of this new record will be transformative for the study of ocean nutrient chemistry from modern to ancient timescales. Yet, a critical gap in our understanding of the coral skeletal matrix is the provenance of the nitrogen used in its formation. Without knowing the nutritional pathways by which the organic matrix is formed we cannot understand the sources and mechanisms by which nitrogen records are created, including any crucial “vital effects” associated with the coral’s symbiotic biology, which can confound our interpretations. Here, I propose to conduct enriched stable isotope tracer studies to track the incorporation of nitrogen and carbon from inorganic and organic sources into the coral skeleton of three representative species of reef building corals which vary in their nutritional niche. By using advanced nanoSIMS imaging, we will be able to reveal the incorporation of important nitrogen sources to the coral skeleton at sub-nanometer spatial scales, and assess the relative importance of inorganic and organic nitrogen sources to CSOM. 石珊瑚的霰石結構是地球化學研究理解古海洋氣候的變化的重要手段之一。珊瑚跟樹木一樣擁有年輪，因此可以依時序去分析珊瑚骨有機基質(CSOM)，特別是晶體結構在鈣化期間，甚至成為化石以後保留的環境資訊。同位素及元素技術反映過去海洋溫度和污染的記錄，值此追溯氣候變化和人類活動對沿海海洋從古至今的影響。隨着研究方法的不斷改進和創新，科學家從珊瑚骨有機基質中記錄到穩定氮同位素(d15N)。穩定氮同位素的出現及其效用對於海洋營養化學的研究方向有顯著性的影響。而然，我們對於氮的來源以及形成珊瑚骨基質的角色仍然貧乏。了解有機基質的形成機制有助於我們的理解氮記錄的組成，同時能進一步辨識珊瑚共生的關鍵作用，在以後研究中發揮了極重要的角色。本研究採用 三種擁有不同營養生態位的造礁珊瑚，利用穩定同位素示踪技術(enriched stable isotope tracer)偵測珊瑚骨中氮和碳的來源與形成。通過納米二次離子質譜技術(NanoSIMS)的成像分析，我們將會識別並確認珊瑚骨的氮組成，進而評估有機及無機氮源對珊瑚骨有機基質的重要性。

17303615.label: Realisation of objectives
17303615.value: Building off of our results documented in the mid-term report, we have made significant progress in Objective 1, 2 and 3, and begun to better understand objective 4. Objective 1: We have determined that the skeletal organic matrix (SOM), which contains the organic nitrogen targeted in recent papers, is derived from varying proportions of heterotrophic and autotrophic sources of nitrogen. This has been shown by tracing enriched nutrient sources (heterotrophic - plankton and DON, and autotrophic - DIN) through the coral holobiont, and into the skeleton. It is clear that the coral uses a variety of nutrients from differing sources, depending on its relative level of heterotrophy vs. autotrophy – we discuss this further in Objective 2. Interestingly, we observed that nutrients that were taken up by the holobiont were recycled within the system for up to 60 days after the initial feeding, continuously being incorporated into the skeleton through calcification. In other words, the complete tissue turnover of the coral may take several months. This has significant implications when analyzing nitrogen signals taken from within the SOM, especially in a historical context. Now, we have concluded that this signal is not only a combination of both heterotrophic food and autotrophic assimilated nutrients, but is also a combined signal over several months. This complicates interpretations of coral core records. Objective 2 and 3: Building off of our original nutrient enrichment experiments, we conducted an intensive feeding experiment for Porites lobata in order to quantitatively trace varying forms of heterotopic (zooplankton and phytoplankton) and autotrophic (DIN and DON) nutrient sources. We made serval major conclusions. First, we determined that Porites lobata is a mixotroph, obtaining a significant portion of its nutrient uptake form both heterotrophic and autotrophic sources. Second, although Porites lobata consumes zooplankton, we found that it does not eat phytoplankton at all. Third, based on the amount of nutrient assimilation, we determined that Porites lobata obtains the majority of its nutrients from autotrophic means, relying on the symbiont to assimilate DIN and DON. Fourth, all of the nutrients that were assimilated, regardless of food source, could be traced to the SOM during calcification. Finally, we determined the nutrient turnover time of the holobiont to be greater than 60 days, with significant nutrient recycling and incorporation into the SOM. Porites lobata was chosen as the target species because of its wide distribution, and is the most common species used for paleo- and historical reconstructions of ocean chemistry via its annual growth bands. Therefore, this was the sensible coral to choose as it had the most application outside of just our original questions. Acropora sp. has also been chosen as the next coral to test, again because of its wide species range, its importance as a habitat builder on reefs, and because of its known autotrophic tendencies. However, our first attempts to fragment and grow Acropora in an aquarium failed because of its delicate nature. We have had to rework our aquarium set up and feeding regime. Thorough a recent pilot study, we have now successfully kept Acropora alive for several months, and can move forward with the same feeding experiment as with Porites lobata. Objective 4: As detailed above, we have successfully enriched coral skeletons with stable isotope tracers from varying food sources and now have a collection of enriched skeletons from multiple species. We have confirmed that the SOM in these samples has been enriched as confirmed by EA-IRMS. Those candidate samples are now being mounted and polished for nanoSIMS imaging of the skeletal structures. We will be collaborating with the Centre for Microscopy, Characterization and Analysis at the University of Western Australia to conduct nanoSIMS imaging and two HKU students will travel there in Fall 2019 for training and analysis. In the meantime we have sent preliminary samples for testing.

17303615.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303615.value: Corals likely assimilate varying forms of nutrients from heterotrophic and autotrophic sources, depending on their needs. We have shown this through feeding experimentation, as well as through SIBER analysis. Nutrients assimilated by the coral are recycled and used for biological processes for several months. All nutrients assimilated by the holobiont are incorporated within the SOM during calcification. Increased nutrients were beneficial some coral (Porites) and helped them to recover, where as too much nitrogen killed others (Acropora). Our work has important implications for historical reconstructions of nutrient sources inferred from coral SOM analysis.

17303615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303615.value: We aim to continue this work for several more species and analyze a suite of these via nanoSIMS. We aim to publish a manuscript in the coming year on the feeding study. Future outputs on species differences are planned.

17303615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303615.value: Coral reefs are dying, and nutrients have been found to increase the severity of coral bleaching events. The analysis of nitrogen within the coral skeleton is a new tool which has been used to reconstruct past nitrogen sources on reefs. Yet, this powerful tool has not been properly groundtruthed, and we do not know what sources of nitrogen are recorded within the skeletal organic matrix. In this project, we conducted stable isotope-labelled feeding experiments with several species of corals. We found that corals are capable of assimilating various autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrient sources, which are slowly transferred into synthesis of new skeleton over the period of weeks to months. This finding suggests that interpretation of historical nitrogen stable isotope records from coral skeletons is complicated by vital effects (diet) which further indicates that similar studies must be conducted on a diversity of coral species. nanoSIMS analysis of coral skeletons grown in captivity will help us to visualize the incorporation of dietary nitrogen into the skeletal matrix.

17303715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303715.value: Statistical inference has often been made under a model pre-selected by a data-driven procedure as if this model were the “correct” model. That this practice has been prevalent in many applied works necessitates a careful evaluation of the effects of model selection on conclusions drawn from standard statistical inference. Better insights into the issue have been afforded by recent studies on the distributions of post-model-selection estimators and predictors, which typically exhibit a complicated form in defiance of the “classical” Gaussian protocol, thus pointing to possible invalidity of standard post-model-selection inference. The problem is particularly acute in regression studies where inference analysis is often acted on a “final” model derived from a data-driven variable selection procedure, without taking into account the uncertainties induced by the selection process. This calls into question validity of standard regression inference tools like t-tests and ANOVA, upon which misleading conclusions may potentially be drawn. It is therefore important to develop accurate estimates of the “complicated” distributions of post-model-selection estimators, for which task the conventional asymptotic approach has been found to be particularly ill-equipped. Standard resampling procedures such as the paired and residual bootstraps fail to provide a satisfactory solution neither, as they often turn out to be inconsistent. This project aims to develop a consistent, more sustainable, bootstrap-based procedure for estimating the distributions of post-model-selection estimators, which will suffer less from the aforementioned difficulties. The proposed procedure is novel and can be viewed as an adaptive modification of existing bootstrap methods. Its performance will be investigated theoretically and empirically under settings where estimation of the distribution is found to be difficult. The project, on successful completion, will deliver a more reliable inference scheme for post-model-selection regression analysis, which will find useful applications in a wide spectrum of quantitative studies. 统计推断经常在被数据导向过程预选出的模型下进行，就好像该模型已被 确认“正确无误”。这种做法在实际应用中非常流行，因此详细评估模型选择对 标准统计推断所得结论的影响变得至关重要。最近关于后模型选择的估计和预测 分布的研究更好地分析了该问题，其中，这些分布通常表现出不同于“经典”高 斯原型的复杂形式，因此很可能导致标准后模型选择推断的不成立。如果针对仅 靠数据导向的变量选择过程所得的“最终”模型进行推断分析，而忽略选择过程 中所带来的不确定性，这类回归研究将使上述问题变得尤为严重。这就使得诸如 t 检验和方差分析之类的标准回归推断工具的有效性存疑，因为它们可能得出具 有误导性的结论。因此，提出后模型选择估计量“复杂”分布的准确估计变得十 分重要，而常规的渐进估计方法已被证实不足以完成该项任务。标准的重抽样法， 比如配对自助抽样和残差自助抽样，因为经常得出不相合的推断，也无法给出满 意的解决方案。本项目旨在提出一种基于相合自助抽样的、更为稳定的方法，用 于估计后模型选择估计量的分布，从而避免上述问题的发生。该方法新颖独特， 可以被视为对现有自助抽样法的适应性调整。我们将在分布估计难以实现的设定 下，从理论和实践两方面观察该方法的表现。该项目的顺利完成将给出一个针对 后模型选择回归分析的更为可靠的推断方案，并且该方案可以应用于广泛的定量 研究。

17303715.label: Realisation of objectives
17303715.value: 1) A general framework of model selection was developed for linear regression, which covers a broad class of model selection/averaging methods based on information criteria or sparse estimation. Weak limits of scaled and centred post-model-selection least squares estimators were established from a local asymptotic perspective. In addition to standard linear regression models, two other frameworks were also considered: (1) special logistic regression, where selection is between homogeneity and ordered heterogeneity in binomial probabilities; (2) quantile estimation for strongly mixing data, for which selection is between iid- and dependent-data models. In both frameworks, asymptotic distributions were established for the scaled and centred estimators. 2) A general residual bootstrap recipe was developed for estimating the distributions of post-model-selection least squares estimators under a linear regression model. The recipe constrains residual bootstrapping within the most parsimonious, approximately correct, models. An iterative scheme was also suggested for enhancing the stability of the residual bootstrap distribution estimator. For the special logistic regression model, an m out of n bootstrap procedure was developed for constructing multi-dimensional confidence regions for the binomial probabilities. For quantile estimation for strongly mixing data, a hybrid block bootstrap procedure was developed for estimating the distribution and variance of quantile estimators. 3) Under a local asymptotic framework, theoretical properties of the proposed residual bootstrap procedure were studied, with sufficient conditions given for consistency of the distribution estimator along fairly general convergent sequences of true regression parameters. Specifically, the proposed bootstrap distribution estimator was shown to approach uniform consistency approximately, whenever wrong candidate models are sufficiently separated from the approximately correct ones. Asymptotic properties of the proposed m out of n and hybrid block bootstrap procedures were also established under the logistic regression and dependent data frameworks, respectively, both from the more conventional fixed-parameter perspective. In both cases, consistency results were proved and utilized to guide empirical choices of tuning parameters required by the bootstrap procedures. 4) Simulation studies were conducted to illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed residual bootstrap procedure. Performance indicators include global measures like the mean and standard deviation of Kolmogorov-Smirnov distances between true and estimated distribution functions, and coverage and length properties of confidence intervals constructed using the proposed bootstrap recipe. A real data example, drawn from a study on the relationship between prostate specific antigen and different clinical measures, was also investigated in a comparison between the proposed and existing methods. Similar empirical studies were also conducted for the m out of n and hybrid block bootstrap procedures under their respective problem settings. The results largely corroborate the theoretical properties established of the two methods.

17303715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303715.value: A mixed residual bootstrap recipe is proposed for estimating distributions of post-model-selection least squares estimators under a linear regression model. Consistency is proved under mild conditions on the order of discrepancy between wrong and approximately correct candidate models. The theory applies to a broad class of model selection methods based on information criteria or sparse estimation. (Output 1) Based on a one-dimensional pivot derived from the criterion function, an m out of n bootstrap procedure and a modified perturbation bootstrap procedure are proposed for constructing confidence regions for multi-dimensional M-estimands under nonstandard conditions. The resulting regions are consistent, transformation equivariant and have shapes driven solely by the criterion function. An important application is found in a model selection context involving order restricted models, where standard inference procedures become inconsistent when the true parameter lies close to the boundary of the order restricted parameter space. (Output 2) The special problem of quantile estimation for strongly mixing data is considered. By subsuming the standard moving block bootstrap and subsampling into a hybrid approach, it is shown that consistency holds for a wide range of block numbers and block lengths. This leads to a general class of block bootstrap strategies with potential gains in orders of accuracy for distribution estimation and confidence interval construction. (Output 3) All bootstrap procedures proposed in the project have been investigated empirically via simulation studies.

17303715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303715.value: As a potential extension the linear regression setting can be fitted into a more general model selection framework, where discrepancies between candidate models may be characterized by problem-specific distance measures. Emphasis will be on distribution estimation for some model-specific statistical functional, and post-model-selection inference will centre on a weighted average of such statistical functionals, with weights informed by a general model selection procedure. The local asymptotic framework then refers to a convergent sequence of underlying distributions. Analogous to results proved in Output 1, weak limits of the post-model-selection statistical functionals may be derived under high-level assumptions on the random selection weights, and a bootstrap procedure, now constrained within a consistently selected model, may be developed for consistent distribution estimation. Apart from linear regression, the above general framework encompasses, for example, post-selection likelihood-based inference under a nested class of parametric models.

17303715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303715.value: Statistical inference has often been made under a model pre-selected by a data-driven procedure as if this model were the “correct” model. Recent studies point to possible invalidity of such practice, which fails to take into account the uncertainties induced by the selection process. In this project, novel and sustainable bootstrap-based procedures have been developed for estimating distributions of post-model-selection estimators, mainly in a linear regression context, with extensions to logistic regression models characterized by order-restricted binomial probabilities and quantile estimation for dependent data. The proposed bootstrap procedures provide consistent distribution estimators, based on which credible statistical inference can be drawn. They help to correct a common fallacy held by practitioners and provide for them a satisfactory solution which may find important applications in standard regression and related studies.

17303815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303815.value: 發展新型金屬催化劑催化的高活性、高選擇性、高原子經濟性且底物適用範圍廣的有機反應如碳-碳和碳-雜原子成鍵反應等在現代有機合成中具有深遠的意義。這些新型催化反應不僅減少了副產物和有害物質的產生，還可降低能耗，對於建立可持續發展的綠色化學十分重要。反應的活性和選擇性是衡量這類反應時最重要的標準。已報導的高活性金屬絡合物催化的高選擇性和廣普適性的實用有機反應屈指可數，例如銅催化的點擊化學、釕催化的不對稱氫化和烯烴複分解反應等都是有機合成催化中的里程碑。金屬離子的催化性能主要由其電子結構決定，並受到軸向配體如反位碳-給體型配體的影響。利用譜學手段和計算化學對反應的中間體和反應歷程進行監測和驗證將為研究金屬絡合物催化反應的決速步提供極有用的資訊。除了受中心金屬影響之外，配體的三維結構對有機反應的選擇性也有極大的影響，因此設計新的配體將是發展新的金屬催化的有機反應中的主要任務。 金屬-碳鍵的研究是金屬有機化學的核心。在過去的幾十年裡，多種碳-給體型配體被開發出來並合成了相應的金屬絡合物。金屬-碳共價鍵可賦予金屬絡合物很高穩定性使之不易發生脫金屬反應。同時金屬-碳鍵的共價鍵性質還可極大的影響金屬絡合物的電子結構，並已成功的應用于合成具有工業應用前景的強磷光金屬絡合物有機發光材料中。然而與之相對應的，通過金屬-碳共價鍵來穩定高活性的不穩定中間體，使之在更溫和的條件下生成以實現具有更高催化活性的金屬絡合物催化劑方面的研究卻很少。最近我們的研究工作表明在金屬卟啉絡合物中引入反位碳-給體型配體可以大幅度提高這類催化劑在原子/基團轉移反應中的催化活性。 本研究計畫將從（i）金屬-碳成鍵作用（ii）具有特殊的非平面配位元構型三維結構的新型大位元阻四齒配體兩方面入手發展用於碳-碳和碳-雜原子成鍵反應的新型金屬絡合物催化劑。首先將研究通過活性金屬-烷基卡賓中間體進行的催化反應，此外將研究具有特殊cis構型手性大位阻四齒配體金屬絡合物的催化應用，預期通過其特殊cis構型可同時對反應底物進行配位並生成活性中間體以實現分子間及分子內反應。本研究的長期目標立足于發展具有高活性和選擇性的包括廉價金屬在內的多種金屬絡合物催化劑體系並應用於有機合成化學之中。

17303815.label: Realisation of objectives
17303815.value: In accordance with the foregoing objectives, we have published fifteen papers in leading international chemistry journals particularly two in Journal of American Chemical Society, two in Angewandte Chemie International Edition and one in Chemical Science. Among the fifteen published papers, three are jointly published with Dr. Zhen-Jiang Xu, the co-I of this project. Objective 1: With the design of new catalysts based on auxiliary C-donor ligands, we have successfully developed three different kinds of C-X (X = C, O, N) bond formation reactions. First, air-stable arylruthenium(III) porphyrins were competent for the efficient oxidations of inert saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons under mild conditions with yields up to 99% and good regio-selectivity observed. The long-proposed reactive intermediate Ru(V)-oxo porphyrin has been trapped spectroscopically (EPR, ESI-MS, UV-vis and resonance Raman), and DFT-calculations further substantiated the claim that Ru(III)-Ru(V)-oxo cycle is a new direction for (asymmetric) C-H oxidation. Second, the use of NHC ligand imparts robustness and stability of Fe(III) porphyrin in alkylnitrene C-H insertion reactions under thermal and microwave-assisted conditions. Besides, the substrate scope is greatly expanded to primary, secondary and tertiary C-H bonds and mono- to tri-substituted alkyl azides by employing such NHC Fe(III) porphyrin as a new catalyst which outcompetes other catalysts. Some mechanistic experiments (kinetic isotope effect and radical clocks) and DFT-calculations were conducted to gain insights into the reaction mechanism. We found that the presence of NHC facilitates azide decomposition and subsequent C-H amination by minimizing out-of-plane displacement of the metal centre. Third, we have also isolated several novel Ru(II) quinoid carbene porphyrins for studying the structure-reactivity relationship, beneficial to the development of C-C bond formation reactions. With the aid of metal catalysts, quinoid carbene (QC) transfer are feasible for different kinds of nucleophiles including halides, O-H bonds, enol ethers and alkenes but relatively less reactive towards C-H bonds. We figured that Ru QC porphyrins could transfer its QC moieties to nitrosoarenes and undergo hydrogen atom abstraction reactions. According to the spectro-electrochemical studies, we found that the isolable Ru(II) QC porphyrins will become much more unstable upon oxidation/reduction, and oxidation/reduction may provide a new means to develop efficient QC transfer towards C-H insertion reactions. Objective 2: To exploit C-O and C-N bond formation reactions, we have synthesized and studied iridium, ruthenium and rhenium complexes supported by various non-porphyrin type ligands with steric bulk. Cis-dioxo ruthenium and rhenium N4 complexes were both studied because they are topologically identical. With the successful isolation of rhenium(V) dioxo N4 complexes, we envisioned that rhenium(V) trans-dioxo could exist using 6-Me2-pyxn ligand while cis-dioxo geometries predominate using R,R-pdp, R,R-6-Mepdp and bqcn as supporting ligands. Also, the bond dissociation energy of O-H bond (DO-H) in [ReVI(O)(OH)(pyxn)]2+ was found to be ca. 74.5 kcal/mol only, suggesting that C(sp3)-H oxidation of hydrocarbons necessitates a much more oxidizing metal dioxo catalyst. As a result, we also studied Ru(VI) cis-dioxo N4 complexes for expediting the development of C-H oxidation reactions. Electrochemical analyses revealed that cis-[(mcp)(RuVI(O)2]2+ and cis-[(pdp)RuVI(O)2]2+ are highly oxidizing with Eo = 1.11-1.13 V vs. SCE (at pH 1), and the DO-H was found to be 90-91 kcal/mol, which is ca. +15 kcal/mol greater than that of rhenium congeners. As expected, the strong hydrogen atom affinity is always accompanied with an increase in strong oxidizing power, and they were able to oxidize highly inert hydrocarbons especially cyclohexane at RT. Also, catalytic oxidation of pharmaceuticals and natural product derivatives could be achieved using cerium(IV) ammonium nitrate as terminal oxidant. Other than Group 7 and 8 metal complexes, we also isolated and crystallographically characterized relatively uncommon trans-dichloroiridium(IV) salen complexes, which were found to be good nitrene transfer catalyst. As a proof-of-concept, preliminary catalytic reactions (intramolecular arylnitrene C-H insertion) were conducted using such complexes under microwave-assisted conditions with yields up to 93%. Furthermore, ESI-MS spectra revealed that Ir-nitrene/imido intermediate could be involved during the reaction. This work showed that Group 9 metal complexes could also serve as oxidation catalyst. Objective 3: Previously, we pioneered the C-C bond formation reaction using ruthenium porphyrin-catalyzed alkylcarbene C-H insertion. Soon afterwards, similar alkylcarbene transfer reactions were achieved using non-ruthenium catalysts. For instance, we found that cobalt perfluorinated porphyrin ([Co(F20-TPP]) can undergo alkylcarbene cyclopropanation of pyrroles and ring-opening in a cascade manner, giving pyrrolizidines/pyrrolizines as final products. This streamlines the synthesis of complicated nitrogen-containing compounds. Besides, it can also catalyze Buchner reaction and arene cyclopropantion via alkylcarbene intermediate with good chemo- and regio-selectivities observed. On the other hand, in collaboration with Dr. Xu, we have successfully used simple iron porphyrin ([Fe(TPP)Cl]) as a catalyst for intermolecular alkylcarbene X-H insertion reactions (X = Si, Sn, Ge) which are unprecedented. Other remarkable features include insertion to primary/secondary/tertiary Si-H bonds and programmable stepwise twice Si-H insertion. Apart from those alkylcarbene reactions, we have also exploited some extra carbene transfer reactions that are relatively underexplored. As the foregoing ruthenium (II) quinoid carbene (QC) species were found to be unreactive under normal conditions, we used the typical rhodium catalyst ([Rh2esp2]) to catalyze the alkylation of benzenes via intermediacy of rhodium QC. Gratifyingly, alkylation of benzenes can be performed under mild and base-, directing group- and oxidant-free conditions, with broad substrate scope (tolerating ester, hydroxy, amino and alkoxy groups) and yields up to 92%. In addition, we have also successfully extended the protocol to late-stage modification of drugs and complicated organic molecules like Chloambucil, Melatonin and Nabumetone derivatives. On the other hand, perfluoroalkyl carbene mediated three-component reaction (alkyne, nitrosoarene and perfluoroalkylcarbene) was also developed using [Ru(4-Cl-TPP)(CO)] as a catalyst with yields and cis-trans ratio up to 96% and >99:1 respectively, leading to formation of highly versatile pharmaceutical intermediates (N-alkyl aziridines). Other than application in bioconjugation (Novol, Estrone and Ergosterol derivatives), we have also captured and characterized the Ru perfluoroalkyl carbene intermediate spectroscopically (1H and 13C NMR), allowing us to further study the structure-reactivity relationship and expand the substrate scope and type of reaction. Objective 4: In collaboration with Dr. Xu, we have employed chiral ruthenium and iron complexes with two labile ligands in cis-configuration as catalysts for asymmetric cis-dihydroxylation reaction. First, we found that the aforementioned Ru catalyst (cis-[(mcp)(RuVI(O)2]2+) can catalyze asymmetric cis-dihydroxylation with moderate %ee observed under non-optimized/preliminary conditions. As a proof of concept, we also studied the same reaction using iron catalysts which also belong to group 8. Efficient cis-dihydroxylation can actually be achieved using [Fe(N,N’-dimethyl-N,N’-bis(2-methyl-8-quinolyl)-cyclohexane-1,2-diammine)(OTf)2], with ee and isolated yield up to 99.8% and 85% respectively. It is noteworthy that limiting amount of alkene and green oxidant (H2O2) can be used. Importantly, we have also investigated the reaction mechanism through O18-labelling, UV-Vis, EPR and ESI-MS experiments. Such mechanistic experiments suggested that FeIII-OOH intermediate could be involved during the course of reaction, and this was further supported by DFT-calculations. DFT-calculations showed that the formation of widely proposed intermediate, FeV-(O)(OH) from FeIII-OOH is both thermodynamically and kinetically unfavourable.

[4] Two important works related to the use of novel group 8 organometallic complexes on catalytic C-H oxidation and amination were developed and published in Journal of the American Chemical Society, 2018, 140, 7032-7042 and Angewandte Chemie International Edition, 2018, 57, 11947-11951, respectively. [5] Synthesis and detailed crystal structure-reactivity studies of unprecedented ruthenium quinoid carbene porphyrins were reported in Journal of the Chemical Society, 2019, 141, 9027-9046. 17303815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303815.value: C-, N- and O-group transfers to notoriously inert saturated hydrocarbons streamline syntheses of bio-active molecules and pharmaceuticals, and minimize wastage of unnecessary reagents and production of unwanted and undesirable wastes. However, direct C-H functionalization always requires harsh reaction conditions and the use of toxic reagents (e.g. halogen-containing compounds). One of the key elements to develop efficient and green methods for organic transformation reactions is to employ novel and new metal catalysts, which are supported by sophisticatedly designed macrocyclic and auxiliary ligands. In this project, we have successfully developed various transition metal catalysts for carbene, nitrene and oxo transfer reactions. Uncommon organo-iron(III), -ruthenium(III) porphyrins and iridium(IV) salen complexes serve as highly efficient catalysts for oxidative C-H functionalization reactions. In particular, the iron porphyrin catalyzed alkylnitrene C-H insertion reaction has shown its potential applications on the synthesis and modification of pharmaceuticals and bioactive natural products. Meanwhile, fundamental studies of cis-dioxoruthenium(VI) complexes shed light on the reaction mechanism, providing new direction of improving catalytic efficiency. Such remarkable findings were published in prestigious international chemistry journals including JACS, Angewandte Chemie International Edition, Chemical Science and Chemical Communications. The aforementioned achievements expedite the development of metal-catalyzed organic transformation reactions in a world-class level.

17304415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304415.value: Owning to their origins in the theory of quantum groups, many varieties that are important in representation theory carry naturally defined Poisson structures that have finitely many torus orbits of symplectic leaves, or T-leaves in short. While the geometry and topology of such T-leaves may be complicated and in fact have been little studied, they exhibit common features such as having trivial canonical line bundles. In this research project, the PI showed that a class of T-leaves to be Poisson groupoids which are at the same time cluster varieties. Particular Hamiltonian systems on the T-leaves and T-moment maps have been investigated. The project lies at the cross road of Poisson geometry, commutative algebras, representation theory, and combinatorics.

17304715.value: 以第14族碳化學為主的π共軛給體-橋-受體（donor-bridge-acceptor，D-B-A）體系已成為用於研究和理解有關捕光及太陽能轉換中的光致電子轉移和能量轉移過程的一種模型系統。在D-B-A體系中，富勒烯衍生物是其中一種被廣泛應用的電子受體，特別是在有機光伏方面。而它們的成功是建基於人們對電荷轉移的性質和支配電荷分離及電荷重組的因素的基礎理解上。這些因素包括電子和能量級聯、自組織、分子間順序和空間排列。由於這些因素在決定體系性質和性能方面發揮著重要的作用，我們不單要理解它們在各個組成基團上的影響，亦要理解它們在D-B-A體系中的影響。目前大多數關於富勒烯衍生物的自組織和超分子D-B-A的研究都集中在純有機體系。除了金屬卟啉、金屬酞菁和八面體d6金屬到配體的電荷轉移（MLCT）體系以外，其他含金屬-配體發色團的系統都很少被研究。而純有機體系的超分子組裝、組織和分子間有序化的研究都還沒被深入地探索和理解, 更何況是其他含金屬D-B-A體系。含D-B-A體系的八面體金屬到配體電荷轉移(MLCT)的發色團的組裝可控性亦很有限。在本課題中，通過把d8金屬-配體發色團引入D-B-A體系，我們相信可藉此研發獨特的D-B-A，為探索它們的分級超分子組裝提供了新的機遇和研究空間，並產生預期的電荷轉移和功能性質。更深入探索利用金屬-配體發色團和它們的D-B-A體系的可控性組裝和自組織來形成納米結構。這些納米結構將具有預期的捕光、光學、電荷傳輸和其它功能性質。除了含碳的衍生物外，我們也將對第14族的硅氧烷籠狀物進行研究。與富勒烯不同的是，硅氧烷籠狀物相對惰性和絕緣，是廣泛用於組成聚合物和雜化材料的納米級構築模塊，以及探索超分子組裝和架構的多功能平台。這可能會產生有趣的功能和形態特性。特別是由於現有關於含有金屬和Si-O的混合體系的探討十分有限，這個研究將為含碳體系提供一個有趣的對照研究。我們相信，對於光學、供體受體電荷轉移、發光等功能性質，以及決定超分子組裝和組織結構形態的潛在因素的理解和相互關係，將有利我們深入了解結構與性能之間的關係，也將有助於未來設計與開發新型功能化的含碳和含硅金屬-配體發色團，以及含金屬D-B-A和Si-O的混合體系。這些超分子組裝體將會產生與可調控分級順序和校準相關的獨特光學、供體受體電荷轉移、電荷傳輸及功能特性。

17304815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304815.value: The Yangtze River is the largest river in Asia and its source is located in the central part of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Due to climate warming, the ice and glaciers in the source of the Yangtze River are melting and the permafrost in this region also shows significant degradation. Although extensive studies have been conducted to investigate the climate change in the source region of the Yangtze River and the response of glaciers and permafrost to the climate warming, there is no study on groundwater flow in this area in response to the climate change. We hypothesis that the ice melting due to climate change has a significant influence on groundwater flow systems in the Yangtze River source region and that both regional groundwater flow patterns and hydrogeochemical properties of the groundwater can be affected profoundly by the ice melting. We propose to develop a large-scale, three-dimensional numerical model coupling ice dynamics and groundwater flow to investigate the hydrogeological processes of the Yangtze River source region in response to climate change. Climate change-induced ice dynamics in the region will be first quantified, including ice area and volume changes, subglacial meltwater fluxes, subglacial infiltration, and permafrost evolution. These data will then be used as input in the coupled glaciation and groundwater flow model. Isostasy and ice sheet loading will also be included in the coupled model. This project will be carried out by an experienced interdisciplinary team with expertise in geology, hydrogeology, Quaternary climate and environment, and numerical modeling and will be the first study to investigate the impact of climate warming-induced ice melting on the regional groundwater flow system in the Yangtze River source region. Successful completion of this study will provide import insights into the response of the groundwater flow system in the Yangtze River source region to climate change. This study will also provide new insights into the coupled processes of ice dynamics and groundwater flow. This research project has not only theoretical but also practical significance in the ecologically and environmentally sensitive area which serves as the source of the third largest river in the world. 长江为亚洲第一长河，发源于青藏高原中部。由于气候变暖，导致长江源头的冰川融化，也使该区域的永久冻土层呈现出显著的消退。尽管已经有许多研究涉及长江源头气候变化，以及冰川和永久冻土层对气候变暖的反应，但是目前还没有涉及到气候变暖对该区域地下水运动的影响。 我们认为由气候变化引起的冰川融化可能对长江源头的地下水系统与地下水水文地球化学性质有显著的影响。我们打算建立一个耦合了冰川动态和地下水流动的大规模三维数值模型，来探讨气候变化对长江源头水文地质过程的影响。首先，我们将量化由气候变化导致的该区域冰川动态，包括冰川覆盖面积和储量变化以及冰川下入渗和永久冻土的演化。这些数据将被用作冰川作用和地下水流动的模型的输入项。 数值模型将会首次应用于气候变暖导致的冰川融化对长江源头区域性地下水流动的影响的研究中。该研究的成功完成对气候变化引起的长江源头地下水流动反应方面的研究有重大意义。该研究也将对冰川动态和地下水流动的耦合过程提供新的见解。该研究对有着生态和环境敏感性的世界第三大河流的源头地区有理论和实践意义。

17304815.label: Realisation of objectives
17304815.value: 1) Collect geological and hydrogeological data of the Yangtze River source region We have collected various geological and hydrogeological reports about the study areas from government organisations, universities and research institutes. We also have collected a lot of papers on geology and hydrogeology of the study area and the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP). In addition, we conducted an extensive literature review on the interactions between glacier and groundwater under climate warming, both on the QTP and other places of the world. 2) Investigate hydraulic properties of the soil and chemical and isotope characteristics of the water in some representative areas in the Yangtze River source region We have had a trip to understand the topography, geology and hydrogeology in the source region of Yangtze river. We have collected more than 100 groundwater and river water samples for chemical and isotopic analyses. We have analyzed water chemistry, stable isotopes (δ2H and δ18O), and radium and radon for 116 water samples collected. Five papers have been published on this topic, which are: Luo et al, 2016; Luo et al, 2017; Luo et al 2018; Kuang et al, 2019 3) Study ICESat and GRACE satellite data to obtain water level in lakes and terrestrial water storage We used GRACE to analyze terrestrial water storage of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, including the Yangtze River source region. We also developed a new method to estimate regional hydraulic diffusivity from the GRACE data. Two papers have been published on this topic: Jiao et al 2015; Hu and Jiao 2016. 4) Investigate climate change in the Yangtze River source region We analyzed climate change on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau from the 1950s. A paper have been published on this topic: Kuang and Jiao 2016. This paper presents an overview of recent progress on climate change on the QTP with the aim of providing a comprehensive understanding of changes in climate variables. Long-term observation data from meteorological stations presented by the published literature were used to show the trends in various climate variables.

17304815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304815.value: The Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (QTP) is undergoing significant warming since the 1950s. The QTP is overall getting warmer and wetter during the past decades. Temperature is significantly increased, especially since the 1980s. The overall warming rate ranges from 0.16 to 0.67 °C/decade since the 1950s during different periods. The warming rate in the Yangtze River source region is 0.30 °C/decade. The annual precipitation in the Yangtze River source region is increased slightly. We also investigated the mechanisms of climate change on the QTP. We found that the glacier area of the Tuotuo River Basin has been retreating in the past 50 years and the retreating rate was accelerated since 2000. The melting rate of the Tuotuo River Glacier in thickness is about 1.06-1.61 m/yr. During 1966-2015, the average glacial mass balance of the Dongkemadi River Basin is -151 mm/a and the accumulated loss of glacier mass is 7.55 m. The effect of temperature increase on glaciers exceeds the increase of rainfall. Glacial mass balance is positively correlated with precipitation and negatively correlated with positive accumulated temperature and glacial meltwater. In the past 50 yr，the total runoff，glacier runoff, and non-glacier runoff in the Dongkemadi River Basin all showed increasing trends，of which 25% of the increase in river runoff was caused by the increase in precipitation and 75% was caused by the melting of glaciers due to the increase in temperature. We also found that there was significant permafrost degradation in the QTP from 1982 to 2012. We found that groundwater discharge accounts for 29% of total runoff in the Tuotuo River Basin. Groundwater recharge and the subsurface outflow are sensitive to the changes in hydraulic conductivity and precipitation. The acceleration of glacier melting will lead to the rise of water table in the Tuotuo River Basin. It will also make more meltwater participate in local groundwater circulation. If the glacier melting rate in the Tuotuo River Basin increase 10 times, the groundwater discharge to rivers will increase by 38%. We also found that the average subglacial meltwater of the Donkemadi Glacier in the Yangtze River source region is 19 mm/yr. In the next 50 years, thickness of the glaciers will significantly decrease due to the temperature rise. Consequently, the amount of meltwater infiltration will also decrease. Air temperature has the largest influence on glacier meltwater infiltration, followed by hydraulic conductivity and precipitation.

17304815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304815.value: Improve the study on the impact of accelerated glacier melting on groundwater recharge and discharge. We will use numerical modeling to conduct this study and write up manuscripts on this topic. Further investigate the mechanisms of groundwater flow in permafrost area, including compare and propose relative permeability model of frozen soils..

17304815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304815.value: In this project, we use existing geological and hydrogeological data, climate data, information from other similar studies, remote sensing, and numerical methods to investigate the impact of climate change on groundwater in the study area. This study will help us understand the glacier changes in the study area due to climate warming. It will also help use understand the recharge of glacier meltwater to groundwater. Through the project, we will know better the changes of groundwater flow system in the study area in response to accelerated glacier melting. This study can also predict the glacier and groundwater changes in the future. The results of this study will provide a scientific basis for the protection of water resources in the Yangtze River source region. This study will also provide reference for studies on other glacierized regions similar to the Yangtze River source region.

17305015.label: Project Objectives
17305015.value: We will analyze the radial velocity data of two close binary star systems (HIP 36616 and 39 Cygni) to characterize the planet orbiting the primary star. The HIP 36616 system will be the most eccentric close binary with a planet, and the planet may be on a retrograde orbit, revolving in the opposite direction as the binary. We will investigate the constraints on planet formation theory from the HIP 36616 system. In particular, we will study the dynamics of km-sized bodies called planetesimals in the context of this system and consider the differences in the dynamics and accretion of these bodies in prograde and retrograde orbits. We will examine the general conditions under which the orbits of the planets in a multiple-planet system with a distant, inclined companion would precess together and remain nearly coplanar. We will investigate whether the statistics of transit timing variations in the Kepler space telescope data is consistent with the small mutual inclinations inferred from all planet pairs in the Kepler data.
