17305015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305015.value: Recent advances in the search and characterization of planets around other stars have made it possible to determine the three-dimensional structures of extrasolar planetary systems. We propose to investigate several problems related to the orbital inclinations of extrasolar planets. (1) We will analyze the radial velocity data of two close binary star systems (HIP 36616 and 39 Cygni) to characterize the planet orbiting the primary star. The HIP 36616 system will be the most eccentric close binary with a planet, and the planet may be on a retrograde orbit, revolving in the opposite direction as the binary. (2) We will investigate the constraints on planet formation theory from the HIP 36616 system. In particular, we will study the dynamics of km-sized bodies called planetesimals in the context of this system and consider the differences in the dynamics and accretion of these bodies in prograde and retrograde orbits. (3) We will examine the general conditions under which the orbits of the planets in a multiple-planet system with a distant, inclined companion would precess together and remain nearly coplanar. The best example of this phenomenon is Kepler-56, where two planets are on nearly coplanar orbits that are significantly tilted from the equator of the host star and a distant perturber has been detected. (4) We will investigate whether the statistics of transit timing variations in the Kepler space telescope data is consistent with the small mutual inclinations inferred from all planet pairs in the Kepler data. 近年來在觀測太陽系以外行星的發展已經使天文學家可以確定一些行星系統的三維結構。我們提議研究幾個關於系外行星的軌道傾角的問題。（1）我們將分析兩個近雙星系統（HIP 36616 和天鵝座39星）的視向速度數據以表徵圍繞它們主星的行星。HIP 36616 將會是存在於雙星軌道偏心率最高的行星，而它的軌道的方向很可能跟雙星的軌道是相反的。（2）我們將研究這個 HIP 36616 系統對行星形成理論的約束，尤其是雙星系統內順行和逆行的星子的動力和增長的差異。（3）一些多行星系統（最好的例子是 開普勒-56）有一個在傾斜軌道的遙遠伴星, 但行星的軌道能保持差不多同一個平面。我們將研究在什麼情況下一個有遙遠伴星的行星系統內的行星能保持近共平面軌道。（4）開普勒太空望遠鏡發現的行星中有一些顯示由於其它行星引起的凌星時刻變化。我們將調查凌星時刻變化的數據統計是否與開普勒數據推導出的另一個結論（多行星系統內的行星軌道有很小的相互傾向）是一致的。

17305015.label: Realisation of objectives
17305015.value: (1) We have analyzed 12 years of radial velocity (RV) data of the 1.9 solar-mass K giant star HD 59686 (also known as HIP 36616) taken at the Lick Observatory by CoI Quirrenbach et al. The data clearly show that HD 59686 is a single-line spectroscopic binary with a secondary star of minimum mass of 0.53 solar masses in a close and eccentric orbit (semimajor axis a = 13.6 AU, eccentricity e = 0.73). Additionally, there is a planet with a minimum mass of 7.0 Jupiter masses orbiting the K giant on a nearly circular orbit with a = 1.09 AU. We have performed a detailed dynamical analysis of the HD 59686 system. We investigated large sets of orbital fits consistent with the RV data by applying bootstrap and systematic grid search techniques coupled with self-consistent dynamical fitting. We performed long-term dynamical integrations of these fits to constrain the permitted orbital configurations. We also tested a large number of mutually inclined dynamical models (from coplanar prograde to coplanar retrograde) in an attempt to constrain the three-dimensional orbital architecture. We have analyzed a large collection of RV data of the K giant star epsilon Cygni taken by us at the Lick Observatory and SONG telescope, in combination with archival data. We fitted Keplerian and fully dynamical models to the RVs in order to explore the properties of a previously known spectroscopic stellar companion and to investigate whether there is an additional planetary companion in the system. Our model characterizes the orbit of the binary to high precision, resulting in a semimajor axis of a = 15.6 AU, eccentricity of e = 0.93, and a minimum mass of the secondary of 0.265 solar masses. There are additional short-period RV variations closely resembling the signal of a Jupiter-mass planet orbiting the primary component with a period of 291 days, but the period and amplitude of the putative orbit change over time. To search for long-term stable regions around the orbit of this putative planet, We also ran a stability analysis using an N-body code, and no stable orbits could be found in a large region around the best fit. Alternative causes for the short-period RV variations, such as stellar spots and oscillations, were examined by analyzing photometric data of the system and comparing its properties to known variable stars with long secondary periods and heartbeat stars from the literature. We have performed self-consistent dynamical modeling and long-term stability test to model the RV measurements of the 1.9 solar mass star HD 202696 taken by the HIRES spectrograph. The RV data show evidence for a two-planet system, with orbital periods of 517.8 and 946.6 days, eccentricities of 0.011 and 0.028, and minimum masses of 2.00 and 1.86 Jupiter masses, respectively. For the majority of the stable configurations, we found an aligned or anti-aligned apsidal libration, suggesting that the system is likely dominated by secular perturbations near the 11:6 orbital period ratio. (2) To constrain the conditions under which the planet in the HD 59686 system formed, an MPhil student under the PI's supervision has performed extensive numerical orbit integrations to study the stability of planetary orbits around the primary star. For coplanar orbits, in addition to the bulk stable region in the (a,e) parameter space, we also found two types of stable regions, which are the horizontal stable islands due to secular apsidal alignment and the vertical stable islands due to mean-motion resonances. These extra stable islands can be present at distances beyond the stability boundary for circular orbits by 17% for prograde orbits and 39% for retrograde orbits. There are also high inclination stable islands due to Kozai resonance, but they have high planetary eccentricity values. The MPhil student has also extended this study to the stability of coplanar retrograde planets in general binary star systems. Numerical results were fitted to derive an empirical formula for the stability boundary for circular retrograde orbits, similar to that of Holman & Wiegert (1999) for circular prograde orbits. We found that the retrograde/prograde stability boundary has a ratio of about 1.6 over large part of binary parameter space and approaches 2 in the Hill’s regime. We generalized previous work on generalized Hill’s sphere and successfully explained this ratio of 2. We have performed two-dimensional isothermal hydrodynamical simulations of protoplanetary disks around the primary star of a binary star system using the FARGO3D code. We adopted the masses and semimajor axis of the HD 59686 binary and explored the differences in the response of the circumprimary disk to a binary companion in retrograde/prograde orbits with various binary eccentricity. (3) We have studied systems with two inner planets perturbed by a distant, inclined perturber and examined the conditions under which the orbits of the inner planets would precess rigidly (and remain nearly coplanar) or independently. We performed a large number of numerical orbit integrations with different semimajor axes and masses of the inner planets and inclination of the perturber. The results were compared to two analytic criteria, one based on the Lidov-Kozai timescale and the other on the Laplace-Lagrange secular theory. We also examined the effect of mean-motion resonances by performing simulations where the inner planets are in 2:1 mean-motion resonance. (4) After the grant period started, we found that other groups have already examined some aspects of the statistics of transit timing variations in the Kepler space telescope data. So we decided to turn our attention to a very interesting new extrasolar planetary system: TRAPPIST-1. It consists of seven Earth-sized planets hosted by a very-low mass M-dwarf star where the period ratios of each adjacent planet pairs are close to two-body mean-motion resonances. The period ratios are 8:5, 5:3, 3:2, 3:2, 4:3, and 3:2 from the innermost to the outermost planet pair. Observations hint at the presence of three-body resonances between each adjacent planet triplets, rendering this system the longest resonant chain system discovered to date. An MPhil student under the PI's supervision has examined the dynamics of the TRAPPIST-1 system using the fits provided by Wang et al. (2017) and Grimm et al. (2018) by means of long-term N-body integrations. Simulations modelling the migration and subsequent capture of the TRAPPIST-1 planets into a chain of two-body mean-motion resonances were also performed to determine the equilibrium eccentricities for period ratios matching the values from the observations. The equilibrium eccentricities are lower than the time-average eccentricities from the fits.

17305015.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305015.value: (1) We have discovered a Jupiter-mass planet and a stellar companion around the star HD 59686. There are narrow regions of stable orbital solutions locked in secular apsidal alignment, if the planetary orbit is nearly coplanar and prograde with respect to the binary orbit. But it is more likely that the planet is on a nearly coplanar, retrograde orbit, which is stable for a large range of orbital solutions. HD 59686 is one of the closest and most eccentric binaries known to have circumprimary planets. We have determined the orbit of the epsilon Cygni binary accurately and ruled out a planetary origin for the short-period RV variations. Alternative explanations also failed, and the variability remains a mystery for now. We have discovered two Jovian-mass planets around the star HD 202696 with an orbital period ratio below 2:1. This system may constrain the properties of disk–planet interactions needed for giant planets to break the strong 2:1 mean-motion resonance. Three journal papers have been published, and another one will be submitted soon. (2) For circumprimary planetary orbits in the HD 59686 system, we have discovered islands of stability due to secular apsidal alignment and mean-motion resonances, in addition to the bulk stable region in (a,e) space. The results clarify why the observed planet is located in one of the islands stabilized by apsidal alignment or in the bulk stable region if the orbit is prograde or retrograde, respectively. We have also derived an empirical formula for the stability boundary for circular retrograde orbits in general binary star systems. Hydrodynamical simulations of circumprimary protoplanetary disks suggest that a disk with a retrograde secondary tends to be larger in size and has global eccentricity less sensitive to the binary orbital eccentricity compared to the corresponding prograde case. Two journal papers will be submitted soon. (3) For two inner planets perturbed by a distant, inclined perturber, the numerical results on the mutual inclination between the planets are more consistent with the predictions based on the Laplace-Lagrange secular theory, but could be larger if the planets are in 2:1 mean-motion resonance. A paper is under preparation. (4) For the TRAPPIST-1 system, only fits with low angular momentum deficit are dynamically stable. Some of the fits show three-body resonances, which could exist independently of two-body resonances.

17305015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305015.value: We are continuing our collaboration with CoI Quirrenbach and former postdoc Trifonov to discover and characterize extrasolar planetary systems. In particular, we have obtained high-resolution adaptive optics image using SPHERE and radial velocity data using HARPS for nu Octantis, which is a binary star system with a circumprimary planet. We will be able to determine whether the secondary is a low-mass main-sequence star or a white dwarf and whether there is a circumprimary planet on a retrograde orbit in this system. Our hydrodynamical simulations of circumprimary disks in binary star systems showed that retrograde disks seem to be more sensitive to the setup of the simulations (inner boundary conditions, use of advection algorithm, etc.) than prograde disks. We will need to conduct a more careful analysis of this issue to confirm the reliability of the results. We are extending our analysis of three-body resonances to determine the conditions under which pure three-body resonance (without libration of the two-body resonance angles) and double two-body resonance can exist. We will analyze the origin and capture probability of the multiple stationary points for the three-body resonance with the same double two-body resonance.

17305015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305015.value: We have investigated the dynamics and origins of extrasolar planetary systems. In particular, we have discovered a binary companion on an eccentric orbit and a Jupiter-mass planet orbiting the star HD 59686. The planet is most likely on a retrograde orbit, revolving in the opposite direction as the binary. We have studied the stability of prograde and retrograde planetary orbits around the primary star in binary star systems, as well as the structures of prograde and retrograde protoplanetary disks in which planets form. We have discovered that the star epsilon Cygni has a binary companion on a highly eccentric orbit and shows short-period radial velocity variations of an as yet unknown origin and that the star HD 202696 has a pair of Jupiter-mass planets in a compact configuration. We have analyzed how the mutual inclination of the orbits of two planets are affected by the gravitational perturbations from a distant, inclined perturber. We have shown that stability of the remarkable TRAPPIST-1 system with seven Earth-sized planets requires the orbits to have low eccentricities, and that the orbits of the planet could be in chains of three-body resonances, with or without two-body resonances.

17305115.label: Project Objectives
17305115.value: Internal Structure and Kinematics of Circumbinary Disks: We have been awarded observing time on ALMA to study the circumbinary disk in the binary protostellar system L1551 IRS5. L1551 IRS5 exhibit interesting similarities (e.g., total mass, circular coplanar orbit), but also important differences (equal rather than different component masses, much larger pseudodisk), compared with L1551 NE. By comparing the two systems, we hope to gain insights on factors that give rise to their different physical properties. Infall from Circumbinary Disk to Circumstellar Disks: We have been awarded observing time on ALMA to study L1551 NE at a higher angular resolution and sensitivity. Our primary goal is to address how matter penetrates the inner clearing in the circumbinary disk to accrete onto the circumstellar disks of the two protostars. This observation also will provide a better separation between the spiral and inter-arm regions in the circumbinary disk, allowing us to refine and check for ingredients not yet implemented into our theoretical model for this system. For the same reasons, we anticipate making a follow-up study of L1551 IRS5 at a higher angular resolution and sensitivity using ALMA. Relative Accretion Rates onto Binary Protostars: We have been awarded observing time on the SMA to study the circumbinary environment of the binary protostellar systems IRAS 04239+2436 and IRAS304169+2702, and anticipate making follow-up studies of these systems using ALMA. Both these systems, like L1551 IRS5/NE, have total masses comparable with the Sun and orbital separations comparable with the most likely orbital separation of main-sequence binary solar-mass stars. We are planning to extend our work to even more binary protostellar systems having similar total masses and orbital separation. By intercomparing systems spread over a large range in mass ratios, we hope to gain insights on factors that affect relative accretion rates onto binary protostars. Circumstellar Disks and Ionized Jets: We plan to image the circumstellar disks and ionized jets of the binary protostars in both IRAS 04239+2436 and IRAS304169+2702 (as well as other systems we plan to select for study) using the JVLA, which currently provides the highest angular resolution for imaging dust emission from circumstellar disks. The orientation of the circumstellar disks with respect to each other as well as their circumbinary disk (if any) will provide an important test for their formation through the rotational fragmentation of a pseudodisk. Furthermore, the relatively sizes of the circumstellar disks provide a measure of the mass ratio of the binary protostars. The orientations of their ionized jets provide independent constraints on the geometry of the system, and a measure of the accretion rates onto both protostars. Orbital Parameters: From multi-epoch measurements of relative proper motions using the JVLA, we plan to determine whether the orbital motion of a given binary protostellar system is in the same direction as the rotational motion of its circumbinary disk, necessary if the system formed through the rotational fragmentation of a pseudodisk. Such measurements, together with the relative sizes of their circumstellar disks, also place constraints on the orbital separation (and hence total mass) and eccentricity of binary protostellar systems.

17305115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305115.value: 恆星是構成宇宙的基本單位。第一代恆星形成標誌著星系的誕生，其後恆星的形成方法也和星系的成長及演變息息相關。對於和太陽質量相若的恆星，它們形成後的殘留物多數能演變成行星。因此，天體物理學的眾多範疇：上至星系演變，下至行星系統的領域無一不受恆星形成研究的重大影響。早於大約三十年前，早期的望遠鏡（特別是干涉儀）已經廣泛應用在原恆星的觀察上。它們當時運作的波長大約是亳米般的長度。隨着更強力的天文望遠鏡建成，例如甚大天線陣（Jansky Very Large Array）和更強的ALMA 阿塔卡瑪大型毫米及次毫米波陣列（Atacama Large Millimeter and SubMillimeter Array），恆星觀察正進行革命性的演變。與此同時，更複雜的理論模型已經成熟發展，數值模擬的進行也令我們對恆星形成有更深了解，特別是物理過程對恆星形成的重要影響。 現時，我們對恆星形成的認知主要來自單一原恆星的形成，和它們對於周遭物的吸引或驅散效果。然而，大部份質量相若或大於太陽的恆星都以雙星系統的形式形成（也有少數可能形成擁有三顆恆星或以上的多個系統）。雙原恆星系統的觀察尤其困難，難度在於分辨兩顆星本身的物質和星體周遭的物質。要做到這一點，測量結果不單需要高角分辨度，也要高靈敏度。分子氣體的研究有助了解星體旁物質的運動和分佈，在以往的望遠鏡觀察中， 雙星系統周圍分子氣體的觀察已經是一個挑戰，更遑論是每一顆星附近的氣體研究了。現時在ALMA的協助下，該等研究已成常規。正因如此，我們第一次有機會跨越以往的限制，嚴格測試和改進雙星/多星系統的理論模型。 我們這份計劃書的主要目的在於清楚解釋一些擁有至少一個太陽質量恆星的雙星系統最初是怎樣形成和如何吸引附近的物質。我們結合雙原恆星系統的觀察所得和理論模擬的結果，期望能複製現時同類系統的特徵。這樣能幫助我們了解當中涉及的物理過程。計劃書的作者把雙原恆星系統觀察的專業技巧和它們的理論模型融為一體。我們的成果為雙太陽質量星體系統的形成帶來決定性的証據，特別是環繞距離比正常太陽質量主序星雙星系統為短的系統。我們透過存在於分子氣體的高密度中心的扁平旋轉結構（假盤）的分裂來得到結論。在其中一個系統中，我們展示雙原恆星所製造的重力轉力矩能在雙星周盤的內部產生清除效果。同樣效果也發生在雙星周盤的螺旋臂上，因為螺旋臂的內圍物質受該力矩影響而加快，並趨向外圍。另外在螺旋臂之間的範圍內，該力矩能吸收角動量而令物質向內推進。現階段我們正研究物質如何穿越雙星周盤的空間而吸附在每個原恆星的星周盤上。我們希望透過比對廣泛分佈（雙星之間）質量比例的雙原恆星系統，能協助我們找出兩顆原恆星增長速率的關係。在宏觀層面下我們希望解釋一個高密度的核心如何分裂出雙星系統的眾多組成部份。由此我們能解答另一個天體物理學的重要問題：恆星初始質量函數（恆星相對數量和它們質量的關係）的起源。

17305115.label: Realisation of objectives
17305115.value: 1. Internal Structure and Kinematics of Circumbinary Disks The results from our previous observation of the circumbinary disk of L1551 NE with ALMA were reported in Takakuwa et al. (2014); the results from our follow-up observations with ALMA are reported in Takakuwa et al. (2017). The follow-up observation clearly reveals two spiral arms in the circumbinary disk of this protostellar system. The southern arm clearly connects with the lower-mass protostellar component, whereas the northern arm is less conspicuous near both protostellar components. This observation also confirms and reveals in greater detail non-Keplerian motion in the circumbinary disk of L1551 NE. We were awarded observing time on ALMA to search for a circumbinary disk in the binary protostellar system L1551 IRS5. A draft reporting the results of this study is near completion, and attached to this report. In brief, we detected a circumbinary disk well separated from the twin circumstellar disks associated with the binary protostellar components. Like in L1551 NE, two spiral arms are detected in the circumbinary disk, each connected to one of the two binary protostellar components. We were awarded observing time on the SMA to study the circumbinary environment of the putative binary protostellar systems IRAS 04239+2436 and IRAS 04169+2702. Only the observation of IRAS 04169+2702, however, was executed. We do not confirm this object to be a binary system unlike that claimed by Connelley, Riepurth, & Tokunaga (2008) based on their infrared observations. The continuum emission from dust may be somewhat extended and have a different position angle than the synthesized beam, so we cannot immediately rule out the possibility that it is a tighter binary than originally claimed. 2. Infall from Circumbinary Disk to Circumstellar Disks We conducted theoretical simulations to better understand the observed properties of the circumbinary disk around L1551 NE. Our model shows the southern arm connects to the lower-mass component, whereas the northern arm connects to the higher-mass component although becoming inconspicuous near this component – in excellent agreement with the observations. The excellent correspondence between the model simulation and the observed structure as well as kinematics of circumbinary disk confirms that gravitational torques from the binary protostars drive non-Keplerian motion (i.e., infall) in the circumbinary disk so as to create the observed density enhancements seen as spiral arms. The results are reported in Takakuwa et al. (2017). We also conducted theoretical simulations to better understand the observed properties of the circumbinary disk around L1551 IRS5. By contrast with L1551 NE, material in the circumbinary disk of L1551 IRS5 is being driven outwards by gravitational torques from the binary protostellar system. In addition, the circumbinary disk of L1551 IRS5 is much warmer than that of L1551 NE. We link the outward motion and relatively high temperatures in the circumbinary disk of L1551 IRS5 to a recent FU-Ori event in this system. A draft reporting the results of this study is near completion and attached to this report. 3. Relative Accretion Rates onto Binary Protostars Tracing accretion and determining accretion rates onto the circumstellar disks of binary protostars is, currently, the holy grail in studies of binary protostellar systems. We have made a significant step forward in this direction by revealing spiral arms driven into the circumbinary disk of L1551 NE and L1551 IRS – the same gravitational torques must play a role in driving material onto the circumstellar disks. Actually revealing accretion onto the circumstellar disks remains elusive, and if possible will likely require observations at higher angular resolutions and sensitivities, as well as in different molecular tracers of density and temperature. 4. Circumstellar Disks and Ionized Jets We have imaged both circumstellar disks of the binary protostellar components in L1551 NE with the VLA. The larger circumstellar disk is found to be associated with the more massive protostellar component, in line with theoretical predictions for tidal truncation. We showed that the larger circumstellar disk cannot be fit by a single power-law profile, but requires a broken power-law profile – the first time that such a geometry has been demonstrated in the circumstellar disk of a binary protostar – as is anticipated owing to tidal truncation. The results are reported in Lim et al. (2016b). We also imaged both circumstellar disks of L1551 NE with ALMA; the primary objective of this work was to study the circumbinary disk of L1551 NE, as reported in Objective 1. We confirmed that the two circumstellar disks have different sizes, and appear to be rotating in the same direction as the circumbinary disk – further confirmation that the protostellar system formed through rotationally-driven fragmentation, evidence for which was first presented by Lim et al. (2016b). The results are reported in Takakuwa et al. (2017). We also imaged with ALMA the circumstellar disks of L1551 IRS5, confirming our earlier work that both disks have comparable sizes. The primary objective of this work was to study the circumbinary disk of L1551 IRS5, as reported in Objective 1. A draft reporting the results of this study is near completion, and attached to this report. 5. Orbital Parameters Our observation of L1551 NE with the VLA suggests that the two protostellar components are orbiting in the same direction as the circumbinary disk, as reported in Lim et al. (2016b). Our observation of L1551 NE with ALMA provides further evidence that the two protostellar components are indeed orbiting in the same direction as the circumbinary disk, as reported in Takakuwa et al. (2017). Observations over a much longer time baseline (decades) are required to derive the orbital parameters of this protostellar system. Our previous work on L1551 IRS5, with the VLA, suggests that the orbit of this protostellar system is either circular or has a low eccentricity (Lim et al. 2016a). Our observation of L1551 IRS5 with ALMA is consistent with a near-circular orbit, although the time baseline is not sufficiently long to refine its orbital parameters. References Connelley, M. 17305115.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305115.value: L1551 NE: Determined the geometry and size of the circumstellar disks associated with the binary protostellar components, finding that the larger disk is associated with the more massive protostellar component. Showed that both circumsellar disks are closely aligned. Demonstrated that the intensity profile of the larger circumstellar disk requires a broken power-law profile, consistent with theoretical predictions for tidal truncation of circumstellar disks in binary protostellar systems. Found preliminary evidence for orbital motion is in the same direction as the rotational motion of circumbinary disk. Physical properties of binary protostellar system consistent with formation through rotationally-driven fragmentation. Results reported in Lim et al. (2016). Clearly showed spiral arms in the circumbinary disk. Showed that one of the spiral arms is connected to one of the binary protostellar components, whereas the other spiral arms fades close to both binary protostellar components. Confirmed and revealed in greater detail non-Keplerian motion in the circumbinary disk. Conducted theoretical simulations to demonstrate that both spiral arms are driven by gravitational torques from the binary protostellar system, and that these torques drive infall through the circumbinary disk. Also found that the circumstellar disks are rotating in the same direction as the circumbinary disk, providing further evidence for rotationally-driven fragmentation. Results reported in Takakuwa et al. (2017). L1551 IRS5: Clearly revealed, for the first time, a circumbinary disk in this protostellar system. Also revealed, for the first time, two spiral arms in the circumbinary disk, each connected to one of the binary protostellar components. Found that, by contrast with L1551 NE, material being driven outwards through the circumbinary disk of L1551 IRS5 by gravitational torques from the binary protostellar system. Furthermore, by comparison with L1551 NE, the circumbinary disk of L1551 IRS5 is much warmer. Linked the physical properties of the circumbinary environment of L1551 IRS5 to a recent FU-Orionis event in this binary protostellar system. A draft of the paper is near completion, as attached in Part C. IRAS 04169+2702: Do not confirm this system as a binary system as previously reported.

17305115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305115.value: As mentioned in Section 5.3, tracing accretion and determining accretion rates onto the circumstellar disks of binary protostars is, currently, the holy grail in studies of binary protostellar systems. We have made a significant step forward in this direction by revealing spiral arms driven into the circumbinary disk of L1551 NE and L1551 IRS – the same gravitational torques must play a role in driving material onto the circumstellar disks. Actually revealing accretion onto the circumstellar disks remains elusive, and if possible will likely require observations at higher angular resolutions and sensitivities, as well as in different molecular tracers of density and temperature.

17305115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305115.value: This report concludes my research on how binary protostellar systems form, funded through two consecutive RGC/GRF awards. The work undertaken by my collaborators and myself has revealed, for the first time, the geometry and dynamics of circumstellar disks in binary protostellar systems, the geometrical and dynamical relationship between these circumstellar disks and the circumbinary disks surrounding the same protostellar systems, and the relationship between these disks and the orbits of the binary protostars. We have established, for the first time, that rotationally-driven fragmentation is one pathway through which binary protostellar systems form. Our work also establishes the presence of circumbinary disks around binary protostars during their formative phase, and the presence of spiral arms in these disks. Our theoretical simulations show that these spiral arms are driven by gravitational torques from the binary protostellar system, promoting both infall and outward motion of material through the circumstellar disk: the spiral arms form where faster-rotating outflowing material downstream collides with slower-rotating infalling material upstream. Some of the material inflowing through the circumbinary disk must eventually accrete onto the circumstellsr disks of the binary protostellar components - pointing the way towards sudying the nature of this accretion and measuring the accretion rates.

17305415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305415.value: 鉍化合物用於臨床治療各種疾病長達世紀。例如檸檬酸鉍和水楊酸鉍與抗生素一起治療幽門螺桿菌感染引起的消化性潰瘍。重要的是，迄今為止沒有幽門螺桿菌對鉍的抗藥性的報道。事實上，鉍藥物甚至能治療抗生素耐藥菌種的幽門桿菌的感染。因此，人們對鉍的其他醫療用途有越來越大的興趣。例如，鉍配合物對其他細菌和 沙士冠狀病毒 表現出良好的活性；放射性鉍 (212Bi 和 213Bi) 也有望成為有效的抗癌藥物。 大多數的抗生素的作用機制是通過對病原體的單一靶標。然而金屬藥物例如鉍、 鎵和銀金屬的抗菌劑作用是通過多靶點實施的。因此，細菌難以對所有這些靶點產生抗藥性突變，因為他們對細菌的生存或發病也是至關重要的。最近鎵化合物的抗菌活性受到人們的關注，硝酸鎵對囊性纖維化患者慢性感染銅綠假單胞菌 (Pa)的活性正在臨床第一階段測試。 由於耐藥細菌的迅速蔓延和快速對常用抗生素耐藥性的演化，發展替代抗生素的藥物，以對抗細菌感染，實在是迫在眉睫。重新利用金屬化合物來對抗耐藥細菌感染也許是一種有效的新方法。了解這些金屬藥物對細菌作用的機制將有助於設計更好的藥物。 我們初始的研究表明，鉍配合物對洋蔥伯克氏菌表現出極好的抑制作用，因此我們的目標是通過先進的新技術詳細的研究鉍配合物對非幽門螺桿菌的病原體抗菌活性，並以鉍為例理順金屬配合物的結構-活性關。具體而言，申請人打算: (1) 鉍配合物的合成，建立化合物數據庫; (2) 篩選對銅綠假單胞菌、 洋蔥伯克氏菌、 MRSA 和有關毒性強的細菌有活性的鉍配合物，並且用鎵化合物進行比較; (3) 通過整合金屬組學和金屬蛋白質組學的方法探討有活性金屬化合物抗菌機理; (4) 通過生物信息學分析金屬化合物的結合蛋白並通過生物測試驗證某些關鍵的蛋白質 (和酶); (5) 教育年輕一代、 培育創新技術。 此項研究將對金屬抗菌劑的作用機理提供重要資訊，因此將會提高我們對金屬配合物的抗菌，尤其是對那些耐藥菌的抑制作用的認識。這項研究的長期目標是建立一個藥用無機化學和無機化學生物學的平臺

17305415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305415.value: In this project, the PI and Co-I conducted a comprehensive study on antimicrobial activities of bismuth complexes towards Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Burkholderia cepacia, MRSA and relevant virulent bacteria by an integrative technique. As proposed, we have built up a bismuth complex bank and examined their activities against key pathogens, and used gallium(III) complexes for comparison. We found that bismuth(III) is distinct from gallium(III) although shares certain similarity. We found bismuth (Bi) agents kill Burkholderia cepacia complex (Bcc) and examined its molecular mechanism underlying their bactericidal activities. Bcc bacteria are important pathogens among immunocompromised patients suffering from the genetic disease cystic fibrosis, but current therapies that involve combinations of even two or three antibiotics can rarely eradicate the pathogen in chronically infected patients. We demonstrate that bismuth(III) agents can inhibit the growth of Bcc and could be a potential drug candidate for the treatment of cystic fibrosis infections. Surprisingly we discovered that bismuth-containing drugs can tame the superbugs (e.g. NDM-1 positive bacteria strains) and restore antibiotics activity, opening a new horizon for treatment of infectious disease by resistant pathogens (Nat Comm 2018 as well as a patent). Partially based on this work, a RIF project was awarded (with PL Ho and Richard YT Kao). We carefully investigated the mechanisms of action of bismuth antimicrobial agents by an integrative metalloproteomic approach (Chem. Sci 2017, 2018; Acc Chem Res. 2019). Based on protein-protein interaction network analysis, we validate certain key proteins (and enzymes) through bioassay. Our study will provide important information on the mechanism of action of metallo-antimicrobial agents, and therefore will improve our knowledge of the metal complexes against bacterial infection. We also establish a preliminary platform for medicinal inorganic chemistry. The PI was invited to write reviews and book chapters on our work and deliver plenary and keynote lectures in international conferences. A grant was awarded from Croucher foundation to promote metals in biology and medicine (i.e. “Advanced Study Institute (AI) on metals in biology and medicine- from molecular imaging to drug resistance” which will be held in Dec. 11-13, 2019 at the University of Hong Kong) Through this project, we have trained young scientists as revealed from the awards they received, and nurture innovative technology.

17305415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305415.value: 1. A patent entitled “Bismuth(III) compounds and methods thereof ” (US Patent: 10,201,518 B2) was awarded partially based on the data from this project. A RIF project was awarded (R7070-18) to continue the work to develop a new therapy for overcoming antimicrobial resistance. 2. An integrative metalloproteomic platform consisting of metalloproteomics, bioinformatics and structural biology, was established. We have extended to examine the mechanism of action of other metallo-antibacterial agents. 3. The PI and Co-I even develop a deep learning approach to analyze the relationship between mutations near metal-binding site of metalloproteins and certain diseases. The work was accepted by Nature Machine Intelligence. Introduction of deep learning and AI in bioinorganic chemistry will facilitate our understanding of metals in biology and medicine. An external grant will be sought to continue this area.

17305415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305415.value: Bismuth citrate has been commonly used for peptic ulcer and Helicobacter pylori infection. Importantly, no bismuth resistant H. pylori strain has been reported so far. In view of increasing cases of drug-resistant bacteria reported and rapid evolution of resistance for commonly used antibiotics, it is urgently needed to develop alternative strategies to fight against bacterial infection. In this project, the PI and Co-I conducted a comprehensive study on antimicrobial activities of bismuth complexes towards Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Burkholderia cepacia, MRSA and relevant virulent bacteria by an integrative technique. As proposed, we have built up a bismuth complex bank and examined their activities against key pathogens, and used gallium(III) complexes for comparison. We found that bismuth(III) shares certain similarity but definitely different. We then carefully investigated the mechanisms of action of bismuth antimicrobial agents by an integrative metalloproteomic approach. Based on protein-protein interaction network analysis, we validate certain key proteins (and enzymes) through bioassay. We have trained young scientists and nurture innovative technology. Our study will provide important information on the mechanism of action of metallo-antimicrobial agents, and therefore will improve our knowledge of the metal complexes against bacterial infection. We also establish a preliminary platform for medicinal inorganic chemistry.

17305515.label: Project Objectives

17305515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305515.value: Recently, topological quantum systems have intrigued significantly research interest both experimentally and theoretically. Various novel properties have been observed in these systems. In particular, the stability of Fermi surfaces and various impurity effects have been paid considerable attention. However, research on Fermi-surfaces of Majorana fermions and on topological quantum field theory of exotic semi-metals is still badly awaited as well as very challenging, even though it is fundamentally important. Inspired by this, in this project, we plan to conduct the following theoretical studies of (i) topological classification and stability of Fermi-surfaces of Majorana fermions; (ii) topological features in a nonlinear-sigma-model of disordered semi-metals and a unified quantum gauge field theory of the semi-metals; and (iii) exotic charge-impurity effects in topological superconductors. It is expected that the proposed research will make a timely and valuable contribution to the emerging field of topological quantum physics. 近來拓撲量子系統體的研究引起了相當的理論和實驗興趣。 但是，關於無能隙Majorana 模式的費米面和新奇的拓撲半金屬的理論研究具極大挑戰 。 鑒於此，本項計劃擬研究（1）無能隙Majorana 模式的費米面的拓撲屬性；（2）無序拓撲半金屬的特性和拓撲半金屬的量子場理論；（3）拓撲超導的雜質效應。 預期該項研究將對拓撲量子系統領域作出及時和有價值的貢獻。

17305515.label: Realisation of objectives
17305515.value: 1. We have established a theory for various Z2 classes of topological gapless bands with time-reversal and/or particle-hole symmetries. Six representative types of models have been proposed and constructed. Moreover, a new set of topological classes for gapless bands with the PT and CP symmetries has been classified for the first time. We have collaborated with an experimental group to realize and manipulate the PT and Weyl-type topological bands in artificial quantum systems, and thus to probe some novel topological properties. 2. We have studied topological features of Weyl-type points with disorders and developed a general response theory for them. In addition, we also proposed some experimental schemes to simulate the Weyl-type and Z2-type topological bands with cold atoms.

17305515.value: Topology has manifested itself in mathematics and physics. For the past decade, topological systems have intrigued significantly research interest both experimentally and theoretically. In this project, we have established a unified theory for various topological metals, which has a great impact on fundamental science and potential applications. Moreover, we have also done the relevant experiment to verify the theory for the first time. Our research results have been published in top/leading physics journals, and made timely and valuable contributions to the emerging field of topological quantum physics.

17305615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305615.value: Interest in studying bacterial glycoproteins has been steadily growing not only for fundamental research, but also for their potential in therapeutic applications. Pseudaminic acid (Pse) is a nine-carbon acidic monosaccharide. Pse and its derivatives are found as components of important surface glycans and glycoproteins in several pathogenic bacterial species including Pseudomonas, Campylobacter, Vibrio, Helicobacter, and Proteus. They are linked to proteins via Ser/Thr or via another glycan. The exact biological function of this glycan is not fully understood. The pseudaminic acid moiety has a complex and intriguing structure that resembles sialic acid, but has different stereo-chirality and functionality. Sialic acid in eukaryotes plays crucial roles in various cellular events during the lifecycle of many organisms, which suggests Pse may have important functions in bacteria. To probe the functions of this glycan and to study the proteins and enzymes that utilize this glycan, we will develop a strategy to chemically synthesize Pse and its derivatives, which have yet to be efficiently synthesized. In this project, we aim to develop a de novo synthesis of Pse starting with a threonine derivative. The next objective will follow on from the successful synthesis of Pse , which will be the total synthesis of P. aeruginosa 1244 pilin glycan. The pili of P. aeruginosa promote bacterial adherence and invasion to the host tissues and are considered to be a major virulence factor. The monomeric pili, pilin is a glycoprotein comprised of 148 amino acid residues containing a trisaccharide (alpha-5NβOHC4-7NFmPse-(2->4)-β-Xyl-(1->3)-β-FucNAc-β) at the C-terminal serine. It is noted that the P. aeruginosa strain 1244 pilin glycan is associated with twitching motility and biofilm formation. The exact role of how this glycan facilitates bacterial host interaction and the assembly of the functional pilin, remains to be explored. With the apparent synthetic challenges and the structural complexity of P. aeruginosa 1244 pilin glycan including the presence of Pse, and its β-linkage to xylose, the total synthesis has not yet been accomplished. In this project, we aim to develop an approach for the total synthesis of P. aeruginosa 1244 pilin glycan and its glycoconjugate. We will extensively investigate the selective glycosylation of Pse with xylose necessary for β-linkage. The success of this project will lay the groundwork for accessing other Pse-containing glycans and glycoconjugates, which will be used for addressing the explicit biological questions of the bacterial glycoprotein, and for developing new therapeutics. 由於細菌糖蛋白的重要生物學意義及其在藥物開發方面的潛在應用，相關研究日益受到重視。作為一種酸性九碳糖，Pseudaminic acid及其衍生物是眾多病原菌如綠膿桿菌、曲狀桿菌、弧菌、螺桿菌、變形桿菌等的表面多醣的重要組成單元。 Pse與絲氨酸/蘇氨酸的或其他多醣結構形成糖苷鍵，進而與蛋白質相連。 Pse多醣確切的生物學功能尚不清楚。 Pse的結構與唾液酸具有相似性，但含有不同的官能團和手性碳構型。類比唾液酸在真核生物生命週期的眾多重要細胞生物學過程中發揮的重要功能，Pse亦可能對細菌具有重要的生物學功能。開展對Pse多醣及與之相關的蛋白質或酶的功能研究，有賴於發展針對Pse及其衍生物的化學合成途徑。然而，截至目前Pse尚未能被有效的合成。在本項目中，我們將發展以蘇氨酸衍生物為起始原料的Pse從頭合成途徑。 在成功合成Pse的基礎上，我們將進一步開展對綠膿桿菌1244菌株鞭毛多醣的全合成研究。綠膿桿菌鞭毛具有促進該細菌與宿主組織的粘附和侵襲功能，並被視為主要的毒力因子。綠膿桿菌鞭毛構由鞭毛蛋白構成。鞭毛蛋白是一種具有148個氨基酸殘基的糖蛋白，結構為(α-5NβOHC47NFmPse-(2→4)-β-Xyl-(1→3)-β-FucNAc的三糖通過β糖苷鍵與蛋白C末端絲氨酸殘基連接。研究表明，綠膿桿菌1244菌株鞭毛多醣與其抽搐蠕動和生物被膜形成相關，而該多醣在細菌-宿主相互作用及功能鞭毛組裝中的確切作用尚待進一步闡明。由於該多醣高度複雜的結構（含有Pse單元及其與木糖單元的β糖苷鍵），其具有極高的挑戰性的化學合成至今尚未被實現。在本項目中，我們將系統研究Pse單元與木糖的β-選擇性糖苷化反應，並進而實現綠膿桿菌1244菌株鞭毛多醣及其糖綴合物的全合成。本項目的成功完成，將為Pse相關多醣及糖綴合物的獲得提供保證，並為後續的細菌糖蛋白生物功能研究和治療藥物開發奠定基礎。

17305615.label: Realisation of objectives
17305615.value: Re Objective 1: Develop a de novo synthesis of Pseudaminic acid (Pse). The easy access to this molecule would help address many fundamental questions of bacterial glycoproteins. We have successfully developed a facile and scalable de novo synthesis of Pse and its functionalized derivatives from easily available Cbz-L-allo-threonine methyl ester (16 steps in 11% yield). The key reactions in our de novo synthesis involve the diastereoselective glycine thioester isonitrile-based aldol-type reaction to create the 1,3-anti-diamino skeleton, followed by the Fukuyama reduction and the indium-mediated Barbier-typed allylation. These Pse and its analogues can now be readily synthesized in gram scale. Re Objective 2: Study the chemical glycosylation of Pse. The diastereoselective glycosylation involving Pse has been reported to be very difficult. We have developed an effective Pse glycosyl donor 5N3/5NTroc-Pse SAd thioglycoside, which is accessible from commercial available L -allo -threonine (400 USD for 100 g) in 16 steps in 8% yield. Three factors (SAd leaving group, 5N -azide, and MeCN participation) were synergistically optimized to maximize the β -preference. In addition, α -selective glycosylation with broad acceptor scope was realized through addition of DMF. Importantly, using the methodology developed herein, both α - and β -selectivity can be achieved using the same donor, which saves considerable synthetic effort and will therefore greatly simplify the construction of pseudaminylated oligosaccharide libraries and glycoconjugates. Furthermore, the 5N -Troc (or azide)/7N - Cbz Pse donor carries orthogonal protecting groups at 5N and 7N positions, which makes it possible to introduce different acyl groups, respectively. Re objective 3: Complete the total synthesis of P. aeruginosa 1244 pilin glycan-(alpha-5NβOHC4-7NFmPse-(2->4)-β-Xyl-(1->3)-β-FucNAc-β-Ser), which has not yet been reported. The presence of Pse and its β-linkage to xylose makes this synthesis very challenging. We fully investigated the glycosylation of Pse donors and identified the structural determinants for its glycosylation diastereoselectivity. Thus, we completed the first total synthesis of Pseudomonas aeruginosa 1244 pilin trisaccharide (α-5NβOHC47NFmPse-(2→4)-β-Xyl-(1→3)-FucNAc), which enabled us to confirm the configuration of the Pse-Xyl α-glycosidic linkage via HMBC analysis of the synthetic intermediates, as the original report determined it only based on the 1D 1H NMR with empirical rules due to the lack of sufficient amount of the glycan. Re Objective 4. Synthesize a glycopeptide containing alpha-5NβOHC4-7NFmPse-(2->4)-β-Xyl-(1->3)-β-FucNAc-β-Ser, which will lay the groundwork for synthesizing the full-length bacterial pilin glycoprotein (1-148). Based on our success on the synthesis of the trisaccharide (α-5NβOHC47NFmPse-(2→4)-β-Xyl-(1→3)-FucNAc), we further conjugate it to a synthetic peptide to form a glycopeptide. This will open up unexplored opportunities to study the biological function and significance of bacterial Pse glycosylation in pathogenesis and develop novel therapeutic intervention.

17305615.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305615.value: In 2017, we have developed a facile and scalable de novo synthesis of pseudaminic acid (16 steps in 11%). Furthermore, we developed a robust methodology for the “perfect” stereocontrolled chemical glycosidation of pseudaminic acid to afford both (only) α- and (only) β- glycosides. This was achieved through the use of a common glycosyl donor (5N-azide)/7NCbz Pse thioglycoside) through the simple modulation of the reaction conditions. The power of the methodology is highlighted through the stereocontrolled preparation of a large number of α- and β-pseudaminylated substrates encompassing a variety of biologically-relevant linkages. Examples of such bimodal selectivity, representing the ‘ideal’ situation, are both sparse and highly sought-after in carbohydrate chemistry, with most donors requiring implementation of directing groups or extensive optimization of protecting groups to achieve a single stereochemical outcome (i.e. different donors for different linkages). This bimodal selectivity is particularly advantageous for the study of pseudaminic acid, not only because it naturally occurs with both α and β linkage types, but also because at present it can only be derived through lengthy chemical synthesis, providing very little material to devote to standard donor optimization. To develop chemical biology tools to study Pse glycobiology, we developed the synthetic route to altrosamine derivatives, Alt-4NAz and Alt-2NAz as chemical reporters, which are chemically synthesized for the first time. Next, we discovered that Alt-4NAz could be successfully incorporated into the biosynthesis of Pse to display a modified LPS carrying an azido group on the surface of pathogenic Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii and Vibrio vulnificus.3

17305615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305615.value: Pseudaminic acid (Pse), first discovered in 1984, has been identified in a variety of pathogenic bacteria as important surface glycan, which has been associated with bacterial pathogenesis, infection and immune intervention. However, the biological and evolutional significances of bacterial pseudaminic acid and its glycoconjugates remain largely unexplored, due to the lack of synthetic access to pseudaminic acid and the structurally-defined pseudaminylated glycoconjuates. We have solved this problem by successfully developing a facile and scalable synthesis of Pse and its various glycoconjugates. This success will open up unexplored opportunities to study the biological function and significance of bacterial Pse glycosylation in pathogenesis and develop novel therapeutic intervention.

17305715.label: Project Objectives
17305715.value: To investigate physicochemical properties, in particular particle aggregation size and ion dissolution rate of zinc oxide nanoparticles (nZnO), with or without surface modification, in seawater under different environmentally realistic combinations of salinity and temperature. To examine acute toxicities of the two different types of nZnO to three model marine organisms, the diatom Thalassiosira pseudonana, copepod Tigriopus japonicus and mussel Perna viridis under the different combinations of salinity and temperature. Special attention will be paid on their interacting effects on the resultant toxicity of nZnO. The results will be essential to the regulation of the use and discharge of nZnO in tropical and subtropical coastal regions. To elucidate possible underlying molecular mechanisms of the nZnO toxicity to T. pseudonana, T. japonicus and P. viridis under different salinity and temperature regimes. The results of this part of the study and those from Objective 1 will provide scientifically sound explanations for the patterns revealed in Objective 2.

17305715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305715.value: Zinc oxide nanoparticles (nZnO) have been extensively used in sunscreen products, because they can effectively absorb both ultraviolet radiation A and B, and offer improved transparency and smoothness when being applied on human skins. Their global annual production is over 33,400 tonnes and nZnO now can be found in one third of commercially available sunscreens in the market. Maximum content of nZnO can be as much as 25% of the sunscreen. Given that most sunscreens will be washed off into the marine environment during their use on beachgoers, it is estimated that the global amount of nZnO being washed into the marine environment can be as high as 750 tonnes a year, and this amount is expected to rise further in the near future. Therefore, there is a great concern about the potential toxicity and safety of nZnO in the coastal marine environment. Up to now, ecological risks of nZnO on marine organisms and coastal ecosystems are still largely unknown, though our recent studies have showed that nZnO is toxic to marine organisms, especially marine diatoms and invertebrates, and its toxicity is strongly attributable to its ion dissolution and the generation of reactive oxygen species. In coastal waters, both temperature and salinity undergo daily (tidal-cycle), seasonally and yearly fluctuations. Both factors can jointly influence the physiology of marine plants and animals, and affect the physicochemical properties of nZnO and their toxicity to marine life. We have recently demonstrated that the ion dissolution rate of nZnO significantly increases with decreasing temperature, its aggregation size is only slightly influenced by temperature, and its toxicity towards marine diatom, amphipod and fish is temperature-dependent and species-specific. We have also discovered that the ion dissolution rate of nZnO generally increases with decreasing salinity whereas its aggregation size increases with salinity; such salinity-mediated changes in physicochemical properties of nZnO can significantly influence the nZnO toxicity to a marine diatom. Nonetheless, the combined effect of temperature and salinity on the physicochemical properties and toxicities to marine organisms remains unknown. This proposed study is, therefore, designed to experimentally investigate the interacting effects of temperature, salinity and concentration of nZnO on the physicochemical properties and resultant toxicity of nZnO to three selected marine organisms, and to establish sound theoretical explanations for the results through studying the underlying toxic mechanisms. The results will be useful to determine threshold effect concentrations for nZnO for the regulation of nZnO-based-sunscreens in tropical/sub-tropical regions. 温度和盐度对纳米氧化锌理化特性及海洋生物毒性效应的影响研究 纳米氧化锌颗粒因具有吸收紫外线（A、B），润肤等特性而被广泛应用于日常防晒用品。目前，全球防晒产品年产量超过33400吨。市面上三分之一的防晒霜中含有纳米氧化锌，且其含量比例最高可达25%。由于游客在海滩活动时对防晒用品的大量使用，导致大部分含有纳米氧化锌的防晒品最终进入海洋。据估计，全球每年进入海洋环境中的纳米氧化锌可高达750吨，并且该数值未来仍会进一步增加。因此，海岸带环境中的纳米氧化锌的潜在毒性及其安全性引发广泛关注。我们最近的研究发现，由于锌离子的释放及其诱导的活性氧的产生，纳米氧化锌可对海洋生物尤其海洋硅藻和无脊椎动物产生毒性效应。尽管如此，纳米氧化锌对海洋生物和海岸带生态系统的生态风险研究仍相当匮乏。 在海洋环境中，海水温度和盐度会经历潮汐、季节、年度等周期性变化。这些变化不仅会影响海洋动植物的生理机能，还会影响纳米氧化锌的理化特性及其对海洋生物的毒性。最近，我们的实验表明，纳米氧化锌的离子溶解率随温度的降低而显著增加，而其聚合体的大小仅受温度的轻微影响。纳米氧化锌对海洋硅藻、端足类动物和鱼类的毒性效应具有温度依赖性和物种特异性等特点。此外，纳米氧化锌的离子溶解率随盐度的降低而增加，其聚合体的大小随盐度的升高而增大；这种受盐度调节的纳米氧化锌理化特性的变化亦能够显著的影响其对海洋硅藻的毒性。然而，温度和盐度对纳米氧化锌理化特性及海洋生物联合毒性效应的影响仍然未知。因此，本研究拟对温度、盐度、纳米氧化锌浓度对其理化特性的交互影响，以及它们对三种典型海洋生物的毒性效应进行研究；并通过该研究来阐明纳米氧化锌对海洋生物的潜在毒理机制。本研究亦将推导出纳米氧化锌对海洋生物的阈值效应浓度，从而为热带、亚热带地区制定基于添加纳米氧化锌的防晒霜的风险管理提供理论依据。

17305715.label: Realisation of objectives
17305715.value: Objective 1: We investigated the physicochemical properties of uncoated ZnO-NPs (20 nm), two silane-coated ZnO-NPs, and bulk ZnO (i.e., micron-sized ZnO particles) in seawater with 25 combinations between five salinities (12/17/22/27/32 PSU) and five temperatures (10/15/20/25/30°C). The particles were characterized in terms of particle size, aggregation, dissolution, zeta potential and surface chemistry at concentrations ranging from 0.5-50 mg/L. We found that increasing temperature and salinity enhanced the aggregation of ZnO-NPs, but reduced the release of labile zinc ions from the particles. An increase in temperature from 10 to 30°C promoted aggregation of particles because the solution viscosity was less at higher temperature and the particles could overcome the energy barrier more easily and aggregate more at high temperatures. Zeta potential of ZnO-NPs was less at high temperatures such that the electrostatic repulsion force between particles became weaker, which would also enhance aggregation. An increase in salinity from 12-32 PSU would compress the electric double layers of particles; the attractive van der Waals force would dominate and promote aggregation. As the size of aggregates increased with increasing temperature and salinity, the dissolution of the particles decreased accordingly. ZnO has a negative enthalpy of dissolution, implying that dissolution of ZnO-NPs released heat. Higher temperature would reduce dissolution of ZnO-NPs. At higher salinity, zinc ions released from the particles can form complexes with the abundant anions (e.g., Cl- and SO42-) in the seawater which would reduce the concentration of labile Zn ions. In summary, coating materials could prevent aggregation and hinder dissolution of ZnO-NPs. Higher temperature and salinity could enhance aggregation but reduce release of labile zinc ions from nanoparticles in seawater. From the Fourier Transform-Infrared spectroscopy, the silane coating materials were covalently bonded to the surface of nanoparticles. Based on the microscopic images taken from Transmission Electron Microscope, there was no significant difference in particle size between uncoated ZnO-NPs and the two coated ZnO-NPs in dry powder forms, suggesting that the coating materials did not significantly increase the particle size of ZnO-NPs. However, the uncoated ZnO-NPs formed larger aggregates than D-ZnO-NPs, followed by A-ZnO-NPs in seawater. ZnO-NPs released more labile zinc ions than A-ZnO-NPs, followed by D-ZnO-NPs. The organic chains of the coating materials on the particle surface built steric hindrance between nanoparticles, decreased the surface energy of nanoparticles and prevented aggregation of the two coated ZnO-NPs. The coating materials also hindered the release of Zn2+ ions from the core particles. Objective 2: We examined the acute toxicities of coated and uncoated ZnO-NPs to the diatom T. pseudonana, copepod T. japonicus and mussel Xenostrobus securis under different combinations of salinity and temperature. It is important to note that we replaced the proposed mussel Perna viridis with X. securis as we were unable to collect enough P. viridis of the same size in the field for various experiments. Key results on the diatom and copepod are shown below while the data on the mussel are still under analysis. The results showed that an increase in temperature from 10°C to the optimum level (i.e., 25°C) and an increase in salinity from 12 to 32 PSU would enhance aggregation and reduce dissolution of ZnO-NPs and thus concomitantly reduce their toxicities. Toxicity of ZnO-NPs was sharply increased at 30°C because this is close to the upper thermal limit for T. pseudonana. For the copepod T. japonicus, the results of the surface response model showed that all test chemicals were most toxic at the highest test temperature and the lowest test salinity, where the copepods has the highest mortality. For all tested species, temperature has a dominant effect over salinity. For algal species, A-ZnO-NPs and uncoated ZnO-NPs were more toxic than D-ZnO-NPs. The sensitivities varied among algal species; for example, the two marine diatoms T. pseudonana and T. weissflogii were more sensitive to ZnO-NPs, A-ZnO-NPs and ZnSO4 than other microalgal species. Damaged cell surfaces and irregular cell outlines were also observed by Scanning Electron Microscope on the microalgae exposed to the test chemicals. Toxicity potencies of the chemicals to T. japonicus followed a similar trend as the algae. A species-specific difference could be found: A-ZnO-NPs and bulk ZnO were more toxic while uncoated ZnO-NPs and D-ZnO-NPs were less toxic (Fig. 2). Interestingly, the toxicity of all particles, except D-ZnO-NPs being significantly less toxic, become hardly differentiated in chronic Naupilus 21-day growth test using low and yet more environmentally relevant concentrations, probably due to the increased tendency of dissolution at low test concentrations. Furthermore, we also found that all NPs could attach onto the surface of feeding and swimming appendages of the copepods, while a significant concentration-dependent oxidative stress was also induced by the tested NPs. Objective 3: We elucidated the possible underlying molecular mechanisms of ZnO-NPs toxicity to T. pseudonana, T. japonicus and X. securis by quantitative real-time reverse transcription-PCR. Based on expressions of genes in T. pseudonana, exposure to ZnO-NPs at lower and higher temperature (10 and 30°C) and lower salinity (12 PSU) caused damage to frustules, inhibited photosynthesis and caused oxidative stress at earlier stage of exposure, when compared to the gene expressions at optimum temperature (25°C) and higher salinity (32 PSU). Differential expression of genes was related to availability of labile Zn2+, interactions between surfaces of particles and surfaces of algal cells, and changes that they caused in the physiology of T. pseudonana. Modification of surface of ZnO-NPs significantly influenced mechanisms of toxic action of ZnO-NPs to T. pseudonana. Down-regulations of sil1 and sil3 genes were observed when algal cells were exposed to uncoated ZnO-NPs and A-ZnO-NPs, indicating that they both impaired formation of silicon frustules in the diatom. Down-regulations of 3HfcpA and 3HfcpB genes were also observed in the diatom, indicating that ZnO-NPs and A-ZnO-NPs also lowered photosynthetic activities of the diatom. When the diatoms were exposed to D-ZnO-NPs, formation of frustules and photosynthetic activities were affected only after 96 h at high concentration (IC50). D-ZnO-NPs also released less reactive oxygen species (ROS) than uncoated ZnO-NPs and A-ZnO-NPs. For T. japonicus, the GST-s, GST-Mu5, mGST-1 and CAT genes were mainly responsible for the differentiation between ZnO-NPs and the two coated ZnO-NPs. Also, these chemicals can induce oxidative stress in T. japonicus through different pathways. Profiles of gene expression in the marine organisms suggested distinguishable toxic mechanisms between ZnO-NPs and Zn ions. When T. pseudonana was exposed to ZnO-NPs, down-regulation of sil1, sil3 and sit1 genes were observed, indicating that ZnO-NPs impaired formation of silica frustules and transport of silicon into diatoms. However, no significant regulations of the sil1, sil3 and sit1 genes were observed when the diatoms were exposed to ZnSO4, suggesting that Zn ions would have less effect on formation of silica frustules of diatom than ZnO-NPs did. Nonetheless, both ZnO-NPs and associated Zn ions induced oxidative stress in T. pseudonana, as indicated by the up-regulation of the SOD, cat and GPX genes. Comparably, a distinct profile of gene expression between ZnO-NPs and Zn ions was identified in T. japonicus. It was found that GST-D, GST-K1, GST-O, GST-T, GST-O1, mGST-3, MnSOD, GPx and GR genes were responsible in explaining the difference between the ZnO-NPs and Zn ions. Most of these genes were positively correlated with Zn ions.

17305715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305715.value: We published two articles in Scientific Reports (Part_C: #1-2 publications), including the results of studying the influence of temperature and salinity on physicochemical properties and toxicity of ZnO-NPs to the marine diatom Thalassiosira pseudonana and the report on physicochemical properties and toxicities of silane-coated and uncoated ZnO-NPs to several microalgae species. Additionally, we published a highly relevant research article to report the combine effect of copper and temperature on T. pseudonana (Part_C: #3 publication). We also published a review article in Environmental Science and Pollution Research discussing the current challenges, insights and future directions with regard to the regulations of engineered nanomaterials (Part_C: #4 publication). Manuscripts on the toxic effects and mechanisms of coated and uncoated ZnO-NPs towards the marine copepod Tigriopus japonicus and other species are under preparation (Part_C: #5-8). In summary, we found that uncoated ZnO-NPs generally formed larger aggregates, but they were more soluble than the two coated ZnO-NPs. Modification of surfaces of ZnO-NPs changed their toxic potencies to microalgae and copepods, with uncoated ZnO-NPs and A-ZnO-NPs being generally more toxic than D-ZnO-NPs. A-ZnO-NPs was more toxic than D-ZnO-NP and ZnO-NP. Our results indicated that ZnO-NPs coated with hydrophobic alkyl chains like D-ZnO-NP may be adopted as an active ingredient for blocking UV radiation in eco-friendly sunscreens. We investigated combined effects of temperature and salinity on toxicity of ZnO-NPs to T. pseudonana, T. japonicus and X. securis. Because ZnO-NPs formed larger aggregates and released less labile zinc ions at higher temperature and salinity, toxicity of ZnO-NPs to T. pseudonana was less at 25°C than at 10°C and less at 32 PSU than 12 PSU. However, the physiological response of the organisms would also be altered by temperature and salinity; hence their susceptibility to toxic effects from ZnO-NPs exposure would be changed. Toxicity of ZnO-NPs to T. pseudonana was significantly greater at 30°C which was near to its upper thermal limit. Likewise, ZnO-NPs was most toxic to T. japonicus at the highest test temperature (35°C) and lowest test salinity (12 PSU). Mechanisms of toxic action of the ZnO-NPs also depended on temperature and salinity. At lower and higher temperatures (10 and 30 °C) and lower salinity (12 PSU), ZnO-NPs caused damage to frustules, inhibited photosynthesis and caused oxidative stress of T. pseudonana at earlier stage of exposure. The data on the mussel Xenostrobus securis are currently under analysis.

17305715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305715.value: Given the evidence of significant influences of salinity and temperature on the physicochemical properties and toxicity of chemicals like ZnO-NPs, it is important to consider combined effects of multiple stressors, enabling accurate ecological risk assessments of chemical contaminants. This study did not include carbon dioxide and pH into consideration; the ocean acidification will be an important aspect for inclusion in further studies for revealing the climate change impact on chemical toxicity to primary producers and consumers. In addition, it is important to develop an early-warning system for predicting the toxicity and effect thresholds of chemicals under different combinations of multiple stressors so that regulators can better regulate the chemical use, and take measures in-time to prevent adverse outcomes. By using the response surface model, we can determine effect thresholds of the chemical under any regimes of temperature and salinity. This ecological realism of the model could be further improved by incorporating other factors like pH. Furthermore, our results showed that ZnO-NPs coated with hydrophobic alkyl chain would lessen their toxic effect to marine life. A systemic study could be conducted to identify the appropriate types of alkyl chains for coating ZnO-NPs with a view to developing environmentally friendly sunscreen products.

17305715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305715.value: Climate change is predicted to result in rising average temperature of seawater with more extreme thermal events and frequent rainfalls in some coastal regions. Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has predicted that there will be more extreme rainfall events and the average sea surface temperature will be likely increased by 2 °C by the end of this century under the projected greenhouse gas emission scenario. The results of the research project showed zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs) were more toxic at lower salinity and high temperatures. Populations of marine diatoms, copepods and mussels which support the marine food webs, might be severely affected by extreme scenarios under the influence of climate change. Moreover, our results also showed coating materials on the surface of ZnO-NPs would alter their physicochemical properties and toxic effects towards the marine organisms. ZnO-NPs coated with alkyl chain (e.g. D-ZnO-NPs) would alleviate the toxic effects of ZnO-NPs to the marine organisms because the hydrophobic coating can reduce the bioavailability of ZnO-NPs towards the organisms. The findings of the research project can provide useful insights into the development of eco-friendly sunscreens that use ZnO-NPs as an active ingredient for blocking ultraviolet radiation.

17305915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305915.value: As part of the increasing attention paid to improving efficiency and reducing waste in the field of organic chemistry, practitioners of organic synthesis have designed reaction sequences in which multiple molecular transformations are performed sequentially in what are known as tandem reaction. In such processes the product of one reaction is immediately used as the starting material for another, and this process can be repeated several times without isolation or purification of the intermediate products. Since these one-pot tandem reaction can greatly reduce the time, labor, energy, and other resources normally required for multi-step organic synthesis, the design and execution of longer and more complex examples of such reaction sequences is currently an active area of research. Recently we have studied the concept of using a by-product produced in an initial reaction as a catalyst for a subsequent transformation involving the first formed reaction product. For example, we have demonstrated that the triphenylphosphine oxide formed in a Wittig reaction conducted by mixing triphenylphoshphine, an alkyl halide, an aldehyde and an amine base together can catalyze the conjugate reduction or reductive aldol reactions of the initially formed alkene product. In such one-pot reaction sequences, several simple building blocks can be efficiently combined into larger, more structurally complex molecules by a series of 4 or 5 linked reactions. In the proposed research project we plan study the possibility of extending this concept of using a waste product productively as a catalyst in other phosphine- and phosphine oxide-initiated reaction sequences involving an initial Wittig-type or Appel reaction. 随着提高反应效率、减少化学废弃物在有机化学领域受到越来越多的关注，有机合成工作者们设计了在一个反应体系中多个分子转化逐步发生的反应过程，即我们所知的“串联反应”。在这类反应中，前一反应的产物作为底物参与下一步反应；并且，这种连续可以进行多步而不需要分离或纯化中间产物。由于这种一锅法串联反应可以大大减少时间、人力、物力，而其他方法通常需要多步合成，因此，设计实施更长、更复杂的串联反应目前称为有机合成的热门领域。 最近几年，本课题组一直致力于研究将前一步反应的产物及副产物分别作为下一步反应的底物及催化剂的设计。例如，我们已经证实了在Wittig反应（由三苯基磷、烷基卤化物、醛及胺参与）中产生的三苯基氧膦，可以催化上一步的烯烃产物发生共轭还原或Aldol还原反应。在这类一锅法串联反应中，几种简单的结构单元通过四、五步反应，即可高效地构建成分子量更大、结构更复杂的分子。在此提出的研究方案，我们计划研究延伸上述设计的可能性，即将起始反应为Wittig反应或Appel反应，其副产物作为催化剂应用于其他有机膦／磷氧化物催化的串联反应中。

17305915.label: Realisation of objectives
17305915.value: While all 5 objectives were addressed, success was only realized regarding Objectives 1, 2, and 5 (see Section 6.1 below). Regarding Objective 3, the intermediates in our proposed synthesis of yuzunone proved to be too difficult to isolate due to their highly volatile nature, something that was not anticipated. Alternative methods and routes to this compound proved fruitless. Similarly, attempts to combine Appel reactions with reductive alkylation reactions (Objective 4) were never successful even though this was attempted using a wide range of reaction conditions. Our observation is that it seems that a by-product of the first reaction seems to inhibit the second reaction, rendering our overall concept infeasible.

17305915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305915.value: The most successful aspects of this research project centered around Objectives 1, 2 and 5. Less success was found regarding Objectives 3 and 4. Research regarding Objective 1 resulted in a publication that determined the scope of the phosphine oxide-catalyzed conjugate reduction reaction of polyunsaturated ketones in which we reported very efficient syntheses of natural moth pheromones that could be used in conjunction with pesticides for insect control. Research regarding Objective 2 resulted in a publication in which we reported the use of electrophilic halogen sources in what were to our knowledge the first known examples of reductive halogenation reactions. This research led to the completely selective organocatalytic synthesis of halogenated ketones that could be used in the synthesis of heterocyclic compounds that are of interest in the field of medicinal chemistry. Research regarding Objective 5 is inspired the phosphine oxide catalysis research discussed in section 6.2 below that formed the basis of a submitted RGC GRF research proposal.

17305915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305915.value: The results of this research project inspired new ideas regarding phosphine oxide, P(V), catalysis that eliminates the need for P(III)/P(V) cycling, and thereby renders reactions more efficient by eliminating the need for a stoichiometric reductant. These new research concepts formed the basis for an RGC GRF proposal that was originally submitted in October 2018, and resubmitted in October 2019, that was focused on catalytic amide and amine synthesis. The reviews of the original 2018 submission were generally positive, so more preliminary results were added to the 2019 resubmission.

17305915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305915.value: This research project was directed towards developing new, more efficient ways of synthesizing organic molecules that could have applications in fields ranging from materials science to medicine. Traditional methods for making such compounds have generally been stepwise. Our research attempted to perform reactions in tandem so that the expensive (in terms of time, materials, and energy) process of compound purification could be minimized. Additionally, another benefit of the research was that we were able to synthesize classes of compounds that were not readily accessible prior to our work. Thus, overall it can be stated that our research was aimed at rendering organic synthesis more environmentally friendly and expanding the scope of compounds that can be synthesized.

17306315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17306315.value: Viscous liquids are often involved in industries, including manufacturing, printing and food processing. However, the processing of these liquids requires a large input of energy and sophisticated setups tailored to actuate them effectively. For instance, adhesives, which represent a crucial component in the processing of electronic circuit boards, often consist of two or more parts; upon mixing, the precursor liquids solidify to achieve the target adhesion between different parts. However, the mixing of the precursors with a large viscosity contrast is limited by diffusion, which tends to be slow. In various biomedical applications, the high water content of hydrogels makes these gels attractive candidates for incorporating cells and bioactive components; however, the high viscosity of hydrogel forming solution, and the possible clogging during its solidification at the nozzle, affects the quality of the final printed structures. To address these limitations, screw-based extrusion methods have been introduced, but these methods generate a large pressure drop and applied stress at the printing nozzles, both of which harm the suspended cells. An approach that enhances the printability of high-viscosity liquids is critically needed. Jets of viscous liquids are difficult to manipulate during dispensing, as observed in our daily experience of pouring honey or shampoo onto flat surfaces - the viscous fluids start to fold and coil. As the dispensing flow rate is increased, the frequency of the coiling often increases more rapidly than the diameter of the jets. While macroscopic folding has been extensively studied, further advances in technologies, such as micro-scaled electronics and 3D printing, require a fundamental understanding of viscous folding at the microscopic scale. Micro-scaled devices based on microfluidics are ideal platforms for investigating microscopic viscous folding. The versatility of the devices also facilitates the incorporation of external controls, such as electrical ones, offering alternative ways to manipulate the viscous liquid jets. The objectives of the proposed project are to (1) elucidate the physics of folding of viscous liquid jets at the microscopic scale, (2) develop an electrical-charging approach to manipulate the degree of folding, and (3) demonstrate how controlled folding can enhance the mixing of viscous liquids, fiber fabrication and printing. In the short term, the study provides a fundamental understanding of the dispensing of viscous liquids, and brings new approaches to manipulate them by electrical charging. In the long term, it will further contribute to the advancement of industrial operations that involve handling of viscous liquids and development of new printing technologies. 粘性流體在製造業、食品加工和工業打印等應用中十分常見，通常需要引入較大的剪切力或複雜的裝置步驟來驅動或有效地處理這些粘性流體。例如在集成電路板製造工藝中十分重要的粘合劑，是一種由兩部分組成的粘性流體，這兩部分流體接觸、混合、反應後固化，從而達到粘合的目的。然而，粘度很大的粘性流體的混合主要靠分子擴散，過程十分緩慢。又例如，在生物醫藥應用中可以用來包載細胞或活性物質的水凝膠前體也是粘度很高的流體，這些水凝膠前體在生物打印過程中很容易堵塞打印噴口，從而影響打印得到的結構。現有的方法如螺旋擠壓法，其在噴口附近產生的壓降巨大，對前體流體的切力也很大，對懸浮細胞的損害很大。因此十分需要能提高高粘度流體的操作性的打印方法。高粘度流體的複雜流變性質很顯著。在日常生活中，當我們傾到高粘度流體，如蜂蜜或洗髮香波時，它們會形成捲繩結構。當流量變大時，卷繩效應的頻率也會大大增加。粘性流體的捲繩效應在微電子製造業和微米級的3D打印技術等先進製造技術中有應用前景，因此需要開展對微尺度流體的捲繩效應的研究。微流體裝置是研究這些現象的理想平台，能夠方便地引入電場力等物理外力，提供多種手段來加強對粘度流體的控制。本項目的目標有如下三點：（1）闡釋微尺度下粘性流體的捲繩效應機理；（2）開發電控流體技術來控製卷繩效應；（3）證明促進粘性流體的捲繩效應可以促進其混合，還可以用來製造微纖維和微觀打印結構。短期來說，本項目闡明控制粘性流體的基礎機理，並提出電控的新方法來控制粘性流體。長期來說，本項目的研究成果將為粘性流體的有關先進製造技術和新型打印技術做出貢獻。

17306315.label: Realisation of objectives
17306315.value: The objectives have been achieved: 1. We have investigated the dynamics of viscous liquid jets under different conditions, such with different viscosities, external environments, and under different fields. We have interpreted the behaviors into different dimensionless numbers, such as electro-capillary number and aspect ratios. We have also simulated the behaviors computationally for different jet configurations. 2. We have characterized liquid jets of different geometries and from different nozzles when the jets are in electric field. Our understanding has enabled new ways to design printed patterns of jets with different geometries from electrically printed jets. Our approach has been shown to have great potential to be used for biomedical applications, such as for printing porous scaffolds for bioengineering with a controllable degree of porosity. 3. We have introduced and demonstrated an approach based on electrocoiling to print multiscale architectures. By spatially programming the voltage applied onto the viscous ink, we show that different filament structures can be printed, and the switching between the structures can be achieved at single wavelength resolution. In addition, we also show that our approach enables printing of centimeter-sized architectures from nanofibers with micron-sized curled structures within a few minutes. The work has shown great promise for custom-design of fiber architectures with unique features, for instance, with spatially varying mechanical properties.
