17306315.label: Major findings and research outcome
17306315.value: - Understand how the dynamics of electrically manipulated liquid jets relate to typical parameters for printing - Introduce new approaches to print filament patterns of different precursors and structures, with proof-of-concept understanding for achieving multiscaled and hierarchical materials - Demonstrate and widen the unit printing structures from drops and jets to curled jets controlled by electro-coiling - Integrate the advantages of electro-coiling and of conventional printing to filaments that are formed from liquid precursors Most of the results have been presented in various international conferences (e.g. 16th International Conference on biomedical Engineering 2016, ChinaNano 2017, Colloids and Interface Symposium 2018, ChinaNano 2019, APS Division of Fluid Dynamics etc.) and published in respected international journals (e.g. Physical Review Applied, Lab on a Chip, Physical Review Letters, etc.), as shown in Part C. While some papers have been submitted and are being reviewed, other results are being integrated with other applications and wrapped up for publication due to their potential for a greater impact.

17306315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17306315.value: By introducing electrically controlled printing, we have demonstrated that curled filaments can be achieved by varying the charging voltage. Printing with curled filamental units is beneficial to microscaled pattern printing, since fabrication of hierarchical structures requires versatile stacking of different printed patterns. Therefore, the works will facilitate any applications that use nanoscaled filaments, not limited to printed electronics and tissue engineering scaffolds. The ideas and tools may also benefit the development of new three-dimensional printing approaches. The proposed course of action includes publishing the remaining works, while discussing the attracting aspects with potential academic and/or industrial collaborators who may need to print multiscaled hierarchical consisting of curled patterns. We also propose to explore the development of our lab-scale models into industrially manufacturable printers through collaborations with large companies or startups, facilitated by research grants, such as the Innovation and Technology Fund (ITF), and other funds that connect the industries and academia in Hong Kong, Shenzhen and Guangdong province. Some of the discussions and developmental plans have already started, with great interest from both scientific and industrial collaborators. Some of the project outcomes achieved are also benefiting other research projects indirectly.

17306315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17306315.value: Printing is an integral technology underlying many modern engineering applications, ranging from printed electronics to complex tissue engineering scaffolds. A challenge in printing is the speed, which is particularly compromised when highly curled filaments are involved. Curled filaments are often printed by adopting a curled printing path, which inevitably involves turns and corners that require deceleration of the printing nozzle. That partly explains why it is less efficient and practical to print structures with large amounts of curls. However, curled filaments are sometimes needed to enhance mechanical properties of the printed materials or to mimic biological structures. In this project, we characterized the dynamics of electro-coiling-based printing under different conditions. We also investigated the effects of electrical control over liquid jets under conditions that are needed to develop coiling-based printing, thus testing the applicability and limitations of the electro-coiling-based printing. We also demonstrated the integration of electro-coiling-based printing nozzles and a printer to print large architectures from nanofibers with micron-sized curled structures. These results will provide the foundation and tools for evaluating the feasibility of an electro-coiling-based printer, and inspire new applications of multiscaled hierarchical structures. The results also suggest possibility for its scale-up for industrial applications.

17500015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500015.value: 科技創新一直被認為是企業競爭優勢的關鍵因素. 在科技快速進步的年代裡, 企業面臨激烈的創新競爭. 一旦決策出現錯誤以及科技優勢被替代, 今日的贏家可能轉眼就變為輸家. 本計畫目的在研究科技競爭與替代在股票報酬中的角色以及相關的風險. 科技替代對於企業有兩種角色: 首先, 新科技取代舊科技使得所有企業整體來說可以取得更高的生產力. 然而, 對個別企業來說, 有些企業會面臨危機因為舊科技被取代與競爭優勢被削弱. 另外有些企業, 尤其是新創企業, 可以使用新科技去佔領市場與淘汰無效率的舊企業. 我計畫先建立一個模型來敘述科技競爭與替代在企業生產函數, 投資決策, 與股票報酬中的角色. 這個模型可以延伸出可實證檢驗的一般性假說與條件性假說. 首先, 我計畫採取單方向資產組合與迴歸檢定的方法來檢驗一般性假說. 接續, 我計畫採取雙方向資產組合與子樣本迴歸檢定的方法來檢驗條件性假說. 在我初步檢測中, 我以各產業中引用的專利的年份分布比率來衡量一個產業的科技替代速度. 如果一個產業引用的專利多屬最近幾年內, 則此一產業屬於替代性快速產業. 也就是說, 在此一產業中的企業被替代的風險相對高. 我使用所有美國上市公司於 1981 至 2010 年間為樣本, 發現在替代性快速產業中的企業所提供的股票報酬相對高. 我的初步結果值得深入繼續研究相關的風險因子.

17500015.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500015.value: 1. We propose that innovative originality/replacement is a valuable organizational resource and that owing to limited investor attention and skepticism of complexity, greater innovative originality may be undervalued. We develop models to predict that ﬁrms’ innovative originality strongly predicts higher, more persistent, and less volatile proﬁtability and higher abnormal stock returns, ﬁndings that are robust to extensive controls. The return predictive power of innovative originality is stronger for ﬁrms with higher valuation uncertainty, lower investor attention, and greater sensitivity of future proﬁtability to innovative originality. This evidence suggests that innovative originality/replacement acts as a “competitive moat” and is undervalued by the market. 2. We compare innovation strategies of public and private ﬁrms based on a large sample over the period 1997–2008. We ﬁnd that public ﬁrms’ patents rely more on existing knowledge, are more exploitative, and are less likely in new technology classes, while private ﬁrms’ patents are broader in scope and more exploratory. We investigate whether these strategies are due to differences in ﬁrm information environments, CEO risk preferences, ﬁrm life cycles, corporate acquisition policies, or investment horizons between these two groups of ﬁrms. Our evidence suggests that the shorter investment horizon associated with public equity markets is a key explanatory factor. 3. Motivated by a theoretical model, we examine for 43 countries whether it is policy or policy uncertainty that affects technology replacement. Innovation activities, measured by patent-based proxies, are not, on average, affected by which policy is in place. Innovation activities, however, drop signiﬁcantly during times of policy uncertainty measured by national elections. The drop is greater for more inﬂuential innovations (citations in the right tail, exploratory rather than exploitative innovations) and for innovation-intensive industries. We use close presidential elections and ethnic fractionalization to address endogeneity concerns. We uncover the mechanism underlying the main result by showing that the number of patenting inventors decreases with policy uncertainty. Political compromise, we conclude, encourages innovation.

17500015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500015.value: 1. Our finding that innovative originality/replacement leads to higher subsequent stock returns, which is consistent with the predictions from a model of limited attention. Nevertheless, we do not rule out risk-based explanations including obsolescence risk, systematic risk due to technology frontier, and financial constraint risk. 2. Although public ﬁrms have more patents, their patents rely more on existing knowledge and are less exploratory. Our ﬁnding provides new insights into the real consequences of becoming a publicly listed ﬁrm, considering that an exploratory innovation strategy is important for ﬁrms to survive and thrive through technological innovation waves in the long run. Our analysis also suggests the importance of future research on optimal innovation strategies. 3. Although a growing literature has examined various empirical links between innovation and ﬁrm- or market-speciﬁc characteristics, rigorous empirical studies that explore how politics affects innovation activities are sparse. Our study contributes to the growing literature on the negative effect of policy uncertainty on the ﬁrm’s real investment decisions and to the burgeoning literature on the negative effect of policy uncertainty on stock prices. More analyses are called for more understanding of the determinants of technology replacement.

17500015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500015.value: 1. Motivated by a popular view of innovation as recombinant search, we measure innovative originality/replacement by the breadth of knowledge used to innovate. Under this view, innovation comes from combining technological components in novel manners or reconﬁguring existing combinations. Innovative originality can be a useful input for ﬁrm valuation. 2. We ﬁnd that public ﬁrms’ patents are more exploitative (i.e., mainly making use of existing knowledge) and less exploratory (i.e., in pursuit of new knowledge) than private ﬁrms’ patents. We also show that public ﬁrms’ patents tend to be narrower in scope but greater in depth in terms of the knowledge domain, and that public ﬁrms produce fewer patents in technology classes previously unknown to these ﬁrms. Private ownership leads to an innovation strategy that emphasizes exploration and scope. 3. We ﬁnd that policy, on average, does not affect a country’s innovation activities. Policy uncertainty, however, adversely affects a country’s innovation quantity, quality, and originality. In particular, the drop is greater for more inﬂuential innovations (home-run projects and breakthrough), and is greater for innovation-intensive industries.

17500515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500515.value: Ordinary investors face pervasive uncertainty in the real world, and have to make optimal consumption-investment decisions in an environment in which they are uncertain about the model structure or time-varying model parameters (e.g., the expected growth rate of earnings or the equity return). It is therefore important for us to understand how rational investors make optimal financial decisions when faced with various types of risks and uncertainty. In this project, we plan to construct a tractable continuous-time general equilibrium asset pricing framework to explore how the interactions of model uncertainty due to robustness and parameter (state) uncertainty due to imperfect observations affect equilibrium portfolio choice and asset returns (the risk-free rate and the equity premium). Model uncertainty and parameter/state uncertainty arise from two major types of incomplete information: (i) incomplete information about the distribution of the state evolution equation and (ii) incomplete information about the true value of the time-varying parameter that is part of the state vector. Hansen and Sargent (1995, 2007) first introduced robustness-induced model uncertainty into economic models, and argued that it provides a new insight about agents' optimal consumption-investment decisions and the joint dynamics of financial markets and the macroeconomy. Specifically, uncertainty averse agents are concerned that their model may be misspecified; consequently, to minimize their utility they choose their decisions as if the subjective distribution over shocks had been chosen by an evil agent. As shown in Cao et al. (2005), Maenhout (2004, 2006), and Hansen and Sargent (2007), this uncertainty aversion leads to limited stock market participation and in turn, a high equity premium. In contrast, Detemple (1986), Gennotte (1986), Feldman (1989), Lundtofte (2008), Wang (2009), and Yan (2009) examined how parameter uncertainty (incomplete information about the growth rate of the dividend process) affects portfolio choice and/or asset prices. The proposed project will examine how the two types of uncertainty interact, and determine the equilibrium portfolio rules and asset returns in a continuous-time recursive utility model. After solving the model explicitly, we will explore the relative importance of each type of uncertainty, as well as risk aversion and intertemporal substitution, in determining the equilibrium equity premium. 17500515.label: Realisation of objectives
17500515.value: All of the objectives proposed for this project are realized. The project has generated two papers. The major paper is entitled "Robustly Strategic Consumption-Portfolio Rules with Informational Frictions" is now published in Management Science (2017). The other paper generated from this project, entitled "Ambiguity, Low Risk-Free Rates, and Consumption Inequality", closely related to the major paper and is now under the third round review at Economic Journal. In this project, we provided a tractable continuous-time constant absolute risk aversion (CARA)-Gaussian framework to explore both the normative and positive implications of parameter and model uncertainty for strategic consumption-portfolio rules in the presence of uninsurable labor income. After solving the model explicitly, we have explored how induced uncertainty due to different types of ignorance, parameter and model uncertainty, have distinct impacts on strategic asset allocation and precautionary savings. Furthermore, for plausibly estimated and calibrated model parameters, we quantitatively analyzed how the interactions of parameter and model uncertainty affect the optimal share invested in the risky asset. Finally, we showed that the welfare cost of incomplete information under model uncertainty is non-trivial and that the welfare cost is more sensitive to the change in the degree of model uncertainty than to the change in the degree of parameter uncertainty.

17500515.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500515.value: In the paper entitled "Robustly Strategic Consumption-Portfolio Rules with Informational Frictions", we provide a tractable continuous-time constant-absolute-risk averse (CARA)-Gaussian framework to explore how the interactions of fundamental uncertainty, model uncertainty due to a preference for robustness (RB), and state uncertainty due to information-processing constraints (rational inattention or RI) affect strategic consumption-portfolio rules and precautionary savings in the presence of uninsurable labor income. Specifically, after solving the model explicitly, I compute and compare the elasticities of strategic asset allocation and precautionary savings to risk aversion, robustness, and inattention. Furthermore, for plausibly estimated and calibrated model parameters, I quantitatively analyze how the interactions ofmodel uncertainty and state uncertainty affect the optimal share invested in the risky asset,and show that they can provide a potential explanation for the observed stockholding behavior of households with different education and income levels. This paper is published at Management Science. In the related paper, "Ambiguity, Low Risk-Free Rates, and Consumption Inequality", we argued that the failure of macroeconomists to predict the Great Recession suggests possible misspecification of existing macroeconomic models. If agents bear in mind this misspecification, how are their optimal decisions changed and how large are the associated welfare costs? To shed light on these questions, we develop a tractable continuous-time recursive utility (RU) version of the Huggett (1993) model to study the effects of model uncertainty due to a preference for robustness (RB, or ambiguity aversion). We show that RB reduces the equilibrium interest rate and the relative dispersion of consumption to income, making them closer to the data, but our bench-mark model cannot match the observed relative dispersion. An extension to a RU-RB model with a risky asset is successful at matching this dimension. Our analysis implies the welfare costs of model uncertainty are sizable: a typical consumer in equilibrium would be willing tosacrifice about 15 percent of his initial wealth to remove the model uncertainty he faces. This paper is currently under the third round review at Economic Journal. In another related paper, Portfolio Choice with Information-Processing Limits, we examine the joint consumption-portfolio decision of an agent with limited information-processing capacity (rational inattention or RI) in the sense of Sims (2003) withina non-linear-quadratic (non-LQ) setting. Our model predicts that, as processing capacity falls,agents choose to hold less of their savings in the form of risky assets on average; however, theystill choose to hold substantial risky assets with some positive probability. Low capacity causes households to act as if they are more risk averse and more willing to substitute consumption intertemporally. This paper is now accepted in Annals of Economics and Finance.

17500515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500515.value: This paper examines the importance of model and state uncertainty due to preferences for robustness and limited capacity respectively in explaining the observed joint behavior of consumption, income, and asset returns in general equilibrium. In the future, it is promising to apply this idea in other important macroeconomic settings: How does the interaction of these types of induced uncertainty affect the optimal investment behavior of firms? Once we can successfully incorporate this information friction into the optimal investment setting, we can address some very important issues in macroeconomics. For example, how robustness affects optimal investment decision and the investment volatility in an otherwise standard Abel-Eberly investment model with uncertainty,and what is the key differences between the traditional adjustment costs hypothesisand the informational friction hypothesis?

17500515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500515.value: Ordinary investors face pervasive uncertainty in the real world, and have to make optimal consumption-investment decisions in an environment in which they are uncertain about the model structure or time-varying model parameters. It is therefore important for us to understand how rational investors make optimal financial decisions when faced with various types of risks and uncertainty. In this project, we plan to construct a tractable continuous-time general equilibrium asset pricing framework to explore how the interactions of model uncertainty due to robustness and state uncertainty due to imperfect observations affect equilibrium portfolio choice and asset returns. Hansen and Sargent (2007) first introduced robustness-induced model uncertainty into economic models, and argued that it provides a new insight about agents' optimal consumption-investment decisions and the joint dynamics of financial markets and the macroeconomy. The proposed project will examine how the two types of uncertainty interact, and determine the equilibrium portfolio rules and asset returns in a continuous-time recursive utility model. Using the U.S. asset market and macroeconomic data, we plan to adopt the detection error probability method and Sims' rational inattention hypothesis to calibrate the empirically plausible amounts of model uncertainty and parameter uncertainty, respectively.

17500615.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500615.value: 員工情緒和提出意見：長遠及雙向關係的研究

17500615.label: Project Objectives
17500615.value: To test a theoretical model that integrates employee emotion research with employee voice research for the first time. The two research streams have been developing separately. To examine multiple positive and negative discrete emotions as predictors of multiple types of voice. Much voice research focuses on either positive or negative organizational experiences as predictors of voice. To examine the impacts of voice on social resources (organizational and supervisor support) and how they in turn affect employee emotions. In so doing, I can identify the reciprocal effects of voice on employee emotions. To investigate how changes in discrete emotions are related to changes in different types of voice (and in social resources) over time. This objective is important because both emotions and voice are likely to fluctuate over time.

17500615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500615.value: 研究人員正在越來越多地關注員工提出建議的行為。這些行為幫助公司識別現有操作問題並促進創新的理念的產生，間接幫助公司的業務提升到一個新的水平。這個研究的目的是為了測試一個新的理論模型，這理論模型可以填補研究文獻中四個重要空白。 首先，員工提出建議的行為研究和員工情緒的研究尚未融合。這兩個領域需要整合，因為員工會否想提出建議，以及他們建議的內容可能在很大程度上取決於員工的情緒。例如，當員工表示“我很滿意，所以我提出建議了”和“我很生氣，所以我提出建議”是兩個非常不同的情景性質。這個空白導致我希望研究員工的情緒對提出建議的行為的影響。 第二，許多研究迄今為止集中在某一種的提出建議的行為。然而，在工作場所，員工很可能會體驗到很多令他們感覺良好和感覺沮喪的事情，而他們提出建議的行為也可能採取多種不同的形式。因此，當研究員工的提出建議的行為時, 研究人員應該採用一個完整的評估, 這個評估需要考慮到正面和負面的情緒和各種不同的提出建議的行為。這個空白導致我希望研究積極和消極情緒對各種提出建議的行為的影響。 第三，很少研究考慮到員工情緒以及提出建議的行為的相互影響。提出建議的行為是相當獨特的，因為它把大家的注意力都引到發言人身上（大部份其它幫助公司的行為，都可以在無人注意的情況下進行）。因此，我有理由相信從事提出建議的行為的員工將無可避免地感受到別人的認同或制裁，而反過來影響員工的情緒。這個空白導致我希望研究提出建議的行為是如何影響發言人所得的資源（例如公司或上司的支持），進而產生積極和消極的情緒。 最後，這方面的研究主要集中於某個時間發生的提出建議的行為。然而，研究人員亦觀察到員工的情緒經歷很可能隨時間而改變。因此，提出建議的行為的強度和內容，亦會隨時間而逐漸改變的。因此，對於研究人員，研究動態(而非靜態的)提出建議的行為, 和員工動態情緒的關係是重要的。這個空白導致我希望探討員工的情緒, 提出建議的行為, 和社會資源的相互影響，是怎樣隨著時間而變化的。 總言而之，填補上述四個空白將幫助研究人員更了解員工的情緒和提出建議的行為之間的關係，和不同的情緒怎樣推動不同類型的提出建議的行為。這項研究也有實踐意義。鼓勵員工提出建議被認為是一個重要的推動生產力的方法。然而，如果沒有先了解不同類型的提出建議的行為的情緒根源，公司可能無法實現他們推動生產力的收益。此外，公司亦很少考慮員工的提出建議的行為的後果。這項研究是要表明，提出建議的行為也可能會最終影響員工的情緒，而造成一個良性或惡性的遁環。因此，深入地了解員工情緒和提出建議的行為之間的密切和相互關係是很重要的。長遠來看更可能是培養一個積極有效的公司文化的關鍵。

17500615.label: Realisation of objectives
17500615.value: I collected two longitudinal samples over the course of the study period. The first dataset served to test the study hypotheses, such as the relationships between specific emotions and types of voice. However, some of the relationships turned out to be not significant, undermining the publication value of this study. Fortunately, I collected several extra variables that addressed my other research interests and was able to create a manuscript about ethical leadership that I believed to be publishable. A majority part of this manuscript still addressed the relationship between emotions and voice. In brief, although the original goals were not completely attained because of the lack of significant results, I modified the research questions to focus on the effects of changes in ethical leadership on employees’ changes in positive and negative emotions (e.g., pride and contempt), changes in voice, and turnover. I also collected a second dataset that focused on two specific types of negative emotions (envy and being envied) and related these emotional experiences with employees’ perceptions of their idiosyncratic employment arrangements, social experiences of being ostracized, and turnover. Although this project did not directly address the relationship between emotions and voice per se, it showed that the negative emotions of envy and being envied had other negative consequences in the workplace, including being socially excluded that eventually led to organizational exits. Taken together these two manuscripts that were generated directly from this grant, this study was able to show to researchers the unexplored effects of changing positive and negative emotions in the workplace.

17500615.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500615.value: Findings related to the original propositions were mixed. While there were significant relationships between emotions and voice, there was limited support for other hypothesized relationships, such as the moderating effects of support perceptions. However, as noted above, I did observe that changes in ethical leadership generated changes in positive and negative emotions that in turn led to positive and negative voice. These findings were consistent with my original conjecture about the effects of emotions on employees' tendency to speak out.

17500615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500615.value: This study was the first to examine the relationships between discrete emotions and voice from a dynamic, non-static perspective. It generated many research avenues for future research, such as identifying the impacts of discrete emotions on both positive and negative job behavior, exploring the affective predictors of different types of voice instead of personal, contextual, and social antecedents, and probing how these relationships changed and how these changes were related to such variables as leadership and turnover. As this study has found limited support for the proposed moderating roles of support perceptions, future research should also consider the other theoretical roles (e.g., antecedents, outcomes) played by these perceptions in the proposed framework.

17500615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500615.value: This study shows that: 1. Employees' level of voice fluctuates over time; 2. These changes are associated with their emotional changes; 3. Those who experience increases in their positive emotions are increasingly likely to display positive voice (e.g., making constructive suggestions); 4. Those who experience increases in their negative emotions are increasingly likely to display negative voice (e.g., making criticisms of the organization); 5. Leadership (e.g., ethical leadership) draws changes in positive and negative emotions; 6. Changes in positive and negative emotions affect turnover likelihood; 7. Support perceptions have limited moderating roles in the proposed emotion-voice relationship.

17500715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500715.value: The current project investigates how reminders of one’s own death can influence individuals’ helping behavior. We propose that to effectively implement charitable appeals there needs to be a better understanding of the motivational mechanisms for helping under mortality salience. By conducting various laboratory and field studies, we aim to increase the theoretical understanding of motivations that underlie helping under mortality salience and ultimately provide meaningful practical implications to relevant non-governmental organizations. Prior research has proposed two main mechanisms for helping behavior under mortality salience. One account suggests that under mortality salience individuals attempt to enhance their feelings of self-worth – the self-worth enhancement account. The other account suggests that under mortality salience individuals seek to defend their cultural worldviews by upholding cultural standards and norms – the cultural standards reinforcement account. Prior work on mortality salience has either tested these two accounts independently or treated them as equivalent, implicitly assuming they always converge and lead to the same outcome. However, in our proposed study of prosocial behavior under mortality salience, we will attempt to formally disentangle the two accounts. We predict that under mortality salience individuals’ helping behavior will be mainly guided by the motivation to enhance their self-worth, unless prosocial cultural norms are made explicitly salient. That is, we propose that the self-worth account is the default account, and the cultural standards account operates under certain circumstances. We propose that individuals will engage in helping behavior to cope with mortality salience by supporting cultural norms and standards only when cultural norms related to prosocial behavior become explicitly salient via contextual factors. We plan to tease apart the two motivational accounts to explain helping under mortality salience by comparing the effectiveness of three types of charitable appeals: those highlighting intrinsic benefits to helpers, extrinsic benefits to helpers, and benefits to recipients. We propose that if the self-worth account guides individuals’ helping behavior charitable appeals highlighting intrinsic benefits to helpers will be the most effective in inducing helping. In contrast, when the cultural standards account guides helping, highlighting benefits to recipients will be the most effective. First, in a series of laboratory and field studies, we will provide evidence for the default account – the self-worth account. Then, in another series of studies, we will identify certain situations in which the cultural standards account operates when individuals help others in need after they are reminded of their own death. 過往的研究曾提出兩種說法來解釋死亡凸顯對親社會行為的影響──增強自我價值感和強化文化標准──這些研究認為，這兩種動機是獨立或同等的，並隱性假設它們會導致相同的后果。在本研究中，我們認為這兩種動機是截然不同的，並建立了一個理論框架來探討這兩種動機在什麼情況下能促進助人行為。我們的研究結果表明，慈善組織須先了解推動助人行為的動機，然后通過相應的慈善訴求來促進助人行為。通過四個實驗研究，我們發現在死亡凸顯的情況下，助人行為的動機主要源於增強自我價值感。在這種情況下，強調對捐贈者（相比受益者）的利益對促進助人行為更有效。然而，當明確地凸顯親社會規范時，助人行為的動機主要源於強化文化標准。在這種情況下，強調對受益者（相比捐贈者）的利益對促進助人行為更有效。

17500715.label: Realisation of objectives
17500715.value: Objective 1. Through several experiments, we disentangle the two mechanisms of mortality salience: self-worth account and cultural standards account. In several studies, we provide evidence that under mortality salience, individuals’ helping behavior is mainly guided by the motivation to enhance self-worth which is distinguished from the motivation to uphold cultural standards. Supporting the self-worth account, highlighting intrinsic benefits to the helpers was more effective in inducing donations than highlighting benefits to the recipients or extrinsic benefits to the helpers. In other study, we uncover situations in which the cultural standards account is distinguished from the self-worth account. Our findings indicate that when cultural norms are explicitly made salient, participants’ charitable support is guided by the motivation to reinforce these salient cultural norms, such that other-benefit appeals are more effective in inducing helping intention than self-benefit appeals. These findings were disseminated at the 2018 European Marketing Academy Conference, the 2018 European Association for Consumer Research Conference, and the 2017 Association for Consumer Research Conference. In other multiple studies, we examined how to reduce a self-focus to increase donation behaviors. Mortality salience is one type of self-threat which increases people’s focus on self-benefits. We show that humanizing money can reduce a self-focus and increase donation. In several studies, we show that construing money as a person increased donation behaviors under mortality salience (e.g., after reading about stories of the victims of the earthquake in Nepal). These findings were published in Journal of Consumer Research (2019A) and disseminated at the 2016 Association for Consumer Research Conference. We also disseminated several studies on how these two accounts can explain people’s help seeking behavior. The findings support the self-worth account in that people perceive greater costs of helping and are less likely to seek help from even non-human entities if those entities are equipped with humanlike features (e.g., a humanlike computerized helper), particularly when they think intelligence cannot be improved with dedicated effort (i.e., entity theorists). The findings were published in Psychological Science (2018). We also have a study showing how consumers interpret service employees’ helping behaviors (e.g., voluntarily providing useful information to customers). Supporting the cultural standards account, customers were more likely to accept employee’s helping behavior when employees communicated with the customers according to cultural standards (e.g., providing friendly gestures such as a smiley emoticon while engaging in online discretionary behaviors). The finding was published in Journal of Consumer Research (2019B). Objective 2. In several experiments, we show that under mortality salience, individuals’ helping behavior is mainly guided by the motivation to enhance self-worth unless prosocial cultural norms are made salient. For example, in two studies, we demonstrate that the self-worth account dominates the cultural standards account, such that intrinsic self-benefit appeals are more effective in inducing helping than extrinsic self-benefit and other-benefit appeals. In one study, we measure donation to a charity and demonstrate that helping behavior is actually instrumental in enhancing self-worth under mortality salience in response to an intrinsic self-benefit appeal. In another study, we show that the effectiveness of intrinsic self-benefit appeals is reduced when the motivation to enhance self-worth decreases via a self-affirmation task. These findings were disseminated at the 2018 European Association for Consumer Research Conference and the 2017 Association for Consumer Research Conference. In several studies, we also show that when mortality is made salient by charitable appeals, people’s helping behavior is more likely to be guided by the cultural standards account when money is humanized. When the cultural standards account dominates people’s helping behavior, people are influenced by warmth perceptions embedded in even non-human entities such as money. Acting warm and caring toward warm people is a cultural norm. In several studies, we show that people apply this cultural norm even to non-human entities such as money when it is imbued with humanlike characteristics. That is, when people construe money as a warm person, they were more likely to donate money to people in need under mortality salience. These findings were published in Journal of Consumer Research (2019A) and disseminated at the 2016 Association for Consumer Research Conference. We also disseminated several studies supporting the self-worth account in online learning environments in terms of help-seeking. These studies focus on recipients’ perspective instead of helpers’ perspective, and show that help recipients are more likely to accept help with less cost perceptions of getting help when the online help system is absent of social presence. The findings were published in Psychological Science (2018). Objective 3 In several studies, we show that under mortality salience, people are more likely to donate money to a charity when presented with intrinsic self-benefit appeals than other-benefit or extrinsic self-benefit appeals. In one study, we examined the self-worth enhancement account by testing whether the act of donating was actually instrumental in bolstering feelings of self-worth. In line with the self-worth enhancement account, these results support our proposition that under mortality salience people donate money to charity to enhance their feelings of self-worth and in such a situation creating charitable appeals focusing on self-benefits was more effective in increasing donation behavior. These findings were disseminated at the 2017 Association for Consumer Research Conference. In other studies, we show that when mortality is made salient, increasing warmth perceptions by humanizing money using a charitable appeal increases people’s donation behaviors. For instance, in one study we show that including humanlike money clipart in a charitable appeal that evokes mortality salience increases people’s helping intentions. These findings were published in Journal of Consumer Research (2019A) and disseminated at the 2016 Association for Consumer Research Conference. Objective 4 To increase external validity of the findings, we measured people’s real behaviors. In one study, we measured participants’ real money donation to a charity. Supporting the self-worth enhancement account, under mortality salience participants donated more money when the charitable appeal highlighted the intrinsic benefits to the donors rather than the benefits to the recipients, and the extrinsic benefits to the donors. The findings were disseminated at the 2018 European Association for Consumer Research Conference and the 2017 Association for Consumer Research Conference. In another study, we show that when mortality is salient and people construe money as a warm person rather than as a mere object, they not only are more likely to donate real money but also donated more money to people in need, which is consistent with the cultural standards account. This finding was disseminated at Journal of Consumer Research (2019A) and the 2016 Association for Consumer Research Conference. Another study examines recipients’ perspective by measuring their real help-seeking behavior during online learning when people’s self-focus is heightened by beliefs in fixed intelligence (a similar self-threat as one evoked by mortality salience). We found that under such a self-threat, people are less likely to seek help from a computerized helper with humanlike features than from one without such features. The finding was published in Psychological Science (2018). Lastly, in a study published in Journal of Consumer Research (2019B), we conducted a field experiment to examine how meeting cultural standards using emoticons during online conversations can enhance customers’ acceptance of service employees’ helping behaviors in the absence of mortality salience.

17500715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500715.value: We found that under mortality salience, individuals’ helping behavior is mainly guided by the motivation to enhance feelings of self-worth unless prosocial cultural norms are made explicitly salient. Specifically, we found that the self-worth account dominates the cultural standards account, such that intrinsic self-benefit appeals are more effective in inducing helping than extrinsic self-benefit and other-benefit appeal. These findings were disseminated at the 2018 European Marketing Academy Conference, the 2018 European Association for Consumer Research Conference, and the 2017 Association for Consumer Research Conference. We also found one way to overcome a self-threat evoked by mortality salience. Mortality salience can be a threat to one’s sense of self, because it makes people narrowly focused on the self. We found one way to reduce such a self-focus and increase helping behaviors. We show that when charitable appeals evoke mortality salience (e.g., a story about the victims of the earthquake in Napal), imbuing money with humanlike characteristics reduces a self-focus evoked by the charitable appeals and makes cultural standards more salient. In turn, people construe money with humanlike characteristics as a warm person (i.e., a culturally normative person), and they act in a way to meet their cultural standards by donating money to people in need. These findings were disseminated at the 2016 Association for Consumer Research Conference, and published in Journal of Consumer Research (2019A). In addition, we investigated help recipients’ perspective since help recipients’ acceptance of help from others is a critical factor to utilize provided help. The findings support the self-worth account again in that help recipients are more likely to accept help with less cost perceptions of getting help when an online help system is absent of social presence. When the online system is equipped with humanlike characteristics (e.g., a humanlike computerized helper), people are less likely to seek help particularly when they think intelligence cannot be improved with hard work and dedicated effort. The findings were published in Psychological Science (2018). We also explore recipients’ perspective in service relationships. We conducted a field experiment to examine how using emoticons meets cultural standards during online conversations, and how it can enhance customers’ acceptance of service employees’ helping behaviors in the absence of mortality salience. The finding was published in Journal of Consumer Research (2019B).

17500715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500715.value: The current research suggests several additional avenues for future research. The current research revealed various situations in which the self-worth account can explain people’s helping behaviors under mortality salience. Future research can explore various situations in which the cultural standards account can explain people’s helping behaviors under mortality salience. In particular, when one’s cultural norms conflict with one’s self-worth contingency, which motivation will drive individuals’ helping under mortality salience, the motivation to reinforce cultural norms or the motivation to enhance self-worth? Future research can further explore what other factors can determine which motivation will guide helping under mortality salience. Another avenue for future research is examining the cultural or individual differences in perspectives on death. One major culture-based variable is religion. In Buddhism and Hinduism, death is not regarded as the end of one’s existence. Thus, mortality salience may not generate as much existential anxiety. As a result, mortality salience may be less likely to increase helping behavior in such cultures. In contrast, Christians believe they can go to Heaven by doing good deeds, so their helping behavior may be more likely to be driven by mortality salience, especially by the motivation to reinforce their religious beliefs.

17500715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500715.value: The current research focuses on prosocial behavior as one of the coping strategies to deal with the anxiety produced by mortality salience and a self-focus. First, we examined which charitable appeals are more effective in increasing donation under mortality salience and disseminated the findings at the 2018 European Marketing Academy Conference, the 2018 European Association for Consumer Research Conference, and the 2017 Association for Consumer Research Conference. Second, we examined how to overcome mortality salience evoked by charitable appeals (e.g., a story about the victims of the earthquake in Napal). We show that when charitable appeals evoke mortality salience, adding humanlike money clipart in the charitable appeals can increase donation behaviors. The findings were disseminated at the 2016 Association for Consumer Research Conference, and published in Journal of Consumer Research (2019A). Third, in the paper published at Psychological Science (2018), we investigated recipients’ perspective and show people are less likely to accept provided help when they feel a self-threat (e.g., believing intelligence cannot be improved with effort). Lastly, in the paper published at Journal of Consumer Research (2019B), we show that customers are more likely to appreciate service employees’ helping behaviors when they are accompanied with emoticons during online conversations.

17500915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500915.value: The aim of this project is to investigate the monitoring role of the press by examining the implications of press coverage of Chinese firms listed in the U.S. We will apply textual analysis software to news articles on these firms from the business press in the U.S., mainland, China and Hong Kong. This technique will produce variables that capture the articles’ level of optimism/pessimism toward the firms, which can be regarded as a proxy for press evaluations of firm future prospects. We will then explore the monitoring role of the press by investigating the following research questions. (1) Can press coverage help investors to distinguish fraudulent from non-fraudulent Chinese firms listed in the U.S. prior to fraud litigation? (2) Are there any differences in the monitoring role of the press in the U.S. and the press in mainland China? (3) Is there any difference between the English- and Chinese-language presses in Hong Kong in terms of its monitoring role? We will carry out an empirical study to address these questions. We will collect and process news articles from major newspapers in the U.S., mainland China, and Hong Kong covering U.S.-listed Chinese firms from 1994 to 2012. For each news article, we will design a tone measure. Tone is revealed by contextual analysis, and captures the positive/negative tone (i.e., level of optimism/pessimism) of a firm’s press coverage objectively. This measure will allow us to investigate the predictive power of press coverage for these firms’ likelihood of engaging in fraud. The proposed project will contribute to the literature in the following ways. First, we will explore the governance role of the press, thereby enriching the literature on the role of the press and media. Second, we will add to the literature on Chinese firms listed in the U.S. by investigating one potential fraud predictor, namely, press sentiment. Third, we will examine the monitoring role of the press in U.S. and mainland China, thereby contributing to the effect of institutional environments on press’ monitoring role. Finally, we will contribute to the finance and accounting literature applying textual analysis by comparing the content of news coverage in English and Chinese simultaneously under one set of institutional environments. 这个项目的目的是探讨新闻的监测作用，通过研究在美国上市的 中国公司的新闻报道带来的影响。我们将用于文本分析软件研究 这些公司的新闻，包括在美国，大陆，中国和香港的报道。此技 术将生成捕捉文章的新闻评价的情绪的变量。此变量可以视为一 个代理公司的未来前景的参考。然后，我们将通过调查下列研究 问题探索新闻的监测作用。(1) 新闻报道可否帮助投资者来区分从 事欺诈与非欺诈于美国上市的中国公司的吗? (2) 在美国和中国大 陆的报纸监测作用的是否有任何差异? (3) 香港英语和汉语语言新 闻报道的监测作用是否有任何区别? 我们将进行实证研究，以解决这些问题。我们将收集和处理新闻 文章基于主要香港、 美国及中国大陆的报刊杂志涵盖从 1994 年 到 2012 年在美国上市的中国公司。对于每一篇文章中，我们将 设计口气措施。口气通过语境分析，揭示并客观地捕获正面/负面 基调 (即乐观/悲观的水平) 的一家公司的新闻报道。这项措施将 使我们能够调查这些新闻报道对于公司从事欺诈可能性的预测 能力。 拟议的项目将对文献有以下贡献。首先，我们将探索新闻界的治 理作用，从而丰富文献中新闻和媒体的作用。第二，我们会将调 查一个潜在欺诈预测（在美国上市的中国公司）的指标，即新闻 报道情绪。第三，我们将比较在美国和中国大陆新闻的监测作 用的异同，从而有助于对媒体的监督作用的制度环境的影响。 最后，我们通过同时比较英语和汉语的新闻报道在一套制度环境的新闻 报道的内容丰富已有的运用文本分析软件的财务和会计文献。

17500915.label: Realisation of objectives
17500915.value: The study carried in the project addressed the research objectives one by one in the following ways. First, we document that overall press coverage can help investors to distinguish fraudulent from non-fraudulent Chinese firms listed in the U.S. prior to fraud litigation. Second, there is an opposite prediction in the monitoring role of the press in the U.S. and in mainland China. Specifically, when the US news tone is high, the Chinese firms listed in the U.S. are less likely to be involved in fraud litigation. Third, both English and Chinese press in Hong Kong exhibit such a monitoring role, while the marginal effect of the English press seems a little higher. Alternatively, our findings are summarized as below. We conduct textual analysis of news articles published in the U.S., Mainland China, and Hong Kong on the Chinese firms listed in the U.S. between 1992 and 2018. We find that while news articles originated from the U.S. have the predictive power to the firms’ fraud likelihood, news articles originated from mainland China also exhibit a predictive power, but they have opposite tone of prediction. Furthermore, news articles originated from Hong Kong, regardless they are English based or Chinese based, show such a predictive power as U.S. news. This study provides an alternative signal which is timelier in identifying fraudulent firms and advances our understanding on the effects of different institutions, both formal and informal, on the monitoring effects of role of the press.

17500915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500915.value: One publication, “Corporate Governance and Resource Allocation Efficiency: Evidence from IPO Regulation in China”, Journal of International Accounting Research, vol. 17(3), 43-67, Fall 2018, resulted from the project finds the following: as a requisite to issuing initial public offerings (IPOs), Chinese companies must obtain approval from the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC). Using a sample of Chinese firms that applied for IPOs between 2006 and 2011, we examine the influence of corporate governance on the IPO application process and firms’ post-IPO performance. We find that firms with more outside directors, smaller boards, and more balanced ownership among large shareholders are more likely to pass the IPO screening. Along similar lines, controlling shareholder ownership is negatively related to the success of IPO screening. Further analyses show that effective corporate governance plays a more important role when firms engage in more complex operations, and it plays a less important role when firms are politically connected. Finally, we find that firms with better corporate governance enjoy better post-IPO performance, indicating that resource allocation is more efficient when the CSRC values firms’ corporate governance. A summary from a working paper resulted from the project: we conduct textual analysis of news articles published in the U.S., Mainland China, and Hong Kong on the Chinese firms listed in the U.S. between 1992 and 2018. We find that while news articles originated from the U.S. have the predictive power to the firms’ fraud likelihood, news articles originated from mainland China also exhibit a predictive power, but they have opposite tone of prediction. Furthermore, news articles originated from Hong Kong, regardless they are English based or Chinese based, show such a predictive power as U.S. news. This study provides an alternative signal which is timelier in identifying fraudulent firms and advances our understanding on the effects of different institutions, both formal and informal, on the monitoring effects of role of the press.

The news from mainland China press about the firms is more favorable, the likelihood of fraud case is higher. Both English and Chinese news from Hong Kong press shows the predictive power. Our research output also indicates that the better overall corporate governance, the higher likelihood of firms being allowed for IPOs in the mainland China stock exchanges.

17501015.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17501015.value: 供应链中产品可靠性和延长质保价格策略优化

17501015.label: Project Objectives
17501015.value: To solve the base model and compare equilibrium supply chain decisions in three supply chain structures (centralized, decentralized with an independent warranty underwriter, and decentralized with the manufacturer as the underwriter) to shed light on how firms can make effective product reliability and extended warranty pricing decisions. To extend the base model to analyze cases in which the manufacturer and third-party insurer have different costs for honoring extended warranties, and to examine how such cost asymmetry affects the retailer’s optimal decision on whose extended warranty to sell. To analyze other contract forms such as the revenue sharing contract, and to study how effective they are in coordinate the supply chain. To explore other extensions of the base model, such as incorporating replacement purchases, to generate more managerial insights.

17501015.value: 二十世紀八十年代後期延長保修期的服務火熱開展起來，從那時起電子產品零售商們就開始積極地提供這樣的服務。 在當今競爭激烈的市場中，電子產品零售商很難從中獲利。 因為電子產品的利潤也就在3%至4%之間。然而延長保修期的服務卻具有50%至60%之間的高額利潤。 比如說，美國零售商百思買集團對於3,000美元的電視機提供一個四年期的延長保修服務，其收費是400美元，其中有160美元給保險公司，剩下的240美元自己留下（Berner, 2004）。延長保修的市場不僅有利可圖，而且該市場的規模也相當可觀。 2005年美利堅合眾國延長保修期服務的銷售額達到了150億美元，其中利潤為75億美元。（Warranty Week, 2005）。 因此，延長保修期的服務成為了類似百思買集團等電子產品零售連鎖店的搖錢樹，在2003年這些連鎖店一半的營業收入來自于出售延長保修期的服務（Berner, 2004）。 為了使利潤最大化，零售商有必要為這些保修服務訂立合適的價格。 各個零售商的定價方案各有不同，而且實際保修服務的價格也大相徑庭，甚至於那些相同產品的保修服務的價格與不同商家也有差別。 例如，松下42英寸等離子電視機四年期延長保修期服務的價格就相差甚遠，百思買集團是按該電視機價格的14%收取，而etronics.com是按電視機價格的43%收取（Warranty Week, 2006a）。 儘管延長保修期服務定價對於零售商來說非常重要，但如果不進行深入的研究，我們仍然不會弄清楚什麼價格才是最優的。 零售商在延長保修期服務中獲取利潤的多少取決於製造商生產產品可靠性的決策。 換而言之，延長保修服務的價值和價格依賴於產品的可靠性。事實上，產品可靠性和延長保修的定價決策可能亦可能不僅由供應鏈中的一方制定。 一些直接將產品出售給客戶的製造商也出售延長保修的服務。 比如說，客戶後購買蘋果公司的電子產品時，可額外選擇是否購買其延保服務。若購買該服務，原本一年的免費服務期將升級至兩年。 在這樣的集中式供應鏈中，產品的可靠性和延長保修服務定價決策都是由產品製造商決定的。 其它公司，比如三星電子公司主要把產品出售給如百思買集團類的零售商，在這種情況下，零售商可以選擇出售由製造商又或者是第三方保險公司提供的延保服務。在這樣的分散式供應鏈中，製造商決定產品可靠性，而分銷商則制定延長保修期服務的決策。 本次提議的研究將研究在不同情況下公司產品的最佳可靠性和延長保修期服務的定價決策，從而解答以下的問題。 第一，製造商直接將產品銷售給客戶，或通過零售商間接將產品銷售給客戶的情況下如何決定產品的可靠性？第二，集中式供應鏈和分散式供應鏈，哪一種供應鏈會導致較低的延保服務的價格？ 第三，在分散式供應鏈中，什麼形式的合同可以最為有效地協調產品可靠性和延保服務定價決策之間的關係？ 第四， 從零售商的角度出發，是選擇出售由製造商提供的延保服務，還是選擇獨立保險公司提供的延保服務？ 如果很多電子產品零售商依靠延長保修服務的銷售以獲取利潤，甚至是生存下去的話，那麼回答上述這些問題將對於電子零售行業的管理者們非常重要。 製造商也可以在制定決策時，考慮產品可靠性對延長保修期服務銷售和利潤的影響，從而從中受益。

17501415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501415.value: 服务营销正在经历日益红火的自助服务技术使用。自助服务技术指的是企业运用某些技术不需员工参与就可以 为客户提供服务（比如超市的自助结账机，银行的自助取款机）。 企业希望通过使用这些自助服务技术来降低成本，提高生产力，优化服务质量，而消费者则希望使用这些技术来节省时间，提高对服务的控制，以及获得更多乐趣和灵活度。然而自助服务技术也给客户带来挑战。和这些创新型甚至非常复杂的机器交流有别与和人交流。最近的一个趋势是使用拟人化来设计自助服务技术。就是说，把人类的一些特性比如外形，行动，情绪，意图设计到自助服务技术机器上。比如，日本零售品牌MUJI 拥有人形的自动贩卖机（有手，眼睛）.以往的研究发现拟人化能诱使消费者把适用于人际交往的知识使用到人与技术机器的交往上。 那么拟人化将有利于提高消费者和自助服务技术机器之间的社交联系和感受到的可控性，从而优化消费体验。 但是，现有的文献很少研究检测消费者对拟人化自助服务技术的偏好。 本项目主要研究顾客密度对消费者使用拟人化自助服务技术偏好的影响。客户密度是一项与自助服务技术紧密相关的情境性因子。 在通常服务情境下（比如银行，餐厅）顾客一般接受服务是也有其他顾客在场。如果顾客们感觉他们之间的物理距离太近以至于超过能接受的程度，这样的服务环境顾客密集度就比较高因而产生拥挤的感觉。拥挤的感受可能是有两种环境因素造成的： 空间因素，社会因素。空间因素是指物理环境里的空间不足（比如店铺面积小）。社会因素是指物理环境里的人员太多（比如店铺里的客人太多）。 以往的研究发现空间密度高会使人们感觉逼仄从而引起与其他人交往时的侵略性行为，因为在此情形下人们使用侵略性行为来获得控制感 。相反，社会密集度高能诱发撤退型定向，也就是说顾客用减少社会交往来帮助他们保护控制感。 基于两类研究结果，一类发现空间密集和社会密集导致完全不一样的社交趋势（侵略性社会行为vs. 撤退型社会行为），另一类发现消费者把适用于人际交往的知识使用到人与技术机器的交往上,本项研究推测顾客密集对拟人化自助服务技术产品消费体验的影响取决于顾客对密集度的归因。如果他们把高顾客密集度（对比低顾客密集度）归因于空间因素（社会因素），他们将会更喜欢（更不喜欢）拟人化的自助服务技术。我们进一步推测这些效应的机制是客户采用不同的方法来强化他们在拥挤状态下感知的控制力。 我们提出这一效应可能会受制于两个条件：自助服务技术的使用难度和人际相似度。另外，我们也会检测这一效应的后续影响比如对服务质量和可以愉悦度的影响。 我们计划用实验室实验和田野实验的方法来测试我们的假设。本项目的发现将对自助服务技术文献，顾客密集度文献，拟人化研究，和合作服务的理论研究做出贡献。同时对于服务行业的实际应用也有意义。

17501415.label: Realisation of objectives
17501415.value: 1. Objective 1 is to examine how customer density and the attribution of density to spatial or social reasons would influence consumers’ preference for anthropomorphized Self-Serving Technology (SSTs). We conducted a series of experimental and field studies in the context of banking, food service, using participants from Hong Kong and U.S.. The results show that attributing the crowding environment to social reasons (e.g., having too many people in the physical setting), as compared with a non-crowding condition, reduces participants’ intention to use or the actual usage of the anthropomorphized (vs. non-anthropomorphized) SSTs. However, when participants attribute the crowding environment to spatial reasons (e.g., having very limited physical space in the environment), their attitudes and intention to using anthropomorphized SSTs are either higher or not different from the non-crowding condition. 2. Objective 2 is to examine the mechanisms underlying the distinctive effects of focusing on spatial versus social densities on preferences for anthropomorphized SSTs. The experiment conducted in the banking service situation shows that attributing the crowding to social reasons (i.e., having too many customers queuing for the ATM service) reduces the intention to use the anthropomorphized SSTs (ATM machine), and that this effect did not occur when participants attribute the crowding to spatial reasons (i.e., having a limited area for queuing for the ATM service). Importantly, this interactive effect is mediated by customers’ social withdrawal tendency. That is, participants had a heightened sense of social withdrawal when they were in a crowding situation with an attribution of the crowding to social reasons, which in turn reduced their intention to use the anthropomorphized ATM machine. This mediation process did not occur for participants in the crowding condition where the attribution of crowding is to spatial reasons. 3. Objective 3 is to examine the boundary conditions for the crowding effect. We conducted a series experimental and field studies, in the context of food service, retailing store, bookstore. These studies show that, providing a contextualized similarity among customers (e.g., having customers to wear the same sticker based on a contrived personality test, a contrived service feature) reduce the perceived social crowding in the physical environment and consequently the effects of social crowding on customer behavior. 4. Objective 4 is to examine the downstream effects of crowding such as customers’ perceived service quality, customer satisfaction. In a series of laboratory experiments, it was found that the effect of crowding on the attitudes and usage of SSTs spill over to customers’ rating of the service quality. In a bigger picture, the impact of crowding on customer experience is found to correlate with service quality and customer satisfaction. 5. The current proposal examines the physical environment of customer density on customers’ preference and decisions, and it also examines the specific marketing tactics of using anthropomorphism in product and service. Relevant to the topics of customer density and product anthropomorphism, we also document additional interesting findings: one is how crowding attributed to social factors influences customers’ choice; the other is how product anthropomorphism influences comparative judgment and decision-making. First, a set of experimental and field studies conducted in a retailing context (e.g., pastry shop) show that crowding attributed to social reasons (i.e., social crowding) increase customers’ choice share of their favorite item in a product bundle (i.e., reducing varieties of choice from the product bundle), and decrease more sales when the product bundle does not contain the popular items, compared with a non-crowding condition. This effect occurred because social crowding triggers a stronger sense of low product availability among customers. This effect is mitigated when customers learn that the product inventory can be replenished frequently. Second, a sets of experiments conducted using participants from USA and Hong Kong show that product anthropomorphism increases consumers’ use of an absolute judgment strategy (versus a dimension-by-dimension strategy) in comparative judgment, leading to increased preference for the product alternative with a more favorable overall evaluation over the product alternative with a greater number of superior dimensions. The effect is mediated by consumers’ perception of each anthropomorphized product alternative as an integrated entity rather than a bundle of separate attributes, and moderated by the motivation to seek maximized accuracy or ease.

17501415.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501415.value: The major findings from research conducted focusing on the current proposal are published in a peer-reviewed journal and presented at two conferences. The first set of studies document the following findings, using research participants in USA and Hong Kong. A manuscript based on these findings is accepted for publication in Journal of Consumer Research. • Product anthropomorphism increases consumers’ use of an absolute judgment strategy (versus a dimension-by-dimension strategy) in comparative judgment, leading to increased preference for the product alternative with a more favorable overall evaluation over the product alternative with a greater number of superior dimensions. • The effect is mediated by consumers’ perception of each anthropomorphized product alternative as an integrated entity rather than a bundle of separate attributes. • The effect is moderated by the motivation to seek maximized accuracy or ease. The second set of studies document the following findings, using research participants in USA and Hong Kong. Part of these findings is presented at the Association for Consumer Research, North American Conference, San Diego, California, USA, October 2017. • Customers are less likely to prefer anthropomorphized self-service technologies (e.g., self-ordering machine in cafeteria, ATM in bank) when they attribute the crowded environment to social reasons, compared with customers in a non-crowding environment. • This effect is mitigated or reversed when customers attribute the crowded environment to spatial reasons. • The interaction between attribution of the crowding and SSTs anthropomorphism is mediated by customers’ social withdrawal tendency. The third set of studies document the following findings, using research participants in USA and China. Part of these findings is presented at the INFORMS Marketing Science Conference, Rome, June 2019. • Crowding attributed to social reasons (i.e., social crowding), compared with non-crowding, increase customers’ choice share of their favorite item in a product bundle (i.e., reducing varieties of choice from the product bundle). • Social crowding in a retailing store, compared with non-crowding, decrease more sales when the product bundle does not contain the popular items. • This effect occurred because social crowding triggers a stronger sense of low product availability among customers, which prompts customers to get more of their favorite items. • This effect is mitigated when customers learn that the product inventory can be replenished frequently.

17501415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501415.value: There are several avenues for possible extension for this research. First, one extension is to investigate the usage of anthropomorphism on smart machine, as a function of the physical environment of social density. Given the increasing usage of AI technology in the service industry (e.g., chatbot, social bot), it will be important to examine how the consumers’ physical environment such as crowding would affect their responses towards the smart machine with humanized features. Second, it would also be interesting to examine the effect of social density on people’s consumption preference relating to the sensory experience such as visual, audio, haptic, olfactory, taste experience. Social crowding causes the feeling of overall social stimulation, which may encourage people to select consumption activities that help them block sensory experience.

17501415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501415.value: Self-serving technologies (SSTs) refer to the technologies provided by firms to help customers produce services without assistance from employees (e.g., self-checkout machine, ATM). By introducing SSTs, service firms expect to reduce cost, improve productivity, and enhance service quality, and consumers expect to save time and have flexibility. There is an increasing trend to employ anthropomorphism in designing SSTs: imbuing human characteristics such as human physical features, action, emotion and intention in SSTs. For example, MUJI’s vending machine has human-like facial and body features. The current research examines the influence of customer density- a highly relevant situational factor-on customers’ usage of anthropomorphized SSTs. Our studies show that customers’ reaction towards SSTs with human features in a crowded environment depends on their attribution. When customers attribute crowding to social reasons (i.e. having too many people), their preference and usage of anthropomorphized SSTs decrease. When customers attribute crowding to spatial reasons (i.e., having too limited space), their usage of anthropomorphized SSTs do not vary or even reverse. This is because a social-based crowding triggers a stronger sense of social withdrawal. This effect spills over to customers’ rating of service quality. Moreover, creating contrived similarity among customers helps mitigate the negative of social crowding.

17501915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501915.value: Accounting rule makers have long recommended firms prepare cash flow statements using the direct method (DM), under which cash inflows and outflows are separately reported in the operating section of the statement. DM proponents argue that DM cash flow components help capital providers better assess firms’ future cash flow and earnings and thus aid resource allocation. However, while the DM is preferred it is not required by most accounting regulators, including the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) in the United States. Preparers of financial statements argue that the DM imposes excessive implementation costs because they do not currently collect cash flows in a way that allows them to accumulate transaction-level data for DM cash flow components, such as cash received from customers. They also claim that the indirect method (IM), under which net income is reconciled to net operating cash flow, provides the same amount of value-relevant information as the DM. In this proposed project, we directly examine whether providing DM cash flow statements reduces cost of debt and cost of equity capital. Prior studies have consistently found that DM components are incrementally useful for predicting future operating performance beyond the information contained in IM cash flow statements. Several studies have also shown that investors and creditors appear to utilize DM components in their trading and lending decisions. Despite the suggestion of these findings that DM components contain incremental value-relevant information beyond the IM format, ex-ante, it is not clear whether firms enjoy a reduced cost of capital by providing DM cash flow statements. First, given the rich disclosure environment for U.S. firms, it is not clear to what extent DM cash flow statements provide incremental information beyond all other existing information sources. Second, it is also not clear, given the amount of available information, whether presentation format affects investors’ assessment. By directly examining the impact of DM cash flows on costs of debt and equity, we provide quantitative measures of the economic benefits of providing DM cash flows and contribute to the overall cost-benefit debate on providing DM cash flow statements. We believe the findings of this project are important for users and preparers of financial statements, as well as for accounting standard setters. 会计准则制定者长期以来都强烈推荐企业用直接法准备现金流量表。直接法使得现金流出和流入被分开报告在经营活动的报表部分。 直接法的支持者认为直接法现金流量表的构成部分有助于资本提供者更好的评估企业未来现金流和盈利情况因而有益于资源配置。然而，尽管准则制定者偏好直接法，包括财务会计准则委员会（FASB）在内的大部分准则制定者并不强制要求企业使用直接法。财务报表的编制者声称直接法会产生额外的实施成本，因为企业现在收支现金的方式使得他们无法收集交易层面的数据（比如从客户处收到的现金）来构成直接法现金流量表。他们还表示间接法（将净利润调整为经营活动产生的现金流量净额的准备现金流量表的方法）和直接法提供同样多估值相关的信息。 在这个项目中，我们直接检查是否提供直接法现金流量表能减少债务成本和权益资本成本。之前的研究一致地发现直接法的构成成分在间接法现金流量表包含的信息基础上对预测未来经营业绩有额外作用。一些研究表明股权投资者和债权人似乎在他们的交易和贷款决策中利用了直接法的构成部分。尽管研究发现直接法构成成分事前在间接法报表格式基础上提供估值相关的增量信息，我们并不清楚企业是否因为提供直接法现金流量表而降低了融资成本。首先，给定美国企业面临的丰富的信息披露环境，我们并不清楚直接法现金流量表多大程度地在已有信息源上提供了增量信息。其次，给定可用的信息，我们也不清楚是否信息的展示方式影响投资者的评估。通过直接检查直接法现金流对股权和债券融资成本的影响，我们对直接法现金流量表的经济利益提供定量的测量并对整个有关直接法现金流量表的整体利弊争论做出贡献。我们相信这个项目的结果对于财务报表的使用者和编制者以及会计准则制定者都很重要。

17502015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502015.value: We study the pricing of distress risk in the cross-section of stock returns. The academic literature has long debated whether distress risk is priced in the cross-section of stock returns, as well as the sign and magnitude of the distress premium if any. In particular, many researchers have looked at how firm-level default probabilities are related to firm-level stock returns. However, much less effort has been devoted to directly determining whether aggregate distress risk is a systematic risk factor. Traditional asset pricing theories (e.g., Sharpe (1964) and Lintner (1965)) suggest that only aggregate risks should be priced, and diversifiable idiosyncratic risks should not be. We test whether systematic default risk is priced in the cross-section of stock returns. If the market distress risk is a systematic risk factor, it should be priced in the sense that stocks with different exposures to innovations in the market distress risk factor will carry different expected risk premiums. Our analysis helps to answer the following research questions: (1) Is market distress risk a factor priced in the cross-section of stock returns? If so, what is the implied distress risk premium? (2) What are the time series properties of market distress risk? (3) How does the composition of distress risk differ across firm characteristics? Does the distress risk factor help explain the size and value premiums? (4) Further, is idiosyncratic distress risk priced? Recent literature has found that idiosyncratic risk is related to average returns. First, we propose a measure of market distress risk, combining and extending methodologies from Vassalou and Xing (2004) and Coval, Jurek and Stafford (2009). We measure the individual firm value fluctuations every month, identify the underlying common shocks, and form the conditional probability of market-level defaults as our measure. It allows for the possibility of correlated defaults, adjusts for asymmetries in firm default probabilities and sizes, and covers a much larger sample than papers relying on information from asset classes other than equities (e.g. CDS) to infer default probabilities. Next, we decompose firm-level distress risk into the systematic and idiosyncratic components. In the core of our analysis, we study the pricing implications of systematic distress risk in the cross-section of equity returns. This relates to the literature connecting distress risk with value and size premia. Finally, we study the pricing of idiosyncratic distress risks in the cross-section of stock returns. 我们研究系统风险在股票市场的定价。 文献大量讨论了违约风险是否在股票回报的截面被定价，以及违约风险溢价的大小。很多研究者研究了公司违约概率和公司股票回报之间的关系。但是，宏观违约风险是否系统性风险因子并没有被研究过。经典的文献总结，只有系统性风险才会被定价，可被分散的个体性风险不应该被定价。 我们研究系统性风险在股票截面是不是被定价。如果市场违约风险是一个系统性风险因子，它应该在股票截面被定价，对风险因子头寸不同的股票的回报率应该有所不同。 我们的研究可以回答一下问题： 1. 市场违约风险在股票截面是否被定价？如果有定价，相应的风险溢价是多少？ 2. 市场违约风险的时间序列特征是什么？ 3. 违约风险和股票特征怎么样相关联？违约风险是否帮助解释公司大小和公司价值溢价？ 4. 个体性违约风险是否被定价？最新文献发现，个体性风险与公司平均回报有关系。 首先，我们在Vassalou & Xing (2004), Coval, Jurek & Stafford (2009)的基础上，拓展延伸，提出一个市场违约风险的测度。我们观测每个公司每个月的价值变动，找出深层的共同变动，简历一个市场违约风险的条件期望。我们的测度可以考虑违约风险的相关，适用于比依赖其他市场的测度更长的样本。 然后，我们把公司层面的违约风险分解成系统性和个体性风险。在主要研究部分，我们研究系统性在股票截面的定价。我们根据文献讨论违约风险和价值溢价之间的关系。最后我们研究个体性风险在股票截面的溢价。

17502015.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502015.value: Using a structural model of default, we construct a measure of systemic default defined as the probability that many firms default at the same time. Our estimation accounts for correlations in defaults between firms through common exposures to shocks. The systemic default measure spikes during recession periods, is strongly correlated with traditional credit-related macroeconomic measures such as the default spread and VIX, and predicts future realized defaults. Furthermore, our measure predicts future equity and corporate bond index returns, particularly at the one-year horizon, and even after controlling for many traditional return predictors such as the dividend yield, default spread, inflation, and tail risk. These predictability results are robust to out-of-sample tests.

17502015.value: We are extending the results to the long sample from 1920s.

17502015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502015.value: This project constructs the first aggregate distress risk measure, and finds that the aggregate distress risk is priced in the stock market. Investors require to be compensated for the aggregate distress risk.

17502715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502715.value: Many investors seek information from traditional and social media to help making investment decisions. Previous research has shown that the sentiment level in stock opinions in media is a possible predictor of stock returns. However, no previous research has considered the difference between the effect of the opinions in traditional media and social media on “penny” stocks (i.e., stocks of small public companies traded at low prices) and “non-penny” stocks. Perceived as risky investments, penny stocks could yield considerable profits because of higher price volatility. However, as information on these penny stocks is often less reported in traditional media, investors may rely more on social media to obtain such information when investing in these stocks. In the proposed study, we will investigate the relationship between traditional media and social media and financial implications of penny stocks and non-penny stocks. We will study how the net proportion of positive words in stock articles can help predict the future stock performance. The moderation effects of penny stocks will be studied. We will also propose and evaluate trading strategies based on our measure utilizing data from traditional media and social media. The results of our findings and applications will be useful for both researchers and practitioners. 很多投資者在傳統媒體與社交媒體上尋找資料來協助投資決策 。過往的研究指出媒體上有關股票意見的情感水平有預測股票回報的可能性。然而，這些研究沒有考慮傳統媒體與社交媒體上有關「低價股」（即以低價格作出交易的小型上市公司股票）及「非低價股」投資意見影響的分別。低價股是具風險的投資，但由於其價格波動較大，回報亦可以相對可觀。然而，有關低價股的資料通常較少在傳統媒體上報導，投資者可能比較依靠社交媒體上的資料以投資這類股票。在此研究中，我們會探討傳統媒體及社交媒體與低價股與非低價股的關係及它們的財務影響。我們除了會研究在股票評論文章上正向詞的淨百分比如何協助預測未來股票表現，也會分析低價股的干擾效果。我們會根據此方法在傳統媒體與社交媒體上的資料作出分析，建議及評估交易策略。此研究的發現及應用將會對研究人員和從業者有用。

17502715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502715.value: In this project we studied the effects of sentiment level in traditional media and social media on predicting the returns on penny stocks and non-penny stocks. Dow Jones News articles (traditional media) and SeekingAlpha articles (social media) were collected and analyzed, and used to predict stock return data collected from financial databases. We found that firms with lower market capitalization levels were more dependent on social media (compared with traditional media) in terms of future stock performance. The duration with significant positive values on the net fraction of positive words is also higher for smaller firms compared with larger ones. It was found that effect of social media on future stock performance for firms in the technology, health care, financial and services sectors can be larger compared with traditional media. Several trading strategies were also developed and evaluated, and the best strategies are profitable on our test data. The findings were published in a journal paper and also a PhD thesis.

17502715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17502715.value: One of our ongoing research projects is to explore how other factors, such author attributes, can affect the predictive power of media on stock returns. Another project is to explore how to better predict stock return by using machine learning models and deep learning models. We are experimenting with long short-term memory models and the preliminary results are encouraging. We will continue testing our data on different machine learning and deep learning models.

17502715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502715.value: In this project we studied how social media and traditional media can be used to predict the returns on penny stocks and non-penny stocks. Dow Jones News articles and SeekingAlpha articles were collected and analyzed, and their sentiment levels were calculated and used to predict stock return. We found that firms with lower market capitalization levels were more dependent on social media (compared with traditional media) in terms of future stock performance. The findings are important to improve our understanding of the effect of media on the stock market. Investors and fund managers should also be aware of such effects and pay attention to the media when making their investment decisions.
