17601715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17601715.value: This study aims to investigate whether and how genre-based pedagogy can be implemented in Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) programmes to facilitate students’ learning of content knowledge and academic literacies, as well as teachers’ and students’ perceptions of such pedagogy. A total of three teachers and 126 students in Hong Kong and Mainland China were involved in this study. Intervention based on genre-based pedagogy was implemented in humanities subject lessons, and students’ performance on the pre-test and post-test were analysed, and compared with those in the comparison group whenever possible. The teachers and some selected students were interviewed for their beliefs and attitudes towards the pedagogy. The findings show that genre-based pedagogy could facilitate students’ development of academic literacies, without trade-off in content knowledge. In the three schools, students’ performance in the post-test was significantly better than that in the pre-test, in both content and language aspects. When comparing the performance of students in the experimental and control group, the students in the former could in general produce better writing, in terms of organisation, logical development and connection of ideas, as well as appropriate use of connectives and academic vocabulary. It is also observed that students with lower English proficiency and general academic ability made more progress than their counterparts. The data collected during classroom observations further showed that genre-based pedagogy served as a guiding pedagogical framework for teachers to systematically incorporate language teaching into the content subject lessons. Teachers and students alike welcomed genre-based pedagogy and they believed it was effective. They highlighted the effectiveness of the pedagogy in helping students to master the structure and language features of the target genre, so that they could express their ideas in a more systematic way. However, the teachers did experience time constraint when trying to incorporate some language teaching into their content subject lessons. A couple of teachers were also observed to struggle when trying to strike a balance between content and language teaching in their lessons. To conclude, this research study demonstrates the potential of genre-based pedagogy in CLIL programmes, which in turn illuminates effective CLIL pedagogy and teacher education. Its major findings have been presented at two international conferences and published in one international journal article. Another manuscript has been submitted to an international journal. Part of the major findings will also be incorporated into a sole-authored book (see Part C for details).

17601715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17601715.value: One limitation of this research study is the involvement of a limited number of teachers and schools. It also happens that all the teacher participants had received some training on CLIL prior to joining this study. Hence, the encouraging findings of this study should be validated in other educational contexts, including tertiary institutions, primary schools and other jurisdictions. The PI has been exploring the possibility of carrying out a similar study in other contexts through her collaboration in Taiwan and South Korea. She is one of the co-investigators on a CLIL project proposal submitted by her collaborators in Taiwan. When marking students’ performance in the pre-test and post-test in this study, the researchers had designed specific assessment rubrics, which were separated into the “content” and “language” aspects. The PI would argue that this is an innovative way of assessing students’ performance in CLIL, and would like to explore this further. She has planned to conduct a small-scale pilot study, which could enable her to write a solid research proposal to apply for another GRF in the near future.

17601715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17601715.value: In Content and Language Integrated Learning (CLIL) programmes, students learn content subjects through a second/foreign language, and they encounter difficulties when trying to master the academic language involved. This study aims to investigate whether and how genre-based pedagogy can be implemented to facilitate students’ learning of content knowledge and academic literacy. A total of three teachers and 126 students in Hong Kong and Mainland China were involved in this study. Intervention based on genre-based pedagogy was implemented in humanities subject lessons, and students’ performance on the pre-test and post-test were analysed, and compared with those in the comparison group whenever possible. The findings show that genre-based pedagogy could facilitate students’ development of academic literacies, without trade-off in content knowledge. Students could produce better writing in terms of organisation, logical development of ideas and appropriate use of academic vocabulary. Teachers and students welcomed genre-based pedagogy and believed it was effective. These findings demonstrate the potential of adopting genre-based pedagogy in CLIL lessons, which addresses a long-lasting concern about how teachers can better integrate content and language teaching in their actual classroom practices. These in turn illuminate effective pedagogy and teacher education in the increasingly popular CLIL programmes.

17601815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17601815.value: 過去三十年，亞洲地區的法律專業發展迅速。律師在司法制度中扮演重要的角色，瞭解他們的價值觀將有助研究有關地區的法律制度之質素；此外，研究法學生的價值觀將有助預測他們未來執業時的行為及道德標準。然而，當西方普通法區已建立一套對律師或法學生價值觀的研究系統時，這類研究在亞洲地區卻相當缺乏。 本研究項目將對這四個亞洲國家的法學生之價值觀進行比較研究，包括中國、越南、日本及南韓。此四國相似之處，在於它們均採用大陸法系；但前兩者的社會制度為社會主義，而後兩者則為資本主義。 本項目集中於五道研究問題：第一，哪些價值對中國、越南、日本和南韓法學生的行為及道德倫理影響最大？第二，這四個亞洲大陸法區的法學生有沒有共同的核心價值？第三，這四個地方的法學生的價值取向有没有相異之處？第四，以上亞洲國家法學生的價值排序有否受性別差異所影響？最後，這些亞洲大陸法區法學生的價值取向跟其他亞洲普通法區的業界同仁有沒有異同？ 本項目的研究方法包括問卷調查及與中國、越南、日本和南韓法學生進行半結構式訪談。這項目是建基於本研究團隊一位澳洲教授之前對當地學生所進行的研究，以及三位本團隊成員正在大中華地區及三個亞洲普通法區所進行的類似研究。本項目以澳洲採用過的問卷內容為藍本，並將律師和法律系學生價值取向這研究範疇，由西方普通法區延伸至此四個亞洲大陸法區。這樣一來，本研究將拓寬目前對律師和法律學生價值觀研究的領域，從普通法世界推廣至亞洲的大陸法系國家。

17601815.label: Realisation of objectives
17601815.value: Objective One (identification and comparison of the values that are characteristic of law students in China, Vietnam, Japan and South Korea) : this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews undertaken with 22 law students in China, 25 law students in Vietnam, 21 students in South Korea and 53 students in Japan; secondly, questionnaire surveys completed with 670 law students in China (China University of Political Science and Law, Jiaotong University, Jilin University, Peking University, Shandong University, Shenzhen University, Tsinghua University), 401 law students in Vietnam (Hanoi Law University), 310 law students in South Korea (Ewha Womans University, Sung Kyun Kwan University and Yonsei University) and 206 law students in Japan (Fukuoka University, Keio Law School, Tsukuba Law school, Doshisha University and Kyoto University). Objective Two (assessment of the significance of values in the decision-making process of law students in these four Asian civil law countries): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews undertaken with 22 law students in China, 25 law students in Vietnam, 21 students in South Korea and 53 students in Japan; and secondly, questionnaire surveys completed with 670 law students in China (China University of Political Science and Law, Jiaotong University, Jilin University, Peking University, Shandong University, Shenzhen University, Tsinghua University), 401 law students in Vietnam (Hanoi Law University), 310 law students in South Korea (Ewha Womans University, Sung Kyun Kwan University and Yonsei University) and 206 law students in Japan (Fukuoka University, Keio Law School, Tsukuba Law school, Doshisha University and Kyoto University). Objective Three (investigation of the effect of gender on the value orientations of law students in these four Asian civil law countries): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews were undertaken with 22 law students in China, 25 law students in Vietnam, 21 students in South Korea and 53 students in Japan; secondly, questionnaire surveys were completed with 670 law students in China (China University of Political Science and Law, Jiaotong University, Jilin University, Peking University, Shandong University, Shenzhen University, Tsinghua University), 401 law students in Vietnam (Hanoi Law University), 310 law students in South Korea (Ewha Womans University, Sung Kyun Kwan University and Yonsei University) and 206 law students in Japan (Fukuoka University, Keio Law School, Tsukuba Law school, Doshisha University and Kyoto University); and thirdly, literature review undertaken on the impacts of gender on value orientations of law students. Objective Four (evaluation of the impact of legal education on the value orientation of law students in four Asian civil law countries): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews were undertaken with 22 law students in China, 25 law students in Vietnam, 21 students in South Korea and 53 students in Japan; secondly, questionnaire surveys were completed with 670 law students in China (China University of Political Science and Law, Jiaotong University, Jilin University, Peking University, Shandong University, Shenzhen University, Tsinghua University), 401 law students in Vietnam (Hanoi Law University), 310 law students in South Korea (Ewha Womans University, Sung Kyun Kwan University and Yonsei University) and 206 law students in Japan (Fukuoka University, Keio Law School, Tsukuba Law school, Doshisha University and Kyoto University); and thirdly, literature review undertaken on the legal education on the value orientation of law students. Objective Five (investigation of other local factors, other than legal education that shape the value development of law students in China, Vietnam, Japan, and South Korea): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews were undertaken with 22 law students in China, 25 law students in Vietnam, 21 students in South Korea and 53 students in Japan; secondly, questionnaire surveys were completed with 670 law students in China (China University of Political Science and Law, Jiaotong University, Jilin University, Peking University, Shandong University, Shenzhen University, Tsinghua University), 401 law students in Vietnam (Hanoi Law University), 310 law students in South Korea (Ewha Womans University, Sung Kyun Kwan University and Yonsei University) and 206 law students in Japan (Fukuoka University, Keio Law School, Tsukuba Law school, Doshisha University and Kyoto University); and thirdly, literature review undertaken on the cultural impacts of Confucianism and Communism on the value developments of law students. Objective Six (identification and development of strategies that can help both the governments and law schools in these four Asian civil law countries to reform their curricula on value development of their law students): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews were undertaken with 22 law students in China, 25 law students in Vietnam, 21 students in South Korea and 53 students in Japan; secondly, questionnaire surveys were completed with 670 law students in China (China University of Political Science and Law, Jiaotong University, Jilin University, Peking University, Shandong University, Shenzhen University, Tsinghua University), 401 law students in Vietnam (Hanoi Law University), 310 law students in South Korea (Ewha Womans University, Sung Kyun Kwan University and Yonsei University) and 206 law students in Japan (Fukuoka University, Keio Law School, Tsukuba Law school, Doshisha University and Kyoto University); and thirdly, literature review undertaken on the value education and ethics education of law school focusing on clinical legal education and legal ethics teaching in China, Vietnam, Japan and Korea. Objective Seven (To evaluate the similarities and differences in the value orientation of law students in Asian civil law countries and their common law counterparts): this objective was fully achieved by firstly, interviews were undertaken with 22 law students in China, 25 law students in Vietnam, 21 students in South Korea and 53 students in Japan; secondly, questionnaire surveys were completed with 670 law students in China (China University of Political Science and Law, Jiaotong University, Jilin University, Peking University, Shandong University, Shenzhen University, Tsinghua University), 401 law students in Vietnam (Hanoi Law University), 310 law students in South Korea (Ewha Womans University, Sung Kyun Kwan University and Yonsei University) and 206 law students in Japan (Fukuoka University, Keio Law School, Tsukuba Law school, Doshisha University and Kyoto University); and thirdly, literature review undertaken on the value education and ethics education of law schools in Asian civil law countries and their Asian common law counterparts.

17601815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17601815.value: (Please refer to items 1-4 in section 8, and items 1-3 and 5-7 in section 9) 1. Overall, law students in China, Japan, South Korea and Vietnam have developed professional values similar to law students in other Asian common law jurisdictions like Hong Kong and Singapore but to different extent. 2. There is a general pattern of feminization of law students in the Asian civil law countries, namely, there are more females than male students in these countries. 3. Some correlation exist between gender and ethical values of law students in South Korea. Female law students are more motivated by the value of ‘morality of case’, ‘ethic of care’ and ‘ethic of justice’. 4. Students in these Asian civil law countries developed similar values like ‘family well-being’, which reflect the influence of traditional Confucian values like ‘filial pity’. 5. In future, law school in these Asian civil countries should expand their legal ethics programmes to inculcate upon their students the value of ‘access to legal justice’. 6. Law schools in the four Asian civil law countries should strengthen the ethical values of law students by developing their ‘personal conscience”, “ethics of duty”, and “ethics of aspiration. They should also cultivate such virtues like honesty and fairness among their students to help them encounter ethical dilemmas.

17601815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17601815.value: As we have studied the ethical values of Asian civil law countries, we propose to expand our research to the other parts of the world, like civil law countries in the European Union. On basis of the findings of this project, Dr Wu (PI) has applied for GRF grants to study the ethical values of law students in four fast growing Asian countries (China, India, Philippines and Thailand) and four transitional and emerging economic countries (China, Russia, Kazakhstan and South Africa) in 2016 and 2017 respectively. He was awarded a sum of HK$844,880 in 2017 (project No. 17602717) and another sum of HK$918,160 (Project No. 17601018) in 2018 respectively. In 2019, Dr Wu (PI) has also applied for another GRF grant to study the the ethical values and well-being of law students in four countries across the religious-secular spectrum (Myanmar, Indonesia, Israel and China) (RGC Ref. No. 17600720).

17601815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17601815.value: The project investigates empirically the ethical values of law students in four Asian civil law countries. It found that law students in these four countries have developed professional values similar to those in Asian common law jurisdictions like Hong Kong and Singapore. This study also recommends the law schools in the Asian civil law countries to cultivate a strong ethical identity among their students in the future. This project is significant as it has enhanced our understanding of the values of law students in China, Japan, South Korea and Vietnam. It is also invaluable in developing a new field of academic inquiry by leading to the research projects on the values of law students in four Asian fastest growing countries as well as four transitional and emerging economies. Moreover, it leads to another project on the values and well-being of four countries across the religious-secular spectrum. Overall, this project gives insights on ethical values of law students in Asian civil law countries. It has contributed to the academic discourse on the ethical values of law students and Asian legal education.

17602615.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17602615.value: 革命先驅：追蹤中國朝鮮邊境的朝鮮商人

17602615.label: Project Objectives
17602615.value: To identify, characterise and categorise the different type of cross border traders there are shuttling between China and North Korea. To obtain an in-depth ethnographic description of the cross-border operations of these small time North Korea traders, and gain an appreciation of the motivations and difficulties they face and the strategies they employ to overcome these difficulties. To understand and establish the prevalence of market activities as well as the practices and norms of marketisation widely practiced in the home towns of these traders. To understand how marketisation have changed the traders' lives at critical junctures between the mid-1990s and now, and to contextualise these changes against the backdrop of larger social and political developments during the same period. To understand the role they play in advancing marketisation in the DPRK, in particular how they negotiate with the institutions of the State on the daily basis with their activities. To examine how these trading activities are perceived and mediated by the North Korean regime, by the local governments of Jilin, Liaoning Provinces and by the Central government in Beijing, and how these activities affects Sino-DPRK relations. To establish if the marketisation efforts on the ground undercuts the effects of external sanctions and at the same time help mitigate the harsh environment imposed by the broken down economy on a daily basis.

17602615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17602615.value: 對很多人而言，今天的朝鮮民主主義人民共和國（朝鮮）仍是一個拒人於千里之外的神祕國度。就連全球化的浪潮，也彷彿在朝鮮的國境前突然停下。我們對朝鮮的無知，除源自她的鎖國政策，亦可歸咎於眾多片面及互相矛盾的消息來源：如韓裔中國人回鄉後的描述、脫北者的証言、國際傳媒的報導、來自韓國的消息及偶而平壤官方的報導。這些消息來源的背後往往帶着偏見和挑釁性，併湊起來亦未必能得出朝鮮的真象。長久以來，朝鮮備受國際社會排斥，前美國總統喬治布殊更認定她為「邪惡軸心」的一員。的確，很多外界對朝鮮的指控，絕非無中生有：如發展地下核子設施、暗中進行軍事活動、惡名昭彰並嚴重侵犯人權的勞改營、公開處決死囚、坐視國內大規模饑荒、卻同時讓少數的特權階級過着搖滾巨星般的奢華生活，酒池肉林，夜夜笙歌。簡而言之，朝鮮就是國際社會中的壞孩子。朝鮮總是引人注目，只因她的行徑常超出我們的理解、預期及常識範圍。面對外界的警告、威脅、誘導、賄賂及制裁，朝鮮總能堅持自己的路線，拒向列強屈服。紛爭的結果，往往跟朝鮮的行徑同樣地出人意表。朝鮮總是能全身而退，就連美國、俄羅斯及中國都無力引導或影響她的行徑。即使如此，朝鮮最引人入勝之處，應在於平壤政府維持政權的韌力。過去二十年，世界各國、特別是韓國的分析員都預期朝鮮政府即將崩潰；然而今天的金氏皇朝卻看似日趨穩固。我們如何解釋這偏離常理之象？本研究提出，我們不應將答案鎖定在宏觀國際外交層面上；取而代之，我們應從微觀層面出發，仔細研究朝鮮邊境的地下貿易活動，找出一個客觀可信、又能暫時排除境外制裁及經濟環境因素的答案。

17602715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17602715.value: 巾斗：一種新發現的宋代詞樂體式

17602715.label: Project Objectives
17602715.value: The ripple effect of this research can be described as forming four concentric circles: The first and smallest “ripple” is to clarify the jindou form itself, by aligning the zhuan lyrics surviving in a Zhizheng (1340) edition of the Shilinguangji with the musical notation of the same tune preserved in a Zhishun era (1330-33) edition. The second, wider objective is to apply these principles to the seventeen Jiang Kui ci for which there is extant musical notation. Third and still more significant is an assessment of the extent to which the jindou form can be found in the hundred or so Jiang Kui lyric songs for which no musical notation survives. The final, fourth, and largest “ripple” is a reasoned and logical discussion of the presumed presence of the jindou form in the 20,000-strong corpus of Song ci as a whole.

The second, wider objective is to apply these principles to the seventeen Jiang Kui ci for which there is extant musical notation.

17602715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17602715.value: As one of the major Chinese poetic genres, ci originally matched song texts to existing musical tunes. It emerged in the Tang dynasty (618-907) in response to the popularity of foreign musical melodies newly imported from Central Asia, and reached the apex of its artistic status during the Northern and Southern Song dynasties (960-1279). By the fourteenth century, the tunes for these lyric songs were no longer sung. With the extinction of its musical component, ci gradually evolved into a purely literary genre. In spite of its popularity, amongst a repertoire of more than 20,000 song lyrics composed during the Song dynasty, only seventeen songs of the poet-musician Jiang Kui (c.1155-c.1221) survive in a decipherable music notation. Through exploration of a newly discovered manuscript copy of the long-lost 1202 edition of Jiang’s lyric song anthology, Baishi Daoren Gequ (The Collected Songs of Whitestone Daoist), my research project aims to elucidate a hitherto unnoticed musical form of the genre: the jindou form. A comparison between this newly discovered manuscript and all early modern editions of Jiang’s songs reveals discrepancies in the stanzaic divisions of four of the seventeen songs for which he provided musical notation. Employing musical analysis, this research project will argue that the opening line of the second stanza in all the early modern editions may well have been intentionally placed at the end of the first in the newly discovered manuscript in order to remind the singer of the jindou form, in which the cadential notes of the first stanza immediately repeat at the beginning of the second. Therefore, these “unusual” stanzaic divisions of the 1202 edition are not mistakes, but rather indications of conventional Song dynasty performance practice as dictated by musical factors. From this starting point, the wider aim of this study is discover a means for identifying occurrences of the jindou form in the myriad surviving manuscript copies of ci for which only the text survives, and to apply similar formulas to some of the 20,000 ci which fall into this category, thereby increasing our understanding of their musical structure, and even the meaning of the text itself. Potentially fruitful anthologies are: Juemiao Haoci, Yangchun Baixue, Hua’an Cixuan, Meiyuan, and Yuefu Yaci.

17602715.label: Realisation of objectives
17602715.value: 1. Using both versions of the zhuan tune in the two editions of the “Shilin guangji” as a point of departure, the jindou form was found to be present in both from the triple perspectives of rhyme, linguistic pitch-tones, and repetition of musical notes. Although a comparatively limited research reservoir from which to draw conclusions, its undeniable presence became the key for unlocking wider implications of the discovery. 2. Jiang Kui’s seventeen pieces for which musical notation survives was the first of these wider circles from which to investigate the presence of the jindou form. Of these seventeen, four furnished evidence as to its existence. A wider scholarly dissemination for this research was my T’oung Pao article that discussed in detail the degree and rigorousness with which the jindou form was applied in these four across an array of different manuscripts and early editions, and sought to evaluate the motives of the various editors that informed their decisions in this respect. 3. My book “Plum Blossom on the Far Side of the Stream” took the issue of canonicity in Jiang Kui’s ci by the horns and made the fullest possible examination of textual veracity across the whole of his oeuvre through a critical edition of the entire corpus that now forms a key component of the monograph. Using the methodology derived from examination of the seminal seventeen, three of his poems written to the cipai “Meifu”, “Yuexiadi”, and “Faquxianxianyin”, for which musical notation does not survive, can be shown to be undoubtedly essays in the jindou form. Crucial to this process were comparisons between stanzaic divisions as applied in bona fide manuscript copies of Song dynasty editions and their subsequent adulteration in early modern editions. Much of the confusion stems from over-reliance on a pair of Qing dynasty anthologies, the “Cilü” and the “Imperial Register of Ci” published in the reign of the Emperor Kangxi, yet both of these compilations were put together several centuries after the high noon of ci creative output and by which time knowledge and direct experience of the literary tradition had become seriously diluted. 4. Having explored Jiang Kui’s application of his jindou form across his entire output as it has come down to us, the fourth and final stage was to evaluate its presence across the whole corpus of Song dynasty ci. Again, it was the methodology of the previous research stage that provided the tools for unpicking the problems posed by the next, that is the compositions of other poets. Only exploration of anthologies compiled in the Song dynasty was likely to yield results, as the beating heart of the tradition still remained strong during this epoch. Of these collections, “Sunshine Spring and White Snow” compiled by Zhao Wenli (fl.1250) and “Surprisingly Fine Lyric Songs” put together by Zhou Mi have proved to be fertile ground. Ming dynasty manuscript copies of Yuan dynasty editions of both anthologies survive and preserve the vestiges of authentic practice before its violation at the hands early modern editors. So far, three cipai, “Suochuanghan”, “Liuchou”, and “Zhu Yingtai jin” can be identified as undoubtedly exhibiting jindou characteristics. Crucial to this process is defining what was authentic practice and what was not – no easy task – and the yardstick generated by the comprehensive sifting of Jiang Kui’s oeuvre has proved to be the only useful methodological tool that can be employed. The prevailing mindset of the early modern editors and even into the twentieth century was to regard the textual “discrepancies” that have indicated the jindou form simply as “scribal errors” whose presence was to be erased and the texts thus cleansed with the wisdom of hindsight. They seem, however, to have completely missed the point, and instead refined away the true aesthetic bedrock of the genre.

17602715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17602715.value: The major finding of this research is nothing less than a complete rethink of the ci as a musical rather than purely poetic form. The tool for attaining this has been exploration of the earliest primary sources for the genre, particularly those pertaining to its musical component, rather than the holier-than-thou early modern editions and their dry-as-dust literary obsessions (Part C, Section 8.1). From a textual perspective, the critical edition that compares eleven manuscripts and eleven early modern printed editions (Part C, Section 8.3, pp. 89-197) and the three facsimiles in “Plum Blossom on the Far Side of the Stream” (Part C, Section 8.3, pp. 189-386) roll out this hunt for urtext interpretations into all corners of Jiang Kui’s work. The historical component is to attempt to evaluate how and why all these processes happened and especially their relationship to the political and ethnographic tapestry of the times (Part C, Section 8.3, pp. 1-83).

17602715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17602715.value: Future directions include: from a horizontal or generic perspective, to compare, identify, and explore the whole pantheon of cipai and how formal patterns are deployed; and from a vertical or historic perspective, to take as a case study one of the four Jiang Kui ci that employs the jindou form, “Rainbow Skirt, Middle prelude, First Section”, and investigate its genesis; Jiang Kui himself indicates that the music for this composition had survived from the Tang dynasty. Having looked at the early history of ci, then to look at later survivals of the jindou form into the Ming dynasty, for example, clear instances of it occur in the opera “Xixiang ji”.

17602715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17602715.value: Re-evaluation of an artistic form from the standpoint of re-establishing authentic practice has been a fashionable trait in Western musicology for more than a century, and few would now argue with the reassertion of lively Baroque performance practice in small ensembles superseding the bloated, ponderous pseudo-solemnity of massed choirs and huge symphony orchestras. A similar mesh of methodologies has been applied here to Jiang Kui’s oeuvre, and the result has been to rediscover its formal identity, its textural veracity, and the historical reasons why these had became overlaid with so much unnecessary baggage. He emerges anew imbued with human energy as a genuine creative master of his craft, and no longer the screen on to which others’ aesthetic aspirations have been projected.

17602815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17602815.value: Private supplementary tutoring is commonly called 'shadow education', because it parallels and mimics official school systems: as the curriculum and scale of the mainstream change, so do the curriculum and scale of the shadow. In Shanghai, private tutoring has considerably expanded as the society has become more prosperous and competitive. Shadow education has attracted increasing public concern, but insufficient evidence exists on its conceptual significance and practical implications. This project will investigate the scale and nature of private tutoring in Shanghai, and implications of the relationship between private tutoring and mainstream schooling for equity, learning, and policies at school and system levels. It will focus on the secondary level of education. Much tutoring is received at earlier and later levels, but the dynamics are different. Data will be collected from students in Grades 9 and 12, which are transition points in the education system when private tutoring is of particular importance. Selection of these grades will parallel 2011-2013 research in Hong Kong, and thus will provide a basis for comparative analysis relevant not only to Shanghai but also to Hong Kong and more widely. The researchers will first solicit data from 1,680 students in a stratified sample of 24 schools. Data collected through questionnaires will be supplemented by interviews. The researchers will solicit information from students who do not receive tutoring as well as from those who do receive it. Parental perspectives will also be secured through questionnaires and interviews. Questions will include the reasons for seeking or not seeking tutoring, and the reasons for choosing particular types of tutoring. Next, the researchers will secure data from teachers. Tutoring may have a backwash on mainstream schooling, especially if teachers tutor their own students. In addition, tutoring may exacerbate diversity of learning achievements, which makes classroom teaching more problematic and thus affects other dynamics. The research is framed by the notion of ecologies of education. Teachers are key actors in the ecologies, and their perspectives and actions may have significant implications for the lives of students. The research will observe contextual elements in Shanghai which differ from those in Hong Kong. They include one-child families, and practices in which teachers tutor their own students. Other social, educational and economic factors will be compared to identify links between components which shape patterns and outcomes. The research will identify both positive and negative features of tutoring, and will provide policy lessons for stakeholders. 課外補習被廣泛成為“影子教育”，因其與主流教育並行并效仿主流教育系統：主流教育系統課程內容和規模發生變化時，課外補習也會發生相應變化。在上海經濟發展及競爭日趨激烈的同時課外補習也得以顯著擴張。公眾對影子教育的關注日趨增加，而對此現象的理論和實際影響的相關研究卻不夠充分。 此項目旨在調查上海影子教育的規模及性質，及其與主流教育系統間的相互作用對公平、學習、和學校及系統層面政策的啟示。不同教育階段的補習的動向各不相同。本研究主要關注9年級及12年級的學生，他們處於教育系統的升學節點，課外補習在這一階段尤為重要。這兩個年級將與2011-2013年的香港研究相呼應，為上海、香港甚至更廣泛地區的比較研究奠定基礎。 研究者會先對24所學校的1,680名學生進行問卷調查。進而通過訪談補充問卷數據。研究者對接受及沒有接受補習的學生都會進行訪談。研究也會通過也會通過訪談和問卷的方式調查家長視角。問題會包括是否安排補習以及選擇特定類型補習的原因。 研究還會向老師收集數據。課外補習對主流教育可能造成不良影響，在職教師為自己學生提供補習的情況尤為如此。此外，課外補習或會加劇學生學業成就差異，為教師教學造成困難而影響到其他動態因素。是項研究立足於教育生態學這一理論框架。 教師是教育生態中的關鍵群體，他們的視角及行為很可能對學生的生活產生至關重要的影響。研究將會觀察上海有別于香港的情境因素，包括獨生子女家庭以及教師的補習行為。研究還會比較其他社會、教育及經濟因素以識別補習模式與結果間的聯繫。研究會同時探索補習的正面及負面影響，并為教育持份者提供政策經驗與借鑒。

17602815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17602815.value: Private supplementary tutoring has developed as a major force parallel to the school system in China. The authorities are very ambivalent, seeing it as a mechanism to improve learning but also adding study burden and exacerbating social inequalities. The research has shed light on the phenomenon and on the complexities in policy responses. In the academic arena, the work has been recognized as having great significance and contributing to comparative understanding; and in the local and national policy arenas the PI and team members have contributed to refinement of policies on the theme.

17603215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603215.value: Since the mid-twentieth century, the question of balancing the scales of procedural and substantive justice in the context of judicial mediation has received significant attention beginning with the work of Owen Fiss and Lon Fuller. Recent work has highlighted the growing inefficiencies of civil litigation in economically advanced countries, while at the same time, caution is given to the potential denial of justice through exclusive reliance on settlement procedures. As a result of civil justice reforms throughout the world, mediation has gained greater significance and importance as a means of facilitating case disposition in both the East and West. As yet however, there has been limited, if any, comparative empirical work examining the impact of judicial mediation structure on perceptions of justice, efficiency and confidence in courts in a comparative context. This research project aims to fill this gap. Judicial mediation can take the form of: 1) court-mandated, 2) court-encouraged and 3) voluntary. The present project thus aims to fill an existing research gap by investigating whether, and if so how, variation in civil mediation policy (mandated, encouraged or voluntary) as one factor, affects variation in judicial efficiency, confidence in courts, and perceptions of justice. This is done by examining three selected court-centered mediation program-models in the following jurisdictions: Court-Mandated: (US Federal Courts, Singapore); Court-Encouraged: (UK, China, Hong Kong) and Voluntary: (Quebec) through a comparative triangulating research methodology drawing on surveys and selective interviews. It seeks to highlight positive lessons learned from these jurisdictions, analyze local circumstances, and distil best practices in the form of law and policy recommendations. 自二十世纪中叶起，欧文费斯（Owen Fiss）和朗富勒（Lon Fuller）的著作引起了对有关司法调解如何平衡程序和实质公义的问题的广泛关注。最近有关的学术工作突出了在经济发达的国家里，民事诉讼的效率每況愈下，同时，完全依赖争端解决程序而导致的潜在的司法不公亦值慎重考虑。 由於世界各地进行民事司法改革，以致於不论在东方或西方，调解作为促进案件处置的手段已经获得了更大的意义和重要性。然而，现时只有很少，甚至没有在比较的背景下分析司法结构对公义的观念，效率和人们对于法院的信任所带来的影响的实证比较研究。此研究项目旨在填补以上空隙。司法调解有以下形式：1）法院授权的，2）法院鼓励的，和3）自愿性的。由是，此项目的目的是通过研究民事调解政策（法院授权的，法院鼓励的，和自愿性的）的变化，作为一个因素是否会和，如是，如何影响公义的观念，效率和人们对于法院的信任，籍此去填补现有的研究空隙。此项目的研究方法是通过分析下列司法管辖区所代表的三个选定的以法院为中心而进行的调解的程序模式：法院授权的： （美国联邦法院、新加坡）;法院鼓励的：（英国、中国、香港）和自愿性的：（魁北克）。以上分析是透过利用调查结果和选择性采访，以及采用三角式的比较研究方法来完成。此项目旨在强调司法管辖区的成功的经验，分析当地情况，和筛选并提出与法律和政策建议有关的最佳做法。

17603215.label: Realisation of objectives
17603215.value: Each of the research objectives of this project has been achieved. They will be discussed in detail below: I. First Objective: To understand how and in what way the approach to civil mediation reform (court-mandated, encouraged, or voluntary) impacts the quality of the resolution process, including judicial efficiency, confidence in courts, and perceptions of justice in East Asian and Western contexts. The culminating output of the project, Court Mediation Reform: Efficiency, Confidence and Perceptions of Justice (Edward Elgar, 2018) provides an analysis of the impact of civil mediation approach on both intra and inter-state developments in the quality of the resolution process, including judicial efficiency, confidence in courts, and perceptions of justice in ten jurisdictions. According to one reviewer, Professor Luigi Cominelli, ‘Shahla Ali's work is an innovative meta-analysis of the trends in the institutionalization of mediation at the macro level. It has an ambitious approach that had not been attempted yet, and paves the way for other future research, as well as providing guidance to policy makers and professionals.’ II. Second Objective: To identify common and conflicting policies, approaches and principles of civil justice reform in relation to mediation case management and administration. This second objective is addressed in the Edward Elgar publication. According to one reviewer, Professor Carrie Menkel-Meadow: ‘Professor Shahla Ali has performed a valuable service for conflict resolution policy makers around the world. Providing diverse and mixed data reports of the uptake and resistance to court (and some private) mediation programs in ten different legal systems, she artfully surveys important legal, social and cultural differences in the uses and effectiveness of voluntary and mandatory mediation programmes. While some seek efficiency, others seek efficacy, through party-tailored solutions or regional integration dispute resolution schemes. Different programme motivations (and the varied role of lawyers) provide variation, not uniformity, in the use of mediation to resolve civil, family, labour and commercial disputes.’ III. Third Objective: To distil best practices in the form of civil justice reform recommendations. The final two chapters of the manuscript distill best practices in civil mediation reform drawing on country case studies and a survey of 83 mediation practitioners. According to Judge Dorothy Nelson, United States Court of Appeals 9th Circuit Judge, the ‘book offers the most comprehensive, qualitative study and insights on Global Court Mediation I have encountered. It should be in the hands of every court in the world.’ Scholarly contribution: The project resulted in 1 book (ranked A by RQF), 8 journal articles/book chapters and 1 under review with CJQ and 22 conference contributions.

17603215.label: Major findings and research outcome
17603215.value: The principal finding of the 10 country case studies, survey research and analysis of civil justice indicators indicate that overall, while both voluntary and mandatory mediation programs demonstrate unique programmatic strengths and are associated with positive gains in the advancement of civil justice quality over a five year period since implementation, sampled voluntary mediation program regions are associated with a slightly higher proportion of longitudinal advancement in levels of efficiency, and perceptions of justice with a nearly equal proportion of advancement in levels of confidence, and an identical proportion of voluntary and mandatory regions experiencing positive advancement in the sub-categories of impartial and effective ADR. Comparative t-test analysis of a non-generalizable small-n 12 country comparison of 2016 civil justice indicators similarly suggest that sampled countries implementing voluntary court mediation programs on average are associated with statistically significantly higher jurisdictional scores for efficiency and non-discrimination with higher, though non-significant difference with respect to the quality of civil justice, effective enforcement, accessibility and affordability and impartiality and effectiveness between voluntary and mandatory mediation systems. To some extent, such findings correspond with insights from ‘nudge theory’ suggesting that non-forced compliance is at least as effective as directions issued through court rules. At the same time, robust encouragement of mediation coupled with high quality mediators and supportive infrastructure can, in appropriate contexts, particularly those charachterized by relationships of ‘heavy interdependence,’ assist individuals, the wider community and judiciaries to achieve high quality outcomes. Correlation of changes in civil justice systems and perceptions of efficiency, justice and confidence over time are not a sign of a causal relationship. With respect to the analysis of 83 open ended survey responses, the findings suggest that while, slight variation exists such that practitioners report higher levels of confidence in mandatory mediation programs (70%) as opposed to voluntary programs (64%), and higher perceptions of efficiency with respect to voluntary programs (77%) as opposed to mandatory programs (68%), both regard voluntary (81%) and mandatory (82%) mediation programs with relatively equal perceptions of fairness. With respect to advancing program quality, the survey findings provide insights into the dynamics, challenges and lessons learned from the perspective of those directly engaged in the work of administering, representing and mediating civil claims. The findings echo insights from socio-legal scholars that, “facilitation and encouragement together with selective and appropriate pressure are likely to be more effective and possibly more efficient than blanket coercion to mediate.”

17603215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17603215.value: There is a strong potential for further development of the research. In particular, much remains to be examined including the need for more in-depth qualitative studies examining intra-mediation program variation and how mediator and participant training interact with the development of surrounding mediation culture and the advancement of social justice including the development of safeguards against bias and the promotion of enhanced cohesion. Future studies by a growing number of researchers will no doubt contribute insights to the advancement of such understanding.

17603215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17603215.value: As judiciaries advance, exploring how court mediation programs can provide opportunities for party-directed reconciliation whilst ensuring access to formal legal channels requires careful investigation. This project explores comparative empirical findings in order to examine the association between court mediation structure and perceptions of justice, efficiency and confidence in courts. This unique study draws on an eighty-three person survey as well as case studies from ten global mediation jurisdictions including Australia, France, Hong Kong, India, and the United States. Given the highly contextual nature of court mediation programs, the project highlights the achievements, challenges and lessons learned in the implementation of mediation programs for general civil claims. In so doing, the study identifies that positive achievements are largely dependent on multiple factors including the functioning of the civil litigation system, the capacities of the mediators, safeguards against bias, participant education, and cultural and institutional support. Findings of the project will be of use to judiciaries and policy makers looking to advance court mediation programs.

17603815.label: Project Objectives
17603815.value: To characterize the acoustic characteristics of child-directed Cantonese tones To examine the developmental differences in child-directed Cantonese tones To test the acoustic cue hypothesis and the pragmatic hypothesis of child-directed speech

17603815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603815.value: Adults and children in different cultures and countries unconsciously modify their speech to young children. One of the most prominent acoustic features of child-directed speech (CDS) is higher pitch and more varied pitch contours. Most studies support that CDS promotes speech and language learning in young children. However, how acoustic modifications in CDS facilitate speech acquisition is less clear. Different hypotheses have been formulated. The acoustic cue hypothesis postulates that CDS makes use of the acoustic information to maximize phonetic contrasts and provide more salient acoustic cues for phoneme discrimination to promote speech and language acquisition. The pragmatic hypothesis proposes that the acoustic modifications in CDS are to express positive affect and regulate the child’s attention, which foster maternal-infant bonding, sustain and encourage interactions, and, thus, enhance speech and language development. The two hypotheses of CDS can be tested by examining the use of pitch in Cantonese. Cantonese is a tone language that uses pitch for both phonemic contrasts and pragmatic purposes. Cantonese has a complex tone system with three level tones, two rising tones and a falling tone. The tones that have similar pitch contour shapes but different pitch height are confusable even for native Cantonese-speaking adults. The proposed study will measure the perceptual accuracy and the acoustic characteristics in monosyllabic tones directed to adults and to children between the ages of one to five years to characterize Cantonese tones in child-directed and adult-directed speech and to examine the developmental changes in child-directed tones. If the pragmatic hypothesis is supported, we expect to observe that the tones in CDS will be produced with higher and more varied pitch. There may be distortions in the pitch contours for the tones due to the use of pitch to convey pragmatic meanings. If the acoustic cue hypothesis is supported, we expect to see higher perceptual accuracy, and larger distance between tones with similar contour shapes in CDS than in ADS. The results will provide detailed acoustic information on adult-directed and child-directed Cantonese tones and shed light on the nature and function of acoustic modifications of CDS and strategies adults use to enhance speech and language learning in young children. The findings will have implications on strategies to promote speech and language learning in typically developing children and children with developmental disorders and will shape theories of early child speech language acquisition and intervention strategies in child language acquisition. 世界各地的人在與幼兒對話時都會不自覺地改變他們的說話方式，例如會提高音調及加強音調的變化，這種說話方式被稱為「兒童導向話語」，不少研究報告都認為「兒童導向話語」有助孩子的語言發展。然而，我們仍未清楚了解到為何會出現這種說話方式的改變。 現時我們有以下兩個說法去解釋這種改變的原因。第一，成人想透過加強語音對比去教導孩子不同字的語音分别，從而協助孩子學習語言。第二，成人想加強情感表達，透過明顯的語音變化去吸引孩子的注意，增強成人與孩子間的關係及促進交流，從而促進孩子的語言發展。 透過測試粵語聲調的改變，我們可以了解以上哪個說法會較能解釋到「兒童導向話語」的真正目的。粵語一共分為六個聲調，其中三個為平調，例如「思」、「試」和「事」，它們的音調變化皆為平調，但音調高低不同。是次研究會透過語音分析和聲調判斷，比較媽媽與成人及孩子對話時，單聲字的聲調特徵，從而了解在與成人及幼兒對話時，改變音調的目的。 假如成人是想透過加強語音對比去教導孩子不同字的語音分别，我們預計成人會加強音調高低的差距，而不會改變音調變化。如果成人是想加強情感表達，則會改變音調變化，因此他人會更大機會錯誤理解本字的聲調。 總括而言，是次研究希望透過廣東話聲調了解「兒童導向話語」的目的。從而建議成人可如何協助一般或有發展障礙的幼兒學習語言。

17603815.label: Realisation of objectives
17603815.value: Objective 1. To characterize the acoustic characteristics of child-directed Cantonese tones Sixty-two mother-child dyads produced 42 monosyllabic words (30 familiar words and 12 unfamiliar words to children) in four conditions: (1) to an adult in isolation, (2) to their child in isolation, (3) to an adult in sentence final position, and (4) to their child in sentence final position. Following the procedures in our previous acoustic studies (Wong, 2012; Wong et al., 2017), the 8634 words produced by the mothers were excise to save in single files, low-pass filtered, segmented, and checked for each vocal pulse. To compare the acoustic differences in tones produced in the four different conditions, ten acoustic parameters were measured for each production and submitted for statistical analysis. Objective 2. To examine the developmental differences in child-directed Cantonese tones Of the 62 children who participated in the study, there were sixteen 1-year-olds, sixteen 2-year-olds, fifteen 3-year-olds, and fifteen 5-year-olds. Developmental differences on the acoustics of child directed speech were determined by the correlational analysis between children’s age and the eight selected acoustic parameters for each tone for each of the four production conditions. Objective 3. To test the acoustic cue and pragmatic hypotheses on the role of child-directed speech Five native Cantonese speakers listened to the mothers’ 8634 productions in to adults and children in the two sentence position conditions (isolation vs. sentence final). The judges’ accuracy rates in identifying the tones in the four conditions were statistically compared to determine if tones produced in child-directed conditions were more accurate than in adult-directed conditions. The acoustic differences and perceptual accuracy of the tones in child-directed speech in isolation (register effect of tone production) and in adult-directed sentence final position (prosodic effect of tone production) were compared to determine whether child-directed speech was a prosodic effect.

17603815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17603815.value: 1. Acoustically, child-directed Cantonese tones were produced with higher pitch. Cantonese tones in sentence final prosody were produced with lower pitch. 2. The degree of pitch elevation in child-directed tones decreased as the children got older, showing developmental children of child-directed speech. Mothers continue to acoustically modify the tones produced toward five-year-old children. 3. Tones produced in child-directed speech were less accurate than tones produced in adult-directed speech, and mothers did not increase the acoustic contrasts to help children distinguishing more easily confusing tones (e.g., mid-level and low-level tones). These findings do not support the acoustic cue hypothesis. 4. Acoustic characteristics and judgment errors in child-directed tones mirrored those of tones produced with sentence final prosody. Together with point 3 above, the findings support that child-directed speech is a prosodic effect. Mothers modify the acoustics in child-directed speech to serve pragmatic functions. These findings have been published in the Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research, a journal ranked 10/58 or Q1 in Health Profession Speech and Hearing (SCI).

17603815.value: Several follow-up studies can be pursued 1. What pragmatic functions does child-directed speech serve? 2. Why are young children attracted to child-directed speech? 3. The effect of child-directed speech on speech and language acquisition in children

17603815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17603815.value: Adults and children speak to young children differently. They tend to speak with a higher and more varied pitch. This study determined the accuracy and measured the acoustic differences of the six Cantonese tones produced in 8634 words to one- to five-year-old children and adults. Comparing to the same tones produced to adults, when the mothers spoke to young children, they raised and changed the pitch of the Cantonese tones, making the tones in child-directed speech more difficult to identify. The degree of acoustic modifications in child-directed speech decreased as the children were older. The findings showed that mothers used child-directed speech to address children as old as five years of age. The younger the child, the more the mother changed the pitch in their speech to the child. Unlike what previous studies have suggested, mothers did not use child-directed speech to exaggerate the speech sounds to make them more distinguishable from each other for children to learn. Mothers’ acoustically modification in their speech to young children appear to serve pragmatic functions, such as seeking attention, showing affection, and expressing feelings, which sometimes compromised accurate production of lexical tones.

17604015.label: Project Objectives
17604015.value: Examine how members of the academic profession in Hong Kong, especially junior academics, are responding to the glacial shifts in higher education since 2007, including Hong Kong’s curriculum and structural reform, and increase in non-local students and international students. 17604015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17604015.value: This research supports Hong Kong’s third participation (1993, 2007, 2016) in the international survey of the academic profession. The third international study will investigate the academic profession with a planned 20 country survey after nearly a decade of change in the professional practices and academic values and attitudes. The conceptual underpinning of the international survey will capture the academic profession’s responses to the glacial shifts in higher education that includes a stronger emphasis on relevance, academic governance and internationalization. The Hong Kong portion of the third international survey will emphasize how the academic profession has adapted to changes associated with the recent transformation to a four-year undergraduate university system with a newly designed curriculum component that aims to broaden students’ capacity for critical thinking, problem-solving, and creativity. Special attention will be placed on junior academics because they will become a key part of knowledge production and undergraduate teaching for Hong Kong in the years to come. Beyond facilitating a profound investigation of the Hong Kong academic profession as it relates to such important issues as relevance, management, and internationalization, this research will establish the association of academics’ personal characteristics and institutional factors with their teaching and research activities, and subsequently, with their organizational commitment, and psychological well-being. Results of this research will permit a more nuanced understanding of how the Hong Kong academic profession and its international counterparts are responding in similar or different ways to global changes in higher education. The Hong Kong data will also be selectively consolidated with items of interest from the data sets of the first and second international surveys in order to establish key trends concerning changes in the nature of the academic profession. Finally the research will identify specific ways in which the academic profession in Hong Kong can better serve the new university curriculum structure while producing relevant research for Hong Kong’s economic and social development, manage work stress, and improve job satisfaction and organizational commitment.

17604015.label: Realisation of objectives
17604015.value: The first objective has been completely achieved through the publication of at least three top-tier journal articles. In the first one, we examined how Hong Kong academics’ perceptions of their work environment (an increasingly more competitive and performance-oriented higher education context) affected their levels of stress and organizational commitment as well as how academics’ stress levels influenced their organizational commitment. In the second study, we investigated how academics’ perceived increasingly higher levels of institutional expectations towards research and teaching contributed to their job satisfaction. We looked into how their self-efficacy in teaching and research buffeted the effects of perceived challenges of their work environment on their job satisfaction. In the third study, we examined how academics’ perceived independence in research and institutional expectations regarding external funding were related to their collaborations with their doctoral students. The second objective has also been completely achieved in that the various relationships proposed in our conceptual model have been tested and our findings have been published in a number of top-tier journal articles. For example, in addition to the three studies just mentioned (which also contributed to the achievement of the second research objective), a fourth study explored the relationship between teaching and research activities, with academics’ self-efficacy in teaching and research considered – and with their demographics and institutional factors taken into account. As another example, in the third study previously mentioned, we also examined how academics’ own ways of thinking affected their collaborations with their doctoral students. The third objective has also been largely achieved. We have examined the three data sets (1993, 2007, 2018) resulting from the three international investigations in which Hong Kong participated and presented some key findings at the Hiroshima conference in March 2019. Findings concerned trends regarding Hong Kong academics’ teaching and research activities. At the same time, by attending the conference talks given by members of research teams from more than 20 other jurisdictions, we identified some notable similarities and differences between Hong Kong academics and academics from other jurisdictions. However, because we have not received the compiled international dataset of this project, we have not been able to conduct any direct comparison between Hong Kong data and data from other jurisdictions. It is in this sense that the third objective has not been completely achieved. Once we receive the compiled international dataset, we would like to make some direct comparisons between Hong Kong academics and academics in selected jurisdictions and to disseminate the research findings via both writing for publications and speaking at conferences, seminars, and workshops.

17604015.label: Major findings and research outcome
17604015.value: The wide range of research findings disseminated through the research outputs mentioned in Part C of this report can be summarized into five key findings: First, Hong Kong academics’ perceptions of their work environment played a critical role not only in their academic activities such as collaboration with doctoral students (*Jung, Horta, Zhang, & Postiglione; manuscript under second revision), but also in their psychological well-being such as job satisfaction (Zhang, Fu, & Li, 2020) and occupational stress (Horta et al., 2019). Second, Hong Kong academics’ psychological well-being has a significant impact on their organizational commitment (Horta et. al, 2019; see also, Zhang, 2019 – a publication resulted from a pilot test in preparation for the Hong Kong survey and one that has acknowledged the support of this GRF). Specifically, academics’ stress and emotions in teaching significantly contributed to their organizational commitment. Third, academics’ belief in their success in teaching and research played a significant mediating role not only in the relationship between their research and teaching activities (Zhang, Horta, Jung, & Postiglione, 2020) but also in the relationship between their perceived work environment and job satisfaction (Zhang, Fu, & Li, 2020). Fourth, demographics (e.g., gender, academic rank, institutional ranking, and academic discipline) could make a significant difference in the findings mentioned in the above three points (see all research outputs reported in Part C). Fifth, based on the three sets of Hong Kong data (1993, 2007, 2018), six key trends have been identified: 1) over the three time points, academics have been working increasingly harder as indicated by the number of hours spent on academic activities, particularly on teaching and research; 2) within the time spent on teaching and research, academics have significantly increased their time on research, but significantly reduced their time on teaching activities over the last 25 years; 3) there was also a significant increase in academics’ preference for research over teaching; 4) of the academics from the eight UGC-funded institutions in Hong Kong, those from top-tier universities indicated a significantly stronger belief that their research activities reinforced their teaching than did academics from second-tier universities; 5) compared with academics in the other participating jurisdictions, Hong Kong academics reported significantly longer working hours; and 6) across the board (among the great majority of participating jurisdictions), academics indicated a stronger preference for research over teaching.

17604015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17604015.value: Given that all three international studies (1993, 2007, and 2018) adopted survey questionnaires, it would be good if follow-up studies would include a qualitative component. In this way, not only could researchers better explain the quantitative findings, but also they could achieve a much deeper understanding of the changing academic profession in the knowledge society. Furthermore, the conceptual framework developed by our Hong Kong team members has great promise in playing a fundamental role in the next international study. There has been some preliminary discussion among international leaders of the third international study (including the PI of this HK study) that the fourth international study will most likely take place in the year 2022. The Hong Kong team has already begun to prepare for the next international study by involving new blood in the team – both Dr. Horta and Dr. Jung have been working with the investigators of this project (as demonstrated in our joint research outputs).

17604015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17604015.value: Known as the “Academic Profession in the Knowledge-based Society” project, this is the third international survey in which Hong Kong has participated. Academic researchers from more than 20 jurisdictions collaborated on this project, each jurisdiction team having collected their own data. In 1993, Hong Kong took part in “The First International Survey of the Academic Profession” conducted by the Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching. In 2007, Hong Kong participated in “The Second International Survey of the Academic Profession” conducted by an international consortium of 20 educational systems. These international surveys help to raise the visibility of the Hong Kong academic profession and to gauge comparative changes with academics in other countries/educational systems. Research findings not only have enriched the literature on the academic profession and that on psychology but also have practical implications for both academics and university senior managers. With a good understanding of the research findings, academics could enhance the quality of their academic activities, while university senior managers could create a more congenial work environment for academics.

17604915.value: 人的一生中有不少重大生活事件(如喪親、大病、婚姻、學業事業上的失敗等)。許多研究都探討這些生活事件如何影響情緒狀態，壓力和健康。在這個研究項目中，我們探討兩個特殊的生活事件(喪親之痛和宗教皈依)是否有更長遠的影響，甚至可以改變我們的性格和價值觀。 人格特質。我們將測試喪親是否加快或阻礙如情緒穩定等的人格特質之發展。我們又將按照Paloutzian等人（1999）的建議，以前瞻性方法研究宗教皈依會否使人之某些個性特徵有深遠的變化。 個人價值。個人價值往往被視為穩定不變。但近期有人觀察到中學畢業和移民會改變一個人的價值觀。然而，我們尚未了解喪親對價值變化的影響。為了填補這一空白，我們將研究喪親和宗教皈依會否加強了仁愛慈悲一類的自我超越價值觀，並削弱了權力和成就一類的自我增強的價值觀。 互動效果。喪親和宗教皈依對個性和個人價值的影響力，可能依賴或受制於其他因素。在這個項目中，我們將研究兩個因素：對命運的信念，以及對世界的樂觀/悲觀。我們也將探討倘若喪親和宗教皈依或其他生活事件同時發生，個性和個人價值會否受到更大或較小的影響。 總結。本項目的主要目的是要了解喪親和轉換宗教可能會在中期和長期對性格和價值觀的影響。這個領域尚未吸引研究人員的注意。第二個目的是為我們和其他研究人員建立一個數據庫，以進一步探索更廣泛的問題：什麼生活事件會在什麼情況下改變一個人的哪些方面？為了實現以上目標，我們會在過去五年所建立的一個縱向數據庫的基礎上，多收集兩波調查數據。有了這七波由大學生樣本和社區樣本組成的數據集，我們便能夠回答上面提出的研究問題。

17604915.label: Realisation of objectives
17604915.value: Objective 1: To understand how bereavement may affect changes in personality and personal values. Over several waves of data we identified individuals who were bereaved, and also extracted a comparison sample of non-bereaved individuals matched on demographics. To determine if personality traits and personal values are malleable due to this life event, we examined changes in both the mean levels and rank order of the outcome variables, and whether the changes are related to each other. Specifically, we conducted a MANOVA on the outcome variables. Results showed effect of time, but no time x bereavement status interaction effect. (http://www.my-research.net/HKU/analysis/Sing/2_Bereavement/manova1.htm). This allows us to reject the Hypothesis 3 in our proposal, that “bereavement would result in the emphasis of such self-transcendent values of benevolence, but weaken self-enhancing values of power and achievement.” We explored further, and found no time x high vs. low impact of bereavement interaction effect. In our examination of rank order instability, however, we found that emotional stability and self-direction were affected by the life event. (http://www.my-research.net/HKU/analysis/Sing/2_Bereavement/A8_IPIP.htm) (http://www.my-research.net/HKU/analysis/Sing/2_Bereavement/A8_SVS.htm) The above analyses and a series of supplementary analyses showed that bereavement has deleterious effect on a subset of personality traits and personal values for some people but not others. This is relevant to the pair of competing hypotheses (H1a and H1b) we stated in the proposal. We demonstrated that both “the rate of increase in emotional stability would be slower among those who have recently lost a loved one, than among those who have not,” and “the rate of increase in emotional stability among those who have recently lost a loved one would be faster than (or at least similar to) that found among people who have not” can be true. With respect to Hypotheses 5 and 6, we found that the effect of bereavement on personality and values would not become any stronger among those who hold strong fate control belief nor pessimistic attributional style. Objective 2: To understand how religious conversion may affect changes in personality and personal values. We extracted data from waves that would give us the greatest statistical power, and compared pre- and post- conversion measures of personality traits and personal values. We are now able to conclude that religious conversion does not have much detectable effects on personality, thus rejecting Hypothesis 2, that “the rate of change in personality traits among people who have recently undergone religious conversion would be different from that among people who did not have a religious conversion.” However, this life event would alter people’s value orientations. In the proposal we postulated Hypothesis 4 that “religious conversion would result in the emphasis of such self-transcendent values of benevolence, but weaken self-enhancing values of power and achievement.” This hypothesis now receives support. Objective 3: To understand whether the effects of the above two life events may be moderated by other factors. In many of our analyses we included as moderators the belief in fate control and optimism/pessimism. For example, we proposed a pair of competing hypotheses: (a) A strong belief in fate control would aggravate the detrimental effects of bereavement on depressive moods, anxiety, and stress. (b) A strong belief in fate control would buffer the detrimental effects of bereavement on depressive moods, anxiety, and stress. To test these hypotheses, we tried to fit several latent growth models (LGM). The first LGMs used were ones with a latent intercept factor and a latent linear growth factor, but no predictor for either latent factors. A latent quadratic growth factor was then added. Demographic predictors of latent factors were introduced next, followed by bereavement status and fate control as predictors, and lastly by the interaction between bereavement status and fate control as predictor. Sequential model comparisons suggested the quadratic growth model of depressive mood with an interaction effect between bereavement status and fate control as the best fitting model. This shows that the effect of bereavement is moderated by a belief in fate control. Other variables such as demographics, personality, and wellbeing were also included as moderators in certain analyses. Our analyses have not exhausted all variables and all combinations of these variables that were measured in the project. For that reason we consider this objective only partially achieved. We shall continue to look for boundary conditions under which personality and personal values may or may not change due to the occurrence of these two life events. Objective 4: To build a 7-wave panel database for further exploration of how over 20 life events, 5 personality traits, and 10 personal values may be related to each other. We have cleaned and anonymized the data. We have also produced a codebook and a set of syntax files. These materials are archived, and are available upon request to researchers local and overseas interested in using the data for their own research agenda. We are also in the process of conducting some exploratory analyses with the dataset.

17604915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17604915.value: Bereavement The loss of a loved one did not alter the mean level in personality, values, and social axioms measured about two years later. It did, however, alter the participants’ rank-ordering on emotional stability and self-direction value. Specifically, whether a bereaved person’s emotional stability would increase depended not on the perceived severity of the loss, but on age, low initial level of psychological symptoms, as well as sleep quality. Whether the self-direction value would be weakened depended on age and the use of religious coping. Furthermore, the stronger was the perceived severity of the loss, the greater was the negative impact on agreeableness. The perceived severity of the loss also interacted with age in influencing fate control, stimulation, hedonism, achievement, and the value dimension of “openness to change”. There was no immediate effect of bereavement on well-being outcomes. However, the loss of a loved one had negative effect on physical quality of life and stress two years later. Furthermore, the stronger was the perceived severity of the loss, the greater was the negative impact on sleep quality two years later. The effects of bereavement changed over time. Latent growth modeling showed that the bereaved people’s mood trajectory depended on whether they believed in fate. In particular, there was an interaction effect between bereavement status and fate control on the latent linear growth factor, and also on the latent quadratic growth factor, of depressive mood. The harmful effects of holding a strong belief in fate control were aggravated by bereavement. Religious conversion Using the convert sample and a matched sample of individuals who had been Christians throughout the study, and a matched sample of non-believers who remained so throughout the study, we found that converted people were transformed not in personality but in symptoms of stress and anxiety, as well as several personal values, including benevolence, achievement, and conformity. Results also suggested a directional effect of conversion on forgivingness. Fate control belief and stimulation value increased more and religiosity social axiom declined more among the religious deconverts (or faith exiters) than among those who stayed in faith. Latent growth mixture modeling indicated that about half of the faith exiters would initially experience an improvement in psychological symptoms, and the other half a deterioration. Poor quality of life at baseline was a risk factor for increase in psychological symptoms post-exit. Changes in psychological symptoms after faith exit can be multi-trajectory.

17604915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17604915.value: The current project provided additional information on how some life events affect human functioning beyond being stressors. Although most life events cannot be manipulated, practitioners would find knowledge gained useful for helping people thrive. Future research should examine how these life events are associated with human thriving. We had also intended to determine the joint effects of these two life events with other major life events. Contrary to our expectation, there were very few people who had experienced these life events with another major event during the past year. Thus we were not able to pursue this supplementary research question. Future research should consider using an even larger sample in order to capture the effects of the co-occurrence of major life events.

17604915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17604915.value: Bereavement is a highly negative and yet unavoidable life event for most people. Religious conversion is less frequent. It is a sharp and rapid change from having no religion to having a religion, or from being affiliated with one religion to being affiliated with another. Contrary to common beliefs, bereavement alters some but not all personality and values. Emotional stability increases for those who are older and have little psychological symptoms initially. It declines for those who are younger and psychologically less well. Whether the self-direction value would be weakened depends on age and the use of religious coping. Bereavement has negative effect on wellbeing two years later. The stronger is the perceived severity of the loss, the greater is the negative impact. The harmful effects of holding a strong belief in fate control are aggravated by bereavement. People who undergo religious conversion are transformed in forgivingness, symptoms of stress and anxiety, as well as several personal values, including benevolence, achievement, and conformity. The current project is important as it shows that personality and values are fairly stable, and yet life events can change some. It provides the knowledge base for practitioners to help people thrive amidst their life circumstances.

To understand both the enablers and barriers to women’s career progression, and entry to senior leadership roles, in Hong Kong.
