17609515.value: The Mercer Quality of Living Index shows a correlation between the liveability of a city and its ability to support a society of excellence. Hong Kong ranks sixth in the 2012 Mercer Infrastructure Ranking, but is well outside the top 50 on the same Quality of Living Ranking. One of the critical and highly visible areas of liveability is the amount of green available to a city, which is also the reason why Chinese cities have implemented a hard rule of a fixed green ratio in all new urban developments, as a shortcut to attaining green city status. However, much urban landscape in China quickly falls into disrepair and where the will and fiscal revenue is available to support highly green urbanscapes, as in Singapore, the costs can become unsustainable. This research takes a new look at the idea of productive agricultural urban green space and asks whether HK can develop an innovative sustainable greening model. The innovative nature of the proposed model is its linking up of community, technology and property rights. The project is suitably and innovatively located jointly in the Department of Architecture, the Division of Landscape Architecture and the HKU Ronald Coase Centre for Property Rights Research. This research has the following aims: 1. Identify and survey workable pockets of private and public land, and multi-level surfaces for cultivation within the pilot study area in the Western District of Hong Kong (Sheung Wan, Sai Ying Pun and Pokfulam). Propose a network of spaces that permeates through the urban farms, in order for communities to flourish around them. 2. Focus on planning feasibility in accessibility, circulation, solar orientation, and waste management, using established engineering solutions for high-intensity food cultivation. This pilot area must demonstrate complex traits in both physical and social terms, combining high-tech and traditional farming methods, in order for it to benefit the rest of Hong Kong, once success is demonstrated on some levels. 3. Investigate the institutional mechanisms that allow the blending of private property rights, public property rights and common rights necessary to make systematic urban agriculture a reality. 4. Position Hong Kong in a unique position in the discourse of food urbanism, by virtue of its particular model of engineering land-technology-property rights for improved food security, and increased land utility. 5. Demonstrate the role of design and planning in overcoming the typically binding contraints of urban agricultural development, and thereby creating win-win-win (private-public-communal) gains in urban environments. 美世生活質素調查顯示，城市宜居性與其維持社會競爭力息息相關。於2012年度調查中，香港的基建排行第六，但整體生活質素中排行五十名以外。城市的綠化面積是其宜居性其中一個重要並可見的範疇，這亦是中國城市嚴格規管發展項目綠化率以達至「綠色城市」之稱的原因。可是，中國大部分城市地貌迅速失修；而即使綠化城市地貌如新加坡般得到政策上及財政上的支持，亦因成本高昂而變得不可持續。 這研究項目重新審視都市農業生產綠化概念，並提出香港發展創新的可持續綠化模式的可行性。提案的創新性在於其連繫社區、科技及產業權益。此研究項目以港島西區作為試點，尋找並調查區內具農業價值的政府及私人土地以及高層樓面，並提出一個貫穿城市農地的空間系統，以促進農業團體及社區發展。研究集中討論城市規劃上的可行性，包括流動性、可達性、日照及廢物處理；以及為促進系統性都市農業發展所需的私人、公家、及公眾業權共融政策及機制。為改善本土糧食安全及優化土地利用，香港必須於城市糧食規劃的論述中確立其取態。

17609915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17609915.value: The poetry of Li Shangyin李商隱 (c. 813 – 858) seems to be at once the most translatable and the least translatable of Chinese literature into English, and for the same reason—namely, its poetic difficulty or “obscurity.” On the one hand, the intricacy of Li’s language and the abstruseness of his allusions place a high demand on the translator, who must not only understand these elements of the poetry but then recreate them in another language; on the other hand, readers of poetry in English have become accustomed over the last century to erudite and recondite diction, and no longer let not understanding a poem get in the way of appreciating it. My project will examine this apparent contradiction by looking at the ethics and aesthetics of poetic difficulty in light of translation and translatability in four ways: (1) I will explain the ways in which poetic difficulty in English can trace much of its lineage to the poetic presentation of China via translation of Chinese poetry (even when such translations themselves are straightforward and accessible, as in versions by Ezra Pound, Kenneth Rexroth, Gary Snyder, and so forth); (2) I will contextualize the matter of poetic difficulty in both the late Tang when Li was writing, as well as in the Northern Song when his poetry first received wide acclaim and was inspirational to successive generations of poets (later known as the Xikun poets for their appearance in the anthology Xikun chouchang ji 西崑酬唱集); (3) I will extract from these contexts of poetic difficulty conclusions about the relationship between poetry and the society in which it is produced and read, considering poetry as a commentary on its own place in the politico-economic power structure of its time; (4) I will enumerate certain techniques for the translation of Li Shangyin and other allusive and elusive poetry, highlighting methods in which innovations of translation technique in English can draw attention to what was new and noteworthy about the source texts at the moment of their origin. Overall, this project will seek to move the conversation from whether poetry can be translated to a consideration of how it should be translated in light of demands on the translator both of knowledge of the source text and performance in the target language. 從翻譯學的角度來看，李商隱的詩歌翻譯既難又易，這則是因為其詩歌本身的文學性和英文翻譯的特性兩者間的微妙關係而決定的。李商隱詩歌中存在大量的典故,辭藻華麗,這對譯者的文學功底提出了較高的要求；亦是，英文現代詩歌的讀者大多早已習慣英語文學中存在的隱晦難點，因此不會過度拆解譯文本身存在的隱晦。我的這個課題將會針對翻譯中存在的這一矛盾對立進行研究：包括證明今天英文詩歌中的隱晦難點是由於早期中文詩歌翻譯所產生的；我還將把晚唐詩史的隱晦風格，同北宋時期模仿他詩作的西昆體詩人在兩個不同語境下分析李商隱詩歌的隱晦難點；進而，詩歌中存在的各種隱晦難點與當下社會間的關聯；最後，我將繼續在這個結論上總結提出若干對此類隱晦難點翻譯文學的實用方法。我希望可以通過這一課題研究達到更深層次上的文學應用翻譯探討，且在這一過程中重新對譯者和原文的認知及譯文和語言表達的雙重探討。

17609915.label: Realisation of objectives
17609915.value: I believe that my project achieved my research objectives; I will delineate my achievements in reverse order: 5. My outputs and my still-in-progress write-ups address pertinent questions in literary studies, not only relating to "modernity," but also to "modernism" (and "postmodernism") as well as larger, or at least more trans-historical concepts such as poetic difficulty. 4. I have made arguments for commensurability between cultures and across times, suggesting that there are no eternal strategy that will always show cultures to be able to communicate with each other, but rather individual and historically or contextually located strategies. 3. Along such lines, I have (esp. in my paper "Dislocating Language into Meaning") demonstrated the role of these strategies, under the name of "cultural translatability," in creating new aesthetic effects and norms such as "poetic difficulty"; an in-progress article continues my elaboration on these notions. 2 & 1. With such aesthetic effects and norms as "poetic difficulty" in mind, then, I have begun to lay a theoretical and philological groundwork for translating Li Shangyin into English.

17609915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17609915.value: As suggested above, my major findings are, in line with my hypotheses, that translation of culturally important yet difficult (or, difficult yet culturally important) poetry is possible. Not only has translation from Chinese to English (and, more broadly, the representation in English poetry of Chinese language and culture) contributed to the development of the aesthetic of poetic difficulty in English (see "Dislocating Language into Meaning"), but the existence of such aesthetics can also be redeployed to bring in elements of difficult Chinese poetry into English (see "Pseudo-Pseudotranslation"). The awareness of the way that translation--and particularly translation from Chinese--has helped shape poetic difficulty in English can also inspire us to new ways of understanding the role of cultural translation in the writing and codification of the difficult Chinese poetry in the first place. In other words, the ways Li Shangyin's poetry was written and canonized in the late Tang and Northern Song, respectively, owes much to cultural translation (see relevant sections of The Organization of Distance and forthcoming publications, based on my MLA presentation); this perspective would be hard to reach without a more comparative, translational understanding of contemporary literature. Of course, bringing difficult premodern poetry into the contemporary context is not the same as bringing contemporary difficult poetry from Chinese to English (see "Strong and Weak Interpretation"). Further examples can be seen in my published translations of Li Shangyin in Chloe Garcia Roberts, ed., Li Shangyin (NYRB).

17609915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17609915.value: With my findings in mind, I and others can have surer footing in endeavoring on the translation of difficult poetry such as Li Shangyin. Not only that, there is much, much more to be said about the ethics of translation vis-a-vis broader questions of cross-cultural representation. This second set of questions has inspired my next GRF application, Journeys to the East: China in Western Literature and Translation.

17609915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17609915.value: Is translation of poetry possible, even difficult poetry from centuries ago such as Li Shangyin's? Yes. It is possible because difficult poetry exists in both contemporary English and premodern Chinese. These different kinds of difficulty are not only similar to each other, they can be shown to have caused each other in various ways. Awareness of the ways that they have caused each other can lay groundwork for further translations, offering new insight into Li Shangyin's poetry in the process.

17610215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610215.value: As the world moves towards knowledge-based economies, increased emphasis is being placed on graduates’ generic skills alongside their disciplinary knowledge. For example, generic skills have been included in the criteria of engineering accreditation bodies, while Hong Kong universities are attempting to improve the employability of graduates by encouraging them to develop individual graduate profiles showcasing their generic skills. In our previous General Research Fund study of over 1700 engineering undergraduates from three research-intensive universities in Hong Kong, it was found that the majority agreed that generic skills are important and are best developed through activities such as internships, community service, projects and hall education. However, little is known about the features or ‘learning ingredients’ of these experiences that facilitate students’ development of generic skills, whether such learning experiences are indeed effective in developing students’ generic skills, and to what extent students are engaged in and motivated to participate in these learning experiences. Thus, focusing on two out-of-class (i.e. internship, community service), one extra-curricular (i.e. hall education) and one in-class (i.e. lecture with group projects) learning experience, the proposed study aims to 1) identify and investigate the specific learning ingredients (e.g. opportunities for observation, reflection, discussion, and receiving mentorship) that engage students in the development of generic skills; 2) investigate students’ development of generic skills; and 3) explore the relationship between the specific learning ingredients, student engagement/participation and generic skills development in the selected learning experiences. Taking a mixed method approach, document review of program/course materials, collection of direct evidence of student learning, and representative surveys and interviews will be conducted. Findings from the study will be integrated to inform the development of a curriculum framework incorporating those specific learning ingredients that effectively engage students in the development of generic skills in out-of-class, extra-curricular and in-class activities in higher education. It is known that if generic skills are to be better developed, study needs to be discipline specific thus, for this study, a science-based discipline of engineering has been selected as the context for this study. It is foreseen that the curriculum framework herein designed for generic skills development can be expanded and applied to other disciplines over time.

17610215.label: Realisation of objectives
17610215.value: All the objectives have been achieved. The findings from a previous GRF laid the foundations for the development of a Holistic Competency Development Framework (HCDF) for this GRF-funded project. The HCDF is an adaption of Bigg’s 3P model (1987). The PI realised that traditional learning processes such as the 3P model do not apply to GS development because students who are deep learners in the academic context do not necessarily become deep learners in GS education. Similarly, traditional assessment will not enhance student’s GS development. Thus, the words ‘deep’ and ‘surface’ with respect to academic knowledge are unsuitable in the GS context. Consequently, the PI coined a new term, Approach to Develop (Chan and Yeung, in review). The word ‘learn’ is fitting to describe academic knowledge acquisition, whilst ‘develop’ is preferable for describing GS education. All the different phases (qualitative and quantative) were conducted to identify and investigate the different learning ingredients to engage students. All the objectives were achieved.

17610215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17610215.value: There are still much to explore in the area of generic skills both in higher education and in school settings. The validated HCDF framework will provide the foundation to further understand how students engage and avoid generic skills within the different learning contexts. As this focus in the engineering discipine area, it will be interesting to investigate and compare other discipline areas such as Business, Social Sciences and Law, as different disciplines may have different displinary cultural factors. The HCDF is already being promoted in different countries through keynote presentations by the PI. Other overseas universities are interested in adapted the framework in out-of-class activities, we are hoping to further collaborate with some of these universities on how different activities in different countries may enhance or hinder student development of generic skills. Another area for further development is the assessment of generic skills. This highly debatable and topical area has been only lightly investigated in this proposal. Another GRF has been submitted to investigate student's and teacher's assessment literacy of generic skills.

17610215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17610215.value: Generic skills (GS) are “skills, abilities and attributes which are fundamental in helping students to acquire, construct and apply knowledge” and “are generic to different learning situations” (EMB, 2005). The importance of GS is captured by a statement in the viral video Did You Know? Shift Happens (2018): “We are currently preparing students for jobs and technologies that don’t yet exist … in order to solve problems that we don’t even know are problems yet.” This is also resonated with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (2018). Engineering discipline traditionally focuses mainly on academic knowledge in classroom settings. Yet, in real life, engineering graduates have to work with various stakeholders using a diverse set of skills such as problem solving, teamwork, adaptability, integrity, self-management, and communication. These skills are often omitted in their curriculum, particularly in the assessment design (Chan et al., 2017a; Vista, Kim & Care,2018). In some cases, GS development and assessment are viewed as matters of ‘ticking the box’ in a checklist imposed by policymakers (Krause, 2014). This project developed an evidence-based curriculum framework for generic skills development in out-of-class (i.e.internship, community service), extra-curricular (i.e. hall education) and in-class (i.e.lecture with group projects/lecture only) learning experiences.

17610315.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17610315.value: 正義戰爭論及暴力倫理：基礎與應用

17610315.label: Project Objectives
17610315.value: Develop a systematic and comprehensive account of the ethics of violence and just war theory by meeting the following objectives: Describe and analyze in detail, drawing on both legal and philosophical scholarship, different justifications for the use of force. Demonstrate the scope, limits, and implications of each of these justifications for the ethics of war. Clarify the moral status of combatants. Clarify in particular who may participate under which circumstances in which wars and why. Apply the findings to a host of special issues, such as guerrilla warfare, drone warfare, terrorism, private military companies, etc. Draw some general conclusions about the nature of war and recommend an attitude towards war which, while not embracing pacifism, is even more skeptical towards war than much of present-day just war theory.

17610315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610315.value: This project consolidates my extensive research on the ethics of violence and provides a detailed and comprehensive analysis of the ethics of war. Drawing on legal scholarship as well, I will describe and analyze at length different justifications of the use of force, such as self-defense, law-enforcement and punishment, and in particular a number of justifications that are often lumped together under the headings of “lesser evil” or “necessity” (but which have to be carefully distinguished from each other), and then systematically consider the scope, limits, and implications of each of these justifications with respect to the ethics of war, regarding both the moral conduct of combatants in war (jus in bello) and the morality of the (political) decision of resorting to war in the first place (jus ad bellum). I will then apply these findings to special issues, such as terrorism, humanitarian intervention, preventive war, mercenaries and private military companies, guerrillas, warlords, remote controlled weapons (drones), and fully automated weapons. A noteworthy feature of my approach is that in runs counter to the currently popular, but, as I will argue, misguided focus on the self-defense justification and on the “liability” of persons to attack (that is, on their having forfeited their right not to be attacked). Instead, I will argue that what German law calls a justifying emergency justification should take center stage and demonstrate that such an approach leads to a far more differentiated (and, I hope, more convincing) account of justifiable harming in war, and of who may participate in which wars and why, than the accounts suggested by alternative theories. Moreover, it will also lead me, in conjunction with some of my other arguments and findings, to the conclusion that while war can indeed be justified, even conventional war might have more in common with terrorism and torture than many just war theorists would like to think, and that this insight should inform our attitudes towards war and armed conflict. Finally, the findings of this study are not only relevant for our discourse about just war theory and the ethics of violence, but also for broader issues like, for instance, political legitimacy, legal and moral defenses and justifications for normally illegal or immoral conduct, the doing/allowing distinction, the doctrine of double effect, complicity, collective responsibility, fairness, reciprocity, and rights. 這研究項目整合了我對暴力倫理的廣泛研究，並就戰爭倫理提供一個詳細和全面的分析。我會同時借鑒法學研究以詳細描述和分析對使用武力的不同辯護，例如自衛，執法和懲處，還有特別是一些常被籠統地概括為“兩害取其輕”或“必要性”的辯護(但我們必須仔細區分兩者)。然後我會系統地考量上述辯護在戰爭倫理中的應用範圍、界限和含義，論題涉及交戰雙方的道德操守（戰時法）和最初應否訴諸戰爭之（政治）決定的道德性（訴諸戰爭權）。我將把這些研究結果應用於一些特殊議題，如恐怖主義，人道主義干預，預防性戰爭，雇佣軍和私營軍事公司，游擊隊，軍閥，遙控武器（無人機），以及全自動武器。我的研究徑路值得關注的一點是，它跟當前流行的－但我認為是誤入歧途的－研究徑路不同，後者把關注點放在基於自衛的辯護和被攻擊對象本身“責任” (也就是說，他們已喪失不被攻擊的權利) 。相反，我會將德國法律中所謂“可作辯解的非常情況”的辯護放在論述的中心位置，並證明，關於戰爭中的合理傷害，還有誰可以參與哪場戰爭以及為什麼如此等論題，我的研究徑路能指向一個相對於其他理論更具識別性(而且，我希望，更具說服力)的論述。此外，結合我其他一些論證和研究結果，它也將帶領我得出以下結論：儘管戰爭確實是可辯護的，但哪怕是常規戰爭，其與恐怖主義及酷刑的共同點，也可能比許多正義戰爭理論家所想的要多。這種認識應該影響我們對戰爭和武裝衝突的態度。最後，這項研究的發現不僅關乎正義戰爭論和暴力倫理的話語，它還與更廣泛的議題有關，例如政治的合法性，法律和道德意義上的自衛以及對通常是非法或不道德行為的辯護，行動/允許的區別，雙重效果論，合謀，集體責任，公平，互惠和權利。

17610315.label: Realisation of objectives
17610315.value: The project was originally planned as one book. It has grown into a trilogy -- thus, I have overachieved, not under-achieved -- since I dedicated to each of the objectives referred to in the list above an even more detailed and comprehensive treatment than I had anticipated. The first volume deals with basic justifications for the use of force , the second volume with the core of just war theory, and the third volume with special issues of just war theory. The first volume is almost finished, the second volume about 70% finished (it will be completely finished by the end of the year), and the material I already have for the third volume amounts to roughly 35%. Clearly, it cannot be expected of me to write three books within a year, therefore I submit that the percentage achieved so far is an excellent result (it amounts to two books). I applied for another grant to complete the third volume.

17610315.value: This project consolidates my extensive research on the ethics of violence and provides a detailed and comprehensive analysis of the ethics of war. Drawing on legal scholarship as well, I will describe and analyze at length different justifications of the use of force, such as self-defense, law-enforcement and punishment, and in particular a number of justifications that are often lumped together under the headings of “lesser evil” or “necessity” (but which have to be carefully distinguished from each other), and then systematically consider the scope, limits, and implications of each of these justifications with respect to the ethics of war, regarding both the moral conduct of combatants in war (jus in bello) and the morality of the (political) decision of resorting to war in the first place (jus ad bellum). A noteworthy feature of my approach is that in runs counter to the currently popular, but, as I argue, misguided focus on the self-defense justification and on the “liability” of persons to attack (that is, on their having forfeited their right not to be attacked). Instead, I argue that what German law calls a justifying emergency justification should take center stage and demonstrate that such an approach leads to a far more differentiated and intuitively compelling account of justifiable harming in war, and of who may participate in which wars and why, than the accounts suggested by alternative theories. Moreover, in conjunction with some of my other arguments and findings, I also come to the conclusion that while war can indeed be justified, even conventional war might have more in common with terrorism and torture than many just war theorists would like to think, and that this insight should inform our attitudes towards war and armed conflict. Finally, the findings of this study are not only relevant for our discourse about just war theory and the ethics of violence, but also for broader issues like, for instance, political legitimacy, legal and moral defenses and justifications for normally illegal or immoral conduct, the doing/allowing distinction, the doctrine of double effect, complicity, collective responsibility, fairness, reciprocity, and rights. For a more detailed account of the project and the results achieved, I have attached the book proposal for the trilogy below. The first two volumes cover what I have achieved so far.

17610315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17610315.value: I have so far dealt with the basic justification for the use of force (Volume 1) and with the core of just war theory (jus ad vellum and jus in bello). The further development of the research will produce a third volume, dealing with special issues in just war theory such as terrorism, humanitarian intervention, preventive war, mercenaries and private military companies, guerrillas, warlords, remote controlled weapons (drones), and fully automated weapons.

17610315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17610315.value: This project consolidates my extensive research on the ethics of violence and war. I describe and analyze at length different justifications of the use of force, and then systematically consider the scope, limits, and implications of each of these justifications with respect to the ethics of war, regarding both the moral conduct of combatants in war (jus in bello) and the morality of the (political) decision of resorting to war in the first place (jus ad bellum). The impact of this project on the philosophical and legal debate should be significant. Most present-day just war theorists focus almost entirely on the self-defense justification and often do so without paying much attention to the legal scholarship of different jurisdictions. By widening the horizon and integrating legal and philosophical scholarship, this project, in contrast, is significantly more comprehensive and systematic than other present-day studies of the ethics of war in particular and the use of force in general. Moreover, the findings of this study are also relevant for broader issues like, for instance, political legitimacy, legal and moral defenses and justifications for normally illegal or immoral conduct, the doing/allowing distinction, the doctrine of double effect, complicity, collective responsibility, fairness, reciprocity, and rights.

17610715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17610715.value: 由宏觀至微觀：歷史時期中國農業社會氣候變化與武力衝突關係的層次分析

17610715.label: Project Objectives
17610715.value: From “macro” to “micro” – To explore and compare the climate-conflict nexus in historical agrarian China over extended period along various spatio-temporal dimensions (ranging from long-term variability and large-spatial aggregate to short-term variability and spatial disaggregate). From “general” to “contextual” – To examine whether and how local socio-political context (i.e., various non-climatic factors pertinent to the cause and distribution of violent conflict) mediates the climate-conflict nexus in historical agrarian China. From “single” to “mixed” – To apply more sophisticated statistical methods (instead of traditional statistical methods) which accommodate both the spatial dependency of observations and the non-linear relationship between climate measures and conflict, complemented with qualitative research methods to cater for those non-quantifiable socio-political dynamics.

17610715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17610715.value: In this project, PI’s research team will examine climate-conflict nexus in historical agrarian China in multi-scalar and contextualized approach, illustrating what and how socio-political factors could significantly mediate the climate-violent link in pre-industrial society. The PI’s research team found in their previous empirical large-N studies that violent conflict in historical agrarian society was triggered by climate-induced food scarcity. The relationship was valid in China, Europe, and various geographic regions in the Northern Hemisphere in pre-industrial era. Nevertheless, the observed relationship has only been verified at a macro level (long-term variability of the nexus is emphasized and data over large area are aggregated), and somewhat generalized in nature (only physical environmental factors are controlled). Three inter-related issues remain unresolved: -First, the key explanatory variable of violent conflicts may change substantially at different spatio-temporal scales. It is necessary to check whether the climate-conflict nexus is valid at a micro level (about short-term variability of the nexus and data in finer spatial resolution), and explore how the nexus changes along various spatio-temporal dimensions. -Second, as the climate-conflict nexus has only been demonstrated in a broad sense, it is necessary to check whether and how the nexus is mediated by local socio-political context. More non-climatic factors pertinent to the cause and distribution of conflicts (e.g., governance, adaptive mechanisms, etc.) should be considered. -Third, the methodology applied in the previous studies assumes spatially-independent observations and linear relationship, which may simplify the climate-conflict link. Moreover, the solitary reliance on quantitative methods may neglect those non-quantifiable socio-political dynamics which mediates the climate-conflict nexus. This project plans to address the above issues by using disaggregated spatial analysis and in-depth case studies, with close attention to local and temporal differences and non-linear nature of the climate-conflict link. China will be chosen as study area. Study period will be delimited to AD1–1911. This project represents pioneering research which systematically examines the climate-conflict nexus in pre-industrial society over extended period in multi-scalar and contextualized perspective. By comparing and evaluating the climate-conflict link along various spatio-temporal dimensions and in different socio-political context, it may help to deepen the theoretical understanding of, and also resolve the current debate over, the climate-conflict relationship. Given the large potential changes in climatic regimes projected in coming decades, the findings in this project may have important implications for the social impact of climate change in tropical countries that are in some ways similar to pre-industrial society. 於本研究項目，項目負責人及他的團隊會以多元尺度及多方兼顧的方式，找出那些影響前工業時期氣候變化與武力衝突連結的社會政治因素。項目負責人及他的團隊在以往的大數據實例研究中，以定量方法證明了在歷史時期，氣候變化所導致的糧食短缺可觸發農業社會的武力衝突，這種關係可套用於前工業時期的中國、歐洲、與及北半球大部份地區。可是，上述發現只在宏觀層面上被驗證（只強調長週期的一致性，並將大面積研究區域的數據作加總處理），而且在概念上頗為概括（只考慮自然環境因素）。到目前為止，有三個相關問題仍未圓滿解答： 首先，在不同時空尺度下，武力衝突的主要解釋變量可能會有所不同，所以有必要檢驗氣候變化與武力衝突的連結是否在微觀層面上仍然有效（針對連結的短期變化，及使用高空間分辨率數據的前提下），並探索氣候變化與武力衝突的連結怎樣隨不同時空尺度而變化。 其次，因為氣候變化與武力衝突關係只在廣義層面上被證明，所以有必要檢驗有關連結會不會被當地的社會政治因素影響，而且，在驗證有關連結時，應同時考慮其他與武力衝突及其空間分佈相關的非氣候因素（如政治管理、社會應變機制、等等）。 第三，以往所採用的研究方法，大多基於數據是空間獨立觀察和變量只存在線性關係的假設，這可能簡化了氣候變化與武力衝突的連結。此外，單單採用定量分析的驗證手段，可能會忽略了那些不可量化，卻又影響氣候變化與武力衝突連結的社會政治因素。 本項目擬通過空間解構分析及深入的案例研究，並針對地區和時段差異與及氣候變化與武力衝突的非線性關係，解答上述問題。研究區域定為中國，而研究時段則定為公元1–1911年。 本項目屬開拓性的研究，在多元尺度及多方兼顧的前題下，有系統地去驗證前工業社會氣候變化與武力衝突的關係。通過在不同時空尺度和不同社會政治背景下比較和評價氣候變化與武力衝突的連結，可有助加深對有關理論的見解，同時亦有助於解決目前對有關理論的爭議。鑑於未來幾十年氣候狀況可能會出現巨大的變化，本項目的研究結果，對預測氣候變化將會為那些與前工業社會情況對應的熱帶國家帶來甚麼衝擊，有着重要的啟示。

17610715.label: Realisation of objectives
17610715.value: In this research project, PI’s research team examined climate-conflict nexus in historical agrarian China in multi-scalar and contextualized approach, illustrating what and how socio-political factors could significantly mediate the climate-conflict link in pre-industrial societies. In order to realize the project objectives, the PI’s research team collected huge amount of fine-grained data of paleo-climate (i.e., temperature and precipitation), climatic extreme (i.e., flood and drought), and wars (i.e., nomadic invasion and internal disturbances) in historical agrarian China spanned 221BC–AD1911 from various literature and historical documents. The most fine-grained data are concentrated in the period AD1470–1911. This made possible the multi-scalar analyses on the climate-conflict nexus in historical agrarian China. Besides, to cater for the possible non-linear and non-stationary nature of the climate-conflict nexus, which is generally overlooked in previous studies, various sophisticated statistical methods such as Poisson Regression, Granger Causality, Multiple Wavelet Coherence, and Partial Wavelet Coherence analyses were applied by the PI’s research team to examine the climate-conflict nexus. Details of the project implementation are stated below: To kick-start this research project, the PI’s research team based on internal disturbance incidents in pre-industrial Europe to conduct long-temporal and multi-scalar examination on the climate-conflict nexus. Time-series and panel data disaggregation approaches, together with Granger Causality, Multiple Regression, and Survival Analyses were applied to verify the nexus quantitatively (Research Output #1). The study was supported by an internal research grant at HKU for the application of this GRF research project. The key finding of this study is about the remarkable disparity of the climate-conflict nexus at lower geographic levels in pre-industrial Europe, which laid an important foundation for this research project. To achieve the first project objective, in terms of spatial scale, apart from examining the historical climate-conflict nexus in the whole of China (large-spatial aggregate) as performed in most of the previous large-N quantitative studies on this topic (Research Output #5), the PI’s research team took a step forward by scaling down the examination to various agro-ecological zones in China (spatial disaggregate). Three agro-ecological zones in China, namely: rice, wheat, and pastoral regions in China, which are marked by different human carrying capacity and socio-political context, were investigated individually (Research Output #3, #4, and #6). In terms of temporal scale, the PI’s research team examined both the multi-decadal (long-term) (Research Output #3, #4, and #5) and inter-annual (short-term) (Research Output #3, #4, and #6) variability of the climate-conflict nexus. By doing so, the PI successfully illustrated how the climate-conflict nexus in historical China changed along various spatio-temporal levels. To achieve the second project objective, the PI conducted an area study in northwestern China, which is an environmentally-fragile region, to see how climate change triggered various demographic disasters (i.e., wars, famine, epidemics, etc.) at the regional level (Research Output #2). Also, inter-regional comparison among the rice, wheat, and pastoral regions were conducted to reveal the similarities and differences of the climate-conflict nexus across China (Research Output #3, #4, and #6). Moreover, the PI’s research team grounded on various non-climatic factors such as population density, culture, government policies, introduction of foreign food crops, and the frequency of famines and epidemics (i.e., local geographic context) to explain the disparity of the climate-conflict nexus across China (Research Output #3, #4, and #6). By doing so, the PI successfully illustrated how and to what extent the climate-conflict nexus in historical agrarian China at lower geographic levels was mediated by local geographic context. This is important to prove that at lower geographic levels, the climate-conflict nexus is context-dependent rather than deterministic in nature. To achieve the third project objective, instead of applying traditional statistical methods (e.g., correlation, linear regression, etc.) which assume the linearity and stationarity of data, the PI’s research team employed some sophisticated statistical methods such as Poisson Regression (Research Output #3, #4, #5, and #6), Granger Causality (Research Output #6), Multiple Wavelet Coherence (Research Output #2, #3, and #4), and Partial Wavelet Coherence (Research Output #2, #3, and #4) analyses to examine the climate-war nexus in historical agrarian China. The above methods (particularly Multiple Wavelet Coherence and Partial Wavelet Coherence analyses) helped the PI’s research team decompose time and frequency components from time-series and hence, the non-linear and non-stationary nature of climate-war nexus in historical agrarian China could be successfully revealed. Those statistical results were also complemented with qualitative scrutiny to cater for those non-quantifiable socio-political dynamics pertinent to the climate-conflict nexus. One of the noteworthy findings is that the climate-conflict nexus was not constant throughout Chinese history. The connection between climate change and violent conflicts was only significant in periods in which population density was increasing or the upper limit of regional carrying capacity was being reached (Research Output #2, #3, and #4). Apart from focusing on the connection between climate change and wars, the PI’s research team also considered how climate deterioration drove the synthesis (i.e., inter-connection) of wars, famines, and epidemics at the country (Research Output #5) and regional (Research Output #6) levels, as well as its feedback effect on the climate-conflict nexus. The related findings supplement the Malthusian theory by demonstrating the inter-connection among various mortality factors, which has rarely been examined empirically in academia. With the implementation of abovementioned tasks, the project objectives have been fully achieved (cf. Section 6.1 Major findings and research outcome). Besides, inspired from and grounded on the key findings in this research project, the PI systematically reviewed all of the large-N studies of the climate-conflict nexus in the pre-industrial period (Research Output #7). It is worth mentioning that the majority of those studies are about historical agrarian China, which is primarily done by the PI’s research team over the years. Some conceptual and methodological issues pertinent to the understanding and examination of the climate-conflict nexus in pre-industrial societies were discussed. Suggestions and priorities for future research on the topic were also provided in the end of this paper. The study may provide deeper reflections and produce constructive insights about the relationship between climate change and violent conflicts in human history, advancing the progress in climate-conflict research. P.S.: Since 01-Jul-2017, the appointment of PI has been changed from “Assistant Professor” (UGC grade G) to “Senior Lecturer” (UGC grade J). As staff at UGC grade J is not eligible to hold GRF grant, the PI applied for the early completion of this project. Therefore, the project duration was shortened from 24 months to 18 months. Given that the progress of this project (including data collection and data analyses) has been completed ahead of original schedule, the implementation of this project is not much affected by its early completion.

17610715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17610715.value: First, previous studies mainly focus on the disastrous societal impacts brought by temperature cooling, while this project supplements it with the effect of climatic extremes (i.e., flood and drought, which is another important aspect of climate change) on violent conflicts. Second, this project reveals the long-term and short-term variability of the climate-conflict nexus in historical China at lower geographic levels. In the rice region, flood triggered internal disturbances at the inter-annual and multi-decadal time scales. In the wheat region, both flood and drought caused internal disturbances at the inter-annual and multi-decadal time scales. In the pastoral region, internal disturbances were associated with flood only at the multi-decadal time scale. Pinpointing to the short-term temporal scale, in general, socio-ecological catastrophes rather than natural disasters were the proximate triggers of internal wars. Specifically, internal wars were triggered by epidemics in the wheat region, and they were ignited by famines in the rice region in historical China. Third, at lower geographic levels, the climate-conflict nexus was diverse and context-dependent, which was substantiated with empirical quantitative and qualitative evidence. The disparity of the nexus at lower geographic levels was attributable to local geographic context such as population density, culture, government policies, introduction of foreign food crops, and the frequency of famines and epidemics. Besides, the climate-conflict nexus was not constant throughout Chinese history. The nexus was only significant in periods in which population density was increasing or the upper limit of regional carrying capacity was being reached. Fourth, the project also demonstrates the inter-relationship among wars, famines, and epidemics under climate change, and its significant feedback effect on the climate-conflict nexus. This supplements the Malthusian theory by demonstrating the inter-connection among various mortality factors, which has rarely been examined empirically in academia. The findings of this research project have been published in six research papers in internationally peer-reviewed journals, including Chinese Geographical Science (Impact Factor in 2016: 1.154), Quaternary International (Impact Factor in 2016: 2.199), Science China Earth Sciences (Impact Factor in 2016: 1.989), and The Holocene (Impact Factor in 2016: 2.324). Besides, a review paper has been submitted to Asian Geographer (indexed in Web of Science), which could be published after minor revision. The PI would like to take this opportunity to thank the financial support provided by RGC and the logistical support provided by the Department of Geography at HKU. Or else, it is impossible to have such a fruitful outcome. Thanks a lot!

17610715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17610715.value: The results of this project imply that the climate-conflict nexus could not be generalized across a large geographic domain, as the relationship itself was subject to, and significantly mediated by, local geographic context. The PI’s research team suggests that when historical climate-conflict nexus (for historical agrarian China or other pre-industrial societies) is examined, data should be boiled down according to geographic regions rather than aggregated spatially in the course of analysis (both quantitative and qualitative). On the other hand, the findings of the existing large-N quantitative studies are pessimistic about the fate of human societies under climate change at the global and hemispheric levels. Yet, according to the findings in this project, the role of adaptation to and mitigation against climate change at the local and regional levels should not be overlooked, as it can somehow weaken the social vulnerability to climate change. But, those related factors are usually treated as control variables in statistical analysis. In future research, the extent and strength of their effect in mediating the climate-conflict nexus could be further investigated such that a more comprehensive view on the topic could be obtained. This can help avoid the accusations of over-simplification and neo-determinism in climate-conflict research.

17610715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17610715.value: PI’s research team examined climate-conflict nexus in historical agrarian China in multi-scalar and contextualized approach, illustrating what and how socio-political factors could significantly mediate the climate-conflict link in pre-industrial societies. The PI’s research team collected huge amount of fine-grained paleo-climate, climatic extreme, and war data in historical agrarian China from various literature and historical documents for the multi-scalar analyses on the nexus. To cater for the possible non-linear and non-stationary nature of the climate-conflict nexus, Poisson Regression, Granger Causality, Multiple Wavelet Coherence, and Partial Wavelet Coherence analyses were applied to examine the nexus. The findings in this project supplement the existing literature with the effect of climatic extremes (which is another important aspect of climate change) on violent conflicts in Chinese history. Besides, the long-term and short-term variability of the climate-conflict nexus in historical agrarian China at lower geographic levels is revealed to be diverse and context-dependent in nature. Furthermore, the inter-relationship among wars, famines, and epidemics under climate change and its significant feedback effect on the climate-conflict nexus are demonstrated. This project may have provided deeper reflections and produced constructive insights about the relationship between climate change and violent conflicts in human history, advancing the progress in climate-society research.

17611615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17611615.value: 大腸癌為常見之癌病。對病患者而言，為了預防大腸癌復發和症狀管理，他們必須於生活模式、自我照顧或生活調節上作出轉變，以求達至身心健康。身心治療是一項非使用藥物，講求整體和諧之介入手法，亦重視患者能夠自我練習和自我關顧。雖然很多癌症患者正練習正念冥想或氣功，然而，缺乏有系統之研究，証明正念冥想或氣功對癌症患者之作用。 正念冥想或氣功正正代表了兩種截然不同的身心介入手法：動態和靜態。兩種手法都重視呼吸，氣功透過連動身體達至身心變化，正念冥想則由思想入手亦能影響身體。唯現有之知識和研究並能深入解釋兩者身心介入手法之極端分別。 研究不止探討正念冥想與氣功對大腸癌症患者的各種症狀、調整壓力荷爾蒙和整體心理健康的作用，亦希望更了解這兩種於基本理念上非常不同之身心介入手法，對長期練習之病患者之作用。 本研究採用三組隨機對照實驗設計，是次計劃將會是首次研究正念冥想與氣功對大腸癌症患者的各種症狀、壓力、精神健康、生活質素、壓力荷爾蒙和正念調節之作用。除此之外，研究結果亦可以顯示動態介入（氣功）與靜態介入（正念冥想）之相同和不同之處，如何影響練習之大腸癌症患者之果效。最後，研究亦可以更了解身體、心理和互惠之影響。 189位來自醫院或地區組織的大腸癌病患者將會隨機抽簽進入氣功組、正念冥想組或等候控制組(為期八個星期，每星期一節，每節一個半小時)。所有參加者於參加組別之前、四個星期後、八個星期後和六個月後接受評估。 研究結果可以增進我們了解大腸癌病患者於接受正念冥想或氣功後之身體和心理變化，亦可以更加清楚身心相連之互惠影響。本研究採用具研究實証之身心介入模式，強調參加者可以容易學習、自我實踐和融合於生活之中。

17611615.label: Realisation of objectives
17611615.value: The primary objectives (1&2) of this study have been achieved. We conducted a 3-arm randomized controlled trial on 127 Chinese colorectal cancer survivors. In this RCT, we examined the effects of mindfulness meditation and baduanjin qigong in comparison with a waitlist control group on a range of measures. The measurements included self-report instruments on self-compassion, mindfulness, mental health, cancer symptoms, quality of life, and biomarkers measures on salivary cortisol. Please refer to the finding section (6.1) and the outputs [8.1, 8.2, 9.1, 9.6, 9.7] for details of the published study protocol and academic manuscript under review. For achieving the primary objectives, we recruited and accessed 284 eligible participants through open recruitment using posters and newsletter advertisements displayed at community organizations servicing cancer patients and local hospitals in Hong Kong. Given the reason that only those participants who were not joining or practicing similar mind-body exercises (i.e. qigong and taichi etc.) could join the study, a lot of interested and eligible cancer survivors were excluded. That created difficulty in recruitment. However, we also learnt from this experience that mind-body exercises are so welcome and popular among colorectal cancer survivors. For this reason, a more robust and rigorous study is important and needed. We then decided not to amend the inclusion criteria just for recruiting more participants but scarifying the rigorousness of the study. Instead, we conducted several additional batches of recruitment, and tried all the means including social media, newspaper, radio and television media programs to recruit participants. Finally, 127 participants were recruited which reached the calculated sample size of 126. In the proposal, we assumed there were attrition rate of 33.5%, thus we intended to recruit more participants (189). In fact, up to the 3rd data collection point, there was no drop out of participants in the intervention arms, and only 2 participants dropped out in the control arm (1.6% attrition at T3). At the end of the study, a total of 18 participants dropped out which is equivalent to 14.2% attrition. The reasons of late stage drop-out included passing away, hospitalization and personal reasons. To supplement the results of the quantitative findings, the research team has also looked into the qualitative data generated from this study. The qualitative exploration focused primarily on the comparative and differential benefits of the two interventions (Primary Objective 2). The exploratory qualitative study found five emerging themes of mental well-being, physical well-being, intrapersonal connectedness, restoring normal living, and spiritual growth. Participants of the mindfulness group (n = 38) and the Baduanjin qigong (n = 22) reported improvements on mental well-being and restoration of normal living, suggesting that both practices have beneficial impacts on psychosocial well-being of colorectal cancer survivors. Nevertheless, differentiating impacts of the two body-mind practices were identified. Specifically, participants of the mindfulness group were found to report improvements on spiritual growth and intrapersonal connectedness; while those in the BDJ group reported more prominent improvements in physical well-being, for example, enhancement of vitality and rejuvenating the physical body through regular practices. The results of the exploratory study suggested different pathways to well-being for those who practiced mindfulness and those who practiced Baduanjin qigong. Lastly, we also found that there were no significant differences in outcome variables other than depression and cortisol slope in the two interventions in terms of magnitude and pace of chance; and two intervention groups did not differ in extended compliance. We have prepared an academic manuscript [8.6] and a conference presentation [9.8]. The secondary objectives of exploring the temporal associations among psychological, physical, and physiological have all been fully achieved. Colorectal cancer survivors are at elevated risk of physical/emotional distress and identifying mindfulness facets that can predict distress and functional outcomes is of clinical relevance. Our team conducted moderated mediation analysis to examine the direct and indirect effects of mindfulness on quality of life and sleep disturbance via physical/emotional distress using acting with awareness as a moderator. The results found no significant direct effects from mindfulness to the outcomes. However, awareness and nonreacting had significant and positive indirect effects on physical and mental SF-12 via physical and emotional distress, respectively. Awareness, nonjudging, and nonreacting had significant and negative indirect effects on sleep disturbance via emotional distress. The indirect effects of nonreacting on functional outcomes increased as a function of awareness. These results support longitudinal linkages between mindfulness facets and functioning in cancer survivors via their perceived distress. Please refer to the manuscript output 8.4 for the details of this analysis. Apart from emotional distress, cancer survivors are at risk of dysregulated diurnal cortisol rhythms, our team performed structural equation modeling to analyze the direct and indirect effects of self-compassion and self-criticism on stress outcomes via affect. Controlling for baseline status, self-compassion and self-criticism did not show significant direct effects on stress outcomes. Self-compassion significantly predicted steeper diurnal cortisol slopes 8 months later indirectly via positive affect 2 months later and self-criticism significantly predicted higher subjective perceived stress 8 months later indirectly via emotional distress 2 months later. These results demonstrate specific indirect linkages and suggest a protective role for self-compassion in improving neuroendocrine functioning via affect among Chinese colorectal cancer survivors. Please refer to the finding section (6.1) for summary of the main findings. We have prepared two academic manuscripts to report these findings in the [8.4 and 8.5] and three conference presentations and published abstracts [9.2, 9.4, 9.5].

17611615.label: Major findings and research outcome
17611615.value: Research data from this study found benefits for both interventions in terms of better functioning in neuroendocrine but not psychological domains. Findings showed that, when compared to the control group, participants in mindfulness meditation and baduanjin qigong interventions showed significantly steeper diurnal cortisol slopes after the intervention. No significant intervention effects were found in domains such as symptom distress, mental health, quality of life, and mindfulness, except for increased observing in mindfulness meditation. In terms of commonalities and differential effectiveness between the two interventions, mindfulness meditation displayed significant improvement in depression but less improvement in cortisol slope compared to baduanjin. There were no significant differences in other outcome variables in terms of magnitude and pace of change. Participants of the two interventions did not differ in extended compliance. Our hypothesis of mind-body interventions leading to multidimensional improvements for Chinese colorectal cancer survivors compared with control is partially supported by empirical data. Nevertheless, the mixed-method exploratory study on qualitative data revealed benefits and impacts of the two interventions for participants on psychosocial well-being, especially in the domains of improving mental wellbeing and restoring normal living. The practice of Badjuanjin, however was found to have more prominent impact on physical wellbeing by means of enhancing vitality and rejuvenating the physical body of colorectal cancer survivors, who have undergone treatment for their disease. Moreover, the practice of mindfulness was found to have prominent impact on cultivating spiritual growth. In addition to the quantitative and qualitative analyses of the major outcomes, we also examined the psychometric properties of the measurement tool used in this study [8.3, 9.3]. This objective is extra to the original proposal and the outputs are derived directly from this study. Mindfulness has emerged as an important correlate of well-being in cancer patients. Our research output further extended to validation of the 20-item Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire in the Chinese context. The five-factor structure with approximate zero cross-loadings provided an acceptable fit to the data with satisfactory reliability. Out of the five facets, acting with awareness predicted lower levels of perceived stress, negative affect, anxiety, depression and illness symptoms and better quality of life, but was not significantly associated with other facets. These findings support the factorial validity and reliability of the scale as a precise assessment of different mindfulness facets.

17611615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17611615.value: This is the first study to examine the homeostatic effects of mind-body practices on HPA axis activities. The presence of physiological effects on circadian cortisol rhythm and lack of effects on psychological outcomes suggests mixed effects for both interventions. First, it could be due to the nature of present sample (older-aged colorectal cancer survivors with both males and females at a later cancer stage). Since these cancer survivors likely have complicated prognosis after cancer treatment, the differences in clinical profiles could modulate the effectiveness of mind-body practices. Future studies should refine the intervention components to better suit the needs of the cancer survivors and extend the investigation to survivors of other types of cancer. Second, the improved moods and symptoms in the control group suggest that these survivors could be receiving alternative treatments outside the present study. This could explain the phenomenon of symptoms relief during the study period. Further studies are needed to test the effects of these practices with higher intervention dosages in a larger sample of colorectal cancer survivors. Longitudinal studies could take into account multidimensional (neuroendocrine, molecular, psychological, or behavioral) factors to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of the mind-body interventions on the outcomes.

17611615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17611615.value: Data collected from this randomized controlled trial investigated psychophysiological effects of two mind-body practices on colorectal cancer survivors. The interventions showed physiological benefits in terms of steeper diurnal cortisol slopes. Benefits on psychological and physical well-being were reported from participants through qualitative feedback but not on the data for psychological outcomes. Participants revealed more impact on the physical wellbeing for Badjuanjin practice and more prominent impact on cultivating spiritual wellbeing for mindfulness practice. Results of structural equation modeling support a mediating role for affect in the temporal relationship between self-compassion and stress outcomes. Participants with greater self-compassionate attitudes showed significantly steeper diurnal cortisol slopes via positive affect. These results demonstrate specific indirect linkages between self-compassion and better neuroendocrine functioning in the cancer survivors. This research validates the short-form of the Five Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire in terms of factorial validity and reliability. The results support its use as a precise assessment of different mindfulness facets. Our findings revealed higher levels of mindful awareness and nonreacting significantly predicted better quality of life and lower sleep disturbance via physical and emotional distress. Besides, Nonreacting appears to play a stronger protective role in improving sleep disturbance and functioning among patients with greater awareness.

17611715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17611715.value: This study aims to explore the undiscovered path of Chinese women’s use of force in heterosexual intimate relationship, including the motives, acts and outcomes, in Hong Kong. Women’s use of force means women use physical, verbal, and emotionally harmful or aggressive behaviors towards/against their intimate partners (Larance, 2006; Miller, 2001). Women can be victims of intimate terrorism, perpetrators of resistant violence because of self-defense, or party to common couple violence in intimate partner violence (Johnson, 1995, 2006), as well as the perpetrators of violence against men (Hines & Douglas, 2010). Indeed, “women’s violence is usually different from men’s violence” (Miller, 2001, p. 1367). The lack of resources and options for women and their relative powerlessness had led to possible use of force/violent acts to cope and respond in their battering relationships (Larance & Dasgupta, 2012; Miller, 2001). Therefore, women’s use of force is not merely a form of IPV, but a reflection of women facing a prolong violence in a prolonged helpless situation. In Hong Kong, over 80% of victims IPV are women (SWD, 2014a). However, the number of male victims among the newly report spousal battering cases in Hong Kong has increased from 11.2% in 2004 to 18% in 2013, almost all of such cases involved heterosexual intimate relationships (SWD, 2014a). Therefore, nearly all perpetrators in male victim cases were females. Women’s use of force is no longer a rare phenomenon, however, our understanding on women’s use of force in Hong Kong is very limited because most studies focus on female victims while neglecting women’s violence. This qualitative study will include multiple in-depth interviews with 30 to 40 women who will be recruited from the programs for perpetrators of different agencies in Hong Kong. To fully understand the complexity of women’s use of force, a contextual understanding of the use, motivations, and consequences of violence (Miller, 2001, 2005) is essential. This study will therefore examine the influence of Chinese culture, especially on the gender and in-law families, in the path of the women’s use of force in order to fill the knowledge gap on this aspect in Hong Kong. With the reference of the Swan & Snow’s model (2006), women’s victimization, coping and childhood trauma will also be included in this study. The finding is vital to develop a conceptual model on Chinese women’s use of force and specific intervention program for women to recover from the violence.

17611715.label: Realisation of objectives
17611715.value: 1. To explore the context of women’s use of force against their male intimate partners, including the forms and pattern of the violent acts, motives and outcomes of using force; o The objective has been achieved. A total of 20 female participants had been recruited from different agencies that provided social services for women who use force against their male partners. The information collected from the participants were adequate to demonstrate women’s use of force against their male intimate partners in the current context. Besides, 15 male victims were also interviewed to provide information about women’s use of force from an alternative angle. From the voice of the participating women, forms and patterns of violence included psychological, physical and sexual aggression, and these women would use more than one form of violence against their husbands, such as verbal insult, long period of scolding, threatening, bite, pushing, slapping, kicking and throwing objects against their male partners. The same information was also provided by the male participants. There were two main themes of motives: to stop violence from partners and/or release their negative emotion due to the abuse history and disappointment on the relationship. However, based on the women’s views on their use of force, violence could not fulfill these their needs behind the motives. (Choi et al., under preparation) 2. To identify the qualitative components affecting the dynamics among women’s use of force, women’s victimization, coping to victimization and childhood trauma, o The objective has been achieved. The findings reflected the common victimization experienced by women who use force in an intimate relationship. All interviewed women reported that they have experienced one to three types of interpersonal trauma/victimization, including being abused in intimate partner violence (16 women), witnessed their children abused by their partners (6 women), in-law conflict (5 women), their partners have (suspected) extra-marital affair (6 women) and childhood trauma (1 woman). Besides, three main types of coping strategies for their victimization have been identified: problem-solving (e.g. exploring solution by themselves); social support (e.g. seeking help from others); and, avoidance (e.g. avoid/escape from the scene of violence/conflict). However, the outcome of these coping strategies cannot stop their victimization, or the coping strategies could only change the form of abuse, or even increase in the severity of victimization. Therefore, the use of force against their male partners became a sort of the last resource to stop these women’s victimization. (Choi et al., under preparation) 3. To understand the outcomes of women’s use of force and its dynamics with the acts and motives of using force, and the women’s victimization o The objective has been achieved. All interviewed women reported that the use of force were not helpful in stopping violence and rebuilding relationships. The cycle of being abused, the use of force to stop violence and being abused kept repeating. In addition, the use of different coping strategies could not stop their victimization effectively; on the other hand, they gradually reinforced the belief that the use of force was the last resort to stopping their victimization. The cycle of victimization and using force were escalated. The concept of such a cycle of violence is an important concept for the helping professions who provide service assessment, prevention and intervention for these women. Besides, we have identified five major themes on the motivating factors for receiving services from the anti-violence programme for women using force (AVPw), and the themes were: Seek emotional support; be awaked by community education; introduced by helping professionals; and self-awareness of using force. These findings can help us understand the needs of these women and design effective services and support for them (Choi et al., under review). 4. To examine the influence of Chinese culture on women’s use of force o The objective has been achieved. In order to understand the influence of Chinese culture on women’s use of force and to prepare corresponding interview guideline, the research team analyzed the data from 12 case records of women who used force against their male partners at the beginning of this project. Results showed that Chinese and Western women had some common motives in using force, but additional motives relating to family roles and in-law relationship relevant in Chinese culture were found (Choi et al., 2018). These findings were also demonstrated in the data collected from the in-depth interviews with the women. Five women out of 20 interviewed women reported having in-law conflict; in-law conflict seemed to be a common concurrence of intimate partner violence. The disappointment and stress experienced by these women should also be a concern. Cultural values play a vital role in women’s use of force, both in their prior motives and help-seeking behaviours afterwards, therefore, it is essential to provide effective gender- and cultural-specific interventions for these women (Choi et al., under preparation).

17611715.label: Major findings and research outcome
17611715.value: A total of 20 women who used force against their husbands recruited from different agencies providing anti-violence programs and family protection services. Regarding the experience of these women, we found a cycle pattern of victimization and the use of force. Two main themes of motives for using forces: stop violence and release negative emotion, and five themes of victimization of interpersonal trauma were identified: 1. Intimate partner violence; 2. Children abused by husbands; 3. In-law conflict/aggression; 4. Husbands’ extra-marital affair; and 5. Childhood trauma. Most motives and experience of victimization found were similar to those found in the Western countries, however, the influence of extended family was also seen in Chinese families. In addition, in coping strategies for victimization, three themes were identified; 1. Sroblem-solving (e.g. exploring solution by themselves); 2. Support-seeking (e.g. seeking help from others) and 3. Problem-avoiding (e.g. avoid/escape from the scene of violence/conflict). However, the outcome of these coping strategies cannot stop their victimization, or the coping strategies could only change the form of abuse, or even increase in the severity of victimization. (Choi et al., under preparation). The cycle of victimization and using force were escalated. The concept of such a cycle of violence is an important concept for the helping professions who provide service assessment, prevention and intervention for these women. Besides, we have identified five major themes on the motivating factors for receiving services from the anti-violence programme for women using force, and they were: 1. seek emotional support; 2. be awaked by community education; 3. introduced by helping professionals; and 4. self-awareness of using force. These findings can help us understand the needs of these women and design effective services and support for them. (Choi et al., under review) In order to prepare corresponding interview guideline, the research team analyzed the data from 12 case records of women who used force against their male partners at the beginning of this project. Results showed that Chinese and Western women had some common motives in using force, but additional motives relating to family roles and in-law relationship relevant in Chinese culture were found (Choi et al., 2018). These findings were also demonstrated in the data collected from the in-depth interviews with the women. Cultural values play a vital role in women’s use of force, in term of their motive and help-seeking, therefore, it is essential to provide effective gender-cultural-specific interventions.

17611715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17611715.value: There is a need to develop further research on the effectiveness of the supports and services for women who use force against male intimate partners as they are different from male abusers in men-to-women violence. Further studies on the views of the women’s use of force on their male partners are highly recommended. The findings would contribute to understanding the dynamic of these couples and develop effective interventions for them. This study focused on women receiving supports from welfare services, who may have experienced severe violence than those in the community. Moreover, this is a qualitative study. Therefore, the findings may not be generalized to other populations. Study on women’s use of force in the community is one of the potential study areas for further research development of intimate partner violence. In addition, further research in different locations around the world is important to explore the similarities and differences across different countries and cultures.

17611715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17611715.value: Women’s violence in an intimate relationship is different from that of men’s. We found a cycling pattern of victimization and using force in women’s use of force. We should assess the women who experienced different kinds of interpersonal trauma, such as intimate partner violence, witnessed their children being abused, in-law aggression and partners’ extramarital affairs, which will help us understand their possibly different motives to use force against their male partners. Besides, we should recognize the disappointment and helplessness women experienced after trying all possible strategies to stop victimizations, which may reinforce the cycle of victimization and using force. This cycling pattern is an important concept for the helping professions provide assessment, prevention and intervention for these women. Also, we had identified the motivating factors for receiving services from the anti-violence programme for women using force: 1. seek emotional support; 2. awaked by community education; 3. introduced by helping professionals; and 4. self-awareness of using force. These findings can help us understand the needs of these women and design effective supports for them. Lastly, in-law conflict is not only a kind of interpersonal trauma experienced by women; it also generates the feeling of hostility towards the in-law and husband. Traditional Chinese and filial values play a vital role in women’s family relationships, so the disappointment and stress experienced by these women in in-law conflicts should be studied separately.
