17613815.label: Project Objectives
17613815.value: To identify the causal neurocognitive underpinnings of the effect of attention-based compassion meditation (ABCM) on neuroplastic changes to the brain. To substantiate the translational values of the ABCM model for the promotion of healthy aging.
rows: To identify the causal neurocognitive underpinnings of the effect of attention-based compassion meditation (ABCM) on neuroplastic changes to the brain.
To substantiate the translational values of the ABCM model for the promotion of healthy aging.

17613815.label: Realisation of objectives
17613815.value: All the objectives have been 100% realized. Objective 1: To identify the casual neurocognitive underpinnings of the effect of attention-based compassion meditation (ABCM) on neuroplastic changes to the brain. It has been widely suggested that meditation can bring about improved mental-wellbeing and the corresponding changes on the brain. We investigated the effect of an eight-week ABCM training on affective processing and resting-state functional connectivity at modular and regional levels in 45 healthy elderly participants who were novices to meditation or relaxation training. As meditation facilitates affective regulation and affects resting-state functional connectivity of both the affective networks [e.g. pontine raphe nucleus (PRN) in the brain stem] and regions related to self-referential processing [e.g. posterior cingulate cortex (PCC)/precuneus], we hypothesized that the ABCM training would increase resting-state functional connectivity between the PCC/precuneus and brain stem regions containing the PRN. Our results were in line with the hypotheses: Comparing to relaxation training, meditation increased the positive connectivity between the PCC/precuneus and the pons. Our findings further confirm the ABCM-induced increase in connectivity was directed from the pons to the PCC/precuneus (Study 2). At modular level, meditation training led to a decrease in intra-module connectivity strength in the default mode network (DMN), salience network (SAN) and somatomotor network (SMN), and a decrease in inter-module connectivity strength between DMN and other modules. According to previous literature, the direction of these changes is consistent with a movement towards a more self-detached viewpoint, as well as more efficient processing. These findings suggest that the ABCM training could induce changes in functional connectivity at network level that might be involved in self-detached behavior observed in meditators (Study 3). In another study, we examined the neural activity of the pons during the perception of affective stimuli in a group of 40 female Chinese participants. Our results demonstrated that the pons was activated when viewing affective stimuli. Furthermore, the functional connectivity between the pons and the cortico-limbic affective regions was positively associated with the self-reported emotional reactivity (Study 1). Taken together, the project has confirmed that short-term meditation training can induce neuroplastic changes that involve a novel connection between the pons and PCC/precuneus at regional levels in affective processing, as well as topological changes of the brain, which implies a generally more efficient functional network organization. The positive neuroplastic changes as a result of the eight week ABCM training provides important insights for clinical interventions on elderly individuals with affective disorders. Objective 2: To substantiate the translational values of the ABCM model for the promotion of healthy aging. To test the effectiveness of meditation training in promoting healthy aging, we examined whether ABCM training brought any cognitive and affective changes in healthy elderly who were at risk for mental deterioration. Their cognitive functioning, self-reported affective changes, and subjective well-being were measured. Meditation emphasizes the “knowing” of moment-to-moment experience, a state which can be achieved by focusing the attention on an object or a physical sensation (e.g. breathing). Any distracting thoughts or sensations are encouraged to be experienced rather than being suppressed or actively regulated. In this experiment, we hypothesized that (1) the ABCM training would reduce positive valence ratings to positive pictorial stimuli and increase positive valence ratings to negative pictorial stimuli, and (2) reduce arousal ratings for both positive and negative stimuli, compared to their active control participants who practiced relaxation training. Consistent with our hypothesis, we found that meditation, but not relaxation, training ‘neutralized’ individuals' perceived valence and decreased the general perceived arousal of affective stimuli (Study 2). These behavioral changes were associated with the synchronous structural enlargements in a prefrontal network (Study 4). These positive outcomes of ABCM training may be driven by the cultivation of both awareness and acceptance that we found to be the potential mechanism of meditation in another study on a group of healthy adults (n=364) (Study 5). Taken together, these findings provide evidence that meditation is an effective mean to promote positive affective changes. Our data also indirectly infers the influence of meditation on cognitive function. The eight-week meditation training is a cost-effective program that can be used to promote healthy aging in the cognitively at-risk population.

17613815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17613815.value: Study 1: We observed the in vivo activity of the pons when viewing affective stimuli. Furthermore, the functional connectivity (FC) between the pons and the cortico-limbic affective regions was positively associated with self-reported emotional reactivity. Our findings support the framework that the pons works conjunctively with the distributed cortico-limbic-striatal systems in shaping individuals' affective states and reactivity (Lee et al., 2015). Study 2: We examined the changes in FC of the PCC/precuneus with the pons after 8-week ABCM training, compared to relaxation control. ABCM versus relaxation training increased the positive connectivity between the PCC/precuneus and the pons, the direction of which was largely directed from the pons to the PCC/precuneus. Furthermore, changes in connectivity between the PCC/precuneus and pons predicted changes in affective processing after ABCM training. These findings indicate ABCM promotes self-referential affective regulation based on increased regulatory influence of the pons on PCC/precuneus, which new affective-processing strategy is employed across both resting state and when evaluating affective stimuli (Shao et al., 2016). Study 3: We examined the changes in functional brain connectome using resting-state neuroimaging data and graph-based analysis after 8-week ABCM training. At modular level, meditation training led to decreased intra-connectivity in the default mode network (DMN), salience network (SAN) and somatomotor network (SMN) modules post training. Also, there was decreased connectivity strength between the DMN and other modules (Cotier et al., 2017). Study 4: We investigated the relationships between behavioral changes and the associated morphometric correlates after 8-week ABCM training in a group of healthy elderly subjects. ABCM caused the neutralization of valence perception on both positive and negative affective stimuli, which were associated with the synchronous structural enlargements in a prefrontal network involving the ventromedial prefrontal cortex and inferior frontal sulcus(Chau et al., 2018). These results explain the affective effects of meditation and offer insight into the neural underpinning of disorders related to affective dysregulations in the elderly. Study 5: We investigated the moderating effect of acceptance on the relationship between awareness, psychological distress and sleep quality in a group of healthy adults. We found that increased level of acceptance weakened the positive relationship between awareness and poor sleep quality, which was partially mediated through perceived psychological distress in a group of community dwelling healthy adults (Lau et al, 2017). Our findings suggest that both awareness and acceptance are important in improving sleep quality via reducing distress, in which sleep problems are phenomena in the elderly.

17613815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17613815.value: Our findings provide solid evidence on the behavioral and neuroplastic changes induced by short-term (8 weeks) meditation training (the ABCM program) compared to the relaxation training control. We found a novel pons to PCC/precuneus functional connectivity change after short-term meditation practice. As the ABCM program combines both attention and compassion based mindfulness training, future studies can further investigate the involvement of the pons to PCC/precuneus connection in different types of meditation practice. Given our study was based on a short-term meditation training, the dose effect of meditation on behavioral, physiological and neural changes cannot be deduced. Future studies that include multiple repeated measures across a longer time-point could provide a more comprehensive picture of the effect of meditation on the above aspects. In addition, our study focused mainly on healthy elderly subjects, whether similar training effects can be observed in patients or at-risk individuals warrant further investigation. We are preparing a review paper titled "The neuroplastic effects of meditation on affective regulation in older people" to summarise the findings (reported in 6.1 above) and project future direction of research on the neuroplastic basis and application of mind training for the promotion of brain health.

17613815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17613815.value: Experience can alter the structure and the functioning of our brain. While a brain with good integrity could bring well-being. The current research has confirmed that short-term meditation (8 weeks) can influence the structure and functioning of the human brain. Short-term meditation practice that emphasizes on the cultivation of awareness and acceptance, the potential underlying mechanism of mindfulness, is linked to changes to brain regions that are important for affecting processing. Furthermore, short-term meditation practice also affect the functional connections of the brain in network level that might imply a more efficient brain. In addition, our findings suggested that meditation practices may improve sleep quality via reducing stress, in which insomnia is very common in aging population. Findings from the current research support meditation practices to be effective intervention programs for the promotion of healthy aging.

17613915.label: Project Objectives
17613915.value: The primary objective is to prepare a scholarly monograph that will make an important contribution to ‘law and film’-studies; the cultural study of law; film criticism; legal history; constitutional law; as well as the wider study of Hong Kong culture and colonial legal culture, by asking the following questions: How is law represented in Hong Kong films of this period? What are the benefits and pitfalls of using film as a primary source for understanding legal history? In what ways does film language such as camera movement, sound, graphics and lighting contribute to a representation of law unique to the genre? How might knowledge of concepts and debates in constitutional law inform our understanding of film? How do films reflect, and participate in, the formation of a distinct Hong Kong identity? What, ultimately, is the relationship between law and film as revealed by their interaction in this period?

17613915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17613915.value: This is a proposal for the first book-length, interdisciplinary study of representations of law in Hong Kong cinema. Focusing on the period between the signing of the Sino-British Joint Declaration in 1984 and the territory’s retrocession to China in 1997 -- the most formative period in Hong Kong’s legal history, during which constitutional issues were widely debated in society, as well as a time of intense film innovation and production -- it examines the ways in which cinema responded to Hong Kong’s constitutional developments, and demonstrates the ways in which knowledge of legal issues of the time can further our understanding of film. The period between 1984 and 1997 was marked by pivotal constitutional events such as the signing of the Sino-British Joint Declaration, the introduction of a Bill of Rights in the aftermath of the Tiananmen Square Incident, the drafting and promulgation of the Basic Law, debates about the nature of the rule of law, and Hong Kong’s return to China. It was also characterized by a preponderance of films about law, including blockbusters such as The Unwritten Law (1985) and Justice, My Foot! (1992). Existing studies of Hong Kong cinema often present legal developments as merely one element in a wider set of political, social and cultural conditions of film production, and studies of Hong Kong constitutional history rarely, if ever, take film into consideration. This project is an investigation of the under-examined overlap between Hong Kong cinema’s new focus on the law, and the constitutional issues and concepts dominating societal debate in this period. It demonstrates that films can be a valuable primary resource for understanding those aspirations, fears, and thoughts that Hong Kongers had about the city’s constitutional framework which ultimately shaped its development. It also shows that foregrounding the legal debates around the time of the films’ production can generate novel interpretations of individual film texts. In this way, the project provides a new model for studying interactions between film and the law. It also re-orients the predominantly Anglo-American-centric focus of ‘law and film’-studies towards East Asian cinema. This project builds on the principal investigator’s strong publication record on law and film. By combining contemporary film theory, interdisciplinary ‘law and film’ scholarship, and primary archival research, it makes an original and important contribution to’ law and film’-studies, film studies, constitutional law, as well as the study of Hong Kong popular culture and colonial legal cultures more broadly. 這個企劃屬首份詳細針對法律如何體現於香港電影的跨學科探究。1984年時值中英雙方簽署《中英聯合聲明》，定於1997年將香港交還中國。這段時期中香港法制發展空前蓬勃，社會大眾廣泛探討政制事務，大量創新的電影亦應運而生。本研究聚焦於此十多年間，探究電影業如何回應香港的政制發展，並展示對當時法制事務的認識如何加深我們對當時電影的理解。 在1984-1997年間於香港發生過的政制相關關鍵事件包括簽署《中英聯合聲明》、「天安門事件」及其後制定及通過的《人權法案條例》、起草及頒佈《基本法》、就法治精神本質所作的討論、以及香港回歸中國等。這段期間亦掀起一股與法律及法制相關電影的熱潮，賣座電影包括《法外情》(1985)及《審死官》(1992)等。現有的香港電影研究多只視法制發展為政治、社會及文化條件中的其中一個元素，而香港的法制及政制歷史探究亦甚少涉獵電影製作，兩者之關連往往被忽略。 本研究旨在探討於上述期間香港電影對法律及法制的關注與當時社會議論紛紛的政制問題及概念之間的相通之處，用以展示電影作為珍貴一手資料如何呈現香港人當時對香港的政制發展框架及其塑造的發展所抱有的期望、恐懼和想法，亦顯示探討電影製作當時之法制討論如何為解讀電影文本帶出新的詮釋。本文提供了一個研究電影與法律之間如何相互影響的新探究模式，亦將一直以來「法律與電影」研究的英美主導重心轉移至東亞電影上。 這份研究有賴主要研究員在法律及電影業相關之研究背景，糅合當代電影理論，「法律與電影」跨學科研究及一手資料探究，為「法律與電影」研究、電影研究、政制法例、香港流行文化以至殖民地法制文化研究作出貢獻。

17613915.label: Realisation of objectives
17613915.value: This study has culminated in a scholarly monograph on how Hong Kong cinema engages with constitutional controversies. It shows that Hong Kong films about law can be interpreted as cultural responses to legal debates that resonates in Hong Kong society. It further demonstrates that through a language specific to the medium (such as cinematography), film registers the affective states associated with these controversies, an aspect which is often elided in conventional analyses within law schools. The book proposal has been sent out and is under consideration by Cambridge University Press. The project focuses on 'law films', or films which either present fictional depictions of law and/or makes substantial references to real-life legal debates on issues such as Article 23 and women's rights. It considers a wide variety of genres, including courtroom dramas, gangster films, documentaries, and even erotic thrillers to demonstrate that film represents law through conventions specific to the medium. Through a series of historically-situated close readings of key film texts, it further demonstrates that thinking about film in the context of legal change can give rise to new interpretations of those texts. Moreover, I have taken on board reviewers' comments from when this project was first funded and expanded the scope of coverage beyond 1997. The analysis here considers the interaction between constitutional law and film from 1984 to 2018. The project can therefore be said not only to have fulfilled, but to have exceeded, its objectives.

17613915.label: Major findings and research outcome
17613915.value: The key finding is that Hong Kong cinema's persistent engagement with the law, either through fictional representations or through documentary depictions of ongoing constitutional events, can be approached as cultural responses to constitutional debates. These debates resonate not only amongst lawyers and jurists, but within society more broadly. The study further demonstrates how film constitutes a forum for understanding how major legal issues concerned not only changes in the law, but how people in Hong Kong constructed their sense of place and selfhood. It therefore underscores the importance of popular culture as a site for understanding constitutional controversies beyond their doctrinal dimensions.

17613915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17613915.value: The study focuses on Hong Kong. The PI already has a solid publication record on law and film in Hong Kong, and has recently co-edited a volume on law and media with key figures in law and film studies in the US and Europe(West of Everything: Law and New Media, forthcoming from Edinburgh University Press). The PI is well positioned to further the scope of research beyond Hong Kong, and to engage with more global manifestations of interactions between law and film. The PI will discuss with his collaborators about the possibility of exploring such global manifestations through an edited handbook on law and visual culture.

17613915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17613915.value: This project has produced the first book-length study of representations of law in Hong Kong cinema. It shows that films about the law can be interpreted as cultural responses to constitutional debates that are of great importance not only to lawyers and people in the legal profession, but to Hong Kong society at large. By considering the key genres within Hong Kong cinema, and by focusing on how meaning is expressed through elements of film language such as camerawork and the use of sound, it demonstrates the importance of the study of popular culture for a fuller understanding of constitutional law in the Hong Kong context.

17614515.value: The three objectives are achieved fully. 17614515.label: Major findings and research outcome
17614515.value: As reflected by the 157 lung cancer patients participated in the study, they experienced significant improvement in physical, emotional and spiritual domains of quality of life irrespective of the type of intervention they received. Compared to I-BMS, CBT led to a greater reduction in emotional vulnerability. Relative to CBT, I-BMS resulted in a greater increase in overall quality of life, spiritual self-care and self-control, as well as more reduction in depression. I-BMS is found to be more effective in improving diverse domains of quality of life, while the effects of CBT concentrate on emotional well-being. Similarly, the respective family caregivers of both groups exhibited statistically significant improvement in the generic quality of life. In addition, Improvement of insomnia, reduction of anxiety and perceived stress were found at follow-up. I-BMS and CBT exhibited equivalent effectiveness in improving psychological distress and generic quality of life. Using the baseline data, actor-partner interdependence modelling was used to analyze the relationships among death anxiety, dysfunctional attitudes, and quality of life. In patients, death anxiety was related to dependency (β = .51) and self-control (β = -.37); achievement (β = -.21) and self-control (β = .34) were related to quality of life. Among caregivers, death anxiety was related to all 3 dysfunctional attitudes of their own (βs = .23 to.32); dependency (β = -.22) was associated with quality of life. Caregiver quality of life was also associated with patient self-control (β = .22) and achievement (β = -.18). Patient self-control mediated the links between patient death anxiety with both patient and caregiver quality of life. The relationship between death anxiety and quality of life was mediated by dependency on caregivers. In sum, the two intervention approaches are found to be effective to facilitate positive psychosocial outcomes in facing lung cancer by both patients and family caregivers. For patients, the two intervention has different strengths. Care professionals are encouraged to dispense interventions based on the idiosyncratic needs and preferences of the patients to maximize the treatment effects.

17614515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17614515.value: Two manuals were produced for the two intervention and co-workers from NGOs were trained in offering the intervention. As the interventions are both found to be having a positive effect on the patients and families, the NGOs can continue to offer these interventions. As there was a differentiated aspect of the effect of the two interventions, further research on “what works for whom” by identifying the moderators of two intervention will be helpful.

17614515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17614515.value: A cancer diagnosis is more than a medical condition, It usually brings significant psycho-socio-spiritual distress. The study developed and tested two psychosocial intervention for lung cancer patients and their family caregivers, which both consist of 8-weekly group sessions respectively. Integrative Body-Mind-Spirit (I-BMS) approach was compared with Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT). There were 157 dyads of patients and family caregivers participated in the study. Patients, who received the two interventions respectively, were found to have improved quality of life. CBT is found to improve the ability of patients in facing emotional vulnerability. On the other hand, I-BMS led to a greater increase in overall quality of life, spiritual self-care and self-control, as well as more reduction in depression. As for the family caregivers, they showed comparative improvement in insomnia, reduction of anxiety and perceived stress. This study provides culturally-sensitive evidence for offering holistic care to both lung cancer patients and family caregivers.

17614815.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17614815.value: 日治台灣通俗文化與漢文小說中現代性的表述

17614815.label: Project Objectives
17614815.value: To revise the customary view that Taiwan’s new literature movement marked the beginning of the country’s literary modernity and the common assumption that Taiwanese literature under Japanese rule was intrinsically anti-colonial and nationalistic. To analyse the impact of print culture on Taiwanese literati writers’ conceptualisation of modernity and global imagination. To shy away from the existing Western-focused, nation-centric approach by highlighting global knowledge diffusion and the roles of individual agencies. To examine the signs of reform and innovation discernable in popular genres that remain understudied thus far, particularly in English-language scholarship. To scrutinise the emergence and evolution of certain popular literary genres and media culture in colonial Taiwan.

17614815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17614815.value: Taiwan’s literary historiography has recently undergone several paradigm shifts - one clear example being the replacement of China-centrism with a Taiwan-oriented perspective. Despite the continued rewriting of Taiwan’s literary history, studies on literature from colonial Taiwan have so far concentrated on the anticolonial ‘tradition’. They have tended to start from the emergence of vernacular literature in the 1920s and highlight works espousing national characteristics. Pre-1920s works, especially the semi-vernacular popular narratives, and post-1920s works dealing with ‘small’ matters have consequently received insufficient study. This project will redress this situation by examining the experiences of modernity reflected through popular fiction, films and songs throughout Taiwan’s entire colonial period. It will analyse the authors’ literary imagination and also the visual representations of Taiwan in each case. The project will address questions that at best have only been partially answered in previous studies: how was modernity articulated in the traditionally-trained literati’s works, and in the concurrent films and songs? What happened during the process of localisation when foreign genres were introduced into Taiwan? How did print culture accelerate knowledge exchange, and how can we understand Japan’s colonialism in Taiwan without the colonised/coloniser dichotomy? Employing textual analysis and genre studies, and paying attention to the production and reception of certain literary/art works, my work will offer an internationally pioneering study on colonial Taiwan, and provide the most in-depth scrutiny of this topic available in English. It will critically examine the anticolonial ‘grand narrative’ in existing historiographies and contextualise Taiwan’s literary field under Japanese rule before developing three case studies. The first will concern the cultural influences and literary inspirations from both the West and China in pre-1920s works by Taiwan’s literati authors, particularly knight-errant/historical fiction and detective stories. The second will investigate the rise of entertainment-oriented Chinese-language tabloids in the 1930s and discuss certain serialised novels in those tabloids, with an emphasis on the themes of new/modern women, romance and family. The third will analyse representative films and songs in the 1930s and 1940s, discussing how popular culture became entangled with wartime mobilisation. By underlining intra-Asian cultural encounters and the individual writer’s role as a cultural mediator, this research will provide an alternative to the master anticolonial literary history and a fresh perspective on colonial Taiwan. It will contend that quotidian modernism reflected through popular forms demonstrates the intricate balance between the authors’ social/moral imperatives and commercial sensibilities, and the intrinsic instability of colonial discourse. 台灣文學史在過去數十年歷經多次典範的轉移，從中國中心到以台灣為中心的史觀的過渡即為一鮮明的例證。儘管台灣文學史持續被重寫，對日治台灣的文學研究大抵仍側重反殖民的“傳統”。學者們多以1920年代白話文之興起作為起始點，強調具國族意識的文本。因此，1920年代前的通俗敘事，及1920年代後關注“小”議題的作品迄今仍有待進一步之深究。 本研究檢視日治五十年通俗小說、電影、歌曲中折射出的現代性經驗，以呈現反殖民之外的另類經驗。主要分析：現代性在通俗文學及影音作品中如何被再現？當外國文類傳入台灣後，台灣作家如何肆應？媒體文化如何加速知識交匯？而在殖民者／被殖民者的對立框架外，可如何理解台灣的殖民經驗？ 結合文本與文類分析，也關注文藝作品的接受過程，本研究首先對現存的反殖民大敘述提出回應。之後將分別探討1920年代前台灣的漢文通俗敘事；1920年代興起的漢文娛樂小報中的婚戀小說；及1930－1940年代的電影與流行歌曲。本研究強調中、日、台之間的文化流動，與個別作家作為文化折衝者的角色，主張通俗文化形式中流露的日常現代性不但說明了作者們的社會／道德誡命與商業感性間的微妙平衡，也說明了殖民話語本身的不穩定性。

17614815.label: Realisation of objectives
17614815.value: By working on colonial Taiwan's popular narratives published in various newspapers and journals, I naturally shy away from the still dominant nationalist discourse and acknowledge the relationship between print culture and (Taiwan's) colonial modernity. Hence, the first two objectives are easily achieved. I particularly pay attention to the less well-known authors and journals as well as understudied genres, such as historical narratives and detective stories. I have presented papers based on my finings at various international conferences, and have published several chapters. Hence, the last two objectives have been met. As for the third objective, I in my articles emphasise the selected authors' aesthetic styles, arguing that they re-invented the West-originated genres in order to make their works more attractive to their targeted local readers. In other words, while they borrowed some foreign elements, their works should be seen as local or localised literary products. In this way, the third objective has been achieved. The main planned output is a single-authored book manuscript. The full draft is more than half ready. The slight delay of my writing schedule is partly because I had to spend time completing another book (Colonial Taiwan: Negotiating Identities and Modernities through Literature) for my tenure and promotion application, and partly because I was editing two books and had full workload in terms of postgraduate supervision (I have 6 students, the maximum number allowed) at the same time. Nevertheless, I have successfully published my new findings in smaller instillments such as journal articles and book chapters. In my book Colonial Taiwan published in 2017, the newly written and added Chapter 3 contains findings of this project. In the edited volume Encounters and Transformations, there is also one chapter which is directly related to this project. And in the book East Asian Transwar Popular Culture: Literature and Film from Taiwan and Korea I co-authored, one chapter arises directly from this project. A journal article is forthcoming from the highly regarded peer-reviewed journal Asian Studies Review. I am preparing one journal article (in Chinese), and I have one English article under review by Brill as a book chapter. In addition to this I was won the prestigious 2015/2016 Yenching Visiting Scholarship by Harvard University based on a smaller segment of this GRF project, was selected to present my research (related to this project) at its 90th year anniversary celebratory conference held in Shanghai, and awarded the Harvard Yenching Workshop Grant to run a workshop (at which I presented findings of this project too), and gave 2 keynote lectures (in Hong Kong and Taiwan) and a string of other conference presentations related to the project globally.

17614815.label: Major findings and research outcome
17614815.value: The project has the archival depth and conceptual breadth that enables it to make a fresh contribution to the existing colonial Taiwan's literary studies. Despite some scholarly attention made to this period's popular narratives, the research so far remains scattered. By focusing on not just the genre romance, my project excavates several little discussed works that warrant scrutiny in order to gain a more balanced picture of the evolvement of Taiwan's new literature, as well as of Taiwan's multilayered colonial modernity. The systematic study of colonial Taiwan's popular narratives and the approach of colonial Taiwanese literature as a result of global literary circuits make major strengths and contributions of the project. It argues that while Japanese became a dominant "national language" during Taiwan's colonial era, Chinese-language writing never became obsolete. Rather, it played an important role in colonial Taiwan's literary landscape. It also points out that while vernacular writing became the mainstream since the mid-1920s, those "new" works are not necessarily "progressive" in terms of the messages conveyed. In a similar vein, those written before in the style of semi-classical and semi-vernacular are not void of "modern" elements as one might have assumed. Some of my major findings are published in my single-authored book entitled Colonial Taiwan: Negotiating Identities and Modernity through Literature (2017). One reviewer noted that "it charts exciting new scholarly waters" (Karen Thornber at Harvard), and two commented that "its depth and path breaking methodology make it a significant addition to the field" (Bert Scruggs, UC Irvine), and "it takes on the important task of deconstructing the 'patriot v.s. traitor' framework (Yvonne Sung-sheng Chang, UT Austin). An edited volume entitled East Asian Transwar Popular Culture: Literature and Film from Taiwan and Korea contains one chapter based on my findings. I have also given talks on my findings at international conferences such as the Association for Asian Studies (AAS) annual meeting, and by invitation at UC Santa Barbara in January 2019.

17614815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17614815.value: From now on, I will concentrate on writing up the remaining chapters of the planned book (the major planned output), and I have been making steady progress. I have discussed my main ideas and possible book title with Professor Rey Chow from Duke University. I will complete the full manuscript and send it out for professional copy-editing at the end of this year and submit the manuscript to the press in springtime next year. I shall be attending the AAS annual meeting in 2020 in Boston to meet some potential publishers such as the Cornell University Press, and Washington University Press. I will also follow up on the publication of my article in Asian Studies Review, and the book chapter which is under review by Brill with the book editor. In addition, I will complete a journal article in Chinese (on one of the authors covered by this project) and submit it at my earliest convenience. I have been invited to give a talk on popular narratives from colonial Taiwan at the SOAS (University of London) in mid-June 2019 as part of its annual Taiwan Studies summer programme, and am preparing for it.

17614815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17614815.value: In any postcolonial societies, studies on colonial literature are usually dominated by nationalist narrative in which works with a distinct anti-colonial theme becomes privileged. For colonial Taiwanese literature studies, existing scholarship in English tends to treat Taiwan as part of the Japanese empire studies. This often leads to the result that Japan's culture influence is taken for granted and only Japanese-language works are covered. Given colonial Taiwan's cultural affinity primarily with China and Japan, research on colonial Taiwanese popular narratives takes a global comparative perspective in nature. The significance and value of this project is at least three-fold. First, it presents a more balanced view on the diversity of literary production of Taiwan under Japanese rule. Second, it focuses on the works written in Chinese and maps out Taiwanese authors' selective appropriation of non-Taiwanese sources so as to explore and establish their styles. Third, the planned book will make the first full-length study on colonial Taiwan's popular literature in English. It will not only enhance the visibility of Taiwanese literature but also add an East Asian case study to the field of colonial or Japanese empire studies.

17615115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17615115.value: Students from East Asia have consistently out-performed their counterparts from Western countries in recent international studies of mathematics achievement such as TIMSS and PISA. While a cultural explanation has been suggested to account for the differences in achievement, the role of language, an important component of culture, in affecting students’ processing of mathematics items in different languages has not been studied in the past. This study investigates the differences in linguistic structure between the TIMSS mathematics word problem items in Chinese and in English, and the impact of the differences on Chinese speaking and English speaking fourth graders in Taiwan and Australia respectively when they process the mathematics items in the two languages. Social network analysis (using the software UCINET) will be utilized to study the linguistics structure of the TIMSS word problem items in Chinese and in English, and eye-movements tracking (using the EyeLink 1000 eye-tracker) will be employed to study students’ processing of the items in the two languages. In the proposed study, the expertise of the PI and the three Co-Is complement each other – the PI’s research has been on comparative studies of mathematics education and the influence of culture on mathematics learning and teaching; Co-I3 has rich experience in research involving neural science; Co-I2’s research has been on the influence of language on mathematics learning; while Co-I1 is an applied linguist and language education expert. This project will fill the gap of knowledge in this under-researched field of the influence of language on mathematics learning and achievement. The research instruments and methodology adopted in the study will serve as important reference for future studies in this area. The findings will contribute to better interpretation of the results of international studies of mathematics achievement such as TIMSS where multiple languages are used in the tests, and may provide insight in cracking the so-called Chinese Learner’s Paradox in mathematics education – the fact that Chinese learners achieve well despite unfavourable learning conditions. This project is of special relevance to Hong Kong, as it will throw light on the issue of the medium of instruction in schools, an issue that has attracted great attention in the education community and beyond in the past twenty years. 東亞學生近年在如TIMSS和PISA等國際數學比較研究中，成績比西方國家優勝。有學者從文化角度解釋成績差易，但文化其中一重要元素 - 語言 - 如何影響學生處理數學題卻鮮有研究。本研究旨在探討漢語和英語的不同語言結構如何影響台灣及澳洲學生處理數學題。研究採取社會網絡分析方法(利用UCINET軟件) 分析漢語和英語TIMSS文字題的語言結構，並且用眼球追蹤方法(利用 EyeLink-1000眼動儀) 研究學生如何運用這兩語言處理數學題。本研究補充了語言如何影響數學學習及成績這研究領域的欠缺。研究所採用的儀器及方法，將為這研究領域帶來參考作用。研究結果可幫助我們詮釋如TIMSS等採用多種語言的國際數學比較研究之結果，並且為解釋中國學習者悖論 (指中國學習者在不利環境下仍能成績優異)帶來亮光。本研究對過去20年香港教育界所關注的教學語言問題亦有參考作用。

17615115.label: Realisation of objectives
17615115.value: As reported last time, the project was seriously delayed due to the unexpected changes in circumstances. There was change in circumstances of the job of Co-I Prof Yang in his university in Taiwan, and the Taiwan part of the project was then carried on by his student William, who was also supposed to assist Co-I Dr Lai in her collection of eye-tracking data in Australia. The other Co-I, Dr Lai changed her job in summer 2017 from working in Flinders University (in Adelaide) to Australian Catholic University (ACU) (in Melbourne), and since we were planning to collect data from Melbourne instead of Adelaide, a new ethics approval from the State of Victoria was needed. Unfortunately, there were further changes in circumstances. Shortly after we learned of Dr Lai’s relocation to ACU, William informed us that he had decided to leave the academia, and could not continue working on the project. Luckily, I have been able to enlist the help of another expert in eye-tracking studies, Prof CJ Wu from Taiwan Normal University, to join the project and take charge of the data collection in Taiwan. With the help of Prof Wu and her assistant Genie, we have just finished data collection for the eye-tracking phase of the study in Taiwan (but because of some technical problems concerning the calibration of the instrument, we haven’t been able to start analysis of the eye-tracking data yet). On the Australian side, while we were waiting for ethics approval from Victoria, there was a further change in circumstance of Dr Lai. She decided to leave ACU and work in the University of Technology Sydney. So if we were to collect data in Sydney (instead of Adelaide or Melbourne), we would need to apply for ethics approval from New South Wales (instead of Victoria). After discussing all these complications with Dr Lai, we decided to revert to data collection in Adelaide (where ethics approval from South Australia is still valid). This will mean that Dr Lai (and Genie, who is now assisting Dr Lai in collecting eye-tracking data in Australia) needs to fly to Adelaide for data collection, and we will need to employ a research assistant in Flinders University to help in the data collection. This will require more funding, but it seems that this is the best way forward. The PI is determined to complete the study using his own resources, despite the ending of the funding from GRC. Item analysis of the English and Chinese TIMSS items has been completed (Objective 1 above), and the results are being analysed. Data collection for eye-tracking in Taiwan has just been completed, and data collection in Australia will start in March 2019 (Objective 2). After collecting all the data, we will proceed to analyse the whole data set (Objectives 2 and 3).

17615215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17615215.value: 過去的二十年, 在文化人類學，人口研究，社會和文化地理學，經濟學的領域，已有不少有關跨國移民, 尤其是並不停留在某一地方, 流動性高的移民的研究 。在社會語言學，有關流動的跨國移民研究, 他們的語言和文化習俗的工作比較少。王愛華（1999）認為，有關跨國移民的研究有助明白他們作為流動人口的社會條件及靈活性, 以及個人與國民身份的關系。本項目旨在研究在香港的印尼華僑, 他們的跨國移民歷史及流動性。 王蒼柏（2003）報告, 近五十萬印尼華僑在 20世紀50年代和60年代, 出於1949年以後對新中國的民族國家認同而回歸中國 。“回歸”意味著重新擁抱中國種族，文化和政治 。然而，他們的歸途是痛苦和有創傷性的，因為當時的中國拒絕承認他們是自己人, 使他們被孤立而不同於"人民"。Godley, M. R. & Coppel, C.A. (1990) 指出, 因為對他們在中國的經歷失望，在20世紀70年代, 當中國放鬆了對這些“海歸” 華僑的出入管制, 超過 25 萬在中國的印尼華僑及他們的後代移民到港澳。但是, 成為香港的新移民使他們再次被邊緣化。 這些印尼華僑保留了獨特的語言和文化風俗, 標誌著他們與其他中國人的不同。香港的印尼華僑懂多種語言: 華僑國語, 先達國語, 潮洲話, 閩南語, 客家話, 廣東話, 印尼多種語言(例如印尼話, 爪哇話, 瑪達話)等等。他們愛聽印尼民歌，跳印尼民歌舞蹈, 穿印尼服飾, 享受印尼和峇峇娘惹食物，與印尼的中國人保持密切的親屬關係，並對他們自身的國民身份有一個矛盾的態度 。本研究以民族誌的方法來研究在香港的印尼華僑以及他們的網絡, 以了解他們的流動性, 和個人與國民/民族身份的關系。

Because of the unique qualities of lexical tones, we will be able to assess the development of SRM in children starting from a much earlier time window than previous developmental studies using non-tonal languages could offer. 18100415.label: Realisation of objectives
18100415.value: Experiment 1 Experiment 1 yielded a total of 52 sets of data form children participants aged 3;6 to 6;11, which has achieved 100% of the target in the proposal to address the requirements for achieving Objectives (1), (2) and (3). Spatial release of masking (SRM) is a measure of the ability of an individual to perform target speech stream-noise stream segregation by assessing the extent of improvement of the individual’s speech recognition performance when the noise stream is switched from a spatially co-located position with reference to the target-speech stream (e.g., target speech and noise stream both from the front) to a spatially separated position (e.g., target speech stream from the front and noise stream from the side). SRM is measure of the head shadow and binaural unmasking benefits. SRM has never been investigated thoroughly in children in such a young age in the international literature due to the lack of reliable speech recognition testing materials for young children especially under testing conditions with masking noise. This research study was a very first attempt to measure SRM in very young children starting from 3 years of age. MAndarin Spoken word - Picture IDentification Test in noise - Adaptive (MAPID-A) was developed, in a closed-set picture identification format, to investigate speech-recognition-in-noise and SRM performance in young Mandarin-speaking children which significantly limits testing time less than 5 minutes using an adaptive testing format. Mono- or disyllabic words carrying lexical tones were used to determine the performance to signal-to-noise ratio (P-SNR) functions of 40 native Mandarin-speaking aged 3.6–6.2 years with normal speech, language and hearing performance. The test item difficulty was homogenized by adjusting the speech intensity level of each item so that the adjusted signal-to-noise ratio for 50% score (SNR-50%) point would overlap at the mean SNR-50% point of all test items. In MAPID-A, homogenized test items were randomly presented in an adaptive testing procedure at a fixed noise intensity level, whereas the speech intensity levels varied in 2-dB SNR steps depending on the response result to each test item (i.e., a 2-dB decrease in intensity (or SNR) for the next item after correct identification of the previous test item, or a 2-dB increase in intensity (or SNR) for the next item after incorrect identification of the previous test item). The SNR reversal point is marked by a change from a decrease to an increase in the SNR or vice versa. Two successive SNR reversal points marked the boundaries of an excursion. The mid-points (in dB SNR) from 12 excursions were averaged to produce the adaptive SNR-50% measure (aSNR-50%). The aSNR-50% results were obtained from another 12 children aged 4.8–5.3 years with normal speech, language and hearing. The average 99% confidence interval (CI) of all participants’ mean aSNR-50% values determined using the mid-points of 12 excursions and the combined results of 2 test rounds per participant per test condition was ±1.61 dB SNR. In other words, 3.22 dB SNR was the average critical difference required to confirm a significant difference in the scores obtained from the same participant under 2 test conditions. Statistically significant SRM was identified in 95% of the intra-participant comparisons; in other words, aSNR-50% obtained from the speech and noise directions of spatially separated conditions (speech from the front and noise from either right or left) outperformed the result obtained from the directions of spatially co-located conditions (speech and noise both from the front). The adaptive testing procedure was highly reliable, with an intra-participant test-retest reliability of 90.6%. See 6.1 below for research outcomes of Experiment 1. The results for Experiment 1 for Objective (2) on the development of the adaptive testing procedures for obtaining the reliability speech-in-noise recognition and SRM measures was published in the journal Public Library of Science (PLoS) in Jan 2019 (Yuen, et al., 2019). Experiment 2 Experiment 2 developed for Objectives (2) and (3) yielded a total of 658 sets of data children aged 3;0 to 6;11, which has achieved 98% of the target in the proposal. Experiment 2 investigated the development of SRM in children using closed-set Mandarin disyllabic words and monosyllabic words carrying lexical tones as test stimuli and speech spectrum-weighted noise (SSN), four-talker babble (4BN), and two-talker babble (2BN) as maskers. SNR-50% improved with age in speech-front/noise-right (NR) or speech-front/noise-left (NL) but not speech-front/noise-front (NF). See 6.1 below for research outcomes of Experiment 2. The results for Experiment 2 for Objective (1) on assessing the development of SRM in children has been presented in the Dublin conference (Yuen et al., 2016). The manuscript which reports these results is under preparation. Experiment 2 also investigated the effects of different degrees of informational masking in the masker signal (from speech spectrum noise to four-talker babble to one-talker babble) on the development of SRM in young children. This experiment investigated the effects of an energetic noise masker: SSN, and two informational noise maskers: 4BN, and 2BN on the speech-recognition-in-noise and spatial-release-from-masking (SRM) performance in young children. MAPID-A yielded the adaptive signal-to-noise ratio for 50% correct score (aSNR-50%) under two different noise masker direction conditions: (a) speech and noise both presented from the front (NF), and (b) speech presented from the front and noise presented from right (NR) or left (NL) via a closed-set auditory-word picture-pointing identification task. The three noise maskers revealed the differences in energetic versus informational masking for speech recognition, and their relative degrees of SRM. Only 3 minutes were needed to obtain an aSNR-50% mean score with its 99% confident interval per testing condition. See 6.1 below for research outcomes of Experiment 2. The degree of discrepant SRMs obtained from energetic versus information maskers opens a new window to research the development of speech recognition-in-noise in young children. The said testing procedures offer a new opportunity differentially diagnosis normal versus disordered central auditory processing functions and evaluate the benefits of hearing prostheses in reducing the interfering effects of masker noises. The results for Experiment 2 for Objective (3) on assessing the effects of masker type on SRM has been presented in the conference presentation in 2018 (Yuen et al, 2018). The manuscript which reports these results is under preparation.

18100415.label: Major findings and research outcome
18100415.value: From Experiment 1, the narrow confidence intervals and high test-retest reliability level of the aSNR-50% outcome measure obtained from the newly developed MAndarin Spoken word - Picture IDentification Test in noise - Adaptive (MAPID-A) suggest that it is a promising sensitive, reliable and time-efficient clinical tool to detect subtle speech-recognition-in-noise changes in children as young as 4–5 years, and to reflect the neurophysiology development of the auditory neural pathway. The MAPID-A will help to track the subtle intra-participant developmental progression of the spatial release from masking (SRM) which is a collective measure of the benefits of head shadow and binaural unmasking with respect to the efferent auditory neural pathway and thus, to identify developmental disorders. From Experiment 2, the difference in SNR-50% between NR and NF, and NL and NF, or SRM, increased with age with an average improvement of 0.1-0.15 dB per month. SRM has a long developmental time, at least up to 6 years of age, which is significantly longer than some previous developmental studies have suggested. The child participants had not yet reached the adult SRM performance level. SRM is a potential clinical measure to reflect the maturation of spatial hearing Also, from Experiment 2, the results systematically showed that aSNR-50% of two-talker babble (2TB) outperformed those from four-talker babble (4TB) and speech-spectrum weighted noise (SSN), whereas 4TB outperformed those from SSN in all noise direction conditions (NF, NR, and NL). SRM was significantly lower in the energetic masker SSN and the information maskers 4BN and 2BN. The discrepancies in aSNR-50% and SRM yielded from different maskers reflect how young children develop active listening skills in noise by taking advantage of the relatively “silent” gaps in the more modulated 2BN and 4BN than the stationary SSN. A developmental trend was found for SRM differences across masker noises. The children participants had not yet reached the adults aSNR50% and SRM performance levels. The degree of discrepant SRMs obtained from energetic versus information maskers opens a new window to research the development of speech recognition-in-noise in young children. The said testing procedures offer a new opportunity differentially diagnosis normal versus disordered central auditory processing functions and evaluate the benefits of hearing prostheses in reducing the interfering effects of masker noises.

18100415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18100415.value: MAPID-A has already been deployed to assess the speech-recognition-in-noise benefits of very young children as young as 3 years old who were fitted with cochlear implants in one ear and hearing aids in the contralateral ear, or bimodally. MAPID-A answers the question for each bimodally fitted child that if there are any statistically significant additional benefits from adding the contralateral hearing aid to the cochlear implant only baseline condition. The results would be instrumental for frontline clinicians including audiologists, speech-language pathologists, and otologists to review and revise the rehabilitation options for each of their pediatric patients individually. Another steps planning underway is to assess the speech-in-noise recognition additional benefits of sequential bilaterally implanted on the additional benefits by the second implant compared with the first implant baseline performance.

18100415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18100415.value: This project produced the computerized testing software MAndarin Spoken word - Picture IDentification Test in noise - Adaptive (MAPID-A). MAPID-A is a very first attempt to assess very young children’s abilities to recognize spoken words, which they are familiar with, under noisy environments. The results revealed that MAPID-A was able to test children as young as 3 years of age reliability which was scare in international literature. MAPID-A offers an error estimate, i.e. 99% confidence interval， for each score, therefore allowing two scores obtained repeatedly from the same participant to be compared to check the presence of statistical difference. This comparison is invaluable to assess individual participant’s change in performance due to maturation, noise type and direction, and rehabilitation strategies. MAPID-A has opened an unprecedented window to researchers in pediatric hearing science to understand the development of listening skills in young children under adverse noisy situations including listening in noise, listening skills using two ears than just one ear (i.e. binaural benefits), and right-left performance discrepancies in listening (i.e. right ear advantage), and also to validate new intervention methods such as new hearing aid and cochlear implant noise reduction algorithms, and direct intervention to improve listening in noise.

18300215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18300215.value: Indexing of data is the very first and crucial step in many data processing applications. Suffix-based indices, such as suffix tree [23], suffix array [15], BWT (Burrows-Wheeler Transform) and FM-Index, have become the indispensable fundamental index structures for full-text search of string data, especially for use in bioinformatics [22]. The aim of this project is to explore, by utilizing some very recent results on external memory suffix sorting [47, 49, 52, 53], new algorithms that would be able to build and use big suffix-based full-text indices to process massive string data at a high throughput, and to develop the essential system technologies for linking these algorithms to applications. The algorithms to be developed are universal for full-text retrievals of both genome and text data. Recently, we have successfully extended our well-known internal memory algorithms SA-IS and SA-DS [51] to the external memory domain, resulting in two algorithms called DSA-IS [53] and EM-SA-DS [52] for sorting suffixes in external memory. The experimental results collected in [47, 52, 53] show that the induced sorting technique can work efficiently in both internal memory and external memory. With these new developments, we are now able to use a computer with a massive disk to build big suffix trees and suffix arrays with much better time and space efficiency. As the next move, we need to consider how to further develop efficient distributed algorithms to scale the problem’s size and solving speed. The first step in this research is to design a general-purpose distributed algorithm for building a big suffix tree using a cluster of computers in a high-speed local area network (LAN) such as Gigabit Ethernet. The second step is to further optimize the general-purpose distributed suffix tree construction algorithm for building a k-order truncated suffix tree [20, 21], in which each suffix is truncated to a fixed length of at most k characters, where k is far less than n for a size-n input string when n is large. Once a big suffix tree (full-order or truncated) has been efficiently built, the third step is to explore new efficient algorithms for using big suffix trees to provide the capability of full-text search in large-scale genome and text databases. Finally, all the source code in C++ for the algorithms developed in the previous steps will be engineered as a library for project achievement demonstration and use by third-party applications. 數據的索引是在許多數據處理應用的第一和關鍵的一步。後綴為基礎的指數，如後綴樹，後綴陣，Burrows-Wheeler變換（BWT）和微小空間中的全文索引（FM-指數），特別是在生物信息學中的使用，已成為在字符串的數據進行全文搜索中不可缺少的基本指數結構。為了趕上處理不斷增大的大型數據庫的需求，本項目旨在探索更高效的算法，以處理高吞吐量的大量字符串數據。通過使用一些最近於外部存儲器上對後綴排序的結果，算法將能夠建立和使用以後綴為基礎的大型全文索引。此外，我們將開發必要的系統技術，用於連接這些算法與應用。待開發的算法是能普遍使用於基因組和文本數據的全文檢索。 最近，我們已成功地擴展我們熟知的內部存儲器算法的SA-IS和SA-DS到外部存儲器的領域，開發了兩種算法稱為DSA-IS和EM-SA-DS以在外部存儲器中作後綴排序。我們最近的實驗結果收集得來的數據顯示，誘導的排序技術可以在內部存儲器和外部存儲器有效地工作。有了這些新的進展，我們現在能夠使用一台擁有大容量的磁盤打造具有更好的時間和空間效率的後綴樹和後綴陣列。至於下一步的工作，我們需要考慮如何進一步發展高效的分佈式算法來縮放問題的規模和求解速度。 本研究項目的第一個步驟是設計一個可運行在一個高速局域網（LAN），例如千兆以太網，中計算機集群的一個構建大後綴樹分佈式算法。第二步驟是進一步優化通用分佈式後綴樹構造算法構建的k階截斷後綴樹，其中每個後綴被截斷為固定長度不超過k個字符。當輸入字符串的長度n很大時，k的數值則遠小於n。一旦能有效建成一棵大的後綴樹（全階或截斷），第三步是開發新的有效算法，以使用大後綴樹於大規模基因組和全文數據庫中的進行全文檢索。最後，是把所開發的算法的C++源代碼，將製作成資料設計作為庫，以展示項目成果及供第三方應用。

18300215.label: Realisation of objectives
18300215.value: Objective-1: Sorting the suffixes of an input string is a fundamental task in many applications such as data compression, genome alignment and full-text search. The induced sorting (IS) method has been applied to design a number of state-of-the-art suffix sorting algorithms. In particular, the SAIS algorithm designed by the IS method is not only linear time but also fast in practice. However, the parallelization of SAIS remains a challenge due to that the induced sorting process in the algorithm is inherently sequential and the performance bottleneck of the whole algorithm. In this part of the project, we designed a parallel variant of SAIS on a multicore machine which is considered as a shared memory parallel model, called pSAIS (parallel SAIS). By a combined use of pipeline and parallel techniques, the inducing process is significantly accelerated using threads to execute the jobs in parallel. By parallelizing each step in the sequential algorithm SAIS, our parallel algorithm pSAIS is shown in Algorithm 1 [1]. The pSAIS is a parallel variant of SAIS in terms of that both have a same algorithmic framework to solve the problem recursively in linear time. The induced sorting process is the performance bottleneck of SAIS, which consumes about half of the total time. It is inherently sequential and the key problem to be solved for turning SAIS into pSAIS. Algorithm 2 [1] shows this process for inducing the order of all the L-type suffixes from the sorted LMS-suffixes. The latter iteration of the loop may read an item in SA written by the former one. In pSAIS, we guaranteed the writing of such an item happens before the reading. Objective-2: Given a size-n input text T and its suffix array, a new method was proposed to compute the K-order longest common prefix (LCP) array for T, where the maximum LCP of two suffixes of T is truncated to be at most K [2]. The method uses a fingerprint function to convert the comparison of two variable-length strings to the comparison of two fixed-size integers, where each integer is the fingerprint of a string. This method can be easily applied on the internal memory, external memory and distributed models, and the time and space complexities are universal as O(n log⁡K ) and O(n) respectively. It is scalable for a typical distributed model of a cluster of d computing nodes, where the time and space complexities are evenly divided onto each node as O((n log⁡K )/d) and O(n/d) respectively. It had been observed from that the average LCPs are typically small for realistic data, or the string T consists of many short strings so that the LCP of any two short strings is upper bounded by the longest size of a short string (e.g., T is a genome database). In these cases, the original full-order LCP-array is actually a K-order LCP-array, where K is the maximum LCP value which is typically far less than the size of T. This motivated us to design a practical algorithm for computing the K-order LCP-array of T, which is defined as: given any two neighboring suffixes in the SA of T, the K-order LCP of them is the longest common prefix of their first K characters, where K is far less than |T|. This work mainly contributed to the following two aspects. The first is to design and implement a K-order LCP-array construction method applicable to the typical internal and external memory models, which can build the LCP-array in O(n log⁡K ) time and O(n) space using the LCP batch querying technique (LCP-BQT) previously proposed for the sparse SA construction. This method can be easily applied on both the internal and external models. The program we developed for the external memory model is composed of less than 600 lines in C++. The second is to parallelize our new K-order LCP-array construction method in a distributed system consisting of a cluster of d computing nodes. The existing parallel LCP-array construction algorithms are mainly designed for shared memory models such as bulk synchronous parallel and parallel random-access machine. Our distributed model of clustered computers is popular in nowadays computation environments, and hence our method is easier to be deployed in practice. An experimental study was conducted for performance evaluation of this method running on the external memory and distributed models. A cluster of computers in a local area network are commonly available in practice, but there is currently a lack of scalable LCP-array construction algorithms for such a distributed model. Our algorithms provide a candidate solution to meet the demand. Objective-3: We parallelized the SAIS algorithm on a multicore machine without compromise, i.e., pSAIS is a pure parallel variant of SAIS by parallelizing each step of the latter in a systematic manner. Virtually, the methods proposed in this work can be applied to parallelize any algorithms using induced sorting, such as SACAK, libdivsufsort and saislite for suffix array construction and that for computing LCP arrays and LZ77 factorization. Because SACAK has an algorithm framework similar to that of SAIS and is more time and space efficient, we are parallelizing SACAK in this way to design an in-place, linear time and fast parallel algorithm for sorting suffixes of constant alphabets. We presented the pSACAK algorithm for the parallelization of induced sorting sufﬁxes in O(n) time and O(K) workspace on a multicore machine [3]. To the best of our knowledge, for a multicore machine, it is the only linear-time and in-place parallel sufﬁx sorting algorithm for constant alphabets reported so far. Since our recent work pSAIS has exploited the parallelism of IS method for efﬁcient memory accesses using multiple threads on a multicore machine, the focus here for designing pSACAK from SACAK is the pipelined induced sorting within the optimal O(K) workspace. A number of new techniques have been proposed to overcome the difﬁculties in the algorithm’s design. Our experimental results indicate that this new parallel algorithm is the most time and space efﬁcient among all in comparison. pSACAK is a parallel variant of the sequential SACAK, saying that both have a same algorithmic framework and the former is obtained by parallelizing each step of the latter. As a result, pSACAK not only keeps the linear-time and in-place merits of SACAK, but also runs several times faster by exploiting the parallel computing power of a multicore machine. While the number of cores and the memory bandwidth of a modern computer are consistently increased, there is a demand in practice for solutions capable of fully utilizing the parallelism of more and more computing resources provided by the machine. This work provided a solution to meet the demand for time and space efﬁcient sufﬁx sorting on a multicore machine. 18300215.label: Major findings and research outcome
18300215.value: We designed the pSAIS algorithm for the parallelization of induced sorting sufﬁxes on a multicore machine. The original sequential SAIS algorithm is memory access intensive. The idea for turning SAIS into pSAIS is to exploit the parallelism for random memory accesses without data race by using the multithreading capability of a modern multicore computer. By using multiple threads for executing memory accesses in parallel, the caches and the main memory are accessed more efﬁciently for maximizing the memory access throughput of pSAIS. In our experiments, the sequential operations of pSAIS contribute less than 20% of the total running time, which implies a good parallelism with fully utilization of the parallel computing power in a multicore machine. Moreover, pSAIS runs faster and uses less space than the existing parallel sufﬁx sorting algorithms. While pSAIS is designed for building big sufﬁx arrays in a multicore machine, our study also gives hints for extending the induced sorting method to GPU for constructing small sufﬁx arrays even faster. We proposed a practical K-order LCP-array construction method that can be easily applied on the internal and external memory models. The program for lcpa-disk-m is less than 600 lines when using STXXL to implement the external sorts. We showed that the proposed method can be extended for running on a typical distributed system of a cluster of d computing nodes, where the time and space complexities are evenly divided onto each node as O(nd(logK)) and O(nd), respectively. The proposed algorithms are simple in design and universal for the internal memory, external memory and distributed models. A cluster of computers in a LAN are commonly available in practice, but there is no scalable LCP-array construction algorithms for such a distributed model. Our algorithms provide solution to meet the demand. Finally, we gave the pSACAK algorithm for the parallelization of induced sorting sufﬁxes in O(n) time and O(K) workspace on a multicore machine. As we know for a multicore machine, it is the only linear-time and in-place parallel sufﬁx sorting algorithm for constant alphabets reported so far. Since our recent work pSAIS exploited the parallelism of IS method for efﬁcient memory accesses using multiple threads on a multicore machine, the focus for designing pSACAK from SACAK is the pipelined induced sorting within the optimal O(K) workspace. The new techniques proposed overcome the difﬁculties in the algorithm’s design. Our experimental results indicate this new parallel algorithm is the most time-and-space efﬁcient.

18300215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18300215.value: For performance improvement of the algorithms, we are investigating techniques to exploit the use of GPUs for speeding up the computation. Moreover, including the algorithms developed in this project, we have been ready to put the technical results into practice by setting up a platform for sorting, indexing and searching. In the next step, we would try to work with the industrial partners such as internet service providers, social media and networking operators and e-commerce companies which are handling huge amount of different types of data being generated every second to advance and develop data manipulating systems to cope with the needs in the upcoming AI and big data era.

18300215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18300215.value: Sorting the sufﬁxes of an input string is a fundamental task in many applications such as data compression, genome alignment, and full-text search. The induced sorting (IS) method has been applied to design a number of state-of-the-art sufﬁx sorting algorithms. In this project, we further investigated to turn the original algorithms running in internal and external memory to multicore computers which is a popular distributed model of clustered computers in nowadays computation environments, and our proposed methods are much easier to be deployed in practice. We developed pSAIS and pSACAK, the parallel variants of the IS algorithms SAIS and SACAK respectively, by a combined use of multithreading and pipelining to accelerate the inducing process by fully utilizing the machine’s parallel computing power. We showed with experimental results that the new algorithms have high degree of parallelism and achieve the best time and space performance among all parallel algorithms in comparison. A new method to compute the K-order longest common prefix (LCP) array of input text T (the maximum LCP of two suffixes of T being truncated to be at most K) has also been proposed. This method is scalable for a typical distributed model of a cluster of computing nodes.

18300415.label: Realisation of objectives
18300415.value: This project aimed to design a supramolecular chemical method to simultaneously detect and degrade organic pollutants. All the objectives were achieved. Throughout the period of investigation, (i) we designed and synthesized totally 11 new bimetallic donor-acceptor complexes, four Fe(II)-Cu(II), four Re(I)-Pt(II), one Ru(II)-Cu(I), one Fe(II)-Pt(II) and one Fe(II)-Au(I) bimetallic complexes. Also, three novel TiO2-Fe(III)-Fe(II)/Ru(II)/Os(II) materials were fabricated during this period. (ii) We found out that these complexes and materials could act as either selective chemodosimeters or chemosensors for a number of pollutants and environmental concern analytes such as cyanide, oxalic acid, sulfides, and organophosphate pesticides. Most importantly, they can simultaneously function as catalyst for pollutants' degradation. (iii) We have already understood the analyte-selectivity of the system which is controlled by the thermodynamics and kinetic of formation of the cyano linkage between metallic acceptor–donor. And (iv) we applied the developed technology to detect the analyte in real water bodies such as river, pond and sea water.

18300415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18300415.value: Selective detection and efficient degradation of persistent pollutants are major challenges in the world. Stable chemosensors that can provide reliable readouts and quick responses and advanced catalysts that can quickly oxidize and mineralize organic contaminants are in high demand. In this project, smart molecular devices/materials have been made to automatically degrade selected organic pollutants when specific levels reach a certain detection threshold is highly desirable. This discovery shed new light on how to real-time monitor and treat other dangerous chemical wastes. The scientific background of how the device can take up multifunctions simultaneously for detection, amplification, and elimination upon detection of organic pollutants was now understood. The researchers have been used the new smart devices for detection and degradation of various hazardous chemical wastes, such as oxalate, cyanide, pesticides and organic sulfide. Finally, the team applied this new technology on the complicated industrial wastewater and food systems.

18300715.label: Realisation of objectives
18300715.value: In this project, the photocatalytic regeneration of organohydride have been studied using a spectrum of 3d metal complexes bearing different macrocyclic or chelating pi-acceptor ligands, e.g. diimine-dioxime, iminopyridine and polypyridyl. As a result of the social movement and worldwide COVID-19 outbreak in 2019/20, the recruitment of RA (mainland China), part of the scheduled experimental works and the communication with the collaborators (Hong Kong and France) have been delayed. Thus, the dissemination of research outcome in forms of publication and conference presentation have been also delayed. A brief summary for the realization of the research objectives (1–5) is outlined below. 1) A series of mononuclear cobalt catalysts containing macrocyclic and chelating -acceptor ligands, e.g. diimino-dioximes and iminopyridine ligands have been prepared and structurally characterized by various analytical technique, including elemental analysis, mass spectrometry and X-ray crystallography. Cobalt diimino-dioxime complexes [Co(DO)(DOH)pnX2] (1 and 2; X = Cl and Br) and the BF2-bridged derivative [Co((DO)2BF2)pnBr2] (3) have been synthesized. In addition, the cobalt complexes of macrocyclic and tripodal iminopyridine ligands, i.e. [Co(CR)Cl2]+ (4) (CR = 2,12-dimethyl-3,7,11,17-tetraazabicyclo[11.3.1]-heptadeca-1(17),2,11,13,15-pentaene), [Co(tachpy3)]2+ (5) (tachpy3 = cis, cis-1,3,5-tris(pyridine-2-carboxaldimino)-cyclohexane) and [Co(trenpy3)]2+ (6) (trenpy3 = tris-[4-(2-pyridyl)-3-azabut-3-enyl]amine) have been also synthesized and characterized structurally. Besides, a series of 3d metal (Co, Cu and Fe) complexes bearing different polypyridyl-based pi-acceptor ligands have also been prepared and structurally characterized. The mononuclear copper complex [Cu(qpy)]2+ (7) (qpy = 2,2':6',2":6",2"'-quaterpyridine), Cu(I) diimine complexes, [Cu(N–N)(PPh3)2](ClO4) (8) as well as the 8-coordinate mononuclear complexes of dialkylcarboxylate diimine ligands [M(2,9-dcphen)2]3+ and [M(6,6'-dcbpy)2]3+ (9 –12) (M = Co and Fe, 2,9-dcphen = 2,9-dialkylcarboxylate-1,10-phenanthroline and 6,6'-dcbpy = 6,6'-dialkylcarboxylate-2,2'-bipyridine) have been synthesized. In addition, polynuclear Cu(I) complexes [Cu2(bppz)(PPh3)4]2+ (13) and [Cu3(btzim)(PPh3)6] (14) bearing the bridging chelating ligands 2,3-bis(2-pyridyl)pyrazine (bppz) and 2,3-bis(2-tetrazoyl)imidazole (btzim) were also prepared. 2) The catalytic activity of the cobalt diamino-dioxime complexes (1–3) for the reductive regeneration of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) and its synthetic analogue, 1-benzyl-1,4-dihydronicotinamide (1,4-BNAH), has been studied in pH 7 aqueous solutions, under electrocatalytic conditions by cyclic voltammetry (CV). The E(CoII/I) of complexes 1 and 2 (1 mM) occur similarly at –0.83 V vs SCE in pH 7 0.1M phosphate buffer. In the presence of 1 mM 1-benzylnicotinamide triflate (BNA+), a new cathodic wave is observed at a potential (–0.89 V vs SCE) slightly negative of the E(CoII/I). The peak current of the new cathodic wave further increases as the amount of BNA+ is increased (1–6 mM), suggesting the catalytic reduction of BNA+ is mediated by the CoI state. Similar catalytic current is also observed (onset at –0.87 V vs SCE) for 3 which exhibits a E(CoII/I) at –0.68 V vs SCE. Similar catalytic current was also observed when BNA+ is replaced by NAD+ in buffered pH 7 aqueous solutions for 1–3. The activity of the [Co(CR)Cl2]2+ (4) was similarly studied using cyclic voltammetry in aqueous solutions. The complex 4 (1mM) was found to be active catalyst for the reduction of BNA+, as demonstrated by the catalytic current occuring at –0.95 V vs SCE (E(CoII/I) = –0.85 V vs SCE), which increases with increasing amount of BNA+ (1–8 mM). Though some of the complexes 5–14 exhibit similar M(II/I) couple, no similar catalytic current for the reduction of BNA+ and NAD+ was observed in buffered aqueous solutions (pH 7) in their CV studies, showing that the complexes inactive for the reductive generation of BNAH and NADH under electrocatalytic conditions. On the other hand, their applications as catalysts for the reduction of carbon dioxide and water (Guo et al 2017 and Leung et al 2018), as well as their photophysical and magnetic properties (Hu et al 2017, Jin et al 2018 and Xiang et al 2019) were investigated and published in international peer-reviewed SCI journals (see Research Outcome). 3) The regeneration of the NADH synthetic analogue 1-benzyl-1,4-dihydronicotinamide (1,4-BNAH) was studied by using the Co diamino-dioxime catalysts (1–3). The yield of the regenerated organohydrides was monitored with both HPLC-UV and photoluminescence. By using respectively metal and organic photosensitizers, namely [RuII(bpy)3]2+, triazatriangulenium and xanthene dyes, 1–3 are found to catalyze the reduction of BNA+ to 1,4-BNAH under photochemical conditions in both aqueous and organic media in the presence of triethanolamine (TEOA) as the sacrificial donor. Under organic conditions 1,4-BNAH were obtained at maximum turnover number (TON, vs catalyst) of 31 and 20 with respectively metal and organic PS. The 1,4-BNAH were also catalytic produced at a maximum TON of 15 in aqueous solutions using these catalysts with xanthene dyes as photosensitizers. In addition, the cobalt macrocyclic iminopyridine complex (4) is also found to be active catalyst for 1,4-BNAH regeneration (TON = 10–20) under similar conditions. 4) The reaction pathway for the regeneration of 1,4-BNAH by catalysts 1 – 3 has been investigated by using chemical, as well electro- and photochemical approaches. To reveal the source of proton (H+) involved in the one-proton/two-electron process, the photocatalysis was performed in deuterated acetonitrile (CD3CN) containing 5% D2O. 1H NMR analysis of the reaction solution afterward showed that the signal of the characteristic methylene protons (CH2) at the 4-position of the 1,4-BNAH was reduced to a large extent in comparison to a reaction performed in CD3CN without added D2O, indicating the H+ in the reduction process originates from the water in the solvent. Moreover, in the controlled experiments performed in both acetonitrile and aqueous solutions without added BNA+, a much larger amount of H2 was obtained, suggesting the BNA+/BNAH reduction share a common reaction pathway as H2O reduction which are reported to proceed via a CoIII-H intermediate upon the protonation of a CoI state. Mechanism for the photocatalysis was also investigated by spectrophotometric technique such as transient absorption measurement (TA) and Stern-Volmer plot. TA measurement showed that the reduced photosensitizer (PS•-) is formed via the reductive quenching of the excited photosensitizer (PS*) by the sacrificial donor (TEOA), which probably reduced the catalyst to their Co(I) state, which was revealed in the above CV studies to mediate the BNA+/BNAH reduction. The formation of BNAH probably proceed via a hydride (H-) transfer from a CoIII-H species formed by the protonation of the CoI state, which is also well reported for water-to-hydrogen reduction catalyzed by cobalt coordination compounds. Results of the investigated have been published in a recent journal paper (Kwok et al 2020). 5) To assess the application of the catalysts in electro-, chemo- and photoenzymatic synthesis using various model enzyme/substrate combinations. The reductive generation of NADH from NAD+ was similarly studied under photocatalytic condition by using 1-3 as the catalyst with organic photosensitizer (xanthene dyes) in aqueous solutions. The production of NADH was verified by photoluminescence measurement and NADH was photocatalytically yielded at a TON of 10–20. When the photocatalysis was coupled with L-glutamate dehydrogenase (GDH), which catalyzes the NADH-driven L-glutamate synthesis from L-ketoglutarate, the desired product was obtained at a slightly lower TON of 7–10, indicating that the photogenerated NADH is enzymatically active. While detailed investigation are in progress, results will be presented in international conference in April 2021 (2020 Directing Biosynthesis VI, Edinburgh, rescheduled as a result of COVID-19).
