18611615.label: Major findings and research outcome
18611615.value: The overarching goal of this project investigated the nature and degree of co-occurrence in reading difficulties in Chinese (L1) and English (L2) among Hong Kong Chinese-speaking adolescent readers with dyslexia. It examined an array of cognitive-linguistic, oral language, language comprehension, and executive functioning aspects of L1 and L2 sensitivity in readers with dyslexia and those without problems and their cognitive and language profiles and subgroups of dyslexia. The findings revealed that readers with dyslexia tended to perform less well than the typically developing readers on the L1 and L2 measures of rapid naming, vocabulary knowledge, visual-orthographic knowledge, morphological skills, syntactic skills, discourse skills, executive functioning, and literacy skills. Multiple deficits in L1 and L2 cognitive and language skills were found in many readers with dyslexia. Among the subgroups of dyslexia, the typical functioning dyslexics generally exhibited a higher incidence of multiple cognitive-linguistic deficit profiles with significant deficits in rapid naming and more difficulties with reading and writing than the high-functioning dyslexics. Furthermore, these findings indicated that given that L1 and L2 are very distinctive languages the co-occurrence of literacy difficulties in the two languages was high. Hence, readers with dyslexia in L1 seemed to have some difficulties in their L2, resulting from cognitive-linguistic, oral language, language comprehension, and executive functioning weaknesses in their L1, which subsequently impeded their literacy skills. Together, these findings have identified both common and specific causes to literacy difficulties in L1 and L2. Phonological deficit is more specific to reading problems in L2, while visual-orthographic deficit is more specific to reading problems in L1. Deficits in morphological awareness, rapid naming and executive functioning of working memory and inhibition may be a common cause of reading difficulties in both languages. This project has published five journal articles, one book chapter, and five conference papers. Practically, the findings of this project may assist students who have clear difficulties in L1 and L2 reading to read better. The results may also enhance our understanding of the characteristics of reading difficulties in L1 and L2 among Chinese readers with dyslexia and thus help us to develop early identification tools and design appropriate treatment methods and intervention programs. Theoretically, the findings probably enhance our understanding of the potentially different etiologies of reading difficulties in Chinese and English and characteristics of the bilingual dyslexic population.

18611615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18611615.value: The Principal Investigator (PI) will explore the possibility of incorporating the findings based on this project into intervention programs that foster the cognitive-linguistic, oral language, language comprehension, and executive functioning skills important for reading and writing in English in order to enhance dyslexic students’ overall reading and writing skills. Also, PI will explore future work on the development of a teacher needs assessment tool for junior secondary students with dyslexia who are at risk of difficulties in English reading and writing. More research is also needed, especially on under which circumstances Chinese and English difficulties may co-occur and, relatedly, under which circumstances dyslexia in Chinese and English may occur across different time points from adolescence to early adulthood. It may be worthwhile to conduct longitudinal studies with more time points and increasing sample size to investigate how and whether the nature and causes of reading and writing difficulties for both languages may change over time.

18611615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18611615.value: This project investigated the nature and degree of co-occurrence of reading difficulties in Chinese as first language (L1) and English as second language (L2) among Chinese adolescent readers with dyslexia in Hong Kong, China. Findings showed that readers with dyslexia in general performed less well on a wide range of executive functioning, language, and literacy skills in L1 and L2 compared to their typically developing peers at grades from 5 to 8. Readers with dyslexia tended to show multiple difficulties in cognitive, language and literacy skills that in turn affected their reading performance. They also appeared to have difficulties in learning L2 in addition to their L1 and to be a heterogeneous group with a number of subgroups identified. Findings of this project highlight the need to consider the issue of how to identify reading and writing difficulties and provide effective interventions that foster different groups of adolescent readers with dyslexia to read and write in L1 and L2 across content areas in the school-based curriculum. The schools and government agencies may consider providing additional Chinese and English support programs for these readers at junior secondary levels in Hong Kong.

18612415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18612415.value: 強互惠是一種用自己的資源補償合作者（正強互惠）或是懲罰不合作者（負強互惠）的策略。強互惠是在進化過程中通過文化族群選擇發展而來。在大型的市場經濟社會中，強互惠起到在族群層面穩定合作行為的作用。個人層面強互惠的萌芽對於兒童親社會行為的發展，理解公平與社會正義，以及公民教育有重大意義。本研究指出不公平規避不足以解釋強互惠的產生，相反，兒童需要採納道德立場才能實施有代價的懲罰或補償/獎勵。也就是說，兒童作為第三方強互惠者並不是簡單的和事佬來減少不公平；他們其實是有道德準則的員警或啦啦隊, 他們獎勵合作者，補償受害者，懲罰不合作者以弘揚正義。本研究試圖驗證強互惠萌芽的道德立場假說，檢視與性別，心智理論，同理心，以及衝動控制和延遲滿足有關的強互惠的個別差異。本研究的另一個貢獻是同時考量正強互惠（獎勵和補償）和負強互惠（懲罰）的發展源頭，因為當前的研究主要考量有代價的懲罰，而忽略利社會規管的積極的一面，也就是維護弱勢者，獎勵合作者。在研究團隊現有的兒童利社會行為發展的基礎之上，本研究旨在揭示在有代價的懲罰，補償和獎勵情境下兒童強互惠的發展變化，驗證強互惠萌芽的道德立場假說，並檢視強互惠的個別差異。本研究會召集4-6歲的香港兒童，並測量他們的錯誤信念理解，同理心，延遲滿足。在5個實驗中，兒童會與玩偶進行最後通牒博弈遊戲以及第三方懲罰，補償和獎勵遊戲，並且回答有關道德和情緒的問題。研究結果會解釋強互惠在兒童中的萌芽，以及在個體層面上強互惠的認知和情感機制。

18612415.label: Realisation of objectives
18612415.value: Strong reciprocity, the strategy to either compensate cooperators or punish violators at own cost, is developed through cultural group selection during evolution and works best in large, market driven societies to stabilize cooperative behavior at the group level. The emergence of strong reciprocity at the individual level has immense implication for children’s prosocial development and civic education. It was proposed that 1) there are developmental changes in children’s strong reciprocity; 2) children as third party strong reciprocators are not simply peacemakers to even out inequality, they are rather police officers who punish defectors or cheerleaders who reward cooperators, even at their own cost; and 3) children would demonstrate moral emotional arousal toward the defectors and cooperators in face of unfair or unjust sharing, which would in turn predict their decision to intervene. In total, the study recruited 134 4- to 6-year-old children (mean age = 68.55 months, SD = 12.17, 70 girls) in a within-subject 2 (equal vs. unequal) X 2 (punishment vs. compensation) X 2 (cost vs. no-cost) third-party multiple-trial sharing game. Participants observed two puppets, one fair player and one unfair player, sharing stickers with each other for several rounds. In the unequal condition, the unfair player accumulated more stickers than the fair players at the end of the sharing; whereas in the equal condition, the fair player “surprisingly” found extra stickers stuck at the back of others therefore the two players ended up with equal amount of stickers. The participants were asked to report their moral emotions, i.e., anger and empathy, towards the two players, and whether they would like to intervene with the result. In counterbalanced order, children could ask the experimenter to give stickers to the fair player or take away stickers from the unfair player, either with or without scarifying their own tokens. Children’s theory of mind development, executive function, and delay of gratification were measured. Firstly, the study demonstrated developmental changes in children’s strong reciprocity. Six-year-old children were more likely than younger children to punish and/or compensate unequal sharing than equal sharing, while the younger children did not differentiate in their strong reciprocity based on the sharing results. There was also developmental change in children’s moral judgment: while 4-year-old children already had a better than random moral judgment, 6-year-old children made sensible moral judgments unanimously. Similar result was found in children’s moral emotion between younger and older children. It appears that moral emotion and moral judgment mature around 5- to 6-years of age, coincident with children’s theory of mind development. In terms of strong reciprocity, developmental changes were more pronounced in differentiating unequal from equal sharing results around the same age between 5- and 6-years, motivated by moral emotions. It does appear that children were more willing to take action when such action was not costly. When they did take action, they tended to compensate instead of punish. Secondly, the study also tested the ethical stance hypothesis that children compensate victims or punish violators in sharing driven by moral emotion: children were angrier towards unfair and unequal sharers, and more empathetic towards fair shares, especially when the fair share ended up with a disadvantage sharing result. Both anger and empathy were positively correlated with the amount of tokens they were willing to give up in no cost compensation under the unequal condition; anger was also positively correlated with no cost compensation and punishment under the equal condition, even when the result was equal, anger still drives children to intervene. Thirdly, in addition to the individual differences contributed by age, gender, and moral emotion, it was found that theory of mind and executive function negatively contributed to extend of punishment or compensation. The result was somewhat surprising, but in line with the dual-process strong reciprocity theory (Rand, 2018) that unconscious morality outperforms conscious deliberation. With executive function and theory of mind, children were more likely to contemplate their moral stance which lead to a less prosocial less moral decision. Especially in the context of strong reciprocity where own interests are at risk, it makes sense that contemplation overwrites the urge to take action therefore leads to self-preservation.

18612415.label: Major findings and research outcome
18612415.value: The result found that children as young as 4-year-old reported empathy towards the fair player and anger towards the unfair player, regardless the results were equal or unequal. While older children tended to intervene in unequal condition, younger children did not differentiate equal from unequal sharing in their decision to intervene. Children were more likely to intervene when the decision did not cost them anything; and they were more likely to compensate than to punish. With age, children gave up less of their own tokens to punish or compensate the players. Hierarchical regression suggested that in addition to age and gender, both anger and the experimental conditions (cost/no-cost, punish/compensate, and equal/unequal) contributed to how many stickers children decided to give to the fair player or take away from the unfair player, with cost being the most salient predictor. The findings suggested that young children not only responded to the unfair result (distributive justice), but also to the unjust sharing (procedural justice) with moral emotions. However, they were more willing to be cheerleaders than police officers, and more likely to intervene when the decision did not cost them anything. The most interesting finding of the study was that theory of mind and executive function negatively contributed to strong reciprocity. Confirming the dual-process strong reciprocity theory, this result provided the much needed evidence that even in young children, contemplation afforded by theory of mind and executive function leads to a less prosocial and less moral self-preservation when own interests are at risk. The outcome of the research was reported at two different international conferences. Another manuscript is being prepared for journal submission. • Wang, Z. (August, 2017). It takes more than a good heart to help others: The role of delayed discounting on altruism. Poster presented at American Psychological Association, Washington, DC, US. • Wang, Z. & Kang, R. (March, 2019). Police officers and cheerleaders: The effect of moral emotion on children’s strong reciprocity. Poster presented at the Biennial Meeting of Society for Research in Child Development (SRCD), Baltimore, US. • Wang, Z. (manuscript). Slothful saints: Strong reciprocity development in young children. Another outcome of the project involves research postgraduate students training. Two PhD candidates participated in the design of the study and data analysis and report writing. They gained first hand experience on planning a research project, coordinating different stake holders in the project, data analysis and interpretation, and report writing.

18612415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18612415.value: We initially hypothesized that theory of mind and executive function would facilitate children’s moral development, specifically in the current study, the development of strong reciprocity. The result turned out to be contradictory to our initial hypothesis. Factor in our findings from the PI’s previous GRF project (#845211) where we found that priming children’s theory of mind would lead to less sharing, we are now convinced that theory of mind functions as a deliberate mechanism that promotes self-preservation instead of self-sacrifice. Future research should address the ontological origins of the dual process account of morality in children: when do children start self-preservation, what cognitive and social competences contribute to such developmental changes, and more importantly, if contemplation undermines strong reciprocity, why do people, adults and children alike, still practice self-sacrifice, when and under what circumstances do they do so, what characteristics can be identified in ultra-prosocial people?

18612415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18612415.value: The study addressed the question that whether children are willing to uphold social justice even when it is costly to themselves, and if they do, what factors contribute to their decisions. It was found that while older children tended to intervene in unequal condition, younger children did not differentiate equal from unequal sharing in their decision to intervene. With age, children gave up less of their own tokens to punish or compensate the players. Children with more advanced theory of mind and executive function intervened less when facing injustice. The findings suggested that young children not only responded to the unfair result (distributive justice), but also to the unjust sharing (procedural justice) with moral emotions. However, they were more willing to be cheerleaders than police officers, and more likely to intervene when the decision did not cost them anything. The findings are significant not only because it systematically demonstrates developmental changes in children’s strong reciprocity, also because it provides empirical evidence from a developmental perspective supporting the dual-process theory that even in young children, contemplation afforded by theory of mind and executive function leads to a less prosocial and less moral self-preservation when own interests are at risk.

18612615.label: Realisation of objectives
18612615.value: Summary: All project objectives have been fully achieved. Outputs include one published journal article, one journal article accepted, one conference presentation, and two conference poster presentations. Financial support from GRF was acknowledged for all the outputs. Sample: The project analysed secondary longitudinal data collected by the Hong Kong (HK) government on the Territory-wide Systems Assessment (TSA) of mathematics and Chinese language. The sample comprised the cohort (with no missing data) of 48,547 Primary 3 (P3) students who sat the TSA at P3 in 2007, at P6 in 2010, and at S3 in 2013. This 3-wave data set was used for Objective 3 of the project. A sub-sample of 18,614 students (59% males) who opted to sit the TSA mathematics assessment in Chinese was used for Objectives 1, 2, 4. Methods: Parallel-process multilevel latent growth modelling using the Mplus software was used to analyse the data. This method was chosen because: (a) latent growth modelling enabled intra- and inter-individual differences across time to be modelled; (b) the sample consisted of multilevel data; and (c) parallel-process modelling enabled simultaneous modelling of multiple outcome growth processes of mathematics and Chinese language. Procedures: First, through linkage items common across test versions and between test events, mathematics data were calibrated using the Rasch model onto a common mathematics ability scale and a common Chinese language ability scale. The Rasch measures (in logits) were used in all subsequent analyses. Second, four models (unconditional/conditional linear/non-linear growth curve model) were fitted to the Rasch measures. Third, data-model fit was inspected using the common goodness of fit indices: Chi-squared statistics, CFI, TLi, RMSEA, and SRMSR. Fourth, after ascertaining goodness of fit of each model, the four models were compared to address Objectives 1, 2, and 4 using Akaike’s information criterion, the Bayesian information criterion, and the sample-size adjusted BIC statistics, with smaller values of the indices indicating better models. Objective 1: Develop models of growth in the curriculum subjects of Mathematics and Chinese Language for Hong Kong students over six years, from Primary 3 to Secondary 3. (Achieved 100%, Mok and Zhu, 2018) For objective 1, the linear models were compared with the non-linear models using the Satorra-Bentler scaled Chi-squared difference test (Satorra-& Bentler, 2010) in addition to the AIC, BIC and ABIC statistics. Findings: The non-linear growth curve models fitted the data better than the linear growth curve models for both mathematics and Chinese Language both under the non-conditional situation and the condition situation (student gender controlled). These results showed that for growth from P3 to S3 in the curriculum subjects of mathematics and Chinese language followed non-linear growth trajectories. Further, results showed that HK students grew faster in both mathematics and Chinese language at secondary than at primary levels, but growths in the two curriculum subjects followed different growth trajectories, being faster for math. These results were reported in Mok and Zhu (accepted 2018). Objective 2: Examine the effects of initial abilities in mathematics and Chinese language on subsequent growth in these subjects. (Achieved 100%; Mok and Zhu, 2018) In order to achieve objective 2, the correlation between the intercept (i.e., initial achievement) and the slope (i.e, rate of growth) of the model were examined to determine the effects of initial abilities in mathematics and Chinese language on subsequent growths of each subject. Findings: The results showed that at the student level, the correlations between initial achievement and growth rate in mathematics were negative both before and after controlling for student gender. This meant that growth in mathematics followed a compensatory pattern: lower initial achievement level in mathematics was associated with faster subsequent growth rate in the subject. The compensatory effect was also observed in Chinese language growth. Objective 4: Examine gender differences in the growth in mathematics and Chinese language. (Achieved 100%; Mok and Zhu, 2018) In order to achieve objective 4, student gender was modelled as a time-invariant covariate so that the extent to which growth trajectories of boys and girls were different/similar could be determined. Findings: The results showed that at P3, females had lower initial achievement in mathematics but higher initial achievement in Chinese language than males had. Nevertheless, females grew at a faster rate than males did in both curriculum subjects. Details for Objective 3 In order to achieve objective 3, two sets of analyses were undertaken. Method 1: the sub-sample of 18,614 students (59%) and the methods of analyses described above were used. Method 2: the sample comprising the entire cohort of 48,547 students was used. Findings using Method 2 were described at the later part of this report. Findings using Method 1 were reported as follows: Objective 3: Explore the reciprocal effects of growth in mathematics and Chinese language. (Achieved 100%; Mok, Zhu, and Law, 2017; Mok and Zhu, 2018) Findings (Method 1): Using parallel-process multilevel latent growth modelling, the study found initial achievement of mathematics and Chinese language at P3 were moderately correlated (r = .604). Further, the growth rates of these two subjects were also moderately correlated (r = .603). In addition, low initial achievement in mathematics was associated with high growth rate in Chinese language (r = -.465), and low initial achievement in Chinese language was associated with high growth rate in mathematics (r = -.130). Two limitations of Method 1 were acknowledged. First, the method made use a sub-sample of students who took the S3 TSA assessment in Chinese. These students were likely to be those who had gone through their lower secondary education with Chinese as medium of instruction (CMI) and these students were reported in previous studies to be weaker academically, and less self-confident than their EMI (English as a medium of instruction) peers. Hence the findings might not be generalised to EMI students. Second, the study did not control for achievement in English (The model failed to converge if English achievements were included). Given these two limitations, additional analyses was undertaken using Method 2. Sample of Method 2 for Objective 3: The sample comprised the entire cohort of students (N = 48,547; 50.85% or n = 24,684 males) from 526 schools who took the TSA assessment at P3 in 2007 and had no missing data in at the assessment. These students were followed longitudinally for six years, with TSA data collected at 2007 (P3), 2010 (P6), and 2013 (S3). Methods: Multilevel cross-lagged analysis with the Mplus software (version 7.2; Muthén & Muthén, 1998-2012) was used. This method was used because it combined the statistical benefits of multilevel modelling, which took into account the nested nature of the data, and of structural equation modelling, which enabled modelling of the constellation of relationships across time among the curriculum subjects while taking into account effects of the covariates including student gender, school type (single-sex/co-educational), medium of instruction and medium of test at S3. Findings (Method 2): The study found significant positive cross-subject bidirectional predictive effect between mathematics and Chinese language across years from P3 to P6, and again from P6 to S3, after controlling for students’ English language achievement, gender, school type, medium of instruction and medium of test. That is, stronger prior achievement in one subject predicted better subsequent achievement in the other subject.

18612615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18612615.value: The cohort of students in this study would have sat the high-stake DSE (Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education) public examination in 2016. The longitudinal data including the 2016 DSE results for these students should be available from the government by now. Future research should focus on more in-depth studies, which make use of both quantitative and qualitative techniques, and include variables that have significant impact on student achievement. A follow up research study could be undertaking by analysing the four-wave longitudinal secondary data. Given that the TSA is a low-stake assessment, some critics might cast doubts on the trustworthiness of the data used in the current study. Empirical validity of the growth model found in this study could be further discerned by including the data from the high-stake DSE. Further, a four-wave longitudinal data set has the additional benefit of being more flexible in model fit (e.g. further examination of the forms of the growth trajectories for the two curriculum subjects) over a three-wave data set.

18612615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18612615.value: Sustained growth in academic subjects, especially in mathematics and Chinese language, two of the four core subjects in the Hong Kong school curriculum which are ascribed great societal value, is an important goal of education. This research study aims to explore Hong Kong students' longitudinal growth in mathematics and Chinese language proficiencies from primary to secondary year levels. Modelling growth yields invaluable statistical information on the form of growth trajectory, growth rate, and average growth to be expected among students at key stages of education. Such information facilitates the identification of anomalies at both system- and student-levels, thus enabling intervention to be initiated where appropriate. This study found evidence on the contributions of Chinese language proficiency to the growth of mathematics achievement, and vice versa. Further, although girls were weaker than boys in mathematics at Primary 3, girls grew at a faster rate from primary to secondary levels. Longitudinal research conducted overseas demonstrated bi-direction effects of growth in language and mathematics. Nonetheless, most of these studies were conducted in English or other European languages. Only a handful of studies have examined relationship between achievement in mathematics and Chinese language. This is the first study to identify a bidirectional association over time from G3 to G9 between achievements in mathematics and the English and Chinese languages for unbalanced Chinese-English bilinguals. It represents a major breakthrough in the area.

18612715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18612715.value: What would we do if our parents fell ill and became dependent on us on a long-term basis? Certainly, if an unfortunate event were to occur, we would rush to them and provide our best assistance. But, if the illness lingered on, we might become less able to give care as readily as before. In these circumstances, how far does morality require adult children to make sacrifices on behalf of their parents? Our response to this question may be affected by a range of cultural and political factors, including the level of government support provided to family caregivers, the cohesion of the neighbourhood in a community, and the general expectations of the society, etc. Besides these considerations, a reasonable explanation of the nature of filial obligations in the case of long-term caregiving will have to fulfill three criteria. First, the explanation should tell us about the strength of filial obligation in relation to the demands of other obligations. Second, as the demands of long-term caregiving may have an indefinite nature, we should be able to determine the circumstances in which adult children are morally permitted to stop assisting their parents. Third, the explanation should be sensitive to cultural diversities and expectations regarding the provision of filial care. In the literature, we may find discussions regarding the nature of filial obligation in analytic philosophy. There is a range of “analogy-based views”, including the debt theory, the gratitude theory, the friendship theory, and special goods theory, etc. However, in the proposed research, we will review these theories and leave them to one side, because they cannot fulfill the above-mentioned criteria. The proposed research will focus on the implications of two normative theories, namely, Consequentialism and Contractualism. According to Consequentialism, adult children have strong duties to support their parents if their general compliance with this rule promotes the overall good. According to Contractualism, adult children have strong filial duties if their caregiving actions involve a moral principle that no one can reasonably reject. Consequentialism and Contractualism can provide explanations of filial obligation from an overall profile of an ethical framework; they allow us to assess the strength of filial obligation in relation to the obligations of other demands, generate reasons for adult children to resist the potentially limitless requirements of long-term caregiving, and may prescribe different moral codes to people living under different cultural circumstances. 假如我們的父母病倒了，需要依賴我們才能生活，那如何是好呢?當然，在他們剛剛病倒的時候，我們會馬上趕到幫忙的。然而，若他們的病情延續，我們或許未必能夠像剛開始時候一樣盡力協助他們。在這樣的處境下，成年子女在道德上應該犠牲多少來協助受長期病患影響的父母呢? 我們考慮這個問題時，會受到各種文化及政治因素影響，包括政府對照顧長期病患者的支援、某地方的鄰舍關係、社區的凝聚力，以及社會大眾對孝道的期望等等。 除此以外，若要合理地闡述在長期照顧父母一事上盡孝的道德責任（姑名之為孝道），應滿足三個條件。首先，須澄清孝道的要求與其他道德責任的要求之間輕重緩急的差異。第二，長期照顧父母的道德要求有一個不確定性，我們須能夠決定，在什麼情況下，在道義上成年子女可以停止援助他們的父母。第三，我們須顧及文化的多樣性及不同文化對盡孝的期望。 在以往文獻中，不難發現以分析哲學角度對孝道的討論，例如債務論 (Debt Theory)、感恩論 (Gratitude Theory)、友情論(Friendship Theory)以及特別好處論(Special Goods Theory) 等。然而，在是次建議研究中，我們會在總結及檢討這些理論之後將諸擱在一旁，因為我認為這些理論不能滿足我在上面提及的條件。 是次研究將集中討論兩種規範倫理學理論對孝道的啟示，這些理論分別是後果論（Consequentialism）及契約論(Contractualism)。根據後果論，若成年子女普遍遵從孝道能帶來最大的好處，他們便有很強烈的責任支持自己的父母。根據契約論，若成年子女照顧父母的行為建基於無人能合理反對的道德原則，他們便有强烈的責任盡孝。 後果論及契約論能從道德框架的整體輪廓中闡釋孝道，使我們能夠評估孝道的要求與其他道德責任的要求之間輕重緩急的差異，為成年子女帶來理由去抵制長期照顧父母一事上潛在的無限需求。此外，這些理論或能為活在各種文化情景下的人，指出有關孝道的不同道德規範。

18612715.label: Realisation of objectives
18612715.value: I have written three papers in regard to this research. They include a paper on Consequentialism (“Caring for parents: a consequentialist approach”), a paper on Contractualism (“The Demands of Filial Morality: A Contractualist Explanation”), and a paper on the various dimensions of the nature of filial obligations (“Caring for Parents: Filial Morality and its Dimensions”). Achievement of Objective One. In these papers, I have analyzed the nature of filial obligation from Consequentialism, from Contractualism, and also from other special theories of filial obligation (such as the debt theory, friendship theory and the special goods theory). Because these theories fall under different domains of consideration, some are more capable of determining the limits of the moral demands of filial obligation than others. Achievement of Objective Two. I argue that adult children are morally obligated to make great sacrifices (which I call the strong principle) for the sake of their parents in an aging population. I put forward arguments separately in my papers on Consequentialism and on Contractualism. I have shown that both theories support the claims of the strong principle (I sometimes use the term “extreme principle” in my papers). The strong principle is demanding. But I argue that the consequentialists will accept it. The reason is that the costs of inculcating such a principle in children are not as great as inculcating an impartial principle of beneficence. And, in an aging population, there will be a great number of recipients who will be benefited from society’s general acceptance of this principle. Besides, I think the contractualists will also accept the strong principle. The reason is that the strong principle of sacrifice cannot be reasonably rejected by any parties who are involved in the promotion of this principle. The adult children, as a negotiating party, will be greatly affected by it. But their condition will not be as worse as the situation of the aging parents. For, if the moderate principle, instead of the strong one, is promoted in society, the aging parents will suffer from a great desperation. This will give them reason to reject any principle of sacrifice which is less stringent than the strong one. Achievement of Objective Three. With regard to my papers on Consequentialism and on Contractualism, I have also examined the moral structure of repetitive caregiving actions, and have analyzed the potential variation of demands in this context. While attending to aging parents, the caregivers may have to respond to their questions, help them get dressed, help them move to and from toilets, take medicines, etc. The performance of each one of these helpful actions requires trivial sacrifice. But if the caregivers cease to do any of them, the recipients (the aging parents) may suffer great distress. For this reason, the moral demands of caregiving will iterate and in the long run, it can generate a great cumulative effects on the condition of the caregivers. In especially my paper on Contractualism, I argue that even the consideration of the serious cumulative effects of caregiving will not give the adult children sufficient reason to reject the strong principle of sacrifice. Achievement of Objective Four. With reference to my paper on filial morality and its dimensions, I have discussed issues of cultural diversity in the aspect of parent-child relations. The paper involves considerations which stem from Contractualism and Consequentialism too. The criterion of moral rightness and wrongness in Contractualism is determined by whether people can act from a principle which other parties cannot reasonably reject. A contractualist investigation is compatible with cultural variability because there are rooms for different social interpretations in regard to the idea of reason. The criterion of moral rightness in Consequentialism is determined by whether people’s acceptance and compliance with certain moral codes can in the long run promote total happiness in society. Given the existence of different established practices, psychological and social constitutions in different societies, the variability of these factors will affect the utility functions in the respective societies. So, both conceptions of normative theories which I use in the investigation can accommodate the challenge of cultural diversity in the current state of the world. With regard to the arguments of my paper “Caring for Parents: Filial Morality and its Dimensions,” they constitute an outline of how cultural diversity may be addressed from the perspectives of Contractualism and Consequentialism. However, the basic direction of the arguments in the paper is not about moral relativism, but is about how the concerns of filial morality affect the different domains of an agent’s life. Although the investigations I have done in the other two papers (on Contractualism and on Consequentialism) will shed light on the matter of cultural relativism too, they are not direct investigation into the problem. So, I will consider this objective (Objective 4) as not fully achieved, though these papers have laid down the groundwork of further investigation in the area regarding filial obligation and cultural relativism. There are reasons for the incomplete achievement of Objective 4. The majority of the work in my investigation has been about connecting the claims of major normative theories with the discussion of filial obligation in the case of long-term caregiving. I also have attempted to analyze the connection between Confucian filial morality and other major normative theories. As a result, I have been paying more efforts elaborating the universalist aspect of filial moral demands than the relativist aspect of it. It is very hard to use a numerical representation to describe how far I have gone regarding the fulfillment of Objective 4. I think I have done substantial work in the other papers to prepare for the discussion of moral relativism and the demand of filial obligations and I am ready to draft an article in this area. So, I give it a 70% achievement.

18612715.label: Major findings and research outcome
18612715.value: As the world is affected by population aging, adult children generally face a stringent moral demand to take care of their aging parents. This puts extraordinary pressure on adult children and there is a need to figure out the nature and extent of these newly emerged moral demands. The problem with the existing special theories of filial obligation (i.e., the debt theory, the gratitude theory, the friendship theory, and the special goods theory) is that whereas they may explain the special relation between parents and their adult children, they cannot spell out the extent of demands which adult children are expected to fulfill. In this project, I use comprehensive normative theories, Contractualism and Consequentialism, to evaluate the various levels of possible sacrifice which adult children may make and explain why a certain level of moral demands is justified and others not. I have shown that both Contractualism and Consequentialism support the promotion of strong filial obligation over a moderate obligation or a weak one. This outcome confirms and clarifies the stringent nature of filial obligation under the current situation of the world. It is important to note that this conclusion makes sense under the circumstance when adult children have to provide long-term care to their parents. This discussion will take place as the moral relation between the two sides is under stress. In ordinary life, members of a family will find it odd that they have to justify their actions to each other or to explain the limit of moral demands in this context. People within a family are generally willing to act to protect each other’s interests. Then, neither the contractual justification nor the consideration of total happiness may connect to people’s motivation to care for their friends and family members. My explanation of filial obligation from the normative theories will not replace the special theories of filial obligation; it only complements them to make the overall picture of filial morality more complete and consistent than before.

18612715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18612715.value: After we have established a Consequentialist and a Contractualist explanations of the demands of filial obligation, we may consider how these views connect to a certain virtue theory. The most representative theory in this area is Confucianism, which develops its contents from the virtue of filial piety. Besides, since societies in the Asian region have been heavily influenced by Confucian ethics and are currently facing serious challenges of population aging, there is practical significance for this proposed research. In this research, we will need to acquire a general understanding of the doctrines of Confucianism and the contemporary interpretations of its filial demands. We need to consider how the Confucian filial demands can be explained under the Consequentialist cost-benefit analysis. For example, will it be too costly to inculcate such a conception of demands into each generation of children? Furthermore, we may ask whether the Confucian demands are reasonably rejectable from the perspective of Contractualism. If the demands are supposed to involve strong sacrifice on the adult children’s side, will they have reason to reject the respective principle? Alternatively, if they involved moderate sacrifice, will the adult children’s parents have reason to reject the respective principle?

18612715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18612715.value: In recent decades, people in affluent countries are generally living longer than before and tend to have only small families. As they grow old, their adult children face serious pressure to provide care and support to them. In my research, drawing reference from two major normative theories, Contractualism and Consequentialism, I attempt to explain the extent of moral demands in relation to the problem of long-term caregiving. I argue that both of the normative theories support a strong principle of filial obligation. Before my investigation is done, no substantial studies have been conducted in this area of research. Although there have been special theories explaining the nature of filial obligation itself, these special theories fail to provide useful guidance regarding how far adult children are morally expected to sacrifice for the sake of their parents. As a research in philosophy, the conclusion of my arguments will provide grounds for everyone in society to conceive the deep meaning of the moral relation between parents and their children. It will also provide theoretical grounds on which governments and organizations formulate social policies in response to the challenge of population aging in the long run.

18613015.label: Realisation of objectives
18613015.value: In the past 3 years, we had successfully recruited both typically developing (TD) adolescents and students with ADHD to participate in the study. In addition, we had also recruited students who are diagnosed with autism and dyslexia to participate in the study. As stated in the original proposal, we hypothesized that, while impulsivity is a common feature of TD adolescents, the relationship between the level of impulsivity and the activity of the dopaminergic neural network may not be a linear correlation. In particular, although the activity of the amygdala-striatum network may exhibit a positive correlation with the impulsivity of typically developing adolescents, the impulsive symptom of ADHD adolescents is associated with the hypoactivity of the amygdala-striatum network. We observed the similar pattern in students with autism and dyslexia. Nevertheless, we are not able to isolate whether the hypoactivity of the amygdala-striatum network is associated specifically with autism or dyslexia or it is due to the comorbidity of ADHD in these participants. To examine the how impulsivity relates to the interaction between the physiological arousal and amygdala-striatum network activity, we tried to collect both psychophysiological measures (e.g. heart-rate and skin conductance) and BOLD fMRI signals simultaneously. It is an approach that we successfully adopted in our previous studies conducted in the States and Canada. However, due to the technical limitation, the scanner at Hong Kong did not have the capacity to collect these psychophysiological measures during an fMRI experiment. We explored the different solutions and ultimately decided to conduct the experiment in the MRI center ta the National Taiwan University via our existing collaboration with the the Taipei Medical University. However, according to the rules of RGC, it requires a major change in the proposal before a virement of research funding to Taiwan can be performed. The major change was not approved until a few months after the official completion date of the project. Therefore, we could not conduct the fMRI experiment with simultaneously psychophysiological measures. To address the technical shortcoming, the research team conducted parallel sessions of data collection. The same protocols, including task switching task, counting stroop task, Go-NoGo task and dilemma decision making task were conducted with a lab session in which behavioural and psychophysiological data were collected and a fMRI session in which brain activity was monitored with BOLD fMRI. In total, we collected data from 125 participants. In addition, we also examined the resting-state network and Glutamate level of the participants using Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy (MRS) techniques. Our initial analysis showed that the level of Glutamate correlated with the activity within the left hippocampus. The results were presented in the ISMRM 2018 Annual Meeting. In addition, the research team identified that the physiological arousal level of students can be monitored in a classroom setting and provided valuable information to teachers and parents in accessing their impulsivity and learning behaviors in a daily basis. Therefore, we worked with our collaborators at the City University of Hong Kong, Hong Chi Association and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology to develop a real-time physiological monitoring system using wearable sensors. In addition to accessing the impulsivity of individual students, we further explored the effect of such real-time visualization on the effectiveness of classroom learning. The system received positive rating from teachers across a number of schools. In sum, the project encountered a major set back of not having simultaneous BOLD fMRI and psychophysiological measurements due to the technical limitation in Hong Kong. We overcame this hurdle by having parallel data collection sessions and successfully collected data to test the hypotheses stated in the proposal. We further applied the knowledge acquired from this project in developing a wearable sensor system that can estimate arousal and emotional state of students in a classroom setting. Although the development of system is still on-going, the initial feedback from the users are positive and encouraging.

18613015.label: Major findings and research outcome
18613015.value: Among the various experimental protocol, we found that the Go-NoGo task and the counting stroop task are the most sensitive ones in examining the correlation between the impulsivity of participants and the activity of the amygdala-striatum network. At the beginning of the study, we examined the effectiveness of using a modified Go-NoGo task to quantify the impulsivity control of adolescents. Unlike the classical Go-NoGo task, the modified version separated the working memory and inhibition components by introducing a contrast between intuitive-NoGo and arbitrary-NoGo trials. The arbitrary-NoGo trial requires a higher level of working memory involvement than the intuitive-NoGo trial does. Behavioral data supports the hypothesis that these two NoGo trials involve different level of cognitive processing (i.e. longer RT in the arbitrary-NoGo trials). We showed that the right inferior frontal junction (rIFJ), along with other parietal regions, commonly activated in the two nogo conditions. However, the pars opercularis was activated more strongly in the intuitive nogo condition. Our results are in line with previous findings that the rIFJ and the pars opercularis have separate functions. Specifically, the finding that the rIFJ is commonly recruited in both nogo conditions is consistent with the hypothesis that it is involved in attentional functions necessary for inhibition e.g. detection of changes in the relevant stimuli. The response of the pars opercularis is largely consistent with the hypothesis that the region is involved in inhibition. For the counting stroop task, our findings showed that in addition to the amygdala-striatum network, the prefrontal executive network also played an important role on the impulsivity of adolescents. Stronger activities in the left prefrontal cortex and the anterior cingulate cortex were elicited when participants were asked to suppress their impulsive/dominate response. The activity of the prefrontal network correlated with the behavioral performance of the participants. Such correlation is more robust in TD adolescents though. In addition, a subset of participants (n=45) completed a reflective decision-making task. We found that the involvement of the prefrontal reflective region is negatively correlated with the impulsivity of the participants.

18613015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18613015.value: Based on our findings, we are developing a real-time visualization system that can estimate the emotional arousal level which is closely linked with one’s ability in regulating his/her impulsivity using physiological signals collected from wearable sensors. We expect that, with the development of better sensors and more sophisticated machine learning algorithms, we will be able to improve the accuracy of such biomarker system. By combining such cutting-edge wearable technology with neuroimaging techniques, we are hoping not only to identify a practical practice in helping students with their impulsivity but also reveal the underlying neural mechanism of impulsivity control.

18613015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18613015.value: This project combines brain imaging techniques and the latest wearable sensor technology to examine the biological mechanism of impulsivity in typically developing (TD) adolescents and the ones who are diagnosed with ADHD. Our findings are in line with the literature that distinct mechanisms are governing the impulsive behaviour of TD adolescents and the ones who are diagnosed with ADHD. While brain imaging techniques provide a sophisticated approach to examine the brain function, wearable sensors on the physiological response provide a low-cost proxy to understand the impulsivity of individual in a daily life basis. By establishing the link between the brain response and body response when ones were engaged in impulsive behaviours, the current project sheds new light on how to translate laboratory-based neuroscience findings into practical classroom practice in helping students with special educational needs, such as ADHD.

21100615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21100615.value: DNA复制是最重要且基础的生物学过程之一。细胞在分裂成两个子细胞之前需要首先复制其DNA。在细菌中，DNA复制起点（oriC）主要是富含AT的DNA序列。与此同时，在低等真核生物例如酵母中，DNA复制起点是一种特殊的顺式调控元件，叫做自主复制序列（ARS）。在DNA复制S期，起始识别复合物(ORC；ORC1-6)可以识别并结合ARS序列，其后ORC可以招募其它的DNA复制许可因子到ARS序列并开始DNA的复制。然而，在多细胞动物中，DNA复制起点没有一致的DNA序列。这些复制起点是如何定义和规范的仍旧是一个有待解决的重要问题。 Lrwd1是一种核蛋白质，它包含两个结构域: N末端LRR结构域和C末端WD40域。这种蛋白在高等真核生物中是高度保守的，但在酵母和细菌不存在。之前我们的研究已经证实了Lrwd1是一种新的ORC结合蛋白，它通过WD40结构域与ORC交互作用。值得注意的是，我们的报告还提到，Lrwd1的WD40域在试管中可以识别组蛋白的H3K9me3，H3K27me3和H4K20me3标记。为了进一步了解Lrwd1的功能，我们培育了Lrwd1基因敲除小鼠。 Lrwd1 敲除小鼠显示出侏儒症的表型，这在一定程度模拟了Meier-Gorlin综合征（MGS）。而我们已知Meier-Gorlin综合征患者细胞内编码复制许可因子（如ORC1/ORC4/ORC6/CDT1/ CDC6）的基因存在突变。此外，Lrwd1基因敲除的MEF细胞也显示出细胞增殖的缺陷。另一方面，我们的染色质免疫沉淀(ChIP)实验的结果表明在Lrwd1基因敲除的细胞中ORC2在HOXB1复制起点的结合水平降低了。与此同时，生物信息学分析表明，在老鼠细胞中，H3K9me3富集的DNA区域和DNA复制起点存在重叠。这些结果一起突出表明一种可能性:Lrwd1在DNA复制中可能有着全新且重要的功能，它可能通过H3K9/K27/H4K20me3、Lrwd1和ORC间的相互作用来确定哺乳动物细胞中的DNA复制起点。 我们提出一种假设，在多细胞动物中，Lrwd1可能有识别被组蛋白H3K9/K27/H4K20me3标记的DNA复制起点的新功能，这种功能是经由其WD40结构域招募ORC到复制起点上。在该计划中，我们的目标是详细解释Lrwd1-ORC的相互作用并阐明Lrwd1-ORC相互作用在哺乳动物里的功能意义和生物相关性。 我们的目标是： 1.确定Lrwd1蛋白的基因组定位。 2.在全基因组层面，检测Lrwd1基因敲除细胞中ORC蛋白在DNA复制起点的结合。 3.阐明Lrwd1与ORC不同亚基以及多种组蛋白标记的相互作用。 4.研究Lrwd1-ORC相互作用在细胞周期进程、细胞增殖和确定DNA复制起点中的生物相关性。 通过完成这个项目，我们将揭开组蛋白K9/K27/K20me3标记、Lrwd1和ORC相互作用的性质和生物相关性，并可能在解释哺乳动物细胞中如何指定DNA复制起点的问题上作出重大突破。此外，研究表明一部分Meier-Gorlin综合征患者在已知编码DNA复制许可因子的基因（ORC1/ORC4/ORC6/CDC6/CTD1）上并没有突变，从这项工作中获得的知识也可能为这些MGS患者提供分子诊断。

21100615.label: Realisation of objectives
21100615.value: Realisation of objectives Objective 1: Examine the changes in gene expression in Lrwd1-/- MEFs. We collected total RNA from wildtype and the Lrwd1-/- MEFs (mouse embryonic fibroblasts) and prepared the RNA sequencing libraries (Fig 4 of the attached manuscript under review). The libraries were sequenced and data was analyzed using standard bioinformatics pipeline. We found that the Lrwd1 mRNA is significantly reduced in the Lrwd1-/- MEF RNA samples, which makes perfect sense. Interestingly, the Lrwd1 is the only gene that is significantly reduced in the Lrwd1-/- knockout cells. From the RNA-seq data we found that the gene Gm7102, which is a predicted protein coding gene, is the only gene that is significantly upregulated in the Lrwd1-/- mutant cells. These results suggest that the knockout of Lrwd1 in mouse embryonic fibroblast does not have a significant effect on gene expression in general. Objective 2: Determine the effects of Lrwd1 on HP1 proteins-heterochromatin organization The LRWD1 protein is enriched at the pericentric heterochromatin. To investigate whether the loss of Lrwd1 would affect the HP1 (heterochromatin protein 1) proteins localization and the heterochromatin organization, we first performed western blot to determine if the total protein levels of the HP1 alpha and HP1 Beta proteins are affected. Our data showed that there is no change in total protein levels of the two proteins in the Lrwd1-/- cells (Fig 3B). We then further performed immunofluorescence staining in wildtype and Lrwd1-/- cells. Our data revealed that while the pericentric heterochromatin localization of ORC2 (Lrwd1 interacting protein located at pericentric heterochromatin) is significantly reduced, the HP1 alpha and HP1 beta proteins are not affected (Fig 3a). These results implied that the loss of Lrwd1 in mouse cells has no effect on the heterochromatin organization of the HP1 proteins. Objective 3: Define the biological significance of Lrwd1 and HP1 proteins in heterochromatin gene silencing To define the biological significance of Lrwd1 and HP1 proteins in heterochromatin gene silencing we performed RT-qPCR and examined the levels of different repetitive repeats in the mouse genome. Out data showed that the expression levels of SINEs (short interspersed nuclear elements) were not affected by the knockout of Lrwd1. Interestingly, the levels of LINEs (long interspersed nuclear elements) were increased significantly in the Lrwd1-/- MEFs compared to wildtype controls. When examining the expression of the Major satellites and minor satellites, which are located at the pericentric heterochromatin and centric heterochromatin respectively in the mouse chromosomes, we found that the expression of Major but not the minor satellites are significantly increased in the Lrwd1-/- cells (Fig 3c). Nonetheless, we found that the Lrwd1 is ubiquitously expressed in most of the tissues and organs in developing mouse fetus (Fig 1D) and the homozygous knockout mouse display dwarfism phenotypes at postnatal stage in both male and female (Fig 2A). Importantly, we showed that the proliferation of Lrwd1-/- cells is significantly reduced compared to wildtype controls (Fig 2B). Since the gene expression profile of the Lrwd1-/- is significantly affected, the cell proliferation and dwarfism in the Lrwd1-/- cells and mouse is likely the consequence of the altered DNA replication initiation as reported by various reports.

21100615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21100615.value: LRWD1, also known as ORCA, is a nuclear protein functioning in multiple biological processes. Using its WD40 domain LRWD1 interacts with repressive histone marks and maintains the silencing of heterochromatin regions in mammalian cells. ORCA also associates with the original recognition complex (ORC) and facilitates pre-replication complex formation at late-replicating origins. However, whether LRWD1 plays a role during development and the functional significance of LRWD1 in vivo remains largely unknown. Using gene-trap approach we generated Lrwd1 knockout mice and examined the expression of Lrwd1 during embryonic development. We found that Lrwd1 is ubiquitously expressed in the majority of the developing mouse embryo. Depletion of LRWD1 did not affect embryonic development but the postnatal growth of the homozygous mutants is retarded. In vitro cultured mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) depleted with LRWD1 displayed a reduced proliferation compared to wild type cells. We also showed that the knockout of Lrwd1 in MEFs increased the expression of the epigenetically silenced repetitive elements but with minimal effect on the expression of protein coding genes. Together, these results suggest that LRWD1 plays an important, but not essential, role in postnatal development by regulating cell proliferation likely through modulating DNA replication.

21101115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21101115.value: 大腸直腸癌（簡稱大腸癌）是一種發生在大腸或直腸的癌症，是世界上男性第三、女性第二最為常見的癌症。每年死於大腸癌的病人數約佔癌症死亡總人數的8%。根據世界衛生組織發布的數據，近幾十年來東亞國家大腸癌的發病率和死亡率具有上升的趨勢。因此，除了改進癌症前期和初期的診斷和預防，更為全面和深入理解大腸癌的分子生物學機制顯得非常急迫。而其中一個關鍵的難點在於大腸癌在分子生物和臨床上的多樣性，即存在多種具有不同分子生物學機制、臨床表徵和對藥物反應的亞型。如何結合臨床特徵數據將大腸癌分類成具有不同分子生物學性質的亞型對於用藥決策與靶向藥物設計具有關鍵意義。我們之前發表了一種基於全基因組表達譜數據的非監督大腸癌分類方法。我們發現了三種大腸癌的亞型，其中第三種亞型（CCS3）的患者預後不良，但是這種亞型不能通過常用的KRAS、BRAF和TP53基因突變來識別。 本項目的最終目的是全面獲取預後不良的第三型大腸癌背後的調控機制。在接下來的三年內，我們將一步步實現以下幾個目標：（1）通過綜合分析各種基因組和表觀基因組數據來得到第三型大腸癌的分子生物學特徵；（2）通過對得到的分子特徵進行生存分析來找到第三型大腸癌的遺傳和表觀遺傳預後標記物；（3）綜合考慮轉錄、後轉錄和後翻譯調控來重建第三型大腸癌的調控網絡；（4）基於遺傳和表觀遺傳畸變對導致癌症發展的下游信號通路的因果作用進行統計建模來篩選潛在的第三型大腸癌靶向基因。利用公共數據庫，我們已經獲取了超過4000個大腸癌樣本的基因組、臨床和藥物反應的數據。為了完成提出的目標，我們將綜合生物信息學分析、統計建模、計算仿真和阿姆斯特丹大學學術醫學中心全面支持的實驗驗證。

21101115.label: Realisation of objectives
21101115.value: Objective 1: Comprehensive molecular characterization of CCS3 colon cancer The first goal of this project was to achieve a comprehensive characterization of the molecular properties of CCS3 colon cancer. Together with the other five independent research groups, we formed a consortium to understand the relationships between these subtyping systems. Using integrated analyses of multi-omic data involving over 4000 CRC samples, we identified four robust consensus molecular subtypes (CMSs). Importantly, the CCS3 subtype we identified previously belongs to the CMS4 subgroup, which is characterized by mesenchymal properties. Based on multi-omic data analysis, we comprehensively delineated the biological characteristics of each CMS. (1) Copy number alteration characterization: We found that CMS1 tumors were hypermutated and had a low prevalence of somatic copy number alterations (SCNAs). Conversely, CMS2-4 displayed higher chromosomal instability (CIN) as measured by SCNA counts. Notably, CMS3 samples had a distinctive global genomic and epigenomic profile as compared with other CIN tumors. (2) Somatic mutation characterization: Although we found clear enrichment of certain mutations within subtypes, e.g. BRAF mutations frequently occurring in CMS1 and KRAS mutations overrepresented in CMS3, none of the subtypes are defined by an individual event, nor is any event limited to a subtype. (3) DNA methylation: Based on the analysis of methylation profiles in TCGA, we found that CMS1 tumors display a widespread hypermethylation status compared to CMS2-4, with significant enrichment of patients with CIMP high status. (4) Pathway characterization: We found that CMS1 is characterized by increased expression of genes associated with a diffuse immune infiltrate, along with strong activation of immune evasion pathways. CMS2 tumors displayed epithelial differentiation and strong upregulation of WNT and MYC downstream targets, classically implicated in CRC carcinogenesis. In contrast, enrichment for multiple metabolism signatures was pronounced in CMS3 epithelial CRCs, in line with the occurrence of KRAS activating mutations described as inducing prominent metabolic adaptation. Finally, CMS4 tumors showed evident upregulation of genes implicated in epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and signatures associated with the activation of TGF-β signaling and angiogenesis. (5) Proteomic characterization: We compared the four CMSs with the characterized proteomic clusters in TCGA samples. We found that CMS1 tumors showed upregulation of proteins involved in immune response pathways, while CMS4 samples had significant overexpression of proteins implicated in stromal invasion, mesenchymal activation, and complement pathways. (6) MicroRNA characterization: We found that CMS2 tumors showed upregulation of the miR-17-92 cluster, a direct transcriptional target of MYC; CMS3 samples had low expression of the let-7 miRNA family, accompanied by high KRAS expression levels, whereas the miR-200 family showed apparent downregulation in CMS4. Objective 2: Identification of genetic and epigenetic prognostic biomarkers Our second goal of this project was to identify prognostic biomarkers for colorectal cancer. To this end, we first performed comprehensive statistical analyses to evaluate the associations between CMS groups and clinical variables. We found that CMS1 tumors were frequently diagnosed in females with right-sided lesions and presented with higher histopathological grade. Conversely, CMS2 tumors were mainly left-sided. CMS4 tumors tended to be diagnosed at more advanced stages. CMS4 tumors displayed significantly worse overall survival and relapse-free survival in both univariate and multivariate analyses, after adjustment for clinicopathological features, MSI status, and BRAF and KRAS mutations. We also found superior survival after relapse in CMS2 patients, with a more substantial proportion of long-term survivors in this subset. Interestingly, the CMS1 population had very poor survival after relapse, in agreement with recent studies showing worse prognosis of patients with MSI and BRAF-mutated CRC that recur. Together, these differences in prognosis with unsupervised gene expression signatures confirm the clinical relevance of the intrinsic biological processes implicated in each CMS. Having elucidated the clinical characteristics of the four CMSs, we did multiple studies to develop prognostic biomarkers. First, we found the epigenetic mark—the promoter methylation level of miR-200s is prognostic in stage II CRCs, independent of clinical factors. In another study involving 736 CRC patients across six cohorts, we discovered and validated an 8-miRNA signature as an independent predictor of CRC recurrence. This novel miRNA signature is superior to currently used clinicopathologic features, as well as National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) criteria, and works regardless of adjuvant chemotherapy status in identifying patients with high-risk stage II and III colorectal cancer. Objective 3: Reconstructing the regulatory network underlying CCS3 colon cancer To investigate the regulatory mechanism underlying the mesenchymal subtype of CRC, we inferred regulatory networks comprising multiple levels of molecular regulation. In particular, we studied (i) transcription factors (TFs), (ii) methylation marks, and (iii) microRNAs as putative subtype-specific regulators. Network analyses were performed to identify which level of regulation was most stringently associated with the subtype-specific gene expression distinction in the TCGA dataset. In the miRNA network, the largest regulatory element was predicted to be responsible for 74.8% of the variation in gene expression. However, the largest elements in the TF- and methylation mark-based regulatory networks account for approximately 10.3% and 10.4%, respectively. The dominant regulatory element in the regulatory network was generated by the miR-200 family, namely miR-200a, miR-200b, miR-200c, miR-141, and miR-429. These findings point to a critical role of the miR-200 regulatory network in orchestrating subtype-specific gene expression. Importantly, both miR-200 loci (miR-200ba429 and miR-200c141) displayed significantly higher methylation levels in CMS4 tumors. Methylation of each locus significantly correlated with the expression of the respective miR-200 family member, suggesting it to be decisive for the differential miR-200 expression. Additionally, the EMT-inducing TF ZEB1, which is a direct target of the miR-200 family, was significantly more highly expressed in CMS4 tumors. Using in vitro and in vivo experimental validations, our collaborator Prof. Louis Vermeulen further demonstrated that the methylation of the two miR-200 promoter regions could identify tumors belonging to the mesenchymal subtype and is predictive of disease-free survival in CRC patients. Objective 4: Prioritizing potential drug targets for CCS3 colon cancer We developed NEM-Tar, which extends the original Nested effects models (NEMs) to predict drug targets by incorporating causal information of (epi)genetic aberrations for signaling pathway inference. An information theory-based score, weighted information gain (WIG), was proposed to assess the impact of signaling genes on downstream reporter genes. Subsequently, we conducted the simulation study to compare three inference methods and found that the greedy hill-climbing algorithm demonstrated the highest accuracy and robustness to noise. Using multi-omic data in the TCGA-CRC dataset, we employed NEM-Tar to infer the signaling network driving the CMS4 subtype of CRC. Our model prioritized not only individual intervention targets such as TGFBR2, CTNNB1, ERBB4, KRAS, and SMAD4, but also the combinations of TGFBR2 with CTNNB1, ERBB4, KRAS, and SMAD4. In addition to NEM-Tar, we also developed RNAMethyPro—a gene expression signature of seven m6A regulators, which robustly predicted patient survival in multiple human cancers. A network-based analysis revealed an intimate functional interplay between m6A regulators and EMT-associated factors via druggable targets such as XPO1 and NTRK1. In addition to the robust prognostic value of RNAMethyPro, we also showed its association with anti-EGFR drug response in cell lines and metastatic CRC patients. With further validation and in-depth mechanistic studies, RNAMethyPro may offer an important clinical decision-making tool in the future.

21101115.label: Major findings and research outcome
21101115.value: 1. Molecular classification of colorectal cancer with comprehensive characterization (Wang W et al., Seminars in Cancer Biology 2019; Gao F et al., Oncogenesis 2019). In collaboration with the other five groups in the colorectal cancer subtyping consortium (CRCSC), we identified four robust consensus molecular subtypes (CMSs) with distinct molecular and clinical characteristics. To implement the CMS system, we developed a novel bioinformatic framework DeepCC. DeepCC transforms gene expression profiles to pathway activities, followed by deep learning using a trainable multilayer artificial neural network. Using multiple independent gene expression data sets involving over 4000 patient samples, we demonstrated the superior performance of DeepCC to other popular classification methods. 2. Genome-wide discovery and validation of a gene expression signature for prediction of high-risk T1 colorectal cancers (Kandimalla R et al., Gastroenterology, 2019). The current risk-stratification criteria based on the post-endoscopic pathological examination tend to overestimate the degree of risk for patients with T1 CRC to develop lymph node metastasis (LNM). However, post-surgical pathology results suggest that only 8-16% of these patients are truly LNM-positive. We developed a novel 8-gene signature for more accurate detection of LNM in patients with T1 CRC. In our retrospective cohort study, we found that the 8-gene signature can significantly reduce unnecessary treatment for T1 CRC patients. 3. Genome-wide discovery and validation of a novel miRNA signature for recurrence prediction in stage II/III colorectal cancer (Kandimalla R et al., Clinical Cancer Research, 2018). We developed a miRNA recurrence classifier (MRC), which significantly predicted recurrence-free interval (RFI) in three independent public datasets. The RT-PCR-based validation in in-house clinical cohorts revealed that MRC-derived high-risk patients succumb to significantly poor RFI in patients with stage II/III colorectal cancer. MRC is superior to currently used clinicopathologic features and works regardless of adjuvant chemotherapy status in identifying patients with high-risk colorectal cancer. 4. Identification of miR-200s as the determinants of the mesenchymal CRC subtype based on a multidimensional regulatory network inference (Fessler E, Oncogene 2016). We explored the regulatory mechanisms underlying CMS4 using a network-based approach involving multi-omic data such as gene expression, DNA methylation, and microRNA expression profiles. The miR-200 family presented as the most powerful determinant of CMS4-specific gene expression, tuning most genes differentially expressed in CMS4, including genes associated with the epithelial-mesenchymal transition program. Furthermore, promoter methylation of miR-200s is predictive of CMS4 and prognostic in stage II CRCs, and has a great potential to identify poor-prognosis patients at early stages.

21101115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21101115.value: In the project, we developed multiple biomarkers for colorectal cancer: (1) an 8-gene expression signature for more accurate detection of LNM in patients with T1 CRC; (2) an 8-miRNA expression signature for recurrence prediction in stage II/III colorectal cancer. The two signatures both demonstrated promising clinical values in public datasets and in-house clinical cohorts. To eventually translate into the clinic, prospective cohort studies with a rigorous experimental design is needed, which is beyond the scope of the project. However, during the project, we have established close collaborations with multiple research institutions and hospitals such as Prince of Wales Hospital, the Sixth Affiliated Hospital at Sun Yat-sen University, the Academic Medical Center at the University of Amsterdam, and the Beckman Research Institute at City of Hope. To start, we plan to apply for a collaborative grant between Hong Kong and mainland China with Prof. Xiaojian Wu at Sun Yat-sen University. We also participate in a NIH grant application proposed by Prof. Ajay Goel at Beckman Research Institute (previously at Baylor University Cancer Center). With sufficient funding support, we believe the CRC biomarkers can be further validated with these collaborators and eventually benefit patients in the future.

21101115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21101115.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths in the world. The distressing fact is mainly due to the molecular and clinical diversity of this disease, making it challenging to identify patients that may benefit from optimized adjuvant therapy. Understanding the biological properties distinguishing colorectal tumors, especially in relation to clinical features, is key to more individualized therapy and targeted drug design. In this project, we identified four consensus molecular subtypes of colorectal cancer characterized by distinct biological and clinical features. For better implementation, we developed DeepCC, a robust CRC classification tool, based on deep learning technology. Explicitly focusing on early-stage (T1) CRC, we developed an 8-gene expression signature for prediction of colorectal cancers with a high risk of lymph node metastasis, which has the potential to reduce unnecessary treatment for early-stage patients significantly. For stage II and III colorectal cancer, we developed a novel miRNA signature for recurrence prediction after surgery, which demonstrated superior performance to currently used clinicopathologic features. Furthermore, based on regulatory network analysis, we identified the miR-200 family as the determinant of the poor-prognosis subtype. The promoter methylation of miR-200s presents a potential biomarker to identify poor prognosis patients at early stages.

21203315.label: Project Objectives
21203315.value: to build an intercommunal theory for geometric probabilities involving random convex cones, to develop a common geometric perspective from which seemingly different problems, such as the demixing of signals, isotonic regression, or spherical isoperimetry problems can be approached, to prove a general kinematic formulas for convex cones and use it to test the conic Hadwiger conjecture, to use the theory of condition numbers to incorporate noise, to examine to what extent the theory can be expanded into the complex setting, to study the class of ellipsoidal cones to test the log-concavity and the variance and entropy conjectures, to analyze subgaussian matrices and try to generalize the theory of conic kinematic formulas into this far more general setting; a first goal would be to prove that the restricted singular values of subgaussian matrices have basically the same asymptotics as the usual (unrestricted) ones, but with the dimensions being replaced by corresponding statistical dimensions.
