21214815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21214815.value: Left-right (LR) asymmetry in our body, e.g. the position of internal organs or the left/right ventricles in a heart, is essential for many physiological functions such as the heart contraction and blood circulation. Errors of LR patterning may lead to birth defects or even death. Yet, how LR asymmetry is formed remains largely unknown. Recently evidences showed that LR asymmetry may originate from single cell’s LR biased motion including cell twisting, migration, and alignment. Cell differentiation may play a role that gives rise to the diverse forms of cellular LR biases, resulting the specific cell-cell LR orientation essential for tissue formation. However, although there have been many technologies to characterize cellular mechanical behaviors, for example, cell contractility, the appropriate platform to quantitatively measure the cell’s LR motion has been lacking. In this proposal, we aim at providing an automated torque microscopy to quantitatively investigate single cell’s LR asymmetry with respect to cell differentiation. Using ferromagnetic nanowire as the intracellular sensor, we recently discovered an unreported mechanical force – torque – being exerted by cells. The cellular torque is either clockwise or counterclockwise depending on cell types. This nanowire magnetoscope is believed as the first technology to quantitatively measuring cellular LR biased motion. In this project, first, we will develop the automated torque microscopy integrating the nanowire magnetoscope, micropost array, time-lapse system, and program-controlled magnetic field. Second, based on the developed platform, we will characterize the cellular torque with respect to the differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells. Adipogenic (fat) and osteogenic (bone) differentiation will be the main focuses to reveal the difference of cellular torque upon the commitment of specific lineages. Third, with the aid of the time-lapse system, we will continuously track single cells’ torque during the differentiation process. A program-controlled magnetic field by electromagnets will also be integrated to explore whether the externally applied magnetic torque would, from the other way around, enhance or suppress the cell differentiation. This combined analysis on single cells will elucidate the time-dependence and the logic causality between cellular torque and differentiation, i.e. whether differentiation affects torque or torque affects differentiation. Overall, we believe that our automated torque microscopy and the integrated analysis of cellular torque vs. cell differentiation can provide a valuable understanding of how cells are enabled with varied types of LR biases, opening up a new direction for cell mechanics, cell-cell communications, and tissue regeneration. 人體的器官位置或心室的左右不對稱對許多生理機能像是心臟收縮或血液循環而言不可或缺。左右不對稱的錯位將導致出生缺陷或甚至死亡。然而，左右不對稱的形成仍有許多未知。近期證據顯示左右不對稱可能源自於單細胞的左右偏向運動，像是細胞扭轉、遷移、與排列。其中，細胞分化可能對多種形式的細胞左右偏向的產生扮演重要角色，進而引發組織形成時必要的特定細胞定向。然而，雖然當前已有許多技術可表徵像是細胞收縮力的細胞力學行為，我們依然欠缺適當平台以定量量測細胞的左右偏向運動。 在本計劃中，我們將提供一個自動扭矩顯微技術以定量研究細胞分化與單細胞左右不對稱的對應關係。利用鐵磁性納米線作為細胞內感測器，本團隊近期發現了一種未報導過的細胞機械力：扭矩。此細胞扭矩可依據細胞類型沿順時針或逆時針方向。我們相信此磁納米線顯微鏡為目前第一個可定量量測細胞左右偏向運動的技術。本計劃將首先結合磁納米線顯微鏡、微柱陣列、縮時攝影、與程序控制的磁場以發展自動扭矩技術。第二，基於建立好的平台，本團隊將特徵化細胞扭矩與人類間質幹細胞分化的對應關係。我們將著重於幹細胞成脂與成骨分化以揭示細胞扭矩對細胞系定型的變化。第三，借縮時攝影系統的幫助，本團隊將持續追蹤分化過程的單細胞扭矩。連結程序控制的電磁鐵與其磁場，我們將探索外加磁矩是否增強或壓抑細胞分化。此整合性分析將顯示細胞分化與扭矩的時間和因果關係，即揭示分化導致扭矩或扭矩導致分化。綜上所述，我們相信本自動扭矩顯微技術與針對細胞扭矩與分化的整合性分析將使我們理解細胞如何被賦予多種形式的左右偏向，進而開啟對細胞力學、細胞間通訊、與組織再生的新方向。

21214815.label: Realisation of objectives
21214815.value: This project has three objectives: 1. To develop an automated torque microscopy that quantitatively measures cellular torque and the associated LR asymmetry; 2. To characterizing the cellular torque with respect to multiple lineages of differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells; 3. To track single cells’ torque during the differentiation process that elucidates the time-dependence and causality between cellular torque and differentiation. For objective 1, we have successfully constructed a nanowire magnetoscope that can, for the first time, quantitatively measure a chiral torque exerted by mammalian cells. Ferromagnetic nanowires were deposited into cell culture and spontaneously internalized by cells. With a uniform and horizontal magnetic field around the cell culture, nanowires inside the cell were first aligned with the magnetic field but subsequently rotated in clockwise (CW) or counterclockwise (CCW) direction due to the cellular torque. Importantly, this torque was found with chiral bias depending on cell types. While NIH 3T3 fibroblasts and human vascular endothelial cells (hVECs) exhibited CCW-biased torques, C2C12 mouse myoblast cells showed a CW-biased torque. Moreover, using the quantitatively measured torque and the analysis of subcellular actin distribution, we found that an actin ring composed of transverse arc and radial fibers is the key factor determining the LR bias of the cellular torque. Together, our finding of LR biased cellular torque measured by the nanowire magnetoscope offers a new approach for characterizing cell’s rotational force and fundamental framework explaining single cell’s LR asymmetry. This part has been published in an international journal (Wei Liu, Yuanye Bao, Miu Ling Lam, Ting Xu, Kai Xie, Hin Sum Man, Edward Y. Chan, Ninghao Zhu, Raymond H. W. Lam, and Ting-Hsuan Chen, Nanowire Magnetoscope Reveals a Cellular Torque with Left-Right Bias. ACS Nano 2016, 10(8), 7409-7417), and the first author, Wei Liu, graduated in Jan 2017 with a PhD degree. We have achieved 100% for this objective 1. For objective 2, we have applied the nanowire magnetoscope for characterizing cellular torque of mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) during the multi-lineage differentiation. However, we faced experimental difficulty. In the original design of nanowire magnetoscope, cells need to be resuspended and re-seeded onto circular cell-adherent micropatterns. However, for induced hMSCs, significant number of cells will die during resuspension and re-seeding, causing considerable loss of cells. Combining the low efficiency of nanowire internalization by cells, only a few number of cells are available for analysis, which makes the characterization difficult and inconsistent. Thus, the use of nanowire can’t provide sufficient evidence. To overcome this, we developed a new assay using the chiral bias of nucleus rotation as the mechanical biomarker. Based on it, we found a direct evidence of differentiated chiral bias upon lineage-specific induction. Cultured on circular micropatterns, hMSCs exhibited an anticlockwise (ACW) -biased nucleus rotation and swirling pattern of actin filaments. Interestingly, with adipogenic induction, the chiral bias was reversed to clockwise (CW) -biased, and such reversed chirality was consistently expressed in terminally differentiated adipocytes. Application of latrunculin A (LatA) suggests that the CW-biased actin filament upon adipogenic induction is caused by the reduction of actin polymerization. This part has been submitted to an international journal (Yuanye Bao, Siying Wu, Lok Ting Chu, Hoi Kwan Kwong, Hogi Hartanto, Yaozhun Huang, Miu Ling Lam, Raymond H. W. Lam, and Ting-Hsuan Chen, Micropatterned Mesenchymal Stem Cells Reveals Early Committed Cell Chirality During Lineage Specification, Advanced Biosystems, in revision), and the first author, Yuanye Bao, graduated in Jan 2019 with a PhD degree. While some deviation was adopted to accommodate the practical issues, we still have achieved 90% for this objective 2. For objective 3, using the assay of nucleus rotation, we further found an early differentiation of cell chirality. Interestingly, the change of cell chirality appears at very early stage of cell differentiation. With adipogenic induction for only 6 days, the chiral bias was reversed to clockwise (CW) -biased. More importantly, using self-organized cell orientation on micropatterned stripes as a model of morphogenesis, we found that, with adipogenic induction for only 3 days, the cell chiral orientation evolved from positive bias to negative bias, which appears much earlier than the maturation of other differentiation markers. Based on the time-dependence, we next explored the causality of cell chirality. Applying latrunculin A (LatA) that forced the CW-biased actin filament recapturing the chiral actin cytoskeleton upon adipogenic induction, we found an up-regulation of adipogenic commitment. Together, our results suggest an early differentiated chiral actin which may serve as a mechanical precursor in a feedback mechanism to engage the lineage commitment as well as to coordinate the chiral morphogenesis at early stage. This part has been submitted to an international journal (Yuanye Bao, Siying Wu, Lok Ting Chu, Hoi Kwan Kwong, Hogi Hartanto, Yaozhun Huang, Miu Ling Lam, Raymond H. W. Lam, and Ting-Hsuan Chen, Micropatterned Mesenchymal Stem Cells Reveals Early Committed Cell Chirality During Lineage Specification, Advanced Biosystems, in revision), and the first author, Yuanye Bao, graduated in Jan 2019 with a PhD degree. We have achieved 100% for this objective 3.

21214815.label: Major findings and research outcome
21214815.value: The primary significance of this work is four-folds. First, the application of micro and nanotechnology provides a new standard for characterizing cell chirality. Assessment of cell chirality can be LR-biased cell polarity, orientation, morphology, and migration, which is nonstandard and sometimes controversial. Here, our results showed significant and consistent difference in cellular torque and single cell rotation on circular micropatterns during cell differentiation, providing a new standard method for quantitatively characterization of cell chirality. In addition, as a new methodology, our concept of nanowire magnetoscope offers a universal platform to quantitatively characterize cell’s rotational behavior. Because the measurement is pure biophysical without the need of viral infection or transfection, which is applicable to most cell types. Thus, it can be applied to trace the torques of multiple cells, enabling the study of the regulatory mechanism in the developmental process. Second, we report, for the first time, a LR biased torque generated by cells, which is clearly independent of other biophysical characteristics such as the widely studied cell contractility. Cell mechanics regulates many physiological behaviors such as proliferation, migration, and differentiation. Our discovery of cellular torque can be considered as a new dimension of cell mechanics, which may also play a role in regulating cell physiology and opens up new possibilities for mechanobiology and stem cell research. Third, we found that the early formed chiral actin cytoskeleton may serve as a mechanical precursor to participate and further engage the lineage commitment. Regulation of cell differentiation has been a central hotspot in stem cell research. Thus, the participation of chiral actin suggests a new perspective in such closed feedback loop to mediate the biological functions. Fourth and most importantly, using self-organized cell orientation on micropatterned stripes, for the first time, we demonstrated the coordination of LR morphogenesis by chiral mechanics of single cells at early stage of cell differentiation. Coordination of LR morphogenesis by cell chirality has been reported, but the status of cell differentiation in this process has been unknown. Here, our findings of early changed chirality in mediating the LR morphogenesis indicates that there is indeed an early mechanical interaction between cells and their neighboring cells to unfold the cell chirality into the LR asymmetry in larger scale, suggesting the importance to establish the LR morphogenesis before the maturation of cell differentiation.

21214815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21214815.value: The research outcome of this project indeed creates a new opportunity. As aforementioned, due to the association with actomyosin activity, cell chiral rotation may early correspond to cell differentiation and even serve as an early mechanical marker predictive to lineage commitment. However, conventional patterning technique is incompatible with stem cell differentiation because cells may escape from the pattern confinement during 2-3 weeks of induction. To tackle this problem, we will collaborate with Prof. Jiandong Ding’s group in Fudan University. Prof. Ding’s group has expertise in producing PEG hydrogel micropatterns for controlling the size and shape of stem cells through the entire differentiation process. Thus, we aim at using the material surface patterning of PEG hydrogel to characterize and quantify the chirality of primary mesenchymal stem cells with inherent heterogeneity. By monitoring cell chirality during different stages of differentiation, we can explore a potential role of cell chirality in predicting the lineage fate. We have applied National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC) / Research Grants Council (RGC) Joint Research Scheme for 2019/20 and is recently approved (N_CityU119/19). With the grant support, we will continue our exploration in 2020 -2023.

21214815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21214815.value: Do cells have chirality, or left-right asymmetry? If yes, how to measure and use it? It is a fundamental question in basic science. In recent years, researchers observe that cells can orient and migrate with left-right bias, or chiral bias, and such bias can later cause formation of tissue architecture with LR asymmetry. Since tissue is in diverse forms, cell differentiation must play an important role. However, observation of cell chirality is not easily accessible. Here, to tackle this question, we develop a microscopic technique that can quantitatively measures torque and chiral rotation of cells. By characterizing such chirality of human mesenchymal stem cells, we found an early change of cell chirality with respect to the lineage fate. Moreover, by monitoring the cell chirality, we further found that the early differentiated chiral cytoskeleton may serve as a mechanical precursor to engage the lineage commitment and to coordinate the chiral morphogenesis at early stage of tissue formation.

21303615.value: 從隨機數學模型研究多細胞生物的生長調節和組織結構管理

21303615.label: Project Objectives
21303615.value: Determine the regulation system on morphogen-mediated tissue growth. We propose to build a moving boundary model for morphogen systems, which can couple with multiple growth mechanisms. The results will help us understand what combinations of regulations can achieve even growth and lead the tissue to reach a robust final tissue size. Determine the mechanisms of noise attenuation in the development of multicellular organisms. Through including stochastic effect in our growth model, we are able to understand how the regulation of growth contributes on maintaining a robust formation of morphogen gradient. Develop an efficient hybrid stochastic numerical method for simulations. Aside from modeling aspect, a hybrid stochastic method combining SPDEs approach and RDSSA will be developed for improving the efficiency and accuracy in our computational studies.

21303615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21303615.value: A morphogen is a signaling molecule governing the pattern of tissue development. Morphogens spread from a localized source and form a concentration gradient across a developing tissue, and induce specific cellular responses depending on its local concentration. A morphogen gradient is not only responsible for tissue patterning, but also contributes to the growth of tissue. Most theoretical studies have focused on morphogen-mediated growth and patterning in an “ideal” environment. However, the most important focus should be on how a precise and robust morphogen-mediated development of multicellular organisms can be maintained under genetic mutations and environmental changes. In this project, we aim to understand how the regulation in growth process plays an important role on the robustness of morphogen-mediated patterning in a noisy environment, such as in an in-vivo biological system. In order to study the correlation between the regulated growth process and the robustness of patterning, we propose to build a spatial stochastic model for morphogen systems with multiple growth mechanisms, which are suggested by the experimental data from the system of the Drosophila wing disc. The model will show what combination of mechanisms can achieve multiple performance objectives for a robust and precise patterning. Aside from modeling aspect, we will develop a spatially hybrid stochastic algorithm for improving efficiency and accuracy in our computational studies. The method combines the advantages of stochastic partial differential equations approach, improving the efficiency, and reaction-diffusion stochastic simulation algorithm, guaranteeing the accuracy. The long-term aim of our study is to indicate the factors that relate to various abnormal developments of embryos. Furthermore, after the results are validated by clinical and experimental data, we will advance our understanding of prognosis and treatment for the abnormal growth of human beings.

21303615.label: Realisation of objectives
21303615.value: For objective 1, we have mathematically studied feedback models for morphogen-mediated patterning and growth. For objectives 2 and 3, we have developed some new hybrid stochastic numerical methods for our system. Our new methods can reduce the time cost of the usual stochastic methods to less than 30%, and the accuracy can still be maintained. It is very helpful for stochastic study in different stochastic biological systems.

Currently, we are working a model that is related to the stochastic effect in virus transmission. Our tools can provide an efficient method to reduce the computational cost for generating computational simulations.

21304515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21304515.value: Street-level air quality is an important issue in many cities. The characterisation of the pollutant distribution within cities is of great interest; in particular architects, urban planners and air-quality modellers require concrete information on the escape of vehicular pollutants and their mixing to background values. However, relatively little is known about the timescales and mechanisms that control ventilation and mixing in urban areas. The need for such information is certain to increase as end-users demand more accurate predictions from urban air quality models. A fairly detailed picture of the time-averaged pollutant statistics has been obtained from numerical simulations of turbulent flow in street canyons and building arrays, but the time evolution of the pollutant field has received comparatively little attention. There are several reasons for this: first, virtually all numerical simulations have been limited to prescribed meteorology, which is most appropriate for the equilibrium statistics, i.e. time means and the fluctuations about them; second, existing diagnostics invoke assumptions, such as spatially homogeneous pollutant sources, that are inappropriate for the analysis of mixing and ventilation by unsteady flows. These deficiencies will be addressed using numerical simulations of a passive, non-reacting pollutant within a street canyon or building array. The turbulent flow generated within these domains will be forced by time-dependent meteorological fields produced by a high-resolution weather forecast model (operated by the Hong Kong Observatory) and by prescribed time-varying heat fluxes. These perturbations mimic processes that affect the distribution of pollutants in the real atmosphere. The pollutant field will be analysed using diagnostics that do not make a priori assumptions about the nature of ventilation and mixing. Ventilation will be characterised by timescales for the mean age and residence time, while mixing will be characterised by the decay rate of the variance. The project will present some of the first results on pollutants subjected to realistic meteorological forcing. The timescales for the key processes of ventilation and mixing will be quantified and the underlying physical mechanisms elucidated. It is likely that the existing conceptual picture of the time-averaged pollutant distribution within urban domains will need to be revised. The results from this project will be of considerable benefit to end-users, air-quality modellers, and researchers in urban meteorology. 路邊空氣質素在許多城市是一個重要問題。城市內污染物分佈的特性有很大的用處。建築師、城市規劃師和空氣質量建模人員均需要車輛污染物的逃逸及與背景混合的具體信息。然而，現時對於城市地區的的通風和混合的時間尺度和機制的認識並不多。隨著終端用戶需要對城市空氣質量更加準確的預測，這些信息的需求一定會增加。 通過在街道峽谷和建築陣列的湍流的數值模擬，對於污染物的時間平均統計已有相對詳細的理解，但對污染物的時間演變的關注卻相對較少。原因如下：第一，實際上所有數值模擬都被規定氣象所限制，這是適合於平衡狀態的統計，即時間平均和其波動。第二，現有的分析具有假設，如空間均勻的污染源，這些假設在非定常流的混合和通風分析並不適合。 以上的不足將通過被動、非反應性污染物在街道峽谷或建築物陣列中的數值模擬來研究。這些區域內產生的湍流將由高分辨率天氣預測模型（由天文台操作）所產生的氣象場和時變熱通量所推動。這些擾動模仿影響污染物在大氣分佈的過程。分析中沒有任何關於通風及混合特性的假設。通風的時間尺度會透過平均年齡和停留時間來分析，而混合的特性會透過方差的衰減率分析。 這項目將提供受到真實的氣象所推動的污染物的新結果。通風和混合的關鍵進程的時間尺度將被量化，其基本物理機制將被闡明。關於城市區域內的污染物時間平均分佈的現有概念很可能需要被修改。這項目的結果對終端用戶，空氣質量建模人員及城市氣象研究人員提供相當大的用處。

21304515.label: Realisation of objectives
21304515.value: The objectives were realised as follows by the following means: 1. Development of new mixing and ventilation diagnostics (Objectives 1,5) New nonlocal diagnostics were developed based on the objective analysis of the scalar field or the motion of Lagrangian particles. For ventilation, they include the tracer age, residence time and exposure time, which were adapted from diagnostics in the atmospheric science and oceanography literature. For mixing, they include the local- and canyon-scale scalar variance, which were adapted from the theoretical fluid dynamics literature. An embedded Lagrangian stochastic model, in which neutrally buoyant particles are advected by the velocity field, was used to calculate the Lagrangian ventilation diagnostics. 2. Calculation of mixing and ventilation timescales for different scenarios (Objectives 1-6) Many simulations with the large-eddy simulation model (LES) PALM were performed. PALM was modified to accommodate time-dependent boundary conditions (e.g. fluctuating inflow winds) and arbitrary initial conditions and sources. Different geometries were considered (e.g. uniform and non-uniform street canyons, building arrays, realistic urban areas) as well as stable and unstable stratification. 3. Elucidation of ventilation pathways/mechanisms (Objective 2) Determining the physical mechanisms driving ventilation under the different scenarios constituted a central component of the project. Standard boundary-layer diagnostics (e.g. mean flow, turbulent fluxes) were coupled with the new ventilation and mixing diagnostics, facilitating an interpretation that does not assume spatial homogeneity or neglect temporal fluctuations. Furthermore, a deeper understanding of the physical mechanisms governing mixing and ventilation was acquired through the analysis of dynamical features, namely the fundamental role played by the mean circulation for isothermal flow and the existence of nonlinear regime transitions for non-isothermal flow. 4. Calculation of statistical distribution of timescales (Objective 4) Roughly speaking, intermittency refers to departures from mean. In the standard Reynolds averaging approach employed in boundary-layer meteorology and urban computational fluid dynamics (CFD), only time-averaged fluctuations are retained. In this work, intermittency of the ventilation timescales was quantified with probability distribution functions (PDFs) of the residence time, exposure times and tracer age. The exact same diagnostic approach cannot be applied to mixing because it is always defined as a spatial average. Therefore the applicability of Lagrangian mixing theories which account of intermittency was assessed. The objectives were fully achieved. 1. Calculation of ventilation timescales Ventilation timescales were calculated for a wide range of scenarios using the diagnostics described above. They include idealised and realistic street canyons, as well as different types of building arrays. Different external wind directions and wind speeds were considered, as well as time-periodic and realistic mesoscale perturbations to inflow winds. Stratification was varied through bottom heating or cooling. 2. Elucidation of dominant ventilation pathways Associated ventilation pathways were derived for each of the scenarios by comparing the ventilation timescales to the mean circulation timescale and analysing the new diagnostics. By appealing to the linear analysis of small perturbations to the basic state (mean flow), it was argued that a qualitatively similar ventilation mechanism applies to isothermal skimming flow (wherein flow above and below the roof level decouples for sufficiently tall buildings), irrespective of the precise geometry or forcing. The explanatory power of the linear mechanism decreases for non-uniform or realistic geometries and wind directions away from perpendicular incident flow. Ventilation pathways for non-isothermal flow were obtained by referring to the flow-regime transition that occurs when the ground is cooled. 3. Mixing timescales A comprehensive analysis of mixing was performed for a street canyon. Mixing timescales were calculated for a single street canyon under different impulse tracer sources and compared to ventilation timescales. Extending the ventilation analysis, mixing in different regions defined by the mean streamline geometry was characterised. Analysis of flow over an isothermal building array revealed similar behaviour, namely separate mixing timescales exist for early and late regimes. Mixing timescales for the late regime are identical to ventilation timescales. The essential behaviour for idealised street canyons and building arrays was established. 4. Quantification of intermittency PDFs of the tracer age and residence time were calculated for each of the ventilation scenarios described above. For the residence time, the region of interest was defined at the mean roof level (for an idealised street canyon) or the entire canyon unit (for a realistic street canyon with sides streets). For the tracer age, the age spectrum was calculated at different heights (e.g. the roof height). The intermittency of the mixing timescales at later times is essentially identical to that of the ventilation timescales. Careful analysis of mixing at early times showed that mixing is determined by the mean streamline geometry (e.g. the Lyapunov exponent or mean Lagrangian strain), confirming that intermittency is weak over short timescales (as with ventilation). 5. Lagrangian statistics PDFs of the residence time and exposure time were calculated for idealised and realistic street canyons, as well as for a regular building array under external wind at different wind angles. The qualitatively similar results for the street canyons and canyon units is consistent with the ventilation mechanism described above. Statistics such as the visitation frequency (i.e. number of times a particle enters a canyon) demonstrated that re-entrainment is weak and explained why mixing reduces to ventilation in the long-time limit. From these results, stochastic models of particle dispersion and mixing in street canyons and building arrays were developed in collaboration with Prof. J. Vanneste (University of Edinburgh). 6. Time-varying pollutant emission rate The PDFs of the residence time and exposure time were applied to the case of a time-varying pollutant emission rate. It was found that the ventilation timescales are independent of time variations so long as the latter is short compared to the time required for the PDFs to reach their asymptotic form (which is typically less than a canyon circulation timescale), in agreement with the analysis of the Lagrangian statistics. Similar conditions apply to the mixing rate: variations in the pollutant emission rate must be even faster in order for an effect to be seen because mixing is only meaningful on timescales that are short compared to the ventilation timescale. The analysis was extended to the case of a regular building array using PDFs of the residence time. The weak sensitivity to the pollutant emission rate was supported by analyses of sensitivity to inflow boundary conditions. For time-periodic forcing of the inflow winds, there is a small but non-zero response.

21304515.label: Major findings and research outcome
21304515.value: 1. Quantification of ventilation. We developed and assessed nonlocal ventilation diagnostics based on the Lagrangian motion of fluid parcels [1,5]. Many ventilation diagnostics had been proposed in the research literature, but they are specific to boundaries or else assume spatial homogeneity. We showed that the mean residence time and mean tracer age show good agreement with the e-folding timescale for the concentration and the mean circulation timescale and are more accurate than popular diagnostics for the local mean age of air. 2. Ventilation pathways. The notion of a ventilation pathway was advanced and elucidated in this project. Previous ventilation studies focused on turbulent exchange at the boundaries of a canyon unit. We found that, under isothermal conditions, ventilation is actually controlled by the mean flow rather than the turbulence [1,2,5]. For non-isothermal flow, the mechanism changes for stable stratification as ventilation through the sides becomes more important [8]. 3. Flow-regime transition for stable stratification. In order to understand the change in the ventilation mechanism, the sensitivity of the mean flow and turbulence to boundary-layer stability was analysed [4]: the mean streamwise velocity and turbulent kinetic energy are approximately constant for weak stratification. 4. Sensitivity of ventilation to initial conditions. Virtually all studies of urban air quality assume a ground-level source. However, pollutants may be emitted or generated away from the ground. We demonstrated that memory of the initial conditions is not lost within a street canyon because most fluid parcels escape before homogenisation occurs [5]. 5. Analysis of mixing. Mixing within a street canyon is strongly influenced by the streamline geometry [6]. At early times, the mixing timescale within the primary canyon vortex may be estimated with an effective diffusivity, while that in the surrounding ‘vortex sea’ is determined by the Lyapunov exponent; at late times, the mixing and ventilation timescales are identical. 6. Intermittency of ventilation and mixing timescales. PDFs of the tracer age [5] and residence time [1] are approximately exponential. This behaviour is consistent with a first-passage stochastic process with steady mean advection [1]. This result has inspired the development of stochastic models of mixing and dispersion. 7. Time-dependent forcing. The vast majority of ventilation studies have been carried out with steady boundary conditions. We showed that the flow and ventilation within a street canyon exhibit a weak resonant response to time-periodic perturbations of moderate amplitude [4]. Realistic non-stationary perturbations derived from a mesoscale model have a much stronger effect [7]. Neglecting transient effects (on the timescale of a canyon circulation timescale), variations in the pollutant emission rate have a weaker effect on ventilation and mixing timescales.

21304515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21304515.value: Future developments will focus on two areas: 1. Sensitivity to initial conditions. Given that pollutants released at different positions within a street canyon induce long-time concentrations that differ by up to a factor of two, there is a strong possibility that numerical simulations with ground-level sources may yield an incomplete picture of urban air quality. Additional numerical studies would quantify this effect for different scenarios and address the issue of optimal design for improved air quality. The effect of pollutant emissions from elevated sources (e.g. cooking emissions from restaurants) is currently under investigation in an experimental/numerical project with Prof. C.K. Chan (CityU). 2. Stable stratification. Since ventilation deteriorates for weak stratification despite the mean flow and turbulent kinetic energy remaining approximately constant, the change in ventilation mechanism must arise from effects that are not captured by conventional diagnostics. Analysis of the Lagrangian statistics, frequency spectra, linearised dynamics and turbulence-buoyancy coupling will clarify the effects of stable stratification. This will help improve the numerical modelling of urban air quality and weather.

21304515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21304515.value: Urban air quality is affected by pollution sources as well as the transport and dilution of pollutants. The former process (ventilation) has been analysed using ad hoc diagnostics that ignore the spatial variability of pollutants; the latter process (mixing) has been neglected altogether. In this project, ventilation and mixing for various urban domains (uniform and non-uniform buildings, with and without intersections, idealised and realistic geometry) were analysed using high-resolution building-resolving simulations and objective diagnostics that do not require a priori assumptions. It was found that the ventilation timescales are largely determined by the time-averaged velocity field rather than the small-scale turbulent flow at the roof level or lateral openings; furthermore, mixing is only meaningful at early times on account of the escape of pollutants. The analysis of these important processes exploited analogies with fluid dynamics and applied mathematics. Key findings include the weak sensitivity to the time dependence of approaching winds; the existence of a broad range of mixing and ventilation timescales; differing effects of ground-level cooling on ventilation and time-averaged velocity statistics; and the persistent influence of the source location. The results of this project may be applied to urban design for improved pedestrian-level air quality.

21305215.value: 高維雙曲守恆律中激波反射即相關問題研究

21305215.label: Project Objectives
21305215.value: Existence of solutions of the shock diffraction by convex cornered wedges to the potential flow equation when there is a rarefaction wave at the wedge corner. Uniqueness and stability of solutions of shock diffraction/reflection and related problems to the potential flow equation with respect to the initial data and wedge angle. 21305215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21305215.value: 此研究課題的目標是研究高維雙曲守恆律， 特別是對於由位勢流方程決定的可壓縮氣體經過凸或者凹契形物體時產生的激波反射或者繞流及其相關問題的數學分析。 我們已經在相關領域進行了相關的研究， 在本課題中， 我們會進一步的發展而關注於出現其它非線性波， 比如稀疏波時， 相關結構的存在性和正則性。 以及對已得到存在性的這些解相對於初始值和角度的唯一穩定性。

21305215.label: Realisation of objectives
21305215.value: Non-existence of solutions of the shock diffraction by convex cornered wedges to the potential flow equation has been proved, which is now available online via "arXiv preprint arXiv:1705.06837". The local stability of rarefaction wave near the wedge corner is proved, see "Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis 228 (2), 431-476". The uniqueness and structural stability of solutions of shock diffraction/reflection problems to the potential flow equation with respect to the initial data and wedge angle has been established up to the detachment angle, which is submitted and one can check online via "arXiv preprint arXiv:1904.00114". Related issues, for example the convexity of the transonic shock in the self-similar coordinates, have been established "see arXiv preprint arXiv:1803.02431".

21305215.label: Major findings and research outcome
21305215.value: During the period, we established the non-existence of solutions of the shock diffraction by convex cornered wedges to the potential flow equation (listed as publications in Part C with title "Loss of regularity of solutions of the Lighthill problem for shock diffraction for potential flow, arXiv preprint arXiv:1705.06837"), local structural stability of rarefaction wave over a cornered wedge (listed as publications in Part C with title "Three-dimensional steady supersonic Euler flow past a concave cornered wedge with lower pressure at the downstream, Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis 228 (2), 431-476"), the convexity of the transonic shock in the self-similar coordinates for the potential flow equation (listed as publications in Part C with title "Convexity of Self-Similar Transonic Shocks and Free Boundaries for the Euler Equations for Potential Flow, arXiv preprint arXiv:1803.02431"), uniqueness and structural stability of solutions of shock diffraction/reflection problems for the potential flow equation up to the detachment angle (listed as publications in Part C with title "Uniqueness and Stability for the Shock Reflection-Diffraction Problem for Potential Flow, arXiv preprint arXiv:1904.00114"), and structure of solutions of the multi-dimensional Riemann problem for non-homogeneous conservation law (listed as publications in Part C with title "Global structure of admissible solutions of multi-dimensional non-homogeneous scalar conservation law with Riemann-type data, Journal of Differential Equations 263 (2), 1055-1078").

21305215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21305215.value: Two-dimensional shock reflection/diffraction problem governed by the potential flow equation is now well-understood. Potential for further development of the research is the two dimensional shock reflection/diffraction problem governed by the Euler equations or the problem for the axisymmetric case. For the Euler equations, the key obstacle is to the degeneracy of the transport equation for the vorticity, while for the axisymmetric case, the state in the supersonic region is not a constant anymore. Moreover, they are nonlinear and nonlocal problems. So these obstacles make these two problems highly un-trivial. We will continue to think about it in the future.

21305215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21305215.value: The regular shock reflection-diffraction problem governed by the potential flow, i.e., the gas with irrotation assumption, is well-understood. The global existence, uniqueness, and structural stability have been established for all possible wedge angles. All possible wedge angles mean the angle allows the local reflection structure at the reflection point at the wedge. The other angles do not have this possibility, so the Mach reflection must appears. It answers the Von Neumann conjecture on the transition of the regular reflection and the Mach reflection for the flow governed by the potential flow equation.

21305415.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21305415.value: 二硫化鉬基催化制氫材料的第一性原理研究

21305415.label: Project Objectives
21305415.value: To reveal the microscopic details of the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolving reaction in crystalline MoS2 and its amorphous phase and the molecular nanoclusters of Mo and S ions. To establish a comprehensive understanding of the catalytic properties of the MoS2-based materials over different length scales, from bulk to nanostructures.
rows: To reveal the microscopic details of the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolving reaction in crystalline MoS2 and its amorphous phase and the molecular nanoclusters of Mo and S ions.
To establish a comprehensive understanding of the catalytic properties of the MoS2-based materials over different length scales, from bulk to nanostructures.

21305415.label: Realisation of objectives
21305415.value: In this project, we first performed the density functional theory study of the electrocatalytic hydrogen production reaction (HER) at the Mo edge of MoS2, which has been regarded as the most active edge for HER. By considering different sulfur coverage and defects at the MoS2 edge as models of amorphous local structures, we studied their effects on the HER mechanisms and energetics. On the other hand, unlike the edges, the basal planes, which make up of most of the surface area of bulk MoS2, are inactive towards catalytic HER. It is therefore desirable to develop means to activate the basal plane of MoS2. Here, we studied the transition metal doping effects on the catalytic properties of the MoS2 basal planes. We also employed machine two learning models, Random Forest and deep forward neural networks, built using the data generated from various doping configurations to facilitate analysis and prediction of the catalytic properties. The performance of these models was also compared. We also studied two nano-scale MoS2-based clusters, [Mo3S4]4+ and [Mo3S13]2-, which were suggested to be active in catalyzing hydrogen production. We evaluated their performance as the electrocatalysts for hydrogen production by comparing the favorable pathways, the energy barriers, the overpotentials and the stability of the two catalysts. Overall, this work contributes to the microscopic understanding of the catalytic properties of the MoS2-based materials over different length-scares. The effects of doping and defects were also investigated. Such understanding is crucial for the design of more robust HER catalysts and the objectives in this project were therefore realized.

21305415.label: Major findings and research outcome
21305415.value: In the study of the MoS2 edges, we considered the Mo edges with different sulfur coverage, namely the edges covered by 0%, 50% and 100% S. We revealed the microscopic details of the hydrogen evolution mechanisms. We also identified that the 50% S coverage has the best performance considering the number of protonation steps and the overpotential needed. Moreover, creating vacancies at this edge was found to be an effective way to promote hydrogen molecule formation. On the other hand, we found that codoping of two transition metals is a viable technique for activating the catalytically inert MoS2 basal planes. Codoping was found to improve the catalytic performance of the MoS2 plane compared to the pristine and the single doping surface. We also found that the Random Forest machine learning algorithms offered encouraging results in terms of prediction accuracy of the hydrogen adsorption energy, and thus the overpotentials. In the study of the MoS2-based [Mo3S4]4+ and [Mo3S13]2- clusters, we found that the [Mo3S4]4+ cluster shows good performance in catalytic hydrogen production. This cluster has a low overpotential, and the energy barrier for hydrogen formation is small, indicating fast hydrogen production. The cluster also shows high stability over the HER cycle. On the contrary, [Mo3S13]2- does not perform as well in terms of the catalytic performance and stability.

21305415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21305415.value: Building on the study in this project, future work could include exploring other means in activating the basal planes of bulk MoS2. These include applying strain to the layered structures, and its synergy with transition metal doping. The study can also be extended to other transition metal dichalcogenides, like WS2, MoSe2 and TiS2, which are expected to exhibit similar properties.

21305415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21305415.value: Catalytic hydrogen production from water splitting has shown promises towards clean and efficient energy storage. Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2)-based materials have attracted great attention to replace platinum as the cheap and efficient alternatives catalysts for hydrogen production. In this project, we studied the catalytic properties of the MoS2-based materials over different length-scales. We investigated the reaction mechanisms and energetics at the edges of the MoS2 crystal. The effect of vacancies was also considered. We also explored the activation of the basal planes of the MoS2 crystal through doping with transition metals. On the other hand, the MoS2-based molecular nanoclusters were suggested to show promising catalytic performance due to similarity in the active site structures as in the bulk MoS2 edges. We studied here the hydrogen production reactions and evaluated the catalytic performance of these nano-scale clusters. This project delivers fundamental understanding of the catalytic properties of the MoS2-based materials. This in-depth understanding is important in the development of efficient and robust MoS2-based materials for catalytic hydrogen production.

21501915.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21501915.value: 在實驗室中觀察到的風險態度可以預測真正的投資決策嗎？

21501915.label: Project Objectives
21501915.value: Understand whether risk preference elicited in simple games can predict real investment choices, including stock market participation, and portfolio choice. Understand the risk preference of actual investors. Estimate how investors may over-weight small probabilities. Understand whether market experience can eliminate behavioral biases such as over-confidence.

Understand whether market experience can eliminate behavioral biases such as over-confidence.

21501915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21501915.value: Recent advances in behavior finance and experimental economics have identified many important aspects of risk preference such as ambiguity aversion, probability weighting, familiarity bias, and preference for uncertainty resolution. These preferences have important implications for financial decision making and asset pricing theories. Yet, most of the studies have been confined with laboratory experiments with students as subjects. This calls into question whether the observed risk preference in the laboratory can actually predict investment decisions among real market participants. For example, stock market participation decision and portfolio choice decision (what stocks are chosen and their weighting in the portfolio). In the proposed study, we will combine the methodology of laboratory experiment and survey to investigate how well observed choices in a set of risk preference questionnaire based tasks can predict actual investment decisions. More specifically, participants will be invited to participate in a short incentivized experiment where their risk attitudes will be elicited. Then, we will correlate the choices observed with the actual investment decisions to see if there are relationships as implied by the models. To understand the impact of experience, we will have different types of subjects, ranging from retail investors to professional fund managers. 行為金融學和實驗經濟學的最新研究發現了不同類型的風險偏好，如含糊厭惡、概率加權、熟悉偏見和對分解不確定性的偏好。這些偏好對理解投資決策和資產定價理論都有重要意義。然而，大多數研究都局限於以實驗室的實驗以學生為參與者。這使人質疑在實驗室中觀察到的風險偏好是否能預測真正的市場參與者的投資決策。例如，股市參與決定和投資組合的選擇（不同股票在投資組合中的權重）。本研究將結合實驗及調查的方法，我們將研究在實驗中觀察到的風險偏好是否能預測真正的市場參與者的投資決策。參加者將被邀請參加一個關於風險偏好的實驗，然後我們將評估在實驗中觀察到的風險偏好和實際投資決策的關係, 我們也會以觀察到的數據來檢驗資產定價模型。為了瞭解經驗的作用, 我們將有不同類型參與者，包括散戶和專業的基金經理。

21503915.value: To investigate how the uncertainty in demand for goods that firms produce affects the firms' cyclical behavior of converting full-time workers into part-time and their vacancy-posting decisions on substituting part-time jobs for full-time. We aim to match these two dynamics with working part-time because of slack work or unfavorable business conditions and inability to find full-time work, respectively. To qualitatively explore the impact of uncertainty in household demand on working part-time for economic reasons in a theoretical search and match model with full-time and part-time jobs. The project will study the involuntary part-time employment on firms' demand side in the labor market, in contrast to the recent research of voluntary part-time employment on workers' supply side. To quantify the pass-through effect of fluctuations in households' demand for final goods on fluctuations in firms' demand for part-time workers (instead of full-time) at industry level, using data from Current Population Survey, Consumer Expenditure Survey, Bureau of Economic Analysis, and the Conference Board. To address policies that can help to accelerate the full-time job recoveries from crises and prevent jobless recoveries in future downturns, from the study of firms' demand for working part-time for economic reasons during business cycles.

The project will study the involuntary part-time employment on firms' demand side in the labor market, in contrast to the recent research of voluntary part-time employment on workers' supply side.

21503915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21503915.value: After the Great Recession, an important constitution of underemployment is working part-time for economic reasons -- willing to work full-time but are working less than 35 hours per week because of slack work or unfavorable business conditions, inability to find full-time work, or seasonal declines in demand. This project will investigate how uncertainty in demand for goods that firms produce affects the firms' cyclical behaviors of converting full-time jobs into part-time and recruiting part-time workers instead of full-time. These two dynamics will be matched to working part-time because of slack work or unfavorable business conditions and inability to find full-time work, respectively, during business cycles. In contrast to the recent research of voluntary part-time employment on workers' supply side, the project will explore the involuntary part-time employment on firms' demand side in the labor market. According to the date from Current Population Survey, immediately after the Great Recession, firms doubled the number of full-time workers who were converted into part-time because of slack work or unfavorable business conditions. Even though this number has been decreasing gradually since 2009, the level of working part-time because of inability to find full-time work has caught up. We will first study this involuntary part-time employment in a theoretical search and match model with full-time and part-time jobs. Then we will quantify the pass-through effect of fluctuations in households' demand for final goods that firms produce on fluctuations in firms' demand for part-time workers (relative to full-time) at industry level, using data from Current Population Survey, Consumer Expenditure Survey, Bureau of Economic Analysis, and the Conference Board. From the now-available part of data, we see that firms substitute a lot of part-time workers for full-time in the industries of services and construction, but not so many in agriculture; the expenditure recovers very fast in food, slower in housing, and slowest in services. We propose two ways of thinking of the problem: income elasticity of demand, and durable versus nondurable. Food is inelastic and nondurable, so the demand for it should not drop too much and recover fast. Housing is inelastic but durable, so the demand for it dropped a lot but increase gradually after the crisis. Service is elastic and nondurable, so it has the slowest recovery process. 經濟大衰退後，就業不充分的其中一個重要組成是出於經濟原因而從事兼職工作的人數大幅度提高。其定義為願意全職工作卻因為以下原因每週工作少於35小時：工作懈怠或不利的商業條件，無法找到全職工作，或需求的季節性下滑。該項目將研究對企業生產的商品的需求的不確定性如何影響企業招募和轉換全職與兼職工人的週期性行為。這兩種行為將匹配在商業週期因為工作懈怠或不利的經營狀況和無法找到全職工作的兼職。與最近對工人自願兼職工作的研究不同的是，該項目將探索公司在勞動力市場的需求對非自願兼職就業的影響。據最新人口調查數據，在大衰退之後，因工作懈怠或不利的商業環境被轉換為兼職全職工人的數量增加了一倍。儘管這個數字已經自2009年以來逐漸減少，因為無法找到全職工作的兼職的人數卻趕了上來。在這個項目中，首先，我們將建立工作搜索和匹配模型來研究這種非自願兼職工作的理論方面。然後，我們將量化人們在工業級層面對企業最終產品的需求波動為兼職工作帶來的傳遞效應（相對於全職工作）。我們使用的數據將來自當前的人口調查，消費支出的調查，經濟分析局和會議委員會的數據庫。從現在可用的部分數據，我們看到，經濟大衰退後，從事服務業和建築業的企業用很多兼職工作人員代替了全職工作，但這種企業行為在農業方面並不明顯；人們在食品方面的消費復甦非常快，但在住房方面消費恢復慢，服務性消費恢復最慢。最後，我們提出造成這種現象的其中兩種原因為：需求收入的彈性和耐用與非耐用品的區別。食物是無彈性和非耐用的消費品，所以經濟大衰退後人們對它的需求不會下降太多，而且恢復快。房屋是缺乏彈性的消費品，但堅固耐用，因此經濟大衰退後人們對於它的需求下降了很多，但在危機後逐漸增加恢復。服務是有彈性和非耐用的消費，因此它具有最緩慢的恢復過程。

21503915.label: Realisation of objectives
21503915.value: This project has investigated how the uncertainty in demand for goods that firms produce affects the firms’ cyclical behavior of converting full-time workers into part-time and their vacancy posting decisions on substituting part-time jobs for full-time. We have matched these two dynamics with working part-time because of slack work or unfavorable business conditions and inability to find full-time work, respectively. In contrast to the study of voluntary part-time employment on the supply side, we have explored the involuntary part-time employment on the demand side in the labor market. We have qualitatively explored the impact of uncertainty in household demand on working part-time for economic reasons in a theoretical search and match model with full-time and part-time jobs. The project studied the involuntary part-time employment on firms' demand side in the labor market, in contrast to the recent research of voluntary part-time employment on workers' supply side. Models have been set up and used to investigate the impact and effects in the labor and housing markets. Comparative statics have been used to qualitatively explore the theoretical results. We have quantified the impact of the dynamics of revenues generated by production on working part-time for economic reasons using data from Current Population Survey, Consumer Expenditure Survey, Major Sector Productivity and Costs, and Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey. We have studied how fluctuations in households’ demand for final goods pass through to fluctuations in firms’ demand for part-time workers (instead of full-time), which is an important aspect of underemployment after the Great Recession. We estimated the mean and variance of the revenue generated by labor input across different industries and calibrated the cutoff points that firms convert full-time jobs into part-time and lay off full-time or part-time workers. We simulated the model and compared with data the cyclical behavior of the firms’ vacancy-posting behavior of substituting part-time jobs for full-time and their decisions on converting full-time jobs into part-time. We have addressed policies that can help to accelerate job recoveries from crises and prevent jobless recoveries in the future. From the study of firms' demand for working part-time for economic reasons during business cycles and the quantitative analysis of the contribution of households' demand for final goods on working part-time for economic reasons, policies have been explored to accelerate full-time job recovery from a crisis and prevent jobless recoveries in future downturns.

21503915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21503915.value: This project explores the labor, credit, and housing market mainly in the United States and United Kingdom. Similar approaches could be applied to the markets in Hong Kong to compare the difference and address the policies to improve the economic efficiency.

21503915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21503915.value: The project has both qualitatively and quantitatively derived the negative impact of uncertainty in demand on working part-time for economic reasons in the recovery of the Great Recession. 21504615.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21504615.value: 会计事务所合并对实体经济的影响

21504615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21504615.value: 在过去几十年里，高度集中的审计市场对经济的影响引起了广泛争论（General Accounting Office， 2003; Government Accountability Office， 2008; European Commission， 2010）。一种观点认为，集中的审计市场能产生规模经济从而降低审计成本（Gong, Li, Lin and Wu，2015）。此外，大型会计师事务所能提供更高质量，更为可信审计服务（DeAngelo 1981; Watts and Zimmerman， 1981； 1983；Chan and Wu, 2011）。更可信的审计师能降低企业的代理问题，促进资本配置， 从而对实体经济产生正面的影响。 另一方面，世界各地的监管机构普遍担心，高度集中的市场会降低事务所之间的竞争从而对审计质量产生负面影响（Simunic，1980）。较差的审计质量不可避免地影响公司的资本配置,从而影响实体经济。鉴于这些激烈的争论，审计市场的整合对实体经济的影响还未能得到一个定论。在这个文章中，我们将充分利用中国审计市场结构的演变来考察审计市场整合对实体经济的影响。与发达的国家不同，中国的审计市场在过去20年里发生了多次的并购和整合。这种审计市场结构的演变为我们提供了一个独特的机会来探索审计市场整合带来的实体经济效益。

21507115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21507115.value: The proliferation of Internet based platforms has created an emerging channel of funding – crowdfunding. In crowdfunding, an individual requests funding for an idea and a large number of unaffiliated individuals contribute to fund the project. Crowdfunded projects range from small creative projects to entrepreneurial ventures seeking millions of dollars in funding. The crowdfunding marketplaces have grown rapidly in recent years, attracting an estimated $5.1 billion worldwide in 2013. In theory, online markets remove some frictions that hinder market transactions, since they empower market participants with tools to lower communication and search costs. In other words, online markets provide a platform where market participants can make a transaction regardless of the location of their partners. As such, people believe that “location”, a key determinant of funding success for traditional channels, might not be critical for online crowdfunding markets. This raises an important question about how the adoption of crowdfunding by entrepreneurs is likely to evolve not only through time but also over space. In particular, how might entrepreneurs at crowdfunding markets react to the adoption of their peers? How do information channels play a role in this relationship? This research project is intended to examine these questions. We conduct our research in two stages. In stage one, we will develop an empirical model to conduct a spatiotemporal analysis of adoption behavior by entrepreneurs at a crowdfunding market. To dig deeper into social interactions of market participants we will pay a particular attention to two variables- geographical proximity and social similarity as a driver of peer influence. In stage two, we will conduct several tests to investigate a role of media in the diffusion process of crowdfunding. We aim to highlight differential effects of different types of media in crowdfunding markets. This project will make several implications. First, extant research highlights the role of geography in crowdfunding. However, the concept of social similarity has rarely been applied to this context. By examining both geographical proximity and social similarity in crowdfunding we extend the literature on crowdfunding. Furthermore, we attempt to examine the role of media in the spatiotemporal evolution of crowdfunding which is important but underexplored. Second, answering the questions can have implications for policy makers and platform providers. A better understanding of how crowdfunding is geographically diffused over time and how the media shapes this diffusion process will help them to implement better strategies to promote crowdfunding in a region. 互联网平台的广泛应用造就了一种新型的募资渠道--群众募资。在群众募资中，个人或组织可以就某个想法或者某个项目申请资助。群众募资项目的范围囊括从小型创意专案到寻求数百万资金的创业事业。近年来，群众募资市场迅速发展，2013年在全球范围预计吸引了$51亿元资金。 理论上，网络市场使得市场参与者降低交流与搜索的成本，从而消除了部分妨碍市场交易的阻力。换句话说，网络市场为市场参与者提供了一个不受地理位置约束的交易平台。因此，人们相信传统融资渠道的成功关键“位置”在线上融资市场中未必成为一个主要因素。从而引出了一个重要的问题：企业家采用的群众募资如何不仅通过时间而且通过空间来演化。特别的，企业家在群众募资市场上会对他们的同行做出何种反应？融资渠道在关系中如何发挥作用？本研究旨在探讨这些问题。 我们分两个阶段进行研究。在第一阶段，建立一个实证模型，以此来对企业家在群众募资市场的采纳行为进行时空分析。为了深入挖掘市场参与者间的社会互动，我们会特别注意两个变量：地理接近度以及社会相似性。在第二阶段，我们会进行一些测试以探究媒体在群众募资的扩散过程中的作用。其目的是凸显不同类型的媒体在群众募资市场中的不同影响。 本研究项目具有几方面的意义。第一，现存研究强调了地理位置在群众募资过程中的作用。但是，社会相似性的概念却很少被应用到这个范畴中。本研究通过检验地理接近度以及社会相似性，使得群众募资的研究范围得以扩大。此外，我们尝试探究了媒体在重要且有待开发的群众募资时空演化过程中的作用。第二，问题的回答会对于政策决定者以及平台供应商提供一些启示作用。当对群众募资如何在地理上扩散以及媒体的扩散形成过程有更好的理解时，决策者们可以更好的实施战略，从而促进当地的群众募资项目。

21507115.label: Realisation of objectives
21507115.value: This project has been going successfully so far. I'm going to explain what I have done to achieve the three objectives. The first objective is to develop an empirical model to explore the spatial diffusion of crowdfunding. For this, I have constructed a panel data at the CBSA (Core-based Statistical Area) and quarter level and developed a panel regression model with two peer effects measures based on geographic and social proximity. Here, one of the key issues was to create peer effect measures to reflect effects from geographically close and socially similar areas. By using the geographic distance and computing the social similarity between each of the CBSAs, we could successfully generate two peer effect measures. The second objective was to examine the role of media in the diffusion. Originally, I attempted to use the Twitter data. Eventually, it was challenging to collect reliable Twitter data at the national level. So, I found an nice alternative data from Facebook. Facebook used friendship networks of people on their platforms to generate the Social Connectedness Index data. Essentially, this data captures how much people in two cities are connected with each other on Facebook. Using Facebook friendship data provided turned out to be very useful in this project. Using the data allowed us to directly measure the level of online social interactions among cities and examine the role of social interactions in the diffusion of crowdfunding. Last but not least, we provide implications for platform providers and participants. For instance, this study suggests that crowdfunding platform providers should focus initially on large metropolitan areas. However, this strategy should adjust over time to incorporate the social similarity effect as local concentration of project creation decreases. The providers need to attract creators from spatially broader but socially similar areas to their long-term sustainability. Our research also provides important implications for creators seeking financial resources. Our study suggests that creators especially from less populous areas should make an effort to serve sparse demand from geographically diverse areas. Because securing appeal to similar people from diverse areas becomes more influential over time, creators need to improve the ability to sell in essentially unlimited local markets. They also need to have a better strategy to target a small set of people who are socioeconomically similar but may be geographically spread.

21507115.label: Major findings and research outcome
21507115.value: When controlling for the adoptions from the same geographical location, our results showed a significant peer effect from socially proximate areas but insignificant peer effect from geographical proximate ones. Moreover, the peer effect from socially proximate areas increases continuously over time during our study period. We further show that using Facebook’s friendship link data, online social interactions between different areas can partially explain the geographical diffusion of crowdfunding. Our results also reveal that entrepreneurs are more influenced by proximate entrepreneurs who succeeded in fundraising than by those who did not, indicating a performance-based peer influence in crowdfunding adoption. We also observed that the peer effect from socially proximate areas is stronger in areas where people have more opportunities and capacities to learn from others, such as ones with strong entrepreneurial culture and a large pool of highly educated people. This outcome-based peer effect offers an important implication that temporal adoption of entrepreneurs of similar sociodemographic characteristics alone cannot explain our main findings. The results of a robustness check with dynamic panel estimators confirm that our main findings remain consistent.

21507115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21507115.value: This project has several limitations that yield promising avenues for future development. First, in this paper we modelled the geographic component in a limited way. It would be interesting for future research to apply various spatial models to the context of crowdfunding more directly. Second, to complement the lack of empirical support of actual social interactions among socially similar peers, we analyzed actual social connectivity using social network data. However, we did not examine the quality or intensity of social interactions due to the limitation of our dataset. Moreover, we had no data on social interactions among creators in crowdfunding. Fruitful is collecting and examining social interactions among creators to answer the question of how peer effect plays a role in explaining the diffusion of crowdfunding among creators. Last but not least, we have attempted to rule out alternative explanations including homophily in several ways. Nevertheless, it would be great if we can find and exploit an exogenous shock that affects the composition and the crowdfunding adoption of peer groups, which also varies by geography and time.

21507115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21507115.value: Crowdfunding has emerged as a viable alternative source of funding for creative projects and ventures around the world. This project attempts to demonstrate that peer effects play an important role in the spatiotemporal diffusion of crowdfunding from the perspectives of entrepreneurs. Using the data on the creation of crowdfunding projects from a leading crowdfunding campaign from 2009 to 2013, the authors find that creators from socially proximate areas are influential to later creators, whereas those from geographically proximate areas are not influential, after controlling for prior adoption in the same area. Online social interactions in different geographic areas support the peer effect from social similarity. Our results also suggest that there exists a performance-based peer effect in crowdfunding adoption. Overall, this study provides new insights into the spatial diffusion of crowdfunding and offers implications for platform providers as well as project creators.

21507915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21507915.value: With the touted benefits of enhancing innovativeness and greater financial returns, firms increasingly adopt open innovations by incorporating external knowledge and technologies in their innovation efforts. However, the realization of these benefits is not guaranteed if challenges of open search (i.e., a process through which firms explore and select external partners) are not satisfactorily addressed. Firms often struggle with different approaches of conducting open search. Employing an inappropriate approach could cause the open search process to be time consuming, costly and laborious. Furthermore, partners selected via open search can have idiosyncratic resources and operational styles from the focal firms. Collaborating with these partners may also bring troubles to the focal firms. This project aims to unleash the potential power of open search via three steps. First, we identify three widely adopted approaches of open search with different levels of search approach openness. Second, we unveil the paradoxical effects of search approach openness (i.e., value-enhancing and challenge-increasing) along the progression of open innovation projects: scouting for external partners and working with the partners to integrate the sourced knowledge with its internal R&D team. Third, drawing on the lens of organizational absorptive capacity, we propose how the three IT-enabled knowledge capabilities (i.e. IT-enabled exploratory learning capability, IT-enabled exploitative learning capability, and IT-enabled social integration capability) play different roles in managing the paradoxical effects of search approach openness. Toward this end, we intend to make contributions to the open innovation literature and paradox management research by recognizing and managing the tensions inherent in search approach openness. A deep understanding of the effectiveness of IT-enabled knowledge capabilities can also benefits firms’ managers and relevant policy makers to better support the open innovation initiatives. Qualitative and quantitative data will be collected in this project. First, we will collect qualitative data such as onsite observations, interviews and documents to refine our research model and the survey measurement. Second, we will conduct field survey and collect archival data to test the research model. 越來越多的公司在創新項目中吸收外部知識和技術。然而，公司常常難以在開放搜索的不同模式中做出選擇。采用不恰當的模式可能會使得開放搜索過程和相關合作變得耗時、昂貴和費力。本項目旨在通過以下三個步驟釋放開放搜索的潛力。首先，我們確定三個開放性程度不同的、被廣泛采納的開放搜索模式。其次，我們沿循開放性創新項目的展開過程（搜索外部合作夥伴並與其內部研發團隊共同工作、整合技術知識），揭示了搜索模式開放性的雙重效果（即價值提升和挑戰增加）。第三，從組織吸收能力的角度出發，我們研究三個IT相關的知識能力是如何在管理“搜索模式開放性的雙重效果”方面發揮不同作用的。这样，我們通過認知、理解和分析“搜索模式的開放性”的內在張力，立志於為開放性創新的文獻和悖論管理的相關研究做出一些貢獻。本研究中基于IT的知識能力的有效性的深刻分析也將有利於公司管理者和相關政策制定人士更好地支持開放式的創新舉措。

21508915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21508915.value: Mobile OTT messaging apps as a new technology are gaining popularity. On one hand, since OTT messaging apps are able to deliver text, voice and video services over the Internet for free, they are substitutes for traditional text and voice services provided by wireless carriers. On the other hand, OTT messaging apps may help drive the growth in mobile data consumption in various ways. The objective of this proposed study is to examine the effects of OTT messaging apps adoption on wireless carriers’ different revenue streams. I propose use a mobile usage dataset from its subscribers provided by a leading telecommunications company in China. I plan to focus on the most popular OTT messaging app in China, WeChat, and examine its impact on the wireless provider’s revenue. As I observe mobile subscribers adopt WeChat app over the period of one year (2013), I am able to use a fixed effect difference-in-difference identification strategy to estimate the effect of WeChat adoption on voice calls, messages, and other browsing activities. I will first estimate the average effect of WeChat adoption while treating all subscribers homogenously, then examine if the main effects are moderated by previous ownerships of other OTT apps. To adjust for potential selection bias, I will employ the propensity score matching method to account for the endogenous adoption decision and test the robustness of the results. And lastly I will further investigate the exact mechanism through which OTT apps can drive data growth and affect wireless providers’ revenue. 移動OTT通訊應用程式作為一項日益普及的新技術。一方面，由於OTT通訊應用程式都能夠通過互聯網發送免費的文字，語音和視頻服務，他們能替代無線運營商提供的傳統的文字和語音服務。在另一方面，OTT通訊應用程式可以從不同方面幫助推動移動數據消費增長。本項目研究的目的是探討OTT通訊應用程式對無線運營商的不同收入來源的影響, 建議使用國內一間主要的電信公司的用戶移動使用的數據,重點將放在中國最流行的OTT通訊應用程或, 如微信上，並研究它對無線服務提供商的收入的影響。透過觀察移動用戶使用微信超過一年（2013年）期間，我可以用一個固定的效果差，在差識別策略，估計微信對語音通話，短信，和其他瀏覽活動的影響。我會先估算採用微信的平均效應，同時把所有用戶均勻，然後檢查擁有其他OTT應用程式是否有影響。為調整潛在的選擇偏差，我將採用傾向得分匹配法核算的內生通過的決定和檢驗結果的可靠性。最後一點，我會進一步調查透過OTT應用程式可以推動數據增長和影響無線運營商的收入的機制。

21600815.label: Project Objectives
21600815.value: To examine the relationships and mediational pathways of the influences of perceived parental sacrifices on developmental outcomes (indexed by achievement motivation, resilience, hopelessness) via filial piety among poor adolescents in Hong Kong over time; To investigate the differences between paternal and maternal sacrifices perceived by adolescents over time; To assess the interaction effect of perceived paternal and maternal sacrifices on influencing filial piety and developmental outcomes among poor adolescents over time.
rows: To examine the relationships and mediational pathways of the influences of perceived parental sacrifices on developmental outcomes (indexed by achievement motivation, resilience, hopelessness) via filial piety among poor adolescents in Hong Kong over time;
To investigate the differences between paternal and maternal sacrifices perceived by adolescents over time;
To assess the interaction effect of perceived paternal and maternal sacrifices on influencing filial piety and developmental outcomes among poor adolescents over time.

21600815.label: Realisation of objectives
21600815.value: The study was a three-wave longitudinal study examining the relationships among perceived parental sacrifices, filial piety and developmental outcomes in a sample of poor adolescents in Hong Kong over time. Totally, 12 secondary schools across Hong Kong joined the study. Data was collected during the period between March 2016 and October 2018. Rather than selecting the respondents who were economically disadvantaged to participate in the study that might create risks of labeling and disclosing their identities to others, the participating schools invited all students to participate in the study. Together with the fact that secondary students commonly did not have clear information of their monthly household income, recipients of Comprehensive Social Security Assistance (CSSA), Full Textbook Allowance (TBA), or the Low-income Working Family Allowance Scheme (LIFA) were used as screening criteria to identify the adolescent sample experiencing economic disadvantage. These screening criteria were commonly used in other poverty researches in Hong Kong (e.g., Shek, 2005). The data was collected during class lessons in schools. Informed consent from parents and students was sought. Researcher and/or trained research assistants conducted the data collection in class. The data collection process was smooth. During Time 1, the students of S1 and S2 were invited to fill out the questionnaires containing the measures of paternal and maternal sacrifice, filial piety (reciprocal and authoritarian), adolescent developmental outcomes (social-oriented achievement motivation, resilience, hopelessness, life satisfaction, cognitive competence, self-determination, self-efficacy, and clear and positive identity), other family variables (e.g., parental control, parent-child relationship) and some questions on demographic characteristics (e.g., gender, age, duration of stay in Hong Kong, family intactness, economic hardship, number of children in the family). The questionnaire was filled in a self-administered format. Identical procedures were repeated in Time 2 and Time 3, with an interval of one year. There were totally 2,133 valid questionnaires collected in Time 1, of which 716 (33.6%) were filled by students experiencing economic disadvantage under the above-mentioned criteria. For the longitudinal data of three waves, there were 1,569 respondents who had completed the questionnaire at three time points, with the attrition rate of 26.4%. Among them, 527 (33.6%) respondents belonged to the economically disadvantaged group. The attrition rate for the economically disadvantaged group was also 26.4%, which was below the anticipated estimation in the calculation of adequate sample size. All measurements showed good psychometric properties in the study. Among 527 respondents who had completed questionnaires at all time points, 48.4% (n = 255) were girls, and 51.6% (n = 272) were boys. At Time 1, the mean age was 13.17 (SD = .97). 310 (58.8%) students studied in S1, while 217 (41.2%) studied in S2. Majority was born in Hong Kong (n = 373, 70.8%). 360 (68.3%) came from intact families, 38 (7.2%), 67 (12.7%), 18 (3.4%) and 27 (5.1%) came from remarried, separated and widowed families (9 respondents reported “others” and 8 did not respond). All the objectives are fully achieved. For Objective 1, cross-lagged panel analyses on the relationships among paternal and maternal sacrifice, filial piety, and adolescent developmental outcomes over time were performed. The results showed that filial piety fully mediated the relationship between perceived maternal sacrifice and adolescents’ social-oriented achievement motivation, resilience, hopelessness, and self-determination over time, respectively. However, the relationship between paternal sacrifice at Time 1 and filial piety at Time 2 was non-significant. There were non-significant reverse mediational effects of filial piety on the relationship between adolescent outcomes (social-oriented achievement motivation, resilience, hopelessness, self-determination) and parental sacrifice (paternal and maternal) over time. For Objective 2, the results of generalized linear models (GLM) showed that while paternal sacrifice was stable across different time point, maternal sacrifice was decreasing over time. However, respondents perceived higher levels of maternal sacrifice than paternal sacrifice across different time points. When examining the different components of paternal and maternal sacrifice, it was found that “maternal time spent on child’s education”, “maternal restructuring of daily routine”, and “paternal restructuring of daily routine” were decreasing across different time points, whereas “paternal shielding of worries” was marginally increasing over time. Economically disadvantaged mothers might face more constraints in supporting their children’s education and development when the children grow up, making the respondents perceive lower levels of maternal sacrifice. For Objective 3, paternal and maternal sacrifice interacted with each other to predict resilience, self-determination, positive self-identity and self-efficacy respectively at Time 1. While perceived maternal sacrifice was positively associated with adolescent resilience, self-determination, positive self-identity and self-efficacy respectively at higher levels of perceived paternal sacrifice, the relationships became non-significant when adolescents perceived lower levels of paternal sacrifice. However, the interaction effects of paternal and maternal sacrifices on adolescent developmental outcomes were non-significant over time. The study is pioneering in social science literature in examining the relationships between parental sacrifice and adolescent developmental outcomes among Chinese adolescents in Hong Kong. The mediational pathways of filial piety on the relationship between parental sacrifice and adolescent developmental outcomes, changes of paternal and maternal sacrifices across different time points, and the interaction effects of paternal and maternal sacrifices on adolescent developmental outcomes were also assessed. Echoed the cultural-ecological perspectives (Super & Harkness, 1986) and the Chinese socialization model (Chao & Tseng, 2002), maternal sacrifice serves as a protector factor that promote positive development of Chinese adolescents experiencing economic disadvantage via the development of filial piety. The findings contribute to the development of Chinese family process model in the context of resilience. The findings of changes of perceived paternal and maternal sacrifice is also novel in the existing literature, which provides important insights for researchers, family practitioners and social workers in understanding the constraints that economically disadvantaged mothers are facing in nurturing their children.
