21611315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21611315.value: This research is about discovering narrative strategies, cinematic language and aesthetics of an immersive panoramic computer animation that utilise technology in virtual reality, 3D audio and computer graphics. Since the invention of cinema more than a century ago, the filmic language has evolved with one thing remained relatively unchanged - the rectangular screen. With the single screen, narratives are structured temporally. One point of view at a time. The frame selects and excludes parts of reality, filtering out but enhancing certain information. The frame also acts as a compositional device, directing the audience’s eyes to see what the filmmakers want them to see. The audience’s construction of the narrative space is metaphorically speaking, on the other side of the screen. On a parallel historical path, panoramic screens, multiple projections, dome theatres, and virtual reality systems have been used to create immersive and sometimes interactive experiences. In most of these works, the frame disappears. The audience’s gaze is liberated. The architectural space where a work is disseminated and received, becomes relevant in the construction of the narrative space. Narratives can be structured not only temporally, but also spatially. Multiple events can be happening in all directions, even behind the audience. Narratives can be polychronic - story threads of different time periods simultaneously presented. These kinds of works are often grouped under the term, “Expanded Cinema”, first coined by filmmaker Stan VanDerBeek in 1967 who envisioned a new mode of film and video experimentation. With the recent revival of interests in Virtual Reality (VR), I propose to explore the potentials of the technology in storytelling. At this early stage of the “VR Renaissance”, most of the interests are in using the technology for gaming, or as a scientific visualisation or architectural tool. However, there is a huge potential of using the current VR technology to tell stories that are otherwise impossible to tell in the linear single screen form. This research will follow the spirit of Expanded Cinema, to understand the narrative and cinematic potentials of VR technology, and to search for new modes of expression. In order to do so, an immersive animation will be produced that will be loosely based on Jorge Luis Borges’ short story, “Library of Babel”. The outcomes of this research will include an exhibit of the animation at the Creative Media Centre, City University of Hong Kong, and at international venues such as SIGGRAPH and Ars Electronica. 此研究項目的目的是透過製作一部沉浸式三維電腦動畫，從而探索利用虛擬現實等技術可以開拓怎樣的敘事手法和電影美學。

21611315.label: Realisation of objectives
21611315.value: 5.3 Realisation of Objectives BACKGROUND The term, Cinematic Virtual Reality (CVR), has emerged in recent years that describes a specific branch of Virtual Reality experiences. Unlike the more interactive, game-like and real time experiences, CVR experiences are usually pre-rendered or captured on panoramic cameras with little to no interaction, and are produced with methodologies and techniques largely borrowed from conventional “frame-based” cinema. In Cinematic VR the absence of the frame is a two sided sword that is both liberating and constraining. The viewer’s freedom to look in any direction offers a strong sense of physical immersion, but it also confounds storytellers, especially filmmakers who are well versed in the cinematic language of manipulating the viewer's attention through framing and montage. Without control over the viewer’s attention, certain types of narratives become difficult, even impossible to convey, especially plot driven ones that rely on tight causal relationship between story events. Looking intently on a small feature in a scene might cause the viewer to miss out the more important event happening behind her. Strategies that redirect the viewer’s attention have been borrowed from conventional cinema. But they do not offer much to the understanding of the narrative potential that the unique qualities of this medium afford. The scattered viewer’s attention prompted me to hypothesize a model of interactive narrative in which the story progresses according to the viewer’s attention, instead of forcing the viewer’s attention to a fixed linear story progression. In other words, the viewer would not be “missing out” any important events, because the story would adapt to her attention. This research is motivated by the questions of how this hypothetical model of interactive narrative would play out in an actual production, what narrative strategies and spatial techniques it would entail, and how it could be applied to storytelling in Cinematic VR in general. This research employs a practice led approach with the creative production being the site of enquiry and with the knowledge embodied in the final work. The creative work is an animated reimagination of the storyworld in Jorge Luis Borges’ “Library of Babel”, produced using techniques of 3D computer graphics and digital visual effects. OBJECTIVES The creative work consists of two parts - 1) an authoring/editing and playback software, and 2) animated content rendered as stereoscopic panoramic movie files. Authoring involves drawing circles in the virtual space that define the “regions of interest”, deciding on how to capture the viewer’s attention, and connecting individual scenes to form a flow graph with each connection representing the viewer’s attention and the resulting scene transition. My team and I spent the first two years working out the possible gaze interactions, designing and implementing the software. Determining the viewer’s attention turned out to be more sophisticated than simply measuring the time the viewer’s gaze accumulated on a certain region. In order to more accurately determine the viewer’s attention in a particular scene, we need to consider the gaze gestures - how fast and when she moves her gaze - in relation to the scenography. Therefore, the authoring and playback software tools are essential to the realisation of the interaction mechanism. The first prototype with very limited functionalities was completed in the first year. It was implemented as an application running inside the Unity 3D game engine. The constraint of this software architecture soon became apparent as there were limited software libraries available within the Unity 3D software ecology for building the graphical user interface (GUI) that we envisioned. Also, the software tools are intended to be used beyond this project by a broader community of creators, therefore, scalability and flexibility are also important factors. We decided to redesign the software from the ground up with the insights we gained from building the prototype. However, with the limited funding, we could not hire a software developer with the needed experience in GUI design and programming. Therefore, we needed a new way to author without relying on the graphical representation. Text based input was chosen at the end though entering 3D coordinates by hand is a lot more tedious than simply dragging out a circle in the virtual space. In the new design, a text-based description file in JSON format describes the topology of the scene connections and how the viewer’s gaze is to be interpreted in each scene. This text based description file can either be generated by a graphical authoring software, or simply created with a text editor. This approach allows us to defer the development of the graphical authoring software until further funding becomes available. As mentioned in the 2nd progress report, another GRF application has been lodged for this purpose. This model of interactive narrative was published in a paper titled “The Library: A Non-Intrusive Gaze Directed Virtual Reality Animation” and was presented at the IEEE VR 2019 Conference in Osaka in March. In terms of research objectives, this paper presented new narrative strategies for storytelling in Cinematic VR (Objective 1). While we were developing the interaction strategies and the software tools that enable them, the story script were being written, and production of the animated content had begun. From the very beginning, I envisioned a visual quality that could convey the physicality often found in stop-motion animations. This requires a certain level of photo-realism in the handling of lighting, surface shading, dynamic simulations and atmospheric effects. Therefore, pre-rendering is obviously more preferable than real-time rendering, because the former could offload the intensive computation from the playback device to the production process, and allow the work to be disseminated to a broader range of hardware platforms. As mentioned in the 2nd Progress Report, the production of the animated content had experienced a lot of technical obstacles in the early stages, because of immature rendering and compositing technologies. These technologies have improved over the past 2 years, therefore, most of the technical problems have been overcome and we have settled in a production pipeline to efficiently create digital assets (Objective 3). The production is expected to complete by the end of March 2020, and the final work will be submitted to international film and media festivals. Unfortunately, evaluation cannot be done until after the work is shown in festivals (Objective 5). However, the project has been awarded the Educational Grant by the International Animated Film Society (ASIFA-Hollywood), and the work-in-progress was presented at the 31st Society for Animation Studies Conference in Lisbon, Portugal, 2019 (Objective 4). Unfortunately, evaluation cannot be done until the creative work is completed and exhibited in festivals (Objective 5). The long production time is due to a number of factors: - Departure of research staff. - Difficulty of hiring research staff with relevant experiences in high end CG animation production. - Animation is a labor intensive process. Without an experienced team of animators, I often had to redo a lot of the work to reach a certain level of quality, thus making the process very inefficient. - Lack of funding to afford more efficient rendering hardware and software licenses, or cloud rendering services.

21611315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21611315.value: Cinematic Virtual Reality is still in its infancy with many unexplored narrative potentials. This research seeks to develop narrative strategies that would harness such potentials. The hypothetical model of interactive narrative described above is one strategy that exploits the scattered viewer’s attention. Although the creative work is still in progress, it has received recognition from the international community as evidenced by the award from ASIFA-Hollywood, and the publications through IEEE VR and the Society of Animation Studies. I am confident that the completed work will receive more recognition and set a humble example of narrative strategies for Cinematic VR. Also, the software tool that we developed to author the creative work is expected to be used beyond this project by other creators and storytellers, so that the hypothetical model could be explored and refined by a broader creative community.

21611415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21611415.value: Economic disadvantage has been found to be associated with delayed cognitive and language development, and mental health symptoms such as aggression, anxiety of children. Chronic cumulative stressors of poverty disrupt their attention, emotional and behavioural regulation, that would further lead to negative impact in early development. As their parents are also affected by stress, they often become unresponsive, harsh and inconsistent in child discipline, resulting in a chronic stress to their children. Mindfulness is defined as paying attention purposefully and non-judgmentally to the present moment. It has been shown to improve attention, promote exposure to unpleasant experiences, facilitate cognitive change, and enhance the ability to cope with life stress. Mindfulness training has been established as an evidence-based intervention for people suffering from various chronic conditions. Its application in a family context, including parents and children, is just beginning. The purpose of this study is to assess the effectiveness of a family-based mindfulness intervention (FBMI) in reducing parental stress and promoting child adjustment. Intervention effectiveness will be tested by conducting a randomized controlled trial comparing a group receiving FBMI to a wait-list control group. Children aged five and their parents will be recruited to participate in the study. Two hundred and sixty eligible families will be recruited, stratified by level of economically disadvantage, behaviour problem scores, and parental stress, and then randomly assigned to the two groups. Intervention groups will be conducted by instructors with professional training. Children in the intervention group are expected to show improvements in cognitive and language development, behaviour problems, attention and emotional/behavior regulation, and physiological stress (reduced cortisol and heart rate variability), compared with the waitlist control group. Parents are expected to show improvements in physiological and psychological stress, and mindfulness, compared with the waitlist control group. The proposed project will be the first of its kind to use mindfulness training in a family context in Hong Kong. It is also unique as it examines the effectiveness of a mindfulness-based intervention with multiple outcome measures related to stress, combining self-reported measures with biomarkers, and psychological tests. For model building and theory development, this study may shed light on assessing the change mechanisms for promoting child learning, emotional and behavioural regulation, particularly in relation to studies of stress physiology and economically disadvantaged families. The results may not only benefit in Hong Kong but also those in other Chinese societies and countries. 文獻顯示弱勢家庭與兒童認知及語言發展遲緩、精神健康癥狀包括暴力及焦慮相關。貧窮形成長期累積的壓力會損害兒童的注意力，情緒及行為的調節，對早期成長造成深遠的影響。與此同時，兒童的父母同樣受到壓力的影響，在管教時有時出現不回應，苛刻或不貫徹形成對子女一種長期的壓力。 靜觀的定義是有意識地及不加批判地將注意力放在此時此刻上。研究顯示靜觀訓練可以改善注意力、提升對不愉快經驗的接納，有助認知的轉變，提升對生活壓力的管理。靜觀訓練已被確立成一種以實證為基礎的介入模式，廣泛應用於面對各種長期壓力的人士。然而，靜觀訓練在家庭層面的應用仍在起步階段。 本研究的目的為評估家庭為本靜觀訓練應用於減低家長壓力及提升兒童適應的成效。介入成效將通過一隨機對照臨床實驗，比較實驗組及輪候對照組來測定其成效。研究將招募五至七歲之兒童及家長參與研究。研究團隊將招募260個家庭，以家庭收入、兒童行為問題指數、家長壓力進行分層隨機分組。小組由曾接受相關專業訓練的靜觀導師帶領。研究假設兒童在介入後與輪候對照組比較，在認知及語言發展、行為問題、注意力及情緒/行為調節及生理壓力（唾液皮質醇及心跳變異率）會有所改善。同時假設家長在生理及心理壓力及靜觀程度與輪候對照組比較會有所改善。 這項研究是本地其中一項最早的家庭為本靜觀訓練研究，其獨特性包括以心理及生理方法測定與壓力有關的介入成果。在模式建構及理論發展的層面，本研究或許能為弱勢家庭的壓力生理研究、兒童學習、情緒及行為調節的提升上作出啟示。研究結果不但能令香港有關群體受益，或許亦能為華人社區及其他國家相關研究提出方向。

21612415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21612415.value: The proposed project will investigate representations of castration and impotence in Anglo-American writing from 1919 to 1945 in the context of both classical psychoanalytic approaches to literature and contemporary interdisciplinary medical humanities. The battlefields of World War I left returning soldiers with manifold physical and psychological wounds that directly challenged perceptions of masculinity, including physical castration caused by injury and infection, impotence caused by the widespread use of chemical weapons and traumatic neurosis which was viewed at the time as a form of feminine hysteria. While the local effects of sexual and psychological impotence have been widely recognised in work by Ernest Hemingway, T.S. Eliot and Virginia Woolf, critics have underestimated the depth of this motif’s influence within the development of modernist aesthetic and political agendas, particularly surrounding the dismantling of empire. This investigation will examine the ways in which images of emasculation animated Anglo-American writing during the interwar period and – as literary images steeped in medical realties – were used by writers to: 1) register and assuage the traumas of World War I, 2) interrogate modern masculine sexualities and 3) ultimately to reconceive understandings of modernity within a new transnational context. The relationship between castration, masculinity and modernity reveals itself in the varied manifestations of this motif in interwar literature. The writers Ernest Hemingway, T.S. Eliot, Virginia Woolf, Bernard Shaw, D.H. Lawrence, Evelyn Waugh, William Faulkner, Jean Toomer and Christopher Isherwood all drew on this topic in a number of ways that reflected the contentious social views on topics including race, nation, empire, sexuality and gender. The proposed project intends to demonstrate how these writers attempted to rationalise their views on interwar society with heavily coded metaphors of nonexistence. Situating this study within the area of interdisciplinary medical humanities will serve to reassert the significance of these literary texts in contemporary applied medical contexts including urology, clinical psychology, psychoanalysis and community health. The proposed project will offer the first sustained account of how the literary uses of castration and impotence resituated modernist aesthetics and shaped a view of masculinity and modernity that played out on the global, postcolonial stage. Beyond this, it will provide evidence of alternative views of male psychosexualities in the 1919-1945 period while explicating the history of how interwar writers reimagined the very material medical issues of emasculation and castration. 21613815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21613815.value: 网络化的社会中，流动的知识、人口、与资本相交融的节点上，文化城市应运崛起。这就对地方性管制提出挑战，地方政府如何在其区域范围内制定、执行政策，以吸引相应地资本、人口；以福柯式的视角，即为如何运用管制技术以形成一种所谓正确的人口与土地的结合。本研究基于中国发展文化城市的背景，集中讨论如何去看待这种地域化的管制技术。 创意产业的从业人员似乎呈现出极端的两面性：一方面创意阶层的工作很“酷”，工作地点很有“活力”；另一方面，文化劳动力主要以项目型工作为基础，因此生存状况很不稳定。在冠冕浪漫的面纱下暗藏着新的社会分化与排他机制 – 道德公民权。道德公民权分离公民与其生存地的公民权利，将社会福利系限制于对经济有价值的群体身上。 在中国，地理学应该关注道德公民权利方面的研究有两个原因：1. 大批的外来务工人员是文化城市、文化区涌现出的新经济体，但是他们多为个体雇佣，也没有去进行交涉的权力。2.户口制度曾是人口管理的地方化工具，如今与新自由主义的道德观共谋，去鼓励个体雇佣的形式。通过地理学层面的探讨，本研究的目的在于对地方化的技术提出质疑：新的户口制度（及其派生出的各类政策、规定等）与道德标准是如何去赋予文化劳动力和文化区生产力导向的倾向的，进而形成去地域化、再地域化的动态发展过程。 首先，该研究将有助于该问题在全球范围内的讨论：道德公民权利是如何被阐释从而促成有选择性的吸引一部分人口同时排除另一部分人，并将文化劳动力置于一个不断寻找求生和成功之处的旅途。因此本研究将会进一步揭示在中国的这种脆弱的地理性。第二，通过社群层面的调查，本研究试图将地域化的技术拓展到一个以多重方式参与的、行动者网络的范围，去揭示一个“更复杂的（国家－社会）在简单化、管控与改进之间的关系。”运用福柯式的研究角度，研究不仅检视意识形态修辞话语或经济战略，并力图检视地域化管制下的国家空间塑造。

21613815.label: Realisation of objectives
21613815.value: 1. Build up the database on the mobility of the precarious cultural community in the two circles A couple of questionnaire surveys have been carried out in Shenzhen and Shanghai to build up the database of the mobility of creative labours across different creative industrial parks. A total of 328 valid questionnaires have been received. Quantitative analyse of the survey data were implemented, to map the general pattern of mobility along both temporal and spatial dimensions. The mobility survey has two purposes: the first one is to capture the temporal pattern of precariousness, measured by the number of indicators summarised from the literature on precarity; the second one is to map the spatial precariousness of creative workers, which entails fixity/flow of workers in different clusters. The second dimension is yet systematically covered by the literature on precarity. The survey has been completed and the first objective has been fully achieved. The survey is published in an edited volume on culture-led gentrification. 2. Identify the wide range of actors, organizations, and their interplays in terms of territorialization and counter-territorialization at the cultural community scale Based on our first-hand data on spatial mobility of creative workers and secondary data from reports, newspaper articles and documentary books, we identified three clusters for in-depth field studies - Dafen Art village in Shenzhen, Fuzhou (PhD student project), and Lishui Barbizon. We carry out ethnographic field works in the three clusters, entailing participatory observation, on-site observation, interviews, and focus group discussions. Fieldworks last from 1 month to 4 months, and we visited each site for at least once per year. Continous communication has been maintained through social media afterwards. In our ethnographies work in these clusters, creative workers in these clusters include painters, makers, and DIY musicians. In the processes of (counter-)territorialisation, we identified an ensemble of actors in their dynamic but hierarchal social worlds, exemplified by the cases of A. Painters villages (Dafen and Lishui): painter-masters, painter-workers, villagers, dealers, government department and government agencies at the province, city, district scales, B. DIY musicians (Shenzhen): musicians, NGOs, patrons, enterprises, government department and government agencies at the province, city, district scales, C. Makers (Shenzhen): makers, entrepreneurs, universities, NGOs, government department and government agencies at the province, city, district scales, etc. The diversified sectors in the creative industries allowed us to explore both particularities and generalities, whereas the geographic locations of clusters also provide valuable sites with variegated contexts. We have kept field notes and interview transcripts throughout the process. Based on our ethnographic work in the three clusters, we have fully achieved the second objective. 3. To contribute to the theoretical understanding of the technology of territorialization, in particular, the technique of moral citizenship imposed upon the precarious population We engage the literature on territorialisation on three scales, the national scale, the city/village/cluster scale, and the transnational scale. On this matter, the method of following the thing (the mobile workers) has allowed us to move beyond one case, but to explore trans-local mutations, and different process when actors encounter different contexts. We explore the polemic relations of the state and the society in this process and explore how the boundary of the state and society becomes porous. Ethnographic studies are very helpful in digging out rich data at very subtle levels. We have finished case analyses and cross-case comparisons. On findings derived from single cases, we have published on top peer-reviewed journals, and now we are in the progress of comparative studies and finding synthesis from different cases. The article “State territorialization, neoliberal governmentality: the remaking of Dafen oil painting village, Shenzhen, China” has been chosen to feature in “Routledge Geography Article Collection 2017”, as one of the four articles in urban geography for its original contribution to existing literature at the conceptual level. The third objective has been achieved fully. 4. To produce monograph publication based on both empirical studies and conceptual exploration The PI is now drafting the book proposal upon invitation from the editor with Edward Elgar, with an initial deadline of January 2020. Another year is anticipated to finish the full monograph. Given that I have published several cases in forms of journal papers and book chapters, therefore, it is anticipated that at least 50% of the monograph are done (with draft versions).

21613815.label: Major findings and research outcome
21613815.value: The pattern and process of mobility and territorialisation The process of (counter-)territorialisation is also very dynamic, featured with fast displacements of social groups, which we argue for a increasingly liquid occupation of spaces. On the one hand, our studies reveal an ephemeral and intensive pattern of mobility, which implies a high uncertainty of life and the precarious life on both temporal and spatial dimensions. On the other, we observe an emerging affective web encompassing nodes and networks, which allow creative workers to get networked and attempt subjective manner of space usage. There is chance for autonomy of the creative workers, although the process is always encroached by profit-driven appropriation and state regulation. In the processes of (counter-)territorilisation, the dynamic interplay of actors must be situated in multiple scales, namely, the clusters/villages/cities, the individuals’ everyday life, and the trasnational scales. Territorialisation as technology of governance Through moral citizenship In the two papers on state territorialization in Dafen and China’s Public Rental Housing Scheme, we adopt the approach of state territorialization, drawing insights from the Foucauldian conception of governmentality as disposition of things—people and land. At issue here is how territorialization deploys the moral citizenship to define the ‘category of worth’, to enable mobility of the population. Through the ambient power of place making In the chapter on the moral atmosphere of Lishui Barbizon, we explore the technology of ambient power of place. Through the case of Lishui, we urge for a diffusive reading of power relations. It is not only any single source which produced a collective moral feeling through central engineering, but also a collection of forces forming a nebulous form of power, which flows through a heterogeneous assemblage of bodily experiences and re-produced through a circulation of affect. The affective and prosaic state space was further investigated in the paper on makers in the Mass entrepreneurship campaign. We argue for a new configuration of space that blurs the traditional boundary between education, work and sociality. Territorialisation as technology for creative autonomy In the paper on DIY musicians and their liquid use of space, we explore the politicisation and policing activities in the process of territorialisation. The spatial changes of Chinese rock, from fluidity to fixity and then a return to fluidity again, did not escape Grossberg’s prediction that subculture might not generate real political changes. Still, they demonstrate a standing-out action that appropriates space by “those who have no parts”, rather than hiding out in cracks.

21613815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21613815.value: In this project, we have basically focused on either the state or the society side, while keeping in minds the two polemic forces are always interactive to each other. In this sense, there are two directions for future studies: Firstly, one of the directions of future research is to focus on the encounters of both. Through this project, what impressed us most is that territorialization is a not a singular process practised by cultural vagabonds alone, but involves multiple forces such as town mayors, planners, cultural elites, youths, the new middle class and even transnational capital and expatriate communities among others (Wang, 2016; Wang & Chen, 2019). Second, the other direction wold be a move beyond the national boundary to look at transnational production of culture and transnational mobility of creative labours, which is another heated topic that involved geopolitics and geo-economy. For instance, the Sino-America trade war on Hi-Technology is one example of the tension when creative industry expand across borders.

21613815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21613815.value: Creating creative zones for the creative population has been deployed by many cities to develop a new economic sector. Labelled with a “flexible specialization” production mode, the cultural community seem to bear dual identities: the creative class with ‘cool’ jobs in ‘buzzing’ places and, the cultural labours who work on a project-by-project basis, therefore living with precarity. The ‘glamorized risk’ justifies the moral citizenship, which detaches welfare entitlement from place of residence and attaches welfare to the ‘category of worth’, serving as a crucial instrument of population management. This raises the question of territorial governance of a highly mobile cultural community. Adding the geographic dimension to moral citizenship studies contribute to the literature through three scholarly questions. First, how is the pattern of mobility and territorialisation of creative workers, with particular attention to painters, DIY musicians and makers? Second, how is the process of state territorialisation, which refers to how state divides territory to different zones, and relocate different population and respective economy to different zones? Third, how is the process territorialisation excised by creative labours themselves, to claim their right in the city? Situated in these concern, we zoom into the nodes to examine how the moral citizenship mobilizes the cultural labour, leading to an always on-going process of de-territorialisation and re-territorialisation.

21615915.value: • To significantly move forward our understanding of basic questions concerning the nature and rise of transnational corporations in the era of globalization by filling key empirical gaps in the literature, and thereby contribute to foundational debates in political economy. • To test the following hypothesis formulated from preliminary research: Corporate nationality remains crucially important in the era of globalization, and the characterization of giant corporations as globally footloose, nation-less, and beyond the control of states is a myth. • To contribute to urgent scholarly and public policy debates concerning corporate regulation, taxation, and inequality in both Hong Kong SAR and world-wide. • To produce the following research outputs: 1) Four submissions (three single-authored, one co-authored with a Senior Research Assistant) to leading academic journals across a range of sub-disciplines (such as International Organization, International Security, Journal of Public Policy, and New Political Economy); 2) A single-authored book manuscript; 3) A co-authored policy paper for an international think tank, as well as opinion pieces for local and international newspapers; 4) Six international conference presentations (two co-authored and four single-authored); and 5) A unique database on the global distribution of corporate ownership and control, wealth and power. • To build upon new relationships recently formed at the Center for International Studies at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology where I am Research Affiliate, including with Executive Director Professor John Tirman and Institute Professor Noam Chomsky (please see “Research Plan” below).

21615915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21615915.value: After over half a century of expanding foreign operations, the world’s top transnational corporations (TNCs) now straddle the globe. And yet, there is no consensus on basic questions concerning their nature. Do TNCs still have a nationality or are they by now “nation-less” in the era of globalization? That is, when many of the world’s top TNCs operate in scores of countries across six continents, is it still meaningful to designate, for example, British Petroleum as British, General Electric as American, Nestlé as Swiss, or Toyota as Japanese? Following from this, can TNCs be held nationally accountable or are they beyond the control of national populations? Are TNCs the expressions of national interest and power or do they represent the rise of a new “nation-less” global elite? Put another way, who controls and/or owns the world’s top TNCs? How or why does this matter, if at all? These questions are essential for understanding the rise and significance of transnational corporations, with widespread relevance for core theoretical and policy debates across academia, government, and civil society on the changing nature of world order in the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries. These questions underpin this Early Career Scheme grant proposal. The core of this research project will address crucial empirical gaps in our understanding of corporate ownership structures and the global distribution of shareholdings and wealth — and the implications of this data for the questions listed above. It will span 48 months, and involve a Senior Research Assistant to assist in data collection and analysis, and to co-publish a journal article and policy paper. There will be four fieldtrips to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), where I am Research Affiliate, in order to scour their databases not available in Hong Kong. This project will create the following research outputs: 1) Conference papers; 2) Four publications in leading journals; 3) A policy paper; 4) A book manuscript; and 5) Once these submissions are published, a database on corporate ownership and control to be made publicly available for the first time. Thus, funding from this grant will provide an excellent opportunity to make a significant contribution towards our understanding of the global political economy, and navigating the policy challenges of the twenty-first century concerning the nexus between corporate and national power in world order. 內容摘要：半世紀來全球經濟迅猛擴張，當世大型跨國公司已然在世界各地拓展業務。有關跨國公司性質的爭論由此展開：宏觀上，它們是否還具有國別屬性，或者已在經濟全球化時代實現“去國別化”？具體而言，英國石油公司、美國通用電氣公司、瑞士雀巢公司、日本豐田汽車公司的運營規模遍佈地球各個角落，現在談論它們屬於某個國家是否只具有象徵意義？問責機制上，大型跨國公司是否要對本國公民負責，或者已超越了一國的司法權限？所有權上，它們還能否繼續代表本國的利益訴求和綜合國力，或者已轉化為去國家主義精英新貴們的利益表達工具？換言之，到底誰在掌控這些跨國公司，一旦去國別化真實存在會產生怎樣的理論觀照與社會影響？在“過去三十年世界格局變遷”問題上的理論解讀與政策辨析已然卷帙浩繁，上述問題的解答將對理解跨國公司的勃興與世界主導權大有裨益，同時也會在學界、政界和民間引起廣泛共鳴。本研究計畫即由這些問題的探討而展開，核心工作力求完善現有實證研究文獻的不足之處，尤其是公司所有權結構、股權財產的全球性分佈，以及實證數據信息對現實語境的解釋力等問題。研究預計開展四年，需要一位高級研究助理共同完成數據收集分析、期刊撰寫和政策報告擬定等工作。此外，鑒於香港的有關資料不夠詳實，我們已與麻省理工學院（MIT）取得聯繫，屆時會借助我客座研究員的身份便利，進行相關資料檢索和數據整理（計畫前往四次）。最後，本研究課題在結題時將形成如下成果：會議論文、四篇頂級期刊論文、一份政策報告、一部專著、一套關於企業所有制和管理權的數據資料庫（學界尚屬首次）。因此，我堅信本課題一旦立項將對全球政治經濟學中的相關主題產生重要影響力和有益補充。在理論與實踐相結合方面，預期研究成果會讓社會各界從一個新穎角度去理解本世紀中企業運行和國家力量之間的互動博弈過程，從而更有效地制定相關政策法規以應對這場世界性變遷。

21615915.label: Realisation of objectives
21615915.value: Project Objective #1: The primary research output from this project is a book manuscript currently under review with Oxford University Press. Professor Noam Chomsky has already provided a blurb for this manuscript in May 2019, as follows: Front—"Fantastic piece of work...really revised our conception of global power". Back—"Conventional estimates of economic power rely on national accounts, primarily GDP. But these measures have lost their significance in the new age of globalization, this compelling study persuasively argues, showing that by the more realistic measure of ownership of the global economy, US power has reached astonishing heights. These carefully documented conclusions undermine laments about American declinism and the rise of China. A major and original contribution to understanding the actual distribution of power in the world order". Widely considered to be the most important intellectual alive, Chomsky has a very wide audience and has been frequently touting the research in this book in his many interviews and public lectures. One example: on August 7, 2020 at a talk at the Hong Kong Foreign Correspondents’ Club (FCC), he opined, “there’s a really outstanding political economist in Hong Kong, one of the best in the world, Sean Starrs”. He then spent several minutes in his talk reviewing the main argument and evidence in my book manuscript. The FCC requested that I give a talk based on this book once it is published. Chomsky’s FCC talk on YouTube currently has over 150,000 views, and a number of these viewers have reached out to me for more information on my upcoming book. Moreover, there are other renowned scholars that have cited my research in this project. Examples include the following prominent scholars in the field of international relations and international political economy, such as Prof. Benjamin Cohen (Google Scholar citations: 14,309), Prof. Daniel Drezner (Google Scholar citations: 11,157), Prof. Joseph S. Nye, Jr. (Google Scholar citations: 97,841), and Prof. William Wohlforth (Google Scholar citations: 10,641), as well as some with no Google Scholar profile, such as Adam Tooze and Robert Wade. Therefore, based on the above metrics alone, I believe I have fulfilled this project objective, and will only magnify this success once my book and other publications currently under review/in process are published. That is, by revealing how the globalization of production and finance by transnational corporations should fundamentally induce us to rethink national economic power, including how we measure it. In addition, concerning the relationship between state and capital as well as ownership and control of capital, especially by arguing for the continued relevance of the nationality of capital in the age of globalization. Project Objective #2: This hypothesis has been tested quantitatively throughout the duration of the project, primarily via annual data collection from the Bloomberg Professional terminal and other databases (such as Thomson Reuters SDC Platinum) at MIT. This hypothesis has also been tested qualitatively via collecting a wide range of examples of the US and Chinese states protecting corporations domiciled in their territories, including in the context of re-emerging techno-nationalism. Project Objective #3: In terms of scholarly debates, I believe my research outputs (including under review/forthcoming) are making such contributions. Moreover, I frequently contribute to media both in Hong Kong and internationally, and these contributions are infused with the insights reached in these research outputs. For example, I contributed 10 interviews/ panel debates with RTHK (Radio Television Hong Kong) between June 2016-November 2020, five for the South China Morning Post, two opinion pieces for The Financial Times, as well as interviews with Bloomberg News, Quartz, The Real News, Hong Kong Economic Forum, HK01 Media, among others. Hence I have contributed to urgent public policy debates with audiences both in Hong Kong and world-wide. Project Objective #4: The following research outputs have been produced, some still under review/forthcoming. My publication schedule has been delayed for reasons that are explained below. 1) Three submissions in academic journals, including one co-authored not with a Senior Research Assistant but a colleague at Sussex University in the UK (Senior Lecturer Dr. Julian Germann): with the Journal of Contemporary Asia, Socialist Register, and Development and Change. Moreover, I am currently almost finished a submission for International Organization (by January 2021), and will finish a submission for International Security by April 2021; 2) The editor-in-chief of social sciences at the New York office of Oxford University Press has sent the book manuscript out for review in May 2019. It remains under review (I have one positive review so far); 3) I have made extensive contributions to local and international media, please see Objective #3 above. As for a co-authored policy paper for an international think tank, I have not had the opportunity to do this, as I focused more on academic publications. But I presented my co-authored piece for Development and Change at the European Union’s Cooperation in Science and Technology (COST) in Brussels in November 2019, which acts like a think tank for the EU; 4) I greatly outperformed this objective with 16 conference presentations of this research between March 2016 and November 2019; 5) The plan was to construct this database in the final 2-3 months of the project before December 2019 by hiring 1-2 student assistants (as I have no experience in this), but the university was severely disrupted by social unrest and protests against the Hong Kong government and universities from June-December 2019. The latter half of the semester was cancelled, and security measures were taken such that students were banned from entering the campus. Therefore, I could not hire any students to construct this database. I hope to be able to do this with funding from my next grant. Moreover, my writing and publishing schedule was even more disrupted by severe stomach pains that started in November 2017 until I was finally sent to the emergency room in December 2018 and diagnosed with acute necrotizing pancreatitis with a 30% chance of death. I was hospitalized for a combined 48 days over six months and had serious surgery in May 2019. From 2016-2018 I also had a very heavy teaching and service load, in one semester 330 students with no teaching assistants, and after 2018 there were 5-6 faculty that did the service roles that I was responsible for in 2016-2018. But by the end of 2021, I hope to have a book contract with OUP and two more A* journal articles, which would more than compensate for the delay according to the schedule laid out in this project objective. Project Objective #5: My Research Affiliation with the Center for International Studies at MIT was converted into a Visiting Assistant Professorship by summer 2016, and my relationship with Chomsky greatly deepened as he has been citing my research ever since I showed him some data supported by this grant at MIT in August 2016. Chomsky moved to the University of Arizona in 2017 where I visited him in January 2020 to show him more data from this research, and he has continued to cite me and my research with the highest praise (for example, please see Objective #1 above). Therefore, I believe this objective has been accomplished beyond my expectations.

21615915.label: Major findings and research outcome
21615915.value: The core of this project is the annual collection of data regarding corporate power and ownership using the Forbes Global 2000 and the Bloomberg Professional databases. Other sources were also used, such as the China Customs Yearbook, corporate annual reports, Thomson Reuters SDC Platinum, and so on. The major findings are: 1) American ownership of global capital (represented by the crème de la crème, the top 2,000 corporations in the world as ranked by the Forbes Global 2000) remains dominant, both in terms of transnational corporations domiciled in the United States as well as those domiciled in various other countries, including China and Chinese state-owned enterprises, from 2010-2019; 2) American ownership of national profit-shares in 25 broad sectors of the Forbes Global 2000 remains dominant, from 2006-2020; 3) foreign ownership of China’s high-value global value chain exports remain dominant from 2000-2019, at over 80%, while only 10% of these exports from China are by Chinese privately-owned firms. Taken together, these three major findings challenge the conventional wisdom of American economic decline coupled with the rise of China, with implications on how we should measure national power in the age of globalization. That is, most observers employ national accounts, most of all GDP, to gauge the national economic power of a state, and since the American share of world GDP has declined while China’s has risen, many conclude that China is becoming more powerful in world order at the expense of the United States. But national accounts do not inform us who actually owns and profits from this economic activity, which is especially relevant in the age of the globalization of production and finance. By the alternative metrics developed in this research project—focusing on ownership rather than geographical location—we can see that American power remains globally dominant with no competitors on the horizon, including China. These findings also have implications on long-standing theoretical debates in political economy on the relationship between state and capital, government and “market”, as well as the importance of ownership versus control of capital. The major research outcome is a book manuscript currently under review with Oxford University Press, which has already received commendation from prominent scholars, including Noam Chomsky, widely regarded the most important intellectual alive. Based on this research, Chomsky has publicly praised me as “one of the best political economists in the world”.

21615915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21615915.value: There are a plethora of uses for these large databases constructed by this project, and I hope to make them publicly available online once my book manuscript is published. Especially unique and useful will be the national ownership structures of the top 500 corporations in the world as ranked by the Forbes Global 2000, from 2010-2019. This can be drawn upon not only by academics but also policy makers, think tankers, the media, activists, and the general public, in order to investigate who owns global capital generally and of individual corporations specifically. My next University Grants Council General Research Fund grant application (currently under review) seeks to continue updating this corporate ownership database annually, and use this to explore new research avenues concerning the apparent resurgence of techno-nationalism in the United States, Northeast Asia, and in Western Europe. That is, the national ownership of especially advanced technology is increasingly seen by major powers as a core national security interest. This has widespread implications on how we view the relationship between globalization and the state, the latter of which is often seen as an irreversible force threatening national sovereignty, instead of a process that is driven by states themselves.

21615915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21615915.value: Scholars and pundits for half a century have been arguing that American economic power is declining, with a renewed wave post-2008 with the Wall Street crash, ensuing global financial crisis, coupled with the continued rise of China. This project corrects this conventional wisdom by arguing that “declinists” have misconceptualized national economic power especially in the age of globalization by focusing on national accounts (most of all gross domestic product) instead of national ownership. Thus, this project amasses the corporate ownership data to demonstrate that by this alternative and more relevant metric of national economic power, American economic power continues to dominate with no contenders on the horizon, including China. This is the first project to not only reconceptualize national economic power in this way but also the first to amass such national, institutional, and individual ownership data of the world’s top 500 and 2,000 corporations as ranked by the Forbes Global 2000 from 2010 to 2019—with widespread uses and theoretical implications. Most of all, understanding the future of international power relations is essential to understanding all manner of issues, including the very prospects for organized human survival given deepening industrial-scale ecocide threatening life on Earth as we know it.

22102015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22102015.value: Hypoxia and ocean acidification are amongst the major environmental threats to many marine populations and ecosystems worldwide. Current evidence suggests that the number and areas of hypoxia zones mapped with human footprints have doubled every ten years since 1960, and the problem has been predicted to further exacerbate due to global warming. At the same time, about one third of anthropogenic CO2 has been absorbed by the oceans, resulting in ocean acidification. The average surface pH has already dropped by 0.1 unit since the early 1900s, and a further drop of up to 0.5 unit has been predicted by 2100. Microbial communities play a pivotal role in regulating the structure and function of ecosystems. In the marine environment, microbial communities of biofilms also serve as a signpost to guide the larval settlement of many benthic invertebrate species. Ample evidence has indicated that microbial communities are prone to environmental changes. However, it is not known whether and to what extent changes in microbial communities in response to ocean acidification and its interaction with hypoxia may alter larval settlement patterns and subsequently, the community structure of benthic invertebrates. Using marine invertebrates across three phyla as models (the gastropod Crepidula onyx, the barnacle Balanus amphitrite and the serpulid polychaete Hydroides elegans), we propose a systematic study to test the hypothesis that hypoxia and ocean acidification can individually and interactively affect bacterial biofilm composition and the subsequent larval settlement patterns. Experiments will first be carried out to investigate the individual effects of hypoxia and ocean acidification and later their interactive effects on the biofilm bacterial composition, using high-throughput pyrosequencing techniques. Settlement assays will be further carried out to test the hypothesis that alterations in biofilm bacterial composition due to hypoxia and ocean acidification will affect the larval settlement pattern of the model species. Results of this novel study will not only shed light on the effects of these two major environmental stressors on marine microbial community, but also for the first time, provide important and necessary scientific information that will enable us to evaluate and predict the ecological consequences and environmental risks of hypoxia and ocean acidification on marine benthic communities in the face of climate change.

22102015.label: Realisation of objectives
22102015.value: Biofilms were allowed to form on surfaces, which were later used in settlement assays at a polluted site and a control clean site. Changes in the bacterial composition associated with hypoxia and ocean acidification (HOA) were examined using 16S ribosomal rRNA gene pyrosequencing. Settlement assays were carried out to test the response of larval Crepidula onyx to the biofilms in control seawater and treatment seawater with a reduced DO and pH level. This provided us with a 2 × 2 factorial experiment with two biofilm levels (polluted biofilm and clean biofilm) and two seawater levels (treatment seawater and control seawater). The co-occurrence of hypoxia and acidification in seawaters within an aquaculture environment mimic conditions that resemble depleted oxygen levels and increasing pCO2 levels as predicted for future ocean conditions as a consequence of eutrophication. We hypothesized that the combined effects of reduced DO and pH levels would alter the bacterial composition of biofilms. Selection of control site and polluted HAO site. Two sites exhibiting different environmental conditions were chosen for this study. Port Shelter in Hong Kong was selected as the control site (22o34’N, 114o27’E), while Yung Shue O Fish Farm at the Three Fathoms Cove of Tolo Channel was designated as the polluted site with the co-occurrence of HAO (22o34’N, 114o27’E). Nutrient pollution coming from aquaculture results in seasonal hypoxia and acdification at Yung Shue O. Crepidula onyx are found at Port Shelter, but not Yung Shue O. Exposing biofilms to the co-occurrence of hypoxia and acidification. At each site, biofilms were allowed to develop for 13 days on Petri dishes (Falcon 1006, 50 × 9 mm) mounted on plastic frames (40 cm length × 31 cm width) submerged at 0.5 m above Chart Datum. After 13 days, triplicate control and HOA biofilms coated Petri dishes were returned to the laboratory. DNA isolation, 16S rRNA gene amplification and Illumina MiSeq Sequencing. Environmental DNA was recovered using the PowerSoil® DNA Isolation Kit (MO BIO Laboratories, Carlsbad, CA, USA) and assessed for purity using the 260/280 ratios on a NanoDrop™ 2000 Spectrophotometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Wilmington, DE, USA). DNA concentration was quantified using Qubit® dsDNA HS Assay Kit and the Qubit® Fluorometer (Life Technologies, Carlsbad, CA, USA) and tested for sample integrity with 1% agarose gel electrophoresis. PCR was performed using dual-index 341F (5’-ACTCCTACGGGAGGCAGCAG-3’) and 806R (5’GGACTACHVGGGTWTCTAAT-3’) primers targeting the V3-V4 hypervariable region. Bioinformatics. Briefly, raw sequencing fastq manifest files were demultiplexed and processed on Quantitative Insights Into Microbial Ecology. Paired-end sequences were demultiplexed with the q2-demux method and denoised with DADA2 at a truncated length of 284 and 217 base pairs for forward and reverse reads, respectively. Output representative sequences were grouped into Amplicon Sequence Variants (ASVs) based on 100% sequence similarity, and taxonomically classified up to genus level using the Naives-Bayes classifier trained on the Greengenes 99% OTUs 16S rRNA genes reference database (v13.8). Bacterial cell density. Biofilms were stained with the LIVE/DEAD® cell viability assays (Invitrogen), according to the manufacturer’s protocol, and subsequently counted from five randomly chosen fields of view using an epifluorescence microscope at a magnification of 1000×. Six Petri dishes were sampled from each site. Larval settlement assay. Larval settlement assays were carried out on the same day when biofilms were collected from field. The DO and pH level of the control and treatment seawater was 6 mg O2 L-1/pH 8.1 and 1.5 mg O2 L-1/pH 7.6, respectively. For each biofilm and seawater combination, there were six polypropylene larval settlement experimental chambers (L× W × H: 150 × 90 × 45 mm). Approximately 150 larvae were carefully pipetted into each experimental chamber. After 24 h, the numbers of larvae that successfully settled on the biofilms were counted. Settled C. onyx have a significant reduction in velar lobes. Tops of the chambers were covered with nylon mesh (pore size: 150 µm), and all six chambers were placed in a large experimental tank (filled with 10 L natural seawater obtained from Port Shelter at 25 ˚C) on an orbital shaker rotating at 100 rpm. Desired levels of DO were achieved and maintained within ± 0.2 mg O2 L-1 by injecting seawater with air only, or together with nitrogen gas. The mean number of larva settled ranged from 44.50 to 55.17 and was not significantly affected by biofilm, seawater or their combination. The mean (±SD) bacterial cell density of biofilms developed at clean site and polluted site was 54.18 (14.57) and 55.88 (12.53) ×103 cells mm-1, respectively. The two means were not significantly different (p = 0.432). Nonetheless, the mean (±SD) percentage of live bacterial cell of biofilms developed at polluted site was 58.91 (4.88) and was significantly higher than the mean (±SD) of clean site, which was 45.38 (9.58) (p = 0.041). A total of 405,441 good quality sequences, subdivided into 193,639 sequences for control and 211,812 for HOA site were obtained after quality filtering. Samples were rarefied to 46,669 sequences to equalize the sampling depth across all samples. Sequences collapsed into a total of 5288 ASVs and 510 ASVs were shared among the two groups. Taxonomic classification of these ASVs showed the identification of 38 phyla, 88 classes, 154 orders and 237 families for the control condition, and 53 phyla, 125 classes, 209 orders and 318 families for the HOA condition. Comparison of phylogenetic diversity and Shannon biodiversity indices from different samples demonstrated that bacterial diversity were both higher in HOA (128.4 ± 18.5 and 9.5 ± 0.1) than control (95.6 ± 3.5 and 7.3 ± 0.05, respectively) environments (Kruskal-Wallis, p < 0.05. Higher species richness (Chao 1 and ACE richness estimators) was also observed in the samples exposed to hypoxia and reduced pH levels (2092.1 ± 530.1 and 2091.5 ± 531.1) than the control site (1387.2 ± 34.5 and 1384.3 ± 36.8, respectively) (Kruskal-Wallis, p < 0.05). These four indices suggest oxygen concentration and pH dependencies, in which biofilms developed at low DO and pH levels showed a higher alpha diversity and species richness than those developed at the control environment. Several taxa were also significantly different in abundance at class and order level. Hypoxia and ocean acidification reduced the abundance of Gammaproteobacteria (contributing to approximately 41% of the variation) and Verrucomicrobiae (2%), but increased Flavobacteriia (17%), Alphaproteobacteria (5%), Deltaproteobacteria (4%) and Epsilonproteobacteria (2%) (Wilcoxon, p < 0.05). At the order level, the relative abundance of Oceanospirillales (29.1%) and Alteromonadales (16.5%) was one-third the abundance in the control condition. Evidently, HAO caused a shift of dominance of Oceanospirillales and Alteromonadales to Rhodobacterales and Flavobacteriales, respectively. Some minor orders such as Rhizobiales, Vibrionales, Campylobacterales and Rickettsiales were more commonly recovered in the hypoxic with ocean acidification communities, whereas Phycisphaerales and Rhodospirillales were rarely observed in the polluted biofilms (Wilcoxon, p < 0.05).

22102015.label: Major findings and research outcome
22102015.value: Biofilm studies from a polluted fish farm with depleted dissolved oxygen and pH levels can elucidate the effects of future hypoxic and ocean pH shift on marine bacterial communities. Our results strongly support the hypothesis that the combined effects of hypoxia and seawater acidification altered the biofilm bacterial community diversity and composition. HOA dependent changes in diversity and composition were characterized by an increase in Flavobacteriales, Epsilonproteobacteria and Vibrionales, but less Oceanospirillales and Alteromonadales. In particular, five out of six ASVs closely affiliated with Photobacterium sp. and Vibrio sp. were demonstrated to be exclusively associated with the HOA condition, suggesting that depleted dissolved oxygen and pH levels could possibly proliferate the presence of these potential pathogens. Therefore, our study suggests the complexity of marine bacterial communities to hypoxia and CO2 levels, including changes associated with pollution and excess nutrient loads in our future oceans, as well as the identities of bacterial communities that are most likely affected. Crepidula onyx larvae were not affected by the oxygen availability and seawater pH during settlement. They also did not respond differently to biofilms originating from a HOA site compared to control biofilms from a clean site albeit these two types of biofilms harbored significantly different bacterial community composition. Our results are different from what was found for Balanus neritina larvae, which appeared to integrate cues from oxygen levels in the water and biofilm oxygenation history for habitat selection. The discrepancy may be explained by differential response among different species to biofilms. Nevertheless, hypoxia may alter species composition and community structure of marine invertebrates as a result of species-specific response.

22102015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22102015.value: The co-occurrence of hypoxia and acidification in seawater within aquaculture farms mimic eutrophication for future ocean conditions. To test whether bacterial communities are affected by hypoxia and ocean acidification (HOA), we examined the diversity and composition of biofilm bacterial communities from a polluted fish farm with low dissolved oxygen and pH levels using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. HOA was accompanied by higher bacterial diversity and richness, and resulted in a different community composition than the control site. HOA resulted in more Flavobacteriales, Epsilonproteobacteria and Vibrionales, but less Oceanospirillales and Alteromonadales. Photobacterium sp. and Vibrio sp. were mostly found to be exclusive to HOA conditions. Our study suggests the complexity of marine bacterial communities to HOA in response to eutrophication, as well as the identities of bacterial groups that are most likely affected in the predicted future. Furthermore, little is known about the effects of acidification and hypoxia on biofilms and larval settlement. So biofilms were tested for larval settlement response in the gastropod species Crepidula onyx under control, hypoxic and acidified water. Our results showed that C. onyx larvae were not affected by oxygen availability and pH in the water during settlement. They also did not respond differently to biofilms.

22200515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22200515.value: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a natural phenomenon developed in microorganisms, and is accelerated by misuse of antibiotics. AMR makes the treatment difficult, costly, or even impossible, thus is causing major health threat as well as enormous financial loss worldwide. Hong Kong also faces serious issues of AMR. Two strategies are effective in addressing AMR issue: (1) use narrow-spectrum antibiotics based on accurate diagnosis, preferentially, using antimicrobial susceptibility test (AST); (2) develop new antibiotics. However, both strategies are challenged by the lack of effective and affordable method to test the response of target microorganisms to drug administration. An AST involves a large number of tests, especially when the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of each drug is desired. Current ASTs are based on observing cell-growth, which is costly, time-consuming, and incapable of dealing with fastidious microorganisms. Similar challenge exists in the drug development which requires large-scale screening. Tremendous efforts have been made to improve AST technology; however, those new strategies, based on PCR, nanoparticles, or dielectrophoresis, are still impractical to be used for real specimens. Herein we propose a microfluidic platform which could have major contribution to addressing the aforementioned challenges. We are developing a fundamentally new strategy to detect the response of microorganisms to drug treatment, using single-cell-level evidences such as morphological and surface-chemical changes, which arise way before the change of cell population could be detected at macro scale using conventional method. Not relying on proliferation, this method also facilitates study of fastidious organisms and “hard-to-detect” resistance mechanisms. The device will be made of a new material, Teflon, which addresses two major challenges in drug-loaded on-chip culture. Also, the system supports high-throughput operation without massive manipulation such as pipetting, thereby improving the reliability of the assay. Moreover, a special detection scheme will realize fully-automatic data-acquisition without sophisticated instrument (such as microscope) or technician labor; this will help release the system to real market. Through this project, we expect an inexpensive, user-friendly but quick and reliable method to benefit the control of AMR. As our method is designed to allow maximum accessibility, the broad range of clinics currently could not afford AST would be able to conduct routine test. At the mean time, the unique platform will allow us to obtain important new knowledge about the mechanism of AMR development. Finally, the platform could be implemented to drug discovery and other applications where similar tool is sought for. 在治療過程中致病微生物會天然地對藥物逐漸產生耐藥性，但這一過程會因廣譜抗生素的濫用大大加快。微生物的耐藥性使得已有的藥物失效，造成疾病的治療變得愈加困難和昂貴，甚至令人們對某些疾病變得束手無策。這給全世界帶來了嚴重的健康隱患和巨大的經濟損失，而這種形勢在中國尤為嚴峻。 解決微生物耐藥性問題有兩個可能的有效方法：（1）在精確診斷的基礎上，使用有針對性的窄譜抗生素，最好是通過藥敏試驗選擇最適合的藥物；（2）及時開發新的抗生素。然而，目前檢測藥物對致病微生物的效果缺乏經濟有效的手段，因而大大限制了以上兩個方法的實用性。例如藥敏試驗是選擇藥物及其劑量的最可靠手段，然而一組藥敏試驗涉及大量測量點，而目前的藥敏試驗是基於對細胞增殖的觀測，其中細胞培養是一項費時費力、相對昂貴的工作。研究者試圖發展新的藥敏試驗方法，提出了基於基因分析或納米科學的新方法，然而，這些方法目前尚有明顯缺陷難以用於日常常規檢測。 為了解決微生物耐藥性的問題，我們在此提出一個基於創新的微流控技術的研究思路。通過在特製晶片上進行細胞培養，和用微流控技術對細胞進行計數，更快地檢測到致病微生物對藥物的反應。我們的晶片由具超強抗汙性能的全氟化合物製成，以解決微流通道被沾汙帶來的各種問題；另外，設備支援高通量檢測和操作，大大減少人工作業及由此帶來的不確定性。此外，對晶片的特殊設計使得細胞培養通道具有天然濃縮功能，進一步加快檢測速度。 通過這一項目，我們希望獲得一套經濟、便捷和可靠的方法，有助於有效控制微生物抗藥性。我們這一方法的初衷就是希望此方法能夠在廣大普通醫療機構普及，因此預計目前能夠進行常規藥敏試驗（AST）的醫療機構都可以運用本專案開發的方法進行常規測試/檢查。同時，這一套獨特的檢測平臺可以幫助我們獲得關於抗藥性及其發展過程的寶貴資料/知識。此外，這一平臺還可用于藥物開發等其他更廣闊的領域。

22200515.label: Realisation of objectives
22200515.value: We have designed and fabricated Teflon microfluidic devices that allow precise and reliable control of drug concentration in the microchannels for culturing bacterium cells (Objective 1). We have also developed a microfluidic technology for detecting effects of drug treatment using changes of cells at a microscopic scale, such as the morphology and hydrodynamic property, to realize the detection of cell response at a much earlier stage than conventional bulk culture-based methods (Objective 2). Meanwhile, we are developing an inexpensive method for detecting bacterium cells in a sample for convenient sample analysis, which could potentially be used for a food safety test, environmental and public security screening (Objective 3). On the other hand, we have also integrated the new technologies that we have achieved in the objective 1, 2 and 3, and developed a fully automatic, high-throughput and low-cost method for AST test (Objective 4). With the use of our AST devices, the turnaround time has been significantly reduced from tens of hours to a couple of hours, where the cost was also reduced by 90%. Finally, we have also accomplished promising achievements in objective 5. The mechanisms and phenomenon of the synergistic inhibition effect of two different antibiotics have been studied with the help of a two-dimensional AST platform (Objective 5). Microfluidics is an innovative and expanding field of research involving multiple disciplines in science and engineering. In this project, we are using microfluidics to develop novel AST tools to combact AMR (Trends in biotechnology, 2017). Firstly, we have developed a convenient yet powerful method to fabricate monolithic polypropylene (PP) microfluidic chips; our article “Reliable and Reusable Whole Polypropylene Plastic Microfluidic Devices for a Rapid, Low-cost Antimicrobial Susceptibility Test” has been published in Lab Chip. Although polypropylene (PP) has been used as an alternative to the Teflon material in the manuscript due to the cost consideration for commercialization, we indeed have designed and fabricated a Teflon microfluidic device in the meantime during this work for comparision. We have published the related techniques for 3D microfabriction of Teflon and other thermalplastic materials in PNAS (2020) and Microphysiological Systems (2018), which are useful for the fabrication of plastic microfluidic chips for on-chip AST. In brief, the microfluidic AST platform in this study contains two functional parts: a concentration gradient generator (CCG) and cell culture chambers. The Christmas tree structure of the CCG is used to generate a concentration gradient of the antibiotic, and the deepened chambers in the downstream are used for bacteria culturing (Objective 1). There are three inlets on the AST chip, for media-doped antibiotic, media, and cell seeding, respectively. For the CCG, when two solutions are injected into a device through inlet 1 (culture media only) and inlet 2 (culture media containing antibiotics), the two solutions split at the nodes, combine with neighboring streams in a laminar fashion, and mixe in the zigzag channels. By this means, eight concentrations are generated at the end of the CCG. As the bacterial cells inside the samples were generally dispersed in a flowing fluid (e.g., buffered solution, urine, and blood) during the antimicrobial susceptibility test, studying the dynamics of bacterial adhesion under this condition is particularly relevant (Objective 2). As known, the fluid velocity gradient in small dimensions associated with micrometer-sized chambers is relatively high, so that large shear stress is generated. This is an important issue for both the attachment and detachment of bacteria because the bacterial adhesion is significantly affected by shear force. In this connection, it also affects the results of AST on a microfluidic platform. In order to minimize the effects of shear force while maintaining the best efficiency of tests, we designed stepwise deepened chambers in our AST chip. Different sizes of deepened chambers were designed, and computational fluid dynamics simulations were employed to investigate the hydrodynamic consequences in the microfluidic chip. The condition of the deepened chambers was simulated, the optimum design for the deepened chambers have been chosen to minimize the influence of shear force. As the majority of novel clinical AST methods realized so far have a variety of drawbacks when used for such environmental surveys, e.g., high cost, dependence on microscopic analysis, and required use of expensive instrumentation. In order to realize onsite screening for the massive environmental samples, we have then developed a resource-independent and cost-efficient AST method that can rapidly do so for a large number of samples (Objective 3). Our “barcode” cell sensor was based on an adaptive linear filter array as a fully automatic and microscope-free method for counting tiny volumes of cells, wherein suspended cells concentrate into microbars through the filtration effect of nanochannels at the channel sides. As the length of the accumulated bacteria bar is proportional to the number of the bacteria in the suspension, the point with the most significant slope is therefore determined as the MIC value. In the meantime, we have integrated the new technologies we developed in objectives 1, 2 and 3. By combining the microfluidic cell culture zone we have developed in the objectives 1 and 2 for exposing bacteria to the tested drug and also the “barcode” cell sensor zone that we have developed in objective 3 for microscope-free cell counting; herein, we have developed a fully automatic, high-throughput and low-cost system for the AST test (Objective 4). With the use of our AST system, the turnaround time can be significantly reduced from tens of hours to a couple of hours, where the cost will also reduce by 90%. We have combined the cell sensor with an on-chip culture that takes much less time than standard AST methods, thereby realizing a low-cost and high-throughput platform for portable AST, from which results can be obtained through a cell phone. In simple words, a cell phone can be used to image the “barcode” and generate analysis results of relative densities of different bars, which provides the information of the MIC value of tested drugs against the tested sample. In this way, microscope-free fast counting of a small number of bacteria is realized, and thus an easy-accessible portable rapid AST is realized (Objective 4). Besides, we also investigated another way to perform AST on-chip. We designed and fabricated two-layer hydrogel chips for standard and two-dimensional AST, which relies on the continuous linear gradients of drugs. This gradient pattern was generated by the diffusion between two parallel microchannels. Meanwhile, bacteria cells were cultured on the top of the device, which avoids shear force brought by channel-culture microfluidic methods and mimic the in vivo environment better than existing microfluidic ASTs. Furthermore, the tested cell sample in cells-on-top AST can be easily gathered after drug treatment and analyzed by downstream analysis on the molecular level with other techniques. Coupled with optic information, the molecular analysis could bring us new knowledge of resistance mechanisms based on the synergistic effect of multiple factors (Objective 5). Our articles “Cell-on-Hydrogel Platform Made of Agar and Alginate for Rapid, Low-cost, Multidimensional Test of Antimicrobial Susceptibility” and “A Multiplexed, Gradient‐Based, Full‐Hydrogel Microfluidic Platform for Rapid, High‐Throughput Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing” were published in Lab Chip and ChemPlusChem respectively.

22200515.label: Major findings and research outcome
22200515.value: During the study of this project, we have developed different alternative strategies to current antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) methods in order to realize a rapid, low-cost, reliable, resource-independent and also high-throughput AST. Research articles have been published for the novel microfluidic AST platforms we developed as well as the novel device fabrication techniques. The article “Cell-on-Hydrogel Platform Made of Agar and Alginate for Rapid, Low-cost, Multidimensional Test of Antimicrobial Susceptibility” was featured in the “emerging investigators” special issue of Lab Chip. This work describes a novel method that cultures cells on a microfluidic drug gradient device combined with conventional plate culture, which could perform rapid, low-cost AST within a few hours, largely accelerated the process as compared to current culture-based methods. The article “A One-Step Strategy for Ultra-Fast and Low-Cost Mass Production of Plastic Membrane Microfluidic Chips” was featured on the front outside cover page of Lab Chip. This work describes a method to produce disposable testing microfluidic devices rapidly (~12 seconds/piece) at extremely low cost (< $0.02 per piece) using plastic membranes, which can be used as an alternative strategy to provide the commercial devcies for antimicrobial susceptibility tests. The article “Reliable and Reusable Whole Polypropylene Plastic Microfluidic Devices for a Rapid, Low-cost Antimicrobial Susceptibility Test” was published in the Lab Chip. This work describes a convenient yet powerful method to fabricate monolithic polypropylene (PP) microfluidic chips; meanwhile, it demonstrated a whole PP chip for a rapid, low-cost, and accurate test of antimicrobial susceptibility. Our system allows for reliable tracking of individual cells and acquisition of AST results within 1–3 hours, which is among the group of fastest phenotypic methods. The work “Rapid, Convenient, and Resource-independent Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing with a “Barcode” Cell Sensor” is to be submitted soon. This work describes a “barcode” cell sensor, which is a rapid, high throughput, and resource and skill independent, onsite AST tool. As a cost-efficient screening tool, our platform can quickly detect any suspected drug-resistance bacteria in environmental samples within 2 to 3 hours. Besides, we also investigated other types of devices for drug efficacy tests and cell-on-chip assays. For example, we published a method to create a 3D diffusion system for cell culture and on-chip assays (Biomicrofluidics, 2016 and Analyst, 2019). All these methods are related to our cell-on-chip AST and have the potential to be implemented in future for quick, low cost, and multifunctional analysis.

22200515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22200515.value: Through this project, we have investigated different alternative strategies to realize an inexpensive, user-friendly but quick and reliable AST tool to benefit the control of antimicrobial resistance(AMR). Our research has clear potential in producing patent and commercialization; and based on its healthcare implementation, subsequent funding support from RGC, NSFC, ITS, etc. have been obtained. Our AST platforms are designed to allow maximum accessibility; thus, with the use of our platforms, broad range of clinics would be able to conduct routine AST. At the same time, the unique platform of this work will help obtain crucial new knowledge about the mechanism of AMR development. Finally, the platform could be directly implemented to drug discovery and other applications where a fast, cost-efficient, high-throughput method for studying the response of microorganisms upon drug administration is sought for. For the future development, we will continue our endeavors to promote the commercialization for our AST platform. In 2019, we established a research collaboration partnership with the Research Institute of Tsinghua, Pearl River Delta to facilitate the commercialization for the Cell-on-Hydrogel AST Platform. .

A similar challenge exists in drug development and also the monitoring of environmental samples which requires large-scale screening. The microfluidic AST platforms we developed can realize a rapid, low-cost, reliable, resource-independent and high-throughput AST which could make a significant contribution to address the aforementioned challenges. Our AST platforms can be implemented to drug discovery; meanwhile, allow us to explore and obtain crucial new knowledge about the mechanism of AMR development. Thus, our AST platforms are expected to become an effective weapon in the fight against AMR.

22300115.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22300115.value: 關於最優控制問題的並行算法

22300115.label: Project Objectives
22300115.value: Design, develop and analyze a new class of parallel optimal control solvers based on a time-domain decomposition and optimized transmission conditions. Establish new results in the theory of domain decomposition methods when the equations are of the optimal control type. Establish new results in the theory of domain decomposition methods when the equations are of the optimal control type.
