22300115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22300115.value: For this project, we will design and develop efficient parallel algorithms for the numerical solution of optimal control problems under partial differential equation (PDE) constraints. In this class of problems, we are given a mechanical or biological system governed by a PDE, and the goal is to find the forcing function with minimal cost that drives the system to the desired target state. The numerical solution of such problems has become an active area of research in the past decade with a growing list of applications, such as the control of fluid flow governed by the Navier-Stokes equations, quantum control and medical applications related to the optimization of radiotherapy administration. When the constraints are PDEs, standard algorithms for optimal control require the solution of very large systems of linear or nonlinear equations, where the number of degrees of freedom can be in the millions or even billions. The extreme storage and computational requirements impel us to consider distributed computing solutions. We propose to follow the domain decomposition paradigm: we divide the time horizon into subintervals to obtain problems that are small enough to be solved on a single processor. We then assign these smaller problems to separate processors within a large computing cluster, where they are solved in parallel. A consistent global solution is then obtained by iteration. The novelty in our approach lies in the use of optimized transmission conditions for communication between time intervals. Based on our experience with elliptic problems, where the use of Robin data greatly speeds up the convergence of Schwarz methods, we propose to use a linear combination of state and adjoint variables as interface data for optimal control problems. Preliminary results show that a judicious choice of the Robin parameter leads to significant improvement in the convergence of the method. On the theoretical front, we will establish convergence results for the new method when the PDE is parabolic, paying special attention to the case where the spatial differential operator is non-symmetric, e.g. for the advection-diffusion equation. We will also design a coarse grid correction to make the algorithm scalable when the number of subdomains is large. On the experimental front, we will test our algorithms on parabolic and other types of problems, such as the Stokes equation and nonlinear diffusion problems, in order to confirm our theoretical results and to assess the applicability and efficiency of our method on problems not covered by our analysis. 在本研究項目中，我們將設計出一套可靠及高效的並行算法來解答關於最優控制的問題。最優控制其實在機械工程的領域已經有很廣泛的應用，但是以往都是用在比較簡單的系統上，比如常微分方程系統。近十幾年裏，隨著多核計算機與集群計算的興起，最優控制開始應用在偏微分方程系統上，而且應用範圍擴展到生物學和醫學方面。然而，傳統的算法不能夠充分利用多核計算機的計算資源，對於這些大型而複雜的偏微分方程系統而言，幫助有限。本項目針對關於最優控制的並行算法的實際需要，以區域分解算法的技巧，設計出一套可以用在大型集群計算機上的新並行算法。基本原理是把整個控制問題在時間維上分拆成多個較小型的子問題，在集群計算機上把多個子問題同步求解，再以迭代的方式逐步逼近問題的精確解。在不同的子區域之間，我們將採用Optimized Schwarz 傳輸條件和粗網格算法來優化算法的收斂速度和可擴性。我們將從理論角度分析新算法的收斂性，以及不同參數對收斂性的影響，例如網格大小，子域數量，方程參數等等。新算法將應用於綫性和非綫性抛物型偏微分方程，以及移動擴散方程與 Navier-Stokes 方程上，務求測試新算法的實際性能。

22300115.label: Realisation of objectives
22300115.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved by developing new time-domain decomposition methods for solving optimal control problems, and by building new analytical tools to analyze the convergence of such methods. For objective 1, two classes of methods have been designed and proposed in Outputs #1 and #4, respectively. Both methods require the solution of subdomain problems, i.e., smaller versions of the optimal control problems posed on a shorter time horizon. The efficient solution of such problems are described in Outputs #2, #3 and #5. For objective 2, new theoretical results have been developed in Outputs #4 and #6 in order to quantify the convergence rates of the resulting methods. For objective 3, we note that the method proposed in Output #4 naturally contains a coarse grid and is proven to be scalable with the number of time subdomains, so this objective is achieved. Finally, for Objective 4, our methods have been tested and shown to be effective on a variety of problems of practical interest in Outputs #1, #2, #4-6, including the advection-diffusion equation, non-linear diffusion problems and the Forchheimer problem.

22300115.label: Major findings and research outcome
22300115.value: In Output #1, we proposed a new time-domain decomposition method for the solution of optimal control problems, where the time subdomains communicate using optimized transmission conditions, which are defined to be a linear combination of the state and adjoint variables. We use an energy estimate approach to show that for the two-subdomain case, a good choice of Robin parameter leads to accelerated convergence of the method, compared to transmitting state variables only. This method is further analyzed in Output #6, where the method is analyzed for multiple subdomains and for cases where the control is only applied to a subset of the spatial domain. It is shown that the method converges much faster than for Dirichlet transmission conditions, but the contraction rate deteriorates as the number of subdomain increases. This is universal among all methods with no coarse grid correction. In Output #4, we designed a different method that contains a global problem to solve. This coarse problem is solved using an inexact Newton method, where the inexactness comes from approximating the subdomain problems with a coarser discretization. The resulting method works for both linear and nonlinear problems, and the linear diffusive case is analyzed comprehensively. It shows that the contraction rate is independent of the number of time subdomains, which is the goal of Objective #3. In each of the above two methods, the subdomain problems must still be solved using an efficient method. This is the purpose of Outputs #2-3 and #5-6. In #2, we analyze a parallel-in-time method called MGRIT, and showed that it is equivalent to an overlapping variant of parareal, another parallel-in-time method. This allows us to prove the convergence of MGRIT for a much wider class of problems. Outputs #3 and #5 propose new methods for the efficient solution of elliptic problems, which form the workhorse of any subdomain solver. Output #3 concerns a simple optimal control problem solved by the Dirichlet-Neumann and Neumann-Neumann methods. Here we showed that for suitable choices of relaxation parameters, both methods converge in a finite number of iterations, so they are in fact direct solvers. In #5, we derive a new quadratically convergent method for nonlinear diffusive problems based on nonlinear domain decomposition-based preconditioning. This provides an efficient subroutine for solving the subdomain problems, where many elliptic problems must be solved.

22300115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22300115.value: One really important question for future investigation is the performance of the methods in the presence of control constraints. Since this is equivalent to eliminating some degrees of freedom in the control, and since we have already handled the case of control over a subset, similar techniques should be able to handle the case of control constraints adequately. A second important future direction is the application of such time parallel methods on data assimilation problems, which can be formulated as an optimization problem under PDE constraints, just like an optimal control problem. Such efforts are already ongoing, with a collaboration with the French institute INRIA-Paris on this topic.

22300115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22300115.value: In many applications in science and engineering, one would like to control the input of a physical system (e.g. energy, external force, speed of the motor etc.) to steer the system to a desired state, or as close to it as possible, within a particular time horizon. The computation of such an "optimal" input can be laborious and time consuming. In this project, we have proposed two methods for solving such problems when we have a lot of computing power, but distributed over many processors. The key is to divide the time horizon into smaller chunks, so that a single processor can handle a different chunk and work in parallel. These processors must then exchange their results until a consistent solution is found. We have shown how to estimate the number of exchanges necessary to obtain a solution of sufficient accuracy. We have applied our methods to problems of practical interest, particularly those that model fluid flow, and showed the effectiveness of the methods.

22301615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22301615.value: The dimeric viral oncoprotein, Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1), is known to be responsible for the development of EBV (Epstein-Barr virus)-related malignancies and the maintenance of EBV episome. Given that carcinogenesis of EBV-associated carcinoma is symbiotically connected with EBV infection and EBNA1 can function (e.g. replication, DNA binding and transactivation) only upon dimerization (formation of the active form), recent studies (including our related findings) have demonstrated that a fluorescent probe consisting of a chromophore and an EBNA1-specific molecule which hampers the dimer formation can be exploited for the imaging and inhibition of latent EBV-infected cells simultaneously. However, these studies with small organic molecules are only available in cytoplasm with limited responsive signal changes, board emissions, short lifetimes and low signal-to-noise ratios; practically unachievable also is the real-time function evaluation of EBNA1 using peptides on their own. In this project, we would like to provide a novel strategy with lanthanide luminescence to study (image) the regulation of EBNA1 dimizerimation and interfere the growth of EBV-associated tumor cells. Long emission lifetime with time-resolved microsopy had already illustrated such advantages on improving the signal-to-noise ratio for molecular imaging. As justified by our recent publications on responsive luminescent lanthanide materials towards various biological tasks in solution/in vitro/in vivo, our research team has thorough experience in lanthanide coordination chemistry, spectroscopy, peptide chemistry, and in vitro biological applications. Therefore, we aim to develop luminescent EBNA1-specific lanthanide bio-probes with high selectivity towards EBNA1 and capability of handicapping the dimerization for in vitro imaging and inhibition of EBNA1 as anti-EBV-related carcinoma agents. To further support our work here, we had performed a string of proof-of-concept experiments to consolidate our hypotheses: (1) several EBNA1-specific europium complexes with tailor-made synthetic peptides had been prepared which can be excited in the visible, even in near-infrared, region, to give responsive fingerprint europium emission to EBNA1; (2) strong binding and high selecticity twoward EBNA1; and (3) they are cell-permeable with different subcellular localizations for EBNA1 in vitro imaging and inhibition. This proposal will pave the way for the development of new-generation responsive lanthanide complexes conjugated with organic chromophores and EBNA1-specific peptides as dual probes with both imaging and anti-tumor properties. Making a success of this research can bring to society a more powerful tool (especially able to combine multi-photon and time-resolved technology) to unveil the mystery and understand the very roles of EBNA1 in EBV-associated carcinoma for further cancer diagnosis, therapy, and research. EBNA1是EBV潛伏感染時編碼的一種同源二聚蛋白，是唯一在EBV相關惡性腫瘤中均有表達的病毒致癌蛋白，它能使EBV以附加體的形式穩定存在於被感染的細胞內。所有EBV相關性腫瘤的發生都始於EBV的感染，並且EBNA1的功能化，包括啓動EB病毒DNA的複制，與DNA結合以及其他EB病毒潛伏蛋白的轉錄啟動等，都是以形成二聚體爲前提（已知二聚體是EBNA1的生物活性形式）。基於此，已有研究（涵蓋我們最近的工作）證實，熒光分子與EBNA1特異性多肽的結合，可形成一類兼具活體成像以及抑制EBV潛在感染細胞功能的特異性熒光探針。然而，這些已開發出的熒光探針只能進入到細胞質中，並且它們與EBNA1的結合僅能産生微弱的熒光響應信號，寬泛的譜帶，短壽命的熒光以及相對較低的信噪比，因而極難分辨；更重要的是，這種EBNA1截取物衍生出的多肽難以肩負對自身實時評估這一使命。 在本項目中，我們有望採用一種新穎的方法，即利用鑭系螢光探針，更為精細的回饋出它們對EBNA1二聚過程的調控機制甚至是對EBV相關性腫瘤的抑制過程。長壽命螢光光譜結合時間分辨光譜技術已經在分子成像領域展現出了極大的應用優勢，如對信噪比的顯著提高，這一優勢也被我們近期報導出的一系列響應性鑭系螢光材料的體內外應用所證實。我們的研究團隊具有豐富的鑭系配位元化學，光譜學，多肽化學以及體內外生物應用方面的經驗。基於此，我們志在開發出EBNA1高選擇性鑭系螢光生物探針，實現活體成像以及有效抑制EBNA1的雙目標，成為對EBV相關性腫瘤具有實際應用價值的抗癌試劑，並期望能進一步揭開EBNA1二聚甚至是EBV相關性腫瘤發生的神秘面紗。 為了進一步支援上述研究目標，我們展開了一系列概念驗證試驗：（1）我們合成出了多款含有EBNA1特異性多肽的銪配合物。在可見甚至是近紅外區域的光波激發下，配合物與EBNA1的結合能產生響應性銪指紋發射峰；（2）配合物對EBNA1展示出了強結合以及高選擇性等優勢；並且（3）這些具備細胞通透性的配合物在EBNA1的成像和抑制作用研究中呈現出了各異的亞細胞定位效果。本方案為開發回應性鑭系螢光配合物作為EBNA1特異性雙功能探針（成像和抑制）奠定了基石。

22301615.label: Realisation of objectives
22301615.value: For objective 1, more than twenty lanthanide complexes conjugated with EBNA1 specific peptides, (lanthanide = europium and gadolinium) have been synthesised. These complexes are able to identify EBV positive cancer cells via targeting EBNA1 in vitro. Foe objective 2, six europium complexes have been chosen from objective 1. These complexes have low toxicity in dark (IC50 value > 0.1 mM) and can be activated by a non-toxic excitation in near-infrared region. Those complexes show strong lanthanide emission after the photo-released of anti-cancer agents from lanthanide complexes. The synthetic methods for those five complexes are optimized with good yield. For objective 3, non-responsive emission enhancement is the disadvantage of upconversion nanomaterials (UCNM) when compared with conventional organic based agents for molecular imaging. We herein show a new strategy by conjugating NaGdF4:Yb3+,Er3+@NaGdF4 (UCNP) with peptides to achieve responsive UC emission enhancement upon binding to a targeted protein – EBNA1. EBNA1 is a well-known viral latent protein for the EBV-associated cancer. Peptide-coating of the functionalized core–shell nanoparticle diminishes upconverted emission intensity drastically. 22301615.label: Major findings and research outcome
22301615.value: In this project, we have shown a responsive lanthanide emission enhancement for in vitro imaging: peptide functionalized upconversion nanoparticles and complexes were synthesized and targeted the EBV latency-essential protein – EBNA1. The responsive lanthanide emission is only achieved upon the binding with EBNA1 in aqueous/in vitro conditions, and this is a rare example a responsive enhancement signal for a real application, especially in cancer therapy. This study offers a simple aggregation method (with optimization required for future studies) by using peptide molecules to link with lanthanide emission, in order to obtain stronger signaling for imaging and to be more specific for tumor suppression. This study has opened up a new window for the biomedical application of lanthanide emission by taking advantage of its merits (e.g. no photobleaching) and is especially important for the anti-cancer drug and tumor imaging agent design.

22301615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22301615.value: In the past decades, EBV has drawn attention due to its substantial contribution in the development of several lymphoid and epithelial malignancies. The crucial and unique roles of EBNA1 in maintaining EBV infection make it an attractive target for therapeutic intervention of EBV-associated cancers. Efforts from the past decade in the design or identification of EBNA1 inhibitors have shown some progress on several fronts. It is important to acknowledge that current EBNA1-targeted inhibitors are far from perfect and not ready for the clinic. Multidisciplinary efforts are required for designing structurally-relevant EBNA1-targeted inhibitors. In this respect, co-immunoprecipitation experiments and X-ray crystallography analysis could provide critical information on the structure of EBNA1 inhibitor complex. Similarly, molecular dynamics simulations as well as docking studies might afford valuable insights. Although L2P4 from this project has been observed in tumor sections by imaging studies, monitoring the whole human body would be more difficult. It would be worthwhile to employ real-time and deep-penetrating imaging modalities, such as PET imaging and magnetic resonance imaging, to gain a better understanding of the functions of EBNA1-targeted inhibitors.

22301615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22301615.value: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects more than 90% of human worldwide and establishes lifelong latent infection in the hosts. It closely associates with endemic forms of a wide range of human cancers and directly contributes to the formation of some. Despite its critical role in cancer development, no EBV- or EBV latent protein-targeted therapy is available. The EBV-encoded latent protein, EBNA1 (Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1), is expressed in all EBV-associated tumors and acts as the only latent protein in some of these tumors. This versatile protein functions in the maintenance, replication and segregation of EBV genome, which in turn established itself as an attractive therapeutic target. In the last decades, efforts have been made for the design of specific EBNA1 inhibitors including decreasing EBNA1 expression or interfering with EBNA1-dependent functions, which also reflected that EBNA1 is the key to treat EBV-associated cancers. In this project, we developed several EBNA1 inhibitors related to different EBNA1 domains and shown the selectively in EBV cancer with very low and safe dosage amount. (4 milli gram/kg) in mice models.

22302815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22302815.value: 人类基因组计划以及人类遗传变异图谱在二十一世纪初宣告完成。这一里程碑式的事件拉开大规模利用生物医疗数据研究复杂人类疾病的序幕。伴随着生物科技的革新与信息化进程，生物医疗的大数据时代已经悄然来临。迄今为止，全世界的研究者已经积累了全方位、多层次的生物医疗数据。这些数据覆盖了从遗传变异到生命体表征的各个层面，包括基因组层面、表观基因组层面、转录组层面、蛋白质层面、代谢组层面。传统的致病机理研究往往限制在研究某一个层面与疾病的关系，而大数据时代的到来使我们能够集成多个层面的信息，更好地实现从遗传变异到疾病发生的整个因果链的全方位解析，从而为个性化的、精准的医疗服务奠定科学基础。本课题致力于统计与计算方法的开发，以服务于多层面的数据集成分析，并期望本课题的统计与计算方法研究能够为更多的大数据分析领域提供新的思路。

22302815.label: Realisation of objectives
22302815.value: The whole project goes quite smoothly. In the following, we will state how we achieved all the objectives 100%. The reference number is indexed according to the references listed Part C. 1. Develop statistical models We have developed several statistical models to prioritize risk genetic variants and improve risk prediction of complex diseases. These models include, EPS [4], LLR [10], LSMM [11], IGESS [9], and LEP [12]. As we showed in the proposal, the key to the success of these models relies on two scientific facts: First, genetic variants in human genome are not equally important for a certain type of traits or diseases. For example, genetic variants with functional role in Brain may be more likely associated with psychiatric disorders (e.g., Schizophrenia) or neurological disorders (e.g., Alzheimer’s disease). This offers the opportunity to prioritize risk genetic variants. Second, complex traits often have a shared genetic component, i.e., they are genetically correlated. For example, auto-immune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and Crohn’s disease are known to have shared genetic pathways. By leveraging genetic correlation among multiple traits/diseases, the accuracy of risk prediction can be greatly improved. Technically, the most challenging issue of combining multiple GWAS data sets of different traits/diseases is heterogeneity. In other words, complex traits can be genetically correlated but the effect sizes of risk variants are not exactly the same. For example, a genetic variant can affect rheumatoid arthritis but not affect Crohn’s disease, although these two diseases are strongly genetically correlated. Our developed methods allow such a heterogeneity by model the probability P(G affects disease B | G affects disease A), where G is the genetic variant, A and B are the types of diseases. There is a similar scenario when considering functional annotations. A genetic variant with a functional role in Brain does not imply it must affect a psychiatric disorder (say schizophrenia), but rather increasing the chance that it may be associated with schizophrenia). Again, this is not a deterministic relationship. Therefore, we proposed probabilistic models to handle this. 2. Develop efficient algorithms for adaptive model parameter estimation We have developed efficient algorithms to estimate model parameter in an adaptive manner. In particular, we have developed expectation-maximization (EM) algorithms and variational EM algorithms to different models. For example, to allow LSMM [11] scalable to millions of variants and hundreds of functional annotations, we developed an efficient variational expectation-maximization algorithm for model parameter estimation and statistical inference. In particular, we explored warm-start in algorithm design, such that parameter estimation is not sensitive to initialization. We have also shown that the developed algorithm can handle a very large-scale of genotype matrix, comprised of millions of genotyped variants from tens of thousands of individuals. As tested on a personal computer with 2.2 GHz Intel Core i7 and 32GM memory, the developed algorithms (e.g., IGESS [9] and LEP [12]) are able to handle a genotype matrix with two million of variants from ten thousand individuals in about 400 seconds for one iteration. The algorithms are theoretically guaranteed to converge. In practice, we have observed the algorithms can often converge in a few hundred iterations. 3. Evaluate model performance using comprehensive simulation study and examine the robustness in the presence of model misspecification. For our developed models, we have always evaluated their performance using extensive simulation studies, in terms of the accuracy of parameter estimation, statistical power, type I error rate, false discovery rate and prediction accuracy. We have also emphasized the robustness in presence of model misspecification. Therefore, in simulation study, we designed experiment to check whether the model performance is reasonably good if the model is mis-specified. In such a scenario, we have observed that the models may slightly degrade from their optimal performance but still maintain their advantages over their competitors. Besides the experimental study, we also investigate model misspecification problem from theoretical point of view. In the community of human genetics, linear-mixed models (LMM) are used to estimate heritability, the phenotypic variance explained by genetic factors. In statistics, this can be cast as variance estimation in high dimensional regression. Note that there could be only a fraction of genetic variants (i.e., variables in regression) associated with the phenotype (response vector). Directly application of LMM to estimate the variance explained by all variants may be questionable. This is because too many noise variables are involved and LMM is misspecified. Surprisingly, in our simulation study, we observed that Restricted Maximum Likelihood (REML) estimator of the misspecified LMM works very well no matter the underlying true model is sparse or dense. Recently, we have shown that REML estimator in the misspecified LMM is still consistent under some regular conditions. Therefore, LMM can have a big advantage over its competitors (e.g., refitted cross-validation and scaled-Lasso only work well for sparse cases) for variance estimation in high dimensional regression. Our theory opens a door to variance estimation in high dimensional regression and it can be used in post-selection inference where the estimation of residual variance plays an important role. This new result has been published in the Annals of Statistics. 4 Apply the proposed methods in real data analysis to generate new biological understanding of complex diseases. We applied the proposed methods to analyze GWAS of complex phenotypes by incorporating hundreds cell-type specific functional annotations. For example, we detect the functional annotation in liver to be relevant to the lipid-related phenotypes, including low-density lipoprotein, high-density lipoprotein, triglycerides and total cholesterol (Global Lipids Genetics Consortium, 2013). For height, >40 cell-type specific functional annotations are detected to be relevant, which reflects its highly polygenic genetic architecture. These relevant annotations include cells in bone, vascular and skeletal muscle which were also shown significant enrichments for height. Recent research has linked some neurodegenerative diseases, which were believed to be more related to brain and neural system, to the immune system, such as Alzheimer’s disease and Parkinson’s disease. 5 Develop a user-friendly software. For each developed method, we have provided a computationally efficient R or Matlab packages for users with user-friendly vignettes. IGESS: https://github.com/eeyangc/IGESS LSMM: https://github.com/eeyangc/LSMM LEP: https://github.com/eeyangc/LEP LLR: https://github.com/eeyangc/LLR EPS: https://github.com/eeyangc/EPS The scale of the problem with 2M imputed SNPs and 10K individuals requires the package to be more efficient in memory storage and computation. It is well known that the 2M by 10K matrix stored in a double matrix needs 160G memory, it is not feasible to handle such a large matrix in most of personal computers. The standardization of each column is also needed. We addressed the above challenges by storing the individual-level data in a char-type matrix (the memory needed reduced to 20G around) or using bit representation with hash table, and keeping only the column means and column standard deviations to avoid saving the scaled genotype matrix (a 2M×10K matrix occupies about 160G memory). With this novel data structure, we are able to handle extremely large-scale genome data. About training PhD student, Ms. MING Jingsi was supported by this grant for her PhD study. The PI (Dr. Can Yang) was her PhD supervisor. As the PI moved from HKBU to HKUST in Sept., 2017, the supervisor was changed to Prof. Lixing ZHU. However, Ms. MING continued her research in this field with the supervision of the PI and obtained her PhD degree in August, 2018.

22302815.label: Major findings and research outcome
22302815.value: In the past decade, hundreds of genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have been conducted to study the genetic bases of complex human traits. Despite these successes, these results present many challenges for human geneticists and statisticians. First, about 85% of these GWAS-identified risk variants are in non-coding regions, which highlights the importance of non-coding variants in regulatory and other unknown functional elements in the human genome. It is critical to investigate the functional role of the identified risk variants and establish how they are associated with human diseases. Second, recent results from GWAS have shown the polygenic genetic architecture of complex traits: a complex trait is often affected by many genetic variants with small or moderate effects. To address the above challenges, we have developed statistical methods that integrate functional annotations of genetic variants and pleiotropy information among complex traits and diseases. 1.We prepared conventional genic category annotations as well as 127 cell-type specific functional annotations from the Roadmap project. We showed that, by incorporating functional annotations, the developed statistical methods not only increases the statistical power of identifying risk variants but also offer more biological insights by detecting relevant functional annotations [4, 11]. For example, we detected the functional annotation in liver to be relevant to the lipid-related phenotypes, including low-density lipoprotein, high-density lipoprotein, triglycerides and total cholesterol. 2.We also showed [1, 9, 10,12] that statistical power of risk variants identification and the accuracy of risk prediction can be greatly improved by leveraging pleiotropy among complex traits. For example, we performed integrative analysis of Crohn’s disease from WTCCC and summary statistics from GWAS of some other diseases, such as Type 1 diabetes, Ulcerative colitis and Primary biliary cirrhosis. Our recently developed method LEP [12] was able to significantly increase the statistical power of identifying risk variants and improve the risk prediction accuracy from 63.39% (±0.58%) to 68.33% (±0.32%) using about 195,000 variants. In the meanwhile, the risk variants prioritized by LEP was shown to be more likely validated in a larger and independent GWAS published by International Inflammatory Bowel Disease Genetics Consortium (IIBDGC). Besides the above methodology development, we investigate theoretical development motivated by GWAS data analyses [7,8]. We have also developed statistical methods for data pre-processing [2,6], e.g., AC-PCA, a principal component analysis-based method for adjustment of confounding variations. Finally, we have summarized the main research outcomes in a book chapter [3], as a tutorial for beginners in this field.

22302815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22302815.value: We have developed a coherent statistical framework to allow simultaneous analysis of GWAS data of multiple organismal traits and functional annotation data of multiple cellular traits. In this project, most of the analysis results are based on European samples. To have a wider effect, we plan to future make the developed methods applicable to the population of East Asia (e.g., the Hong Kong population). The current project is devoted to connect well-defined phenotypes (e.g., cardiovascular disease) with human genome by development of new statistical methods and tools. However, how to connect more complex phenotypes (e.g., human face) to genome variation largely remains unknown. It is very challenging to pre-define some factors to characterize a complex phenotype, e.g., human face. As further development of this research direction, we aim to develop new tools to extract the features of a complex phenotype adaptively, and then connect human genome with those phenotypes tools to extract the features of a complex phenotype adaptively, and then connect human genome with those phenotypes. The integrated analysis of multimodal data may bring more interdisciplinary research and innovation projects, contributing to a broader field, such as precision health and precision medicine.

22302815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22302815.value: With the innovation of gene sequencing technology, the era of human genome big data has arrived. The value of genomic data is largely dependent on our ability to link genes to human phenotypes such as facial features, cardiovascular disease, and more. The success of this project offers new possibilities for improving this capability. Specifically, the methods developed in this project make use of the following facts: 1. Genetic variants are NOT equally important to a certain type of diseases or traits. 2 Different complex traits/diseases can share common genetic bases, which is formally known as pleiotropy. With the developed methods and tools, the statistical power of risk variant identification and risk prediction accuracy of complex diseases can be greatly improved. These technical advances will bring more benefit in precision health.

22304115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22304115.value: 卟啉是人工合成葉綠素同系物，其作為光敏材料在染料敏化太陽能電池中取得了12%以上的光電轉換效率。然而由於易聚集和電荷傳輸效率低等缺陷的原因導致其在本體異質結有機太陽能電池中的應用受到限制；另外，卟啉類分子在500到600納米範圍吸收光譜比較弱，一定程度上影響電池光電轉換效率的提高。但由於小分子具有聚合物材料無可比擬的優勢，比如清晰的分子結構和分子量，以及純度高和器件重複性好，因此發展卟啉類有機共軛小分子，提高其有機溶劑溶解性，改善其易聚集特性，提高電荷傳輸效率，然后作為給體材料應用于本體異質結有機太陽能電池，有望取得較高的光電轉換效率。主要研究方案是以硫、氧、硒等雜原子取代傳統卟啉環中的氮原子，合成具有特定光譜和電化學性質的新型卟啉中心用於構建有機共軛小分子；同時改變卟啉環周邊取代基的結構，以烷基鏈取代傳統的苯類，有效增加分子之間的π-π相互作用，從而提高電荷傳輸效率。另外，設計合成和卟啉類給體材料吸收光譜互補的非富勒烯類受體材料同樣對提高電池的整體性能具有重要意義。

22304115.label: Realisation of objectives
22304115.value: We believe that porphyrin-based small molecules should play a more important role in bulky heterojunction organic solar cells (BHJ OSCs) with judicious structural optimization due to their strong absorption spectrum, high molar absorption coefficients, and unique photophysical properties. In the traditional porphyrin structures, peripheral meso-phenyl substituents stand almost orthogonal orientation relative to the porphyrin plane, which prevents the intermolecular π-π stacking, as well as intermolecular charge transport. And the porphyrin framework with meso-alkyl chains instead of meso-phenyl substituents has never been investigated in the construction of small molecules for BHJ OSC applications. It was believed that the long alkyl chain could not only improve the solubility of small molecules in most organic solvents, but also control the film morphology and crystallinity, leading to the enhancement of charge transport. In our preliminary work, we synthesized three new unsymmetrical push-pull A-D-A small molecules (SMs) consisting of 5,15-meso-alkyl substituted porphyrins as electron rich donor (D) units, ethynylbenzene as π-linkage, and 3-ethylrhodanine (RH) as electron deficient acceptor (A). Specifically, the the alkyl chains on either porphyrin or phenylene linker have positive effect on the film morphology, charge mobility and photovoltaic performance. This kind of porphyrin molecules show good solubility in common organic solvent, a broad absorption in the visible and NIR regions, a relatively high hole-mobility and good film-forming properties for solution processed BHJ OSC. Based on the blend film of SM/PC71BM spin-coated from a mixture with 3% pyridine in chlorobenzene, a high PCE of 9.20% was achieved. The results indicate that the A-D-A small molecules based on meso-alkyl substituted porphyrin core are very promising donor candidates for highly efficient BHJ OSCs. Though porphyrin-based donor materials have demonstrated their enormous potentiality in photovoltaic applications with outstanding performance, porphyrin based materials have an important disadvantage with lacking of light-harvesting ability beyond 850 nm, thus limiting their cell performances. Since 50% of the total solar photon flux is located in the red and near-infrared (NIR) spectra (600–1000 nm), it’s quite urgent to develop efficient NIR absorbing molecules for high performance organic solar cells. So we are motivated to develop a new class of conjugated porphyrin to optimize light absorption and energy level, with the highlight of pushing light absorption into near infrared region, and developing highly efficient NIR organic solar cells (OSCs). Definitely, the coupling two porphyrin macrocycles through an ethynyl linker is a conventional method to obtain an essentially coplanar porphyrin molecular, which is an effective way to extend the absorption of a porphyrin toward deep-absorption region. Besides, employing meso-meso linked porphyrin dimers can improve extinction coefficients regularly with the strong exciton coupling between two porphyrin moieties and decrease the π–π* gap concomitantly with the increased π-conjugation. This strategy is especially successful for the highly efficient porphyrin-based dyes sensitized solar cells with light harvesting in NIR region. Herein, we strategically constructed new A-π2-D-π1-D-π2-A molecule (CS-DP) with highly visible-NIR absorption, in which two porphyrin monomers is tethered via ethynyl linker (π1), and ended with electron deficient 3-ethylrhodanine (A) via the second ethynylbenzene (π2) linker. Moreover, aliphatic side chain substitutions can be readily introduced to the orthogonal position in porphyrins to manipulate material solubility and solid-state packing. Notably, the absorption spectrum of the conjugation elongated porphyrin molecules was extend light to 700-1000 nm region. The new architecture and appropriate energy levels give rise to the low energy loss feature when CS-DP is used in BHJ OSCs. The synergetic effects of thermal annealing (TA) and solvent vapor annealing (SVA) under the optima conditions can effectively improve the charge mobility in solid-state thin films by either lowering the glass transition temperature or thermally enhancing molecular motion. Using pyridine additive, TA at 110°C and THF SVA for 20 s, the champion blend CS-DP/PC71BM thin film was produced with a maximum of the short circuit current as well as the fill factor, yielding a power conversion efficiency up to 8.29%. Specifically, this super small bandgap dimeric porphyrin is very promising for use in ternary and multi-junction applications as well as NIR photodetectors. Following a similar strategy stated above, we designed and synthesized two new acceptor-donor-acceptor structural small molecules (DPP-2TTP and DPP-2TP) based on diketopyrrolopyrrole-ethynylene-bridged porphyrin dimers. Both show strong absorption in ranges of 400–550 (Soret bands) and 700–900 nm (Q bands) and their intrinsic absorption deficiency between the Soret and Q bands could be perfect compensated by a wide bandgap small molecule DR3TBDTTF with absorption in 500–700 nm. Impressively, the optimal ternary device based on the blend films of DPP-2TPP, 20% DR3TBDTTF and PC71BM, shows a PCE of 11.15%, while the binary devices based on DPP-2TTP/PC71BM and DPP-2TP/PC71BM blend films exhibit PCEs of 9.30% and 8.23%, respectively. The high compatibility of the low bandgap porphyrin-based small molecules with the wide bandgap small molecules provides new threesome with PC71BM for highly efficient all-small-molecules ternary organic solar cells. On the other hand, non-fullerene molecular acceptors incorporating perylene diimide (PDI) have also been investigated as it is an excellent electron transport system. Porphyrins are a group of naturally occurring intensely colored heterocyclic compounds with 4-meso and 8-β positions readily to be appended with multiple PDI units for high electron mobility. To exploit new PDI-based acceptors with high electron mobility and optimal light harvesting in OSCs, we developed new perylenediimide-porphyrin acceptors, 4PDI-ZnP and 2PDI-ZnP, which were facilely synthesized by the acid-catalyzed condensation of perylenediimide-substituted benzaldehyde with respective dipyrromethance and pyrrole, and subsequent Zn(II)-complexation. For their spectral absorption properties perfect complementary to the common polymer donor, PTB7-Th, the two acceptors have been evaluated together with PTB7-Th for non-fullerene BHJ OSCs. High power conversion efficiency of 9.64% has been achieved using the blend of 4PDI-ZnP:PTB7-Th for its optimal visible sunlight harvesting, favorable morphological properties and efficient charge dissociation upon photon absorption. This represents hitherto benchmark photovoltaic peformance for PDI acceptors and PTB7-Th donor systems. Conclusively, poprhyrin-based small molecules can be finely engineered for their applications as either electron donors or electron acceptors in BHJ OSCs. The high PCE of 9.3% was achieved for the single junction OSCs and 11.15% for binary devices. More importantly, new PDI-Porphyrins represent new class of non-fullerene acceptors, and realized a PCE of 9.6% using the blend of 4PDI-ZnP:PTB7-Th in BHJ OSCs. In the future, we will make our effort to upscale manufacturing of small molecule OSCs, in order to decrease the cost and advocate a practical approach for OSCs production.

22304115.label: Major findings and research outcome
22304115.value: Porphyrin-based small molecules as donors have long been ignored in bulky heterojunction organic solar cells (BHJ OSCs) due to the unfavorable aggregation and low charge mobility. Aiming to strike a delicate balance among solubility, morphology, energy levels and charge mobility, we for the first time developed a series of new porphyrin-based small molecules (SMs) with as donor materials in OSCs. The molecular design strategy can simultaneously facilitate stronger intermolecular π-π stacking and higher charge transfer mobility in the active film, leading to the highest PCE of 8.21% in the conventional device. The results were published in Chem. Commun. 2016, 52, 3713-3716; Chem. Sci. 2016, 7, 4301-4307; J. Mater. Chem. C 2018, 6, 3341-3345; J. Mater. Chem. A 2018, 6, 14675-14680; J. Mater. Chem. C 2018, 6, 9111-9118; J. Mater. Chem. C 2019, 7, 380-386; Org. Electron. 2019, 73, 146-151. Continuously, we developed series of near-infrared absorbing dimeric porphyrin-cored SMs which show strong absorption in ranges of 400–550 (Soret bands) and 700–900 nm (Q bands). And the intrinsic absorption deficiency between the Soret and Q bands could be perfect compensated by a wide bandgap SM DR3TBDTTF (D*) with absorption in 500–700 nm. Impressively, the optimal ternary device based on the blend films of DPP-2TPP, DR3TBDTTF (20 wt.%) and PC71BM, shows a PCE of 11.15% (J. Mater. Chem. A 2017, 5, 25460-25468; ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2019, 11, 6283-6291.). At the same time, we designed and synthesized a series of peripheral perylenediimide (PDI) conjugated porphyrin-based new non-fullerene acceptors. Their energetics and spectral absorption properties complement nicely to those of common donor polymers such as PTB7-Th for efficient light harvesting and conversion to electricity. The OSCs devices with active layers of 4PZnP:PTB7-Th show favorable morphology and efficient charge dissociation, corresponding to a respectively high PCE of 9.64% (Sustain. Energy Fuels 2018, 2, 2616-2624.). In addition, we prepared Zn(II) and Cu(II) complexes of 5,10,15,20-tetrakis{4-[N,N -di(4-methoxylphenyl)aminophenyl]}porphyrin (ZnP and CuP). Both exhibit excellent thermal and electrochemical stability, specifically a high hole mobility and very favorable energetics for hole extraction that render them a new class of hole-transporting materials (HTMs) for efficient and stable perovskite solar cells (PSCs). As expected, ZnP affords a competitive PCE of 17.78%, which is comparable to that of the most powerful HTM of Spiro-MeOTAD (18.59%) under the same working conditions (ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2017, 9, 13231-13239; J. Mater. Chem. A 2019, 7, 10200-10205.).

22304115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22304115.value: We are still working on the molecular structures' refinement and optimization of processing conditions, and mechanism investigation of charge separation and transportation. It's expected that those porphyrin-based electron donors and non-fullerene acceptors would play a very important role in the commercialization of organic solar cells.

22304115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22304115.value: Photosynthesis with chlorophyll as the centerpiece produces giant energy for nearly all life on earth and nature systems. An organic solar cell (OSC) is a type of solar technology that uses semiconducting organic polymers or small organic molecules for light absorption and charge transport to produce electricity in a branch of electronics. And synthetic porphyrins, analogues of chlorophyll, exhibits a very intense absorption in the visible region. Herein, we devoted to design and synthesize new classes of photoactive porphyrin-centered small molecules, and improve their optical, chemical and electronic properties. After several years effort, we have screed out several kinds of porphyrin-based small molecules, which show highly efficient light-harvesting capability, good solubility in organic solvent for solution processing of device, appropriate energy levels and optimal morphology in active layer for efficient solar light conversion into electricity. As a result, impressive performances with 11% power conversion efficiency have been achieved in OSCs with those porphyrin small molecules as the main components in the photoactive layer. In the future, we will make our effort to upscale manufacturing of small molecule OSCs, in order to decrease the cost and advocate a practical approach for OSCs production.

22503015.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22503015.value: 控制感恢復：社會排斥和消費者的轉換行為

22503015.label: Project Objectives
22503015.value: Understand the proposed effect of chronic or temporary social exclusion on consumers’ switching behavior (either switching a brand or a product). Examine the underlying mechanism for the proposed effect, that is, the lower sense of control experienced by those who are socially excluded. Identify possible boundary conditions for the proposed effect.
rows: Understand the proposed effect of chronic or temporary social exclusion on consumers’ switching behavior (either switching a brand or a product).
Examine the underlying mechanism for the proposed effect, that is, the lower sense of control experienced by those who are socially excluded.
Identify possible boundary conditions for the proposed effect.

22503015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22503015.value: When do consumers deviate from buying the same brand or product anymore and start a journey with another brand or product? And what factors drive such switching behavior? Understanding consumer switching behavior is of practical importance to marketers. By knowing the antecedents for possible switching to other brands, marketers can come up plan to retain their consumers or unyoke consumers from competing brands. With the increased product line complexity in many companies, switching may happen within a brand: for example, a loyal consumer of Crest may try a newly launched red wine flavor instead of sticking to their usual green tea flavor. Marketers attempting to persuade consumers to use premium products instead of low-tier ones will be eager to ascertain how to initiate such a switch. Various environmental and personal factors can induce consumers to switch products or brands, such as price or advertising, a shift in consumer preference, the launch of a new product, etc. However, have you ever thought of that, instead of being a result of the rivalry among different product offerings in the market, switching behavior can be unrelated with any market efforts and consumers’ preference? In this study, we propose that consumers’ switching behavior could be founded purely on a psychological factor, social exclusion, that are pertinent to neither marketing mix nor personal preference. Social exclusion (i.e., being alone, isolated, or ostracized) is a rather common but threatening experience such as being ignored at parties or in office conversations, the ending of friendships, and receiving letters of rejection from companies or universities. Experiences such as these are painful because our fundamental concepts of socialization are challenged. Advances in communication technologies and the growth of social media have resulted in less personal contact, increasing the prevalence of social exclusion. This research links social exclusion with the topic of switching, and aims to use the consumer switching behavior platform as a means to reveal novel insights behind social exclusion. Specifically, we argue that social exclusion increases consumers’ switching orientation. We propose that this effect is mediated by the sense of a loss of control among socially excluded consumers, which can be restored simply by a switching behavior. At last, familiarity and anthropomorphism of the switching target can serve as boundary conditions for the proposed effect. 消費者何時會從購買同一品牌或產品轉換到其他的選擇呢?哪些因素會構成這樣的轉換行為? 了解消費者的轉換行為對營銷有實際的意義。透過理解轉換行為的前因，營銷機構能制定計劃來留住固有的消費者或從其競爭品牌中吸引更多新的消費者。隨著很多公司發展更多的產品線，消費者的轉換行為能在同一品牌內發生。舉例說，Crest的忠實消費者可能會轉用品牌新推出的紅酒味牙膏，而不繼續選用一貫的綠茶味牙膏。一些試圖說服消費者從較低層次產品轉換至高端產品的營銷人員渴望查明如何引發這些轉換行為。多種的環境和個人因素能誘發消費者對產品或品牌轉換，包括價格、廣告推銷、消費者喜好的轉變及新產品的推出等。然而，你有沒有想過消費者的轉換行為可能並不是不同產品在市場上競爭所導致的結果？或者他們的轉換行為可能與偏好和市場的狀況沒有任何關係？在這個研究中，我們提出消費者的轉換行為與市場營銷組合和個人喜好無關，而可能單純是因一項心理因素而致，這就是社會排斥。社會排斥（即處於單獨、被孤立或排斥的情況）是一種相當常見的現象，但也會有一些令人恐懼的經歷，例如在聚會或辦公室對話中被忽視、友誼的結束和收到由公司或大學發出的拒絕信。因為我們的基本社會化概念受到衝擊，所以這些經歷都是痛苦的。隨著通訊科技和社交媒體的發展，人與人之間的接觸減少，增加了社會排斥的發生。這項研究將社會排斥與轉換行為連結起來，旨在透過消費者的轉換行為以揭示對社會排斥的新見解。具體而言，我們認為社會排斥增加了消費者的轉換取向。我們提出控制感的喪失對這個假設有著中介效果。消費者能透過轉換行為恢復因受到社會排斥所失去的控制感。最後，轉換目標（產品或品牌）的熟悉及擬人化程度可作為上述效果的邊界條件。

22503015.label: Realisation of objectives
22503015.value: 1. This study examines the effects of social exclusion on consumers’ brand and product switching behavior. Specifically, we found that that consumers who perceive themselves as being chronically or temporarily excluded exhibit more switching behavior than their peers who do not feel socially excluded. In our first study, we uncovered the relationship between social exclusion and switching behavior by linking survey and archival data. We had a group of university students complete a survey about their social media use. We then retrieved information about their daily lunch routines. The data consisted of contactless electronic payment records, the primary method of payment at this university, and details on which canteen or restaurant the student visited on campus each day for the previous three months. We found that the students who had fewer social media friends or joined fewer chat groups were more likely to switch to a different canteen or restaurant from the one they visited the day before. In another study conducted in a lab setting, the participants experienced social exclusion through a computer ball-tossing game (dubbed “Cyberball” by psychologists). Afterwards, they were given the opportunity to switch to a different free gift than the one they had chosen earlier (a refrigerator magnet). We observed that the socially excluded participants were more likely than their included counterparts to switch to a different gift when presented with the option. 2. We found that this effect is mediated by a decreased sense of control after social exclusion. Our studies 3 and 4 have indicated that social exclusion results in the loss of an individual’s control, that is, the sense one has of his or her ability to exert influence on or master his or her environment. This is quite understandable, as being rejected or ostracized by others leads to an inability to influence others in social activities, which impairs perceptions of control. From an evolutionary perspective, control is an important factor associated with survival. Subsequently, people are motivated to find ways to boost their sense of control after being socially excluded, a journey we refer to as “control restoration.” Meanwhile, we argue that a sense of control can be restored by the decision to switch when faced with a choice between “staying with the status quo” or “switching to another brand/company.” Switching to a different brand provides apparent and salient evidence of the consumer’s mastery of his or her environment. It also provides the consumer with a different option, such that he or she has an alternative and thus is not constrained by his or her environment. Both of these factors boost the consumer’s sense of control. Taken together, we conclude that social exclusion results in a decreased sense of control, which motivates people to use switching to restore their sense of control. 3. Finally, we found that the effect disappears when the incumbent option possesses the function of maintaining social belongingness (e.g., when the incumbent option is socially conformed or symbolizes social connection). Our last study indicated that the switching behavior among excluded people was weakened or disappeared when their previous choices allowed them to fit into a certain group. For example, people are less likely to switch to another gym, even after being socially excluded, if their peers go to the same gym. This indicates the importance of the effect of social connectedness on brand and product switching.

22503015.label: Major findings and research outcome
22503015.value: When attempting to create consumer loyalty, it is easy to look in the wrong place. Companies may craft the perfect product or have the swiftest service, but their customers may still switch to other providers. Our findings offer novel evidence to explain why this happens. A pilot study first tested the notion of whether switching is more effective at boosting personal control than other choices. Thereafter, across five studies, we showed that socially excluded consumers demonstrated a higher intention to switch across either products or services. We further showed that this effect was caused by a heightened desire to restore the sense of control among socially excluded participants (studies 3 and 4). Moreover, this effect was moderated by the belongingness maintenance capacity of the incumbent option (study 5).

22503015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22503015.value: The current research also suggests that there are several questions deserving future research. First, consumers switch brand and product options under very different circumstances. For example, some types of switching behavior may represent an approach tendency (e.g., to pursue new and better product options), whereas others may be driven by avoidance motivation (e.g., to get away from the unsatisfied incumbent option). Because we are mainly interested in process-driven (but not utility-driven) switching behavior, in most of our studies we controlled this motivational difference by providing the participants with somewhat neutral information regarding the switching context (e.g., the mere availability of new options or the incumbent product needed to be replaced for exogenous reasons). We believe that the effect of social exclusion on switching that we observed is robust and can be generalized to various switching contexts. However, the different motivations underpinning consumer switching behavior and their antecedents and consequences are important research areas that deserve further investigation. Last but not least, Pfundmair et al. (2015) recently showed that people from different cultural backgrounds react differently to social exclusion. For example, individualists experience less fulfillment of their psychological needs after social exclusion than people from collectivist cultures (Pfundmair et al. 2015).

22503015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22503015.value: In our research, five studies including both a field study and lab tests were conducted, and the results demonstrated that individuals who felt social exclusion engaged in more switching behavior. In our first study, we uncovered the relationship between social exclusion and switching behavior by linking survey data with archival data. We first got a group of university students who voluntarily completed a survey about their social media usage behavior. With permission from the university, we retrieved the students’ daily lunch routines (i.e., which canteens or restaurants they visited on campus) for three months after the survey. What we found was that the students who had a lack of friends or joined less chatting groups on social media platforms were more likely to switch to a different canteen or restaurant from the one they visited the day before. In another study conducted in a controlled lab setting, we observed that the socially excluded participants were more likely to switch to a different gift when presented with the option compared to the participants who did not feel social exclusion.

22607115.label: Project Objectives
22607115.value: To reach a thick description and understanding of how the development of digital technology converges with feminist and queer activism in China. The study will contribute valuable outputs for scholars in media and communication, gender and sexuality studies, as well as China studies. Findings will be published as journal articles, and possibly a book monograph for academic readers. It will be the first bilingual non-commercial website dedicated to documenting queer and feminist media activism in China. The online database will also serve as an important nodal point to connect with other feminist and queer websites based in China, which are sometimes censored and filtered by the government or by internet service providers. The website can also be a teaching tool for classes related to gender, sexuality, media, and cultural studies, or for classes on contemporary China, providing social contexts on issues such as domestic violence, sexual assault and abuse, social inequality and discrimination relevant to gender and sexuality, etc. To explore the often overlooked dimension of gender and sexuality in relation to digital activism in China and make available some research findings in Chinese. The issues of gender and sexuality are marginalized socially and academically in China. This study, with its findings published as journal articles, will contribute to public knowledge for citizens generally, as well as activists. 22607115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22607115.value: In the last decade, aided by the development of communication technologies, feminist and queer media activists in China have been using a variety forms such as documentary workshops, online campaigns, webcasts, webzines and so on to promote sexual and gender diversity. In this process, digital technology has played an unprecedented role in assembling nvquan (feminist) or kuer (queer) discourses and practices in community building, public education and advocacy. Despite the significant growth of feminist and queer media practices in China for more than ten years, not much has been written about this subject. The explanation for such under-exploration is twofold. On one hand, while many studies explore how digital technology has influenced the production, circulation, and consumption of feminist and LGBT (lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender) media in the American, European and other Asian contexts, the research on feminist and queer media in China is disproportionally small. On the other hand, although research on communication technologies in China, particularly Internet activism, has flourished considerably, the issues of gender and sexuality remain marginalized. Intersecting feminist and queer media studies and studies on communication technologies in China, this project aims to examine how digital technology informs the development of feminist and queer activism in China, and, at the same time, how alternative media practices attuned to gender and sexuality issues can shed light on feminist practices and the queering of digital technology. Drawing from semi-structured interviews with various feminist and queer media practitioners, analysis of key events and media productions, participatory observation, as well as documents from relevant organizations, this project will analyze the convergence of digital media and feminist and queer activism in China. Ultimately, the project will generate a scholarly understanding of how digital technology informs the development of feminist and queer activism in China. It will also make available a bilingual online database for archiving feminist and queer media activism, providing useful information for the general public in China and Hong Kong. 在過去的十年間，隨著通訊科技的發展，中國的女權/女性主義和酷兒媒體行動者運用不同的方式，包括紀綠片工作坊、電影節、網絡廣播和網路雜誌等來推動性和性別多元。在這個過程中，數字化技術在聚集女權/女性主義或酷兒論述和實踐、建立群體認同以及公眾教育和倡導方面扮演著前所未有的位置。雖然在過去的十幾年間中國女權主義和酷兒媒體有重要的增長，但是關於這方面的研究卻很少。一方面，很多研究是關於數字化技術在美國、歐洲或亞洲其他地區如何影響女性主義和酷兒媒體的製作、發行和消費，而對於中國的女權主義和酷兒媒體的研究是不合比例地少。另一方面，關於中國通訊科技的研究，特別是互聯網行動主義的研究是相當蓬勃的，可是，性和性別的議題是被邊緣化的。通過訪談女權主義和酷兒媒體參與者、分析重要的事件及媒體製作、參與觀察、查閱相關組織的紀錄，此項目將會分析中國數字化媒體與女權和酷兒行動主義的關係。除了學術論文以外，此研究所收集的資料將會呈現在一個中英雙語的網站上，為中國內地及香港的大眾提供有用資訊。

22607115.label: Realisation of objectives
22607115.value: 1. Three articles published in three SSCI-indexed international journals explain how the development of digital technology converges with feminist and queer activism in China. First, PI published “Aesthetics of Queer Becoming: Comrade Yue and Chinese Community-based Documentaries Online” in Critical Studies in Media Communication (2016), a leading journal in communication studies. The essay is well received and is now reprinted in an anthology called Queer Technologies: Affordances, Affect, Ambivalence (2017) edited by Katherine Sender and Adrienne Shaw and published by Routledge. The article examines how the medium of the video, with its capacity for dissemination online, functions as a unique format that gives rise to a new set of queer aesthetics and politics through first-person audio-visual constructions. Second, a more theoretical article “Beijing Meets Hawai‘i: Reflections on ku’er, Indigeneity, and Queer Theory” was published in GLQ: A Journal of Lesbian and Gay Studies (2017), a leading journal in gender and sexuality studies. Analyzing the ways queer film festivals, documentary workshops and online media groups in China appropriate the idiom of “queer,” this article offers a reconsideration of queer theory and practice useful to both area studies and indigenous studies, which have both critiqued how the epistemic structure of queer studies, by particularizing the non-West, supports the domination of the West. Third, an article on feminist media activism titled “Digital Masquerading: Feminist Media Activism in China” was published in the journal Crime, Media, Culture (2017). It looks at how the new wave of feminist media activism (re)negotiates the line between the public and the private in the digital age through “digital masquerading.” Further details of the major findings will be explained in 6.1. 2. A bilingual (Chinese and English) online database for archiving feminist and queer media activism is now available via https://feministqueerchina.wixsite.com/media. This website categorizes the feminist and queer activities related to media into three areas: Feminism/Gender and Media; Youth Feminist Action School (YFAS); Queer and Media. The section “Feminism/Gender and Media” illustrates the development of feminism and the events relevant to feminism/gender and media. This section summarizes the major events related to both feminism/gender and media since the 1990s, including 1) the establishment of organizations and activities targeted at media (e.g. monitoring mainstream media reports on gender issues); 2) the organizations and activities which leverage both mainstream media and social media to provoke public discussions or to advance their causes; 3) the feminist/gender activities that have attracted great amount of media attention, most of which were unprecedented and/or very influential for future activism. A brief introduction to each event and links to other relevant sources are provided. Information on the establishment, development and mission of organizations working on media and feminism/gender is also provided. The trajectory and influence of key activities related to media and feminism/gender are also described. The section “Youth Feminist Action School (YFAS)” introduces the new generation of feminists and the new wave of feminist activism. This section summarizes YFAS’s important and influential feminist activities from 2012 to 2015. The activities are categorized into the following 9 topics: 1) fighting for equality in the public space; 2) anti-domestic violence/gender-based violence; 3) anti-sexism in education and in workplace; 4) anti-sexual harassment and anti-rape; 5) fighting against gender stereotypes; 6) anti-sexism in media; 7) cooperation between feminists and LGBT activists; 8) gender and working-class issues; 9) the Feminist Five case. This section also contains the influence/result of the feminist activities: 1) some feminist activities had direct influence/result, namely the four lawsuits regarding sexism in the workplace from 2013 to 2015; 2) some feminist activities had indirect influence/result. Since they explicitly targeted certain gender-based issues and policies, the implications of such gender-based issues and the change of policies are thus listed here accordingly; 3) some feminist activities did not have any direct and/or indirect influence/result for the present and thus are not shown in the table. The section “Queer and Media” introduces the development of LGBT movements in China and their media-related events. This section summarizes the major events related to both the queer community and media, including 1) the LGBT-related activities that focus on film and media; 2) the organizations which use the film and/or media to promote LGBT culture among the LGBT community and/or the public; 3) the LGBT-related activities that have attracted great amount of media attention, most of which were unprecedented and/or very influential for future activism. A brief introduction to each event and links to other relevant sources are provided. Information on the establishment, development and mission of organizations working on media and queer issues are introduced. The trajectory and influence of key activities related to media and queer issues are also described. Additionally, the section “Selected Bibliography” contains a bibliography of references and further academic writings pertaining to both feminist activism and queer activism. The section “Other Links” points to additional resources on the feminist and queer movements in China. 3. As explained earlier, the website is bilingual and contains the data regarding media-related feminist and queer activism in China gathered during the research. One of the research output, “Beijing Meets Hawai‘i: Reflections on ku’er, Indigeneity, and Queer Theory,” was translated into Chinese and has been made available to the general public via the website in the “Selected Bibliography” section.

This study, with its findings published as journal articles, will contribute to public knowledge for citizens generally, as well as activists. Selected English publications will be translated into Chinese and made available to the general public via the website.

22607115.label: Major findings and research outcome
22607115.value: The major findings are presented in three articles published in three SSCI-indexed international journals. First, through the examination of a new wave of community-based documentary workshops, including the Queer University (kuer daxue) Digital Filmmaking Training Camp, PI finds that the medium of the video, with its capacity for dissemination online, functions as a unique format that gives rise to a new set of queer aesthetics and politics through first-person audio-visual constructions. Second, through analyzing the ways queer film festivals, documentary workshops and online media groups in China appropriate the idiom of “queer,” PI offers a reconsideration of queer theory and practice useful to both area studies and indigenous studies, which have both critiqued how the epistemic structure of queer studies, by particularizing the non-West, supports the domination of the West. Thinking beyond the binaries of West/East and white/indigeneity, this essay calls for a kind of transversal queer alliance that does not equate “cultural specificity” with cultural authenticity, but critically uses it as an entry point to reveal the structural hierarchy between the local and the global, the particular and the universal. Third, exploring the practices of the Feminist Action School, PI finds that this new wave of feminist media activism (re)negotiates the line between the public and the private in the digital age through “digital masquerading” in three ways. First, these feminist media practices in the digital era are active and self-conscious acts leveraging the specificity of media to increase public influence and avoid censorship. Second, these practices tactically use images of women’s body and the digital alterability of these images as a form of masquerade to circumvent censorship and possible criminalization. Third, the notion of digital masquerading points to the interface between the medium and the subjects, which involves collective efforts in assembling activist activities and remaking publicness. PI also presented and disseminated the findings in three international conferences, including a conference on Digital China at the University of Oxford, the annual conference of the Association for Cultural Studies held in Sydney, and the annual conference of the Inter-Asia Cultural Studies Society held in Seoul (see Part C for details).

22607115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22607115.value: While collecting data during field trips, PI noticed the frequent reference to rights-related concepts by feminist and queer activists. Many feminist and queer activists leverage different media platforms and events, such as women’s and queer film festivals as well as media campaigns, to advocate different forms of quan (rights) for women and sexual minorities, using terms such as nüquan (women’s rights), quanli (rights and interests) and quanyi (rights and benefits). In particular, the concept of nüquan (women’s rights) has gained currency beyond the activist circle. What does the term quan actually mean when used by different individual feminist and queer activists and communal organizations in different contexts? How do the activists use media to engage, develop, or challenge rights-based concepts related to gender/sexuality? Conversely, how do different media platforms and institutions shape gender/sexuality rights advocacy? PI plans to make sense of the emergent discourse of quan in feminist and queer media culture and has applied for a new GRF in year 2017-18.

22607115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22607115.value: This project investigates the role of digital technology in feminist and LGBT activism in China. First, video-making provides a tool to challenge conventional understanding and diversify representation of marginalized sexuality. NGOs leverage documentary workshops and online platforms to promote gender and sexual diversity, as well as for community building. Second, examining how the term “queer” circulates in queer film festivals, documentary workshops and online media groups, this project critiques problematic assumptions in Western theory, and encourages marginalized groups in the West and non-West to forge alliance. Third, the project shows how a new wave of feminist activism leverages digital media to collectively create and circulate images in a way that influences the agenda of legacy and online media, increases public awareness and circumvents state censorship. The results and data will be useful for scholars from sexuality and gender studies, media and communication studies, and China studies. The findings, especially the bilingual website on feminist and queer media activism in China, can benefit activists engaged in media activism in China, and feminist and queer activists in other places. This project will also raise public awareness on issues of gender and sexuality in China and other Chinese-speaking societies.

22608115.label: Project Objectives
22608115.value: To address a pressing need to better understand the use of social media in relation to political engagement among Hong Kong youths and the implications for contentious political behaviors. To examine the precise role of social media and other enabler technologies in shaping political attitudes and behaviors among Hong Kong youths, particularly in comparison with other socializing agents. To clarify the link between social media use and contentious political behaviors among Hong Kong youths, and identify possible contextual or confounding factors that might intervene their relationships. To provide opportunities for reflection and dialogue with young citizens in Hong Kong regarding their collective identity and aspirations, as well as civic and political engagement. To facilitate evidence-based dialogue with educators, parents, and civic organizations regarding the opportunities and risks in the use of social media for civic and political engagement among young people in Hong Kong.
