22608115.label: Realisation of objectives
22608115.value: In-depth interviews were conducted with Hong Kong youths who have directly engaged in the recent social movements or political activities in Hong Kong. All research participants had been involved with the Umbrella Movement. Most participants reported involvement in the Umbrella Movement through setting up road blockades, sitting-in at the occupied areas, and distributing supplies (food, water, etc.) to other protesters. As the occupation was spread across different sites, many participants had volunteered to coordinate the movement of protesters by appealing for reinforcements and warning about impending dangers at the sites. Several participants also shared their experiences of protecting the occupied areas from police action, storming police barricades, scuffles with the police and counter-protesters, and getting hit by tear gas or pepper spray fired by the police. Objective 1: This research has advanced a better understanding of the use of social media in relation to political engagement among Hong Kong youths and the implications for contentious political behaviors. The findings show that Hong Kong youths were quick to embrace social media in efficiently mobilizing groups of participants for political activities without involving formal organizations. Online communication through social networking sites have enabled them to share and coordinate available resources and disseminate information on political activities to a broader public quickly through interpersonal networks in social media. Research participants also expressed that they can share grievances, sense of powerlessness, radical thoughts and integrate their opinions among themselves in their social media networks. In addition, social media have opened opportunities for new types of symbolic and dramatic tactics for contentious political behaviors which have not been practiced in the same way offline. Youths, who are more technologically savvy and adept at using social media, are likely to be more unpredictable in their tactics and strategies in relations to political engagement when compared to their older counterparts. In addition to enhancing formal political participation, social media amplify emotions of young people according to certain political events, intensify their motivations to participate in radical social movements and other forms of contentious politics and eventually turn intentions into action rapidly. Objective 2: Research participants expressed different attitudes towards the role of social media in their political participation. To begin with, social media, such as Facebook, helps them to track information on politics daily. Moreover, they perceived that social media facilitate the sharing of the most recent and up-to-date information in a faster manner compared to traditional media. The efficacy of using social media for obtaining information was highlighted by the participants. The information in relation to various political concepts, viewpoints shared on social media would also increase their political knowledge and awareness, and even shape their political beliefs. For some, the use of social media has been already considered as part of political participation and engagement when it comes to entering political discussions or engaging with political content. According to many participants, they would comment, post or discuss government policies and political issues with others on social media, to some extent, helping to shape public narratives and understanding of political affairs. Furthermore, the participants suggested that social media facilitate greater involvement in direct actions and contentious political behaviors by offering an efficient means to mobilize and express political sentiment. They felt that online affective connections create solidarity for the collective actions unfolded offline. Their narratives also implied that political participation is empowered by online affective statements of viewpoints that in turn give rise to broader support and tangible connective involvements in contentious political actions. Objective 3: Research participants acknowledged the constructive role of social media use in contentious political behaviors in terms of getting access to immediate information on politics, sharing political sentiments, exchanging political opinions, mobilizing political activities, and so on. However, social media use was not the only factor that facilitate contentious politics among Hong Kong youths. Most participants reflected critically on the idea that youths’ political involvement could be situational which means they make decisions on different approaches vis-à-vis surroundings, circumstances or their own conditions. Specific cases such as controversies about National Education, political reform were direct mobilizing factors for contentious engagement. Besides, with a feeling of personal experience of togetherness, some of the participants who joined political events and adopted radical tactics in social movements claimed that their contentious actions are mainly influenced by their politically active friends in real life instead of the push from the virtual world. Nevertheless, potential backlash of adopting contentious political behaviors is a vital concern for Hong Kong youths while participating in contentious political movements as they must consider risks involved when they start their career or families. A fraction of participants pointed out that they are limited in terms of self-expression when using social media. Worrying about online verbal attacks, doxing and future career, they are wary of what they post on social network and prefer participating in political events including radical actions offline than discussing political issues online. Objective 4: Research participants were all Hong Kong young citizens aged 18 to 25 who have been participated in recent social movements and political activities in Hong Kong. During the interviews, they were asked a list of questions concerning different categories, such as personal political attitudes and beliefs, civil disobedience, radical behaviors, media consumption and usage, personal identity and issues of localism. Their perceptions on political engagement and understanding of identity issues were reflected throughout the interviews lasting from 40 minutes to 90 minutes. It is noted that a strong collective identity was felt within most of the participants, who believed that Hong Kong, as a special administrative region of China, should enjoy a high degree of autonomy under the “one-country, two-systems” constitutional principle. Collective values have formed an important part of the practical, day-to-day involvement in political events and trigger their political engagement, especially when their perceived “core” values of Hong Kong were violated and therefore in need of greater protection. Objective 5: The PI has presented the research findings at both local and international conferences as well as a peer-reviewed article in Chinese Journal of Communication (indexed by Social Sciences Citation Index) and a competitive paper (43% acceptance rate) published in full conference proceedings at the International Conference on Social Media and Society (see Part C). The publications provide a peer-reviewed source for evidence-based dialogue regarding the use of social media for political participation. In addition, the PI has shared research insights from this project on youth disconnection with social workers and other professionals working with local youths (including many youths and a few parents) as an invited speaker at the International Conference on Cyber Youth Work on 17 May 2018, organized by The Boys’ & Girls’ Clubs Association of Hong Kong, Caritas Hong Kong, and The Hong Kong Federation of Youth Groups.

22608115.label: Major findings and research outcome
22608115.value: The research outcome of this project highlights Hong Kong youths’ disconnection and ambivalence toward the use of social media for political purposes emerging from a major participatory experience in the Umbrella Movement. Two major theoretical contributions emerge from the research in this project: First, this research readdresses the overemphasis on the strengths and connectivity of social media by attending to how young people negotiate its drawbacks and disconnectivity in the political context. The findings indicate that perceptions of hostility, social risk, and futility impede online political expressions while the promises of embodied experience draw participants toward offline participation (see item 9 #1 in Part C). Furthermore, the findings (see item 8 #1 in Part C) show that despite their active and open informational sharing and political expressions on social media alongside their in-person participation during the eventful protest, many young participants became wary of such expressive use owing to their perceptions of de-energization, disconnectedness, and disembodiment. Rather than completely withdraw from political activities on social media, we illustrate how these politically inclined and technologically savvy youths embrace “disconnective practices”— passive engagement (lurking), selective expression (moderation and exposure-limitation), and offline participation (embodied collective action)—to avoid the overwhelming, fractious, and inauthentic conditions of mediated participation. Second, this research explicates the implications of protest participation which transcends the usual standards of civic and political engagement for youth moral and civic development (see item 9 #2 in Part C). Participating in the Umbrella Movement was shown to constitute “moral edgework”—a form of voluntary risk-taking that entails escaping and resisting the normative model of civic and political engagement. The thematic analysis of participants’ experiences reveals how moral edgework enables young people to deploy the necessary skills, competencies, and symbolic resources to develop their own ideas about civic and political engagement as well as realize their moral identity and capacity. The findings illustrate the self-actualizing and action-centered political socialization engendered via participants’ empowering emotional experiences and skillful practice of negotiating the normative and performative boundaries of contention (civility, lawfulness, peacefulness, and nonviolence). In doing so, this research contributes to a more pluralistic understanding of young people’s political socialization through emphasizing their role as creative agents in their own development.

22608115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22608115.value: Conceptualizing disconnective practices as tactics to avoid, disrupt, or circumvent conditions that enable certain forms of mediated participation to be undesirable or exploitative, the research in this project demonstrates how a group of politically active young people turn to various non-mutually exclusive disconnective practices to appropriate social media for political purposes while shielding themselves from the attendant pitfalls. Although disconnective practices may help young people to avoid certain drawbacks of mediated participation, they are not without problems: the switch to passive engagement could engender political apathy in the longer term, the turn to selective expression has the potential to breed echo chambers and groupthink, and the affinity for offline participation as a performance may encourage more radical physical actions. Future studies should examine the influences of such disconnective practices on young people’s political attitudes such as trust in authorities and their intentions to engage in protest movements and other political actions. The research in this project can also be further developed through a comparative study of older people’s disconnective practices to explore if various age groups perceive the drawbacks of using social media for political purposes differently and adopt unique forms of disengagement.

22608115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22608115.value: The Umbrella Movement has been the most significant political event in Hong Kong’s history post-1997 and its impact, particularly among youths at the forefront of the movement, has yet to be conclusive. Against this backdrop, this project has examined the use of social media for political purposes among young people in Hong Kong, focusing on its role in shaping their political participation during and after the Umbrella Movement. Unlike most studies which emphasize the strengths of social media in connecting people and promoting political engagement, this research highlights the drawbacks of social media and how it disconnects young people from politics. Rather than completely withdraw from political activities on social media, the findings show how these politically active Hong Kong youths avoid the overwhelming, hostile, and inauthentic conditions of online participation through “disconnective practices” such as passive engagement and limiting their expressions on social media, preferring instead to engage with politics offline. In addition, this research reveals that participating in the Umbrella Movement has enabled these young people to apply the necessary skills, capabilities, and symbolic meanings in developing their own ideas about civic and political engagement, especially in terms of their belief and capacity of taking radical political actions.

22609415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22609415.value: This project examines how the interlocking relationships between governing practices and global culture shape youth subjectivities in Beijing and Hong Kong. While the global economic recession has directed attention to the rising China, China itself faces mounting challenges of sustaining growth and a fast-growing ageing population. When China’s leader Xi Jinping speaks about the “Chinese Dream”, he specifically calls for the contribution of youth. China’s future relies heavily on its youth, who grow up in a prosperous China in which global culture is part of everyday life. Research into desires and aspirations of Chinese youth is scant, in particular when compared to the number of youth studies in the West. Also, China as an authoritarian state has confined Chinese youth studies largely within the political framework, overlooking the role of global culture in shaping the behaviour and aspirations of youth. This project addresses this lack by examining, first, how desire is incorporated in governing practices; second, how desire is enabled by global culture; and, third, how desire that is enabled by global culture directs acts of resistance. Acknowledging the significance of everyday life in cultivating desire and shaping one’s subjectivity, the PI grounds the study of desires on an empirical investigation of concrete but understudied food practices and home interiors – two daily necessities that are central to youth culture. Subjectivity refers to the ways that an individual comes to understand her/himself as a subject vis-à-vis the external world. Informed by Foucault’s governmentality, the term subject bears two connotations: the first refers to the processes whereby an individual is subject to control by social forces and the second refers to an individual as an autonomous being. By comparing youth in these two cities, the project investigates how different historical and social settings shape youth. Youth in Beijing, born after the Cultural Revolution, are mostly in single-child families; whereas, youth in Hong Kong have experienced major transitions brought by postcoloniality and the city’s retrocession to China. Recently, growing political tension and income disparity have sparked an outpouring of anger and frustration, making youth a pressing study subject. The research outputs, which include three academic articles, will 1/ bear political implications on the wellbeing of China; 2/ provide knowledge on how to inspire youth and have impact on youth-related policy; and 3/ theoretically, provide an empirical study of governmentality in a non-liberal setting and how globalisation works within the nexus of governmentality.

22609715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22609715.value: Shanghai urban culture and literature in the 1930s is often used as an example of Chinese Modernity. As the earliest developed city in China, Hong Kong began to see its own literature with a modern consciousness emerge at this time as well. Yet, this cultural history has been excluded from the scope of most scholars. To fill this gap, this three-year research project focuses on the 1930s in Hong Kong by exploring Hong Kong’s development as a modern city and its relationship to the emergence of modern Chinese fiction. Adopting Leo Ou-fan Lee’s Shanghai Modern as a model, this study has two parts: 1) understanding the nature of urban culture in Hong Kong during the 1930s by analyzing various elements such as public space, fashion, film, and mass media development; 2) examining the cultural activities of writers and analyzing works of fiction with a modern consciousness by studying their aesthetics and their relation to urban culture. Hong Kong literature was still budding in the 1930s, and due to various historical circumstances, such as Japan’s occupation from 1941-1945, most fiction writers who published in newspapers and magazines did not become well-known. Consequently, this study includes both established writers such as Lu Lun（侶倫）and Tse Sun Kwong（謝晨光）, as well as unknown or “anonymous” authors. Due to an incomplete record of the early history of Hong Kong, this project begins by collecting and organizing primary sources from various historical documents, such as newspaper databases and memoirs. The principal investigator will analyze this data from historical, cultural, and aesthetic perspectives in order to map a multidimensional picture of urban culture during the 1930s in Hong Kong. These findings will lead to an analysis of the intersection of city life, writers, and the aesthetics of modern fiction. Finally, this study will explore the literary and cultural relationship between Hong Kong and Shanghai in the 1930s. It will compare the similarities and differences between the two cities to tease out the trajectory of Hong Kong’s development as a modern city. The output from this research project entails 4-5 scholarly articles published in refereed journals, and the publication of an academic monograph.

23501215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23501215.value: Economists have devoted substantial effort to studying how to promote innovation as it is the main engine of long-term economic growth. The effect of competition on innovation has been one of the central questions in these studies. The existing literature has mainly considered the case in which the quality of an innovation is exogenous and patentable. However, there are many situations in which innovating firms can choose the quality of targeted innovations. For example, to develop a new mainframe computer, a firm can choose to devote R&D resources to marginally improve existing chip architectures or to develop a substantially faster speed new chip. In addition, an innovation may not be always patentable since an essential requirement for an invention to be patentable is that it must be non-obvious. In other words, to be eligible for patent protection, the quality of an innovation has to be sufficiently high. Thus, the strictness of patentability requirements can affect firms' choice of innovation quality. The proposed research project departs from the existing literature to consider the possibility that innovating firms can choose the quality of their targeted innovations. In particular, I will study how the interplay between the strength of patent protection and the degree of competition affects the choice of innovation quality and consequently, determines the incentive to innovate and welfare. To this end, I will develop a theoretical model and conduct an economic analysis. The preliminary analysis suggests that the traditional understanding of the effect of competition on innovation may not be complete once the choice of innovation quality is taken into consideration. The main twist is that an increased competition may, under some circumstances, induce innovating firms to choose lower quality innovations and thus, negatively affect the overall innovation incentive and social welfare. This research project will aim to contribute to the literature by providing a new piece of economic analysis on the joint effect of patent protection and competition on innovation, an important topic in the economics of innovation that has received little attention. The research project will also aim to derive testable results on the relationship between market competition and innovation quality, to shed lights on the recent debates on the effects of declining patent quality, and to offer some practical suggestions for the optimal design of patent system. 經濟學家投入大量的精力去研究如何激勵創新因為創新是長期經濟增長的主要動力。創新經濟學中一個中心問題是競爭如何影響創新。已有的文獻主要集中研究創新程度是固定的和可獲得專利保護的情況。但是，在許多情況中創新公司是可以選擇創新程度。而且創新不一定能獲得專利保護因為創新要符合非顯然的條件才能獲得專利保護。換句話説，創新程度要足夠大才能符合受專利保護的要求。所以，獲得專利保護要求的創新程度會影響公司對創新程度的選擇。 申請的研究計劃与現有的文獻不同在於本計劃考慮了創新公司可以選擇創新程度的假設。具體的説，我研究專利保護和競爭如何共同影響創新程度的選擇，從而影響創新的誘因和社會福利。為了達到這個目標，我建立了一個經濟理論模型并進行了分析。初步結果顯示在競爭如何影響創新的傳統研究未必完整如果我們加入考慮創新程度的選擇。主要的原因是增加競爭可能使得創新公司選擇較低程度低創新，從而降低了創新的誘因和社會福利。 本研究計劃希望能提供一份新的經濟分析到已有的文獻。本計劃也希望能得到可驗證的定量結果，提出新的觀點到最近熱烈討論中專利質量的話題和提供關於最有專利設計的實際建議。

23501215.label: Realisation of objectives
23501215.value: To achieve objective 1, we have developed a theoretical model to study the effect of patent protection on innovating firms' equilibrium choice of innovation quality or direction. Specifically, firms in the model can conduct R&D in a safe and a risky direction with different innovation sizes or qualities. An increase in patent protection or patentability standards will influence the static and dynamic incentives for the new entrants to conduct R&D. Regarding objective 2, we have shown that as patent protection rises the rate of industry innovation initially increases and eventually decreases. Thus, more intensive market competition has a non-monotonic impact on the rate of industry innovation. To achieve objective 3, we have shown in a theoretical model that compared to the social optimum, market incentives for innovation are deficient. Thus, an increase in competition measured by the number of entrants generally benefits society. Regarding objective 4, our theoretical results suggest that raising patentability standards may indeed improve innovation direction. In particular, R&D is biased toward (against) the risky direction under the low (higher) patent standards. Moreover, if the quality improvement required to be granted a patent is determined and depends on the current technology state of the industry (as in some countries), firms have higher (lower) incentives to invest in the risky (safe) direction than under the fixed patentability policy. Thus, our results suggest that the patent protection should be further strengthened if patent policy is state-dependent. Finally, our findings indicate that the desirable patentability requirement could be lower in developing countries to promote innovation.

23501215.label: Major findings and research outcome
23501215.value: The research project has provided framework to study how patent policy may impact the rate and direction of cumulative innovation when firms have multiple options in R&D intensities and direction choices. We found that patentability standards affect the rate of industry innovation through both the number of entrants and their R&D intensities in the free entry equilibrium. As patentability standard rises the rate of industry innovation initially increases and eventually decreases. Moreover, compared to the social optimum, market incentives for cumulative innovation are deficient for both R&D intensities and the number of entrants. Furthermore, there exists a critical level of patentability standard under which the innovation direction is efficient. If patentability is the only policy variable available, then the optimal policy, which balances the trade-off between the rate and direction of innovation, will in general be different from the one that maximizes social welfare. Our research findings have been presented in high-quality workshops and conferences such as Biennial Conference of Hong Kong Economic Association, Hong Kong Economic Association (Hong Kong, 2016) and International Conference on Government Regulation and Policy (Hangzhou, 2016). The research paper generated from this project has been published in International Economic Review, a top general-interest journal in economics.

23501215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23501215.value: One potential direction for further development of the research is to consider asymmetric market power of innovators. Specifically, one can develop a more general model to incorporate the possible actions taken by dominating firms such as incumbents in markets. Though the analysis will become more complicated, we believe that a tractable but flexible model can be developed to address some interesting questions that have not been answered yet. We will continue to explore this direction building upon our current existing works.

23501215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23501215.value: Economists have devoted substantial effort to studying how to promote innovation since it is the main driving force of long-term economic growth. The effect of competition on innovation has been a central question in economics of innovation. The existing literature mainly focuses the case where the size for an innovation is exogenous and patentable. The research project has departed from the existing literature to consider the possibility that innovating firms have options of choosing the size for their targeted innovations. The research project has contributed to the literature by providing a new piece of economic analysis on the patent protection and innovation. The research project has also derived some testable results on the relationship between patent protection and the rate of innovation, to shed lights on the recent debate on the effects of declining patent quality, and to offer some practical suggestions to the optimal design of patent system.

23601015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601015.value: My research analyzes how U.S. power shaped international human-rights initiatives after 1945. During the ECS grant period, I will investigate the connections between human rights and American efforts to stimulate the growth of media infrastructure and media access in the decolonizing world in the late 1950s and 1960s. In this transitional geopolitical moment, diverse American actors argued that an individual’s capacity to access mass media—newspapers, radio, films, and, increasingly, television—formed the material basis for the enjoyment of rights. Without mass access, they argued, ordinary citizens could not enjoy their right to information, which had been inscribed in the United Nations’ Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948. The project will connect their promotion of information freedoms to contemporaneous development initiatives intended to expand U.S. power abroad, including the world’s first satellite-broadcasting system and English-language teaching outside of U.S. borders. Much existing historiography has approached human rights from legal and diplomatic perspectives, focusing on the development of international human-rights instruments in the 1940s and on the political activism of non-governmental organizations in the 1970s. These emphases lead many historians to underplay the U.S. government’s promotion of specific human-rights policies as a means of waging global cold war—policies echoed in the post-Cold War calls for a “right to internet access” supported by Washington. My project expands the field of human-rights historiography by analyzing how U.S. freedom-of-information policies shaped social research, media cultures, and global language politics across the postwar decades. The project also contributes to an emerging body of scholarship that connects political and economic power to embodied language practices: I show how U.S. initiatives designed to stimulate cross-border media exchange bolstered English’s stature as a global lingua franca after 1945. These archival contributions will recast our understanding of postwar human rights, bringing 1950s and 1960s media-development initiatives back into focus. The research is international in scope. As a doctoral candidate, I conducted substantial archival work in Europe for my dissertation. An ECS grant will provide a key means of gathering materials from U.S.-based archives that I did not have the chance to access while preparing my dissertation (which I submitted in July of 2014). It will fund two semesters of archival research at five collections in the United States, discussed in more detail in my research statement. I aim to secure a book contract with a major university press by the end of the grant period. 我的研究分析1945年後美國的權力怎樣塑造和影響了國際人權的倡議 。 在ECS 的撥款時期中，我將調查一九五十年代末和一九六十年代，國際人權和美國各種刺激非殖民國家的媒體基建發展和媒體接觸的關係。在這個地緣政治的過渡期，不同的美國演員均主張個人與媒體的接觸 - 如報紙，電台，電影，和電視 –形成享受人權的基礎。 他們覺得如普通市民不能接觸大眾媒體，就不能獲得列明在1948聯合國世界人權宣言中的享用資訊自由的權利 。這個計劃將連接資訊自由的推廣，以同時發展計劃擴展美國海外勢力的行為，包括建立世界第一個衛星廣播系統和提倡英語教育。 現存的史學多從法律或外交角度研究人權發展史， 如集中看一九四十年代國際人權發展 的法例，和非政府組織於一九七十年代推行的各樣政治運動。 這些重點均令許多歷史學家忽略了美國政府從推廣特定的人權政策來發動全球性冷戰的角色 - 同類型政策如 “進接互聯網的權利”也在後冷戰時期被華府所擁護。 我的計劃將從考察美國資訊自由政策怎樣在戰後時期影響和塑造社會研究，媒體文化，和國際語言政治，而擴闊人權歷史學的領域。這個計劃同時有貢獻於新興有關政治，經濟權力和語言體現實踐的學術研究：我將顯示美國於1945後刺激跨邊界媒體交流的各種倡議均有加強英語作為國際通用語言的成果。這些存檔的貢獻將改寫我們對於戰後人權狀況的理解，更把焦點重新集中於一九五十和一九六十年代媒體發展的各項倡議。 我研究的範疇是國際性的。作為博士學生的時候，我在歐洲為論文進行了不少檔案的研究。ECS的撥款將提供一個寶貴機會給我在美國的資料庫中搜尋之前未有機會接觸的資料 (因我在2014年7月已提交博士論文)。它會資助我在美國五個不同的資料庫中做檔案研究，詳情在研究陳述中有更詳細的討論。我的目標是在最後撥款期前得到一份主要大學出版社的書約。

23601015.label: Realisation of objectives
23601015.value: All of the original project objectives have been completed or are nearly completed. • Objectives 1 & 2 will be met with the publication of my book manuscript, Barriers Down: Freedom of Information and American Power, by Columbia University Press in spring/summer 2019. In my initial ECS application, my goal was to secure a contract with a top-tier international publisher by the end of the grant period, which I have done. The manuscript has been peer reviewed and is essentially finished, apart from some light revisions which I will finish in summer 2018. The board of Columbia UP recently approved my revisions plan and will not require the manuscript to be sent out for review again. In addition, I offered a brief sketch of the ideas outlined in Objectives 1 & 2 in the chapter I co-authored (50%) for the Routledge Companion to Media and Human Rights, “History of Media and Human Rights,” which was published in 2017. • Objectives 3 & 4 were met by the publication of my article, “‘The Universal Language of the Future’: Decolonization, Development, and the American Embrace of Global English, 1945-1965,” in the Cambridge UP journal Modern Intellectual History in 2017; and by the submission of my chapter “The End of Empires and Some Linguistic Turns: British and French Language Policies in Inter- and Post-war Africa,” which will appear in an edited volume currently under contract with Palgrave Macmillan. • Objectives 5 & 6 will be completed with the publication of my book manuscript (see above).

23601015.label: Major findings and research outcome
23601015.value: Major findings of the project can be grouped under three broad themes: international efforts to facilitate the spread of television as a development tool; the United States’ role in the emergence of satellite broadcasting; and American efforts to bolster the status of English as a global vehicular language. At the Lyndon Baines Johnson Presidential Library in Austin, Texas, I consulted governmental records—including many previously classified documents—on U.S. satellite policies in the 1960s. These resources provided a detailed picture of the U.S. pursuit of a single global satellite broadcasting system that was intended to provide service to the entire Western bloc. They also illuminated American anxieties about the emergence of competing satellite systems. In addition, the LBJ Library collections revealed the United States’ role in the installation of television service in Vietnam, which it pursued as a tool of both warfare and development during the Vietnam War. These materials are used extensively in chapters four, five, and seven of my book manuscript. At the Rockefeller Archive Center (which houses the Rockefeller and Ford foundation collections) in Sleepy Hollow, New York, and the Frank Laubach Collection in Syracuse, New York, my research yielded documents that showed how private American foundations and actors worked with the U.S. state on development projects in Asia, Africa, and Latin America, particularly relating to the spread of English abroad. These resources informed my article for Modern Intellectual History; my chapter for the Palgrave Macmillan edited volume; and chapter three of my book manuscript. Relevant documents from the Rockefeller Archive Center also related to private foundation involvement in Cold War mass-communication research; these were used in chapter two of the book manuscript. My research at the Henry Cassirer Papers at the University of Texas at Austin centered on efforts to use broadcasting as a development tool in the developing world in the post-1945 era. The papers of Cassirer, a naturalized U.S. citizen and UNESCO official, provided an important counterpoint to other development policymakers and experts featured in my book manuscript. I made extensive use of the Cassirer Papers in chapter four of my book manuscript. More details about the research outputs for these findings are listed above (in section 5.3) and in Part C of this report.

23601015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23601015.value: The main action still to be taken is to complete revisions on my book manuscript, which I will do in late summer 2018. Again, the manuscript is already contracted and Columbia UP’s board has approved my revisions plan, so I do not anticipate any major obstacles to its publication in spring/summer 2019. This will conclude Objectives 1, 2, 5, and 6. Regarding Objectives 4 and 5: In the process of researching American, British, and French investments in language education in the late colonial and early postcolonial eras, I have discovered a surprising lack of historiography in this area and exciting archival and intellectual possibilities for pursuing further research. I present a greatly expanded and refined discussion of these possibilities in my current GRF application, which focuses on the emergence of the field of applied linguistics in the United States and Europe after 1945.

23601015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23601015.value: This research project demonstrates various ways in which post-1945 American policymakers embraced government action in order to enhance global information flows. The hand of government became especially visible in the 1960s, when President Kennedy and the United Nations announced a global “Development Decade” designed to promote socioeconomic growth in Asia, Africa, and Latin America. Under presidents Kennedy and Johnson, the United States helped to fund educational television in places ranging from Colombia to Nigeria to American Samoa. It encouraged the construction of ground stations for satellite reception across the developing world. It funded efforts overseas to spread and institutionalize the English language. In publications stemming from research at collections including the Lyndon Baines Johnson Presidential Library, the Rockefeller Foundation archives, and the Ford Foundation archives, I show how international information flows were shaped by U.S. policymaking and diplomacy in the second half of the twentieth century.

23601615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601615.value: Income inequality has risen drastically around the world in the past decades including in the United States, Hong Kong, and mainland China. The research study proposed here will investigate the reactions of the general public towards extremely high salaries and extremely high business incomes in three geographies: Hong Kong, mainland China, and the United States. Given previous research documenting the American belief in economic individualism and the free market, few people expected large numbers of Americans to show strong disapproval of income inequality prior to the Occupy Wall Street movement. However, American discontent with extremely high income inequality has been severe and has led to policy changes to curb runaway income inequality and financial instability at the top. Even more heavy-handed measures such as bonus caps were recently enacted in the European Union in response to public discontent with income inequality. It is therefore important to examine the attitudes of the general public towards issues such as income inequality because of their potential implications for public discontent and even social unrest. The research proposed here will investigate how people in Hong Kong and mainland China are reacting to the extremely high levels of income inequality that we observe today at the top levels of the income distribution. This study is motivated by and will build directly on previous research conducted by the principal investigator (PI). The PI’s previous works have examined the reactions of the general public to extremely high salaries in the United States. The proposed new study will use data from large-scale population-based survey experiments to address the following questions a) What are the reactions of people living in Hong Kong and mainland China to very high incomes (both salaries and business incomes)? b) How do these reactions compare with those of the American public? c) What are the determinants of these reactions in these three geographies? d) How do the determinants of these attitudes differ in these three geographies? 在過去數十年間，收入不均在全球各地包括美國、香港以及中國，都有加劇的趨勢。本研究將針對香港、中國及美國地區，探討大眾對於地區內極高薪及極高營業收入的看法。 有鑑於以往一些關於美國人信奉經濟個人主義及自由市場的研究，在佔領華爾街之前，小數人會预料到有大量美國人對收入不均表達強烈不滿。事實上，美國人對於極端收入不均的不滿已經十分嚴重，亦導致國家改變政策來控制收入不均與其所引申的問題。歐盟地區更制定嚴厲的措施例如設置獎金上限以回應民眾對於收入不均的不滿。由此可見，瞭解大眾對於收入不均的看法和態度十分重要，因為它們對民眾不滿甚至社會動盪等現象都有潛在的影響。本研究將探討香港及中國大陸民眾對於在收入分佈最高層觀察到的極端收入不均之看法。本次研究是受到首席研究員過去的相關研究所啓發，並將以此為基礎。首席研究員過去曾探討美國民眾對於當地極高收入的看法，而這次擬議的新研究將使用基於人口抽樣的問卷調查去探討以下4個問題 : a)香港及中國的居民對於當地極度高收入（包括高薪及高營業收入）有什麽看法？ b)這些看法跟美國民眾的看法對比起來是怎樣的？ c)影響此三地民眾對於高收入看法的決定因素是什麽？ d)民眾態度的決定因素在此三地有何差異？

23601615.label: Realisation of objectives
23601615.value: As described in my grant proposal, I designed and conducted a total of five population-based survey experiments in partnership with the survey company YouGov. Of these five survey-experiments, one was conducted with a sample of the United States (N= 1,170), two with samples from Hong Kong (N= 1,170 and N= 1,239), and two from mainland China (N=1,170 and N=1,235). As mentioned in my project objectives, these studies and their resulting papers aim to contribute to the literature primarily in distributive justice and the moral economy. The data sets resulting from this project are uniquely suitable for investigations of what moves evaluations of extremely high pay. In other words, among others, these data are well-suited to address the question: what factors and considerations lead members of the general public, in these three societies, to think that a given extremely high pay is fair or unfair, right or wrong, too much or too little? Previous work points to a variety of possible factors and considerations which may move attitudes toward extremely high pay (specifically, executive pay and entrepreneurial income). Among others, some of the key factors and considerations which move attitudes and which my work focused on during this period are the following: the financial performance of a company, the company’s contribution to the job market (in the form of job creation or layoffs), entrepreneurship, beliefs related to a free market ideology, beliefs about the roles of management and teamwork in a large company, beliefs about the existence of equal opportunity, beliefs about the closeness of the interests of high and low-income groups, and beliefs about the degree to which inequality is seen as problematic. More broadly, the resulting datasets include causal factors (i.e. experimental variables), attitudinal measures, open-ended qualitative items, demographic characteristics of respondents, as well as manipulation checks and attention checks for the experimental conditions. Before being fielded, these survey-experiments were pretested to minimize any errors, based on previous work on survey-experiment methodology (e.g. Dillman et al. 2014, Alvarez and Brehm 2002, Tourangeau et al. 2000, Weisberg et al. 1996). The data resulting from these studies are carefully documented by myself and YouGov’s team. The data are well-matched to address the questions and objectives of this study, and this is why I am indicating in the section below entitled “Summary of objectives,” that the objectives of the study have been achieved at the 100% level. I would like to note, however, that while three papers using these data are already under review, more work will be completed in terms of analyses and publication, especially with regard to a three-society comparison (please see more on this below). Currently, I have three manuscripts using these data under review in international and well-established peer-reviewed sociology journals. I am also beginning to write a fourth manuscript, to be sent out for review, using these data. Please see the below section for some of the major findings from this project thus far. Smyth and Leah Melani Christian. 2014. Internet, Phone, Mail, and Mixed-Mode Surveys: The Tailored Design Method. Wiley. Tourangeau, Roger, Lance J. Rips, and Kenneth Rasinski. 2000. The Psychology of Survey Response. Cambridge University Press. Weisberg, H., Krosnick, J.A. and Bowen, B.D., 1996. An introduction to survey research, polling, and data analysis. Sage.

23601615.label: Major findings and research outcome
23601615.value: All three of the following papers are currently under review at sociology journals: The first of my papers based on these data is a manuscript entitled, “Explaining Attitudes toward Executive Pay: Evidence from a Survey Experiment.” I invited Erin Cumberworth of Stanford University’s Center on Poverty and Inequality as my co-author for this paper. This paper uses data from the United States to examine whether people would agree that a given extremely high amount of pay is too high or too low, fair or unfair, and right or wrong if they could be more certain than typically possible regarding a high-income earner’s contributions. One of the major findings from the data is that there aren’t significant divisions across political ideologies and across political parties in attitudes, beyond the effects of the predispositions and beliefs mentioned in the previous section. These findings are highly relevant in the U.S. context where much of the literature shows divides in attitudes across political ideologies and parties. This paper was presented, using conference funds from this ECS grant, in August 2017 during the International Sociological Association’s Research Committee 28 (RC28) conference at Columbia University. The paper was well-received by the audience and the chair of the session. The second of these papers is entitled, “What Moves Evaluations of Executive Pay? Evidence from Survey Experiments in Mainland China and Hong Kong.” For this paper, I invited Jin Jiang from Lingnan University as my co-author. Previous work in the field shows that Chinese people are broadly accepting of inequality. The literature on attitudes toward inequality in China guides this paper as the paper offers an examination of possible sources of such acceptance of inequality and how these sources move attitudes. In contrast to previous work in the field which looks more generally at inequality, this study finds that we can at best describe attitudes toward extremely high incomes as tolerant but not as accepting. The paper offers a two-society comparison and consistently documents much higher levels of acceptance of extremely high pay in the mainland China sample in comparison with the Hong Kong sample. The third of my papers is entitled, “Attribution of Executive Pay: How Ordinary People View Extremely High Pay.” Long-standing research from the U.S. shows that people tend to explain wealth with individual (i.e. merited or justified) reasons. This paper uses qualitative data from an open-ended item in the U.S. survey-experiment to bring those data to bear on the question of whether this finding from previous work (i.e. that individual explanations prevail) stands when we turn our attention to extremely high incomes. The study finds that respondents turn to structural, not individual, reasons when making sense of extremely high pay and argues that a different set of justice principles drives evaluations of extremely high pay than what drives evaluations of ordinary levels of pay.

23601615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23601615.value: As mentioned above, I am currently continuing to analyze these data with the aim of preparing a fourth manuscript. Based on my current plan, this manuscript will focus on the distributive justice principles people use to evaluate the pay of ordinary positions (i.e. that of an ordinary employee in the sales department of a large company) in comparison with how they evaluate the pay of top positions (i.e. that of a CEO). For example, does effort (operationalized in my ECS data as work hours) count in pay evaluations as much for a CEO as it does for a salesperson? If not, what other factors and considerations are salient in evaluating each case? Among other factors, this paper will also consider how these evaluations vary with the gender of the earner in question. In terms of future development, these studies (detailed earlier) shaped in ways that led me to form a new collaboration, with Prof. Katherine Weisshaar of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. In collaboration with her, I am now beginning a related new line of work stemming from the projects supported by my ECS grant.

23601615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23601615.value: Previous work shows that rising inequality, as experienced in the U.S., Hong Kong, and mainland China is due, besides other sources and in important part, to a rise in top incomes in the past decades. Theoretical and conceptual guidance for this project comes from the literatures in distributive justice and the moral economy. Scholars in these fields have argued that how people justify inequalities will determine the trajectory of inequality in the future. As scholars in this field have pointed out and as I mentioned in my proposal, although we know a great deal about the rise in income inequality in many countries around the world, we know comparatively far less about how the general public is reacting to that rise in inequality. This project responds to that necessity of understanding what the general public thinks about extremely high pay and what factors and considerations move their attitudes toward top incomes. The study features five population-based survey experiments, one conducted in the United States, two in Hong Kong, and two in mainland China. The survey-experiments are conducted in partnership with the survey company YouGov.

23601815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601815.value: My proposed research concerns two distinct but related issues. The first concerns the idea in moral philosophy that what we ought to do is explained by reasons. The idea is that in standard choice situations, there will be a variety of important considerations that provide reasons to do a variety of incompatible acts and the act that ought to be done is the act which “wins out in the competition among these reasons”. A simple but serious challenge for this theory is to say what it is to “win out in the competition among reasons”. Though there are many aspects of this challenge, I will focus on one issue: sometimes we can have two reasons to do an act and their strengths add up so that the strength of support for doing the act is somehow the sum of the strengths of the reasons individually. In order to develop a systematic theory of how these cases work, I will do two things. First I will determine whether all cases in which we have two reasons to do an act involve this kind of addition (they do not) and develop a theory of exactly which cases do. Second, I will consider what sense can be made of adding strengths of reasons. Addition involves numbers so adding the strengths of reasons presupposes that strength are numerically measurable. Philosophers of science and mathematicians have developed so-called measurement theory which allows for rigorous analysis of whether and how a quantity can be numerically measured. I aim to apply these resources to study the strength of reasons. The second half of my research concerns the structure of reasoning. In earlier work, I argued that reasoning about which acts we have reason to perform displays a certain non-transitive structure. During the term of this grant, I plan to explore this question from an abstract perspective. There are two main tasks. First, there is the philosophical question about what is it about the nature of reasoning that can explain why good reasoning has a non-transitive structure. Answering this question requires engaging with the rich literature in epistemology on so-called ampliative inference (such as, e.g., inductive inference). Second, there is the more formal task of providing a general model of this kind of non-transitive reasoning. This requires engaging with work in computer science and logic that formally models reasoning. 研究題目：理據及推理的結構 本研究關注兩個不同但相關的議題。第一個議題有關道德哲學中的一個觀點。該觀點認為應做的行為之所以應該，可由背後的理據來解釋。它的意思是指在一般需要作出抉擇的情況下，通常有眾多不兼容的選項，其背後都有重要的考量為其提供不同的行事理據，而應做的行為就是「綜合考慮所有理據後勝出的那個」。 現有一個對這個理論簡單而嚴重的挑戰，就是甚麼為之「綜合考慮所有理據後勝出。雖然此項挑戰包含很多不同的面向，筆者會專注於一個問題：有些時候我們有兩個支持某一個行為的理據，而這兩個理據的力度似乎可以相加，以至於該行為被支持的強度是兩個理據分別支持該行為的力度之和。 為了建立一套理論來探究以上這類情況，筆者會進行兩項工作。第一，筆者會探討是否所有存在兩個支持某行為的理據的情況下都牽涉此種相加性(筆者認為不是)，繼而建立一個理論來刻畫有此相加性的個案。第二，筆者會考察如何理解把理據的力度相加。加法牽涉數字的運用，能將兩個理據的力度相加已假定了它們能被數字化地計量。科學哲學家和數學家建立了一套所謂的測度理論，用以嚴格分析某一個性質能否及如何被量化。筆者打算運用這些現存的理論資源來進行理據的力度的研究。 本研究的第二部份有關推理的結構。筆者在較早的研究中提出了在思考哪些行為是有理可依時，此種推理展示出非傳遞的結構。在本研究中筆者打算從一個抽象的角度來探究這個問題。 本課題有兩個主要的任務。第一是回答一個哲學問題：如何以推理的本質來解釋為何好的推理有其非傳遞的結構？而回答這個問題時需牽涉知識論中關於擴展式推論（比如歸納推理）的豐富文獻；第二是提供一個涵蓋更廣的非傳遞性推理的形式模型。此項工作需牽涉電腦科學及邏輯學中關於推理模型的相關研究及著作。

24100015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24100015.value: 節肢動物構成世界上>80％的動物物種，當中的成員包括昆蟲，甲殼類（蝦，蟹，龍蝦），多足類（蜈蚣千足蟲和），和螯肢亞門（蟎蟲，蝎子，蜘蛛，馬蹄蟹）。它們的發育過程是通過精確地控制它們獨有的荷爾蒙系統 -由三異戊二烯單位組成的倍半萜類激素。倍半萜類激素，例如金合歡酸甲酯和幼激素已被證明分別調節在非昆蟲節肢動物和昆蟲的發育和繁殖過程的激素。這些合成非昆蟲節肢動物金合歡酸甲酯和昆蟲幼激素的最後步驟都是合成速度的決定步驟，並取決於保幼激素甲基（JHAMT)產生的酶。 以前研究倍半萜生物合成的調控包括：(1) 調查有限物種範圍，從而阻礙我們得出基本和普遍的結論，和 (2) 儘管微RNA在生物學的許多方面獲得廣泛重視，已知可以調控節肢動物倍半萜類激素的微RNA仍然缺乏。 根據我們的初步分析，我們已經成功地確定了幾個微RNA能夠調控不同的昆蟲和甲殼類動物的保幼激素甲基。我們的假說是，這些微RNA能調節所有的節肢動物的保幼激素甲基和倍半萜生物合成。在這個項目中，我們將測試1）這些微RNA是否能夠調節非昆蟲/甲殼類節肢動物保幼激素甲基; 和2）這些微RNA如何在果蠅相互作用和調節保幼激素甲基。 該項目將在節肢動物調控倍半萜類生產的微RNA提供有價值的新見解，以及這些微RNA是如何能在體內調節保幼激素甲基。了解節肢動物倍半萜類的生產調控將是未來必要的發展和應用，如提高水產養殖產量和打擊農業害蟲，也將更好地了解這個世界最大的動物組激素調節的演變。

24100015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24100015.value: The phylum Arthropoda contains the majority of terrestrial and aquatic animal species, including insects, crustaceans (e.g. shrimp, crab, lobster), chelicerates (e.g. spider, horseshoe crab, scorpion), and myriapods (e.g. centipede and millipede). Understanding their evolution is therefore a central question in biology. Hormones sesquiterpenoids control the arthropods’ development, reproduction, novel behavior such as eusociality, and morphological structures such as wing development. Therefore, differential regulation of biosynthesis and actions of sesquiterpenoids plays an important role in the evolution of arthropod morphology and adaptation to diverse habitats. However, the precise roles noncoding RNAs such as microRNAs, previously thought of as junk, play during these processes were unknown. This project has identified, for the first time, a set of microRNAs that interact and control sesquiterpenoid hormonal pathway genes in different arthropods. This provides convincing evidence that noncoding RNAs regulation of sesquiterpenoid hormones was an established mechanism in the last common ancestor of arthropods 530 million years ago. In addition, as hormonal pathways are major targets for the development of new approaches to agricultural pest management, disease vector control, preserving or promoting endangered species, and improvements in aquaculture productivity, this study provides new strategy for using microRNAs in designing specific candidates for arthropod control.

24101015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24101015.value: Members of the Roseobacter clade constitute a monophyletic Alphaproteobacteria lineage with a maximum divergence of 11% in their 16S rRNA gene sequences. They are primarily found in the ocean, both free-living and particle/phytoplankton-associated. In some coastal waters, 1 in 5 bacterial cells is a member of the Roseobacter clade. They are major players in marine carbon and sulfur cycles and in climatically active gas production. Roseobacters are also dominant bacteria associated with various economically important marine plants and animals, causing physiological changes of the host. Over 50 genera and nearly 200 species have been described. Because of their large genome sizes, versatile metabolic pathways, and rapid responses to favorable conditions, Roseobacters have been classified as ecological copiotrophs. Recent culture-independent studies, however, showed that oceanic uncultivated Roseobacters have streamlined G+C-poor genomes depleted with genes involved in cell-cell interaction, suggesting that wild Roseobacters parallel to ecological oligotrophs. Because heterotrophic bacterioplankton assimilate and transform >50% of oceanic primary production, these ecological strategies (oligotrophy versus copiotrophy) have global-scale consequences for carbon flux to the atmosphere and sequestration in the deep ocean. This project aims to understand the genomic diversity of uncultivated planktonic Roseobacters. A previous study (Buchan et al., 2005) summarized 13 major lineages of Roseobacters, in which the DC5-80-3 cluster, the NAC11-7 cluster, and the CHAB-I-5 cluster remain largely or exclusively uncultivated. We have collected multiple single cells from each of the 3 lineages, and will sort additional cells from new samples. Partial genomic sequences will be generated using single cell genome sequencing technology. Preliminary analyses showed that these lineages are all monomorphic, leaving a possibility to assemble a nearly complete population genome from multiple partial single cell genomes for each of the 3 lineages. We will analyze their metabolic potential, and compare them with the cultured Roseobacters, and estimate their relative abundance in tropical, temperate and polar ocean waters by analyzing the global ocean metagenomes. We will apply phylogenomic and population genomic approaches to understand the evolutionary mechanisms giving rise to the systematic differences in genome size and G+C content among Roseobacter lineages. This study will allow us to establish a genomic basis of Roseobacter diversity in global ocean waters, understand mechanisms underlying genome streamlining in free-living bacterioplankton, and appreciate their roles in climate change. 玫瑰杆菌在α-变形菌中构成一个单系。其成员之间进化距离在16S rRNA基因序列水平上达到11％。它们是海水中的优势菌群，在某些沿海水域， 5个细菌中就有1个是玫瑰杆菌。经常呈浮游态或者附着在颗粒和浮游植物表面，是海洋碳和硫循环的主要参与者，能产生二甲基硫等活性气体直接影响气候。玫瑰杆菌还是很多海洋植物和动物表面附着微生物群落中的优势菌群，包括大型海藻，珊瑚，海绵，鱿鱼，仔鱼，海胆和牡蛎等。玫瑰杆菌时常作为病原菌或者抗病原菌，对这些具有重要经济价值的海洋生物起作用。 文献中已报导超过50个属200个种的可培养的玫瑰杆菌 。利用前沿的单细胞基因组测序技术，我们获得了多个未培养的玫瑰杆菌的单细胞。对于已经测定基因组的3个单细胞进行了分析，发现它们比可培养的玫瑰杆菌具有更小的基因组，完全不同的碱基组成和显著差异的基因内容构成。此项新的课题申请书提出测定更多的玫瑰杆菌单细胞，对其进行系统的分析找出更多的在基因组水平上的差异，并且结合生态基因组学，系统发育基因组学和群体遗传学等手段对这些多样性的产生机制进行研究。

24101015.label: Major findings and research outcome
24101015.value: We revealed high genomic diversity of uncultivated Roseobacter lineages and the evolutionary mechanisms driving this diversity. First, the uncultivated members of DC5-80-3 collected from iron-limited Southern Ocean show ecotype diversification from the cultured members of this lineage isolated from ocean regions under nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) limitation. They are differentiated in nutrient scavenging and energy conservation strategies. The former carries a dicitrate transport system fecBCDE for iron uptake, whereas the latter possesses high affinity ammonium and phosphate transporters. For energy conservation, only the latter ecotype uses iron-requiring mechanisms including bacteriochlorophyll-a for light acquisition and possesses sox gene cluster for sulfur oxidation, whereas the former ecotype replaces them with the simple proteorhodopsin for light acquisition (Sun et al. 2017. Environ Microbiol). Second, we provided evidence showing that genetic drift, rather than natural selection, drives genome reduction of the uncultivated Roseobacter lineage SAG-O19 (Luo et al. 2017. Nature Microbiol). Another major contribution is that we demonstrated the evolutionary mechanisms giving rise to the high genomic GC content in Roseobacter lineages including most uncultivated members. Since a GC pair uses one more N than an AT pair and since the N use in the genome affects the N use in the proteome, genomes with low GC% are repeatedly postulated as an adaptive strategy for bacteria inhabiting surface oceans. The simplest hypothesis is mutation bias towards high GC%, which was verified using a mutation accumulation experiment on the representative Roseobacter group member Ruegeria pomeroyi DSS-3 followed by whole genome sequencing of the mutant lines (Sun et al. 2017. ISME J). The question remained whether this mutation bias is sufficient to give rise to the GC-rich genome in DSS-3, and what other mechanisms drive its GC% evolution if mutation alone cannot explain it. We quantified the contribution of multiple factors to the change of GC% of DSS-3 using an agent-based genome-scale model. A novel finding is that carbon limitation drives its long-term genome evolution, which differs from the traditional concept that N availability is the key driver of genomic GC% evolution in marine bacteria (Hellweger et al. 2018. ISME J).

24101015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24101015.value: It is generally recognized that the ecological success of the Roseobacter group in various marine habitats is supported by a highly diverse genetic repertoire, including patchy distribution of functional genes, genome size, and genomic GC content. Only the evolutionary mechanisms of genomic GC content were addressed in this completed ECS project. We are planning to study evolution of genome size diversity and functional gene gain and loss in the Roseobacter group. This requires an extension of our existing model to include gene gain and loss and a genome-scale representation of metabolism (using flux balance analysis, FBA). We are currently at a stage of discussing the general ideas with our collaborator Prof. Ferdi Hellweger at TU Berlin.

24101015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24101015.value: The uncultivated members of the Roseobacter group show unexpected large genomic diversity. We provided evidence that genetic drift, rather than natural selection, drives genome reduction of the uncultivated Roseobacter lineage SAG-O19. In the study of DC5-80-3, we found the uncultivated members collected from iron-limited oceans show phylogenetic and metabolic diversification from the cultured members isolated from ocean regions under nitrogen and phosphorus limitation, and the metabolic differences in nutrient scavenging and energy conservation match well with their habitat differences. Another major aspect of genomic diversity is that Roseobacter members including most uncultivated lineages have greater genomic GC content than other prevalent marine bacterial lineages. We developed an evolution theory guided mathematical model and showed that carbon limitation drives their long-term genome evolution, which differs from the traditional concept that N availability is the key driver of genomic GC% evolution in marine bacteria.

24110515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24110515.value: Murine beta cells retain some ability to replicate spontaneously upon injury. However, such an endogenous regenerative capacity of the pancreas is insufficient to overcome the rate of beta cell death/dysfunction during development of diabetes. Emerging studies focus on strategies for inducing beta cell replication and replenishing beta cell mass which are beneficial for both type I and II diabetic patients. Recently, it has been reported that endothelial cells or paracrine factors secreted by them contribute to regeneration of multiple organ systems including the liver, lung, heart and bone marrow. Recruiting or expanding the endogenous pool of endothelial cells may, therefore, promote regeneration and recovery of damaged tissues. Importantly, previous studies have demonstrated that removal of the blood vessel next to the pancreas in frog embryos results in failure of insulin expression; whereas ectopic vascularization in murine posterior foregut leads to ectopic insulin expression. This seminal work suggests a critical role of endothelial cells in beta cell function. Indeed, our preliminary results also show that beta cell replication was accompanied by endothelial cell replication during the embryonic and neonatal stages. Therefore, we hypothesize that recapitulating endothelial cell replication (vascular regeneration) could drive beta cell regeneration following beta cell death. One of the approaches for inducing vascular regeneration following beta cell death is to upregulate local expression of the vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). Recent reports suggest that short-term overexpression of VEGFA in pancreatic islets induces beta cell replication but sustained VEGFA expression has deleterious effect on beta cell survival and function, suggesting the need to finely regulate the duration and dosage of VEGFA expression. Therefore, we propose to use a novel delivery approach in the pancreas via human VEGFA (hVEGF) modified mRNA (modRNA). Our preliminary results reveal that increased formation of blood vessels induced beta cell replication and improved glucose tolerance 28 days post injection of hVEGFA modRNA following beta cell death. Therefore, we propose to study the long-term regenerative capacity of hVEGFA modRNA following beta cell death; as well as the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying hVEGFA modRNA-mediated beta cell regeneration. This proposal will provide new insights into development of hVEGFA modRNA as a therapeutic platform for amplifying the endogenous regenerative potential of pancreatic beta cells in a pre-clinical setting.

24110515.label: Realisation of objectives
24110515.value: We have finished this proposal with completion of all objectives and the work has contributed to publication of 13 journal articles. The main finding has been reported by Lu S et al., Lui KO, Frontiers in Endocrinology, 2017, 8:242. Here, we also show the abstract of the work: Despite the βDTA (Ins2-rtTA; Tet-DTA) mice have been developed as a valuable tool to study β cell regeneration, their individual variation in therapeutic efficacy has not been characterized. Here, we demonstrated that the βDTA mice exhibited significant variations in both spontaneous and acquired β cell regeneration. We found that doxycycline (DOX)-induced β cell death was sufficient to cause polydipsia, translating even subtle difference in drinking habit into large variations in actual DOX intake among individuals within the same group. Accumulating evidence shows that transient expression of VEGFA enhances β cell functional recovery after injury. Therefore, we utilized the chemically modified mRNA (modRNA) technology to enable transient yet efficient VEGFA expression in the pancreas after DOX-induced β cell death. Surprisingly, under optimized DOX dose permissive of β cell regeneration, VEGFA modRNA only demonstrated marginal benefits on β cell functional recovery with large individual variations. We also revealed that the therapeutic efficacy of VEGFA modRNA on β cell regeneration was dependent on the degree of β cell loss induced by the accumulated DOX intake. Therefore, our results highlight a significant contribution of individual variation in the βDTA model and call for attention in evaluating potential efficacy of therapeutic agents in β cell regeneration studies.

24110515.label: Major findings and research outcome
24110515.value: In this study, we revealed that the βDTA mice exhibited significant variations in both spontaneous and acquired β cell regeneration. Such variations could be explained, at least in part, by the subtle difference in individual’s drinking habit and, therefore, DOX intake within the same group, amplified by a positive feedback loop between β cell loss and polydipsia. Furthermore, we also demonstrated that the therapeutic efficacy of VEGFA modRNA in promoting β cell regeneration was sensitive to the initial degree of β cell loss as a result of internal variations in individual’s drinking habit. Since underestimating the internal variations within groups would contribute to biased interpretations as well as the difficulty in reproducing results from β cell regeneration studies, our study emphasized the importance of evaluating individual variations in response to therapeutic agents during β cell regeneration; and addressed the potential source of internal variations using the βDTA model.

24110515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24110515.value: Since we found that VEGFA modRNA offer therapeutic potential in promoting β cell regeneration, we plan to expand this study to include a larger sample size for investigations; and to test the effect of VEGFA modRNA in not only type-1 but also type-2 diabetic mice. Moreover, we will also want to test the efficacy of VEGFA modRNA in larger animal models such as pig. We will apply for additional funding to support these new experiments in the next phase of grant application. Moreover, we have also been collaborating with industry with the hope to generate RNA medicine for the use in human patients in the future.

24110515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24110515.value: In this study, we found that a standard line of research tool (the βDTA mice) has been developed to study β cell regeneration has some intrinsic yet unappreciated issue. For instance, their individual variation in therapeutic efficacy has not been characterized leading to over or underestimation of the therapeutic efficacy of various agents tested using this model. We demonstrated that the βDTA mice exhibited significant variations in both spontaneous and acquired β cell regeneration. We found that doxycycline (DOX) induced β cell death was sufficient to cause polydipsia, translating even subtle difference in drinking habit into large variations in actual DOX intake among individuals within the same group. Accumulating evidence shows that transient expression of VEGFA enhances β cell functional recovery after injury. Therefore, we utilized the chemically modified mRNA (modRNA) technology to enable transient yet efficient VEGFA expression in the pancreas after DOX-induced β cell death. Surprisingly, under optimized DOX dose permissive of β cell regeneration, VEGFA modRNA only demonstrated marginal benefits on β cell functional recovery with large individual variations. We also revealed that the therapeutic efficacy of VEGFA modRNA on β cell regeneration was dependent on the degree of β cell loss induced by the accumulated DOX intake. Nevertheless, since we demonstrated the therapeutic efficacy of VEGFA modRNA in type-1 diabetic mice, we believe that our results give clinically relevant insights into using the clinically proven safe modRNA medicine for the treatment of insulin deficiency in the future by promoting beta cell regeneration. We will perform more follow up studies such as the use of large animal models to confirm the therapeutic efficacy in the near future.

24115815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24115815.value: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), the hepatic manifestation of metabolic syndrome (i.e. obesity, diabetes, insulin resistance and dyslipidemia), is an umbrella term used to describe a spectrum of hepatic pathologies ranging from simple steatosis to steatohepatitis (NASH) in the absence of excess alcohol intake. Epidemiological evidence supports that NASH significantly heightens the risk for cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). With the increasing prevalence of obesity, it is expected that NASH will become an important cause of HCC in coming decades. However, the molecular mechanism by which NASH promotes the development of HCC remains elusive. Lysosome-dependent degradation of lipid through the autophagic pathway is growingly recognized as a crucial mechanism for lipid utilization whereas dysfunctional autophagy may contribute to NASH development. Our preliminary findings suggest that autophagic impairment in NASH is caused by defective lysosome acidification. Specifically, increased levels of asparagine, whose formation is catalyzed by asparagine synthetase, directly interfere with lysosome acidification in hepatocytes. Importantly, such impairment is even more severe in NASH-associated HCC tissues and is associated with oncogenic nuclear factor-κB activation. Based on our preliminary data and the reported tumor-suppressing functions of autophagy, we hypothesize that autophagosomal-lysosomal impairment in NASH-associated HCC could (i) activate nuclear factor-κB signaling through the autophagic substrate p62/SQSTM1; (ii) promote inflammatory microenvironment via inflammasome activation through reduced clearance of damaged, reactive oxygen species-generating mitochondria; (iii) elevate the levels of oncogenic microRNA-224, a known autophagic substrate that targets Smad4. We also propose that targeting asparagine synthetase could restore autophagosomal-lysosomal function, rectify the associated pro-inflammatory/oncogenic signals and reduce tumor burdens in NASH-associated HCC. It is anticipated that findings from this proposed study would not only further our understanding of the molecular pathogenesis of NASH-associated HCC, but also promote the development of novel therapeutic strategies. 非酒精性脂肪肝(NAFLD)又稱非酒精性脂肪性肝病，是一種肝組織學改變與酒精性肝病相類似，但無過量飲酒史的臨床病理綜合征。與肥胖、糖代謝異常、胰島素抵抗和血脂紊亂等代謝性疾病有密切關系。 流行病學研究顯示，非酒精性脂肪肝可加劇肝纖維化和肝癌的疾病進程。隨著肥胖症和代謝綜合征在全球的流行，非酒精性脂肪肝增長迅速且呈低齡化發病趨勢，我們有理由相信非酒精性脂肪肝在未來將成為導致肝癌的重要因素。由於脂肪肝發生發展過程中的具體分子機制尚未被充分闡明,目前臨床上還尚無有效、安全的靶向治療藥物。因此,脂肪肝致病機制的揭示及新型藥物研究和開發多年來一直為世界性醫藥領域研究的熱點。最新研究顯示，自噬-溶酶體系統介導的“脂噬”在脂質代謝和利用中發揮重要作用，因此非酒精性脂肪肝的發生可能與自噬功能的失調相關。 申請者前期研究發現:非酒精性脂肪肝中自噬功能的失調可能與溶酶體酸化功能損傷相關，主要顯示為天冬氨酸水平明顯增加；在非酒精性脂肪肝相關的肝癌組織，這種溶酶體酸化功能的損傷中則更加嚴重，並與原癌基因NF-KB的激活相關。基於前期研究結果及自噬在腫瘤組織中被抑制的現像，我們認為：非酒精性脂肪肝相關性肝癌中自噬－溶酶體通路損傷可能以下幾點相關（i）自噬底物p62/SQSTM1的累積會導致NF-κb信號通路的激活；(ii) 線粒體損傷並引起內質網應激反應，使活性氧在機體內不斷累積，從而抑制炎症小體，激活炎症微環境; (iii)靶向性的激活Smad4的原癌基因microRNA-224表達水平。我們期望通過靶向天冬酰胺合成酶，從而激活自噬-溶酶體系統，促進脂質代謝，抑制相關的促炎／原癌信號，降低非酒精性脂肪肝誘發肝癌的幾率。本研究將不僅揭示自噬在非酒精性脂肪肝相關性肝癌的發病機制，同時為新的干預、治療方案提供科學依據。

24115815.label: Realisation of objectives
24115815.value: Autophagic impairment is implicated in nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) and its associated hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but the molecular mechanism is unclear. We found that autophagic flux was significantly inhibited in 3 murine models of NAFLD. Interestingly, the number of acidic organelles and the level of mature cathepsin D were reduced, suggesting defective lysosome acidification. Asparagine synthetase (ASNS) was induced by endoplasmic reticulum stress, leading to the generation of asparagine, which inhibited lysosome acidification. Both steatotic- and asparagine-treated hepatocytes showed reduced lysosomal acidity and retention of lysosomal calcium. Knockdown of ASNS in steatotic hepatocytes restored autophagic flux. As a potential biomarker, increased serum p62/sequestosome 1 (SQSTM1) level was an independent risk factor for patients with steatosis and lobular inflammation. Nevertheless, targeting relevant events failed to prevent NAFLD-HCC in animals. This might happen as a result of suboptimal ablation of ASNS, p62/SQSTM1, NLPR3 or miR-224 by shRNA during protracted process of NAFLD-HCC formation. To extend the therapeutic utility of autophagy modulation in NAFLD, we also investigated the effects of polydatin, a natural precursor of resveratrol and a known autophagy modulator in other biological context, in a murine nutritional model of non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) and a cell line model of steatosis. Results showed that oral administration of polydatin protected against hepatic lipid accumulation and alleviated inflammation and hepatocyte damage in db/db mice fed methionine-choline deficient diet. Polydatin also alleviated palmitic acid‐induced lipid accumulation in cultured hepatocytes. In both models, polydatin restored lysosomal function and autophagic flux that were impaired by NASH or steatosis. Mechanistically, polydatin inhibited mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) signalling and up-regulated the expression and activity of the transcription factor EB (TFEB), a known master regulator of lysosomal function. In conclusion, polydatin ameliorated NASH through restoring autophagic flux. The polydatin-regulated autophagy was associated with inhibition of mTOR pathway and restoration of lysosomal function by TFEB. Our study provided affirmative preclinical evidence to inform future clinical trials for examining the potential anti-NASH effect of polydatin in humans.

Lysosomal acidification was disrupted by asparagine catalyzed by ASNS whose knockdown abolished autophagic flux in NASH (Figure 6 of Research Output 2); 5. 24115815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24115815.value: Our study supported the clinical significance of serum p62/SQSTM1 as a biomarker for identifying patients with steatosis and steatohepatitis. Validation of this marker in larger cohort is necessary to translate this discovery into clinical benefit. We also provided useful animal efficacy data and mechanistic insights to inform future clinical trials for examining the potential anti-NASH effect of polydatin in humans.

24115815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24115815.value: In summary, we demonstrated that defective lysosome acidification underlies impaired autophagic flux in the evolution of nutritional steatohepatitis, which could be attributed to the increased synthesis of asparagine by ASNS upon ER stress. The latter could further exacerbate autophagic impairment, resulting in hepatic cell death and liver damage in the pathogenesis of nutritional steatohepatitis. Improving lysosome acidification and inhibiting ASNS might be alternative therapeutic strategies for these patients. Serum p62/SQSTM1 is also a potential noninvasive biomarker for identifying patients with nutritional steatohepatitis. Our study further showed that the herbal compound polydatin could exert its therapeutic effect in nutritional steatohepatitis by up-regulating the transcription factor TFEB and subsequently restoring the lysosomal clearance of autophagosomes.
