24305115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24305115.value: This project aims at expanding the frontier of min-max theory in geometry and its applications in topology and mathematical physics. Min-max theory is a variational method to construct unstable stationary solutions for nonlinear problems naturally arising from geometry and physics. An outstanding example of such a solution is minimal surfaces, which provide physical models for soap films. Min-max theory can be used to build up a general framework to find these interesting objects in nature, especially in situations where minimizers fail to exist. The geometric and analytic properties of such special objects give much information about the underlying space. For example, minimal surfaces have been a useful tool in the study of three-manifold topology and mathematical relativity. In this project, the PI aims at achieving a deeper understanding of the geometric and analytic aspects of min-max theory of minimal surfaces (and minimal submanifolds) in general ambient spaces. We study the connections between the topology and Morse index of such minimal surfaces and the geometry of the underlying spaces. This could bring substantial progress in the understanding of spaces with positive curvatures. We also expand these ideas to other geometric constructions such as free boundary minimal surfaces, constant mean curvature surfaces and self shrinkers in mean curvature flow. These objects are related to black hole horizons, phase transition problems and surface theory in molecular science. 本項目旨在推進極小極大理論在幾何中未開發的領域以及拓撲學、數學物理之中的應用。 極小極大理論是在幾何及物理的非線性問題中求不穩定駐解的變分方法。比如肥皂膜的『極小曲面』模型便是非常重要的例子。極小極大理論提供了一套能用來解釋廣泛自然現象的構架，特別是在極小解並不存在的情況。這些駐解的幾何與解析性質可以用來揭示其背後空間的幾何特性；舉例來說，極小曲面在三維流形拓撲和廣義相對論領域都有深入的應用。 這個項目的主要研究者希望能推進對一般空間裡極小曲面（和極小子流形）的極小極大理論中的幾何與分析性質的理解。一方面，我們會研究這個空間的幾何性質跟這些極小曲面的拓撲和Morse指標之間的相互關係。這會對正曲率空間的研究帶來重大進展。另一方面，我們也會應用極小極大理論來進行其他的幾何構造，例如帶自由邊界的極小曲面、常平均曲率曲面和平均曲率流理論中的自相似解等等。對以上這些幾何曲面的研究與黑洞視界、相變問題以及分子科學裡的曲面理論等密切相關。

24305115.label: Realisation of objectives
24305115.value: We achieved a great advance in the understanding of the properties of minimal surfaces arising from min-max constructions, especially in the free boundary setting. We proved the fundamental up-to-the-boundary curvature estimates for stable minimal hypersurfaces. This, in turn, is a crucial ingredient in completing Almgren-Pitts min-max theory to manifolds with boundary. Our discovery has led to further work on the compactness of minimal hypersurfaces with bounded index. Together with his collaborators, the PI has also obtained an optimal Morse index upper bound for free boundary minimal hypersurfaces arising from multi-parameter min-max constructions in the Almgren-Pitts setting. It is fair to say that with our works (and the following works by others), we have achieved a fairly deep understanding of the geometric and analytic properties of min-max minimal varieties (Objective 1). We succeeded in extending the Almgren-Pitts min-max theory to the free boundary setting, hence completing the program set out by Almgren in the 1960s in building up the Morse theory for minimal surfaces in general Riemannian manifolds (with and without boundary). We also discover using Lusternik-Schnirelmann theory that the boundary geometry (namely convexity) plays a key role in the existence of infinitely many free boundary minimal hypersurfaces. Our work has also partly inspired the recent proof of the longstanding Yau's conjecture by A. Song. We have worked out all the main ingredients, including curvature estimates and maximum principal for example, needed in extending the min-max theory for manifolds with boundary, hence completing Objective 2. About half-way after the commencement of this research project, there are other research teams who have worked out the min-max theory in the setting of constant mean curvature surfaces (Xin Zhou and Jonathan Zhu) and self shrinkers of mean curvature flow (Daniel Ketover and Xin Zhou). Therefore, in some sense, the min-max theory in these two geometric variational problems have already been developed. However, the PI has also been working on various alternative approaches to these problems, which may have different applications in contrast with the existing min-max theories. The results obtained are still in preparation which has not yet been submitted for publications. In summary, all the objectives set out in this proposal have been completed (some already achieved by other research teams).

24305115.label: Major findings and research outcome
24305115.value: We succeeded (see Research Output 1) in completing the program of Almgren on developing the min-max theory for free boundary minimal hypersurfaces in general Riemannian manifolds with boundary. This answers the longstanding question on the general existence and regularity of free boundary minimal hypersurfaces in any dimension. An application of our general existence result combined with the work of Marques and Neves shows that for any compact Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature and convex boundary, there exist infinitely many properly embedded minimal hypersurfaces with non-empty free boundary. This work is used in A. Song's recent proof of Yau's Conjecture on the existence of infinitely many minimal hypersurfaces in closed manifolds. Our work discovers a new phenomena called the properness of free boundary minimal hypersurfaces, which has already inspired a lot of follow-up works in the past few years. This work is accepted for publication in Journal of Differential Geometry. In Research Output 2, we prove uniform curvature estimates for immersed stable free boundary minimal hypersurfaces satisfying a uniform area bound, which generalize the celebrated Schoen–Simon–Yau interior curvature estimates up to the free boundary. Our curvature estimates imply a smooth compactness theorem which is an essential ingredient in the min-max theory of free boundary minimal hypersurfaces. We also prove a monotonicity formula for free boundary minimal submanifolds in Riemannian manifolds for any dimension and codimension. For 3-manifolds with boundary, we prove a stronger curvature estimate for properly embedded stable free boundary minimal surfaces without a-priori area bound. This generalizes Schoen’s interior curvature estimates to the free boundary setting. This work is published in Crelle's journal. In Research Output 3, we establish a boundary maximum principle for free boundary minimal submanifolds in a Riemannian manifold with boundary, in any dimension and codimension. Our result holds more generally in the context of varifolds. We introduce in this paper a novel ideas called orthogonal foliations to handle spaces possessing weaker regularity properties. This idea has been further expanded in the recent work of C. Li (to appear in Invent. Math.) on singular spaces with positive scalar curvature. This work is accepted for publication in Comm. Anal. Geom. In Research Output 4, we discuss some recent results on free boundary minimal surfaces in the Euclidean unit-ball, concerning their existence as well as the geometric and analytic properties. This work will appear in the Proceedings of ICCM.

24305115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24305115.value: Our work has pointed out several new directions that are worth serious investigations. In particular, some of our techniques can handle geometric variational problems in spaces possessing certain type of singularities. We propose further future work on the existence theory of minimal surfaces in singular spaces, and also other geometric boundary value problems like capillary surfaces.

24305115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24305115.value: This project expanded our understanding of the existence of minimal surfaces, which are mathematical models for soap films, in a very general setting. This gives a theoretical understanding of how stable and unstable geometric structures in nature should look like. The research project utilize many state-of-the-art methods from geometry, analysis and differential equations to address these fundamental questions.

24501215.value: 试比较两种激励机制：一种授予任务执行者确定的奖赏，另一种授予任务执行者不确定（随机）的奖赏。哪一种奖赏会更有激励效应呢？一般说来，不确定性意味着风险，而人们通常选择风险规避。在现实生活中，我们确实可以看到很多有意规避风险和不确定性的行为。比如说，人们会放弃一个50%机会收益3000港币和50%机会收益1000港币的可能性，而选择一个100%机会收益2000港币的确定选项。在行为科学界，决策学研究也证明了风险规避行为的存在意义。然而一些新近研究表明，当任务执行者专注于任务本身并且没有事先去算计这份奖赏值得他们付出多少努力时，相对同等的确定奖赏，他们反而会为了不确定的奖赏而付出更多努力 。 在本项目中，研究者试图构建一个全新的、全面的理论框架来认识不确定性的激励效应。具体来说，本项目研究者致力于探究以下这些问题： 1. 为什么人们说他们不喜欢不确定的奖赏但是却愿意为不确定的奖赏付出更多努力？究竟是什么内在原因决定了人对结果不确定性的态度？ 2. 有哪些外在因素可以左右人对结果不确定性的态度呢？是不是有条件操纵这些外在因素来影响人对不确定性的态度呢？ 3. 如何在现实生活场景中（非实验监控条件下）设计和实施有关不确定奖赏的激励机制？ 4. 我们知道任务执行者会为不确定结果付出更多努力，但是当任务结果至关重要时，任务执行者还会有同样的表现吗？人对不确定性的态度是否会随着结果重要性的变化而变化？ 5. 以上这些现象具有文化普适性？东方人和西方人对不确定奖赏的反应是否大相径庭？ 在本项目中，研究者设计了两个方向的五个实验来探究上述具体问题。所有实验将在严格控制的实验室和自然条件的生活环境中对照进行。第一个方向着重于项目的理论价值。项目作者提出以好奇程度解释风险偏好方向：越是对结果好奇的任务执行者可能越会在工作中努力付出以求获得奖赏和满足好奇心。第二个方向着重于项目的外部效应。为了更好的了解不确定激励机制的实际适用范围，研究者将检验各种不同等级的奖赏。同时，不同文化背景的不同人群将参与这两个方向上的各种大规模实验测试。 本项目基于决策学研究和激励机制设计，同时也旨在为决策学研究和激励机制设计提供可靠扎实的研究成果。从理论意义的角度讲，项目两个方向相辅相成，在研究意义的深度和广度上同时发展。从现实意义的角度讲，所有实验结果和研究结论对商业和公共事业中各阶层激励制度设计都具有宝贵的参考价值。

24501215.label: Major findings and research outcome
24501215.value: Luxi Shen, Christopher K. Hsee, and Joachim H. Talloen (2019), “The Fun and Function of Uncertainty: Uncertain Incentives Reinforce Repetition Decisions,” Journal of Consumer Research, 46(1), 69-81. "This research studies repetition decisions, namely, whether to repeat a behavior (e.g., a purchase) after receiving an incentive (e.g., a discount). Can uncertainty drive repetition? Four experiments, all involving real consequences to each individual participant, document a counterintuitive reinforcing-uncertainty effect: individuals repeat a behavior more if its incentive is uncertain than if it is certain, even when the certain incentive is financially better. This effect is robust; it holds in both lab and field settings and at both small and large magnitudes. Furthermore, the experiments identify two theory-driven boundary conditions for the reinforcing uncertainty effect: the effect arises (a) only if the uncertainty is resolved immediately and not if the resolution of uncertainty is delayed, and (b) only after, not before, one has engaged in repetitions. These results support a resolution-as-reward account and cast doubt on other explanations such as reference-dependent preferences. This research reveals the hidden value of uncertain incentives and sheds light on the delicate relationship between incentive uncertainty and repetition decisions."

24501215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24501215.value: In the field experiment of this project, I found that the patterns of the uncertain outcomes could affect people's motivation to repeat. Inspired by this finding, I started another research project exploring the effectiveness of uncertain incentives with different designs: positive vs. negative skewness. Skewness describes the shape of a probabilistic distribution. In real life, perfectly symmetrical distributions are rare; people mostly encounter outcome distributions that are either positively skewed or negatively skewed. Which kind of outcomes—positively-skewed or negatively-skewed—keeps people going further? I propose that people repeat an action more if its outcomes follow a negatively skewed distribution than if they follow a positively-skewed distribution. The intuition underlying our main hypothesis is simple: occasional bad events make the rest of our lives seem better. I plan to empirically test this proposition with experiments entailing real work experience and real payoffs. This new project is built upon the completed RGC-funded project and is expected to extend the line of research on uncertain outcomes and expand the impact of the completed RGC-funded project.

24502615.label: Project Objectives

24502615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24502615.value: The output of a service product, especially professional services, heavily depends on a service provider's expertise and/or effort. Oftentimes, the effort of the service provider is not closely observable to a buyer of the service. This problem is known as a principal-agent (or moral hazard) problem in classical economics and operations management literature, and much of the existing literature focuses on designing a contact that will lead to a provider exerting sufficient effort on behalf of a buyer. A performance-based contract (PBC) is one way of incentivizing the provider by tying the payment to the provider with the service performance. In some industries where the outputs are explicitly measurable, PBC's are shown to be quite effective. However, in many professional services such as consulting, tax, legal, and medical services, outputs are often multi-dimensional and noisy, thus it is very difficult to explicitly measure the output and its quality. Such uncertainty arising in measuring the service output may become a subject of dispute after the service is performed. In such cases, PBC is not necessarily the most efficient mechanism to induce the optimal effort. This research project focuses on evaluating and designing a contract when the two parties involved cannot explicitly measure or determine the output performance. More specifically, we plan to examine how much inefficiency is caused by this inability of determining the exact performance, and analyze how a classical PBC fails to restore the efficiency loss. Then, we will propose novel but simple mechanisms that can induce the service provider to exert more efforts than a classical PBC would do and show how those new mechanisms can restore the efficiency of a trade. Finally, we will examine numerous domains of service procurements to suggest which contract types are most suitable for each specific application domain. To the best of our knowledge, this is one of the first projects that analyze the performance of a professional service contract. We expect that the findings from this project can be applied to several service products in different domains. As Hong Kong is an epicenter of global procurement trades of manufacturing and service products, we envision that the study greatly benefits the local economy by making the service procurements more efficient. In parallel, we also believe this work would make important contribution to the literature, adding to the increasing stream of works that focus on improving service procurement mechanisms. 服务产品，尤其是专业服务，的产出严重的依赖于服务提供者的专业知识及努力程度。通常，服务提供者的努力程度并不能被服务购买者所观测到。在经典的经济和运作管理的文献中，这个问题通常被称为委托-代理（或者道德风险）模型，并且很多现有的文献专注于设计能使服务提供商使出足够的努力的合同。依据表现的合同(PBC)把给提供者的付款与服务表现联系起来来激励服务提供者。在很多产出能被显式地测量的行业中，PBC被证明是非常有效的。但是，在专业服务诸如咨询，税收，法律及医疗服务中，产出通常是多维并且有噪音的，因此显式地测量产出及其质量是非常困难的。这种在服务产出的测量中的不确定性可能成为服务完成后争议的主题。在这些情况下，PBC不一定是诱导最优努力的最有效的机制。这项研究专注于对涉及的双方无法显式观测和确定服务表现的情况进行合同的评估和设计。更具体的，我们计划检测因为无法决定精确的表现会带来多少的无效率性，并且分析经典的PBC如何无法还原效率损失。然后，我们将提出全新的但是简单的机制，这些机制能诱导提供者使出比PBC机制下更多的努力，并展示这些机制如何还原一项交易的效率。最后，我们将检测许多的服务采购领域，并在每一应用领域建议相应的最合适的合同类型。据我们所知，这是分析专业服务合同表现方面的最早的项目之一。我们期望这个项目的结果能够应用到不同领域的多个服务产品。由于香港是生产与服务产品的全球采购贸易的中心，我们预想这个项目能通过使得服务采购更有效率而让当地经济受益。同时，我们相信这个工作能够对文献有重要的贡献，会丰富越来越多的专注于服务采购机制方面的工作。

24502615.label: Realisation of objectives
24502615.value: All the objectives were achieved. In this work, we show how efficiency loss in a classical PBC is driven by noisy measurement of service output. Our proposed mechanism which implements post service auditing options is proven to improve the efficiency of the contract compared to PBC. In particular, we examine various situations where the measurement errors are additive and/or multiplicative to the actual output of the service and our results show that the performance of the new mechanism varies.

24502715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24502715.value: 美國公司在過去三十年來逐漸國際化。數據顯示，標普五百大公司中，近百分之九十公司有海外業務，且近半收益來自其海外業務。隨著海外盈餘比重持續增長，公司所持海外現金也大幅度增長。這現象引起監管單位，制度制定機關及投資者密切關注。當跨國公司海外業務獲取現金盈餘時，需決定是否將持有現金送回國內或留在海外，而這一決定對公司未來盈餘有深遠影響。 本文章主要研究跨國公司海內外現金之變動是否影響盈餘持續性及投資者是否能了解其中之意涵。 本文假說可從以下幾方面論述。第一，公司海外業務增長可能高於其國內業務，所以將更多現金留在海外讓公司更有效的運用，可增其盈餘持續性。第二，過多留在海外現金所產生之代理問題可導致未來盈餘及盈餘持續性降低。第三，由於海外繳納稅款率通常低於國內繳納稅款率，公司可能把海外現金投資在金融資產而非其它能創造更大利益的資產上，結果導致盈餘持續性降低。基於上述觀點，本文推論海內外現金變動對盈餘持續性可能有不同程度的影響。 本文主要貢獻在探討盈餘持續性是否受海內外現金變動影響及投資者是否能了解其中之意涵。除此之外，對監管部門是否推動更多企業披露海外業務有隱含意義。

24502715.label: Realisation of objectives
24502715.value: We have completed the project with the stated objectives. Overall, we have completed a working paper with solid results. We have presented this paper at various interactional conferences, including Financial Accounting and Reporting Section Midyear Meeting, the American Tax Association Midyear Meeting, EAA Annual Congress, and the EIASM Conference on Current Research in Taxation. In addition, we have presented our paper at workshop at various universities such as Erasmus University, Nanyang Technological University, National Tsing Hua University, and Washington State University. The paper is currently under second round review at Journal of Accounting and Economics. We believe the objectives are fully completed as follows: 1. Regarding the objective 1, in contrast to the common belief that accumulating cash in foreign subsidiaries leads to inefficiencies, we show that changes in foreign cash are as persistent for future earnings as changes in domestic cash. The results are robust to a battery of tests. 2. For the objective 2, we find a positive association between current foreign cash changes and one-year-ahead stock returns, suggesting that investors under-react to the performance implications of foreign cash changes. We further document that investors are more likely to misprice foreign cash changes when information processing costs are higher and when firms have poorer information environments. 3. We have also achieved Objective 3. The SEC has long been concerned that total cash reported on the balance sheet does not accurately reflect the amount of cash firms have at their free disposal. The FASB is also considering requiring firms to disclose the amount of foreign cash related to permanently reinvested foreign earnings. Our finding that investors underreact to foreign cash changes, especially in subsamples where investors face higher processing costs to decipher the nature and implications of foreign cash changes, suggests that the SEC and FASB’s call for expanded disclosure on foreign operations might be warranted. 4. For objective 4, we show there exists predictable cross-sectional variation of the association between changes in foreign and domestic cash and future earnings. Foreign cash changes have higher earnings persistence when foreign operations offer better growth opportunities and when repatriation taxes are lower. Therefore, for earnings forecast and firm valuation, analysts and investors can improve their forecast by better understanding the specific circumstance of each firm foreign cash holdings.

24502715.label: Major findings and research outcome
24502715.value: In this project, we evaluate the association between changes in foreign and domestic cash and one-year-ahead earnings. In contrast to the common belief that accumulating cash in foreign subsidiaries leads to inefficiencies, we find that, in the overall sample, changes in foreign cash are as persistent for future earnings as changes in domestic cash. However, there exists predictable cross-sectional variation. Foreign cash changes have higher earnings persistence when foreign operations offer better growth opportunities and when repatriation taxes are lower. Our second analysis investigates whether investors efficiently price the earnings persistence implications of changes in foreign and domestic cash. We find a positive association between current foreign cash changes and one-year-ahead stock returns, suggesting that investors under-react to the performance implications of foreign cash changes. We further document that investors are more likely to misprice foreign cash changes when information processing costs are higher and when firms have poorer information environments.

24502715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24502715.value: Our results provide a reference point for assessing how firms will respond to tax policies that aim at reducing repatriation tax burden and encouraging domestic investment. Not all firms will view the repatriation tax reduction as equally valuable. For example, for firms facing low repatriation taxes, their foreign cash changes are more persistent than domestic cash changes, so these firms are less likely to repatriate foreign funds. The recent change of tax law (i.e., Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) of 2017) removes repatriation taxes on most future foreign earnings, motivating MNCs to repatriate cash to the U.S. Our results suggest that for firms facing low repatriation taxes, their foreign cash changes are more persistent than domestic cash changes, so these firms are less likely to repatriate foreign funds. Future studies can examine whether TJCA has achieved its intended purpose.

24502715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24502715.value: Over the past 30 years, U.S. firms have become increasingly global. 89 percent of S&P 500 firms had operations abroad and 49 percent of their income was from foreign operations. As foreign income continues to grow for multinationals, foreign cash holdings also pile up quickly. Recently, the record level of U.S. multinationals’ foreign cash holdings has attracted much attention from regulators and policy makers. Shareholders are also concerned about whether retaining a significant amount of cash overseas is the most efficient allocation of firm resources. Using a hand-collected sample of U.S. multinational firms’ foreign and domestic cash holdings, we find that on average changes in foreign cash have similar predictability of future earnings as domestic cash changes. Moreover, we find a positive association between current foreign cash changes and one-year-ahead stock returns, suggesting that investors under-react to the persistence implications of foreign cash changes. Our findings implies that more salient or standardized disclosure on foreign operations is warranted. FASB recently directed its staff to investigate the operability of requiring firms to separately disclose foreign cash related to permanently reinvested earnings. Our pricing result echoes the FASB’s concern that current disclosure on foreign cash and permanently reinvested earnings might be insufficient.

24503515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24503515.value: Economists have long been puzzled by the wide fluctuations in market asset prices, as the observed fundamentals have never fully accounted for them. Many researchers, including John Maynard Keynes (1936), George Akerlof (2009), and Andrei Shleifer (2000), have come to consider investor sentiment as an important driving force underlying the markets. Although efforts have been made to measure investor sentiment in the stock markets (Baker and Wurgler, 2007), the same sentiment in the housing markets has not been well quantified. In this project, we propose a novel measure of sentiment in the housing markets: the ratio of the Google enquiry volume on the real estate investment of the targeted city searched from outside to that searched from within the city. Potential outside investors have limited information about local fundamentals, and are thus more likely to speculate because they do not live in the city. This search volume ratio will quantify the propensity for speculation unrelated to the fundamentals, or investor sentiment in the markets. People search for useful information before a transaction. As a result, this sentiment measure could provide a timely prediction of housing market dynamics. We will begin by relating the sentiment measure to non-owner occupied home purchases to determine whether it prompts a rise in house purchases for non-residence purposes. Then, we will consider builders’ responses, as they may ride the hike in sentiment and exhibit a tendency to build more houses in the local markets. Accordingly, the sentiment measure could predict the increase in the number of housing permits. Finally, we will examine the effects of investor sentiment on housing prices, as the former may predict housing prices in both ways depending on whether the local markets are dominated by speculation demand or building supply. We will introduce the geography determinants of supply elasticity developed by Saiz (2010) and hypothesize that investor sentiment’s positive prediction of housing prices should exist in areas with strict supply constraints. 一直以來，經濟學研究者對市場價格的大幅波動感到困惑：觀察到的基本面經濟數據並不能完全解釋價格的變動。諸如Maynard Keynes (1936), George Akerlof (2009), and Andrei Shleifer (2000) 等經濟學者認為市場情緒是驅動市場變化的重要因素。於是近年來，人們着手開始測量投資者的情緒，研究其對資產價格的影響 (Baker and Wurgler, 2007；Da, Engelberg, and Gao, 2014)。然而這些研究主要針對的是美國的股票市場。在全世界範圍內，各國的市場情緒如何測量，這些情緒對資產價格有什麼影響，這些影響會受各國的哪些特徵決定？不僅僅是股票市場，這些情緒會對房地產市場有影響嗎？ 在這個研究項目中，我們將利用Da, Engelberg, and Gao （2014）的方法構造投資者的市場情緒。具體來說，我們會蒐集人們通過Google搜索經濟和金融的關鍵詞流量來度量不同時點的市場情緒，負面詞（例如失業，衰退等）的搜索說明人們對當前經濟環境比較擔心，正面詞（例如增長，就業等）的搜索說明人們對市場變現的信心。Google 提供各國搜索關鍵詞的流量，據此我們可以構造全世界範圍主要國家的市場情緒。 我們將研究各國市場情緒對本國資產價格的預測能力。這種預測能力反映了情緒對資產市場的影響程度。這能否為我們提供新的渠道去預測各國的資本市場波動？我們還會蒐集各個緯度的國家特徵來考察哪些因素會影響預測的能力。 我們還計劃能把這項研究擴展到房地產市場，去探究市場情緒如何影響房地產交易和房價波動。我們會考察市場情緒能不能預測房地產動態。具體來說，我們會把市場情緒與房地產需求方（投資房購買，居住房購買），房屋供給以及房價聯繫起來。 最後，投資者往往在交易決策之前就會蒐集有用的信息。因此，這種基於搜索構造的市場情緒可以及時提供信息用於預測市場價格的動態。這對投資者做投資決策和市場監管者監控市場風險都有助益。

24503515.label: Realisation of objectives
24503515.value: I originally proposed to construct a measure of sentiment in the US housing markets using households’ Google search behaviors. The panel commented that “the proposal appears to involve a large amount of work involving big data analytics that may ultimately turn out to be only of marginal interest”. Following this key suggestion from the panel, to broaden our research impact, I extended the scope by constructing sentiment indices around the world. Specifically, with my coauthors, I tracked households’ search behaviors on Google in 38 countries during the 2004-2014 and constructed a weekly sentiment index on both economics- and non-economics-based dimensions. We then completed a paper titled "Googling Investor Sentiment around the World". Our paper has been accepted by a number of international conferences and academic seminars. We have got positive feedback from the audience and the paper was among FMA Annual Meeting Semifinalist for Best Paper Award in 2016. In the later stage of this project, we polished this paper and submitted it to the Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis (JFQA), a top-tier journal in finance. After several rounds of revisions, the JFQA has accepted our paper for publication. We have also followed the panel's suggestion by posting the paper on SSRN.

24503515.label: Major findings and research outcome
24503515.value: Major findings: We use households’ Google search behavior to construct weekly sentiment indices for 38 markets for the period between 2004 and 2014. We take advantage of international settings to validate the non-economics-related component of our measure as a proxy for sentiment based on an event study of sports outcomes. We show that our sentiment measure is a contrarian predictor of country-level market returns. We further mitigate potential endogeneity issues by conducting two difference-in-differences analyses around plausibly exogenous shocks to difficult-to-value and limits-to-arbitrage channels. Finally, we document an important role of global sentiment in driving sentiment and predicting market returns across countries. Research outcome: Our paper has been accepted by a number of international conferences and we have presented in seminars in several research institutions and universities also. We have got positive feedback from the audience and the paper was among FMA Annual Meeting Semifinalist for Best Paper Award in 2016. The paper has been accepted by the Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis (JFQA), a top-tier journal in finance, for publication.

24503515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24503515.value: Our sentiment indices are useful for future research. With our international sentiment indices, researchers could improve our understanding of international markets from a behavioral perspective. Moreover, heterogeneity across countries, capital market integration, and the implementation of specific policies and regulations provide rich opportunities to explore the sentiment effect in a broader context.

24503515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24503515.value: We study how investor sentiment affects stock prices around the world. We track households’ Google search behavior to construct a weekly measure of sentiment for 38 countries during the 2004–2014 period. We show that the sentiment measure can negatively predict country-level market returns. Furthermore, we document an important role of global sentiment in stock markets. With our international sentiment indices, researchers could improve the understanding of international markets from a behavioral perspective; practitioners are likely to design profitable trading strategies; regulators may consider the sentiment effect and design policies to make markets more efficient.

24600415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24600415.value: This project aims to study how materialism can create unresponsive behaviors in interpersonal relationships, and to test how these unresponsive relationships may partially explain the negative effects of materialism on psychological well-being. Materialism has been consistently found to undermine individual well-being. Importantly, although well-being can be substantially promoted by interpersonal relationships, individuals with materialistic aspirations tend to have dissatisfied relationships. It is important to examine how materialism undermines relationship processes, in order to identify ways to undo its undesired impact. Till now, the causal mechanisms between materialism and relationship processes are still far from clear. This project proposes one mechanism: responsive behaviors to other's needs. It is hypothesized that a person's materialism undermines his or her responsive behaviors as well as the partner's. Subsequently, both parties cannot obtain the normal interpersonal benefits from these unresponsive relationships. Three studies are proposed to closely examine the link between materialism and responsive behaviors within both dating relationships (Studies 1 and 2) and friendships (Study 3). Responsive behaviors will be measured by self-report questionnaires (Studies 1 to 3) and rated by observers (Studies 2 and 3). A longitudinal study (Study 1) and two experiments (Studies 2 and 3) will be designed to (a) investigate whether materialism causes unresponsive behaviors of both relationship partners, (b) examine whether, by reducing responsive behaviors of both partners, materialism may further undermine relationship partners' perception of each other's responsiveness, and (c) examine whether materialism can persists over time and undermines relationship quality and psychological well-being by prohibiting relationship partners to sense responsiveness from each other and appreciate the relationship more. In sum, the proposal examines how materialism may undermine well-being through its negative impact on interpersonal relationships. By addressing this issue, the project identifies potential ways to help materialistic individuals develop more fulfilling relationships and sustainable lifestyles. Moreover, given the prevalence of material temptations in modern societies, the project also sheds light on how individuals should pursue their happiness. 本項目旨在研究物質主義如何構成人際關係的不協調，並測試不協調的人際關係是否物質主義構成心理不健康的其中一個機制。 不同的研究都一致地發現物質主義減低個人心理健康。雖然人際關係可以改善個人心理健康，祟尚物質主義的人通常都有不愉快的人際關係。透過認識物質主義如何破壞人際關係，我們將有辦法消除物質主義的不良影響。可是，時至今日，學界對物質主義如何破壞人際關係的機制仍然不太瞭解。本項目提出一個機制：因應對方需要的協調行為。我假定一個人的物質主義會減低自己及對方的協調行為。結果，雙方都無法得到在人際關係中正常的得益。 本項目提出三個研究去了解物質主義對情人 (研究一及二)及朋友關係(研究三)的負面影響。協調行為將會透過問卷(研究一至三)及實際觀察(研究二及三)去測量。我設計一個縱向研究(研究一)及兩個實驗(研究二及三)去測驗以下三組問題：(一) 一個人的物質主義增加雙方的不協調行為，(二) 透過增加不協調行為，一個人的物質主義令雙方都感到對方不協調，(三)結果, 物質主義持續，並減低人際關係的質素及心理健康。 總體來說，本項目測試物質主義對人際關係的影響。透過這個研究，我們可以幫助祟尚物質主義的人建立更好的人際關係及可持續的生活態度。除此之外，當物質的誘惑充斥著現代社會，本項目可以解構現代人應當如何追求快樂。

24600415.label: Realisation of objectives
24600415.value: We have run the three studies as planned and fully achieved all the following four project objectives. Below are the particulars: -------------------------------------------------------------- Objective 1: To examine whether materialism can reduce behavioral responsiveness of both relationship partners to each other, in a longitudinal study (Study 1) and two experiments (Studies 2 and 3) Based on the proposed design, we have run one pilot study and three studies to test the effects of materialism on behavioral responsiveness. The results were inconsistent across studies. In our published pilot study (Hui & Tsang, 2017, we found that, during self-disclosure, an actor's responsiveness to the partner's needs was negatively related to both parties' materialism. However, in both longitudinal and experimental studies we ran later, we did not observe any associations in between. Our hypothesis on the links between materialism and responsiveness was therefore not strongly supported. -------------------------------------------------------------- Objective 2: To test how materialism can, by reducing behavioral responsiveness of both relationship partners, undermine the perception of responsiveness from the partner (Studies 1 to 3) To test this mediational chain, we examined three necessary conditions: (a) materialism should be linked to behavioral responsiveness (as to be in Objective 1), (b) materialism should be linked to the perception of responsiveness, and (c) behavioral responsiveness from an actor should be linked to his or her partner’s perception of responsiveness. In our studies, the conditions (a) and (b) were not met. However, we reliably observed (c). Although our results did not support the mediational hypothesis, we had published a thorough analysis of the link (c) from our studies (Hui & Tsang, 2017; Hui, Ng, & Shieh, in press). -------------------------------------------------------------- Objective 3: To test how materialism can, by reducing both relationship partners' perceived responsiveness from each other, undermine relationship quality and subjective well-being experienced by both partners (Studies 1 to 3) To test this mediational chain, we examined three necessary conditions: (a) materialism should be linked to the perception of responsiveness (as to be in Objective 2), (b) materialism should be linked to relationship quality and subjective well-being, and (c) perception of responsiveness from an actor should be linked to his or her well-being. In our studies, the conditions (a) and (b) were not met. However, we reliably observed (c). Although our results did not support the mediational hypothesis, we managed to publish a paper that summarizes these associations and considered additional variables (e.g., prosocial spending; Li, Ng, & Hui, in preparation). -------------------------------------------------------------- Objective 4: To examine how materialism can, by reducing both relationship partners' perceived responsiveness from each other, persist over time (Studies 1 to 3) To test this mediational chain, we examined are three necessary conditions: (a) materialism should be linked to perceived responsiveness (as to be tested in Objective 2), (b) materialism is stable across two time-points. In our studies, the condition (a) was not met. However, we reliably observed (b). Therefore, the perception of responsiveness does not contribute to the stability of materialism across time. -------------------------------------------------------------- To summarize, we have addressed all our objectives with the planned studies. The effects of materialism were not as strong as I initially proposed.

24600415.label: Major findings and research outcome
24600415.value: The past findings and laypeople’s wisdom have suggested that materialistic individuals are more self-centered and dissatisfied with their social networks. As a natural extension, this study examined whether and how materialism may undermine close relationships by undermining responsive exchange between partners. Contrary to our predictions, our longitudinal and experimental studies showed that materialism did not relate to responsiveness and relationship-well-being of both parties. It appears that the interpersonal processes arisen within close relationships can diminish the detrimental influence of materialism on relationship well-being. In this research, we tried to look closer to the communication of responsiveness via specific behaviors (e.g., advice-giving in conflict discussion and prosocial spending on the partner) and tested how materialism may relate to the use of specific behaviors that can communicate responsiveness. While we did not observe the effects of materialism in these studies, we published some results on the prosocial behaviors and responsiveness (Hui, Ng, & Shieh, in press; Li & Hui, 2019).

24600415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24600415.value: We have two major research directions: 1. Contrary to our predictions and lay beliefs, our studies did not find significant effects of materialism on responsiveness and relationship well-being. To further clarify how materialism matters in close relationships, we will try to differentiate two components of materialism (i.e., preference for material goods and self-enhancing values) and explore how different components of materialism may shape mate preferences (e.g., preference for short-term versus long-term mates and rich versus considerate partners). 2. As we looked closer at how responsiveness processes took place, we discovered that the communication of responsiveness was far from perfect (Hui, Ng, & Shieh, in press). In future studies, we will look at how well relationship partners understand each other's needs and preferred types of support and how this understanding can facilitate more responsive exchanges between partners and coordination for shared goals.

24600415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24600415.value: The past findings and laypeople’s wisdom have suggested that materialistic individuals are more self-centered and unhappy with their social networks. As a natural extension, this study examined whether and how materialism may undermine close relationships by undermining responsive exchange between partners. Contrary to our predictions, both longitudinal and experimental studies showed that materialism did not relate to the responsiveness of both parties. It appears that the interpersonal processes arisen within close relationships can diminish the detrimental influence of materialism on relationship well-being.

24601515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24601515.value: 全球最大的地震發生在俯衝帶，除強烈的地面震動之外，有時會引發致命的海嘯。減少此類地震帶來的災害要求我們更好的來了解地震的機理。通常，人們利用震間大地測量結果來定性的估量未來地震的可能情境，而相應的定量評估則非常少見。這項研究將利用數值模擬進行定量研究，來提高我們對震間大地測量與未來地震之間關係的認識。很顯然這類工作具有直接的社會效應，而結果也將為減少俯衝帶地震及海嘯災害提供依據。 2012年9月5日，在哥斯達黎加Nicoya半島發生了一個7.6級地震。在此地震之前的大地測量觀測，以及這次地震中觀測到的同震滑移創造了一組新穎獨特的數據，因為得益於Nicoya半島距離海溝的距離較小，這裏是世界上大地測量觀測精度最高的地方之一。這項研究工作將利用GPS觀測執行如下任務：1）在震間觀測基礎上進行地震破裂動力學有限元數值模擬，2）將模擬的同震滑移與觀測到的結果進行仔細比對，3）評估俯衝板片幾何形狀和介質屬性對震間鎖閉及同震滑移的影響。預期結果將是第一個將震間觀測定量轉化為同震滑移，並將數值模擬結果與實際同震觀測進行對比的工作。 儘管這裏以Nicoya俯衝帶為例，預期結果也可以應用到其他俯衝帶，並且高分辨率的震間和同震觀測在其他俯衝帶也已經逐漸展開。在此項研究中，一名研究生和兩名本科生將得到系統的訓練。研究成果將在國際會議上展示，並將與教學內容相結合。這項工作也將為香港地震研究與教育打下堅實基礎。

24601515.label: Realisation of objectives
24601515.value: We have successfully completed all objectives as originally proposed in the project. Efforts include testing the effects of subduction fault geometry, subduction zone structure, and hypocenter location on earthquake rupture propagation, conducting ground motion predictions based on interseismic locking distribution, and deriving frictional properties on subduction faults. One PhD graduate student was trained to conduct spontaneous rupture simulations in this project. We conduct rigorous investigations on the effects of subduction zone structure and subduction fault geometry on rupture propagation. First, we compute initial stress distribution on the Nicoya megathrust from interseismic locking models by adopting a half-space and a 1-D depth dependent velocity structure. The difference in initial stress with different structures is minor (<1MPa) (Yang et al., 2019, J. Geophys. Res.). Then we nucleate ruptures at the hypocenter of the 2012 M7.6 Nicoya earthquake with the two initial stress distributions. Simulation results indicate that the rupture scenarios with different structures are nearly same in final slip distribution and moment magnitude (Yang et al., 2019, J. Geophys. Res.). We further test the effects of strength distribution on rupture scenarios. The model with along-strike varying strength distribution fits the kinematic model slightly better compared to the model with uniform strength distribution (Yang et al., 2019, J. Geophys. Res.). In addition, we compare the simulation results with a curved fault model and two planar fault models with different dipping angles (in Bing He’s thesis, 2017). The curved fault promotes larger final slip and moment magnitude compared to the planar faults. We also investigate the geometry effects on rupture extents in long-term earthquake cycles (Yu et al., 2018 Tectonophys.). These results have addressed the objectives 3 and 4. Furthermore, we develop a framework to derive coseismic slip from interseismic locking distribution and validate our results with actual seismic slip constrained from observations (Yang et al., 2019, J. Geophys. Res.). More importantly, we have found the significant hypocenter-dependent effects on rupture scenarios derived from interseismic locking models (Yang et al., 2019, Earth Planet. Sci. Lett.), which were not discovered before. Although we may estimate initial stress from interseismic locking models, hypocenter locations for future earthquakes are unknown and unpredictable. We consider all possible nucleation sites on the Nicoya megathrust given the initial stress estimated from locking distribution. Simulation results indicate that hypocenter location has a great impact on rupture scenarios, and consequently affects seismic hazard and tsunami potential. For instance, nucleation from neighbouring zones with identical initial stress distribution leads to completely different earthquake magnitudes, posing challenges for seismic hazard assessment. Ruptures initiating from deeper portion on the megathrust tend to produce larger shallow slip and seafloor displacements, leading to higher tsunami potential; while ruptures initiating from the shallow part may lead to larger slip downdip thus enhance seismic hazard on the Nicoya Peninsula. The results of hypocenter-dependent earthquake magnitudes and tsunamigenic potential not only pose challenges in estimating rupture extents from locking models, but also underscore the significance of quantitatively evaluating seismic and tsunami hazard in subduction zones. These results have well addressed the objectives 1 and 2. Motivated by the progress to obtain the above results, we broaden the scope of the project. We are striving to predict ground motion from interseismic locking models, because we can not accurately forecast future earthquake magnitudes due to heterogeneities on fault. Synthetic ground motions are generated for rupture scenarios with different nucleation sites and compared with observations in peak ground velocity (PGV), a critical index in seismic hazard assessment (Yao & Yang, 2019, conference presentations in Chi-Chi 20, SAGE/GAGE, and CGU). We calculate the average value of PGV prediction among all scenarios with moment magnitudes over 7.4 as the model prediction at each observational site. The average misfit in PGV predictions among all stations is under 15% in the low frequency band (0.02-0.25Hz). Such small misfit underscores the potential application of those locking-based ground motion predictions in future seismic hazard assessment. These results have addressed the objective 2. Moreover, we investigate the coseismic frictional properties on thrust faults by conducting dynamic rupture simulations. We utilize kinematic source models and near-filed observations to constrain the frictional properties during the 2012 M7.6 Nicoya earthquake (Yao’s PhD candidacy proposal; Yao & Yang, 2018, conference presentations in CGU, DEEP, and AGU, Yang & Yao, 2019, conference presentations in EGU, Yao & Yang, 2019, conference presentation in NMEM) and the 2015 M7.8 Nepal earthquake (Weng & Yang, 2018, J. Geophys. Res.). The derived dynamic rupture models have excellent fit for near-field observations. Moreover, we find significant differences in frictional properties between the two earthquakes, which may be attributed to different hydrologic conditions. These results have addressed the objectives 2 and 4.

24601515.label: Major findings and research outcome
24601515.value: Predicting earthquake magnitudes is critical for seismic hazard assessment, yet remains challenging due in part to our limited knowledge in earthquake faulting and stress distribution on seismogenic faults. It is well known that large earthquakes relieve huge amount of energy, which was accumulated during the interseismic period. The energy accumulation is qualitatively described by interseismic locking distribution that was generally derived from geodetic measurements. However, how to quantify the accumulated energy from locking remains challenging because of a number of complex factors. Furthermore, earthquake rupture propagation is controlled by a few factors, such as heterogenous stress distribution, fault geometry, and so on. Focusing on how to estimate future earthquake magnitudes and scenarios from interseismic locking distribution, we have produced a series of research outcome, as listed in Part C. Major findings in the project include (1) developing a framework to quantify slip deficit from interseismic locking distribution in the Nicoya region [Yang et al., 2019 JGR; Yang et al., 2019 EPSL]; (2) deriving coseismic slip distribution and rupture scenarios from locking [Yang et al., 2019 JGR; Yang et al., 2019 EPSL]; (3) validating numerical rupture scenarios with kinematic source models constrained from observations of the 2012 Nicoya earthquake [Yang et al., 2019 JGR]; (4) highlighting the dependence of earthquake magnitudes on hypocentral locations [Yang et al., 2019 EPSL], which poses significant challenges in seismic hazard assessment because we can not accurately determine future earthquake hypocenter; (5) suggesting that seismogenic width and low-velocity fault damage zone play critical roles in rupture extents [Weng and Yang, 2017 GRL; Weng et al., 2016 JGR]; (6) discovering the complex effects of subduction fault geometry on long-term earthquake cycles [Yu et al., 2018].

24601515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24601515.value: Motivated by the findings in this project, we are presently working on two aspects of better assessing future seismic hazard. First, we are striving to derive frictional properties on seismogenic fault immediately prior to large earthquakes. Second, we are working on ground motion predictions based on interseismic locking model. These efforts will extend and broaden the scope of the project, and may leverage further research opportunities and funding supports.

24601515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24601515.value: Earthquakes can not be predicted, and one of the reasons was attributed to unknown stress state on seismogenic faults, which is nonuniformly distributed from multiple lines of evidences. In this project, we first develop a framework to estimate stress distribution on the megathrust from interseismic locking, a static image that had often been used to qualitatively evaluate accumulated strain energy and thus infer future earthquake potential. However, how to convert such kinematic interseismic locking into future dynamic earthquake slip and rupture extent remains enigmatic. By conducting dynamic rupture simulations, we show that, for the first time, the final earthquake magnitude depends on where the rupture starts, although we assume knowing the stress state on the fault. The results of hypocentre-dependent earthquake magnitudes lead to a new perspective in physics-based earthquake hazard evaluation, and also underscore the significance of quantitatively evaluating seismic and tsunami hazard in subduction zones.

24606015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24606015.value: This proposed study aims to examine the dynamics of international regulation in developing countries. To this end, China’s food safety regulation is selected as a case study. This study intends to compare different self-regulatory regimes deployed by different food businesses in Guangdong Province. These range from food businesses producing for the domestic market to overseas markets, from agricultural products to processed food products. For the sake of systematic analysis, this study will build on Hood et al.’s (2001) three control components of a regulatory regime as a basis of comparison, including standard-setting, information-gathering and behaviour-modification. In this way, tensions between the internationalisation of regulation and other local factors such as the incapacity of food businesses to comply can be further assessed. In recent decades, ‘risk’ and ‘uncertainty’ have emerged as important concepts in policy making and business management. The direction of interdisciplinary approach of combining perspectives of political science, sociology, law and media has brought a new advancement to the research of risk regulation. One of the main academic debates in the field of political science considers how regulators interact with other actors in the regulatory space to manage risk issues. Under the circumstances, it is not surprising to observe sectoral and regional variations in different regulatory regimes. However, existing researches have paid little attention about how private sectors such as food businesses respond to international pressure and obligations; and how their self-regulatory regimes are adjusted accordingly. This proposed research project of food safety regulation in China fills in the research gap by looking into the self-regulatory regimes deployed by food businesses in Guangdong Province. By a comparison of four cases, this research tries to find out the potential national and international factors which influence the choice of regulatory tools selected by food businesses. To comprehensively explore the nature of regulation including decision-making and enforcement, the dynamics of the three control elements, namely, standard-setting, information-gathering and behaviour-modification will be explored and compared. This approach is novel and innovative in the sense that it tries to examine an internal regulatory regime of the private sector by ‘transplantation’ from the control theory perspective that is usually used to study state regulatory regimes. This contributes to the existing academic debate by analysing how established theories on regulation explain behaviours of food businesses in China. This helps improve the existing theories of internationalisation, public/private interests and opinion-responsiveness in the context of China as an industrialising country. 本研究主要探討國際監管對發展中國家所產生的影響，並以中國食品安全監管作案例分析。本研究將比較不同食品企業採用的自我監管機制，當中除了包括以海外市場及本地市場為銷售對象的企業，還有生產加工食品及農產品的企業。為了進行有系統的分析，本研究會以英國著名行政學者克裡斯托夫‧胡德等 (2001) 提出監管機制的三個基本元素包括標準設定、資訊採集及行為改變為基礎，剖析監管國際化與其他地方因素如食品企業無能力履行監管職責等之間的關係。 近十年來，「風險」與「不確定性」已成為政策制定及企業管理的重要概念，而風險監管的研究集合了政治學、社會學、法律及媒體等跨學科領域。監管機構如何在監管這一環上與其他持份者進行互動，管理風險問題，更是其中一個政治學的重要議題。在這種情況下，由於當中的監管機構及角色廣而多，所以監管機制出現行業和地區差異是可預計的。但是，現有文獻並未充分探討私營機構如食品企業如何回應國際社會給予的壓力與責任，及在此因素影響下企業如何調整內部的自我監管機制。 為了彌補現時有關食品安全監管研究的不足，本研究會深入分析中國廣東省食品企業採用的自我監管機制。通過六個個案的比較，本研究除了嘗試找出影響食品企業選擇監管工具的潛在國家及國際因素外，還會比較監管機制三個基本元素的變化，包括標準設定、資訊採集及行為改變，藉以從決策和執行等層面全面探討監管的性質。這研究方法的創新之處，在於它將一般應用在分析國家監管機制的控制理論，「移植」到研究私營機構的內部監管機制。本研究重點剖析現有的行政學理論如何有助解釋中國食品企業的行為，不但豐富現有的學術討論，而且鞏固在中國這個工業化國家背景下的國際化、公共/私人利益及輿論反應的理論。

24606015.label: Realisation of objectives
24606015.value: 1. To examine the implications of the internationalisation of regulation in China as a developing country This project has examined the evolution of China’s food standard-setting procedures in the context of the internationalization of regulation. It finds that after the reform and opening-up in 1978, state actors and leading enterprises monopolized the process of national food standard setting. With further participation in the global economy in the 21st century, China has become familiar with the international standard-setting procedures and has modeled its domestic policymaking on these practices. This has resulted in a more transparent, inclusive, scientific, pluralized, and consensus-based form of decision making. By contrast, the standards of the strategic industries have been harmonized to the standards of international counterparts through a top-down and authoritarian approach. In other words, China uses an accommodative approach, trichotomizing suitable standards and decision making procedures in terms of inclusiveness and transparency, which suits the developmental needs of the domestic market, food export markets, and strategic industries. 2. To fill in the research gaps in the literature about how the business sector in less developed countries cope with international obligations and pressure Previous studies tended to study regulations from the state perspective. To fill in the research gaps, this project conducted two surveys in China with the business sector - farms. In the first survey, this project has examined the phenomenon and pattern of pesticides overuse based on the data collected from 861 rice farmers in Jiangsu and Anhui provinces in China. These farmers range from those working in factory farms, to medium farms and individual farming households. The project has estimated the marginal productivity of pesticides and further explore factors leading to overuse of pesticide among farmers. The findings suggested that the marginal productivity of pesticides is close to zero, indicating that there is excessive use of pesticides in the surveyed areas. At the same time, farms which are export-oriented and on larger scale are less likely to overuse pesticides. In the second survey, data of 986 farmers from five major agricultural provinces in China were collected following a stratified random sampling method. Built on the theory of planned behaviour framework, the project has examined how perceived behavioural control, behavioural goal, behavioural attitude and subjective norm influenced farmers’ intention to comply with pesticide application standards. The results showed that perceived behavioural control was the most influential factor, while subjective norm was the least influential factor in determining farmers’ intention towards compliance with pesticide application standards. 3. To study how globalised risks are regulated at the national and supranational levels This project has analysed how China’s inter-governmental arrangements have functioned in different ways to reduce global food risks. While there is greater transparency, consistency, and inclusiveness in the process of setting food safety standards than in the past, the central government has almost exclusive power over these standards. Local governments are mainly responsible for gathering timely information and enforcing standards. This institutional design has redistributed costs for both the food producers and regulators alike, and enhanced public participation. In other words, the effectiveness of the food safety regulation system depends on the cooperation of all the parties concerned. Even though the government has legal authority, the transaction cost of enforcing that authority could be very high when food production is widely distributed as it tends to be in China. 4. To put forward the academic discussion by examining how and why the business sector adjusts its self-regulatory regime This project finds that voluntary compliance by a large number of small-and-medium-sized food producers, together with monitoring and reporting by the public, the mass media, and non-governmental organizations are crucial for successful food safety regulation. At the same time, this project has discovered that female farmers, farmers with knowledge about pesticide toxicity, pesticide residue and farmers who hold the view that massive use of pesticide is inimical to the environment, and farmers who participate in pesticide training organized by the government, are more likely to overuse pesticide. On the contrary, experienced farmers have a lower chance of overusing pesticides. In view of the findings, this project suggests that proper training should be provided for farmers. 5. To assess the explanatory power of existing theories on regulation Previous studies tended to focus on the role of external stakeholders such as government agencies and pesticide retailers when examining regulatory compliance, the attention paid to regulatees’ intrinsic motivations is relatively limited. To improve the theories on regulation, this project investigates into various psychological motivations and assess how they bring about compliance behaviours. Based on the survey results, this project finds that information and knowledge help the formation of awareness and risk perception, which in turn enhances compliance practices. 6. To conduct interviews and participant observations to collect in-depth information about the potential determinants of the control system Extensive fieldwork was conducted in the research period to collect information and data from primary and secondary sources. 39 interviews were conducted, with: six government officials at the central government level, 10 officials at the provincial level of Guangdong, five representatives from food industry associations located in Beijing and Guangdong Province, two representatives from civic organizations for food safety, nine managers of large-scale food enterprises located in Guangdong Province, three owners of small food workshops in Guangdong Province, two lawyers, one scientist, and one consultant to the central government body involved in national food standard-setting process. These individuals were selected because they either directly participated in, or were consulted, in the food standard-setting process. The comprehensive coverage of state and non-state actors in the regulatory landscape provides a solid background for understanding how food standard-setting in China has evolved. To collect primary data, the researcher also conducted participant observations in regulatory agencies and food businesses. She stayed in two regulatory agencies responsible for monitoring agricultural and manufactured food at the city level, and two food enterprises. 7. To provide policy insights about how food safety regulation in developing countries can be improved. This project does not only contribute to our understanding of the Chinese political, economic, and social spheres, but also provide implications for other developing countries and authoritarian regimes. This project finds that in the face of national strategic needs, such as promoting the global trade volume of certain products and compulsory international obligations, the authoritarian logic of decision making remains dominant. In other words, an accommodative regulatory approach is used by the government, which trichotomizes suitable standards and decision making processes for the developmental needs of different sectors. This could be described as a form of selective adaptation, which is a process by which foreign ideas are received and assimilated into local conditions especially in developing countries. Since “local conditions” are diverse among countries, this results in an array of different adaptations of international standards or standard-setting processes.

24606015.label: Major findings and research outcome
24606015.value: In the recent decade, food safety issue in China has elevated to national agenda and received much international attention. To better understand the evolving food safety regulatory regime, this project has studied the issue from the perspectives of standard-setting, information-gathering and behaviour-modification along the food supply chain. The project has examined the evolution of China’s food standard-setting procedures in the context of the internationalization of regulation (Chu, 2018). The findings suggest that after the reform and opening-up in 1978, state actors and leading enterprises in China had monopolized the process of national food standard-setting. With further participation in the global economy in the twenty-first century, China has become familiar with the international standard-setting procedures and modelled its domestic policy-making on these practices. This has resulted in a more transparent, inclusive, scientific, pluralized, and consensus-based form of decision-making. By contrast, the standards of the strategic industries have been harmonized to their international counterparts through a top-down and authoritarian approach. This project provides a new insight to the field by suggesting that China uses an accommodative approach, trichotomizing suitable standards and decision-making procedures, which befits the developmental needs of the domestic market, food export markets, and strategic industries. This project has also analysed how China’s inter-governmental arrangements have functioned in different ways to reduce food risk (Chu & Wang, 2018). While there is greater transparency, consistency, and inclusiveness in the process of setting food safety standards than in the past, the central government has almost exclusive power over these standards. Local governments are mainly responsible for gathering timely information and enforcing standards. This institutional design has redistributed costs for both the food producers and regulators alike, and enhanced public participation. Finally, the project has studied the behaviours of pesticides application of Chinese farmers, and identified the influential factors inducing pesticides overuse based on the data collected from 861 rice farmers in Jiangsu and Anhui provinces in China (Wang, Chu & Ma, 2018; Wang et al., 2017). The findings suggested that the marginal productivity of pesticides is close to zero, indicating that there is an excessive use of pesticides in the surveyed areas. The project has also discovered that female farmers, farmers with knowledge about pesticide toxicity, and farmers who hold the view that massive use of pesticide is inimical to the environment, are more likely to overuse pesticide. On the contrary, experienced farmers have a lower chance of overusing pesticides.

24606015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24606015.value: In terms of state regulation, the increasing responsiveness and pluralization in certain food industries’ standard-setting process, as well as factors that are influential over the regulatory changes should not be seen as a stable trend, as these principles are not institutionalized or mandated in the Chinese political structure. The political environment in China is constantly changing, and its style of governance, exemplified by items such as the tension between decentralization and recentralization, is largely determined by distinctive leadership styles that tend to have different priorities over time depending on the country’s strategic needs and plans. Thus, for future research, other determining factors that decide the regulatory approaches of the Chinese government should be explored further. In terms of self-regulation, non-deterrent and supporting measures such as guidance and education are supposed to facilitate self-motivations and hence regulatory compliance. Future work may study the role of other non-state actors such as farmers’ cooperatives and food certification bodies, and assess how they promote safe pesticide practices when compared with formal government regulation.

24606015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24606015.value: The research project examines the evolution of China’s food safety regulation in the context of the internationalization of regulation. By conducting extensive fieldwork to collect information and data from primary and secondary sources, this project suggests that through policy learning and modelling, the national food standard-setting procedure in China has become more transparent, inclusive, scientific, pluralized, and consensus-based. In particular, the accommodative approach of decision-making procedure allows the government to accommodate the developmental needs of different industries. At the same time, to enforce food standards and reduce food risks, China’s inter-governmental arrangements have functioned in different ways to redistribute costs for both the food producers and regulators, and enhance public participation in the regulatory process. In particular, while the central government has almost exclusive power over the setting of standards, local governments are mainly responsible for gathering timely information and enforcing standards. This research project also studies the compliance behaviours of the regulated food industry, and finds that pesticides overuses are common among Chinese farmers. This project suggests that in addition to state regulations, other non-state and non-deterrent measures have to be implemented in order to modify the non-compliance behaviours and reduce food-related risks.

24607115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24607115.value: The aim of the project is to investigate the early Khmer ceramic production centre of Angkor and its relation to Chinese ceramic production industries so as to assess to what extent Chinese elements were adopted by Khmer craftsmen during the ninth to fourteenth centuries. Although the artistic, historical and archaeological evidence of Khmer ceramic studies has been widely acknowledged in scholarship on Southeast Asian ceramic art and archaeology, previous studies have focused mostly on Khmer ceramic stylistic variations and kiln technology illustrations, leaving ceramic production sequence and its relationship with Chinese ceramic illustrations largely neglected. The neglect may be ascribed to the conventional assumption that early Khmer ceramic production centre was primary initial innovated without any in-depth level cultural exchange with China, in particular, vessels stacking skill for firing and kiln building technology and the wide gap emerged between the ceramic craftsmanship from two regions in the same period. This conventional assumption has lately been challenged, new archaeological evidence and chronometric data shed light on the changes in conception between cross-cultural exchange between China and Southeast Asia in pre-modern period. The proposed project aims to undertake an integrated study on Khmer ceramic production and establish a framework for analyzing the patterns and correlation between Chinese ceramic consumption in inhabited sites and Khmer ceramic production sites in Angkor. The outputs of the proposed project will include a database and a series of academic papers on the following issues: (1) The different and similarities between ceramic production sequence within various Khmer ceramic production sites in the Angkorian and post-Angkorian periods With the supply of solid and new archaeological evidence, the proposed project will consider if internal cultural exchange and technological innovation take place within various Khmer ceramic production sites in-depth level on production sequence for making ceramics. (2) Early Khmer ceramic production centre of Angkor and its relation to Chinese ceramic production industries Focusing on new archaeological evidence and an untouched source of ancient Chinese chronicles, recipe studies for making ceramics and image-analysis on petrography of ceramics, the study will examine the extent to which Chinese elements were adopted by Khmer ceramic craftsmen. (3) The integrated analysis on the connection between Chinese ceramic consumption in inhabited sites and Khmer ceramic production sites in Angkor The study will investigate the patterns and correlation between Chinese ceramic consumption sites and Khmer ceramic production sites in Angkor to study the modes of cultural exchange and social-economic motives behind Khmer ceramic production. 此研究計劃主要探討柬埔寨吳哥時期（九至十四世紀）高棉陶瓷業與中國之關係。以往高棉陶瓷業的研究主要集中在藝術、歷史與考古學研究幾方面，特別是陶瓷形制和紋飾的轉變及窯爐技術的討論, 陶瓷生產工序及其與中國陶瓷的關係討論甚少。一般認為高棉陶瓷業的革新與中國的文化交流只屬淺層水平，這主要因為兩地陶瓷工藝技術水平存在較大差異，例如裝燒陶瓷的方法及築窯技術的顯著不同。然而，隨著近年新考古及年代學證據不斷湧現，原有假設受到新挑戰。新證據讓我們重新審視歷史時期中國與東南亞跨文化交流的模式。本研究計劃旨在對高棉陶瓷業進行綜合研究，利用近年新考古及年代學等證據重構陶瓷生產工序；使用中國古代文獻、陶瓷配方及岩相學分析對比其與中國陶瓷的異同；綜合吳哥地區的居住遺址與高棉陶瓷生產窯址所出土的遺跡及遺物，討論兩地的跨文化交流模式及生產技術變革的社會經濟動因。

24607815.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24607815.value: 稅收与發展：以中國為例

24607815.label: Project Objectives
24607815.value: To analyse the relationship between tax incentives and development in the context of the development of international tax norms; To examine how China has sought to use its tax law regime, particularly its international tax system as a tool of economic development in attracting inward investment, encouraging cross-border trade, and, more recently, facilitating outbound investment; To evaluate the effect of China’s tax incentives and concessions on investment and hence development against the framework of international studies in this area; and To make recommendations for tax policy design for the purposes of effectively promoting development and facilitating economic activities between China and its major partners, particularly Hong Kong.
