To examine how China has sought to use its tax law regime, particularly its international tax system as a tool of economic development in attracting inward investment, encouraging cross-border trade, and, more recently, facilitating outbound investment;
To evaluate the effect of China’s tax incentives and concessions on investment and hence development against the framework of international studies in this area; and
To make recommendations for tax policy design for the purposes of effectively promoting development and facilitating economic activities between China and its major partners, particularly Hong Kong.

24607815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24607815.value: Taxation is viewed as a developmental tool that is vital to both state capacity-building, the furtherance of social and economic development, and enhancement of well-being for the general public. For the most part, the literature to date follows one of two general paths. One school looks at the relationship between good governance in administration including tax administration and revenue raising capacity. The other looks into the ways in which a country uses tax laws to offer incentives to encourage investment in developing countries or to attract investment within its own borders. The proposed research project focuses on the second school of tax and development studies, using China as a case study given the enormity of Chinese tax concessions to attract foreign direct investment and the significant impact of the practice on neighbouring jurisdictions, in particular Hong Kong, and jurisdictions outside of the region. The objectives of the project are to examine how China has sought to use its tax law regime, particularly its international tax system, as a tool of economic development in terms of attracting inward investment, encouraging cross-border trade, and, more recently, facilitating outbound investment. The study has two components. The first part looks at the question of tax incentives and development from a generic perspective to establish a framework for more specific analysis of Chinese initiatives. The second part examines the application of tax incentives in China, by reference to the benchmark framework established in the first part of study. The remarkable economic success in China within a comparatively short period has been viewed as primarily a result of foreign investment and international trade. The extent to which this investment has been made via tax incentives is, however, unclear. The study will evaluate the impact of China’s tax incentives and concessions on investment and hence development against the framework of international studies on this topic. The research findings will be of significant value to the evaluation of whether tax concessions should continue to be an element of China’s development programme or whether continuation or adoption of new concessions is providing unnecessary windfalls to investors without impacting significantly on China’s economic development.

24607815.label: Realisation of objectives
24607815.value: The four objectives envisaged in the research project have been completely fulfilled. The qualitative and quantitative research was systematically undertaken in line with the objectives. The realisation of each objective is summarised as follows. Objective 1: The analysis and conceptualisation of the relationship between taxation and development was the starting point of the research project. A thorough research documenting the development of the relationship was completed against the backdrop of the development of international tax norms. The research project documents three important findings on taxation and development from an international perspective. First, mobilising domestic resources for developing countries needs to focus on not only state building, accountability, and effective capacity development at macro level, but also improvement in specific tax rules such as rules to combat transfer pricing and the shifting of profits to low tax jurisdictions at micro level. It is also crucial for developing countries to enhance transparency in data reporting by multinational enterprises and in tax administration. Such findings benefit developed countries too, to the extent that they reflect their renewed awareness on the pitfalls of international and domestic tax regimes. Second, at international level, illicit capital outflows that are facilitated by tax systems susceptible to harmful tax practices and flawed tax administration have been identified as a key obstacle to revenue mobilisation for development. Solutions to this problem, however, rely on the joint efforts of both developing and developed countries but not individual countries alone. Third and last, in most recent years, the significant rise of the importance of taxation in the global and domestic political agenda has led to a notable paradigm shift in international tax practices and principles. In addressing the challenges of tax evasion and avoidance arising from cross-border trade and investment, the G20 and OECD have identified, among other things, that tax incentives and concessions to attract foreign investment, if used inappropriately, could harm the revenue interests of other countries and encourage aggressive tax avoidance. Against the general background, the project investigated and critiqued the literature discussing the role of taxation, in particular tax incentives, in attracting foreign investment for economic development in China over the last four decades. The literature has to date been rather limited, notwithstanding the extensive and frequent use of tax concessions in practice in China. By analysing and conceptualising the relationship between taxation and development with a China focus, this project generated a set of literature focusing on theories and empirical studies in general and in China in particular. This not only contributed to the scholarship in this area but laid a solid and necessary conceptual foundation for the research project. Objective 2: The objective of examining how China has used its tax law system as a development tool to encourage inward investment and facilitate outward investment was successfully fulfilled, which generated a comprehensive set of data. The set of data includes a subset of data of all currently effective tax incentives issued by the central government and a subset of tax sparing arrangements in all of China’s bilateral tax treaties concluded from the early 1980s to 2018. The first subset was carefully organised with a systematic categorisation of the types, functions, purposes and other key features of those formal incentives and concessions. Due to the constant changing of tax incentives and policies in China, the project made special effort to update the dataset through investigating and modifying relevant tax circulars providing the incentives and concessions at a 6-month interval during the research period. The dataset of tax incentives and sparing articles in tax treaties significantly extended the knowledge of the use of tax incentives in promoting economic development in emerging economies such as China. The dataset records various notable features of the use of tax incentives and concessions in China, such as the wide scope and the generosity of tax incentives on research and development (R&D) and the increasing emphasis on small and medium enterprises (SMEs), which to the best of my knowledge had never been formulated in a thorough and sophisticated way in any public or commercial database and in the existing literature. Objective 3: The evaluation of the effect of China’s tax incentives and concessions on development was fully achieved by way of qualitative and quantitative research. The former includes group discussions and individual interviews with government officials at central and city levels, tax practitioners, and selected resident and non-resident enterprise taxpayers. The latter primarily relied on existing landmark studies by international organisations, including the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank, and by tax researchers and scholars. The quantitative research also used the datasets collected in this project and official statistics on inward and outward investment to evaluate the correlation between the level of foreign direct investment in China and Chinese tax concessions targeting foreign investment. Such method was also applied to assess the link between tax concessions for outward investment and the level of Chinese investment oversees encouraged by China’s “Go Global” policy, typically the One Belt and One Road initiative (BRI) launched in 2013. Evaluating the role of tax incentives and concessions in investment, particularly foreign direct investment, has proved extremely challenging for scholars and policymakers. While the difficulty can be explained by many factors, this project focused on three aspects that are relevant to China’s context. First, tax law and policy operates not insolation but within a wider socio-economic framework. It is almost impossible to isolate the impact of particular strategies in a spectrum of developments as increased foreign direct investment could be driven by tax holidays and tax reductions, but could also be explained by other factors such as market size and easy access to skilled labour. Second, investment decisions are not made in static worlds, and changes in tax rules may be viewed by investors as valuable not in terms of after-tax monetary returns but in respect of their non-tax effect on protecting private investment in China given the country’s past history of nationalisation without compensation. Third, for cross-border investment, the impact of tax concessions in the host jurisdiction such as China depends as much as on the investor’s business structure and its home jurisdiction’s rules as it does on Chinese rules. Guided by this objective, the research project documented certain positive effects of the use of tax incentives on development in certain industrial sectors, but had not found conclusive evidence to prove such positive effects as a whole. Not surprisingly, the use of various tax incentives created many problems in tax administration and compliance. Objective 4: The research findings in realising objectives 1, 2 and 3 described above helped form a robust foundation for achieving the project’s final objective. In particular, the project highlights the importance of undertaking systematic and sophisticated research on tax incentives and concessions before putting them in use in the case of China. Absence or insufficiency of such research may result in costly operation and detriment to the rule of law in taxation in the country.

24607815.label: Major findings and research outcome
24607815.value: The research findings are summarised below. First, while tax incentives and concessions were initially to attract inbound investment into China, there has been a surge of the use of tax incentives in promoting outbound investment from China in recent years. This feature coincides with the Chinese government’s development policy, which has been shaped by not only its own development needs but also changes in international investment environment. Second, the project identified the different purposes of using tax incentives to foster economic growth between developing and developed countries. Although both general and targeted incentives could be adopted to serve various purposes, a hybrid of targeted and general tax incentives may be an efficient approach for developing countries, including China, to adopt in designing their tax policy to facilitate cross-border investment and trade. Third, legal documents on tax incentives need to be as much clear, detailed, and certain as possible. In China’s case, tax circulars providing tax incentives have been very fragmented and subject to constant change. The ambiguity of the rules has left too much discretion to tax administrators. The frequent change and ambiguity of tax rules have caused uncertainty and non-transparency problems to taxpayers, and increased administration costs. The centralisation of tax policy-making power at the national level and the competition for foreign investment between local governments has led to illegitimate tax practices at the local levels. Unless the tension between central and local fiscal relations is resolved, the illegitimate practices would continue in China. Fourth, the tax incentives may be exploited in tax avoidance and evasion schemes. Inappropriate use or manipulation by investors may cause significant revenue losses to jurisdictions involved in abuse activities. As a result of the globalisation and free trade had been a race-to-the-bottom competition between governments in using tax incentives to attract and retain foreign investment. The most recent reform on international taxation principles has attempted to prevent this phenomenon. The design of Chinese tax incentives must be in line with the new principles. Fifth and last, the project makes several recommendations on specific international tax rules in China. One such recommendation is to reform the current complex foreign tax credit (FTC) rules. The lack of efficient FTC rules to relieve double taxation has put Chinese enterprises in a disadvantageous position in the international market. A participation exemption for dividends may be a good approach in revising the FTC rules.

24607815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24607815.value: The current project has largely focused on tax incentives and concessions offered at the central level. Further research could be undertaken to explore the use of tax incentives and concessions at the local levels to gain more in-depth understanding on how tax incentives have actually been applied by different levels of government in practice. What are the differences in the local practices, and why such differences, given tax policies are all centrally made with prohibition on local modification? Further research can also be taken to exam specific areas or activities for which tax incentives and concessions are frequently provided, such as R&D, SMEs, and development of financial and capital markets. To what extent do the application of tax incentives on these activities generate positive results? Are there any other non-tax factors to explain the results? If no obvious positive effects, why such case? The collected dataset on tax incentives and literature in the area can be used to conduct the further research to address the research questions described above.

24607815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24607815.value: Tax incentives have been widely used to promote foreign direct investment, and in some cases to facilitate outward investment, by many government for economic development. The research project uses China as a case study to examine the relationship between taxation and development, given the enormity of Chinese tax concessions to attract foreign direct investment. China has used its tax law regime, particularly its international tax system, as a tool of economic development to encourage cross-border investment and trade. This research project evaluates the impact of China’s tax incentives and concessions on investment and hence development against the framework of international studies on this topic. The projects finds there is no affirmative evidence to prove significant impact of tax incentives on China’s economic development. It suggests that the adoption of tax concessions needs to be carefully studied and designed before they are put in operation as many concessions have merely provided unnecessary windfalls to investors without obvious positive impact on development. The introduction and application of tax concessions may lead to unintended consequences to government revenues and the development of rule of law in taxation.

24610615.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24610615.value: 大東亞共榮圏：日本在第二次世界大戰期間的混合帝國

24610615.label: Project Objectives
24610615.value: To explore the rise and fall of the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, Japan's new order in East Asia during World War II. To use the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere as a means to understand the nature and dynamics of the Japanese Empire, one of the most important but least-studied empires in the modern world. To place new light on the importance of Southeast Asia in Japan's expanding empire. In this context, I hope to show the negotiated nature of Japan's unfolding empire in Southeast Asia, and to investigate how weaker states on the periphery were able to exercise influence on Japan. To complicate the widely held assumptions that the Co-Prosperity Sphere was solely an instrument of Japanese oppression. Granted, Japan's wartime empire was highly brutal, oppressive, and domineering. But it was also useful in the colonial present. By focusing on the Philippines and Burma, I hope to reveal how the Co-Prosperity Sphere was useful for state-building projects and decolonization in Southeast Asia.

24610615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24610615.value: This research project aims to transform our understanding of the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere, Japan’s ambitious vision for a new order in Asia during World War II. In the process, I hope to break new ground in Japan studies and Southeast Asian studies, and to contribute to broader literature in the study of empire, international order, decolonization, and transnational history. Japan declared the Co-Prosperity Sphere on 1 August 1940 in a radio address by Foreign Minister Matsuoka Yōsuke. In part an autarkic economic bloc and in part a new regional community of nations, the creation of the Co-Prosperity Sphere by 1941 came to be accepted as the ultimate goal for Japan’s Empire and was invoked as the touchstone for all important national policies. This ultimate goal would be put into practice when Japan launched war against the West in late 1941. Since ridding Asia of the West became a critical component of the Sphere, existing scholarship largely focuses on whether the Sphere was a euphemism for imperialism or a sincere attempt at the liberation of Asia. The Co-Prosperity Sphere, however, remains understudied in two important ways. First, although the Sphere is understood to represent the height of Japanese expansionism, very little scholarship grapples seriously with its political visions in a way that sheds light on the new international order or empire that Japan sought to build. Second, most studies of Japan’s wartime empire remain firmly grounded in sources from the imperial center, so fail to account for the ways in which subordinate states made use of and at times influenced the Japanese Empire. My project will study the ruling elites in Japan, Burma, and the Philippines to fill these gaps in our scholarship. I hope to highlight the ways in which Japanese visions of the Co-Prosperity Sphere reflected new understandings of the Japanese Empire and its role in the international system. I suggest that Japan sought to construct a hybrid empire, a system that hierarchically divided Japan’s empire in a way that (perhaps unconsciously) reproduced Great Britain’s division of its own empire into dominions and crown colonies. Moreover, I aim to show how Japan's Co-Prosperity Sphere--although harsh, domineering, and brutal--was also useful in the colonial present. Filipino and Burmese leaders used the rhetoric and reality of the Co-Prosperity Sphere to engage in state-building projects and to create a future free of colonial control. 本研究計劃旨在改變我們對大東亞共榮圏的了解，日本在第二次世界大戰時的願景是在亞洲建立新秩序。在研究過程中，我希望可以在日本和東南亞研究開闢新見解，和為帝國、國際秩序、非殖民地化及跨國歷史研究的廣泛文獻作出貢獻。 於一九四零年八月一日，日本外相松岡洋右在電台發表建立大東亞共榮圏的宣言。所創造的共榮圏一部份為自給自足的經濟團體而另一部份為國家新地區聯盟，於一九四一年共榮圏被公認為日本帝國最終目標，和被援引為所有重要國家政策的標準。在一九四一年末，當日本對西方國家發動戰爭時，此最終目標將被付諸實行。由於共榮圏的重要成分是為亞洲擺脫西方控制，現行的學術研究大部份集中探討共榮圏是帝國主義之委婉說法，還是真誠試圖解放亞洲。 共榮圏在兩個重要方面仍缺乏研究。首先，雖然共榮圏代表日本擴張主義的高峰，很少研究竭力解决政治願景問題以闡明新國際秩序或日本試圖建立的帝國。其次，大部份日本戰時帝國之研究仍以帝國中心為依據，無法解釋附屬國怎樣利用此概念和不時影響日本帝國。 本計劃會研究日本、緬甸和菲律賓的統治精英以填補學術研究之缺口。我希望突出日本願景之共榮圏怎樣反映日本帝國的新詮釋和日本在國際體系中的角色。我認為日本尋求建立混合帝國，一個將日本帝國作分等級劃分之系統，而該系統在某程度上複製英國將其帝國劃分為自治領土和英國皇家殖民地。此外，我旨在顯示日本共榮圏 ─ 雖然嚴厲、專橫跋扈和殘酷 ─ 也對現行的殖民地有幫助。菲律賓和緬甸領袖利用共榮圏之言辭和事實從事建立國家的計劃，及創造擺脫殖民地統治的將來。

24610615.label: Realisation of objectives
24610615.value: I have completed my objectives for this project, and in some senses exceeded them. The research project intended to do four main things. First, it was meant to explore the rise and fall of the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere. Second, it used the Sphere as a window into Japan's wartime empire. Third, it placed new light on the importance of Southeast Asia in Japan's wartime empire. Fourth, and finally, this project highlighted the notion that Japan's wartime empire was brutal and oppressive, but also in some ways useful in the colonial present. I have achieved each of these objectives and more. My research has looked at Japanese visions for order during World War II in the Asia-Pacific, and investigated how those visions for order were interpreted, understood, and sometimes co-opted by nationalist elites in the Philippines and Burma. Thus, I have developed a broad-based understanding of Japan's ambitious attempt to create a new order in East Asia, and have also gained a strong understanding of Southeast Asia's position in the Co-Prosperity Sphere. In the process, I have published academic articles, and have a book on the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere forthcoming at Cornell University Press. The book will be released in the Spring or early summer of 2019.

24610615.label: Major findings and research outcome
24610615.value: My major findings are that the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere must be understood as more than a simple economic bloc, a slogan for Japanese imperialism and regional control, or the ultimate expression of a virulent Pan-Asian ideology. It was also a reaction to the challenges of diplomacy and empire in the post-World War I era, and a sincere attempt to envision a new type of political and economic order for the region during a time of turmoil. Further, although it was highly oppressive and domineering, the Co-Prosperity Sphere also featured active cooperation of nationalist elites across East and Southeast Asia. My book project thus highlights the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere as a contested process, both in Japan and across Asia. In Japan, intellectual and policy elites struggled to define what it was and how it would shape the postwar order. Various groups engaged in debates and domestic struggles to promote their own visions for the future. But since it was dependent on success in a war Japan had little chance in winning, the Sphere never became a true ideology. It never consolidated into a consistent way of looking at the world or of ordering public affairs and private lives. Instead, it was constantly in flux. For nationalist actors in Southeast Asia, however, collaboration within the Sphere provided the context for their continuing efforts toward independence and decolonization. Nationalist elites in the colonial capitals of Manila and Rangoon can be thought of as "patriotic collaborators" who co-opted aspects of Japan’s wartime empire. They pursued state-building efforts, and in the process sought to use the Japanese Empire for anti-colonial ends.

24610615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24610615.value: I do not intend to develop this research any further. That said, future research could tie Japanese high policy to developments in other Southeast Asian territories, like the Netherlands Indies, French Indochina, or British Malaya. Moreover, there is also room for further research in the Philippines and Burma, to show how legacies of World War II impacted both countries' future political, economic, and social trajectories.

24610615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24610615.value: This is transnational historical research on World War II in Asia. It studies Japanese visions for the future during World War II, and how those visions were understood, interpreted, and co-opted by "patriotic collaborators" in the Philippines and Burma. Studying the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere is important because the Sphere was always more than a slogan: it was also the epitome of Japan's goals for the region, and vision for political-economic order that bound the region to Japan. In this sense, understanding the Co-Prosperity Sphere is important for understanding Japan's motives and goals for waging a war for Asia. This also provides a historical corrective about the crucible of the 1940s. The era of World War II in Asia was in part the history of a brutal, oppressive, and domineering Japan attempting to take forcible control of Asia. But this history also had important impacts for East and Southeast Asia--without exploring the Co-Prosperity Sphere, we cannot truly understand ways in which Asian decolonisation began. Also, exploring the Sphere provides a useful corrective to those in Japan who still view the Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere as the zenith of Japan’s “holy war” and a sincere effort to liberate Asia.

24613115.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24613115.value: 青少年抽菸成因分析: 同儕效果及性格之交互作用

24613115.label: Project Objectives
24613115.value: Define and operationalize personality, and study its impacts on adolescent's smoking decision. Investigate whether individuals with similar personalities are more likely to nominate each other as friends, i.e. study whether personality is one of the selection criteria for social interactions. Study how peer effects on smoking are different within and across peers of different personalities, using the selection-corrected spatial autoregressive (SC-SAR) model. Explore the robustness of the results, and the extent to which the results are generalizable to different settings, countries, and health behaviors.

(ii) 檢驗本研究的發現是否在不同的群體或國家依然存在 (iii) 研究性格本身是否會受同儕影響. 同儕效果的研究通常都面對兩個主要的認定問題. 首先, “映射問題” 討論當個人受到同儕行為影響時,同儕也受到個人行為的影響. 因此要區別同儕對你,或是你對同儕的影響是困難的. 第二個問題是來自 “相關效果”. 此效果認為同儕之間行為的雷同有部分是來自於環境上共通性,例如相同的教室及相同的老師.本研究所使用的空間計量模型將利用詳細的朋友網絡資料來解決 ”映射問題.” 為了處理個人層面的 ”相關效果,” 我們將拓展一般的空間計量模型並導入網絡形成的分析. 此分析網絡形成的計量模型將引用虛擬變數來捕捉個人層面所觀察不到的要素,例如能力,偏好, 對於朋友選擇及行為變數的共通影響. 我們將利用所謂的“安慰劑檢驗”來測試此模型是否能處理此困難的同儕效果認定問題. 本研究計畫所使用的主要資料欄來自於美國的青少年健康長期追蹤計畫.使用此追蹤計畫資料有三個好處: 首先, 次計畫資料提供詳細的青少年朋友資訊幫助我們解決同儕研究中的 “映射問題.”其次, 次計畫中的某些問卷可被利用於衡量青少年的三大性格指標:情緒不穩定性,嚴謹自律性,及外向性.此三大性格指標將提供我們研究同儕效果在性格方向的異質性.最後,此追蹤資料主要的受訪對象是七年級至十二年級的中學生.由於大部份的成年抽菸者反映18歲是他們開始抽菸的年紀,因此我們所使用的追蹤資料可提供最相關的群體來研究抽菸行為開始的原因.

24613115.label: Realisation of objectives
24613115.value: We report the accomplishment of the project and the associating research activities in correspondence to the project objectives. I. Define and operationalize personality, and study its impacts on adolescent's smoking decision. We adopt the widely-accepted taxonomy from the Psychology literature, which is the so-called “Big Five”, to measure personality. • Openness to experience (“the degree to which a person needs intellectual stimulation, change, and variety”) • Conscientiousness (“the degree to which a person is willing to comply with conventional rules, norms, and standards”) • Extraversion (“the degree to which a person needs attention and social interaction”) • Agreeableness (“the degree to which a person needs pleasant and harmonious relations with others”) • Emotional stability (or Neuroticism, “the degree to which an individual experiences the world as threatening and beyond his/her control”) Using Add Health as the empirical data set in the project, we follow Young and Beaujean (2011) to use the factor analysis to extract the measures of Emotional stability, Conscientiousness, and Extraversion from various survey responses. Unfortunately, Add Health does not provide survey questions which allow us to extract personality on openness to experience and Agreeableness. The survey questions in Add Health and the corresponding personality measures are listed in the Appendix Table A1 of the attached paper. Based on the result of factor analysis, we obtain the personality measure for each individual students in our sample. The summary statistics of variables (including the dependent variable, smoking dummy, smoking frequency, and drunk dummy, and other independent variables) are provided in Table 1 of the attached paper. The three personality measures that we use in the project are listed in the first column, namely, emotional stability, conscientiousness, and extraversion. Other than the full sample, we also classify the sample into the strong and weak personality groups based on the group average of personality measure. The mean and standard deviation of the personality measures are also reported in Table 1. The impacts of personality on adolescent's smoking decision are summarized in Table 4. We find that students who are emotionally stable, conscientious and extrovert are less likely to be smoker or smoke less frequently. II. Investigate whether individuals with similar personalities are more likely to nominate each other as friends, i.e. study whether personality is one of the selection criteria for social interactions. We examine whether there is a homophily effect in terms of personality or not. We specify a network link formation model and specify the difference of personality measures as explanatory variables. To be specific, the model is specified as a Logit model in Equation (4) of the attached paper. The estimation results from the Add Health are presented in Table 5. From the estimated coefficients and standard errors, we found that emotional stability and extraversion are important for network link formation, while conscientiousness is not. The larger the difference between two individuals’ personality measures, the less likely that two individuals will form friendships. III. Study how peer effects on smoking are different within and across peers of different personalities, using the selection-corrected spatial autoregressive (SC-SAR) model. We study four kinds of peer effects within and across weak and strong personality groups, i.e., weak-to-weak, weak-to-strong, strong-to-weak, strong-to-strong. We specify the SC-SAR model by incorporating latent variables which influence both network link formation and outcome interactions. The model is specified in Equation (5) of the attached paper. In the above equation, individual own latent variables Z and correlated latent variables WZ are controlled, and thus we can dissolve the issue of omitting variables which result in an endogeneity bias on estimates of peer effects. We compare two sets of estimation results from the Add Health. The first one is based on the SAR model which is presented in Table 4 of the attached paper, while the second one is based on the SC-SAR model which is presented in Table 5. From the SAR model results, when studying heterogeneous peer effects (columns 3 and 4) for the binary indicator of smoking, it is found that the peer effect from “weaker” personalities to “weaker” personalities is strongest, albeit more strikingly so for emotional stability than for conscientiousness. Two individuals who are both emotionally unstable affect each other more in smoking, compared with two individuals of which at least one is emotionally stable. However, the results for smoking frequency (columns 7 and 8) show that emotionally unstable individuals are affected by both weak and stronger peers, while emotionally stable individuals are affected much less. Since emotionally stable peers tend to smoke less, the smaller estimated peer effect from strong-to-weak in the binary definition of smoking is therefore likely to be driven by a lower frequency of smoking among the “strong” peers. Comparing results of SAR model in Table 4 with the results of SC-SAR model in Table 5, one can see that estimates of endogenous effects drop when replacing the SAR model with the SC-SAR model, which show the effectiveness of endogeneity bias correction. IV. Explore the robustness of the results, and the extent to which the results are generalizable to different settings, countries, and health behaviors. Our binary definition of smoking arbitrarily classifies individuals who smoke at least once a month as smokers, while others as non-smokers. Here, we investigate the robustness to this definition, by using a more restrictive definition of smokers as those smoking at least once per week. The results are very similar to our main definition (See the results in Appendix Table A12). Additional robustness check is to study how specific results are for the case of smoking. Smoking is known to (i) severely affect health, (ii) be related to personality, and (iii) be vulnerable to peer pressure, and therefore represents an excellent outcome of our study. Nonetheless, if our results are specific to smoking, this would limit the moderating role of personality in general social interactions. Therefore, we estimated the same set of models for another health behavior that is known to affect health and to be vulnerable to peer pressure: the prevalence of getting drunk. We present the homogenous and heterogeneous peer effects on getting drunk (See the Appendix Table A12). The average peer effects are slightly smaller for getting drunk than for smoking, in particular given the higher prevalence of getting drunk vs. smoking (31 percent vs. 22 percent). Nonetheless, we observe a very similar pattern when stratifying the sample with respect to personality. The interactions between two individuals who are both emotionally unstable are most vulnerable to peer effects, while the other interactions are closer to the average peer effect. This suggests that the vulnerability of social interactions among emotionally unstable individuals is not specific to smoking, but a general finding that exists across a wider set of unhealthy behaviors. Although we study robustness of the results using the other behavior outcomes, but unfortunately we are not be able to examine robustness of results using the other data sets because we later found out the second proposed data set -- Framingham Heart Study -- keeps its network data confidential and does not release to outside research groups. There is the same issue for the third Taiwanese adolescent development and adaptation data set.

24613115.label: Major findings and research outcome
24613115.value: We used friendship nominations from the Add Health data to study peer effects in smoking; in particular, whether peer effects are weaker among emotionally stable and conscientious individuals. We extended the SAR model to (i) correct for the endogeneity of the spatial weight matrix, (ii) estimate heterogeneity in peer effects, and (iii) allow for unobserved contextual effects. Our results suggest that the conventional SAR model overestimates endogenous peer effects, yet that our extended SC-SAR model provides a promising method for studying homogenous and heterogeneous peer effects. Our main conclusion is that an individual’s personality plays a very important role in social interactions, and it does so along two main dimensions. First, the average peer effect masks considerable heterogeneity in responses with respect to personality. Even though the average peer effect in smoking is non-negligible, it is particularly pronounced within certain subgroups of students. We show that the individual personality trait of emotional stability is an important moderator of peer effects. Emotionally unstable students are significantly more vulnerable to peer effects than emotionally stable students. Despite being an important driver of smoking decisions, we find no evidence that conscientiousness plays a similar role in social interactions. Second, apart from moderating the vulnerability to peer effects, personality also plays a role in friendship formation: individuals with similar personalities are more likely to hang out with each other. This is consistent with studies in social psychology that suggest that even though generally people value the opinion of high-status or popular peers, not all adolescents desire identification with high-status peers. Instead, they will adopt a local set of norms that may be more salient to these adolescent’s identity development.

24613115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24613115.value: One direction to further develop this research is to consider the dynamic (co)evolution of networks, smoking outcomes, and personality. Since the current study uses the cross-sectional individual and network data, it relies on somewhat ad hoc model assumptions to break the simultaneity of these three endogenous variables. If there is a panel data of network links, individual characteristics including personality, and smoking outcomes, we can exploit variations of variables over time to enhance the argument of causality in our approach. Nonetheless, given data availability, it will be interesting to further study the moderating role of personality on peer effects for long-term outcomes such as working status, marriage status, and others.

24613115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24613115.value: This research project finds new evidence from a survey data of U.S. high school students that one individual personality -- emotional stability -- can moderate the size of peer effect on adolescents' smoking behaviors. Compared to other cases, when two emotional unstable students interact, there is a higher chance that the non-smoker will be influenced by the smoker and starts to smoke. We also finds that individuals with similar personalities are more likely to hang out with each other. As a result, these two findings suggest a potentially harmful cycle in which emotionally unstable individuals are more likely to smoke in the first place, are likely to hang out with other emotionally unstable individuals, and in turn lack the skills to stand up against the peer pressure of initiating/continuing smoking. This pattern is not restricted just to smoking, but also holds for the prevalence of getting drunk. Hence, the benefits of personality traits such as emotional stability in social interactions provide a promising mechanism through which personality affects health behavior, and potentially even socioeconomic life outcomes.

24613415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24613415.value: 香港的民主正處於轉型的階段。由於目前半數立法會席次以及香港特首並非經由民主選舉產生，學者、政治人物和公民都對香港尚未完善發展的民主選舉制度表示憂心。香港2017年的特首普選因此成為香港最重要的政治議題之一。普選議題不僅造成香港黨派的對立以及對民主定義的爭論，更引起國外媒體的注意。 此研究計畫引用網絡結構議題設定(network agenda setting)和黨派選擇性接觸(partisan selective exposure)這兩個理論框架來檢驗媒體如何報導普選議題。此外，也分析香港公民在選擇性接觸政黨媒體後對此議題的認知結構。 進一步說明，此計畫要探討： • 香港與台灣的媒體在針對香港特首普選議題的網絡結構議題屬性為何？政黨媒體造成網絡結構議題屬性上有何種差異？政黨媒體的網絡結構議題屬性是否有跨國上的異同？ • 香港民眾對於特首普選的網絡結構議題屬性為何？香港民眾的政黨傾向是否會影響他們對普選議題的認知和網絡結構議題屬性？ • 媒體與公眾的網絡結構議題屬性如何演化？如何相關？ • 政黨媒體的網絡結構議題設定和黨派選擇性接觸如何影響民眾的認知、態度與政治行為？ 美國已經有許多網絡結構議題設定的相關文獻，但是擁有不同政治文化脈絡的亞洲區相關研究仍少。黨派選擇性接觸的相關文獻也指出政黨媒體在閱聽眾選擇性接觸政黨媒體時會強化議題設定效果。這一現象使學者們憂心社會民主化的發展。因此，此研究將分析普選議題的相關屬性在不同的媒體中如何連結架構。議題屬性的網絡結構顯著性又將如何植入民心。此外，檢測香港與台灣媒體針對普選議題的報導亦可以了解跨國間的媒體議題設定。此研究的時間長度也同時可以了解媒體報導與公眾意見對此議題的演化。 此研究的結果將推進網絡結構議題設定和黨派選擇性接觸的相關研究。研究主題因關注現時香港最具爭議性的普選議題，也有很高的社會影響力，更可進而對媒體效果，民意演化，以及民主社會的發展有所貢獻。

24613415.label: Realisation of objectives
24613415.value: Overall, the three objectives set out in this project have been achieved. Drawing upon three theoretical concepts—the network agenda setting model, selective exposure, and deliberation—this project examined how Hong Kong media shape a political issue in different ways and link different attributes to portray the political issue. It also investigated how citizens consume different news media and develop the perception of the issue in a network-like cognitive structure. In addition to assessing issue perception as an outcome of citizen competence, this project paid attention to cognitive, attitudinal and behavioral outcomes. It also extends the definition of media consumption from traditional media use to social and mobile media use. The network agenda setting model has been empirically tested in the United States, but evidence is still lacking of network agenda setting effects in Asia. The PI and three coders conducted a content analysis of coverage of the universal suffrage issue in Wen Wei Pai, Ming Pao and Apple Daily from January to August 2015. Results from the content analysis demonstrate that in the Hong Kong newspapers, political attributes dominate the discussion on the general election as they are located at the center of the network and have the highest centrality in all three networks, and there are nuanced differences among the three outlets in terms of attribute adoption and associations among attributes. Second, rather than focusing on the universal suffrage issue, which was relatively short-lived and has become less salient as this project has progressed (I have addressed this in the mid-term report and also in the project change), the PI shifted to examine the Hong Kong-mainland China relationship. Because the Hong Kong-mainland China relationship is more general and covers diverse topics and attributes, Hong Kong respondents were more willing to speak up and answer the thought-listing task in the online survey after several rounds of pilot testing struggled to improve the response to the open-ended mind-mapping questions in the survey. This issue provides the flexibility to capture media and public agenda. The PI conducted another round of content analysis of 30 Hong Kong media outlets with the help of three coders. WiseNews and Crimson Hexagon were the two databases used to retrieve relevant news articles. The results demonstrate that pro-establishment and pro-democracy media connect different attributes to portray the Hong Kong-mainland China relationship. For instance, the cultural and self-identity attribute is often paired with the social movement attribute in pro-democracy media, while it is often paired with the mainland politics attribute in the pro-establishment media. The social welfare attribute is also paired with the population and mobility attribute in pro-establishment media, but not in pro-democracy media. These findings demonstrate that partisan media can create and strengthen the connection between attributes when covering an issue. News media might not adequately perform their role as crucial sources of political information, but instead deliver slanted information because of their political position and to cater to their target audience’s political preferences. In sum, the first objective was achieved. For the second objective, three surveys were carried out. The first survey was to understand the issue of universal suffrage in 2015. The 2015 survey asks many questions about media use and political predisposition and includes a thought-listing task to understand the cognitive mapping of the universal suffrage issue in Hong Kong. In this task, respondents were asked to write down the first things that come to their minds and then expand those things into branches and sub-branches as fast as they can. The second survey asked similar questions but focused on the 2016 Hong Kong Legislative Council. In the second survey, questions about new media technology use (such as social media and mobile media), network characteristics (i.e., network heterogeneity), and measures adopted in spiral of silence research (i.e., self-censorship, outspokenness, and opinion expression) were included given that the mind-mapping questions did not successfully capture people’s cognitive processing in the 2015 representative survey. Building on previous fieldwork experience and findings, the PI conducted the third survey in 2017. The PI incorporated the deliberation literature and the concept of argument repertoire to develop the measure of opinion repertoire. Opinion repertoire helps to understand the network agenda setting effect not only on individuals’ own opinion repertoire, but also on their thoughts about how oppositional others perceive the issue. This distinction proved to be significant, as it served to add another layer of explanation to the selective exposure effect. Because it remains unknown to what extent the public’s network agenda would be affected by news media with different political orientations, which can be considered pro- or counter-attitudinal to a citizen in terms of his or her political leaning, the PI also furthered the agenda setting literature by distinguishing the consumption of partisan media as consumption of either pro- or counter-attitudinal media. The findings document that different partisan media had different network agenda setting effects on either one’s own or oppositional repertoire, depending on whether an individual engaged in partisan selective exposure or not. The PI advanced the study of network agenda setting methodologically by adopting the measure of explicit association between attributes (i.e., asking respondents to indicate the strength of the association between two attributes they came up with) and opinion repertoire. The PI also made a theoretical advance by considering individuals’ media consumption patterns, highlighting the effect of pro- and counter-attitudinal media on citizens’ issue perception in the network agenda setting model and developing different cognition dimensions of issue perception (i.e., one’s own and the oppositional opinion repertoires.) The second objective was achieved. The third objective was achieved through the assessment of media consumption and different forms of citizen competence via the above representative surveys. In addition to the findings that traditional news media can influence not only how we think about an issue and related attributes, but also how we think the oppositional others think about an issue and related attributes, the PI also identified the significant role of social and mobile media in influencing the reasoning process (i.e., expressive and discussion behaviors), knowledge, attitude and behaviors. Results show that the levels of counter-attitudinal information (i.e., political disagreement) and publicness promote the spiral of silence on social media and make Hong Kong citizens less likely to express disagreeing opinions and more likely to withdraw from social media activities, such as actively deleting posts. The PI also found that social and mobile use for news as a second screen promotes political expressive behaviors, enhances political knowledge and heightens political efficacy. These outcomes also serve as mediators, which in turn mobilize participatory behaviors. Overall, the findings highlight the network agenda setting effect in Hong Kong and the significant role of traditional and digital media in influencing cognitive processing and attitudinal and behavioral consequences. In sum, all objectives are well achieved through content analysis and representative surveys in different stages of studies.

24613415.label: Major findings and research outcome
24613415.value: This project has generated insights on the network agenda setting model, selective exposure and the important roles of digital media in citizen competence. [Example: Chen et al. (2020). Network agenda setting, partisan selective exposure, and opinion repertoire]. The findings first support a general network agenda setting effect that the news media are able to transfer the salience of a network of attributes—not just the salience of individual items—to the public agenda. The project further advances the theories by demonstrating that different partisan media had different NAS effects on either one’s own or oppositional repertoire, depending on whether an individual engaged in partisan selective exposure or not. Results show that among those who demonstrated a pattern of partisan selective exposure, pro-attitudinal media consumption was significantly related to not only how they think of an issue, but also they people think that oppositional others perceive the issue. By contrast, for those who did not engage in partisan selective exposure, counter-attitudinal media consumption was significantly associated with the perspectives of oppositional others. This project found that a portion of people in Hong Kong consumed more pro-attitudinal information than any other types of information, which could potentially cause an echo chamber effect since their political beliefs appeared to be significantly related to the proattitudinal media they consumed. These people’s information processing pattern would strengthen their existing political position or attitude and foster a stereotyped evaluation of the political outgroup because their mental maps of the outgroup party were significantly related to the likeminded media. This would inevitably reinforce the political polarization of society, blocking the opportunity to bridge political divides in Hong Kong. This project also identifies the vital role of social and mobile media in facilitating hybrid media practice and promoting different pathways through enhancing cognitive, psychological, attitudinal and participatory outcomes to engage in politics [Examples: Chen, H.-T. (2019). Second screening and the engaged public; Chen, H.-T., & Li, X. (2017). The contribution of mobile social media to social capital and psychological well-being]. However, the findings also demonstrated that when counter-attitudinal political perspective and publicness are heightened in one’s social network, the spiral of silence process will be enhanced on social media, and people will be less likely to express disagreeing opinion and more likely to withdraw from social media activities [Example: Chen, H.-T. (2018). Spiral of silence on social media and the moderating role of disagreement and publicness in the network].

24613415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24613415.value: This project has extended the network agenda setting model in several theoretical and methodological aspects. The understanding of how the effect of network agenda setting varies based on one’s partisan selective exposure and how pro- and counter-attitudinal media relate to one’s own and oppositional opinion repertoires could lead to further research with more classic deliberation measures, such as argumentation, political debates, and interpersonal discussion. This project also probes the complexity of public opinion and cognitive processing, which is worthy of further investigation of different cognitive dimensions. For instance, in addition to one’s own and opposition opinion repertoire, how one perceives those with the same partisanships think of an issue can be further developed. Further research can focus on different types of issue given that Hong Kong’s political climate has increasingly become more polarized and Hong Kong’s media landscape is continuously evolving. This project also acknowledges the limitation in content analysis that comes from limited content and human coding. Computational analysis and supervised machine learning can be included in the further development of the research to analyze more comprehensive traditional and social media content and compare the effect of network agenda setting across different countries and regions.

24613415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24613415.value: This project examined the network agenda setting effects of pro- and counter-attitudinal media on Hongkongers’ perceptions of the Hong Kong-mainland China relationship. Through this project, we understand that news media can influence individuals’ cognitive perception not only by telling us what to think about and how to think about it, but also how to associate different messages in news media. More importantly, news media affect not only how we think of an issue, but also how we perceive the oppositional others think of an issue. Accordingly, when partisan media outlets cover issues in a different way, they will lead partisans to view the political world differently. However, it is worth noting that one’s news media consumption patterns matter in this effect given that partisan media have a stronger influence on how partisans perceive an issue when they consume pro-attitudinal media compared to counter-attitudinal media. If people have a relatively more balanced media diet from different sides of media, counter-attitudinal media can help partisans to understand oppositional others’ perspectives and form more accurate mental maps of oppositional others.

24613715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24613715.value: 香港政策建议者的政治化与政策建议的外部化

24613715.label: Project Objectives
24613715.value: First I will study the impact of politicization of policy advisors on policy advisory activities at the system level. I will survey and interview politically appointed policy advisors, senior and middle civil service advisors, members of statutory advisory bodies, managers of major think tanks and legislators to gauge their views of change of policy advisory activities. Second I will specifically focus on three policy domains where new values and political demands emerge: first, in the environmental policy domain (new values and technology emerge from civil society to challenge traditional values of economic development); second, in the education policy domain (competing values on issues of curriculum design in response to integration with China); third, in labor-business relations (competing values in response to the widening wealth gap). Lastly I will study the impact of the nature of policy problems on the externalization of policy advice. Policy issues in each of three selected policy domains along two dimensions will be reviewed: high/low degrees of reliance upon scientific and technical policy advice; high/low degrees of values conflicts/partisan interests in the policy community. I expect that politicization of policy advisors has less impact on the supply of policy advice in issues that have a lower level of value conflicts and partisan politics.

24613715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24613715.value: Policy advisory systems are important because they concern the quality of policy advice and ultimately the quality of governance. This project aims to contribute to the theory of policy advisory system by studying the impact of politicization of policy advisors on the supply of policy advice in a democratizing environment. Unlike other studies that focus on role perception of policy advisors and location of policy advice, this study seeks to explain both locational and qualitative dimensions of policy advice by looking at governance structural change. Using survey and interview questionnaires that include items from previous studies conducted in Canada, New Zealand, Belgium, Denmark and European Union, we can compare Hong Kong’s development of policy advisory system in a democratizing environment to those in democratized countries. This study examines the development of policy advisory system in Hong Kong during three periods, 1997 to 2002, 2002 to 2008, and 2008 to the present. By explaining variation of externalization of policy advice among cases in policy domains where new values and interests emerge to challenge the dominating values and interests, the study also tests whether the nature of policy problems moderates or amplifies the effect of politicization of policy advisors on the location and content of policy advice. Through archival analysis and interviews, I will also identify changes of policy advice supply over time on similar issues. This study is the first step towards understanding the impact of changing political context on the policy advisory system in Hong Kong. The next questions in future research include what types of policy advice are more influential in policy decisions, how policy advisory system will evolve and whether it will contribute to democratic governance. 摘要： 本课题旨在研究在一个民主化的环境中政策建议者的政治化对政策建议供给的影响，以此对推进政策建议体系理论做出贡献。 本课题将对香港自1997年至今的政策建议体系的发展进行调查，主要着眼于政治委任的政策建议者与高级公务员之间在某些政策子系统中进行政策建议活动时是如何分工的。 为理解政策建议活动中内外政策建议者之间的网络关系，本课题主要研究人员将会对法定和咨询机构进行问卷调查，并会访谈所有活跃的智库，立法会成员以及主要党派的领导人及其助理。 问卷和访谈将集中于研究政策建议者和政策建议的特征，获取建议和产生建议的过程，政策建议者自我认知的角色，政策建议活动的变化，以及影响政策建议影响力和质素的因素。主要研究人员将会比较不同政策建议者的回应。

24615215.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24615215.value: 中国城市中的抗争管理：威胁、可见度与变迁

24615215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24615215.value: This research will examine state-society relations in urban China at a critical node of state power and citizen rights: state responses to popular protests. Protest management in authoritarian regimes is an emerging field of studies in contentious politics, and the case of China presents a puzzle. On the one hand, the authorities have been unrelenting, or even increasingly harsh, in response to some forms of dissent, such as political or ethnic activism. On the other hand, China’s leaders have spent substantial efforts on the professionalization of protest management: they have regulated local authorities’ behavior and have counseled against coercion when more mundane demands are voiced. It is reasonable to suggest that quantitatively, repression has declined over recent years, and that qualitatively, the repertoire has divided into two lines. This bifurcation of coercive behavior warrants further substantiation and explanation. Scholars have begun to engage in conceptual work and have offered case studies. So far, however, little systematic data collection has been pursued. Evidence has therefore remained anecdotal and fragmented. This research seeks to fill this particular gap. Using a broad range of media sources, it will collect evidence on protest incidents in urban China between 2007 and 2014. The project will quantitatively examine how dimensions of threat and media visibility affect the state’s inclination to use coercion and how the repertoire of repression has evolved over time. It will also draw on interviews with government officials and policy researchers, in conjunction with an analysis of archival materials. Theoretically, the generated evidence will open new opportunities to engage broader scholarly debates on state coercion and authoritarian resilience, social movement societies, and protest policing. Practically, it will help to understand an ongoing transformation of coercive practices in China that has not yet been widely recognized by the policy community. The research will be carried out between 1st September 2015 and 31st August 2018. It is expected to produce several articles in peer-reviewed academic journals. 这项研究将考察中国城市的国家与社会关系在国家权力与公民权利的一个关键节点：国家应对民众抗争。 威权国家的群众抗争管理是抗争政治学中新兴的领域，中国的情况就是其中一个未解的难题。一方面，中国政府一直无情甚至是越来越苛刻地应对某些类型的抗争，如政治异见或民族主义事件；而另一方面，领导人又努力推进抗争管理专业化：他们监管地方政府的行为，当民众只是提出一些民生方面的要求时，他们会劝阻地方政府采用强硬手段。所以，有理由相信，从数量上看，抗争的打压越来越少，从性质上看，抗争控制策略已经发展出两条分支，这一发展需要进一步细化和解释。 学者们已经进行了一些概念性工作，并且提供了一些案例，但是鲜有进行系统性的数据收集。因此，目前的证据通常仅为一些零散的记事。本研究旨在填补这个空白。 这项研究将收集中国城镇2007年至2014年期间的媒体报道的抗争事件，然后定量考察事件本身对政府的挑战以及媒体报道可见度这两个范畴是如何影响国家使用强制措施的倾向性，同时也考察政府的抗争管理策略如何演变。研究将访问政府官员、政策研究者，同时也将分析现有的文件资料。 理论上，新收集到的证据会为更广阔的学术议题提供新的探讨机会，如国家强制、威权韧性、社会运动以及示威控制。实证上，它将有助于理解强制抗争管理策略的转型，而这一正在进行中的转型尚未得到政策界的广泛认识。 这项研究将于2015年9月1日开始，至2018年8月31日结束，预期产生多篇国际认可的学术期刊论文。

24618115.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24618115.value: 解離傾向者的自我相關社會認知功能：實驗心理病理學研究

24618115.label: Project Objectives
24618115.value: To study the source attribution of mental representations generated by oneself or derived from other people in different dissociation groups. If the hypothetical diminished sense of self is a socio-cognitive dysfunction of dissociation proneness, a tendency to misattribute the source of self-generated items as other-provided is expected in nonclinical dissociators. To examine whether the classic effect of self-referential processing on item recognition will be weakened in dissociators. According to the hypothesis, the diminished sense of self may influence the process of referring an item to oneself. As a consequence, the beneficial effect of self-referential processing on memory may appear in non-dissociators but decrease in dissociators. To test whether dissociators will perform differently than non-dissociators at spatial judgment on the basis of ego- or allo-centric reference frame. According to the hypothesis, incongruency stimulated from these two frames should not interfere with dissociators compared with non-dissociators. To investigate whether dissociators are less capable of accurately detecting the mental states of others. As a clear sense of self is a requisite for mind reading capability, dissociators may confuse the perception of other people’s mental states with their own feelings and perform poorer than non-dissociators on mind reading tests. To test if dissociators’ atypical performance on the socio-cognitive tasks can be statistically accounted for by early interpersonal adversity (parental dysfunction or potentially traumatizing events). To examine whether the atypical socio-cognitive performance is specifically linked to dissociation proneness when other comorbid psychopathology is controlled.

24618115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24618115.value: 解離是一種精神功能失常的表現，臨床的特徵是原本整合良好的心智功能遭受打斷，例如與情緒和身體感受脫離（失自我感），無法提取自傳式記憶（解離性失憶），和動作執行缺乏自我控制感（認同轉換）。解離的病理機轉一直是研究者關注的問題，過去的研究多將注意力擺在童年負向人際經驗和一般認知失能，沒有太多的研究以自我感的異常來概念化解離。然而自我感的改變卻是許多解離症狀的共通特色。這個研究計畫的假設是自我感的異常是發展出解離傾向體質的一個內生性因子，而這個自我相關的社會認知脆弱性可經由檢測解離傾向者在自我相關的訊息處理而獲得。這個假設在我過去的一個臨床研究中獲得初步支持，我的結果顯示有高解離症狀的精神科病人相較於低解離症狀的病人對自我提取的實驗項目犯了較多來源歸因的錯誤，而兩組病人對實驗者提供實驗項目的來源歸因錯誤則無顯著差異。這個初步的結果支持自我相關訊息處理的異常與解離之間的關聯，但不清楚的是，這個自我相關的社會認知功能的脆弱性是否為解離傾向的內生因素，亦或來自臨床解離病患遭遇到的童年負向人際經驗。另外，沒有一個研究系統性地探討這個自我感的異常對於不同面向的自我相關社會認知功能的影響。本研究就聚焦在這些文獻上的缺漏。這個研究有兩個主要的問題：（一）自我相關社會認知的異常是否為非臨床解離傾向者的特徵；（二）這些自我相關的社會認知異常是否可被負向人際經驗解釋。不同的社會認知實驗派點皆會被採用以分析自我感的異常對記憶、來源歸因、空間知覺、和同理心的影響。童年的人際創傷經驗和父母管教方式也將被評估以探討負向人際經驗是否可解釋解離和自我感異常的連結。研究的結果被預期可以幫助對解離的社會認知面向的了解，也可提供未來在解離疾患與創傷壓力研究的新方向。

24618115.label: Realisation of objectives
24618115.value: We have accomplished the research project as planned. There is no under-achievement. How the project objectives achieved: 1. A research ethics approval was obtained (CRE-2014.036). 2. Self-report instruments for constructs under study including 1) dissociation proneness (dissociative experiences, somatoform dissociation, and dissociative process), 2) parental dysfunction, 3) traumatic experiences, and common comorbid psychopathologies (anxiety, depression, hallucinatory experiences, and delusional ideation) were developed and validated. 3. Socio-cognitive functioning batteries tapping into the self-and-other functions that were targeted at the study were designed, developed, and validated. Finally five tests were available, including 1) the Self-versus-Other Source Monitoring Test, 2) the Perspective-taking Self-referential Memory Test, 3) the Ego- and Allo-centric Perspective-taking Test, 4) the Multifaceted Empathy Test, and 5) the Read Mind in the Eyes Test. 4. Several research visits were held in Leiden, Taipei, Tainan, Beijing, and Soochow for the development of the global project and the design of an individual behavioral test. 5. One hundred and fifty-nine participants were recruited to test the hypotheses 6. Participants came to my laboratory three times to answer all of the standardized self-report scales and complete the socio-cognitive functioning battery. An individual assessment was conducted by either the research assistant of the project or a student helper at each visit. 7. Data entry (self-report measures) and data cleaning (computerized tests) were performed collaboratively by the research assistant and the student helpers. 8. The PI (CDC) performed the data analysis and interpreted the results with three oversea collaborators (Prof. Elzinga Bernet and Prof Marieke Tollenaar at Leiden University; Prof Yei-Yu Yeh at National Taiwan University). 9. Regarding output, 1) seven papers in total were published under this grant; 2) five conference presentations were made; 3) six invited presentations were done in other universities, hospitals, and a governmental social welfare sector; 4) thirteen undergraduate and postgraduate student theses were finished. What the major findings are: 1. The association between source attribution and dissociation scores was tested. A significant negative correlation was reported, with more source misattribution of self-generated items in dissociative individuals. 2. We have examined the correlation between classic self-referential effect and dissociation proneness. A significant correlation was unfolded. The typical accessibility advantage of self-referential memory was absent in dissociative individuals. 3. The efficiency of taking ego- and allo-centric reference frames in dissociative and non-dissociative individuals were examined. A main effect of reference frame was found, indicating the processing advantage of taking the habitual, predominant egocentric reference frame. However, this efficiency of perspective taking did not significantly correlate with dissociation proneness. 4. We examined whether there was a main effect of dissociation proneness on emotion attribution and emotion sharing, two separate measures of mentalization ability. A significant association was found between dissociation and emotion attribution, despite the null correlation with dissociation proneness. Our results suggested dissociators feel that they share the emotional feelings of other people, though their perception of their emotions may be inaccurate. 5. For the three socio-cognitive dysfunctions associated with dissociation, we conducted covariance analysis to ensure whether the correlation could be accounted for by their elevated early interpersonal adversity including parental dysfunction and traumatic experiences. All the correlations remained significant after controlling for the early interpersonal adversity measures. Note-worthily, traumatic experiences had shown independent effects on socio-cognitive dysfunctions. Poor source attribution, a tendency to misattribute externally derived materials as internally generated, was associated with childhood betrayal trauma. Childhood betrayal trauma played a moderating role between the association of lower accessibility to self-referential memory and dissociation proneness. 6. Common comorbid psychopathologies of dissociation including anxiety, depression, psychoticism were controlled for to test the specificity of the links between dissociation and aforementioned socio-cognitive deficits. Our results showed the comorbid psychopahtologies could not readily explain the associations. We hence provide preliminary evidence for the specificity of these dissociation-related socio-cognitive dysfunctions. To what extent the project has been achieved: 100%

24618115.label: Major findings and research outcome
24618115.value: Several discoveries were made during our investigation of the role of socio-cognitive processes in the controversial trauma-maladaptation link. From our study of self-referential processing in nonclinical population, we found that a low accessibility to self-referenced representations moderated the link between early relational trauma and dissociation proneness (Chiu, Tollenaar, Yang, Elzinga, Zhang, & Ho, 2019). That is, individuals with the information processing style that did not prioritize self-referenced representations may suffer from ineffective synthesis of self-schema, which can be the cognitive diathesis for dissociative tendency in the presence of traumatic experience. Another problematic socio-cognitive process in dissociative individuals was identified. As predicted by our hypothesis, source misattribution was found negatively correlated with dissociation scores, meaning dissociative individuals tended to attribute externally derived representations as internally generated (Chiu, Ho, Tollenaar, Elzinga, & Zhang, 2019). Individuals high in source misattribution propensity could internalized the instable growing environment, which would compromise the integrity of self-schema, and perpetuate the impact of traumatic experience. The association between dissociation proneness and the third socio-cognitive process, mentalizing other’s emotions, was investigated. Using the Multifaceted Empathy Test, mentalizing ability was measured by emotion attribution and emotion sharing. A significant association was found between dissociation and emotion attribution, despite the null correlation with dissociation proneness (Chiu, Paesen, Dziobek, & Tollenaar, 2016). Our results suggested dissociators feel that they share the emotional feelings of other people, whilst their perception of their emotions may be inaccurate. Covariance analysis was performed to test whether the aforementioned correlations between dysfunctional socio-cognitive processes and dissociation proneness could be explained by early interpersonal adversity, or comorbidity of other psychopathologies. For early interpersonal difficulties, all the correlations remained significant after parental dysfunction and childhood traumatic experience were controlled for. Similarly for comorbidity, anxiety, depression, psychoticism were controlled for, while the links between dissociation and the socio-cognitive deficits remained significant. Hence, the influence of these self-related socio-cognitive dysfunctions on dissociative proneness is specific. Our project has shown that childhood trauma do not necessarily cause adulthood maladaptation. Rather, it is the dysfunctional socio-cognitive processes that results in a dysfunctional self-representation that plays a pivotal role in deciding one’s vulnerability to relational stress and thus proneness to dissociation.

24618115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24618115.value: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic research about the various layers of self-representations in the dissociative mind. As the feedback we have collected from our manuscript reviewers and conference audience, we believe the findings will have critical theoretical and clinical implications, including the operationalization of dissociation (e.g., to incorporate self dysfunction as a defining component of dissociative pathology) and the conceptualization of the relationship between dissociation and childhood trauma (e.g., to shift to the diathesis-stress model and emphasize the role of neurocognitive anomalies in the moderation of post-traumatic stress adaptation). For future studies, we believe a systematic research into the role of self-representation in clinical populations are crucial. Self pathology are common yet varied among mental disorders, such as negative self-image in mood disorder, fragile self-understanding in personality disorders, and a diminished sense of self in psychotic disorders. Only a systematic investigation of various layers of self-representations, together with a transdiagnostic approach to measuring psychopathologies across varying clinical populations can unveil the specificity of disturbed self functioning in different mental disorders. The success of this project suggests our paradigm should be useful to tackle this challenging yet timely question in mental health fields.

24618115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24618115.value: Unhappy childhood has been a common factor we attribute for our mental problems in adulthood. In clinical practice, stressful childhood experiences are usually reported by patients with mental problems. However, scientific research in the past twenty years suggested otherwise, as several well-designed researches did not find a reliable effect of stressful childhood experiences on adulthood mental problems. This inconsistency leads to a debate whether childhood experiences are important for psychological health. In the current study we addressed this issue by investigating whether this dampening impact of stressful childhood experiences can be moderated by the way we deal with emotional memories. That is to say, stressful childhood experiences may not necessarily result in long-term mental problems, if we can carefully manage the memories that we are avoidant and feel uncomfortable to think over. Using various psychological experiments, we found evidence for our hypothesis. Most importantly, we found that stressful childhood experiences could increase the risk of adulthood dissociation (i.e. a specific mental problem common for psychological trauma) only in people having a disadvantage of remembering memories that they used to define themselves (whether it was close to the identity).

25100815.label: Project Objectives
25100815.value: Objective 1 Validate the role of ZBTB20 in liver tumorigenesis – in vivo gene validation Zinc finger and BTB domain containing 20 (ZBTB20) was first confirmed with The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) human liver cancer genomic and human cell line expression (RefExA) databases for disease significance. However, there are still many unanswered questions regarding the genetic mechanisms associated with ZBTB20 in liver tumorigenesis. Hence, a reverse genetic approach is required to validate ZBTB20 in vivo and firmly establish its role as a bona fide HCC oncogene and elucidate the genetic mechanisms associated with disease evolution. This in vivo validation approach involves the use of fumaryl acetoacetate hydrolase (Fah) mutant mice and the Sleeping Beauty (SB) transposon-based gene delivery (Fah/SB11 mice). Using a transposon vector that simultaneously expresses both Fah and ZBTB20, it can be stably incorporated into an expanding population of hepatocytes to test its oncogenicity using a relatively simple method involving hydrodynamic tail-vein injection. Objective 2 Determine the association of ZBTB20 with HBV-induced liver tumorigenesis through the canonical WNT signaling pathway Asian countries have high numbers of viral hepatitis induced HCC and it is known that HBV infection plays multiple roles in liver carcinogenesis. ZBTB20 will be co-introduced with an HBV oncogenic gene in Fah/SB11 mice to test its role in HBV-associated HCC. Important genetic information will be established in this study since there is currently limited data in TCGA regarding HBV-induced liver cancer. The oncogenic potential of the HBV X gene has been previously shown to be associated with the Wnt signaling pathway. Since the CTNNB1/WNT molecular subclass represents a large majority of human HCCs, the association of ZBTB20 with HBV-induced liver tumorigenesis involving the canonical WNT signaling pathway will also be examined

25100815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25100815.value: When cells deviate from their normal developmental state as a result of external and/or internal factors, their growth behaviour changes and if left unchecked, disease like cancer can occur. Cancer research has progressed tremendously over the past decades and many important genes that contribute to cancer development have been identified. However, there is still no definitive cure for cancer and the occurrence of some cancers are even increasing. The incidence of liver cancer is increasing worldwide with no effective treatment regimes. It is becoming apparently clear that liver cancer is a very complex disease, which is made up of several genetic subgroups that ultimately have to be treated differently from each other for effectiveness. In order to have a focused and effective means of treating liver cancer, we need to study cancer genes at the genetic level on how they work and influence each other in promoting cancer. In a previous experiment to discover new liver cancer genes, the zinc finger and BTB domain containing 20 (Zbtb20) gene was identified as a top candidate gene amongst many other genes. Zbtb20 has been shown to be essential for normal developing brain and liver during early life but its role in liver cancer remains unclear. This research proposal will validate the role of Zbtb20 in liver cancer using an animal model and determine how it contributes to this deadly disease on the genetic level. The transposon or jumping gene system, will be used to deliver Zbtb20 back into the livers of the animal model and its effect followed carefully. Liver tumors that develop as a result of the changes in Zbtb20 gene levels will be isolated and analyzed for its genetic information. Therefore, information derived from this proposed research will enable the identification of new targets for therapeutic development for this specific subgroup of liver cancer. This will hopefully lead to the era of personalized medicine for this subgroup of patients, where treatment can be given according to the specific gene(s) that caused the liver cancer. The knowledge obtained from this research will be a further step forward in the understanding, treatment and prevention of liver cancer.
