25103015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25103015.value: 項目概要: 慢性阻塞性肺病是一種非逆轉性的氣道阻塞疾病。在香港居住的70歲以上長者當中, 大概有9%的人士患有此病。活動時呼吸困難往往是限制患者做運動或進行日常活動的主因。 除了影響呼吸外，文獻顯示慢性阻塞性肺病也會造成全身性的影響包括改變肌肉形態和組織代謝、減少腦部和組織灌注從而影響氧攝取量。這與慢性阻塞性肺病患者所表現的認知功能和身體功能障礙有關。 太極注重以意念控制呼吸及每一式的動作。科研顯示慢性阻塞性肺病患者在進行12週的太極訓練後，在肌力、功能耐力及平衡力等各方面有顯著的改善。然而，其背後的原理則有待探討。 因此，此研究項目致力於研究 1) 12週的太極訓練是否能提升慢性阻塞性肺病患者的腦部和/組織氧; 2) 並探討腦部和/或組織氧的改變是否與認知功能和體能表現有關。

25103015.label: Realisation of objectives
25103015.value: This project, which examined the effect of 12-week Tai Chi program on promoting oxygen uptake at cerebral and/ or muscular level in people with Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), was completed. The followings summarized how the objectives have been achieved. For objective 1 - To determine the effect of a 12-week Tai Chi program on promoting oxygen uptake at cerebral and/ or muscular level in people with COPD. Methods: We have conducted a Randomized controlled trial recruiting people with COPD who met the diagnostic criteria of GOLD ranging from GOLD I to GOLD IV. Eligible subjects were randomly allocated into one of the three groups, i.e. routine care (control), ergometry and Tai Chi group stratified by 6-minute walk distance and percentage of predicted level of Forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1). High compliance rates were obtained in both Tai Chi (ranged from 83.3% to 100%) and Ergometry group (ranged from 83.3% to 95.8%). Results: After the whole program, people in Tai Chi group demonstrated an improved cognitive function as reflected by shortened time to complete the cognitive tasks which were not seen in other groups suggesting the beneficial effect of Tai Chi, a mind body exercise, to induce training/ preserving effect on cognitive function. For the physical function, our data suggest that patients in Tai Chi and Ergometry groups have demonstrated improved exercise capacity as reflected by 6-minute walk test (6MWT) and submaximal ergometry test but not in the routine care group. Similar trend of improvement in subjective component was found in both Ergometry and Tai Chi groups with no significant difference. Conclusion: Tai Chi program is beneficial for improving physical and cognitive function in people with COPD. For objectives 2 and 3 - To evaluate the association of cerebral oxygenation and cognitive function and examine the association of muscle oxygenation and physical performance. Methods: We have used the cross-sectional data measured at baseline for examining the association of cerebral oxygenation and cognitive function as well as the association of oxygenation of the main muscle for locomotion and physical function using standardized cognitive tests and exercise capacity including symptom-limited ergometry test and 6-minute walk test. Results: Our data demonstrated people with COPD have lowered resting tissue oxygenation level at quadriceps than age-and-gender matched elderly with normal health. Tissue oxygenation and disease severity was found to be main contributor predicting the exercise capacity in people with COPD. Comparing with elderly with normal health, people with COPD, despite similar level of educational background and score of Montreal cognitive assessment (MOCA), demonstrated domain-specific reduction in cognitive performance and that the performance was found to be associated with the levels of cerebral oxygenation. Conclusion: Dyspnoea on exertion and reduced oxygen supply are consequences for the detrimental effect of COPD. Our findings support the reduced oxygenation levels at tissue level would affect different bodily functions. In this project, we proposed to recruit a total of 60 subjects. We came across difficulty in subject recruitment especially during the peak seasons of flu and the nature of COPD symptoms. People with COPD usually complain of dyspnoea on exertion which may refrain from doing exercise leading to poor compliant rate in joining exercise program in pulmonary rehabilitation. Thus, considering the potential dropout rate, we proposed to recruit 66 subjects. We had 67 people with COPD being referred from respiratory specialist clinic or recruited from community. Ten subjects were excluded due to the co-existence of heart disease (n=3) as reflected by the changes in resting ECG, refusal to complete lung function test (n=1), failure to reach the preset ratio of FEV1/FVC <70% (n=5) and with known history of cognitive impairment which would affect their compliance to the program and understanding to the test (n=1). Fifty-seven eligible subjects joined the study and 6 subjects were dropped out for the whole study due to various reasons, including acute exacerbation (n=3), busy with other engagement (n=1), loss of follow up (n=1) and fracture of toe due to accident (n=1). However, given the time constraint and the long duration (3-month) to complete each program, we have finally obtained 51 completed sets of data. To overcome any potential impact (due to 5% less than the calculated sample size of 60), we have used intention-to-treat analysis (i.e. n=57) for final analysis to prevent any bias in data analysis.

25103015.label: Major findings and research outcome
25103015.value: As listed in Part C, the project resulted in one peer-reviewed journal, one manuscript in drafting stage, two conference abstracts presented at Australian Physiotherapy Conference in 2017 and Asian Pacific Society of Respirology (APSR) Congress (abstract indexed in the journal “Respirology”) in 2018 when the PI (Ngai) was awarded APSR COPD Assembly Award in this congress for this abstract. The major findings are: (1) appropriate selection of clinical outcome and biomarkers for people with COPD (Peer-reviewed journal, Ho et al., 2017); Comparing to age-gender-matched elderly with normal health, people with COPD demonstrated a lowered level of tissue oxygenation in the main locomotor muscle, i.e. quadriceps and that the oxygenation level was found to be one of the main contributors predicting the physical function (Conference presentation, Ngai et al., 2018). Despite having similar level of education background and similar score in cognitive function screening test, people with COPD was found to take longer time to complete most of the cognitive tasks involving visuoattention, cognitive processing and executive function. These domain specific cognitive tasks were found to be moderately associated with 6MWT and ergometry workrate (Conference presentation, Ngai et al., 2017). These findings supported that people with COPD had impaired cognitive and physical function and significantly lower domain-specific cognitive performance. Besides, some specfic cognitive performance was found to be moderately and strongly associated with physical function suggesting that COPD affects both cognitive and physical performance in the victims.

25103015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25103015.value: The current study indicated that Tai Chi program improves physical function and cognitive function in people with COPD. However, with the time constraint, we did not conduct follow up measurement to examine if the carryover effect of the program existed and whether or not people with COPD could remain active after the completion of program. Thus, future research study with the consideration of these issues is needed. In addition, this study showed that people with COPD have impaired baseline tissue oxygenation and that the levels were predictors for physical and cognitive functions. However, the association between oxygen intake and tissue utilization is yet to be done. Understanding of this would be important as people with COPD have impaired oxygen intake and that may potentially affect the oxygen utilization at different tissue levels. Thus, further addressing such association would be helpful in understanding the disease and its management.

25103015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25103015.value: Exertional dyspnoea is one main complaint that refrain patients from physical activities or activities of daily living. With the impaired oxygen intake, it is hypothesized that the level of oxygen to be delivered to different muscles or organs would also be impaired affecting the associated functions. Though exercise training is beneficial in improving physical function, exertional dyspnoea is usually one main reason leading to poor attendance and high dropout rate in pulmonary rehabilitation. With the nature of “mind controlled” component of Tai Chi, it may potentially induce cognitive training. This study showed that people with COPD have lowered level of tissue oxygenation when compared with age-and-gender matched elderly with normal health and that the levels were found to be related to the functional performance which supports our hypothesis. Our data also supports that Tai Chi program is beneficial to improve physical and cognitive functions in people with COPD. As Tai Chi is convenient to perform and does not require expensive equipment or space, the proven beneficial effect of Tai Chi program provides evidence to support patients to perform Tai Chi as home exercise to preserve their functional levels. Future exploration on the maintenance effect of Tai Chi program is suggested.

25200515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25200515.value: Glass workpieces can be thermoformed into various products of complex geometries for daily usage. However, this process becomes of little use in precision optics, where the geometry and physical properties of an optical element must be highly precise. The production of high-quality lenses nowadays still depends on dedicated grinding/polishing systems. The mere reason for adopting these material-removal processes is that they are at room temperature and do not change the physical property of glass. These processes are extremely expensive, and become even unviable when the optical components are of complex shapes and/or with small-scale surface features (e.g. the aspherical lens, Fresnel lens or micro-lens system as shown in Fig. 1). Can the low-cost thermoforming also be high-precision? Can it be more predictable and less trial-and-error? Thermoforming would be applicable for making most optical elements and be immediately scalable for mass production. However, the process design currently still depends on trial-and-error experimentations and skilful artisans, which in most cases are costly and formidable. To break the barrier from the grass root of the technology, an accurate constitutive model of glass, which can predict the material behaviour in a thermal process and ascertain the physical properties of the final product, must be established. This is the objective of the proposed research and has been underpinned by our recent achievements on both fundamental theories [1,2] and experimental investigations [3]. The nature of glassy state is one of the major scientific problems [4] remaining unresolved. The phenomenon under investigation is that at an elevated temperature, the amorphous structure changes spontaneously with time and all physical properties vary towards their respective equilibrium magnitudes. The timescale of relaxation is highly temperature dependent, varying over ten orders of magnitude in a narrow temperature window near the glass transition point. To unveil the details of structural relaxation, the physical properties being investigated were conventionally volume and enthalpy. In this project, we propose to use elastic modulus as the additional observable, which can be probed efficiently and accurately even at a high temperature using the impulse excitation (IE) technique. By installing a tailored dilatometer in the IE station, the simultaneous measurement of two variables, modulus and volume, will be achieved for the first time. The novel stochastic models of glass, to be established based on the state-of-the-art understanding that a macroscopic glassy system relaxes through microscopic fluctuations, will then be developed, parameterised and validated using experimental results. 玻璃可以通過熱成型製成各種器皿，但是精密光學元件的製造通常不採用熱成型工藝而採用機械研磨的方法。傳統的機械研磨過於昂貴，且不適用于製造具有特殊幾何形狀的光學元件。這使得人們开始考慮利用精密模壓的方法製備精密光學元件。 玻璃器件的精密模壓顯然易於形成大規模生產，因此具有成本優勢。但是其通常無法達到光學元件對尺寸精度和物理特性的苛刻要求。由於玻璃物性對溫度複雜依賴性，溫度的改變通常帶來難以預料的折射率，尺寸，密度和內應力的變化。因此現有的通過精密模壓製成的光學元件，都是有經驗的工匠反復試驗的結果。 要從根本上改變精密模壓工藝所面對的困難，必須要建立玻璃態物質的本構模型以描述其在熱和機械耦合作用下的變形和物性改變。本項目旨在通過研究玻璃的結構弛豫現象提煉出數學模型以達到此目標。具體的研究工作包括測量彈性模量隨溫度和時間的變化以得到玻璃弛豫的規律，建立基於微觀弛豫機理的玻璃本構模型，并通過實驗數據驗證此數學模型。

25200515.label: Realisation of objectives
25200515.value: We applied for a half-year extension for more experiments on a suspected intermediate glassy state. Therefore, the total duration of this project is 42 months, in which we have achieved all proposed objectives, or more conservatively, we have conducted investigations following the objectives and publish eleven related papers. Nevertheless, we acknowledge that the nature of glass transition, as a long-standing open question in condensed matter physics, remains still obscure. For this basic question, we achieved some interesting findings under the support of this project and elaborate hereunder according to the objectives. (i) To characterize structural relaxation of glass through measuring the variation of modulus with temperature and time We proposed to characterize structural relaxation of a glassy material by monitoring elasticity variation because the latter is at least two orders of magnitude more significant than that of volume (or enthalpy) in a glass transition range (note that dilatometry and calorimetry are the most frequently used in glass research). In this project, Young’s moduli were measured in-situ based on the impulse excitation technique (IET) and Fourier analysis (i.e., to excite a free beam vibration, record the sound generated, identify the fundamental peaks in an acoustic spectrum). With a dedicated IET furnace, these measurements led to a series of characterizations of structural relaxation for commercial optical glasses. Some of these works have been published [1-3] (see part C). In the research output [1], we demonstrated the difference in the relaxation behavior of two types of commercial optical glasses, borosilicate (for visible-light imaging) versus chalcogenide (for infrared imaging). While the borosilicate glasses were “normal”, i.e., the viscosity determined from the decay rate of the vibration amplitude was consistent with reported viscometer measurement, the chalcogenide glasses appeared to be much more rate-dependent, i.e., their viscosity was 3 ~ 4 orders of magnitude smaller in the dynamic tests (i.e., using IET) than that in a static (viscometer) measurement near the glass transition point (Tg). This observation motivated modeling efforts based on strong non-exponentiality in [1], i.e., the short-time behavior differs from the long-time one. Through a collaboration with the State Key Laboratory for Advanced Metals and Materials in University of Science and Technology Beijing, we studied a series of metallic glasses and revealed a pronounced sub-Tg relaxation in the research output [2]. Such a sub-Tg relaxation is unlikely observed using dilatometry and calorimetry. We characterized the relaxation time of sub-Tg relaxation and revealed that the significance of the sub-Tg relaxation can be well correlated with the plasticity of a metallic glass because they have the same structural origin, i.e., the propensity of sub-Tg structural rearrangement. In the research output [3] we revealed double-peak acoustic spectra obtained from a fluorosilicate glass and explained it based on the picture that the oxide network becomes fragmented when heating beyond Tg. The vibration and interaction of the fragmented patches lead to the observed double-peak phenomenon. Very unexpectedly, when we used IET to probe crystalline phase transformation in a dual-phase (ferrite and austenite) stainless steel, we found a pronounced sudden drop in Young’s modulus at 900 ~ 950 °C if the steel was co-rolled (see the research output [4]). We ascribed this drop to a two-step phase transformation with the intermediate phase being amorphous. Such an assertion was due to a thorough theoretical analysis ruling out other possibilities based on crystalline phase transformation only. We spend quite some time trying to directly observe the intermediate amorphous phase using a transmission electron microscope (TEM), causing the extension of this project, but the efforts were still inconclusive owing to the technical difficulty in the in-situ high-temperature TEM. We stress that this unexpected finding shows the worthiness of using IET to probe structural relaxation of glass, which can reveal new phenomena in glass transition and phase transformation. The basic synthesis and characterization of this novel steel were also partially supported by this project. Therefore, the related publications [5-7], though seemingly unrelated to the main theme of this project, is also listed part C, as they acknowledged the support of this project and are also related to the finding of intermediated glassy phase in the ferrite-to-austenite transformation. (ii) To establish and validate the novel constitutive model of glass on the basis of dynamical heterogeneity of glassy state With the experimental results elaborated above, the associated constitutive models have also been established in [1, 3]. The model established in [1] is a rational viscoelastic model based on the assumption that glass transition is through a series of memoryless structural changes, described by a temporal probability density function. To account for the observed rate-dependence in the chalcogenide glasses, the proposed model involved the Cole-Davidson expression of relaxation spectrum, which revealed a wide separation of short-time and long-time relaxations (i.e., a consequence of dynamic heterogeneity), therefore, rendered an account for the difference in viscosity measurement between IET and viscometer. However, we acknowledge that the proposed model may not be the only explanation. Another way of thinking is that the relaxation in chalcogenide is both temperature and stress (or strain-rate) dependent. This idea has motivated another funded GRF project for further exploration. In the research output [3] we proposed a model of alpha-beta relaxation of glass derived from the normal mode analysis (NMA) of potential energy landscape (PEL). With an assumed Lorentz distribution of normal modes, a novel viscoelastic model was established, which could well fit experimentally obtained double-peak spectra. The model indicates that a subtle vibrational relaxation mode can lead to a remarkable peak in an IET spectrum when the frequency of a beta relaxation peak is close to the natural frequency of the specimen. Furthermore, the experimental results indicate a negative temperature-dependence of the frequency of beta relaxation in the fluorosilicate glass which can be explained based on the physical picture of fragmented oxide-network patches in liquid-like regions. (iii) To establish the numerical simulation scheme for implementing the novel constitutive model With the support of this project, we have initiated a collaboration with Prof. TF Zhou at Beijing Institute of Technology (BIT), who worked on machining (for molding tools) and glass molding experiments. This collaboration has led to the publications [8, 9], in which the constitutive model of chalcogenide glass has been implemented into a numerical simulation scheme to describe the mechanical response of materials and predict the influence of key processing parameters in a glass molding process. In general, the predicted force-displacement curve of a molding process agreed with experimental results. For the sudden drop of Young’s modulus in a two-step phase transformation described in the research output [4], we have devised a master-equation-based multiphase transformation model. This model can be incorporated into the governing equation of Euler-Bernoulli beam for investigating the coupling between phase change and mechanical response. The computational scheme has been established, which can well explain the experimental results in terms of the anomalous drop of elastic modulus and the associated surge of loss rate [4]. In addition, the research staff supported by this project also developed phase-field models to study mechano-chemical coupling in oxide growth and corrosion [10, 11]. These studies are related to glass molding (e.g., oxidation of molding tools) and chemical treatment (e.g., ion-exchange strengthening) therefore also listed in Part C.

25200515.label: Major findings and research outcome
25200515.value: The efforts in this project essentially corroborates our conception that structural relaxation in a glass probed by elasticity change can lead to more ample phenomena than those based on volume and enthalpy variations. This is anticipated because of the larger variation of modulus in the glass transition range, and more fundamentally, because elasticity is an autocorrelation function of microscopic fluctuations which is more sensitive to the heterogeneous dynamics in an amorphous system. We proposed to use in-situ IET to characterize glass and have shown that the frequency-domain analysis gave rise to a high-fidelity measurement of the temperature-time dependence of Young’s modulus, which can be used to establish a phenomenological understanding of glass. Moreover, an acoustic spectrum can be used to determine not only elastic modulus but also other physical quantities. For example, the decay rate of vibration amplitude can be converted into viscosity for borosilicate glasses, and the additional peak in a spectrum may indicate additional relaxation modes. These investigations have been summarized in the publications [1-3]. In addition to these published results on glass, we have recently found that the glass transition point could be more precisely determined based on the memory persistence of historical disturbance in aging experiments, that is, below a critical temperature near Tg, the memory of history does not fade to zero. Note that this phenomenon is in line with the spin-glass transition, suggesting ergodicity breaking in long-time aging. The persistent memory is rather small, which can only be observed by probing modulus change using IET with enough accuracy and resolution. This work has just been finished, uploaded to arXiv (see publication [12]), and submitted to a journal. Our technique has also been used to probe the intermediate amorphous phase that could occur in a crystalline phase transformation, as revealed in recent model experiments with colloids as well as atomistic simulations. We reported such a phenomenon for the first time in a real material, a duplex stainless steel with a high degree of metastability after severe plastic deformation. The evidence of the intermediate amorphous phase in the temperature range of ferrite-to-austenite transformation is a sudden drop of modulus together with a surge of decay rate (see publication [4]). This work is associated with a few more publications on the basic characterization of this new alloy, which has also been included in the list of research outputs [5-7].

25200515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25200515.value: This project initiates the investigation of glass transition through probing elasticity variation. The confirmed validity and the ample phenomenon as introduced above have warranted further research along this direction to unveil the nature of the glass transition and the glassy state. To be specific, we suggest the following topic worthy of successive actions. (i) Nature of rate-dependence in chalcogenide glasses Chalcogenide glasses have very broad applications in infrared optics (e.g., thermal imaging, optical switches, etc.). The results of the rate-dependent viscosity could have a significant impact on their thermoformability. It is worth further investigation to make clear the mechanism and the associated theoretical description so that the associated precision molding technology can be of high yield. (ii) Aging effects Our finding of a persistent memory when T < Tg should be further confirmed in different glasses and the effect of the waiting time of a disturbance (i.e., the aging effect) should be clarified. This helps to unveil the critical phenomenon of glass transition. (iii) Intermediate amorphous phase The intermediate amorphous phase in a tow-step phase transformation needs further confirmation through in-situ high-resolution experiments. These investigations can greatly expand the picture of crystalline phase transformation and provide new way of microstructure engineering.

25200515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25200515.value: The nature of glassy state and glass transition, after questioned by the Nobel laureate P.W. Anderson in 1995, has become one of the most significant unsolved problems in condensed matter physics. The puzzling lies in the difficulty to establish a relation between property and structure because there is not a structural indicator to differentiate one amorphous structure from another. Even if there is one, it would be difficult to quantify by any existing diffraction or direct imaging techniques. Therefore, understanding glass is basically through observing the variations of physical quantifies with temperature and time, which hints internal structural change. Conventionally, dilatometry and calorimetry are the most used in characterizing structural glass. In this project, we measured the acoustic spectrum of a glass beam after it is tapped and reported interesting phenomena such as the separation between short-time and long-time relaxations or two relaxation modes. These results lead to a more accurate phenomenological model of glass to describe its property change in a thermal process. On the technology side, such a theoretical model brings about more predictability in the design of a thermoforming process to replace tedious machining processes in producing high-precision optical components, such as camera lenses or screen covers.

25202615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25202615.value: 由於易於展現和操作的特點，圖（graphs）在自然科學、工程和社會科學等各領域都有廣泛應用，其中一個重要角色就是表示大量數據。大多數時候，從這些數據得到的圖應該有一些特殊的屬性。但由於不可避免的錯誤存在，直接從原始數據中得到的圖實際上總是不滿足這些屬性。因此在分析這些實驗數據的時候，首先我們就要找到可能的錯誤。一個常見的計算模型就是將其表達成圖修正問題：如果通過盡可能少量的修正讓原圖滿足指定屬性。絕大多數圖修正問題都是從這樣的應用場景中抽象出來。另一方面，因為許多難解問題，包括最大團（clique）、獨立集（independent set）、染色（coloring）和圖同構（graph isomorphism）等，在某些特殊圖（例如平面圖、二部圖和弦圖）上變得非常容易，圖修正問題也可以用作中間步驟來解決這些難解問題。此外，圖修正問題還與稀疏矩陣的運算有精密聯繫，而且跟許多經典的計算問題等價，譬如點覆蓋（vertex cover）、反饋集（feedback vertex set）和最大割集（maximum cut）。因此，這些問題的高效演算法一直受到大量關注。 大多數圖修正問題是NP完全的，因此不太可能有任何情況下都適用的辦法。一個在相關應用中常見的事實是，只有修正數量比較少的時候解決這個問題才有意義（例如，如果數據有大量錯誤那就沒有修正的必要了）。基於此觀察，人們提出參數化計算模型（parameterized computation）。它的目標就是針對只需要少量（不超過k）修正的時候設計演算法，這些演算法的運行時間是f(k) n^c，其中f是一個只跟k有關的函數，c是一個常數。這方面的研究已經帶來不少演算法。但他們通常有一個共同問題，那就是常數c太大（有時候甚至超過5）。因此，這樣的結果離實用還有一定距離。此外，至今仍有一些重要問題懸而未決，它們很難通過現有技術手段解決，因此我們可能需要發掘新的技術。 本項研究旨在圖修正問題的演算法，其中研究重點是實際問題中的高效演算法。它與已有研究結果的區別主要體現在兩個方面。首先，我們會同時考慮函數f和常數c，這樣我們設計的演算法才有可能運用於大規模數據。第二，在演算法設計的過程中，我們將信奉簡潔至上的原則，這樣我們得到的演算法會比較容易實現，而不是只停留於紙面。本項研究還預期發現相關圖類的組合特徵，它們和新的演算法設計技術一起將對有助於本領域的發展。

25202615.label: Realisation of objectives
25202615.value: The purpose of this project is to develop efficient algorithms for graph modification problems. A graph modification problem asks whether one can apply a small amount (at most k) of modifications to a graph to make it satisfy certain properties. By modifications we usually mean additions and/or deletions, and they can be applied to vertices or edges. These problems arise naturally in many applications and have theoretical significance because many classic problems can be formulated as graph modification problems. Apart from developing algorithms, the objectives of this project include discovering combinatorial characterizations of related graph classes, and providing complexity evidence that some graph modification problems are intractable, and find lower bounds on some tractable graph modification problems. When we proposed this project, the most notorious open problems in this area are those toward interval graphs and other related graph classes. They are part of the motivation of this project. Our achievements in this regard is more than expected. Since interval graphs are chordal, and their study has been mostly interrelated. Early efforts for solving these problems started from the techniques used for chordal modification problems. We take a different approach, and start from another relatively less-known superclass of interval graphs, namely the circular-arc graphs. In revisiting the relation between interval graphs and circular-arc graphs, we noticed that the class of normal Helly circular-arc graphs is the smallest natural subclass of circular-arc graphs that still contains all interval graphs. This class had not been sufficiently studied because it was believed to be too special to be interesting. Even the most fundamental problems on it, characterization by forbidden induced subgraphs from the combinatorial aspect and a recognition algorithm from the algorithmic aspect, were open at that moment. We solved both problems. The structural results of normal Helly circular-arc graphs are our main tool to the modification problems toward interval graphs, for which we take a two-phase approach. After dealing with small forbidden induced subgraphs with standard branching, we observe that the remaining graph is close to a normal Helly circular-arc graph, on which the problem can be actually solved in linear time. This observation also applies to modification problems toward unit interval graphs. Again we use its connection with a subclass of circular-arc graphs, namely, the proper Helly circular-arc graphs, and take a similar but far simpler approach. All these algorithms run in linear FPT time. For some of these problems, we also developed approximation algorithms, which run in O(n + m) time, where $n$ and $m$ denote respectively the numbers of vertices and edges of the input graph. We also spent a significant amount of efforts in developing kernelization algorithms (preprocessing with rigorous analyses), which are a theoretical formalization of efficient preprocessing for (NP-)hard problems, for graph modification problem. Again, we attack unit interval graphs. For the unit interval vertex deletion problem, Fomin, Saurabh, and Villanger [ESA'12; SIAM J. Discrete Math 27(2013)] have developed an $O(k^{53})$-vertex kernel. They use the powerful sunflower lemma, which is the main reason behind the huge exponent in the kernel size. Instead, we use a constant-approximation solution (provided by our approximation algorithm developed early) as the modulator, and study its interaction with other vertices. We partition the vertex set of this unit interval graph into cliques in the most naive way (too naive to be ignored by other researchers), and pick a small number of representatives from each of them. This leads to a significantly improved $O(k^4)$-vertex kernel for the problem. More importantly, our constructive proof for the correctness of our algorithm, using interval models, greatly simplifies the ``destructive'' proofs, based on destroying forbidden structures, for similar problems in literature. Our algorithm can be implemented in $O(m n + n^2)$ time. After solving all the modification problems to interval graphs and unit interval graphs, we focus on another family of important graph modification problems, namely, the H-free edge modification problems. Given a fixed graph H, the H-free editing problem asks whether we can edit at most k edges to make a graph contain no induced copy of H. In contrast to the systematic results on vertex deletion problems, most notably, those of Cai (IPL 1996) and Yannakakis (STOC 1978), the picture for edge modification problems is far murkier. We tend to believe that H-free edge modification problems admitting polynomial kernels are the exceptions. Our exploration suggests that graphs on four vertices play the pivotal roles if we want to fully map the territory. We are thus focused on the four-vertex graphs on which the problems have not been solved. Since the H-free edge deletion problem is equivalent to the H'-free edge completion problem, while the edge editing problems are the same for H-free and H'-free graphs, where H' is the complement graph of H, there are only three four-vertex graphs to study. Thus far, we have produced polynomial kernels for edge modification problems toward diamond-free graphs and paw-free graphs. The incompressibility dichotomy for H being a 3-connected graph and the classical complexity dichotomy suggest that except for H being a complete/empty graph, H-free editing problems admit polynomial kernels only for a few small graphs H. Therefore, we believe that our result is an essential step toward a complete dichotomy on the compressibility of H-free editing. During our study, we discovered new combinatorial characterization of graph classes. The most important are the results on normal Helly circular-arc graphs. We fully characterized its minimal forbidden induced subgraphs, and developed the first certifying recognition algorithm for it. We also obtained structural observation on diamond-free graphs, which might be used for other purposes. As mentioned, many important problems in applications are nothing but graph modification problem. The minimum fill-in problem arises from the application of Gaussian elimination to a sparse matrix. Given an n by n sparse symmetric matrix with m nonzero entries, performing Gaussian elimination may turn some zeroes into nonzero values, so called fill-ins. The minimum fill-in problem asks whether it is possible to perform the elimination with at most k fill-ins. Rose gave a graph-theoretic interpretation of the minimum fill-in problem: the minimum fill-in of a symmetric matrix M is exactly the minimum number of edges we need to add to an associated graph G to make it chordal, i.e., free of induced cycles of length at least four. The hardness of the minimum fill-in problem had been an open problem, until a six-step reduction was given by Yannakakis in 1981. His reduction blows up the instance significantly, so that it is not applicable to fine-grained complexity. Bliznets et al. (SODA 2016) managed to iron out some step of this long reduction path, which leads to a weak lower bound. Instead of further improving these reductions or finding alternatives, we start from scratch and devise a completely new reduction from the vertex cover problem, which turns out to be surprisingly simple. The reduction we discovered can be easily turned into a linear reduction. Our new reduction enables us to exclude the existence of polynomial time approximation schemes, assuming P is not equal to NP, and the existence of $2^{O(n^{1-delta})}$-time approximation schemes for any positive $delta$, assuming the Exponential Time Hypothesis. Also implied is a $2^{O(k^{1/2 - delta})} cdot n^{O(1)}$ parameterized lower bound.

25202615.label: Major findings and research outcome
25202615.value: The major findings of this project are a sequence of algorithms for graph modification problems. We developed linear-time FPT algorithms for all the modification problems to interval graphs (SODA'16) and unit interval graphs (Information and Computation 2017). We also developed O(mn)-time constant-approximation algorithms for the vertex deletion problems to (unit) interval graphs. Another approximation algorithm we developed in this project is an algorithm of ratio 2.5 for the cluster vertex deletion problem (DAM 2017). A small but surprising result is the best algorithm for the feedback vertex set problem (SOSA'18), the most studied problem in parameterized computation. This result has opened a completely new perspective for the research of this problem, and related problems. This project also produces several kernelization algorithms. The first is a kernel of O(n^4) vertices for the unit interval vertex deletion problem (JCSS 2018), greatly improving the previous kernel of O(n^53) vertices. A systematic attack on the kernelization of H-free edge modification problems leads to kernels for the diamond-free edge modifications (ESA'18) and paw-free edge modifications (under review). We give polynomial-time algorithms or proofs of NP-completeness for most of the vertex deletion problems from one subclass of chordal graphs to another. In particular, we show that the vertex deletion problem from chordal graphs to interval graphs is NP-complete. (FSTTCS'17, TCS 2018) As expected, the project produces some structural results on the graph classes. It characterizes the class of normal Helly circular-arc graphs by minimal forbidden induced subgraphs, and develops a certifying recognition algorithm for it (DAM 2017). We have also found novel combinatorial characterization of chordal graphs, interval graphs, unit interval graphs, and proper Helly circular-arc graphs (SODA'16, Information and Computation 2017, JCSS 2018, TCS 2018). These properties have been used in our algorithm designs and by other authors. Matrix computation in scientific and engineering computation tends to be very time-consuming because of the size of matrices. Since the pioneering work of Markowitz, it becomes crucial in matrix computation to exploit, and more importantly, maintain the sparsity of the matrices. One of the most used matrix computation is Gaussian elimination. However, performing Gaussian elimination to a sparse matrix may turn some zeroes into nonzero values, so called fill-ins, which we want to minimize to keep the matrix sparse. We have presented almost tight lower bounds for algorithms for the problem, as well as the first hardness result for the approximation of this problem. These results were obtained through collaboration with more than ten researchers from five countries. This project also supported three postdoc researchers, who are holding faculty positions in universities in Czeck, France, and Macau.

25202615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25202615.value: At a late stage of this project, we started a systematic study of the kernelization of H-free edge modification problems. We have solved the problems for H being the diamond and the paw. The main open problem is then the claw-free edge modification problems. After that, we will try to fully demarcate the border between compressibility and incompressibility for these problems. We will continue our pursue of the kernelization of interval completion problem. We have recently made great progress on it: We produced a polynomial kernel when the input graph is chordal. We will try to solve the problem. We need to strengthen our lower bounds for the minimum fill-in problem. In particular, we want to exclude the existence of constant-ratio approximation in polynomial time. Moreover, we plan to extend it to the interval completion problem, another important problem originating from sparse matrix computation and solved as a graph modification problem. Lastly, our study brought the circular-arc graphs to our attention. Since it's far more complicated that chordal and interval graphs, there are quite a lot of questions unanswered here, including characterization of its minimal forbidden induced subgraphs. We will try to attack this and other major open problems on this class.

25202615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25202615.value: Easy to visualize and manipulate, graphs are widely used for modeling structural data in natural sciences, engineering, and social sciences. The raw data are almost always contaminated with errors, and hence we cannot get the expect structures. The first step of studying these empiric data is thus to identify the hidden errors, and one computational model is to use graph modification problems, which ask for a minimum number of modifications that transform a given graph to have a certain property. Most graph modification problems are formulated from this the primary source. Second, since many hard problems become tractable on special graphs, graph modification problems to these special graphs can be used as subroutines to solve these hard problems. Moreover, problems in matrix computation are frequently solved with graph formulations. Therefore, efficient algorithms for them have been intensively sought. Most such problems are intrinsically difficult in general. A common fact observed in aforementioned applications is that only a small amount of modifications are of practical meaning (e.g., data contaminated with too many errors are useless and have to be discarded). In view of this, we try to design tailored algorithms for this special situation. This project has produced both efficient algorithms and evidence that some of them may not have.

25203215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25203215.value: Shareholding Cooperatives (SCs), or gufenhezuoshe in Chinese, have tremendous impact on the urban development of rural China as more and more villagers rely heavily on the share dividends and social welfare services provided by their SCs to make a living after losing their arable land to urbanization. However, despite the important role they play in facilitating villagers’ rural-urban transition, the actual impact of SCs on shaping the process and outcomes of China’s urbanization remains largely under-explored. To understand the impact of SCs on urbanization requires a comprehensive and rigorous analysis of how SCs really operate in the management and allocation of villagers’ collectively owned assets. This study focuses on the Guangzhou Lougang District (GLD) in which a total of 517 SCs are managing the ever-growing collective income derived from urbanization to provide village infrastructure and social welfare provision for more than 100,000 “land-losing” villagers. During her doctoral research, the Principal Investigator (PI) conducted intensive field research in 8 villages to examine the impact of SCs on reconfiguring the institutional arenas for the interaction of local actors in daily governance. In this proposed study, the PI intends to extend the scope of the study to all SCs in the area. Using sets of longitudinal and cross-sectional data gathered from 517 SCs in 52 administrative villages, the core of the research will combine qualitative analysis with quantitative modelling to examine how these SCs have interacted with state policies and informal rules (such as village norms and customs) in shaping their economic outcome and performance in social welfare provision. The findings of this study will provide new insights into how SCs have enabled and/or constrained the urban transformation of rural villages. They will enrich a growing body of literature on China’s urbanization which is paying increasing attention to the impact of SCs on transforming the collective land ownership system and reshaping local governance practices. The relevant findings will provide useful insights helping SCs to improve their operation. The findings will also provide concrete evidence for the city government to critically evaluate the impact of its intervention strategies. This will inform policy making towards better social welfare provision for “land-losing” villagers and better community development in urbanizing villages.

25203215.label: Realisation of objectives
25203215.value: Project Objective #1 has been achieved. The PI has collected five categories of data relating to a total of more than 500 SCs in Guangzhou Luogang. They included: spatial features and socio-economic characteristics; organizational structure; financial status; conditions of land use and development; and government strategies and policies. This database was collected through a number of channels. They included: (1) the Platform of Village Information Disclosure which is an online system built by the Guangzhou Municipality for the public to oversee the operation of SCs and village governance; (2) the archival records kept by the Villagers’ Committees; and (3) the documentary sources such as government working papers, government policy notices, leader speeches, past development layout plans and aerial photographs. Moreover, the PI conducted more than 120 face-to-face interviews with local actors, including local officials, village cadres and villagers, to collect and clarify this database. Project Objective #2 has been achieved. Existing studies tend to view shareholding reforms as a bottom-up process mainly driven by the initiatives of villagers to defend their economic and social interests. They therefore suggested that the domination of lineage-based power was the main cause of income inequality among villagers. In this ECS project, the PI emphasized the need to bring the role of the state back into the analysis of income distribution at the SC level. Using a mix of qualitative and quantitative methods, the PI examined how the state policy has interacted with village institutions to determine the management and distribution of collective income among villagers. The core of the study examined three sets of inter-related factors, including (a) leaderships of village cadres (e.g. % of vote in grassroots election/re-election, education level, or number of reported cases of malpractice), (b) the cohesion of villagers from different clans (e.g. number of shareholders from the same family), and (c) policies on shareholding reforms and land development control (e.g. statutory land use zoning pattern, planning permission). The analysis results shows that the informal institutions such as traditional norms and traditions were not as obvious as existing studies expected. Rather, the local state had decisive effects on the economic performance of SCs through its direct interventions in land development as well as infrastructure and social welfare provision. Project Objective #3 has been achieved. The findings of this ECS project show that the economic performance of SCs mainly varied in the form of dividend payment, and income from “reserved commercial land development” projects. Villagers from three urban areas, namely, Luogang Street, Yonghe Street and Dongqu Street earned higher collective income than those from Jiulong Town, Lianghe Street and Xiagnng Street. The villagers living in Jiulong Town earned lower income. They held a large amount of land compensation fees and reserved commercial land. But, due to the remote location of their land, they earned lower collective income than those living in Luogang, Yonghe and Dongqu. Comparatively, villagers from Lianhe and Xiagang earned much lower collective income, even though these two areas were also well-developed. The villagers living in these two areas did not own many reserved commercial land, as their arable land were mostly resumed in the 1980s when villagers were offered with urban hukou rather than reserved commercial land as compensation. To this end, villagers in Lianhe and Xigang could only earn little collective income, even though their reserved land were located in well-developed urban areas. These findings suggest the amount of “reserved commercial land” and the proximity of such lands to urban infrastructure were the most important factors directly affecting the economic performance of SCs. Project Objective #4 has been achieved. The PI has identified two major impacts of SCs on the urban transformation of rural villages. First, shareholding reforms during the 1990s impeded the urban transformation of rural villages as they strengthened the village self-governance organizations and allowed a revival of informal village norms and customs in the management and distribution of collective income. Second, the ongoing shareholding reforms since the early 2000s has enabled the rapid urban transformation of rural villages as they undermined village-wide mechanisms (which were traditionally governed by informal rules such as customs and norms) by halting villagers’ indigenous entitlement to the collective land and assets. Project Objective #5 has been achieved. Based on the findings of this project, the PI made three key policy recommendations. First, the local state should continue to enhance its financial input to improve public goods and social welfare services for villagers. Due to the different economic performance of SCs, direct interventions by state in the provision of medical care services and old-age pensions are essential to ensure villagers from different SCs to have equal access to social welfare. Second, while increasing financial inputs to improve social welfare for villagers, the local state should allow sufficient decentralization of administrative authority and delegation of power to the villages and effective decision making at the village level. This requires the local state to consider a fundamental policy shift, away from sole reliance on the means of formalization and integration, to greater emphasis on the benefits of informality in the local governance.

25203215.label: Major findings and research outcome
25203215.value: Shareholding Cooperatives (SCs) provided the share dividends and social welfare services for villagers who have been forced to embrace an urban way of life after losing their arable land to urbanization. The current trend of shareholding reforms have enabled the urban transformation of rural villages. However, the varying economic performance of SCs created increasing economic inequality among villagers. The findings of this projects suggest that the increasing autonomy of SCs in the management of collective assets and the resultant fragmentation of village governance contributed to the income disparities between the villagers from different SCs. However, this is not because governance fragmentation undermined the control of the state over villages or enhanced the power of local cadres and lineage-based power to manipulate village governance in favor of the interests of their clan members. Instead, it is because the fragmentation of village governance gradually undermined a village-wide mechanism that counted on both formal and informal rules to reduce distributional inequalities among villagers. By removing the village-based mechanism for ensuring distributional justice, the state has made ongoing attempts directly intervene in the management and distribution of collective assets. The methodological implication of these findings is that the analysis of SCs can lead us into questions of community building and identity, issues of property and development rights and what they imply for the restructuring of state-village power relations in urbanizing China. Drawing from these findings, the PI generated new, critical insights about China’s unique patterns and latest trends of urban development through publications in top academic journals. As shown in Part C, two papers have been published in International Journal of Urban and Regional Research (IJURR), and The China Quarterly) respectively. Currently, 3 papers are under review by Environment and Planning A, Land Use Policy, and Journal of Urban history respectively. Furthermore, the PI has delivered presentations in three international conferences to discuss the implications of the findings of this project on advancing the existing and new theories in the field of urban studies. Moreover, as invited speakers for some symposium and forum organized by universities and local governments, the PI explained the policy implications of this project through presentations Last but not least, the PI organized three symposia/seminars on the topics related to this ECS projects with the aims of providing a platform for knowledge exchange.

25203215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25203215.value: This ECS project provided both new theoretical perspectives and methodological insights into studying the complexity of state-community power relationships in urbanizing China. It led the PI to succeed in the applications of two research projects as follows: (1) GRF Grant 2018/2019: Urban Regeneration in Chinese Cities: An Empirical Study of “Village-in-the-City” Redevelopment in Guangzhou (GRF 15219318) (2) Ford Foundation Grant 2018: Community Planning and Self-governance Capacity Building for the Emerging Urban Communities in Periurban China: An Action-oriented Research Approach (Ford Foundation 0175-1049)

25205315.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25205315.value: 高性能RFID协议的设计分析与实现

25205315.label: Project Objectives
25205315.value: Enabling PHY concurrency to improve RFID efficiency. The most basic operation in an RFID system is to identify each of the individual RFID tags labeling different physical objects. Since the RFID signals are wirelessly transmitted and a large number of RFID tags share the wireless channel, the concurrent transmissions of multiple tags result in collisions. To avoid collisions, current commodity RFID systems define a sequential identification process. The tag arbitration schemes aim at avoiding transmission collisions through ordered schedule so as to improve the efficiency. These approaches, intrinsically limited by the sequential operational property, suffer from heavy wireless collisions and contentions. In the proposed investigation, we plan to develop novel physical layer concurrent transmission techniques, which allow multiple RFID tags to transmit in parallel. We will synthesize the recent collision recovery technique and the priori knowledge of RFID upper layer specification. With the help of such techniques, we are able to develop highly parallel RFID identification approaches where multiple tags can be queried and identified concurrently and the restriction of exclusive channel occupation can be removed. Developing efficient RFID estimation algorithms. Estimating the number of RFID tags and searching for a particular list of tags are practically important in many applications. For instance, we need to count the total number of passenger baggage attached with RFID tags, or in port inventory management examine RFID tag labeled goods in cargo containers specified in a particular list of items. Those problems can be easily reduced to identifying the IDs of all RFID tags and enumerating them. As aforementioned, however, current RFID identification approaches suffer from low. Knowing the approximate result with some guaranteed accuracy and confidence level will be adequate in many application scenarios. For example, it suffices to know the approximate amount of products instead of the exact number in shipping a large amount of cargoes. Previous estimation schemes have explored to adopt various probabilistic methods, which only differentiate busy/idle slots, extracting 1-bit information from each time slot. Unlike those works, we plan to explore the possibility of further improving the estimation efficiency by extracting more information from collisions at RFID physical layer. We plan to learn the collision patterns with different number of concurrent transmissions and count the number of colliding tags to extract more than 1-bit information in each time slot. Then, we plan to aggregate the information extracted from all the time slots to estimate the tag population and achieve higher estimation efficiency. With the help of such approaches, we expect to significantly advance the state-of-the-art performance bound. Software defined RFID platform for prototyping, debugging, and testing. The intrinsic software hardware bind of RFID technology leads to excessive difficulties in systematically testing and implementing new protocols. Existing RFID readers are generally black box systems which provides only limited configuration interface for external researchers. These systems do not provide low-level flexibility to observe or modify the MAC or PHY layer operations. Thus, the PHY/MAC layer modification is only accessible for hardware manufacturers. For this reason, most researchers can only evaluate RFID protocols by simulations before they accumulate enough confidence to redesign the RFID hardware. The provided flexibility allows PHY/MAC functionality to be easily modified through rewriting user-level software components. In this proposal, we propose to build a SDR based framework for prototyping, debugging and testing the large-scale RFID protocols. We plan to incorporate the Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) platform and WISP programmable tags into our SDR-enabled RFID framework. To the best of our knowledge, this is a pioneering work that incorporates SDR platforms into RFID prototyping, debugging and testing. In spite of validating our proposed algorithms, the successful implementation of the framework itself provides RFID research community a novel way and proven experience in supporting large-scale implementation.

25205315.label: Major findings and research outcome
25205315.value: All key objectives have been successfully achieved. 1 PhD student has been trained and graduated. 11 journal papers and 5 conference papers have been published. Major fundings and research outcome can be summarised as follows. 1) We developed novel physical layer concurrent transmission techniques, which allow multiple RFID tags to transmit in parallel. We investigated to leverage the prior knowledge of RFID coding schemes and spatial-temporal diversity of RFID backscatter signals in physical layer. With the systematic integration of existing signal processing and proposed collision recovery techniques, we developed highly parallel RFID identification approaches where multiple tags can be queried and identified concurrently. This funding indicates that it is indeed possible to enable concurrent transmissions of multiple RFID tags by resolving collisions in physical layer. 2) We developed efficient RFID physical layer information extraction algorithm to estimate the colliding tags in each response slot. The extracted information helps improve not only the cardinality estimation efficiency but also guide the subsequent queries in tree based RFID identification schemes. We proposed to estimate the colliding tags by counting the number of clusters exhibited in RFID physical layer. This finding indicates that the clustering patterns in physical layer can be used to estimate the number of colliding tags. 3) We built experiment platforms for RFID physical layer investigation. The software defined RFID platform consists of USRP N210 software radio which acts as RFID reader and several WISP tags which allow flexible programming and protocol testing. Such a software defined platform enables us to conduct physical layer protocol design and implementation. We plan to further develop the software defined platform for wireless communication and mobile computing research and education.

25205315.value: We plan to further develop the software defined RFID platform for various types of wireless networking and mobile computing research and education.

25205315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25205315.value: RFID technology has recently attracted wide attention from the academia and industry. An RFID tag can harvest energy and transmit data to RFID readers to enable item tracking, identification, and logistics. However, as the number of tags increase, current RFID readers cannot efficiently address tag collisions. As a result, the reading efficiency is very low. This project studies this problem and proposes innovative physical layer techniques to fundamentally improve the operation efficiency of RFID systems. The proposed techniques include collision resolution algorithms that can support concurrent transmissions of multiple tags, efficient algorithms to estimate the number of colliding tags, and software defined testbed which can be used for research and education.

25208115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25208115.value: Engineering novel materials that support the unique phenomenon of one-way wave propagation can bring strong direction-dependent energy and information transmission. Such effect is highly beneficial for many applications such as logic devices construction and signal processing, therefore has drawn considerable attention and research effort. Unidirectional materials allow wave transmission only in forward direction while blocking the incident signal in reverse direction. The development of such materials is immensely challenging due to the reciprocal nature of acoustic and optical wave propagation. Zeeman effect and modal splitting in ferromagnetic atoms induced by magnetic bias were utilized to realize nonreciprocal electromagnetic wave transmission. For acoustic wave, engineered structures containing active materials, for example piezoelectric plate with nonlinear electrical control circuit and new three-port acoustic circulator, have been demonstrated this year as possible nonreciprocal solutions. However, their essential requirement of providing continuous electric power supply may turn into a crucial obstacle that will eventually limit the practical use. Alternative approaches were also studied within a number of scopes including phononic crystal and nonlinear medium. While those approaches provided reasonable passive schemes, the resultant materials are generally bulky in size. At the same time, they have not been able to practically address the important issue of insufficient energy transmission in forward direction. Based on the above-mentioned considerations, this proposed study aims at introducing the concept of metamaterials to the development of novel passive unidirectional acoustic medium. It is believed that the proposed study shall ultimately result in the first passive nonreciprocal acoustic metamaterial that can fulfill high forward acoustic wave transportation, while maintaining broadband high contrast ratio. The proposed research will be implemented in two phases including: (i) developing new passive unidirectional acoustic metamaterials with high forward direction transmission, (ii) exploring non-reciprocity with passive acoustic metamaterials. Theoretical modeling and numerical simulation shall be adopted. In addition, samples shall be fabricated and experimentally examined both in air and in water to measure the performance and verify the metamaterials design. It is expected that the target passive unidirectional acoustic metamaterials will be able to provide appealing integration solution, enabling not only the construction of next generation acoustic logic devices but also new control methodology in noise cancelling, biomedical ultrasound imaging and underwater acoustics technology.

25208115.label: Realisation of objectives
25208115.value: The objectives of the project “Design of passive unidirectional acoustic metamaterials” have been adjusted accordingly to focus on the study in air environment, based on the comments from the external reviewers and the adjusted budget. I'm happy to report, with comprehensive study conducted during the project, all five projective have been successfully realized. Below I would like to report in detail the realisation of five project objectives. Objective No.1: To adopt the metamaterials concept in developing novel passive unidirectional acoustic medium. This new approach aims at solving the challenges of external power requirement, bulky size and low transmission. Realisation: In this project, we successfully adopted the concept of acoustic metamaterials into the design of novel passive unidirectional medium and developed two different types of acoustic metamaterials. Both of them are small in size, can achieve high transmission, without the requirement of any external power. The first one is an all passive acoustic PT-symmetric metamaterials crystal. This acoustic PT-symmetric material is constructed through periodically interleaving two different passive meta-structures, the groove- and holey-structured metamaterials, along the radial direction inside an acoustic waveguide. Arranged in the form of a 2D circumferentially expanded Bragg reflector within the annular sector region, it provides balanced real and imaginary part modulations, required by the passive PT-symmetric system, to the refractive index. This complex modulation offers a unidirectional wave vector toward the sector centre. At the frequency corresponding to the exceptional point, wave vectors of the incident wave, the reflection wave, and the unidirectional wave vector provided by the complex modulation offered by the metamaterial crystal are mismatched for forward and backward incidences, leading to a trivial effect of bidirectional reflectionlessness. The second one is a helical-structured acoustic metamaterial with gradient index distribution. Each unit cell of this metamaterial is a deep sub-wavelength resonator designed based on space coiling principle. The helical-structured acoustic metamaterial consists of four spiraling blades spaced at 90 degree to each other, connected through a central slender column. Its geometric properties can be described by outer diameter, inner diameter, overall length, and thread lead, which is the distance along the unit cell’s axis that is covered by one complete rotation of each blade over 360 degrees. All four geometric properties are smaller than the wavelength of sound in air. Inside the metamaterials, acoustic waves are forced to propagate along a space-coiled helical path instead of the normal straight route. The refractive index can be decided from the ratio between the helical path length and its projection on the propagation direction. The study on this acoustic metamaterial also realized the second project objective. Objective No.2: To conduct theoretically and numerical study of unidirectional acoustic metamaterials that consist of deep sub-wavelength space coiling resonators. Realisation: In this project, we successfully realized this projective by conducting theoretical, numerical and experimental study on helical-structured acoustic metamaterial designed based on space coiling principle and the effect of applying gradient index distribution. We investigated the helical-structured elements whose pitch has linear variation along the middle axis of the cylindrical unit cells, to match the impedance of air with small helicity density at both ends. By using the transfer matrix method, the validity of the effective media model for gradient helicoid metamaterial was theoretically verified. We have experimentally measured the energy transmission efficiency to be approaching 100% and evaluated the dispersion and loss mechanism of a helicoid unit cell. A flat metalens is designed, fabricated and experimentally demonstrated to work in a wide frequency range. A very important accomplishment is that the acoustic behavior of the gradient index helical-structured acoustic metamaterials can be predicted by the effective parameter model, which paves the way for the “inverse design” methodology from demanded character to a corresponding metamaterial structure and greatly enriched the flexibility and possibilities. Objective No.3: To explore the realization of non-reciprocal passive hybridized metamaterials consisting of periodically arranged coupled deep subwavelength scatter and absorber units. Realisation: In this project, we successfully realized this projective. Our designed the all passive acoustic PT-symmetric metamaterials crystal material is constructed through periodically interleaving two different passive meta-structures along the radial direction: the groove-structured (as deep subwavelength scatter) and the holey-structured acoustic metamaterials (as deep subwavelength absorber units) arranged in the form of a two-dimensional circumferentially expanded Bragg reflector within the annular sector region. The combination of two passive metamaterials provides balanced real and imaginary part PT-symmetric sound modulations to the refractive index. This complex modulation offers a unidirectional wave vector towards the sector center. For forward direction incident plane waves, strong specular reflection only takes place in particular positions where incident and reflected wave vectors satisfy the wavevector-matching condition. For the backward propagation, large mismatch of wave vectors would lead to diminished reflection due to the unidirectional wave vector of the acoustic PT-symmetric metamaterials crystal. The resultant overall two-dimensional PT potential goes beyond the complex gain/loss dimer configuration, generating equivalent unpaired k vectors to enable unidirectional reflectionlessness and one-way sound focusing over spectrum. Objective No.4: To fabricate the 3D structure acoustic metamaterials sample and conduct thorough experiments with audible sound in air to validate the proposed designs. Realisation: In this project, we realized this projective with successful sample fabrication and experimental measurements. For the all passive acoustic PT-symmetric metamaterials crystal, the real part metamaterial modulator and the frameworks of the imaginary part metamaterial modulator are fabricated using additive manufacturing based on fused deposition modeling. The base material is polylactic acid, which can be treated as rigid for airborne sound due to the large contrast in acoustic impedance. The mesh fabrics of woven with monofilament fibers for imaginary part modulation are firmly attached to the framework. For the gradient index helical-structured acoustic metamaterial, samples were manufactured by 3D printing with the photopolymer (Somos GP Plus) material. We have successfully conducted experimental measurements on fabricated samples with audible sound in air. Generally, computer controls an automated scanning system with microphone via LabVIEW to scan sound field distribution with phase information. The lock-in amplifier is used for signal generation and acquisition. Objective No.5: To assess the actual performance of proposed passive unidirectional acoustic metamaterials and discuss possible design optimization. Realisation: In this project, the fifth projective has been successfully realized. We have conducted numerous experimental measurements on the all passive acoustic PT-symmetric metamaterials crystal and gradient index helical-structured acoustic metamaterial samples, to assess the actual performance. The outputs acquired during the early stage experiments have been used to provide feedback to the optimization of theoretical model and metamaterials design.

25208115.label: Major findings and research outcome
25208115.value: With this project, we have the following major findings and research outcome: - We have designed, fabricated and assessed the first all passive acoustic PT-symmetric metamaterials crystal. It is constructed through periodically interleaving two different passive meta-structures, the groove- and holey-structured metamaterials, along the radial direction inside an acoustic waveguide. Arranged in the form of a 2D circumferentially expanded Bragg reflector within the annular sector region, it provides passive balanced real and imaginary part PT-symmetric sound modulations to the refractive index of the metamaterials crystal. This complex sound modulation offers a unidirectional wave vector. At the frequency corresponding to the exceptional point, wave vectors of the incident wave, the reflection wave, and the unidirectional wave vector provided by the complex modulation offered by the metamaterial crystal are mismatched for forward and backward incidences, leading to a trivial effect of bidirectional reflectionlessness. Major part of this find is included in paper titled "Unidirectional Wave Vector Manipulation in Two-Dimensional Space with an All Passive Acoustic Parity-Time-Symmetric Metamaterials Crystal" published in Physical Review Letters included in Part C. It is also utilised in other related work in Part C. - We have further integrated our all passive acoustic PT-symmetric metamaterials crystal into a ring resonator. Inside this acoustic parity-time-symmetric ring cavity, an annular PT-symmetric index modulation that supports unidirectional eigen whispering-gallery modes at the exceptional point, a monopole sound source may generate a whispering-gallery acoustic wave field exhibiting completely reversed chirality. This abnormal phenomenon, which we call as spontaneous chirality reversing, is a result of the coalesced eigenstates interplay: the destructive interference between the two excited eigen-WGMs leads to complete sound field cancelation; and the trivial in-phase reflection accumulates into a nontrivial WGM in the opposite direction. Major part of this find is included in paper titled "Revealing the missing dimension at an exceptional point" published in Nature Physics included in Part C. - We have also designed and thoroughly studied a gradient index helical-structured acoustic metamaterial based on the space coiling principle. It has been experimentally demonstrated to be able to modulate sound wavefront with nearly perfect transmission over a broad bandwidth. Taking advantage of the linear spectral phase shifting, a thin flat metalens is constructed to demonstrate sound focusing with the extraordinary transmission for more than 1/3 octave band. Major part of this find is included in paper titled "Theoretical and experimental study of gradient-helicoid metamaterial" published in Journal of Sound and Vibration.

25208115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25208115.value: In contrast to the balanced gain-loss configurations that require external power, our all passive acoustic metamaterials crystal provides intrinsic parity-time-symmetric potential to modulate the effective refractive index in complex domain. Moreover, the absence of cut-off in such acoustic parity-time-symmetric system makes the extension of general parity-time symmetry study to multi-dimensional space highly feasible, which remains a great challenge with other classical wave systems. Our demonstration provides a new degree of freedom to the realization of unique wave dynamics for applications like noise control, acoustic sensing, and imaging. For the next step, we would like to propose to construct logic acoustic devices, for example unidirectional sound beam splitter, with our all passive acoustic metamaterials crystal developed in this project. Our major finding of the spontaneous chirality reversing in passive acoustic PT-symmetric systems is beyond the conventional eigenspace-based knowledge. It reveals new degree-of-freedoms associated with the interaction of coalesced eigenstates at exceptional points. For the next step, we would like to propose to study the generation and manipulation of orbital angular momentum with demonstrated chiral sound. The successful realization will promise a possible route for next-generation acoustic vortex source and devices.

25208115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25208115.value: Engineering novel materials that support the special phenomenon of unidirectional sound propagation can bring strong direction-dependent energy and information transmission. It is not only with high scientific value, but also highly beneficial for many applications such as logic devices and signal processing. Acoustic PT-symmetric system with gain and loss elements provides suitable candidate for the target. However, there is no gain medium in nature for such system. With our project, we successfully solved this problem and designed an all passive acoustic PT-symmetric metamaterials crystal. This new material is constructed through periodically interleaving two different passive metamaterials, the groove- and holey-structured metamaterials. Without the requirement of any external power supply or circuit control, it can provide unidirectional wave vector to manipulate sound wave from different directions with high flexibility and robustness. We have conducted numerical simulation and experimental test to verify the performance of designed PT-symmetric metamaterials crystal. It is used to break the current limitation of only one-dimensional PT-symmetry materials are available. The first two-dimensional PT-symmetry demonstration in any classic wave systems was also realised with unidirectional sound reflectionlessness. This finding with significant value can be further extended to different wave systems for new wave phenomena.
