25220615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25220615.value: Research Motivation: China has built the world’s longest network of High Speed Rail (HSR) systems within 5 years duration. With the expected opening of the Hong Kong high-speed railway in 2017, the 26-km long Hong Kong section of the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong express rail link will connect to the 16000-km National high-speed railway network and enhance Hong Kong’s role as the southern gateway to the mainland. Although standard life-cycle assessment (LCA) is an advantageous tool to evaluate the environmental and economic impacts of the HSR system, it is difficult for LCA to quantify the interdependence effects between alternative transportation modes, e.g. from HSR to airplane, bus and train. In order to overcome this challenge, Agent-Based Modeling (ABM) will be implemented along with LCA to include dynamic passenger occupancy analyses under various policy scenarios. The framework boundary for analyzing both direct and indirect impacts in environmental and economic perspectives includes: (1) infrastructure construction; (2) vehicle operation; and (3) fuel components. The energy consumption, greenhouse gas emissions, and other emissions, such as SO2, CO, NOx, VOC, and PM10 emissions per passenger-kilometer (pkm) of each mode will be calculated as a benchmarking. Intellectual Merits: Assessing the life-cycle of HSR by taking spatial information, ridership uncertainty into account constitutes a new tool of multi-agent LCA for infrastructure sustainability analysis. This approach is able to comprise both interdependent cost and environmental information of transportation modes for decision-making. The results of the study are expected to provide an advanced means to characterize the HSR system and understand environmental consequences under various policy scenarios. In addition, the research framework has the potential to correlate with other infrastructure systems and to assist complex decision making for other infrastructure development of Hong Kong, such as further expansion of Hong Kong International Airport or diversifying electricity supply to encompass environmental concerns. Broader Impact: The potential benefits of this research are broader than providing critical information and estimating the environmental impacts for the proposed HSR system. The method developed in this study can be applied to other non-established infrastructure systems to predict the associated environmental, economic, and social impacts with dynamic components globally. The educational impact of this project includes integrating the developed framework into undergraduate and graduate courses and curricula. New course content based on these modeling approaches can help the next generation of engineers and policy makers to understand complex issues in urban infrastructure systems and obtain multidisciplinary skills. 近五年來中國高鐵建設如火如荼的展開，營運里程已達1.6萬公里。 到2020年為止包括連接主要城市的城際交通系統將全線建成。屆時中國高鐵網路將達到5萬公里並覆蓋90%的大陸人口。 廣深港高速鐵路也是中國客運專線中，京廣高速鐵路至深圳、香港的延伸線。 廣深港高鐵連接了廣東省的廣州、東莞和深圳以及香港，是珠三角城際快速軌道交通網的骨幹部分。 隨著香港高鐵在2017年底的開通，香港高鐵將吸引眾多乘客，而原有的廣州到香港的交通模式載客量(例如廣九直通車,大巴,飛機)勢必將受到衝擊。 全生命週期評估方法被公認為是評估高鐵系統內容影響的有用工具，但是全生命週期評價把每一種交通模式都看做一個獨立的研究物件，不能系統地評估整個廣州到香港交通模式，這些交通模式之間的相互依存與相互影響的關係無法真實地體現。而交通模式載客量與其經濟性能和環保性能密切相關。因此本研究將運用代理人仿真模型改良傳統的全生命週期評估方法並結合地理信息系統來分析香港高鐵與現有交通模式的相互依存關係。進而從香港高鐵的基礎設施階段，車輛營運階段和燃料生產階段分析環境與經濟的影響。其中以每乘客公里為單位的能量消耗，溫室氣體排放與其他氣體排放包含SO2, CO, NOx, VOC, PM10將作為基準測試數據。本研究預期為高鐵的永續發展提供可靠的決策支持，研究結果將可作為其他城市的高鐵建設與交通規劃參考的理論基礎。

25220615.label: Realisation of objectives
25220615.value: To alleviate fossil fuel use, mitigate the traffic congestion, and reduce air emissions, it will be necessary to find sustainable mobility alternatives and better adapt existing transportation modes to move people in a more environmentally sound and economically feasible way. In recent years, sustainable mobility system starts to emerge with novel technologies such as high-speed railway, autonomous vehicles, and bike-sharing. Current literature on the sustainable implications of a transportation system is often neglecting the interactions between the emerging mobility and existing transportation modes and the heterogeneous individual travel patterns that affect the environmental performances. Therefore, to better understand these emerging transportation systems and inform decision making, an interdisciplinary approach tightly linking life-cycle analysis, agent-based modeling and geographic information system are used to form the behavioral rules of passengers choosing different transport modes, simulate the vehicles traveling in real-world road networks, and evaluate the economic, social, and environmental impacts of the multimodal transportation system. Three case studies focusing on three emerging systems: high-speed railway, autonomous taxis, and bike-sharing are proposed to demonstrate the benefits of using this hybrid method. Objective No. 1 and No. 2 In recent years, high-speed railway (HSR) has become a popular transport option with its fast, comfortable, and environmentally friendly features. However, the whole lifecycle of the HSR system should not only include the operation of HSR but also consider vehicle manufacturing, infrastructure construction, and so on. After the opening of an HSR link, passengers may shift from other transportation modes to the HSR, and their mobility habits may change. This project is the first study that takes into account the interactions between existing transport modes and a newly built HSR and the changes to the whole system’s environmental performance with the introduction of HSR. To understand the complex interdependence of HSR with competing modes on passenger occupancy (objective No.1) and investigate the environmental and economic impact of HSR with competing modes (objective No.2), a spatial agent-based model for environmental assessment of dynamic transport system (ALENT) is developed. ALENT combines agent-based modeling (ABM) and life-cycle analysis (LCA) to explore the environmental impacts of an existing passenger transportation system with a newly introduced HSR. A logit model combined with the small-world theory is applied to simulate the passengers’ mode choice behaviors. ALENT was built to simulate the operational and lifecycle environmental performance of HSR and other competing modes with the influences of dynamic market behaviors incorporated, an addition beyond traditional lifecycle thinking. Based on the simulation results, several recommendations are proposed to improve the lifecycle environmental performance of the cross-boundary system. First, the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong SAR HSR needs to sustain a high occupancy rate, more than 80%, to lower the environmental impacts. Second, shutting down the through train, which provides the same service as the HSR but with longer travel times, can mitigate system lifecycle environmental impacts by up to 30%. Objective No. 3 ALENT also can achieve the objective No. 3 of the project. As previously discussed, HSR can mitigate environmental impacts such as reduce energy consumption, carbon emissions, and SO2 emissions by maintaining a high occupancy rate. The main driver to influence the occupancy rate is the ticket fare. ALENT was used to simulate different scenarios. The results show that the HSR’s occupancy rate is the highest when the ticket fare is set as HK$60/100km. However, the whole environmental performance is worse than the baseline scenario because of the low occupancy rate of aircraft. The optimum combination of occupancy rate and environmental performance emerges in the scenario of an HSR ticket fare of HK$85/100km, with a resulting occupancy rate of 0.808. ALENT is used to examine the Hong Kong-mainland China cross-boundary transportation in this study, but the framework of ALENT cab be applied to other cities for environmental performance evaluation of transportation system development. Decision-makers can use this modelling tool to determine appropriate actions within their particular jurisdiction. Objective No. 4. To further assist policy-making for sustainable transportation infrastructure development, this project expands the framework of ALENT to other emerging transportation systems. The autonomous taxi study evaluates the travel costs and environmental implications of substituting conventional personal vehicle travel with autonomous taxi travel based on real-world road networks. The autonomous taxi study demonstrates that to meet daily commute demand with wait times less than 3 minutes, the optimized autonomous taxi fleet size is only 20% of the conventional solo-commuting personal car fleet. However, the environmental impacts of autonomous taxi do not show significant improvement over conventional vehicles. Another emerging transportation system, the bike-sharing system, is also discussed in this project. Bike-sharing systems have rapidly expanded around the world in recent years, but the impacts of bike-sharing on travelers’ usage of other transport modes in an integrated transportation system remain unclear. The project team simulates the environmental and human health impacts of bike-sharing on travelers’ usage of other transport modes in an integrated transportation system, considering their interactions through the modeling of the modal split based on the heterogeneous mode choice behaviors of travelers. The results of this case study indicate that using bike-sharing to solve the first/last mile problem of the transit system can be the most sustainable strategy. This project further upgraded the framework of ALENT with the input of Big Data. A data-informed spatial agent-based model is developed to understand the interactions between stakeholders to assist the bike-sharing design in an integrated transportation system. Although bike-sharing has been recognised as an active and sustainable transportation mode, the dramatic expansion of free-floating bike-sharing services generates problems such as illegal parking and low utilisation. The key design decisions considered are the locations and capacities of bicycle parking lots in the system, as well as the connected bike lanes between parking lots. The model has been applied to the case of Hong Kong for a demonstration. The results show that the parking lots with higher capacities are mostly close to the metro stations. Most people to be willing to change the parking location, the minimum fare discount rate should be set to at least 30%. The average trip time can be reduced by 3.8%, and per-user cost can be reduced by 2.4% with an expected investment of HK$1 million to build new cycle tracks and connect existing cycleways. Last but not least, this project extended the scope not only to the transportation infrastructure but also to consider the energy-saving in the manufacturing and building sectors. The project team conducted another study using data envelopment analysis (DEA) to develop a comprehensive decision-support tool for guiding the selection of energy-saving measures according to geographical characteristics across China. Future studies may consider the interdependencies between different infrastructure systems (e.g. transportation, building, water/wastewater, etc.) for improving the overall sustainable development.

25220615.label: Major findings and research outcome
25220615.value: This project mainly generated 5 peer-reviewed journal papers. The research findings are presented in two international conferences. The first paper presents an urban transportation simulation model for evaluating lifecycle environmental performance. This is the first study to integrate geographic information to quantify station’s accessibility levels and construct real-world intercity transportation maps for high-speed rail (HSR) systems. The main findings of this paper are: 1) the occupancy rate of the HSR should be maintained more than 80% to lower the environmental impacts; 2) The Guandong to Hong Kong intercity through train is suggested to gradually shot down to mitigate the system environmental impacts by up to 30%. The second paper evaluates the travel costs and environmental implications of substituting conventional personal vehicle travel with autonomous taxis (aTaxis) travel by an agent-based model (ABM). The results indicate that to meet daily commute demand with wait times less than 3 minutes, the optimized autonomous taxi fleet size is only 20% of the conventional solo-commuting personal car fleet. Commuting cost decreases by 38%, and daily vehicle utilization increases from 14 to 92 min When using internal combustion engine aTaxis, energy consumption, greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and SO2 emissions are respectively 16, 25, and 10% higher than conventional solo commuting, mainly because of unoccupied repositioning between trips. The third and fourth papers investigate the impacts of bike-sharing on travelers’ usage of other transport modes in an integrated transportation system. Spatial agent-based models are developed to understand the interactions between stakeholders for assisting the bike-sharing system design. The results suggest: 1) free use of sharing-bike to connect the transit system can be most sustainable with 1.5 million US dollars in transportation damage cost saved per year; 2) the minimum fare discount rate should be set for 30% for sharing-bike users to park in the closet suggested parking lot. These spatial ABM models can be powerful tools to help policy-makers improve the sustainability of a multi-modal transportation system with bike-sharing. The fifth paper extends the scope to not only the transportation but also the manufacturing and building sectors. This paper develops an efficiency evaluation framework by using data envelopment analysis to guide the selection of the most efficient energy-saving measures in different parts of China. The results indicate that the reconstruction of industrial boiler furnaces is the most energy-efficient measure in the manufacturing sector, while energy management systems are the most efficient measure in the building sector.

25220615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25220615.value: The main goal of this project is to reduce the environmental impacts of transportation infrastructure development. This project develops an interdisciplinary approach tightly linking life-cycle analysis, agent-based modelling, and geographic information system to generate the behavioural rules of passengers choosing different transport modes, simulate the vehicles traveling in real-world road networks, and evaluate the economic, social, and environmental impacts of the multimodal transportation system. The further development of the research can focus on 1) modifying and applying the developed models to other infrastructure systems (e.g. building, energy, water/wastewater, road and bridge systems) to understand their system’s interdependence and quantify the environmental impacts; 2) integrating advanced technologies (e.g. neural networks, deep learning, reinforcement learning) to further enhance the models. The project team has been working on these two directions for more than two years. One of the studies has been presented at an international conference in 2018. One paper about exploring the most efficient energy conservation measures has been published in Energy Policy in 2018. Another paper about evaluating the policies for promoting energy conservation toward sustainable development in the industrial sector is now under revision by One Earth, Cell Press.

25220615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25220615.value: To alleviate fossil fuel use, mitigate traffic congestion, and reduce air emissions, it is necessary to find sustainable mobility alternatives and better adapt existing transportation modes to move people in a more environmentally sound and economically feasible way. In recent years, sustainable mobility systems have begun to emerge, encompassing a range of novel technologies and solutions such as high-speed railway (HSR), autonomous vehicles, and bike-sharing systems. To better understand these emerging transportation systems and inform decision making, an interdisciplinary approach tightly linking life-cycle analysis, agent-based modeling, and geographic information system are used to generate the behavioral rules of passengers choosing different transport modes, simulate the vehicles traveling in real-world road networks, and evaluate the economic, social, and environmental impacts of the multimodal transportation system. This project developed a series of advanced computational models to help policy-makers improve their decision making for enhancing the sustainability performances of transportation infrastructure development. Several strategies and policies are recommended (e.g. the occupancy rate of HSR should be maintained at 80% or more to lower the environmental impacts; Free use of the shared bike to connect the transit system can be more sustainable with HK$11.6 million in transportation damage cost saved per year.)

25221215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25221215.value: Clouds usually cover more than 50% of the earth’s surface area at any given time, and are important for the transport and redistribution of atmospheric constituents. Fog, another form of atmospheric condensed water, is a kind of cloud that touches the ground. Clouds and fogs have many similarities yet are often treated indiscriminately in terms of chemistry and chemical processing. Clouds and fogs play important roles in earth’s radiation budget, hydrologic cycle, and atmospheric chemistry. The interactions between clouds/fogs, atmospheric gases and aerosols could change the fate of trace gases and the physical-chemical properties of aerosols, and are seen as the most important forces driving climate change. Recent studies have revealed large knowledge gaps regarding the cloud processing of organic species, especially the secondary organic aerosol (SOA) formation through aqueous-phase reactions in cloud droplets. Our understanding on this atmospheric multiphase process is far from complete, and many uncertainties still remain, including precursors, intermediate products, detailed mechanisms and effects of cloud composition. These processes may significantly influence the particulate and haze pollution, which are the extremely severe air pollution problems in China’s major cities, including Hong Kong. Previous studies in Hong Kong have suggested the presence of high concentration of SOA, which, however, was underestimated in some modeling studies mostly due to the unclear mechanism in aqueous phase. The chemical characteristics of cloud/fog waters and cloud-aerosol interactions in Hong Kong have not been well addressed, thus little is known about the abundance and contribution of in-cloud produced SOA in this region. Therefore, we propose a first field study to measure the water-soluble organic species in low-level cloud/fog waters at a mountain site in Hong Kong, as well as other key species, followed by comprehensive data and modeling analysis. The goal is to understand the chemical composition of cloud/fog waters and aqueous reactions/production of major organic species in clouds/fogs in subtropical Hong Kong, and to evaluate their contributions to SOA formation and air quality. This study will fill the knowledge gap on cloud-aerosol interaction and atmospheric multiphase chemistry in a polluted environment of Asia, and will improve the performance of current air-quality models which are used in the formulation of pollution-control measures. 地球有一半以上的面積經常被不同類型的雲層覆蓋著，雲對大氣成份的輸送與分佈有著重要的作用。霧是接近地面的雲，兩者的化學行為和化學過程非常相似。雲和霧在影響地球輻射平衡、水循環和大氣化學方面都扮演著重要的角色。大氣痕量氣體、氣溶膠與雲霧的相互作用以改變痕量氣體的大氣壽命及氣溶膠的物理化學性質，因而被視為影響氣候變化的重要驅動力。國際最新研究發現雲霧過程可以影響大氣有機成分的濃度和分佈，並可通過雲霧滴上的液相反應生成二次有機氣溶膠。但目前對於液相二次有機氣溶膠生成的前體物、中間產物和詳細機制等方面的認識還存在嚴重不足，而這些化學過程對許多城市(包括香港) 目前所面臨的氣溶膠和灰霾污染具有重要影響，亟需進一步的深入研究。 以往研究表明香港大氣中存在著較高濃度的二次有機氣溶膠，但是現有的空氣質量模式模擬往往低估其含量， 而模式缺乏詳細的液相反應機制可能是造成這種誤差的主要原因。目前針對香港地區雲霧水化學特徵及雲霧與氣溶膠相互作用的研究還未充分開展，因此該地區雲霧過程對二次有機氣溶膠生成的影響尚不清楚。本項目計劃在香港地區高山站開展針對雲霧水中水溶性有機成分和相關物種的現場觀測，並進行數據分析和大氣多相物理化學模式分析。本研究旨在了解亞熱帶香港地區雲霧水的化學成分和有機組分的雲霧液相反應過程，並探討大氣液相反應對二次氣溶膠生成和空氣質量的影響，預期可以完善對亞洲高污染條件下云-氣溶膠相互作用和大氣多相化學過程的認識，也可提高當前空氣質量模式的模擬性能。

25221215.label: Realisation of objectives
25221215.value: To achieve the project objectives, comprehensive field measurement, data analysis and modeling studies were conducted during the project period. 1. Two comprehensive cloud measurement campaigns were carried out at the summit of Tai Mo Shan (TMS, 957 m a.s.l.) in Hong Kong during October-November of 2016 and March-April of 2017. Eighty-four cloud/fog water samples were collected during the campaigns, and the aerosols, trace gases (i.e., O3, SO2, NO/NOx), and meteorological parameters were also measured concurrently during the campaigns. A series of laboratory testing were firstly performed to optimize the analytical methodology for trace-level organic species in cloud/fog droplets. The chemical composition of concurrent gas-, aerosol- and aqueous- phase samples were then characterized and quantified in the laboratory using the optimized analytical methods, including DOC, water-soluble inorganic ions, mono- and di- carbonyls, carboxylic acids, and the stable carbon-13 isotopic composition. Data analysis was subsequently performed, and the abundances and characteristics of carbonyls and carboxylic acids in cloud/fog waters were obtained, for the first time in Hong Kong. Cloud water was found very acidic in Hong Kong, indicating that cloud water was significantly influenced by anthropogenic emissions from the PRD region. Methylglyoxal was the predominant carbonyl species, followed by glyoxal, iso-pentanal and glycolaldehyde. Oxalic acid was the most abundant diacid, followed by succinic acid in autumn and phthalic acid in spring. Backward air trajectory analysis was performed to characterize the measured organic species in air masses from different origins. Polluted cloud water with abundant dissolved organic matters was observed in the continental air masses. Further analysis showed that high loadings of carboxylic and carbonyls compounds in cloud waters in autumn are mainly attributed to anthropogenic sources, including fossil fuel combustion and biomass burning, whereas marine emissions play a significant role in organic compounds in spring. Through intensive field measurements, we obtained the first insight into the chemical characteristics of low-level cloud/fog waters in Hong Kong, and characterized the abundance and variation of water-soluble inorganic and organic species. Objective 1 was fully achieved. 2. To investigate the partitioning of different organic compounds among cloud/fog droplet, aerosol and gas phase, simultaneous multiphase measurements were conducted at the mountain site in HK for the first time. The partitioning of carbonyls and carboxylic acids among different phases were examined. The mono-carbonyls mainly present in the gas phase (~98%), whereas di-carbonyls existed in both gas phase (~50%) and cloud water (30-50%), with only a small fraction (~1%) in particles. Around 20-30% of the formic and acetic acids, and 30-40% of oxalic acid were present in the particles, with the majority of abundance in the cloud droplets. The measured aqueous fraction of carbonyl compounds was compared with estimation from Henry’s law equilibrium considering the hydration reactions. Significant aqueous-phase supersaturation was found for less soluble mono-carbonyls and methylglyoxal, with 1-3 orders of magnitude higher than the theoretical partitioning values. The dependence of partitioning behaviors on different factors was further examined, including the cloud water acidity, liquid water content, salting-in/out effects, in-cloud aqueous reactions. The acidity of the cloud water can primarily affect the reactive uptake of di-carbonyls on droplets and influence the partitioning of carbonyls. The variation of measured components in cloud/fog water and aerosols along the cloud evolution was investigated to understand the processing of different species in clouds. The cloud scavenging ratios were determined for inorganic species (0.68-0.85) in the early stage of cloud processing. Meanwhile, growth rates of 0.05-0.52 µg m-3 h-1 for organics during cloud events were quantified. The analysis of gas-phase precursors with aqueous products suggested that glyoxal should be of great importance in the formation of secondary organic matters in cloud water at TMS. As the heterogeneous process of HOx radicals on cloud droplet and wet aerosols also play important roles in atmospheric radical cycling and aqueous oxidation reactions, a multiphase theoretical model was used to evaluate the roles of different parameters in determining the uptake of HO2 on a sphere droplet, including metal ion concentration, accommodation coefficient, aqueous-phase acidity, as well as production reactions. The results demonstrated the size dependence of HO2 uptake, and identified the key factors dominated the uptake coefficient on wet aerosols and cloud droplets. Through the first atmospheric multiphase campaigns at HK and in-depth data analysis, the partitioning and processing of carbonyls and carboxylic acids in cloud/fog droplets and aerosols were characterized, as well as different influencing factors. Objective 2 was also fully achieved. 3. The cloud-aerosol interactions and the impacts of cloud processing on aerosol properties were examined based on the measurement. The species ratios (i.e., oxalate/sulfate, formic/acetic acids) were employed to investigate the in-cloud formation of organic, and the effects of acidity on the in-cloud organic formation was identified. The compound-specific stable carbon-13 isotopic composition of dicarboxylic acids was examined to better evaluate the contribution of anthropogenic emissions, photochemical production, and long-range transport to the measured organic acids at TMS. The aerosol compositions in pre-cloud and post-cloud periods were compared in different cloud events, and significant sulfate and organics produced in cloud water could remain in the particle phase after cloud dissipation and lead to the mass increase in droplet-mode particles. To further evaluate the contribution of heterogeneous chemistry on SOA and haze formation, another intensive field campaign with simultaneous measurements of VOCs, carbonyls, organic aerosol was conducted at Heshan during a severe regional haze episode in HK-PRD region in January 2017. Enhanced oxygenated organic matters were observed, demonstrating a significant role of SOA in the formation of haze pollution. The relationship between carbonyls and carboxylic acids was examined, and the potential precursors and formation pathways of di-carboxylic acids and SOA were identified. Aldehydes and ketones, produced via the photooxidation of anthropogenic VOCs, were the main contributors of the carboxylic acids through both photochemistry and heterogeneous reactions. The positive matrix factorization (PMF) model was applied to understand the sources of VOCs measured at Heshan. Four anthropogenic emission sources were identified and quantified, with gasoline vehicular emission as the most significant contributor, followed by diesel emissions, biomass burning and solvent usage. An observation-based photochemical box model was developed, with the incorporation of heterogeneous processes of di-carbonyls and gas-particle partitioning of low-volatile products with the gas-phase oxidation mechanism. The comparison of model-simulated carbonyls with measurements suggested the significant roles of heterogeneous process in atmospheric evolution of di-carbonyls. Modeling sensitivity analysis was performed to investigate the atmospheric budget of di-carbonyls and to evaluate the contribution of heterogeneous chemistry of organics on SOA formation. The heterogeneous chemistry of di-carbonyls can explain ~21% of SOA formed during the several haze episode in the HK-PRD region. Moreover, a quantum chemistry model based on density functional theory was used to investigate the chemical reaction mechanisms of di-carbonyls with O3. By analyzing the geometrical and thermochemical parameters, the favorable reaction pathways were identified. The aqueous glyoxal reaction with O3 can produce acids, which could undergo further reactions and make significant contributions to SOA formation. Through in-depth data analysis and modeling studies, the formation mechanism of carboxylic acids and photochemical production of the precursors, VOCs, and carbonyls, were characterized in the HK-PRD region. The impacts of aqueous-phase reaction and cloud processing on SOA formation and haze pollution was evaluated. Objective 3 was also fully achieved.

25221215.label: Major findings and research outcome
25221215.value: Through three years research, some novel and scientific findings have been achieved, as summarized below. 1) The first comprehensive cloud-aerosol-gas multiphase field campaign in Hong Kong gained valuable insights into the origins, partitioning and transformation of various organic species in cloud waters in HK (Zhao et al., 2019; Li et al., 2020). The cloud water was found very acidic with abundant dissolved organic matters, which was significantly influenced by anthropogenic emissions in the HK-PRD region. The partitioning behavior of carbonyls compounds among cloud droplets, aerosol and gas phase was obtained in HK for the first time. Significant aqueous-phase supersaturation was found for mono-carbonyls and methylglyoxal. Valuable information on gas–cloud–aerosol interactions was obtained, and significant roles of clouds were demonstrated in altering the compositions and physical properties of aerosols via aqueous chemical processing (Li et al., 2020). 2) A severe regional haze episode in 2017 was captured and characterized by a large abundance of organic matters, followed by nitrate and sulfate (Yun et al., 2018). Enhanced contribution of oxygenated organics demonstrated important role of SOA in haze pollution. The anthropogenic source of precursors was identified and quantified using PMF, with vehicular emission as the key contributor, followed by biomass burning and solvent usage (Ling et al., 2019). The formation mechanism of carbonyls from anthropogenic VOCs were identified, while photochemical and heterogeneous processes were of comparable significance in carboxylic acid and SOA formation (Chang et al., 2019). The optimized VOC/NOx emission reduction scenarios for O3 pollution control were recommended based on model analysis (He et al., 2019). 3) A systematic understanding of heterogeneous HO2 uptake on wet aerosol and cloud droplet was obtained through a multiphase theoretical evaluation. The key factors dominating the HO2 uptake process were identified, and uptake coefficients were suggested for different atmospheric conditions (Guo et al., 2019). A photochemical box model was developed, with the incorporation of detailed heterogeneous processes of carbonyls and gas-particle partitioning of low-volatile products into the gas-phase mechanism. The derived heterogeneous parameters and modules can improve the model performance in predicting O3 and SOA formation. Observation-based model analysis has quantified the contribution of heterogeneous chemistry of carbonyls in SOA formation during haze episodes (Ling et al., 2020). The project findings fill in the knowledge gaps on atmospheric heterogeneous/multiphase chemistry in the polluted subtropical environment, and can support the formulation of air pollution control strategies in Hong Kong. The project has produced 9 peer-reviewed journal papers and 4 conference presentations.

25221215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25221215.value: The findings from this project revealed the acidic nature of the cloud droplets in HK-PRD region, and the significant influence of regional anthropogenic emission to the cloud droplet. It could also lead to acid rain, which is a severe regional environmental problem that causes more damages to the ecosystem in Hong Kong. Continuous and long-term monitoring of cloud and rainwater chemistry should be performed. In addition, the results of the project highlight the importance of cloud-aerosol-gas interactions on transforming the air pollutants and on regional air pollution formation in the HK-PRD region. It will be of great interest to extend the study of atmospheric multiphase mechanism to different conditions and other urbanized regions. This study also indicates that the factors affecting the multiphase processes and cloud-aerosol-gas interactions are more complicated than previously thought, and further studies are needed to improve the parameterizations in air quality models.

25221215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25221215.value: Clouds are ubiquitous in coastal cities, like Hong Kong, and play important roles in transport and redistribution of air pollutants. Cloud/fog can scavenge gases and particles, and also provide a medium for aqueous phase reaction that promoting new species formation. A first cloud-aerosol-gas multiphase measurement was conducted at a mountain site in Hong Kong, and the chemical composition of cloud water was characterized. This research discovered the acidic nature of cloud water in Hong Kong, and abundant dissolved organic matters in cloud water that significantly influenced by anthropogenic emissions. Valuable insights were obtained through data analysis into the origins, partitioning and transformation of different organic species in the cloud waters in Hong Kong. The findings demonstrated the essential roles of cloud processing in altering aerosol composition through scavenging and aqueous reactions. The multiphase and heterogeneous reactions were found of significance for volatile organic compound oxidation and secondary organic aerosol formation, therefore largely affecting the air quality in the HK-PRD region. The findings and improved model mechanisms are useful to improve the model performance in predicting the air pollution formation, and thus will be helpful to support the mitigation of haze pollution in the HK-PRD region.

25223215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25223215.value: Sustainable urbanization can be defined as urbanization practice which complies with sustainable development principles. Sustainable urbanization is a dynamic process that combines environmental, social, economic and political-institutional sustainability. It brings together urban and rural areas, encompassing the full range of human settlements from village to town to city to metropolis, with links at the national and global levels (UN Habitat, 2004). It has been projected by (UNDESA, 2014) that, in China, 76% of the population will live in cities in 2050. The figure is already 54% in 2014. This rapid urbanization growth has led to the need to understand urbanization as a major contributor to resource consumption and environmental damage. Such adverse effects brought on by urbanization have generated greater pressures on governments to re-think their urban development policies to be sustainable ones. In line with the promotion of sustainable urbanization, international institutions and governments at different levels are seeking solutions that integrate, in harmony, environmental, community and economic requirements. With the aim of understanding and monitoring urban sustainability performance, different assessment tools have been developed (Maclaren, 1996; Huang et al., 1998; Devuyst et al., 2001; Deakin et al., 2002; Li et al., 2009; Munier, 2011; Singh et al., 2012; Deakin and Reid, 2014). The tools include different performance indicators according to particular needs. Shen et al. (2011) developed a set of International Urban Sustainability Indicators List (IUSIL) after examining the practices in 9 different cities. Now what we need is a new and better method for assessing and communicating the urban sustainability performances of the different cities to various stakeholders including governmental officials, business sectors and the public, leading to the promotion of knowledge and experience sharing. Fuzzy logic systems allow an indicator to be assessed in qualitative terms (e.g. as good, poor etc.) as opposed to a definite measure and this is often more appropriate for evaluating urban sustainability performance of a particular city. This proposed project will further develop the fuzzy logic approach. Further, since little research has been done to examine the potential for sustainable development of a city and identify those areas that can be improved, the proposed model will integrate fuzzy logic with dynamic modelling to assess urban sustainability performance, simulate sustainable urban development, and identify potential areas that can be improved for a sustainable city. 可持續城市化可被定義爲依照可持續原則來推進城市化的實踐進程。可持續城市化是壹個動態的過程，涵蓋環境、社會、經濟及政策的可持續性，同時將鄉村和城市區域進行整合，其內涵覆蓋從鄉村到城鎮到城市再到大都市，以及到全國和全球層面的人居環境的整合。根據聯合國經濟暨社會理事會的預測，到2050年，中國將有76%的人口生活在城市。截至2014年，中國已有54%的人口生活在城市裏，應注意到的是，快速的城市化進程導致了大量的資源消耗和環境破壞，其所産生的負面效應對政府管理者産生很大壓力，管理者不得不重新審視現有政策並推行可持續的城市化策略。 在可持續城市化推進的過程中，國際各級機構和政府都在試圖尋找將環境需求、社區需求以及經濟需求進行良好整合的策略。爲了更好的理解和監測城市的可持續發展，學者們運用了不同的評估方法對城市的可持續發展表現進行評估，包括根據具體需求制定的指標體系。 目前，我們試圖構建壹個新的評價方法，以便于不同的城市利益相關者進行可持續城市化知識和經驗的分享，這些利益相關者包括政府官員、商業部門以及社會公衆。 模糊邏輯方法可以運用定性的語句對評價對象進行評估（例如，好，中，差等），對于城市可持續化評價的壹些難以定量的指標，可以用模糊語句代替，因此模糊邏輯在對城市的可持續發展進行評估方面有著較顯著的優勢。 模糊邏輯方法將應用于上述所提及的研究工作中，另外現有關于城市的可持續發展潛力以及哪些領域有改善潛力的研究尚欠缺，本研究將會通過整合模糊邏輯方法和動態建模來評估城市可持續發展績效，模擬城市的可持續發展進程，並確定那些有潛力改善的領域，以提升城市可持續發展方面的表現。

25223215.label: Realisation of objectives
25223215.value: Objective 1: To make a comprehensive review of the urban sustainability indicators used by different cities and best practices in promoting sustainable urbanization by different cities for storage in a database; Objective 1 has been achieved. Based on a comprehensive literature review, eight frequently employed sustainability assessment methods were identified, including ecological footprint method, data envelopment analysis method, life cycle assessment method, input-output method, substance flow analysis method, comprehensive evaluation method, and fuzzy method. Various indicator systems were also reviewed. For example, Phillis et al. (2011) developed a SAFE model for sustainability assessment, which contains 75 indicators to evaluate the sustainability performance of 128 selected countries. The Urban China Initiative (UCI) adopted a four-level hierarchical structure for urban sustainability assessment with 23 basic indicators The data for the best practices of sustainable urbanization in China were collected by visiting the official websites of various sources issued by many official organizations, such as UN-Habitat and the World Bank. Around 150 best practices have been collected and stored in a structured database. Objective 2: To develop fuzzy logic and system dynamics models for evaluating and simulating urban sustainable development with the three dimensions: current status, sustainable development potential and response strategy; Objective 2 has been achieved. An adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) to assess sustainability of countries was developed (see Journal paper1). The membership functions and fuzzy rules are generated from 128 training samples. An adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems (ANFIS) approach for urban sustainability assessment was developed (see Journal paper2). With collected training samples from the Urban China Initiative, and the ANFIS approach was used to rank 185 selected cities in China. A system dynamics model for simulating urban sustainability performance was developed (see Journal paper3). The system dynamics model comprises four sub-systems, namely, the economic sector, social sector, environment sector and resource sector. The system dynamics model is used to simulate the sustainability performance of the city, Beijing, with three scenarios. Objective 3: To generate fuzzy membership functions and fuzzy rules using ANFIS and training data derived from those city practices which actively promote sustainable urbanization objectives; Objective 3 has been achieved. The Urban China Initiative (UCI) data were used for training the parameters of the established ANFIS models. The ANFIS in the MATLAB software package uses the hybrid training algorithm, which incorporates a gradient method and the least squares estimate. The bell-shaped membership function was used. However, the membership functions could be linear or nonlinear. Also, sustainability assessment involves complexity, dynamics and nonlinearity. Three other types of MFs: triangle, trapezoid and Gaussian were also tested. The urban sustainability of 185 cities, from 2010 to 2011, was reassessed by using these three other types of membership functions. The results show that the nonlinear MFs fit the UCI ranking much better than the linear MFs, which also indicates the nonlinear nature of the sustainability assessment process. Furthermore, the ANFIS models with Gaussian membership functions fit the UCI ranking best. With the collected data, the fuzzy if-then rules can also be trained. For ANFIS 1, there are five inputs, and each input is represented by using three linguistic terms. With the input and output data collected from the UCI, the 243 if-then rules were trained. Objective 4: To select or develop computer-aided tools to facilitate the assessment process; Objective 4 has been achieved. The fuzzy logic toolbox of MATLAB software package was selected to develop ANFIS models and train the membership functions and fuzzy rules. Objective 5: To apply the model to a number of selected cities in China such as Hong Kong, Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, Guangzhou in order to help those cites have a better understanding of their current status, sustainable development potential and response strategy. Objective 5 has been achieved. With collected training samples from the Urban China Initiative, and the ANFIS approach was used to rank 185 selected cities in China. In this study, a System Dynamics model that comprises an integrated economic-social-environmental–resource subsystem is established to assist simulating the performance of sustainable urbanization. The System Dynamics model can improve the accuracy of the assessment results by considering the complex and inter-dependent relationships between the variables in the process of urbanization, and through the results analyses under different simulation scenarios, different policies and strategies can be implemented to guide the development of urbanization. For example, based on the scenario analysis of Beijing’s sustainability performance, it can be summarized that that the urbanization speed has an impact on Beijing’s sustainable development. The low speed development pattern will contribute to a higher urban sustainability performance than other two scenarios. The total performance will keep declining even at the current urbanization speed. Therefore, the imperative task of Beijing is to improve the quality of urbanization rather than the speed of urbanization.

25223215.label: Major findings and research outcome
25223215.value: Findings: (1) An adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference systems (ANFIS) approach for urban sustainability assessment was developed. With collected training samples from the Urban China Initiative, and the ANFIS approach was used to rank 185 selected cities in China. The results show that the ANFIS approach is appropriate for assessing urban sustainability. (2) For ANFIS approach, the nonlinear membership functions fit the training samples better than the linear membership functions. The ANFIS models with Gaussian membership functions perform the best because Gaussian membership function is natural and can be used to approximate any real continuous function with high accuracy. (3) Predefined fuzzy rules and simple linear membership functions have generally been used in most existing studies. The assessment results may not reflect the real sustainability performance because the predefined rules and membership functions are mostly based on expert knowledge. An appropriate integration of fuzzy-set theory with other methods may provide a solution. ANFIS is a good example. Research outcomes: Publications: three journal papers and two conference papers. Please refer to Part C.

25223215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25223215.value: The ANFIS approach for sustainability assessment can be further improved by using training data from other sources, such as UN-Habitat and World Bank. Moreover, sustainability assessment is a dynamic process, which requires the assessment method also to be dynamic. Compared with traditional methods, the ANFIS method can meet the dynamic requirements to update the fuzzy rules and membership functions through new training. In future studies, the new source of training data and new training process can be explored to make sustainability assessment more accurate and meet the dynamic changes of the environment. Furthermore, the ANFIS method can also be used for sustainability assessment in different levels, including industrial level or project level in future studies.

25223215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25223215.value: Sustainability is a complex and dynamic issue. Many assessment methods have been developed. However, the main challenges are vagueness, subjectivity and the dynamics involved in the assessment. To overcome these problems, an ANFIS was introduced in this study for urban sustainability assessment. The fuzzy rules and membership functions can be obtained from training data rather than from expert knowledge. The robust validation process reveals that the ANFIS method is appropriate for evaluation of urban sustainability. The training data is important for the successful application of ANFIS method. In order to model behavior that better reflects the real world, there is a need for an appropriate selection of training data. The accuracy of the ANFIS method can be further improved in further study by collecting training data from different sources, such as UN-Habitat, or World Bank. Furthermore, the whole domain of sustainability assessment is currently part of a dynamic process. Consequently, it is expected that the indicators, benchmarks, or rules may change with the changing environment. The ANFIS method has the potential to perform better than other methods due to its adaptive learning ability, but this needs to be demonstrated through new training, with new collected data.

25300815.value: Revisit important convex optimization problems arising from recent applications like compressed sensing from the gauge duality perspective. Develop efficient algorithms for solving their structurally simpler gauge dual problems. 25300815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25300815.value: In this proposal, the PI and his coworkers will consider new solution methods for a class of structured optimization problems. These problems arise as different models in important applications like compressed sensing, matrix completion and the system identification or realization problems from the control literature, and are either convex or nonconvex optimization problems that approximate the original problems. These problems are usually presented in large scale, involving millions of variables. Our work will be conducted along two lines. On the one hand, we will revisit the existing representative convex models in these application fields from the gauge duality perspective, which leads to structurally much simpler dual problems. Taking advantage of the simplicity of these dual formulations, we will develop new algorithms for solving them. In particular, this dual perspective enables us to develop algorithms that work on a lower dimension and can incorporate more structure of the problem to speed up the solution process. On the other hand, motivated by the empirical effectiveness of various existing nonconvex models in the aforementioned applications, we will develop general iterative schemes that can solve a large class of existing and new nonconvex models. Development of such methods will encourage the proposal and study of new nonconvex models for the above applications. 本項目將研究一類帶結構的優化問題。此類問題包括一系列凸或非凸的優化問題，並常用作建構壓縮感應、矩陣填充及系統識別等應用領域的數學模型。問題規模大，可牽涉上百萬個變量。本研究將就兩方面進行。首先，我們將運用gauge對偶理論重新分析上述的凸優化問題，從而推導出更簡單的對偶問題，並探討新的求解算法。一般而言，對偶問題涉及更少變量，且其結構更利於發展高效算法。另一方面，鑑於上述的非凸模型在應用中非常有效，本項目亦將針對現存以及嶄新的非凸模型探討求解算法。成果有望促進非凸模型的研究與發展。

25300815.label: Realisation of objectives
25300815.value: One of the aims of this project is to develop globally convergent algorithms for nonconvex structural composite optimization problems by suitably adapting algorithms originally proposed for convex settings, and analyze their convergence. In this regard, we studied in “Further properties of the forward-backward envelope with applications to difference-of-convex programming” a variant of the forward-backward splitting method in a possibly nonconvex setting and investigated how second-order information can be incorporated so as to accelerate the convergence. This paper was completed jointly with Dr Tianxiang Liu, a postdoctoral fellow hired under this project at the time. This work was presented by Dr Tianxiang Liu at the SIAM Conference on Optimization in Vancouver in 2017, with her trip supported by the project funding. To further address the goal concerning nonconvex splitting methods, we also studied in “A proximal difference-of-convex algorithm with extrapolation” a variant of the forward-backward splitting method with Nesterov-type extrapolation and analyzed its convergence. We also established local convergence rates of the method under Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz (KL) assumptions. The KL property was further studied in the subsequent paper “Calculus of the exponent of Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz inequality and its applications to linear convergence of first-order methods”, where we described a general strategy for estimating the KL exponent of an optimization model. This work was initiated and finished via a sequence of skype meetings with Dr Guoyin Li from University of New South Wales in Australia. The KL exponent is an important quantity for analyzing local convergence rate of first-order methods in nonconvex setting, including forward-backward splitting, Douglas-Rachford splitting, Peaceman-Rachford splitting, etc. The findings in “Calculus of the exponent of Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz inequality and its applications to linear convergence of first-order methods” have been presented at an international conference (International Conference on Continuous Optimization 2016 in Tokyo) and several local workshops. In short, we have adapted algorithms to nonconvex setting and analyzed their convergence. The other aim of this project is to revisit important convex optimization problems from a gauge duality perspective, and use this as the basis for developing efficient algorithms. Some key ideas included taking advantage of the simplicity of the constraint and incorporating second-order information for solving large-scale instances. To achieve this, Professor Michael Friedlander was invited to visit Hong Kong in the Summer of 2016. The PI then visited Professor Michael Friedlander at University of British Columbia for around two weeks in each of the Summers of 2017 and 2018. During these visits, we initiated and finally finished the paper “Polar convolution”, which presents a new strategy for deriving smooth dual problems that is consistent with gauge duality. Specifically, one can solve the smooth gauge dual problems with simple constraint efficiently and then attempt to recover a solution of the original primal problem. A new variant of proximal point algorithm, called the projected polar proximal point algorithm, was proposed and its convergence was analyzed. This algorithm was constructed based on the newly defined “polar envelope” and “polar proximal map” in the paper. The findings in this paper have been presented in some local and oversea workshops. Besides, gauge was also studied in “Further properties of the forward-backward envelope with applications to difference-of-convex programming” in which we looked at the problem of minimizing the difference of norms as regularizers for inducing sparsity in the second part of the paper. Based on a reformulation of the problem into the sum of a smooth nonconvex function and a nonsmooth convex function, we discussed how second-order information can be suitably incorporated for acceleration. In short, we have looked further into gauge duality and developed a framework for deriving smooth gauge dual problems that are structurally simpler to solve. Incorporation of second-order information was also performed on a special class of gauge-related nonconvex problems for possible acceleration.

25300815.label: Major findings and research outcome
25300815.value: Four journal papers are published as research outcome of this project. The first paper is “Further properties of the forward-backward envelope with applications to difference-of-convex programming”, which was also reported in the midterm progress report. In this paper, we further studied the forward-backward splitting method and also investigated how second-order information can be incorporated for acceleration. This work is joint with Dr Tianxiang Liu, a postdoctoral fellow supported by this project. Splitting methods in nonconvex setting were further studied in two subsequent papers. The first paper, “A proximal difference-of-convex algorithm with extrapolation”, investigated yet another variant of the forward-backward splitting method in the nonconvex setting: more specifically, the difference-of-convex setting. The class of difference-of-convex functions is a large class of nonconvex functions and arises naturally as loss functions and regularizers in contemporary statistical and engineering problems. Another paper, “Calculus of the exponent of Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz inequality and its applications to linear convergence of first-order methods”, outlined and studied a general framework for conducting convergence analysis for a large variety of first-order methods including forward-backward splitting, Douglas-Rachford splitting and proximal gradient algorithm with inertia term (the so-called iPiano). Finally, a recent paper “Polar convolution” described and analyzed a general smoothing framework based on gauge duality. The smooth dual problem is a structurally simpler gauge optimization problem and one can take advantage of the simplicity of the constraints to solve this smoothed dual. Further discussion to extend the constructions studied in this paper to cover all convex optimization problems was also presented. Results in “Further properties of the forward-backward envelope with applications to difference-of-convex programming” were presented by Dr Tianxiang Liu at SIAM conference on Optimization in 2017 and some results in “Calculus of the exponent of Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz inequality and its applications to linear convergence of first-order methods” were presented by the PI at the 5th International Conference on Continuous Optimization in 2016.

25300815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25300815.value: There are several venues for potential further development. First of all, the gauge duality results developed may be further extended to develop algorithms for general convex optimization problems. Moreover, the techniques developed in analyzing convergence of the splitting method may be adapted to analyze other first-order methods.

25300815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25300815.value: The PI and his coworkers developed and analyzed new solution methods for a large class of large-scale structured optimization problems that arise in important applications such as compressed sensing, matrix completion, system identification or realization problems from the control literature. On the one hand, we further developed the gauge duality theory. Based on this dual perspective, one can develop algorithms that can take advantage of simple constraints in the dual problem and make better use of second-order information available for acceleration. On the other hand, we developed some splitting-based iterative algorithms that can solve a large class of nonconvex models and studied their convergence rate for a large variety of objectives. This development can lead to the proposal and study of new nonconvex models in all the aforementioned application fields.

25301115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25301115.value: Learning theory considers problems of extracting pattern, model, and knowledge from data. For high dimensional data, the presence of inactive variables not only blurs the true model, but also spoils the accuracy of the inferred predictors. The proposed project focuses on the mathematical analysis of two promising kernel-based non-linear variable selection algorithms for removing irrelevant dimensions and identifying variable interactions. The first algorithm assigns one reproducing kernel to each variable and uses the Hadamard power of the weighted sum of the kernels to train the predictor. Sparsity enhancing regularization is employed to eliminate the weights of inactive dimensions. A surprising pilot simulation shows that with linear complexity, the algorithm is able to capture two- or even more-way interactions. The second algorithm uses the l^1 penalty on both the gradient and the Hessian. A data dependent hypothesis space is used to simplify computations. We will investigate the complexity of the reproducing kernel space based on coordinate kernel polynomials, and develop bound on covering numbers. Techniques from approximation theory will be applied. We will develop the theory of model selection consistency and the rate of convergence of the algorithms, of which two the relation will also be studied. We will develop mathematical foundation for the interaction selection consistency observed in simulation. For different coefficient vectors for the kernel polynomials, the relation between the corresponding reproducing kernel spaces will be investigated. 學習理論研究從數據當中提取模式、模型和知識的問題。對於維度很高的數據，不活躍的變元不僅模糊了模型的本來面目，而且會降低經由數據訓練得到的模型的預測精度。本課題專注於在數學上分析兩個有應用前景的基於核方法的非線性變元選擇算法。這兩個算法設計用於除去無關維度，並且探測變元之間的關聯效應。其中，第一個算法在每一個變元上設定一個再生核，並利用這些核的加權和的Hadamard方冪來訓練預測模型。我們使用有稀疏性偏好的正則化方法來降低或者除去無關維度對應的權重。一個令人振奮的小規模數據實驗證實了僅僅使用一階的參數空間複雜度，我們的算法可以探測二階，甚至更高階的變元關聯效應。第二個算法使用l^1罰函數於模型的梯度和Hessian矩陣。我們使用與數據有關的假設空間來簡化計算。我們計劃研究基於座標核多項式的再生核函數空間的複雜度，並得到覆蓋數的估計。逼近理論的一些技巧會被應用到分析過程中來。模型選擇的一致性，以及算法的收斂性會被研究。同時，我們將研究這種一致性和收斂性的內在聯繫。我們會建立在數據模擬實驗中發現的變元關聯效應探測能力的數學基礎。不同的核權重導出的不同的再生核空間的關係也是研究的一個方向。

25301115.label: Realisation of objectives
25301115.value: The proposed project objectives have all been successively achieved. In [2], we developed and analyzed a family of empirical feature-based learning algorithms called the Thresholded Spectral Algorithms (TSA's). As a general framework, TSA unifies two broad families of learning algorithms: the spectral algorithms, and the kernel projection machines, between which the intrinsic relation is revealed. Reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces are adopted as feature spaces to approximate the target functions in nonlinear regression learning problems. The complexity of a reproducing kernel space is characterized by the decay rate of eigenvalues of the kernel-based integral operator. The complexity of the empirical feature space is controlled by the soft thresholding function that drives sparsity. By using empirical features, the variable and interaction selection is achieved by the selection of empirical features. The relevance of the empirical features to the probability distribution and the geometry of the input space is represented by the corresponding eigenvalues. The relevance of the empirical features to the output space and the conditional probability distributions is evaluated by the soft thresholding function. The feature selection consistency is formulated as the ability to recover the features (the eigenfunctions of the kernel-based integral operator) that represent the true regression function. Our analysis in [2] implies that when the true regression function is represented by a finite set of features corresponding to which the eigenvalues of the integral operator are isolated (otherwise it is well known that feature selection consistency is impossible), then with a sufficient sample size TSA is able to identify (with overwhelming probability) the correct set of empirical features, which, as the sample size tends to infinity, converge to the features that represent the regression function respectively. Our research [2] reveals that even without assuming any sparsity of the target regression function, the TSA output function is still representable sparsely by empirical features with overwhelming probability, and the output function converges in L2 metric to the real regression function in a near-optimal speed with overwhelming probability. Explicit convergence rate is obtained for two kinds of kernels with the eigenvalues of the integral operator decay polynomially and exponentially respectively. The theory is developed for general reproducing kernels with the coordinate kernel polynomials as important examples. In [4], we developed the theory of Coordinate Kernel Polynomials. For the learning problems with high dimensional input space, we assign one reproducing kernel to each dimension (alternatively, one can divide the dimensions into different families and assign one reproducing kernel to each family, for the problems with known pattern of grouped sparsity), add these kernels, and raise the sum to a power d, where d is a positive integer. The complexity of the reproducing kernel spaces is controlled by the l1-penalty on the coordinate kernel coefficients. We formulated the algorithm and demonstrated empirically that for a synthetic model raised in the literature, our algorithm outperforms the algorithm SR-SIR, the classical LASSO, and another famous algorithm COSSO in both variable and interaction selection consistency, and prediction accuracy. On three real data sets (Ionosphere, Sonar MR, and Wisc. BC, from the UCI Machine Learning Repository), our algorithm achieves the state-of-the-art performance in literature. Theoretically, we proved the consistency of the predicted functions, in the form that with overwhelming probability, the generalization error of our algorithm decays in the speed O(sqrt(m)) as the sample size m tends to infinity. In [5], we study a reproducing kernel-based distributed MEE algorithm, DMEE, which is designed to work with both fully supervised data and semi-supervised data. Minimum Error Entropy (MEE) principle is an important approach in Information Theoretical Learning (ITL). It is widely applied and studied in various fields for its robustness to noise. The divide-and-conquer design is employed. DMEE significantly reduces the computational complexity and memory requirement on single computing nodes. With fully supervised data, our proved learning rates equal the minimax optimal learning rates of the classical point-wise kernel-based regressions. Under the semi-supervised learning scenarios, we show that DMEE exploits unlabeled data effectively. First, under the settings with weak regularity assumptions, additional unlabeled data significantly improves the learning rates of DMEE. Second, with sufficient unlabeled data, labeled data can be distributed to many more computing nodes, without spoiling the learning rates in terms of the number of labels. In [6] we show that the kernel ridge regression (KRR) with offset is well connected to the regularization schemes with centered reproducing kernels. By the aid of this connection and the theory of centered reproducing kernels, in [6] we established the generalization error bounds for KRR with centered reproducing kernels and the offset. We proved that the algorithm can achieve minimax optimal rates. Kernel-based learning algorithms have been extensively studied in the past two decades paralleling their successful application in scientific and industrial research. In classical kernel methods such as kernel ridge regression and support vector machines, an unregularized offset term appears naturally. Although its importance can be defended in some situations, it is commonly agreed that the offset term brings essential difficulties to the optimization and theoretical analysis of the algorithms. In [6] we overcame the difficulty by designing and employing centered reproducing kernels. The idea of coefficient regularization was applied in [1] to study the inference of the dynamics of gene regulatory networks. The complexity of the hypothesis space is controlled by removing the two-way and more-way regulations, and also by downgrading the edges of which the output expression levels are sensitive to small parameter changes. The proposed algorithm, local edge machine (LEM) has achieved the state-of-the-art inference performance of the gene regulatory networks. In [3], we studied a parameter inference problem for Poisson and zero-inflated Poisson distributions. While most of the regression learning algorithms consider continuous output space, we considered in [3] the discrete output space motivated by a lot of applications with their nature of output as count data. The observations of Poisson random variables are divided into finite groups, of which the number represents the complexity of the hypothesis space. In [3] we designed an algorithm which uses prior information about the unknown parameter to search for the optimal grouping scheme with a restricted group number. The Fisher information is employed to quantitatively describe the efficiency loss for the best grouping scheme, which simplifies the selection of group numbers. In [7], a numerical algorithm is introduced and implemented for computing the Fisher information of the negative binomial distributions, with high precision and acceptable computational complexity. This algorithm provides reference to the information loss for the parameter inference with grouped and right-censored data from negative binomial models.

25301115.label: Major findings and research outcome
25301115.value: In [2], a family of empirical feature-based learning algorithms called the Thresholded Spectral Algorithms (TSA's) are designed and analyzed mathematically. As a general framework, TSA unifies two broad families of learning algorithms: the spectral algorithms, and the kernel projection machines. Explicit convergence rate is obtained for two kinds of kernels with the eigenvalues of the integral operator decay polynomially and exponentially respectively. In [4], we developed the theory of Coordinate Kernel Polynomials. On three real data sets (Ionosphere, Sonar MR, and Wisc. BC, from the UCI Machine Learning Repository), our algorithm achieves the state-of-the-art performance in literature. Theoretically, we proved the consistency of the predicted functions, in the form that with overwhelming probability, the generalization error of our algorithm decays in the speed O(sqrt(m)) as the sample size m tends to infinity. In [5], we study a reproducing kernel-based distributed MEE algorithm, DMEE, which is designed to work with both fully supervised data and semi-supervised data. With fully supervised data, our proved learning rates equal the minimax optimal learning rates of the classical point-wise kernel-based regressions. Under the semi-supervised learning scenarios, we show that unlabeled data may improve the performance of DMEE. In [6] we show that the kernel ridge regression (KRR) with offset is well connected to the regularization schemes with centered reproducing kernels. We proved that the algorithm achieves minimax optimal rates. In [1] we designed a distributed coefficient regularization scheme for the inference of the dynamics of gene regulatory networks. The designed algorithm (local edge machine, LEM) has achieved the state-of-the-art inference performance of the gene regulatory networks. In [3], we studied a parameter inference problem for Poisson and zero-inflated Poisson distributions. We designed an algorithm which uses prior information about the unknown parameter to search for the optimal grouping scheme with a restricted group number. In [7], a numerical algorithm is introduced and implemented for computing the Fisher information of the negative binomial distributions, with high precision and acceptable computational complexity.

25301115.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25301115.value: The insights of coordinate kernel polynomials could be used in the design of artificial neural networks for the purpose of variable and interaction selection. The idea and the analysis developed for centered reproducing kernels could be applied for score-based ranking and distributed pairwise learning. We shall use the ideas in our future research of deep learning, and pairwise learning.

25301115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25301115.value: Machine learning is a fast-developing research area in the last twenty years, providing vital support to industry and other science branches. In this project, we developed and analyzed a set of closely related new machine learning algorithms. The performance of these algorithms in terms of the precision of variable selection and prediction is studied using mathematical analysis and empirical testing. The ideas and methodologies developed have been applied to many areas in machine learning, such as feature selection, interactive component learning, sparse representation, minimum error entropy algorithms, distributed learning, etc., and are applied to the inference of gene regulatory network in systems biology, and survey study in computational social science.

25303815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25303815.value: 能源問題是本世紀人類面臨最大的挑戰之一。自工業革命以後,人類依靠化石燃料作為主要的能量來源。社會的經濟增長和發展與化石燃料需求息息相關。在全球超過70 億人口壓力下, 人類對化石燃料的需求持續增長. 然而化石燃料是非可再生能源,人類必須致力發展可替代化石燃料的可再生能源以滿足不斷增加的需求。此外,燃燒化石燃料時所產生的環境污染亦是發展替代化石燃料的主要驅動力。事實上,燃燒化石燃料以獲得能量,已造成大氣中二氧化碳水平達到了驚人的高水平，即400ppm。高濃度二氧化碳不僅會導致全球溫度增加，而且還間接導致極端氣候，影響農業生產, 引致糧食供應不穩定。因此，國際已有共識，各國需要即立採取行動，減少碳放排，以應對大氣中高二氧化碳水平的問題。 儘管小分子過渡金屬催化二氧化碳還原的研究已經進行30多年，大部分的工作一直專注於電化學還原二氧化碳。相反，以過渡金屬配合物催化光化學還原二氧化碳的研究相對比較少。 並且主要的工作是基於使用第二和第三排過渡金屬離子。這些過渡金屬離子在地殼的藴含量比較少, 而且價格非常昂貴。 因此如要以分子催化劑作大規模太陽能轉至化學燃料,我們必須採用地球上藴含量比較豐富的金屬含離子作小分子激活。 受到大自然的一氧化碳脱氢酶的啟發，我們計劃開發地球上藴含量較豐富的金屬催化劑以可見光驅動二氧化碳的還原。我們將通過配體的設計以優化催化劑的效率和選擇性。此外我們 亦會利用各種光譜技術和計算研究反應機理。 除了分子催化劑的研究，我們將開發蛋白偶聯過渡金屬催化劑以可見光驅動在水介質進行二氧化碳排的還原。 我們的研究將對於開發高效催化劑把太陽能轉換到燃料提供了一個新的方向。

25503315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25503315.value: To response trends and consumer needs promptly, the manufacturing speed of fashion goods continues to move at a faster and faster pace. Combined with the lower cost of materials and labor, the rapidly produced goods encourage people to buy multiple clothing items at once and then discard them shortly thereafter. This practice is often criticized as running counter to the sustainability trend in the fashion industry since fast production is likely to neglect workers’ welfare, and fast consumption results in increasing fashion waste. Some practitioners in the industry have claimed to slow down the fashion cycle from the fast production and consumption loop to resolve sustainability issues. This is refereed as to slow fashion. This project posits that fast fashion and slow fashion are not in a dichotomous relationship, given that each fashion system has distinctive strengths and strategies; thus, it is believed that the two fashion systems may enrich the fashion industry by fulfilling different roles. Particularly, since slow fashion practices involve quality production at a low speed, small fashion businesses and young designers may benefit from slow fashion, rather than large firms which mainly rely on the economy of scale strategy. This proposed project is aimed at seeking effective ways of creating profitability for small businesses based on slow fashion. This study posits that slow fashion promotes local branding which capitalizes on local resources and heritage, thereby providing unique products and achieving distinctive market positioning. To this end, this study will find which slow fashion attributes contribute the most to increasing consumers’ purchase intention, willingness to pay a price premium and acceptable amount of price premium to buy slow fashion products. Indeed, considering that small scale businesses are likely to lack resources, focusing on the most salient factors will be critical for them. The respondents will be recruited from the U.K., Hong Kong and South Korea. Finding and discussing the similarities and differences of the attributes from different countries will shed light on the enhanced applicability of the slow fashion business model. Economic profitability of slow fashion through successful branding will consequently resolve the sustainability issues raised in the fashion industry. In addition, local branding is not just limited to the community, but can be expanded to national branding; thus, the local branding strategy helps the development of the local community as well as the domestic economy. -

25506015.value: 在企业战略管理领域中，如何降低市场竞争率和解释竞争企业绩效的区别向来是一个核心研究课题(e.g., Chen & Miller, 2012; Hitt, Ireland, & Hoskisson, 2012; Porter, 1980; Smith, Ferrier, & Ndofor, 2001)。尽管越来越多的战略学者开始从语言选择和沟通方式的角度来研究各种企业现象，但至今为止关于企业语言选择和沟通方式对企业竞争的研究还没有出现。于是，对于企业语言选择和沟通方式对竞争企业的互动是否有影响和如何影响，我们了解甚少。此篇提案就将从心理学和沟通学的角度来提出两篇关于企业语言选择和沟通方式对企业竞争的研究。 第一篇研究是关于市场上现任企业模糊语言的使用对于试图进入一个新市场的竞争企业是否进入该市场的决定的影响。对于一个市场中的现任企业来说，新的竞争对手的进入往往意味着下行的市场占有率和企业利润度。根据战略沟通学的研究，我们推测现任企业在跟市场的沟通中使用更多的模糊语言可能可以阻碍新竞争对手的进入决定。而现任企业模糊语言的使用程度也将与这些企业在市场中面临的新竞争对手的威胁程度有关。 第二篇研究是关于企业选择如何描述他们的竞争性举动和竞争对手将如何回应和挑战这些举动的关系。尽管大量现有的企业竞争动态学研究都证明竞争对手对企业竞争举动的反应越慢对企业来说越有好处，之前的研究似乎都忽略了相同竞争举动被不同的语言描述后是否会对竞争对手产生不同的影响。在这篇文章中，我们试图研究两种不同的关于竞争举动的描述：侵略性描述和共有性描述。我们推测使用侵略性描述的竞争举动将吸引更多竞争对手更快的反击。相反的，使用共有性描述的竞争举动可能会较慢的吸引较少的竞争对手反击。 我们计划使用计算机文本内容分析的方法来量化企业各种各样的语言使用和沟通方法，例如企业年报，新闻稿，演讲稿，和电话会议记录等。我们将总共收集8个不同行业跨越15年从1995年到2010年的数据。这其中包括竞争强度较大的行业，像航空公司行业，汽车行业，制药行业，杂志行业，和一些竞争强度较小的行业，例如食品行业，家庭耐用消费品行业，金属与采矿行业等。如果我们的研究能够表明企业语言选择和沟通方式对于竞争对手之间的互动和结果有深远的影响，那么这篇研究将为企业未来如何更有效地更战略性地使用语言和沟通方式来达到企业竞争和战略目的提供重要的依据。

25506015.label: Realisation of objectives
25506015.value: Overall, the objective of this grant proposal (objective #1) has been achieved as planned. With the support of the grant, I conducted two studies to explore the role of language and communication in competition and successfully published both articles at a leading management journal. For objective #2, I published an article at the Academy of Management Journal to explore the effect of vague language on rivals' new market entry decisions. Thus, objective #2 has been accomplished as planned. For objective #3, based on reviewers' comments, I revised the study to focus on how firms' framing of competitive decisions influence whether and how rivals respond. Although the dependent variable changed from the speed of rivals' response to the intensity of rivals' response, the primary objective of understanding the role of language signals to help firms assess the vulnerability of their rivals has been accomplished as planned. In conclusion, all three objectives outlined in the grant proposal have been achieved. While all research objectives have been achieved, I have unspent funding for two main reasons. First, the university provided me with a $10,000 internal grant after this proposal received a 3.5 rating in 2014 after the first submission to get started with this research. Second, I initially planned to purchase the data needed for these two studies from Thomson Reuters. However, after some initial exploration with their sample data, I realized that Thomson provides limited coverage of the firm's historical data. Based on reviewers' suggestions, I developed Python code to extract data from public websites to build the dataset. Thus, compared to purchasing the data from Thomson Reuters, the amount of funding needed has substantially reduced.
