25506015.label: Major findings and research outcome
25506015.value: The quest to understand the conditions that deter interfirm rivalry and explain performance differences among competing firms is a fundamental issue in strategic management (e.g., Chen & Miller, 2012; Hitt, Ireland, & Hoskisson, 2012; Porter, 1980; Smith, Ferrier, & Ndofor, 2001). Although the importance of language in competition has long been recognized by industrial organization economists (Porter, 1980) and strategy scholars (Rindova, Becerra, & Contardo, 2004), no prior studies has systematically examined its impact on firm competitive interactions. In this regard, the two studies completed as part of this GRF grant represent two pioneering studies that explicitly examined corporate communication as a determinant of interfirm rivalry. Study one investigates the effect of vague language used by incumbent firms on potential entrants’ decision to enter a new market. I find that when the managers of incumbent firms perceive a high threat of new entry, they are more likely to use vagueness in their corporate communications to make their strategies and actions harder to discern. This lessened interpretation results in fewer competitive entries by potential entrants. Study two examines how the framing of competitive moves influence whether and how rivals respond and challenge such moves. I find that when rivals reported performance decline, the intensity of competitive actions initiated by the focal firm will increase to exploit rivals' vulnerability. Moreover, when rivals use more complex and vague language to justify their performance shortfall, these language attributes signal the vulnerability of those rivals to the focal firm and intensify the focal firm’s reaction to rivals’ performance shortfall. Using computerized content analysis to quantify language use in corporate communication from a variety of sources, including annual report, press releases, and earnings conference calls, this research presents strong evidence that language and communication matters greatly in interfirm rivalry. Traditionally, most studies of competitive dynamics have predominantly focused on observed actions as predictors of rivals’ competitive responses. By underscoring the role of communication and language use, this research sheds new light on how corporate communication can be used strategically to achieve competitive objectives, an issue at the heart of competitive dynamics and organizational research.

25506015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25506015.value: This project is one of the first attempts to systematically examine how the use of language in a firm’s communication affects its rivals’ competitive behavior. Researchers have long acknowledged that corporate communication matters in interfirm rivalry. Nevertheless, little has been done to date to unpack how specific use of language affects rivals’ behavior. In this project, I conducted two studies to examine how a firm’s communication affect its rivals. In study one, we focused on the use of vagueness in corporate annual reports and how such practice may influence their rivals’ market entry decisions. Although competitive signaling theory has strongly emphasized the value of a firm’s explicit and aggressive communication in thwarting invasions by rivals, we challenged this prevailing view by demonstrating the competitive benefits of a firm’s vague and equivocal communication and found robust support for our hypotheses. In study two, I examined how critical events that befall a rival may be indicative of its vulnerability and thus motivate a focal firm to act. Moreover, this study considers the importance of language as an indicator of rivals’ underlying conditions and a facilitator of the focal firm’s competitive decision-making.

25507315.label: Realisation of objectives
25507315.value: All the four objectives are achieved successfully. Regarding the first objective, we find that income smoothness is positively (negatively) related to the ratio of price to the estimated intrinsic value (P/V) among undervalued (overvalued) stocks. For an undervalued stock, a higher value of the price-to-value ratio means less undervaluation and thus greater fundamental valuation efficiency; for an overvalued stock, a smaller value of the price-to-value ratio means less overvaluation and thus greater fundamental valuation efficiency. Regarding the second objective, we find that the estimated relation with the implied cost of capital gradually increases from significantly negative to significantly positive as we move the estimation from bottom P/V quintile to the top P/V quintile, which we interpret as evidence consistent with the fundamental valuation efficiency-enhancing effect of income smoothness. Regarding the third objective, our evidence supporting the second objective demonstrates that the measurement error of the implied cost of equity capital as the proxy for investors’ expected returns are systematically related to income smoothness. Therefore, we may not be able to draw conclusive conclusion about the relation between income smoothness and investors’ expected returns from the estimated relation between income smoothness and the implied cost of equity capital unless we can adequately gauge the bias, which seems empirically impossible. Our evidence based on income smoothness and 10 other mispricing-associated variables convincingly illustrates the importance of recognizing the fundamental valuation efficiency of the stock price in research design and result interpretation, which is the fourth objective of our research project.

25507315.label: Major findings and research outcome
25507315.value: As the proxy for expected return, the implied cost of capital (ICC) is subject to a mispricing-driven measurement error because the price of a stock used to compute ICC can deviate from its intrinsic value. For undervalued (overvalued) stocks, the mispricing-driven measurement error is positive (negative) and increases (decreases) with the degree of undervaluation (overvaluation). Therefore, ceteris paribus, lower ICC is equivalent to higher (lower) fundamental valuation efficiency (FVE) for undervalued (overvalued) stocks. Furthermore, our evidence, based on income smoothness and ten other mispricing-associated constructs, shows that the estimated relation of an FVE-associated construct with ICC is a potentially biased estimate of its relation with expected return because its estimated relation with ICC also captures its relation with the mispricing-driven measurement error, the sign of which switches between undervalued and overvalued stocks. Existing methods (instrumental variables, portfolio grouping, and large samples) do not seem able to address the bias.

25507315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25507315.value: We find that the finding about the relation between income smoothness and the implied cost of capital could be applied to any mispricing-associated variable such as accrual quality, stock liquidity, firm size, firm age, and idiosyncratic return volatility. Now we are developing a unified conceptual framework to generalize our findings. And we have already worked out a working paper and presented the results in the 2018 Greater China Area Finance Conference.

25507315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25507315.value: As the proxy for expected return, the implied cost of capital (ICC) has a mispricing-driven measurement error because the price of a stock used to compute it can deviate from its intrinsic value. As a result, the estimated relation between an mispricing-associated variable and ICC captures not only the relation between the variable and expected return but also the relation between the variable and the mispricing-driven measurement error of ICC. That latter relation causes the estimated relation of the variable with ICC to be a potentially biased estimate of the variable’s relation with expected return. To make inferences about its relation with expected return from its estimated relation with ICC, we need to gauge the sign and magnitude of the bias (the relation between an mispricing-associated variable and the mispricing-driven measurement error of ICC), which seems an extremely difficult if not impossible task. Income smoothness is one exemplary mispricing-associated variable.

25600515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25600515.value: Metaphor is the description of one thing in terms of another. Some linguists and psychologists (Gibbs, 2008; Lakoff, 1993) claim that we describe X in terms of Y because we also think and reason about X in terms of Y. Metaphors might therefore be useful in psychotherapy, a mental health activity where thoughts and feelings are discussed and analyzed. There is considerable research in the psychotherapy literature on the forms, functions, and effects of metaphor use by therapists and patients. However, from a discourse analytic perspective, contextual characteristics and theoretical nuances which can enrich the description and application of metaphors in psychotherapy have been critically overlooked, especially in under-researched settings such as Hong Kong. This project examines metaphors in Hong Kong psychotherapy talk (HKPT) in three progressive phases of ‘description’, ‘comparison’, and ‘application’. It draws upon, integrates, and further develops a series of related studies on metaphor in psychotherapy (Tay, 2010, 2011a, 2011b, 2011c, 2012, 2013, 2014b, 2014c, 2014d). Phase 1 describes metaphors in HKPT with independent but complementary methodologies of rich contextual analysis (Tay, 2013) and log-linear analysis (Agresti, 2002), where qualitative study of metaphor characteristics is followed by quantitative study of interaction patterns among metaphor-defining contextual variables. Besides providing a comprehensive and contextually grounded description, the underexplored potential of log-linear analysis for metaphor research is also developed. Phase 2 compares Phase 1 findings with my previous work on US psychotherapy metaphors, which adopted a similar conceptual and methodological approach. Besides contributing to cross-cultural metaphor scholarship (Kövecses, 2005), the consolidation of findings from HKPT and US psychotherapy provides an important basis for Phase 3. Phase 3, the application phase, interrogates two specific metaphor-based therapy techniques: the 7-step interview protocol (Kopp & Craw, 1998) and 6-step model (Sims, 2003), which exemplify the tendency in the psychotherapy literature to overlook the contextual and theoretical nuances of metaphors. The findings of Phases 1 and 2, which were precisely concerned with explicating these contextual and theoretical nuances, are thus expected to point towards implications and recommendations for refining or enhancing these techniques. Throughout the three phases, periodic discussions will be held with a practicing psychotherapist to ensure the therapeutic relevance and applicability of the analyses. Overall findings will be shared with other psychotherapists to raise awareness of their potential applications. In sum, the project promises significant theoretical and methodological contributions to metaphor scholarship, and the translation of theory into practical application through cross-disciplinary dialogue. 隱喻是用另一件事件和經驗來理解并表達該事物和經驗。相關語言學家和心理學家(Gibbs, 2008; Lakoff, 1993) 認為，隱喻根植于人類的認知機制，人類用關聯的概念結構Y來表述和解釋X，源自於人類用概念映射的方式，以Y來理解和認知X。目前已有相當一部分研究，從使用方式，使用效果，專業心理咨詢師和受詢者之間的溝通等方面進行考察，表明隱喻可以被用於心裡健康保健、咨詢、和支援方面的活動，以及有效的隱喻使用所發揮的重要作用。但是，有關隱喻在香港及其他華人區域心理治療的應用語境特征和理論的細緻話語分析的研究，顯得匱乏。 本項目對於香港心理咨詢的隱喻應用分析，分為三個漸進式階段：“闡述”、“比較”和“應用”，借鑒、融合、並進一步拓展筆者對於心理治療的一系列隱喻相關研究 (Tay, 2010, 2011a, 2011b, 2011c, 2012, 2013, 2014b, 2014c, 2014d)。 第1階段“闡述”，對香港心理健康咨詢的隱喻應用研究進行梳理，指出相對獨立的語境分析方法(Tay, 2013)和對數線性分析方法（Agresti，2002）可以相互補充的可行性，對於隱喻特徵可進行定性研究，而對於心理咨詢談話語境下隱喻使用的互動模式採用定量研究方法。由此，此階段不僅提供全面而詳實的語境闡述分析外，還深入拓展了尚未被大規模使用的對數線性分析方法。 第2階段為“比較”。研究者之間曾經對隱喻在美國心理治療的使用進行相關研究，并使用與第一階段相類似的理論概念研究框架方法。第二階段的比較，將香港方面的隱喻使用研究與之前美國方面的研究進行比較，除了在跨文化隱喻使用領域方面的意義(Kövecses, 2005)之外， 第二階段的對比，為第三階段提供了堅實基礎。 第3階段為“應用”階段。本項目援用七階段面談方式(Kopp & Craw, 1998) 和六步模型法(Sims, 2003) 這兩種心理咨詢治療方法的主要模式，以力證不可忽視對隱喻的使用語境和理論的細化分析的研究趨勢。而這與第一第二階段的研究結果相呼應，并有利於說明隱喻對於兩個主要模式的強化支援效果。 在三個漸進式階段中，研究者定期進行與執業心理咨詢師的討論，以確保研究分析的臨床治療相關性和適用性。總體研究結果，將與其他專業心理諮詢師進行共享磋商，以提高強化隱喻的潛在應用意識。總括之，該項目以期在理論和分析研究方法方面，以及跨學科的對話，并將理論付諸實際應用方面具有重要貢獻。

25600515.value: Each objective will be separately discussed with relevant publications referenced. Objective 1: To describe the contextual characteristics of metaphors in Hong Kong psychotherapy talk, and/or other Chinese speaking contexts This objective has been fully achieved. In line with the primary discourse analytic/descriptive aim of the project, a series of publications in both English and Chinese has detailed the unique contextual characteristics of metaphors in the under-explored Chinese context. These have been published in both the discourse and mental health literature, covering aspects such as the close interaction between therapist and client metaphors, the deliberate character of metaphors used in psychotherapy, the embodied quality of metaphors and its implications for therapeutic work, and statistical associations between metaphor and discourse/contextual variables. The findings were also disseminated in other ways to strategic target audiences (e.g. as a plenary talk at the 5th International Conference on Cognitive Semantics in Chongqing, China). The body of work generated by the project has also been systematically citedt in recent mental health research and practice (e.g. Törneke, N. (2017). Metaphor in Practice. A Professional’s Guide to Using the Science of Language in Psychotherapy. Oakland, CA: New Harbinger.). Additionally, the special issue mentioned under Objective 2 will include the theme of applying metaphors to psychotherapy practice. The contributions will discuss how different metaphor-based therapy techniques can be enhanced through various forms of language-related analysis. Publications: Tay, D. (2016). Objective 4: To introduce the combination of rich contextual analysis and log-linear analysis as a method for metaphor research This objective has been fully achieved. Two methodological papers were published which demonstrated the applicability of a mixed-methods approach: log-linear modeling and contextual interpretation of significant associations, using metaphors in Chinese psychotherapy talk as examples. The second paper in particular furthered the methodological discussion by introducing time series analysis (with ARIMA models) as a more elaborate technique to model 'time' (i.e. session number) as a continuous rather than categorical variable. A third relevant book chapter is also in press. In addition, the methodological insights have also been disseminated through other channels including postgraduate student training sessions and academic talks. 25600515.label: Major findings and research outcome
25600515.value: The major findings are summarized as follows: i) Metaphors are pervasively used by interactants (i.e. therapists, clients, and online help-seekers) across different Chinese psychotherapy/counseling contexts including face-to-face counseling, academic counseling in universities, and the new phenomenon of online e-health websites and forums. ii) Cantonese and Mandarin Chinese metaphors demonstrate the contextual characteristics reported in previous work in other cultural contexts; e.g. they range from highly conventional to creative, draw from invariant/embodied as well as culture-specific source domains, cover a range of therapeutically relevant target topics, and are collaboratively constructed in ways oriented to therapeutic objectives. This applies to both face-to-face counseling and online e-health websites. iii) Metaphor use as described by key variables (e.g. topics, speakers, functions, phase) is not arbitrary, but fit multivariate categorical (e.g. loglinear) models. For example, practitioners are much more likely to use metaphors in expository ways when discussing therapeutic/theoretical ideas, while clients are much more likely to assume the expository role when discussing their personal situations. Metaphor use is also modelable from other perspectives (e.g. as a time series) across multiple sessions, where previous sessions exert some influence on current and future sessions. These regularities underlying the seeming arbitrariness of metaphors suggests some concrete usage strategies for practitioners; e.g. clients are more willing to assert agency/be more expository when using metaphors to describe themselves. iv) Metaphors in Chinese psychotherapy provide insights into specific interactional dynamics not found in other discourse contexts; e.g. in the manifestation of transference, where clients’ past experiences are projected as an overarching source domain to different aspects of their present, reflecting the operation of high-level conceptual metaphors like PRESENT IS PAST. This in turn suggests that metaphor can serve as an intervention tool when therapists try to work through transference; e.g. explicitly inviting clients to frame the past as a 'source domain' , and introduce 'cross-domain mappings' as a conceptual resource or activity.

25600515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25600515.value: The comprehensive description of metaphors in Chinese psychotherapy contexts will provide a foundation for further research related to therapy processes and outcomes. For example, specific hypotheses being suggested by the present findings include i) metaphor use has generally positive effects on different dimensions of client experience (e.g. affective engagement, conceptual understanding, sense of agency), and ii) the evolution of metaphors across sessions is not just a spontaneous and 'messy' reality of discourse, but patterned in implicit ways that require more nuanced statistical modeling. Both these hypotheses are currently being investigated in greater detail, supported by ongoing GRF projects obtained by the PI that are building on the presently reported one. The first relates to measurable/observable aspects of client feedback such as offline survey ratings and online skin conductance responses while the second involves detailed analysis of specific metaphor variables with ARIMA time series models.

25600515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25600515.value: We use metaphors when we describe something in terms of something else (e.g. 'life is a journey'). Research shows that metaphors also help us understand abstract things using concrete things, and they are therefore useful in psychological counseling where people have to express difficult emotions, behaviors and so on. This project investigated how metaphors are used in psychotherapy in Chinese-speaking contexts. It examines their linguistic characteristics, contents and patterns across time, how counselors and clients use them differently, and how Chinese language metaphors compare with English language metaphors in psychotherapy. The findings have both theoretical and practical value. Theoretically, they help language researchers understand the nature of metaphors in psychotherapy and how they should be further researched. Practically, they have been applied to help counselors develop better and more natural ways of using metaphors in their work to help clients.

25603315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25603315.value: The human head houses the brain, and several major sensors including vision, hearing, smell and taste. The head requires many specialized products such as respirator, goggle, helmet and headphone to enhance and safeguard all these critical components. No matter the purpose, the head and face related products demand a high level of fit and comfort. Product design and engineering relies on accurate modelling of 3D surface data in order to create proper fit for the user. Various complete 3D head surface models and head forms have been developed using the Frankfurt plane alignment. Since most head related products partially cover the head, it seems logical to build 3D surface model using relevant localized area. Besides, shape variation analysis depends on alignment method. However, the effects of selected product specific area and different alignment methods on 3D head modelling and localized variation have not been carefully studied. A 3D surface modelling method is needed in order to create more accurate models for the specific head related products. In addition, the contact pressure from products can cause soft tissue deformation further affecting the fit and comfort. The soft tissue deformations at discomfort and pain thresholds on the head and face can serve as important evaluation and error tolerance check. However, these thresholds under various pressure levels are still unknown. The relationships among 3D head shape, soft tissue deformations at discomfort and pain thresholds, and tissue thickness are essential. Based on previous studies, this study proposes to develop a 3D modelling method to create 3D head surface models with multiple deformation layers for specific product design. Although product specific area will be considered, proposed method will be able to develop a complete head model that may be desired during product design process. The models will be built based on comparisons of alignment methods, selection of area of interest, statistical analysis of 3D shape data, and soft tissue deformation information. Four selected areas related to different types of products will be modelled and studied in detail. The validation will be conducted by a fit test using respirator prototypes generated from different methods. The results of this research have direct impact on 3D anthropometric study, biomechanics, product design and the understanding of the human head and face. 人體頭部包含大腦以及多種主要感覺器官，包括視覺、聽覺、嗅覺和味覺等。很多頭面部專用產品都是為了加強感官體驗和保護這些重要感官而設計的，例如面罩、護目鏡、頭盔和耳機等。不同用途的頭面部產品都對產品舒適度有極高的要求。因此，產品和工程設計師們需要精準的三維頭面部模型以提高產品的舒適度。目前，三維完整頭部建模一般采用法蘭克福平面校準的方法。由於大部分頭面部產品其實僅為部分接觸，運用局部區域進行三維建模的方法顯然更為合理。並且，外形差異分析會受校準方法影響，然而局部區域的選擇和校準方法對三維頭部建模和局部差異的影響還未被系統和徹底地研究過。因此我們需要一種針對頭面部產品設計的更準確的三維表面建模方法。另外，與產品的直接接觸壓力會導致頭面部軟組織變形從而可能進一步影響產品舒適度。由於軟組織變形而導致的不適甚至疼痛感覺其實可以作為一個重要的評價依據和容錯校驗方法。然而不同的壓力水平下導致的頭面部不適和疼痛閾值還不得而知。因此，對三維的頭部形狀、軟組織變形而導致的不適及疼痛閾值、以及軟組織厚度之間關系的研究對於頭面部產品設計至關重要。基於之前的相關研究，本項目提出了通過三維建模的方法為特定產品設計創建具有多層變形的三維頭面部模型。雖然考慮的是局部區域，但是本項目提出的方法將會創建一個可以應用在整個設計過程中的完整頭部模型。該模型會建立於校準方法比較、特定區域的選擇、三維形狀數據分析和軟組織變形等相關信息。本項目會進一步系統研究不同產品類型的相關區域的影響。不同方法設計的面罩會被用來驗證模型的效果。該研究結果將會對三維人體測量學、生物力學、產品設計和頭面部知識產生直接的影響。

25603315.label: Realisation of objectives
25603315.value: Objective 1: To study the effect of selected product specific area on 3D head modelling error and localized variation. Objective one was successfully achieved. An experimental study was designed to achieve the research objectives of this project. The 3D scanning was performed using Artec Eva 3D scanner to get the required point cloud data necessary for 3D head modelling. Data was acquired from two-hundred eighteen Chinese adult participants (109 male and 109 female). To address the first objective, the acquired 3D point cloud data for all the participants was first post processed using Rapidform software to remove the unwanted data and fill the gaps in the scan. Then the 3D point cloud data was processed using MATLAB programming where the landmarks and surface fitting were used to create accurate 3D head model with the same number of vertices for all individuals. In order to study the effect of product specific area, the whole head model was divided into 32 areas. Depending upon different product coverage, these areas can be merged to create different product specific area. The localized variation using specific area was calculated and compared with the whole head model. Objective 2: To identify the effect of alignment methods on 3D head modelling and localized variation. Objective two was successfully achieved. For addressing this objective, three different alignment methods including Frankfurt plane alignment, landmarks alignment and Iterative Closest Point (ICP) alignment were conducted and compared. ICP alignment method demonstrated the smallest localized variation while Frankfurt plane alignment showed the largest localized variation. Objective 3: To develop a complete head surface model even when only localized product specific area is considered. This objective was successfully achieved. The Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was used to analyse the shape variance among the individuals and to develop a global head surface model. For developing localized head model, a modified PCA method was implemented by adding a weighting matrix in the equation on the global head surface model. For this, the head surface was initially divided into two regions: area of interest and area of no interest. In order to have a smooth transition between, the area no interest was divided into transient area and area of no influence. These areas were then merged together to create a smooth, localized and complete 3D head surface model. Objective 4: To study soft tissue deformation at discomfort and pain level at different locations on the head and face, and then develop a combined 3D head surface model with deformation. Objective four was successfully achieved. A custom designed ultrasound indentation system was used for measuring soft tissue parameters like thickness and pressure/tissue deformation at discomfort and pain thresholds. Pressure values at the discomfort and pain thresholds were recorded using the load cell housed in the ultrasound indenter. Pressure sensitivity maps were generated using this data for both the gender. Tissue deformation data was calculated from the ultrasound data using the principal of time of flight. Based on the results of cluster analysis for pressure threshold data at seventy-six locations, the number of locations for measurement of tissue deformation was reduced to eighteen. Since the pressure threshold data is subjective in nature a study was conducted to test the reliability of data. For this, sixty participants whose pressure threshold were measured were invited to repeat the experiment. Intraclass correlation analysis was used to evaluate the reliability of the data. A combined layered model was generated for both the gender using tissue thickness and the amount of tissue deformation at discomfort and pain threshold on the global head surface model. Several challenges were faced while addressing this objective. Namely, custom requirement of computer and hardware drivers for the custom designed ultrasound indentation system and the huge amount of data from the ultrasound sensor of the indentation device. These challenges took some time to solve. Objective 5. To find the relationships among 1D dimensions, 3D head shape, soft tissue deformations at discomfort and pain thresholds, and soft tissue thickness. Objective five was successfully achieved. For addressing this objective, statistical analysis was performed on the acquired data in SPSS software. Descriptive statistics was performed to evaluate the range of data. Correlation analysis was used to identify relationship between different parameters, independent sample t-test was used to detect the gender specific differences and cluster analysis was used to identify the regions with similar pressure sensitivity ranges. Objective 6. To validate the proposed model using one product with different design features. This objective was achieved. The protocol of eight respirator masks were developed for male and female separately. The masks were designed from two models (global model based on Frankfurt plane alignment and ICP based alignment) * two frame hardness (hard ABS plastic-based frame and soft ABS frame layered with foam) * two designs (complete and frame only). User’s evaluation regarding this mask was acquired using a short questionnaire, whereas the thermal data was acquired using thermal camera and pressure data was acquired using thin film sensors. One challenge was faced while addressing this objective. We found that the sensitivity of pressure sensor was important for the experiment result, therefore, we had to test several different type of sensors to decide the most suitable one. This challenge took some time to find the solution.

25603315.label: Major findings and research outcome
25603315.value: The 3D generalized human head model with localized variation for male and female Chinese adults were developed. A total of 32 independent areas which can be merged for different type of head and face related product was developed. Different alignment methods including Frankfurt plane, landmarks plane and Iterative Closest Point (ICP) algorithm were compared and ICP method showed the better results for consideration of product specific areas. Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was used to calculate the shape variance among all individuals and create the 3D generalized head model. Weighted PCA was further developed to create the complete 3D head model with localized area variation. Pressure threshold for discomfort and pain were measured at seventy-six locations on the head and face region, using which pressure maps were generated. These pressure maps would act as effective reference tools for product designers. For two third of the landmarks there was a significant difference in the pressure threshold between the genders. On average, males had comparatively higher pressure thresholds than females. It was also identified that pressure thresholds were independent of age and BMI parameters. But at every landmark the pressure data had a high correlation with pressure data at every other landmark, showing consistency in pressure sensitivity for the data. The data suggested that the skull area was less pressure sensitive, while the pressure sensitivity was high in the facial region. The temporal and forehead region had a medium level of pressure sensitivity. The pressure threshold data was reliable for the pooled pressure discomfort and the pooled pressure pain data. Reliability at the most landmarks was within the acceptable range. Deformation data and tissue thickness data was successfully measured at eighteen landmarks on head and face. By using these tissue thickness and deformation data, a 3D soft tissue deformation model was further developed on the base of the complete 3D head surface model. Parameters like effective Young’s Modulus and tissue deformability were also measured. Data showed a relationship between BMI, tissue thickness, effective Young’s modulus and maximum deformation. With increase in BMI, tissue thickness and maximum deformation increased, whereas the effective Young’s Modulus decreased. Two journal papers have been published, three are under review process and one more journal paper is in preparation. In addition to that six conference papers have been published.

25603315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25603315.value: This study helped develop a 3D head surface model with localized variation for Chinese adults. The study also measured the pressure thresholds for discomfort and pain. This data can provide a good reference for product designers when designing different products. Other than soft tissue, inner head structure could also affect the product fit and design. PI plans to explore this area further and create more detailed head model. Also, this study was limited only to Chinese adults, a comparative study with the similar data acquired from other ethnic groups can help understand the variance in order to create better products. PI plans to design further collaborative studies in this area. In the current study the size of the indenter was kept small and constant. This led to acquisition of concentric loading pattern, whereas in real world when a wearable product is worn the surface area is larger and the load is distributed. Hence there is need to understand the impact of indenter size and the relationship between pressure thresholds acquired using concentric loading and distributed loading. PI plans to use the acquired data from this study to perform simulation analysis to explore this area.

25603315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25603315.value: Wearable products for head are designed to perform the function of protection, sensory enhancement or telecommunication. For them to perform their functions effectively, they need to be in close contact with the soft tissue. To ensure good fit for wide population range, it is necessary to develop products based on generalized anthropometric data and surface data. Also, since the product maintains a close fit, it exerts pressure on the contact soft tissue which can lead to discomfort or pain. Hence this research tried to evaluate the shape variance and pressure threshold parameters for different regions of the head. For developing generalized head model, 3D scans were acquired from two hundred and eighteen participants. Using mathematical algorithms, average head model were developed for both genders. Also, pressure discomfort and pain thresholds were recorded at seventy-six locations on the head and face. Using this data pressure maps were created. 3D head soft tissue deformation model was also developed using the deformation measured at eighteen locations for discomfort and pain thresholds. These models can act as excellent reference for product designers to help design better ergonomic products. This data also finds application in clinical sciences, forensic sciences, diagnostics and medicine.

25604915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25604915.value: Many decisions with real economic and social impacts (such as firefighting, decisions made en-route during trips, and impulsive shopping) are made in complex environments where information cues are ubiquitous and change rapidly. Studies have found that decision-making in dynamic real-world contexts is different from the predictions of classic decision-making models, which usually assume rigorous, rational cognitive processes based on static information displays. A better understanding of decision-making processes in real-world settings is needed to inform theory and provide practical insights for marketers and planners. To fill this gap, scholars have studied naturalistic decision-making (NDM). Previous studies focused on decisions with three boundary conditions (i.e., expertise, time pressure, and ill-defined goals) and highlighted the use of knowledge by experts and the cognitive processes of proficient decision-makers. However, many decisions in real life (such as decisions made en-route during trips) have characteristics that the NDM literature has not considered, including lack of expertise, loose group structure (high autonomy of group members), impulsivity, and the information processing moving through the information space. Also, previous research has not addressed the fact that mobile information technology such as smartphones and tablets is increasingly mediating decision-making. Therefore, the proposed research will explore decision-making in motion, with an emphasis on determining perceptions of complex information spaces, as well as processing and evaluation strategies. In particular, this study will focus on the decision processes of individuals or groups of tourists walking through an urban environment with and without smartphones. Tourism provides an ideal context because unplanned/impulsive behaviors and changes to planned behaviors are ubiquitous in urban tourism, and the information landscape in tourism is varied and dynamic. The goal of this project is to close the gap in our understanding of decision-making in motion, including information-processing strategies (e.g., the order in which to digest information cues and the processing of information presented in different manners) and the rules, heuristics, and themes embedded within decision-makers’ discursive accounts of their decisions. The proposed study will be qualitative and use an iteratively grounded theory strategy. It seeks to better reflect the contextual and new technological realities of decision-making while moving through urban information landscapes. In the long term, the findings from this research will provide implications for public space/signage design, urban planning, contextual advertising, and the designs of location-based services and augmented reality applications.

25604915.label: Realisation of objectives
25604915.value: Both objective 1 and 2 have been completed. The research outcomes include the conceptualization of the context of on-the-go tourists (i.e., objective 1) and the summarization of the patterns of information-processing strategies when tourists interacted with different kinds of contexts (i.e., objective 2). How have the project objectives been achieved: details in data collection and analysis The main purpose of data collection is to capture tourists’ movement through the information space, information searching/processing, and decision-making processes while strolling through the urban environment of Hong Kong. As such, from May to August, 2016, we traced 35 cases were completed. Specifically, the participant recruitment advertisement was posted and disseminated through a variety of social media websites. Also, the recruitment advertisement was distributed at the entrance of breakfast buffet restaurant in Hotel ICON, one of the five-star hotel located in Tsim Tsa Tsui East. As a result, 20 qualified travel parties were recruited from social media websites, and 15 qualified ones from Hotel ICON. The data acquired include interview records, voice memo, and video clips from the wearable camera. From September to December 2016, the interview transcripts had been prepared and cross-checked. The video clips were summarized. For each case, a data portfolio was established, including interview transcripts before the trip and after the trip, videos of day trips from wearable cameras, audio records from tourists’ think-aloud activities, and the written transcripts of the audio records. The day trip was broken down into scenarios, such as lunch, first attraction visit, and navigating. The coding of the transcripts followed four steps: line-by-line coding, focused coding, axial coding, and theoretical coding. In the coding process, “constant comparative methods” were used to establish analytic distinctions. In total, all the text corpus were coded for five times with the evolving coding scheme which emerged from the raw data and the comparison of extant theories. To what extent have the project objectives been achieved: research outcomes The data analysis generated enough evidence for the conceptualization of the context of decision-making in motion and the classification of information-processing strategies in a variety of scenarios such as changes of transportation routes, shopping, visit attractions. Details of the research outcomes refers to 6.1 below. Briefly, for the objective 1, seven dimensions were identified to consist of the context of decision making in motion, including servicescape, social, information, intrapersonal, geo-position, time, and weather. For the objective 2, four information-processing strategies were identified in the tourist-context interactions, including responsive, interpretive, evaluative, and operative mode.

25604915.label: Major findings and research outcome
25604915.value: The research outcomes include the conceptualization of the context of on-the-go tourists (i.e., objective 1) and the summarization of the patterns of information-processing strategies when tourists interacted with different kinds of contexts (i.e., objective 2). For the objective 1, seven dimensions were identified to consist of the context of decision making in motion, including servicescape, social, information, intrapersonal, geo-position, time, and weather. While tourists stroll through the urban environment in Hong Kong, they made on-site decisions under different contexts, in which different dimensions of context presented to influence the decision. For the objective 2, four information-processing strategies were identified in the tourist-context interactions, including responsive, interpretive, evaluative, and operative mode. Responsive mode deals with reactive-behavioral interactions representing the direct contextual impact on human performance, behaviour, and wellbeing. For instance, 16 scenarios were identified into this categories in which respondents actively searched for information to overcome the constraints from weather, physiological conditions, or time budget. Interpretive mode refers to active-cognitive interactions dealing with the areas of cognitive representation (e.g. beliefs, attitudes, images, perceptions) of the context on the basis of individual’s goal, belief and experience. For instance, 18 scenarios were found in this mode, in which participants actively justify the unplanned activities during the day trip. The research outcomes have been presented in three international conferences (Part C, Section 9). Some preliminary findings have been submitted to a journal and is currently under second review (Part C, Section 8). A journal paper titled “Tourists’ unplanned behavior in the era of mobile Internet” is under preparation for the submission to Tourism Management (A Level journal), which will report the main findings of the project. The journal publication of this project is delayed due to the late arrival of the PhD student, the structure of PhD program, and the large amount of data analysis. The ECS project only can support a PhD student, rather than a full-time research assistant. In the first year of PhD study, the PhD student has to completed courses and learn about the study context. As such, the data collection was delayed. Furthermore, this study collected a large amount of unstructured data such as video clips, verbal illustrations, and pictures. The analysis of these unstructured data requires substantial efforts. Thus, the journal paper reporting the main findings will be submitted in this August (2018).

25604915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25604915.value: This study focused on identifying the contexts of tourist decision-making in motion during a day trip, and describing the cognitive process of information cues. Due to funding limitation, the completed study was conducted in a limited scale. We only followed one-day trip of a travel party. The focal decisions are onsite decisions during the day and mainly about the arrangement for the next few hours in a day. A further development of this completed study can be a study regarding tourists’ decision-making for destination activities during the whole trip. The future study aims at developing propositions to conceptualize the process of tourists’ decision making for destination activities during the whole trip. The tourists’ decisions for all kinds of destination activities will be investigated. We will follow the whole stay of each participate travel party. Thus, besides a more comprehensive picture of in-destination decision making, the proposed study will go beyond the descriptions to develop theoretical propositions regarding the phenomenon.

25604915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25604915.value: Tourists make many decisions on-the-go to pursue the optimal experience. Studies have found that decision-making in dynamic real-world contexts is different from the predictions of classic decision-making models, which usually assume rigorous, rational cognitive processes based on static information displays. Therefore, this study was conducted to describe the contexts of decision-making in motion and to identify the information-processing strategies. This study traced 35 cases of tourists’ one-day in Hong Kong. Wearable cameras and think-aloud activities were applied to capture the tourists’ onsite decision-making process. The study identified that modern tourists tend to make more decisions with the unfolding of their day-trip. A dynamic and multi-dimensional context was found to overarch the decision-making on-the-go. Tourists make decisions under the influence from servicescape, social, information, intrapersonal, geo-position, time, and weather. Tourists selectively capture and process the information from their surroundings and interpret based on their goals, preferences, and previous knowledge. The online information input through instant chatting apps play an important role in initiating decision-making on-the-go. The research outcomes provide implications for public space/signage design, urban planning, contextual advertising, and the designs of location-based services and augmented reality applications.

25606215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25606215.value: This project is a cultural history of political conversion in Republican China. It examines Communist and leftwing activists who fled to the Guomindang side after the erstwhile political allies fell out in 1927. It sheds light on a largely unexamined phenomenon that traversed party politics, ideological polarization and the history of the body in a tumultuous period. Political conversion has long been a sensitive topic. Orthodox Communist accounts typically dismiss it as an instance of moral lapse. This project returns political conversion to its historical context. Of interest is not only individual turncoats' life stories but also the larger sociocultural milieu to which it belonged. Switching sides was, to be sure, motivated by personal considerations. But ideological changes and state actions played equally important roles in determining one’s decision. Surrendering to the Guomindang was, in addition, not a one-off event. For young political offenders, the process entailed stints in provincial reformatories. For intellectuals, it meant socializing themselves into mainstream Guomindang society as political cadres. Experiences of conversion were also public occurrences, mediated through state-run magazines, accounts of individual turncoats and theoretical debates. They tie in with the Guomindang’s anxiety over not only insurrectionary movements but also the erosion of social order by urban, cosmopolitan habits that were gaining purchase over China since the 1920s. Insofar as most of their writings appeared in either publications run by the state or those that supported it, converts’ self-representations were part of the Guomindang’s propaganda network. Rather than merely providing a perspective into their individual stories, these writings actively contributed to a discourse of anti-Communism in both the elite and popular realms. Collectively, they helped articulate a nationalist critique of Marxism. They also co-authored an anti-Communist discourse that appealed to fears over modernity of a patriarchal, hierarchy-obsessed and stability-desiring community. As such, conversion concerned not only narrowly-defined state politics but also featured as a populist conservative reaction against modernity. To reconstruct the multi-faceted phenomenon of political surrender, this project scrutinizes a range of textual and visual sources concerned with individuals who renounced their Communism and pledged loyalty to the Guomindang government. These included confessions, political prisoners’ fiction and poetry, and social commentaries written by former Communists. The project will result in three journal articles and one book chapter, suggesting that turncoats illuminated a deeper ideological strain in modern Chinese history.

25606215.label: Realisation of objectives
25606215.value: By parsing through archival and published documents held by institutions in Taipei and Shanghai, the PI is able to realize all six objectives. A conference paper was delivered at the Association of Asian Studies Annual Conference in Seattle at a panel on revolutionary and reactionary politics in interwar China and Japan. The paper was then expanded, after more thorough research into magazines published by reformatories in various provinces, into a journal article. It discusses the experiences of less well-educated converts and they ways in which they described their disillusionment with Communism. Another journal article takes the social democrat Zhang Junmai as an example of the Chinese intellectual elite. It broadens our definition of political conversion and explores how the more nuanced changes in Zhang's political thoughts was inflected and determined by his anti-Communism. Taken together, the conference paper and articles have allow the PI to realize objectives one to three. Undergraduate students have also been exposed to the materials, particularly illustrations, the PI collected as part of his research in lectures he delivers.

25606215.label: Major findings and research outcome
25606215.value: The most tangible outcomes of this project are the conference paper and two articles published or to be published in well-regarded journals focusing on Chinese/Asian studies. Less tangible is the wealth of materials that the PI has managed to dig up and study, prompting him to rethink the very category of political conversion itself. The PI has come to embrace a more catholic definition of political conversion. While former Communists who deflected to the Nationalist camp still occupy the mainstay of political conversion, the PI believes that the phenomenon should include those who renounced left-wing sympathies due to their opposition to the Communist movement in China and the state it created. As a result, the non-Communist left who gave up their socialist and anti-imperialist convictions has been included under this project's purview. Careful reading of writings attributed to political converts demonstrates that opposition to Communism was indeed imbricated in concerns about gender roles, sexuality, patriarchy, young people exposed to new ideas, and China's embattled position in the world throughout much of the twentieth century. This project has revealed that much of anti-Communism was not about Communism per se but values that challenged nativist, idealized visions of a hierarchical, stable social order. This project also sheds light on how animosity against the Communist government in Beijing compelled left-wing intellectuals to modify their political ideals in favor of the US-led capitalist order in Asia in light of the Communist ascendancy in mainland China.

25606215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25606215.value: Political conversion continued to be a significant but little studied phenomenon under the Nationalists after it retreated to Taiwan. Former Communists, having renounced their erstwhile beliefs and gained the trust of the authorities, became active in Taiwan politics. The most famous politician who belongs to this category is none other than Lee Teng-hui (1923-), who presided over the government headquartered in Taipei from 1988 to 2000. Some prominent figures in Taiwan's intelligence service and academic circles focusing on mainland China were also former Communists or at least held communist sympathies. In the future, the PI may undertake a project on how political converts contributed to the construction of knowledge on mainland China in Cold War Taiwan.

25606215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25606215.value: This is the first in-depth study of political conversion from the left to the right in modern China. Using unpublished archival materials and published sources, it reconstructs political conversion as a peculiar phenomenon in Nationalist China, where the state worked actively to destroy Communism as a political force. Those who renounced their left-wing convictions included both elite intellectuals and the less well-educated - school pupils, workers and peasants - across the country. This project studies their writings and explores how such renunciation intersected with other concerns such as gender roles, youth problems, and China's precarious position in the twentieth-century world.

25608215.label: Project Objectives
25608215.value: To study the development of both the physical and conceptual boundaries and the construction of identity in the northwestern borderlands in early medieval China. To investigate the significance of regional cultural and ethnic identity in the disintegration of early Chinese empires. To publish two to three papers in reputable peer-reviewed academic journals (in Chinese or English). The proposed papers will deal with the following questions: • to identify and analyze the strategies of political legitimation used by the northwestern regimes to establish and consolidate their governance in the early medieval period. • to analyze the interactive relationship between ethnicity and regional identity among the northwestern military elites. • to compare the military and diplomatic relationships between the northwestern states and other contemporaneous regional polities in the Chinese territories, thereby showing how regional culture and identity underpinned the strategies and policies adopted by the northwestern regimes. To prepare for two future research projects of mine: 1) on the variations of concept of violence in early medieval China, and 2) on the discourses of “medievality” in the shaping of medieval China in modern historiography.

25608215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25608215.value: This project is the first attempt to fully explore the history of forging regional political identity in northwestern China during the second to the fifth centuries of the first millennium. The region in question covering the areas of modern provinces of Gansu, southern Ningxia, eastern Qinghai, northern Sichuan, and western Shaanxi, was a porous frontier zone between the Chinese regimes and their Inner Asian neighbors since antiquity, and was not fully incorporated into the Chinese realm until the first century BC. In such a frontier zone only the tough could survive, and not surprisingly it came to have the largest concentration of men of martial background, from which regional culture and identity characterized by martial spirit and skills prevailed. The influx of various Inner Asian peoples along the frontier further complicated the ethnicity and cultural identity of the region. In the time span this project covers, the northwestern borderlands provided a breeding ground of military forces that countered the idea of a unified Chinese empire. These forces also fostered a series of polities ruled by local strong men and their highly militarized clans. In order to consolidate, sustain their governance and to overcome ethnic conflicts, these northwestern regimes adopted different strategies to establish their political legitimacy and solidify the regional identity. This project will unfold the story by (1) tracing the origins and development of regional culture and identity in the northwestern borderlands, (2) elucidating the background and composition of the various parties that constituted the regional polities, (3) analyzing the strategies of legitimation and consolidation adopted by the regional polities and their consequences, and (4) recounting the rivalry and diplomatic relationships between the northwestern polities and other contemporaneous regimes across the China area. This research will not only advance our understanding of medieval Chinese political, military, social, and cultural history but also provide a case of regional culture and identity for comparative studies in world history. In addition, as the northwestern region of China is still a place of mixed ethnicity today, this project will shed light on the discussion of ethnic culture and identity in contemporary China. 涼州作為秦漢帝國的西北邊陲之地，一直是一個多元文化與族類並存的地區，亦正因為該地區處於帝國與內亞接壤的邊疆地帶，在帝國的對外開拓與防禦之中扮演了重要的戰略角色，也造就了當地居民濃厚的武勇色彩。同時，相較帝國核心地區而言，西北地區作為帝國的領土為時尚短，在很多方面均與帝國內部的發展未盡一致，造成該地區在兩漢時期多有反覆。及至東漢末年，涼州地區的武裝竟然成為了葬送東漢帝國的急先鋒，遂開啟此下數世紀的亂局。 西晉經過短暫的統一，卻迅速陷於瓦解，當此之時，在帝國中央力量崩潰以後，涼州地區有何新的政治動向？涼州的各方力量如何爭奪在該地區的政治與軍事主導權，並從而建立新的政治秩序？涼州的軍事力量如何配合塑造當地的政治認同？以及族類問題在涼州地區建立新政治秩序的過程中究竟發揮了怎樣的作用？凡此種種問題，均為本研究項目所欲探討者。本研究項目希望可以為了解中古早期涼州地區以至當時中國的政治和軍事問題，以及政治文化提供新的視角與討論。

25608215.label: Major findings and research outcome
25608215.value: This project focuses on the development of regional culture and identity of the northwestern frontier of late classical and early medieval China. Through the examination of the relationship between the northwest and the imperial center and the conflicts, in various forms, between the regional military elites and the civil officials of the imperial state, the publications produced by this project collectively sketches a big picture of the political culture of early and early imperial China. It also provides a regional perspective of understanding the establishment and destruction of early empires in Chinese history. A case study of the Former Liang kingdom in the northwest demonstrates the importance of regional identity influenced political allegiance in general and the complicated development of hybrid culture in multi-ethnic frontier zone in particular.

25608215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25608215.value: Although the formal period of the project has ended, the PI will continue work on the same topic, and hope to work out a comprehensive book focusing on the regional identities and cultures as well as multi-allegiance of the northwestern frontier in early and early medieval China. The research being undertaken in this project is also highly relevant to a current GRF project of the PI. Both projects will interactively function and equip the PI to delve deeper into the world of early medieval China in the years to come.

25608215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25608215.value: This project traces the development of regional culture and identity of the northwestern frontier zone of China, where still characterized by its frontier nature today, in the first three hundred years of the first millennium. The research findings tell the complicated interactive relationship between the frontier and the political and cultural center of the early Chinese empires, and therefore help us to understand the significance of regional identity as a facilitator, some time, and as a hindrance, more often, in the process of empire formation. It provides not only a regional perspective of reading early medieval Chinese history but also some insights of considering the role of regional cultures in shaping identities and political allegiance.

26100315.label: Project Objectives
26100315.value: To identify and characterize Arf proteins involved in the sorting of Frizzled6 at the TGN. We will (a) identify the Arf proteins that regulate TGN export of Frizzled6, (b) explore the functional roles of the identified Arf proteins in the cargo sorting process, and (c) reconstitute the sorting process using defined protein factors. To identify additional protein factors that regulate sorting of Frizzled6 at the TGN through an in vitro TGN budding assay. An in vitro assay that reconstitutes vesicular release of Frizzled6 from the TGN will be performed. Novel proteins that regulate TGN sorting of Frizzled6 such as ArfGEFs and ArfGAPs will be pursued by fractionating any cytosolic proteins that are required for vesicular release of Frizzled6 from the TGN (a). Additionally, vesicles containing Frizzled6 after the TGN budding assay will be immunoisolated and the protein composition will be identified to reveal additional regulatory factors (b). To analyze whether the identified protein factors are important for the propagation of the PCP signaling process. Fibroblast-secreted exosomes promote breast cancer cell protrusive activity and mobility via PCP signaling. We will use fibroblast-stimulated cancer cells to test whether Vangl2 and Frizzled6 are sorted in different transport carriers at the TGN and whether these transport carriers are directly delivered to their specific destinations through live imaging analysis. Moreover, we will test whether the identified protein factors are important for the asymmetric localizations of Vangl2 and Frizzled6 as well as fibroblast stimulated cancer cell protrusive activity and mobility.

26100315.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26100315.value: Planar cell polarity (PCP) is a phenomenon in which epithelial cells are polarized in a plane perpendicular to the apical-basal axis. PCP plays a crucial role in development and defects in PCP are associated with a variety of human diseases. The establishment of PCP is controlled by a group of conserved signaling receptors that are localized asymmetrically on opposing cellular boundaries. This asymmetric localization is critical for accurate propagation of the PCP signaling process. How PCP signaling receptors are delivered to the plasma membrane as well as how their asymmetric localizations are established remain unclear. The trans Golgi network (TGN) is an essential transport hub within the cell where newly-synthesized proteins are sorted into distinct transport carriers that are transported to various downstream destinations. We hypothesize that the asymmetrically-localized PCP signaling receptors are sorted away from one another by distinct cargo sorting machineries into specific transport vesicles at the TGN, and polarized post-Golgi trafficking of these transport vesicles contributes to establishing PCP asymmetry. We therefore aim to identify the protein sorting machineries that mediate TGN export of Vangl2 and Frizzled6 (Fzd6), two important asymmetrically-localized PCP signaling receptors. Our previous analysis revealed that TGN export of Vangl2 is mediated by a small GTPase of the Arf family, Arfrp1, and its effector, the clathrin adaptor protein complex-1 (AP-1). In contrast, TGN export of Frizzled6 is independent of the Arfrp1/AP-1 machinery. Moreover, Vangl2 and Frizzled6 are enriched in different populations of vesicles formed in an in vitro assay that reconstitutes vesicle budding from the TGN, providing further support for our hypothesis. In this proposal, we will extend our study to investigate the molecular mechanisms that regulate sorting of Fzd6 at the TGN through fluorescent imaging as well as cell biological and biochemical approaches. We will also test whether protein sorting at the TGN is required for a specific PCP signaling-mediated process, fibroblast stimulated cancer cell protrusive activity and motility. These studies will establish a clear mechanistic understanding of the sorting of PCP signaling receptors at the TGN and provide novel insights into how their asymmetric localizations are established. Moreover, these studies will guide the rational design of mechanism-based inhibitors to down-regulate PCP signaling by inhibiting sorting of PCP signaling receptors at the TGN, which will provide a novel therapeutic strategy for blocking cancer metastasis and progression. 平面細胞極化是細胞沿著組織表面極化的一個生理過程。平面細胞極化在生長發育和癌癥轉移過程中起著非常重要的作用。平面細胞極化是由一組信號受體調控的，這些平面細胞極化的信號受體在細胞膜上不對稱的分布於細胞連接處相對的細胞膜上。目前關於平面細胞極化的信號受體是如何運輸到細胞膜上以及它們在細胞膜上不對稱的分布是如何形成的，我們知之甚少。反面高爾基網絡（TGN）是細胞內部一個重要的物質中轉站。很多的新合成的蛋白在TGN上被篩選到不同的囊泡中，然後這些囊泡被運輸到特定的位點。TGN上的篩選過程如果出現錯誤將導致新合成的蛋白被運送到錯誤的位點，從而使這些蛋白不能行使正常的功能。我們的目標是研究平面細胞極化的兩個重要的不對稱分布的信號受體Vangl2 和 Frizzled6在TGN上被篩選到不同的囊泡中的分子機制。同時我們研究在TGN上的篩選過程是否會影響平面細胞極化所控制的腫瘤細胞遷移。我們的研究將提供全新的見解來解釋為什麼這些受體膜蛋白能夠不對稱的分布於細胞膜上。我們的研究也為設計抑制平面細胞極化所導致的腫瘤遷移的藥物提供有用的信息。

26100315.label: Realisation of objectives
26100315.value: Planar cell polarity (PCP), a phenomenon in which epithelial tissue is polarized within the plane of the epithelium, plays a crucial role in development and organ function. The establishment of PCP is regulated by an evolutionarily conserved set of signaling proteins including Vangl2 and Frizzled6 (Fzd6). PCP proteins adopt characteristic asymmetrical localizations on opposing cellular boundaries. How the asymmetric localizations of PCP proteins are established remain largely unclear. The trans Golgi network (TGN) is an essential transport hub in the biosynthetic trafficking pathway. In this project, we aim to identify the protein sorting machineries that mediate TGN export of Fzd6. We found that TGN export of Fzd6 is mediated by clathrin and a clathrin adaptor, epsinR(Ma et al., 2018). Arf proteins play important roles in regulating membrane recruitment of cargo adaptors. We found that two Golgi-located Arf family proteins, Arf1 and Arf3, redundantly regulate TGN export of Fzd6. Arf1 purified from mammalian cells recruited purified epsinR/clathrin complex to synthetic liposomes in a concentration- and GTP-dependent manner suggesting that Arf1 can mediate membrane association of the epsinR/clathrin complex. We then performed mechanistic study to reveal insights into TGN sorting of Fzd6. Protein interaction analysis suggested that epsinR forms a stable complex with clathrin and that this complex interacts with a conserved polybasic motif in the Fzd6 cytosolic domain to package Fzd6 into transport vesicles(Ma et al., 2018). Moreover, we found that Fzd6-epsinR binding dissociates epsinR from AP-1, which may separate these two cargo adaptors from each other to perform distinct cargo-sorting functions(Ma et al., 2018). We also performed super-resolution imaging analysis to study sorting of Fzd6 and Vangl2 at the TGN(Huang et al., 2019). We found that the TGN/endosome-localized cargo adaptors, AP-1, GGA2 and epsinR, form elongated structures of over 250 nm in length at the juxta-nuclear Golgi area. Many of these structures are associated with clathrin. We found that AP-1 is spatially segregated from AP-3 and GGA2, whereas a fraction of AP-1 and GGA2 punctae are associated with epsinR. Moreover, we observed that Vangl2 and Fzd6 associate with different cargo adaptors-AP-1 and GGA2 or epsinR, respectively-when exiting the TGN. Knockdown analysis confirms the functional significance of this segregation. Our data indicates that Fzd6 and Vangl2 exit the TGN at spatially segregated micro-domains mediated by different cargo adaptors: the spatially segregated cargo adaptors GGA2 and AP-1 regulate sorting of Fzd6 and Vangl2, respectively and spatially associated cargo adaptors, GGA2 and espsinR, cooperatively regulate a specific sorting process(Huang et al., 2019). To further reveal mechanistic insights into TGN sorting of Fzd6, we developed an in vitro assay to reconstitute the packaging of Fzd6 and Vangl2 into TGN-derived transport vesicles(Ma et al., 2018; Tang et al., 2020a). Our analyses indicates that this approach recapitulates the requirements to enriched Vangl2 and Fzd6 into vesicles at the TGN(Ma et al., 2018). The immunoisolated epsinR-clathrin complex stimulates vesicular release of Fzd6 but not Vangl2. Immunoblotting of released vesicles indicated that Vangl2 and Fzd6 exit the TGN in separate compartments(Ma et al., 2018). We found that Fzd6 enriched vesicles contain another planar cell polarity protein, Celsr1, and Celsr1 promotes anterograde traffickaing of Fzd6(Tang et al., 2020b). The size of Fzd6-enriched vesicles is significantly larger than the size of vesicles enriched with another cargo protein, epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). We developed a large scale vesicle formation assay in combination with quantitative mass spectrometry analysis to analyse protein profiling of transport vesicles(Huang et al., 2021). Quantitative mass spectrometry analyses revealed several transmembrane proteins, including a SNARE protein VTI1B, that are specifically co-enriched with Fzd6 but not EGFR in TGN-derived vesicles. Mechanistic analyses revealed that VTI1B enhances the interaction between Fzd6 and its cargo adaptor, epsinR, and promotes the release of Fzd6 into transport vesicles at the TGN. Functional analyses revealed that VTI1B regulates the TGN-to-cell-surface delivery of Fzd6. These analyses indicate that VTI1B is an important factor regulating TGN sorting of Fzd6, suggesting cargo sorting is coupled to vesicle targeting. In addition, our study established a novel approach to uncover protein profiling of vesicles enriched with a specific signaling receptor, providing a robust tool to identify novel cellular factors regulating vesicular trafficking (manuscript in preparation). We then investigated whether the identified cellular factors that regulate TGN sorting of Fzd6 is important for the propagation of the PCP signaling process. It has been reported by other labs that the conditioned media from mouse fibroblast L cells potently stimulates the protrusive activity and motility of human breast adenocarcinoma MDA-MB-231 cells via PCP signaling. We originally sought to analyze PCP signaling in MDA-MB-231 cells. However, the commercial antibodies did not detect a clear signal of endogenous Fzd6 or Vangl2 in MDA-MB-231 cells, presumably because the expression level of these two PCP proteins are low in MDA-MB-231 cells. The majority of the tagged versions of Vangl2 and Fzd6 were located at the ER when they are overexpressed in MDA-MB-231 cells. As an alternative approach, we utilized Drosophila to analyze whether the Drosophila homolog of the identified cellular factors regulate TGN export of Fzd6 are important for the propagation of PCP in vivo in Drosophila wing. The Drosophila wing hairs, as an example of the PCP phenomenon, are oriented distally to the Drosophila body. In collaboration with Prof. Yan Yan’s lab at HKUST, we used the engrailed-Gal4 (en-Gal4, en>) driver and UAS-RNAi to specifically induce gene knockdown in the posterior territory of the wing disc. Our results indicate that the wing hairs are oriented toward the distal side in control wing. Knockdown of Frizzled or drosophila homologues of Arfrp1, GGA2 and epsinR causes defects in wing hair orientation. We also found that knockdown of epsinR causes defects in surface localization of Frizzled. These analyses suggest that the molecular machineries that regulate TGN sorting of Vangl2 and Fzd6 are important for PCP signaling (Manuscript in preparation). In summary, we have addressed all of our objectives utilizing biochemical, cell biological and super-resolution imaging analyse. Our study revealed novel cellular factors and underlying molecular mechanisms regulating TGN sorting of Fzd6. These analyses indicate that newly synthesized PCP proteins are sorted away from one another by distinct cargo sorting machineries at the TGN. Differential sorting causes packaging of PCP proteins into separate vesicles and polarized post-Golgi trafficking of these vesicles may contribute to establishing the PCP asymmetry.

26100315.label: Major findings and research outcome
26100315.value: Utilizing robust experimental approaches including the TGN vesicle formation assay and STORM super-resolution imaging, we uncovers novel factors and underlying mechanisms regulating TGN sorting of Fzd6. These analyses indicate that newly synthesized PCP proteins are sorted away from one another by distinct cargo sorting machineries at the TGN. Differential sorting causes packaging of PCP proteins into separate vesicles and polarized post-Golgi trafficking of these vesicles may contribute to establishing the PCP asymmetry. The following are major findings and research outcome: 1) We developed an in vitro assay that reconstitutes the packaging of Fzd6 and Vangl2 into transport vesicles. This assay indicates that Vangl2 and Fzd6 exit the TGN in separate compartments. Mechanistic analysis indicates that epsinR forms a stable complex with clathrin and that this complex interacts with a conserved polybasic motif in the Fzd6 cytosolic domain to package Fzd6 into transport vesicles. Arf1 and Arf3 redundantly mediate membrane association of epsinR-clathrin complex. Moreover, we found that Fzd6-epsinR binding dissociates epsinR from AP-1, which may separate these two cargo adaptors from each other to perform distinct cargo-sorting functions. Many of these findings have been published in JBC 2018 and Bio-protocol 2020. 2) STORM superresolution imaging analysis indicates that Fzd6 and Vangl2 exit the TGN at spatially segregated micro-domains mediated by different cargo adaptors: the spatially segregated cargo adaptors GGA2 and AP-1 regulate sorting of Fzd6 and Vangl2, respectively and spatially associated cargo adaptors, GGA2 and epsinR cooperatively regulate sorting of Fzd6. This work have been published in Frontier in Cell and Developmental Biology in 2019. 3) We developed a large scale vesicle formation assay in combination with quantitative mass spectrometry analysis to analyse protein profiling of transport vesicles. Using this approach, we identified and characterized proteins co-enriched with Fzd6 vesicles. We found that Fzd6 enriched vesicles contain another planar cell polarity protein, Celsr1, and Celsr1 promotes anterograde trafficking of Fzd6. In addition, we identified a SNARE protein VTI1B, co-enriched with Fzd6 in TGN-derived vesicles. VTI1B enhances Fzd6-epsinR interaction and promotes the release of Fzd6 into TGN-derived vesicles, suggesting cargo sorting is coupled to vesicle targeting. Some of these findings have been published in JBC 2020 and PNAS 2021. Some of these findings are in preparation for submitting. 4) Our genetic studies in Drosophila indicate that the Drosophila homolog of the cellular factors that regulating TGN sorting of Vangl2 and Fzd6 (Arfrp1, GGA2 and epsinR) is important for the PCP in Drosophila wing.

26100315.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26100315.value: In addition to VTI1B, we also identified other cellular factors, such as SCAMP2 and SCAMP3, that co-enriched with Fzd6 but not EGFR in TGN-derived vesicles. An important future direction is to study whether these molecules regulate TGN export of Fzd6. It is also important to collaborate with other labs to perform experiments in mice to test whether the identified cellular factors regulating TGN export of Frizzled6 are important for PCP in mice. Cargo sorting is the first step to achieve polarized trafficking. Another important future direction is to investigate how post-Golgi trafficking of Frizzled6-enriched vesicles achieve a specific directionality to be delivered to their specific destinations. PCP plays important roles in promoting cancer progression. Our study uncovered important protein interactions that are important for surface delivery of Frizzled6. It will be important to design inhibitors to block these interactions to down-regulate PCP signaling by inhibiting biosynthetic trafficking of Frizzled6, which will provide an alternative or complimentary therapeutic strategy.

26100315.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26100315.value: Planar cell polarity (PCP), a phenomenon in which epithelial tissue is polarized within the plane of the epithelium, plays a crucial role in development and defects in PCP promote cancer progression. The establishment of PCP is regulated by an evolutionarily conserved set of signaling proteins including Vangl2 and Frizzled6. PCP proteins adopt characteristic asymmetrical localizations on opposing cellular boundaries. How the asymmetric localizations of PCP proteins are established remain largely unclear. The trans Golgi network (TGN) is an essential transport hub in the biosynthetic trafficking pathway. In this project, we identified novel cellular factors and underlying mechanisms that mediate TGN export of Frizzled6. These analyses indicate that newly synthesized PCP proteins are sorted away from one another by distinct cargo sorting machineries at the TGN. Differential sorting causes packaging of PCP proteins into separate vesicles and polarized post-Golgi trafficking of these vesicles may contribute to establishing the PCP asymmetry. These studies not only provide a clear mechanistic understanding of the sorting of PCP proteins at the TGN but also aid in the design of mechanism-based inhibitors to down-regulate PCP signaling by inhibiting biosynthetic trafficking of PCP signaling receptors, which provides a novel therapeutic strategy for blocking cancer progression.
