26103915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26103915.value: Regenerative medicine constantly requires new biomaterials to facilitate stem cell transplantation and control cell fate decision. Our goal is to use programmed cellular synthesis to make elastin-like protein (ELP) based hydrogels that contain biological information needed to program cellular behavior. Biochemical and mechanical properties of our protein hydrogels, unlike materials from synthetic or natural sources, can be genetically programmed with high modularity and unprecedented precision due to the accuracy of cellular translational machinery. To assemble protein hydrogels, we will not only use a newly developed SpyTag-SpyCatcher (SS) chemistry to covalently stitch proteins/peptides together under physiological conditions, but also expand SS chemistry through directed evolution and protein engineering to develop new reactive protein/peptide pairs. These new pairs together constitute a toolbox of “genetically encoded click chemistry” (GECC) that combines the efficiency, selectivity and modularity of click chemistry with genetically encoded reactants. The establishment of such a toolbox will enable us to covalently decorate material scaffolds with diverse biomolecular species, ranging from short oligopeptides to complex folded proteins, for regenerative medicine. In this proposed study, such information-rich hydrogels will serve as 3D artificial ECMs to elucidate the discrete and synergistic effects of extracellular signals such as axonal growth promoting factors and antagonists of growth inhibitors on neuronal behavior and axonal regeneration. We will use rodent spinal cord injury (SCI) models to examine the ability of these tailor-made materials as growth permissive bridges to stimulate axonal growth in vivo. The feasibility of using genetically engineered cell grafts -- that modulate the local extracellular matrix by producing and secreting network-forming protein precursors -- to facilitate axonal ingrowth into lesion sites will also be explored. This is a multi-disciplinary project, crossing from chemistry and materials science to protein engineering and regenerative neurobiology. A combination of our strength in chemistry/protein engineering/gene regulation and Dr. Kai Liu’s expertise in spinal cord regeneration will enable us to gain a better understanding of regulatory mechanisms governing axonal regeneration. We are confident to accomplish this proposed study on time if funded. 再生医学不断需要新的生物材料，以促进干细胞移植和控制细胞分化。我们的目标是利用细胞合成具有生物活性的水凝胶以实现对细胞行为控制。 得益于细胞合成的准确性， 这种新的基于蛋白质的水凝胶材料，在设计上是高度模块化， 并拥有前所未有的合成精度。 要装配蛋白凝胶，我们将会利用已有的SpyTag-SpyCatcher chemistry, 同时也通过定向进化的方法进一步拓展此类蛋白质化学。 我们将其统一称为"基因编码的点击化学"(GECC)。 在这项研究中我们利用GECC组装各类具有生物活性的水凝胶。 这类材料会被用来研究轴突生长促进胞外信号离散和协同作用因素和拮抗剂对神经行为和轴突的生长抑制剂再生。我们将使用啮齿类动物脊髓损伤 (SCI) 模型来检测的能力。

26103915.label: Realisation of objectives
26103915.value: 1. Expand the Toolbox for Constructing Protein Hydrogels (100% of Objective I). Multiple interactions including metal coordination, mechanically interlocked p53 dimerization domains, and AdoB12-dependent light-sensing CarH photoreceptors have been used to construct protein hydrogels with varied biophysical properties and stimuli responsiveness. In order to create redox-responsive hydrogels, cobalt ions were introduced to form inter-chain crosslinks among His6-tagged protein molecules. The cobalt-His-Tag coordination can be switched from dynamic and moderately stable to permanent and extremely stable in a reversible manner by controlling the oxidation state of the metal ion, Co (II) vs. Co (III) under mild conditions. We have successfully synthesized a protein hydrogel with a combination of the SpyTag-SpyCatcher and cobalt chemistry. We also observed that the stiffness of the resulting hydrogel can be tuned by controlling the oxidation of Co (II) to Co (III), which is highly indicative of the redox responsiveness of the material. We further expanded this metal-directed protein assembly strategy and developed protein networks with distinct stress-relaxation behavior—a process that involves the folding and reconstitution of a pair of split IgG-binding GB1 proteins. In addition, metal-ligand coordination within the protein networks exerted great influence over their viscoelastic properties. The resulting protein networks are self-healable, amenable to biochemical decoration via SpyTag/SpyCatcher chemistry, and compatible with 3D culture of fibroblasts. This study points to a simple and robust strategy for designing recombinant protein hydrogels with tunable biochemical and mechanical properties. The importance of the material’s viscoelastic properties such as stress relaxation in regulating cell behavior prompted us to develop protein hydrogels with genetically programmable stress relaxation rates. By incorporating the p53dim domains that form interlocked topological links into the gel network, we created a protein hydrogel that exhibited rapid stress relaxation under a fixed strain. The viscoelasticity can be varied through a combination of SpyTag-SpyCatcher chemistry and the p53dim domains. We were also able to make photo-responsive protein hydrogels by taking advantage of the AdoB12-dependent photoreceptor CarH protein. Two telechelic protein constructs, SpyTag-ELP-CarH-ELP-SpyTag (ACA) and SpyCatcher-ELP-CarH-ELP-SpyCatcher (BCB), were produced using a standard recombinant DNA technology and Escherichia coli expression system. The reaction of these two proteins in the presence of AdoB12 in the dark led to the formation of a hydrogel, which can further undergo a rapid gel-sol transition upon light exposure. This light-induced gel-sol transition has been utilized for the facile recovery of cells from three dimensional (3D) cultures and the controlled release of protein molecules. 2. Injectable Microsphere-Based Neuron Encapsulation (100% of Objective II) and Delivery System (100% of Objective III). Spy network hydrogels have been shown to be able to support the growth of mouse 3T3 fibroblasts, mouse embryonic stem cells and dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons. To create a neuron transplantation system with minimal invasiveness, we synthesized monodisperse Spy network hydrogel-based microspheres using a two-channel microfluidic device. These microspheres were also tested for their ability to encapsulate and support the growth of fibroblasts and DRG neurons. Recombinant neurotrophins have also been successfully expressed using E. coli expression system and have been tested for their influence on neurite growth in these 3D cultures.

26103915.label: Major findings and research outcome
26103915.value: To assemble protein hydrogels, we not only used a newly developed SpyTag-SpyCatcher chemistry, which can covalently stitch proteins/peptides together under physiological conditions, but also took advantage of other protein-protein interactions to make the materials stimuli-responsive and tunable. The establishment of a rich toolbox for protein hydrogel design has provided a versatile platform for biomedical applications. In this study, the protein hydrogels were used to elucidate the discrete and synergistic effects of biochemical and mechanical signals on neuronal behavior and axonal regeneration. We also developed an injectable delivery system for cells and proteins, which potentially allows us to inject cells and neurotrophins directly into lesion sites. Since 2016, the entire study has led to one US patent, 16 articles published in top research journals (12 as the corresponding author), 1 submitted manuscripts and one Hong Kong-based biotech startup.

26202815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26202815.value: Gas turbines are used extensively for power generation and aircraft propulsion. They are efficient and reliable but emit harmful pollutants such as nitrogen oxides (NOx), contributing to acid rain, respiratory illness, and global warming. To reduce NOx emissions, gas turbine manufacturers are switching to lean premixed combustion, but this tends to promote thermoacoustic oscillations in the combustor. These are pressure oscillations arising from resonant coupling between heat-release-rate (HRR) oscillations and acoustic oscillations. If severe, they can increase pollutant emissions, accelerate wear and fatigue, and even lead to catastrophic failure. Our current understanding of the physical processes occurring in combustors is insufficient to enable thermoacoustic oscillations to be engineered out at the design stage. Instead, trial-and-error experiments on full-scale multisector rigs must be conducted, which is an expensive and time-consuming process. In developing the next generation of low-emissions gas turbines, it is therefore essential to exploit a better understanding of the mechanisms driving thermoacoustic instability. One key mechanism is coupling via hydrodynamics. In most combustors, the flow field supplying reactants is hydrodynamically unstable and can therefore amplify incident perturbations. This amplification strengthens the coupling between HRR oscillations and acoustic oscillations, thus strengthening thermoacoustic oscillations. However, there is a type of flow with global hydrodynamic instability (GHI) that is less sensitive to incident perturbations and could potentially be used to weaken thermoacoustic instability. One aim of the proposed study is to test the extent to which that weakening can be achieved. A flame with GHI acts as a self-excited oscillator with an intrinsic natural frequency and can synchronize with thermoacoustic oscillations at nearby frequencies. Another aim is to explore that synchronization and to develop low-order models for understanding and predicting its characteristics and mechanisms. This will improve our understanding of the nonlinear interaction between self-excited hydrodynamic oscillations and thermoacoustic oscillations, thus improving our understanding of thermoacoustic instability in practical combustion systems. Experiments will be conducted on a hydrodynamically self-excited premixed flame in a longitudinal duct whose natural acoustic frequency can be adjusted relative to the natural GHI frequency of the flame. The synchronization characteristics and boundary conditions will be measured using thermographic particle image velocimetry, chemiluminescence and microphones. The data will be analyzed using nonlinear tools from dynamical systems theory in order to develop coupled-oscillator models for prediction and control. If successful, this concept will enable GHI to be used as a passive method for controlling thermoacoustic instability in the next generation of low-emissions gas turbines. 燃氣輪機已經被廣泛應用於發電機組和航空發動機中。雖然它是有效並且可靠的動力系統，但是它會在工作過程中排放有害污染物如氮氧化物（NOx）。這會產生酸雨，引起呼吸系統疾病，以及導致全球變暖問題。為了減少氮氧化物的排放，燃氣輪機的研發設計者們開始轉向使用一種貧油燃燒技術，但是這種技術的使用會加劇燃燒室內熱聲耦合振盪問題，即由於熱釋放率和聲振盪頻率相互耦合導致的壓強振盪。如果嚴重的話，他們反而會增加污染物的排放，加速設備磨損和機械疲勞，甚至導致災難性後果。由於我們目前針對這一問題的物理過程的認識不夠充分，因此我們無法在設計階段就將該問題解決，並且需要開展大量全尺寸實驗研究工作，使得設計過程耗費大量時間和資金。因此，在發展下一代低排放的燃氣輪機之前，我們需要對熱聲不穩定問題的觸發機理進行更好地研究。 這其中一個重要的研究方向就是利用流動特性對熱聲不穩定進行耦合抑制。在絕大多數燃燒室中，輸運反應物的流場是不穩定的，因此會對隨機擾動產生增益作用。這種增益加強了熱釋放率和聲振盪頻率之間的耦合作用從而加劇了熱聲不穩定振盪。然而，我們發現存在一種具有全局流動不穩定性的流動過程，其對於隨機擾動不敏感，並且具備應用於抑制熱聲不穩定的潛力。 我們主要研究目標有兩點。第一，檢驗這種流動過程所能抑制不穩定的能力。我們將會設計一個具有全局流動不穩定性特徵的火焰，它在實驗中被視作一個具有固有頻率的自激振盪源，並且能被同步到與熱聲振盪相近的頻率。第二，探索同步化並建立低維模型來理解和預測這種火焰的特徵和機理。這將有助於提高我們對於流動自激振盪和熱聲振蕩之間的非線性作用關係的認識。 我們將會主要開展以下實驗工作。將一個具有流動自激性的預混火焰置於一根長管中。該管扮演燃燒室的角色，並且可以通過改變管的長度來調整其固有聲頻。我們將使用熱成像式粒子圖像測速儀，化學發光法，以及高靈敏度的麥克風來測量研究同步化的特徵以及聲邊界條件。我們將會對採集到的數據利用非線性動力學方法來分析，以便更好地建立可用於預測和控制耦合振盪的物理模型。如果順利的話，這一研究思路能夠使得全局流動不穩定性成為控制熱聲不穩定的可行被動控制方法之一，並且在下一代低排放燃氣輪機中得到應用。

26202815.label: Realisation of objectives
26202815.value: We have designed and built a prototypical thermoacoustic system to investigate the synchronization between the natural acoustic modes of a combustor and the natural hydrodynamic modes of a turbulent premixed flame containing global hydrodynamic instability (GHI). As detailed in my ECS proposal (Section 2B: Research Plan and Methodology), the system has provisions for both open-loop acoustic forcing (for Objectives 1-3) and natural flame-combustor coupling (for Objectives 4-5). Using this system, we produced turbulent premixed flames stabilized behind a bluff body, which offered precise control over the strength of GHI, optical access for non-intrusive measurements, and the ability to change the length and velocity scales via a simple change of the bluff-body geometry and/or the flow rates of the reactants. We collected time-resolved data pertaining to the heat-release-rate (HRR) from the flame (CH* chemiluminescence), the velocity field (particle image velocimetry) and the pressure field (microphones). We did this under conditions of (i) forced synchronization, via external perturbations applied by loudspeakers and (ii) mutual synchronization, via natural coupling of the flame and combustor. We then analyzed the data using tools from synchronization theory so as to develop low-order coupled-oscillator models for prediction and control. Overall this project has shown that GHI is a promising strategy for passive control of self-excited thermoacoustic oscillations in combustion systems. To achieve Objective 1, we investigated the forced synchronization of a bluff-body stabilized turbulent premixed flame containing GHI. Through spatiotemporal analysis of high-speed CH* chemiluminescence videos and acoustic pressure signals, we found that (i) when unforced, the entire flame oscillates at its intrinsic natural frequency owing to GHI; (ii) when forced weakly, the shear layers of the flame oscillate at the natural frequency but its wake oscillates at the forcing frequency; (iii) when forced above a critical amplitude, the entire flame oscillates at the forcing frequency, producing a globally synchronized mode corresponding to `lock-in' ; and (iv) the HRR amplitude decreases just before the onset of lock-in, with the magnitude of that decrease increasing as the forcing frequency shifts away from the natural frequency. This shows that the presence of GHI in a turbulent premixed flame can reduce its HRR response, particularly near lock-in. To achieve Objective 2, we investigated the transition to GHI of a turbulent premixed flame under unforced conditions. On varying the equivalence ratio for a fixed Reynolds number, we found three primary flame modes: (i) a steady mode, (ii) a symmetric mode, and (iii) an asymmetric mode, based on the flame macro-structure and the amplitude of flame-edge oscillations. On reducing the equivalence ratio, we found that the flame becomes increasingly unsteady, transitioning from the steady mode, to the symmetric mode, and then to the asymmetric mode in turn. By calculating the Strouhal number for both oscillatory modes, we found evidence that the asymmetric mode is caused by local absolute instability, consistent with Benard von Karman vortex shedding arising from GHI. By contrast, the symmetric mode was found to arise from local convective instability in the shear layers, consistent with a Kelvin-Helmholtz instability inducing a spatial-amplifier flow. We then investigated all three flame modes in terms of the flame stand-off distance, HRR, shear-layer thickness, recirculation-zone size, and reverse-flow velocity. By analyzing the dominant modes and their energy distribution via proper orthogonal decomposition, we found that the asymmetric mode arising from GHI generates better mixing than the symmetric mode arising from local convective instability. These findings show that GHI is beneficial for mixing and can be readily produced in a turbulent premixed flame. To achieve Objective 4, we investigated the mutual synchronization of a coupled flame-combustor system, which consisted of a longitudinal duct combustor coupled to a turbulent premixed flame with GHI. We induced mutual synchronization between the acoustic modes of the combustor and the GHI mode (vortex shedding) of the flame by changing the combustor length so as to change its natural acoustic frequency relative to the natural vortex-shedding frequency of the GHI mode. On varying the combustor length, we found that lock-in always occurs via three distinct stages: (i) a desynchronized stage, (ii) an intermittent stage characterized by bursts of synchronized and desynchronized epochs, and (iii) a fully synchronized stage. We found that, under some conditions, the thermoacoustic amplitude of the coupled flame-combustor system can increase until lock-in occurs. Nevertheless, we also found that, under different conditions, the thermoacoustic amplitude can be suppressed near the onset of lock-in. Collectively, these findings show that GHI in a turbulent premixed flame can indeed reduce the thermoacoustic amplitude, provided that the natural frequency of the acoustic mode in the combustor is carefully tuned relative to the natural frequency of the GHI mode in the flame. To achieve Objectives 3 and 5, it is crucial to have tools for low-order modeling of forced and mutual synchronization. Previous studies have shown that such tools can be developed on prototypical hydrodynamic oscillators, such as a low-density jet. Such oscillators can synchronize with external forcing via one of two universal routes: a saddle-node (SN) bifurcation or a torus-death (TD) bifurcation. We used complex networks to analyze these two routes to synchronization in a prototypical low-density jet with GHI. We built the complex networks using two different methods: the visibility algorithm and the recurrence condition. We found that the visibility networks are high-clustering, hierarchical, and assortative in the degree of their vertices, but only the TD networks are scale free. We also found that the assortativity coefficient is a sufficiently sensitive indicator by which to distinguish between the SN and TD routes and to forecast the onset of lock-in. As for the recurrence networks, we found that their topological features differ between the two routes to synchronization, but vary predictably along either route. This shows that complex networks can be a powerful tool for distinguishing between the SN and TD routes to synchronization, and for forecasting the proximity of a system to its lock-in boundaries. Using a nonlinear dynamical systems framework, we developed a low-order model for the GHI oscillator based on the normal-form equation for a Hopf bifurcation (the Stuart-Landau equation) and used that model to establish subcritical Hopf bifurcations (including bi-stability and hysteresis), a universal scaling for the onset of GHI, a Pomeau-Manneville type of intermittency, and coherence resonance. From there, we embarked on several further studies to explore the mutual synchronization of thermoacoustic oscillators, focusing on effects such as dissipative and time-delayed coupling, a cross-talk section, symmetric/asymmetric boundary conditions, and the presence of an intrinsic GHI mode. In particular, we found that, contrary to long-held assumptions, the pressure and HRR signals from a combustor with a GHI flame need not always be perfectly synchronized after the onset of thermoacoustic instability. This highlights the need to be exceptionally careful when selecting a diagnostic signal from which to calculate nonlinear measures of self-excited thermoacoustic oscillations, as the pressure and HRR signals can be desynchronized by the presence of GHI in the flame at a frequency different from that of the dominant thermoacoustic mode. Crucially, we were able to identify the specific conditions under which a novel state of complete suppression ('amplitude death') occurred as a result of mutual synchronization. These results will be invaluable for the design of passive control strategies for the next generation of combustion devices such as low-NOx gas turbines.

26202815.label: Major findings and research outcome
26202815.value: Major research achievements: (i) we established that global hydrodynamic instability (GHI) is beneficial for mixing and can be readily produced in a turbulent premixed flame; (ii) we demonstrated that, when forced weakly, the shear layers of a GHI flame oscillate at the natural frequency but its wake oscillates at the forcing frequency; (iii) we showed that, when forced above a critical amplitude, the entire GHI flame oscillates at the forcing frequency, producing a globally synchronized mode corresponding to `lock-in'; (iv) we established that the heat-release-rate (HRR) amplitude decreases just before the onset of lock-in, with the magnitude of that decrease increasing as the forcing frequency shifts away from the natural frequency; (v) we showed that mutual synchronization between the flame's GHI mode and the combustor's acoustic modes occurs in three stages, namely a desynchronized stage, followed by an intermittent stage involving bursts of synchronized and desynchronized epochs, and finally a fully synchronized stage; (vi) we demonstrated that, depending on the frequency detuning between the combustor's acoustic mode and the flame's GHI mode, the thermoacoustic amplitude can either increase or decrease; (vii) we proved that complex networks are a powerful tool for distinguishing between the saddle-node and torus-death routes to synchronization, and for forecasting the proximity to the lock-in boundaries; (viii) we developed a low-order model for a prototypical GHI oscillator based on the normal-form equation for a Hopf bifurcation (the Stuart-Landau equation) and used that model to establish subcritical Hopf bifurcations (including bi-stability and hysteresis), a universal scaling for the onset of GHI, a Pomeau-Manneville type of intermittency, and coherence resonance; (ix) we discovered that the pressure and HRR signals from a combustor with a GHI flame need not always be perfectly synchronized after the onset of thermoacoustic instability; and (x) we identified the specific conditions under which a novel state of complete suppression ('amplitude death') occurs as a result of mutual synchronization. In terms of student training, 2 PhD students (Yu Guan and Manikandan Balasubramaniyan) and 1 MPhil student (Yuanhang Zhu) have worked on this project and other relevant projects. In terms of research output, we have written a total of 10 journal papers: 7 published, 2 under review, and 1 in preparation. We have also delivered 13 presentations at international conferences, including The 69th-72nd Annual Meetings of the APS Division of Fluid Dynamics (USA), The 12th Asia-Pacific Conference on Combustion (Japan), and The 24th International Congress on Sound and Vibration (UK).

26202815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26202815.value: The experimental/theoretical findings and model predictions from this project have provided new quantitative and qualitative insight into global hydrodynamic instability (GHI), its effect on turbulent premixed flames, and its ability to weaken self-excited thermoacoustic oscillations. Although by analyzing these findings and models we have been able to identify the conditions under which thermoacoustic instability can be weakened in our bluff-body-stabilized combustor, further analysis and data collection are needed if universal design rules are to be established for a variety of combustor geometries, such as those employing swirl-stabilized flames (rather than the bluff-body-stabilized flames studied here) and even laminar flames, which are surprisingly common in industry, e.g. in domestic gas boilers and heaters powered by matrix burners for material processing. Consequently, the next logical course of action is to extend the present project to other common combustor geometries, so as to determine the universality of the role of GHI in passively controlling self-excited thermoacoustic oscillations.

26202815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26202815.value: Gas turbines are used for electricity generation and aircraft propulsion. They are efficient and reliable but emit NOx, contributing to acid rain, respiratory illness, and global warming. NOx emissions can be reduced via lean-premixed combustion, but this causes thermoacoustic oscillations. These are pressure oscillations arising from the coupling between heat-release-rate and acoustic oscillations. If severe, they can exacerbate wear and fatigue, leading to catastrophic failure. Fortunately, there is a class of flow with global hydrodynamic instability (GHI) that is less prone to acoustic coupling and could potentially be used to weaken thermoacoustic instability. In this project, we performed experiments on a turbulent premixed flame in a duct combustor whose natural acoustic frequency could be adjusted relative to the natural GHI frequency of the flame. We examined the synchronization dynamics via high-speed chemiluminescence imaging, particle image velocimetry, and pressure measurements. We then analyzed the data in a dynamical systems framework to develop low-order coupled-oscillator models for prediction and control. We were thus able to show how and under what conditions GHI could weaken thermoacoustic oscillations in a combustion system. These findings will help enable GHI to be used for passive control of thermoacoustic instability in low-NOx gas turbines and other combustion devices.

26206115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26206115.value: The high cost of the Pt-based electrocatalysts for oxygen reduction reactions at the cathodes of the proton exchange membrane fuel cells has hindered their widespread adoption. Core-shell catalysts synthesized via a galvanic displacement reaction have attracted great attention due to their extremely high Pt utilization. However, the application of core-shell catalysts in fuel cells has been unsuccessful mainly due to incomplete Pt shell coverage in gram-scale batch synthesis. The core-shell structures are also very sensitive to temperature due to thermally induced atomic diffusion. These important issues have not been systematically studied previously. This proposed study will tackle both the synthesis and stability problems with novel techniques and approaches using Pd@Pt as a model system, which will be expanded to core-shell combinations of other transition metals. The proposed method is to add selected additives in the displacement reaction solution and to understand their roles in controlling the quality of the Pt shell. For the first time, a mathematical model will be developed to understand the kinetics of Pt-Cu displacement reactions and obtain key parameters that determine the quality of the Pt shell. A prototype reactor for gram-scale batch synthesis with optimized parameters will be fabricated. In addition, using a new and novel approach, we will explore the thermally induced evolution of catalyst structure by both experimental and theoretical techniques, including density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations. The success of this project will greatly advance our understanding of the mechanisms underlying the galvanic displacement reaction and heterogeneous nucleation and growth of Pt on foreign metals. It will also give us a fundamental understanding of the pathways and kinetic energy barriers associated with atomic inter-diffusion. The threshold temperature at which the core atoms start to migrate to the surface will be determined. This result will be critical, serving as a guideline for choosing proper methods to fabricate the membrane electrode assembly (MEA). With an optimized synthesis protocol which produces perfect core-shell structures and MEA preparation method which maintains their structural integrity, we will be close to achieving commercial synthesis of core-shell catalysts. 高成本的鉑基氧還原反應（ORR）催化劑阻礙了質子交換膜燃料電池的廣泛應用。因其極高的Pt利用率和活性，通過鉑離子和欠電位沉積（UPD）形成的銅單層之間的置換反應合成核 - 殼結構催化劑已經引起了極大的關注。然而，由於在大批量合成中，鉑殼並不完全覆蓋核，使得核 - 殼催化劑在燃料電池中的應用並不非常成功。 這些核 - 殼催化劑通常表現出比預期低得多的活性和穩定性。此外，它們的穩定性還對溫度非常敏感。甚至在被置於燃料電池測試之前，由於熱引起的原子擴散導致核原子遷移到表面，使得活性和穩定性大大降低。這些重要的問題還沒有得到系統的研究。本項目以鈀@鉑作為模型，將發展和應用新的技術和方法解決核-殼催化劑的合成和穩定性的問題。具體地說，我們將在置換反應液中加入適當的添加劑，並研究其在控制鉑殼形成中的作用。我們還將建立一個數學模型來研究鉑 - 銅取代反應的動力學，並獲得決定鉑殼的質量的關鍵參數。我們還將通過實驗和密度泛函理論（DFT）和分子動力學（MD）模擬研究溫度導致的結構變化。該項目的成功將極大地推進我們對金屬置換反應和外延膜生長基本機制的理解。本課題的結果將作為指導選擇合適的方法批量生產催化劑的關鍵參數。用優化的合成方法生產完美的核 - 殼結構，同時保持它們的結構完整性，我們將接近商業化生產核 - 殼催化劑。

26206115.label: Realisation of objectives
26206115.value: 1. To identify additives that adsorb on Pt and Cu surfaces but not on Pd at the potentials where Cu-Pt displacement reaction occurs and fully understand their adsorption behavior. This objective was fully achieved. We have determined that citric acid can significantly improve the activity of Pd@Pt core-shell catalysts. We also conducted a series of electrochemical experiments to reveal the underlying mechanisms. 2. To develop a mathematical model to describe the reaction kinetics of Cu-Pt displacement reaction with and without additives and determine the key factors controlling the quality of the core-shell catalysts in a gram-scale batch. This objective was fully achieved. A general kinetics model that can be used to fit the experimental data was developed. 3. To establish an optimized protocol for synthesizing Pd@Pt catalysts in gram-scale batches. This objective was fully achieved. An optimized protocol for synthesizing Pd@Pt catalysts was established. A custom reactor was built to synthesize gram-scale batches of core-shell catalysts using commercial Pd nanoparticles supported on Ketjen Black (Pd/C) as the core materials (TKK, 35 wt.%). The reactor comprised a graphite sheet as the working electrode, carbon cloth as the counter electrode, and an Ag/AgCl leak-free reference electrode (BASi). The procedure of core-shell catalyst synthesis is illustrated in Fig.4. In a typical synthesis, the Pd/C nanoparticles were dispersed in a 50 mM H2SO4 solution and then added to the reactor. The Pd/C was pretreated as needed to wet the powder. After pretreatment, a deaerated aqueous CuSO4 solution in 50 mM H2SO4 was added to the reactor to obtain a Cu2+ concentration of 50 mM. After addition of the CuSO4, the potential was held at approximately 0.37 V vs. Ag/AgCl to deposit an atomically thin layer of Cu on the Pd nanoparticles. Immediately upon completion of the Cu UPD (under potential deposition), a deaerated aqueous solution of K2PtCl4 was added dropwise to the reactor to perform a galvanic replacement of the Cu by the Pt. In addition to the Pt precursor, citric acid was also included in the Pt precursor solution to minimize the formation of Pt clusters. After the reaction was complete, typically taking 30 minutes, catalysts were filtered and rinsed with ultrapure water (Milli-Q UV-plus water). The resulting catalyst powder, denoted as Pt/Pd/C, was dried in a vacuum at 60°C. 4. To determine the mechanisms of thermally induced inter-diffusion between the core and shell atoms and the threshold temperature at which the structural evolution commences by combining the experimental and theoretical approaches. This objective was fully achieved. Theoretical modeling was conducted to estimate the thermal energy needed during the interatomic diffusion between the core and shell atoms. An external thermal energy ΔE is necessary to overcome the activation barrier to push the core-shell system toward the global equilibrium, i.e., Pt diffusing into Pd core. The temperature corresponding to this thermal energy was calculated to be 272 °C.

26206115.label: Major findings and research outcome
26206115.value: 1. The role of citric acid in controlling the uniformity of Pt monolayers on Pd is revealed. It is found that citric acid strongly adsorbs on Pd, Pt, Cu/Pd and Pt/Pd surfaces, especially in the double-layer region in acid solutions. The strong adsorption of citric acid slows down the Cu-Pt displacement reaction, which is caused by the fact that Pt atoms deposited on the Pd surface in the early stage of the Cu-Pt displacement reaction are covered by a dense layer of citric acid in the potential range of the reaction. This prevented the further deposition of Pt on the already existing Pt atoms covered by a citric acid layer to form 3D clusters. (S. Zhu, et al, Journal of the Electrochemical Society 2016, 163: D3040-D3046. 2. The synthesis protocol of core-shell electrocatalysts is optimized. The ORR activity of the materials synthesis is more than 4 times higher than commercial Pt/C. (S. Khateeb, et al, Journal of the Electrochemical Society 2016, 163: F708-F713). 3. The pathways of atomic diffusion in the core-shell structure, the initial and propagation of atomic diffusion as a function of temperature , and the threshold temperature at which the structure evolution starts to occur are identified. (Y. Zhang, et al, Chinese Journal of Catalysis 2019, in press)

26206115.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26206115.value: In this project, a uniform platinum monolayer is formed on palladium surfaces by using citric acid as the additive in the synthesis solution. The role of citric acid is also systematically studied. For the first time, the pathways of atomic diffusion in the core-shell structure and the threshold temperature at which the structure evolution starts to occur are identified. These findings are very important for the piratical scaling up of this type of catalysts and application in fuel cells.

26211515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26211515.value: The rise in wearable devices with varying computational capabilities, numerous sensors and multiple options for communication open the door to a vast spectrum of applications that can collectively leverage these resources. Nowadays, application developers tend to use the concepts of wisdom of crowd and collective intelligence to produce more sophisticated and capable mobile applications by taking advantage of the fact that community-based motivations drive people to be cooperative. Our preliminary experiments in Mobile Augmented Reality (MAR) application development using Google Glasses once again justified that wearable devices demand resourceful nearby devices (e.g. smartphones). The proper selection of the latter constitutes a complex process that depends on the effectiveness of each mobile device, also known as reputation. However, the mobile operating systems (OS) are not as mature as the conventional for providing such services. The aforementioned observations imply that a distributed reputation system, serving as a middleware and built upon a mobile OS, can be beneficial. To this direction, it has to expose functionalities to crowd computing application developers. In this proposal we present OPENRP, an ambitious middleware for any mobile application that need to evaluate the reputation of other mobile devices. OPENRP (i) utilizes low level components of the OS like the network modules and the embedded database, (ii) processes the information it collects, and (iii) exposes a set of operations to application developers in the form of an application programming interface. OPENRP works as a distributed reputation system and is able to detect events that are useful to estimate users reputation as well as it exchanges these collected information in order to create a more comprehensive consensus. However, in mobile networks with autonomous agents, the received information is not always trustful and it can be sometimes misleading. Learning algorithms and Bayesian inference techniques are used to examine the quality of the received results and impose proper rules to enforce trust. Furthermore, OPENRP is designed with the constraints to be lightweight, in terms of resources and battery needs, and scalable. It works in a delicate way when there are available resources while being up-to-date in the highest possible degree. The data size of the reputation system can increase exponentially, to avoid this issue we propose a data management algorithm for historical data. We also plan to conduct realistic experiments at urban areas. Additionally, to increase the usability of our system we also maintain the privacy and security protocols in our system. 移動設備不斷增強的計算能力、眾多的傳感器、以及通信上的多種選擇，為大量應用程序創造了條件，使其能夠共同利用這些資源。目前，應用開發人員傾向於使用群體智慧的概念，基於群體動機來驅使人們合作這一優勢，開發更加復雜的移動應用程序。我們使用谷歌眼鏡開發的移動增強現實應用也再一次証明了可穿戴設備需要附近的設備（如智能手機）提供資源。對於這些附近設備的選擇是一個復雜的過程，它依賴於移動設備的有效性，也就是我們所說的信譽。然而，移動操作系統並沒有成熟到能夠提供這種服務。上述觀察結果表明，一個建立在移動操作系統上，能向群計算應用程序開發人員顯示功能的分布式信譽系統能夠解決這個問題。在該方案中，我們提出了OPENRP，移動應用程序能夠用它來評估其他移動設備的信譽。OPENRP （1）利用操作系統底層組件，例如網絡模塊和嵌入式數據庫，（2）處理收集到的信息，（3）通過應用編程接口的形式，向應用程序開發人員顯示了可執行的操作。作為一個分布式的信譽系統，OPENRP能夠檢測到有利於評估用戶信譽的事件，以及交換收集到的信息，達到更全面的共識。然而，在自治代理的移動網絡中，收到的信息並不總是可信任的，有時會產生誤導。學習算法和貝葉斯推理技術被用於檢查接受到的結果的質量，並實施適當的規則來加強信任。此外，OPENCV的設計是可擴展並且輕量化的，比如對於資源和電池的需求。當有可用的資源時，它會自動更新后工作。信譽系統的數據大小可能會呈指數增長，為了避免這個問題，我們提出了針對歷史數據的數據管理算法。我們將會在市區進行實驗。為了提高該系統的可用性，我們會在系統中加入隱私和安全協議。

26211515.label: Realisation of objectives
26211515.value: The project had two objectives, one theoretical and one technical. Both of them have been met successfully. In more detail: We published an article titled: "OPENRP: A Reputation Middleware for Opportunistic Crowd Computing" in IEEE Communications Magazine (a technical magazine with high visibility) where we discussed the need for a distributed reputation system. We proposed the first solution and used publicly available datasets to examine its performance. The scope of this work was to communicate the importance of the framework we are developing. Moreover, we published an article titled "Have You Asked Your Neighbors? A Hidden Market Approach for Device-to-Device Offloading" in the IEEE International Symposium on a World of Wireless, Mobile and Multimedia networks (WoWMoM) 2016. In this article we use auctions and focus on incentives to formulate mobile users' interactions mathematically, and discuss the existing incentives. We further extended this work by conducting an equilibrium analysis of the economy of shared resources and published it in IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing with the title “FlopCoin: A Cryptocurrency for Computation Offloading.” Also, we designed a payment scheme for D2D ecosystems to complement OPENRP. This work was published in ACM Mobihoc 2016, with title “LocalCoin: An Ad- hoc Payment Scheme for Areas with High Connectivity.” Furthermore, we examine various types of applications that can benefit from our framework and investigating the importance of information exchange between mobile users in the robustness and truthfulness of our distributed reputation system. This work was published with the title "Asynchronous Reputation Systems in Device-to-Device Ecosystems” in ACM MobiHoc 2016 - HOTPOST workshop. Additionally, we analysed three datasets that contain traces of mobile devices and their connectivity to a mobile network and discussed the feasibility of D2D ecosystems, on top of which the proposed architecture is designed to work. This work is published in IEEE Communications Magazine with title “D2D Task Offloading: A Dataset-Based Q&A.” Also, to examine the effect of users' mobility we published two articles in Nature Scientific Report with the titles: "Navigation by Anomalous Random Walks on Complex Networks" and "Memory and Betweenness Preference in Temporal Networks Induced from Time Series" and two articles in Chaos: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Nonlinear Science titled “Multitarget search on complex networks: A logarithmic growth of global mean random cover time” and “Predicting search time when hunting for multiple moving targets: A recursive harmonic law.” Regarding the technical research objectives we have implemented a usable API for application developers for two different communication protocols: WiFi-direct and NFC. The research work on WiFi-direct was published with the title "Video Compression in the Neighborhood: An Opportunistic Approach” in IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC) 2016 and the work on NFC was published with title "Keep Your Nice Friends Close, but Your Rich Friends Closer - Computation Offloading Using NFC". Moreover, in order to share our experience on computation offloading, we published "A Hitchhiker's Guide to Computation Offloading: Opinions from Practitioners" in IEEE Communication Magazine and “Dandelion: A Unified Code Offloading System for Wearable Computing” in IEEE Transactions in Mobile Computing. The growing research interest from both industry and academia in mobile augmented reality motivated us to investigate this topic in the context of this project. We applied many of the insights developed during this project to mobile augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) systems. We have examined the network characteristics of mobile augmented reality applications and published two papers, respectively titled “Future Networking Challenges: the Case of Mobile Augmented Reality” in IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems 2017, and “On the Networking Challenges of Augmented Reality” in ACM SIGCOMM Workshop on Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality Network 2017. The first paper focuses on the lower communication layers, while the second one analyzes the challenges of AR applications. We then developed several frameworks for AR and VR. We published “Jaguar: Low Latency Mobile Augmented Reality with Flexible Tracking” in the 26th ACM international conference on Multimedia (ACM MM), 2018, describing a framework for low-latency AR offloading. We also explored the possibilities of computation caching in “CIRCE: Real-Time Caching for Instance Recognition on Cloud Environments and Multi-Core Architectures” in the 26th ACM international conference on Multimedia (ACM MM) 2018. FInally, we studied the possibilities of collaborative AR in “CARS: Collaborative Augmented Reality for Socialization” published in the 19th International Workshop on Mobile Computing Systems & Applications (HotMobile) 2018. Furthermore, we proposed a mobile augmented reality real-time recommendation system that is also related to our framework. The paper was published with the title "ReadMe: A Real-Time Recommendation System for Mobile Augmented Reality Ecosystems" in ACM MM, a top conference in multimedia. We did not encounter any problems nor did we deviate from the original plan.

26211515.label: Major findings and research outcome
26211515.value: This project lead to the development of algorithms and methods for distributed reputation system. These methods targeted multiple areas, including networking and computations, user mobility, distributed computations, and incentive systems for crowdsourced computations. In the network and computation area, we focused on how can significant amounts of data be transferred to multiple external machines to be processed with low latency. We developed frameworks to distribute computations among multiple heterogeneous, ranging from dedicated cloud servers to nearby smartphones and other mobile devices. Each framework was focusing on a specific network or computational aspect, for instance, GPU computations, task scheduling and execution, device-to-device communication, mobile networks, and also less conventional methods such as NFC computation offloading. In the case of crowdsourced computations, user mobility is crucial to ensure the stability and scalability of the system. We thus analyzed multiple large-scale user mobility datasets, and derived models for exploiting user mobility within large-scale device-to-device computation clouds. These studies showed the feasibility of the proposed system. Finally, we studied how can one provide incentives for users to share their available resources with others. We developed several perspectives, ranging from auction systems for resource sharing, to crypto-currency-based payment schemes. The methods and insights developed during the project were applied to various applications, among which augmented reality (AR). Due to its strict constraints (constrained systems, high computational cost, large volumes of data, and extreme latency sensitivity), AR represents a good application case for the research performed over this project. After analyzing the constraints of AR applications and their integration in a mobile environment, we developed several frameworks and systems for computation offloading in AR to a wide array of heterogeneous devices.

26211515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26211515.value: Developing OpenRP lead to several new research questions and directions. First of all, developing such a system for large-scale crowd computing system proves to be challenging in real life. Most studies rely on either dataset studies or small-scale experiments on homogeneous hardware. However, to the best of our knowledge, there is no practical study on large-scale heterogeneous environment. We expect in such environments to encounter multiple physical limitations, related to both the execution environment, the heterogeneity of the devices, and the network behavior when connecting dozens of devices together. During the development of OpenRP, we used Augmented Reality as a use case for our algorithms and methods. This allowed to uncover multiple issues specific to AR applications. In particular, the extreme latency requirements of AR combined with the larges amounts of data to be transferred require specific attention. We also exposed numerous interaction issues with AR headsets, that we plan to explore in further works.

26211515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26211515.value: The rise in wearable devices with varying computational capabilities, numerous sensors and multiple options for communication open the door to a vast spectrum of applications that can collectively leverage these resources. On the other hand, some application require more resources than existing devices such as wearables can provide. A solution resides in offloading some of the computations to nearby devices. However, doing so requires trusting nearby devices to perform the required tasks. OpenRP is an ambitious middleware for any mobile application that need to evaluate the reputation of other mobile devices. OPENRP (i) utilizes low level components of the OS like the network modules and the embedded database, (ii) processes the information it collects, and (iii) exposes a set of operations to application developers in the form of an application programming interface. In this project, we developed a robust and truthful distributed reputation system and a scalable and lightweight communication protocol between mobile devices for information update. We implemented this system within an API for Android devices, and used Augmented Reality as a use case for our system.

26600915.label: Project Objectives

26600915.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26600915.value: Since the 1990s, two conspicuous political economic changes have coincided in Xinjiang: an unprecedented increase in oil and natural gas production, and an increasing number of violent confrontations related to Xinjiang’s largest ethnic minority, the Uighurs. Although a number of scholars have suggested potential links between natural resources and ethnic tensions, little systematic evidence has been presented to support a causal relationship. The proposed research aims to examine the causal impact of natural resource development, a major booster of Xinjiang’s regional economy in the past two decades, on ethnic grievances and violence in Xinjiang. To examine the causal impact of resource development on violence, we carefully test how oil and gas production have changed the political economic conditions across ethnicities that are closely related to ethnic violence. In particular, we focus on three potential changes in Xinjiang due to resource development, all of which have been discussed as causes of ethnic conflict: the change in ethnic composition, economic competition among ethnic groups and the quality of local governance. We claim that distinguishing between these mechanisms is important not only for academic purposes but also for policy implications, since each causal path suggests different practical implications in regard to the central government’s approach to ethnic violence and resource policies in Xinjiang. To analyze the mechanisms, we implement mixed methodology. To test the claims statistically, we plan to collect novel data on natural resource production including accurate location of all oil and gas fields and precise production information. We also incorporate vast data on demography, local government performance and economic development within the region. 自1990年代起，新疆同時經歷了兩個顯著的政治經濟變遷：一方面是石油和天然氣產量空前增長，另一方面是與新疆最大的少數民族（維吾爾族）相關的暴力對抗不斷增長。儘管諸多學者指出，自然資源和民族關係緊張之間存在潛在關聯，但極少有系統的證據來論證這一因果關係。本研究旨在探究自然資源開發，這一過去二十年裡新疆地區經濟主要的驅動力，對於民族衝突暴力的作用。為檢驗資源開發和暴力的因果關係，我們審慎地探究了石油和天然氣產量如何改變與民族暴力衝突緊密相關的政治經濟條件。具體而言，我們集中于新疆三個由於資源開發帶來的潛在變化，這些變化被視為是民族衝突的根源：民族構成的變化，不同民族之間的競爭，以及地方治理的狀況。區分這些機制之間的差異，不僅合乎學術旨趣，也有著政策意涵。每一個因果路徑，都闡釋著中央政府應對新疆民族衝突和資源政策的不同方略。為檢驗這些假設，我們計畫收集新穎的資料，包括新疆全部油田和氣田的具體產量，以及大量縣級層面的人口、地方政府績效、經濟發展等資料。

26600915.label: Realisation of objectives
26600915.value: Our main research question is whether resource extraction in Xinjiang has a deflating effect on ethnic violence. We also ask how historical cultural distinctions within this region interact with resource development. Together, these questions constitute an examination of the channels through which natural resources might affect Xinjiang’s level of ethnic confrontation, if at all. We hypothesize and empirically investigate four potential mechanisms debated in the existing literature on resource politics and civil conflict: outside investment, employment opportunities, quality of local institutions, and religious and cultural cleavages. To examine whether and how oil and gas production have affected levels of violence in Xinjiang, we collect novel field-level data on oil and gas production and reserves in Xinjiang along with detailed information on each of Xinjiang’s 86 counties. The data on natural resources include accurate locations of all oil and gas fields in the region, and precise production and proven reserve information from 1998 to 2005. Our violence data are incorporated from various academic and media sources. In order to measure historical, cultural and religious differences across counties, we collect mosque location information dating back to 1949 when Xinjiang was included in the People’s Republic of China. To further analyze the mechanism through which resource development affects ethnic contention in Xinjiang, we also collect geographic, demographic and socio-economic information at the micro-level, including individual-level census data. Methodologically, our approach enables us to circumvent potential endogeneity issues between the outcome - the location of violence - and the causes, which are the locations where resource extraction is occurring and the locations that stand out as culturally and religiously more distinctive. Building a causal relationship between causes and outcomes is a fundamental difficulty in violence research. For instance, low economic growth can be both a cause and a result of violence. Therefore, finding exogenous factors that affect violence but that are not affected by violence has been a major concern among scholars. The same difficulty exists with regard to religious identity and violence. It is hard to prove whether strong ethnic or religious identities intensify violence or vice versa. Our empirical analyses suggest that, contrary to the resource curse argument and popular expectations regarding Xinjiang’s violence, an increase in oil and gas production significantly decreases the probability of ethnic violence. Employing data on resource reserves, which are exogenous to previous violence or other confounding covariates, we confirm that natural resource endowments have significant negative effects on the occurrence of violence in Xin- jiang. Nevertheless, the mitigating effect of natural resources is conditional on the historical presence of Muslim religious sites. In counties with distinctive cultural and religious back- grounds instrumented by pre-1949 mosque density, the soothing effect of resource production dissipates. Through what mechanism does resource development reduce violent incidents? We find no evidence that the soothing effects of natural resources are driven by enhanced public security measures, nor by the emigration of ethnic minorities out of the resource producing areas. Our analyses show that local government security expenditures do not increase with resource production: no significant statistical association is found between resource production and total population, Han immigration or Uyghur emigration. Instead, we find that resource development provides important economic opportunities for the local population. Employment rates and individual-level income increase when a county produces more natural resources.

26600915.label: Major findings and research outcome
26600915.value: This study investigates the effects of oil and natural gas development on violent incidents in Xinjiang, China, using data from its 86 counties. Contrary to the resource curse claim, we find that areas with larger quantities of resource production have lower rates of violence. The analysis of reserves data confirms that this finding is not driven by endogeneity between violence and resource production. This soothing effect of resources subsides, however, in areas with high mosque density. While we find no supporting evidence for drastic ethno-demographic changes or strengthening of public security associated with resource extraction, the analysis shows that resource development contributes to local economic conditions, particularly to employment and SOE employees’ income. The outcome of this research is forthcoming in the British Journal of Political Science.

26600915.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26600915.value: While our analyses largely provide countering evidence to the resource curse claim, it is unclear what has driven the sharp changes in violent events for the past two decades, a period during which resource production has consistently increased and the distribution of religious sites has been stable. In addition, while we currently observe violent events less frequently compared to the late 1990s, we find that ethnic tensions remain high or have even been exacerbated in Xinjiang. These trends require further investigation regarding various socio-economic changes and the influence of external armed conflicts in countries adjacent to Xinjiang. Due to limited data access, it is possible that we are omitting a number of factors or mechanisms that may affect violence in Xinjiang. As our study represents one of the pioneering studies employing systematic data to study this region, many questions remain unanswered. We leave alternative mechanisms to be explored in future research.

26600915.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26600915.value: Our empirical analyses suggest that, contrary to the resource curse argument and popular expectations regarding Xinjiang’s violence, oil and gas production reduces ethnic violence in Xinjiang. We find the oil and gas production promotes peace through improving economic conditions such as local employment and SOE employees’ income. Nevertheless, we also find the peace-promoting effect of natural resources is smaller in areas with a high concentration of mosques, meaning historical, cultural, and religious distinctiveness plays a key role in deterring violence.

27103715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27103715.value: Accumulating evidence has shown that inhibitory synapses are not only plastic but also participate in modulating excitatory transmission and induce plasticity of excitatory synapses during learning. We previously demonstrated that dendritic spine plasticity was an important feature of fear associative learning in the frontal association cortex, but it is still unclear what mechanisms underlie such plasticity. Schizophrenia patients have interneuron deficits, loss of dendritic spines in the frontal cortex, and impaired fear associative learning. In view of the dendritic spine pathology and interneurons deficits in schizophrenia, we hypothesize that parvalbumin-expressing interneurons play an important role in mediating pyramidal neurons dendritic spine plasticity and lead to behavioral changes in fear associative learning. In this proposal, we aim to determine (1) the roles of parvalbumin-expressing interneuron in memory acquisition and consolidation of fear associative learning, and (2) the link between dendritic spine pathology and impaired fear associative learning in schizophrenia. First, we will investigate the short-term and long-term structural plasticity of pyramidal neurons and parvalbumin-expressing interneurons in the frontal association cortex by in vivo transcranial two-photon imaging in normal mice. Second, we will determine the roles of parvalbumin-expressing interneurons in the structural plasticity of the dendritic spines of pyramidal neurons in the frontal association cortex using optogenetics and the DREADD (Designer Receptors Exclusively Activated by Designer Drugs) system to activate or silence parvalbumin-expressing interneurons at memory acquisition and consolidation phases. Third, we will use an animal model of the genetic risk factors for schizophrenia (conditional knockout of ErbB4 in parvalbumin-expressing interneurons) to study baseline and fear associative learning-induced synaptic plasticity in the frontal association cortex. We will further manipulate the activity of parvalbumin-expressing interneurons with an aim to rescue the fear associative learning impairment phenotype in this animal model. Taken together, our study will provide important insights into the basic mechanisms of fear conditioning and the roles of parvalbumin-expressing interneurons in fear associative learning, which could help in the development of new therapeutics and prevention strategies for schizophrenia.

27105415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27105415.value: Time to treatment for acute myocardial infarction (AMI), commonly known as a heart attack, is essential for reducing mortality and morbidity. Pre-hospital delay, the time from onset of symptoms to arriving at hospital, is a common problem both locally and worldwide. Although the time between hospital arrival and treatment has shortened, pre-hospital delays have not improved. Patient delay and transport delay contribute to pre-hospital delay, but the former contributes the most. In Hong Kong, the reported median pre-hospital delay time ranges from 3 to 54 hours. Delayed hospital arrival is the most common reason for not receiving reperfusion treatment (e.g., thrombolytic therapy or primary percutaneous coronary intervention). Patient delay, the time from onset of symptoms to making the decision to seek professional medical care, depends on three factors: 1) recognising the symptoms of a heart attack, 2) correctly identifying the need for immediate professional medical care, and 3) taking appropriate action to seek emergency medical care. Patients with poor knowledge of AMI symptoms and/or who make inappropriate decisions in seeking medical care often prolong this delay; in particular, older people tend to experience longer delays. There is a pressing need to reduce the pre-hospital delay, particularly with a rapidly ageing local population. Before we can develop interventions, we need to investigate the likely decision processes of patients following the onset of AMI symptoms. In this study, we will identify socio-demographic and medical factors that can predict the expected level of knowledge of the symptoms of AMI and expected immediate treatment seeking behaviour of older Chinese in Hong Kong. The study will reveal misconceptions about AMI symptoms and treatment seeking behaviour. A cross-sectional population-based survey will be conducted to assess the knowledge of AMI symptoms and treatment seeking behaviour among Chinese aged 65 and above in Hong Kong. Cluster sampling will be used to randomly select six centres from the 18 Elderly Health Centres operated by the Department of Health. The participants will be interviewed by trained research assistants using a structured questionnaire developed for this study. The findings from this study will be used to facilitate the formulation of public education programmes to promote the correct perceptions about AMI symptoms and appropriate treatment seeking behaviour. The ultimate goal is to shorten the pre-hospital delay, which would decrease the mortality and morbidity rate and the disease burden of AMI. 就醫時間對急性心肌梗塞(俗稱心臟病發)的治癒尤其重要。可是無論在本港或是世界各地的急性心肌梗塞病人都延遲了送院時間。縱使醫院能縮短從到達醫院至得到治療的時間，但是院前的延遲並未得到改善。院前的延遲涉及病人及交通，而病人本身往往是延遲的主因。有研究指出本港急性心肌梗塞病人由病發至送院時間的中位數為3至54小時不等，而延遲送院是沒有施行再灌注治療(例如，溶栓治療或搭橋手術)的主因。 病人延遲由病發至決定尋求專業醫療支援的時間受三個因素影響：(1)能否察覺心臟病發的症狀；(2)正確識別需要立即尋求專業醫療；及(3)採取適當行動，以尋求緊急醫療照顧。對不認識急性心肌梗塞的症狀，和/或採取不適當求醫行為的病人而言，他們會有較長的延誤，長者往往有更長的延誤。本港的人口迅速老化，所以我們要迫切提早送院時間。我們要研究市民如果患上急性心肌梗塞時的預計決策過程，從而在日後設計相應的公眾教育計劃。 在這項研究中，我們將探討本港長者對急性心肌梗塞症狀的知識水平及預計即時尋求治療行為的相關因素(包括社會人口及病歷特徵)。這項研究將揭示本港長者對急性心肌梗塞症狀的誤解及不當預計尋求治療行為。我們會採用一個以人群為基礎的橫面研究調查，以評估本港65歲及以上的中國人對急性心肌梗塞的認識及預計的尋求治療行為。我們會以整群抽樣來隨機抽取衛生署轄下18間長者健康中心之中的6間中心。受訓後的研究助理將利用結構式問卷訪問參加者。 這項研究的結果將有助於制定公眾教育活動，以提昇公眾對急性心肌梗塞症狀的認識和提倡適當的尋求治療行為。最終的目標是提早送院時間，以降低死亡率和發病率，從而減低急性心肌梗塞對醫療及社會的負擔。

27105415.label: Realisation of objectives
27105415.value: We conducted a face-to-face structured questionnire survey among healthy elderly in Hong Kong to assess their level of knowledge of heart attack symptoms and expected health seeking behavior. A cross-sectional population-based survey was conducted at the Elderly Health Centres in Hong Kong from March to September 2016, with a sample of 1804 elderly. A manuscript is published in an international journal. All the three objectives have been achieved. In terms of misconception, we found that our survey respondents incorrectly expected a very high intensity of discomfort during heart attack. In fact, the chest pain intensity was reported to range from 2 to 10 (on a 0-10-point scale) among local AMI patients, indicating the possibility of mild pain. A false expectation of high-intensity discomfort (scoring at least 8/10) might lead to a longer delay in seeking treatment. In addition, many of the respondents did not recognize atypical symptoms, e.g. absence of chest pain. This would also lead to treatment delay of heart attack, as older people are more likely to have atypical symptoms of heart attack than younger ones. In terms of expected treatment seeking behaviour, we found that our respondents opted for calling ambulances in some possible heart attack scenarios but not scenarios with low pain intensity or in the absence of chest pain. The reasons claimed by the respondents were mostly the perception that the symptoms were not of cardiac origin. This also echoed with our findings in terms of the misconceptions. This finding indicates the need to educate the population before heart attack. In terms of predictors of poor knowledge of AMI symptoms and inappropriate expected treatment seeking behaviour, multiple logistic regression analysis indicated that age ≥75, male sex, lower education level, and absence of heart disease were associated with greater likelihood of poor knowledge of AMI symptoms. Furthermore, non-married status (i.e. single, widowed, and divorced), living with others, without hypertension, and poor knowledge of chest pain and neck pain as AMI symptoms were associated with greater likelihood of inappropriate expected treatment-seeking behaviour. Public education programs should target elderly populations that are more likely to have poor knowledge of heart attack symptoms and expected health-seeking behavior.

27105415.label: Major findings and research outcome
27105415.value: The findings were published in Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health (Chau et al., 2017). A total of 1804 participants were recruited at EHCs from March to September 2016 and completed the interview. Among them, chest pain (80.2%), palpitations (75.8%), and fainting (71.9%) were the major symptoms recognised as AMI-related. Meanwhile, stomach ache (46.9%), coughing (45.4%), and neck pain (40.8%) were recognised as not AMI-related. One-third of respondents recognised at least five of the common symptoms reported among Hong Kong AMI patients. About 33.0% of participants perceived chest pain as the key sign of AMI onset. The mean expected discomfort intensity during AMI onset was 7.7 out of 10 (SD=2.1). For 24.4% of respondents, the expected discomfort intensity score was 8 or 9, and 20.4% expected the highest intensity pain, of 10. Regarding the expected treatment-seeking behaviour, seeking non-emergent medical care was the most popular action when AMI symptoms emerged during the day, without chest pain or with lower discomfort intensity, whereas calling an ambulance was the most common option when AMI symptoms emerged at night or with high discomfort intensity. Only 25.6% of respondents opted for calling an ambulance in at least three scenarios.

27105415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27105415.value: This project has led to the successful award of a Impact Project Proposal under the Knowledge Exchange Funding Exercise. Our project, named "Raising the knowledge level on heart attack symptoms and appropriate health seeking behavior among the elderly" aimed to raise the knowledge level on heart attack symptoms and appropriate health seeking behavior for elderly in Hong Kong by disseminating health education through video. The video reached over 12,400 older people and their family caregivers during the month of screening in the 18 Elderly Health Centers in Hong Kong. The audience participated in the evaluation study showed positive feedback towards the video, and their knowledge on heart attack symptoms and anticipated health-seeking behaviour was improved as compared to the statistics reported in our ECS project. The audience now understood that apart from chest pain, there were other symptoms that were related to heart attack. They also learned that calling ambulance was the most appropriate immediate action. The video was also uploaded to the website of the HKU School of Nursing to reach a wider audience.

27105415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27105415.value: Patients with heart attack need a timely medical treatment, and early presentation in hospital is essential to reduce morbidity and mortality. However, pre-hospital delay of heart attack is common globally. We conducted a study among healthy elderly to assess their level of knowledge of heart attack symptoms and expected health seeking behavior. A cross-sectional population-based survey was conducted in Hong Kong from March to September 2016, with a sample size of 1804. Our study identified many areas that the elderly have misconceptions or knowledge gap. Only one-third of our respondents could recognize at least five of the common heart attack symptoms, and many failed to recognize atypical symptoms. Moreover, near half of our respondents expected dramatic pain intensity during heart attack If patients are not aware of various symptoms, they are less likely to notice heart attack and thus may delay treatment. Our respondents opted for calling ambulances as expected immediate action in some possible heart attack scenarios but not scenarios with low pain intensity or in the absence of chest pain. These findings indicated the need to educate the elderly population as they are more likely to have poor knowledge of heart attack symptoms and health-seeking behavior.

27119715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27119715.value: Normal brain function requires the proper formation and development of synapses. Excitatory synapses are located primarily on specialized protrusions on the dendritic arbors of neurons called dendritic spines. The maturation and stability of dendritic spines is driven by growth factor and synaptic activity and depends on synthesis of new proteins. Interestingly, protein synthesis in neuron does not only occur in the cell body but also happens locally near synapses. To achieve synaptic protein synthesis, mRNAs need to be transported from cell body to the dendrites by specific RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) through the molecular motor kinesin. To understand the molecular mechanisms behind dendritic spine development, a fundamental question is to ask whether and how extrinsic stimuli regulate these RBPs and motor proteins, and hence the mRNA trafficking and local protein synthesis. Despite its clear importance in synaptic function, the molecular mechanisms that control dendritic mRNA trafficking remain largely unexplored. One potential regulatory mechanism for RBPs and motor proteins involves post-translational modification. Whereas phosphorylation by kinases represents the most-studied form of protein modification, emerging studies reveal many other ways by which proteins are post-translationally modified. However, many of these modifications are poorly characterized in neuron and their functional significance remains elusive. One post-translational protein modification involves the addition of methyl group on arginine residues, and is catalyzed by the enzymes protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMTs). The study of arginine methylation has been mostly focused on the modification of proteins inside the nucleus during regulation of gene expression and splicing. Our preliminary data revealed that PRMT5 and PRMT8 were unexpectedly present in distal dendrites and synapses in neurons. We further found that the dendritic RBP Staufen1 and the kinesin protein KIF5B are arginine methylated. These observations prompt us to hypothesize that PRMT-mediated arginine methylation might represent a novel mechanism to control dendritic mRNA trafficking during dendritic spine development. In the proposed study, we will examine the effect of depletion of specific PRMTs on dendritic spine morphogenesis. Moreover, the PRMT-mediated arginine methylation of Staufen1 and KIF5B at synapses will be investigated. We will elucidate the morphological and functional consequences in neurons with aberrant arginine methylation of Staufen1 and KIF5B. Given the emerging importance of neuronal RBPs and dendritic protein synthesis in synapse function, and the link of their dysregulation in various brain diseases, the proposed study should substantially increase the current knowledge on the cell biology of neurons under both normal and diseased states.

27119715.label: Realisation of objectives
27119715.value: Objective 1 To examine the synaptic localization of different protein arginine methyltransferases (PRMTs) in the brain, we prepared synaptoneurosome (SNS) mouse brains and analyze the expression of various PRMTs by Western blot. Among the six PRMTs that were examined, PRMT5 and PRMT8 showed considerable expression in the SNS. Importantly, we found that PRMT8 expression was significantly increased from postnatal day 7 (P7) to P14 and peaked at P21 in the hippocampus in vivo. This coincides with the period of spine maturation during which the abundance of filopodia declines. PRMT8 expression also increased in dissociated hippocampal neurons upon maturation, and its expression was significantly reduced by blockade of action potential with tetrodotoxin. Immunostaining revealed that endogenous PRMT8 existed as distinct puncta on dendrites of dissociated hippocampal neurons, and almost 30% of the PRMT8 puncta showed overlap with the postsynaptic protein PSD-95). To confirm the postsynaptic localization of PRMT8, we generated a GFP-tagged PRMT8 expression construct. Upon transfection into hippocampal neurons, the PRMT8-GFP appeared as discrete puncta along dendrites, and ~41% of the puncta were present in dendritic spine heads. In contrast, although protein arginine methylation is a major regulatory mechanism in the nucleus, the PRMT8-GFP expressed in neuron was not enriched in the nucleus. The control of spine morphology depends heavily on the re-organization of filamentous actin (F-actin). We found that ~15% PRMT8-GFP puncta in dendrites partially overlapped with the phalloidin-positive F-actin-rich hot spots. To elucidate the relationship between PRMT8 subcellular localization and F-actin, hippocampal neurons were co-transfected with PRMT8-GFP and mCherry-LifeAct, which encodes a peptide preferentially binds to F-actin, followed by time-lapse confocal imaging. Interestingly, the amount of PRMT8-GFP was significantly reduced over time in dendritic spines undergoing actin polymerization. These findings suggest that PRMT8 might play a crucial role for dendritic spine maturation by negatively regulating actin polymerization locally at dendritic spines. Objective 2 In this objective, we characterize the methylation of putative substrates involved in neuronal transport. By performing knockdown and rescue experiments in dissociated hippocampal neurons followed by confocal imaging or electrophysiology, we demonstrate that two homologous kinesin I motor proteins, KIF5A and KIF5B, have distinct functions, with KIF5B specifically involved in the maintenance of mushroom spines and excitatory synaptic transmission. FMRP, a dendritic RNA-binding protein (RBP) depleted in fragile-X syndrome, preferentially binds to KIF5B, and depletion of the two kinesin individually leads to differential effect on FMRP trafficking and localization of Camk2a mRNA, a FMRP cargo. Through the construction of KIF5A/KIF5B chimera, we delineate the last 23 amino acids at the carboxyl-terminus confer the functional specificity of KIF5B. Within the RGG motif of this region contains two arginine residues (R-941 and R-956), which are not present in KIF5A. We have confirmed the arginine methylation of KIF5B but not KIF5A when heterogeneously expressed in 293T cells. Using reciprocal immunoprecipitation with antibodies that recognize the mono-arginine methylation or KIF5B, we confirmed that KIF5B was methylated in the SNS. We substituted the two arginine residues to histidine by site-directed mutagenesis, which retain the positive charges of the residues but do not undergo methylation. Arginine methylation was completely abolished in the double mutant (R941/956H), indicating that R-941 and R-956 are two major methylation sites of KIF5B. Pull-down assay of the GST-fusion protein of KIF5B with various PRMTs detect strong interaction between KIF5B and PRMT1 or PRMT5. In vitro methylation assay confirmed the induction of KIF5B mono-arginine methylation by PRMT1. Our findings identify a previously uncharacterized functional specificity between two closely homologous kinesin motors, which is determined by the short carboxyl-terminus of KIF5B where a RGG motif is present that undergoes arginine methylation. We also determine whether PRMT8 regulates the function of RBPs that transport and regulate the translation of dendritic mRNAs. Through immunoprecipitation and Western blot with methylation-specific antibodies, we found that Staufen1 was arginine-methylated in the SNS. However, Staufen1 did not bind to PRMT8. Instead, we identified the two other dendritic RBPs, namely G3BP1 and G3BP2, by mass spectrometry as PRMT8-interacting proteins. We therefore study G3BP1 instead of Staufen1 in order to elucidate the role of arginine methylation of dendritic RBP in spine morphogenesis. G3BP1 was dimethylated in the SNS, and the methylation was significantly reduced in Prmt8 homozygous knockout brains or cultured neurons, indicating that PRMT8 is a major methyltransferase of G3BP1. The arginine methylation was completely abolished when both R433 and R445 in the RGG motif were substituted to histidine, thereby identifying the major methylated sites on G3BP1. Reduced amount of proteins were pulled down from mouse brain homogenate by the FLAG-tagged methylation-deficient (R433/445H) G3BP1 compared to wild-type counterpart, indicating that arginine methylation of G3BP1 is crucial to regulate its protein-protein interactions. Objective 3 We performed multiple experiments to support an essential role of PRMT8 on dendritic spine maturation. Knockdown of PRMT8 by shRNA leads to significant increase in the number of filopodia and reduction of mushroom spines. By generating the methyltransferase-deficient mutant through substituting Gly-121 by Ala or the nuclear-restricted variant through the addition of nuclear-localization signal (NLS) for rescue experiments, we have demonstrated that PRMT8 promotes spine maturation through catalysis of arginine methylation and the effect is not explained by its nuclear function. The role of PRMT8 on spine maturation was validated by neurons isolated from Prmt8 knockout mice. Furthermore, CA1 hippocampal neurons of adult Prmt8 homozygous knockout mice exhibit longer spines, and the mice display anxiolytic behaviors in open field test and elevated plus maze, indicating the function of PRMT8 in spine morphogenesis and cognitive functions in vivo. Notably, Rac1-PAK signaling is over-activated in PRMT8 knockout brain, which is coupled with increased phosphorylation of the actin-depolymerization factor cofilin and elevated F-actin to G-actin ratio. We further performed photobleaching after recovery (FRAP) on mCherry-LifeAct to demonstrate reduction of F-actin turnover in dendritic spines of PRMT8-knockdown or knockout neurons. Importantly, knockdown of G3BP1 mimicked the over-abundance of filopodia and the reduction of synaptic actin turnover, and both phenotypes can only be reversed by wild-type G3BP1 but not the methylation-deficient variant. Pharmacological inhibition of PAK1 completely abolished the immature spine phenotypes induced by PRMT8-shRNA or G3BP1-shRNA, indicating that elevated PAK kinase activity is responsible for the spine maturation defects. Our findings uncover PRMT8 and G3BP1 as key regulators of synaptic actin dynamics by keeping the Rac1-PAK signaling under control PRMT8, and indicate arginine methylation of dendritic RBP as a novel mechanism for synapse maturation To ask whether arginine methylation affects KIF5B function, we performed pull-down experiments using the FLAG-tagged wild-type or methylation-deficient mutant (R941/956H) of KIF5B. The amount of FMRP pulled down by the methylation-deficient mutant was significantly reduced when compared to wild-type KIF5B. To address whether arginine methylation is required for the synaptic function of KIF5B, we compared the activity of wild-type and methylation-deficient mutant in the formation of mushroom spines using the KIF5B-shRNA rescue experiments in dissociated hippocampal neurons. Co-expression of wild-type, but not the methylation-deficient KIF5B, reversed the loss of mushroom spines induced by KIF5B-shRNA. Whole-cell patch recording also revealed that co-expression of wild-type, not the methylation-deficient KIF5B, with the KIF5B-shRNA significantly increased the mEPSC frequency. These results indicate that arginine methylation at the carboxyl-terminus is essential for KIF5B function on dendritic spine development and synaptic transmission, and suggests a mechanism through regulating binding to cargoes such as FMRP.
