27615515.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27615515.value: In 1859, writer E. S. Dallas predicted that by the end of the century literary authors would die out and be replaced entirely by journalists. Dallas was not alone in this belief, and many of his contemporaries worried about the social transformations that such a shift could bring. In an 1854 letter, novelist Anthony Trollope called even the Times a “tyrant” and blamed it for the public malaise surrounding the Crimean War. My project focuses on the competition between the novel and the newspaper in shaping a growing reading public and its relationship to a national imaginary. This project will trace novelistic depictions of the modern newspaper across the second half of the nineteenth century. In particular, I will examine how serial novelists critiqued the ways in which the popular press modeled the expanded reading public. Although published in serial format, mainstream novels resisted imagining national identity in terms parallel to the market, where members of the public are exchangeable and replaceable. Instead, the novelists I examine privileged a liberal approach to the public, which valorizes the individual’s participation in a shared public sphere. The project will focus on novelistic sub-genres that have been commonly associated with news-- realism and sensationalism—and will include canonical authors like Anthony Trollope, Charles Dickens, and Wilkie Collins, as well as non-canonical writers like Israel Zangwill and George W. M. Reynolds. A core case in my project features the feud between Charles Dickens and George W. M. Reynolds, a popular writer and editor of working-class publications. Contemporary critics often conflate Dickens with the growing mass media, because he embraced a celebrity status and participated in the commodification of his novels. However, he shaped much of his career in opposition to Reynolds, even founding his popular journal, Household Words, as a moral and social corrective to Reynolds. Dickens marked off artistic creation as a space of ownership and fought for copyright legislation; Reynolds made his reputation on plagiarisms of Dickens and treated creative, fictional writing as part of the open market. Whereas Dickens claimed a difference between journalistic and creative writing, Reynolds’s actions refused this distinction and treated “literary” writing no differently than journalism. This project will explore the extent to which Dickens, Reynolds, and a number of other Victorian authors are influenced by their imaginations of a national public. 傳達「英國性」：維多利亞時期小說與報章中的民族認同 作家E. S. Dallas曾在1895年預測，到十九世紀末，文學作家將全部被新聞記者所取代。同時代的其他作家也有類似的擔心，認為社會轉型將會導致這一趨勢。小說家Anthony Trollope在1854年的一封書信中，甚至將《泰晤士報》稱為「暴君」，指責其在克裡米亞戰爭問題上給社會帶來的不安。 本研究聚焦於小說與報章在塑造崛起的公眾讀者群體過程中的競爭，以及二者和民族想像的相互關係。本項目將追蹤十九世紀後半葉小說對現代報章的描寫。特別是，本人將仔細研究連載小說家如何批判主流媒體對不斷擴充的讀者群體進行的塑造。雖然主流小說多以連載形式出現在紙媒上，但卻拒絕與大眾市場對民族認同的勾勒保持一致，因而讀者群體是不斷變動轉換的。相反，本研究所涵蓋的小說家對讀者取向持較為開放的態度，從而穩定並維持了個體讀者在公共領域的參與。本項目的主要研究對象為與新聞特性相關的小說次文類─寫實主義與感覺主義，並將對權威作家，如Anthony Trollope、 Charles Dickens， 以及 Wilkie Collins，和非權威作家Israel Zangwill 及 George W. M. Reynolds進行剖析。 本研究項目將對Charles Dickens 與暢銷作家、工人階級出版物編輯 George W. M. Reynolds 的對立進行主要案例分析。Dickens 與大眾傳媒的結盟受到當代評論家的熱議，因為他利用自己名人化的趨勢，促使其文學作品商品化。然而，Dickens將自己的文學生涯對立於Reynolds，並創辦了頗受歡迎的週刊《家庭文學》（Household Words），以此作為對Reynolds 的道德與社會矯正。Dickens認為藝術創作應有歸屬，並為建立著作權保護制度不斷奔走，成為倡導版權立法的先驅。Reynolds 則認為創意及小說寫作應屬自由市場，從而通過效法Dickens 的作品而使自己名聲大噪。雖然Dickens 將新聞寫作與創意寫作嚴格劃分，但Reynolds 的行為卻與之相對，將二者並為一談。本研究將重點探索Dickens、 Reynolds及其他維多利亞時期作家，受到他們對民族想像的影響程度。

27615515.label: Realisation of objectives
27615515.value: This project generated an article and a book monograph that fulfill the objectives outlined in the original application. The article, called “‘Our Impending Doom’: Seriality’s End in Late-Victorian Proto-Dystopian Novels,” examines utopian/dystopian time and serial form in several late-nineteenth-century proto-dystopian novels, including Anthony Trollope’s The Fixed Period, James De Mille’s A Strange Manuscript in a Copper Cylinder, and H. G. Wells’s The Time Machine. Through mingling the futuristic orientation of utopias and the presentist cause-and-effect experience of serial form, late nineteenth-century dystopias do not set these other worlds in the distant future; rather, they ask readers to see signs of their mortality in the everyday. In doing so, these paradoxical temporalities combine to highlight the finiteness of late-Victorian institutions in the face of more expansive depictions experience. The article is part of a special issue on seriality of the Journal of Modern Periodical Studies, and it rethinks the role of seriality in the late-Victorian novel and its relationship to nationalism and subjectivity. My book manuscript, Plotting the News: Nation and Newspaper in the Victorian Novel, is complete and under review with an international university press. This monograph is about the ways that nineteenth-century novels envision newspapers and incorporate, problematize, and transmute news stories into fictional narrative. By fictionalizing a discourse that lays claim to factuality, the novels examined in this book interrogate the operations of “narratives of the real” and their effects on a community of readers. Fictional narrative serves as a form of media theory; novelists deploy the news in varying ways in order to explore the types of individuation and communal formation enabled by an expanding and diversifying newspaper press. By experimenting with the narrative operation of the newspaper, the novel also undergoes a process of formation as it tests out the ways that texts can function. Victorian novelists thus emerge as early media theorists, thinking through the contrasting (and sometimes overlapping) systems of reality offered by newspapers and novels. This means that nineteenth-century novelistic form partly is a self-conscious practice of experimentation and re-creation, a generative process that is particularly salient in representations and mediations of the newspaper. I draw my examples from novelists such as Charles Dickens, Anthony Trollope, Mary Elizabeth Braddon, Wilkie Collins, George Eliot, and Anglo-Jewish writer Israel Zangwill. This monograph is called, “Plotting the News,” because it traces the ways that Victorian novels experimented with news discourse by refashioning and injecting it into varying kinds of plots and modalities, from the bildungsroman to melodrama to the Anglo-Jewish novel. However, this monograph could also be titled, “Analogizing the News,” since these novelists conceived the news through metaphors and analogies as a means of theorizing its formal and social workings. Novelists across the nineteenth century cultivated a variety of analogies for the newspaper press, including “acres of print,” a “corps of scribblers,” Mt. Olympus, an “ever-whirling wheel,” and, perhaps most familiar to readers today, “the fourth estate.” Newspapers claimed, in some form, to represent the nation (or fragments of that nation), and novels interrogated this representative claim through metaphorical and narrative logic. Critics have long charged that the realism of the Victorian serial novel worked alongside the newspaper to produce and control the nation. Among the most prominent voices in this tradition are thinkers as various as Franco Moretti, D. A. Miller, Linda Hughes and Michael Lund, and, most famously, Benedict Anderson. In Anderson’s account, the novel and the newspaper served as “the technical means for ‘re-presenting’ the kind of imagined community that is nation,” both as formal analogues and as a means for “thinking” nation. However, this book argues that, while nineteenth-century novelists do recognize a powerful link between the news and the formation of national community, they sharply distinguish between news and novel. Representing newspapers as fraudulent, libelous, and deceitful, the novel exposes the ways that newspapers represent the fictiveness of national imagining. Victorian novels thus emerge as an early form of media theory, thinking through the contrasting systems of reality offered by newspapers and novels. They emphasize the fictiveness of the news and invite readers to re-examine the operations of realistic narratives, thus interrupting the apparent immanence of nation and community. They do so at the level of representation, in scenes of newspaper reading, writing, and circulation, as well as at the level of style, narrative, and characterization. The novel both incarnates and represents ways of interrogating national and communal affiliations, showing that an individual’s connection to nation is one of constant self-examination and revision. On the one hand, as I will show, novelistic form shares some of the paradoxes of journalism, making the depiction of news and newspapers an important site for self-reflexive formal experimentation. On the other hand, novels feature newspapers that restrict the social experiences of characters and communities. Fictional iterations of the newspaper and other print media create breakages and disruptions in plot and narrative that then require the novel to rework itself into an adapted form. Thus, the novels in this monograph constantly interrogate the ways that print media shape communities. This monograph clearly engages with the objectives of the original application, particularly objectives 1, 2, and 3. Objective 4 is addressed throughout the chapters. For instance, Chapter 1, called “‘These Acres of Print’: Charles Dickens, the News, and the Novel as Pattern,” shows the growing distinction that Dickens drew between fiction and nonfiction, novel and newspaper, in his communal visions for serial publication. In doing so, I look to Dickens’s anxieties surrounding the writings of popular writer and editor, George W. M. Reynolds. Chapter 3, “‘The End is No Longer Hidden’: News, Fate, and the Sensation Novel,” examines the sensation novel, a sub-genre known for fast-paced plots drawn from real life.

27615515.label: Major findings and research outcome
27615515.value: As I indicated in 5.3, this project has yielded an article (accepted for publication) and a book manuscript (under review) that show the importance of news discourse to the nineteenth-century novel. When nineteenth-century novels incorporate newspapers and news stories into their fictional narratives, they play with the lines between fact and fiction. This book suggests that novelistic depictions of newspapers represent a continued project of articulating and theorizing narrative realisms. The novels in this monograph represent and analyze news in ways that critique the operations of the press and the structure and form of the newspaper. The newspaper’s claim to reality is multifaceted, both inherent to its generic and formal structure as well as the implication that it refers to external events. Yet it also varies across newspapers and even particular genres within the newspaper. I argue that novelistic realism emerges in tension with the newspaper’s own brands of the real. George Levine has called realism a “process” rather than a concrete genre, and he claims that nineteenth-century novelists “were already self-conscious about the nature of their medium.” Realists were responding to changes in their environment and engaging with ways to “reorganize experience and reinvest it with value.” I argue that part of this process of realism entails a complication and, at times, dismantling of the newspaper’s claims to the real. In this sense, these novelists are neither naïvely mimetic nor repressively totalizing in their representation of a real world; instead, they narrativize competing discourses of the real as a means of evaluating these realist claims and encouraging readers to become similarly conscious readers. The novel’s preoccupation with news highlights its own formal tensions and processes.

27615515.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27615515.value: This project opens up opportunities for theorizing serial form more extensively, in ways that are less engaged with nation and more with affect and feeling. Recent scholarship on nineteenth-century serial form tends to highlight a text’s materiality, regularity, and immediacy. The term “serial form” means the text’s production and consumption on a calendrical basis. By contrast, I am now working on a paper that argues for another understanding of serial form, one that refocuses attention on novelistic form and aesthetics. I will argue that Anthony Trollope’s serial form involves characters, plots, and settings functioning as part of a series of repetitions that reappear, with subtle differences, across his novels. In doing so, serial form invites affective retrospection and anticipation, thereby blurring the lines between past and future. This essay has developed out of my research for Plotting the News and promises to make a significant contribution to work on serial form and nineteenth-century literature. I plan to submit it to an international journal in the next few months.

27615515.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27615515.value: Plotting the News is a timely project, as we live in a world characterized by allegations of “fake news.” Newspapers are constantly lying in the worlds of Victorian novels, from the false report of John Harmon’s death in Our Mutual Friend (1864-1865) to allegations of extra- marital affairs in Phineas Finn (1867-1868). Yet characters continue to believe what they read in the newspaper, assuming that news must be recent, relevant, and true. Victorian novels thus explore the contradictory logic of news: claims to journalistic reality sit uneasily alongside unrepresentative, malicious, or even false news. This book argues that nineteenth-century novels analyzed the formal and social workings of news through a shifting series of metaphors, analogies, and plots. By incorporating newspapers and news discourse into their narratives, Victorian novels experimented with the ways that generic and formal qualities might reshape communal and national imaginings.

28200215.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28200215.value: 一種基於案例的複雜圖紋統一生成架構

28200215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28200215.value: 研究摘要 圖紋，作為一種重複或關聯部分、基本圖案等的佈置，在天然或人造物件中，廣泛地存在。在自然界中，圖紋的作用是促進生長、保護個體免受攻擊等。在大多數人造物件的例子中，圖紋的作用主要是發揮裝飾效果。就是因為有了多種多樣的圖紋才使我們的生活變得多姿多彩，有吸引力，甚至驚艷。不驚訝地，人們本能地喜愛創作圖紋。這也是為什麼圖紋能夠跨越所有民族，廣泛地存在於各個國家和地區的原因。然而，對於沒有接受過任何藝術訓練的新手來說，圖紋設計通常不是一項簡單的任務。在古代，圖紋設計和生產的手藝是經師傅傳給徒弟的。甚至當今，迪士尼和其他動畫公司都只僱傭專業人士來從事電影製作中的圖紋創作。計算機輔助圖紋生成，能夠很大程度地幫助新手設計圖紋，也因此成為了計算機與工程界一個熱門的研究課題。 大量圖紋生成方面的工作已經出現在文獻中，它們中的絕大多數可被歸類為兩個主要部件：生成規則和規則被應用的重複元素。例如，一個圖或基本圖案可以被由反射、旋轉和平移構成的17 種裝飾設計方式挪動過平面 [1]。過程式方法如L 系統用文法編碼植物的規則結構，每條文法代表一條控制結構變換的生成規則 [2]。給定一個展示紋理要素的小圖紋，合成方法能夠生成具有相同特性的較大紋理 [3]。儘管以前的方法能夠產生令人愉快的結果，然而他們的生成規則是為對應的元素專門設計的，並且這些元素通常是由用戶預先簡單指定的。 這項研究的目的是提議一種統一生成架構來生成複雜圖紋，例如圓形文化圖紋、抽象藝術作品、及花壇圖紋等，正如圖1、圖4、及圖5分別闡明的。以前的方法有兩個原因不能處理該類圖紋：（1）該類圖紋中的元素可以是任何形狀的形式；且（2）元素被集結在一起，卻沒有清晰的規則。我們的方法有兩個主要階段：圖紋分析和圖紋合成。通過分析，我們為複雜圖紋找到高階和統一的表示。因此，新的圖紋可以通過結構變形和元素填充來合成。

28200615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28200615.value: One of the new features that characterised continuing urban transformation in both global north and south in the recent decade has been the emergence of a knowledge-based economy, consisting of high-tech industries, producer services, and creative industries, as the new source of energy and locomotive for urban growth in an increasingly competitive global economy. Economic prosperity brought about by the active pursuit of creativity-led and innovation-based development strategies has been, however, accompanied by a widening gap between the rich and poor, the knowledgeable and uneducated, and the privileged and disadvantaged. To date, however, little research has been done to systematically investigate the link between knowledge-based urban economic restructuring and uneven income distribution in emerging economies of the global south. Existing studies of the changing dynamics of urban economic growth are focused overwhelmingly upon the sources and origins of enhanced urban competitiveness to the relative neglect of its implications for social equity. The rich literature on inequality determinants in urban China has made little reference to China’s ongoing structural transformation towards a knowledge-based economy. Theoretical inquiry into social transformation in global cities has shed little light over the social process in ordinary cities off the global city map. Noticeable gaps and missing links are apparent in the existing literature. This proposed research will investigate the pattern and process of inter-city differences in income inequality in urban China since the early 2000s when the knowledge-based sectors experienced dramatic expansion in Chinese economy. It will conduct systematic quantitative analysis to examine the relationship between the uneven development of knowledg-based economy and the change of income distribution in Chinese cities at prefectural level and above. The project will contribute new knowledge for our better understanding and evaluation of new urban competitive strategy and facilitate better policy making for managing and planning an equitable growth for the Chinese urban economy that will be of direct relevance to the strategic interests of Hong Kong economically and academically. 近几十年来全球城市转变的一大新特征无疑是包括高新技术产业、生产性服务业以及创意产业等知识型经济的兴起及其在日益激烈的竞争环境下推动城市经济增长的引擎作用。但是基于创意和创新的城市发展战略在推动经济繁荣的同时也带来了贫富之间、不同知识背景的阶层之间以及城市精英和弱势群体之间不断加大的收入差距。迄今，很少有研究来系统地探讨发展中国家基于知识型经济的城市战略转型与城市内部收入差距之间的因果关系。已有的城市经济增长动力机制的研究主要聚焦于城市竞争力的源泉而相对忽视了其对社会公平的意义。众多探讨中国城市收入差距决定因素的研究很少会考虑面向知识型经济的战略转型因素。而对全球城市社会转型的研究则主要聚焦于少数几个位于全球城市金字塔尖的少数城市，而较少关注全球城市地图之外的大量一般城市。现有的文献中存在显而易见的知识漏洞。 本研究分析新世纪以来在知识型经济不断扩张的背景下中国城市内部收入差距的区域分异模式和过程。通过对地级及以上城市定量数据的系统分析来揭示知识型经济的非均衡性及其与城市收入差距的关系。本项目将有利于我们更深入地了解和评估新城市经济竞争策略，为制定包容和公平的城市增长方针提供政策建议，对处在致力于发展知识型经济的香港有着重要的学术和实践意义。

28200615.label: Realisation of objectives
28200615.value: Objective 1 has been successfully accomplished through the collection and analysis of three sets of data: 1) the average wage of on-post staff and workers across industries in 35 major Chinese cities covering municipalities directly under the central government, provincial capital cities, and quasi-provincial capital cities in China during the period of 2003-2013; 2) the average wage of urban workers across industries in 30 provinces/provincial-level units during the period of 2003-2015; 3) individual-level data coming from 2013 China household Income Project (CHIP) containing rich and detailed data about income and other information of individuals in urban area. Following the original plan of research methodology, three indexes, namely coefficient of variation, gini coefficient and Theil index, are calculated to measure the pattern and process of inter-city differences in industry-based wage inequality in urban China, based on the first and second set of data. Similar indexes are also calculated for the surveyed cities based on the third set of data. My careful analysis of these cross-city data through descriptive and decomposition analysis has generated novel research findings submitted for publication in internationally refereed journals (See Research Outcome and Research Output below for details) Objective 2 has been accomplished satisfactorily as originally conceived. Regression models have been estimated based on both panel data during 2003-2013 and the cross-sectional data in 2013. Defining the development of knowledge-based economy as the employment share of 7 1-digit sectors in broad sense and 5 1-digit sectors in narrow sense, modelling analysis has been undertaken to quantify the relationship between the development of knowledge-based economy and the change of income distribution in Chinese cities, controlling for a series of city-level factors that may exacerbate or ameliorate the inequality impact of knowledge-based sectors. My research has generated important findings on the determinants of urban inequality in China undergoing the proclaimed transition to a knowledge-based economy. Overall, I am quite satisfied with the results of my research as what I have originally planned.

28200615.label: Major findings and research outcome
28200615.value: This project has generated several important findings, some of which have been submitted to internationally refereed journals or presented in international conferences and others in the pipeline of submission and publication. My research findings include: 1. There existed considerable inter-city differences in wage inequality. All the industry-based wage inequality indicators display a similar pattern of change characterized by a rise in the early years after 2003, reaching a peak in 2009 before showing a declining trend thereafter. 2. Within-sector inequality was more important than between-sector inequality in shaping the evolution of China’s urban wage inequality during 2003-2015. 3. Cities with a higher share of employment in knowledge-intensive sectors are more likely to exhibit higher level of wage inequality, controlling for a series of city-level independent variables. 4. The growth and expansion of knowledge-based sectors has gradually stepped up their impact on both within-sector and between-sector inequality since 2003. 5. Urban wage inequality within knowledge-based sectors was mainly brought about by the spatial concentration of a disproportionate number of high-paid jobs in a few developed, first-tier city-regions in the eastern coast. 6. Chinese cities with more globalized development of producer service economy exhibit higher level of income inequality. Global centrality of Chinese cities has significantly positive impact on the wage of professionals, employees with post-graduate degree and those working in knowledge-intensive producer service sectors at the relative expense of ordinary workers, workers without a college degree and those in consumer service sectors. 7. Unlike the situation in the western context where the decline of manufacturing employment contributed to enlarged urban inequality, manufacturing sector has been found to exhibit significantly positive impact on China’s urban wage inequality mainly because of its low-end nature relying on cheap labor costs. 8. The strength of state-owned enterprises in urban industrial output, the size of urban public sector and the share of urban fiscal expenditure on social welfare, all display significantly negative effects on urban wage inequality 9. Policy suggestions to ameliorate the impact of knowledge-based sector on urban income inequality can be made from between-sector and within-sector aspects. From between-sector aspect, attention should be paid to the low-level average wage of manufacturing workers and policy initiatives that can enhance the wage of industrial workers should be encouraged to narrow down its wage gap with knowledge-sector. From a within-sector perspective, policy efforts could be made to promote the development of knowledge-based sectors in central and western regions in order to reduce the inter-regional wage gap within knowledge-intensive sectors.

28200615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28200615.value: Two important issues lying beyond the scope of this research project are believed to have significant potentials for future research. First, this research has used the employment share of producer or creative sectors in urban employment to measure the uneven growth of a knowledge-based economy in urban China. Further research may use Research and Development input and output indicators such as R&D personnel, new product output and number of patent applications and granted patents and so on to explore the impact of innovation as an important dimension of knowledge-based economy on urban inequality in China. Second, this research has mainly employed quantitative and modelling analysis of statistical or survey data to examine the pattern of association between knowledge-based sectors and urban inequality. Further research may choose some knowledge-based sectors in typical Chinese cities for case study or comparative analysis in order to probe into the mechanisms through which the development of knowledge economy brings about enlarged urban wage inequality.

28200615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28200615.value: This research investigates the relationship between knowledge-based economy and the pattern and process of income inequality in urban China since the early 2000s. The growth and expansion of knowledge-based sectors is found to exhibit a significant and positive impact on industry-based wage inequality, controlling for a series of city-level factors. The impact of knowledge-based sectors is reflected in both its gap in average wage with other economic sectors and the inter-regional wage gap within knowledge-based sectors. Chinese cities with more globalized development of producer service economy tend to display higher levels of wage inequality. Contrary to the popular perception of de-industrialization as the main cause of urban inequality in the west, the presence of sizable manufacturing sector is found to be associated with enlarged urban wage inequality. The strength of the Chinese state in industrial ownership, public employment provision and social service expenditure serves as the stabilizing force in Chinese transitional economy to ameliorate the inequality-enhancing effect of knowledge-based economy. For China to pursue an equitable growth of its urban economy, special attention should be paid to the low-wage nature of its dominant manufacturing industry and the considerable spatial gap in wage for its employees in knowledge-based sectors.

28300015.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28300015.value: Carbon dioxide (CO2) capture, sequestration and fixation are potential methods to alleviate the rate and magnitude of global warming. Among these, microbial CO2 fixation has attracted much attention because of its characteristics of low energy consumption and effective conversion of CO2 to products with high economic values. To date, most studies that have been conducted to investigate microbial CO2 fixation efficiency have primarily focused on algae and hydrogen oxidizing bacteria. However, algae require light during cultivation and cannot resist high CO2 concentrations, while hydrogen oxidizing bacteria require large amounts of hydrogen gas, which has limited the application of these two types of microorganisms. In addition, cost effective methods are not available for the large-scale application in the field. Therefore, it is necessary to isolate highly efficient CO2 fixing microorganisms that do not require light or hydrogen to enable a wider range of applications. In our previous studies, we successfully isolated non-photosynthetic microbial communities (NPMCs) from 12 locations in four oceans of the world to improve the efficiency of microbial CO2 fixation efficiency under aerobic conditions without the aid of hydrogen. The findings also indicated a mixture of electron donors (i.e. NaNO2, Na2S, and Na2S2O3) may further enhance the efficiency. Soil impoverishment is another important issue that we face. Traditional improving measures for poor soils with fertilizers always significantly enhance soil respiration, thus simultaneously releasing more CO2 to the atmosphere. The application of non-photosynthetic bacteria in poor soil can effectively fix CO2 and accumulate organic carbon in soil without the supply of light and hydrogen. However, the inhibitory effects on the NPMC, CO2 fixing pathways and energy supply are still the key limiting factors for CO2 fixation by NMPC. Determining the typical soil organics (e.g. fulvic acid, humic acid, simple sugar, lipid and proteins) that inhibit CO2 fixation by NPMC and reducing the metabolites of organic carbon that have negative effects are the key factors favouring CO2 fixation by NPMC in poor soil environments containing some organic matter. The experimental results from this study can help in improving the efficiency of microbial CO2 fixation using non-photosynthetic microbial community by further abating the inhibitory effects. The results of this study will widen the application of microbial CO2 fixation and provide a feasible and applicable method for the mitigation of global warming. 發展微生物固碳技術對於環境中CO2的吸收與資源化具有重要意義。然而目前公認具有較高固碳效率的微生物主要是微藻和非光合的氫-氧化細菌，由於這些微生物在固碳時需要光照或供氫氣，限制了其在土壤等無光/無氫環境中的應用。我們前期的研究已從海洋環境中分離到一群不用光照與供氫的固碳微生物，其固碳效率已超過氫-氧化細菌的水準。土壤和大氣碳庫存在一個動態平衡，如能實現該菌群在貧瘠土壤中的二次固碳，將游離CO2持續同化到土壤中，既可降低大氣CO2濃度又可提高貧瘠土壤的有機質含量。然而研究發現一些有機物對該菌群的固碳效率有抑制作用，因此在含有機質的土壤中其固碳效率較低。為此，在闡明該菌群優勢固碳途徑的基礎上，研究典型土壤有機質與該菌群的相互作用及其抑制效應，揭示其主要的抑制靶點和作用機制，將為發展一種簡便有效的有機質抑制消減技術，進而實現該菌群在貧瘠土壤中的二次高效固碳奠定理論基礎。

28300015.label: Realisation of objectives
28300015.value: Different research activities have been conducted to investigate the inhibitory effects and mechanisms of typical inhibitors on CO2 fixation using NPMC and to propose abating measures to prevent the inhibitory effects on CO2 fixation by applying NPMC in soil. The activities are (1) to identify the major inhibitory organics on CO2 fixation by NPMC; (2) to identify the fixation pathways and their key enzymes of CO2 fixation by NPMC; and (3) to understand the inhibition mechanisms of identified organics. The activities were conducted during this reporting period: (1) Comparison of the effects of major inhibitors commonly found in the soil on the microbial CO2 fixation; (2) Study of enzymatic pathways and key enzymes of CO2 fixation; and (3) Study of the effects of inhibitors on NPMC community structure. The inhibitory effects of typical soil organic(s) on the efficiency of CO2 fixation by NPMC under aerobic or semi-aerobic conditions were successfully compared and characterized. The enzymatic pathways of CO2 fixation by NPMC and to evaluate the inhibitory mechanisms of the identified organic(s) on CO2 fixation by NPMC in the view of the metabolic pathways involved were successfully explored. The inhibitory mechanisms of the typical soil organic(s) with high inhibitory effects on CO2 fixation by NPMC were successfully clarified. Possible measures to reduce the inhibitory effects of the identified organic(s) on microbial CO2 fixation by NPMC according to the results of objectives #1, 2 and 3 were successfully proposed.

28300015.label: Major findings and research outcome
28300015.value: In this study, we have significantly improved the CO2 fixation efficiency of non-photosynthetic microbial communities (NPMC) isolated from global oceans (Hu et al., 2016). The maximum CO2 fixation capability of the NPMC was closed to the level of microalgae (Zhang et al., 2018; Hu et al., 2019). The NPMC contains not only chemoautotrophs but also a high proportion of heterotrophs. Moreover, the CO2 fixation efficiency of predominant chemoautotrophs isolated from the NPMC was substantially lower than that of the NPMC (Wang et al., 2019). These results indicate that the high CO2 fixation capacity of the NPMC is greatly ascribed to the synergistic effect between chemoautotrophs and heterotrophs (Wang et al., 2016a; 2016b). The CO2 assimilation process is inhibited when the growth substrate of chemoautotrophs contains some external organic matter in pure culture systems. The findings also indicated that soluble microbial products (SMP), which was generated throughout the chemoautotrophic cultivation process, may exhibit an inhibitory effect on CO2 fixation using typical chemoautotrophs (Wang et al., 2017). Two typical sulphur-oxidising bacteria (i.e., DSM 505 and DSM 15147) that fix CO2 by the CBB cycle were selected to further investigate the characteristics of self-generated SMP and its impacts on CO2 fixation efficiency during chemoautotrophic cultivation. The results showed that the SMP gradually accumulated accompanied by an increase in the CO2 fixation yield in both strain. The SMP/TOC ratios were relatively high at the beginning of cultivation, and then declined during the fast growing phase, especially from 12 to 72 h, but gradually increased during the stationary and later phases due to cell death and decay (Wang et al., 2018). Extracellular dissolved organic carbon (EDOC) has been identified as the potential inhibitors of microbial CO2 fixation. The variations of CO2 fixation of four sulphur-oxidising bacteria, namely DSM 505, DSM 15147, DSM 506 and DSM 18155, during the chemoautotrophic cultivation were monitored in terms of EDOC (Wang et al., 2019). EDOC was accumulated in all strains during the cultivation process. The EDOC of DSM 505 and DSM 15147 increased significantly, while the EDOC DSM 506 and DSM 18155 increased slightly and was relatively stable. The findings indicated that the cbb gene transcription efficiency decreased with the increase in EDOC accumulation in the culture medium. Therefore, the EDOC generated during the CO2 fixation process may exhibit an inhibitory effect on the cbb gene transcription efficiency.

28300015.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28300015.value: In this study, the NPMC that can fix CO2 without light and hydrogen has been successfully screened and isolated from global oceans, and the efficiency of CO2 fixation by using NPMC has been significantly improved by mixed electron donors. The NPMC consists of chemoautotrophs (i.e., microorganisms that derive energy from the oxidation of inorganic compounds) and heterotrophs (i.e., microorganisms that use organic carbon for growth). Based on the isolation and identification of dominant functional chemoautotrophs and heterotrophs from the NPMC, the NPMC structure with balanced composition of chemoautotrophs and heterotrophs will be modified. The proposed study is also expected to clarify the detailed mechanisms of synergistic effect between chemoautotrophs and heterotrophs to improve the overall CO2 fixation efficiency through the investigation of their carbon metabolism and energy utilisation. The results could provide useful aids to design, develop, and optimise a continuous process using the modified NPMC for effective, controllable, and stable CO2 fixation. The findings can also help to develop stable and efficient microbial CO2 fixation systems for real applications in barren soil and large-scale waste gas treatment systems.

28300015.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28300015.value: Continuous and stable microbial carbon dioxide (CO2) fixation systems have gained great potential for reducing atmospheric CO2 concentration. Compared with microalgae and hydrogen-oxidising bacteria, non-photosynthetic microorganisms that can fix CO2 without hydrogen have the advantage of CO2 reduction implemented safely in dark environments. The results could provide useful aids to design, develop, and optimise a continuous process using the modified NPMC for effective, controllable, and stable CO2 fixation. The findings can also help to design a continuous CO2 fixation process using the modified NPMC with higher efficiency, controllability, and stability and develop stable and efficient microbial CO2 fixation systems for real applications in barren soil and large-scale waste gas treatment systems.

28300215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28300215.value: Optimizing transportation networks is crucial to many major cities, especially in congested areas where road expansion is not feasible. To optimize transportation networks, we have to understand user equilibriums and the global optimum. A user equilibrium is similar to a Nash equilibrium where users choose their route non-cooperatively to minimize their own travelling time; usually, a close-to-optimal state is achieved. Nevertheless, whether these states emerge naturally from a group of un-coordinated users remains an open question. More importantly, even if a user equilibrium exists, it is not necessarily a global optimum, where the global average travel time is minimized only if some users travel on a slightly longer, seemingly sub-optimal route to avoid congestion. In this case, instead of optimizing routes individually, one has to coordinate the combination of the routes to optimize a global goal. It is a computationally difficult task since one has to take into account the impact of individual routes on each other, and determine the routes for all users simultaneously. Great efforts have been made to solve the problem by mathematical programming, but various limitations such as tractability make these techniques impractical in real applications. More importantly, we are unclear about the theoretical limit of the extent transportation networks can be optimized. In the proposed research, we will apply statistical physics to understand the nature and the limitation of transportation optimization, and use these insights to derive practical optimization algorithms. Similar success by statistical physics has been demonstrated in other optimization problems, which has led to ground-breaking advances. Our objective is threefold. Firstly, we aim to reveal the dynamics and the interplay of routing strategies leading to user equilibriums. We then formulate a simple model to understand analytically the emergence of these sub-optimal states. Secondly, we aim to devise algorithms which coordinate the spatial-temporal routes of individuals, driving the system towards the global optimum. We will also reveal the density of sub-optimal states in the state space, which lead to insights into the intrinsic sub-optimality of transportation networks and thus the limitation of optimization algorithms. Finally, we aim to devise algorithms to optimally divert traffic in cases of disturbances, e.g. road blockage due car crashes, which are less explored but as important as recurrent traffic optimization. The above findings will be tested on real datasets including those obtained from the London Metro network and Waze. 優化交通網絡對許多大城市來說至關重要，尤其是在擁擠的市區，道路擴建己不可行。要優化交通網絡，我們必須了解駕駛者平衡態及全局最優態。駕駛者平衡態類似拿殊均衡點，在沒有合作的狀況下，個別駕駛者選擇路線以減少自己的行車時間，達到近似最優態。然而，這個駕駛者平衡態是否在現實中存在仍有待考証。再者，即使駕駛者平衡態存在，它亦可能不是全局最優態。要達至全局最優，亦即對所有駕駛者而言平均行車時間最短，某些駕駛者必須選擇一些看似較長的路線來緩和擠塞。在這情況下，我們必須同時間協調所有駕駛者的路線，避免個別駕駛者只優化自己的路線。要計算出全局最優態相當困難，因為要優化的是路線的組合而非個別單獨路線，我們必須同時考慮每位駕駛者的行車路線及其對他人的互動影響。線性規劃及其他數學方法己經應用在上述問題，但基於各種限制，大部分研究仍停留於理論層面。再者，交通網絡有多大程度能被優化仍是未知之數。 在本研究中，我們將應用統計物理來分析最優化交通網絡的本質及限制，並利用這些結果實現全局最優化算法。以統計物理解決跨領域問題，己在其他優化問題中取得突破性的發展。我們有三個研究目標。首先，我們會揭示以達到駕駛者平衡態的路由策略及其相互作用。我們會建模以理解此狀態出現的條件及後果。其次，我們將推導一個算法，以協調所有駕駛者在空間及時間位度的路線，使系統達至全局最優。我們也會揭示交通網絡的次優狀態及次優狀態在態空間的密度，從而了解交通網絡有多大程度能被優化，及交通優化算法的極限。最後，我們將推導算法以減少由交通意外對交通網絡所帶來的影響，如有效把交通分流以減少因車禍帶來的堵塞。研究結果將在真實數據包括倫敦地鐵網絡，及Waze所提供的交通網絡進行模擬測試。

28300215.label: Realisation of objectives
28300215.value: OBJECTIVE (1) (a) In [5] (Tai and Yeung, 2019), by using cellular automata on two-dimensional square lattices, we studied a model of vehicles repeatedly commuting between random origins and destinations, to examine the impact of random routing of individual vehicles on the whole transportation network. Comparing between cases where vehicles always follow the shortest path with those where vehicles occasionally route randomly, the observed various interesting phenomenon related to user equilibria, such as the former outperforms the latter in the free-flow state as expected, but congested state emerge at a higher vehicle density in the latter which is a great benefit. These led to an advanced understanding of the emergence and the nature of user equilibria in transportation networks. (b) In [6] (Po, Yeung and Saad, under review), we employed analytical tools originally developed in the studies of spin glasses, i.e. the cavity approach, to analyze how vehicles re-route from an initially optimally coordinated configuration of routes to minimize their own cost. The re-routed states are sub-optimal. We conducted simulations to further examine how the final sub-optimal Nash equilibria are formed after multiple rounds of re-routing. Using cavity approach, we obtained the analytical results on cost increment from optimal state to the sub-optimal states. These analyses lead us to an understanding of sub-optimal user equilibria in transportation networks. (c) In [1] (Zeng and Yeung, 2016) and [2] (Ji, Lu, Yeung and Hu, 2017), we used numerical simulations to find that diffusion and spreading can identify highly correlated nodes. The correlation in the nodes are useful to understand user equilibria in transportation networks, and are relevant for identifying traffic bottlenecks when traffic accident occurs in highly correlated. OBJECTIVE (2) (a) In [4] (Yeung 2019), we tackled the dynamical route assignment and coordination problem by converting the original spatial transportation networks into space-time networks, and apply the cavity approach to derive a message-passing algorithm capable to optimally coordinate the routes of multiple vehicles. The algorithm aims at optimizing a global objective, for instance, minimizing the total traveling time for all vehicles. The derived algorithm has a lower computation complexity, converges well and its validity is shown by comparing with another algorithm derived using the cavity approach without the loopy space-time networks. To examine the effectiveness of the algorithm, we showed that our algorithm outperforms multi-start greedy search in saving as much as 15% of total traveling time, when the number of vehicles on the network is large. This derived algorithm is readily applicable to coordinate the spatial-temporal routes of vehicles in real transportation networks. (b) In [5] (Tai and Yeung 2019), we introduced an adaptive algorithm to adjust the tendency of individual vehicles to route via a random direction. Our results show that the adaptive algorithm leads the transportation network to a state with shorter average journey time and distance compared to cases with a centralized tendency of randomness. The results are highly relevant to navigation software in identifying the fraction of shortest paths recommended to its users which may benefit the whole transportation network. OBJECTIVE (3) (a) In a PhD student thesis and a manuscript under preparation (Tai and Yeung, unpublished), we applied the cavity approach to derive a message-passing algorithm capable to optimally divert the traffic after road blockage. The algorithm takes into account the traffic before road blockage, and optimally divert the traffic subject to a global objective, e.g., to minimize the resultant cost after traffic diversion. We tested the algorithm on generated and real networks such as the Seoul road network which yield the optimally diverted traffic configurations. (b) In [3] (Po, Yeung, Zeng and Wong, 2017), we applied our derived optimization algorithm to optimize the transfer of resources on power-grid networks with increasingly more broken links; our results show that the original load on broken links can be optimally diverted to the other part of network. OBJECTIVE (4) (a) In [4] (Yeung 2019), we examined the intrinsic hardness of spatial-temporal route coordination by analyzing the existence of the so-called replica-symmetry breaking (RSB) phase in transportation networks. We examined the divergence of hamming distance between two probabilities distributions with identical recursion relations but different initial conditions, and found that RSB emerges beyond specific vehicle. The emergence of RSB corresponds to the existence of numerous local minima in the energy landscape of the optimization problem, which always leads to hardness for optimization algorithms to identify the global optimal states. Our theoretical predictions on the phase transition to the RSB phase for spatial-temporal route coordination agree well with algorithmic results. Our results thus reveal a clear physical picture of the fundamental hardness for coordinating spatial-temporal routes. (b) In [5] (Tai and Yeung 2019), we conducted simulations on cellular automata to reveal the intrinsic sub-optimality of spatial-temporal route assignment on transportation network. Specifically, our results show that congestion emerge easily when vehicles always follow their shortest path; our results thus reveal that route coordination is essential, but there are intrinsic limitations as vehicles may tend to follow the shortest path to their destinations and congestion emerge. (c) In [6] (Po, Yeung and Saad, under review), we applied numerical simulations to examine the Nash equilibria states achieved after multiple rounds of selfish re-routing; we found that with a small vehicle density and a small fraction of selfish vehicles at each round or re-routing, the system results in a Nash equilibrium state close to the global optimum. Nevertheless, when vehicle density or the number of re-routed vehicles increase, a state with cost much higher than the optimal one emerges. Simulations are conducted using the England highway network and similar behavior are observed. These results show the intrinsic hardness in optimizing the transportation network from the perspective of individual vehicles as they always optimize their individual cost. OBJECTIVE (5) (a) In [6] (Po, Yeung and Saad, under review), we conducted numerical simulations to examine a system in which vehicles selfishly re-route to paths that minimize their own cost. Starting from an initial optimized configuration, the system slowly evolves to different user equilibria (or Nash equilibria) depending on vehicle density and the number of selfish vehicles at each round of re-routing. These results suggest that the global optimum is connected with different user equilibria of transportation networks through re-routing of individual vehicular routes. (b) In [7] (Liao, Wu, Zhou and Yeung, under review), we tested our previously derived route coordination algorithms on real road and railway networks including those from London, Beijing and New York, using a realistic cost function from the Bureau of Public Roads, which can be interpreted as the total latency for vehicles traveling on the road. We compared the transportation cost obtained by the algorithm to that obtained by shortest-path routing. Our results show that transportation cost can be greatly reduced with our route coordination algorithm, implying that the global optimum is much better than the user equilibria in terms of total traveling time. (c) In [8] (Zhao, Zeng and Yeung, under review), we analyzed cell phone data from individuals in a city in China and revealed their mobility pattern in high spatial-temporal resolution; the results are relevant to enhance our understanding of the relation between user equilibria and the global optimum.

28300215.label: Major findings and research outcome
28300215.value: (1) Enhanced understanding on the role and benefit of random routing – We showed in [5] (Tai and Yeung, 2019) that congestion emerge if all vehicles follow their shortest paths; occasional random routing may be beneficial. A new phase called congested-flow state is observed. These results are relevant to navigation software in suppressing congestion through recommending alternative paths. (2) Enhanced understanding on the role and benefit of selfish re-routing – In [6] (Po, Yeung, Saad, under review), we showed that a small ratio of selfish users improves uncoordinated transportation networks, but degrades initially optimized ones. Phase diagrams characterizing the gain and loss of selfish and compliant vehicles are analytically derived; similar behavior is observed in the simulations based on the England highway network. Repeated route-switching leads to Nash equilibria close to the optimal routing. These results show that selfish re-routing may benefit the transportation networks. (3) Enhanced understanding on the fundamental hardness in coordinating spatial-temporal routes – In [5] (Yeung, 2019), we employed the cavity approach to analytically identify the vehicle density beyond which algorithmic hardness emerges, which agrees well with simulation results. A scaling law which connects the vehicle density to algorithmic hardness is identified. These results are relevant to the design of optimization algorithms for coordinating spatial-temporal routes. (4) Derivation of algorithms for coordinating spatial-temporal routes – In [4] (Yeung 2019), by using the cavity approach on space-time networks, we derived an optimization algorithm capable to coordinate spatial-temporal routes. Our simulation results show that vehicles can save up to 15% of total traveling time from our algorithm compared to multi-start greedy search. The algorithm is readily applicable to coordinate spatial-temporal routes on real networks [7] (Liao, Wu, Zhou, Yeung, under review). (5) Derivation of algorithms for traffic diversion – In the manuscript under preparation by Tai and Yeung, we derived an algorithm to optimize traffic diversion due to road blockage, and are tested on generated and real networks; in [3] (Po, Yeung, Zeng and Wong, 2017), we derived algorithms for diverting traffic in power-grid network due to cascading failures. These algorithms are readily applicable on real networks. (6) Derivation of protocols for diffusion and spreading processes – In [1] (Zeng and Yeung, 2016) and [2] (Ji, Lu, Yeung and Hu, 2017), we applied diffusion and spreading processes to identify highly correlated nodes in various networks including transportation networks. Human mobility patterns are analyzed using cell phone data [8] (Zhao, Zeng and Yeung, under review).

28300215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28300215.value: (1) Implementation of the derived spatial-temporal route coordination algorithms in navigation software – the algorithms derived in the project are readily applicable on real networks; as shown by our simulation results, substantial traveling time can be saved if vehicles follow the identified path configurations. We will continue to explore opportunities to implement our algorithms in navigation software and examine if the same benefit can be observed in real networks. (2) Derivation of spatial-temporal route coordination algorithm taking into account selfish re-routing - even an algorithm capable to coordinate spatial-temporal is implemented in navigation software, some vehicles may not follow the recommended paths; we will attempt to combine our two major findings, namely the spatial-temporal route coordination algorithm and impact of selfish re-routing on an initially optimized network, to derive a modified route coordination algorithm taking into account selfish re-routing. (3) Improving the derived algorithms on computational complexity – with the potential to implement our derived algorithm in navigation software which involves a large number of vehicles, we have to further decrease the computation complexity of our algorithms. Modified algorithms which compute quickly through the consideration of incremental changes can also be explored.

28300215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28300215.value: Traffic congestion is severe in many major cities. Since it is usually infeasible to expand infrastructure in metropolitan areas, coordinating the dynamical routes of vehicles is a promising solution to suppress traffic congestion. Nevertheless, existing navigation software only recommend a set of routes for individuals to choose, since coordinating the dynamical routes of vehicle simultaneously is a complex optimization problem. As a result, traffic in metropolitan areas are usually uncoordinated and sub-optimal. In this project, we improved our understanding on dynamical transportation networks, and applied analytical tools from statistical physics to derive optimization algorithms capable to coordinate spatial-temporal routes for multiple vehicles. We found that in contrary to our common belief, random routing or re-routing from the uncoordinated shortest paths to minimize individual cost may benefit the whole transportation network in some cases. By applying our derived algorithms capable to coordinate the spatial-temporal routes of vehicles, simulation results suggest that up to 15% of the total traveling time can be saved. These results suggest that the transportation networks are sub-optimal if all vehicles only follow the shortest paths, and it is promising to suppress traffic congestion and save traveling time by coordinating the spatial-temporal routes of vehicles.

28600615.value: To understand the income-achievement gap in early development and learning in Hong Kong; To examine income-related differences in the self-regulation of Hong Kong pre-schoolers; To elucidate whether self-regulation can mediate the relationship between family income and early development and learning in Hong Kong; and To investigate whether self-regulation plays a compensatory role in early development and learning for children from low-income families in Hong Kong.

28600615.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28600615.value: Early achievement is predictive of academic and occupational success in later life. However, there is a wide and persistent achievement gap globally between children from low-income families and those with greater advantages. Prior studies traditionally focus on family-level mechanisms in achievement gap, while evidence from Western literature has identified self-regulation as an important factor in narrowing this income-achievement gap. Self-regulation has been found to mediate the relationship between household income and early achievement and may serve as a compensatory component in early development and learning for children experiencing risks early in life. Although the issue of the income-achievement gap has been hotly debated in Chinese societies, few empirical studies have addressed the income-achievement gap in the early years and its relationship with self-regulation in Chinese societies, in which children are socialised to exert emotional and behavioural control both within the family and at school, regardless of household wealth. This study will address the following questions in a Chinese context (Hong Kong): (i) Do income-achievement gaps exist in the early development and learning of pre-school children? (ii) Are there income-related differences in the self-regulation of pre-school children? (iii) Can self-regulation mediate the relationship between household income and early achievement? and (iv) Among children from low-income families, does self-regulation play a compensatory role in early development and learning? Twenty-four kindergartens from high- and low-income districts of Hong Kong will be randomly selected and the children of one K1 (3- to 4-year-olds), K2 (4- to 5-year-olds) and K3 class (5- to 6-year-olds) in each kindergarten (n ≈ 900, based on a class size of 12 to 15) and their parents (n ≈ 900) will participate in the study. All of the children will be assessed in terms of their holistic development; K3 children will be further assessed in their readiness for school. The self-regulation of the children will be assessed via a battery of tasks. Their parents will be surveyed about parental investment, parental sensitivity and situations relating to family functioning. The findings will enable us to better understand early development and learning and to identify a possible developmental link between household income and early achievement in Hong Kong and perhaps further afar by elucidating the role of self-regulation. Given the importance of evidence-based policy, these findings may also assist in the design of a high-quality intervention study to ascertain effective intervention programmes and appropriate policies to close the early income-achievement gap. 早期學業成就能夠預測日後的學業與職業成就。然而，大量研究顯示，在全球範圍內貧困家庭兒童與富裕家庭兒童的學業成就之間存在顯著差距。西方的研究顯示，自我調節能力能夠調節家庭經濟收入與早期學業成就之間的關係，並對處境不利兒童的早期學習與發展具有補償作用，因此對於縮窄早期學業成就的差距有重要意義。中國社會重視幼兒情緒和行為的自我控制與管理，但鮮有實證研究去探討在中國社會中幼兒的自我調節能力與早期學業成就差異之間的關係。 本研究以香港作為研究基地，探討以下研究問題：1）香港社會是否存在與家庭經濟收入相關的早期學業成績的差異？2）幼兒的自我調節能力是否與家庭經濟收入呈現顯著的相關關係？3）幼兒的自我調節能力是否能夠調節家庭經濟收入與幼兒早期學業成就之間的關係？4）對於來自低收入家庭的幼兒，自我調節能力對他們的早期學習和發展是否具有補償作用？ 我們將在香港的高收入地區和低收入地區隨機抽取24所幼稚園，並邀請其中K1，K2，和K3各一個班級的幼兒（共約900名）及其家長參與此次研究。我們將對所有參與研究的幼兒進行關於早期學習和發展狀況和自我調節能力的測查。對於K3幼兒，我們將同時對其學業準備情況進行評估。我們亦會對所有幼兒的家長進行有關家庭經濟能力、教養情況、和家庭功能等方面的問卷調查。 通過對幼兒自我調節能力對於家庭經濟收入和香港幼兒早期學習和發展能力的可能調節作用的研究，本研究的研究結果將有助於加深對幼兒早期學習和發展的認識，並有助於設計高質量的早期干預方案以縮窄與家庭經濟收入相關的早期學業成就的差距。是次研究亦能夠為相關教育政策的制定和實施提供實證依據。

28600615.label: Realisation of objectives
28600615.value: A total of 951 children (448 girls) aged three to five were recruited from 18 kindergartens in 10 out of 18 regions in Hong Kong. The mean age of the participants was 56.54 months (SD = 10.77, ranged from 32.83 to 85.77 months). All children were assessed with a battery of five self-regulation tasks (i.e., pencil tapping task, tower of Hanoi task, card sorting task, the head-toes-knees-shoulders task, and gift task) and items selected from the Hong Kong Early Childhood Development Scale (HKECDS) to understand their holistic development in different domains. The primary caregivers also reported the demographic information and their childcare practices at home. With the comprehensive data we collected, we are fully able to address the four research objectives (ROs) proposed. RO1: To fully understand the achievement gaps in early years, we extended our exploration by examining the income achievement gaps at both the family and school levels. We also used SES, a composite index including family income, to better capture the early achievement gaps in Hong Kong. The family-level SES was index as family income and parental education, while school-level SES was index as the average family SES of the students. The hierarchal linear modelling was adopted in the analyses. We found family-level SES matters for children’s early development in the domains of academic achievement, general knowledge, and gross motor development, while the school-level SES significantly predicted children’s academic achievement, general knowledge, and fine motor development. These results indicate the existence of early achievement gaps at both the family and school levels in Hong Kong. RO2: Approaches similar with those addressing the RO1 were adopted to understand income-related differences in early development of self-regulation. To understand self-regulation from a holistic perspective, we categorized self-regulation as cool and hot aspects with the exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. The hierarchical linear modelling revealed that family-level SES significantly predicted Chinese children’s cool but not hot self-regulation after controlling for the confounders. In contrast, the school-level SES significantly predicted both the hot and cool aspects of self-regulation. Therefore, both the family and school SES backgrounds influence children’s early development in cool and hot self-regulation. RO3: Based on the results related to the RO1 and RO2, we conducted multiple-level structural equation modelling (MSEM) to analyse the mediating role of self-regulation in the family- and school-level achievement gaps detected. The results based on three MSEMs showed that both the family- and school-level cool self-regulation significantly mediated the relationship between family- and school-level SES and children’s early learning outcomes in the domains of academic achievement, general knowledge, gross motor and fine motor, after controlling for multiple confounders such as child age, gender, parenting practices, and school structural quality. The results indicate that cool self-regulation can partly explain how family- and school-level SES influence children’s early learning outcomes in different domains. RO4: To address the last RO, we separate the 951 children into three groups according to their family SES: high- (n=135), high-middle- (n=173), and low-middle- (n=306), and low-SES (n=212) groups. We particularly selected children who were assigned to the low-middle and low-SES groups to address the RO4. Children’s performance on hot and cool aspects of self-regulation was also categorized as high-, medium- and low-levels. The moderation effects of cool and hot self-regulation in the relationship between family SES and children’s performance on the four domains addressed in this study (i.e., academic achievement, general knowledge, gross motor, and fine motor) were examined. The results show significant moderating effects of children’s cool-self-regulation. Therefore, cool self-regulation can be considered as a compensatory role in early development and learning for children from low-income families in Hong Kong based on the data collected in this study.

28600615.label: Major findings and research outcome
28600615.value: The major findings of this project can be understood from four aspects. The first aspect is related to early achievement gaps. The second aspect is about early development of self-regulation. The third aspect is about the relationship between self-regulation and early child learning outcomes in early years; and the last aspect on early achievement gaps and the role of self-regulation. We found the existence of achievement gaps in Hong Kong were not only at the family level but also at the school level. Children from low-SES families did show lower performance on domains of academic learning, general knowledge, gross motor, and fine motor skills, compared to their counterparts from more advantaged families. The results related to self-regulation indicated that self-regulation can be categorized as at least cool and hot aspects as they were found as independent but correlated factors and there are different patterns of the early development of cool and hot self-regulation among Hong Kong Chinese children. In particular, children’s performance on cool self-regulation is found to increase steadily in early years, while Hong Kong preschoolers demonstrated a high level of hot self-regulation and the increase in early years was not significant. The examination on the relationship between self-regulation and early learning outcomes showed that cool self-regulation significantly predicted all four domains examined, while hot self-regulation only significantly predicted children’s gross motor development. Finally, the analyses related to the role of self-regulation in early achievement gaps showed that cool self-regulation significantly mediated the school-level but not the family-level achievement gaps. These results currently have been or will be presented at prestigious international conferences on child development and early instruction and learning. One manuscript is under review and two more manuscripts are in progress. The conference presentations include: 1. Sun, J. & Kang, R. (2019). Individual- and school-level self-regulation: Their distinctive mediating roles in early development gaps in Hong Kong. Pater presented at the 18th Biennial EARLI Conference, RWTH Aachen, Germany. 2. Sun, J., Kang, R., & Ip, P. (2019). Cognitive and Emotional Self-Regulation Predict Early Achievement in Chinese Preschoolers. Pater presented at the at the 2019 Society of Research in Child Development Biennial Meeting, Baltimore, USA. 3. Sun, J., Rao, N., & Wu, D. (2018). Family SES and Chinese children’s behavioral and emotional self-regulation. Poster presented at the 25th Biennial Meeting International Society for the study of Behavioural Development, Gold Coast, Australia.

28600615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28600615.value: The findings of this project suggest more in-depth examinations regarding the early development of self-regulation and its role in facilitating early learning outcomes in Chinese preschoolers, especially those from the disadvantaged background. Several lines of studies can be further conducted. Firstly, the results indicate different developmental patterns of hot and cool self-regulation in early years among Chinese preschoolers and these two aspects of self-regulation have different predictive effects on early learning outcomes. Longitudinal studies should be conducted to examine the developmental trajectories of hot and cool self-regulation and its relationship with early learning outcomes in different domains, which can lay the foundation for future intervention studies. A GRF proposal on this topic has been submitted in 2018/19. Secondly, based on the results related the family-level and school-level early achievement gaps detected in this project and the mediating role of cool self-regulation between the school-level achievement gaps, further studies should be focused more on the mechanism on the achievement gaps at both the family and school levels and how cool self-regulation works. A PPR proposal related to this topic will be submitted in 2019/20.

28600615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28600615.value: Early achievement is predictive of academic and occupational success in later life. But a wide and persistent achievement gap can be found between children from low-income families and their more advantaged peers across the world. Hong Kong is one of the societies with large gaps between the rich and the poor. It is therefore important to understand whether and the extent to which early achievement gaps exist in this society. This project detected significant family-level and school-level early achievement gaps different domains in Hong Kong and identified a mediating role of self-regulation, the ability to manage arousal, attention, emotion, behaviour and cognition and to engage effectively in goal-directed activities, in the early achievement gaps. These findings may shed light on the implementation of high-quality intervention study to ascertain effective intervention programmes and appropriate policy to improve the equity of early learning and education of underprivileged children and to close the early achievement gap in Hong Kong.

28601415.label: Project Objectives
28601415.value: To compare and contrast the state of budget openness in Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan through the application of the OBS methodology. To explore whether and to what extent do democratic transitions determine the state of budget openness of Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. To develop a new and unique set of case studies on the state of budget openness of Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan so as to stimulate scholarly research activities in the field of comparative budgeting. To provide local policy community with useful information, data and policy options on budget reforms by learning the international best practices on budget openness and identifying the room for improvement within Hong Kong’s budgetary system. To better inform the teaching and learning activities of undergraduate and post-graduate public finance courses organized in local tertiary institutions by providing the most updated public finance research in respect of Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan.

28601415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28601415.value: In recent decades, academics and transnational organizations have taken an increasing interest on budget openness, suggesting that the disclosure of fiscal information to public will provide stronger incentives for government accountability and therefore promote good governance (Seifert, Carlitz and Mondo, 2013). A large body of empirical research was developed to demonstrate the positive consequences of budget openness on various governance outcomes such as higher sovereign credit ratings, higher fiscal discipline and better control over corruption (Reinikka and Svensson, 2004; Hameed, 2005; Glennerster and Shin, 2008). Within comparative budgeting literature, the emergence of Open Budget Survey (OBS) as a comparative statistical tool has recently attracted much attention within the Western academia. Developed by a non-partisan budget think-tank namely International Budget Partnership (IBP), the OBS has been conducted on a bi-annual basis since 2006 (International Budget Partnership, 2006, 2008, 2010 and 2012). While the OBS was originally designed as a policy advocacy tool for the purpose of assessing the global state of budget openness, it has increasingly been adopted by comparative scholars as a research tool for conducting cross-countries studies (de Renzio and Masud, 2011; Seifert, Carlitz and Mondo, 2013). By providing a set of objective, comparative and time-series data on budget openness, the OBS methodology was regarded by many academics as a reliable quantitative measure of budget openness and thus a comparative literature based on OBS data has been developed rapidly in recent years (Khagram, de Renzio and Fung, 2013). This research project is a pioneer project that applies the OBS methodology in the assessment of the state of budget openness in Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. More specifically, this research project aims at addressing the following two central research questions: How to objectively compare and measure the state of budget openness in Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan through the application of the OBS methodology? Whether and to what extent do the democratic transitions of Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan determine and shape their state of budget openness? Through the development of a new and unique set of case studies on Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, this research project will enrich the theoretical discussion by examining the correlational relationship between democratic transitions and the state of budget openness. The findings and conclusion of this research project will therefore make an important original contribution to enriching the currently underdeveloped but rapidly developing theoretical discussion on the determinants of budget openness. 近年，學術界及跨國機構都越來越重視「開放預算」，認同向公眾發放更多的政府預算資訊，將有助提高政府問責性，並促進良好管治。不少實證研究已指出，「開放預算」與「管治指標」例如主權評級、財政紀律和控制貪污，呈現顯著的正相關。 在比較研預算研究的文獻中，由國際預算夥伴關係自2006年起定期發表的「開放預算調查」，逐漸成為西方學術界普遍採用的比較研究工具，被不少學者用於進行跨國比較。「開放預算調查」提供了一系列客觀、持續的量化數據，被不少學者視為一項可靠工具，用以研究開放預算，因此近年湧現大量根據「開放預算調查」數據所發展出來的比較研預算研究。 本研究計劃是首項將「開放預算調查方法」應用在香港、澳門和台灣的比較研究，希望能夠解答兩個研究問題：怎樣透過應用「開放預算調查方法」，客觀地量度及比較香港、澳門和台灣的開放預算程度？香港、澳門和台灣的「開放預算程度」，是否及有多大程度上與三地的「民主發展程度」相關？本研究計劃希望透過建立香港、澳門和台灣這一組獨特的個案研究，豐富現時有關「民主發展程度」與「開放預算程度」關聯性的討論。本研究計劃的結果和結論，將對現時仍然有待發展的「開放預算」文獻作出原創貢獻。

28602715.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28602715.value: 現代化城市的崛起：香港殖民地時期(1920-50)第一代華人建築師

28602715.label: Project Objectives
28602715.value: Recognize and promote heritage values for surviving and demolished architecture designed by first-generation Hong Kong architects and architectural firms, based on a criteria list set by the PI and professionals in the field and contribute to long term heritage policy and awareness locally and abroad. The list, including architectural style, patron, and design intention, will take reference from those recognized by the Antiquities and Monuments Office and seek to improve them where there are shortfalls. Review current heritage policies in Hong Kong and compare with international cases, ultimately enhancing and improving policies for local heritage from this research. Findings of the works will not only inform the public and professionals with new understanding of the field, but also combine in an innovative way heritage policy with education. Formulate and expand on a database of modern architecture and heritage by Hong Kong architects. The database would further enhance and propel the PI's work and engagement with DOCOMOMO, a non-profit organisation network with other local professionals and academics, where they collaborate on regular meetings and output of public lectures, exhibitions, and publications. Reveal the architecture that are mediated through colonial architectural prototypes to produce new identities and typologies in Hong Kong, and align with discourses on Chinese and Western modern architecture. Formulate an improved approach to interpret the architecture in the research by rooting the study in existing Western and Chinese research methodologies and theoretical frameworks and developing an enhanced perspective to analyse the works. Reconstruct Hong Kong’s early twentieth century modernization by collating previously obscure sources including private archives and conduct interviews with architects’ descendants. Educational factors are crucial in the research, including generating public workshops, seminars and websites.
