28602715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28602715.value: 建築遺產保護與研究於香港特區政府2007-08年施政報告實施文物保護政策後逐漸發展成為一個獨特的專業和議題。 自那時開始，文物保育和教育一直在本地發展政策中備受關注。 這項研究將重新審視香港殖民地時期的建築設計，並探討二十世紀初的第一代華人建築師在現代建築和中國傳統文化之間的張力。 二十世紀初的二十、三十年代，一批華人建築師從海外或本地完成建筑或工程學業，紛紛想在香港大展拳腳。他們開始建立自己的設計公司，投入各方面的設計項目，並為一個正在現代化的香港做出巨大的貢獻。 然而，許多學者常視這個時期的香港建築設計較其他中國城市落後，經典的例子包括許多有關上海的研究。學術界近期的新研究及發現 (包括這項研究在內) 會將以前被低估及忽略的香港建築推進一個新的層面和研究角度。本研究將會記錄一些已拆卸的建築物，亦爭取保留一些香港先驅建築師的設計，加上實地考察及訪問，目的是從新審視及調整以往對本地建築歷史的認識及理解。 這項研究將植根於西方和中國學術研究框架，並明確界定二十世紀初期的建築設計如何在西方殖民地建築形式和中國傳統文化之間作出取捨。此研究將改善當前的文化遺產政策，並為香港現代建築的教育工作進一步奠定基礎。

28602715.label: Realisation of objectives
28602715.value: The six objectives have been archived within the 30 months project period through research, education and reinterpretation processes; and will be separately discussed respectively in the following. Regarding objective 1, documentation has been done on various local architectural firms from the period of the 1920s to 1950s for understanding the development history of local Hong Kong architecture and the relationships between these architects, social elites and the overall architectural atmosphere in the British colonies at the time including Hong Kong and Malaysia. The project targeted certain significant but relatively unknown and under-researched Chinese architects such as Mr. Kwan Wing Hong and Mr. Chau Iu Nin and comparing their architectures in Hong Kong and abroad. By comparing these architectures, we began to understand when and how modernist architecture was tested in colonies by these young architects creating their own “eclectic”, art deco and modernist styles which embedded their own professional knowledge, own identities, and needs from clients. In order to effectively promote the heritage values of modernist architecture which had been neglected for long in Hong Kong, published articles such as “Self-fashioned Identities: Art Deco Architecture in Hong Kong as Resistance and Empowerment” (Lau 2016) and “Building a modern city: Legacies of residential development and architectural adaptation in colonial Hong Kong” (Lau 2017); a mobile application has also been output to extend the impacts for other professionals, students or even laymen to appreciate these architectures. Regarding objective 2, current heritage policies have been studied alongside conservation cases of modernist architecture like the State Theatre in Hong Kong. This topic is still ongoing and the PI have just submitted another paper (under review) on how to apply sustainable theories into these modernist architectures for the sake of society and safeguarding heritage values. This case and other conservation cases like the Sham Shui Po Public Dispensary and apartments on Prince Edward Road are also examples for the PI’s students to understand heritage values like architectural merits through lectures and guided field trips. The PI also published the article mentioned above for the interpretation and promotion of modernist heritage. In spring 2019, an exhibition on Art Deco was held in the City University of Hong Kong for five months and resources gathered in the project has been transmitted to other universities and the crowd through this exhibition and other guest lectures invited by other professional institutes related to conservation like the Hong Kong Institute of Conservationist (HKICON) and Hong Kong Architecture Centre in 2018. The PI also shared her findings on modernist architecture on mass media like ViuTV in 2017/2019 and in a radio interview on Metro Radio conducted on 2018 commenting on Art Deco architecture. Apart from the output by the PI, students on a heritage-related course led by the PI were also self-motivated to hold a symposium on heritage conservation issues and sustainable development in Hong Kong. It is obvious that the achievements were fruitful and continuous during and after completion of the project. As for objective 3, DOCOMOMO, which the PI was in, actively engaged in the ‘saving’ or grading process of the State Theatre with other local concern groups like Walk-in-Hong-Kong. Until today in June 2019, although the PI is no longer in the association, she still actively commenting on the conservation issues with the State Theatre and reviewing heritage policies of Hong Kong with many other new approaches and theories from sociology, sustainability, and anthropology. With new publications, related conferences and lectures, and exposure on mass media are sharing the knowledge of modern architecture and conservation matters. The connection with professional institutions and heightens awareness to the public is paving the way for better conservation of modernist architecture in the near future. The database has also been formulated for further research and academic use. Although DOCOMOMO had now lost its active in documenting modernist architectures, the database is still useful for academic studies and promoting appreciation on local architectures. Objective 4 of this project aims at analysing the buildings while aligning with discourses on Chinese and Western modern architecture. As mentioned above, this project has conducted research on surviving or even demolished modernist buildings in Hong Kong. The project was able to identify the buildings which evolved from a classical or colonial style to a more simple and modern design, with local elements as well as influences from around the world. Together with the personal biographies of these architects, we are able to read and interpret their works with historic and social timeframes. They are also making sense of the place as extensions of colonial architectures in a very local manner. All those buildings that created new identities and typologies of architecture should all be carefully documented, discussed and mediated to the next generation to appreciate how the society was entangled with the cityscape to act as evidence for a complete Hong Kong historical study. Regarding objective 5, the research methodologies and theoretical frameworks are achieved and also continuous at the same time. As there are many ways to interpret architecture, apart from a traditional aesthetic interpretation, the PI is trying to incorporate other frameworks borrowed from sustainability, history, social science and anthropology into the scene for enriching the understanding for a single heritage. These frameworks are often neglected from the conservation sector that deals with the modernist architecture. The intention of PI is to extend the impact of the project to heritage conservation sector by all the outputs mentioned above for protecting these architectures with not only documentation but also improvements on heritage policies in Hong Kong to truly understand the heritage value. Objective 6 has also been achieved, as twentieth-century Hong Kong architecture in this project was largely reconstructed through public archives rather than interviews with architects’ descendants due to various practical reasons. Nevertheless, in terms of education, it is a huge success as the resources obtained in this project benefited many students from UGC-funded courses and professional institutes on enriching their knowledge on the modernist architectural history of Hong Kong. As mentioned in the research outcome and output section, a number of public lectures and seminars had been done from 2016-2019. A recent "Art Deco exhibition" in which the PI collaborated with City University also took place this year. More importantly, a mobile application named “ARchi HK” combining artificial reality technology and database obtained in this project has been created for the teaching and learning of local heritage. The targeted audience is not only university and local students but the general public, or even tourists. It is hoped that the database can be easily accessed and with a much-prolonged impact. Generally speaking, the objectives have been achieved, while some are continuous and ongoing in hopes of generating other opportunities on further promotion of local modernist architecture and heritage conservation through publications, social engagements, and public activities.

28602715.label: Major findings and research outcome
28602715.value: The PI has published two articles related to this project: Lau, L.K.P. (2016). Self-fashioned Identities: Art Deco Architecture in Hong Kong as Resistance and Empowerment. Postcolonial Text, 11(3), 1-20, and Lau, L.K.P., Lai, L.W.C. & Ho, C.W. (2018). Quality of life in a “high-rise lawless slum”: a study of the “Kowloon Walled City". Land Use Policy, 76, 157-165. The first publication reveals how certain modern architectural styles, particularly Art Deco style, can be understood both as the imposition of power by the colonizer and the demonstration of resistance of the colonized in early-twentieth-century Hong Kong. The study also demonstrates that the historic buildings of this research are not passive objects but rather subjects that are able to consume the dominating culture to self-fashion and self-represent. Using postcolonial theory, the paper critiqued the dynamics between the dominated-subjugated in colonial Hong Kong with a focus on a local modern Chinese architectural firm Chau & Lee, and concluded that modes of resistance and empowerment can be identified in the colonial built environment in the 1930s-40s. As for the second article, the PI used reliable and publicly available information seldom used in historical or heritage study to identify the designs of flats and builders of the “Kowloon Walled City” and reliable oral testimonies to refute some myths about the quality of life within it. The research confirms the view that the City, although mystified as a horrifying, disorderly-built, and unplanned territory, was in fact a product of un-organised small local builders that are previously unspoken of in local research. The article adopts a ‘quality of life’ model, which has hitherto been limited to medical and social, rather than historical or anthropological, studies, to evaluate how design and housing satisfaction affected the Walled City residents’ quality of life. An Art Deco exhibition was also one of the major research outcome of this project. Collaborating with City University Exhibition Gallery, the exhibition “Art Deco: The France-China Connection” reveals the history of Art Deco in China, and of the reciprocal influences between French and Chinese artists and architects. The PI was able to contribute in the architectural section of Hong Kong and a catalogue was also published with the PI’s research in a chapter.

28602715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28602715.value: The project has already led to a Teaching Development Grant funded from within her University to produce a digital and innovative mobile app and an online learning platform for heritage education, as well as an Art Deco exhibition “Art Deco: The France-China Connection”, collaborating with City University that just took place from March to July this year. There are many more future development prospects of this project, and for instance the PI has also already submitted a GRF application to study Art Deco and modern theatres/ cinema buildings and culture in Hong Kong. The PI is currently engaged in a book project together with colleagues from EdUHK on Architecture and early Hong Kong education in the Central & Western district. It is targeted to be published by next July for the HK Book Fair, by Chung Hwa Book Company, and will be a book for the general public to understand more about the early beginnings of Hong Kong education via the lens of architecture, politics, history and urban landscape.

28602715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28602715.value: The project not only focuses on the research of modern architecture and Chinese architects in Hong Kong, but also has a special focus on heritage education. The project has resulted in journal publications to further understand about local modern architecture using e.g. a theoretical and postcolonial perspective, as well as public exhibitions, seminars, media and televised interviews and public talks to engage the general public further and spread the significance of modern architecture and its conservation. Currently the PI is also working on improving the local heritage policy on conserving these historic buildings and has completed writing another journal manuscript, as well as a book publication on historic buildings such as schools. From field trips to mobile apps and online learning platforms, both university students and the general public were and will continue to be able to benefit from this project, enabling and guiding them to learn about the historic buildings outside of the classroom environment.

28603715.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28603715.value: Ostracism means being rejected or ignored. The ubiquitous and significant nature of ostracism has aroused considerable interest among researchers seeking to examine its potential impacts. Although the burgeoning literature has accumulated substantial understanding about the impacts of ostracism, current knowledge is still very limited. Whereas prior studies have mainly focused on how ostracism influences emotions, relationship satisfactions, self-regulation, and behaviors, relatively little research has examined how ostracized people comprehend ambiguous but potentially threatening social events in the environment. As Williams (2009) noted, considerable amount of research is required to fully understand the impacts of ostracism on different aspects of daily life. In particular, the present investigation aims to fill the knowledge gap by examining whether ostracism increases conspiracy beliefs, which may provide a way for ostracized people to promptly comprehend and make sense of different social events in daily life, but at the expense of accuracy. When people are ostracized or socially excluded, they perceive themselves as vulnerable because they cannot obtain the benefits associated with harmonious social relationships. Such feelings of vulnerability motivate ostracized people to closely monitor social environments in order to promptly detect and avoid potential dangers. When they encounter ambiguous events, they may tend to endorse conspiracy beliefs because they need to promptly comprehend the causes of these events to decide whether there are potential dangers, and because false alarms are often less costly than failing to recognize threatening situations. When ostracized people’s feelings of vulnerability are reduced through interventions, they should no longer believe in conspiracy theories. A series of studies will be conducted to test when and why ostracism promotes conspiracy beliefs, and to examine how to weaken the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs. Given the omnipresence of ostracism and conspiracies in every aspect of daily live, it is critical to understand how this negative interpersonal experience can influence conspiracy beliefs. A better understanding of the mechanisms and contexts involved in triggering and reducing ostracized people’s conspiracy beliefs can help to advance existing theories and develop intervention programs that enable people to better cope with the negative consequences of ostracism. 社會排斥是指被拒絕或忽略。因為社會排斥無處不在，研究人員對探討它對人的潛在影響有相當大的興趣。雖然學術文獻對於社會排斥的影響有一定的了解，目前的知識仍然十分有限。以往的研究主要集中探討社會排斥如何影響情緒，關係滿意度，自我調整，和行為。相對較少的研究曾探討被社會排斥的人會如何理解社會上一些含糊但具有潛在威脅的事情。Williams (2009) 指出，相當數量的研究仍然需要進行，以充分了解社會排斥對日常生活上不同方面的影響。本研究旨在探討社會排斥會否令人更相信陰謀論。當人們被排斥時，他們會認為自己是脆弱的，因為他們無法獲得和諧人際關係所帶來的益處。這些脆弱的感覺會促使被排斥的人密切留意社會環境，以便及時發現並避免潛在危險。當他們遇到模棱兩可的事件時，他們可能會更傾向於相信陰謀論，因為他們需要及時理解這些事件的原因以決定是否有潛在危險，而且由於誤報往往比沒有發現受到威脅的代價更低。當人們被排斥後所產生的脆弱感覺通過干預措施被降低時，他們應該不再相信陰謀論。我們將進行一系列的研究以探討社會排斥在什麼情況下會導致人們更相信陰謀論，和探討如何削弱社會排斥對陰謀論的影響。鑒於社會排斥和陰謀論在日常生活中各個方面都無處不在，了解社會排斥和陰謀論之間的關係是一個重要的心理學課題。本研究的發現可望有助於推進現有理論和制定干預方案，使人們能夠更好地應對社會排斥所帶來的負面影響。

28603715.label: Realisation of objectives
28603715.value: This project aims to test when and why ostracism promotes conspiracy beliefs and to examine how to weaken the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs. All of the project objectives have been successfully achieved. Realization of Objective 1: We have empirically tested whether ostracism increases people’s tendency to endorse conspiracy beliefs. Realization of Objective 2: We have developed a new theoretical model that elucidates the psychological mechanism underlying the link between ostracism and conspiracy beliefs. We have also systematically investigated whether heightened vulnerability mediates the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs and considered other possible psychological processes in influencing the relationship. In particular, the results of a series of correlational and experimental studies revealed that ostracized participants reported higher levels of vulnerability and were more inclined to endorse conspiracy theories in various real-life and hypothetical situations than their nonostracized counterparts. Furthermore, the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs was significantly mediated by enhanced feelings of vulnerability. We also ruled out the possibility that changes in negative mood following ostracism can account for the link between ostracism and conspiracy beliefs and found that vulnerability still significantly mediated the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs after controlling for the influence of negative mood. Realization of Objective 3: We have tested the effectiveness of utilizing situational interventions in mitigating the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs. Specifically, we found that a brief self-affirmation exercise (i.e., offering participants a chance to reaffirm their important values) would reduce ostracized people’s tendency to endorse conspiracy theories. Realization of Objective 4: We have also examined whether the context in which the conspiracy theories evolve moderates the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs. We found that the negative impact of ostracism can be alleviated if people perceive that the context of the conspiracy theories is irrelevant to them.

28603715.label: Major findings and research outcome
28603715.value: In this project, we have formulated an innovative theoretical model to explicate the psychological mechanism underlying the effect of ostracism and conspiracy beliefs and exemplify how to weaken ostracized people’s tendency to endorse conspiracy beliefs. We have also empirically tested the hypotheses derived from the theoretical model. Adopting a multi-method approach, the current studies provided converging evidence showing ostracism increases conspiracy beliefs through increased vulnerability and that self-affirmation exercise effectively weakened the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs (Poon, Chen, & Wong, 2020). Moreover, we found that vulnerability still significantly mediated the link between ostracism and conspiracy beliefs after controlling for the effects of negative mood (Poon et al., 2020). We further found that the negative impacts of ostracism can be moderated by people’s dispositional characteristics, such that people with high trait mindfulness were less susceptible to the negative influences of ostracism (Poon & Jiang, 2020). We also found that the negative impacts of ostracism can be ameliorated by various contextual factors and situational interventions, such as nature exposure (Poon, Teng, Wong, & Chen, 2016), importance of following social rules (Poon & Teng, 2017), and perceived costs of their decisions (Poon & Wong, 2019). These findings have been published in top-tier peer-refereed international journals in psychology, such as Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, Mindfulness, Journal of Environmental Psychology, and Psychology of Violence. We have also presented these findings in various international conferences, including the Association for Psychological Science Annual Convention and the International Convention of Psychological Science.

28603715.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28603715.value: Our correlational and experimental studies provided converging evidence unveiling that feelings of vulnerability can account for the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs. Future research may test other potential psychological processes in elucidating the link between ostracism and conspiracy beliefs. Moreover, the present research unfolded a brief self-affirmation exercise to weaken the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs. Future studies may consider the application of self-affirmation in attenuating other detrimental impacts of ostracism and helping people effectively cope with ostracism and other related forms of interpersonal maltreatment. Finally, the current research only focused on the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs. It would be worthwhile if future research examines how post-ostracism increase in conspiracy beliefs carries further implications in people’s psychosocial functioning and subjective well-being.

28603715.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28603715.value: The current research revealed that ostracism makes people become vulnerable, thereby increasing their tendency to endorse conspiracy theories. It also found that self-affirmation can effectively weaken the effect of ostracism on conspiracy beliefs. Altogether, these findings carry both practical and theoretical implications for the role of vulnerability in influencing various responses following ostracism and the use of self-affirmation in ameliorating the detrimental effects of ostracism. The current research also advances existing theories and provides novel insights into the development of intervention programs that enable people to better cope with the negative impacts of ostracism and related forms of interpersonal maltreatment.

28603815.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28603815.value: 家居摩擦：晚期現代主義、英國小說及文學中款待客人的問題

28603815.label: Project Objectives
28603815.value: To identify the significance of hospitality as an overlooked yet critical paradigm in late modernist English novels. To investigate the extent to which domestic renderings of host-guest tensions were used to explore broader political and historical issues leading up to, during and following the Second World War. To demonstrate that changing understandings of local and international relations lay at the heart of such explorations. To situate late modernist representations of a crisis in domestic relations between host and guest within and against a novelistic tradition of hospitality and to consider the implications of this positioning for our understanding of the development of the English novel.

28603815.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28603815.value: Building on the recent surge of interest in hospitality, both as a philosophical concept and as a literary critical paradigm, this two-year project proposes to examine fraught literary representations of domestic forms of hospitality and host-guest relations in a number of late modernist English novels, from the late 1920s to the post-war period, revolving around the global catastrophe of the Second World War. It aims to investigate the multiple ways in which seemingly insignificant representations of household tensions invoke and reflect upon larger political and historical issues; more specifically, acts of political diplomacy and the reception of refugees, on the one hand, and the decline of the British Empire in parallel with the rise of the welfare state, on the other. Troubling visits, sanctioned or unsanctioned, recur in the fiction of this period and the clash between the theory and practice of hospitality repeatedly figures as a core narrative dilemma with meaning beyond the personal exchange. Above all, the project seeks to probe the complex implications of these visions of problematic host-guest exchanges in the context of an English literary tradition of fictional acts of household reception, at least as old as the novel itself. It is a perceptible crisis point in hospitable relations delineated in late modernist writing, reflecting a broader international crisis but equally a critical turning point in the history of the English novel, which will form the focus of the study. This dual dimension is exemplified in the closing image of an annexed house of fictional hospitality—family home, yet also archetypal literary model, overtaken by military army—at the end of Evelyn Waugh's Brideshead Revisited (1945), a novel nominally structured around the act of visiting. Not only is such an archetypal model rendered defunct or outdated by the war, it is transformed from the inside in the post-war era by new voices and cross-cultural perspectives. Drawing on the important philosophical work of Emmanuel Levinas, the project will explore the ways in which an ethical approach to alterity is put on trial by a number of late-modernist and post-war novelists including Elizabeth Bowen, Evelyn Waugh, Elizabeth Taylor, Patrick Hamilton, Rose Macaulay and Muriel Spark. In line with the more recent theoretical interventions of Giorgio Agamben and Jacques Derrida (via Immanuel Kant) and with equal attention to archival material, it will further approach such interrogative treatments of host-guest relations from the perspectives of territorial and human rights. ‘款客之道’ 這個理念既是哲學概念，又是文學批評之範籌 ，它近年在學術界頗受重視。以此為基礎，這項為期兩年的研究計畫將會圍繞二次大戰殃及全球的災難性後果作為討論中心，審視幾部由二十世紀二十年代至後二戰時期，英國晚期現代主義小說中，所呈現的家庭化的款客之道與主客關系。此計畫的研究目的，是檢視在文本中看似無關緊要的家庭張力如何複雜地反映，引喚出更深廣的歷史政治議題。更確切而言，這些議題一方面包括外交政治動作和難民接收等問題，另一方則關乎大英帝國的衰敗及於此同時，福利國家的興起。不管是深受，或未受限制，令人費神不安的探訪情節恆常地出現在這時期的小說中。而呈現在這些小說裡的‘待客之道’ 在理論和現實層面的沖突，更重複地被用作核心的敘述難題。這些由此沖突引起的難題之所以如此重要，是因為它們的涵意遠比人際交集中所能透露的答案更深遂。尤其重要的是，此計畫將在小說化的家庭接待活動，這一項歷史悠遠的英語文學傳統的背境下，探究這些有問題的主客互動所帶來的複雜意涵。晚期英國現代主義小說中所描繪的主客關系，很明顯已經瀕臨崩潰。這現象折射出的不只更廣泛的國際危機，同樣重要的是，它亦是英語小說史的轉捩點，此項研究的焦點所在。伊夫琳。沃的《重返布萊茲布海德莊園》（1945），一部以接待、探訪為結構主軸的小說的卒章的意象－一個被吞併的家居，體現了這二元性：一處家庭居所，同時作為一文學原型，被軍隊所強佔。後二戰時期不但令這文學原型變得不合時宜或再無用處，它所帶來的新思維和跨文化視角，亦使這文學原型從內而外地蛻變。 建基於伊曼紐爾。列維納斯的重要哲學著作，此研究將探索人在面對他者性(alterity) 時富有道德的處理手法，如何被英國晚期現代主義者，和後二戰時期小說家，包括伊利莎白·鮑恩、伊夫琳·沃、伊麗莎白·泰勒、派翠克·咸美、露絲·麥考利，與穆里爾·斯巴克等多方位挑戰。沿用喬治·阿甘本和雅克·德希達（籍伊曼紐。康德）較近期的理論介入，與同等重要的檔案材料，此研究會以領土權和人權的角度，對已被深入探討的主客關系作更細緻的說明。

28603815.label: Realisation of objectives
28603815.value: I would like to reiterate my thanks to the UGC for the generous grant which has given me the opportunity to devote time and resources to developing this research project. The grant has enabled me to access materials in remote archives, to translate certain key materials into English, to present my research at a number of international conferences, to develop and publish articles in prominent journals, to impart my knowledge in a pedagogical capacity through teaching and workshops, to advise and train a team of talented student assistants, and to lay the foundations for future intellectual work. It was a rewarding two years and I am immensely grateful for the support of the UGC in undertaking this research. My work on this project took place over a 24-month period from May 2016 to April 2018. During the first year of the project, I carried out the bulk of the data collection on specific authors through visiting a number of archives in the United States: the Daniel A. Reed Library in Fredonia, New York; the Harry Ransom Center in Austin, Texas; and the McFarlin Library in Tulsa, Oklahoma. During the second year of the project, I spent approximately six weeks working at the British Library in London where I accessed miscellaneous materials unavailable in Hong Kong as well as consulting a range of newspaper and exile periodicals from the Second World War. In this year, I also worked closely with a Senior Research Assistant to translate some of the most relevant German language materials, particularly from the Stefan Zweig archive in Fredonia. Achievement of Objectives: The objectives of this project were largely achieved though not in the expected way. The project evolved in accordance with the quality of the collected data. In other words, the archival research I carried out in the first year significantly altered the direction and scope of the project since the archival material supplied the data for analysis. Firstly, I was forced to adjust my focus in terms of authorial examples. For instance, I initially saw Stefan Zweig as a somewhat peripheral figure in the overall project but the letters and documents I encountered during my visit to the Stefan Zweig Archive at the Daniel A. Reed Library offered very rich source material and inspired two of the articles I came to write. Similarly, the Muriel Spark papers proved to be very fruitful and germane to the topic and her work has assumed a more prominent position as a result. By contrast, certain other writers have been sidelined somewhat in the project due to the paucity of materials I found in their archival files. My original aim during my time at the Harry Ransom Center was to study the files of Elizabeth Bowen, Arthur Koestler, Sam Selvon, Patrick Hamilton and Evelyn Waugh. Unfortunately, these particular files did not yield the kind of information I was hoping for. Instead, I spent considerable time in exploring the enormous P.E.N. collection. The P.E.N. was formed in the 1920s as an organisation tasked with addressing and protecting the rights and freedoms of writers on an international level. I was interested in the work of the London branch of this organisation, particularly its role in receiving and helping refugee writers in Britain during the wartime period. I found a wealth of useful materials on the P.E.N., both at the Harry Ransom Center and at the McFarlin Library, which I continue to work through. Secondly, the concept of empathy emerged as a key conceptual paradigm to consider alongside and in relation to hospitality (both involve an engagement between self and other) and I have devoted considerable energy to exploring these two concepts together as a theoretical and conceptual basis for the project. The project has thus matured into a study of authorial responses to the problematic engagement of discourses of hospitality and empathy in political and institutional life around the Second World War in the context of wider scenes of suffering and displacement. Conferences, Dissemination and Publications: I presented work from this project, drawing heavily on my archival materials, at a range of international conferences during the 24-month period, including the annual conference of the ‘Space Between Society’ at McGill University in Montreal, Canada (June 2016), ‘Historical Modernisms’ at Senate House in London (December 2016), the British Association for Modernist Studies (BAMS) conference at the University of Birmingham (June 2017), and the Modernist Studies Association (MSA) conference at the University of Amsterdam (August 2017). I also organised a seminar on the ‘Analogical Imagination’ at the American Comparative Literature Association (ACLA) conference at the University of Utrecht in July 2017, in which scholars from the UK, the United States, Germany, New Zealand, Hong Kong and the Netherlands participated. In February 2018, I was invited to speak on my archival work on the P.E.N. at a symposium on ‘Cosmopolitanism: Literature, Language, Pedagogy’ at Trinity College Dublin in Ireland. The project has produced four key research outputs. The first article, an extended version of a paper delivered at Senate House in London and also prompted by my visit to the Daniel A. Reed Library, was published earlier this year as part of a special issue on ‘Archives, Authority, Aura’ in Papers on Language and Literature. It concerns a postcard written by Salvador Dalí to Stefan Zweig. I used this postcard as a basis for some broader reflections on Zweig’s status as a political exile subject to the hospitality of others as well as the experience of carrying out archival work in the twenty-first century. The second article, drawing on archival materials from the Daniel A. Reed Library and based on the paper I delivered at McGill University, is due to be published by Novel: A Forum on Fiction in August 2019. It focuses on the work of Zweig and his experience of empathy under wartime surveillance as an exiled guest in Britain and the Americas during the 1930s and 1940s. It was accepted by Novel without any required revisions. This is a significant achievement given that this is a top-tier journal which ranks consistently in the Q1 quartile for literature and literary theory journals. I have completed a full draft of a third article on the work of Muriel Spark. This article, a composite and extension of the two papers delivered at the universities of Birmingham and Utrecht and utilising materials from the Muriel Spark Papers at the McFarlin Library in Tulsa, concerns Spark’s use of narrative distance as a response to an emerging political discourse of care after the Second World War. I am planning to submit this to another Q1 journal, English Literary History (ELH). I am currently revising the draft very carefully in order to ensure the article is of the high standard required of this journal. The fourth article is currently in progress and will combine ideas from the two papers delivered in the University of Amsterdam and Trinity College Dublin on the subject of the English P.E.N. and the bureaucracy of hospitality during the war. This paper draws on extensive materials in the P.E.N. archives both at the Harry Ransom Center and at the McFarlin Library. It will be ready to send to Literature and History this summer.

28603815.label: Major findings and research outcome
28603815.value: My research has amply demonstrated that both hospitality and empathy came to the fore as key literary paradigms during the war and in the post-war period, in response to the developing refugee crisis. I explore this emergence in line with the precarious position of the ‘guest’ figure or subject of empathy in both Zweig articles as well as in my research on the P.E.N. In exploring the P.E.N. archives, I observed a paradox in that organisation’s conception of hospitality during the 1930s and 1940s, a paradox that might be better understood in terms of a clash between a social etiquette of hospitality (expressed through P.E.N. social gatherings) and a wider politics of hospitality (expressed in its drive to facilitate refugee reception in Britain). Similarly, my two articles on Zweig show that representations of interpersonal and domestic acts of reception and empathy register broader political and historical tensions. Zweig’s late writing, for example, forms an attempt to work through his own conflicting wartime experiences of compassion, as recipient of political and personal forms of hospitality, but it also offers a sustained reflection on the implications of a broader crisis in empathy and hospitality around the Second World War. His work exemplifies a kind of anxiety surrounding the appropriate depiction of suffering that would come to shape key strands of postwar writing, philosophy, and political theory. This is an anxiety that also enters into Muriel Spark’s writing which, as I have found, dramatizes the intersection of local and international concerns; The Girls of Slender Means, set against the backdrop both of the emergence of the welfare state within Britain and the devastating development of atomic power beyond Britain, manifests a distrust of emotional empathy, on a political level, in favour of an unempathetic perspective, on a narrative level. For Spark, the reality of suffering must be met not with sentimental expressions of care but with clarity of purpose and her work, as such, offers a critique of rising forms of empathetic state surveillance. In each of these cases, representations of domestic friction between hosts and guests, empaths and objects of empathy, agents and recipients of charity and compassion, negotiate and trouble the line between the personal and the political at a time of great change, both nationally and internationally.

28603815.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28603815.value: My work on hospitality and refugee reception around the Second World War has led organically to an interest in questions of narrative empathy and biopolitics in women’s writing of the mid-century period and it is in this direction that I see my research developing in the future. I have become interested, in particular, in a strand of mid-century fiction that saw women writers move away from the more empathic narrative modes of their modernist predecessors, those modernists concerned with getting inside their characters heads, towards more unempathetic forms of narration which emphasise cognitive over affective empathy. I interpret this, in part, as a reaction to the rise of empathetic models of governance (typified by the welfare state) but also as a response to the forms of emotional manipulation that accompanied extremist politics of the 1930s and 1940s. I hope to investigate the degree to which these unempathetic narratives represent a response to the strategic engagement of empathy and care in biopolitical discourses and methods of control. I await the outcome of a GRF funding application on this project and envisage both ECS and GRF projects as contributing to a full-length monograph on the topic in due course.

28603815.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28603815.value: This project examined fraught literary representations of interpersonal interactions with suffering subjects in late modernist and post-war writing through the concepts of hospitality and empathy. In analysing works by mid-century British writers like Muriel Spark as well as exiled writers in Britain like Stefan Zweig, it explored the ways in which these representations invoked and reflected upon questions of refugee reception, immigration and welfare leading up to, during and after the Second World War. It further revealed that these writers as well as those advocates for exile and refugee literature working within organisations such as the P.E.N. struggled with the question of how best to respond to situations of suffering, whether in terms of narrating that suffering or in providing more tangible forms of support. In its consideration of troubling portrayals of relationships between guests and hosts, sufferers and surveyors of suffering, patrons and beneficiaries, the project explored the shifting dynamic of power that defines such exchanges and, at a remove, writers’ own attempts to negotiate that dynamic in narrative terms.

28605215.label: Project Objectives

28605215.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28605215.value: Mathematics Disability (MD) and Reading Disability (RD) are two major learning disabilities, each affecting around 10% of the population. The two disabilities co-occur at a high rate. More than 25% of the people with one disability also have the other disability, which is well above chance level. The issue of comorbidity (co-occurrence of two disabilities) between MD and RD, however, does not receive much attention from the psychological literature. It is not clear why the two disabilities co-occur at such a high rate. The current proposed study therefore aims at comparing different hypotheses concerning comorbidity (alternate forms model, phenocopy hypothesis, double dissociation hypothesis, common etiology hypothesis, and cognitive subtype hypothesis) in terms of explaining the MD+RD comorbidity issue. A large sample of first graders will undergo a brief screening on their reading and mathematics achievement. By employing a stringent cutoff (i.e., 10th percentile) and repeated testing (twice in two years), three groups of children with persistent learning disabilities (MD, RD, MD+RD, N=35 for each group) will be identified. The large initial sample allows the use of stringent cutoff and repeated assessment in identifying children with MD and/or RD and hence reduces the false positive rate in the identification process. Their cognitive profiles in reading-related, math-related, and general domains will be compared with an age- and IQ-matched control group. The relevance of different hypotheses in explaining the MD+RD comorbidity issue will be compared. The current study is one of the first few studies which examine the MD+RD comorbidity issue in a comprehensive manner (e.g., repeated testing with stringent cutoff, comprehensive battery of domain-general cognitive measures), which would enable us to compare the relevance of different hypotheses in explaining the MD+RD comorbidity issue and hence to identify the potential reasons for the high comorbidity rate. This is also the first MD+RD comorbidity study in the Chinese setting, which will inform us about whether the MD+RD comorbidity issue is language-dependent. The current project also provides a valuable opportunity to identify any factors that are uniquely related to the comorbid MD+RD group, so that interventions can be tailor-made to suit the needs of these children. As both poor reading and poor mathematical skills are related to low financial and psychological well-being in adulthood, the comorbidity group is certainly one of the groups that are most at risk which our society cannot afford to ignore. 數學障礙和閱讀障礙均是主要的學習障礙，各自影響大概10% 的人口。這兩種學習障礙的共病率很高。在患有其中一種學習障礙的人中，至少有25% 同時患有另一種學習障礙。這共病率顯著地高於正常的水平。然而，數學障礙與閱讀障礙的共病，卻沒有在心理學的文獻中引起其應得到的關注。我們並不清楚為何兩種學習障礙的共病率會如此高。本研究希望藉測試各種共病理論 (異表徵理論、表徵模擬理論、功能雙分離理論、共病因理論、及認知次分類理論)，找出數學障礙與閱讀障礙共病的成因。 是次研究將邀請過千名就讀小學一年級的兒童，參與一項為期兩年的篩選，以找出一些數學及/或閱讀能力長期屬於最低10%的學童。這三組學童 (純數學障礙、純閱讀障礙、數學障礙與閱讀障礙共病，每組約35人) 將被邀請作出更深入的評估。本研究小組會將他們各方面的認知表現與其同齡及智力相約的對照組作比較，以找出數學障礙與閱讀障礙共病的成因。 本研究是少數關於數學障礙與閱讀障礙共病的研究。通過全面且嚴謹的研究設計 (如重覆篩選、嚴謹的取錄線、全面的認知能力評估)，本研究能夠更準確地找出數學障礙與閱讀障礙共病的成因。本研究亦是首個在漢語領域的相關研究，結果能讓我們了解到語言系統對數學障礙與閱讀障礙共病的影響。是次研究將提供一個寶貴的機會，讓我們找出與數學障礙與閱讀障礙共病相關的因素，藉此設計出對應同時患有這兩種學習障礙的學童的需要的相關培訓，以提升這群學童學習數學和閱讀的能力。由於數學和閱讀能力均是預測成人生活指標的重要能力，同時在這兩項能力出現困難的學童，絕對值得社會的關注。

28605215.label: Realisation of objectives
28605215.value: 1. To establish the prevalence rate of MD and the comorbidity rate between MD and RD in the local context. The prevalence rate of MD and the comorbidity rate between MD and RD were calculated based on a total of 1,833 second-graders. Children who scored below the 10th percentile in their mathematics/reading achievement at two time points (end of Grade 1 and middle of Grade 2) were considered as persistent MD/RD respectively. Among the 1,833 children, 88 of them met the criteria of persistent MD, 152 of them met the criteria of persistent RD, and 36 of them met both criteria and were considered as having persistent comorbid MD and RD. The prevalence rate of persistent MD was therefore 4.8%. Among children with persistent RD, 23.7% of them also had persistent MD, and among children with persistent MD, 40.9% of them also had persistent RD. The total prevalence rate of persistent comorbid RD x MD was 2.0%. This objective was fully achieved. 2. To identify the cognitive deficits experienced by children with MD, RD, and MD+RD respectively. To examine the cognitive deficits experienced by children with persistent MD, RD, and MD+RD respectively, 2 x 2 ANCOVAs were conducted, with children’s nonverbal IQ and level of inattention serving as the control variables and their performance in the cognitive measures being the dependent variables. A total of 244 children were included in the analyses (53 children with pure persistent RD, 35 children with pure persistent MD, 20 children with persistent comorbid, 136 typically-achieving children; 5 children with persistent RDs were excluded due to missing data). From the ANCOVA results, significant main effects of MD were observed in several cognitive domains, namely visuospatial working memory [F(1,238) = 19.60, p < .001, partial η² = .076], updating [F(1,238) = 8.79, p = .003, partial η² = .036], processing speed [F(1,238) = 38.51, p < .001, partial η² = .139], naming speed [F(1,238) = 32.08, p < .001, partial η² = .119], and visual attention [F(1,238) = 30.00, p < .001, partial η² = .112], suggesting that children with MD suffered from deficits in these constructs. Significant main effects of RD were observed in two cognitive constructs, namely shifting ability [F(1,238) = 7.40, p = .007, partial η² = .030] and naming speed [F(1,238) = 7.03, p = .009, partial η² = .029], meaning that children with RD were slower in naming objects and switching between different cognitive tasks. There were no meaningful MD x RD interaction effects, and children with persistent comorbid MD x RD appeared to have an additive combination of the cognitive deficits experienced by the single persistent LD groups. As the cognitive deficits experienced by the three LD groups were identified, this objective was fully achieved. 3. To determine the mechanisms underlying MD+RD comorbidity by comparing the relevance of different comorbidity hypotheses in explaining concerned comorbidity. The current project was set out to examine five different comorbidity models, namely the alternative form model, the phenocopy model, the double dissociation model, the common etiology model, and the cognitive subtypes model. Based on the aforementioned ANCOVA results, the persistent comorbid group had an additive combination of the cognitive deficits experienced by the single persistent LD groups. Such additive combination of cognitive deficits provided support to neither the alternative form model (which suggested that the two disabilities shared the same cognitive profile) nor the phenocopy model (which suggested that the comorbid group shared the same cognitive profile with one of the disability groups, but not both). The deficit in naming speed was the only cognitive deficit shared by both RD and MD, and no RD x MD interaction was observed, indicating that the magnitude of naming speed deficit in the comorbid group was sum of the magnitudes of deficits observed in the single disability groups. This is consistent with neither the common etiology model nor the cognitive subtype model (which are indicated by an under-additive and over-additive magnitude of deficit respectively). The double dissociation model, which suggests that the comorbid group should have a cognitive profile that is the additive combination of the cognitive profiles of the single disability groups, was the only model supported in the current study. The current findings converged with those double dissociations observed in other RD x MD comorbidity studies in alphabetic languages (Moll et al., 2015; Raddatz et al., 2017; Wilson et al., 2015) and thus increased the generalizability of the double dissociation model of RD and MD across different linguistic and cultural contexts. The relevance of five comorbidity models was compared based on their fit to the current data and the best-fitting model was identified. This objective was fully achieved.

28605215.label: Major findings and research outcome
28605215.value: Based on the data collected from the current project, various interesting findings have been observed. On top of the aforementioned cognitive profiles of different LD groups (as reported in manuscript 3 below), the PI also observed significant difficulties in decoding arithmetic word problems among the persistent MD group (as reported in manuscript 1) as well as a significant relation between visual attention and arithmetic that was mediated enumeration skills (as reported in manuscript 2). Furthermore, the PI is now collaborating with other researchers on the fourth manuscript concerning the relations between RAN and reading versus mathematics. 28605215.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28605215.value: Based on the current data, the PI has identified the cognitive profile of children with MD. Such information is of high practical significance as it allows educators to better identify children with MD in Hong Kong as well as to design interventions that target at their specific cognitive deficits. Based on such findings, the PI is now collaborating with the Education Bureau in preparing a proposal concerning the development of a comprehensive assessment and support system for children with MD in Hong Kong. Such a system is currently lacking in Hong Kong, and there is no systematic way of identifying children with difficulties in mathematics. If the project is funded, children with MD can be systematically identified, and their learning needs can be catered by the specifically designed interventions that target at their cognitive deficits.

28605215.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28605215.value: The current project aimed to examine the cognitive profiles of children with persistent mathematics disability (MD), persistent reading disability (RD), and persistent comorbid mathematics and reading disabilities (MD x RD). Over 1,800 second graders were assessed on their reading and mathematics achievement as well as some cognitive capacities such as working memory, executive functions, processing and naming speed as well as visual attention. The results suggested that children with persistent MD had difficulties in various cognitive domains, including visuospatial working memory, processing and naming speed, as well as visual attention, while children with persistent RD were slower in naming objects and switching between cognitive tasks. Children with persistent comorbidity showed a combination of the aforementioned deficits. The results suggested that persistent MD and persistent RD were two independent learning disabilities, at least on the cognitive level. The findings increased our knowledge concerning the difficulties faced by children with different learning disabilities, and such knowledge will be used to develop a comprehensive system for assessing and supporting children with MD in Hong Kong.

28605415.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28605415.value: 本研究聚焦於民國時期的古代文學研究，並以個案研究作為主要方法。 1917年文學革命後，古代文學不斷受抨擊。然而細察民國時期的古代文學研究，會發現無論在研究視域、目的、方法、抑或採用資源，這時期的古代文學研究都與以往的不同；其中，抒情概念元素的置入與提倡是最為觸目的一處，而這又與新文學背景息息相關。至於李商隱和黃仲則兩位古代詩人，在這段時期廣受關注，並且有大量研究成果。故本研究以之切入，能具體而深入地分析以下問題： 1. 1917-1949年的古代文學研究與新文學背景的關係； 2. 此時期將「抒情」元素概念置入古代文學研究的方法和意義； 3. 此時期的研究成果的現代性與學術史意義 本研究將搜羅、整理和分析這時期的報章副刊、文藝雜誌，出版書刊等相關的文本資料，以論文和專書形式分享研究成果。 This proposal focuses on the Studies of Classical Chinese Literature in the Republican period and uses case studies as the major research method. After the Literature Revolution in 1917, Classical Literature received criticisms unceasingly. However, with conscientious observation on the studies of Classical Chinese literature in the Republican period, one may discover that it was different from the previous studies in terms of research field, objective, methodology or resources being used; the insertion and advocate of lyrical conception which closely related to the background of New Literature was the most conspicuous part; while Li Shangyin and Huang Zhongze, the two ancient poets, had received great concern and enormous research achievement within this period. By deeply penetrate into it, this proposal specifically and throughly analyzes the following questions: 1. Relationship between the studies of Classical Chinese literature and background of the New Literature in 1979 -1949; 2. Methods and significances of inserting lyrical conception into the studies of Classical Chinese literature within this period; 3. Modernity and academic historical significances of research achievement within this period. This proposal would gather, collate and analyze relevant texts such as newspaper, literary supplements, literary magazines and publications to share the research achievement in form of academic papers and academic book.

28605415.label: Realisation of objectives
28605415.value: 本研究從「抒情」角度切入，考察民國時期的古代文學研究，並對照當時及後來文學史的編寫方式，審視這時期這方面的研究，有否進入文學史書寫並成為定論。本研究選擇黃仲則和李商隱作為重點研究對象，乃注意到前者（黃仲則）在民國時期出現研究熱潮，而且研究的焦點和所見，跟清人的觀點大異其趣。而後者（李商隱）則從宋至民國一直受人關注，尤其清代產生箋釋李詩之風，體現出與前人不同的審美趣味。到了民國，學者對李商隱詩的接受出現了分歧，而這又跟當時的學風和古典文學的本質追求有關。於是，本研究將兩個具體個案的相關資料作了系統整理，及深入探研，最後撰寫了幾篇論文，完成本專項的目標。 目標一：「抒情」概念的變異與文學革命背景的關係 本研究遍閱搜集到的資料，留意到民國時期討論古代文學的「抒情」時，有突出愛情的傾向，這種對愛情的重視，跟古代語境援用的「抒情」概念並不一樣。「抒情」一向包括各種情，然在價值判斷時往往頌揚家國民族，而輕個人情愛。民國時期則不然，他們受「人的文學」號召，及抒情主義薰染，普遍欣賞古代作家的愛情生活，以之為真實內在的反映。以上發現，在本專項寫出的研究成果普遍應用，也有專門論述。 目標二：李商隱研究和黃仲則研究所反映的古代文學研究的新發展 兩個個案的研究都能夠反映當時的古代文學研究新發展。黃仲則和李商隱都有戀愛軼聞，並都由新文學家撰成專著（章衣萍《黃仲則評傳》及蘇雪林《李義山戀愛事跡考》）；二書之出現亦引發了當時學人對古人情愛的更深廣關注。黃仲則在民國時期的重塑，全面地體現在相關的著述及詩選，也直接影響了後來文學史對黃仲則的書寫。而李商隱的戀愛事跡發掘，使當時學人重思了詩歌箋評的方向及功能，對於深厚的箋釋傳統如何切合現代所需作出了種種反思。 目標三：古代文學研究與文學革命背景的關係 當進一步理清這些文章的出現背景和闡釋邏輯時，便發現文學革命不僅主導著新文學的構建和發展，也影響著古代文學研究的方向。可以說，當時的古代文學研究正努力尋求現代價值，刻意挪用新文學、西方文藝資源是他們尋求古典新義的方法之一。本專項特意就胡適文學革命號召、周作人「人的文學」主張、國故整理運動、廚村白村和戀愛論的引進等思潮，論述它們與當時古代文學研究的關係，證明了當時古代文學研究也呼應著新文藝思潮，完成其從舊到新的轉化。而延伸探討的香港新文藝雜誌《紅豆》如何詮釋和發揚古典新義，也能從側面了解文學革命背景對古代文學研究的影響力。 目標四：古代文學研究的現代性及意義 現代性不是一個時間詞，本專項特別關注研究者的身份（新文學作家）、與新文學家的關係（作者與胡適、郁達夫等人的關係）、新方法的運用（個人主義、抒情主義）、新體例的出版物（新式叢書選本），目的都在論述古代文學研究的現代性是多維度的。 簡言之，本專項充分地完成預設目標，並已撰寫及出版相關文章。本專項亦有延續性，未來尚有進一步的成果陸續發表。

28605415.label: Major findings and research outcome
28605415.value: 本研究從「抒情」角度切入，考察民國時期的古代文學研究，並對照當時及後來文學史的編寫方式，審視這時期這方面的研究，有否進入文學史書寫並成為定論。本研究選擇黃仲則和李商隱作為重點研究對象，乃注意到前者（黃仲則）在民國時期出現研究熱潮，而且研究的焦點和所見，跟清人的觀點大異其趣。而後者（李商隱）則從宋至民國一直受人關注，尤其清代產生箋釋李詩之風，體現出與前人不同的審美趣味。到了民國，學者對李商隱詩的接受出現了分歧，而這又跟當時的學風和古典文學的本質追求有關。於是，本研究將兩個具體個案的相關資料作了系統整理，及深入探研，最後撰寫了幾篇論文，完成本專項目標。 本研究發現，民國時期學者研究古代文學時，側重以「情愛」來闡釋「抒情」，而這又特別體現在為古代文學研究尋繹現代意義時。當時受五四運動影響，學人對文學探求人生及人的內在情感產生強烈興趣，加上受東洋和西方的思想、尤其是戀愛論影響，故出現了一批專以發掘古人戀愛事跡的研究文章，而黃仲則和李商隱便是熱門討論的對象。二人既是才子、又有戀愛軼聞，加上遭際不順，故戀愛可以成為詩人「苦悶的象徵」，以抒其情。本研究進一步發現，當這些文化背景引入作家研究時，改變了以往的傳記寫作方式和目的，這就等於由軼事好奇和整理，影響到評斷作家價值的層面。另一方面，本研究結合當時的出版文化，如出版社之經營環境及競爭，探討了這種研究新方向如何在叢書編纂中傳遞到普羅大眾。 於是，本研究能夠從具體現象，深入到知識構建和傳遞（文學史）的層面。

28605415.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28605415.value: 本研究尚有進一步伸延的空間。例如三十年代中期抗戰思潮的興盛，對以「情愛」主導「抒情」的路向有所調整，本研究在論文雖已有提及，但未及展開論述；而且，抗戰時期的古代文學研究資料，散佚非常多，研究者僅從有限資源下作出收集整理，並未足以進行深入研討的資本。另一方面，地域與文學思潮的關係也可延伸探討，本研究所用的資料大都在上海或北京發表，但同時，這股思潮也深入到不同的地域，如香港。本研究進行期間，曾依手上材料撰寫過一篇關於一部香港新文藝期刊如何從研究古代文學中發展古典新義，若果能處理廣州、澳門等地方的相關思潮如何互動，當能展現一幅更精準、更有意義的嶺南文化圖景，說明嶺南學風與新文學思潮結合下如何「更新」古代文學研究的路向。

28605415.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28605415.value: This project investigates how the studies of Classical Chinese literature mutually influenced under the wave of Modern Literature. Literary Revolution obviously influenced the establishment and development of Modern Literature, but how the studies on Classical Literature proceed its transformation from old to new is still awaiting enough attention from the recent academy. This project focuses on Huang Zhongze and Li Shangyin. It is found that the researchers deliberately used modern literary ideas to conduct their research, explored many values in line with the modern literary thought, and they adjusted the traditional literary research methods at that time. At the result, their achievements and findings were presented in the literary selected works and literary history writings. In other words, this project allows us to know where some of the judgments and concepts of literary history come from and how. We will also know how foreign literary thought and publishing environment affect the transmission of Classical literature in that period.

28605615.label: Realisation of objectives
28605615.value: The overarching aim of the present research is to understand how creativity is related to the nature and quality of musical exposure through the lens of the arousal-and-mood hypothesis, postulates that music listening affects subsequent cognitive functioning through the indirect effect (or the mediation effect) of emotional reactions. Such hypothesis highlights the critical role of individuals’ emotional reactions in determining whether music listening has a beneficial effect on subsequent cognitive functioning. In achieving this overarching aim, the present research has the following specific objectives: 1. To extend the research on the arousal-and-mood hypothesis by applying two standardized creativity tests that captures different aspects of creativity; 2. To extend the research on the arousal-and-mood hypothesis by investigating both the immediate and sustaining effects of music listening on creativity; 3. To examine whether the types and the duration of the music effect in creative thinking can be moderated by individual characteristics in relation to emotional reactions towards musical stimuli. In the realization of these objectives, the following important research activities have been taken. I. Successful development of appropriate experiment materials The first step of the study was to develop the appropriate experimental materials (i.e., the musical excerpts) that fit into the nature of the present research. Because this research aimed to understand how a musical stimulus induces positive or negative emotions function differently on creativity, it was essential to ensure that the musical stimuli are able to reliably induce the corresponding emotional reactions. Taken reference from past research, the musical stimuli selected for this research consisted of 10-min excerpts of music that had been shown to successfully induce positive (i.e., Mozart’s Sonata for Two Pianos in D Major) or negative emotions (i.e., Albinoni’s Adagio in G Minor). In considering that music perception may be influenced by cultural factor, two 10-min music excerpts were extracted from a well-known Chinese music ‘Butterfly Lovers Violin Concerto,’ which was shown to induce positive or negative emotions in Zhang and Chen’s study (2009). A pilot study with 60 college students (28 males, 32 females; Mean age = 19.8 yeares, SD = 1.54) was conducted to examine the effectiveness of these musical stimuli in inducing the corresponding emotions. Manipulation check with paired-sample t-tests showed that participants showed significant change in their arousal and valence scores between the pre- and post-test conditions, suggesting the appropriateness of the selected musical materials for the study. II. Successful completion of the quantitative and qualitative studies The main study consisted of both a quantitative and a qualitative component. 1. The quantitative study In the quantitative study, we were able to successfully obtain data from a total of 714 students in Hong Kong (54.4% girls; mean age = 16.8 years, SD = 2.35). The participants were randomly assigned to three groups: a positive music group (n = 241), a negative music group (n = 240), and a control group (n = 233). Standardized measurements were used to assess the important constructs in the study: (1) Creative thinking were assessed with the Test for Creative ThinkingDrawing Production (TCT-DP) and the Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking (TTCT); (2) emotional reaction was assessed with the Affect Grid; and (3) individual characteristics in relation to emotional reactions were assessed with the Overexcitability Questionnaire-Two (OEQII). We tested both the immediate and sustaining effects of music listening on performance in the two standardized creativity tests. By analyzing these obtained data, we were able to achieve the research objectives well. First, Objective 2 is well achieved by the results that showed that both positively and negatively arousing music enhanced creative thinking; the results of the mediation analyses using Hayes’ PROCESS procedure for SPSS suggest that only arousal, and not valence, mediates the music-creativity relationship in both conditions, i.e., listening to positively or negatively arousing music. This pattern of finding was observed when creative thinking was measured by two different standardized creative thinking tests, namely the TCT-DP and the TTCT. While the TCT-DP aims to tap into one’s creative potential using a gestalt approach, the TTCT taps into one’s divergent thinking using a psychometric approach. The results suggest that a consistent pattern of findings was obtained to support the arousal-and-mood hypothesis when different creative thinking tests were used. Second, the data obtained in the present project suggest the critical role of individual characteristics (i.e., overexcitability) in determining one’s level of creative thinking, as well as the effect of music listening on one’s creative thinking. Specifically, the results the hierarchical multiple regression analysis suggest that three kinds of overexcitability (i.e., emotional overexcitability, imaginational overexcitability, and intellectual overexcitability) played the most significant role in determining one’s performance in a creativity test. Furthermore, individuals with higher overexcitability demonstrated a stronger and longer music effect on creative thinking. These results suggest that Objectives 3 and 4 are well achieved. 2. The qualitative study In line with the overarching aim of the research project, the qualitative study aimed to understand the underlying emotional experiences and mental processes relating to the effects of music listening on creative thinking via a qualitative approach. We interviewed 24 (22 female) college students immediately after they had listened to 10-min music excerpts and after completing assessments of their creative thinking. Results of content analysis suggest that music listening can facilitate creative thinking by optimizing individuals’ arousal levels and by strengthening individuals’ associative abilities, holistic perceptions and abstractions. All in all, the findings of the present study enrich the research on the arousal-and-mood hypothesis which highlights the important role of emotional reactions and individual differences in the music-creativity relationship. Drawing together the research findings generated from the present project supports that the overarching aim of the research is well achieved.

28605615.label: Major findings and research outcome
28605615.value: Overall, the findings of this project lend partial support to the arousal-and-mood hypothesis in the creativity domain, which enrich the discourse of the hypothesis and shed light on the understanding of the music-creativity link. Some interesting findings are highlighted below. 1. One important finding of the present study is its direct measure of the mediating roles of emotions (i.e., arousal and valence) in the relationship between music and creativity. Adding to the existing literature, this research presented direct empirical evidence with respect to the arousal-and-mood hypothesis by (1) employing a standardized measure of emotional reactions (i.e., the Affect Grid) to assess changes in arousal and valence in response to the music listening experience and (2) applying Hayes’ statistical procedure (Preacher & Hayes, 2008) to determine the mediation effect of arousal and valence on the relationship between music and creativity. 2. The present research illustrated that both positively and negatively arousing music contributed to creativity enhancement. While the arousal-and-mood hypothesis postulates that any optimally arousing stimulus that induces positive moods should enhance performance on cognitive tasks, the findings of our study show that both positive and negative emotions can enhance creative thinking, as long as the music experience can successfully arouse an individual’s emotion. These findings are important because they suggest that the generalizability of the arousal-and-mood hypothesis is not limited to positively aroused emotions. 3. The third important finding of the study showed that only arousal, and not valence, was a significant mediator of the music-creativity link. The finding differentiating the role of arousal and valence may enrich the discourse of the arousal-and-mood hypothesis, which posits that both arousal and valence play a parallel and equally important role in mediating the relationship between music exposure and cognitive functioning. 4. Our findings also supported the critical role of individual characteristics (i.e., overexcitability/OE) in determining one’s creativity, and the effect of music listening on creative thinking. Specifically, emotional, imaginational, and intellectual OEs played the most significant role. 5. The findings obtained from the in-depth interview suggest that associative abilities, holistic perceptions and abstractions constitute the important underlying mental processes that contribute to a positive music-creativity link. Most of these research findings have been shared with the scientific community through publications and conference presentations (please refer to Part C). It is also anticipated that two more publications will be produced based on these findings as the manuscripts are under preparation.

28605615.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28605615.value: Several potential research areas are worthwhile of further exploration. First, although the arousal-and-mood hypothesis generalizes that any pleasant or enjoyable stimulus, either musical or nonmusical, that arouses positive mood can enhance a wide range of cognitive functions, the present project focused merely on musical stimuli. Future research should be generalized to other types of musical stimuli and also to nonmusical stimuli. Second, creativity was assessed with only two standardized creativity tests (i.e., TCTDP and TTCT) in this project. Although these tests have been suggested to be a reliable and valid test of creative thinking, the TTCT and the TCT-DP was designed to tap into one’s divergent thinking and creative potential, respectively. It is important to explore whether the findings can be replicated if other creativity tests are used, especially when creative problem solving is tested. Third, participants in this study first listened to music and subsequently performed a creativity task; it is interesting to further explore whether similar or different results will be found if participants work on a creativity task while simultaneously listening to music. Future research should also explore whether similar or different results will be found in other cognitive domains.

28605615.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28605615.value: Can music make people smart? This project enriches the understanding regarding the effects of music on creative functioning. Demonstrating that the effect of music exposure is the result of an individual’s emotional reaction to musical stimuli helps to resolve an intriguing issue that for whom and under what circumstances listening to music enhances cognitive functioning and what type of music is effective. Such findings are important to explain why some past research support the idea that listening to a piece of music composed by Mozart or other composers can enhance cognitive functioning when others cannot. The generated findings imply that the potential benefits of music depend more on the interactions between individual factors and the type or style of music. Given that not all individuals benefit equally from all types of music, individuals might benefit from any piece of music that provides optimal arousal and evokes either a positive or a negative hedonic tone. Simplistic solutions such as the Mozart effect can give false impressions and unrealistic expectations. Highlighting the nature and the quality of music exposure and searching for the optimal music that arouses an individual’s appropriate emotional reactions would be more important for the facilitation of cognitive functioning.

28608115.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28608115.value: In Hong Kong, which knowledge-based economy depends on having an educated population, the increased manifestations of sustainability consciousness of the secondary school graduates who participate in tertiary education might illustrate the outcomes of the transformative learning ignited by the New Senior Secondary Liberal Studies (NSS LS) curriculum. The purpose of this study is two-fold: 1) to describe and analyze environmental aspects of the sustainability consciousness of secondary school graduates who have entered the tertiary institutions; and 2) to arrive at an understanding of what NSS LS curricular features might have fostered this and how we may use educational research to inform and align liberal education practices at all levels of the Hong Kong educational system. The study stresses the importance of understanding and analyzing students’ and teachers’ self-perceptions of sustainability consciousness that transforms participants’ values and beliefs into social action. The proposed study will focus on the environmental aspects of sustainability consciousness and examine issues in the fields of education and psychology. The study will rely on the use of two theoretical perspectives, based on Bateson’s transformative learning model and Hanvey’s conceptualizations of global awareness. Data sources will include a target of 5000 questionnaires of secondary school graduates who are current students of the eight Hong Kong’s University Grants’ Committee (UGC) funded institutions and up to 50 semi-structured interviews with secondary school teachers. The research team will liaise with the Educational Bureau (EdB) on this project which has the aims of developing recommendations for updating the LS curriculum, and providing advice to secondary school teachers about how to utilize the new NSS LS course materials and its resources for fostering sustainability consciousness in students. The proposed project is built upon our pilot study of over 700 secondary school graduates and 20 teachers, which was conducted in 2013 and 2014 by the proposed research team at the Hong Kong Institute of Education and supported by the Department of International Education and Lifelong Learning (Grant No. IELL_MP2013 and IELL_MP2014). 是項研究關注學生於新高中通識教育課程下在環保議題上所獲得的知識。研究目的乃描述及分析中學畢業生的環保意識和環保行為；並了解中學畢業生對環保議題的認知和他們的環保行為是否在新高中通識教育課程的學習過程中產生。研究重點分析學生自身對環保意識的觀念及教師對於如何通過新高中通識教育課程，提升學生對環保議題關注的概念。是項研究引用兩個理論模型，包括貝特森的變革學習模式及漢威的全球意識概念。是項研究於六所香港大專院校，邀請大約7200名大專新生透過問卷調查方式收集數據，同時邀請50名香港現職教師作為面談訪問對象。香港教育學院「國際教育與終身學習學系」已於2013年和2014年向大約700名學生進行試驗性的研究。

28608115.label: Realisation of objectives
28608115.value: OBJECTIVE 1 accomplished. This objective aimed to examine the self-perceptions of Hong Kong secondary school graduates about their sustainability consciousness resulting from the New Senior Secondary School Liberal Studies curriculum (NSS LS). A total of 5240 Hong Kong secondary school graduates who entered the eight publicly funded tertiary institutions completed a questionnaire. Online data collection of the 2016/17 student cohort (n=1989) yielded fewer responses compared with the previous 2015/16 cohort (n=3251), which was surveyed on paper. Document analysis included 989 student reflective narratives. The rigorous analysis revealed that NSS LS led to students’ high level of sustainability consciousness but low level of activism, participation in environmental groups and activities. At the same time, the study uncovered a unique feature of students’ sustainability consciousness, an action- and future-oriented mentality that allowed students to actively shape their sustainable realities by applying critical, imaginative, reflexive, and eschatological approaches. The descriptive examination revealed three major descriptors of students’ sustainability consciousness: Intention to make a difference; engagement with complex issues regarding identity, society, and nature; and students’ eschatological perspectives (See Section C Part 8 for related publications: Savelyeva & Douglas 2017; Savelyeva, 2018; Savelyeva, 2019; Savelyeva, 2019, in preparation). After each stage of data examination and analysis (2015 pilot stage; 2015/16 first student cohort; 2016/17 second student cohort) the results were released to the general public and published as reports on a project website (See Section C Part 12). During each research stage the findings were widely and actively disseminated and discussed with experts at international conferences, symposia, and workshops, and published in a reputable international Q1 journal as part of its special issue, co-edited by the PI (Savelyeva & Rickards, 2017); in an award winning Handbook, as part of a section edited by the PI (Savelyeva, 2018); and in a Japanese journal specialising in curriculum studies, in collaboration with Tokyo Gakugei University Curricular Centre For Teachers (Park & Savelyeva 2019, in Japanese) OBJECTIVE 2 accomplished. This objective aimed to explore the teachers’ perceptions about what features of the curriculum might have elevated students’ sustainability consciousness. 31 in-service secondary school teachers voluntarily participated in the semi-structured interviews. The analysis revealed a unique teaching model responsible for fostering sustainability consciousness in NSS LS classrooms. This model included four features: teachers’ quick adaptation, wide socialisation, deep innovation/creativity, and parents’ involvement. Teachers’ quality appeared as another important feature, together with the quality of teaching support. Teachers cited the following major hurdles to fostering sustainability consciousness: Disconnect between the values taught in class and those practiced in some of the students’ families; low-income family background; families’ different financial status; parental disengagement and lack of parental connection with NSS LS. Teachers reported tension between severe examination-related demands and their teaching aims to grow sustainability-minded, free critical thinkers as another major limitation. The objective has been thoroughly communicated and discussed with teachers in a series of research workshops, offered by the PI in 2017, 2018, and 2019 at the annual conference of Liberal Studies Teachers, in collaboration with the Hong Kong Liberal Studies Teacher Association, Hong Kong Teacher Union, and EdUHK (See Section C Parts 9, 12). The PI also delivered international workshops for teachers and teaching faculty in the Philippines, India, the UK, and locally at the Institute for General Education, CUHK, China. The PI gave talks at the Hong Kong Radio Television Backchat talk show, maintained a column in the Sing Tao Daily newspaper, and wrote an article for Hong Kong Economic Journal (See Section C Part 12). OBJECTIVE 3 accomplished. This objective aimed to contribute to the ongoing EDB series of NSS LS implementation studies (Ref. EDB150/4/4(10)) that examines students’ knowledge base in light of new developments in the secondary curriculum. The PI attended a meeting with EDB officials to discuss the directions of NSS LS in 2016 (See Section C Part 12). In December 2018 the curriculum entered a new policy implementation stage as the EDB formed a Task Force with an intention to revise NSS LS’s structure (See Section C Part 8, Savelyeva (in preparation) and Park & Savelyeva, 2019). The PI met with an EdUHK-based task force member and discussed a possibility for research contribution in the support of the governmental efforts. OBJECTIVE 4 accomplished. This objective aimed to provide first-hand data about a sustainability module of the curriculum and its ability to influence students’ values, beliefs, and goals. A vast amount of data generated from this study are organised in three reports which have been made publicly available on a project website (See Section C Part 12). The first-hand data about the curriculum and its ability to influence students’ sustainability consciousness has been communicated to local and international academic, teaching, and school communities through academic publications, public talks, via local media, at the conferences, symposia, and workshops. OBJECTIVE 5 accomplished. This objective aimed to identify methods and strategies to improve teaching for transformative learning in the NSS LS course. The study revealed three major methods and strategies for NSS LS classrooms: (1) infusing teaching methods that foster imaginary and creativity; (2) using the Internet and social media materials in LS classrooms; and (3) involving parents in NSS LS. The results also clearly showed that sustainability-wise, NSS Liberal Studies make a huge difference in fostering sustainable mind-sets of Hong Kong youth and thus the subject is worthy of its continued support and public investment The research informed participatory teacher workshops run by the PI and suggested specific methodologies to improve the NSS LS. The 2019 teacher workshop promoted an adaptation of the on-line Canton Trade Game into an activity for the NSS LS classrooms (in collaboration between Hong Kong America re CUHK, Maritime museum and Koding Kingdom) (See Section C Part 9 and 12 for workshop titles). OBJECTIVE 6 accomplished. This objective aimed to establish institutional collaborations for addressing the issues related to NSS LS implementation in secondary schools, as well as at tertiary levels of Hong Kong education. The study resulted in collaboration with the following public and private institutions: Institute for General Studies, CUHK; Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Lingnan University, The University of Hong Kong; UNESCO Hong Kong Association; Hong Kong American Centre, CUHK; Maritime Museum, Koding Kingdom; Sing Tao Daily newspaper; Hong Kong Economic Journal; Hong Kong Professional Teachers’ Union; Hong Kong Liberal Studies Teacher Association; World Institute for Sustainable Development Planners; Manchester Metropolitan University, UK; Loyola Marymount University, USA; O.P. Jindal Global University, India; the Tokyo University, Japan; Tokyo Gakugei University, Japan; Hiroshima University, Japan; University of Santo Tomas, Philippines; Macquarie University, Australia; Monash University, Australia; Hong Kong Radio Television (See Section C Part 12). OBJECTIVE 7 accomplished. The objective asked to increase the visibility of Hong Kong’s educational and research initiatives in the international arena by building up a strong on-line presence. The study created two websites that contain research-related information, resources for teachers, as well as references to public media sources that discuss the NSS LS developments and issues. http://sustainableducation.com https://www.eduhk.hk/LSPHK/
